detailed_description: Are you ready, kids? The cult classic is back, faithfully remade in spongetastic splendor! Play as SpongeBob, Patrick and Sandy and show the evil Plankton that crime pays even less than Mr. Krabs. Want to save Bikini Bottom from lots of rampant robots with your mighty bubbles? Of course you do! Want to underpants bungee jump? Why wouldn't you! Want to join forces in a brand new multiplayer mode? The battle is on! GAME FEATURES Play as SpongeBob, Patrick and Sandy and use their unique sets of skills Thwart Plankton's evil plan to rule Bikini Bottom with his army of wacky robots Meet countless characters from the beloved series REMAKE FEATURES Faithful remake of one of the best SpongeBob games ever created High-end visuals, modern resolutions and carefully polished gameplay Brand new horde mode multiplayer for up to two players, online and offline Restored content that was cut from the original game like the Robo Squidward boss fight and more

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game highly for the nostalgia. _childDocuments_.review: It's uncanny how familiar yet unfamiliar this game is now. But, it's missing some small details that, now they're gone, I just can't ignore it.1. NPCs don't make sounds when you hit them.2. Cardboard box TP animation is gone.3. The bubble bowl plate animation is gone (they just instantly pop down).4. Squidward doesn't yell at you for hitting his painting in his house anymore.5. In Jellyfish Fields, the cruise bubble plate instantly spawns the Tikis without any transition.There might be more, but the whole game feels a bit off in general.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has many bugs like crashes which are frequent, rendering issues that act up a lot, and many Frame Rate drops in many different areas. They made the game easier with bigger hit boxes that lasts longer  on the characters. The Patrick sections literally have everything auto targeted where as the older game allowed you to learn the physics engine to aim Patrick's shots leaving a unsatisfied use of Patrick as a character. I have played this game for three hours and I already crashed 5 times leaving me with a unsatisfied play of the game. If I were you I wait for them to fix the game and just play the old one if you still have it.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was sorta disappointed with this game because the controls felt too different from the original and there were weird unpolished bits, such as broken seesaws that would hinder your jumpingRock Bottom's last spatula even bugged out on me, where it would no longer spawn but also wasn't counted towards my total, forcing me to start over since I wanted to 100% the gameNeedless to say I was quite frustratedHowever on a second playthrough, the newer movement started to grow on me - such as Spongebob's double air stall and Patrick's attack now acting as some sort of dash - it enhanced the platforming and allowed me to do many sequence breaks that were satisfying to pull off and sped up the game tremendouslyWhile various things feel unpolished/unfinished which led to a very lukewarm first impression, the longer I stood with it the title the more I started to like it - even getting to the point that I now prefer this version over the originalIt was just a matter of getting used to the newer nuances, and learning how to take advantage of them

_childDocuments_.review: The rehydrated version isn't as good. more glitches, characters teleport where they're not supposed to when fast traveling. you can't replay the credit sequence, SpongeBob is animated newer (everybody agrees that SpongeBob has been progressively animated to look worse through the seasons.) Pictures on the wall feature new (bad) episodes. And he does his "bad A" quotes pretty much every time you use bubble powers in the new one as opposed to only when you get a super monster combo like in the old one. When sandy lassos robots, they explode in the air rather than her slamming them down. I swear many parts were easier to perform (though it might just be that I'm on mouse and keyboard now). You can get the sock at the top of the sea needle without the cruise missile in the new one as opposed to the old one. You can get 11/10 socks on sand mountain which means that you will have one sock left after 100% the game in the new one. Many people have reported the snowmen on that level just not spawning in so they CAN'T 100% the game. They didn't put in any new animations for character dialogue where they talk about interacting with objects. Squidward doesn't say "HEY" when you paint a mustache on his painting in his house. And the safe that falls on you in SpongeBob's house only showed up the first time for me and SpongeBob didn't even say "OWE" My first introduction to the game showed the classic opening cutscene with their mouth's movements off sync with their speech. I found me soft locking myself quite the bit because the cardboard boxes seem to not activate as easily in the new one which makes skipping them possible and this plays into characters going where they're not supposed to be with the fast traveling mechanic. There are countless out of bounds glitches, The bubble bowl's audio cuts out, dialogue sliding glitches, down town Bikini Bottom has buildings you can get to the top of that don't have any hit boxes,Oh, and they didn't even wait until ray tracing before remastering:(

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game for my 8yr old son as he saw it when I was browsing the summer sale. So far he has spent a lot of time playing but has gotten hung up in the city while playing as Sandy. He was having a hard time so he asked me for help. I took the controller and spent a few minutes learning the mechanics. Pretty simple stuff. The games controls seem to work when they want to. Pressing buttons seems to either perform the intended action or it does nothing. Tested my controller latency with other games to make sure I wasn't having that issue. Nope. Pretty precise and on time. But in this game, pressing a button may or may not do anything. Makes things like traversing a jumping puzzle almost impossible. Trying to lasso Sandy across the map with a 35 second timer was unbelievably frustrating when the lasso has a 50% chance of working. The other 50% of the time you fall to your death. Also, the "arm" that grabs you when you fall down a pit likes to come on the screen and grab when you are in mid jump, and nowhere near falling, causing you to have to start over. This game has some serious bugs with it's gameplay. Shame because my son insists on playing it because he loves SpongeBob, but can't really make any progress in the game because of the faulty controls. This 8 yr old child is able to play streets of rage 4 on hard difficulty on PS4 at a decent level, so it's not like the game is too hard for him or he doesn't understand it. Just controls that work when they want to. Too bad he's played it too long for me to get a refund. I'll pay closer attention next time he gets a game he wants so that of it's broken, I can still get my money back before it's too late.

_childDocuments_.review: Never played the original, so not sure what parts were added quality of life, but it was a solid game.Voice acting sounded like it was the actors from the show (apart from Mr. Krabs), which is always a solid/arguably needed touch. I only watched the early seasons of the show, but the levels chosen and references they managed to fit into the game were impressive.The hints for the spatulas were nice as was the accompanying fast travel system. By the time it came to finding the last socks though, I wish they had done similar hints. Each level/area is 3-4 zones; it would have been nice to know which of those 3-4 zones was hiding the last sock rather that scouring the whole level and eventually using an online guide. I understand why game devs make certain decisions (e.g. Spongebob and Patrick die to falling in "goo" AKA water in an underwater setting), but the game does tend to punish you for exploring even though some socks are in dangerous locations that require said exploration. Final gripe is the character switching: wish they had made switching possible wherever you were rather than at set locations; I shouldn't have to go to zone 3, switch to Patrick, box travel back to the beginning of zone 3, warp to zone 2, and backtrack half of zone 2 just to get 1 collectible.To end on a positive note, the Cruise Bubble ability is awesome. Reminds me of the bug in Rayman Arena and the Batman Arkham remote batarang.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a an extremely faithful remaster of the original Gamecube game of the same name, and is still just as fun as ever. I, like most, played this on the Gamecube, and the music, visuals, atmosphere are all very well executed in this remaster, bringing one back to the Bikini Bottom of yesteryear. So far, I personally have not experienced a single bug in this game, and am very pleased with my experience going down memory lane. Great game, great remaster, highly recommended for anyone who remembers this game, played it back in the day, or simply loves platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: Are ya ready kids? Ay Ay Captain. Ohhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh, who lives in a pineapple under the sea? Spongebob Squarepants! And with those word I want to welcome you to SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom – Remad.. Uh I mean Rehydrated.This is a game I loved to play on the PlayStation 2 and now finally became remade, in fully glory and now FINALLY after all these years, we don’t get a different port or game on the PC but the same Jump and Run game like on the console! Yes, we have to consider that many people that are hyped for the game are those who used to play the original 2003 Version of the game and that’s why we should do a neutral review on the game. It already begins with the icon Theme song and an overhauled menu that we all know. And I think that is beautiful. The first time I started the game I was so pumped in seeing the beautiful introduction cutscene of the game and Instantly saw something I could have raged upon….You see, I played the game in the German version at the start. Why? Well I live in Germany and want to perfect my German… and I got disappointed… The Cutscene is not synchronised with the audio. It was 2 seconds delayed… I do not know if it only occurred to me? Or if it the developers messed it up, but for a game that coasts 30 Euros I certainly can expect that something like this does not happen. And no, its not only the introduction scene but every kind of talk I had in the game, so as it annoyed me, I just swapped the language to English. That is bad for a first introduction. Also I have to point out that there are some flaws within the animations when you are in a talk, but they are something you can dismiss as they are not so annoying LIKE THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SPEECH AND MOUTH MOVING WICH IS SOMETHING YOU SEE 90 PERCENT OF THE TIME TALKING TO SOMEONE. Ahm. Back to tracks.The In-Game menu also got visually overhauled, which is beautifully made and remembers of the old classic title. Also, the In-Game music has been remade into stereo. Well you think it is remade, but everyone who played the original knows: It is the original soundtrack. But made with a little weird stereo effect that is on it. But some of the boss soundtracks have gotten another Instrument playing here and there. But I don’t care, as the soundtrack is still beautiful and sets the tone of the game perfectly well.It is still the game we remember. Where nothing has changed. But now the game is on the PC and doesn’t has a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ PC port…. Like in the old days…. yeah….. you remember it too right, dear reader?It is fun, it suites everyone who likes Spongebob and a 3D Platformer. And it is also good to play with your child or nieces or idk…. As it is just Spongebob.If you want a full review about the game, check out LambHoots review of the original game. As there is nothing much changed: Oh and btw. You can actually play this game with keyboard and mouse. Yes I am not kidding. I tried it and it worked like a charm. Its something to get used too. But it works good even in faster pace.Thank you for reading till here my dear reader. I hope to see you in my next review. And if you found any error or just want to tell that I can ♥♥♥♥ off then go ahead and tell me. I am always open for corrections :D

_childDocuments_.review: It doesn't necessarily eclipse/replace the original for people like me who grew up with it, but this is still a (mostly) well executed and faithful remake of a beloved classic that returning fans should be pleased with. Definitely recommended for fans of 3D Collectathon Platformers like Banjo-Kazooie and the first Jak & Daxter.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just as amazing as I remembered it from my childhood. Purple Lamp has done a beautiful job with the animations, the colors, the humor and in general with building on the stuff that made the original so good and bringing it up to a 2020 Standard. They even cooperated with Speedrunners to catch the spirit of the original and to give it a new spin that still feels unique.  So if you want a cute, fun Jump'n'Run thats just bright and engaging here is the game for you. Even as an adult despite the rather low difficulty its just a nice experience to escape into the fun world of Bikini Bottom with its amazing characters and to feel a bit nostalgic. Although I also think that people that are new to the world of Spongebob especially younger ones can get a lot of fun out of this game and maybe learn to like the characters a lot of people hold dear in their memories.The game just reminds me of days when living felt easier, memories werent as clouded, and I am grateful for that. I really recommend Spongebob SquarePants BfBB - Rehydrated and now actually kinda feel the urge to watch the series again with now 22 yrs of age haha.Now thanks for reading and have a great time even if you dont buy the game! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, my childhood has been remade!!I've been excited for this game ever since it was first announced. Seeing one of my favorite childhood games getting remade got me excited and already determined to buy. There are so many good things about this game and few things I have some problems with.First, the negative:While the game is pretty polished, there are still a few bugs in the game. The first noticeable one was poor audio syncing with the opening cutscene. While it fixed itself in later cutscenes, it was still noticeable and not a very good first impression. In fact it got me worried what others bugs await me in the game. The others that stood out to me were getting caught on small floor clips or rocks and slipping off of platforms. Thankfully, it didn't ruin the whole experience for me and I do expect them to be patched out later. Thankfully that loud audio glitch with the waterfalls in Jellyfish Fields is no longer there.This next negative is more of a pet peeve, or a mixed issue, and that's the use of the original audio. On the one hand, great, they didn't change much of the original sound effects, music, or voice acting. On the other hand, they didn't change much of the original sound effects, music, or voice acting. Mr. Krabs and Mermaid Man are not voiced by their original actors. I could let Mermaid Man go since you don't encounter him a lot, especially after the Mermalair level, but Clancy Brown can't be that hard to reach to voice Mr. Krabs lines. Considering how you interact with him a lot in this game, Mr. Krab's voice is just weird and uncomfortable to listen to. As for the music, I do love that they kept the original soundtrack, but that's all they have. It would've been nice to hear a one extra song for each of the levels instead of hearing the same music on a loop for the entire time you're playing the level. I don't have many problems with the sound effects but they could be amplified a bit more, sometimes the alert for enter the robots agro zone is practically mute. The last negative has to deal with the controls, specifically for PC. It's very awkward to and a little uncomfortable, at least for me. I ended up plugging my Xbox controller in and the game become sooo much more playable after I did that. That's all for the negative, now for the positive and there's a lot. This game is so pretty! When I first entered Bikini Bottom, I thought it was alright but then I became blown away when I entered Jellyfish Fields. Oh my gosh, every single color was vibrant, the lighting makes it gorgeous, and the textures look like something out of a painting. After that I was continuously blown away with every new level, my favorite being Rock Bottom for it's great use of dark blues, purples, and neon. It is a treat to the eyes and it's exactly what I expect for a Spongebob game in 2020. One thing that impressed me right off the bat was the addition of brand new animations. The characters are far more expressive now than they were back in 2003, and it should be like that. While I do miss the original animations, I am welcome these new ones. It's great to see their body language and facial expressions change to match the tone of their lines, rather than hold one pose. The combat in this game is still the same as before but now it feels like it's been smoothed out. I'm not sure how but the characters actions feel more natural or better executed. Spongebob's bubble powers are still fun to use and his attacks have a lot more weight to them. Patrick feels like your driving a tank and it should feel like for a fat starfish. Sandy's combat is the most fun with sped up karate chops and kicks and her lasso. Story and dialogue wise, it's still the same. Same story and same jokes, and I honestly prefer it that way. Why change something that already works? In fact, I find the jokes funnier now than I did when I played this when I was five. I finally get the joke "Retirement Home Girls Gone Wild." Ew. I know I've made my grief about the music, but it really is nice to hear the original soundtrack again, it's such a great nostalgia trip. In fact, this whole game is a nostalgia trip. It brings me back to a simpler time when I would spend hours in the basement playing this game on my Nintendo GameCube. Playing this makes me wonder if THQ Nordic has plans to remake their other Spongbob titles. I would LOVE to see a remake of Creature from the Krusty Krab, the Spongebob Squarepants Movie, or even Lights, Camera, Pants. Heck I'll even take remakes of the Jimmy Neutron games, especially Jet Fusion and Attack of the Twonkies. THQ Nordic, if you remake these games with the same quality as Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated, I will buy every single one! In summary, this a great remake for fans who have played the original game. If you're a fan of spongebob, I highly recommend getting this game. At $30, you can't go wrong with buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game, loved playing through the whole thing for the first time in years.  If you're looking to relive this game, this is a wonderful way to go about it.  If you're looking for a fun, short, 3D platformer collectathon, this is again a wonderful way to go about it.  However, if you are looking to speedrun this game just like the original, just go load up an emulator man. While this game is already developing its own run, its really not similar to the original's.  However, I still believe this new run will also be fun, but more casual.9/10 - Great, fun game that'll get ya 8-10 hours, 12-13 if you 100%. (Worth the $30 for sure)

_childDocuments_.review: Spongebob BFBB Rehydrated was a decent remaster for $30. It doesn’t change the gameplay hardly at all, i felt pretty much like i was playing the original most of the time. Visually, the remastered graphics are great, albeit the colors are a little oversaturated.It was really nice how they added expressive animations  to the dialogues sequences. They look 100x better now then the lifeless original.My primary gripe with the game is how they really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up some of the animations and sound effects. A good handful of the original sound effects have been needlessly replaced (and occasionally removed!) with inferior sounds. Also, many of the animations both in cutscenes and gameplay look stiff or very awkward. Audio desync was an issue in some cutscenes.The playthrough was mostly bug-free, although a couple of times i got stuck in a falling animation glitch that took a good 30 seconds to break out of, probably by luck.I havent played the multiplayer mode because idc about it but ive heard its pretty subpar and tacked on. One major disappointment was the broken promise that the devs made awhile back to add in cut content like patricks dream, the squidward-bot boss fight, glove world, etc. Instead of these being added into the game like promised, they are lazily hinted at in the tacked on multiplayer as islands. The squidward bot is just an enemy spawner. Lame. Also, dont bother paying to enter the theater at the end of the game; the cool original concept art has been replaced with just screenshots of the game? idk why they botheredThe playthrough was mostly bug-free, although a couple of times i got stuck in a falling animation glitch that took a good 30 seconds to break out of, probably by luck.I give the remaster a 7/10. The $30 price point saves it, if it were $60 that would be a big ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ problem. I recommend this to people who played the original, but more so to fans of platformers who never did play the original; this is a great hidden gem for any platformer fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I still can't even believe that this even happened. Heavy Iron Studios' Battle for Bikini Bottom has a special place in my heart, the early seasons of Spongebob Squarepants is easily one of my absolute favorite shows and this game is a love letter to that era. The references to the show are spot on and this game just feels like a Spongebob episode. Not to mention that as a 3D platformer, it's one of the bests in the genre. As a remake however, I feel it is lacking.Pros:- A chance to play this game on current gen consoles- The graphics are spectacular, almost every level and music track look amazing- The robot redesigns are great, easily better than the original. The only exception being Robot Patrick, as he looks much more threatening in the original- The boss fight changes are welcome, like Flying Dutchman's increased difficulty - Some quality of life changes form the originalA quick side note, I don't really get this game being called a remake. I greatly commend the developers for building this game from the ground up and being this incredibly accurate to the original, but very little was added on to this game. The cut content from the original that was teased for a year is barely anything, despite the fact that the original game has tons of unused content, and the small amount they include is designated to a lackluster multiplayer mode. No Patrick phase with Spongebot, Patrick's unused dream level is used as a small island in the multiplayer, no Glove World, and Robot Squidward is just a glorified robot spawner locked in the multiplayer instead of an actual boss fight. Cons:-Lack of polish in many areas, especially animations and lighting during gameplay and cutscenes-Mr Krabs and Mermaid Man retain their voices from the originals. Mermaid Man makes sense due to Ernest Borgnine's passing, but why not Clancy Brown? -You can't refight the robot bosses -Mr Krab's spatula prices are absurdly increased from the original version, as if they weren't expensive enough already. What were they thinking?- The only real new addition, multiplayer, is mere filler and isn't really even worth a playthroughAs a remake, this game kind of falls flat. But as a remastered version of one of my favorite childhood games, I can recommend it. The controls, gameplay, collecting are still as fun as they were in the original with beautiful HD textures. The hub world and the 9 levels look better then they ever have. Purple Lamp Studios' effort put into this game and love of the original are apparent, but I think they somewhat missed the mark in terms of this being a remake. Very few of the originals games biggest issues were addressed. The restored, unused content had great potential but was just tossed aside. The new mode is unnecessary and boring, though I can see kids being mildly entertained by it. If you haven't played the original and you love old Spongebob, give this a shot. If you own the original, I'd say stick to that as it's equally, if not more, fun to play than this version. I still prefer the original, but I'm glad that this game got enough support to even have a remaster in the first place. I just hope the success of this game encourages Nickelodeon to never let Activision anywhere near a Spongebob game ever again

_childDocuments_.review: Great remake. I'd give it a shot even if you've never played the original. + As with the original, it's an exceptional collect-a-thon with tight controls and tons of character. The dialogue and interactions between characters are genuinely funny and entertaining. The attention to detail turns what would be filler areas with unimpressive NPCs in other games into lively environments that reward you for exploring them with little easter eggs or nods to the series. It's probably one of the best uses of a TV show license implemented into a video game.+ Purple Lamp made a significant effort to stay faithful to the original version of the game. Subtle attention to detail is preserved and even more content is added. I particularly loved the museum in Rock Bottom and seeing the artwork in a higher resolution. I had completely forgotten about the mime that appears in the window of the Krusty Krab and little things like that are a delight to anybody looking for a nostalgic experience.  + The game looks beautiful and I'm thrilled to live in a time where I can see a giant high-res Squidward model drift through the air.+ Audio is crisp, now stereo, and faithful to the original while making slight improvements.Minor issues could and should be fixed with an update. - I found two typos throughout the game, one where the audio doesn't match the text in a dialogue, and one where there wasn't a space between two words.- I glitched multiple times when interacting with liquid that causes you to bounce. I would find myself stuck in the bouncing animation typically caught in a rock or under a floor until a robot shot me with tar-tar sauce to free me.- The momentum on teetering platforms is completely wrong. They constantly eat your jumps and it just doesn't feel right. I was playing the game casually and it felt buggy and incomplete. Nothing like how the original felt.- The momentum exiting slides is also completely wrong. Especially in Jellyfish Fields, where there are collectibles only attainable by jumping off the ramp at the end of slides, I found it incredibly difficult to not have my momentum entirely eaten by getting caught on the ramp. I wasn't missing the collectible. This wasn't a challenge, it felt like a bug. It felt like there wasn't polish. I eventually got used to it and adapted, but that is no excuse. I shouldn't have to adapt how I play around bad design.- The Bubble Bowl could use so much work. I can never get it to work on the ramps designed for it, often over or under-shooting by a large margin. Its detection on the spinners/wooden wheel pegs throughout the entire game is off and requires unreasonable precision, and its detection on the stone block in the rolling ball area of the Mermalair is inexcusably poor. I literally had to search for what I was doing incorrectly after trying to throw a bubble bowl into the stone block from several different angles. This is coming from someone who played the original and knows the solution to the puzzle. I can't imagine getting stuck there as somebody who's never played the original.- This is by far the worst minor issue. The stone tiki collision sound effect isn't changed with the SFX volume. It is literally painfully loud and 100% unexpected the first time. If you play at full volume, you won't tell, but if you turn the game down significantly like I did, it's enough to make you avoid throwing stone tikis unless it's required. The same issue happens when breaking shhh tikis.The gate opening sound effect has this issue too, specifically the last clicking sound at the end of it. I'm not sure how this was missed. I think any play test would've caught it if they played around with the volume at all. Major issues likely won't be fixed but are a disappointment.- Shiny object grinding should have been made less prominent or easier. I understand Purple Lamp was trying to stay faithful to the original, but this was something they could have improved on and I think everyone would enjoy. If you play through the game casually, you will simply not have enough shiny objects for all of Mr. Krabs' golden spatulas. This means you must grind for them. Resetting a checkpoint in Goo Lagoon 200 times isn't captivating gameplay. It isn't fun. It isn't what I wish came back from my childhood. I suggest they add thousands of more shiny objects in the ending credits level. It would make the level more useful and interesting instead of being just a fun afterthought. They could buff the skee-ball fair game after you defeat the final boss so there are more engaging ways to grind, while also not affecting shiny objects early on.- The new theater simply lacks content, and based on my previous point, I'm sure you can assume it is NOT worth grinding for the shiny objects necessary to open it. I'd suggest making it open by default or add content if it's going to remain so difficult to unlock.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the time fool you. I have played this game for many, many years on the PS2 all the way up until February when I learned that this game was getting a remaster.  tldr: Don't trust the critics. Trust the fans. Great game. Great remaster. So many childhood memories brought back. 10/10 overall rating. Let me first start off by saying this... I'm a 25 year old man who is soon to be married, works a 9-5, owns two cars, and has a couple of student loans under my belt.  I'm not a child, but I am still passionate about this game. This game is really a reskin of SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom from 2003.  But it's perfect in every way.  IGN and the other ya-hoos that have reviewed this game gave it low scores because of "just being a reskin." "not innovating or updating gameplay." and "The Last of Us II is a 10/10." THEY DON'T KNOW WHAT THEY'RE TALKING ABOUT! I'm glad the developers who remastered this game kept the controls and gameplay just how it was. It was fine without needing to be upgraded.  Graphics: Graphically, the game is absolutely stunning.  The colors are bright and vibrant.  It runs well on my PC with zero frame stutter.  Unless you go into the data files, you can't really mess with the game's graphics at all (at least I assume you'd have to go into the files to change stuff up).  There are a few things to note... When you wander through Jellyfish Fields, the GRASS MOVES AS YOU WALK THROUGH IT!!! How cool is that?!?!Sound: The sound is basically copy and pasted over to this game.  All the voice characters are the same (so sadly, Mr. Krabs is not voiced by Clancy Brown, but that's okay).  The soundtrack is just as wonderful and charming as I remembered.  I pre-ordered this game and was able to get access to the soundtrack as well.  There are sometimes when audio doesn't match up with characters or it disappears entirely, but it's so minuscule, you barely even notice it.  There may have been a few sound tweaks to the game, but other than that it is pretty much the same just with updated sound quality.  Replayabiltiy: I've played this game many, many times as a child -- letting my imagination take over and coming up with my own stories long after I was finished with the main part of the game.  In my later years, I returned just trying to complete all the challenges and find all of Patrick's missing socks.  I doubt I have the fuel to imagine some of the wild adventures I conjured up as a child while playing this game, but if I'm able to, I can assure you, I will be playing it for years to come.  In conclusion: This game is a 10/10, and here's why... It's a perfect, tediously well-done remaster of my favorite childhood game.  Playing SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom now brings back so many good memories from when I was young, carefree, and happy.  To sit down and play this game now, it offers me a little bit of hope and escape from my 9-5 job, bills, and worries about what the future may bring.  It really reignited my inner child, and I love that.  From the bottom of my heart, I am thankful to the developers who took the time and dedication to bring my favorite childhood game back to life.  I hope and pray that one day perhaps Tak and the Power of Juju might also be remastered (probably my 3rd or 4th favorite game).  If you stuck with me through the end of this review, I also thank you for taking the time to read through it.  Have a great day and stay safe out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original game. I've seen it, but Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated does seem like a way to get more people playing this classic than upgrading it.That said, this game is TOTALLY worth the price if you wanna complete it, plus the soundtrack is great and is definitely something I listen to all the time.As someone who only played one of the sequels (Truth or Square), I can see why this game is considered so great. It's really good! I expected an 8/10 game when I first streamed this and that's what I got. Just what makes this game fun?The game follows a humorous plot of Plankton trying to get the Krabby Patty formula by using robots. However, he accidentally makes the robots unruly because he forgot to enable the obey mode (Plankton believes in robot freedom, or he's just an idiot), this causes them to destroy Bikini Bottom and it's up to Spongebob, Patrick, and Sandy to TAKE HIM DOWN.Every character is really fun to use and allow have their own unique moves. Spongebob is in the middle between the two. he's agile but can also attack decently. Patrick is heavier, slower, but can throw objects and beat up enemies with his "moves." Sandy is the fan-favorite to control, she's incredibly agile, can swing around, and can combat enemies pretty well.This game is one where you have to complete missions to get items to progress. This game is split up in three acts, each with about 3 full levels each. The first act sees you going through natural, iconic, and outdoor places in Bikini Bottom. The second act sees you going to more industrial but nearly as welcoming places. The third act has some difficult challenges in a variety of environments generally seen as scary in the show.Each act has an easy mini-boss and a slightly more difficult robotic version of one of the main characters. Robot Sandy, Robot Patrick, and Robot Spongebob being the last one. The bosses are all fun and simple and usually have one or two characters you play as.This game is really fun and I would highly recommend it, even if it isn't the upgrade it promises.

_childDocuments_.review: Tldr: If you want a better gameplay experience, play the original. If you're in it for the visual aspect or a quick nostalgia trip, you'll prefer this one. I suggest trying it out first, then getting a refund if you don't like how it plays.BFBB was one of my favorite childhood games, so I was really looking forward to this remake with promises of better visuals and restored content that was cut out of the original game.I originally planned on getting this game on the Switch since they promised it would run at 60 FPS on Switch as well, but that turned out to be a lie after gameplay footage was uploaded. I then turned to the PC release, hoping to get the most optimal version.Right off the bat, the issues were already apparent. The game was not straining my computer at all, yet it was perpetually losing 15 FPS at 1080p due to the fullscreen mode just being a borderless window mode instead. Because the game has basically no graphical options, I had to fix this by manually going into the config file and enabling the true fullscreen mode, which fixed the issue as long as I didn't alt-tab out of the game.With that problem resolved, I started playing and was having a decent time....But then I started noticing the other problems with this remake, and even the devs.PS: I went back and checked my original GameCube copy to confirm if any of my problems with this remake were there. This isn't someone being blinded by nostalgia - these are legitimate issues with Rehydrated.UPDATE: I refunded the game. Didn't want to wait any longer for them to fix the game. If it's any better now, that's nice, but I'll stick to my original GameCube copy since it's much more enjoyable for me.

Godrays and extra particle effects add to the feeling of being underwater which is a small yet appreciated addition! To conclude the game is far prettier i will still always love the original cause its the game i grew up with but Rehydrated is a great update to a great classic That new and returning players will enjoy! overall rating is 9/10. _childDocuments_.review: - Visually beautiful.- Faithful level recreation.- Convenient and novel menu for tracking collectibles.- Multiplayer mode = slightly more content.- Patched a handful of exploits from the original.- Mr. Krabs and Mermaid Man still have their AWFUL voice actors from the original game.- Bug: Camera options reset when switching characters at a bus stop.- Mr. Krabs' spatulas are insanely expensive. Completed the game except for his spatulas and I still need more shiny objects than I collected throughout the entire game thus far.- "Rebalanced" some of the robots, which really just means the game got even easier than it already was.- Temperamental enemy hitboxes. Often when attacking an enemy you will collide with them but deal no damage. This is most obvious with tartar sauce robots and the triple stack robots.- Physics interactions with balls (SpongeBob's ball form and bubble bowl, and beach balls most notably) are terrible. Also, any time a ramp is involved, there are strange collisions with what appears to be nothing.- The camera has a feature which automatically makes objects invisible if it thinks they're in the way, but more often than not they disappeared when I need to see them to jump on them rather than when they were actually in the way.Overall, a fun old game with improved graphics. It takes a lot of work to remake a game this precisely, so not having much to point out is a good thing in my book. Removed a couple bugs and added some other ones, though most of them didn't impact the game in any consistent way so it's not much of a problem.

_childDocuments_.review: Battle for Bikini Bottom is a fairly traditional collect-athon platformer. If you played the original you'll feel right at home here. It doesn't really push any boundaries and is definitely more geared towards fans of the show, featuring a lot of original characters. It features lots of neat little mechanics you use to progress through levels and will have you switching between characters to utilise all their abilities to fully complete levels. There is a great deal of diversity to locations and the soundtrack in each area mimics the feel of the levels accurately. Ultimately this game plays out well, if not a little generic. I'd recommend if you either like platformers or are/were a fan of the show. Anyone outside of that demographic I think would find this a little underwhelming as there's no real challenge. The only challenge is if you happen to fall to your death (or die, but that's far less likely), all enemies in the area will respawn and whilst they pose no challenge themselves, you'll have to slug through an area, often a large part of it, all over again if you didn't have a checkpoint. The same "reset" applies to some puzzles which can take a moderate amount of time to finish, so falling off a ledge at the last hurdle can be quite tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to say I took the time to 100% the game including all of the socks and unlocks in the game like the theater in addition to the 100 spatulas. Also this review is based on the game post updates as of August 16th 2020.I was a big fan of the original game when I got the original Spongebob Squarepants Battle for Bikini Bottom when I was 8 years old on my playstation 2 in 2003. It was essentially a very well made 3D platformer with your favorite sea sponge being taken to all of the familiar settings in the show to stop robots running amok thanks to Plankton's plans going horribly wrong. I would argue that game was probably the best "licensed" videogame ever made and captured all of the fundamental 3D platformer elements almost perfectly and I'm happy to say this game revives the magic of the original game with a modern updated twist.Graphically the game looks stunning using the Unreal Engine, the original was made with an engine made by Heavy Iron themselves (the original dev team in the classic game) and I think Purple Lamp captured the art style of the original very well. Purple Lamp's art style is more similar to later seasons of Spongebob to better capture kids who are fans of the show today, and honestly it works to their advantage, the colors are vibrant, the world is alive. I enjoyed playing the game and just looking at how well the environments were done. The gameplay is basically the same as the original game and its for the best because the original game had an almost perfect interpretation of the 3D platformer genre, as the old saying goes "if it ain't broke don't fix it". Perhaps the most impressive thing about the gameplay is that it essentially mirrors the original but Purple Lamp did not have access to the source code of the game so they went off of just how the original game played which is phenomenal. The gameplay itself of course includes some changes and tweak in certain levels, some of the symbols are different to make it more kid friendly, minor changes to Sand Mountain and the Vine slide slides, but its 98% the original game and the tweaks works in their favor. Not to mention that Purple Lamp includes little easter eggs and callbacks to later seasons of the series which I thought was a nice added touch.In terms of bugs and glitches the only ones I encountered in the game were minor nitpicks, such as problems with some of the lip syncing at times, in the beginning I got soft locked in the starting area in Spongebob's library where I got stuck behind a button. Other than that the game ran smoothly. I know there was an issue of loading screens but post patch they lasted no more than a few seconds so I'm glad it was fixed. My only other complaint is that I feel like the multiplayer was kinda just rubber stamped into the game, I understand they wanted to make their own addition to the game which is fine and all but I don't see myself playing online here anytime soon, I might do it just to try it out though.All in all I am very impressed with the love and care Purple Lamp put into this game, it's a very well done love letter to a cult classic and childhood favorite of mine and to Heavy Iron studios, and with Purple Lamp supposedly only having something like 8 or 9 months to develop this game on its own is very impressive. Well done Purple Lamp and THQ Nordic, I look forward to what other games you release because this game is a masterpiece. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Spongebob battle for bikini bottom (BFBB) is a nice game if you are into this type of games. If you havent played the original then it is important to know that this is not a story driven cut scene based game. This game is all about collecting items which can be used to unlock more levels. Sometimes you need to do a certain task to get the item. That being said, there are quite a few boss battles which are very easy compared to the rest of the game.Pros-1. Very nice level design2. Beautiful surroundings and nice particle effects3. Engaging combat mechanics4. Humorous  character interaction.5. Couple of game modes to shake things up.Cons-1. The game requires you to grind constantly ie. searching every inch of the map to collect the items and doing nearly impossible stuff which can get a little boring.2. The character shadows are terrible which makes the game much harder than it was meant to be. For instance, when jumping from one platform to the other, you cant tell if your character is going to land on the next platform or going to fall down. in other words, zero depth perception.3. Couple of bugs here and there.4. Mermaidman and krabs voice not upto mark.To conclude, this is a nice game but its a bit too hard and sometimes boring.

_childDocuments_.review: As a wee lad, I have only played so much of the original BFBB on the og Xbox without getting too far due to being frightened to death by the robots in Jelly Fish fields. Besides not getting to experience all of the original I have a fair amount of experience with the mechanics due to playing the movie game as a child and also have been watching speedruns of BFBB for over 2 years now. That is the extent of my knowledge of the og but I know how tight the controls were and how solid of a platformer it was. I feel I can fairly compare this remake to the og.   BFBB Rehyradted to me is a super solid remake and almost perfect 1 to 1 recreation of the original and with the time purple lamp had and also dealing with a global pandemic, I'm surprised the product is fully functional at a CASUAL level. The controls in my opinion for each of the characters are far superior to the og besides some sloppy animations, for example, Bubblebash and Bubbleslam,  Sandys swingers all feel a bit off but don't ruin the overall experience in the slightest but would make it way better if they were polished up more. To me controlling the characters felt more responsive and satisfying to play. BFBB Rehydrated is a super solid platformer for any fans of the show or just in general fans of the genre will enjoy the product. What are the negatives? As mentioned Purple lamp was rushed in development and you can definitely feel that as you play more and more even as somebody who's not familiar with the whole game. The end of the game is super unpolished, **** SPOILERS ****  The final boss Robo Sponge feels super unfinished, really buggy, lack of announcer the whole boss fight, in general, has a considerable amount of jank and rushed feeling too it. Some of the "artistic choices" most notable the abundant fog in Sand Mountain is super distracting but doesn't detract too much from the product and also there is a little too much over-saturation and bloom in certain levels but overall I personally really love the art style and fits in with the current look for the show and movies.  The lack of polish near the end and tons of audio glitches randoms bugs start to show their ugly face once you sink more and more time into it. I feel those are nitpicks beside the glitches and can easily be fixed with a patch. The one glaring flaw the takes away from the casual experience compared to the original is the increased price of shiny objects for Krab Spatulas and forces the player to grind for super long as in a rough estimate would be 2 hours to get 100% and that's just because you will get bored doing it. That is only an issue for 100% but a glaring issue nonetheless. The game overall improves on a ton to the original heavy iron SpongeBob games and is well worth the 30$ for fans of the original or just love the show or 3d platformers. Hopefully, Purple Lamp will patch those issues and make a proper new game in the near future.  Just Please Ignore the IGN and Gamespot reviews for the game that don't justifiably look at the product fairly and only dislike due to it not changing too much which isn't what Purple Lamp wanted to do. Defo not a 2/10 or 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Are you ready kids? I don't know if you said the thing but you should be this is a great remake of a childhood favorite. Graphics:I don't dwell on graphics but sometimes the graphics are amazing at most points of the game. It also has great new animations for it as well.Performance:The game runs great I don't have too many problems with it, however there is plenty of pop-in to go around in this version of the game even the cutscenes have some noticeable pop-in when the original game didn't.Keyboard & Mouse Controls:This is where I get negative. You can get used too it eventually but unlike most PC games I've played, this game doesn't let you remap the keyboard & mouse which is something I've come to expect in a PC game. However, the controls aren't the most awkward thing to get used too on Keyboard & Mouse in fact I managed to get through most of the game with just Keyboard & Mouse. Controller support is good though, so if' you're playing with a controller it's perfect for you. As someone who prefers Keyboard & Mouse I'd give the K+B support an, it's alright.Proton (Linux/Steam Deck):I don't have a Steam Deck but I have played this game on a Linux Desktop before using proton and it works great. I only had trouble with the last boss of the game and even then all I had to do was restart my computer and try the boss again (I probably did something wrong).Overall:It's a good remake with a couple of dents in it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game so far is good and I would recommend it to any fans of the original. There are however things you should be aware of before buying it.The movement: In the original, this was the thing that made you want to play. The way spongebob felt to hop around and move throughout the maps (as well as Sandy) felt fluid and stiff but you were in full control. Here it's a little bit more stiff, slow, and it feels like there's a little bit more friction. Patrick however, is improved greatly. He feels very good to move around with because his attack launches him forward a little.Bugs: There are some quirky things here that I ran into in my short time. Clipping through things, bubble bowl getting stuck on random objects or ramps and becoming an object I can physically stand on in game. There are more but they slip from my mind. There is nothing game breaking, just little things that I feel could've been polished out if the devs were given more time. I believe they are putting out updates to try and fix these, but don't quote me on that.Game Jank: The cutscene animations don't sync to the mouth, but there is still a lot of charm to be found in how characters move and react to what they are actually saying (which the original didn't have) There are still weird audio problems just like the first. When I respawn randomly every noise will be much louder than usual. It levels out after about a second but it was weird. (It only happened on Goo Lagoon for me)The game itself is now beautiful though and the gameplay loop you know and love is still in tact. I plan on 100% this in like 3 days and casually coming back and just hoping around and doing things when I need some brain off time. This game is VERY fun to play because of the charm and feel of it all. It's feels different, to the original, but not better or worse IMO. A true remake in that sense.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited for this game. I grew up playing the original, and I still play it from time to time on my old PS2; it remains one of my all time favourite games. Rehydrated is a mostly faithful remake, with beautiful graphics, nice animations, and fun gameplay. That being said, this game isn't without it's flaws. The game is riddled with small bugs and polish issues that really threw me off during my first playthrough. Most of the bugs I've encountered aren't game breaking, like if you teleport into Spongebob's pineapple when you're playing as Sandy or Patrick, you won't turn back to Spongebob. Even so, the amount of small bugs makes it extremely noticable. Same with the polish issues. Some parts of the game felt like maybe they just needed a tiny bit more time to go over the game and see if there was anything that could be changed or fixed to improve the overall experience, like the invisible boatmobile in the Mermalair, or how some of the set dressing messes with the Spongebowl ability. Again, lots of small things.A bigger issue I had was with the way Steam achievements work. In my first playthrough of the game I was unable to receive the achievements for 100%ing because of an issue with a spatula in Spongebob's dream (which meant I also didn't receive the achievement for that), and an issue with the 80th sock. I decided to start another playthrough, and after I collected one sock and a few spatulas in this new game, I was awarded the 100% achievement and the 80 sock achievement. The same thing happened after I collected a few spatulas in Spongebobs dream. i don't know if this is a problem on Steams end or on the games end but either way, when I did 100% the game it didn't feel as good, which I guess is a subjective feeling but oh well.Even with the bug and polish issues, I would still recommend this game mostly to people who didn't play the original, as they're less likely to notice the small imperfections. You can tell that the dev's put a lot of work into making the levels look really bright and beautiful , and making the robots look really neat. Overall I still prefer the original, but that's because of a mix of nostalgia and preferred gameplay mechanics, but this game is good enough on it's own that I'll still be encouraging my friends to give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated adds lovely visuals to a classic 3D platformer that has aged better than I thought it would. Excellent controls, imaginative and compelling level design, and plenty of belly laughs make this game worth going back to nearly 20 years later.”8/10 – PC Invasion“A gorgeous remake of a cherished game adaptation. With tons of unlockables spread across levels with tons of variety, it doesn’t rely on its namesake alone to carry it. While SpongeBob fans will undoubtedly be happy to play through a game that retains the show’s sense of humor and colorful animation, its solid platforming and the freedom it provides players with to explore its diverse levels make it one of the better remakes we’ve seen.”4/5 – Game Revolution“The "rehydrated" version of Spongebob Squarepants: Battle for Bikini Bottom is an all-round entertainment product for a younger audience, who can take the opportunity to learn about the franchise, or on the other hand consolidate it with an original and fun adventure to play. Also confirmed by my teenage double, who enjoyed playing it from start to finish.”7.8/10 – The Games Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who had enjoyed this back in the days wouldn't have miss the current release. Even if you haven't played it before, it's a good game to relieve yourself from the never-ending AAA titles which hit you with moods and emotional stories.As usual, Plankton tried to rule Bikini Bottom with his own made robots, but instead effed up by not having them obeying his command and they've gone wild in many areas. Your main objective is to collect Golden Spatula to bypass Plankton's security system and bring a stop to the robot generator. That's it, no more.3D platforming action which consist of puzzle solving elements, you might find yourself travelling back and forth from cleared maps to obtain "golden spatula", which is required to progress to a new area. You play as Spongebob, Patrick and Sandy each having different abilities required to solve certain puzzles, but that's up to you to explore.The game was forgiving enough, each enemy you encountered can be defeated with one hit (with exception to 2 enemy). There wasn't much problem apart from audio issues, which can ruin your experience.  Multiplayer section were, uhh.... not so worthwhile. Do not buy this if you think this is a coop/ multiplayer focused game. All characters who had been remake looks extremely well, with the exception to Spongebob (he just seems weird). The environment color design are set to such a high saturation and vibrance which makes the older release looks obselete. But with the upgraded graphics your surrounding can look a bit too overwhelming from time to time. I felt uncomfortable when exploring Jellyfish Fields, but other areas were fine.Truth to be told, it looked like it could've used more time to polish and fix the bugs. Audio issues wasn't that much of an issue due to it only existing on cutscenes (audio delay), some sound effects were tid bit too loud. Also you can sometimes be stuck on certain levels because one of the key puzzle wont work. I haven't encountered major bugs but if you could, wait for future bug fixes before buying.8/10, enjoyed a goofy playing experience. Would recommend for anyone who want to take a break from major AAA release and just wanted to relax. But if you can't justify 30 dollars for ~10-15 hours of content, it's best to wait for a sale.Completion time: 15 hours (18 hours for 100% achievements)

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who never played the original game growing up, I went into this with 0 nostalgia, or expectations but I left the game with a smile on my face and a very memorable experience overall. It's clear that this game was made with love and passion, and is a love letter to classic Spongebob. I grew up watching the show and being able to explore Bikini Bottom and its many iconic locations in this game was an absolute joy. The platforming and boss battles were fun, and the game didn't overstay its welcome. If you're a fan of the show, this is a must play.  Spongebob and friends have probably never looked as good in a video game as they do in this game. 2D shows don't always translate super well into 3D character models, as we've seen before with Spongebob but they nailed him, and the other character models this time around. Not only are the character models well done, but with the exception of Mr. Krabs they all sound just like they do in the show as well, which was a nice surprise. Bikini Bottom itself has never looked better, with iconic locations such as Jellyfish Fields, and the Mermalair being incredible fun to explore and traverse. Every location looks and feels distinct from one another, with a super fun soundtrack to top it off. The game feels like you're just playing out an episode of the TV show, which is something not many licensed games can capture very well. Battle for Bikini Bottom is a fairly straightforward collectathon 3D platformer, with you travelling through different locations, completing tasks and collecting golden spatulas in order to progress. It's simple but it works. You will battle a variety of robots each one with different attacks, which keeps the game fun. You can play as Spongebob, Patrick, and Sandy, and each one has their own abilities, keeping the gameplay fresh. The boss battles are quite fun, with each one unique and a treat to play. There's a couple puzzles to keep the gameplay fresh, some of which are actually pleasantly challenging, and the sliding sections will never not be fun! In conclusion, Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated is a brilliant love letter to classic SpongeBob, with fun gameplay, beautiful locations to explore, and a collection of boss battles that are a joy to complete. If you're a fan of the show you will absolutely love this game, and it's worth picking up. For more reviews, follow my

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea why IGN gave this a 5/10. If I had to guess it would be because it has too much water. This game is so much better than what the game journalist sites would leave you to believe.This game does a wonderful job of reviving your favorite childhood video game. I was skeptical at first when I heard it was being remastered, but they really blew this one out of the water! This remake sticks to the source material with faith and did a wonderful job of bringing back your favorite characters. There are a few areas that feel a bit unpolished such as the Sandy boss fight and a couple of areas, but other than that it is a wonderful game. The multiplayer is lackluster and definitely feels as though it was rushed. There are times when I feel like there should be sounds playing but nothing is heard, and it is very easy to die by clipping through the floor. But it does show potential if the developers make it into something more. It simply leaves more to be desired.Everything else though is very nice and a ton of fun. _childDocuments_.review: BFBB - Rehydrated is everything I wanted out of the original game's remaster. Firstly, movement and attacks have been completely untouched in this remaster. It feels exactly as it did back in the early 2000s, and that's a very good thing in my opinion. It doesn't feel outdated by any means. The one thing that has changed drastically is the graphics. The game looks like a modern platformer while still retaining the charm of the older game.Playing as the three playable characters is a lot of fun. Spongebob as the obvious main protagonist has the most in his kit to defeat enemies, with his basic attack, ground pound, uppercut, bubble-bowl, and cruise missile. Patrick has a basic attack, as well as a stunning ground pound, which allows him to pick up enemies and throw them at others or buttons to activate certain things around the map. Sandy gets a basic attack and a lasso that can be used to destroy enemies in a single hit on most occasions, but she also gets to swing from special floating Texas icons around most maps and hover after using her double jump to cover more ground. There is enough variation in all three of their play styles to not get too bored of using any of these characters for too long.Enemies types vary significantly, changing up your strategy for defeating them slightly, but not making it an ordeal. I found myself dying more to being shoved off a ledge than actually running out of underwear (your life bar), which is somewhat annoying, but thankfully respawning takes no more than two seconds and checkpoints are plentiful enough to where you don't have to be scared of spawning too far away from where you last died. There are three main bosses to play against and to avoid spoilers, all of them are not very challenging, but are still quite entertaining to defeat. Also, Realistic Fish Head narrates every boss battle, which is a lot of fun to listen to during the battles.In terms of post game content, you really only have the option to go find the rest of the golden spatulas to 100% the game. My time in the post game has been fairly relaxed, as you now get to freely explore each stage you've visited before to find the missing spatulas, as well as Patrick's socks which can be redeemed for additional spatulas. I don't mind that there's not much to do after beating the final boss, but I can see why other people might have a problem with it.I want to make a point on the game's music because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ does it get it right. Every song fits the environment of the stage its set to. Almost every song is catchy and sets the tone perfectly. While it may loop over and over again in the background, I never found myself dying to turn the music off.Occasionally, I would stumble into small bugs regarding collision or getting stuck behind an invisible wall that I couldn't escape from, but the game besides these issues is incredibly polished and refined. Just be careful when you decide to explore every nook and cranny of the hub world, that's where it happened to me the most.I haven't tried the multiplayer modes because it doesn't particularly interest me, so I can't speak on the quality of that, but I don't think extra co-op content would hurt the quality of this game by any means.One complaint I do have towards this game as a remaster are that they should have included another playable character. Squidward shows up frequently throughout cutscenes and even in the ending cinematic, which only made me wonder why we never got to see him as a playable character for the campaign. All of this for only $30 is a remarkably fair deal. Please try this game if you haven't already, you probably won't regret it. Now just remaster Spongebob Squarepants The Movie The Game, and we'll be all good.

I'm glad one of my favorite childhood games of all time got a remake, and I hope the SpongeBob Squarepants Movie Game gets the same treatment from Purple Lamp Studios. I absolutely recommend buying this.Score: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I've never played the original, so I have no nostalgia for this game.You basically get what you expect, a remaster that improves visuals and animations, but gameplay has early 2000s design flaws. It's no Mario Odyssey, but it's a good, relaxing collect-a-thon.Pretty much all of the iconic Spongebob places are in this, like the Goo Lagoon, Jellyfish fields or the Mermalair, also,  the characters personalities are as close to the TV show as possible, sadly the humor misses the mark.To the gameplay:It's quite slow, none of the characters are truly fast and it can sometimes feel tiring to go from A to B. The game usually makes it blatantly obvious what you have to do, so puzzles are rarely a challenge. Combat isn't this games strength either, the few bosses are quite easy, additionally there's a clear lack of freedom, you barely are able to cheese anything and if you have an idea the game just puts an invisible wall infront of you or you get resetted.The resets are a different story, most of the time you end up getting resetted because you touched the wrong grain of sand or the game doesn't make it clear if an object is in the reset zone, that makes exploring somewhat annoying, although it's a good feature to have to not punish you with an instant death.Patrick is basically Spongebob's ripoff, you can carry things, other than that there's no reason to play as him.Collecting socks in Bikini Bottom is annoying, you gotta hit random objects to get em.Lastly, I feel like the game really lost its polish in the last world. Mermalair and Rock Bottom were great levels, but World 3's Kelp Forest is basically "carry something from A to B" and the Dutchman Shipwreck is missed potential mixed with clipping through various objects.Don't get me wrong, it's a 7/10 game, it's relaxing, Spongebob has good abilities, there's a good variety of enemies, collecting feels rewarding, most of the worlds are greatly designed with many references and the new graphics look wonderful, it's one of the rare good licensed games, but some problems really give it away that this game is from 2003.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello fellow quasi-boomers! I also happen to fall within the widening demographic of post-9/11 kids who grew up on jello-square looking rectangle-machines and a swath of licensed games that run the gamut from okay to god-awful! According to THQ Nordic’s release trailer, we’re old enough to have kids that have developed spatial-reasoning skills.  As someone who is part of this increasingly troubled demographic, I like to think I’m fairly immune to giving things a pass just because I grew up with them, like frosted tips and the Patriot Act. With that said, Battle for Bikini Bottom: Rehydrated takes an above-average licensed game and perhaps gives it the graphical polish it doesn’t necessarily deserve – not that I’m complaining, having played it multiple times as a bored young-un. It’s definitely great to see the ACTUAL game on PC as opposed to . Seeing as this is a 1:1 remake of the original Battle for Bikini Bottom, this review skewers more in the direction of a review of the actual game, but I’ll be sure to mention anything that THQ may have added or changed.The number-one thing that BFBB has had going for it is its religious devotion to the show. Plenty of licensed games at the time played lip-service to the show’s basic premise and setting but felt paint-by-numbers otherwise. It really goes to show how rich the first three seasons of Spongebob really were – they had enough memorable characters locations and that BFBB feels like it’s trying desperately to cram the entirety of Bikini Bottom into a 1-year development cycle.  Add (most) of the vocal talent from the show and writing that’s 50% chuckle-worthy, 30% meh, and 20% hot gas, and you have a pretty darn faithful game to a show worth being faithful to.BFBBR not only has the blessing of being made by fans back in Spongebob’s glorious heyday, but clearly given another passion-pass by a newer, sleeker, sexier generation of Spongebob fans. While Rehydrated doesn’t add any new locations, it’s shocking how nearly 20 years of graphical and artistic development can turn what originally was “passing for Spongebob” to genuinely great looking. Jellyfish Fields are now rolling; Rock Bottom now has a neon-glitz; Spongebob’s Dream has an extra haze. Beyond the locations, characters look and animated much better (no doubt partially a result of Nickelodeon nailing the “3D Spongebob” look down for Sponge Out Of Water). On top of all of this, Rehydrated adds very contemporary, erm, “references” to the show in surprising places – try not moving for a little and see what happens!And here comes the most critical part of the review – the gameplay. Remember those licensed-platformers that took Mario 64’s basic collect-a-thon formula and didn’t do much to it? BFBB is definitely in that league. The core of collecting coins (somewhat meta-named Shiny Things) and power stars (Golden Spatulas), combined that with Spongebob, Patrick, and Sandy’s unique abilities is a decent gameplay loop that doesn’t stray too far from tradition. Level design can occasionally get pretty frustrating and tedious at times, especially when your objective isn’t clear - I know it’s fun to hate on professional reviewers, but there’s absolutely something to be said against level design that feels obfuscated and time-wasting. The ability to outright skip levels if you have enough Golden Spatulas is a pretty neat feature, if not a little self-defeating. Overall, I appreciate that THQ religiously adhering to the source game for Rehydrated, especially in a wholly different engine, but flaws from back in the day are in full display here.A highlight of Battle for Bikini Bottom is its musical selection, which in some places is genuinely great. Jimmy Levine starts with the familiar steel guitar in Jellyfish Fields and from there goes to mid-90 techno, Metal Gear Solid sneaking music, and 60’s surfer rock, amongst other genres. It was a genuine delight hearing them again and is a fantastic example of how diverting from source material in just the right way can elevate a work that much more.If you’re a Spongebob fan, Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehyrdated is a must-play, full-stop. It’s a grand tour of all the best Spongebob can offer within a platformer, sprinkled with references both new and old. If you’re looking for a platformer regardless, you could do worse. it’s definitely not up there with the greats in that respect, but it’s definitely a nice, light experience in an era with so many complicated games out there. If you’re a nostalgic over one of the weirdest decades to be nostalgic over, you’ve probably already bought it. “It’s good for your soul!”“Please. I have no soul.”

_childDocuments_.review: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom is a great, and admittedly flawed platformer. I played this game a lot as a young child, and have fond memories of it being one of the only licensed games that I played that was actually any good. It was always just a little rough around the edges, and not quite as polished and perfect as other collect-a-thons like Mario 64 and Banjo-Kazooie. But it was still a lot of fun, and felt a lot like the first few seasons of the TV show that were absolutely flawless. So when I heard they actually had a remake coming out, I was ecstatic. A chance to be a kid again, to remind myself of simpler times. The aptly titled "Rehydrated" version of this game does plethora to breathe new life into the dustier parts of the old game, while also missing a few spots. I went and completed the game 100% and also tried out the new content that was added to the game for a more well rounded and review. I was able to complete it within 16 hours, but I don't know the exact time as I left the game on for a few hours while I took a nap.First, the good. This game is still really fun! The way that the game plays, feels genuinely great. This is one of the greatest improvements in my mind from the original. All of the moves have been revamped to be slightly quicker, and much more responsive than what was on display in the original title. The game also looks brilliant, with good color usage and the same vibe as the old game, without changing the art style to the point of unrecognition. The same soundtrack comes back, and is also pleasant, with a couple of really standout tracks that are memorable and faithful to the show. No real changes there from BFBB. Lastly, the characters and dialogue are superb. As previously stated, you really do get the feeling that there was a lot of care taken by the writers and voice actors to make the characters feel like they are from the first few seasons of the show. Lots of in-jokes and references, lots of really genuinely funny lines and inflection. Not every single line is pure gold (more on that later), but for being a kids game, there really is a lot of laughs to be had here.Now for the not so good. I only have a couple of critiques here but they are important. The first of which, is the general jank that surrounds this game. It has to be said that the old game was jank in the same ways, and this game has improved upon that. But there is still a lot of moments whether it be in the combat or in the platforming that will leave you wondering "Well, why did that happen?". It is by no means unbearable, and it is less than before, but I wish it was just a little bit more polished for all the people playing this game for the first time. Second, is an issue that has transferred from the old game, because they kept all the exact same voice lines from it. The voice actor who plays the characters Mr. Krabs and Mermaid Man, sounds nothing like either one of those characters. All of the rest of the cast is actually reprised by their original voice actors, but for some reason those 2 characters were left out of the loop back in the day, and have been dredged back up with the re-release. Next, is the overall length of the game. I have played it many times and I always find myself wishing there was just a little bit more to chew on. Its not short, but just not quite as long as I'd like. Finally, there was talk about this game restoring cut content and making use of original concept art to create new elements of the game. What this really means is that there is now a very bland, boring, and repetitive multiplayer "horde mode" that you and a friend can play. The arenas they created all look fine but the actual gameplay is reminiscent of games like Dead Ops Arcade except there are no powerups, and if you pick a character that uses melee weapons, you are at an objective disadvantage over your friends who picked characters with ranged weapons (the difference of which you can't tell from the start menu). This is easily the weakest part of the game and honestly, I wish it wasn't there if it was going to be so mediocre. Just sours the rest of the experience slightly.Overall, this game is a quality title! It definitely has some rougher spots, but it is still very much a gem and worth playing if you have never played the original release. If you did play BFBB, this is going to be much of the same but definitely a fresh coat of paint along with some general handling improvements. Just don't bother with the multiplayer mode unless you and your friend just want to give it a shot. TL;DR  This game is good fun, would recommend to fans of SpongeBob or to fans of collect-a-thons. Don't bother playing multiplayer mode.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom is a fun but flawed experience, it's simple to play but has some frustration when going for 100% and the remake introduced a few bugs which can hamper the experience.Pros - fantastic reimagining of a cult classic, fantastically presented without losing anything that made the orginal special.- smooth and fluid controls which makes controlling the chracters a dream.- plenty of content to keep you busy with varied locations and activities - lover letter to fans especially the original 3 seasons - mostly all voice actors are back with great performances Cons - fairly frustrating game, of course this isn't dark souls and you have unlimited lives but some parts can be a bit testy and certain tasks for 100% aren't that fun- music is good but loops pretty quickly so it can be quite frustrating - some voice actors couldn't return the worst offender being Mr Krabs, it's bad. - all the added content for this game isn't that good, it plays with the idea of cut content but it isn't implemented in a meaningful way, basically just some mp horde mode, we do get robo-squidward but not in the way we wanted. Conclusion  All in all a pretty fun game, little janky in spots and some wonky difficulty especially for a kids game but as a jaded, miserable fat old man I still had fun with the spongebob game.

_childDocuments_.review: Man this game brought back a lot of nostalgia for me. Now whether the game is the best way to play the original game, that's up in the air. But this a bad game? Not at all.
