_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: As a game, it's great! I can definitely recommend it if you haven't played the original before, and like old-school collectathons. The graphical overhaul alone makes this one of the best looking 3D platformers I've ever played, and that's coming from someone who LIKES the visuals of old GameCube/PS2/Xbox Games. In addition, there are some quality of life improvements added (i.e. Patrick can attack in midair, Sandy's attacks are faster), but strangely, some were taken out as well, like cheat codes for example. As a remake of the original game, however, I'm a tad disappointed. It's obvious that this game was rushed so its release would coincide with the new upcoming SpongeBob film, but that eventually got delayed, so I don't understand why that wasn't the case for the game as well. I can see that Purple Lamp put as much love and care into this remake as they could, and hopefully the issues present will get fixed later down the line. One thing that no one seems to talk about, though, is the multiplayer mode. Straight up, it's horrible. It feels like it wasn't even playtested. You're best off playing it local, because you're never gonna find anyone online. Another thing that just baffles me is some of the blatant lies in the promotional material. Purple Lamp claimed to be bringing back cut content that wasn't in the original game, specifically the scrapped Robo-Squidward boss, the original version of Patrick's Dream, and the unused additional phase of the final boss fight. You know where all that went? The multiplayer mode! Robo-Squidward shows up and just... sits there while other robots attack you, and you don't even get to fight him! Patrick's Dream and the extra form of SpongeBot? Nothing more than set pieces for you to fight robots on top of! It's a shame too, I'm a huge SpongeBob fan, I loved the original, and these selling points were the main reason why I was looking forward to Rehydrated. I would also complain about Mermaidman and Mr. Krabs still not having their original voice actors, but Ernest Borgnine sadly isn't with us anymore, and to be honest, they never bothered me as much as they did with some people. Hopefully they'll redo all of Krabs' lines with Clancy Brown in an update later down the line. Finally, I have to mention the glitches. Oh boy, the glitches. After my first play session, where I got about 1/3 into the game, my save file got corrupted, and I had to start over. Not a huge issue, but I can say this review would be a lot more negative if it happened after I 100% completed the game. Also, you can't rematch bosses in this remake. Instead, it just drops you into their arena and leaves you to walk around aimlessly. I've heard this is being looked into, so I hope it gets fixed at some point. Since you can't rematch bosses, you can't see the ending cutscene more than once. This means, If you're a completionist like me, you have to get every collectible in the game before you challenge the final boss, or no secret ending for you! The developers also said they'd make the Spongeball arena replayable, which is weird because it was already replayable in the original version after beating the game. In Rehydrated, once you leave it the first time, it never lets you back in. Again, this will probably get patched at some point. OK, for all my complaining, I still overall must recommend this game if you don't have a way to play the original, since the gameplay is almost exactly the same, and if you don't find the humor of SpongeBob seasons 1-3 entertaining(which this game perfectly replicates), there's something seriously wrong with you. If you have played the original, it's up to you if you want to replay the game in a prettier engine. Also, IGN and Gamespot have no idea what they're talking about. "Why does it take more than one game journalist to change a lightbulb? BECAUSE THEY'RE SO DARN STUPID!"

_childDocuments_.review: Battle for Bikini Bottom was a game that I saw videos and images of, but never actually played myself. When the remaster was announced, I was curious. I wasn't entirely sure what to expect, and was somewhat surprised when I found myself really liking it. By the time I finished it, I could safely say that it was one of the best games I've played this year. + The game retains the same wit and charm that the TV show is well known for, and is a brilliant video game representation of the world of SpongeBob. It's also good to see most of the original voice actors reprise their roles. Shame about no Clancy Brown though.+ The levels all feel distinct from one another. Each location is iconic both in its visual design and its level structure. There was never a moment where I felt the levels were lacking. If anything, I'd say the levels are my favourite aspect of this game.+ Although not that different from the original, the game is really satisfying to play. Most of the mechanics are smooth, and the combat is quite entertaining.+ Each level introduces either a new mechanic or a new enemy. Because of this, the game always feels refreshing.  + The game is rather easy to play, but there are moments that can genuinely be challenging and force you to approach the situation from a different angle, something that I wasn't expecting and was pleased to see.+ The updated visuals make the environments and the character models shine. The bright colours give everything more life, and as a whole, make the levels much more memorable.+ Being able to play as Patrick and Sandy as well as SpongeBob varies up the gameplay a bit, removing the risk of repetitiveness. They're both also very fun to play as. + The story itself is quite decent. Yes, it's childish, but it's exactly what you would expect from SpongeBob. It's an amusing, silly and memorable experience. - A couple of mechanics such as Patrick's throw and SpongeBob’s Cruise Bubble feel a bit off. Patrick's throw is annoying to aim, and the Cruise Bubble can be awkward to control in enclosed environments.- Although a minor problem, sometimes the camera would feel a bit janky. It’s more noticeable when switching characters. Most of the time the camera is fine, but there is the odd instance where it got in the way.Battle for Bikini Bottom took me by surprise. I wasn’t expecting to have so much fun playing a SpongeBob game that was obviously aimed at kids, but regardless, I did. As somebody who used to watch this show as a child, it took me back. The same childish humour is there, and despite a couple of different voice actors, the characters stay true to their cartoon counterparts. However, it’s the level design, the gorgeous visuals and the (mostly) smooth game mechanics that really make this game shine for me. The game never became repetitive and it never lost its charm. It found ways to keep itself feeling different and interesting.Yes a few of the controls and the mechanics feel a bit off, and that is a shame. I haven’t tried the multiplayer, and according to some reviews, it’s not great. Nevertheless, I don’t think these issues dumb the game down that much. If you were a fan of the original Battle for Bikini Bottom, a fan of the show, or just want a fun platformer, then I highly recommend this. It’s one of the best games I have played this year.9.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom emerged as a cult classic of the mid-aughts for putting the trademark writing and tone of the never-ending animated series into a fairly solid collectathon platformer. The movement is still a bit on the slow side, and some tricks from the original game have been removed, but this remake largely keeps the core experience intact and with some welcome quality of life improvements. Don't expect anything ground-breaking, but this bit of millennial nostalgia still holds up quite well.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were to tell me we would get a remake of a 17 year old licensed 3D collectathon platformer I wouldn't believe you but here we are in 2020 with a summer release of BfBB.Before I start this review I want to thank the small but   of speedrunners for saving this underrated gem from obscurity. I would also like to mention  &  (I'm being gracious just sharing a clip of Gamespot's review) garbage reviews since they both did poor reviews of the game & just reinforces why short videos don't do a good job explaining anything at all.To begin this review after replaying the original BfBB (been a long time since I booted it up) for a tiny bit & completing everything in the remake there are a lot of flaws & improvements that the original didn't have which I'll list.1) Delays with most of spongebob's attacks except for the bubble helmet (upward attack) & the missile + an odd sound mute when you fully charge the bubble bowl. (I miss the bubble trail)2) Delays with Patrick's throw, the auto-aim being a pain while carrying around throwable items & the fruit staying black while your carrying it. Only praise I can give the fruit is that it now moves around compared to the original. I also noticed delay with Sandy's lasso while swinging, delays with her lasso glide & her double jump animation not coming out after letting go of a Texas hook.3) For players that don't use WASD you're screwed since there isn't any rebindable keys unless you're fine with a controller & an extreme lack of graphics options (Lots of FPS problems too) since the entire time playing I had to turn down the gamma since it gets too bright especially while doing slide challenges.4) Personally disappointed that the cut content that never made it in the original ended up being multiplayer only since I was curious what the new boss battle & revamped Patrick's Dream level would've been like.5) The worst redesigns I've seen in my opinion are the Thunder Tikis, Tar-Tar (sad that his tar doesn't slowly melt away), Monsoon (his attacks are too slow compared to original), Robot Sandy being too small + weird hit detection with her 3rd phase (love the added fire effect on her tail), minor nitpick on Bubble buddy being too bright + Larry being too small, Arf being too small & Sleepytime (weird bug where he sometimes doesn't die) being too small. The only good redesigns are Ham-mer (don't like his new hit radius when he slams), Chuck, G-love, Slick, Tubelet & the effort that the devs went to adding new facial animations + gags for the conversations.The other robot enemies haven't changed too much except for Chomp's bite being way too slow now & also barely seeing the green breath unless you turn down the gamma. More minor nitpicks I have are with how small Spongebob's arms & legs are when he's jumping, The teleport box being too small + no animation & the new location for the golden underwear at the police station.6) The camera sometimes softlocks unless you hold down right click & new auto-reverses like the wall jump in the Chum bucket for example.7) Clancy Brown not returning to voice Mr. Krabs.I never did understand why his voice was never in the original but I personally think it had something to do with the Revenge of the Flying Dutchman game being terrible or it was a union thing being in the way.8) Sliding isn't as smooth as the original is but very small praise goes to adding a slow down when pressing backwards & Spongeeing (Bungee) is really janky too where it makes the Sea Needle in Downtown Bikini Bottom a pain to progress through as an example.9) The new theater reward is garbage compared to the original so don't bother grinding 40k shiny objects.Graphically this remake is capturing current season Spongebob with the happier, bright animations compared to the early seasons (the era I grew up with & left after the Spongebob movie) & I have to commend the dev team on a job well done especially with improving levels like Spongebob's Dream as an example since it has more eye candy or making the Mermalair being less of a pain with its puzzles (sometimes the Rube Goldberg puzzle completely glitches the ball) so I like some of the redesigned levels (still would look better with more graphics options to offer). Musically they did a good job not screwing up anything from the original at all & letting players buy it for the very first time & the only Golden Spatula requirements that haven't aged well for me are Mermaid Man's slide challenge & grinding shiny objects for Mr. Krabs.If you don't mind the bugs/glitches (devs are doing a top notch job addressing problems), never played the game or are just returning to it for nostalgia purposes then I can proudly say that Rehydrated is worth full price to buy. I'm personally still cautious of companies owned by THQ Nordic especially with the infamous 1 year EGS exclusivity of Metro Exodus from Deep Silver but I'm happy to return to the closest licensed game that could compete with popular 3D platformers like Super Mario 64 & Banjo-Kazooie.If the team at Purple Lamp or THQ Nordic are reading this please bring back the Spongebob Movie game (impossible because of licensing but I want to believe there's a chance), Scooby Doo Night of 100 Frights (another great licensed game from Heavy Iron) & Spongebob Lights, Camera, Pants. I can't wait to see what other classic Nick games are coming back to PC & console since I do miss the Tak trilogy (another underrated gem) personally & feel like the game trilogy has been completely forgotten. For upcoming speedrunners I want to share one of the best runs I've ever watched on the original BfBB & would personally recommend waiting till all the bugs/glitches are cleaned up before speedrunning the remake. For a bonus here's a past developer Q&A featuring the speedrunner that did that great documentary on BfBB. EDIT: I nominated this game for the 2020 Steam Awards in the Labor Of Love category.

_childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of potential with this game. I mean a lot of it. As it stands, I do not think it is as good as the original. However, I am not considering that the fault of Purple Lamp. This game was on a rushed development cycle and just didn't have the time to polish it fully. There are so many little issues with this original version that it does take away from some of the experience. Many of the boss animations just seem very unfinished and there are some glitches in this game that really hinder my experience. It is annoying to have to switch my camera back to horizontal invert, my preferred control method, every time I switch characters. I have faith that Purple Lamp will work many of these bugs out. They have shown that they care about the game. It is just very unfinished. The only major gripe I have outside of the unpolished and glitchy things is that the cruise bubble does not control in a way my brain can understand. I have never been able to control flying mechanics non-inverted. It really does not make sense to me, so one suggestion I have for future updates is to add an option to invert the cruise bubble controls more to make them feel more similar to the original game, which is the way I am used to controlling all flying machines in games. Overall. I think this game is worth picking up if you want to experience the game on PC without emulation or on any other platform. I especially like that it is DRM free, which explains my low play time as of writing this as I did play this game most of the way through bypassing Steam. Just as it stands, it could use some work.

_childDocuments_.review: Before i start this review i should say that i have played the original the game so there may be some nostalgia talking.Pros--The game is just as fun as you remember-The game looks great-90% of the original voice team is acting their roles (exceptions are Mr.Crabs and Mermaid Man)-LOTS of references to the early seasons of the show-No game breaking bugs at launch-The low amount of spatulas required to beat the game makes this great for your kids to play and beat.Cons--Small audio bugs (the bubble bowl audio stopping half way in the animation)-Some small details missed from original (the checkers board missing in the retirement home and Squidward shouting "Hey" when drawing a mustache on his painting)-The Shiny Object requirements for Mr Crabs spatulas has been increased dramatically, so you now have to farm for them even after 100% the rest of the game-To difficult for the average games journalistAt the time of review i have 100% the game and loved every bit of it, this is a wonderful fun recreation of a classic game. The movement has been changed from the originals, in Rehydrated jumping feels alot more floaty which i imagine was done to make the game more accessible for kids, this isn't really a bad thing as this game isn't exactly hardcore and if made to be fun. Also they changed the images in the theater from concept art to in game stills, not really a downside just something i wanted to point out.Not all changes are bad however the additional idle animations are wonderful, the extra art spread throughout the game is a fantastic nostalgia trip for not just the game but the early show as well.In summary this game is a fantastic buy for any fan of the show young or old, or anyone that loves early 2000s platformers. The games not perfect, but all of the issues i have with it could easily be patched out with future updates.Thank you for reading my reviewThank you Purple Lamp Studios and THQ Nordic for your amazing work recreating a part of my childhoodVICTORY SCREECH LOLOLOLOLOLOL

_childDocuments_.review: Spongebob Battle for Bikini Bottom- RehydratedScore: 7/10The good:BOBB is a faithful remake of one of the best licensed XBOX 360/PS2 games of the 2000's. The textures and details look simply beautiful, and is done in such a way that nothing looks jarring being in HD. The levels are exactly how you remember them, but you're experiencing them in a brand new way with new detail and a smooth framerate. Load times are significantly reduced from the first game (thank goodness). Game is easy to understand, Spatulas are pretty easy to get. If you enjoyed this game as a kid, or just like Spongebob in general, you'll definitely love this game.The Bad:Music in the levels get repetitive very quickly. Each new area has a new song that goes with it, but that song has a short loop that repeats forever and only ever changes if you're in a boss fight or a challenge. This game also uses the original audio from the first game that was remastered and put in the remake, so you still get knock-off Mr. Krabs and Mermaid Man100% the game, while not hard, becomes very tedious at the end. In order to complete the game, you must purchase Golden Spatulas from Mr Krabs. In the original game, you needed 39,500 in total to get these. In Rehydrated, you need to get 108,000 Shiny Objects. You'll definitely need to do some grinding to get both this and the 40,000 to get the Cinema, which can become tedious to do when you just want to finish the game.You can only get the 100% reward if you collect everything before the main boss fight. If you do the boss and then collect everything, you can't fight the boss again. So you never get the 100% cutscene. Game Engine can also be prone to some strange bugs as well, particularly on character models. Conclusion:This game is definitely great for relaxing or killing some time! Anyone who loved Spongebob as a kid will absolutely adore this game, its story, and its humor. Aside from some nitpicks and some things that come off as tedious, this game is super fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewing as a 25 yo playing this game for the first time. It was an awesome time. The visuals are pretty crisp, the gameplay is pretty good, the voice acting. The enemies could be sneaky tough and you do need to time your attack right. The best part of this game is that while it’s a pretty good 3D platforming collectathon, it’s also really good at reminding you just how awesome SpongeBob was, and why everyone in college can quote it by heart.This is a remaster, people say that the original game has better feeling controls, but these controls are still good. If you like Spyro, Donkey Kong 64, Epic Mickey and the like, you’ll probably like this.Also, definitely check out the speedrunning community on YouTube for this game. You might be shocked but the original BFBB is a very well known speedrun and the way they were able to break the game is fascinating. The developers of the remaster even reached out for input for this game. Some things ared disappointing, apparently there is a lot of cut content including a whole section and a part of a boss fight. I won’t say I miss it cause I haven’t played it but this is a pretty short game to 100% so more content would’ve been cool, even as a dlc. I also think it’s disappointing that they didn’t include a co-op mode for the story but that would’ve taken a lot more work to accomplish since some parts of the rvells are built only for 1 characters special abilities, so it wouldn’t be easy to do and still be faithful to the original. NbdAll in all, I’d play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Couple things you should know about this game, but before i say any of that I will say that this is a *good* game, no matter how you decide to play it, through emulation or through Rehydrated, or even on your old consoles, this game is seriously great. Spongebob theming aside, this is an excellent 3D platformer with Super Mario-esque worlds and gameplay objectives. Play it.This port though? Hit or miss on almost every aspect. I'll touch on a couple reasons why this falls through in the long run. One big thing? You wanna know the reason why you don't slap unreal engine/default unity grass into every 3D platformer to make it look "good"? Because you need to be able to see your own shadow for precise jumping and positioning. Im not saying this game is kaizo, but you should be able to see your shadow when jumping on some of these platforms. Not every level has this obnoxious grass everywhere, in fact only a couple do, but even in the upper levels of Jellyfish fields? You need to be able to make some of those jumps. They try to use some weird backface culling to put the shadow on top of whatever shading layer they used for the grass but it just doesnt work. Speaking of backface culling, could you guys just not get the normals right on those underpants models? Really? Lmao.Controls are pretty tight, but they should be. Spongebob should control like butter if you're gonna slap him in a 3D platformer like BFBB. But they made him *slow*. Like, really slow. I don't mean movement speed, I'm pretty sure that's true to the original, but his animation speed, some of the ways he reacts to the environment, they all play out like they're in molasses. It really contrasts to the original, where most things were tight and snappy. Also, hit collision, what? Why is it that sometimes when you swing once, you'll hit things for two to three times with no additional input? Why is it that sometimes your character's hitbox will remain on the ground while you're in the air? Bugs? Not too sure. Watch yourselves.Sound is pretty.. Well, they didn't change *too* much. I guess in 15 years we couldn't figure out how to loop a song any better, though. I mean, I like all the music, but hearing it fade in and out while it loops every time is annoying. I'm pretty sure the original suffered from this too, but again, it's been more than a decade. A lot of the voice clips remain the same, with some really bad impersonators or voice actors way too out of their touch filling in for some new lines, which are.. just awful. just terrible. the "new" ""writing"" is horrible. some of the voice actors you could find better on fiverr.since that covers most of the game's issues or differences from the originals im gonna write a paragraph to nitpick too. no graphics settings? i mean that's fine but make sure your game runs well universally, which it doesn't. I'm lucky in that my rig can support 144 throughout the entire game at 1080/2k just fine but even with my specs the game can chug at 4k and I know some friends who had issues at 1080p. the performance is pretty good actually, not a whole lot of stuttering or frame pacing like you'll get from a lot of ports and remasters. solid performance, but that's just to be expected. a couple other small things worth mentioning is the menus are all super boring now. go look at the old game's UI and compare it to this one, just lacks so much soul. in the original, hearing the "shiny objects" collection noise was so nice and they would change the pitch to scale it with the amount you'd collect, now it's super jarring just to collect one or two here or there with no real variation. these small things are the components that made the original game so much more than this remaster, and i'm really sad they never capitalized on these details, it shows that the prerogative now is just that much more different than the philosophies this game was created on.also a fish dabs.7.5/10 def recommend the original but play this too

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I highly recommend this game, it does have many bugs that simply can't be ignored. I'm not sure if it was just me but using a controller made the game continuously skip dialogue by acting as if I pressed X twice. It also had the strange effect of letting me fast travel to places where I didn't receive a task, so at the very start of the game I could go into the Chum Bucket lab, which was just strange. Eventually just decided to use a keyboard and mouse which wasn't that bad, only using WASD for movement and E, Q and right click for the bubble attacks. There's also the fact that with the controller the game sometimes crashes upon manual saving. Finally, achievements are bugged; my brother and I have two separate saves and the game combines the total number of spatulas and socks we got, so we have the 100% completion achievement despite it not being on a single save.All in all, the game is great; just as I remember it, but using a controller can just be hell and achievements really need to be fixed, though those are the only two bad points I can say about the game and it's not really due to the gameplay itself

_childDocuments_.review: Spongebob Battle of Bikini Bottom Rehydrated was one of my anticipated games of 2020. I’m really glad it got remastered, since I had never got to play it as a kid and absolutely loved watching SpongeBob. I had played the game Alantis SquarePantis on my DS when I was young and loved it. This game was very enjoyable for me personally as an early 2000’s kid. The way games were made in early 2000’s had a whole different kind of vibe. There is something so relaxing about listening to SpongeBob jams while wandering around in Bikini Bottom for Patrick’s dirty socks and golden spatulas. Each world has unique soundtracks that really are enjoyable to listen to. The game has been brightened up with a higher contrast quite much which some find to be too much, but I like it this way. Some of my favorite worlds were Kelp Forest and Rock Bottom. It’s fun bumping into characters from the show like Squidward and Garry, not to mention the “fake” Mr. Krabs and his horrendous voice I’m wishing I could forget. You bounce around in a taxi visiting different spots from the show.Some issues I have with the game is it feels like it was rushed because of the amount of camera issues I had. There were a few more bugs I had here in there which didn’t overall hinder the gameplay enough, but were present. This game is pretty much a reskin of the original so don’t expect anything new from it if you’ve played it before.In conclusion I really enjoyed this game a lot. I think anyone who grew up playing or watching SpongeBob will love this. There is a charm these types of simple games hold and I will always cherish it.

_childDocuments_.review: I played BFBB day in and day out as a small child, then went back to 100% it on an emulator as a teenager, and let me just say I'm very, very pleased by this remaster.First things first: this game is absolutely GORGEOUS on the eyes! Iridescent bubbles, translucent goo, suspended particles drifting in the undersea current... and a whole rainbow of vibrant tropical colors to truly breathe new life into every level. The level design is identical to the original; even the moving/sinking/tilting platforms have the same timing and animations.The camera is surprisingly intuitive. A slight auto-correction occurs to guide the camera behind you as you run, but it's just subtle enough to be actually convenient instead of a nuisance... unlike the camera in the original BFBB, which I had to actively wrestle against.Controls are responsive and the characters look bouncy to match. The platforming requires the same pinpoint-accurate jumping and landing as the original BFBB, but there's little surprises to be had if you know what you need to do. Spongebob especially handles well and feels absolutely delightful to platform with. If anything, using a mouse & WASD makes this leagues easier than the classic GameCube joysticks.A new QOL change I like: for challenges involving the Throw Fruit or Sandy's lasso, targets will be auto-selected with little white chalk circles, and pressing the given button will then guarantee a hit. Patrick won't miss a targeted button or Duplicat-o-tron with the Throw Fruit, and Sandy can grab the next Texas Hook in a series without needing to let go of her current one. It takes a lot of the guesswork out of it.To those who are looking for more streamlined challenges than the original's puzzles, such as the infamous rolling ball room: look elsewhere! This game still provides the same challenges and demands the same platforming precision as the original. However, I will say this: the robots are definitely easier to get the jump on, which is great for tight spaces. The pesky hammer robots, in particular, no longer wind up their weapons before you're even able to hit them. Projectile-based enemies such as the tartar sauce robots will also put bullseyes on the ground to signal where their attacks will land. The game and its challenges feel fair and achievable. In ~4 hours I was able to get every spatula from Jellyfish Fields up through the Mermalair, including the rolling ball!Every bit of sound-design is completely intact, up to and including that satisfying ring from a purple Shiny Object. The main menu, however, has been reworked: instead of a scrolling menu-type level selection, the levels are now shown all at once on a map, and from there, you may view your collectibles at a glance or taxi to individual spatulas just as you could with the original's menu. The exact buttons for the controls are not customizable, but I have no gripes with their choice of controls. Everything's either on the mouse or in easy reach of WASD.The only downside: occasionally, the controls do bug out! Sometimes, clicking the mouse for an attack doesn't register, and you may have to click again before the attack actually goes through. Early levels also saw two non-consecutive instances of a bug where the camera got "stuck" in a 180-degree field, but got fixed upon respawn. However, these aren't gamebreaking, as my aforementioned gameplay pace ought to show. For all the hubbub about BFBB being so merciless, this game is definitely forgiving enough to allow even several missed attacks in a row.TL;DR:- Looks beautiful with great animations.- Near-identical gameplay to original BFBB.- QOL changes are minute; game still requires skilled, precise platforming.- Biggest downside is occasional bug: missed attack or stuck camera, nothing else.- Solid 9/10 remaster.As a longstanging diehard proponent of the original BFBB, this is truly a "rehydration" and has my full endorsement!

_childDocuments_.review: An instant classic from my childhood remade. Speaking as a man who has owned the original on every console it came out on, this remake does a bunch of cool things right, and a bit not so great.First up, the negatives. Everything feels a lot slower now in terms of movement. You can charge up the Bubble Bowl so long that the sound effect just stops playing while you charge because the original clip isn't long enough, and the Cruise Bubble feels so much slower, both because it is and because they don't crank up the FOV when you use it, as was done in the original. Turning is a lot stiffer than in the original and one of the fun exploits was removed that made you faster. Turning isn't just stiff in mid-air, either, as the camera is also very stiff, and if you turn the camera while on a slide, your player turns with it. They also removed one of the most fun aspects of the game, which is the ability to freely control Sandy's swinging. In the original, you just had to press B or Circle or X (depending on console) and you had the ability to transfer the momentum of a jump into your swing, or just swing around in a circle to build up speed before yeeting yourself out of it. In Rehydrated, you have to hold the button instead, and the entire swing is a preset animation that you can only affect the release direction of, which is rather disappointing. On the more nit-picky side, Squidward doesn't shout "Hey!" after you give his portrait a moustache, Spongebob's foghorn alarm no longer triggers when you smack it, and Patrick's rock no longer has a Gramophone you can smack to play music. But that's really it for the negatives.On the positive side, they allowed patrick to attack mid-air, and made it so that he gets a slight speed boost every attack. They also allowed spongebob to use the Bubble Bash after jumping once, and allowed Sandy to use her rope attack mid-air, granting her a jump if you do so. This leads to interesting movement in its own right. So needless to say, this game sets itself apart from the predecessor. On top of the changes to movement and gameplay, many changes were done in the interest of fixing some of the problems the original had.  One such problem is the dialogue cutting out in boss fights, which now properly play at the defeat of a boss, as opposed to the original's cutting out at the cutscene trigger. On top of this, many more dialogue emotions were rendered so the characters can express a bit more during dialogue. In terms of visuals, the remake is bright and saturated, exactly what you'd expect in a children's game, which is wonderful for all the new kids coming to enjoy a beloved classic that will be remembered for even more years to come. Alot of new idle animations were made that reference Spongebob memes, so take that as you will.The new multiplayer mode is wonderful, as back when I was a kid my brother and I would play this game together, and hand each other the controller whenever we swapped characters at a bus stop, so being able to play with him at the same time is pretty cool, and I hope many future siblings will come to appreciate this game in the same way that we did when we were little, even if it is just a glorified arena mode, it still would have been amazing to have back then, which is why I'm glad that it's a part of the game.All in all, this remake sets itself apart from the original in terms of movement while making the combat more accessible. Pick it up for the nostalgia, or pick it up for future nostalgia. Either way, you're going to love this masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: So i've played through jellyfish fields and the city level and have decided to write a review about how i feel about the game so far.Pros>It completely recaptures the overall feel of the original ( i played it on gamecube).>It runs really well on my computer>It's very easy to get into and navigate through the levels.>The platforming sections are the same as the original.>I love the idle animations for the characters>I love how they added in newer spongebob memes into the game( Like handsome squidward).>Alot of the old bugs that plagued the original are gone.>The characters in cutscenes are animated beautifully.Cons>The style of graphics feel odd to me, they went with a more realistic version of everything but it isn't terrible, it started to grow on me as time went on.>The movement of the characters feel much heavier than they did in the original>When lassoing enemies you can't see the unique lasso animations for all the different robots that were present in the original sadly.>The way the Tar-Tar shoots is not as good as the original games imo, it was harder to dodge the attacks in the original but the Tar-Tar feels like a joke in this game.>Not really a fan of having to hold a button to swing from place to place as sandy. (can't remember if that was in the original or not).>Some of the battle music segments are messed up in the game.One i found was in jellyfish fields when you have to destroy the water towers for ms.puff.>Patrick can't fit in the teleport boxes very easily. I found myself having to have to force him into the box.Overall the remaster is enjoyable. I think its a fair price for what the game offers,and im glad i was alive to see a remaster of this masterpiece. When i play more i'll add more pros and cons.

_childDocuments_.review: A really great remake of a classic 3D platformer. It's very faithful to the original, with identical music, identical lines, and identical level design and missions. Some things here and there were tweaked to make the game a tad bit easier, most notably the bosses, but they weren't too challenging in the original either IMO so it's not a huge letdown. The graphics have definitely been improved in the right way, where it retains the original artstyle and has improved textures, materials and models. I think in some cases it can look a bit wonky, most notably with reflective materials it kinda just steers too far into the realm of... how can I put this... y'know those Unreal Engine tech demos you see on Youtube? Yeah, sorta like those. But thankfully that's not the case most of the time and the visuals do a really good job of maintaining that original, cartoony art direction, and while obviously this means it doesn't look like some amazing, breathtaking, realistic game from a triple-A studio, it really doesn't need to anyway, since the artstyle it has chosen ages far better and complements the gameplay and atmosphere infinitely better.The story is pretty simple, and it doesn't need to be much more: Plankton's built an army of robots, but they go haywire so Spongebob, Patrick and Sandy must save Bikini Bottom from being overrun by evil robots, and helping Plankton reclaim the Chum Bucket. You also collect golden spatulas along the way, and the reason you do that is explained perfectly by one of the in-game characters Bubble Buddy: "Because, Spongebob..." I kid you not this is actually a line in the game, and it sets the tone for the story perfectly. The robot enemy variety is really cool and diverse, with different ways of killing each of them and them all having unique attack patterns. More robot variants show up throughout gameplay, where the further you go the harder the robots are to counter, which makes for a really solid difficulty curve. The missions are fun, with some being harder than others, and some being impossible if you're an IGN reviewer. There's also Patrick's socks you can collect in each level, where for every 10 socks you give to Patrick he gives you a golden spatula (or "golden back-scratcher" according to him). These are probably where most players would look up a walkthrough, since some of their locations are pretty damn hard for anyone to find on their own, unless you don't mind spending ages in levels looking in every nook and cranny.If you're into Spongebob, 3D platformers, or you just played the game as a kid and want to relive some nostalgia, this is definitely worth the purchase IMO. It's reasonably priced at £24.99 and it makes for a really great experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good; however, I feel it lacks polish and it doesn't really do anything to justify purchasing it for those who still can play the original.The original game was a 2003 3D collect-athon platformer originally developed by Heavy Iron Studios and published by THQ. What made the older game so beloved was that it was a good licensed game based off of a very beloved intellectual property. Most licensed games at the time usually were not so good, and made just to solely generate a profit. Heavy Iron Studios and THQ actually put some effort into the title; they understood what makes a good game of this genre, and how to make the game fit the IP. Now, here we are, Spongebob Squarepants Battle For Bikini Bottom: Rehydrated, developed by Purple Lamp Studios and published by THQ Nordic. There are some tweaks to the characters such as Sandy being able to lasso grab in the air (and multiple times too), and Patrick being able to move a bit faster if you spam his attack button. Other things that were changed were: The flying missile launching robot's projectile was made much slower, robot's projectile's landing spots are now highlighted, and Mr. Krab's dream can no longer be cheesed like in the original. There are also some questionable changes like: robots cannot be beaten by luring them into goo, and robots cannot be defeated by launching other robots into them. Also worth noting that Clancy Brown still doesn't reprise his roll, and Spongebob's voice while launching the cruise bubble doesn't have that "transmitter" effect anymore. Can't exactly explain why, but the remaster feels like it's missing some polish. Everything else is the same.Does this remaster offer any new content over the original? Just the multiplayer mode, which is pretty boring. Just a mindless beat-em-up that drags on for way too long. The theater is now filled with new concept art for the remaster. That's about it really. There are stuff in the game's files that showed Purple Lamp wanted to finish Patrick's dream, which was cut from the OG game due to time constraints. Guessing time might've repeated itself.Again, the remaster is good. I just felt like it could've been better, y'know. If you're thinking of playing this for the first time or you have played and are unable to play your original copy, then I can recommend. For those that still play the original, you might want to wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated is a remake of the original Console game released back in late 2003, being the first time the PC Gaming community has access to this experience outside of Emulation. By itself, the game is a wonderful entrance to the Platforming-Collectathon genre popularized with other releases within the original's time frame (Super Mario 64, Banjo-Kazooie & Tooie, Donkey Kong 64 are prime examples from the Nintendo 64) with just the right amount of items to collect- 100 Spatulas, and 80 Socks.Battle for Bikini Bottom's Rehydrated rendition has some noteworthy differences compared to the original release:- Additional Idle Animations & Background Decor that refer back towards the show (Mostly between Season 1 and the season following the 1st Movie).- Unused Voice Lines re-implemented(ie. Spongebob's "Mission Control" line when using the Cruise Bubble now has an alternate take without the microphone filter).- Larger Methods of Traversing: The levels are built to-scale, however each character has been given an additional boost in movement; Patrick's normal attack inches him forward, Spongebob has slightly more vertical movement & can Bubble Bash during a single jump, and Sandy can perform an additional jump with every Lasso Pull. Spongebob's Spongebowl move 'Sticks' to surfaces or slopes more and- along with allowing a jump to be performed when exiting this state- can allow for some sequence breaks to occur.There are other various quirks that this game presents, but at the end of the day "Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated" is a faithful port to all Current-Day consoles using Unreal Engine 4.

_childDocuments_.review: Battle for Bikini Bottom is one of the best 3D platformers/collect-a-thons I've played in close to a decade, and easily the best 3D platformer to come out in recent memory (not including Switch exclusives). The inclusion of multiple characters may put off some people who panic remembering the horror of Donkey Kong 64's version of this mechanic but BFBB nails it almost perfectly. The characters are different enough that you'll clearly need one of them for specific parts, but also unintrusive enough that you can progress through the majority of the game without switching very often. If you've played Banjo Kazooie, Super Mario Odyssey or DK64, you know what you're in for. A heavy focus on exploration, puzzle-solving and collecting items. There's also combat, which is actually pretty laid back and enjoyable. I've had very few frustrating fights so far, or frustration with anything in this game.The levels are colorful, creative, fun to explore and are great callbacks to the series. I particularly enjoyed Rock Bottom myself. If you aim to collect every collectible in each level, you can expect about an hour or two worth of content depending on how familiar you are with the game. The presentation of the game is surprisingly well done - it's graphically appealing, it runs at a flawless 1440p/144fps for me throughout the game and it plays extremely smooth. Few to no camera issues so far, and even fewer bugs. Honestly, my only complaint is that they changed Mr. Krabs voice actor. He does a great job, but the characters original VA from the show is extremely iconic and it's a noticable, if minor omission.Overall, if you're looking for something fun and laid back to relax with then Battle for Bikini Bottom is an easy recommendation - ESPECIALLY if you're fond of the genre. I can only hope the developers of this remaster give other 3D action titles from this era the same treatment. Simpsons Hit and Run would be a dream come true.

Spoiler alert I would not have hundreds of hours on the original if not for the speedrunning side of this game. It is why so many people who grew up playing this game never lost interest. The speedrunning side of the game was like a new way to experience your childhood happiness. All this new game does is allow to relive my childhood trauma while I wish I was playing litterally anything else. The best thing this game has done is show me how much of a miracle it was that the speedrunning community came along and discovered cruiseboosting. I really feel bad for all of the poor souls that paid full price for this game or anyone who had zero nostalgia for the original and heard that this was actually a fun platformer worth their time and money because this game has been rated so good purely and the success of the original alone. If you still are considering buying this game you need to be1. Super nostalgia ridden for the  original game2. Delusional as ♥♥♥♥I rest my caseSave your money and just look at screenshots if you think it looks pretty

A problem I have with games currently is that although the game is long or endless, I'm not having much fun, however with Spongebob Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated, I can confidently say it's well worth steams current price, and I would go as far as paying £40 or more, being an original player. _childDocuments_.review: I have a ton of nostalgia for this game, I am wearing the rose-tinted goggle just as much as anyone else who grew up with this game, but honestly the gameplay just aged a lot worse than I was expecting. The remaster left the gameplay almost entirely untouched, and while that's a good thing in some ways, it works to the game's detriment in others. It's a collectathon/platformer hybrid but both the collecting and the platforming are just plain boring. There's a lot of dull back tracking if you ever miss a pickup, and while the music is nice, you'll get sick of every track by the time you hear it loop 50 times in the course of completing the level. That being said, this game is a pretty faithful remaster of the original game, and is definitely worth experiencing if you have nostalgia for it. I also think this game would be great for young kids. But as an adult, even an adult who has extreme nostalgia for this game, I am never going to touch it again.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a visually fantastic remake, but its programming is flawed. Three achievements surrounding obtaining 100 spatulas, 80 socks, and collecting all of both have been bugged and won't unlock. I also heard reports that some of the levels lack proper boundaries, allowing players to travel to unintended areas in the background. The camera is pretty mediocre, as it has been programmed to "snap" in front of whatever geometry it may overlap. This has led to several occurrences where the camera would rapidly flash close to Spongebob and far away from him in a strobe light manner. I'd recommend the developers to implement camera functions so that the camera will zoom in and out based on whatever obstructions are in the way. Many have criticized the alterations that stray from the original, but I do think some of the changes were needed. For instance, Spongebob's ball form was very floaty in the original and would easily lose speed after colliding with any piece of geometry. The remake tightens up the physics of the ball form so that it doesn't get knocked around as easily, and just overall controls nicer. I thought this was a welcome change that's an improvement from the original.Beyond this, it's a game that's perfect for kids and alright for adolescents/adults. I'd give it a B- overall, as the game holds up relatively well today and retails for a reasonable price given its length. The movie theater's reward was ruined though. It originally showed off concept art, but now they just show some larger images of mission thumbails in the menu. I have no idea what these people were thinking. That is just insulting to the kids who are playing this for the first time, and it's disappointing to the fans of the original. I don't even think you get an achievement for it either, so I don't see what's supposed to be the reward when you have to grind money for what I'm guessing at least an hour. If you're really that curious to see what's in it, just use Cheat Engine to give yourself the money. Trust me, you'll feel much worse if you actually spend time grinding for the money than if you just edited some values in memory.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the same game it's always been, but with a fresh coat of paint. If you liked the original, you'll like this too! A lot of this enjoyment is, however, tied directly to the player's enjoyment of Spongebob.A lot of the style, music, and level design can be appreciated by anybody, but the real meat of the game is from its self referential humor. If you aren't a Spongebob fan, this probably won't sway you either way on the franchise, but it's still a decent little 3D Platformer with solid levels, fun music, great visuals, and a lighthearted world that just feels nice.The gameplay itself hasn't been updated very much from the original game. Certain strange quirks and floaty style holds true even in this version. It feels outdated and at times unfinished, but if you played the original, nothing new will stand out. Even despite that, the game feels good to play. I can't stress how much fun Sandy in particular is! That Lasso is so satisfying.I haven't checked out the extra content yet, but I have to say I'm excited to! This will stand as the definitive way to play Battle for Bikini Bottom (unless you're a speedrunner that is!)

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for the core experience, the tried and true 3d platformer, then this is the game for you. It captures the charm that the original experience had and more. the visuals are gorgeous, the character designs (most of them anyway) are fantastic, and the animations are stunning. there are plenty of issues though unfortunately. some of which i feel were easily avoidable. for starters, while the style of the game is great, i do feel that a lot of the original charm that drew me into the original game did end up getting polished off. little details such as the shiny objects flying towards the player at the end of a combo, or the sound of the shiny object counter ticking up repeatedly per count when you grabbed higher numbers of shiny objects are gone. spongebob's slight air time bonus by spinning mid-air is also gone (though it was given to patrick which is nice). I do know that the bugs, glitches, and exploits from the original game being removed is a major downside to some, especially to the speedrunner community that actually even saved this game from obscurity, but i personally wasn't affected all that much by it as i am not a speed runner. and while i believe it is a valid complaint, i don't think it's a valid criticism. that being said, there have been some new bugs that i have noticed that have popped up during my 100% playthrough, such as severe clipping issues that have caused me to relaunch the game entirely, and the (hopefully patched) missing sock/golden spatula bug. That being said, it would be a disservice to not bring up the improvements that this rehydrated version has brought to the table. like i stated earlier, while the character and personality was unfortunately polished out, the visuals in this game are still beautiful. the vibrant colors of jellyfish fields, the new bright visuals of the kelp forest to allow us to see clearly, and views in spongebobs dream, the level designs look amazing. some of the new gameplay features included have also been a welcome addition, with the new dedicated sneak button making sleepy-times and sleeping tiki's less of a pain to deal with, the new hidden ability to spin attack chuck's missiles back at it, as well as allowing patrick to finally be able to attack in the air, with him being the only playable character to not be able to in the original, spongebob squarepants: battle for bikini bottom - rehydrated is still an experience i will love for a long time. it's far more accessible to more people than the original was, and i'm grateful that it's a version worth enjoying

_childDocuments_.review: A rightfully named cult classic, that has been improved to be even more awesome than I remembered it. Despite playing this as a 10 year old (29 now) it still has that whitty charm, funny moments, and smooth gameplay. Its hard to believe that this could be funner than most games out there, but it just is. Its simple, but addicting, and what video games should be.From that bright colors (a tad bit too contrasted, the brightness of Spongebob's colors is almost blinding, but it is what it is) to the music, its fun to explore what a 3D version of Bikini Bottom would be like if you were there.To play as other characters, each with their different quirks and abilities is awesome too.Very addicting, in where if you started playing at 12:am, you'll find yourself still playing at 1am (or at least that's what happened for me).The price is not outrageous either, and you can easily afford 23 bucks to relive your childhood in a new and improved version.Also the improvements are awesome, everything feels meaty, almost like you can reach out and grab a hold of Patrick's chunkiness, and it would feel like blubber! Lol!As far as if its for you or not, its a nice change from the hoohum, just to keep in your library, and role it out to play---full controller support.If you want a game for yourself of for your kids, this should be your first choice.If you're trying to find a game that has GTA gore, or Mortal Kombat fatalities, naw bro you came to the wrong place, this game might be to tame for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that this game is undeniably good. However, it's important to acknowledge the initial problems that emerged. Surprisingly, removing the glitches would diminish the game's beloved charm, as they contribute to its unique appeal. Alongside these glitches, there are two other notable issues—one being the missed opportunity of having Clancy Brown voice Mr. Krabs instead of the Chum Bucket version we received. Despite these setbacks, the game manages to shine.The remaster is exceptionally well-made, staying faithful to the original models. The developers have masterfully modernized the visuals while preserving the essence of the cherished PlayStation 2 version. It effortlessly transports players back to the nostalgic era, evoking a sense of fond reminiscence.While the single-player experience deserves praise, the multiplayer component falls short of the expectations set for it. However, the inclusion of the cut Squidward boss compensates for this, injecting an intriguing element into the game. It's a case of "you win some and you lose some."In conclusion, this game is a faithful remaster that successfully captures the spirit of the original. Despite its flaws, it remains an enjoyable experience that rekindles cherished memories. Whether you're a long-time fan of the original release or discovering it for the first time, this well-crafted remaster offers plenty to appreciate. Embrace the nostalgia and embark on an adventure that will make you smile, glitches and all.

(Ghost Graveyard from the Pineapple)Negatives for changes:- When I went to destroy certain things that crunch you'd get from hitting things like the items in SpongeBob's house was absent like a my father.- Some sound effects with motions left out. (Hitting the horn next to spongebob's bed as an example)- Shiny Objects were used more. Which is something weird for me to say, you need more of them NOW than you did in the original game.- The theator felt more empty as you only put in like 6 images of at least alpha stage images. Would have even prefered you added a section of the OG concept art to this as it would have been a kind gesture to the original game.Aside from all of that the game is how any remaster of a beloved game could have ever been. Even if I feel I am being a little harsh as I am striking even the part you save 40k shiny objects for that has no real purpose to completing the game other than an unlock.Overall I give the entire experience a 9.5/10 for a remaster, They tried some new things in terms of sound effects or taking them away in this case to a point and it made the game a little emptier instead of adding to the game play which is the biggest fault. _childDocuments_.review: This game was essentially a nostalgia run for me. I borrowed the original game years ago from a friend but I could never get past the second area due to the disc being badly scratched. Unfortunate as it was, I was never able to obtain the game for myself so I accepted the fate that I'd never get to finish it. And then the remake happened. So, I finally decided to buy it on a whim as I wanted to actually complete the game for once. The Pros: The game is easy to complete and can be down in 1-2 play sessions. Including gathering all achievements if that is your sort of things. This game really is aimed for the older gen so that they can relive playing games that they once played on consoles such as PS2. It looks refreshed from what I remember and controls seem to be a bit smoother too. For what I paid, it is worth the price. Not too expensive for a remake. If it cost more I probably wouldn't have bought it. The story is easy to understand, objectives are explained in simple terms and boss fights have easy enough ques on when to attack. Collectibles are easy enough to locate though a guide had to be used for a few that where in obscure places that I'd have never have thought to look or found. For a short game the levels are all vast and different with their own atmospheres and music that helps to make you feel like you're in certain areas. The Cons: The difficult spike seems to appear out of no where once you finish the first robot boss. With no gradual ease into more difficult areas, it does lead the change in difficulty unexpected. Certain levels also aren't that enjoyable and it's more of a grind and chore to finish such as the Kelp Forrest and Spongebobs Dream due to how often you can and will fall into the water/abyss as it's very easy to fall of the platforms.The cut scenes did seem to have extended awkward pauses between them. Especially when transition from them to a battle or continuing on with a world. As well as that there is no real want or need to play it once it has been completed unless you're a die hard fan who enjoys the games. Also, if you use a Playstation control it doesn't appear to support it so unless you're able to remember what button is what, then you're in for a bit of a bad time. Overall I would recommend it to people to play if they're in the mood for a challenging game to pass the time but also feel some irritation at the fact you will fall to your doom a lot and will spend some time looking for the collectibles. But if you're looking for a game that you'll spend some time on or to want it to have a lot of replay value, then this isn't for you.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, since it is based on a good game. But looking at it from the perspective of it being a remaster, the developers did the bare minimum.The Good- Remastered Music- Good Textures- Based on a good game.The Bad- The characters in general have very few animations. The developers only added very few ones.- Tons of Glitches/Bugs- Absolutely barebones Display options. No way to change graphic settings.-  No reinserted cut content as promised (which may or may not do with the whole pandemic situation).Overall the gameplay feels good, but the rest lacks any polishing at all by the developers. It feels like a rushed job (maybe due to COVID-19?) that overall feels like more of a cash in then an honest attempt at a remaster like the Crash and SPyro ones for example.Visually, the game looks good in stills, but the characters don't feels very much alive, looking like fish (pun intended), most of the time, due to most being so poorly animated.Considering this is a remaster from the ground up, I don't think that the vast amount of glitches I have encountered can be excused.I think 2/10 is too harsh, considering the game is very fun. I would give it a 5-6/10, but would recommend getting it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up on platformers/action-adventure games meant that this game smashed me right in the gaming organs as soon as I started playing it. I'd heard good things.. this being the "best SpongeBob game ever" and "one of the best 3D platformers of all time" etc. but I had never played it back in the day.This game is just flat-out wholesome fun. The levels are all interconnected in a way that makes the world seem more open world-like than a series of set levels has any right to be. Multiple entrances in and out help with this feeling but it also has the ability to grab a taxi back to any point (I'm not sure if that is new or in the original but it's great).I'm not as super familiar with a lot of the older SpongeBob stuff - though I'm going back to watch them now having started playing this and seeing the references in the game that throwback to events in even the earliest episodes is nice. The 'Kandy Bar' machine in Rock Bottom actually required me to look it up though because I was worried that I was missing something gameplay-wise rather than just a clever reference to a particular episode.The visuals are fantastic, though there are still some bugs/control weirdness that will occasionally throw you up.. and there are some weird things happening with audio levels at the moment as I could not get it to work with the surround setup defaults that most of my other games work fine with. It's also sometimes unclear on when you'll hit a liquid (crazy being underwater hey) and whether or not you'll bounce off it or if you instantly 'drown'. The game is very forgiving though - you don't lose shiny things (one of the main collectables) on 'death'.. there are no lives making you restart whole sections, you just get put back pretty close to where you made the mistake.. which is great because there are still some enemy attacks etc that feel like they cheese death you sometimes.If you love - or heck, even just enjoy - puzzle platformer action adventure collectathons with sliding action sequences, jumping puzzles and specific boss mechanics then you should definitely put this one on your list.I think the average age of people who enjoyed SpongeBob as a kid are now in their mid-twenties.. I missed a lot of it originally being in my mid-thirties but my nephew absolutely loves SpongeBob and I'm looking forward to playing this with him when he reaches the arbitrary age we set on videogames (four.. lol).

_childDocuments_.review: Although this feels new and refreshing, I love it because it still feels like the original and that's all I can ask for from any remaster and rankly, this game would have to be my favorite remastered project. The ambition by the developers and community is extraordinary and I'm hoping for the best with future updates and patches. Seeing THQ Nordic supply a means of reporting bugs and issues is also hopeful. Multiplayer could be better, I feel bits of the game were false advertised, we were told some cut content from the original like the Squidward Robot boss fight would be implemented but it was dropped into the multiplayer with no boss fight and just a background effect really, along with Patrick's dream sequence made into a battle island. Multiplayer just feels half-assed and only put in so we'd get the promised content. I can understand keeping the campaign close or the same as the original, but it would've been exciting to see an expanded experience for old school fans. I recommend this game to the old fans, new fans, speed runners, or anyone always interested, a breathtaking experience that is very enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I have not played the original, so any thoughts put forward will be purely based on this remake.Overall, this game was a fun 20 hours. I've 100%'d the game and I enjoyed every second of it. There was not one world that annoyed me or made me want to rush through to get it over with, which is something that is not easy to pull off. The presentation is great, vibrant, and colourful.The gameplay was solid; the separate worlds did not blend together in a way which made me feel like I'm just going through a re-skinned version of the previous world. They built on top of each other well, and all of them were a joy to play and look at.The dialogue and voice acting is great, what you'd expect out of seasons 1-3 of Spongebob.There are however a few non-polished aspects present. These do not detract much from the overall experience, but if patched up, the game will feel that little bit better to play.1) I feel that the movement speed is a bit too slow for worlds that are sometimes quite large and spacious. This isn’t too big an issue most of the time, but occasionally, when you spot an item you missed in the distance, the movement speed might put you off from backtracking. 2) The keyboard & mouse controls aren’t the greatest. The menus aren’t very response to the mouse. For example, when you hover your cursor on something you can click, it isn’t immediately highlighted, instead, I had to click once or twice on it before it highlighted the appropriate map or menu. The camera also has some issues when using a mouse. In tight spaces, you will seemingly hit a wall with the camera, and you are not allowed to move the camera any further in that direction. This same issue is not present when using a controller.3) A minor complaint is that the hitbox for the spatulas might be a little too small. This caused some annoyance in SpongeBob’s dream world. One spatula requires you to jump off a ball. I saw SpongeBob come very close, within centimetres of the spatula sometimes, but it took me 10 minutes of trying over and over to finally get it. If the hitbox was altered slightly, or the Spatula was maybe lowered a tiny bit, it could potentially prevent some frustration.4) In game, and in cutscenes, there is occasional texture pop-in.Those were my main gripes to the game. Again, this was very enjoyable experience, and I do not regret purchasing and completing it. If the developers patch these issues, this game will feel like a more polished experience. Thanks for the wonderful 20 hours of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played the original BFBB, but I really love this remake. I pre-ordered it in May 2020 and have since beat the game twice, with 100% completion on my second save file, and just recently started another save since I haven't played it since 2021. SpongeBob is very special to me and is one of the few cartoons I still enjoy as an adult, so Rehydrated immediately jumped out to me when it was announced.One of the most obvious improvements over the original is the graphics. While the classic still has a charming visual style, Rehydrated is more like what you'd expect from a game based on a cartoon. It's vibrant (but not in a way that's overwhelming imo), the lighting and particles look good, the animations are fluid and expressive, and overall it just looks very pleasant. Even the character models are a huge improvement, they managed to translate the 2D characteristics of the main cast into the 3D space and still have them look accurate to the show.Then there's the world and level design. I love all of the environments that are featured, it really feels like you're in the world of Bikini Bottom. You get everything from SpongeBob's neighborhood and Goo Lagoon, to Rock Bottom and the Flying Dutchman's territory. It's a blast exploring these locations that you're only given glimpses of throughout the cartoon. Despite the map being separated into different areas, each zone is pretty big and detailed which helps make the game feel less linear. There are typically multiple ways to get over and around an obstacle, so it's best to experiment. Each level is constructed in a way that prevents you from getting lost but also doesn't hold your hand, you can still walk around as you'd like and get to your objective when you're ready.Where gameplay is concerned, the controls are very smooth and responsive. The platforming feels satisfying and creative. Being able to play as SpongeBob, Patrick, or Sandy unlocks more opportunities to mess around with the moveset. Each character has their own unique abilities which you may need to unlock certain collectibles. The combat is non-intrusive and simple, but it really adds to the game. Nothing feels boring or repetitive.Overall, there's a lot more I could say about Rehydrated, but I think this about covers the basics. If you're a SpongeBob fan or even just want a good platformer, I'd highly recommend this game. It's great for adults and kids, especially since there are some optional challenges which will provide something a little more difficult for older players. The multiplayer gamemode isn't anything spectacular but it's there if you're interested in it. IGN must've been on some different kind of spoiled Kelpo to give this game a 5/10, don't trust them. It's at least a 9.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I never reviewed a game before on Steam, I'll be glad to start off with this game. I played the OG version on my PS2 and thought it is a masterpiece of a platformer and many other things it is great for like the characters, humor, and abilities you can do with Spongebob, Patrick, and Sandy. Awesome for 2003. The OG game is too memorable to me that when I heard it's going to have a remaster with a few things added I am truly excited. I will give out my Pros and Cons on the game and give you all my final thoughts. Pros:- Spongebob and Patrick can now attack in mid-air and Sandy can now lasso robots in mid-air. This is a very good thing since in the OG, your attacks to the flying robots are limited and can get a bit frustrating unless you are Sandy. - The textures look really colorful and fit the tone in some of the levels. - Also relating to the levels, the amount of detail put into them look amazing like the grass in Jellyfish Fields or the darkness kept in Rock Bottom. Also the dream level hub looks beautiful as well as Bikini Bottom and Kelp Forest as it has a little less dark in lighting then the OG. - Some of the models of the characters look good and fitting with the shiny textures like Sandy or Larry the Lobster, also Mr. Krabs. - The script stayed the same as the OG. Very good thing to do regardless it's too memorable.- The idol animations are amazing and very good references to classic and modern Spongebob as also the OG game.In Between:- The pick up items in this game now have bubbles around them. I kinda do and don't like this since it kinda ruins the looks of the object. Idk that was just a little nit pick. - The OST although it is memorable and I love it, the OST is indeed the same but the difference is that the OST is now in MONO instead of STEREO like in the OG. I do love some of the tracks in mono but tracks like Rock Bottom or the Final Boss fit best in stereo as you can tell it's more dramatic and for Rock Bottom, more ambient.Cons: - The VA for Mr. Krabs in the OG game STILL exists in this game. To me, the VA for him is bad. Sad we can't do anything for Mermaid Man too as well, but at least his I can tolerate. - Back to the levels, although I did say I love them and how beautiful they look. Some of them have a little too much color and kinda blend in to the environment. - The dream level hub does look nice, but when you gain access to certain dreams the same hub background appears. Mostly in Squidward's and Mr. Krabs's dreams where the backgrounds originally were dollars and music sheets that actually FIT the looks of the dreams. - Kelp Forest, the HARDEST level in the game has an infamous challenging slide that makes me mad sometimes. They altered the vine slide to have walls and stuff to make it easier as well as to have some tone to make it look like it is in a forest. As much as I like that detail and that I hate the slide in the OG, the thing actually pays off when you successfully complete it in the OG. Sometimes it's best to enjoy things you don't like and the vine slide brought a challenge to most people who play the OG including myself. Wish the challenge of the slide is still there in the remaster though. - The shiny textures in the models although do fit with SOME of the characters but to ALL of them does not fit well with this even some of the models look like awful dolls like Mermaid Man mostly and the Flying Dutchman too as well also somehow lost his transparency. - The sliding sections of the levels still have this distracting motion line effect to act like you're sliding down fast. I know what the devs were trying to do, but I just don't like that feature. Maybe it be a bit better if it's a little transparent like lower it a bit down so we can still see it but it won't be in a solid white as what we still got. - The Multiplayer...... SUCKS. As much as i was very happy to see that the UNUSED CONTENT from the OG is going to be in this game I was excited. This point deserves multiple points: - ALL of the unused content I mentioned only exists in the multiplayer. - You can play as 4 different characters (not counting the main 3 in the campaign) all of them have similar move sets compared to the main three to play as in the campaign. To me, that's a bit lazy. But some of them do act a bit different like Squidward and Robo-Plankton but that does not change much.- The Robo-Squidward boss however is cool to see in action, the problem is you don't do much of anything to damage him other than pressing buttons after you beat waves of robots. - Speaking of robots, very FEW of them only exist in this mode and it's not really much of a challenge and is easy to defeat them as all of them are the starter robots from the beginning of the campaign up to the G-Love. - This mode takes very little time to complete.        I do love BFBB, I really do but I do consider this a good remaster but not a great one. As much as my heart is on the OG version, this game is good to play and I do consider it faithful to the OG. I know even with the Cons I said, the devs did try to put a lot of heart to this and that's why I still play this remaster. It's good to see that and I hope we do get more good Spongebob games in the future. And for that, I do recommend this game but ONLY for the main campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game is great on its own and is a remake of a cult classic. How does it stand up to the original? Me personally, no i do not think it stands up to the original for there are several difference in it compared to the original that makes it stand out on its own as a unique title. Everything that made the original great for casual play still remains the same. Fun platforming, basic story, fun characters to play as, and a timeless appeal for anyone who used to play it as a kid and newcomers who never played the original and want to experience this game casually. I have mentioned a couple times the word casually. that is because if it was not for the community of the original game, most important SHiFT!, this game would not have been possible. The speedrunning community kept the original alive and seeing so many new people what it was all about with this one as a casual experience. Formulating your own opinion about the game is more important that what i think, or say IGN thinks, because in the end, it is up to you to come up with your own thoughts and opinions on the fact of the matter. I still think this game is great to play casually. 7.8/10 too much water.

_childDocuments_.review: This has been a game I've been looking forward to for over a decade and I'm so happy to finally be able to play it. Don't let the big-time review sites fool you, this is a fantastic 3D platformer collectathon with a ton of heart and charm from the early days of Spongebob. The controls are rock-solid, the visuals are downright beautiful, and the remastered music is incredible. Only 30 bucks, too! Fans of the original, definitely pick it up. People who never played the original, if you're a fan of games in a similar genre I have no doubt you'll find this game a delightful romp.EDIT: It's been over a year and with more time to reflect, I'm a little disappointed with a number of things surrounding this game. So many bugs have been left unpatched, lots of grievances pretty much ignored... It's still a fantastic game but it's still dampened by the lack of post-launch support by THQ Nordic.
