_childDocuments_.review: I played the original game back on the Gamecube and it was a wonderful experience. The world was really immersive for its time and one of the best plattformer back in the old era.This remaster is a wonderful rehydration of the old experience. Graphics and animations are done beautifully and if you would take away the HUD, it would look straight out of a new Spongebob movie.That said, the game has numerous bugs and visual quirks that take away of things that were immersive back then. I completed the game (up to the Spongebob bossbattle, not 100%) and I encountered numerous and partly game breaking bugs.-Enemies spawned from a Duplicator don't have any visual spawning que, the can hits the ground and the enemy instantly pops up, it looks bad.-There is fog all around Bikini Bottom, not sure why this is a thing since it doesn't really hide anything and just looks like a thin semi-transparent layer. Without it the game would look way better.-Sometimes, bubbles don't appear around spatulas.-Some animations are done really smoothly, like Patrick's jumping animation, other animations however look almost laggy like when Spongebob picks up a spatula.-In the Robo-Patrick bossfight, right when the second stage hit. My Robo-Patrick was outside of the playable area, but managed to glitch itself back into default position. From then on however I wasn't able to damage him anymore and needed to reset the mission.I can't judge the multiplayer since it seems like no one is playing it right now.Despite all this flaws the game is still a great and new way to play the game. For fans looking to play there favorite game again this is an absolute must buy. I just hope that Purple Lamp is continuing to work on this game and patch out all issues.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played the ever loving heck out of this game as a kid on the PlayStation 2, this was probably my most anticipated game at the time of its announcement. 4 years later, does it hold up? Well...it depends.The game is practically beat for beat from the original (even  the voice clips were recycled, which means having to listen to Joe Whyte as Mr. Krabs and Mermaid Man), so nothing changed THAT much. However, as someone who played the original religiously, it does feel REALLY different, and takes time to get used to the newer controls, but its almost certainly not going to be a problem to newcomers if this is the first version you play. It's also worth noting that I've encountered a couple of glitches and bugs throughout my experience (which isn't the developers fault, as Nickelodeon rushed this to meet a deadline to tie in with the movie "Sponge On The Run", but nothing game breaking (the worst I've dealt with was the multiplayer mode softlocking after completion, and that was on the Nintendo Switch release).So do I recommend it? Sure. If you wanna see what the fuss is (was?) about remaking a cult classic, you'll probably get a kick out of it. But if you're a veteran to BFBB, I'd say approach with skepticism, and if you don't mind the changes here, you'll like it fine, although I really wouldn't recommend paying full price for the veterans. Wait for a sale to happen.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting review to write. Short of a few rentals I never played the original console B4BB back in the day, as I played much more of the totally different PC release which I have immense nostalgia for. That being said, I have a lot of nostalgia for similar games of the time such as the licensed Dreamworks games. This is all to say that I'm going in relatively unsulied by past experiences with the game to really know whats happening.I'm gonna start with the bad, just because if we're being honest its why you're here. First noteworthy issue, the game has some pretty common issues among eh PC releases. It launches SteamVR on startup if you have a headset plugged in. I once had my framerate cut in half because I got a steam message and it only recovered after I restarted the game. It has some audio balancing issues. Nothing too major, just kinda annoying. Then you get to the game itself. The biggest cons of the game itself are the pretty awful hit detection on certain things, a few voices being changed (strange story, for some reason the original game didnt use the actual voice actor for Mr. Krabs and this game just kinda decided to reuse that instead of re-recording them. Same with another character or two.), and just a sort of feeling of cheapness to it. it's hard to describe, but it just doesn't feel like it has the love poured into it that more recent efforts like Crash and Spyro have. Everything just feels very cheaply redone. It kinda feels like a really really really good fan remake, not what you'd expect as the official release. All that out of the way, the game is a great time. Yes sometimes you'll get very annoyed at bad hit detection or cheap animation, but the rest of it is just a ton of nostalgic fun. It's still awesome to get to explore Bikini Bottom and remember the moments from all the episodes. The gameplay is pretty fine. Its just a good licensed game, nothing to really berate or praise, it very much relies on being based on a fantastic license to carry it to success.

_childDocuments_.review: As one of many who grew up with the original game, I gotta say this is a fantastic remake. Not to mention the extra content put into this. If you love and or grew up with the original, obviously pick it up and if you aren't you should still give it a try. Still a solid collect-a-thon platformer that hits me with the right level of nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: ARE YOU READY, KIDS?AYE AYE CAPTAIN!A remake from 2003 Battle for Bikini Bottom on PS2. This remake sure have some great improvement from the original, albeit the physics isn't the best and not as wacky as the PS2 version. I listed some pros and cons of this remake according to my own opinion:Pros+ Better graphics and animation update+ Great atmosphere on Bikini Bottom surroundings+ Great characters design and detail+ Some, hilarious, new cutscenes compared to the PS2 version+ Inclusion of some unused dialogues during idle/attacking animations, not new but unused dialogues+ Some robots are actually harder to beat than the original, example like Ham-mer and Tar-Tar 'cause both having slightly faster animations than the PS2 version+ Improve boss design and battle, all of them are having a more robotic movement and faster animations making them slightly harder to beat than the PS2 version+ New references from the Movies and Season 3 onward+ Improvement on some level design, like Spongebob's Dream+ Usage of L2/ LT buttons on the remake for Sneak+ This remake release date coincide with my favorite game series anniversary, Sonic The Hedgehog :D+ Steam preorder get a slightly improved OST for free and also a 10% discount price from the original price XDCons- Clancy Brown doesn't reprised his role as Mr. Krabs in this game- It's kinda buggy- Framedrop during gameplay, noticeable if there's too many Shiny Objects or robots- Somehow, some stages are too small compared to the PS2 version.- It's missing some animations that already being presented on PS2 version, example like Flying Tiki pop-up and robots spawn animation not presented in this remake- Inclusion of some assist crosshairs like Tar-Tar's sauce crosshair and Robo-Patrick's acid droplet crosshair that somehow make this game easier than the PS2 version- Sometimes, it's taking a while to render some level's detail- No difficulty select; like Easy/Normal for newcomer, Normal/Hard for those who have played before or just Hard for more challenges (I take Sonic Forces' difficulty selection as an example)- No Advances Graphic settings, everything is already set to High...likely- Sounds are too low, even on maximum in-game setting- No new recorded lines- Boss battle phases remain the same without any extra battle, I was hoping MuscleBob BuffPants phases for Sandy and Patrick during the last battle at the Chum Bucket- When civilians are hit by the player, either on hub world/stages, most of them are just fall down to the ground rather than having their own fall-down animations like in PS2 version- Horde mode doesn't have any dialogue on EVERY characters, there's a music in Horde Mode but it's too low you can barely hear it. Robo-Squidward doesn't have any robotic sound effect, unlike the other robo-bosses and you don't beat him. He'll just die after you beat tons of robots.Well, although I write too many cons on this review, but honestly I really like this remake and have been waiting for this game since last year and here it is. Still love this game and can't wait the get this game again for the physical Switch version.EDIT: After I finish this game to 100%, I just realized that I can't beat the Robo-Bosses again after I select the Golden Spatula. Does anybody also have the same problem? It also missing SpongeBall Arena entrance after 100% so it's kinda bummer

_childDocuments_.review: Due to its widespread popularity as a staple Nickelodeon children’s TV show, running successfully since 1999, SpongeBob SquarePants has received several game adaptations featuring its eccentric characters and the wacky town of the Bikini Bottom. Some of the most notable games include The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie (Game), SpongeBob’s Truth or Square, SpongeBob SquarePants featuring Nicktoons: Globs of Doom (my personal favorite), the original SpongeBob SquarePants Battle for Bikini Bottom, and more. The original SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom was co-developed by Heavy Iron Studios, AWE Games, and Vicarious Visions, and published by THQ in 2003. The game was available on PS2, Xbox, GameCube, and more. The remake, SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom – Rehydrated, was recently released onto Steam on June 23rd of this year. It was developed by Purple Lamp Studios and published by THQ Nordic and, like the original, it is an action-adventure game with multiplayer and co-op modes and positive reviews from players.Bikini Bottom really comes to life in this game’s world design and graphics, everything is fun to look at and there is so much for you to interact with. SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom – Rehydrated is designed as an open-world game where venturing to new areas is especially fun because of the uniqueness that areas of Bikini Bottom already have in the original TV show and the familiarity of locations mixed with the new features the developers brought to the table. Each area is recognizable and includes some of the nostalgic characters and features of classic SpongeBob episodes. Characters sound and act like their television counterparts, so dialogue flows naturally with a comical and lighthearted tone.From the start of the game players can already expect appearances from and references to Bubble Buddy, the iconic French narrator, and the “jellyfishing” episode as well as appearances from the staple characters like Patrick, Gary, Mr. Krabs, Plankton, and more. Most of the well-known characters and settings (if not all) show up at some point throughout the game.Like an episode of SpongeBob or a SpongeBob movie, the story of the game is simple and easy to keep up with, but good enough to keep you engaged in what’s going on because of how it is intertwined with the other random events of the world. The story is the same as the original game. The main conflict is that Plankton, in an attempt to take over the world, created an army of robots to work for him that, of course, malfunction and proceed to not only attack Plankton, but to also wreak havoc on the rest of Bikini Bottom. Plankton coerces SpongeBob and his friends into helping him stop the uncontrollable robots from destroying anyone and everything in their path. During his robot fighting adventures, SpongeBob does various small tasks to help other characters, like the Flying Dutchman, King Poseidon, and Mrs. Puff, all of which still ends up tying into the main story.SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom – Rehydrated is very clear about the keyboard controls, but I found that it worked more smoothly with my PS4 controller once I figured out how the controls translated over. You start off with three lives, which are displayed in the form of underwear, and the underwear are fairly easy to come by. Other objects in the game (Golden Spatulas, Patrick’s socks, Shiny Objects) act as a form of currency that will help you pay your way into new areas on your journey. There are pretty much no changes that you can make to the difficulty settings for the story mode, so the difficulty you are on is pretty much all you have. Luckily, the game is not bad about the setback for running out of underwear. There are check points in areas and enemies are not so persistent that you can’t run away and recuperate when you’re at risk.Another fun feature of the game is that there is a multiplayer mode, where players fight all of the different variations of robots in waves, moving from area to area. You can choose from a couple of the main characters of the SpongeBob universe, and each character has their own unique fighting style. All in all it was a great game that is fun whether you are looking for fun game play or just want to experience the world of SpongeBob SquarePants again!9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Its been 10 years since I last played this game as an 8 year old running around collecting golden spatulas while my parents watched me have the time of my life, and to this day I still really enjoy this game. So BFB or Battle For Bikini Bottom is a casual 3D Platformer about Plankton the owner of the chum bucket, creating a robot army that will obey his every command to take over bikini bottom. After his efforts he fails as the robots do not obey him and start to rampage all over bikini bottom causing all sorts of chaos and problems for everyone, and your job is to try to put a stop to these robots as Spongebob, Patrick, and Sandy and roam around bikini bottom destroying robots and solving fun puzzles in places like Jellyfish Fields, the Kelp Forest, The Flying Dutchman's Graveyard and many more.Gameplay: Good fighting mechanics and abilities, fun collection system, puzzles and minigames, I rate the gameplay 9/10.Music: All your favorite songs from the TV show plus more, there are actually some bangers in here. Chill and enjoyable music that sets the mood of the zone or situation you are in very well, I rate the music 8/10Amount of content: The game offers atleast 8-10 hours of gameplay if you finish the game and collect most of the collectibles, some of the collectibles may prove slightly difficult to get so if you want to completely 100% the game it would probably take around 10-15 hours. A good amount of content, just as much as your average platformer would have, I rate the amount of content 7/10.The only things the game lacks is replay-ability unless you want to speed run it, it's a known game in speed running I believe. The other thing that it lacks is story obviously since its a game created from a kid's TV show, the story isnt bad but its not really good either its just okay but it doesnt make the game any less fun. If you are looking for a story rich platformer I would recommend Hollow Knight or Celeste, both of them are amazing and I do have a very detailed review of Hollow Knight if anyone reading this is interested. So to conclude, I'm confident enough to say that if you enjoy and love platformers you will most likely enjoy this game, maybe not as much as people that played it when they were younger and came back several years later to play the remaster but you certainly will have fun. Overall I would rate the game 8/10.

There are still many annoying bugs with the game, it's easy to get glitched inside of objects and then have to reload the map or even the game, the controller support doesn't really work properly, it keeps dropping connection and removing audio whenever I plug in my controller, which is an issue I haven't had with any other game so far, and even the animations can look stiff at times, such as after Spongebob picks up a Golden Spatula (although this is really the least of my issues). _childDocuments_.review: This is a nice, good remake of the original Battle for Bikini Bottom. I do own the Playstation 2 version which is also a good version of the game that I've played years ago. I did notice that the game uses cloud saves over local game save files. So if you accidentally uninstalled and reinstalled your game you won't lose your progress. The cloud saves are also convenient if you've installed the game on your pc and steam deck where you can play the game back and forth between the two systems fine with the same cloud save file. There is one last thing, and that is the local multiplayer mode that makes you have to play with another person. So you can't play this solo, though in a way you can kinda play it solo with another controller still plugged in like I did. It is playable that way, but once you've cleared the first area of the game. It tells you to press the space bar to continue, but nothing happens and doesn't accept my input either keyboard or controller. So I have no idea whats wrong with that, you can barely try playing the multiplayer mode that way which is kinda a bummer to where you have to leave the mode by selecting the main game menu or just quiting the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A jump and run collect-a-thon set in the world of SpongeBob SquarePants at its prime.Battle for Bikini Bottom sees you take control of the titular sponge as he traverses various parts of Bikini Bottom and helps out his fellow sea dwellers. The game is split into three acts, each of which contains three rather expansive levels, each themed after an iconic location from the early seasons of SpongeBob. Each level contains various collectibles as well as quests for you to complete, ranging from reaching certain locations to collecting a number of hidden items and various smaller challenges which shake up the core platformer gameplay.That being said, the core gameplay is rather solid in itself, doing a good job of alternating jump-and run sections, light puzzles, fights and action set pieces, such as slides or bungie jumps. Every level also allows you to switch to either Patrick or Sandy, each of which has a different set of abilities. As you progress through the game, there's also a steady stream of new mechanics as well as a rather large number of different enemy types to fight, all of which does a good job of making levels feel unique and further keeping things fresh gameplay-wise.The different levels are accessed through a hub world comprised of some key locations from the show, with new levels being unlocked by completing a certain number of quests. Each act also requires a set number of completed quests to finish, rewarding you with a boss fight you have to beat in order to unlock new abilities and expand the hub world, letting you access new levels. These boss fights feel quite distinct and feature multiple phases that mix up the fights' base mechanics.Difficulty-wise, the game falls mostly on the easier side, though a couple of sections also provide a good amount of challenge, especially in the later levels. Due to the way progression works, you may also skip most tasks or even avoid entire levels if you get stuck on them.Beyond completing the game's story, you're of course also encouraged to complete all quests and gather a decently big number of collectibles throughout the game's levels, which I found to be quite fun. Certain areas and objectives also require you to return t them at a later point in the game, providing some additional incentive to revisit levels. As part of the remaster, there's also a newly added multiplayer horde mode, which tasks you and a friend with defeating waves of robots. While this premise sounds interesting, it's executed in a rather basic way, with very little gameplay depth and a noticeable lack of charm compared to the rest of the game.All of this is wrapped in a light story centered around Plankton scheming, which carries things along but ultimately isn't important nor interesting. Where the game shines much more is in the presentation of the SpongeBob setting, with locations and characters feeling like they're taken straight from the show and many references showing how much care was put into making this a SpongeBob game. Dialogues as well as the little sub-stories told with each quest feel right at home with the show, capturing its humor in a very enjoyable way.The game's remastered graphics are genuinely beautiful and frankly don't even compare to the original look. The art direction is noticeably more saturated and colourful, noticeably deviating from the tone of the original game and the TV episodes it's based around. And yet, everything still feels like SpongeBob - presented in a stunning style. Levels are also enhanced with a boatload of additional props and other graphical elements, making them feel much livelier.Battle for Bikini Bottom's sound effects and music were also redone, though the changes feel less extreme, mostly just upgrading the original game's sound quality. For the Soundtrack in particular, this is a very good thing, since the game retains the extremely catchy and diverse tracks perfectly setting the mood for the different locations you're exploring.I played through the game using the German localization, which unlike the original game features the actual German SpongeBob voice actors. While this is a nice change in concept, I quickly had to learn that many of the actors have either passed away or were otherwise replaced by now, meaning that the dub rarely felt like the SpongeBob I know and love. This is further compounded by the fact that the direction given to the voice actors seems to have been less than stellar, with certain line deliveries sounding way off from what they're meant to convey. Sadly, this is especially noticeable on some of SpongeBob's repeated catchphrases. Having played with the original stand-in voices, I'd honestly have preferred them over the incomplete cast of the show, due to their much more fitting performances.As for another negative point, the final phase of development on the remaster seems to have been somewhat rushed, with some of the later levels feeling noticeably less polished than the prior ones. There are also a few minor mistakes, like supposed figurines performing animations or the entrance to the game's credits level being missing from the hub world. Sadly, these minor problems were never addressed, as patch support for the game was quickly ended.With all that being said, I had a lot of fun completing Battle for Bikini Bottom. Whether you want to relive a childhood favorite or try the game for the first time, I can only recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of SpongeBob back in the day, I can tell you this is an okay collectathon.It looks very pretty, it sounds great (wish more of the original voice actors were in there) and the levels are fun enough. My main issue with the game is that the gameplay mechanics are too Playstation 2, which is perfectly fine considering this is a remake of a PS2 game, but I'm playing it in 2023 and this year alone, I've played games that felt way better than this. Check out Hell Pie or even Lil Gator Game. Traversing the maps in those games is fast, smooth and super addictive. Here it's just too slow and the levels are quite simple so they don't push your limits. Also, having to change characters in specific points for certain abilities was a pain in the arse for me.For kids this is probably going to be an amazing game and I'd definitely recommend for that audience. Or maybe if the nostalgia hits hard on you and you played the original game. But if you are experienced in 3D platformers and collectathons, this is probably just a downgrade from what you are used to and like me, you should probably pass.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm saying yes, I'd recommend this game, but there are a lot of flaws that I'd like to talk about as well. If i could give a "Maybe" recommendation, I would honestly do just that. But let me go through all the pros and cons.Pros:-Visually, the game looks great. It's bright and colorful and looks very modernized compared to the original.-Gameplay is pretty smooth overall, platforming mechanics and combat are textbook for a 3D platformer.-Remastered soundtracks. Yes, YES, YESSS!!!-Glitches that are good for speedrunning.Cons:-Main boss fights are awful. Two of the four were ruined in almost all ways (Robo-Pat and Robo-Spongebob's Brain along with Robo-Plankton), one was slightly improved (Robo-Sandy), and one was basically unchanged. (Robo-Spongebob)-Glitches that are bad... in general.-Overhyped. Nostalgia trip just wasn't there. As I was playing I just wanted to go back and play the original. (which is exactly what I did).-The game is more aimed towards kids. When I say this, I'm mostly referring to gameplay, level design, and boss fights. Everything is ten times easier than the original, which had some segments and a specific boss, Robot Patrick, that actually had quite a bit of difficulty behind them. This was basically thrown away entirely, and while this was an understandable decision, it's just more of a reason for people like me, who wanted to re-experience what I played when I was five, to steer away from this game and play the original again. That's why I'm considering this more of a con than a pro.So... yeah. The game is good for kids, definitely. If you buy this game for your eight year old son, he'll get those classic jokes from when I used to watch Spongebob as a kid (which are much better than today's Spongebob Episodes), you'll probably find them glued to the damn screen. But for people like me, it just didn't hit me the way I wanted it to. I wouldn't necessarily say it was bad in any way, but it just didn't satisfy my hunger for the nostalgic feeling I was looking for, and I feel many would agree with me also.6/10, Above Average. The multiplayer isn't even worth talking about, so I aint gonna.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing. I'm very mixed with this remake, as someone who's played it when it first came out, I'm overall mixed with the game.Overall, the game is extremely broken, and nothing like the original. If you plan on playing this game yourself, try not to compare it to the original. It is its own beast with it being made in Unreal Engine 4, it being the first project for Purple Lamp, and with the many issues it has, it still has some good moments that you'll have to experience yourself while playing it.Even after this game,  I would still recommend newcomers to get their hands on the original. They focused on making this a visually appealing game first before thinking of actual gameplay. It isn't bad, but isn't great either.These pros and cons are compared to the original game● Graphically looks very nice.● Every level is redesigned from the ground up, pretty much a one-to-one recreation.● A new Mulitplayer Mode with a variety of playable characters.● 32 easy to get achievements.● Game can be 100% completed in less than 10 hours. ● SpongeBob can perform a Bubble Bash after his first jump.● Patrick's grounded belly attack pushes him forward a little bit, making him slightly faster than SpongeBob if spammed. ● Patrick's grounded belly attack can be performed in the air, allowing some harder jumps to be possible with him.● Visually nice looking HUD.● All soundtracks were remade for high quality audio. ● Despite multiplayer, there is NO new content. They promised cut content would make it into the game and yet its pretty much the exact same game.● They used the old voiceclips as the original instead of creating new ones.● Bubble Bowl and Cruise Bubble have new/wonky controlling and doesn't feel right.● Many bugs and glitches all throughout the game.● Many death planes that will punish exploration and easy shortcuts that would otherwise be possible in the original. ● Sandy's swinging mechanic has been entirely redone, now only allowing a scripted swinging segment.● Sandy's swinging mechanic can be easily bugged, allowing you to extend the length of the rope during some segments.● Many audio and sound issues, clips being delayed, some sound effects not existing at all, and sound effects being in places they shouldn't be. ● Cannot refight the bosses, once they are beaten, you can warp back to their levels, but the boss will not reappear.● With proper glitches, this game can be beaten in less than 3 minutes. From the start of the game to the final boss fight.● Bosses are glitchy, sometimes appear in areas they shouldn't and have missing animations. ● You can warp characters to levels that they shouldn't be in through an oversight, such as Patrick being in SpongeBob's House and Sandy being in Jellyfish Fields. Edit: 11/25/2020 - Still good

_childDocuments_.review: "Spongebob Squarepants: Battle for Bikini Bottom" was one of my very first PS2 games as a kid, so this remake had a lot to live up to in regards to retaining the soul, spirit and nostalgia of this yellow sponge's adventure. I am truly amazed by this remake; nearly everything is identical to the original game except for a few quirks here and there. I don't exactly remember much about the PS2 version, but I feel that some level designs have been changed (i.e. the Kelp Forest slide). If that is the case, these are very welcome changes. In addition, I feel the physics in Rehydrated is much more grounded than the original BFBB. Lastly, the music...its fantastic! The quality of the soundtrack in Rehydrated is great; making out the bass, guitar and other small details while sliding down Sand Mountain or getting Barnacle Boy's crystals in the Kelp Cave was very enjoyable.One negative I have about this game is that I heard that they were going to add some levels or sections that were cut out from the original. For example, in the original game, Patrick was supposed to have his own dream level, but they cut it out. Unfortunately, these cuts were not added to the Rehydrated version. I really hope it comes out as DLC, but that's highly improbable.I wouldn't pay full price for the game, however, when it does go on sale, this is a 100% must buy for anyone who enjoys old school PS2 platformers. Now, where is the Spongebob Movie Game remake?

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best SpongeBob game I ever played. I didn't play the original back then, but the fans are saying It's faithful to the classic, so that's perfect. This game really got me back to the PlayStation 2 golden era. THQ did a fantastic job! Thank you so much for bringing a new SpongeBob game for us! This is my childhood all over again and the nostalgia I'm feeling is unspeakable. Very fun gameplay and gorgeous visuals, awesome details and easter eggs from the cartoon series that every fan will love to see. It really feels like you're inside the SpongeBob series and this feeling is amazing. You get to control Patrick and Sandy too, which is super cool, but I was expecting to control Squidward also (I really like him). The price for the game is very fair, it was a well spent money on it and also got this in pre-order. I didn't finish the game yet but I can see it has a long lenght and of course this is very good. It will take longer for you to complete if you go after collecting 100% of all items. If you like SpongeBob and/or 3D platform games, ignore the bad reviews from the "critics" and just play this. For real. It wasn't for nothing that it was one of "PS2 GREATEST HITS" back then. Now with this remaster it's even better! Like I said before, thank you THQ for doing an amazing job! I would absolutely LOVE to see a new SpongeBob game in the future, perhaps a remaster for "SpongeBob Squarepants The Movie" videogame that it was loved by many including me. And please... I'm also a huge fan of Scooby-Doo! Loved the games back in PS2. We really need a new game for it ASAP!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the original game for possibly hundreds of hours as a kid. And this game does not disappoint. _childDocuments_.review: Growing up, I played The Spongebob Squarepants Movie The Game, I never played this one. When I saw this game was remastered I was hesitant to buy it, being that I knew nothing about it. Not to mention a lot of popular reviewing sites were giving it negative scores. I decided to take a leap of faith. I went into the game blind hoping that it would be worth the full price. I have never been so pleasantly surprised in all of my gaming career. The levels all feel unique. The music is catchy and stays with you after you close the game. All of the dialogue feels genuine, just like out of an actual episode (even if some voice actors are different). Not to mention, the game is just fun. There is one portion of grinding (yes I am referring to the Mr. Krabs spatulas), but even then I found enjoyment. It took me 25 hours to get everything in this game, which is probably longer than it takes most, but I was really only able to play in increments of 2 hours at a time. In conclusion, whether you have played this game before or not, whether you have seen the reviews or not, I highly recommend buying it. It is worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful remake of a perfectly average kids' game. Very straight-forward but challenging enough to feel accomplishing. Humor is about the same as the show. Almost has the entire voice cast. (Clancy Brown and Ernest Borgninge are still unavailable unfortunately.) Colorful and runs good. Cutscenes are a tad weird because they're animated from scratch but is accompanied by the same audio recorded and mixed by Heavy Iron Studios from 2003, so not every lip and body movement is in sync with the audio. The multiplayer mode is a bit dull for my tastes but for a child it'll definitely keep them entertained.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lukewarm remaster of a decent platformer.Hopefully, the developers will look at this constructive criticism and tighten up areas of the game that I feel need some work.- Within the first hour of the game I noticed a few janky collisions. For example I tried jumping on a purple bouncing tree from a lower tree, and I feel like I should have landed the jump, but I am blocked by an invisible wall. I didn't even touch the purple tree. This kind of thing is very immersion breaking and unfair to the player. - The out of bounds are not defined enough. In Jellyfish fields there are lower platforms that look like they should be able to be landed on, in fact SpongeBob CAN land on them, however the floating hand takes you away the moment you do.- Dying in this game can range from annoying to outright frustrating. If you die, you re-spawn at a checkpoint that could be really far away from where you died. SpongeBob isn't as fast and mobile as other platforming mascots, and trekking through whole chunks of a level you've already ran through is nothing less than a chore. I was really hyped to play this today, and while the visual upgrades are incredible nearly across the board, the game's flaws need a lot of addressing before I can recommend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished 100%ing the game and can say I enjoyed this as much as I did back in the day, with the original. Game play wise, they didn't change much at all. Dialogue continues on past what shown in the text box. And in several cases, I found the wrong dialogue playing. Level boundaries aren't entirely clear, and while I think that's actually pretty neat, I've ended up getting hard stuck at various points. _childDocuments_.review: Spongebob squarepants battle for bikini bottom rehydrated. might just be my ideal game, and i do not say that lightly. I will describe my tastes and how BFBB:R fits them shortly. But first the preamble.As a remake of a classic early 2000's era 3D collect-a-thon platformer widely considered the best spongebob game BFBB:R has some rather large (and squeaky)shoes to fill. First off graphically this game looks amazing. The original did not look bad by any means, but with the remake the game has recieved a complete face lift. High defenition models, an increase in saturation and a huge increase in draw distance leaves BFBB:R an improvement across the board. However there some minor graphical issues that while small should not be ignored, such as spongebob losing his eyelashes periodically in cutscenes.Sound wise BFBB:R far as i can tell uses all of the original audio. For better or worse, be that ost. Character voices. Or enemy sounds. Which is great! But it does mean that voices they could not get for the original, such as the case for Mr Crabs. Will not have their official voice from the show here either. This will have varying degrees of importance to people but keep it in mind.Now for my tastes and how they apply to the game. Something i can tackle at my own pace. This is not a long game at all. Stages will take roughly 45 minutes to an hour to complete depending on your familiarity and completionism. The world is broken up into zones further broken up into 4 stages, with 8 golden spatulas(the main metric of progression) each. As well as a handful of various collectables. You can tackle these in roughly any order you want. Leaving and returning freely. Which you'll need to do as you unlock new abilities. Each zone branches off of a hub world taking the form of lower conch street. Containing small buildings such as spongebobs home. Each level has its own theme challenges and obsticals that prevent the gameplay from going stale. Be it the slides and time trials of sand mountain. The rooftop swinging of downtown bikini bottom. Or the goo lakes of goo lagoon.For the second criteria: progression.This is a simple one. By defeating bosses and unlocking additional areas of the hub world spongebob unlocks new abilities to aid in future and past levels. On top of this patric and sandy have their own abilities with levels requiring frequent switching, the need of which is handily choreographed by bus stops in the level and environmental itemsSpongebob is easily the most versitile. Equiped with a standard attack. An upwards jumping attack. A ground pound. A ranged bowling attack. And a remote controled cruise missile all under a cute bubble theme.Sandy is mobile equiped with her standard attack. The ability to swing and glide with her laso and able to instantly destroy larger robots and tiki's from a distance.Patric is strong. He gets a standard attack and a ground pound. But is also able to pick up tikis. fruits found in the environment. and robots stunned by his ground pound for use in combat and puzzle solving.All of this is taught gradually to the player with increased complexity further into the game allowing a simple but satisfying sense of progression.Finally the third: defined goals.This is a collect-a-thon. You have a defined checklist to fill out. Each level has a menu detailing its objectives and collectibles. What you have found and what you need to find. You know what completion entails and how close you are to achieving it. Most importantly this is a game that respects your time. Everything is achievable in a single run, and it wont be overly difficult to do so.BFBB:R is a short curated experience that actively takes steps to avoid overstaying its welcome. And to a degree understays its welcome. Had there been a couple more zones i dont think i would have complained. An easy 95/100 that i'd reccomend for fans of the show of all ages.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm probably part of a very small population of people that both A) like 3D platformers & B) never watched SpongeBob. The controls and physics are both fine, not among the best of platformers (most of which are indie at this point), the graphics are mostly okay, but there are inconsistencies, clipping, and gaps in the terrain that can be pretty noticeable. The level design varies from completely linear areas that are mostly fine, and more open/non-linear areas that can be pretty dull because of the low walk speed.I can continue like this, but it would be pretty redundant to just call everything "fine", so I'll stop here.

_childDocuments_.review: I never grew up with this game as a Child, I was just never a big enough SpongeBob SquarePants fan. While I enjoyed the show growing up SpongeBob just never hooked me to get really any of his games, so I never got to enjoy "Battle for Bikini Bottom" of "The Movie: The Game" which from what I understand are considered the best games based off of SpongeBob SquarePants. Now saying all this I wish that I had gotten this game as a kid, my younger self would have loved this game with a passion. if you are a fan of SpongeBob SquarePants or just a fan of collect-a-thon type games like "Banjo Kazooie" or "Conker's Bad Fur Day" then this game is a great way to relieve the good old days.Visually the game looks amazing, the graphics of the games make it look like it was a game made in recent times, and Purple Lamp Studios should feel proud of this, they went above and beyond with the looks of this remake. Gameplay wise this game plays fine, getting to play as 3 characters helps with keeping the game from going stale super fast. my major problem with gameplay is that while you get to play as 3 different characters, only SpongeBob gets upgrades, and while I get that he is the main character of the game I wish that Patrick, and Sandy got a least one new power up during the game, my other problem with the game is that after a while it dose start to get a little stale with combat, while SpongeBob gets 3 upgrades for the game, for the most part you usually use the power ups for hitting stuff that gets you through the world. The Audio of the game is really my last complaint with the game, while the graphics of the game got a major overhaul and the game looks brand new a lot of the audio sounds like it game from 2003, and for the most part its not a problem but there are two characters that if you are a fan of the show you will laugh at the fact that they are not voiced by there original voice actors from the TV show, which if they only showed up every now and then it wouldn't be that big of a problem, but for the most part they show up a lot in the game. I just feel like that if you are going to redo the graphics to the point of making it look like a new game, and as this game is being stated as a remake why not redo all of the audio.With all that, this game is still fantastic to play, while audio feels lazy, and gameplay can get a bit stale. its still a fun game that old and new fans of SpongeBob SquarePants will enjoy this game, and like I said if you have an itch for a collect-a-thon type game, I say this game is a good way to go, although maybe wait for a sale, I feel like $30 is a bit to much for a halfish remake game.Rating: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pure eye candy, nostalgia, and an absolute beautiful recreation of a classic. Jellyfish Fields looks lush, Goo Lagoon is bright and lively. The lighting is beautiful and makes levels that I loathed in the original favourites. Characters are now much more expressive in cutscenes and in mid-game dialogue. The cutscenes in the Mermalair are my absolute favourite in the game due to how hilarious they animated Mermaid Man. I do have my nitpicks here and there about some of choices made in the game; none game breaking. I'd prefer if the HUD and Pause Menu was more tuned to the classic game with the 3D models of the Shiny Objects and Spongebob's Underwear, Patrick's Socks, and that it used the Spongebob font. Then the textures for objects that can be Bubble Bashed and wall jumping are also different. Then there's the cardboard boxes and the out of bounds animations. Like I said I'm nitpicking and none of these things make or break the game for me.The only real problems I have with this game is the knockback from enemies and the environment. It's very extreme and has caused me to fall to my death several times. Sandy's swinging is also very uncontrollable and forces you to swing at mach speed.Then don't even get me started on the tedious multiplayer added. Sure it's cool that you can play as other characters aside from the original three but NONE of the characters have any voice lines in the multiplayer. If you're not playing with a friend on a voice call, you'd just sit in a virtual silence as the same bland music from the Rock Bottom level plays through out 26 islands. Then due to enemies' knockback set to max you get yeeted off the map if you're anywhere near the edge, instantly dying, anytime you get hit by them.The multiplayer aspect was extremely disappointing and I wish they would have just added in multiplayer for the campaign. THAT would have been way more interesting.Overall this game is still a masterpiece and I hope for more remakes from THQ Nordic in the future.EDIT: There is no option to return to SpongeBall credits level. Big Sad. When you enter Shady Shoals Spongebob comments on the game checkers, but there is no checkerboard. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: OverviewAs someone who played the original back in 2003 and spent well over 1000 hours in total playtime on the original I was hyped as hell when I heard the game was getting remastered and releasing on not just console but on PC as well. I have not played the game myself in at least 12 years but a lot of it remains fresh in memory and it is one of the few nostalgic games I have played that have retained its sense of enjoyment and replayability over the years. I was 8 when the game came out and I still feel like I can enjoy it to the same extent now as a 25 year old.ProsExtremely fun missions and Boss fights with well thought out mechanics (no changes at all there from the original) the game is well crafted and despite the fact I thought it would be horrible on PC I couldn't be more wrong, all of the controls are extremely well done and there is nothing there I can complain about.the game obviously isn't going to have an amazing in depth story but for the kind of game this is it does its job perfectly this game is about just down to earth dumb fun just as most of us expect from a Spongebob game.ConsStory so as I said before the Story is your typical dumb fun kids story it won't blow more mature players out of the water but in the end this shouldn't matter too much.So this hasn't happened to me as my experience thus far has been smooth sailing but some users are reporting out of sync audio in cutscenes though none of the ones I have seen said this applies to actual gameplay audio.Bits of Lag so some areas/actions can cause small bits of lag here and there but in general It has been relatively smooth sailing for me though one time when extending a ladder I thought my game might crash though it recovered real quickly.Overall Score 8/10If you love Spongebob this game is a must buy and has plenty of hours worth of playtime and is one of the few games I would say the game is worth another playthrough after completing.I have not tried the Multiplayer mode yet from what I heard it is kind of a let down but I expected this if you are coming here for Co-op unfortunately the Multiplayer is not a Co-op Campaign but is instead a Arena survival from what I heard, I will probably try it here and there but it was not the selling point for me or most of the Community from the original game transferring over to the rehydrated copy.

_childDocuments_.review: If you grew up loving the original game, you'll enjoy this remaster. The world looks incredible and I was always surprised and excited to see what they did to the next area. The gameplay is a little smoother in some areas and the charm and humor is still there! As far as remasters go, this is one executed fairly well. That being said some of the changes didn't make much sense to me. Some of the model changes looked like a downgrade, the one that bothered me most was the new look of the golden spatulas for example. Not bad by any means but the original looked far better. I also noticed models of other little details missing, such as Patrick's record player under his rock. I specifically remember hitting it as a kid and running around in circles while the tune played (ik, it was epic). These are little things but they're examples of some details I noticed. Some character models also looked more robotic in their animations. Nothing that horrible but I just have to question why some of these decisions were made.Another thing that caught my attention was the difficulty seemed easier in some of the more challenging parts from the original game. I'm not just saying this from my memory as a child, I've probably replayed the original half a dozen times over the years. Platforming sections I specifically recall having difficulties with were a cake walk and there were some changes to boss levels, such as labeled target areas and such. I'm not sure how I feel about it but I can see why they changed some things and I can overlook it. Overall this game is still fantastic for old fans and new! Give it a shot, the core game still feels timeless as a Spongebob fan. I can see myself replaying it in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this faithful remake of SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom. I played it back when I was younger, and since I had brief flashbacks I decided to get the original game. I had to get a PS2 from some shop online, but it was worth it. I wasn't able to complete the classic game, but playing this remake makes me nostalgic.I highly do recommend this faithful remake!

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent remake that brings back great memories of the original. As a huge fan of the original, I'm hoping this remaster will bring new fans to this classic game.Pros:Looks gorgeous (especially in dark levels like Jellyfish Caves, Kelp Forest, etc.)Level design nearly identical to the original (which was amazing)Good quality of life changes (such as the redesigned menu)Cons:Movement is a little clunky at timesSandy boss fight starts right away, which is kinda weirdNon-inverted look controls aren't default. Look controls are reset every time you switch characters (I'm sure it will be patched though)Some new content that was hinted at (such as Patrick's Dream) isn't in the final gameOverall, an amazing game. Thank you Purple Lamp Studios for showing love for the fans of this game. I know it was kind of a time crunch to develop this game, especially with the pandemic, but the creators did a fine job and gave the game the respect it deserved.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally had no interest whatsoever in this game but after a large number of my friends told me I had to try out this "God tier platformer game" from their childhood I decided why not. I've obviously never played the original so i don't have any sort of nostalgia for this game or even this franchise since I didn't really watch SpongeBob as a kid. I'm a completionist so as of writing this review I've 100%'ed the game and seen everything there is to it.In terms of gameplay it's a very solid yet simplistic platformer game where you can control up to 3 different characters all with unique abilities. The level/world structure is very nice and is rather fun to traverse through even though some worlds definitely stand out way more than others. There's not that many bosses in this game and honestly I was a bit disappointed by that since the ones we've got are quite bad. Out of the 6 or so bosses in the game only 1 of them felt interesting to fight. Unfortunately this game does have quite a lot of bugs as of right now but most of them have been patched.I was watching some gameplay of the original game and honestly the colors in the original looked extremely dull. I definitely think the remake's got a much brighter and happy feeling color scheme. It's a kid's game so the story really doesn't matter. Most of the dialogue in the game are just short one liners or introductions.While I do think the game's got a lot going for it, I just don't think it's a god tier platformer like so many claimed it to be. In my personal opinion it gets easily beat by other games such as Ratchet and Clank, Sly Cooper, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro and Jak and Daxter. With that being said though I still think it's a solid 8/10 game, I just wouldn't call it a god tier game.

_childDocuments_.review: As a trip down memory lane, this game is a faithful remake of the original, while the movement does feel different from the original. It may not hold up by today's standards for a AAA release, but for $30, whether you played the original or not, it is certainly worth the price. The graphics and sound are beautifully done, with fun easter eggs thrown in that weren't in the original, but don't change the gameplay or overall tone of the game. It's a fun, lighthearted action platformer with dated mechanics but as this faithful remake stands, I'd recommend it. Although  patches would be welcomed to fix some of the minor bugginess... like my entire screen going upside down in Rock Bottom??? It made me laugh though, and after I jumped into a pit and respawned it was fixed, so everything is good as far as I see it.

_childDocuments_.review: There has been a lot of discussion in the past few years a to what a remake is vs a remaster vs a re-imagining is supposed to be defined as has been a contentious topic. This game is A PERFECT DEFINITION OF A    R E M A S T E R. Almost everything you see in this game is simply a modernization of a beloved console game with some added content and some polish where need be. Almost everything you see in this game is EXACT same as the original. That being said, 17 years of foresight has allowed Purple Lamp to create the best possible version of this game without changing what this game is at it's core. For instance: adding the ability to hold LT/L2/whatever the left trigger is called to sneak has turned the level "Rock Bottom" from a frustrating broken mess of a level into one of the more fun and challenging levels in the game. It's obvious that Purple Lamp took immense care and attention to detail to make the most faithful, but improved versions of a beloved adn best collect-a-thons of all time.... also multiplayer exists but it doesn't detract from the experience so whatever.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game to play if you just wanna sit down and relax for a couple of hours but it can also be enjoyed all day.The main goal of the game is to collect enough spatula's to unlock all areas and finally to be able to fight the final boss. While I wouldn't consider the combat amazing or deep it gets the job done without being annoying. In this game you mainly play as Spongebob but in certain areas you can also play as either Patrick or Sandy. Out of these 3 characters Sandy has the most statisfying combat but all characters have just enough variation in their skillset so that combat does not feel monotonous.Aside from the vibrant colors of this game each area has its own unique aesthetic and the layout of the levels also differ greatly. This makes exploring the levels a blast and at no point did this game feel repetetive to me. The levels are designed in such a way that you really want to explore them and in the process you will collect extra spatualas so that backtracking shouldn't become an issue.This game also offers some environmental puzzles. The puzzles are not portal tier where you really have to put your brain to use but they are clever enough to not feel useless. Many of the puzzles also have some kind of quirky twist so you dont feel like you're doing the same puzzle over and over again. So in short I would say the puzzles are just right for this game and fit in very well with their environments.Before I end this review I especially want to shout out the "waterslide" sections in this game. There are more of them than I expected when I first started playing this and each slide felt unique and challenging in it's own way. These parts for me are without a doubt the standout moments of the game because they are just so damn fun. For platformer fans this really is a must play but I think almost everyone will be able to get enjoyment out of this game so I highly reccomend giving this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: To me, as a person who played the original countless times on the PS2 and later the GameCube, this damn near brought me to tears and took my breath away. With that in mind I want to say that if you've played the original, you should play this, period. Is it a perfect recreation? No, and why should it be? If you want to play the original game you can play the original, but this brings it to life very much in the same vein as Spyro and Crash remakes.Moving on from nostalgia, I'm going to critique the qualities of the game as fairly as I can, given my bias.I mean this as no offense to the other aspects of the game, but the visuals and presentation are all around the best part about the game. They're absolutely stunning and timeless, unlike the original which while cartoony has not aged well visually. The new animations, especially for dialogue, brings new life to the lines being spoken and often enhances the humor. For this PC version, it runs pretty well given I have an OK-at-best GPU - only using ~50% of my GTX 960, though crawling up pretty high sometimes. The only visual complaint I have is that sometimes destroyed objects such as tiki parts and robot parts and whatever kinda just dissapears instead of fading from existence. Some of the same issues as the original exist coincidentally, namely a few shots that are over or underexposed. When I first saw this game in action I pictured the game felt like a "typical unreal engine project" game, but the visuals and gameplay in action completely proved me wrong - which flows into my next point.The gameplay, while not completely polished, is pretty good. I want to make it clear that no, the game doesn't control as bad as it looked from the early gameplay footage - it plays pretty damn well. There are many subtle changes as well as many explicit ones. Firstly, the game handles fairly differently. It's not jarring, but it's just ever so slightly more rigid than the original. That's not to say it controls bad or that it's unresponsive, but it's just not as fluid and loose as the original. In its place, is much heavier and punchier movement. Every move is much faster and a lot snappier, moves can flow into each other in new ways and things like the Spongeball are much easier to get a handle for and control as a result.Small glitches here and there are acceptable and expected, and of course they're found here too sometimes. However, there is one thing about this game, glitch or whatever it is, that is very annoying: the camera. I love the original game, I'll say it over and over again - but the camera was very 2003. This camera, it's very 2003. Better, yes, there are more options including proper invertions and a smart camera and all, but it still gets ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up by the environment and objects sometimes. That be how it do.Now, I said it needed some polish, and it has mostly to do with environmental stuff. Again, the visuals, the geography, the levels are very well realized - it's just all those small things that add up, y'know? So short of making a comprehensive list of every little thing that annoyed me, I'll just list the more egregious ones that come to mind:Characters will repeat lines a leeetle bit too often. Especially for Spongebob in specific areas to which he will comment on, there's clearly a timer to make sure he doesn't repeat it too often, but no check to which Spongebob has actually exited and re-entered... I think.Things will tend to load into the level as if it was the first time it had. i.e., when you enter goo lagoon with all the lighttowers doing their thing, massive earrape. Same with gates, if you enter an area the gates will open again and I'm pretty sure each part of the gate makes the gate openning sounds so earrape.etc.Again, it just needs some polishing, everything else about the game is great.That describes the game as a whole: "great, but needs some polish". So I recommend the game, cautionarily for now presuming that it eventually does get polish work.... also, I hear murmurs of mods? Hmmm...

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gorgeous rehydrate of a game from my childhood, well I actually really wanted it but only got a used copy when I was a teen and it blew me awayNow I payed full price for this and it was really worth my time, the stages are beautiful the jokes still work and the Tunes are full of charm and perfectly embody the atmosphere of each stage.The game is a bit short lived but has some replay value, especially for younger players that maybe like me could just not get enough of the fun Hub World where you can visit the buildings of Bikini Bottom. The stages also visit iconic places from the show like Rock Bottom, the Kelp Forest or the Goo Lagoon, turning episodes of a show in fully blown stages with fun little references.The difficulty is well balanced I feel for anyone it should be a good mix of challenge and relaxation, the very final stage I found a bit of an unfun hardness to it but nothing crazy, its not even that long and gives a great conclusionAnyway if you or your kids like Spongebob this is a great buy even without the nostalgia criteria its a great platformer for fans of the genre :)

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst I immensely enjoyed this game (I never played it when I was younger and had only seen about half an hour playthrough), I can not in good faith recommend this to everyone. If you are well and able, feel free to pick up the game, however, if you have any form of disability, I don't recommend this game, there are no accessibility options other than subtitles. There's no colour blind assist, no button remapping, no difficulty adjustments, etc.For anyone who is able, I should also point out, that if you're an achievement hunter, or just like getting 100%, you may not be able to do so, I have collected every collectible, but due to a bug, I am stuck at 97%, this is not an uncommon bug.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:great music great original humour great fast travel system great controller support local and online play funny cut scenesgreat original voice acting( except mr crabs and mermaid man who are way off)plenty to collect and find and explore15-20 hours to 100% the gameCONS:too easybosses too easy and followed easy patternsmultiplayer online with friends onlycharacters all move too slowlya couple small glitches- my controller disconnected and the storyline's voices kept going without the video keeping up. cant tell where you can explore, or not, on some areasMr Krabs achievements are ridiculously grindy and take no skill. You can abuse the achievements by having multiple accounts, collect 90 golden spatulas on 1 account and 10 on another... ruins the fact that people have earned it.simple storyline done well, like spongebob has always been. really enjoying so far, has some great collect-a-thon stuff and challenges, included timed challenges and sliding crash bandicoot style runs. unique bosses, and characters. no penalty for deaths except back to checkpoint.EDIT: they fixed mr krabs acheivement!
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: THE NOSTALGIA!!! Big heads up though, I couldn't run this game the first time I installed it but after uninstalling and reinstalling the game, it didn't have even a hiccup after, hope that happens to you when you play but remember that steam has a refound option in case you can't work your own, now back to the gushing.I played this game back when I was in gradeschool, I bought this game because I wanted to experience the game again (with achievements) and I got exactly that, this game is almost unchanged besides a little visual glow up. _childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: The people behind Rehydrated obviously put a lot of hard work into it. The game is awesome, staying true to the original BFBB game, while also adding it's own twist into the gameplay, levels, and cutscenes. I would totally recommend getting the game if you've played the original. However I think most people will enjoy the game, regardless of if you have played the original. All in all great game.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, I didn't play the original so no nostalgia for me.That being said, I really enjoyed the game and 100% it in two sittings, didn't use any guides, it's a pretty easy game because while you may take damage here and there the game just throws health pickups at you left and right so except for the times where you miss a jump and fall down (which doesn't happen that often because the platforming is on the easier side) you don't really die. While this may sound like a bad thing the game didn't get boring once for me even after playing for hours so they did something right. Also this is a game for kids after all so expecting some hardcore difficulty would be dumb. Sometimes the camera glitches through the floor for a split second if it collides with some walls but it's a rare thing and doesn't hinder gameplay.You should play this if:-you like Spongebob.-you like collectathons.-you like simple but fun platforming.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming remaster of a collect-a-thon I played when I was little.  Checkpoints are plentiful through majority of the game and the fact you can teleport to every collectible challenge once you discover it makes backtracking for 100% completion a breeze. Visuals are very cute, looks like Spongebob; I like the soundtrack too. There's a couple of difficult segments where you'll be aching for a checkpoint towards the end of the game, but every time you encounter a spot like that you'll only have to go through it once due to being able to teleport.Had a lot of fun playing this!Unfortunately, Spongebob moves slightly forward when charging up his Bubble Bowl move, rendering it literally unplayable.2/10
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: From a person who played the original as a kid, I am glad to say it is an amazing adaption. The gameplay is slick, entertaining and the level design is almost always on point. The visuals of this game are the main selling point; they are brighter, more colourful and vibrant than before. The music is catchy and a joy to listen to with all the cast voicing their characters; however, Clancy Brown still is not voicing Mr Krabs, which I will admit is a little disappointing. Same goes for Squidward and barnacle boy. It's sad but I can look over this.While maybe not a perfect game overall, it is a perfect Spongebob game.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom – Rehydrated is a remastered version of the classic 2003 platform game, capturing the humor and charm of the beloved animated series. In the game, players control SpongeBob, Patrick, and Sandy as they try to save Bikini Bottom from a robotic invasion masterminded by Plankton.The remaster brings significant visual improvements, offering a vibrant, detailed look that feels like a 3D version of the cartoon itself. The sound design, featuring iconic character voices and energetic sound effects, effectively enhances the gameplay experience and brings the underwater world to life.The game delivers classic platforming mechanics, blending item-collecting and combat elements. Each character has unique abilities such as Sandy's lasso-gliding that keep the gameplay fresh, though some levels may feel repetitive.Battle for Bikini Bottom – Rehydrated is a nostalgic return to a classic that appeals to both fans of SpongeBob and younger players. While the mechanics may feel somewhat dated for today’s gamers, the colorful world, lighthearted humor, and simple yet enjoyable gameplay make this a recommended pick for anyone looking for a fun, casual adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: Great early/mid 2000s styled platformer. This game really hit the spot. Lots to collect, explore, fight, and interact with. The visuals are up to date, and more in line with the current look of the show, and there's even new little easter eggs thrown in for good measure. Know those in-between poses that became memes? They included some of those as simple idle animations. Something I thought was a nice touch. The game even offers an optional challenge in 100%ing the game, but allows you to reach the games storyline conclusion if you wish to just experience that. It's not without faults, the occasional glitch rears it's ugly head, and the completion achievements are glitched currently, which takes an exploit to achieve. Overall, this didn't bother my main experience. I always had fun, got some good laughs, and my moneys worth.Multiplayer, an isometric platforming horde where the goal is to defeat robo squidward by stepping on switches. It's surprisingly fun, a bit hard to control at first though. Has options for online, local, and remote play. Now the online games have not been too hot, but the game excels at being a great local co-op experience. I wish there was an option to play the level by myself, but my nephew and I had a great time.Overall, if you like platformers in the vein of Mario 64, you're gonna have a good time. If you like Spongebob, you're gonna have a good time. None of the above? Maybe not so much.EDIT: I nominated this game for The Sit Back and Relax Award, it's a very chill game. Very easy 40 hours for me.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: This review is sort of biased, as I played it back when it came out on the PS2, but I remember playing and replaying the original all the way up through high school, and it was always a blast. My only complaints are things they didn't fix from the original such as the missing voice actors, that sometimes the game is just too darn bright with the new graphics, and they changed the animation and sound from the teleport boxes (it just sounds wrong to me). I would Highly recommend checking this game out.

_childDocuments_.review: Ideally, a remake should strive to be the superior way to play a game. This is very not that. There's a lot of mechanics missing,  level design choices that are necessary that were forgotten about. There's a lot of bugs and glitches that make the game less fun than the original and more frustrating. I loved this game as a kid, played it constantly after I got my gamecube when I was about 4 or 5. The graphics for this are good, there's a lot here graphic-wise that they do better than the original. But otherwise this feels like it was slapped together in Unity by someone who was making a game for the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such an underrated gem. Fun gameplay, great soundtrack, and somewhat challenging at times. I achieved 100% completion after just over 8 hours. But honestly that's because I know the ins and outs of this game from playing it so much over the years, since its original release back in 2003 on the OG Xbox, GC, and PS2. If you like platformers or collect-a-thons like Psychonauts or A Hat in Time, then you'll adore this game.     As far as performance is concerned, I had maybe 1 frame drop below 75fps for a second or two in the Kelp Forest. Im on an RTX 2070. The game runs near flawlessly and is a visual treat. A chill experience through and through. And even if it's not your thing, it's still leagues better than The Last of Us 2.     An easy 10/10 in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: From playing through the game I found it to be generally good As it has a very nice updated cartoony art style and is a all around good platforming and collecting game. I played the original when I was younger and used to love it. However there are many minor bugs and glitches throughout the remaster, though none of them have too much of an effect on the game and none appear to be game breaking. It also appears to be very easy to clip out of bounds in many locations throughout the game, especially as Sandy. All mouse controls also appear to be quite unreliable and unresponsive sometimes as attacking and attempting to use the characters abilities which require right mouse clicks sometimes becomes very difficult or even impossible at times.The only major glitch I encountered is that the achievements for gathering all the spatulas and for gaining 100% completion haven't unlocked despite gathering everything throughout the game. Which I believe means if I wanted those achievements I would have to go through the entire game again from the start to be able to unlock them.Overall however I would recommend the game and would say the game as being very good and a solid recreation of the original PS2 classic. I'd give it a 7.5/10. The only advice I would give to anyone picking up the game and playing through it is whenever you enter into a new area or sub area make sure to check the entrance for any nearby boxes as some of them do not open when loading into the new area as you do not spawn close enough to them for them to activate. And travelling back to the start of some areas to leave can be very annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: This is all around just an incredible time. It's a great remake of an old school classic that showed that not all video game tie-ins had to be bad. _childDocuments_.review: Can recommend this game only to young kids. The main campaign mode is not too bad, it can be completed in less than 2 hours and it's easy enough even for young kids. All dialogues are voiced, so kids don't need to know how to read to play. Although there are many instructions in the game that require ability to read, but kids will be able to figure it out also without reading all the signs.The game looks outdated (graphics, sounds, gameplay). There's a bug where occasionally SpongeBob gets stuck between objects and can't move away, in this case reload the game. The Co-Op unfortunately is a disaster. It is just an endurance mini-game (my kids stopped at island 20 because they bored), where you have to smash as many enemies as possible. Without special moves, rewards or any other new mechanics to make it interesting or worth spending time on it.Overall i think this game is worth at most 10$ (current price with the discount), there are much better games for kids in the 30-40$ range.Final verdict: buy on sale, avoid at full price

_childDocuments_.review: This version is a great recreation/remake of the original game from 2003, thus it keeps a lot of design elements and gameplay style from that game. Honestly, it just feels too slow nowadays and some bugs that are still in the game can ruin the experience especially for 100% completion. Overall, a good game which I can recommend, but if you are not a fan of the original game/show, it might not live up to your expectations.
