_childDocuments_.review: ARE YA READY KIDS?!?There aren't many expectations for a licensed game. Its rare to even see a re-release of one that was even good in the first place. BFBB was a beloved 3D platformer that was made popular by some fun gameplay, decent writing and some great voice acting from the original cast of the show (most of them). It was a fun collect-athon 3D platformer with linear but fun levels. So how well does it hold up? And what about the remaster?To put it simply: both work out really well but set your expectations for the remaster. The controls and are still fluid, the new character animations for dialogue interactions absolutely blow out the original. Conversations and interactions are just animated better, the jokes in general just flow more naturally. Some characters have lacking lip-sync but they're still expressive and fun. The environments also stand out. The draw distance has been increased and some of the texture work is outstanding. Jellyfish fields has a great color palette. Gone is the terrible color balance and brightness from the early previews. Gone is the very flat look the original game had at times with its basic CG. Instead of doing some crappy cell-shaded abomination, Purple Lamp Studios opted to make something stand-out. While Sand Mountain leave much to be desired with its poor blue haze effect in its environment, places like Goo Lagoon really shine and show off some great talent that doesn't poop on the original.The core gameplay is still good. Moving, jumping, finding Golden Spatulas, switching between the 3 playable characters (Spongebob, Patrick, Sandy). It's all there and still a joy. Enemy variety is solid, the game features its share of boss fights that are still fun. Not to mention all the cutscenes and gags.Let's start with the marketing from the store page "Restored content that was cut from the original game like the Robo Squidward boss fight and more". Now if you carefully sift through press releases and interviews you'll find that this is cutting room floor content that was shoved into the multiplayer. None of this stuff is in the single player like we expected. Worse, the multiplayer itself is terrible. All the characters play the same, there's little variety in just fighting the same waves of enemies with bare-bones platforming and level design. All you do is fight robots that spawn from a robo-squidward model. You don't even fight the boss itself. What? That isn't even a boss fight. That's a "subordinate fight". The Patrick's Dream level that was cut from the original but was still totally possible to add in the game because there still was a Golden Spatula? It's not here, it's just a bunch of assets that were going to be used as platforms that were themed like candy and ice cream, chopped up and re-purposed as an island of platforms in the boring multiplayer. You're walking on them for maybe a few minutes.That is completely up-acceptable. Almost as un-acceptable as all the bugs this game mysteriously has. Now when I did my original video I didn't notice too many but now I'm starting to notice progression-halting bugs and bugs that aren't fixing on restarts. I can't progress through the Mermalair or re-fight Robo Sandy at this current time.Let's briefly mention the QoL features before we wrap it up. One of the cool things about the original as I've already mentioned was the dialogue and boss fights. You could fight the 3 robot bosses in the game at any time but you could not re-fight side-bosses that would appear at the end of a level. King Jelly Fish, Prawn, you just can't redo the fights or even re-watch the cutscenes. There isn't even an audio archive (that I could fine) of all the dialogue to re-watch. And because there are only 3 save slots I gotta replay the whole game or just try to find what I'm looking for on Youtube. Never mind the fact that I have to start over from an early save if I want to fight some of the bosses. Extremely disappointing.I should briefly mention that the voice actor for Mermaid Man passed away and never had any work done for the original. Clancy Brown still isn't in the game doing Mr. Krabs either, due to a union disagreement. Basically, if they got Mr. Krab's voice actor to do lines, everyone would have to be compensated to do new lines. Which is completely ridiculous to me. The original voice acting was great and they shouldn't have to change everything on a budget title to get one voice changed. It feels like a cash grab despite some good effort from the developers. I can totally see why some critics are giving this a 6, 5, or even a 4/10 because there are lot of things under cooked with this release. It doesn't deserve a 2/10 though, that Gamespot reviewer is a moron from what I've gathered. For all its flaws, its still the original with a really nice new coat of paint. I have no doubt the bugs will be fixed after launch. It doesn't feel so much like a wasted opportunity but the misleading marketing does not help that. If you've never played the original but are a fan of the show, wait for a patch. If you enjoyed the original and expect nothing to change except for the visuals, it's still a fun game and some of the small improvements are a nice touch. If you're expecting a bunch of extra content, I'd probably pass on picking the game up at launch. It helps that the game is still fun even after all these years and that's one of the reasons I can recommend it.Thank you for reading! If you want some more info, I linked the multiplayer review (5 minutes) above and I made a separate video below regarding my first impressions.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: My usual stance on remakes stands especially true with this remake on BFBB. The original release is one of my all-time favorite games, and just a really strong platformer. It became a cult classic, and in the modern wake of constant remakes, it was a nice surprise that this was made.However, as with most remakes, it has its pros and cons. My main issue is, ironically, the graphics. There is something phenomenal about the older, grayer look of the original game. Rehydrated almost goes too overboard with the colors, as if someone cranked the saturation to 200%. The newer models ironically have less character to them; Purple Lamp are clearly basing them off of the newer seasons of the show.Weird details like the physics have been messed with. Everything from the Bubble Bowl, to the Spongeball, to the weighted platforms all feel strange compared to the OG game. The Bubble Bowl gets caught on geometry, making it far less accurate. The Spongeball/throwing Throwfruit/Sandy’s lasso have a lock-on now, making them less skill-based. The weighted platforms seem to be based on framerate, as they work way less often on the chuggy Switch version of the game (hilariously the mobile version runs better, it even has graphics quality options). And the magnetization of items seems to be stronger, as items are easier to pick up. This defeats the purpose of some platforming, especially collecting the steering wheels Downtown.And dear goodness, I hate how the new Sand Mountain looks. I get wanting to make it actually look like sand over snow, but it makes the level much uglier/way less charming. Smaller complaints are no/wierd animations like the Teleport Box, bus, and giant hand. Then there are the few things that were left unchanged that should have been! Like why would you not get Clancy Brown to come back and rerecord the Mr. Krabs lines? I’m sure that’s a contractual thing but still...Anyway, I’m glad this game is now much more accessible. But as someone who has played the original for likely hundred of hours, it is impossible not to notice these small details.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it! A good remake of the original game with enough mechanical changes to feel fresh. If you're a hardcore speedrunner of the original BFBB, this might not be what you had in mind, but if you're a fan of the original or just want a good, collect-a-thon, PS2-era game with the 2020 visual upgrade, this game is perfect. Also, Dutchman's Graveyard has the best soundtrack, but in general the soundtrack is solid!
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still of the opinion the movie game would have been a choice, but BFBB was a solid platformer and still is. The remake is crisp, runs well, and it's a good little time waster. If you miss old school 3D Platformers, this is one of them. But how much you'll enjoy this might depend on how much patience you have for Spongebob Squarepants.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine having worse physics than a PS2 game.Bubble bowling goes through some platformsSandy's lasso swinging is now a 100% canned animation where as it's freeform physics swinging in the original Also it un-inverts my controls every character switch.Edit:  Since so many consumer nostalgic-baited people gave this game amazing reviews, maybe I should point out more crappy things about this game! I'll update this as I see more downgrades and bugs.  This is the full list:--Like fighting robots?  G-Loves now CANNOT be killed with basic attacks, even when stunned.   --STILL like fighting robots?  Tar-Tars can now fire on you within a frame of hitting them. Oh, and they have no attack windup either.  Have fun taking random damage.--Like lasso swinging segments?   Well, goodbye physics!  Enjoy the fun-draining downgrade.--Like inverted controls?  Well, too bad! Every character switch un-inverts them.--Like platforming? Well, Too bad!  The "teeter-totter" platforms basically stick you to them.  You are working against the physics system to jump as early as Jellyfish Fields.--Like throwing fruits?  Now they have physics and roll away! ...But only sometimes.--Like sliding levels?  Now your camera jerks around as you change direction.  Goodbye, Sand mountain, you now make me want to spew!  --Like fun?   Go play the original.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, you can't play the campaign in co-op - there's just a 30 minute long arcade basher. The campaign itself I cannot comment much on, as the "checkpoint" system is frustrating, like every time you go out of bounds you don't respawn in the nearest place, bu you start from the last save and when you combine it with wonky controls and bugs, it's just not enjoyable anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: I really like Spongebob but the game is just extremely okay. Some areas look awesome, but the characters seem kind of lifeless in this. It also feels like the movement is much slower than I would have liked compared to other 3D collectathon platformers like it. Some enemies and challenges run unnecessarily slow, to the point where most of your time is either waiting for an event to finish so you can act upon it at the correct time, or waiting for your slow character to traverse the map. The soundtrack and vox is occasionally cool but rather boring/repetitive and obnoxious at times, especially with characters repeating their dialogue often during gameplay. Some interesting use of character movesets and the collectathon format (the way the surfboarding is programmed in this is actually pretty great), I can understand how Spongebob fans would have picked this up and appreciated it nostalgically speaking.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle of Bikini Bottom so I can't judge how the remake holds "the standards". This game however is really well made and it's not horrible like many of other games that are based from cartoons. The platformer side is solid and sometimes even challenging, especially the dream level, and it shows the effort from the developers into creating a modern and refreshed experience of the original game.It has lots of references and puns from the show and has a very clear story line. The graphics is a 9/10 for the genre, every level is colourful and alive, there are some bugs here and there but they are on remote parts of the levels and you can encounter them only if you are searching for weird spots for socks and spatulas.I cannot recommend this game enough, it's a fun and casual experience that you can enjoy on your couch.

_childDocuments_.review: Great new graphics yet the same experience as i play the original game from PlayStation 2. The Rehydrated has an improvement player control and also remastered music. A bit disappointed for me because there's no new level (i thought they put the Patrick's dream level from the original beta). This game also had a short game play time, i achieved 100% for like 18 hours or so. The online multiplayer isn't bad, i hope they updating more new levels, and fix the server because sometimes i get "internet connection lost" notification even though i got a good internet connection.Nevertheless, i still enjoy every second i play this game, it bring back the memories from my childhood 'cause this game has a piece of a place in my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I wanted to like this game, but I just can't. It's plagued by a lot of issues. Janky controls, broken hit detection, level design that ranges from mediocre to bad (Spongebob's Dream is the worst offender, literally a straight corridor with very awful platforming, at least one broken Golden Spatula, and terrible enemy placement).For fans of the show, the pacing and dialogue isn't great either. You're thrown in the middle of boss arenas with no real introduction, reason or coherence. One moment you'r in bikini bottom, the next you're in a ring fighting a giant robot with like 0 transition. It feels very..cheap? I don't know, it feels wrong and stringed together hastily.And last, what I'd consider the worst offender, the 100% reward and process of getting it. The game requires you to collect a TON of it's currency (shiny objects) to get every collectible in the game. Most normal players would consider that a post game thing, right? Well, if you do it post game, you'll miss out on the 100% ending, as there's no way to fight the final boss. On top of that, the process is tedious as hell. Not to mention, the game actively makes you waste 30 minutes to farm those shiny objects, since it gives you so few while playing the game normally. I had to spend like 45 minutes farming somewhere around 50.000 of them just to get 100%. Ridiculous.Overall, I just don't recommend this game. Even if you're a huge fan of Spongebob, you're better off sticking with the show. The game feels like random moments of the show (not necessarily good or funny ones) strung together very poorly. It's not worth the time investment or the price.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: I was very surprised by the low quality of this game. Apart from all the bugs, like out of sync audio, black screens, soft locks... The gameplay and content is also severely lacking. Hearing the same voicelines 20x everytime I do a specific task/action gets frustrating very fast. The combat is extremely basic and not really fun. The level design is often awful; going back and forth to constantly change a character to do a menial task only that specific character can do, just to go back and change to the other character and repeat the process again... The graphics are pretty bad but it's not that noticable with the cartoonish design. The characters and character animation are decent and probably the best part of the game. I got this game in a bundle and was intrigued by the positive reviews. The 30€ price is nowhere near what this game is worth. I would only ever consider this game if you are an big fan of Spongebob and don't mind playing a bad game.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Good visuals/animations/graphics compared to original game. The old game however still has some charm making this not too much of an upgrade.-Controls are not too complicated and can easily be picked up-Music and Audio Quality sounds just as well as the PS2 version if not betterCons:-Glitchy. There are some physics items that you rarely come across that can catapult you just by standing on them while they move (Balls or Buoy in Goo Lagoon). -In most cases when you fall out of bounds (not falling into goo) it just cuts to black screen and reloads a checkpoint. The only time you get Hans the hand is if you walk out of bounds in the level select area. While nothing big it also takes you out of the experience a bit considering the sudden cut and reload.-When using cardboard boxes you don't get the box closing and then showing it shuffling around like in the PS2 version. It cuts to black and loads the new area. While nothing big it also takes you out of the experience a bit.-Some actions feel slower or just more sluggish. It might be either rose tinted glasses or things like the bubble torpedo were slowed down a bitTake it as you will:-Everything is practically the same. The songs are not redone in any meaningful way and neither are the levels/plot/puzzles. Good if you wanna be nostalgic but you are just buying a pretty version of the original.-Not all characters are voiced by their actual voice actors.-There are memes in this game including a dabbing fish-I had unlocked 100% achievement/all spatulas/all socks before I actually got all socks/spatulas. It happened on the last few collectibles so it didn't really matter much. More of a glitch used on cutting down on grinding/searching.-Any glitches seem to be either benefiting the player (unlocking achievements early and skipping to the any stage), require intentionally performing them, or are so spread out that it doesn't matter in the long run.In summary:Good game for those who have or have not played the original. Those who have played the original will notice differences but its more of the flavor of the game than the actual gameplay/audio itself. While it is somewhat buggy it is not Fallout 76 bad and can be played and completed normally without too much interference. Bear it mind, this game is a kids game and thus will not be too complex and will be taking on the current aesthetic of the show than the first few seasons'.Also IGN and Gamespot have no idea what they are talking about.

_childDocuments_.review: A graphic remaster of a cult classic, Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated brings back the classic game design first made great by Heavy Iron Studios.For reference, I grew up playing the original in 2003, with well over 500 hours in the original. The game's replayability has not faded in that time. With SpongeBob, Patrick, and Sandy all playable in the single player mode, the game's main story offers reward for platforming skill and thorough exploration. Multiplayer offers a fun take on horde-style gameplay featuring several new playable characters and the arrival of Robo-Squidward (who was only previously featured in the GBA version).Pros:Classic game given new life graphicallyIntuitive and accessible controlsVariety of level types and gameplay features (time trials, platforming, beat-em-up, etc)Cons:Infrequent lighting glitches when close to wall-objects and surface cornersEnemies can sometimes glitch and not be defeated (minor enemies only), but they become obstacles and don't attack either (Glitch only experienced as Patrick thus far)TL;DR - If you want the best licensed game based on a cartoon, and a colorful experience accessible to all ages, BFBB Rehydrated is an excellent choice.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very Faithful Re-creation of the original. 8/10  1.Presentation : The graphics are great, the voice acting for the most part is great (looking at you Mister Crabs),and sound tract is good.    2.Story: It's like a very long form episode made for the game.if you love classic Sponge Bob seasons you will enjoy it.Basic plot: Plankton has made robots to get the secret formula, it back fires on him and the Robots take over the town It's up to Sponge bob and his friends to stop the Robots.Most of the jokes land and will make you chuckle.                  3 Game play: The game is enjoyable. It's genera is a Platfomer collectifon game.. You grab golden spatulas to unlock other levels. you have side objectives like getting shinny object to mister crabs and Patrick lost sock collection.This game genera is known for back exploring and back tracking. Don't be ashamed looking at a guide. there are many robots in the game they always introduce more of them so it dons't get repetitive. you need to have different attacks to defeat them       Sponge Bob out of the three characters has the most abilities in the game.he has his spinning attack, a bubble bowling attack, an upper cut attack, a ground slam attack, and a long range bubble missile attack.Prick and Sandy while enjoyable are not as fleshed out as Sponge Bob. Patrick is of course the Big strong one of the group. (What where you expecting, Solid Snake?) He can grab items heavy objects to progress though the levels.His attacks are a belly slam, a belly flop that stuns enemies and can throw stunned enemies. Sandy is more of a Platform heavy character. using a her lasso to hang on to "hooks" in the levels. Her attacks are a karate chop and her lasso that has a range attack.      My recommendations is a to make another save file. i have come across a weird bug that makes a Golden spatula disappear and sandy not being able to sneak one of the robots. other than that not a lot of bugs.    Never played the Multiplayer   This game is a good example of how to Do a remake

_childDocuments_.review: If you don’t have a really good PC, get this on PS4 or Xbox One; this port of the game isn’t good. There was so much lag the entire time I was playing, the goo in Jellyfish Fields was white, there was a lot of pop in, and the audio for the opening cutscenes was out of sync. These probably wouldn’t be so much of a problem if the game allowed you to lower the graphical settings but you can’t and I think they’re set cranked up. That’s the big deal breaker here. Not allowing those with a less powerful pc to have a decent experience. You basically have to go into the game’s files to change this stuff. This is a great game but a really bad port of it. Again, it your pc is great, then you should have a good experience. But if you don’t, then stick to a console version.

_childDocuments_.review: I rented the original game from Blockbuster as a kid, and barely reached the first checkpoint in Jellyfish Fields, so my impressions of this game should match those of a fresh player. While nothing's perfect, I thought this was fantastic! Despite using a big commercial game engine like Unreal 4, it has that strange harmony of polish and exploitability, that just screams "sixth-gen." There's a few skips and cool routes to be found, and all kinds of silly unintended stuff that does not negatively impact playability.  My only complaint is the same as for every good platformer: It felt short, I wish there was still more to do, beyond some of Patrick's lost socks.While they obviously include valid criticisms, critic reviews of this game seem to miss the intent of the remaster, and dock it points for ridiculous, arbitrary reasons. The player reviews here show a pretty stark contrast. We did not give it a 2/10, just because we were too impatient to learn the Bubble Bowl.

_childDocuments_.review: BATTLE FOR BIKINI BOTTOM - REHYDRATED:Rating: 8/10This is definitely one of the best remakes of a game. It stays faithful to the original while modernizing pretty much everything. It's a decent platformer game, but an awesome video game adaptation. I had a blast at some parts, while other parts of the game I'm talking to you, golden spatula collecting), were honestly just a bore and painful at times. If you are a SpongeBob fan, this is a 100% recommendation. If not, watch the show, and then if you like it, buy this game.Achievements: Most of the achievements aren't bad. They are straightforward, and most of them you will achieve if you are thorough when trying to beat the game for the first time. What is bad, however, is getting all the spatulas and socks. A couple of them are very difficult to find, and I had to honestly look up a few. I wish there could be a way to maybe get a hint or a closer view on the final few collectables, but oh well.

_childDocuments_.review: While I do recommend this game simply for the nostalgia factor, I will not lie that this "remaster" left me a little disappointed. The visuals have been updated to look very clean and there are some extras added into the game (nothing ground-breaking though). What really disappointed me was THQ's failure to fix features such as mismatching subtitled audio, grammar mistakes and other minor issues such as glitches (a popular one I had was getting stuck in objects and continually falling downward as if I was in a forever jump). While the glitches are easily solved by taxi-ing out of the area, I feel like there could have been way more polish put into this project, it just feels very lazed in some portions, and it shows.Also, the multiplayer, I could never find a multiplayer lobby, so if you want to test those features, you'll need to get some friends together. All-in-all, definitely worth the $10 for the disk version I bought at Walmart. A must-have for Spongebob fans, though if you still have a copy of the original PS2 version, it may be worthwhile to just wait for a sale or until you can find a deal like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of F.U.N! Only bug I've encountered is my camera settings changing when switching characters, very minor. Performance is fantastic. Low CPU usage on a 8750h, consistent frame-times, and my 1060 has maxed at ~60% utilization at 1080 60hz (mostly Goo Lagoon), with it generally much lower than that everywhere else. No graphical settings can be changed other than resolution and vsync, which is fine for me. Can't turn off depth of field, but there's no motion blur.Some nice quality of life improvements such as being able to lasso in the air as Sandy and attack in the air as Patrick are very welcomed. The only significant gameplay problem so far are the bungee jumps; very janky with camera and controls. Other stuff such as detailed animations and cutscenes have been great.Great game to just relax with! Nothing crazy, just collect stuff and defeat robots. If you played the original, this game won't be 'new'. I'm a bit biased since I grew up with the original and loved it very much. Some people may call these games average or mediocre, which I can understand, but is also misleading. I think the significance though is that these games (original and remake) don't do anything bad. Dialogue is humorous, level designs are fun and explorative, music is bangin, platforming is rewarding for all three characters. For myself, this makes this game absolutely amazing!

_childDocuments_.review: I was recommended this video game to play as my fiancée first played this when it was first released and loved it. As someone who hasn't actually played the original (insert gasps here), I think it's a wonderfully bright and fresh game with chirpy music and a fun and simple plot. The buttons are easy to learn, there's enough challenge for completionists to attempt, and even though Mr. Krabs' voice really grinds my gears, everything is bundled together real nicely. I've had a couple of little bug issues (I know a certain YouTuber influenced the game's production to keep it as close to the original as possible) such as falling through the floor and collision errors, but the game still runs very well, and the graphics are really really good. Overall I'm loving this game, and I'm looking forward to achieving a 100% on it. Money well spent, definitely.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - Amazing visuals. - Fun platforming. - Great voice acting, feels like you're in an actual Spongebob episode. - Music is great as well, very upbeat and light-hearted. - Feelings of nostalgia abounds.Cons: - Somewhat buggy in certain instances (Teleporting to Spongebob's house while Patrick and watching the TV results in Patrick going through Spongebob's dialogue, etc). - Objectives can be somewhat vague and you might wander around a bit if you haven't played the original. - The camera is a bit too free-form, you can practically see your insides if you so much as get close enough to a slightly larger rock than yourself and turning the camera. - A bit basic of a platformer, so may not give much enjoyment if you're looking for a challenge and don't have nostalgic feelings towards the game.Having not played the original game, I was interested in trying this for myself rather than watching some gameplay. And as a result, I find myself wondering if the original had some of these same problems (More like nitpicks, really).

It’s not winning any narrative awards, but the story is a serviceable enough excuse to explore Bikini Bottom, complete tasks, fight enemies and tell (some bad and some good) jokes. For a game like this, that’s all you needThink Super Mario 64 but with SpongeBob characters and locations. The first 2/3 of the game is really good fun but the last levels got some really big problems with the jumping mechanic and level designs. _childDocuments_.review: Save Bikini Bottom from rampaging robots created by Plankton. Clear through the fields of Jellyfish Field, sandy dunes of Sandy Mountains, and the depths of Rock Bottom. Fight Jellyfish King, giant robots, and Flying Dutchman. Circle between Spongebob, Patrick, and Sandy to clear each stage using each of their unique abilities.+ Detailed tutorial+ High quality graphics+ Interesting Plot+ Unique abilities for each charactersx Remaster onlyA great title finally remastered for PC. Have played this game in my PS2 and now the title is coming to PC. There's not a single difference between the PC and PS2 version, only some details are changed to make it fit better in the game, like tar-tar bottles model. The game itself has an interesting story. I find this game has ideal length, not too short but not too stretched. The bosses and spawns are pretty well balanced, not too hard but not easy enough. I'd say this game did better compared to any other platformer available in the market. I gave this game a 8.75/10 because of the sale, for the full price I rated it 7.25/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Super beautiful remake of one of my favorite combat platformers ever. They've really pumped out as much new detail as they can into every level without being unfaithful to the original. Gameplay is also solid, and a bit more refined than the original. Which is a good thing 99% of the time. Though some projectile enemies have been made too easy with slower attacks and less agro from a distance. This is most likely to fix a lot of situations in the original game that often would very easily screw the player. So its more of an improvement than anything else.It does also need some tweaks like an option to remove or reduce fog in Sand Mountain. I don't know why that was done. Its the only level that looks worse than the original as a result .Alternative anti-aliasing options would also be nice to get a less blurry image than from FXAA. Otherwise looks and runs great.

_childDocuments_.review: This rejuvenation of a classic is my first encounter with Battle for Bikini Bottom. Assuming no gameplay was changed in the process of releasing the game again, I found it fell quite a bit short of the variety, length & challenge in the Spongebob Movie game. This is about what I expected, as that game released after BFBB, using the same engine, assets & gameplay, and evidently the team had a better idea of how to build upon the first game's strengths. However, second place is still worthy of celebration. This is a fantastic game. As a remaster, Rehydrated itself bears minimal bugs, and is polished to a mirror sheen.All additions made in the follow-up game were for the better and I often found myself missing them, save for the semi-open world unique to BfBB, which charmed me enough that I wholeheartedly recommend getting this game regardless. I'd recommend holding out for a sale, since in the end, Rehydrated is just a slightly prettier version of a game from 2003.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: I don't NOT want to recommend this game. I think if you really liked the original, this is a fun little throwback. But if anything, playing through it just made me want to pull out my PS2 and play the original. Doing so just made me quickly affirm the issues I had with this game.As a standalone game, it's acceptable. As a remake of the original, it really misses the mark on so many notes. The game has a lot of graphical and mechanical bugs (I don't have the 100% achievement unlocked despite collecting literally everything in the game.) And I even feel the visuals (aside from maybe Jellyfish fields and Kelp Forest) don't look quite as good in some areas as they did in the original. That may be subjective, but areas like Goo Lagoon I found to be overly bright in contrast to the more warm colors that the original provided. Having messed about with the original for a bit after playing this one, the controls in this one aren't  exactly bad, but they're clearly quite different, for better or worse. I found the sliding controls here a little better than the original, but movement through the worlds in general didn't feel as smooth.With all the bugs that are still present even after the day 1 patch, I'm thinking it might be best to wait on this one. It's still by all means, a great looking game, and it isn't even a bad game at that. I just feel in terms of the "remaster" treatment- this one misses the mark. Perhaps with the Crash and Spyro remasters the bar was really raised, and it's pretty evident this wasn't on the same level of budget, thus making it feel rushed in some areas. Buy at your own risk. Haven't played the multiplayer mode yet, heard it wasn't too great but I think it's cool they went the extra effort to add a mode that was canned in the original.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this when I was younger and love spongebob and, for the most part, i think this is a good remake. The updated graphics and audio really make playing the game bright and fun and brings me back to the bright fun I had watching spongebob as a kid. Most of the animations are also updated and seem fun. Facial animations are good too. The graphics are really good although they could be better. Colors bleed a little too much and theres no Anti-Aliasing, which leads to sharp edges and resolutions looking lower quality than they should. To me that stuff should be standard in a game.My main complaints would be that a few parts feel low effort. Certain events have minor animation bugs/differences. Like sometimes if you take damage a certain way you wont get a death animation. Theres no TP box animation anymore. In Downtown the animation for the falling floors was removed. Enemies almost seem to just appear instead of coming from the machines. Little stuff that it seems they just didnt put the effort into and banked on people buying it anyways because its an emotional slam dunk. and I dont like when companies use peoples emotions to make money, but regardless, I have enjoyed this immensely.TLDRGood game that captures the essence of the original and adds upon it graphically so people can relive a classic with the quality of technology today, even though its not as good as it could of been and suffers from certain low effort choices.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: This remaster stays true to the original in terms of frame-by-frame cutscenes and abilities, while also fulfilling the role of "remaster" with outstanding visuals. While the game itself looks and plays beautifully, there are a few things I believe are more of a negative change. Firstly, the battle sound effects, such as attacks and breaking different tikis, are much less impactful than the original. Where destroying tikis and blowing things up used to feel powerful, now it just feels subpar and a little disappointing. This also includes the jump sound for each character, which used to be definitive of their character now feels muted and pushed aside. Secondly, the voice lines were not updated at all. While this wasn't an expected change, the knock off Mr. Krabs is definitely more noticable and out of place in this updated game. Otherwise, nostalgia is a huge motivator in playing this game and it fills that purpose. Enjoy revisiting an amazing remaster of a classic childhood game!

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've 100% the game and done everything...even wasting my shinies on the theatre, I can say that this game is fantastic. There are some things that could be improved upon, but it's still a ton of fun.It's best going into this game knowing it's a 1-1 remake of the original, meaning almost nothing "new" was added in regards to content, which is a bit disappointing, but for the price it makes sense. _childDocuments_.review: Seemingly worse than the original. The controls layout on PC is good but the controls themselves feel unresponsive and it can feel like the game deliberately doesn't want to attack despite your insistent clicking. The save system makes no improvement over the original apart from save slots, which can lead to frustrating situations where you get stuck doing something you don't want to do (Sand Mountain slides).Some parts of the game are just as unforgiving as the original, like the ball puzzle in the Mermalair which can take many tries to get right while also wasting your time because parts of the puzzle have long wait times.The visual improvements are obvious, but don't look very special. There is detail in places where it doesn't belong (like the pores on SpongeBob's skin), and many textures still have flat shading apart from ice and emissive materials. The animations are more expressive and there are more of them but they still lack responsiveness or context, seemingly something modern games fail to do (Please take notes from Half-Life 2).I haven't even played the co-op mode but I already know it's a joke that has no relevancy to the game, it's just a repetitive survival/horde-mode mini game that failed to grab my attention from the beginning.In short the game improves upon very little, and the remake is little more than the flashy images you can see on the store page. So if you want to experience this remake, then just go look at those wallpapers.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game out of nostalgia because I played it when I was like 3 to 4 years old. I was incredibly hyped for this to come out. That being said, I hated the Remake. It wasn't anything the Remake did per se, it was just... playing this made me realize I hated the original as well? Nearly every level gave me a feeling of "oh ♥♥♥♥ not this again", except for like 2 or 3 of them and I wasn't exactly hooked on those either. At the time of me playing the original, I only had access to 4 games and as a then more avid Spongebob watcher, this was the first game I ever 100%ed. Twice. I loved it at the time but some levels I dreaded more than others even then, namely the Beach and the Jungle. ♥♥♥♥ the Jungle. I personally can't genuinly recommend this game because of my hindsightful experience, telling me I hated everything about it even back then? It's really weird to me. That being said, you might still very well enjoy this game, it's mechanically all well. Another game I played back then was the original Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy. It is conceptually exactly the same, but I guess the differences do add up, as I still generally love that game. Anyway, yeah, buy it or don't buy it, just don't be too hyped.

_childDocuments_.review: Most video games based on licensed properties tend to be overly simplistic in nature, made to cash in on the success of a certain property. But Battle for Bikini Bottom is not one of those, and there's plenty of reasons why this game became such a cult-classic and got the remaster you see before you today.BfBB brings in the world of SpongeBob Squarepants and manages to turn it into a well-done 3D Collectathon that's simple and easy to grasp for players of all ages, with plenty things to do in each world, the unforgettable charm and humor of the characters, and great music that won't sound out of place in a normal episode from the original show.SpongeBob, Patrick and Sandy may not have that many abilities in compared to most characters in other games similar to this such as Banjo-Kazooie or Super Mario 64 but what they do have manages to work really well with the challenges in the world and fits in with their overall characters.The game itself does play a bit too safe and has glaring instances that would require some polish but once you get across that, what you'll find is an great game for beginners to the Collectathon genre that although basic, still manages to be entertaining and guarantees you a F.U.N time.

They're all about their fans, and that means much more than trying to be, "innovative and new." Fantastic remake, and it's not even a money grab given it's the same price as the original from 2003 console releases. How much more wholesome can you be as a company???

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer, I've played the original game repeatedly over and over. I'm a huge fan of the original game, but... if I could give Rehydrated a mixed rating, I would. Rehydrated is rough around the edges. There are some small changes that really enhance the experience compared to the original game, but there are others that really detract from it. There's also some really interesting bugs and glitches. I'm loving the updated graphics and remastered soundtrack, the animations are so smooth, and the core gameplay remains as fun as ever, but the game is currently unpolished and needs some patches to make it truly the Best Day Ever.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: After the trainwreck that was FF7R it's nice to see someone remaster a classic game and do it justice.Rehydrated is a near perfect recreation of the original game but with better graphics and controls. While it's a relatively short game (you can easily get through the whole thing in under 10 hours), it's 100% worth the price. What this game lacks in content, it makes up for in it's soul and charm.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom - Rehydrated

_childDocuments_.review: Basically if you're a fan of SpongeBob, the original game, or just looking for an excellent platformer. GET THIS!!  They did keep the original dialogue and music from the original. Some of the voice acting might sound off since it's not the original voice actor from show (Mr. Krabs for example). Other than graphics, this game is identical to the original. It's a relaxing yet challenging platformer game that revolves around collecting items and destroying robots. You can play as Spongebob, Patrick, or Sandy in the main story. The new mode for Multiplayer is a good bonus from the original, but boring and repetitive in my opinion. All you do is fight off waves of robots on different islands.

_childDocuments_.review:
Are you ready, kids? The cult classic is back, faithfully remade in spongetastic splendor! Play as SpongeBob, Patrick and Sandy and show the evil Plankton that crime pays even less than Mr. Krabs. Want to save Bikini Bottom from lots of rampant robots with your mighty bubbles? Of course you do! Want to underpants bungee jump? Why wouldn't you! Want to join forces in a brand new multiplayer mode? The battle is on!

GAME FEATURES
- Play as SpongeBob, Patrick and Sandy and use their unique sets of skills
- Thwart Plankton's evil plan to rule Bikini Bottom with his army of wacky robots
- Meet countless characters from the beloved series

REMAKE FEATURES
- Faithful remake of one of the best SpongeBob games ever created
- High-end visuals, modern resolutions and carefully polished gameplay
- Brand new horde mode multiplayer for up to two players, online and offline
- Restored content that was cut from the original game like the Robo Squidward boss fight and more

name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos
detailed_description: OTHER GAMES YOU MAY LIKE Just updated - Patch note available About the Game Are you ready to dive into a tactical RPG chock-full of charm, humor and crazy characters?! They are clumsy, inexperienced and feisty but...they’ll have to endure each other’s company to get the dungeon’s treasure. However, a feeling of déjà-vu quickly arises... Guide this team of unlikely heroes in an adventure full of humor and chaos! The Naheulbeuk universe is an original creation by French author John Lang. It started as a very popular audio comedy series parodying role-playing games and heroic fantasy tropes. Now the story is available in English and as a video game for the first time! Game features Play with seven classic role-playing game characters complementing each other’s skills as you level them up: the Ranger, the Elf, the Dwarf, the Barbarian, the Magician, the Ogre and the Thief! Every member of the team has their own skill tree to upgrade their abilities and equipment. Choose one of three additional companions to join the team on their adventure! Exciting turn-based battles, with creative support mechanics between team members. An adaptive difficulty system: from an accessible and fun story mode with simplified combat to the “nightmare mode” where the smallest tactical errors will doom you! An expansive bestiary (more than 100 enemies!) pushing you to think more tactically with every fight. Epic boss battles where you’ll have to muster both strength and smarts to emerge victorious! Hidden and destructive objects (including beer kegs) with surprising status effects will turn the tide of battle for the better...or worse! Explore a huge and surprising dungeon from the cave up to the luxury quarters of the evil lord Zangdar, passing through the goblin iceskating park and even an extremely lively tavern! Escape traps and solve deadly puzzles to unlock the most impressive treasures! Bizarre conversations, absurd situations and unusual encounters await! Experience an exciting main storyline and many side quests for your heroes

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it but that's a though one.I'll be blunt (and probably a bit unfair) but this game, for all its qualities has one major flaw. It is one of these strategy game you can play with your brain turned off.The % of success in your action means nothing, the devs implemented a system allowing the IA to cheat to prevent you from getting too good results. So if a certain action is giving you too much on an edge, the game will correct it by making you miss. Also it is useless to try to reload because, apparently, dices are thrown at the begining of your turn and, no matter what you do, a similar action will get similar results.So how is that allowing players to play with their brain turned off ?Well the game is also preventing the IA to get too much advantages over you. Therefore the more reckless you are, the less likely it is to punish you.Once you understand that, you'll just have to rush, AOE everywhere regardless of the position of your team and you'll be fine. It took me some times to get the logic (around 5 to 10 hours) but once I understood how the IA was working most fights were over in 3 turns top. It literally took me 2 turns to beat the final boss. Broke his shield one time and rolled on him.Aside this fact the game is pretty cool imo, price is correct and you get some fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Will update later if the game story sucks since I only have 98 mins in it so far. A cute, fun, introduction to the turn-based rpg genre. I really dig it so far. Always was a fan of diagonal positioning in turn based. The only thing I feel is wrong so far is it feels clunky on pc mouse & keyboard. I think it would be easier to play on controller. I am not a fan of Q & E being the camera positioning instead of for example holding the right mouse button and swinging it around. Also, would be nice if there was a way to permanently tick interaction areas instead of holding down tab every where you go to find loot etc etc. Last thing I don't like so far is the map being so small. Would be nice if you could put it on the middle of the screen like Diablo.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, yeah I'd recommend the game. Played it till the end, so that's got to be something. Writings ok, pacing is a bit sub par for something that's trying to push a comedy angle, needs a lot of QOL improvements, and for me it started to get buggier in the last third, and no spoilers, but the ending was underwhelming.Still, kept me going for the full playthrough, so if you're looking for a D&D lite with some tongue in cheek, then yeah I'd recommend this - just don't expect to be swept away.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lite party based, turn based combat RPG. Most of the RPG parts are pretty lite, from the equipment to the simplified skill trees etc. There's a bit more complexity in combat with some class synergies and cover/backstab/dodge system that is interesting albeit not too complex.There's lots of humour too, from the crude type, to the dad jokes, to the references to other RPGs, like the ranger Binsc searching for his hamster Moo... ring a bell?!I believe this game is based off a French well known RPG parody, but I'm not familiar with it. Guessing those who are will enjoy this game even more.I'm not normally a fan of playing with sound on (weird I know) but the voice overs are nicely done and with the humor they're very worth it.If you're looking for a party based RPG without the complexity of character builds and super tactical combats like Pathfinder, this is a good game for you. If you prefer more complex stuff, Pathfinder Kingmaker is a better game (at the time of this review I have not yet played Pathfinder Wrath of the Righteous)

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Game will not win any major reward for it's story or characters but they seam solid enough to push you further into the game. It may be childish but if you like toilet humor you may chuckle a few times. Graphics are quite nice and the cartoonish style adds to the slapstick convention of old-time DnD sessions.Cons: Battles which are 90% of the gameplay. At first they seem pretty good with a few nice touches to the 2AP system. Later on you are presented which mechanic which could be really fun but ended up the most annoying addition ever - ill fate gauge. Every time something goes wrong it goes up allowing you to use special skills to weigh the scales in your favour (could save the game from filthy save-scammers like me). Or it could if the developers would not ensure that every fight now on will be painstaking to make this feature usable. Let's play 'Bad Design Bingo' based on my recent fight (luck based situations mentioned here happen in most of the fights): -Enemy have a mage with 1 hit KO spells which he uses every turn. It's also an AOE so you can say goodbye to protecting your back line-Enemies run through entire map and attack you on your defensive positions in their first round. (I estimate 4AP worth of movement for player characters.)-Enemy mage have same HP as your tank and same DMG as your damage dealer. -Enemy tank have twice your HP for a good measure.-At this example at least i was not outnumbered (7 enemies - 7 PC). Oh wait... 1 hit KO AOE which ended up burning half of the party...-Most of your skills and attack misses. Remember the ill fate gauge? :)-Ill fate gauge skills are useless. Amount of bad luck needed to use it makes it a rather bad joke. It honestly feels like developers would want to achieve Dark Souls level of difficulty but with RNG, anti-player design, and without any of the 'GIT GUD' mechanics where knowledge makes you powerful.TL;DR For other DnD lovers: Too much 'Tomb of Annihilation'. And also you are dead.Edit: After beating the game I can say that it is badly balanced. Early game is too hard while last boss can be defeated in one turn in the first try. (First review after attempting Hard and edit section was written after Normal difficulty.)

_childDocuments_.review: Now this is a fun albeit somewhat zany game. I purchased it on a whim knowing nothing about its background (its based on a French audio drama) and first impressions were solid. I did think at first 'what is with the voice acting?'  - the dwarf has the most outrageously cliche dwarf accent imaginable and the elf is always somewhat shrill. But then understanding what its based on, it all makes sense.The game itself is really solid and oozes character. Its fun just to change the party leader sometimes to see how they run out front, from the Ranger's swagger to the Elf's skipping. The graphics are excellent - definitely zoom in sometimes to see the quality and the soundtrack is always high quality.Combat is a detailed turn based affair, with characters spending action points to move, attack or use specials. There are attacks of opportunity and Overwatch mechanics in place and positioning is the key to success in battle. The range of skills is expansive - just get Dwarf Toss for the Ogre, trust me ;) Each character has their distinct flavour and all play very differently. You can naturally build them in different ways, for example my Ranger liked swords but he could have been specced more for bows instead, My Priestess originally liked dealing damage with holy lightning, until around level 8 when I changed her to a pure buff/heal machine. Once criticism here is that its perhaps too easy to just stack 1-2 stats, agility and strength for most. There again, Courage determines the order you attack in, so there are tactics that can be built around high Courage and Courage buffs too.There is copious loot ranging in quality from trash to truly epic. Changing main armour also upgrades the look of the characters; the dwarf becoming more and more like a tin can, the elf becoming more covered in flowers with every upgrade, and the Ogre just adding random pots and pans to himself. It all works very well.The humour is relentless - and its the thing that will make you love or hate this game. If you like zany, somewhat slapstick D&D parody jokes they come at your constantly. This isn't a game for people who take everything seriously, but just let yourself get drawn into the silliness and you'll have a blast.One particular favourite is the constant insults between the Elf and Dwarf. For example when the Elf levels up you sometimes get this exchange:Elf: I'm getting better!Dwarf: Better than rubbish is still rubbish.I'm not sure there is much replayability, but the first playthrough is a good 30-40 hours and worth every moment. I shall be sad to wave goodbye to the Ranger, Dwarf, Elf, Thief, Barbarian, Ogre, Wizardess and Priestess, and shall be crossing my fingers for a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: 83/100Great gameplay, entertaining characters and plots, solid cartoon graphics, and genuinely funny dialogue (for the most part) - this game has just about everything going for it and is definitely worth paying full price if you love turn-based strategy or if you're craving a DnD parody. However, keep in mind that it is  H E A V Y  on the parody. The comedy angle is really going to be the deal breaker for most people, I think. Just like any game though, if you're on the fence just watch 10-20 minutes of real gameplay (no commentary ftw) and if you're still unsure you can always wishlist then grab it on sale. SteamDB price charts are a godsend - just check to see if a sale is coming up, seems like the game's on sale for ~week at 50% off or more every 2-4 months. If you think you'll like the humor then there's only one other thing worth mentioning: spelling & grammatical issues. These come up pretty often but they're BARELY noticeable - missing periods, misspelled words, confusing or misleading flavor text, oddly worded skill descriptions. The only obvious instance of this is that six or seven times across the entire game + DLC the subtitles won't match the spoken dialogue, though what's written and what's said are pretty much synonymous so it's not a big deal. Also, once you beat the game if you want more of their antics then know that the game's based on a French audio series! There are also comics, which are pretty good but they are French only afaik - no English translations, fan or otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game and I wish I could give it more time. Seemed like a fun game with great banter and some cheesy lines. However the combat is atrocious. Abilities are useless with extremely slow cool downs, rendering them useless. God forbid you miss, big rip with those cool downs. Needs some more fine tuning to make it more engaging and fun. Don't get at full price but there are much better games like this out there. Divinity series, Solasta, Gloomhaven, Pathfinder series, Baldur's Gate series, Pillars Of Eternity, Wasteland series, and hell should I add Shadowrun series being much better.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of really good elements to this game.  It's very polished, the battle system is really fun, and the character customisation is fairly good for a game of its type.The humour is...  well in the native French it's quite funny but it is somewhat of a coarse and cringy style of humour that is not going to appeal to everyone, plus the Wizard's voice is horrible.  The English voices however seem to be mainly American and they completely lose this quality, a lot of the humour is 'lost in translation'.  Frankly I do not find American voices very appealing in a fantasy RPG.I refunded for two reasons, firstly the camera is really awful.  It's terribly zoomed in and lacks one button that can rotate the camera, these are two QoL features that the game really needs.Secondly the movement of the group is really annoying.  They have this weird delay or acceleration that makes movement feel very unresponsive and clumsy.  This might seem like a nitpick but you spend so much time moving around in the game world that it's actually really annoying.Lastly some keys are unable to be bound, such as the bracket keys, I was using these as programmed hotkeys so I had to go into my software and change them just for the game, a slight annoyance but I feel like hurling my PC around the room whenever a game refuses to let me rebind keys properly so I'm mentioning it.So ultimately it's a thumbs down from me, honestly if the camera wasn't so bad I probably would have stuck with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. It seems like a game that requires to try every combat twice (second attempt being real easy) or just just get very lucky with RNG. It's not a bad game but very much style over substance.

_childDocuments_.review: It gud! It's fun, with good combat. I am not really an RPG guy, but I am a TBS guy, so I skip through the story then scream blue murder when I don't know what to do. The first few levels are pretty frustrating, but once you get your accuracy up you can start doing some damage, and this game doesn't insist on its xcom luck - While there's a crit fail mechanic (seems to happen about 3 times a battle on a largish battle), if the game says somethings got a 100% chance to hit, and your opponent doesn't have a dodge stat, you have a 100% chance to hit. I think the game could do to explain some of its mechanics upfront a little more. At the start of every battle you have to press t to see all the stats alteration that are relevant atm. I think this is kinda annoying because I don't understand why I can't just toggle it on/why it's even possible to toggle it off. TBS are all about information and the less information you have the worse the experience. A lot of the mechanics aren't readily explained and sometimes the mechanics of the mechanics (i.e; how the effect actually works) are not clear or predictable. It would be nice to always know exactly what will happen,  since the game is trying to be perfect information. I'd also love it if the game let you undo movement. Any dice roll, 100% hold me to it, but sometimes you are guessing if a square is in range and the game decides that you're not (diagonal range measuring is very unintuitive in this game) I'm not quite finished, but I will finish it soon. I'd call the game long enough to warrant the price tag (maybe go for a sale) and the combat is deep enough to keep you enjoying the game. I was always a save scummer in xcom (hey, I was a teenager, give me a break) and I haven't found myself doing that in this, much more willing to simply restart the battle when it goes haywire, since its usually on me to fix my plan. I'd give it an 8/10 for combat, a ?/10 for story and a 6/10 for user experience. The gameplay is good and everything else is... passable or irrelevant to me. Give it a go if you like TBS games like modern XCom!

_childDocuments_.review: I would make this a qualified yes.  Playing on Tavern Song level was pleasant enough.  A couple fights needed to be re-started due to bad decisions but over all decent.  The Epic Gest level is just stupid.  I achieved the 'cursed die' achievement which is get 100 critical failures.  A critical failure should be relatively rare, not 20% or more of your rolls.  The Splatt and Vanna fight shows that NPCs aren't restricted like PCs.  Their spells have zero cool down, don't seem to burn any astral energy, and never (so far) fail.  Also, even when cornered and surrounded, Splatt dodged 13 of 14 attacks.  All attacks were made at 85% probability or higher.  Many of  these where chained attacks meaning 2 or more characters attacked him the same round.  So, that means he also doesn't suffer from the 1.5 reduction for subsequent dodges.  That whole fight is just lazy on the part of the developers since each round there is either a global buff or a global debuff.  Guys, if you can't code up a decent NPC AI, I get it, but it's not fun game play to just bend the rules for the NPCs without a reason.  Additionally, there are cases where Splatt runs in and out of AOO for the PCs without suffering an attack.  Even though the PCs had not used their AOO that round.  Finally, the Randomia gauge updates randomly.  Instead of updating after a critical failure, it sits under 25% and then suddenly, jumps to 60% in the space of one character's turn.A couple of the side missions, the Courier Gold mission specifically, encourages evil behavior.  Give the gold back and 1) You get no reward (other than the exp which is constant for all decisions) 2) The guard gets the gold, and 3) The courier dies anyway.  I'd say if you're going to get the game, wait for a sale, don't pay full price.  The replay ability is not great, some of the puzzles maybe just didn't do well in the translation as they're completely opaque as to what is expected.  Others are just so simple as to hardly qualify as puzzles.  Maybe this is the state of turn-based RPGs today, I'll admit to not having played one since Gladius on the XBox so that's been a whle.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a turn based tactics game with an excellent sense of humour and so so many Easter eggs from start to finish.Character development is fairly simple and straight forward and there is replay value in choosing your last character.  Levelling up stats as normal and then choosing between 1 of 3 skills per tier and building on them at first. The level cap is 10.This is not ground breaking or different to the usual formula for  tactics games but the jokes and general banter between characters does make it stand out.  The jokes might not be everyone's cup of tea and some of the Easter eggs are easy to overlook but I genuinely enjoyed it.  A good example is the side quest to find Moo (the hamster) for Binsc the warrior you meet in the bar, I was actually surprised at the Baulders Gate reference when it came up! And this is quite a deep cut, there are tons of these throughout.No crashes or glaring bugs while playing in the steam deck either which is a big bonus.  If you enjoy tactic games then this is worth playing. There is enough depth to keep you going on the high difficulty.  If you are new to the genre it's actually quite forgiving too so its a good starting point as well and the humour should keep you invested.

_childDocuments_.review: Bases itself on the DnD system to evoke a gameplay that, without a DM, is unfun.Has no system to counterbalance luck, allowing you to Critical Fail gain Pity points for failing and Critically Failing on the Action the Pity system granted you. Critical Failures are also terribly punishing and could happen even for sneezing.There's a very clear reason why this system works in TTRPGs and that is because of the DM's intervention towards the fun of the players.

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyable tactical RPG.The story is humorous at times, if not particularly original.Some of the (English) voice acting is pretty good.Some of the writing is decent, and genuinely funny.  I particularly loved some of the in-combat callouts from other characters when a party member critical-fails an attack and ends up injuring themselves, or fails a roll for an environmental hazard.The combat and progression mechanics seems pretty well balanced for the majority of the game.  It starts out pretty difficult, and remains challenging up until the last 15-20% of the game.  At that point, if you've been looting everything and optimizing your builds, (respec potions are plentiful and cheap), you will start to steamroll the last dozen or so fights with your full epic gear and highest tier abilities.The game is pretty accommodating to limited play sessions as well as you can save at just about any point, even mid-combat.I give it a b+ overall.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is borderline for me. At it's core, it's a strong comic-fantasy-themed dungeon quest with XCOM-like combat. There's fun to be had, as the tactical system and character advancement are enjoyable. Unfortunately several flaws keep me from recommending it.First the "comic" part of comic-fantasy leaves a lot to be desired here. The game was made by a French studio, and if you've ever played a comedy game made by continental Europeans before, you'll know that the humor doesn't hold up when translated to English. Expect your party to engage in near-constant sophmoric sexual and insult humor with a lot of needless banter on the side. There were a few chuckles to be found, but mostly the humor just hovered at "eye-roll" level.The story, too, is silly, and somehow manages to be both inane and bewildering. By the end of the game, characters were appearing that we had supposedly met before that I had almost no memory of, I honestly could not keep straight who was who and doing what and who was on whose side.Finally, while there is a good core to the combat system, there's also a lot of room for improvement. Characters can use items on their belt on their turn, but this takes the place of their main action, which means that any item that is simply a buff and doesn't heal or attack just isn't worth it the action cost. If you had the option to use an item in place of your move I think that could go a way towards making them more useful. Also, when it comes to character advancement, while it's nice when your level up and get stronger, often the best options for active and passive skills will be pretty obvious from the get go, making the choices less interesting. There's things to like in TDoN:TAoC, and overall I enjoyed the combat, but the game's problems are just enough from giving it a thumbs up. What we've got here is a mostly-unfunny starting point for a true fantasy-themed XCOM experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, satirical take on the classic dungeon crawler trope, that despite it's cartoonish look and comical tone is surprisingly deep on a strategic level.PRO: - Decently written characters and entertaining story- Deep strategy; diverse characters with their own unique abilties, unlockable skills (that you can't all pick so you have to strategize for combos), combat system (attacks of opportunity, precision stat, facing, and a wide variety of enemy types.- True to the dungeon crawler trope, there's also a lot of hidden stuff that you are going to search hard for.- Oh, and puzzles.CON: - Some things are not explained very well. - Characters's repetetive barks can get annoying after a while. Luckily you can turn this off.- PuzzlesAll in all, a surprisingly well-crafted RPG that veterans of the genre will find entertaining and laugh at the many in-jokes.Solid 5/7, would get time-looped again!

_childDocuments_.review: Briefly summarized, as a decades-long roleplaying and pen&paper player, Dungeons of Naheulbeuk touches a lot in me and brings back many memories of past games and also table roleplaying sessions. But I'm pretty sure that even normal people and non-nerds, who have simply consumed a few fantasy books, Lord of the Rings movies or corresponding games, can understand most of the gags in Naheulbeuk.Whether it matches everybody's humor is difficult for me to judge, but I think in general it should fit. Sometimes the cliché thing gets a bit overused, but almost all the time a humorous, slightly chaotic game emerges from it, which I certainly enjoy a lot.The stories the game tells are not incredibly complex dramas or high-fantasy epics. But it is also never completely undemanding or boring. Some side quests are kept simpler, as in almost every game. But as compensation, there are also really complex switch puzzles and small hidden secrets, which raise the level again.A particularly positive aspect of the game is the depth in both the role-playing systems and the tactical battles. Here you can feel the experience of the developers through their last project Space Hulk Tactics. There is often an atmosphere similar to the genre king XCom. The impressive camera movements at heavy hits and special events known from there are also present.All in all, I am also convinced by the very high production quality and the loving and varied design. And I suppose, if you know the audiobooks and comics, this game will become a dream.It’s really hard for me to find anything you could complain about in The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk: Amulet of Chaos. The fully-scripted story of course reduces the replayability of the game, but the extensive skill decisions and the three potential group members from which you can only choose one will at least provide some incentive in this direction.To my knowledge, a NewGame+ is not included yet. Since the game is self-contained, I don’t expect any major expansions through updates in the actual gameplay. But I can imagine that this new brand has a very good chance to become a long-term franchise through story DLCs and possible successors.I haven’t finished the main story yet, but after 15 hours of testing, I’m now roughly in the middle or at the beginning of the second half of the story. I’m not the turbo player, some people would reach this level faster. So I would roughly guess that most players can get at least 20 to 30 hours of fun with one playthrough.The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet of Chaos costs 34,99 €/$ in the base price and is available now at Steam, GOG, and Epic Games. For this price, you get a high-quality single-player tactical role-playing game, with an exciting story, appealing graphics, good sound, complete voice output in English, French, and German.For this really well-rounded full package, I would like to give a baseline rating of 85%. Since the game has no big quirks, problems, or other serious disadvantages, nothing will be deducted here. I would upgrade the game by up to 5% if the developers would increase the replay value with patches, for example with a NewGame+ or the possibility to play through random dungeons.EN DE

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons of Naheulbeuk can’t be accused of taking a lot seriously, but it absolutely refuses to make a mockery of its D&D foundations. Sure, all the expected tropes and stereotypes are mercilessly scorned with ditzy airhead elf archers sharing a hate/hate relationship with selfish, materialistic dwarves, but it has no issue putting all that aside when it matters. For a satirical game, its combat is no joke; turn-based squad battles with X-Com-like hit percentages tapered by dodge stats and environment hazards. Magic attacks grounded by intelligence stats with percentile chances of status effect triggers like poison or ablaze. You can set up chains of attacks that string into epic combos. Maybe if you hit that orc warrior with the barbarian’s special attack, it will proc fear, wherein the orc will hightail it away from any current threats. However, in his panicked escape attempt, maybe he’s broken ground next to the ogre, which will trigger his attack of opportunity, giving him a free swing at his fleeing foe. Or, maybe the ranger’s been set to overwatch, letting him ping an arrow into his retreating form. Or, maybe the nefarious thief has set up an ice patch the hapless orc has sprinted into, failed a stability check and ended up flat on his arse, prone to all manner of elevated attacks until he’s able to pull himself to his feet. Maybe all of these! But, also, maybe none of them. Maybe the barbarian failed his virtual dice roll and ended up missing the orc entirely, muttering to himself while the rest of his party ruthlessly mock his ineptitude.There’s equipment to be won in battle or looted from chests, difficult choices to be made on whether you’d be better off with that silver ring that refreshes 2HP every turn, or the stone one that increases your melee defence. There’s experience to be farmed, stats to be bolstered, skills to learn. And while some of these skills might lean towards the ridiculous, their effects do not. It would be easy to point at the ogre’s belch skill and claim toilet humour, but it’s an AoE attack that hits anyone in close proximity and offers a high chance to stun. The elf’s ability to blow kisses to the frontline from cover may seem dumb, but it’s a ranged heal that can give back some serious HP if her charisma stats has been well maintained. The thief has hen bombs, which are exactly what they sound like. It seems a worthless waste of a turn, but lobbing a quintet of furious, lightly-singed hens into an enemy backline could cause chaos. They can interrupt mages channelling high-powered spells, or annul archers posted on overwatch, or just get under the feet of advancing brawlers.Juxtaposed to that is the frivolousness and deriding world of Dungeons of Naheulbeuk, lifted right from an parody audio series that takes aim at all the genre tropes. To that end, the story revolves around a first time adventuring party taking on what they believe to be a never before explored dungeon crawl in order to retrieve the statue of a god that none of them can pronounce. It doesn’t go particularly smoothly. They’ve barely started exploring before they come across a huge magical lock far beyond their meagre understanding, so they elect to wallop it. This doesn’t work, but it does scatter the party throughout the first floor of the dungeon, forcing the now solitary ranger to track them all down. The elf’s been locked in the toilet, much to the chagrin of the desperate orc eagerly waiting outside. A distressed and distracted orc is an easy victory, even for the rookie ranger, but this doesn’t stop him bragging that it was a horde of hardened warriors he rescued the elf from rather than one poor sap trying not to crap himself. The thief’s found cowering in the shadows. He’d much rather stay there. The ogre’s been locked in the pantry. He’d much rather stay there.As standalone subjects, such heavy-handed gags might contain an unhealthy amount of cringe, but Dungeons of Naheulbeuk commits hard to its shtick and that commitment pays off. While there’s plenty of winking at the cameras and light threatening of the fourth wall, because the world around the bumbling party is treated so respectfully, the humour is often found in the stupidity of their actions and the knee-jerk reactions in trying to right their errors. They’re cursed early on because they take part in a random spin-the-wheel gameshow hosted by goblins that couldn’t be a more obvious trap. Even after knowing a golden amulet gained from it is magical and untrustworthy, the party is forced to take stock of it anyway thanks to the dwarf because gold. Then they fight a drag out battle among the ticker tape and gaudy banners against goblin blunderbuss snipers and greenskin assassins, where if they don’t win the battle quick enough reinforcements shuffle on from stage left to join the fray.
