_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon of Nahelbeauk  is a game based on a French classic. It is a tactical dungeon crawler with all the RPG elements you may ever want. You control a party of EIGHT characters in extremely difficult, tactical encounters and experience the crazy story that features excellent humour and really epic battles.Check my video review here: With EIGHT characters you can use in combat, here is what really got me: the game is extremely rich here! everyone has TWO skilltrees (active and passive), 9 gear slots they equip items on and 6 characteristics to evolve, plus a HUGE NUMBER of secondary stats. Items come with various unique properties, too so it not just flat stat bonuses. Armor ignoring daggers? Here you go! Special proc effects activating - also there! This keeps the levelling system and gearing really exciting and gives you a lot of choices.This game has a ton of RNG but it also has a system in place to counteract it - a special misfortune bar fills up whenever you get unlucky (you miss or critically miss - yes, those are two different things). You will gain access to four special skills based on how much of the bar you have filled up, allowing you to gain extra moves, heal and cleanse your characters and gain cool buffs.Combat borrows a lot from X-Com and other tactical games of the genre. We have a fully functional overwatch system, cover, flanking, backstabs, positioning - the only thing we're missing is high ground. Your characters work together - there are special passives that provide your team with powerful bonuses when specific characters stand next to each other in combat.Monsters and combat encounters always feel  unique! The fights are scripted, with reinforcements coming in, environmental hazards, special tiles, traps, enemies that have unique moves - overall, it's an exciting and wholesome experience! This comes with FOUR difficulties, so if the combat is a bit too challenging, you can dial it down, while if you want your fights to really test your mettle, you can indulge, too. Higher difficulties add extra opponents to fights, which means it's not just bloated stats.The music is BEAUTIFUL, the game is FULLY VOICED by excellent voice actors. The characters are really cool when they argue with each other - we have a cocky ranger, bimbo elf, charismatic wizardess, discombobulated ogre, panicky thief, horny priestess, lisping bard and a glory-hungry paladin. The characters make tons of meta-refernces to other games and fantasy popculture. Plus a ton more of those that you can only get if you're French I guess.Now, the game has some small issues.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to the combat, imagine if Xcom had random fails for everything, the AI was a prick about even the slightest mistake, and every disadvantage feels deliberate yet frustrating. From the very get-go, every encounter starts with some frustration. You always start short on cover, meaning that you've got to prioritize correctly or the one guy who doesn't have cover is going to get stomped at before it's their turn.I'd forgive that if it didn't also happen that you'd frequently have a few points of cover short for just your ranged characters, except when you do but there are explosive/poison barrels that you thought were just decoration. Should that have been tutorialized? Maybe, but considering how obnoxiously hard this game tutorializes everything else, I was genuinely shocked that the game didn't say a single thing about them.Pacing seems to be quite an issue all in all, in fact.The tutorial drags on quite a bit, almost frustratingly holding your hand through every little thing and mechanic it wants you to employ. At times, it wasn't perfectly clear about what it wanted to show me, locking me into the exchange until I stumbled upon what it wanted me to do.The pacing basically died before it had a chance to begin, and it's not helped by your slow exploration speed. In fact, why is there a wind-up to the walk when tapping thumbstick? Didn't we already phase out this terrible method of controlling a character?Then you have the conversations that want to be funnier than they are which, sure, that might be subjective. I can handle some silly dumb humor sprinkled (quite a bit) with base foul language. Problem is when those shenanigans are combined with the already dragging tutorial. It's all just a mess of moment after moment of the game going "Look at how funny we are!", interrupting the flow of the game constantly.If you'd like a game that knew how to pace it's silly comedy with its gameplay, Magicka is a good example.In a single sentence, I'd say this game is a collection of good/passable ideas that are brought together in an amateurish way.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a pretty good experience. The story and comedy is actually shockingly good. The voice acting of the main characters is all good and matches their personalities well. Most of the other voice acting is good as well. Combats are tactical and interesting. Controller support works well.The biggest problem with the game is the difficult is a little much in the early game. And it isn't a good difficulty but an annoying one. First, there are too many enemies so the combats can tend to drag sometimes. Second, enemies have too many AOE attacks which can get bothersome. But the worst problem is that of purposefully making random outcomes work against you. The game FAQ even mentions that the player has worse odds than the enemies. The worst part of this is the 'critical failure' when attacking. They happen at least once or twice a round for you. They happen even when you are attacking a knocked out opponent or attempt a heal on yourself. Really a dumb mechanic because it doesn't adjust based on the difficulty of what you are attempting. It makes for some really frustrating battles when you setup everything perfectly for one of your special attacks, only to have a critical fail. Add this on top of the common dodge an parry from the enemy (even when backstabbing them) and it makes for a lot of unenjoyable times.I finished the game despite this, but it would have been near perfect otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk The Amulet Of Chaos is a (largely) turn-based dungeon crawler fantasy game.Anyone familiar with Dungeons & Dragons, or really any fantasy RPG (both analog and digital) will feel at home. You control up to eight characters, each a standard class of the fantasy genre (ranger, thief, barbarian, etc.) Each have distinct drawbacks and benefits. As you gain experience fighting battles and exploring the world, you can not only enhance the statistics of each character, but can grant them special abilities and passive bonuses. You're capped at level 10, so you'll never be able to choose them all, and there's a lot of exclusivity in the choices. You also can choose your eighth member between a Bard, a Priestess, and a Paladin, or forgo an eighth member and divide the experience a little quicker.The core of the game is mostly battles. (The non-battle parts of the game maybe make up 15% of the campaign, and largely involve exploration, riddles, and puzzles. They're pretty simple, depending on the difficulty level.) Battles are where the game really shines, because not only are there plenty of options to take, each of them is pretty meaningful and there's usually not an obvious choice. Sure, there's a standard attack and a defense, but there's also a "lookout" option that grants an extra attack if anyone goes in your area, and the special abilities are all fairly useful and straightforward. Positioning is important; flanking and backstabbing grant bonuses depending on where you are in relation to the target. While it seemed tedious at first, it ended up flowing fairly naturally. The storyline and humor are very tongue-in-cheek. While the harping between characters gets a little old after a while, it's just funny and engaging enough to not be annoying, and at any rate you can skip dialogue if you don't care for it. I, personally, found it mildly funny at first and quickly tiresome, but not enough to detract from the game.There's only a few things I don't care for in the game. Most are minor, but one is somewhat big.The minor ones first: the overall story seems a little short, and unlike similar games you run the campaign and you're done. You can certainly play through again, and choose a different eighth character and choose different options, so there's some replay value there, but you'll already know the exploration and puzzles. Still, I got a solid 40 hours of unique gameplay, so at the price point it's not that bad. Second, there's no real reason to keep old armor or weapons, so you can easily sell off your old armor when you find new armor; this has the effect of the weight limit being largely not a problem, and you'll never have a reason to not always have gold. At higher difficulties it's a *little* tighter, but not by much.The major thing is a problem a lot of games like this have: they follow the "We are going to give you a bunch of super cool abilities" school of design, quickly followed up by the "You aren't allowed to use them" school of design. It's frustrating to get an ability that, say, allows you to stun an enemy, only to find that all of the enemies you encounter from that point forward are either immune to stuns or get a huge defense against it. Got an ability that lets you attack three times? Suddenly, all enemies around the time you level up to this get a bonus against dodging multiple attacks in one round. There's one ability that takes two rounds to play (i.e., first turn is the setup; the second turn is the attack) and not once did I get to pull it off; enemies I encountered after that all got some special ability that always countered what I did. That said, on net, the game is really fun to play. It is turn-based and tactical, and the humor is cartoonish and a little broad, but if the gameplay in the videos looks to be up your alley, I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: TDoN is based of a 6 season french language audio adventure which parodies well known fantasy universes (LotR, H Potter, Warhammer Fantasy Battles and others) as well as famous fantasy films of the 80s & 90s. It features censored swearing (bleeped F-bombs) and an abundance of toilet humour. Though to be fair this is one of the few games where you will routinely encounter toilets that look like a gents in a pub at kicking out time at the weekend.The game itself is fairly standard tactical RPG fare: each party member has 2 action points by default with one reserved for movement; leveling up sees you gain 2 stat points (3 at levels 7&8, 4 at levels 9 & 10), 1 active skill point and 1 passive skill point; gear comes in 4 qualities denoted by background colour (black, bronze, silver, gold) with 8-10 slots depending on character options for shield, melee weapon & ranged weapon; every one friend or foe gets one round before the turn counter resets. Combat events are scripted, so there is no way to trigger a fight randomly other than encountering a quest marker. This makes side quests very much essential for improving your team. The TAB key will be your friend for finding hidden loot when exploring as all interactive items other than side quest find X are highlighted yellow.Some of the more novel features are the injury systems - performance dips as the health bar goes from green to yellow to amber to red, as well as temporary stat debuffs that you acquire through being rendered unconscious. The dips can removed through the use of an appropriate consumable. You can also choose at the start of chapter 3 to add one extra character (paladin, minstrel or priestess) that can't be swapped out. There are also neutral combatants (chickens) that will attack the nearest non-chicken, irrespective of who's side it is on. Each merchant has different rates for buying stuff from you, but all will sell the same item for the same price.Gripes:Have encountered a graphics issue with the image seeming ghostly when paused. Had to play around with the visual settings to clear the issue. EDIT: Resolution was to play in windowed mode.Lack of ability to set facing before the characters turn ends. Say you want to shoot an enemy to your west and then have the character face north. You have to attack first and then move. If you move first then attack you'll be stuck facing west. No option to confirm you've finished your turn. There is a feature that allows you to give a character plus one action; however this must be chosen before they've used both their default action points otherwise they've missed their chance.No way to stop the mini-map rotating - whichever direction you are travelling becomes the 'northern point' of the mini-map. Has given me navigation headaches.EDIT - amongst the various game settings you can alter the end turn from automatic to manual and you can lock the mini-map so that it will always face North no matter how much your rotate the camera. You have to pause the game and go half way down the settings menu to adjust them. The game doesn't explicitly tell you about this.

_childDocuments_.review: "I've got nuts for the squirrels!"Finished this one on normal difficulty in 57 hours (playing "Ironman" style). If you enjoy RPGs with a turn based combat system like Divinity Original Sin, and you don't mind the constant toilet humour, then this is worth picking up.However, some of the game's shortcomings are.....- Lots of RNG bullsh*t just like the Divinity Original Sin games. Combats always seem to begin with enemies in favourable starting positions to your characters, the main enemies in a fight always seem to take their turns first, and your party seems to suffer far more critical misses on their attacks and critical hits from enemies than what the enemies do.- Also, the combat system can be a bit uninformative. You can't really check most of your enemy stats, and you can't access or even view your party inventory during a combat. Also you can't view any of your characters outside of their turns to check their skill cooldowns etc.- Exploration is clunky. Your characters all have to move together at the same time, which means everyone gets damaged by traps if you do not have the thief as your lead character detecting them. Avoiding combat is impossible as it automatically triggers as soon as your party walks into certain rooms in the dungeon.- The book collection system sucks. You find random books in the dungeon for various topics and if you complete the collection (each collection typically requires 3 to 5 books of the same name to be found), then your characters gain bonus stats for each collection of books returned to their matching bookshelf. The problem is that each set of books must be returned to a specific bookshelf and unless you have a really good memory, you will have to run back to each bookshelf individually to find the correct one as your map does not show each bookshelf's name and you can't make notes on your map.- The voice acting is pretty good but if you're a bit hard of hearing like myself, you will have to turn on the subtitles as almost all the characters in this game seem to speak really quickly for some reason.On the plus side, the combat can be quite fun (where else can your ogre toss your dwarf into a crowd of enemies?), there are some really funny moments in the game, and the loading screen art is hilarious (though sadly there are only about 6 different scenes for this).Recommended otherwise - 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I never expected to be able to get so pissed off at a game like this did. I'm playing on Epic Gest difficulty, and honestly it is the most frustrating thing I've played this far. Coming in from XCOM 2 and DnD, I thought that this game would hit the spot for me. But I hit the third fight in the Goblin Workshop, and I'm tempted to rip off my mouse and throw it at the screen, since the difficulty spikes up like my ♥♥♥♥ in the morning. The combat. The combat is just too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ unfair. First off, they deal way too much damage for any sort of tactics to work, and for goblin gunners it's like their weapons have infinite range, so while you're stuck fending off the tanky enemies and their goons, the gunners at about 666 miles away are comfortably shooting up your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You can go through a turn and find half your squad's health gone, which by the way also affects your stats. Theres also goblin bombers, who can whip out a virtually infinite set of grenades that will never miss, before most of your squad could even move anywhere. At least in DnD AoE attacks like this require the target to fail a Dexterity saving throw, but not here. Also, the accuracy rating that appears when you attack does NOT take into account the dodge/parry chances enemies have, so while your archer has a 92% chance to hit, the goblin also has a 24% to dodge that you'll have to manually inspect them to even know about. Enemies also pretty much ignore the risk from opportunity attacks, and will move as they please while they charge at your weakest member about 6 tiles away.And Critical failures. They are way too frequent to convince me that it's supposed to simulate rolling a 1 on an attack roll. Just before this review I've had at least 3 critical failures on attacks and even BUFFS which all dealt damage on myself, even though the probability of this happening is supposed to be 3%. The game tries to "offset" this by putting in a randomia or whatever meter that fills up whenever something unlucky happens to you, but it doesn't fill up enough to actually make much of a difference, and the effects aren't that useful to begin with, they only prolong your suffering.And the game has the gall to put in reinforcements for certain encounters, before the party has even dealt with the present crowd.SInce heals are on cooldown rather than spell slot, you can't just revive someone whos down and then revive someone else next turn. This would be all well and good, if said healed target didn't also immediately die by next turn, due to the insane amounts of damage they deal. The voice acting and dialogue is ok, but it doesn't really shine through for me. TL;DR: would be alright if not played on anything higher than normal, ♥♥♥♥ combat mechanics, and I'm glad I only bought this on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: ***** From our review on the blog. This is not my direct review, so don't mind my hours of play *****The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet of Chaos developed by Artefacts Studio and published by Dear Villagers is a turn-based tactical RPG set in a humorous fantasy world. The player takes control of the following group of seven characters with an additional added into the mix after a certain point in the story. The Ranger, the Elf, the Thief, the Ogre, the Wizardess, the Barbarian, and lastly, the Dwarf. The campaign is fixated around the party of heroes finding the Amulet of Chaos and guiding the group of unconventional heroes along their journey in finding the amulets origins as well as figuring out why dark forces are after it.The game starts out with an extremely helpful tutorial that teaches the player how to utilize each hero individually. You start off with the Ranger fighting a single orc. Shortly after, you are led to find the remaining members of your party throughout small-scale battles all while learning the mechanics of combat and each character. The tutorial does a solid job at easing the player into the plethora of options given to them without being too overwhelming. After a few fights and learning the technical of combat our heroes are united for a final fight. It is in this final fight that our heroes win the Amulet of Chaos via a goblin game show and start their journey down this treacherous path.After locating the Amulet the party is introduced to our central location, the Dungeon of Naheulbeuk, or more specifically the inn inside of the dungeon. The inn is the party’s main area in which they will act in a multitude of options such as: taking a rest and restoring health points, trading with merchants, talking to other bystanders, and meeting the other three playable characters. There are three additional characters that the player may recruit into their party after reaching a specific part of the story. One by one they will join your party for their own quest, giving the player a solid chance to see each character’s abilities and move sets.... _childDocuments_.review: I have to recommend this game to anyone who wants a turn based D&D style game with goofy characters and party banter. A lot of the dialogue is corny in English, but every once in a while it's laugh out loud funny. If this looks like the type of game you'd like, it really executes on what it wants to be, and I don't think anyone's ever made a tactical RPG quite this cute.    That said, I have one HUGE complaint about the game design that comes up a lot. Every attack has a percent success rate, but after hours of playing the game these rates are clearly not accurate. Game designer Sid Meier famously pointed out a quirk in human psychology: if you tell us we have an 80% chance to succeed at something, we'll feel cheated by RNG if we only succeed 80% of the time. Sid's solution to this was to secretly increase the player's chances, so the percent chance to succeed you see is actually lower than the actual chances. In The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk, they seem to have decided the opposite approach is better: tell people they have a 90% chance to succeed, and then make them fail about 1 out of 4 times. Part of this is because there are defensive systems like dodge and parry that aren't calculated into the success chance the game displays. But I'm pretty sure a character with a 65% chance to hit ends up missing every other attack. Whatever it is, something really feels like it needs to be adjusted here, whether it's boosting the player's chances secretly behind the scenes or just accurately calculating their success rate in the first place. As it is, the game makes you feel like you're perpetually unlucky... probably not what the designers were going for in a game that seems to be about goofy characters and light, fast paced turn based combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, though the game isn't perfect, this has been one of the most enjoyable gaming experiences I've ever had. The rich, detailed environments are astounding. Everything is so clean & vibrant. The characters are the same -- so alive and unique. But aside from the visual quality of the game, it has a crazy amount of personality. Some of the humor falls a bit flat, but some of the inside jokes are truly hilarious. The more you get to know the cast, the funnier the gags become. The story is excellent. The tactical-style battles are exciting & give you lots of options how to approach different challenges. It's the same with character-building. You have 3 different NPC's that can accompany the party, and each of them brings something different to the chemistry. Each time a character levels-up, you can choose a different set of increasingly powerful abilities. There is a learning curve to the game, but once you get to know the different characters (and their talents) you can help them work together with greater effectiveness. You will develop your own strategies that work best for your style. There are quite a few typos in the dialogue, but maybe that is because it was originally done in French (I believe). The voice acting is top notch (though the lines range from hokey to hilarious). Felicia Day's wizardess is particularly well done. It has quite a bit of adult language, as well, for those who care about such things. The variety of opponents could be better, and all the traps in the game are exactly the same. However, some encounters have different goals instead of simply killing. As you get better gear, your party changes its look to reflect becoming a higher-level group of adventurers.To sum up, the visuals, voice work, personality, and tactical battles are all an A+. The humor & story are an A. The typos & lack of enemy variety are minor annoyances that most players probably won't notice. But the game really has no drawbacks other than the price -- though I'd say it was worth every penny. My only complaint is that the DLC's are not coming out as quickly as I'd like. I can't wait for more content!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR A must-have tactical turn-based RPG for D&D fans and the Frenchies alike!Wot I liked- Explore dungeons, battle monsters in turn-based combat, grab loot, sell extra loot at the merchant, buy new loot at the merchant - the most basic fun gameplay loop that so many RPGS manage to fail;- Well-written, good-humored dialogue. Female or male narrator;- Smart, simple and logical tactical combat — it’s challenging, thought out, balanced (or unbalanced in a good way), with a GUI that actually helps you to analyse the information;- A proper D&D adventuring setting: a tavern, some storekeepers and a dungeon;- The game has 10 classes, each with its own skill tree (and other minor things like skins, equipment, banter and animation);- It seems that the game is based on a famous French webcomic - I'm real glad that the game adaptation was done so well;- Goodhearted parody of roleplaying with a bunch of geek references;- Enemy AI is far from the dum-dums you usually get in CRPGs;- I really enjoyed reading up all that flavour text and I haven’t found it over the top or corny;- The equipment changes your characters' appearances;- Good soundtrack (Rooftop, tavern and smooth jazz are my favourites);- Great customizeable controls with all the shortcuts one might need;- All the major fantasy archetypes are present: from a barbarian to... a dwarf;- Lighthearted artstyle.Wot I disliked- Bosses: the final boss, the final boss of the 2nd DLC, the secret boss - they ruin the game, I was very close to disliking the game in my review and certainly will never replay this game just not to experience them;- DLC fights are rife with unbalance: you fight with enemies who have 2x your numbers 3x your hp and 4x your damage;- DLC fights remind me of tactical puzzles from HoMM3;- There're a couple of difficulty spikes here and there- AI can abuse positioning because enemies have 3-4x health of your guys as AoOs are not powerful enough;- Some enemies can attack more than once per turn, you - don't;- Consumables take an attack action, which makes them highly unpopular;- My only nitpick to the controls - you cannot rotate the map with your mouse;- Lotsa rooms are locked till a certain point in the game (a chapter or a quest) without any explanations;- Minor typos;- You gotta backtrack through all the empty rooms in order to place a book in the cabinet or look for a questgiver;- Inability to customize your party reduces replayablility value (you can only do it in 1 DLC).To sum it all up, it's been an excellent, light-hearted challenging fun adventure embodying the spirit of adventuring mainstream D&D games lost 10-20 years ago. Makes you happy that the 2020s are giving us gem after gem: Pillars of Eternity 2, Pathfinder series and Dungeon of Nububaba have everything a true CRPG ought to have to join the pantheon. Hope a sequel with just more of the stuff is underway.P.S. No spoiler advice: stock up on consumables and don't sell your stuff when you're nearing any story end.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! (9,5/10) You have a fixed group of 8 given characters, that have several interactions and ways to combo with each others. Great tactics and well designed fights, combined with uncomplicated and relaxed story/exploring. I was skeptical at first, as I usually do not like the "wacky pop art style and humor in games, in Naheulbeuk it surprisingly works though. I then realized that this game is not only hard, it also has a deep, well made and thought out fighting system with great mechanics. These fighting mechanics, which are very close to D&D 4E are easy to learn but hard to master. Everything is transparent and has a clean presentation. However, after 3 playthroughs on nightmare I can ensure that there is a HUGE learning effect and understanding the different team interactions is not trivial. Like: -D&D 4E Style of combat (3-4 different and unique powers per characters with distinct effect and damage)    -Diverse Party members that compliment each other in different ways-Nearly every stat effect and power is well described -Fantastic encounter designs, enemies do compliment each other in their ability -Linear story with not too much searching around (yes for me, that's a plus!)Dislike (minor):-At the beginning the game is TOO random: Your guys do miss a lot (even if you use buffs and positional bonus) AND the opponents have a chance to parry/evade as well. As the game progresses, hit rates quickly cap out at 97% and the game depends less on the odds.For me, BY FAR the best D&D 4E like turn based combat game, so far. Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: This game really surprised me.  I initially skipped this game when it came out because the cartoony graphics were unappealing and parody games usually aren't very good for more than a cheap laugh.  However I ended up buying it because it was made by a French studio, and my partner was studying French for a job, so I would play it in French and my partner would practice by translating to me.  It turns out, this is one of the better turn-based tactical CRPGs of the past 10 years.The first thing that struck me is the excellent UX.  The UI is crisp and clear and easy to use, whereas many games in the genre have terrible UIs and poor information on how the game works (looking at you, Owlcat's Pathfinder series).  The inventory management is easily the best I have ever seen in any RPG.  The victory screen at the end of combat gives you all the loot right there, whereas most other games require you to individually click each body and sort through all the loot.  The victory screen also gives you an after-battle report of all the damage and injuries your characters received, with buttons to easily spend your consumables to heal them.  There are very clear tooltips for every stat on the character screen, making it easy to understand how the game works mechanically.  The game lets you know when you've found a best in slot item by giving it a gold border.  If there isn't a best in slot item for that slot, none of the items for that slot will have a gold border.The tactical combat is fun and engaging.  On hard difficulty, it requires some careful thought, planning, and good character building, which is exactly what I want out of a turn-based tactical RPG.  Character abilities are unique and interesting and each character has a lot of options in combat by the later levels, but not too many.  While it is possible to build your character poorly, the game's build recommendations actually explain how to make an optimized and effective character, another thing most CRPGs do very poorly.The cartoony graphics, while I dislike personally, make sense for the style of game.  The animations, however, really grew on me.  The character animations are very funny and add to the comedy of the story, especially the ranger's derpy run.  My partner loved the chickens.  The comedy story is nothing special, and the style of humor is dated and feels very early 2000s, and there are a couple lines that use ableist language, but some of the less offensive jokes got a good laugh out of me.  The voice acting was quite good, sometimes the actors' delivery alone carried a joke when the writing wasn't that great.The game engine feels smooth and good, the load times are quick, and the game runs almost as well on my 10 year old gaming PC as it does on my brand new gaming laptop.  Despite being a much newer game, it runs far better than Pathfinder: Kingmaker or Pillars of Eternity: Deadfire.  I'm not sure how the devs managed to make the game run so well on old hardware, but kudos to them.  The game was nearly bug-free.  I think I had one single lockup in over 100 hours of play, and one bug towards the end of the game, which the devs fixed in their final patch!  Bugs remaining unfixed years after development seems to be accepted practice in the CRPG genre and the gaming industry in general these days, so it's nice to see such a smooth bug-free game for a change.Overall, my expectations were low for this game, but it ended up landing on my list of top 10 CRPGs of the past 10 years.  I did multiple playthroughs in about 120 hours and had a lot of fun every time.  I wish other CRPG developers would look at what Naheulbeuk does right with UX design because it's better than all of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Get this game if you like this type of game!!!I have to give credit to the devs. for coming up with this near master piece. The dialog is just perfect and I never once skipped anything because I wanted to hear how the characters interacted. Especially, the insults between the dwarf and elf are top shelf.I do have a couple of things I didn't like:- When you move a character, you are only told who you can hit with ranged attacks but not the hit %- When you want to attack something, you are told how much damage you will do, but the numbers you see don't take into account any deduction the monster has. Thus, the damage you do will be less than what is indicated and that means your planning goes out the window.- Traps will reappear even after you have cleared a level. This is nothing game-breaking but just annoying especially if you just rested back to full health.- I like that all characters have two kinds of abilities (active and passive) but some have more useful abilities than others. For example, some ranged characters get a bonus if they stay next to a melee character, which is pretty useless since you don't want you ranged units in melee range.- The ogre needs to spend two ability points on skills that will let him break through some special doors throughout the game. These two points are otherwise completely wasted. Okay, you don't need to open those doors but you will miss out on some loot and in one case, a side quest. Adding something else to those skills would make it easier to choose them.- I never found out how to reset my abilities, but that may just be my own fault.- There are some rooms that require you to answer a riddle in the sense that you need to give the door the object that is the answer. However, these objects take up weight in your bag and can be sold, so you may not have them when you need them. This means, you need to run back to the vendor you sold it to. Generally speaking, this is a bit of a headache.None of the problems mentioned are game breakers and I will not hesitate to buy a DLC for the game or another similar product from the same developer.Also, it shows that I have 11.6 hours played but that isn't correct. It may be because I played most of it in offline mode since I had no internet for some days. I completed the game earlier today and would say I played around 25 hours in total.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you like Dungeons & Dragons and have a lot of patience, you might enjoy this. But fair warning, it's a bit buggy, inconsistent, and the voice acting is definitely not for everyone. It's a turn-based party RPG set in a tower, on a quest that is a lot more complicated than it seems. It feels similar to playing a real DnD campaign with friends. There are bad jokes, sweary dwarves, and a lot of fantasy cliches. Overall, there's a decent game in here - but enjoying it takes a bit of effort and perseverance. It has some great ideas and a coherent style, although it's missing that final level of polish that makes it really great.+ Genuinely made me laugh+ You can set waypoints for moving to avoid certain enemies+ Characters swear just like a person playing DND (and they're beeped out, which is always funny)+ Comical weapon names like a "Lame-ass longbow"+ The male narrator's voice sounds like Wil Wheaton+ To help counteract "hit percentages", you gain charge in a meter every time something 'unfortunate' happens, which you can then use as a buff later (although the fails are a bit over the top, and the gauge doesn't compensate enough)+ References to Monty Python, LOTR, Skyrim, Baldurs Gate and Doctor Who+ My Wizardess rolled a critical fail on a spell, and the Dwarf yelled "Yer magic is ♥♥♥♥♥!", later someone else called her a "useless muggle". My Wizardess rolled critical fails A LOT+ The ogre gets a move that lets him pick up the dwarf and throw him at a group of enemies+ Most of the game is fully voiced- Completely unpronounceable and unmemorable title- There are a couple of "run around an entire floor until you find the right thing to click on" quests which aren't entertaining- The voices are generally pretty good, but some of them are really annoying- Aside from the original 7 characters, you can also choose either the paladin, priestess or bard. Choosing one removes the other two from the game. It's a shame - I did want all of them, or at least swap out / have them around to try- Moving the characters around when out of combat is really clunky. 1, Characters stop moving if you rotate the camera. 2, Trying to rotate the camera is way too sensitive on keyboard and swings around wildly- There's no combat log, so I can't see what just killed a character if an enemy used an ability. The Priest is randomly taking damage at the start of her turn with no debuff and I can't find out why- Characters talk too quickly- I probably would have preferred the characters to say nothing in battle rather than the same 2 voice lines per character on repeat for 30 hours- Loading screens are quite long on an SSD- The game takes a really long time to get going. Abilities are limited for a long time, and it's only after about 20 hours that the thief becomes useful- If a fight is too hard, there's basically nothing you can do about it. There's nowhere to go and level up, and if all the sidequests are done and you've bought all the gear...- Characters have a Stamina/mana bar and each ability has a cooldown. The stamina and mana seems kinda pointless because the cooldowns are so long, you can usually use each ability only once per fight- Finished it in 35 hours. It could do with being about 10 hours shorter- The rolls can be kind of a joke sometimes. I got 3 critical fails in a row, in two separate fights- The game was originally French, and the number of copies sold seems to be quite low, which means there's no info on the internet about the puzzles, or some of the abilities- One of the NPCs is bugged as IO_NAME_AS_C06_GisbertCell- The elf and the priest both have the skill that stops lightning and ricochet arrows from hitting allies, but from chapter 6 onwards, it always bounces to allies- You can attack people through walls, both ranged and melee.- The marker for handing in Co-op Heist is wrong. The marker says the courier is off the map to the south west of the dungeon, but he's standing in the Inn- Some achievements don't pop- When you're deciding where to move, there are indicators for whether you can hit an enemy with a ranged weapon. Sometimes the indicators don't show up- After using a skill reset potion, all my characters in the menu disappeared and were replaced with a white box- Cure major wounds is a 'anged' spell- Loubet's anticipation "developped"- rats as big as baors- Elven Ricochet targets "friend of foe"- If I am to believe my dictionnary- Books: "The Barbarians 1/3", "The Barbarians 2/3" and "Barbarians 3/3"- In the English version of the game, the save menu has a button that says "retour" (return, in French)- controling- negociation- destructible objetcs- faittful
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long time since I laughed this much while playing a game. This is the type of game I always want to play. Some good points:- Endless humors: you will find it everywhere, from the item / skill names and descriptions, to the narratives, the conversations and even in the random stuff the characters say from time to time. At one time I had to listen to my phone while playing, and thus keep the characters idle for a few minutes and hear they complain, lol it's nothing new, most RPG has it but the way the say it is completely unexpected. In short, you will laugh more than you think.- Voice acting: it has really nice voice acting. All the characters sound natural and unique. Oh I love it every time the Wizardess tells me to be careful with her books.- Pace of the game: the pace is really nice. There is nothing to grind, nothing to rush. There is some backtracks to do but  very minimal, and just for a completionist sack. Overall if you pay close attention the the surrounding, and highlight intractable objects regularly you won't miss much. It takes just about 40 hours to complete the game, and trust me it's a wonderfully relaxing 40 hours.Some things the game can improve:- The balance: the game is a bit hard in the beginning, but too easy mid game on with only challenging battles being boss battles. I played in the hardest difficulty and mid game on I just breeze through most of combats. In the beginning it's sometimes too hard that I had to turn off the persistent RNG seed option and save scum a few fights, I haven't played it on easy but I think it would be too easy from beginning to end then.- Build options: each characters have 2 recommended stats, but honestly I mostly just dump points into agility and courage. Agility for accuracy, which is everything in this game, and courage for CC resistance (which is also everything in the early game) + to put my characters in correct action order. It's the same build for every characters, dumping AGI in the early game, then late game respect and give just enough AGI for accuracy, then the rest to STR/INT for damage, all that while keeping relative COURAGE for action order. Other stats simply don't play a big role at all.- Items: similar the point above, the items are very limited, each characters have only like 2-3 pieces of equipment for each tier (bronze / silver / gold), so there is not much options to do.I guess that the game's main focus is not about char building, it has 8 characters with their own expertises and it's about using their expertises efficiently. In that sense I can understand the cons listed above, it may be a bad thing, but may also be a good thing. I think because there are not many options for me to do, it's rather a relaxing run for me.TL;DR: worth picking at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Why oh why does steam reviews do not have neutral option... Or better yet scale grading system. Because on the scale from 1 to 10 the game is somewhere around 6 or 7. Although maybe i did not play it long enough, but still here are my thoughts about it.The game itself is tactical rpg with humor and parody thrown in. The funny bits are not as bad as some other games i know, can make you chuckle for sure. The common tropes are executed really well. It feels like you are following a story of defaultish guys (like, a bimbo, a jock, a nerd, That Silent Guy, and such) playing their first DnD campaign, and i really like it most of the time. So narrative wise the game is solid 9 (would be a 10 if i did not find myself too tired of some jokes).But then comes the gameplay. The gameplay itself is fairly simple - you run, you loot, you solve some default-ish puzzles, you speak to NPC with barely any (there are really ultra rare cases where you can select an option) control of the dialogue whatsoever (which makes me sad) and then you fight. Last thing is what you do most, so lets stop on it a bit more.The fighting itself is mostly basic: you have two AP, which you spend to move, to attack, or both to strafe. You have special abilities, which you use to turn the tide of battle in your favor. There are status effects like poison or knocked prone. Some guys are melee, some are ranged, you can speck yourself somewhat towards the playstyle you would prefer. But it all feels... lacking. For example, with movement you spend your AP no matter how far you moved. I mean, sure, there is a way to place waypoints, but why? It's feels too basic by todays standarts, it's like playing RTS which doesn't use rmb to move/attack and you have to select those manually. The other problem with combat i have is that just as moving any ammount of distance = spending ap, doing anything at all = spending the other. Thief goes stealth? Costs ap. Ogre sniffs for invisibles? Costs ap. Ranges activates aura? Costs ap! And you need to activate aura each and every time you enter the battle. Since the game makes fun of DnD, maybe it also should learn something from it, like move actions, free actions, re actions... Many actions are just not worth the action point you spend on them. Meanwhile enemies are actually throwing marks or getting extra AP for free. Feels annoying man.Also the gear, it is quite lacking in the gameplay related department. Like, there is crapton of fluff funny "haha, chopped goblin arm, lets take it" stuff, but i found another axe for dwarf at the chapter 4, meaning all the time before he had to walk around with basic chopper. And it wouldn't be as bad, if it was also somewhat like DnD, and better axe meant a tiny bit more accuracy and damage. But here it means double your previous damage, which means that you REALLY need a better gear. And while the dungeon has four (or maybe even more, i just don't know abouth other ones yet) shops, they sell you barely any equipment. But a lot of beer and sausages. Yay i guess.Also your party has access to some easy healing. Like sorceress can actually cure minor wounds (multiclassed into priest that one, i'm telling ya). Ranger learns some basic first aid. Elf with some elven magic makes pain pain go away-sies. But if you didn't do all that stuff before the combat end, tough luck, your only way of pain relief are potions and sausages now. Why, exactly? Also lets talk about potions: there are stuff like burn heal, freeze heal, posion cure which would be nice... if using one did not spent your acton point. And ate a slot at your belt, because no accessing inventory in fight. And you need specific type of potion for specific type of ailment. So you would rather just go without them and just tank the status effects like a man.Finally i don't like the fact that i can't make my own party. I mean, i get it, storywise they are all important, and i shouldn't be greedy. But then make them actually not sucking for *insert your deity of choise name here* sake! Like the thief which has no need to go invisible, since he has 0 passives to dish out damage on unsuspecting opponents. Or dwarf, which was (and still is) just a walking meat shield. By the way, why does his charge ends in him just chopping the enemy? I mean, it may be me not understanding the joke here, but shouldn't charge attack be made as a tackle with your shield? Or helmet with horns at least? So yeah, i can live without me being able to make my own party. But make the default party feel not so wastefull then.On a side note, the side quests - they suck. Barely any reward, and any satisfaction for completing them.Overall the game is okay to good, but not at the must play territory. If on sale, then take it, if not, then think about whenever you would wan't to play some X-COM but worse. I am putting no just to balance it a little bit towards the 70% of positive rewievs, which i believe is quite right for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've not heard of the original "Le donjon de Naheulbeuk", but the game introduces the player into the world very well.I'm not too big on turnbased combat games and i failed miserably on the hard difficulty, but once i switched it to normal it was very enjoyable, even for a beginner in the genre.You start with a large party of characters:The Ranger, the Thief, the Wizardess, the Elf, the Dwarf, the Barbarian and the Ogre.They don't actually have names, they only refer to each other by their classnames basically.Each of them pretty much does what it says on the tin, no surpises here, but the skilltrees do offer a nice bit of customization on how you want to build your party.You could focus on more offensive abilites, defensive or supportive ones or have a nice mixture of each, as all character usually get a good choice of skills that each cater to different playstyles like that.So even though the Barbarian will probably mostly focus on dealing as much damage as he can, you still get skills like his warcry, which let him buff the damage and accuracy of the attacks of allies in range.Early on in the game you also get the chance to recruit one more character to your party to round things off:The Priestress, focusing on healing, the Paladin, focusing on defense and lockdown and the bard focused on supporting and debuffing.In the beginning of the game i found combat to be a little lackluster, as you lack a lot of options, but once you level up a few times and can choose abilities to your liking, the combat really opens up.You get a lot more control of the battlefield, be it through statuseffects on enemies or movement abilities that let you travel around the battlefield much more efficiently, at which point it became a lot more fun.There's only a few things i disliked about combat, mostly early on.The game gives characters differing amounts of exp after each battle, depending on how much they contributed. More importantly though, they can also get a penalty to how much XP they gain if they "died" during combat.In my case this led to one of my characters being constantly behind and less effective in combat for quite a while and him getting less XP each combat only made the issue worse. This didn't really add much to the game other than making characters that already lag behind even worse and the game probably would've been better off without it.Another thing i disliked was the healing after battles.In the early game gold is pretty hard to come by and healing potions are quite expensive (as well as bandages to heal permanent injuries you suffer when a characters HP reaches 0).For the price of a few potions you could however go to the tavern and rest to fully heal all characters' HP and wounds, for a relatively cheap price, definitely cheaper than buying potions and bandages to heal each character individually.This kind of leads to the player being incentivized to constantly backtrack to the tavern while exploring the dungeon or following the quest, since healing on the go is too expensive early on (and still inefficient later on even when you have enough gold).I would've preferred if you just automatically healed after each fight and made potions more geared toward useage during fights instead.These are overall not that big of a deal, however they're still pretty annoying issues overall in terms of gameplay.Still, all that is swept away by the charm of the storytelling and the characters' shenanigans, as well as the fantastic voice acting (i played with english voices) of the main party.The humor certainly is not going to be everyones cup of tea however, so do be warned that it's very crude and meanspirited in nature.For the most part the characters really lean into the stereotypes of their classes and races, like the Barbarian being dumb as a brick and caring for naught but battle or the Dwarf being a stingy, greedy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.You get a lot of dialogue strewn throughout quests, mostly of the Party bickering and insulting each other or whichever foe they just ran into.The game doesn't take itself serious at all so the meanspirited dialogue doesn't become too overbearing and i found it just very funny overall.Most NPCs share the same few voiceactors just doing different voices. They're mostly not as amusing or as fitting as the main casts' but they still get the job done most of the time. Sometimes they feel a little unfitting but it's not a large issue, since you won't be speaking to most NPCs a whole lot anyways.Overall i rather enjoyed my time with this game and may even check out the original stories if they're available in english.The cast is leaning very hard into DnD-tropes and makes fun of it's stereotypes.If you're a fan of that, meanspirited humor and turnbased combat, this is probably going to be the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Tons of potential, none of it acted upon.Let's start with gameplay. i.e. combat. It seems fun at first glance, and tempts you early on, but battles are fought in a constant state of losing. Even if you end up winning, you're always losing along the way, and it doesn't work as fun. Every battle after the tutorials are so insanely hard, that I'm pretty sure they're designed with the expectation that you'll lose about half you're party every fight. Which means if, like me, you get a combat with insanely bad luck (4 crits for the enemy, 3 crit misses for me, a quadra miss on a 4x attack, a partial parry by an enemy surviving with 2 HP, etc.), even the mechanic designed to offset bad luck isn't enough. Once the AI has spent ~10 seconds per enemy thinking about what it wants to do, it is absolutely brutal, flanking and backstabbing regardless of personal positioning, which is especially hard to deal with if you can't start someone weak behind cover and they go near last in initiative order.Then there's the characters/dialogue. Again, lots of potential, but poorly executed. The ranger's voice sounded interesting at first, until it's clear he reads everything without verbal punctuation, which kinda sets the tone for the dialogue as well, 80% is jokes, 5% of which are funny. I laughed at one. The humor isn't bad, it's just forced in between every line of meaningful dialogue, and quickly becomes repetitive. I did like the thief character, and every character has a sliver of something intriguing, except maybe the elf, but there constant repeating of the same three jokes each one tells becomes grating quickly.Again, there's clearly potential here. Some of the basic humoral and non-humoral premises are fun, the level up mechanic caught my interest, and I love the idea of an XCOM style combat with fantasy themes and melee abilities. I just found that I spent most of my non-combat time feeling like everything was taking too long, and most of my combat time like I was losing an unfair battle and wanted to kill somebody. And it was especially annoying watching the enemy whose turn it was idle for sometimes up to around 10 seconds before taking its turn.If it looks like something you'd like, give it a try, but I was personally disappointed with my experience. Take that as you will.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really wants to be a fun, comical, D&D-like experience. Where players laugh, be merry, and go on weird, quirky adventures. The humor is just poorly and lazily written, the characters unlikable and 2-dimensional, and the combat pretty generic. The tutorial is cumbersome and slows down the actual game - if I have to go through a 2-hour multi-part tutorial to play your game, you've already lost me. As a huge RPG player with hundreds of hours in turn based strategy games, this is a game that I literally could not stand to sit through after less than an hour. Its cringe comedy and campy, and it's just not my style.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I enjoy the game. It is fun, and enjoyable. It is honestly a very approachable games that just about anyone can play...as long as foul mouthed chuckle head heroes don't bother you. Controls are mixed, in the sense that I switch between XBox controller and Mouse/Keyboard on the fly.  I prefer each for specific reason. Traversing the dungeons feels better with controller, as it just gives a nice smooth feel.  Mouse and Keyboard are great for the turn based combat. Your mileage may vary.Second, issues. If you go with one control method over the other, you will undoubtedly find things that annoy you.  Just don't let the mild control issues deter you.  The dialog is also not for children.  Innuendo's and all manner of swearing is abundant here.  I have no issue with it.  However, I wouldn't recommend this for little Timmy that wants to have a fun dungeon romp with cartoonish graphics.  It isn't raunchy, but it is definitely something to keep an ear out if you let Little Timmy play.Lastly, the strategy is not overwhelming, nor is it difficult to understand.  There are difficulty levels that you can play this game at to meet your enjoyment/challenge preferences.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing - for the price the game has a lot of content, took me 28h to beat it on normal mode and I avoided most of the side quests and riddles. So just for content/price ratio I recommend it.Second thing - the humour in the game is nice but also cringe and cliche, so after a few first laughs you will probably start skipping the next banter between chartacters and npcs, and the next and the next and the next... But overall the humour apart from making fun of other games and known fantasy tropes is what you could hear in any pen and paper RPG session (especially supported with beer) where players make fun of each other characters and overall fantasy themes.Third thing - the fighting in the game is done nicely with a lot of tactical stuff to consider. I.e. you can try try to stick together and get bonuses from characters standing to each other, but be prone to AOE damage, or you could spread for defence but loose some of the synergies and support these tactics with each character skillset (resetable by elixir if you chose wrongly). Positioning in the game is important as well as facing enemies to support other characters hitting them and you not showing your back to the enemy so they can not backstab you for more damage.The ugly thing - I get the game is about being cursed by the god of the misfortune, but when you have 170% chance of hit at knocked down enemy and you get two critical misses in a row resulting in your characters slipping over and knocking themselves down it can be frustrating. As well as having enemies, critially parry, dodge or immune and live with 1hp. I guess that's how it would look in traditional RPG with dice rolls and criticals on 1 and 20. But it would be less frustrating if I had max 95% hit chance and miss than having almost 200% hit chance and critially miss. Or at least would have note somewhere that would say that I always have 1% chance to critically miss even if I hit.The nice thing - graphics are OK, a bit plastic but it gives the charm to the silly overall theme of the game. And the main story line is actually quite captivating.

_childDocuments_.review: "The worse — the better" is this game's motto. But not the utter lack of balance in mechanics.After completion of the core game on Gzor's Nightmare difficulty with no save-scumming during combat, all I can say is DON'T.Play on normal, uninstall and forget. And a mature 18+ tag.This is NOT the game I would allow my children to play."Prepare your ass!", my ass.Apart from that, it COULD be a good game. But it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very charming turn-based RPG that likes to make fun of the genre and not take itself seriously. I just happened to stumble upon it while looking for something new to play.  The premise is very simple: you're a (awful) band of adventurers that were hired to undertake a quest into the Dungeon of Naheulbeuk and recover a statue. The graphics remind me of something on the WC3 or Torchlight level, but it's very charming. The voice acting is very well done, and includes a lot of sarcastic humor. Some folks might find the Elf annoying, but she doesn't bother me. I think all of the characters are charming. Inventory has tabs that you can select to more easily navigate your items (all, weapons, armor, misc, etc.). Leveling up is done in a standard RPG fashion. You gain enough exp, level up then invest 2 stat points and 2 skill points (one passive one active) per level. Equipment is done in a somewhat paper doll fashion. You equip the items in the slots and your character's appearance changes. The one thing that really does bother me about this game is the camera. You can play in isometric view or third person view, but neither is that great. isometric doesn't zoom out enough for my taste and the third person feels awkward for such a large party.Despite not taking itself seriously, the combat is actually pretty deep and tactical. There are objects that you can blow up to create hazards and afflict status ailments (think DOS and DOS2, but without all of the combos), there are plenty of skills to learn (both passive and active) to create diverse builds and you can can do one movement and one action per turn. You can also delay your turn to help improve strategy. There is also an observation phase before combat, that allows you to place your party within a selected area to prepare for battle. If a character falls in battle, you get 3 turns to heal them to bring them back into the fray, or they are out for the remainder of combat. Characters who fall in combat will suffer injuries (up to a level 3 severity) which cause penalties. Also, make sure to pay attention to the tool tips and plan ahead! Certain characters are good and bad at things (the Elf is great with the bow, but sucks in melee, the wizardess is a great caster but frail, the barbarian hits hard but has low accuracy, etc.). You will need to use certain combos and placements to help boost the chances of your party's survival. Flanking, attacking from behind, status effects and much more all affect the chance to hit, dodge attacks and survive. Have fun with it and experiment! There are also several difficulty levels you can choose from. I am playing on normal and combat seems very well balanced, so I imagine the harder difficulties will give you a greater challenge.Everything this game does, it does very well. I personally haven't encountered any bugs yet, but that doesn't mean they might not be there. The autosave feature is very aggressive, but you can create manual saves so I don't see the harm in that. If you want a lighthearted RPG that doesn't take itself seriously like the Divinity series, but want turn-based combat that can get pretty intense (also like Divinity), this game might just be for you. I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I played in french to get the original Naheulbeuk feel from the audio seriesAnyone who already knows that they enjoy Naheulbeuk content should get the game, because, even if you don't like the gameplay, the game is worth going through for the story/humor/writing/references (just put it on normal or easy). That said, I do think some of the voice acting (especially for the secondary characters) is subpar, and that the timing/arrangement of lines sometimes undermines the delivery. But still, it is fun and funny.As for the gameplay, it is a mix of TTRPGs and XCOM (characters can flank and have overwatch), with a bigger focus on abilities and melee combat. If you hate RNG, this is not the game for you! That said, you get rewarded with special abilities when you get unlucky enough times, which is a nice balancing mechanic. But the mechanics are interesting, and even those which I have seen before in other games have been tweaked enough to feel fresh.I definitely recommend playing on difficulty 3/4 like I did. For the first ~half of the game, the level of challenge felt just right, with some very close victories with a single character still standing and the occasional reload. There was only one fight that I found really stupidly hard. Around level 5-6 though, the game started getting easier and easier until the encounters felt really too easy. The last couple of fights (plus the bonus/secret one) felt better but not perfect.The lasts a good while, though maybe 50 hours is a better estimate of how long it would take to finish the game for someone not going out of their way to do ALL of the extra stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Refreshing look at party-based RPG. This game is filled with humorous pokes at fantasy genre tropes and other more subtle references in the culture without stepping too far out for immersion. I felt more like I was having fun around a table with nerdy friends than trying hard to comprehend a story that took itself seriously.The characters were stereotypical representatives of the fantasy genre we've seen over the years, so true fans would get a kick out of the shallow displays of their tendencies and traits.  The elf is an airheaded forest bunny. The ranger is a 20-something "hero guy" with an underdog style of leadership. The thief is a shivering coward. The dwarf is everything you'd expect of a Gimli impression from LOTR. The barbarian is a close approximation of the Conan character from the 1980s films, and the mage is like an intern just trying to navigate her way into what she once thought to be her dream job. The ogre (who looks a bit like Shrek, but only speaks in ogrish) seems like a sidekick with 2-dimensional quips about eating.This is NOT a serious big-story RPG for hardcore gamers of the RPG genre. This IS a great time for fans of the fantasy genre who also enjoy RPGs looking for a chance at having fun in a more comedy-centered experience.The music and sound design are excellent. The art is a bit cartoony, but it works. The gameplay is pretty solid for a turn-based tactical styled RPG. Loading screens take too long, in my opinion.All in all, a fun time. I definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun turn-based tactics RPG with deep, satisfying combat. As a fan of this genre, I found a lot to like here. Humor and style is similar to  so if you appreciated that game, you will almost certainly like this one.  is not without it's flaws, but they're mostly outshined by the great battles.The good:* Excellent combat really makes the whole game. Enemies are varied and interesting. Tactics stack well and combos are satisfying.* Some unique mechanics that I haven't encountered before such as "backstab" (bonus damage) when a character is facing away from an attacker and the ability to revive fallen heroes if you can get to them fast enough.* Skill trees are fun to explore and encourage experimentation.* Normal difficulty offers a good balance of light challenge and steady progression. I found I could win most battles on the first try (except 1-2 side quests where I was outclassed and needed to return later). Fallen heroes are not permanently killed so losing 1-2 in battle isn't too punishing. Die-hard players looking for a tough challenge might see that as a negative, but I thought it was a good way to keep the game moving forward.The bad:* Moving around the dungeon in between battles gets tiresome quickly, especially in later chapters when you're bouncing around to places you've already been. Traps will sap your party's health repeatedly until they're dismantled, which is more annoying than anything.* Inventory management is also tedious. Loot is easy to come by on Normal difficulty, but the UI to match new equipment with the characters who can actually use it requires too much clicking around. New and old loot also gets mixed together in inventory. There's a  option that's supposed to help with that, but I didn't find it very useful.The ugly:* The game is full of dated stereotypes that feel totally out of place in 2022. The elf bimbo and flamboyantly gay minstrel are the most cringe-worthy examples, but it doesn't end there. Strong males make up the front lines while the womenfolk are relegated to the back as range casters and healers. I get that this is based on a French audio series from twenty years ago, but that's no excuse. Fortunately, there are game settings to turn off the idle character chit-chat, which makes their personalities somewhat bearable.Overall, if you're a fan of turn-based tactics, this game is worth your time despite its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: The game combines tactical turn based combat, exploration and character progression with a quirky story, and I liked this combination a lot. The writing is whimsical and refers to many cliches in fantasy books, movies and RPGs. This is probably not everyone's cup of tea, but I found it funny, and sometimes the game genuinely made me laugh.But it also made me angry, especially when an enemy with 20% dodge chance evaded three attacks in a row (probability of that is less than 1%) and then resisted the next hit negating the damage. However, the battle system is built around the fact that your heroes will miss or otherwise fail their attacks. The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk features a unique anti-bad RNG mechanic: when you fail, you get energy that can be spent on positive actions in addition to your heroes' action. The most expensive bonus even allows you to ressurect the whole party, so until at least one of your characters is alive, it's not over.Keep in mind, I finished the game on the highest difficulty where enemies have more HP and resistance, so it will be easier on normal, but even then your characters will miss with their attacks, get parried or evaded, or even make critical fails, hurting or even incapacitating themselves in the process. However, failing is a part of the game, and unlike in XCOM or BG it doesn't feel unfair. The only fight I wasn't able to beat on the highest difficulty is the optional boss, and only because he summons unlimited adds which I can't kill fast enough, so they overwhelm the party eventually (focusing the boss doesn't work because these adds can heal him for 20% HP and he already is rather beefy).Overall, The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk is a great mix of turn based tactics and RPG, and if you are fine with the fact that the game won't take itself seriously and will break the fourth wall all the time, then you should definitely try it.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally I said some bad stuff about this game more so about how unfair it is against the player ie some enemies have 3 moves per turn, some even do buffs that skip your turns almost entirely, and enemies can go farther than you and still attack you. My biggest gripe with this game is missing with a high hit percentage about 50% of the time which makes no sense but RNG can go both ways. AoE's are the way go because those skills will carry you throughout fights. The game is beautiful from the art design, character designs, weapons, and on-point cliche characters that stand out, my favorite one is the bard because I do love how he not only buffs allies & debuffs foes but also packs a punch. _childDocuments_.review: At the core, there's a robust and rewarding turn based squad combat game, and the graphics and sound design are solid. But so far there's too little combat (mostly 'signature fights', not really anything along the lines of trash mobs to work on your tactics or understand your squad), the interface can be sluggish, and the fights are frustrating in terms of introducing new mechanics without any explanation (see the lack of trash mobs).Also I'm not sure how so many reviews are praising the writing- it's too bland to even be juvenile. It's like an old Dungeon or Dragon magazine comic stretched out for an entire game.  Not confident enough to either be serious or tell actual jokes, the dialogue just pinballs around things that the writers thinks were cliches but I'm not sure ever were. The Ranger is horny! This isn't really interesting as a concept and none of the lines around it would be funny to a 14 year old, but it's all they got. The dwarf is greedy, and they're going to remind you every 5 minutes. The elf is ditsy, and you get reminded of that every 4 minutes.  The Barbarian is sorta based off Conan? Every 2 minutes. This would maybe be less of a problem if cutscenes didn't seem to occupy as much of the gameplay as the brief moments you get to explore an area.

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting tactical RPG with lots of funny synchronisation of the game characters and a nice and long story. The game graphics and items are designed beautifully and the mixture of the game tactics and characters complexity, as well as simplicity makes the game for an old school role-play gaming fan like me a very interseting alternative to sometimes too complicated RPGs, where the player may loose himself in the unnecessary abundance of choices and possibilities. The game is easy, straight up and also suitable for younger people. As conservative RPG fan, you will probably have to give the game a chance and some leeway in the beginning, since it has some rather unique way to introduce the story and the dungeon, which some people might find a little bit to constrained; but believe me it's the start of the game and then it really develops into a nice rather classical-style RPG with lots of modern and funny elements. The only thing that bothered me though, were the sometimes inadequate descriptions or lack of tactical fight parameters and the pesudo-randomization, e.g. critical misses, that seemed to be intrinsic over a few rounds, so that a continous saving of the game was unfortunately very necessary and the intrinsic game character tactical faults could only be avoided by either doing something total different (like dodging or moving, instead of attacking) or just accepting the fault and the collect some failure compensation points, that are used in the game to somehow equalize the "bad luck", which is unfortunately intrinsic and not renewed randomly calculated like any sane programmer would do. Nonetheless a very recommendable RPG! I loved the game playthrough. JakobGu

_childDocuments_.review: Very polished game. The dialogue and story is 100% comedy, which can swing from cringe-worthy unfunny to genuinely funny. However, the characters are preset with a single skill-tree, there are no random encounters, and the only replayability may come from choosing one of three characters for your eighth party member. It is not really enough to replay the same game. So if you're wondering why this game doesn't have a "community," it is because it designed to be taken out, enjoyed, then put away, like any story. It is a fun, streamlined, and polished experience, but with no replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A charming, funny, turn-based RPG with more depth and interest than you might think. It's very fun to play, and hard to put down. You'll be doing "one more thing" and then realise five hours have passed. --With Baldur's Gate 3 entering early access, I wanted to scratch the turn-based RPG itch, and this game scratched it alright, though not in the way I might have expected. Based on a series of French stories with the same name, Dungeons of Naheulbeuk is at first quite a simple proposition - you start with a predetermined party of 7 archetypal characters - ranger, elf, dwarf, ogre, wizard, barbarian and thief. Early on you'll get the choice of 1 more party member from a selection of three - paladin, minstrel or priestess. I was initially a bit gutted at not being able to make my own character, but it quickly becomes apparent why that's not an option. Each pre-made character is wonderfully written and voice-acted throughout the whole game. The party dynamic is fun and funny, and you can tell a lot of work has gone into the creation and animation for this band of misfits. The game has a lot going for it. It's lengthy (finished it at 45 hours), it's funny, it looks great if you like the cartoonish animation (which I definitely did). The combat, being the main area of interest, is well done. Think X-Com, it's all about positioning, use of cover, synergy of abilities and generally hitting the sh*t out of enemies. The spells available and the animations make the combat feel great. It's far from perfect though. The difficulty curve is not where it should be - the game starts quite difficult but then your power gains through levels and items make the encounters feel fairly trivial from about the halfway point on-wards. Fights are still enjoyable, but I rarely felt at risk of losing a fight whilst playing on the default difficulty. There are also very few choices to make in terms of the story - this isn't a sprawling web of decisions like in some other RPGs. Instead your decision making comes from gear, spell and talent options. This is fine, but it can make the game feel a little too linear if you're expecting thoughtful and impactful choices. It's also littered with typos which annoyed me - you can barely go through a single conversation without some error in the subtitles. Talents and spells have typos too, and I must've read the word "objetcs" rather than "objects" about 100 times. I've read reports of bugs, but I didn't really encounter other than a couple of visual bugs (like a character running on the spot for no reason). The only thing that broke the flow for me was the constant auto-saving, but that's far from a deal-breaker.But overall the negative points are far outweighed by the positive. It's great fun to play, I really had a hard time quitting out to do other things, as I was constantly just thinking "I'll just do one more thing..." and then half a day had passed. That, to me, is a sign of a good game. It's just fun, simple as that.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first review I ever write for a game, I just felt I had to.I have played other dungeon crawlers before but none of them have got me engaged in a battle at nightmare difficulty for over 30 minutes just hoping to be unlucky in order to fill the bar of my Randomia gauge to give me that little boost I need to survive this brutal battle since I forgot to rest my characters at the tavern and didn't equip my heroes with potions and bandages.Never before have I felt the need to make preparations before a battle nor the importance of support items. It has been my experience that you can just make do without them in other titles since you can depend on other game mechanics to heal your party or give you some sort of edge. NOT IN THIS GAME.Making sure your party is up to task for the next battle is just but one small step however, since the game's RNGsus is most likely not gonna favor you on your way through the dungeon. Critical Misses and just plain bad luck can have you at the edge of your seat swearing at the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ elf who somewhat manages to always hit your own characters no matter how much you improve her precision, so what seemed like an easy fight is now a miriad of bad positioning and awkward situations for your main frontline characters who you moved in to secure a kill on the annoying range character who was decimating your party. And then of course once you try to take him out he manages to dodge everything and gets away in order to kill one more of your squishies.The sense of strategy and randomness to this game is very appealing and while I am sure the humor is not for everyone I am sure that the gameplay is certain to be enjoyable for all.
