_childDocuments_.review: The combat in this game is so much fun! With experience in X-Com & DOS2 the mechanics were fairly familiar and I was mentally prepared for failing crucial attacks. On the harder difficulties most of the fights feel like an absolute slog and usually one or two more strokes of misfortune would end with a restarted fight. It handles its RNG quite well, with a gauge that fills up whenever you miss, critically fail or get critically hit, giving you access to powerful action-less abilities that can turn the tide back in your favour. Reading some comments I see the game was plagued by bugs on launch (most games are these days though for whatever reasons) yet I haven't stumbled across anything that bothered me. A couple of typo's here and there, a few momentary screen stutters as I land a finishing blow but I'm not anal enough to say that took anything away from my enjoyment of the game.In terms of the narrative, I actually quite like its linear nature. So far I've not found many moments where you have a decision to make that impacts the rest of the game, but the decisions I have made do seem to have had a large impact. There's plenty of opportunity to run around doing side quests too, which usually leads to more fights. I'm all for that.The humour grew on me as I got used to the characters behaviour but personally I just find the combat really fun and is the main reason I play. The story, humour, inventory management, side quests & levelling up characters is fine. They don't feel like a chore & they don't get in the way, even if I am frothing at the mouth in anticipation of feeding everyone I come across to the ogre.Overall I found myself turning into the Barbarian, lusting for a fight at every corner. If you're looking for a challenging turn based game where the combat is the main attraction I do highly recommend The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk, just watch you don't end up a devout follower of Crom afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos, where dungeons are as treacherous as a politician's promises and heroes are as competent as a one-legged bard trying to dance.In this rollicking RPG adventure, you'll lead a band of misfits through a dungeon filled with danger, laughter, and more questionable decisions than a goblin with a treasure map.Picture this: a wizard who's convinced he's the next Gandalf but can barely cast a spell without setting his beard on fire; a barbarian who swings first, asks questions later, and usually ends up tripping over his own feet; a dwarf who's grumpier than a troll with a toothache and twice as likely to curse you out; and that's just the start of your dysfunctional party. The game's humor hits harder than a critical hit from a rogue with a fondness for puns. Whether it's the wizard's failed attempts at magic, the barbarian's accidental trap triggering, or the dwarf's constant stream of insults, you'll be laughing until your sides ache.Visually, the game is a treat, with colorful graphics that capture the whimsy of its fantasy world. And the voice acting? It's so good, you'll wonder if the actors were paid in ale.But don't let the laughs fool you – beneath the comedy lies a challenging dungeon crawler that will test your tactical skills and patience. The difficulty spikes are as frequent as a bard's attempts to woo a dragon, and the puzzles will have you scratching your head like a goblin with fleas.Despite its flaws, The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk is a riotous adventure that's best enjoyed with strategy and a hearty sense of humor. So grab your dice, gather your party, and prepare for a journey filled with laughter, danger, and more chaos than you can shake a gelatinous cube at.Pros:-Hilarious humor and quirky characters make for a memorable adventure.-Solid turn-based combat and strategic gameplay keep things engaging.-Vibrant visuals and top-notch voice acting bring the world of Naheulbeuk to life.Cons:-Combat can feel repetitive, but at least you'll be laughing while you're doing it.-Difficulty spikes may frustrate some players, but hey, where's the fun in an easy dungeon crawl?-Humor may not appeal to everyone, but if you don't find a dwarf yelling insults at goblins funny, you might want to check your pulse.Overall Rating: 9/10 – A dungeon-crawling delight that's as entertaining as it is chaotic, perfect for anyone who enjoys their RPGs with a healthy dose of humor. Just remember to watch your step...The missing point is to be included in the next expansion!

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe I'm not the right audience for THE DUNGEON OF NAHALBEUK: THE AMULET OF CHAOS, but then, I also think the right audience for this game deserves better than this.Mechanically, this game is a tile-based tactics game a-la the modern XCOMs, intensely influenced by tabletop Dungeons & Dragons. Characters have a combination of move and attack actions, take overwatch shots, have zones of control, and so on. Each character can make opportunity attacks if an enemy tries to leave their immediate melee range, pushing players to keep their weak characters out of close quarters, and to carefully mind where their paths will cross. In play, this amounts to lots and lots of small-point chip damage, and whether or not that’s “fun” is probably a question of taste - maybe you’d enjoy that risk in your tactics game, maybe not. For me, it meant quite a lot of turns where a character was stuck in melee with a less-important enemy unit they shouldn't be bothering with. It's especially challenging since, unlike XCOM, turn order is fixed at the start of a fight, and if you need someone to act at a specific time, you're S.O.L. unless you want to delay their turn to the end of the round. I found it strict, but not so strict that I ever felt a fight was unfairly stacked or impossible.Easily this game's most interesting mechanic is an Unluckiness meter. The miss-to-hit ratio seems a little high compared to something like Final Fantasy Tactics, but presumably it's using the D&D staple of 1-in-20 for critical success/failure (a broad average of 5% adds up a lot, over a whole game). To make critical failures more interesting, the player gets compensated with a few drops into the Unluckiness meter, and they can spend this meter to get free actions, free heals, and the like, once they've experienced enough bad luck. It's a fun and fair compensation for putting up with missing (an otherwise-frustrating mechanic beyond the player’s control) and it persists between fights, prompting some good long-term decision-making. Unfortunately, you could get this, or a comparable tactics experience, from games that are much less annoying. This game is apparently based on a French comedy podcast(?) that's been around since 2001, and ooooooooh man, does it ever smell of the 2000s. When foreign-language humor gets translated, some nuance tends to be lost, and the jokes can suffer as a result. Sadly, I don't think that excuse applies here, because this script leans so hard on simple cliché and obvious pop culture references that there’s no way the translators lost the tone. Don’t mind the occasional line that sounds clunky or awkward in English, because the foundation of this game's comedy simply isn't interesting. These characters are D&D archetypes, stock personalities that even I, as someone who has never actually sat down to play any D&D, have seen a hundred times already: the angry dwarf, the nerdy wizard, the reclusive thief, and of course Conan The Barbarian, in an all-but-infringing rip from the 1982 movie. I promise you, you've already seen all of our protagonists in other media – but the twist is that, yes, this simplicity is the intended joke, right down to each one being named “The Ranger” or “The Ogre,” evoking a common bad habit of grognard gamers to never learn another character’s real name and refer to them by class. The problem is that the writers didn’t commit much more to them either, and for a character-driven comedy, this is a death sentence. Each scene features our gang of talkative TV Tropes pages bickering and name-calling at length, despite the English actors racing through the script. This, in turn, does not exactly endear any one of them to us. Dialogues are packed with tons of it's-a-reference humor tied to utterly ancient pop media like Monty Python (nerds, we live in the 2020s, please move on from Monty Python), and a "lolrandom" fixation on chickens. There's even an overt reference to Baldur's Gate, with a warrior hamster and everything, and it lands with none of the source material’s charm. It's as if this game expects the player to fondly recall playing D&D with high school friends, but it's going about it all wrong, and showing you that your juvenile adventures had far less “adventure” and far more “juvenile” than you knew. Playing it was a secondhand embarrassment, to be honest, and I do not think this script has the deftness to make ribbing its audience into an intentional point. To cap matters, I stopped playing around chapter 3-4, where one character looks at our token Dumb Blonde Elf and insinuates that he plans to rape her, alive or dead. And yeah, that's about as 2000s nerd humor as it gets, huh?Comedy is subjective, and delicate, but the simple fact is that this game barely made me laugh once for the 9-ish hours I gave it. Call it distaste on my part if you want, but you could find a much more compelling RPG story in Wildermyth or the modern Shadowruns, a much neater tactics game in XCOM or Overland, a much funnier cast in Psychonauts, and a much better dark comedy in LISA The Painful. That is, unless you really, really need to hear the joke about the killer rabbit one more time.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, well-executed dnd-style adventure that's also a parody of the genre. Straightforward and accessible but not overly easy - it felt just right to me. Everything about this game is straightforward fun. There's not much depth in terms of character personalities and story but it's a great time from start to finish nonetheless, in large part thanks to almost every line of dialogue being voiced.There are a few hiccups with voice-over lines not matching subtitles (or occasionally being just plain bad line reads), a lot of little grammar errors, the occasional text glitch (overlapping with images or using a code reference), and some slight hangups during auto-saves. None of that is overly distracting however, as the core of the game functions very well (combat/exploration is smooth; triggers for voice-lines seem very well handled also).

_childDocuments_.review: Like many people here, I really wanted to like this game. And it has its merits: it's pretty to look at, the characters are well animated, especially for a game of this budget, and the writing is solid (you have to enjoy that kind of humour though).But what should have been a nice little narrative rpg experience rapidly turns into a chore. I blame the difficulty that is spectacularly poorly managed. Many people in negative reviews blame the punishing RNG, yet this is not my experience. Yes, there are critical failures, hidden dodge stats and the like, but I never found them to determine the outcome of a  fight on their own. Instead, the multipliers the enemies get on higher difficulty settings are insane. A rat, a basic enemy, will have as many hp as most of your characters at lvl2, and they will hit just as hard. They will always outnumber you, and your crowd ontrol at low lvl is absent, because the AI will always tank your puny attacks of opportunity to get behind you and inflict three times the amount of damage. A luxury you are not afforded because in the early game, your party is full of glass canons that can barely tank two hits before going down.You might say "git gud" or "play on normal difficulty", and you'd be right except... Normal difficulty is a walk in the park. Here lies the problem: winning fights or losing them never feels satisfying, as they are either so easy no strategy is required, or so hard only RNG can allow you to win them. I can appreciate the devs wanting to provide a challenge but the difficulty spikes from one fight to another lead only to frustration after a little while.If you're considering buying this game, and I suppose there are good reasons to, do so understanding its balance is subpar, even when compared with the meme "XCOM chance to hit".

_childDocuments_.review: The optics are okay but whats most bothering me is its cringy humor ("dumb big boobed elve cliche, "porn scroll", arrow to the knee jokes in 2022 etc..) and the way the already slow gameplay flow gets completely stopped in its tracks through expositional dialogue, tutorial tool tooltips or cutscenes. It takes ages to actually get started. Maybe this is just the first time when you play the tutorial but that couldve been solved more elegantly. Also not being able to rotate the camera with mouse buttons/being forced to use keyboard keys to do it is pretty annoyingI got this for relatively cheap through humble choice. _childDocuments_.review: Almost but no.  Game resembles Grotesque Tactics games that i loved so much many years ago but this one got much finer polish and even dumber humor and characters but this one fails in it's core design when it forces you into fights that are a RNG fest. Classically in games like these when you encounter something that is too hard for your party then off you go to level up a bit before trying it again but there are very finite ways to gain XP in this game. Plus relatively early on it becomes clear that your characters take dives in battles all the time but before you know it you start encountering fights where characters may take up to 3-4 dives per battle... You already know where this is going: You eventuallyu encounter fights where tactical decisions are limited and there is no way for you to 'git gud' first on the bigger map so a RNG fest it is. Or reading up on wikis and min-maxin accordingly. Needless to say some people love this. I don't. For me this is a critical flaw because once the game reveals it pushes hard this kind of game play then it is a game for a specific kind of audience and i am not that kind of audience. I want the game to progress steadily and if i am going to be grinding then there must be at least an illusion of advancement. There is none here, just restart and try again if you think your tactics are the best and well... i am using to the max all the skills and equipment i have but with this design it is a RNG time sink you are fighting. No thanks. Real world time is a luxury that not even these ancient and buggy Grotesque games wasted but this one does that so a 'no' it is. With caveats though: If you think RNG is your friend then by all means go ahead you will like this. There is a reason why those ancient Grotesque games got a cult following back then.

_childDocuments_.review: Game ruined by bad game design decisions. Example the fight against goblins and golems. ON NORMAL: Not only are there Goblin archer, no, the sword goblins have aoe range spells! Why give classes of enemys any weaknesses that you can work around, hm? Fun fact:  They nearly oneshot some characters with a critcal, too. Additional, you may hit, but they evade. This makes every single goblin like a tank, you can't oneshot them, you have to hit and they can evade and they are plenty.And In this state, your tanks aren't really strong enough to soak up all the damage of all the archers and aoe. Your healing skills are gine fast. There are like 10-12 goblins + 2 golems who can all crit and do so, while you only crit failure and lose the game without any chance. I have never seen an enemy with critical failure btw...So that's how to kill fun.Maybe I could have solved the situation with consumables? No, they take a full action that means you do no damage, that means you get damage a whole turn without dealing damage so nonsensical.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game has many fun elements and is pretty well-written (save for a few tired dad jokes peppered throughout), The combat eventually turned me off entirely from continuing.  I realize that a 94% success rate is not a 100% success rate, but with that said, those percentages seem to be more decorative than informative.  The game feels like it's just tilted to favor enemies more in order to build up the arbitrary "chaos" meter at the bottom, which is used to give you a leg up for when you feel like the game has been cheating you out of fair outcomes.Now go back and reread that last sentence and you'll understand the core problem with this game and why I'm not recommending people play it until that gets addressed.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of all games turn based tactical (X-com, Wasteland, Baldur's Gate and the like) I wanted to really give this game a run as it looked right up my alley with some good comedy to boot. What I found out was that every fight in this game past to first couple of hours seemed like a big FU to whatever plans you were making.I couldn't figure out how my characters with 100% chance to hit with a flank attack or backstab where constantly failing with by being dodge or parried. The whole critical fail element with it's RNG humor...f' that. I get sometimes missing with a 90% chance to hit (that's X-com baby) but all the freaking time. And the critical failure killing my teammate when I try to heal. No thanks. I don't want to spend hours doing fights with RNG giving it to me in the rear, failing and then having to start over the ordeal.Look, for its trappings, its a good game for what it shows you. But on execution, I have better games to play to waste time on, and feel some sense of accomplishment then getting it in the backside and having to redo it again. For those that are considering this because they think it might be a different form of X-com, it is not. Look for something else.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's a decent TRPG though the writing is kinda lame, but it should appeal to many on both counts even if it does less so to me, especially reading other people's reviews. Therefore I'm mostly going to focus on the negatives and what I think could improve.Full disclosure: I usually try to get further into a game before reviewing, but I think I have a pretty good idea of this one so far and will update as needed.Combat seems to take a more "randomness is fun" approach, not just in that hit chances are low but roughly everything is chance-based. The elf has an attack which hits one target of your choice, but can ricochet and hit teammates. Poison on the floor has a percent chance to cause the poison status per tile moved. Ranged attacks have a chance to hit teammates. After enough bad rolls of the die, a sort of "bad luck" meter fills and can provide beneficial effects. There were times I way praying for a critical failure on an attack so I could fill this meter. I think there's a good idea in there, but it's neither predictable enough to reward proper strategies, nor random enough for completely unexpected and "fun" things to happen.The combat has a lot of depth, with area of control for if an enemy steps into one of the three tiles in front of one of your characters, overwatch/line of site, many different status effects, injuries, passive abilities, and both primary and derived (from the primary) stats which the game is upfront about showing. Additionally, the party size is pretty large compared to most squad-based TRPGs.As with most TRPGs, the initial battles will be tough as nails on difficulties higher than normal, but after gaining a few levels become much less of a problem. In a recent battle, I walked into a group of level 5 enemies and didn't struggle too much with my level 3 and 4 party, partly thanks to the fourth ability on the bad luck meter (heal/revive 6 of 7 party members). I knew the devs probably wanted me to wait on this battle until I'd leveled a bit more, but it didn't much matter. This is mostly to say that if you struggle in early encounters, don't put the game down because it's "too hard" because it gets easier later.The writing has jokes around every corner, and I liked this about Pop-Up Dungeon, but here they feel juvenile while attempting wit. The elf is a dumb blond and hates the dwarf who is a drunk and loves god and hates the elf, The ranger acts like like a stoic, mission-focused adventurer, but gets flabbergasted whenever a woman he finds attractive appears. The thief is depressive and no one listens to him. Jokes so often revolve around setting an expectation and revealing the opposite to be true that you'll be saying the punchlines in your head before they appear on screen. Sometimes we refer to characters as flat when they lack depth, but they don't have much width here either and that almost seems intentional.All-in-all, I think Duneon of Neheulbeuk is a fine game which many will love the heck out of. They will love the humor and depth of combat as well as the DnD setting. I am on the fence about whether I'd recommend it to others so I'll stick a "yes" on this review for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't beaten this one yet, as due to unforeseen circumstances I've had to restart it a few times, but...Y'all this is a genre of gaming that has been woefully under-represented in the last 20yrs: Silly, but very well designed and executed. If you grew up on things like "Monkey Island" then you understand what I'm getting at.It does suffer a bit from writing issues. The story is written wonderfully, but the dialogue and jokes are spotty. In some ways the dialogue is fantastic; for instance, it relies very heavily on excessive vulgarity for humor, but that vulgarity comes out sounding extremely natural, which is not something a lot of games manage when they use too much of it. In other ways the dialogue seems like it was either written by an eight year old who knows that certain words and situations are funny, but doesn't really know why, or was written by someone who isn't a native English speaker, and is maybe trying to translate cultural jokes from their language into English...and failing.Don't let that last paragraph about the dialogue fool you though. This game is fantastic! It's simple, and uncomplicated. But it also has a decent amount of strategic depth. The graphics are cartoony and perfect for the genre. The characters all look incredible. It's such a good game that I have neglected playing other games from triple-a studios because I'm enjoying this one too much to stop (and based on the number of amazing triple-a games that came out last year, that's really saying something).tldr: I've never bothered to write a review for a game before, but felt compelled to do so for this one. This is an absolute buy.edit: I have now beaten the game multiple times, on 3 of the 4 difficulties, and can still say that I love it, and enjoy playing it. I'm trying to convince myself to go play something else instead of doing another play-through of this game on Nightmare difficulty and trying to get all of the achievements. Turns out that the places where the humor seems awkward is largely a part of translation (apparently this was originally a French serialized radio program).

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? A fantastic fantasy role-playing game that suddenly appeared out of nowhere (for me...). Exploration, party development, interactable hotspots, crisp graphics, lots of funny dialogues, challenging turn-based tactical fights, inventory management... You lead a party of seven adventurers in real-time and in isometric perspective through the dark hallways of the Dungeon of Naheulbeuk to loot some gold (although there is an old prophecy to fulfill as well). The dungeon contains everything you'd expect, p. ex. a pharmacy, a tavern, quite a bunch of REALLY absurd NPCs, tons of different enemies. Your party constantly talks amongst themselves, which is quite funny, as they are not the brightest or most experienced bunch as well. The whole dungeon is kind of a parody, from the cleaning guy to the owner of the pharmacy shop. Expect weird encounters and conversations on all seven levels of the dungeon.Your party of seven characters is pre-determined, you cannot create anyone at the start of the adventure. They consist of seven of the most common RPG archetypes: an elvish archer, a ranger (kind of the leader of the group), a greedy dwarf, a barbarian, an always hungry ogre, a clumsy thief and a sexy wizardess (if you find redheads sexy, like I do). The wizardress is also probably the most reasonable and intelligent member of your party. They can carry a main and secondary weapon, equipment, armor, boots, a helmet, rings, a belt, a necklace... Despite tons of loot, inventory management is very well made. Actually, each character has his own equipment, and all the rest is carried by the strong ogre in his large backpack. The ogre might be inhumanly strong, but there is a weight limit on how much even he can carry. Besides weapons and armor, you can find consumables, quest items, books, misc... really a lot to carry around. Some items cannot be used by everyone, a lot of things are only usable by certain characters. Like the cooking pot that the ogre uses as a fashionable helmet (and for cooking goblins). While the ogre is the mule, the wizardess writes the quest journal and the automap. Very handy! The game comes with a main quest and quite a bunch of side quests, but it does not give you the freedom to do anything whenever you want - the story is scripted and you are, more or less, required to follow it.Each character has a long list of attributes. They are divided into the main attributes of agility, strength, constitution, intelligence, courage and charisma and in 14 secondary abilities and a skill tree. The main attributes can be raised when a character levels up after he has earned enough experience through fighting. Levelling up also allows to learn new skills, with a long list of active and passive skills, individual for each character. Experience points after fights are allocated to party members depending on how they fought in combat.Combat is turn-based. First you select starting locations for everyone, already seeing your foes. Then the usual turn-based fight starts. Each character has two action points - to move and to fight or do something else like using a skill. Overwatch, backstabbing, many individual skills, environemental dangers, friendly fire... there are so many options, I love it. The combat in this game doesn't have to hide from it's specialized tactical combat rpg brothers at all! Characters can receive wounds that reduce certain abilities (depending on the wound) and have to be healed (by using a bandage, first aid kit or whatever), otherwise they might get worse.The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos is fully voiced. Seven characters, the narrator and a bunch of NPCs. They all talk a lot. Playable by gamepad, even the more complex operations like selecting the right spell and casting it at the right place work perfectly (after some training). Save/load anywhere (even during combat). You can also always (while exploring or fighting) zoom and turn the camera, very well made. No bugs found (after the first two patches), apart from the random french texts sometimes. Ultrawidescreen works fine.RPG heaven, as long as you don't mind a challenging tactical RPG with a story that does not take itself too seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon crawling RPG with turn-based combat and mostly linear story (occasionally you will make some decision that will change your reward and one important where you choose one of the companions). The combat takes about 80% of playtime, so if that is not a plus for you, stay away. Occasionally there are some small puzzles, but this game is mainly about combat. Although not perfect (some remarks are at the bottom), I enjoyed it enough for multiple playthroughs. I played on the hardest difficulty + ironman, lost my first game about 40% through the game where it became clear I misbuilt my characters. That is OK on itself, but it showcased how "random" is the difficulty of battles - you can go through 4 battles, completely smashing the enemies and then suddenly the next battle is super hard, the next one easy again and so on. That makes it difficult to realise you are doing something wrong until it is too late (for example I spent too many stat points on Constitution, which is not a good strategy).The bad part of the game is when you are not in combat as walking through the dungeon is a pain: you can move your characters by clicking on the ground, but pressing ANY button - including just rotating camera - cancels the move. Moving with WASD is a pain because you cannot turn by mouse, so you constantly have to adjust the camera with QE. Selling items requires unnecessary many clicks.The ugly part is that there are, although not too many, traps. If you step on them, entire party takes damage, so you have to go to tavern to heal or spend your potions before the next fight. There is plenty of resources, so it does not really server any other purpose then to annoy the player. Thief can disarm them, but in the trap-searching mode your party moves twice as slowly. Why is this mechanic in the game is beyond me.Luckily, most of the game you will be in combat, so if you enjoy that, the game is quite likable.Mechanics defining the combat: - It is initiative based, i.e. both your and enemy characters take turns in order of their initiative.- Combat encounters are pre-scripted, which lowers the replay value a bit.- Each characters gets 1 move and 1 action each turn, occasionally some enemies will have 2 actions (you can also get extra action with some abilities). While I like this in general, problem here is that it's rarely better to spent your action on something else then attacking or healing. I pretty much never used any buff potions, since using them means you are not hurting the enemy, which brings me to next point.- Characters get debuffs for having less then 50%, 75% and 90% health. This makes the previous problem even bigger - why take a buff potion, when you can debuff enemy by attacking to get basically the same result while also moving towards the end of combat?- "attacks of opportunity", which you may know from other games (once you are in front of a melee enemy, moving away from it will give them free attack). - Accuracy bonuses for each friend aiming at the same enemy, although I did not find that particularly important. But combined with attacks of opportunity, it makes direction play a big role - you can choose a direction you end up in after movement and it automatically changes when you use an attack on someone.- Once your character loses all health, they become unconscious and you have three turns to revive them with a healing spell or potion, otherwise they are out of combat. Once revived, they have a debuff until end of combat.

_childDocuments_.review: SHORT REVIEWThis review is for the base game without any DLC.The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk is a turn based tactical combat dungeon crawler which is apparently based on a French satirical cartoon poking fun at a D&D adventuring party.  The game relies heavily on humour and the interaction between the characters which I find quite amusing but as humour is subjective its very much a case of “your mileage may vary” on this one.PLOT:  The plot is okay but not great but that doesn't matter.  Its a satire for the RPG trope as opposed to a serious game and it is the humour which really carries it.  The interactions are scripted so there is actually very little “role playing” input to vary the outcome.  I found the ending to be a real damp squid and it really let the game down.GAMEPLAY:  3D dungeon exploration game with turn based tactical combat system.  Personally I found the pacing of the combat a bit off, even if you turn the animation speed up to maximum it feels a bit slow and sluggish at times.  This isn't helped by the party size of 8, often against a similar number of enemies meaning each round takes a long time.DIFFICULTY:  Its quite hard.  I started playing on the 2nd difficulty level (Tavern Song) which was okay for a while but after running into one particularly difficult fight I resorted to dropping it to Gripping Tale.  How people manage on Gzor's Nightmare is beyond me.GRAPHICS & SOUND:  Graphics are pretty nice and what you would expect from what is a relatively recent recent game although there a few performance issues.  One the sound side of things the voice acting is excellent and whilst there is ambient background sound it is just that, i.e. in the background, and isn't at all intrusive which is nice.REPLAY VALUE:  Poor.  The encounters are scripted so there will be virtually no variation in the plot and once you've heard a particular gag it generally doesn't improve with a second telling.  There is a choice of which of the three available NPC's you take as the 8th character but that is about it.ISSUES AND BUGS:  Works “straight out of the box”.  There are some performance issues with this game that I will expand on in the long review and it did completely lock up once requiring an Ctrl/Alt/Delete reset when I was cleaning up some old saved game files.ACHIEVEMENTS AND TRADING CARDS:  Full integration with the Steam platform, Steam achievements and trading cards for those interested.VALUE FOR MONEY:  It a “wait for the discount in a sale” type of game.  I think its a bit expensive at full price but that might be a sign of my age.  Although its only 3 years old now the base game manages 65% off in steam sales making it very reasonable but add in the DLC as well and that would make this an expensive proposition.LONG REVIEWWhilst The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk can be played as any other dungeon exploration game with turn based tactical combat system it is a game that is very much aimed at a target audience and that is people how have played Tabletop Role Playing Games.  I suspect those who haven't played tabletop games might miss out on a lot of the humour.There is a narrator for the story but mercifully it only appears occasionally and isn't at all intrusive.  There is also the choice of a male or female voice for the narrator which is a nice touch and not something I've seen elsewhere before.  The graphical presentation might make might make people think it is suitable for a younger audience but the language is quite “colourful” at times with liberal use of the “F” Word the occasional references to nudity (there is no actual nudity in the game) so it's not suitable for younger players (or when there are younger people within earshot).  The WOKE brigade might also be offended but they can go die in a ditch.As I said above there are some performance issues with this game.  The overall optimisation on PC is extremely poor, I'd even go as far as to say exceptionally awful.  There is no way this game should be a resource intense as it is and, even though my machine is well above the recommended specifications I had to turn the shadow quality and resolutions down to low to stop it stuttering.  There is also an issue with party movement which is rather clunky and sometimes seems to get stuck, its as if all the characters get a bit too close together and all start tripping over each other.  The final issue is that occasionally the subtitles and voice over don't quite match, this isn't a major issue, just a minor irritation.  I believe the original was in French so I wonder if something got lost in translation.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun.  I'd prefer an open world game (like POE and POE3) but beggars can't be choosers.  At $35 it's a bit pricey for the amount of content, but it's still a yes from me.That being said, there are definitely some weak spots in this game.  For example, not only does the game follow a strict plotline, the game actually forces bad decisions on you (decisions I would never have made if given the choice) and then makes you deal with the consequences.  Also annoying is you can't use food and healing spells to heal between battles, you can only use them during battles.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun tongue in cheek RPG game which has been well put together. The characters are fixed for the party but levelling up does often some customisation. There is full voice acting in a cheesy way throughout the whole story line/adventure with great banter between the characters which is unique for the encounters.This is not a sandbox game more of a main quest and some side quests, but my play through took over 70 hours. The combat is turned based and is surprisingly a good tactical system with a number of options including chicken grenades which summon a chicken that will randomly attack the nearest target. As well some destructible pieces of cover or barrels of poison, oils etc that can explode. The NPCs also use them to their advantage as well. However combat can take a bit of time. The critical misses fit perfectly into the story line but can be annouying if they happen at the wrong time but the monsters can also suffer them.The only issues I had with the game was it would slow a little when moving around and the selection of options would sometimes have a delay or require reselection. I really enjoyed the game and think it is worth while playing especially for those not after a serious game and are ok with over the top stereotyped adventurers and references to fantasy op culture.

_childDocuments_.review: I have tried playing the game one level harder than normal difficulty and boy was I surprised. Game has some weird issues about difficulty. First of all, everything hits like a truck in the early game. You can try different strategies to overcome challenges (doh, it's a turned based rpg) but no matter what you do, the AI is always better than you are. And this is why:The AI has no regard for losing their health or their allies health. They don't care about burning their allies with grenades or taking attack of opportunity hits. They have no regard for their survival as long as it mean killing you. This is all fun and games but becomes a pain to play through since every single mob in the game does like x3 damage than you do. For example, you cornered an archer with 2 of your toons. Normally, it should be using its melee ability which is a knock back and get out of the corner and shoot you. Well, instead he will just take the opportunity hit (you will be doing like it's 15-20% hp with one hit) then it will run away and shoot you for around 50-80% of your hp. Good for AI, bad for your gameplay. I don't know why they so overtuned the AI in terms of damage. They are already tanking and filled with utility items and CC abilities. There are no "dumb" enemies, everything got something on their sleeve which is great. This overtuned damage causes you to use support abilities (and pots) like non-stop making the fights last a lot longer and less fun. I'm 3 hours into playthrough, the "normal" mobs I am facing the fights are usually doing 40-60% of the tank's max health in their "normal" attack (without backstabing or stealth). These toons are all jacked up in survival attributes, passives and skills. They still go down in one turn without giving the enemy any advantage like stealth hits or backstabbing. 80% of my income goes to pots and bandages due to party members getting one shotted quite commonly. I sincerely regret tuning up the difficulty up 1 notch even though I'm 20 years of seasoned turn based rpg player. You have to fish for good roll for yourself and hope for bad rolls for the AI, that's how it works - otherwise well, get ready to replay 20 minutes of fights again and again. Your "advanced" tactics will mean nothing in the face of overtuned damage and damage sponge mobs, they will power through it and make you suffer even if they die in the process.Great game, just play it on normal difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Great TBS / RPG game, one of the most fun i have played in the last years. A pleasant surprise and worth the full price, but if you can get it on sale, even better. The humor and constant jokes about (but not restricted to) RPG and adventure games overused stereotypes  is something that i personally enjoy but there could be some of you who would find it a bit annoying. The battles are very serious though and you need to think and use the characters and their synergies really well to win. The classes skill trees and loot system are very well done and you can get a lot of builds to try and have fun with (there is a respec potion available so you can do it anytime). Overall a 8.5 / 10 game, has its small flaws and sometimes the RNG will not be nice to you but i think it is one of the few games that does what it says really well and doesn't bite more that it can chew,

_childDocuments_.review: Look, you're not going to get like, anything exceptionally magnificent here. It's not world breaking. But do I recommend it? Definitely.What you are getting is a cheekily sarcastic, cutely designed tactical rpg that lets you run a team of what is basically a DnD adventure. The story is straightforward, but the characters and voice actors make the game super entertaining. I love Xcom, Fire Emblem, and other games like this, so I picked it up. I think it's worth a playthrough if you're a fan of similar games. If you're not into tactics and more into narrative/challenge/mechanical games, it may not be for you. _childDocuments_.review: Decent Game with an awfull ending.At first glance one would be forgiven for thinking, this was an Xcom-Style game. But the combat system has much more in common with a tabletopwargame-like-tabletoprpg like Dungeons and Dragons, especially its 4th Edition. Positioning, attacks of opportunity and flanking are much more important.Combat itself is pretty fun, especially once your characters get more abilities. I say this because all special abilities have a cooldown. Since most of your adventurers start with only a single special attack, once it is used, you are stuck using basic moves and all tatical decision making becomes extremly limited. This makes the beginning by far the worst part of the game. With more skills unlocked, the games combat becomes a lot more tactical: coosing who to stun, trip or push, and which weaknesses to exploit is critical for victory, making defeating hords of foes surprisingly satisfying.The story is not exactly great and is basically just an excuse to joke about fantasy tropes and how incompetent your party is. The characters barely change and grow, which is a shame because, at least to me, having a bunch of idiots become good friends is usually one of the best things about a story of group of companions. Sadly this does not happen and even in later levels your, now much more competent, heroes are still treated like unqualified beginners. The ending is extremly unsatisfying and exactly the kind i would only make if I wanted to piss my players of. While the game is clearly meant to be a satirical interpretation of the classical fantasy adventuring party, it would have still been nice if the game took itself at least partially seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently, i can't recommend this game for purchase.  This is coming from an incredibly die-hard fan of Xcom Enemy within/Xcom2 and darkest dungeon.  I've beaten XCOM Enemy within on Ironman/Classic with ease, and Darkest Dungeon i've sunk 230 hours into.   I like RNG mechanics and strategy games in general, and love the challenge that some of those games bring.   This game however is completely broken when it comes to RNG.  Critical Failures when i've got a 105% chance to hit the target.  Dodges when i've got 3 assist players surrounding a lone target, and i'm striking that target from behind.   I'm playing on MEDIUM difficulty..and it's beyond any difficulty that XCOM 2 or Darkest dungeon could throw at me.   The mobs don't follow behavior rules like MY heros have to follow.  For instance some of the goblins throw 8 or 10 bombs/consumables over the course of the fight - i'm limited to *3* depending on my belt.  If they would just program the RNG to be *NORMAL* instead of trying to screw the player at every turn w/ completely bogus RNG roles that are clearly designed to be -20% or even -30% different than what is shown on the screen - this game would be LOADS of fun.-----------------------------------  **In response to Developer Below** ----------------------------------------I appreciate your response.  Thank youI understand the explanation for the goblins.However -- your explanation around the dodge/parry roll is the true underlying issue.   Why is this not pre-calculated for the player and that information presented?Strategy games don't have hidden metrics that determine accuracy. If a unit is behind cover for instance -- it will clearly display a -15% chance to hit the target due to the cover and then subtract that number from the overall hit chance.   This is exactly what i'm complaining about with this game. It's why players make educated decisions in strategy games. If i'm being shown on screen that i have a 95% chance to hit a target - i'm going to take that chance nearly every time. If you openly display this hidden dodge/parry chance as a separate metric, and the hit chance drops to 72%.. I may think twice about attempting to swing at that target and instead take a different course of action. - This is why i feel the way I do currently. Is there a way to actually view ALL calculations and get an idea how often an enemy is going to dodge/parry an attack? This is critical information in decision making!  Without it - it's not "strategy" - it's a guessing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe it's just not my cup of tea, but I found the humor more annoying than funny, and the characters flat and boring. They are basically all stereotypes, and most of them they couldn't even bother to give NAMES---just "The Ranger" and "The Elf". If you wanted to play with RPG stereotypes, you could have subverted them (like make the bard really chaste and the paladin the horny one, or make the ogre surprisingly intelligent and the wizard an idiot); but instead they basically just played them straight. There's barely any plot, and at least in the early parts there seems to be no control over your party composition; people swap in and out but it's not your decision. The tactical combat was sort of interesting, and had some nice original touches (especially the use of ranged flanking and overwatch, which gives it a bit of an XCOM feel), but its positive qualities fail to compensate for its poor balance and overall awkwardness.It has its moments, and maybe it would grow on me over a longer playtime; but there are much better tactical RPGs out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Regarding to some negative reviews, for being "huge fans of turn based games" those people give up on games like this pretty quickly it seems. I've won fights in this game I was sure to lose just because there's nearly always a way to turn the page or changing tactics, OR suddenly you're the one parrying everything with a 1hp-dwarf. So far I only had one (optional) battle I had to "retreat" from to get to it later on.Naheulbeuk is nearly a perfect homage to pen & paper roleplaying games with exactly these oh so hated RNG-systems which are as much your enemy as they are your friend, and it's even forgiving enough to spare you extremely powerful spells for failing. I'm by far not a tactical genius, but if you already give up and stop caring in the middle of the fight you will lose it anyways in Naheulbeuk. One of the things bugging me in this game is the fact that you're resurrecting party members veeery often from time to time, but at least it's possible with every healing item or -spell. I'm just not a huge fan of this system.In Wasteland 2/3 or Divinity Original Sin 1/2 you can always easily "cheese" battles with the same tactics again and again as they are balanced much worse due to the open classes (especially Divinity's systems are way too easy to trick, even accidental - hi, teleports!) and so it was very nice to get an actual challenging game that hits you hard for tactical failure or wrong positioning instead of giving you countless possibilities to win regardless.Unlike a lot of the crying people in negative reviews I can't compare Naheulbeuk with X-Com as I didn't play it.So.. don't get this game if you hate any RNG or really stupid humor. Not sure why you even considered giving it any chance after looking at the advertised game above then. I guess you love to hate, you're some strange sort of masochist or you're having too much time to read reviews for games you don't like anyways.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was really impressed by the quality of this game. It has full audio in German, French and English with even a male and female narrator! The comic graphic is very well made and the writing is so good. The production value is so high here but it really lacks the fun in gameplay, which is a huge drawback for me. They clearly set the wrong priorities here.I love stereotypes and this game serves so many. It is very hard to find something that is not 100% political correct at this time. Again, this game serves many stereotypes! If you don´t like that, please don´t buy but also please don´t complain about the political incorrectness! The dialogues, the story they are all very well written and fun listen to. Each of the characters serves a different stereotype that matches the theme very well. Due to that, character customization is almost non-existent.But that is about it, the focus was clearly more on the narrative side and not on the gameplay side. This game is based on a series of books/comics and I think if you are interested in that you should rather read those than play the game.I am a big fan of turn-based strategy games and played most of the big titles. It is hard not to compare it to titles like XCOM. And compared to other turn-based strategy came Dungeon of Naheulbeuk really lacks flow in the gameplay. Every single turn felt very cumbersome and complicated which, for me, never resulted in a fluent game play experience that I could enjoy.It comes with a few tweaks and improvements compared to other turn-based strategy games, but in principle is not very much different. For me it did not work out, although I enjoyed the theme and the story writing a lot. Combats were just too cumbersome and took too long for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: The game is more frustrating than fun. Some fights are just to tough and are impossible to get in the first try. Now, to win these fight, the strategy is to learn what the "random" events will be and anticipate them. For a chance based game there is no to little left to chance. For example, the fight on the 4rth floor againts the wheel of misfortune, if you play it a few times it is always the same "random" events that happen in a certain order. Not counting in the fact that in that fight there is an enemy that can basically teleport and instantly kill anyone at any distance, so no tactical defence againts him, which is not the point for a tactical game. Also for some reason the cloaking mechanism does not work on the thief, there probably is an explanation but it is never given. This is also an example of how unclear some mechanics are.Maybe I'm just not good at the game but even in easy mode some levels are just to hard. But the hard fights are followed by a few really easy ones, which makes the gameplay inconsistent. This is really demotivating to play the game.Please do not waste your money on this game unless there are some balance changes because the overall idea is really good.

_childDocuments_.review: Literally just bought this game earlier today without any prior knowledge about the developer.  I only went off of the videos/screenshots from the Steam store front.  Let me tell you, this game is worthy of the price tag and runs incredibly smooth.  You can normally tell with indie titles the kind of quality you'll get within the first 5 minutes of playing, and I instantly knew I wouldn't regret my purchase.  The game is linear, so if you are expecting a vast open world this isn't that kind of game.  You play as RPG archetypes as you make your way through a dungeon with various floors.  The characters are incredibly charming and fully voiced acted.  Interface is professional and easy to use.  Turn based combat feels rewarding and all the character's abilities work in harmony to create some very interesting encounters and combos.  Every character has their own skill tree, and you can customize their gear/items.The story is silly, but that's what makes this game fun.  It's almost as if the developer's are poking fun at the genre, while nailing all the elements that make this genre amazing.  Kudos!!

_childDocuments_.review: What we have here is a classic dungeon crawler game with alot of childish humour, not the bad kind, but the kind that will leave you laughing, well sometimes sighing as well, at why did you find that funny. Dungeon of Naheulbeuks story line is the basic you get in this type of game, there is a bad guy you have to go and kill him and free the world, this time the world is a dungeon. The graphics to the game are great the music fits the game well, and the character inter-reaction, makes you fell part of the story as they go on their way of freeing the dungeon. So on to the combat and AI, well i say Ai, sometimes i feel the AI is just like holly of Red Dwarf, it sometimes stops, looking like the game has frozen, but that happened only 3 times in entire play through. So Holly (the AI) seems to stop and think, just like holly checking his/her big book for answer when dave asks them a question, before making their move. The order of combat on the time line, you can sometimes find the adds have 6 of them have a go before you can do, but that is not such a big problem, also you find detrucables on the ground which lay fire,oil, posion etc, holly seems to know its there and will not move the adds through it. The Combat can be unforgiving above story mode and i would surgest if new to this type of genre, go story mode first then go up the 4 levels, as the adds can overwhelm you, even though you have 7 characters. so is the game worth the price and your time, well, simply put YES, it is worth it, even though holly can be a bit slow and you can miss attacks often, but that is down to setting skills etc up right, overall i would give this game a 8.6/10 only reason for score not being a 10 is holly being slow

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: The dialog is sometimes crude but is hilarious. The quests are ridiculous but fun enough.Cons: Combat is turn-based. The movement system is a two-step process; you tell each character where to go and which direction to face. Facing is critical because flanking a character and backstabbing a character do greater damage. I also disagree with parrying an arrow shot from behind you. Since you have a minimum of 6 characters at the beginning of each combat, combat is long and tedious.Summary: The humor of this game does not compensate for the drudgery of the combat. Unless you are a fan of detailed combat simulations, I recommend not purchasing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not understand reviews speaking about bugs. Not a single bug on my side so far (8h). [To be honnest only one, very minor : dont use "continue" option when you first launch the game ; that option should not be available in that context].That game is story driven so no grind but I think it is better. What is the interest of grinding and then running over the combats. There are secondary quests though.Combat system is deep. Deeper or more advanced than Xcom for instance. There is inspiration from Bloodbowl (control zone, support...) or Fire Emblem (bonus when some characters are near each other). Wounds on characters have an impact on their efficiency. Overall it is very good.All characters are very different. So it makes the system even more interesting.Good graphics (no pixel art thx) and effects. Humor (if you enjoy Naheulbeuk or mad fantasy).Great game ![Edit] And I forgot the best idea of all time : an "unlucky" bar ! When you fail your actions, it fills the bar and you get bonus actions from it. I am usually very unlucky in games, so this is just perfect. No frustration any more ![Edit]I just beat the game after 42h in normal mode ; so good. Only one bug, no drama. It was fairly easy assuming you know tactical rpg games. I will replay it on higher difficulty, and with another additional character (you have to chose one out of three possible early in the game).

_childDocuments_.review: The most important thing in video games is the fun factor. Forget the visuals, forget the story, forget everything else; it’s all about fun, fun, fun.  isn’t aware of that, which makes you think whether its developer even had any people test it out. The storytelling bit that mocks D&D tropes tries too hard to be funny and fails while at it, with the playable characters being a bunch of completely unlikable “heroes.” As for the actual, turn-based strategy affair, while definitely the better part, it has some severe issues of its own, with the most game-breaking one being the existence of an aggravating RNG that frequently ruins one’s plans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Such a shame.Great franchise for those who speak french, had a blast with the story, the voice acting and all the inside jokes and references.Problem is the game mechanics are busted by the Critical Miss mechanic which is way too present (5% for ANY action, some enemies RAISE that number). When randomness becomes an integral feature of your combat system, in a TACTICAL RPG, it's just plain bad.And the critical misses aren't just on hostile actions against something that could resist or counterattack, it happens just as much on buffs that the targets accept with open arms. Best example, the Brabarian has a shout that buffs everyone in a large radius. Cast it on turn 1 to start off the fight, critical miss, DEBUFFS all targets. I mean, what the actual fu*k.Oh, and don't try to reload the fight to try and get a different result, the encounters are seeded. So by doing the same actions, you'll get the same crap. Not bad for a game thats core feature is randomness...It also feels like the game devs were counscious that the critical misses were a problem so they added a bogus "balance" mechanic which is a gauge for special actions that fill up the more you fail. Long story short, it doesn't balance ♥♥♥♥.Really wish I could recommend such a great story. But since I had to bump it down to the easiest of difficulties so that the bullsh*t critical misses wouldn't break all the fights, I really can't. Having followed the franchise for almost 20 years, I forced myself to finish the game out of sheer... fandom? But in the end it was just a long slog to the finish line. I ain't getting the DLCs, hell, I ain't putting myself through any more of this sh*t.

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY: If unresponsive, glitchy, janky controls drive you up the wall, avoid this like a plague.Seriously, movement controls during exploration mode are so abhorrent, that it makes the exploration and puzzle-solving part of the game almost physically painful. It gives subtle vibes of poor console port / poor animation transitions / poor zone loading / poor UX design -- all at the same time. This review was once a negative one, with a long rant detailing the movement control woes. You have been warned.DO BUY: If you can look past the above and are interested in a fun (albeit rather short) solid tun-based tactical combat with RPG-style progression.The game is essentially a sequence of predetermined turn-based battles stitched together by short interludes of exploration / looting / simple puzzle-solving. The combat is solid and rather fun, with strong similarities to x-com series (it does have the same random hit / miss mechanics as x-com, in case that happens to not sit well with you). Playing grids are quite tight (no wasted turns) and the action is quick, intense and provides a good assortment of moves and skills to be used.The character building for the most part can be min-maxed to 1-2 builds for each character. It's a fun "puzzle" to solve, but there isn't much build variety, if that's what you're looking for. Some skills/passives/consumables/stats are just orders of magnitude better than others. So I strongly suggest to not look up builds online, figuring the "good" ones is a significant part of the game.Puzzles are on the simpler side (e.g. "find a book with a sequence of words in gibberish, find a book that translates gibberish to color names, pull 4 colored levers in the sequence given by the first book -- the books and the levers are all in the same room"), but they are well designed and varied. Adjusted for the clearly intended art style, visuals, audio, voice and writing are all quite impressive.

_childDocuments_.review: Super enjoyable game. Great voice acting, really engaging straight forward storyline with just the right amount of sidequesting. _childDocuments_.review: I do enjoy this game because it has this fun, light-hearted feel to it. The characters are cute & amusing, the one-liners make me chuckle.  And there is a decent gameplay loop with interesting progression and mechanics, like having to use bandages to heal wounds after a fight (healing potions aren't enough).  The critical fumbles can be annoying when they happen to you, but they are great when they happen to the enemy.  I like their presence in the game, though, as it fits its silly style and adds some challenge & chaos. There are critical successes, too.  And there is a mechanic with a meter that builds as things "go wrong" for you, and then you can use that meter to gain some special boost or advantage and the like.  So that helps to offset critical failures (which don't happen too often).I will admit that some of the negative comments I've seen about the one-liners getting old or the gameplay feeling repetitive have some validity.  For me, however, I play this is in small bursts when I am in the mood for something silly & light.  It isn't a game that sucks me in for an extended period of time.  That is okay for me because I like having games like this to turn to for something different.  Also, with a growing library and a busy life, not every game can be a time suck.I can say that I have not lost the desire to play it.  I want to see where the story goes, I want to see the characters through to their max level, and I want to revisit them in the DLC.  I will just do it in short sessions over time.  So if any of this appeals to you, this game is definitely worth buying, especially on sale (which is how I purchased it).  If not, it is reasonable to pass.  But there is a fun game here, especially if you embrace what it is and don't take it seriously--it definitely doesn't and that is a big part of why I really like it.

_childDocuments_.review: One of those rare games that I do intend to finish eventually, but would nevertheless not recommend.Nothing about the game is abhorrent. The combat is decent. The story is passable. The worst offender is the inane meta "humor" which falls flat 90% of the time, and frequently comes off as sexist. Bugs and crashes are also fairly common. For a better indie turn based fantasy RPG, I would recommend Druidstone. For higher budget, there is of course Divinity Original Sin 1 and 2, which excels over this game by miles.The best part of the game is the system of (relatively) frequent fumbles, which don't feel too bad because they charge a "bad luck" meter that unlocks powerful effects. This is such a good system I'm thinking of adapting it into my tabletop campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: A mixture of a dungeon crawler and a turn-based tactics game that has fun, interesting characters and wonderful game play. The characters remind me of Bard's Tale in that they are the game's heroes but a cast of misfits at the same time, which makes for a lighthearted and fun experience. There are unique skill trees for each character and the tactical combat is a good mixture of challenge and fun. Haven't found any real problems so far and it's been a while since I've had so much fun playing a game.  If you're looking for a solid tactics type game, give this a try, you will not be disappointed!

_childDocuments_.review: What a gem of a game. It does not feel overwhelming, as there is no huge open world to explore, and not the fate of life itself in your hands. Just one location with different levels and a limited number of characters to interact with. The dungeon looks great, I very much enjoyed the style, full of lovely little details. And the characters are fun, sometimes the humor gets a little too much but in general I could enjoy it alot. The voice actors mostly did an amazing job, and I quickly fell in love with the group of heroes and their interactions. And, since I am old now, I very much enjoyed the X-Com kind of fighting, where you do not need to have quick reflexes, manage twenty buttons at once and be aware of your surroundings at the blink of an eye. You have time to check the situation, plan your next move and enjoy if it works. This game looks and plays like a labour of love.

_childDocuments_.review: A silly Turn based RPG that makes fun of fantasy tropes.  The writing is, for me personally, pretty cringe.  However, If that's what you enjoy, this is for you.  Gameplay-wise, it's not a bad game.  There are some things that prove to be slightly frustrating; like obstacles that take two hits to destroy, being hit behind full cover, backstabbed from the side...  You get a full range of classes, though all your characters are pre-made.  Some have complained about the RNG.  I.e. missing with 80% chance to hit.  I don't mind it THAT much... because it is RNG after all, but I can see how it would be frustrating if it happened time and time again.Read the devs own synopsis of the game before buying.  It's pretty spot on.  For me, I've tried a couple of times.  While I love and look forward to just about any turn-based RPG, this is hard to enjoy... even with the sound off.  Yes, it does have VA and some of which is pretty decent, the writing (or translation) let's it down.  However, I'm not sure much could be done with the way the game is scripted in itself.Anyway, I can't get into this.  The fun takes the fun out of it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: is a tactical turn-based RPG with heavy emphasis on the humorous story.The story follows a team of unique individuals through a wacky dungeon world in order to find a statuette. It's simple enough to follow, and the writing is rather funny. You can skip the dialogue in this game but I wouldn't recommend that you do so.You will have a party of different individuals of various races and classes. Each character has their own special skills. They each level up learning different skills and have different weapons as well as armour.The main part of the game is the combat. These battles are turn-based and are not easy. They are rather tactical. Each character will have 2 action points that can be used for moving and to perform an action like dealing damage, healing, or using a skill or item.There's no grinding to gain extra levels, so you are dealing with what the game gives you. This is part of the increased difficulty as well.The game progresses with the strong story-based element, so as above, I do think that following the story is a big part of this game as well.The graphics are fantastic, the 3D animations are very nice. Even when zoomed in, everything looks really good.The music provides a nice atmosphere. Almost all of the dialogue accompany spoken voices. This is done well.The game can be fully played with a controller or a mouse and keyboard. Both work fine.The price feels a bit steep, since it's close to an AAA game. It has artwork quality similar to one as well. I have encountered 3 freezing bugs and there are some minor issues as well. There are some translation errors  also. If everything could get fixed, I would say that it's worth the full price because of the production value. is a real gem, and if the major and minor issues could be fixed, it would be a really nice addition in the Steam library. It is not an easy game, even not at some lower difficulty settings, so players shouldn't look to play it looking for a casual game. Listening to and reading most of the dialogue is a big part of the game, so make sure to pay attention to these. If you only came here for tactical battles, you might wish to reconsider.Score: 8/10 (I would consider increasing the assessed score if these major and minor bugs/issues are fixed.)

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games I really wish Steam had a sideways thumb icon for.I should love this game, but I don't.Can't pinpoint why... maybe just a little too cartoony for it's own good.It's fun for a while, I got 20 hours from it, but then it becomes a bit too uninteresting, and getting lost becomes a real pita.Get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The humor is a bit on the nose, but I guess you get some giggles out of it in one playthrouh.Difficulty can be set to be challenging, but not unfair, so I like that. The seconds between each turn feel like an eternity, as they add up.Still, it is not a full priced game and for what it is, I can still recommend it to people who want a challenging turn based combat dungeon crawler.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game on the epic quest difficulty (2nd highest) and up to like half point the game was challenging. towards the end it got easier and it the end was slightly too easy.+ The game has great voice acting and it's fun!+ Battles have nice support mechanic which promotes positioning of certain characters+ Battles all in all are pretty fun! unlike in divinity original sin where you have to get rid off the armor in order to use disables here you can use it all the time so you can actually utilize your skills without first 3 rounds going to damage dealing only.+ all characters are useful and has their role+ Even side quests are fun and give good battles.+ Good puzzles, good amount of them and varies enough.+ I like that you only have certain amount of items you can carry in a fight.- UI could use improvements. is skill up window you can only see the base stats and have to access inventory in order to see the improvements done by gear for example.- The difficulty should be other way around so starts easier but gets harder.- even tho all characters seemed useful after certain point some just felt lacking in early game. Thief is horrible in the beginning and I don't think I used the stealth at all. I even didnt care if he died in the fight and just kinda played without him until certain point when he got actually really strong.- Moving around is sluggish... sometimes the characters simply does not move when you click- Traps are kinda pointless. I mean it's just annoyance which makes you consume some potions before fights but doesn't really add anything to the game. Same with weight limit.. not necessary imo as I only reached it once or twice during the play through- The story felt a bit rushed towards the end.Saw some complaints about the RNG but there's nothing out of ordinary here. the 3% critical failure chance can be buffed by enemies in some fights and you end up failing a lot but the game is balanced around that.All in all 8.5/10 can recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing... It's been a while since I had a game that I enjoyed from start to finish!  You know how in many RPGs people skip the dialog?  Well you do not want to skip it in this game, it is very funny!  It takes me back to games from the 90s such as Day of the Tentacle, Leisure Suit Larry, etc.  Your party members like picking on each other.I played it on normal and the battles seem pretty balanced, the only one that seemed a bit tough was the first time you encounter the books!  But using strategy such as dwarf toss or have your barbarian jump into a group, it is doable.  The performance is fine, no stutter or lag (and I played it on an MSI Laptop).  I only ran into one issue, at the very end of the last battle just before the credits roll, the game stayed on a black screen.  The devs fixed this issue but the patch isn't ready yet - to avoid the problem just reload the game at the last battle auto-save and it will work fine leading you through the credits and into the DLC if you purchased it.Good game for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: This game. I have mixed feelings about it which mostly come down to "meh". At this point I think I'm just forcing myself play this game because "oh i'm so close to the end"The writing is comedic but rarely punches in a giggle and some jokes keep getting repeated until they are kind of annoying. I don't necessarily care for the gag being that the groups participants hate each other over and over. I wished that they would start to feel comradely at some point (and not just ranger being nice when he sees a pair of tatas). The comedic world building is the better side of this.The combat mechanics at first were deeper than I thought. As itself it is fine and I had some fun. Personally didn't mind the flimsy RNG but the length of some of encounters was a bit much for me. (RNG warning: you can have a 110% hit chance and miss the shot, it doesn't take in the chance of the opponent parrying or dodging the attack and also you always have a 5% change of just farting on yourself and fainting. I see most of the negative reviews complain about that)Collectibles are fun and give you stat boots. Only thing that bothered me was that you had to travel to hand over collectible sets to gain those stat boost. Each set has its own delivery place. Which again is fine but the game already has you going back and forth so I started to wish for one consistent place for delivery.also something seemed a miss with the balancing? Prices for items were odd and armor stat bonuses seemed pretty minimal so it wasn't necessarily that exciting to acquire them nor to put them on your characters. Also the bombs become useless after early game and status effects are also pretty pointless except freeze.Nothing here is exceedingly good or overly bad, expect voice acting, the voice acting pretty good and fits the style.Either way the game is "ok", but would I recommend it? _childDocuments_.review: There are some GLARING issues with this game.First off is the movement outside of combat. Its about as poorly put together as it could possibly be. Its as if the developers thought about what the most awkward movement system might be like and used the worst option available. Honestly, who makes a game where you can either run or move the camera with the mouse. You legit have to mouse run and keyboard turn the camera, exactly WTAF? "Yes, I understand we have a working system with keyboard running and mouse camera panning, and yes people like this system. THATS WHY WE SHOULD REVERSE IT!" Exactly.... STUPID.Then there is the combat system. Where some of your characters will miss constantly with an 80% chance to hit and some will hit nearly every time with it. You will spend every healing spell you have the round after the first enemy contact, because the enemy will always be able to flank you, or deal aoe and status effects, or flat out one shot you, on normal mode, with some well overpowered normal attack, which in turn requires you spending tons of gold buying bandages to repair injuries because you have half the HP you need to be playing an ACTUAL RPG. And then you have 3 turns to pick the person up, which is fine, unless it decides they will take 2 turns of death counter each turn, and then well, you dont. Randomly.... And lets not talk about clicking a skill and it moving you instead, just wow. Making skill bars you can click through should have died in the 90s. Basic QA failure right there. Hows about missing a 102% chance to hit attack? Remember the game calculates the enemy chance to avoid into that number, so anything at 100% or over is a.... miss???All that being said, the story is so far great, the comedy is pretty much nonstop, and its presented in a decent format, but with such almost intentionally obvious issues, its hard to give it anything but a soft no. Maybe on a 75% off sale. Fixing either the terrible movement issues, or the terrible balance of combat would would help, fixing both and I would say buy at retail price. I would love to come back and change this review later. I hope I get the chance.
