_childDocuments_.review: This is a tricky one. I would say my recommendation would be to wait for a sale or a bundle before picking this one up. As much as I enjoyed it I would say mechanically the fights tend to very annoying.First off let's get one thing straight, if you come into this expecting something like D&D you will be a bit disappointed. The combat system is very different and it takes some getting used to before you start figuring out what works. Mechanically it feels more similar to something like xcom with all the cover taking and overwatch shenanigans. This is a tactical game first and RPG second as there isn't really any character customization or actual roleplaying.  One thing you need to understand upfront is that the game is incredibly linear aside from a few side quests. Every encounter is scripted and paced with the story. There is no grinding for loot or XP or gold, you get what you get. Even the stores only sell a premade list of items that doesn't change only only restocks after advancing certain chapters.The pros:- Generally good voice acting (english version). Some of the side characters are shaky(thinking you cheese wizard, what ♥♥♥♥♥♥ intern did they get to do that?) but the main cast is quite good.- The humor. Rarely laugh out loud but got quite a few smiles out of me.- Great art design. Love the cartoony designs or the world and characters.- Really good music. Apparently composed by the original creator of the series.- Likeable main cast depending on your preferences. The Meh:- The story. Serves its purpose as a general vehicle for more comedic bits and tropes but is otherwise unremarkable. There's no character growth, no forging of bonds, no sense of a broader world outside of the dungeon. The party is the exact same group of bickering ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ by the end of the game as they are in the beginning. - Weird mechanics. Like I said, this game is not D&D. Where in D&D you would have only AC vs attack in this you have precision which affects your chance to hit. But wait! You also have parry and dodge, and the final damage is affected by your protection rating. To me it seems like an unnecessarily complicated system.- I'm not sure I like the skill system. Early on it's very difficult to tell what skills would actually be useful and use factor is all over the place. Some skills/passives feels incredibly OP while others feel like you've been ripped off.- Some consumable buff items seem a bit useless and there are wayyyyy too many of them considering you mostly need to keep healing on your belt for emergencies and you only get 1-3 slots. Since you can only earn a finite amount of gold in this game I saved all my money for gear upgrades which are a permanent buff.- Dice rolls are fixed based off of a random seed meaning that any time you reload a fight you're going to get critical fails in the same order. Also affects if you can disarm traps while exploring, no amount of reloading will make a fail on 75% chance roll un-fail.The cons:- Weird tonal shifts into areas I would consider too dark for what is otherwise a light hearted fantasy romp. I blame it on the game being French.- Incredibly frustrating RNG. Like Xcom it suffers from missing a 95% chance to hit. Even worse are the critical failures which apply debuffs and can occasionally knock down your characters, taking them out for a round. Enemies can fumble too but you're going to be seeing it way more often for your characters.- No ability to grind. Unlike a real CRPG there is no ability to compensate for difficulty by grinding for XP so some fights can be brutal.- Due to the isometric perspective and ability to rotate the camera it's sometimes impossible to see traps until you blunder into them. You can switch to the thief to see them but his walk speed is incredibly slow. Just kinda feels like it's deliberately wasting your time.- Some of your buffs require your heroes to bunch together but by the midgame most enemies can spam AOE so there's never really a happy medium between having a shieldwall and just letting your guys spread out.Conclusion: DON:TAOC is a beautiful game with good music, likeable characters, and amusing humor but I find that its clunky tactical combat mechanics hold it back from being a truly great game. While I was initially excited by the greater complexity of the combat system compared to 5E, I eventually realized that its complexity added no depth and just added annoyances and frustrations. If the main thing that attracts you to this game is the humor and setting I would honestly just recommend blasting through it on easy. I think it would be best enjoyed as an episodic fantasy romp with as little friction from the combat as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: [Review as of chapter 5]Someone had told me long back that this game was adapted from a popular french D&D like audio-show, so had my eyes on this one for a long while. Naheulbeuk is a curious case where the game looks and feels like a western RPG but is a rather linear experience with fixed characters resembling more a JRPG. Now why am I reviewing this when I'm not even close to completing it? Quite frankly I'm bored already even though I enjoyed my time with it.This is one of those games where the quality really depends on what you expect to get out of it. Are you someone who prioritizes gameplay above all? Good, this game prioritizes that too, so lets talk about it. The tactical turned based combat is fairly well designed, the inspiration rather obviously being Divinity Original Sin 1 and Xcom. The skill trees feel a bit lacking in variety but you get a steady supply of useful abilities to keep battles from getting monotonous. Despite the linear nature of the game, there's enough of an incentive to explore and get new loot too. There are very few fluff battles apart from a couple of side quests. It's apparent that fights in the main quest are designed carefully since the game always forces the starting position of both enemies and your party, often in inconvenient places and every time I only barely made it out alive. Now for me, this neither a positive or negative since the what you gain in the dev's careful design, you lose in freedom present in something like D:OS.What does grind my gears is the dice rolls in this game, I urge everyone to play on lower difficulty if you prefer your strategy to shine in battle instead of dice rolls. I'm not sure but suspect the game influences dice based on difficulty. The game takes an absurd pride in crit failures, going so far as to design a weird system which rewards you with some abilities the more crit failures you have. I understand the value of % chance in tactical combat, but there's a fine like between amusing moments of failure/success and moments that make you want to tear your hair out and I'm afraid this game crosses that.But what about the story, you may ask as that's the cornerstone of RPGs in general. I would be remiss to mention that given that I haven't finished the game, judging the story would be a mistake now. Be that as it may, what I've seen didn't fill me with confidence. There's a prevalent comedic vibe to the whole writing here that saves it from mediocre drudgery but the jokes are also very hit or miss, more misses for me. Since I knew the game was French in origin I switched to that VA at first and while it's certainly better than the English VA for most of the cast, I wasn't a fan of how the wizard and the dwarf sounded so switched back. Maybe jokes land more in french? Could be but I wouldn't know until I get better at the language.That brings me to the characters, which are... certainly there. Like, every character is just a parody of their class without the extra spice to make them stand out. There's 1 character in the whole party that you have choice in picking who had her own quest but it's just an excuse for comedy and combat that anything meaningful. I had been watching the Critical Role Vox Machina animated adaptation recently and while the writing isn't anything to write home about, the characters are all lovable and worth following in their adventure. That is not the case here.Overall Naheulbeuk is an interesting game with fun combat that's worth playing in small chunks if you get that DOS itch. It's certainly a cut above most turn based games I've played. I myself will probably return someday to finish it, who knows, maybe the story improves later on.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics, sound and performance are good. I'm enjoying the Xcom-style combat. The battles are challenging. The AI is decent and tactically impressive. I haven't seen it make any stupid or shortsighted moves yet. The game mechanics, hit-chance modifiers and the buffs/debuffs are well balanced. There's plenty of items, skills, abilities and environmental interactions to give you the best chance of success. When you do get a run of bad luck, the game has a "super-bar" that fills up whenever you catastrophically fail; allowing you to even the score should you experience too many bad rolls.The skills and level-ups are varied with plenty of choice within and between characters. The dialogue, story and narration is a fun pastiche of the fantasy roleplaying genre. I expected it to be annoying but I found it engaging. I didn't expect this game to be anything special but I was impressed with it. I'd recommend it to anyone who likes Xcom and the tabletop fantasy genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The whole style of this game is very tongue-in-cheek and it is based on a DnD parody, which might be off-putting to some people. The questing is very linear and you just progress through a dungeon level by level with the occasional side quest with some limited scope for different choices. The itemisation and skill trees are not that extensive but give a bit of room for player decisions and ways of approaching the game.However, the combat is done really well in this game - it is turn based with grid based movement and action points for attacks/items/spells each turn. Not all of the fights are challenging but there are several during the game which require a change in tactics and quite a bit of strategic thought. I died numerous times during my playthrough and had to change my approach to the harder fights, which made it very enjoyable as a challenge to overcome. The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk is a short, simple and silly game but is well made for what it is and the fights make it worth playing in my opinion. I would give it a 5/10 but with a positive slant.

_childDocuments_.review: The oddball humor here struck the perfect balance for me. The voice acting does a nice job of making characters sound very natural despite the frequent hijinks, but the names of skills, items and enemies provided me with a lot of moments where I simply laughed aloud. The comedy might not be for everyone as a lot of people want dark and serious stories, but it’s well enough done here that  shouldn’t be dismissed just because it puts such a focus on humor. might be the most defining characteristic, but the core gameplay mechanics are quite sound as well. They are seldom surprising, but they are well done and the combat – which is where you spend most of your time – is satisfying. At its core, you move around the field of battle, making attacks, with heavy influences based on which direction your character is facing and pulling heavily from Dungeons & Dragons in terms of who combat works out. You are in control of several characters from the get-go, which definitely makes things a little more interesting and complex compared to many strategy games that let you sort of dip your toes in the water with a character or two, introducing new characters (and by extension new classes) along the way. That lends itself to the early challenges, but also the game’s more unique elements during combat. The characters all have their strengths and weaknesses, but they have some unique traits that make the strategy elements more compelling as a result.If The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet of Chaos was content just to tell a goofy story with a bunch of charming humor, it would have been a pretty solid offering. However, this is also a very solid tactics / RPG hybrid that offers a really fresh take on a very familiar genre.- An interesting dungeon crawling RPG- Great humour on display- Combat is fun to get to grips with- Good story- Menu layout is pretty confusing initially- No respawning enemies to level those units that missed some experienceDISASTER | BAD | MEDIOCRE | OKAY | GOOD |  | AMAZING | MASTERPIECE

_childDocuments_.review: Good RPG overall. Not the greatest, not the most polished one, but definitely a fun game with a lot of stupid puns and dialogues and some good old RPG mechanics.Well-suited for neophytes on RPGs, as most of the mechanics (character progression, inventory management) are simpler; still a fun game to play with some challenging fights for more experienced RPG players.+ Nice art direction+ Puns and silly dialogues all the way+ Everything a RPG should have (exploration, dialogues, battles, character progression) but more accessible than most RPGs+ Unique story based on the original audio saga- Lacks some polish (moving around / interacting with items sometimes feel weird, as each character must reposition before the interaction can be done)- Sometimes feels slow (interface, saving as there is no quick save option, fight animations too but there is an option to accelerate them)- A few bugs remaining- "Iron-man" mode still missing

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, there is a lot of deep tactical action here, to the point where I spent weeks on this in a row, cracking the main game and the 3 DLCs.  The 3 DLCs together add on about the same content as the main game, so getting the whole package is well recommended.However my big warning here would be, only get if you like involved tactical combat, as playing at the 2nd hardest, I felt this was the perfect balance of challenge and reward.  As besides that there are some big turnoffs.For starters, the story is pretty forgettable.  So there's little to make you invested.  Some of the characters are ok, but they're not my favourite in RPG history.  And I think this comes do to the abominable script.  Thankfully some of the DLCs eschew story and dialogue a lot more than the base game, and focus on the game's strong point - combat.  But by and large it's hard to listen to.  It has to constantly try and fail to be funny, I believe there was only a few occasions in the game that elicited anything more than a smirk from me.  And the chatter is so constant it becomes very irritating.  It comes down to the fact that it's French production I believe. The sense of humour is very alien to what I'm familiar with, and it's compounded by the fact it hasn't translated well in a number of parts.  Some of the lines just do not make sense, even though they are largely technically correct from a grammatical standpoint.  No one in native English would ever say these things.But if you can get passed that, you are in for a treat as the battles are numerous, varied, and exciting, and there's a decent bit of RPG leveling up and armour and weapon upgrading to boot.

_childDocuments_.review: In general game is not bad. Simple, but colorful graphics; interesting game mechanics; XCOM-style battles with lot of possible party builds and tactics; slow, but steady progression. Where it is really takes a dive in quality is storyline, writing in general, and voice acting (with few exemptions). While game is clearly meant to be a parody of typical fantasy dungeon crawler, writers clearly think that all humor consists of three types of jokes: characters hating each other (not creative or witty type of hate, just plain disdain); toilet and sex humor (again, nothing creative, just "look, he said poop!" or "look, boobs!" type of jokes); and literally swapping two letters in a name of person or a place and thinking that they created a parody. All dialogs are cringeworthy and trying to follow the plot is quickly becoming a chore. If you are ready to play this game for it tactical battles (which are good) and don't worry about skipping all dialogs - then try it out, of course. Otherwise I would recommend playing something different, just to avoid these sad attempts at humor from the writers of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend, but as a warning if you are frustrated with X-Com style missing then this is even more frustrating. (I mean it depends on the enemies dodge, parry, resistance too but some enemies in early and late game will cause you to scratch your head on the design in my opinion).Positives: + Music is really great. + Art Direction is also very fun. + The dialogue quips and writing are funny. (Elf with dwarf, Ranger and Thief, etc).Okay stuff: ~ Loot design is okay as you will start seeing better loot mid game. ~ No Spoilers, but the game seems like it should have ended during the major boss fight that is being hyped up but it sort of just continues which felt weird to me. I felt no attachment to the end boss fight, but to each their own.Negatives: - The critical failures are not too bad, but some fights it will feel very frustrating. - Also not being able (at least from what I have seen) to add items to your belt during combat even if it adds action points is weird design).- The boss fights later on the game (the major ones) seem to be just made to be frustrating which I guess is part of the appeal but did not sit right with me.        - The Difficulty spikes remind me of Divinity Original Sin which turns me off on these types of games. It         is very possible I just am not good at these games, but when half your party gets one shot it can feel l         like not worth playing. (This is on normal btw).- The Reinforcements mechanic did keep me on my edge for some fights, but others it just felt like padding to add more to the fight when actual mechanics could have been used. - The pick "this skill upgrade between 2 upgrades" just seemed to be either be Area of Effect or more damage which was seemed lacking. Some of the characters skill trees seemed very situational. (Like adding the Elf or Paladin to get stamina back after a kill when they are super tanky or can just straight up miss shots)  TL:DR : Overall I like this game but more for the dialogue, music and art direction. The gameplay mechanics are not fun to me.

_childDocuments_.review: I strongly recommend this game for any lovers of the Donjon de Naheulbeuk franchise, especially when played with French sound settings.This game feels like you're stepping right into the audio story of Donjon de Naheulbeuk, and brings with it the pleasure of a fun game to play. The 3D cartoony graphics look nice, everything worked well, and the combats on the whole felt balanced and enjoyable, with enough variety throughout the whole game to keep me going.There may have been a few too many orc and goblin fights near the beginning, and the rarity of traps makes them annoying, as the player forgets to look for them, and then when they are caught out, they carefully walk around, only to find no other traps to disarm. Every so often the mouse-based controls get in the way, such as when clicking and holding to go around a large obstruction (the characters might start dancing from side to side without going around the obstruction), or when clicking on a location and then clicking on the lift, which makes the characters pause briefly.Overall would say that this is a great game. It was a good introduction to a simple RPG dungeon crawler with turn-based combat, while providing a fun story, especially to those who already know the setting.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this game a recommendation of "maybe" or "only when significantly on sale" I would. I don't write reviews pretty much ever, but I felt I should with this one. I purchased this game because like many denizens of the internet and geekdom, I like Felicia Day and find her hilarious. Her talent could not carry the game enough for me to give it a positive rating though.The game is very well polished, the English voice acting well done (with 1 or two exceptions), and the graphics are decent (not bad, but not spectacular either). One very wonderful thing about the game is that it has the unique position of being bug free as far as I could tell. I'm sure if someone digs deep enough they could find them, but there was nothing obvious, large or small to break immersion from the game. For a PC game that seems rare to me that a game is so bug free.The gameplay though was average. There is very little character customization outside of your stat points and the small skill trees. For my playthrough, my characters ended up with 3-5 specialized skills each outside of standard attack, defend, use item, and move. This gives the game a more casual RPG feel to me. Each character is suck in their individual class and you get to pick one additional character if you wish, but there is a good amount of overlap between characters' skills and ability, unless you heavily skew everyone's stat points in different areas. A few characters had unique skills such as the thief's trap detection and disarmament, but with that example there was so little risk to stepping on traps and the exact same item reward (the basic grenade that is quickly useless after a few levels) from each disabled trap regardless of level or playtime it felt unnecessary. The combat was standard fare and executed well; nothing bad but nothing unique or that stands out.The story fell flat for me. Prior to playing the game, it seemed like it would be hilarious and comedic. While playing the game, there were lots of jokes, but the best they could get from me was a small chuckle and not a laugh. The humor here was generally based on RPG stereotypes and failure, with nothing feeling too original except for the elves being morons instead of highly intelligent. However, everything was fairly silly, so it wasn't awful either. Many of the things the characters will say are the same, just stated in slightly different ways (e.g. the Barbarian always wants to fight and his god hates everything unrelated to fighting, the thief is a coward and everyone ignores him). I felt very little depth to the characters and often was bored by them.So, do I recommend this game? No, not at full price, unless you are a person who loves any RPG and can more easily find things to be funny than most people.

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is just absolute gold. Whoever wrote the script for this game needs to be given a bloody medal. It is right now the *only* thing keeping me trying to enjoy this game because it has the single worst, most infuriating RNG system I have ever experienced in a game since the 80's.I knew it was coming too. Everything was going pretty well until the game introduced the "hey if things go bad, here is a meter of buffs that will fill up to make you feel better". The second that came up I immediately knew the game was now going to go out of its way to screw the player over and I have yet to be disappointed.Every single combat since that thing has been a non-stop chain of critical failures, 90% miss streaks, constant enemy crits and oh, I missed the explanation where they discussed how NPCs don't pay any attention to attacks of opportunity. I have given up on even trying to set up units with threat squares as the NPC will routinely just stroll right through them without a care in the world.I really want to like this game but at this point I barely make it through a single combat before I have to stop playing because the game is just that dead set on making you miserable. Hell I found Darkest Dungeon less aggravating and that game comes right out and tells you it is designed to screw you over.So sorry, this one is getting a thumbs down from me on my review. Really really wanted to enjoy it and I tried. I would watch a show if they ever made one based on the game so long as they hire the same writers but as a game it is just not enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid turn based action rpg. Had a lot of fun and actually finished whole thing over the span of two months, which is something I rarely do anymore. The game has just the right length and finishes before you get bored with it.Best part is the turn based battle system. You should turn up the difficulty to have some challenge but then it delivers with just the right mix of casual fun and optimizing turns and skills/equipment. Especially the fate bar is a welcome addition to the tactial rpg genre. If fills up whenever your characters roll a critical failure and you can use it for a couple of useful, but not overpowered global spells. This way you never get too annoyed with a string of bad rolls.Gear is character specific and recommended attributes are highlighted, which makes things a bit too simple, but the skill trees are quite nice and fun to spec into.The humor is a bit hit and miss. I assume a lot of that is due the game being translated from French so the jokes don't translate so well.While the characters can be a bit annoying at times, they grew on me a lot during the chapters. And yes, the elf's voice is grating but I think it's on purpose and quite fits the character.

_childDocuments_.review: Just Nope...This is the third or 4th time I've tried to get into the game and just as many times as I've uninstalled it.The banter is fun, character interactions are entertaining for about.... all of 5 minutes then it gets annoying.We want to be witty, we want to be cute, we want to be funny... But we fail at tactical turn based gameplay.The gameplay is just frustrating and you spend more time as a group of rejected morons than a group of capable adventurers.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really surprised how people can find this game a pleasurable experience. The jokes and the voice acting are really cool.But the fights - the tactical pleasure isn't there. They are long and clunky. The game throws at you countless enemies, super long encounters, poor character development and freedom in exploration nor in building your team. You miss attacks that are sold to you with a 120%+ hit chance regularly like 5 times in a row. Your characters are more or less one hit, overwhelmed by 30 enemies that cannot be killed in under 30 minutes since there are nearly no workable AoE's and they stack in line behind your frontliners because of how spongy they are. Yes - I do play on the hardest difficulty like I always do but oh boi, some design choices in this game cannot be understood by me. And I feel really exhausted to continue playing, I'll finish it at some point since I paid for it. But really this game is not enjoyable. If you thought this would be a nice turn based divinity-ish rpg like I thought before I bought and played this, yes - it's not. Do yourself a favor and skip this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure why this game has only 89% rating at the moment, but it's great.Well polished turn-based combat with a couple of fresh mechanics, loaded with good humour and about 60h of gameplay (completionist, hard mode).Do NOT get discouraged by RND for attacking in this game as I did on beginning. Characters will miss alot, enemies will parry and counter. But that applies fairly to both sides. Additionally, devs introduced awesome Randomia mechanic that will ease the RND frustration to the minimum or even to a point where you will even want to miss an attack.If you are slightly interested, stop reading this and buy the game already. Worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Miss miss miss miss - that's what this games combat is like. Be prepared to watch in frustrating disappointment as you carefully set your guys up to pull off special moves that could change the course of a fight only to miss and miss and miss again. Pump all your points into agility and courage no matter what class you level up because that's the only way you can do any damage. You have to stack precision on all your gear, which is the hit stat, and stack agility which also gives precision, but you also need courage so you aren't always last and swarmed by enemy mobs every combat round. Even then if you do all that you are lucky to get maybe a 50% hit rate. I've lost fights to mobs with 1 health because of insanely long strings of misses. Other than the god awful combat experience the game is pretty cool, its dorky but in a fun way and I don't have any complaints about the graphics or sound or voice acting or anything. I was originally going to make a very positive review but the absolutely horrible rng combat got me so frustrated that here we are.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game if you like DnD or if you would like to get into it. The combat really feels like what i remember DnD was, with a few differences, i think to simplify it. Their is alot less to explore compare to a game like baldurs Gate 3, but still the levels are well designed. BG3 takes itself very seriously, this game in comparison really leans heavely into humor, wich i love. The party feels more alive with you're characters bantering the whole way, it's pretty great. You get to choose for each hero a simple but interesting skill tree. Placing youre stats is great, i don't like modern games that place them for you... so i appreciated that aswell. Maybe you're items feel less of a choice... and more of a linear progression... I think their could be more items, and more ways to make youre characters unique trough them...making you choose what to spend youre gold on, that would be my one complaint. Same for exploration, their are sidequests but for the most part it's pretty linear so far. That said, it's still a good game, if you like BG3, you will most likely like this one aswell. I recommend giving it a shot :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't take itself too seriously, which is good. If you jump into it looking for a story-driven game, with super interesting plot-lines and intrigue, this game isn't for you. The story is decent, but it's there mostly to give the players an objective to navigate towards. You have a cast of charming characters, with some humour and awesome voice-acting. The gameplay itself, class variety, and battle system is pretty good too, and it was what motivated me the most to say.The negatives, in my opinion, are a few things related to Quality-of-Life. The camera feels unnecessarily clunky at times, and during combat it can be difficult to see the effects of certain attacks from enemies who are standing far away from your party. The fact that no fast-travel exists apart from the Lift is a bit of a negative for me as well. If you like turn-based rpg's, and aren't looking for something with a long and in-depth story, pick this up! Particularly if you find it on sale. If you're looking for awesome story-lines, you may want to give this game a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loathe the RNG in this game. It is my biggest turn off of a game I should adore. How can a 140% chance to hit backstab, not only fail to connect but also be critically parried causing your enemy to kill your team? Your abilities often hit your own team mates despite the odds being 6% or lower for friendly fire. Quite often you'll find members of your team can and will be killed before they even get a turn.If you do get this game do not bother with the higher difficulties.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: It's a somewhat simplified turn-based rpg game. I'm using term simplified because including jokes and characters, skills and items everything is like that. Their humorous joke about dwarf "you got dwarf, it's just dwarf" also worked for their game. You got game, it's just game. By all means it's not a terrible game but somewhat lacking, as i said skills are basic and limited, items are basic and limited. Jokes are... sailing between somewhat mediocre and a bit good. Characters are predetermined and you can't create new ones like crpg games. There are no shortcuts on skills so you need to tediously click them every single time, there are no skip, fast forward even speed up options on enemy AI so you need to watch every. single. combat. action. also they got some absurd RNG, while i'm not unfamiliar rng system (i love playing hardest difficulty games like xcom, wasteland, mordheim, darkest dungeon etc.) this game maybe one of the most broken rng between all listed. It feels there's no difference between %90 and %50 hit chance, you can critically fail your action and damage yourself while you got %90 chance to hit with two character supporting you while flaking enemy. I mean wtf. In the end, i decided to refund. I would %100 play it if it was crpg and a bit more detailed and polished for sure. Just try it maybe it was your cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a no recommend based on what kind of player I am. That is to say, a semi-casual simple gamer.I like tactics, I like strategy. I like chess, checkers, Age of Empires, games that have a set of rules and parameters that one can work within. I also like XCOM, Divinity, Pillars of Eternity. These games do have some RNG, but for some reason this game right here takes RNG and rubs your face in it. If you hate bad luck, inconvenient coincidences, and "of course that would happen" situations, this game will probably not be fun for you. I saved scum my way through this game. Combat can be fun, SHOULD be fun, but it's not. Everything that can go wrong will probably go wrong. It's just not fun for someone who expects things to work as they should. I set up a multi-layered move that took multiple turns with skills that are on 3 to 4 turn cooldowns it's kind of frustrating when the final piece of the puzzle gets smacked out of my hand because the game decided it didn't want to follow the parameters. In conclusion, having a critical failure mechanic is not fun-inducing. Better yet, having a critical failure mechanic that is not able to be mitigated is even worse.Outside of that this game is alright. I enjoy the puzzles, the loot, the somewhat linear gear scaling, the limited skill tree. Like I said, I'm a simple gamer. Art is cute, humor is light and childish. I'm easily amused. I just don't recommend this game for casual gamers who don't like pulling out their hair.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: I like cRPGs well enough.  BG3, Pillars of Eternity, and others.  I knew this had a humorous tone going in, but what I didn't expect was this to have virtually no story, and be so  incredibly annoying.  I was at one time thinking "well maybe this would be a good game to turn my young kids onto cRPGs," but there's a ton of swearing that can't be turned off, so it isn't good for that either.Not sure who this game is for, but it sure as hell isn't me.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun tactical RPG with AAA production value, especially the voice acting. The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk's corny humor was not my thing but I challenge you to not laugh repeatedly throughout a playthrough. I'm guilty of laughing at far too many of The Elf and The Dwarf insult jokes. The combat is similar to D&D 5e with perhaps more depth and complexity. _childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Anybody who loves D&D or dungeon crawlers or turn based rpgs should play this game.  It is one of the best turn based rpgs that I have played.  Enemy AI does not pull its punches; it will generally do what a human player should have.  Also, unlike X-Com or Fire Emblem, each character is unique and their role is defined by your leveling choices.  That said, it does have numerous flaws.  First of all, the humor is kinda hit-or-miss.  It's mostly obvious references to older games or mechanics: i.e. there's a quest involving Binsc and Moo.  If Family Guy's style of reference humor works for you, then this game's probably will.  Personally, I didn't find it very funny.Second, the game is totally linear.  Therefore there is no reason to make the player wander around areas they have already cleared.  I would have been much happier with a Final Fantasy Tactics kind of thing where you just move from battle to battle.  None of the in-between stuff matters.Third, the game makes you choose between three characters, only one of which can be added to your party.  Why didn't we have the option to make our party as we saw fit?  Out of nine characters, why can't the player decide which seven are best for a given battle?  It makes no sense to me.Takeaway: great game.  Some design choices made me like it less, but still... great game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Good fun, good humour, nice presentation. Gameplay is much the same as Xcom, with two actions per turn (one movement, one attack/use item). For people complaining about RNG misses when you attack, there is a gameplay mechanic to compensate called randomonia skill. The meter charges each time you have an unlucky miss and you can elect to either redeem an instant skill boost or save it up to four tiers, unlocking a plethora of choice in free buff/skills. However the game is challenging and by no means should you expect to waltz through with ease, even if you are experienced. There is good skill and stat and equipment progression, though I heard there is a level 10 cap at present. Don't know how long the story is and what replay value there will be (DLC's or additional modes added?), but I would recommend if you're interested by this sort of game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dungeon Of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet Of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it!Plot, story, and characters were engaging. The dialogue was giggle-worthy, and not quite PG. I really enjoyed the animation and the graphics are beautifully done in that cartoony style that WoW made popular for fantasy characters. I bore easily when games get a bit too repetitive, but this kept me engaged. I'm even going to try and replay it (which is not something that i ever really do).

_childDocuments_.review: This is supposed to be a tactical rpg and while it nails the RPG aspect of it with the fully voiced (and hilarious) conversations between the entire party and anyone they encounter, combat is an absolute horrible and extremely frustrating experience. _childDocuments_.review: Selecting a new game from the main menu screen will then allow you to choose your games difficulty. There are four difficulties to choose from, Gripping Tale, this difficulty is for those wanting to experience the story and battles are more manageable to those who have no or little experience of tactical RPG’s. Tavern Song difficulty is the basic difficulty of the game in which the other difficulties are built upon. Tavern Song is ideal for those who want to enjoy their first playthrough or beginners looking for a tactical challenge.  Epic Quest is where there’s danger abound and every step forward a victory. This difficulty is for those who want a real challenge and for those who have completed the game already. The final difficulty is Gzor’s Nightmare, a nightmarish, legendary experience (just like me). This mode is only for those tactical RPG experts who know the game inside and out and want to achieve the unthinkable. There are also Advanced Options for Tutorial, you can turn this On or Off but it’s recommended if playing the game for the first time. Assign Attributes Automatically, with this turned on, your characters’ attribute points are automatically allocated in their most central attributes. Iron Man (greyed out for now will need to be unlocked), in this mode you can only have one save and cannot change difficulty levels once a game has begun. If all your party dies then it’s game over and your game save will be deleted. And finally, there’s Narrator Gender, there’s only two options here Male and Female. After deciding on your game settings you’ll be asked to start with these settings, hitting Play will start the game.  You begin Chapter One “A Felling od Déjà vu" after a short battle ending with a mysterious voice laughing as your characters lay defeated upon the cold stone floor. After which the narrator will start narrating about the group of adventurers who have just entered into the Dungeon of Naheulbeuk. There’s a steely-eyed Ranger, a brutal Barbarian, a ruthless Ogre, a Wizardess with fiery hair, an agile Elf, a wily Thief and just a Dwarf. This rat-tag bunch is your group of dungeoneers, whom you’ll guild through the dangers of the Dungeons of Naheulbeuk. You’ve entered the dungeons on a quest to recover the Twelfth Statuette of Gladeulfeurha. The statuette is guarded by a powerful warlock in a treasure room hidden somewhere within the dungeon. As you look for the Twelfth Statuette of Gladeulfeurha you will come across other characters. Some of these will have a quest for you, some will join your party on a quest. Some of the characters will want you gone, when this happens, you’ll enter Combat Mode. Each character will have Two Action Points to use each of their turns. These points can be used to perform an action such as move or attack. The amount of movement is dependent on the character, this is highlighted in Blue on the combat field. You are able to use both action points to move this will increase the range and is known as Sprinting.  Once you have moved to where you want to be you can set your characters Orientation, this is important and can help you from being backstabbed or flanked depending on where you have positioned your character. Using boxes, tables and other items as cover will also help to protect your characters reducing the damage dealt to them. However, beware of what you hide behind, somethings explode and can leave you and an area on fire or may leave a slippery mess behind on which you can slipover on to your botty. Moving to an adjacent section to an enemy on the battlefield will allow you to attack with Melee. You can attack from range if you have a ranged weapon, most characters can carry both types of weapons. This will give you some extra tactics when it comes to combat. You will also have other forms of attacks and skills as you level up your characters and give them new abilities. Highlighting an enemy will give you some details on them such as the Type of Enemy and Stats, pushing the middle mouse button while highlighting an enemy will detail extra information like Statuses and Afflictions. You can also set your character to Defence and Overwatch, Overwatch will allow you to cover an area and should any enemy cross that area under overwatch your character will attack the enemy.   Having your characters beside each other could result in them gain Support Bonus, this bonus will usually give you a 5% bonus to your Precision stat. You can stack multiple support from multiple characters, although you will have to unlock these abilities in the Skill Tree. The Skill Tree consists of Active and Passive Skills, here you’ll also be able to increase your characters Stats, Agility, Strength, Constitution, Intelligence, Courage and Charisma. You gain Two Points for your Stats and One Point each for Active and Passive Skills each time you level up your character.  At the start of every combat phase your characters will start within a zone or zones on your side of the battlefield. You can place your characters anywhere within these zones to suit you, once you have done so to your liking then you can select “Fight” and combat will commence. At the end of battle should you be successful win spanking some botty you’ll be rewarded with some Experience Points and some lovely Loot.  Some characters have extra abilities such as The Ogre is your walking inventory and will carry all your loot, potions and items. The Thief can help save you from traps by spotting them as you move forward through the dungeon. You will have to select the Thief as leader in order for him to spot any traps around. As the Thief you will walk slower than normal as you search for traps. Once you have found any you are able to disarm them and you may gain something in return.  There are multiple levels in the dungeon and you’ll have to unlock them in order to progress further with your ultimate goal of finding the Statuette somewhere amongst the levels. You start off in the basement and will work your way up through each level. On one of the levels is a Tavern where weary travelers can get some rest, do a spot of trading or find new companions to aid you. You can also find some new quests for you and your party. In the settings you’ll find options for Game, Graphics, Keyboard and Mouse, Gamepad and Audio. There are quite a few settings in the options to name here but there should be plenty for everyone to setup their perfect game. I’ve found The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet of Chaos to be a very enjoyable and funny game to play. The characters are quite funny and play off each other's dialog which is funny but if you find “French” offensive then you may want to cover your ears. The graphics are great and the music and sounds are good.  Positives + Looks and runs great + Great characters + Funny Dialog + Has achievements Negatives - Control issue using keyboard - No cards currently Lead a rag-tag bunch of unlikely heroes on an adventure full of humor and chaos in The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet of Chaos. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this the same time as King Arthur: A Knights Tale, and I have to say, this is by far the superior product. Where King Arthur is bland, drab, and uninteresting, The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk shines. The art direction is great. The characters and enemies all have a cartooney charm that fits together really well, and the entire dungeon is varied and interesting, each with it's own quirks and puzzles. Movement is a bit spongy, but a minor annoyance. The combat is well-thought out, with character skills having several choices depending on play styles and what you want from them. You get 6 to begin with, with a chance to choose one more early in the game to make it 7. What I really like is the ability to synergize character skills, for example, using one character to lock an enemy in place to allow another to execute a powerful attack, or just having the ogre turn the dwarf into a lethal lawn dart. There is a lot to consider, but it's far from overwhelming. You get one movement point and one action point, so you have to consider your positioning well, otherwise the enemy will punish you.Character loot is solid, loads of potions to choose from, the weapon and armour progression is well balanced, and your character model changes as you get higher level loot, which is a nice touch.The story has some humour in it, as the characters constantly break the 4th wall, and really, this leans into the "typical" DnD session where a bunch of inept players who don't really know each other decide to straight up murder everything in sight. You can even get a "Murderhobo" potion to help achieve that. The charcters all have solid dialouge, but the clear winner for me is the Dwarf, who's uncompromising hatred of the Elf allows the delivery of the best one-liners, like "Why don't you go p!ss your tea somewhere else" and his constant referrals to anyone his doesn't like as "fat ♥♥♥♥".There is an RNG element to the game, that is undeniable, and therefor carries that XCOM element of lining up a perfect attack only to watch your character to pull a critical fail and bollocks the whole thing. This is in line with the DnD experience of rolling the dreaded "1", but also comes with two caveats: (a) the enemies are also liable to fail like this and (b) the Randomiser bar. I really like this mechanic, where essentially every fail fills a bar that grants you certain perks depending on how full it is, such as give a character an extra attack one round or even heal the entire party. A fail in one round can lead to a game-changing move later on, so it feels less punishing. The bar even stays filled between encounters, so you could start a tricky fight with an extra edge.It's worth noting I have played this on Normal difficulty, which wasn't too bad. I had to restart a few tricky fights, but not once did I feel the urge to wing the pc out the window. I have read that higher difficulties make the RNG seem worse, but I can't comment.All in all, I have really enjoyed this game, it's been a while since I had a such a well-rounded turn-based game experience. 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I love the genera and it looked like a light hearted, fun little game, but its not really enjoyable for a couple of key reasonsPros:- Graphics are very charming- Voice acting and the banter between the characters is goodCons- Besides chosing one companion, you dont have any control over your party makeup- The level cap is 10 and each level you get one active skill and one passive. This means the build variety is very limited- As far as i know, loot is fixed, which is a cardinal sin for a game like this imo. - You have stats you can level up, but its utterly imbalanced. Agility gives hit chance, parry chance and dodge chance so 9 times out of 10 you would want to pick that with any character- The map is tiny and besides some obvious and super easy "puzzles" there is not really anything to explore- There are very few side quests and the ones that are there are pretty short and give little in terms of rewards- This ties into the two former points, but there are no ways to fight enemies, gain XP or loot or do anything really outside of the main or very few side quests. This makes the game incredibly linear - The battles which is the core gameplay here ranges from decent, to total RNG ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Between hit chance, parry/dodge chance and crits there are 3 layers of RNG at play here and more often than not, the more difficult fights get decided by dumb luck rather than tactics. I have not even finished the game, which is something i rarely do, but i got to the point now where it feels like a chore to start up the game and thats not a good sign

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun. lightweight dungeon crawler.  That said, "lightweight" does not mean "easy".  Even on the normal difficulty I find myself challenged by the AI which can be pretty hit or miss in these kinds of games.  I also don't usually like games that are heavy handed with their attempts at comedy (usually because they think they are funnier than they really are) but this one has actually made me crack a smile.  Hell, I even chuckled once or twice!  Don't go in expecting Baldur's Gate- that is not what this game is.  This game is a fun, humorous romp through a dungeon that will definitely give you enough options to keep you coming back for more - but not so many that your brain will hurt.  Give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm new to modern turn-based RPGs, having not really played them since the Gold Box D&D days. This could be such a great game, if it didn't feel so cheap in its execution. I want a game that reminds me of playing tabletop RPGs with big rule books. This is only possible if there's one set of rules for players and enemies. Unfortunately, there are two sets of rules in this game. I finally got past the Cook Boss, I'm at level 3. The enemies hit me every. single. time. They never miss. A rat bites my elf and half her health is gone. A rat! Enemies walk right up to me, walk behind me, and backstab with no danger of being subjected to an attack of opportunity. If I try this, I immediately get hit because the AI enjoys a different set of rules for opportunity attacks. What's the point of providing a tactical layout if the AI is just going to do whatever it wants to win? I wouldn't play D&D with a DM who lied about their die rolls, and I don't want to play a CRPG that's always got its thumb on the scales so it can win.

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell, the game is so full of itself that it leaves very little room for gameplay.  Or fun.  We get it.  You've played an RPG before.  Every situation requires at least a comment from every character.  Walking into a new area for the first time takes over two minutes of dialog.  When the option came to choose another character for the party I opted for no one.  Not because I wanted more challenge, just because I didn't want one more voice added to the noise.Occasionally, between conversations, there is an actual battle.  This is where the game is much better.  The combat is challenging and engaging.  The mechanics are fairly deep.  The randomness seems a bit lopsided. I have seen more than three times as many critical fails as critical hits for my party, while they seem to be more balanced for enemies.The loot system leaves a bit to be desired.  Loot, mostly.  Getting new equipment is an event, and the RNG can be cruel.  Going through the hassle of solving a puzzle to find a hidden chest is just as likely to yield a couple of potions and three pieces of junk as a new weapon or armor piece. It doesn't help that the general store only updates it's inventory with the chapter.In a nutshell, if the game would just shut up and let you play it would be much more fun.  But it won't.  They paid those voice actors good money, and by all the Gods you'll listen to them whether you like it or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Get ready to miss half your attacks. You miss so often that the game is just about unplayable. The WASD controls are terrible. Your characters keep stopping for no reason and have a delay when starting back up. The camera is really bad too.2 things that would change this game DRASTICALLY: Let you move the camera by holding down the middle mouse button (like MANY tactical games) and allow the option to restart the battle on death.I put a lot of hours in the game just to lose all my progress because my autosave saved over my manual save in the middle of a losing battle. That SUCKS!Edit: A developer helped me out and even changed autosave slots. The feedback was great! Just give everyone a LOT of agi right away to increase precision and you should have a much better playing experience. The game really is a lot of fun

_childDocuments_.review: Early review.  Ok, I'm 12 hours in.  A couple hours of that is restarting and replaying a few combats to try to get a better result.  This is an outstanding game so far.  Combat is standard turn-based combat goodness, but it is VERY well done, and different enough to keep me interested.  The characters are goofy, the story is goofy and a bit amusing.  And, I LOVE goofy!  This game certainly doesn't take itself seriously, but the combat is not watered down at all.  It's very hardcore, and can be pretty brutal.  I'm playing on the next to hardest difficulty, and am enjoying it so far.  I may have to turn it down to normal difficulty later on, but we'll see.  Lots of loot, lots of cool skills to learn, and lots of plain old fun.  I compare the combat to Druidstone: Secret of Menhir Forest, one of my absolute favorite turn-based combat games in the history of mankind.  Naheulbeuk has that puzzley aspect to combat, but there are certainly many ways to beat the battles.  It DOES have that XCOM RNG that will break your heart at the most inopportune times with lots of misses, and I feel that there are too many critical fumbles.  The A.I. also misses quite a bit, so it balances out fairly well.  Hopefully the devs will work on some balance patches.  It's not a game breaker, but all the critical fumbles can get annoying.So, great fun so far and highly recommended.  This is still a very early review, but I hope I don't have to change my review.  Jake and Elwood give this game a hearty "Rawhide" with super dark sunglasses up.  Game on, my turn-based friends![Update 9/5/2020]  Well, I am 42 hours into this game, and still going.  I just finished chapter 5, so I'm guessing I still have 10-15 hours left.  Not sure how folks are beating this game in 40 hours.  Probably playing on Normal difficulty.  I'm playing on Epic Gest difficulty (second hardest).  This game is brilliant, and has made its way to my top five favorite turn-based combat games.  [Update 10/26/2020]  I finally finished this wonderful game.  66 hours.  I still love this one, but the delays in the enemy moves got a little tiresome after a while.  And, there are still bugs, missing books that you collect for stat upgrades, healing items only work if you re-equip them after every battle, Precision stat not "visually" updating on your character sheets when you equip items with Precision bonus.  But, all that aside, the game is solid and was a blast to play.  I'm glad I persevered at the difficulty level I chose.Fabulous game.  Please make more stories in this world, developers!  I will play them all.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so bad, that I have come back after putting 20 more hours into this junk, just to give it an even worse review than I did at the beginning.My first gripes were simply with the RNG.  And yes, everyone complains about it in tactics games... but there are certain games that balance it properly, so that the combat is still fun.  I have never banged my fist on my desk more while playing a game, than I did when playing this garbage.  You literally miss 60-70% of your attacks... period.  There is no opportunity to gear a different way (see below) or level up a few more times (again, see below).  You are simply stuck missing nonstop the entire game, for no other reason than to create a placebo of difficulty.  It is INFURIATING.  And I have 1000+ hours into tactics games... I am a min-maxxer at heart... and I can confirm that it is not just me not prioritizing the right stats, or understanding how potions and debuffs work.  Next... the "loot" in this game SUCKS.  There is no sense of goals to achieve for some shiny piece of armor... no satisfying reward for slaving through one of the boring encounters for 45 minutes.  Each "Upgrade" might contain a single stat increase over the prior piece. Do not be surprised when you are stuck wearing the same horrible piece of armor for multiple chapters of the game.  Loot is few and far between... you pick up tons of garbage to sell, but there is nothing exciting to buy... no increased rarities, or "Epic" quality items to work towards.  Not to mention, you have to hold tab to see the (few) lootable items that ARE on each level... which means you pretty much play the entire game holding down the Tab key so you don't miss anything.  There is SUPPOSED to be a shop on the First Floor that changes it's stock every chapter... but at this point I am 80% of the way through the game, and it still has the exact same garbage items it had back when I hit Chapter 2.ALL of the encounters are scripted... there is no option to go grind out a few extra battles to help you get past a difficult quest, or try to increase your stats so you don't have to suffer through the endless back to back "MISS" "DODGE" "CRITICAL MISS" "PARRY" garbage that each encounter turns into.  Each boring encounter is a minimum of 30 minutes long... and only about 25 of those minutes are "action".  For some reason there is a tear inducing 2-3 second pause between EVERY... SINGLE... THING the AI does.  That doesn't seem like a lot... but when there are 7-10 enemies in a battle, and each enemy does these slow unnecesasary pauses after every portion of their turn, it stretches out into a torturous chore.  Move camera *pause*... AI walks to target *pause*... turn towards target *pause*... swing weapon *pause*.   KILL ME!   And YES, this is after I have gone into the option and turned the speed of the Heroes AND AI up to max.Lastly... there are so many blatantly cliche tricks used to make you spend more time doing stuff you dont want to do to begin with.  Doors that only open from one side, so you have to go alllll the way around the zone to get to the area you need to... or "coincidental" pillars that have fallen into your path, requiring you to take some roundabout detour in order to get to the chest, which will inevitably contain garbage anyways.  It gets to the point where there really is ZERO reason to attempt to open a door or gate when you find it... instead, just start looking for a way to get through the BS detour that is sure to prevent it's opening.I originally started this game on "Epic" difficulty, but it was so tedious and boring, that I turned it to normal difficulty just so I could spend less of my life enduring this torture.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a GOOD game, but only that. It fails to rise above "good" for a number of reasons, which will be touched upon further down in my review. I believe that it's important for people to understand that this game is a comedic/satirical game first and foremost. It does not take itself seriously (and that's okay) and if you're looking for an intricate, epicly woven, turn-based CRPG, you won't find it here. However, what you'll find here is a pleasant, enjoyable experience with some fairly funny moments, a light but engaging story, and a decent combat system that leads to some fantastic fights. It's a 7/10.Breakdown (of a few things):COMBATYou begin the game with 7 unique characters, with the option of adding an 8th member shortly into the adventure. Each character has their own class and when combined, essentially make up a traditional table-top party (roles like the Archer, Rogue, Barbarian, Bard, and Paladin). Attribute distribution and skill trees are expansive enough to allow room for some strategy, but they aren't in depth enough to really alter how a class is played out in subsequent playthroughs. I appreciate how the combat system is both easy enough to understand but also deep enough to allow players to strategize, and some of the skills are both hilarious and also really well done (the Dwarf Toss is fantastic). My primary gripe with the combat, beyond some repetitive enemies, is the Critical Failure system and Randomonia. I see what they were going for, but I think the system ends up feeling more frustrating than rewarding when you hit 2-3 CFs in a row and end up severely hindered in a fight. The more significant the element of chance, the less strategy matters. The game attempts to offset this with the Randomonia metre, but the abilities you're given do not equate to the loss of action economy you suffer from CFs.STORY & VOI found that the voice acting was decent throughout the game but that many of the characters either fell flat or were reused. Perhaps this was intentional (to mimic a Dungeon Master using different voices?) but I thought that the performances could be better. I also thought that the male narrator was quite insufferable to listen to compared to the female narrator. In terms of the dialogue, I thought it was witty at times but that the satire landed about half of the time. Sometimes a line was quite funny and at other times I was left scratching my head. The overarching plot was quite straightforward, albeit interesting, but you won't really find much here, especially compared to some other epics like Pillars of Eternity or Divinity: Original Sin.LOOT & CUSTOMISATIONTo me, this is another issue Dungeon of Naheulbeuk suffers from. Although it might feel like you receive a hefty amount of loot throughout your playthrough, once you divide it by 8 party members, it's really quite scarce. There were multiple occasions where I had party members equipped with old weapons for entire chapters (and sometimes more than one chapter) until I found a replacement. I wish there were more loot options that offered unique abilities, and more shared loot that could be used by multiple classes. Due to the nature of the game and it's preset classes and characters, there's also zero customization, which is always a sad thing in a turn-based, fantasy RPG. Again, this is understandable given the context of the game, but I think it only hinders it in the long run. The ability to complete customize characters in subsequent playthroughs would have been a nice compromise.BUGSI encountered a few visual bugs (for example, a dwarf appearing to hold an axe but no axe showing). The game also crashed on me several times, primarily during loading screens.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like turn based tactics, satisfying character progression, tongue in cheek comedy, bright colourful spell effects, and a storyline that pokes fun at all of the fantasy dungeon crawling tropes, then pick this game up at full price. _childDocuments_.review: I won't bring anything new to the table here, but I enjoyed The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet of Chaos way more than I anticipated. Humor is hit or miss in games, but it works pretty well here, even though the companions do get a bit redundant after you've played for a while. It's hard to consider this a true RPG when all the characters are pre-made, and you only get to shape their skill trees and attributes when you gain a level. I think "tactical turn-based adventure" is a more apt description. The main story and sidequests are fun and lighthearted, and you'll feel quite satisfied by finishing each one. There have been numerous complaints by other players about the critical miss/critical failure gimmick in the game. This did not bother me at all as you are given PLENTY of ways to work around a character's failings. I could see it being a problem with a small party, however you have SEVEN adventurers to work with, so failure will not impact you too adversely. The enemies can fail as well...it seems pretty well balanced to me. I had to restart a couple fights on normal difficulty, which is the setting I play all games at. I don't feel the need to torture myself on high difficulties, life is short and there are a lot of games to play. The pacing is great. the battles can last a while but aren't too long (like how some in Divinity: Original Sin can be) and the game shouldn't stress you out. I grabbed it on sale and I recommend you do as well!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, does this game get old fast. Its fun for a few hours, and there's obviously something here for someone, but it's just not for me. If you're a teenage boy, or your idea of good game writing is constant "witty and irreverent snark" then this might be for you. If not, well, prepare to be stuck in a book seemingly written by a pre-teen fan of Terry Pratchet with much less skill at turning a phrase.We get it, the Dwarf and Elf hate each other, the Ranger likes girls, the Wizardess is the straight (wo)man. But while that's fine for a few hours, they need to grow or it gets old.So the dialogue starts to drag, the "plot" is a mess (I think on purpose? I dunno), and then the combat starts to drag.Basically, every single fight is: you have little cover, the enemy has lots of cover, you cant fall back to more cover or start the fight on your own terms. That's fine - I don't need a game to be realistic if it's fun -  but then it stops being fun. Now it's repetitive and grindy.At core, enemies begin to resist many of your cooldown abilities. Your abilities can miss (XCOM, heartbreaking style), or just get flat-out resisted. Sometimes they will critically fail as well. (80% hit on three people, naw, -20 health bro. Ha! Ha!). Now that spell is back in cool-down though. Add to that enemies that have special abilities of their own (and most enemies seem to have AoE's which are kings in these often 8-on-10 battles) and you just start to drag. You have healing, but the "right" way to play combat seems to be to let characters get killed (a lot) and mostly heal only after they've dropped. That's an approach I guess, but not a super fun way to balance encounters.So yeah, the first thing to lose its luster is the story, and then the battles start to drag as well. Prior ReviewThis is a fun, funny game with solid mechanics. If you like turn-based games, you'll almost certainly like this.This game does not take itself seriously, and while that's refreshing, it does get a little old after a while. That's a personal take though, and honestly, it's a super small quibble. It's not high, epic fantasy, but it's a ton of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: DoN is a party-based, turn-based dungeon crawler, which leans heavily on standard fantasy tropes and mechanics to build a very successful experience. You will navigate a team of seven (eventually eight) scripted classic characters (ranger, elf, barbarian, wizardess) through the hand-crafted cartoon-like dungeon of Naheulbeuk. Each toon has its own unique skill tree and at level-up you may select/upgrade one active skill and one passive skill. The primary (strength, intelligence, etc) and secondary attributes (dodge, precision, etc) may also be guided by you through granted points at level-up. You will do the standard dungeon things in between the scripted fights. In battle, each toon and each enemy unit gets one turn a round, with a turn comprised of either two movement actions, or one movement action and an attack/skill (in any order). The battlefield is grid-based (squares) and features interactive objects.Pros: YMMV:Cons:Summary: This really is a must-buy for fans of party-based, turn based dungeon crawlers. The interlocking systems produce highly engaging tactical battles. Your character-builds really seem to matter and open up satisfying combos. The art and humor combined with the scripted quests produce a fantastic result. I played through this game twice, which is the ultimate compliment for me to pay a game. Overall: 9.0/10

_childDocuments_.review: The hardest thing to write is a good comedy. The easiest thing to write is a bad comedy. The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet of Chaos is the latter. It is a silly, satire-focused CRPG that does exceedingly little to separate itself from contemporaries, save its almost supernatural ability to make the player cringe at every unabashedly unfunny moment of it. In the beginning, it’s easy to be lulled into thinking the game is going somewhere. There’s a casual charm to it. The exposition is fine. The environments are better. The combat is unoriginal, but it’s still that standard turn-based tactics style that consumers have been gobbling up for years. And even the bubbly cadence with which the characters converse, perhaps only at first, doesn’t ring any alarm bells.Then Dungeon of Naheulbeuk attempts to tell a joke. Then another. Then another. Then another.Dungeon of Naheulbeuk is absolutely inundated with bad dialogue. This is a major problem because nearly half of the game is spent in either a cut scene, where the player is forced to listen to this atrocious back-and-forth among the characters, or in a battle (at about a 50/50 clip) where it is also pumped out with frightening regularity. With that much time dedicated to its writing and plot, it would be negligent not to alert a potential player coming here to experience a good story that they should sprint as hard as they can in the opposite direction. The story, in lieu of telling one, is much more interested in creating a hellscape in which the player is damned to live out eternity (20 hours) watching seven bad comedians try to top each other's handicapped wit.Like. We get it, the barbarian’s feet smell because he’s a barbarian and he’s stinky. We get it, the elf has big boobs and is completely naive to the fact that every male party member wants to experience them. You don’t have to keep jamming into the script—everywhere the stupid declarations might fit—that the barbarian is likely suffering from a fungal infection, or that the elf’s mammaries are ample. Aside from being completely unoriginal (unoriginal by design, as each character is purposefully a trope), there’s nothing funny about any of it. Dungeon of Naheulbeuk is like an etiquette test that quizzes adolescents on whether they’ve reached an acceptable level of maturity for public consumption. With one of the main questions being, At what point are you old enough to stop finding stinky feet and large breasts, without a punchline or context, funny? Now, what if I say it 50 to 100 times, what then? What if I never, ever stop saying it? As this massive fart-joke-on-steroids takes center stage, it quickly and irreversibly pulls focus from every potentially positive moment of the experience. There’s actually some decent content buried here. But as the deluge of indulgently bad dialogue continues, that decent content becomes harder and harder to distinguish. Eventually all you notice is tons of shockingly bad humor. So, strap in for bad jokes! And repeated bad jokes! And cringey jokes! And, my personal favorite, completely illogical jokes(!) like this winner: “[This situation] is worse than kissing an albino pony.” Good one, fellas; because everyone can relate to that!I’ve spent most of my adult life enjoying turned-based combat games. As video game genres go, and specifically as an RPG staple, they’ve become difficult to avoid. There’s a canonized formula to how the action unfolding in combat situations is built to work. And this game is mostly the same. You will control your party of seven (or eight if you so choose at one point) characters that all come with their own set of unique attributes and skills to use in combat. And I will give Dungeon of Naheulbeuk a lot of credit in this regard. The combat works, looks, and feels good.However, I don’t trust the RNG.  After a severely inordinate amount of “Critical Fails” that were sending my fired arrows back into my own characters’ faces, I furiously decided to reload a Save. Upon reloading, I tried the same move—and I got the same result, critical failure. So, I tried it again; the same result continued. Then I decided to try other moves. I was shocked to find that no matter what move I attempted (an attack, a heal, or a buff), I was destined to critically fail. And because the game does a poor job of differentiating between the enemies, the spells or attacks you elect to use are even more important than they usually are in battle. You really can’t waste a move, as there’s no great way of telling which of all the different spells your foes will be resistant to, or what they have at their own disposal to counter you with. In other words, no matter how accidentally appropriate my input was for the given situation, it was always going to fail. My choice never mattered. How can you critically fail a roll that never happened? If reloading is cheating, so too are loaded dice. The aesthetics (which you might notice when the game avoids talking for longer than a minute) are quite nice. The environments through which the party travels fit nicely within the pantheon of fantasy dungeons. Expect the usual suspects. There are plenty of rats, spiders, orcs, and goblins to kill. And even if some of it is undoubtedly hackneyed, the game still does a respectable job of creating a world that makes sense in a fantasyverse. As a bonus, there’s a tavern enhanced by appropriate music. It’s frankly the only part of the game I’d recommend playing un-muted. It’s a charming respite from the misadventures (and abhorrent literary composition) awaiting outside its doors. Somewhere here, buried deep inside, is a decent turn-based tactics game, which I enjoyed at first. However, what slowly cocooned around the core was a hardened tumor that prevented any decent idea from flourishing. Each continuing hour of the game was another hour spent in a realm of tit jokes, fourth-wall breaks, and poorly utilized pop-culture references. And the more they came, the more my contempt grew.A boss late in the game describes the entire setting as a “s****y dungeon” in an attempt to be funny. It was, ironically, the first time the game made me laugh. I bet you can guess why.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, the quality put into this game is apparent right from the beginning. The amount of quality voice acting and polish is abundant.  I appreciated a lot of the fantasy pop-culture references thrown in. Especially being someone who grew up on D&D & Conan the Barbarian movies and stories. The mix of comedy in this game is also appreciated. Reminded me of an 80's movie similar to Goonies where you have all your character tropes going on a crazy adventure where chaos ensues.Now for gameplay. I haven't beaten the game yet but the difficulty of this game caught me off-guard. I played on the default difficulty. (For context, I've beating X-Com 2 on veteran difficulty I've also beaten Darkest Dungeon so I'm familiar with punishing gameplay.)But I wasn't expecting the amount beat downs I'd get right from the start of this game. For at least the whole beginning act you will be at a severe disadvantage whether being outnumbered or always starting out surrounded by enemies. Not to mention the amount of physical resistances, dodging and misses on your part that will happen. On top of that, the AI is very smart. Think you've got everyone locked down with 'overwatch'? Nope, the enemy might just stand still so not to trigger your overwatch or lob a projectile at you breaking your overwatch completely... it's so disheartening... Want to trigger that perfectly setup 'attack of opportunity' by knocking an enemy back? Nah, you either miss, they dodge it or they get hit but physically resist being pushed back... oh the frustration. The funny thing is as you grow in power, all of these problems become less and less as you can withstand a lot more damage and miss less. It also seems the enemies themselves become easier as you encounter higher level enemies. Where as beginning enemies like goblins and spiders always have projectiles and melee weapons at the ready, higher level enemies like Deathknight can only melee.Yes, it is more rewarding to win because of these difficulties but less so when your strategies are negated by their innate defenses and you have to settle for just bludgeoning your enemy to death with brute force instead. It's not always the case but happens often enough.My conclusion, it's a fun quality game if you can muscle through the beginning parts. The love and passion put into this game is obvious and is worth buying in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10This is a really funny and entertaining turn based game that pokes fun at fantasy and D&D tropes and stereotypes.The game is fairly linear, you do get to make a few story choices but other than the choice to add Priest/Paladin/Bard to your party the other choices are minor.I would totally recommend this game, it was almost bug free for me. The main pain points I had were:* The movement (out of combat) is not good. It feels really awkward to move the party with keys and clicking is frustrating. Pro tip: You can just hold the mouse down which I discovered way to late. Still not great though and given the weird map layouts I had to open the map constantly (even with minimap zoomed out) to make sure I didn't dead end myself.* The primary bug I experienced multiple times was when moving I would try to rotate the camera or use the highlight objects button and the party would stop. Thankfully you can "fix" this by selecting a different character to lead and try again, usually that will fix it, at worst you have to try a few more. Loading probably fixes it for the affected characters as well.Despite the above, I really enjoyed the ride and am definitely considering doing another play through.
