_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game, but just for content before chapter 7.I haven't played any turn-based tactitcs game other than FFTA and FFTA2 before, which are the two tactic games that I will replay every one or two years, and recently I just found that there are actually some other similar PC games, like this one.For the first few chapters of this game I actually really enjoyed,  good graphic design, good animation and lots of details, although the gamepad controlling is not really good to me, and the lack of comparison on equipment is a bit annoying to. But as I said on the title, I personally would only recommend playing until chapter 7, where the battle on the bridge happens, and I've searched online and found that I'm not the only one who was stopped by this battle. I played under normal mode, because of course I don't want it to be too easy but also I just want to play what is default at first and also to enjoy the game more. The whole time it was fine, with a few challenging battles which I eventually handled by putting a little bit more thought. BUT, until I started the battle on the bridge with the lever, of which IMO the difficulty is totally not what default mode should look like. I tried twice with normal mode and then I finally managed to get through this battle by switching to the easy mode, which I think totally made the whole gameplay experience broken to me. This battle made me feel like I need to build my team during the whole gameplay very carefully before I start this battle or the chance would be really low for me to win it. I know some people love challenging, and I do love a little bit of challenge too, but not like a difficulty jump from 5 to 10 challenge, and I really don't want to torture myself when playing a video game... So it all comes to this point: the default difficulty is already a hard mode for most of the people, which doesn't make sense at all because if I can only switch to an easy mode or spend hours and hours to deal with some of the battles then it would be so frustrating playing this game, making me feel stupid. Citing words from a review by Cory Cauthon on RPGFan: 'I shouldn’t have to lower the difficulty to story mode to avoid trash monsters chaining critical hits on my party. ' which is what I want to say, I think default mode should be like you can handle all of the battles without draining your brain, while the default mode in this game make me feel like when it comes to hard battle, you can either rely on luck or you have to take every step really really carefully, which is really tiring. The bridge battle really made me don't want to play this game anymore. It's so weird that I couldn't stop playing this game the last two weeks but a single battle just totally changed my mind.. It's such a pity because I did have a lot of fun during the first few chapters.However with such a bad experience I would still recommend this game, most of the things in this game are really great to me, but like I said only before chapter 7, unless you are those who just want to challenge yourselves, or in other words, torture yourselves..oh btw I bought all dlc after the first day playing it and now I regret it...

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon crawler that is initially a lot of fun, but quickly turned to more on the clumsy side.Initially the humor, characters, and the story create a really funny vibe. Sadly the comically overdrawn characters turned out to be overly stereo-typical for my taste and after a few levels the writing of the narrator gets worse and the humor starts to be not that funny anymore. In the last third of the campaign i just tried to ignore it. The encounter scripting, lack of control over combat, limitations in encounter settings, and the ridiculously low effectiveness of buffs (or how long they last) makes the combat less and less enjoyable over time.Based upon this I don't see myself to ever replay nor to pickup other DLC.You might still enjoy this game if your play that with your friends over a couple of evenings and beers.If you want to experience RPG and dungeon crawling you might be better off to pick up or replay Baldur's Gate, Planescape Torment, Icewind Dale, Neverwinter Nights, or Divinity Original Sin as they offer a far better experience and more replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly well made game. On the technical side, The UI is user-friendly, the game run well even on lower spec, with a very well made fluidity in term of movement, both from characters and camera. The music is good, but a bit forgettable. Voice acting is top notch, both in english and french.Gameplay-wise, it's a surprisingly solid tactical game with a 30 hours lenght, with each character having his own aesthetic, gameplay and role, with enough builds to make a few different runs. Difficulty is quite hard in the beginning, then lower little by little. Story is engaging, but what drive the adventure is definitely the characters, with a top-tier banter, faithful to the original Donjon de Naheulbeuk.Honestly, a very, very solid game. If you like fantasy, tactical games, and to have fun, then it's one of the best you can have today.

_childDocuments_.review: I am on the fence because I really thought I was going to like this game. The first hour or so was very enjoyable, but it became kinda boring and repetitive very fast. The witty one liners were fun at first but eventually they lost their charm as they were constant. A joke becomes uninteresting when you hear it 10 times and a funny quarrel between two adventurers becomes attritional after the 5th time.I get that the universe itself is meant to be a parody of RPG fantasy but if it didn't feel it was trying too hard to be funny, it would have probably been much more enjoyable past the first couple of hours, at least for me.Overall maybe give it a try if it's on sale and if you enjoy turn based RPGs, but it's not worth the full price for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not the best game out there in terms of tactics or combat. But still it's decent. The game makes fun of RPG clichés, offers plenty of good humor, a bit of adult humor and overall, the game makes the player feel like he is part of a comedy show of some sort. The voice acting is really good. I also like the story very much. It is full of mystery and unfolds slowly.Each character has a unique personality, and this is really important when you have to control 7 characters. They are not just minions or pawns. The player gets to care about the characters even after an hour in the game.Everything else about the world design, I guess is top notch in this genre. Beautiful graphics, music and sound effects. The RPG mechanics are solid but with a funny twist. You have XP, skill points, attribute points, gear, inventory consumables etc...It is like XCOM (combat), Divinity (artwork / medieval theme) combined with your favorite comedy show.Pros:-Humor!!!-Voice acting-Dialogues-Story-Artwork-Combat-Character development / gear, skills etcCons:I think the game could be a little lighter in terms of hardware requirements. I mean it feels heavy. It needs a decent GPU so as to run smoothly. As for the gameplay, I guess the mechanics of miss/dodge/parry/failure etc could be a little less frustrating... Character animations at some point can get a lower framerate than the rest of the game, but it doesn't happen often and I am getting very picky now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for September 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before October 4th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.D&D humor for good or bad. I hate this game’s name because I’m sure I’m butchering it but Dungeon of Unnecessarily long name is based on a French D&D podcast of a similar name, though obviously in French. A group of 7 adventures go into a colorful dungeon and work their way through a series of encounters with the goal of loot, loot, and more loot. The combat here is good, and the progression of the game will keep the player engaged, with one of the party members usually being swapped out for a visiting character. There’s English voice acting that sometimes works, though I’m showing one that didn’t. The real problem is the humor and writing here aren’t great. If you’re a fan of the podcast, I’m sure you’ll enjoy this title, and if you love D&D jokes, you’ll probably get a kick out of this, however, I struggle with this. I played this for Game Pass, but replaying it now made me realize the core issue. These are not new jokes,   A custodian named Jan Hitor, a dwarf shouting “Nothing goes over my head”, Dwarves and Elves fighting, a cowardly thief… Someone likes these jokes as the game is popular, but I found them tired. Pick this up if you like the comedy, though I recommend you watch someone play this for half an hour and then make a decision. Some people like this, but personally, I didn’t enjoy either playing for four hours or playing it again here. On the other hand, if you do like the humor the tactical gameplay is great, and there are four different difficulties so there should be the right challenge for however you want to play this game. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon of Naheulbeuk is a strategy game in the guise of an isometric RPG. Yes, you do wander around a dungeon but the turn-based combat is where its true heart appears to lie.First, the good:- Funny, ribald story and excellent (albeit explicit) voice overs.- Lovely comic-like artwork- Decent soundtrack (although it seems to be mostly muted in the game).Then the bad:- No mission level difficulty. When quests or subquests are handed out, there's no way to tell how hard they'll be. You will get stomped on badly if you choose the wrong sequence until your characters are high enough level or geared well enough to survive the combat.- Combat. The starts are scripted and cannot be avoided to progress in the narrative. The starting deployments very limited and very biased in favour of the computer. Almost all of the time you're significantly outnumbered by computer characters who have counters for offensive and defensive tactics, and keep throwing reinforcements at you if you can't get the prior lot down fast enough. There's no tanky-attraction so your squishies will get squished fast; archers cannot fire if an enemy is in melee range so the computer sends small. fast disposable critters in through any holes in your line and then uses acts of opportunity to prevent relocation. The random critical failures seems to hit my six characters a lot more than the opposing horde which makes combat incredibly frustrating; hard I get, but frequently it's close to impossible. At one point you need to choose a specific sixth character class to help your team, and that's a permanent choice; it appears -- I could be wrong -- that if you make the wrong choice then your life it going to be a whole lot harder a bt later on in the game.Generally I like my RPGs as an interactive story with fighty bits rather than fighty bits with a periodic narrative; this game tends towards the latter. It's definitely more Warcraft 3/Heroes of Might and Magic than, say, Balder's Gate which was what I'd been expecting. Lots of people love this game based on the reviews and I can understand that, but ultimately it was too frustrating for me to complete.

_childDocuments_.review: I was kind of sceptical, because of the comical aspect (although I like comics), but this was washed away very quickly.It is not only absolutely funny , but also a challenging tactical combat game.I fall in love with this crazy crew and their hilarious comments and all the crazy ideas - like a crime scene cleaner, who is not too happy about the mess you leave behind after your fights.A very well done variety of enemies and combat settings.I played it twice, because you can choose only one out of 3 additional companions, each with a personal quest.And because I could not get enough, I played the Back to the Futon DLC as well, which goes along with the story and provides many more hours of entertainment .I recommend it highly to everybody, who enjoys challenging (turn-based) combat , a good story and well written dialogues.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dungeon of Naheulbeuk: The Amulet of Chaos is a turn-based strategy game with RPG elements. Most of the time you will think you're in a D&D Adventure. This is TBS at it's best. This will be a classic in the genre in a few years. But first things first. A Group of seven.. beings goes into a dungeon for a quest. Early on they get separated and you'll find them one after another. This works as a tutorial to learn the mechanics of the game slowly and it works perfect as it combines this, with the characters and the world. Thanks to that, it's not your typical boring tutorial.Each character has different abilities, stats, advantages and disadvantages. The Ranger is an all-rounder whereas the elf is an archer. Every character in the group is different. The turn-based fights work as in almost every other TBS game. Comparing it with XCOM Dungeon of Naheulbeuk is just as great.You know, when you have a 99% chance to hit your target and your attack misses? This will happen in DoN, too. Although not as much as in XCOM, so don't worry. It may happen on higher difficulties more often though - so if you're a fan of that try it out. I'm playing on normal difficulty and it is easier than normal in XCOM (well, after leveling up 1-2 Characters it is easy there, too). If you want a real challenge, go for the higher difficulties or Iron-Man. DoB does not have base management. Instead, it is more like an RPG. Every character gains EXP after fights and quests. For every level, you can choose one active and one passive ability, as well as spend points in personal stats such as power, courage, intelligence, etc. Aside from all that, you get gold which you can spend to buy potions, weapons, clothes, armor and a lot more. Like in most RPG's you can make your character stronger when finding or buying better equipment. One of the strongest aspects is the story. The story is like a fairy tale in a D&D Adventure. Almost every conversation is dubbed. Even side quests are fully dubbed. There even is a narrator and the voice acting is high-class. I'm playing with german synchronization. Most of the time, games aren't well dubbed in german but this here is one of the best dubs I ever heard and the game is not even made by germans. I can't imagine the English or French version being bad. Every character in the story has their personality. And I really mean it.The story is lovely, funny and exciting. Everything you expect a D&D Adventure to be.Everything in this game is atmospheric. The setting, the music, the voice acting, the aesthetics, the story and the fights. I can't imagine anyone who is into strategy games not liking the game. DoN is a love letter to the genre. Don't wait for a sale, buy it immediately. It's well worth every cent and every hour you put into it. It's around 40 to 50 hours long.

_childDocuments_.review: The game (I won't even try to pronounce it's name, I just call it Dungeon :) has one of the best turn-based tactical combat in the recent years.Don't let the colourful graphics dissuade you, the game mechanics is deep and all battle encounters are handcrafted. In the days of total simlification, when most RPGs have party size reduced to 4-5 characters, the Dungeon lets you field 7-8 (even 10 for a time) chars, each of which is unique and useful.Even though it's pretty subjective, I liked the humor too; it perfectly captures the spirit of the tabletop RPG atmosphere with everyone bikering and making fun of each other.I full-heartedly recommend the game to everyone who likes interesting and challgenging tactical battles.

_childDocuments_.review: I see you asking why thumbs down. Believe me, I tried.  Let's look at what are the upsides first.Pros:+ nice graphics. The artwork is remarkable in general.+ character interaction in combat is good+ full voice actingThe above are all great. It would make a good quality game. But...Cons:- the game tries to be funny. All the time. Like the uncle you have who gets drunk at the first 5 minutes of every party. After a while it becomes tiresome rather than amusing.- the game keeps referencing other games / movies / books. Literaly every minute. Yes, I did play all the cited games. And miniature giant space hamsters were marginally funny even back then.- mature jokes can be fun. Again, not in this concentration.- the above makes for zero immersion. I can't be drawn into a world without any originality. - limited customization of characters. You are given a party and that is that. No customization of appearances  and only a limited skill tree. No customization of perks / quirks. Not layered enough to be worthwhile by far.- small combat arena size- combat is scripted, rather than free. Makes the game very linear despite the effort to make it sandboxThis is not the party based fantasy RPG you are looking for. This is a well drawn adult cartoon, and mediocare at that. Sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brilliant game. It's like an XCOM dev had a drunken D&D session with their mates and decided to make it into a game. The vast majority of the game is voice acted, which is a HUGE plus for me. The characters even swear! It reminds me of being around a D&D table with my friends without worrying about which dice to roll and referring to my character sheet every 30 seconds. I picked the 2nd most difficult setting for my first play-through and at about halfway through the game (presumably) it feels fair; it's one of those deals where the early game was way harder than the current mid-game once your character skill choices start getting more fleshed out.The story is really fun, the quests have brevity and there's very few (if any) "filler side quests". Any that exist are extremely tongue-in-cheek and resolve themselves well before expectations. The stat/skill system for your party is interesting, dynamic, and allows for plenty of personalty and choice. At this point I'm at [minor spoiler]  and I couldn't be happier with my purchase. I haven't touched the DLC and this game is already a 9/10 for me. If you're a fan of games like XCOM, like a bit of innuendo, and the game is on sale, buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an enjoyable game to play.  The graphics are good, the voice acting is great, and it plays well.  This is a dungeon crawler comedy of sorts that reminded me of shows like 'Harmon Quest'.  Each character is a fantasy stereotype played to the max in jest.  Characters like the Barbarian, who dresses like Conan and calls upon his god Crom.. or the Ogre who has really low intelligence and has the Magician translate for him..  They are all called as such too: The Elf, The Dwarf, The Ranger, etc. and the game is filled with adult humor and pop culture references.  I especially enjoyed the Binsc and Moo mission referring to the character Minsc and his space hamster Boo from the Baldur's Gate games.You control a full party of 7 characters and eventually pick up an 8th.  Some characters will leave and come back as the game is scripted as such.  The story flows together with the quests and there is enough to do.  Plenty of puzzles and areas to explore and plenty of ridiculous conversations abound.  Each character has their own skill tree and inventory to manage with the Ogre carrying all the items for the squad they are not using.  There are plenty of consumables and projectiles to use including chickens... which you can throw at people... Combat is comfortable to a degree.  Everyone has a few skills they can use on a timer and some basic every turn skills.  Characters get benefits from being next to other characters (sometimes specific ones) and your facings matter as a flanked or rear attacks will hit harder.  Cover is around to use as are destructible objects on the map.  Before each battle you get to maneuver your team around for placement and then you fight in turn based combat.  Your characters also do not heal after battle, so you have the option to use potions after combat or chance walking back to the tavern to sleep and heal.  Characters who are knocked out in combat suffer injuries that affect what they can do until they are healed with the proper item or rest.Combat problems come from the AI.  Most AIs in games are tuned to the monster you fight.  So, if I fight rats (for example) I expect them to be a bit reckless and attack the first character they encounter, whereas say an evil mage might stay in the rear and summon things to protect him.  Here the AI takes the best path to maximum disruption regardless.  So, for example, I move my Ogre (Tank) out to face incoming rats with my archer behind cover in the back, the rats literally run past my Ogre taking opportunity attacks from him (and damage) just to get a group flank attack on my archer.  Its just not practical and it gets frustrating at times especially if there are reinforcements coming in on certain turns.  There are some tank skills to get their attention, but then they just start maneuvering around your character and group attack at will.  Considering you are usually outnumbered, this is an issue.  Best thing to do is hold back and keep your team together.  Then you deal with their AOE attacks.  Once you find a balance with spacing and advancing, it becomes much easier to finish the fights.Overall its a good game, enjoyable and comfortable with a good amount of laughs to have and some fun combat.  Worth a look and definitely worth a sale price.

name: SkateBIRD
detailed_description: Grind on bendy straws, kickflip over staplers, and carve killer lines through cardboard and sticky tape parks, in SKATEBIRD®! You're a lonely lil' bird, and your Big Friend has hung up their board for good. Their job sucks, and lately, they're barely ever home to play with you. You're gonna fix all that with the power of being a chill little skateboarding bird. You may be tiny, but the more you skate, the more friends you’ll make. _childDocuments_.review: I hate to rag on indie games and I reeeeeally want to like this game but I can't...It draws you in with a promise that its like old Tony Hawk games but ends up being a novelty rip off on par with Simpsons skateboarding or Disney extreme skate adventure. The physics are ass, the board doesn't stay level when you ollie causing random bails unless you do their weird air ollie thing (the only thing unique to this game) just to not drop a combo from what should be a normal landing, when you ollie near a wall it always wants to put you ON the wall then makes you bail, carving ramps is weird because it gives you an inhumane speed boost. Sometimes when you do flip tricks off a quarter it moves you slightly forward so when you go to land on the ramp again instead you just smack into the coping instead and get stuck against a wall. Doing manuals randomly ends your combos for no reason. The combo system doesn't really make any sense, its like a weird hybrid of tony hawk and skate but cant make up its mind about how the multiplier should work. They clearly borrowed a lot from tony hawk but missed all the fun mechanics like reverts, other types of manuals, transitioning between tricks for more points, acid dropping into ramps (huge one for me). Makes the game just feel like its a 3D platformer collectathon that just so happens to have a skateboarding mechanic. The missions are boring and uninspired, one of them is literally "skate to this spot and ollie 30 times"...The map design is questionable, random trip hazards around the map, some edges look grindable but aren't, the top of the cooker in the second to last level is just a pain to navigate because you can't transfer into the pan and there's no smooth surface to skate on, there are just random unused areas like underneath cabinets and stuff that should just be blocked off because they serve no purpose in gameplay, some banks have their weird lips at the bottom meaning you have to ollie onto them and loose all speed you had built.The soundtrack does have its good moments but is mostly like someone heard Goldfinger in Tony Hawk and said "I want that!" you don't need trumpets in every punk song guys. Then when you finally do get a good song after skipping 10 of them you start a mission and it loops back to the first boring track that sounds like elevator music. Not even going to talk about the writing or lack of voice acting cuz it really shouldn't matter in a skateboarding game but the gameplay and mechanics DO NOT carry this game AT ALL.Currently at the time of writing this review there are 2 achievements in the game that ARE NOT ACHIEVABLE and I had to join the discord just to find that out AFTER finishing the whole game TWICE. I'm not convinced a single person on the dev team has ever actually stepped foot on a skateboard in their life or has played more than 30 minutes of a tony hawk game. I feel like they could have done a lot more with the bird mechanics, the only thing this game has that isn't present in other skating games is how floaty jumps feel and that weird aforementioned air ollie glide thing which doesn't feel good to use, it just slows you down half the time.TLDR: not as bad as Disney Extreme Skate Adventure but its close, atleast that game had "Wheres you're head at?" by Basement Jaxx but they get bonus points because the trick are named correctly in this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I love skating and I love indie studios making crazy games about it, so I'm very biased. Still, that didn't keep me engaged with SkateBIRD. Many of the game's issues have been discussed on review sites around the Internet, so I won't go into loads of details, but here are some of the game's major flaws, all of which could be fixed to make a much better game, one that fans would love to play.1) Bad Lines: skate parks are designed with riding lines in mind, but StakeBIRD's lines are hard to figure out, the space between obstacles too wide or short, or obstacles block lines. My guess is that the level designers don't skate/play skateboarding games.2) Clipping Issues: Accessories clip into the bird models. Finish the game so you can use the secret characters instead.3) Camera Issues: Especially in the character customisation window.4) Janky Physics: You can turn and ride back up a ramp without hitting the bottom of it. You can also ride in the opposite direction of your momentum if you land in reverse (fakey). 5) Poor Writing: The story is interesting enough, but the dialogue is full of jargon and functionally weak. There's little unity in the formatting too, so conversations read like teens texting each other. 6) Boring Challenges: The challenges (quests?) are usually too easy or very difficult, and mostly uninteresting. Instead of using the challenges to help you learn the stage, you often have to find items that are very close together, in one spot. I enjoyed the challenges where you're building ramps, but again, the lines are usually boring or impractical. Overall, I finished the game to finish the game, not because I felt challenged or like I was exploring SkateBIRD's huge maps.7) Deck Selection: It would be great to see more real-world skate decks included in SB. Skaters love them. Collectors love them. They have real meaning and would give players a reason to keep playing, especially if you needed to hit high scores to unlock them. 8) And couldn't we get a "Done for Today" button that takes you out of the game right away? I'm already on the menu guys!The game includes loads of options for customising your character, and a good selection of songs, but none of these won me over. I love that the stages are huge, but I think this gave the designers a big handy cap, since they couldn't make all of each stage interesting.Overall, SkateBIRD is a game I want to love but that has a lot of work to do to get good.I was given the game as a gift.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the story and that's probably all I'll be doing until more patches roll out.I looked forward to this game a lot while it was in development. It had a ton of charm to it and I definitely knew the game was gonna be of the goofy kind watching the trailers and playing the beta, so I didn't expect tight controls and extreme replayability like Tony Hawk, more so a parody/love letter to that franchise.*But Jesus Christ*I'd say it took me about 2 hours of gameplay until I had every accessibility option turned all the way up to make the countless inexplicable bails and combo breaks a little less unbearable (100%ed every tony hawk game on playstation 1 and 2 by the way, its definitely not that i'm bad at skating games).My main gripes were:  -combos ending after ollie'ing out of a manual, with the total score becoming null and void.  -your character tripping over seemingly nothing all the time  -some ramps don't launch you all the way up, causing you to exit the bowl/halfpipe involuntarily or crashing into the wall     behind the ramp  -lots of bothersome invisible walls in the later levelsIt's not all bad though, the game has some fun things going for it:  -Character customization is very fun with tons of bird species and accessories obtainable in the various maps  -The maps themselves have some fun theming, especially the manmade mini skateparks in indoor levels.  -The NPCs are really charming and the dialogue is fun.So far the negatives still outweigh the positives though. _childDocuments_.review: I really really hate to give this a No, but I'm in the middle with this game - leaning a bit soundly on No. I'm a long-time player of Tony Hawk and other skateboarding games and, while I really love the concept and overall aesthetic - the gameplay is total trash.On the good side, I love this game's sense of humor, writing, and soundtrack. Every part of the presentation is charming and gives the kind of semi-serious, semi-silly whimsy you would see in Katamari Damacy (but with birds on boards). Customization options for your little buddy are also extensive and allow you to pick from an impressive number of bird species. You can tell that the developer had a fun concept and decided to run with it as far as it could go....however, that's where the good parts end.As I said before, I've played a lot of skateboarding games in the past - both good and bad - but this one overwhelmingly takes the cake for worst gameplay in a skateboarding game. While I could write quite the long list about what's going wrong, I'll summarize the worst points:-Stalls vs. GrindsThe game never seems to know the difference between making you do a stall or a grind. Even when you go high-speed at an angle to the lip (which would be a grind in any other skateboarding game), you're stopped dead in your tracks doing a stall which messes up the entire combo.-OlliesOllies in this game try to be clever by including a double jump (since you're a bird and can fly), but jumping as a whole is so terrible that this mechanic works against you more than for you. I can't count how many times I try to ollie up to a very low rail, only to be bounced off in the opposite direction for...reasons. I can't explain why.-SpeedSpeed works very differently in this game. The logic is incomprehensible. I can jump full speed ahead at a platform and suddenly my bird loses so much momentum so quickly that it looks like I hit a floating mass of molasses that slowed me to a crawl. On the ground, things are not much better. You're fighting against the game to get enough speed to go up a halfpipe and, more often than not, you slowly but surely slide down without ever having reached the top.-TransfersTransferring in this game is comically bad. When trying to transfer out of a halfpipe, the game seems to randomly accept this request and, worse yet, may actually bounce you off in the complete opposite direction when you are trying to transfer forward up to a platform. This probably ties into how broken the ollie system is, but that's something I can only speculate. This problem means that trying to exit a halfpipe, or even doing a spine transfer (which has its own issues being too iffy/random) is a gamble. What's even more mystifying is that transferring out of a pipe takes an actual dedicated button press (RB) instead of hitting the ollie button while holding up.The only saving grace are the accessibility options that allow you to, among other things, turn off the timers for goals. I swear, if I couldn't turn off the timers this game would be the skateboarding contemporary of Superman 64. At the end of the day, with the gameplay, I am somehow a little impressed this could be made so poorly. I know there's the reasoning that this is a bird on a board and we can't expect much from that - but it feels like the developer forgot to make the skateboarding fun.Overall, have your expectations incredibly low for this game. With its combination of horrible physics and a heaping dose of charm on top of an interesting concept - think of this like the Goat Simulator of skateboarding games. If that doesn't sound appealing to you, then it's completely understandable to pass on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited when I heard the premise of SkateBIRD, and I was familiar with and enjoyed the work of some of the people on the team behind it.  My excitement was a little muted by some of the early reviews of the game, and ultimately I think that much of the criticism I've seen is fair, but there's still a good chunk of fun to be had here.  This is a positive review, but I'm going to break down both the strengths and weaknesses to help you decide if you want to pull the trigger yourself..  And parrots, chickadees,  cockatoos, and conures.  I imagine about a hundred other reviewers have already made this joke.  You are a bird, on a skateboard.  There are five small-to-mid-sized themed areas in the game that you can roam freely, including a bedroom, an office, and a rooftop.  Each area has several hidden collectibles which open up new music and character customization options, and is populated by local bird denizens who offer quests.  Quests all require you to show off your skateboard skills in a variety of ways, usually by racking up points, reaching various locations, collecting scattered objects, or executing certain tricks, all within a time limit.  There are about 20 quests per area, with ~6-7 of them being designated as "story quests" which are required to unlock the next area, while the others are just for fun.  You have to keep in mind that this game is made by a very small dedicated team, and not a giant company.  SkateBIRD is considerably more causal than TPHS.  There's no "career" mode, no cash system, no tweakable stats or progression, and no competition levels.   The skateboarding is much floatier, and it feels like there is overall less emphasis on combos.  A high combo absolutely increases the score, but the exact way score multiplayer works is unclear.  A "Fancy" meter also builds up as you skate, but I never worked out how to execute special moves, if any exist.  Grinds and lip tricks are also a big part of the game.  Manuals are present as well, but performing a manual in SkateBIRD instantly ends any combo you have going.  With this said, there are only a handful of missions in SkateBIRD where score matters at all, and the majority of them are quite easy.  The character customization system lets you select from a large number of birds that you can deck out with tons of fun cosmetic items - if you want to be a sparrow with a pirate hat, steampunk goggles, a fashionable belt, superhero cape, and a bee stinger attached to its behind, SkateBIRD has you covered.  There's loads of music in the game as well, by real artists.  There's a track selection in the menu where you can add or remove songs to your regular playlist, and even direct links to artist websites in-game.  There's so much music in the game you may finish the game without having heard all of it.  Finally, each time you start a quest in SkateBIRD, there's a fun little dialogue exchange that introduces it - these little scenes really are what kept me playing, because I wanted to see the next one. - Overall things are pretty smooth, but there's some texture clipping in places, certain bits of level geometry may trip you up unexpectedly, and momentum and collision in the game can work in funny ways.  There's a few bits in the levels where navigation is somewhat of a nuisance, like the steam vent and magazine halfpipes in level 4.  There's a few missions that whatever reason do not reset your location when you select the restart option.  None of this really detracted from my enjoyment of the game, but it is present..  I was able to complete all of the game's quests and locate all of the hidden items in 3 sittings of about ~2.5 hours each.  Part of this is because about 65% of the quests are easy enough where they can be nailed on the first attempt with over a full minute to spare. I would say another 20% of the quests in the game I was able to do comfortably on the second or third attempt, and about 5% of the quests were on this weird difficulty spike that took me a good number of retries to finally get.  Fortunately, if you are having trouble, robust accessibility options can make things easier in a variety of ways - I really appreciated this.  Overall, the game wraps itself up before getting too hard or dragging on too long, and it's worth picking up if it's the type of thing you are in the mood for.

_childDocuments_.review: You're a bird on a skateboard riding around finding other birds to talk to. They give you missions via humorous and whimsical text-based dialogue as the only voice acting here are bird chirps. The NPC birds have personalities (there's one obsessed with snacks, another who likes to set things on fire, etc), some re-occurring between multiple levels, making you feel like part of a team trying to accomplish something, as opposed to a lone skater wrecking havoc.The level design is mostly basic, taking the form of typical human environments bastardised as skate parks.I used to play a lot of THPS 2 & 3 a very long time ago and in those games I remember the controls being: flip trick is button 'c', grind is 'v' and grab is 'b', as well as movement being the arrow keys, so I didn't need to use the mouse at all besides menus. I used those controls for SkateBird and I got through the whole game with those but it never felt as crisp as those games before. There was quite a bit of struggle involved in dealing with the controls and camera. Things like when you ride off a ledge the bird and skateboard will just tumble to the side, making it near impossible to land wheels first, when you ollie once the bird will jerk backwards wanting to have the skateboard land on the backside, and when the camera is facing forward, and you push forward, the camera immediately turns 180 and you end up going backwards.With those shortcomings, all the missions are still doable, you can still string long combos, and the game is really enjoyable. The story was silly and cool in the right way that made things fun and made me want to finish each mission to see the next joke and story bit. Nice soundtrack as well.

_childDocuments_.review: SkateBIRD is an incredibly chill skateboarding game. Its complexity is along the lines of the Tony Hawk's series. But most importantly, it's a relaxing game that just emanates good vibes.You play as a bird on an adventure to try and make their "Big Friend" feel better. The story is cute, and gives you motivation through funny and short conversations that you get from quest givers. I found them all really cute.The gameplay itself is relatively simple. At the press of one button, you will do a flip. Depending on what direction you are holding, your bird might perform a kickflip, or a pop shuvit. The same goes for grab tricks. If you press the grind button when on an edge, you will initiate a grind, and in typical skating game fashion, be prompted with a balance meter that you need to try keep in the middle.The same goes for balancing on a ramp lip, or doing a manual.Finally, if you're interested in experimenting, you can set down spawn markers if you'd like to teleport back to a specific spot.Doing tricks does have a unique importance in this game, as they will increase your "fancy" meter. Which allows you to make higher jumps off of ramps, so you can navigate more easily.There are a few maps to be unlocked through story progression, each with their own theme and quirks to experience. Although you can freely skate around, sandbox style, there are NPCs scattered around that give you short missions to complete, like performing a specific series of tricks, reaching a high score, or collecting a certain amount of items. These quests give you a bit of direction, help you learn your way around the map, and move the story forward in a natural way.You can find collectibles throughout each skatepark, and I loved hunting for them.They're not that hard to find, but they do unlock new songs to listen to, as well as customization for your character.Which brings me to the best part of the game: customizing your birb. At any point, you can change your species, and pop on a variety of hats, belts, glasses and more, on your cute, feathered friend.The soundtrack contains a variety of genres, ranging from punk rock to low-fi. You can customize your playlist to match your mood. I enjoyed most of what I heard.Overall, the game is just adorable! I found it to be really relaxing too. It might not feel as weighty and good as some other skating games, but I believe that its cutesy aesthetic and vibe is the biggest selling point for most people.To address some of the negative reviews I've seen, I have never had an issue with clipping or getting stuck. The controls are responsive and worked for me 100% of the time. The camera felt a bit awkward for me in the first 10 seconds, before I realised it was inverted by default, and changed it in the options. Other than that, I can not mirror the complaints about control. However, I do recognise that learning the game can be a bit rough if you haven't played many other skating games. It will take some time, but you will get the hang of it! I highly recommend checking the controls in pause menu instead of relying on finding the tutorials throughout the campaign.I haven't beaten the game yet, and will update my review accordingly when I do, but from what I've played so far, I recommend it if some casual and cute skating sounds up your alley!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Not Tony Hawk. Just good, simple game for skateboarding newbiesIf you're looking for something that's as technical, varied, and replayable as the Tony Hawk games, you're going to be disappointedIf you're looking to buy a game that'll take you a while to 100%, you're going to be disappointedIf you're looking for a game with tons of maps, tricks, music, secrets, and more, look elsewhere.If you don't care about all that and want a game that is simple, enjoyable, an introduction to the skateboarding games, has fun early 2000's skating music, and has charming humor... _childDocuments_.review: The gameplay feels quite floaty and I swear I've had so many times where a half pipe would somehow made me crash with something, because my bird would not align to fall back into the half pipe, but instead to land on the floor which would ruin my tricks. There's also details like Manuals and Grinds having a vertical gauge both, instead of Grinds having it horizontally, the fact the game doesn't seem to know what momentum is since you build speed by filling a "fancy" meter, and then your speed just stays the same until you lose said meter. The reason I'm not recommending it is cause I feel it's more of a goat simulator than a skating game, you're there basically for the adventure and the sillyness, not the crazy tricks and acrobatics; it's fine to chill and have a good time, just... not my thing.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of skateboarding and skateboarding games like Tony Hawk and Skate, I was very excited for this game. Prior to the games release, I read the average reviews but still decided to buy the game because its a game about skating birds, whats not to love? I launch it and within the five minutes of playing, one word came to mind: This game is not bad, its just very rough and needs some proverbial sticky tape in the form of updates and patches. This is a list of some of the issues I've dealt with that I hope to be addressed in the future:- Attempting to grind when at the top of a ramp. In Tony Hawk, the difference between a stall and a grind is easy to distinguish in gameplay and was never (if rarely) an issue. In this game, you have to be at quite a descent angle to grind, otherwise you will perform a stall which completely halts your momentum. - Fancy meter straight up does not work. I can do 720 melon grab and the bar barely goes up. I ride up the wall and do a 180 that doesn't even register, the bar goes up half way. I'm not sure where the consistency is here, you would think the more fancy moves you do, the higher and faster the bar goes up, just like in Tony Hawk, but it appears to be the opposite at the moment. - Grinding a rail and at the top and attempting to transfer to another rail (like a telephone line) will sometimes have you fall off the board and just have the bird spin until you fall to the ground. Usually the second Ollie would help you recover, but this acts as a bail. - Turning around too quick may make you fall off your board. - Ollieing off rails to get to another area is wildly inconsistent. As an example, getting up the highest ramp to the corner area in the first level was much harder than it should have been. - Holding the A button on Controller in order to move will sometimes cause to to Ollie, even though my finger never lifted off the A button. - Going up a ramp and attempting to do a grab or flip trick will sometimes cause you to do which i would best call a half transfer, so instead of going up and down, you will go up and your character will tip horizontally and land straight rather than vertically. This sometimes happened in Tony Hawk but you could tell why it happened, usually because you push the left stick forward. In this game, it will do it regardless of if your holding the stick forward or not on an inconsistent basis. - You bail so easily. Hit a wall? Bail. Hit a corner? Bail. Hit 1 pixel off the ramp entry? Bail. The bird should not be this fragile. - You get stuck in walls very easily and either have to reset by pressing up on D-Pad or furiously pressing all the buttons until you bail.- Going up ramps straight on will sometimes have you veer left and right and cause you to fall.- Distant and even close up objects can be quite blurry, making it hard to find your next mission at times. I would say those are the biggest issues I'm facing with this game. Outside of that which can be fixed, the game itself is very average. It follows the THPS 4 structure of finding other birds and doing missions for them, whether that's grind 3 soup bowls or get a certain score and more. I've only beaten the first level so far but the originality of the quests is disappointing and I doubt it will get better (I'll update the review if later stages show more variety). The missions them selves also just feel like marking things of a checklist rather than the zany fun of Tony Hawk games. The two levels i played so far ranged from interesting to bland. The first level is a bed room and is quite original with pizza boxes being used as ramps, pencils creating grind rails, magazines creating ramps and more. I liked the look of the level, but it doesn't flow as nice as a skateboarding game level should, rather its 2 or 3 segmented areas put into one level. The second level, the roof, loses any originality the levels had going for them. its just two building roof tops with some fans that allow you to transfer between them easier. The colours are a dull grey and white with a slight spark of blue coming from a broken wire. To give a positive to this game, the music is pretty good, with a mix of early 2000's inspired rock music to what I will describe as Lo-Fi documentary music. You can also collect more in the form collectible mix tapes.While I ultimately recommend this game, i would say either wait until more patches are released and or play if you like skating games enough to look past this glaring issues. I'm resisting the urge to refund because the developer has shown they are listening to the criticisms and rather than just releasing the game and saying "that's it", they are working towards fixing the the issues, which I appreciate. When it works, it is quite a fun and charming game with lots of customisable options for your bird of choice with lots of delightful bird friends to speak to and a dedicated 'screm' button. I just only wish it was more consistent.

_childDocuments_.review: I am bad at games, and don't mind failing and trying things over and over again. So, to get this right out of the way, the camera is bad. However, there are a few settings for it and it can be pretty good at times. As for maneuverability,  there are a LOT of options in the menu that you will need to mess around with. Also, this game doesn't have a real tutorial, so you will be reading the handbook over and over. But, I think its worth the charm at this point. I think this game is meant to be a bit hard at first. But, in the first 10 minutes I went from basing into walls to pulling off a few tricks and being able to navigate pretty well. _childDocuments_.review: The aesthetics and story are good, however the skating ruins it for me. Skating doesn't feel good and is very lack luster. Doing tricks isn't fun because there no variety. Sometimes the bird feels as weighty as a cotton ball, other times as heavy as a boulder. Skating just feels like an annoying slog. Like the skating is part of the obstacle rather than your only mode of interaction. The story and aesthetics are the best parts of the SkateBIRD, but there are plenty of other games with interesting stories/aesthetics that have better gameplay. If you want SkateBIRD's specific story and aesthetics, Youtube videos let you engage with those aspects without purchasing the game. And if you're looking for a skating game, I recommend checking out other skating games on steam or emulating an old Tony Hawk game. I don't think SkateBIRD is a bad game, but I personally don't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Skate like you are Tony Hawk, except a tiny hawk. That's basically it. A good clean skating game with pretty crisp controls and everything you want: manuals, lip tricks, grinds, ollies, you know. Also a dedicated screaming button, so you got that going for you, which is nice. Groove.(I did kickstart this, and have a lot of hours in the demo.)

_childDocuments_.review: SkateBird's physics might be a bit wonky, and, by virtue of the player character being a bird, might be hard to control at times, but its lax conditions for victory go a large way in countering those frustrations. I'm not experienced with skating games in the slightest, but as the missions in the first level helped tutorialise me, I slowly but confidently found my footing. Perhaps it's because I don't have experience with other skating games that SkateBird's occasional jankiness never threw me off the deep end? Maybe, aided by not having played a Tony Hawk game to compare it to, I'm able to see less frustration in SkateBird's controls than people who have?Asides from gameplay, the game's quite charming, and whilst dialogue so far hasn't been "laugh out loud" funny, it's given me a silent, sensible chuckle more than once. The story of birds coming together to help their friend, whose life seems to be full of stress, overwork, and ennui, is very wholesome. There may be some clipping with the graphics, but with it being an indie game, I didn't expect AAA graphics going in. On the visual side, I do concur that it would be helpful to have a rotation option when customising your bird so as to see the back, and to be able to view the board without needing to pull a trick so as to have the bottom facing you.While I haven't  any other skating games, I have watched a friend play through a lot of the Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 + 2 remake — and if the music within that game is any indication of good music to skate to, SkateBird will deliver well for you. It's very appreciated that from the music page, you can get linked to different bands' pages to support them directly, as Steam policy doesn't allow mention of them in the game page (boo).I've enjoyed what I've played of SkateBird so far, and I'd recommend it, particularly if you're new or inexperienced with skating games. However, if you do have experience with other titles, I'd say you can still have fun with it, so long as you leave your expectations for it to be the same as those titles (particularly ones with AAA budgets and development cycles) at the door.
_childDocuments_.name: SkateBIRD

_childDocuments_.review: Pros and cons in no particular order:+ Soundtrack is very good, with unlockable licensed music that makes you feel like you're playing THPS again at its best+ The visual aesthetic pairs really well with the music for the most part, some attention to detail too. Your bird will bop to the soundtrack, etc.+ When the setting is right, it feels good to play. It's got most of the fluid THPS mechanics with minor alterations.+ The way they do combos is good too. You have a combo bar that you have to keep filling by doing original moves, so you're not doing manuals all the time to get around.+ Being able to ollie a second time in the air and being generally floatier as consequence of being a bird is a cool idea.- I don't really like the writing. I was kind of confused when they decided to give the birds dialogue in the first place. It all seems totally out of place when you put it up against the tone that the rest of the game sets up. You're the only character that actually rides a skateboard, and everyone's lines are desperate and constant attempts to be funny le'random. When I saw the story was about a guy who doesn't have time to skateboard anymore unlike his pet birds, I expected a narrative about growing up and dealing with your friends changing, but  and that's it. Really breaks the aesthetic and it stops feeling like a skateboarding game.- Some of the levels (especially the first and last levels) feature some aggressive geometry that isn't conducive to the game mechanics. A level in THPS is laid out in a certain way so that you can interact with most everything while keeping the setting believable. In this game, you have halfpipes adjacent to ungrindable slopes or awkwardly-sized and bumpy terrain adjacent to tight spaces that will force you to bail repeatedly if you run into them. It seems as if many assets were stuck into levels without considering their hostility towards your movement scheme.- Maybe this is a bug, but jumping out of a manual seems to stop combos cold a lot. I don't know why that would happen.- The speed boost you get from filling the special meter is pretty much necessary to navigate the map, and for some reason the fastest way to fill it is to slalom along a slope / go down ramps (as opposed to doing tricks, which fills the meter little or sometimes not at all). This makes filling it seem like a chore you just have to do after you bail.The negatives are pretty unimportant, and the game actually feels good when you're in the zone or trying to wind down, so I give blue thumb up. Good game
_childDocuments_.name: SkateBIRD

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an absolute beginner when it comes to skateboarding games, so my frustration tolerance for the gameplay itself is likely fairly low, but the game as a whole just feels unpolished. The visuals look outdated and the gameplay is clunky. The fact that it's an indie game is somewhat of an excuse, but sadly this doesn't improve the quality.Visuals: SkateBIRD sadly doesn't look like a game released in 2021, which includes the birds. There are 20 or so species to choose from, but most of them are reskins of a small number of models, and the models themselves are just okay.Same for the animations, which are limited. If you fall off your skateboard, the bird stiffly rolls over the floor without moving except for flapping its wings (which have no collision and clip through the floor) until you press the reset button. I was expecting a ragdoll or some falling animation, so this was a bit disappointing. When you're creating your bird and choose the paint job for the skateboard, the bird's feet also clip through the board quite visibly.I also want to quickly mention the UI. It doesn't really impact the game of course, but it added to the overall impression of low quality. Pop-ups that can't be clicked away, mismatched fonts, and the menu navigation was confusing.Gameplay: I can't really draw a comparison to other skateboarding games since I've barely played any, but for me as a beginner it wasn't very entertaining. There's no tutorial, I got a tool tip on how to do an ollie, after that I was pretty much on my own. Tried to do a quest where I had to find... something, somewhere. Aimlessly traversed the room, unsuccessfully tried to do some tricks, ran out of time, and didn't see a reason to try again.
_childDocuments_.name: SkateBIRD

_childDocuments_.review: A charmingly cute game, there's so much here to like. You're a little birb of your choice on a skateboard, going on an adventure spanning five maps to help 'big friend' find happiness despite his awful job. You'll be doing missions ala the old thps games for various birbs each with their own personality quirk, and sometimes these missions will lead to a slight change in the environment.That said, you should know what you're getting into before grabbing this. While it may be reminiscent of the old thps games, this is nowhere close to the level design, tight controls, or general fluidity those games. The levels don't have long, complex combo chains to grind through. Missions are basic and the most complex they ever get is go to marked place and do x tricks, with the most challenging being high score/combo missions, but I found those difficult more due to the way combos work in this game.Combos don't end when you stop stringing tricks together. I assume because there isn't a revert mechanic, combos instead end when a timer runs out, that you can refresh by doing more tricks. The more tricks you do, the bigger your score multiplier gets, but tricks have diminishing return point values, so the best tactic I found was spamming flip tricks then holding out an extended grab trick, lip trick, grind or manual once the multiplier was high enough.So while it isn't quite the same experience, at $20 and with how charming the birbs and their writing is, this game was enough to scratch that skateboarding game itch I've been having for some time.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like birds? Too bad. As everyone knows, birds aren't real - at least they aren't anymore. This is the next best thing.Back before birds went extinct and were replaced by government androids, they used to skateboard non-stop. This game is a glorious historical re-enactment of the glory days where you could see real birds grinding tech decks in nature. _childDocuments_.review: Consider this the mildest "yes" ever - a 5.5/10. At it's best ,this is a new THPS game that didn't sell out to the EPIC money bin.At it's worst it's a deeply frustrating game that feels *like* THPS, but falls apart at the edges.  Random geometry that trips you, then 2-4 respawns directly on top of that same geometry.  Parallel grindable objects that are nigh-impossible to transfer between.  Obtuse mechanics for speed and how high you ollie off of a given half pipe.  Unpredictable This game needs another dedicated polish pass to realize it's potential.

_childDocuments_.review: SkateBird is everything it promises to be and nothing more. It's a great, chill time. Customization, good music, easy to pickup but nuanced skating mechanics/controls, a story mode with a solid mix of a good message but good humor - what more could you ask for for $20?Edit: After reading some of the other reviews I'd be remiss to not mention some of the jank around getting stuck on s*** - I've been stuck in corners after bailing or crashing, or hit some b.s. after attempting a trick but you know what you either roll your a** out of there while you're on the ground and "screm"-ing or you press jump (while also "screm"-ing naturally) until you get out and it's all fine because Skate Birds try their best. People who are complaining about that stuff are taking this game way too seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Skatebird is a fun little skating game that follows a group of birds on a silly adventure to help their Big Friend (Owner). The dialog is cute/funny as you use your skateboard (and bird logic) to solve all the missions of each level. There is a large quantity of collectibles to be gathered to customize your bird, board, and mixtape throughout your adventure. This game would have benefited greatly if it had a photo mode. This is not Tony Hawk Pro Skater. The controls plays like an actual bird on skateboard: kinda cumbersome and not very good, but will eventually smooth out as you learn to master your board and set of wings. I'm glad I picked this up. If you are looking for a casual skating game, give this one a go. Best picked up during a sale.Great on Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: I've heard of this game years ago but held off on getting it because it seemed nice to look at but not much else.My recent obsession with birds (Although I'm more of a chicken guy) made me pull the trigger, and I can't say i regretted it. Skatebird is a simple, understated skateboarding game that's mainly about stringing together tricks and completing busy work objectives to progress the story and overall progression. It's a nice game to play on and off, and I find myself playing this pretty often with my Steam Deck rather than at my PC, and my only complaint is that the game's cloud saves don't seem to work cross platform, and the busy work objectives are an overall drag for the pace of the game, but that's not an opinion i hold with much confidence. I would've just liked a faster overall rate of progression, really.Zany bird mechanics and story and stuff aside, the game boasts a pretty surprising selection of songs outside of the OST, with unique little bands that aren't my thing, but I think others would enjoy them if they were interested in ska or punk rock. You'd have to obtain cassette records to be able to listen to the bands' music, which is then unlocked as background music that can be disabled via a menu if you don't like them, which I appreciate.Anyway, skatebird Is overall a great pick-up-and-play game that'll keep you busy if you like skateboarding games and/or birds. Even if you don't, it's a good entry point for the former, especially in the wake of other titles like Session or SkaterXL.

_childDocuments_.review: While this isn't a BAD game, with the overly positive score i need to bring some negativity.Every time I stopped playing this game was because the controls got on my nerves - as often you'll randomly fall of or be unable to control speed and in the case of the damn micowave mixtape and manual-ing up a hill it is that damn difficult to control.If you have no intent of ever getting all achievements and just wanna chill with birds on skateboards? Sure, have fun. If yolu're like me who is determined to 100% every game? Save yourself the headache.
_childDocuments_.name: SkateBIRD

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I supported this game on Kickstarter back when.Some (hopefully easily) fixable bugs and wonky parts aside, Skatebird is exactly what I was hoping for - An extremely cute little skating game full of birbs and a ton of style. Sometimes the camera is a bit counterproductive, but other than that, getting into the game is very easy and the controls are pretty intuitive. I'm awful at skating games, always have been, but the tutorial is decent and the accessibility options help out if executing tricks with all the buttons is too strenuous, so even newbies and people with disabilities can safely give this a shot. The graphics are absolutely adorable and there are a ton of customization options, so chances are high your favorite bird is in there (though I am hoping for a shoebill DLC) - And you can wear adorable hats! Shoutout also to the very funky and lovely soundtrack, I love grooving to it even while fumbling a trick for the tenth time. There are more tracks to unlock, too.All in all, I have no major complaints - Skatebird is the game I really hoped it would be, and I can only hope it sees the success I think it deserves.PS: There is a dedicated "screm" button, and it is indeed a valid way to extend your combo.
_childDocuments_.name: SkateBIRD

_childDocuments_.review: Is it the best skateboarding game? Nah. Is it an adorable skating game? Absolutely. Cute and charming narrative, silly characters, funny bird jokes, I can screm, I can dress up my birb with little hats and things. The grinding is a little wonky and I definitely had my fair share of frustration, but overall the charm made up for it. Also, you can pet the birb!
_childDocuments_.name: SkateBIRD

_childDocuments_.review: Haven gotten every deck, board, mixtape, and done every mission in the game I can say that it is a really nice game to play. Without spoiling anything, I will state that there are a couple missions where it is rather difficult to do without any exploits or just because of how the game handles grinding as well as jumps. Some of the things you'd need to do in order to get certain missions and items are very specific and irritating. Thankfully, none of the missions nor items I have mentioned are key to actually beating the game, only to 100% it. That being said, I will state that I have been playing this only on keyboard and mouse (though, I'd recommend just using the keyboard as I have found it much easier than just using the mouse) My main complaint is that (at the time of this review) there isn't a way to change the button layout on the keyboard. Primarily where the reset button is. The game defaults the olly botton as E, the reset button as R, and the transfer button as T. Both ollies AND transfers are key throughout the whole game so having a button that just resets you to your last checkpoint in between these two button's makes it annoying.The music is amazing and I love all of the soundtracks, It honestly made me feel like I was back to playing those old Tony hawk pro skater games just grinding away and getting a huge combo!The story I had also found to be charming and amusing. I loved the characters, even the one's we don't talk to a lot, especially with how they all had their own personalities! I would honestly get this game for the story alone because of how much I enjoyed it. However, I will say that if you don't like the characters nor the story itself then this game just might not be for you.Overall, I wish there was more levels and missions to warrant the $20. Maybe a level editor where we could share with others or more tricks we could do as birds would warrant the $20. I hope in the future that there will be DLC for this game because above all I throughout enjoyed this game and will honestly play some more in my spare time just for how chill everything is alone! :)Just because numbers are lovely and people like them my number rating would have to be 7.5/10.TL:DR              Some issues with core mechanics that will most likely be patched as the game gets older but overall an amazing game. I would recommend this 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: My name is BirdFacts®, and I approve of this game. That said, I definitely have a little bias reviewing this game, as I love the concept of a skateboard game where you play as a bird. I've also never played any other skateboard games before, so that also factors into my opinion.While this game is certainly a little rough around the edges, I still had a lot of fun with it. The character model and the customization to go with it is wonderful, as you get to be a bird. The original soundtrack creates a perfect vibe while playing, while including other more "skater" music, that I personally disabled in favor of keeping just the original sountrack on. The dialogue for quests is charming, the parks have a consistent style, and are well decorated with objects to enhance your skating experience. I've seen a lot of reviews complaining about controls, both them being janky and the game not explaining them that well. For my first maybe hour of playing the game, I could agree. But the more I played, the more I understood the controls, got the hang of them, and started to enjoy myself a lot more. The tutorials are a bit hidden, as you have to do quests in the first area, then hit pause to read the tutorial about the trick you need to do for that quest. The physics can still feel a little weird from time to time, and every once in a while I'll find my bird in likely unintentional places or traveling in unintentional ways, but for the large part I'm enjoying myself, doing some sick tricks, and racking up those huge combos.I'm excited to see the updates the game receives in the future. The developers seem passionate and responsive, so I'm sure it will only become more fun as time goes on. Big things I'd like to see are more parks, some large extra modes or minigames to increase replay value, and while I imagine it'd be quite the undertaking for a small team, I'd love a multiplayer feature. TL;DR Great concept with charming atmosphere, but a little rough around the edges. If you're willing to put in a bit of time to learn to get past a bit of jank, you'll have a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: SkateBIRD

_childDocuments_.review: After roughly two hours I feel like I can finally give my full review:The good bits:- The birbs are good, I love a good birb.- The dialog and references are pretty okay and enjoyable.The bad bits:- The game is extremely buggy. You will get stuck in terrain. You will bail for no reason.- The camera is awful.- The controls are awful.TLDR/SummaryOverall the game almost makes up for the lacklustre controls and repetitiveness with the cute dialog and design, but unfortunately a flurry of other issue bring the game down overall. With countless bug fixes, a camera overhaul and potentially improved hitboxes, this game could be a masterpiece, but until then it is unfortunately a series of repeated missions, buggy tricks, broken cosmetics, and a very repetitive soundtrack that tried too hard to be The Offspring.

_childDocuments_.review: If you go into this expecting a game that feels like Tony Hawk's Pro Skater, you will be disappointed.The controls are very float-y and unresponsive. Tightening up the turn radius in the settings helped a lot, and the double jump is very forgiving. There's also a setting to turn off the timer for missions, if you find that you need a few extra seconds to complete one of many fetch quests. An arrow to guide you to mission objectives, and a world map that shows the available missions are a couple other good quality-of-life features to make moving through the game a bit easier.It's a fun game, and from the first hour that I played, you can tell the developer put care into making the game's progression smooth. But i think more polish and tighter controls could have made a huge difference. Very nostalgic to be back on a board, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there were "Warning" review tags instead of just a recommend or not. Anyways, this is not a review that is necessarily positive or negative. -I loved the general vibe of the game, it's very laid back and the OST is enjoyable-I loved all of the character customization that it gives you right out of the gate.-I loved being a skateboarding bird, there aren't enough devs out there that take chances to do something different or weird; so for that reason I have really enjoyed my short time with it thus far. -That being said, the controls are VERY stiff and gaining speed is much more of a chore than literally any other skateboarding game I've played. The game also doesn't do a great job of making you feel like you are gaining any significant amount of speed. A satisfying sense of locomotion just isn't quite there.  -The angles at which you need to approach a grind on a half/quarter pipe are stricter than I would have expected. I more often than not ended up doing a stall trick. -Compared to the OST, the licensed songs are a real drag. They follow the skate punk genera, but they are NOT good songs. I get that not everybody can afford top tier songs like Tony Hawk can. But with an OST that's as good as this is, it's really kind of a bummer that the licensed songs are as bad as they are. So all in all, I think the bones of the game are really good, but I think it needs some tweaking to the locomotion, the camera/control stiffness, and the removal/replacement of some of these god awful licensed songs (maybe get more original songs, I hate having to skip 1/3rd of the sound track because the developers wanted to put some edgy ♥♥♥♥♥♥ skate punk in) I will gladly change my review to positive if the devs can make some of these changes (most importantly the sense of locomotion and camera/control stiffness)

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot going for it:Customisation - GreatMusic - Pretty GoodCharacters and Humor - GreatPlot - Silly and FunThe issues that see 72% of the players drop off before the 2nd level and 92% by the 4th are:1. {{Edit}} The camera's default setting suck, it starts with a narrow FOV zoomed in too close and has background blur turned on but, I assume these are hardware accessibility options but it's odd they are default, you can undo all this in settings and the camera is mostly fine.2. Your momentum is all over the place - You can't wallplant or shove, if you run into a wall that's it, prepare to mash your self up against it because it's a legitimate challenge to stop, I feel like half the time I am skating and half the time I am fighting with the game to stop pushing me forward. The quick recovery just compounds on this because I just respawn and get mashed into the same wall again. 2.5 The game is always moving you forward, you can stop but redirecting feels awful and half the time it just pushes you forward against your will anyway. Austin Powers doing a 100 point turn in that tight hallway is a smooth ride by comparison to you trying to just turn around as the game keeps mashing you into the wall you are stuck in3. Controls are too floaty - Sometimes I go over a small bump and it's fine, I go over another one and suddenly I flip upside down, there seems to be no logic to it.4. Inconsistent physics - So I noticed in a few areas like the sparking wire in lvl 2. Sometimes it's easy to grind and other times you just float straight through it as if it's hitbox is 1 pixel or something. Again on level 2, that rail connecting the roofs for the photobomb mission. I tried to jump off the ledge onto the wire but because I was within a certain distance of the ledge it just flipped me 90 degrees, killed my momentum and faced me toward the ramp underneath as if I had pressed switch5. {{Edit}} Grinding and stalling can be a pain - If you are directing yourself forward, that input will immediately register on the balance meter and you will bail so many times by accident which just feels awful in a game where you fall over a lot already due to it's floatiness. The devs pointed out Deadzone options in the settings which do help but I don't know why I have to go to setting to fix such a basic problem, I mean at least the settings are there but why would you want the scuffed default ones?6. The FANCY system - Skating in a wavy line along the bottom of a ramp gathers speed but going up a ramp, getting 7ft of air and coming back down again gathers none. If you want speed you need to stop skating and engage in this arbitrary system. Also if you are going too fast, you can stop but the second you move again, boom, max speed because your FANCY meter is doesn't fade, you HAVE TO BAIL in order to slow down which involves completely resetting your speed from 0.  Just get rid of the FANCY system, it sucks ass7. Base jump height- It's too low. If you reset and have no momentum, your jump height will be an inch shy of the rails and you will just bail.I like cutesy games, I am an avid bird watcher, I have a flock of birds I feed twice daily, I also have a real soft spot for skating games, I am probably the most key demo the game is looking for, it should not have me putting it back on the shelf within 2 hours. I think most of this games problems with controls comes from how floaty it is and  the fact it's always pushing you forward, I hope it gets better because I'd like to keep playing but I won't fight with the controls to do it*TLDR:* Controls are absolute , unfiltered ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, you will spend more time falling over for no reason than actually skating, it completely ruins what I can tell is a good game but it is buried under these terrible controls which are only made worse by it's floatiness. You can play around with the options to make it a lot less frustrating but the fact you need to at all shows a clear lack of polish
