_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I have yet to try the patch out, but seeing that they put one out so quickly makes me much more hopeful for this games future. Additionally, once you manage to get past the first ~4 missions, it is a pretty fun and very cute game. I'm really looking forward to trying it out with the patch.----------------------------------------------------I REALLY, REALLY, REALLY want to like this game. I've been super excited for its release, and was THRILLED when I saw it was out! But I'm pretty disappointed so far. The character select is adorable and I love it so much. But the game itself is incredibly frustrating. Every time you crash into something, the camera gets stuck when you get back on the board so you can't easily turn away from what you just crashed into. This and other issues make it WAY too difficult to complete the first few missions because you spend so much time trying to work around the awkward controls and camera bugs. The first missions at least should be easier. I can't get into it when I can't accomplish anything from the very start. I really hope the developers will do something about this. My suggestions: 1. Fix the camera problem when you crash into something. It makes it impossible to know which way to turn when you first get back on the board, so you just waste time and crash again.2. Increase the time limit on the first few missions. People can't enjoy a game where they can't accomplish anything at the very beginning.3. I also might consider changing the jump/ollie mechanic so you jump when you click instead of when you let go. The current control isn't intuitive and makes everything way more frustrating.Again, I am really hopeful that some of these issues can be fixed and that it can become a really enjoyable game in the future! I would LOVE to share this game with my friends who love birds once some issues are worked out. I just can't recommend it in its current state :(

_childDocuments_.review: Updating my review (original below for context) as v1.02 seems to have fixed the issues I had, specifically the resolution which now updates in real time and persists, but more importantly the handling seems to have been tweaked and now it just feels right! THIS is the game I was expecting and really pleased to see the dev active on the reviews etc. The revised handling has made this much more fun to play and now I am happy to recommend it!Original review for context:-The look is utterly charming, LOVE the character models. The parks look nice, but the textures could be a little more detailed - what is there looks ok.I backed on Kickstarter as I liked the concept and wanted to support the dev. Given the overall quirky vibe (it's birds, skating, after all) I kind of imagined it would be a little more accessible. My first impressions of the game (and gameplay) are not super positive, but there is scope for improving it.For instance, I cannot change the resolution in the options, as there does not appear to be an apply button and when you leave that screen it resets back to the default res. Having given up trying I decided to jump into the game.LOVE the character designer, the models are super charming - if a little low-res - but the amount of customisation you can do is impressive. What would be great is if you could rotate the character as you customise them because at the moment you cannot see any of the items that go on the back. Also when changing the board itself, this does not update on the character screen meaning you need a bit of trial and error, so again I gave up and left the default set.Once I eventually got into the game (after exiting by mistake and accidentally randomising my character (maybe a confirmation screen would be helpful here?)) you are kind of chucked into the deepend. Not being a great skater myself, I was not sure what all the tricks or names mean, and the game doesn't do a great job of explaining them - not an issue if you are into skateboarding, I am sure, but defo could use a little more explanation/tutorial. I wasn't sure if there is a structure or whether it is sandbox.The camera also struggles with the geometry at times. On the first park there is an overhang, if you skate up this (so you are directly under it) it completely obscures your bird so you cannot see what you are doing.The points above can be resolved with patches (this is v1 after all), but unless you are in to skating and (or birds?) I cannot recommend at the moment. I will keep an eye out for future updates and will happily amend my review if these are addressed.Finally, also a bit disappointed that having backed on Kickstarter this is available day one on Game Pass, meaning that had I not backed it I could have saved myself a few quid and still played it upon release. Oh well not going to break the bank, but it is the principle. You live and learn.TLDRGraphics: FabConcept: FabPresentation: OKGameplay: meh at the momentSummary: Not for me at the moment, but YOU may love it!

_childDocuments_.review: Borb.SkateBird can almost be carried alone by getting to play as a bird on a skateboard, and the amount of funky birds available. No noises when you perform certain moves or get high combos.While you do have birb friends asking you to do silly tricks and be true to the call for seeds, SkateBird is also missing some of the exploration that existed. _childDocuments_.review: I was extremely excited for this game, big fan of the Tony Hawk games back in the day, hundreds of hours into TH2 and Underground, and 100% the TH1+2 remake in like 2 days. Add birds to that and you have a direct line straight to my heart. Followed the kickstarter but couldn't back at the time, so I waited eagerly and bought it as soon as it was availableBut honestly, I do not recommend the game in its current state. I do not understand how the devs thought this was ready for sale. At first I was having fun, and was able to laugh at some of the janky physics and silliness. But as soon as you were supposed to be doing anything more complex than simple ollies and flip tricks...if this was labelled as "Early Access" (which at first I thought it was honestly) I could forgive it, even though early access is used as a scapegoat for badly programmed games that the developer never intends to finish. This game is not finished, don't let the full release status fool you.The graphics are decent, nothing amazing, but not ugly. It looks like a PS2 game, which I suppose is apt, but I am pretty certain that this was made in Unity, and that engine is capable of more than what we got here, Textures are a bit too low res, shaders feel flat, and lighting is static and uninspired. The models and animations (however few there are) are cute though, low poly and all (never had a problem with them). I love that grab tricks are done with the beak, and I do like that you can dress up your bird. If only the dress up menu had a confirm button, rather than the obtuse resolution of just pressing back to indicate you're done.The Ui is...fine. It's not terrible, but it's just...bland. Instantly forgettable. Which I realise isn't that big of a deal considering immersion etc., but it isn't clear what's happening sometimes. The HUD will sometimes just disappear when you exit a menu, the HUD gets completely covered up by the mission popup when you skate near it, mission objectives are tracked on the UI first to last even if you do them out of order, things like that. And the control customisation screen is...did they just leave the entire screen as the default Unity UI elements? Why???The camera is my biggest problem. I don't think I have ever seen or felt a worse camera in a video game. You *can* move it freely, but in this style of game, that's not something you should be doing other than to look around you while stopped to get you bearings. So instead it should follow you, which it does. Too well. It sticks to you so precisely that the slightest movement causes it whip around chaotically, while it tries its best not to clip through anything. Whatever you do, do not go into tight corridors, it can be a nightmare to figure out. Oh wait, the game forces you to do that in at least one mission...and these spots are seemingly everywhere.The controls are also subpar. The layout is almost identical to the Tony Hawk series, which is good because its the only good control layout other than arguably Skate (which I still personally do not like), but the are REALLY stiff and unresponsive at times, whether wireless or wired on the controller. Some of the functions that the game taught later I just straight up thought weren't in the game at first because they just do not work sometimes, such as transferring, and a lot of functions just result in crashing. Also good luck controlling whether you grind or stall on any given half/quarter pipe. Nine times out of ten I would stall when I wanted to grind. I get that it's probably trying to be more forgiving than Tony Hawk, which was a little too precise with the angle for stalling, but it feels like you need to be going at a 30° to actually grind. And lastly the presentation is lacklustre. The sounds the birds make are all budgies or similar birds, even when playing as a Galah, Cockatoo, Kookaburra, hawk, etc. There's almost no feedback for doing anything, good or bad. Some actions just feel forced and unnatural (such as transfers). Nothing feels like it has any real weight to it. The game doesn't really explain itself very well either, for example, the fancy metre, I have no idea how it fills, and sometimes it fills partially just by you moving forward after crashing...I can absolutely see where they were coming from with this, and I genuinely do hope that the controls and camera get fixed at least. But come on devs, you are clearly capable of better than this, what is good about the UI, visuals,  etc is really good, just...finish the game before you release it and add more animation.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, with caveats. It definitely fits the "cute novelty game" bill, complete with an option to "birb-ify" the character dialogue that I appreciated. You can even customize your bird and give it little hats and accessories. That said, it's still very much a skating game with a gameplay focus on mastering different tricks and maneuvers. Several of the sidequests demand a trial-and-error approach that can grow tedious and frustrating more often than not - if you want every achievement you're probably looking at over a dozen hours for full completion. This is compounded by the somewhat ungainly movement and controls, especially the grinding mechanic - without intense precision it's difficult to jump onto the wire or cable you want to grind without multiple attempts. I also wish there was a proper map system with actual waypoints and marked collectibles. Thankfully, there's an impressively generous suite of custom difficulty options (like turning off mission timers and making it easier to grind without losing balance) that generally mitigate these issues. The OST is also pretty nice, though I'm not sure if I ever warmed up to the ska punk.
_childDocuments_.name: SkateBIRD

_childDocuments_.review: The main design goal of the game has been "Classic THPS with birds as skaters and Micro Machines-esque tiny skate parks" and it mostly nails that.- Plays like classic THPS (I didn't try the recent remaster but I have played the PS1 games quite recently). There are some differences but most of them are for the better (except maybe the fancy meter mechanic, I still find that annoying – though the recent "Pet the bird" feature makes it a lot easier to fill). Yes, when you finally get to a hard-to-reach spot and then your bird decides to skate straight over the edge, it can be frustrating, but old THPS also worked exactly like that. SkateBird at least lets you set custom "reset points" so you can quickly teleport back to where you were, at least outside missions- The mission structure itself is more like THPS4 / THUG than THPS 1-3. You can freely skate around on the map to find NPCs (and collectibles), then you trigger the actual missions one by one by talking to those NPCs. They give you a small set of objectives to complete within a time limit (collect this thing, do that trick etc.), all fitting loosely within an overarching story. All missions were relatively easy to understand and the difficulty curve is also mostly OK. (There were only 2-3 missions that I struggled with.)- The levels look a bit more boring and less polished than I have hoped for (two of them are great, one is OK, and two are meh), but the theme / atmosphere is good overall- The bird related content is 10/10. There's a create-a-bird custom character creator, a dedicated buttor for screaming, double jumping with your wings and delightful dialogue and animations.The last point is quite an important bit. Your experience will largely depend on how much you are into this theme. If you are a fan of wholesome bird content, well, then this game has plenty of that, and it really does make you forgive the flaws. If you are here for "just a skateboarding game", however, then yes, this is not the best one.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like birds + I played a lot of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater. The tutorials helped me get the hang of it more, though. You learn to grind, grab, transfer and do tricks.PROS:+ The gameplay is good and feels like a Tony Hawk game (the game even making subtle nods to the Tony Hawk games, like the SKATE letters), many missions and cute birb friends to meet.+ You can screm and monch your board.+ There is a bell hat, I used to have a budgie who loved to put his head inside of a bell so that's absolutely perfect.+ Flapping your wings is like Tony Hawk with super powers, it's a cool addition to the skating.+ Creative level designCONS:- High contrast isn't actually high contrast as it's white on white text now, with a subtle black border. Ideally the text in dialogs would be completely black, with a white background.- Bird models are somewhat unique, but they don't reflect how the birds actually look. This is probably a trade-off to make balancing the gameplay more stable during development as the collision hulls for the birds now remain the same. But it results in budgies & cockatiels looking just as thick & round as any other bird.Yes, those are minor complaints, I actually really like this game. It's fun to play and filled with content for you to enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: SkateBird is a very interesting game, both in the idea and final product. A game where you play as a bird that skates around on a tiny skateboard across 5 open levels where you take missions from other birds to advance the story. Really speaks for itself, but it is at least very cute in how it's all executed. I enjoyed the game myself as someone who loves birds and likes skateboarding games in general like Tony Hawk. Though a game like this isn't near the same quality as say Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 and or 4, but I still have to give credit where credit is due, there are plenty of settings to change how you prefer to play, with adjustments on skating speed, handling, braking, etc. There are also plenty of bird skins to choose from, they even had one of a "Quaker Parrot" skin, which I own as a pet, so I how could I NOT say no to that. :3I will say that I also really liked the story, sure it was nothing grand or too thought provoking, but for an adventure based on a little domesticated house bird owned by a person who lives in an apartment, it seems to fit the bill just right as far as scope goes, lol. You also come across some colorful characters such as a business bird with a fascination for money, a bird that will do anything for snacks, a radical skater bird that might be a little bit too obsessed with tricks involving fire and many more birds you gather on your quest to reach "Big Friend" / your owner who is at work. The aesthetics for ramps, rails and hazards are creative and admirably cute; With the hub levels themselves being detailed and varied quite well, though the last level is just the first level with a different coat of paint, but to be fair this comes together nicely for the story aspect at the very least.Time to talk about the controls and gameplay, which there are both positives and negatives to this, the controls are responsive and tight with similar patterns and coding as any other 3D Skateboarding game, though with a frame rate that is a bit choppy it can be noticeably bothersome at times when you are trying to make super accurate moves during a more difficult mission. The skater bird can also suffer from some lag in certain places of the levels, but you can really start picking up speed well when your combos are high and egg gauge is full, there will hardly be any lag in that state, I guarantee it. ;)The OST / Background Music is completely original and packaged solely for this game, but it can also be purchased seperately (though I didn't get this myself, just got the game). And unfortunately I do have some slight problems with the music, now don't get me wrong, some of the tracks do sound really good, great in fact. But some of the lyrics from certain tracks can be well, to put it bluntly, Political...... One track sings about how the President is Trans-phobic, another sings about racist jokes and this may not be much of a problem if it was just the music, but there is also a quick convo you have with another bird in the game that talks about how Capitalism must fall and I don't know if that was put in for bird humor and shouldn't be taken seriously but it kind of annoyed me, which if people don't mind this, all the power to them, but I really dislike it when people force their political views into a product made solely for entertainment. Real World Problems are unavoidable, I get that, but sometimes we watch movies, play games and stream shows to avoid those aspects in our lives. As someone who hates getting involved with politics, it is a real hindrance for the game, luckily any and all tracks can be turned off / on for personnel preference during gameplay, so thankfully, this added feature really helps in the long run in my opinion as you are allowed to play and or listen only to the tracks that you may like best. :)Overall I must say that I do like the game, despite some of it's flaws, the aesthetics and ideas made for the game are very charming and pleasing to me, how could you go wrong with Birds and Skateboarding mixed into one product. I do recommend the game to those that like birds and skateboarding too, and I'd even go as far as to recommend this game to casual players, but a word of advice, if you are looking for an absolute top tier skateboarding experience you may not find it here, because as most 3D indie games, it has some of it's flaws and doesn't have the peak perfection gameplay like those made by legit gaming companies. Still I'd recommend the game nonetheless and the price of 20 dollars I think is worth it too. :DThanks for reading my review of SkateBird, I hope you have a Blessed day. ^_^

_childDocuments_.review: (8.5/10)So I went in to this knowing nothing and i was happily surprised.  I will say it was initially kind of hard for me to wrap my head around how to get started.  There are a few little interface things that probably could use some polish and tune ups, but once you have a bird, and you are skating, it is surprisingly engaging.The overall physics are a little floaty but you are a bird, on a skateboard, so they probably should be.  Speaking of that, trying to approach this game strictly like a tony hawk-a-like is going to kind of be an exercise in frustration. Yes the influence is obvious but tony hawk did not have literal wings, and did not throw screeching tantrums when he would fail to land a trick, so absolutely don't approach this game like its 'just' one of those games.Give it a little time to just slowly figure out the way this sucker flows and you will absolutely be rewarded.  That said the tutorial opening area is a little cryptic and it isn't always obvious between missions what you should actually be doing next.  Its ok though, just slowly learn how to get to the various areas in the bedroom, when you find the little tutorial birb friends, talk to them and take their missions, and learn the overall flow and layout of everything.The game gets so much more engaging when you give it just that little bit more time and learn to think outside the pipe so to speak.  Especially the 'double' jump (aka you know, flapping your wings, since you are a bird) there are so many new ways to traverse using that method and it will take you a while to get a feel for it, but it is absolutely worth taking the time to get there.  In the end, its a superbly charming little game with a silly premise, a wonderfully derpy birb maker (especially the stellar's jay, oh my god if you have never seen those guys they are absolutely the derpiest of birds in real life), and a truly new skew on the classic skateboarding formula.  To get that final piece in place it is absolutely a joy but you will have to put in some time getting used to how things go, and put up with a few little interface inconsistencies, but its charming enough, and even failing is fun/silly enough that getting there isn't too much of a tall ask really.Oh and one last thing, do try and get everywhere.  There are so many cute little hidden and fun things to find and explore that you do yourself a dis-service if you just try and jump from mission to mission.  Take the time to wander around and try and explore every little nook and cranny of each area, you'll be glad you did.

_childDocuments_.review: Other complaints about this game are kinda bad, and in some cases just flat wrong. That said, I still recommend against it, quite strongly.There ARE quite a few tricks you can do (one person said there's only one flip, one grab, one grind, which is obviously completely false the moment you turn the game on).The physics are a little annoying, but they're not that bad. The game plays fairly well, but it does feel a little floaty compared to other skater games, but maybe that's a feature because you're a bird?The controls are kinda bad, but it's not "that" bad as other people are complaining. It does play like the old THPS games we love, but manuals are really frustrating to get, and there's no reverts. You also bounce around off stuff quite a bit, so it doesn't feel right. Overall, I just didn't find it fun to play, which is obviously problematic, lol.My biggest gripe is that the missions are perfectly linear. You start with a single mission available, and you CANNOT move on until you complete it. Then you get your second, and only your second. And it goes on like this, so you MUST complete the current mission to move on. There's no options. Also, you have to find the random quest giver somewhere on the map, so you end up rolling around randomly just looking for the next one. But the fact that you can't do anything else is what's frustrating. I did like 14 missions or something, almost beating the first level (I think) and then I got to a collect stuff mission, and there was a single item I couldn't find. I played the mission three times, scouring the entire map, unable to find the last piece. So I guess I can't move on, and there's no point in playing the game? That's a terrible game design decision. Even the THPS games had it so you had to complete like 60% of the level in order to move on, or something like that. This, nope, you have to do everything, completely linearly, or else you don't get to move on, so you're stuck.Also, I only played one map, and it was bad. I realize there are other maps, but I just couldn't be bothered to continue playing. I really wanted to unlock another map to see if it was better, but the problems above prevented me. The map I did play is quite large, but super empty. Huge areas of just flat group, then objects that you can't really skate, and then random quarter pipes for some reason. Very few grindable objects, basically no real flat ramps, just quarter pipes. Nothing really works together to flow, or create runs. It honestly just feels like a large empty room with a few quarter pipes thrown around. The good part of these games is the flow you can achieve, and I don't think I had one moment of flow in the hour I played.Overall, I love the concept, and wish we had more devs making skate games. These devs also basically got the feel "almost" right, so props to them. The problem is mostly in the level design, and actual gameplay. I think if the levels had flow, were interesting, and filled with actually skateable objects you could grind, I'd probably keep the game.

While I didn't play a ton of different THPS games, I did play quite a bit of the first one on N64, and that still holds up better than this game. The wonky physics is the biggest issue. THPS games didn't have the most realistic physics, but it gave a great sense of weight and momentum while riding around and doing tricks. SkateBird just feels off, it's doesn't feel right, there's clipping issues which add to that feeling, it seems like the devs really love the THPS games but couldn't quite pin down what made them feel good, and the result is something that resembles a THPS game at it's core, but can't keep it together, and it just ends up falling flat.

That's what I was hoping it was, just decent, THPS-style fun, featuring birds.But sadly all is not as it first seems, as the negative reviews say, it's a pretty badly broken mess at the moment. The camera is an obvious concern, the devs have even said they'll be working to rewrite the entire camera system from scratch (here's to hoping they deliver). But I think there's a bigger issue here, kinda hidden behind the hazy mess that is a shaky camera and overbearing DoF; it just doesn't control well.Firstly, the physics. The controls are too physics-based. Often when you're skating around if you don't take corners wide enough, you'll clip some kind of raised corner and be sent into uncontrollable somersaults. Sure, your "air ollie" might save you from this, but not always, especially if you hit something else as a result of your altered path through the air. Even if your board lands on its wheels, there's still a chance that because you were spinning, you start skating in a direction you didn't want to go in.Second, the "Fancy" system; this game's frankly fairly underwhelming version of the THPS Special gauge. Where Special could temporarily unlock unique tricks on top of an overall speed boost, this game only gives you the speed, not even any of the UI feedback and that's when you manage to get it going which is a problem in of itself. The game tells you to cut across ramps in a shallow arc to gain Fancy but half the time it doesn't count. Other times you get a near full gauge from going straight down a big ramp, other times you don't. It's very unreliable.Third, the levels themselves. I appreciate that levels can change based on mission progress, but the changes are never big enough to really feel like progress is being made. I've only beaten the first two levels so far but from what I've seen it's mostly cosmetic. You don't get major new areas, you don't get secret zones, in fact with the first level things get more empty as you go. There's so much open space and it only gets worse as things are removed from the level. Additionally, the maps are static. There's no moving objects at all. There are fans that can yeet you but that's the best you get from what I've seen.Finally, the specific control bugs. It's quite easy to get out of bounds or to mash buttons to yeet way too far off of ramps. That's all I've found myself really, but they're still pretty glaring flaws when you know about them.I know I've been hard on the game here, but if you're reading this review in full you'll see I still gave it a thumbs up. That's because despite everything I've seen, I still enjoy what does work here. And unlike Cyberpunk, most of the game does actually function, I just took the time to go over my gripes. I just think it needs its glaring issues fixed, then some good polishing on those wheels; it doesn't have far to go to be a great little game. c:

on point, this is not the the game i thought it would be. skating is very stiff, turning radius at full tilt is rightfully very wide, but its equally wide at low speed making it damn near impossible to navigate some tighter portions of the levels. unfortunately, its also very floaty and unforgiving. i was always a big fan of the pro skater games, THUG 1+2, hell even american wasteland, every one of those games made for the PS2 outclass skatebird in every way, because they were polished experiences. tricks and combos had great variety and made you fell like an absolute master, but skatebird _childDocuments_.review: I'm starting this by getting it out of the way: This is NOT Tony Hawk. I repeat - this is NOT Tony Hawk.Other than both sharing a name related to a Bird, it is nothing like Tony Hawk. Please do not get this game if you're hoping for THPS with a bird as a character instead.I've been following this game since it was first announced and whilst I wish nothing ill on the devs - this is not a good game.I'm going to cut my review into separate categories and give my thoughts on each. I apologise if I repeat many things - I'm not used to writing reviews, but as a MASSIVE skateboard fan, I feel the need to do one for this.The Gameplay is probably the most difficult thing that I can write down because I don't even know what words to use to describe it.  It feels one part physics game, one part ... I don't even know.  As you can guess from the name of the game, you play as a Bird (or as the game likes to cutely call it, a 'birb') on a Skateboard.  Once you start the game, you're dropped straight in the middle of the bedroom - think of the Toy Story stage in Disney's Extreme Skate Adventure for scale - and limited to do one of two things; skate freely to get used to the controls, or find another Bird to speak to in order to start a mission. The game works similar to the later Tony Hawk games, think Pro Skater 4 and on wards, where you have to find characters on the field in order to start a mission. However, unlike Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4 - a game that came out 19 years ago, you cannot select the missions from a menu. This means that a lot of time will be spent mindlessly skating around in a game that has horrible controls - which I'll explain later on - trying to find a bird to give you a mission.The problem is that, due to the game's weird controls and graphics, you'll not only have a hard time getting to a bird, you'll have an even worse time *finding* the bird. Moving onto the graphics: For some reason, the game has a HEAVY. I mean, HEAVY, blur effect just a few feet in front of you which means anything in the distance is just a complete blur. Birds do not have any kind of icon above their heads, which means you HAVE to find them yourself and interact with them. I have no idea why it's like this, it just is. I may have missed it, but I could *not* find an option to toggle the awful blur effect - only an option to change the FoV which doesn't affect the blur.The graphics themselves are pretty nice - they're simple. A blend of cartoony with a hint of realism - a style I personally am extremely fond of. But that's where my compliments on them end. Do you remember when I said the game has horrible controls? it does. It really does. as I said at the beginning, this is not Tony Hawk. The only similarities are Triangle to Grind, X to Ollie, Square to Flip-trick and Circle to Grab-trick. Tricks do not work like Tony Hawk, because the game does not allow you to execute any - I don't mean that in a way such as "Oh, this game is so difficult and I can't execute a trick." I mean that there are simply no tricks to use. You can ollie, double tap Ollie to flap your wings and do an "air-ollie," Kick trick, or grab trick. You can also transfer, but since you do not gain any air going up ramps, you're not going to be able to continue your tricks. You *cannot* do combos. It's just not a thing the game supports.As for audio? The game sounds great. The soundtrack is extremely chill and despite how critical I've been with the game so far, I could see myself buying the soundtrack because of how nice it is to listen to. Birds make chirping sounds (though, only one kind which is a bit strange - Budgie sounds coming from a Raven makes no sense, but to be fair I'm not expecting the devs to go out of their way to record a raven or any other bird.)The game appeals to anyone of any age, but kids will get bored of it after a few minutes and anyone over the age of 12 will have an awful time trying to understand the controls. There's a cute little story about a bunch of birds trying to help their big friend, who I presume is the human who owns the birds, with tasks such as making their bed, but that's pretty much it - as far as I got to, anyway. I didn't feel comfortable with the idea of forcing my way through controlling my bird in this game to try and see where the story went. I doubt it went anywhere important given what kind of game it is.The difficulty is hard to explain because a majority of it comes from the awful controls - not the actual game itself. You'll accept some missions which are "grind this, collect this, collect SKATE" but good luck actually doing any of them. At one point, I had to collect S K A T E letters using a full ramp and two small ramps on the other side with one of the letters in between the two which I had to do a transfer for.   Transfers do not work in this game except for going OVER a ramp - rather than transferring from one ramp to a ramp next to it.You're not going to have a good time with this game unless you have the money to spend, laugh at the concept, mess around for a bit and then move onto something else.  The price is unjustified in it's current state.  It's not worth it unless you get it for something like £5 / €5 / $5, and even then I think that's being generous.At the end of the day: This is not Tony Hawk, It's a game that feels like was made in a month and put onto the steam store for a quick buck and I'm extremely upset that it had to end like this.Gameplay - 0Audio - 8Controls - 0

_childDocuments_.review: Really devided about Skatebird right now.First off, I'm not a skateboarding pro. I know that an ollie is when you jump, kickflip rotates the board in a specific way... I don't have the vocabulary of a skate master. When I launched the game for the first time, I got thrown words I knew nothing about, and reading about it without proper demonstration helped a little, but a real tutorial to show you the mechanics one by one would really have helped me.There  icons on the screen that show you what you can do at any given time, but they're too small by default without turning on  in the options, and most importantly it goes way too fast to know what to do and  to do it. I only rarely knew how to use the  command, for example.While reading other reviews, I see that many people found tweaks to make their own experience great through the options menu, but I find the descriptions too vague. ? ? What difference does it make when I increase these values or decrease them? Will it make my game easier, as I'm having a hard time? Will it go harsher on me?When it comes to how the game handles, I started off playing the game through Remote Play.It was not a pleasent experience. I believe input lag (as small as it is over my own Wi-Fi network) made everything terrible. Controls felt very heavy, none of my commands seemed to work, despite a crystal clear signal on my TV.I decided to give it another shot on my PC, and it did feel a lot better. I find it hard to control your speed though, and the fact that you are constantly moving makes it difficult to focus on something you wanna interact with. I don't know if this has to do with speed too, but I found myself falling on the ground at times when I thought I'd land properly, and other times I accidentally thrashed myself into obstacles, walls and stuff and my bird was just fine. I'm not exactly sure what causes me to fall every time I fall...? Another big issue I had was the reaction time I was given between the moment I wanted to grind and started grinding. Same applies with Manuals and stuff that uses the "balance gauge". I don't feel like I have enough time to read the information and react in consequence to do tricks I'm happy with (just like with the action icons). Maybe it comes with experience? For now I thought that was tough.Other than that, it is clear the design is great. I love the characters, I love the textures, the dialogues are fun, and if you're not into that "birb talk" it isn't even enabled by default; dev did a great job at making a world where everyone can feel happy in. Music fits the mood perfectly, sound effects are well done too. The missions are nice, although as everyone already said a timer on the first ones isn't the best way to experience the game for new players, as failure will repeat a certain amount of times. Once you get the hang of it though, you have plenty of varies and fun objectives.Finally, in my opinion, the game could be better with more details:Of course these suggestions are my thoughts, but having options like that in the menus would be way better.All in all Skatebird doesn't feel like a full-fledged game at first glance, but more of an Early Access; which pains me to say because I can see the work that's been put into it. But it still has that sketchy feel to it; having this much to discuss with barely over an hour of gameplay makes me believe I'm not 100% wrong.Hoping I'll change my rating in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the THPS games, this seemed like it could be a fun twist on that formula. Characters look great, for the most part, and while the 'birb' humour and puns may not be for everyone, I found it ranged from amusing to eye-rolling without dipping into annoying territory. The soundtrack is also good, with a selection of original jazzy/funk tracks as well as some licensed rock and punk songs.Unfortunately, the game fails most with the core skating gameplay. The controls just don't feel tight enough and it's far too common to get stuck on bits of the scenery. Your skater also feels a bit weightless - sometimes just trying to corner will cause you to fall over, and going off a ramp at the wrong angle can send you into a barrel roll.These issues with precision controls wouldn't be such big problems if the levels didn't become increasingly reliant on traversal to reach the next objective. Besides being more frustrating, later levels just aren't as interesting and reuse a lot of the same assets - I can understand a load of skater magazines in someone's bedroom but why are they also littering the office and server room levels? It's also a shame for a game about skateboarding birds to not feature any natural spaces - an actual park seems like an obvious choice, for example, and would go a long way to mixing up the visuals and colour palette.Overall, I can't recommend the game unless the bird theme  sells it to you. THPS fans in particular should steer clear because it just doesn't measure up to the games that inspired it.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm a bit disappointed with this game. Normally I try not to get "hyped up" with what I think a game will be like as it can lead to a subpar outcome. I should have taken my advice.Unfortunately, I was looking forward to an Indie skating game that was reminiscent of classic THPS games, and well this game feels a bit more scrambled than I would have liked. The mechanics feel like it wants to take both bird and skating elements semi-seriously, but then falls flat on both fronts. The floaty mechanics of a bird mixed with the tighter feel of skating makes this feel like your fighting on ice sometimes. Bouncing into objects, and getting stuck constantly is frustrating. On top of all that the objective starting areas could've been placed a bit better so I'm not just sitting on top of where I need to go, so I can actually build some kind of speed or path. Also, like other people pointed out this is an Indie game, and I don't mean to seem harsh in this review, but a little polish can go along way. Customization and level design from what I have experienced is great, but because of the gameplay it sometimes makes me wonder why some stuff is laid out the way it is. Overall the textures for your bird, board, and the level all look nice and I can tell where most of the effort went in.Sound is okay, I mean it's more than just some tweeting, but nothing crazy. The soundtrack however is great and I do quite enjoy listening to it while trying best to skate around.If I were to give this game a rating it would probably be a 3/5 . It's a good attempt but misses what I took as the goal.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and fun, but it has some flaws. The first thing I had to change was the keybindings and the camera settings. If there was a multiplayer challenge map it'd be much better but then they'd have to fix the "reset button resetting the position but not resetting the combo score" problem first. some materials are either too shiny or too rough, and the normal map multipliers are set too high for some materials. Simple objects like different kinds of bowls need to look different as well. Particle trail behind the skate should be able to customised just like the clothing and skins. Some mission briefs look like they were translated poorly by an ai. I also noticed that some beak models are far off from the real counterparts, but I don't think it's a priority. These are the things that caught my eye so far, and I hope these can be fixed. I haven't seen any game breaking issues, so I had fun overall. This game definitely feels like it's made by genuine "birb" lovers who are familiar with bird related subreddits. I'd recommend buying this game on discount and I will be sure to let my friends about this game since it's already on discount now.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game at sale for 4.7 euro and for that price it is definitely worth it. However I don't think I would recommend buying outside of a sale.As for how the game plays, it somewhat reminds me of the skating minigame from Spyro: Year of the Dragon (which was one of my favourite parts of it growing up). The tricks and combo system are pretty easy to understand and you have many nice QoL options (such as disabling the timer for quests if you prefer to just take your time) and the abillity to set down manual checkpoints can be quite nice when I remember to actually use it.One weakness of the game is the quests. They feel repetetive and (I think) they also disable the manual checkpoints  for the duration of it (instead the checkpoint is set to where the quest starts).

(I bumped it down a tiny bit myself) Tips:Manual is direction up+down or the other way around. The "Monch" isn't a manual lol (press grab button while just on the ground to Monch)For extra precision on grinds, I lowered the game speed even more than usual. _childDocuments_.review: SkateBIRD is a ridiculously cute and fun indie skateboarding game. I loved the stages, the overall vibe and being able to customize my birb. The controls, honestly, took me a little to get used to but I also haven't played a lot of Tony Hawk games in the past. What's been really impressive, to me, is how responsive the team has been to create patches and hot fixes for various issues brought up by the fanbase and community. This is a very small team, at least the core team is, so this kind of passion, engagement and response to the players is a very good sign and it shows how invested Megan and crew are in SkateBIRD. With each new patch that I've played (on Steam builds) various points brought up by reviews and players are being addressed. It's making SkateBIRD that much more polished and easier to master. If you tried it on launch day and haven't revisited the game, I urge you to give it another shot. If it's still not for you - that's more than okay. But I think (and hope!) that these fixes (both big and small) will have a positive impact on most players. Full disclosure - I'm the composer behind the OST of SkateBIRD as well as a player. I've playing it on both Steam (Mac build) and on the Nintendo Switch. Obviously the power of my computer is much better than the Switch and I'm able to play at super high specs while the game runs like BUTTAH. I am having an annoying issue with controller support but I've been assured this is a Mac/Steam issue and not a SkateBIRD one. So, while playing on the keyboard is clunky IMO - it's doable. Playing on the Switch is, honestly, a scaled down experience. Most likely out of necessity. So if you can, play it on Steam or Xbox. If Switch is your only option, it will work. It's just not as smooth as the other platforms in my experience. My sons also like to play the game! I hope you enjoy SkateBIRD and please check out the OST! If you like the game and if you liked the soundtrack, please spread the word! It means the world to the people behind SkateBIRD. Thanks to all that have played it so far!

_childDocuments_.review: You're a birb and you get to chill while skating around. Played enough to get to the second level and had a good time doing so. I was surprised by the amount of customization of your birb from the start. A bunch of species and cosmetics available right away, with more as collectibles in the levels. Though I do wish there was an option to change your birb from the main menu instead of having to start a level and then change it.  The lo-fi OST is pretty great and really adds to the chill vibe of the game. As other reviews have stated the controls and camera can be a bit janky. Personally they didn't bother me all that much, with a couple exceptions of being under the bed in the first level and feeling like that camera was way too close to my  birb. Fortunately I didn't find the depth of field to be troublesome as others have, though it did make spotting distant objective objects a bit a of a pain. Overall, if you're expecting a AAA title backed by a huge dev team with everything as polished as possible, you're probably going to be disappointed. If you're expecting a cute, fun game that you can kick-back, have some drinks, smoke a joint and just relax and chill with, you'll probably love it..

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun game.  It took a little bit to get used to the sensitivity, but turning down the game speed to 0.9 REALLY helped me get comfortable. Some of them are HARD and take quite a few retries before you really nail it.  Sure the camera gets wonky sometimes, sure you glitch in the middle of a 100k+ combo, but whatever.  For being a fresh release it's pretty darn good.  The bird customization is really awesome, I was surprised to see so many options of birds.  One nice touch was the option to make the English dialogue less or more "birb".  I don't really care for the "birb" meme language so I really like that I didn't have to force myself to read that, but it's still there if you really enjoy that stuff.The only criticism I have is that the ONLY punk band about birds isn't on the soundtrack! _childDocuments_.review: Now this is a game which both makes me have fun and feel frustrated at the same time. Being in the third world, I finally gave up on a mission which seems just plain IMPOSSIBLE to execute, even with glitching and trying to spam around.General:First of all, it's to be expected that this game does not have the same controls and gameplay feeling as a certain skateboarding game with a certain birdname, but for a little input on how this game works: The missions play like the fourth THPS -> open world and random birds one the map asking you for stuff.Having a doublejump is quite exciting, but after finding out how to do infinite combos with double jump AND screm, creating some high score got lame pretty quick. BIG Negativ:The game physics in combination with the camera control are really frustrating. You barely scratch a stair or a wall and you bail, losing all your special gauge (called fancy here) and combopoints and what so ever. Your fancy gauge is very inconsistent to get, sometimes you're in your 20k+ combo and it doesn't fill up at all, but driving up a ramp without even reaching the edge = fancy is full?!?; doesn't make sense to me at all. The camera should sometimes blend in an epileptic warning for switching perspective every 0.005 seconds 300x in a moment, either while being near a ramp over your head or just spawning on the map without doing anything at all. Not to mention what the camera can do if you glitch out off the map. And you get stuck a lot. A LOT. The only solution is to reset to your spawning point.EDIT: I forgot to mention your double jump almost everytime changes your direction while beiing in the air 180°into the opposite you were aiming for, so trying to double jump up a ramp to reach platforms behind the ramp actually moves you AWAY from these platforms. Sometimes you even change direction on a rail you are landing as if you are reverting but without pressing a button, which confuses a lot in the beginning and angers you a lot after some repetitions.For some positive aspects: - For example being on a rail (like a cable or something else up in the air) and bailing out of it still gives you the chance of landing your combo with a double jump, which feels a bit awarding. - The costumization of the bird is really lovely too, it fits the humour of the game pretty well.  - Music is lit and ideal for a skateboarding game, a mix between jazz, rock and some selfmade vibing songs from the publisher itself. - Every collectable hidden unlocks new styles, music and skateboard customization, which also feels very rewarding. Some little minus points are found in the third level, where one-two hidden unlockables are almost impossible to get with the games current physics. - You can set individual spawning points, which helps spawning back on high platforms if you try to collect some hidden stuff but fall down to ground zero everytime.All in all, I will still try to 100% this game in terms of achievements, but for people who just wanna have fun plaing this game a few hours, I'd not recommend getting this game for the actual price at the moment. It gets really frustrating reaching certain missions and like I said: Collecting stuff in the open world becomes quite impossible or plain stupid to reach in the third world.EDIT 2:I'm in the fourth world and smashed two controllers now. HORRIBLY BAD spawning points for the missions (for example: reach this spot and do a manual, but I'm spawning RIGHT AT THE EDGE TO FALL DOWN TWO FLOORS WTH?!?) and while it is possible to do so, scoring 200k points in 3min while getting CANCELLED by EVERY wall and edge INSTANTLY, so that 100k combos are done for NOTHING. This game is getting more and more frustrating...EDIT FInal: Ok, I calmed down, beat the core game, I'm pleased for the moment. Devs gonna change camera behavior und some missions/collectables were adjusted. It's fine

_childDocuments_.review: While it isn't without its janky moments (the camera or bird getting a bit stuck on some of the more geometrically awkward sections of the levels), if you come to this with the right expectations, there is a lot to like here. The first thing to get out of the way is that, despite the obvious associations people will make, it isn't a Tony Hawk's equivalent/alternative, and nor do I believe it is really trying to be. What it is, though, is a charming as hell skating game with interesting levels, a cute customisable character, some fun dialog setting up the various missions/challenges, a pretty sweet soundtrack, and, after an initial period of getting used to the feel of the controls, you can pull off some very smooth/satisfying runs. So, if you are looking for a "serious" skating game, competing with the likes of THPS, perhaps give this a miss. But if what this game actually is appeals to you, and if you can live with some occasional physics mishaps (which may even be addressed given time), I do believe the love which went into this shines through and it's well worth a play.EDIT: Updates released after my initial review greatly improved the camera handling and "jank" I mentioned.

name: Cake Bash
detailed_description: Fight to be the tastiest cake in Cake Bash! A frantic four player party game where adorable drawn-to-life cakes beat the crumbs out of each other. Pick your favourite cake and battle in a variety of lifelike arenas with unique goals - cover yourself in sweeties or hurl fruit into a pie, there’s plenty for everyone! Try an assortment of minigame treats - roast perfect marshmallows, pipe the finest frosting, or be the last flan standing in Fork Knife. Guide your cakes through the bakery as they dress to impress the customer in Get Tasty! Buy delicious toppings in a series of games to be the chosen one... You could also just play your favourite mode again and again, it’s up to you! Compete on the same screen, find challengers online or battle well-baked bots. It’s time to get out of the oven and into the fray!

_childDocuments_.review: My girlfriend loved it (she hates all my other games lol) and we were busy 5+ hours unlocking every achievement and every character. The simplicity of the "input method" option in settings is the most useful feature I've seen to split-screen a game. You can even play the tutorial in shared/split-screen! And the in-screen tutorial image showing you what to press to do the current action will change depending who's pressing the buttons at that time, making it easy to learn for both players (keyboard and controller), that's AMAZING with Caps On. BTW this game's amazingly fun, you'll laugh a lot (also get mad a lot lol) playing it in shared/split screen or with friends online, and I can see the devs have the potential to create new modes to make this game even more amazing: new difficulties to improve the bots, new tops to buy in the shop, new achievements to hunt, new characters to unlock. Looking forward to play again!  And big thanks for bringing some love to the PC gaming community and the shared/split-screen community, glad to see someone cares! Nowadays I don't know why but game devs seems to assume PC player's don't like to play split-screen lol, they're wrong. Thanks for proving them wrong High Tea Frog ♥ w

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun party game with so much charm and character. Highly recommend 10/10The game consists of a collection of different mini games somewhat reminiscent of Mario Party or the mini games in Pokemon stadium.There are different cakes to unlock for completing different challenges, one I have just unlocked is a pirate chest for the fancy cake that even opens with some chocolate coins inside, a lot of love and care has been put into the different cake designs and it really shows. The mini games get unlocked for freeplay as you come across each for the first time.The different mini games are all quite varied and very good fun. It provides the same chaotic fun and joy that I used to get from the old Mario Party mini games. I really enjoy "Neapolitan" which tasks you to capture ice cream drops that fall from the sky onto a cone, as more drops are captured the stack starts to wobble and you need to start moving to keep it balanced. At the end I had a stupidly tall stack of ice cream!The art style seems to be styled from real life doodles. and its pulled off very well. All the playable cakes have cheeky smiles and wavy arms. I love the attention to detail, my favourite being the little monocles on the scones and the bowties on the s'mores in the "Scones and S'mores" mini game!I really wanted to eat a cupcake after a few rounds. everything look so delicious!The soundtrack is really nice and fits the whole aesthetic very well. I love the little giggles and cheers that the cakes make while they are beating each other up and stealing their toppings!The controls although simple are very tight and intuitive. Its very easy to pick everything up, even for the first time on different mini games.You can play the game local and online against friends or against bots. The game also has matchmaking, but its tough to find games at the moment :( MORE PEOPLE NEED TO GET IT!!!I have however had a lot of fun playing online with my friends, and the bots are very well programmed.Overall its a very fun enjoyable experience and definitely worth a play, especially if you are a fan of the Mario Party series.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up because it looked and sounded like Subnautica with less water, and good grief the actual Subnautica sequel is taking its sweet time getting finished! Unfortunately, I've very rapidly become... disappointed. It's impossible to avoid comparing JTTSP to Subnautica, since they share so many thematic elements - you're stranded on a foreign planet, no other humans for light-years in any direction, employed by a comically awful corporation, and have to collect materials and craft your own way home while dealing with hostile local wildlife and solving age-old mysteries. Problem is, if you DO compare it to Subnautica, it just falls VASTLY short in a wide variety of areas.First and foremost, the thing that disappointed me right out the gate... no base-building elements. You're stuck operating out of your crappy landing-craft for the entirety of the game. Collected resources are solely used for upgrading your gear, turning this into something of a first-person Metroidvania. A Metroidvania without any kind of map. Off to a great start, aren't we?Second, I realized soon afterwards - no survival-elements. You don't need to eat or drink, you don't have to worry about heat or radiation - go jump around on those chunks of red-hot rock floating in a river of magma, no worries! - and your weapons and gear have infinite ammo and battery-life. The only kind of limited ammo you have to deal with are the throwable 'secondary' weapons, and most of those LITERALLY grow on trees. This leaves the entire weight of the game resting on exploration (without, again, a MAP!) and the combat. Plain old first-person shooting. Compared to cleverly sneaking around the big sea-monsters in Subnautica, it's just... boring. Very, very boring.And finally, the bit I probably should've seen coming: If you take away the water from Subnautica, what you're left with is... platforming. First-person precision platforming. There are very few games, historically, who've done first-person precision platforming really well, and this ain't one of them. Not that it's TERRIBLE or anything, it's just... ergh. Basically, first-person platforming is like inverse pizza, you know? If it's bad, it's REALLY bad, but if it's good, it's... still kind of bad.Now, I'm not COMPLETELY down on this game - the alien world you've landed on is intriguing, colorful, and just generally makes you want to go out and explore it. The mascot 'puffy birds' are amusing, and there are some other interesting and creative critters around, even if all the actual ENEMIES I've met so far have been remarkably derivative. How many more times am I gonna have to fight flying jellyfish and burrowing, armored lizards that can spin-dash towards your Sonic-style? Probably a great many. Compared, once more, to the fascinatingly alien sea-beasts of Subnautica, they're not worth much more than an eye-roll.I suppose my main problem is that everything this game has going for it, Subnautica has too - while it's missing a TON of what made Subnautica great. Well, I suppose it does have SOME things that Subnautica doesn't... like... umm... well... hmm. Oh! Gross-out humor. Lots and lots of gross-out humor. So if you're an old Ren & Stimpy fan, that may be enough to carry the game for you all by itself.As for me, I'll give it a few more hours to surprise me and prove me wrong... then I think I'll just give up on it and take another run through Subnautica.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is proof that social media ads work. I kept seeing ads for the sequel on my timeline and thought it looked good when I finally paid attention. I came to steam and saw that it wasn't out yet, but there was a first game; Journey to the Savage Planet. I decided to give it a try.Firstly, the game runs great. It doesn't seem particularly demanding, so I played at 4k/triple digit framerate. The story is pretty straightforward, in that you're an intergalactic explorer paid to discover a new planet for humans to infest *cough* colonize. They did well with the humor and the AI companion is nicely done and ads some flavor the the game.Combat is fairly simple, with your main gun and a secondary resource discovered on the planet. These secondary resources are a big help in combat against fast and strong enemies, so it was a nice touch. If there's one knock on the game I would say that it's a touch formulaic. You need ti get ti ab area, discover it's inaccessible, and have to go to another area to acquire certain resources to craft into gear that makes the area accessible. Pretty much every area is like this. In my personal opinion, that is a nitpick, as I didn't find it to be a real negative, and it was always fun going from place to place to acquire the materials to upgrade my gear.My only real gripe is that a map would have been nice, but that's a small gripe that didn't truly detract from the experience.The visuals are colorful and fun, as are the hilarious creatures you encounter. A bit of the environmental humor is a bit dark, but not bad. Overall, I'm glad I stumbled on this game. It's funny, fun, has a lot of cool ideas that work well. I'm looking forward to the sequel!Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey to the Savage Planet, For me again one of those games where I not only want a thumbs up or down, but also the option of a neutral rating option. Since reviews are actually always a personal opinion and not always have something to do with the quality of the game, this option would be really desirable.... But let's just start with the game itself because that's actually, I think, to be rated really positively.According to our client, the exploration of AR-Y 26 is only about scanning the environment and collecting samples. This is to ensure whether a colonization of the planet would be possible. Unfortunately, our spaceship crashes on the planet and we have little idea, let alone any kind of equipment at hand, and so this exploration mission also turns into a rescue mission on our own behalf. Since we want to find out whether a life on the planet is possible, we run around most of the time with our scanner and scan everything that comes in front of the lens. Apart from a wide variety of biomes, the planet also has a lot of strange animals that we can kill with our weapons to exploit resources or step into circular saw traps. The opportunities for improvement that we are offered by doing research or consuming the orange goo are to be rated positively. This increases the "rank" and you unlock new equipment that you can then 3D print in the spaceship.Now for the negative part for me:Unfortunately there is no card in the game, which often requires a lot of patience. Sometimes the game is just completely opaque and you waste a lot of time looking for things because of the missing map. Due to the inadequate control, both with keyboard and mouse, as well as with the controller, some jumping and climbing passages quickly become annoying and frustrating challenges.My recommendation is to finish playing the game in one go. I couldn't do that due to a lack of time and when I was at it again I had real difficulties finding my way back into the game and often didn't know what I was last doing and how it should go on... ✅ colorful game world ✅ funny opponents ✅ varied level design ✅ good fast travel system ✅ research is rewarded ✅ a lot to discover ❌ Too much searching due to missing card ❌ very high potential for frustration ❌ no saving ❌ bad control ❌ only one level of difficulty ❌ low replay value

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little game about planetary exploration. I'm a sucker for these kinda games so this was right up my alley, that being said - the game is pretty short and it's relatively easy. Does this stop the game from being very solid and a fun romp? Heck no. I absolutely adored the visual style of this game. It felt like I was playing through a weird Dreamworks movie. It's pretty astounding how well the game runs too, ran it maxed out with an RTX 3080 and a 5900x, never dipped below 100 fps even in very visually heavy scenes. The environments are also pretty decently varied, starting off in a snowy area, quickly moving onto a forest area and it continues to divvy up where you are. Unfortunately, can't really say the same for enemy variety, which was the sore spot for me and this title. There's the ever present big puffy bird things, the irritating squids and a couple other baddies that are re-used throughout the game, additional to that, there's only really 3 big boss fights, which to me was enough for the run time of the game, but may not be apt for other folks. The game feels fairly simple but starts opening up relatively quickly. Within the first hour or so, you get a double jump, a little further down, you get a grappling hook and so on, which are necessary for the latter areas. Essentially, if you see a far off space, chances are there's stuff to find there and you have multiple means to get to it. The game's upgrades are hard locked for the majority of the run time, but aren't needed, the game opens up a LOT more after you defeat the final boss to give you room to just go nuts and explore at your leisure. There's 100 orange globs to find, which will boost your HP/Stamina and there's misc. elements that will help you buff up your gear for more capacity, a double jump, etc.The exploration is where this game truly shines. It's an incredible amount of fun to just go around, grapple to a floating island then solve mini puzzles to get more alloy or other goodies, searching every nook and cranny for these orange globs and other goodies. The combat is fairly basic and doesn't really evolve past the 1 gun you get at the start of the game, it's serviceable, but could have used more ways to get up close and personal imo. The hard lack of enemy variety is what keeps it from being a "great" title for me though, you can just about complete the game in 6 or so hours w/o much exploration and around 10+ if you decide to be a completionist (which I was not for this particular title - full disclosure). It's a short enough romp that doesn't overstay it's welcome and shines with it's spectacular art and environment variety.

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals and map design are outstanding. Getting upgrades through gameplay opens up new paths in previously visited map parts. Parkouring is pure joy because jumps are snappy, grappling to the point and railways are as fast as they are rewarding.I enjoyed the story because it does not take itself seriously. It is scifi tropes turned  slapstick all the time. There is so much love to silly details: the advertisements are funyy, spam mails just great, the cards you pick up for your Javlin have sick twisted artstyles and even bobble heads have cynical voice lines. The game does not overstay its welcome. It took me 12 for 100% completionist playthrough. Thoroughly enjoyed my time on this savage planet.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've always wanted to be stranded in an alien world, where you can punt the wild life, slap the snot out of annoying encounters, swing like Tarzan, or be poo'd-burped-farted-vomited-and-all-manner-of-splatted on, Kindred has the perfect opportunity for you!As a bonus, you will be provided the most fantastic sarcastic AI you'll ever meet in the universe! If you're a lucky candidate, you'll spend hours exploring every planetary orifice while collecting beautiful postcard souvenirs of where your last body met its untimely demise. Be the first, be the last, be the 42 that come between! It's a win win...or maybe a when-when. anyhow, stop thinking about it, and just give them your money already! Not convinced? Here's a poem to help seal the deal: Spikes and stones may break your bones, but bombegranates will exterminate most everything.Come on, already! Hop to, before you get a poke in the eye! You'll break your fun-o-meter for sure![Disclaimer: No sentient creatures or devices were hurt while typing this public service message.]

_childDocuments_.review: This is an OK game.  I was originally going to give this game a thumbs up, but I just can't bring myself to play this game anymore.While the world is very pretty and the writing is good, I do not enjoy the environmental puzzles.  At first it was fine, it was just minor stuff, but now it's all like platforming and trying to use grappling hooks over bottomless pits.   This is just not some sequence where you have a clear path.  No, it's a puzzle where wrong turns mean death.It doesn’t help that monsters respawn either while you're trying to do all of this.  I am fine if you leave the area, and then come back and the monsters respawn, but no, in this game they respawn on a timer and if you're trying to figure out one of these puzzles, you just keep getting attacked again.Maybe this just isn’t my kind of game.  I really tried to give it a chance, but the game is more of a chore rather than a fun experience for me.I'd describe this as a first person exploration / environmental puzzle & platforming game.  If that appeals to you, then maybe this game is for you.  It is just not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a lot, I have had my eyes on it since I got to play it at EGX London and speak to a developer there who showed great passion so ideally this stuck out most over the industry dominating titles I was excited for. Now onto the actual game, it is short and sweet, it doesn't overstay its welcome and has a very rewarding sense of progression. You can just blast through the game collecting the upgrades and move onto the next section but the most fun was returning to previous areas and using my new upgrades to obtain items that was previously unreachable. The game starts out weird yet charming and opens up to a beautiful playground for you to use all what is given to you to your hearts content. I 100% recommend this game for a casual experience just to kick back and enjoy the gorgeous art style the team have created and you can even bring a friend along for the journey making the experience the more the merrier.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game to finally come to Steam. Epic can go piss itself for all I care. But the game is great. The kind of open-world experience I was looking for, and the humor wasn't too bad! It's easy if you know what you're doing and get every upgrade. But it's also rather short, having beaten the final boss in less than 8 hours. But I still had fun exploring the world and am very willing to go get every little thing.Even though the magic alien goop maxes out at 50. So the other 50 is literally for completion sake. All and all, not really worth the $30, but if you can get it on sale, most certainly worth the buy.Oh, and pick the Dog. Dog good boy. He claims planet for humans. Humans good human. 10/10, would dog again.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It's basically Metroid Prime meets Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, and every part of it works so well! You get the same sense of isolation and adventure that Metroid Prime excelled at, but at the same time I can't think of a game that made me laugh out loud more than this one. I was a little hesitant at first because a lot of the reviews said it is too short, but if I were the developers I'd take that as a compliment because it means we didn't want it to end. Besides, I think a lot of the humor (and especially the hilarious ads) would get stale and repetitive if the game lasted much longer. Seriously, I can't think of a single criticism.Final Verdict: BUY THIS GAME! Even if you only want a game that lasts for more than 20 hours, buy it when it's on sale, it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: In general I like the game. Though it can get boring relatively quick. BUT I have to repeat what I already wrote hundred of times: It is a VERY BAD idea to use invisible walls in an exploring game! Especially if it has Groundless holes, where you can "die"! I foxing HATE that!!! And I totally understand if you can't pause the game (e.g. during using the main menu) in multiplayer games. But it is also a terrible idea during single player game! You quickly have to run to the loo and find your char dead when you come back. Why on earth do devolper come to such stupid ideas???Such mechanics are a proof that it is just developed as a new-school-kiddy-cashgrab-game instead of making it a serious game with though-out concept.So as much as I like the game and would like to give it a recommendation, I only can rate it the way the devs obviously WANT it to be rated. I am NOT sorry for the thumb down here.Edit:The more I play this game, the more I see from the dirty and loveless punched together tec-side of the game. The maps are not even build proper. Have fun falling into the void. And I do NOT mean the space between the isles, but the REAL void where you fall through the whole map! (at least the game has mercy and let you die at a falling depth of around 8 or 9 kilometers) Also the gun doesnt shoot at the first click. Its such a pain.Seriously: I want QUALITY games from QUALITY Design and Programming specialists! NOT some pricey rushed together cattle food from marketing clowns!Edit 2:Achievements that can be reached ONLY in coop...? Nice, you received the "negative review for sure"-achievement with this further GREAT idea! <3Edit 3:Even the ending is a nothing. Don't waste your time to 100% the game. Its not worth. The best you can do is to leave the planet asap without the seed. Then you get a little bit more entertaining ending at least. I really don't understand what people mean by saying this game would be soooo humorous. Yes it's entertaining (the ads are awesome!), but humans also keep telling me, that I would be a funny guy. (...and I am not.) Lets come to a compromise and say its a "mildly funny" game. Think that's fair enough.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful looking game that's held back by a thousand grievances. +The music is great.+The game looks fantastic- the design of "The Savage Planet"  truly feels like you're on an alien world.  +Great teleport system.-The platforming is mostly clunky, slow and tedious -The combat is very poor, with only one sluggish pistol to your name that holds no proper amount of ammunition. -More about the combat. Enemies appear out of thin air, hitscan you, reload speed and frequency is painfully often and slow, hitboxes are all kinds of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up- yours and the enemies. You are clearly shooting at the "glowy bits" but nothing is happening- nothing hit you, but still did. You get knocked around, blown away, and smudged with goo 24/7. It's incredibly frustrating to get anything done when there's green/purple goo on your camera or you're flying through the air over the map. Also, everything is so colorful that enemies blend together, making some very hard to spot in time.  -The game is mostly a long fetch quest, coupled with very easy, but long winded and frustrating combat sections.  -The usable items are mostly pointless, except for a few -The "super jump" power-up is incredibly clunky and un-fun to use -The narrator's "humor" gets old very quick. -Abrupt ending, gets nothing resolved. -They expect you to 100% this game? Jesus.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey to the Savage Planet – Space Exploration’s Wackiest Adventure 🚀😂Congratulations, recruit! You’ve just landed on ARY-26, an alien world full of wonders, dangers, and, frankly, some of the weirdest creatures you’ll ever see. And by “landed,” I mean your spaceship is barely holding together with space duct tape. But hey, Kindred Aerospace, the fourth best interstellar exploration company, believes in you—probably because you're cheap labor. 💼✨This game is a laugh-out-loud mix of slapstick comedy and surprisingly solid exploration mechanics. Every corner of the planet oozes charm, from the adorable-but-deadly Pufferbirds to the sarcastic AI that narrates your every failure. The humor is top-tier, but don’t let it fool you—there’s a genuinely great adventure underneath all the jokes. 🌱💥The visuals? Gorgeous. The gameplay? Delightfully chaotic. The sense of achievement when you finally figure out how to feed some alien goo to a screaming plant? Chef’s kiss. If you want a game that combines colorful exploration with absurd comedy, Journey to the Savage Planet is your ticket to interstellar hilarity. Just don’t forget to file your report—Kindred’s counting on you! 😜📊Created with <3

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, action-packed platformer/shooter. You'll get a lot of laughs out of this one, and it's got a fun story too. Two minor drawbacks, but they're so minor, that it REALLY SHOULDN'T impact your decision to get this game:1. There's A LOT of verticality to the platforming, so I was a little miffed when I encountered an invisible wall. It only happened once, but for a game all about jump-boosted flinging yourself up and around floating rocks, where you can fall to your death... an invisible wall felt REALLY lazy to me. Fortunately, it only happened once, and the game is anything but lazy. It's full of hidden gems and beautifully packed details. 2. More linear than it should have been. Again, for a game about flinging yourself about a chaotic jumble of floating rocks... I kept encountering progression walls. Can't go here until you get X upgrade... oops, can't get to X upgrade without B upgrade. It forces you to complete most of the levels in a very specific order, which really felt unneccessary to me. That said, every "room" and mission is unique enough, that I didn't really notice it aside from the few moments where I encountered an obvious progression wall: *sigh* really!? again!? Moving on... *forgotten, and back to fun*

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing within first few hours. Than it's great, and eventually ends up being good. But overall I have very pleasant memories of my Savage Planet discovery !Wether it is for the visuals, aesthetic, designs, mechanisms and voice acting, it's all making a weird yet addictive world to roam in ! It's beatiful, dumb af and catchy, and you simply want in, whatever comes next.Basically a Zelda-like in first person view, where you unlock items and features on the go, and have to back track in order to discover hidden collectibles. A really refreshing take on the formula despite its limited gameplay.That said now, it wears off a little over time. Once the amazement is over, the game pulls its sleaves up and have you master all the things you learned by working hard. Thing is, it gets quickly repetitive, and if it wasn't for the end game being slightly more challenging, the experience is nowhere near as interesting as the post-landing period.But as I said, the game made quite the impression for me, and let alone the second half of the game being grindy and a bit tedious, I was enjoying myself very much on this planet.I mean if you just want to kick some cute aliens, just grab it on sales !
