_childDocuments_.review: 5/10 - I wish I could give a neutral rating!Journey to the Savage Planet definitely is not a bad game! I just couldn't bring myself to finish it.On the positive side:+ The humor is fantastic (e.g. when you die...)+ The design of animals, plants, landscapes is appealing, absurd and pretty cute!+ I like all the fun tools you unlock to help navigate over the planetHowever:- This game gave me physical headaches, and I usually don't get those when I game. I assume it's a combination of saturated colors, lots of movement, jumping, running, and shooting. I couldn't play it for longer than an hour at a time.- I found the world and quests a little overwhelming?? I often felt lost and struggled to find the correct route to jump and slide to the quest destination. I know it's also about exploration etc. etc., but I personally would have liked  a little more guidance and a little less visual input. Idk, the game just overwhelmed my senses in a way :'D Which, again, doesn't mean it's a bad game at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Sure!I mean, on its own, it's an FPS exploration game, in the mould of other games where you explore a limited area, find tech that lets you explore more area, to find tech that lets you explore more area, and so on.  You know the name of the genre, and typing it in gives me the hives.The game is visually lush and the combat hasn't been hard either.  The majority of the damage I've taken in-game came from flubbing jumps trying to go off the beaten path.  Since there's a lot of hidden gewgaws, going off the beaten path is kind of the point.The real difference here is the guy who did the writing for Borderlands 2 has done the writing for this game.  It's clear he's got a style, a style I described as "Ha ha dystopia" to my wife.  Terrible things happen (off-camera, as part of the universe) and they're presented for yukks.  There's a lot of social satire action going on with in-ship commercials.  Things that buff your character you are casually informed give you "benign cancer", haha, because the corporation views the human assets as having less value than the mechanical ones.  Ha ha, the crew are fungible assets.Here's a commercial for a food product that morphogenically adapts itself to taste like any one of 21 billion different possible delicious foods.  It also kills you slowly.  Ha ha!  It's a dystopian world, and that's the guy's style.You are sometimes encouraged to do horrible things to the friendly fauna "for science".  Like drop-kicking them through whirling blades.  I guess you don't have to, but those science experiments won't conduct themselves. Ha.Now, I'm also playing it in French, and it's all in Quebecois French, which makes my day like you wouldn't believe.  "icitte", "déniaise," etc.Oh yeah, and coop!  We started playing, my wife and I, got to bumbling about a bit, and then got distracted by other things and didn't go back so I'm playing it alone.  But that's not a reflection on the game, more than it's a reflection on our senses of whimsy.So yeah, get it.  Especially if you thought the writing in Borderlands 2 was ace.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting much when I picked up Journey to the Savage Planet. It looked like a short, fun, linear version of No Man's Sky and, at the time, it was on sale so why the hell not?My comparison was wrong in a lot of ways and right in others. The world is great, the humor leans in the Portal/Portal 2 direction, which I loved, and the game runs incredibly well on an older system. (i7-6700k, MSI 1080, and 16 gigs ram)There's a touch of Metroid here as you explore a strange, alien world, gather upgrades and use them to further explore the odd, colorful planet AR-Y 26.Combat is light and of the big glowing weak spot variety but the creatures, both predator and prey, are fun to look at and definitely lean on cute more than fierce or frightful. The platforming, especially when you've got all the upgrades, is responsive with some tight controls and speedy gadgets. Nothing groundbreaking, but still a good time.Considering the length of the game I'm not sure I'd recommend it at full retail but if you find it discounted and enjoy exploration with a pretty linear path to the end game you'll love Journey to the Savage Planet.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sits right in the middle of good and bad for me.  The game is pretty fun right off the bat for the first few hours.  I did this co-op with a friend, and I really liked the implementation of that feature a lot; it made the game a lot more enjoyable to me.Buuuuut this game has a lot of weak points.  The humor gets old and gets worse as the game goes on.  It's almost as bad as Borderlands at some moments, maybe even a bit worse.  A lot of the zones feel monotonous and not fun to explore too, especially at the end.  The level design could have definitely used some work.  The final area and boss in particular were both unfun and anticlimactic.  We did play the DLC too, and I DO think that was one of the better segments of the game.  It still wasn't GREAT, but it was still fun enough.  Overall, this is the okayest game I've played in a while.  I feel if I didn't have a friend to play this with, I probably wouldn't have finished it.  I have more negative things to say than positive things, but the first few hours of the game ARE fun, and the DLC is good, too.  But it kind of sucks that a game that took almost 9 hours to complete with DLC got tedious, when that's sort of short for a game like this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is early access quality.Fairly early in the game, you're tasked with getting an alien alloy. After getting it, I decided I wanted to take a break, but I wasn't sure how the game handled saving. So I opened the in-game menu and clicked Return to Main Menu. Practically every modern game I can recall playing would offer some warning about what will happen, and ask you to confirm. Journey to the Savage Planet takes you straight back to the menu in one click.When I resumed playing, I was given some cheeky narration about having died. Apparently returning to main menu is equivalent to committing suicide in this game, and this is never communicated to the player. I needed to go back to where I was on the planet in order to retrieve my stuff, then go back to the ship to use it.Upon returning to the ship, I was unable to proceed with the main quest. There was nowhere for me to deposit the alien alloy. Looking it up online, this is a game-breaking bug that has existed for at least 10 months. If you obtain the alien alloy and stop playing before depositing it in the ship, your save file is forfeit. The only remedy is to restart.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine you are back in the 90's and you play a game where you can complete the collectable objectives. There's a bit of challenge but nothing that seems impossible. You don't need to find a guide because there's no ridiculously placed items only someone with mods could find. Doesn't that sound satisfying? This game is heavily based on collecting and scanning various things for various objectives and to be honest I found it so fun. So many games are near impossible to complete and this one hit the sweet spot. I don't remember the last time I could actually complete a game (At the time of this review I have three things left to scan!). I work a mentally demanding job and the last thing I want to do is have to think too much when I finish work and start up a game. I saw another review speaking negatively about the fact each area is basically the same but you know what? Thats great. I dont want to figure out what I need to do per new area. You get character level ups and new abilities anyway. Each new area is a different design and new creatures. I walk into this new area and I can go and do something straight away. Brilliant!The sarcastic humour of the AI that narrates the game is hilarious. At no point did I ever think 'Shut up' like a lot of games. Congrats to whoever thought of this character style, I could listen to the AI go on for hours (and I guess I have!) There is a creature called a Baboushka which is highly entertaining wonderous thing. The games probably worth buying to witness that thing alone. Yep, of course I recommend the game. Chill out, grab a beer and collect some goo.

_childDocuments_.review: This would be a neutral recommendation if such a thing were possible, but with only having two sides, I'll pick the negative one.The game isn't terribly bad, but it simply fails to persuade. The graphics are adequate, sound is appropriate, controls more or less work (there's a couple weird keybinds and double ups... but you can easily rebind those). But gameplay wise... it's just so damn shallow. Combat is simplistic, 'exploration' comes down to following a HUD marker along the most obvious obstacle courses I've seen implemented in a game. Progression is... kind of there, but it's again very shallow.In essence, you could compare this game to a Metroid title like Metroid Prime. Except take out all meaningful challenge, all sense of wonder and epic, and add in quirky, but quickly repititive, humor and poop jokes (because, yeah, that seems to be the games shtick from start to finish. And, as often seen with these games, it's easy to overdo it).Also, make it a really short adventure that you can, on a blind playthrough, as a mediocre action player (think: a scrub who couldn't beat Dark Souls), beat in 5 hours without even dieing ONCE. Like, the game isn't even trying to be difficult whatsoever. (Literally Jumping off a cliff doesn't kill you.) Even the boss fights are trivialized by virtue of medkits (healthplants) being plentiful available next to any kind of combat situation, which provide a rather quickly regenerating health boost.So, overall, the game is too simple, too short, too silly.It's not utterly terrible, but given the alternatives you could pick up instead, this game simply isn't worth your money and time.Rating: 4/10PS: Bought in a pack with the DLC, but after beating the main game I can't even muster the interest to check out the DLC level. So don't grab that one, either.

I did!Total playtime for the main story was around 8 glorious hours.

_childDocuments_.review: "It's something to do" is my summary. This is another one of those games that deserves a "meh" rating in my book but in lieu of that option on Steam, I'll default to a Thumbs Up. On the plus side, the game is vibrantly gorgeous and runs very smoothly with the exception of a few crashes when getting stuck in the environment.  This is most certainly a completionist's game, but it lacks substance.The problem for me is that it just doesn't do any one thing well. It has main quests, side quests and grindy challenges that give you something persistent to strive for but it lacks any real purpose.  The main focus is exploration in a slightly metroidvania-style world.  There is minimal combat and absolutely no challenge to the game.  You will upgrade weapon damage, health, etc. but there is no real incentive that makes these upgrades worth seeking.  These are just mindless objectives to pursue throughout the 6-8 hour course of the game.  I genuinly mean the following statement in the best possible way: if you're needing to kill a few hours and don't mind menial task-oriented gameplay then this is definitely a satisfying game.  It's just not rewarding nor gripping in any meaningful way.  I would definitely recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: 3 / 10As a disclaimer: I actually very much enjoy games that encourage grinding and collecting and running around upgrading gear/perks - and this game just...doesn't deliver on that.It is a nice looking game and it runs reasonably well, but the game just lacks a sort of spirit. I really want to like it, but just cant with how little game is actually here for the price. Its a pretty tired setup in the story with you crashing onto a planet and need to find bits and pieces of your ship to leave, "oh and do this thing while you're here." There is a central tower (the thing) in the map that they lean into pretty hard with narrative to go and explore it.  The whole thing just felt generally lazy and lacked aforementioned spirit. The overall mechanics of your character are slightly entertaining for a bit, then everything just kinda gets same-y. The world obstacles are all kind of the same, the aliens don't have a great variety. The dialogue can be a bit amusing at times and that quickly turns into annoying one-liners. To me it is very disappointing to have this game laid down in a very linear gameplay fashion when it is labeled as an exploration game. There is very little incentive to actually go explore. Collectibles are sparse and there are no side quests at all. Sure you can run around and do a few things, but there is no real point - there is not much to collect and only about 5 different types of enemies in the world to fight. Recommendation: Look into Supraland if you are looking for something looks and feels as this, but actually delivers a lot on what it promises.

_childDocuments_.review: I've bought about 13 games in the last few months, just looking for something that was truly entertaining and new. This seems so far to be exactly that. A fresh new take on exploration in a wild alien world. Enough to do to keep you busy alone and even better to play with a friend. Lighthearted and not too serious. Not scary or frustrating. Just downright relaxed fun!Graphics: are great. cartoony and fun. Nice looking shadows and a full range of color if that's your thing. Co-op exploration:  is fun and can keep two people going in the same or different direction without getting bored. Story: Great, fun, funny, enough continuity to appreciate. Trying not to spoil anything.Story / Character dialogue: Awesome, funny, comical, flows throughout the story.Definitely worth the $17.99 I paid for it. _childDocuments_.review: Journey to the Savage Planet has a lot to recommend it. It has a quirky, fun sense of humor that is clearly patterned off of the Portal series. Its world is vibrant and beautiful. Its creature designs are very cute and the world is impressively detailed. I've played a lot of gritty/post-apocalyptic games this year (e.g., Days Gone, Grim Dawn, Control) and JttSP offered just what I was looking for: a cartoony world in which to shoot things.So where'd it go wrong? Well, for one thing I'm not all that big on Metroidvanias, so this game started at a bit of a deficit for me. I find that this genre involves pretty regular background frustration as you find you can't do this right now, can't do that right now, or worse you're left to guess at whether your failure to accomplish something is down to a lack of skill with the controller or to a missing item.Then I got to the platforming. I guess I should say I'm also not that big a fan of 3D platformers, and I like it even less when the perspective is first-person. So jumping around on mushroom caps that sink rapidly if you stand on them for so much as a second was not that satisfying an experience, and started to sour the mood for me.At least with a controller, the gameplay experience isn't all that smooth either. You have to use the left and right D-Pad to move around between item options, some of which are essential to killing certain types of creatures. There's no radial menu that slows down the action around you or anything fancy like that. Your gun is also kind of a pea shooter, although there's hope that upgrades will eventually boost your firepower.As time went on, I just started dying a lot, and in particular dying more frequently than I was having any especially rewarding or fun moment in the game. And I question the wisdom of any creative team that has your robot side-kick say "you did your best, but it's too bad your best wasn't good enough" every. single. time. you. die. I know there's an option to completely silence EKO, but that's not what I want. I just want to not hear the same mockery over and over.Git gud, right? If the juice was worth the squeeze, I would have.If you like Metroidvanias and enjoy precision platform jumping, consider this a recommended game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

So if you need to reinstall windows or such, you may lose your game save unless you back it up. Usually backing up saves aren't a big deal but this game saves as an undescriptive folder named "Towers".

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game per se, it's just a collect-a-thon masquerading as a game. If you like games where the game itself it a collectible seeking hunt, then you may enjoy this. The main story is a comic attempt at the players expense of being a planetary explorer and ranges from almost funny quips to annoying one liners. The game is short, at about 10 hours (and that's a stretch) for the main story. If you really want to set about collecting everything, you can probably squeeze 20-25ish hours out of it. I have three big complaints that force me into not recommending the game. First, the combat. It's awful. I mean, it really, really feels like it was tacked onto a explorative-platforming game because they thought at the last second, "people have to fight alien wildlife!" The dodging mechanic is the worst part. So many times, I would try to dodge an attack and my character would crouch. They're the same button. The enemies continuously respawn and they are more of an annoyance than anything. The second complaint is the randomness of the collectibles. You do need to collect a few to progress the story. Some are hidden in plain sight, others require abilities that you have to unlock and then there are the ones that feel like someone closed their eyes and dropped the collectible on the map and you need to play Mission Impossible to reach it. My third and last complaint is the unlocking of the abilities. This is a fundamental part of the game. You have to not only find the ability in the game, but you have to then have the resources to unlock it. Then you have to be in the right "exploration tier" to unlock it. How do you unlock the exploration tiers? By doing achievement-esque stunts like falling 50 meters and using your double-jump to survive or tagging 3 different aggressive monsters for research and so on. These tasks should be as they sound. Achievements. Not a requirement to access skills in your skill tree.Conclusion, it's a short game with terrible combat mechanics, a not-so-funny story of space exploration, and an achievement-locked skill tree, all the while disguising itself as a game. The game is just, "collect all the stuff and we put it everywhere, isn't that fun?!?" After completing the "story", I can firmly say, no, it isn't fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for 40 minutes and then requested a refund, as I didn't enjoy it. As a disclaimer to my review, I acknowledge that 40 minutes of gameplay is probably not fully representative of the game - the game likely gets more advanced and sophisticated as time goes on. But hey, this is my review:I expected an exploration game similar to the Outer Wilds, Subnautica or Satisfactory, but that is not what this game is. Instead it feels more like a platformer, with similar vibes to the Ratchet and Clank games.I felt like the game was extremely linear and felt a bit like an old PS2 game where you do one mission and then the computer tells you where to go for the next mission. It didn't feel like there was much scope for exploration. You can choose different upgrades etc, which likely allow branch points in your progress, but ultimately it didn't feel very deep.I found the UI and controls generally a bit uncomfortable and clunky - I didn't think they were particularly natural.The combat did not feel particularly interesting or meaningful. Most enemies I encountered were fairly harmless and boring, and died after a couple of shots. There is unlimited ammo. The gimmick of throwing bait/sticking balls/bouncing balls did not feel particularly intuitive and I didn't really enjoy that feature. The art style is nice and the integration of live-action videos into the game to provide you with story is interesting.I can see the appeal of this game, but it wasn't for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game I did love, I actually really enjoyed it, and did a livestream of the whole thing a few months ago.   My problem is that even though I did enjoy the visuals and the gameplay something just felt... off about the whole experience.I do not play very many fps games.   So this is different for me.   Most of my experience comes from Metroid Prime series, which I love to death.   But I think part of it is that I think my PC its self does not read the right stick on my controllers properly.  Which made the camera an absolutely pain for me to use.  It didn't help that the lock on feature was pretty finicky all things considered.   This also made strafing INNATELY difficult.  So the Kapyena fights that ocurred later in the game were rather consistently difficult for me.   The platforming controls I found pretty good, but was often deceptive early on.  I consistently had jumps where I just BARELY missed the platform.  By like a foot which was far enough the guy couldn't grab onto the edge.  I understand the jump stabilizers helped mitigate fall damage but this is also the ONLY game I've ever played with fall damage where the damage negate happens right before you LAND rather than when you JUMP, IE ground pounding in 3D mario games.IE I wish I could give this a slight thumbs up than a full thumbs up since this to me is a solid 6.5/10 game.  Not spectacular, not mediocre, not absolute trash.  But it would fall near the upper portion of the second quartile imho.  But hey this is my first written review in over what 3 bloody years? _childDocuments_.review: Making Planetary Exploration a Mediocre ChoreGood:-movement and controls are good (i.e. Jumping is responsive, things like auto climb work, etc)-game looks very colorful and well designedBad:-the humor. If I could give life to an overused meme or twitter account this would be it. There's so much I hate about the "jokes" that I could do a review on that alone.- the challenge. For the amount I played there was none. Life regeneration is overly abundant in the rare instances you need it. - the stamina bar. Why does this exist? Or why is it even a factor in the beginning of the game? You are able to run for about 3 seconds before you run out of stamina. Guess what this game has you do? Travel long distances to get items and then return to your ship at the beginning. This leads to another point.- having to return to the ship to get new items/abilities. This is what officially killed the game for me. It's not bad enough you have the stamina of a lifelong smoker bound to a wheelchair. You have to use that stamina to travel vast distances and come ALL THE WAY BACK. This is something you have to experience to see how bad it is. It makes the music and scenery which was once quirky into agonizing punishment. - everything else. This seems like an alien race or sentient robots tried to copy the formula for a good game and had no idea that fun was one of the components.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's weird, in a funny way. It's a fun exploration game, solo or co-op. It's a little on the short side in terms of playtime, expect to finish the game in around 12-ish hours if you're taking your time, and expect to 100% it in roughly the same amount of time if you already know what you're doing. However, you will be engrossed throughout those entire 12 hours in some way.The writing is either hit or miss with some people, I personally find it to be pretty hilarious (in most cases). People find the main AI to be either annoying as hell or fun and witty, but you don't really know until you play it. It feels like the writers had a bunch of fun creating the logs and creatures, with names like Fizzlebob and Chumcumber, and pits that "smell like sex."The story is alright, it's enough to keep you engrossed throughout the experience but don't go in expecting the greatest story ever told. There are some fun sidequests to do, but it feels like they're there mostly to give some more witty dialogue than anything else, as most of them aren't really brain teasers. Unfortunately, I would say that this game isn't replayable unless you give it a long rest between sessions- and by that I mean forget literally everything that happened. Once you know what to do, it's a cakewalk, as you can brute force your way through just about everything in the game. It's a REALLY easy game. But it's a fun one.If you get tired of exploring, you can just sit down and read through the hundreds of logs and scanner descriptions for the world. While not all of them are bangers, some really do make you laugh.Overall, it's a favorite of mine. It's a chill game to play alone or with friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game and i enjoyed it a lot.The style of the game, the movement and upgrades are awesome and put well into place. I played it with a friend in coop and this is the point where the game starts struggling.Difficulty:===========Kind of easy. I don't remember if there was an option to choose the difficulty. If there is you may want to take the higher difficulties for a slightly bigger challenge. Since i dont remember choosing a difficulty all i can say is, that it was very ez. Bosses were down quickly and didn't pose a real threat. Co-Op:======The coop is not really optimized and by that i mean that my game (as the host) crashed a total of 3 times in 8 hours of playtime. And according to my mate it's extremely buggy for the connected person. This shouldn't be happening and hopefully it will be fixed some day. Content:========Let's talk about the content: The game is short. Maybe it was because we were playing coop and could figure some ♥♥♥♥ out faster this way but we almost did a 100% run in about 8 hours. All we have left is scanning some plants etc.. And i think for a game that 30€ the amount of content is not very much. If we would rush the main story i think we would have had about 4 hours. Should you buy it?==================Both me and my friend are thinking very much alike that a game is worth it when we get as much hours out of it as we pay for it. So if we pay 10€ for game, we want to get about 10 hours out of it so we end up paying like 1€/h. This calculation is not always coming together and in this case here we completed the game with 97% in 8 hours with no real replayability. This is kind of a bugger but its something you can get over with if the game is fun enough. And it is. As i said in the beginning i enjoyed it a lot, though i was a bit skeptical in the first hour of playing. It hooked me. DO NOT ABSOLUTELY NEVER IN A BILLION YEARS buy the game for the full price of 30€. It's not worth it. Buy it on sale - play for about 2 hours and decide if it's a game that suits you. But in my opinion it's not worth more than 15€.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a very well designed and thought out co-op game. The movement is very smooth, the story is okayish, it doesn't really have a narrative depth. The map is decently sized with many unique missions and each new area has something new to explore. The performance is good at the highest options, but you will notice losses in some huge areas with plenty of entities. The playtime may be a bit short (7h without DLC), there are many different types of monsters, many upgrade possibilities with the resources you get from killing mobs and finding secrets or ores, there are many nice areas to discover, i like that you are more or less thrown into the world without much explanation etc. and that you have to discover and test out a lot by yourself with your coop partner but you have some guidance of what direction you have to go, which is good because there are so many different height levels etc.. I can recommend this game and will soon play through the DLC as well and suggest that you try it too!

_childDocuments_.review: Journey to the Savage Planet, is a quality metroidvania and likely the best of it's genera for the year 2021.  The game has a great (but sophomoric) scene of humor, but never pushes it too far.  The exploration is fantastic with a fun and interesting world to explore.  The movement is slightly clunky, and combat is slightly limited but neither problematically so.   My biggest criticism is that a few of the puzzles were really unintutive, and I had to turn to a guide for a solution.  Even after looking them up, one or two really did not give players enough guidance in the game to complete them.   With that all said, I really had fun with Savage Planet and was compelled to finish all of the content.  It is genuinely quirky fun and rewarding, but I cant call it one of the best in it's genera.  I strongly recommend it if you want a first person shooter metroidvania with a crude scene of humor.  If that is not exactly your cup of tea, there are plenty of other Metroidvania's that will likely be a better fit.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty good game. Not a great game, but good. It does look stunning, and the initial gameplay feels great. The intrigue of the story also helps the game. Exploring does feel a bit tedious near the end due to a lack of map and due to you being able to miss objects to scan and due to some things/places being more obscured. The story also has a few glaring plot holes at the end, once you think about it too hard.While this may sound a bit harsh, it is, as I said, a good game. As a collectathon it is never too hard, nor feels the combat incredibly frustrating. It's a pretty interesting one-time ride, but there isn't really any replayability apart from speedrunning this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a game I can recommend. It follows a simple loop of "Explore area to find new tools -> Unlock a different area with the new tools and repeat".In the end it feels more like a collection of mechanics and objectives/chores than a full-fledged game. Individual game mechanics also have very little depth. There is a resource and crafting system which makes very little sense. For critical upgrade materials, you don't collect them as much as they are straight out given to you once you reach a certain point. There are secondary resources which you get by killing creatures, which is just an excuse to include combat as it is boring and provides very little challenge. You can also get them from resource nodes spread throughout each area so you will rarely find yourself missing something.You don't even have a resource inventory and everything is automatically dumped every time you get back to your ship. The only reason to get back to your ship being to "craft" you new upgrades. The way you get back to your ship is via instant travel from the multiple portals spread out over each area. This make the whole ordeal so superficial that they might as well give you the upgrade and trash the whole resource and crafting system. It's not something you are involved in anyway.Same as the combat, the exploration is not at all challenging, and at times it feels like you are just along for the ride instead of in charge of the gameplay. My harsh opinion might very well be caused by the fact that I was personally not invested in the story. The Portal meets Subnautica humour was overall dry and I found myself wanting to silence the game dialogue altogether. By the time the credits rolled I thought to myself "Why did I even bother? Was all that even fun?"

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game, it rewards deep exploration but also makes you focus on getting upgrades at a reasonable pace, each secret was very well crafted, story is also surprisingly interesting, even if it is very campy. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Game is prettyCool aliensMenu music is fun to bop side to sideCons:-Very weird/anti ease-of-life mechanic choicesBroken and short storylineDesync in co-op even though we're on LANAchievements don't unlock correctly for second player in co-opLots of backtrackingPlease note, this is a review with purely co-op gameplay in mind. I wish I could say yes. Bf and I finished this in less than 5 hours first playthrough.. Which for us, is in one sitting. Which, is fine for the £6 we both paid for it (each), however for the asking price, is a joke. I get Shadow Warrior 3 vibes -_-. There are a lot of weird flaws with this game. It works if you're playing it with someone who doesn't really game or is feigning interest, like a partner. But for 2 people who consistently game, it fell a little flat sometimes.Firstly, early game is too linear.. And there are so few quests that you just have one person tagging a long essentially being useless, and feeling useless. If I tried to do any side quests, I'd be met with an ability I don't have yet, that requires the main story progressing. Which will be an objective all the way across the map which bf is working on doing, or roles reversed, and it gets boring just standing around waiting for them to do their bit so that I can then do my bit. It felt like co-op was crowbarred into this and I'm unsure how they managed that. They could have avoided this issue somewhat as well, if they allowed any co-op partner to go back to the ship and deposit all the resources both characters have collected. So that neither of us are waiting around for the other person to find a teleporter back to the ship. It felt like the game was primarily built single player and co-op was crowbarred in with no major afterthoughts.The game itself had a few pointlessly questionable mechanics, that just felt like a way to try and elongate the game. Such-as above and if you leave the game without making your way back to the ship, the game counts it as a 'death' and you have to go out and retrieve your belongings again (luckily not tools, just the last batch of resources you've picked up). On top of this the game has a lot of achievements, one of which is for killing one specific boss in co-op, the irony of this achievement is that, my partner didn't get the unlock for it, only I did. Even though he also killed the boss in co-op.. Having achievements like these again is artificially making the game longer for achievement unlockers and is kind of frustrating and a questionable choice.The endgame in this is alright imo definite improvement to the start of the game, it started to feel somewhat challenging (not so much the end boss fight lol, he ez. But navigating the maps etc), we started being able to do quests separately and had stuff to do and weren't locked behind abilities. Neither of us felt pointless. We had just acquired every tool needed to navigate the maps, all excited to explore. Then we made our way to the last boss, arguably easier than some of the mini bosses.. And the game ended. We noticed that we'd probably unlocked about 1/2 1/3 of the crafting tree. But what was the point of continuing.. The game tries to tell you that 'you can stay here for a bonus if you complete the optional objectives' and that's cool but bonus for what lol. The game is over, there is no point, you killed all incentive by, creating a game that relies on story and making the story a poor mans Subnautica. At least Subnauticas was good and piece meal and the game lasted many more hours..Iunno, I left this feeling like it could have been REALLY cool. It had so many shining points, the environments were cool, the enemy design was cool, the humour was sometimes amusing (albeit sometimes forced. It's not 'Borderlands humour' as someone else stated in the reviews, it's Satisfactory dry humour on steroids.).I think to enjoy this properly, play it with someone who is new to gaming, partner or more ideally, a child. They won't notice the major flaws so much.. But that doesn't and shouldn't excuse them. By addressing the issues and removing some of the weird choices for mechanics, and giving difficulty levels (as there's only 2 and the second adds 'difficulty' in the form of timers. Which. Your game is already short as hell, why force people to not explore - in a game where exploration is honestly at this point it's only major redeeming feature - and time them? Just make enemies more aggressive like most normal devs do).It's not a bad game, just, could be really good but it's missed the nail on too many things that as a result has lead to a mediocre experience, with an insane price tag. For that reason, is a no from me :/ - but don't let that dishearten you - it's still a playable fun (minus the frustrations) game, for a miniscule amount of time.

It's funny to figure out all creatures functions.When you see a creature dangling on two legs with its excessive eyes and hanging mouth, you are not sure whether to attack it or to leave it alone and see what it'll do.Not all creatures are friendly, some are also hostile to even pretty difficult as you progress through the game.To protect yourself from this, you have a weapon that you must 3D print short after the start.This weapon can be upgraded later in the game, you can also upgrade yourself with certain abilities such as double jumping and many others.It is not completely open world, but the freedom is there although the zones have limitations,you will usually have to follow a certain route.Journey To The Savage Planet brings curiosity to the player because most of the things you will see in the game are either cute or funny and unknown at the same time.10/10 sci-fi adventure!The game is also great on a steam deck:

_childDocuments_.review: So, what I expected going in was a fairly standard coop optional survival crafting game. What I got was a relatively short linear adventure game. I beat the main campaign in about 12 hours the first playthrough, but that included a lot of running around aimlessly and trying to figure out how to get some collectibles. Overall, the movement feels good, the shooting is better than you'd expect for a projectile shooting pistol in a game that doesn't completely revolve around shooting mechanics, and the story is relatively basic but interesting if you're willing to go out of your way to read the data entries and hunt out the optional stuff. The art isn't going to blow anybody away but it looks nice enough and has some cool vistas, and the comedy lands just often enough for the over the top satire (if you think about the stuff on TV from the first Robocop movie you're in the right ballpark) to be mostly charming instead of obnoxious like it very well could have been. I also really think the music is excellent, as the main theme lends an energy to combat that would otherwise not be particularly present.I think the game suffers from being pretty small, as the achievement for beating the game in under 4 hours is extremely doable if you vaguely remember where stuff is. It's a barebones game in a lot of ways and very little of the fun is emergent, so a second playthrough is going to feel stale basically immediately. It's also pretty limited in what you can do in combat, with most encounters being trivialized by having the bile throwable that locks enemies in place or the electric fruit that stuns them, if they aren't encounters you can win in a couple shots anyway.The DLC is okay, but if you're expecting a lot out of it you'll be disappointed. It felt about 2/3 the size of any given base game area and didn't have a whole lot new to do, and while the upgrades are nice (especially the infinite stamina) they don't do enough to make me consider trying the game again with them unlocked.Overall I'd recommend the game if you want something to kill a weekend with or to have a fun romp with a buddy in the evening, but not if you want a singleplayer game that you'll be able to stick with for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey To The Savage Planet is an amazing game. It's fun, colorful and humorous. First thing that captured me when I saw the Journey was the graphics. From enemies to environment everything is colorful. Wherever you go there are vivid colors everywhere. The game plays like any open world survival game. You start weak and powerless; as you explore and find new materials, scan enemies and environment, find collectibles you unlock new upgrades. The game offers hours of fun if you are a collectathon fan. I went out of my way to collect everything before finishing the story. There are story missions. Some of them require you to have certain upgrades. When you meet the requirements, you can continue the story and finish your journey. The soundtrack is catchy, I like it. The writing is humorous and deserves a praise. Especially those ads you see when you are in Javelin. I love those hilarious ads, and it's clear to see that they are made by special love and care. Most of the developers don't put interesting things like these ads in their games. After finishing the story, I started the DLC and fell in love with the game again. DLC's starting area Boomerdale looks beautiful. The beach, the sea, puffer birds in the jungle everything is eye pleasing. DLC is pretty short but at least you get some new upgrades. At the end of the day I loved Journey To The Savage Planet. There are lots of generic and boring open world survival games that I forget everything about it after playing it. But Journey is not one of them. It made a special place in my heart with its visual aesthetic and funny writing.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of weird decisions. Lots of unsatisfying platforming, puzzle solutions, and combat, and tons and tons of eagle feathers and health upgrades to pick up over a map where you're punished if you die, but not if you fall off the map. Lots of material grinding in the beginning yet you end with 10x more mats than you'll ever use. Random crap that can kill you in seconds, even though you can shrug off a miniboss for a solid minute just standing still. Died to combat twice, once to the final boss when he did an attack not repeated on my second attempt, and once to the first miniboss before I knew you could use shift to dodge instead of middle-click. Died to fall damage about a dozen times, probably half of which were in one single vertical section. The game starts out as hard as it will ever be and only gets easier as you progress, as many games unfortunately do. This means it starts off as a steep uphill climb where you have to play wisely, and quickly devolves into a collect-a-thon where enemies pose no threat and your biggest enemy is the player controls. Not a game I would have played the first time had I known all this and I won't be playing it again, I'm sure there are people who like this type of game though, but I have no idea why.DLC is one unfathomable decision after the next tbh. Do not even attempt it without every metroid upgrade & health boost, and at least half the crafted upgrades. Whoever tweaked the final settings on the jetpack needs another go at it to be honest. And why do attacks either kill you in seconds or not matter at all, with no in-between?TIPS: 1) Use E on everything, even when it doesn't seem like it would work, then shoot it like 4 times to be sure. Not many things need a bomb. 2) You just hold Alt and let go to use the super jump, no spacebar. 3) Most of the upgrades are near useless, or are actually detrimental, and not worth using materials on. Only the damage and mandatory upgrades are worth it for the most part. 4) Very little combat in the game is actually required, you can waltz right by larger enemies with just a few dents and save yourself probably hours over the course of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Savage Planet is very chilled and relaxed adventure. Common enemies - tiny creatures (mostly chirping birds), aren't a threat to you, they mind own business and attack only if you slap them hard. Which you will, right? Bigger enemies, those guarding story areas and rare bosses, are very static and slow in attacks. You have all advantage and tools. The world is big. Has multiple caves and dozens of floating islands. Each greats you with new animals, equipment and hazards. Overcome these and earn a new upgrade! Then, previously locked doors open sharp with electro punch, grappling hook takes your between locations and acid sack melts obstacles. Don't get over-confident. If you're one jump-charge short - goodbye orange goo. Out of bombs - can't crack them protective shields on a space frog. Safer to return later... or just go on and risk it all! _childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game - seriously.If you like your sci-fi laced with a massive dose of humour then JTTSP is definitely for you. Corny jokes, potty humour, silly and whimsical animations and sounds and garish colours make for a wholesome, satisfying and above all entertaining experience. Common sci-fi tropes from all franchises are blended masterfully and crafted to perfection. If you like the Guardians of the Galaxy type humour, you'll fell right at home here.Yet the game brings a deceptive depth to the table. You're always encouraged to find more of the myriad of secrets hidden throughout the compact but intricate zones. Those hidden items help you level up and craft better items. Platforming takes a front seat, reminiscing of GuildWars' jumping puzzles. I suck at platformers, and I had my fair share of frustrations, but as you upgrade your gear and abilities it gets gradually easier and at the same time more fun. The game mechanics are wonderful, you end up leaping through the air above endless abysses or bubbling lava to get that precious alien goo or alloy with which you can progress further.The monsters are another highlight. Animations are great, the challenges are sizeable but fair. Yes you might die at times and you need to regain your loot from the vicinity, but eventually you get over the hurdle. I'm no good at shooting or dodging, I have slow reaction speed and reflexes, but in the end even I could progress. I can't judge the controls via a controller but with a little reconfiguration I found playing with keyboard and mouse fine.I got this game in a bundle somewhere (Humble or Fanatic, can't remember) and for the €3-4 I paid it's an absolute steal. I'm about 50% done with the main game (got the DLC too) and I play quite slow compared to others at 33h. It's such a blast and I can't wait to see the rest! I haven't tried the co-op mode but I bet it must be even more fun! Get it if you can!

_childDocuments_.review: Please keep in mind, the rating here is as close to "neutral" as it can get, but since I couldn't bring myself to finish this game, I can't really recommend it either.Journey to the Savage Planet is a first-person action-platformer with Metroidvania approach to level design and environmental "puzzles". Oh, and also it's a comedy game. So it has a lot of elements in it, but, unfortunately, it executes none of them well enough to actually make the game as a whole fun.The action consists of just two things (well, not really, but more on that later): your melee kick/slap and a plasma pistol. The latter can be upgraded to have a charged shot and, later, a bounce charged shot, but it doesn't work like you'd think it would: you can only charge your shot once per minute or so, which means that during most combats you can't rely on that, especially since it also takes time that you could otherwise spend shooting and concentration (since you have to hit the button at the right time, or it will fail and lock your pistol for a few seconds) that you should otherwise spend dodging. Oh, and speaking of dodging, there are basically just a couple of enemy types that should be dodged, and both of them are extremely inconsistent with the timing of their attacks and can sometimes, but not always, track your dodges. The rest either die in one hit so you should just be faster than them, or are too slow to not just use normal running.The "puzzles" aren't really puzzles as much as just Metroidvania-type stuff where you need a certain thing to progress past a certain obstacle. Unfortunately, there are multiple problems here, all stemming from very odd game design decisions:1) There is no map. There are no markers. If you've encountered something you couldn't get past, good luck remembering about it several hours later when you finally get the required item.2) Most of the things that allow you to pass the obstacles, except your jetpack and your grapple beam, are thrown consumables, which you have to find and collect to use. This is baffling to me, since there isn't really any sort of challenge there, it's just wasting your time to go and collect some more.3) I guess for some of them the reason is that they can be used as weapons (bombs, acid bombs, electricity fruits), but your basic gun is better for any normal combat (since it's much faster and easier to use), and the only time you'd really want to use them is against enemies who are immune to your gun until you break their defense with one of those, so it's still less of a "weapon" and more of a "thing you need to actually progress".However, even when you have everything you need to get past any puzzle/obstacle, that's when you actually start realizing how annoying and unrewarding exploration really is.I've already mentioned that there is no map. What makes navigation an even bigger problem, however, is that the "levels" start to have more and more confusing layouts as you go on. You start on a sort of hill-ish ice plane with a couple of caves, then move on to a warm area with huge height difference between its parts, and by the end of the game you're navigating a series of floating islands. Even as someone who will defend Xen in Half-Life, this was just too much.Then there's the fact that you really get nothing for actually trying to explore after some point. The gear upgrades have some that you clearly want to get, and some that you just get because there's nothing else left, so you don't really care about getting more resources for those, and the only other thing that you can find (bar some incredibly unfunny text logs) are your health/stamina upgrades, but guess what: way before you collect all 100 of them, your health and stamina hit their caps, so there's really absolutely no point in doing that after I think about 50?Lastly, again, as someone who defends first-person platforming, you have to put extra care into it, and this game doesn't. The precise point I've quit at was when I was faced with a puzzle where I had to charge my jumps to go through a moving gap in the ceiling while the floor below was moving as well... several times in a row... and later the gaps also had lasers in them.But then again, you can play as a dog.

_childDocuments_.review: Review contains minor spoilers / gameplay descriptions.  TLDR at the end.The game starts out by making fun of the overall theme of "exploring an alien planet", explaining why you're there, and why everything is terrible when you start.  Some of the chatter from the computer was cute, others merely "meh".  It's not heavy handed, so for the most part it works.Gameplay-wise, the game is 3/4 platforming/exploration, and 1/4 FPS.  There's some gathering, but it's more get a certain number of Resource A,  B, or C to upgrade your character.  Other than that, there's not any crafting (which is a plus in my book).You're armed with a gun that can be upgraded as you progress, and then some consumables that can also be used either during battle or as you navigate the alien world.  The gun has a certain number of shots per recharge, but otherwise there's not any ammo management to have to consider.As it's part FPS, there are some battles that you need to contend with.  The mechanics of which tend to be fairly easy to suss out as you find them.I really liked the death/respawn mechanic, I felt that it really fit with the overall tone that they're going for.There is also 2-player coop mode, though I haven't tried it yet.Now for some of the more frustrating bits:  I managed to collect a lot of the collectibles, beat the game, etc and it took probably around 8 hours, so not the longest game.You'll eventually be able to craft ways to see the collectibles, though more of a general location.  This unfortunately doesn't really help with a few of them, so I ended up giving up with around 90% completion.  Kudos to the completionists with more patience than I.I didn't really care for the infomercials that you'd eventually unlock and would play in the background of your ship.  Relatively minor, but still somewhat annoying.TLDR:Overall the game is pretty short, but what's there checked most of the appropriate boxes for me.  I definitely recommend, though given the brevity, waiting for a sale/price drop is probably prudent.

_childDocuments_.review: As many others, I'd mark this review neutral.The game looks nice, sound is aight, the beginning gets you hooked.Problem is, the game pretty much never expands. Sure, you get more tools but they don't interact with each other. The green bile you get as a jump pad at the start? No cool interactions - you'll never use it to launch Roundbird into the Meatgrinderflower. The sticky bile is very potent but then, combat is both very easy and very coarse. The dodges don't feel like they work. Actually, why dodge at all if you can just sticky bile your enemy and then spam whatever you need? The puzzles are made for younger gamers. You rarely are shown things that give you this "a-ha! I'll have to come back here later to explore this super cool new place", they're more like "I need red key to access red doors." The new powers don't unlock new mechanics and them being combo'd with old ones. No, they're basically keys.Honestly the best part of the game were the videos. It really felt like some funky student group wanted to show their funny gags but needed a video game to justify publishing them.Also, markers lie to you. Why? Hell if I know.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Exploring has been fun, especially since I didn't do it solo. Might have gotten bored playing solo since there's not really any intelligent NPC interaction. Very funny game. Wonderfully unique world and creatures, as well. Strongly recommend doing the scientific experiments asap as being able to scan for stuff and get the booster upgrades are 100% necessary to find everything and complete some of the challenges (although not for completing the story). Note: you’ll need some of the weapon upgrades to be able to do all the science experiments, so it's a bit circular.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey to the savage planet is such a well conceived game , it has a very simple story and funny with some dark humor but so well achieved and with a great sound track.It is a walking simulator with a bit of action here and there and some exploration enough not to make the game too tedious or hard , the co-op is a must on this game if you play with a friend this game gets a lot more funnier and enjoyable .The only negative side that i saw is that Tycoon Studios no longer exists because of Stadia Gaming closure because othe rthen that it is a very enjoyable game , i give this one a 8.5/10 and hopefully we will get a sequel .

_childDocuments_.review: ” Welcome, explorer!! As the doomed person in our company, we will make you explore this strange planet and give us its latest discoveries.. sooooooooo good luck!!”The game is about exploring a planet far from our solar system, diverse with its creatures and geography. You will find flat, elevated and flying areas as well, and you will always find secret places such as caves and others on every corner of the world. In terms of the world design, it is designed more vertically than horizontally so that each new area is located on a layer above you, and you find yourself jumping, climbing, or even sliding to reach new places and areas. These areas are distinguished by their monsters which are considered rather unique but some of them are repetitive with minor differences (ex.. one is armored and the other explodes). You may encounter some armored monsters that you can only eliminate by using some materials, and these materials can be obtained through the plants around you that may also help you solve some puzzles. Can you gather some resources for crafting?? Unfortunately, no....there is no crafting mode in this game, but there are some resources that you use only to upgrade your abilities.In terms of abilities, the abilities in the game are very simple and useful. All the abilities you get at the beginning of the game help you to reach your goal of climbing, fighting, or solving puzzle. Most of these abilities will unlock with you as you explore the world and finish the main story. You may encounter some "hard-to-reach" places or strange puzzles, but after you unlock a certain ability, you can go back to it and solve it. And FYI, most of the abilities you cannot read about them until you reach the advanced stages of the game (that is why I was somewhat lost when I found a puzzle in front of me and did not understand how to solve it).Also, you -as an explorer- will have a scanner to scan the whole world, and this thing is very interesting and encourages exploration.Unfortunately, with all these advantages, the game is very short. Short in terms of the worlds you discover and the fun you receive in the game. And even in the number of main bosses you are fighting. I finished the game, and I didn't understand that I finished it. As if the developers ended it here due to lack of time. It was very sad. I consider this to be one of the big disadvantages in the game. The other drawback is that there is nothing to do after you finish the game. Except collect some abilities and examine the world around you more. I didn't find anything really important in it or even side missions.... This is very sad...The story in the game is simple and direct that you are trying to discover the world to know if it suitable for humans and trying to fix your own spaceship and through your discoveries you may talk to a scientist and he will guide you to your goal and he may throw some jokes, either directly or through advertisements that may appear in your broken spaceship.As for the music, it is somewhat acceptable, but it was not important, so I started reducing it so that I could talk to my friends. The game does not require much concentration. As for the graphics, they were very impressive. I enjoyed the scenery and the variety of colors in my first moment in the game. The graphics are close to 3D cartoon graphics and this design is very suitable for the game, especially since the game has a strange joke side.- The game does not have a minimap.- The game has a co-op mode. You can play with your companion and listen with him during your trip.This is one of the games that I enjoyed playing and exploring, but unfortunately it was not perfect. It was too short. If you want to buy it, don't buy it at full price.aaaaaaaaaand that it <3

_childDocuments_.review: It’s like a cute version of The Outer Worlds with just a hint of No Man’s Sky mixed with Borderlands humor while emphasizing on one great planet instead of infinite mediocre ones. Or Subnautica without as much water. Somehow the game managed to combine all the things I liked about No Man’s Sky, Outer Wilds and Astroneer in a funnier, lighter and more intriguing package.It's essentially a first person Metroidvania.  I don't think calling it a shooter is really quite fair and it definitely favours platforming, exploration and backtracking over combat. The influences from the Metroid Prime series is unashamedly apparent, and if you liked those games I'd definitely recommend giving it a shot.Journey to the savage planet is exactly what I hoped the outer worlds would be. It really feels like you’re discovering a new planet, and the humor really worked for me. This game scratches an itch I've had for video games of old. The levels of weirdness just for weirdness sakes truly reminds me of early point and click games. The world design is a blast, the creatures are truly something unique to this world, game design is so fun even more so in coop, exploration feels really rewarding. The traversal in this world is so fun and there are so many different ways to go about it. Add in an upgrade system that exists to just give you crazier tools for exploration and involves eating random piles of goo you found on the planet...it just didn't feel like any recent titles I've played. All while you have this tongue in cheek story that doesn't take itself too seriously at all. Yeah, this is a budget Metroid Prime, love it or hate it, it’s good and the closest thing to Metroid Prime out there. Overall I had an absolute blast, blew through it in a weekend with my wife’s boyfriend. It's not overly long like so many titles these days and actually gives you multiple endings which I didn't expect. I'm now achievement hunting because I just want to goof off in the world more while my wife spends time with her boyfriend. They’re so good for each other.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, the game looks amazing as far as overall design and detail goes (minus a few holes in some rocks and models) and I have no complaints about the style or menus that the game uses to portray it's image, it's very well done.My only issue is with the gameplay itself, some minor bugs here and there along with some other larger bugs having to restart the game or mission, as well as movement and item inconsistencies that made it frustrating to play the game at times.I feel if a lot of these are hammered out, as well as balancing out some damage/enemy spawns and adding in other features (personally want to kick the birds around like a beach ball with them not exploding, I think that would be fun) I could revisit this game and finally finish it.Things I didn't like-Purple goo reduces enemy damage taken, making a certain mission more difficult than necessary-Dashing to the side when trying to run forward-Mouse aiming in general-Grapple points randomly disappearing when close enough to grapple or falling-Enemy speed vs character speed (even with dashing, ex. frog using tornado ability)-Credits rolling mid game? (Before rocket, which gives 2 endings so 3 endings? half the game was like 3 hrs)Overall: Could've been a better game for the price

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Great visuals; the environments are detailed and varied, and the semi-cartoonish filter is a nice touch. Feels truly like you're on a (devastated) alien planet.- Good dialogue; the AI who accompanies you is particularly snide and treats you like the meatbag that you are, a character trait that is always prone to the occasional chuckle.- Excellent level design: the world layout does not necessarily make it a walk in the park, and creates a fun platforming experience.Cons:- Repetitive missions: quickly boils down to a series of glorified fetch quests, occasionally throwing in a fairly generic bossfight (shoot glowy things, don't die). Difficult to become invested in the storyline as a result. The side missions (apart for the science missions which add some more amusing tasks) are literally all fetch quests.- Linear combat mechanics: while the platforming elements make exploration of the world fun, the combat feels very samey, and leaves little wiggle room for approaching fights differently each time (don't get me started on the useless stealth mechanic).- Short game life: Finished both the main game and DLC in just over 18 hours.Conclusion:Fun little romp of a game, gets a bit stale after a while but has an addictive "gotta-catch-em-all" vibe to it all the same. I recommend it to any amateur of first-person scifi who enjoy Metroidvania-style games.

_childDocuments_.review: What starts as a fun adventure , turns into an annoying repetitive game, with many flaws.Because of it's broken save system, it forces the player to re-thread the same level and puzzles every time you die. Controls are not precise enough for all the platforming the game requires the player to do, causing a few deaths. And there is a lot of platforming. Combat is very simple, and limited. It's not fun. There are a few boss battles that require to kill the same boss several times, because the game keeps spawning the same enemy.This game doesn't even have cloud saves.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing gem of a game, I don't know how I haven't played it until now. The game starts with you rocketing down to an unknown planet to find out what's going on there, and what you find out is signs of advanced civilization, so on to exploring. And exploring is really the best part of this game, there is a whole open world to traverse, lots of puzzles, secrets, and most of all the local wildlife can be cute, hilarious, or even dangerous. And accompanying this is your trusty ship computer. There is humor everywhere you look at, so it's just a pleasure to play until the end of the story, or even until you manage to collect and document all of the planet, which is actually fun an not a chore. Have still to play the DLC, but hopefully the developers decided to make a sequel one day.

_childDocuments_.review: Savage Planet is a fun romp through a beautiful and very colorful alien planet.  The look and feel of the game is whimsical, verging on goofy.  No difficulty settings or game modes reflects the casual, almost easy gameplay.Playing the game reminds me of Half Life.  Relatively easy progress, until you get to the parkour sections and the Level Bosses.   Then it gets harder for a while.  You will be doing fine, then round a corner and see some gigantic freaking thing!   The Bosses do have their weaknesses, and can be defeated after figuring that out.Very good attention to detail, both in the design of the world, and the game story.  The support characters and voice acting is awesome.This game has been very successful, and deserves more updates, content, and especially the implementation of some very good player-suggestions.Specifically, in my only beef with this game:  We could definitely benefit from a "Peaceful Mode": Enemies attack only when attacked, and especially a way to complete the game without attacking the very cute little critters that are otherwise minding their business.All in all, Savage Planet stands out from the mountain of survival games out there with unique gameplay, art and design, and story.  Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Its pretty fun, even to complete 100%. This game is literally the combination of Subnautica and Hob, both great games. Although I do recommend those 2 more than this one, if you have limited time on your hands and can't play all 3. For some reason, I thought it was gonna be an open world game, which caught me off guard, because its not, but it happens. The map of this game is pretty grand, great variety of nicely built areas. The humour was so ridiculous, I liked it. Now, what I don't like about games like these is how overwhelming the compact nature of the map becomes. There's dozens of places to go to and it becomes extremely confusing at certain points. Also, what awaited at the tower seemed rather insignificant as well, after a build up like that it felt a bit... childish, if the humour of the game is what caused that, then I'd rather have gone without it. Overall a very pleasant experience though.

_childDocuments_.review: Metroid Prime by way of Borderlands. Carries its sense of humor throughout, which made me nervous at first, but the game uses it in moderation and it ended up being charming and funny.They make the (imo) smart move of letting the player explore anywhere, even "out of bounds", without any real invisible walls. It means you can see the rough edges sometimes, but I appreciate the freedom. They even know it - the text on the third bonus-jump upgrade made me laugh. That said - if you're a Boundary Break fan, you can do some OOB exploring of your own, in co-op!Nearly 100%ed it in ~10 hours (minus some scans I'd have to look up). May go back and finish it properly!Overall, worth the time and worth the price! Recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I would say it's good. Not outstanding, but it's alright. Visually it looks fantastic of course. Great art direction, great lighting, and the colors in every location absolutely pop. The controls in general are very tight (with one little exception). If you're looking for a really good SHOOTER game, I would argue that this is probably not the game that will do it for you. It has shooting, and the shooting feels fine, but you only have one gun, and shooting isn't really the focus. This game plays a lot more like a 3D metroidvania platformer.Controls-wise, I really dislike how they've mapped the "charged shot". Your weapon only has a few shots before it has to reload, so if you are like me, you are constantly tapping reload to make sure your clip is full. The problem with that in this game is that, if your clip is full and you tap reload, it activates the "charged shot" QTE where you must tap reload at a precise time to activate the charge shot (they are trying to imitate the Gears Of War thing but it doesn't really fit or feel necessary in this game). But since I am always tapping reload to make sure my very small clip is always full, I often start this sequence by accident, not even caring about the charged shot. This causes me to miss the timing or just ignore the sequence. But if you miss it or ignore it, your guy goes into a "gun jam" animation sequence which stops you from engaging in all kinds of other functions for several seconds, such as using your hookshot. So for example, if you try to quickly reload and hookshot in midair, not realizing your clip is already full, you'll just fall to your death. It's not great. To make this even worse, even if you DO successfully engage and WANT the charge shot, if you then open your scanner or perform a slide, you lose the charge and have to do it over again. Amazing. You might think that you can just remap the button for initiating the charged shot. NOPE. The reload button and charged shot button are always the same key, no matter what you change it to, so it's cursed basically. But ASIDE FROM THIS... the controls are actually very good. The slide feels good. The jump physics feel perfect. Launching up enemies and shooting them in mid-air feels just right. Every other aspect of controls feels 10/10. It's only the charge shot where I feel like a poor decision was made.In general gameplay terms, I enjoy exploring around, trying to find all the alien treasures and orange goos. This gives me the most enjoyment of any part of the game. I wish the game didn't spam floating islands so much, and the exploration is pretty firmly gated once you get your bearings enough to recognize all the obvious gates, but generally the exploring around and treasure hunting is pretty satisfying. Where I like the gameplay a little bit less is that your XP and leveling up (and therefore skill unlocks) often don't have as much to do with discovering new areas, finding treasures, or defeating enemies. XP is instead awarded by completing "research tasks", but this is often really tedious "achievement hunting" type stuff. For example, one task is just to walk up to a specific series of enemies and poke them. You do these 3 at a time. Don't bother poking every enemy you see to check them off as you go. It doesn't count unless the task has been given to you. Similarly, there is another task where you must kick 5 enemies into the air and then shoot them. That's fine. It's a fun thing to do. But even if you've already done this 3,000 times in the game already, none of them counted, because you had not been given the task yet. See what I mean? That's obviously annoying. So while you want to get out there and explore and make progress, the game will make you piss around with filler like this to a certain extent.I guess overall I'd sayVisuals: 10/10Controls 9/10  (that charged shot mechanism is the WORST)Exploration 7/10"Tasks"  6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, just completed it 100% blind and for the most part it was really enjoyable. I love the atmosphere, art style and most parts of the humor. The movement feels nice, especially after getting all the upgrades, and all the collectibles fill my completionist hard with joy. But one thing that really bothers me is the combat against certain enemies, some attacks feel impossible to doge even with the side step. Only way to deal with them without getting frustated is stunning or sticking them. But overall this is one of my favorite games recently.And when I really like a game I usually want more of it. But this game shows me that there are exceptions to this...The DLC "Hot Garbage" has a quite fitting name. It's not necessarily bad, but it feels completely pointless. It doesn't add to the story, none of its secrets are, well, secret, and the combat gets even more frustating because the few new enemies have insane accuracy and actually deal decent damage. The new upgrades in the DLC are also almost entirely useless, especially in the main game. The healing buff is nice but only really matters against the new DLC enemies, the gas mask doesn't even protect you from the blight bombs and only works in a certain area of the DLC and the infinite stam is also practically useless, because the enemies in the DLC deal so much damage that you need an upgraded character, but an upgraded character has so much stamina you can't run out on accident. Would've preferred a running speed upgrade. And don't get me started on the ocean, it shuts off all you movement and you have to very slowly walk across the sea floor. That would be okay if you weren't supposed to go into the ocean in the first place, but it got quite a few scanables for the Kindex as well as collectable post cards....So, overall a great game but didn't like the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a lot of fun with this so far at 8 hours, I've collected maybe 80% of everything and beaten the final boss. The gameplay loop feels really good with a few different resources you need to collect to upgrade and progress. I rarely felt like I was going out of my way to collect extra because the map design does a good job of funneling you to upgrades and the portals are spaced fairly well for going back and forth as you unlock more areas.Combat isn't much of a thing which I think is perfect for this game. The platforming is simple but refined.The dialogue from E.K.O is wonderful and I only wish I could interact with them more.As with all games there are some things that could be changed or improved or removed but I feel like the experience Journey to the Savage Planet has given me is a very good one, so I'm not going to bog that experience don't by complaining about how it got boring after watching the orange goo animation for the 50th time.I had a good time and I think this is a good, low difficulty and fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: A short fun planet exploration. This game is bird brain silly and stupid. Went to all areas with almost 100% completion and went back to clean it up for that 100%. I cannot express how few flaws i found with this game. (Played Coop btw) We encountered very few bugs. A few non important creature(s) spawned in the geometry, a parkour section that wouldn't reset properly in multiplayer, and a bad terrain spawn in the final area with a 3 scan crate which was the only game breaking bug that could lock your game up but in coop we were able to find a work around which was just warping out. If i had to guess you could just quit the game in single player. The environment was diverse and explosive with color, upgrades though few were all impactful (literally and figuratively), dialogue for this game is top tier. The dialogue is a refresher and it sounds and reminds me of the silly intrusive thoughts of GLADOS with a sprinkle of friendly lethal sarcasm. Did not play the DLC but having just finished the base game it does peak my interest. This is a game to play with a friend and i cannot stress this enough, the coop is a QOL many coop games should have. It's mind bogalling why more games don't have this seemless coop style where you dont need to be joined at the hip to do everything but caaaaan be joined at the hip. You don't need to be good at FPS games either, just semi attentive and looking around and NOT PANICKING WHEN THINGS RUN AT YOU! If you are on the fence, know this; its about 6-8 hours of fun and if you can get it on sale, do it, its a cheery game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the weird combination of a sci-fi, open-world, metroidvania, platforming, FPS, comedy game. With a genre like that, I just had to try it out. The core elements are strong here with fun movement options and a vibrant world, but a lot of things in this game are  for me to like it. The combat is fun, but just complex enough so that I never got bored. The enemies are varied, but just enough so that I had to change up my approach a few times. The humor is a bit annoying, but just enough jokes landed for me to be okay with it.I see a lot of people take issue with the game's length, but I think it was running low on steam towards the end and being longer would've hurt it. JttSP isn't the best metroidvania I've ever played, but it's got just enough going on for me that I enjoyed it plenty. I mean I even thought it was worth it to 100% the game, so that's got to count for something. Also, I played this game alone but I can tell it makes a killer co-op game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played in 4k on a 4080 & Intel 13700KF processor with all current drivers and patches manually installed on Windows 11 x64. All options were set to their highest level except AA and blur.I own all the DLC and played through it as well.I played with an XBox One X controller and sometimes a keyboard and mouse and both worked equally well.I will update this review if I continue to play and have more to add and will leave comments on.PROS:- It felt like someone mashed up a smaller-scale Fallout 4 with a Metroidvania game; it has similar adventuring and exploration with a veneer of that "shady corporate comedy".- The music was completely appropriate and fit the world. It was nothing I'd listen to outside the game though.- Fun voice acting, great goofy video segments, and some legitimate solid comedy.- It ran very well the entire time I played it. Very little in the way of hitching, and very quick load times.- Achievements!- The big sell to me way the moment-to-moment gameplay. I really enjoyed moving around in the environments and all of the mechanics didn't get to be too much as happens often with Metroidvania games. From beginning to end I was having a darn good time. It's a "smooth" game experience that I stayed up way too late a few nights in a row to get through because I couldn't wait to see what came next.- Zero bugs experienced that I noticed.NEUTRAL:- There's a passable through-line story in the game that was fun to get through, but it could have been told better.- Some people may find the game easy, but I'd prefer to have fun the whole time instead of banging my head on a wall over and over again. If that's you, just jack up the difficulty when you start.CONS:- I want more of it and there isn't any more. Hopefully a sequel? The DLC was a little short given the price and didn't add a ton.DID YOU FINISH THE GAME?:Yup! And the DLC.CONCLUSION:While it won't stick with me for years, it was great while it lasted and I would 100% play more in the series. If you enjoy exploration, play this.
