_childDocuments_.review: This comes as a difficult decision to make.  I absolutely love the artistic style, the humor, and the general feel for the game.  Even though I abhor platformers (jumpy puzzles, as I call them), mostly because I lack the coordination to pull off the skill in most games, I found the platforming requirements of this game to be intuitive and easy to execute.  I really want to like this game. However, after four hours, I'm uninstalling.  Why? Game (not artistic) design is the answer.  There are two main issues with the game design:1) no map of any kind.  With exploration as its theme, I can understand not immediately providing a map to players.  However, as players explore and open up the world (literally), there should be a way for them to track their presence in that world.  It's a common component of modern game design, and its absence in Journey to the Savage Planet is jarring.  2)  Boredom in quests.  Every quest is "You can't proceed until you find an upgrade.  Go find the upgrade.  Then return here (without a map) and we'll grant you your upgrade."  Got a little too repetitive for my tastes. Long story short - if this game is on a deep sale and my two complaints don't bother you, then go for it!  You'll love the artistry and humor.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Does what it says on the tin. It's nothing amazing but there are very few flaws. You might notice some odd terrain or the occasional collision which causes you to get stuck, but every time I managed to get myself unstuck pretty quickly. There are a few bosses but their difficulty is not particularly hard. If you have half a brain (like me) you can do them in a try or 2. There are some trap encounters which are harder than the bosses.It's borrows some metroidvania elements in the bosses and the equipment you unlock as you go unlocks other areas, but mostly for collectables. There's no sprawling world here, it's mostly linear.The world is quite pretty and interesting to explore. Exploring the environments and finding all creatures (and collectables) are really what makes this game interesting. There's so much to collect, this game may as well be called a collect-a-thon first and an action-adventure second.The writing is serviceable. It's really just there as an excuse for the game to exist. _childDocuments_.review: (JTSP) is a single-player and co-op first person metroidvania centered around open-world exploration and questing. Set in a relatively close future where space exploration is at its apex, this title will have players impersonate one of the many explorers employed by Kindred Areospace. Sent to an unknown planet, players will have to craft, fight and platform their way to success or die trying.🟩 🟥 🎮 Gameplay is divided into Exploration, Combat and Crafting.Is the main activity, and is performed using a variety of tools such as double-jump modules, plasma grappling hooks and several indigenous plants with unique effects, like spawning jump pads on-demand. The planet is actually an ensemble of fragments floating in space, each with a different biome housing its own "set" of creatures. The same animal may have multiple variations based on the zone it grows in, each with unique abilities or more powerful attacks. The useful scanner tool is invaluable to find secret paths, get info on the local wildlife and even solve some puzzles.There are a LOT of secret areas hidden everywhere, most of them only accessible later on when the correct upgrade is gained (though some can be "cheesed" with clever jumping tricks). Scanning new plants, animals or minerals may unlock new recipes in your spaceship, so it's a fundamental thing to do. The fact most collectibles actually are useful for gameplay and not just meaningless tokens makes it worthwhile to look for them. Teleport shrines are scattered in the world, allowing fast travel once unlocked.Plays out in FPS fashion, using a plasma pistol as primary means of offense, though also a melee attack is available and useful to dispatch the weakest creatures. Side-dodging is also a function with low cooldown, useful to avoid fast frontal attacks or bullets when the need arises. Ammunition is unlimited, however the gun needs to be reloaded once in a while, and can also use a special "supercharged" attack requiring a precise quick-time event to unleash it. Death means respawning at the ship, and having to gather all resources on the death location (dark souls style). Unless a specific mode is selected, lives are unlimited.Is performed with the 3D Printer present in the spaceship acting as base of operations. Materials gathered while outside are deposited each time one teleports back to the ship, and used when needed. Most recipes are locked at first, either behind story-related progression or side quests and challenges, requiring players to accomplish specific feats each time. While most upgrades are not mission-critical, they surely help a lot against the increasingly difficult navigation, enemies and bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: ---{ Story }---It's interesting enough, you're a pioneer stranded on an alien planet, and the company you work for didn't plan for your return, so you have to explore the mildly dangerous habitat in order to gather the resources you need to get home. Also Aliens. ---{ Gameplay }---Mostly platforming, and a bit of shooting. The platforming is imprecise at best, mostly because there's no way to tell when you can/can't grab onto a ledge. The way a grapple should work is, if you're in range and facing the grapple point, you can grapple. Not in this game. Sometimes it works, sometimes you fall and have to start a tedious climb all over again. Or die. The shooting is inaccurate, and the most dangerous monsters are immune, except for tiny, moving, weak spots. So... that obviously wasn't thought out very well. Even if you trap them in goo, the weak spot moves around a lot, so you're just spamming bullets until you're lucky enough to land a shot. Oh and sometimes, as if that weren't enough, their weakpoint is on their back/tail, but despite being stuck in goop, they rotate so they're always facing you... that's either a bug or brainless game design. Also their attacks can just reach you anywhere. As in, an enemy will anti-grav up a tree just to hit you. The dodge mechanic seems pretty useless. The enemies you have to dodge seem to lock on to you, and are much faster than you, so.... what's the point?There's no map. For a game based heavily around exploration, this seems like a huge oversight. You constantly come across puzzles you don't have the equipment to solve yet, good luck finding/remembering all of them without a map or waypoints. EDIT: This is made a bit easier later once you unlock radar abilities for the collectables.---{ Graphics }---Absolutely beautiful. Nice vibrant colour palette. World design is cool and trippy. ---{ Audio }---The music is awesome but there really isn't much of it. Shame that. ---{ Difficulty }---Not hard, just hard to play. ---{ Grind }---Lots of collectables, otherwise not really. ---{ Bugs }---There's no pause function. In 2023. ---{ PC Requirements }---Max settings on an i5-9600K and an RTX 2070 = constant 60fps.---{ 4 / 10 }---It's only challenging because of bad design. This is the gaming embodiment of a turd rolled in glitter.

_childDocuments_.review: So I promised myself that I would start writing more reviews, as only every doing technical manuals on a daily basis makes my teeth hurt. So here we are.Journey To The Savage Planet is predominantly an exploration game, where you traverse a series of floating islands to catalogue the alien species, refuel your spacecraft, and eventually get back home. It's almost like a reverse Subnautica in a way; you're actually supposed to be on the planet, you move up instead of down, and there is no base building.Exploration works well. There are four main areas to explore, each with a number of fast-travel points and loads of collectables, some in plain sight, some hidden, and some totally inaccessible to you until you get the right upgrade. This system is a bit Zelda-y, in the sense that in order to progress to later areas you need to obtain something that provides you with some form of mobility, like a grappling hook, or a door breaker. The game looks nice enough, with very bright colours that remind me of Sanctum 2.JttSP deliberately styles itself as a comedy game, and I'd say about 3/4 of it works. There are some genuinely funny moments that I won't spoil, however it does fall flat on the moments where the joke is basically "this is a video game". The adverts, though, are really funny, and provide a reason to go back to base besides just dumping all the resources you collected.There are some issues with the game. The charge shot is basically useless except for winning a handful of optional objectives, as most enemies can only be damaged if you hit their weakspot. And if you miss the charging QTE, then you spend a few precious seconds whacking away at your gun while all the time a dog is trying to chew your face off. Enemies in general are hard to fight, and there needs to be some kind of indicator when you're low on health as the health bar is tucked away in a corner.This is less of an issue, more feedback, but it would be very helpful if we could have some sort of indicator that shows how many of each collectable remain in each region. I got bored of zipping around the world in my last couple of hours trying to figure out where the last few collectables were, and given some of these contain the actual story, Overall, Journey To The Savage Planet is a burger game, by which I mean it doesn't really do anything that new, but pretty much everything that it does do, it does well - and that's totally fine by me. If you like exploration games, then you'll most likely enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst charming, the game ends up falling a bit short in terms of interesting gameplay. Writing is okay, not amazingly clever but its light-hearted and funny at times. It is supposedly about exploration, but in reality you just follow a dotted line with the game holding your hand as to where to go essentially all the time. The sensation of actual exploration is simply not there.Co-Op is written well into the game, but the writing is about all that's good about it. It's just now 2 people going down the exact same path doing the exact same thing. It doesn't create new and interesting gameplay that wouldn't be there otherwise, other than 2 people going off and collecting stuff in different locations (but at that point, what's the point of co-op?)Overall, if you want something that uses humor and pretty visuals to keep you interested, this might be for you. Sadly, it wasn't for me, it was all too surface level for me to really sink my teeth into it, the exploration was incredibly lacking, and it just became a game I finished the main story of over a couple of short sessions.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this in my wishlist for quite awhile but was skeptical I would actually like it. I'm glad I finally picked it up, especially on sale at $12 for the base + Hot Garbage DLC. This is a very light, entertaining game that combines light exploration & resource gathering mechanics with Doom-like movement mechanics but very light combat. There's really only one enemy type that's challenging throughout the game and aside from the few boss events everything else is a breeze. The gameplay is supported by an entertaining narrative of your character being a corporate owned explorer, one among countless others, that lands on what was expected to be an uninhabited planet. Narrative is delivered through a combination of email messages, video transmissions from your company owner, and dialogue from your AI assistant. Humor underlines all these interactions and the videos and video advertising you receive in your ship adds a sense of connection back to the rest of the very consumer oriented world you left behind. Progress is continuous. Game doesn't really ever get to the point it feels grindy unless you pursue a 100% completionist attitude. In about 21 hours I got about 90% - 100% of most of the objectives and the DLC I completed within a 8 hours or less. Problems I had:Crashes. I experienced about 6 or more of these in my less than 21 hours of gameplay. This is on a 1080 Ti, Windows 10, 10850k, 64 GB RAM, NVME. Nothing preceded the crashes and the game ran very smoothly and looked very good the entire time. Game has no real manual save feature but the autosave seems to be robust enough for what you are doing. Getting stuck in the environment. In the base game I had this happen maybe 2 -3 times, in the DLC twice as much despite being half the size. Extremely annoying. Character would just get stuck in place, apparently to nothing and I could not move. Jets, jumping, explosions, nothing would fix it. Sometimes an enemy would attack and then I would be free. The pistol overcharge mechanic is clunky and looking at comments on youtube more than a few people didn't understand it nor was it explained in the game. Your pistol has 3 additional overcharge capabilities with upgrade. However, its so slow and clunky its more of a novelty than an actual utility in combat. First you have to reload your pistol, then you hit reload again, then you must hit reload while within a small colored area in a gauge that comes up, each subsequent capability requires you to hit reload again with a smaller and smaller area to hit in and if you miss time any of these then there is a minute long cooldown before you can try again. This only gives you one shot. Its cool but just isn't usually worth it and the enemies you would want to use it on can often just deflect the attack making it pointless. I would be really interested in further Savage Planet DLC or a sequel. Ideally something a little bit bigger and with more video narrative / interactive content. Perhaps something that explores your findings a bit more deeper?

_childDocuments_.review: Is a wild ride through a wacky alien zoo, and I mean that in the best way possible. It's a PvE adventure, so you can blast those bizarre creatures without any pesky player drama. The enemies are challenging enough to keep you on your toes, but not so punishing that you want to throw your controller across the room.This game is all about exploration and discovery. You'll be crawling through caves, grappling up mountains, and uncovering the secrets of a strange, vibrant alien world. There are tons of weird and wonderful creatures to encounter, both plant and animal (or at least we hope they're animals...).  Just be prepared for some seriously strange sights!Now, let's talk about your AI companion. They're basically your sarcastic space guide, constantly throwing shade and snarky remarks your way. Let's just say their bedside manner needs some work, but hey, that's half the fun!  Plus, the game fully supports controllers, so you can explore this wacky world in comfort.As a huge sci-fi fan, I absolutely loved Journey to the Savage Planet. It's got that perfect blend of humor, adventure, and exploration that just scratches that sci-fi itch.Here's the only real downside: Completionist gamers beware! You can't unlock all the achievements without buying the DLC.  While I didn't grab the DLC myself, the core game still offers a ton of content to keep you busy.So, if you're looking for a hilarious, adventurous, and surprisingly charming sci-fi romp, Journey to the Savage Planet is a must-play. Just be prepared to develop a love-hate relationship with your AI companion, and maybe a little FOMO (fear of missing out) on those completionist achievements.

It's casual, you are butt of the joke sometimes, sometimes it's situational humor. There are a number of games with corporate silly overlords humor, Portal for example, and in some cases it works, but in others not so much. Here it was done pretty well and it doesn't overwhelm you with forced corpo jokes. It's satirical just enough.Even better, I didn't know, but a sequel is coming in 2025, so that's great. _childDocuments_.review: Solid metroidvania style exploration FPS. You're dropped on a weird alien world and have to explore it to repair and refuel your ship. There's lots of weird aliens to investigate (and shoot). As you progress you unlock more abilities which let you access new areas. The world is very pretty and very colorful. The aliens are mostly harmless with a few slightly dangerous ones. Lots of collectibles to go around and collect, with a bonus that they also power you up. There's an AI that leads you along and makes silly tongue in cheek jokes, ala claptrap. The writing is good enough that its not too annoying and most dialogue is pretty short. Some tips I wish I had known:- Don't neglect the explorer side quests. Increasing your explorer level unlocks more upgrades.- Scan everything. There are some puzzles that use scanning.- Later on you can unlock scanning that shows you where collectibles are.

This game  a First Person Shooter  like a Call of Duty, a Halo or Deep Rock Galactic.Journey to a Savage Planet is a  game where you mainly run around, try to reach areas with your jump abilities, explore interesting environments, search for secrets and be amused(or not) by the jokes the Developers put in. There is  combat in this game like small enemies or bosses, but the  game is about I personally enjoyed my time with it  and I plan on beating it again on PC where I will play the DLC too. I did like that it is not a FPS first since there are far too many of those already around. In Journey to the Savage Planet all you get is  Pistol, that can get some upgrades like a Charge Shot among other upgrades like a double jump.If what you search is a relaxing, laid back Action Adventure where you can run around a pretty Nintendo-like world then I would give this one here a shot. It is very similar to the Metroid Prime games in the sense that you can Scan the environment and find allot Secrets. But it has less Combat and weapon variety then the Metroid Prime games. _childDocuments_.review: My specs;CPU: Intel Core i7 10750HRAM: 16 GB GPU: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 Ti 6 GB How does it runRuns well with a consistently high frame rate and zero stuttering. GraphicsJourney to the Savage Planet places you on the vibrant alien rogue-planet of ARY-26, a jumbled mass of floating island precariously held together by otherworldly technologies. Each nook and cranny of these floating islands has been lovely crafted with an immense attention to detail, opening up for great and organic opportunities for exploration leaving you with a real sense of accomplishment when you find a secret area hidden just out of view. This care is also afforded to all the funa and flora you're tasked with documenting. Both the alien creatures and strange plants that call ARY-26 home are creative in terms of appearance and how the move/interact with the world at large - there were times I'd just stand and watch what these strange beings were up to, and how they went about their day. There aren't a great deal of graphical options for you to play with, but so long as you have a strong enough rig, you'll be delighted with the sights you'll see. The game also hosts a library of live-action videos (don't worry, these aren't the C&C cheese of yesteryear) that range from in-universe ads - all with a satirical, anti-corporate slant - and direct messages from the CEO of Kindred Aerospace, your employer, Martin Tweed (played by Adrian Bishop) that play just like the boring corporate videos that some of us are forced to watch on our first day on the job. Music, Sound, VoiceThe music here is used far too conservatively for my taste, used mainly as audio cues that play at the end of a fight or once you've discovered a secret. The voice acting is top-notch, from the noises produced by the locals to the voice of you AI companion EKO (played by Kendall Savage) who accompanies you throughout your journey and offers colourful commentary based on where you are and what you're doing, all with attitude of someone who thinks, no who knows, they're better than you in every way. Moment-to-moment gameplayDuring your time on ARY-26 you'll be scanning the local funa and flora, exploring the floating island in search for all manner of minerals and materials to understand just what is going on as well as to upgrade your equipment so you can explore more and more of the island. The exploration espouses a metroidvania approach, meaning you'll come across things you know you need but lack the necessary tools to get it. You'll have to come back once you're better equipped.Combat can be deceptively challenging where situations can quickly become out of hand if your not using all the tools at your disposal, still once the everything but you stops moving, and you get the appropriate audio cue to tell you that yes, everything around you is now dead, you'll feel like a real resourceful little explorer.Journey to the Savage Planet is a one of the most enjoyable experiences I've had exploring an alien world at I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys exploration based games like No Man's Sky or Subnautrica.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun.The story part of the game has relatively easy platforming, gradually building up the challenge level as the player progresses. That also goes for the story bosses, where most of the challenge is figuring out their moveset.All the difficult and interesting platforming parts of the game are concentrated around the collectibles, orange goop that usually serves as a reward for exploring/some advanced platforming and give health/sprint stamina, metal balls you can use to upgrade your equipment usually locked behind a puzzle/bossfight (this is where the actually difficult bossfights are), and a couple more spoilery collectibles locked behind even harder platforming sections. The environment and the first consumable can also be heavily utilised to get to places slightly earlier than the developers intended, though you probably won't break the story doing this.The enemies range from annoyances to real threats, for flying ones the biggest dificulty is trying to use the danger chevrons to pinpoint their position, but as you get good at the game the biggest annoyance is enemies where you have to wait before you can attack them.Otherwise the world design is pretty fun, the creatures are akin to something found in Ratchet&Clank, while the stages resemble something out of Jak&Daxter.Story 6/10, not gonna weight it too much because this is a platformerLevel design 9/10, relied a bit too much on the grapple mechanic from the midgame.Collectibles 8/10, they are there, there are a lot of them, they aren't that useful and a bit too many of them are locked behind late game abilitiesEnemies 7/10, a lot of them are a bit too annoying to deal with, especially those who are only vulnerable after an attack.Progression 7/10. You get upgrades, they open up new opportunities, some of the tasks required to get optional upgrades are a bit too reliant on herding a lot of enemies together though.Overall 8.5/10, good game, worth the price

_childDocuments_.review: It's nice, but I don't think it's worth more than half of its already 40% discounted price. Really short, fairly linear exploration game. Past shoving 60 scoops of orange goop in your face it's pointless to look for them, since they don't increase your health/stamina nor even give satisfying popups. Same with other collectibles.Played with a friend, got about 80% of collectibles in base game and 40-50% in DLC in about 6 hours total + breaks with the game running. As well as nearly all the upgrades. Not that the rest of collectibles were hard to find, just wasn't anything to gain in looking for them at that point.First location in the game is great to explore. Second is mediocre. Third is pretty good. Final stretch is meh, but the boss is okay. Didn't like the DLC location at all. It reminded me of Borderland's 2 Doctor Zed DLC, except the local Claptrap wouldn't shut up about your oily fingers the whole time.Monologues from the AI throughout the game were nice to listen to as background noise and the ads on the ship were nice, but I don't see them as a selling point. This is more of a platformer with very simple puzzles that are fun to do at first, while you still think they get more complex. But they don't evolve at all later on once you get the upgrades that remove the restrictions from your tools. In the first area you could blow up a wall with goop behind it if you get a bomb seed and can throw it before its 5 second fuse expires. But later on you just pull out that same bomb seed with no restrictions and blow up the wall blocking your path and that's collectible done.Third area is probably the most fun due to story relevant challenges that freshen up the experience, but those aren't very common.Combat is not worth talking about much, using your tools will make it so you'll breeze relatively easily through most enemies. Charged shot on the pistol is completely useless, though. There are 3 levels of charge, and you have to charge from 0 to 1, from 1 to 2 and from 2 to 3. The effects on it are cool, but the whole mechanic just doesn't function with the game's monsters at all. Most enemies that live long enough for you to care to charge up only die when their weakpoints are hit. And it's way more convenient to hit them with regular spam fire, since a charged shot will often times just bounce away and only hit the single spot it was fired at.Same with bosses. You could spend a few second overcharging and nailing a shot on a boss's weakspot, but breaking it like that wouldn't do more damage than just spamming regular shots that are way harder to miss and don't take half a minute to cool down.Might be a regional pricing thing, but it's absolutely not worth the price for this amount of content compared to most other games. If it actually was half its current discounted price, this review would be positive.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really not sure if this game is wroth a rec' at the moment.While it and its DLC are rather short and the exploration extremely linear, it is still a pretty fun experience IF the humor works for you.I bought this game with a friend and we casually played through the game and its DLC in less than 6 hours - we have about 80% of the collectibles in both the main game and the DLC.I'd say the game would take a solo player about 8 to 10 hours to get done to the same point at the most.The short duration of the game is it's Achilles' heel.Usually short games like this can kind of bet on the replay-ability. Unless you want to speed run this game, there really is no reason to go right back in for seconds, or come back to it to replay the same content a second time. A potential fix for the short duration of this game would be a randomizer-function or a map/planet creator to be used by the community to increase the content the game has to offer.I'm rather curious where the devs want to take this game in the future. More, maybe cheaper or even free, DLCs? More storylines built into the main game? A general price cut to the price? The game as it would stand at the moment - 30 euro for the main game and an additional  8 for the DLC - is really not worth it.Even the current promo price tag of 18 bux for the main game or 20.5 bux for the deluxe edition are a big stretch if you ask me. IF you could get the main game for, let's say, 13 and the DLC for an additional 4 bux it would be a very solid recommendation as it would give very casual solo players entertainment for two to three days.All of that being said, I just can't really recommend this game right now but I really do not want to shy people away from it, as the game itself is well done and it was a fun experience. I wish Valve would give me a neutral option here.Graphics are pretty neat, I really enjoyed the look of this game, however, I really wish it would have a FOV-slider, the stock setting was really not ideal for me and it took about half an hour to get used to. The gameplay is rather engaging for an exploration game once you get the first few suite- and staminaupgrades and feels decently well done.It mostly consists of running or teleporting from A to B with a bunch of platforming thrown in.Platforming in this game is mostly very well done. The only issue i personally have is the charged jump because using it for anything than the ledges that specifically ask for it feels very odd and flow breaking.It even has some bigger swing and grind sections that feel really really well done. When they worked as intended they felt so good that I wished for more of them. The combat is mediocre, and so are the boss fights. The combat in the game consists of shooting, slapping and dodging and looks as follows:You either shoot/slap an enemy and it dies.You throw something at an enemy and then shoot it and it dies.Or you have to shoot a specific are on the enemy and it dies.I don't really feel like the game should be judged on its combat system however, as the main activity is exploration and puzzle solving. The game feels rather well polished and mechanically complete.The only big issue I had gameplay wise was during the more sophisticated swing/slide sections. Sometimes the prompt for the hook just would not show up and I feel to my death. Or I flew over most of a rail and grabbed to the wrong side of it and got flung in the wrong direction, however there are not a whole lot of these sections in the game. Other than small things like that, the only big bug we encountered was a game freeze after a respawn - I died and respawned, the game still ran perfectly fine, I heard the dialogs but I just could not move or do anything. The only fix was to alt + F4 the game and start it again. The humor overall is rather dark and sarcastic. It has a lot of pop-culture references and "parodies" in a way and is a pretty big part of the experience. The Soundtrack of the game is also really well done. I'd grab the soundtrack of this game in a heartbeat if it were available for sale on steam.It really reminds me of Borderlands when it comes to the comedy.Sadly the dialog can repeat the exact same thing over and over if you run out of and back into certain areas. It also kind of falls apart in a coop game where both players split up and decided to explore different things. The dialog basically walks you through the game and gives you hints on what to do. We had a few times were we got confused which dialog was meant for which player because both of us heard everything. Us playing coop and running around rather split up was also the main trigger for double and triple dialog triggers. Solo players will not run into most of these issues at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun first-person shooter, mixed with platforming, exploration, and collectable hunting.  Or maybe it's a platformer mixed with first-person shooting, collectable hunting and exploration.  Something like that.  Overview of Gameplay:  Your ship has crash-landed on the planet you were sent to survey.  The planet turns out to be a bit different than what you were expecting, so your boss tells you to scan EVERYTHING before you even consider returning home.  You'll encounter a lot of strange creatures out there, about ninety percent of which want to eat your face.  When you kill these, they'll drop a small shower of resources In a Doom: Eternal style.  There is only one gun that you'll use for combat throughout the game, but you'll find items all over the planet that can be used to upgrade it.  There are other collectables that will upgrade your health as well.Eventually, you will have found all of the fuel and materials needed to repair your ship and return home.  However, you should probably take the time to get 100% on all scans before you do this, just so you'll get the 'good' ending.Plus, as you progress, you're treated to obnoxious little television ads, which the developers obviously put a lot of thought into.I'd give this game a 10/10 (Would blow up adorable Pufferbird again).P.S. At a glance, this may look like it was procedurally generated like No Man's Sky, but it's actually not.  Doesn't take anything away from the experience, though.

_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: The game is exactly what you expect. An exploration focused game, with some silly aliens and a bunch of collectables. You get different abilities throughout the game that let you explore more and more.The humor is very corny and kind of anti-corporate, but it's tolerable enough. The storyline is nothing new either, but wasn't offensive or anything.Mechanically it's solid, and the co-op works very well. No bugs, de-sync issues, or anything of the sort. Very good game to play with a buddy.If less than $10 and you like exploring games, especially co-op, pick it up. I just about 100% explored it in the 10 hours on my save.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Let's keep this one short and simpel.This game completely blew me away. It is exactly the right kind of exploration, with a very, very well designed planet to explore and many upgrades and collectables to chase after. It has humor that isn't out of place, the world itself is beatiful and well crafted and the movement mechanics feel smooth and work very well in tandom with eachother.I usually go on and on in my reviews, comparing both negative and positive aspects of a game to then come to a conclusion. But, well... there isn't much to dislike here. If you want to play a fun exploration adventure with a little bit of combat sprinkled in, go for it. This title easily deserves my recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: I had a really fun time with Journey to the Savage Planet and I do recommend it! This is a first person Metroidvania with a focus on 3d platforming and environmental puzzle solving. This is a big time collect-a-thon. I really liked the heavy exploration in this game. The game world is big and vertical and takes some time to not just figure out where to go, but how to get there and actually perform some of the challenging traversal. There were quite a few leaps of faith taken trying to get places. And the gambles didn't always pay off, but it was always fun trying. There is a ton of stuff to collect. Even later in the game, where the items are marked in the game world in real time, it's still challenging to find the secret way to get access to them. The game took about 16 hours to complete the main campaign and Hot Garbage DLC while collecting around 90% of all the items. The final boss kinda sneaked up on me. I didn't realize that was the end. This kind of game feels like it should be longer. The game world is the star of the show here. The world is populated with huge buildings and vegetation that dwarf the player and give a lot of places to explore and make the player have to figure out how to navigate their way around. There are so many nooks and crannies; it's easy to miss things if not paying close attention to the environment. The graphics in this game are really beautiful and the game is just really nice to look at. There is a lot of humor to the game. This game is in the same vein as games like Borderlands and Outer Worlds. Certainly not all the jokes land, but enough do that I did enjoy the humor of the game overall. Some of it seemed played out, though. The Hot Garbage DLC was just ok. It offers only a little variety from the main quest, but it's basically more of the same only not as good. Hot Garbage includes sections with limited flying and the ability is recharged flying through rings in the air. I did not have fun with this. The learning curve was annoying and it just wasn't fun to complete the flying sections. I definitely recommend Journey to the Savage Planet. The 3D platforming is really on point and there is a lot to like about this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. Short experience, but its filled with great exploration, fun puzzles, unique and interesting creatures, and plenty of humor. Feels like and "old-school" game that's been modernized. You explore the world using items you find in the environment and crafted upgrades. There isn't a huge emphasis on combat, but the combat there is is fun and simple. The game is funny, colorful, and incredibly endearing, and is easily one of my new favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: I really can't say enough good things about this game. Sure, it's not the hardest game ever, although you will die here and there, but that's not the point. If you're the type that enjoys wandering and exploring, this game will be right up your alley. There's a lot of different collectibles and things to find/scan, and this game does it in a way that makes the exploration fun and doesn't get old looking for the items you're missing. On top of that, the environments are seriously fantastic. I find myself just stopping to look around sometimes because it just looks so good and everything from the biomes to the monsters feels unique. One of my favorite parts of the game is getting to a new area and just looking around for new things to scan. The sounds are also very nice. I've gotten some laughs out of the humor and things they poke fun at as well.If you're looking for a chill adventure game, look no further than this game. If there's a downside, I guess it would be that the humor might not be for everyone, but I haven't felt it ever detracted from the experience. 10/10 for me and definitely worth the full price, but if you get it on a sale then even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game and nice mechanics, and overall the game is beautiful! However the fact that this game was forced from dumb console onto PC is very obvious! Crouch is toggle-only and sliding is a different key (developers probably never heard of Apex legends) which is very annoying. Changing weapons instead of 123456... is just 1-2 to scroll up and down, which is completely stupid - there should be more work done on overall controls. Movement is also very arcade pre-scripted without any physics, but it isn't a big deal.But you can see behind every corner that developers probably never played a PC game.The game is otherwise very nice and I still recommend to play it. It has good black humor, funny vibe and quite unique mechanics
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Steam deck. It was a fun game, humor was good for the most part. Controls were solid. Humor and setting reminds me of The Outer Worlds, except not a fleshed out adventure/story. This is like an extra long sidequest in a game like The Outer Worlds. Still fun, but glad it wasn’t too long and would only recommend on sale, not full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice Metroid Prime-like game.The graphics are good, although almost too bright and colorful.Creature-design is good as well, lots of fun creatures.The gameplay is of the Metroid Prime variety, which means there are a lot of things to scan and shoot.And of course there are several upgrades that influence where you can go in the world and what you can do when you get there.I also quite like the world/level design of the game, the designers really used 3D space quite well so there are plenty of tunnels and nooks and crannies to explore.The combat is fairly easy, you mostly just have to figure out the weak points of the mobs and bosses and target those.It's not the main focus of the game, but it's certainly fun enough that I didn't get bored of it.The audio is good, I don't remember there being any sounds that annoyed me and all the animal sounds were good.There isn't a lot of voice acting in the game, but what there is is done very well.None of the humor had me laughing out loud, but it had the charm of some of the smaller things in Futurama.So, would I recommend it?Yes!Although I'm my feelings about the game are enhanced because I was in an exploration-based game mood and this scratched that exact itch, I still think I would've really enjoyed this game even had that not been the case.And although I didn't get to enjoy the co-op mode, the inclusion of said mode is always a huge plus IMO.

_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: A great game for a sick day, or otherwise when you just want to relax and explore a visually interesting world and story. The game-play is fairly solid and you get a hang of it pretty quick, although there is a lot of additional features that just keep getting introduced which can seem overwhelming if you are not paying attention or otherwise just trying to get through the story quickly. The only downfall this game has is the repetetiveness there comes later on in the story some of the tasks seems very much recycled multiple times, some times the objectives can seem hard to figure out what you have to do because they don't tell you how the world works you just have to guess, which can be good for a game, although here it becomes annoying after a while when you just want to be done with a mission and you are just walking around aimlessly. However the world building is great, the mechanics are fun, the world is cool to explore and enemies are satisfying to kill, the often new introduced mechanics and quirks make for great progression sense and keeps the game-play interesting if you keep your wits about you. So overall a great game and I wish there were more of it i could play.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: So, me and my wife just completed the game and we have put in 11.5 hours, so it is a shorter game. We have had a ton of fun exploring the map together and finding new places and creatures. This game lacks any kind of decent story besides the fact that your exploring a planet. IF you are looking for a good story to follow along with this is not the game fore you. However  we did have a lot of fun non the less and exploring different aspects of the game. I am very glad we grabbed this one on sale because i dont think I would have wanted to purchase it at full price for only 11.5 hours of game play.Last thing ill throw in is that i dont think this game would be nearly as good exploring on your own, it is best suited for co-op to share your finds and explore together in.

_childDocuments_.review: A vibrant, funny, open world platformer with light puzzle elements. Collect ores and minerals to upgrade your equipment, find a bunch of collectables, kill bosses and explore the planet! A really fun game set in a colourful world. Those that enjoy exploration will love it, it's tons of fun, although pretty short. My only issue was coop mode. When it works it plays well, but the servers are broken. Disconnections happen over and over again. This has been a known issue for at least a year and has never been fixed which is a shame. Absolutely recommend this lovely game for solo play, but not for coop as the disconnections ruin the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a terrible game, it is just incredibly average and unoriginal. It plays well enough but that isn't surprising given the number of ideas it seems to have borrowed from other better games, like Doom 2016, Portal and Metroid. The game is also limited by the lack of enemy variety and large number of fetch quests, basically turning the game into a scavenger hunt. Ultimately the game is fairly inoffensive, has some colourful environments and is moderately amusing but nothing I would recommend you spend real money on.

_childDocuments_.review: RIP Typhoon Studios.  Made a deal with the devil (Google / Stadia) and got shut down when Stadia tanked.  Don't count on a DLC-2.  Real shame too because the game is great.  This is one of maybe 4 3D platformers I've enjoyed enough to play all the way through.  The map and movement are phenomenal, it's got tons of hidden areas and there's usually more than one way to access an area if you get inventive.  Art direction and general world design are fantastic.  The humor can be a bit grating at times.  All the flora and fauna are entertaining to find / fight against.  It's a bit short but easily worth it on sale.  Worth noting DLC-1 is VERY short though.

_childDocuments_.review: Before game worlds like the one in The Outer Worlds presented you with a fully corporatized space colony to live in, there had to be people like the main character in this game: Forward explorers who checked potential planets for habitability and exploitability--the latter one being more important than the fore. So begins your Journey to the Savage Planet: An open world  Metroid-like platformer where your main goal is to catalog all the flora and fauna and report it back to your corporate overlords.In truth you're just one of several explorers they have out doing this sort of thing, but what makes your situation unique is that the planet they sent you to turns out to have signs of intelligent life. Could be a real legal snafu, so you have to look deeper into it for the CEO.  At least you have plenty of time to do it in, and lots of things to find in between.I really like this game as it ticks a lot of boxes for me: The colors and graphics are bright and mostly cartoony, there are a lot of things to collect and catalog, and I feel very rewarded by my curious nature with secrets or upgrades to my equipment. Combat, while my least favorite part of the game, is not so punishing that I dread having to get into it with the hostile life forms. The platforming yields the occasional challenge that makes me feel triumphant when I make it to the end.The crafting in this game is appropriate negligible. You gather one of four resources: Carbon, Silicon, Aluminum, or Alien Alloy, then combine it into upgrades back at your ship. I do agree with some that having to go back to your ship to unlock the upgrade does feel like it breaks the flow of progress when you've just gone deep into an area you've never explored before and have so much more to explore there. Seems to be a purposeful gimmick, though. The game only saves when you a) make an important discovery or b) return to your ship and deposit the resources you've gathered. Thankfully, the different sections of the world aren't too vast and there's at least one teleporter in each so you can quickly run back to save and quit in most situations.One should be aware that this game does have a minor level of grossness to it. One of your "tools" is purple poop you throw to stick something to the ground; another looks like a booger but expands into a jump pad (also gross-looking) when you toss it. I had to suppress my gag reflex when I watched this commercial the game has for something called a Meat Buddy. The buddy itself didn't phase me but the commercial has footage of different meat being dropped onto plates and in the garbage, and it just triggered something in my throat.The ads are pretty amusing the first time. Since you are in a corporate vehicle, you get them blaring on your monitors anytime you return to your ship. You can turn them off mid-play and just watch them on your ship's personal computer, which is what I always did since it was closer to full screen. Otherwise, they're just mindless background noise to me.By far my favorite part of the game is Martin Tweed, the CEO of Kindred Aerospace. He has a face and personality that just screams "arrogant slimeball." I look forward to his videos and what new way he plans to try and placate me with corporate jargon.Now while I do recommend this game, there are several things about it I kinda take issue with. For one thing, the length vs the price. I was able to get the main game and DLC for around $20 which I think is a good price considering the fact that I'm 10 hours in and more than two-thirds done. Normally in my region it's $30 for the base game and $8 for the DLC, which seems a bit much especially since they have an achievement for beating the game in under 4 hours.Then there's the limited amount of flora to scan. Kudos to whoever sculpted this world because there are a lot of beautiful and interesting things to see in it; unfortunately, not all of the plants you see can be added to your Kindred catalog. It's especially disappointing in the DLC which added some really amazing looking trees that just read as background objects to your scanner. For a collectathon, it has a strange limit on things to "collect".The targeting system could also use an update, especially if you're using a controller to play the game. There's aim assist which helps you "follow" a target around but the icon that locks onto the target can be very dodgy to engage. I've been absolutely frustrated by trying to get it to lock onto targets that were even just standing still and ended up just shooting wildly in the general direction. They should have just done homing shots, which would have still been a challenge because most things move pretty swiftly when you're in combat.The rest of my complaints are minor little nitpicks like some frustrating jumps and how sometimes my character will not pull itself up onto a ledge when I'm holding the "pull yourself up" button. Overall, the game has been very entertaining to me and I recommend it to anyone who wants a quick platformer to occupy their spare time for about a week.

The game's witty writing, amusing creatures, and quirky humor keep players entertained throughout. While not the most technically advanced title, its charm and surprises make it a must-play for those seeking a lighthearted and enjoyable gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: In Journey to the Savage Planet, you are an employee of the 4th best interstellar space exploration company. The game is light hearted, comical and a bit whacky. The game disguises itself as a metroidvania, but is really more of a linear platformer in disguise. Each area has a final blocking section that you can't progress past without the next upgrade (double jump, bomb seeds etc). Going back to old areas with new abilities might yield collectibles, but they're entirely optional. Art direction, sound and animation are all coherent and pretty, and the voice acting fits in well too, although I started to find it rather grating.- Lighthearted voice acting and art style- Pretty- Abilities are fun to use, and original. Your main abilities come from various things you find on the planet like grapple seeds (grapple hook points you can throw on certain areas), exploding seeds, blobs of goo that throw enemies in the air etc- Large variety of creatures and hazards- You can scan everything- Lots of interesting little areas to find- Too expensive; wait for at least 50% off. It's only 7-8 hours long- You can't pause. Apparently it has multiplayer but that's no excuse when playing alone- There are invisible walls everywhere. If your game is about 3D exploration with double jumps and jet packs, don't use invisible walls. Design your levels better.- The voices, especially of your guiding computer are repetitive and can get annoying- Started as an Epic Store exclusive- There are adverts in the game (fictional, not real) that play every time you enter your ship. It's supposed to make you feel part of a cheap low-grade space exploration company but they get really annoying- You charge your super shot by reloading when you're already fully reloaded. For people who are used to reloading out of habit, this means you regularly accidentally start the charging mini game- Most of the game progresses at a decent pace, but there's one spot in particular where you have to find 3 crystals to progress, and they're spread over a huge area with no direction. In an 8 hours game, I spent 2 hours searching for the last crystal, hidden on a platform out of site, below the edge of the world
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: A much needed addition to the sparse First person Metroidvania sub-genre. Explore a lush alien planet collecting resources and upgrading your equipment so that you can unlock new areas and repeat the process, with a loose story to follow along with plenty of humour riffing on cliches and corporate culture to keep you entertained as you go.Co-op is also a great feature if you don't want to be lonely while you shoot innocent birds and get covered in alien slime.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: A great little exploration/platformer. Going into this, I didn't actually know it was a platformer, and if I had known, I may not have played it, as it's not really my genre. But I am glad I did! This game is bursting (both figuratively and literally) with colour and humour. Weird creatures, gadget upgrades, interesting and varied alien landscapes, a few puzzles and just a whole lot of fun. Finished the story and 100%'ed the in-game index in around 18 hours. I bought this game on sale and absolutely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

Could have been a bit longer with a couple more ideas for upgrades, the suit and weapon stuff is pretty standard. Only has a couple of bosses, nothing fantastic, nothing terrible. _childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: I can not recommend this game as it fails to deliver its purpose.The game aims to be an exploration adventure, with metroidvania elements. However, it does not provide the necessary tools to make the exploration enjoyable. Walking is slow and running does not last long. On top of that, going back to the ship is not easy as the teleport sites are scattered and there can be huge distances between them. You can not get beamed to the ship at will.There is no map. Backtracking after getting power-ups becomes a tedious task, as you may not remember where the missing loot you left behind was. In any other metroidvania, there are hints on a map of the places you missed to explore. In this game, there is a lack of tools to save that information in order to use later. It is a game about exploration which does not like you to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: So boring. Even (or maybe especially) in Co-opMan, this is all set dressing and no game. A pretty world of fetch quests. I played in co-op with a friend and it's so hard just staying with your buddy. The world is all over the place as it's kind of an exploration game, which is fine I suppose but you have so little information on anything that you just end up following the waypoint to the next thing (there are lots of things) you need to tick off the list and that's about it. There are invisible walls too so if you go off piste it doesn't like it. There are just so many things I didn't like about this that it's hard to remember them all.

_childDocuments_.review: I managed to beat the game, but I wouldn’t recommend it.I liked the game’s humor and the atmosphere it tries to convey, and I appreciate that there aren't many 3D Metroidvanias. However, the game felt very bland overall. Exploration wasn’t as enjoyable as it should have been, and the last of the three main areas is a chore to navigate. A map could have helped improve the experience.Another thing I didn’t like is when you get an upgrade but still can’t craft it because you need to search for materials. This really kills the pace of the game. Combat is also disappointing—it’s either too easy or frustrating.To sum up, I think the studio has a good concept, but the game needs more polish. Hopefully, the sequel that’s in development will address these issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun and there are lots of secrets to discover and many things to watch out for.The graphics are very pleasing, the dialogues are entertaining and the sound design is well-done!If you are focusing on story only, you can complete the game in a couple of hours, but collecting everything takes some time.Grab this game on a sale, you won't regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Very pleasantly surprised. Grabbed it to play a bit of co-op as we'd played every co-op game out there and it turned out to be a blast. Mad Rick and Morty style fun with a friend. Wasn't expecting much gameplay from a "comedy" game but discovered a really decent platformer with some nice puzzle challenges and a solid dose of decent jokes and silliness. Made with a lot of love and definitely worth getting on sale for at least a weekend of fun. Felt a bit like Mario64 in first person. Definitely had a classic 90s game vibe in a modern package.Tbh, its worth it just to see the stupid space adverts that play on your ship. Laughed my ass off on those! Nice colourful trippy visuals are a welcome contrast to the doom and post-apocalyptic gloom of most fps games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty good exploration game with n̶o̶ ̶b̶u̶g̶s̶  (There were a decent amount of bugs at the end with one requiring a reset) and It doesn't overstay its welcome like some do. I tried playing with a controller, but found it was no better. I think I got halfway through the game and realized there was virtually no incentive for me to keep playing. There's no larger story revealed early enough to entice you to want to explore further, so if that comes in the second half of the game, sadly the gameplay was so terrible I didn't consider it worth it. Even though I paid very little for this game, after close to ten hours, I decided I would rather invest my time in a game with a more compelling narrative. The kitsch also wears on you after a time. The computer is annoying, the guy sending you messages is annoying, and so you eventually long for the company of everything trying to kill you. There are far better exploration games.

_childDocuments_.review: Now, for my review of Journey to the Savage Planet. It is easily one of the better games I have played in a long time. It blends the wacky comedy, over the top capitalistic, run away absurdity dystopia of games like Portal, Outer worlds, and the movie Wall-E, with what I can only describe as Mario 64 with a blaster, Metroidvania (which is always a win with me, as I love games with power ups that unlock previously unpassable obstacles and environment puzzles). The combination of Platforming, utterly VILE and morbid comedy. Almost everything you fight is cute as all hell, and the ways they die are often gruesome and tickle your morbid funny bone unless you just can't bring yourself to pull the trigger.  This one multiheaded snake like thing called a Boubushka or something like that, has this horribly funny and endearing scream when it sees you coming, and yes, you need to kill it sometimes. Not many things try to hurt you at the stage I am at, but the little bird dudes, which are adorbs as ♥♥♥♥, are also things you have to often kick into the jaws of hungry predators who kill and devour them in the worst imaginable ways... The game is filled with slime, colorful gore, weird alien poop and genitals, and a wise cracking AI companion that would be right at home next to the one from portal. The gameplay loop is fun so far, but I get the feeling that sooner or later I am going to tap out from feeling like I have already sampled the best parts of the game. But it's on sale ATM for 40% off. It is also co op (only 2 player though... but that seems like it would be fun). Dying is even funny. And the way you teleport... it doesn't even hide the fact that the teleporter literally kills you and you are reconstructed in the new place and memories injected in your brain.This game is like the sweetest sour you will ever eat in your life, it is a case study in loudly colored absurdism. 20$ well spent.

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many amazing things about this game it would take me forever to write a review about them, but I really can't recommend this game enough. It gives you the sense that the devs knew exactly what they wanted from the beginning, planned it out in advance, and then stayed true to their intents until the very end.The game is on the shorter side for its price point (main story line in ~9hrs, but it will take you longer to beat it completely), but for all the work that went into all the other details of the game, the music, the adverts, the art design, the levels, the dialogue, the abilities, and every other detail, I can definitely say that if you're able to appreciate these sorts of things about a game rather than its length, you will love it.In short, this game is a witty, light-hearted, subtly anti-capitalist 3D platformer with heaps of character. I believe it's the perfect length with just the right amount of variety to enjoy it all the way until the end.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a wonderful exploration game mixed with a few minor survival mechanics. Explore the new planet to uncover materials, alien artifacts, and upgrades, while slowly climbing your way towards your main goal. Its a nice metroidvania that feels fun to just exist in.Controls are fluid, although some things like the dodge mechanic and certain enemy attacks feel buggy. Dodge is based on timing rather than their distance to you and if you do it too early certain enemies can turn/adjust on a dime and hit you anyway.Collecting all the items/upgrades/scans/logs are a fun part of the game, rather than being tedious to just get 100%. The game gives you generous hints at where stuff is, as well as upgrades to help locate them along the way.Combat is lackluster, which is fine as its more of an exploration game, but certain parts make you fight, which is when the game shows its roughness. Enemies can hit you through walls/objects, certain enemies have an un-dodgeable homing attack on you if they are close enough, bosses have weird hitboxes sometimes, the pistols overcharge/reload/bounceshot all bound to 1 button make some combat very frustrating. This is mitigated somewhat as the game is pretty generous with the health plants, especially if you have a lot of health upgraded and/or you have x upgrade from the dlc. Enemies are pretty barren. There are really only about 8 different enemies in the game, and others are just variations of the same enemy with a slight difference in weakness/moveset. As this ties into combat, its not a big deal, but it is pretty noticeable. Luckily, after the whole Google buyout and Stadia debacle, Typhoon has mostly rejoined as Raccoon Logic and have re-acquired the rights to JTTSP so a sequel may still happen down the line.Overall the gameplay, combat, charming dialog, insane ingame (joke) ads, and world exploration make it worth the price, especially on sale.8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I got this on a sale for 7.50 and it was worth it. But for full price (30) it's too short. I didn't even realize I went into end-game lmao, as it was this short. After I finished the game I spent time gathering upgrades and such, but there are some achievements that I'm just not interested in pursuing (slap every alien at least once? Ain't nobody got time for that).There's also two different achievements for winning after finishing 100% or below that. I have no idea how to get the "below" one, now that I've done 100% so I kinda feel like I've been punished for winning xD It also has separate achievements for co-op, so I'm not getting the achievements either way, as I always play singleplayer.Anyway, as for the mechanics, look, the game is kinda weird. Certain mechanics are introduced, but then only used once or twice, and other times there's no point in them. For example, poison melts amber, so there's some creatures that have amber armor, but most of them are passive, lol. When they're aggressive, it literally takes 1 throw to melt its armor, and then you can play like normal.In general, I hardly used any of the extra "weapons" (apart from exploration) in fights. I just used the bomb a lot at the final boss (which, for some reason, was much easier than other bosses).The upgrades are unlocked through doing exploration feats, some of which include some dreaded stuff like "kill 5 animals with 1 shot" and stuff like that. Fortunately, they were easy to pull off. But the upgrades themselves are pretty much just "more damage" or "more bullets".Look, it's a fun game, I had fun playing it, the planet is cool and all. But for 30 euros I'd feel scammed honestly.So yeah, I recommend it, but only on sale.I don't think I'm buying the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very mediocre.It feels more lackluster the longer you play it, but sadly I was already past the 2 hour mark at that point.6 / 10Pros:* Decent graphics.* Funny live action videos.Cons:* Clunk movement.* Unoriginal item unlocks.* Bad combat mechanics.* Tedious level design.* Even more tedious controls.Notes:Rather quickly, the game gives you a . It will be the cause of your deaths more so then the actual dangers in the game due to it often not registering a point to shoot or telling you it can fire, but won't.You can backtrack after getting additional unlocks, but there is no good reason to do so beyond some non-required upgrades. It feels very weird that they have all these areas, but once you're through them there is no need to go through them again, except for some additional health and possibly some materials.Later enemies get "weak points" which you require to hit to kill them. But the hit registration on these are often terrible, and require the enemy to be in a certain "state". Even if you clearly see your bullets hit the parts, it will simply bounce off because the enemy wasn't "stunned" or "just finished a big attack".Final boss is super underwhelming and made the game feel like a waste of time. Bugs wise, I got stuck on random things a lot. You can just kind of walk into certain objects and creatures, and not get out without somehow pushing yourself with an explosion of sorts.Game also "kills" you when you exit to menu outside of the ship! Requiring you to walk back to your previous location, where your loot can be picked up.It's just needlessly tedious, which is kind off the name of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: It is not the game that was described to be from the trailer and store page... Not by far. There's far too little to be "explored" since the level design is extremely narrow and one-minded. There aren't any alternative paths to your goal, very few secret areas, and the game is painfully short. I'm not saying the trailer and store page are wrong and that I'm 100% right, but I would've enjoyed the game a lot more if I had known what I was getting into. It's not a bad game at all. Just not at all what I was expecting and I was let down as the hours passed...What I believe was advertised to me: -Metroidvania (unlock abilities that allow you to backtrack and reach previously locked areas)-40+ hours of gameplay-Tons of hidden collectibles down secret paths-Talent-tree system where you spend points or use materials to unlock pegs on a tree, branching out to customize your character development, reinforcing your own unique character specialization and allowing for maximum replayability-An open world worth exploring at your leisure and areas to perform tasks in your order of choosingWhat the game actually is:-Metroidvania (unlock abilities that allow you to backtrack and reach previously locked areas)-8 hours of gameplay-No hidden collectibles besides health upgrades, but the game is so easy you don't need a single one, not joking-Talent-tree system but you WILL unlock every single one in the order the game presents them to you. Any reason you wouldn't unlock something is because it's worthless/pointless, and there are more than a few of those-A very linear narrative-driven world that ends when you beat the game. There's never a "tutorial complete!" moment when the game drops you off and leaves you to your own devices. The entire game is "hey I marked a spot on your map. Go kill this/pick this up. Hey, the game is over, you won!"

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing amazing game! To be totally honest, I have 0 recollection of ever buying this game. I found it in my steam library one day, and didn't recognize it in the slightest. _childDocuments_.review: I loved this game, it's got such a nice atmosphere and humor that is present throughout the entire playthrough. You seldom see it without being cringy or flat out boring, I think this game does it great with having constant humorous dialogue that is not "too much". _childDocuments_.review: Game was a great time all the way through the story, even at it's low points. Maybe a bit short, but the loop of this game is undeniably fun all the way through, for most players who want a great, open world, crafting game. For someone like me however, who is an achievement hunter, is unable to 100% the game simply because I don't know anyone who wants to play the game with me. _childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! It's a 3D Metroidvania with gorgeous graphics and a quirky story. The story is in the veins of the Outer Worlds in that it's A LOT of satire but it didn't quite stick the landing for me. I can see what they were going for but it's still a meh story. The graphics as mentioned are stunning, the environments are all very vibrant, lots and lots of color and just very pretty in general. The combat is also relatively good. The main mechanic that dominates miniboss and boss fights are finding the enemy's weak spot which is fine. It's nothing new and they could have come up with something new. However, it's still serviceable. The main set of abilities you get are your typical Metroidvania abilities so nothing new there as well. I did have some issues with some frame drops in certain areas(have 2070 super and was playing on ultra). Also another thing that I don't think I've ever seen in another game. When looking at monsters from very far away they seem to animate at like 10 fps. I don't know if this was intended or what but it's weird as well. Overall, I thought this was a great game to experience despite some minor hitches as it reminded me very much so of Supraland, another great 3D Metroidvania. The abilities all come together in a cohesive way to help you explore these gorgeous environments and can even help in fights. Definitely give this game a go if you're a fan of Metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun with a friend. It's 'only' a story mode game, but it takes place in a semi open world, so you get to do things in your own order, to an extent. It does have some rogue-like elements so you end up backtracking to other parts of the map to get to new parts, if you want the extra health etc. That is not hard to do with the teleporters though, so it's not annoying or frustrating to do.Overall it's a very fun and cute game.Not too much replayability, unless you're like me and try to get all achievements. Sucks that the DLC Achievements are included in the main game however, even if you don't own the DLC.Graphics, Gunplay and Movement are all very satisfying and it seems like a very polished game.Can be a bit choppy/glitchy if you're not the host in coop, so make sure to let the person with the better connection host the online game.Haven't played the game solo yet, so I am not sure how much fun it would be on your own, but I highly recommend this game for some good coop fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Satirical\Crude humor + Metroid= this gameJust as repetitive as Metroid with the backtracking but more focused on "exploration" than combat and more brighter colors.The main weapon is snappy and fun to use, I like the colorful environments to keep your eyes busy as you go back to find all the collectables to upgrade your jump, jetpack, and blaster.The writing is a solid average (Not counting the commercials) your AI companion tries a bit too hard to be funny at times.Speaking of the title: Journey To The Savage Planet? More like journey to the floating isles. Most levels are floating islands over endless pits, you get a grappling ability among several other items to traverse through an obstacle or a string of them but thats about it.So overall its an above average 3d Metroid with satirical commercials at its peak, but it all kinda stops after the final boss so have a podcast ready as you backtrack through all scattered isle's to see the ending or for 100% completion.
