_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this on the gameplay itself, which is a solidly enjoyable 3D metroidvania that's mostly linear but has enough exploration to satisfy & has a fairly colorful & diverse world to explore, isn't excrutiatingly long, and gives you pretty good tools for collection on top of teasing you with lore and small upgrades as a reward for collection. The gunplay isn't very satisfying but it's a minimal aspect of most of the game and most fights are cheesable with the right tools & the very generous health refills. In that aspect it's rarely frustrating and can be pretty engaging to play once it gets going.As a complete package, I kinda hate it. The humor and writing is painfully juvenile. I can't imagine anyone old enough to play it by its ESRB rating even enjoying the humor at that age, and frankly considering some of the  content I'm surprised this didn't get that M rating - the meat vortex and one of the commercials are particularly visceral in terms of gore and completely out of place alongside the rest of the game, and the constant toilet humor - even in the aforementioned lore! - is just. Exhausting. The "haha capitalism made everything terrible" throughline is tired and has no payoff, it's just "haha the world sucks isn't that funny" and none of it is amusing.I started off this game trying to be respectful to this new world I had explored, not breaking anything I didn't need to, not killing things unless I had to, but any respect I have for this as a complete package was shot less than two hours in and I basically just blindly went on a murderous rampage from that point onwards - because that's how the game expects you to play, anyways. It treats you like a child in both its humor and its mechanical expectations - there's not really any true exploration here either, you're handheld through the entire story and told when it's time to go home once you're done.I dunno, separating the mechanics from the rest, on that level if I tune out most of the gross and unpleasant aspects of this, I could have a good time platforming about and collecting and all that. Not an amazing time, but an enjoyable one. I recommend the game on that aspect alone but I cannot stress how dangerously close all the other aspects of this game came to making me flip that rating, and it's definitely too short and shallow to justify its $30 price tag, too.Oh and lol it has DLC that not even fans of the main game like. Yeah, I ain't touching that.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: A quirky and unique approach to the action-adventure and exploration genre. This science-fiction game, although more fun with a pal, is a niche little gem that offers stunningly vibrant colours and crisp textures. The gameplay is nothing too intense, rather laid-back and easy to enjoy in long sessions or in short bursts. The inclusion of real-life video for fake in-game adverts was somewhat jarring (in a similar sense to how the animated film  featured videos of real-life footage) but didn't detract the overall gameplay.  is a refreshing, upbeat, and colourful experience that never takes itself too seriously.  and  offers plays with a straightforward, well rounded story and game full of comically grotesque yet winsome aliens to blast apart, collectables and upgrades to acquire, and flora and fauna to scan for research (this feature is somewhat trivial). 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: First: I played on SteamDeck so I had to lower the graphics else it could become a slideshow.But I did not include this into my negative review.The game started promising. You land on a planet and need to explore it.I somehow thought this would be like "hardspace shipbreaker". Kind of mission for a company.And by the story, it is. You work for a company discovering planets.But you only discover one single planet, not different.But somehow ... I couldn't arrange with it.Maybe I hated the enemies/animals.The first pain was when I had to kill a smaller one which had its weakpoint on the tail.It was so difficult to hit this weakspot. Especially using a controller.I also didn't like the "ads" playing in the videos. I know, they were nicely done and "funny".But it reminded me on movies like Bad Taste or Braindead etc. and I just hate this style. ^^The exploration and scanning of the stuff is also not that difficult. In most cases the difficulty isto find something on the map (since you don't have a map) or getting to the object.Which to be honest could be challenging sometimes.I also had issues with the sound. I am not native English speaker. For me it was really difficult to understandthe stuff the female voice told you. Especially during a fight ... when you even can't read the subtitles.I think this "mechanical" effect on her voice made it so difficult to understand.The boss fights were okay ... fair and challenging.What I disliked the most was the way you have to collect exp for the next upgrades.You had to accomplish tasks which were partially annoying. So I just stopped.I will maybe give it a try again on the PC, but somehow ... the game just didn't have anything to keep me going.I didn't like the main char (neither by the look nor by anything else). I also didn't like the animals etc.Also the fact that you cannot deselect your "second" weapon (the items) ... you always have to hold something.This distracts me all the time.The colors and level design were nice.Oh and yeah ... the "special" attack of the gun is so annoying too.You have to press Y and then press it again at the right moment to shoot it.Else the weapon becomes overheated and you have to reload it ... during a fast paced fight ... thisis nearly impossible. Didn't like that.Scanning enemies while they attack you is also a pain. I still don't know how to scan these flying f*cks which can teleport themselves everywhere.It was a 4/10 for me to be honest. Expected something more.I think in these games I prefer either a good character or a routine work like in "hardspace shipbreaker".Bye
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game if you are a fan of exploring and collecting all the things in a 3D platformer. If that is not your jam then stay far away from this game as that is what you be doing 90% of the time. The rest of the time is subpar gun play.# StorySimple but does a good job of keeping you progressing through the game. The live action videos that you watch are a lot of fun and are the highlight of the story. It is fun to discover different creatures and environments and that really is the story; the discovery.# GameplayPretty weak tbh. The gun aiming is not great as it is not very precise. The is also no upgrades that really changes how the gun works. You can just increase ammo, reload speed, and bullet damage. The exploration tools are a little better as there is more variety but the the movement is awkward.# ArtIt's ok, very stylized. I was not a fan of the music.

_childDocuments_.review: The games world and atmosphere is fine, its quite the charming/funny adventure.Issue is its combat is absolutely garbage. Dash-dodging doesnt seem to work properly, jumping over ground-slam attacks often hits you anyway, and most of the ways you have to deal with armored enemies hurt you and they immediately charge into your face faster than you can get away.Exploring is fun and man theres a lot of secrets, but every time i face a "boss" i just get pissed because mechanics i was told by the game to do simply do not work.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Well, while all I can do is to appreciate and applaud the game for the overall world design the devs came up with for what it is, I just sometimes can't help to feel an urking sensation while looking at certain... "anomalies" in this game. I don't know if it is because some of their pores and holes trigger my trypophobia but it becomes harder for me to continue playings this one the more anomalies I discover. Which is literally the point of the game; to search and discover more about this alien planet you've landed on and the creatures and organizms in it. And I feel incredibly sad since the game looks extremely fun but I can't subject myself to it or I will probably puke after a while I reckon.I don't know if I will try to pick this one back up for another time in the future, but for now I can't seemingly continue to play... It's a shame really since I'm missing out on a seemingly really fun game... I guess this might serve as a warning for other people with the same "condition" (I know it's technically not a certified phobia but that doesn't change the fact that I simply can't even let myself to look at some of the things I encounter in the game without them sending shivers down my spine). Definitely check out the screenshots before your purchase.But if nothing affects you the way they affected me, all the power to you! You have a fun collectathon type of adventure ahead of you and I can't help but to say I envy you and that normal functioning brain of yours... Have fun on my behalf too if you can...

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I cant recomend this one. The concept is there but man, lots of things bug me about this one. But first: it looks very good, nice design. It also plays pretty good, the controls are kinda clean and intuitive...ok I'll make this short:- its not open world, even if it seems like it. - upgrades needed to progress in the world, but they feel like gatekeepers and there only use is in getting over the next hegde- farming resources is almost trivial in this game- I finished the game with only 4-5 upgardes unlocked, the other 20 or so where still locked for some reason and I honestly didnt care, just wanted to finish the game- 80% of the aliens are basically the same - companion voice gets really annoying- most of the enemies are to easy and dont require any strategy- that being said, two of the bossfights are actually designed in hell, they are not fun, not challenging, just exhausting (but first boss is actually pretty good)- the ending is just dissapointing- no couch coop mulitplayerIm sorry. _childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to anyone who would like a really fun Co-Op experience AND to anyone who can actually even start the game!I managed to get it started a month ago after a multitude of error messages and problems and it was really fun, Trying to start it again today just won't work!The game is plagued with "Failed to connect to Steam servers..." and "Fatal error...", but if you're willing to gamble it's a really great game...If you get it to even run!Unfortunately for me I guess I'll have to ask for a refund 😥🤬EDIT:I found a fix!I was suspecting something going on with the audio because I managed to get to the start screen, but without sound, after some tinkering.After seeing this video  I tried deactivating ALL sound outputs (NVIDIA High Definition Audio and Sonic Studio Virtual Mixer) except for the one I'm actually using (Realtek High Definition Audio) and now it starts without a problem, so try this! 😎👍Why it didn't log in to Steam Servers when the sound hardware was not correctly set up for the game is a mystery though 🤔

_childDocuments_.review: I just about never write reviews, but this game is a gem and anyone who likes quirky humor and mechanically interesting game play should really consider picking it up. I have only played the base game so far, but it is a masterpiece that had me alternating between loudly belly-laughing and sweating profusely from concentration throughout.The only issue that I could see with the game is that a player can't make multiple saves on the same profile, so if one were to run into a game-breaking bug or something (not that I have), that would be an issue. However, for me the game was very stable and I never encountered any issues.In all it's a really fun and lighthearted game with technicality to it and some interesting lore that I highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I utterly love this game and I am so happy that it finally arrived on Steam so I can play in on PC. I immediately had to buy it including DLC. You can go explore anywhere and you will probably enjoy it way more that way than if you just follow markers.I like PC version a lot more because I can properly aim and move around. _childDocuments_.review: This game is dead.The publisher was bought out by Google who then proceeded to shut down all third party publishers. If you've been wondering why it's all been screenshot events, that's why. Because it's all there is left. There are going to be no more updates. No patches. No additional DLC. What you see is what you get. This game is dead. The developer no longer exists. That said, it's a pretty fun game. Short, but enjoyable. If you can get it on sale, do it... IMPORTANT UPDATE!!!!Typhoon Studios has reformed under the name Raccoon Logic and has gained the rights to Savage Planet from Google. It looks like while this game might still be a wash, they're looking into continuing the series.Good news for all of us and enough for me to change my recommendation. It's not going to get additional DLC, but there is a future for the series.UPUPDATE!!!!Revenge of the Savage Planet has just been announced. If you're interested in it, I'd suggest picking this up. If you liked this, chanced are it's going to be a good one. God knows it's sitting on my list.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly fun. Mechanics and movement feel tight and well thought out. Unfortunately, 9 hours into my game and I launch the game to a message that my profile has been corrupted and must be deleted. Now I'm starting over from scratch.It seems that save games aren't being cloud-sync'ed and they're prone to being corrupted with no apparent way to recover them. That feels like the ultimate let down.Edit: Despite this issue, I ended up finishing the campaign ... and I really enjoyed it. _childDocuments_.review: Graphics were great and crisp! Was not expecting this to be such an open world. I loved all the hidden orange globs, searching for them in unexpected places and finding one filled my curiosity. The maps were gorgeous, and the transition from one area to a completely different climate area was so smooth and satisfying. I really enjoyed that there were no cutscenes and that it was mostly about adventuring into the unknown! The teleporters were fantastic, gotta love a game that values your time. Launching the game and the loading screens didn't take too long either so thats great. I was surprised, there were hardly ANY bugs too!  I'm a bit sad that it ended so soon, but I'm glad I played it. The only negatives I have:- The ending to the storyline ended pretty abruptly once you complete everything on the planet and fly home, I was hoping that we would get to do something with the seed and have a choice ending like seeing the planet grow or having the aliens that made the statues come back to their planet... - Collecting all the orange glob mission seemed pointless after glob number 80 because your health and stamina don't increase- I was hoping you would eventually run faster, but you don't - You always have to hold something in your left hand, which was a bit annoying because it took up about 20% of the screen- The maps that had mobs constantly chasing you and killing you were not that fun to explore- It was a bit annoying having to come back to maps you already explored to have to open a certain cave when you finally unlocked an upgrade- The seeds were not very self-explanatory and I didn't realize how useful the purple sticky glob thing was until the end of the game- The gun kinda sucks
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially skeptical with some of the negative reviews I had read and the change of ownership of the game. The game also starts out really slow and so this had me worried. However, those worries were unwarranted and up until this point in the game I have had an utter blast! There's so many ways to engage in the game and I love the feeling of exploration on what is truly an alien world. None of the faux humanoid aliens - or boring aliens. This was great - and a great satire on corporatocracy. It is definitely a game that is better with friends. I do think they could polish up the multiplayer aspect of the game by allowing for separate offline character files. Definitely get it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is alright. It's fine. It's a pretty basic fps metroidvania, although quite linear for a metroidvania, consisting not of a large map of interconnected zones but a few fully distinct areas with a few large zones each. The game has a lot of missteps and little irritations, like how certain gates or blocks require items that are both useful in combat and you have an extremely limited inventory of,  which means that even if you have the upgrades and progression to get into a secret, if you happen not to have the key items you need to get in when you find it, you need to remember where it is in a game with no map, backtrack to an area with the resource you needed, grab the resource, then go back to the secret. It's highly irritating.Enemy variety is middling to weak, weapon variety is nil (a pistol with an unlockable charge shot I barely used) and the bosses are all extremely mediocre. At least environment variety is pretty high. The areas are all pretty consistently interesting, unique, and/or pretty.The upgrades you get are mostly meaningful, and the way that the grappling hook is implemented is great, especially if you figure out how to launch yourself with grapple cancelling. It does bug me that the high jump needs a basically post-game upgrade to actually be fun to use, but I digress.This is a game with a lot of flaws, but a combination of good art, occasionally funny writing, and good core movement (at least once you have all the upgrades) was compelling enough to get me through getting all of the collectibles even once I'd beaten the final boss, as well as through the DLC. If I had bought this at full price, this review would almost certainly be negative, but on a deep discount, I'd say this game is worth trying if it looks interesting to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey to the Savage Planet is a cute and chill exploration game. The gameplay is rather simple: Walk around the map, explore the different regions, scan your environment, gather items, develop new technologies, etc. There is much to see and great technology to develop. You will also have some main missions to complete, which basically guide you trough the world (there will be times where you can’t advance without the necessary technology, which you will get by playing the main story). The campaign is rather short (4-5h), but you can keep playing and exploring the game. I finished the main story and still didn’t see all the locations.It looks like the game was designed by children. All the creatures are extremely weird and cute. And the whole world is colourful. The developers might have been on some drug. But it looks really cool and unique. I enjoyed that rainbowy art style.The game itself isn’t very challenging. It is a game to play when you want to chill with a couple of friends. I absolutely recommend exploring this crazy world with some friends. It is much more fun.The graphics are beautiful and the commentary is fun. The soundtrack suits the ambient.To sum it up, a cute adventure game. Totally worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey to  the Savage Planet is a pretty decent exploration game.  The world is very bright, colorful, and alive and the various mechanics and engagements make sense.  There's not much to the story "find a fuel source to get home, and document everything you find," but the game does a good job of keeping you engaged as you reveal more of the world and more potential entries for your codec.  The CEO of the satirical company that shot you into space has some obnoxious pitches when your at the home base, but you do not have to engage with them if you do not wish to.The Good:- Wide selection of flora and fauna to discover- Solid pacing regarding essential game mechanics- Engaging world that was fun to waste 15 hoursThe Bad:- The pacing for non-essential QOL upgrades was too slow and I remained annoyed at having to grind through side quests in order to unlock more jumps or a bigger utility belt; these are not strictly necessary to beat the game, but they will definitely make the job easier- Specific variants of flora and fauna are treated as separate entities in the codec.  When certain fauna have a much rarer spawn chance this made 100%ing the job much more of a grind than it other wise should have been.- The stated mission of the game as told you by the eccentric CEO is to discover everything on the planet by visiting every corner and turning over every rock; however, the invisible walls prevent seamless exploration and the occasionally poor geometry resulted in my character getting stuck on multiple occasions.  There is no return to base option so If you are stuck you can try blasting your way out with bomegranets otherwise you'll have to restart the entire game- The only real replay value is in achievement hunting, nothing in the game world compels a second look after completionOverall:- Okay game but worth waiting for a sale
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty and pretty goofy game! Very polished, and a fun gameplay story which keeps me playing after the main story arc. I found, almost bizarrely, that JTTSP struggles with finding its own identity for the first couple of hours. This is with similar setting and humour to titles such as the Outer Worlds, Breathedge and Deep Rock Galactic. However, JTTSP really comes into its own when fully entering the platforming mechanics of gameplay. It's a lot of fun to hop between islands and search for hidden bits and pieces, and it's worthwhile revisiting early areas with new abilities to find things that you missed or couldn't get before.There isn't too much of a difficulty curve, which isn't altogether a bad thing. I managed to complete the main story/quest with about half of the available abilities (besides the essential), nothing above Level 1. You can increase your number of abilities/enhancements by levelling up via side missions, but the game doesn't get really difficult enough to warrant doing this besides completion. Visually the game is incredibly pretty and polished, something the devs make the most of (rightfully so) with an in-built photo mode. I also didn't encounter much in the way of bugs, which speaks volumes itself for a game of this type and from a small developer. You have my standing ovation. In sum, a fun and goofy game to spend several hours with.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Metroidvania.No, I'm dead serious.The game functions and plays almost exactly like Metroid Prime; platforming, shooting, scanning creatures and attaining new powers to explore more and more of the world.The only difference here is that Journey to the Savage Planet (JTTSP) is incredibly vulgar and humorous, which is a trait the game wears with pride. Everything about the game is morally dubious, from the lore to to your AI companion to even the fast travel system, but that's exactly why I love it so much. The humour in this game is dark and it never pulls a punch, especially during the ads you can watch on your ship's TV, and it's the game's most defining aspect.It plays just fine and there are a lot of fun ways to get about each level, such as the classic grappling hook and the absolutely game-breaking triple jump. Each area is visually appealing and has their own feel to them, and each of the creatures you'll encounter are absolutely horrible in only the best ways.I just wish the game did more with what it had; it's a rather short experience. I beat the main game in about 14 hours and the DLC in about 2. There are only three main areas here, excluding the final area and the DLC area, and I sort of wish there was more to see on the planet with how much I was enjoying myself.The bosses as well were a low point as well, almost an afterthought really. They don't pose an incredible threat and all of them essentially boils down to "shoot it". Only the first boss has any semblance of strategy put into it, but even then it's a little lackluster. Such a shame too.But the game itself is good and worth playing if only to explore the world, which thankfully is very fun to journey through no doubt thanks to the uniqueness of each level and the witty quips from your AI companion, EKO. It IS worth your time, but not at $40 CAD. Wait for a sale on this one if you absolutely need to play it.Oh also there's co-op. I never used it so I can't give a critique, but it's there if you're interested.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: If this game didn't come with a 'hilarious snarky AI,' it'd be mediocre. Anything this does right, The Outer Worlds does better. Everything else this tries to do was either a mistake (Snarky AI) or so blandly poor that it's not worth playing for. Also, the grapple beam is super lazy, and has no real physics. You will never use it in an interesting way.The aesthetic is basically straight from The Outer Wilds, though more fantastical and cartoony, and less concerned with internal consistency. If there's any reason to play this game, this is it. I'd still recommend The Outer Worlds instead, even disregarding all the other ways that game is better. The gameplay/combat takes inspiration from Metroid Prime, except simplified to the point of dullness. You've got your basic 'gun, dodge, eventually double jump' setup- this could be acceptable, if any of the enemies were interesting or interestingly placed. You never have to mix platforming and fighting, all the enemies are in broad arena-esque areas.  Dodging is always easy, just spam it if the enemy's vaguely about to attack and that's good enough. The gunplay never changes, just number go up. You'll notice in the trailers that you get a grapple beam. Do not be deceived. There is no physics on that grapple beam, it pulls you along a fixed trajectory for each grapple point. You will never do anything interesting with it. The 'humor' is... imagine Borderlands, but the only characters are you and Claptrap.Your AI's commentary is either supposed to be funny because it's annoying, or funny because it's cruel, or funny because poop/barf. The only other jokes are taking the piss out of corporate culture, which I'm normally all for, but this doesn't do all that well. It's just not snappy enough, spending about two minutes setting up an anemic joke about how Kindred Aerospace is doing medical experiments on their employees. Also, if you want to do a fake ad right, you either want a farcically stupid product that you could see some corporate dumbass thinking is a good idea, or a product which makes sense in lore and actual advertising techniques are applied farcically. Just making an ad for a gross product is in fact just gross.

_childDocuments_.review: I love colorful games. Is there too much color? Yup - this game. To the point it all blends together. Its pretty, don't get me wrong. I kind got used to it. The game loop is FPS platformer with Metroidvania elements. After you finish most of the story it allows you to craft helmet that detects the secret areas, allowing you to go one more time with indicators. Mad respect for that - it means you can experience the game fully, while it does not waste your time.  The game is not hard, and the path is mostly obvious. This is great for kids (the humor is not exactly kids friendly), or for people who want to chill and explore. The bosses are not hard, nothing in the game requires fast reflexes, deep thinking or posses any real challenge. Great for relaxing with gf/wife, or after work  - you get the point.The coop works good, but the problem is that its not required or needed in any way. And with obvious paths, the experience looks more like "catch me if you can", "the floor is lava" and not like a coop fps.Its a short game. Does not overstay its welcome. In term value for the money - get on sale.I had enough fun with it to recommend, but not enough to get the dlc for 9 bucks. The comments for it, said, its 90 minutes. The base game is around 10h-12h, if you run its obstacle course twice.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey to the Savage Planet immediately reminded me of Metroid Prime: unknown planet, alien flora and fauna, scanning vizor, energy gun, ...And the more I played, the more I noticed Metroid play-style elements : areas that cannot be accessed without specific skills,  scanning symbols to unlock stuff, alien artifacts,  ...It's not Metroid, but Journey to the Savage Planet is funny with a very cool gameplay.The good- Simply fun to play: metroid style with some platforming- Basic but funny story- Beautiful and colorful areas to explore- Mechanics are straightforwardThe bad- No pause in Single Player mode: you can find yourself dead if you step away while in the wild.- You cannot exit while in the wild: it would be the same as dying.- No map, which is weird since pretty much the first thing you get is a cartographer.And the ugly:- Equipment upgrades are locked behind very specific "challenge-style" missions (such as hit X stuff with Y, and the like): they're not too difficult, but some are pretty annoying to pull. The upgrades are not really needed as the game is not particularily difficult, but having them makes the game more fun.- There are a few areas from which there is no way to get out. You have to exit the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing Journey to the Savage Planet yesterday, and it is really quite good. It is a mix a 3d metroidvania exploration, survival game and light combat elements. Reminds me of Supraland a lot, but it focuses more on story, exploration and survival rather than puzzle solving. It starts out in an enclosed area, which is a good thing in survival games imo. The comedic story is presented at a good pace with a reasonable amount of content, the graphics are colorful and beautiful for this type of game and you are introduced to some really nice metroidvania traversal gear after learning the basics in the first "play area". The combat is nothing to write home about, but it is a lot better than in Supraland at least. It feels good to control the main character and shooting stuff creates some nice squishy effects.I think the game loses some momentum when you teleport to the next level instead of continuing to climb the same tower in one continuous level like you have been doing for the first couple of hours. That takes away some of the epicness of the exploration aspect, which is a shame, because that aspect was one of the strengths of the game. The game does a pretty good job of making everything you can see explorable, but there have been one or two times when I have fallen to my death after clipping through surfaces that should have been solid.I would recommend the game broadly to people who are interested in metroidvania games and survival games. It is easy to pick up, it starts to be fun right away, but it is challenging and rewarding to find the secrets and complete the bonus objectives that are hidden away on the planet.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey To The Savage Planet has a lot of charm and humor that is definitely inspired by Borderlands. As a fan of Borderlands, I really enjoyed this game.A lot of effort was taken to build not only the world around you, but showing you how humanity has progressed in the form of hilarious TV ads that play on your main screen in your ship.The exploration and abilities that you gain as you explore are a lot of fun to use. This is the game's strength, and I had a blast uncovering more areas and secrets along the way.My only gripes with the game revolve around the poorly executed gun play and mechanical glitches. The gun does not feel good to use, so the parts of the game where you are forced to use it just feel like a chore. Some poor design choices in some areas, specifically towards the end of the game, where you are getting bombarded with damage by creatures / traps that you cannot deal with while solving an exploration puzzle were a bit infuriating, but they did not ruin the overall experience.I also had numerous instances where I would get stuck on an object and be unable to get off of it without exiting the game and taking the death. This was extremely frustrating, especially considering it happened while doing one of the end game puzzles.Overall, I recommend the game. Typhoon studios did a phenomenal job with the world building and I am excited to hear that they managed to keep ownership of the IP, so I am looking forward to the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey to the Savage PlanetBy Typhoon Games/505 GamesGenre: First-Person MetroidvaniaRelease: January 28, 2020 on the Epic Games Store, the same day 2021 on Steam-----If it's not already clear from several of my past reviews, I love Metroidvania games. The concept of gated exploration, the acquisition of new abilities and items to get to areas I had to pass up before, is quite appealing to my analytical mind – when I recognize the geographical callouts that map designers provide, I begin thinking naturally about what do I have that can get through them, and if I don't have anything, to keep in mind to come back to this area later.This is no different with Journey to the Savage Planet. It may be in first-person, and it may look a lot like some recently released survival games such as No Man's Sky or Subnautica, but there are no survival elements to be concerned with here. The only major issues you have to deal with, which are dangers in many games like this, are ubiquitous enemies and bottomless pits.The storyline is somewhat standard sci-fi: you are a pioneer, sent to find new potential Earths, so to speak. You land on planet AR-Y 26, which seems to be composed of multiple biomes in several small areas. The reason for that is something you'll discover is your primary goal: Finding the World Seed, a McGuffin that can amalgamate parts of nearby planets and other celestial matter into one, though as you'll remember if you've seen Star Trek III: The Search for Spock with the Genesis Device, that's hardly ever a stable proposition.That's all through observation, and being versed in various science fiction tropes; I don't feel I've spoiled everything here. Suffice to say, there's a whole lot more going on than a dangerously unstable cobbled-together planet.Unfortunately your employers, the fourth best space exploration firm in the galaxy, Kindred Aerospace, did not see fit to equip you with anything in the way of supplies, so you'll just have to 3D print them using materials you find on-world. Amounts of carbon, silicon, aluminum and the rare alien alloy are required to craft around 40 implements and upgrades which will help you traverse the many treacherous landscapes of AR-Y 26.The first three of those, can be found either in geodes that you crack open with a smack or your weapon, or in the various docile or hostile fauna throughout the world. Each one of them also has a very humorous scan-result color text – scanning to reveal details of the nearby terrain and creatures is another peripheral feature of Metroidvanias that I dearly enjoy. The game surely revels in coercing you to off pretty much every creature you see in various ways, whether it's just shooting them with your standard energy pistol; kicking them into "meat vortexes" that act like wood chippers; stomping them; blowing them up with grenades; melting them; and pretty much any other thing you can think of to do with the materials around you.You are rewarded for your travels with humorous emails and video clips of fake commercials as well as messages from home reminding you of your mission, and of what an absolutely crapsack world you live in, the corrupt Kindred Aerospace and its CEO, Martin Tweed, being at the center of many of the bad things that have happened Earth. All of that, however, is handled in an extremely dark comedy style. I can best describe it as "cheerfully cynical."If you can handle this comedic style, if you like Metroidvanias like I do and if you like exploration games in general, I do highly recommend this one. Enjoy your explorations, and remember: eat the orange goo!

_childDocuments_.review: Leans into the joke so much there's nothing but the joke. That the game then tries to deliver a plot later via collectible logs is pretty hard to take seriously.Mechanics are alright but the levels themselves don't feel robust enough to let you enjoy them. A lot of the levels can be skipped in some fashion with uses of earlier mechanics. Ultimately the game is also over *very* fast and then....well that's it. No ending really, no real conclusion. _childDocuments_.review: Journey to The Savage Planet feels like the natural offspring of the sci-fi gaming zeitgeist in recent years; it has a NMS-like art style combined with a Borderlands-but-less-explicit approach to humor, leading to creatures that poop all the time, 'wacky' infomercials to watch, and a calloused AI commenting on your progress. Combine this with vaguely Metroidvania-esque ability progression and a basic combat system, and you get something that's pretty good all the time, but never .+ Visual design is decent, and communicative (interactable items and objects are easy to see). Level design is also good.+ Consistent ability progression lets you play with new abilities such as grappling hooks, double jumps, and a variety of throwable objects which can help for puzzle solving or fighting enemies.+ Game pacing moves fairly quickly, and 100% completion is optional for those who don't want to hunt down everything.+ Multiplayer coop is fun and can help in fights or exploration.+ Endgame upgrades make finishing the remaining completion objectives easy, instead of turning into a slog.+ Parkour is actually pretty decent! While the game doesn't have true parkour mechanics, grappling, rail grinding, and double jumping can lead to fast movement that's slightly reminiscent of Ghostrunner.- The final area has some iffy level design that may leave players stuck for longer than necessary.- No part of the game really utilizes coop, and not even cutscenes integrate the second player. There are no team platforming areas or combat challenges that require coordination. If one player is better than the other they will likely make all the progress in the game, with the other player getting babysat.- Story is meaningless, with nothing interesting to find. Collecting all the lore confirms a very basic history that any player could have guessed.- Boss fights overall are serviceable, but not memorable.- Scanning everything should be automatic or not a completion requirement, but it isn't automatic and it is a completion requirement. This will keep me from truly 100%-ing the game since I'm not going to spend an hour going between the game and a wiki trying to figure out what mobs or plants I missed.- Main questline is quite short, and even with collecting everything and finishing every side quest (except for scanning everything), my fellow player and I finished the game in about 9 hours. This might be slightly longer as a solo player, so factor on an extra 1-2 hours if solo.Journey to The Savage Planet feels like an incredible game trapped beneath some issues that land it in the "good" area. I have no comment on the dlc, which I likely won't buy unless it goes on sale for a decent price in the future. If the developers can make another game that expands on this mechanical base while breaking out of the now-tiring "lol random" humor style, it could be absolutely savage.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey To The Savage Planet

_childDocuments_.review: Congratulations, you have been chosen to explore planet ARY-26 working for the “4th Best Interstellar Exploration Company”, Kindred Aerospace. Sadly, your arrival at the planet did not go very smoothly and you’ve crash landed. You will have to not only explore this planet but you’re going to be tasked with trying to put your ship back together. If only it were that easy… You see there seems to be more to this planet than everyone was led to believe. There are ancient structures that shouldn’t be there, and you’re going to have to figure out what that’s all about as well in Journey to the Savage Planet. This is a game where you’re going to be upgrading your equipment as you go. You’re going to be given tasks to complete that will allow you to unlock upgrades so that you can get further into the game. You’re going to need a gun, a jetpack, a grappling hook, upgrades to your health, stamina, visor, and more, and you’re going to have to get all of these things through tasks in the game. The health and stamina portion will increase as you ingest Orange Goo, some absolutely vile natural plant/organism that after you’ve ingested enough of it will increase your health and stamina. The rest of the upgrade/unlockable pieces you’ll have to work for. Most of the time you’re going to be given the task of trying to find the suitable alloy or components needed to unlock the upgrade, which can then be created in the 3D printer on your ship. My advice to you is to scan EVERYTHING, once you get into an area that looks a little different, turn your visor on and find all the scannable things and scan them. Scan the rocks, the trees, planets, creatures, statues, anything that glows that lovely shade of orange. I really do wish that all you had to do was scan everything, but the final step in almost all the unlocking of items is a boss fight, most of which took me two or more attempts to complete. All of the bosses have patterns, and you just have to figure out the pattern, but I will give you a helpful hint, DON’T STAND STILL. Yes, I know it is a fatal flaw of mine, I get wrapped up in trying to land that perfect shot and so I stop moving, don’t do that, you’re more likely to get your ass kicked than do the ass kicking, I promise. There are a ton of areas that you’re going to have to come back to once you’ve gained the correct ability to access that area. There are areas that require the use of electric fruit, bomb fruit, the ability to power stomp, and the ability to power grapple. Most of these abilities will be pretty easy to unlock as long as you’re following the story, as some of those power ups are needed to advance the story. Speaking of the story, I got the credits to roll within 10 hours of starting the game, however there was about 35% of the game left to play. I point this out because I know that there are some completionists out there who fear the credit screen thinking that maybe they can’t get their perfect score if they go ahead and beat the final boss (who is a frustrating piece of work).There was definitely a balance of frustration and fun that I had in the game. There are some jumps or grapples that I thought I had, but missed and so I ended up falling to my death, or having to start a complicated section all over again, but overall I enjoy this game. There was a level of silliness to it, I mean look who your employer is, right off the bat, you’re working for the 4th best, and the scientist that you’ll be reporting to throughout the game screams crazy, possibly mad, scientist. So if you’re up for a first person shooter, action, planetary exploration game, I'd say you check this game out.

name: Resolutiion
detailed_description: An old killer escorts a curious AI through chaotic combat, puzzling secrets, and unsettling calm in a dreamscape of madmen and sane animals. Resolutiion is a fast-paced action-adventure created by two angry German brothers leading a band of vagrants who loaded it with lovely pixels, dirty jokes, deep ideas and badassemotional tunes for 20 hours of punishing combat, rewarding exploration, and layered storytelling. Will you be the player or will you be played? In the Infinite Empire nothing is as it seems. Explore a fractured future, gathering weird weapons and stories, to piece together the past: a friend betrayed, a family broken, worlds at war. To solve the mystery of the Cradles take on a multi-cultural-mashup of cynical gods, emotional machines, zealots, luddites, and furry critters in a world that doesn’t care if it confuses or kills you — oh hey, a kitty! Features: 16 hour playtime Explore a grim cyberpunk world where nothing is as it seems Experience a dark story where you might be the hero - or the villain Unlock new abilities to defeat your enemies Survive in brutal fights and crush gruesome bosses Listen to a badassemotional cyberpunk Soundtrack Here kitty-kitty…

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I'm one of the developers of the engine used to make Resolutiion (Godot Engine). So I'm of course enthusiastic about this game in part because it's a great showcase of the (free and open source) software I work on.That being said, I'm playing Resolutiion as a regular gamer, as I find it very enjoyable. The art style is of course a big hook, obviously inspired from famous predecessors but combined with the great music and intriguing storyline, it makes Resolutiion stand out for itself.I've only played a few hours so far so I'll likely update this further down the road with more thoughts, but I really enjoy the various sceneries that the developers built, going as far as taking some screenshots to remember the most striking locations, which I rarely did up to now while playing games. Walking or dashing around to explore these gorgeous locations while listening to the great music is a nice experience in itself.The hack and slash gameplay works well, and even though the first few minutes may seem a bit dull, don't be fooled: you'll quickly unlock new abilities (a gun, a run/dash ability, probably a lot more as they're a lot of room in the inventory) which make it all really fun, and are also quite necessary to succeed in the challenging fights.I can't say much about the story yet after only a few hours, but so far so good. I enjoy the writing, which fits the universe well and is also witty at times, while distilling elements about the universe's lore little by little. You'll be lost at first, but it seems to be intentional and it works IMO fairly well.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of games that were inspired by 'Hyper Light Drifter' and they mostly failed as individual games for various reasons, but out of those that I played I liked this one the most. Despite the visual similarities to HLD that many people are calling a ripoff, Resolutiion clearly had a talented artist and I don't want to take anything away from him; the games might look similar but it's not a clone of HLD. Surprisingly the best part of this game was the story, the writing was just excellent and absorbed me into the universe, although the delivery of that story was somewhat questionable, mainly because I felt like the characters came and went too quickly. Still, I thought the lore for the universe was very compelling, from what I understand the humanity was taken over by technological advances and those few that remained isolated started a war against the 'progress', although It was kinda vague and confusing. It took me about 5 hours to get the 'easy ending', but the game is not truly complete until you do some post-game content, and that could take a few more hours with no hints. I personally would not replay it since developer already said that saving characters does not impact the game in a significant way. So yea apparently you can avoid killing most of the enemies and even some bosses, but I murdered everyone, even cute bunnies and other innocent wildlife. The combat is pretty basic, it does not get more complicated than dodging and following up with an attack, similar to bullet-hell games. There are a few sub-weapons that you can unlock but generally, the power-ups are there to progress in the story, kind of like a metroidvania. For example, there is a power that turns you into a small yellow creature that can travel through little holes which previously were not accessible. I have to say the soundtrack and the sound design were exceptionally good, one of the best I ever heard in the game. So I am walking through the forest area and my controller starts to vibrate every couple of seconds with no enemies around, so I am like -"WTF where is the vibration coming from", turns out there is a big beating heart in the forest and it pulsates my controller - that is just ***** cool. Even the way the music was used was very professional, like the speed of the songs will adapt to what is going on the screen, which is really awesome because most developers just loop the music. Other than that, the game has a good visual variety, such as a desert, underwater city, forests, towns and infected area - with a couple of secrets sprinkled around for maximum health, stamina and lore. + dude the soundtrack & sound design, one of the best+ really good writing, not good delivery of it, but enjoyable lore+ combat has intuitive timing+ good stage variety, lots of different themes+ achievements, secrets, some replay value, hidden lore - I had to hug every wall in this game to find my way through it. It's bad enough that foreground often covers a lot of the exits, you can tell that devs deliberately made some areas cryptic as hell. At the very least maybe put little icons next to exits, and I think it needs to be more obvious how some power-ups work (that thing with puke and a face, and that tentacle puzzle - kinda random if you ask me). There is a map but it really did not help me that much. - One of my biggest problems with games in this genre is when a game does not give me a good reason to fight things. At one point I was just bored of pressing the same button and frankly it was just easier to dodge all enemies. Not every game needs to be an RPG, but I wanted just enough to change the pace, maybe another melee attack or two. The game was slightly lacking in combat variety and it had a few annoying segments with navigation, but ultimately the story and music saved it for me. The narrative was so unique, I don't think anyone can compare it to HLD beyond some visual similarities, this game deserves to be looked on its own. The length of the game is a little confusing because it shows credits more than once, make sure you explore it fully to get the complete experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very "maybe" "No", but I think I would be hard pressed to think of a situation where I would actually recommend this in it's current state, and I suspect the problems it has are unlikely to get addressed ever. It has an aesthetic and a mood and it mostly nails it. People compare some of it to Hyper Light Drifter but that's only certain parts of certain areas, otherwise it's just due to the pixel art being a similar color palette (and the dark clothes of the character you control).Exploration - this is where it gets into a double edged sword. There are a lot of secrets hidden around, and you are encouraged to find them. You also have some freedom in which of the 3 main goals you get after the intro area to head towards. And, to a point, the layout and connection is pretty interesting and clever. However, it has a LOT of really, staggeringly bad design choices as well. A lot of one-way paths, meaning that if you go past an area you want to explore more, you have to circle around a LOT of ground to check it again. This is compounded by what has to be the worst fast travel system in any game I've ever played that HAS a fast travel system. The fast travel itself isn't unlocked until you beat one of the 3 main goals you get marked for you. Meaning you could unlock it basically 90% of the way through a "normal" playthrough. That's bad enough, of course, but even if you unlock it right away or decide to go explore more, the fast travel hubs themselves are very scattered, in weird places, that often aren't helpful, and you have to be at one to use it which means the time saving is actually minimal to none unless you're going very far. Fast travel would be useful if it were just the checkpoints you find and you unlocked it earlier, or it would be even better if it were a combination of the two because those checkpoints aren't that common either. Between the god awful fast travel, the numerous one-way paths in already convoluted areas, and the general obtuseness of the secrets, it just doesn't feel fun at all to actually explore. You are frequently better off avoiding checkpoints so you can quit to the main menu and continue from the previous checkpoint, and not in a "speedrunning" kind of sense, in a "saves you 10 minutes of backtracking through an area with nothing in it with no other options to get there" sense.If the combat was super fun and interesting, maybe the backtracking and exploration would be more compelling, but it's basically a more tedious and less deep system that reminds me of the top-down Zelda games - hit once, back off, wait, hit again, repeat, except you have no interesting gear to help if you want to (you do get secondary weapons, they're just bad and use your dash energy which is a billion times more important to not die). Despite all that, it feels really close to being a pretty good game, or at least, pretty interesting, but it sits around 5/10 or 6/10 for me due to the myriad of inexcusable design choices. These aren't even in the spirit of old-school philosophies, they just are bad designs that seem obviously bad.

_childDocuments_.review: 40.8h (based on steam, 100% achievement, 2x playthrough) Yes (1 achievement). Yes (10 achievements). No. is a fast-paced action-adventure game with exploration as its focus. The game has a lot of vast maps and secret areas that you have to find.- You can tackle most areas in any order that you want- Secret areas and optional collectibles to find- Unique bosses- 2 endings- Exploring the whole map several times might tire out people at some point, especially if you're looking for well-hidden secrets- Some secrets require you to think hard to solve- One of the endings requires you to walk very long if you kill too much------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The game uses 2D pixelated graphics with vibrant colors and no outline on the characters. You might notice the similarities to  at first glance, although I can't say more about it at this point. The game is also making great use of lighting to enhance the environment aspect.I can't say the same with the portraits though. The portraits look like a rough sketch since I saw some pixels to be out of the line. The shading is also not adding any depth to the portrait. I'm not sure if it is intentional or not, but seeing that it happens consistently on most graphics, I assume it might be the artist's preferred style.To be honest, I was completely clueless when I started playing this game, which coincidentally resonates with the main character's loss of memory. Most characters talk either in riddles or hard to understand words, which makes me have to read the dialogues at least twice to understand what they meant.I still don't fully understand the story at this point, but at least I know what's happening. The well-polished world-building makes up for the lack of story and you'll understand most of what's happening in this world after you collect the optional collectibles.Exploration is the main part of the game. You'll explore a lot of areas, where most of the areas are so huge that you need to spend hours to explore the whole map. You might even explore the whole map several times just to find a missing collectible or new items after you unlock an item to explore more areas.The huge map might confuse people who have a bad sense of direction, although people who like to explore the whole map in every game like me might enjoy it more. However, the exploration becomes boring and tedious at some point, especially after you do it several times.Most of the area details aren't shown in the map since the map simplify the areas by drawing big squares as a representation of it. This also includes secret areas since you'll end up having to hug most walls and look for any secret pathways that you can explore.Some areas don't have enemies in it although some areas might annoy you with the number of enemies and constant battles. You can melee them with 3 combo attacks or use other items to kill them. I find the melee attack to be the most powerful though so I usually wipe them out with that.However, killing too many enemies might give you trouble when you finish one of the endings. You need to traverse a long path with the dead bodies of the enemies that you killed and it took me minutes to reach the end of the path when I killed 200+ enemies in my first run.There are 5+ bosses in this game. Most of them are unique and the difficulty varies on how many items and upgrades you have at that point. They are not hard to beat if you have most of the items and upgrades although I can't say the same if you only have some of them. Luckily, I still could beat most bosses after a few tries in my first run so you don't have to go crazy with the upgrade hunting just to beat the bosses.Aside from the melee attacks, you will have 9 extra items that will help you to either defeat the enemies or explore more areas. Most of them can be found when you explore the main areas although some are hidden in secret areas.The game mostly autosaves although you can only load your saves from checkpoints. Your health and stamina will be fully restored at checkpoints and you'll be respawned at checkpoints when you die. Speaking of dying, there is no penalty if you die.The game doesn't make clear with its story progression. I thought the game only has one ending and I was confused since the story just ends without me making sense of everything. There is no way I would have known that there is a second ending and there are more things to do after you finish the game if I didn't read  thread.As I said before, the game has 2 endings. You can continue the game after you get one of the endings so you can aim for both endings in the same run. You might want to start a new save if you want to aim for a specific achievement though.There are a lot of collectibles in the game; there are items and upgrades that will help you to fight bosses, stories to know more about the world-building, and  that do nothing but give you some tips. These collectibles are spread in several locations on the map and some are located in secret areas.There is a secret in the game where you have to figure out a puzzle to unlock some areas. These puzzles are too vague though; you might need to think hard to solve the ones with the hint provided and there is even one with no hint at all . There's no way I can solve them without  thread.Actually, the game isn't that long if you know where to go. I finished my first run in ~8h and then I continued to finish the second ending and unlock all secrets in ~21h. The game doesn't have any replay value aside for one achievement and it took me some time to figure out how the achievement works. The in-game timer still says that I completed my second run in ~3h though.The game crashed on me twice and there were times when I couldn't control my character after I moved to a new area. I couldn't seem to reproduce most cases though and I suspect that it's mostly because of my low spec device. I already sent the log to the devs to investigate the crashes and they are looking into it.The windowed mode is also not placed properly since it's moving a bit to the right and bottom, making it impossible for me to look at the bottom-right corner unless I'm playing in full screen.It's a great fast-paced action-adventure game that is focused on exploration. The story and progression might be a bit vague and require you to think hard to solve some of its secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but I just don't have that much fun with it.The comparisons with "Hyper Light Drifter" are accurate insofar as they relate to the story. The story of this game is indeed very interesting and the layered way that it goes about revealing certain aspects to you is charming.However, the gameplay is... repetitive. Even after getting the dash ability and chromatic aberration, I couldn't bring myself to enjoy the core combat loop. Hit, run away, hit, blast. It's very plodding and dull. In "Hyper Light Drifter" you have a grand time dodging, weaving, finessing your way through combat. Here, I'd rather avoid combat altogether. The "puzzles" aren't anything to write home about, either.If you're okay with churning through the combat to get at the story beneath, this can be a good game. But I can't personally justify the time required to do so (16 hours, as it says on the box).

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? YES. It is a labor of love in pixel art, a story-telling masterpiece in a dystopian world, full of exploration, discovery, and combat.  You play a limping guy who has lost his memory, and you have an AI named Alibii attached to your brain. Alibii is your guide, your mentor. Working for the Infinite Empire, your task is to carry Alibii into the heart of the enemy territory where she can dismantle the terrorists network from within. Traverse through interconnected levels in an open world action RPG, finding items, meeting characters, killing bosses. The story is often told through the environement, by watching closely you learn about the dystopian world you travel through. Alibii talks to you, but she never really explains everything, she just throws tiny bits of information at you.The tutorial takes place in a rather clean Cloud City, but soon you find yourself in a decaying, polluted world - a junkyard, a desert, a barren pit or a destroyed city. There is quite a lot to discover, the gameworld is big. Find chuncks of your memory to learn more about who and where you really are. The game starts slow, you won't enjoy it if you are looking for an ultra-fast action only title, but you will enjoy it when you love to dive deep into this strange world and have fun discovering its secrets (killing a bunch of opponents on the way).Controller worked fine, ultrawidescreen is not supported.Great action RPG in pixel art with a focus on exploring and understanding a dystopian world.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly very frustrated that I can't seem to enjoy this game. I believe much of what makes up a video game of this style come from three places: Combat, Level Design, and Story. This game has such a mixed bag of critical elements that I think it's difficult to review. But here I am. I wanted to play this game more before reviewing, but eventually my frustration levels reached their limit and I thought: "Why am I playing this?"The combat is essential to these types of games. It needs to be engaging and fun. Monolith of Minds do a decent job of it, but it's nothing special at all. It's very basic, and sometimes can seem like a chore. I found myself running around enemies to get to more important sections of levels because there was usually no reward. There is also a problem with speed of combat. The player slows down when attacking, but enemies do not. Therefore, timing attacks matter less because there is a higher chance of you being hit just because...that's how the game is.While the graphics are pretty, the level design is very flawed. There's not really a clear sense of where you should be going until you get through the first hour (and maybe next 30 mins) of the game. Even then, the map isn't explained to you. Backtracking is something you will be doing regularly.The story is honestly an absolute mess. I am so disappointed in this aspect of the game. The opening scene probably makes sense towards the end of the game, but you go from some possible flashback to dropped right in the middle of the game without any backstory. The game then tries to make sense of this with a character that appears during a few critical scenes. Later it goes down a different path. It's just a mess. On top of that, dialogue with NPCs is unfathomable. I'm not sure why they decided to have so many NPCs with useless dialogue, but that's what you get. Many of these are jokes that sometimes seem to make fun of the game itself. Think along the lines of "wow, why did we put so much dialogue in here?". Could be funny if any other aspects of the game were good.I still have no clue what some pickup-able items do. Eventually I accidentally blew all of my "money" on unlocking part of the map (???). I had no idea what the currency was, and didn't understand that a transaction was taking place. The part of the map I unlocked led to nowhere, and just looped back around to the starting area I paid at. Part of the confusion for me is that there is not choose-able dialogue. You simply walk up to NPCs to talk with them / make decisions.I want to say that I believe that this game could've been great, or with some tweaks it could be good...but having just written all of these negative things, I can't. This is just my opinion, as there are quite a few positive reviews. Good luck with future endeavors, Monolith of Minds. Thank you for supporting Linux. Godot is a wonderful tool, and I appreciate that you used other open-source tools for developing this game. I'll be looking out for your next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Was really hoping I'd like this one, and while there are a fair number of good ideas and features to this, overall I think it's kind of a miss for me. It's not a bad game per se, but I wouldn't really call it good either. There are lot of almost good things here, though.Some examples of "almost good:"The combat has some interesting options but it feels a little stiff and clunky. Slow stamina recharge and limited attack directions bring this down a bit.The environments look good but there is a lack of clarity in what is the foreground and background in a lot of places. Thankfully you won't die from running off an edge or something, but you probably will run into a lot of barriers that look like pathways or you just won't notice the bridge you need to cross.The story and lore seem interesting but they aren't really allowed to flourish, if that makes sense.Everything is weird. Bizarre graffiti covers a city populated by sentient file boxes. A giant cat tunnels through the ground to eat you in the desert. A giant worm eats you when you play music (that's the fast travel system). You turn into a tiny version of that worm because a shattered skinless flesh giant made a DnD character sheet for you. There is a whale named God who sneezes eyeballs at you. This game is strange, but it doesn't really seem to have a rhyme or reason to it.There are other issues with this, too, but that kinda gives a glimpse into my feelings towards the game. I was hoping for a similar experience to HLD, and while it is in the same ballpark, Resolutiion strikes out for me. I give it 2/5 kittens you accidentally found while high on blue goo.
_childDocuments_.name: Resolutiion

_childDocuments_.review: Resolutiion shares many similarities with Hyper Light Drifter, particularly in looks and tone. It's an action RPG featuring pixel graphics, a somewhat confounding plot and retro music. However, whilst Resolutiion starts off in a rather derivative fashion, it quickly blossoms into something really creative, featuring puzzles and gameplay mechanics that are fresh and unique. Combat is slower, more methodical than Hyper Light Drifter. Enemies often only require a few hits, but timing is everything. You have to stand still when firing your revolver, which I imagine will upset some. Your abilities use up your energy very quickly, so it's very much a case of attack, retreat, cool-down, attack.  Some of the upgrades are truly bizarre; one allows you to play an instrument to fast travel the map , whilst another allows you to turn yourself into a worm to access secret areas. The final upgrade is super inventive and subverts the game entirely - but I won't spoil the discovery here.I think what sets Resolutiion apart from HLD, and similar pixel action RPGs, is its post game content - if you can call it that. The end is not really the end, rather just the beginning, and reverses much of what you've already done. There's a further secret collectable quest that some players will never see. The developers have spent a long time crafting this game - and it shows. It really is a labour of love. There are secrets and puzzles that wouldn't be amiss in a game like FEZ.To see everything, you're looking at a playtime of up to 20 hours. I've heard there's future DLC planned too, which will add even more to the game. Give Resolutiion a chance, and you'll see why it's one of my favourite indies of 2020.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: "If it's not fun, why bother"This quote rings true the more I spend time with this game. Please note that my real playtime is 4 hours as I play this game offline on my Steam Deck.I initially bought this thinking that it will be as good as Hyper Light Drifter, with the same art style and all. But this game just feels like a cheap dollar store imitation of HLD.Starting off with the gameplay, immediately I noticed that I could just hold the attack button to initiate the combo. And it didn't exactly feel good as the combo ender animation only consists of 3 frames, I felt it was really low effort. Then I attacked an enemy, and it just did not feel punchy or had an impact on the enemy at all. Enemies are spongy but not in a good way like in HLD because the game does not let you feel the impact with each of your swing, it just felt flat. Oh, and you can get the "dash" ability about an hour into the game. I say "dash" because it's a sprint button that accelerates your movement speed rather than rolling in Dark Souls or dashing in HLD, it didn't exactly feel good to use either as this ability is more used to get out of your opponent's attack range and close in on them faster. The gun is useless and does miniscule amount of damage and use up your energy, which the dash also uses.On the dialogue side, the writing is nonsensical, and I hate to say that word, but it is "cringe". I prefer a more "show, don't tell" approach in regard to cryptic games like these, but these dialogues just took me out of it. I have played games that have cryptic dialogues like Hylics but this game, there is something that I can't quite put my finger on that makes me dislike it very much, pretentious probably?And the music, god the music, it's so generic. In HLD, the ost was so atmospheric and subtle, the music accomodated the environments that you were in, which were ruins, past civilizations that are now desolate and empty. Here it's just the same generic Synthwave chords with 5 - 7 notes played over and over throughout every stages.Overall, I do not vibe with this game, it just makes me want to replay Hyper Light Drifter instead. This game just feels like a cheap soulless imitation of a great game instead. I do not often drop games, but I'd rather not waste my time playing something that I don't like or not immersed in its universe/story.

_childDocuments_.review: after 3 hours now: truly a piece of art, in every sense! (after 6 hours, I must confess, it gets a little bit boring/repetitive.)At first I thought: "wow!", because of the pixel art, but after a few minutes: what a crappy hyper-light-drifter-rip off, with slow movement and it seemed as it was all about grinding (mashing objects and nothing else) etc. I stopped playing, waited one day, gave the game one more chance and it really happened: I got hooked. In fact, of course the influence is obvious, this game takes the Hyper-Light-Drifter influence - also other relevant games - and uses it to create something new, more story driven, outstanding. _childDocuments_.review: Alright so the reason why I write a review so fast is because I've already completed the switch version of the game, and to be honest, I LOVE THIS GAME.And yes, the fighting system is basic, the pixel art may seem like other games and the story and map is confusing at first, I know.So why do I like it so much ?First, the soundtrack. It is a pure MASTERPIECE. Each song has an identity, the assault tracks are absolutely AWESOME and bring you an energy like you've never seen beforeSecond, the story. It may not seem like it, but Resolutiion has a very complex story, which also leaves space for the players to try to make theories and figure out "What the hell happened here ?"The characters and their designs also give that feeling that makes you wonder about the things behind.Then, there's the look of the game. Everything stands out for me on that part. The minimalistic yet very efficient pixel art, the lights and shadows, the various zones of the game and their elements, the characters and ennemies, they all have something very unique in them, which is again a great thingNow for the things that are not good but not bad :The map system. It's.. difficult, at times, to figure out where you have to go through to get to an objective. It takes some time to actually understand how to read the game's map, but once you get it, you won't struggle anymore.The level design also has issues in some places. The game wants you to explore around but sometimes doesn't make efforts to try to force you to do so, aside of showing you that you need a certain item to keep going but without giving you any idea of where it is, until somehow you stumble upon it.And finally the fighting system and certain items : Again the combat system is very repetitive. Hit, run to avoid attacks, hit, repeat. It may be annoying for certain players but i personally don't mind, as the lack of other options brings an interesting challenge at times against some bosses that can make you feel like in a bullet hell.As for the items, there are some that you can just finish the game without using them, at all.The last thing I have to say in this review before concluding is that, and it's fully personnal, the difficulty of the game is perfectly adjusted for me. The bosses go from easy to really challenging, giving you a feeling of progress that only a few games gave me.In short, Resolutiion is great but misunderstood. It suffers from certain aspects that most gamers aren't used to see, but if you manage to like, or at least accept those aspects, and dig a bit deeper in the world that the game offers.. you might find a true masterpiece, that can bring your imagination to whole new places, with those awesome soundtracks and that complex universe hidden under layers of confusion. And that. That's what I seek in modern games. Developpers have to make us imagine things without revealing all to us. And Monolith of minds perfectly understood it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's magnificent. The atmosphere is luscious and fitting, the music is outstanding and the combat is smooth and fast. I enjoyed the story, letting the player clue together the plot and proceed freely with enough direction to go anywhere in this open-world game that's a lot smarter than it might initially seem for this genre.Killing things randomly actually carries weight, when you take an enemy out they crash to their knees or wave their arms panicking and you can give them mercy and just leave or finish them off. NPC's can be attacked or spared in the same way, their behavior and dialogue responding appropriately. Butchering everyone has a real effect, and thorough exploration and patient guesswork is always worth the discovery.Each area is distinct and fun to explore, the boss fights are intense and vivid. The difficulty of the game overall is about average, it's telling a story and creating a world to uncover more than the laser-focus on combat such as Dead Cells or whatever. That's not to say the combat is bad, it's fluid and fun and easy to pick up. It's fast and well-animated. The game was great, the ending that you have to dig deeper to achieve was awesome and really rewards those who play passed the credits.Edit: needed to say again, the music is AWESOME.
