_childDocuments_.review: I got into vanilla DF a few years ago and despite the insanely steep learning curve I managed to find my footing a put a few dozen hours into the game. The game is ridiculously complex and overwhelming for new players, and even with this "premium" version of the game which adds mouse support (didn't exist in vanilla, it's completely keyboard controlled), graphics (in the truest sense of the word, vanilla is text ASCII display unless you download a community made graphics pack), helpful popups (vanilla didn't deign to tell you anything), and bare bones UI (icons and tooltips?? fancy) its still completely overwhelming. I've built my fortress into a thriving community of 60+ inhabitants and there are still things I don't know how to do (like streamlining soap production or manipulating water without killing everyone). If you've ever looked at DF and thought "that seems interesting" but held off cause you're intimidated by its deserved reputation of being nearly impenetrable, well it's still impenetrable but this is as accessible as its going to get.
_childDocuments_.name: Dwarf Fortress

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game on and off for about 15 years.For any new player... it's not like most games. It has it's flaws, even in the steam version the controls are complex and take quite a long time to get used to. But there's a reason it has a cult following. it has depth like few other games.I think I can summarise with one of my favorite dev-log entries:Dev Log: "...the necromancer managed to raise both a skeleton and a walking hollow skin... which I suppose I'll keep since it makes about as much sense as a walking skeleton."It's a hard game to get started playing but it's worth the effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Dwarf Fortress

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played the original Dwarf Fortress because I just couldn't bear the UI\UX of the ASCII graphics, so I've been waiting for this release for a very long time.The tutorial felt nice but as I kept playing I started feeling more and more uncomfortable.And here am I - about to put negative review on the game with tons of fans and 98% positive reviews.I do understand that sprites is better that ASCII graphics but there are literally no animations for the dwarfs. Is he working, talking or walking - you cannot be completely sure until you select him. I do understand that those limitations may be imposed by engine's complexity, but it feels like DF is still a text game with some sprites on top of it.I've decided to plant some seeds. Read through the help..As the tutorial recommended, I've created a farm plot and selected 'Plump Helmets'A few minutes later I've come to check how the plants were to find out that my selected option says 'No seeds'After a few seconds dwarfs 'teleport' to my plot, stand on it, and then go away. The recently selected option says 'No seeds' as well.However, I've noticed that there's a list of items at the bottom of the menu - with my seeds in it.I am still not sure whether they've been planted properly since plot looked exactly the same - no visual indication of my seeds at all.That one is pretty much the same as the previous point, but a bit broader.The game seems to dislike numbers. Once more, this is game about survival in the harsh world and it doesn't give you information about itself.I wanna assign a new worker for mining. I open the jobs list. How many information about suitability of the workers I get?Turns out only a single line - either the person is a miner already or you get literally no info. Maybe the dwarf dislikes mining? (sounds blasphemous but everything can happen)You wanna see stats - there are only text descriptions. Is 'Adept' better than 'Skilled'? Find out on your own.There are literally lots of free space in the menus but the game doesn't utilize them at all.The words highlighted with colors has no tooltips. Come on, that's not rocket science - most RPGs do that, Rim World does that. Why cannot DF just give me the information it already has inside of it? I wanna see  the numbers and be able to tell which dwarf  wins through a brief glance at a single stats list\table.I wanted to make a few cups for dwarfs since they got debuf for drinking without cup\mud.I've opened workshop, searched 'CUP' - no results.There's a submenu called wood - you open it and then you can select cup.?Now you need to make 7 cups and there's no duplicate task button - only repeat infinitely (imagine spending all your wood on cups).Also, imagine yourself opening some menu with filter and starting typing. Ideally, your results will be filtered, or at least nothing happens. But in DF, where every button is a shortcut, you will start doing things. It's not a major issue, but I've faced it dozens of times through first hour.Limiting user input to the active menu doesn't feel  hard.Dwarf Fortress did a lot for the gaming industry - there's no doubt. But as a modern game it just feels too unpolished. I would not put the negative review if this was an Early Access, but after 11 years of development I've been expecting much more.Main killer feature of the update - graphics - are not really used to give the player information about what's happening on the screen. Neither does the menus.I would really want to love this game. In it's current state, though, it's still too harsh for those get used to modern game design.P.S. Feel free to call me a casual player if you'd like.
_childDocuments_.name: Dwarf Fortress

_childDocuments_.review: I deeply respect the long history of this game, and how it has been a core influence on so many games that followed.But right now? I can't honestly recommend it. If you have already played it, enjoyed it, and would like to do so again, then stop reading my review and go have fun. But if this game is new to you at this point, don't bother. It defined a genre, but there are newer and better incarnations of the central concept. This was the historical start of a whole new genre, but at this point, it shouldn't be your start in this genre. The games that have drawn inspiration from this one have done great work to refine the central concepts into something much more enjoyable. They cut the fat and retained the meat.
_childDocuments_.name: Dwarf Fortress

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for 150 hours I just want to take some time to thank the Adams brother for dedicating the time requires to make the best story generator I've ever played.  I am not an OG or a long time player, but a newbie just floundering my way through forts getting my ass handed to me, and ive never had so much fun in my life!  I've died to salt water crocs, flooding, dehydration, ghosts, spiraling rage, and a few hard restarts after failing at base design.  I soldier on and aim to create a fort designed to weaponize forgotten beasts!!  If you are a fan of rouge likes or a DND fan or an RTS fan this is the game for you.  This is one of the most well made games ive ever played!

name: Panzer Paladin
detailed_description: User-forged Weapons Showcase Forge your own custom melee weapons with the Blacksmith and find them on the Panzer Paladin Steam Workshop. Share them with your friends and upvote your favorite weapons crafted by the community. About the Game The sight of giant swords blazing through the night sky might be hair-raising, but stand your ground! The sinister Ravenous and his legions of brutal demons are poised for battle. Even all the armies of the world can’t stop them, but humanity has one final ace in the hole: cutting-edge power armor called Paladin. It's now up to a strong-willed android named Flame to become a Squire, pilot the Paladin and track down all Weapon Keepers and their diabolical leader. The showdown between mankind’s technological prowess and the powerful forces of the occult has begun! Seize weapons from the denizens of the Netherworld and give them a taste of their own medicine! Show them the power of cutting-edge technology fused with masterful swordplay. Slash, bash and thrust your way through a series of mind-blowing levels around the world, all of it rendered in glorious 8-bit graphics! Hop in your Paladin and take up arms! An engaging action-platformer with fun and intuitive swordplay! Take control of Grit, the mighty Paladin power armor, or eject and play as Flame, the small-but-swift Squire pilot! Robots meet demons! Crush the forces of the occult with the power of cutting-edge technology! Over 100 melee weapons to seize from enemies! Forge your own custom melee weapons with the Blacksmith and find them on the Panzer Paladin Steam Workshop. Use weapons profusely: wield, throw, or shatter them! Snap a weapon in half to cast a powerful spell! Slash, bash and thrust your way through 17 mind-blowing levels located around the world! Carefully crafted 8-bit graphics, just like you remember them! CHALLENGE CORE CONTENT UPDATE This free content update includes the following new features: New Challenge Mode with 11 rooms to truly test your skills Speedrun replay and leaderboard now available for all new rooms Brand new Classic 8-bit Soundtrack option Blacksmith weapons storage increased Panzer Paladin is an action-platformer game featuring intuitive swordplay mechanics. The protagonist pilots the Paladin power armor to fight giant demons by using their own weapons against them. Swordplay is the core of the game mechanics in Panzer Paladin. The player can equip and use any weapon dropped by defeated enemies, attack or block, aim high or low, use weapons advantageously through a rock-paper-scissors style weapon type system, and cast spells by breaking weapons. Weapons abound in levels, so the player is encouraged to use them profusely. The Paladin is the main way to fight enemies, but players can also eject and control Flame, the small-but-swift Squire pilot. Flame uses a laser whip to attack enemies, swing across gaps, and even recharge the Paladin’s energy. Giant weapons — swords, lances, hammers — hailing from the dark depths of space, blazed across the sky and pierced their way through historic locations all around the world. As a declaration of war against mankind, the Parthenon, atop the Acropolis of Athens, was first to be cut through by an ominous blade. Upon impact, each of the weapons opened a breach in the fabric of reality and unleashed legions of colossal demons. In anticipation of such unforeseen Earth-threatening events, the International Security Council formed Gauntlet, a science committee developing super-sophisticated defense technologies. Gauntlet discovers that denizens of the Netherworld can only be defeated by their own weapons. Spirit Weapons are forged with spirits of the deceased and humans can’t brandish them without becoming corrupted by their foul energy... However, a machine would be immune to demonic corruption! Gauntlet recommissions Flame, a former rescue operations android, to become a Squire. She takes control of Grit, the last remaining Paladin unit — a state-of-the-art suit of power armor capable of wielding Spirit Weapons. To arms! Overseeing operations from aboard the Avalon, their flying headquarters, Gauntlet is ready. The showdown between mankind’s technological prowess and the powerful forces of the occult has begun! It's up to Flame and Grit to defeat the Weapon Keepers, and ultimately face off against Ravenous, the sinister leader of the invasion.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game that I think a lot of the negative reviews miss the point of this entirely. I wasn't going to write a review till I saw people slamming mechanics that even I'm grasping and I'm dumb & I've only got 2 hours in it. The game is about balancing your weapons.Each weapon has benefits to using, some have longer reach, more damage and a skill if you shatter it.Reviews say it's BS that you throw a weapon and it breaks, what they seem to be missing is this attack amplifies the weapon's damage massively when thrown.Okay, say your  weapon has 1 swing left in it, you can throw it and get possibly 8x or more damage out of it instead of one swing. Each weapon's throw damage is different & can devastate small enemies or do solid damage to a boss. "The checkpoints take a weapon sacrifice but offer no reward" You don't understand the mechanics of the game at all if this is your complaint. Again, each weapon has a skill if you shatter the weapon, they can heal you, buff your attack/def, increase the durability of any weapon drawn for a while- and AFTER the level is done you can sacrifice weapons in a lab to increase your mech's HP. So, you have to look through your gear and see which one you're willing to part with so you can have a checkpoint, meaning you're either missing out on points for an max HP upgrade or a good weapon in combat that could have a good skill. You have to pick what you want. Weapon sacrifice is ENCOURAGED to a point. Have too many weapons and you have to fight a mini-boss in the stage- but if you beat him you can get a really powerful weapon EVERY, TIME. A weapon you can even design & customize the stats of. I understand not liking the mechanics & desiring a more simple gameplay, but people complaining about the mechanics & saying they don't make any sense either played 1 level and didn't bother trying to grasp it further or just had no interest. And if you don't like having to gather weapons in stages as you go to gather weapons? Replay an old/easy level, gather weapons and sacrifice them to buff your HP a bunch. Which you don't really need to do. HP replenishing  weapons are fairly plentiful, you can carry them between levels and there's also healing stations. It's less about the weapon being used and more about the skill. Use a weapon with durability up, fight till it's about to break- shatter it before it does to buff the next weapon with more damage and crush enemies for a bit with far more durability. I'm not really into precision platformers and this one is kind of that (no wall jumping, dashing, tight jumps) but there's some mobility options that make it more fun for me and, the best part- you don't have Castlevania knockback. Getting hit isn't gonna send you 10 feet into a pit. You barely move. Now if you get hit OVER a pit, you fall straight down.Basically: I like Mega Man X more than Mega Man classic. It's adapted Blaster Master's ability to get out of your vehicle and run around as the pilot. But with a bit more of a reliable character with a stronger weapon. Negatives?There are some stretches without a checkpoint & one level had a lot of pits that was frustrating while I was trying to learn the game.It's clear there's a lot of heart & effort in the game, I think the durability works well in this game & really forces you to use you to think on the weapon you fight with, use the skill of and sacrifice. I recommend it even with my disinterest in precision platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love retro platformers and wanted to like this game, unfortunately it was not meant to be. I've played up to the first level of the "Wily fortress"-esque final stretch on normal.Good things: the presentation is really good. Each stage looks gorgeous and a lot of effort was put into the backgrounds. Stuff like the cool intro when starting a stage is nice. The music was alright but a bit 8-bit generic (still some tunes were stuck in my head, so that's a good sign that at least the game has good tunes). Generally the bosses are fun to figure out and are satisfying to fight. Almost all my fun when playing this game came from (most) boss fights.Not much else to say about the good, so let's move on to the bad.- The stage design is subpar and uninspired. Most of them are long hallways with enemies and holes, every now and then the stage becomes vertical aaaaand that's about it. This would've been fine if the enemies threw in some spice, but...- ... The enemies are also terribly boring and uninspired. They get recycled over and over and over again, with every stage adding one or two new enemies (if any) and they aren't that interesting either. How many times were those knights and bugs reused? Even in the bit of the final stretch I played they were used constantly. Classic NES Megaman games, which this game takes great inspiration from, added new enemies in every stage and the design of those stages were much more varied. Even in the later Megaman NES games when they started to run out of ideas and some stages became more repetitive, they threw in cool new enemies and situations that used them well, so overall the experience was much more rewarding. In this game the stages were constantly the same thing over and over again and the enemies were so boring to fight.- The game has some enemies that utilized your mecha's shield, the so-called Zelda II enemies. Those were fine on your couple first stages until they became more of a chore to fight. Once you get the hang of it they become really easy so I opted to skip them jumping over them. The only enemies that used the shield mechanic interestingly just... became boring as well.- The game is very easy and demands very little platforming skills outside of a few key points, which are very unfair difficulty spikes, although calling them difficulty spikes is a disservice because most of them were cheap deaths. For example, almost every stage has these very meh sections outside your mech. They felt tacked in just to have a platforming section using the girl since all of them consisted on a couple of grapple jumps until you can call your mech again. One of them in Tanzania has you grapple from one point to the other and, since it's your first time through, I waited for a full cycle to know where I'm jumping to. Grave mistake. On the other side there was an enemy that throws a bullet the second it appears on screen. Since I didn't jump on the very first possible cycle, there was nothing I could do but take the bullet mid grapple and die. Now that I knew that I had to jump on the very first cycle it became trivial, but that's exactly why this is so bad: a cheap death. These grapple sections are notorious for stuff like this, since this has happened to me at least 2 more times. The final level that I played (in the Wily Fortress) has right before the boss these incredibly weird spike jumps. Hitboxes in this game are mad weird, and I was never able to get comfortable with the mech's one. Spikes aren't instant death but they completely stop your movement, so here I am trying to maneuver through these weird spike jumps over a death pit and the moment you touch one you stop in your tracks and die. This part feels more like an oversight to me than anything, idk. As I said, overall the rest of the game is very easy, bosses usually die in 1 or 2 tries if any, but these unfair spots just make it very clear how unpolished this game is. I love difficult games, but this is not how you make your game hard.The China boss battle also has a breath attack that appears instantly accross the screen without much warning. That was a decision.- The game has tons of weapons but they all function the same. The only thing that you should care between weapons is its length and maybe its attack power in bosses. The longer weapons are strictly better for obvious reasons. There's no reason for a falchion, a mace and a spear to be essentially the same weapon, but it's exactly what it is. Now, I think this is this way because the game has a weapon design option, which is pretty cool and they didn't want to have weird hitboxes, but I would gladly sacrifice this option if that meant some variation between weapons. There's also a mechanic that if you carry too many weapons a miniboss appears after the first checkpoint of a stage. It's the same everytime, even in the final stretch of the game. Just an inconvienience and after the sixth time fighting him it's just whatever. If there are other aspects to the items burden mechanic I have no idea what those are. Also apparently there are rock paper scissors weaknesses for bosses. Didn't know about this until I read it on the Internet. Go figure.- Using weapons to upgrade your mech was such a cool idea, but there are only 5 HP upgrades. That's it. Nothing more. No cool new movement options, no attack or defense buffs, no temporary items (something that is only in effect during one stage), no cosmetics, no nothing. Why?Overall, and after all this ranting, I don't think this is a bad game. It's a mediocre one slightly tilting towards bad. It takes many ideas but doesn't execute any of them particularly well, on top of being a very simple game with no depth to the controls. Uninteresting linear stages, boring enemies that get reused constantly as pallette swaps, weapons that all function the same, the use of weapons to upgrade your mech with so much potential but ultimatelly does nothing, some VERY cheap moments and insta death traps without prior knowledge of the level or clunky hitboxes... All these issues pile one on top of the other making this experience really sour, until I quit the game.I'm sure there was a lot of heart and passion put into this game but for this price, I can't recommend it. If this came out 8 or so years ago before everyone's standards for indie platformers became so high (Hollow Knight, Shovel Knight, The Messenger, Blasphemous, Bloodstained, etc. etc.) I for sure would have liked it. But that wasn't the case, especially for this price. I know the team is capable of something very good, but it just needs much more polish and thought behind the game's mechanics.I recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I love to play games on my Commodore Amiga 1200, connected to the large TV in the living room. It just gives me a good feeling to play those games from my childhood again. Panzer Paladin gives me the same feeling. It is just like from the good old times. You play an android piloting a large battle mech and fighting alien invaders all around the Earth. Fight with large melee weapons as mech, or leave the mech and use your laser whip. Reach the end of the level and defeat the boss. All this in a game that looks, plays and sounds like it was made in the late 80s during the heyday of the home computers and the NES. So, is it a masterpiece? For me, yes. Solid retro action platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: It kinda pains me to give this game a negative review, as I've really enjoyed Mercenary Kings, Ninja Senki DX and NES style action games as that's what I grew up with. Tribute games puts out some stuff I really like, but I think this one in particular needs more refinements.First issue is that there's too long of a stretch in between stages without an additional checkpoint, so if you fall in a pit or something, prepared to redo quite a bit from your last checkpoint. Over and over.Second is the upgrade system, but really a lack thereof. You get only 5 chances to upgrade, but it's all only hp- and a very TINY upgrade it is at that. More varied upgrades would've been appreciated.Third is the weapons. It basically boils down to the one with the longest reach is best, all the others only serve to use a checkpoint or break it for an ability. And speaking of abilities, it puts an icon in the screen but you have no idea how long it lasts at all unless its for extra hp, (which again, isnt all that much). Fourth is difficulty. I played in normal and felt like it was quite difficult. My characters hitbox felt too big, and also the sprite is somewhat large too which doesn't help. Also, when you jump and do an attack upward it gives you another small boost upward too which feels unnatural. Character movement speed is a little too slow for my tastes and the jumping feels floaty as well.Chunky 2d pixel art and soundtrack is great, and the simple storyline flows pretty well. I made it to this games version of Wily's Castle and just wasn't having fun anymore. If they ever tweak some stuff I'll gladly give it another go and see what happens.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: I feel the same way playing this as I do with every other Tribute Games title. Great concept, but the gameplay is so slow and repetitive, it feels like they borrow too much from old games, including the bad.[] MovementStiff jump/fall speed and movement. You can get out of Grit (your mech) as the pilot (Flame), but her segments are 10% of most maps, save the last 2-3 stages. They barely last and it's too bad.[] WeaponsVery tedious weapon durability mechanic. Your strategy will quickly bog down to using each weapon and before its last durability point, break it to use its special ability. Few are interesting. You can throw a weapon, but it is destroyed in one shot and is never really worth it.[] Weapon Variety You get hundreds of weapons (dirks, glaives, hammers, etc) and they all have the exact same singular thrust attack. There's no basic combo, there's no charge attack, nothing. Aside from reach for long weapons and some cooldown to spam the attack button again, they all function the same. Within two minutes you will understand this and feel a bit cheated as the differences are just cosmetic and more as a tool to create pop culture references. There are blocks in the world which guard weapons and can only be destroyed if you use the right weapon type (blunt weapons like hammers, thrust weapons like lances or swords, etc). But that fantasy quickly evaporates when you realize that yes, they are all still just thrust attacks. [] UpgradesYou can upgrade Grit by melting weapons you found, which is fine, but the only thing you can do is increase his health. There could have been upgrades to mitigate durability loss, increase hit rate, improve the back-dash, something.[] Same Enemies EverywhereThey really abuse the Zelda II shielded enemy type where if the their shield is up you crouch to stab them and if they crouch, you stand to stab them. This gets boring fast as many maps have easily a handful of them and for no reason. Once you realize you can just DuckTales/ShovelKnight bounce over them and ignore them, they become more of a hurdle than a fun challenge to look forward to.[] StagesLast too long and there are too many (17) for the gameplay available. There is a Wily fortress at the end and it's seven stages long. [] BossesSome bosses have no tells in the animations of their attacks leading to a lot of free hits. Again, these are all small gripes which add up and make it feel like they mean well, but it isn't fun.I mention the most egregious things because it's worth taking into account. Concept is never really the issue when I play Tribute titles, if they just make some more fast-paced and deep gameplay, I'm all in.

_childDocuments_.review: Same as the Switch version, only it has workshop support.Basically a combination of several game idesBlaster Master ( small pilot controls, exitiing mech )Flinthook ( their previous title ) the grappling mechanicsMegaman  ( chooseable levels by By Boss ) Shovel knight ( it's firmly rooted in retro game territory, but with upgrades, and checkpoints in levels ( there's more influences, but these feel the strongest ) Seems to be the same engine as Ninja senki DX ( which means you have no resolution options, windows at 1280x720 or fullscreen to whatever your monitor is  - and the CRT filters are back as well ) You basically are playing a big dumb 70's Anime mech pilot, complete with sentient mech.You have to stop all the alien enemies ( weapons ) Megaman style, and you do this by swinging your big dumb mech arms with melee weps.The melee weps play a huge role, they're your main form of attack ( but not the only one ) they also serve as a means to enable a checkpoint ( using the wep in the process ) You coillect various ones, find them stuffed in breakable walls ala Castlevania , sometimes you get rare ones from checkpoint cutscenes ( without spoiling what that means ) You can throw them, whack enemies with em, pogo jump by attacking downward, or gain some extra air by attacking upwards as well.Oh, and you can break your wep for a magical attack. You can hold several weps at once - and, when the level is completed, youre given the opportunity to exchange weps to upgrade your mech.The blastermaster influence is strong here, oftentimes you are leaving your mech to go on foot ( you also have a wep as apilot, a n energy lasso thing that you can also use to grapple across hazards ) You find charging bases for your mech, and pads to summon one to you ( in case you break it, I htink .. haven't broken it yet, but it will summon one to the platform ) The story is played out in cheesy 70's anime style, and it's clear the devs put a lot of passion into the presentation, because despite a limited color palette and pixel density, they did a bangup job making it look sleek, and stylized, right down to the loading screens for the levels themselves.I have more time on Switch, but I'll probably play this version more once the Steam workshop starts cookin.it really is a perfect Switch game, with the pickup and play any time functionality the console offers.so that's your choice; mobile gaming, or steamworkshop?The game only runs at 60 fps as well, and I severely doubt it supports UWS.recommended to people that enjoy the tribute games' lineup, retro platformers in general, or big dum 70's anime mechs.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: It almost pains me to say but Panzer Paladin is the epitome of a 'meh' experience. The game is fun during the first 2 levels or so - but once you realize that the game is not going to introduce any new mechanics or challenges throughout the campaign, the gameplay loop quickly wears out its welcome.There are a whopping 17 levels in Panzer Paladin. Normally, this might be a good thing but each level in this game plays exactly the same way - the player will navigate through a somewhat boring and tedious platforming section before reaching a boss battle at the end of the level. To its credit, the boss battles in Panzer Paladin are fun and each feels unique. Sadly, the monotony of the platforming areas makes getting to these boss battles more of a chore than an exciting prelude. If I were to recommend this game, it would be with the caveat that you can get a copy for EXTREMELY CHEAP. Like, I'm talking <$3 USD kind of cheap. Moreover, I'd only recommend it to folks with a deep-rooted passion for old-school, 8-bit, Mega Man-style games. The again, what do I know? I'm just some guy. Maybe this just isn't my type of game. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

_childDocuments_.review: After playing and succesfully completing the main story i can finally put up my review for it :3As an old ass gamer who was born and raised in the 90's seeing and playing this 8-bit homage is a full dive into the nostalgia, where i've been playing such classic games like: Chip'n Dale, Castlevania, Darkwing duck, Megaman and yatta-yatta through all of mine summer break.Well if you're still with me, you're gonna love what you gonna read next ;)You're piloting the mech and travel across the world (megaman stage select style) to fight the Mythical Spirits who posses the sacred weapons with super powers, which came from space. So what you gonna do, use these weapons to rule over the world or break em all in order to save it and keep the balance?The PROs:+ The game resembles classic titles like Megaman / Transformers / Castlevania in terms of gameplay style and the pace+ 8-bit large pixel graphics (with few screen filters for true nostalgia)+ High difficulty spikes, due to the large distance to checkpoints and deadly pits+ Cool & cheerful 8-bit soundtrack loops and sfx!+ 10 countries to visit ;)+ Lots of weapons (and the ability to create your own, or download others works via Steam Workshop)+ There are destructible walls with secrets, with weapons or 1up's+ Interesting bosses+ You can exit the robot and play as the pilot+ There's a REMIX mode, speedrun, and tournament for all of your needs and replayability ;3For CONs:- Difficulty spikes, you can get easily frustrated by that, cause you're gonna restart the whole level if you're not careful sometimes- Hitboxes on the enemies and mecha are confusing and jank, and that combined with clunky jump speed and height, leads to a lot of way too difficult jumps and damage that doesn’t feel like it should have happened.- Out of mecha sections feel tacked on and forced. The Pilot lack of an upwards strike and unforgiving, grapple based platforming which can lead you to the restarting the level.- Weapons all swing the same no matter the type they are (Sword, Spear, Hammer)

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but just like most Tribute Games's products, it looks amazing and has a neat concept but it's just executed terribly.In this game you play as a mech, his normal attack is a punch and when you kill some enemies there is a chance a weapon might drop, these weapons have durability and also a "spell" that activates when you "break it" yourself, the game does a decent job a providing you with a good number of weapons but a lot of the time the fact the weapons degrade over use makes you not want to bother killing enemies, game is easy enough that you can simply skip them by jumping over them and just not bother, you're spending your limited durability weapons by killing them, why would you do that? There is a particular enemy kind that behave like shielded swordmen enemies from Zelda 2, you hit them up or down depending on the placemente of their shield, they are neat at first but the soon become a chore to fight, as they bring the progress of the game to a full stop, at least they often guarantee a weapon drop, I guess, but soon I started to simply skip them by jumping over them too, except for the final areas where they force you to fight them by putting them in tight corridors, fun wasn't had.Enemies are very uninspired, not necessarily by visual design, but in their function, there is a lot of enemies that just do the same thing, walk around and wait for you to kill them, you'll notice they like putting 3 of the same enemies in a platform in a row, they do nothing but serve as weapon wasters, and they just use reskins of them in different stages, and are just not fun to fight either, the enemy placement is also really weird,  there is long corridors of barely any enemies but then places 3 next to each other in the same platform, but they're very spread far inbetween, which leads me to wonder if this was done on purpose because the devs realized you'd be wasting weapons fighting random minions, this is a problem too because there is only certain enemies that will drop weapons to you, enemies like wall walking slimes, flying brids or the sadakos from the japanese level will NOT drop weapons, so what's the point in killing them if they can be avoided easily most of the time? Enemy placement also can be cheap, there is a couple levels where they simply put them in a way so you'll get shot before completing a jump so you'll be stunned into falling to your death, cheap deaths.There is another gameplay in the game when you lose the robot's health, you can play as the pilot, Flame, this small girl with a whip which can take like 3 hits, usually, before she dies, there is some forced segments in the game where you have to play as her before being able to pick up the robot again, her gameplay feels a little nicer compared to the robot who feels really stiff and a huge walking hitbox in comparison, and Flame has better range with her whip at least, but her damage is way too low and even basic enemies can take up to 3 hits to kill, it's a chore and that brings her down a lot, if you're on your last legs and are fighting a boss with Flame, be ready to one of the most tedious experiences ever, her damage is so low, and bosses are so tanky you'll take FOREVER to kill one of them, you're better at letting yourself lose a life to get the robot back and try again.The Flame segmentes are pretty short, like REALLY short, usually you just go through 1 small room, jump some death pits and spikes, and get the robot back again, in these segments you can also find a health pickup to heal your robot, but beware, THESE HEALTH PICKUPS DON'T RESPAWN IF YOU HAPPEN TO DIE, so you'll have a way rougher time replaying that level segment if you didn't reach a checkpoint before that, also checkpoints REQUIRE a weapon so you can use them, you'll usually have one to use, but it's such a weird decision to have, there is no reward for not using the checkpoint, like in shovel knight for example, and keeping your weapons is not really a reward, another thing is that you can only have 4 main weapons in quick swap, so you'll like have to pause the game, select a flimsy weak weapon to equip, just to use it on the checkpoint, stuff like this slow downs the pace of the game a lot.The game really tries to go hard on the whole weapon picking and breaking idea to the point it's an hidrance, there is no items in this game, only weapons, the weapons are basically items, as the spells behave like such, some swords heal you, which can go from small, middle, large and full heal, small heal is so minuscule it's not even worth to use, honestly, but the worst thing about it is that "breaking" weapons to use the spells takes like 2.5 seconds to use, and when you're in a boss fight, that can be real dangerous as you have to keep both triggers on your controller to initiate the breaking process, even if you're not in a boss fight, and you're in like, the previous room, and you want to be full health, it's a slow process to: pick the weapons that heal you, then break each one of them until you're full health, and that is only if you want to heal, that is not counting if you want to apply a defense, attack, or durability buff from the weapons you have stored, but again, you can only have 4 quick slots, and those are the ones you CAN "break" in gameplay, you can't "break" anything from the menu, so have fun swapping and breaking everything you need.There is no other upgrades in the game besides a health upgrade, which you can only do in the stage select menu and requires weapons to upgrade, you'll eventually have enough to upgrade most of it, but the health upgrades themselves are so small too, you'll barely feel the difference until you have upgraded yourself at least 4 times, and there is ONLY 5 small health upgrades, I keep wondering when am I gonna be able to upgrade weapon durabilty, your backdash (yes you have a backdash for some reason)  get an extra jump, more base damage to the mech or AT LEAST upgrade Flame's whip or health, she is a robot too so there is no thematic reason for her not being able to do it.It's so ridiculous that there is nothing in the way of upgrades or unlocks IN GAME that the most you can find in SECRET ROOMS in the game is just LIVES, and they don't respawn if you die in the level either, getting these feels so not rewarding, I kept expecting the game to throw me something else, but I never got it.The game has a weird amount of design decisions that came from other games, you got the Megaman style level structure and stage select, you got Master Blaster's leave your vehicle kind of gameplay, but not as deep, Breath of the Wild weapon durability mechanics, to the point that throwing your weapon at enemies also breaks it, breaking them this way doesn't trigger spells though, that'd be too nice, you have a Symphony of the Night backstep for some reason, doesn't really feel good, specially when your character moves so slow that I kept jumping midair and looking backwards so I could foward-backdash through the levels, because as clumsy as it was it was better than moving so slowly, game should've just had a foward dash, Megaman X-like, or something, FINAL BOSS SPOILERS , and finally you got the Zelda 2 shield mechanics, along with the enemies, all of these things aren't necessarily bad, but they make for a really mixed package, and they didn't really pick the best of these, but also the bad with it.There is a Wily Castle section at the end of the game that is like 7 levels long, you can't go back to the normal levels or you'll lose progress, so you got to finish all of these in one sitting (you can quit the game and pick it back up on the last level you left, supposedly, I didn't really check as I beat them in a row), these levels are VERY LONG and tedious.I'm running out of text to type but I don't recommend it unless on sale!

Mostly, it's because of the infuriatingly punishing chain-whip swinging sections of EVERY level...Much like other Tribute games, it's obvious the devs have a deep love for games (both new and old) and making them.The look and sound of everything experienced is perfect!Much like other Tribute games, the devs continue to use old, broken and punishing NES era design decisions/gimmicks that make people quit early.

_childDocuments_.review: Why do games from Tribute Games always look and sound fantastic, but never have more than mediocre gameplay?!Here are my biggest complaints:- taught gameplay mechanics are barely used to traverse the levels, such as the back dash and the high jump- the downward attack feels too clunky to be used regularly, e.g. to jump from enemy to enemy- the throw attack always destroys the weapon on enemy contact (instead of weakening it)- there are no real platform challenges, except for some chasms that mean instant death if you fail- the checkpoints don't reward you (as in Shovel Knight) for skipping them, but require a weapon to activate them (keeping the weapon is not a reward, you have plenty anyway)- you can only switch between four selected weapons quickly, selecting them via the menu always pulls you out of the action (it would have been better to group weapons by magic effects and skip duplicates when switching between all of them)- with weapons you can improve your health, but only health (why not the durability of weapons or the strength of magic effects)- the difficulty settings only affect how much damage you take (which makes the previous point even more useless)- all weapons are basically the same except for their magic effect, range and damage only matter in boss fights, because most other enemies die with one hit, even the ones that need two or three hits don't notice any higher damage- all the bosses feel the same, they have different designs but hardly require different strategiesIn the end, Panzer Paladin has a lot of potential, but gives it away all over the place.

_childDocuments_.review: Great graphics, fun music and solid controls for what they are going for.After playing this through however I have to ask: would I recommend this over other platformers at this price point. After the inevitable no we then must ask would I suggest it after someone has played those first.Frankly no.The blunt truth is that as well presented as this game is it has little to actually offer. Despite setting up interesting mechanics they don't amount to all that much when the levels are frankly rather bland. I'm not especially convinced that the core mechanics are up to much either, again other games are out there that do everything a little bit better such as Blaster Master for the pilot mechanics, The Messenger for the challenging platforming, Shovel Knight for combat or even the developer's own Mercenary Kings for boss-centric battles. There's nothing to offer in this title that allows it to stand on it's own, aside from teh aesthetic.Only for people who have exhausted anything else and you are looking for a game to mindlessly waste an afternoon on. Maybe wait for a sale?

_childDocuments_.review: Among countless NES spiritual successors on Steam,  is easily in the top five.  And I should know!  I spent my entire childhood burning my eyes out on games that only  they were so good!  We start off , with our svelte android pilot and her beefy rescue mech foiling a demonic assault on an Earth Defence Force base in Canada.  Here, we learn the ropes of wielding the giant destructible weapons scattered everywhere, some of which are player-made:  each has a perk attached -- Attack Up, Life Restoration, etc. -- which only becomes active when you  destroy it by holding both triggers, and  in the course of ordinary, combat-related breakage.  Many enemies, including bosses, can be parried, which opens them up for additional licks, while lesser baddies might also give up a weapon.After the introductory stage, we're treated to a gorgeous cinematic the ol' NES could likely pull off with a bit of finagling, and the level select opens up -- Tanzania, Sweden, Tokyo, and many others, each with its own themed demon-boss (my country, appropriately, is besieged by the arch-temptress Lilith).  After conquering those, you've got to take down the Cosmic Forge, any part of which is double the toughness of the standard stages.Tribute has nailed both presentation and gameplay here, and flush into the mahogany!  Your walking and jumping is ever pixel-precise, with zero butterfoot bullpoop to blame your spiky deaths on; and in an indisputably objective satisfaction of a quality platforming requirement, you can ease over and stand by the tip of your steely toes from the edge of a ledge!  The breaking of mystic weapons is punchy and potent.  The flash- of a successful parry is an instant and electric signal to your slavering reptile brain that you need to start hammering that attack button like a maniac.  To diversify the action, there are frequent segments where Flame has to get out on foot and swing (responsively) across pitfalls, and these are when you snag the majority of your 1UPs.  Of course, if your mecha is destroyed at any time, you have no choice but to go at it .  This can result in some very tense, very  video game moments -- like at the end of a boss fight where you've whittled the baddy down to a sliver just before Grit becomes disabled . . . and everything boils down to if you can survive long enough for your lithe but fragile android lass to whip the rest away . . .People call this -esque, but those touches are only superficial, as none of the actual weapon powers are permanent, unique, or even  for any particular sequence.  I see this as a definite strength; instead of wasting all their time building levels around silly gimmicks, the developers concentrated on the pure essentials of action platforming, allowing a more deeply satisfying degree of jumpin' and slashin' action no matter the weapon load-out. is, without a doubt, one of the all-time greats!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for June 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before July 6th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A classic-style game, with a completely modern sensibility and excellent gameplay.  Players will pilot a mecha, collecting fragile weapons and fighting their way through multiple levels in a great throwback to an ancient era. The gameplay is pretty unique as well.  Players will have to constantly seek out new weapons as there’s a durability system in the game that will cause weapons to break.  There are quite a few styles of weapons and interesting designs, but there’s also workshop support so players can include additional weapons, from a library of 2000, or create their own and share them.  Though sadly those only appear in certain locations. The art is great, the music is amazing, and the 8 or 16-bit era graphics look fantastic.  There are also multiple difficulties, a remixed mode for an extra challenge, speed runs, special challenge maps, and more.  Pick this up if you like solid 2D platformers with sword-based combat.  There’s something very satisfying about this game and makes me want to see more of it.  Still, this is an old-style retro with a bit of modernization, so if you want something that feels like it only could come out this generation, this isn’t it.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: it's really JUST ok.i got this on humble, and i don't feel bad about the time i got out of it, in fact, i'd even recommend it if it goes on a sale for $5 or lessthe game has some pretty good music, but the game suffers from some visibility issuesthe game tries to communicate to you what similar elements are in a stage through color: platforms are a color, the backgrounds are muted in comparison, enemies are a different colorthe problem comes when certain stages' backgrounds get a bit more garish- you'll start having issues actually picking out what's a platform and what's not.the combat is alright for a couple hours, but a lot of the enemies start reoccurring and getting old, and since you get better at the combat, they're just a solved issue that you get tired of dealing withthe main mechanic of the different weapons is cool, but it has the issue of how your mech is fully "upgraded," just a health upgrade, btw- by halfway through the main stages. you gain upgrade points by melting down your weapons, which you WILL have an excess of.there's some other cool mechanics at play, too- you're occasionally forced to jump out of your mech to tread on foot as a smaller character, or if your mech dies, you continue on foot as well. the problem with this comes with how like 50% of the foot sections use a rope-swing mechanic that i never felt properly eased into, even when nearing endgame. i'd still occasionally jump into a pit due to lacking momentum. on foot, you only have 1 weapon- a whip that feels castlevania-ish, which i don't feel fits with the rest of the game very much due to how stiff you feel while using it, which is different from the mech, which always feels at least mildly maneuverable during combat, which doesn't make much sense to me. why would i be stiffer outside of the big robot?despite my review recommending against this game, i wish the developers the best. i did have a good time with it for all of the $1 i really paid for it, and i genuinely thank you for that.all in all, this game is alright on the surface, but once you play it, you realize that it's a case of "death by a thousand cuts"- lots of small annoyances add up to a generally mildly unpleasant experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the game on Nintendo Switch and decided to buy it once again on Steam to support the developers. My only complaint is the game is too easy, even on Hard difficulty. In my experience, the gameplay ends up being much more about managing your weaponry strategically and knowing what to break/what to store than being skilled itself. This strategic approach is what many times allow for pleasant learning curves and a somewhat innovative platforming experience. People who are saying the game is hard are most likely not making appropriate use of weapon break spells, are throwing their weapons too much, or aren't used to retro platformers at all. I reached the final boss with over 9.000 spirit burden and didn't even fully upgrade Grit. All you need to beat a boss in a few seconds is an Attack Up buff and a boss weapon. If you're quick enough or if you have healing spells, you don't even need to dodge attacks. Nonetheless, it is a fun retro platformer with an extremely catchy soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: Had a lot of fun with this game. I don't know if easy mode changed checkpoints, I played it on normal, but if there were an option to increase checkpoints I would take it. _childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin looks good, plays average, gets boring and repetitive real fast. I met Panzer Paladin through ads on reddit and I should've known that if a game was being advertised on reddit, it cannot be a good game. The spritework and animatons are quite good, they kinda remind me of Monster in My Pocket from the NES, its soundtrack is also very good but sadly, that's where the good line ends. Everything else is mediocre and they get worse and worse as you progress. Gameplay starts off good and interesting. You can pick up weapons, you can throw them, break them to release their spells to gain some buffs etc., make your own weapons, play as the Squire sometimes and this is what you will be doing for like 3 to 4 hours in very long levels. Level design is alright but some of them have instant death traps which will force you to replay a long section of a level if you die and that is frustrating. Game itself is not difficult at all. Even on hard, it feels like a cakewalk. Story is just... there. It feels uninspired like the whole game. There are classic and remixed story levels and remixed ones are a bit more challenging than the classic ones. Alternative game modes also don't add any replay value. There's this boss rush mode which is interesting since bosses themselves are interesting. It's like they only worked on the bosses and recycled the rest of the enemies. There are also like hundreds of weapons but they all reskins. There's a speedrun mode and as soon as I've noticed it, I asked myself: "Why would anyone speedrun this slow paced game? Like who thought that adding a speedrun mode was a good idea?". There's also a challenge mode which is... kinda interesting. Oh, you can also change its soundtrack to 8-bit version but it already sounds like that so this is just another unnecessary addition to the game in my opinion. To sum up, Panzer Paladin is a wasted potential and it makes me sad because I was expecting a lot more than this when I heard it was partially inspired by Mega Man. I was going to give it a positive review just for the sake of that it could be a good beginning for those who never played platformers before but later, I've realized that this game could be extremely misleading about the genre overall, so I've decided to give it a negative one. I believe those who have written a positive review about this game haven't played enough platformers to judge it fairly. Avoid this game and play Mighty Gunvolt instead if you're planning to dive into the platformers since that game is actually very good, unlike this one.

_childDocuments_.review: The game does plenty of things right but falls short of becoming great due to a few overlooked issues.I love the graphics ( very retro) and the weapon system it uses is fun when you understand it.The soundtrack is catchy and doesn't start to bother you.Levels are decently build.The things that bothers me about the game is it controls and poor checkpoint placement.IT almost killed the game for me.And the controls don't feel solid. dodging is a nightmare to be honest, I am used to a system in which whatever way you are walking and you press dodge, it rolls in that direction.This game will roll in which way you are facing at the moment of the input. I could never adjust to this system.It deserves a thumbs up but it also could have been a solid great game up there with others if the devs had sorted out a few issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, super oldschool.  You can counter guys by blocking with your shield and they drop more weapons.  You can also store weapons for later.  I didn't realize this till after mostly beating the game and it makes the game way easier.Edit:Just to add more specific details: This game is a lot like megaman in stage design but with the shielding techniques from zelda 2, with the jumping out of your vehicle mechanics of blaster master.In case you didn't get the references:Zelda 2 had a sidescroller battle map and could jump around and block and duck and stab them with your sword. The combat is extremely similar to that.Megaman is a great platformer where you have bosses and minibosses and stylized stages based on their themes. Blaster master is a game where you ride around in a tank and can jump out of it and fight as a little weak and fragile person.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't think I was going to like this game, which is odd considering I actually love this genre.While quite reminiscent of a  (as we get tons of those on Steam and other platforms), the game hits close to home for me as it feels more like a  game than it does anything else. I'm a huge,  Mega Man (X) fan, so this little project made me  happy.Booting up the game, you are greeted by an 8-bit (Yes, true to meaning 8-bit, not 16-bit/32-bit claiming to be 8-bit) opening video that heavily reminds you of those 80's/90's anime openings. The music is fantastic, as it is as close as it possibly can be to the catchy tunes from the NES/SNES days.You're a robot inside of a robot. Well to be more specific, you're an android co-piloting a sentient robot (Paladin) named Grit. Can it get any better than that? Yes! It can! It's not just robot on robot action. But TLDR; Here's some even  nostalgia!Right off the bat, you're thrown into an introductory stage that also semi-serves as the tutorial. It teaches you how to attack, jump, treat your enemies like Goombas, and abandon Grit to do tiny android things. It also teaches you not to hold on to material objects, as things do break because of limited durability. You also sacrifice a weapon you're holding to save a checkpoint on the stage you're trying to complete. I accidentally went into the first boss with no weapon and literally ; I, accidentally, gave myself the "Pugilist" achievement by beating this guy with my bare hands.For any Mega Man fan out there, you know there's usually no reason to go back to a stage you've completed unless you missed a power-up; or in the X series, an E-Tank, Heart-Tank, or Armor piece. But in , you can go back and farm weapons or refight old bosses! I went back to the tutorial stage and beat the living hell out of the boss within 10 seconds for the "Blink Of An Eye" achievement.One of the most unique mechanics for this game type is the Grit-Flame swapping mechanic. There are places that only Flame can go and Grit can't, but Flame can't pick up any weapons, only Grit can. Is Grit low on health? Use Flame to find a restoration station to heal up. I have a little issue with the hitboxes though, as you can be out of range by a few pixels and still take damage from an attack. It's nothing game-breaking, just a bit more of a nuisance. It made a few things difficult but didn't make the game any less fun.There are a few more modes other than Story mode; Two which I can name from where I am right now are Blacksmith and Speedrun. Blacksmith allows you to forge your own weapons, from the physical design of the weapon to the stats that it brings to the table; you're given a set of skill points that lets you modify the damage, attack speed, durability, throwing power, and spell it activates when you break it for buffs. I spent quite some time in Blacksmith before I even started playing the main story.Speedrun is... self explanatory. It's more of a time-attack mode I suppose? I haven't really played much of it.There's also a remixed story mode! I don't know what it is yet, but the option is there!OH MY GOD THE MUSIC IN THIS GAME IS FANTASTIC. Everything is catchy, everything sounds awesome. It's exactly the type of music you want to hear in a sidescrolling game. It gets you hyped up enough to want to keep going forward. There is absolutely nothing negative I have to say about this. If you've enjoyed the music from the NES/SNES era, you'll have no qualms with the soundtrack for this game.Well... as mentioned above, I am nowhere near completed with this game, and so I will not be writing about the Story here. But from what I  know:Magic is real and being used to... No, magic  are real and monsters, called Weapon Keepers, are appearing all over the world wielding them and causing havoc.You are earth's last defense, an android named Flame co-piloting a sentient Paladin named Grit. Together, you two fight through a dozen or so stages and TAKE THEIR WEAPONS FROM THEIR CORPSES.That's an actual TLDR of what's happening.I highly, HIGHLY recommend this game. I thought I wasn't going to like it but I fell in love with it and I've only played about an hour or so of it at the time of this review. If you want to satisfy that Mega Man itch you've been feeling for a long time, BUY THIS GAME! No questions, no hestitation.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice retro challenge, Panzer Paladin offers some modern elements like the weapon system with some old-school platforming and bashing. Most levels feel similar and the platforming sections are not usually very ingenious. In the end it is a fine addition for any retro collection but it has its issues...

_childDocuments_.review: My main criticisms are about the jumping arc and spikes in the game. The platforming over spikes is so insanely tight that i fell into the spikes 95% of the time. This wouldn't be an issue, but the health penalty for spikes is INSANELY disproportional compared to enemies in the game.I can respect what this game is trying to be, a sort of Mega Man mech suit game, but it doesn't really hit those same highs that the Mega Man games do (personally I've only played Mega Man 1, and with save states, so mileage may vary)I also need a game that respects my time, and the checkpoint system is barely passable. The biggest reason I quit playing difficult games is if the punishment for death is too high. Celeste is a perfect example of a difficult game that respects your time with an aggressive checkpoint system. What this game has is passable; a few checkpoints in a level, but having only 3 lives means most of my time is spent practicing the level, getting completely annihilated by a boss, then quitting because all I really want to do is keep fighting the boss, not go through the level again.Again, I want to state that I understand what this game was aiming for, but it just doesn't quite hit for me with modern sensibilities. Fans of Mega Man ought to check it out, but this is definitely not one for me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's almost great, but its plagued with lots of questionable design choices that don't blend well together which really drag down the experience.For example, excess weapons you find can be converted to energy to use in a shop. This creates a risk/reward balance of breaking weapons during levels to access their temporary buffs, or sending them back home to convert to points.However, literally the only thing to buy in the shop is more Max HP, which is entirely useless as 95% of your deaths will take place out of your mech from awful forced segments where you are required to leave your mech, chain together 3 clunky grappling hook swings over a spike pit, and falling into spikes that result in instant death and going back 3 minutes to your last checkpoint.In the end, all this system does is encourage you to facetank bosses with OP weapons Horseman just hands you at the midpoint of each stage instead of learning their patterns at the risk of losing 8 minutes of progress through a stage that is awful to navigate.It is generous with the number of levels compared to a megaman game, but doesn't really do much to make the weapon lords or narrative between the beginning and end interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so the game looks great, sounds good, and plays pretty good.  100% derivative parts of better games glued together in a scattershot method that never meshes together, but isn't bad.  It's not very difficult and the majority of the enemies die in a single hit making them obstacles at most.  The issue is that all of the levels are just long and boring.  Too many repeating rooms with minor differences chained together on what could have been a fun game, but is instead 2x-3x as long as it needed to be.  Plus there's a large increase of precarious jumps in the final few levels in an attempt to stretch out your time in this game even more.Good production, awful levels.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: oh.... ohgod the last area wth is that design decision, I have no idea which way transitions the screen and I absolutely can't be assed with these enemies, its just not fun. Like many here, I too am kinda disappointed with the depth. The concept and stylings are very good, but not much else gives you that retro satisfaction of beating up/solving something that actually challenges your knowledge of the given mechanics and environment. There's pilot mode, varied weapons/buffs, and even the high low combat of zelda II but none of those neat mechanics are expanded upon meaningfully. Or, they are expanded upon but not gracefully, like the inventory system totally killing off the pacing as you shuffle about finding something to sacrifice for a checkpoint. I wish pilot/combat were more of the focus and meat of the game than worrying about whether or not my weapons are about to break or if I should keep them for buffs. Oh, and the weapons are already expendable yes, but not desirably so, please don't also make us use it for upgrading as well, searching through inventory to figure out what i want to keep is already tedious enough... give us some other rice points for fodder, like how many weapons used for buffs or broken.   Stuff  just really falls flat when there's lack of clever or fun environmental constructs/interactions or monster variety that makes the high low combat more meaningful than just ignorable obstacles. And the combat and shield movement animations alone are also too stiff to accommodate split second decisions. The weapons varying in stats and length really bogs down the flow of the game. A great concept, bad in practice cause it messes with pacing in combat. Mucking about in the inventory does not add anything meaningful or fun in this case because of the expendability and constant randomness.      I really wanted to like this game, but I ended up enjoying the silly blacksmith mode the most cause, as much as it hurts to say it, it actually brought up an actual conundrum and hurdle to me for how I might fit my silly ideas in such limited color palette and given space. Unlike the majority of the game where the simplicity was drawn out and didn't dare to change drastically or challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game with not much in mind, saw the graphics and it looked interesting for me so i gave it a try. After completing the game i think i should do a review cuz i feel there isn't a good number of them about it.So, it goes like:- Combat: it feels nice to go around doing your thing, bouncing off rows of enemies and fighting the more complex ones, generally you will start the level going about your business on easy to kill enemies and stoping every so often to fight a tougher dude that knows how to block your attacks and mix you up with high and lows, you face them as you see fit with the amazing dodge button, playing outside their range or just parrying their attacks, attacking and dodging is fluid and it feels great to get on the gameplay loop.- Mechanics; just the combat would give you a good time but there are more things from outside of it that make it more enjoyable, weapons have durability but that isn't just it, it works along other things like throwing your weapons for more damage but losing it in the process or casting spells dedicated for each weapon that also breaks it, spells vary from weapon to weapon but they are always from that one weapon and that's great because you can actually save them in your inventory for later use, very fun to mess around.- Level Design: its pretty solid for most of the time and not much difficult either, at least for me, however you will find some rooms in specific levels that can be troublesome but you always have ways to deal with stuff, never had a single time i felt enemies where out of place even if some placements were ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. Also, every level has one or two sessions that you are forced to play outside your Mech, pretty cool. Though, the checkpoint system is bad, not by how it works but how few there are around, just 2 per level and boy oh boy, the leves are BIG.- Soundtrack and Graphics: both are good in their own ways, graphics specially, a lot of animations looked fluid and nice to look at, even enemies and much more on bosses. The music is also good and the game shows it from the very start in the intro, its catchy to listen and never bothers you, nothing really amazing sadly.- Story: pretty simple to be honest, its nothing to brag about but gets the job done for the game to roll in, you can expect something on Megaman level since the game takes inspiration from it.Overall, its a very fun and well made work of love, most of the plataforming and combat feel good to do while hearing the game's musics and stuff but the level design can break it for some, the lack of checkpoints can get annoying at times but i was having fun and kept playing till the end. The game has a fair amount of play time too, even after beating it so that's a good thing, you should definitely give this game a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a platformer that borrows heavy elements from lots of other well known games from the past. This is evident with its graphical style which is very NES-like. You play as a girl in a mech-suit and you collect various swords and similar weapons from the foes you defeat. The game does get quite tactical with this mechanic as each weapon has a special move like healing or attacking all enemies onscreen with the consequence of that weapon breaking. The other cool thing that makes it stand out from similar games is that you can exit the mech-suit and access hidden areas as well as swing on hooks around the levels. However it does seem these sections are set pieces within the levels.You can choose whatever level you want to take in any order which reminds me of Megaman (although theres no boss weakness to worry about) and there is even a Dr Wily's castle type thing after you've completed them. Even some of the sound effects seem to have been taken out of a combination of Megaman and Castlevania. The game's difficulty was a bit easier then what I was expecting and I pretty much cruised though it on normal difficulty with only a couple of sections that gave me grief, however there are multiple difficultly levels should you want to turn the challenge up or down as desired.Overall, this is a pretty enjoyable platformer that takes you back to the golden age of old school games and with it's various difficulty levels, a remixed story mode and other unlockables, theres quite a lot to it. Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game!  Nice real pixel art (none of that varying pixel size or rotating pixels) and an amazing soundtrack.  The in-game weapon creator is a nice touch since so much of the game focuses on your weapons.  $20 is a little high so maybe wait for a sale, but don't skip out entirely.  This is a retro game done right.Some might be turned off by the weapon degradation but it makes sense here.  You sacrifice weapons to activate checkpoints much like smashing checkpoints in Shovel Knight.  I do however wish there were a few more checkpoints.  There are a lot of pitfalls and instant death areas that can get frustrating.  For a sequel I'd much rather see something like Mega Man X; where you can hunt upgrades to make the game easier or go for a buster only run for those that are insane.I'm also kind of hoping for a 16-bit remake or sequel.  I'm not saying the 8-bit graphics looks bad.  They actually look too good with animations so smooth they could never have existed on an 8-bit system.  16-bit would just help everything mesh a little more IMHO.

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a cute game but it's main draw is it's main flaw. this is a mech side scroller where you can hop out and run around with your pilot. she has a long ranged whip and can graple/swing on hooks and when you find tanks around you'll need to get to them with her to refill a bit of energy. the mech can block shots with its shield, has a back dodge, a jump (slashing up give you a extra hop and hitting back and dodge can let you get across sketchy holes), a counter, and can use weapons it finds around to stab in any direction. the weapons are this game main feature. there are tones of them and you can hold 4 that you can quickly swap between the rest will be stored away so you can swap them out or use to upgrade the mechs hp. the weapons can be found at specific spots or drops by enemies. they each have different stats and using them will slowly break them. there is a durability bar so you know when it'll break. you can also destroy it to cast a spell. this will be listed above the break bar. i do have a problem with the replaceable weapons though and that is that you do not get invested in any of them. some of them make you feel like you should care so much about them until you break it down for hp 5x, spell casting, used at a save point or because it just breaks. this is mainly because it's not really that much better than the other weapons you have. it also makes something that should feel like progress (new weapon or upgrades) not progress anything. like you get a sword from a boss but it feels like your first weapon drop and weapons are not random so what would be found or dropped by enemies would be there if you killed other bosses or not.it's still a decent sidscroller even though they use the enemy just out of site to make you fall into a pit gag and the "wily castle" bit gets a little cheap. don't expect anything great because the experience is mediocre at best.
