_childDocuments_.review: I bought it on sale. This game is awesome. I've been a fan of Tribute Games since forever. They make their games with such love of games in general. Great pixel art paired with boppin' music and overall fun Megaman/Castlevania gameplay that honors the games it pays homage to.The combat is simple. You can do like 3 things: Hit, throw, and spell. From swords, to spears, to hammers; you've got a lot of variety to do some damage. Hitting an enemy is the easiest. You can smack them once, Scrooge-McDuck cane bounce (or pogo-ing on enemies), or "double jump" with any weapon. A successful hit with your weapon lowers that weapon's durability, until it breaks. You can even throw each weapon to do more damage, unfortunately instantly destroying it if lands on an enemy. Finally, break your weapon to cast a spell. Each weapon has its own spell effect from healing to damage up... There's a lot of spells so I'll leave you to figure it out. The game constantly encourages you to use and break your weapons though, so don't feel bad if you lose your favorite one. Oh, I forgot to mention two things: Dodging and "Out-Of-Mech Adventures".There's a dodge/dash back button basically giving you i-frames. It's like the reverse Megaman dash. I had already beaten 3 bosses without it, but it's almost required if you plan on beating the rest of the game. Don't be me, learn the dodge.The "Out-Of-Mech Adventures" isn't anything grand. If you've played any Blaster Master game you basically know what to expect. You can climb out of your mech and walk around. It's required for some sections and if your mech's HP goes down, you're forced out. During these "adventures" you can find secrets, heal your mech and even fight the boss of the level if you're feeling frisky.The levels are long. You'll really feel the length when you play each one. Just keep that in mind if you go out to try and beat a level. You won't get a checkpoint until you hit the halfway mark and that's TRULY halfway in a level. So, if you're constantly dying, you'll end up having to redo all the parts over again. What fun right? It's frustrating having to redo a lot of the level, but you'll eventually master it. Like... I know we hear it a lot, but it really is "get good".Reaching a checkpoint requires you to give up one of your weapons to "activate" it. By the time you hit each midway point though you'll be swimming in disposable weapons to active the checkpoint.It took me an afternoon to beat, but I honestly wanted to continue playing. Beating the game rewards you with the Remix Story Mode. Whats fun is each level is remixed, and that's where the true challenge begins. There's hours more of content to do (challenge modes, boss rushes, and a sword designer if you're feeling particularly meme-y).I played it and I thoroughly enjoyed it. If it sounds like the kind of game that scratches your retro itch, give it some love.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a megaman-esque game that hits many of the same notes; choose a level (and associated boss), then fight your way through the end. Kill the boss, and you get a special weapon.The game has a few interesting aspects to it. You fight in a mech with many different weapons that drop from enemies. All those weapons have a durability meter and they can break after too many uses; but you can break them manually before that happens and get a bonus for doing so, like a higher attack or defense, or a screen-clear. They also all have different stats and are used for upgrading your mech as well. While in the mech, you can also block attacks or deflect projectiles and parry enemies; and, for some sections (and after the mech being destroyed), you jump out of the mech to continue as Flame, the mech pilot.Panzer Paladin ultimately has a few problems, though, that made me recommend against it, though I feel like my opinion is more mixed. One problem in the game is the jumping; it is very stiff and almost all pits you have to jump over require you to have pixel perfect timing, or fail the jump (and, often, die and lose one of your very few lives). The platforming issues continue as the mech pilot, Flame, that has a whip weapon used as a hook shot - this mechanic is very flimsy and, again, failing it means you die and, if you are unlucky, have to redo the entire level again.Speaking of levels, most of them are a bit too long for my taste. The bosses are also a mixed bag - some are complete pushovers, while others can kill you in a few hits for no real reason. The color palette and artstyle are also not to my taste; it can get really blocky and hard to discern backgrounds and foregrounds at times.After finishing the "main game", you get to the last section of levels, which made me quit the game in frustration; the levels become way too vertical, jumps become too frequent and failing them means you die instantly. The game also throws more and more instant death spikes at you, some of which are placed in such a way that you have to start making small or partial jumps, which just doesn't work very well.Overall, I think other games do what Panzer Paladin set out to do much better, though I like the music and the weapon system. On a heavy sale, you can check it out if you are a big fan of the Megaman games, though I'd rather play those at the end of the day.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: The best game never released on the NES.Where this game shines is in Challenge mode, where you can compete to rank in leaderboards with other players around the world. The best part is, you can replay other people's speedruns with the click of a button meaning competitors can learn from one another rather than be left to wonder at what arcane techniques their fellow speedrunners used to achieve such a high ranking. You can also race against your own ghost, making for some wildly exhilarating runs as you try to shave milliseconds off your previous time.The campaign is also enjoyable due to the tight controls and rhythmic action. I'll admit that the boss battles, while fun, are rather weak. It is too easy to exploit weapon-breaking to your advantage, which means you can basically follow bosses with a decent weapon and hack away at them until they explode, undermining any necessity to read their patterns and plan your moves. Also, one can avoid the mid-level horse warrior entirely by keeping their spirit burden below high, which is as easy as breaking weapons (LT+RT), reducing the overall challenge.Last but not least are the stellar art style and soundtrack, which really help to set the mood for an outstanding gameplay experience. I highly recommend this game for speedrunning enthusiasts and fans of the action platformers of yesteryear.P.S.: I was rather surprised that my nephews (6 and 4) enjoy this game about as much as I do, even though they can't yet beat the first level or pronounce the title properly. They love the fact that you can jump in and out of your mech, and especially enjoyed creating their own swords. There's a great deal of fun to be had here.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: It's sorta fitting that Panzer Paladin is made by Tribute games: because their game is a tribute to a lot of different games and popular media. Between the character designs having similarties to Gundams, the Mega Man styles of unique weaponry and bosses, and the Zelda 2 blocking with the shield, this game take a bunch of influences and smashes them together. But what's key here is that it does it smartly: as the game wisely integrates them together to make an interesting yet challenging experience that does help make it stand out from the genre. I had a lot of fun in the first few hours, and while I do have to warn that several people have indicated that the mid/end game can start to show more problems, I didn't seem to run into many of them. It pushed me but not to the point of breaking, and switching weapons every couple of enemies, trying to maximize their effectiveness, really works with the breaking weapon spell system.It does show signs that maybe some scope was cut: Flame's sections that are specific to him seem to be very very short at times, and once in a while there's a screen or two that just doesn't seem to flow naturally along the game's reasonable pace. It doesn't distract from the main action enough to make it feel like you're getting a worse experience, but it's something that pops up here and there. The soundtrack is fantastic and really feels like a tier below the classic Mega Man soundtracks, but only one tier below. Visuals are a bit more subjective: the animations made it easy to see what was going on in most cases, but every so often the color schemes started to blend together and felt samey (especially with certain enemies). Sound design does everything is needs to in order to stand out compared to others. In the end, my first 2 hours with the game justified the games cost in my eyes, and it definitely is worth a strong look if you're any sort of action platformer gamer.  list]
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Excellently crafted action platformer that mixes bits from all your favorite 8-bit titles. There's pieces of Rastan, Blaster Master, Duck Tales, Castlevania, Trojan and what have you in here. At times it might feel a little light on identity, but the parts blend well and it looks great, sounds great, plays great and has amazing style.Don't let complaints about unfair difficulty dissuade you -- if anything it's a bit on the easy side once you get a hang of the jump. Performance might not be as great as you'd think if you're on an older system though.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin has a lot of interesting ideas behind it.  the devs thought using this exact genre to explore them was a good idea is beyond me to understand.Pretty much every unique idea the game has is undermined by either the type of game it is, or its level structure. The weapon and spell system encourages constant weapon switching- but, oh wait! Because the game is a retro 8-bit platformer, the combat can't be too complex. So all of the weapons behave the same, and half the spells are boring stat buffs. Each level has region-unique weapons- but, oh wait! They can be played in any order, so all of the variations have to act the same. Else the player will get confused. Perfect-parrying an opponent will disarm them and give you their weap- but, oh wait! Since any level might be the first the player picks, all of them have to shower you in weapons to avoid boredom and frustration.But even when you look past the original parts, the core execution leaves a lot to be desired as well. The music and artwork are good, but without any interesting movement options of note, the level design ends up being bland and repetitive. Enemies are simplistic and uninspired, and the bossfights run the full gamut between forgettable, passable, and infuriating. And to top it all off, Panzer Paladin is the type of game enamored with plentiful instant death pits, coupled with scarce checkpoints to waste your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: A so-so retrogame. It's not particularly bad, but it's not particularly good, either.The graphics and the audio have a very good NES-style. Playbility is good as well - this is not a hard-for-the-sake-of-hard game.On the other hand, there's nothing particularly distinctive about it. The game intends to distinguish itself mainly in two ways:1. river <> robot modes. this is intenresting in itself, but there's nothing special happening in the sections where driver mode is required2. weapons. there are a few mechanics, but they're not particularly interesting. weapons distinguish themselves mainly in terms of balance power<>speed, but they don't change the strategy significantly, and in terms of special moves which... seem to be very insignificant.Checkpoints are well positioned, and they're "sacrifice" based - one sacrifices one weapon for the checkpoint, which is one modern way of checkpointing.Suggested only IMO to NES junkies, but there's better.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Nostalgic yet new and unique. Simple but satisfying. It's great.I really enjoy the art style, the music, and the simple yet responsive controls. The game difficulty is great in that it's challenging and rewarding but not insanely tough.I do wish there was a bit more complexity or more diverse play throughout as it's a bit repetitive but that was somewhat expected coming into it.Highly recommend for those who were fans of old, 2D side scrolling action games. Think Mega Man, Strider, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin caught my eye immediately and I bought it in a flash because I enjoy 8-bit platformers like Castlevania and Blaster Master, but I feel like I should have stayed my hand. Before I get into the negative aspects of this game that make me regret my purchase, I'll speak on what I do like. I should also preface that this is not necessarily a terrible game, but it has too many flaws to be worth the cost and your time.Aaaand that's it for what I find enjoyable. Onto the negatives.That's all I can think of for now, besides one very important thing that I will talk of in detail now.If you know anything of Aboriginal cultures, you may have heard of a certain spirit that you are not supposed to name, lest you curse yourself and others around you. That spirit is the one that is hyped up to be the boss of the first level, but is killed off before the fight by the actual boss. I'm not one to be spiritualistic, but it's pretty disrespectful to a culture to not only name & depict a spirit they don't want you to name, but to kill it off so you can fight a pretty unicorn instead to make it look like a joke. In conclusion, this game fails to be engaging and leaves me feeling distasteful. It feels incomplete and as if the developers wanted to copy all of their favourite NES games but decided to also exaggerate their flaws. I’d much rather play the new blaster master games or even go back to play the original Mega Man than this. Either get this game on sale or go buy Blaster Master Zero 2 instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: I don't dislike this game by any means, but it's very basic, even more basic than the games it is inspired by.It's a retro action platformer similar to Mega Man with hints of Blaster Master, but rather than taking that and expanding on the concepts and giving it a modern twist all that's there is just some basic platforming and enemies and very few under-utilised out-of-mech sections. Neat ideas like the weapon system and using them as currency and for checkpoints, but just not really explored enough and no interesting uses for said currency. There's also the pointless feature of being able to draw some weapons yourself.Nice pixel art and very authentic feeling, clearly a lot of effort went into it, but when compared to other retro love letters it just falls short.Can't recommend for the current price as it is basically a well presented NES game.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Game looks lovely, has a catchy soundtrack and has an OK core game loop. My main problem was that I found it to be the wrong kind of retro for my tastes, though. Personally I think very few games work well with the arcade-style lives/continue system; much of the legacy of this system was as a business model rather than a particularly fun style of play. This game isn't one of the exceptions--losing level checkpoints to the lives system doesn't feel worthwhile. The levels aren't technical enough for me to feel like I've gained something when I cruise through earlier parts of the level perfectly on subsequent attempts.Even if you're more interested in that specific aspect of retro gaming, the combat and platforming isn't really something to write home about. Weapons feel indistinct and other than range and damage type they're semi-randomized and they break extremely quickly--it becomes a bit tedious to dig into the inventory and figure out both which weapons you have available and which spells they can produce.Excellent presentation, but too fiddly for how satisfying the flow of the game is.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those moments where it's not you it's me, well in this case mostly me. I don't know why, but I can't get used to the controls, mechanically speaking as I found it difficult to platform and attack enemies, mechanically speaking, plus it doesn't help the checkpoints aren't generous, so if you are a brawling type of player (like me) don't play this game. This is definitely a niche game for those who grow up with an old-school 8-bit, not to say Panzer Paladin is a game, oh no, as far as I played, it has a nice 80s vibe and pixel art, along with an anime cutscene and somewhat of interesting gameplay of you piloting a giant mech soldier collecting multiple weapons to fight monsters. Or exiting out of your mech in tiny human form with you being at your most vulnerable but having more agility to navigate the level with their grapple, Castlevania style.All of that was what excited me to play this game, but overall it is just not my type of game. I wish I had grown up with this type of game so I have the skill to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: between the old school nes styled graphic, the banging soundtrack, and that tight gameplay in both mech and on foot it really feels like all the best metroidvania styled games. story is fun enough but realistically youre here cause you love classic megaman styled games, really makes you FEEL like batman.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is an amazing 2D Action Platformer with Retro graphics which brings back the good old days of retro games. You play as Flame (The Squire Female) along with your buddy Grit (The Panzer) on a journey to take down the Evil forces.The music in the game during stages as well as boss fights is so engaging and very well composed. brought back very good memories of retro games. The controls are solid and the platforming sections can be challenging at time but manageable. The boss fights have very nice designs along with their different color palettes, loved every single one of them.The game uses an equippable weapons system which has a Durability bar, and breaks upon depleting that bar. Also, by deliberately breaking a weapon, you gain its unique spell which can be (Heals, Attack Increase, Defense Increase...etc).I really enjoyed another amazing game from Tribute Games Studio. If you're a big fan of 2D Action Platformers, then you should really check them out.Overall Rating 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: SO GOOD. It gets everything right. Even the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ difficulty from the good old days are back. I first played PP years ago and dropped it because my pride stopped me from playing on easy mode. My advice is to go ahead and play on easy mode the first time, and crank it up next time.  Each stage has a distinct and interesting theme, in the aesthetic and in the music
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a solid little action platformer. The titular paladin controls a lot like Zelda 2's link: a high-low shield mechanic, a weapon attack that can be performed in a number of directions. The addition of a back-dodge adds some depth to movement, which is good because the paladin can feel sluggish. The main gimmick of the game is it's consumable weapon system: You'll gather buckets of weapons over the course of the game, which are spent for... basically everything you want to do in this game. Don't be too precious with your weapons or you'll have a bad time, non-weapon sources of health are few and far between, and running out of health is an overall miserable experience. It can be a bit frustrating at times, but it's not overly difficult, although full disclosure I only completed it on Normal mode, I can't speak for hard mode or any of the bonus post-game content.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: So yeah, as a huge mecha fan I must truly and wholeheartedly reccommend this game. It has mecha action, an female android pilot with energy version os Belmont's chain whip's from castlevania, that NES feel... So yerah, the plot is simple, but then again, super robot anime plot, so cool xD Art is amazing, I can say being a pixelartist myself.And speaking of which... you can design your own weapons... in pixelart!
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: A little rough around the edges and a very superficial story, but otherwise a FANTASTIC GAME! a really fresh take on the megaman formula that i didnt know i need it. I've beaten both versions of the campaign and I already want more. I hope to see more of this in the near future. I feel it has the potential of becoming a very fun and enjoyable franchise.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I'd heard about this game way back when I owned a Switch... I remember people would watch a trailer of it on Youtube then proceed to talk about in an all "hushy hushy" tone of voice, as if skeptical it might not live up to the expectations. Fast forward a couple of years and here we are... Panzer Paladin lived up to its expectations and is as addictive as I'd imagined it would be.The game is fully in NES-style; however, everything is well animated... to a fault. You control Flame and Grit, two bots, one a knight and one a paladin. Now the thing is Flame can literally drive Grit. Grit has a huge arsenal of weapons, dropped by his enemies occasionally, that he will NOT KEEP FOREVER. Flame is plagued with very low HPs but has a lasso that is required to navigate through the levels, that only she can use. As you'd deduce, you'll have to alternate between Flame and Grit to finish a level and each level has a nasty boss at the end, called a Weapon Keeper. The game is fully functional online and, bear with me; it's AMAZING what the devs have done with Panzer Paladin: You can actually create a weapon... submit it online, and another player can pick up as a reward for defeating The Horseman (a miniboss that you'll come across, A LOT), all through the online function: Spirit Forge... How cool is that?The bosses are also so well designed, with each monstrosity belonging to its own country's folklore. The bossfights were indeed quite memorable. Weapons also provide an advantage if you decide to break them... and you'd lose them if you throw them and they hit an enemy in the distance and that's something that's sometimes necessary to avoid coliding with a flying spear and falling to your doom. There are also five modes: Classic Story (normal story mode), Remixed Story (it's an Arcade mode that's much more difficult), Tournament Mode (Boss Rush mode), Speedrun mode and finally Challenge Mode (a set of challenges for you to go through, similar to those from Mighty Number 9). All in all and even if you somehow do not like old graphics, you should still get this game simply because it can either provide you with over 15 hours of Nostalgia, or it could show you what your parents had been playing in their youth, which can bring you closer to them and let you understand them more... or not. It's a beautiful 9/10 game that I can never get enough of... I just wish they think of a sequel somewhere down the road cause games like this one are quite rare.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't finished the game yet, but have beat a few stages and all i can say is that it's a bit underwhelming, it's fine but not great.The graphics are charming and the OST is good, but the game suffers from having cool mechanics that aren't explored much, let's see, you can play as an android or as a mecha, but your android character can only whip to attack enemies and go across some rare platforming sections that feel like the developer remembering she exists more than anything else, in fact, the levels are another thing, they just feel too...i don't know safe in a way that i wouldn't notice in other games but is certainly felt here.And yes, you move slowly in this game, which is fine as the levels aren't too long, you can still dodge everything which is all that i ask for, the combat is very simple, there are absolutely no combos, just one strike and then pushing the button to do another strike, also, weapons do break but you tend to get a lot of them and if you use the menu, you can unequip them and just punch things, but you can get to a point where you don't mind breaking weapons or using spells to survive and the only strategy becomes saving the best stuff for boss fights.As for difficulty, i am playing on the hardest one and it's easy, honestly, if i die it's something cheap like jumping and being hit by an enemy and falling to a bottomless pit, but those aren't common at all, enemies are really easy to beat, and bosses are easily beatable if you come prepared with some good weapons, and if you lose your mecha, you can still use your squishy android, it's not a very hard game...but some cheap parts may make you annoyed, doesn't help that you have finite lives in any stage and that they have checkpoints which require spending a weapon to activate, if you lose far away from a checkpoint, too bad, you get back to where you previously saved, also, weapons that were part of the stage to be picked up are now gone, which can be frustrating.And don't expect much for the upgrades, it's just increasing the HP of your mecha, and they're small increases, for a game like this with breakable weapons, you'd think the upgrades costing weapons would be something big, but nope, it's a small increase of HP for an easy game.Despite all of this, it's not a bad game and i can see that a lot of love was put into it, and it's a decent platformer so far, but that's it, after beating some stages i don't really feel like this is worth the full price sadly.One more thing, the game forces you into a stage, but after beating it, you get a Mega Man style game where you can pick stages or the bosses you fight...this is pointless as far as i can tell since you don't get new upgrades, unique weapons or skills from the bosses you beat, it's really just about deciding what levels you want to play at each time, nothing more.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem. Two story modes - classic and remixed, each with three levels of difficulty, tournament mode (boss rush) and speedrun mode ensure great replayability. Weapon spells are not just some gimmick but actually working game mechanics (you better keep the weapons with healing spells, you might need them later). Look for hidden items and rooms to get more lives. Knock out enemies with your mighty steel fist, jump and bounce over the heads of harder ones (or - if you have wings - just fly over them). All in all this game is a lot of fun. Pixel art is top, so is music (powerglove!). It could only be better if it had mech and level editors. If there's going to be a sequel, i'm buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Repetitive, boring and predictable level design. Uninteresting game mechanics.Poor choice of color palette, when I think of this game game I can only remember the color orange for some reason, even though the screenshots above seem more balanced.I forced myself to finish this one, got the bad ending by mistake 😂, and then just didn't care anymore. Bad ending seemed better than the good one anyway (I YouTubed the good ending).5/10. Not recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda sorta got the game for free? It was a humble bundle choice from a long time ago I finally decided to try out.Very fun combat game that is unfortunately shackled to a very bad platforming game filled with punishing, cheap, instant death jumps that send you back to the last (very far sometimes) checkpoint while removing one of your precious few lives for the level.While I can't personally recommend it, anyone who can tolerate the platforming will probably have a great time
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Concept is a 14/10 to start with(Mecha knight Vs. Mythological creatures all over the world), Story is simple but has enough there, the cut-scenes are serious eye candy, OST is jamming, Difficulty is absolutely present (completed a hard play-through, dunno about the other modes but hard kicked my ass a fair bit.), and is seriously fun. I love the weapon spell mechanic and the fact that hoarding weapons makes your life harder. You wanna keep all those weapons? Now you're gonna have to work for it. And the cherry on top is the blacksmith feature, allowing you to create and receive custom weapons to drop from your friendly(?) neighborhood horseman. Game's great, love it to bits.Oh, but Sky Gate was evil. puuuure evil.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: (X-posted to my wordpress blog, Gunlord500). This is SUPER fun, kinda (but not quite) Metal Warriors/Gun Hazard mixed with Panzer World Galient! Essentially, in the future, demons are invading earth, but the only way to fight them is with their own demonic weapons, and those corrupt the users! So an android named Flame and her giant mech called Grit, who are somewhat resistant to the corruption, have to save the world! This game is a platformer where you guide your mecha through side-scrolling stages, avoiding bottomless pits and spikes, and fight demonic invasion by picking up swords, axes, etc. your enemies drop. You can get out of your mech and play as the android, who's much smaller and can squeeze into tight spaces, but is also much much weaker. There's not too much else to say about it--the graphics are a great example of the retro style, there are some fun anime style cutscenes throughout the game (really making you feel like you're playing an anime game from the 80s), the controls are super tight and smooth, and the music is GREAT. There are also a few more extra modes and stuff to play after you've beat the game, like Blacksmith mode, where you can make your own weapons, which is super fun, so this adds a good deal to the replay value. Awesome, definitely worth 20 dollars, even if you're not as much of a mecha fan as I am! Awesome job from Tribute Games!
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good and brings some memories of classics:-Castlevania: Flame's mode of attack-Megaman: Stage Design, The Paladins' Weapons.-The Legenda of Zelda II: Link's Adventure: The side scrolling swordplay.Tribute games did make those references and they're pretty good, but by no means this means the game is easy.In a world where the occult is real and is been invaded you, are called to a battlefield to save the world. The character, Flame pilots a Mecha called Grit. Take Control of it, and save the world. A simple, yet effective story. Maybe too simple for some though.First Impressions:-The game has its own charm, sure it pays tribute to castlevania, Megaman, Zelda but, it has its own charms. With a dual control character mechanic, choose between flame and Grit.-Simple mechanics, tough world. Choose a Stage, get a weapon and advance. The decision taking is not limited to just what weapon do you use(you can change weapons as you progress) but also there is a function that unleashes a powerful attack at the cost of breaking that weapon. Surrounded? Use a weapon OR take it to the limit and BREAK it. But be careful, because if you arrive to the boss WITHOUT WEAPONS, it's going to be literally, living hell for Flame and you.-Hp to Zero does not mean defeat: You can fight as Grit or Flame, if your mecha gets damaged you can fight as Flame to win the battle but albeit it's harder, it has its merit.-Controls are a bit confusing at the start, but you can adapt kind of fast. The duality between Mecha and pilot maybe too hard for some to adapt, but you can get over quickly.-Decent difficulty: Despite being a 2d simple game, it has its difficulty to use checkpoints you must lay down a weapon. To remove the weapon, means no more checkpoint. Defeated by a boss? You can have the weapon at the risk of undoing the checkpoint.These are my first impressions. As I play I will add good and bad aspects. This game is good and I find it sad, it has no in depth reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: first half of panzer paladin solid mega man like game, 6/10 because it chooses to keep the abritray difficulty of old mega man games, last half of panzer paladin 0/10 take every problem with mega man games and amp them up to 100 out of a possible 10, then throw in troll and jump-scare instant death pits, and the same boss literally recycled every single level. 2 check points per level one before the mid level boss and right before level boss, they are optional and when you die either if you didnt set the check point you get sent to the start of the level. the primary mechanic of collecting weapons encourages hording and never using items, similar to rare items in rpgs. then there is the issue with the final section of the game, like in mega man you head to the villians base to clear it out and fight the final boss. this wouldnt be a problem if it was only 3 levels like old mega man or if it saves progress in between levels. this game chooses to place over 5 of these levels and does not save progress. if you turn off the game you are forced to repeat all these levels again. this wouldnt even be fine if the levels didnt take upwards of 10-20 minutes (depending on how much you fall prey to the troll deaths). 1/10 would not recommend buying unless you are okay with these problems or on a heavy (50%+) discount
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Good to look at, disappointing to play. It nails the aesthetic and overall visual design but just dopes not feel good to play. The loop of having to find weapons constantly and push on forward is ruined mostly by the weapon system. Weapons having some amount of durability and a unique skill for when you shatter them makes regular combat feel lifeless and more of a chore outside of bosses. I never want to use a weapon or skill outside of a boss room because of the impermanence of them. I'd probably be a little less annoyed by the combat if the movement was enjoyable in any way. It's not that it feels sluggish or unyielding it's that it doesn't have any enjoyment to it. There's no sense of satisfaction or fun when I move just that I am merely moving at what feels like the default rate for the engine. It's boringly inoffensive and bland for some good visuals but definitely not worth your time, especially at $19.99.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun! Gameplay was fun, boss design was wicked. I enjoyed collecting, like, a million swords. Music is bopping (seriously, even if you don't play it, look up the soundtrack). Felt like an NES classic. In the final stretch of the game, it is a little unforgiving of errors, but I only actually ran out of lives once during my first playthrough (on the normal difficulty) so I didn't think it was too bad. I received the game as a gift from a friend, and would 100% buy it again as a gift for another friend.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Blaster Master Zero, I love the style, including the graphics and music. They've nailed the classic style really well!But at the other side, the gameplay feels rather simple, and it get old and tedious fast.They've an incredible complex weapon management system (You pick up different kinds of melee weapons that varies in durability, damage, speed, range, throw damage, 'break' effects) for weapons that all...just functions the same?The most notable difference that the weapons has is their 'break' effect to unleash a spell. These break effects are pretty important. but other than that, it's quite a hassle to manage the many different weapons you have. And if you don't focus on the break effect, the combat looks very standard.Remaining weapons can be used to upgrade the mech, but it only upgrades the health, so there's only little sense in progression.You've the ability to switch from Mech to Pilot, this was a nice nod to Blaster Master. And it allows you to keep using the Pilot once the Mech broke down, I liked that idea!However, in practise, this makes the game more difficult to progress, you cannot pick up weapons, you cannot checkpoint without your mech, and I havn't found a way to restore the mech once it breaks down, unless I end the level.So the Mech moves slow, has a short range, needs to break weapons for one-use abilities, combat/movement is rather simple and doesn't seem to improve later on.The game looked promising, but after playing through the first 2 levels, I feel the rest of the game plays the same way. I'd like to give the game a second chance some other day though, it's artstyle and music is so great that it has a missed potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: I'll try to keep this short and sweet: is a side-scrolling platformer with a mecha mechanic akin to the cult-classic . The idea is you traverse levels using your mecha (and sometimes just your pilot) to navigate levels while killing enemies and bosses with their own dropped weapons that you collect, not unlike . The idea sort of works, but the weapons all feel pretty similar. The mecha never really reaches the point where it feels like it's getting stronger, or more capable, even with the simplistic upgrade system maxed out (which isn't hard to do).The art is nice, as is the music, but the core gameplay feels lacking, even for the era it is stylistically trying to emulate. The weapon mechanic, before long, becomes a chore to deal with as despite not really feeling different during use. There is a limited inventory, which makes sense, but weapons have distinctly large variance in effectiveness which means you're usually forced to remember or constantly open menus to compare to make sure you're not lugging worthless garbage around. That's a big ask for a side-scrolling game that doesn't have a wealth of other mechanics going for it. Worst of all, it's painfully easy but very slow.I got to the end and decided 6 hours was enough of an attempt to extract fun out of this. I like side-scrollers, and this has a bunch of "bonus" points for style and themes, but it ends up being a shallow experience. I ended up buying  the other day, which ended up being a lot more fun and had a lot more to offer for around the same price (including a deathmatch mode with online/local options); if you're checking out this game for the  vibe like I did, take a look at  instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game!  The platforming is incredibly solid and super fun; the level design is fantastic and the boss fights are super cool.  The music is incredible, right up there with the soundtracks of Ninja Gaiden and Mega Man II.  The inventory management elements fall a bit flat with a platformer; during most of the levels, it ends up being best not to use a weapon at all, since your fist kills standard enemies in the same number of hits and doesn't have a durability stat.  That's in a game about cool swords.  The game's endings  throughout the entire game, we see and enjoy awesome weapons from different real-world cultures, which makes the experience of wielding them feel deeper and reminds us of our respect for them.  Ultimately, the ending cinematics are beautiful and fun, I want to be clear: despite my little gripes, this game is absolutely great, and I had a fantastic time playing it.  I highly recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool Megaman x Castlevania game with Mechs and Demons. The world is your map, and each stage is themed around a certain demon/god/supernatural entity native to that country. The levels also have their own sets of enemies to match the themes. The artists definitely had a blast creating and designing the visuals, and it shows. The cutscenes are great, and if this was released back on the golden days of the NES, it would've blown many minds.Grit is fun to control and I love punching enemies back to oblivion. Oh and there are tons of melee weapons too! Alot of them reference other games and mythological weapons of folklore. I had many "Ah Ha!" moments when I recognized a particular weapon or god. This game is fun, but it can be challenging for more casual players who didn't grow up with the classic NES games. If you are the type who gets easily frustrated when you mistime a jump or attack, and get punished severely for it, this game might not be for you. But if you are the type who doesn't give up or mind a few setbacks here and there, this game's difficulty curve will keep you engaged. It's challenging but rewarding. Also the music is really good! Definitely fits perfectly with other NES era games.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This game's a recommend from me ONLY if you like "nintendo hard" games and have patience enough to learn the gimmicks and get good. _childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a rather good retro platformer where you're a super fighting android piloting a giant robot armed with various destructible melee weapons you can break to cast spells.There's actually an editor that lets you design (and stat out) weapons pixel by pixel which then can be dropped by minibosses.Another unique gimmick is you can jump out of your mech to fight on foot with a laser-whip, its required for some sections where you use the whip to swing between hooks but it can also come into play when the robot gets taken out of action like in a boss fight, possible to continue on foot and win.Overall this game is something I highly recommend. _childDocuments_.review: An excellent combination of style and mechanics from games such as Zelda 2, Mega Man, Metal Storm, Blaster Master, etc.  Fantastic art (the intro/cutscene animations are amazing), great nostalgic sounds, and an awesome soundtrack (especially the Switzerland stage music, which even seems to have train-esque pacing and notes).The weapon system is absolutely marvelous (everything from durability, throwing, breaking for spells - even abandoning to activate a checkpoint).  It adds so much variety to the game in what your character can do and how you can complete each level.  It also integrates well with much of the rest of the game - whether it’s finding the right weapon type for an enemy’s weakness, needing certain types to break blocks to reach additional weapons and areas, or deciding which weapons to keep for their spell, speed/range, damage/type, etc.  As a weapon’s durability gets low, there’s a great bit of decision-making for whether to throw it, cast a spell, or stash it in the hopes of finding the occasional weapon-repair item (or later use for upgrading Grit’s maximum HP).The blacksmith feature (which I only tried out after completing the game) is surprisingly fun to tinker with, and it’s really smoothly integrated into the Steam workshop stuff (first game where I’ve even paid attention to workshop items).I’ve seen a bit of the remixed stages but haven’t yet started up my own playthrough.  What I can say though is that there’s a ton of interesting changes and significantly increased difficulty (including boss changes) that should require some really good platforming and weapon/spell usage.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: It's got some great music and cool spritework, but the physics are a bit clunky, difficulty is kinda wack sometimes, levels feel a bit too similar, and the weapon breaking/durability mechanic doesn't really work in something like this. If you like how classic castlevania plays this is probably something you'd enjoy a lot though.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This is literally Megaman but worse. I got this game off of humble bundle for cheap so I don't care about the $1 I consider lost on it. If you are thinking about buying this game just don't bother. It's like a 10 hour experience MAX, and, like I said, it is quite literally Megaman, except your weapons break too often and there's no interesting boss weaknesses.Level design feels cheap and sloppy at times. It's hard to describe but once you play a few you'll start to see the cheap hits the game throws in. The mechanic of switching between the robot and girl is not interesting at all because the only effective difference is that you have no health as the girl. In the first level of the final gauntlet, the spike texture is literally broken: instead of the non spike texture being transparent it's straight up black. That just shows me that the team working behind this game don't really have the skill (which isn't the case because there's no notable bugs or framedrops) or they just really didn't care. The game lacks heart which is showable.The worst part? The lives system. There is no reason on the planet to still have a mechanic designed for grabbing quarters in a game that doesn't want your quarters after the first purchase. The death system is by far the worst part of this game because it makes it so tedious if you are stuck on one boss to have to replay the whole just okay level over and over again to get to the boss. I mean for goodness' sake, you lose your weapon upon death, maybe lean into that aspect more and give infinite tries at checkpoints at least! Did you guys not learn from the mistakes of the game you are trying so hard to replicate (Megaman)?
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: I was super intrigued with the concept, especially since the studio has given me a solid 100 hours with previous titles. The demo was absolute fun and making my own weapons was cool. (Although the repeated sound almost made me mute the game, forshadowing whats to come.)The full version is... ok. Overall, I am kinda disappointed because it lacks variety. The enemies are -for the most part- color swaps of the same few enemy types, seldomly a sprite swap for a unit or two. The levels themselves were straightforward enough and if you played any megaman before, the difficulty was boringly easy. If you run through a level blind, the game punishes you a bit, if you take a breather every other screenwrap, there are no surprises that get you. No real puzzles or challenges, just the occasional "Oh no, the ground is falling. Better keep pressing right." I switched to easy after 4 or so stages, not because the stages were difficult, but I wanted to get them over with faster. The Bosses are ok as well. Some gave me a decent thinking on how to defeat them/understand the pattern. Overall, the reward for beating the boss was a weapon that would break rather easily. You quickly get that BOTW rythm of not using your best equipment so that it cannot break. I was also out of upgrades after level 6 and since I had no reason to stockpile weapons, I would blast through bosses by yeeting all my sharp edged clutter at them. Shame that most bosses have no reaction to being pelted with knives other than to stand in awe long enough to be pelted again, but maybe that was dev intended. If the game had more upgrades (like higher move speed, god the paladin is slow), I would probably see a reason to replay levels. When I, after the 4th stage of the mandatory final dungeon marathon, absent-mindedly closed out into the world map and lost all my process inside the final dungeon, I decided to quit and I will probably not continue. Real shame, awesome concept, neat graphics, mediocre/repeated execution.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let's go over the "Pros" before I get to the "Cons". Since I really wanted to like this game, and there are a lot of good things about it.[Pros]:- Movement feels fluid & accurate- Level select- Easy to learn boss patterns/animations- Charming visual style both in game and in cutscenes- Combat works well- No input lag- Challenging but not too hard[Cons]:- Most levels are tediously long- Combat quickly gets repetitive- Very little enemy variety, until near the end- Lots of pixel perfect jumps- Beginner's traps- Leaps of faith- Camera panning issues- Outstays its welcomeAlright folks, that's the main gist of it - for those who wanted a quick review. Now, for those who want a more detailed one - feel free to continue reading."Panzer Paladin" is very mechanically sound, and at first will remind people of the days of NES gaming - but on a slightly easier level. However, with the attempt at recreating the feel of an NES game - the developers ended up recreating a little too much. For, it's riddled with many beginner's traps over bottomless pits; a camera that doesn't pan up or down until the player forces it to, leading to jumping into off-screen hazards and full-fledged leaps of faith; repetitive combat encounters that you'll start to notice, upon hitting your third or fifth stage; and some fairly uninspired LJN style level design on a small group of stages (which likely comes from there being too damn many stages, for the kind of game it is).With the mention of stages, I have to say that the game definitely has a good chunk of them to chose from. A grand total of 17 levels. You heard me right "17 levels". Ten of which are the first set that you go through, before the Wily's Castle style gauntlet of seven more. And, while normally I would rejoice at a good amount of stages in a game - the levels themselves are so long, you start to understand why companies like Capcom and Konami limited the amount of stages in their games.With the stages being as long as they are, going through four stages could take around 40 minutes to an hour - depending on your experience with action platformers. Some stages are shorter, yes. But, often times you'll find yourself wondering just when the stage is going to end. And, the cause of this is often those beginner's traps, leaps of faith, and hits from off-screen hazards/enemies - that I mentioned earlier. As, most of the time you'll find yourself plummeting into a bottomless pit because of them - with knock-back and mid-air stun-locking being a VERY real thing in this game. With checkpoints being very few and far between, as well as only being activated by the player - through sacrificing a weapon to the altar. It can lead to repeating a section that took around 8 minutes to complete, because there had yet to be a checkpoint to appear on the stage - and one of those leaps of faith was not the right one to take.After a while, you'll find yourself having stopped trying to avoid damage when certain set-pieces show up yet again. As tanking the hits on the ground, so that you can actually keep moving and abuse those i-frames - will by far be the fastest way to keep on moving through the level.It eventually got so tedious, that I found myself wanting to take breaks from the game - because I was hoping it would just line-up the final stage and finish already.And, when a game that's not really hard becomes tedious enough to make the player desire for the game to be over - it's failed as a game, and has become a chore.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel borderline guilty in giving this game a thumbs down. The art and music are absolutely fantastic. Everything in the presentation melds together into a very satisfying aesthetic. But the depth of gameplay is frustratingly shallow. The most enjoyable throwback games build and expand upon the mechanics of their inspirations. Yet the one concept here that can't be found in Panzer Paladins forerunners is the weapon durability system -- something that is questionably enjoyable in the modern games that employ it, and certainly a confusing choice here. To its credit, there are some clever bits of level design. Ironically these sparse challenges serve to highlight how rote the platforming and combat is otherwise. Again, the presentation of this game is impressive and endearing. But it would have benefited from being a more ambitious game.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: It's not that the game itself isn't fun.But there's the lifes and checkpoint mechanic.Die three times and you have to start the whole level again, kind of a system we are used to.But when you die once, the items you already collected don't appear again.And to save checkpoints, you have to put a weapon on a pedestal, therefore loosing it. Later when you return to that checkpoint, you can get the weapon back, but it unchecks the checkpoint.And this whole mechanic can make things annoying. You die once, you can have a better chance now that you learned the enemies' mechanics, but in this "second chance" you have disadvantage, in which can lead you to die again and start the whole level from zero.

_childDocuments_.review: Game has a lot of issues, levels are too long with few checkpoints, really cheap enemy placement, fall deaths, foreground and background are not differentiated sometimes, hard to tell apart, there's almost no point in jumping out of the mech. I was beneath a fire spitting plant, my only option was to poke upwards and kill it while taking a hit just to clear the platform, really cheap situation, the goblins throwing knives will stand on a tiny platform where you are suppose to land, if you get hit that's an instant death. Shame, graphics are nice and the game shines here and there but frustratingly bad design in many levels.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Beautiful aesthetics and musicAwful platformer mechanics (slow and clumsy either in mech or at foot) and overall not good level design IMO. Choosing your own path in the stage select is all beautiful and all and a nice callback to megaman, but having merged the combat challenges with the platform ones mid level makes you only learn the mechanics (as the ring grabbing) in the worst scenarios, killing you if you dindt pulled it off by luck or making you repeat all the level again if you don't until you finally understand when you have to press which button. _childDocuments_.review: This game manages to perfectly capture the feel of old-school consoles - and by that I mean a platformer where the true enemy is the limited control you have over your character.Jump is bound to Z, attack is bound to X. There is no way (as far as I can tell) to change this. Trying to jump over canyons immediately recalls the terror of the original Super Mario Bros. where as soon as your feet leave the ground you remember you have almost no horizontal momentum and have to pray to the gods you were close enough to the edge when you jumped. If you really enjoy that classic retro feel, then this game is probably for you - but if you aren't looking for a game whose key bindings are specifically designed to emulate the feel of a blocky NES controler, than this game probably isn't for you. I am only fifteen minutes into the game, so granted my opinion is not very educated, but the inability to assign key bindings to mouse buttons is already making me tear my hear out.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a 2D sidescrolling platformer with a focus on melee combat. If you've played Zelda 2: Adventure of Link, imagine that but with more platforming and an emphasis on disposable weaponry.I beat the story mode of this game, and while there are extra modes such as "Remix Mode" which apparently changes some aspects of levels and bosses, I won't be playing any of them. Panzer Paladin was a slog to play through and I only realized as much after I'd already passed the 2 hour time limit for refunds.The biggest flaw this game has is the disposable weapon system. I'm the type of player that hoards goodies in games, and any game that adds finite resources such as this and forces it to the forefront of gameplay always rubs me the wrong way. You find weapons throughout the levels just laying around or dropped by enemies. Each has different damage, ranges, swing speeds, durability, and a spell you can cast by intentionally destroying your weapon (it does not activate by durability running out, for instance). The game throws plenty of weaponry at you in levels so you'll pretty much never run out, but they're usually low durability weapons. You can also throw weapons as a projectile which does heavy damage and will likely one-shot anything you land a hit on with, but that weapon will be destroyed in the process.The major problem with this, other than the common "too good to use" problem that often takes place with this kind of system, is the fact that the game has a built in "spirit burden" system that punishes you for hoarding too many weapons. If this burden stat is too high, enemies deal more damage, bosses become spongier, and a miniboss will spawn after the midlevel checkpoint. If this was explained from the beginning, I probably would have been chucking weapons left and right like the devs probably intended, but by the time I saw this on the stat screen and looked it up, I had so many weapons and was playing this way for so long it would have been more of a hassle to find opportunities to use all of the weapons, either for tossing or spells.With my main gripe out of the way, here's a few other things I felt the need to complain about:- Lack of movement options. A lot of damage feels unavoidable because the best thing you've got is a backdash move ala Castlevania, which you can kind of use if you turn in midair before using it, but a lot of areas suffer from having no other options to avoid having your massive hitbox collide with something.- Level segments that require you to leave your mech being littered with instant death conditions. If you play this game, do yourself a favor and practice on the first hook you can grapple to so you can get a feel for how flipping quickly your character sinks like a rock after their jump, because if you fail it later there is inevitably a bottomless pit or set of spikes to kill you if you fail. Admittedly the whip hitbox stays out for a long time which does help matters, but the whip also takes long than you would expect to come out. This is especially annoying since these segments are never directly after a checkpoint, they most often feel like they're right before the end of the stage, and stages are obnoxiously long already.- Spells are mostly useless. Beam and Wing are probably the only two useful ones, which allow you to shoot a bullet when you swing and jump infinitely for a short time. Any other spell that isn't a heal or a stat buff do very little to bosses, and even the stat buffs don't really feel worth it.- Healing is almost nonexistent. There's a couple of healing stations in the level that maybe fill a quarter of your healthbar, otherwise you have to rely on spells that will heal you, and of those the only one that really heals anything worth a damn is "Large Heal" which heals about a quarter of the bar as well. These weapons are also rare compared to other weapons. Normally I'd be right there with others telling people to "git good" if it wasn't for the other level design problems on top of this.- Soundtrack is uninspired. Just chiptune with some rock guitar layered onto it. I think the song from the sewers on the final set of levels is the only one that stood out to me as being particularly good, everything else was forgettable.So yeah, I would not recommend this game, unless maybe you got it on sale for like $3 USD. I got it on sale for around $12 and it was not worth it. Don't let the admittedly cool 90s aesthetic draw you in.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a very old school 8-bit NES action sidescroller game, sort of a Megaman style of game. You pilot a robot but can also get out on foot, where you use a whip to attack and swing around on things. This is really the only innovation over other games of the genre, and it stays true to it's old school roots by sticking to simplistic action and platforming.It's sort of hard, mainly because both forms you can assume are weak. Your robot is slow and clumsy, but can use a variety of weapons and has a large pool of HP. Your pilot is small and nimble but has hardly any HP. The game forces you to assume the pilot role from time to time, and will place some spongy enemies in your path. This just makes you feel weaker. The platforming is OK. It's a product of the generation it's emulating, so expect stiff jumps and unforgiving gaps. Both of these factors kind of sucked away my desire to play, but I will probably fire this up again because sometimes games like this scratch a certain itch.This game isn't bad, I'm just not sure who I'd recommend it to. It's got this nostalgia-bate feel to it, but honestly people who grew up with these games can go play the actual games they remember as a kid, and honestly there are dozens of more approachable and just plain better games from that era. If you're not interested in replaying the 8-bit games of yesterday, there is fun to be had here, but it doesn't offer much you haven't seen before.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't exactly say that this video game is to "die for", but it's pretty good!This is an interesting take on a metroidvania...to battle against the evil demons and help an archangel from the heavens, you play the role of an android gal and her living mech companion on a quest to save innocent humans from terrorist monstrosities.For 20 US dollars? I will admit that it has replay value. But for a digital only copy? I'd wait until it's AT LEAST discounted by 50 percent...being at 10 US dollars or less!
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: A rather disappointing example of quantity does not make for quality.Like at first glance this game sounds amazing. Mech combat, retro sidescroller platformer, tons of weapons and unique bosses. Cool af, right? Only, in every way that matters beyond presentation, the game is just a sad flop.The stages look great and are unique visually, but do not offer anything cool mechanically wise. A snow stage doesn't have slippery surfaces, a city stage does not have you deal with traffic or vertical buildings, every stage is made so it can be done in any order, just like megaman, but that also means none of them gives a distinct sense of progression or a new thing you have to learn. Same enemies, same hazards, same distant checkpoints with lines of cheap deaths all around. yay.All of the 100 weapons pretty much act the same, they really don't feel different except for the reach and powers, like other reviewers said. The game keeps tossing you more and more and almost expects you to do some inventory management. That's not fun.The cheap deaths and traps this game lays are just annoying as hell, especially combined with the lack of checkpoints. See, this is one of the game where you have a huge-ass health bars that you'll likely never die unless against bosses. BUT, you have instant death traps left and right, and regardless of your HP, you hit one and it's back to checkpoint. With the fact that these checkpoints are pretty far away, I hope you love doing the same parts over and over again.The controls are... not great, IMO. We're back to the "Enemy damage" knocks you back, no recovery allowed era, where the moment you take damage in mid-air over a gap, RIP. You don't get cool movement abilities, only a back dash and an upward dash done by attacking. So you're either always attacking upward to cross pretty wide gaps or doing some janky reverse back-dash. Ahhh... you got hit? Down in the hole and back to checkpoint. Even the enemies that are supposed to be predictable and you can block and parry move super fast and will get a cheap shot in before you react.I dunno man, there's so many good retro platformers, this one sadly doesn't hold up.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever tried to go back to old platformers like Mega Man and realized how bad they are? _childDocuments_.review: this game looked very promising, but ends up disappointing.it takes inspiration from classics like megaman, rastan, and a little of blaster master. these are all fine games except this game takes inspiration from their faults too.the art style is your standard pixel art. it does a lot with what it has and gives you some interesting boss fights with interesting weapon designs. i really enjoy how each country has weapon drops based on that region and with all of the different properties on the weapons, gives you a lot to work with and plan out. using weapons to save for later and break to cast spells. even some special ones requiring a special maneuver or hidden in walls. you can even make your own with unique stats to upload to the internet for other players to find. the environments are all varied as well and it was enjoyable to play through the different stages.the robot moves a bit clunky, but as you get used to it, the controls do feel as natural as piloting a large mech would be. your movements need to be more deliberate like in rastan or castlvania. you are given some agility though with a upwards attack to jump higher and a back-dash to dodge. overall, the game play is simple, yet gives you enough options for enjoyable combat... until you leave the mech. leaving the robot is a cute idea, but it's never used in any interesting ways. it's usually just to find a secret life, which brings me to my first complaint.this game has a pointless lives system. when you die, you either go back to a checkpoint or the start of the level, so having these lives just means if you lose them all, you have to start all the way over. this is what arcade games did to make you spend more quarters and was brought over to home consoles to make you replay levels to artificially extend your "Gameplay". the good news is that if you play right, managing your weapon spells, playing cautiously, upgrading your health, you shouldn't have any problems losing these lives. the game is challenging but fair... except when it isn't...taking a page from megaman 9, they decided to fill the game with instant-death pits so you can lose all those lives you've been accumulating. remember those deliberate controls i was praising? well now they're working mostly against you and, if you die, you go back to the last checkpoint so you'll just end up replaying the level over again and hope your jump doesn't get interrupted the next time. that's not even mentioning the mandatory pilot sections that involves swinging over bottomless pits or spikes which will also kill you instantly. these sections are just filler that accomplish nothing but to try to make the pilot seem more useful. the swinging physics are wonky where you need the maximum amount of momentum or you just die, sending you back again.overall, this game isn't hard. i would almost call it easy. although it's combat is fair and fun, it's platforming is ruined by the outdated mechanics of the past. cheating you of your your progress and the lives that shouldn't be there.for the record, i have played all the levels except the finale. i do plan to finish the game, but i already feel i can't recommend the game due to it's terrible design decisions.edit: it gets sooo much worse in the final stages and there's just more levels with deadlier death-pits. nothing against the developers, tribute has made good games in the past, but i don't even know why i have a health bar some of the time. i;m getting through levels unscathed, just to have my jump gimped and lose all my health in a pit.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start with what I really like about the game.  The music is awesome, the boss animations and cut scenes are really slick.  This game has presentation down and the 8-bit"ish" aesthetic looks really good.My problem lies with playing the actual game:Movement feels really stiff and slow.  There is a "jump back" move (think Castlevania) that you can utilize to get certain areas, but the standard jump left me in the spikes more times than I care to count unless I was hanging on the edge of every pit.Weapon variety was fine from what I played, but constantly breaking weapons for heals or buffs, durability of weapons used, and throwing weapons left me empty-handed.  To the point of the second level I played I just started skipping enemies if I could.Losing gear/buffs and having a feature for more lives doesn't make sense.  If I die using all my gear to attempt to defeat a boss and can respawn at a save point for another attempt without any of the gear, what chance do I have this time?There is an upgrade system, but it's a chance to get a sliver of heath per upgrade for a total health upgrade that isn't really worth the effort.I'm not upset with the purchase and think it's worth a try at a sale price.  But in a growing market of retro-inspired games, I think Shovel Knight is still setting a high bar

_childDocuments_.review: Fun on easy but once you try doing hard you'll find yourself dying more to stupid spike falls and getting knocked back into pits and dying than the actual bosses. _childDocuments_.review: Game overstays its welcome and manages to be the worst parts of some NES classics fused into one.Shovel Knight and Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon (1, not 2. God no 1's better) still hold "KINGS OF RETRO NEW RETRO" title, and it ain't hard to see why. They're concise, fun experiences that don't drag on. Panzer Paladin's a knock-off Mega Man meets Bionic Commando with an armored suit dash of Blaster Master, and it has the worst parts of all 3 (Suit's lame and doesn't get upgrades beyond health. Weapons are just tactical beatsticks and you can clap horseman cheeks with a blunt/impact weapon. Flame gameplay is forced and that little droning droop sound Grit makes when you go out? That's my mood when it comes time for a forced "swing session". Ugh, and this is as someone who kinda' likes platformers a lot.)PS: The bad level design doesn't really show up until the Wily Castle (You'll know it when you get to it), but is seen as early as a level with an auto-scroller. Putrid Paladin starts the "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this is actually bad boss design" ♥♥♥♥. Don't doubt it - a boss without tells even SLIGHTLY is bad. While this boss can be cheesed easily, it shouldn't have to be if they're pushing you to parry and be skillful. Get near this boss? INSTASHOTGUNTOTHEFACEHAHATAKEDAMAGELOSER. Nah. I did a run of the game on Normal until that boss served me up, then I dropped the game on Easy and proceeded to still slog. All lowering the difficulty does (apparently?) is ensure you have more lives, maybe take less damage. S'bout it. Still waiting on Cyber Shadow before I throw my hands up and stop getting into these NES-style new games. They -can- be good, but this is..average at best. I've played worse, but if I want to play "little sprite with a grappling hook has to navigate peril", then there's a game called I Wanna Be The Guy: Gaiden that does it a lot better..and it's the core gameplay, so it's not FORCED ON ME when it's the CORE FOCUS.

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is one of thousands of 2D retro pixel platformers glutting Steam.  In this case it's notable that this was professionally produced rather than just being the traditional asset flip/game construction kit template.  Instead, this is console ported from the Nintendo Switch.Despite being professionally produced, there's inexplicable, obsolete 2D retro pixel "art" used instead of proper PC graphics.  Usually this is simply because developers lack the budget or skill to do their job properly.  In this case the choice may simply be because the game was designed for the Nintendo Switch, and the little console peasant mobile device doesn't have a lot of horsepower, so can't do graphics from the late 1990's onwards. Due to the lazy pixel art being used instead of contemporary PC graphics, the visual quality here is very low.   Often we'll see a bad game with nice graphics and call that lipstick on a pig, but here they seem to have gone out of their way to make the pig look ugly.   Regardless, I didn't spend thousands on a gaming rig so I could pretend it's a NES.   And if I wanted to do that, I'd use an emulator, not pay the 50c they want for this...Wait a minute.  They want a ridiculous $20 USD for this.   Not 50c.  WTF were they on when they thought retro pixel garbage was worth AAA pricing?  What a joke!

_childDocuments_.review: If I may be honest, it's not a bad game at all, but I am not really able to enjoy it that much.I been trying to playing the game on hard mode, since I love challenges, and while the bosses are really fun and the mechanics are solid, what stops me from enjoying my time is the lives system alongside some problems brought by the weapon durability system.The idea of weapons that will eventually break is an interesting concept, but the way the game uses it can be a bit frustrating since whenever you have no weapon equipped it automatically equips you with any weapon you pick up, even if you didn't intent it to, making preserving newly collected weapons a bit of an annoyance since you have to manually go to the menu and unequipped it every time.Saving weapons also feels a bit underwhelming as the health upgrades are neat, but there's not much you can do with your kept weapons otherwise, I feel it's a miss-opportunity that we are not allowed to craft weapons we really like by using soul power of other swords.The whole mechanic of getting out of the mech is certainly interesting, too, it works really well as the final struggle in bosses, but outside of that, it doesn't really seem to fit very well in the rest of the levels since you can't activate checkpoints nor collect weapons with her, so you are forced to either find a healing item for your mech (which there aren't many through most levels), die to respawn or complete the rest of the level as a very weak player character.As I said before, I don't think it's a bad game, some people might enjoy it much more than I do, but in my case, it's just not my thing

_childDocuments_.review: This game combines several elements from Mega Man, Blaster Master, and Castlevania, resulting in a unique and enjoyable action game. The variety of spirit weapons plays a pivotal role in the plot; however, their large number renders most of them insignificant, disposable, and forgettable.Despite the multiple ending variations, the game has a fairly light storyline. The setting is interesting, but it would require more work to make the story truly memorable.The longer length and higher number of stages, which exceed the average Mega Man game, result in more play hours upon completion. While the game offers more content than the average stage-divided action game, much of it becomes repetitive, which might cause the player to lose interest midway through. More story-driven elements would help sustain engagement during the journey.

_childDocuments_.review: Criminally underappreciated. The platforming is pure Megaman (Classic) and, unlike many of its retro cousins, this one doesn't pull any punches. Some levels are long and instead patting you on the back for every obstacle cleared, they demand a pretty decent amount of consistency. The music and the animated cutscenes (by David Liu) are a nice, premium extra. Charming designs for most characters and bosses.The spirit weapon system is a bit of a miss for me and the mech aspect of it felt a little underutilized but, overall, it's a fair challenge on Hard that requires patience at times. As seen in some of the negative reviews, if you’re so eager for your dopamine shot that you don’t realize the upwards attack acts as a half-jump, you aren’t going to have a good time.
