_childDocuments_.review: Modern Retro at its finest!Its kinda like a combination of shovel knight, mega man and blaster master with some level to level souls/rogue elementsWhy do i feel these games paint a picture?- Mega ManThe mission/level structure is very much like a mega man game. Solid 2d platforming with bosses at the end that grant you their respective weapons- Shovel KnightThere's a surprising amount of mobility for a 2d hack n slash platformer. A lot of satisfying downward slashing, bouncing, momentum carrying weapon generated platforming- The SoulsWeapon degradation.... Now hear me out.... Its actually fun in this game! You find, throw, wield and break numerous weapons on your travels and can keep on you a bevy of found weapons. Each use degrades a weapon till it breaks OR you can just manually break them yourself to get power-ups! (those power-ups vary from weapon to weapon such as damage + to healing to flying lol)- The Rogue-likeYour constantly living off the land finding new weapons as you go which is fun- Blaster MasterYou have an awesome robot suit but.... you can get out of it! There's plenty of times you need to for platforming purposes. This isn't bad! Your tiny hero can sneak through all sorts of shortcuts and swing from tethers to get all over the place! While sure, your dealing drastically less damage, you can in fact complete levels and bosses with her alone (I've had to due to poor planning lol). So, If your robot takes too much damage, your gunna hafta hoof it until you can find a place you repair your suit OR be brave and do it as a tiny hero.all in allthis is a gem that takes known gaming tropes, mushes them together gracefully, has tight controls, a cool story and plenty of challenges along its decent runtime
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: The game is too difficult to really be fun, unless you are an extreme masochist gamer. It runs technically well, and only has a few bugs. But the game is brutally difficult.I play plenty of platformer games without any trouble, but in Panzer Paladin, I can't make any progress at normal difficulty, and can barely make progress on easy. There are some levels I can't beat on easy at all.A lot of my deaths are caused by the character's low mobility. You move slowly. There's no dash. There is a sort of double jump, but it's very difficult to do. There is no wall grab or wall jump. Falling down a cliff is instadeath.There is a snowman boss that has an attack that causes snowballs to fall from the ceiling. If one falls near you, you will not move fast enough to move out of the way.When you die to a boss fight, you lose all the items that you spent fighting that boss, and then return to the last checkpoint. This puts you in a worse position to try fighting the boss again. If you end up with no weapons at all, it may be impossible.Some of the game mechanics aren't explained at all, and take a while to figure out. The "spells" of weapons don't do anything when in your inventory, or in your hand, or when they are destroyed. The only time they have any effect is when you intentionally use the "break" control to break the weapon. "Breaking" the weapon from durability loss does not activate the spell. Breaking the weapon by throwing it at an enemy does not activate the spell.I don't like having to micromanage the durability of weapons to remember to activate their spell just before they are destroyed.All weapons have a very small durability -- around 10-15 strikes. When they break, they are gone forever. You can replay old stages to try to get more weapons, but the stages never get any easier. There are no "easy" stages to stockpile weapons.Between stages, burning weapons in the laboratory is the way you permanently upgrade your character. The only upgrade available is a tiny health upgrade, which requires multiple harvesting runs' worth of weapons each time. In some cases, it's difficult even to end a stage with more weapons than you started with. This makes the upgrade grinding process slow going, if even "going" at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: A nice throwback to the NES-era of platformers, albeit with a few rough edges.You control Grit, the titular Paladin, throughout the 11 levels of the game. Grit's moveset is simple he can attack in the cardinal directions, has a downward attack that lets him pogo on enemies Scrooge McDuck style and a rising upward attack that gives him slightly more height. He can also block attacks with his shield, similar to Zelda II, and do a quick backstep to dodge incoming threats.It's also possible to control Flame, Grit's pilot, to progress on foot. She has much less health and just one simple attack, though, so you'll probably use her when she's required to progress or when Grit's health reaches zero.The weapons are interesting: there are a ton of them, and it's even possible to make your own thanks to the Editor, but they're all pretty simple despite the apparent variety: they can attack in the cardinal directions, have limited durability and can be broken to unleash one of the various special abilities, from recovering health to flight or launching projectiles from Grit's weapon.Weapons can also be consumed to increase Grit's energy, but not much beyond that.The stages are standard Mega Man fare: occasional gimmick, midway checkpoint and a boss at the end that drops their weapon once defeated. These are just strong weapons, not unique ones like in Mega Man.Overall, it's an enjoyable experience, though it has its frustrating moments especially in the beginning when one's learning to control Grit and his stiff movements.There are also extra modes to play, like a boss rush, timed challenges and the Remix campaign, where the layout of the levels is different.Recommended for those nostalgic of the 8-bit era platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a very interesting game. While the concept of an action platformer with weapon durability may sound a bit strange it turns out to be a very awesome and engaging mechanic. Constantly breaking and tossing your weapons to defeat tough enemies and to get buffs for your mech to help you in a pinch kept me very entertained from start to finish. My first playthrough was around 4 to 5 hours which is just the right amount of playtime for a game like this. If you happen to love the gameplay a lot there's extra modes that'll keep you coming back for more. I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing through the game. I agree with the critics, that it could have more checkpoints, since the levels are pretty long. But if you play not too recklessly, you should be fine in most of the parts. But there are the one or other situations where you need to react quick.But this is what Mega Man did too. You had only two or three checkpoints in a level (one before a Boss Fight). So it's a thing you can get used to and on your next run you know where the dangers are.I wrote this review after i finished the Story Mode. With a fair share of deaths.So the playtime is OK for the regular price. Don't forget that the Playtime is actual playtime and not inflated by finding collectibles or grinding for XP or Resources.

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a charming retro-styled game that gets better and better as it goes on. It can feel underdeveloped in the beginning, especially since you don't have much at your disposal as a player yet, but the game opens up after you level up your health and get used to the whip-swinging mechanics. Although grinding the first level (Canada) to increase your weapon points and buy health is a little tedious, the rest of the game is great fun! The graphics are well-detailed and bright (the backgrounds in particular), the controls are tight and responsive, and the core gameplay loop prompts experimentation in using your weapon loadout. The amount of content in this title is also impressive, with an equally-fun Remix Mode, a customizable Blacksmith Mode, and extra Speedrun, Tournament, and Challenges Modes as a cherry-on-top. This is an easy recommendation for anyone interested in classic-styled action-platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Very nostalgic feel, great retro look, music, and difficulty.  Unique take on a mech platformer where your weapons have durability and "break" abilities if you force break the weapon rather than just breaking the last hit on an enemy. Also each weapon has a spirit count that adds up in your inventory which increases the enemies power, but also can be used by destroying the weapons between matches for health upgrades.  Overall very enjoyable and just about right length for vanilla campaign, and there is still a new game plus along with a couple other modes when I return for some more.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Had a lot of fun with this! Its clearly inspired by several of the old 8bit classics with a couple of new mechanics thrown on top. I enjoyed the gameplay in and out of the mech, Platforming and combat is straightforward and fun once you figure out to use up+attack to maneouver in the air. The highlight for me was the weapons system. Weapons degrade quickly so you are constantly picking up and switching weapons, or you can manually break it to unleash a special spell effect. This introduces fun decisions like which weapons to use, which to save for boss encounters and when to "break" them for their benefit spells.Checkpoints could be more frequent, but even with the single checkpoint you get per level you never need to repeat more than 5-10 minutes. Also bonus points for having a Switzerland level with the Böög as the boss :D
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This game brings me back to the styles of eld. I wasn't good at those games. And I'm not the greatest at this. But it is fun to play on my Steam Deck as I'm laying on the couch. Don't know if I'd sit on my computer and play it as it seems limited for it, but the Deck makes this worth it in my opinion.Awesome level design. Simple controls a dumbass could learn (me). And some cool cutscenes with old school dialogue.Yeah I'm digging it.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: The thing that stood out to me the most about this game is the combat. Being able to block projectiles and attacks using the shield makes for some pretty fun interactions. My favorite parts were the ones where you duel an enemy that has the same properties as you (blocking, attacking high or low).My main issue with the game is that sometimes it takes too much inspiration from the NES era, not only in graphics or audio, but in design decisions as well. In particular, instantly dying when touching spikes or falling in a hole can get really frustrating.All in all a fun experience though!
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Smooth and solid retro platformer - with Mech! It has the old Megaman games vibe. The arts are good and the gameplay concept revolving around the weapons system are pretty creative and fun once you got familiar with it.Now my personal criticisms... There are many bosses to fight but sadly it goes meh after a while as majority of the bosses post no threat to you, many of them absolutely can't win a standstill face-to-face brawl with your mech if you have the ATK & DEF buffs on... They just go down after 10-ish secs of button-mashes which make them rather uninteresting to fight once you've amassed proper weapons & spells.On the other hand, the so-called "challenge" of this game (at least to me) were actually coming from those platforming deaths (spikes & holes insta-kill) + long distance between checkpoints. There are "cheap" deaths that's rather intense in few stages, I was particularly upset in one part of the Japan stage, where they purposely(?) blended the trap floor with spikes into the ground with those monotonous coloring so it's hardly visible, those got me killed by accidents numerous times... and well to me that's not fun at all.Another small gripe from me is the attack patterns of certain enemies type feels rather "retarded".. For example: like there is this huge demon enemy that looks menacing but all it can do is throws fire right in front of them, so you literally just stand slightly further and hit it numerous time to kill it.. It won't bulge or change attack patterns or whatever, it just stand there like a meat wall even though you hurt it... Maybe it's just me, but it feels like dumb filler and serve no actual purpose at all other than delaying you going through... Few other enemies also gave me the same vibe like you are coming from the left but they threw attacks right below them / away from you <_<Overall though I think the game still feels more of a positive experience than bad, especially since it's an indie, no deny I've had good fun with it. Recommended if one like old-school platformer or cool mech.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a game that you can clearly tell the developers poured a lot of love into, but some of the ideas, despite being interesting on paper, simply didn't translate well into the game when accompanied by other mechanics on the game. With that said, let's go by parts.While it does sound enticing that you can collect tons of weapons with different stats, manage their durability levels (in a similar fashion to BOTW where better weapons would normally be reserved for stronger enemies), break them to use spells, and sacrifice them in exchange for a checkpoint... all of that falls apart on the first few levels.For starters, enemies drop weapons quite frequently and you can hoard as many weapons as you like with little to no consequence to the gameplay. There's a Spirit Burden mechanic that increases the "danger level" of the game based on the amount of weapons you have, but all it really does is slightly increase enemy damage, and allows you to fight The Horseman on each stage's middle point for EVEN MORE weapons (and those are usually high-tier weapons), which is pretty disappointing due to something on the story that would tie-in perfectly with that mechanic.Thanks to that, after two or three stages the entire system will boil down to the following strategy: Trash weapons from lower enemies become checkpoints, weapons with better spells will be kept around to be used before a boss or a trickier section of a stage, and other weapons with longer reach (range is king, speed comes second, and damage in third) will be the boss killers.You might ask what would be used to deal with regular enemies, and the answer is simple: Grit's bare knuckle is more than enough, as no regular enemy in the game is too much of a threat to warrant the use of actual weapons, and the enemies are repeated a lot on almost every single stage of the game so you'll get used to their patterns very early on. This is where the game draws inspiration from multiple games released on the NES era, with Mega Man and CastleVania being the most prominent sources of inspiration. Grit has a good weight to him and makes it feel like you're controlling a giant mech while Flame (the pilot) is a lot more nimble but far more fragile as well, which makes it really unfortunate that the stage layouts aren't the tightest and most of the time it either feels mindless, or frustrating for both characters.The mindless parts are mostly located on the selectable stages, while the frustrating parts will mostly be relegated to the Inverted Tower, this game's very on-the-nose rendition of the "Wily Castle", where you'll find some cheap enemy placements, leaps of faith and insta-death traps as well as some unintuitive stage design right on the first Castle stage.Flame's sections don't feel particularly interesting and they barely add anything new to the experience besides the grappling hook and the Extra Life hunting.The artwork itself is nothing short of amazing, everything is exceptionally detailed from backgrounds to characters, and nearly all character and stage animations have clear cues to help give you an idea of how to react to a given situation.The only nitpick here is, again, on the "Inverted Tower" where some of the palette choices look rather bland, and things that seemingly shouldn't hurt you (or insta-kill, for that matter), do while other objects that look like they might have a functional purpose are only there for set dressing.In true Tribute Games fashion, this game's soundtrack is excellent overall (if you like their composer's style), and i only have a minor complaint. Most of the tracks are really catchy and the mix of 8-bit chiptunes plus guitars and drums does work very well.However, the selectable "pure 8-bit" renditions of the tracks aren't as good and feel like they were afterthoughts, which isn't really a big issue since those can be considered "extras". **The difficulty isn't really that high unless you're doing a Squire run (flame-only) or are playing the game on Hard Mode where the biggest difference is that the game gets more annoying with the enemy selection and placement.Part of the reason why is because the levels and enemies are rather simplistic, and also because of Grit's massive health bar (which can be upgraded by sacrificing weapons, but doesn't really matter since the increments are minuscule) which, allied to the weapon hoarding cited previously, means that you can just give yourself every single buff imaginable prior to a moderately challenging session if you so wish.Those seeking a better challenge will probably want to get into the Remix Mode (or NG+) as fast as they can, as that mode is where the game finally gets a more challenging level design without relying too much on cheap enemy placement.Don't expect much from this, it's barebones but works well enough to give the game a good sense of progression, so basically your average 8-bit platformer. It has multiple endings but it all boils down to a single choice instead of tying in with the weapon system, which is a big missed opportunity.Besides the aforementioned main modes, the game also has additional modes such as the Speedrun Mode, which has you completing each of the game's levels as fast as possible in exchange for medals, a Tournament Mode that's essentially a boss rush, and a Challenge Mode, which is meant to test your skills on the game's mechanics.It's safe to say that if you really like the game, there will be a lot of content to sink your teeth into, though i personally didn't feel the urge to. Panzer Paladin has its issues, yes, but they're either minor annoyances, or don't show up nearly as much to become a serious blunder on what's essentially a pretty good experience overall.It's a solid 8/10, or 7/10 if you don't tolerate this game's issues as much as i do.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic retro platformer. In the spirit of Megaman with a healthy dose of Macross/Patlabor Panzer Paladin is a fun game with an earnest love for early 90's gaming and anime. Great music, solid controls, fun level design and challenging but not to challenging game play, this is a great fit for retro-platorm gamers. Great stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a retro-style action game developed by Tribute Games, which was released in 2020. As a fan of classic side-scrolling platformers, and robots, I was excited to try this game, and I was not disappointed. Here is my review of Panzer Paladin:The gameplay in Panzer Paladin is fast-paced and satisfying. The player controls a powerful mech called the Paladin, which can wield a variety of weapons, from swords to hammers to guns. The combat is challenging, but never unfair, and it is extremely satisfying to take down tough enemies with a well-timed attack. The controls are responsive and intuitive, and the game is easy to pick up but difficult to master.One of the most unique aspects of Panzer Paladin is its weapon durability system. Each weapon has a limited amount of durability, and once it runs out, the weapon breaks and cannot be used again. This adds an extra layer of strategy to the gameplay, as the player must decide when to use their strongest weapons and when to save them for tougher enemies.The game also has a strong sense of style, with colorful and detailed pixel art graphics and a synthwave-inspired soundtrack. I used to blast the theme song at parties with the homies, screaming "SUPER ROBOT GALORE!!!!!!" while crashing and burning. The levels are varied and interesting, with different environments and enemies to face. The game also features a number of fun and challenging boss battles, each with their own unique mechanics and attack patterns.One minor issue I had with the game was the lack of story. While the game does have a basic premise (the player must save the world from an invasion of demons), there is little in the way of character development or plot. However, this is a minor quibble, as the gameplay is so enjoyable that the lack of story does not detract from the overall experience.If you love robots, then you'll love this game!Overall, I highly recommend Panzer Paladin to anyone who enjoys retro-style action games. It is a challenging and satisfying game with great gameplay, unique mechanics, and a strong sense of style.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot like early Megaman games, where the concepts are solid but the quality and difficulty is a little all over the map.  As long as you know that going in, and it's something you like, you'll probably like this game.  The art is amazing and the basics are all solid, but there's lots of cheap deaths, instant enemy attacks, and evil enemy placement.  The weapon durability is better than Breath of the Wild - which is not the only Zelda reference this game has.  The parts of the levels where you're forced to be outside the mech aren't very fun - if they had focused on making those sections be difficult but no-death platforming sections while the rest of the game was about enemy placement, I think it would have been noticeably better.  Worth it if it's on sale or if you love NES Megaman games.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a solid platformer. Feels good to play, great soundtrack. My one big gripe is that the game is way too easy. With controls this solid I would have liked more interesting challenge, but even while playing on hard I breezed through 90% of the game. Enemies shamble around lined up to be killed. You're aparently supposed to keep low on weapons so that you don't have to fight a mini-boss, but he's so easy that I didn't even bother and was fully stocked with good weapons.I haven't gotten to the post-game stuff yet, but at this point I'm not super interested. The game's so easy that I'm auto-piloting it and that's a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good mix of old school and some new ideas. The music is good, the platforming has that old school feel where it takes an attempt or two to really get it under your belt, but thankfully the moments that require more attention are not too numerous. The mechanics play well, and you never feel like you've got an unfair challenge ahead of you. The bosses are generally interesting, and if you are having trouble there are a few things you can do to make the game easier, without a difficulty modifier. Overall a very solid old school platformer. I highly recommend it to anyone thinking they might like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a side-scrolling action game where you play as Flame, an android tasked with protecting Earth from nefarious interdimensional demons. Though greatly outnumbered, Flame has something that the enemy does not—a powerful mech called Grit, which she uses to lay waste to the demon hordes.Whereas a lot of games in the genre tend to give the players access to a couple of different weapon types, Panzer Paladin takes a very different approach. Here, weapons are treated more as disposable tools. As you make your way through the levels, you'll come across many different weapons, each with their own stats such as durability, damage, etc. As durability suggests, each weapon gradually wears down as you use it, until it eventually breaks. Because of this, it's important to choose the right weapon for the right situation. Playing into this is a weapon triangle system. This essentially means that each weapon in the game falls into one of three categories—swords, axes and lances. While a sword may be a great choice against an enemy armed with an axe, it's not ideal when going up against an enemy armed with a lance. Although this system isn't crucial to beating the game, it's good to be aware of, especially since the game can be pretty tough at times. Besides using the weapons directly for fighting with, it's also possible to break each weapon for various effects ranging from getting a health boost to unleashing a devastating lightning attack.There are many more game mechanics in Panzer Paladin, several of which are clearly influenced by classic games from the NES era of gaming. You have things like the pogo jump mechanic from DuckTales, which allows you to bounce off of enemies while dealing damage to them. It's also possible to switch between piloting the mech, or having Flame be on foot, something which players familiar with the Blaster Master games will recognize. This mechanic is used frequently as some spaces are too small for your mech to enter. When on foot, Flame is able to use a whip both for attacking enemies, and for attaching to pieces of the environment to swing across pits and other hazards. Another big influence are the Mega Man games. Panzer Paladin uses a level structure similar to that found in those games, where you get to decide which order to play the levels. Towards the end of the game however, it becomes more of a linear affair. Even the Castlevania series gets a nod in that some walls in Panzer Paladin can be destroyed to reveal hidden goodies. This creates an incentive for not just rushing through the levels but to take the time to explore.Other mechanics include the the Backdash move, which if performed at just the right time can be used to gracefully pass through enemy attacks without taking damage. It's also possible to throw the currently equipped weapon at the enemy for massive damage, as well as blocking either high or low attacks.While having all these different options may sound great, this turned out to be one of my bigger problems with Panzer Paladin. There are so many different mechanics that quite a few of them end up feeling a little underdeveloped, and as a result the game feels a little unfocused. Another example of this that comes to mind is the upgrade system in the game, where it's possible to upgrade your health a couple of times in exchange for some of the weapons you've collected. While I usually really like upgrade systems, there's nothing to upgrade here besides your health. I would've loved to see a wider range of upgrades so that you could for example choose between upgrading your defensive or offensive capabilities. This is something I think would've done a lot to add more replay value to the game as well.As far as the visual goes, the game looks fantastic. The environments you traverse all look excellent and have all kinds of visual flourishes. Likewise, the characters all look great, and I was especially impressed with how well they animate. For those who want it, there are also various CRT-filters available for use, which is something I always really appreciate, especially as this is something that developers often seem to omit.The audio side of things is equally as impressive, and composer Patrice Bourgeault has done a great job composing each of the tracks.Panzer Paladin is a surprisingly long game, and will likely take most players around 5 to 6 hours to complete. Personally however, I found that the game could have benefitted from being a bit shorter, as the levels in the game do tend to overstay their welcome, often having very long stretches between checkpoints which you can easily end up having to replay multiple times if you end up making even just a tiny mistake. Another thing I found a little strange, is a recurring miniboss fight against The Horseman. Since this fight happens several times throughout the game, it soon stops becoming a challenge, especially since his pattern remains the same for every encounter, something which feels like a bit of a missed opportunity compared to if he had evolved a little every time you refight him.Although I may come off as negative, there is definitely a lot to love about Panzer Paladin, and despite its shortcomings I would highly recommend it to anyone who grew up with older consoles like the NES, or who just happens to be a fan of games from that era.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer freakin’ Paladin. From what I was promised, based on the trailers & footage, was a straight-on 8-bit mecha vs giant demon action experience. And after playing through the game, I can safely say that it absolutely delivers.The plot, in its simplest form, involves giant weapons crashing down to Earth, which act as gates for demonic forces to come and rough up every major city around the world (or at least the ones used for this game) and now it’s up to our heroine, rescue android & squire Flame to pilot a Paladin mecha named Grit to stop them and send them back to where they came from. and that’s about it when it comes to the plot. Sure, other characters could’ve used more development. At least Flame, while limited to being fun and cool, is still a better & interesting female character than any Disney Star Wars heroine. Grit is awesome as well.I didn’t mind the non-linear approach when it comes to choosing which stage to begin with, although why Canada is the very first stage you’re forced to begin the game with bogs my mind. Each stage is unique with their own music and boss characters based on numerous mythologies such as Medusa, Anubis, Lilith & Wendigo despite the fact you get to fight him in remixed mode. And while we’re on the subject of bosses, why is there no Norse Mythology boss like Loki? So much for inclusivity, if you ask me.When it comes to gameplay, you basically fight as Grit, laying waste to any monsters that stand in your way while simultaneously receiving any weapons most of them will drop and use in battle. While he moves a tad bit slow, he makes up for with an upward air attack that doubles as a double jump and a Scrooge McDuck-style downward air attack that’s useful in taking down multiple enemies on the ground. The shield protects you from most projectile shots whether you’re jumping or walking, and the parrying technique is very easy. I could not even describe in words how good it felt to deflect an enemy attack, and mostly swiping their weapons from them in the process. If there’s one nitpick with Grit, it’s that he would’ve benefitted great from a forward dash. Now there is a backwards dash which is very useful in dodging certain enemy attacks, but a forward dash might’ve helped me avoid getting hit from blasts raining down on me during certain stages or for getting to the end of the stage faster, especially during speed run mode. And couldn’t we have gotten a better upgrade system than just, “Oh, you want better jumping abilities? Defense upgrades? Again, a forward dash? Tough break, you will take your health increases and you will like them.”But there are times where you will need to eject Flame from Grit and use her to get past areas where your mecha buddy can’t reach. Flame is fun to use whenever the situation calls for it. She’s quick and nimble and she can use her whip to go Castlevania on enemies, recharge Grit’s energy when you come across a recharge station, or swing from one side to another. The downsides? Well, for starters, her health gauge is as small as Thor: Woke & Thunder’s box office earnings and she does little damage to bigger enemies. So, when Grit loses his health and Flame’s on her own to defeat the boss, good freakin’ luck. To be fair, I have gotten lucky and managed to defeat a boss as Flame with only a little bit of health left on a few occasions.The weapon system is very accessible, allowing you choose which weapons you want to use as you progress through each stage, to insert into checkpoint spots to safe where you left off in the event of your death, or preserve for more powerful bosses. Mind you, every time you slay an enemy, your weapon comes close to breaking, so your only options are to either attack, throw it, or by holding two buttons together to unleash a powerful spell that can help you to your advantage. The beam, healing, attack up and defense up spells are what I found most useful. When it comes to extras, you’ve got your new game plus (aka remixed mode), speed run mode, a tournament mode where you fight all the bosses, and a challenge mode where you gotta collect all the orbs before reaching the goal. But the best one of all is the blacksmith mode, where you create your own weapons to be uploaded to the game. As the creative type, I've so far made some neat weapons such as Thor's hammer, Sephiroth's sword and Charles Bronson's friend Wildey. Mind you, these items only drop whenever you duel with the Horseman on any stage.While I haven’t gotten far in remixed mode, I can determine, at least based on a few stages I’ve beaten (on hard difficulty, might I add), that this game should’ve gotten a slight bump in the difficulty. So if you’re starting this game for the first time, do yourself a favour and play this game on hard difficulty at all costs.The retro graphics are good, and the animated cutscenes are impressive. Sure, there’s more oranges, but I honestly didn’t mind the colour scheme they went. Character designs, particularly Flame & Grit are nice nods to 70s & 80s sci-fi anime such as Tekkaman & Robotech. Also, while I wasn’t pleased with the soundtrack at first, it eventually grew on me as I kept playing. Some awesome  tracks include the main themes (including an awesome cover by Power Glove), Japan, Egypt & USA.ConclusionPanzer Paladin is a must-have for those aching for a combination of 8-bit graphics & full-on 2D mecha action. The difficulty levels and the lack of much needed gameplay mechanics are this game’s few flaws, but that shouldn’t deter you from jumping into your Paladin mecha and laying waste to numerous demons while simultaneously obtaining their weapons. Here’s hoping Tribute Games makes a follow-up to this good game with improved gameplay mechanics & cranked up difficulty. Until such time, Panzer Paladin gets 4 Grit & Flame tag teams out of 5.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a really neat game inspired by old school platformers from the Nes era. If you're a fan of retro games you'll feel right at home with this one. You control a mech that can punch, backdash and collect melee weapons. The weapons are the main focus of the game. Each one has a durability meter. You can sacrifice your weapon by throwing for extra damage or destroy it to unleash a spell that can damage enemies, buff attacks or gain health. You can only carry 4 at a time, but in addition any extra weapon is added to your storage which you can equip from the start menu at any time. Also, the weapons are used for currency in order to upgrade your mechs health points. Lastly, you'll also have to give up a weapon in order to activate the checkpoint(s) throughout the levels.The game feels very inspired by megaman, blastermaster and ducktales which I welcome. The difficulty wasn't a problem at all for me. I feel like the game is a little more difficult than others have said. I will say that at times I wish I had a checkpoint closer to an area where you're more likely to die over and over. While I do like the combat mechanics, the movement leaves a little bit to be desired. The mech at times feels a little sluggish to control and dodging boss attacks can be a pain. Your dodge can only work by moving backwards. You have to do an upward attack to avoid low moving attacks. There were times when it felt very difficult to not get hit. Other than that I really enjoy what I've played of the game so far. Really scratches that nostalgic itch I have for old school games. If it's discounted at a reasonable price I'd say for sure pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly fun platformer with some minor annoyances. Great graphics and music that really nail the both 8-bit & late '80s anime aesthetic, they really pulled me in during the few minutes of play. Gameplay is fairly straightforward old school platforming and this could turn off some players: falling into pits means insta-death and be set back quite a bit in the levels. The game mostly involves going around with your big mech but you can leave it and use the pilot instead. This is mostly fine except for sections where you're forced to leave the mech behind and these usually involve platforming challenges. Given the insta-death nature of failing those challenges these sections can be annoying if you're not used to them. Level variety is also a bit of a mixed bag, end bosses are distinctly different and fun to fight, but the levels themselves tend to lack different mechanics that would make them stand apart. Recommended if you played lots of old school platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Ok I left my last review in a fit of frustration, and I do still believe there needs to be 1 more checkpoint in levels, at least on easier difficulties. But the game is worth grabbing while on sale.The workshop weapons are cool, I'm kind of curious as to what exactly decides what weapons can be obtained and what ones can't, as I haven't gotten any of the phallic weapons yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game but to be honest with the huge gap between checkpoints it can be pretty unforgiving at times, mainly around bottomless pits and cheap shots you've got very little time to react to. I wouldn't mind them so much if it didn't set me back 10 mins. Still, game is interesting and the weapons add some fun variety.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: A mixed bag of good/interesting ideas combined with annoying/frustrating ones.The good:- The variety of weapons is refreshing.- Constantly juggling and breaking the weapons keeps things fresh and different.- Having unique spells to use per weapon type is fun.- Making your own weapons that will drop from the mid-boss is a nice feature.- Switching between the mech and pilot makes for different and interesting platforming.- The different stages (and there are many) are all visually unique with unique enemies and platforming challenges.- The hard mode is more difficult without being an absolute wall.  I played through both Story modes on Hard (pending the last 2 stages in remixed) without needing to worry too much about the enemies being too hard to deal with.The bad:- The level design is uneven between different stages.  Some are complete non-challenges, while others are so littered with instant-death spikes and pits that it's just a chore.  Especially when...- Checkpoints are far apart, and there aren't many.  You only get 2 in each stage, one at the mid-mark and one just before the boss.  And heaven forbid that you lose your mech, as there is no way to activate a checkpoint without stabbing a weapon into it, which you can't do as just the pilot.- There are ridiculous portions of the game where you need to make it through narrow spaces with instant-death spikes in the ceiling and the floor, as well as bottomless pits.  If you know ahead of time that this area exists, you can sometimes use the Wings spell to just trivialize it, but in other cases, you need to make edge-hanging jumps of a precise height to clear the pit without blowing up your entire mech on the spikes.  These are the most frustrating deaths.- Certain platforming challenges as the pilot are problematic due to the priorities of the whip.  If an enemy is anywhere near one of the "mech health recharge stations", you can forget about attacking that enemy.  Your whip snaps to the station, even if it's empty.  Similar things can happen with the swinging rings.General comments that are neither good nor bad:- Mech health drops are non-existent, but you can break certain weapons to heal, so that's kind of the same thing.  If you're a platforming veteran, you won't really be losing your mech due to damage (outside of maybe a boss-fight where you go in unprepared).  There are also these tanks of healing juice that you can whip as the pilot that get you a small amount of mech health back.- Pilot health pickups are actually fairly generous, in my opinion.  In the spaces where you are required to be out of the mech, there are health pickups sporadically placed in the area (usually only 1 is needed, and that's all that is there).
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Had a great time with this game. The art and music are great, I was instantly in love after the initial opening. There are plenty of levels and extra modes. I likee the megaman aspect of being able to select your stages in the beginning with a glimpse of the boss that awaits you there, I think the later levels could have benefited from the same treatment. I enjoyed the gameplay quite a bit. Managing weapons and breaking them to cast their spells was an interesting way to add another layer of strategy beyond timing and pattern recognition.  The Zelda II style sword and shield mechanics are fun. The challenges that come with mobility limitations remind me of getting through old NES games like ghosts and goblins. You have to adapt and change the way you play to get through with what you have. The mech is a little slow, so you have to compensate in some situations with other options. There's a back dash that gives invulnerability. You can pivot and back dash to dash foward on the ground or in the air. Getting the hang of this was important for late stage levels. Some folks say there things you just can't dodge, it's probably something you need to get past with a back dash. Each level has a mid stage checkpoint and pre-boss checkpoint. Folks who maybe didn't grow up with NES games may find this pretty harsh, but at least you have infinite continues.The thing I probably struggled with the most weirdly was using the whip to grapple and swing across hooks. It's not very intuitive and in many cases the punishment is instant death and a level restart, sometimes very far into the level. I was trying to time my jump right when I was getting to the end of the swing like a normal person would, but after some practice I learned that it was actually better to jump late after peak swing. If you are early or even on time, you'll fall like a rock rather than arc. This felt broken and frustrating because you'd have to get really far in a level just to attempt it again, only to die from what should be a simple maneuver. Once I got the hang of it I never had trouble anymore, but for a while it was driving me ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nuts. Other than that the rest was great.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This game pays homage in the right ways to games of yesteryear. Tough and challenging and most mistakes feel like you made them instead of bad design. Combat design is a great balance of durability management and breaking weapons to cast spells, with how many weapons drop I would highly suggest leaving your "gear fear" at home and try out everything. Sound design is killer and with the Powerglove theme it hits what it's going for. A must buy for fans of old 8 bit games, music, or just good balanced gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: One big con: the mech is quite slow. Megaman 1 movement speed, not Megaman X. This is disappointing given the mech can to this reverse-dash, but cannot forward-dash. Otherwise this is a total labor of love, the music slaps and the artwork is great. You just have to be tactical, not reflexive. Interesting weapon mechanics: you pick up melee weapons from enemies, you can consume the weapons to cast spells (unique per weapon, eg. heal, lightning bolt, absorb, durability+, etc), the spells are tied to the durability of the weapon, and you can throw weapons (generally destroying them), they can also be inserted into checkpoints to save your checkpoints - or be removed to delete the checkpoint while carrying your weapon forward, so there's an interesting tradeoff there. Worth checking out if you're big into the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Music- Dat 80s pixel art in the cutscenesCons:- Slow as molasses movement paired with fast combat is a terrible mix. Genuinely un-fun to play. Absolutely huge negative.- Le epic difficulty becuz the NES did it. Shovel Knight has been out for 7 years now we know how to do retro difficulty right. This mixed with the bad movement is frustrating.- The gimmick of ditching weapons constantly is worthless as every single weapon attacks exactly the same only the damage varies. So just use weak ones for ranged and strong ones for melee.- Absolutely useless dodge.Recommended? 100% no Shovel Knight is what you want not this.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Playing as a clunky slow robot in a melee based platformer just doesn't work.  Ninja Gaiden for the NES worked because you were fast and had multiple ways of attacking your enemy.  It s felt smooth and quick.  This game gives you the large clunkiness of a huge robot, in a tight platform setting.  And it just doesn't work.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzel Paladin is a good mash of games like Metal Storm, Megaman and  Master Blaster creating a unique experience that I can get behind. At first I was annoyed at it's durable weapon system but after figuring out the mechanics I started to enjoy myself. The bosses aren't too difficult so far but I love fighting them and figuring out their patterns. The music is great.  I don't think It will take me long to finish this game since I'm used to 2D platformers but id recommend Panzer Paladin if you want something short and sweet.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: If you really, actually like classic side scrollers, the negative reviews do not mean anything. Levels are linear, some areas with traps, sometimes you go right, sometimes you go left. Yeah, that's a side scroller. I am not sure how that's a negative. Side scrollers ARE repetitive. You know that going in. For the next few hours, you'll be doing pretty much the same thing. If you can't stand that, honestly I don't think you enjoy side scrollers.What's important in this genre of games is, the gameplay. Does it hold up until the end? Yes. It does. Soundtrack is good, visuals are good, the rest is classic side scrolling action. If you grew up with this kind of games, there is no reason you shouldn't like this. Ignore the negative reviews. See for yourself. You should be able to tell if you want to continue playing or not in 2 hours in a game like this that is only a few hours long.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!  The game is moderately difficult until you understand how to use the Weapons and their abilities.   Liked the mech/ pilot gameplay along with the interesting abilities.  Lots of bosses and enemy types with lots of levels.  The only complaints I have are that there are too many refights with the centaur if you go my route and horde tons of weapons.  Also that there is not really a clear distinction between normal and hard other than spikes doing 1HKO.  Will check out this studio's other games in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer paladin is a great game that suffers from a weirdly unneeded trope of old school games difficulty, what is that you ask? pits...looot's and lots of pits, now I'm not against them but when 90% of what kills me is an annoyingly placed enemy and pit it...isn't exactly the most fun, at least not in a lives system game, there are fun varied enemy types that are difficult in their own ways and although throwing weapons or using their other functions can mitigate pits it's not always as simple as that if you don't have that weapon or a weapon to use at all which honestly shouldn't ever be a problem luckily dood.Of course I say that but as much as the pits bugged me personally I know people who seem to like a lives system and don't mind them as much so I guess if you like them good! especially considering the game really is good, interesting enemies and bosses alike, great music an interesting play style mixed between mainly playing as an awesome robot and then a little android gal with a futuristic castlevania style whip who can fit into small spaces and traverse area's with that very whip and there's a lot of great weapon designs as you go through the game, there's not much story sadly and that's a shame because the characters seem like they would be a lot of fun dood!If you don't mind pits and a lives system then you're golden, this is the game for you, I enjoyed it and I can't stand lives systems and pits so that says a lot, that said even with remix mode I think I'm pretty done with it after a single run so I hope ya'all give this game a chance and enjoy it if you do dood!
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Like the other games developed by Tribute Games that I've played, aesthetically this game is great.  Unlike the other ones, I didn't drop this game.  In other words, Mercenary Kings, Flinthook, and Panzer Paladin have gameplay that I consider to feel repetitive which can evolve into frustration after a while.  The difference is that Panzer Paladin is short enough where it doesn't overstay its welcome, but it did begin to feel like a slog about 3/4 the game.  It feels like the core gameplay, while technically an interesting idea, isn't as fun when actually playing.  I felt the rarity or uniqueness of some weapons encouraged weapon hoarding which then discouraged experimenting or usage of them, since they will eventually break and are bothersome to obtain again, somewhat similar to the problem of saving up rare elixers and potions in rpg games.  Weapons can be thrown for long range attacks but immediately shatter upon impact, so to get the best bang-for-your-buck, the player repeatedly scrolls through their weapons to find the cheapest ones to throw while in mid-combat; it felt like not having long range engagement at all might've been better.  While there is a Laboratory for spending spirit points, it only sells small health boosts, and it does nothing else once they're gone.  There's not really any decision making involved, so the health boosts might as well have been given at the completion of each stage.Otherwise, it has simple, solid platforming and combat.  It also avoids one of the gripes I have with other 2D platformers which is the floor is  pit falls.  Of the 2D platformers I have played, later stages of the game include increasing amounts of pitfalls that instantly kills the character when fallen into, which for some games essentially massively negates any health related buffs the player has worked for.  Combined with the mechanic of how touching enemies bounces the character away and how they're located right at the edge of platforms to block player progress, I haven't really found this idea to be fun to experience.  This game avoids that for the most part, and while there are pitfalls in the stages, they're not that numerous and not all of them are deadly.Overall, I felt this is better than the other Tribute Games I've played, but I was far more captivated by the aesthetics than the gameplay.  I hope to one day play a game by the developer where I'm captivated by both.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun retro-style game! Of the countless NES-style indie titles to pop up since the retro revival boom began, in my opinion this game is definitely one of the most successful. The gameplay is simple without being one-note, the difficulty is challenging without being frustrating, and the art style is super faithful to the retro-anime time period it's inspired by without feeling like it's knocking off of the classics. Oh, and the music is pretty great too; where most chiptune composers these days try to fake feeling with complexity & hyperactivity (just add more notes!), I give this score & its composer a thumbs-up for having a solid theme weaved throughout the soundtrack.If you're looking for a good new game to scratch the NES-style itch with, definitely give Panzer Paladin a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: How is this not getting the same level of notoriety as Shovel Knight?? This game is outstanding. I usually like to leave long winded reviews, but I'll keep this one short just by saying, this is a hidden gem if I ever did see one. If you enjoyed Shovel knight, you'll much more than likely enjoy Panzer Paladin too. It borrows elements from Shovel knight, MegaMan, and even Breath of the Wild, as well as adding some of its own unique game mechanics. This isn't going to baby you, but it does give you full control over your checkpoints, depending on how you want to proceed, and the adrenaline of having your lives really mean something is in full force with this one.Steam gives you 2 hours to know if you're going to like something, and this game doesn't have any filler at the beginning, so I would encourage anyone who hasn't tried this one yet to dive into it. If it's not your thing, just refund it, but don't overlook this one just because a few reviews on major gaming outlets complained about the difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy it. Though it can't make up it's mind about what console it was supposed to be for and to me that's really bothersome.Blaster Master Zero and it's sequels have chosen the PC Engine/Turbografx, which is a pretty good choice. But this has an NES color palette with sprite power of a PC Engine, which just kind of feels wrong IMHO. Then attempts to use a lot of them limitations of the YM2612 (Which in theory with more memory could handle PCM sampling just fine and would be an acceptable large target, even if it isn't the Genesis/Mega Drive perfect.)Don't play this game for it's fake nostalgia value and play it on it's own merits. It's not a bad game but I'd buy it on sale, I got in a humble bundle and that was an acceptable cost
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: So far It's fun. It reminds me to good old NES era games. Play it if you like typical platformer NES games. Swords are always fun.I'd wait for sale if I were you. I kinda didI'll update this review when I finish the game=== The Soundtrack is beautiful ===Edit: I finished the game. I still recommend it, it's great!
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: An okay pixel platformer that swipes a lot of retro concepts, mashes them all up, and then sprinkles in slivers of other ideas that don't mix together as well as they ought to. You can kinda see the connections that Panzer Paladin was trying to bridge, but the way things are actually laid out makes most mechanics shaky and questionable. The details of weapon durability, types, breaking, spirit points, and inventory management could’ve used some fine-tuning. Individual weapons could’ve been much more distinguishable or interesting to wield. The Master Blaster pilot idea is cute, but pilot segments are scarce, the pilot’s gameplay is really basic, and their health is so low that they’re useless in boss fights.You could pick and choose any mechanic to remove and very little would change about the flow of the game. With a bit more focus on interconnectedness, maybe it could've all slipped together. Otherwise, to give a few generic compliments, all the sprite work, music, and controls are solid enough to do a decent job of masking how confused the game is deep down. Check it out if its retro-ness catches your eye and there’s a good deal around for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, its a great game, really captured authentic retro experience. Sure it leads to some negatives like clunky platforming, insta death spikes and pits level design, but once you get used to its quirk, its very fun. Loved the boss battles, every single one of them felt unique. Art was amazing, wish theres more pixelated anime cutscenes though, because the few cutscenes that were in the game just looked spectacular. Music was jamming as well, there's no bad track whatsover.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic gameplay in this 2D sidescroller. Choose your level like Megaman. However, the weapons you get from bosses and enemies don't seem to counter other bosses. You will be collecting weapons all the time. Each weapon has a durability bar that reduces as you strike enemies and certain blocks. They can be willfully broken to cast spells, or thrown at enemies as projectiles. Once you clear a level you spend them on upgrading your mech's durability i.e. your mech's health bar.You will be forced to jump out of the mech and play as Flame at times. She is about half the size of Grit and if you die as Flame you will be reset at the last checkpoint. She uses a whip that can help you swing across gaps and gives you some distance between enemies. She is weaker than Grit so you'll be whipping enemies a lot to kill them. You can choose to get out of the mech, or if Grit breaks you basically have a second chance. When you make it far enough to get Grit back or finish off the boss as Flame it's an extra rewarding experience.If you've got a penchant for sidescrollers, and you enjoy classic Castlevania style combat then this game is right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a modern day love letter to the 8 and 16-bit eras with influences from Mega Man X, Castlevania, Blaster Master, Metroid and Duck Tales.You take control of a robot that pilots a mecha on a mission to stop monsters from destroying the world.Combat and item management go hand in hand as the weapons you'll find throughout each stage can be used in direct combat with enemies or destroyed in order to buff your mecha.(Tip: Use your weapon until it's just about to break and then destroy it for it's buff)The soundtrack is fantastic. The combat and item system is unique. The artwork is beautiful and lively. The campaign can be short, clocking in at about 4 hours; however, with multiple endings, adjustable difficulty and the most recent update adding a challenge mode and the ability to create your own weapons, there is good reason to return for another run.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin looks like it has everything to be the next indie action platformer to come around with clean sprites and a great 8-bit soundtrack that perfectly emulates the feel and sound of NES games. Unfortunately, where games like Shovel Knight innovate and stand out by modernizing the controls and general frustration of those early NES games, Panzer Paladin seems to embrace them to an almost inane degree which is a shame because it has a lot of great ideas and clever ideas to make it stand out. I think if it had a better progression system, no lives, and better checkpointing I would remember it as being pretty great but as it stands, it is if not a fairly generic retro tribute game in the vast sea of this over-saturated genre. This review sounds really harsh but there are a lot of great ideas here and I would love to see them iterated upon in a sequel if that could ever happen. This game had a lot of potential and while I still recommend it, it is just barely in the positive.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: I was pleasantly surprised by this game.  It's similar in many ways to Mega Man, with a little Castlevania and Blaster Master mixed in.  The core mechanic is that you get these weapons (mostly dropped by enemies, but sometimes found) which have durability and will break after a little use.  There isn't a lot of difference between them aside from their hitbox size and damage stats.  When a weapon is close to breaking, rather than letting it break on a normal hit, you can throw it at an enemy, or you can break it yourself to use its one-shot spell.  These spells are pretty standard fare, but they are also a core gameplay component.  Common spells are typical buffs (attack up, defense up), healing various amounts (small/med/large/full), and other things such a Thunder which is a screen wipe or Beam which makes your other weapons shoot energy balls for a short time.The game is challenging, but not overly difficult, and it does have three difficulty settings and a variety of extra modes.  I haven't finished it yet, but I don't get the impression it's more than a few hours long.  If you're looking for a good Mega Man-like platformer, this is a good choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a sidecroller action game which differentiates itself from the rest in 2 major ways: first, you can dismount from your mech and play as the android pilot which comes in handy in a few occasions, but it's mostly useful for getting through sections were the mech doesn't fit. It's pretty cool to be able to do it though.Second, but a lot more important, is the weapon system. These are the main power up in the game and can be found in abundance by defeating certain enemies or simply by progressing through the levels, they are mostly made out of cardboard judging by how fast they break. You can also throw them as projectiles or break them for a special effect. Furthermore, you can even design your own or get new ones from the workshop, these special weapons only drop from a particular miniboss, but since they are custom made, they can be very powerful.At first I didn't like the system very much because there's no other form of progression in the game besides some minor health upgrades, but the system grew on me eventually. Once you've got a decent amount of weapons your options increase a lot, obviously healing spells are useful in any situation, but so are other buffs. The game becomes almost too easy as it goes on because of this.This game also features some platforming, especially on the later levels, but it's nothing to write home about, it's clearly not the main focus of the experience. Finally, Panzer Paladin is aesthetically brilliant, the graphics and music are simply awesome. You can see for yourself in the promotional material, the level of detail is insane even for the backgrounds, and the entire game looks this good. There are also a few animations at key points during the story which are also wonderful.Ultimately, I believe Panzer Paladin is a pretty good game, but the weapon mechanic is a love it or hate it kind of thing in my opinion, I can see it turning people off. I'm also still in awe at the art direction.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome art, great assortment of weapons, excellent level design with just enough challenge to make it compelling. Retro look with tight, contemporary controls. Unique style, I can't say enough about this game. It was on my wishlist for a while and then was in the Humble Monthly. Nothing like getting a great game for essentially free.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a great megaman/castlevania style game.When I started playing I had a really hard time getting used to the robot "weight", the weird jump attack and the backwards dash (like in symphony of the night), but after half an hour the controls just felt natural.The coolest feature of this game is the weapon creation, It is really simple to use and from time to time the devs add best weapons in the workshop to the base game.If you like games like oldschool megaman and castlevania you probably will like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Great NES/Mega Man inspired game!Play the intro level then choose your boss. 1 intro level/boss, 10 levels/bosses followed by a "Wily Castle" stages (unlike Mega Man you wont fight them again) with unique bosses and the Final Boss.Great music, gameplay and stages!Choose between original and 8-bit soundtrack and after you are done with the game, play the whole game againo in remixed mode.Highly Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun, old-school 2D action-platformer (a la NES Megaman games, with a tiny bit of Blaster Master), with a killer 80s anime aesthetic. A little on the short side if you're good at these sorts of games, but there seems to be enough to give it some replay value (remix mode, challenge module, difficulties etc). Overall recommend if you're into these sorts of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Liked:- Fun, satisfying gameplay- Variety of levels, enemies, weapons, and challenges- Fun and unique bosses- Story is good but doesn't interfere with gameplay- Art style is retro but still very expressiveDisliked:- One hit kills of pits and some spikes, especially with long gaps between checkpoints- Life system means that game overs make you replay more of the level
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: A great game severely dragged down by bad difficulty ballancing.On one hand most regular enemies are complete pushovers that are super easy to defeat and do very little damage even on the hardest difficulty. This leads to many parts where you practically sleepwalk your way through the levels.On the other hand you have one-hit-death spikes and pitfalls that may seem harmless for everyone who played Mega Man but are surprisingly hard to avoid, due to your characters being rather slow and immobile. Combine this with checkpoints that are way too far stretched out for the size of the levels and you will find yourself being forced to "work" through long sections that you have already mastered the first time, just to get to the part where you suddenly need to be confusingly careful.Sure, you have movement options like the upwards attack that (once again) make most jumps trivial. However, since this move prevents you from using other attacks, it feels rather clumsy and not fun to use. It never feels like there is a solid middle ground, where the game is challenging but not artifically frustrating.The solution imho would have been to very slinghtly increase the movement speed, add another movement option to get faster through the levels or add a countermeasure to the one-hit-kills. Especially option 2 would increase the skill ceiling for experienced players while giving less experienced players more ways to avoid frustrating instant death traps.Sadly, this strange problem is what reduces this otherwise fun retro plattformer for me from a clear recommendation to a "buy it on a discount".
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Overall good but some game some gameplay decisions are keeping me back from giving this game an even better score. So 7/10 at best.Edit: Managed to beat all the bosses within 4.5 hours. Reached to inverted tower and stopped playing. I absolutely have no patience or have the strength to finish a huge zone that has 6 levels in it. Having a "final marathon" level was a NES thing and should be a NES thing, even when you're mimicking a NES game.Again 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good, short but fun platformer. A lot easier than many games like it. Checkpoints could be a bit closer together though. I prefer slightly shorter sections with a higher challenge to longer ones with low challenge, especially if instant death is possible. Good music, cool bosses and the mechanics around weapons are interesting, if kinda pointless. But the best part about this game is the art. Beautiful use of colour, gorgeous background and levels, great animation on all the bosses. Very pretty.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This is a well-crafted platformer, but it can be a little difficult to get into because of the way Grit handles.  He's bulky and ponderous, and his attacks have very particular arcs.  For some players, that might be a plus, rather than a minus - it definitely feels distinct from Shovel Knight or the Messenger.Until you get a feel for how he jumps and dodges, and get used to standing tall to present your shield to high attacks, rather than trying to crouch under them, you may feel like enemies are darting around you and tagging you with impunity.My one serious complaint is that checkpoints are very far apart.  There are definitely times when I fall into a bottomless pit and then say, "Never mind," and quit for the day rather than redoing half of the level.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Okay i might like this game just because theres robots but, the game is fantastic i love the multiple uses for weapons from checkpoints to upgrades to healing it feels really tied together. The music is fantastic and so is the pixel art. Only real complaints would be some of the boss designs are basic and it can feel pretty easy for a megaman style platformer but that might be due to the slow deliberate movement.  And the name of the game. And the screen scroll can be nauseatingly fast when moving between screens.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Going to start with the bad and go up to the good, but here's a summary. The game has potential but lacks key components that would make it go from average to outstanding. It is quite frustrating at times, but the music elevates a mere 6/10 game up to at least a 7/10. Lots of Mega Man comparisons to be made, but ultimately it falls short. If they ever make a second game with this one as a basic starting point, they could blow us all away. It's a mega man style game where killing bosses doesn't offer you any substantial upgrades. You use melee weapons that all behave close to the same, and they break. You can get more hp from grinding out levels. Boring. HP doesn't make a game more engaging and the devs should know this.Instant death pitfalls. I rolled my eyes when I read about this on a different comment, but the levels are quite long and not overly varied. You have a lot of hp, and it's a real gauntlet from start to finish. One pitfall will set you back to a previous checkpoint (which costs a weapon, which is also bad), and usually this means repeating the level. It's not like mega man at all, where the levels are shorter, the checkpoints are well placed (and don't cost a weapon to activate), and jumping mechanics are way better. Stages are sometimes great, and sometimes terribly designed. It's almost like two different people made the levels. The graphics are confusing, and sometimes you step onto a moving platform without realizing it's about to move, which then means you accidentally hop off and die. Back to the start of the level with you! Enemies are fun to pop, occasional duels with random monsters are pretty fun. It's missing something, but the basic swing and punch is nice!You are incredibly talented, and I know you probably won't read this, but wow! This is your calling!Imagine mixing that with boss powers as well. So much potential!
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: There are so few words that could accurately capture the retromodern joy that is Panzer Paladin.Graphics: 8-Bit 10/10.  That is to say, this game is rendered completely in 8-Bit graphics, but pushes them to the absolute limit. Looks like it was made towards the end of the NES's life cycle (around '92 or so).Music: 10/10. AAaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaand, you can choose between modern or 8-bit music!Gameplay: 9/10. I might have dug a little bit more upgrading ability than my health bar, but otherwise perfect. You play mostly in your Paladin, a 18 foot tall or so mech. Occasionally, you will switch out to your pilot, whose Castlevania styled electric whip allows her to swing from things.The game mashes the feelings of Megaman, Blaster Master, Bionic Commando, and, yes, even Castlevania into a near perfect Nostalgic Treat.Treat yo self.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun and seriously a gem and I'd strongly recommend buying it, however it's not without it's flaws:The spritework is gorgeous but uhhh... cluttersome, sometimes it's really hard to decipher what's solid and what isn't, specially in the later stages.Also Flame's gameplay as a whole was poorly implemented in my opinion, the fact you can ONLY activate checkpoints with Grit and not with her really throws a wrench in any interest a player might have in keeping going after losing the mech, most of the time it's better to just kill Flame as well to restart the stage again than to keep going, yes you can revive Grit if you happen to find a recovery tank for him with Flame but not every stage has them before a checkpoint and sometimes you could make a lot of progress, get to the boss and not find a single piece of recovery for the robot, essentially meaning you wasted your time. Those are the only two problems I could find tho, don't get me wrong, they ARE pretty significant problems that DO get in the way of the game sometimes, but overall this game is fantastic, buy it if you like some NES-styled platforming action.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin has great, easy to learn controls and the gameplay loop is very straight forward: Get weapons, kill bad guys, defeat boss. Quality pixel art brings each of the 17 levels to life in their own way. Grit, the mech, feels like a piece of heavy equipment. Juxstaposed by Flame, who handles much quicker, there's a good rhythm to the gameplay.There's also an amazing soundtrack, each stage matches so perfectly with the accompanying music and each song keeps me pumped throughout. It's right up there with the likes of Bastion or The Messenger. I've had this on repeat at work.To top it all off is a nice little Blacksmith feature where players can create and upload their very own weapons and customize not only the stats and attached spell, but the appearance as well. It's surprisingly addicting just drawing in the editor and working with the space and colors allotted.Overall a very enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute blast from the past!  Every time a play a Tribute games I truly feel like this is a game made for 10 year old me but as grown ass man and this is no acception to that rule. Bad ass Robot? Check!Bad ass little wipping dudette? Check!Customizable Weapons? Ashbringer made by me check!Awesome community made weapons being dropped by a giant sword weilding centaure? Double check check! I have not finished the game but everytime I dive back in I'm greeted with a  a warm fuzzy feeling inside bringing me back to my childhood basement sitting crosslegged on my mom's shaggy carpet burning my eyes sitting to close to that old wooden cased CRT tv and I love this game for it. oh and the music rocks!
