_childDocuments_.review: Many things are wrong with this game, but mostly a lack of attention to detail and lack of care. For example, one of the bosses I defeated just by standing underneath it and doing up attack 30 times in a row. It didn't move from its spot once. You can do the levels in any order but the lack of difficulty across levels and bosses is great. The robot moves very slowly, not so fun to control. There's many sections in levels where you have to use a whip to swing across but it's very imprecise. One wrong jump and you fall down a gap leading to instant death. Often when you're falling there is some trap you never could have predicted. There's nice things about this game, for example the dodge mechanic can be fun to use, but mostly it's just kind of annoying and thoughtless.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Paladin

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a fun throwback platformer in the vein of classic NES titles like Mega Man and contemporary games like Shovel Knight. The combat system features a surprising amount of depth, with the ability to parry attacks and cast spells that enhance the player’s abilities. Weapons are the bread and butter of Panzer Paladin’s combat, while the player could theoretically play through the game without using any of the weapons, they provide a surprising amount of utility. The variety or swords, spears and hammers naturally do more damage than a simple punch from the player’s mech, but weapons can also be intentionally broken to activate spells that provide protection or bonus combat abilities. You can also throw weapons, which does more damage than the usual swing but destroys the weapon without spell casting. Adding another dimension to the combat is the Spirit Burden meter; while using weapons may make combat easier, having too many in your inventory can actually make the game harder, denoted by having a high Spirit Burden in the inventory screen. I found the weapon management added an enjoyable dimension to the combat, where I had to weigh how much I needed weapons against how much I might need their spells in the future. For example, I may have had a high Spirit Burden in one moment, and had to choose between breaking a weapon with the Wings spell or the Full Heal spell. The former would give me the ability to fly, which would help in sections with tricky platforming, whereas the latter would refill my health, helpful when fighting bosses. These decisions also push the player towards using the spells, instead of simply stocking up on weapons.Perhaps one of the best components of the weapon system is the Blacksmith. While I didn’t use the in-game Blacksmith to make any weapons myself, the game has the ability to pull from user created weapons found in the Steam Workshop, allowing players to come across many fun creations from the community. There are many cool creations on the Workshop page, including references to other games (An Ace Attorney “Objection!” sword) to cute weapons like a dog on a leash.  Presentation wise, Panzer Paladin is a gorgeous game to look at, with graphics that are evocative of classic 80’s platformers. However, at times I found the level design wasn’t conveyed as clearly as it could have been. Occasionally I would come across a part of the level that led me to think I needed to eject from the mech and proceed on foot. This made the game harder for myself as Flame, the pilot, is much weaker than the mech, Grit. Eventually I would either die or get far enough to see that there was enough space for Grit the whole time, realizing that there was a platform I could have jumped on that I initially thought was part of the background. One aspect of the game’s presentation that really excels is the soundtrack, which featured a variety of catchy tunes. I enjoyed it so much I even picked it up on Steam, where it’s actually quite cheap! Unfortunately, I wasn’t as enamored with Panzer Paladin’s story as I was with the rest of the game. Panzer Paladin features short cutscenes that are meant to expand on the world and character motivations, but as a whole the story that’s told is very sparse and surface level. Story isn’t always associated with retro platformers, but I would have preferred the developers either flesh out the narrative more or just forego it altogether. As it stands, Panzer Paladins’ narrative doesn’t drag the game down, but it feels superfluous to the overall experience. As a complete package, Panzer Paladin is a game that plays great, looks great and sounds great. The story mode is paced well with multiple difficulties to choose from, an additional remixed campaign mode and the ability to create your own weapons and use those made by the community. While the level design isn’t always the clearest and the story is underwhelming, Panzer Paladin excels as a combat platformer. If you’re a fan of Tribute’s previous games (Mercenary Kings, Flinthook) or just looking for something to scratch that NES-like itch, then Panzer Paladin will deliver in spades.Update: Nominated for the Steam Awards 2020 Best Soundtrack Award!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a little megaman with some mecha flavor and some blaster master mixed in for good measure.  The result is some delicious gaming. _childDocuments_.review: Panzer Paladin is a very enjoyable retro-modern action platformer. This becomes even more true if you enjoy the old school robot anime aesthetics or if the prospect of a mech traveling all over the world to duke it out with mythological monsters excites you. If that doesn’t rock your boat, that’s fine too. The game still has interesting mechanics such as the weapon spell system and the last chance mode that allows you to play as Flame, the pilot, to fall back on. Level designs, visually interesting backgrounds, and great music are also something that I would like to add to that list. Not all is fine and dandy as there are still kinks to be ironed out such as certain parts of the exclusive non-mech sections and oversight on inventory system that hinders the overall depth that game could have had. Regardless, Panzer Paladin is a homage to the games of old that I will heartily recommend to any action-platformer and mech enthusiasts that welcome the past.For a detailed account on how this conclusion comes to be or for other reviews, visit .

_childDocuments_.review: It'll probably only take 4-6 hours to get through 's campaign mode, but it's decently replayable and the pacing remains even and engaging throughout. It never really feels like the devs ran out of ideas or put in filler to pad out the hours, so it's pretty much exactly as long as it needs to be. Was definitely worth my $20, but I wouldn't say no to more. The game's level design has a classicvania feel in that the levels are tightly designed around what abilities you have available, and you'll sometimes need to stop and chill for a sec since charging forward will get you wrecked. That said, I bumped up the difficulty to "Hard" after a few stages since Medium didn't feel challenging at all. While Hard was overall a good fit, it was also somewhat imbalanced since various environmental hazards turn into one-hit kills, and you're definitely going to feel that more on some stages than others. Also, while the level design was good, the bosses were pretty hit-or-miss and definitely felt like the roughest part of the game. Some are cool and novel and do interesting things forcing you to swap between Flame and Grit to get out on top, but many had "cheap" attacks with no tells, which were impossible to avoid taking damage from unless you were experienced enough with the boss's patterns to know that you had to get well out of the way if there was even a chance of them using it. Others had long periods of time where you basically couldn't attack them at all and had nothing to do but dodge for awhile. The ability to make your own weapons and have them show up on the Workshop is cool, and I'd like to see if Tribute Games is interested in doing anything more with that, or adding more types of weapons you can build instead of the basic beatstick. It's a mecha game, so sky's the limit really.Visually, the game is done entirely in pixel art with a deliberately limited color palette per object, all the way to the faux-anime cutscenes. For the limitations they set on themselves it's quite impressive how good everything looks. Everything is stylistically solid, the renditions of all the countless weapons were cool, and the animations of all your various enemies and bosses are expressive and smooth. However, I did have some issues with conveyance. It wasn't always clear whether a part of the environment could be stood on or not, and it wasn't clear when a projectile could be blocked or swatted, or had to be dodged.Really enjoyed the music, each one keeping strong themes of whatever country of origin it was set in, with a smooth and enjoyable blend of chiptune and rock.While  has some rough edges here and there, it's overall a well-made game and I look forward to seeing if Tribute Games is interested in adding to it. I'll definitely be keeping an eye on their future titles as well. Controls are responsive and easy to grasp, and the core gameplay loop is clear within the first five minutes. The devs clearly drew influence from a number of classic platformer titles, but they did an excellent job melding and morphing them into something that is nevertheless distinctly their own.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only finished 2 levels but so far this game is really good, -Visually you have anime style cutscenes that looks like an 80s mecha show, followed by a beautiful pixel art 2d side scroller. -Gameplay loop is based on stage selection, think old school megaman and in each stage you have to beat a boss at the end that gives you a powerful weapon. You control a mech that attacks with different weapons, there is a lot of variety in the weapons you can use, each weapon has a skill you can use if you break it.  When your mech is destroyed you control a pilot that can use a grapple hook to move through the level until you can get to a station that recovers your mech. -Controls are tight, although it might take time to get used to since your mech makes a lot of your movement delayed, you can jump higher if you do an attack while in the air. On the other hand the pilot controls are easier to get into.  Difficulty wise it's alright most of the challenge comes from the platforming, however i do think the bosses might be easy to cheese with the weapon breaking mechanic.   I'm having a blast so far, looking forward to what the other levels offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Being 80's kid, Panzer Paladin feels like homecoming, but with just the right amount of modern design choices. Spikes kill, checkpoints are scarce, bosses hit hard. Every death feels justified and all you can do is to try to learn from your mistakes. A limited number of lives keeps you on your toes as you progress through the levels. Controls are tight and I do appreciate that developers took a risk by making the Grit feel more heavy to move around, which feels like you're actually controlling a weighty armored battle suit.I LOVE the fact you can  I went hitting on every block in search for narrow passages only the pilot can fit in. Hidden goods inside of walls are as rewarding as ever. Switching in between the weapons feels smooth and learning to use the spells by breaking or throwing them is tactically satisfying. You can even design your own weapons and use them in the game, alongside with those made by the ever so creative community. Hilarity ensues.Panzer Paladin looks and sounds gorgeous! Each stage stands out with unique scenery, a few different enemy types and music which fits the theme. I can't praise the sound design enough, but every sound effect feels just right and . I've found myself humming the main theme while writing this down. It's so BAD!I have very little bad things to say about the game. There could have been more optional routes for Flame the pilot, especially since her whip swing mechanic was so much fun, but overall the stages were really well designed. The laboratory, where your only option is to upgrade Grit's health, felt a bit trivial though.Thank you, Tribute Games, for bringing this to life. Proving once again, that it's not wrong to long for the good old days.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% achievement No. Yes (14 achievements). No. is a 3D platformer with puzzle and combat elements. It features a vast, open-world area where you can explore and choose the levels that you want to tackle first.- Freedom to explore 3 of the levels in any order that you want- Variety in defeating enemies- Unable to backtrack to the previous checkpointsIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650The game uses low-poly models on its characters and a huge emphasis on its surroundings. Levels are distinct with a certain theme in mind, giving some sort of variety to the visuals. However, the water in the game feels like a liquid with blue paint on it - they are not transparent and look thick as a result.The story was told by an old man to a child. It feels as if you are reliving the story, doing whatever the main character is doing. It can be weird sometimes, especially when you die and the narrator reassures you that it was not what happened to the story. Since the story was told to a child in the game, there isn't much depth to it, although it also means that it can be safely watched by children.All dialogues are voice dubbed. The voice is clear enough although people who still have trouble listening to them can read the subtitles instead. However, I found that some subtitles don't match with what the character is saying. The dialogues still have the same meaning, although it feels weird to see the discrepancy.The game mostly focuses on 3D platformers. A lot of obstacle courses will be presented throughout the levels, forcing you to time your jump or react quickly. However, the nature of the timed jump might give difficulty to some people who are not used to it, although it is still easy in general.You are free to explore three levels in any order that you want. There is a vast open-world map in the game, allowing you to explore optional areas for minigames and rewards. Four levels are also accessible from the same map, where the last level can only be accessible after the other three are completed. The vast map might confuse people who want to explore everything, but the exploration is mostly optional. The only benefit that you'll get from exploring these areas is achievements, so you don't have to be afraid of missing out.Simple puzzles are also spread to the levels. There aren't any instructions on it, although the hints are usually nearby. It doesn't take long for me to understand how to solve each puzzle despite how vague they look.Combat is simple. Most enemies can be defeated by spamming your attack, although some enemies require you to beat them with heavy attacks. As someone who likes to use light attacks, the fact that there are enemies that can be defeated with heavy attacks encourages me to use that particular attack. New skills will also be learned upon arriving at each of the three levels, allowing you to deal with enemies easily. Since combat is not hard, the use of these skills isn't needed to beat the game, although it's still helpful to use sometimes.Boss battles tend to be obstacle courses rather than boss fights. Bosses have the same skill throughout the game that is easy to dodge if you know what to do. The difficulty in the fights comes from the obstacle courses instead, forcing you to traverse through the level to reach a device that can damage the boss. However, the checkpoints in these battles are weird. Some battles require you to restart from the beginning, while some will allow you to continue after the last time you damaged them if you die.I finished the game in 5.45h with all achievements collected. As I said before, the game is easy to beat although it's easy to miss collectibles if you are unlucky. Levels tend to be split into several checkpoints and the game won't allow you to visit the previous checkpoint after you reach the next one. Moreover, some points of no return aren't obvious. I even missed some optional collectibles because of it.To be honest, I got interested in  since the store page has a picture of a macho old man with a beautiful logo in it. I never thought that it would be a solid platformer game. The main character can look a bit odd sometimes compared to the rest of the visuals, but luckily, you won't see him at close range that much. The game is easy enough for casual players to play, and checkpoints are abundant if needed. Casual players that are looking for platformer games will surely enjoy it if they like the visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR at the end.When you start the game, right off the bat, first thing I noticed is how unpolished the game is, the animations for opening chests for example seem half-assed, the combat basically consists of just mashing heavy attack and later on when you unlock the boomerang move (which for some reason is even stronger than the heavy attack while also being a huge AoE) and you spam that instead you have to watch that animation in slow-motion On the narrative side, the story is very basic but that's not why I'm here for, and the voice acting is pretty lame and you'd keep hearing the same voice lines over and over again for example every time you open a blue chest you get one of two voice lines, and you open quite a lot of them.Talking about blue chests, they are sometimes hidden or presented as rewards for challenges but basically all they do is give you experience points which you also get from killing enemies, breakable objects and runes scattered around which all seem to respawn.I like to run around, discover and collect everything but a lot of the times I just felt like I'm wasting my time getting all those runes and fighting all those monsters when all they give me is just a sliver of exp.Besides all that, what you're left to do in this game is to collect relics, this was the part I was excited about, I wanted to 100% this game but as I progressed I realized this game often blocks the path behind you when you enter rooms, locking you off some content so if you missed something tough luck, you can't get it.That part was a real problem, once I reached the windmill's outer walls I saw some runes and blue chests below and what seems to be a shortcut lift, so I jumped down but the shortcut didn't trigger so I was stuck and when trying to retrace my steps back up doors were locked, fortunately reloading my last save point solved this.This was really my biggest gripe with the game, I can deal with all the stuff I said about polish, narrative and combat, the game is still fun and I was looking for something casual to just pass my time while I collect everything, but why lock me out of an area once I finish it?I feel like I missed some things and focused on the negative but those are the things I think the devs should be worked on since my experience was mostly clouded by all this, the game still has it's moments and I wish they'd continue to support and patch and game and maybe even add more content in the future, also I think having a Discord server and talking with the players would be a good idea.TL;DR:This game feels like an early access title but I believe there's still fun to be had , and I'm still on the fence about it, I was really frustrated at some points in the game so it's possible I got something wrong and you could actually backtrack and I just missed something or could find it later, I will give it another chance and try to complete it, but as of now I cannot fully recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the game explicitly "strongly recommending" use of a controller, the mouse and keyboard controls feel surprisingly precise, reactive and intuitive, too, and I can whole-heartedly say that not owning a controller is no criterion against this game. I did play most of it with a controller and that does feel like the way it was meant to be played but the alternative has been done really competently as well.The game's main focus lies on exploration, platforming and some basic combat but outside of the dungeons the semi-open world surprises with a lot of additional content and a non-linear progression. You unlock new abilities by progressing the story , while relics and additional experience are hidden off the mandatory path.Once you figure out the rhythm of combat , battles can start to feel rather trivial , which is probably due to the intended target audience. The main challenge comes from the platforming sections, of which there are a lot, both mandatory and optional. When climbing a 30 story tower via moving and/or breaking platforms, this aspect can at times become a bit frustrating when one wrong step means starting all over at the bottom but with the lack of fall damage, it could easily be more frustrating than it is. That said, dying to one-shot traps in the dungeons can get  frustrating, especially when there are two recorded lines of narration for each time Galand dies and one of them  plays. In one particularly punishing section, it made me want to mute the game.One aspect where this game's difficulty feels just right is the optional speed racing challenge, in which you have to follow a predetermined path, visualized by green energy beams, as quickly as possible. Missing a single checkpoint pretty much means the run is a failed attempt here. I was pleasantly surprised with the harsh difficulty of that race as it actually managed to challenge me. I only wish there were more of them .The game's story is presented as a POV tale the protagonist tells to the titular young girl Effie. It describes how said protagonist, Galand, has been cursed with old age by a witch for being too lazy to help her and follows his quest to regain his youth. The only entities who have the power to restore Galand's youth, refuse to do so until they can be sure that he is kind of heart. They grant him a magical shield to aid him on his path and thus his journey begins.During the game, Galand - as the narrator - will comment on what the player makes Galand - as the tale's protagonist - do in a humoristic way and in third person (like Effie doesn't know it's supposed to be him). For example if the player manages to solve a puzzle on their first attempt, the narrator might say something along the lines of "Of course Galand made it on his first try. Why would I make that up?" or at other times, when the player still lacks something to progress at a point, he might instead say "At that moment, Galand couldn't do that". The delivery of lines like that feels very genuine and gives the game a nice little cherry on top.Beside the main plot the game also features a surprising amount of  that you can unlock and read by finding optional , adding some  flavor to the mix. is practically bursting with highly saturated colors and features sharp edges and thick proportions reminiscent of the  art-style or that of , which is probably going to age very well. The design of the world is very phantastical and the enemy designs are more adorable than terrifying. Despite its cuteness and colors that could have emerged from a kid's coloring book, the game also features some impressive lighting, shadows and particle effects. One thing, that is easy to miss but that I very much appreciate, is that  perfectly knows when to just hide all of the UI. So simple but so effective nonetheless.The songs featured in this game brilliantly work in tandem with the visuals, both supporting and influencing the atmosphere with tranquil and innocent but also epic and heroic tracks and, at times, even tunes that sound like something out of  or a  movie. The game cross-fades between them with the right amount of time to not make it feel like a sudden switch, at the appropriate moments. and fans of  and  are probably the main target audience and can have a plenty good time with  but  probably won't regret getting it, either. Think  with humans, orcs and witches.If you recognize yourself in the above "Target audience" section, you can't possibly go wrong with this indie gem. It feels a lot more polished and a lot less bug-ridden than what some major "AAA" developers and publishers in the industry sell for a much higher price. You're looking at 5~7 hours of fun. Potentially more for completionists.If you're looking for  levels of difficulty,  complexity and style of combat or a  like story, you're setting yourself up for disappointment, though. This game, first and foremost, is for those that fondly remember classics like  or  but don't feel like replaying them because they have aged rather obviously and poorly.

_childDocuments_.review: Effie is a standout action-adventure game inspired by classics such as Jak and Daxter, Crash Bandicoot and Ratchet and Clank. Everything from the gameplay to the bright graphics and voice-overs is sure to bring back nostalgia for fans of the genre. The variable mechanics and quirky enemies kept me entertained for my entire playtime, with the only main downfall being the inability to change the difficulty and every opponent is exceptionally easy to beat.+ Inspired by original action-adventure classics.+ Beautifully crafted environments with vibrant colour schemes.+ Melodramatic narration.+ Large variation in gameplay including puzzles, platforming, open-world exploration and combat.+ Steam achievements.+ New combat mechanics and enemies are introduced as the game progresses.+ Collectable relics to find.- Enemies are awfully effortless to defeat, including the final boss battle.- Lack of a difficulty option to boost the challenge.- Melira's voice becomes quite tedious with the repeated 'HEEYA' every single time she attacks throughout each of the chapters. Her attacks also remain the same throughout the entire game (boss battles).- Overuse of the term “It's an ambush!” or “It’s a trap!”.The game is told through a story-book fashion to a young girl, named Effie. It recounts the adventure of Galand, a boy who was cursed by a witch and subsequently lost his youth and is transformed into an old, albeit, muscular man. This fantasy adventure doesn't end there and follows Galand on his quest to overcome the nefarious witch, Melira. To achieve this, the protagonist must obtain rune of evil in each city in order to finally face her for the final battle and free the kingdom of Oblena from her wicked grasp.Effie manages to brilliantly mimic the success of the original 3D platformers and includes many features that we all know and love, including temporary platforms that shatter under players' feet, trap doors, lava, swinging saws and so much more. I did not use a control to play and I am impressed at how fluid the gameplay was, I could jump from platform to platform with ease. Effie is sure to scratch that itch for players looking to experience the classic old-school style and although the difficulty does steadily increase, it remains straightforward and enjoyable to play right to the very end.Galand is armed with his trusty magic shield and each chapter unlocks new abilities, which help to keep players engrossed. Each combat move utilises the mouse and it is in general, a very easy system, especially when Galand levels up and increases his health. However, the accumulation of these abilities makes the character  unreasonably strong and causes the game to lose all sense of challenge. I do not believe games such as these should be necessarily complex, but not having any struggles can make the game a bore. The abilities themselves are interesting and reminiscent of well-known titles and include holding RMB to create an earthquake, spinning the shield around in a circle to hit anything in Galand's radius and of course heavy and light attacks through LMB and RMB. Players have the opportunity to explore the lively world of Oblena, surf the water using your shield, increasing the speed through hitting yellow circles (Jak and Daxter, anyone?).  Not only surfing, but players can explore hidden mini towns to find secluded treasures and an excess of runestones, which are used to level up and gain experience.Each chapter is segregated into a city and shield surfing is strictly prohibited in them, represented by a candid sign simply stating, 'no surfing' and trying to rebel and surf will result in the narrator comically berating us. As shown in the screenshots, it is clear that the dynamic world of Effie is beautiful, vibrant and fun. Each chapter has its own theme with differing colour schemes and backgrounds.  The developers manage to successfully combine classic gameplay and spice it up using more updated graphics, resulting in a nostalgic PS2-like world. The over-dramatic voices for each character make the developers inspiration behind Effie crystal clear. From the narrators deep, sharp voice to Melira's evil cackle and Effie's young jejune voice. They all add together to transport players into the flippant universe and spark players' motivation to unearth Galand's heroic qualities and save Oblena from the witch’s reign.Overall, Effie was relatively bug-free, and I could play from start to finish without experiencing any major issues. Although not supposedly a glitch, when surfing, if Galand were to try and reach land and bump the side of the ramp, players will instantly drown, or teleport into the water. Not a game-breaking problem by any means, however it does become tiresome.On two separate occasions, I also noticed significant frame rate drops when exploring high-up areas [RTX 2060,i5,16GB].Yes, this is an excellent game for anyone who is a fan of the genre or any of the classics that inspired Effie's development. Effie's 6-8 hours of playtime (possibly more for those looking to complete to 100%) is teeming with whimsical cities to explore, runes to collect and foes to fight. Highly recommended for anyone looking for some nostalgia, to relax or to relive the PS2 era. This review copy was provided to the OCG-Curations curator.

_childDocuments_.review: This is again more of a neutral rating than a definite positive one. But let me get more into the details to explain.Effie is a typical Unreal 3D-platformer made by a small team, and this shows, in both good and bad ways. On the positive side you can definitely see the dedication and work that was put into the environments of some levels (like the Vineyard or Windmills City), the platforming sequences are decent, too, and the many runes to collect give some good incentive to explore. Difficulty stays in a casual to easy range, yet doesn’t get too boring. Music was quite fitting as well, not too much variation, but also alright on the whole. So I have to admit I had fun regarding those aspects all in all. I didn’t mind the sometimes a bit clunky movements, or the narration style (a voiced narrator tells the game like a story to his grandchild). But the design and technical flaws sadly always pulled my experience down in between.Probably the biggest problem are the many fights. I completely understand why they are there, they are meant to give some variety to the game, but they are doing just the opposite. The roundabout 8 types are all very predictable and easy, so most of the time you just button-mash like crazy because of their too many hit points, with only rare evasion in between. After a short time it’s getting extremely repetitive and tiresome, or even annoying, as there are those throwing-type enemies who will hit you even from the other side of a large room and through obstacles. Like I said, those fight parts happen regularly in between, sometimes as surprise attacks as waves, sometimes enemies are present in rooms from the start. There’s even an extra short arena part, and even 3 of the 5 boss fights consist only of these wave-like enemy fights. Speaking of, the boss fights all in all feel rather superfluous as well (the others are more or less platforming sequences), every time only against the same boss (the witch Melira) over and over again. I don’t know, call me crazy, but sometimes I actually think it’s better to have no boss fight at all than a tedious needless one. Which reminds me, there’s also some kind of annoying depth-of-field bug. As soon as an enemy sets eyes on you, the environment will blur for dynamic reasons and only focuses on this enemy. Problem is, this happens even if this enemy is behind you, behind a wall or building or even way off, so sometimes the whole environment turns extremely blurry for seemingly no obvious reason at all. The other big problem is the checkpoints/autosaves system. Thing is, the game saves most of the time when entering a new room, but at the same time the door behind you closes, and there’s no way to get back into the old room. Which is extremely annoying considering the game features collectables, and once you accidentally go through the wrong door, bang, no chance anymore to get this collectable (and thus various achievements). Especially critical because you can’t replay any level, so once you missed one, theoretically you’d need to start a new game. Backup saves again might help you a bit here (I’d advise that at least), but anyway, the general feeling, that you never know when this save will kick in and if you’re gonna miss something is getting on your nerves over time. Another weird save mechanics, in the small open world area these auto saves are even timed obviously, so if you collect some runes there, and die before this timed autosave happens, you’ll have to collect everything again (you can be lucky if you recall where they exactly were). Speaking of collecting again, the same applies if you accidently die in a room, like when falling in the water (instant kill), you’ll have to gather all runes again, and also all enemies respawn, which can get kind of tedious in levels where you have a lot of water.Long story short, it’s a bit sad, without those design flaws and some bugs (like stepping on a wrong switch might get you caught in a never-ending cutscene-loop) Effie would have been definitely more enjoyable in my opinion. I nevertheless give it a careful thumbs up. It wouldn’t be my first choice when you want to play a small non-famous 3D platformer (e.g. of the same type I personally liked Skylar & Plux or Ginger better), but if you already played everything else and dig indie stuff, it definitely got some of those moments you might be looking for, and can still be a solid way to kill a few hours if you don’t mind the above.----------------Update: By the way, meanwhile I quickly threw together a Steam guide with quick references for the collectables. So if you’re interested in the game, but the autosave problem bothers you, you might want to check it out. Hope that maybe you can enjoy the game more this way than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Nope, but it is a beautiful action/puzzle platformer inspired by classic 3D platformer masterpieces of the 90s.The narrator tells a young girl named Effie the story of Galand, a young man cursed by a witch and turned into an old, vertically challenged but still quite strong man, armed only with a magic shield, you have to travel through the large country of Oblena. Jump around, climb walls, solve puzzles and collect runes and other stuff in a large open world. Improve your character by finding items and by experience.Your magic shield is quite versatile, you can use it to smash monster's heads, to surf around the countryside, to hit treasure chests with it to open them, or to glide down from great heights. The land is full of minions of Melira, the evil witch that cursed you. Those minions mostly look more cute than evil, and defeating them is not too difficult, even though you can die fast during the boss fights.The graphic consists of beautifully crafted environments using vibrant colour schemes, the narrator comments regularly on the story progression. I'd highly recommend playing Effie with a gamepad.Nostalgic 3D platformer in a large world tailored towards a younger audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in 3 hours with only missing 2 hidden collectibles. You can not re enter any place after finishing it, making missing collectibles very easy to miss. There are not really bosses in this game. All bosses are either mob fights, lack luster platforming, or a combination of the 2. Story is okay, but you are unable to skip cut scenes.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid action platformer game that is short but sweet. Collecting the numerous floating items serve a useful purpose in that gathering enough of them permanently increases your maximum health/stamina. The system is much better than unlocking concept art or whatever nonsense that other collectathons sometimes do. The combat system has your standard light/heavy attack with a special attack upgrade for each one. Your weapon is a shield and it also becomes a hoverboard in the somewhat disappointing open world. There is no map so you have to just ride around and look for the main dungeons (easy to find) and other side locations (harder to find). The platforming has your standard jump/double-jump/dash controls which makes most of it fairly easy, although the later stages of the game have checkpoints that are too far apart. Worth getting for 5 bucks or less.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.8/10 ~ Effie is an adorable little game! It reminded me a LOT of Ratchet and Clank except free-roaming/open world-ish which felt great. The game design was beautiful & the concept of the story itself was lovely. I really, thoroughly enjoyed this game!However: I will say that for the price & only 5 hours, a little disappointed I was but nonetheless a good game to play and enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: 6h 4/10 1 Yes, I used  No Yes, the 18 relics are missable because you can't replay levels. No No No No No NoThis is an amazing action-platformer. It feels a lot like the platformers from the Playstation 2 era. In each level, you'll get a new ability that you need to use to progress. The first level is always the same; after that, you arrive on an overworld map. On this map, you'll find the most relics and you'll be able to unlock the most achievements. After every level, you get back to this map, so you don't have to get everything on there the first time you enter it. It will make the game a lot easier though, if you farm everything on the world map first. That is because you can find a lot of experience there, which will level you up and give you more health. You can choose the order in which to complete the next 3 levels, but I would highly suggest to go to the mills first, then the Woodborn and lastly the Vineyards. You make it a lot easier for yourself in that order, because of the skill you unlock in each of those levels. I didn't go in that order and had a hard time in some sections.If you want to play the game only once and not miss out on 2 missable achievements (one for collecting all the relics and the other for getting all achievements), I highly suggest to at least follow the guide linked above for the relics chests. There is an achievement for getting to level 6. After you get that achievement, you still can level up but there is no achievement for getting higher. Once I reached that point I stopped looking at the guide for those chests and only focused on the relics chests. If I saw an easy to reach experience chest I still would pick it up (because the higher your level, the easier the last boss fight), but didn't go out of my way anymore to get to them.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful little indie-gem with minor flaws - 8/10Really enjoyed this one, the story is pretty standard but I liked the gameplay and the graphics of the game.You play as Galand, helping him with his fate to clear the region of Oblena from evil. You jump, surf, smash enemies and solve simple puzzles. The game is relatively easy to complete so suitable for all ages.What I did not like: You can't change the options while you are playing, only in the menu, pretty annoying when the dialogue is too loud for example. Furthermore I did not like that you can't replay levels once you finished them, you always come back to the main open-world though, so you don't have to complete everything there immediately.At the end a really enjoyable platformer.100%-Achievement-Difficulty: Easy, took me ~7 hours. Keep in mind that you can't replay levels.

_childDocuments_.review: As I looked into Effie's (EF) reviews, I got the impression of a short platformer that had heart, but might lack polish and refinement. That's not the worst thing to hear about an indie title, as a soulless cash-grab almost never winds up any good. I've played several 3D platformers, but it's been a while since I've leapt around gathering shinies for whatever reason, so this sounded like a good way to get my fix sated.  Platformers are usually pretty basic, and EF fits that to a T. It'll present an obstacle, most often a locked door, you'll go down the only path available to one of the needed keys, opening a branching pathway to get the next one, and so on. There's a nice blend from the stage design between following a more linear route, going from point A to B, and having a small hub that you keep cycling back on before you finally get to the next location. Navigating these areas primarily relies on platforming and solving the occasional puzzle, but the game also has combat. Although it does make a shield into a viable weapon on its own, bashing enemies around is less the grandeur of Spartan combat and more a chore.  I think this style of game is perfectly suited for a controller, and for most of the game I had no issues with it. One downside came from the shoulder charge, because when you do it mid-air, the distance it covers is pre-set. You can adjust it while you're falling, but I inadvertently overshot a few platforms when I'd use this instead of making a committed double-jump. The combat handles alright, but you'll primarily spam light attacks because they come out faster, saving heavy attacks for enemies that can only be beaten that way. I never blocked or put up the shield, yet never even came close to dying from a fight.  EF is narrated by an older man telling a story from his own life to a young girl, who serves as the title of the game, for whatever reason. Galand was a powerful man in his prime, but didn't like going out of his way to help others, so when a witch asks for help and is scorned, she turns him into a geezer. Running to a temple for guidance, which would have been more work than just helping her, the elders tell him they can't ascertain the nature of his heart and won't help him. Then they give him a shield that only the pure-hearted can use, which would serve as a litmus test for that matter and creates a giant plot hole... but sure, they have no way to figure it out without sending him on a quest first. By the end, EF gets kind of cheesy and doesn't answer the question of what Galand's ultimate fate was.  Considering the smaller scale of this project, I think it looks pretty good. Environments don't look bland, and characters had enough range in their movement to not look robotic. Something that holds back how the characters look is their stiff facial expressions, as Galand's goofy grin didn't waver under any circumstance. However, the problem with the settings are less how they look, and more about their composition and conception. For instance, the city of overflowing wine is somewhat like Willy Wonka's chocolate factory and the chocolate waterfall, but is far less believable because it's scaled up to an entire city surrounded by a wine pond. Another example comes from Woodborn: if the wood is so sturdy that it's arguably stronger than steel swords, how would traditional sawmills process the lumber? Even small towns desperately surviving due to one industry aren't build solely around it like an amusement park. With these locations being so unfeasible, it makes the shaky narrator less credible and calls into question the truth behind any of it.  Since EF kind of has a fairy-tale vibe to it, I find the background music matched this aesthetic well. The instrumentals are well-suited for a fantasy world, though one more focused on unicorns and wonder than gruesome beasts and nightmarish fiends. Galand's voice lines were delivered pretty well, but I wasn't as impressed by how the witch performed.  🌟 I liked when the boss fights emphasized platforming more than the combat, because they were more interesting and distinct. Dodging around sawblades is more engaging than beating up a few waves of basic enemies. 🌟 Although a few checkpoints might be a bit on the long side, the difficulty of the game should be well-suited for less experienced gamers. There's no game overs to punish mistakes. 🌟 Even though I'd sometimes botch a jump and some areas could be a bit tricky, no jumps stood out for requiring absolute precision or being too finicky.  ❌ It's not clear from the stage design when an area is the way you're supposed to go or leading to a secret. Plus, some areas will drop a door behind you after you cross the threshold, forever barring you from going back the other way. I also had difficulty getting into the Vineyards. I'd start exploring the area, die instantly when I fell into the wine, and would respawn back in another town. I was so confused, I looked up a video to make sure I was going to the right place. ❌ Smaller details about environments also hurt the world-building. When moving platforms don't have a place to transition off the screen to and merely disappear, that doesn't make any sense. Also, I thought there might have been some grim meaning behind the bones mixed amongst the grapes and the goblins on their own factory line, but it had no pay off. ❌ I don't understand why the game is named after the girl. For a while, I thought it was because of a plot twist the game was building to, but that didn't pan out. She's just listening to a story; why name the game after an audience member? 🔍 The boomerang attack is overpowered. Defeating basic grunts took six hits, but getting hit once by the boomerang move would one-shot them. So it both hits multiple enemies, and also kills weaker foes with only one hit. Conversely, the Earthquake attack seemed lackluster, though it seemed to be intended for the brawnier guys. 🔍 Not only are there more than enough runes for you to level up several times throughout EF, ones scattered around the stage also respawn. If you see some stray ones you missed that's out of your way, it's not really worth the effort to get them.  Aside from how short EF is, the other main downside is that it's rather simple and easy. If it focused solely on platforming I think it'd have been better, as the combat was rather repetitive and monotonous. However, this is from the perspective of someone who started playing games like this back when Super Mario 64 first came out, so it's not surprising that it seems like baby's first platformer to me. It would also be unfair to compare the design quality of the two games against each other. I do believe genuine effort was put into EF, which makes some of the oversight in stage design and the plot hurt all the more. It could have been alright for a beginner's platformer, but with the blemishes and design flaws, I wouldn't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is all around okay, and I probably would've finished and enjoyed my time with it, however. This game has one awful design decision that stops me from enjoying the game. If you move forward in levels it will lock doors behind you, and if you complete a level you can't go back in it. This is one of those design decisions I don't understand. I see literally no benefit to doing this? If it was for combat sake you should open up the door after combat. If it was for exploration sake? Then you need to design your levels in a way where it's easier to understand where to go.

_childDocuments_.review: This game just doesn't feel right to me, like it has 5 different ideas all poorly tied together. I don't like the story at all and I still don't know why this is named Effie, maybe I forgot, but then I'd say you shouldn't have the title of your game be forgettable. The story often feels abrupt and with little originality or foreshadowing, just constantly "this is happening now". I liked what I saw of the open world area (the red plains). but I'm confused is this supposed to be an open world game, and if so why start with a very linear enclosed tutorial area, doesn't really mesh well. Also I almost immediately got trapped in the next area so I couldn't even explore the plains as much as I would have wanted to. The animations feel very.... stilted and stiff. I feel confused about the damage I take during combat, as some enemies seem to have constant damage on contact and others don't. Additionally the attacks just feel like they have a bit of input lag and just feel clunky. I would like to at least have the game explain somewhere what is the blue energy stuff, or that the shield has a light and heavy 3 hit combo or why does the blue stuff heal me/ give me xp? also what happens when I level up, I have a lot of questions. The level design is sloppy in some places, as I got into an area that had jars to break but I was then stuck and had to kill myself. The shield surfing is fun for about 3 minutes and then just feels like a means to getting around as you can speed up, brake and jump (like 1/5 the character height) and that is it. Except in places where there is a sign saying no surfing. I forgot to mention, you can only have 1 save file, trying to start a new game will overwrite that file.The game just feels clunky, abrupt and arbitrary.

_childDocuments_.review: Very empty. Movement on point, surfing is relaxing, and the platforming is solid though. You get abilities as you play  but their is a leveling system with no foreseeable purpose beyond getting more attack power. It is a solid $5 game whenever it gets down to that price. Once you beat the town area you are barred from entering because there are "people" you never see that returned so its the worst part actually and points toward the empty feeling. I gave up after 1.5hrs.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming little game, but this is the reason I always look up missable items in games because you can easily get locked out of achievements (and more importantly some lore, which while meager is still interesting) and have to start from the beginning of the game if you miss getting a relic on your one and only pass through of each main dungeon.The game is extremely short, but colorful and whimsical and you can tell it came from the heart. Also I liked that the kid said things that don't really make sense sometimes and tried to jump ahead in the story, because that is what ACTUAL kids do all the time. I found that particularly endearing.It's pretty bare bones as far as gameplay goes, but it has a lot of good ideas. I just don't think that they took it quite far enough to make it a really good game. All in all a decent platformer with a very simple story. A good way to relax and get away from the stress of more demanding titles and to get away from the things going on in the world right now.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is quite fun with the standard "fight the boss" elements which require platforming and figuring out the "pattern" of the boss.  I especially enjoyed being able to surf around on my shield and explore the main map and find items that increase your strength.  Each level was of appropriate length and wasn't too difficult. But there is a bug which does not let you go back and try the race again after you exit without finishing. You have to play from the start again to get that achievement and the relic that comes with it to get the "all trophies" achievement.  Since I was especially bad at the racing part, I don't really want to play the whole game over again just to get those three achievements.I would recommend it even though there are some flaws.  But definitely wait for a good sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get into the review itself, I'd like to mention that I received a copy of the game for free by the developer for review purposes. I also played the game via mouse & keyboard and had no problems at all - the game itself recommends you the usage of a controller but as I just said, playing it with a normal mouse & keyboard combination was totally fine.The story can be summarized and understood fairly quick. It is about a strong, young man named Galand who was cursed by a witch and lost his youth since he was turned into an old man. He then proceeded to visit the "Temple of the elder protectors" since he was told that the Elder Protectors were able to restore his youth. Once he spoke to the Elder Protectors, he was told that Melira the witch (which also happened to be the witch that cursed him) tries to bring darkness over the kingdom of Oblena and Geland had to proof that he has a kind heart by defeating her and destroying the so called "Gems of Evil" to stop her and rescue the kingdom of Oblena. Only then, the Elder Protectors would restore his youth.Before Galand heads out for his journey, the Elder Protectors also provide him a shield named Runestone that guides him on his adventure and assists him in various ways such as combat and parkour. The game itself is a 3D platformer that consists of harder getting jump and run's, tricky riddles and secrets to solve and occasional combats and (mini) boss fights. Once in a while, the player gets introduced to a new mechanic such as a new dash which he then can use to his advantage in further jump and run parts of the games or fights with stronger getting hordes of enemies. During the players adventures, he also has the option to collect as many rune stones as possible (by finding hidden chests, collecting them from the ground or simply beating enemies) to get a level up once he collected enough. Level ups increase the players strengh and these hidden rune stones in several spots give the player an incentive to try out different paths and look for hidden places. In my case they also rewarded fancy/experimental movement attempts on places that looked like I might reach them to reveal some secret loot.Between the chapters, the game also offers you an open world type of area where you can travel fast by surfing on your shield and head to the next location to continue with the story or battle a bunch of enemies, explore some extra buildings and collect even more rune stones.Here is a little screenshot of me traveling with that surf shield by the way. There are also a bunch of speed boosts available on the area while surfing so you can gain a lot of speed, use some ramps, crash into enemies and just have some fun between the levels. The overall atmosphere of the game is quite nice. The kingdom of Oblena looks pretty and all the levels got some lovely details too. Steady loot and respawning enemies make the most areas also look quite active so there are no dead / boring parts of a level. The game often has multiple places to explore and it makes the player think twice before he choses a direction instead of directly giving him a waypoint / goal to pursue. Additionally the game also has some cool voice acting and neat soundtracks so the overall atmosphere of the game is well-made!- Nice platformer with harder getting challenges that require jump and run skills and riddle solving- Rewards exploration with hidden extra loot- Good balance between levels with certain objectives to achieve and free open world explore time - Occasional boss fights that are quite fun and challenge you to make use of every mechanic the player knows if you want to master the combat (admittedly in the early stages of the game you can simply win by button smashing but the battles get harder over time and you need to put more and more effort into them as you advance)- Narration over the course of the story by a nice voice actor- Steam achievements and full controller support!- No game breaking bugs- 19.99€ on Steam is a bit expensive in my opinion, I could rather see this game at 9.99€-14.99€ but if you are looking for a nice 3D platformer to pick up and truly love this genre then this purchase is always justified of course!- Some over-used voice lines when Galand opens a chest (there are a bunch of loot chests in every level and considering that the narrator always says one out of two voice lines when opening one, it gets quite repetitive over time)- Combat with enemies seems a little bit too easy in some casesOverall I had a good time playing this game and didn't encounter any frustrating issues at all. I could see myself playing this game again in future to finish all the levels since I can already tell that the game still has some nice challenges waiting for me.The biggest downside is probably the 19.99€ price tag but admittedly this one is not a big issue either. If a game is genuinely fun and some content gets added once in a while, it's still alright 7/10 - Definitely a nice game with appealing visuals, a good atmosphere and some challenging levels to spend a good weekend on completing the game! If you are a game developer and would like to get your game reviewed, feel free to email contact@dnbmedia.co

_childDocuments_.review: short, enjoyable 3D indie platformer with nice visuals (low polygon count + simple texturing + fancy UE4 lighting is a combination more games should use) and solid level design. worth playing for 3D platforming fans even if it requires putting up with a fair bit of jank attributable to its low budget and small team (some questionable checkpoints, a few unclear level objectives, English voice acting that doesn't match the subtitles, etc).not to be confused with Elli, a similarly named but entirely different indie 3D platformer with a somewhat similar art style that came out a bit later in 2020. I liked this one better, though
_childDocuments_.name: Effie

_childDocuments_.review: Short plot recap. Once upon a time, there was a man, a lazy one. One day a random lady appeared before him, asking him for help. He refused. That lady turned into a witch, a powerful one… And turned him into an old man. Now he have to regain his youth – and save the world in process.Now to the point. Yes, this game is kind of short (it took me ~9 hours to fully complete it), yes it’s kind of simple, yes it plays as it was designed for younger players. All correct. Why positive then? Because this is the main point of the whole game! You have to appreciate little things in life – or you will just lose your time between days gone… Not everything on this world must be super hardcore to be fun, and not everything must be complicated to make you stick with it to the end. This game is not perfect (there are some glitches), can make you angry sometimes (there are one hit kill traps) – but it’s beautiful, both outside and inside! Give it a try – but only when you (and I mean – you) are ready to follow Galand on his quest ;) And maybe – just maybe – you will find your own answers? I totally give this one a thumbs up!
_childDocuments_.name: Effie

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, worse than this game being bad, this game is just an absolute nothing sandwich. It just has no real personality or depth to that I don't really care. The world is bland, the characters are completely flat, the story feels like a placeholder plot that they forgot to replace.The character controls are clunky as hell. How are you going to make a modern platformer and not give your character the ability to run? Your character moves like they are training for Olympic Racewalking rather than an adventure to save the world.The world itself is empty and desolate. The decision to make the world such an aggressive shade of blood red that will make your eyes hurt if you stare at it long enough just further makes the world seem lazily thrown together and bland. The hoverboard is actually a pretty fun way to traverse the world, but it unfortunately just ends up shining a light on how empty the world is. I would love to see it implemented in a better game.Overall, I just can't recommend this game to anyone. I can't get my four hours back, but maybe I can stop you from wasting yours.
_childDocuments_.name: Effie

_childDocuments_.review: Effie is an Action Platformer set in a story told by the protagonist to a young child by a fireplace. This young child's name is Effie. That is the only relevance the title has to the game itself. Take that as you will.The game is split into 5 unique levels, each with an interesting theme and unique mechanics. The levels are set within a hub world in which you get to surf around on your shieldboard and go really fast. The hub world has its own collectables, and there are even a few interesting locales with side objectives if you want to go collectable hunting, I recommend doing at least that much to break the monotony of going between levels, because the game doesn't give you much else in the hub world.Combat is basic, but there is a form of progression in levelling up your power, which increases both your health and mana to allow you to do more stuff with your shield.It's a quick game. It's a simple game. There's really not much else to say. Give it to your kids as an introduction to action platforming.
_childDocuments_.name: Effie

_childDocuments_.review: Effie is easily one of the better 3D platformers that I’ve played in recent memory. A solid mix of platforming, combat, and puzzles make this one a winner in my book.IntroEffie is a somewhat open-world action-adventure game with 3D platforming elements. The game is heavily inspired by classic 3D platformers and I’ll even admit that it made me quite nostalgic for some of my favorites of yore. If you’re a fan of 3D platformers like myself, do read on because this one’s quite fun.Story and CharactersAmazingly, Effie manages to tell a pretty competent fairytale-like story with only 3 actual characters. The main character that you play as is named Galand who was cursed with old age by the evil witch Melira. In order to restore his youth, he takes on a quest to rid the world of evil by ultimately defeating the witch. Equally amazing is the fact that there are only 2 voice actors in the entire game, One for Galand (Who also acts as narrator to the story) and one for Effie and Melira. Outside of these 3 characters, the world is largely inhabited by Melira’s evil minions and all of the humans have disappeared, or so I assume because there is no-one else. It does raise a lot of questions about what happened to everyone but I mostly just assumed the monsters killed everyone, easiest explanation.The story can be completed in a little over 4 hours but there are quite a few side areas that you can visit as well. Something I wish I knew because I missed out on because I assumed after the 3 major towns you go to fight Malira. Still, the game can take upwards of around 7-8 hours if you visit every location across the world. The side areas are easy to miss though, which is why I wound up missing them on accident.Platforming!Platforming plays a major role in Effie as it’s largely how you progress through each level. One thing I will gladly praise about this game is its excellent level design. It’s incredibly well crafted and each one reminded me of the classics in how everything was setup. The levels start quite simple with rudimentary puzzles to solve and easy platforming but with each one, the difficulty increases with the final boss including literally everything that you learned up to that point. The final boss tests your abilities and I wound up dying a few times myself, but I beat her in the end. Thankfully during the final boss, it autosaves with each phase so you don’t have to start the entire thing over again, which takes some of the brutality away but don’t expect it to be easy for most players.CombatEffie also has some combat elements which have Galand utilizing a shield (Or Runestone, as it’s called in the game) much like Captain America. In the early portions of the game, Galand’s attack range is fairly limited but as you progress through the major cities, you’ll unlock new abilities. These abilities include Dash, Earthquake, and Boomerang. Earthquake and Boomerang are AoE (Area of Attack) skills that can defeat multiple enemies in one hit, so they’re very handy. Dash is used in both combat (To avoid enemy attacks) and platforming (to reach faraway platforms) and it’s pretty easy to master its use, just don’t get too trigger happy with it during platforming and you’ll be fine.There aren’t very many things that I didn’t like about this game, and what I did was incredibly minor. One of them had to do with combat. Your regular attacks could be a bit.. inaccurate when facing multiple enemies and I felt a lock-on ability would help matters. Later in the game, your regular and heavy attacks are made outdated by the AoE attacks but it’s kinda repetitive spamming just 2 attacks so I mixed up the combat with some regular attacks too. Made things more entertaining.VerdictOverall, I enjoyed Effie a great deal and felt that it was one of the better 3D platformers that I’ve played in some time. Gameplay-wise it’s perfect with its balance of puzzles and platforming, combat could feel a little clunky at times but it wasn’t awful and wound up being fairly fun, and it’s quite gorgeous to look at to boot. So, as far as 3D platformers go, I’d have to say this one is quite solid, so I’ll be giving it a Save. Very fun game and I enjoyed my time with it a great deal.

_childDocuments_.review: Effie is a short adventure story about a hero called Galand who was cursed with old age. To try and reverse his aging, he was tasked by the Elder Protectors to defeat the evil witch, who coincidentally, had also cursed him.The gameplay itself is fairly simple, with only a light attack and heavy attack with their own combos, along with some special moves you unlock in each of the 3 main levels. There are a good variety of enemies, but there is only one boss to battle, and unfortunately mostly ends up fighting becoming an arena fight with an annoying AOE from the boss every 3 seconds or so.There is a hub area to explore with relic chests scattered across it, which Galand can surf across on his shield, which was very fun. There are 3 levels where most of the platforming takes place, and imo the best was the Vineyards, which had some cool sections going through big barrels and exploring rooms.While there are many runes, boxes and chests scattered around, the main reason to collect them is to level up Galand's health and magic pools, but are otherwise completely unremarkable as the only tracked collectable are the relic chests. These provide some backstory on the world and each location which is nice.Pros:+ The surfing mechanic is pretty cool+ The Vineyard level is great fun+ No bugs (that I encountered at least)+ Music is quite good, and the art is also nice tooCons:- Narrator can become grating when opening chests- Story is very basic- Animations are a bit too simplistic- not much reason to collect runes except for achievements and for health for the final boss- combat could be fleshed out further with jumping attacks or other combos- Boss battles are very predictableOverall Score:6/10TL;DR: Effie is a short and simple adventure game, which can be good to pass an afternoon away or for kids to play

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hidden gem! I didn't expect much when I launched the game, but it blew me away. Yes, there is a few graphic glitches where you poke through a wall and yes, the camera angle goes a bit wonky sometimes, but this is very rare and not really disturbing enough to hold your attention for more than a sec or two. I've seen much way worse with "popular" games that cost a bunch more than this one.The surf feature is amazing and controls are on point! I had a blast surfing over the extremely pretty red landscape while searching for treasures. The game itself is super easy and I would even say kid-friendly. Its a casual, but very entertaining little game with straight forward puzzles. The combat system isn't outstanding, but I think it fits the game very well and you learn to control it a bit more throughout the game. My biggest complaint is the length of the game - I want more!This was so good, that I finished it 100% with all achievements in one sitting.

_childDocuments_.review: Platforming perfection collect-a-thon, with some slightly nagging issues.If you enjoy excellent 3d platforming- buy this game. It's superbly well done. Even the boss fights are fun to because it's more of the great platforming going on there too.The music is nice, game controls fantastic and no bugs, glitches or crashes. The graphics, while kinda simplistic, are bright, sharp and colorful. You can upgrade your health by collecting the things scattered around everwhere and defeating monsters which is cool. Theres quite a few collectibles to find in the main world map that you can get anytime and encourages exploration. Surfing around the world in your shield is fast, fluid and fun- there's also a mini game you can tackle as well which was probably the most challenging part of the game too. The game length also doesn't overstay its welcome, at around 4-7 hours depending on if you do some exploring or just stick with the main story.However, there's some bad points, and man....if they just adjusted them this game would be top tier to me. The biggest gripe I have with the game is that once you clear an area, you're locked out afterwards, so no going back to get any collectibles. Second, while the game world is fairly small, there's no map to pull up besides a giant stone map in the ground, (no mini map either). If you don't remember (or know) where it is chances are you may not even realize it's there, (however, I need to say this- the main places you need to go are usually pretty large structures that you can see from far away, so that does help). Third, the story setup is, well...stupid. Like really stupid. However the ending was really good and made sense though so I'll give it that. Finally, it's kinda easy. There's only one difficulty and it seems it's geared toward young gamers so it may put off some people, but it didn't bother me at all.So if you can get past all that and enjoy some well crafted platforming action do yourself a favor and buy this game, I highly recommend it because this game is what Yooka Laylee SHOULD have been.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game does have its flaws (combat feels very limited, only a small handful of enemy types that never change after the first hour of the game, a bit barren of an overworld for how big it is, and most especially the collectathon elements pushed into a game that really doesn't feel like it should have them considering any lack of backtracking in the main levels)...Well, for what the game actually is, I did find it pretty enjoyable. Especially like how diverse and unique the locations are - a castle built of windmills, a haunted logging mill city, a massive distillery - and the platforming, while not super diverse, generally felt satisfying. The game isn't very long, not very challenging either - only ever died due to instadeath traps and death is usually not very punishing either - and the hoverboard feels a bit underused compared to how big of a selling point it is - it's only for traversing the overworld, which is only as big as it is because you can hoverboard around it, really - but I dunno, I liked the scale of the world, the way the entire game world exists in one space, with big levels inside an even bigger overworld in real space, and there definitely is something thrilling about blasting through the overworld at top speed too. It's definitely a bit lacking in polish, the plot is very minimal, and it's not going to offer much of a challenge, but it was fun and charming for what it was regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: Automatically-closing door simulator 2020.This indie game is competantly made and relatively fun, but it could have been better. My biggest annoyance is that doors shut behind you even when it makes no sense. So many times I've noticed an alternate path that might have a secret, and been blocked from exploring it, because of the stupid doors. I actually finally ragequit because of this to write this review.Outside that... the 'overworld' section with the surfing is visually quite cool, but it's very sparse, and I'm not sure how much it adds to the game (besides surfing being cool, there's no need for fast transit if they got rid of the overworld, which only has a handful of non-dungeon locations)And... prepare to hear "Ambush! It was time for Galand to fight again" over and over again.The other thing that bugs me is that falling into liquid = death, not just respawn at the start and take damage. If you're going to have a wine-themed level with pools everywhere, missing a jump should mean redoing the jumping section, not having to fight enemies and collect XP again.It may sound like I don't like the game. It's moderately fun, if a bit easy. But there's a number of rough edges that feel like they could be improved by a patch or two.

I only found one time-trial.The combat is OK, a lot of button mashing. There's a block, but you don't need it. The only challenge was the final boss, and even then, it only took a couple tries. I didn't expect a challenging game, but wow, I feel like I breezed through. Since you can go to the levels in any order, they all must be equally hard. Also, exploring rewards you with experience, which makes the game even less demanding.Overall, Effie is fun, and I enjoyed it all the way through. Part of the fun is "supposed" to be exploring, but if you know you might miss something you need, then you have to follow directions to the letter. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for June 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before July 6th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Effie is a strange game.  The first twenty minutes is a rather boring 3d platforming game.  Then the player gets a shield and uses that to beat enemies for another twenty minutes.  Then there’s a large open world segment in the game, without a firm direction given to where the player should go.  It’s like Effie didn’t focus on one style of game. The problem is Effie struggles to be interesting in anything but the open-world segments, and even there, it’s only a short part of the adventure. There’s a ton of runestones that just feel like a collect-athon.  But those go to a leveling system that didn’t feel necessary. There’s nothing wrong with Effie, but it’s just average, even with all these systems and styles.  The puzzles are a bit too easy, the combat is simple, and even when the game is good, it’s merely good.  It doesn’t even have an interesting concept on its own, nor does any of its ideas or style stick around long enough for players to even appreciate them. Pick this up if you want a very average game.  Effie isn’t bad, but it’s also not good enough to recommend and that’s probably the biggest issue.  I could imagine someone playing through the entire game because there’s nothing that harms the experience, but I also see players will likely put it down for dinner or bed and move on to something else because there’s not a strong reason to return. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay of Effie is a bit lackluster. It's a decently produced 3D platformer with a decent narrative, and it sure looks the part. Sadly, I abandoned my campaign as I finished the second chapter. First off, the game was not challenging in the least. I died a few times falling off a platform, but the hardest thing I had to deal with was pathfinding. Enemies are your typical zombie orcs, they attack you without a purpose, and killing them off is ridiculously easy; button mash long enough, and you're good. If any of them is anywhere near you, even behind walls, get ready for minutes' worth of their grunts, which sound unpleasantly like belching. I'd sometimes get out of my way just to find and kill them to get rid of the noise. The collectibles and treasures you keep collecting aren't very exciting either; they're your typical busywork. I persevered for 2 hours, but despite its artistic charm and clever narration, I just couldn't get into it.  Considering its gratuitous violence, there's no way I would recommend this for children; the only demographic I could recommend this to are adulst with a high attraction to fairy tales, and who like simple platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: Story: Honestly I found the story to be trite, and unintentionally (at least I hope it was unintentional) misogynistic. There was no way to target any of the enemies, so you find yourself just flailing around trying to hit things - but the 'good' news is that the combat is so bland that it really doesn't matter.Content: Well apart from the main quest (and skills from there), there are all these runs/chests that you can find that will eventually increase your level - however the combat is so tame that I never felt that it made any difference what level I was. The relics seemed to be completely useless and I found that after a while I didn't even try to get all the runes. There just wasn't any reason to really explore the bland, bland world other than to go through the storyline (which frankly isn't worth it).Level design: The levels were somewhat interesting and appropriately themed. None of it was difficult, but there were a few moments where I almost felt like I was having fun. Verdict: Hard Pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Effie is an adventure game evocative of older games like Crash Bandicoot and Spyro. The main focus is on platforming that starts out simple and gets more complicated as you progress through the levels/dungeons. On your way through this charming little story you will roam the open plains on your shield-surfboard, complete dungeons and acquire new traversal and combat moves. While the platforming is fine, you shouldn't expect much of a challenge. Combat is a button-mashing affair, with very little depth to it. However using special moves does make it more satisfying. You will also need to solve some simple puzzles. All in all, if you just want a short and sweet fantasy adventure story with gorgeous visuals and fun (if simple) gameplay, then I highly recommend Effie.
