_childDocuments_.review: Effie is a short little puzzle platform adventure where you play as Galand, an adventurer who has been cursed by the evil witch Melira and needs to retake the cities crystal and stop the forces of darkness to regain his stolen youth. Being granted a magic shield, you will literally be bashing your foes and unlocking new shield skills as you progress through the game.About 5-6 hours long, you will find yourself exploring and surfing the Red Plains of Oblena, but while it may seem like a large area, you are gated by the towers and invisible walls that keep you inside the game zone. Although quite vast and empty there are small activities scattered within the plains where you may find experience chests and Relics that grant you lore bits and insight on the world you are playing in. Without mentioning the tutorial dungeon and final area, there are three main cities you need to retake and is the meat of Effie; each city granting you a new Runestone Skill as well as unique puzzles and platforming challenges.Effie narrates that Galand enjoy his adventure, and that is exactly what i did. Not a grand epic, but just a slice of fantasy pie. I do feel, however, the full price may be a little steep for such a short experience.

_childDocuments_.review: What could be a decent game dragged down by several poor design decisions. The biggest issue is the open world area, the Red Plains. It is huge and barren. Navigating it is a pain due to infrequent landmarks, no real differentiation in areas, and no map. And 12 of the I believe 18 relics in the game are there. Add on to that the fact that surfing feels... not great. The game would be much, much better if the open world were removed entirely, with the relics moved to some of the side challenges in the main areas.There's also the fact that combat is pretty mediocre. There's very limited enemy variety, and once you have a few level ups, you have more than enough health to just tank your way through damage and button mash.The platforming is fairly fun, but not terribly rewarding. You occasionally get a relic, but mostly you'll just find experience chests, and honestly, they give very little experience and leveling just feels really unnecessary after about 3 level ups.I just can't recommend it as is. If they cut out the open world area, maybe added one or two main zones to compensate, and focused more on the platforming challenges, this would be an alright, albeit not great, game. But the awful open world, the mediocre combat, and the somewhat unrewarding exploration just make the game not worth the cost or your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start off with some context. Inverge Studios, the developers of Effie, are a team of 13 (plus a dog), headquartered in Spain. Effie happens to be Inverge's first release, and I sincerely hope they learned a lot from it. While I wouldn't recommend this game to others, I would recommend keeping an eye on Inverge's future plans, as I believe their team is quite talented, not to mention passionate.Now for the actual review. I went into this game honestly hoping to enjoy it. The fantasy setting, the cartoon-ish art-style, and the soundtrack were more than enough reasons for me to try it out. I'm the type of person who adores the tried and tested medieval fantasy genre, as well as platforming, which Effie relies on quite a bit. I don't, however, have much love for beat-em-up combat and needless exposition. The game's main story, which took me roughly three hours to complete, felt more like a tutorial or tech demo than a full game. It showed me that, while this game has excellent potential, it was subject to feature creep from a very early stage. This was apparent to me from the moment I launched the game, with SteamVR opening up in the background. While virtual reality might make for a good selling point to some, I've found that its use is situational with the current technology, and the developers' time would have been better spent on smoothing out animations and transitions to make the game feel better to play. The feature creep didn't stop there, though, and upon reaching the overworld and learning the shield surfing mechanic, I found myself passing by a racing minigame. I'll admit, at the time of writing this review, I've yet to test my mettle in a race. My main reason for skipping past it was fuelled by a desire to simply finish this game and move on to something which could keep me more engaged. All in all, I didn't hate Effie, but the developers obviously didn't have much of an idea of what this game would be when they started it, instead letting the features of their game engine of choice decide for them.Pros: - Beautiful art direction - Good soundtrack - Plenty of graphical settingsCons: - Overly repetitive gameplay loop - Little to no replayability - Poor English translation - Lack of consistent vision/feature planningWhile I didn't receive this game for free, it was a part of a game bundle, so I believe I got it at a discounted price.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Can not recommend a generic game that feels like a kids first adventure game. Nothing here is unique or entertaining. Play one of the games Effie is inspired by, but don't play Effie.It's just another generic 3D Platformer with weird combat. Somehow the movement during the combat never looks fluent, which makes it feel unpolished. I ended somewhere in chapter 2 because it felt so generic and bland. Because there is no hint or quest system, you will have to listen to the cutscences to know where you have to go. Only problem: The cutscences are so boring, that you might fall asleep and miss any info on what to do anyway.The visuals look bland and boring, nothing really sticks with you while playing it. _childDocuments_.review: A marginal thumbs up for this short 3D platformer.The good:Controls and responsiveness are good enough to get the job done in combat. Worked well with my controller.The puzzles and platforming aren't too frustrating. And there are a couple of optional secrets to keep completionists busy.It's 7 hours and that's exactly how long it should be.It's obviously a labor of indie developer love.The meh:The character designs, voice acting, story and cut screens are derpy and amateurish.The final boss was a bit of a difficulty spike. I actually enjoyed the challenge (it took about 40 minutes), but some might find it frustrating when compared to the rest of this comparatively laid back game.The bad:Once you get to the overworld map, which is overly large, I felt a bit at a loss about where to go.  In fact, it was this lack of guidance that led me to take a break from the game for several months.  After checking a YouTube walkthrough, I found which places needed to be on my "hit list", but some hints would have gone a long way towards making this more fun.Verdict:This is a nice bit of nostalgia if you're pining for the Super Mario 64 era. But wait till it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I really couldn't recommend Effie. The world seems mostly empty and uninspired, the writing is... bad. Go here, collect McGuffin, kill witch levels bad. The boss fights are uninspiring and repetitive, at least from what I've played, and the combat is worse. The combat is just mash light/heavy until all enemies are dead, but I guess you can throw in one other, objectively inferior bonus move if you feel like it. The surfing mechanic shown in trailers was the main draw for me, but it's disabled everywhere except the overworld, which is empty save for sparse time trials and small unrewarding outposts. _childDocuments_.review: Recommended, but only on a heavily reduced sale because the current price point is not the right amount for what you get in this game. 5.6 hours to get 100% achievements, though its probably closer to 4.5 hours as I left the game on pause for a while.This is a 3D platformer collectathon that has great style but not a lot of substance. On style it has a sprawling hub world, a prologue dungeon, three reasonably large dungeons that look great, and a final boss arena. The music is excellent, and there is some good humour in the cut scenes.Gameplay is very basic and not challenging at all. Light attack, heavy attack, double jump, dash, and a couple of powers. The only unique aspect is traversing the hub by riding on your shield (just a glorified vehicle to be honest). Hardly any enemies types, they either swarm you or lob rock projectiles from a distance, though there are a couple of heavy bosses that have charge attacks and spawn minions that you will come across on occasion. Boss battles are just platforming and enemy wave challenges. Platforming is about using your double jump and dash to get to each platform, not much precision required, though you do have to get used to an ineffective double jump. Collectables are all over the place and aside from the relics they arent tracked, only give you XP (same as smashing boxes, killing enemies and opening chests), so they lose their value very quickly.The game is well made but it is quite limited in its scope and there is not much too it. I definitely had fun, it doesnt outstay its welcome which is nice, but i have no desire to play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent 3D platformer.The visuals are fine, with the typical Unreal Engine vibe.The music and sound are good. The plot is average.Why is this called "Effie"? I didn't understand! They should've come up with a better title.The controller is highly recommended for playing this.Platforming may feel clunky during some sections. Combat is very simplistic. Skill upgrades are not that useful, particularly the last one. I didn't use it that much.Boss battles are a series of platforming sections mixed with regular enemy combat. Not that challenging.It consists of four areas and a final boss battle. Of which one area is available for free roaming. Surf all you want in the same looking red area.There are several collectibles called relics in each area. Make sure to collect the relics from the 3 main cities; otherwise, you will have to play this game from the beginning since you can't backtrack to these areas. The same applies to the free roaming area before entering the final section.Overall, it is a casual game with which you may get 5 to 7 hours of decent fun.Just make sure to complete all of the achievements in a single run (reading the guide is recommended to locate collectibles).Get this at a discount or when it's available in any bundle in the future.My verdict: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's very rare for me to dislike a game, but Effie really was a bad experience. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Take old reviews (mid-2020 or before) with a few grains of salt. Most of the issues complained about in those older reviews  and are no longer an issue. I read those reviews between two sessions of play in Effie. Compared to most of  those early reviews, it's now a different game. It's been balanced; the weapons seem nerfed or enemy damage buffed where necessary. People complained about things that were part of the game that aren't anymore. People also complained about things weren't in the game that have been added since. Effie seems to me to be a better experience than what those old reviews describe.Are 3D platformers hard for you? If so, this one might give you a challenge. Do you enjoy 3D platformers or think they're easy? Eagerly anticipate dancing around a lot and having fun in Effie in many places, if so.Pros: Good (as opposed to bad) music. It's better than it would be if it were bad, anyway. Skilled 3D platforming ability required to beat everything the first time. Easy enough that you'll think, "Sure, why not? I'll give it another go," five times in a row because you keep missing one jump's angle or failing to get an item you want from a rotating platform when obstacles are present.Either way, you probably won't feel challenged most of the time.Cons: When playing with a gamepad, the camera doesn't auto-center. There's a button for that, but still. . . The puzzles seem tedious and/or repetitive at times; I sometimes feel like I'm doing the same things to find the key(s) needed for the next door or the next item required for progression, even when the on-screen action and in-game environment can be widely varied.IS IT A WORTHWHILE GAME? Yes, but it might not grip you for as many consecutive hours in a session as some other games you've played. I got it via Humble Choice (as it's now known), and (IMO) it's a much better use of time than some of the games I've gotten from either there or elsewhere. That said, some games have very satisfying but very short play sessions. It's all about the type of game and I probably shouldn't compare Effie to those (e.g. many retro arcade games, which were designed to be addictive and yet fast because they were also designed to make money for the arcade's owner).CONCLUSION:  It is what it is (and it's not what it's not!), just like every other game is and probably will be. I doubt I'll play it much after finishing, but I would like to finish it, unlike MANY other games I've played.Edit: When I'll get around to finishing Effie I do not know. My desire has waned somewhat since writing this review.

_childDocuments_.review: I had really fun playing through this game. The puzzles didn't bring a huge challenge to complete and at some instances the puzzles felt more like a task to do, like the answer was staring me in the face as soon as I looked at it and had a quick look around the environment I was in.Having that said, I am still going to recommend it because the things I felt the game did well it did REALLY well and it overshadows the less good parts about the game. It's a cozy casual game so if you're looking for that I can totally recommend it... if you're looking for more of a challenge I can not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: 👍 I don't want to write a review for this game, but I do want to give this game a thumbs up to help the games ratings because I think this game is good for new players 👍I'll be upfront. I didn't like this game. But that's because I don't think this game was made for me.Effie is a game made for people who don't play a lot of games, and for people who are new to gaming in-general.A lot of content in this game I found to be serviceable at best, and undercooked at worst.Effie definitely has some sections sprinkled through the game that definitely elevate it and give the game some flavor and great design for when the game is getting a bit numbingly bland.I personally feel like Effie would've been better cut out a bit more of the combat, and focused more on interesting collectables and platforming. Because the action moves you pick up actually do lend more to interesting and fun navigation and movement than actual combat.I looked online to watch some gameplay and it truly is a shame for me that I can't bring myself to bring myself through the monotony to enjoy some of the fun platforming and combat sequences this game has to offer (especially in boss fights.)But I do recognize that my issues with the game stem mainly from someone who has been an active gamer ever since I was a child. And has poured thousands upon thousands of hours into this hobby. And thousands of dollars into buying new games and getting a wide taste of things under the sun.If you are someone who is new to gaming, or is someone who doesn't play all that many games. I think Effie is a solid game for you to pick up. A variety of issues carried within probably will not affect you at all or bother you all that much as they did for me.I think this game could've done with some more bug-testing as there is a couple gamebreaking bugs I encountered. And there really should've been some more attention to showing the player where they need to go and stream-lining of content. As the game can get pretty busy with its openness where you can find yourself going down 2 sidepaths before going down the main path. Or going down a main path thinking it's a side path. It's a little messy.Anyways. While it's unfortunate it's not for me, I definitely appreciate this games existence and I think games like this are necessary for new-comers to gaming, and for those who don't play many games or don't have the time to play many games but still want a good, fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the simplicity of the game. The puzzles are pretty easy and the combat is very easy. It is a nice casual game to sit back and play for a bit. My main complaint with this game is that, to my knowledge, there is no way to keep track of what you have really done. I played for a couple days and got about halfway through the game, then I took a 2 month break and when I returned I could not remember anything I was doing. There is no map to show what you have completed or where you need to go, there is no journal to tell you what you have done or where you need to go. I spent an hour zooming around the expansive open world of red grass trying to figure out what I was supposed to do next, but it was a fruitless effort and I have given up. _childDocuments_.review: Effie is a short game meant to feel how you REMEMBER old-school collectathons feeling. Graphics to hint at the old style while polishing off the corners your child brain and fuzzy TV ignored. Shorter levels so you get it done in a couple sittings, just like you did when your gaming sessions could be half a day instead of an hour or two. There are a few types of actual recorded collectable "relics" in white chests (and a little tracker on the menu with their level), but most of the collectable "runestones" just go to your XP bar. Something that is slightly filled by smashing boxes, just so slightly enough that you don't see it rise but substantial enough to easily make up for a few missed runestones. All narrated as a grandfather telling a story of a lazy knight to his granddaughter Effie.It's not perfect, it has an DK64 style basic beat-em-up combat system that you earn more moves for as you play, if that's not for you that's valid. The game is also around 4-5 hours long, so pretty short, though I'd argue it's to keep it from overstaying its welcome and letting all the old flaws with the style show. But if you're looking to give your kid a taste of what gaming was like back in the day, or just looking for a serviceable hit of nostalgia, it's a good game to pick up from a sale or bundle. For someone who grew up playing her dad's old N64, it was definitely a pleasant 7 out of 10.Edit: to refute some other reviews- To exit the tutorial you have to assemble a glowing map of the levels. Even if you forget that, there is a large road going from level to level. and even if you can't work out that the road with arrows and signs is going the right way, there's only 4 major things on the horizon. If you can't figure out where to go, the game's not at fault. and the "surfing system" is a sprint button. it's am overworld-only sprint button. It's not a main part of the game, it's fast travel with a few optional races. If you don't like it you can be at the next level and done with it in seconds.

I am happy with the purchase and thing others will be as well, and since the game is short but not too short, I am satisfied and able to move on to the next in my library with no regrets.I would enjoy it if the Colosseum and Quick Imp areas were expanded, or made to be replayable though!Actually, I'd enjoy if all areas could be replayed. _childDocuments_.name: Effie

_childDocuments_.review: Effie is a fine 3D platformer with a colorful and bright visual style combined with an easy to understand combat system.  It was a joy going around the game's world collecting runes and gaining new abilities.  Aside from some minor platforming control issues, there was very little to be upset about here.  Can be completed in a single sitting, but there are tons of secrets to unlock, including relics, books, and more.  Was never too challenging, which made the game very therapeutic in a world where most developers are attempting to crush a player's spirit through high difficulty ceilings.  And the sound design was just top notch, although the voice acting for Effie seemed a little forced.  The end credits theme is perhaps one of the best tracks I've heard in quite some time.  Effie is most definitely worth a look to anyone in need of a simple but beautifully realized 3D platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: Effie is a 3D action-adventure game that combines classic elements from the genre with the exploration of an expanded world. Live a unique fantasy adventure, free the cities from a powerful and dark evil, and relive the look and feel of old-school video games.

name: Eastward
detailed_description: Eastward: Octopia DLC is Available Now! Sam and John return in an all-new adventure! In a remote mountainside village, Sam and John start life anew as farmers. Work the land, tend livestock, and cook heartwarming meals for familiar -yet strangely different- friends. Enjoy the good life in peaceful pixel surroundings! About the Game Eastward is a beautifully detailed and charming adventure game, from Shanghai-based indie developers, Pixpil. In the near-future, society is starting to collapse, and the human population is at an all-time low. A deadly toxic presence has spread across the land, destroying and devouring everything in its path. Those who could escape the miasma flocked to underground villages to start a new life. But for a hardworking miner and a mysterious young girl, the hope of a thriving outside world beckons… Escape the tyrannical clutches of Potcrock Isle's subterranean society and join Eastward’s unlikely duo on an exciting adventure to the land above! Discover beautiful yet bizarre settlements and make new friends as you travel across the world by rail. Contains adult humour and some mature themes. Game Features Discover the wonderfully weird world of Eastward. Climb aboard the cross-country railway which spans this decaying continent, stopping off to explore its bustling towns, curious campsites and shady forests. Fend off peculiar monsters and ferocious bosses with John’s weapon of choice - be it a flamethrower, cog-shooter or your trusty ol’ frying pan. Feeling merciful? Try temporarily stunning them with Sam’s kinetic blast. Switch between John and Sam to solve environmental puzzles and fight your way through formidable dungeons. Separate the duo to unlock hidden paths or stick together as you traverse a perilous landscape. Get to know a quirky cast of characters with oodles of personality! Immerse yourself in a heartwarming story-driven adventure, packed with fun and wacky humour. Create deliciously authentic Eastwardian cuisine using (mostly) fresh, organic ingredients from toxic forests, potcrab farms and abandoned malls. These delicacies will grant health bonuses, power boosts and secret boons. Bop along to a wonderfully upbeat soundtrack composed by Joel Corelitz (Death Stranding, Hohokum, The Unfinished Swan ), with sound design from Irish studio, Hyperduck Soundworks ( Dust: An Elysian Tail, Kingdom Rush )

_childDocuments_.review: I was so exited for this game. I thought that I found a diamond in the rough. The opening cinematic was incredible, the art style looked painstakingly hand crafted, and the characters were all visually distinct from one another. But as I poured hour after hour in this game, my cheery optimism gave way to confusion which gave way to pure hatred. I will try to keep this spoiler free.Starting with what many seem to think is the biggest flaw of the game: the characters will not stop talking. While I don't think this is what outright killed the game for me, it does contribute to the issue that did. If you are planning to play this, the first thing you should absolutely do is turn dialog speed to high. Even the most mundane events will have entire Greek novels of text to wade through before you are able to play again. There is no skip cut scene button so get ready to click X for 30 minutes while the NPC you decided to talk to runs their mouth off about nothing of interest.The game play itself is also nothing to write home about. Combat boils down to swinging your frying pan at the foe until it dies or, if it has quite a bit of health, stun it and then hit it to death. Better equipment and abilities don't change up play style at all either. They just have better range or do more damage. Puzzles are also bland and uninspired that just consist of splitting up John and Sam or hitting a bomb across a gap. I never felt challenged by many of the bosses either because whatever damage they did to me I just ate a meal and was back to full health. Some of the later bosses do get a bit harder, but it feels too little too late.Many little gripes pile up as well. When you try to dodge an attack, Sam who is trailing behind you always takes damage. The Earth Born mini-game that is constantly mentioned to be one of the best video games in the world of Eastward is some of the worst turn based combat I've ever played. You get a bunch of salt (Eastward's currency) whenever you kill enemies but never have a reason to spend it on anything other than more inventory so it just piles up once you have maxed it. The music is alright, but the same songs get played over and over (this one song that plays at heartfelt moments was played something around 30 times in total).All of these are bad, but what killed the game for me was the story. I wouldn't mind if characters talked nonstop if the entire story between the beginning and end wasn't filler. Entire plot lines and chapters are focused on people who do nothing once they are off screen. It feels like the story is a continual stream of consciousness on what a story should be. This happens and THEN this happens and THEN this happens without building on any characters. What the story should be is this happens THEREFORE this happens THEREFORE this happens. The entire meat of the story is just filler. You can take the first chapter and the last chapter of the game, cut everything else out, and plug in anything else and it would be exactly as cohesive as before.So if I had to say anything to you if your browsing the reviews to see if you should get this game, I have one word to say to you. Don't.Update: They added a skip dialog button and a fast travel along with a bootleg Stardew Valley dlc. Unfortunately, they can't fix a fundamentally broken story.

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from save fridges inducing an existential crisis and forcing into question the very foundations of philosophical anthropology,  has a lot to offer. In a refreshing yet polarizing game inspired by Earthbound and Zelda, you follow John and Sam on their post-apocalyptic journey, , eastward.Shanghai-based indie game studio Pixpil offers you an  flooded with beautiful pixelart, a uniquely wonderful and immersive story, and all the feels. It's a shame this game only appeals to... a very specific audience.  thrives in it's immersion, characters, art, and story; combat serves more to advance the narrative than being a central mechanic. Of course there's plenty of combat, but it's obviously supplemental. In , the sum is most certainly greater than the sum of its parts. Most critiques I've seen can be summarized by what John Koenig calls : "frustration that you're not enjoying an experience as much as you should... which prompts you to plug in various thought combinations to try for anything more than static emotional blankness, as if your heart had been accidentally demagnetized by a surge of expectations." To many, the narrative pace, heavy dialogue, omission of narrative detail and clarity, and more simplistic combat (at least early on), are reasons to call the game . My conclusion is that these very features are what makes the game charming and worth playing. The heavy dialogue helps with immersion and truly fleshing out the characters and atmosphere. The story, although a bit obscure, is not your standard structure and felt like few stories I've seen recently that tried something (with great pay-off, I'd say). But it's not a game for everyone: if you like narrative-driven, immersive, and explorative adventures, you'll probably love . If you want something more action-heavy, straightforward, or casual fun, this might not be the game for you. + Artstyle and Animations are some of the best I've ever seen, especially for pixel art. The color choices and environment design is unparalleled. + Characters are well-designed, fleshed out, and help immerse you in the story and environment.+ Atmosphere is probably the shining feature for me about this game. If atmosphere and being drawn in is important to you, Eastward is for you. + Story is unique, emotional, makes you piece together and theorize, and is perfectly supported by every other element in the game. Won't say more for spoiler purposes. + Combat is simplistic but has enough variety to stay fun for those sections. + Cooking was a blast in this game -- and I usually  resource collecting and cooking in games. + Collecting was at a perfect amount, and was a pleasure to complete.+ Difficulty never seems too hard, in combat or puzzles, but still enough to keep you involved. + Earth Born -- it's a whole game within a game! I love when developers do this and how it's weaved within the environments and a bit of the story. It was certainly fun to try and master. ~ Guides or information about many parts of the game are incredibly difficult to come by and more so for achievement completionists (see below).~ Pacing may take a while to truly grab you; it's a slow burn that requires/rewards patience and curiosity. I say give it until the end of Chapter 3 to see how you truly feel about it (even though each chapter is truly different and it got more fun personally as I went on). Full disclosure: I put the game down after Chapter 2 and it took a year before I came back to it... then I couldn't stop. ~ Story leaves... questions and a lot of it can be open to interpretation or is left unclear. This could be a good or bad thing depending on your preferences. The achievements are all fair and a blast to do. There are plenty of missable achievements, even just from the prologue (before many realize they'll want to complete it), but thankfully in one of the recent updates they created a chapter selection and added Earth Born to the main menu as well. This helped me go back and find some missing chests, get upgrades, ingredients, and so on. However, the bad news was it wasn't completely optimized. Despite going back into multiple saves it wouldn't completely work with recipes and eating all the food items as there are some missing even though there shouldn't be. (This problem is not standalone to me.) There also should be a way to see which food/chests you're missing, or at least which ones you have, for reasons like this. The most frustrating though, is I beat Earth Born via the main menu, but it didn't unlock the 4 pixballs it should have when going back into the saves to the machines. So there's no reason to play it through the main menu and to get certain Earth Born achievements you need to beat it through the saves. I now need to complete it all over through the save to get the pixball achievements -- this is unnecessary and they should either add a machine to the main menu, make it universal across saves, or have it so beating it in the main menu unlocks it in the saves. But overall this experience will forever stay with me and is worth the price. 9.13/10

_childDocuments_.review: EastWard brings back what was lost in today's adventure rpg games. Games like Space Quest, KingsQuest, Quest For Glory. The Game play isn't a story that drags, where you just want to finish so you get your money's worth. EastWards storytelling, is realistic, and for me, does what today's games no longer do! They cause real feelings of love, ager, and hate! Not to post spoilers, but I'm not even far in this game yet, and want karma to bury that evil Mayer!! Puzzles are like the old Sierra games, and get more difficult as the game progresses.For those who like to cheat in games like this, a huge warning. Do not add items you have not gotten in game yet! Adding more tokens, chips, gold, and salt, and locking ones HP is the only safe type of cheating you can do!Increasing bag size, and adding better weapons and items before you get to the parts of the game where you get them will forever softlock you from ever completing the game. It's not an anti cheat, it's triggering game flags that look at the items you have, and remove the code for the events that would have opened up new reagons for you, and instead forever keep them out of your reach.EarthBorn game, the only safe cheat is increasing gold and adding exp. Don't raise the levels, because doing so will result in game flags being passed up that give you needed items and reagon unlocks. Adding exp so levels go up nature, by realistic numbers, is only safest cheat to level up. For example, if you have 88 exp and 400 is level up, then add 312 and fight something. Don't go adding 200,000 exp all at once, or your game will softlock!I'll fix this review to format it better on my PC. Doing this on my phone.Game play and controlls is simple enough, but a game controller for battels Is highly recommended.Don't like the controller options, try a utility called Xpadder. It's a utility I myself use, to program the gamepad keys the way In comfortable with. This is great, if you play several games with a configuration your used to, and want this game to use the same configuration. I don't recommend Xpadder for valve games like TF2, as it's been known to accidentally trigger false VACs due to changes it makes in memory.Eastward reminds me also of the old Ultima and Final Fantasy games, using multiple player characters to complete puzzles, only they can do.The animations and especially the intro was done with great thought, and not thrown together, just to fit similar game formats.Back your adata save folder up often! This way if you make a mistake, or auto save, loses a good game, you won't have to start over. The only thing I severely dislike about this game, is having multiple intro screens, forced down ones throat , with no way to bypass. It's important to give credit where credit is due, but after the first time, if I'm paying for a game, I don't want to be forced to watch all the games creators, every single time I load the game up. Even running off an NVME, it's damned annoying!The game starts off, in an underground city. It looks as if an apocalypse has struck, where science of our time, has long been lost. The city is run by a corrupt mayer, who has convinced his citizens that the world above, is a dead and baren wasteland. Question the Mayer, and you and your family vanish. Sent off to what all believe are their deaths, never to return. Sam is found in a stasis, and through has no memory of her past, somehow knows the truth of what exists above, mostly by a spirit of herself, that tends to appear in times of danger. There are a lot of hidden rooms and treasures that your treasure Meter won't announce, so keep your eyes open for them. This is a single player game, but one the entire family can play together.Definitely worth the price!

_childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend Eastward to players. The gameplay is poorly paced and never rises above OK. The story ranges from OK to bad filler of an anime/tv show. The style and the world are almost worth playing the game despite its issues, but I wish the game was 10 hours shorter.  You play as both John and Sam as they team up to go on adventures. Using John to melee attack enemies and his bombs to solve puzzles. While Sam gets a ranged stun that doubles for some puzzles.   The combat is slow and clunky because your character gets no defensive options, and hit detection is spotty at times. Stunning with Sam then switching to John to kill is never worth it, because enemies recover too quickly. The later weapons feel bad to use, and later enemies charge quickly at you making it so either you have to play defensively or trade hits, both of which make the combat drag.  Puzzles in the game can be really enjoyable, when they split up your characters so Sam and John are on different parts of the room and have to help each other, it can be really fun. The issue is that most puzzles are not that, and tend to be simple walk around and use your characters ability to progress. In the final dungeon there were a pair of puzzles on right and left which was just using Sam's default attack to get around, the issue was it was the same exact puzzle, but reflected so you did the same "puzzle" twice in a two minute span.  The story has a huge problem, John is a silent protagonist which can be fine if written well. The issue is that the character never takes an action so I don't know if John cares about any characters outside of Sam. It's always Sam who speaks up for John, so it feels like John is a nothing character that is just there to do gameplay. Later on in the game a character declares their love for John, and I go "why?! You've known him for a day, and he's literally said nothing." After 21 hours with this game, I still don't know who John is and that bothers me considering he was there the whole time.  The plot itself is OK, but some of the filler was driving me nuts early on. The whole 2nd chapter could be removed, and no one would notice. Later on, you do a fetch quest to get a thing, and right before you hand it in, another character goes "oh, can I have that?" and Sam being the creampuff that she is, just gives it to him. Then we have to do another 2 hours of running around to make up for that. There's not even a good pay off for that, it just felt like a waste of time.  Others have mentioned it, but later on in the story it gets a bit unhinged/kingdom hearts/legend of zelda timeline levels of magic evil darkness. It makes the later chapters feel cheap, because there never seems like there's any logic behind the "villains." End of game spoilers   The game has style for days, and the locations you go to are both fantastical and grounded at the same time. Seeing new locations was half the fun of the game. The only issue is you spend too long in most areas so the charm wears off.  Don't buy. The game play drags, the story drags, and the world while great doesn't make up for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Now I'm torn about this game. Is it a great game? No. If there was a better rating system in place then I'll give this game a 6 out of 10. What makes it worthwhile play is the aesthetics; the graphics is phenomenal the little details and the movement is all beautifully presented and on top of that is a great soundtrack. Everything hits those 16 bit era feel just right with a modern twist to everything. The story starts of intriguing if a bit slow to start but it builds character sadly that story loses focus midway where it shoe horns some weak story beats that dont quite belong. Then we get to the pay off and its a tad underwhelming and somethings are left un answered for but its also slightly heart warming.So the gameplay is very A link to the Past - lite, you have your dungeons and basic functions of a melee weapon. Along the way you are provided with more weapons but they are never really utilised to any satisfying results. Also the attack can be iffy at times, I dislike how you are stationary when executing an attack and on occasions i was unable to hit the target resulting getting injured. The attacks are very basic to a fault and rather slow in comparison the enemy who tend to be a tad faster. Thankfully the game is very forgiving, if you die you are not sent too far back plus encounters are not too difficult.The puzzles are on the easy side, very similar to Zelda games and even the chest opening music cues and posing is borrowed from zelda games. I enjoyed the puzzles but nothing too taxing.Now the games biggest problem is how slow everything moves and that includes the text boxes, which has no way to speed up the dialogues and if you accidentily hit interact with an NPC again u have to sit through the whole ordeal again. And by god there is way too much dialogue, though they are well written it goes on for way longer than nessecary. Even saving the game there is a pointless dialogue box to siv through. At 20 hrs it did feel it did over stay its welcome way before the endgame.Now why i say i recommend it is because there is huge potential on display here. The game is very similar to Zelda and the story can at times be intriguing and there is heart. I think the graphics and the music alone can draw your attention through to the end but definitely its not a game for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, how to put this. It's not the game I though I was getting, honestly, but nevermind that, my problem with it is that it's not as unique as everyone seems hinting in reviews, it hardly features any originality when it comes to gameplay mechanics if I do say so myself and as for the story - I'd say it unravells just at the right pace to keep you captivated (with the exception of the complete 2 hours long stall at Monkolywood), but ends up with this half baked sort of explanation that doesn't really explain anything, to be honest...Let me tell you what I didn't like, cause if you got this far, it must be because you are curious. Lets start with long unskippable logos when you launch the game. Not a big issue, but still an issue, the faster you can get into game, the better. Boring dialogues that cannot be properly fast forwarded - this is a huge issue, cause there really are many and mosttimes, I just didn't care and game didn't let me skip it. Unconsistent art style - game seems to server certain cute pixelart idea, and then all icons, markers, concept art, even the opening cinematics ship you something much else. Combat is missing certain... je ne sais quoi, so to speak, something like block or dodge would definitely spice things up, it just feels very rigid this way, that's all I'm saying. The Earth Born? Pokemon game within the game that you can play on in game consoles... this is usually not a good concept for any game really, Witcher had Gwent, Horizon Strike, Stardew Valley that weird cowboy game, right, but it doesn't help story driven game at all, it just takes away the concentration and prolongs already quite long game (16 hours seems about it).What I did like, some characters were interesting, sadly, none of them was in the focus long enough, besides Sam. The pixel art is interesting, some effects left me speechless, like how they managed water or the elevator platform in the end. It seemed to merge nicely pixelart with 3D way I have yet to see. Boss battles made use of latest acquired mechanics which is always a fresh breeze and I did kinda like the ending, even though it made no sense.That being said, it's not a bad game, but it's not excellent or awesome... I struggle to call it good really, as I like to play good games again from time to time, but this one I know I won't be coming back to. Had my fair share, there are far more superior games of the genre to play or play again - Crosscode definitelly set the bar high for me, if you are wondering whether to grab this game or not, I'd say - probably not. Unless you are super hyped from trailer or something like that, You will very likely not get hooked by it when you get to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: A really amazing pixel style game! The art is really beautiful. Probably the best I've ever seen! The puzzles aren't that hard, which provide just the right level of challenge without becoming frustrating.However, despite these strengths, Eastward suffers from being too long! Chapter 3, in particular, stands out as a low point, with its unnecessary back and forth fetch quests that feel like tedious filler content. _childDocuments_.review: I want to begin this review by saying that I, like many others, really wanted to enjoy this game. However, as I wrote out this review, it became strikingly obvious to me that this game's issues far outweigh the joys.Now that I've finished the game, I want to say that Eastward is not a game I would recommend buying for $25 and playing, at least if you are the average person. I'm a big fan of Earthbound-likes, and I'm glad that I played it simply to experience what it was like unspoiled, but several parts of the game left a very sour taste in my mouth and really ruined the final experience. Below is my comprehensive list about what was good and bad about the game, at least to me.The Good- First off, this game's artwork is incredible. The sheer amount of work that must have went into making everything, from the completely unique and detailed environments to the literal hundreds of NPCs with unique animations really baffles me.- The game's characters are all diverse and potent in personality, which really makes the places you visit feel teeming with life. On a side note, Sam (the white haired-girl) is absolutely adorable and a joy to have throughout the game.- The overall gameplay is very good. I had a lot of fun throughout my playthrough.- The music is pretty nice. Not really Toby Fox level, have you, but still good.That's about all I can think of for what's good about the game. Now... getting to what I didn't enjoy.- Easily the worst thing about this game is the massive amount of holes in the story the ending leaves for you to think about. No explanation is given as to why the main events of the game actually happened. No backstory, no lore, no anything. All of the supernatural events of the game (including a massively strange final area and boss fight) just seemed to have happened... because. I feel like the idea may have been to leave this stuff up to the viewer's interpretation, but that just feels like an excuse.- It seems like 75% of this game is dialogue. I understand this is supposed to be a story-based game, but there were a lot of times where I just had to mash my space bar to get through some dialogue that I didn't want to sit through because it was filler and/or had nothing to do with the story.- A final scene reveals the fate of John and Sam, and I personally find it to be nonsensical. I don't want to spoil anything, but it really seems like the creators of the game just wanted a happier ending and half-assed one without any good explanation as to why the hell it actually happens.- This game really has a LOT, and I mean A LOT of filler. I feel like chapters 2, 3, and ESPECIALLY 6 could be taken out of the game entirely. They contribute little or nothing to the story and feel really forced.- The feel of the game from chapters 1-4 and chapters 5-9 are completely different. There's really no plot progression from chapters 2, 3, and 4. It really feels like you're not going anywhere and are just kind of living the life of John and Sam. It finally gets going in chapters 5 and 7-9, but even this part is kind of ruined by the fact that none of the main events are actually thoroughly explained in the end.- There's this villain that the story tries to set up that feels entirely tacked on. I have no idea why they decided to put him in the game, as he has little to no plot significance. He shows up in three different ages, each of which seems to be a completely separate person. This is not explained at all.- There's a twist villain at the end. Their motivation seems unreasonable and what actually happens to them at the end of the game isn't shown. Do they die? Do they survive? Perhaps their motivation would make more sense if we actually knew their backstory, which is alluded to a couple times but never actually explained.- Story aside, the puzzles are often very simple. There was only once or twice in the game where I had to scratch my head to figure out an answer to one.- The combat has its issues. The post-hit invincibility does not last nearly as long as it should, and sometimes you just get half of your health removed by one enemy because of it. - Sometimes the difficulty just ramps up for no reason. The end-game fight with the twist villain and this escape scene right before it were unreasonably difficult. You can get one-shot by these fish in the sequence (which happened to me 3 times, as the game barely gives you enough time to react to them appearing).- There is no back-tracking in this game. Once you finish a chapter, the treasures and sometimes optional upgrades left there are gone forever. Not to mention that this game has 100% completion achievements for just about anything you could think of. It feels like a big "♥♥♥♥ you" from the developers, really.That's about it. Overall, the game is OK, but its problems are common and glaring. Even though the gameplay has its issues, I think that at the end of the day the part that ruins the experience is the story. The writers either just didn't think to explain anything past the main points or wanted to put it up to player interpretation. Either way there is just not enough context to have a satisfying ending.Overall I would give this game a 4.5/10. It certainly has its moments but there is a lot, and I mean A LOT that could be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: i really want to like this game, and ive marked this as a positive review because i want to support a studio that went through a lot of turmoil to make this game, but there are some serious fundamental problems i think people should be aware of before they buy this gamethe whole gameplay loop in general isnt particularly deep or engaging. the combat is uninteresting and clunky, the puzzles dont really require any brain power, and most of the quests youll be doing are fetch-quests with no real plot relevance.the story is a mixed bag. it starts off very strong, the first two hours or so of this game are by far the best in terms of plot and gameplay, as there is a lot of mystery and intrigue built up around the end of the world and a town mayor who clearly knows more than he's letting on about what happened and a prison break, and a middle aged man seeing the outside world for the first time.my main problem with this game is that all of that intrigue doesnt really go anywhere. the story after reaching the second location you arrive at after the tutorial zone becomes quite slow and meandering, and the whole end-of-the-world plot surrounding sam and her powers and connection to the MIASMA that is destroying the world is seemingly abandoned until pretty much the end of the game in favour of cute, but reasonably short adventures in one location that focus more on character writing than plot writing. thankfully character writing is one of the game's big strengths, but the pacing is ruined by this extended series of fetch quests.i think the main problem is the game wanted it both ways, it wanted some cute soft-apocalypse slice of life stories, and a big exciting plot about saving a broken world from a cosmic evil, but the two never really converge. nothing in the slice of life stuff is ever interesting or exciting enough to really get invested into (as well as often being pretty padded and contrived, like  or ), and the big saving the world story is never really explained well enough to make any sense. its hard for me to even explain what happens in this side of the narrative because i find the overarching plot of the game to be that confusing. theres a number of sections i think are meant to have narrative purpose, like , or , but all of those events SOUND much more interesting and engaging than they actually are, because none of it is ever really explained. the plot becomes a lot better after playing because all the superfluous sections are forgotten, and all the story is only explained in as much detail as a faded memory anyway, so you think back on it more fondly thinking theres a bunch of other cool stuff youve just forgotten about.this is a good game to buy and play if you like strong character writing, slice of life adventures, fetch quests, and extremely pretty visuals, those are the games core strengths, but its definitely a 'brain-off' experience. you cant think about it too much or the whole thing will just fall apart. i look forward to pixpil's next game because i do think theres a lot of potential in this studio if they are given the time and budget they simply didnt have with eastward, but i do also badly wish this was the game that was advertised by the opening animation and trailers

_childDocuments_.review: I was torn on what type of review to leave this game but I think if given the chance to go back and not play it, that's what I would opt to do. Therefore, this will be a "Not Recommended" review.The game starts off fairly simple in terms of combat and puzzle solving and never really progresses too much beyond that, only adding a few simple variations to your existing abilities. But what really makes this a "Not Recommended" title for me is the pacing and overall narrative. _childDocuments_.review: I LOVE THIS GAME!!!The pixel art and the environment created by it—the animations, the effects, the story—all are simply surreal. For the impatient, the game allows you to speed up the cutscenes too, which is awesome!The gameplay is not very complex; you get a variety of weapons and bombs and make your way through enemies and puzzles. Personally, this is a very good thing for me, as I still struggle to play and understand some games where the gameplay is quite complex.For those who like to collect stuff, you can collect ingredients, recipes, treasures, and figurines from a popular in-game series. That series also has a built-in RPG with Eastward. It's basically a whole game inside of this one!I was initially hesitant to buy this game because I heard it had some major bugs. For a long time, this game has been on my mind, so I decided to risk it and purchase it. I believe since the game has been out for 2 years now, the developers must have fixed those bugs, as I found none of the ones I've seen some people mention.Another thing to mention is the number of places to explore. If you like this, then Eastward presents you with a variety of vast maps with enemies, puzzles, secrets, and stories to complete.With all of this said, I'm ready to invest in Eastward's DLC, Octopia!

_childDocuments_.review: Eastward is very very good, and also very very bad. The world is incredibly detailed, with multiple areas in each of the five main locations that all seem very thought-through and cohesive. These locations are also filled with an almost overwhelming amount of npcs, all of which can be talked to. Most of the npcs have dialog that changes according to the events of the game which gives the sense that they all have little stories you can piece together. Some of them also have side quests that can be accomplished. I really enjoyed all of the npc interactions, but if you're not someone who wants to poke around and learn every detail of a world they can be very irritating. The dialog often is very long and unskippable. There were many times that I accidentally talked to someone I'd already spoken with and had to sit through a minute worth of dialog I'd already read. The pacing of the game is also an issue. The game is very very slow, with many of the main questlines requiring you to sit through a lot of unnecessary cutscenes that don't add anything at all to the story and are sometimes just plain boring. One of the main chapters of the game feels more like a movie where you back and forth between scenes than a game. The combat is also amazing in some ways and awful in others. The core mechanic, which is having two characters and switching between them, works very well both in the combat and the puzzle areas. There are new mechanics introduced through the game that kept this part of the game feeling interesting and novel. However, I played with the keyboard controls and I had a lot of issues. It's impossible to disable the mouse and just use the keyboard, so the only way to aim is to use the mouse. I ended up trying to position the mouse in a specific corner of my screen and then running around trying to keep the enemies to that side of the characters, but I almost stopped playing at the first dungeon because of this. Finally, the story and lore are in my opinion the place where this game excels, and also the greatest flaw. (Very very mild spoilers ahead) The game is constantly providing small details that slowly build up the lore so that it feels like you are personally uncovering an incredible mystery. The whole game seems to be building up to a really really interesting finale where you will finally understand how all of these puzzle pieces fit together. Characters are introduced, and then introduced again, and then cryptic details about their past come to light, and it feels interesting and exciting. The game is intentionally giving you questions about the world and about the characters, and for me, the drive to learn the answers to these questions was the whole reason I continued playing the game. But then at the end of the story, literally nothing is explained. More questions are introduced right up until the end of the game (why a train? why monkeys? why is this character appearing again? Where did that character come from? what happened to that other area? what is the relationship between these two characters? why do these people know your name? how did you get to point a from point b?) but the answers to these questions just don't exist at all. I found the end of this story to be a complete disappointment because of this. I think someone who likes interesting puzzle mechanics will really enjoy parts of this game, but not others. I think someone who really enjoys story-based games will like parts of this game, but not others. I'm not sure if people who like combat will get much out of this game, although I enjoyed the combat since it seems pretty much the same throughout the game. Basically, I'm really not sure who this game is for.

_childDocuments_.review: Eastward is a game that I can't recommend enough.The story at the beginning was incredible and really got me immersed in the world. As the game progressed I couldn't help but fall in love with the characters more. Everyone was unique, the side quests were fun, nothing really felt forced.While I love this game to bits, I will say that as you progressed the story diminished a little and felt like there was a little more to be desired. I feel this could have been solved with the gaming being a little longer and expanding on a few details that weren't as fleshed out as the beginning of the story. That's not to say there isn't enough content or the story is bad, the game took a lot longer to finish than I had expected which was great and the story overall was done well and I enjoyed it.If you're on the fence about trying it, I would say go for it. Between the minigames and the game as a whole, I think there's something for most and that it's an experience you won't find again for a while. I will be eagerly awaiting any more games that Pixpil might create in future and consider Eastward to now be one of my favourite games.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long time since I tasted a game like this; the gorgeous graphics, banger retro soundtracks, fully animated cute characters, fun puzzles, and intense battles, this game has all of it. Seriously, I can't get enough of Sam's walking animation, the way she walks by small steps is too cute!Nevertheless, I feel that the story is lacking. I like the concept of MIASMA and all, but the story plot is just.. Let's just say that there are a lot of unexplained things. This  guy as one of the villains also doesn't fit the seriousness of the story . It's even worse starting from the second-half of the story, the story feels rushed and it definitely failed to appeal to me. Perhaps I can say that the way the story is driven is cliche or classic. Finally, the ending is a normal, bitter-sweet, and not really fulfilling.And why do I still recommend this game? The story being classic doesn't necessarily mean that it's bad. I also believe everyone's story interest is different, so you can give Eastward a try and then judge it by your own. After all, the gameplay quality is very great.

_childDocuments_.review: This hits as one of the best Indie and Pixel Games I have every played.-The beauty and atmosphere is stellar, with such a colorful world and excellent world building, each place visited offering something new, with a retro soundtrack that fits with both the graphics and style to the earlier era of games. -Gameplay is quite dynamic and enjoyable, especially when it comes to the creative roster of boss fights, and the various weapons at the player's disposal.   Along with a companion system that is very well done; being able to switch between one and the other on the fly with the push of a bottom, and each with their own traits, making the feeling of taking down an enemy with both of their skills easy to pull off and satisfying when it hits.  That along with how the gameplay can feel like it is changing with each level, while still keeping true to its identity.  Plus the inclusion of a game within a game (if you haven't played it yet, you'll find out) that goes even further to the retro style.-Finally the story: Oh my god, and anyone who makes the false claim that video games aren't art, need to just stop talking.   I was invested from start to finish.   NO SPOILERS, but the narrative is very well told.  I can't say there isn't a character that wasn't entertaining.  When the emotions hit, they hit hard.  And I got to say, this game probably has one the best silent protagonists, even able to present him with character without ever saying a single word.  While there are some parts that might feel like panning to some, I personally still enjoy them because it introduces more likable characters, while presenting others as very three-dimensional.   Which is probably my personal favorite highlight with the story, how there is an emphasis on characters over plot.Overall this game is masterpiece in my eyes with how creative the experience (which is something I love) is and I can't actually think of a single complaint.

_childDocuments_.review: Look John! A steam review!Eastward is a weird fantasy and sci-fi-esque game with dystopian elements and a Zelda-like fight system which also realies heavily on dialogue, so much so that this feels like a visual novel and a walking simulator mashed into one, rather than being an adventure game. The puzzles are creative, and the game always teaches you something new that you didn't really think you could do so far. However the story is a slowburner, you don't know where the story is heading, and you are trying to make sense of the puzzle pieces you get along the way. It is an interesting concept, and the majority of the time it works. You play 2-3 hours, then quit but there's nothing to give you the "I want to play Eastward again" feeling. You need to be in a certain mood to play it, but when you do, it is an enjoyable experience with both funny, cute, and sad moments. Currently at Chapter 3, so this review will be updated once I finished the game.

_childDocuments_.review: great game. the art and music are outstanding and definitly what lead me to buy the game. i got in on sale after having it on my wishlist for ages. usually i play games in the life sim genre but the art in this one intrigued me. the game has some issues with pacing. i would love to get a asked if i want to continue not after saving but rather before jumping to the next plot point because you can't go back to any area once you left it and triggered the corresponding plot element. and since the game encourages exploration it is rather easy to meet a boss or trigger the next scene when you haven't finished exploring. the world is beautiful and the characters are maybe  bit shallow but fun.the combat and little puzzles play nicely and kind of remind me of the browser flash games of the early 2010s. it is not too hard but still challenging a bit. up until chapter three i encountered one timed challenge where you had to run from something while defeating monsters and solving small riddles which was by far the hardest part of the game yet and i died multiple times.the game doesn't really tell you how it works but you get a oment to explre everything new you encounter. it is still intuitive enough to not need a ton of guidance. there is game within the game which is also interesting and not neccessary for the plot. you will need to play it for the achievements though. right now after playing it for about 10h i would definitly recommend eastward. it is a nice game and worth your time. even if it is just to listen to the music and look at the great pixel art.

_childDocuments_.review: There are enough reviews heaping praise on the game. This is not one of them. I usually do not leave negative reviews. If I don't like the game I just uninstall it and move on. But this time, I felt the need to warn others, as too many comments here will try and convince you that this game is perfect and you must buy it.The biggest advantage of the game is how beautiful and cute it is. That's why I bought it - I wanted to play something nice and fun, after a few more demanding horror games I have played, I wanted to relax. I did not expect to play a game that is dark and infuriating. I absolutely despise the trend of "subverting" the tropes at any cost, and if a game advertises itself with its cutesy characters, animations and intros, I do not want to deal with basically aiding genocide and following around broken and psychologically scarred characters. I do not care about meeting all these almost unrealistically nice people, just to have them killed off. Add on top of that just how much the game is in love with itself, and the result is off-putting and honestly revolting. Yes, it's gorgeous. Yes the music is great. But man, the story is tedious, the characters are absolute one-dimensional caricatures of people, and in the end it left me angry at wasting my time playing it and with zero desire to see it through till the end. Bought it on steep discount and still regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been crying for the last hour. While the game could do with some shaving down, I am deeply attached to this game and all its characters. _childDocuments_.review: You're probably like me. You saw this game or waited for it to come out and thought "Wow, this ticks all my boxes: Pixel art, good music, and an interesting looking plot!" And you'd be right! ...for the first few hours. This game sets up a very interesting, if derivative, plot right from the start and then just never does anything with it. - Side characters show up with their own interesting problems and are never heard from again, which not only clutters the story but left me wondering about them ...which distracted me from current story events.- Incredibly interesting topics  are thrown around and then left to rot because we have to see the next cutesy thing Sam does. (Don't get me wrong. She is cute.) - The music is fantastic until you've heard each song for the 50th time, because there just aren't many songs. Also, each song is way too short and doesn't loop well, so you'll be halfway through a minigame or boss fight and the music will just jarringly restart itself without even a fade-out/fade-in. There are a grand total of two songs that are longer than 3 minutes and less than 75 songs total, just to show what I'm talking about.- Before I just rag on the game for the whole review, I did truly enjoy the art style throughout the entire playthrough. It's an incredibly pleasing game to look at and the environments are highly varied, which is why I was able to finish it without quitting out of frustration from the above points.I would not recommend you buy this game unless you just really, really enjoy the look of pixel art or waited since the game was announced in 2015 (like me) to play it. Its music is fine, but there are so few tracks that are of decent length that the listening experience is not good. The plot trips itself up by adding way too many side stories and details that are much more interesting than the actual plot.(Finally, I see people attempting to pass this game off as if it's Zelda-like or Earthbound-like. Just know that this game is definitely NOT like those games, but oh boy does it like its references.)

_childDocuments_.review: I've known about Eastward for a long time, but I couldn't get past Chapter 1 due to language barriers. Today, I completed 100% of the main storyline and about 50% of the Octopia DLC. I'm very happy with my decision; the game is great and meaningful. I'm a fan of 2D pixel games, especially ones with beautiful, colorful settings. To me, this is the most beautiful 2D pixel game I've ever played. I'm very happy and grateful for the efforts of the game developers. If anyone needs a recommendation, I personally suggest you own and try this game.

_childDocuments_.review: When I found this title, i was originally searching for something to fill the nostalgia hole left by the unavailability of the first three games in a series called zenonia, which was a childhood favorite of mine. Wow did this game hit the nail on the head for me. From mechanics, resource economy, art style, right down to the amazingly heartwarming story (promise no spoilers ;)). The mechanics, while pretty simple, are very unique for the genre, having two main characters with very different abilities to switch between, which allows for much more dynamic game-play, especially since the combat isn't bogged down by turn-based mechanics, which outside of nostalgic favorites, I'm way too impatient for. The puzzles and time limit areas were simple enough as to not present a severe obstacle to story progression, while also making you think just enough to be interesting most of the time. The game also felt very intuitive, i wasn't slogging through tutorials for every new weapon or bomb type, with there only being small text-banner hints for the new stuff, which let the story/dialogue have a lot of room to breathe and grow. The only real criticism I have for the mechanics of the game has to do with the resource economy. The game includes a limited crafting system in the form of cooking, which allows you to make different food items that buff your stats, while also restoring health or providing an overshield to your healthbar. While this isn't all that different from other RPGs, the way to acquire ingredients felt a little lack luster, as outside of the selection of items you could buy at the food shops, the only way to get ingredients was to defeat enemies, and hope that the RNG gods would bless you with a good drop. The Ammo also felt somewhat similar towards the beginning, but by mid game you would probably have collected enough in-game currency to not have to worry about buying refills, and they introduce a time-based refill feature. You can probably tell by the previews in the store page, but the art style of the game is gorgeous, while lacking the depth of field of similarly illustrated games like octopath traveler, the highly stylized pixel art design is incredibly endearing, and character design is very unique. There are little to no recycled elements (oustide possibly the dungeon areas, I'd have to go back and really scrutinize) and each character and dungeon just screams with personality. My biggest compliment would definitely be to the story, outside of a few points mid-game (which did, by game's end, give more meaning to the ending) everything felt important, and the story didn't feel all over the place. From reading other people's reviews, the most common criticism I see is that the story's pacing is a bit sluggish. I can absolutely see where they're coming from, as I feel the marketing strategy was more focused on the combat and action sequences (which there are plenty of anyway IMO). However, personally, I was very much appreciative of the time I got to spend getting to know the supporting cast of characters, rather than the time spent in menus or trying to read item lore after the fact. The story telling really gave weight exactly where it needed to be in the events leading up to the ending, and really built up the player's emotional connection with the characters. What I will say regarding this, though, is that If you come into the game expecting a quick pixel-art dungeon crawler, then this title will certainly not meet your expectations, it is surprisingly long, and I enjoyed every minute. 100% would recommend this game, and I'll definitely be coming back to 100% complete in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game but I feel as though it just wasn't for me.The art design is honestly some of the best I've seen in years, it feels like it's breathing new life into pixel art, which has been growing repetitive in the industry for some time now. This game oozes charm from every part of the story, including the character writing, soundtrack and world.The only thing I didn't like was the gameplay, largely due to the fact that this game is outside of the genres I typically play, with RPGs and fast paced roguelikes being my main cup of tea. It felt very Zelda inspired, but with slower combat, which for me was enough to turn me off of the game. The story also tended to break up the gameplay, causing long periods of time where you only did one or the other.Honestly, despite this criticism, this game is a lot of fun, I'd recommend getting past the tutorial before deciding how you feel, and if you decide to stick with it, get all the way to the end!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR (All personal opinion)Story: 8/10Combat/Mechanics: 6/10Graphics/Style of art: 9/10Controls: 7/10Sound/music: 10/10If you made it past the TL;DR congratulations, here is my personal opinion in detailStory:The story itself is mostly in one piece, however there are some parts that personally left me confused. Those confusions didn't really clear up until I have progressed a bit more into the story. Personally, the story seems a little to segmented for it to be fluid, but regardless the main story goal is clear from the beginning.Combat/Mechanics:I was kind of disappointed with the combat system. It was bland and cliche type of dungeon crawler type with different enemies with different pattern of attack. The levels and the difficulty of enemies were too erratic. Some levels were so easy that I could run through without losing a single heart, or it was so difficult that it took me several tries to even get past the first enemy. However, what saved me from most of the difficult situations is the god-like cooking system. Personally, this little mechanic in the game where you can spend your precious currency to buy ingredients to cook and buff yourself up for battles and encounters were a god send. It adds so much more purpose in trying to gather ingredients and make new foods that buff you in different ways.Graphics:Personally, I am a big sucker for these kind of retro rpg graphics. Even though it looks simple from afar, but as you play the game you notice details that the developers put in to make sure that it's not a simple old style graphics.Control:I played on a controller so I can't really say for those who will play on keyboard and mouse. The controller controls were a little wonky at first, but relatively easy to get used to. One problem I had is that when switching weapons, there is the way to switch with the D-pad and the lower joystick. If you have drift on that specific joystick, it changes weapons constantly which caused me to die few times.-EDITED- HOW CAN I FORGET SOUNDSound/music:Original, unique and fits in like a puzzle to situations accordingly. Every battle, every cut scene and the background music when you are running around are all exceptional. Powerful, sad, happy and countless ways to express situations have a music attached to them. It is safe to say that this game's one out of the two pillars is music and sound. Kudos to the sound and music team!Overall, it is such a beautifully made game. You will fall in love with characters pretty easily and come to care for them. It is definitely worth the price. BUY IT

_childDocuments_.review: (( Edit: Pre-Octopia Opinion, please read recent reviews instead. ))Not the most engaging combat, but that's about the worst I can say.Original story, interesting mechanics (that are if anything are simply under-explored, hence the less engaging combat) and adorable characters.There's another review I saw that said the characters felt empty and hollow.I reaaally need to stress that that's entirely false from my perspective. Maybe they didn't like the characters, maybe they didn't play enough of the game to actually see more sides of the characters, but I can guarantee you that they're not empty or hollow. The charm of this game comes entirely from its story, characters, and the fact that the main storyline is very easy to follow if you're not looking for all the secrets.You DO need to progress to get to the good puzzles, and you DO need to actively search for the secrets to be able to find the challenging puzzles... But all that tells me is that they wanted anyone to be able to complete the story. You don't need to be great at the game to beat it, but you will need to learn how to use the mechanics to your advantage if you want to find everything.Severely underrated, incredibly heartwarming, and undeniably original in its setting and story.If you NEED good combat to enjoy a game, maybe don't play this one, but if you're able to accept a game for what it is, and not what you want it to be, give it a shot... I promise you you'll find something about the game that you like.Combat definitely feels like it wasn't fleshed out enough, but as I said, that's the worst I can say about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I think there's a lot of great art and detail put into this game. It's good I've enjoyed the parts I have experience but I have a huge quirk and that's the dialog.  if I hit a or x it needs to appear instantly so I can then read it instead of painstakingly waiting for it come up and be read.   I'm sorry but this game is already very long and drawn out and at times a gauntlet of patience when it comes to getting through the dialog, especially when the current plot is so obvious you really don't need to read through it.  Criticism two:  sometimes the dialog gives you descriptions and they are counter intuitive to where you should actually go.  Example: someone asks you to meet them at the cemetery Downtown... The cemetery is in a place literally called Uptown and it's north on the map... Criticism 3:  Let me skip the long as intro, no not the cool animation which you can skip, the painfully slow fade in of the eastward title that then EVENTUALLY brings you to the menu...  Most infuriating thing about this game is the lack of being able to skip or move quickly through cut scenes and dialog when you want to.  A lesson in game design for the creators, I know you put blood sweat and tears into this game but forcing us to appreciate that hardship leads to me appreciating it a lot less than I would if I had some control over the pace of the game.
