_childDocuments_.review: EastwardDespite all the negative things the critics have gathered their attention on this game means a lot for me. I mean it. For me the atmosphere and the story, the way it is told matters a lot, and this is what I loved about this game the most. It's the characters, their emotions, their stories, their desires. I felt ALL of that. And it hit me hard. I have a tendency to feel sorrow and tough times characters go through more than I feel their joy.For me Eastward is a sad story about brave people who got the courage to do things they believe in even if it's the death they have to face. The good times John, Sam, and others had have taught me to enjoy me life more, you can never know when it can all be gone in the blink of an eye..The way the story is told leaves a lot for player interpretation. The critics say the story is not very understandable and doesn't tell a lot about the setting and that. However it completely changes the way a player gets to know the story, so it doesn't feel like a movie about John or something, it feels more like the player learns stuff about Eastward's world alongside with John and Sam!  And I love it. Oh! And of course I would love to know more about the setting, so I hope for a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: Eastward is an excellent title but some strange design decisions keep it short of being a masterpiece.⠀The first thing that appeals to the player and anyone interested in this game is the gorgeous pixel art. Not only is it well designed (but not quite pixel-perfect yet, see the negative section) and beautifully-animated but Pixpil have taken it to the next level by adding great lighting and animation effects. This blend works out extremely well and is jaw-dropping right until the end. I found the story very good overall but as a potential buyer, be aware that most of the gameplay is reading speech bubbles and watching cutscenes while combat takes a back seat. Speaking of combat, I found it very interesting if a little basic. The bosses are great and beating them gives you a warm feeling of accomplishment. There's also crafting in this game through cooking. It's nifty but could be improved by directly selecting the recipe if you already know it and have all the ingredients. The music is excellent for the most part and that chiptune vibe goes really well with the visuals. Finally, I really enjoyed the ingame mini-RPG with its Amiibo-like figurines to collect. It's a nice addition to take a break.⠀One thing that bothered me a bit is how the story regularly drags on and some parts almost feel like filler material. It nicely alternates between dark and funny moments but it's quite unfocused at times.Edit: A new pixel-perfect mode is now available, making the visuals nice and crisp. Thanks for implementing it!
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: THE TRAILER IS MISLEADING!!!! No journey with Izzy and Jasper while in the trailer they are there plus the train is different. Unless the game developer intended a different story then they should have made a different trailer. I love the game but so many questions left unanswered. The game ended without any explanation what's going on plus I hate the kind of quest where I have to go to point A to fix point B then go back again to A to fetch another item. Also! the time island issue is annoying, spent 30 minutes repeating the same dialogue and then sent back in time again and to repeat the process. REALLY CAN'T SKIP DIALOGUE SO BE PREPARED to spend most of your time reading and spam pressing the keyboard/controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: - Wonderful visuals and art, the pixel art here is seriously one of the cleanest, most fluid and expressive I've    ever seen.  - Forgettable soundtrack, played for 30 hours and I can only remember 3 or 4 songs that played on every    single cutscene and combat encounter.- Infuriating combat where enemies jump towards you constantly yet there's no dodge option and can only    run at a determined speed, exacerbated when a bunch of enemies spawn in a small arena and you    constantly take damage while they jump in and out of your attack range. - Aimless story focused mainly on fetch quests and talking to various NPCs. Has an interesting hook during    the first 2 chapters, but does nothing with it and instead spends the next 10 hours setting up plot threads    and character arcs that at best are forgotten by the next chapter, and at worst actively harm the narrative's    coherence. I was forcing myself to finish it to see if at least the ending would make up for some of these    issues, but it does such a terrible job at making you care about these characters that I can't even be    bothered to finish the last chapter to see how it ends.Buy it at your own discretion or if you want to support any future projects from these devs, but you'll probably get more enjoyment out of it by watching someone else play through it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: Eastward is a fantastic game! I love pixel art games, and this one did not disappoint with the direction of the art style.  Lighting is done really well and each different environment is unique and interesting. The animated intro is also so fun and animated really well. Another thing is the soundtrack...  amazing! Great ambience when your walking around the environments, eerie when it needs to be mysterious, intense during boss battles and heartfelt during special moments. I really enjoyed the story and all the characters are lovable and fun! Looking forward to my 2nd playthrough and 100% with achievements! Thank You Pixpil and Chucklefish!
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: An RPG that wears its influences on its sleeve. The art style and music are the real draw here. The puzzles are pretty good, and the gameplay/combat is fine, though there are frustrating difficulty spikes out of nowhere. _childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: Like many I was hyped for and wanted to love this game, and while it looks beautiful it falls short on story.Pros:- (Almost) flawless artwork.- Beautiful sound.- Fun characters.- Alright combat.Cons:- Story is too cryptic and never explained.- You leave the first area too quickly and can never return to a previous area, meaning you can miss items.- You can't skip dialogue you've already heard.

_childDocuments_.review: This game may have been in development for a long time but hoooo baby was the time spent worth every bit. You can see the amount of love and care overflowing out of this game.The story, The variation, The mechanics. Its all so engaging. The spots i thought would would become a slog to go through were actually quite good and well paced to prevent everything from becoming monotonous. I highly suggest this game to anyone who enjoys the Zelda series, and/or the Earthbound series. or the adventure genre overall. Thank you so much for this amazing game.I look forward to the next game that Pixpil comes up with.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: Eastward is a magical RPG, really unlike anything else out there. It's closest influences definitely tie to the protagonist tropes of Mother 3, but with light adventure combat and puzzle-solving, and alot of dialogue. My biggest criticisms gameplay-wise would be some of the early chase sequences when you have very little health really ask alot out of you in responding quickly to solving a puzzle and the simple movement makes early combat tough; remember to use both characters' abilities. Remember to explore around everywhere you can each time you go through an area for secrets, because your opportunities in each location are limited; It's called Eastward for a reason; you never go west.But my biggest piece of advice?DON'T blaze through the story. Take your time, take it slow. Reserve your expectations and let the game delight you. The magic of this game isn't in the overarching plot, though it has great hooks, some neat plot twists, and knows how to pull the right emotions out of you. The magic of Eastward is the beautiful 3D-lit, 2D-made pixel art style, the amazing music, the stunning environments (with secrets to find!) and especially in getting to talk to the 200+ unique characters spread across the game. Talk to them after every event change, they all typically have something new to say, which builds up the world so much. The overall tone of the game can feel extremely heavy at times, enough it gave me nightmares a couple nights. But amidst that is a beautiful-if-sad world still full of life fighting against the oppressive moments of the game, helped especially by how adorable and cute Sam is at all times.Don't expect a perfect story. But accept it for what it is, let it surprise, shock, delight, and intrigue you, and I think you'll come away loving this game in spite of what flaws it may have.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: A little over 15 hours into this game and really enjoying it!1.  in this game is absolutely  and can't be overstated. Beautifully rendered environments, buildings, and colors. I'm not usually one who goes for pixel-art games, but there's something truly magical going on here.2. In the same vein,  in Eastward is handled very well.3. Overall, I'm enjoying  in this game. While there's a deeper narrative going on throughout the background of this game, this game could more accurately be defined by its smaller moments. The simple, character focused storylines and character quests ground this game and give it a certain charm that just makes you smile.4. As more of a casual player, I enjoyed  displayed here. It isn't overly burdensome, but still allows for enough interesting mechanics and pathways to keep things fresh. 1. Although I've enjoyed the combat so far, I can't help but feel  to break up some of the narrative sections of the game. As I said, I'm more of a casual gamer myself, but even so, I found the game to drag significantly towards the middle.2. That brings me to my last complaint, which I'll basically sum up as . Eastward is a beautiful, charming game with lots to love as a casual gamer. Even so, I definitely felt the burden of this game's slow pacing. I'm about 15 hours in with no real understanding where this story is going or how long it's going to take to get there. Right now, I'm simply meandering from one low-stakes quest to the next with no real signposting of how this fits into the overall structure of the game. While I've enjoyed the simple, slice-of-life stories told through the calmness of the game, it's becoming increasingly difficult to stay focused within the game with no clear goals set before you. If this was 100% a casual game, this could have worked. However, with the sporadic combat and larger narrative moments sprinkled throughout, you're continually reminded that a larger story is going on in the background. You're just not included on what that story is, how it relates to your presence in the game, and when you will actually get back to that story.Eastward is a joy to see, hear, and play. It harkens back to simpler times in life and puts heavy emphases on the small moments. It's truly something special and I'm glad this game exists with all of the nostalgia it brings. The pacing isn't great and the game struggles to find balance between its overall world story and the intimate moments of the everyday. I think with a slightly tightened up mid-section and perhaps a bit more from the combat/action - this game would have easily risen to one of my all time greats. Overall, definitely worth a play!

_childDocuments_.review: I had such high hopes for this game. It's pretty to look at, but the plot is so ridiculous and the game itself is repetitive and boring. I played for 20 hours and just gave up in Chapter 6. I don't even care about the ending, that's how tiresome this game is. The boss battles require arbitrary strategies are completely opaque. I don't care about the characters one iota because they aren't interesting in the least. Too many idiotic tropes (like the gay Jasper character or the helpless female character Uva who falls in love with the main protagonist after one afternoon--huh?).
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game a lot, but have mixed feelings after finishing it. It starts very strong, but towards the end kinda switches gears, muddying the overall impression.Won't spoil any specific details, but probably don't read further if you prefer to go into games blind.It establishes a world and characters for you to care about. It gives you a mystery to ponder. And a looming threat that's actually unsettling.It does a great job! A lot better than many other games I played.And then it all kinda stops.The game itself continues, though. There are fun bits and pieces, there's something to do, something to see. But it all feels disjointed. Like when you decide to finish some random side-quests in a big RPG before the final mission. But here, you can't opt out.Eventually, there's a buildup to an ending. And it concludes with some impressive scenes!Except, it leaves you in about the same place you were a few chapters back. You learn new information, sure, but it mostly confirms what you already could've guessed. You get some character moments, but they don't contribute much to their development. I'm fine when there are secrets that never get explained. I love to figure stuff out on my own and interpret what's left blank.But I think Eastward just does not resolve its mystery and the character arcs in a way that brings closure. To not end on a downer: I liked the game! What's good here is really good. I loved the characters and the story, aside from the ending bits. The art is gorgeous, the gameplay fun (bar a few one-off mechanics), and the music catchy. Looking forward to the DLC, whatever it will end up being!
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: It's very cute, the gameplay feels fluid but shallow. The game feels so slow - like every where you run is 30% too far, or the "dungeons" are 30% too long without feeling worth my time. I don't know, it may be that the sort of minimalist style is not for me, but I really vibe with the aesthetics and tone, the "game between cut scenes" mechanics just didn't grab me.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so fun! I have been playing for awhile now and I love how detailed and graphics of this game is. There is so much to explore and to find hidden chests and secrets within the maps. I don't usually care for story but this game is great at it! I love the mix of characters and the story I get to experience along with them. Going back to the graphics of this game, the colors used is almost like a grungy, rusty feel to it which I really like because it is so unique. Exploring New Dam City was so incredible, the details put into the buildings and the music really puts it all together. In this city, there are little tales told by a ghost which is a nice eery touch! As for the combat of this game, I love it as well. You get lots of weapon choices with the two characters. I usually use the pan and gun then use Sam to stun which is very useful. The bosses are very cool too since each are very different so you do not get tired of fighting them. You have to figure out how to first defeat each bosses and experiment. It is so satisfying figuring out how to damage the boss!! My favorite part is the puzzle-y parts where you and Sam split off and help each other get through the room!  There is SO MANY unique concepts about this game that I adore so much. I really recommend this game to other players especially if you appreciate nice pixel art and good combat! I love this game so much and I am going to continue my adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: The beginning was strong and then the game got pretty repetitive and had simple puzzles throughout the game's dungeons. The story take a dip as it tries to wrap it up and really ruined my experience. The game is super pretty, the characters are awesome but once you leave an area you never see those characters again, even after you beat the game which is super lame. _childDocuments_.review: !!!TLDR: Wait for sale for this game!!!Got this game when it first came out, finally put in the time to finish it. _childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: its a little rough around the edges, and its no deep narrative, but its a pretty good game. 15-20 hours, a bunch of puzzles, the combat is a bit rough, the cooking mechanic is very hit or miss though you can learn how it works and exploit it for heals. Give it a shot if you have some spare cash, if you like story, you cant go wrong with this.First, the negatives - The pacing is way off. The start is super slow, and it suddenly ramps up to what it should be. The initial bump is after the first area outside the start, though you will quickly become accustomed to it. Most animations, dialogues, and cutscences are not skippable.It can go from feeling very slow to very rushed in terms of story, particularly towards the very end, though I didnt mind this and felt that it added to your momentum and feeling of urgency.The story is a little flat at times, though I will touch on this more in the positives. And now the good - The art direction is GORGEOUS, communicating everything from grungy, cramped tunnels to a wide sprawling forest to more... unconventional spaces. Environment design and character art is stunning, just do not expect the most polished product.The story is a little bit of a toss up, though I think its more good than bad. It can be a bit hard to get invested if you want action and plot right off the bad. But the initial section, getting into a day in John and Sams lives, helps greatly with immersion. You can get an idea of what they, particularly John, feels about their situation. Sure, it may fall off a little between the middle and the late game, but the resolution feels immensely moving. Generally, the story is usually engaging if not weirdly paced at times. Overall - I highly recommend the game. For those who like puzzles, theres plenty, even if they can be tedious. The combat is... rough... but face tanking is a viable strategy if you take a few steps off the linear path to find some health upgrades.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is amazing, the art direction is amazing, the music is amazing, the animations are amazing, the game mechanics are fun, the puzzles and dungeons are fun, and the world is interesting. Alas, this game is also a massive slog with terrible pacing and a convoluted story. And that is super sad! This could have been a great game if it had been a little more streamlined and had tried to be less bombastic.I still recommend it, because beating electric snails with a frying pan feels great. However, do get it on sale, and be prepared to loose all motivation to play about half-way through.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute game. Pixel art is phenomenal. You should buy it even just for the aesthetic. It's very obvious they put a lot of effort into every tiny detail.Story felt a bit flat for me though. It takes too long for story to initate. Also game starts without a backstory explanation. Characters just met already and it feels like you start the game from the middle.Gameplay doesn't have much depth in it too. Just aim and swing. You get to play as the girl after a while and she's a bit more complicated than the other one so thats nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: A Cute and Incredible Game.I will try to explain what this game has made me feel while playing by parts:From "better" to "worst" (in my opinion)   Without a doubt the most charming side of this game. The Pixel Art really shows how beautiful this game can be, I really liked every single place that the game shows you, every city really looks lively and maybe possibly real, of course, the animations and little details are also incredible well done and cute (Sam above everithing else).Also the initial drawed animation is great.  Another well done thing, the music is immersive when needed and catchy at the right times, and never got tired of listening it. I really recommend searching the ost.It is quite probable that I will search the music for my phone.  Personally, I liked the history (a bit cliche in some parts) and loved the main characters until the very end. I'd like to know about how some characters would continue at the end.Lovable personalities you never get tired of.I'll add here that it is good  to speak with the people in the cities through the history, there is a lot and I mean a lot of conversations and many of them interesting that will make seem that the npcs actually live their own lives.  A little bit lacking in some parts but always rewarding the curiosity of the player, even at the cities.On the other hand, incredible complex in some points, that will make most of us leave things behind without us knowing.Classic puzzles.  In my opinion it is what has the most flaws or at least it is what has least interested me.The variability of weapons is good, but , the combat system is... shallow, you try to hit an enemy from a safe position and try to not get touched, and repeat, if you get hit to much, restore HP with the food you cook whenever you want during combat.Truthly I liked more to speak with people at cities and get immersed in the history and its incredible characters.I don't know if it's fair to put a number in this artwork. But If I have to it will be a  maybe even a little more.It is a game that I will surely remember during a lot of time, and I will think that "it was a really good experience and great game"."Earth Born", Great game inside the game by the way.I'm hoping to see more fanarts.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: I was so excited for Eastward, and while I finished out the game, I completely regret the purchase. What you experience in the trailer- amazing artwork, great sound, and an interesting sci-fi world - are all excellent. What you cannot experience from the trailer is that the game play is miserable - sluggish movement & combat, forced backtracking, and slow dialogue text (even when sped up) which make it punishing to explore the story. The combat and movement were so poor, I ended up just running past enemies - which you have no incentive to fight except a few forced segments - and since that's the only challenge in the game, it became a sluggish movie intercut with some boss fights.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really, really liked the first half of this game. The visuals were absolutely stunning throughout the entire game, and the sountrack was consistently great, but a lot of issues start shining halfway through the experience.The gameplay was fine, I liked some of the puzzles, but it feels like it came down to clicking faster than the enemy. Later in the game you'll need to deflect projectiles for some, but for some reason there's always a delay when hitting with the pan, so it always felt really clunky and badly timed???As for the story - they set it up with a cast of very interesting and colorful characters and locations that, after moving "past" them in the story, you just don't ever see again. You can't return to past areas to get the secrets you missed, you cant talk to them and see how theyre doing, it feels like wasted potential or like the devs were rushed to get the game out. Even in the game's ending, you get a message that effectively says  without actually seeing any of the characters the game spent 5 hours each fleshing out.The entire second half of the story is horribly paced, because it feels like they decided to cram 80% of the story into the last 50% of the game -- up until that point you got snippets of things happening throughout the first half, but most of it was entirely unrelated scenes of fun stuff. Don't get me wrong, this was still very, very enjoyable, but it made cramming 80% of the story into the last half feel horribly rushed and awfully paced -- so much so that it was hard to follow along and actually understand what was happening for this half.The game's got a lot of dark undertones and they bring a lot of interesting ideas to the table when hinting at everything when the game starts getting into its later chapters, but then when it actually comes time to address and pull the tarp off, they hardly actually show anything of importance or actually explore the concepts theyd been hinting at throughout the entire game. I wanted to SEE , but the game only lightly touches on any of it.The ending was just entirely unsatisfying. Without going into too much detail, , again without actually SEEING any of the characters the game spent 20 hours having you get to know up until that point. No going back and talking to them or hunting for secrets, it does what zelda does and saves right before the final scenes, the only difference is that zelda doesn't have a "point of no return" whereas eastward has you constantly moving past characters you're fated to just never, ever see again. The amount of characters (not including the protagonists) you see past the "final battle" is, when the game easily had 10 to 20 memorable characters I was left wanting to hear from after the events of the ending.And it sucks, i thoroughly enjoyed the first half and the visuals never let up in how beautiful they are, every place felt unique and wonderful, but unfortunately i can't recommend this game if you're looking for a good story (or any sort of complex gameplay, for that matter).If they make a sequel in the same universe that focuses on different characters, play this one for prior knowledge. Otherwise, I was left feeling really unsatisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable Zelda-like with a gorgeous artstyle and really amazing soundtrack. Strong Recommend if you enjoy quirky games with enjoyable characters. The game nosedives on the pacing a bit around chapter 3 but it picks itself up very quick a couple chapters after that. Also comes with a really addicting Roguelike that you can play along your journey, still have to get the true ending on that as its very RNG based with the skills of your party. Overall a really enjoyable relaxing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: Eastward has great art, adorable characters, and a charming sense of humor. Gameplay is solid, and the character switching is smooth and makes for interesting and varied challenges.However, it is bogged down by its balance of gameplay and story. There are LONG stretches of wandering around town talking to people and derpy little sidequests like "go to the bar and get drunk while Sam is at school".I thought I would love this game on paper, but in practice, I'm finding it frustrating. 15 minutes of going to a new town, meeting all the characters in the town, and dealing with a very forced love story has seriously bogged down my enthusiasm.If you love pixel art and charming story, play this game. If you love Zelda-style gameplay, beware! There is a lot of filler in between dungeons.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: The world's most beautiful visual novel.  For every 1 minute of gameplay, there are 3-5 minutes of extremely boring dialog.  Why say something in 2 sentences, when 44 speech bubbles would suffice?  The difficulty only cycles between boringly easy and obnoxiously hard, with half of the enemies dying in 3 hits or literally 20 hits.  Combine that with some really boring childish quests: "make dinner for a mob boss, but only using the yummiest berries in the land!" and I just couldn't be bothered to even finish this one.Damn pretty though.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely adventure.  I recommend if you enjoy good adventures with interesting stories.  If you aren't sure about it, wait for a sale, but I really enjoyed my time with the game.  Great music, lovely pixel art, an interesting story with a lot of room for interpretation and a really interesting world.  Hope to see a sequel just so I can see more of the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: While I don't think I'm near completing this game yet (at least I hope not) I have so many upsides to it so far I feel it's worth a review at my 7 hours. The art style is by far a huge thumbs up, I was invested in this game long before there was any idea of what it would release. In fact I don't think I would've picked up this game if it didn't have the art style it does. For me it's fun, inviting, cozy, and as an artist it's also inspiring.The story has kept my interest and while I honestly didn't get into this game for story I'm quite pleased with it so far. It's not fantastic but I hope it maintains interest as I continue through the game and I always fear the ending decisions so if things turn around in the end I'll update my review!The combat is really pleasant in my opinion, as I said before this is not a game I normally pick up because I don't usually love the feeling of combat. That's probably just my experience with these types of games, they aren't bad but just not something I got into. This one hasn't disappointed me or turned me off from wanting to continue which is a plus side for me.All in all I think this game deserves a lot of props for its art style and overall vibe of the game, their artists do not go unnoticed. It's absolutely one of my favorite looking games.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very, very text heavy. I really should've read the reviews before purchasing. I'm 11 hours in and feel like I've gone nowhere. I think I've been through two boss fights, which were very easy and predictable. It is very clear that this game is more about the story than the gameplay. The puzzles and combat have been incredibly simple so far. I wouldn't really say this is a visual novel, but it's pretty close to it. The dialogue has been very tedious at times. I'm recommending just because the game is visually stunning.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I like any aspect of this game. The story, the aesthetics, the characters, the story, the soundwork.It's just boring. Characters who are unlikeable, a story that honestly doesn't seem to really go anywhere quickly, tepid Zelda-esque gameplay without the cleverness or sense of progression. If you're into the aesthetics and don't have high standards it's probably worth a go, but I'm goijg to have to grit my teeth I think.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: this game. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game it absolutely outstanding. the writing is great, the characters are charming and actually have personality in the little interactions you have with anyone, the soundtrack pleasing and always sets in the right atmosphere, and the fights always progress and have somewhat of a difficulty to them. it reminds me so much of the mother series and it brings me so much joy that a story game like this can be so enjoyable to play. seeing these two characters adventure throughout the undergrounds and see them go through ups and downs and make it through makes me so happy. john being silent but still portraying emotions was nice, and sam being the joy bubble she is lightened up every room. the ending, nearly made me cry. after finishing this game and seeing nearly everything, it has become one of my favorite games of all time.thank you pixpil and chucklefish for releasing this amazing game that i'll never ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ forget. 10/10 <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, and so underrated. I stumbled upon it last year and had never heard of it. But i am so glad i played it; the pixel art style is amazing and detailed, the story is fantastic with well thought dialog that makes the game surprisingly deep, and the gameplay is fun and doesn't get old. If you're unsure about this game, just play the prologue and you'll fall in love instantly

_childDocuments_.review: Eastward is very Earthbound in its art, but also very much its own thing and it looks great. I've had a fun time playing Eastward, my only gripe is that one or two missions are drawn out, maybe five minutes longer than they should have been, other than that I've had a really fun 30+ hours. _childDocuments_.review: Blown away by how good this game was. I went into it expecting a good indie title, instead I got an AMAZING indie game. I would recommend this game to everyone who loves good story, clever combat, and well thought-out puzzles that were at times challenging, but never too challenging. I found myself exploring and talking to everyone I could to get all the dialogue and hidden stories because they were so satisfying to complete, ranging from silly to so sweet.10/10 I loved this game!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: It's almost as if they had all those great concept arts and pixel-dioramas and didn't know what to do with it.In stark contrast to the strong visuals the shallow gameplay and pacing was pretty disappointing.There are a lot of fillers and backtracking. And as beautiful as the game is: It's all just scenery without any real interaction.This makes it somehow even more lifeless. The first two hours deliver a very good impression of what to expect from the rest of the game. So, if it doesn't catch you there, then it surely won't later. This is one of the cases i would wish for an option between "yes" or "no". But like this i unfortunately cannot recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a lot for its art style, music, and 2D zelda-esque gameplay. My only criticism is with the story.The story was interesting, and I enjoyed it, but I can't help but feel I missed something with the story. I found myself fast forwarding through dialogue frequently as it sometimes feels like it drags on a little too long. To be fair, I think this was a me problem, not the writers. I felt like there was almost too big a cast of characters and it left me feeling confused and not really connected to any non-player characters at all.However, the overall story and the ending left me feeling satisfied. The final level and boss battle was really cool and memorable. Overall, I definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: I typically don't play pixel art games but this game caught my eye.The art, animations and story were so expressive and smooth. It was something I would never have expected from a pixel art game. It blew me away. You can tell how much love, time and thought the devs put into this game. Hidden stories/puzzles/areas that you only find if you explore the environment they created. Apart from the art, the game does a great way of showing you through little things in the background how to solve puzzles instead of telling you. A great experience for solving puzzles, relaxing yet satisfying.The only downside is the fighting/ gameplay. At times it gets repetitive and slow but I would understand since they focused so much work on the graphical aspects. Solid 8.5/10 game for me!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but the ungodly amount of dull and unskipable dialogue/cutscenes, paired with the clunky animation-locking combat system have made it feel like a chore so far. _childDocuments_.review: Wow.I've just finished my first of likely many playthroughs of this, and let me say it was a beautiful experience from start to finish. I can't overstate how gorgeous Eastward's graphics, music, and characters are. Yes, the story is often a bit hard to follow, but this is definitely a game worth playing. I'd recommend to just about anyone looking for a fun, emotional experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is undoubtedly the worst game I've ever read."Gameplay":Eastward isn't a game that you play, rather it is a series of random dialogues with irrelevant characters interspersed with shallow puzzles and sluggish combat sections. Over the course of five hours I'd say there were a total of 6 sections where the game actually allows you to do more than loot random crates and talk to people.Each of these are roughly 15 minutes of awful puzzles designed for room temp IQ morons, and enemies that you'd have to try to die to. The game could use more lootable crates to distract me from the lack of things to do, since I searched and found a total of 14 or so boxes to loot over the course of five hours. Switching between characters is fun, but it is almost entirely unnecessary apart from solving puzzles. Cooking is nice, but the game is far too easy for you to need to eat all that often and basically boils down to: Choose ingredients, play the slot machine, and enjoy the cooking music. Didn't play that much of the RPG within the game but from what I did, it was okay. Intentionally awful writing and easy gameplay. There are far too many puzzles with not enough mechanical depth to really challenge players, but they are a nice break from the dialogue.Combat:I genuinely liked the first ten minutes of combat. The simple enemies, lack of threat or complexity, and general clunkiness were tolerable. However, it quickly dawned on me that there was nothing to the combat beyond spamming the light attack to stunlock enemies. The heavy attack is a botched idea, since it requires you to first throw a light attack and then hold down the button to perform. There were a total of three "bosses", which to be honest I liked quite a bit. The first two are pretty fun, but the third one is just kinda there and gone. They ranged from pitifully easy to mechanically frustating, but it was at least something to do other than listen to people tell me what random minigame I'd be doing that day.Story:The plot of this game is unironically brilliant, 10/10. Things just seem to happen with little rhyme or reason, characters come and go, and it is simultaneously rushed and far too slow. Most of the time you're just running around doing random things for people until the plot decides to actually happen for little to no reason.You're constantly being interrupted so that you can listen to entirely unrelated people talk about things that have no bearing on the actual plot. Chapter 2 is the worst example I've encountered thus far with a whole scene of character growth for a character we just met, someone who will die two scenes later off-screen. The game tries to make me care about the second town so it can set up a tragic backstory, but it seems like John and I are in agreement in not giving a flying ♥♥♥♥ about it. On that note, John being a silent protagonist that literally ignores the obviously marked for death love interest was pretty kino, and I found that to be pretty funny. Though I doubt that was intentional in the slightest. Most characters are soulless beyond being "Oh So Quirky", and completely one note.Sam is awful, just awful. She is the designated mouthpiece for John since he refuses to engage with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of others. As a result, most of the abhorrent dialogue comes from her or is instigated by her, and I just can't forgive that. Other than that she's generically childlike in all the worst ways.TLDR;Shallow gameplay, awful story, and barely even a game at all.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 - great story, tarnished by bad combat and very strict linearity Grand narrative with wholesome characters. The story is the main winner here, it’s a (very strict) linear game, and that can be a good and a bad thing. It’s a great thing if you are looking to enjoy a story and find a secret or two along the way. It’s a bad thing when you want to complete the game 100% as it is extremely easy to miss stuff and get locked from areas because you forgot to check every corner after every stage of every single quest just in case you can now go there and have all the necessary tools. If you don’t, you will probably miss out on a lot of stuff – including abilities for the main character ?! I enjoyed the story; it was a great ride, and the ending – spoiled only by the unresponsive controls and sluggish character movement – was phenomenal. Yes, the combat is a weird thing in this game; it’s very easy in all but the final stage of the game, where the sluggishness and unresponsiveness become sadly apparent as you must act quickly and precisely. Overall, I say I enjoyed the game and were I not locked out from areas I knew I missed but just could not get to because some guard told me to…. I would bum it up to 9/10 (the combat still sucks mechanically – regardless of the very easy difficulty).

_childDocuments_.review: GREAT game. Fantastic visuals, I'm usually a little dubious about pixel art, but this game has BEAUTIFULLY done art and animations. It even handles non-pixel visuals interacting with the pixel sprites in a way that looks good, which is rare for me to see in games. The music is out of this world, can't even say much about it. The gameplay is, very unfortunately, honestly just serviceable. It's basically a top-down beat-em-up with occasional puzzles that are usually really easy. The characters are adorably quirky with the earthbound style the art is obviously channeling. The story is good, made me tear up a bit at the end (though I am a bit of a sap and quick to cry at media). MOST IMPORTANTLY, there's a game-within-a-game that's a roguelike jrpg with Gameboy graphics that completely ensorcelled me. You can even spend in-game currency to buy gachapon balls that have effects for the game-within-the-game.ANYWAYS THIS GAME IS GOOD!! GET IT!!

_childDocuments_.review: Too much dialogue with no option to skip. One of the biggest design mistakes in a video game is to take away the player's ability to move and interact by forcing them to sit through dialogue, and not at least offer them the chance to skip ahead. It's supposed to be a video GAME not an interactive story.After playing for a few more days, somewhere in Chapter 3, I'm abandoning my playthrough. I found the combat very lacking. It's comparable to 2D zelda, but much worse. You have no movement options beyond WASD, and you're not small like Link, you're big and slow, can't get out of the way, and there's 2 of you who both can get hit. You don't have the reach to zone enemies out, you don't get pushed back far enough to escape an enemy in your face. You can heal with cooking, but you can't farm ingredients. Overall, the combat feels unfair.Exploration is also not well curated. A few times, I found myself either having no where to explore, or the places I did explore had nothing but dead ends, I just wasn't supposed to go that way yet, so why was it even open to me?The art is pretty, animations are great. That's all the praise I can think of.I find it sad that they invoke the influences of so many great games but don't seem to follow their examples in any way.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr This game is just very good. Beautiful artstyle, good OSTs, and a story that was interesting to follow throughout the game.Disclaimer: This review might contain spoilers.The story here isn't complicated. It has no deep meaning in it. It's just simple, but it was decent. It's decent enough for it to be interesting to read. It's enough to make me smile from good moments, it's enough to make me sad from bad moments. As I said before, it's just decent, and that's all. The most important part about this game's story is that the ending isn't something not ordinary. it's very predictable but just ideally for this type of games. People actually might want to see something more complicated, but I didn't need anything other than the one we got in the actual game. Sam and John are very different characters in terms of how they behave. While John is always silent and his whole appearance shows you that he's just a simple man and hard worker, Sam is a very cheerful and inquisitive girl who's ready to help everyone with anything they want. I really liked how they were just like family even with their differences, even though a lot of stories use this idea about the difference of heroes. The gameplay here is just your average Zelda-like game. Heroes have to go through enemies to get to the next location. Have to complete puzzles to continue the story or unlock any extra goodies. There is nothing special about combat, but I don't think that it should be like in souls-like games (no jokes, I've seen people complaining about how simple the combat system was here and I honestly don't know if they want a really complicated system with blocks and rolls or they just complain about everything. I personally don't think blocks should exist in this game, since Sam can just stun enemies).There're 8 bosses (one for each chapter), they're good in terms of mechanics and artstyle, but they for sure are not hard to beat, this game becomes very simple once you get something besides your lovely pan to beat monsters. Even though I liked bosses, I'd like to mention only one boss here. Not even boss, but mini-boss - Isabel. The fight wasn't difficult, but it was the most unique of all fights. You had to understand the actual rhythm of her attacks in order to counter them. Almost like rhythm games lmao.The last thing I wanted to mention is Eastward's style and its beautiful OSTs. Artstyle of this game is very unique compared to many pixel games. While some locations don't stand out with something unique, they just look beautiful. Other locations are striking in with its beauty and details of these large cities and small places. OSTs in this game are insanely good. It complements the atmosphere by showing the mood of the characters or the mood of the locations in which you are. Complements certain dynamic situations or simply doesn't let you get bored while running from one point to another.Little things like cooking or Earthborn are just nice additions to this game. While cooking is almost necessary to do in order to be prepared to fight, Earthborn is just a JRPG "minigame" that you can play in your free time. Obviously, there were some not-that-good things about this game, such as getting a little bit boring in some chapters because they force you to go through an insane amount of fighting in order to continue the story or specific enemies who, for me, weren't really easy to fight against because I'm just simply dumb. Some people really complain about the amount of talking here (even compared Eastward to some visual novels lmao), but for me, it's just one of the pros. As a person who don't play games a lot and really enjoyed Eastward, I'd rate it 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Eastward is a beautiful looking game. It has a charming story and charming characters. With a main duo you will cheer for. The music suits the game. It fits perfectly actually. It really gives you a true feeling of what type of world this is. The combat is a bit hit or miss at times. It can get you a bit frustrated but most of the time it works real well. With John being the one with his legendary pan and several other weapons. While Sam has her magic they make a great team and gives you plenty of ways to defeat the enemy. With this said the games biggest flaw is phasing. Sometimes it feel that some stuff didn't need to be there. or they feel really slow and frustrating. at the end of it Eastward is a wonderful game with a great story most if not all should experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a few mixed feelings about Eastward but overall I feel like the positives outweigh the negatives.Positives:-John and Sam make for an adorable team. John's silent protagonist angle works really well coincided with Sam's childlike wonder and curiosity. They have strangely good chemistry despite John never saying a word.-Art and music direction is beautiful. Some really well done sprite work and the tracks fit all the moods really well.-Combat feels satisfying, thought a little simple.-The games highs hit really hard. The emotional beats come through quite nicely.-Some clever and well written dialogue.-Once the main cast is established they have solid moments.-I personally really like the ending. Leaves things a little more open ended than they could have been but in a way that still feels satisfying to the journey.Negatives:-Game has some definite pacing issues. Some chapters feel like they needed more exploration and others feel like they drag.-Some of the side characters fall a little flat and the ones that are developed well wind up not getting used very much.-The story runs in circles just a little, and takes too long to find its footing. If you're looking for a more story centered RPG, you'll probably enjoy Eastward. There tends to not be a lot of combat so if you're looking for something a little more action packed, you won't find it here. I really hope the devs continue to make games though, because I think if they can push past some of the issues here then they'll have something truly wonderful to share.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased Eastward in December 2021 and played it in March 2022. After beating the game in January of 2023, I’m proud of what it offered me each time I played it. The art style inside and outside the game is fun and comforting, adding flair and detail to character and setting designs. John and Sam are a delight to play, and I never questioned why John was mute because it never became a clear-cut issue. Every character John and Sam meet has neat quirks because you spend entire chapters alongside them. That’s without mentioning the dark and foreboding MIASMA enveloping everything the game’s setting contains. The empty black space adds tension to each chapter after exploring the game’s world and NPCs. The game’s antagonist, Mother, drives many of the game’s bosses to try and stop you, culminating with Mother fighting John as the final boss.As for Eastward’s combat and puzzles, some feel too difficult, whereas others feel too easy. The inconsistency varies depending on the player’s abilities, both with a controller or keyboard and Sam and John’s abilities and weapons. The combat mechanics uses John’s arsenal of a frying pan, a gun, a flamethrower, a cog shooter, and three types of bombs to deal damage and Sam’s small but vital arsenal of telepathy to stop enemies and activate other puzzle elements. However, the puzzles and bosses add a challenge regardless of skill level. It’s especially the case towards the end of the game, bar the final boss if you stock up on food beforehand. There are also a few mini-games to add to the game’s experience. Firstly, it has Earth Born, an entire JRPG inside the game. Secondly, there’s cooking, done via a combination of ingredients, which changes the recipe, and slots, which boosts the health given by the food. It gets a bit tedious after 20+ hours of making more food, but it’s a quaint negative to the experience.However, Eastward could have been so much bolder than it is. Its focus on the MIASMA and Mother could be more present than it was, especially in the first couple chapters. The dynamic between Isabel and Alva could have the same treatment, as their relationship hints at being more romantic, but the game never goes further. The game has more potential than it offers, but it doesn’t mean it’s a waste. I hope the developers have a second crack at something similar to their first outing because streamlining aspects of the story will heighten the experience and create a beautiful adventure. Not everyone will love this game as I do, but that’s a pitfall I’m willing to live with for a story filled with companionship and the determination to deny the end of the world.

_childDocuments_.review: It's so pretty, but I couldn't bother to finish it. Like so many other indie games, Eastward is an amazing labor of love that suffered from deep ambition cuts and a lack of undefinable polish. The result is a very unique Love Letter to classic pixel adventure games. The game makes constant reference to Nintendo's Earthbound (Mother 2) as an inspiration, but it's closer to Illusion of Gaia in execution - long stretches of stilted combat adventuring and light puzzle solving punctuated by towns filled with painfully dull dialogue. The charming artwork and animation pulled me most of the way through the game, but the lack of story payoff and an increase in combat clunkiness over meaningful progression just made the slog unbearable. "Monkollywood" was the nail in the coffin of my interest. I did not experience what some have described as character progression, just a lot of static, two dimensional stock characters talking way too much about banal things, without the ability to speed up the text scroll. This post-post-apocalyptic world deserves more time to develop and better combat feel. I look forward to seeing what this team can do with more time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Eastward is a game that's trying to be too many things at once. A dark and gritty post-apocalyptic sci-fi narrative; a love-letter to 8 and 16-bit JRPGs; a tough dungeon-crawler with full-action combat and puzzle-solving; a fun adventure with goofy, lovable characters; the journey of a stoic man and his cheery, optimistic daughter.Parts of it really work, like the artstyle, world, and characters. Others really don't. The story and tone feel whiplash-inducing at times, telling a tale I think is far darker than necessary (given the endearing characters and goofy moments), and the game's combat system is honestly very poor. The plot is revealed piece-meal, dragged along by vague dialogue and a veneer of mystery, that ultimately never lives up to its full potential.With that said, the game is extremely beautiful, the characters are super memorable, and the soundtrack is outstanding; and by buying it, you're supporting a type of game that really doesn't get made much anymore. To me it's worth it for those things alone, but it certainly isn't the greatest game I've played.

_childDocuments_.review: I have found myself not only enjoying, but obsessing over this game. Eastward has an adorable art style, charming music, colourful characters, and a memorable story. Characters don't address Sam's abilities, the in-game RPG Earth Born barely gets addressed aside from the first chapter, up until the seventh chapter(though you can play it throughout the game in various areas), and the save point refrigerators don't seem to have real meaning behind they're cryptic messages(though I do adore them, regardless.) In the end, after 30 hours(and nearly completing the game, though I will admit I haven't yet), I can safely say that this game has brought me 30 hours of joy, exploration, puzzles, fighting, and love for a new game. Easily worth the purchase!Edit: I finished and now I want to cry, what a lovely game.Bonus edit: I got an Eastward tattoo. I recently purchased the Octopia DLC and... my goodness. It has reignited my love for this game in an entirely new way. The DLC doesn't just add something to the game, it's an entirely separate game! It's the perfect way to wind down, and emotionally recover from the story of Eastward. I genuinely cannot recommend this game enough to anyone. Please, if you're even considering it, get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Eastward is a frustrating game because on one hand I want to fully endorse it but it is not without its problems. Combat is a knock off of past 2D Zelda games but lacking plenty of tweaks that would otherwise make the whole ordeal feel less clunky. No dodge roll, but enemies can dodge you, you're also forced to stand still until a swing animation completely finishes. Doesn't help that for 95% for the enemies deal damage on touch and all of your fry pan attacks edge you forward so you'll hit them but you're also going to take damage. All this leads to is you relying heavily on health items.Healing is an issue, unlike Zelda which regularly drops hearts for you, Eastward very rarely drops a heart pick up which means you'll need to rely on cooking. Cooking is a tedious affair. Toss 3 random ingredients into the pan plus a seasoning and then wait for the roulette mini game to pop up and run for you. The more symbols of the same kind you line up will add extra benefits. This is all well and good but as the game gets on with it, cooking will take up more and more time. Every time you cook up a new recipe you'll be forced to watch what is essentially the same animation to completion. But some of the dishes can also heal as low as 2 or 3 hearts and when you're near the end of the game and sporting a health bar of like 18 hearts, it becomes incredibly tedious to heal. Temporary hearts also have a weird issue, if you already have 3 temp hearts and then eat a dish that would give you 2 temp hearts, it doesn't add to your pool of temp hearts, they just get lost in the 3 you currently have. Which can be frustrating when some of the dished exclusively give you temp hearts.I also found the game to overwhelmingly stingy with ingredients. You'll be stuck with a small selection from whichever town you're currently in, so bad that when I unlocked the recipe for a Hamburger and was given the side task of making one for a villager, I literally couldn't because one necessary ingredient was impossible to find. Eastward ultimately suffered from borderline enforcing a slow and steady pace, rather than letting the player have any kind of choice in the matter. So many things feel slow and make the 23 hours I poured into it feel a bit of a slog. The story is interesting and the characters help make the whole thing worthwhile though. It cannot be understated that the presentation of Eastward is utterly fantastic. Animations are gorgeous and pixel art feels so inspired and layered giving a lot of depth to the world. I would personally complain about the length and frequency of the cutscenes you have to sit through but that's more of a subjective stand point. They don't entirely waste your time though, the world building is fun and getting to meet such a fun line up of characters is a good time. Overall this is a solid 7/10 experienceI hope Pixpil can learn from their combat missteps and make an overall smoother experience in their next game, but for now, Eastward is a decent title from a promising studio.

_childDocuments_.review: “John, what are you waiting for? -Let’s go!”I'm not a big fan of reviewing things, but this one's special. -"Eastward" is a game that takes you on a journey. It's destination? -That's for you to find out, within environments that are and intricately crafted, characters that are teeming with uniqueness, and scenarios that you can immerse yourself in.From the very start of the game what stands out the most is its atmosphere. -Dark, rustic, and desolate. -Yet, the characters which lived in it bestowed it with the warmth, and the color it needed to feel inviting. The environments, and the setting perfectly captures story set in a post-apocalyptic world where humanity is on its last legs. -And as the journey progresses, you come across various other locations which adds stark contrast to where you start the game originally, all the while maintaining the overall atmosphere of it. In addition to that, the attention to detail that you find in each of these environments is simply gorgeous. From the depths of the earth where scant light filters in, to the fields that are bathed in soft afternoon sunlight, “Eastward” has its world crafted masterfully.When it comes to the characters, the game goes vivid. You find a set of characters that stands out under their own spotlights. Unique, vibrant, and exciting. -From cowards that uses others as an excuse to save themselves, to lovers who wish their love becomes true, to comedians that wants nothing but the best in life, to heroes that put others before themselves, “Eastward’s” characters go above and beyond to add that “light” and “life” that its world lacks. Every character who comes into contact with John and Sam on their journey adds their own flavor to it. Be it an NPC of the main quest, a simple bystander that shares tidbits of their life, the conversations are crafted in a way that makes you – the player – feel a part of their world.The story of “Eastward” stands out as one of the best in its own right. The journey of John and Sam is rich with emotion as they come across various situations, and characters of the world. The game is brimming with moments that are simple happiness, moments of solemnity and calmness, and of course moments of sorrow and anguish. -And they come together in perfect balance as John and Sam makes their way through the world of “Eastward” making it stand out on its own. Without giving any spoilers, in each part of the world of “Eastward” that John and Sam travels to, brings to them their own set of “troubles” (To which Sam dives headfirst with her bright and cheerful nature, and John simply follows her.). With a mystery element that simply gets you craving to find out what happens next, “Eastward” draws you in to its world filled with adventure, and paired with it, danger.The gameplay of “Eastward” is very smooth with little to no rough edges. Clearly this game is meant to be enjoyed on a controller, but keyboard and mouse works just fine as well. The weapons in game were simply brilliant, using skill to use them in combat and in puzzles -The puzzle system of the game is crafted to perfection, with just the right amount of critical thinking factor put in to keep you on edge. -Finally, the boss fights were often exciting, providing greater sense of accomplishment, and euphoria upon triumph.Overall “Eastward” was a game that I will remember a long time. -Not simply as a “game” that I played, but as a “journey” I took together with John and Sam to find out the wonders of its world. -And on that journey I found so much  more than I ever hoped for.

_childDocuments_.review: Played from – to: (2022-01-18 – 2022-02-07) – PC controller.‣ 10/10 – It will all pan out in the end.‣ Game Audio / Soundtrack - 10/10‣ Graphics – 10/10‣ Atmosphere – 10/10‣ Main Story / Characters – 10/10‣ Side Activities / Exploration – 10/10‣ AI – 9/10‣ Ragdolls / Physics – 10/10‣ Movement – 8/10‣ Combat – 8/10‣ Final notes: It is rare for a game to have so many characters and make them feel unique and interesting. However, I am glad to announce that Eastward nailed it. Well maybe not the monkeys, but anyone else you meet will be great. They have their unique motivations, back stories, and fantastic visual design. Eastward shines in its artwork and carefully crafted facial animations and more. The journey I took with this game was long and very interesting. I won’t deny the story did leave me confused at times, especially when the time concept got introduced, but overall, it was great and really felt outstanding in the pile of 2021 games that I have played. Honestly, as you play the game you see how much love and care the developers put into this. I got nothing but praise for this apart from a few nitpicks here and there. The soundtrack is always fitting and memorable, beautiful even. Food cooking reminded me of Zelda but had its own use and we will leave it at that. My only complaint is the combat. Even if it is a big part of the game, something more puzzle like would’ve suited it more. The last few boss fights really showed how a more pattern-based combat could’ve been more enjoyable even if repetitive. I would have rather had pattern-based combat of some sorts than a one move-based combat. Yes, you have a nice arsenal of tools at your disposal, but in the end it all comes down to John swinging his pan in the same motion repeatedly. In any case, the nice balance between puzzle solving, fighting, and exploring made combat a nice change of pace and the boss fights were great that I am willing to accept the version we have even if I would have loved a dodge button. Overall Eastward is a very interesting game, at first, I had no idea what I had gotten my self into, but the more I played it the more invested I got. At times it felt like a children’s story and at times it rivaled the seriousness of games like God of War.

_childDocuments_.review: I should preempt this review with the fact that I usually like these types of games. Before anyone jumps my gun at the Earthbound comparison, I am not the first to make this. Literally, every piece of media coverage and YouTuber that’s picked the game up has called it an “Earthbound-inspired” game. There’s literally an optional half-Earthbound parody called Earthborn you can play. The influences Earthbound has had on Eastward aren’t the slightest bit subtle and I think it comes at the game’s detriment. Something that is going to be extremely prevalent in my writing on this game is that I don’t think Eastward has its own identity. Every part of Eastward plays things so extraordinarily safe and it still falls flat.Let’s lead with the gameplay because it’s the only thing it tries to do to distance itself from its obvious influence, except it takes too much from its other source of inspiration. It plays exactly as if Link’s Awakening had the screen limitation cut out. This wouldn’t normally be a bad thing since not many games play like LA, but Eastward doesn’t experiment that much with this. Aside from a greater focus on ranged weapons. The frying pan is just a reskinned sword. Weapon variety is very limited with access to more weapons being restricted by chapter unlocks. Weapon upgrades are so rare and insignificant to the point that I stopped seeking them out, which didn’t exactly fix the situation either. Enemy variety is fairly small and I think the number of bosses surpasses them. They were all laughably easy considering the frying pan stun locks some of them and the rest you can just spam bullets into. The greatest step with experimentation stems from the Mario & Luigi style partner swapping with silent protagonist John and the actual character on the cover art, Sam. This mechanic is used for some rather slow and simple, but inoffensive puzzle design. There were probably upwards of a hundred puzzles but not one stuck with me. Whack a bomb across the ledge. Pull this switch so John can pass and then pull this one so Sam can follow in pursuit. Spam your energy balls with Sam. I never had to really stop and think about a puzzle. And while it’s much worse for a puzzle to force you to look up a solution, I think it’s a huge problem when both your combat and puzzles are so tediously simple.But oh my god, the writing is easily the most irritating part of Eastward. Most RPGs have fun and interesting scenarios to put you in. Eastward just tries to think of the most entertaining time-waster to keep you occupied until they have to actually continue with the plot. The first chapter of the game starts out fairly interesting. You’re plopped into a town built into an underground subway system with a corrupt mayor that banishes anyone he doesn’t like to the surface. Lots of questions get put into place like: Why is everyone living in a subway system? Why is the surface so scary? The story continues into the second chapter immediately after you’re banished to the terrifying surface. You find a town and then Sam does the dumbest possible action ever and faces zero consequences for it because she conveniently doesn’t remember it. Mild spoilers, but lots of people die! Where do you think the story goes after this point? If you guessed we spend half the game making several meals for a mob boss because of a random bet with no actual established risks, you would be right. Chapter 3 is the definition of filler and it doesn’t get much better with pacing until the final few areas of the game. The main two villains don’t offer much in threat factor or even entertainment. Solomon is the one you’ll primarily be encountering and he’s played off as a joke half the time before becoming an actual problem out of nowhere. The only comedic moment that got me feels unintentional as it involves a one-sided romance story with a silent protagonist that shows zero reciprocation. Several story points and character motivations are very confusing as well. It got to the point where I thought it was just a me issue, but the wiki pages for this game are so barren and discussion on the plot is so divided that I realized it was just how the game was written. I cannot stress this enough, Eastward’s plot is boring at best and frustrating at worst. It doesn’t help that a lot of the tropes I personally despise are very common.The soundtrack is another one of Eastward’s weakpoints. It’s generally rare that I can’t find a single highlight in the OST for a game, let alone for an RPG. I think my problem with Eastward’s music is how generic it sounds combined with how small it feels when compared to the actual size of the game. Describing what makes something generic is rather difficult, but every musical piece sounds like something I’ve heard before. The battle music sounds like it could be pasted into any other game. The suspenseful encounter music is the exact same. It’s the exact same for every other song. Especially when something joyous happens and the happy song plays. That song gets spammed to oblivion throughout the dialogue dumps. I personally feel that Eastward lacks an identity in its soundtrack and I will never be listening to it again.The art is something I feel conflicted on as well. It’s mainly the character sprites, the actual background environments look gorgeous. Eastward has a bunch of unique locations that are beautifully put together. I mentioned earlier there’s a town built into an old subway station, but there’s also one built entirely into a singular train! While not nearly as absurd, a city being built entirely on and around a dam with there being class segregation for how high up you live was another neat place. And the human factories were probably the most off-putting locations I’ve seen. The story really wasted the unsettling nature of seeing hundreds of test-tube people tended to by the emotionless breeder bots in those segments. The pixel art for the backgrounds is absolutely stellar and I really like how they incorporate semi-realistic lighting into it. I cannot say the same about how people look in this game. I feel as though too much detail was put into their design. Several characters show off every pore, blemish, wrinkle, foundation, etc. shown off in their sprite. Luckily John and Sam themselves look fine, but there was one moment when Sam opened her mouth really wide that looked really off-putting to me. Characters are also overtly bouncy with their idle animations which isn’t too much of an issue by itself. It’s when that bounciness translates to a lot of the female characters having somewhat exaggerated breast jiggling that it feels distasteful. Performance is something that I can praise Eastward for at least. The game never crashed and there wasn’t a single game-breaking bug. The worst offender I encountered for bugs was some NPCs ignoring the collision of objects during cutscenes, as it appears that their pathing doesn’t always factor in the environment. There were no other technical or visual errors that occurred outside of this. I feel as though this is important to stress as more and more releases are forgetting about the importance of stability. Despite my many blatant problems with Eastward, it is still a polished and complete game. I’ve played worse games, but I’ve also played much better games. I cannot recommend Eastward because it doesn’t stand out to me. There was some optional content that I skipped out on as previously mentioned, but I have no desire to check it out currently.

_childDocuments_.review: What sold it is the finely polished pixel art, specially great sceneries and buildings; dungeons and characters look fine at a lesser extent.; But you won't enjoy the moody and relaxing art so much as you'll be constantly bashing the A button to skip long unnecessary dialogues on the cities, or still bashing the same button over and over to kill most enemies in this tedious and simplistic battle system. A solid part of the game is making the character walk at a predetermined speed (slow) through the same scenarios over and over in search for some trivial object or character to end some tedious sidestory (I won't consider these sidequests, as you can't opt out of any of those even as most of them aren't directly related to the main quest).Soundtrack is nice, but what plays in the background almost all the time is the same - an 8-bit soundtrack that repeats itself for hours.With this completely linear story there are no choices that could change the plot in the slightest, so what's the point of reading all the excessive dialogue lines? There's plenty of save points - all of them useless, as every scenery is an autosaved checkpoint. Also there's an useless subway/train - it's there but you'll choose to use it only when the story calls for it, and usually won't have (and won't want) to get back to any point you already have been to.Surprisingly your character will find some arcade machines with an enjoyable minigame inspired by the first Zelda games.Bottom line: If you like long tedious storylines interrupted by several pointless sidestories in a game where you can't make any meaningful choices (neither in combat style, in character development or on the storyline), this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Eastward

_childDocuments_.review: The best parts of this game are the art style and the music. Seriously, this music is excellent on its own, Hyperduck Soundworks can do no wrong as far as I'm concerned.The side characters were funny and most of them were pretty interesting; conversely I think the main characters were pretty weak because they kept making bad decisions to pad out the plot, and were often inconsistent (except for John, who's consistently a non-entity as a VERY silent protagonist). The tone was all over the place; from major tragedy to funny fetch quest to major tragedy to funny sidequest, and the "funny" parts were always way too drawn out. It can't decide what kind of game it wants to be; weird or dark. And that ending was just not satisfying... It just feels like they left too much to speculation.The gameplay was okay, though attacking was weirdly inconsistent and it has the Breath of the Wild "cooking makes health a joke" problem. Once you have the the ability to easily refill ammo combat is rarely difficult except for figuring out boss patterns, which is fine; I feel like if it was actually hard it'd be really frustrating. Puzzles were rarely hard (except when I was being dumb) but could get a bit repetitive.Overall, I can't in good conscience recommend the game. Buy the artbook and the OST, look at/listen to those and imagine a good retro game. Unless you're okay going in knowing that the story just isn't, it's just not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: It is not a Zelda game if that is what you are looking for. The game is 70% unskippable cutscenes and dialogue, not good dialogue, mind you; it's the cringy anime-style JRPG dialogue. Every time the game gets good, It halts to a stop and forces you to watch the cringiest cutscene. You will be stuck mashing the A button for, no joke, 8 min straight until the cutscene finishes. The characters get so annoying after a few hours. Sam is cute, don't get me wrong, but there's only so much she can do to carry the story. John is the closest thing to a cardboard cutout I have seen in a video game. They tried to give him the silent protagonist treatment but failed to add any nuance to the character. It's a saving grace in disguise since you won't have to listen to more dialogue.It's a shame. The combat is simple but very fun and the dungeons are great to explore, even with the straightforward puzzles. The pixel art is gorgeous, with beautiful environments and scenery. The game's biggest problem is that instead of telling a story with one sentence, it uses 10. It's almost like a high school student trying to meet the minimum number of words on an essay by adding sentences that add zero value, and its only purpose is to extend the length.

_childDocuments_.review: Boring dialogues are a plague of this game. The gameplay is good, puzzles are great even, but everything story-related is slow, annoying, poorly paced and presented. There's no good structure in the story, either, and Chapter 6 is a plain filler. There are some good sparks here and there, visually it's very appealing, the music is wonderful. But ultimately, I did not have a good time. Especially with slow animations of everything, every transition, every action outside of combat, camera pans — everything is painfully slow, and there are so many unnecessary animations too, like little winning dance on too many occasions. But the worst part is the lack of proper conclusion to each chapter and the game itself.UPD: devs added option to fast-forward dialogues and scenes, so one of the biggest issues is now resolved. The point about story not having a proper conclusion and most dialogues being boring still stands, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game, because everything regarding the visual part is drop dead gorgeous: locations, character design, world itself, ambience, color palette... But the gameplay is just so frustrating to me. The chill explorative vibe gets cut off by run-and-fight-and-change-weapons-on-the-go and opening inventory to eat and restore health and switch between character is so stressful and not fun at all. I don't like this sudden and mismatched change of pace (too chill vs too fast and difficult), I quit the game for several days after I encountered the miasma level, and then I got back to it, it was as much annoying as the first time and it made me not want to play this game anymore :(Which is a shame, since I really loved everything about it except this one aspect of game mechanics which was unfortunately enough to absolutely ruin it for me personally..

_childDocuments_.review: Eastward has incredible style that is executed on perfectly.  It captures classic RPG elements and brings them to a modern standard while upholding all of those classic values from 90's era games.  Thematically it is reminiscent of many other media sources that start with protagonists trapped underground.  It's cute where it needs to be, it's cool where it needs to be.  If you like story based RPG's which have active gameplay this is a great pick.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun. At first it's a bit linear you get a melee weapon, you fight enemies over and over, some puzzles are present too, and a lot of story lines. I saw that some people complain about there being to much story, and too little gameplay. I am sure those people didn't even finished the prologue, as after the prologue (chapter 1) there comes the exploring stuff and that is where Eastward becomes a masterpiece. Every pixel is designed with taught in mind, everything blends together and presents the dystopian world that this games takes place in. The graphics are nice, the use of advanced lightning and pixel palettes are interesting and vast. The story is cool enough, and I think not many games use this kind of narrative, but I will let this spoiler free. So i suggest you try this game, but keep in mind the first chapter is a little bit slower than the rest of the game, also Sam is the cutest 32x32 pixel grid character I ever saw :)))
