_childDocuments_.review: Wow...I've sunk 13 hours into this creation. What do I say?I've thought a lot about how I would phrase this, and here goes...It’s clear to me that the creators of this game had a story to tell, but not so much a game to create. When there is gameplay, it's quite fun, and the music is amazing. But this game is 70% story and dialogue. The last six hours of my gameplay felt like a fight against my attention span, with a constant internal argument as I tried my best to just finish the game. I made it to Chapter 6 and finally couldn't continue. I just wanted to get back to the main story and finish the game, but there are endless scripts and side missions forced into the experience.I simply couldn’t do it anymore. It became mind-numbing, and I started hating every second.If you're someone who loves a lot of dialogue and wants a wacky animated movie that you get to play occasionally, this is the adventure for you. As for me, I'm just exhausted.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, probably some of the most skilled pixel art I've seen, everything is so detailed and the colours give every area such nice vibes. It's truly impressive given how large it is. Soundtrack also slaps, the music in Johnny's is probably one of my favourite shop themes going. The complaints about the pacing and main storyline are definitely valid, and as someone that loves achievement-hunting it's very frustrating that there's no way to go back and see what treasures you missed after completion. However if you're the kind of person that loves exploring amazing settings and talking to every npc you see, you'll enjoy it anyway I think.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: 2D top-down action game. Stunning art and music is hampered by rather basic combat and a linear, under-cooked story. May be worth one play-through, but not much else.EDIT: As of today, an update has come out that fixed a few issues. Chapter Select is now available from the menu so you know longer have to re-start the game for anything you missed, fast travel makes back-tracking easier, and item drops from monsters have been increased.  Overall rating is the same, but it is more player-friendly now.Eastward sells expectations of a journey. The name alone paints a picture in your head of... well, going eastward. And the art catches your eye like few other games can. With those two things in your head, one expects a large, sprawling, free world to explore at your leisure, uncovering more of it as you progress. In reality... well, it's about as linear as a train track can be.Let's start with positives. I've mentioned it twice already, but the art in this game is FANTASTIC. On it's face it's pixel art, but the high resolution, vibrant color palette and lighting effects make every area look unique and eye-catching. From overgrown forests to bustling crowded city streets, Eastward never fails to deliver. It wears the retro style on it's sleeve, with character designs clearly inspired by Earthbound and the like. Some may be tired of the style, but it lends itself well to expressive characters. And the accompanying music is also good too. While not on the level of AAA games, the soundtrack has a couple of bangers and it was always fitting to the situation. And both of these things compliment the dungeons you'll go through as well: A delicate mix of combat and some  real unique puzzles involving both John and Sam's abilities make them compelling to go through. While not difficult to complete, they are memorable and they're satisfying to complete.Unfortunately... none of these things can really make the story any more interesting. While Sam's a cute character, and watching her interact with John and other characters can be very sweet, the plot feels very undercooked for 80% of the story. We never really learn that much about John or his desires. He just kind of goes through the story because... he cares about Sam. And while the game drip-feeds you story throughout the playtime, the rest of the story scenes feel more like filler for all the impact they have on the greater story. The dialogue isn't bad... but it's extraneous. It develops the characters a little more, but not the world around them. And the combat is really only serviceable. For John, he has 1 melee attack that gets upgraded at set points, and 3 ranged weapons that largely do the same thing. For Sam, she gets a stunning projectile and a few special moves, like a shield or an extra-wide screen stun effect. It's basic. My least favorite aspect of the game is it's linearity. I have no problem with linear games, honestly. A linear game makes sense in some narratives and it gives the developer control over the pace of the game. It just feels like a shame that you only get to visit these varied, beautiful areas once before being railroaded to the next. On a lesser note, some weird design decisions made this more tedious than it should have been. Switching between characters feels like it has a bit of a delay, which makes it harder to use their abilities on the fly. There's no good way to speed through dialogue you've already scene, which can make it time-consuming to speed through scenes. There's a fanfare animation that plays every time you beat a special encounter, which you can't skip.  None of these things are bad on their own, but together, they make for an experience that's needlessly annoying at times.I want to recommend this game enthusiastically, but right now, all I could really say is "yeah, it wasn't bad". Go into it for the visuals and the music, and the combat may give you a few surprises at times.  You'll get a good 20 hours out of it. Just remember, with the dialogue taking up much of that, it's more like 12 hours of gameplay. If you can deal with all that, you can go eastward. For everyone else, maybe just let this train pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Scratched my itch for wanting to experience a new adventure!+ Absolutely beautiful and inspiring art style, including nods to their inspirations (Miyazaki being an NPC, a building with several japanese films written on it, etc). Each area has such loving attention to detail.+ Soundtrack fits each moment to a T, with equally dark and whimsy tunes. Definitely worth a listen out of game.+ Very loveable/unique characters to accompany you throughout your journey. And a lot of them, too!+ The way the new combat elements are introduced gives a fresh feel to the game and its battles. Cooking in-game is adorable, and BOTW-esque.+ For the most part, the story keeps you engaged and on the edge of your seat wanting to move to the next chapter. Tear-jerking at times, humorous, but also grim.- Combat lacking a dodge mechanic, although not needed, it often feels like there's no option to avoid taking damage in a fight other than stunning with Sam and then bashing the enemy's skull in, or haphazardly wiggling your joystick. Enemy rooms can feel overwhelming if you aren't on top of it.- Story pacing is a little odd at times, and although I'm posting this without having completed Chapter 8 yet it seems to lack closure in some areas. But could just be up to interpretation!- Repetitive? Puzzle rooms seem to stretch on for a teensy bit longer than you would expect, without introducing any new way to solve them. Combat doesn't change up much after you get all of the options, save for a few unique boss mechanics.My first review so idk what else to say but it's a solid 8/10 !! Enjoyed my time with it and would recommend to anyone craving a new indie game.

In the near-future, society is starting to collapse, and the human population is at an all-time low. A deadly toxic presence has spread across the land, destroying and devouring everything in its path.

Those who could escape the miasma flocked to underground villages to start a new life. But for a hardworking miner and a mysterious young girl, the hope of a thriving outside world beckons

Escape the tyrannical clutches of Sandfill's subterranean society and join Eastward's unlikely duo on an exciting adventure to the land above! 

Discover beautiful yet bizarre settlements and make new friends as you travel across the world by rail.

name: Legend of Keepers: Career of a Dungeon Manager
detailed_description: Newsletter About the Game In this original mix of Dungeon Management and Roguelite, you will lead your career as a Dungeon Manager! Features Join the Dungeons Company and climb the corporate ladder Crush so-called 'heroes' and protect the company's treasures Hire monsters, manage your employees and your stock of traps Deal with employee strikes and other fun events RogueDefender Each run will be different but players will keep some of their Master's bonuses between runs. Like we've already mentioned, our game is a mix between Roguelite and Dungeon Management. How did we achieve that? By running many tests to find the perfect balance between management and dungeon phases! Dungeon Phase First, you will have to plan your defense against a group of adventurers. Check their stats and resistances, then place the best traps and monsters to defeat them! When you think your dungeon is ready, let the crawl begin! You will then be able to watch those heroes die! It's a reversed dungeon crawler: heroes will move through your dungeon and will trigger the traps you placed. When a group of adventurers encounters a group of monsters you positioned in your dungeon, a turn-based fight will happen! Games/Series that inspired us: HeroQuest (Board Game), Naheulbeuk (French audio series), Kaamelott (the best French series), Monty Python (English series). Video games: Darkest Dungeon, Slay the Spire, Dungeon Keeper, Final Fantasy, Divinity, For the King, Chroma Squad, Battle Brothers, West of Loathing and so many more...
about_the_game: In this original mix of Dungeon Management and Roguelite, you will lead your career as a Dungeon Manager! Features Join the Dungeons Company and climb the corporate ladder Crush so-called 'heroes' and protect the company's treasures Hire monsters, manage your employees and your stock of traps Deal with employee strikes and other fun events RogueDefender Each run will be different but players will keep some of their Master's bonuses between runs. Like we've already mentioned, our game is a mix between Roguelite and Dungeon Management. How did we achieve that? By running many tests to find the perfect balance between management and dungeon phases! Dungeon Phase First, you will have to plan your defense against a group of adventurers. Check their stats and resistances, then place the best traps and monsters to defeat them! When you think your dungeon is ready, let the crawl begin! You will then be able to watch those heroes die! It's a reversed dungeon crawler: heroes will move through your dungeon and will trigger the traps you placed. When a group of adventurers encounters a group of monsters you positioned in your dungeon, a turn-based fight will happen! Games/Series that inspired us: HeroQuest (Board Game), Naheulbeuk (French audio series), Kaamelott (the best French series), Monty Python (English series). Video games: Darkest Dungeon, Slay the Spire, Dungeon Keeper, Final Fantasy, Divinity, For the King, Chroma Squad, Battle Brothers, West of Loathing and so many more...

detailed_description: Your farming life begins in Mineral Town, a charming village surrounded by nature. You've returned after many years to restore your late grandfather's farm to its former glory. Care for crops, livestock, and more as your very own story of seasons unfolds. Tend to the Farm! A menagerie of fruits, veggies, and livestock are waiting for you. Raise them all with love and care, and you'll have plenty of products to harvest, sell, or cook with! Stroll Down Memory Lane! Mineral Town is full of friendly faces, both old and new! Head into town, give gifts, and learn all about your neighbors as you befriend them. Fall in Love! Mineral Town is home to several eligible bachelors and bachelorettes. Get to know the boy or girl of your dreams, and you might be able to date them, get married, and even start a family! There's More to Explore! Go fishing, cook fresh meals, and when your work's all said and done, take a dip in the local hot spring. Experience the farmer's life like never before!

_childDocuments_.review: I put over 80 hours into this game in 2 weeks, so that should say a lot. While I didn't play the GBA game of the same title much, Harvest Moon 64 is one of my all time favorite games. I've been having too much fun getting back into this franchise and seeing the old characters I loved so much. (Although I'd love to know why so many character relationships were changed between 64 and FoMT, lol.)My only complaint is that they've removed rival marriages for some reason. I have no idea if it's a possibility, but I really hope they patch that in in a future update.Highly recommend, if you're a fan of farming games and particularly if you were a fan of the HM franchise. Story of Seasons is the franchise you remember - just under a different title.

_childDocuments_.review: Ahh Story of Seasons: Bisexuals of Mineral Town.I remember back in the day as a young girl being forced to play as a boy farmer and having to marry the girls, when I would have rather play as who I was IRL. Then when I could finally play as a girl feeling meh about it because I didn’t dislike the guys, but I really wanted to just marry the girls now. What a horny and hormonal mess I was back then. Now that marrying anyone regardless of gender is standard in this game, playing means so much more to me. Who knows, maybe one day I’ll get to marry the sprites. Or the horse.Anyhow, like many others have mentioned the game’s main selling point is nostalgia. A lot of the people playing it now (like me) grew up with the original game. I haven’t played many of the more recent SoS titles but I wouldn’t be surprised if FoMT kinda falls short in comparison.I personally wouldn’t have it any other way though. I play to relive my childhood and I appreciate how simple the game is. I’ve outgrown the complex game mechanics that’d you see in Stardew Valley. If you’re new to the series don’t be discouraged though, the game it’s so worth it. Honestly it’s so peaceful and will make you feel like you’re 8 playing in your PS1 again. My only criticism in this game… they changed 80% of the names from the old game … But left Karen to suffer the cruel fate of her identity.I also still can’t get over the fact that the Doctor doesn’t get a name, just… Doctor. I married him purely because of that. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great for nostalgia. The Harvest Moon series (later renamed ''Story of Seasons" - not to be confused with the newer "Harvest Moon'' series) is the ''grandfather'' of role play slash farming simulators like stardew valley. It inspired many games within the genre today so if you're buying this for nostalgia, you won't be disappointed (aside from the time speeding up too fast!) but if you're a 1.) player with no prior knowledge of the series spanning as far back as the game boy advance era (and beyond) and 2.) a young player coming from newer games like "Stardew Valley", "Rune Factory" and "My Time in Portia'' - You'll most likely be disappointed by this game alone. Compared to newer games, this is barebones + it costs more although I would be the last to discourage new players to try this games because it still has its charm especially if you love games in this genre! Overall, as a player since the game boy advance era, I found this to be ''good enough'' and I intend to play the game more often since I havent really finished any Harvest Moon games. I just wished they added more to this remake of a classic favorite. It could've been more but I suppose the intention of the developers was to change nothing (gameplay-wise) and focus more on making the game look modern which is fine but that's why I suggest getting this game only when its on sale simply because you'll get more content from other games at this price point.

I can't explain why but actually playing the game on the big screen makes me not hate the art anymore, especially the character portrait. I can see a lot of subtle details on the portrait that looks really charming (the tiny screenshots I've seen before made the portrait look flat and less detailed). Moreover, the depth of field effect looks really nice imo.I've only played it for 1 hour but I'll keep the game because it's the FoMT I've known and loved now that my problem with the art has been resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: Addiction, thy name is Story of Seasons!The farming is addicting, the art is cute, the story and it's characters are wholesome, the farming is addicting, the mining is kinda fun, the livestock variations are funny, the festivals are engaging, did I mention the farming is addicting? Cause it really, really is.If you are looking at this game, you are probably familiar with Stardew Valley. Well, this game is a remake of one of the games that inspired Stardew Valley. It is a remake of the GameBoy Advance game Harvest Moon: Friends of Mineral Town.But it has a lot of major differences from Stardew Valley, and I like these differences, the ones I think are most important to mention are;1- Time stops while you are indoors2- It's very lighthearted, stories are never very dark (so nothing like someone getting drunk and trying to off themselves, for example).3- No combat, there are a lot of fun activities in this game, combat is not one of them.4- The progression is mostly through various things like tools and animals, not so much your character. Tools level up, animals grow and make better product, the character can gain more stamina and costumes (the costumes are strictly cosmetic).5- And this is really important: PET. CAPYBARA.As of this writing, Stardew valley lets you pick a dog or a cat to be your pet. This game lets you have a choice between several kinds of dogs or cats, penguins, and CAPYBARAS!P.S. The store page says "Partial Controller Support" but I've only used my keyboard to type in names. Even changed video settings with the controller.P.P.S. Native DualShock 4 support with proper button icons, I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an old school gamer, I bought this game to reminisce my childhood.There are 2 major complaints I had with this game :1. Horse racing breaks everythingBro, sis, this game is farming simulator. You're supposed to, farm, what else?So why every prices is so marked up?1k for a pet treat10k-30k for a pet (worth a large house and hothouse)Having to buy and impregnate a cow multiple times to get golden/platinum/X produce, where they will produce nothing when pregnantThere's an achievement which requires you to own 5 million gold and if you think 5 million gold is a lotThe most expensive item in this game is worth effing 100 million. 100 million!!The answer is the infamous horse derby. Making money off horse derby felt like a necessity, because everything in end game is so jack expensive, and it RUINS YOUR SENSE OF PROGRESSION!!Why would you plant 20 batches of pineapple (like I did in HM:BTN) today, if I can just spam horse racing tickets?We're supposed to make money off FARMING, not betting!!2. After 1200+ floors of mining, it has vexed me greatly that the FAINTING animation is too slow, too long, too dramatic, when it can be just under 0.5 seconds like it did in HM:BTN.You said, how issit a huge issue? Then try it. Avoid horse racing, try make money off the mines to get the level 6 tools, do it the hard way like I did. I dare you.Conclusion : it's still worth to buy, I'm still supporting the devs who originally made HM:BTN, but compared to it's predecessor, it's a sad remake with no sense of progression and achievement.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's fine, nevertheless I am refunding it. I don't know how they thought this game was remotely close to being worth $40-$50. They could've added layers to town life, like attracting merchants. Farm plot expansion. There is no excuse to limit gameplay to what this is in 2020. I'm ok with supporting the original devs but they don't get to recycle the same game four (?) times in 30 years with no real innovation along the way.DO BETTERBalanceChopping wood and stone is much more profitable than actual farming.

_childDocuments_.review: Great remake of a great game with improvements.I'm sure many people probably remember Harvest Moon: Friends of Mineral Town. It was one of the best GBA games released. This game is basically an improvement on the old series. And the list follows.1. Addition of two new townsfolk you can marry.2. This game is basically a combination of "Friends of Mineral Town" and "More Friends of Mineral Town".3. You can walk through the plants.4. You can collect a bunch of soundtracks from the original game AND previous Harvest Moon titles along with originals that're actually quite lovely.5. You can ride your horse OUT of the farm! As many who have played the game know, you could only ride your horse in the farm. Now, you can ride it just about anywhere.6. More animals to choose from and breed.7. Costumes to wear and clothes you can change into.8. Additional content that helps you travel faster.9. Higher upgrades for your equipment.You get the idea. Overall, it's an improvement of one of the greatest Harvest Moon games to be released. It might not be Stardew Valley, but this is what inspired it and perhaps it's the nostalgia talking, but this game is probably on par. Though I feel the two games are different. A great and enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Before the series was named "Story Of Seasons", this series was also known as "Harvest Moon" (in case some people did not know). I fell in love with the Harvest Moon series with Harvest Moon 64 being my all time favorite game of the series. With Harvest Moon: Friends Of Mineral Town being right behind it, I knew that Story Of Seasons had a "Harvest Moon" feel to it. I literally felt like a little child again raising my farm and trying to win Elli or Ann's heart (Sorry, it's Elly and Ran now in Story of Seasons). I cannot seem to stop playing this game because of the childhood memories i had.  Now, I understand that it is now Xseed games, not Natsume that are making these games but, I couldn't help that this particular game did miss some features that the original game had.This is still a Harvest Moon game. While some of the names have been changed (Ran used to be Ann and Elly used to be Elli), I chuckle when i saw this. However, there are some flaws in this game.CONS- It is still the same farming sim game but, the biggest change that I noticed was the rival marriages were taken out. I still do not know why they took this feature out. I feel like with this added feature, you can help people get marry and continued with the story. Why I can't see Karen and Kai get married or even Elly and the Doctor? There is no rush to get married in this game. This was in the original game and i couldn't help but wonder, WHY?-No sick animals or even dead animals. There is NO consequences of your actions if you neglect the animals. In the past Harvest Moon games, your animals can get sick and eventually died if you do not take care of them, which, will affect your endgame. In this game, you can neglect them but, they will not produce milk, eggs, fur etc.- Time does go by fast. About 10 seconds playing, ten minutes will elapsed. You will need to watch your time and make sure you meet your deadlines. PROS- A Harvest Moon remake of the original friends of mineral town- New animals- Huge field for your crops- Mines are the go to for money- Harvest Spirits FTW- Can now marry male and female if you choose to. Meaning if you're a male and you want to marry a male, you can.Overall, do I feel the need to spend $40 dollars for a game like this? Nope. I feel like this would be better priced at $25. No DLC have been announced, minus the DLC which is above (costume DLC... ok...)

_childDocuments_.review: I am a hardcore fan of the original Gameboy Advance version of this game and this remake is perfect.It is the two GBA games (Harvest Moon Friends of Mineral Town and Harvest Moon More Friends of Mineral Town) combined into one remake with extra sprinkles and removal of annoying features in the original game.The original story, characters, map, strategies, music are all back with a few improvements.Things I love in this version:- Two game modes, easy and hard- No more pushing animals around, just ring a bell and they come outside- More romantic partner options and same sex marriages - More animals- Better inventory system (stackable items and no more basket) - Save almost anywhereIf you are fan of the original game you will love this, it might take you a few minutes to get over the fact they have moved the pond, but once you are past that it is all good :) I also recommend you check out wikis for this game, there is a lot more to it than meets the eye.

_childDocuments_.review: It is hard to describe this without bracing for critics from Stardew Valley/Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons exclusive players. But here we go:>>>>FOR PLAYERS WHO PREVIOUSLY ONLY PLAYED HARVEST MOON/STORY OF SEASONS:This is it! The long awaited GBA "(More) Friends of Mineral Town" remake! Finally the feeling of playing HM: FoMT in the classic graphics of PS1 HM: BtN!In this game, FINALLY AFTER DECADES AND MANY SoS VERSIONS WE CAN NOW HARVEST THE CENTER OF THE CROPS!!! HIP HIP, HURRAY! They brought all the FoMT goodness and patched most of FoMT badness into this one! No need to connect other HM games to unlock special contents here!In my opinion, the only MAJOR downgrade in this SoS version are the absence of rivals marriages - which hit the "thrill factor" really bad. About the graphics, I'm still wondering why the very same author decided to change the nostalgic character graphics style instead of just HD-fying them.>>>>FOR PLAYERS WHO PREVIOUSLY ONLY PLAYED STARDEW VALLEY:This is the HD version of that one game which inspired ConcernedApe, the creator Stardew Valley! If you compare it with Stardew Valley, expect much simpler gameplay, Story is lighthearted, and no battle here. Time is stopped indoor, but flow really fast outdoor. So, expect the mixed feeling of relaxed and speedrunning in this game. For every completionist, expect some irreversible "game collectible trap". Therefore, reading a walkthrough is highly advised.Expect a VERY LONG POST-GAME with A LOT OF POST-GAME EVENTS/UNLOCKABLES. Yeah, this game was originally designed for portable console gaming, so it is very understandable.Honestly, the only Story of Seasons game comparable with Stardew Valley will be the upcoming Story of Seasons: Pioneer of Olive Town, which won't be discussed here.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing the original Mineral Town games before the big divide- but what I feel is that this version is far superior to the original GBA one. For starters, you can marry either gender no matter which you play, which I consider a great bonus of content. You can also walk on your plants now, which feels a bit more natural. Adding in new characters, seeds, and a difficulty option are all fantastic ways they improved the game. And, of course, you can play male or female in one game. Finally, there's the auto-save. You can have many save files, but the auto-save is great if you want to restart a day or forget to save after a number of days and want to continue where you left off! Basically, I really like this version of the game so far. Achievements don't hurt, but it's really the added content and abilities that really pile up to make it a splendid purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to play harvest moon back when I was 10 years old and now I am 30, its been over 2 decades since I wished for a non emulator official release of a game like this <3 OMG I hope they keep on updating it and bring more stuff into it, PLEASE Make this game great :D oh and I know its impossible but a multiplayer option would be a sick addition :DStory of Seasons: Friends of Mineral Town is a remake of the 2003 GameBoy Advance game Harvest Moon: Friends of Mineral Town and its female counterpart Harvest Moon: More Friends of Mineral Town (the Harvest Moon name currently belongs to a different publisher). Players choose one of four player models (2 boys, 2 girls), and take over their grandfather's farm. During a day, players can tend to their crops, pet their animals, forage in the forest, mine in caves, and talk to the townsfolk to befriend or romance them. It's the formula that inspired Stardew Valley, down to the backstory of the farm's inheritance, and it's largely gone untouched. The graphics have been changed from pixel art to a cute, crisp, chibi 3D style. Players can save anywhere, not just from their rooms. In the West, same-sex marriage has been added. An easy mode has been added, and some names have been changed. Beyond that, this is largely the same game from 17 years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: I have not played the original version on Game Boy Advance (either Harvest Moon Friends of Mineral Town or Harvest Moon More Friends of Mineral Town) so this would be from someone who has played through the game for first time.Now onto review - It is great casual farming game! It may seem basic when comparing to likes of Stardew Valley and games after that, but that's what makes this game appealing to me in first place, as I wanted breather from littering my farm with objects just so I can turn object A into object B. It's not deep, and I don't think it needs to be that. My only gripe is having to harvest every single crop with a button press, you can't just hold button and mass-gather quickly. Scythe in this one doesn't help you either, as that just kills the crop in process. (It tells you in-game, so I haven't done it unless I wanted to kill crop on purpose like at end of season) So each time I wake up to field full of crops I let out urgh. Thankfully there are harvest spirits who can help you as long as you hit enough FP with them, I just usually have them water my crops since with animal care they're kinda meh (Lack of FP building with farm animals, and they straight up sell items instead of putting it in some sort of temp storage). Now onto NPCs and other aspects of the game - I like the cast of villagers, it was fun enough watching the events as you stumble into them and generally learn little stories they have. Sadly, though this is minor issue - the stories don't really solve themselves, aside from few characters their story never gets closure of any kind, so it was sad to see as I'd like to see the story develop over years go by but considering this *is* GBA remake, I'll give it a pass - and it doesn't stop the game being good in my eyes.The town itself as well outside of it is very basic, exploration isn't really thing I'd say. You can forage for stuff, and once you know the usual spots its case of running there and see if it's there each day. And mines themselves - I am not really biggest fan of these. Hammer upgrades meant nothing in mines as it doesn't work, so you are either slowly breaking rocks around when using hoes to dig up to try find ladder to go down. Save scumming works though, so you can save, dig around, find ladder then load save & it'll be in same spot which saves stamina. Which makes it quite cumbersome, so when I got to bottom floor of each mine (there are two) and got what I wanted, I never went back to mining.Fishing is alright, I guess. It doesn't have minigame so you just fish and mash A/Cross when you get bite. The problem is while there are different fishes to catch, they are merged into either Small Fish, Medium Fish or Large Fish so selling them isn't really exiciting when all fish (of size) sells exactly same amount of cash, and that's from someone who likes fishing to make money/to pass time. Fun though to try for achievement as well getting guardian fish.Achievement hunters may want to re-consider going for 100%, unless you are prepared to spend long time on this. I started out playing naturally till year 4, and then it felt bit pain because my chickens didn't drop Small or Medium Egg, so I had to sell one to get new one to fill my inventory so I can cook and there's also item that drops from sheep which you need for one of recipes (two, in fact but last one can be from rabbit or alpcha) that has very low drop rate of 0.4% and that's after having it out gaze for 1,000 hours (in-game!). Getting pets are nightmare because you can only get them from special NPC that you need to unlock, then only available on 15th of each season... if not rainy. Then you can't buy another pet until you get 8 hearts total, which goes up each time you buy pet. So yeah if you want all achievements you are in long haul.To sum it up - Great "basic" farming simulator with quite lot of stuff to do, mining I'm not too fond of, decent villagers and some minor annoyances that keeps it from amazing game for me but overall I can recommend this if you want to try out "old" Harvest Moon game to see what it's like.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played Harvest Moon as a kid, but I do love farming sims so I couldn't pass this up and I have to admit, I am a bit bummed. The game play is a bit too simple for me (that's not to say it's a bad thing... sometimes simple is good), and after about forty minutes of play time I already knew I wasn't going to enjoy it so I decided to refund it. It's hard not to compare this game to newer farm sims of our generation and I've been spoiled by them. I know I would become too bored too quickly with this one. It does seem wholesome, but it's just lacking a lot of content other farms games have.In my opinion, this game is not worth $50, maybe $25 at the most, but definitely not $50. It's clear they are playing off people's nostalgia, and that's fine for those of you who want to relive a bit of your childhood, especially at a time like now in the world. I do like the graphics though, even the big ol' heads the little characters have, they are quite cute. And to wrap it up, I would not recommend this to an older audience, to me it comes across more as Baby's First Farm Sim game. It would be great for younger kids.

_childDocuments_.review: Story of Seasons: Friends of Mineral Town was originally a Harvest Moon game on the Game Boy Advance in 2003, and was indisputably the best farming-life game around. But since then this genre has become improbably crowded. From Stardew Valley to My Time at Portia, Kynseed to Rune Factory, there is no shortage of video game tributes to an idealised agricultural life, many of them made by developers who grew up playing this one. This PC remake feels like coming home: it’s warm, comfortable and familiar. If you ever feel down and need cheering up then this is the game made for you.PROS:✓ Lively characters, with fun and distinct personalities✓ Coffee, Fruit, and Strawberry Cows!✓ Has a really relaxing tone to it✓ Forgiving with an emphasis of working at your own pace✓ Introduced a lot of QoL improvements✓ Charming artwork and music✓ Enjoyable relationship-building system✓ Nostalgic for any previous fans✓ Easy to play✓ Story moments provide meaningful character insights✓ Real and classic Harvest Moon gameCONS:- Lackluster character models- The game is devoid of voice acting- Excessive grinding- Gameplay can be a little simplistic- Festivals need more interaction- Some more character customization options would be nice

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot in good conscience give this game a negative review, as I'm having a lot of fun with this remake.  However, bear in mind that most of this review may just be me complaining about things.  With that being said, here goes:If you grew up with the original GBA version of this game in China, or played it in Chinese, you may be familiar with a community known as "pirate9".  It was an online forum dedicated to this specific title - "Harvest Moon: Friends of Mineral Town" for the Gameboy Advance.  It was a bustling community, people wrote fanfic, used in-game assets to create comics and storyboards, fanart, playthrough blogs, you name it.  Of course, that community also came together and pulled an impressive encyclopedia on FoMT - glitches, NPC schedules, game data, even gameshark codes, you name it.  I would wake up to dozens of new posts every day and read through all of them, even contributing a bit, however juvenile it was at the time.  It is still the most memorable summer break I've had to date, and I spent nearly all of it online in that one message board.  Like many of the people on pirate9, I must've dumped thousands of hours into FoMT.Pirate9 is long gone now, I still have the site bookmarked on my browser today for nostalgia, but the forum links are dead, the resource packs are no longer present, and aside from a few featured articles forever etched into the front page, its last activity dated 2008.  With even Flash obsoleted in the year 2021, the domain is but a shell of what it used to be.  So when I see this game on the Steam page, I bought it for the same reason the in-game main character returned to the farm to begin with - nostalgia.So is the game good?  Well...Reluctantly, of course.Compared to modern Story of Seasons titles, or even more modern farming sims titles entirely, FoMT has very bare systems.  I'm currently one of those people waiting for Rune Factory 5 to drop on my switch, and I've spent some quality time with friends on Stardew Valley.  I can claim without controversy that those are now superior titles to what this Story of Seasons title mounts up to be.  Even Pioneers of Olive Town - which I do not personally play but have seen - have way more features than Friends of Mineral Town.  This remake of FoMT is supposedly faithful.  Yams are still broken as all hell, the Flying Stone is still there at the bottom of the mines, and even the algorithms by which mine ladders can spawn are preserved, but...Putting aside subjective matters like character redesigns (which I personally don't mind but I see many others complaining about) or new characters (I don't mind the inclusion of Brandon/Jennifer but I see others complaining about them), it seems that some of the choices that were ultimately made were disappointing.  I can understand these changes are made to not discourage casual play, but that's frankly an insulting excuse.  I was 11 when I first played FoMT on my Gameboy, I was far from a hardcore gamer back then - and even now - so the things that were ultimately removed in this remake left the game incomplete.I'm talking about my three biggest no-nos in this remake, system-wise, let's run through them:In the original titles, if you waited too long to marry a bachelor/ette, they would be married to their rival.  This feature was taken out because it may be punitive to a casual player, but let's be honest - a rival marriage occurs at Year 5 if you're still single.  No matter how casually you play, you'd be married in even a chill playthrough at worst 2 years before that.  With no more rival marriages, the amount of rival love interactions are reduced - only the first two are retained in this game and the rest no longer here.  It leads to a huge part of the game feeling incomplete.  I actually  some of the villagers to marry each other, I think it's very sweet, but now to be left hanging at their first two events forever just feels bad.In the original, chickens have an average lifespan of 3 years, sheep 4, and cows 5.  As it takes a long time to gain enough friendship with your livestock to gain higher quality byproducts, losing an old animal in your farm sucks.  But that's precisely what kept the animal system in check.  You were incentivized to keep a large group of animals, and to keep them bred and loved constantly.  Now that livestock are no longer plagued by their imminent mortality, you can eventually have a barn full of stacked animals and never look back.  Ultimately, it just reduces the amount of complexity in an already simple game.Man, that poor phone in the bar just no longer sees use.  In the original, furniture were purchased every Saturday from the shopping network.  You had to pay money to some mysterious shopping show and the product will be delivered 3 days after the call.  The original game had this system to provide the player with some sort of actual milestone - every Saturday, pony up the money and work your way up.  And believe me - you had to.  This was the only way to get the fridge, the cabinet, the kitchen, and of course, the double bed for marriage.  It also hurried you to get your house expanded, as without the proper expansion, the shopping network stops offering you new things.  This system is completely gone.  The fridge and bed are bought from Gotz (Gotts), and Jeff now peddles your cookware.  Frankly, I liked it better when I had a milestone goal every in-game Saturday.  And it's left me feeling wanting.Because it's still a good game.  I'm 13 years older since I first discovered the pirate9 community and dumped thousands of hours into FoMT, trying to buy that billion-dollar villa.  Whether it is out of sheer nostalgia, or just something else, the fact that FoMT remains so simple is surprisingly elegant, in its own way.  There aren't nearly as many things to do compared to Stardew Valley, and nowhere near as much exploration and skill juggling as Rune Factory (and I hold RF4 as one of the best games I've ever played), but it's still the Mineral Town I knew and loved - quiet, quaint, and just a calming time.I can have fun peacefully, both reminiscing and just casually enjoying my time.  And that's good enough for me.(If you  enjoy your time at all, that is, since in-game time now goes by twice as fast)

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute, it's as advertised (A 2003 gameboy advance game reskinned) and that's about all that's good. TL;DR- Game starts off cute and enjoyable then quickly becomes horrendously painful and boring compared to Stardew/portia and others, clearly an overpriced 2003 nostalgia scam. Gives me some hope that a new 2020+ game could actually be good. But not worth $50First off, if you buy this for $50 you're in for a very bad time, if you manage to get this for $10-20 maybe you can justify it. Me, I couldn't I gave it an honest attempt but it's just boring and you can easily see the lack of current Quality of Life that is needed in games like this. The big flags: 1) Farming/Crops - are your biggest money maker however even if you upgrade your tools your stamina depletes at the same rate as if you just watered one by one. Another thing there's no automatic watering unless you use the Nature Sprites (we'll get into that soon). Stamina can be addressed here, there's a very annoying little cutscene that plays every single time your stamina hits 50%/25%/10%/0% even when you refill it.. you see it again... and again...and again 2) Nature Sprites - This is your hired help along the farm, I say hired help because you have to get them to 3/10 hearts via gifts and then every time you ask for their help they lose hearts unless you keep gifting them. Plus they actually start off VERY BAD at their jobs so you have to play minigames to make them better. Which doesn't sound bad at first until you realize that you make very minimal progress each minigame and that minigame only works on that 1 sprite out of the like 7 that there are. 3) The mines: The mines are complete ♥♥♥♥, you progress by breaking rocks for ore and then hoeing the ground to uncover a ladder. The problem is you deplete your stamina so fast that you need to leave and enter the hotsprings up top just to recover it and upon entering the mine your progress is reset back to floor zero. If you actually want to make any real progress you have to cheat/abuse the Save/Load system since ladder locations are locked upon entering the mine. So what you need to do is Enter > save > dig for ladder > reload the game > go straight to ladder spot> go down a floor> save > repeat.... just awful gameplay design to be blunt good enough for 2003 but doesn't need to exist now. those are just 3 big flags that I saw within 7hrs of gameplay, Maybe I'm off the mark here, maybe there's things I don't know that might make the game better/more enjoyable. But after that amount of time I can't see the progress at all in this game, it's just simply outdated. (still very visually appealing though I will definitely give it that)

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Harvest Moon since the SNES, I had to play this.This game is a remake of a remake, and it brings a lot of improvement over the previous iterations. Playing it is pure nostalgia for those who played Back to Nature or Friends of Mineral Town for GBA. It's the same game, but with improved graphics, more interactions, new animals, new marriage candidates, improved mining, and also the possibility of choosing between a male or female MC, and now with no restriction of gender of your marriage candidates, and you can get pregnant (if female) and choose the gender of your child. Downsides: 1. Limited heart system for animals, which obliges you to have several generations of them nimal until you can max the hearts and win the festivals to have the golden variety of their produce. 2. Your child remains a baby forever. It never learns to speak, it just learns how to walk at some point. This game could be better if they used the child growing mechanic from A Wonderful Life.3. This game is pretty repetitive, just like most farming simulators that derive from Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons. If you just want to chill and improve your farm, take care of your animals and your relationships with villagers, this game is great. But, it never actually ends, and after some time you feel the overall lack of sense of progress.I actually recommend it if you are a Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons/Stardew Valley/Rune Factory fan. But, don't expect much change, especially after 2/3 years in-game years. Just chill and enjoy it. This game is the best version of Back to Nature/Friends of Mineral Town, but it could be much better.

_childDocuments_.review: (ENGLISH Technical Review, by an also developer)*Recent edit: more than ONE YEAR since last patch note at 8/20/2020 and critical issues listed here have not been reviewed or implemented in the game (I've also sent it by email too), which makes me sad. Using a controller and check the calendar still keeps bugging the entire interface, this is inadmissible and a disrespect for the consumer. As a developer, this is outrageous. Please, don't abandon development that way! [Update: Years passed and I never saw the prize or even a message from xseed. I never bought anything from them again.I'm going to give a 'Not Recommended' because of their fraudulent art contest, lack of fixes and to have the Dev. attention more easily since I bring some technical issues that must be checked. I'll update this review as I analyze the game further! For now some critical and minor points, some of them are problems of the ancient versions of the game that have remained in this one:1. Initial configuration of the game language does not match that of the steam properties. Opening initially in Japanese. You need to access the in-game settings and change the first option until you find a readable language. (I think this is already fixed)2. There is no command to type text through the steam controller, even if the steam controller input is turned on, it does not accept the text being typed there. Also DON'T recognize the keyboard capital letters input ( The only way is to use Ctrl C + Ctrl V)*Also not possible to type accents (only from Copy and Paste)3. Insufficient character number for the character name input and the farm name. (only 8 max characters, including spaces) I can't even use 'Wanderyen', and I always use it in any game...4. Does not offer Portuguese-Brazil translation (I even volunteer for that, I already translated about 90% of the game Alice: Madness Returns). What is strange since Brazil always has localized titles, including dubbed.5. Everytime that I check the calendar, when playing with a controller, suddenly all the icons for controller buttons on the interface disappears, and in place, white squares on all of it. (Pic: 6. The text in the dialogue balloon, when there is a line spacing between one speech and another, makes the screen cut the dialogue very fast, making it difficult to follow.7. There is a lack of key association options for controller such as Bag, Farm Information, Relationships. (Existing on the keyboard settings)8. You can skip any lower tool upgrades, eg: Upgrade directly to Mithril Sickle if you have the materials, without the need to perform predecessor upgrades. I know the "price" for that choice is the time without the tool, but doenst sounds fair enought. The amount of materials for the upgrades is also quite mediocre.9. The tool level, although mentioned in some objects, is not mentioned in any interface10. In the cave, the location of the stairs and the prize of all the rocks in the mine are predefined and are not affected by loading saved games. the player can save the game, locate the places, load the game and then save stamina costs to easily descend the floors and get key drops. * The game only stores the location of everything on the floor where you are, it is not possible to predict more than one floor of the mine. I recognize that maybe this mechanic of using the Journal is part of how the caves work, but it still sounds kind of ridiculous to be able to go back in time for any mistakes that are made in the game. (Maybe a new game difficulty where you can only use the bed journal?)11. In the cave, If you find a HOLE, just save and enter it several times until you drop as many floors as possible, since the game does not preset this data on the current floor. But I do not recommend it, holes are very disadvantageous!12. During the event on the beach on day 1 (Summer) it is possible to fish until the inventory is filled, since it does not spend Stamina. (This is not a big problem, is a fun exploit with limitations)13. You can fall from exhaustion every night (before midnight), go to the hospital and you will wake up naturally at 6PM at home with your whole stamina AND fatigue restored. It's more efficient than sleeping in your house, and it doesn't cost a penny!14. There is no accessible button in the game to delete saves, nor a padlock system to prevent saves from being deleted by mistake or bad intent (I have traumas)15. The hitbox of the adult horse is very large, causing mobility problems after dismounting it every single time.16. When using the stamina when throwing the fishing rod, in some moments of the character's reaction (such as getting tired) the fishing action is canceled and you are unable to complete the fishing action in which the stamina investment occurred. It's like throwing stamina in the trash.17. When improving the house for the second time, the single bed is thrown to the side and there is an ugly space left (space reserved for the double bed, where the couple does not sleep in the same bed, which is very strange!). I believe that a customization system that allows moving furniture is already possible in 2020 and would bring more useful life to the house, solving the simple and aesthetically not so good design of the current house.(in addition to giving a more personal look to each player)18. I received a letter at the house about the achievement of the consecutive improvement of the house that I did in my save game when I moved to another save (my sister usually plays in this one, which is hers)19. It is not intuitive or indicated anywhere, that I know of, that you can display gifts received from NPCs on the table in the house.But I have to mention that I'm having a good time, beside the problems. The character illustrations are lovely, as the item icons. The item drop animation is the best and the music, very nostalgic. _childDocuments_.review: Recommended for people that played the originals back in the day. This is a remake, and is not intended to push the boundaries for these types of casual farm simulators and slice-of-life games. They made a lot of quality of life improvements to the originals. Being able to save at any time is especially welcome. If you played Friends of Mineral Town on GBA, you will find a familiar, but improved experience. You can see your current energy level. There are inventory management screens that help avoid mistakes, like accidentally throwing turnips away when you miss the shipment box. Now you can just access the shipping box and select all the things you will be selling. You can now plant in every square, since you can access them all. No more "C" or "O" planting. The new easy mode also allows you to play through the game with greater forgiveness. Relationships are easier to develop and manage, you make more money, and things are cheaper. Finally, animals no longer die, and you have many more options than in the original.I see many critiques that malign this game because it is not Stardew Valley (which is a clone of the Harvest Moon games). While this is not a valid criticism of the game, I understand the sentiment. Fans of the genre will love this game, but perhaps new, casual players will find it harder to get hooked. For those that played the originals, you will appreciate reliving this game in HD with the added improvements.

And it makes it even harder to like new characters like Brandon who in addition to having barely anything to say, almost never changes his facial expression. The art style's fine, I guess, if a little safe and increasingly "cutesy."It's been a minute since I played the original game, so I can't remember how many of the sprite and dialogue issues are carried over from the GameBoy, but it's not 2003 anymore so I'd expect more out of a game remake that has less limited space than its original release :\ I'm glad I got it for 40% off, but I still feel like that was pretty expensive for what's here...

_childDocuments_.review: So, first off, this is NOT worth $50.  This is a $20 game from sunup to sundown.  This game is, almost verbatim, a remake of an old Gameboy Advance game from the early 2000s, with very little in the way of technical or graphical advancement or innovation.That said, it is, almost verbatim, a remake of probably the best Harvest Moon (or Harvest Moon-esque) game that was ever on the market.  There's a couple changes, sure, and a few more robust minigames and upgrades added, but the core of the game is the same as it ever was, and the core was good.My only complaint with the original, and which carries through to this one, is the mine.  Well, mines.  2 mines that are 255 floors deep because that's how high a hexidecimal value goes.  It was always tedious, and as a completionist, I HAVE to get to the bottom because the jerk designers actually put unique content down there.  A massive quality of life improvement is the introduction of an elevator to go down to the 50th and 100th floors once you've reached them, but for all practical purposes 100 was a PERFECTLY FINE ending point.  It requires great effort and preparation, good tools, and/or a hell of a lot of gumption in the form of saving/reloading to get down that deep, but nooooooo.  Jerk devs needed to keep the most annoying part of the original game in.I suppose there's always cheats if I just want to see the content.  That was certainly never an option on the GBA.  Definitely get this game if you're a Harvest Moon or Stardew Valley fan (especially because there's a relative dearth of farming slice of life friendship games on Steam), just wait for it to be on sale.  It's not worth $50.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played any of the original harvest moon games so this is my first SoS game to date. I’ll break down my review into a bullet points to highlight aspects that are important to me - Graphics. The game style is adorable! Characters, animals are cute, environment is crisp and lively. It reminded me of BDSP Pokémon game - Farming. You can start planting from day one and get live stock as soon as you have money for it. At first non upgraded tools are a bit tedious to use, however, nature sprites can be asked to help with watering crops - Combat. There’s none. Perfect for me - Day length. I never found myself annoyed by days passing too slowly. Time stops inside buildings and that’s amazing! I have time to complete everything I need (excluding festival days) - Fishing. Some farming games have annoyingly tedious fishing mechanics. I hated it in Stardew and Dinkum. In here it’s easy- NPCs. I loved interacting with townsfolk. Every character is well written and feels alive, cutscenes are adding them depth- Romance. You can date anyone and at the same time (there’s an achievement for dating everyone) You can marry both genders and have a kid - Events. Events are well spaced throughout the year and they seem quite entertaining. I made some good money on autumn derbyThere are a few things that I didn’t like much. Animal breeding is a bit tedious and lengthy, especially for cows, alpacas. There are multiple things that you should do from the very beginning to play effectively like giving gifts to Kappa and Harvest Goddess. Some NPC romantic events are hard to trigger. Also, in the beginning I was a bit upset I couldn’t store my crops anywhere but my pockets until I have money for house upgrade and a fridge 😅Overall I’m having a great time and want to unlock all achievements for this game

_childDocuments_.review: Friends of Mineral Town: A Foreword...This particular game ignited my passion for farming games. While there's simulators akin to farming sim 20xx, I don't enjoy the depth into which they go regarding tools and machinery and their operation. But I LOVE the depth into which Story of Seasons - style games go into regarding RPG - like elements for relationships, upgrades, hidden items and events, and the general progression to end game content. I originally acquired it around age 10 on gameboy advance, and i still have it and was recently playing it. My thumbs are too sensitive now for the old D-Pad, so i switched to a ROM of More Friends of Mineral Town. This game combines the two, changes things up, polishes it, removes the issues with A Wonderful Life connectivity, and leaves me, overall, satisfied.The MeatYou like the traditional SoS game styles? Tired of what harvest moon has become? Doraemon not to your taste? Well, my good friend, come to my town and enjoy my latest harvest. Maybe we'll see the mayor or try to catch a drink with Karen. If we get too far under, we'll see Doctor for a tune up, though, i hear he tries some experimental stuff now and again. We can roam the beach, looking for bottles and different items, maybe play Disc with the dog, get ice cream. It may be a small town, but it has a lot going on just below the surface. you only need NOT SAY NO AT THE START OF THE GAME OMG. It literally asks you if you want to own the farm and if you say no -credits roll-. BRILLIANT! thats what im here for. SoS in it's purest form.~Changes~for starters, the biggest and most game-changing change is the inventory. it is INFINITELY larger than the GBA titles, even from day one. and their mechanics are different as well, leading to more possibilities. if anyone dare complain about that, just remember: a wonderful life had the biggest inventory of any game i can think of. page after page of rows upon rows of slots that went up to 99 each? that was monumental. the added inventory makes some "mine grinds" a little simple, but it's welcomed. no longer having to run from field to bin every 3 harvests is a big win, but i SWEAR they balanced it by changing the flow of time itself. Im not 100% sure on this, though it does seem to take the same amount of time.the sprites appear to have been nerfed. its a bummer, in my eyes. i have 3 when id usually have 1. but no matter. it can be seen as welcomed balance. BUT they have been improved in the hiring dialogue so you can fix mistakes without ruining your harvest. thats infinitely more valuable. walk through any crop! game changer! no more 3x3 boxes with the middle of an edge missing. you know the shape ;). just till everything, plant, and go nuts. the horse also has better controls over obstacles (as in, ignoring them entirely). and being able to bring the horse to the town and mountain is a LIFESAVER. though, it appears as though he doesnt have the saddle bags.one of my biggest issues at this point is the targetting. you want to brush that cow? it HAS to say their name in the box or you will miss. even if you are facing them and within a tile. that DOES help with overlapped animals, but slows down play a tad.controller support is 100% fluid. its a little configurable, but nothing too crazy. keyboard configuration is next to non-existent, especially with the mouse. ~graphics~10/10. 100%. everything looks professional. though, some characters appear to have been changed slightly from how i imagined them in the original, but, alas, such is the problem with going from 128px to god knows how many pixels. colours are awesome. portraits have so much personality.~sound~8/10, with music being 5/10. sorry guys, some sounds are bad and about half the tracks are really out there (KEEP IN MIND IM ONLY CONSIDERING THE ONES THAT ONE WOULD EXPERIENCE AS LONG AS THEY DONT BUY ANY FROM VAN) fall and summer have some... interesting tunes. winter is very nice, spring is acceptable. cows i find are a little percussive. theres no music in the mines, but, to be honest, youd hear the same start of the same song over and over on GBA anyway. footsteps hurt my ears. theres limited options for sound configuration. id just like to limit animal sounds and footsteps. ~character~hoo boy, you get either a boy or a girl, and either one can marry either a boy or a girl! i played a girl and married Ran. I wont ruin how it accommodates for the hopeful parent. its beautiful. all ill say.outfit choices are on point. romance options are endless**might be about 10, but, come on, thats nearly endless.one small issue i had was acquiring the dog. its a somewhat hidden trick to getting him. its not DIFFICULT by any means, but not as simple as GBA. on the same note, theres more pet options, on rotation. neat.~~summary~~there will be those who love this title. there will be those who scorn its very existence. some changes are huge and bring the game to nearly an entirely different state, but, honestly, are they not justified? it brings back ALL the memories of the earlier versions. i feel just as rewarded for every thing i do. id say if you have enjoyed eastern farming/rpg sims, especially those of SoS or the (earlier) harvest moon (which were SoS in disguise!), id recommend it. easily. its pure wholesome goodness.i thank any and all readers. let's get back to the farm!-Omniguous

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. When I saw it,I knew that I wanted it straight away, and my friend was kind enough to get it for me as a birthday present when it was on sale. The graphics are great, The 3D format is different from other farming sims I have played, the farming business isn't too hard and therefore you have far more time to run around the town doing other things compared to other farming sims. The time stops when you enter a property which is really handy as usually in these games, time always ticking away is always a big stressor; however there are a few downfalls:I would say the character depth is a little shallow, and the fact that you can catch different types of fish, but they stack as only 'small' 'medium' or 'large' is a bit disappointing. There is also a feature where you cannot go outside on windy days, which I hope they will change, because the only option is to go back to bed, and sometimes it can be several days before the wind stops.The events throughout the year, though I have not experienced all of them yet, seem to be quite shallow with not much script or thought put into them which makes them dull rather than exciting -such as those events in Stardew Valley which are absolutely brilliant.Never the less, I will continue to play this game because I really do love it, even though it has the potential to be much better; however I recommend that it is bought when on sale, as I am not sure it is worth it's full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, my enjoyment of this game was pretty positive with some minor issues.First thing to be said, yes, this is a remake of Friends/More Friends of Mineral Town on the GBA.  If you liked Friends/More Friends of Mineral Town on the GBA, Back to Nature on the PSX, or Harvest Moon 64 on the N64 back in the day, you will love this game.  This is a faithful remake with some much needed quality of life upgrades and a few additions to make life easier.  Pretty much, if you have played the GBA games, you can easily dive into this game and know what to do, who is who in mineral town, where certain villagers go at certain times of the day, what shops are open and when, what villager likes what present, the original heart events and some town events.Let's get into the positives first:-No littering.  Holy crap, it was so annoying in the GBA version when you accidentally tossed something on the ground because you pressed the wrong button.  Or even worse, when you want to give them something and you accidentally drop it (BIG problem in the 3DS games, even better when you're near a body of water and your gift goes flying in the lake). -More bag space.  You start out with 4 tool slots (Up to 12 with upgrade), and 9 inventory slots (Up to 27 with upgrade), and items stack up to 9 in the inventory (So you can carry say 18 1 star turnips, but they only take up 2 slots in your inventory slot bag).  I'm so glad we no longer have to carry around the big basket whenever we go anywhere.  In fact, fun Easter egg, you can actually find the basket in Jeff's shop still.  >.>  The grown up pony, however, does not have a pouch, so you still have to run to the bin to empty your inventory.-Bell for herding animals outside.  Animals can go out on sunny/snowy days and will automatically go back inside the farm at 8 pm.  As long as you have grass for the barn animals outside, they will graze, and chickens and rabbits will eat on their own.  So you basically don't have to worry about it.  -You can keep track of everyone's friendships in the menu screen.  This includes love interests and town friendships, which you'll need to raise for some recipes or to see some events/new events.  Very useful when it comes to the sprites.-You can have 5 pets now and can choose between dogs, cats, penguins, and capybara.  You can choose what type or color of your animal too.  There's 3 kinds of dogs and 3 kinds of cats and two different colors for the other animals.  I haven't found any use for the pets beyond the disk throw, since in previous games, your pet kept wild dogs away from your animals.-Same sex marriage.  About freaking time.  And this is implemented in a very good way.  Playing as a female, the majority, if not all, the rival events range from being friendship to close friendship, the only way for you go beyond that is to confess to one of the same sex love interests.-A bit of customization at the beginning of the game.  You can choose to play as the original characters or new character designs and change your skin tone.  You can also customize your outfit to the original in different colors, the newer outfits in different colors, or other costumes, like the cow costume, the sprite costume, and other DLC costumes.-Some new little things include:  Farm rank, fishing and guardian fish, Alpaca, 3 new cows, bunnies, white and brown colored chickens, new heart events, 2 new love interests (male and female), keeping track of what's on your farm via your map (What crops are growing, where your horse/pet is)Now to things I'm neutral about or just an opinion that can go either way:-Mining.  It's basically the same as the original, and the only real way to go down is via save scumming or having the elevator ready.  You either are gonna love it or hate it.  It is what it is.-Gifting the Goddess.  I personally hated having to go to the pond every day to feed her gifts, mostly because you HAVE to do it.  She's the only way to unlock the pet seller and a NPC that will give you certain recipes, so you need to go here and do it asap.-No multiple gift giving.  That means you can't load up on grapes and then mass give them to Cliff and get him red heart in one day.  This could be seen as a negative, but I didn't care too much either way.-Some cheats are still left in the game.  Some people may like this, but I think it cheapens the game and the wrecks the replay value.  As much as it's nice to see me go from like half a million to almost 3 million cause of the horse derby or being able to grow pineapples all year around and see the money roll in, it does make one grow bored with the game fast.-Winter is still a dead month.  I mean, it's the perfect time to do mine stuff, but honestly, you can knock that out in one season if you plan right, and then what are you left to do next winter?-Graphics and character design changes.  I personally liked most of the new designs, but some people might not like them or the chibi like graphics.  It's kinda jarring because remember, the characters are supposed to be in their early to mid 20's bare minimum.  -Minor censoring.  Any references to wine and drinking are censored, I noticed.  I'm guessing to hit that E rating.  Very minor issue for me.And now for the bad:-Breeding.  This is a good concept in theory.  And it works fine on chickens/bunnies.  But it's horrible on barn animals.   Basically, the only way to go beyond 5 hearts for all animals save pets is to breed them.  Chickens and bunnies don't take that long to breed, but the barn animals, all take at least 21 days to give birth, then more time to grow up.  AND on top of that, the new cows are not affected by each other.  Say you have a regular cow and a fruit cow, and you bred the regular cow so that the new baby cow will get 8 hearts.  That does not apply to the fruit cow, as it will give birth to a baby with 6.  So it's going to take maybe 3-4 in game years at minimum to get all your barn animals to 10 hearts.  Best fix would be to make the cow pregnancy 14 days instead of 21, or have 2 pregnancy bins for a small barn and 4 pregnancy bins for a big barn.-No rival events.  I really don't get why this is such an issue in Japan, because rival events and seeing your friends get married along with you is natural progression.  Seeing characters have obvious crushes on one another and never get married is weird and kinda sad.  Also, some characters lose their growth because of it (Best example is when Karen marries Rick, she gets better at cooking in the cooking festival.  You won't see that growth now).  The easiest fix to this would to put an option in the menu and toogle it on or off, or even do it at the beginning of the game.  -New love interests are boring.   It's an opinion here, but I don't care much for the two new characters, they're boring compared to the others.-Bugs.  Switch version can't get Mythic ore (Big bummer), and Brandon's dialogue is currently bugged.  Also minor issues like lag spikes in certain areas and getting stuck that the button to go through stuff doesn't fix.-Can get boring really fast.  This is because it's very simple game, there's no real overarcing storyline, so you can get bored before hitting year 3, depending on how you play.-Price.  This isn't a 50 dollar game, imo, it offers way less than Trio of Towns and Trio has way more to offer.  Not a big deal to me, but this could be an issue for others on a tight budget, especially nowadays.Overall, even with some of the negatives, I'd still enjoyed playing this game and recommend it to any fan of the series.  I hope Marvelous fixes the bugs and maybe improves on some things or adds in rival events as DLC in the future.  I had to cut down on the review a bit (Got too long to post), but if you don't know about the Marvelous/Natsume situation, please go to the discussion boards, most people there cleared it up.

_childDocuments_.review: "Welcome to the old friendly Mineral Town" Story of Season Friends of Mineral town is a remake of the classic Harvest Moon: FOMT/MFOMT with a touch of modern visual upgrades and improvement but still retain the core of the original series that everyone loves. _childDocuments_.review: This is an updated version of Mineral Town for the Gameboy Advance, merging both the boy and girl versions of the game into one package. You can easily break the game in half whenever you desire by taking advantage of multiple item gimmicks.I give the developer props for actually having the guts this time around to allow marriage to any of the dating choices, as opposed to having a 'best friends ceremony' if you go same-sex. Respect.What I cannot respect, and easily is the biggest mark against the game is that your dating choices have most of their events removed. This means that nobody in this town will develop relationships or get married besides you. While it's nice that you don't have to worry about somehow losing your choice anymore, it really does make the town feel that much more lifeless when there's no changes to anything as time goes on.If you can look past this bizarre decision, this is indeed the game that was the inspiration for Stardew Valley and worth a play if you're into farming games.Also if you're into super extreme grinding challenges? This is easily the king of the grind for the farming genre of games. Random challenges that deliver absolutely no reward and take hundreds of hours to do? This game has got you covered with the farming degree system and the seven rings to be obtained.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing Harvest Moon games but never played the original FOMT, so I was excited to play it for the first time. I can't comment on changes/additions to the game, but it definitely feels like an old game... in a bad way. The gameplay gets stale very quickly because there isn't much to do. If you want to have any decent amount of crops on your farm, you won't have enough energy to tend to them, so you need to either employ the nature sprites or use all your energy and then sit in the hot spring waiting for it to replenish so you can finish. Rinse and repeat every day. I'd guess that this gets better as you progress but at nearly 20 hours, not much has changed and I don't really want to keep playing. My main issue is the game's graphics. There's a huge disconnect between the 3D graphics and the 2D gameplay. Cutscenes feel weird because of it and a lot of things that I'm sure probably looked cool in the original pixel art just fall flat in this version. Even without this problem though, the graphics are generally just not very good. With some better textures and more dramatic lighting, the game might look okay, but the graphics feels really cheap as is. The character portraits look great, although the characters look VERY young considering that you're romancing and marrying them. Feels weird. The only redeeming part of the graphics is the animals. The cows especially are adorable.I genuinely feel that an HD port of the original with some small tweaks would be a lot more enjoyable (for maybe $15), but this version just feels like a quick cash grab from Marvelous. You might enjoy the game, especially if you played the original, but it's absolutely not worth $40. I got the game half off and it still feels like a rip off.

_childDocuments_.review: Friends of Mineral Town was one of the first Gameboy games I owned as a child. I was rubbish at the game and when my safe got corrupted, I realised just how much stuff I had missed in my first playthrough.This game is huge. It was one of the first of its kind where the player had to befriend the town folk and, ultimately, build their own family. Scenes, events, building your farm -- all these elements are what make the Harvest Moon franchise so different. You come to love the characters.For new players, the game can be a bit overwhelming, which is why the easy mode was implemented. If you've never played a game like Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, etc., the easy mode will save you a lot of heartache.To the features of this particular edition of Harvest Moon:You could argue that this sounds just like Stardew Valley and I wouldn't disagree; however, what makes Harvest Moon better is the friendships you get to forge along the way. The game contains several mini games and events which really set it apart.Are there any negative points?Needless to say, this version of the game contains a tutorial. As soon as you meet the requirements of scenes/events/places, you will get a popup. These notes are absolutely necessary for beginners and will help you survive your first year.Is the game worth full price? Although I love the game, it wasn't worth the price for me. If you are totally new to the franchise, full price could be, however, totally worth it.One tip for anybody: Don't forget to befriend Cliff! Don't let him move away.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a general nostalgia for the Harvest Moon/Story of Season games. Magical Melody was one of my favorite games growing up and Harvest Moon: Cute edition on my DS was a well worn favorite. I was hoping Friends of Mineral town would be a similar experience. It was not unfortunately. Before I begin: Friends of Mineral Town is not a bad game. In fact, if you're trying to get someone who hasn't played many games before into the genre, I think this would be a good first venture. It's easy-going, a small map, and there's a reasonable amount of characters to keep track of. It's cozy to say the least.That being said, if you're like me who has played the later entries in the series or have played other farm sims, the game play gets dull rather quickly. Many of the objectives feel given to you, there feels very little sense of progression except the knowledge you must eventually get better crops and more animals. While it's understandable that Mineral Town is less dynamic than other games in this series, it doesn't make the fact that I don't feel compelled to play any longer any less true. If a game makes me want to play a different game rather than this one, than something is wrong. If you're looking for a blast of nostalgia or if you're new to playing games in general and want a simple experience, it wouldn't hurt to give it a go. Otherwise, while this game has a lot of building blocks of later installments both in the Story of Season games and farming sims in general, for $40, you can find other games much more worth your time that have taken the foundation that Mineral Town laid down, and make a far more complete and satisfying experience.
