_childDocuments_.review: Well... It all started in 2008, when I had 10-11 years. I bought an used PS1 game from a friend. Wasn't an original game, and the label on it was just "fazendinha" ("little farm" in english). He was selling it for a pretty cheap price, so I couldn't refuse it.When I started, I was greeted with a heartwarming music and the game's original title. It was "Harvest Moon: Back To Nature". By the time I selected that "New Game" option, I've opened a door to a kind of game that I would love from now on. Yeah, I fell in love with farming simulation games. I fell in love with games where the enviroment was a country town. And most important: I fell in love with games with lots of things that you're actually motivated to discover. Oh, and another important thing that happened with me when I started playing it: I actually was starting to learning english, thanks to the game. It kept me interested enough to the point I was willing to learn english just to understand what was happening on each part of the gameplay.The memories are pretty clear in my mind: I didn't have a good computer at that time, but it helped me a lot to go through the game. It was that kind of white-ish computer that would turn yellow with the time, the hardware probably wasn't the best, and I was basically stuck on Windows 98. Internet connection wasn't possible for me, since the telephone cable wouldn't reach the plug, and the computer, for some reason, was unable to read USB drivers. All I could do was to grab up my 3 1/2" diskettes and go to the free lanhouse that I used to go, and copy in notepad files everything related to the game, from cutscenes to recipes, go back to home, turn on the videogame and computer and keep playing. Joystick on one hand, english-portuguese dictionary on the other, and making a pause from time to time to read those files.And this remaster is pretty much the same game that I used to play on my childhood and transcribes the same feeling I had when I was a little kid, but with lots of upgrades in some aspects, like selecting the gender (on the past, there was the two versions for the game, one with the male protagonist and the other with the female protagonist), riding the horse wherever you want to (you were only able to ride the horse on the farm), and etc.There's basically only four aspects from this game that I didn't like (which I'd like to remember, it's just my opinion, don't hold back on buying the game because of it):1st: There's no greenhouse. Yeah, I know, this game is actually a remaster of Friends of Mineral Town, from GameBoy Advance, and there wasn't greenhouse as well, but... Since this remaster is an "upgraded" version of the game.2nd: Some missing NPC characters from the PS1 game, like Greg (the fisherman that used to live next to Zack) and Louis (the entomologist that used to live with Gotz, now known as Gotts). If there's some new characters on the game, why not keep the old ones too?3rd: No brazilian (and/or even european) portuguese language available. I don't bother playing it in english, as I said, I learned by playing the game, but for people who doesn't understand, it's kinda difficult to keep playing. I'd even volunteer myself to help on the translation, if possible.4th, the most important: The game still doesn't start for some players. It was closing after starting for me on the first three days since the game was released. It was something related with the "AVX instruction", which isn't present on some processors, like mine (Pentium G4560, but already changed to a Ryzen 5 1600 AF, which supports AVX). They already patched it, even added a "Compatibility Mode" to work around this problem. But yeah, the game still won't start for some people. Nothing that a refund would solve, or some patches that the developers will kindly release.There are also some minor bugs within the game, that I believe they'll be corrected with the time. But the game is amazing, nevertheless. You should try it, for real.Sorry for any sentence mistakes that I committed (probably there's a ton of them). I'm still learning the language. Heheheheheh.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad to see that Marvelous took Mineral Town and improved upon it, but imo, they did NOT go far enough.First, you can WALK on crops. Meaning, you can fully utilize your fields!! It's disturbing how long it took to get this far. For some reason, you still can't walk over weeds.And something I've been wanting since 1997. A BELL. That's right. You NO longer have to INDIVIDUALLY push livestock out/into the barn(s). There's a bigger coop for the birds. There's MORE animals. They've really done it.Fodder grows like sod instead of seeding.Now for the bad.The MINE/GODDESS/KAPPA. You have to wait once a day to gift Goddess/Kappa to unlock further characters/rewards. Since crops have rating systems and Kappa/Goddess have personal tastes that should effect how much it unlocks. For example, If i give Kappa a 5-star cucumber (his favorite) that should count as 10 gifts. There's no reason to give them expensive stuff as it all counts the same. 75 straight days just to unlock Lou. That's almost a year and only if you have enough gifts to NOT miss a day.The mine is TOOOO big. You can get an elevator through the goddess, but see above paragraph. Plus, your upgraded tools CANNOT be utilized in the mine.Romance. You can't harem it up and they don't help around the farm. The slumber party is only available for the female protagonist. The western version allows Homosexuality and there's an achievement to confess to every romance option. You have to confess to ALL of them regardless of your character's backstory.Once married, they all assume the base personality, becoming this background prop. Each spouse should have different traits/benefits for marriage. Don't even worry about the personality when choosing a spouse because once married, it's gone. Pick the hottest and get over it.They should have Pros and cons. Karen's an alcoholic so you have to watch her around the kitchen or she'll burn your house down, but she's good at making stamina drinks, etc. That's an extreme example, but at least it distinguishes and carries her personality.  Ran is a busy-body so she's ideal for homemaking. Popuri grew up on a farm, so she helps around the farm. etc. Librarian figures out ways to increase yield and quality. etc.Winter, just like in the original, there are NO winter crops. Which is a real shame. I literally sleep through the month. Having the sprites do all the work.The beds are crammed together. You can upgrade your house, but it's the 90's method of everything crammed into an open space. The upgrades should include an upstairs and individual rooms. Like a normal house. You're literally sleeping with you kid and wife...The Ugly:They got rid of the lumber storage. You have to personally put it INSIDE your house cabinet. 9 pieces at a time. because that's where people store building materials???? Fodder is no longer automatically stored, either.Festivals are boring. This is on a console/pc in 2020. The original FF7 has a better chocobo/horse racing mechanic. Someone needs to upgrade the mini-games.I give it 2/5 stars because it improves upon some features, but ultimately adds nothing to the series. If they could merge this with the HM gamecube's tools (milkers, seed mixer, etc), and various fields for crops and orchards, it'd be a perfect game.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly makes me feel like a kid again, I had the game for the Gameboy Advance and I still have that working copy of the game too and my lord comparing this to the GBA version, just so much QOL.- The updated inventory is a god send, having things stack makes life so much better- The fact you can't just throw away items by accident or mis-clicking anymore, god I hated that so much on the GBA version.- Pitfalls are a blessing, hated mindlessly trying to find the way down in mines.- Walking over crops is great, I remember when you had plants that had multiple yields you couldn't get the middle ones due to you can't access them.- Different variations of livestock. (Although some are definitely on the quirky side).- Same-sex marriage, good for the people who wanted that, considering the original games were gender locked marriages and also separate games for the male or female protag.- Following that last statement, the fact the game isn't split in 2 for either gender.- Actually being able to see how much stamina you have, it was visible but not in a bar form.- Crop rarities, definitely a cool add, also gets you more money.I do miss some of the things though, some of the original names/character models, probably just old nostalgic me wanting to see them again.- Zack was drastically was changed, I do prefer the older version.- Some names got slightly adjusted like Mary/Marie, Ann/Ran, Elli/Elly, Won/Huang, etc. While I'm not sure why they decided to do name adjustments, I'm not too bothered by it.- The beginning story was changed a bit from both ends of the game compared to this one.- Controls are kinda weird.- The price is kind of a yikes, I bought it on sale, so I'd wait till then to buy it.- The achievements are definitely on the rough side if you're trying to get them all.While I only have minor complaints, none of them really interfere with the gameplay at all, I still enjoy it a lot. The game gives me nostalgia from those late nights as a kid playing this game on my GBA, 10-12 years ago. Playing this remake makes me feel old in a good way. I just hope they remake Magical Melody that was on the Gamecube. I recommend this game to any who has played the game before or wants a relaxing and laid-back game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the spirit of casual farming, an awesome game to boot up when you just wanna relax but still feel like you're doing something important. Even then, if you're feeling like talking to people and managing farming at the same time is a chore, there's a difficulty setting for that.Still i wouldn't say this game is for you if you aren't ready to devote a lot of time to it. I have played 42 hours and only just now got married and my crops are only level 3 at most. The game is split up in days, seasons and years, some events are season specific or will not occur until year 2 or later.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I just tried it, and I know I'm being biased. But I already loved it. And if you loved the original Harvest Moon Back to Nature, then you will instantly love this too. They kept all the beautiful things that made me fell in love on the first game. The iconic music that I hum even after 20 years from the first time I played it, it's still there! And even the satisfying sound effects when doing various things! So I thought "Did they just re-skinned the entire thing?" but no. They also added a whole lot of QOL improvements.I played a lot of HM and SOS games, but I always loved Back to Nature the most. I emulated this game on all my devices (ipad, laptop, and phone) with three different saves. And I've completed the game more than twice. There is really nothing to hate here. If you are new to Harvest Moon or SOS, then you might like some titles better, but for me, this just hits me in the heart. Now I can't wait to woo that librarian once again for the 10th time.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons series and I held the original Friends of Mineral Town in high regard and it has long been my favorite in the series but it's hard to ignore the this remake sticks so close to the original and makes this title feel like it was made in a vacuum. This title sticks so close to the original and the game feels like a GBA title restrictions and all. Picking up items/brushing animals feels so stiff, when working to a grid based control when watering if feels so archaic and unwarranted to move so slowing same with gathering crops. The graphics are fine in the context of sticking to the original and the updated character art is nice.It's hard to ignore the competition such as Stardew Valley and simply how much more gameplay, better UI, character interactions and more and for a fraction of the price. I've put in 23 hours at time of review and I won't like that the nostalgia has kept me playing and its almost like comfort food but I yearn for more especially at this price point. Fun but its like going back in time for better and worse.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so relaxing.  Everything is cute and the music is peaceful and uplifting. There's no rush to do anything in particular.  You farm what you want, you go mining when you want, you go fishing when you want, you make friends or get married if/when you want.  I really think this game was designed without stress triggers.There are no real surprises for fans of the series, although they've added a few new animals that I hadn't seen in their other games: angora rabbits, llamas, strawberry milk cows and fruit milk cows (in my mind they are clearly banana milk cows).All in all, it is fantastic on PC and works great with a controller.  I hope they bring more of them over (like the new Rune Factory Switch port, please).  Highly recommended for fans of the series or for anyone looking for some stress relief.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:If you're looking for a nice and simple nostalgic game to unwind, I think you would enjoy this. I recommend you to play it very slow, no need to rush at all. Also, use console. For a remake, the job's done, that's all there is to it. But to be honest, it's a yes and no for me. I expected more content. Although, it's still a nice game overall, I don't hate it.---Before anything else, I haven't played the original FoMT series. I've played A Wonderful Life and I'm sure it has similar function and the amount of plot. I also hate comparing games, so I won't be doing that.Visually, I think SoS: FoMT did a pretty good job on the character redesign. Also overall style seems to be fitting, nice and cute. I also enjoy the new added characters and animals. Memory is also not big so that's a plus!And now I'd like to point out some things.Firstly,I think this game is pretty fast paced (story wise) and it gets boring after you finish the plot. I feel like most of the goals only revolves around the residents. And in the first year (normal mode), I managed to max out almost all residents' FP and LP (besides Kai, and the specials). After you max them out, I realize that there's nothing else there. I think the resident's FP will go down if you don't talk/give presents after a certain amount of days, but there's nothing new to achieve. And since it only focus on the character's stories, there's also not much going on besides that. Sure, there are seasonal events, collectibles, other activities, but especially mining and fishing, to me, seems too mundane and repetitive. I think there is room for improvement there.Secondly,I'm glad that this is released on PC. However, I find it quite challenging to use on mouse and keyboard (if you don't have console, like me). I find the key/button shortcuts don't seem to be very efficient, some keys also can't be changed, like the exit key, which is a "Backspace" (later I found that it's also a left click, phew!)Lastly,I got this on sale. But for a full price, I think this game is a bit overpriced. Again, I don't like comparing, but I expected more if I'm paying that amount of price.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not normally a review writing kinda guy, but something compelled me to start writing this one up for one of my favorite games as a child. I know this review is negative, however, most of my gripes with the game are due to it being a 2021 release. I still love the game, putting 75 and a half hours as of writing this in the last week and a half to bust out all the achievements. It's just that there are better games for cheaper. This review will be split into 3 parts ; Part one for general game stuff such as controls, part two for if you've played the original Friends of Mineral Town for GameBoy, and another part for if you have never played it and/or have no idea what this shhh even is.Part 1 : GeneralRight off the bat, it's immediately apparent this game is pulled directly from some mobile device, my guess is the Switch. The default "Cancel" button is BackSpace. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BackSpace??? And I couldn't find an option to change specifically that in the controls. But I got used to it... after like 20 hours of playtime. And the limited direction of movement makes it clear this was coming from the GameBoy, as moving in a non cardinal direction is less then ideal on a keyboard, which makes it more clear it comes from the Switch. I wasn't originally planning on getting every achievement to the game, hell, I wasn't even planning on writing a review for this, but around hour 50-60, I felt compelled to speak my mind. So around the middle to end of Summer, or 25-30 hours in I started working on that. On a first play through, playing to the end of the day, midnightish, every day, should take about 20 hours of play time to get through 1 season. Sounds like a lot right? Well yes but no. Remember, this is a farming sim, it's literally designed to eat your time. While you can see most of the content the game has to offer in a single season, the little nuances remain to be seen until you go through an entire year. One thing I will mention, spoilers for in game content/money making,  I went the first 2 seasons struggling to afford the things I wanted. I would plan what to buy and what not to, but then that came around and, OOPS, I'm a millionaire. It defeats the purpose of the final thing you can buy in the game, which I didn't even bother to purchase, because to OBTAIN said money, you have to sell EACH ITEM INDIVIDUALLY ONE AT A TIME to Huang. Like... WHAT?! It took me an hour to sell an entire inventory, and I even tried to set up a macro on my keyboard so I wouldnt ♥♥♥♥♥♥ have to do it. But I digress. Autumn Year 1, and I have 2 million. I spent half of that between Fall 18th and Winter 18th. I never spent money for the rest of the game. Lastely the mining in this game is dated and archaic. I hate it. Avoid mining except to upgrade tools or if going for completion. Speaking of which, I coulda shaved off like 20 hours of playtime if I didn't think I had to ship every item in the shipping log for an achievement, and if it didnt take almost a FULL YEAR to get 8 hearts with a pet to get a new one. I guess I can touch on that, the final 2 achievements that took me like 15 real hours were the 5 pets and the cook/ eat all recipes ones. the 5 pets is just stupid, and cook every recipe, the Autumn Sun is the last one you'll get. X Animal Produce is damn near impossible to get in a normal playthrough, let alone quickly. From this point on, you now move to the part of the review which best suits you, Veteran or Newcomer.Part 2 : Return for NostalgiaIf you played the original FoMT on GameBoy, and you want to relive that, 100% buy this game... on sale. Because it is the EXACT same game. over 15 years later. For $40. Stardew Valley does eveything here but better and more, for over half the price. Only buy this for a trip down memory lane. The content is just as lack luster as it was back then. I can not recommend this game anymore then that. Revisiting a ton of old faces with redesigns and even glow ups is breathtaking the first time you see them **Although I don't like how they massacred my girl Karen**. The only noteable improvements from the original is they ditched the basket bullsh!t and went with the Stardew Valley approach to inventory in that you have a hotbar now, and see your whole inventory right there. And you can now see your stamina at all times, instead of having to get the Goddess Gem this time. Although the Goddess and Kappa Gems are still in the game, but have different functions. And the truth jewels are less useful in this version because of it, and surprisingly, 10x harder to get the last one. So, whatever. And as for how you used to have to leave that one tile open to harvest your crops, they got rid of that too. Which thank god for. Mining is still just as BS is it used to be, as stated in part 1, only do it to upgrade tools or for completion. The money isnt worth it, there is however now  As for anything else, that's pretty much all that I can say for Veterans. Buy this game if you want a nostalgia hit, but don't bet on Horse Races if you don't want your sense of money ruined. Oh, and they got rid of Rival marriages, but added same sex marriages and 2 new canidates, Jennifer and Brandon. NO RIVAL MARRIAGES??? 0/10Part 3 : NewcomersSo you've never even heard of a Friends of Mineral Town huh? Well you might have heard of Stardew Valley, or Harvest Moon in general, but realized that modern Harvest Moon games are dogsh!t. Well for those still unaware, sometime in 2007ish, the actual creators of Harvest Moon lost the rights to using the name, and made their own thing, which the publishers got the name, and then decided to make their own games with the name, which every one of them after that point was kinda dookie, and the real Harvest Moon creators had to legally use a new name, and they went with Story of Seasons. Even myself didn't know this until recently, and apparently they have other SoS games, so might check those out. Anyway, this is an EXACT copy of the GameBoy Advance title under the same name, with a couple minor tweaks for quality of life and some random name changes. As for the game, assuming you have played Stardew Valley and are looking for more farming content... this aint it. going from Stardew to this, is a complete down grade. The amount of content to price in SV to this is baffling if you never played the original. There is little to nothing added to help elongate the end game, the amount of unique dialogue lines is shockingly small, and 1 in game year is enough to show you all that it has to offer.Overall I think that :This game should be avoided if you never played the originalIf you DO buy it, buy it on sale, or better yet, I think it would handle better on Nintendo Switch, as it seems thats what its meant forDO buy it if you want to support the REAL Harvest Moon creators, thus propelling the name back to where it should be, and maybe making more new games?And I know this entire review is negative, but I love this game... as someone who played the original. Do I love it as much as $40? No. But I fall under the catagory for all the reasons you SHOULD buy this. So I enjoyed you. You probably won't. But I did.And uhhh Marie had a glow-up on god.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good performance, and the graphics are quite unique but you get used to them, and now I like them. There aren't that many changes to the game from the Game Boy version, which you could say is good or bad. I'm not sure I could put too much trust in these developers to make too many big changes. I only say that because some of the changes they did make are pretty bad. A lot of these changes seem fine on the surface, but you only really start noticing the problems after playing for a long time.There are 4 big changes to talk about, and they are all kind of connected.1. No cooking without using a collected recipe. I honestly have no idea why they made this change other than maybe if they thought cooking was too complicated before. But it was such a cool aspect of the old game, and it was fun to experiment and find the best way to cook each thing. Also 10 of the recipes in this game are given out by a character named Lou who only appears after you give 75 offerings to the Harvest Goddess (1 per day). Giving offerings is sort of a hidden mechanic, but is very important. In my opinion some of the rewards should be moved out of it, like Lou could just already be there from the start of the game.2. New animals. Not entirely new though, more like variations of existing animals. There are now 3 different types of wool, 4 different types of milk, and still 1 egg even though there are 2 chicken colors. This would be fine, however there are literally zero cooking recipes that use these new products, and you can't convert them to milk, cheese or butter. The different milk types do ship for slightly more than the original, but overall it feels not very useful to have these animals at all. On top of that, if you are a completionist and trying to ship one of everything, these new animals only serve to make the game much much longer.3. Animals start with a maximum of 5 hearts out of a possible 10. How do you increase the maximum? You must breed them. This is kind of annoying but fine for chickens or rabbits, but when it comes to the other animals, it's a different story. Cows/sheep/alpacas have a pregnancy period of 20 days, and then after that they take another 20 days to become an adult. You must breed them 5 times for every single type of animal, that's 6 types, or 8 including chickens and rabbits. This means that it is impossible to start winning cow or sheep festivals until at least year 3, and that is if you are extremely fast. More realistically it'll be year 4 before you can win and start producing gold products. Notice I said "start" winning. With there being 4 types of cows, it'll take another 3 years to win once with every type. If you want to ship one of everything, you also have to be very careful you don't accidentally have your animals outside too much before they all are producing gold, or else when you do win a festival they might skip right over gold and go right to platinum products.4. Animals can no longer be hurt by your tools, or get sick, or die of old age. I can fully understand removing the ability to hurt animals, as you would usually only do it on accident anyways. However, this game has cooking recipes which require specific sizes of animal products. If you have all animals at 10 hearts, are at maximum capacity, and you need small milk, your only choice is to sell an animal, buy a new one, and then after you have enough of the small milk, sell that animal and breed another. But just wait it gets worse, because you need a lot of small and medium milks, and you probably won't want to rely on the harvest sprites to take care of your animals for you since they brush them and might get their hearts up too fast. But even just milking or shearing gets their hearts up, so you might be screwed regardless. There is absolutely no way to lower their hearts. Furthermore, with animals never being able to get sick or die, it really makes animals feel less real and more like a machine; you input fodder, output milk. You can feel secure in knowing that after you have all animals at max hearts, you never have to feed or interact with them ever again unless you want their product. This is so bad for what is supposed to be a simulation of animal farming.There is one other small change that I'd like to complain about, and that is being able to own more than one pet. Obviously, being able to have more than one, on its own is totally fine, or even a good thing. It's more the surrounding systems that are the problem. You need to have a ridiculously high 8 hearts with your newest pet before you can get the next. This isn't that bad, more of a slight annoyance, but if I had to guess, I think the main reason the devs did this is so that you don't have to play the disc throwing mini-game too much at a time. That and just to extend play time. But the hearts go up quite slowly on pets, and the guy who sells pets and pet treats only does so once per season, and all the pets are season exclusive. It's easy to forget because of how infrequent it is. It just makes the whole experience needlessly frustrating. There is absolutely no reason he couldn't be selling every week. And on the topic of mini-games, this game has a bunch of them, and honestly they are pretty good, but you are expected to play way too much of the same thing repeatedly. Even in the original version, you could play one of three mini-games with all seven of the harvest sprites every day. This version of the game does nothing to alleviate this problem.This version also removes rival marriages, apparently because people felt too time pressured or stressed. Well it would have been nice to at least have the option. There is also same sex marriage which is fine but also means it isn't really possible to just be friends with everyone. Even if you don't give them the new item in this game that gets you officially "dating" you'll still receive chocolate or invites on festival days, which is clearly romantic in nature. That's not even mentioning the heart events or dialogue.Now, this game quite well programmed, very few bugs, but there are some other basic things that lack a bit of polish that you'd think would be fixed, like how the horse is so massive that it's hard to dismount anywhere, and when you do dismount it, you are placed inside of its hitbox and cannot move parallel to the horse, only away from it. Or how there's the one leaf pile in autumn that is too low and clipping into the ground, constantly flickering (Z-fighting). Or like how they reduced the cost of the town house, but forgot to change the amount in the description of it on the world map. Also I find it strange that there wasn't any new house customization added, like wall colors. That would have been an easy good change. Anyway I still recommend this game, but be prepared to grind your face off even more than the original.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to recommend this game, but I'm rather conflicted about it.I grew up on Harvest Moon: Back to Nature. I don't think I ever truly played Friends of Mineral Town, except maybe for a brief bit on an emulator as a phone game. And I adored BTN, and loved it for years.Honestly, the nostalgia of this is excellent- and it's lovely to see the characters I missed and the world I loved in 3d, and hear the songs of my past brought from 8 bit into actual instruments. But there's a number of relatively minor complaints that I just cannot get over.-THE ANIMATIONS ARE SO LONG OH GOD WHY. it's insane! I've heard complaints that the day is too short, but honestly, when the animation for watering your crops takes a full 10 ingame minutes, and it takes your dog 30 minutes to pick up a ball and run back to you, no wonder the day feels so short! something that took a second in BTN seems to take ages in this game. if there was a mod to just make animations run just like 50% faster, I'd take it in a heartbeat.-For those playing on keyboard and mouse- you can definitely tell the game is made for controller. Some of the base controls are awkward but workable (I got used to using left click for select/confirm and right for exit/go back pretty quickly) but there's also some things that are just a plain nuisance- for some reason, I cannot seem to bind the "Put away" button away from "Backspace," of all things, though I've definitely tried the more standard "escape" and even a specific mouse button, and none seem to register. It seems minor till that's the only way to get off the horse you're mounting and dismounting all day.-Just annoying collision things. The fact that there are angles where your animals refuse to interact with you, despite you being close enough to push them- or, the fact that you can't push animals while holding items (like, y'know, their feed) and that the animals love to just clip in to eachother. cue me spending 10 minutes to wait for my sheep to wander out of my pregnant cow so I can actually groom her. or 4 cows wandering on top of a pregnant sheep. or chickens standing on top of their eggs. For the life of me I cannot remember if this was an annoyance in the main game and I just wasn't used to anything better, but dang.And more! so idk. maybe they won't stop me from playing, but I'm still grumpy about it.If you're a longtime fan of harvest moon- idk, play it for the nostalgia. For those just getting into the series, I absolutely recommend a game based on a game based on a game I love! just, y'know. expect some annoyances.

_childDocuments_.review: A nostalgic trip for those who played previous Harvest Moon titles, with a few quality-life-tweaks to help make the experience a lot less frustrating. NPC portraits are a hit-or-miss though, and are generally less attractive than the original portraits in my subjective opinion. For newcomers, I highly recommend SoS:FoMT as a casual, relaxing farming experience. It's far simpler than most other farming sims out there, also far more charming. No virtue-signaling or less-than-subtle commentaries on corporate economics here, just a plain old farming fantasy.I do, however, suggest that newcomers check out a few guides once they familiarize themselves with the basics. There are a lot of hidden secrets that are not obvious at first glance, like the helpers that you can hire to work the field with you.

_childDocuments_.review: Like almost everyone here, I played the original HM:FoMT when I was a kid. The game has a very special place in my heart. Also like everyone here, I picked up the game out of nostalgia. I am somewhat enjoying the ride as a walk through memory. As a farming simulation game though, I can't really recommend the game, not at this price.When you compare this game with Stardew Valley or even My Time at Portia, SoS:FoMT just does not have a lot of things to do. FoMT might have been a breakthrough when it came out all those years ago. But at this point in time, it simply lacks contents. I have this feeling that I will reach end game by the end of Fall at the rate I'm going.As I said, I still enjoy the game as I recall bits and pieces from my childhood. But for 50 bucks, you can obtain far superior options nowsaday. Heck, if you have played Stardew Valley, installing a freemode there probably give you more contents than starting this game anew.Updated: I'm a lot further in the game now, and nothing has happened to change my mind. Most of the contents run out by the end of the first year. The few stuffs left to do are still there only because it requires grinding or are excessively time-gated. For example, livestock now can only increase max heart if they are born on the farm. This is fine for chickens but for barn animals, they give birth and grow very slowly. It takes a month to obtain a mature barn animal that is born on the farm. So to get an animal with 10 max hearts, you need about 5 month. And that's just one type of animals.My original comment stands. I did enjoy the game because it brings back my childhood memories. As a standalone title, this game should cost $30 at most.

_childDocuments_.review: I have little to no experience with Harvest Moon games, so I can't compare this to the rest of the series. The game is absolutely adorable graphics wise, and that carried me through way more of the game than I would have really bothered with otherwise. That being said, behind the friendly smiles and gentle faces, exists only empty husks devoid of any sign of soul or true personality. There is little to be gained from interacting with villagers, and not much subsistence in other areas either.The farm cannot be customized, which on it's own doesn't really make-or-break anything, but it honestly removes any sense of pride to be gained from farming itself. Buildings, crop space, indoor decorations, are all predetermined and locked in. Farm animals are just depressing. To get better animal resources (eggs, milk, ect.) you need more hearts with your animals, which is pretty standard...... except each animal has a limit placed on how many hearts you can earn with it. The only way to increase this limit is to breed new ones and throw away the old ones for generations (years upon years of in-game time). Not worth the time or the energy. Pets are kind of cute, but are obnoxious to get a hold of due to high cost and seasonal restrictions. The festivals are as lifeless as the rest of the town, the cooking system is essentially the same as any other game in this genre, and I honestly can't remember much if anything of the story, so there isn't really anything remarkable in that department either.I liked the game, it was cute, and I had fun with it for a while just relaxing and enjoying the simple farm life. I wouldn't recommend this game to any of my peers with there being so many other games that can do everything this one does, and more, at the same price point. I would recommend this to younger players that don't mind a superficial level game, or those who are newer to video games that want to ease their way in with the absolute basics.

However, the number 1 thing most of you are thinking of...is that pricetag. Trust me I know. That price tag is ridiculous.I mean...50$ for this? That's absolutely ridiculous. _childDocuments_.review: I want to start my review by stating that I never played the original Harvest Moon.  However, I do have over 280 hours in Stardew Valley.  If you played Stardew Valley, I think you’ll like this game as well.  Both have similar aspects, but are also different enough that you can enjoy both.I originally picked up this game because while loving Stardew Valley, I was a bit tired of it.  I had romanced almost everyone and frankly didn’t want to put in the time to reach the new, later goals the game has in store.  I wanted an experience that was similar to Stardew, but offered new relationships and a new story.  Having now logged almost 41 hours in Story of Seasons, I can say that I truly enjoy this game and will continue to play it.  Below is a comparison for those who may have played Stardew Valley and are contemplating buying this game as well.  Obviously, these are subjective opinions.Stardew Does Better    • Customization – While you start out with more outfits in Story of Seasons, there are no fun hats for you or your horse.  You also cannot customize the layout of your house.  There are plenty of additional furniture pieces to buy, but their locations are pre-determined.  This is especially evident with the “big bed” required to marry a bachelor(ette).    • Mining Levels – Once you unlock the elevator, you get a stop every 5 levels.  With Story of Seasons, it’s every 50.    • Overarching story – In Stardew, you’re introduced to an overarching story early on with clear major goals.  There may be one in Story of Seasons as well, but I’m starting Year 2 and haven’t encountered anything yet.Story of Seasons Does Better    • Instant Products – With Stardew, you were able to get the mayo and cheese makers pretty quickly, but it took a bit for them to produce the product.  With Story of Seasons, it takes a bit longer to save up the money/materials for the machine, but you can do multiple batches in one and the result is instant (i.e. make 1 stack of 3 eggs into 3 mayos instantly)    • No Relationship Decay – If there’s any relationship decay, I’m unable to tell.  You can go a week without talking to someone and pay no penalty.  Some may find this a fault, but I like not having the pressure of having to talk to everyone everyday.    • No 2 AM cutoff – You can keep going as long as you have Stamina; there’s no penalty or instant fall asleep at 2 AM.  You may start with less stamina or more fatigue the next day, but you don’t have to worry about getting into bed before 2 am.

_childDocuments_.review: So, where to even begin with this. Is it a good game? Yeah, it's pretty fun....however, compared to other games out there of this genre, it falls woefully short. Is it fair to compare it other games like this? Given most of those 'other games' came out years ago, absolutely. Friends of Mineral town feels like a cheap Stardew Valley. Does it have mining? Sure, but it lacks the intricacies of Stardew. Does it have crafting? No, not really - you can SORT of make stuff like mayo, etc, but when it comes to actual crafting beyond cooking, you're out of luck. Monsters? Nope. Minigames? Sure, but most of them are not great. The characters are nice, but the portraits...whew, not exactly my cup of tea. Does it have neat things to upgrade your farm, sprinklers, etc? I've dumped 23 hours into this so far, and at least currently...no, there is not. There are harvest sprites to help you water/gather crops or do other menial chores, but there's no real customization.THEN it comes to the price. For a game that lacks SO MUCH compared to other games of this genre, could I suggest paying full price for it? Not a chance in hell. If you can get it 50+% off, is it worth it? Sure, it's a time killer, or if you've played Stardew/My Time at Portia/Rune Factory into the dirt and have done everything, then yeah, it might be a fun thing to dip into. Just don't expect the depth of any of those other games.Cannot say I recommend it when there is so much out there that does EVERYTHING better, and for a cheaper price.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been giving this another go after playing it on Switch and being too disappointed and underwhelmed by it to continue. I will state upfront that I never played Mineral Town on the Game Boy Advance back when it was still under the Harvest Moon name, so it's not scratching that nostalgia itch the way it would for fans of the original and that's likely heavily effecting my experience. All that said, after giving it another chance, I've come to the conclusion that it is a decent game. I was able to get some enjoyment out of it, it just doesn't hold a candle to the previous two for me personally. I would probably give it a "mixed" rating if it were available, but with my own bias in mind, and again, not having played the original, I decided to go with a thumbs up with some big caveats.The first two Story of Seasons are among my all-time favorite games, second only to Rune Factory 4. Having played all four Story of Seasons titles, there has been a noticeable (and in my opinion, negative) change in tone and style compared to the previous two, the first in particular. It's more compact, less detailed, and the world and characters just feel sterile in comparison, which is depressing considering how pretty the 3DS games were and what they could have achieved visually on a more powerful console, but didn't. The first game in particular dealt with heavy topics; the town  animals falling ill and dying of old age or if not cared for properly, elements which in this game appear to have either been glossed over or removed entirely.My biggest issue with Mineral town is a somewhat subjective and arguably a shallow one, but it bothered me immensely nonetheless. While I know this is a remake, as mentioned before, there's been a  shift in art direction since the first Story of Seasons game, particularly the portraits, which were much more painterly and detailed, and much less bobble-headed in previous games. As a visual novel junkie, portraits have always made a massive difference in immersion for me, and while the character sprites and portraits in this series have always been on the cutesy side and not completely proportionate, for me they still managed to strike a good balance between being cute yet able to be taken seriously when needed. This installment feels like they just grabbed the chibidometer and cranked it up to eleven to unsettling effect. It's a look that bugs me a lot less and I think can work well in titles like Animal Crossing, but in a game where you're procreating with the human townsfolk, it just doesn't do it for me and greatly detracted from my experience. Even the animal models look less appealing (cows in particular went from cute and stylized to big marshmallowy blobs barely resembling bovines) and this isn't just true of the Mineral Town remake; it's something they carried over to Olive Town, too. I really hope they eventually return to the old style, but if the most recent game is anything to go by, we'll be lucky if future games . While I didn't like the portrait style of this game, I'll still take it over the cold, soulless 3D stares of Olive Town any day. To me, Mineral Town marks the point where the series started taking a nosedive, and it's a little heartbreaking.One significant improvement that I do want to give Mineral Town credit for is the addition of same-sex marriage. Bachelors and bachelorettes are no longer gender-locked or relegated to being "best friends". You're free to romance them all with your protagonist of choice, and even if you prefer one demographic over the other, it's still nice to be able to see everyone's stories without having to start an entire new game to do so.Despite my issues with it, Mineral Town isn't a bad game in and of itself. Style and tone aside, the core mechanics remain largely the same, so it's still a solid farming/life sim that's sure to be loved by fans of its Harvest Moon predecessor, but if you're buying it as a die-hard fan of the first two Story of Seasons games like me, you may want to taper your expectations before diving in.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the old Harvest Moon and now Story of Season games. Since I'm an oldtime-fan, I was very hyped when this game came out but I actually have to admit...it's boring after some time. They cut the rival events down and there aren't proper rival couples anymore, the animals can't die or get sick which makes animal care boringly easy, you can't try-and-error-cook anymore but have to find recipes first before you even can fry rice...and the two new characters also don't spark much joy. For a reboot of a very beloved game, there was a huge lack of new features but a big cut on already well balanced game-play. Now you have a washed down Friends of Mineral Town for young children.Now don't get me wrong, I also don't need crops that have a freshness level and stuff but a bit of a challenge that carying for your animals is more meaningful would have been nice. More interaction between the characters like seeing their own weddings and children and such would have been amazing.But as it is, this is just a cash-grap run on the nostalgia of fans of the original FoMT. I really hope this is just a means to earn money during Covid-Times to fund the next Story of Seasons. I hope they really add up with new features...because balloon-cartoon-characters in a washed out FoMT-Version just won't cut it.6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Story of Seasons Friends of Mineral Town is such a blast to the past. Such a simple, relaxing title to the old Bokujō Monogatari series that's one of the most beloved for a reason and playing it again in 3D with more content is more than I could have asked for seeing this game come back to an even greater glory. There will always be a side of me that will prefer the charming bit-style visuals of the original FoMT but the QoL improvements in this enhancement also make it really hard to go back to play. I find it totally reasonable for anyone unwilling to spend 50 on this game but as a longtime fan I really don't feel bothered. The credits rolled around the beginning of Spring Year 2 but what I love about these games is how much credits really mean nothing with how much more left there is to do just after the single year you work your way up towards marriage and I've felt like I've been unable to put the game down since I launched it the day of release. Surprises me today how much there is to do in such a small map but that's what makes it so great. I don't know what it is about Stardew Valley that makes me bored after the first few seasons because the farming and farm customization is honestly 10/10, but I generally don't really care about the rest of it. The characters don't personally grab me at all and some other things that push me away whenever I try to start another run. FoMT has almost no bland characters and are all fun to get to know and unlock cutscenes for, only part I wish they included into the remake is the rival marriage scenes.speaking of marriage I genuinely tried going with another girl for the new run but I found myself under Elly's spell pretty much after the first few days and have chosen to marry her for the 500th time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is, as a re-re-release of the '99 "Back to Nature", or re-release of the '03 "Friends of Mineral Town", is pure nostalgia, and probably one of the best modernisations of a game I have seen to date.Not only is the original game praised as the best entry of the series, but the gameplay is modernised in fitting ways and while the 3D-Graphics are not impressive, they give the game a very retro feeling.The most important changes are the beatifully redrawn character portraits, the controls perfectly suited for the new platform and a whole new inventory system. But also some smaller changes like walking on crops and changes in tool usage make it more comfortable to play.New additions are new animals, the option to play as a girl (which was introduced in "More Friends of Mineral Town"), a new Bachelor and Bachelorette and new events.All in all, if you liked any older entry of the Harvest Moon series, you will love this game, since it brings all the good memories from those games back. But please be aware that the newer series entries play quite different, and are therefore not always comparable.

_childDocuments_.review: The thumbs down of this game is not because of the quality of the product or lack thereoff, but for the simple fact that this game when compared to similar games just is loosing constantly.Therefor, if you already own the other two games I will compare this game with and you just dont want to replay them again (which I can 100% understand) this game might actualy be a thumbs up for you. Review: I will compare this game to two similar games that I played before, "Stardew Valley" and "My Time at Portia".So let's look at the content first. 1)Stardew Valley not only has different Farm Layouts to start with that change (sometimes only slightly) the way you can build up and grow your farm, the map also feels/is bigger then the one of SoS:FoMT. And you can also decide to choose between two ways to improve the farm/town by choosing the Market or the Community Center.  In My Time at Portia you have only 1 Layout of your Workshop. The world itself however is so large that even tho you get nothing for crafting more busstations to fast-travel you be constantly keeping one or two of them in reserve so when you open up a new part of the world you have to walk or ride there just once and after that plant a busstation for quicktravel there. The Town is way bigger aswell and has quite a few hidden treasures to find. And while you are mainly a builder, the fact that you activly compete with another builder makes you decisions how to plan your days and build up your workshop/farm feel much more relevant. You aren't forced into hard competition, but you sure can do that and it's encouraging to see you turn from someone who get's constantly beat to someone who dominates the competition after a while if you put the effort into it.In SoS:FoMT there is (or I found only) one layout for your farm and the only choice you have when it comes to how you wanna play is wether you focus on animals, farming or try both equally. No story choices (I've seen so far) that have any impact at all. The Map of SoS:FoMT is also realy small. It is 10 maps (1. your farm; 2. the wood below (verry small, one house and a couple of trees you mostly cant interact with); 3. The lower town part (relativly small, 3 or 4 houses); 4. The upper town part (relativly small, about 10 houses); 5. the beach (like the wood barely anything to do and two houses of which 1 is only open in summer); 6. the town square (tiny, could have easily been integrated into other maps but because it's the area where you are stuck on most holidays hasn't been); 7. The "hidden" map to the harvest fairies whatever (tiny, only one house, is only not integrated into the main map to make it "hidden"); 8. the area to the west of the wood (large area with basicly as much size and stuff then 2,3,5,6,7 combined, which makes me question why the other areas had to be seperated to begin with); 9. A small plateau north of 8. from where you can view the city (tiny and nothing to do); 10. Some area to the west of 8. that is blocked by stones that you need to remove with advanced tools you get later (cant say how big because upgrading tools in this game feels like a drag. You can basicly skip steps in between and upgrade from your basic to second best tier by just keep using the tool after at says you can upgrade to the next step.) That might sound like much, but even though it's been quiete a while since I played Stardew Valley, I believe SoS:FoMT is smaller. 2.) Graphics:Now when I say graphics I'm not talking about how many polygons or pixels everything has, I'm talking about how it looks, and for me with games like that most importantly, if it looks cute.That is a point where I cant say anything bad about SoS:FoMT. The graphic designers have done a great job at creating some super cute stuff. The animals are adorible and I have to admit going to the barn after waking up and talking to and caring for the animals makes me realy happy. Not only but especialy the cows and chickens. So this is where the game measures up.3.) PeopleI remember in all three games I had a tough start when it came to making friends because first I was focused on doing a good job as a farmer/builder, and later couldn't decide how to best start making contact. Therefor I always resorted to using guides to look up stuff like when is someone's birthday or what kind of gifts do people like. My Time at Portia felt like the most fun there because not only are there different activities you can do with each other, but also making friends has actual in game benefits and or quests specificaly for them. SoS:FoMT may be as good as Stardew Valley when it comes to making friends, but since I barely have done so I'm not sure.4.) PriceNow, that is a problem. SoS:FoMT cost about 4 times as much as Stardew Valley or My Time at Portia which is absolutly ridiculous. There is just ZERO reason why anyone should by SoS:FoMT, when you can buy both the other games, who are already better to begin with, and still pay only halve as much as for SoS:FoMT alone. The only reason I bought the game where the great reviews and I feel like there is a lot of nostalgia involved in them that just doesn't apply to me. I only started liking and playing farming/life sims maybe 4 years ago. So I'm just looking at them from a non nostalgia point of view. And I have to say that paying more then 20€ for this game is simply not worth it, and even then only after you dont want to spend them on Stardew Valley or My Time at Portia.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Play Rune Factory or Stardew Valley instead.I first played this game as a child on the playstation, back when it was called Harvest Moon. While I'll admit there have been some serious graphical and quality of life improvements since, this game does not hold up to modern standards. I will be comparing it to Rune Factory 4, which is the most recent spin-off entry in the Story of Seasons series.First, it takes way too long to travel in this game. Most of your day isn't spent on watering crops, raising animals, but walking from your farm to, and around, either the mountain or village areas.Second, the town feels pretty dead. Compared to Rune Factory, where villagers roam outside their houses, most SoS:FoMT villagers stay inside their home, which can make them difficult to find at first. As such the town feels empty as you walk from house to house. Also, Rune Factory has random town events outside of festivals, involving numerous villagers, which serve to flesh out the people in the town. In FoMT, other than increasing heart ranks, the dialogue you see each day stays the same, and can quickly feel robotic and repetitive.Third, the menus in this game can be clunky. Take watching the TV - you cannot click back button to exit the option of channels. Instead, you need to find and select the stop watching option. Switching tools consumes time, unless you enter the tool menu, and swap tool positions. Holding an item also requires time, and it is cumbersome to switch to the item you wanted to hold.Compare this to Stardew valley or Rune Factory. In Stardew Valley, you can assign items and tools to hotkeys [1]-[0], and can easily access them without wasting time. In Runefactory 4, you can press LT to open a menu (pausing the game) where you can change your equipped weapon/tool, as well as select a held item.Fourth, the overall game cycle is boring and repetitive. Occasionally, you might head to the mines to get some ore for improving your tools. Otherwise, all you do is water and harvest crops, feed your animals, and walk around to hand out gifts. In Stardew/Rune Factory, you can also fight monsters to mix things up, but not in SoS:FoMT.Various in-game rewards achievements require you to do repetitive actions, most notably giving gifts to the harvest goddess. Every day you can give her one gift. Every 10 days of gifting, you may unlock a reward. You need to give her 100 gifts to unlock the mine elevators, which are necessary for reaching the bottom of the mine without stocking up heavily on stamina items.In general, I can not recommend this game, as there are better versions of this type of game out there. If you have a 3DS or a Nintendo Switch, get Rune Factory 4 (and soon 5) instead. However, if you haven't been exposed to Rune Factory or Stardew Valley, then maybe you won't mind the lack of modern/optimized features or action RPG elements.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a remake with better graphics and a few quality of life changes added. If you're an old fan of the Harvest Moon series, by all means go for it. I'm a huge fan and the nostalgia undeniably feels amazing. It's a trip down memory lane indeed. However, there's still a few flaws that could have been fixed or improved with minimal effort.Relationship building is a huge part of the game and is part of what made this type of farming simulator unique, but there are no improvements to the townsfolk's dialogues. They repeat the same one or two lines regardless of your friend meter and heart meter, and the worse part is, it is still like this even after they become your boyfriend or girlfriend. It feels really lackluster, as if the heart events were merely just for show and outside of those, the townsfolk are just robots. A simple dialogue change depending on the friend meter or heart meter would have breathed more life into the characters. Animal hit boxes are a little wonky; barn animals can even prevent you from moving if you're in the same tile as them when you get out of the barn. Endgame content is still absurd, some, such as the final truth jewel, requires you to be married for 50 years to be unlocked. I'm sure there are people who can play legit to get there, but for the majority of the players, they'll never get to unlock it without skipping years through hibernating. By the end of year 5-10, you would have probably unlocked everything, so hiding this last item behind decades is just unnecessary, especially when it isn't even game-changing to own.Don't get me wrong. I love this game and I want to see it become better. I know it's a remake and they're trying to keep it as close to the original as possible, but they've added new characters, changed some character designs, and added quality of life changes, so a few more adjustments can't drift it further away from the original than this.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original as a kid and it's still very similar to the original.Exact list of differences from the original (from :- Same sex marriage + two new marriage candidates (Brandon and Jennifer)- Marriage candidates have two new heart events- Items now stack in your rucksack (no more needing a basket and those were removed from the game)- Mining now has elevators and pitfall holes- Crops now have a star ranking (1-5)- New crops- You can now walk over crops (no more relying on the sprites to fully use your field)- Barns now have a bell that automatically moves animals outside (anyone who played A Wonderful Life may recognize this feature)- New farm animals- Horse can be ridden outside of the farm- More pet options- Mirror allows character customization(My observations)- A new park in the upper part of town, a forest trail through the middle of the lower part too- No more wild dogs to harass your animals at night- Your tools don't startle your animals- Fences no longer really serve much of a purpose (as a result of the above)- Golden lumber doesn't anger villagers- New villager menu addition that shows exactly how many friendship points each villager has towards MC- You can date every single marriage candidate before getting married with no repercussions (doesn't anger anyone)The game is and always has been very time management heavy, days pass fast and you need to always be on the move in order to maximize your efficiency at getting stuff done. If you're looking for Stardew Valley, you'll probably be disappointed as this game is again, very much like the original, where games were much much simpler. I am however a huge sucker for nostalgia and was maybe in year 50 on my childhood cartridge which is now lost forever, so you can imagine how I'm more than happy to grind away at this one again! I quickly picked up my same old childhood strategy and it still works exactly the same as it did all those years ago.If you find yourself struggling I recommend looking up some strategy guides, again like the original, the game isn't hand holdy and won't tell you exactly what you need to do to be successful. They give you the basics and tell you to go ham, that's it. Back in the day, you went to GameFAQs or Neoseeker to figure that out, or you just lived with your snail slow progression slowly figuring out the game as you went (but kids nowadays don't like exploring a game and want it explained to them, sigh), and it's still the same. I'm actually grateful that they didn't change this because I like the challenge of the classics, games these days are way too easy in my opinion.IF YOU ARE WANTING SOMETHING MORE MODERN - I would look forward to and go with the new Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town. I'm not sure if it will also have a PC port or be Switch only though...

_childDocuments_.review: I personally love the old Harvest Moon: Back to Nature on the PS1 and this game is a wonderful remake of the original (GBA version) with tons of quality of life improvements. The soundtrack takes a while to get used to again but it still has the charm that the old one had. The models and art style of the game is really adorable and fits the game so well and gives it that breath of fresh air that it needed. The game doesn't pressure you to become successful in the span of 3 years anymore which means that you can play the game at your own pace. Being able to date the villagers with the same gender as you is a nice addition for more diversity.Some minor gripes I have with the game are the following:- The flashback from the intro is cut short and doesn't have the same impact the original one had. The humming part with the childhood friend was also removed which was for me, really iconic.- Getting stuck on the streets or other tight areas due to NPC's blocking your way can get mildly annoying at times.- The time passes by just a bit quicker but enough to have an impact on some tasks that I need to do daily.Overall, the positives greatly outweighs the negatives. An amazing game to play regardless if you've played the other games or if this is your introduction to the series. Marvelous truly deserves all the praise for making one of our childhood games almost perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't play it for very long because it didn't appear to be very polished.  Lets talk about some simple things that were off:  * Its a blatant console port so the key defaults are annoying and you seemingly can't rebind the cancel/skip button of BACKSPACE to ESCAPE which is annoying. Generally it doesn't follow PC conventions.  * The textures at the start of the game (look at the ground of your farm at the start) seem lazy and uninspired.  * The fixed (can you change it?) camera perspective doesn't feel right, feels claustrophobic to me.  * The sound design is grating. The sound they've chosen for walking is a like a bloody hammer, this is one of the principal reasons I stopped playing.  * The collision detection is lazy. In an open world game, the squares the maps are designed with shouldn't be obvious but often while skirting NEAR but not through a tree, it will block you. It was possible to easily get blocked by a stone in a forest where you would have to walk in an unexpected direction to free yourself. The grid system generally feels slightly off.   * Nobody appears to have been responsible with authority for player experience, when someone appears to speak to you, you have to wait for them to run right up to you until they start talking. If, at the start of the game you decide not to become a farmer the game ends (this is kinda funny) but then the credits roll and they're UNSKIPPABLE so you have to kill the process to restart. The above left a sour impression on me and given there are other available titles that are already knocking the genre out of the park (Stardew Valley and My Time at Portia) I didn't feel compelled to invest the time in this one. Maybe I'll try it again a bit later and update my review. But I expected a more polished experience than my Early Access experience I had with My Time At Portia and I expected more.  Also, why did they change the name from Harvest Moon?

"Story of Seasons: Friends of Mineral Town" is the ultimate farming escapade that will have you tending crops and raising livestock with a big smile on your face.Picture this: vibrant, charming graphics that transport you to the idyllic town of Mineral Town, where every corner is brimming with character and charm. From the moment you step foot on your quaint little farm, you'll be hooked!But wait, there's more! Get ready to dive headfirst into a whirlwind of activities, from planting and harvesting crops to raising adorable animals. And let's not forget about the delightful townsfolk who are just waiting to become your new best friends. With their quirky personalities and heartwarming stories, you'll find yourself eagerly anticipating every interaction.But it's not all about farming! In Mineral Town, you'll have the opportunity to build romantic relationships with the eligible candidates in town. Whether you fancy the shy bookworm or the adventurous animal lover, there's someone for everyone. And who knows? You might just find yourself walking down the aisle and starting a family of your own!And the festivals! Oh, the festivals! From the Easter Egg Hunt to the Fireworks Festival, there's never a dull moment in Mineral Town. Get ready to join in on the fun and experience the joy of community spirit like never before.But don't just take my word for it. "Story of Seasons: Friends of Mineral Town" is a game that speaks for itself. So why wait? Grab your hoe, put on your sunhat, and embark on the farming adventure of a lifetime. Your journey to harvest happiness awaits!

_childDocuments_.review: *I'd like to note my Steam hours don't reflect my gameplay hours, I've put over a 150 into my copy on the Switch.Long-time Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons player here, with the original Friends of Mineral Town being my nostalgic favourite - so this review is heavily judgemental in all aspects given how much this title means to me specifically. I have fond memories of playing this on long-trips and late at night on my GBA back in the day. So.. with that out of the way ..SOS: FOMT does a fantastic job of recreating the title. There. If you trust a long term fan of the series opinion who has been disappointed time and time again by the mainline series (HM), then look no further. If you're interested why, I'll offer the simple reasons below.. Right off the bat - the graphics are an adorable improvement, with my only complaint being on  of the new portrait art, but overall, that's overshadowed by how great the game looks. Obviously - it's a pretty bold move to take a nostalgically adored game like FOMT, with it's memorable pixel art and characters, and transfer that into a 3D environment. But they really pulled it off. Everything looks just as cute as you imagined it would when you were a child. Furthermore, they have expanded on several of the areas, which feel like  expansions, given how used to the size of the town an old player like me is. On top of that, the new areas look great. They aren't just added in as an afterthought, they make sense with the layout of the town, and even make travelling a little easier in some cases.They could have pushed it a little further - while there is new text dialogue, a new (generally unloved) set of bachelor/ettes, there is a few oversights that could have made the game a bit better. They really should have capitalized on new generation console and pc technology to bring out the best in the game - perhaps a little more ambience in the rendering and lighting, stronger cutscenes, that sort of thing.If this is your first entry to the HM/SOS series, or you are a nostalgic, longtime player like me that has a fondness for FOMT, this is 100% worth your time and money. Speaking on behalf of the oldheads .. remember when FOMT time sucked you into doing every little thing  before you turned it off? How there was always  to forage, some animal to tend to, some crop that was  a day or two away from fruition, so you had to keep playing? This did the same damn thing to me. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a treat for anyone who enjoys farm simulators! Even if you haven't played the original FoTM game, it's still very much an enjoyable experience. There are some similarities with Stardew Valley and other less popular farming games, and the overall style of the game is just very cute and pleasant. positives:+ cute, enjoyable atmosphere+ good soundtrack+ customizable keybinds+ the game isn't demanding at all, but you can tweak graphic settings to make it even less demanding if you need it+ romance/marriage options aren't restricted by gender + feels fresh while still preserving the core aspects of the original gamenegatives:- character customization is limited to gender and skin color, though the available character models are pretty good in my opinion- some mechanics might feel a bit 'old fashioned' to people used to simpler/more modern farm games (very limited inventory, slower progression on Normal Mode), but it's not that bad if you like variety in your gamesThe price might seem a bit steep, but it feels like it's worth it to me since I really enjoy this genre, and I'd like to support Marvelous so that they might consider bringing more SoS/Harvest Moon games to pc. If you feel the same way, consider buying it! I feel very happy with my purchase and definitely recommend it :D

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good remaster if you catch it on a sale. 40 dollars on an almost tile-for-tile remaster is a little crazy in 2024 when games with vastly more content and arguably love put into them like Stardew Valley for 15 dollars. The game also does have quite a few quality of life improvements, that do help the game out quite a bit. Additionally, I would have liked some more/improved dialogue. Dialogue is boring uninspired and uninteresting. I mean the librarian lady says, "The library was built so people can read Papa's books." That is almost all she will say for a while until you're friends with her. Most of the characters have the exact same dialogue every single day and it makes it pretty difficult to be interested in talking to them. It makes it feel more like a chore than an activity you want to participate in. They also removed features like rival marriages for some reason, which is and feels like an odd choice since we can see characters flirting/showing interest in one another throughout the game. I really appreciate the art style, it feels like an appropriate art style for the original visuals of the game. The game does have some minor technical issues, for example, the game is limited to 1080p in fullscreen, and if you have display scaling on, say, a 4k monitor the game will become absolutely HUGE and you need to do some hacky technical workarounds to get it playing native 4k on your display.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, fun game. Relaxing, calm, mindless sandbox farming with some interesting relationship events with town folk. Not to mention cute visuals and great art for characters.That being said, for a remake of old GBA title... I personally wish they were a bit more loyal to the original... Or had it as an extra difficulty level instead of "easy" mode which sounds like even easier experience on top of already easy game.Really miss that grim feeling when you forgot to feed a cow, or storm made you lose a day and one or few of your animals get sick. Need to manually move your livestock in/out of their building, having to build fences for your livestock so it doesn't wander off too far around (animals now pass through everything like ghosts, including boulders and your crops). Not to mention, ability to walk through crops. I get it, it makes sense. Just because there is a carrot it doesn't mean you can't walk around it, but having to plan and think on what crops can be planted nearby and what needed gaps for harvest added some sort of strategy to your field. Appreciate bigger bag, but also, not a fan of how building stone and wooden logs take space now. Would be passable (afterall, you HAVE to carry them somehow, can't just have 999 logs on yourself like it's nothing), but that makes some big problems when it comes to fodder... Cutting half of field worth of grass to turn into fodder you can't carry in your bag is annoying. Especially as it just disappear if you enter any building (imagine making mistake of going into barn to empty your inventory because time doesn't pass inside buildings and learning it hard way). But hey, only downside of starving animals is loss of produce for one day, so who cares. Speaking of animals... that's one of my personal pet peeves in this remake:By the time you have your barn animals in position they would matter, they are already irrelevant for you as a player. Hear me out on this. Affection now starts at 5 hearts. That's medium produce at best. To raise max level, you have to breed. Cow breeding takes 21 day. Another 21 day for cow to grow up before it can be bred (because now it has 6 hearts max, and that specific cow needs offspring for extra +1 on that offspring). 5x42... 210 days of breeding single cow line. That's roughly 2 years since your cow purchase to have it at it's best potential. And that's only single cow variety (out of 4). Sure, upgraded barn has 2 breeding spots, and while waiting for one cow to grow up you can breed different animal (sheep for example), and in the end you can breed 9 heart animal to finish up filling up your barn with 10 heart offsprings, but getting there takes time... Time, in which you are most likely to become millionaire, finish majority of game content, get married, explore both mines to the deepest floor, upgrade and customise your farm to it's maximum, get best tools in the game, and probably even win some contests with your chickens and rabbits. Contests, that are complete waste of time unless winning animal has at least 7 hearts of max affinity./rantSure, there are some good improvements when it comes to remake, but if you ask any fan of the original, they would probably say it just makes game easier without fixing anything as it wasn't broken in the first place. (because apparently save-scumming mine or events was intended way of playing)All in all, fun game if you can look past questionable changes or never played original. Wouldn't say worth full price, but games don't come free. And to be honest, there are better games of this genre. Not to mention, game still fails to explain some things in-game, leaving player either to randomly guess or stumble upon some things by mere chance (or look it up on wiki, which kind of defeats the purpose.)
_childDocuments_.name: STORY OF SEASONS: Friends of Mineral Town

_childDocuments_.review: Why would you play this game when Stardew Valley exists?Stardew Valley has better graphics, better controls, better dialog, better story, and (from what I read here) less impossible tasks being set.Also, overall more quality of life options; this gameflow feels so 'clunky'.Example: Day 1, obviously I wanted to start my farm. So I made some space, tilled the ground, and then realised I didn't have any seeds. But when I arrived at the General Store (all the way at the back of the town), it was closed. Not that that mattered, because apparently you buy your seeds somewhere else (even further away). Someone came at my door at the start of day 2 to tell me that. Good, let's go! When I arrived at the spot, there was no-one there. Turns out I was too early. Not that there was a sign with opening times... When I finally could buy my seeds, I could choose from a whole list, of which just one seed was suitable for the current season. And I could only buy enough for a small 3x3 plot.So clearly farming wasn't how I was supposed to spend my time. What then? Surely not the social interactions with other villagers: there was no dialog, just one line per person.Mining then? Yes, you can do that. Repeat the same two actions until you are out of stamina, leave the mine to regain you stamina, and go back in. What fun!This is still very clearly an old game; pity that it hasn't been brought in line with its modern counterparts.

_childDocuments_.review: Story of Seasons: Friends of Mineral Town is like the superstar of farming games! It's got these super cute graphics and chill gameplay that hooks you in, no matter your age. Here's the lowdown:Nostalgia Galore: Loads of folks love how this game takes them back, especially if they've played the original Harvest Moon: Friends of Mineral Town. It's got that same vibe but with cool updates that fans totally dig.Friendship Vibes: The best part? The relationships you build with the folks in town! It's like real life – you talk, hang out, and watch those connections grow. Makes the town feel alive!On the Flip Side: Some players say things can get a bit samey after a while. You know, doing the farming thing, chatting with locals, and hitting up events might start feeling a tad repetitive if you're at it for ages.All in all, Story of Seasons: Friends of Mineral Town is a total getaway to this awesome world. It mixes nostalgia with new stuff so well, you won't want to put it down. If you're into farming games or just want a cozy spot in a virtual world, this one's a must!FOLLOW ME---------------------------------------------------Youtube: Facebook: Instagram: TikTok: Twitter:
