_childDocuments_.review: Main advice, do not play this game with a keyboard and mouse. Maybe acceptable with a controller.This game was determined not to let me enjoy it. First it started super zoomed in and took me a few hours researching the bugfix before I finally managed to load into the game. Second, the sound quality was too awful to leave the sound on, and unfortunately you can't actually adjust the sound settings until you make a player character and start the entire game off cutscenes and all, so I had to skip through them to fix the sound and restart the entire game from desktop to watch the cutscenes, bit of a disconcerting experience.Finally I'm in the game and I began to come to terms with how painful the keyboard and mouse porting is. You can't assign actions to most buttons on the keyboard, leaving you a really restricted set of keys, so your hands are constantly crossing over each other. To make that worse, you can't close menus using the same button, so every time you open a menu you have to cross your hands to close it again. After earlier Harvest Moon style games it feels like it is really punishing you for everything you do, because every menu you open or action you take is so clunky, and requires the use of buttons from all over your keyboard. After 15 minutes playing it flared my RSI because I couldn't set up a convenient keyboard set up with the buttons it allows you to allocate keys to. No idea how the game actually plays, for all I know its an amazing game if you can get past the bugs and the controls, but the bugs and terrible keyboard porting were impossible to get past to actually get into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: STORY OF SEASONS: Friends of Mineral Town. It is a healing life simulation developed by Marvelous and published by XSEED Games. This game is a remake of what was released in 2003, and the 2003 version was also a remake of Harvest Moon(1996). In a nutshell, 'STORY OF SEASONS: Friends of Mineral Town' is a remake of the remake. As you may already know, this series has inspired another healing life game, Stardew Valley a lot. Knowing the origin of a famous game can sometimes be very informative and interesting. Let's take a look at it with Nyanco-chan! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)When the game starts, you head to Mineral Town. There is something your grandfather prepared for you. A family farm where you often went to play when you were childhood is now hand you down from your grandfather. You can interact with various villagers. It affects their favorability, various events and even the marriage system for the player. Planting vegetables, breeding animals, mining, and fishing are also possible. There are various collection elements. This game is definitely based on a healing village life, but if you want to experience all events, you have to be very busy playing it. How you enjoy this game will be up to you.There are easy mode and normal mode in the game. If you are not familiar with this genre game, it is good to start with easy mode. This mainly includes features that make managing your farm easier. You can choose your playable character among 4 characters, and also have your own name. You can change the look through costumes, and some special animal costumes can be unlocked via DLC. The flow of dates follows the calendar concept. However it is the seasonal-based, not 12 months. There are two maps available, Mineral Town and your farm. Basically, managing the farm and interacting with the villagers is the main gameplay. Best of all, the dating and marriage system is pretty impressive!STORY OF SEASONS: Friends of Mineral Town. It is a definitely great relaxing life simulation game. Not only did the original game already prove the value of the gameplay, but now it comes back to us as the remake version. Of course, this remake is not perfect. The graphics are still out of date, and there are quite a few things that need to be polished. However this game will be fun enough to evoke again your nostalgia for the classic masterpiece. The real pleasure is that you can be relaxing in the game. There is no need to compete with other players. You experience and enjoy an idyllic life. You can be dating your favorite character, getting married, and creating your own family in STORY OF SEASONS. What are you waiting for? Even if reality would disappoint you, this game will be honest with you. Highly Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: A new and improved remake of the classic Harvest Moon game, SoS: Friends of Mineral Town brings back that feeling of nostalgia with fresh faces and features.+Pros++Relaxing farming experience+Smooth game play and controls+Cute, soothing interactions with characters (familiar and new alike)+Charming romances (now with same gender relationships!)+Set down roots and start a family+Lots of content that will keep the game entertaining for a long while (typically 60-120ish hours at least)+Literally Harvest Moon from one of the original companies, just under a different name, Story of Seasons+Achievements-Negatives--Yikes, that price tho... It's worth it for fans of this genre and series but get it on sale if at all possible.-Your character has some choices for appearance but they aren't entirely customizable.All in all, it's a solid addition to the series and fans will hopefully love it as much as I do. I can't recommend it enough, especially on sale, for fans of relaxing farm life sims, story/lore rich games, animal lovers, romantic plot lines, and, of course, Harvest Moon games.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love SoS:FoMT! It’s a beautiful remake of the classic Harvest Moon games that got me hooked on the series in the first place, but with improved graphics; some new characters and animals, and updated mechanics. For the Old/returning players that miss the good old days in Grandpa's farm, it’s definitely worth the purchase! Although the change in the rival/conflict mechanic might leave some wanting and some quirks may come as a bit annoying (i.e. purchasing and or equipping animal feed), overall, the game is certainly a great example of a remaster done right.For newcomers, I would say that the game is a solid entry to the series (and this is true for all age groups). If you had your first shovel from a more modern farming sim, you might find it slightly underwhelming though. But the charm of the HM/SOS, I think, has always been about letting the players enjoy the perfect balance of farm and family life; community engagement and exploration at your own pace, and this game definitely offers all of that without being imposing. SOS:FOMT makes it really easy for you to lose track of time and fully immersed in Mineral Town for hours on without end. The only reason I stopped playing is to write this review, my first review on Steam, to tell you that I recommend it 101% percent.

_childDocuments_.review: Safe to say that fans of the GBA version will enjoy this remake.I'm having fun with the game so far and although I don't have much to make note of beyond that which has already been referenced in other reviews, I'll go ahead and list just a few positives and negatives:+ The updated character portraits look pretty nice (mostly).  + The in game music stays true to the original. You'll immediately recognize the familiar seasonal songs and event themes. There have been a couple of songs that played around the farm that I didn't recognize, but I'm not sure if I just don't remember those songs or if they are new or not. + Ability to choose playable character gender and premade appearance (albeit from quite limited selection of 4 premade options, but still).+ Ability to change keybinds, including reassigning LMB and RMB to keys.+ Ability to pick opposite OR same sex marriage partner.+ Duplicate items placed in your rucksack will now form stacks of 9, which is great. + Free herding bells perm installed at the front of your coop and your barn, which, when rung, will call all your barnyard birdies and bovines to the fields and back. The best is that the bells will automatically ring at 8:00 PM to make your animals return to the barn and coop on their own. Very convenient.+ Kappa is a cutie boi now and redesigned Karen is a hot babe. - Overall aesthetic. I know this is just a personal preference, but I'm so tired of this chibi art style constantly showing up in HM/SoS games. I wish my cows looked like cows instead of rotund middle school drawings. Flashbacks to Magical Melody. - Rival marriages have been removed. This is a big bad. No idea why they did away with this feature. - Livestock affection. This has been changed so that you can only get a 10 heart animal by breeding that animal line. The default animal will start at 5 hearts, and when you breed it once, its baby will have 6 max hearts. You then breed the 6 heart offspring and it will birth a 7 max heart offspring, so on and so forth until you get to the 10 max hearts. I really dislike this as it ultimately means you'll need to either sell your original livestock buddies in order to max out your farm profits and stuff, or, keep your average affection animal (because you're sentimental and they were the first cow you ever had, dammit!), which unfortunately takes the space where you might have raised a 10 max heart animal instead. I'd recommend the game,  - if you have greater willpower than I do - put this one on your wishlist and wait to grab it when it goes on sale. The current price is steep for the content, imo.

_childDocuments_.review: Game's very fun and nostalgic from the old days, improved in graphics and a new character or so. A lot of farming, animal care, animal contests, npc character events, secrets, mines and choosing the love of your life. It's all fun and games but when you max out everything and marry your partner, there's not much to do anymore besides trying to make your chickens lay golden eggs and your cows etc making the highest quality resource. I discovered a way to make a ton of money during the 2nd year of spring that kind of killed the game. Huang was a merchant who lives with Zack at the beach. When you get Huang to 6 musical notes, he'll offer you to play a game which you can play any amount of time, on any day, no matter the season. The game is a memorization game of switching 3 apples and picking the one he wants you to find. After winning about 10 times in the game he rewards you with a mystery flower which is worth 100k (actually 70-87k individually). If you win the entire game 10 times, you get 10 mystery flowers which you can give to the goddess for a goddess flower that costs 1,000,000 when sold back to Huang. If you don't want to ruin your Harvest Moon experience, I'd suggest you steer clear of Huang. Overall, the game is 9/10 stars, would be a perfect 10 if not for Huang.

_childDocuments_.review: The art style loses a lot of the charm of the Back to Nature or even the original HM: Friends of Mineral town. It's and garish and empty. It looks like it was made explicitly for toddlers, rather than just being an all-ages aesthetic like the others. Maybe that's nostalgia goggles, or maybe my tastes have just changed.There are also some vestigial issues they skimped over. In the original, there was no Stamina meter. The only indications were when your character stopped working and did an animation expressing how tired they were. But the more you worked, the longer these animations were, kind of "punishing" you for exertion. They added a Stamina meter here, removing any need for the interruptions... but they programmed them in anyway, forcing needless waiting at common intervals.The other quality-of-life improvements are nice, though. And it's also good to see some of the new characters and animals and hear some of the new music. It's still a working classic that holds up on its own.

_childDocuments_.review: I've preordered this in a hot minute when i've heard a Story of Seasons game coming out to PC on steam. Although I do regret not preordering the physical copy as well for that cute pink cow plushie with a strawberry tail. As a die-hard of Harvest Moon series, and after the rebrand into Story of Seasons, by XSEED/Marvelous, I MUST get this game and play it as it is a remake of one of my favorite titles: Friends of Mineral Town and More Friends of Mineral Town. I highly recommend getting this game if you really love JRPGs, marriage, agriculture and ranching, along with exploration, and befriending villagers. There's plenty to do despite it's practically the same thing over and over. _childDocuments_.review: This is such a cute and relaxing game – slow, but in a wonderful way that makes you really live in the world of Story of Seasons. And the graphics are just so adorable. You arrive to a run-down farm and slowly bring it back to life (and I mean it – the process will be so slow you'll spend the whole day living through an in-game month). So if you enjoy life simulation farming, give this a try. Here are my favorite features:- Character costumization (the choices are limited, but you can still choose from 2 female and 2 male avatars and pick their outfits); - Slow pace (feels like real life where you have your in-game clock and the freedom to explore each day. Or plan it out to be more productive and achieve your goals faster);- Various ways to gain gold: growing crops, taking care of your animals, fishing, mining, gathering various outdoor plants;- You have 1 month for each season, and 4 months a year. Each season/month has its own festivals, character birthdays, and even your own birthday. Some of those events have cute mini-games, others are simply fun to look at. - Animals: you get a variety of farm animals that you can take care of (but aren't obligated to): chickens, cows, pink sheep, angora bunnies. And you can get up to 5 pets (cats, dogs, even penguins). - Friendship system – you can befriend the villagers over time, but it will take time to do so. Each of them has their own background story, and it's interesting to watch how their attitude towards you changes during the game. At first, everyone sort of treats you, like, "oh, you're the new guy/girl" and are somewhat indifferent. And once you've proven yourself, you can see they respect you. - Romancing system: you can get married, have a child. And you have so many options to choose from! You can also have same-sex couples. There will be romance events as the relationship grows. Oh, and your choices/actions matter. - Cooking! I saw a lot of reviews that demanded cooking to be included, so I'm guessing I've purchased this game with an update because there are cooking options once you upgrade your house. - And of course one of the main reasons to even look at this game – farming! I love farming games, and this one is my favorite. There's just so much freedom in this game. You can choose what animals you'd like to have, what crops to grow, and so much more. And I absolutely love how you start with nearly nothing and grow over time, upgrading your house and farm, even the tools. The only thing I think some people may find challenging is *learning* how to play this game. I, personally, love it. But the game doesn't tell you the "right" way to play it. There's not tutorial. You have to find it out for yourself, which is probably part of the fun for most people. You can find some manuals in the library and the bookshelf inside your house, or learn stuff from the villagers. Or simply google a guide. Do I recommend this game? Yes, definitely. If you like the things I listed and aren't scared of googling some information or simply playing through to discover *how*  to play this – then yes, this is a game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who played MFoMT back in the day, I can't recommend buying this game at full price. How can I justify paying $40 for a 2005 game when Stardew Valley is less than half the price and has far more content?Also, while the quality of life improvements are great for casual play, it also reduces the play time significantly. Because your backpack has so much more space and items stack, you're going to clear the mines much faster. So not only is there not much content, but you're going to go through it a lot faster compared to the original.Taking out the rival marriages was also a mistake. There aren't a lot of villager events to begin with, and now a huge chunk of villager interactions are gone. The new events from the two new villagers aren't enough to replace this.Did I enjoy this game? Yes. Coming back to this game after all these years was fun. _childDocuments_.review: On a superficial level this is the most normal Story of Seasons game on steam. Not too many bells and whistles, and probably the heaviest farm emphasis. If you want to progress meaningfully (increase stamina, get the last two tiers of each piece of equipment, unlock any amount of Quality of Life) get ready to pull up a guide because you're going to be committing to daily arcane rituals. They have been made a little easier compared to the GBA version to my knowledge (I played it but didn't seek anything obtuse) but there are still aspects of unlocking that require 100+ days of doing seemingly unrelated tasks, strange time gates, extremely slim drop rates on specific floors of a 200+ level mine. If you want to go the route of completion, this game will keep you busy, but it's a tad too nonsensical.I think without any of that the game is just fine, if you wanted to relive the gba game or even the snes game this scratches that itch. The animals are cute, the townspeople are the usual, vacuous npcs that the earlier games always had, and managing the farm itself stays simple. I think as a SoS game I may prefer olive town and I wish the character defaulted to dpad control when managing the farm itself, but I can probably just modify that with steam inputs.If you want a farming game to pass time that isn't bloated by arbitrary mechanics (until you obtain 99 insight and open your third eye) this is a good time.Oh also this one has same sex marriage, you can play as a girl and no marriage candidates are barred so it's kind of an amalgamation of FoMT and MFoMT to my knowledge.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this because it's a great game, really. But there are still some rough edges to this port. This might just be because of my laptop specs, but for a game as light as this, my HP Spectre 13 (2018) should be enough.Don't turn every setting off; turn off anti-aliasing and shadow type, then make sure your ultrabook is running at full performance and there shouldn't be any trouble playing the game. After updating my settings, I'm playing at a constant 60fps. Just this is enough to change my mind and recommend this. Because the frame rate jump is what really turned me off before.Steam marks this as only having Partial Controller Support because there's no in-game keyboard. If you're prompted for a name, you'll have to type it with your actual keyboard. But this isn't a problem because the game can switch between the two modes instantly.There may be some parts of the game that became way too easy because of the quality of life updates but that just makes the remake more bearable. Without those updates, this would just be an old game ported to modern consoles.If there's anything I wanted more out of this, it would be a more qualitative upgrade to the game. There's not really much difference with the original game and I feel like it's a cash grab as it is. Because let's be honest, nothing is really stopping us from playing the original game and we're getting this remake solely because we love the original.Original review:It runs on a minimum of 25 fps on the highest settings which I think is good enough. It stabilizes at 30 fps most of the time too. The problem is the running speed is highly dependent on frame rate. When there's fewer objects to render on screen, the FPS jumps up by more than 10 and that speeds up the run speed of my character. Imagine a crawl speed becoming twice as fast for a couple of seconds then slow back down to a crawl. I'd suggest a frame rate cap to handle it better....None of those are deal breakers and I'm hoping to change this review or post another one after a patch. But for a game that's remade like this, quality of life updates should cover a wider scope than stackable items, and walkable crops.

_childDocuments_.review: If this game was half the price, I'd give it a thumbs up. I guarantee you, if you don't have childhood memories with this game, it is NOT worth 50 bucks. The "overwhelming positive" reviews are skewed by a lot of people rating it off nostalgia. Stardew Valley and My Time At Portia will offer you the same chill, feel-good atmosphere with twenty times the content, for a quarter of the price. Positives:- Charming music.- Cute, chibi graphics (may be a negative if that's not your thing).- The cutscenes are acceptable. Short, but they get the point across and can be pretty endearing.Negatives:- There's a lot of villagers sure, but they all say about...five things. Throughout the whole in-game year. One thing per season, and 1 thing if they're in a different-than-usual part of town. Unacceptable for a 50 dollar game.- There's an item you get pretty regularly in the mail (I wont spoil how), that you then sell to the merchant on the beach for 57 THOUSAND. Suddenly all the farming you've been doing becomes completely pointless. Your crops and animal goods are pity change. - Walking and mining sound effects are nightmarish. XD- The animations for each stage of stamina drain/fatigue will take half your game time. Really wish there was an option to turn these off.- Speaking of stamina, you never get better at things, or drain less with better tools. So stamina is always an issue. The beginning of year two feels like year one still. - There's no museum or anything to work towards...museums/collection type things aren't timed or anything, so you can't even say it "puts pressure on the player". It just means there's...nothing to work towards. - There's no customizing your farm, or even the inside of your house...and believe me, as you get more stuff, it starts to look ugly. At this point, I'm just going to keep playing until I've married the three best boys (Cliff, Gray, and Doctor), and then I'm...probably done. What's left? Get to the same dialogue I've seen thousands of times? Get more money despite already being basically a billionaire? I don't have more main story to unlock or ruins to explore like My Time At Portia. I can't still build my dream farm or finish collections like Stardew Valley. There's just nothing. This is "Nostalgia; The Game", and it's kind of insulting they're charging fifty. At twenty or twenty-five, okay, but...jeeze man.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:[+] SAME SEX MARRIAGE!!! As a Bisexual, this makes me incredibly happy, as I can now marry Elly as a girl!!! Something I’ve always wanted to do ever since I was really young![+] Can walk through crops (No more “U” shaped crop plots, thank god)[+] New crops & animals added![+] New Bachelor & Bachelorette to court![+] Updated the looks of the villagers and Bachelors/Bachelorettes from the OG game, and Im a huge fan of the redesigns![+] Game runs smoothly at 60 FPS[+] Lighting and the overall environment throughout the weather and seasons is absolutely gorgeous! My favourite season is Autumn[+] New music plays on the weekends and I absolutely love it! Gives a whole new feel when working on the fields everyday, rather than hearing the same seasonal tune for 30 days straight.[+] The Himbofication of Kappa pleases me[+] Mining is SO MUCH easier and smooth; all the minerals go into your bag after breaking the rocks instead of pressing dumb buttons to put it in your bag, added extra work on your part.[+] Animals have a generational system, so the animals you buy will have a MAX of 5 HEARTS unless you breed them; in which that will increase the maximum hearts to 10 once you hit 5 generations into breeding. This puts a whole new meaning and challenge to breeding your cows, chickens, sheep, ect. And I absolutely love it!Negatives: [-] Time goes a bit too fast for my liking. (5 seconds = 10 minutes)[-] The graphic, AKA the chibi style of the characters is kind of off putting. It reminds me of Harvest Moon: Magical Melody, which isn’t too bad, but it could have been executed a lot better.[-] Bon Viviant (Gourmet) being happy is the most disturbing thing I’ve ever seen with my two eyeballs that I never want to see again.[-] Rival Marriages are removed[-] Dialogue for the villagers can become a bit stale after a while; which is kind of what it was like in the OG games, but it could have been improved upon in the remake, so I'm kind of disappointed it wasn't.Overall, I give this game a 9/10! I might be blinded a little bit by nostalgia, but this game stayed faithful to the original GBA games, and even improved upon them as well, and I cannot stop playing this game. It's one of those games that you tend to play for so long that 12 hours will go by and you thought it was only 3 hours; and throughout that entire time you forget to eat, shower, and sleep. I hope in the near future, we'll be able to play the game with mods, cause I would love to see what the community could do/improve with this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty early into my playthrough as I write this, and I'm enjoying myself a great deal.  Overall, it's a pretty stellar game, and it's excellent to see this classic franchise working its way over to PC.  Hopefully that pattern holds.While I do recommend it, I will offer one bit of warning.  It's a very faithful remake of the original game. _childDocuments_.review: Given the number of hours I've spent on this game, I obviously like it. It's a solid remake, very cute.Things I love:* THE STAMINA BAR and the fatigue smiley. These are HUGE improvements. * AUTO-SAVE HAS SAVED MY LIFE.* The abundance of save slots.* That you can date characters of either gender as any gender.* Brandon and Jennifer are great. I love their designs and I think their personalities supplement the existing marriage candidates well.* The redesigns for the characters are excellent and I particularly like the new Harvest Goddess, Manna, Anna, Lillia, Rick, and Karen designs. * Honorable mention to Huang, whose design no longer contains overt racism.* The mechanic for breaking the curses on the cursed tools is less of a pain. Things I thought were fine but had a comment or criticism about:* Doing away with the rival events was a good thing from a heteronormative standpoint. It would have been even cooler if the matchups of rival couples could have been affected by your choices (in the form of setting up certain couples via events or something.) I know there is obviously something to be said for the status of gay marriage in Japan but having NPCs other than the player's spouse get gay married could be really cool.* On one hand, if the game is set in a fictionalized Japan, it makes sense for the cast to be largely racially homogenous, but that's not established beyond not localizing Yu, Mei, Mugi, Ran, and Saibara's names. On the other hand, it wouldn’t have hurt to do a bit of race bending, particularly among the marriage candidates for a bit more diversity, imo. So many games with a dating element have this problem and it would've been nice for Marvelous to do something about it in this remake. * I wish that there was a way to know whether you've seen a heart event for a marriage candidate.* RE: Golden Lumber - * This is very nitpicky, but * While they are helpful in this game, I wish you could give the nature sprites better instructions. I wish you could ask them to:** Not ship a specified crop or animal product quality** Water fully grown crops that regrow** Let you hand-feed livestock instead of wasting fodder in the bins** Put certain animal products in the maker for youThings that I don't like:* Kappa's redesign is... a choice...* Huang's redesign and dialogue did not completely eliminate stereotype. * I don't like that you can't make medium tier fences with stone.* The True Magic Red flower can't be foraged, or at least it is so rare that I've never come across one without growing it myself. Even then, I get maybe 4 in a season. I've also tried to destroy blue ones I've planted and plant new seeds, but that maybe adds 1 new red one each time. I've been able to forage it in previous games, so I don't remember it being [italics] this [/italics] rare.* You need the backspace button for things like getting off your horse when the right-click could've sufficed. You never need the option do a backspace thing and use a tool (right-click) at the same time. It makes things a lot less seamless to take your hand off the mouse to do something on the keyboard. You can’t change this in keyboard settings either.* Animals can occupy the same space as other animals. As a result, they tend to clump together in the barn, making movement in the barn (without pressing LShift to dash) a nightmare and makes animal care difficult and (irl) time consuming.* It also means that when you let the animals out of the barn in the morning, they pile on top of each other in Old MacDonald's eldritch abomination. They glitch through each other and it's a very strange sight in a game that is otherwise very polished.* I like that you can have more than 1 pet now, but [spoilers] you can get maybe 1 pet/year.  Van only sells pets on the 15th of a month, only if it's clear, and only if your most recent pet has 8 or more hearts, which takes about a year anyway. Van only sells 1 type of animal each month (cats/spring, penguins/summer, dogs/fall, capybara/winter) so you have to wait a full year if you only want one type of pet. Oh, and not to mention that the only way of speeding up the animal friendship process is to give them treats that cost 1000G a pop (and that's not a typo.) [/spoilers]* I wish that either there was more content that pops up after year 5 or * Another minor thing, but Things I actively hate:* Some of the character redesigns make some of the marriage candidates *coughPopuricough* look like children. I recognize that this is a game [italics] for [/italics] children, but if the intent was to make them look like they are of an age that's able to get married and have children, they didn’t succeed. * If you're doing animal care and you miss the animal you want, you have to sit through the whole task animation uninterrupted before it lets you continue. It only takes a second, but it feels like forever.* I honestly don't remember from past HM/SoS games if this is the case or if I'm just very used to Stardew Valley, but that you have to till the ground in the mines to find the stairs is OBNOXIOUS. Many levels don’t have pitfalls, which you kind of want to avoid because of the falling damage anyway. Time doesn't pass in the mines, which is great, but tilling for the stairs is so time consuming irl and it's such a waste of energy, even if you've found all the power berries. It's more efficient to purchase Stamina Boosters from the clinic than make them yourself because the True Magic Red Flower is so rare, but you end up spending thousands of G to maybe get that much back in gems. In my opinion, it's very unbalanced.* The reward for compiling the  is lackluster at best and a waste of time at worst.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, okay. I was sceptical about the £43 price tag as it's a remake of a 17 year old game but I cannot stop playing. I played FoMT and HM:DS as a kid and SoS:FoMT has brought back that nostalgia feeling, with some neat quality of life tweaks and a graphical upgrade!For newcomers to the series, the story follows a simple plot: the Mayor of Mineral Town invites you to visit your grandpa's old farm, and you decide to stay. Gameplay mainly consists of raising animals, growing crops, mining, socialising, and foraging - your main goals being to make money, expand your farm, and get married. It's  repetitive, but you can absolutely sink hours into this game without realising it. If you're a fan of Stardew Valley then this will absolutely be your cup of tea.The graphics are bright, colourful, and cute (an upgrade, in my opinion, from the original FoMT). The character portraits displayed during conversation are full of personality, and the UI is clean and easy to understand and navigate. The animations are basic, and there can be some weird shadows in certain areas, but I wouldn't let that put you off. The artstyle is what gives the game it's charm.The audio is basic, and can get repetitive at times. This falls in line with all the older Harvest Moon games though, and has a certain nostalgic feeling to it. When you first hear the Seasonal soundtracks though, they're so happy and joyful! Animal sfx make my heart melt. - Sweet graphical upgrade- Runs at a consistent 60fps (which is the framerate cap fyi) - Charming characters - Cute animals (seriously, I can't stop sending pictures of my cows to people who don't care)- You can walk over your crops- Flawless controller support- Chill af gameplay- Hefty price tag - Music can get a little repetitive - Certain aspects of the game aren't necessarily explained to new players ( for example) Would I recommend this? If you're a fan of Harvest Moon games or Stardew Valley then without any hesitation I would absolutely recommend the FoMT remake. It's got that addictive farming gameplay loop, yet it's so calming and there's no sense of urgency whatsoever. If you've never played a causal farming game before, I'd maybe wait until it's on sale and advise doing a little research on Youtube because this game can be tedious and extremely cute at the same time - if that's your kind of thing then go for it! ps: Marvelous please give us a Harvest Moon: DS port next, I miss Nami ;n;

_childDocuments_.review: This is Friends of Mineral Town alright. About a couple years ago, I did a let's play of the original Friends of Mineral Town on YouTube. This playthrough made me fall in love with the Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons games, as it is extremely laid back than most of the games I typically play. You inherit your dead grandfathers farm, and it's up to you to keep the farm running and in top shape over the course of the game. How you go about doing so is entirely up to you. You can go fishing, you can mine ore to upgrade your tools, you can cut down wood to renovate your house as well as the barns and chicken coop and stable you start off with. Plus you can also woo and marry this games many different marriage candidates, (and even marry those the same gender as you, if that's your thing). As far as remakes go, the only things that have changed so far from what I can tell is mainly the graphics and the music. The graphics are gorgeous to say the least, and while I can't say the GBA's version of the soundtrack was memorable to me, the instruments used in this soundtrack add so much more to the soundtrack that there were several times I caught myself humming along to this games music. If you're looking for a fun, relaxing sandbox style game, then I'd heavily recommend this one. You're getting your money's worth, especially since this game doesn't quote on quote end.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Harvest moon franchise, and although I've never played either the original FoMT or BTN, I feel like this is a great direction MARVELOUS! is heading. The art style is cutesy (I like how I'm literally just a living pop figure), the pacing isn't too hard or too rushed, and the economy is great (especially if you are smart and get pineapple seeds early). Also gay marriage is a thing, which isn't possible in most if not ANY Harvest moon game, now I'm not gay personally but it's cool to know that that's an option for players who are.Now people DO complain that the game is a bit of a grind, and it is... but to those people I say... What Harvest moon game ISN'T one? That's part of what makes it great, building a routine and improving on it. Making friends with the locals and having a family of your own. Working hard everyday and getting rewarded for it in the long run!good game, 9/10. Taking a point off for the faster day speed, but that's my only real compliant.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a review saying you should not get this game.This is a review saying you should ONLY get this game during a sale with a 30% discount at the minimum.New content that was not in the original FomT:2 new possible spouses, Jennifer and Brandon.Upgraded graphics.More trees on your farm.Same sex marriage (congratulations, LGBTQ+ community).Pets! Including a penguin! New animals, them being rabbits, alpaca sheep, and genetically modified cows (having cows produce chocolate milk from its udder has to be unnatural).Remixed version of the old soundtracks. Not exactly an addition, but it gives you a nostalgic feeling.More random townsfolk events.A huge backpack to replace the basket (quality of life change).Bells for your chicken coop and barn. Recipes can no longer be discovered, and food can only be cooked after obtaining its recipe from events or fishing. Content that are removed from the original FomT:Rival heart events above purple heart.Rival marriage. Telemarketing on Saturdays.The basket (replaced with the huge backpack). Why I do NOT recommend buying this game :I can completely understand everyone in the "recommended" section who are blinded by the nostalgia when this game first dropped. However, to me, I was expecting a little bit more. But first, the positives.The new characters (Jennifer and Brandon) are fantastic additions to the game (decent character sprites too). Jennifer's dialogues are interesting and definitely not as dry compared to her female counterparts. I admire her love for nature, even though Karen was, is, and always will be the best girl. Brandon's character is not made for everyone, and I believe that was the creator's intent. As a world famous artist, he can definitely seem condescending or pompous at times, but after the player gets to know him, he's an alright dude. Another great addition to the game is the bell in front of your chicken coop and barn. I remember the days when I had to manually push my cows out one by one because I wanted a Milk (X) (or was it Milk (P)?). Well, those dreadful days are over. Ringing the bell once when the animals are indoors will bring them all outdoors, and they will automatically return at 8 PM every day, saving you the trouble of pushing them back, just in case it's raining the next day. The transition from a basket to a large rucksack, and having items stack is a huge quality of life change that made farming and mining much quicker and easier. This also means that it's now much easier to get money in the very early game, which leads to the negatives.A lot of players should know the trick on how to get boat loads of money during horse races. I believe a lot of returning players would've easily hit 6-digits in their bank account on the third week of Spring in year one. With the huge amount of money comes a lot of upgrades. Which is outrageous to me why the developers would remove telemarketing on TV every Saturday. The telemarketing service every Saturday was the way to move forward quickly in the culinary world of FomT. And now its been replaced by "praying for Jeff's letter he'll finally sell you another kitchen utensil". Speaking of culinary in FomT, it is another brain dead move to change the cooking system to not allow players to discover recipes on their own. Players are now only allowed to cook from the recipes they own, which can only either be given by townsfolks through their events (which in itself requires high friendship level), or through fishing. Gone are the days of mixing weird items together and having the pleasant surprise of discovering a dish. It's a shame I can no longer cook like Karen. According to the almighty Reddit, Karen is the second most popular girl in FomT behind Popuri (well, FBI, open up). And in this re-make, Rick is going to stay single, even if you did not choose to marry Karen. That's because surveyed Japanese players did not like rival content, so the developers just removed them. You will now only see the black and purple rival heart event, and nothing beyond. I would also like to take this time to mention that the rival event BGM is much better than the heart event the player has.tl:dr:The new additions were good. Some good quality of life changes are included. But way too much content has been cut from the original game. Thus, not really worth paying full price. Verdict:4/10. 5/10 if we're being very generous. If you just want a farming simulator? Get Stardew Valley. If you played the original FoMT and wanted a bite out of the nostalgia cake, get this game during a 30%-50% sale.*Edited for one last time so the review feels smoother to read.

_childDocuments_.review: You really do get sucked to the simple farm life in the countryside. In a short period of time you will get accustomed to waking up early, watering the plants in the morning, cutting the woods, appeasing the harvest goddess by throwing vegetables into the waterfall, go to the inn, library, and then the grocery store to catch up on the latest gossip, got to know more of the townsfolk and hopefully wed one of them, and of course learn the tools of the trade to improve your farm and get tons of cash. I would like to believe the key ingredient as to why I can get absorbed into this game is because the town doesn't care about you. Each character has their own schedule, agenda, goal, and development, as tiny as it seems. The town is not molded for you, YOU are the one that needs to know more of the town. You need to respect the fact that most of the store opens at 10AM but some opens up one hour early and some close on certain days. This also extend to the NPCs, you need to learn their behaviour if you wish to get to know them more. You need to learn that a certain girl goes to church every sunday so she might be unavailable in the grocery store during that time. She also really likes wine. This is where the magic happens. You need to commit more to talk to other people, and you will be rewarded accordingly with fun interactions that makes the town felt alive. You could even find interactions that are only hinted through conversations if you know where to look.I'm 100% biased because I grew up on this game but I the atmosphere is just perfect. The nostalgic tune that gives a perfect picture of the countryside whether it's the soothing spring, the relaxing fall where everything tones down, or the festive winter where people are excited to end the year with festival. The bombastic harvest festival where you need to serve the best dish, the sun-drenched summer you spent chilling wkth the bros on the beach. You just ends up humming along to the tune of the village.The pain point that I encounter is that by the end game-ish, if you want to min-max your farm, it could become too tedious. Watering a small field is fine, watering a large field where it could take the whole day to cover all of them and you need to do that for a month can becomes unbearable and this is with the help of fairies that you can hire that lives next to the church. You can become too focused on the farm, maximizing the amount of money that you can produce that you forget to actually connects with the townsfolk and gets entangled in their interesting lifes. Maybe that's lowkey the point that the game is trying to make.I recommend this game if you want to take a break from your high-pace modern life and chill in the countryside. That goes double for all of you that used to play the original game in your childhood. Karen best girl.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a more neutral instead of an thumbs up or down but alas.TL:DR;  I can only recommend this game if you are looking for the Harvest Moon nostalgia hit, like I was, or if you are curious about how the old Harvest Moons used to be.  That being said, I cannot recommend it unless it's on sale at or below the same price as Stardew Valley.Pros: -Same-sex marriage.  It's nice to see it included since it was not in the original game.  A nice way to bring it into the modern era.  Now my female farmer gets to be with Popouri.-Adorable art style.  The chibis are crisp and cute.  The character cartoon art is nice with the option to see it in full.  The graphics are nice and crisp.-Simple gameplay.  The game isn't to complicated and a lot of it comes naturally with lots of tutorials as you acquire more animals and tools.  The most complicated aspect is finding out how to automate your farm via the sprites.-Time limit.  The time passes at 10 second intervals and pauses inside buildings and mines so there are plenty of ways to take your time when needed.-Save anywhere.  What it says on the tin.  Perfect for save scumming.Neutral:-Simple characters.  While they are cute and personable, they have about one line per season and one per few friendship points so their dialogue gets very repetitive, very quickly.-Grind.  It takes a very long time to get animals to a high enough affection before you get good rewards, usually a few seasons.  You have to use tools before you can upgrade them and it can take a thousand uses before to get to the final few levels.  To upgrade them to the top level means getting every tool to max level, finding a cursed tool which has a tiny chance from a mine only accessible in winter, uncursing it through various means (usually lots of use), then finding a jewel in the said winter only mine that's also absurdly rare so prepare to wait to lots of save scumming.-Character events can be a pain to trigger.  I know NPCs have their own schedules that they follow but some of them make no sense, like I couldn't trigger a certain NPCs events because it was summer and had to wait for Autumn and then it triggered all of them for me one by one.-No combat.  It's expected but some people might expect a little more excitement.Cons:- While you can never truly "miss" something, if you do it'll be a year before you get the chance again.  The winter mine, for example, has items that are absurdly rare, only show up on certain floors, and if you miss them without save scumming you have to wait a year to do it again.  If you miss a recipe on the TV due to an unavoidable event, like marriage, you have to wait a year to get it again.-Repetitive game play.  I know this is a farming game but once you hit Summer of your first year you've basically seen everything the game has to offer.  If you haven't had fun by then, it doesn't really get better.-Stamina is very limited.  Another common aspect of these games but until you upgrade your house you will be relying on tons of forage or spending tons of time in the hot springs to keep up your stamina.  Once you get the house and can cook, expect to keep stacks of food because upgraded tools consume an incredible amount and even with max stamina it goes by very fast.-Small map.  The town is small, your farm is small, the mountain is small.  There's no real exploration to be had as stumps, rocks, and forage all spawn in the same location.  There's no real hidden locations and the closest thing to a discovery I had was finding some gems by clicking on random objects.While I got about 20 hours, which got me to the end of my first year and I'll probably play until I hit the 2nd year and then stop, I can't say I've really had any fun once I got to the end of my first summer.  I don't feel like spending a year raising animals so I can stand a chance in the festivals.  I don't feel like going through another year of farming because I have to keep running to the far end of the map to get the sprites to do it all for me.  If I don't get the sprites to do it for me I don't feel like spending all my stamina and day just tending the farm but you have to without sprites if you want to be slightly profitable.  While yes, in the end it is a farming game but all it really did was make the game crisper and cuter without really bringing the systems into the modern era.In the end... this game was nice for the nostalgia but I cannot recommend it unless it's on sale and at a price point below Stardew Valley which does the same stuff Mineral Town does but better, cheaper, and has a modding community that expands everything about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying i did not play the original Harvest Moon game. I bought this game because I am a big fan of Stardew Valley and My time at Portia, and wanted to try out a new farming sim game. I read online that FoMT was one of the best HM/SoS games out there, so I bought the game when it was on sale 30% off.Although I did have fun through the first few seasons, it is definitely not in my opinion worth its full price. Even with have gotten it on a sale I feel I payed too much. I would say wait AT LEAST a 50% sale to get what it’s worth.I generally rather enjoy the concept of upgrading tools and farm supplies for QoL and making more money, but SoS:Fomt will make you wait too long for upgrades or make you do tedious tasks for X amount of time before the upgrade is available.I stopped playing in winter of my first year because of this as I didn’t see the point anymore to wait such a long time just to fully complete the game.Examples: Animals produce better products with higher heart-level. You buy animals with a max heart-cap of 5 hearts (max is 10). You can’t upgrade an animal’s heart-cap once boughten, you need to breed the animals and their offspring will have 1 heart-cap higher. So you need 5 generations of animal to reach 10-heart cap. Coop animals don’t take so long to breed (3-7 days), but Cows/sheep/alpaca take 21 days to breed... that’s almost an entire season for one heart! So a 10-heart cow would take you 21x5=105 days just in waiting (that is if you don’t forget the feed the pregnant animal, otherwise it’s longer)(oh and you also need to wait for the offspring to reach adulthood before breeding that one, so add another 7 days to adulthood x5 offspring =35 days), then you need to do animal care every day to actually raise the heart level. And you can only breed 1 coop and 1 barn animal at a time, 2 if you upgrade their building. After a year I just had two 6-heart cap barn animals. I had got to one 9-cap in the coop. Definitely not worth the wait just to get better animal produce, especially considering your farm should be pretty big by then. You would think you only need some ore and money to upgrade the tools, but you also need a “percentage of usage” for each tool. Which means you could have all the money and the ore needed to upgrade, but didn’t swing the tool enough. Rocks and tree stumps spawn every day, but you don’t gather their resource everyday as it uses a lot of stamina. So to upgrade your tools without having to wait for stumps/rocks to spawn, you need to swing your tools on nothing so they gather EXP, and that wastes stamina/time in your day. The mines are impossible to go down unless you save scum (save, dig to find a ladder, remember were the ladder is, reload and dig it up). There are  levels and without the save trick you would use all your stamina and pass out around levels 10-15. You need to go down the entirety of the  levels of one of the mines to continue upgrading your tools which takes HOURS. And there are two mines like this. However, there is a way to get , but this involves . I got to the bottom of one of the mines and it took me 4 hours of just save scumming. I gave up for the second mine. To cook you need recipes, food and kitchen utensils (like an oven, whisk, pot…). Most recipes need multiple utensils to cook. Your kitchen comes with no utensils; you need to buy them at the general store. No biggie, right? However, you can only buy one utensil, the next ones unblock in intervals of 10 days (there are 8 of them). So you can’t really cook that much at the start. You could have the recipe and all the food needed but oops, no whisk! You can’t make it. I didn’t even bother with cooking as I couldn’t do most recipes I knew, and there weren’t really any profit to make based on cooking alone. When I stopped playing (mid-winter), I had 6 or 7 cooking utensils. As I am a completionist, I read online on how to find certain objects and what they are for. (Spoilers for purposes of certain objects in the game). First of all, the pedometer. At the start of the game, you get a pedometer that counts the number of steps you take. The game doesn’t say more. I wondered what it was for so I googled, it said after a certain number of steps something would happen (I didn’t read what at first). I kept it in my bag, and after X number of steps,  Nope.Second, the truth jewels. Many of them are easy to find around town, but one of them would take  to get. You read that right. In fact, it’s at  that you would get it. Nope, nope, nope!So all in all, this game still had the classic farming sim features as in foraging, befriending NPC’s, farming, taking care of animals that has a relaxing tone to it, but everything becomes way too long at the end (after not even an in-game year of gameplay). There also isn’t really any quests in the game, so there’s nothing really to look forward to except the upgrades.tl;dr: Fun game at the start, but the upgrades take way too long. Most of them are just waiting-games, or repetition of a same task. Not much gratification either after the wait. Wait at least for a 50% sale for this game, or don’t buy it in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: A basic farming sim.    • Gameplay includes: farming, animal caretaking, fishing, foraging, cooking, mining, social affection increasing    • Crafting/smithing is done by an NPC.    • No combat.     • Time passes in 10 minute increments per 5 actual seconds. Time stops when inside buildings, a mine, or when dialogues/cutscenes are happening. However, some cutscenes will automatically skip time, depending on what happens.    • Romance can be with men and women regardless of character’s gender. Romances can be done simultaneously until marriage (in fact, there’s an achievement to do all of them).     • A baby is born or adopted after marriage automatically. Player can choose between a boy or girl or choose to be “surprised.”     • You can save at any time. Thank you!    • Gameplay can be addictive (more so in the beginning).    • Adorable animations for all the animals. The cat animations include rolling around on the ground! So f*cking cute!    • You can get several pets: cat, dog, penguin, & capybara. (I am a little disappointed that it takes a while to obtain the capybara though.)    • Cute chibi appearances for the character sprites, then lovely cartoon art for the portraits.     • I like the goddess offering rewards system. I think that’s an interesting way to unlock things and obtain items.     • Some of the character romances are cute or amusing.     • A controller works well with the game, with exception of one or two actions that must be done with a mouse instead.    • No overall story. Your character inherits the farm and that’s their new life. That’s it.     • I feel like this is a game that they cared too much about being kid-friendly that they failed to make things more interesting because of it. Which is silly, because you  make kid-friendly stuff interesting. Adults really underestimate children’s reading/story comprehension.     • Mini-games and events are bland/boring.     • Very limited exploration. The town is small. The forest and mountain area outside the town is small.     • Ridiculous item discovery percentages. 0.4% for rare tools that can be discovered in a mine,  once you have  tools, you can finally mine for a rare ore that is also at a 0.4% chance of appearing. Without the rare ore, you cannot upgrade all the original tools to their highest level. The mine that you get the rare tools in is only available during winter, so the player has 30 days each year to find them, unless they want to reload their save file a lot.    • This is another game that has achievements that attempt to coerce the player into playing the game long after they’re done with it. If devs want players to have long play times, then put in a lot of content instead of being cheap.     • I’ve read that supposedly a cabin in the mountain area unlocks at Year 50. Fifty. 5-0. 5X10. Bruh … bruh … no one, absolutely no one, wants to play that long. Oh, and there’s nothing that special about this cabin. Just like there isn’t anything that special about the town villa or the beach house the player can obtain.     • Animals aren’t programmed to stay away from entrances or items the player uses regularly, so sometimes they’ll be in the way, and they’re not easy to move.    • In the character creation, there are only 3 skin tones: super light, slightly tan, and light brown. … Come on, devs. Wtaf?    • There is only one light brown main NPC in the game. Everyone else is light-skinned. Later, you can unlock a special NPC that starts visiting the town, and she’s between tan and light brown. Needless to say, the devs didn’t even care if their tokenism was super obvious. I didn’t hate the game, but I definitely felt like with all the issues I’ve complained about that I can’t actually recommend it either. I got it on a severe discount, which I’m glad about. So, if you were still interested in this game, I’d suggest doing the same to actually get your money’s worth. I’ve read that SoS: Pioneers of Olive Town is better than this one. There’s also another coming out called A Wonderful Life. If you’re unsure about this game, maybe look into one of those instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I've posted a video on my YT channel with the review in case you'd prefer to watch instead:But I'll also write here the main points for me and if it has fullfilled my expectations as someone who has played most (old) Harvest Moon and SoS games:THE GOODFirst of all, most of the positives rely on the (many!) quality of life improvements to the gameplay mechanics:1. You can now increase the size of your bag and can stack items in your inventory.2. Now you can upgrade your tools and water bigger areas - that may sound basic if you have played other farming games like stardew valley but in past harvest moon games we could NEVER reach that tile in the middle (which was pretty annoying)3. You can have many different types of pets and they are actually pretty cute.4. The map is now much more detailed and you can click on the buildings to check their opening times which is pretty handy.5. Now you can also check your relationship levels with other characters in the main menu.6. In past harvest moon games everything was a secret. You could never figure out the sprites and other mechanics without looking up on a guide. Now the game teaches you the most basic mechanics which is pretty good for any new players.Apart from that, half of the fun of this game really is the nostalgia of the classic old harvest moon games, where time pass by slowly, you get uncover secrets little by little and get to meet those characters you love once again.THE BAD1. The animations your character does when you run out of stamina are way too frequent and extremely disruptive. It feels like it half of my gameplay time is watching my character tired every 5 seconds i use a tool. Really really wish there was an option to turn these off.2. All the cutscenes with the bachelors and dialogue in general is just not engaging. There is a lack of dialogue where the NPCs basically say 2 or 3 things the whole season. It feels empty, has no sense of progression and one of the most interesting mechanics they used to have in previous games, which was the rival cutscenes, were cut off.3. Also in this game, you can't try and error cook anymore and to get new recipes is not intuitive whatsoever. The main way is watching the tv in specific days which is pretty annoying.4. There isn't much customization. Considering this is a recent game it's pretty limited. You can't customize your farm, your house and to get new outfits you need to pay for DLCs.5. The world itself is not interesting, there is no main story anymore and the places aren't explorable. You can't walk pretty much anywhere besides the road path making it feel very limited.6. Even though its true to the original game, there is nothing to look forward to. Animals dont die or get sick, so you dont really need to care after some time. The pacing is extremely slow where after you upgrade your farmhouse there is a sense of not really having anything to do in your day. Your earn money but don't have anything interesting to spend it on.THE UGLY1. Art is a very personal preference kind of thing, the art style overall is okay and some portraits and redesigns are really nice, but some are just awful. Essentially it looks like it was supposed to be a mobile game, and I don't know. It's just personal opinion really innit.2. The music of the game is excellent and really chill really nice BUT sfx are awful, really low quality recordings. First 5 minutes playing the game and you will instantly notice.3. The User Interface, like i mentioned in other reviews i work with this everyday so i'm a bit particular about that. Even though the overall user experience you have with the interface has improved a lot in comparison to previous games, it doesn't look nice and can still be improved a lot more, just by providing more guidance and making it clear the functions you have in your menus.Personal OpinionOk overall, this is a remake not a new game. I think that is the most important point because if you look at the previous harvest moon games you can see this is a great improvement but it still has a lot to catch up with other farming games from this generation. This game is essentially about nostalgia. It's not a remake like FF7 where we got lots of cool new stuff and a new view on the game, this is more of a remake for those who played the harvest moon friends of mineral town in the past and really want to feel that nostalgia again.Hope that is helpful somehow and would love to hear your opinions on this as well.Cheers

_childDocuments_.review: Want to preface this by saying that I was a HM: Back to Nature player and was SO excited for this title, like the most excited I had been for a release in a while.+ cute. everything and everyone's cute+ first lgbt friendly HM/SoS title where u can marry whomever regardless of your gender+ addition of bachelor/ettes, including the hidden ones+ house upgrades feel nice+ strawberry? fruit? coffee? there's a cow to satisfy each of ur milk cravings +/- feels like pure farming without much time to socialize with villagers or even go fishing+/- day feels too short (see in -'s below); however, this creates incentive to keep going onto the next day and allows you to progress through the years faster- if you don't have the Sprites to do your tasks for you, there's no way a full day is anywhere near enough to tend to your farm, even a smaller one (for reference, i only have a little over 2 full rows of crops (spanning the width of the field) and silver watering can)- it's been ~2 decades and yet the stamina/fatigue system still feels about the same;- buying recovery items is essentially getting robbed blind by the Clinic- you can't rely on cooking for a while due to the 1/week recipe broadcast, as well as having to depend on whether or not you've even unlocked the required cooking tools- trying to mine feels impossible. inability to use tool charges, floor resets, and back to the issue of energy usage. (maybe i've been spoiled by Stardew but thinking that SoSFoMT has 200+ floors like this blows my mind)- this is essentially a bathing simpersonal -'s:- feels kind of weird and jarring that once nighttime hits, the music just cuts (though I don't mind the ambiance)- why the bear and angora rabbits sound like that- doctor's name is Doctor lolIt's great for that nostalgia if you played older entries in the series or if you really want just a pure farming grind, but for me it's just too tedious and boring simultaneously, jumping to try and tend to all my crops and then sitting in the bath for hours, just to get out and do it again. If the Sprites are there to help, I still don't feel like I can get much done in a day other than lumbering and breaking down a few rocks. I wanted to recommend this game so badly but I can't. :^(

_childDocuments_.review: This a *fantastic* game. It is mostly the old "Friends of Mineral Town" and "More Friends of Mineral Town" games combined into one (you have your choice of 2 female and 2 male PC models when starting a new game) with updated graphics and music that remind me of Windwaker. It does change a few names, introduce a few new faces and new events, and some of the dialogue has subtle changes from the original script. It also features some key quality of life improvements over the original games- such as connecting the hot spring area to the lake area with a path, adding an unlockable elevator to the mine for depths you've *already reached by hand* and, most importantly, you can finally walk through your crops. It also allows for same-gender romances if that's your thing.Don't worry, just like old times, if you bring Karen french fries and wine, she'll rock your world.I think you can certainly argue that the full new-release price ($50) is a little steep for what you get, but I didn't hesitate- FoMT and MFoMT as well as my GBA are all pushing 20 years and I know they won't last much longer. If you're a big fan of those games like I am, having spent thousands of hours in them and still going strong, this game is worth the price.TL;DRGood remake. Small amount of new content and quality of life improvements. Harvest Moon fanatics it's absolutely worth full price, if you're on the fence, nab it when it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a remake of a remake of the OG farm game: Harvest Moon Back To Nature! And ti's really good!Positives[] YES! YURI HAREM BABY! I can play a girl character now and date girls. If you're a guy and guys are your thing, you can do that too. BUT HEY I'D RATHER HAVE A YURI HAREM ANYTIME OF THE DAY![] Character redesigns were made, along with some renaming as close to the Japanese names. [] The game feels very responsive and not clumsy. [] The map layout is based on Harvest Moon Friends of Mineral Town (from GBA).[] The gameplay is simple, good, and relaxing. There are no animosity or enemies that are hostile to you.[] The game is 3D! Not an indie 2D fan reimagination of the OG Harvest Moon! Finally I can have fun both gameplay-wise and graphically!Negatives[] Sadly, there's no Windows 7 support (as of the time of writing). You have to be Win 8 or above to be able to play this game.[] Some animation times are significantly longer than previous Harvest Moons/Story of Seasons. Brushing, milking or shearing animals takes 3-4 seconds. Harvesting crops is really slow too, it takes roughly 1 sec per crop, multiply that to the number of crops you have and you can be there for a very very long time.Side Note: • We're comparing apples and oranges, but just don't expect Animal Crossing New Horizons levels of island customization or art style. You can customize your farm to a degree like where to plant where, but you cannot remodel the whole town. The art style is good too, but not to the cuteness that is Animal Xing --- they both have their own identity and art style, let's just respect that.• You want automated watering in the form of iridium sprinklers? You'll have to befriend the Harvest Sprites. Actually, I'd rather have the Harvest Sprites since they are more helpful. They can harvest for you, water your crops and care for the animals, all for the low low price of friendship and occasional gifts.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played Friends of Mineral Town before, then absolutely try it. It's a staple of the series and worth playing if you're a fan! And even if you have, there are a lot of things that are improved upon (an actual stamina bar is life changing) but, there are more than a few things that are changed or left out that I feel were pretty essential in their own right.If you remember the old GBA game, here are a few things that might make the new game a difficult transition to make. This review will focus on those.-Updated Character Sprites/NamesA plus for some and a minus for others. Some characters are only improved; the marriage candidates in particular have been upgraded and a lot of the only barely passable bachelors are properly handsome now! But the changes do mean even the largely unchanged characters lose a bit of their old charm, and the characters that do get changes seem to be for little reason. Carter is a major personal disappointment, he looks actively worse.[Mostly upgrades with some inexplicable and potentially negative changes.]-Greater Variety of AnimalsOn paper this is only a plus. There are different kinds of cows, new pets, alpacas and rabbits and so on. The art style makes most of them look more silly than cute, though not in an unwelcome way!But with this boon there is a drawback in that the friendship system has undergone a bit of a re-haul that I can't say I'm in favour of.In the GBA edition, any animal you had was able to reach maximum friendship with you, so long as you treated them right. In this game, every animal comes with a hard capped friendship at about half its usual capacity - which affects the quality of the items that you're getting from them. The first cow you ever purchase will never give you high-quality milk. The first chicken you hatch will never give you high-quality eggs. It's possible that their friendship increases more quickly than previously, but a) this removes the sense of accomplishment and companionship you used to forge with you animals as the seasons passed and you grew closer, and b) doesn't matter anyway because once you've maxed out the friendship they're allowed to have, your only recourse is to sell them.Normally how it worked was you would make a large payment on the initial farm animal, and spend much less on miracle potions to raise offspring and fill your barns. The affection cap new animals are given seems to encourage the same behavior, as the friendship cap can only be raised slowly over generations - an extra heart added to the cap for each new generation of animals born on the farm.In theory, this is a lovely system because it means that you're progressing towards a perfect ideal slowly over time, the entire point of these games. But in practice the relationship you have with your animals will suffer for it. At some point your first cow, the start of your little farmstead home, will have to be sold off. And so will her children, and their children, until eventually they have enough affection to be worth holding on to. Mothers separated from their calves the instant they give birth because you need the space to get the next animal pregnant and start expanding their generational affection meters too. It's a little discouraging![Changes to the friendship system mean all your animals are temporary and its hard to get attached. It takes exponentially longer for worthwhile products.]-No More Experimental CookingAnother change that makes more sense on paper than in execution. Cooking is now an exact art: you either have the recipe or you don't. No more testing different ingredients or being rewarded with secret family recipes from well liked villagers. It seems the only way to improve the foods you make is with better quality of needed ingredients instead of additional ones that you could add at your own discretion. Once I had the recipe for Curry Udon I never needed to make anything else, so the fun of it was rather lost for me. The tl;dr version is that the game is improved in a lot of areas, especially visually, but there are some unfortunate stumbling blocks on the path of improvement and not all of the changes are welcome. I've still put a lot of time into the game, and will continue to do so; but my overall impression is that there are just a few too many things that make me miss the un-updated version.

_childDocuments_.review: I reinstall Friends of Mineral Town after months of not playing, and quickly remember why I uninstalled it. A load of tedious actions that were okay for a 90s mobile game, but not for a modern game. Wonderful that they stuck very closely to the original, but I do not enjoy several second animations to explain that I am tired for the 400th time, or managing seven different little """elves""" to do everything I want, or giving people the same things every day, or spending some time in a mine, waiting to regenerate stamina in the spa, then rinsing and repeating. OR THE ONE CHARACTER IF YOU CLICK ON HER ON ACCIDENT YOU HAVE TO LISTEN TO A MONTH OF DIALOGUE. Too many textboxes and stupid bound controls make Emi angry.Yet I'm still playing it. If you ignore how basic this game is and don't treat it like a chore like I do, I'm sure you'll have so much fun maybe. It is really cute.TL;DR The more you remember this is a grindy 90s Gameboy-Advance game, the less you care for the flaws. On sale worth uwu30 hours more playtime: I feel like there's a lot of content and I'm just not finding it or figuring it out. What am I supposed to be doing? Who is giving gifts to a waste of time for or not? Does the Villa even let me sleep there? How many times do I need to throw valuable things in a river for someone to like me? How long until ANYTHING? New characters pop in and it's like "... okay thank u. Cosmetics and cooking recipes all around, yay. I'm starting to feel frustrated running the same route everyday getting the same items, giving the same gifts, and doing the same routine each day. Makes it even worse I failed to earn a horse fast. Medic20 more hours playtime, July 31st 2022: The game has become a repetitive grind fest that I reluctantly chug through. Why did they choose a GBA game to remaster. I'm sick of getting stuck on things and the unmemorable childish map and the goals meant for a kid in the 90s with no school.August 29th, 2022 - After re-installing and thinking about the game more: Why not make money in real life. There's no automation here that isn't annoying af, so why not go do something in real life that's way more fun that doesn't make you sit through an animation when you accidentally walk too fast and lose your breath. This can go into a whole "what's the point of any game" situation but it goes soooo just... checklist-like for a game that's supposed to be about stress-free living. I strongly advise just going for walks or exploring your real life neighborhood instead, you may enjoy it more.The one positive I miss about this game, is that at least seasons are fast. Sometimes in real life, I miss certain parts of Summer when it's Winter, and vice versa. This game says eff that and makes days last seconds, meaning you can experience years of your life within hours. (Seasons, relationships, career, finances, etc)September 1st 2022: It was all fun and games until I got stuck with a cursed sickle for five days. eff u im playing olive town

_childDocuments_.review: I dumped hundreds of hours into Friends of Mineral Town on the GBA when I was a kid. For better or worse, this is essentially just a basic remake with some nice quality of life features and two new characters. Those QoL features are good, like having a better inventory system and saving almost everywhere, but I feel like there was so much potential to add more stuff. Same sex marriage is also a plus, and every bachelor and bachelorette are available for everyone. Unfortunately, the rival marriages were cut, which makes the game feel more limited. The village ends up feeling static and unchanging while your farm evolves over time. FOMT runs well on the Steam Deck, but it occasionally will have some visual glitches in its menus. It's nothing game breaking though.I can only really recommend this to people who played one of the two original versions of FOMT. People new to the farming genre are better off playing Stardew Valley, especially since it has a much better modding community.

_childDocuments_.review:
Originally released for the Nintendo Game Boy Advance in 2003, STORY OF SEASONS: Friends of Mineral Town is a complete remake that will let series fans revisit the charming world of Mineral Town, while also introducing it to a new generation of farmers. In this peaceful setting, players will grow crops, take care of animals, and build relationships with villagers.  * Rediscover one of STORY OF SEASONS' most beloved entries: This Nintendo Switch remake of the classic game preserves the compelling gameplay, colourful characters and rustic charm of the original 2003 Game Boy Advance release. With buttery-smooth HD visuals and a heartwarming reimagining of the iconic locale, series veterans and newcomers will soon find themselves welcomed by the gentle rhythms of Mineral Town.

* Live the simple life in Mineral Town: Tap into the power of nature as you breathe life back into your grandfather's farm, tending crops and raising livestock to earn your keep. With more than 20 varieties of crops to grow, and animals ranging from alpacas to angora bunnies, no day is the same as seasons cycle and new skills await.

* Forge friendships with the townsfolk and win their hearts: Mineral Town is full of friendly faces willing to help you find your feet in your new hometown. Get to know the locals and learn their stories as you go about your daily life, and you might even find love along the way!

* Activities galore for days off from the farm: Whether it's high-tailing in horseraces, catching a champion trout or showcasing your culinary creativity, the busy calendar full of festivals means that there's never a dull day in Mineral Town. If you're looking for a quieter time, take yourself away to the local hot spring, delve deep into the mines, or seek out the seasonal secrets of the town.
