name: Disjunction
detailed_description: 2048. Following the arrest of a prominent community leader, New York stands in disarray. Suspicions and allegations run rife throughout the city, as an insidious drug known as ‘Shard’ spreads throughout the underworld. With the city’s future in doubt, three hardened citizens rise to discover the truth and uncover a conspiracy threatening to alter the city’s fate. Inspired by tech noir classics, Disjunction is an intensely atmospheric stealth-action RPG that follows a trinity of interwoven narratives, and features a reactive story where your actions have real, persistent consequences. Choose your playstyle and use an arsenal of futuristic tech, cybernetic upgrades and weapons to blast through levels in brutally fast combat, or take a silent approach by using stealth and non-lethal takedowns to leave without a trace. Nobody needs to die… unless you decide they must. KEY FEATURES: Challenging stealth-action gameplay that lets you play the way that suits your style, whether it’s sneaking through levels or attacking head-on. Three playable characters, each with individual abilities, cybernetic upgrades and talents to customise your playstyle. A reactive story where the player’s choices have real consequences. Stylized pixel art environments and characters. Atmospheric musical score by composer Dan Farley. Gameplay: Disjunction features unique stealth-action mechanics and abilities for each of its three playable characters, giving players the freedom and flexibility to choose the playstyle that suits them. Tackle encounters in lethal, high-octane combat, or use your wits to stick to the shadows, utilizing distraction techniques and non-lethal attacks to reach your objective. Augmentation: Unlock cybernetic upgrades to augment your abilities via upgrade trees, and build upon your playstyle to improve your stealth or increase the lethality of attacks through talent trees. Find upgrade kits to reach your true potential and become a feared killer or remain anonymous throughout New York's shady underground. Reactive Story: Experience a reactive story shaped by your actions. Your approach to situations can have serious consequences for the future of New York City, with the repercussions of choosing to spare or kill even one person rippling throughout the underworld. Crush entire factions or convince them to aid your cause. Your destiny is yours to write. The World: The year is 2048, and the world is plagued with economic downturn, environmental disaster, and societal destabilization. In the United States, natural resource scarcity and severe climate change have led to massive urbanization, with millions of Americans forced to seek new lives among the sprawling steel and concrete of America’s cities. These swelling urban populations, coupled with intense civil unrest, have culminated in greatly increased crime rates, with many cities becoming dense hives of vice and lawlessness. City governments and law enforcement do their best to stem the rising tide of crime, but are often ineffective due to severe corruption and the increasing sophistication of American criminals.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I don't think Disjunction is a good game.To give you a small impression where I'm coming from: I love stealth games and Deus Ex and the old 2D Metal Gear games are some of my favorites. So when I get the option to sneak around, without killing anybody, I will do that.As a stealth game, Disjunction doesn't get, what makes stealth games fun to play. It is one of those "Try to stay out of cone shapes" games, which take a naive approach to the genre. You don't use your wits or cunning, there isn't any meaningful interaction with the environment, you aren't exploring interesting spaces - the only challenge in every room of every level is to avoid cone shapes, while collecting the same keys, lore dumbs and upgrade items. You're mostly just reacting to the movement of the enemies, as you hardly have any room to breath and observe the movement patterns, which itself can feel like trying to unravel a plate of spaghetti.That itself might be tolarable, when Disjunction wouldn't be so repetitive. There is only one checkpoint per level and you have to replay the whole section, if you fail at one point. I get it, challenging games are fun, but you, dear devs, need to figure out, why challenging games are fun and what part of a challenging game might be not fun (ever noticed how From Software shortened the walk up to their boss battles?). Especially annoying are checkpoints, that are covered by enemies and set you up for an auto-failure when reloading those checkpoints, forcing you to replay the whole level (which, to fair, happened only one or twice).The story is a big case of needing to "Show, don't tell." Between missions you have dialogs between characters and there are some keywords, that reveal additional lore. Reading that is optional, but also necessary to keep up with the world around you, but there's also too much of it with too little of value to stay interested. At some point I couldn't keep up with the story and lost interest. Guys, you have to give me a reason to care about the stuff that happens in your game.There are RPG elements, but also like the rest of the game, there's a misunderstanding of why certain things work and why some don't. Disjunction repeats the same flaw of Deus Ex and binds abilities to a finite amount of energy, which means those abilites end up being underused, as you don't want to waste your energy in case you end up in an emergency situation. As for the upgrading part of the RPG system, you don't learn any new exciting abylities, as you're just upgrading a few key values, that hardly feel like they are doing a difference.To summarize it all, I hate to say it, but Disjunction feels like an amateurish game, that is clearly inspired by some great games, but doesn't understand why those games work. Playing it like Hotline Miami might be a better experience, but as a stealth game it's way too underwhelming.The art and music is pretty dope, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm... I don't know if recommended is really what I should place this game under.But it's not bad and it's cheap !This game is quite weird because the story is very mature, It can also be quite bloody if you go full rampage...The music is awesome and could be described as some kind of dark ambient, the pixel art graphics are fantastic though repetitive.But the gameplay is childish... The game consist of small levels divided in two floors each time with a save point located on each floor which you can use at any point but you can use it only once... The game would be perfect for a kid to learn how to handle stealth games, it is a very good introduction to the stealth genre.The game is very repetitive and the AI is quite dumb. The challenge is created by the fact you have only one save point on each floor and because when enemies find you, you're as good as dead. (but not in early levels)The game teaches you about corners and line of sight, dragging bodies, stunning enemies, basic sound detection... And the use of abilities accross 3 characters which are honnestly all the same ! (they have slight differences with their abilities but in the end, you'll still play them the same way)The character does respond well though and the game is very enjoyable but even with that,If you're looking for a short-lived game teaching you about stealth or a nice little narrative experience, then this game is for you. Do not expect much replayability unless you absolutely want all achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: People need to stop tagging anything that has "XP" or "Talents" as an RPG. This is not an RPG by any reasonable definition.The game bills itself on being able to shoot your way through, which sounded okay to me since I don't normally like stealth. The problem is that your ammo count is limited and the game explicitly goes out of its way via NPC dialogue to not shoot your way through things. Fine, we can do melee - except then enemies start being unable to be knocked out in one melee strike even as a sneak attack.Actually yeah let's talk about melee some more. Melee stuns an enemy on hit for a brief time. You can chain together enough hits to KO an enemy from full without them being able to act, but if you haven't upgraded your attack speed or stun time (not always reasonable), you need nearly perfect timing or the enemy will get to act anyways. The timing shifts away from "sneak attack at the perfect time" to "play a rhythm game or you take damage", which is perverse design.There are three characters, but the story keeps shifting between them and their skillsets aren't meaningfully different, so all this accomplishes is delaying your limited progression by splitting up experience and upgrades between them.I got suckered by the RPG tag and the promise of shooting your way out. That was a damned lie. What's left isn't enough to keep me hooked, especially when checkpoints are so scattered that one mistake requires you to perfectly do everything else again for the third or fourth time. You're better off finding something else if you don't really, really love stealth games.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't gotten very far with it yet but having played with the first two characters, that being the Private Investigator and the Boxer, I've had a lot of fun so far! Disjunction not only has an interesting narrative, but the gameplay is very addicting and you'll easily find yourself switching it up from time to time to fit different situations. The combat, whether you go for a stealth approach or a shootout approach, is very fair and doesn't fail to impress. If you're looking for a Cyberpunk game similar to games like Hotline Miami in terms of the art style, you should definitely consider picking this up.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm thoroughly enjoying my experience with Disjunction. You play as three separate characters whose storylines intertwine and run parallel to one another. Despite being advertised as a stealth-RPG, the game gives you a plethora of options to customize your gameplay. You can play non-lethally with melee, lethally with different guns, or use a combination of both. Your choice in lethality affects the dialogue, characters, and endings. The game can also be quite challenging depending on your playstyle. The art fits the setting extremely well, from dark and dingy apartments, to colorful and ominous cityscapes. I was especially impressed by Frank's apartment. The chilling techno music adds a nice ambiance (I would also recommend the soundtrack bundle). The UI is simple and easy to understand, with objectives clearly emphasized, sidequests tracked, and a map to assist you. Maybe the most robust part of this game, other than its flexibility in gameplay, is its story and lore. The game designates key words (characters, organizations, relevant terms) and offers you tool tips within the dialogue for each one. If you forget your character's backstory, why you're investigating something, or what "shard" is, you can hover your mouse over the name or word each time it's mentioned for a reminder. As you play, you can talk to NPCs and find pieces of lore that build upon the story and give you an in-depth understanding of the world. I highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting pretty eagerly for Disjunction since I heard of the concept and especially since I tried the demo. I'm a big Deus Ex fan and there are a lot of things I miss about the older concepts and design philosophies of the 90s and 2000s. Disjunction really makes an addition to this legacy of stealth-action.So far I have only been ghosting (No combat, full stealth) and I am really happy with the possibility but also challenge of doing that approach, as in Dishonored, or, to a lesser extent, Heat Signature. The story has been very reactive to the level of stealth as well as dialogue choices. I feel an appreciation for the characters as you meet them but also as your craft their in-game approaches and dialogue responses, really feeling out their struggles and principles.The soundtrack philosophy also hits the spot for me. It is somewhat ambient but really distinctively entrenched into the tone of the game. I am currently beginning Joe's story, and really feeling the anxiety and dread of his scenario come through the music as he embarks on an existentially last-ditch investigation as to why his life was shattered.Disjunction is a fantastic signal of developers seeking to continue worthwhile traditions of the past, and I hope this game will also revitalize expectations of deep storytelling woven with engaging gameplay for new audiences.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little game, but this is not a long game, and for the price it doesn't feel like it was worth it. It is simple, reliant on the 'tell' part of 'show don't tell' story presentation, and for a stealth game is a bit shallow. Give it a shot for sure on a nice sale, but you will be done before you realize it.

_childDocuments_.review: i don't normally write reviews for games, but i had to make an exception. this is an absolute gem of a game. only a couple hours in, and i got completely sucked in. the story is detailed and immersive (i LOVE that you can hover over text to learn more background). every level feels very carefully thought out and put together, and i enjoyed replaying levels to see all the different ways i could beat it. i personally find the sneakier method more reliable, but it was also super fun to go full-on murder mode. and what can i say, i'm a total sucker for the grungy, cyberpunk pixelated aesthetic.AND to make this game even better, it is SO REFRESHING (and exceedingly rare) to see a game that features an asian-american character that doesn't tokenize or otherize them (like other games that feature foreign asian characters or are set in asia). as an asian-american woman, this truly means a lot to me. thank you for the tasteful representation, devs :).anyway, if you want a game that allows you to be creative and has a (disturbingly realistic) depiction of dystopian NYC, you will not regret buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I suppose I can recommend ? While it's certainly not great, it does enough I like to leave me with a positive overall impression.First off, I enjoyed bouncing between these three different characters - gaining proficiency with their abilities and "leaning in" to my preferred gameplay style using the talent and upgrade system available. The gameplay itself was generally satisfying, with satisfying  from sneaky melee strikes and the visual information necessary to help you maintain stealth if you so desire.However, there were times that melee hit detection felt imprecise and the game required a particular orientation towards an enemy you were attempting to strike. Getting detected or killed after having your swings fail to register never feels good. Also, I'm fairly tolerant to challenge in stealth games, but I felt that there was a bit too much time between each checkpoint in . A superior system, in my view, is the one used in the stealth game . In this game you're given a limited number of saves per level, and once they're gone, .Although I liked the visual design of the characters, abilities, and setting, the level environments felt somewhat repetitive to me. I also didn't love the music, although there were a few tracks that stood out. The sound effects, like the melee attack I mentioned earlier, are satisfying and crisp.Honestly, the biggest strike I have against the game is the story. I had a lot of trouble actually following what was going on, bouncing between these three different characters. After a while I stopped trying to follow it and tried to just enjoy the combat and stealth gameplay. These systems were strong enough to hold my attention without a coherent narrative, but only just so.If you're a fan of top-down stealth games that give you enough information to work with and a couple alternatives for how you approach encounters, you'll probably enjoy . However, I still much prefer the 2D side-scrolling stealth of games like , , , or . And if you're looking for a cool cyberpunk story, maybe take notes? I don't know.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing little gem of a game. It is exactly what it looks like -- a pixel art top-down cyberpunk action, where you choose if you want to go in heavy, or try and use stealth. It's retro in a good sense: a bit hard sometimes, but you get better as you go and become a true master of the game closer to an end. Also it took me 15 hours to beat, which is exactly what I like in the games these days -- no need to invest hundreds of hours -- get in, get fun, get results. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Disjunction is a stealth-action game in a cyberpunk setting. Combine Deus Ex and Dishonored together and you get Disjunction. Pixel art is great, it has that retro feeling. Level design is good. Every level offers you different approaches. If you find one path difficult, try the other one it can be easier than the first path. It is a stealth game so memorizing enemy patterns and behaviors is the key here. Once you get caught, you are not defenseless. Every character has a gun and different abilities to defend themselves. You can gun down 2 or 3 enemies and solve the crisis you in easily. Your choices matter. Who you spare or kill etc. Everything has a consequence in the end. It has a replay value because of that.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: I really like stealth games so Disjunction is a fairly good one. I think if there was a save at any time function, it would be way too easy although there were some times when I felt it was a bit frustrating. The threat escalation is really good. The basic enemies are nothing compared to the enemies towards the end of the game. But gradually, through the upgrades, I never felt entirely overwhelmed. When I died, it was because I rushed.  Disjunction demands something of a continuous  attention to it. The setting and art was great too. Sometimes with cyberpunk stories, it's very easy to be heavy-handed with the metaphors but this was well put together that I really wanted to see the story to its conclusion. The sound design is pretty great too.My criticisms of the game revolve largely around the very bland level design. There are a handful of level types and although some care is put into enemy placement and the like, they feel very same-y very quickly. The missions themselves are also very repetitive. It's always, no matter what, move through a set of levels and find keys to unlock doors. Yes, you get some choices to make, but it would be nice for a little more variety to the mission types.Also, for a stealth game, there's very little in the way of real ability to influence the environment. I was hoping to find things to deactivate, or tamper with etc. Just a couple of extra ways to make it feel a little less like a hotline miami that's trying to be quiet.Overall, I do recommend this game for a fun but short cyberpunk experience and I hope the developers keep making games and expanding on their concept because it is very solid.

_childDocuments_.review: Just when you thought the cyberpunk genre was about to die (just kidding) Ape Tribe Games stokes the flames with their new stealth-action RPG, Disjunction. Set in 2048 in the seedy underworld of New York, you will play as three unique characters with three intertwining stories dealing with city corruption, murder, and a new drug called Shard that is ravaging the city.  Each character has their own style and progression tree of upgrades and talents to create a dynamic mix of stealth and action gameplay.You’ll start off playing as Frank, your classic private investigator, then switch off to Joe, a cybernetic enhanced boxer with a metal arm and jaw, and finally Spider, a gifted hacker that uses her tech skills to enhance her combat.  Disjunction is designed so that you could technically play the game without killing anyone.  In fact, early on Frank gets yelled at over the phone if/when you do kill some guards.  Enemies like robots, drones, and sentry guns don’t count, but using your weapon at any time has a good chance of attracting human opposition.  Additionally, at the end of each chapter you usually come to a boss where you can make the decision to kill them, turn them over to the police, or simply walk away.Disjunction relies heavily on stealth gameplay…until it doesn’t.  When you crouch you go into a silent/slower movement and vision cones appear for all the enemies including robots, cameras, and sentry guns.  As long as you stay out of the yellow zone you are free to sneak around and either avoid enemies or get up close and do a melee takedown.  Some enemies are tougher than others and might need 2-3 swipes.  If other guards are on a patrol route you might want to pick-up and hide the body.  It’s also worth noting there are environmental hazards like shock panels on the floor that you must run across rather than sneak, which of course means loud footsteps that could trigger guards.  One nice feature is the ability to pan the camera around your current view, allowing you to see enemies just off the edge of your screen.Disjunction took me back to the 80’s where all the games looked like this.  I really dug the cyberpunk vibe, atmospheric soundtrack, and dynamic gameplay across the three characters.  Yes, the game is repetitive if played for too long, but there is just enough story here (should you choose to read it all) that will keep you entertained until the end.Read full review at

_childDocuments_.review: Disjunction is a decent top down stealth game which is a very niche genre. There are three characters that you cycle through between missions to keep things a bit fresh. The story is OK, nothing special but not bad. The stealth is the best part of the game but it's not exactly much to write home about. The strange thing I find about the stealth that will ruin it for hardcore stealth fans is you can beat someone up directly behind an enemy but since they don't hear anything, they'll never turn around. You would think there's 0 sound recognition for the AI but there's not, they can hear you running behind them. I think the game would be too frustrating if attacking enemies would alert nearby guards though. Each character has a few abilities and they all feel useful. It's nice to change them up between levels to keep things fresh. There are several different enemy types but you'll learn after a while that the best way to approach any enemy is to stand around a corner they walk to and just spam melee attacks when they reach it. The game is just decent in my opinion but it's good enough if you're interested in top down stealth games. If you're not interested in top down stealth games, you should skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a few hours in and have just reached the third playable character. This game is easily worth the 15 bucks. The 2048 setting is really cool because it's in the future, but it's close enough to 2021 that elements from real life have an impact on the story. For instance, being familiar with NYC neighborhoods is rewarding because you can see what Brighton Beach has evolved into in this dystopian timeline. Even if you don't really care about story and learning more background, the gameplay is challenging without being frustrating. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever finished a game as quickly as I did this one. Not because it wasn't hard enough (be prepared to die a lot) or short, but because I was fully addicted to the game-play. It's super fun and dynamic. You can choose a particular play-style (which can be augmented by various upgrades you obtain), but depending on the situation and resources at hand, you can be forced to fully abandon your play-style and plans. And if you're as much of a fan of MGS (Metal Gear Solid) games as I am, then you will 100% love this game. The art-style is also amazing - it made me a much bigger fan of pixel-art than I already was. The story was intriguing, with some great NYC references, and fun/witty dialogue options that had a lot more impact on the development of the story than I anticipated. And last but not least, the soundtrack was the cherry on-top, helping to create and sustain the high-action, dystopian environment.Everything combined makes gives it high replay value, and I'm definitely one of those people who will play it all over again to make sure I didn't miss anything. This game is absolutely worth it, you won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of cyberpunk attitude, but not much to recommend it.No real choices, no apparent RPG mechanics. Even playing for stealth, mechanics are very twitch-oriented - and the field of view is so limited, and you have no real sniping ability, so as a stealth game it is a loss.Also some lame things like deciding whether to use controller by whether one is connected at startup, no choice in game.From the store page, I expected something much richer. This is very disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: A good sci-fi stealth game. The game play is simple and enjoyable, and the story is just kind of there to give you a reason to visit different locations, although I have to admit I skipped through a lot of the dialogue.The story just kind of throws you in and has a lot of names and locations that don't really mean anything, but I don't really think the story is the main focus of the game. Anyway, here's my experience and criticism of the game.Quick summary: The game play is simple, difficulty gets harder as you go. Characters have decent game play variety. The choices that change the endings are just that, choices that give you different endings. Story is something that just exists. You can kill everyone if you want, but take note that the game is built for stealth. If you're looking for a stealth game with cool pixel art, then I recommend Disjunction!For game play, as I said before it's very simple. You can run, crouch and see enemy vision cones, and use three abilities unique to three characters. There's a variety of enemies you can knock out, avoid, or kill as you progress through the game, difficulty increasing as you go. The game play heavily favors stealth, as killing everyone is limited to shooting your gun. Only two characters have abilities that are related to lethal aspect, Frank and Joe, although Frank's ability is a passive one. You can't knock out everyone and then shoot them while they're knocked out, you have to shoot them when they're still active to kill them. The gun aspect of the game is favored towards enemies, as they can shoot extremely fast and move fast when alerted and chasing you. You can die very quickly.The stealth aspect of the game is what I bought the game for, and I can say that it's a fun experience. However, it's essentially the entire game, which isn't necessarily a bad thing. My only criticism of stealth is that vision cones will constantly change how far they are depending on your location. For example, you might try and sneak through three enemies through a small area that has no vision cone, but suddenly the enemy vision cones expand and now you're spotted. It's really weird, I'm not sure why vision cones keep moving all the time. If there is a reason for that, I don't know what it is.For the User Interface, it's good, but there are two things I would like to see changed. First, the map size is a bit small. I have a large widescreen monitor, so the map would just be super small. The player dot that shows where you currently are is a single pixel, which doesn't help. I have to move towards my screen to see where I am. Another thing, PLEASE ADD A WARNING TO THE "RESTART LEVEL" BUTTON! I'm lucky it only happened once. Accidentally restarting a whole level when I wanted to go back to the checkpoint mega sux :'(The pixel art is great, it's another main reason why I bought the game. The visuals are very pretty. There's enough variety for levels to make things interesting. The train ride animation that plays every time you go to a new place is cool, but I think it shows up a little bit too frequently at the beginning of the game. I don't really care though, I always just stared at the lights moving across the train every time it happened lolNow for the characters. There are three. Frank, Joe, Spider. I feel like their abilities served purposes that were too similar. All three have a throwable. Frank's smoke bomb, Joe's grenade that deals non-lethal damage, and uhh whatever Spider had I forgot but I think it stunned enemies. Only Joe's throwable actually affects people from a distance, which I found the most useful. Frank and Spider's abilities either stunned or blocked/distracted enemies. Their abilities basically just made knocking out enemies easier, so they felt the most similar. My favorite character to play as was Joe because he looked cool and his abilities were the best (in my opinion). His knockout grenade was my most used ability in the game, I think. His charge ability was fun to use but I only used it occasionally. His combat stim I used the least.Spider's cloak and stun grenade were the only things I mainly used when playing as Spider, I didn't use the cute cat hologram one a lot.Frank's abilities are basic enough. You can heal yourself, shoot a stun bolt, and throw a smoke grenade. The last two abilities mainly helped me knock people out, same with Spider's abilities.The upgrades for each character are okay. The upgrade kits for character abilities are mainly just stuff like less cooldown or lasts longer, nothing really that will allow for unique play styles. The XP upgrades just do stuff like move faster, faster attack swings, faster reload, more health and all that. Again, nothing really noteworthy.The story and the different choices, I can't really say much about it. As said before, it's just there idk. It gives you replay value to get different endings I guess.For the levels, I think there needs to be more than just one save area per level in the later areas. The endgame areas are difficult and really big. Having to redo large chunks of a level every time I die or reset was frustrating. I get why the save areas exist, but it's just my personal want.Well that's all I want to say about the game. It was really fun. It's a fairly short game, my playtime was around 9-10 hours (mainly because I kept dying so much lol).Thank you for a cool game!
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a notification or heads up than a review (I really enjoyed the demo too)At the time of writing this (07 FEB 2021) The game runs at 44fpsThis is a known issue for those with high refresh rate monitors.The fix/solution offered at this stage is to manually set your monitor refresh rate to 60 fps - this allows the game to achieve 60 fps for smoother game play (I can't confirm this personally)I have not done this as it shouldn't be necessary and honestly, nobody in their right mind would do this for one specific game when they want to play it.99% of other games achieve their locked frame rates just fine by coding it into the software.It is a bug that is yet to be addressed and until it is patched I would recommend you avoid playing the game.By all means buy it, the demo was fantastic and I really want to support the developers, it's a shame that this has tainted my first attempt at the full version.I will change my review once this issue has been patched.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the good promise, story is heavily shoved on your face by walls of text, and stealth mechanics either conflict with gameplay or are questionable at best. If the complaints here don't bother you, you should grab it. Otherwise, steer clear. Also, PROPER GAMEPAD SUPPORT, THANKS!Despite offering a "good narrative with branching paths based on decisions", at front, all that meant was "you can either kill or knock people unconscious". Since Steam forces you to either like the game or refund in less than 2 hours, couldn't risk staying longer and trying the rest, since the initial experience was already pretty bland. Hope I'm wrong on this part, because there is barely anything interesting in "branching a narrative" by just making it "kill or not". There isn't even any reflex of this decision in particular on the characters themselves. Why not at least make the hard-boiled detective ask himself "have I gone soft?" for not killing anyone? Instead, you have a rich background story shoved on you through walls of text with orange snippets that have other walls of text on them. It's wall of text in a wall of text. It's a whole building of text.Then, the RPG-stealth gameplay. The "RPG" side means selecting a collection of upgrades that substantially change how the characters works. And since re-spec is free and done at any mission start, you can mix and match, and try new things at your hearts content. This was done quite well, but calling this "RPG", specially considering the lackluster "role-playing" side of it on the story is a bit of a stretch (but this last bit is nitpicking on a stupid industry that still tries to use the bad tool of "genres").The stealth part of the gameplay is interesting, until you start noticing how some mechanics don't agree between themselves. When getting near an enemy, if you're crouching, you can see their vision cone. The game doesn't tell you (less hand-holding, good design) is that when near a shadow, usually near walls or some objects, enemy view distance is about halved. This was a good base for a stealth framework, until you notice your view range is extremely short, even while aiming away (at least on controller). Another thing that compounds on this, is the fact that when on a shadow, you see the view distance reduced, but actual enemy view distance remains the same, to the point you can throw a concussion grenade on someone only to discover that there was a camera or someone else watching that person, and you had no way of knowing that they were in range (either because range was reduced because you were in shadows, or because it was too far away). In short, you either scout really well, or you get a nasty surprise. This slows down the gameplay a lot for stealth play, and since combat is twitch reflex on the level "1~2 seconds till you're dead", the pacifist option will over-extend the gameplay A LOT. Your choice is basically "do I suffer through this, or do I finish a level in a quarter of the time while thinning out the population a bit?".Straightening out the stealth side of things, game would be really good, if buildings of text doesn't heavily bothers you,
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game. Just know what to expect.The game is NOT a realistic stealth simulator. It has pretty simple game mechanics. But it does what it wants to do pretty well.Pros:* very classical Cyberpunk setting* nice Cyberpunk story* very good visuals and music* nice gameplay that kept me coming back for moreContra:* Can be sometimes frustrating* You have to learn core game mechanics by trial & errorOverall:Recommended, but not for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: This one i will give a thumbs up because i enjoyed the story and the characters, but be aware of some of the issues:-Gameplay is repetitive, basically grab a key, open the door and find the objective.-Save system consists on one link that you activate per floor, on later levels they can be far, and lead to frustration, since you have to repeat from the beggining of the floor if you fail.-I found the characters unbalaced, Joe (the cybernetic arm dude) is very strong, with some very powerful skill. Frank (the cybernetic eye guy), although not powerful as Joe, have some very cool skills and the only with a self healing ability. Now for the Spider (the hacker gal), i found her the most frustrating, she favors stealth, and has a health pool close to Frank, but without self healing, you have to play way more carefully.Putting the bad stuff  aside, i have to mention the nice graphics, and (once again) the story, which is pretty well done, with quite some lore put into it. I would not complain in seeing a sequel or prequel of some sort.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: Who needs AAA when indie games can be so good? A thumping soundtrack (and my new subwoofer) is all I need to get my wife crazy (not in a good sense), and this game delivers!With a visual style reminding me of the fantastic Crossing Souls, this game lets you sneak around facilities swarming with guards (humans and robots), going in silently and running away with the information you want without anyone ever noticing you were there. Ok, just joking. You MAY be able to play that way, but bloodthirsty guys like me just enter the building and kill everyone and everything they see. This works perfectly, even if the press later writes about a massacre and my friends are disgusted with my modus operandi. Well, the job has to be done and they could do it themselves, don't they?During the game you can play three characters, each with three very different abilities. A private investigator, a heavy-weight boxer and a sneaky assassin keep the gameplay varied, while you you uncover a conspiracy with multiple choice dialogues and quite a bit lore to read - between the missions. The characters can be upgraded with cybernetic enhancements, which mostly improve exisiting abilities.So, is this game a masterpiece? Well, it is damn good, but of course it is limited to entering a building and getting to your mission objectives. It is just what it says: A single-player, cyberpunk, stealth-action RPG set in a dystopian New York. You can play sneaky or as a killer. If you like that - it is a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic so far. Above all else, the game is responsive and fluid. Simple controls combine with complex environments and branching character specialization options to produce a playground for experimentation. Disjunction implements lethal vs non-lethal approaches to gameplay seen in other stealth-action titles, and executes this paradigm in as brilliant a fashion as any AAA title could muster. I find myself replaying sections of some levels not because I failed, but because I thought of another way I could approach something, and the game is just that fun to play around with.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: Disjunction is a great stealth game. The mechanics are well shifted towards this state. Enemies are hard hitting, fast reacting. Really your only option is to engage with the stealth mechanics regardless of your play style.One of my favorite things about the game is the music. It is reminiscent of blade runner and never ceases to bring gravitas to any of the missions or interludes.You get to play 3 different characters with very different play styles, sampling each of them but by the end you get to choose which one you want to use so no time is wasted on any of them.Finally the only thing that may detract people from this game is the saving system. You only get one and in the middle of the mission. You have to think carefully about when to use it. Do you use it after you've incapacitated the next room over? Do you use it when you have got the upgrade kit? Or do you simply use it immediately upon finding it. The choice is difficult and those first few times may be frustrating but i can say with confidence that you get used to it. The game does not hold your hand in this regard, when to use it is entirely up to you.Overall I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a good stealth game.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: Disjunction is a very good game. The developers have clearly poured their hearts and souls into it, and it shows in every pixel. Whether you prefer a stealthy approach or going in guns blazing, the game always offers a fun challenge to overcome. Each level feels like a meticulously crafted puzzle. When combined with each character's unique set of abilities, there's so many ways to achieve your objectives. If you're a fan of the cyberpunk genre, top-down stealth/action games, or just great storytelling in general, do yourself a favor and play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: Hello,Good game, but perhaps consider getting it on sale. I don't know the history of the developers, but this is at least the first game they released as this studio, and it definitely feels like it.  Its clearly aspiring to be like more ambitious titles like Hotline Miami or Deus Ex, but the gameplay is just too simple as it is. The three characters, while interesting as a glance, fall into the trap of ultimately being variations of the same theme, and a stealth playthrough (which is encouraged) feels more or less the same with each character. Small levels with one checkpoint and dumb AI that is mostly about focusing on avoiding vision cones can feel rote even just halfway through.EDIT: Having finished the game, I pretty much still agree with this review, but I also would like to note that by the end levels being to feel extremely samey in design.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: A pixel adventure with a criminal conspiracy involving three characters, dead beloved ones and control freaks that want to take over EVERYTHING. You have some grudge that must be settled and  it's up to you whether you are going to think your actions thoroughly or just shoot everyone that crosses your way. The story won't send gravitational waves throughout the universe, but I wouldn't call it bad either. The gameplay mechanics is pleasing. If you like sneaking around or combining sneaking with shooting, or just butchering down everyone, then you gonna love this little gem. A good 10 hours of going deep into enemy territory, snatch up things or liquidate unwanted individuals.The game itself uses a limited set of building blocks and some late game extras (extra perks and enemies) would've been welcomed, but they vary them in a good way and it kept me entertained, so if you are up for some good ol' pixel based sneaking around don't hesitate to pick up Disjunction.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: I hesitated recommending the game or not leaving any review. I liked : the atmosphere, the cityscape art and the soundtrack that I found very fitting and relaxing. The characters are simple but well written, and the story is nothing exceptional but works.I didn't really like :  the gameplay and the level design, pretty basic and not very challenging. Is it a cyberpunk Hotline Miami ? Or a stealth game ? It's hard to tell. A bit of both, but it feels it's failing at both. For me, it would be a 6/10 : I wouldn't say I didn't like overall, it deserves some credit for some elements, but far from a must-do.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: This was my favorite demo from Pax and it I've loved every hour I've play.  The focus is stealth but having some weapons at hand when necessary makes for excellent gameplay.  The enemy actions are clear and I never feel cheated.  I die a lot but the respawns are quick so I can learn from my mistakes and don't get too frustrated.The music is perfect for the game.  The tension it builds is just right, making me feel like my senses are heightened and I need to be ready for anything.I've made a few choices so far and I get the impression they meaningfully will affect the game later on, so I'm excited to to replay it and see were other paths go (though I'm not looking up any spoilers, so they paths might just converge).
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, some amazing pixelart alongside very good writing and story. I really enjoy the setting being a close-to cyberpunk-ish setting. That said, this game is hard. I'm mostly after the lore, and not the smartest/best at these types of gamer. The game kicks my ass regularly when I ♥♥♥♥ up some small thing and I keep quitting frustrated, but coming back every time. If you're easily frustrated, maybe think again. Otherwise, amazing game by a very good small studio.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: Disjunction offers a tight cyberpunk experience that doesn't outstay its welcome.At its core the game is all about stealth and using the three protagonists' various abilities to get through the levels. And the stealth mechanics and abilities are good, although the main gameplay loop does start to get a little repetitive towards the end.The soundtrack and sound effects are good and the pixelart is also very well done. However, the environments does lack a bit of variety and things start to blend together after a bit. You'll be seeing a lot of warehouses and offices, although there are a few more interesting areas sprinkled in as the game goes on.Disjunction's story will perhaps not blow any minds, but it's well written and feels just right for the cyberpunk genre with its noir atmosphere and themes of corporations taking power away from the people.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I'm leaving my positive review, but need to add a few caveats. Having played significantly more of the game - and in particular, all three characters on multiple missions - I now find myself more frustrated and dissatisfied with my experience than before.The biggest issue is that the third character - and later the second character too - break what I  consider a key aspect of a stealth game. When playing that character, you basically can't take people down without being detected, meaning you basically have to run through everyone in one shot, since you can't clear spaces to act as staging grounds as you go. The first character can do this, but for some reason they decided to design the other two characters to not allow this. It makes their missions a frustrating game of trial and error until you discover the one path you can just run through, being spotted by someone you could not have noticed because you can't stop to think, and having to do it all over and over and over again.If this game had been only missions as Frank, the first character, I'd have considered it an amazing 2D stealth game worth every moment. But with the other two, I would encourage much greater caution. Unless you don't care about being seen in a stealth game... but I trust that hardly needs to be elaborated.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: Disjunction is far from perfect; the environments tend to all feel "same-y," the checkpoint system can be frustrating (especially in the second half, when the encounters are more challenging), and the story doesn't quite deliver on the promise of its initial build-up. That said, Disjunction is a game I highly encourage fans of the stealth genre to give a try; the raw Metal Gear Solid-esque mechanics are absolutely solid, the level design accommodates for a variety of play-styles, the RPG spec-ing is a welcome twist to the main game loop, and the cyberpunk theming is outstanding. I may have a handful of criticisms to the final product, but I'd like to see more of these types of games made going forward, and I can't wait to see what this developer does next!
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game. At $15 this is a complete steal.The story and setting are incredibly made and pair amazingly with the awesome art. The setting is already amazing but the devs allow further immersion with expanded details that just add another level to the world building, without overwhelming you if you don't want to. As others have mentioned, the gameplay is tough but rewarding. It isn't frustratingly hard, but it makes you work for that victory. Different abilities for each character adds a twist on how you can tackle levels. Currently I'm taking a stealth approach but I look forward to going back through with a guns blazing style and seeing all the changes. Ultimately, the levels cut a good balance of difficulty that results in elation and self congratulation afterwards.  Overall this is an amazing game and everyone should check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: The theme and art-style are really good. A down and dirty cyberpunk feel, not neon and hypercars. It has smooth controls and I can make a holographic cat to distract people before i sneak up behind them and force them to get CTE scans in the morning.The gameplay is good and feels fair, whenever something goes wrong it's invariably my fault. You get to upgrade/mod your abilities and switch the mods so if you figure out what suits you best. You have different abilities on the different characters so they each have their own feel(Spider #1) as you avoid, concuss or murder your way through the levels and the story. The game gets more fun as you get better, you just see more opportunities/possibilities than you do when you first start and it's rewarding to pull them off. My first play through is very stealth-centric but I'm going to Hotline my way through enemies on my next one.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: Just really into it. It's fun, it's smart, it's artistically fulfilling. Easily worth the purchase.It is not easy (but not keyboard-smashingly-frustratingly-hard) but it really feels like I've accomplished something when I beat a level.The branching talents/upgrades system is fun and is balanced and responsive to which abilities i like to use the most.So pleasantly surprised by the music and art! The music is really really good and some of the levels are so pretty.Oh man, the level design is so good! Levels all have multiple paths and routes to where you want to get to, and often after I die I end up trying the other way to see if I can get it done.The story and setting are cute! The depiction is a dystopian New York City done better than most in the archetype, with real neighborhoods flavored with local knowledge and landmarks. The geopolitical cyberpunk situation is grounded in extrapolated-history, similar to Fallout but, with a better knowledge of geopolitics. Have really enjoyed the characters, dialogue and the branching story choices and have lost many minutes sitting at screens deliberating what I was going to choose to do w/ certain NPCs.I have really dug this game, and I'm not normally an indie gamer guy. Love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

_childDocuments_.review: Disjunction is a cyberpunk stealth-action RPG set in the dystopian underworld of a 2048 New York. Experience a reactive, intertwining story of three playable characters, working to uncover unfortunate truths that will change the fate of their city forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Disjunction

name: The Ascent
detailed_description: The Ascent is a solo and co-op Action-shooter RPG, set on Veles, a packed cyberpunk world. Welcome to The Ascent Group arcology, a corporate-run metropolis stretching high into the sky and filled with creatures from all over the galaxy. You play as a worker, enslaved by the company that owns you and everyone else in your district. One day, you are suddenly caught in a vortex of catastrophic events: The Ascent Group shuts down for unknown reasons and the survival of your district is threatened. You must take up arms and embark on a new mission to find out what started it all. You belong to the corporation. Can you survive without it? SOLO OR CO-OP Play the entire game alone or work together with up to three friends in local or online co-op. EXPLOSIVE SHOOTER Aim low or high, switch weapons and equip lethal gadgets, take cover and use the destructible environments at your advantage and keep adjusting your tactic as you face new enemies. RPG ELEMENTS Customize your character with cyberware that suits your playstyle. Allocate new skill points as you level-up and try various augmentations to take down your enemies in new creative ways. A VIBRANT CYBERPUNK WORLD Meet new allies and enemies and find loot as you explore the brimming world of The Ascent and its wide range of districts, from the deep slums to the higher luxury spheres.

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely has it's fair share of bugs, but so far I haven't encountered anything that I would consider game breaking, or a detriment to the experience. I'm playing a 2 player session with a friend currently and it's incredibly fun. There's loads of guns and lots to explore. The game is graphically beautiful! There's always a lot of really beautiful scenery, especially if you love this style of world design. The quests are a bit funky in the sense that we were doing a lvl 7 side quest and it took us to an area with lvl 22+ enemies, so that was fun. We've encountered quite a few bugs that required a restart on both of our ends, as well as minor bugs that didn't really bother us that much. While bugs can be frustrating, I've found that I'm really enjoying this game regardless. It's fast paced, exciting and wonderful with friends. TL;DR look out for the bugs, but honestly don't be afraid to pick this game up and give it a shot. Especially if you want to play with friends. Also 10/10 soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Finished it in a bit over 20h. Fun ride! Graphics are spectacular, simply breathtaking. The gameloop is fun and the shooting over cover + augmentations (like deploying a buddy robot to fight along you and robotic spiders and many more) makes it even more fun. If you like scifi and shooting the gotta play this. Bit of a mix between Doom, Cyberpunk and Blade Runner.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I love the environmental details they put into this game. Its beyond words. I can take a screenshot and stare at it for hours just looking at all the details in it, and how it tells a story of that segment of location. This game's graphics is beautiful. If you're into cyberpunk theme, you have to get this game. Just for the graphics alone...10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: A diablo-esque top down shoot-em-up, The Ascent is a fun little game, as the main quest takes no more than 10 hours to finish on Medium difficulty.The game's got polish, it's got style, it's also got good in-game mechanics as far as such games go. What is lacks is the meat, as options for different playstyles are not varied. Storyline is not something to write home about, but it serves it's purpose. Despite all these little criticism, I enjoyed the overall experience, specifically the fluidity of the combat mechanics, especially during the late game. Watch some gameplay footages or try out the "free demo" prior to purchasing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Its an outstanding game, an incredible and immersive experience. The gameplay is fun and action-packed, fast-paced, and varied. Outstanding game design, outstanding art design (some of the most incredible graphics I've ever seen). A lot of bugs. Missions that won't load in particular. Nothing more frustrating than being 6 hours into a game, only to realize I have a corrupted game file where a main mission just completely won't load and I'll have to start over. Beyond just that main mission - side quests that won't load, mission goals that are unclear or at least are not activated by compass...half the time I'm not sure if its a feature or a bug. If you can iron out the game-ruining bugs, I'm all in. Otherwise, I really don't recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: The RPG elements are shallow.....but the detailing is DEEP.Beautifully designed and detailed cyberpunk world that's a pleasure to explore. I find the twin-stick shooter controls a bit clunky and would have preferred a traditional ARPG control system, and more depth to RPG elements too, but aside from that, and a few bugs and inconsistencies (slowww fast travel, side quests given before you can access them), it's a really enjoyable game. Combat is simple but fun with a good meaty feel, and the world building is top notch, the details even have details on their details, and the whole effect is stylish and atmospheric. If you want cyberpunk vibes, give it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game actually sucks, I just have this thing where I get really aggravated by games so I continue playing them for some reason. This is one of those games where you really want to like it because it has beautiful graphics, its visually stunning, the environment and ambiance is set really nicely. What's not setup nicely is the actual gameplay is garbage tier quality, the amount of game-breaking bugs encountered is incredible for a fully released game, and the amount of frustration you will have trying to get over seemingly basic hurdles will be immense.If you enjoy becoming frustrated until you hate something, maybe this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the hour 1 impressions are awesome.  The music is phenomenal (Ghost in the Shell + John Carpenter).  The gameplay feels very Shadowrun + Diablo.  The world has heavy overtones in Necromunda (the table top version) + Blade Runner.  It looks like it is going to be a lot of fun.4 hour review: Best weapon combo I found so far has been grenade launcher and shotgun.  You can kind of use the minimap to aim the GL without the enemies being on screen or seeing you.  M+K is way easier to aim with than a controller.  You can change your appearance for free at any time if you don't like something.  The armor colors are not my preference, so ended up just rocking black with grey highlights.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, wonderful sound track.   It is a great mix of twin stick shooter and ARPG combat.  There are flaws and of course some launch bugs but over all it was well worth the money I paid for it.   As of writing this I am just under 30 hours total play time and have done all of the main story as well as all but 2 side quests, fully upgraded 2 weapons and hit level 30.   I highly recommend this game to any one interested in cyberpunk themed games, shooters, twin stick shooters or ARPG fans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Oh the stutters, it stutters, oh yes it does. Even after apparently loading up shaders at the start,  this game has frequent , sometimes random stutters when 1. ( entering new areas ) 2. Revisiting said areas) 3. (Just random i`ll stutter when i feel like it) The game is clearly loading shaders, assetts, textures , or whatever the hell its doing in real-time not efficiently at all causing the stutter in both dx11 & 12. The devs have acknowledged it but until its fixed i just can`t recommend it at this point. Its a beautiful looking game, the setting, the weapons , the music , its all great but the stutter.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Collected balls as my first side mission whist committing genocide on the innocent population. In all seriousness this game is godly with raytracing (except ambient occlusion is spelt wrong in the menu, and i cant change the RT settings) and is just absolute eye candy. Props to the modeller/texturer. Map is a little confusing, need to be able to set custom waypoints that the scanner tracks to. Voice acting is excellent too. Camera is a bit weird in some areas, but mostly fine. Audio was a bit funky, i needed to change the preset as it was really quiet, and some guns dont sound punchy enough.I give it a final score of the amount of innocent civilians i murdered over the amount of times i sold the exact same gun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are insane for a top down game, crazy amount of details !And the levels are vast !High quality in game cutscenes with voice acting.Interesting story and universe.Coop is a great addition, although quite buggy.Gameplay is sometimes dull, but becomes good when you find a fitting loadout, enemy swarms, boss battles with music ramping up.Lots of walking, lots of back and forth, even when using fast travel. Background music got repetitive really fast.All this for half the price of a AAA game is stunning !
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: A fun twinstick shooter with rpg elements!I recommand the game and here's my thoughs:+Cyberpunk universe well build and world is good+Satisfying gunplay and related features like the cover system+Good RPG elements to customize your playstyle+Good amount of exploration-Game would need some polish (enemies might spawn in front of you, missing sounds in dialogues...)-It would have been to rotate the camera-You can be stuck in the environment and it can be frustrating-Fight on stairs is janky+- Story is ok+- characters are forgattable+- Can be repetitive on long terme depending on what you like+- Progression loop force you to do side missions to continue the story+- Map and navigation are average and can be misleading sometimesOverall a good first game for an indie studio.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: How in the ♥♥♥♥ in this day and age do you release a game that is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ buggy! Seriously why did I pay money for a game that crashes and bugs out all the time when I try and play with my buddy? There should be a lemon law for games like this because we should not have to pay and deal with a broken product. The game is fun when it works and I would actually like to keep playing it but in this state there is no reason to keep trying till it is fixed "or if it ever gets fixed."DO NOT PURCHASE THIS GAME UNTIL IT IS FIXED!! YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED BY PLENTY OF REVIEWS SO BUYERS BEWARE!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I am loving this game. The graphics and the world are amazing. The back ground, from the crowds to the scenery immerse you in the world. The combat runs smooth, the skills, tech, armour and weapons all play  part in your combat style. The game doesn't hold your hand and lets you explore until you find your self in way over your head. This has an amazing potential to expand its world, maybe in becoming your own corporation boss / crime lord or what ever in the future. I hope they expand this and not let it be a one off. _childDocuments_.review: The quality of story, art and voice acting are all really spot on. There are made up words that don't make me cringe! (well, the words in English, the in game language is an abomination as spoken by the side NPCs) The world makes a semblance of sense! These are all sci-fi musts that make the game story and world feel alive.It feels very polished for a 12 person team from a presentation standpoint save from a few graphic glitches mostly related to traffic that flys around on screen.The game itself has good level design and exciting gunplay, however...The skill based aspect of the shooter is poor, as is the RPG mechanics. Let me explain:The game has 2 augments slots that act as more frequent usable abilities. These abilities thus far have really fallen flat in terms of impact and enjoyment. There is a drone that gathers equipment... terribly. There is a punch that punches real hard... some other stuff that I simply don't care about? Its all pretty lackluster... Their best feature is often the special effect.Then there is a tactical ability. This ability takes time to charge up. This time can be reduced with a stat, and at this point the stat feels mandatory. Because they take forever to recharge. Absolutely forever. The abilities are again incredibly boring and just don't fit with the pace and flow of combat. The only one I used extensively was to finish a side quest that was incredibly uninspired (kill 10 guys with your tactical ability!).Speaking of stats, they seem pretty pointless as well. They don't feel well laid out in terms of why they are there, they just feel like "well we need a health stat so here she is!". Upping my accuracy and crit certainly impacted my gameplay. I'll work on my tactical charge next so I maybe use my tactical ability? Honestly I don't even pay attention to leveling up... Not a good sign for a RPG system.Equipment and stats are honestly pretty confusing. Lots of different seemingly pointless sets of armor with no rollover information on what icons or symbols mean. I am not sure why it's so different either. I don't see it doing anything better. Information is still cluttered and menus still get overused. The map is fine after a while but honestly very poor at communicating information. Not like triple A games don't screw up here either, so I can't really hit them for inventory management and a poor map. I don't mind wandering the world anyway.Hacking was... an afterthought. 5 hours in and all it has been is another key to press periodically and some blockers I have no clue how to mitigate. Just leave it out or do something interesting with it. I don't need you to include it just so you can say "deck" a few times for nostalgia's sake.Last complaint? I've crashed 2x to desktop. Thankfully the auto save appears competent.The game is good and I enjoy playing it, but there was definitely some design decision that could have gone differently. Trying to be fair here as I know (as has been re-iterated perhaps too much) that it's a 12 person team, but I think the criticism was the individuals implementing skills and stats (the RPG system) didn't know what they were doing. They're far too obtuse and take no risks as if there is a balance fear which shouldn't be there. Make it fun first then balance it. You can have obtuse mechanics, but let me play with them and have them produce something. The system you have in place is illegible from a gameplay perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: Cliché cyberpunk in Shadowrun style for a fair price - but what a feast for the eyes. The environments, enhanced by ray tracing, are incredibly impressive, especially when you consider the size of the developers' team. A world full of neon, full of dirt, full of violence. Various automatic perspective changes and many small details lighten up the whole thing as you move through the world.On the hardware side, don't be fooled by the isometric view - a Ryzen 3700x and an RTX3080 have a lot to do with activated ray tracing (at 1440p), even with DLSS (Quality) there are no high frame rates.In terms of gameplay, it's a solid twinstick shooter (of which there aren't many left).From my point of view, there is only one real point to criticise: the side quests and the orientation in the world are in extreme need of improvement. You are bombarded with side quests early on, but can't do them because the regions they are in are only unlocked by later main quests. Very frustrating. Also the general orientation in the game world - the map is a joke. Unfortunately, the side quests lose a lot of their value because you think "do the main missions first, the side quest is in a locked area anyway". At some point you don't think about them any more and when you do remember them again, you are hopelessly overlevelled, so they are far too easy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really was a nice surprise -- I hadn't heard of it at all until I watched ShillUp's review on it. The fact that it is half off the normal price of a game is also a big deal.The lore, worldbuilding, level design, and graphics are absolutely A+, and personally are worth the price of admission alone. How a team of 12 members managed to create a game this dense and full of life, creating a truly astounding atmospheric experience, is beyond me. This is especially pronounced as you ascend past the first tier and into the city, and I spent a considerable amount of time just appreciating the design (although this effect weakens over time).The gameplay loop is solid, with some simple cover mechanics that enable some complexity. A good variety of weapons as well, with a basic but welcome upgrade system. There are also a ton of abilities (augmentations) that extensively impact how you approach some of the tougher battles. A basic skill point system that affects the power of your augmentations is also present, and combines with the above to create a much deeper experience than your typical twin stick shooter. Character customization is also well done, with a bevy of armor pieces to choose from.The main story is also very solid, with decent voice acting. A lot of funny lines and moments, without too much forced exposition. Some side missions are quite good, but most of them fell kind of flat. I do wish there was a bit more content, however. The ending of the game is a fizzle compared to the spectacular opening The Ascent has.Throughout the game, the loop does begin to feel a little repetitive, especially if you're not constantly experimenting with different loadouts. I didn't find navigation as difficult as some others, but it is still generally a pain compared to some other games also set in dense urban locales with multiple levels. Co-op also has a few bugs that are certainly annoying, but I did not run into many personally. Chasing down certain chests is also very annoying.To top it off, this game's soundtrack is top tier, which combines with the visuals and design to create that amazing cyberpunk atmosphere we all wanted 2077 to have. I really hope some DLC comes out down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: I can definitely say I love this game, but there's also definitely work that needs to be done.  The game is quite buggy as of this review.  There's certainly patch work needed.  I've not seen anything game breaking myself, but here are a few of the issues I have with the game currently:1.  Cosmetic items found in game don't seem to stay in the inventory after quitting the game, the next time you load up, it's all gone.  The currently worn item remains active, so if you find something you like, use it.  but if you take it off after quitting, it's gone until you find it again.2.  The Objective tracker and the Map/waypoints can get a little glitchy, sometimes directing you around in circles, to a seemingly empty area or even to inaccessible areas.  I understand that areas are locked behind progression, but locking the side mission out until you progress to a point in the story where you have access to the required areas, or even just a little heads up on the mission indicating it is not yet completable would solve this. (On a side note, the map is unnecessarily complicated and difficult to read clearly.  I never quite know exactly where I am in reference to where or what I’m trying to get to)3.  DX12 performance is still not where it should be.  The game does seem to settle down after a few minutes to a playable level, but every time it loads a new area (or you load the game up the first time) performance is poor with lots of lurching and jumping for 30-60 seconds (admittedly this could be me running setting too high, but an RTX 3060 should be able to tackle this at 1080P max settings with DLSS set to Performance).  I just love how good it looks with everything at max though, so I'm personally willing to take the hit for the first 60 seconds of loading a new area, then settle for a mostly stable 40-60fps.4.  I’ve not been able to get an online co-op session working.  Granted I’ve only attempted this with one friend, but every time we would try to load into a game together, we would get a “Disconnected” error.  We could join a lobby together, but no matter who hosted or if we used new or existing characters, as soon we tried loading to the game, it would disconnect the client from the host. (Both using the steam version, checked and double-checked versions were the same and followed multiple troubleshooting options to no avail)5.  This one is a minor QOL issue, but when finding chests that you can’t currently open due to insufficient “I.C.E.” level, a permanent indicator on the map as to the “I.C.E.” level required should then appear.  This would make keeping track of chests as you progress through the game much easier and avoid a ton of unnecessary backtracking.I know I’ve had a few more little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and issues, but they are obviously not noteworthy as I can’t remember any specifics.Even with these issues though.  I must say I have thoroughly enjoyed the game so far.  The way the game feels to play is excellent, with plenty of variety in the guns and playstyles.  The cover system is a welcome addition and adds a lot to the tactics and gunplay.  Controls are simple and both Keyboard/Mouse and Gamepad work well.I like that each location in the world has a fixed enemy level (and doesn’t just level up globally with the player as many games do these days), with select areas that are too high a level to fight through initially, where enemies will 1 shot you, soft-locking you out until you are more powerful (or just brute force through with multiple deaths and some lucky dodging).The world aesthetic is full of detail and character and beautifully rendered with top notch lighting, textures and sounds that I often find myself just taking a minute to soak in and appreciate before moving on.The story isn’t amazing (so far at least), but it hits enough beats to service the gameplay and keep you playing.  The side missions are also decent enough, some more interesting than others, but none that have felt tedious or boring (yet), offering worthwhile rewards for the most part.Levelling and character progression have also been great so far with lots of variety and options in how to build your character, getting noticeably stronger as you level up and find new gear.  The gear system allows for additional bolstering of skills and abilities to better match your playstyle and build, beyond just “getting stronger” as you find higher level gear and augmentations.  I tend to keep a selection of gear options available to switch between depending on the situation and whether I wish to boost defences against damage types or boost certain skills and augmentations more.With everything said, and for all its current flaws, it’s still a great game and well worth playing.  If you plan on mainly playing online co-op, I will say hold off for a bit and wait for the fixes to come for that side of the game. If you want to put on some headphones and get lost in a beautifully rendered Cyberpunk Asymmetric Shooter, this is definitely the game for you.

For me, every time I entered a new area and rolled, shot, killed an enemy, or killed a civilian my game would have a major frame drop for about 5 seconds. I'm not sure if this was something that I was doing wrong, but I felt like sometimes side quests were given too early. I say this not because they were too hard, but the ones that it seemed you could do were sometimes in zones that were straight up not unlocked for me, quick example was delivering the bag to the guy in corpZone but the building he was in was just not unlocked for me.Energy damage type needs to be nerfed, it felt like this damage type was either the most effective or close to effective for nearly every mob I went up against. There does not feel like enough to customize my character. In addition to components, I think there should be an attachment system to the guns that could alter some of the stats that stay constant when using components to upgrade weapons. Some pretty basic examples could be an attachment that increases clip size but also increases the weapons weight making you slower while wielding it, or an attachment that increases knock back but could reduce clip size. I would have also liked if getting one of your skills up to max rank felt more like a reward that gave you something new. Maybe, There could be an aug slot or module slot that are specifically reserved for 20/20 skills. Some examples of this could be if you 20/20 Evasion you would get a new module that gave you a third dash. Or if you 20/20 Balance you get a skill that allowed you to break through walls and cover, that would be pretty funny. NG+ system would be cool idkMore updates, more weapons, more areas, more bananas augments i would loveAnyway I liked it cool

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game - the lore and the story are great - it's the kind of sci-fi/cyberpunk story that has a very Asimov feel because they are not holding your hand or explaining everything - which from a story in a video game is pretty refreshing.  We all used to some long-winded blowhard character telling what everything means (one-word: Claptrap) - this does not do that and it adds to the immersive feel of the game right away. I've played a lot of top-down isometric action RPGs - but my experience with shooters in that format is limited, so this had a pretty steep learning curve for me.  At first, I was convinced that the combat was just chaotic and too difficult - but eventually I figured out the mechanics and stopped getting my ass handed to me by enemies that seemed to be coming from everywhere at once.  If you are like me - keep at it and be methodical until you get the hang of it. By the end I felt like a bad-ass mowing fools down in waves. The fact that this game came from 12 developers is impressive as ♥♥♥♥.  It looks and plays like a game that would end with a 10 minute credit sequence, but this was the effort of a handful of people. Well done you crazy genius ♥♥♥♥♥.
