_childDocuments_.review: An isometric top/down Action RPG Cyberpunk Shooter that does a fantastic job with atmosphere, gameplay, and overall pacing. I do really enjoy this game, but there are a few flaws I'll get out of the way:The Bad (kinda)1) Difficulty spikes. You'll be cruising thru the game thinking you've already mastered it's mechanics and then you'll run into a swarm of enemies and/or a boss and your whole world is wrecked. Especially early in the game when you're still trying to figure everything out, and you don't have all the best gear you'll be left struggling trying to make what you have work while trying to understand everything else. It can be frustrating. The silver lining here is these moments are supposed to make you understand what all of the other weapons and gear and armor actually do and when you're supposed to use them. So you're not left just running thru the game sporting the same armor and weapons all the time. Certain aspects of the game will force your hand into learning these things.2) Story. So this is subjective, but I found the story here to be pretty bad. The whole premise is that you were supposed to be an indentured servant to a corporation only to find out they go belly under once you arrive, and now you're left trying to find out what happened all the while trying to survive while you end up working for a different company. That isn't very compelling to me. The most interesting character is a side character you don't see very much who helps you hack systems. He's pretty much the only character with personality. Everyone else seems to act very one dimensional and doesn't show much at all in the form of much personality. Perhaps the developers were going for a bleak view of this world, and so most people end up being rather stoic and jaded to the world around them? I just wish there was more personality, more motivation to do things you're doing, and better reasoning for just everything around you happening. The game turns into a series of simple quests strung together. If you're looking for compelling narrative here you won't find it. Fortunately, skipping dialogue and cutscenes can be done easily. So if you're just playing the game for loot and gameplay aspect you can do that.3)  Progression. So this is a bad and a good thing depending on how you look at it. Skill trees are really simple. There really isn't a whole lot of customization here. You're just upgrading certain skills like aiming, various biotics, critical hit rate and so forth consistently. For a new player this will be great at first while you're learning the game. However, progression is a bit slow and you don't exactly fly thru the XP like you would in say a Diablo III for example. I'm only in the mid 20s of XP and I've been playing for 26 hours as of writing this review. Enemies you encounter are all over the place in levels, and this gets exacerbated the further along you play. I've run into enemies that were a level 4 while I'm sitting pretty in the 20s and then just a minute or two later will run into a level 13 enemy, and then a few minutes later I'll be swarmed by enemies that are just slightly one level above me. This can be annoying and frustrating trying to get thru the game.The good:1) Atmosphere is amazing. The cyberpunk feel is nailed here. It really feels like an extension of the movie Blade Runner for example.2) Graphics are great. From time to time things will glitch out. I've had a weird mesh thing happen with transparent effects every now and then. Could be my video card I suppose, and NPCs and/or enemies will float in weird spaces from time to time. However, these are far and few between.3) Gameplay is where this game will hook you. It definitely has that "just one more mission" feel to it. Even though the story is garbage, it is the addictive nature of the looting and gunplay that keeps you coming back for more. I would recommend playing with a controller though. I use a wired Xbox One controller to play this game. I've tried with Keyboard and Mouse and while you would think this style of game would suit that, there are fine aspects to the game here that lend itself better to the analog control sticks and triggers that a keyboard and mouse cannot do. However, switching weapons and special abilities is done with ease. There will be instances here where you'll have to go into your inventory and completely switch stuff out due to a situation you might find yourself in. However, doing this doesn't punish you and allows you to go in and change things without worrying about being killed unlike how some games get cute with having inventory screens up and enemies can still kill you while doing so. I don't know I suppose some players actually like that. That doesn't happen here and I really like that. Unlike the BS that happens in a game like Dark Souls or Diablo when switching inventory. So for me this is a positive. If you like your game not having enemies attack you while picking thru your inventory then this will be great for you.Overall this is a solid experience. I originally played this when I had Xbox Game Pass. Then I picked it up later on a sale for around $10. I suppose I might be annoyed had I paid more for it. So you get great value for your money here. The Ascent has a way of keeping you engaged with its fun looting and gunplay with many of its missions. Even though they can be repetitive, it's a fun sort of repetitive way as well. There's also the ability to have friends join in with you for co-op which is a nice touch if you're looking for a multiplayer aspect. If you're a fan of sci-fi, top/down shooters and/or Action RPGs with the emphasis more on the action than the RPG element there's a good game to be had here.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game. gameplay is fast but not overwhelming, fights can be hard but you can try different approaches (or grind a couple of levels). Plot is quite good, I hope they do a sequel.The character stats system is interesting. Each level gives 3 point to invest in 8 "skill". Each skill gives some passive bonus and increment by 1 one of the 4 base attributes. Those attributes affect the abilities (wich are equips, so can switched) in various way, explained in the ability's description.You have another equipment, the tactical ability. This is a powerful ability wich use tactical charge, gained on the field and by dealing damage to enemies (if you put some points in the right skill).Weapons are decently enough, and there are 4 kind of damage wich basically is: ballistic for umanoids, energy for robots, flame for dot (robots resists) and Cyber which is not very clear to me (one class of enemy will try to hacker you doing such damage I think).In the end is a very nice esponent of this genre, and the cyberpunk atmosphere is very engaging. If you give it a try, note that for the first hour you wont get many ability, but the game opens up after the "welcome quests"Some cons: 1) Sometimes the lightning is too much, making hard to even spot the enemies. The camera isn't very far, making snipers a bit meaningless.2) While the AI is challenging, the civilian are pretty dumb, often running at you during firefights. Could be a nice idea to make them at least run at low profile (so you don't kill them while aiming).3) The skills system is nice, but I think it kills replayability. There isn't a cap, and most abilities are very effective even with not many point in the relative skill. Maybe each attribute could affect each ability in different way? For example "motorics" could affect all melee damage, so if any skill deals that kind of damage would be buffed by it, and maybe Cybernetics could effect ability duration, if applicable. I think this would make different builds enjoyable and more deep.4) Weapons are cool, but they lack something.. maybe upgrades? (something like mass effect 3 for example could be cool)Thanks for reading this wall text, hope this helps you decide, but my suggestion is to try it, is definitely a very good game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: A few bugs and what not, but the game is great for a small company. Took us forever to figure out press "T" to call a taxi, it's just not mentioned anywhere in the game that "Hey, you can take a taxi now." The bounty system is odd, any bounty is 1000 credits, and a taxi is 1000 credits, so a taxi ride is the same as a murder....I don't know what I'm supposed to do with my money, I have a millions credits and nothing to spend it on. All that is insignificant compared to the game play and story, both are truly great. My group is enjoying the game very mucho!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous game, really impressed with the level of detail and the artwork. Game play is satisfying, I admittedly pretty much ignore the cover mechanic for the most part because I'm too impatient. I've definitely held back when there are a lot of innocent civilians around to avoid killing them - this usually leads to my death. This is probably incredibly lame, but I'd like an option to turn on a friendly fire mode because I am a baby and feel bad about accidentally killing all these virtual NPCs, haha. But the more I think about it, this is probably a stupid idea as it adds a fun layer of difficulty to the game.One time I stupidly spent all my materials upgrading the wrong gun; the game auto-saved so I was stuck with a garbage weapon, so yeah, don't do that. Overall, great fun, addictive game play, 10/10 artwork and graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Unplayable in its current state, at least if you're playing co-op with a friend. My friend keeps dropping through the floor, his minimap doesn't show half of the markers that i'm seeing (if it works at all), and he didn't get a gun that I got, even though we're supposed to share all the loot that we get???? I can't say anything about the single player experience, but definitely let this one cook a bit before you get it, because its stability is questionable. AS A SIDE NOTE, THIS IS ONE OF THE, IF NOT THE MOST GORGEOUS CYBERPUNK/POST CAPITALIST NIGHTMARE SETTINGS I'VE EVER SEEN. 11/10 ART DESIGN, MUSIC DESIGN, UI, ETC, AND THE GAMEPLAY DOES FEEL VERY SMOOTH AND RESPONSIVE IF IT WORKS. But the bugs make it absolutely unplayable, at least in co-op. If you're gonna grind this out on your own, probably give it a shot, but also, with all the games out there, it doesn't hurt picking something else up, and waiting for this to go on sale somewhere down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, story was significantly more interesting than I went in expecting.Combat can be a bit slow but once you get geared up and some good mods you can really pick up the pace.Game has an interesting weapon system were there are just a handful of weapons in the game (~20) but they can be upgraded to higher tiers to stay relevant as you progress in the game. Some weapons obviously just have better base stats but you can more or less use anything you want from early game in the end game if you upgrade it. 100% worth the buy if you get it on sale; I can't recommend this at full price as game is a tad short at around 12 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I would pick this game up if it is on sale. My friend and I had a blast playing through the story co-op but we encountered countless tiny bugs. All of the bugs that we encountered required a restart but would be fixed each time. I've read that many people have had save files corrupted and while we didn't encounter that it was a fear throughout our playthrough. Overall the game has a great atmosphere and level design, the combat is fun, and the story is decent, but the bugs severely limit how much I can recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, the game is pretty. The graphics would be fine for an ego shooter. The scenery is nice looking, the streets look busy and grimey. The Cyberpunk look is there.This is where the good aspects end. I was stupid enough to ignore all the negative reviews and thought: this can't be that bad, huh?It is very grindy, very boring. Minutes of walking through the same old empty areas. No running function. Shooting is boring and uninspired, cover meaningless. Weapon and character upgrades are handled very poorly and uninspired. The map is confusing and not very helpfull. The whole game doesn't feel like a game, but like work. Like an endless slogging chore. It reminds me of the cheap Diablo 1 clones that appeared out of east asia after Diablo 1 was a hit. Or early free to play online games. If you want something similar that is not as pretty, but actually good, play Alien Shooter, Redeemer or Ruiner
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, someone described it as diablo/scifi type of game and I think that it kinda fits. Here are some bugs that forces you to exit and re-launch the game and you might get stuck in some parts, but nothing game-braking. I did got stuck in one mission and needed to re-do it for 2nd time, but no big deal...
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: At first it looked very promising but soon it unveiled all the flaws. Gameplay and early monsters reminded me of childhood game called alien shooter. Map is huge and makes you think there might be a lot of stuff to do... well you couldn't be more wrong, Gameplay and story is so basic that it makes you wonder why they bothered with creating rich environments and not putting anything to do there, whole gameplay is based on walking from point A to B thorugh huge ghosttowns and killing some bad guys occasionallyNow a little about UI:Map is completely useless in those multilevel towns, it's impossible to tell where you're supposed to go down/upstairs. Selling is a chore also as confirmation window has yes button on right and enter clicks no. Camera is like separated living thing inside this game and focuses on showcasing environment rather than making it usefull for player, the angles in some places are terrible.Overall it feels like they wanted to create something akin to fallout 2 but failed miserably. This game had so much potential but seems like they created the world and had no idea how to utilize it at all
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Goot Game. Looks great, very fun to play. It does crash occasionally, I am not sure if that is because my computer is not meant for playing games, or if it is a bug in the game. Also sometimes the game glitches out and you can't interact with stuff, but that has only happened 1 time in 8 hours of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Ruiner and Hard Reset? Well, if you do, this might appeal to you.The beautiful isometric/top-down style meets the dystopian desolate and grungy world you might've seen in Hard Reset.The world plus the music really sends you some dark vibes that can really make you feel stuff. The story is nothing too extraordinary, it's your average corpo stuff with some extra to make it a bit spicier. Without getting into too many details, i will say the story is a 6/10. Not bad but not too unique or special.The gameplay has a good range of elements, you get your average cyberpunk shooter that you expect, with some minor RPG elements to keep things interesting, you build your loadout with different abilities and weapons, all you need to do is find out what works best for you and build your strategy accordingly.I would also suggest you to try the Photo Mode, even if you are not into taking screenshots, but just to explore and take a look at details. The developers did put a lot of effort into a world that 99% of the people would only see only from above, and that's very admirable.The game does have some glitches and bugs, and i will list them at the bottom of this review.All-in-all, great game, very atmospheric and dark, with some nice humor here and there. I can't wait to play the sequel if there will be one.What i would want from a sequel? I really would love to have melee weapons too, maybe more character customization, and definitely a better health/regen system. But for now, the game it's as good as it can be.If you read all of this so far, i will reward you with a fun fact: The game takes places on a planet called Veles, in Slavic mythology, Veles (Volos) was a powerful deity. One particular logo from the game slightly resembles the symbol of Veles.Some bugs i found:• The game rebinded my actual keyboard keys, so if i alt-tabbed, my WASD were replaced by the arrow keys and viceversa. The problem persisted even after i closed the game. Unplugging the keyboard didn't fix it, but a PC restart did.• Sometimes some particular controls just stop working, but if you switch to keyboard from gamepad, or if you were on a gamepad already and switched to a keyboard, you can continue playing. On my gamepad at some point i just couldn't shoot anymore, but i could move and everythingOn my keyboard, movement keys stopped working but i could shootThese were on separate occasions• Side quests got bugged and i couldn't finish them as there wasn't an objective anymore. Similar to CP2077's sidequests (insert PTSD flashbacks)• In one mission, i forgot its name, there was a Mech boss supposed to spawn, but if you died, it didn't spawn anymore so you had to restart the game to progres furtherI put these here because the devs might check the reviews, and they seem to still actively work on the game. By the time you read the review, these might be fixed. I don't think they occur to everyone, though.As a closing note, i would like to pay respects to the families of those poor alien civilians that got killed in my crossfires on Veles, but also to those that i shot for my sick twisted sense of fun: F
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: So yeah, not gonna lie...was bored with all my other games and this one popped up on sale.  Well Holy hell, I was incredibly surprised, Great game. Was concerned the overhead would bother me, but it actually added to the game. The story is basic, like your favorite cheesy B+ sci-fi movie. Would be nice if you actually had control of camera angles though. But otherwise solid game and enjoyable, short and to the point. If you do buy it and you feel like you are missing things and looking for more but can't find it, don't worry it's not there.  while enjoyable this game doesn't have a lot to it, just beautiful scenery and very well done sound, Kudos to the sound team. hopefully they'll add more content. But for less than $20 for the whole package you're not gonna lose. This was a wonderful find.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: + Game is very beautiful, both in terms of graphics (played on max settings, 1920x1080p without RTS and DLXX) and visual design. This is one of the best looking if not the best looking Cyberpunk worlds I've ever seen. The level of detail is simply amazing and visuals were probably the only thing that kept me going till the end.+ Music is good. Not always, unfortunately, but in "special" story fights (boss battles or "defend the point" battles) music was really good.+ Surprisingly rich amount of lore. Although, to be precise, I'm talking mostly about quantity. Can't really say anything about quality, because I wasn't really interested in reading tons of text explaining different corporations, races, etc. Still, it's definitely a good thing that all this exists in the game.+ The core gameplay is simple, yet satisfying.- The story is boring. And that's the kindest word I can use to describe it. First of all, your characters doesn't have any... well, character. They're (you can play either as male or female, not that it matters) not voiced, they don't say anything during dialogues, just listen to briefings (most of which are just "go there and kill everyone") and maybe sometimes you can ask some questions, again, not that it matters. Second, the characters you interact with, are also very boring. Over the course of the game I didn't care about any of them, they're just dummies made to advance the story.- The difficulty (curve?) is horrible. There are basically two types of battles in game: you either steamroll everyone on your path or getting gang-raped by an army of undying enemies. And the second type becomes more and more often towards the end of the game. Also, there is no auto-level, which is partly the reason of this problem.- The AI of enemies is "unfair". Usually, developers, in their games, try to not stoop so low to make enemies overly aggressive: you usually fight against several enemies simultaneously and, if they will fight at their max strength and full aggression, they will just decimate you, because you're all alone and there is not much you can do. Unfortunately, that's exactly the case with The Ascent. Enemies use covers very rarely and just constantly push you which is a problem because you get quickly overwhelmed. Maybe it's easier in co-op, but, in that case, it's still a problem, because there are people who can play in single mode only.- Enemies have too much health, even on normal, sometimes it's getting so ridiculous that you just sit for half of a minute shooting one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ turret. And that's just normal difficulty and I was using Mk10 energy weapon (max level of upgrade)! Also, developers decided to use the worst possible way of making the game harder (both on harder difficulties and over the course of the game) - enemies just do more damage and have more health. That's just lazy and, again, unfair because your health is capped at 20 skillpoints that you can use to increase it.- Many weapons are useless or, to be precise, not worth the effort, at least in single mode. Shotguns? LoL, good luck trying to use them effectively when enemies run around like crazy and you die in several seconds without cover, plus their clips are very small meaning you'll have to reload very often. Sniper rifles? Again, enemies move much faster than they should so good luck trying to hit them, and even when you do the damage is not that great. Machine guns? Even on maxed accuracy, you get horrible spread if you'll hold LMB for more than 2 seconds.- Same can be said about augments and passives. 80% of them are garbage. More money? Drone that picks up loot? Are you serious?- Stairs work horribly, you can't shoot enemies who stand on lower levels, while, in reality, you should have an advantage over them, or, at least, be able to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hit them.- Ridiculous amounts of walking. Yes, there is fast travel (even two of them - taxi and train), but it's still not enough - most of my game time I was just running from A to B, usually doing some side quest. Also, the game world is divided into 4 "floors" and you can't fast travel between them, the only way to travel from one to another - is through one specific elevator and it's horribly inconvenient.- Turrets and spiders. Both are OP and are disbalanced crap that should be either nerfed or cut out. If you have turrets on your side - the battle will be ridiculously easy, because enemies can't do ♥♥♥♥ to them. If you're fighting against them - get ready to sit behind the cover (or run constantly run around if you're fighting a mortar) for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of time while shooting them. Spiders are just plain BS, they're basically kamikazes and do a lot of damage which wouldn't be a problem if: 1) They didn't have so much health (for a suicider type of enemy). 2) They didn't spawn behind you, in area that you just recently cleared. 3) They couldn't jump on you before blowing up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Descent third person isometric shooter.  Love the Bladerunner feel.  Not a deep RPG game but entertaining for the price.  The soundtrack makes this games atmosphere.  The dialogue is very well done and quite entertaining, some LOL moments.  Easier to kill innocent civilians than take unwanted damage.  Wish I had known about the T for taking the taxi at the start.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: The game world and graphics are top notch, music is atmospheric and fitting.This is often referred to as a twin stick diablo-like game, this is more in the sense it is a dynamic isometric game with RPG elements. You will get random look, you have skill points to invest across talents and attributes (they are all stacked together) and you have augments which give you abilities to cater to your play style.I have about 9hrs of game time and that was done across 2 sessions, needless to say, it's really fun and I am enjoying the world.In relation to graphics, playing on DX12 Ultra is non-issue, issues people refer to in relation to performance are with DX12. I run a 5600x and 3060ti, the game in DX12 with ray tracing and DLSS looks amazing, but does have a few stutters, something that just needs patching/optimizing. DX11 ultra runs smooth on this system and my other system running a 3600 and vega 56, all maxed out on 1440p (no ray tracing) and stillots of eye candy.The world building and story is entertaining, it's a game where you can and should kick back to take moments to walk around and talk to NPCs, it's all about exploring to see what you find in between action moments, enjoyable.Overall, 8/10 on graphics and fun factor alone. Worth a purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I admit that this game is very enjoyable to play, but the issue lies with save system. This game relies on an auto-save feature that is janky. For me I have had no problems as of yet, but the friend that I play with has gotten their entire save files and steam backup files wiped from the system. This seems to have been an issue since launch involving this save system the game follows. I highly recommend you wait until the developers acknowledge this issue. An issue that has been frequently occurring for over a year. You either have to accept having to back up your own files repeatedly or face the threat of your saves being wiped.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I was recommended to play this game by a friend, not expecting much to be honest. I was blown away by the game play, graphics, and the the immersive game play. My first time playing the game I thought was about an hour or two, turns out it was 4 hours of play time. I do not regret buying this game at all. 10/10 would recommended to anyone
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute triumph of a game. I was astonished to find out that this was the debut title of 11-person studio, Neon Giant. The level of polish... the meticulously framed environments... the sense of scale and awe. I felt like either my jaw was on the floor or my heart was pounding through my chest the entire time, I kid you not. This is the GREATEST cyberpunk experience ever made, in my opinion, and I simply cannot wait to play whatever Neon Giant releases next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game you feel bad leaving a negative review for, because all the heaps of praise on the visuals are well deserved. And effort was clearly put into the game. I just didn't have much fun playing through the single player campaign. The parts I felt needed the most work were the story, dialogue, and characters, none of which I could get in to. Also, the navigation and map. They are so bad you will click the guiding path button endlessly and follow it mindlessly. It was about a 5/10 for me but could be a 6 or 7 for some. I did not encounter any corruption to my save file or major bugs of any kind.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic game with great graphics and awesome details and atmosphere. a lot of work was put into the design which is in every area you explore. there are some bugs but nothing an effortless quick google cant help solve.I am writing this review seconds after earning the last achievement adding it to my "perfect games" list :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: A really great game.My wife and i played this one last year and had quite some fun with it. 50 hours of playtime including cyber heist (which is indeed a great expansion). There are still a couple of side quest missing here and there.. So with all done we might end up with probably 60 hours. And thats it. Which is fine for me. Especially with the price that i paid. Playing it with a controller makes it much easier imho - but that is also subject to personal preference. The only downside is: i would have loved to see another expansion.. which never happened so far. However - still a very fine game. The atmosphere, the thrill and the action, along with a unique and very fitting soundtrack are the parts i liked most. The difficulty is pretty well balanced. And i also liked the storyline. So - no real bad parts. A fine game - especially when considering its price. (woohoo - its available for 9 Bucks today... come on.. give it a try :D )
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: It's a beautifully crafted world with an insane level of world detail.Strong RPG like elements keep you busy leveling up your character and game style.A very enjoyable experience.The only one negative i have is that the last update has caused my game to crash often but it was flawless before the update.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Great graphics, outstanding level design from an aesthetics perspective... but:- Repeated crashes- Constant and repeated tutorial messages that interrupt gameplay (and reset on crashes)- Level design makes it difficult to navigate; there can be multiple layers but doesn't seem to be an indicator for objectives above/belowIn summary: Feels like a AAA early access/late beta. If you were thinking of buying, I'd hold off for a couple of months and see if patches fix the crashes and other bugs that have been reported.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: It's a gorgeous game, the detail is amazing. the gameplay is fun ONCE YOU LEARN HOW TO TARGET SOMETHING, I'm using a Mouse and Keyboard and it was frustrating not understanding how your target and actually shoot something. the game needs a better tutorial system to explain it to us NOOBS. I'm not a fan of the camera angles i understand its a top-down game but sometimes it is hard to spot the enemies, But over all i would give it a 8 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the aesthetics and the feel of combat. First few hours were really fun but then you start to find the game lacking.Graphics are good but the way game loads assets you get major hangs and dips in performance when the game seems to first load any given asset. Enemy levels are a bit odd at times and you can find yourself getting wrecked if you wander to wrong places too early and I seem to do it quite a lot when trying to find those collectable "chests" in the map.I find trying out new weapons bit of hassle as you can't really seem to be able reasonably compare the power against your current one which is most likely already upgraded and you don't want to waste upgrade items if you don't like how the weapon handles. Some kind of weapons range with different level training dummies might be an answer if there was one.Cyberdeck and hacking is just half-assed, an afterthough. You find chest and doors that can't be unlocked as your deck isn't good enough and the upgrades seem to be randomly placed around the main quest areas so it takes a while to get ICE level. Also I've found chests just don't open even with correct ICE level (bug). Why can't I upgrade the cyberdeck via merchants? Why use random placement?Quest progression is really bad. You can get side missions which are impossible to complete before you progress main quest to certain points. Quest tracking is also quite bad. Marker can lead you to wrong place at times and it shows way to nothing for side quests if it's impossible to complete at the time. I'd also like to see how far the objective is in the quest log or just show all of them in the map screen. Now I tend to complete side quest accidentally as I don't use tracking for them because of above reasons.There's a quite fun game somewhere here but in it's current state can't really recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: For those of you who've felt their Cyberpunk needs went unfilled with, well, Cyberpunk 2077 this might just be the game for you!It's Cyberpunk meets Diablo (which is such a fantastic idea it's a wonder why no one had done it before) and whilst the game play is much as you would expect from such a descriptor (tho more dodge oriented than Diablo) the enviroments are crafted with such amazing detail i defy you not to have your mind blown constantly!This is also a world with incredibly rich world building, with codex entries for every area you enter, all the enemies you face, the various mechanics involved in living in it's world and even every quest giver, even the side quest guys!Long story short (too late): This is an incredibly fun game set in an utterly beautiful and deep world. Top recommendation!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is fairly unstable with crashes and bugs, I'd highly recommend this game.The atmosfere is incredible, the gunfights enjoyable and the story sets up to be expanded upon. When it works, it's a very enjoyable coop experience and gives fair reason for multiple playthroughs.Let's just hope they fix the issues before continuing the story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Worth the PurchasePROs: Fun & addictive gameplay. Great environment. I took my time and spent 22hrs completing the main & all side quests. Re mapped a couple of keys but used mouse & keyboard for the whole game. There is no end game or new game+ to encourage you to continue playing once you finish the game. Would reinstall if a feature like that is added. Cons:Couple of crashes playing solo. The quest side quest system lets you take quests even if the area for the quest hasn't opened up yet. If you run into this it means you have to continue the main story to get the areas to open up. I did not play co op but read other players had several issues. _childDocuments_.review: By default, I won't be recommending this game. But definitely check it out when it is on special.The good:- great graphics (although some areas are extremely bright to the point you can't see your character)- smooth gameplay and control- great game mechanics and fluid combat- no penalty when you actually die in combat regardless of difficulty levelThe bads are unfortunately what I consider as deal breaker.- Misleading mission recommended level. From time to time, you will collect missions to complete, but yet, the level recommendation is extremely misleading. Missions that have recommended level of 7 as example can present to you enemies of level 15 or even 20+ (marked with skull). These will basically one shot you, sucking the fun out of the game.- Tied to first point above, as you explore or move around in combat fighting enemies of your level ranges, you can bump into one of those over levelled enemies and they will join the fight in no time. If they are melee, you probably have a chance dodging around, but if they are ranged, have fun being one shotted from off screen ! This is what I personally think as terrible design because it punishes "Exploration" and tunnels you to focus on story missions instead.- You can't save manually. There are ways to "trigger" manual game saves, but upon returning to the game, you will be put at different location than when you saved the game. And guess what? Sometimes you can be put in area surrounded by enemies ! Again, you probably will stand a chance if the enemies are within your level range, but if you are unlucky... yep, have fun seeing the death screen !- Game crashes, quite frequently. It crashed upon my first time loading the game even! And there is no way for you to find out what caused it.- You don't have "View" mode, to scout ahead and assess what level the enemies are. - invisible walls. Sometimes when you are moving, you can get stuck for no reason. You press the directional button, but your char won't move towards the said direction, even when there is open space. This also includes when you try to dodge when this bug occurs, you will just dodge in the same spot. In combat, this is a major disaster !These are just 100% unacceptable considering the game has been out for years, and hence, I would recommend only getting the game when it's on specials.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful, somewhat buggy (as of this review) game.    It may have the best environment art I've seen in the last... 15 years?  I don't know how to quantify that, other than to say everyone should at least consider buying the game just to see the sprawling mega city.   The combat is... okay.   Wonky aiming (I played with auto aim off), in that even with your laser lined up on a guy's head, and max accuracy, sometimes the most accurate sniper rifles just simply whiffed on the target.  Is it a parallax issue, where the isometric view is causing some misses? Not a huge deal, just go full auto or automatic rocket launcher to solve the problem. The storyline was acceptable, but some characters seemed to kinda get dropped in at the very end of the game, making me wonder if some story basically got cut out for length/development time.  Same for some of the best weapons, you find them, or at least I did, when I was approaching level 30, and had completed the majority of the game.  Far too many boring weapons early on.    This also applies somewhat to enemy types, a lot of the more boring enemies get spammed early on, and you don't get any of the really entertaining enemies until basically the end of the game.Overall, a solid, enjoyable game, just probably requires a pretty decent setup to run at  a reasonable framerate.  I look forward to the Ascent 2, or some expansion to this game.    Speedy players can probably burn through this game in around 10-12 hours, especially if they use the fast travel (taxi, Metro) options.  I have 23 hours according to Steam, but I walked everywhere (or spammed movement skills) just to see the gorgeous map, and tried to find every chest/side mission.  Apparently I missed a few side missions though. This game has also made me really want to replay Ruiner, so I'm probably going to reinstall that other dystopian future nightmare game soon.

_childDocuments_.review: OVERALL OPINION: This game is great in a lot of ways, but that greatness is limited by some seemingly rookie issues the devs haven't managed to fix yet, even after all the time it's been out. Worth it on sale though.This game is beautiful. The soundtrack is awesome. The gameplay is decent; a little challenging, but not too much so. The story is also decent. The lore is deep and well thought out. You get vibes from every scifi movie you've ever seen, be it Blade Runner to The Fifth Element, and it all meshes well. And now for the problems.The game crashes randomly. Each lock up requires a full relog; you can't just back out to the opening screen. For no real reason. It's not every five minutes, but there is nothing worse than getting into a game this good then repeatedly crashing out for nothing. The devs have said nothing on the topic, so no idea if they're planning to fix it or have taken their money and are laughing at the people complaining.There are limited upgrade items. This means you can only upgrade the weapons the *game* tells you to, rather than deciding you like one of them and maxing it out, or eventually reaching a point of maxing your entire arsenal. This is a mistake that limits the player's ability to determine the right path to take, as if you already upgraded the wrong weapon, you're SOL, as you cannot reverse your decision and get those parts back again.My overall opinion on this game? It's worth your time, but you need to be a patient sort. If things like I've described can ruin a game for you, you won't like this. Basically a very well polished, but flawed gem.

_childDocuments_.review: The negative: - It still has a few bugs (nothing like cyberpunk 2077 though ;)) - It's a bit short for my tastes and there is no endgame. once you've done every mission you can roam around and open the chests you missed, but a diablo-esque always looking for better gear and interesting combinations doesn't happen. - crafting is also a bit lacklustre. The only thing you can upgrade are the weapons, which all have fixed stats. Armor is just there and the only upgrade is a different armor. The Meh: - Story .... The Positive: - Gunplay and general Gameplay are GREAT! it takes a while to get used to, to shoot high or low, but the combat really is great fun! The choice of weapon matters, and the augmentations add a nice tactical layer. There is a difficulty setting, but I found it challenging enough on normal on my first solo playthrough. Will maybe put it on high when going in in coop. - Leveling up and upgrading weapons feels right. you feel the difference when upgrading weapons and you really should! Skillspoints are a bit more like in a real RPG. You get 3 per lvl and find some lying around. Every skill is maxed out at  20 points and level cap is high, although I was at lvl 30 when finishing it. - The graphics are really nice to look at, especially with RTX and DLSS, but even without it looks great! The design is very detailed and the map is big and varied. - The sound is really good, although it's a bit quiet on headphone mode with my settings (Arctis wireless pro,  dts headphone:x, peace eq). But when you crank it up a bit it really is just pure enjoyment. The soundtrack is usually nicely in the background and paints the atmoshpere a bit thicker, but when there is a boss fight it really ramps up and gets the adrenaline going. The weapons sounds are varied and meaty. The humming and buzzing of the machinery and tech in the background is great. - Performance with i7-10700K, 32GB RAM, SSD, RTX2080 at 2560x1440 at most things on Ultra with RTX and DLSS Performance mode is good (about 70-90FPS), sometimes when the game is loading a new part ofg the map it can stutter a bit, but only a few seconds. In conclusion: I want to play more! Devs: PLEASE add endgame content or a few nice long add-ons.

_childDocuments_.review: I will re-write my recommendation after the launch dust has settled and the release of Ascent's first major patches. Love some cyberpunk action?  High tolerance for big nasty bugs, up to and including resetting your progress in the game completely?  Dive right in.  Otherwise, I suggest waiting a bit for bug fixing patches before putting your money down. The Ascent is an action shooter with rpg elements and worldbuilding, and twinstick shooter controls, set in a cyberpunk inspired world.  If you like some light legged ARPG style combat set in a seriously delicious cyberpunk setting with gorgeous visuals and a banger hard synth soundtrack, this is probably right up your alley.When you get going on this game and catch sight of the city you're playing in proper, I instinctively compare it to the biggest budget releases, and it holds up,  darn well, in fact.  Its unbelieavable that this game was brought to life by a very small developer team consisting of 12 devs.Moving onto gameplay, the action bits play pretty well.  At its core, the game plays like a very capable twinstick shooter, while looking sexy as hell with its extremely detailed setting, great music, overall solid sound design and violent explosions and effects.The term 'Action RPG' in the adverts for the game should be interpreted in the loosest of senses, however.  The only RPG you find here are a fairly basic character creator, skill points to specialize your guy or girl as you like, and dialogue options to fill out some lore for the game.  The only decisions you get, is if you want to accept or decline sidequests.One very important thing to warn about however is that the game is buggy as hell right now.  Ascent was really not ready for release, but here we are.  Expect crashes, items not adding to your inventory after picking up, quest mobs not spawning as they should even after reloading the game, effectively killing your playthrough, save files disappearing, also of course killing your playthrough, your characters' weapons randomly firing endlessly without you pressing anything, and more.  I'm sure some reading this will feel the urge to chime in that they didn't have any bugs so the game is fine, to you I say, I belive you and I'm happy for you, consider yourself very lucky.  Because this game needs bugfixes, badly!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Despite the bugs I've read about, I've been really fortunate to not have to experienced any of the game breaking ones. I really enjoyed this game for a variety of reasons and I'd suggest getting it.This game has received a lot of criticism and rightly so. The bugs in this game are NOT few and far between. They're constant and in your face, but manageable. I've read about the save deleting bugs, but considering the team behind this game is so small, I'm willing to overlook it. I've been save-scammed by a AAA title before, but I hope you never experience it in The Ascent.Let's talk about the good first though.The Ascent is a game with a well thought out design. They really nail that "High Tech Low Life" aesthetic and even reference it on a loading screen. The sci-fi aspect is also pretty well integrated, though I was certainly surprised when I encountered it initially since I went into this game with a complete media blackout. That said, they've blended the races into the world with finesse. The races don't feel particularly out of place, and there's enough background information for you to get an idea of the general qualities that each race possesses without it feeling hamfisted. The Ascent immediately starts throwing their homebrewed cyberpunk jargon at you as if you're already a resident of the world; you don't have to be a genius to figure out what the words mean which makes it easy to stomach.The gunplay is solid, and despite lacking a huge weapon roster, there are still plenty of different weapons and unique weapons to allow you to pick and choose how you play the game. You're not meant to just pick 2 guns for the entire game, and you're meant to have a large toolkit at your disposal. The upgrade system lends itself to this nicely. That said, be careful about your MK9 and MK10 upgrades, as there are limited resources to upgrade weapons to the final 2 tiers. I wasn't a huge fan of the "aim high ADS" system because it felt really out of place, but it's part of the gameplay and you learn to make the most of it. If you can get used to it, it really enhances the gameplay experience. There's armor which can look great, but also can look kinda ♥♥♥♥. It takes a bit of work to get a cool armor set going IMO. Once you understand the damage types, you can start equipping armor that's the most effective for your given situation.Now, the not-so-good.Mobs have an aggro range and if they leave their aggro range, they'll basically be invulnerable and walk back to their spawn point. In most MMOs and other games with an aggro range, this isn't a big deal. However this is where one of those ugly bugs rears its head. On occasion, a mob's AI might not reset correctly when they return to their spawn location. They'll loop into a return path while taking single digit damage and not attacking the player. You can safely ignore these mobs however.The soundtrack and audio design is all really well done and atmospheric and thematic. I was surprised to hear YUC'e's music in the game too! I love Nightclub Junkie! However outside of this singular song that I already really like, most of the sound design and soundtrack is rather forgettable. It' good, but there's nothing that makes me want to listen to it outside of the game, or outside of a cyberpunk TTRPG like CPR or SR5.The transmogrification system is a lifesaver. As I mentioned earlier, a lot of the armor, while thematically appropriate, doesn't really allow you to get a more Corporate-aesthetic which is one I like a lot. There are some pieces you can kitbash together to make a great armor set, however this is kind of let down by the lack of preview-ability as well as the lackluster color palette. The voice acting for the story is really good, however the story itself leaves a lot to be desired. It feels like Neon Giant has had a lot of influence from Borderlands, WH40k, and Shadowrun but has cleverly blended it into their own style and own world. While there are some things that I find to be similar, it doesn't feel completely familiar. The story and a lot of the NPCs are pretty forgettable.As a final note: The game can be difficult at times. I've heard of people dying A LOT and I have no idea what difficulty they were playing on. I was playing on normal and died somewhere around 10 times. There's a lot of trial and error. All in all, if you buy this game, I hope you have a great time and don't encounter character or save killing bugs!

_childDocuments_.review: The Ascent is an absolutely gorgeous collection of art. Too bad, then, that it's a pile of garbage video game.Make no mistake: the art isn't enough to save this garbage fire, but it is  art. Every single environment is absolutely stunning, better than any I've seen in any isometric/top down/CRPG game. Unfortunately, the camera both cannot be controlled by the player  has a mind of its own, frequently swinging in ways that show off the environments but make actually playing the game difficult. I understand wanting to show off the art assets, but this is the wrong way to go about it.But enough of the only positive aspect of The Ascent. Let's talk gameplay.The Ascent's gameplay consists of twinstick shooter sections strung together with fetch quests. Dozens and dozens of boring, repetetive fetch quests. You'll do nothing in this game but: 1) spin around shooting enemies without strategy or thought, and 2) run, in real time, across the entire map, over and over.I cannot overstate how much meaningless, time-consuming  this game is full off. You walk through hub cities. You walk to elevators. You walk up and down levels of the map (which is horrible at telling you where you actual are). You walk to fast travel points that don't take you anywhere near where you want to fast-travel to. You can press a fast-travel button that will drop you nowhere near where you want to fast-travel to, so you must walk more.I have 14.5 hours of played time in The Ascent, and 2/3rds of it is just walking. I honestly don't believe someone played this game and found it fun. All you do is walk.Characters in The Ascent have a number of stats they can level and specialize into, but none of them feel terribly impactful or really differentiate one character from another. These stats also appear on gear where their presence means absolutely nothing. You literally cannot tell if gear is boosting a stat. Gear also has a number of damage reductions on it, but they also mean nothing and the possible need for them is completely uncommunicated by the game. You just pick the highest rarity gear and wear it, because why not.Weapons are the most important piece of gear in The Ascent and they are impossible to compare. How? Well, when a weapon is upgraded all copies of that weapon are permanently upgraded for that character. This means that, when trying to figure out if a newly found weapon is better, you're always comparing an upgraded weapon to a non-upgraded weapon. There is  to see a weapon's pre-upgrade stats so you can compare two weapons at the same level. A worthless system.But that's just the gameplay. The Ascent is (apparently) a cyberpunk story. Is that where it shines? .The setting of The Ascent is that you, player, are an indentured servant (slave) working for a massive, world-spanning corporation. Then, something happens and that corporation dissolves and other corporations come swarming in to pick its bones clean. How do you feel about this? Who knows. The player character is utterly and completely uncharacterized. You have zero thoughts, zero reactions; you literally just do whatever a voice on the radio tells you to do. At one point in the story another corporation takes over your indentured servitude contract and you simply start obeying that voice instead of the previous one. Marvellous.So the setting is mostly generic, welcome-to-the-dystopia cyberpunk. But what about the events of the story? What do they have to say about a corporate-dominated world that chews people up and spits them out? Nothing, not a damn thing. Your corp dissolves, a new one buys all its bits, you work for that corp now. Unquestioningly. Do you fight for your rights or humanity? No. Do you burn down the old world? Nope. You collaborate with a corp from start to finish, a good little lapdog.So much for cyberpunk.Side quests aren't any better. In fact, they're worse. At least the main story establishes the pathetic storytelling above; the side quests are essentially all just jokes. They contribute precisely zero to world building, which is actually kind of impressive. It almost had to be intentional to make running errands for the people of a dystopia teach you nothing about the world.If all that was bad then the awful cherry on the top of this terrible cake is the final boss fight. You  Do you fight them to the death in a grand battle? Nah, you just hold the 'use' button on four different computer consoles and they disappear. What a wet fart of an ending, but it should have been expected after all the other attempts at 'storytelling' that came before it.All told, The Ascent is terrible. Fantastic art can't make up for a worthless camera, endless hours spent walking, meaningless stats on both character and gear, and one of the worst stories I've ever been forced to endure. Under no circumstances should you play this miserable game.

_childDocuments_.review: Going to remain Negative until they fix the ungodly amount of issues with the CO-OPI've never played the Singleplayer but I assume it works just fine, but the co-op is straight broken and crashes from the most simple functions. Within the first hour of the game you can get stuck in a conversation with an npc and will be unable to exit the conversation unless you restart the game, from my knowledge only one player or the host can do the interaction, anymore and players will be trapped. So you can work around this, by having the one player who actually cares about the story doing the dialogue. Another issue are cutscenes, feels like a coinflip between which of the four players are going to randomly crash for no reason, and whats better is if you crash during the cutscene the other three players see a black screen and have to restart the whole session so you may or may not lose a good chunk of progression because of rng.And the stores / shops are a menace, they either crash when someone buys an item or they don't, it's pure luck if they'll be a source of your millionth crash. Granted most of the items you get from shops are pointless anyways as you'll likely pick them up as a drop anyways but it still boggles my mind that a main part of the game can crash your game unless you have the host baby-sitting your shopping spree. Besides the crashing part, the game has some minor gameplay issues. I enjoy the general gameplay, shootings great and it's been a bit since I've played a top-down shooter that peaked my interest, and the environment and music is amazing, I really want to enjoy it all if it wasn't bogged down by all the headaches it gives you, as it can feel like a breeze in co-op or maybe the leveling / scaling system is just wrong, we took a level 17 side mission and decided to do it at level 15 for the challenge, got to the area and the enemies are around level 8 or so, and the "boss" is level 9, but I guess 8+9 is 17 so that was right. I think the only time we died was when we didn't know the whole game ended when one person died and the time we got gangbanged by a bunch of weeaboos who kept teleporting in. But this was early game so maybe there's a spike in the difficulty, but the crashing has prevent me from seeing that just yet.tl;dr I'd wait if you want a new co-op shooter because it's a buggy mess, but I'm seeing these issues have been around for awhile so who knows when it'll be a functional co-op game, but if you want a pretty alright top-down cyberpunk shoot em' up for yourself because you have no friends, this might be your cup of tea.

Still worth playing, just keep in mind that you may lose progress through no fault of your own.Edit: After playing more the word that comes to mind is "rough".  There's a lot of places where the game seems unpolished and there's questionable gameplay decisions.  If you like to explore the map, prepare to get murdered by much higher level NPCs...a lot.  Straying a hair off the path will put you face to face with things that will one shot you without any warning.  We ended up using this as an indicator that we were going in the right direction- did you die after turning a corner? reload, that's the wrong direction then.  This is especially difficult because it wipes out your grenade and tech power and there's boss encounters where you have to have both of these to succeed.  this doesn't even touch on the arcane stats and indications of what they do.  This armor has normal protection, but no digital protection.  What's digital protection? do I even need it? _childDocuments_.review: Overall: 4.5/5This game was not at all what I had expected it to be. I expected it to be a sort of procedurally generated roguelike/lite where you tried to fight level to level, always climbing higher, to try to reach the top of the arcology while fighting a variety of enemies (gangers, CorpSec, mutants, robots, etc) and equipping a variety of gear in order to eventually reach the top and do... something?What the game actually IS a a beautifully and intricately imagined crapsack sci-fi dystopian story-based game more akin to Diablo than Hades. I liked all the characters, I didn't have any gripes with the voice acting, I loved all the set pieces, and most of the guns feel sufficiently distinct from eachother that it's worth experimenting to find favorites (although it seems like some of them are better for almost all situations than others, and damage type distribution by enemy weakness seems to be a little bit skewed, but eh). The world is expansive, and rewards you for exploring by hiding various goodies and chests and rare equipment in various corners and behind various locked doors.The story and world are immersive and intriguing, and the art and soundtrack definitely help pull you in. Gunplay is fast, snappy, and reasonably tactical. Augs and tactical/grenade abilities add another layer of customization that significantly changes combat flow.Minus points:- As of the current build, two cutscenes have an issue where the animations and audio are misaligned (the first encounter with Kira, and the final cutscene of the game)- nogHead the hacker has a few lines toward the end of the game delivering exposition about what's really going on that have VERY different text from the audio delivered over that text- In a number of cases the "recommended level" associated with many of the sidequests is seemingly arbitrary, and there are a few sidequests that actually can be picked up WELL before the location where they can be completed is unlocked- There are hackable turrets in the game. They are never anywhere that would actually be even remotely useful, and you cannot hack a turret that has aggroed on you. There are mortar turrets that, at present, can only be destroyed with grenades or a specific augmentation that shoots rockets, but switching to those in the midst of play empties the gauges that let you even use those thingsBonus points:- At points the game's difficulty seems to spike, though this can generally be adjusted by shifting gear around to find guns that exploit enemy weaknesses, armor that blocks enemy damage type, and grenades/augs/"tactical equipment" that can strategically turn the tide. Thats said, THE ONLY THING DYING COSTS YOU IS TIME. You don't lose XP, you don't lose money, you don't lose durability. In fact, loot picked up before death is kept, making it very easy to grind for money and xp, and potentially get some very good (and in one specific case ABSOLUTELY NECESSARY) gear.Areas of confusion:- Until nearly the end of the game the random bounties are all, as far as I could tell, "low grade" bounties, regardless of what level they were or how hard they hit. Every single bounty turns in for 1000 uCred regardless of what level that bounty was. More than half of the guns in this game can be sold to vendors for more than 1000 uCreds, meaning disposing of bounties is less lucrative than selling a bounty's weaponry. Weird point of worldbuilding.- I kept expecting there to be more consequences to my inadvertent slaughter of uninvolved civilians than mild and occasional scoldings from my boss. Something like actually having corpsec, or one of those huge rocket mechs descend from the sky out of nowhere in the middle of a fight and try to ruin my day, maybe. Never happened.- It would be cool if, after doing jobs for the Liquid Quiks, some of the "neutral" gang members hanging out in various places became allied (green) characters, in recognition of your work for/with them. Same with the Rojin. At present, that's not a thing, which lends itself well to the whole "fight your way back through this entire neighborhood because you're too cheap to call a taxi" thing, but it still feels... weird.Altogether, I really enjoyed playing The Ascent and found it to be both a fun game and a very pretty intentionally dystopian-looking world to run around in,

_childDocuments_.review: Once upon a time, Origin Systems released an isometric action game in the 90s called Crusader: No Remorse. In it, you played a former corporate enforcer on a quest for revenge against the company that made him and along the way, escalated negotiations with an eclectic collection of weapons from slug throwers to the dreaded UV rifle that tanned the flesh off of your foes. Your rampage took you through everything from the dingy techno guts of a space base to fancy corporate offices whose glass block partitions disintegrated before your personal 401K.Neon Giant's The Ascent is kind of like that -- the spiritual successor to the the kind of 80s and 90s action bombast celebrated by everything ranging from The Running Man to Total Recall (the good version) to Robocop and given life by games like Crusader. Mix in a little of Smash TV with a world where aliens and humans live in uneasy proximity to a promise of prosperity most will never see in their lifetime, and this is the result.After customizing your toon with a preset collection of bits and bobs, you're thrown in as an "ident" whose life is owned by the monolithic Ascent Group. In exchange for a trip to a new world, you (like millions of others) are now indebted to work off your tab at Ascent's arcology tower -- a city, but stacked vertically with the very rich and privileged enjoying the view of actual sunlight and clouds at the very top. But you're just a lowly indent whose job it is to fix ♥♥♥♥ at the very bottom while wading in it. Needless to say, you've got a long way to go and before you know it, opportunity knocks.The Ascent is a twin stick shooter which plays great on a controller (I used a wired Xbox 360 controller that still somehow lives) but you can play it with a mouse and keyboard. If you're a veteran of titles like Grim Dawn or Diablo, it might take a bit of getting used to (clicking on a spot doesn't move you, movement is controlled instead with WASD keys so it can be a bit awkward at first). You can even take cover behind objects by crouch walking behind them and shooting over, though in most firefights, it felt like most enemies will just run up and try to facetank your shots. Red "splats" also show up with boss fights to show you where the most damaging attacks will head to next and you have a dodge roll to help keep you alive.The main action centers around a linear series of story quests but it's open enough to ignore it to some extent and push how far you can get by exploring. A lot of my time was actually spent doing the decent number of side missions and pushing how far I could go before high level enemies began one shotting me on my quest for better gear. It's really tempting to call it a Diablo clone with guns but it didn't feel that way to me for a few reasons. For one, you wont't often be zerged by mobs of critters and the loot pool is nowhere as deep. Your inventory is also all the stash you'll ever need.There are also no random stats on the gear you get so getting multiple copies of a type of weapon (like a certain type of pistol) will stack that weapon in your inventory. On the other hand, it still scratches that loot itch with what is there. Powerful armor and ridiculously impressive weapons and cybernetics found in far off areas are nice rewards for those that take the time to look around. There's also a decent variety of weapons in each class from energy pistols to different types of rocket launchers. And you have unlimited ammo. Weapons can also be upgraded via modules (which come in three different grades). Once a specific pistol type is upgraded, all types of that pistol share the same benefits.Hacking consists of holding down a key/button near an object and triggering it to unlock or, at higher upgrade levels, spew credits or free health and energy. Upgrades are found after putting in a bit of exploration and each one will activate a new ability (like hacking ATMs) or improve certain categories (for opening harder doors or chests).Death also has no consequences aside from putting you back at the last checkpoint the game made. The good news is that the checkpoints are pretty forgiving (no manual saves, though).Leveling up awards skill points for improving things like your health or cybernetics. These stats, in turn, also affect how well your augments work (magic abilities). You can also reset your skill points but as you go up in level, so does the cost. Combining augments with certain throwables created a high tech power fantasy of being able to summon a guardian robot, set off spheres of stasis, and mow down enemies with a machine gun firing exploding bullets or a Gundam bean fired from your body. Because of the game's blend of cyberpunk dystopia with galactic civilizations, the sci-fi tech ecstasy produced by certain gear and aug combos creates some pretty dramatic scenes of carnage for flesh, robot, and concrete shattering backdrops alike.The Ascent goes all-in with neon lit storefronts, rotting sewage, rusting tech, restricted secret laboratories, and enough exploding props to send Arnold Schwarzenegger to Mars and back again. The soundtrack is also really good -- I'd jump into fights or walk around just to listen to the different tracks whenever I could. The game is also packed with a lot of text entries detailing nearly everything, even that NPC that appeared for only one side mission and never again anywhere else, so if you love that kind of thing (like me), you'll get plenty here.The Ascent isn't without its problems. Three quests failed to advance because enemies didn't spawn (restoring from a previous checkpoint fixed it though sometimes meant I had to fight my way back to where it should have worked) and a night club that I needed to get into for a side quest but couldn't even after opening the door. Only until later in the story could I go in for something else. The story also has a few issues such as one particularly pivotal moment for your character largely going ignored by certain important NPCs that treat it as if it was something you picked up on the way back from the grocery.Once you've found the "best" stuff there's really no reason to go back into the game and farm given how stingy mobs are unless you love reliving mow down moments with your favorite weapons and augments, limiting replayability. Even I got tired of so many random bounties randomly roaming about. There's also no New Game + mode.Then there's the run speed. Once I found dodge rolling, I dodge rolled nearly everywhere I went because it was just slightly faster than my default speed of narcolepsy. Fast travel, once unlocked, was a bit bittersweet with some drop off locations -- joy at getting there, loathing at jogging like a turtle to where I really needed to go.In a lot of ways, it feels like a spiritual successor to Origin Systems' Crusader series where you played the part of a corporate enforcer now set on revenge against his former employer, only in this case, you're busy just trying to survive as a cog in a galactic dystopia of corporate feudalism. When I made it to the end after traveling through the Ascent's arcology from start to finish with dungeons as dingy city streets and restricted secrets scoured by an arsenal of cyberpunk gadgets and weird weapons, it didn't push me on whether I had gone too far in replacing my humanity. Instead, The Ascent eagerly serves up a diet of chrome, bullets, and burstfire in the hopes you'll go looking for something else along the way to make that stasis field grenade turning people into exploding balloons any cooler.

_childDocuments_.review: The Ascent is absolutely one of the better cyberpunk games out there. Its city is unrivaled, it is  gorgeous. The lighting, the buildings, the way people interact; it all adds to an amazing atmosphere. It’s the one aspect that managed to impress me right until the end.So, when I’m praising the world building aspect of the game so much there certainly must be something wrong with the gameplay, right? Well, yes and no.The press has frequently mentioned this would be similar to an action RPG - and technically it is - but unlike games like Diablo this plays more like an isometric action shooter with cover mechanics. You have to line up your shots and click (or hold). And there are definitely stats to be upgraded; they just don’t seem to have a gigantic impact on your character in terms of power. But you have augmentations for that.Also, for those that want to know if this has a character creator: yes, it does have one.You can walk the world freely after a short introduction, but there are a few blockades here and there that might open up later during the game. At times it’s recommended to explore because you might find some good loot and at other times it’s not because you might just encounter some high-level enemies that will kill you with just a few shots. On several occasions I was walking to my quest destination and came across some (then still) overpowered enemies that killed me pretty quickly. I’m still not sure if I was too underleveled or I just had some bad luck, but maybe a bit of both, even though I followed and completed the main quests until then and quite a few side quests. Areas afterwards had same level enemies again. This could also have been a bug, who knows (most likely not), but a friendly heads-up nevertheless. The game saves frequently though, so you’ll never lose a whole lot of progress when this happens.When you come across an enemy then usually a whole swarm of enemies will arrive from all sides. It’s integral that you then use the cover system in order to survive. With the click of a button you can hide behind objects and with another you can then either aim high or low. You can also do this without cover but it usually makes no sense to do this outside of cover. What I really loved was that when the shooting began innocent bystanders would cower and run away. This made the world feel all the more believable, so well done to the team!Enemies reward you with XP, as does completing quests, and when you level up you can put some point in upgrading your character. For example, you can speed up reloading or make aiming a little easier/more accurate. Weapons can also be upgraded if you have acquired the correct materials.There are also augmentations you can use to do make yourself more powerful. Examples of these are Overclock (almost instantly reload your weapon) or Spiderbots that are ideal to have when facing large(r) groups.Since I already mentioned the absolutely stunning city and its atmosphere I can be short about the rest of the graphics: everything is created with lots of care and love, some of the characters up close could be a little more detailed though, but these moments aren’t very frequent anyway so it’s not a very big deal.The sound effects are great and pack a punch and the music is satisfying and fits the theme of the game. Voice acting is there but limited to real sentences as well as gibberish. Some of it is great, some of it isn’t; it’s a bit of a mixed bag.I had a few issues with the game that I thought were unintuitive or frustrating. Let me discuss these a little more:On some occasions the camera was blocking my view. This happened especially when entering a building or moving toward a part where you can’t see your character in the first place (usually the more hidden areas). These moments lasted just a few seconds fortunately.I’ve also had a few instances where there was an insane increase in difficulty, usually when I had to defend an area for several minutes, especially later in the game. I had to drop the difficulty in order to get through these sequences. But I also already mentioned overpowered enemies on the way to the next main quest.The user interface for augmentations and grenades felt very unintuitive until much, much later in the game. And I then only noticed it because I was paying extra attention to the UI. This should’ve been explained from the beginning and it’s something I’ve seen and hear other people talk about as well.And the last but certainly not less important issue would be that you can only keep track of one quest and only one. This makes the length of the game artificially longer and I always hate that. If there was a way for a main quest *and* a side quest it would’ve been a bit better but you can only track a total of one for both categories combined. A big no no and whoever came up with that should get a lesson in usability.And now to end this already overlong review:The Ascent has a breathtaking, living city, that’s a must-see if you’re even remotely interested in cyberpunk games. As for the action; it’s solid and kind of addicting, despite several issues that are not always related to the gameplay. You can grab it on Gamepass to give it a try first but if you like to buy games in general then this one is worth the asking price, no doubt.

_childDocuments_.review: is impressive. What stands out immediately is the level of detail, to the degree where I'm left wondering if this started out as an isometric game. The closer you focus your gaze the more that is revealed, be it small scrolling text on monitors or small unique clutter in businesses. The game is beautiful, its designs unique, and its atmosphere excellent. The world is divided into tiers, and those tiers divided into districts, each recognizable via their own motifs. Media with a cyberpunk design can often feel same-y; an overuse of neon there, trash there, high rises here - but   carves out enough variety to avoid this.Regarding gameplay, this is a fairly simple twin stick shooter however the enemy AI is surprisingly competent. You'll be rushed from multiple sides, NPCs will use cover, and you'll often deal with tactics from a mixed variety of enemy types. You begin the game with a fairly typical assortment of weaponry, however later on there are a number of unique weapons, and the augmentation system especially expands your options with strong but specialized options to allow for unique playstyles. These range something basic like long range AOE damage to something less so, like a health absorbing tank or movement restricting localized nuker.What I wish  had was a better paced gameplay loop. The world is complex and beautiful, but really could do with more interactivity. I'd love to grab a drink at the number of bars, dance at a club, or play at the casino. Simple immersive actions would fit so well here, because the world is already built for it. That the entire game is combat and has no point where a slower approach is encouraged is a large negative. Likewise, any sort of endgame or challenge mode would fit well - you have many unique weapons that are only available in the last few story missions, and once those are complete you have nothing to use them on as the side missions are all level capped to the point where it's easy to one shot things.Some sort of DLC would likely alleviate most of my concerns. Nevertheless,  is a great experience right now.

_childDocuments_.review: The environments look cool, and maybe it's fun in co-op -- I only played solo. But combat and navigation (i.e. most of the actual gameplay) are both pretty terrible.Mobility is what makes combat fun in twin-stick shooters, but The Ascent is in many ways more of a cover shooter. You're also often fighting enemies that are off-screen, and combat tends to be pretty binary -- it's either almost trivial to kill everything or you're getting one-shot.Navigation is tedious and frustrating. Map icons are offset so much from their actual location that it can be difficult to tell where they actually are, especially when there are many icons on a map. Areas contain multiple levels of elevation and it's often not easy to locate stairs and elevators on the map. There is a button to reveal a path to your quest objective, and that simplifies navigation when working on a quest, but there's nothing interesting about spamming a "follow this line" button, and the fact that they felt that was a needed feature in the game is a bit of an indicator of how bad navigation often feels without it.Overall, it's an action game where running around the world and fighting stuff is rarely fun. I've stuck with it this far because I already spent the money on it so I feel like I might as well finish it, but it's really not fun or interesting so I'll most likely abandon it pretty soon.
