_childDocuments_.review: The Ascent is an average mix of RPG with twin-stick shooter set in a cyberpunk setting. Shooting is fast and responsive, but the weak story and non-existent balance makes the whole experience boring in the long run. I beat the game in less than 14 hours (main story and all side quests). I would say that three or four hours less would be ideal.Sadly, I can't recommend The Ascent. There was some potential for a good title, but it was largely unfulfilled. Neon Giant studio had big ambitions, but their beautiful vision lacks any substance. The story is just dull. It slowly gets better after 7-8 hours, but it's nothing to write home about. The spineless and voiceless main character doesn't help either. We're just a slave of the corporations doing whatever we're told to do. Zero choices, unless you count the rejecting side quests. Go x and kill y, fetch something from somewhere, blah blah blah... After finishing the game we got light teasing of the sequel... which probably will never happen. The ending itself felt flat af. It's both weird and underwhelming.The side quests are no better than the main story. Most of the stuff is average (at best) and the dialogues are not well written. There are two or three slightly better missions, but that's mainly because of the extra lore from the datapads.Important note - I finished the game playing solo. Things may feel differently (for better or worse) while playing with friends.The early gameplay is carried by the shooting system. It's simple but enjoyable. You can choose from various weapon types (you can loot them from chests/dead enemies or buy from the shop). Each of them requires a different fighting approach from you. Add grenades, "skills", and modificators, and you have a really solid base.You can crouch behind objects and they will act as your cover. It's not super reliable, so pick your covers wisely. The balance of the game is all over the place. The difficulty level spikes randomly from time to time. It can make you unable to proceed with the story without additional grind.The enemies respawn too fast, which makes travels even more annoying than they already are (the taxi system helps with it a little bit). The economy only works in the early stages of the game. Selling duplicate weapons/clothes makes you rich too fast. I'm not a fan of the weapons upgrade system. It works, but it's uninspiring. Find resources, and then upgrade the gun at the gunsmith's. It will only give you extra stats. Meh.The camerawork can be wonky. I understand that the authors wanted to show us pretty backgrounds, but it's annoying at times. It makes some fights harder than they should be. At least it doesn't disturb the exploration that much (minus moments where you need to find some doors).As usual with cyberpunk-style games, the world map (M) is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful. I'm not sure what's wrong with the UI designers. They can't make an intuitive modern map? It's really that hard?The lack of manual saves is just dumb. The autosaves are not bad, but there are times when I simply want to save by myself.  Visually, The Ascent is amazing. The environment design is on another level. The "vibes" are vastly different depending on where you're at. The lowest levels are just all grim and dangerous, with tunnels everywhere. Later, we traverse more "classical" cyberpunk locations - neons and all that crap. The highest levels are only for the richest - sterilely clean rooms and a clear atmosphere above the clouds.Character models could be more detailed. The NPCs aren't even that bad (some cool designs). The main character is the problem here. It looks low quality when compared to everything around you. The customization doesn't help. Almost all available options are simply ugly.The music and the rest of the audio are solid. Nothing particularly memorable, but also nothing atrocious. Everything fits the cyberpunk setting, which is the most important part.The quality of the voice acting is uneven. Characters from the main story are voiced fairly well, but everyone else... lifeless.The first launch of the game already shows problems - it froze while loading the start menu. You need to wait ~30s and it should fix itself. Other than that, somehow, I didn't have any big problems. It's possible that I was just lucky. No crashes, wiped saves, or broken quests. It doesn't mean that they don't exist. Many people reported these issues, so it's good to be cautious.Smaller issues are common, though. For example: your character can get stuck inside random objects or even inside the enemy. If you're unlucky, you can get stuck for good - restart the game to fix it. Enemies also can get stuck, so you can cheese your way through some fights.Non-hostile NPCs are beyond dumb. Their only role is the make the world feel "alive". Unfortunately, the authors didn't even bother to make their AI any good. Besides staying in one place, wandering around, and running when there's a fight (which often doesn't even work properly), they do literally nothing.I left the biggest problem for the last. The performance is atrocious. I had CONSTANT performance drops. Sometimes bigger (from ~140 to 70 FPS), sometimes smaller.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend getting this game on sale. (I did)Unfortunately, this title really ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed on its characters, story, and overall contribution to cyberpunk as a genre. As someone who has a lot of respect for the philosophical underpinnings of cyberpunk, this proves to be another 'cyberpunk themed' romp that speaks little to the political/economic and technological forces that impact the human experience. The most I got on this front was perhaps a genuine feeling that my character was a cog in a machine - not from anything in the game text, but from the bland, overdone story and mission delivery. The player character has quite literally zero agency in the plot, you spend the entire game being hand-held through a milquetoast cyberpunk corporate conflict story: Corporation 'A' wants something Corporation 'B' has, thinly veiled by a pretty disappointing mystery over the fall of The Ascent Group. Adding insult to injury, the inciting incident of the story doesn't matter by the end of it because they return to the same status quo with essentially the same people in charge. The only difference is now you're on better terms with the corporate overlords you've been doing dirty work for the whole game and you've earned your freedom. Which also doesn't matter because your character is an undeveloped stand-in.The gameplay is fine, if you've ever played a twin-stick shooter type with special abilities then The Ascent won't provide much new to you. There are some nuances that I appreciate like the cover and aim height systems that make encounters feel more dynamic than they would otherwise. Enemies do love to run right at you, occasionally using cover themselves, so you'll still be dodge spamming across the map in between trigger pulls. The world design is where I think The Ascent shines brightest. The attention to detail is superb, and while you may get lost in some of the environments, the multi-level areas and hidden chests are interesting enough to explore that it never feels labyrinthian. The density of npc's in the city and the design of the world around them make an immersive cyberpunk environment. It even contributes to the feel of the firefights: civilians will flee from gunfire often getting caught in it/ becoming accidental meat shields as enemies press towards you. Often times I could become confused mid-combat between an enemy I hadn't hit yet (no healthbar showing) and random bystanders, which would lead to me accidentally lighting up some innocents. This really emphasized the darkness of the world for me, I felt a bit horrified after I unintentionally mowed down a group of shoppers. So if that's all well and good, then The Ascent will provide a good 20-30 hours of game for you to whack at. I had fun playing it, but ultimately The Ascent was a hollow experience.

The artwork, the animations, the music, none of it disappoints. The atmosphere is absolutely beautiful. I love the upgrade and customization paths. Augmentations and loot boxes? Yes, please!The missions are fun, and it runs smooth! The only drawback is that there are currently some bugs in co-op play, but the Devs are already on top of it with a thread started for posting co-op issues.Definitely a game I can see myself playing for a lot more hours. _childDocuments_.review: The Ascent Review: A Cyberpunk Visual Feast with Room for ImprovementAfter initially downloading a cracked file, I was blown away by the visuals of The Ascent, prompting me to support Neon Giant by purchasing the game and all DLC during a sale. What stands out the most in this game is the environment, which is undeniably cyberpunk and more impressive than even Cyberpunk 2077. It's clear that the developers put a lot of effort into creating a visually stunning world.Unfortunately, the voice-acting is not up to par. Many of the side-missions feel like they were voiced by people with no prior experience in voice acting. However, the DLC does offer substantial improvements in this area.While the gameplay is enjoyable, it does become repetitive after a while. It requires you to turn off your brain and just accept it for what it is. The combat system could benefit from a hybrid approach between Realtime, Realtime with Pause, and Turn-based gameplay. This would allow players to enjoy the game in different ways and increase its appeal to a wider audience. Something along the lines of a combination between Diablo 3, X-Com 2 and Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous. This would be a straight up 10/10 for me.Overall, The Ascent feels more like a proof of concept rather than a fully-fledged game. Despite its flaws, the game is still an enjoyable experience that cyberpunk fans will appreciate.

_childDocuments_.review: long story short: Core gameplay is fun and the level design is spellbinding. There are minor and medium flaws in every aspect of the game, but they are not significant compared to the overall experience. Without any loud and pretentious promises, The Ascent is much better cyberpunk RPG than 2077. I recommend this game to any cyberpunk genre lover.>My first impression was enjoyable nostalgic feeling because of similarities with great underrated game  by silverback studio, 2003. Especialy in terms of sound and level design - it shines bright in Ascent.The main disappointment after finishing the game was the lack of a  mode. There is a solution for this (Google will help), but it is definitely not how the developers intended.core gameplay (fighting hordes of mobs) sometimes are buggy, but i'm sure it will be fixed in a few weeks.There a lot of confusion - which i guess could be fixed in future by designers - with skills, augmentations, armor and weapons. Game tutorials and UI design wasn't enough for me to clarify which branch of skills or which weapon should i choose. or how different layouts affects gameplay. In the end i felt like there wasn't big difference between skill branches and wish they could be more strictly diversified (with classes for example).The transport system in the game is somewhat original, but underdeveloped.  function is fun, but I think it wouldn't be needed if the metro system was more wast and easier to find.Level design can be improved with some gamma settings | colors to make navigation in areas more familiar.Story felt very background, i'd like to see some choices in dialogues and through missions (whom to kill / spare and so on). But in the end it wasn't a big problem, cause the main gameplay (kill anything that moves) was dominating the morals.

_childDocuments_.review: So, to start off with - this game is really very fun! If you're into twin stick shooters, cyberpunk or action games then you will find plenty to like here. A note before I go on, the review is written after completion of the whole story and around 1/2 of the side quests (says just under 20h of play, but at least a couple of those were dead time with the game running in the background).Now to get to the nitty gritty. Contrary to what some people seem to think, this is NOT and ARPG and that is a absolutely a positive. You wont be finding loot drops and random stats here, this isn't Diablo with guns. I cannot quite express how happy I am to see a game in this day and age where there isn't a bland, number grinding endgame that everything works towards. This game has a campaign, unique weapons and armour, side content (that can be finished off after the credits) and a definitive end with a potential sequel hook. From start to finish of the campaigns 8 multi-part missions, you will be taken through the almost whole map, organically progress with levelling, items and powers until you reach the end with a battle that will use all your skills. For that alone, this game is worthy of praise.The gameplay loop is functionally just combat and getting-to-combat. There is a pretty diverse selection of weapons, but you will ultimately find a couple of guns and powers you like by midway through the game and end up using them while upgrading their stats. This isn't really an issue, and certain encounters in the game made me rethink my loadout, but largely there will be a comfort zone. Within that comfort zone, the shooting will be great! especially before you find amazing armour (I was getting the best loot near enough to the final level of the story), you will have to tactically position yourself, hipfire AND aim-fire various enemies while utilising various bits of cover. Theres a wide spectrum of enemies that won't let you facetank all the damage so combat sometimes gets frantic but is almost always fun. I personally hated the shield enemies, but I know why they're there. So a big thumb up for combat and gameplay. A quick mention about the story - its there, it provides good context, and is written and voiced well. Nothing to write home about here. This ain't Dostoyevskiy or Asimov, but it shouldn't be. Its a pulpy cyberpunk story that offers a good reason for your character to go and kill random enemies while visiting diverse sci-fi locations. No gripes here. As good as it needs to be, with no pretensions at something its not. Visually the game is stunning! The sounds are good, the music is fine (nothing special, but fits the game and the action). I have literally zero complaints about the aesthetics, other than when you find good armour, it usually doesn't match and your character ends up looking like an absolute clown. Not a huge deal, but I did end up using less effective items to prevent the goofy looks you could end up having. That this didn't prevent me from finishing the game is a good thing. So another thumb up for visuals and sound.Now, the game definitely isn't perfect. By the time I write this, many people will already have pointed out issues with DX12 and certain visual features. All I can say is, read up on the issues before making a decision about the game. I personally didn't try it in DX12 to avoid issues and had no visual problems whatsoever. On a 1070 and an i5 6600k, this game ran on a mix of Ultra and High (1080p) at a stable fps >60. The only times it dropped (literally for a second) were with very congested fights where explosions, "cyber" effects and more than a dozen enemies were on screen (final fight for eg). Equally, I encountered 3 crashes to desktop over my whole playthrough. From a non-technical side, the biggest issue I felt was the walking around and certain checkpoints. There are a couple of thematically appropriate fast travel methods in the game and they work perfectly fine. However, some missions mean you have to get to certain locations where a fast travel point is still far off. Especially by the end of the game, the running around took up more time than I'd care for. This isn't as much an issue early on, as encounters and exploration are fun. However, it starts to drag on a bit. Equally, checkpoints were a mystery more than anything to me. When not entering and exiting locations, I cannot for the life of me say where a checkpoint is made. Some are done before bosses. Some are done before bosses + a mob encounter. Some seem random. Don't know. All I can say is, some felt very much ok, while others were rather annoying. I can also see some issues in a lot of the weapon variety being somewhat wasted as it feels like certain guns are flat out linear upgrades to others. That is a very small issue, but bears mentioning. Overall - this was probably the most fun with a game I've had in ages. The fact that I could finish it in roughly 10-15h (including most sidequests) while levelling up a character to have a complete beast by the end is amazing. Low commitment, high return. With how fun the combat was, I will likely replay this game at some point and it lends itself very well to a "simple, but exciting" type of game you can relax on by shooting baddies. I can heartily recommend this with the caveat that people check the state of performance at time of buying (though you can't go wrong with steam offering refunds if it doesn't work well). Great game, especially for the price. Hope to see a sequel/expansion.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun concept, beautifully realized aesthetic, and the mechanics seem competent, so it's too bad the main quest is broken and refuses to spawn the enemies necessary to progress during what is only the second main mission of the game. I'm sure it's not directly the devs' fault, but it speaks poorly of any testing that was done if there's a gamebreaking bug in the second mission of the main quest-line on release. The inevitable comparisons to Cyberpunk are especially grating considering that with that particular title, despite the frequent graphical glitches and other issues at launch, I was still able to progress the story.Revised after restarting: The world is by far the best part, though the combat can feel adequately punchy and  the story is engaging enough when carried by the characters. Parts feel under-polished which is understandable given the small development team, and taken as a whole, it is a far more impressive experience than a good number of AAA titles that have come out recently. Though the backtracking can grow a bit tedious, it's not too out of line for what is typical of the genre, so if this seems like the kind of game you'd enjoy, it's definitely worth the time invested.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on a predominantly co-op experience.This game does a decent job creating the atmosphere through visuals and music.  Leveling and gearing up also feels reasonably rewarding, but that is the extent of what was done right with this game.The map is horrendous.  It's exceptionally difficult, relative to other games, to really interpret where things actually exist in the world without spending far too much time scanning.The minimap makes it near impossible to even see where your teammate is located.  It's just some faint shadow, and if said shadow was too far away, you'd have no way of determining general direction without popping open the map itself.There are numerous instances of invisible terrain blocking movement.Keybindings reset on multiple occasions.  Fine for those that use default, not so much for those that do not.The real deal breaker is that missions just seem to arbitrarily break.  Missions will show no objectives, but clearly haven't been completed.  Kill missions will fail to actually spawn in required creatures to enable completion.  Zone elevators refusing to operate, completely blocking progression of both main story missions and side missions alike.  There is no game to be had if the missions themselves frequently fail to function.I recommend against buying the game until the bugs are addressed, particularly if you intend on playing with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: There are games I understand, and there are games that I don't. Especially when it comes to combat. This is one of those that I don't get. Immediately at the beginning I find myself attacked by ten enemies all at the same time, and my handgun barely makes a dent in them. I die. Wow, what an introduction.I don't enjoy combat. It's not an interesting challenge. So I avoid games that are based on it. That's why I clicked "ignore" on this game on Steam. But then I found it for less than €2.5... And since cyberpunk usually is a favorite genre/setting for me, I just had to try it. So I did. For 15 minutes or so.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros. 1. If you enjoy the cyber punk aesthetic,The world literally feels as though your in ghost in the shell or Bladerunner. The visual art direction and the sound direction draw you into the world.Fantastic art design by the art directer and artist on this project.2.A wide selection of armours to customize the look of your character.It has transmogrification so you look like how you want to look.3.Good take on the isometric shooter game play as you can duck behind cover and evade.4.Many different weapons and skills to chose from for customizing you character leading to different game play types.5.The variety of the enemies were great.The game has a cover system however enemies actively try to keep you from just hunkering down and shooting.Firstly by behaviour trying to flank you and secondly by enemy  design some enemies  are shorter so cannot be hit by firing over barricades,some enemies fire mortars to flush you out ect .Cons.1.Story is just okay.2.The camera angle some times causes problems but only in minor sections in the game.3.Although there is lot of variety in weapons and skills to use.There are a certain sub set of skills and weapons that are clearly superior to the rest of them.Conclusion.If you like cyber punk,customization and great shooting action but don't mind an average story this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a weird one for me. I recommend the game on sale with the knowledge that there are crashes. I played the game on the steam deck so that may or may not have added to it. The main things I want to touch on are the things I feel this game is missing or what doesn't work.First thing, I don't like the healing mechanic. The health pick ups being the main source of healing just feels off to me. Yes there are active abilities to help mitigate the issue, but they feel like half measures at best. I would have preferred having a main healing resource with charges or a cool down. Leaving the main source of healing to be RNG makes the early game feel artificially difficult. The game finally felt properly balanced after I had gotten the healing aura.The next thing that felt off is the lack of a sprint. The maps feel a touch too big for the game's own good and the reload locations a bit too far away from where I died. This wouldn't feel as off if the dodge roll was unlimited use. But with two uses only, using the roll as a pseudo sprint is painful. It's not like there is no more room for controller players. There are two sticks and one goes unused. Map grenade to right stick and sprint to left. The shotguns are my last point of contention. They feel strange in a way that is hard to describe. The spread feels a bit too random and too wide. The low ammo and slow reloads feel like they should be enough to make the shotguns feel right. Shotguns always get put into crowd control/area weapon when I feel they should be single target high damage.Other than that the game feels decent to play and looks good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great ARPG for the value. The world is so vibrant. If you enjoy the Cyberpunk aesthetic this game is a must have. There are currently some bugs to deal with but nothing game breaking. Weapon skins and Shirts don't currently save from game to game. There is a busted elevator. I also had an issue where enemies would just not spawn. I reloaded and it fixed the problem. Another issue is that it's hard to tell which quests may be gate-locked by the main quest line. Sometimes that really hinders your progress.The guns are fun to use. A decent amount of variety. Be sure to search the nooks and crannies of the maps to find stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: While it might not be the most polished game released this year, The Ascent provides solid and satisfying gameplay with incredible cyberpunk visuals and an atmospheric soundtrack. The core gameplay loop could be seen as repetitive, especially with the lack of randomly generated loot - however, Neon Giant absolutely nailed the controls, resulting in the game not feeling stale no matter how long you’ve been playing for. I’m left hopeful for a sequel that expands on all aspects of the first.If you’re in any way interested in cyberpunk worlds, isometric RPGs, and/or satisfying gameplay, The Ascent may be worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews. Never been that great at expressing how I feel about something - however I feel I need to praise The Ascent and the devs on such a fun and engaging cyberpunk action RPG. This is what Cyberpunk 2077 should have been. I won't spoil anything but do yourself a favour and explore! you will find badass weapons if you do! - My favourite gun so far is one that shoots exploding bullets!The game play is fun and engaging keeping me wanting to move forward and try and find different weapons and augments to see what else is out in this game! 10/10 would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absurdly good for the on-sale price point. Hidden depth to the mechanics, large variety of weapons and builds, excellent balancing (at least, so far on Hard). But especially I cannot believe the detail the dev team (11 people, I think) put into the world. The ambiance is excellent, the world feels alive, the story is well thought out. It's one of the best examples of sci-fi large scale cyberpunk worldbuilding I can think of offhand, all half-hidden away in a top down, twin stick style diablo-esque hybrid. But since most people are just here for the murder: this game has really good murder. Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, I really do. It has great gfx, interesting story back story and in many ways (though on a isometric 3D level) this game shares a little bit of game mechanics from Flashback, for any of you reading this that came from the 80's and 90's. _childDocuments_.review: A newcomer to the twin stick shooter genre of games (besides a small but intense run-in with Robotron: 2084 at an old arcade), I can say I'm very pleasantly surprised with the way this game turned out, how it plays, how it looks and sounds; everything about it is a complete treat. Neon Giant came together and produced this incredibly addictive twin stick shooter with action R.P.G. elements sat in a futuristic dystopian and grim Hellworld experiencing the collapse of a tyrannical, subjugating all-encompassing corporation known as The Ascent Group. It is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beautiful.With only around four hours into the game at the time of this writing (and definitely more to come, assuredly), I'm completely absorbed in the action in this game, which while sometimes spaced out between segments of peace and quiet only makes me want to fight even more. Engagement in combat in this game is extremely exciting and gets the adrenaline flowing, and interwoven with the setting and the story? It's going to keep you pressing on for more combat, and more combat, and even still more combat beyond that. The twin stick approach to the gameplay keeps the action fluid at all times and feels completely stable in its control; it never feels like a nuisance or like a stupid gimmick that the game is based on.The game plays a lot like the 2016 entry for Doom: keep your ass moving or you're going to get shot and die. That's largely responsible for how fast-paced and crazy this game can get, but with how the controls feel so naturally you're not going to be bothered by it. If anything, you won't be able to wait to get back at it. Much of the world can be learned about by talking to people, reading datapads, engaging with the environment around you, much like Deus Ex: Human Revolution. A lot of parallels can be drawn to that game and several others of this future, cyberpunk kind of game. And trust me, even now the world's pretty damn deep to me.The R.P.G. elements of the game keep the action even fresher and as you unlock more and more upgrades for your character, the more exciting the combat potential becomes as you're able to choose from all the classic R.P.G. stats that affect your mobility, your H.P., how you handle weapons, your critical hits, all fitted specifically for this setting and the gameplay. Given the combat, you're never going to feel like you're needlessly grinding at all and even if you actually are sat on doing that, it's not like you're going to be bored at all getting those levels up.Graphically, the game's just beautiful. It's a cluttered mess of a world all polished with tender loving care. There's garbage all over the streets, statues and living settlements in varying states of decay, everything is filthy and grimy, the cities are neon-lit Hellscapes and it's exactly everything you could ever expect and desire in a game about a futuristic dystopian nightmare. For you ray-tracing nerds, this game will support that too. Accompanying the visuals of this game is a soundtrack that further supports the setting, a soundtrack so good that I'm thankful that they put it up for purchase (and rest assured, I bought that too). If I had to compare the soundtrack to anything at all, it's very reminiscent of Deus Ex: Human Revolution's. It fits, perfectly.The game's extremely stable and in my experience as of right now it's only crashed once, which was likely to happen given all the processes I had running in the background at the time, so that's not really the fault of the devs. It runs extremely smoothly, well over 60 frames-per-second even on the highest settings, which keeps the action flowing exactly where you need it to be at.There's also the option for multiplayer (which I haven't tried yet), but that's definitely going to be something I'm always going to keep an open lobby for when I play this game because playing this game with people has to be a blast, since it's already so addictive as a single player game. Though it's important to note that as I'm writing this, multiplayer seems dead in the water. Not sure what that's about.Let's break this down easily. The map system's a little messed up but you can get used to it or, if you remember Dead Space at all, there's a button that you can press that will show you a path to your waypoint that's kind of like that. So that's kind of a solved problem but many people might like to use the map system. It's one of those 3D things so, use it at your own peril.Second, the battle music can get a little old at times but it's kind of hardly noticeable since you're going to be blasting people in the face and stealing their ♥♥♥♥. It's something I actually noticed as an afterthought after so many combat sequences; "Is that really the only combat music there is?" Being that I'm so few hours in, I've heard some boss tunes but that's about it for now. Maybe it varies as time goes on. It's still killer music, I just sort of wish there was more variety in the mix.Third, I'm going to get into the H.U.D. It's a small rectangle in the bottom-right corner of the screen that has a lot of vital information on it: your health, your energy, ammo, level, experience points to next level gauge, what weapons you have equipped, and what power-ups you can deploy. For a game whose action is on the center stage, it would be nice to be able to scale this information in a much more user-friendly way rather than me having to glance downward and risk some unnecessary damage or, God forbid, a death.Fourth, possibly finally depending on when I finish this damn game or if I find something new:This isn't really a gripe but this is the kind of game that's begging for a survival mode and a deathmatch mode paired with its single-player and multiplayer experiences. The controls, weaponry and set-up are  for it. It's too good an opportunity to waste.Taking a chance on these devs and The Ascent definitely proved to pay off in spades, and I don't recommend sleeping on this one or ignoring it. This game's a love letter to the cyberpunk genre and it's definitely a critical entry into said genre. This game is kick-ass and it brings a nice breath of fresh air into any stagnating Steam library. The devs clearly loved what they were doing and they had the talent to pull it off, and their effort amounted to this game. Pretty badass. Yeah, it's got the typical cyberpunk tropes but what do you expect?Anyway,Acidmeadow approved.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only been able to play solo so far as I haven't convinced any friends to get it, so I can't comment on multiplayer.However, eight hours in so far? I'm having a blast. It scratches a very specific set of itches:-Cyberpunk setting-Action RPG with an emphasis on movement and shootingLooks absolutely gorgeous, fights are fast and fun, guns are great, powers so far are great. That said, some things to consider coming into it.-This isn't a large scale looter shooter. You won't find 10 variants of the same gun. Guns are static in stats, but can be upgraded with resources you find. Armor is also static.-No classes, you build yourself up based on skill point investment, and what equipment you use, which consists of two main guns, a "tactical" weapon (Grenades, healing fields, etc), and two Augs that can include things like bionic punches and nanoswarms that make things violently explode on death.The gameplay loop itself is pretty simple: Kill things. Get money and EXP. Use those to make yourself tougher. Rinse, repeat. Simple, but it works.You won't find something overly deep here, but what you will find is fast, satisfying gunplay with cool cyber powers and an beautiful setting that makes it hard for me to believe only 11 people worked on this. Seriously, it looks amazing, environment wise.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I go on, I do believe The Ascent is worth buying because of its incredible cyberpunk setting and engaging twin-stick shooter gameplay. That being said...The Ascent is a weird game to review. The setting is incredibly "authentic" cyberpunk, the music and art design all support that feeling, the story is a mostly-compelling cyberpunk "low life high tech" story, and the twin-stick shooter gameplay is decent. All of the individual pieces are there for the game to be a truly incredible cyberpunk experience there to assuage the pain of a certain other game from late last year.The problem is that none of these different positives work well together.The incredible setting serves are very very impressive wallpaper and background noise to a twin-stick shooter that seems to be humming along to a Doom soundtrack instead of synthwave music. There is no way for the player to interact with the setting beyond "shoot" or "accept quest/ask setting related questions", which means there is no melee barring 2-3 cyber abilities, no hacking beyond a system which mostly serves as a glorified "master key", no conversation/talking your way out of combat, and no cyber augmentation beyond 2 "power" (active) and "modification" (passive) slots.It really is a pity because this game has such an awesome world that was right on the edge of greatness, but none of the individual choices in setting, mechanics, or game type "played into" one another.All things considered, like I said at the beginning, I still recommend this game because the setting is awesome, the gameplay is good, and the ambiance is incredible, it's just a pity they didn't come together into an even more incredible whole.PS: I haven't tried multiplayer yet, but I only ever had 1 CTD through my 20 hours of playing, so I can't confirm the experiences of other players with instability.

_childDocuments_.review: It took me almost 12 hours to complete and the only word I can use to sum up this game is exhausting. I had put off playing this game for the longest time as I heard really mixed reviews, but the aesthetic pulled me in to playing it and I can't begin to express how disappointing it was.The setting and initial introductions to features make the early game seem promising, but after getting to the second hub tier of the game, it just highlights the lack of thought that went into the design around some of the core systems. Travelling - You have an option introduced for fast travelling, but this does nothing to stop the tedious back and forth you have to do to get between areas and the initial quest givers. The quest marking system may as well not have been in the game at all (this might have been preferable!), and the 'map' doesn't even overlay properly to where you are actually going, just showing off a vague shape of the area you will be in. If you want to go do a quest on hub level 1 after being given a quest on hub level 3, you have to go through two separate elevator rides to do it (because presumably due to poor planning, the elevators can only go between two floors! Thought this changes in the penultimate mission, as you are almost laughably given an express elevator that takes you right back to the top level, but it isn't marked, so you can miss it entirely), and because the movement starts dragging on you after a few hours of playtime, it makes the journey between quests and zones all the more boring. For example, after completing a main mission I noticed some more side missions had become available, and then I travelled from the hub town, to the elevator, then through another area to another elevator, then through another area to reach the small quest area, then leave. This was so bad that I gave up on doing side quests once I saw how it was never going to improve. It almost felt like a piss take when one of the ending missions has you trekking from the top layer all the way down to the bottom, once again, to have your quest giver say 'well humans need exercise so treat it like another perk' as if the developers were having one last laugh at making you slog through their unforgivably poorly designed zones.Combat - The return of top down dual-joystick directional combat I thought was a fantastic idea, and I am glad to see it make a comeback, but the sheer frustration of enemy design makes this feature feel more like a hindrance than a good system. When you reach a specific point in the game, the enemies stop being human and shift over towards robots, and upon your first encounter with them, you would be forgiven to have thought that there were specific damage types to combat specific enemy types. This clearly could not be further from the truth, in using ballistic, energy or heat guns, the robots and late-game mobs all turn into frustrating bullet sponges. The slog of getting through robot battles forced me to cheese my way down a dual mini-gun focus fire build to just melt the bosses before the combat dragged on too long. This was spurred on by the mechanical spider fight that I hope anyone who has played will understand how utterly frustrating it is to fight against. The end zone had felt like such a slog, I ended up running through most of the mobs until I died enough times to set myself in a different spawn point to avoid tediously clearing zones again. On top of this, when you are fighting enemies, you will have enemies spawning behind you out of completely cleared areas, just appearing out of nowhere, and if you are already fed up with clearing the mobs each time, you will get even more annoyed having a few more to contend with appearing from the ether behind you to muck up your time. Story - I honestly couldn't after playing this for 12 hours give you a notable or even likeable character from this entire story. Your character has no voice lines, which is a perfectly acceptable thing to do, but then with every main story line character introduced, I was almost screaming for my character to have the option to tell them to shut up. Working your way up the tiers of the building you are in doesn't feel rewarding, there are no noticeable changes to your characters story, and you feel more like a side character than an involved and participating lead role. The 'mega-corporations in a hyper-capitalist futuristic society' trope has been told so much better so many times before that this lacklustre attempt to make 'yCorp' or 'Ascent Group' or any of the other forgettable factions of the game seem interesting, falls flat and hard on it's face. This is compounded by the lack of any real world building behind the story. You are told this is who you are, this is the world name, this is the reason you are there. Then proceeds to give no meaningful development on any of these for the entire breadth of the journey. The end fight made me laugh as I truly thought it couldn't get any worse when mysterious space tentacles appeared through a wormhole opened by the end boss. Not only could you not use the breathtaking combat you have to endure to deal damage to it, you have to interact with four terminals to... do damage? I saw this story going in so many different directions, and it felt like they chose the most boring of all of them for this. All of this, and not even a mention of the restrictive camera field of view, enemies engaging you off screen, focused and forced areas of view that just make it jarring to enjoy. Not a mention of the bugs of duplicated NPCs sat on top of each other, other NPCs knocking into you during cut scenes, being damaged during conversations by randomly spawning enemies etc. I didn't experience any of the major bugs that other people have been reporting, so it may be a fixed issue, but there is enough to complain about without adding those on top. In a game where you have to progress upwards, find out reasons for the world being the way it is, and have some semblance of a fulfilling ending, play another game where the main character doesn't speak, Stray. You will have a much better experience and time playing that genuinely interesting game than this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very repetitive and somewhat boring. It follows a very linear path both on map and character levels. [ENEMIES]Enemies are always either too low level or too high level for you. To have an enjoyable experience you have to strictly follow the linear path laid in front of you. Even then, the missions recommended levels do not match. When it says 18, expect level 22 enemies.[LEVEL GAP]The gap between your level and enemy levels  leaves no place for exploration or deviating from the linear path. You kill enemies below your level in one shot, and you die from 2 shots from enemies slightly above your level. And yes, I have upgraded my weapons and wear current linear armor.[COMBAT]I find the cover function only enjoyable with lower level enemies. Same or higher level enemies leave you no time to use covers laying around all over the place. Enemies will rush you (and they run slightly faster than you), and SPAWN on you. That is the most disappointing feature of combat.EVERY encounter is this: You see a red dot on minimap, you engage, some enemies will get behind cover, some will rush you, and some will SPAWN (usually 2-3) behind you. Even though you cleared behind you, if you run back to evade or find cover, you can always expect enemies to appear right before your eyes. Other enemies will spawn during an encounter, some have the effort of coming out of houses or buildings, but most of the m will just appear out of thin air.[MOVEMENT]This game makes you run all over the map with no running function (yes I do use taxi when I can). I find myself using the evade function non-stop to get places, and even then it feels way too long to get there.Combat movement: The only thing I have to say on this is you will get stuck often in corners and props all the time. Getting stuck in a prop surrounded by enemies because you tried dodging.[BUGS]It has some bugs, but I haven't found that many game-breaking ones. Sometimes the map will have icons that shouldn't be there or icons will float and move with your mouse. I have found myself stuck in a mech, unable to move until I died.Optimization: Badly optimized, running on an AMD Radeon 6900 XT, I often get lag spikes. Sometimes dropping to 30 ish FPS in combat. I have tried running it in DX12 and it results in a lag fest.

_childDocuments_.review: Only SP play here.It's a gorgeous looking game/world and the potential for almost unlimited content is here and I really hope the Neon Giant will continue to work on this game BUT the release version have some problems that need to be resolved before I can recommend it to anyone.Bugs are to be expected, no game is without them at release. I did not encounter any totally game-breaking ones although some of them are maddening like selling all duplicate items resolving in not getting any money.Unbalance - I guess that is to be expected too when you are making co-op games but SP is plagued with unbalance especially during boss fights and the final mission is frustrating to the point you HAVE TO change the difficulty to easy to be able to finish the game. The game itself is trying to resolve the unbalance by lowering the number of enemies and/or their level whenever you get back to where you died. Also, there is no death penalty, at least I did not spot any.RPG here is... underwhelming. You are a silent hero without any say in what's happening or what you are saying so do not expect any decision making here other than what loadout of Weapons/Armor/Augments you will use. Some Augments are totally useless too and you are restricted to only two active and two passive (modules) same goes with weapons and armour although that may be dependent on your build and I am not totally sure that it does as the character attributes here influence things that are, again, often useless like stagger resistance.All in all, it's not a bad game just don't expect too much from it at least not now until it's bug-free and with some quality of life improvements. It took me 17h for completing the main storyline with some side missions (there is plenty left) so overall for its price it's a good bargain.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cool, flashy title with some great combat, but it's weighed down by some of the worst pacing I've ever experienced.PROS:*  Striking visuals and environmental design give pretty much everyone who plays this the "wow" factor*  Great sound - music, combat, atmosphere and voice are all great.*  Combat is pretty fun.  There are a lot of different weapons and they each feel and sound different.  You're encouraged to switch things up by swapping weapons based on the type of damage they do; there's a rock-paper-scissors damage model.*  Decent enemy variety.*  The world is really cool.  It feels alive, and the worldbuilding surrounding the way it's organized is pretty interesting.*  It's fully co-op (more on that in the cons section)*  I could summarize everything with one word: style.  This game has it in abundance.CONS:*  Absolutely horrendous levels of back tracking.  Just playing through the campaign I've had to run back through THE ENTIRE WORLD on several occasions!  I'm not even joking - I just completed my first mission on the highest level of the Arcology (I'm a couple missions in to the final act) and I just had to run back down to the Deepstink (the starting level).  This is the second time I've come back down here for a main quest, and side quests (which I'm outright ignoring at this point) have you do the same.  You can't just fast travel through them, by the way (taxis and subways exist but they're only to sparsely populated points of interest) - there is always a degree of traversal involved.  I understand building this big, beautiful world and wanting the players to see it, but I would have gone exploring and revisiting places on my own because the world is so wonderful.  With the number of times I've been forced to run back through everything I now feel it's overstayed its welcome and I'm eager to wrap this game up to be done with it, which is a damn shame.*  The map is annoying to read at times, which exasperates the aforementioned issue.*  The currency you use to upgrade your weapons is hard to come by, which means you basically want to choose a couple weapons you like and dump all of your upgrade points in to them.  The P9000 is what I chose, because that thing is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incredible.*  Bugs.  There are quite a few, and they often times result in me thinking a particular system is broken.  It can be things as trivial as dialogue being incredibly quiet in a conversation to as bad as waypoints disappearing or not rendering on the map.  Multiplayer had a host of annoyances which caused my friends to give up on playing this co-op and stick to single player (the biggest example would be the big cinematic moments when you walk in to a new area where the camera pans over the region - every NPC would t-pose for my friends, which completely ruined the experience).

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with what everyone's been saying. This game's buggy. Not annoyingly so in my opinion. There are others who lost their progress and make sure you get to Cluster 13 (about 30 minutes to an hour or so in) before you play co-op since you can have your missions completely reset. I don't have the final achievement for some reason and experienced several moments where missions glitched out. The game could've used a small amount of time further in development.That being said, this is actually the second time I've played through this game and I felt it was a good chance to give the game a review. I initially played this on gamepass and enjoyed it so much that I bought it on Steam to ensure I'd get the soundtrack. The combat, presentation and music are all stellar. Voice acting is surprisingly good and the lore of the world is pretty interesting and underused for a typical cyberpunk setting. The actual setting itself is far more interesting than the way the story itself plays out but this game does just as good of a job being a mindless shooting gallery.There are intense spikes in difficulty here and there with some mission designs being questionable. The "hunker down" segments in particular can get grueling and they throw some unfair enemies at you occasionally. The flip side of these difficult fights is that you'll proceed to find more and more overpowered weapons as you progress until you plateau in difficulty again. In a lot of ways, this game feels pretty old school and I really like it for that. It seems the Steam version of this game both runs better and has more options than the gamepass version but I'd recommend trying it there if you're unsure. This isn't an amazing game or anything but it's a lot of fun and that's all you need sometimes. That and the satisfaction of exploding rival factions into a fine red mist.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun shooter with BEAUTIFUL scenery/setting. Difficulty isn't too bad, I died about 6 times. The gun upgrade system is unique - even if you sell the gun, when you get another of the same type, it remembers the upgrades. _childDocuments_.review: This review is based on 100% completion and 23.4 hours of gameplay.Do I recommend this game? Absolutely! To be honest, I had low expectations for this game, but I was pleasantly surprised. If I'm being honest, this is the experience I wish Cyberpunk had when it first launched. The visuals are stunning and far exceeded my expectations, while the sound design is exceptional and perfectly complements the setting. Yes, the gameplay is sweet and simple, but I found it very enjoyable. Using various weapons and abilities throughout the game kept me well entertained. The game is small and can be completed in a single playthrough, so waiting for a sale is always the best option, but if you can't wait, the full price ($50 here) isn't too bad for what you get, in my opinion.The game truly transports you into a new universe, making you feel as if you are exploring a bustling, vibrant city. The main area is lively, filled with activity that immerses you completely in its world. The sound design stands out with its dynamic music, which enhances different areas of the game, and the dialogue delivery is impressively clear and engaging. Ambient sounds and in-game audio effects are top-tier, contributing to a rich, immersive experience. Additionally, the art design is spectacular, with stunning visuals that just captivate. Gameplay is not just fun but thrilling, making each session enjoyable and memorable.These are all the things I noticed while playing through the game. Nothing listed here was anything more than a major inconvenience.

_childDocuments_.review: God-tier art direction, really delivers the cyberpunk dystopia like no other game that I have played (does so  better than Cyberpunk 2077, for instance), and makes me nostalgic for '90s sci-fi and '90s isometric PC games. The setting feels quite unique for the genre, and is  cyberpunk in the sense that this is a world that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks to live in, everyone is a lowlife struggling to survive, and violence is rampant and normalized. Unlike Cyberpunk, this game really wears its themes, and doesn't stupidly try to shoehorn modern 2020s/2010s culture in for reasons of "please buy this game, dear young person who is not into this genre"; rather, it shows the anachronistic fantasy from the '80s and '90s in all its glory (or complete opposite thereof).But all that GOTY-material potential is hampered by the game being, uuh, essentially a twin stick shooter and not much of an RPG - despite having world-building like that of an RPG; lacking refinement on gameplay as well as level and encounter design; and having a lot of UI that is just too difficult to read. This is a game in which some of its individual parts are of divine quality, but the sum of those with the other, more amateurish parts, doesn't come together quite nicely.Still, it's worth experiencing if you have the patience to overlook the flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a shining beacon in a genre full of sub-par crap that barely merit participation trophies.The most important aspect of any game for me is ALWAYS the actual game-play.  The combat in this game is so incredibly well designed that the incredible aspects of art, sound, and level design seem more like icing on the cake.  It's a fun and unique experience with a lot of thought put into the RPG elements rather than copying traditional isometric action-RPG tropes that almost always lead to uninspired meta-builds.  I haven't played the game enough to see if this changes in the late-game, but I can tell that the RPG elements are meant to augment the action rather than replace it like so many other games do.  I can't speak to the longevity of these design decisions in the context of "end-game" content, but it's making the journey much more interesting.The art, level, and sound design are solid.  The world is immersive and believable (better than other well-known cyberpunk games, at least).  Some of the story, dialogue, and text/UI elements could use some polish, but it's often forgivable for how hard they nailed the feel of the cyberpunk genre.  Oddly enough, some of the previously praised level design can also be difficult or annoying to navigate, and there are times when the levels seem either too crowded or too open.  I definitely found myself losing interest in traversing non-combat zones until quick-travel was unlocked.  Walking simulators suck, even if they're in a badass cyberpunk arcology.  Bugs are prevalent in the COOP portion of the game, which probably just needs some time to fix up.  Most of my time has been spent in single-player (a bug free experience for me so far), but in the hour or so that I joined some friends, there were some pretty serious bugs.  I'm hoping this gets fixed in time, but the actual COOP was fairly well done and enjoyable.  I'm very satisfied with my purchase, and incredibly impressed with this developer.  I sincerely hope that this game gets more fans, and they are able to expand on this title and any future endeavors that they want to try.  They deserve the opportunity with the incredible quality of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Visually this game is gorgeous, a grand spectacle that oozes cyberpunk grit every where you walk.  Every inch makes you want to stare and wonder about it's history.  The problem is that for all of it's atmosphere it serves no greater purpose, it's just a static world in which can look but not touch.I hope you like walking and spamming the waypoint key, because that is what you will be doing the majority of the time.Gameplay wise you have a half-decent twin stick shooter.  The cover and height system is clever, though the longer I played the less I ended up making any use of it.They attempt to give you some loose RPG like elements, just very watered down.  This isn't like Diablo and isn't a looter shooter, and as a result the reward for playing felt hollow.After a few hours of playing I decided this game wasn't for me.  The game feels like it does a lot of stuff well but end up being a game I have no reason to continue playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy this game, or download on Gamepass. Seriously.Quick: Is it worth the money? Yes.Quick Review: 8/10. As far as theme, atmosphere, and the story goes, totally awesome. The game world is amazingly beautiful, and the devs 100% have my eyes locked on screen, all over the screen, every waking moment. I actually took a two hour tour through one area just to impress myself with the visuals.Other than that, fairly average gameplay, twin-stick shooter (similar to Diablo 3, Inquitor, and other ARPGs).Graphics are seemingly amazing, and every bit the cyberpunk world you'd expect. This is, visually, the world Cyberpunk 2077 should have been. Story works fine. Blood and gore from combat looks good. Combat overall is quick, and there are a bunch of different weapons to choose from but you can only equip 2 at a time, as well as tactical abilities (mostly grenades, one at a time), and two augments (Cyberpunk Augs, from a big punchy fist, to missiles rocketing out your spine to drop on to foes. Big lasers, explosive machine gun bullets, tesla rifles and summoning robot spiders to explode upon your foes! What's not to like?Is it worth 30$? Heck yeah. I'd have paid 50$ for it and not felt a drop of remorse. This game is visually amazing. _childDocuments_.review: Art wise, this game does everything right. Atmosphere is great, music is awesome. The cyber-noire aesthetic is just marvelous and while hard to navigate (we'll come back to that) the world looks gorgeous. Neon lights, shining down on alien races milling in the streets, while under the constant shadow of a towering megacity rising around us.However, while the game is nice to look at and listen to, gameplay wise it does just about everything... alright. It's not always inherently bad and sometimes even shows a semblance of "good" in there.Combat feels nice and chunky. Enemies come at you in small groups, or big enemies come at you alone. At worst they are flanked by ads that aren't too tanky. Guns feel powerful and pack a punch. Until it doesn't. Out of nowhere, enemies come in armies. 10 at a time, three times in a row. Pairs of combat mechs taking an unreasonable amount of damage to kill, flanked by insanely hardy enemies. After that combat encounter... 5 enemies you can one-shot. If you don't get killed by the camera, which cannot turn and will sometimes hide enemies out of sight... as your character is off-center on the screen.Missions become incredibly similar. "go to [place], pick up data, kill [one or more enemies]" and any combination of those objectives. The plot is kind of boring and hard to follow and while the game looks great and interesting, most lore is dumped in text or dialogue without any interesting worldbuilding. Characters are forgettable, factions blend together. You'll see Yakuza samurai fighting side by side with maintenance bots and your average slum ganger.On top of this, missions become a slog. The world is big... and at the same time it's not. You'll go through certain areas time and again. And it's a long run. A long run through similar (good-looking) neon-clad streets, through groups of enemies that may or may not end up being a small country's worth of combatants or such a small nuisance that their placement is entirely pointless. Add onto this that you can unlock sidemissions before the main quest allows you to access certain areas. The doors open, but the prompt doesn't appear. Then there's hacking doors. There's not really anything to it. Push a single button on your keyboard and the game's arbitrary number will decide whether you can pass or not. No keys, no puzzle, no skills. Just waiting till the game allows you to continue.All in all, this game is a flawed 'it's alright' twin-stick shooter. After 9 hours, I am getting achievements only 1/3rd of players have. It's sad to see the drop-off, but I understand why. If you like isometric twin-stick shooters, pick it up on sale. It deserves a completely neutral rating if it were up to me. Despite all the flaws listed above, I didn't hate my time with it so far. Maybe I will even come to finish it. As for now, this game is not worth full price and feels like it is too big for its britches. Hopefully the studio learns and gets the funding and team to make their next game all it can be.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS REVIEW WILL CONTAIN SPOILERSPlayed on hard and singleplayerSo now that I've beaten the game and finished all but one side quest simply because it is literally impossible to complete in my play through, I can now write a review more focused on the several aspects in this game. Good stuff goes first, bad stuff comes later, and other comments.GoodGraphically wise, this game is beautiful. If I didn't follow stuff about gaming, and you told me this was Cyberpunk 2077, I would've believed you. Atmosphere is great, it really depicts a dystopian vibe really well, especially as you note the differences between the tower tiers and zones.Weapon sound and design is great. The weapons sound like they pack a punch and they are pretty unique. I tried pretty much most of the weapons and while i only used at maybe 5 of the 15+ ish guns, mainly because of my build, I would for sure use other weapons had I built differently.Voice acting is solid. The main characters that you interact with throughout the story give you a sense of personality and not some monotonous drone, although the side quests talk in basically The Sims language.Skills in this game are amazing. They have unique looking effects, all perform differently and utilize the build that you focus your character on. My favorite are the Homing MIM and Neutron Beam.Armor design is really well done and have unique appearances. There are armors that go well together if you're going for looks rather than stats.Music is a banger.BadThe map is useless outside of locating chests. The map fits the cyberpunk aesthetic, but it is so poorly design function wise that it is counterproductive. You have a hard time discerning if a chest is above, below, on the other side of a wall that it basically pads time.The game uses a checkpoint system. There is no manual saving, nor do I think there should be since you don't have any choices outside of saying "yes" or "no" to accepting a side quest. However, it gets incredibly frustrating when you die and get sent all the way back to the entrance to the zone itself, especially when you make it 3/4th of the way. On top of this, the game is incredibly inconsistent whether it decides to respawn all the enemies on the way before you died, to outright making them nonexistent. When you die, you also lose all of your tactical charge which is a huge factor when playing. There are 4 ways to recover health in this game: Safe zones, vending machines, enemy pick-ups, and tactical charges. Safe zones are usually pretty far from conflict so this is a no-go.Vending machines can be destroyed putting you out of luck unless you decide to go to the main menu and reload.Enemy pick-ups are RNG which is especially terrible because its by chance and also competes between health, energy, and tactical charges. On top of this, you can easily die in trying to move over to the pick-ups. You can even get to a point where you are barely alive so the solution is to get to one of the above methods or kill yourself.Finally the Revu-field which is one of the most expensive tacticals in the game at a whopping 1200 charge. For reference, the cheapest is 250 for the shockwave grenade. When enemies drop a tactical charge, it is only 100. Now unless you're spec'd into tactical sense or use tactical charge as a module, good luck trying to utilize this tactical because if you die, getting it back depends on a lot of luck as to whether enemies will drop tactical charges or you live long enough to use it because this tactical can also be destroyed.Combat is on a fence leaning over onto the negative side. While I did say the weapon designs are unique and sound good, I am baffled by how guns in this game can pack a decent punch but not enough to make it so enemies will be staggered and stop shooting at me momentarily, to the point where I could be unloading a 200 round minigun point blank into their face but they still have a semblance of sheer willpower to accurately launch a burst of rounds at me or come rushing at me with a tire iron, forcing me to dodge or if i am surrounded, die. Now before you out me for saying "well it's a game, and far from realistic!", this game features a stagger system already. However, the way its implemented is by requiring you to deal enough damage in order to stagger them. When fighting enemies around my level (- / + 3 levels), even with a max upgraded minigun, I can stagger them at most once, before the bar resets and they continue on their merry way to murder me. I would much prefer if the system was that they staggered after being hit after a certain amount of times, say 5 for humanoid enemies and 20 for the chonkier and heavier boys, before having a 5 second cooldown before another stagger can occur. 5 seconds may not sound like a lot, but with the pace in this game, it is a LONG time.There are two enemy types that stick out that are a big pain and makes me wonder why the developers thought they were a good idea. First is the Barrager, and the second is the Megarachnoid.The Barrager carries a minigun that is around 2 and a half size times larger than you, and he can obliterate you in seconds unless you find cover or stagger him in order to run away. However, the Barrager is usually never alone, so if he sees you, good luck trying to stick to cover because then you have to deal with enemies that will charge at you and flank you. When you get in cover, you must crouch and crouching slows you down IMMENSELY. While you're fending off the flankers, the Barrager if he isn't already just putting lead down range,WILL move to flank you and just turn you into goop. On top of this, they are incredibly tanky, it wasn't until I acquired the Homing MIM that I could reasonably take on the Barragers and the other goons at the same time. The Megarachnoid (I'll call him 'noid for short)is a giant heavily armor spiderbot equipped with a flamethrower that launches an infinite amount of pods that spawn spider drones that will kamikaze you and deals a whopping half a bar of health per drone. When you deal damage to these pods, it will trigger them to spawn, however the 'noid launches these pods in directly in front of itself so chances are you will end up hitting them in the process of trying to kill the 'noid. Now you can hack these pods so that they do nothing, but you have to be fairly close to the pods and 'noid in order to do so. An enemy that is extremely resistant to damage, can roast you alive in mere seconds, drops jihad drones at a rate of a man dropping turds after eating a bad batch of taco bell. Oh and there was usually a pair of them whenever i encountered them.OtherThe game has a bounty system where there is a named enemy that spawns with bonus health and damage that you can kill, pick up an item and sell it for money. This system is almost useless because there aren't differing tiers of bounties and you also don't get anything other than money. The amount of money you get per bounty is enough for a single taxi ride(1000 credits) anything worthwhile that you would want to buy is usually 30,000 credits or more. On top of this, the rate at which bounties spawn makes it only really worth doing, if they aren't in the way to a mission is just to save money on a taxi fee to a zone.Overall, I did find it enjoyable than I had problems with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I will divide this review in two separate sections; Single Player and Co-op.I go along the things I think are great and will name things I think can be done better of which some that desperately need to be fixed asap. TLDR: Great Single Player game, Co-op is stuck with too many game breaking bugs. Gets worse the more you progress co-op.::: SINGLE PLAYER CAMPAIGN :::▪ ▪ ▪ ▪ INITIALIZING CYBERWARE ▪ ▪ ▪ ▪▪ ▪ ▪ RECHARGING ENERGY  ▪ ▪ CHECKING FOR EXPLOITS    ▪ STARTING BLOOD PUMPWelcome to The Ascent.The single player has an amazing story and the cut-scenes, voice acting and overall cinematic features are all done amazingly well. The game really lets you play and feel like you're pretty much a Blade Runner in a dangerous and lively cyberpunk world. The story pulls you in greatly if you give it the chance. I say this because the most addictive part of the game is the combat itself. If you tend to lose attention to things quick and don't want to listen to each cut-scene or character voice-over, then you will skip these just to do the combat. The story isn't that long. As you can see I have played for 19 hours and that includes 3 hours of co-op game play. I have finished the single player campaign but even so, I enjoy to keep playing for quite a number of reasons. Below are a couple of points what make this game worth while:♠ Beautiful Scenery and Scening♠ Great Atmosphere & Great Voice Acting♠ Amazing characters♠ The details of this game will have you stopping mid-combat to admire♠ A decent variety of enemies♠ Decent difficulty♠ Single Player is bug-free as far as I know (I did not run into any bugs).♠ Different ways of building up your character.::: CO-OP CAMPAIGN :::▪ ▪ ▪ ▪ INITIALIZING CYBERWARE ▪ ▪ ▪ ▪▪ ▪ ▪ REFITTING CHARACTER  ▪ ▪ CHECKING FOR BUGS.... WARNING BUGS DETECTED!    ▪ STARTING ANGER MANAGEMENTWelcome to The Ascent - CO-OP CAMPAIGNWhen you go play this game online with your friends, be prepared that you will run into a lot of bugs.A lot more than when you play it in Single Player. As soon as you reach the first city, all the bugs that are annoying will start to happen. The bugs that I and my friends have run into are but not limited to:♦ Getting stuck in Cut-scenes (Annoying and freezes the game. Easy to fix by reloading game).♦ Save File gets corrupted (You will rage as you will need to start a new game).♦ After one of the first battles after discovering the first city, your picked up weapons, gadgets and such may randomly disappear and... they will NOT come back until you find them again. At this point in the game you don't have the money to simply buy them again so you're basically stuck with only a simple gun and no augmentations, no skills, no armor. ♦ Aiming the mouse suddenly stops working (Annoying but reload of save / game fixes this).All in all I give the game 7/10.Please fix your game breaking bugs before you create more content please.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A cyber punk themed simplified Diablo with insane graphics. Important to note that the game has a couple of crashes on co-op.Story: Probably the weakest aspect of the game as it doesn't manage to keep your interest for more than the first quarter of the game, and that's being generous since it all kinda blends together. I played the whole thing co-op and having all main protagonists be silent doesn't help. In short, your character arrives on the planet with what seems like a complete bs contract and ridiculous debts to pay, so you're basically the lackey of the company ''The Ascent''. After what seems like a few missions, things go sideways and you're now the lackey of another, bigger company. Still doing whatever they ask you to do. The time is obviously set in the future and the world is built vertically, so as you progress you go higher and you get to see the difference between low class and higher class.... Yeah there's not much to say regarding the story. Gameplay: What sets The Ascent apart from other dungeon crawlers is the fact you can crouch and/or shoot above your head. It allows to both shoot from cover and shoot at enemies which may be on higher, or lower, heights than you. It can also affect crits. It can be very interesting when you're fighting multiple enemies and need an edge, and does, in fact, allow for a more in depth combat experience if you're into that sort of thing. However it's important to note that while it works well, the game doesn't always take advantage of it and it sometimes just becomes a run and gun, which is also fine if you're into that sort of thing.Your loadout include Weapons, Armor, Augmentations and a technical. This will be your main customisation. I mean you can customise your character but it doesn't show THAT much (for you crazy tansmogs people, it's in this game too).Weapon, augmentations and technical are where I found the funner part of the gear. Armor was dull and pretty standard. Weapons all have infinite ammo, but that's fine since you need to reload and it doesn't impact the gameplay. You can improve your weapons with collectables to make each individual gun more powerful, but you might want to hold off until you find one you really like since they get more expansive after every improvement. There are also types of dmg which work better on some enemies, an easy example of this would be that robots take more dmg from electrical type weapons.Augmentations are basically like your powers (or magic if you prefer), you can only equip 2 at a time. They are very varied and pretty awesome looking so experimentation is key here. If I'm to give a lil' piece of my mind here, I would've wished for more HP regenerative augs since it seems the best one is easily to miss and can only be obtained from a sidequest. There are also a couple of passive slots where you can equip things like extra health regen on health pick ups, a different type of dodge, things like that.Technical is simply your grenade type slot, well... Kinda. I say grenade but you can easily put something else in there, like a stasis grenade, a drone, spider mines, or my favorite: a pocket mecha! There are many more and again, experimentation is great here. As you damage enemies both with your weapons and your augs it'll refill your technical and depending on what you put in there it can change the way you play significantly or turn the tide of the battle easily.As you level up you get 3 skill points and you can spend them in 8 different skills (each capped at 20). They all help with different aspects of your character so it's important to think on how to best spend your points depending on your playstyle, they may not be apparent right away but read carefully and it'll come to you.One more thing, camera is fixed. I heard there's a mod for this but I didn't look into it at all. Most of the time it won't bother you too much, but it may happen that you'll be getting shot from an enemy off the screen, so it's just that much more important to look at that lil' radar and use that cover. Armor, though randomly dropped, have static stats, so you can easily end up finding 10 times the exact same crappy armor and they just stack in your inventory.Graphics: All I can say is wtf. I've seen AAA games go all out on graphics and not look this good. While most of it is not interactive, it looks and feels amazing. A lot of effects happen during combat, ranging from some destructible environments to different types of screen distortion. The city looks crazy detailed, neon signs everywhere, RTX, lots of NPCs that don't even need to be there.... It can be a bit taxing on a PC and you sometimes wonder why it's even present in this title... But it's still a sight to behold. Audio: While the combat music might become somewhat repetitive, you can't really blame the game for that. I rarely play games that are set in a dystopian futuristic world so it all sounded pretty damn good to me. Guns sounded spot on too.An important sidenote is that the game was made by a small studio, and we're talking REAL small here, studios like this need encouragement, competition is good, after all.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game and it was nice. PROS:It is like Alien Shooter in it`s core, just pumped up to the max. And story is much better. Leveldesign is great, details and such - marvelous.Controls - adequate.CONS:Endgame needed. Or NG+. Or some different gamemodes. Or just modding tools, the gameworld is great it just lacks endgame content.Two achievements still bugged - Comprehensive and Flatliner. DX12 stil causes stuttering, Had 2 or 3 CTDs with DX12, reported them. On the other hand, DX11 runs great with ultra settings on my RTX 2080, 2560*1440. Key NPCs sometimes missing, have to reload save. Key events sometimes don`t start - have to reload save.And Co-Op --- it definitely requires some serious bugfixing. I DO NOT advise to join Co-Op in this state of game.OVERALL: Still, I really enjoyed this game. It is good and you will like it if you ever played Alien Shooter games to the end. All the CONS i mentioned - they don`t really break your ability to complete the game. It autosaves every 2-3 minutes, it seems, so you will not loose several hours of your gameplay.
