_childDocuments_.review: I have completed the campaign and side-quests, done some achievement hunting, and injected Snooze into my eyeballs.  I think I can talk about The Ascent now.: I recommend it.  If you love a William Gibson-esque dystopian future, the atmosphere and world of The Ascent will deliver.  It's kinda like Diablo and Deus Ex had a baby, and the soundtrack is great.The game tells a solid story, and the ending didn't happen where I expected it to.  There are enough NPCs to interact with and background people having conversations to make the arcology feel like an actual, living, functioning place.  The setting is well designed to tell the story of the Ascent Group and the future as it exists on Veles.You will get some info-dump fatigue, though.  Kira will show up and drop a LOT of words on you, which can be a little overwhelming.  I did like that Kira reprimands you for killing innocent bystanders, though the lack of any actual repercussions didn't stop me from being a psychopath sometimes.The version I was playing seemed to run buttery smooth, even on the Ultra settings and streaming on Discord.  I don't have an RTX card, so couldn't test that, but no performance issues to speak of, and the game is very pretty.Combat feels good, and while the game pretends to be isometric/2.5D, some of the dramatic camera moves really lend a cinematic quality to the game.Armor sets look cool, and seem more coherent than the cyber shabby-chic of other games.The alien designs are pretty neat, distinctive, and interesting, and really add to the flavor the arcology.Did I encounter bugs? Were some things weird? Yes.  I found that restarting the game occasionally helped.  I think there might be an issue with leveling, because I'd have a section where I was level 28 and the enemies were level 9 and still one-shotting me.  Then I'd restart the game, and suddenly all those level 9 enemies were just balloons full of blood.There are side-quests that say they're level 2 or 5, but you have to get past level 12 enemies to reach the quest area, or the area isn't open until you do a much higher-level quest, so the quest levels are at best suggestions, and at worst, uselessly misleading.The map is frustrating, because there are times when it shows a giant chasm or void that just isn't there.  Sometimes the best route to a goal will be via the Interlink, but the HUD icons will take you the long way instead.  Don't trust the navigation blindly.Enemy levels aren't displayed until  you engage them.  It makes for a clean UI, but it'd be nice if I knew that guy was 12 levels above me before I walked in.Don't spend money on precision weapons, a sniper rifle doesn't really grant any advantage because of the third-person 2.5D view.I never got a bounty that wasn't "low-level," and every bounty sells for 1000 uCreds, regardless of if the enemy was level 2 or level 32.  I woulda liked a bounty board or some way to intentionally track and hunt bounties, especially to farm components for weapon upgrades.  Or a way to buy components!  I finished the game with over a million uCreds, so by the end, money isn't a problem.Funny note on uCreds:

_childDocuments_.review: First thing I must say about this game, absolutely beautifully detailed!  The sound, music and graphics meld into a wonderful Cyberpunk world.  Exploring every corner of the map is a must.The overall game play is kind of arcadeish.  Running, gunning, dodging and taking cover to kill and survive.  However it is done in a way that makes it very pleasant to play.There are no classes, you modify stats and swap out gear for different builds.  Respecing points is doable but very expensive, however I have found very little to spend my credits on.The main quest line is not overly complex, go here, get this, kill that, talk to person, bring back.  Typical questing.  Voice overs and cut scenes add a nice element and depth to the story.This game is easily worth the $26 and with the map formatting, the opportunity for DLC is endless.If you like ARPGs like Grim Dawn and Diablo, you will not be disappointed.Performance Notes:AMD 5800 / EVGA 3070 / 32GB Mem / NVME 4 drives Display - 32 inch 2560x1440DX11Ultra Settings with no stuttering or lag like some have reported.

_childDocuments_.review: The artistic style perfectly captures gritty scifi-cyberpunk from a 3rd-person perspective. Sound design and voice acting is fantastic. Quests are typical 'go here, kill this, retrieve Maguffin, return' fare, with a bit too much backtracking, despite having a fast-travel system. Weapons all look, work, and sound cool, while enemy design is sometimes interesting but rarely mind-blowing. Soundtrack doesn't do too much, relying on the visuals to carry it though. Couple annoying issues like armor-repainting not being on toggle, meaning you can't see what new pieces look like unless you return to town. Some really fun weapons (such as the Dismemberer whose name should give away what it does). Overall, solid B+ to A- if you're a fan of the genre and enjoy power-fantasy shooters, so do yourself a favor and pick this one up if that's your jam. It'll help a small studio too!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, but I didn't love it 100% of the time. It's dripping with aesthetic, the voice acting is good, the gameplay is generally satisfying, though early on there's not a lot of variety available to you in terms of weapons/abilities. I could see them adding a lot more to this game and I hope they do. I honestly think there's something here that is franchise-worthy and I'd love to see it expanded on.The main problem is the myriad bugs/glitches, some of which (at the time of reviewing) seem to permanently block mission progress,  that forced me to start a new character after playing through it on coop softlocked my solo progress on that character, costing me a considerable amount of wasted time. For the most part, though, I've been able to overlook those issues. The game is fun enough  of its problems that I can wait patiently for the very small dev team to work out those glaring flaws or work around them myself.Also of note: the game runs surprisingly well on cards as low-grade as the 660 TI, which the Store Page suggests is within minimum specs but left me concerned as other games have listed a 660 TI in their minimum specs  Plenty of areas cause stuttering and frame drops, but even with many of my settings on medium-high the majority of the game runs at a decent FPS and looks amazing. I was afraid to get the game since the visual aspect was such a large selling point and I didn't want to play the Kidz Bop version of it on low graphics with only 30 FPS, but I was pleasantly surprised that wasn't the case. So, friendly for older rigs and laptops. Big thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. Its cyberpunk meets Diablo in  a way. It has a lot of major selling points and some "wait for the sale" points.This game is an absolute work of art. Period. The environment is so amazing and flawlessly designed in that controlled chaos kind of way. Street corridors twist and turn and and every single square inch of the city feels alive and non repetitive. I looked and i could not see a single reused setting. every location is unique and feels hand crafted by a professional cyberpunk artist. Most of the buildings you can go into and ones that you cant are few and far between. You can see robots on lower levels repairing damaged ad displays and people using vending machines. Really just perfect. The game area itself is seamless for the most part. Other than a few elevators that take you from one floor to another or entry ways into some more story focused buildings there are no loading screens. You can walk from one side of the map to the other if you wanted to. The music is really great... For the first like 6 hours. its very Hades like in that it amps up the more you start blowing stuff up and really gets you pumped. After about 6 hours though it kinda gets repetitive. Gameplay feels great even on a keyboard and mouse for a "2 stick shooter" I could have walked over to my tv and grabbed an xbox controller but i just dont like them and it wasnt a bother to play with keyboard and mouse at all. The story cut scenes are pretty good. you get the feeling like you are really putting in some real missions and accomplishing things as your character progresses. The story seems to be of high quality yet it felt very complex and confusing. Its almost like I came in and sat down in the middle of a movie and wasnt sure the backstory so i felt kinda lost. There are a lot of "tech" words made for the game that are thrown into every day conversation that are thrown at you in almost rapid succession in some of the earlier dialogue. Its not a big deal but its just kinda a lot of info and a lot of corporation names and group names and they can really overwhelm you to the point where you are like "what.. go to map marker and kill stuff? got it!" This can also be said for the majority of the side quests where all of the alien type characters seem to all speak this gibberish language. THIS LANGUAGE SUCKS TO LISTEN TO. Its so bad. It feels like you are listening to the same 5 sounds over and over in different order. This was the most annoying part of the game honestly. So much that I had to stop reading the side quest dialogue and spam through it. It doesnt impact gameplay but I would have much rather heard an english version of the dialogue and it would have helped me want to pay attention more. This should really be changed out for english voice cast. Ill do it for free. Send me some scripts lol. The weapons are not randomly generated. They are static specific pieces. When they drop is mostly random but what drops is the exact same thing you probably already have. There are bout 25 to 30 different weapons in the game and some of them feel super weak even when upgraded fully and others feel so overpowered you cant help but use them. (Im looking at you Rocket Launchers with homing missiles)The tactical and other abilities are pretty unique and some are really cool and over powered but others are super weak. Like the Pocket mech which does pretty much 5 damage per bullet when you are hitting things for 700+. What it lacks in damage it more than makes up for with damage resistance. But thats a double edge sword. You can hop in the mech but you cant hop out until the timer runs out. And since you cant really do any damage things start to pile up around you and you have to wait for the timer and then spam some aoe abilities and hope you dont die. Its great for the last missions though (wink wink)Tactical grenades should land on a designated location. I know this is harder to do for non PC players but it can be done. Throwing grenade only to have it go the opposite direction i wanted to throw it feels bad. Or have it not go as far as i wanted it to go. Chest loot from ICE upgrades feels bad. Overall the loot feels bad. But i spent a while going around collecting upgrades to the cyber deck only to finally unlock my first ICE 3 chest (the hardest chest to open in the game) and i get 172 ucreds. Really? I get more than that killing a low level bounty. I can randomly pick that up ioff the ground sometimes. Very disappointing. Speaking of low level bounty guys... every bounty i have found so far even after beating the game and the majority of the side quests is a "bounty of low skill" or whatever and are only ever worth 1000. Im not sure when there are going to be hard bounties but by the time I get to any of them I wont need the ucred. I already dont. I was easily able to buy everything in the game after about half way through the story with tons left over and im sitting at half a million right now with nothing to spend it on. We should be able to buy upgrade pieces for weapons. This game is in need of scaling enemies. Its very tedious to run through old areas only to be swarmed by level 4's talking mad trash that you can kill by breathing on them almost. It makes the end game very dull. There are a few bugs in this game but they are not that big of a deal. in 16 hours of play I crashed 3 times. But the game saves so rapidly that when I came back I had only lost about a minute of play each time. There was a bug with a boss add spawn that became unkillable and it was required to be killed for the boss battle to be considered over. it stood in one spot and spun there over and over without attacking me and I was unable to do damage to it. After many tried and abilities it finally blew up. So only mildly annoying. Once per reload of the game it seems the tutorial pages pop up again when entering the gun store or any of the other stores. Even revisiting the "press ctrl to crouch" location again after reloading the game caused this page to pop back up. This is a small bug and im sure it will be fixed soon. Those are the 3 major bugs ive seen. Nothing I wasnt happy to play through as they were not in my face every 5 seconds or anything like that. more like 1 bug every 5 hours. So not bad at all. This game is amazing. I know I gave it a lot of crap above but thats mostly feedback really. Things I would like to see changed. The world environment alone is worth the money. The art department knocked it out of the park and landed on a nearby golf course and got a hole in one. The rest of the game feels lacking in some ways or another but it was an overall enjoyable experience. It needs to be longer and with more random loot and better abilities. Some abilities need tuned down (rocket launchers) and others need buffed (pocket mech). The game has very little to do end game and overall has no drive to keep me playing. Co-Op needs the ability to join random people. And the biggest thing that needs to be fixed is loot drops. Give me more loot. Give me random drops and ways to redo story missions at end game to get better loot from the bosses. (think diablo torments... this game needs that) Otherwise. What am I even playing for after the story? This could be the next Diablo. There are just a few things missing to give it that replay-ability. Im not recommending this game in its current state only because of how quickly you run out of stuff to do. The game begs to be grinded and played more and more but it has no way to do so. And can we please get a "press spacebar" on dialogue options. Clicking them was bothersome and sometimes even difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: *Review updated after recent fixes*This game really is a diamond in the rough. The gameplay, atmosphere, graphics and sound are great even without an RTX card and it combines elements from lots of games and pop culture I personally enjoy. As a big fan of the old Crusader: No Remorse / No Regret, Deus Ex, Diablo, as well as Ghost in the Shell, Bladerunner and a little bit of Star Wars, the purchase was pretty much a no brainer and well worth the intial price of 27€. I especially enjoyed the gunplay and experimenting with all the different cyber tools. There's all types of crazy guns, grenades, augments, hacks, minions... combat never felt boring and is not tied to character classes, just how you distribute your skill points (which can be re-distributed at any time, though for a hefty amount of credits). It was easy to sink into the gritty, but vibrant game world and the story wasn't that bad either. You meet many interesting characters on your way and it's suprisingly humorous at times, not just dark and depressing. Humans, Aliens, Cyborgs... everyone on drugs and into wierd sex toys... Love it! Some might say that's not enough, but it's still an action game, not an RPG and I'm glad they're not constantly interrupting the game flow with text orgies and unskippable cutscenes. As an action gamer, the balance worked very well for me and I had around 30 hours of good fun, doing all the side quests and exploring every inch of the game world.However, the game also has some obvious problems that may be dealbreakers to some. There are lots of bugs and potential plot stoppers, like getting stuck in geometry or falling through the floor, bosses not spawning, double bosses spawning, enemies getting stuck in doorways while being invincible so you can't make it past them, quest progress not updating, quests leading you into areas where enemies are way beyond your character level despite the quest being rated below... the list is long and in the game's current state, you are almost garanteed to find some every few minutes. Espceially if you play coop, but that's not something I want to even try out at this point. I guess I got lucky and was able to fix the worst bugs by simply reloading, but others  weren't and there are numerous reports of players who were unable to progress through the main quest line aka Game Over! That's a big no-go, of course.There are also some questionable design flaws, for example the excessive backtracking combined with a suboptimal fast-travel system and low movement speed. There is no agility skill or augmentation that lets you upgrade your base runspeed. I put max points in dodging incl. dodge upgrade which lets you move a bit faster if you spam the button, but it still felt painfully slow. You can call a taxi or use the subway, but they rarely get you close enough to your destination. I really wish there were mounts in this game, like a badass motorcycle, hoverboard or something...Enemies will generally stay in the area they spawned in and if you kite them too far away, they will retreat, become invincible and heal themselves back to full health. On the one hand, this prevents players from being pursued to death if they end up in areas that are far beyond their capabilities. On the other hand, it prevents players from exploiting those retreating enemies by shooting them in the back, slowly cheesing their way through areas they have no business in. I get the idea, but it just feels strange and can lead to wierd situations, like those invincible enemies getting stuck in doorways or stairs.Another topic is the controls on mouse and keyboard. In order to walk straight, you have to press to press 2 buttons, W and A/ D or S and A/D. You always have to walk in a diagonal due to the isometrical view and fixed camera angles. You get used to it, but it's probably way more enjoyable with a dual stick controller. And even then, that wouldn't fix the wierd camera angles where you sometimes outrun the screen, depending in which direction you're going.One Hint: People are complaining about bad performance even without raytracing and after the first patch has dropped, which was supposed to fix DX12 performance. I also sufferd from single digit FPS when switching from DX11 to DX12 and it took me a while to realize what was going on. The game ALWAYS activates raytracing when switiching to DX12... even if you don't have an RTX card!!! If you switch to DX12 and restart the game, make sure to check the graphics menu once again and turn that stuff off! After that, performance was fine mostly, between 70 and 144 FPS (G-Sync). There was some annoying stuttering when entering new areas, but I have an old system with GTX 1080, i7-5820K and 16GB DDR4 RAM, so that's Ok I guess. Considering the amazing visuals, I expected less to be honest.Conclusion: In a way, The Ascent reminds me of the old Stalker games: Feels like a beta, lots of bugs, performance issues, design flaws... but superb atmosphere, game world and action that will let you immediately forget about all the problems once you sink into it and nothing is glitching out for a few minutes.7/10 copies of Billy Idol's "Cyberpunk" album plot-stopping his career,8/10 cyborg geishas if you're into that kind of stuff.9/10 grams of Orange Snooze if they fix the most critical bugs... or if you're so high on RTX fumes that you don't recognize anything else anymore.

The game feels gritty in a way that has been lacking from the cyberpunk genre for years with everything else being some kind of matrix ripoff.Unfortunately It also suffers a lot of the bugs Cyberpunk had - it's just more forgivable due to the price and team size. If you can tolerate bugs and the idea of having to potentially restart - I'd say buy it and enjoy it. If you're going to be frustrated by bugs - maybe wait a few months until they get a chance to iron things out.Overall I hope they are able to polish the game up and look forward to what else this team comes out with.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. Top-tier graphics. Really stellar visual design. Great writing with cool lore that's engaging to read. Doesn't shy away from potty humor but doesn't really on it either. Slick world design with neat characters and factions. Great music and voice acting. Deep but not cumbersome mechanics. I don't like getting bogged down in menus and that's no problem here.The real winner is the combat system though. I wasn't looking for an isometric twin stick shooter. I've played enough of those to have a certain set of expectations that aren't immediately enticing anymore. But when I gave this a try I was greeted with a system with such a clever wrinkle that I was quickly hooked. The posture-based cover system has just enough of a formula tweak to really engage you. It's got a crunch and sizzle to it.You can get lost and maybe even just so slightly bored in the initial couple hours finding your footing in the massive world despite how beautifully it's rendered. Definitely play it until you get into your first real fight against other shooting enemies. The initial fights are against simpler melee enemies and don't do justice to the combat. This game's combat loop is what keeps me coming back. The rest is delicious icing. Really delicious icing. Great game. This is a studio to watch.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that is visually amazing done extremely well when it comes to characters, and especially the huge city and area you will be adventuring in. City areas actually filled with hundreds of citizens, visuals, and feels like a matrix futuristic city that your going thorugh. Extremely well done. Great characters and npcs, cool enemies to fight, always with great visuals in between. Nice voiceacting also. Now it comes to the bad parts. Exploring those huge matrix cities and areas is very confusing with multiple levels, directions, dead ends, and your mini map not quite showing the path to get to places. Along with often bad directions and waypoint quest markers that aren't correct often leads you to explore for a hour just to find out your not going the right way, and the correct way is no where close to where you think it is. Fustrating. Amazing city to explore, horrible help to explore it.  As for combat, its fun but the camera angles are set so often you are trying to shoot something but there is no way you can actually see it until you move closer, which ruins the reason to try to shoot something far away. Most of the game is very close ranged combat where your trying to circle and stay away from near foes enough to shoot them. Didn't like this.Quests are ok, but often again you have no clue where to go, and even worst you can access some side quests only to find out you can't really do them until you progress further into the story. Ok, why did you open this side quest this early if i have to play another few days to actually do it?  And you don't have any idea which quests this applies to. Lots of backtracking, very basic and lacking shop system, limited weapon types and armor that does the same stuff. Oh we have 5 types of machine guns.. not much different so pick one. Ok, why not just have 1 type in the game they basically are the same.  So, overally a fun game. Its slow and confusing at the start once you are learning how to navigate the very confusing city areas, but if you give it time it will pick up in the later game. It gets repetative and boring late game again, but for the price on sale? A must have i would consider.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I've had an eye on for the last few months and I did not think I would get it on release. As a rule I tend not to buy a game until it is patched up a little more and I can scope out some reviews. I don't know what compelled me to buy this on release day, but I am glad I did.Gameplay is good. I played with keyboard and mouse, and it played really well. I realised a few hours into playing that the trailers showing people walking were probably people lightly using the sticks of a controller to move. The combat is a lot of fun and you really feel like a crime lord enforcer at the start of the game; pushing people out of the way and accepting civilian deaths as acceptable losses.There are some things that hold back the game and I can't help but feel there was some things chopped to get the game to release date. For example, it is odd that you can upgrade weapons but cannot upgrade your armour nor special abilities. One of the themes of cyberpunk is to upgrade oneself. And it is also odd that the stats of armour doesn't change with levels. This is something that makes me think it was cut from the final game. You are sort of forced down certain aesthetic choices just to get the stats.I have played this coop with a friend and it is amazing. There are some bugs that are coop specific that I hope they rectify i.e. Only one person can initiate a conversation with an NPC at one time, otherwise the other person will get stuck and have to quit and rejoin. And often they can only see the dialogue in text form while one watches a cinematic.Another annoyance is every time you quit the game, you lose all of your character and weapon skins. If you've equipped one onto a current weapon it will stay on there. I wonder how the devs will fix that and compensate for everyone having lost skins.The game is drop-dead gorgeous. The cyberpunk aesthetic is there and you can spot hints from lots of different references. I see you LAPD tower! The camera does a good job of allowing you to take in some amazing scenery. You also can't help but think what you might be missing from the isometric-style camera. I'm playing with HDR and the colours just pop!The game has a fixed camera and that is both a positive and negative criticism. 99% of the time it is perfect and doesn't hinder you at all. There are a few odd choices when it almost turns side-scrolling but you soon get the knack of how to fight in that. Sorry civilians for shooting you in the back! I would ask the devs to make it so when you are moving downwards it allows you to see a little farther down. The view is very limiting.The soundtrack is incredible. Hints of Ghost in the Shell on the menu and loading track. And when the action kicks in you get a beat that reminds me of playing deathmatch in old turn-of-the-century FPS games. It's the sort of soundtrack I wish CP77 had. I sometimes turn off music in games as I find it distracting but I will never turn the music off in this.The sound effects are great in this as well. A lot of the bigger weapons sound beefy and have weight behind them. I particularly like the screams when people die. It just adds that little extra to the immersion of you being a cold killer in a cold world.Speaking of immersion, how great is it to see a properly populated cyberpunk world? There are people everywhere. And they are just going about their lives until someone decides to open up and have a gun fight. Then they scream, fall over to get away, and sometimes get hit. The lack of retribution for these deaths just shows how much value lives have in our future. I wouldn't mind a bounty system if we accidentally kill a slightly valuable indent and you have to fight off hunters, or pay an admin fee to the aggrieved corp.I've just completed my first playthrough with a friend and we both thoroughly enjoyed this, despite the bugs. My friend had to quit to menu a few times and rejoin, but this took seconds thanks to the surprisingly fast loading speeds. We were both left with the feeling of wanting more, which is weird for us as a lot of coop games become a slog near the end and we just want it to be over. We're so ready for any DLC expansions!

_childDocuments_.review: Think about it many times. I did have a blast and I got almost all achievements except the two multiplayer ones. However, I still cannot recommend this game at the current state and let me add my own 2 cents. I wish there is a "Errrr... that depends" button.0. Whether you will play this game or not, remember this game is done by a studio with only 12 people on a very tight budget. The level of details is astonishing. There will never be a lack of praise for this game so I will just save time here.1. So here starts the bad and the ugly. First, there is no public multiplayer. You can switch your lobby to public but currently there is no way to join a public game, not even a lobby browser. In earlier days coop can even corrupt your save and NeonGiant hasn't put multiplayer on their road map yet. Wonder when the experience will be fixed.2. Does not have a proper ultrawide screen support and fov slider. The game has a fixed horizontal fov, meaning if you have a wider screen, you will see less vertically. I have a 32:9 monitor and the game is unplayable at the beginning. I have to use unreal engine unlocker every time and use the console to adjust the field of view. The process is simple enough but hey, this game is using UE4 and if a single line command in console can give you a proper wide screen support, why don't just spend 5 minutes and code it into the menu? Also it is easy enough in UE4 to move the UI so probably another 5minutes to give us a UI position slider? I have even seen developers on reddit respond to wide screen problems but they JUST DONT WANT TO DO IT. You cannot complain, they only have 12 people.3.1 The level design left much to be desired. The first is the transportation problem. This game has a metro system and a path finder button but they cannot be combined. To save yourself time you have to open the map multiple times to check where the metro station. The game can give the player a toggle button to show the route to destination directly or to show the route to destination with metro involved, or both, with different color. By the end of the game I just spend 1000 and call taxi, making the metro station useless. At least, always show the latest metro station on map.3.2 Traveling between layers can be a chore. After mid game you will need to switch between layers a lot to finish quest and get stuff. To get from warren to high street, you need to go to the center circle, kill a bunch of mobs and take the elevator, EVERY, SINGLE, TIME. Just give us the option to fast travel between layers by metro or taxi will ya? I understand it is part of the lore, that different layer represents different social status and clearance to high layers cannot be earned easily but come on, it is a kill-n-loot shooter, give us the capability to move between levels.3.3 No sprint button, making the walking painfully slow out of combat. The player can at least gain faster movement out of the battle to save time.4.1 The game design left much to be desired, too. I like reading about lores so I know all the NPCs and enemies in the game, but they don't differentiate that much in terms of game play. There are only three types of enemies, the melee, the range, and the big bois. They are only different in terms of fire power, or maybe you need to switch to weapons with different ammo type to take care of robots but that is about it. I enjoy this game because I am a cyberpunk sucker and the gun sound in this game is so satisfying.  In core this game lacks the potential to have a high skill ceiling and depth. 4.2 The bosses are underwhelming because most of them are just a bigger version of the regular enemies or a giant robot that is used again and again and again in my scenes. We need more diversity and more delicately designed boss.4.3 The gun stats in this game is currently broken. You cannot tell if a gun is good or bad based on the stats. For example, the gun with the second highest DPS actually does very little damage. The highest level upgrading material in this game is limited and you will find yourself very disappointed when you spend your rare material upgrading the gun that is not remotely as good as you think it is.4.4 Following the last remark, we need a gun range to test things out. A lot of RPG there give player a dummy to test and this game can use that too. Give us a room in the cluster 13 and we will be happy. Also it would be nice for player to test the maxed out version of all the guns unlocked so one can decide which to upgrade. If the devs don't bother testing the weapon out, then give us a chance to test it ourselves.5. Design flaws. Of course this game is beautiful and it looks even better under ray tracing. However, there is the problem of "over design", meaning that an important aspect of design is to determine what not to design. Sometimes is very hard to find where the player is at. The game will still be the game if there are fewer fancy bars in the map that serve absolutely no purpose, but it will be better if the team chooses to spend the limited resource on gameplay. The art is solid but generic, as well as the music. I wish the art and the location can be deviated from textbook cyberpunk a little bit, making this game more unique. Everything you see and you hear is too typical.6. We need manual save and a more detailed save prompt. Sometimes you died and you found out that you need to run through the entire map all over again, which is really not nice. Also, the last two missions are considerably harder than the previous ones and offer a lot of good loots, but you are unable to upgrade your weapon unless you decide to go all the way back. I found myself underleveled and under upgraded in the final stint because I still have not figured out which weapons to max out because the stats are broken. I went out, did all the side mission and maxed out the weapons recommended by reddit. I mean you do need to make the last moment epic and longer than usual but at least allow people to upgrade and ready themselves.I love this game, but it still has a lot to improve. Wonder what the game will be in like several months after.

_childDocuments_.review: how to describe this game in one sentence :  Cyberpunk Diablo with gunsThe strenghs of The Ascent are: -its gorgeous Cyberpunk visual/art, especially with Ray Tracing on.-its solid and exciting gunshot/gameplay. This is basically Diablo, with guns. I first played this game on Gamepass and LOVED its visual and gameplay so much that I decided to buy it on Steam. I rarely buy games full prices, so that tells a lot how much I liked this game.However, you quickly notice after a couple hours, that despite its excellent visual and gameplay, this is not a perfect game. -This is not a LOOTER-SHOOTER per se. The looting sytem is poor, you basically loot the exact same guns or equipment, with the exact same stats.  You end up with many identical guns/equipments in your inventory, Thankfully you can level-up each weapon type/group, they will then make more damage. -the map system is extremely confusing, think Metroid Prime. It's not awful, but not great either.-the backtracking is awful! Since you can only follow one mission at a time, you end up going back and forth in the world, again and again. It's not like in Diablo or Borderlands in which nearby quests are shown in the map, for ex. -world is beautiful but it can get quite repetitve after a while. Same goes for the soundtrack.-the difficulty is not well balanced. Enemies get tough quickly, you basically HAVE to do ALL main/side quests + farm for XP in order to level up and stand a chance. -The final boss fight is a joke. Other bosses are not really inspired either. - there is no end game. Another thing, I see people praising this indie studio for making such a beautiful/quality game, with only 12 employees?  The credits shows that much more people were involved in the making of the game (including other studios)Overall I would recommend The Ascent, especially if you like fun shooter or diablo-like. The gameplay is fun and solid, the game should keep you busy for 20-25 hours.  Just don't expect something perfect. Still, a much better game than Cyberpunk 77  ;)I'd give this game a 7.5 out of 10Will I play this game again? I'm not sure.REVIEW UPDATED to get Steam Awards achievement  :)

_childDocuments_.review: Set in a beautiful, hand-crafted dystopian cyberpunk world, this twin stick isometric "dungeon" crawler is a fantastic entry into this year's catalog. There are some RPG elements that add a little variation to playthroughs, and you can change this up (using in game credits) at various places in the world.Fighting enemies is fun, the crowd mechanics are interesting and believable, and NPC's behave randomly enough to be convincing that they are busy in the world. The lighting is fantastic, and the scenery in the various locations are distinct enough to help you navigate pretty easily (if you're walking. You should be taking the taxi with "T"). You'll want to engage enemies all the time to hear the great music, as well.There are some low points, but they are easy to overlook as you continue playing. For example, the loot system is kind of weird. You'll find everything you ever need on the ground, dropped from random enemies. However, there's no variation. Just duplicates. You can skin your weapons to make them look a little different, but seeing that your character is so small on the screen, there's really no point.

_childDocuments_.review: With a heavy heart I leave this poor review, as someone who was beyond ecstatic for this game to come out so I could run a fun Co-oP shoot wither 3 other friends.. this has been the buggiest experience I've had since Cyberpunk 2077 with the difference being I played that game to completion because it was actually fun.Bugs ranged from guns not shooting, players stuck in dialog and interactions who were left unable to quit the game besides alt+f4 or being kicked from the session, to the worst offender the MAIN QUEST BREAKING - we got to the onyx fight and after loading into it nothing spawned and we couldn't leave, so I reset the session only to come back to the lift where there was no prompt and no way to complete the quest. We tried one more time just to be sure and ended with the same result.tldr; interesting ideas as a game, tight controls, wonky pacing, riddled with bugs, pretty graphics, and online connectivity seemed fine. Don't play this at launch, look for some big bug fix patches a few months down the road. GL everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: The Ascent : By Triple FIn the vast and intricate landscape of video games, few titles manage to capture both the imagination and the adrenaline quite like "The Ascent." Developed by Neon Giant and published by Curve Digital, this cyberpunk masterpiece offers a breathtaking blend of immersive world-building, frenetic combat, and an irresistible neo-noir atmosphere. Prepare to embark on a journey that transcends the boundaries of gaming and ushers you into a world teeming with technological wonders and sinister secrets.From the very moment you set foot in the neon-soaked streets of Veles, the sprawling metropolis in which "The Ascent" is set, it becomes evident that this game is a visual marvel. The level of detail that Neon Giant has poured into every nook and cranny of the environment is nothing short of astonishing. The towering skyscrapers, bustling markets, dimly lit back alleys, and intricate cybernetic enhancements on characters all contribute to an immersive cyberpunk world that's hard to tear your eyes away from.A successful cyberpunk tale hinges on its ability to create an atmosphere that is simultaneously futuristic and nostalgic, grimy yet alluring. "The Ascent" excels on this front, presenting a world where corporate overlords rule with an iron grip, while downtrodden citizens and rogue AI populate the underbelly of society. The ambient sounds of distant hovercars, the electronic hum of holographic billboards, and the chatter of NPCs all meld together to create an environment that feels alive and tangible.At the core of "The Ascent" lies a gripping narrative that keeps you hooked from start to finish. As an indentured worker thrown into a chaotic conspiracy following the collapse of The Ascent Group, you'll navigate a labyrinth of intrigue, betrayal, and self-discovery. The character interactions, augmented by well-written dialogue, shed light on the complex dynamics of this cybernetic society, and your personal journey becomes interwoven with the fate of the entire world.The combat system in "The Ascent" is a symphony of destruction, blending traditional twin-stick shooting mechanics with an array of cybernetic abilities and devastating weaponry. Whether you're engaging in frenzied firefights against various factions or facing off against towering bosses, each encounter is a thrilling test of reflexes and strategic thinking. The upgrade system, which allows you to customize your character's abilities and gear, adds a layer of depth that ensures no two playthroughs are the same.To add on, "The Ascent" becomes even more electrifying when experienced in its cooperative mode. Team up with friends to tackle the challenges of Veles together, sharing the excitement of battles and uncovering secrets as a united force. The seamless drop-in, drop-out multiplayer allows for a fluid gaming experience, further enhancing the sense of camaraderie and exploration.In the realm of gaming, few experiences manage to capture the essence of a genre as perfectly as "The Ascent" does with cyberpunk. Neon Giant's meticulous attention to detail, combined with a compelling narrative, jaw-dropping visuals, and exhilarating game-play, solidifies "The Ascent" as a true gem in the vast sea of video games. Whether you're a fan of dystopian futures, explosive combat, or simply yearn for an otherworldly escape, The Ascent beckons you to ascend to new heights of gaming excellence.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like Ascent. The world, environments and characters are all pretty well done. The story is pretty interesting too once you get far enough into the game to start to understand some of the lore. The skill progression and gear progression is great as well. I feel like there are always things to upgrade/improve. I love that the gear progress/upgrades is tied to exploration and finding chests. This allows me to explore and upgrade my items when I feel inclined to do so. Negatives-----------There are several bugs I've encountered throughout the game. Many of which I believe could have been avoided by paying my testers to run different quest/game scenarios. I've probably encountered 4-5 quests that didn't load correctly until I restarted the game. It is also quite odd that I could be level 15 and not have unlocked the area of objectives yet to complete a level 2 quest that I currently have active.In the games current state it is quite fun and I would probably give it a 7.5/10. With more polish and less bugs I'd say this game could easily be a 9.0/10. I hope they continue to work on it and release some expansions/DLC. It would be really cool to see what they could do with an Ascent 2 as well since there base systems are fantastic as they are.

_childDocuments_.review: is a totally underrated Twin-Stick-Shooter in a dystopic cyberpunk world with a really nice graphic style where Blade Runner fans will find reminiscences.The combat has a lot of tactical options with RPG elements (like different skills), a set of upgradable guns and weapons (ranging from small pistols up to as big as a gatling gun) as well as different tactical charges (like grenades and some other really wicked stuff) and two augmentations which gives further options. Additionally you can shoot from the hip or aim for headshots and use the environment by taking cover behind blocks. There are small weaknesses like the map locator which sometimes leads you into the wrong direction, some level scenarios which achieve difficulty only by throwing hordes of enemies at you and sometimes you can't skip cutscenes of boss encounters which can be annoying when you've to restart over and over again but besides that the game and especially the fights are motivating and fun.Although the story isn't that bad and has some interesting elements i wouldn't expect hollywood style for this kind of games. I've made in ~38h but at a slow pace. Even when you completed a run the replay value is high and a co-op mode is available too.

_childDocuments_.review: 11 Hours in - Multiple Profiles - Solo and Co-op PlayerPros:+ No detail too small for this incredible cyberpunk city landscape+ lots of exploration to be done, if you can see it you can likely find a way to it+ lots of graphic options for systems that might chug a little while running this game+ even on low settings this game is very satisfying to look at+ lots of weapons and armor          - a huge worry for me was that the weapons and armor drops would be repetitive and not too unique                   but so far i am pleasantly surprised with how much variation there is+ Quests have unique objectives when it comes to the story they provide+ characters are unique, memorable, the voicing is fantastic+ character leveling is fair and i have yet to notice a difficulty drop off point where im either over leveling or under leveling my character+ your armor and your skill set need to work together in order to get the best gains which adds a little nuance to a system that is otherwise very straight forward. + shooting literally everything and anything has yet to get old...Cons:- while the story is good so far and definitely keeping me interested quests can be predictable in that you can expect this format; Quest > travel > shooting gallery > boss fight > cut scene > travel > repeat- some side quests you pick up will not be playable until you unlock the area that quest requires. the game will not tell you this though and will instead leave you feeling like the objective is glitched.- PERFORMANCE. this game is very surprisingly a beast. while there are plenty of adjustable graphic options some computers may still have a hard time getting the performance they'd like while playing multiplayer games specifically.- while single player is very playable it can be much more frustrating than playing with a squad and in my opinion a little less fun.if your looking specifically for a looter shooter then just pick up this game. its worth it.if you are on the fence about looter shooters in general i would say this is definitely one of the best ones in recent memory. there are bugs since this game just released but if you are a Solo player then you will likely not encounter any of these bugs. if you are a team player that only plays looter shooters with a squad then i would definitely recommend giving this game a little time to get an update or two out before you buy/play. as i mentioned earlier the bugs are essentially only there in multiplayer games. the more players you add (4 max) the buggier it may get. we needed to restart our games multiple times, some players lost items and progress and were forced to buy them again which was only a minor setback but annoying nonetheless. highly recommend this game especially once the updates start rolling in. keep up the good work!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a very pleasant surprise for me, and the core of that came from the absolutely stunning environmental feel that was put into creating Veles.  Not just in the graphics, which were beautiful and fluid for a number of the various cinematic camera angles involving the Arcology and its machinery, but also in the music and sound design, which really drew in and helped sell the sense of aspirational hope amidst oppressive downward pressure.  The action is easy to pick up and smooth, though somewhat limiting given the amount of customization that is available.The biggest criticism I have for this game is it feels like the creators spent the upfront investment in time and effort on world-building, lore, and environmental music, graphics, and texture to create something that could have honestly rivaled 'Mass Effect' as a truly memorable and top-tier Sci-Fi, Cyberpunk RPG with some action elements, but got shot down by the publishers and the suits in marketing and were forced to create a 'good' action game that has some RPG elements because that's what would guarantee a return on their investments quickly and with the lowest capital inlay.  Very Ascent Group.  This is obviously pure conjecture on my own part, but given the quality and detail put into some of the curious aspects of this game, that's honestly what it feels like happened.

_childDocuments_.review: I truly mega-wanted The Ascent to be great, but I'm afraid I always have to be brutally honest with every game I review. The Ascent is a masterfully crafted Cyberpunk game in terms of AESTHETICS and ART DIRECTION. But it lacks the crucial polish everywhere else.The game is decent, if you have the patience for it. The Ascent scores a 5/10 solo and 6/10 if you have a buddy to enjoy coop together. I wished I had a neutral button for reviewing, but as it stands it is barely a  recommendation from me, with its amazing visuals helping it to pass my rating.Pros:Masterfully crafted Cyberpunk aesthetic - If you are looking for the definitive looking cyberpunk game, this game fully delivers it. The Cyberpunk world in this is pulled off accurately and full of mindblowing detail. In terms of its visuals, it is a 10/10 for me.Good sound design and soundtrack - Guns, explosions and music all sound crisps. They have a very satisfactory reverb to them. Very impressive.Exploring via main story - Along the main story quests, it slowly introduces more and more unique Cyberpunk areas. Makes you look forward where you are going to end up or seeing next.Cons:Repetitive mission chain - Quests are repetitive with no real story context to it, mostly fetch me that and kill these people for me type quests.Terrible Checkpoint System - If you die in a boss fight prepare to restart 5-10 mins earlier in the area going through the same tedious mobs over and over again to trigger the boss fights.Not balanced for solo play - Some boss sequences are clearly meant for 2-3 players to complete, making solo experiences at times hair-pulling difficult.No interesting characters and poor plot - Most of the cast are extremely one-noted. A lot of the cast in the game are not voice-acted as well. As for the plot, I have no idea what's going on during 80% percent of the game. I recommend getting it on sale and playing it coop with friends, if you are playing solo prepare to get your experience dampened. The Cyberpunk world is truly insane and impressively crafted, and if that is what only truly matters to you, then I say go ahead.

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing "end of the year" surprise...I didn't have any expectations towards this game when I started it, I only know that I generally like twin-stick shooters. I prefer to play them alone, however. Rushing around a map with other people is not my thing, I love to linger as long as I like and check all the details.And this game has a lot of them, I mean... as in... nowadays you really don't get that very often anymore.It reminded me of classics like "Crusader: No Remorse" and I was directly brought back to the good old days, when games were full of details.The modeller(s) and level designer(s) did an unbelievable job. Such variety in objects and environments is very rare these days. Every scene is literally littered with ...things. Cables, rusty bolts or generally just junk. And every corner of the "city" feels fresh and doesn't have a construction kit vibe to it.Shady back alleys, small and bigger bars, a casino... or do you prefer the premium waiting area of an airport? Even after getting the achievement for discovering all areas I stumbled across parts of the city which I hadn't seen before.It's like the game designers said: "We will have XY main missions and YX side missions." But the level artists didn't care, they already planned out and modeled the whole city. ...and they would have done it anyway, because it looks like they had fun doing it.For some people it might be too widely stretched, sometimes you need a little patience going from A to B. At least for me the map and fast travel system was hard to grasp and only at the end I half-way understood how it worked. But this also might have come, because I enjoyed walking around.I really don't like it in games nowadays that every maggot is levelling up with you. Not here... (big grin) After you levelled up and also treated your tools with a little care, life expectancy of everything opposing you will go down to zero.Emphasized by great sound effects (the most violent and scary sounding flamethrower I came across in a game) and film like explosions it's pure entertainment. ...or, it was for me... I only faced a game-braking bug once, just after the end, my character fell through all floors and could only be "saved" by bringing up the main menu again. However, I have to say that the auto-save system worked really nicely throughout the whole game. I never had to repeat minutes of gameplay after the character died. Only before boss fights there can be the notorious cut-scene which has to be skipped to be able to quickly continue.Oh, did I mention the photo-mode? Finally a (vanilla) game in which you are able to truly move the camera in a free and unlocked way. Sure, you can see the "backstage area", all the parts of the game which might not be as glorious as the rest. But that's just the reality of how games are made and if this doesn't take you out of the overall atmosphere you will get a great photo tool, which allows for some creative shots.I'm full of praise for the game, which was truly unexpected for me. But, if your aim is to play it in co-op I probably would listen to the other reviews which focus more on the multiplayer side. My single-player run was a great experience and I can only recommend it for people who like the overall setting and don't need company. I hope there will be much more content coming, because I'm looking foward to return... I'm quite sure, I haven't seen everything yet!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I really hope they do more DLC I would pay full price for it, or preferably a full length sequel storyThe Pros:The world was absolutely amazing from the design to how it felt full and alive, tons of NPCs everywhere, you never feel alone. Even looking through windows on the floor theres ships, npcs, robots going about their lives.The world is bladerunner/cyberpunk but does it far far better IMO.32in IPS 2k monitor with ray tracing and max setting and the game is MIND BLOWING.There is so much attention to detail from random stuff on the ground to looking better then AAA third person games.Your personal AI after the upgrade was jokes.The main story in both the main game and DLC is a satisfying climb from nothing into corp hitman/asset acquirement role.The main game ending was good and left me with questions.The gameplay was really good for a top down shooter, (on M&KB, i didn't like controller aiming).The weapon choices was better then I expected and the augments and tactical's were really diverse and enjoyable.Cons:Honestly cant think of any real ones, with the exclusion of one: There is sometime an annoying amount of walking/back tracking unless you have the extra credits for the taxi.Maybe on a lower end pc it would not run very well but I cant speak on that.Its not a con because whats there is great, but I wanted more of this game it was longer then most indie games and some AAA games but since I actually enjoyed it (rare these days) I wanted more and there was none to be had.Character customization is really basic but I had armor on the whole time so its not a big deal.The color system could be better I was trying to match my colors for the corp I was working for but couldn't most of the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing like Diablo, a review claiming this was the reason i bought it. Extremely shallow game. Limited weapons heavily relying upon upgrading them through components to increase weapon stats. Limited Gear slots (3) upgraded similarly to the weapons. Some basic stat management but lack of obvious indicators in what each stat does. Main quest line is voiced beautifully, side quest lazily falls into sh*t speak. The game is filled with corners cut leaving it feelings shallow, empty and overall dull in an underwhelming stale experience of pointing and shooting at stuff with the weapon you favour and probably found in your first hour of playing. Attribute system is boring, a few builds spring to mind but only a few. Most people will opt in for small spread high crit. Don't expect thousands of different pieces of gear. This expands to character customisation. You get to chose like 6 hair styles, 5 faces, 10 colours (wowzers) which are applied to your clothes and will be the default colour of all the (armour) you find. Sick.The game-play is okay. Augments do things and pressing e or q will activate them when ready. G lets you use a grenade every few minutes. shooting relies heavily on aim assist to accurately hit things. Turned it off and when cursor is directly on the target you hit random things. Feels like a sub-par console game to be honest. This has absolutely nothing on the higher tier ARPGs.  Story is lame, you're practically a "slave" that gets paid. So you're not a slave. Business goes bust after the suits fold. The workers/middle management essentially continue business. That's it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really good, and a refreshing take on the cyberpunk genre. I have consumed a lot of cyberpunk media over the years and there aren't many works that have alien races in the mix with humans. Humans are cool and all, but when you mix in alien races and their unique cultures, skills, etc it can be way more interesting. The level design is out of this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ world. Each area in the game has an insane amount of detail, the most detail I've ever seen in level design. The world feels alive and is filled to the brim with every bit of trash, litter, the poor, killers, grime, and crime you could hope to see in something befitting the cyberpunk aesthetic. It's a neon bathed Arcology that's beautifully sculpted.The story to this game is really solid. It has a lot of cyberpunk stereotypes thrown into the story and lore, but that isn't a bad thing. It's a tried and true concept, with some interesting variations thrown into the mix. It's not a terribly long game either but it has a pretty satisfying end, it took me 22 hours to get every achievement in the game and finish up the story.My biggest complaint with the game is that I feel like it was perhaps too easy, one of the rarest achievements is dying one hundred times, I feel like that sums it up pretty well. It's far too easy to just settle with two guns and call it good. I played the majority of the game with the HMG42 Dominator and the ER Chrome Puncher, both of which are excellent guns at dispersing any foes you face. I had to turn the difficulty to hard, and force myself to use a different combination of weapons to enjoy it personally, but that's also because I like to suffer when I play games.The difficulty curve is pretty intense, with the early half of the game being a cake walk and the later half being something I actually considered insanely fun. It was literally a bullet hell at the end, and that was what I was looking forward to from the start.All and all this game is really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good, and it stands as a solid addition to the cyberpunk genre. The end of the game made it seem open to the idea of a future DLC, or perhaps a second title which I would love to see. I definitely recommend playing this.

_childDocuments_.review: dear cybergods you heard my calli expected a very good looking, but simplistic twin-stick-shooter/top-down-shooterwhat i got is a full fletched cyberpunk world, character building, tons of secrets, quest, loot, world-building and probably the best grafics around it's not just that The Ascent is objectivly impressive from a technical point of view (might even be more technicaly advanced then CP2077): the design is breathtaking. fully prerendered movies don't got this much detail in every corner. it's pretty much open world, you can go back and forth between already done and new areas at your leisure (some doors/elevators might be locked until certain story-beats are hit). you can run through bustling markerts and go on a shoppin spree, or visit some side-bar to grab a low-key-legwork side-mission. it's about as far from a simplistic top-down-shooter as it can get. heck, you can even money, loot or level grind, since enmies do respawn (thank the gods).it's honestly more an arpg, with top-down-shooter gameplay. and it's f***ing great.story, quest and important npcs are fully voiced (and the voice-work done is top notch), random npcs having scenery conversations speak more a fantasy language, but their conversations are translated via text-bubblethere's a lot of world-building done just by simply talking to a npc like Proone. your journal (more or less a complete inventory) does the rest. the "codex" version of the Ascent is amazing. everything from enemies, npcs, manufacturers of gear, corporations in this world got either very detailed 3D models and flavor text, or wonderfull artwork. in your journal you can access everything from the map, loadout (to equip new weapons/armor for example), to skills and augments (kinda like passive perks mixed with active skills). and the visual design of the menu is just as good as the rest of the game. CDProject Red lost it's cyberpunk-throne to a 20 to 30 bucks game...which is kinda hillarious. then there's the soundtrack. oh my lord. even the start-menu music is out of this world. melancholic, techn-noir, to beat heavy techno tracks. the soundtrack is a straight 10/10 and some tracks even give me Ghost in the Shell vibes.about the only negative i could find is the way the game loads assets into the cache. new effects, new models seem to not get preloaded (when you first encounter them), but cached the moment they appear, which can lead to loading-stutter when you encounter something for the first time. funny enough: once loaded in, the game never seems to load anything else. for major areas there's sorta, kinda an elevator (ingame) loading screen, which takes about 5-10 seconds on my HDD (SDD currently full). then there's the price. it's downright criminal. when you look at some other games released recently at fullprice when they should've been around 20 bucks, this insane pearl goes for the price of a tiny, 2D, indy-product...funny times.the most important thing: it's mad fun. weapons feel great, evasion is tight, having 1 tactical skill (drones, grenades, etc.)which you sustain by doing damage, 2 active skills (like a super-punch, or a debuff that makes enemies explode) which run on an energy ressource , mixed with the amazing optics and soundtrack...it's amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Got on sale for £5. Absolutely worth that price point if you like top-down shooters and/or dystopian futures.It basically feels as though the Shadowrun series went from being a turn-based & party-based RPG to a 3rd-person shooter and most of the budget for plot/writing was given to the graphics people instead.There are a few things that could do with a polish - for example:1. Explaining that picking up Cyberdeck upgrades physically replaces your current Cyberdeck with the next model name. I spent a long time hunting for a Cyberdeck shop vendor to buy the next deck, assuming that they functioned the same way as weapons and that deck upgrades just gave you v2, v3, v4 etc of your starting deck type. Just generally taking a little more care and attention when it comes to signposting stuff to the player, because there's a lot to take in. Same with weapon damage types, armour types, etc.2. Transport. There are a couple of fast travel options (which is great) but there's also parts where you're forced to run for frankly unnecessary amounts of time in order to go to a new area *through parts of the game you've already cleared* due to the gradually unlocking hub-and-spoke system they use. I think this does a good job of reminding you of the scale and size of the hive you live in, but it also just isn't amazingly interesting when you have to do it.3. There are some slightly jarring story notes which aren't explained or elaborated on. I won't spoil anything here, but there are some characters you're introduced to, and you either enter conflict with them and their faction without warning, or you suddenly become best friends with them, and it doesn't seem to elicit much response from your earlier friends, even when they're enemies with your new mates. There's just a bit of disconnect in how the world sees you and what you do (e.g. killing scores/hundreds of people from various factions), and how they treat you or each other as the game progresses.4. The map and minimap could be a little clearer. It isn't always obvious how to get from one place to another, or what level a chest/shop/train station is on, and the minimap could do with a height indicator via fading, rather than things just appearing or disappearing.All of that said, these are just minor issues. They don't significantly impact the game.There is a solid laundry list of weapons, techs, upgrades, augmentations and gear that let you tailor your character how you like.Most of the guns are solidly different, good sounds, good visuals etc. Great explosions and gibs et al.Atmosphere is really good - filthy hive city with downtrodden inhabitants, lots of background chatter and datapad notes scattered around, great mix of neon and grime.Music is fine, but does occasionally jar when "fight music" starts in areas you've outlevelled, and then ends immediately because you blatted everything in 2 seconds flat.Have only played solo thus far, but imagine it could be great fun with co-op.Other games with a similar feel (but significant differences) include:- The Riftbreaker (top-down shooter, but with base-building and resource management on a verdant planet)- Necromunda games (same vibe of a hive city, but different genre of game)- Shadowrun games (top-down cyberpunk, but party/turn based)So yeah, get it on sale with no regrets, a strong game to spend a weekend or two on. Don't forget to pick up as many chests as possible first time round (keep checking your map) so you have minimal backtracking!

_childDocuments_.review: The Ascent tries to be a stick shooter, cover shooter and light rpg and basically fails at all three.First the good- The game is STUNNING! The level of detail on display here is insane and the game world is truly beautiful. From the neon soaked streets and bars to abandoned tenements and waste tunnels every area feels lovingly crafted and is 100% pure crack for the eyeballs. This alone has kept me going long after I tired of the gameplay.- The soundtrack is great, mixing Deus Ex style synths with more ambient tracks reminiscent of Dying Light it fits the game world perfectly.- Sound effects are also top notch. Guns are generally punchy and explosions have a nice oomph to them.The BadFar and away the worst offender is the combat which is annoying for a number of reasons:- Enemies activate and engage you before they're visible on screen and as such you'll spend most of your play time staring at the farther reaching minimap instead of the world just to see them coming. Sometimes entire firefights are resolved without actually seeing who you're shooting at.- Its all but impossible to avoid fire. Your character moves so slowly and even with your dodge move enemies have zero problem adjusting their aim and hitting you. When you throw in enemies with homing bullets and area effect attacks/abilities things only get worse.- Cover shooter? NOPE! Cover is rendered mostly redundant by enemies spawning all around you 90% of the time,  instantly running around/ignoring/leaping/teleporting over it, or there simply not being any close enough to the fight to use (also enemies can only pursue you so far before retreating and become nigh invulnerable when they do, so leading them to a better killing ground often isnt an option).- All the above leads combat to be basically a war of attrition, feeling less dependant on skill and rather on mashing your best augs and whatever health packs dropped from enemies or nearby vendors to prop you up for the next fight.- Aiming/projectile collision is off. When mouse aiming theres a small reticle in addition your guns laser sight, however the two arent correctly aligned. Also, you'll often line up a shot and it'll sail harmlessly through the enemy (this could be general jank or just due to the games perspective which changes slightly and often to confuse things).- Apart from picking up an occasional new augmentation thats never as good as the spider mines you've basically seen everything gameplay-wise within about an hour. The core gameplay loop doesnt change and 15 hours in you'll be having the exact same broken firefights you were at the beginning, only with more annoying enemies.The Meh- RPG? You can put skill points into stats like health or crit chance etc but each increase is so minor its unnoticeable level to level and the game would be no worse off if these upgraded automatically ala Diablo 3. Shame theres no upgradable passives like in say Borderlands to tailor your character to a particular playstyle as this game seems perfect for it. - Armour attributes. Beyond increasing your ballistic/energy dmg resistance these seem mostly redundant, increasing them having no noticeable effect on gameplay. Better armour drops see sudden jumps in quality so its never worth hanging on to an earlier piece with worse dmg res just because it has '+2 to something you wont notice' on it.- Side missions. Dull. Trudge across the map, click a thing, return. None are interesting and most are given out in various irritating alien gibberish voices which you'll just click through to get it over with. Many are also locked behind story progression but the game doesnt tell you this, you'll just follow the waypoint to a building you cant enter or a character that isnt there and think its bugged.- Objective markers. While these will generally lead you to your objective via the shortest route, on several occasions they got confused and started switching directions suddenly or leading me into dead ends. Also some didnt show up at all on the large map, only the minimap.- Plot/Characters. The game technically has them but its all entirely forgettable even by stick shooter standards. This is a real shame as the world itself is so beautifully realised.- Getting stuck in scenery. This happened often enough to mention it but thankfully never required a reload. Annoying in the middle of combat naturally.One complaint I kept seeing crop up from review sites was about sudden difficulty spikes but I only really encountered this running into higher level areas I wasn't levelled for, never mid mission. I never felt I had to leave a mission and grind and come back later (which would be redundant anyway as a few extra skill points assigned wouldn't stop a boss crushing you).OVERALLProbably more fun coop where multiple players with different loadouts could outweigh some of the combat jankiness but solo this quickly began to feel like a repetitive slog. Hopefully devs will give the game some love via updates and tighten up the combat, as well as improve some of the less useful augments. While I cant recommend it for its solo gameplay you should probably still buy it if only to look at its sheer beauty until your eyes melt in neon orgasmic wonder...

_childDocuments_.review: This game might be worth it after some patches or on a sale. The concept is cool but its riddled with bugs.6 hours in and we have had:Game crashesplayers becoming invisible (sometimes needing to disconnect and re join)5+ "Lost Connect" errorsMissions not possible to complete because they glitchedMissions saying recommended level 6 and being to hard for a level 11The idea to the game is cool and the visuals look great. _childDocuments_.review: Avoid.+ stunning surroundings of hightec city on alien planet;+ nice visual effects;+ huge map to explore, gather loot and fight enemies;+ atmospheric music and sfx.- terrible too bright lights everywhere hurting eyes and making it hard to pass or, worse, fight there;- too much of useless backgrounds, silent crowd; after few minutes I start running through to a quest pointer, ignoring environment, even in new places, because there is nothing to hear, see or interact with;- terrible camera, it flips around changing view, confusing and making it hard to fight enemies or explore, perhaps this is a problem only on utlrawide resolutions;- stupid AI, ranged enemies run past you to a closest cover, melee runs directly to you, meaty mini-bosses;- lacking UI with awfully small health indicator, but huge number of bullets left (unimportant due to infinite ammo and fast reload);- no difficulty indicator, I often get one-shot by much higher level enemies shooting off-screen, entering such areas should trigger some kind of warning;- useless assistant, when it talks it's mostly garbage, but then important comment can be easily missed and there is no log or way to replay it;- no fast travel, running back forth all the way quickly become not fun, no sprint either;- bugs and crashes;- dialogues are generic, the information given in dialogues is way too complex (I had to switch to russian, otherwise I was overswarmed with lots of unknown terms I couldn't remember in English);- weapons and gear are too generic, the moment I found rocket launcher I only use that;- VERY hard to navigate map, no custom markers, no way to mark PoI for later (e.g. chests I can't hack yet), the PoI are shown with long pins, which make it harder to navigate even more;- map is not detailed, you can't find a way to a PoI, only general direction;- switching between quests require too many clicks;- hard to spot loot, as I already say game is way too bright, loot is barely visible when it drops, I often fight missed loot when running back to a quest giver lol;- dialogues have VERY small buttons to click, when it's a dialogues without UI, then I often shoot myself with rocket-launcher while trying to click very small "finish" or "continue" buttons;More likely I was expecting another game to buy, some corridor-like shooter with camera showing me surroundings from with good overview. What I got is some kind of semi-open-world game, where I have to take quests and run very long time back and forth, killing some enemies on my way. Enemies often comes from nowhere, which I dislike.I was hoping for better skills, which allow me to quickly move in a battle, disabling enemies, shooting, throwing grenades, etc. But the combat looks very awfully with too narrow view of too close camera (perhaps ultra-wide screen problem, I don't care), with stupid AI and some complex UI, where I have difficulty to choose between any piece of gear, simply because of lack of any kind of information.Games feels first of all very ambitious, but at the same time unfinished, poorly tested and unpolished. This is proven by generic model for ALL npcs in journal, worse, NPC names are not shown in-game, so I am talking to no-names. The rich surroundings are defeated by terrible camera, which makes me wish to quickly run past certain "beautiful" place, just for it to return back to an expected camera. I hate when in-game camera switches, it should only do so in cinematics and never ever when I am controlling the character.After completing just 3 side-quests I feel it's enough for me. Slow running, generic fights, terrible loot, poor skills, unclear everything (I don't want to watch tutorial videos explaining game, sorry).. I'll go back to play Cyberpunk 2077, sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: F**K this game. 5 hours of playtime and out of nowhere when going to launch it one day my save file is gone. 5 hours and I got that save file error everyone else complains about in the reviews. This is on perfectly functioning current gen hardware where there were no other system issues. 5 hours and here is what I remember from this piece of trash: This game is beautiful. The Art, Visual,  Sound and Level Design teams/people for this game did a fantastic job. Sincerely hope they all find work at far better companies. Whoever was in charge of the gameplay design mechanics should never work in the industry again. The travel system is painful. All movement in this game hurts. The combat system is so unfun, boring and complete trash that they have to convolute it with giant blocks of explaining text and meaningless weapon tiers and classes. The "Spell" system is also boring and unengaging and also comes with giant blocks of explaining text. Do you like that part where you get a new job and some clown sits you down infront of a bunch of power point slides to explain how things work around the place, for a stupidly long amount of time, only to find out that once you actually went to do your job none of that information even matters, because the whole place is actually held up by a bunch of complex systems of bulls**t that don't even need to exist and often operate to the detriment of the company, so you are just going to do your own thing anyway? That's this game. A game like this that has to force you to look at paragraphs of text to understand it is trying to explain why it doesn't suck, but it just does.
