_childDocuments_.review: First off, I will say that I am enjoying this game. I'm several hours in and wanted to compile some notes.The atmosphere, lore, world building, textures, and environments are absolutely nuts and like nothing I've experienced. And killing enemies is pretty fun and satisfying.Here are the slight cons that are preventing this game from being amazing:Invisible Side Mission Gates- Often times i will have a low level quests that I cannot access because I need to progress in the main mission first. The main mission quest being much higher in difficulty. Why offer a level 2 quest to the player, only to have them need to complete a level 10 quest first?- Additionally, nowhere does it describe that I need to progress in main mission first. I will find myself navigating toward a side quest icon only to have nothing happen because i can't access it yet.Multiple quests- Please let me track more than one quest at a time in my map. Unclear Armor/Weapon Icons- Weapons and armor have attributes associated with them that are somewhat unclear. It's hard to tell what equipping something is going to do.- Additionally, because there are several attributes on weapons and armor, when I find a new piece, it's hard to tell if this is going to better or not (this is an opinion, but i would prefer to have a more simplistic, step-function version of, yes this gun is much better than that gun, look at the green stats and up arrows.)Map is hard to read- The style of the map makes it incredible difficult to decipher. I find myself opening the map regularly to figure out where I am and if I'm going the right direction. It's also hard to tell where chests or quests are located because of the orientation and style of map. - I would much prefer a top down map in which I could toggle through the different levels (I understand this is probably not possible due to the layout of the deep environments in the game, where there are several levels)Enemy tuning- It's impossible to tell if I'm entering an area in which I'm not prepared for. Only after enemies have engaged are their levels revealed, often killing me immediately. Some sort of mini map indicator or visible enemy levels before aggro would help- Often times higher level enemies are mixed into areas with lower level enemies, making the item listed above create a confusing experience. If I had more knowledge of their levels beforehand, this obviously wouldn't be an issue.Tutorials- I read through all the tutorial information, but I am still googling things. (For example, I don't really know how to increase my ICE level).

_childDocuments_.review: You take all the good elements of the Diablo series (Cosby Room Free), Mass Effect 2, and the Cyberpunk 2077 that should have been released. You get the absolute gem The Ascent. The game manages to cherry pick elements of legendary games in the past, yet still manages to feel completely original. It's the best game of the year at the time of this writing.

_childDocuments_.review: Impressive and beautiful cyberpunk world. Amazing music... perfect for the setting. I went into the game thinking "Cyberpunk Diablo".  It's not. Very simple skill "tree" (more like a branch-less trunk), basic item customization (you level up your weapons), only a few weapon categories, and no real classes. The story didn't really pull me in.  It's a very pretty and atmospheric cyberpunk game but you essentially just run around and shoot stuff.  Still recommended but you won't be replaying this down the road like you probably did with Diablo or Torchlight.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I wanted to like this game and I only have 1 hour of play time in it but I've probably watched another 5 or so hours of game play and my friend is the one who convinced me to finally give it a try. The story (like most have said) is boring, the character creation is dull, and while the game does undoubtedly look good the scenes get incredibly repetitive but, none of those things are why I don't recommend this game.Here's my experience: Started the game off, made my character and proceeded to go find dude in room after walking through hallways. Please not I am using a Xbox controller. Shortly into the game I was prompted to open the map and WHOA - the slightest movement of the analog stick had me bouncing around menus all over the damn place which gets REALLY annoying but, no matter ill use the D-pad. Sweet. 5-10 minutes in the first annoying bug hit me. All the map icons (which I thankfully only had chests on my map) started sticking on even when I exited the map. They stayed on even after I closed the map and after I opened the chest. So now I'm playing with map icons all over my screen. No biggie whatever keep rolling. I open my map again a little later when trying to find something and come to find out the chest I just opened was now stuck to my map cursor meaning I could move the icon around on the map itself. Cherry on top when I closed the map the icon was where I left it. So now I have icons on my screen and a map that doesn't work because the icons aren't in the correct spot. I could literally move the map icon into the "blackness" of the map. At this point I'm annoyed, not happy but hey kinda cool to shoot things blow stuff up... so I press on. I finish the first part of my mission and reset the "SI" and then the door locks down or whatever and then I encountered a game breaking bug. I could no longer shoot. Yes. In a twin stick shooter I couldn't shoot either of my weapons. I could throw grenades though. I tried to just make a break for it and roll my way through the mission tapping "A" like my life depended on it (which it did) to no avail. I died. Thinking reloading the game after death might solve my problems I quit and try again and I *poop* you not - same thing happened. In total I encountered 3 different bugs one of which was game breaking in less than 1 hour of playing and about 10-20 minutes of that was character creation & paused to help my GF move something. I cannot recommend a game with this many bugs this far out from release and still pushing new content. Fix whats here before releasing new things that also probably contain more bugs. Very disappointing and I will not be trying this again for a long time.Game Play 5/10Story 2/10Game Quality 1/10Controls 5/10Graphics 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended on Sale!Its a fun game and much to explore. An interesting desolate urban world with lots of violence and interesting back story. The world is interesting to explore with lots of pockets of violence and action around every. The environment is very attention grabbing with lots going on. Though after a while it can all seem a bit similar. Interesting world but constant stream of enemies... everywhere. Why are they targeting me constantly... Ever re spawning enemies to deal with... I think that really got to me as sometimes it made no realistic sense for them to keep attacking me. And those guys attacking me in the posher parts of the middle layer made even less sense.The customisation of the character is severely limited. you can add on armour and weapon and then some augmentation though the game makes it seems like these augmentations are a lot more impressive then they are... and your limited to two.... The story keeps the game going and the constantly changing environment. Though the game seems to hit a ceiling fast... and what do i use all these bloody ucreds for... after a while they were somewhat pointless.Its not a bad game really. I think it just lost its luster near the end as i was just trying to finish it. The last level ramps up the difficulty fast for some reason. I was playing easy for good sake. The developers really decided to go all "f*** y**" on the last level with enemies multiplied by 10 and harder to kill suddenly.  It really turned the game from rpg to murder valley fast.FURTHER UPDATE To be honest i think the last levels ruined it for me mostly as it really became enemy around every corner which i can't stand. Its just not realistic. The DLC seems to mirror and somewhat intensify that last level alot of constant stream of enemy. Really kills any want for exploration which is an issue as theirs a lot to see in both the main and DLC. DLC is far worse for it though and the main game world is quite interesting when you have a space to breath.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome Diablo-like game, but with a cyberpunk theme.  The atmosphere and music is heavily influenced by Blade Runner and Ghost in the Shell, so if you're into that type of Sci-Fi, this game is for you.  The story is mediocre, but the game play is where it's at.  The fight sequences are pretty engaging and can come at you pretty fast, so the pace can pick up in no time.  Running around with that music score in the background and sound effects are just great, the gun fire and explosions in this game is intense, so headphones are a must.  The character building is not bad either.  Plenty of options to go through and you can change your choices later in the game as well at the Grafter, nice touch should you want to change up your character and allocate your skills.  The hacking aspect of the game is a nice touch.  You get to open up harder loot crates and areas of the map as you progress and get better equipment and tech.  Also, the game has a choice for co-op for up to 4 players, local or online, should you want to switch up on a solo mission.  This game is just so damn good looking, the graphics and art style is just superb, great job that the devs did on this. Worth every penny in my opinion, just so much fun playing this.

_childDocuments_.review: I think my recommendation comes down to one thing:Right from the start of the game, you can wander a few steps away from the path the designers want you to take and get nuked by a mob that's like 5 times as leveled as you. One or two shots and you're down. You get one warning the first time you enter an area like this that doesn't really make it clear the area ahead is way out of your league, and after that it happens just about any time you wander off the beaten path. In a game like this, I want to explore and see all of an area, but I'm discouraged from doing so unless I want to continuously get one shotted by random mobs lurking about.I just can't fathom the design choices that culminated in, "let's not let the player explore too much."
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty completionist, and I finished the game probably 1 hour ago.  Single playthrough, 1 character.  Do I recommend it?  Definitely... if you like Diablo 1 and 2.  It is basically that, in a cyberpunk world with aliens.  LOTS of running around and shooting stuff and blowing it up.  Wish there was more uses of hacking.  Is it the best story?  No... but for what it is, it isn't bad.  Are there a bunch of different valid and fun character builds?  Yes... but it will be even better when they release this next DLC with melee weapons.  There are plenty of enemies with them... yet, for some reason, you can't buy them, pick them up, or equip them.  That is a bummer.  I heard this upcoming DLC will let you play after beating the game... so fully intend to download it and then try out the new stuff, to include the melee weapons.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game for the price point, I played through it with Co-Op the entire way. Amazing visuals (on a 1060 mind you), good gunplay, and a great take on the CyberPunk genre. While the story ramps up linearly and then just... ends... sometimes it's fun to just go around mowing down enemies indiscriminately, while being chastised by your CO with how expensive it is to keep you off the bounty boards due to the now-dead civvies that got in the way.We did run into a few crashes, mainly when my Co-Op partner would loot something or buy something he "wasn't allowed to", but otherwise nothing game breaking, and the auto saves were timely enough to not loose too much progress.9/10, even at full ($30) price for this game.

_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: While I do recommend the game as it is pretty fun, there are a few glaring negatives to the over all gameplay experienceThe biggest and probably most aggravating is the fact that while you can fast travel to places, if you are trying to figure out where to go during a mission it DOES NOT actually highlight where you need to fast travel to to be anywhere near the mission zone.  If you don't fast travel, you have to walk(there is no run just like in games Just Cause, and it's rather annoying when combined with the lack of proper waypointing).  These two things combined mean you end up either spending several minutes fast travelling from point to point to see if you are closer, or just walking to the area as that's usually the least painful option.  The game is pretty unoptimzed, consistent lag spikes, and random bugs all over the place.  Overall even with the few glaring issues I have, it is a fun twin stick shooter with plenty of variety and a nice little playground to run around in, I'd say watch some breakdowns that really dive into the positives and negatives to see if it's something you can tolerate.

_childDocuments_.review: A simple test: Read the following words and short phrases, and consider how they make you feel:-Hyper detailed backgrounds-Interstellar Cyberpunk Dystopia-Isometric reaction-based combat-Being able to punch people so hard they literally disintegrate-Twin Stick ShooterDo any of these items, in combination or isolation, elicit a positive reaction from you? If so, you should look closer at this game. If not, do not look closer at this game. (Limitations apply, the game was apparently buggy for a lot of people, I have encountered none so far, which is probably due to luck and definitely not due to any effort on my side.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Mass effect and cyberpunk had a child which later started dating warhammer 40k. Mass effect for the aliens and lore, cyberpunk for the general look its known for and warhammer for the awesome design of a city hive and some of its weapons. A top down scroller game, easy to get in and mod your character in decent ways, interchangeable skills, builds with basically no restrictions other than what they give you. Shooting is fun, giving us a nice combo of quick shoot outs where you can actually take cover, dodge or just tank through the damage depending on the situation. Ennemy Ai's can be pretty decent in some levels taking to cover and flanking. The story was quite cool, opening up the veniew to an entire world/universe that I would love to revisit. Would honestly pay for offshoots of this game with no problem. Currently doing new game+ and really debating going for a full achievment unlock.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had exceeded the expectations I had for Cyberpunk 2077. I highly recommended it 100%. The story is okay; nonetheless, the RPG elements, sounds, visuals, weapons, augmentations, hacking, etc makes up for it. You won't regret your purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game! Gets the theme, aesthetic and linguo perfect. A lot of it just feel straight out of a William Gibson book. The visuals are incredible, the voice work is great and the combat is really fun with lots of options. The isometric view felt perfect to show the verticality of the world and make the cover based combat cool.There is some rough spots that feel a bit weird. I had 4 crashes during my playthrough, also the first time it booted up it auto picked 4k resolution and slowed down to a crawl. My biggest complain is not being able to properly select windowed fullscreen at my monitors proper resolution. With the 1080p monitor it would default to 4k in windowed fullscreen. With the 1440p monitor it picked a weird stretched resolution to extend to two monitors. Weird. Also, DLC achievements without the DLC being in sight of release is lame.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: it's like Diablo meets Remnant: From the Ashes.  I wouldn't quite call it a souls-like, but all the rpg elements from those games are there.  Unlike Borderlands and Diablo, you're not going to get a million copies of items with incrementally better stats the whole game - rather each item (weapon, armor, ability) is predefined in the game and specific to certain builds or approaches.  Co-op shares items with friends instead of everyone fighting over them.  And the world building is spectacular.  The areas you go are well-populated and feel alive.  Great sound design too, which really immerses the player in the world far more than the visuals can.Cons: sometimes the game likes to crash, and when it does, you're locked out from your desktop/task manager.  The workaround is to press windows-key+tab and move to a different desktop to open your task manager to kill the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The only complaint that could be lobbied at this game is that, for how excellent it is, it's just not long enough.Meaning to say that, while the game IS quite fantastic, and isn't really a short game, it's so excellent that you'll definitely wish it was way longer. I think it has to do with aRPGs often being the kind of genre that players expect some sort of nearly endless endgame from. That isn't what you find here. It's a few dozen hours of a really solid game-play experience, then it's pretty much done. You could start all over again, but it's not really going to mean a fundamentally different game-play experience.Still, don't let that stop you from making this purchase if it is at all interesting to you. There's a lot to do, the environments and atmosphere are absolutely top-notch, and the game-play itself is very good, if just a tad short of excellence. Don't get me wrong, the game IS fun to play, extremely fun, to be honest. It's just not as "oh my God, how is this even possible?" as the world that the game takes place in.Seriously, the arcology, the setting, the feeling of being in the world you're dropped into... It really is remarkably well-done. Should you buy the game? Hey, I'm not going to tell you what to do, that would be awfully presumptuous and bossy of me. Would I buy this game? Dumb question, I already did. Would I buy it again, if it somehow got erased from my library? Well, after fussing and getting angry and going on Reddit to complain about it like it's some sort of effective strategy of fixing the world's problems, then cooling down for a few months before realizing that changed absolutely nothing...Yeah, probably.

_childDocuments_.review: Just stunning, the attention to detail is amazing. Neon Giant really have created a fantastic atmospheric environment with a believable cyberpunk feel. You can almost feel the grit and grime on the lower levels as you wander around. It's simple levelling and weapon upgrading system is nothing over complicated and a welcome change as it really doesn't need to be anymore than that.Coop makes it even better, however excluding steam users from playing with gamepass users is bonkers and one of it's minor flaws, but it is what it is and probably not their choice. I would happily say for the 4.5 hours I have played I feel that I have already had great value for the money and do hope they bring DLC to this game at some point in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I had to tab out of this game to write a review.I am not far into this game, but seriously I cannot get over how amazing the visuals are. Neon Giant absolutely nailed, going on over performed, the cyberpunk world encompassing archaeology. its a vertical mega city of awesome scale and detail...  They know it, and show it off. The camera will pan to show you something huge in the distance surrounded by tech, wires, and conduits. Honestly for anyone that likes this type of scifi its worth the buy just for the visuals.Game play wise I've had nothing but fun. Mostly it isn't easy-- you can't just circle strafe enemies (or use auto rifles a la Biomutant). Controls are fluid, progression is  consistent and the dual stick shooter with a modern twist of high/low shots is really awesome. Easily one of my favorite games played in 2021.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game was surprisingly very good. The city environments are straight out of a cyberpunk Star Wars world with a variety of alien species and neon signs galore and the music is right in line with those themes. Twin stick shooters were fun but not anything special to me in the past, but this game gave the genre a more tactile feel with new (to me) combat elements to keep it challenging and engaging. Played it once through, then once again NG+ in only a few hours the 2nd time through. Plenty of RPG elements for customization and intriguing story and side quests to keep you interested.Graphics are pretty demanding, especially with ray tracing, but even on lowest settings the game looks amazing. Definitely worth a play.

_childDocuments_.review: CyberPunk 2077 meets Blade Runner meets Diablo.  AMAZING. This game is so achingly beautiful to look at, the devs really gave it some love.  I wish you could rotate the view around, or zoom in/out like in Diablo/Grim Dawn, but that's not a deal breaker. This game is so much fun. 3 hrs in, and I can see another 30 hrs in my immediate future. I've been looking for something different from all the Diablo clones, and I finally found it. YEAH!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game that Cyberpunk 2066 should aspire to be! The style, grittiness, visuals! There is so much eye candy that really put you in the mood of the game! The combat can be a bit tricky at first but you soon get used to combing all of your assets when things get crazy! A few bugs here and there but nothing ground/game breaking! If you love loot shooters, get this game! Everything is amazing about it and I cannot wait for the developers to add to it!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite all its flaws, I cannot not recommend The Ascent. This game represents fun. A lot of fun. I wish it was perfect in its execution so I wouldn'd have any hesitation into recommending it. It's not. There are a few bugs that will force you to restart some missions. Nothing gamebreaking for me yet so I'm willing to let this one go through.The opacity of the game systems and the paper thin tutorial did not help but after a few hours I had a pretty good grip on what the game wanted me to do. And I'm loving it. Every second of it.I know it's a personal preference thing, but the theme, the music, the art direction, everything is on point. Something I haven't seen in other reviews is the stellar work they did for the voice acting (especially the Poone guy).Wait for a discount if not sure. _childDocuments_.review: The Ascent is a solid top down fixed point of view shooter.  I love the worldbuilding, and I think the art and soundtrack are absolutely outstanding.  During my online co-op playthrough, my partner and I thankfully didn't encounter as many game-breaking bugs as other reviews implied.  (There was a crash every 5-6 hours or so though.)  I wish there was a bit more weapon variety, more interesting side quests and well, just more game to play.  Looking forward to returning to this game to play any DLCs/Expansions though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this from beginning to end, and looking forward to anything else from this studio in the future. Tons of weapons, skills, mods, and augments to switch around for different encounters & play styles, and felt top notch to use. Visually it has the most impressive and detailed environments I've ever seen in a game.Very few cons over all. Biggest for me was the map, and how quest objectives are displayed on the map. It did function correctly the entire game, but was difficult to understand at times. In 28 hours played only 1 crash and a hand full of minor bugs (stuck in environmental objects), otherwise ran perfect.Great experience, high quality product, would definitely recommend: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I have never left a review but I felt compelled to leave one for this game. I usually play FPS but have been looking for a entertaining immersive game that is relaxing to play. I waited excitedly for Cyberpunk because I was attracted to the futuristic large world Cyberpunk theme. This game delivers what I expected Cyberpunk to and even more by it being based on  different planet. I have had it 24 hrs and have left the game going since . I woke up several times last night and played as I could not get enough.Its easy to hop in and play as the action is broken up evenly .  I normally would not off downloaded this game but stumbling by a stream made me get it. Now I wonder if my decision to really only play main stream shooters have made me miss games like this one. I wonder why this is not the #1 stream this weekend on Twitch. I hope the studio great success with this title.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so I literally just finished the main game. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastically fun, with beautifully detailed environments just dripping with style, and effortless multiplayer. From a ludicrously small dev team, this game punches above its weight class in every way. And at $30, it's an absolute steal. If you dig the genre, or are just looking for a fun twin-stick shooter with friends, this is your ticket.There's a handful of bugs, but because it's so easy to hop in and out of co-op games, their impact is (mostly) negligible. Do yourself a favor and pick this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: ***Steam Deck Playability is nearly perfect. A top tier for the handheld.***Performance - 8/10Gameplay - 7/10Graphics - 8/10Style & Sound - 9/10Story - 6/10This game is way better than it was on release. Originally I tried this game on release (gamepass) and it was a bit of a buggy mess, but seemed to have potential.  The only bug I have encountered that halts the game is it can hang occasionally on start up on Steam Deck specifically, but all you have to do is close game and re-launch, once into the game it isnt a problem. Well, here we are, the expansion released and I picked it up on sale as a bundle as I heard it had become a staple game for Steam Deck.  Well, it is. It runs incredibly well on the Steam Deck and on my desktop (of course.), and looks gorgeous on both. I cant believe how well optimized this game has become since  release. I have played 5 hours as of writing this and I cant put it down, i played all 5 hours in one day on a day off. Absolutely fantastic stick shooter with co-op (Both Couch and online.). Story is great, graphics are a gorgeous cyberpunk fantasy world and it has a fantastic soundtrack to top it off. The one down side that I can say is the game hits a STEEP difficulty wall around 6 hours in when you start fighting a lot of robots. Electrical firing weapons help but the enemies begin to come in pretty big swarms that fire things like rockets to push you out of cover and just have a lot more armour/health and I find that I end up dying A LOT more often around here. It never feels impossible, but I would understand if some folks got frustrated with it around there. Whats even weirder, is turning from regular difficulty to easy really doesn't make it much easier either, you'll still find you die a lot. So if you dont like your games challenging, this might not be for you. Absolutely recommended otherwise, especially on the steam deck.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my favourite game of 2021. Really good gameplay, surprising weapon variety and incredible graphics with amazing vistas. Your characters look even changes depending on stat allocation, your character becoming my cybernetic the more stats are allocated into cybernetic/mechanical stats.Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to like it for the atmosphere and subject matter, but the FOV is claustrophobic.   The deal breaker though was the choppy controls. _childDocuments_.review: Single player seems to be working okay, but co op is still very buggy. The host will mostly be fine, but the person joining will probably be screwed. Things don't save for them, they can lose their cyberdeck, gear, quest rewards...The game is interesting and fun to play. Story is pretty good. _childDocuments_.review: This game is nice to look at but just isn't satisfying to play. Other reviews say the game is short, but for me it is even shorter because I don't even want to play it or finish it anymore.I feel like I spent more time in this game walking from place to place than shooting things. A train and taxi system can take you to areas you've already been to, but if you're going to a new area for the first time (which you will do a lot.) you'll have to do it on foot without a run/sprint button. It does give you time to marvel at the game environments, but 95% of the time I just wanted to get to the next part of the game already.The RPG aspect of the game is weak. You can put points into stats like reload speed (the only stat that actually feels like it matters), max health/energy, faster spread reduction, etc. but it doesn't amount to your character being very different from another person's. There are special abilities and you do have some choices there, but most of the time you will be using your guns so these choices don't feel very important either (high energy costs and long cooldowns on some of these don't help).You can carry two guns, but the currency for upgrading is so scarce that you might as well upgrade and use one gun for the entire game. Your second gun's usefulness is also limited by the fact that you can reduce your first gun's reload speed to basically nothing.This would all be fine if the game had good action, but it's just too easy after the first hour. It doesn't take long for the player to outscale the enemies, at which point you can beat most encounters with the forbidden technique of moving and shooting at the same time. There's a higher difficulty setting but all it does is give enemies more health/damage, kiting is still just as effective.These problems could be fixed but as it is I can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. As a fan of anything cyberpunk, this game hits the mark for me. Gorgeous graphics and as a shooter it is fun. This gamer has enough content to satisfy your hunger for anything cyberpunk and science fiction. I had a blast playing it. I do admit  I enjoy anything cyberpunk so I'm sucker for these kind of games.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing shooter!The game is beautiful and fun to play, and the combat is engaging enough that you have to pay attention but its not too hardcore where you have to have nano second reflexes to do well. I am also very happy that this game is not trying to be one of those infinite looter grinders, the stuff you get is set in stone (there is random drops) but the stats are hand crafted. To some this is bad thing but I like it more than chasing after that unicorn of a loot for hours on end.The games world is just amazing. It is so detailed and even when it is just cybercity, it still feels varied and colorful. The has been many times when I just stop shooting and just stand there listening the beautiful music and just watching in awe the locations. This is one of those games I wish I would get a closer look at but what we are given here is just pure gold.After 10 hours I have not encountered any major game breaking bugs, few game halting ones but those were fixed with a reseting the game. They are annoying, but hopefully they will be fixed.This games biggest issue is its UI. Some of the icons are just too damn hard to read, some of the mechanics are maybe messed and not working properly and the UI does not tell you well. ICE mechanics is one of these. The game says I can open ICE1 chests, but when I approach one it stays locked, but when I go to ICE2 chest they open. The map is also one that can and will cause you trouble at first but once you figure out the layout and how it works the map becomes very easy to read, but that too would need some more work.Overall this is worth buy and your time, IF you like simple shooters like this. This is not Diablo3 like hack&slasher loot fest, but more streamlined game where you can find the best bazooka right of the bat if you know where to go.I hope the devs will fix the games biggest problems and bugs and keep giving us more of this amazing world because I just want more and I have not even finished the game yet and I hate DLCs but if they make more for this game I am there on day1 getting it!Thank you Neon Giant for this amazing and fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is DOPE. If Syndicate Wars had a baby with Diablo, this would be that game. About 11 hours in and loving every minute. Solo player. Combat is very well balanced between the feeling of being a real badass, and then underestimating a fight and getting crushed. The design of the game is second-to-none, truly. The most immersive and amazing environments in a game I have ever seen, so so well done. I wish there was more depth to the loot, but I also appreciate that you don't have to grind endlessly for that one derivation of an item, or farm a boss for some unique drop. I'll drop an edit after I beat the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, well designed, and I would recommend for anyone looking for a twin stick arcade shooter... BUTThis game is not Cyberpunk Diablo, so don't go into it thinking that it is. It has a story, ,and had dialogue with some voiceover, but it is not an RPG in the sense that your responses and decisions matter... It just has RPG elements to give it depth and flavour.There are some minor bugs and QoL improvements to be made, but it still feels very polished. For instance, the automatic enemy scaling ramps out of control, causing automatic death every so often becasue there is no way you can defeat the overpowered enemies it throws at you if you've been playing a while. After dying the scaling resets back to an appropriate level against your character, but the cycle eventually happens again.Side missions need alerts if you do not meet the requirements to access the zones, otherwise you go on a long trek for nothing.One minor gripe is that I wish the game had melee weapons. I feel like having a 3rd weapon  slot dedicated to melee would round out the combat a little better so you didn't have to kite as much.Needs a bit of refinement on the raytracing side of things, but not a dealbreaker.Game immediately gave me Total Recall vibes. Everyone says it's Bladerunner, but I felt the colours, design and background story lent itself more to the subjugation aspect of Total Recall than Bladerunner.Game is well made, properly priced and you will like it if you enjoy twin stick shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I just finished this and figured I'd leave a review before I decide if I want the DLC.TL;DRThis isn't a looter shooter or random drop arpg like Borderlands or the Diablo franchise. Yes, it's about movement and aim, but there's more emphasis on cover, and the loot progresses like you would expect in a traditional RPG (linear progression with no variables). Weapons feel good, but some are clearly better than others. Abilities feel good but there aren't enough of them. Story and voice work is great, but the ending falls a little flat. About 15 hours for 30 bucks, but I got it on sale for like 10 or 15. 7/10Pros♫ Unreal 4 still looks great, especially on top down games like this.♪ The music SLAPS in a lot of places.♫ Immersion felt great (so great sound design and pacing)♪ There's a lot of running around, but there's a rudimentary fast travel system that semi works.♫ Gun play is fun. It's the reason to buy the game. Play co-op.♪ You can just upgrade the gun you like instead of being forced to change weapons for dps gains.Cons♫ The game isn't well optimized, at least for my setup. I had constant stuttering in some areas, I generally didn't notice.♪ Bosses just kind of disappear when you kill them. At least, that's what it felt like. I was really struggling to see any kind of cool death animation for any boss fight (except for one that gets a cut scene), and it felt anti-climactic.♫ The fast travel system doesn't do a good job of telling you how close to your target you are going to be. I think there was one time where maybe my hud marker showed up in the fast travel menu, but I couldn't get it to happen again after that, so maybe buggy?♪ Co-op crashed a few times. I've heard that some people lost saves, but this didn't happen to me.♫ Not particularly big in scope. That can be a good thing, because the story didn't drag, and I loved the set pieces that were there. I just wish there were more that I didn't have to buy.♪ New Game Plus incentive felt weak without variable gear drops with mods and rare loot sets. Maybe that isn't the case, but if so, the game did sh|t job of explaining that when the new game plus prompt appeared.♫ Side quests are varied and interesting, but there's not much incentive to do those either other than story, which isn't terrible, but didn't catch my attention.

_childDocuments_.review: The Ascend is a fun game that is held back by some of its flaws that ultimately limit the experience. If you can overlook some of its weaker points, it is certainly worth the purchase if the gameplay looks appealing to you. For the 20+ hours I spent playing I came away with an enjoyable Isometric action experience that blends together a variety of concepts ranging from RPG's to shooters in a Cyberpunk setting. At its core the game is all about shooting things with various weapons, with a little bit of story, setting, loot and passive skill-points mixed in. There are several things that the Ascend does well at the cost of a range of things it doesn't do so well.The Cyberpunk world looks solid and breathes atmosphere that helps make it come alive down to the gritty details. From civilians roaming the streets to neon-lit signs, the game captures the feeling it set out to bring to players. The only detriment being the quality of the character models, which occasionally fail to live up to the quality of the surrounding environments. Unfortunately, the main character is no exception, coming with a tiny amount of customization options and occasionally suffering from various clipping issues in regards to the various equipment you find around the world.The core gameplay the Ascend offers is fun, though limited. The game offers a variety of weapons, including various types that offer benefits against certain enemies, but never really explores the system of strengths and weaknesses beyond the superficial. Sooner or later raw firepower wins out even on the hard difficulty. The various armor you find throughout the game works in much the same way with the same flaws. On the shooting side the variety of weapons the game offers mostly do a fine job of creating variety while fighting your way through a variety of enemies that employ different weapons and tactics.  The game's focus on action and carnage ultimately could have used an even wider variety of enemies to spruce up some of its encounter design, which tends to boil down to running and gunning your way through. The various augments and tactical equipment the player can equip to grant them unique abilities help keep things fresh, though I found some of them underwhelming compared to others. The game does have a few other hit-and-miss points. Some of the boss encounters are relatively well designed allowing players to shoot and dodge their way through their unique move-sets but others come down to fighting off waves of enemies for a set period of time. Though novel the first time, the concept is reused several times and the encounters don't always feel very engaging. The issue is further compounded considering that most of these encounters face off the player against the regular enemies they've already been shooting up for hours by this point. One of the unique elements to the Ascend is its isometric camera angle in combination with the core run and gun gameplay. The angle works well with the actual core gameplay and creates a unique experience. The game also uses various camera angles to highlight some of the impressive environmental pieces that highlight the atmosphere. Unfortunately, this occasionally comes at the cost of actual gameplay as the camera occasionally shifts around at odd angles. Some of these stylistic angles can cause enemies to disappear behind objects, put the player off-center in the middle of a fight or simple witch to a point of view that doesn't work well with the top down run and gun style gameplay. Aside from cut-scenes and the occasional set-piece outside of a combat zone I would have much preferred for the camera angle to just remain fixed. The story and world-building is another point where the Ascend tries to make an impact but doesn't completely succeed. The civilians that go about their business and ultimately get in the way of your firefights only to end up a red smear on the concrete make the world feel alive. The game also makes a notable effort to explain its setting and some of the unique elements from indentured servitude to corporations to super AI's that run entire cities. The story itself takes some of these elements to try and weave a unique narrative but falls flat in its delivery. Supporting characters feel somewhat bland and though the narrative is interesting and actually has some decent twist, the delivery of said plot points often leaves a lot to be desired. This is a shame because with better exposition and supporting characters the story would probably make a larger impact. The fact the main character doesn't talk and seems to have no opinion on anything compounds the issue and leaves the player feeling detached.The Ascend is very much a diamond in the rough that could have been even better but still delivers a very decent game that is a worth a playthrough. If you don't demand perfection and are content with shooting up hordes of baddies in a unique Cyberpunk world that features some creative ideas in both gameplay and setting, the Ascend will be a very enjoyable experience. If you're looking for a game with lots gameplay depth, encounter variety, and a thrilling delivery of narrative you may want to pass this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: It's...okay. I play it, because it's pretty easy to pick up and play for 20min at a time on a Steam Deck, and I like the environments, but the gameplay is pretty forgettable. This is a very, very weak recommend.Pros:+ The world has lots going on. It feels very alive, and there's NPCs everywhere. It certainly looks and feels like a future plutocratic dystopia.+ The VAs do a great job.+ The sound design is very good.Cons:- For a looter-shooter, there's not much loot. No RNG random guns a la Borderlands.- You are an "everyman," but instead of feeling open-ended, you feel like a replaceable nobody.- No classes. Guns are your "class."- The guns feel lifeless. Guns get stronger by upgrading them with a special currency, after which you'll find another gun that's slightly better but performs similarly.- Enemies are kinda dumb. The melee guys zerg you. The gun guys shoot at you. Some take cover, and most just stand out in the open. Bosses were unique, though.- Menus are kinda messy.Overall, I'm more enjoying being in the world than the actual core gameplay This would be a great setting for a detective game, but the combat is pretty stale. I hope they keep making games, because they obviously have a good eye for world design.

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely rules, the art and environment are amazing (I followed this game because Tor Frick is my personal hero). Yes, there are some very annoying bugs, but it definitely skews in the "still worth it" territory. It's also a game that would really do well with some quality of life improvements (i.e. making it easier to understand enemy weaknesses and more streamlined fast travel systems - the taxi/monorail system is a bit annoying).I can definitely see how people say it has a Diablo, Twin Stick Shooter, Cyberpunk vibe and that feels fair and accurate. It throws a lot of the same loot at you, but I found myself upgrading weapons/gear at a fast enough rate to feel like there are enough options, but slow enough to where I'm not just constantly changing what I'm wearing (well, apart from optimizing gear for specific fights and stuff like that).

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid 8/10 for me. Impressive debut from a small studio.I don't remember exactly how I came across this game, but it looked good, was inexpensive, and reminded me a lot of Ruiner - so I bought it. Glad I did because it was an enjoyable experience. First and foremost, the atmosphere and look of this game is really great. The graphics (in relation to the art style) are excellent. With the good soundtrack, cool lighting and locations, and full sound design, it's really easy to get immersed in the world. even though you're watching from above. That's what I remember the most tbh, the mood and atmosphere. It's just very aesthetically pleasing.The gameplay is fun, too. I'm one to stick to the same couple guns, but I never got bored. Sure, running through the city over and over can get pretty tiring as a swarm of high-octane enemies will come flying at you every time, but you got fast travel so. Getting into a giant mech and cutting down crowds of enemies with a mini gun was very satisfying, as was deploying explosive spiders. Shootouts are electric. I'm glad they added transmogs because my outfit was looking a bit scuffed the way I was wearing armor for stats. Still looked decent because the individual pieces themselves weren't ugly and matched colors thanks to the dye system. I digress. Progression was well-tuned. Don't remember many pf the bosses or major encounters. Some, like the final boss, or the one where you get to the top of the tower, stay in mind. The side quests were actually pretty engaging, I still remember a couple of them. And I enjoyed doing them so that helps. Other side content, like bounty hunting and collectibles, isn't a pain (you'll naturally find all the codex stuff if you explore all over, it wasn't annoying). I liked bounty hunting and turning in a giant list of names to bartenders. The characters are fun to interact with and the writing itself doesn't take itself too seriously. Lots of comedic moments, lines, and situations, especially with the AI character you have during the game. The story besides the main objective isn't memorable but that isn't the focus in this game. Gameplay and progression definitely come first. You start at the very bottom and fight your way up to the top, unlocking new areas as you rise. The Japanese region is awesome with its neon lighting and rain, as is the corpo peak with its elegant design and uniquely bright, clear sky. It's very satisfying to get stronger and see your progression in so many ways. Like you really made it! Some awesome set pieces in here as well.The DLC was really short and essentially more of the same, so buy at your own risk. If you thoroughly enjoyed the experience of the base game, it's worth checking out the DLC. The new area is cool and has a nice score. The climax is awesome with heavv rain, a train section and a corpo-military base on the water. Unfortunately short and mostly forgettable, though.I don't have too many major complaints with this game, I just don't know if it's incredible enough to warrant a higher score. Like this doesn't feel higher than an 8/10 but it's definitely worth looking at if you're interested.Finished the main game on August 30th, 2021 and finished the Cyber Heist DLC on October 3rd, 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: Stunningly beautiful, it is perhaps one of the most aesthetically comprehensive experiences I ever had. Well, at least audiovisually, it is the best cyberpunk city in videogames for sure.The gameplay is not very challenging and quite simple, but not that much to consider it boring (it should be fun to play it co-op, can you imagine having friends to play with?).The plot is ok, but is just as optional as lore, side quests, background dialogues and notes. I'd call the plot filler: it is not bad, but it starts from nowhere and leads to nowhere, pure exploitation in fascinating decorations.I didn't notice any significant bugs, although it did crash once.Overall, I recommend it and plan to buy DLC as well.

_childDocuments_.review: A better cyber punk game then Cyberpunk2077.   - It looks great, some really nice set pieces thrown in now and then and overall the world has the right vibe. - Good voice acting, music and general sound design.- The combat is repetitive but I never got bored of it, however some mind find it a bit tiresome after a while.- The travel between location does get boring/tedious though, could do with a much better fast travel system. Overall I got to the end of the game (completed all main and side missions) and wanted more, so that says a lot.EDIT: I should add that I bought this on sale (-33%) and recommend it based on that. I don't reccomend it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: You belong to the corporation. Can you survive without it? The Ascent is a solo and co-op action RPG set in a cyberpunk world. The mega corporation that owns you and everyone, The Ascent Group, has just collapsed. Confusion and chaos ensue, security and order are in disarray, and without protection, everyone is left to fend for themselves. Stop gangs and hostile corporations from taking over and discover what really happened.

name: Gordian Quest
detailed_description: Discord About the Game A sinister curse corrupts the land. Darkness reigns. Monsters roam. Scoundrels loot. Cowards flee. Heroes emerge. Lead heroes on an adventure to save what’s left of this fallen world and destroy the root of evil abound. Will you fall at the claws of your enemies or the consequences of your poor decisions? Your Gordian Quest is about to begin. Gordian Quest is an epic deckbuilding RPG inspired by old-school classics like Ultima and D&D, using modern gaming concepts like roguelite elements and turn-based strategic combat. You will form parties of heroes whom you will have to lead and manage on grueling missions. Help them forge bonds and discover new skills among them. Be fearless and unwavering as you work to unravel the curses laid upon the lands and defeat the ultimate evil at the heart of it all. Feature List Campaign Mode - Venture through 4 Acts, taking you from the troubled lands of Westmire to the enigmatic Sky Imperium, in an epic journey to save the land of Wrendia. Realm Mode - A frenetic and fast-paced roguelite mode. Challenge an ever-changing version of the game with unpredictable threats and rewards. Complete 5 realms, or take on an endless challenge to see how far you can go. Adventure Mode - An end-game mode where you can explore procedurally generated areas or take on solo challenges. Skirmish Mode - A 1v1 mode were you pit your party of three against a friend. Ten heroes - Each with their own unique class, skills, and playstyle to form a party of three and bring to adventure. Play as the Swordhand, Cleric, Ranger, Scoundrel, Spellbinder, Druid, Bard, Warlock, Golemancer, or the Monk. Hundreds of skills - The heroes have a combined total of close to 800 passive and active skills that can be deployed during turn-based battles, allowing players to discover and formulate their favorite combos. Train and equip heroes - Heroes can be upgraded, trained and equipped with a large selection of weapons, armor and enchanted trinkets to enhance their abilities. High replayability - Procedurally generated maps and dungeons and randomized hero skills make each playthrough different from the last. Various difficulty levels - Take on hardcore mode for a teeth-gritting permadeath experience, or play more casually where death is only a setback. Loot galore - Gather items and relics throughout your journey to boost your heroes’ abilities. In the future, you will also encounter mysterious items that can bless your heroes but also cripple them with a curse at the same time. Carryover rewards and progression system - Get rewarded the more you play through an Artifacts system that can benefit Realm Mode, Campaigns, or Adventure Mode. Decisions to make - Shape the course of your adventure with critical decisions and dice rolls.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a little rough going at first, and I think some of the UI elements could be polished (explanation window hovers awkwardly over map checkpoints and obscure the map), but there's a great RPG behind some of the surface faux pas. I think they should build on the skill system, sockets, and the card concept to really add depth.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I'd like to love this game I simply cannot. Why, I ask myself. The developers update it often and you can tell they have put in a lot of work. The anime-like artwork is slick and well above average. The cards are very easy to read and the synergies are there for you to exploit them. There's no lack of mechanics (cough cough... maybe too many) The setting is...  the setting is okay. It's your usual dungeons and dragons homebrew experience. Nothing wrong with that. Is there?Wait. maybe there's something wrong with that. Maybe it's just an indicator of the lack of soul of this otherwise very technically adept game. And it's that technical near brilliance that hampers the whole experience: I see the shiny cards and nice artstyle and expect more narrative, world-building and overall personality to go with it. And there's simply not enough of it. Barely any. Lucius's smirk is the extent of it.As any GM worth their salt would tell you barebones world-building plus a contrived narrative makes for very poor adventuring. And I know, this is not an actual tabletop game - only one inspired by DnD - but at some point deckbuilding and inventory management is just not enough to keep you engaged, is it?

_childDocuments_.review: Positives: Parties are fun to build and with four starting builds per character it creates varied possibilities for what even the same character can be doing for your party.Card balance rewards you for having cards of all 3 rarities only needing one or two copies of the rares to really make a deck work.All the great mechanics from Slay the Spire, but multiple party members can help cover weaknesses of an individual character including the ability to heal or soak up damage.Negatives:Beginning vs End Game Difficulty feels skewed. This comes from the fact that you can become incredibly efficient in killing later on but in the beginning even taking out one enemy can require most or all of your actions for the turn. The other problem is late game healing from talents makes taking hits way less meaningful than in the beginning where the only means of health recovery other than having the cleric or druid in the party is consumables.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played >200 hours of this game, did full run-throughs (at least through act 4) with almost all the characters. It's a great game. What I really enjoy is having great synergy between characters and for the most part, most cards are viable. There are a few mechanics that don't really work that well, see below. Major comments: 1. I love the art, might be the best part of the game2. Characters are all unique and have interesting abilities (for the most part). In one of the initial iterations of the game, mastering cards gave unique abilities specific to each character, which gave each play-through a more memorable feel. Now they have generalized abilities that make things kind of boring imo. 3. The "synergy" aspect seems superfluous. I almost never use any of the synergy abilities except the initial one that allows you to shift especially since it counts towards your max card count.4. At higher levels, the game stagnates. You usually have a routine for every battle since you've honed your deck down to essentials and have maximized the card levels. At this point, you are basically playing for legendary items. 5. Items in general are trash. The legendary items sometimes have interesting / useful features, but for some reason (even though there seem to be dozens of them) I keep getting the same item multiple times in a play through, either awarded randomly or as part of the "gamble" feature, which is really annoying. The legendary items can really be build-defining, so maybe if you made the items better overall and less frequent it would feel less frustrating.6. This is my biggest criticism. There is way too much grinding in this game. The levels (starting with Act 2) feel repetitive very quickly, especially at low levels. There are like >50 nodes per map, which is exhausting to slog through (especially when you develop a routine for each fight, as above). This is the main reason why I haven't gotten to Act 5, because it just feels like a chore after a while. Like I said, great game. There's a reason I put 210 hours in this game (after TW: Warhammer 2, this is my most played game). Has some serious flaws that hold it from its true potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I was gifted this game by a friend, but was not paid to review this game.There are four acts of the actual story (which was pretty well done and entertaining as far as simple, "save the world" type scenarios go), and a sort of post-game fifth act that follows after the story's completion.  Fully completing each act of the campaign took between 20-30 hours for me, exactly as advertised.  The issue with the campaign mode is that I had a fully complete build for all three of my primary party members before the end of act 2, and despite gaining another 30+ levels, there was never any meaningful change or growth to those builds for the entire rest of the campaign.  To put it simply, the combat got stale.  There were around 5 or so new enemy types with each new act, not counting unique bosses, but the actual mechanical differences from one enemy to another weren't quite impactful enough to stop me from just using the same strategy for the entire campaign.That said, the game is still fun, and I can see how it was primarily designed for the rogue-lite experience, which plays out in a much faster and more frantic fashion.  In my opinion, stick to that mode of play, and you'll likely have an amazing time.

_childDocuments_.review: A blast for the first 10 hours, but soon runs out of steam.A lot to love intially. Card based battles in the style of Slay the Spire or other deckbuilding roguelikes, but with a ton of extra content. - A grid based combat that allows you to manouevre to avoid attacks or target different enemies- 10 different characters with unique decks- Equipment that can buff and add new cards - Runes that can modify equipment- Skill trees that allow a lot of customisationClearly a lot of work went into the game and there's a ton of content.Unfortunately there are a lot of issues which become apparent by Act 2 and 3.- By Act 2, it is really easy to reduce your deck down to 8-10 cards. With talents that let you draw extra cards you can more or less see your whole deck every turn. This leads to the gameplay being very repetitive. Every turn you string together your strongest combo until the enemy dies. You don't really have to modify your strategy at all. So combat doesn't feel dynamic and the interesting decisions and positional play of early act 1 quickly becomes irrelevant. By the middle of act 2 you become virtually untouchable.I would strongly recommend the devs remove the 'edit deck' feature. Force people to remove cards through level ups rather than immediately getting rid of all the basics. - This is especially true of characters you recruit later. Because they start at the same level as the rest of the party you will level them up 20-30 levels all at once, immediately making the 'perfect deck'.- It also means a lot of the equipment you come across loses interest. In practise you will put void runes in almost all the equipment that gives you new cards because even if they are powerful they interfere with your hero's synergies.- None of the enemies really force you to rethink your strategy (unlike Slay the Spire where many fights will play out differently due to you enemy's unique traits).- All the mechanics are very linear. Because of the way cards scale, you want to make every character specialise in either Strength, Dexterity or Intelligence and pump everything into that stat. If you apply chill, you don't want any burn. There's no real room for a 'jack of all trades' approach - every deck is super specialised and overtuned.- All 4 acts play out very similarly. Maybe that's to be expected, but don't expect any radical new features or challenges after act 1.- Maybe the tutorial mode will be improved, but a lot of the features like Skill Grids, Runes, camping etc, aren't very clearly explained - I ended up having to take to google to work out how things worked.- Be aware that sometimes the UI lies! If you have a buff on your character it may say that you are hitting for 50x2 when in fact only the first attack will hit for 50 and the second will hit for much less once the buff has worn off.- There are probably too many status effects. Vulnerable and bleed are quite similar (increase incoming damage), Might and Fury and Critical all increase your damage in slightly different ways; not very clear or intuitive. Chill, burn and shock all play very similarly. It can be hard to keep track of what is doing what.A final note that if you are experienced with deck building games like Slay the Spire and the like you will find the game quite easy. Normal mode is a real pushover and I'd recommend starting on a higher level.I'm still giving this a thumbs up because I had a blast playing through act 1, but as soon as I've reached the end of the campaign I'll be back to Slay the Spire.

_childDocuments_.review: INCREDIBLE Turn-based tactics, with cards unique to their empire/heroes background. There are three main statistics Strength, Dexterity, and Intelligence, There are per-hero skill-trees - similar to each other, building upon what you feel is needed, or making up for heroes' weak areas.The adventure is pretty cool, you're needed to defend, and help others on your journey.The map is very easy to navigate, and speak with people in your vicinity, The fights are wave-based in many cases, with an elite enemy usually moving in per wave. There are in many cases also allies to play with you, and they auto-fight in their turn, while on your team.The graphics are crisp, and delightful to watch. It's a very nice distraction to play when taking a break for online games, because as you continue, you keep building your character, and the allies you meet along the way! The fighting tactics are simple and effective to overwhelm the enemy and prevent being overwhelmed as well. Some fights will last 2-3 rounds, and some of the major boss fights will have 6 rounds more or less, and I can see it becoming more as you level up. Great game to sink some time into. There's also 3 modes to play the game, standard / rogue-lite and /rogue-like,You can also play a little, quit, come back later to Resume, HOWEVER< when you click play in the main menu, and try to proceed, be careful to not start a new game accidentally. The resume option is under New game.Will expand on this as I play more, as I'm sure it's going to be a fun journey.The layout is very easy to navigate, and makes the journey less cumbersome  in the long term :)

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 2: When I first picked this up I thought I was going to play the campaign once and put it down, but I'm on campaign three and about 60 hours of playtime, and I'm still enjoying myself. It's a flawed game with too much going on, but the gameplay is an addictive mix of Slay the Spire and the micromanagement of a light tactics RPG.Here's a list of things that could be removed from this game to make it better: the inn/renting a room (just have the healer), the junk system (or just use right click to mark junk), shrines, the map mini-game (although I kinda like it), the exhaustion system, rune slot colors, leveling runes, the artifacts meta-progression (+1 stat for a character? What kind of reward is that?), fate, half the statuses (why are fury and might the same thing?), half of each character's cards (characters only have 1-2 viable strategies anyways), half the nodes in the skill tree, half the nodes in the game... I guess this game is just twice as much as it needs to be. I hope they keep that in mind when they're making their next game. I'm excited to play it.EDIT: Everything I've read about the game has affirmed my review, to the point that it feels redundant. I'm another twenty hours in, and I have to say that this janky game is still a ton of fun. It's so cheerfully overstuffed with content that I can't helped but be charmed. Even when it's a little boring, there's so much to do. I wish the pacing were quicker in the early game. You don't have enough Action Points or resources (and never enough crafting supplies), then all of a sudden you're flooded with weapons. The the pace picks up midway through Act Two, you get almost too many AP in Act Three, then all of a sudden at the end it gets weirdly difficult. [P.S. I did end up playing Realm Mode, and I have to take back what I said about Gordian Quest not being a massive rip of Slay the Spire lol. I can't fault them, though, Spire is a great game. And this is too, when you get into the groove]I've been playing through the Slay-the-Spire-likes and eventually made it to Gordian Quest. At first I thought it was a pretty shameless rip-off, especially the soundtrack, but Gordian Quest is only partially in debt to Spire. I haven't tried Realm mode yet (I have ~20 hours on a friend's account, so I've played more than it says on here), but the main game is a long-form, multi-campaign quest with rudimentary story elements. Each campaign takes several hours to play through, although I acted like they were different runs and chose a new set of heroes for each one.The game reminds me a lot of Griftlands, a Spire-like with a more open overworld map and multiple ongoing quest lines. The gameplay is Strike-and-Defend combat like Spire, but the action occurs on a small grid like a tactical strategy game. You control three characters, all with four aspects and multiple viable card strategies. It's daunting to have to choose an archetype at the start of the game, but it's fairly forgiving about switching from one strategy another through respec points and a choice of stat grids tile with different card sets on them.The start of the game turned me off. The starting cards are boring and it felt like it took several hours to start getting interesting items and weapons (crafting materials are particularly scarce). I almost bounced off because the rounds seemed endless, but once I realized that the game had the pacing of an RPG, not a Spire-like, I settled in. There's a turning point maybe 10 hours in where all of sudden you are flooded with weapons, stats, talents, and choices and the pacing really picks up. The main problem I'm having with the game now is actually the over-abundance of everything. There are simply too many nodes, too many weapons, too many enemies, and too many choices. I love skill trees but you get a new point every couple of so you're always going back and forth between menus. The item management and shopping feel micromanage-y, although I often feel that way about games that let you sell weapons. It all starts to feel redundant. I wish the rounds were shorter and the combats less frequent. I wish there were fewer upgrades that felt more impactful. I wish the game were slighly harder; normal mode is so easy that I've only died twice (and only because the game was so easy that I took all of the defense cards out of my deck).That said, I think this game is worth buying and sticking with. It's smartly designed and has a lot of satisfying mechanics. Even though there's a lot of game, you zip along quickly between everything. I've been playing a lot of Spire-likes and I'm pretty exhausted with the length of some of the battles. Here, you can get out of a lot of battles in a minute or two, which is awesome. The weapon system is neat, with the chance of some powerful combinations. It feels like a lot of care was put into the game, and it's fun. I may only play it for 30-40 hours, but in the year of our lord 2022, $20 is pocket change and the game is a definite buy for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Even in beta this is one of the best games I've ever played.  It's a card battler with epic scope reminiscent of "The Malazan Book of the Fallen" and Dungeons & Dragons.  It could be most readily described as Slay the Spire times three, in that you have three heroes on the board fighting at once, instead of one.  You navigate a series of maps representing whole regions of a vast fantasy empire, and the maps have way more nodes and possible paths than Slay the Spire.  The mechanics are very tight, just like in Spire, and the result is that same sort of tension and focus that makes Slay the Spire shine.  There's a great crafting system, too.  Finally, you also control teams of other heroes, sending them on missions while you're out on quests with your three heroes.  You can rotate in the other heroes to your team - they're playable.  Oh yes, and the skill trees in this thing make the Enhancement trees in Dungeons and Dragons Online look simplistic.  I'm blown away by this thing.  Most definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Gordian Quest is an absolute labor of love. It's like the devs had a hundred different ideas and instead of choosing the best to implement and refine, they went ahead and added all of them. This game desperately needed a strong project manager to reign things in. Compounding that problem is the lack of good help pages/tutorial for each mechanic. The game is only about a week away from leaving Early Access and the help pages still leave off way too much relevant information.Some examples:1) Before you choose the talent skill node, you have no idea what talents are at all. 2) In some instances, cards that create other cards don't show what the created cards do3) The game does not define what "expend" does4) Crates and money that appear on the battlefield show no information as to what they are.5) Camping help doesn't explain what any of the numbers or symbols mean or what many of the cards do.

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a fantastic card battler game.  Graphics and sound are great, balanced game play with tons of things to do, and 10 heroes to work with.  The campaign game is broken into Acts.  Act 1 is well done with plenty of side quests to help you level up.  Act 2 becomes a bit of a 10 level grind to continue the story, but you don't need to be at the recommended level to finish.  You can get pretty powerful if you build well.  Act 3 is the long grind before the final act.  Fight areas need to be reset after sleeping to be able to hit level caps before act 4.  Act 4, the final act in the campaign mode, is a small area and a very slow grind if you want to hit the lvl 60 cap.  There are other things to do after Act 4, so you don't need to hit lvl 60 to finish.You will have a total of 10 unique characters to control each with their own special cards/skills to grow and use.  You fight with only 3 heroes at a time (plus summons), so you can focus on how you want to play since the characters vary enough that strategies will change depending on party structure.  Each character has multiple equipment slots to fill up and each can be enhanced with runes or other skills.  Equipment can also be leveled up or augmented to other items.  Same goes for skill cards which can also be leveled up or mastered for different effects and damage.Battles are played on 'tracks' with characters being able to move on the battlefield both to get into and out of range for attacks.  You can see enemy intent so you have the chance to move or build enough block to not take damage.  The game has a wide variety of monsters to battle and plenty of synergies for your party members to level up.  Cards and synergies will cause other members of your party to be able to act when someone attacks or share block abilities or heal.  It all depends on your party structure.Aside from battles there are maps to explore in a mini game where you can find items and supplies and story moments where you will need to make skill checks to pass or sometimes take negative effects.  Post Act 4 has a few areas to explore with your current party members and a never-ending dungeon area to keep exploring.  These options can also be played instead of the campaign mode.  The game says the campaign takes 15-30 hrs to finish, I was getting that per act trying out all the characters and grinding levels and legendary items.  Overall I got almost 190 hrs from the campaign when I finished.The game has replay-ability since you have tons of different ways to level up characters and many different party makeups to use.  Each character has 3 different areas they can focus on or use a combination of all 3.  I also was able to use any party makeup I wanted and had no problems during battles.  Keeping my levels maxed out many of the fights were either comfortable or me overwhelming my opponents.  I didn't have a single character knocked out during the entire game.  So, for most hard core card battle players, normal might be a bit too easy.  Fortunately you can up the skill level and adjust things to make it harder.A good, fun card battler.. 8/10, worth playing!

_childDocuments_.review: Well, where do I even start...I really really want to like this game but it's impossible at this stage.Every single mechanic in the game feels clunky, unpolished, unnecessarily complicated and frustrating.The campaign is tedious and incredibly boring.Events don't make any sense, 90% of them are basically screwing yourself over for nothing. Also I'm not going to change items to wear +STR/DEX/INT check just to pass a useless event and then dress back into combat gear. It's very very tedious.Legendary items are expensive and only 2 or 3 of them are any useful. Itemization in this game is just very very subpar and straight up bland.There's zero incentive to try heroes other than the first three as the inventory management in this game is insanely cumbersome and infuriating at times. Setting up skill grids is clunky and tedious.The battles are extremely repetitive and weird, I never know who will the enemy attack at any point in time.Camping is overly complicated and overall just pointless. Supplies are there just for the sake of being there.UI in general is a hot mess, especially the shop. Also you never know if it's an arrow back button or the map one to bring you back to the previous screen.The card system is very subpar to all the other popular deckbuilders. The upgrades are minimal and don't feel like big improvement, compared to say Slay the Spire, where card upgrades are often gamechanging.The difference between blacksmith and gamble dude feels exactly like playing a mobile game where blacksmith is a free player choice and gamble dude is for whales. Blacksmith is utterly useless past the first 30 minutes of the game. Same goes for the enchanter and the jeweler. All of them could be just one person with different tabs and probably better loot.There are combat mechanics that just don't make any sense. So if you play as Rocky, you can smash rocks to deal damage to enemies behind or around them. Except you CAN NOT destroy rocks spawned on YOUR side of board or if a stone is BEHIND an enemy. That makes absolutely zero sense. Look at Gloomhaven at how it's implemented with Cragheart character and learn a thing or two from it.The "adventure" mode where you travel by putting nodes on a sepia page is just not needed at all imo. It has zero synergy with the deck-building aspect of the game, most of the time you either don't get anything or get damaged by enemies chasing you.I'm honestly very surprised how all of this made into a full release. I see other reviewers complaining about the same issues, so it's not only me.
