_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxing city builder with a unique twist - your city is airborne.  As such, in addition to all your standard issue city managing infrastructure, you must also build things like fans, wings, and propellers to stay afloat and stay mobile as you soar the skies.    Visually, this game is gorgeous, evoking a warm, nostalgic feeling.   The background music captures the adventurous yet laid back nature of the game, however there are only like 2-4 tracks.  I bought this game on a whim and I'm certainly glad I did.  I don't know how often I'll play it in the future, but the time I have put into it so far has been very enjoyable.  It was a very rewarding experience watching my tiny aeronautic community grow into a legit kingdom/city.  If you like city builders though, don't expect anything crazy in depth like city skylines.  This game is far more minimal - stylistically and functionally.  A big part of this game is flying around collecting resources or doing quests for the landlubbers below.  Fortunately, resources are abundant and renewable.  I haven't played hard difficulty, but on normal I have not run into issues where it seemed like all my hard work was about to be undone in one cruel twist of fate.  I could safely explore, quest, and build all at my own pace without worrying about all my beautiful little people dying in fiery debris pummeling the earth.  I very much enjoyed playing this game as a way to unwind before bed.  TL;DR - Very pretty and relaxing game that scratches that itch to nurture something.

_childDocuments_.review: What a charming little game! A bit short, though, and very easy: I completed the main story on hard difficulty in 9 hours. It was fun, but I'm not sure about replay value.  The game is quite original and very stylish! It's definitely not a city-builder or a colony sim. You are building a ship, not a community. In that sense, it seems silly that building is restricted on a 2D plane, with only some "stacking", 3-storey buildings. Building downwards is not possible at all. I would have liked some Laputa-style observation kites or something. The lift/drag/tilt mechanism works nicely, and is well balanced. The aerodynamics are pure fantasy, of course: in the real world a wing provides zero lift if it is not moving forward! And the little aeroplanes are hauling surprisingly heavy loads of timber, ore, and water. They look like they could carry one or two people, but not much else. Maybe they should have rather been designed as blimps?Anyway, two thumbs up here!

_childDocuments_.review: What a gem this is. Satisfying city-building with a couple of basic production chains, light problem solving and research. As the game progresses, you need to keep your city aloft with enough lift, moving with enough propulsion, balance the weight out relatively evenly and keep your population satisfied, all by placing buildings (or, if necessary, moving them around). You also need to constantly explore and navigate the map to gather enough resources and complete quests.However, this is not a stressful game: the speed controls, gorgeous soundtrack (an absolute highlight!), atmospheric visuals and stately pace make it extremely zen-like. I really enjoyed sitting back and letting my city glide through the sky, over cliffs and marshes, set to beautiful sunsets and sunrises. There's some fantastic attention-to-detail: for example, if you look up at night you'll see twinkling constellations of stars. There's also a lot of satisfaction to be had in arranging your city in the most aesthetically pleasing/realistic/fantastical way (whatever floats your boat). The problem solving elements are never so demanding they get in the way of creativity, and it gives you plenty of time to experiment.The main weakness of the game is the lightness of its backstory – it's a pity greater quest variety and fleshed-out writing weren't used to bring the world to life, especially the darker inferences of exploitation suggested by the gameplay. After the first hour or so, it becomes quite obvious the story is just an engine for game progression.Expect roughly ~8-12 hours of playtime to complete the campaign. If you enjoy the atmosphere/creativity, you can repeat it with a semi-randomised world, although the story remains the same; there's also a sandbox mode. I originally bought this out of curiosity on the Epic Games store (despite preferring Steam) and was blown away. Now I have the opportunity to get it on Steam (with the rest of my games), I'm happy to do so to support the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Airborne Kingdom has the clever idea to combine a city/colony building game with a open world exploration game. This is really novel, but it ends up being both the games greatest strength and greatest weakness. You get the pleasure of going out into a world and discovering things, and you get a fairly distinctive resource management dynamic where gaining any resource is based on where you are, with different resources being more or less plentiful in different locations,On the other hand the game is mechanically extremely simple for a colony builder, something that the novel premise can't entirely overcome. The progression system seems to assume the player will be rebuilding parts of their flying city semi-regularly, but doing this is cumbersome. There's a lack of visual variety to a lot of the game, but most significantly with the city itself. This is not a game for people who like to do cosmetic builds. Finally, because so much of the game is driven by exploring an unfamiliar landscape, there's extremely little replay value. You'll already be familiar with what needs to be done, and there's not enough depth or variety to the mechanics to make a second play through feel meaningfully different. Additionally the new game plus and higher difficulty options do make the game more challenging, but mostly by adding tedium.My first play through was around 11 hours to do pretty much everything. It was simple but enjoyable and I recommending it for anyone who thinks colony builder + exploration seems like a fun combination. Just be aware that you aren't getting much more than that.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little economic city builder type game. Took around 14.5 hours to 100%, including two playthroughs, one normal and one NG+. Played through both times on hard difficulty and still found it quite easy. Has some limited replayability with the NG+ mode. The soundtrack is very good.You play as a floating city that devours resources across the land like a plague of locusts. You pretty much strip mine all resources you come across to survive and develop your city while doing quests for each of the 12 Kingdoms and recruiting more workers from settlements and by finishing quests. Each Kingdom has two quests, first quest is generally some sort of fetch quest and the second is to build a sky tower to ally with the Kingdom. The goal being to ally with all 12 kingdoms and return to your starting point. Some areas are more challenging than others and have limited food or coal for example. There is also an optional challenging northern area to complete. Developing your city is quite straight forward. You build houses for your citizens and amenities to keep them happy. Research buildings, resource collection, resource production, storage and refining buildings. Buildings to provide lift to keep your city afloat and propulsion to help it move faster. Easy once you know what each building does and what kinds of buildings you need. Like the Eastern Orthodox aesthetic of some of the buildings.While I enjoyed the game, at the time of writing it costs $36.50 AUD on Steam. Recommend purchasing when on sale with a decent discount.

_childDocuments_.review: "Airborne Kingdom" is a refreshing take on the city-building genre that offers a unique and engaging experience. The game is set in a world where civilization has taken to the skies, and the player takes on the role of a leader of a floating city.One of the standout features of "Airborne Kingdom" is the game's world-building. The player must balance resources such as food, water, and building materials in order to maintain and expand their floating city. The game's economy is complex and requires the player to balance supply and demand, which adds a layer of strategy to the gameplay.Another impressive aspect of "Airborne Kingdom" is the game's exploration system. As the player's city travels through the sky, they will encounter a variety of islands and settlements to explore. Each island offers unique challenges and resources, which encourages the player to explore and expand their city even further.The game's art style is charming and whimsical, with a colorful and vibrant world to explore. The soundtrack is equally impressive, with a variety of tracks that capture the adventurous and optimistic spirit of the game.Overall, "Airborne Kingdom" is a must-play for fans of the city-building genre, and a great entry point for newcomers looking for a unique and engaging gaming experience. With its complex economy, immersive world, and charming art style, "Airborne Kingdom" is a game that's sure to captivate players of all ages.

_childDocuments_.review: There was once an ancient kingdom that thrived on knowledge, peace, culture, and living in the clouds, but many centuries later most of their technology has become lost in dusty libraries. That is until your town found blueprints that helped create the center ship that allowed you to take to the skies. You will now be tasked with building a floating kingdom, reuniting all the kingdoms, and creating a great collection of people to bring the world together and to bring peace. In Airborne Kingdom you will be in charge of managing resources and the well-being of your citizens. As your population grows you will be tasked with more areas of importance to your citizens, and as long as you keep those areas in mind you will be able to continue to grow your population.This game lulls you in at the start and if you are not careful, which I was not, you will quickly find that you’re going to need to start the game all over again. Now this isn’t a bad thing, but I can definitely tell you that your first play attempt probably will not be your only one. There are a couple of immediate reasons for this. The first being that the layout of the game world will change. The changes will be subtle, but it is enough to keep you on your toes. Another reason is that the blueprints that you will need to purchase to unlock new technology have a bit of randomness to it. There may be a playthrough where you will find one type of propulsion in a certain part of the game, but you may not see that exact type until much later. The final reason is that as the layout of the world changes so does the placement of resources, and so your strategy to obtain and store said resources will change. There are three main resources that you’ll always have to keep an eye on: coal, water, and food. If you run out of coal your flying city will cease to fly. If you don’t have food or water your citizens will abandon you. I found out the importance of extra storage of those last two in one of my later playthroughs of the game. I know it makes perfect sense now, but the more people you have the more taxing they are on your resources, and it’s amazing how fast you’ll start burning through those resources if you’re not careful. Citizens are also a resource you have to think about. They will be needed to man different buildings in your city, they will be needed to build new buildings, they will be needed to gather resources, and I can’t tell you the number of times I thought I was being crafty by keeping my population low in the beginning only to get burned when it turned out I didn’t have anyone left to build the new buildings I needed to survive.This is a challenging game, and as you go into new areas of the the map you will be faced with different challenges (less food to harvest, or less water to gather), but there is something about the overall feel of the game that does have a soothing quality, even when you’re stressing out over the fact that you’re almost out of water, food, or coal. Does this game get frustrating, of course, but there’s something about it that even if I royally screwed up I was always willing to try again and deploy a new strategy to hopefully not get blindsided by whatever caused my latest defeat. This is not a game for everyone, but it's a solid game for those who are looking for something a little different when it comes to city-builder games.

_childDocuments_.review: so i review stuff nowa short and sweet experiencelooking forward to the sequelwhat you see on the store page is what you getpros:- fun concept- scratched a sort of frostpunky itch- cool vibes- fun progression- i like the building aesthetic- interacting with the world (e.g. kingdoms) was fun- the different ways you can lay out the airship was cool- desires mechanic was satisfyingcons:- feels like a proof of concept - technology tree flourishes mid game and then trails off, i think it would benefit from more variety in research options, like what's the point of increasing or reducing ranges of stuff that you'd already placed for maximum benefit. stuff like reducing the number of workers required for a building - there's very minimal micromanagement, which may be a pro to some but it sometimes stagnated gameplay that destroying stuff was your only option for moving workers around- there's very little (easy to see) stats in particular when it comes to desires, like it's impossible to know without adding stuff up how much health you have vs requirements etc. if it is possible i didn't find it- frozen tundra expansion was vvv underwhelming (unfortunately), but it was free at least. once you unlock the single new research item you can just fly out, build a few and that's the difficulty gone. you just end up flying around for 15 mins collecting stuff and that's it. felt very underbaked and really unrewarding. in fact at the end overall: all of the ideas are cool and the experience is fun and chill but i don't really feel like it quite gets going, the early and mid games are by the far the best but you reach a point where you're able to be mostly self sustaining and that's kinda the game done. _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - I really like this game, but I'm disappointed it's so short. Ofc it's hard not to recommend a game when the only problem is that there isn't more of it.I really like the aesthetic of this game. I often find myself wanting to optimise everything in games like these, but this is the first time I've been really tempted to set that aside and just design a flying city that looks great. All the different structures you can unlock to keep your city in the sky have their mechanical pros & cons, but I wound up using most of them as ornaments in the late game.The writing is minimalist, but it evokes the setting really well. It'd be nice to see a bit more of it, but maybe it'd lose its feel if it was more text-heavy.I also just really enjoy the premise. It feels so wholesome. You find an ancient legend about a flying kingdom that goes around helping people, uniting the world, and better yet - it comes with a set of instructions on how to make your own.Since getting into city-builders though, I'm starting to notice a pattern - lots of fantastic concepts, not a lot of seeing them through. While this game doesn't actually feel incomplete, like some others I've played, it is pretty short. Idk how the replay value is, but I'm probably gonna find out in the next couple of days. I really hope there'll be an expansion, or a sequel, or that some modder gets obsessed with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't say I've played 31 hours, more like 4 (and left it running paused while I did other things) This game is beautiful, and easy to pick up. There seems to be a lot of story. This game is very simple, almost to the point that it feels unfinished. There are only a few quests, and they don't require enough resources to make them challenging. There seems to be almost no benefit to voluntarily adding people to your city. There are several game mechanics that seem like they should interact--like stacking housing should decrease resident happiness, or the amount of buildings should affect speed of your city--and this seems like a missed chance to add complexity to the game. If they add more content, I will gladly pick it up again, but as-is it didn't have much to hold my attention.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a relatively positive do-not-recommend review. It's kind of a neat idea, really, and a good chill feel-good game for a few hours, and the graphics are beautiful. I just think it's just a little bit *too* chill.The central challenge, resource management, is just not quite challenging enough, even on Difficult mode. The start of the game is blessed with fairly abundant resources, especially relative to your small crew; once you have charcoal huts and a couple of the early-game allies, the ticking countdown for coal is meaningless. The secondary challenge — city design — is a little underdeveloped. There is one class of building such that you need all the houses to be nearby. There is another class of building that you should never have near houses. And you need it all to balance, between weight and lift and propulsion to find your next resource. But the solutions to layout are straightforward, and while someone is *trying* to complicate things with a variety of mechanics, none of them seem to have enough impact — especially by the second game when you're wise to what's coming. Something is missing.The final challenge, unlocked by your success at the first two, is the treasure hunt: navigation, spotting things from the air. The people who are really into the treasure-hunt feel will no doubt be well-entertained. For the rest of us, mostly it just happens. Sometimes it's actually neat. Sometimes, a little more often, it's just a trifle frustrating, thought not too badly.Modestly creative end-sequence twist about the premise of the game; prop to whoever came up with that. If you have completed the treasure hunts for the Wonder items, New Game Plus will unlock new a new Town Center that gives you a starting power-up that has the same effects as the wonder. One of them is perhaps a bit overpowered: among other things it will show you exactly where to navigate to in order to get the other two effects.

_childDocuments_.review: The game loop is very simple, and pretty boring. Every quest is the same quest. They send you to a place, you click on the place, you get a little story blurb, then you go back to the town you got the quest from. I'm not joking, that's the extent of literally every quest. The management of your city is also not particularly difficult. Build buildings to meet whatever need you currently have, while scooping up free unlimited resources off the map. The tilt mechanic is very easy to manage, while the tech tree is extremely small, with only a handful of meaningful unlocks followed by "% bonus to X stat on Y building" researches. Ultimately there's no real tension, challenge, or interesting choices. All the creativity went into the general atmosphere and premise.

_childDocuments_.review: Revised review after the developers published fixes for some game breaking bugs.The game is very light on content. I completed the 'campaign' in about 6 hours of gameplay and that's while fighting with a pretty horrible bug that caused my buildings to get stuck when moving without tons of gyrations (when quickly selecting buildings, pressing Z and then trying to select their destination, the building being moved would get stuck on the cursor and the rest of the UI elements would stop working until you re-entered the Build menu by pressing B on the keyboard.)Given the minimal content, I do not believe the game is worth the price tag attached to it, but when on discount it's a charming and beautiful game that is very relaxed. I played both a new game and new game+ (which offered randomized start locations but I think pretty much everything else was where I expected it to be. Although, perhaps it also shuffled which town was in which town spot.) I finish that playthrough in 4 hours after the devs posted that they fixed the issues that I had in my first playthrough and I felt compelled to give it another chance so that I could revise my review. Everything seems to be fixed now.You will not complete the research before finishing the game, so things could be better tuned as far as both total content as well as the speed of research. (My second playthrough I focused on always being at 100% speed and discovered that this is too fast for the gathering planes to do a proper gather cycle as you fly by.)But after my first playthrough and a good sense of where resources were located, I just flew through the game (NG+) in under 3 hours.All in all, I give this a thumbs up. It would be better at sale prices. So save your monies till then. (But I appreciate the devs fixing game breaking bugs, so I'm not going to give this indie developer a hard time by not recommending it after the effort it took to collect bug reports, identify replication steps, fix the code, test it and publish a fix within a couple of weeks of my purchasing the game. _childDocuments_.review: Nice game, but not worth 25€; If you get it on discount, like under 15€, it's great. Took me 9H to finish; would have been a lot faster if I had not visited the differents places in order.The map is divided in 3 zones + outside world. I have not tried the outside since the game ended when I finished the scenario; may give it a try later. First zone is simple. Second and third zones lacks some ressources. You got a warning about that when you start wandering in those zones, which is good.There are some annoying things, like: you need some "ressources" (food, but also lift and propulsion). You can make building to make those ressources. But you don't know how much until you've actually made it, the game has only three option: low, average, and high. It won't tell you more. At some point I had to make more lift; I needed to choose between two building. For lift, the game tells you exactly how much you win; however it doesn't tell you what it will cost (how many people and coal to have it run), only the initial construction cost. So one had an average cost, low worker need; the other had a high cost, no worker. I got to my coal consumption, and see that I have 3 of the first building, costing me 0.6 coal per hour; which make 0.2 per building. The other building cost me 0.5 coal per hour. Since I was low on coal, I make the first one. BIM those now cost me 1.2 coal per hour instead of the expected 0.8, meaning new building added 0.6 by itself. After that, I just made thing without looking to much at the cost and tried to keep it all balanced.The tilt is weird too. For what I understood, too much tilt is bad (never got too much tilt so dunno, it's easy to keep things balanced). However, there is like no scale. At some point, I had a 1° left, 3° back tilt; it says no tilt problem, everything great. I go to put another building, adn before placing it the game told you how it will affect the tilt. Well, I kid you not, it told me I would have a 1° left, 3° back tilt so no change, right?) which now would be considered as HIGH TILT. So it's like, all good or all bad, no middle ground at all. It's easy to keep a nice tilt, so not too bothering, but still weird.But the one big thing that triggered me was the workers management (spoiler: nonexistant). Their need changes depending on the number of habitants; and it works by level. 100 habitants, one more need. But, when you start the game, you don't have the buildings to cover those needs; you'll discover them in the kingdoms you encounter. Great, except that to meet the 4 needs when you get 100 habitants, you have to visit kingdoms in each zones. Don't go the obvious linear visit; instead keep switching between the zone. Well, I didn't know, so I didn't brought my city all the way to the other zone, and kept searching for kingdoms with the needed building in my zone. While people in my city would felt dissatisfied...And leave. They leave like, 6 by 6. then you get under the 100 stage and BAM, they're all happy again. But then some new people join and BAM, they're unhappy again. Worst part is, they weren't even angry. The game has 5 happiness level, and they were all either in the middle or upper. So mostly, happy? NO! They leave! And you end up not having enough workers to work your city because, and that's the big flaw: THERE IS NO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WAY TO DISABLE BUILDINGS. You have to destroy them, so that workers won't work on it anymore; then they'll be able to go gather ressources for you because, yes, you can't choose the work priority either. Everyone works on the city, and IF you have some free workers, then they gather ressources for you. Spoiler, if you can't gather ressources, you're dead. So I spent half of the game taking people in, growing...then destroying my city because they left. Thinking I will definitely find that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ building, I take people in again. Get stuck again when they left. WHY CAN'T I CHOOSE WHAT THE WORKERS DO?!Yeah, so that was what made me hate this game. But appart from that, it's pretty nice, not even hard. No one ever left because of a lack of ressources, my city never crashed (though it started getting really low at some point), the graphism are nice. It's a lot repetitive though, apart from the fact that the second and third zone lack a ressource and have a new one, quests feels the same: move and find thing, come back and give ressources, done we're friend. Do that with 12 kingdoms, while growing your city. Building is easy, moving building doesn't cost too much, making sure bad building aren't near house isn't hard at all (make houses on the side, bad building on the back, here you go). Research is FRICKING LONG. Like, I haven't done HALF of it in 9 hours. I finished the game with half of the researchs. Most of them are not needed at all, really.Bonus point, you can find some location that will give you personnalisation option for your buildings (colors theme). It's nice.So, overall a nice game, with some BIG ANNOYING flaws but if you get in on discount i's still worth it I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: I was sleeping on this one for a little while, but I went back to give it a trying the demo for the Empires sequel. Anyways, I decided to dust this off the shelf and give it a play.Overall, I enjoyed my time with this game. It was pretty chill to play, and I made a big of a challenge to myself to play entirely at 1X speed. There wasn't a whole lot of time that I had to sit and do nothing. Having the (extremely slowly) ticking clock(s) of food, water, and coal ends up being a boon to the game, as it encourages you to keep moving. It helps to think of this a bit as an adventure game, rather than a full city builder. The game off the bat gives you some very clear goals, get 150 citizens and ally with the 12 kingdoms of the map. This main plot and goal really helps tie the whole game together, and it does a fantastic job of helping keep the game moving. You're not building for the sake of making more production, or for an endless desire to growth; instead, you're building to fill out your population goal. You're also building towards specific goals, either being able to process enough materials, or to satisfy the citizens needs.I ended up liking how research worked in the game, mostly; My one complaint is that you can't pause a research. If you lock into a 16 hour research, you need to wait 16 game outs to pick a new one, and if you swap early, you lose your progress entirely. This is especially rough when you buy a new blueprint you need to progress, and before you can build the building, you need to do a quick 2 hour research on that building. The research time isn't much, but if you were already 4 hours into a research, your options are to abandon the past 4 hours of research, or wait another 12 game hours before you can use the new piece you bought. I ended up planning my routes and research progression around this, knowing I'd need it open soon because I was planning to buy a new blueprint, but a pause feature would still be very nice.When it comes to city planning. You can get away with a lot of inefficiencies. I never did more than a vague plan of 'residents in the front, industry in the back' and it ended up working just fine for me. This likely wouldn't be true if I tried the optional northern region where your city can freeze. Going there, or playing in hard mode (I played in normal) probably make the layout of your city matter quite a bit more. This is probably the ideal sort of balance, since I ended up quite liking the look of my quirky city. It would likely be fun to play through again and try a more planned and perfected layout.Overall, if you have some time to spare, and are open to a simple adventure with a bit of a unique character (in a way, the city itself is your character), then this is a great pick up. The ticking clocks aren't as stressful as I imagined they'd be, and the way the game has you split focus between building the city, thinking about your research path, and scanning the ground for resources, settlements, and extras means you'll rarely have a moment where all you have to do is sit and wait. Even while moving the city, it's helpful to keep an eye out at the nearby resources, plan for which ones to grab as you fly past, and generally keep things moving. It gives a nice feeling of successfully balancing spinning plates when you get into the groove.

_childDocuments_.review: Good fun, very relaxing - until your kingdom starts to fall from the sky or you run out of food or water, killing all your subjects. You definitely want to avoid that stuff. Other tips:-Stick around the first area and build up your resources before moving on. The first area has plentiful resources, so you definitely want to get your storage up, maybe build your water condensers and farms. -Watch out when returning to kingdoms to finish quests. All of a sudden a bunch of people will join your kingdom, so try to always have a 10 empty house buffer at all times. -Monitor your kingdom's happiness - if all the people are not at least satisfied you may start to lose settlers.-Difficulty is basically 0 at the starting area, then 1 for the water area, 2 in the plateau area, and 5 in the tundra - you'll want to have a bunch of finished resources and lots of food and water storage for the tundra, there's literally no food or water available except on occasion when you pick up stranded adventurers. -Completing the Orrery quest gives you a revised map that shows all settlements and quest sites. Finishing that quest as soon as possible is a big help later on. -Plan your community to include space for Faith and Health buildings. Comfort is a generalized stat that you can raise by planting trees anywhere, lighting is the same.-If you keep space open around your community center, you can move around your lift engines (turbines etc.) to keep the kingdom balanced. If it gets too off-balance people get unhappy.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game.  It was a nice change of pace from a blitzkrieg style of play compared to new games hitting the market these days. And a totally different way to city building.  I've played a few city games over the years (Sim City, Civilization, FrostPunk, Cities:Sklines...etc but this one adds a twist.  The basics are pretty much the same as any city game harvesting resources to meet the needs of the city and its inhabitants all of which become more complicated as you progress and expand your city.  Power, food, water, wood, brick, glass and there's even structures to help boost morale taking people’s minds off the haphazard way you built their home. Airborne Kingdom doesn't have any combat at all and that’s a good thing since keeping your city alive and off the ground is combat enough.  You start with a little balanced floating town but once you start placing houses, hangars for your planes, research buildings, engines and more you need to keep an even keel (left, right, front and back) like a regular ocean liner or suffer the consequences.  Too much tilt and your citizens drop the "Dear John" letter on you jumping ship like a horde of rats! If you're not careful you won't have enough people to gather resources anymore. You find and recruit your citizens from settlements and by completing quests so when they leave it can put you in the hurt locker possibly even resulting in destroying buildings to plan your recovery. As valuable as people are coal is just as or even more so as it keeps your city in the sky and without it you're back at ground zero...literally! The world below your city is as important as what is in your city since everything needed to keep it afloat and your people alive are down there. There are no places to build on the ground and the map is finite so you can explore as fast or slow as you wish.  There are small settlements and cities to discover and trade with and believe me those came in handy a few times I was down to a handful of stale bread for 200 citizens!  You'll do some survival, resource and architectural management but not to the point it feels like a chore and you'll have a crisis here and there mostly a result of your own doing.  The game was fun and visually appealing. The map design created biomes (took that from Subnautica) presenting different visual topologies. Many times I just stopped and spent a few minutes peeking through clouds to see what was down below or perusing my own city. There’s never a need to rush as there are no timelines and that’s good because you’ll make a lot of adjustments throughout the game keeping in mind the weight and drag of your city as you add to it. There is a meter showing how much float factor you have so if needed throw in a fan or wing when it turns yellow and if it seems like you’re moving along like molasses some propellers or oars will help with that.  All of these things require resources, workers, space and endless tweaks meaning you're never finished designing, planning or changing your city. Not that you always have to but it's just a lot of fun.  By the end of the game my city was architecturally a train wreck looking like puzzle pieces that didn’t quite fit together but, it's still my puzzle and I enjoyed putting it together. I hope you enjoy putting your puzzle together too!

_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A hybrid of adventure/exploration and city builderThere's a main quest and subquests you fly around doing while slowly growing the city. There's a bunch of resources, but they're generally not a challenge to find, and the main limiting factor is always people. For example, there's an area where food is really scarce. so you can't just send people down to get food, you need farms, but farms take people, so you have less people to gather the other resources. Farms also use water, so you need more water, but you can also collect water from the air, but that requires people....so there's a lot of decisions to be made with how to use people to make the resources work. And then the way you get more people, is do the quests, which are basically just flying from A to B and back to A or something similar. As a city builder maybe kind of weak since you don't spend a whole lot of time building.I beat it in 6 hours. I didn't manage to find all the parts to build the wonders, I dunno if I'll bother.Was neat. Soundtrack with middle east vibes was really good and gave a lot of immersion.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game but way too easy. All you have to do is survive and research the important stuff (Population uses less food, store more coal etc) and you're good for most of the game. Definitely worth about $8Suggestions:Make late game research require late game resources (e.g. iron, canvas, some other rare resource)Make larger population require more variety in food and water (see the Anno Series)Make quest rewards allow for larger population or research (similar to how relics allow current research)
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Very entertaining chilled out city management game with an RPG twist. I adore the sort of Arabian nights theme and attention to detail is very nice. I am only on the second area, so far resource management has been on the easy side but I can see the difficulty in having a higher population for sure. Looking forward to dumping another 10 or so hours into this! Will certainly be buying Airborne Empire as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Game is visually beautiful with equally beautiful sound and music, the devs took a extremely unique approach with this game. I've played my fair share of city builders and this one by far stands out. Game play is relaxing and thoughtful, with a unique story that gives the world substance, giving the world a dreamy otherworldly feel. The approach of sustaining a city completely in the air forces you to plan your building placements carefully, with the risk of tilting your city you have to think ahead. Would definitely recommend if your looking for a slow pace and relaxing city builder. Looking forward to their next instalment in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I just love airships so I feel like that makes me unfairly biased here. Secondly, this is a very addictive game and I love it. There is very little not to like, everything flows together nicely, the graphics are amazing, and customization is very fun to play with. Whether you choose to stay at the recommended 150 person kingdom, or push the limits (This game will test some older hardware, but mine ran fine in 3840x1080 until I peaked over the 175 mark. i7-3770, 16gb 1866mhz RAM, RX 480 8gb, SSD). I pushed it to close to 400 inhabitants and I slowed waaay down, but that was to be expected on my hardware and I was impressed. I already added the sequel to my wishlist and look forward to playing it in as much depth as I have this game!* * * * *
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first playthough, and I can definitely recommend this. A lot of the game is kind of generic city builder, but your city can move, go out and explore and visit other cities for trade and to complete quests, Like any good rts there are a lot of plates you have to keep spinning: lift, balance, food, water, fuel, population, four different needs to keep your people satisfied., etc. And while the game does have a kind of casual vibe, your colony will crash to the ground if you're not careful. (There are autosaves, but I recommend not using them; just start over but without repeating the same mistakes you made early on.) While the game does have an ending, it's also open ended, so after the final credits you can reload and continue to explore, tweak your layout, optimize your resource production, or just continue to expand until your GPU can't take any more. There is also a whole bonus area to explore post-game which I haven't touched yet. And there are  hard mode and new game+ options if you want to start again from scratch. Without these things the base game alone would be short by rts standards; my first complete playthrough was 30 hours from start to final credits, but there's probably several times that in replay value and value for price should not be a worry. The art and music are a plus as well, but you can probably check that on the store page.This is an indie game and often has that indie quirkiness. For example there is no money; everything is direct barter. (Exchange rates vary from place to place btw, so it pays to shop around.) Your inhabitants are a bit stick-figure-like, but you don't spend a lot of time looking at them anyway.Summary: A good city builder/exploration crossover, relaxing but engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a masterful piece of gaming pleasure. Very relaxing, methodical and beautifully crafted. Love the cutscenes and the narration, gives me Homeworld feels. No bugs what-so-ever. It was nice to take a break from the combat in other games, and help out those in need. Cant wait for the sequel. Keep up the good work, Devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. To me it's one of those games that feels like I've been playing for 15 minutes and it's been 3 hours. Completely lose myself in this game. Absolutely wonderful from the city building sim to the tiniest details of maintaining overall balance: forward/back, left/right, and all while trying to mainain population harmony. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say the ratings in the first trailer on the page are pretty accurate. It's a beautiful game, the management portion of it is very easy to accidentally do wrong (I almost lost my city after a few hours to a small miscalculation). I felt like the world could have had more things in it, the left half of the map is completely unused, and the north most area could be integrated into the win condition in some way. But I did enjoy my time, however brief, floating my city around and discovering the world. I didn't feel too attached to any of my settlers so having them abandon me meant nothing, and it's almost guaranteed that you will have people leave your city with how the citizen needs system works (you need all 4 desires before you hit 100 population, I hadn't even been to the third biome yet). Ultimately, I felt like my time with this game was longer than it actually was. The game does have New Game+, but I don't tend to partake in those systems so I wouldn't recommend this at full price unless you're willing to spend time perfecting/decorating your city, exploring the north, and partaking of NG+. Despite that, I'd still give it a 4/5 just due to how enjoyable it was as an experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very good and a lot of fun to play.  I enjoyed doing all the quest and following the story and completing my airborne kingdom.  My only complaint is that once your done all the quest it just left me with a huge floating city with no real objective to keep playing.  But other than that I do recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a settlement building game. The story flavor of the flying city feels very different, and the soundtrack is lovely. The tech tree does control what you can use, but you also have to carefully plan out your placements. Tilt due to weight/lift is a factor, as is running out of resources. Each building required materials and people to build the building, but the people amount specified are dedicated to that building. So, if you have 5 idle people and build a building needing 5 people - you will find there is no one left to gather resources on the map. But higher populations mean more draw on your resources and other city factors (e.g. might need to build housing which can affect lift and tilt). Most buildings have a minimum number of people stated, but I haven't figured out anyway to set just the minimum to a building (i.e. like I would want to do if I had enough of a produced material but now needed more coal). I got snagged in trying to focus on engineering research and lost a lot of people because I hadn't researched desires. Monitoring your population is a must as there isn't a way for the player to reduce people in buildings to the minimum required levels (that I have found).So, you can end up with decisions about demolishing buildings just to keep some idle people around for gathering. I got snagged in trying to focus on engineering research and lost a lot of people because I hadn't researched desires. You can add more recruits from villages/cities on the ground, but this is related to the happiness level of your current populace. If your people become unhappy, and start to leave, it can become hard to keep the level of resources you need, and hard to recruit new people.Still going to finish out this play-through, but if I restart, I think I will look into having my paths be 2 squares wide. I was really frustrated with having to build the lights, due to where they have to be placed. They take up a single square, and have to be supported by a path...but they can break a grid pattern which I was using to make sure I kept my city balanced. But if my paths were 2 squares wide, I could still grid out my city, and after researching the lights would be able to more easily insert them where they are needed. This will cause a bigger draw on my lift, though, so, not sure how that will play out. [So, they have a new(?) checkbox about if I got the product for free. My spouse gave it to me as a gift after they played the game and thought I would like it. No additional compensation received.]
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere, fantastic soundtrack, relaxing gameplay.I love the design of this game and how the gameplay is executed by navigating your colony through the air and collecting resources on land via scout aircraft.I also like with each building placement effects the weight and balance of the entire settlement.Overall superb game!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing to play, with a smoothing soundtrack as well. The balancing of the city and staying airborne is a nice added challenge. The main game is easy enough to complete, the optional ice part a solid challenge. This section is near impossible without It's not an absolute masterpiece, and I wish that the city and settlement interactions had more variety to them. I also wish I could have selected multiple buildings by click and drag selection, instead of individual clicks.Overall, definitely a recommendation! I'd say, buy on sale to justify the cost/hour. It was definitely a cool, fun, mysterious experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent enough game. There's not much to the city building and balancing/finding resources isn't very demanding or engaging but the theme is pretty engrossing. The music carries the experience, frankly, and probably had me stay with the game a lot longer than I would have otherwise.The game pretty much revolves around fetch quests for random towns you find around the area. Do 1-2 tasks for them, build a port and then they become your ally. Get enough allies and you win
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give the game a 7/10This game is a great experience, but lacks replay-ability. I love everything about building a city in the sky, and in that aspect the game play nails it. Your city is more like an airship, it needs fuel to stay alift, and must stay balanced  or it will plummet to the ground. Resources can be mined from the ground as long as you have an airport and idle workers or they can be bartered from the kingdoms. The kingdoms offer new blueprints for relics, as well as alliances for quests. Relics can be found by searching lost ruins dotting the vast open world.Unfortunately the kingdom alliance system is where I think the game gets kind of dull. You either find something for them, repair something for them, or both and then they just agree to align with your sky kingdom after you build an airport for them. However the rewards are rarely as fulfilling they as the blueprints, they each just give you +1 free wood and a handful of new workers. Yep that's it, rinse repeat! I think this could have been fleshed out with more player choice in how they impress the kingdom.Looking beyond the main story, its still a great relaxing city builder with visuals out this world and thus I do recommend. They nail the steampunk city builder and something about mid-eastern architecture just jives so well with the steampunk genre. I recommend it with caveat of waiting for a sale as most players put in 10-25 hrs.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of cool, but short.  I played through about half-way, restarted and then won after 30 hours.  It does have a New Game+ that I haven't tried.Their are some weird gameplay choices.  There's only one save game so there's no going back if you make a bad decision, so its kind of a city builder in hard-core mode which is novel I guess.  This does prevent you from playing multiple Kingdoms at the same time which just seems like a BIG oversight.Designing your own flying kingdom is a lot of fun if you're a little bored of city builders and want to do some building, but different.  The graphics are beautiful and you can customize your city in all sorts of ways, but its single player with no in-game sharing or anything, so I guess you send all your friends snapshots?I bought this at full price.  Was it worth it?  Maybe, I'm still undecided.  If New Game+ has enough replayability and isn't just the same game but harder, maybe I'll be hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Management sim where you fly between places and harvest materials to keep yourself aloft.  The building mechanic is fun, and not overly deep.  Replays and the post-credits endgame of flying into the cold north probably isn't worth it unless you really enjoy it.  Art is great, both the buildings and the map you fly over.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a chill no-combat game centered around exploring and managing different resources. This is the game for calming, almost meditative survival; the music and visuals wash over you and you relax most of the time you are playing. You can get yourself into tight squeezes with limited resources, and running out of coal is something you should experience at least once lol.I started a second playthrough and while the game is short, I am enjoying chilling out with it. The timer-based tech tree and city-building aspects are also an interesting part of the game, providing some tension as you try to resolve what's going on with your city's balance (both physical and desire).Update: I've completed the Tundra DLC and I have to say, thank you for this additional challenge!The new mechanic really brought the management aspect into tight focus, and I ended up circling the map several times until I was at 996 settlers! My finish was a bit janky but it was fun rearranging my city to make it work better. Feedback: there could be some quality of life improvements around setting multiple buildings or trees to move at one time.Oh, and since the game doesn't autosave, save every hour because you will likely ditch multiple times getting used to the new mechanic AND to having to go up to tremendous scale! This was a really great extension of the original game!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game, But be aware that it is very short if your use to a normal city builder like Civ you will steam role through this very quickly. which for me was a nice change but I recognise wouldn't be for everyone. Also don't get it at full price, £15 is the absolute max I would pay for it on a good day.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Very good, simple, straightfoward city building game. Made by an indie studio.Brilliant idea (a flying city, WUT??), interesting lore (though pretty simple). Game is also pretty short if you don't want to play in New Game +. Though 6-7 hours is fine for games like these that have a story. You can play indefinitely though.And the music is pretty great.Only con is the optimization, although for games like these it does not matter that much.Great job developers! 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Is it long? No. I cleared the game in under 20 hours.Is the game worth the money? That is hard to say, since you know your budget. But for me I think the game was worth it. It was a beautiful city builder, with a relaxing vibe, great music and aesthetics. Perfect game if you are looking something more on the casual side.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a RTS/City simulator, without the combat (at least where I'm thus far into the game).  Just 4 hours in I can fresh mechanics and see how they mix things up.  I like the touch of having to watch the tilt of your city, and having a moving city where you can move after exhausting the resources in your area is cool.  This is contrasted to old RTSes like say Starcraft where you'd need to load a new map to get more resources.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Had a bit of a mixed view of this game when I first played it. Couldn't tell if I enjoyed it as it is not your typical city building game.But honestly I ended up engrossed, this game has fantastic visuals, an interesting take on the environment you're roaming and combines stories and quests with building and managing your city.I almost gave up at first as I didn't like how muddled and confused my city layout was. However, you can move any building you want at a cost that can be reduced via research. The games story flows well with the development of your city and I found myself traversing the map with many a goal whether it was working towards self sufficiency or gathering resources and objects for completing quests.Just like the tropico series and other story like city games, you can lose your city if you are not careful, so it makes for a nice strategy building sim. Would recommend if you are looking for a relaxing new game.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Not a huge game, but a fun piece of art. The mechanics are very simply but the penalties are punishing. As long as you pay attention to your kingdoms balance and resources, you can't really fail this game.The city building aspect feels very rewarding and the visual effects are awesome. I won't see myself playing for hunderds of hours, but the hours I did put into it were absolutely great.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A very good experience. In the sweetspot between relaxing and challenging, Airborne Kingdom take an already innovative idea (a city builder with a MOVING city) and keeps on innovating, creating a story to follow, making an Hybrid between city builders and adventures.Recommended if you like city builders and want to try a different spin for a change.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A fun chilled out city management and resource collection game.Visually one of the most stunning games in years, the artwork is superb, the music is also very chilling and relaxing.Both the art and music is a very Arabian nights kind of feel.Got everything I wanted done in a couple of play-through.Not a steep learning curve.The wonders and statues (north area) give a great addition to the city and the three wonders give good functionality (though more description of what that is would be nice).The Negatives.Navigating using a click on the map would have been VERY nice, but sadly is not possible, meaning you have to look on map, then close it and click in the distance and then re-open to check you are headed to the right spot.The map, while amazing, has one issue, it is a tapestry, but the edges or no go area is torn up paper and not torn up material as you would expect.A couple of things could have made it easier, like a temperature overlay to see those things at that part of the game and getting temperature from existing buildings, pretty sure a charcoal maker is hot after all!Tilt, is that positive or negative up/down on the font/back left/right? Also left/right should have been port/starboard really.A few achievements could have been added for fun, like crash the city, flip the city, get to 100% speed with the city.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really lovely and wholesome games. I love this kind of game and yet this one is quite unique as far as I know because of the fact your little city floats. It is a really well executed idea and I enjoyed it greatly.For anyone who likes the city building and resource management type of game, this is a really great one, really interesting but at the same time, with a sense of calmness that I really appreciated.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute delight of a game!Because now I partially know exactly how Rosalind Lutece felt like.And that alone is worth it.It also catered real well to my long lost childhood dreams of living on an airship.Airships and submarines.I am clearly noticing a pattern in myself of wishing to go where very few people live.It started early.Like some sexual preference.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice city builder/manager game with a cool twist. The city is always on the move, roaming the world in the skies, looking for new resources and helping other (surface) kingdoms.The main game on normal difficulty is somewhat a big tutorial, all the requirements are pretty low and there are almost no difficulties. I was gonna say that the game is way too easy, but i guess it's fine, especially for people without excessive amount of experience in this type of games.The really nice surprise was the New Game + on hard mode. It still was >not< that difficult, definitely not as difficult as I was expecting, but it was way more interesting, a bit more demanding on planning and resource management.Over all, very positive surprise, a nice idea in a good looking package that will keep you entertained for a few afternoons.Full completionist time: around 20 hours, not pushing it
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: It took me about 15 minutes to realize this is a pretty good game.  I can tell without having played very much that it's going to take some time to figure everything out and understand the basic strategies for a successful play-through.  Simple at first but enough resource management required to demand some thought.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Took me 11 hrs to complete the campaign/story. Very lovely. At "normal" difficulty I only had to struggle twice, coal was empty and workers left because of my flying kingdom went too much weight behind. I will start the creativitiy mode once I got time again - because music, gameplay etc. is very chill.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: It is a nice but short game. Worth the money on sale.It's a really good game, the art style is very chill and cozy, the city building mechanics is a bit refreshing with the "tilt" having to be considered.If you like chill games and city builders, this is a very good option, however I will not recommend it at full price, 21€ is a bit too much compared to the length and replayability of the game. In just around 10 hours have I completed the story and with 83% of all achievements. (The rest are game+ repeat)Is the game on sale, like midweek madness 50% off, then definitely woth it.Is the game not on sale, then I wouldn't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable! Took me three tries to get my city's economy thriving well enough to make it all the way to the end, but even the failures were fun to build. There does seem to be some randomness in when you get some of the technology, which can make it a little harder to progress - for example I found street lighting in the first area the first two playthroughs, and then not until I was in the second area on the third one, and it's one of the things needed to keep your inhabitants happy beyond a certain population threshold. Had fun, and do plan to play it again some time.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, quite fun. Recommend if you like flotsam or similar colony games. That being said, some weird oversights with it. Some buildings are objectively worse than their lower tier counterparts. You get pigeon held a bit into building a specific way that can require you to tear down your old structures to replace them in a similar but different pattern. That is, until you realize that most of the games base mechanics are kinda optional. You don't have to make your people jubilant, there's basically no downside to having them be satisfied (you might be able to recruit one less person at a small civilization, big whoop). Base tilt is basically never an issue since you can always pick up and move your structures. Researching zero cost to move structures basically just breaks the game and makes it easy mode. All that being said, still a solid game, and very good for what it sets out to accomplish. The ambiance, music, and exploration is all done very well. 6.6 our of 10
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game. I played through the campaigns, they were pretty easy but noticed the main differences in level were mostly the rate of consumption for things and speed to build/change. I think there were some bugs mainly with draw distance and it kinda seems like this game has been abandoned by the dev teams so unless some strangers decide to do a good one and patch, this game will remain in the same "meh" dev state. I really enjoyed it, I think $12.49 is a fair price and I really feel it was relaxing mostly.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Before buying a game, I use to count that in beers. If I spend my friday evening playing it, I save at least 3 beers. Which is between 15 and 30€.  So it was worth it.Besides, have you ever seen Aladdin? Well, that's the steampunk version of it where you need to build the carpet tho.And there is kind of endgames thing which is a cherry on the cake !
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: fun and pretty, relatively low stress and breezy (even if it's mechanically very inspired by frostpunk, it doesn't have the pressing sense of urgency and the feeling of danger). The mobility of your town feels pretty novel, and gives it a nice modal feel of 1) designing your town while 2) waiting to reach your destination and grabbing resources you see along the way.  Not a game that requires much pausing and thinking, even though you're doing two things at once. Lots of secrets to find while you're going, which rewards keeping an eye out even while you're not active.  The two level gameplay plus the great music and aesthetic means you can get really absorbed in this and not notice time pass, and what more can you ask for from a chill city builder?
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: 3.9/5 stars: great ideas, interesting incidental lore and aesthetic. Points off for UX/ease of use, pace of play. Fun resource survival game, but doesn't quite feel finished. Lots of good ideas and generally a fun way to kill time. Fastest play mode is the only mode worth playing on once you figure out which buttons do what.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game, and I enjoyed the game. I learned valuable life lessons from the game, and I felt happy while playing it. It feels like an old school game you play to have a good time, and not a modern online game you grind endlessly through while hating most of it for 100+ hours for some worthless cosmetics and an online profile badge.It is a gentle and peaceful game that promotes the ideas of cooperation, working with others to achieve a goal, honor and values, being a hero and helping people. Essentially, it's the exact opposite of league of legends.The game is wonderful. A little bit short, I finished the main quest-line in about 10 hours but it can be done a lot quicker if you are not taking your time to slow down and enjoy things. I got it on sale so it was good value for money, but I think people who pay full price for it may be a bit disappointed in the value for money compared to other games that are available and have a lot more content and replayability for the same (or a similar) price.The one important thing to note is that this is a small indie game made by a few people and not a large team, so the lack of content compared to a modern big studio game with 20-100+ staff is understandable, having said that, Bioware had A LOT of people working on Mass effect Andromeda and Airbourne Kingdom is a much better game. If you buy the game, you support the team, who will hopefully be making a lot more games in the future and will build and improve on the skills they developed while making Airbourne Kingdom. While I would like to see more content added to Airbourne Kingdom ( I kind of feel it needs something like an extra level of advanced upgrades added to the tech tree which are unlocked after the first play through is complete) it does feel like a complete game and not some half finished early access game that gets launched before it's finished so the dev's can sell you the second half of the game in multiple dlc's.I am not sure if I could recommend the game at full price, especially since it has been out a while and they took money from Epic games to sell it exclusively for a long period of time, but if you can get it on sale at half price (or close to that) I would 100% recommend it. However, if you have money to spare, then paying full price means the money will go to a good group of people who made a wonderful game, and will hopefully support them to make many more in the future.I wish everyone on the team all the best for their future endeavours, and look forward to playing more of their games in the future.9/10 at full price.10/10 on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightful game. It portrays a lot of TRUTH in this world. I enjoyed hovering above the clouds as if i was flying as well, breathtaking. I love how we go down on planes and gather the materials, make alliances and trade technologies. Enjoyed playing it at the same time relaxing as well! Concept, Design, Music. LOVE IT!Please make some more like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth every last penny, I am so happy it has arrived on Steam and I could finally play it. It is a magical adventure with a very reasonable campaign length. It is by no means a hardcore city-builder (although I have yet to play Hard mode), if you are looking for a brutal challenge, look elsewhere. Instead, AK puts the emphasis on the absolute gorgeous visuals, a chill and heartwarming story and world, and the clever game mechanics of having to balance your resources and the very city itself from toppling over by tilt or weight. If you aren't careful with planning for the lack of certain resources in the territories, then the game WILL force you into a "fly of shame" back to the starting area for better preparing (or crashing straight into the ground), so do not take the warning messages lightly.I do not know if there is a sequel planned or in the works, but I am holding out for one! All around wonderful job, dev team, 10/10, it is an instanct classic for me which I will no doubt revisit often down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: An addictive city builder in which you manage resources, balance your floating city and your people's desires, and explore a map that unfurls around you.It has a Middle Eastern aesthetic which was refreshing, though it felt weird to put Halloween and Christmas decorations on the buildings. But the graphics are enjoyable and the music was perfect: nice but not obtrusive. I only noticed some performance issues at the end, which the game fairly warned me was because I had too many people.The resource managing/exploration balance is very well done. I felt just challenged enough to always want to play a few more minutes. My only issues were the timing of discovering each desire vs. the number of people: at one point I couldn't make my people jubilant because they didn't have 4 needs met, but I hadn't discovered the 4th need yet. Also the Wonders were difficult to find (I hear turning off map fog helps). But I really appreciated having an end goal rather than sailing around forever.Overall this is a great game to zone into over a weekend or a long plane ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend on saleThe game is basically what you  see in the trailers and gameplay, there is the loop of find something collecting resources and moving on, after a while it gets old and boring the only times that it gets "challenging" is when you reach a growth threshold and suddenly all your pops need a new requirement, that for you to unlock you have to find a city buy the blueprint, research the building and them build it, so in this meanwhile all your citizens get angry and a few leave.The game is nice, have a cool concept but it has nothing more than that, the map is bland what makes the travelling (a core of this game) also bland
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: If it's on sale it's definitely worth it for an idle city builder. Music is OK but repeats infinitely which can be a drag, and the game is in no way difficult if you pay attention. Balancing the ship is fun and the lore is pretty cool, though I wish they had kept the narration through out. All and all very solid relaxing time. I binged it at had a self sufficient ship by end of game in 17 hours. I plan on checking out the North and retooling my ship for just travel, and try and find the 3 treasures so I suspect I'll get another few hours out of it at least. Also the fact the game could have easily been made more difficult but wasn't is a testimony to the experience you're in for.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting twist on the city builder type of game, while the main game itself is quite short, you can spend lots of time trying new build styles, there are a few areas that may benefit from quality of life improvements (such as being able to disable certain buildings so you have the workers available, especially after you lose citizens). But over all this is a great game and very relaxing
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the unique gameplay, even though the game will be completed in 10 to 15 hours at max. As visible in various screenshots and videos your objective is to build a flying city while you explore the environment to finish tasks. Meanwhile you also need to manage ressources. The game is a great. I don't think it offers replayability
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic city builder game!Tons of aspects to think about and keep track of when building your city, but it doesn't feel overwhelming.Honestly my biggest gripe with this game is that there aren't more sound effects from the machinery in your city, you only hear gears grinding/etc. from the town center. I think it'd be awesome if you could hear noise from the citizens and other buildings as they do their thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A chill, non-violent city builder. Your city being mobile allows for some novel management twists; you can fly your city across an expansive map to gather specific resources, recruit citizens, and visit surface towns. While I had hoped for a bit more depth in its systems, I found the experience very enjoyable overall.The building aspects of management are simple but fun. Your city requires lift to remain airborne, and propulsion to move forward. Everything you build adds weight and drag that counter these, and uneven building practices can tilt your whole city, decreasing both propulsion and citizen happiness. Some buildings add positive or negative modifiers to the ones surrounding it, so experimenting with layout is the name of the game.Most buildings require citizens to function; these citizens can be recruited from settlements or earned as quest rewards. Each citizen requires food, water, and housing, and as your city grows, more citizen needs (Faith, Health, and Comfort) are introduced one at a time. Unlike many city builders, Airborne Kingdom is mainly campaign-driven. Your three goals are:1. Remain airborne.2. Recruit 150 citizens.3. Unite the 12 surface kingdoms.This third objective makes up the bulk of the campaign. As you explore the skies, you'll come across kingdoms in need of help. Many require certain resources, while some ask of you to explore ruins or track down lost search parties. The tasks are basic, but the strong writing and personality of each kingdom are engaging enough to encourage their completion. Plus, winning over a kingdom will net you extra citizens and permanent resource boosts.While the game is exceptionally beautiful, performance hitches are not uncommon.  Once you reach 200 citizens (which I did well before the end of the campaign) you are notified that further recruitment may negatively impact performance. There are a few graphics options to help with this, such as replacing animated citizen models with simple pawns, but I found that they didn't help for long. Eventually I turned every graphical setting to low or off, but did not notice much improvement in performance.More complex cities impact performance dramatically. I chose not to play the free Tundra DLC simply because the game couldn't handle the sheer awesomeness of my kingdom. I'd like to come back to it eventually, provided these problems are resolved.On three occasions my airship's shadow began strobing sporadically. A hard restart fixed this each time.Beautiful atmosphere and music, and a sleek and lovely UI make for a mostly friction-free experience. I had issues with a few hotkeys (Z to move buildings during construction mode was especially inconsistent), and found it frustrating that bringing up in-game menus did not pause the game in the background (since you burn through resources even while idle).Playing at a leisurely pace, I reached 150 citizens in about 8 hours, and united the kingdoms by hour 12.There is a free DLC area I have yet to explore due to the technical issues mentioned previously, but I plan on coming back to it once those are hopefully sorted. I found Airborne Kingdom well worth the price of entry. While the experience as it stands is a bit simple, I see the seeds of amazing ideas here. A sequel with deeper systems and mechanics would be an instant buy for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I play games that focus on controlling a single character, and so most city-building games fly under my radar. But what if the character you control WAS a city that you also have to build? Not only is Airborne Kingdom great, it also got me re-interested in the genre. And the art, animations, writing, and music are excellent. Highly recommend checking this out.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very enjoyable, chill-out city builder with a twist. With its very distinctive graphic style that is refreshing to see. And easy mechanics that allow reasonably quick progress through the stories. After the first play-through, I found myself adding my own challenges on arranging the city, when to build what, etc. So replayability might be low, even with new biomes. Still I keep coming back to it to have just one more go.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Airborne City is a very solid mashup of a city builder combined with a survival exploration game. I enjoyed completing all the quests to ally with the 12 kingdoms, but had a rough time for a while because I felt like I quite literally couldn't research fast enough to keep my population happy while also getting enough food and resources to explore and do quests. An important thing to know is that the map is randomly generated, so if you're struggling to find certain things, you can't rely on guides to help you. Get it while it's on sale, I'd say.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, got it as a gift from a friend and has saved me hours of boredom.The music is really nice and chill, a perfect complement to the gameThe art style is really pretty, a mix between a diorama and a map really conveys that weird mystical feeling.The difficulty is there IF you don't know what to do, AKA the first run, after that you know what buildings need to be used and where they have to be placed.Unfortunately this game is reaaaally short: 12 cities and that's it for the main game; sure they added a new "frostpunkesque" section of the map but unless you're achievement hunting it is completely optional.A really really nice game, hope to see more stuff in te future if they keep updating it.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Short but relaxing city building/management sim. Art style and music stand out as high points for me. No real threats or enemies in game other than meeting the needs of your citizens and keeping a steady stream of resources going. Fly the city around, gather resources as you go, find the Easter eggs on the map.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxing and chill (flying)city management game.You'll have to scour the lands for resources while making sure your ship doesn't go down, looking for all sorts of treasure.You'll keep unlocking new stuff to add onto the city, make sure it doesn't drag you down too much though.The music is fantastic and the art style makes me think of the amazing game Ilomilo, very handcrafty.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: If you are tired of combat and shooting stuff, you need to try this game out. Control a flying airship, build onto it, recruit people at the places you find while exploring the realms of this game. The artwork is amazing, the sounds soothing, and the idea inspiring! This has to be one of the best games I have ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool take on a colony building game. It has enough depth that you need to plan how to set your kingdom up without being to complicated, plus after some research the drawback to demoing or moving your structures is lessened and then outright removed which opens up all sorts of redesigns. It has a nice light story and easy to grasp system. Definitely a great game to relax and play.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Airborne Kingdom is a pleasure to spend a relaxing few hours with. It has a refreshing approach to the city building genre which is genuinely unique and although it eschews conflict and drama, the survival elements, resource collection tasks and challenges of building an optimal floating city are both engaging and relaxing. Airborne Kingdom has an outstanding core premise and aesthetics but lacking some genre-standard features like a sandbox mode or customizable structures, it can offer up its pleasures and be done a little too quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom
