_childDocuments_.review: Pretty neat game, the only issues are not much replayability, moving buildings can be really awkward/not work sometimes, and this is a meta complaint but simulating citizens was pretty pointless in this. Your town won't ever get big enough to really care about how far they have to travel to workOtherwise, pretty fun little game with a fantastic soundtrack
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: a nicely polished city builder, with intriguing setup (you need to make sure your floating city does not tilt or fall). lots of interdependencies make sure you have to think through your moves, not just build-build-build.I'm at around 40% after 7 hours. not sure to see much of a replay value, but good entertainment for the coming hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A cool little settlement building / resource management game from independent studio. The concept of movable settlement is not new, but the setting is nice and well made. It has this 'one more minute' vibe, where You want to do next thing, like finding the resources You lack or fulfilling the quest. There are some tense moments, when You run out of coal and frantically look for source, or when population starts complaining and all idle workers disappear. Well balanced, it keeps You always on edge of running out of something, even with advanced research. Graphics is also nice, especially for such small team - well done. Sound doesn't disappoint neither.It has some replayability value too, mainly to collect all missing pieces of wonders. I think I could, and probably will, pump next few hours into it.Finishing the game took 9 hours, well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most interesting city building games since the birth of the genre. The core premise is really innovative and makes the game feel fresh even for someone like me who hasn't put more than a couple hours each into the latest city building games in years due to boredom with the same basic gameplay. It doesn't hurt that the world is beautiful in its own way and together with the music comes together to evoke a real feeling of an ancient world that fell apart. Despite the need to constantly manage resources and needs it still feels very peaceful and relaxing to play. My only real complaint was that I was initially not happy that you had to demolish buildings in order to re-allocate workers but I soon realised exactly why the game was designed that way and so even that fell away.Highly recommended and I look forward to playing through it again as well as the potential sequel in the future. A great game by a small but talented bunch of people.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: It is a beautiful game except for the mind bending, eye bleeding tedium of trying to find bits and pieces made even more difficult by nights and clouds to the extent where you want to scream and then swear once you have beat the game you will NEVER EVER play it again...oh yes, you may need trauma counselling too.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting city builder, I would like to see them add oceans instead of what looks like an ornate tabletop, but that aside I have played some hours on it and I am hooked, balancing out the city, flying it around, working out the placement of structures and trying to find the lost artifacts. It will kill time, you may lose track of time playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Game is tranquil and fun! Just finished (on normal) the campaign and starting to head to the other parts (thanks to the wonder).In the beginning resources are scarce and the more techs you unlock the more independent everything becomes.No micro-management necessary so you can focus on the grander scheme of things ;-)Looking forward to next update / DLC!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: It's a city builder game, except you're a floating city. You can move! And you have to worry about tilt, lift, and speed in addition to normal city issues. The only way to get new citizens is to recruit new ones from settlements and by completing quests for other kingdoms down on the surface. You need a steadily growing population or you'll quickly find you don't have enough people to build or gather resources. If you're a fan of resource management and worker placement heavy games, this should be right up your alley. Oh, and the board game aesthetic is very cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: It is addictive and I can't stop!!  I am madly in love with this game.  It is incredibly beautiful, I love the Steampunk appeal.  It is cleverly designed with a story, quests and music that make you feel you are in another world.  I love managing the city building and organising my city as it grows, and as I do research to learn new technology to add to my build.  You have to manage the weight of your city along with the speed it can travel along with the balance of the weight... so many things to consider, along with providing your inhabitants with their needs.  It is very challenging and exciting.  Also soothing, I find it relaxing and a great escape from reality and stress.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A solid, enjoyable ten hour experience. The colony builder parts are more like a puzzle game than anything else, but still very fun. The game is relaxing and easy to work through at your own pace as well. I opted not to play the New Game+ or hard mode, but more time to invest if you enjoy those things, too!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Get it on sale, the game is casual fun and it is enjoyable, but you don't get a lot for your money. I got a few 0.1% achievements and beat the game in just under 10 hours. After the first 2 hours you've already explored all the game has to offer.There's no design challenge here like you'd normally find in a city builder game. The game feels half finished, and it should really be changed to early access on steam. I ran into multiple bugs and it seems the build options are very limited and often don't add anything new to the game. The renewable resources you get from the cities (with the exception of wood) are completely useless too. There's just not very much here.The core game and vision is done, but the actual game mechanics and execution of buildings / design are just very lacking.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Hard review to write, but in 9hrs i went way overboard with the city building side of things and also completed the main story. If i'd gone bare bones city building, then it's really only a 3-4hr campaign is my bet. I liked it well enough, but I even realized about 45mins in that "this is a game i'll only play once then uninstall"
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice and chill combination city builder and exploration game. There aren't enemies trying to shoot you down, your "enemy" is instead running low on vital resources. The difference between this and other games is that in other city builders there is usually a long lead time between setting up farms and delivering food. Here you just have to fly around and find farmlands and then descend upon it with your fleet of planes to pick the land clean.There is some replay in New Game+ and Harder difficulties but personally once I played through and experienced the gameplay end to end there wasn't a very strong desire to come back to it. Early on its a great experience but unfortunately there is a limit to what kind of new mechanics it can really introduce so by about mid-game you've seen just about everything and while you can always tinker with your city to make it more efficient there isn't really a "late-game" phase to push you to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: AK - the reverese Frostpunk you thought you didn't need but ended up playing through and starting a NG+ just to squeeze it just a little more and get all those themes collected and you didn't get enough of that builder-fix (I mean you gotta get it right this time, that one building that tilted the whole thing wrong). Great music tracks as well while cruising your large flying city in the air above the dunes towards the sunset. Don't mind the labyrinthine pathways stretching out like a huge Nazca bird; I'm just collecting the berries all over there while looting relics back over here.The game is just atmospheric, super wholesome & relaxing!I give this little hidden gem
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Very calming and beautiful city builder with lots of potential.Mod support / DLCs or a sequel would be great, to have more individual options in designing a city.Some minor UX annoyances can get a bit tedious at times, e.g. - Navigation, especially over longer distances is not possible via the map but only by clicking on the horizon, checking where you clicked and hoping that it's somewhere near the place you want to go, if not, rinse and repeat. - City Movement and looking around both set to the right mouse button can lead to a lot of accidental movement. - You should be able to permanently assign people for work in the hangar and remove them from your "available" worker pool. These are some of the points I noticed while playing, however this didn't stop the game from being an absolute marvel and I hope there will be more coming in this style.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what it says on the tin. "What if city builder but your city can fly" is a good concept. It lets you do the normal city builder stuff while also being able to go on quests and explore a world like you do in other video games. Most of the enjoyment I got out of the game came from the city itself. It's very aesthetically pleasing, seeing your city drift serenely through the sky like a gentrified UFO, your little dudes flying their gliders down to the earth to gather resources with little contrails tailing behind, fans spinning and fins flapping to keep you aloft and moving forward. Aside from that, though, the rest of the game doesn't have much to offer. Pretty much every quest in the game is just a fetch quest, and the ones that aren't are even less complicated. When new resources or research is introduced, they do little to distinguish themselves thematically, and just offer another way to make your bad numbers smaller and your good numbers bigger, and as a result, you kind of see everything there is to see in the first major area (of which there are three). Overall though, it's a recommend, although more of a "sure, if it's on sale, and the concept appeals to you" sort of recommend. And honestly, if they made a sequel to this with more... well, everything...  I'd love to see it.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a particularly big game, but what is there is very well polished and refined. Played through it twice, once with NG+ and 100%ed it in 12 hours, and it was 12 hours well spent. If you're looking for something to sink 100s of hours into, this probably isn't for you, but otherwise I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable fantasy game, calming music, great visuals, finished the main quest in 2-3 sittings, the arabic-like concept feels really fresh, it's been forever since I was this hooked to a game! Would love to see some sort of expansion to a more complex city builder and/or more incentives to increase replayability. Buy on sale for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxed game, though probably going to screw up your first play through, The most chill way for me ended up learning a layout in creative that I could use in the regular game. First city got all kinds of screwed up because I didn't know what i was going to have to plan for with new buildings and tech.It is possible to move buildings.. but it sucks and is the worst part of the experience.To move buildings, ideally there is research to make it free to move or destroy buildings BUT, the players must have the resource storage space or the materials are lost anyway and if the player has spent the time to make changing the city layout less of a chore by having storage space and research ready, the players still must maintain the city's weight distribution. Not keeping the city balanced makes the citizens angry and they might start leaving as your trying to fix the city so that streets have the proper lighting or healthcare access. (and those needs aren't obvious in the beginning because citizens only want them after you find new discoveries like street lights or religion) To make it worse buildings need to be connected by paths.. unless they can be grouped.. except the player doesnt know how big groups are until trying out different configurations of buildings. Like houses can be in groups of 4 .. only 1 house needs to connect to the path for that whole group.. but trees have an unlimited group (you can build a tree next to another tree without needing to place it next to a path) Farms can group.. and having roads to connect things while your shuffling buildings is a bit much, and the interface sucks for moving buildings and there is a lot of extra clicking.For example, if you wanted to move a house. you have to click on the house, find a place on a made path to move that house. confirm it is going there.. and then if its a stacked house.. you have to do that individually for each house in the stack.. and in this game EVERY person has a house.. so after you get going if you wanted to move your neighborhood of people or re-organize them.. you might have to individually move and confirm 50+ houses. And that process gets exasperated by balancing the city so its not leaning to the side by shuffling things around as your moving individual buildings in stacks.. and other building types also stack.And this is kind of a slow paced game.. so screwing up my first play through was.. dumping a few hours into it and then figuring out it would be easier to start over. It can start getting boring waiting for research.. until I remembered to just build more academies.. and then that part was fun again.Would recommend as low stress game if you like planning and exploring and you dont mind spending some time figuring out an ideal layout so that part doesnt detract from the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Relax and fly a city in the clouds through a tapestry of scattered towns, lakes and forests. Then proceed to have a heart attack because you weren't watching your coal reserves and now your lovely little town is about to blow up. In reality its a fun game for those saturdays when its too hot or too cold and none of the boys are online.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A Very Enjoyable Eco Journey.This game is wonderfully delicious.  The theme and the particulars are so refreshing.  I don't want to spoil it too much for you, but pretty much Surviving the Aftermath and a dash of good stuff and poof!  It is great fun.  Just eco, no wars or dramatics.  The story is great and enjoyable.  You'll fall in love with the look of it I'm sure of it.  Oh heck, just get it already.  You'll love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Unique city builder with some new mechanics you will have to learn to balance like the tilt of your cityIt is in the more chill end of citybuilders and can border on boring when you travel from location to location.Could also benefit from being able to  select travel point in map instead of clicking a point in the horizonYou really also should be able to close a building or lower it's worker number. It really sucks that you have to destroy an entire building when you are in critical need of workers
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Not quite what I was expecting but a solid entry, nonetheless.  In truth, this feels more like a survival game than a city builder.  In the early parts of the game the placement of your buildings doesn’t matter that much. A lot more emphasis is put on navigating the world in order to find resources so that your people don’t go hungry/thirsty and that you have enough coal to keep the engine running.Towards the second half of the game, buildings and their placement become a lot more prominent, but it stills feels like a hybrid instead of a traditional city builder.  Also note, this is not a very long game.  Without rushing I was able to reach the end of the game in about 6 hours.  I think this is an appropriate length for the experience it offers but don’t go in expecting to spend 40 hours building the perfect city.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: negative first i suppose. One of the most frustrating thing about this game is not being able to set a way-point despite it being a travelling game of sorts. Going back and fort between the map just too see if im going the right direction is frustrating seeing as the only thing you can see if lights in the sky, even those can mess up your orientation a little. the idea is brilliant just poorly executed in my opinion. Your meant to be connecting these lost kingdoms together, even that is a pointless as i found these is nothing unique about them. you barely  have interrelation with any of them to say the least.another frustrating thing about this game is not being able to distribute your works to where you need them. removing that control from the players hand. Once a worker finishes a construction, and if said construction needs workers for it operate, your worker just moves in and starts working. So your there wondering what happen to my workers. So five hours into the game i then realise there is citizen everyone you recruit is a worker. and the majority of things you build needs workers. this game will often leave you without any depending on how your building, sometimes you have to scramble to find workers you can recruit.i can write a whole list of negatives found in this game. the only positive i have is the games building mechanics, totally unique and different from most city building games. this is obviously the selling point, most of hours came from the game being pause and me just building.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: In my honest opinion this is a bit short for a game but it is really fun to see that game developers have taken a different approach of city building, if you like city building games that floats then this is for you, the music is really nice, environment is excellent, but can be challenging to make sure your city stays afloat. Pros + Easy to learn+ Tech tree is not complicated+ Resources are easy to find+ Good tutorial+ Good storyCons-Too short gameBut this is just my opinion feel free to comment what pros and cons you have about the game, but in overall i'd give this game a 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: a fun , relaxing resource management sim. You do also build a city but you'll spend most of your time keeping track of various resources. Kind of like an ANNO game but you can float your city wherever you want to go so long as you have enough supplies to make the journey. Collect more resources and people along the way, solve minor problems for bit cities and keep building while keeping your people happy. If that sounds appealing to you , check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: 2 Complete play throughs, one on normal, one new game+ on hard.Its an easy game for someone that knows a city builder / resource manager but I think it's more about the experience of a new type of play style than the difficulty.Was really fun but I see no reason to play it again which is a shame because I'd like to.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This game has gameplay very distinguishably in contrast to other city-building sims. 2-axes weight-balancing system and reasonable scale limiting are unique and desirable.But the map to explore is a bit small, and the contents are not so much to play with for a long time; I could beat the scenario in only 5 hours short.Overall this game is recommendable, but the price is a little expensive to buy without any discounts for now (but future updates are expectable).
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking for something fresh, casual and constructive, and the unique style of this game scratched that itch while managing to tie a feel good but mildly forgettable story into the mix. Building and piloting a floating city while exploring a highly stylised world map with its own fictional history made for a really engaging and almost ethereal experience. I especially loved the music, which just gave the whole experience a dreamlike quality with a middle eastern flair that tied the whole theme of the game together perfectly.What a fantastic game, it's beautifully executed, I think everyone should give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: So fun and addictive. A really unique take on an RTS. My only criticism is that there isn't more of it! The campaign is pretty short (<10 hours), New Game + is pretty much the same campaign, and Creative Mode honestly removes a lot of what makes the game interesting (food/water/coal management, specifically).
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Played through it in about 7 hours, and I don't think there's too much replay value. I could maybe spend another 10 hours to complete the achievements. I would rate it "meh" if Steam had that option, but I'm giving it a thumbs up because it's an indie game and could expand to something more interesting (more tech tree, combat, puzzles). I wouldn't spend more than $10 on it.It's an interesting game, not too hard, not too complicated. It's a city builder, where the city flies around to gather resources and to complete a few "go here and spend resources" quests. It got a little boring by the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: The core premise of being a moving, coal-chugging, resource-devouring and weight-balancing city is cute, simple and well executed. I spent 6 hours finishing the main campaign, after which there is a new game+ and a hardmode, but I felt like I had seen what the game had to offer at that point. Gave me slight Homeworld vibes.I feel like the game could have expanded on the core premise more, and it does feel VERY indie although polished, but it is a small team and I assume they ran out of money to beef up the game more.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Airborne Kingdoms is easily the coziest "colony sim" base builder I've ever played. The runs take a reasonable amount of time, and the gameplay, while a bit repetitive, doesn't get stale. I'd recommend playing your first game through on Hard, because the challenge keeps things engaging, and it may be a game you only play through once or twice.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Airborn Kingdom is one of those cozy, chill city builders that are not disturbed by meaningless combat or fights. The freedom of traveling around with your city instead of spreading from one area to another like a locust swarm is comforting - and 100% in line with the storyline. Resource management is rather easy, too, and grouind resources will regrow over time.This of course also means, that if you are looking for a more hardcore city builder with a lot of micro management and great strife - this one is not for you. But if you are looking for something chill you can come back to from time to time, Airborn Kingdom will not disappoint.My personal down sides are the very fast playthrough, as the game barely needs more then 5-6hours to play through the story. Also the music (basically 1 song playing on loop) gets really bland, and the unlockable colour patterns for your city are not really eyecatchers. But those are minor details
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Airborne Kingdom is one of the most charming and artistically distinctive city-builders I’ve played in a long time, even if its gameplay and campaign are a little slight. This would be a great jumping-on point for players new to the genre, but even as a veteran I found the art to be gorgeous enough to sustain my goodwill for its eight hours or so.Equal parts Studio Ghibli, Orientalist fantasy and Game of Thrones tilt-shift toybox, Airborne Kingdom sees your floating hamlet range over a landscape of faded grandeur, restoring trade to scattered land-bound cities and eventually bringing them into your alliance. Along the way, you must amass your own resources, please your growing population and rediscover ancient technologies. Aside from a few barely-noticeable wrinkles such as managing lift and tilt, this is a watered-down version of city-builder classics like Caesar, with straightforward quests keeping you occupied as your workers scoop up resources and beaver away on the simple tech tree.Where Airborne Kingdom stuns is the beauty and attention to detail with which its steampunk fantasy is realised. From the Moorish tiling of its stylised landscape to glimmering lights of your workers’ planes, setting off for a shadowy oasis as dawn begins to break, a host of thoughtful details add up to an absolute triumph of visual design. My only quibbles are that later levels tend to be gloomier and more fog-ridden than the beginning desert world, lending an unwelcome ominous note to the unbridled joy of the game’s first half, while the sky – in particular, the clouds – could have been more gloriously Ghibli. The soundtrack, too, is an uplifting instrumental homage to the game’s Orientalist fantasy, that would have benefitted only from longer periods of windswept silence between its tracks. The fiction feels undercooked, however, with perfunctory text descriptions left to do a lot of heavy lifting, and a total lack of conflict or human drama.In short, Airborne Kingdom is a confident and accomplished debut by its small team of creators, with more than enough visual flair and sheer charisma to make up for its simple gameplay. Those who enjoy this particular brand of stylised city-builder will likely appreciate Frostpunk’s grimdark, meatier campaign, while those who enjoyed roaming this otherworldly landscape and managing scarce resources may want to check out the much more involved and accomplished fiction of Sunless Sea.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game is such delightful and calming.The game is easy to understand, has a nice drawn graphic art and can take some time to finish.You can also just enjoy building in creative mode, if you like.The story is also nice with its story and intel pop ups when traveling or clicking on tiny buildings in the horizon.If that sounds good for you, buy it and explore the games world!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it;  The city building aspect is a bit... shallow in my opinion.  There's more challenging out there for sure. But i really enjoyed how they combined this airship exploring to the end of the world universe.  It's not super detailed- but it has this real charm to it that feels really nice to find a new area and explore something you haven't seen.   worth the 20$ I paid for it.  It was relaxing not too over the top... screwed up a few times but it didn't end my game (nice... after being obsessed with rougelike genre stuff).  you'll like it.  definately has some moments that are a bit frost punk.  but frost punk is awesome..  so it was kinda nice to notice that too
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended. This game is a short but sweet experience with a neat premise. At least if you like city builders/management sims. It's also quite forgiving, since your airborne city can always rely on harvesting the resources it needs from the ground to make up for deficits in a pinch. You'll find it hard to take breaks from this game as you travel around, complete quests, unlock new buildings and expand your castle in the sky! The game isn't that deep mechanically, but thanks to its short length it really doesn't overstay its welcome.To really enjoy it, make sure to put some effort into the layout of your city right from the start. All buildings can be repositioned instantly, for free with the basic ones, so you can experiment around. Once you find a layout you like, watch in satisfaction as it soars majestically through the clouds. You also get to pick a color palette for your city which just makes the city building even more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Airborne Kingdom is a game i highly recommend for anyone who's in search for a relaxed and smooth gameplay within the City building genre.For the game gives you an experience, where you'll be flying around with your very own fantasy kingdom. Helping folks left and right. (In order to prove your self that YOU are the prophesied Airborne Kingdom.) Whilst keeping your very own people fed, sheltered and happy! To also mention that you'll be taking up innovations and allies in exchange for a thing or two. ALL this while you build up your own KINGDOM from a humble beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: nice relaxed game play, i like how you can continue on after you finish the story but would have been better to open up more map with distant lands and new tech buildings ect.  currently have a 350 pop with a city that dose not have to harvest from the ground trying to max out build area and pop limits on materials given from the ground but again would have been better if there was more land to explore maybe make 1000 kingdoms haha  throw in some portals and gate ways ....
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: You know when someone did a piece of art with love. This is that case.It's just enough of a challenge to keep your attention on multiple things at once, as well as giving windows of opportunity to just enjoy the design and floating serenity of your city and the sky voyage.I quite recommend it for those who want a piece of escapist fantasy, since the narrative doesn't have an antagonist and the world is a combination of three lands with 12 peaceful kingdoms. After finishing the story (assuming you gathered all three 3/3 pieces for three wonders), you can do a game+ (or sandbox) with a different city heart that gives bonuses, which is neat and I liked it.Particular attention needs be paid to music. The world is inspired by 1001 Arabian Nights with a dash of steam and clockwork, and the music wonderfully embraces this sun-soaked journey with playful and delightful movements.This is a game that doesn't want much from you, but offers a certain form of escapist therapy, therefore I give it as much love as I want to and I'm happy with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I will warn you that this is a short game as of now. It is a beautiful game with nice game play elements. It needs more to do and to add some more value to the story as it is relatively short. The music is nice and the graphics give it a great casual feel. I highly recommend it if you enjoy city builders, but do be aware it is painfully short.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I've always liked the idea of a unique city builder, but this game takes it to another level for me. I really like how you have to think ahead with your resources, because they won't all be available at all times. The characterization of each major city and even some settlements is surprisingly good for the genre, although some of their quests get a bit lazier as the game goes on. The art, however, is amazing. I love the style. If the game is on sale, and you like this genre, I'd say buy it immediately, not to say it isn't worth its normal price if you really enjoy these kinds of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A short and relaxing game. It's a nice resource-management game, not too challenging even on hard mode. Plenty of scope for creativity when building the sky-city - it's completely customisable which is a big part of the appeal for me. I like that it has a quest and end-goal, but also a purely creative mode if you just want to build a flying city.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Really beautiful and calm game. There are no enemies to fight here and I love it. It can be challenging at times, but for me I was looking for a bit more of a challenge. Maybe in Airborne Kingdom 2 we will find shifting winds and weathers?  I would love that. I got all done in 22 hours. Haven't tried creative mode yet. That I will start someday when I feel the need to take on to the skies again. There is some replay value here still, even after two finished runs. And even though all is done, I'm pretty sure I will return to this game time and time again. Haven't seen a game with this much calm atmosphere that is so well done and stands out from the rest, not since Settlers 2!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: a fun game, just minor flaws,- few days ago found upper bar info sometimes not updating (30 april), in my case (water or lift value)- just realized this on last tapestry area, managing citizen are bit more difficult (4+2 aspects) than resources.- it would be nice, if could navigate via map or disable building
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Controls are a little counter-intuitive... but the graphics an game-play are really unique and fun and in a mine-craft sort of way, very beautiful. The research pages layout could be improved and the page switching... research to build pages etc are a bit cluttered, but again, it didn't detract from the fourteen hours I played off the bat... love this game...
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Now, I've only gotten started with this one. . .but it has been delightfully surprising and entertaining. The story is neat and there isn't some rush to the end feeling with the game, which is nice for once. The graphics are decent for the type of game. The music is excellent. To be honest I was surprised this was listed as an alpha after playing it. Props to the devs of this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A few bugs left but an overall enjoyable experience. I recommend it.Could do with a few improvements:- Allow to disable/turn off building so that workers inside can be relocated elsewhere. (instead of having to delete buildings and recreate them when you need them)- Mark special site that you have seen differently from the ones seen and visited, specially if you can get dye from some of them but only once you get to a certain points, hard to remember which site you visited and which you still have to visit.- The research that improve the possible max speed of the ship-town is bugged. both updated lower my max speed instead of keeping it at current level or improving it. (going from 44% to 40% with the second one as an example without having change anything to the configuration of the town)
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: While this game misses two things: ability to set a movement goal on the map and endgame content, everything is pretty much perfect. The soundtrack I keep hearing in my head, crisp, easy to use interface inherited from the Frostpunk, unique mechanics of tilt and air travel with the whole city, incredible Arabic/fantasy aesthetic that feels refreshing and yet not merely exotic, but rich and on point - all of it just kept me playing all in one go.Of course, I finished the game in about 10 hours as a result (9.2 as of this review and just about 5 places to visit for 100% completion), so it feels a bit small, but the lack of endgame content is the problem of the whole non-violent survival citybuilder in general, so it isn't as much of a flaw as solving it would be an actual breakthrough for the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A city builder, exploration, and resource management game where you travel around the map as a floating city, trying to restore a floating city of legend that helped and advised the different kingdoms of the world. You have to manage different resources to make sure your populace is happy and to build new upgrades and fulfill quest goals, and build such that your city doesn't become too severely tilted while keeping it aloft and moving at a decent speed. It's chill and enjoyable. I liked the music, I thought the premise was interesting, and the gameplay was fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: after now 12 hours of non-rushed gameplay (i took a lot of time to explore!) i finished the main story and HOLY COW i loved every bit of it. this game is VERY lightweight (~1gb only) and the graphics quality is not on par with triple a titles, but the game still manages to create a very epic and dynamic atmosphere that captured me from the first moment on. the amazing soundtrack by paul aubry contributes to this a lot. building your kingdom, researching new building types, finding other realms and completing quests for them while constantly keeping track of your resources, citizen satisfaction levels and the degree of tilt on your flying city is an amazing challenge that kept me hooked through the entire experience. i cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Airborne Kingdom is a relaxed pace city builder, where the twist is you are flying your city around, re-uniting a fallen ancient civilization.  The game play is intuitive and not terribly difficult, even on hard mode.  In general there is no particular sense of urgency as you work through slowly growing your city, and it makes for a very good relaxing game to play to unwind at the end of the day.  The only critique I would have is that the game runs out of content - I still want to play more, but there really isn't anything further to do yet.  It's absolutely worth it for the content that is there, I just want more.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: novel idea, cool gameplay, nice music, adventure and exploration, excellent price to buy the gameCons: resources do not replenish unless fully depleted, workers will pick up more resources that you can store (wasted resources), you can't disable building productionIn conclusion: Airborne Kingdom is fun game that needs a lot of polishing. There are occasional hiccups, but if can look past that, you found a cool game.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: the game is great and beautiful when it works but when it doesn't it is a graphical mess. I had little to no problems early game but after 12 hrs of game play is became very laggy and it even broke the graphics after loading into the game again. i tried resetting my graphics driver, redownloading the game and even deleted my save but the graphics are still broke. I was soo close to the end of the game and now i cant even play it because all i can see in my game is the UI and the rest of the screen is black. Please fix this
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a dream of recapturing a golden age, not just technologically, but in spirit. Beautiful and chilled, yet not boring. Absolutely amazing experience, despite the short play time. I suggest playing on hard from the start as the other difficulty felt like a story mode. I do hope that they add more varied flavour text to colour in the world further. It seems like the easiest way to add to an already great experience. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful take on the standard city builder game, it makes resource management easier than most. The quests are a nice addition, and playing into a story is a nice change. The artwork is gorgeous, having a bit of an Islamic flair, the environment and designs a refreshing change from the medieval European standard. The game is not really re-playable once the main story has been fulfilled, which is unfortunate. There are large empty areas on the map, so hopefully the game designers will add DLCs. That aside, I highly recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty enjoyable little city builder. It's certainly got a unique theme and a fun gimmick- I mean, how many city builders have you played where you can fly your city around the map? Having to manage lift and literally balance your city's tilt is also pretty interesting, and the game's middle-eastern aesthetic is also uncommon and appreciated.It's not particularly deep or challenging, but it was still fun and I would recommend it. Playtime is indicative of 1 relatively thorough playthrough trying to find all the secret wonder/monument type structures.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous, sweet, and meditative townbuilder with a postapocalyptic medieval Islamic steampunk twist. Unlike most postapoc games—many, many postapocalyptic games—the focus here is on rebuilding and reconnecting in the wake of some unknown societal collapse. You'll build bridges, repair elevators, clear fouled reservoirs, and reestablish trade and intellectual networks. Plus it's blessedly short; you can complete a thorough initial game in under 20 hours. Succeeds wildly at its own goals; highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I find this game to be different from other survival city builders because of the location and the ability for your whole civilization to travel and expand, however, while I explore and ally with other kingdoms I find I am constantly trying to juggle abilities and discover what do I do next. I need time to research all the options given to me thoroughly and the impact each ability or option has on the whole, which is most important to concentrate on but I am so busy trying to keep my inhabitants alive and my city afloat. It is a nice challenging game. I would like to be able to take my time with each item, research everything fully but I do like to explore
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Not exactly a game changer in city building in terms of mechanics or depth but really a nice game that has most of the things you may want to see in such game. Its deep enough, yet if you wish you can do a very simple run without delving too deep into intricacies. A good and beautiful game to spend some time on
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Not really a city builder - feels more like Homeworld or FTL. The replayability is not great and getting 100% achievements took me just 14h. Good game if you just want to chill out a bit and do a few fetch quests with your flying city.If you liked this one you might want to check out "Sable" and "Merchant of the Skies".
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game in 11 hours. There is another game mode unlocked after completing the first run of the game. I didn't start it yet, so all the following is in regards to the "base game".It is a nice casual game, exactly what I needed this week. The most enjoyable part is the exploration and I think the team did a great job in making a world you want to see more of.The music, art and mechanics are great. The story is wonderful and I really liked how the flavor text gave a unique personality to each Kingdom.I only have two minor issues with the game. One is a coloring choice in the map. Both the starting area and high lands were differentiated in the map by differently colored land masses. However, in the shallow land the map shows this pale green in the water, which made me think that part of the game wasn't finished or something.Also, in the high lands I had prompts about how people I recruited heard rumors of the land and of how it worked. I was looking forward to that when going to the shallow lands, but didn't see any.I saw reviews saying it is boring, but I didn't find it so. The beginning of the game might be, since you have all the resources you need close. But, then you move to other areas, which are more challenging. The quests themselves are repetitive, since there are only two types. But I didn't mind that, since the focus is on exploration.Overall, a very nice and relaxing game, chill atmosphere, beautiful design and art.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely lovely game! This is exactly what I want a city building game to be 😊 Relaxing but fun, visually pleasing, beautiful soundtrack, satisfying resource management and research tree. A friend recommended this one and I couldn't be happier with the purchase. The team behind this game can be proud of what they made 😁
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty nice game, feels good to play a game where there's no war or fighting. Goes to show how much we can achieve if all we do is help each other. However, even though I didn't find anything to complain about, I don't see myself playing this game again after beating the main story, which took me about 8h.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed my play through. I know some folks are looking for more difficulty which is understandable however, i found it relaxing and can always appreciate a decent story while building up my city. looking forward to another same style game. Can definitely say its a different take to most settlement building games considering they take a minimalist approach on the physics behind keeping a air born full fledged city in the sky, yet fun nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: At best this is an amusing game, I would struggle to give it higher praise. Most of my hours were spent min/maxing my city, making it self sufficient while accepting every migrant, because I'm brain broken and enjoy tedium. For me this game lacked any real difficulty. I quickly quit normal and went to hard difficulty. There needs to be at least four more difficulty levels, as it stand you basically have story mode and casual.All the work was done on the appearance. Meaning that the gameplay is lackluster. Go here, do this, you are hero, type of stuff. The difficulty never ramps up and the last mission is exactly the same as the first, as is everything in between. Send two workers, build sky port, win. Would have been nice to see the missions further in the game require more resources, more workers, maybe have two fetch quests in a kingdom rather than one per.My other gripe is that wings and oars are clearly superior to the other choices (balloon and wing are perfectly equal), rendering choice unnecessary, there is no design trade off. You can tell that they tried to have design trade offs, but unfortunately didn't balance anything very well. Playing on hard, having nearly 200 population at the end, with no farms or condensers, one of each of the fabrication buildings, and a ship speed of 10%, I still never came close to running out of resources or being unable to satisfy my population. Coal is the only resource that can get sketchy and that's because it's artificially difficult due to coal storage being the only finite aspect of this game. Good thing that the most effective lift/propulsion structures use only a single worker and do not take coal. Why can't we grow trees in the kingdom for lumber to make charcoal? Why are coal burning structures less efficient than a single persons labor? That's not how things work in the real world.I'm glad that I bought it, and it was fun. I do recommend it. Just unfortunate to see so much wasted potential coming down to balance, or lack there-of.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing yet simple game wherein you balance your cities needs with exploration of the world around you. My only main criticisms are that you can quickly trivialise resource gathering and management by having a large population, which is not hard to get. Other criticism is simply that it's too short, all achievements can be gotten in two playthroughs (One base difficulty, one NG+ run on hard) and there's no real reason to keep playing beyond that.Beyond those criticisms the game plays incredibly well. Feedback from the game is good and you can quickly work out what you need to do and what has gone wrong when things become problems. It's very quick to just pick up and play through a 6 hour game and you can really lose yourself in the moment to moment gameplay of fulfilling needs and seeking resources and objective completion.Minimal skill floor to play though the skill floor and skill ceiling are really only an inch or so apart in truth. An incredible game to reccommend to people who don't play a lot of games or wish for an easier game in the genre to sink their teeth into.It's an amazing start, and I look forward to seeing what the studio does with the game if anything. I quietly hope for expansions and updates that will allow for expansion of this idea, as it has a great amount of potential!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. If you're into city builders, this game is up your alley. My only gripe is that it is a story line game, so you'll really get one playthrough of it. That said, I personally enjoy starting over to design, and redesign my build, so I know I'll play it a few more times to complete all the achievements, optimize my ship and play through the New Game+ that makes it a more open world.I am content paying $28.99CAD for this game because I am the type of person that will get my money's worth out of the time I will spend starting over and rebuilding. However, that is a lot of money for a game you can beat in ~6 hours, so if you do not think you'd replay the story to start from scratch and rebuild, I do not recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A city building stategy combined with exploration. Which is possible, because the city in question is flying.Visually the game takes inspiration from One Thousand and One Arabian Nights (the city itself, the ornaments on the landscape) and Studio Ghibli films (various land kingdoms). It has a very unique and cute style. The arabian inspiration is also apparant in the bacground music.There are three distinct areas - a desert, highlands and a shallow sea with distinct look and resource distribution. This affects the building strategy and planning of the city's route. The objective is to maintain a working and growing city, explore and recover lost technology and reconnect with local kingdoms. This is usually achieved by fullfilling a simple quest. Apart from material needs of citizens and some services, there is also a need to maintain town's lift, propulsion and balance. The existing buildings can be easily moved for rebalancing. Despite complex systems, the game is not punishing (at least on normal difficulty) or overcomplicated. Failing the game would probably require a concerted effort.This is a short, completely non-violent and positive game. Excellent for stress relief.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: a somewhat simple and short city builder-ish game. not very complex . therearen't a lot of mechanics to struggle with. so expect a laid back experience with somerelaxing music.didn't bother playing the + mode , after going through the story in normal.for its cost , well worth the experience. but maybe not for gamer's that likedifficult and complex city builders.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Good city builder/planner that can punish mistakes but is also lenient. Very relaxing to play and you definitely lose track of time playing it. The main critique I have is the campaign/story game time. You can easily beat the game under 10 hours and anything more than that is a bit of a stretch, even with trying to explore and perfecting the base. Other minor issues I have was the music, character animations, and some limitations. I love the music but I wish there was different music for the other zones as you transitioned into them. The character animations are a bit lazy. It's repeating animations of the guy standing still waving his hands around etc. I would rather the characters go into the building and lights go on at night or something rather than that. Lastly, only some buildings can be paused and I didn't see a way to stop manufacturing to free up people to do other work. Rather, I have to deconstruct buildings which I would rather leave up to keep organized. Similarly, if I stop moving forward I wish the people would pause to work on other tasks, even if that meant you couldn't move forward until those positions are freed up again. That's about it, the game was a lot of fun and worth the purchase if you like city building or just a relaxing game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR;- Citybuilding: A- Resource management: B+- Questing: COverall: Excellent relaxing vibe, focusing creativity in a nonhostile world, but lacking a little challenge and replayability.I would like to commend the devs for the inspiration and recognise *I enjoyed this game* which is the most important part.Pick it up and try it!!!The city building here is amazing. The moment it came together for me was when i discovered they had correctly implemented torque, meaning i had a few spots for my heavy lifting and 2 fans id move up/down left/right to correct my balance.The building tree doesnt have a lot of depth but thats honestly not a bad thing, as you will be finding the right balance of the buildings you have to fulfill the various needs without overcomplicatedness.However, it lacks a lot of planning tools which can make modification not straining but a process never the less.The resource management is hit-and-miss. My favourite moment is when i had too many people consuming food/water, but no *extra* people to build farms / water-condensers and had to sprint around crazylike draining lakes and shrubbery to survive long enough to recruit people to automate those needs hahahaHowever, after a short period of play you find your stability and automation and then... You just stockpile. It would be nice if there was a reason to have to many resources, something you can sink it into.Questing was... ehh. At the point of writing this everything is really variations on a delivery quest (which thematically fits but does get a little tedious when you realise thats all the quests).Suggestions to the developers / context for lack of replayability:PLEASE NOTE: I do recognise this game is like 10 days old and its FANTASTIC for that!!!Never the lessCity Building:- Straight up, let me build/move to planned path tiles.Resource Management:- Idle buildings will idle peeps. Factories not running or propulsion buildings when at a halt freeing up thier peeps would actually be an awesome feature. It would allow a little depth in the planning as you could become a light-weight city balancing speed and gathering, or a monolith of industry stopping at a location and spamming all the planes.- Pay-To-Win towns, letting me provide wood or water to the farming city to improve thier crop turnout, or metal to the coal cities to make more coal available.- Questing variation:-- If there was a conflict in the game i feel like this would be a great place for it. Making difficult choices like do i take the artefact from X for the kingdom of Y (hurting X relations and improving Ys) or scour the lands for a blueprint to make my very own for a high cost (improving X and Y for $$$).-- Mixing it up with mini quests, settlements that wont provide peeps until they get assistance with resources or transportation.-- Long-duration quests like leaving peeps to repair the bridge / collapsed temple but theyll be there for a week and need to be picked up to be recovered.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Airborne Kingdom is a really pretty game with a different take on the classic RTS/builder genre and a fabulous OST. In addition to all the usual plate-spinning for survival and growth needs, we take on the challenges of lift, propulsion and tilt. In addition, we actually get some lore and quests, which are quite rare in the genre. As a completely new player to the game as well as dealing with the additional challenges of flight, I had about 30 hours in before the credits rolled. The only thing that was a disappointment is that the credits rolled before I actually completed every task. I would not expect to have success without completing everything, so color me surprised and a little confused.Fortunately, I can reroll in Hardmode and do it all over again! Since every map is random and procedurally generated, it will be a new reroll on a new map with greater difficulty.Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I just have to say, this is a wonderful game and I have enjoyed all 22.8 hours of my first playthrough. Nice epilogue as well. 💖Took a nice slow approach, trying to stay low on resource demands and spending long stops sipping on nearby oasis and thickets while researching techs, and moved toward self-sufficiency as alliances and techs allowed it. Relaxing and low-stress while also engaging.New Game+ looks like it opens up a just interesting new approaches and challenges as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A decent survival game with an interesting story and unique gameplay. My only gripe is that it was over too soon. Some minor stability issues with some crashes, so save often. The base gameplay is solid, so there is a good deal of potential here for a randomly generated, infinite map, perhaps with multiplayer. That addition would make this infinitely replayable.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: AK is a good enough game, but overpriced. I got a good 12 hours of enjoyment out of it, but it lacks replayability. The story is pretty bland, and there is really not so much creativity involved in managing your kingdom.The idea of being afloat and having to deal with tilt and lift as you build your city is refreshing and fun, but there's a lack of variety in what you can do with each building.Get it when it's cheaper, and don't expect it to rock your socks.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Airborne Kingdom has an interesting new touch to the city building aspect. Not just that the city is flying, no you also have to keep the city in literal balance. That combined with the importance of satisfying your people to get literally anything done is unique enough to give this game a chance and I finished it in one 6.5h session.The game is generally neat. Nothing that blows your mind, but a relaxing mix between building your city and exploring the world. For the completionists, you can achieve a city state where everyone is happy and you are generating a plus on all important resources. And for the beauty builders, there is a Creative Mode.The story is indeed relatively short, but you can continue playing beyond that point. In the days of 60+ hours action games, this game is like a short rest on the bonfire. Rest as long as you want and when you decide to come back, there is always a New Game+ for you to explore.Possible improvements would be to add more areas to explore, so there is simply more of the game. Then I found the research too slow, when I already had 5 research buildings, or the research buildings too demanding on population. Another would be to make moving buildings easier, since now I have to click every building and press "move" and only then I'm able to say where I want to place it. This is especially annoying when moving multi-story buildings, where you have to repeat this process for every story of a building. I suggest a "move mode" where one click picks up a building/story and holding for 1 second picks up all stories at once and the mode doesn't turn off after every move.Overall, can recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. was a breath of fresh air for a "new to me" Genre. was captivating and very interesting to say the least. Based on the time and energy put into the actual story and gameplay, im 100% fine with the lackluster graphics. Very short game though, i beat it on normal mode in around 10 hours, including my first city drop because i was getting use to monitoring resources and making my city self sufficient (minus trees). Cant wait to see what comes of this, dont give up on it, for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing city builder/exploration game with some resource management and some novel balance, speed and lift investment considerations. The world is great to look at and explore at first, but story is pretty light with some minor worldbuilding through ingame blurbs set around simple fetch, find and timer quests and a somewhat repetitive map. Great concept, fun to play, but I think there's a lot of unrealized potential in this currently somewhat overly simplified city builder.The good:- Excellent artstyle- Enjoyable research tree with useful upgrades and variations- Good building variety to balance resource burn and research time sink vs varying QoL boosts- Sizable map to explore with a few interesting environmentsThe meh:- Little reason to ever optimize/redesign cities- Too many samey resource types- Resource management comes down to: top up every bar at every opportunity- Repetitive quests and map locations (towns/ruins)- Light on story beyond pre-game voice overThe bad:- Technically unoptimized- Artstyle sometimes hinders UI legibilitySome more building interactions, more meaningful resource management decision-making and more unique locations and quests could lift this game up from quirky little ambient experience to a solid indie city building masterpiece. For now though, it still feels a little early-access.Certainly recommended even in current state if you're looking for a chill city builder-lite experience of 6-8 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightful and fun little game, I highly recommend grabbing it on sale - I completed the game and all non-grind achievements in about 6 hours.* The city building aspect is fairly standard, though flying adds a very interesting dimension, managing your weight capacity and tilt ends up being trickier than one might imagine.  * The resource pressure is also excellent, you have to pretty careful about how much time you spend gathering vs travelling.* The structures themselves are pretty fun, especially as you get more lift and propulsion options.* The research and happiness mechanics are kind of a mess.  As you progress, your citizens will have greater desires, but learning how to fill those desires requires finding and trading with the ground kingdoms and if you do them in the wrong order, you can end up in a state where your people are unhappy and leave your city, making it next to impossible to build the buildings required to make them happy enough to stay!* Research takes a LONG time.  That's generally fine as time is your primary resource (you never really get 100% self-sufficient, even into the late endgame so you're always hemorrhaging resource).  The problem is that even after finishing the game, I have literal hours left of sitting around with nothing to do but wait for research to complete.tl;dr: Fun game, has some issues, grab it on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Airborne Kingdom is a pretty simple resource management and "city builder". It took me about 8 hours to complete all the achievements, but I really enjoyed the game.It is highly relaxing, with a unique art style, theme, and story. You control the flying city and must ally with the 12 kingdoms to complete the prophecy.The game is not very complex, and is not punishing. This can make it feel easy, but there are some hurdles you must overcome to "win". Overall, I really enjoyed the relaxing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be very good. But its just medium. The main thing it lack is narrative choice en impact on the world. The quest are dumb and very easy. While the city building is naise and the idea of flying this city through a open-world sounds superb. There is very little to discover. If its would feel your actions or choises had impact on the world and the game had mutiple endigs it would be more engaging and replayability would go up a ton. Now i'm pretty much done with it after 6 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: 8-12 hours of quality game (depending on if you want to replay on hard for that achievement) play but then it's all over.Tips for new players:- Build double or triple roads (they're free except for weight) so you can later delete them and place lights and bushes.- You can get an upgrade to delete buildings and retrieve all materials so don't over think it too much.- Buy the schematics for wings otherwise you'll be working too hard to not run out of coal.- Prioritise lift but don't skimp propulsion, moving slow means a slow death.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: The design is of the games map is wonderful to look at, its has a beautiful charm as you move through the skies. Some of the most interesting city-building mechanics i've seen. Balancing tilt, lift & propulsion on top of your resources offers for some very interesting gameplay!Cons:The UI-design is very flat, monochrome and without contrast - so resources are not as easy to overview at a glance as they could be & the activities for the main & side quests are mostly fetch-quests. So the exploration aspect of the game gets a bit stale after some time - the most exiting part is being able to unlock new blueprints with structures to build for the city. Recommendable Experience overall!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Airborne Kingdom is a unique take on city sim, it combines city sim with some elements of survival, yet not as challenging as frostpunk, making it suitable for casual players as well. The aesthetics are pretty interesting, gameplay difficulty is increasing naturally as u progress through the game, from managing the resources in different territories, as well as the desires of the residents of your airborne kingdom. So far I'm pretty happy with how the game turns out, even though i have yet to complete it once yet.I have met with a small annoyance though, is it possible for the developers to make it so that we can allocate our staff in the buildings freely? Or disable buildings temporarily? When understaffed, there are buildings of low priority, i would like to disable them instead of destroying them.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This game's tough to review. It's a fun city-builder with a plot - surprisingly enouugh - that actually uses its movement mechanic relatively well, making you explore the game map for plot-related missions and resources. Visually, the art style is also pretty nice.There's a pretty big caveat, though, in that I don't really see too much replayablity in this game, and it's neither a especially hard nor a long game to finish. There aren't tons of ways to make interesting and unique city designs, so this game doesn't have legs in the same way a game like Cities Skylines does. Whether you should buy it or not really comes down to if you think the price is worth a pretty good, but short 8~10 hours experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Every once in a while you just come across that get its hook in you. I wasn't really looking for a game like this or have a long history with this style of game, but I absolutely enjoyed playing this game. I just finished my first playthrough and completed the story. I played more than at the time of the review as I was playing outside of steam first. I loved the level of micromanager it had and the literally balancing act you have to do to keep the city running. I loved that there is no combat but i did not feel safe. Overall I couldnt put this game down, as soon as i finished all i could think was how to play again but theme a different style of city. If you liked Frostpunk but didnt want to deal with the blizzard and you like SimCity but wish there was a bit more "risk" or function to city design,  you would probably enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Pretty simple gameplay, find a city, do a quest or two and they ally with you, the whole point is to ally with all 12 cities. Casual and peaceful experience, at least until you notice your coal supplies are low because you were not paying attenion and you have to scramble to mine some before you fall out of the sky. Very cool to be a mobile city that can extract resources and turn them into materials for building, extract all the stuff in an area and fly off looking for more. All while making a bigger faster ship. While building the city is simple and easy you do have to be mindful of the tilt of your ship, balancing the weight as you grow. Other than that and the overall weight you can support you can make your ship however you want, making it look cool or a horrid mess like i did. The game can be beaten pretty quickly if you rush it, and at the moment with only one campagin it's not the most replayable game, but I'll probably play it a second time now that I know what I did wrong the first time. Game also looks very pretty and the music is good. If you like city builders or like steampunk themed games I'd recommend Airborne Kingdom.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just what I was looking for. Unlike many other city builder/colony sim games, there's an actual goal/story to it, which makes figuring out how to best build your city that much more fun. There's also a wonderful sense of adventure to the game. The campaign feels a little short. I've played four hours and I feel like I'm probably 3/5ths of the way through the game. The good news is that this game will probably be worth replaying at least once. At any rate, it's a fun and fresh feeling city builder with an interesting narrative, actual goals, and a healthy dose of exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely steampunk art style, lovely music, solid yet simple game play, almost no bugs.It's not the greatest game, but it is solid, and reasonably fun.  I like the artstyle and music quite a bit.The mechanics of the game itself are pretty simple, but simple can be good.  The lack of bugs is pretty surprising in this day of buggy game releases.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Its a decent, chill city builder with a unique twist and challenges, but i found that it snowballs WAY too quickly, to the point i was able to complete the game 3 times on Hard in just 13 hours. Also on a personal note, i think this concept would also go great in a conflict and war type of scenario, using your airborne kingdom as your mobile base of operations (Food for thought, devs??), though that might step it into  'Homeworld' territory.Either way, would recommend to anyone that wants a chill builder game, but dont have too high expectations of something that will keep you occupied for weeks on end.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: The game is short. It can be completed in a day, even if you take your time. But what it lacks in campaign scope it more than makes up for in its execution. It has a great visual feel supported by chill audio and game play. The addition of balancing your floating city is a fun way to spin what would otherwise be a straight forward city builder. I'm looking forward to what might be next for this studio.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, with interesting mechanics, resource management and fantastic art with an attention to detail. It definitely has it's issues with game stability, but it is worth the headache in my option. The story, thought basic, is interesting and compelling enough that the open ended conclusion makes me hope for a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun city-builder except that your city travels around completing quests. It's a very fun concept, as others have said, your foe is gravity and balance. The devs did an excellent job limiting your ability to be self-sufficient which forces you to be on the lookout for resources you can extract to keep your floating city moving. If I could recommend a DLC it would be a steampunk version with... guns! Yes, combat! But I realize the devs intentionally avoided combat and that is fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely little treat. Is a settlement sim? An exploration game? An RPG? Sure! Come for the soothingly beautiful visuals and soundtrack; stay for the simple-yet-satisfying strategic gameplay; fall under the charm of the surprising amount of narrative woven throughout. Not a long game, and not necessarily one I'll play through again at this stage, but definitely a novel experience well worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game if you (like me) don't like to fight wars but still want some challenge. The hardest part of the game is to keep up with the demand for housing while keeping the balance of the city and finding diamonds to buy the blueprints.  It's great fun to explore the land and finding all the lost cities.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very chill little city builder, that counters it's lack of replayability by forcing you to not only expand but expand wisely less your city tip over. By the end of the game I had gotten the hang of it and wanted to continue to expand, which you can indefinitely as long as your computer can handle it. At some point there was nothing more to research and no point going further. You can make yourself self sufficient but only to a certain degree, you can get enough income of trees in to allow yourself to convert it to fuel but it's limited, and adding more buildings that take up that fuel puts you in a position where you have to go collect it yourself again. That's the point that threw me off and pushed me to finish the game.All in all I put about 10+ hours into this little gem, and I would recommend it to anyone who needs a break from other more stressful city builders. The music is calming and beautiful and kept me relaxed even at the one point I decided to wreck my residential district to rebuild it and most of my citizens got pissed and abandoned ship.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: This game will probably only last you a few play sessions. It's cute, okay? It looks nice and begins with a solid premise. It doesn't waste a lot of time on the pretense that is the story, and that's fine. Albeit I have not "beaten" the game, but in less than 4 hours I seem to have annihilated the economic aspect entirely, and on the hardest difficulty. Already there is no more concern about running out of anything. I have researched most of the games technology (certainly all the important ones) and the only thing left to do is continue devouring the regenerating fields, grazing over the land with my sky castle swallowing forests like bits of grain and... stop to pick up villagers 3 at a time at settlements until i hit pop cap. Sure there are a few more fetch quests to do, and some alternative means of doing what I already do very well (generate lift and propulsion) but there's no real incentive to grow larger and the game never transitions into much beyond what you discover quite quickly. If you are reasonably decent at sim management games, you will tear through this fairly light snack of a game. It's tasty, mind you, just maybe not too filling.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps you need to think twice if you are buying this to enjoy the landscape.Yes, they tried their best to input some element in the game. But the game obviously has some limitation. Still, I would like to give them a recommended rate since this let you enjoy somewhat freedom.Lagging on GTX 1660 super 6G gives me some question. Then it has no reason to run the client on this Minecraft like texture. The price well reflected about the concern of this frame rate issue.You better know your expectation before buying this game. The game play is interesting but visual. This depends on your preference though. Airborne Kingdom Keep making me to compare Frostpunk. So...just say this is not my taste. The game play can be praised though.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim and I'm glad I did.  This is a really chill, whimsical game and building a floating city is a really cool take on the city building genre.  It's a very easy to play and understand game, and you will be balancing your citizen needs with the city needs--as in lift, propulsion, and your typical resource needs.  TLDR: Chill, calm game, and a cool take on a city builder.  If you like city builders you'll like this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game overall, a little short, completed the base game in about 7 hours, not 100% the run with special wonders but completed the main task and got the ending cut scene.Recommendations for the game:There is a harsh bottleneck/punishment to try and get things balanced and sustained. You get punished for growing your kingdom and hating you if you don't get all the desires from each kingdom region. It was a little annoying but you can power through with some stubborness. As a result human population becomes a massive bottleneck to do anything in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely short review:It´s relaxing, easy to get into and not that challenging. You basically build a city in the sky, have to manage resources, happiness and tilt angles in order for the city to stay horizontal, really not that hard.As always I recommend you to watch a video on Youtube and base your purchase on whether you like casual sim games.
_childDocuments_.name: Airborne Kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: My 5 ish hour opinions:Pros------Great aesthetics. Game has a cool concept with an excellent design, style and music.  Runs Well.
