_childDocuments_.review: This game is a decent walking simulator with some pretty well done environments, but the experience is greatly hampered by technical issues and a weak story.For glitches, every single time a loaded a save, my character got stuck. Fortunately, I looked online and there's a very easy solution. If you change your Head Bob setting it fixes it, but only for that one load. You'll need to toggle that setting every single time you load your game. This issue was reported years ago and never fixed, which is absurd. While annoying, at least there's an easy solution to getting stuck. There's no easy solution for how poorly optimized the game is.  For example, I was running at 60 fps and then an alarm with a flashing red light goes off. Just that one light flashing crashed the FPS from 60 to 17. My PC can run modern AAA games like Halo Infinite and Death Loop, so I know it can handle this indie game. You either need to put you graphics setting really low or deal with the game constantly going from 60 down into the twenties or teens. Very annoying.The tech issues could be forgivable if the story were better. It's not terrible and there are interesting elements, but it very much feels like they shoved a bunch of plot elements together without ever thinking through whether or not the plot makes sense. I also wish they had focused less on the boy's personal story and more on the alternative history setting. I think the setting was the most interesting part. *Minor spoilers regarding plot*Examples of issues with the plot:Why did the Germans blow up everything on the surface (including their own country) with tactical nukes rather than just putting the nukes on their V2 rockets and then nuking enemy cities until they surrendered? One document seems to imply they lacked a long range nuke delivery system, but you expect me to believe that the Germans developed all that advanced computing and bunker tech, but they couldn't get a few hundred more miles out of their V2s? Relative to the other tech they had, even ICBMs aren't that high tech and, since it seems that the USA remained neutral in this universe, they would really only need to hit Britain from France (they could already hit London with V2s in our timeline, they just didn't have nukes) and the big cities in the western USSR. Much easier than building crazy bunkers and super computers. It very much feels like the person who made this game just wanted an excuse to make a Nazi bunker game and then molded the setting/plot in illogical ways to get to that predetermined destination.In the same vein, they never adequately explain how the Poles, with no super sci-fi tech manage to take over the German bunker and in only like 3 years. It seems to imply that maybe the super computer assisted them, but it seems they got very deep into the facility before they got to the first terminal. How did they initially get in? Why weren't they blown up by the nukes? How did they find the bunker?The documents from the Polish fighters say that the war is still going on the surface, but the German documents seem to state pretty clearly that they are wiping everyone out, including their own people, so who is fighting who on the surface? Are there still active German armies? Are the Poles fighting the USSR? Nothing is made clear. I think the writer just wanted the Poles to overcome the Germans, but, like with the reason for the bunker being made, the writer didn't know how to do it, so they just never explained anything. It seems like the game was made by people with an interest in WWII, but without the kind of deep knowledge needed to make a convincing alternate history story, which is why many things don't make sense. Also, I think that's why the game sharply pivots away from the historical aspects about an hour into the game and then just focuses on the main character's personal issues. The MC's personal story is decent, but, considering how the game is framed on the store page, I was expecting a story that focused more on the alternate timeline.

Why would wood creak constantly while sounding like someone is walking above the player when there isn't anyone there?Why does the player character walk normally but the audio sounds like he's stomping in anger every step he takes?Interacting with anything is annyoingly specific, you have to be on top of the interaction to even start it.Levers, cabinet etc. Really didn't need extra interaction to be opened/moved.Why is there a run option if it really is just one unit faster than walking?Why are the calendars in English?Why are the globes in English and they're maps from 1700's?Why isn't the wood furnish in the MG42 asset made to match the statues they used the asset for too?Small details like these should be not looked over, especially in a walking simulator where a player probably pays more attention to the world around them. _childDocuments_.review: Such a dissapointment this game turned out to be.First it started off great with the concept. There are many ideas i really like implemented into the setting and parts of the story. The major downside is the awful voice acting. It felt like robots talking trying to mimic human reactions with the emotional capacity of a toster. Seriously, let people speak their native language. They should have talked in Polish and put subtitles. During the early part of the game it was difficult to differentiate whether it was the Germans writing/talking or the Polish resistance. Everything is in broken english for some reason.The Slavic symbolism is something I want to see more of in media. As I am of Slavic descent It always peaks my interest when I see anything related to old Slavic culture. Saddly it is not really explained here as I would have wished. It comes off as wanting to look cool and different since most of the players don't even have a clue about any of the symbols or the citation of Szymon at one point (He referenced the meaning of Kolovrat at one point).Graphics and sound design are serviceable. I mean, the game looks very nice but spacial audio design isn't done as well. Asside from the voice acting, everything is fine.Now the main problem - "Gameplay and optimization". First I was confused when I opened the options menu. For some reason the resolution changes managed to missalign the crosshair with the actual crosshair (mouse pointer). And when I managed to fix it the game just suddenly started without me pressing the New Game button... right from the options menu. So far so good? The controls are weird. You have a sort of running button but all it does is zoom the camera a little without providing any movement speed improvements. This shows just how much they playtested this and "fixed" bugs. Every time you load your save you can't move at all, so the workaround is to open the options menu, click accept and everything will be fine. The devs haven't fixed this one even though there are a lot of guides and discussions about it. And the glitch always happens. The way you interact with the environment is annoying. Just a simple click would be enough. Selecting dialogue shouldn't be done with the mouse scroll. Didn't realize it once and returned to a checkpoint just because i thought it was a glitch. And the final thing is that prompts dissapear. I pressed to open a door, the animation happened but the door remained closed and I couldn't progress further, had ro reload save.In the end I don't recommend this game. It is slow and for about half the time very boring cause of the slow walking speed and bad voice acting. The concepts are great but the delivery, lack of depth and poor gameplay filled with bugs and glitches makes this a net negative. The developers could have solved some minor things but not even that was done.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface, I've played some walking sims, Firewatch, What Remains of Edeth Finch, Dear Esther, Everybody's Gone to the Rapture, etc and generally I enjoy them. That isn't the case here though, this game is painfully slow, both in the story and the actual gameplay. "Sprint" is slower than most other games walking speed, it seems like the FOV zooms out a little to give the illusion of speed but your actual pace increases maybe 5 percent, and 5 percent of painfully slow is still slow. For the first hour you will think "whats the point of picking things up" as there is no lore, audio, nothing to find, nothing to really see at all. You can spin items halfway around, but if you think walking is slow you'll probably uninstall as soon as you start to rotate an object. I wanted to stop playing in the first half hour the next half hour I considered uninstalling, but finally the story started to pick up, but I haven't finished the game and honestly I don't know if I will. The story just is interesting enough and ill probably watch the rest of the game, but playing it is so painfully slow.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game, its basically an interactive movie or "walking simulator" as some people call it.  Its actually a really good story, somewhat predictable once you're 50% through but still worth it.  The beginning is definitely slow but it picks up.The world they built....wow.  The environments look amazing and the attention to detail is incredible.The only recommendation I would make to the developers are that sometimes the voice prompts are too quick.  Like you get into a new area or pick up something and the voice starts talking immediately, instantly telling you what it is.  For a game like this where its more about discovery, it would be much more suspenseful if the voice prompts started on a bit of a delay so the player can look around for a second and realize where they are before the voice prompt kicks in.Its a fun experience with no jump scares or anything scary and is about a 4 hour-long experience (if you look around and do everything you possibly can - less if you just run through it).Is it worth it? _childDocuments_.review: If you can get past the abysmal walking speed ‘Paradise Lost’ offers a graphically beautiful, atmospheric and detailed world to explore set in an alternate history timeline. The story is a linear slow burn and there are no puzzles or gameplay other than plenty of interactable objects and the occasional (not very) hidden area. _childDocuments_.review: It is a short game, we can call it a walking simulator. It is not an easily digestable game. There are hints of the Jewish holocaust here and there in the game, what is oppressive, but it does not contribute to the better understanding of the story. Because of this, I would not recommend it for children. You walk in an empty Nazi bunker deep under the mountains. checking old documents and objects, trying to find a man in a photo, supposedly your father. It has long and boring parts sometimes, but sometimes it has a tenseful atmosphere and quite creepy as you hear your own footsteps in the empty corridors and you don't know what is going to happen. Though I was confused by some elements of the story, alltogether I think it is wortwhile to have a go and play it, it is not an ordinary game, but an artistic and heartbreaking piece. A bit hard to digest. Though I did not play through all endings,  I think it desperately needs a second part to make the story more complete.Negative: If you want to get the secret achievements at the end, you need to go back BEFORE the final scene and restart the last chapter otherwise you have to start the whole game from the beginning. Check the solutions of the secret achievements on the Community page, before you start to play them!

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the premise of the game (even though the whole end of the world after WW2 trope  has been done quite a lot), and I enjoyed reading all of the notes left behind to tell more of a story. That said, I didn't like much else:- Everything. Is. So. Slow. Walking is slow. "Running" with shift makes you go 5% faster. Every climb, drop, and weird little shimmy is so slow. And the ladders. OH MY you better strap in. After two rungs, you gotta stop for 2 seconds to catch your breath.- Small gripe, but when looking at your shadows, your character model stands like he's so buff that he can't put his hands down by his sides. It's so awkward, and his arms barely moves when he walks.- I get that the main character is supposed to be 12 (judging at the very earliest by how tall everything is) but the sounds he makes outside of conversations are odd. I think the voice acting is fine, but whoever synced different sounds to different actions might need a talking to. Small hops are given super loud grunts and just WALKING causes your character to pant. Maybe from all the ladders.- INSIDE of convo, however, everyone seems to lack a lot of emotion. It's very monotone. The guy on the computer, though, is probably the best in terms of emotion.- There are a lot of interesting rooms that add to the environmental storytelling, but there's no other reason to explore. Nothing to collect, no dialogue about the world, no characters, nothing. It's detailed but empty at the same time. The only saving grace here are the notes.- The 'interact' little minigames are cool at first but VERY overdone. Every door you have to push forward, every drawer you have to pull back, every level to the side, etc. etc. It loses its charm very quickly.- On the topic of interacting, it takes a few seconds for your character to line up and actually begin interacting. Not a lot, but considering this happens 20-30 times per level if you read everything, it gets annoying. And accidentally hitting right-click means you gotta DO IT AGAIN.- I've gotten lost a few times because the path forward is either hidden or in a very dark corner. EVERYTHING is dark, and it's only made worse by how slow you walk. If you made a wrong turn or backtracked, that's easily 10 minutes of walking wasted.- The notes. They're pretty great, but you hold them super far away from the camera, and they're not even centered. I have to lean forward about 6 inches in front of my monitor to read some of the text.- If you quit midway through a level, have fun. Loading back in will lock you in place and you'll need to do it all again.- The distance you need to be from things to interact seems very inconsistent. Sometimes I can read a note from any angle, sometimes I need to be clipping into it and looking right at it. Same thing with doors, and accidentally right-clicking puts you far enough away that you'll need to reposition to interact again. Seems like a glitch to me, or at best infuriating design.- The story seems sound so far, but I'm honestly struggling to care about the main character. The only background about his family we have is him being a baby, being lied to by his mother, and then threatening to leave her, all within the first 4-ish minutes of gameplay. When its discussed later, I just couldn't care. There wasn't enough effort to make an emotional impact.- I have no clue why the levels are named the way they are. Stages of grief? They have nothing to do with the story. It's cliche and feels "I'm in 8th grade and this is deep" for lack of a better word. Same with the name of the game. I get that the place is named paradise, or whatever, but the comparisons to Milton's epic about the fall humanity are very vague if at all present.Otherwise, if you prefer slower walking simulators with "find out for yourself" stories, you'll like it. Otherwise, you probably won't like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: To me, this game defines what a walking simulator is all about. A great one feels like a good book that you take your time to contemplate and put yourself into the story. The slowness of the story allows you to do so. It is not for everyone because of this. Taking the time to look at everything helped me understand the story and people who had been there. The details are not designed to jump out at you, they are there to make you take the time to look for and think about and learn from.  I am older (58) and more patient and more willing to learn and grow and change than when I was younger. I was actually hoping it would spend more time in revealing more details of what happened. I understand sacrifice for others better now and don't think the ending is sappy or contrived. I have seen people live this kind of sacrifice in the real world on a day to day basis. Most people are too cynical today to believe there are real people just like this kid who really exist and would do what he did.From a technical perspective, some minor things. Video got choppy intermittently ( probably my pc). Took a bit to calibrate to get turns not too slow or fast. Had the issue with not being able to move at all  from auto save points, but easy fix in settings (head bob). No real show stopper issues though. Well done POlyAmorous team!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is nice, but it's more of a story than a game.  It's very straight forward.  From start until the last scene, you really don't have any choices.  The game guides you through it and the only real choices may be which path to take forward first, but it will lead you back to any other choices you may have had.  I've gotten 8 out of 12 achievements in the six hours I've played and I truly believe the other 4 may have been the only choices I could have made at the very end of the game.  Do I save my sister and let her live?  Do I stay on the island instead of leaving it?  I'm positive those are at least 2 of the achievements.  There was a ritual to perform, maybe if I didn't do the ritual, I would get a different achievement as well, but again, that was near the end of the game.  For 17 GB of data, there truly is very little interaction that would make the game yours and not just a story you are following.  The graphics are good, but a bit disappointing.  You can run across a lot of mirrors, but never see yourself in one.  In the main dining hall, you can open all the doors on your right, but if you go back to the main area and go to your left, you eventually get to the same area as you did on your right.  No special achievements for that, you just get to explore the whole area instead of only half of it.  This game probably could have been done in half the time I did it, but I wanted to explore as much as I could, just to see how many choices I had in the game.  It's a nice story, you don't die and are never in danger, but there is also not really any puzzles to solve, only interactions with computers and doors and buttons to push.  No thought really needed at all.  I believe this would be a good game for small children, but the story may be a bit too dark for them.  A few well placed puzzles that need to have a purpose to be completed and some choices to make this seem like a free wandering do it on your own experience would make this a much better game to play and promote.  As for the game itself, I had to play it over a couple of days.  The game saved, but when I returned, sometimes I was unable to move.  At that point, you need to go back to the main screen and restart the level, then you're able to play.  The left trigger allows you to walk faster, but you never really get to run.  Some of the points in the game need to real interaction to trigger to jump down or climb up, but sometimes it doesn't register, so you have to hit the button to jump down or climb up.  Mostly, the white dots were just a way for the game to tell me where it wanted me to go.  I read a lot of notes that actually did nothing for the game.  I was wondering if there was an achievement for reading every letter.  There wasn't, near as I can tell, I am just guessing what the last 4 achievements are as they are not unlocked.Sorry about the length, but you did want a description of what I liked, didn't like and why.

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Lost is a walking simulator with an interesting story and a haunting atmosphere. In this alternative reality, the World War II did not end as we know, and the world was punished by nuclear missiles. The story takes place in an underground world.Despite that engaging premise and its good graphics (and voice acting) the game has several problems. Firstly, the movement is ridiculously slow (it's not necessary to run like Bolt, but it needed to be this slow?). On the other hand, the optimisation is bad, there are too many FPS drops. And finally, there's an important bug: when loading game, you may be stucked. Although can be easy solved (just go to the options and "Turn off/on Head bob"), I can't explain how, being a problem that persists from the beginning, the developer hasn't fixed it.I can't recommend a game with these problems and with such a lazy developer.✪✯✪✯✪✯✪  ✪✯✪✯✪✯✪

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could say this was a great game, but it suffers a lot from bugs and story issues. Right off the bat the largest issue by far is the broken saving. The game is split up into five or so sections, and that's the only way you can save. Why? Because the actual saving system is broken and if you try to use it the game loads you in with one caveat: you can't move. A break from the bad, this game has a lot of beautiful environments to walk through, filled to the brim with details and seamless blending. Speaking of environment, the story is underwhelming at best. It suffers from a predictable plot twist as well as the fact the information is conveyed to you in a clunky way. Without spoiling anything, the ending is sub-par and while there are TECHNICALLY 4 endings, in practice it really only has one real ending with only small insignificant changes that don't really improve your experience. I would only recommend this game if you like environments and it's on sale. I hope the developers improve it, as I'd love to give it a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve played through most of the popular walking simulators (Edith Finch, Firewatch, Dear Esther, Stanley Parable, SOMA etc.) and Paradise Lost is the least satisfying of them all (even when compared to Close to the Sun).I can't recommend this game, despite all of the amazing work done by environmental artists:1) Story is meh. If you've seen the trailer - you've seen it all. Some plot ideas were straight up taken from other games.2) A huge amount of bugs - ranging from minor graphical issues to portions of levels disappearing below your character's feet for no reason and objects becoming non-interactive, hindering your progress.3) Audio design - some sounds used by developers are plain BAD (not fitting surfaces the character is walking through) and voice lines don't have a proper queue/trigger system in place - sometimes they're overlapping or replacing each other mid-sentence, because you’ve made it past the checkpoint.

_childDocuments_.review: The plot is really interesting and fits well with the post-apocalyptic atmosphere. The visuals and art design especially are really great. Levels looks amazing. However, the game CTD twice and even reset my PC once, and there are some performance issues as well, but nothing that can't be patched. In conclusion, I recommend it if you are looking for a really good story to go through in one evening.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Paradise Lost. It's a gorgeously visualized world to explore, full of science fiction-y details and careful craftmanship. Unfortunately, it's also a bit shallow and predictable in its writing (I guessed a major twist pretty early), and it's uneven in what it chooses to focus on and sparse in supporting documents and other environmental elements you can actually interact with. So, given that it's not expensive and doesn't run long enough to overstay its welcome, I felt like it was money well spent and would recommend it to folks who like that sort of low-stakes environmental exploration. But I do feel like it falls short of greatness.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a maybe in between the yes and now buttons, as this is a maybe game through and through:  - the visuals in the game is really good, it was fun looking at the architecture and the far off parts and just wondering how it looks - the story: I won't go into spoilers, but I enjoyed the story, from gathering clues in notes in the game to the audio parts of the voice recordings scattered throughout the game. - the audio is also very good, especially with some quality headphones, which makes the ambiance in the game go that extra mile   there is no real gameplay except walking and the occasional area where you need to hold in the right trigger and press up on the right analog stick.  holy hell this is one of the biggest gripes I have with this game, the atrocious walking speed. let's put it this way, half an hour into the game I looked for a mod to increase the walking speed of the main character.   the game has 4 endings, but with that horrible walking speed there is no way I am going to play it again, even though there were areas I might have missed.so even with all the bad in the game, I enjoyed the story and what went on in the world of paradise lost.

_childDocuments_.review: A premise: if I played more than 3 minutes it was because I wanted to write a detailed review to properly dissect this game, because I had the feeling it would have been a really bad game, but only playing it and exploring it the way the developers intended, I would have been able to do so.It took me barely 5 minutes to figure out the plot and about 20 minutes later I had also figured out what would have been the role of the female partner the protagonist meets. Everything it's tremendously cliché: every dialogue, document, audio recording found around.What murders the game is something else: the walking speed. The walking speed in this game is obnoxiously slow and there is no way to speed it up. I get it: these people want the player to walk slowly to both make the game last longer and to let the player apprecciate the environment (in which they put oh so much attention and care); what they failed to realise is that if they make a chore going from point A to point B, there are little to no chances that the players will ever explore any more than what is strictly necessary to proceed. Let alone replay the game! Supposing that the first time you play the game you don't get instantly frustrated by the ludicrously slow walking speed (like I did) and quit the game (like I didn't, but I've already explained ). Walking around to read one more piece of paper or to take another screenshot, felt excruciatingly tedious. Exploration, in this walking simulator, was a punishment; let that sink in for a while.It may seem I just want to talk as bad as I can of this game but I'm just pointing out all the things that are wrong with it. To give credit where it's due: the graphics and sounds are awesome! I have a lot to object with the voice actors but this is only because the graphics and sounds set the technical bar very high. Speaking of this, it's nothing less than a tragedy that the gameplay and the story are such a drag! A true pity because, especially later on the game, the aesthetic of the levels is gorgeous: the colours, the geometry, everything is exceptionally well done.However, here as well, I must make notice of two terrible problems. The first is that although for the majority of the play through my frames were somewhere in the 80's and up to 140, in a few sections they went down to 6, and the whole last chapter had no more than 20 frames per second; clearly an optimisation issue, but that hinders an already crippled game. The second one is even more absurd, and therefore intolerable: you can't turn off subtitles, however, certain dialogues have subtitles missing; what's funny, or so idiotic that makes you go through the 5 stages of grief that give name to the game's chapters, is that sometimes there are polish words or even phrases and nobody cared to subtitle them! So if you know polish, good for you; if you don't... Well, screw you!I'm sorry but no. No. No. No. This is not even worth the 1,24€ I spent. Playing it was just a waste of my time, and buying it just a waste of my money. I don't know what went wrong during the development, if they lacked any kind of insight regarding the solidity of the plot, if they had received criticism but rejected it because they thought they knew better; and same thing for the unbearably slow walking speed. There's no way anyone playtested this game and thought it was fine walking as fast as my grandmother when she had parkinson (if not slower!).If you need ratings:Graphics: 8/10Sounds: 9/10Longevity: 3/10Gameplay: 3/10Overall: 4/10This is a game, with an obnoxious plot, that should last about one hour and half, if you could just walk at a reasonable speed and skip the dialogues if you prefer reading to listening. However, it carries on for a few hours due to its unbearable slowness of movement, which makes the whole game a terrible chore to play through. It's a shame because technically, aside for some optimisation problems, it's truly well executed, and on top of all this, the finale puts the player in front of ethical choices that may help the most carefree players ask themselves some serious questions, which I believe everyone should ask themselves.I can't recommend this game, by any means, I can't find any reason to do it; I played it and wrote a review so that you could save a few hours of your precious time, do yourself a favour and take my word for granted.If the developers are reading this: you have no idea how angry you made me: this game could have been such a nice, short, walking simulator but you plagued with every flaw I could think of, while keeping the technical side on a very high level. I hope you will learn from your mistakes in the future: I can tell you're talented.What follows is a personal consideration that I believe it might be interesting to read for some; since these opinions are strongly subjective, I added them at the end of the review to keep the criticism of the game free from the criticism of the ideas conveyed through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Lost

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say enough good things about this game.  It's by far the best walking simulator I've ever played.The writing was nothing short of amazing.  Without spoiling anything, Paradise Lost has such a dynamic and multi-layered plot spanning from the main character's present to several generations in the past the likes of which I have never seen before.  If this were a movie it would have earned a boatload of Emmys.Some people complained in other reviews that the movement speed was a little slow (and it perhaps is about 10% slower than other games), but I don't think they really appreciated the game for what it was because there's so much to look at.  Everywhere you go is an intricately crafted work of art, showcasing beauty, sadness, hope, despair, horror, fear, or mourning so many things that have been lost.  Half the storytelling of this game came from walking around these amazing environments the developers presented us, so I was happy to slow down and enjoy the epic journey.A lot of games use notes, diaries, business memos, newspaper clippings, letters to friends and loved ones, and even audio recordings to reveal the story - and most of those other games do it so poorly, I end up skimming or skipping them entirely.  Not so with Paradise Lost; every scrap of paper I found was a joy to read, as it revealed another intricate facet of the story or deep hidden secret.The voice acting was on point.  Every character felt like a real, dynamic person, and when combined with what gets revealed about the story and the setting though other channels, these voice actors took me on a roller coaster of emotions.  They evoked so much empathy, sorrow, and fear for their well-being.  My mind was reeling from all the horrible possibilities that might possibly befall them.My only complaint was there were a couple little bugs that caused me to get stuck, and I had to reload the last checkpoint to try again.  Luckily, the game saves very regularly, so each checkpoint isn't far back.  You can save yourself a lot of grief in advance by going into the menu and turning off "head bob".  That's what got me stuck a couple times, and seems to be what everybody is complaining about.Other than that tiny complaint, I am very pleased with this game.Paradise Lost was truly a masterpiece of storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Lost

_childDocuments_.review: ProsParadise Lost is a very atmospheric game and has some incredible environments to explore and reminded me of the Metro games in their level of detail.  The storyline is told well through the voice work of the main characters and through both the recordings found throughout the game and the logs you find.  The scenes are also used to good effect in service of the story.ConsWhile the game is nice, there is not much in the way of choice in terms of exploration or plot until the ending.  Recommended if you like a quick, moody and atmospheric walking simulator with a good story that asks some interesting questions about life and living.

Trying to get all the achievements is tedious and kinda boring- Before starting playing, please disable "Head bob" in the settings. _childDocuments_.name: Paradise Lost

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game. I am always a fan of alternative history and “what could have been” fiction. Paradise Lost does a nice job of blending that storytelling and providing an interesting story to go along with the game. If you are the type of person that really likes to look and feel immersed in a world, while learning bits and pieces of the lore, I really recommend this game. It has a casual-walking based bioshock feel to it while not trying to be an action focused game. I also kept thinking how it would be worthwhile to experience this in VR at some point. It is a slower paced game, but one that does not get too botched down in how it tells its story. Every “level” in the game has its purpose and pushes the player to advance the narrative. If you want to run through the level to get to the next section, this may not be the game for you. The pacing is deliberate. Don't expect it to be fully dynamic in interactions with the environment as it does not really have too much more than basic interactions with notes, switches, and recordings. It would have been nice to have smoother interactions here. However, the dialogue and music are  great. I give props to the music especially. These two pieces really set the tone well for this game. I felt like I was there exploring this world even if the controls at times took me out of it. With that said, it honestly is a great game for what it does and reasonably priced for what you get. Took about 5 hours to complete the story or so, and... I wanted more.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Lost

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this experience love that there are different endings  Paradise Lost is a really good walking / exploration game. My only complaints are that you have to start from the beginning to see other endings and also at times the game felt slow due to walking speed is rather slow, running, is not a option. The voice acting at times felt very like they were reading a script and never felt that engaging to the story which was a let down but not terrible they never really expressed emotions well so you could never really tell if they were happy or sad. I would recommend the game to any walking simulator fans that love a good story to keep them playing to the end

name: Haven
detailed_description: Does love really conquer all? Yu and Kay have escaped to a forgotten planet, leaving everything they knew behind. Play two lovers at the same time as they settle into an unknown world. Explore the planet looking for parts and material to fix your ship and make it a cosy home. Enjoy moments of everyday life as a relatable couple while cooking meals, crafting and collecting precious resources to make it to the next day. Fight against those trying to tear you apart by synchronizing actions in combat, finding the perfect timing and rhythm, while controlling both characters and battling to keep them and their relationship alive. In this unexpected RPG adventure, explore the beautifully eerie and unstable planet while enjoying the thrilling soundtrack of renowned musician, DANGER. Key Features: Play two characters at the same time while exploring a fragmented planet, fending off enemies or building your relationship Make the choice about what's worth sacrificing to stay together, and if you're willing to give up everything else for love Glide over the grass, gather flow and clean the rust as you explore this dreamy planet and uncover secret areas Choose which Yu and Kay you want to play as: a woman and a man, two women or two men. Fight as the two characters in real time and relying on tactical sense and timing Immerse yourself in a romantic space adventure, the saga of two lovers trying to stay together against all odds Play a relatable couple in an intimate relationship, treated with maturity and humour Immediate to play, accessible, a pause in a busy day, a game that will make you smile A solo game that you can also play with a friend or romantic partner: a second player can join or drop out anytime in local co-op to share the adventure. Two controllers required to play co-op. The original soundtrack by renowned electro musician DANGER heightens the game’s emotional experience.

_childDocuments_.review: i really, really enjoyed this game. the gameplay was simple, but it was engaging enough to keep me from getting bored. where this game really shines is in yu and kay, though. they're absolutely amazing-- i got so attached to them by the end of my 12 hour run, and i would play a sequel SO hard. they really felt real, and their interpersonal interactions were so adorable i had to punch something. i appreciate that they didn't tone down the same sex pairings in terms of physicality: male yu is still jumping into male kay's arms for a healing hug which is just chefs kiss lol. i really would highly recommend this game to anyone who isn't looking for something Mega Deep in terms of gameplay and wants something character driven. 5 stars, would send kay and yu around holding hands again.p.s: the voice acting is so cute and well done; the VAs did an awesome job.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: This is another one of those 'I have a lot of mixed feelings about the game' games.I ADORE Yu and Kay and their story, and by god I could gush about the gorgeous art they have for the load screens and animations, along with Danger's FANTASTIC music for days, but the actual 'game' part has many, many problems that make it difficult to fully recommend to people who want an easygoing experience (that this game states that it provides). The combat is incredibly frustrating and clunky, and the movement (while slick) is finicky at best but most of the time is another source of annoyance (esp when trying to follow aerial flow threads). The crafting systems are set up in a way to seemingly deliberately waste your time as to need to slowly add individual items, then watch the animation of the cooking/crafting/touchpad, then slowly select the option to craft another one and repeat each time you want to make another item. I could rant more, but I don't want to be overly negative. Overall, I did have a decent time with it, just the issues did wear me down until I was ready to throw in the towel and not bother finishing getting all the achievements.I make the 'positive' recommendation almost solely based on the story/characters, OST (seriously, buy/listen the soundtrack and put it on loop forever), and its art because the 'game' part could have used some more work/tweaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.  (I actually have 10 hours in the game, finished the main story) Minor spoiler's below regarding the game's setting.This game isn't really about fighting or growing, its about exploring the relationship of the two principal characters, Yu and Kay, after they have escaped a sci-fi fascist society. Their dialogue is cute, believable and seems so wonderfully natural that you will be drawn into their story as you play the game. The writing in this game is nothing short of phenomenal in my opinion.The world presented is colourful and brilliant with a number of interesting creatures and cool ideas.If I had to complain, it is that the battle-system is a bit too simplistic, better they went with a more conventional real-time strategy or focused more on exploration/platforming (the platforming in this game is extremely light to begin with). And this game is too short, I feel there could easily have been 1-3 more story developments either directly related to the main plot or (and I would have preferred) side-stories exploring ideas like the previous colony, Yu and Kay starting a new life with new buildings/clothes/something, or befriending the animals of the planet.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game! The beautiful artwork, amazing voice acting, and genuinely fun gameplay was nice to relax with. The chemistry between the two protagonists was cute and heart-melting all of the time as I could see myself and my girlfriend in their interactions. The option of being able to choose Yu and Kay's genders was one of the main reasons I took an interest in the game and I appreciate the representation. Shortly after my girlfriend gifted me this game and I'm glad it went above and beyond my expectations as I knew little to nothing about this game before playing it. The combat was fresh and new as it deviated from the typical turn-based system which felt more hectic but skilful and rewarding. Every encounter felt refreshing with this twist to combat  Props to being compatible with co-op. Exploring the islets was satisfying as you scrubbed through every rust spot on each one while finding little trinkets or knick-knacks to bring home. Each item unlocked more cute interactions between the couple which made me sure to explore every inch of the game. As a person who has 100% of the achievements the little extra work put into the small details and interactions were fun to uncover although puzzling at times and the optional bosses felt challenging but doable. I highly recommend looking at the top-rated achievements guide for Haven as it provides very useful tips for people just starting out the game. (Being able to move the camera while gliding with mouse was a game changer as it helped me not get motion sick playing on pc.) This game put a smile on my face and made me think of my girlfriend the whole time and it was very easy to binge in a day or two. Overall I thoroughly enjoyed playing through and experiencing the game's story and would definitely recommend Haven to anybody.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the very few games I wished was longer it had such a rich story and very lovable characters, the interactions with the 2 gave me some very relatable feeling whether it was the mushy and loving moments or the heart-aching arguments. The combat was great also it heavily relied on teamwork and in a way is a good thing, when playing with a friend or loved one it builds a connection with each other and allows you guys to communicate and work with each other better by either doing duo attacks or just spreading out whos doing damage, defending, and pacifying.I expect great things from these developers in the future and these types of games. If any new people want to get interested in the series then bring a friend, close friend, loved one etc. And trust me you will have a great time.As for playing alone well....Uhh still a good game but wheres the fun in playing a game like this by yourself sorry to say.

Having the chance to play a local co-op was nice with this one in particular because of how well the characters are built and to follow along their story by contrasting our own choices at times was engaging. I kinda wanna elope to a deserted planet now.From His POV: It's quite difficult to get a co-op game with potential, let alone having the right touches between Story, Drama, Romance & Action. _childDocuments_.review: This is when I wish I could give a "neutral" rating instead of thumbs up / down. The game has both its good and bad aspects, and the two largely balance themselves.The good: the concept (of two lovers exploring and surviving in a fantasy world) is sweet and terrific, the characters are believable and well-written, the music is very nice.The bad: the appearance of the world is like in a 20 year old indie game, the map is much too fragmented and it is frustrating to get around, the story is poor and it didn't leave an impression on me.It's like they had a fantastic idea for a game, but didn't really know what to do with it and just made some mediocre garnish.

_childDocuments_.review: Taking place on an isolated planet named Source, Haven is about a couple - Yu and Kay, who can be played as any combination of M/M, M/F, or F/F genders for inclusivity - who escaped an oppressive society ruled by a 'Matchmaker' that pairs people off in pursuit of true love together. The game follows them as they explore their new home, try to repair their damaged ship, and understand the mystery of the Rust, a corrosive substance that has taken over the damaged planet. Above all else, though it's a story about a relationship; a couple going through thick and thin, with an emphasis on being written realistically.I'm gonna give it a 7/10!+Character writing is consistently strong. You get a real sense of Kay and Yu's personalities.+Their relationship feels very realistic. They bicker, have their own preferences, and share intimate moments. Their sex life, hobbies, and moments of friction are all portrayed really well.+The art style is very cute and the music is pretty enjoyable techno/electronic.+The game feels mostly the right length, about 10-15 hours.-Combat is janky as hell and never really feels like it 'clicks' even once you understand it.-Exploration, while fun, is a bit padded out. Lot of just collecting stuff for crafting ingredients that doesn't feel rewarding.-Lots and lots of loading screens.If the game had a bit less combat and felt a little more confident in just being story-driven without needing 'standard action-adventure gameplay', it might be an all-timer. As it is, it's still a very worthwhile experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I so wanted to like this game, I really did, but holy crap what a GD waste of money. DO NOT BUY. NOT EVEN ON SALE. There is NO explanation of what you're supposed to be doing, the controls are AWFUL, and there is no way to just experience the story without being forced into the mysterious gameplay that sucks. There's CONSTANT interjections from the characters that you're doing everything wrong with no explanation of what's RIGHT. How the hell are you supposed to learn anything that way? The "tutorial" teaches nothing - just throws you into the deep end and constantly tells you you're doing it wrong.Like I said, I really wanted to like it. But it seems like the devs didn't want me to.

_childDocuments_.review: A really enriched, unfiltered and earnest game with its chemistry the same way, making the couple the center-stage as you navigate Source, a planet left in peril, that's not only an escape from an otherwise confined, isolationist point-of-power, that attempts to bring others together through acts of endogamy, while teaching both the player and couple how to come together even in times of despair.I think my only problem with this game was in the combat, which I was not expecting at all. It's not as free-flowing as it could be, and kinda stifles progression. It's avoidable basically always, but at times when the act of movement, or 'flowing' around the map becomes a tad jank, it kinda forces you into it, without wiggle room for escape. Although, the combat itself is also so barebones and inoffensive, it doesn't ruin the overall experience whatsoever. It's more like... a hiccup. But a brief one at that.  A wonderfully robust narrative that allows the reader to really explore just what goes on outside the confines of its main couple, with a lot to uncover, and a lot of cute, enchanting-for-the-couple-secrets that give nuance, and have fun with the chemistry the couple in the game shares.

_childDocuments_.review: So I was very late to the party on this game, since it didn't really come up on the radar when it came out among the pandemic and other major developments in my life. Particularly, in 2020 when the game came out, I realized I was a trans woman - a realization with far reaching effects both in terms of the way I perceived the world and the way the world perceived me. Of especially notable significance was the role of queer representation in my life: representation the game was sadly lacking when it was originally released.But then over the next year or two, the devs did an amazing thing. They gave players the ability to choose to play as a same sex couple! Moreover, this change wasn't merely cosmetic, but fully ingrained into the central messaging, flow (heh), and central theme. They re-recorded a whopping 80 *thousand* lines of dialog, thus transforming the game from another tale of "heterosexual persecution" to a much more nuanced depiction of queer relationships and the oppressions both great and small that they face.It still took me some years to rediscover the game, but when I did, I found out about the update and then I couldn't download it fast enough. As a lesbian, playing a lesbian couple on the run from an oppressive government that uses love as a means of control is... powerful. Without spoiling anything, the backstory of Yu in particular is so strongly affected by this change that it's a wonder the game wasn't written this way from the beginning.In terms of gameplay, the game itself is simple enough that I think it firmly qualifies as a *narrative* game. That is to say, any lover of games regardless of skill level can easily pick up this game and not be particularly challenged by it. Of course, this is by design: the focus of the game is (rightly) placed on the central relationship between the characters, and not the difficulty of the mechanics.If I have one gripe, it's that the central gameplay loop can feel somewhat tedious. Generally speaking, you'll arrive in a new area, clean up the magic gunk that serves as both a narrative and mechanical plot device, and hunt down new parts for your spaceship as a way to advance the story. Of course, things happen along the way that regularly shake things up, but it doesn't completely override the minor annoyance of having to backtrack through several regions, even when shortcuts and fast travel options open up.Even so, the banter between the characters makes even the relatively uneventful parts of the game come alive, and no matter how many times Kay cheekily remarks on "the view" from behind as we're zipping over the landscape, or Yu sneaks a bite of creamberry while harvesting the rare delectables, I feel like I'm being invited to watch this special relationship grow.I think it's inevitable to feel a bit of emptiness as you go through a game like this and realize the dialogue options aren't unlimited. Once I got to the point where showering no longer meant sniping back and forth about whose hair may or may not be clogging the shower drain, or jocking for control of the Nest's precious supply of hot water, the game felt just a little bit more empty. This is, of course, not a knock on the game - short of recording another 80,000 lines of dialogue, it's an inevitability in any game like this - and if anything it speaks just how beautiful of a connection has been crafted here.And the romance is *beaitiful*, too. A game like this could have easily come off as cringe, and while Yu and Kay certainly have their well placed moments of cringe (who among us hasn't?), the interactions between them are, on the whole, natural, heartwarming, and SEXY.And oh boy did they bring the sexy? While the narrative never crosses into explicit adult content, one thing that becomes very clear as the fame progresses is that our protagonists are having a *lot* of sex. And honestly? Good for them! I think it's so beautiful to have queer love represented in media as being every bit as titillating as heterosexual love, and the game delivers on that front.Throughout their adventures, Yu and Kay make horny little passes at one another, tease one another about encounters had, and (perhaps most importantly) express vulnerability both in and out of the bedroom. I think it's SO IMPORTANT that relationships be depicted in this way. It's realistic, compelling, heartwarming, and relatable.For example, in one exchange that particularly stood out to me Yu asks Kay if they can switch sides of the bed (she says "I just want something different"), to which Kay agrees, only to find out Yu's side of the bed is "sticky" from a romp that took place before the scene. "And who's fault is that?" Yu asks, to which Kay says something along the lines of "I regret nothing."So yeah. To summarize, this is a beautiful game, and a triumph of queer representation, even if that representation took an extra couple of years to get to us. I'm fully enjoying the experience of playing it, and as I come up on the ending not knowing what the future will bring (kind of like the protagonists), I know the story will stick with me, and leave a lasting mark.And yet, a part of me hopes to forget the characters and the story, if only so I can have the pleasure of playing it for the first time all over again.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is a different kind of game, and I admit that's what interested me in it.  It's a bit runner-y, a bit craftsy, a bit visual-novel-y, very story-centric...  it's an interesting mix.And while I've heard some complain about resource gathering being "monotonous" I dunno, I don't really feel like it's painful.  Even the Appledew Stew with Appledews is breathtaking in its own way, you know?While you can play this solo, you are missing out on a LOT if you're not playing this with a partner- and maybe in that regard this isn't destined to be everyone's cup-of-tea...  or Applebrew, or whatever.My wife and I game together quite a lot, and we enjoy the synergy the game promotes.  It's a niche, but it's our niche, so it's cozy, cute, and fun.If you think this is the sort of experience you and someone special might enjoy?  I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute blast to play! The gameplay itself is quite simple, but entertaining, while the highlight of the game is the wonderful lovestory between Yu and Kay. Both protagonists feel very alive and their relationship genuine and natural. It's just...so...♥♥♥♥♥♥♥...cute! Personally I really appreciated to be able to play two boys in love (with wonderful voice acting and outstanding original music). I hadn't realized before how I missed this in games, being gay myself.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is nice, it's not overly complex or simplistic; it's there to fulfill its function. Personally, probably wouldn't have loved it if they hadn't updated it with same sex options, I don't think it would have spoken to me in quite the same way. But they did, so it did, and it's stuck with me.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: The only issue I truly have with this game is how short it is. It only takes about 12 hours to beat and thats if you grind for max level. The games story is really great and the romance between the two characters is incredibly relatable.The combat is kinda weird to get used to at first but after you get it down it is not a difficult game at all. While the combat is the weakest point in the game, it makes sense, the game is meant to be a story about a couple and their romance which is forbidden in their own world, not an RPG, if you are disappointed by the game strictly due to it's combat, you completely missed the point of this game.Just like Game Baker's other incredible game Furi, this game is fully voice acted, which means a lot more here since it is a bit longer than Furi. The Soundtrack is by Danger, who completely nails the atmosphere of the game with wonderful Electro/Synthwave music.I played through this game with my partner and we enjoyed it a lot. I'm sure the game is just as good regardless but I definitely loved playing it with her.Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun! Like really fun! But can be slow at times, Especially if you have to move from one side of the map to the other, which will slowly grow in distance as you explore the world, But apart from those moments the game can get really sweet, It has a brilliant at style and a calming, yet intense soundtrack, best played with headphones.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is the best game I've played in recent memory. Not particularly for its gameplay and mechanics mind you. They are fluid, intuitive and fun (controller recommended), but nothing special. Where Haven truly shines is in the relationship of its central characters, Kay and Yu. The game is full of so many small shared moments of daily accomplishments, struggles, worries and bits of intimacy. In more than two decades of gaming, I have never seen such brilliant depiction of a healthy, grounded, loving, adult relationship. For that experience alone Haven is worth half a day of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: So what is Haven?Haven is a third person, co-op possible, lite exploration and combat game focused primarily on the relationship between the two leads. The game revolves around their relationship and their problems. It is very much a microcosm built around their rather unique premise. Haven was released in December 2020 for Windows, PS5, Xbox 1/Series X, and on Switch the following February. It was developed and published by The Game Bakers. Known primarily for Furi. They released a Couples Update (Released in March, 2021), which allows you to choose who the two leads are. So you can have a Male and Male, Female and Male, or Female and Female pairing of your choice. However you would like to have their relationship represented. Which is cool. I do feel like this update broke the really vibrant and colorful intro and outro animations that worked prior to this update. So I hope they fix that. -=-=-Gameplay-=-=-Haven feels like it was designed around, and requires a Controller. Considering that combat controls are rather unique, I found myself gravitating to my controller rather than Mouse and Keyboard. In combat, both analogue sticks control the actions that your characters are going to do in combat (You can also use the D-Pad and Buttons). Each coordinate, up, down, left, or right, builds a charge meter for the action you want them to do. Once the meter is full, you can release the tension on the sticks/buttons to let them perform the actions you want them to do. Or you can hold for a more opportune moment. There is a mildly irksome situation where you can input a command and get stuck waiting for an enemy to finish it's attack animation before your characters perform the action you selected. So you can get hit by an enemy that you could've dealt with. Also, there is no selection for targets. It's handled automatically. I figured I'd share that, as I know that can bother some people. Outside of combat, you float about and move on hover-boots to zip about the various floating islands on the Source. It's quick but not quite nimble experience. You are also able to travel along "Flow Threads" which are glowing, bright blue paths that crop up in various locations that allow you to either build up Flow, which I never figured out the significance of (outside of it being a power source) and for navigating the environment. Flow Threads are required for navigation and completion of the game. There's only one I would say that's super challenging in terms of pure navigation (there's an achievement tied to it) but other than that, they're not too difficult. However, figuring out which one you need to ride to get into and out of some of the Islands can get rather frustrating at times. As they only show up at a certain range around you and you can't tell which ones are connected to a potential exit without riding it 90% of the way towards it's destination. So you can get stuck traveling along several threads until you find the "right" one that takes you where you want to go. Furthermore, there's a Hunger mechanic. It ticks down over time after you've had your last meal. Both protagonists seem at times, obsessed with food, as they'll comment on being hungry as the bar decreases over time. Yu in particular is a bit of a glutton. It's amusing for a little while, but it gets frustrating when it carries over into combat. If your Hunger meter depletes low enough: your Charge Rate for actions slows down. It's a significant debuff that, while it doesn't cripple, it can make some battles very frustrating. Obviously eating meals is the way to fix this problem. You can only cook/eat at a Camp or at The Nest. Which is the main base. So you either have to find a Camp or be at The Nest to resolve the only really debilitating status effect. If you use a Camp, be warned that you cannot set up another Camp until an unforeseen timer expires. So if you didn't eat something at a Camp (because the bar was too full) you can't set the Camp back up until that timer finishes. So it's something to be wary about.You can also only bring 6, non-combat related items into your expeditions with you. So with such a limited inventory, you have to choose between prepared foods (which restores more health), or medical supplies, or other supplies on your trips. I really wish there was a way to expand on that limit, as while it didn't feel too limiting, it also didn't feel all that great to have such a wide variety of items and not enough space to really take advantage of them all. -=-=-Story-=-=-If the initial premise and their relationship does not interest you, there's not much I can really say here that isn't spoilers. It didn't take any particularly noteworthy twists and turns. If you know how these stories go, you'll pretty much be able to predict how things go. It doesn't stop it from being interesting, given the uniqueness of the setting, but don't expect to be surprised by something novel either. The relationship between the two is realistic and entertaining enough for the duration of the game. -=-=-Final Thoughts-=-=-It took me about 11 hours after The Couples Update to beat the game. I was interested in what the update might've brought and ultimately ended up starting over because of it. You cannot change an already started file as far as Yu and Kay are concerned. So who they are at the start is how they are for that particular run. Haven made me interested in the world and the universe, Yu and Kay are a part of. Even if the game-play didn't particularly stand out to me. The story will very much make or break your enjoyment of Haven. I'd say if you're not enticed by the Premise of "A Young Couple escapes to a Unknown World in a Futuristic Sci-Fi setting, and tries to make a living together" doesn't appeal to you. I'd look elsewhere.Otherwise, it's not bad at what it does. I'd recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: This one hits different.Amazing music.  Great art direction.  But the real reason you're here is the writing and voice acting.Seriously, it's good.  Natural dialog that gives a mature glimpse into a real adult relationship.  If you've ever been in a serious relationship you'll see a lot to relate to in the main characters and their slice-of-life interactions.  I didn't realize how underexplored this is in video games until seeing how well Haven does it.  I only hope others will follow The Game Bakers' lead.And to be clear, by "writing" I don't mean the plot.  The plot is fine, but it takes a backseat to the outstanding development of the characters and their relationship.  The short one-off cutscenes are great and I found myself going back for 100% completion just to make sure I saw them all.The gameplay is very casual.  Entertaining enough for the 15-ish hours of playtime, but not really the selling point of the game.  Mostly it's a vehicle to push the cutscenes forward.Bottom line: highly recommended on the strength of the music, dialog, and overall narrative experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. At the start i was a little afraid that i wouldn't have liked it. After some hours of playing, this feeling disappeared. This romance-based game is one of the many that makes you feel happy, sad and scaried like the characters, you don't have to play this game, you have to feel it, as said from another reviewer. If you are searching a chill-game, that could make you feel good, this is absolutely the one you are searching for.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: France's take on Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga.This is the Frenchest game ever.  Bright pastel colors and French House music that make me feel like I'm in Porter Robinson and Madeon's Shelter tour.  A story about a couple that is already a couple when the game starts (no crappy hunting and chasing.)  Partnership, emotional intimacy, (and the other kind of intimacy) discussed in a mature and thoughtful way.  Criticism of conversion therapy and totalitarianism.  Its all just...wow....Alright, fine, I guess I'll talk about gameplay.Gameplay is a straightforward adventure game with coop capability.  Combat borrows from Mario & Luigi with coop in mind (Timed Hits become a very different story when you have to time them with another player.)  There are very light survival elements with very little time limits.  Players gather what they can from the environment to craft very simple healing items and boosts in combat.  You level up with a night of boozing (earned through experience from combat and eating an assortment of dishes you create.)  I will say that playing with another player can be a challenege.  You will have to use Remote Play if playing remotely.  And two players gliding accross the environment can get rather awkward.  And something in the "best" ending can get uncomfortable.  But the positives are so good that I don't recommend experiencing this alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Loved every single bit about this game. The soundtrack is amazing and the graphic style just looks stunning in my opinion. You have this cute and cozy story line which gives you plenty of time to just enjoy the setting of the game and explore what it has to offer. This with a lil mix of some RPG combat keeps the game refreshing and challenging.I definitely recommend this game and i hope to see more like it in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because of the art. I wasn't expecting a dark sci-fi hidden in the background. Despite everything, it was a fairly positive experience. The game offers more content than one would expect. The combination of exploration with visual novel-style dialogue is quite enjoyable. Additionally, the dialogue between the protagonists is realistic and the voice acting is well done. The music is also very fitting.Though you can see where the developers were cutting costs. For example, we have no interiors of any buildings. What we get each time is a dialogue set against a dark door into which the protagonists have entered. A bit of a shame. Quite strange is the combat system.  When you play solo you have to play for two. It is better not to leave fast fight to the computer when you have more opponents because it makes strange decisions. The health of the same enemies is sometimes low and sometimes several times higher. And when robots appear in 3 and are able to heal themselves it's not what I would call "very easy" as the developers inform you at the beginning of the game. I think the game would be better if they didn't hold back on the adult content. On this level, two young people who are also a couple of runaway lovers is quite unrealistic being alone on a strange planet for weeks at a time. There are scenes suggesting it from time to time, or the only scene where they sit naked on their ship, but suddenly they're even showering in their underwear? Also good are the endings in which are quite life-like where there is no perfect choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent story telling game the combat gets a little repetitive but I think it can be overlooked for what this offers. Like I said it has an excellent story with two great characters who have a functional and healthy relationship and I could not recommend this enough for those who are looking to experience a good story.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer, I enjoy story based games, I played this game solo and also do not mind sometimes repetitive game-play as much as you might. The game is small but charming, the maps can sometimes feel a bit empty but they are not large and there is always something to see. the game rewards exploration with dialogue and short cut-scenes. perfect for me but not everyone's cup of tea.The main characters are pretty well fleshed out, not perfect but you get to know them fairly well, however I wish the two other human characters we see had more than 1 scene each. The ending felt a tad rushed but was satisfying, but I wish we did confront (insert big bad) in some way shape or form but I was still happy to see Yu and Kay come out successful in the end. Overall its dialogue and exploration heavy, do not go into this with other expectations or you maybe disappointed, overall its charming and I enjoyed the world and story thoroughly. I would like the ending to not be AS short but thats not too its detriment I just wanted more story. 7/10 for me not perfect, but enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: First off, a big thank you to the devs for adding a free LGBTQ+ update. You can tell they care about the game and its players. The end result is an engaging and enjoyable narrative-first game that offers a real sense of progression. I did have an issue with the ending, however.Pros:+ Great music that reminds me of early 2010s chillstep. I found it nostalgic+ Sweet, believable relationship.+ Pet many cute aliens. Adopt a cute alien.+ Fantastic art direction. Loved the liberal use of red/blue neon.+ More content than I expected, which encourages you to slow down and enjoy exploration. The writers did a great job balancing the main relationship and world-building.Cons:-  This was fixed with a patch shortly after the free update was released- You can fast travel to almost every island but you can't fast travel from all of them.- You can copy your save to experience all dialogue options, but it must be done from the title screen. Loading a different save file must also be done from the title screen and there are no manual saves.My gripe with the ending (spoilers!):The good/true ending (there are two total) has a plot hole with  It seems like it was added as a spicy plot twist that maybe symbolizes  but poses real concerns about  Obviously, there are no perfect outcomes when running away from a dystopia with advanced military technology... but with the way things are written, I can only assume that  but I don't remember this being specified and it would introduce its own challenges for the duo's permanent stay on Source.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful, not very challenging game (it doesn't make any claims to be, even says so right at the start) and a pretty love story with... for me anyway... only less than good endings, sadly. Suggestion for people who are like me, who are fine with getting the best end possible and leaving it at that: I really would've wished for a third ending option in which you get to try and fight it out with the antagonist and bring home a solid win, but this'll have to do I suppose, I'm just not sure why the game needed a bad ending at all... wellh, there's a fetish for everything.I'm also a little unsatisfied with certain plot details that didn't get finished up and the situation at the end of the game, with either ending could harbor the wild possibility of deserving some form of follow up... but that's just me tootin' the horn of "I want moar", really.Controls and general scheme of movement might take a little while to get used to, at least they did for me, and the game is best played with controller(s). From what I've seen of the coop it's.... rather less than well executed sadly. Being forced into shared screen CoOp in a game where both characters move around the map so quickly can be disorienting, less than pretty to look at and at times even nauseating, while combat and crafting in coop tends to be extremely simplistic and just needlessly time consuming (tho thankfully not excessively so, simple solution would've been to allow the player(s) to bulk craft their consumables of choice). The art style of the game is fantastic in every way in my opinion. Simplistic where it doesn't matter and detailed in the places it counts. Only thing that chafed with me was that many of the critters you meet fall on the ugly-to-disgusting side rather than anywhere pretty or cute which was somewhat unnecessary but hey, matter of taste I guess.Last but most certainly not least the phenomenal soundtrack by Danger has to be mentioned. Listening to certain pieces quite frequently these days, very nice!All in all, I would not recommend to get this for Co-Op unless you're both really in it just for the story and can play relatively synchronously rather well, but if you do try, tell me what you thought of it! We sorta gave up on the coop rather quickly for reasons of nauseating camera-to-movement reasons.Take from all that what you will.

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game about a couple still figuring their feelings out for each other while running away from an oppressive society. The soundtrack is an AB SOOO L U T E BANGER!!!!! The banter between the couple is charming and witty and some what organic, i found myself smiling more often than not while playing.First ever couples game for me, so I was completely surprised by everything this game brought. But AGAIN! The soundtrack man, sooo good!!Def. worth the buy! Especially when its on sale!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to play this game with my boyfriend as it seemed to be a game you mostly play as two players, but had a single player option. However when we started this game up, it became quickly evident it was the opposite; a single player game with a two player option. In two player mode you do not play as two individual characters. The only independence you really have is to walk around on your own, until the other player forces the both of you to start flying wherever they want. You both have to agree on conversation responses for each character, you both control a single camera and direction, you both play together as one entity that controls the characters rather than playing as two individuals who work together in the game. I was very disappointed to have such wonky controls ruin the experience of what seemed to be a game with great story. I highly recommend playing this game as single player ONLY unless you each want to take turns sitting back letting the other person play. A good example of true co-op gameplay would be A Way Out.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and wholesome game about love, freedom and the cost of those things -- and how, even if sacrifices have to be made, it's worth it.The gameplay, albeit with a slightly repetitive gameplay loop, is sweet and calming, and the interactions between the protagonists keep it from being boring or annoying. The combat can take some work to master, but it's intuitive and keeps us going after the best strategies for each enemy, and it doesn't get tiresome.But most of all, the story of the love between Yu and Kay is what sets this game apart: It is beautiful, and best of all: not perfect. They disagree, they fight and they worry about each other even through that, becoming closer than ever after all the experiences and sacrifices they've made, and it is, in my opinion, a beautiful representation of love.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous story about love against all odds, set against one of the most unique gameplay loops I've seen in a while. The only catch is that the creativity of exploration and combat can take some learning. Also, you might get lost a lot, as many regions kind of look alike. If you can get past those issues, though, it's a fantastic experience that personally earned an easy place in my favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit of an odd game, I am not entirely sure what the target audience is but I enjoyed it.The voice acting, music and 2d art are all amazing. However the 3d art, mostly the environment, is a bit of a letdown compared to the other aspects to the game. Many areas look bland and low poly, like they are from an old game. The gameplay is also rather basic, but in the end graphics and gameplay is not what this game is about. (which is a weird thing to say I've got to admit)This game is generally about vibes. When you roam around you got a great soundtrack to listen to, and when you are back at the Nest you can enjoy Kay and Yu's many interactions. Some of those can be a little awkward but most are just plain old fun.There is also Oink, Oink is good.This game is certainly not for everyone, so I can't tell you whether you should play it or not. You'll just have to try it and see.

_childDocuments_.review: It was pretty well done. I enjoyed it over all, though much of the gameplay was repetitive and more geared towards playing it with a second person. But there were a lot of the little things of a loving relationship between two people comfortable with each other. And the character moments of the ones not part of the main two were well done. They were single scenes but they clearly conveyed every feeling and thought that you need to know about these characters and why the main characters are willing to leave them in the past.I would say it was probably an 8/10. Might be better if you have a partner you can play it with.
