_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I don't generally put a lot of stock in video game romances. But I believe that Yu and Kay love each other.Haven is a game about real love. Not storybook love where all problems can be fixed by gazing into your partner's eyes, but a love where things aren't always perfect. And when they're not perfect, both people are willing to put in work and compromise and self-sacrifice... because their partner is worth it.There's a game here, and it's a decent one for flying around some beautiful landscapes while listening to chill music. But the reason to play Haven is to see Kay and Yu interact, and to watch their love grow and mature over time. I have never seen a video game romance that is so completely true to life. Haven is a singular joy to play, and it should not be missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay can get a bit repetitive, but can also remain enjoyable since the game doesnt drag on for too long. On the other hand, the character development and voice acting were very good, while the artwork and music were absolutely astonishing. Even the Credits were an incredible experience. Go watch those after you're done with the game!

_childDocuments_.review: At first it feels weird to play a game that is most likely supposed to be played in co-op solo but you get used to it. If you have the opportunity to play it with someone else definitely do that but I think even alone it's still fun to play.For me the combat system is the worst part of the game. It's very simple and annoyingly slow to charge up attacks. Each fight gets repetitive fast.I don't like that there is no dedicated save function that you can trigger manually. The game only saves when there is a loading screen.The idle animations are very cute (and they can heal you)!I love that you can choose between a hetero, lesbian and gay couple. Representation matters!The game runs perfectly on the Steam Deck and the game is great to chill on the couch.The dialogues are cute and romantic and the voice acting is great too although at the beginning there were some sections where the quality of the recording wasn't that good and it sounded like the lines were recorded from farther away or something.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of my favourites, and it is for a very good reason.This game follows story of Yu and Kay, two lovers who was not chosen for each other, but yet decided that o´mighty "matchmaker" is wrong and leave their home planet "Apiary" stole a class d ship "The nest" and used so called "flow bridge" to get to the planet called "Source", this all happens before actual story.The design is great, and nice to look at, character sheets at corner of screen during conversations are great,the 3d models look good, not as good as sheets, but still good.Game tends to be sometimes very, very full of love and relationship stuff, if you don´t like that, this is not game for you.Story is building sometimes bit slower, but it is not that bad, characters usually give a good hint what to do so you don´t find yourself struggling that often.I also love option of same gender couple.The best part of this game however is by far is the music.background music is great.The intro sequence animation is awesome, and it sets the game perfectly.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really debating getting this one. Having that said - I abolutely loved the game. The chemistry between the two main characters, the beautiful world, voice acting. The way of conveying character's past via casual conversations. All of that is amazing. And Danger's music to top it all of. Possibly the best game I've played in 2021 so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is a mostly relaxing and easy-going game good to play with someone else.  I will say that the game is basically one continuous string of suggestive language, so if you play it with someone you don't sleep with, there will probably be some weird moments.  But not necessarily in a dirty way, there's also a lot of hand-holding, hugging, kissing, etc.  You'll end every day either at home or camping which involves cooking and crafting together, having conversations, etc.  It's a "nice" game that doesn't involve any graphic nudity or anything like that and portrays a healthy and somewhat normal relationship.As far as gameplay, you'll spend most of the time exploring and collecting plants and rust (the red stuff) and following flows.  Flows are strings of energy you collect by traveling along them from end to end and can also be used to reach otherwise inaccessible areas.  Most of them are not difficult but there are occasionally flows that are particularly long or have a lot of twists and turns.  The other big gameplay mechanic is battling.  There are several actions you can take in battle.  Enemies are often vulnerable to one attack or another, and all enemies must be pacified with a finishing move or they'll get back up.  There isn't any killing except for some mechanical enemies which are destroyed.  Animals/monsters are made non-hostile by pacifying them.  Most of the game is pretty easy, but some battles will require timing actions with the other player to do combo attacks or to hit a monster while it's vulnerable from a previous attack.  All in all, I have to give this game a big thumbs-up because my wife and I really enjoyed it and wish we had more.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I'mma be real, I have tried to finish this game three times now, and only finished it once. The story was a bit meh for me when I first played and the combat, while being unquie and a time based system that I didn't have much experience with( But thought it was super cool), frustrated me a lot. So I quit the first time around 2 years ago, and a second time a year or less ago. But.. I tried again and found a sort of deep joy and embarrsingly deep love for the characters, how they interacted, acted and the kind of people they were. I knew most of the story, where certains plot points where located and most of the stuff I needed to do to progress the game, but I can honstly say, I hadn't expected a lot of the things I saw on my third playthrough.Hidden beach island, rust wastelands and the ending was quit unlike what I had expected. I even forget to go the svanna area I saw last I played, just from how interesting all this other stuff was.It's good, play it just once and spend about 15 hours of honstly pure wholesome, romanc between two people who dares to go against a dystopian future that sounds way more interesting then most other games "dystopias".Plus it can be played as a straight couple, two guys or two girls. _childDocuments_.review: It has the tag 'Action-Adventure', but this "game" has the complexity of a mobile game and is as exciting as watching rust grow... Merely the love story seems to be enjoyable, especially for couples who play in coop mode, and that's the only reason why I give this "game" a positive rating:Everything else is not worth the money or time.The gameplay loop consists of:That last one bugs me the most... There's a cutscene. Then the protagonists say "Let's eat" and then you're forced into a 1st-person mode where you "walk" around the ship as a disembodied entity and can't do anything but trigger the cooking cutscene in the kitchen. After eating the protagonists say "Let's go to sleep" and you're forced into 1st-person mode again and have to "walk" in the bedroom and manually trigger the sleeping cutscene. Next morning the protagonists say "Let's go outside" and you're forced into 1st-person mode again and have to "walk" to the front door and manually trigger the forage mode...Why is that boring shit even in the game? You control the protagonists directly outside of the ship - why not inside, too? Why are we like Schroedinger's observer: present like a 3rd character, but also not actually present at the same time?That stupid 'having to trigger everything manually' would only make sense, if I had other things that I could trigger like side quests or if the order I do it in is important to an event... but there is absolutely nothing to do! This is tedious bullshit.Other than experiencing the love story in coop this "game" is a boring waste of time and money.Also, I had wished to play as a female Kay and a male Yu, but that's not possible, despite both character variants being in the game, fully animated, and fully voiced. Apparently white guys aren't allowed to date dark-skinned girls.

_childDocuments_.review: Moderate ending spoilers aheadPlaying Haven is like drinking a fine wine: you can chug it down like a neanderthal and miss out on 3/4 of the experience, or you can take your time and savour all the little things it has going for it. For better or worse, I tend to be attracted to grittier, more grounded games that revolve heavily around combat. Haven was a sudden, and welcome, departure from this trend, and I can say with confidence that playing the first 10 hours of Haven made me feel happier than I've been in a long time. Concurrently, Haven is also... a bit of an enigma. Coming from the developers of Furi, a hyper-violent game about a literal god of death escaping from actual prison, Haven follows a pair of star-crossed lovers on their journey of self-determination, and escape from the metaphorical prison of an overly-controlling intergalactic society. While the overarching setting may be a little bit... idealized (ex. both lovers are overtly pacifistic, vegan, and generally dismissive of the costs that modern society brings, despite directly benefiting from & wholly relying on hyper-advanced fabrication & space-travel technology), the emotional and relationship issues Yu and Kay deal with on a daily basis are very much believable and grounded in reality. Haven is slightly less of a romantic game, and more a largely believable simulation of a young couple trying to balance independent survival while maintaining a healthy relationship. Again, despite the futuristic fantasy setting of Super Sayian jet boots, space travel & Star Trek replication technology, the day-to-day problems the two face are very realistic; small things like laundry, hygiene, cooking, dealing with daily stresses, and compromising on different worldviews. These smaller, slice of life interactions are what really make this game work: Yu & Kay joke, flirt, fight, and compromise in very realistic ways. It's all very charming, and I loved watching all the little moments the two shared together, especially the romantic interactions.Exploration is the other main attraction to this game: the world of Source is beautiful, and the distinct art direction lends itself towards incredible vistas and unique alien wildlife. Again, it's the little details that really make this work: Yu & Kay will make occasional comments based on what's happening in the world & how they view it. Each has distinct skillsets that come into play as they travel along, with Kay being a biologist and Yu being a mechanic. They hold hands as they fly across the landscape, they can pet the wildlife they help purify, and they have numerous interactions when doing activities such as camping or swimming at a beach. All in all, it makes for a fantastic and charming atmosphere.  At least... for the first 10 hours.I want to make this abundantly clear: Haven is an incredible game and I can't recommend it enough. On sale, off sale, doesn't matter, it's absolutetly worth getting, especially if you have a significant other that might enjoy playing with you. With that said, Haven was a 15 hour game for me. I didn't get all achievements, but I did clear all the islands and get a maximum relationship score. Unfortunately, the last 5 hours became a bit of a grind, and the very last hour left a really sour aftertaste to an otherwise fantastic game. Enough to ruin the experience? No, but enough to sour the good bits.I mentioned before that Yu & Kay are quite pacifistic. That doesn't mean there isn't combat in this game, in fact there's quite a substantial amount of combat throughout it's runtime, in the form of purifying/pacifying corrupted creatures. Haven itself states that combat isn't particularly hard, indeed it's fairly simplistic at it's core: you have ranged attacks, melee attacks, a limited-use shield, and combination/charged attacks. Some enemies have certain weaknesses, and some later ones have multi-stage weaknesses (ex. one type might require an initial ranged attack, and melee follow-up). For it's part, Haven makes use of this system extremely well, and does just about everything it can to spice things up across it's runtime. For me though, it wasn't meant to be stretched out over 15 hours. Some of the later levels get a tiny bit sadistic, requiring multiple single-use items per fight & constant healing, and generally making the last 5 or so areas an unnecessary slog. The crafting system also tends to exasperate these problems. Early game is fine, but the lack of automation means that food, healing & combat items can only be crafted one at a time, and late game fights can easily consume 2-4 single-use items a pop. Factor in another potential healing item & up to 2 food items for transportation to & from your home base, and you can begin to see why the late game started to wear me down.Where the real issues began popping up were in the game's story, or at least the last third of it. Again, heaping initial praise on Haven's design, it's main story is generally well done. The central gameplay loop of exploring a beautiful sci-fi fantasy world, bopping to the amazing soundtrack by Danger, cleaning the small islets of corruption, discovering the secrets of the previous civilization that one inhabited the planet, and then returning home at night to develop your relationship generally works well. As the story progresses and the more serious issues start rearing their heads, your choices start mattering more and more. Tracked by their "confidence" metric, Yu & Kay's dialogue choices dictate how committed they are to staying on the planet & openly defying their authoritative government, or if they've started having second doubts and contemplate returning home. For the vast majority of the game, the impact of your decisions are plain to see: actively working on your relationship, avoiding unnecessary conflicts with your partner, and tackling your problems directly boosts your confidence and overall makes Yu & Kay a better couple. While being lethargic, combative, and running from your problems decreases confidence and leads to ever-growing problems with their relationship. The message being sent is quite clear.Putting it bluntly, the last hour completely fumbles everything the previous 14 hours tried to set up. There are two endings to this game; a "good" ending with significant costs and severe underlying problems, and a "bad" ending that can very easily ruin the entire experience. Usually I go into great detail regarding things like this, but Haven is so good that I don't really want to spoil things more than I already have. So I'll say this: after spending 14 hours laying out very clear themes around the costs of self-determination and tackling your problems head on, Haven does a complete 180 within the last hour & throws that all away, leaving you with two generally inconclusive and unsatisfying endings to an otherwise great story. Again I don't want to sound too negative; Haven is an incredible game, with a fantastic atmosphere, amazing soundtrack, and tons of small relationship moments that I greatly enjoyed. Yu & Kay were a cute couple, and I very much appreciated all the moments they shared together, from their constant flirting/lovemaking, to managing their vastly different personalities & working out problems productively. For the vast majority of the game, my only real issues were minor ones like combat becoming repetitive, movement being a touch sticky at times, and the lack of automation when crafting multiple items. But then the finale hit, and... I don't know. I don't want to say that it ruined the game for me, but it definitely put a damper on the 14 or so good hours I had with it. I actively regret looking up the bad end.I still give this one my full recommendation. The core game is still one of the best I've played in years, and I very much recommend playing it in 1-2 hour sessions to preserve it's runtime. Just... be aware that both endings may take some of the wind out of your sails.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun. I won't mince words about it. The only problem I have with it is the pre-programmed conflict between the two main characters. There should be options that don't provoke the other one. Not all relationships are defined as in this game. It is very much possible to have a healthy and happy relationship with your SO without having conflict because of insignificant details as presented in the game. It makes me feel as if the designers are either single, divorced, or otherwise uninitiated into the world of a healthy and loving relationship. _childDocuments_.review: The story is the driving force of this game, it's beautifully written and the amount of detail they put into the main characters and their interactions is really impressive. After finishing the story it felt like I just read a good book and will remember Kay and Yu for a long time.The gameplay itself is pretty basic though and can get repetitive quickly. Exploring itself becomes boring after a while because there is little to no variety in the stages and even though there is a good amount of enemy variety the simple combat just makes it all feel like the same thing.The developers have made something really unique with Haven. They took the idea of true love in a healthy adult relationship and built a whole game around that core concept. You can clearly see this come back in every little aspect of the game and I can really appreciate that. The storytelling is clearly the key focus and I think the simplicity of the other game aspects were made that way to not take away from the story. It's definitely not perfect, but a very engaging and fun way of telling a love story as opposed to media like Visual Novels, Books or a TV show.The game definitely isn't for everyone and at the end of the day it really comes down to what you like. If you are someone that likes a challenge, in-depth combat combat systems and have a great control over your character's growth... then this game is probably not for you.If you are someone that's in the mood for a wholesome and heartful story, with great character design, easy to get into controls and game systems... then this game is something you will probably enjoy a lot.Two notes for the PC version:Co-op: Local co-op requires 2 controllers. Both the PS4 and Xbox controllers worked well for me. Remote Play is supported and worked okay-ish. My online friend had some issues with a pixelated screen so now and then and a little input delay. But that's most likely because of the internet connection not being good enough.Save files: the game ONLY autosaves and this happens when you move from one zone to the other or exist the main hub (the Nest). So if you want to quit make sure to do this before shutting down the game. Also very important: near the end of the story there is a point of no return. If you don't go back into the title screen and make an additional save, you'll be eternally stuck in the Epilogue chapter. The developer is working on this part for an update, but hasn't given a ETA yet.For more information make sure to check out the full video review!

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is a small, charming indie game focused on the loving relationship between the two main characters, Kay and Yu, and the various challenges that will be crucial obstacles in the security of their relationship. In Haven, on a lost planet far from the society in which they are fugitives, Kay and Yu, controlled by yourself or with another person in co-op are to explore the many zones in which gameplay is tailored. In here, you will explore, craft, and learn about the planet, the remnants of past activity, and about each other. Despite being a rated M game, Haven has a distinct lack of themes such as violence or profanity that is ever-present in other M rated games. Profanity is replaced with in-universe, childish-sounding swears that are amusing to us players. Combat consists of a faux turn-based system (akin to the OG Final Fantasy 7) where Kay and Yu's attacks, either individually or as a pair, damage the various enemies until they are defeated. There is no killing. Combat ends with machines being destroyed or the various creatures being cleansed of a corruption pervading the entire planet. Instead the Mature rating stems from the explicit sexual themes seen throughout the game, of which there are many.Exploration consists of visiting several different islands in the world, cleansing the corruption from the land and creatures, and interacting with objects that trigger conversations that expand on the plot and with Kay and Yu's relationship. Exploration can become a bit of a slog, especially when you explore more and have to travel farther after resting at the home ship. But the dialogue and uncovering more of the story and the characters makes it worth it, in my opinion. Easily the best part of Haven is the main characters of Kay and Yu and their relationship. The developers have been able to write a relationship between the two that feels real. It's set way after any honeymoon phases (unique for romance stories in general), but you can still get a sense that the two love each other. They fight and argue about small and, relevant to the plot, big things, but it only serves to strengthen the "legitimacy" of these two characters. This all makes for a memorable pair of characters and one of the best couples in fictional media. Overall, Haven is a hidden gem that is well worth it for a story to surely pull you in.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Funny story: I actually bought this game and Hades at the same time. I figured I'd give Haven an hour first before I tried Hades. Next thing I knew, it was two hours later and it was the middle of the night.Haven is a chill game. It's a game for those who just want to have a vacation to a beautiful blue alien world and experience chill relationship drama, and without spoilers that's most of what you're going to get from Haven. The music is a relaxing bit of electronica that reminds me of the Youtube producers I grew up listening to, and the characters have a likeable dynamic and a fun relationship to watch.Control-wise, it controls pretty well for the most part. The game seems set up for a controller, but I haven't had any problems with a mouse and keyboard. The one thing that's a little counterintuitive is how the singleplayer mode is accounted for. In battle (minor spoiler but there are battles), each character has four possible inputs, designated by WADS for the left hand and OK;L for the right. It's a little hard to wrap one's head around and it does mess up my timing and rhythm, but it's a smaller part of the game and it's inoffensive.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, and especially its characters, have me positively enchanted. I cannot believe I fell so helplessly in love with Kay and Yu from the get-go, but the game really knows how to make you care about them instantaneously. That's likely in large part due to their stellar voice actors and the hysterical - and even sensual - dialogue constantly being tossed between them, no matter what you're doing. These scenes made up the lifeblood of the game for me, as every action I took and task I completed was almost guaranteed to reward me with an endearing interaction.That was not entirely surprising to me - even the trailers showed that I'd likely love these two one way or another. What I didn't expect was the lore and story present in the game. I kept being pleasantly surprised to learn about the Apiary, about the hornets, about the matchmaker. Some of it was fun and funny, other portions were truly chilling (hello, recalibration). As a writer, seeing the developers integrate genuinely interesting worldbuilding and plotlines into the gameplay flow and intertwine lore into the narrative in organic ways was a blessing in every way.So, are there downsides to this game? Without a doubt. I primarily struggled with the combat. The controls simply aren't intuitive or natural, even if I understand what they were going for. There were even portions of the battle system - such as being able to charge your Duo attacks to higher levels, and how to do so - that eluded me until endgame because there was no explanation of how to do so. But my biggest problem by far was that characters would often have their attack charged, only to just...stand there...and do nothing. No idea why.Thankfully, the above is assuaged by two things: one, there are difficulty settings that allow you to make battles a breeze if you really can't get a hold of it (without any penalty to the story or your achievements); and two, even with the issues, I actually found myself invested in battles and felt there was a genuine, balanced challenge to them.If you're on the fence about this game, I can heavily recommend that you pick this up regardless of your doubts. You WILL fall in love with Kay and Yu, likely to the point of appointing them as your newfound OTP - and that alone is worth the price of admission. All of the gorgeous artwork, the spot-on voice acting, the relaxing exploration, the head-bopping music, and the satisfying storyline are much-appreciated bonuses.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is a third-person action game about two people in love escaping from the fates that the others assigned to them, cutting all ties and burning all bridges to settle on a seemingly uninhabited alien planet. It's very intimate with basically only these two populating the cast, and the game heavily signals that it's better when played in co-op with your other half.For whatever reason I was expecting to roll my eyes at the characters, not really expecting anything serviceable in the personality / writing department. But, despite sometimes coming off as some L.A. golden kids with first world problems (they kinda are, at least one of them), the characters turned out to be very likeable and were nearly the single driving force behind me finishing the game. So, props to the writing team. The world the two lovebirds escaped from also unravels itself gradually, not dumping a bunch on lore on you all at once, instead using the drip feed approach. My only gripe is I guess a few loose ends like Music is by Danger, an artist who already collaborated with developers on Furi, and it's a very pleasant electronic dance ambient pop or whatever. Sometimes it's a bit repetitive, and there are way too few really outstanding tracks for my liking. Yet, I'm deep into my 20+ listen of the game's , accompanied by artsy watercolor animation (which sadly didn't get enough budget allocated so 50% of it is reused throughout the video).Gameplay is the weakest point in my opinion. It's hardly engaging, with not much happening besides exploration of bite sized islands and battles with the animals inhabiting them, the latter a faux turn-based spam of one of 3 actions: defense, melee and distant attack. Leveling (which occurs as the two protagonists bond), and consumable crafting hardly alleviate the variety issue, and their main value comes down to new dialogue scenes. The game is pretty easy, as it tells you right at the beginning should you pounder selecting "story difficulty" over normal. All in all, a 100% completion run took me about 20 hours.Visuals are a bit simple on the technical side, nothing fancy, with an overdone acid color "alien planet" palette (see No Man's Sky etc). But sometimes it's very pretty. Nice grass, reminds me of thatgamecompany's Flower.Sometime after game's release out came an update that has added an option for some gender bending. For whatever reason, it only focused on same gender couples and left out chocolate tomboy + albino boy pairing option. Devs' excuse? Too technically complex to execute and it would make the characters fit stereotypical gender roles too much, which is somehow a bad thing. So yeah, I'm not sure I'm feeling that. Anyways, the new female to male character's design is really lame so I don't know if I chose it even if it was an option. But the brownie tomboy is really cute. If I ever replay the game I'm definitely doing the lesbian run. Although, given how barebones the gameplay is and linear story there are few incentives for replaying.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm typically not one for reviewing games but this one really deserves some praise.The storyline is simple but still brilliant with little hints sprinkled in along the way towards twists or key story points. I often couldn't stop thinking about the game when I wasn't playing as to what might happen next and trying to peice together the universe and events prior to the game's beginning. I really liked the sound/music design, 'Space Caress' is especially powerful, you can feel the emotion in it and even seems like it's telling their story. Voice acting is good.Dialogue is great, plenty of funny lines/moments that made me laugh.One of the best things about the game i think it's how the pair actually feel like a genuine couple and not some generic characters with no personality or one single trait that dictates everything they say or do (e.g. dumb aggressive person, tsundere, know it all etc)The free update with same gender couples option is a nice touch as that allows more people to fully immerse themselves and relate to the characters better, also it means they paid money for more voice actors as well as a few design tweaks fully knowing it wasn't going to gain them money so kudos for that. Environment and creature designs are beautiful, gliding around the landscapes on flow thread's is a fun mechanic.So many little animations that bring the game to life e.g. (doing flips off cliffs, idle animations, even the not currently controlled character gliding up to your side to hold hands opposed to the typical following single file like in every other game. _childDocuments_.review: A lot of reviews say not to play alone, but forget about that. This game doesn’t make much sense playing co-op; only one person can control the characters. The co-op only works well during combat, and combat won’t even make up 10% of the total gameplay, so don’t worry if you don't have someone to play with. If you do, it’s still worth it because the character dynamics are very good and relatable. Yu and Kay are a well-written couple. The gameplay is super fluid and relaxing, with a fantastic OST playing throughout. We’ve got great characters, story, music, and gameplay here, so buy it now.

_childDocuments_.review: What an experience. Filled with the trials and celebrations of any relationship, Haven follows two star-crossed lovers lumecs away from our world, and let me tell you: what blooting good time.From repairing the Nest to fermenting appledews this fantastic world truly goes beyond what I thought I would ever need in an RPG: Fast-travel with an appropriate cost, fun and satisfying exploration, not to mention the "flow" of relationship and story plot dynamics are remarkably written and displayed with a flourish of cheesy and cringe-worthy cuteness.Felling a little down from battle? Rest. A lil snuggle will heal you right up! Still too injured to fend off a rusted Oink? Blast some flow or hit a stream and glide into the sky!  The semi-turn-based-real-time (?) battle sequences are reminiscent of a few of my favorite strategy games with even more infectious flair and addictive successes. Games are for a good time after all so the default difficulty is perfect! If you want to enjoy it even more, there is an easier play option that I cannot wait to explore. It leaves me begging for another dauntless duos to accompany as they too escape the clutches of the Matchmaker. Cannot wait for more!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! The relationship between the two main characters is beautifully developed, with dialogues that are often funny and even downright hilarious at times. While the world design isn't particularly standout, it serves its purpose well enough. The combat system takes some time to master but becomes rewarding once you do. The story is decent—nothing groundbreaking, but it keeps you engaged.This is the first game i played and finished it on my Legion Go, and it ran very well.Overall, I had a great time playing this. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Ya know, it's funny... if you map movie-genres onto games, you'll find that there's loads of Action Games, a fair few Comedy Games, the occasional Disaster Game... but Romance Games? That basically just translates as 'visual novel', which in my book barely qualifies as a game in the first place - they're more like digital choose-your-own-adventure books.Well, here's the missing link, then! Haven really cannot be called anything but a Romance - a love-story in game form, with love and relationships and all of their pitfalls being the alpha, omega, and everything in between. And, yes, it's still an actual GAME, with actual GAMEPLAY. A pretty original approach to it, too, with a combat-system that's built around the same themes as the story, requiring the leading couple to cooperate in all kinds of different ways to bring down their foes, while being virtually helpless on their own.Add to that the adventure of exploring a mysterious, alien planet, collecting materials for curatives and cooking, finding odds and ends to decorate your home base and unlock new events... it all adds up to a very satisfying gaming experience, all wrapped in an intensely emotional romantic tale. While I could quibble about how even the good ending seemed rather unsatisfying due to 'Endor Holocaust' logic - that is, pondering the consequences of the 'happy ending' that the story strategically leaves out - but a sequel could resolve that issue in due time. Honestly, I think that the biggest minus of this game is the unrealistic expectations it could give you for romantic relationships! Few real-life relationships could measure up to the one depicted in this game, so if you find yourself comparing your SO to either of the leads, you'd probably best stop right there... :P
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is a exploration focused game wrapped with a coherent and well done story in a world with enough lore to be believable. The art style is remarkably well done and shines in most of its uses within the game. Haven is definitely worth playing if you like story driven games with exploration. While Haven isn't a gem of a game, It is very close to being one.Pros:-Amazing art style-Well done story-You can pick the genders of the main characters ( its not perfect but its good overall)-Most of the games systems aren't annoying and most of them will naturally be used in a playthrough-Movement was fun when it worked well-Reasonable achievementsCons:-As much as I enjoyed the combat, I also really didn't feel like it fit in the game. It is really tedious and I found the auto battle mode right near the end. I was glad to see options to minimize combat difficulty as it made it so they weren’t suffering.-The gender swapping of characters was incomplete in some regards. Most things had it be invisible but some events, animations, or even pre-rendered cutscenes were jarring when they weren't adapted well. Instead of embracing that the main characters could be of any gender it felt like it was added on very late in development and not really used as well as it could have been. The masculine Yu felt like it just wasn’t fully completed and lacked differentiation that would make sense for the masculine version. Kay who is the default masculine character was really well done which made masculine Yu feel half done.-I wish there was access to the outfits system prior to endgame as it would have been a great exploration reward.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Haven... A beautifully made indie game where it focuses on the couple Kay & Yu. They escape their current lives to find a new planet, to focus on their relationship and to live a new lifestyle. You explore the planet to find edible food, find items to add to the ship. Further more, experiencing the new world in a rather romantic way among the characters. PROS- Amazing soundtrack.- Runs very well, had 0 crashing when playing.- The relationship between Kay and Yu feel natural, which I find rare in RPG's.- Dialogue throughout the game is written well.- Love the colour platelet for the game.- No half arsed voice acting.CONS- Wish it was a bit longer (personal opinion)- No mass crafting for food/itemsOverallPlayed the demo, instantly added to the wishlist. Picked it up recently and loved every moment of it. I hope the devs make more games similar to this because this truly was a one of a kind RPG. The game itself is rather simple to play and has a relaxing vibe with its soundtrack and banter with Kay & Yu, If you are looking for a relaxing RPG experience then I'd highly recommend Haven.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is the most amazing, beautiful, and heartwarming game I've encountered, Tbh I've seen for the first time the possibility to choose the gender of the main characters in that way, and I LOVE that, and I wish all games would provide that idea, especially for co-op games. _childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is a wonderful game that explores territory that not a whole lot of other games or even other media explore: the relationship between two lovers already in a relationship. It's very much a story and character based game, the gameplay of exploring islets and fighting off critters is solid, but mostly serves as a vehicle for character interactions and storytelling. This is not a bad thing, as these interactions are smartly written and helped by some great voice acting. I also have to give it props for the way it depicts their relationship: it's not all kissing and grand romantic gestures, it more focuses on the little things that keep their relationship going. It's about two people who definitely want to be together and are willing to put forth the effort to make that happen, even when things get tough. It's a comforting game, definitely worth checking out if you're looking for a story-based game.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: shuddup an buy it. its worth every penny, sale or not.while you're at it, get the soundtrack too. it comes in FLAC and MP3 formats, pre-organized in 2 folders. replay value here, measured in uniqueness.the uniqueness of this game means you'll not get the specific itch this game scratches, anywhere else.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much! The characters feel believable and the player is given a lot of control over how their relationship plays out on-screen. Most of the time it doesn't feel like you are watching Yu and Kay on-screen, but wholly immersed in their cutesy, quirky floating-island/islet planet escape lifestyle. There are optional items to find to further enhance their home lives and their combat and movement capabilities improve as you level up their relationship. This is done via discovering new things, recipes, places, interactions, etc.Playing solo was an interesting challenge for me due to having to control both characters at once in combat situations using the mirrored keyboard layout, (WASD vs. OKL;). I feel like I have learned a new gaming skill in mastering that as someone who tends to run away from anything even remotely turn-based and prefers to control one character at a time. It's not quite turn-based and note quite free combat either. It's more like ...hmmm... self-timed key presses to get desired results and coordination.I do wish there was free-play to enjoy after completing the main storyline, which would provide room for DLC (similar to the development model in Slime Rancher). I am taking my time to explore everything before playing the final stage, even though I know a save is kept before the point of no return.If I am ever lucky enough to find my significant other, I look forward to playing this game all over again in co-op mode with them.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cute game, featuring one of the best adult couples (gay or otherwise) that I know of. The two protagonists are practically acting like a married couple. They will have fights, but they talk things out. They will flirt with each other, but not every talk is flirty. (Though there are definitely times where you can steer conversations to that direction.) They aren't squeamish about sex, they embrace it as if it is normal. I just love that this relationship feels very real, which is very rare for video games. The music is very chill, somewhat low-fi, somewhat house, but very unique. It has about 1 and a half hours of this stuff for a 8-15 hour game. The game is also fully voice acted, and as of the last update, also includes 2 other couples which are fully voice acted as well.Gameplay wise, this game is fairly simple, but it does go through the paces of making things a little tougher. Though, for me, it kinda got easier towards the end. That may be because of a very OP healing ability, if you figure out how to abuse it. It can be a also be a bit awkward to control at times, particularly when gliding into a wall, which leads to characters turning around into another wall.That being said, there are two things that kinda brought the game down for me. The first is the frequent loading screens and the travels you sometimes need to do. While there is fast travel, getting back home is often not worth seeking out a fast travel spot, especially if you can't remember where they were.The second can be kinda considered spoiler so I'll only mention it briefly. The game feels like there should have been an Act 3 to the story, but it feels like that was cut. There were voice lines hinting towards it, and then it just kinda gets... dropped? This in particular hurts one of the two protagonists, who gets one thing near the end, which doesn't really get elaborated on. (Though maybe it was in some random events. I didn't do too many of those in the end as I didn't need to heal much.)Overall, I love this game, even with the flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I first discovered Haven when the demo dropped half a year or so ago, and immediately got hooked by its relaxing nature and interesting premise and gameplay, and am currently playing through the full game.So far, about 8 hours into the game, I really like it, and highly recommend it. It's a relaxing piece of game that has interesting characters and an interesting story, and while it's not a game I feel the need to play through as quickly as possible, it's none the less a game I feel that I'll play through to completion.I am glad that this game got made and that I have gotten the chance to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful little indy game with a magnificent soundtrack that just grows and grows on you. The story of Yu and Kay takes center stage whereas the overall plot is a bit more throwaway. You play this game for the character banter and interactions between our two love birds, and to see them as they work together to overcome any challenge that is put in front of them. The RPG battles are fun enough, but anyone looking for really in-depth mechanics or complex systems are not going to find them here.I'd say that this game really shines playing it co-op with a significant other. My wife and I have been playing through it as we have time (I think we are a little over halfway through it), and even though there are certain things that only one player can do at a time, its never been a problem with us as sharing is one of the core concepts of any relationship <3. It's really nice to play a game where the relationship is already established, and you are playing out life as a couple, hearing them love each other, disagree with each other, and everything in-between is a refreshing take apart from most other games. Each character has their strengths and weaknesses, likes and dislikes, but they compliment each other well and show how to support each other and make their partner stronger in a very healthy way.I'd say if you have a special someone to play this with its an easy recommend, if you were thinking of playing this solo, i'd personally wait until you do. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, relaxing game about 2 lovers. Gathering resources, crafting, some semi jrpg-like fights and many cool dialogues. You will mainly fly across isles and it's like I said relaxing - at least for me. Voice acting is excellent (you can feel the mood!), music - nice, melodic (I'm about to buy the soundtrack), I adore the relationship between Kay and Yu (they argue, love and laugh with each other - sounds like a classic romantic story but I like their characters and how different they are). Story is simple - lovers want to be together so they run away ;) (it's not spoiler!) Play if you like romance, relaxing gameplay and manga-looking like character are not bothering you.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: What if SuperGiantGames was french?Because thats the feeling im getting with the GameBakers, at just two games I know that im getting a good story, memorable music, intriguing characters, worlds that are familiar but also alien and surprises full of color.I dont know if either would take offense at the comparison but both of their games really do carry a similar feel, I cant say this game is for everyone but Yu and Kay´s relationship does the heavy lifting for this and it makes other RPGs that have romance look anemyc by comparison.Danger really outdid it this time, the soundtrack is absolutely amazing and the gameplay loop while simple is adicting.It definately is worth a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: How can I say this without sounding too wordy? I LOVE this game. I love this world. This has been one of the best 2-player purchases I've made. It's only got one tie up at the top with it.I bought this for myself and my partner, and playing it together has been one of - if not the - best gaming experience/s I've had. The gameplay itself can get a little bit boring for the person not steering (or someone with bad directional/navigational skills like me), but the overwhelmingly staggering amount of positives I feel this game has bypasses that.I love Kay and Yu. Both independently and together. The fact that the devs portrayed an adult relationship while both straying away from actually showing anything explicit, but also having such a thin veil of "horny for each other" that the veil is just clear? Chef's kiss. I love it. 100/10I loved that we were just thrown into the world, and that we discovered more about it through conversations. And speaking of conversations! There were so many! There is still so much that I know we missed! I'm looking forward to replaying it and taking more time to sleep and eat, both in and out of the home, to get them all!The world itself is beautiful and more than just "interesting". I would love to know more about it. I would love to enter the world of the Apiary as another pair of lovers leading a revolution, inspired by Kay and Yu. Leading an escape and maybe manually mapping a way to Source through old-world kind of travel.  Maybe a different planet. Seeing the ramifications of what happened  There are so many possibilities for what can be going on in the Apiary, I feel.I'm already getting too wordy but three last praises I'd like to leave and dip:-The music is outstanding. Hell give it a listen on its own! It's incredible-The combat can be frustrating with  or if you run into multiple enemies with knockbacks that decided today is just your day to stay down. But other than those two instances, it's great. It's like [hold to do a thing]. Some enemies have weaknesses. You can synch attacks with your partner for more damage. Just, the mechanics of it are fun.-The graphics are stylized and colorful. I mean you see them above. It's not gonna be everyone's style I think, but I personally love them. Very cute and charming.Overall, I would highly  recommend this, especially to anyone looking to play with a partner.

The combat controls have stupid timing for no good reason and is so boring I almost fell asleep a few times.The voice acting is top notch and story may be good, if you can manage to stick with it. _childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is a third person adventure game about love. You play as Kay and Yu, a couple that has fled the obligations of an authoritarian society, and, stranded on a remote and desolate planet, they enjoy their time together eventually realising that they are living on borrowed time. As you explore a large number of floating islands connected through various so called flow bridges you encounter creatures corrupted by a strange force. Combat is a hybrid system stuck somewhere between realtime and round based action that is unfortunately more of a chore and at times unresponsive. Nevertheless, if you play this game you are here for the story. Exploration is necessary if you want to experience all the interactions in the game. As mentioned above you follow an ongoing romantic relationship without the normally mandatory drama. The only thing that bothered me was the ending. I would have wished the writers had had more courage ending the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I have only one word to describe this game, The story, The cut scenes, The art style, The world, The Voice Acting, I have never written a review for a game before, like ever. But Haven is just that good. Easily my favourite game of 2020.The story follows the adventures of an adult couple in love, and portrays this so well. From tender moments to misunderstandings and fights, all of it well written and beautifully acted. Combat is fun, but complicated playing single player, I'm sure playing co-op with good communication would have been better, but it was definitely not a drawback what-so-ever.I recommend it, 100%, whole heartedly, enough to leave a review.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: So this is not a AAA game, what is it is a game with a lot of heart. You play as a couple who have run from a tyrannical regime  to be together. The combat is a bit weird, but pretty easy once you get the handle on it and the exploration is simple but fun. The art style is a cell shaded style which makes the game look pretty nice at all times. The two things that really separate this game from the rest is the sound track and the characters chemistry.  The soundtrack is created by Danger an it is amaaaaaaaazing. The different songs hit every moment right, whether you're flying across an islet or staring up on the stars. Like genuinely do yourself a favour and go and buy the sound track if nothing else.Next are the character and boy are they done well. What really separates  Kay and Yu from every other romantic pair in video game history is that they are REAL. And what I mean by that is their relationship is real, it's not all sunshine and rainbows. They fight, they argue, they make up. Like any real relationship and that makes it all the more endearing. They're a bunch of kids who held hands, took a leap of faith together and are finding out the rest along the way, which really is what most relationships are. Their moments are heartwarming and you can tell they really love each other and that's not an experience you want to miss.So all in all, for a very well priced games, do yourself a favour and buy it to add a bit more brightness in your life. Load it up and find your Haven.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just difficult enough that you feel like you're accomplishing something, but you can still focus primarily on exploration and building the story. The graphics are gorgeous and the story is so adorable. The content is definitely adult-centered but there is not any direct sexual content. I highly highly highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: barely a co-op game, it really shouldn't be labeled as such. player 2 does absolutely nothing, its one of those games where your mom gets mad at you because you wont play games with your little brother, so you play this and hand him the controller, knowing his inputs 100% are arbitrary. story seems... somewhat interesting? but they just throw you so many terms and words at you that it's difficult to keep track of, I understand the point is that you have to speculate what all of the lore means, but It's hard to care when there's so many things thrown at you. other than that, the writing for the main characters are pretty cute, and they do have pretty good chemistry together. the gameplay loop is really boring, go to place, explore the same looking areas, fight boring mobs, clear the area, unlock fast travel. it doesn't help that the combat is extremely dull, fighting mobs feels like a chore, you can speed the battles and completely skip them entirely, but its like... why? the battles are supposed to be a break from the monotony of exploring. the only time the battles are enjoyable is during boss fights, I had to actually use my brain and strategize with my friend who was on player 2.I can only really recommend this if you plan on playing this by yourself, it's on sale, and have some time to burn. If you're looking for a game to play with your partner or a friend, I really can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I found the game really enjoyable. The characters relationship is very sweet and filled with lots of cute moments, and the plot was genuinely interesting, and the areas are fun to explore. It's not a hard game, the combat is mostly pretty simple (though it is a bit more complex than it seems at first), resource management and crafting are important, but it's never particularly hard to fine enough materials for crafting, but the system is complex enough to be entertaining for most of the game. I finished it in about 15 hours so by the time I felt like the the game mechanics started to get predictable I was over 2/3's of the way through the game, and the plot had really hooked me by then.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: At first, this game seemed boring and not very good. The way of traversing the map felt uncomfortable, and playing it coop didn't really make it any more fun. Then I started playing by myself, and as I unlocked more skills that made manouvering easier, as well as a map, I started enjoying the game much more. It is by no means perfect, but I found it pretty enjoyable once I got past that first hour or two.I ended up finishing the game and enjoyed it very much. I grew fond of the characters, got involved in the story, and felt satisfied when finishing it.If, like me, you got attracted to this game because of its original approach to relationships, artstyle and story, I recommend that you have patience because it eventually pays off.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: The games soundtrack is pretty swag, The writing is pretty neat/cute. The game works better in singleplayer but Coop/remote play is just as fun. I really enjoyed it. In terms of art style its the same as Furi but that's where the comparisons end. Both are completely different games. I enjoyed both :) <3 (:
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game with my non-gamer girlfriend, and we both absolutely loved it.It's perfectly designed to be played in co-op, and in a way where a more "pro" player can effectively assist and manage to make the experience more pleasant to an inexperienced partner. My girlfriend had trouble even with the simple 3D movements, and the combat timings were initially very hard for her; however I was able to support and move the game forward by taking more often the lead, until when she got more proficient and became essential in the later game fights. Overall, it felt like the game was designed exactly to be experienced as we did. I certainly would not have enjoyed it as much if I were to play it alone, as the combat is really quite simple, and in general every action in the game becomes more meaningful when played with another one. The mistakes, the divergences in the fighting strategies, the indecisions about what to explore first, or what to say, or what to cook... Every small thing is there to make you talk to your partner and share things with them.The plot is interesting; not too deep but always enjoyable and well narrated. The music and graphics are very pleasant too. It stays there in my top 5 games for 2020, and well up in it. If you have someone, especially a significant other that is open minded enough to give videogames a try, definitely go for this.

_childDocuments_.review: =================================================((( PROBLEMS FIXED!!! PRODUCT IS NOW RECOMMENDED!!! )))   =================================================Please rate this review so it stays on the front page so others can see what a good job the devs are doing. Within a week of reviews the problems were almost all fixed and this review will disappear without reviews so please would you kindly ;)DEV REPLY: THANK YOU!! YOU'RE FIXING IT!! I'm almost certain I wasn't running into that bug because we were definitely playing with two controllers, but I just tried it again and it seems like the suggestions that were given in my review were taken to heart and it is now playable :winter2019joyfultearsbulb:- The camera zooms out now to keep both characters on screen, the camera in general is more zoomed out which is a very welcome alteration it still has some issues where the aforementioned problems with the camera crop up, but it is *significantly* better than it was before- When the character not controlling the camera appears off screen, they are given an extremely quick speed boost to get back near the other character and actually stay reasonably close to each other now. Still have some issues where they don't always catch up very quickly and lag off-screen for 5-10 seconds, but again, markedly better than beforeThe only thing now is please allow the controls to be rebound to any button/key and I'll be a very happy camper, please especially the down on the analog stick for u-turn... it gets accidently pressed SOOO often..... Thank you for working on fixing things it's great to see devs like this! Just a little more tweaking and I think this will be flawless! I hope this still gets seen as proof that these devs listen and respect the ideas and wishes of their customers and players and want to do right and good by them. *********************************************************************************************************Original Review Below: (( NOT RECOMMENDED ))I really, really want to love this game. I don't even write reviews, but I felt that this deserved one because I want to love it so bad but it has such a huge problem with it that I hope the dev's see it and implement some fix. From what I feel, this game should have been made with the co-op in mind FIRST and the single player would be an after-thought, but unfortunately, the game is mind-bogglingly and bizarrely built the other way around.The art is phenomenal, the story is great, the concept is fantastic, it's a perfect little couch game that you can play with your SO and have a nice little cute time together relaxing and playing through a game together.BUT...The co-op integration is absolutely awful. The camera is so bad it is nauseating if you are both trying to control it. The worst part is the controls are both hooked up to basically both controllers, so you end up either A) fighting over the controls and it ends up being a nauseating mess where both charaters end up flying all over the place getting nowhere, or B) you resign to the fact that only one person will be allowed to use the camera in order for it to be remotely playable. However, this leads to an even bigger problem. It is IMPOSSIBLE for the other player to control their character when the other is manipulating the camera or the glide mechanic. I hate to say this but, this is hands-down the worst implementation of a co-op camera in any game I have ever played, and I've played a LOT of co-op games. It comes down to whoever the second player is, who is not in control of the camera (because of aforementioned reasons) if they get behind the "main" player in the slightest bit, they get blown off screen and it becomes near impossible to get back on. There are no catch-up speed boost mechanics, there is no off-screen indicator for where your character is, no information at all. They just disappear off screen for 10-15 seconds and then only after you fly in one direction and don't move do they slowly come back into frame, and ONLY if that person completely let go of their controls.Speaking of controls, some of them are bound to just ridiculous buttons. Seriously? U-turn is set to DOWN on the d-pad? So guess what happens, if you turn one single degree past left or right then it triggers a down input and you end up doing a u-turn which whips the camera around extremely fast and awkwardly. Even worse, you CANNOT REBIND MOST CONTROLS!! How can any dev these days not allow every single control to be rebound?? GIVE PLAYERS OPTIONS!!All in all, this game could be easily fixed so clearly with just a few simple optional toggles. Like a keep both characters in frame at all times camera toggle, or engage split screen when characters get too far, or option to show an off screen indicator to where your other character is, things like this would be so easy to implement and add so much to the experience. Please devs if you read this please implement one or more of these options it would make the experience vastly better and more enjoyable.Without going on for much longer, it really is a shame this game has such terrible coop camera/controls. There is no way to even move the camera while you are gliding without changing which direction you are going, because your forward direction is tied to the camera facing and not always the character facing. If the camera was independent of the movement and/or had a much, MUCH wider field of view or at the very least zoomed out to keep both characters on screen at once that would be all this game needs to shine and be fixed. I just can't recommend this game because it deserves to be played co-op, and right now it just isn't working, at all.TLDR:: If you want to play this by yourself, it works great. No problems whatsoever. If you're buying it for the coop, the camera and coop controls are so bad it is unplayable. This game has such an alluring story that will make you feel such love and affection and the voice acting and general style and feel is so amazing but unfortunately it is crippled by mood-ruining frustrations and lack of options that overall just make the game a muddy mess of feelings.Devs, please fix. I want to experience this the way it deserves to be. x

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics and music. The characters are fine enough for the story the developers were going for and to me seemed realistic. Battle system is simple enough and this game does fine with multiplayer. Also the hug and the hand holding and other minor actions are just too cute. It's a simple and predictable game but I don't think it was trying to be anything that unique honestly and that's fine. I played this with single player but did play with my partner as well and it runs fairly decent once we know the mechanics haha.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: The reason I only have a couple hours is because I played most of the game through, erm, other means but I decided to buy it to support the developers. Does it have the best gameplay? Not really. Revolutionary graphics? Nope. But it doesn't need to. It's a lovely game whose themes are almost never explored in depth in video games. Relationships are usually an afterthought in games but here it is the central focus of the story and gameplay to an extent. Yu isn't the main character and neither is Kay, the both of them and their relationship are. Like I said it's a theme that is cruelly underutilized in video games and I wish there were more games like this.If you're planning to play with a friend or even better your significant other, I don't suggest you play the co-op mode. Rather, you can just pass the controller to eachother and choose the dialogue options together. The simplicity of the gameplay means your partner doesn't even need to be very good at video games, and there aren't many consequences to failing.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: This game hit home. The conversation choices don't always fit, there's some typos in the subtitles, and the camera can freak out sometimes... But I don't care, because this game is just so good. I played with my girlfriend, and it was a really nice bonding experience. And a really fun game on top of that. The gameplay loop is satisfying, has good pacing, and good mechanics. The story is decent and flows well. Controls mostly make sense, and take little adjusting to. The music is amazing, but I wish there was more of it! There's not enough of this awesome music! Sound effects are great, too. Art style is subjective, but we enjoyed it very much.Dialogue is imperfect, but it does a good job of conveying a relationship that needs work. Putting that work in is satisfying, and shows development between the two characters, together and individually. Their tones, moods, and attitudes are well-portrayed most of the time, and the voice acting is killer!We particularly liked how realistic and natural their interactions felt. Depicting a meaningful relationship between people is hard in games and movies, but this game nailed it in my opinion. Oh, and uh, fair warning... The flirting and implied s*xual interactions might not be stream-safe. The amount of times we looked at the camera and went "hi, Twitch Admins... >.>" was pretty frequent toward the later half of the game. The flirting and playfulness of the Yu and Kay is great, but Twitch might disagree. Great game! It's one I wish I could have helped develop it!Great systems, great atmosphere, great characters, great music. Great deal. Get this game and play with someone you like spending time with. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)I just recently finished Haven and I am being completely honest when I say that it was one of the most enjoyable gaming experiences I've had in a long time. Admittedly, this is primarily due to the Couples Update, so I'm pretty happy that I waited so long to play it. For those that don't know, the Couples Update makes queer relationships possible and this made my insatiable lesbian heart really happy. The level of care that Game Bakers put into that update was incredible and I'm truly thankful that they didn't just slap something together and throw it out there. The story itself is fairly simple. You play as a couple, Yu and Kay, that have fled their homeworld to elope and end up landing on another planet, only to be stranded when an earthquake damages their ship. What unfolds afterwards is, simply put, an extremely fluffy romance novel in the form of a video game. You do explore and enter into battles, but there is no overt challenge to the game that requires grinding or anything of the sort. It's essentially witnessing the love that these two women (in my case) have for each other and it was SUCH a relief to see a sapphic love story portrayed like this.What made it even better is that Game Bakers didn't skimp on the voice acting. Haven had solid voice actresses that made the already fantastic dialogue feel very natural. Everything just felt so well done. The game is definitely not for everyone, though. Those who enjoy a challenge will not find that itch satisfied with Haven's pretty simplistic battle system and those who aren't fond of a sappy romance certainly won't like it either, but if those things don't bother you, there is enough here for me to fully recommend it. I picked Haven up on sale, but all the swoons, giggles, and kicks of my feet that this game provided me with more than make up for the full $25 pricetag.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! I wasn't expecting to want to play again, but I finished a playthrough with Yu and Kay both set to women and now I'm playing again with them as men. The environments were beautiful, although they did get a little same-y at times, as was the music. The creature design was also wonderful. The romantic aspect was cute - I love games with characters interacting with each other so much, and the conversation between the two was really nice. It worked seamlessly with the gameplay, too. I definitely recommend this game if you're looking for something relaxing but still engaging, and also something gay.

_childDocuments_.review: In Haven you play as Yu and Kay. They are a pair of star crossed lovers fleeing an oppressive government called The Apiary, who have crash landed on the broken paradise of a planet called Source. Your wrecked ship, called The Nest, serves as your base of operations, which you set out from to explore the planet. Soon you discover that our protagonists aren't the first to arrive on Source and they encounter a goopy, crystal like cranberry colored substance called Rust. Rust is negatively effecting the local flora and fauna. It then becomes your mission to clean it up and collect this stuff, not just to help the planet and it's weirdly adorable animals, but because Yu realizes she can use it to help fix the ship. You collect Rust by gliding over it. Gliding around the environments is how you navigate them via these blue lines called flow lines. It's akin to grinding a rail in a game like Jet Set Radio, or Tony Hawk's Pro Skater. It's fun, but not very deep, or engaging, which is about what can be said for the combat system as well.You enter combat by touching a Rust infected animal. Combat is turn based, but not in a traditional sense. Enemies can attack you while you are taking your turn, or charging up an attack. You have few options in combat. There is Blast, which fires a Ki type blast from your hand at the enemy and Impact, which has you physically hit your opponent. Certain types of enemies are weak to one ,or the other type of attack, while later enemies will switch their weakness back and forth between the two. You also have the option of shielding, which puts one character on guard duty to negate incoming attacks. The combat isn't challenging though and I found myself rarely using this function. Later in the game you gain the ability to craft items that act like super powered attacks and AOE attacks. However, you can only carry 5 of each on you at a time, which makes them super limiting and more for situational usage than anything. You can also combine Yu and Kay's attacks into dual attacks for an even bigger hit, but at the expense of being vulnerable. There are higher levels of the combined attacks you get as you level up in your relationship, but to access them you have to charge the attack for a much longer period of time, which leaves you increasingly vulnerable. On top of this the window for striking an enemy when they are dazed, or vulnerable is extremely small. I was never able to line up that window with a big charged attack. It always took longer to charge the attack than the window allowed, which taught me to never use those attacks. It's almost always better to use the basic attacks, or maybe a level 1 charged dual attack than to go for a level 2 charge and try to inflict big damage. You inflict massive damage if you do manage to hit an enemy when they are vulnerable anyway, which just leaves the higher level attacks feeling meaningless. When an enemy is defeated it will fall down and then you can purify it, but if you aren't quick enough do so after it's down, it'll heal and reenter the fight. Some enemies have incredibly small windows to purify them, which can make for quite the frustrating time. Source is beautiful, but also very empty. Rather than have one big interconnected map, the game world is a grid of these tiny floating islands, which all feel very much same. Other than a few land marks and their color there isn't much to differentiate them. You do the same thing on each one. You float around, collecting rust and beating up critters to purify them. Occasionally, you will encounter scrap that can be used to fix your ship, or an interactive building, but these are far too few and far between. Even worse, the buildings our heroes can enter aren't playable spaces. Yu and Kay go in the building and the player is left outside to read a dialogue exchange about all the cool stuff inside that we are missing out on. This is a hugely wasted opportunity, as exploring these spaces would have been the perfect vehicle for players to learn about the people and cultures that make up this beautiful world. There is a crafting system in the game as well, but it's equally shallow. As you explore Source, you can collect about half a dozen different plants and combine two of them at a time into medicine, or food. You can cook at a campsite or in your ship. Cooking at a campsite only allows you use half the ingredients, even if you've collected the other plants and have them on hand. You can cook different things at camp than you can on the ship. So there is quite a wide variety of dishes to make, but unfortunately you can only eat them when camping or back in The Nest, which is frustrating since food is a primary source of healing. If you have eaten recently, but need to heal, the game will not let you eat to restore your health. You will have to use medicine. Also, the food you can cook in the Nest is better in every way than the food you can cook at camp. Since you can bring food with you when you go out exploring cooking at camp feels pointless. Haven has all of these great systems, but they are all extremely shallow and basic. They never deepen, or evolve into anything meaningful, or form a cohesive whole. What you experience in the first hour of the game is really all that there is for the gameplay. It's not bad by any stretch, but it's not good either. For this reason Haven is not a game that can be recommended for it's gameplay. However, it is a game that can be easily recommended for it's narrative.In stark contrast to the gameplay, Haven's narrative portions are deep and engaging. The narrative is told through dialogue sequences that play like something out of a visual novel. The characters of Yu and Kay are masterfully done, well voice acted, likeable, relatable and endearing. Thanks to the couples update you can also choose if they are a gay/lesbian couple in addition to the stock straight couple for even better representation and freedom. Much of your time with our heroes is spent in the Nest, which you navigate in first person mode while Kay and Yu lounge around at the different stations. The Nest is chock full of tiny details about their life and adventures together from before they arrived on Source. You can add to this as you grow and deepen your bond as a couple on Source, which is really cool. These little easter eggs change depending on which Kay and Yu couple you choose, which is a nice touch. The narrative of their relationship goes beyond just them into deeper territory regarding relationships in general. I found myself laughing out loud at many of their interactions as a couple, such as the shower not draining, because it's clogged with Yu's long hair, or going through a spicy picture book in an attempt to liven up the bedroom, or commenting on each others quirks, because it's so human. It's almost therapeutic in way, because of how human and relatable these things are since everyone whose been in a relationship has encountered these things at some point, which is what makes Yu and Kay so relatable and likable. It instantly puts the player on their side. For the nearly 17 hours it took me to finish Haven, I was glued to the story and couldn't wait to see what was going to happen next. The soundtrack is also incredible and does a killer job of establishing the mood in every scene.  I did not enjoy either of the two possible endings for reasons I can't discuss here, because of spoilers. However that didn't dampen my overall enjoyment of the game. If you're in the market for a great story in a pretty world and can overlook the lackluster gameplay then Haven is sure to delight.

_childDocuments_.review: A very laid back explorative RPG about two lovers fleeing to a distant planet to escape an unjust matchmaking ceremony. The more slice of life elements are a lot of fun, Yu and Kay are adorable together and have impeccable chemistry, and the game does a great job of building a vision of it's greater universe without ever actually showing it. Can be played solo or in co-op with a loved one.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. The story is engaging, the characters are endearing, and the writing is generally clever and well-done. The gameplay gets a little samey after a while, especially exploring all the islets, but the game's not so long that it really drags.The combat works; splitting your attention between the characters may take some getting used to if you're playing single-player but it never gets particularly challenging. You get more experience from domestic interactions and cutscenes than from combat so don't forsake milling about in the nest. You get unique interactions from camping so do that, too.I love the option for different character genders. It's nice to have some lgbtq+ content that focuses on the relationship but isn't a visual novel. If you like romance that doesn't skimp on the fluff or the drama, this game definitely delivers.[Talking about the ending here but I won't explicitly spoil anything]I really hope this game gets a sequel, not just because I've grown attached to the characters but because the ending is kinda bland and leaves some interesting threads untied. That said, I suspect there may be at least one other ending than the one I've got so maybe my opinion will change.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic romantic sci-fi RPG with a perfect soundtrack that explores some deep themes about love, dedication, individual autonomy, and society. Has lots of funny, lighter moments too. Combat is a bit janky, but this is only an annoyance in a few boss fights and even here the concept of coordinating the two characters is fresh and interesting even if the execution could have used a little work (why no targeting selection?). Flying around on Source with the jet boots collecting flow and rust is too much fun to be called gimmicky. The opening animation seems slightly out of place at first, BUT actually adds a lot; watch it, then watch it again after finishing the game and understanding the universe it takes place in better.
