_childDocuments_.review: Main selling point of the game is extremely buggy or just very poorly designed, at least with my experience using Steam's Remote Play.Co-op just straight up doesn't work if you have the control scheme as Two Controllers. Partner's controller isn't recognised at all. Works with all other games so it's not the controller or steam's controller support.Switching the mode to Keyboard and Controller, forces the game into Co-Op mode with no way to turn it off other than to return the Co-Op control scheme back to Two Controllers, attempts to turn it off via down on the d-pad just results in it automatically turning back on when the player moves the character. In the Keyboard/Controller Co-Op Scheme the controller only controls the male character and the keyboard only controls the female with no way to switch between them.The Co-Op option in the title screen, states that you require two controllers to be plugged in and while this is expected with local play I suspect it may be a requirement for remote play as well, given that the only input it recognises is what is currently plugged in to the host player's set up.Currently the control scheme works as if sharing a setup. If I use the keyboard (under the Keyboard/Controller set up) my partner cannot play at all since his controller isn't recognised.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply incredible experience. The game is not for everyone and there are some faults with a relatively simple combat system and tricky controls, I will admit that, but it is also an incredibly unique game that will resonate very well with a lot of people. It is hard to put into words how the game made me feel, it just needs to be experienced. It is by far my Game of the Year, and additionally my favorite of all time. I am sad it's over, but I know it will always have a special place in my heart and I will be revisiting it for years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Option to play as lesbian couple, gay male couple, or straight couple is perfect. Bravo. Lovely story.Excellent characters with a really sweet, believable relationship. Voice-acting is on point for all characters. It's good to see a game that normalizes sex (not explicit) & flirting between characters who are in love.It has a really high cut-scene to gameplay ratio, so you don't feel like you're stuck grinding like a lot of rpg games. It makes the characters feel real. Unique gameplay. Flying is fun!Cons:Combat isn't explained. Even when I understood combat, I didn't love it. No option to change difficulty without restarting.Conversation choices don't have consequences. I'm someone who likes to make the "good" choices in games, and restarted Haven several times because the initial conversation kept ending badly no matter what I said. I realized that only small reactions and insignificant details can be affected, but all conversations will end on one script. Overall, I loved this game. It's short, story-focused and memorable, and I'd love to see a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: The adventures of two space disaster lesbians and their lizard child!I love them all and would commit multiple felonies for them.I don't usually write serious reviews, but the game really connected with me emotionally so I feel I should do so for once. Haven is a very enjoyable game about a couple and their ups and downs. It's very chill and enjoyable to fly around cleaning up toxic waste, and collecting flow threads (an activity you'll be doing a lot of) is very lenient on you like 95% of the time... though there are one or two I've found that are a little rough. The combat can get a little hectic if you're going for a "pacify all" in every battle but even then they have an optional relaxed difficulty setting if you want to use it.I found Kay and Yu to be charming and quite fun as characters, and the VAs did some very nice work with the script. I also have to admit, there are some scenes which I found enjoyably spicy! It comes across pretty well that these are a couple of flawed people who are very much in love with each other. Overall it's a game I'd very much recommend to most people.Semi-spoilerish territory begins below.The "good" ending was fairly satisfying, and leaves room (and hope) for a sequel at some future point. The bad one, though... if you're at all sensitive to some of the darker themes that are hinted at during the story such as "recalibration," I'd highly recommend not getting it, even if you're a completionist... it's kind of heartbreaking as someone who's spent hours getting to know and like these two characters.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice game if you are on a "romantic streak" and want to go beyond Visual Novels for that particular thingy.The entire narrative experience is pretty good, with a few hiccups, but overall a comfy relationship to see developing. On the gameplay side tho, it suffers a bit, if we just focus on Turn Based Combat - You are constantly interrupted while attacking, without any well thought out visual aids (besides the red glares from the enemies), if you want to implement a system like this, i would say the combat would benefit from looking how games like Grandia and Shin Megami Tensei handles that particular aspect. Pretty good, i recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: An impressive deviation from Furi, but a flawed one at that.The Game Bakers impressed pretty much everyone with their last release, Furi, a pretty damn hard boss rush game with incredibly intense gameplay and tight controls. Haven is pretty much the inverse of that. Here, we are much less concerned with combat, and much more worried about exploration and character development. Furi's story was pretty barebones, and could be ignored for the most part, while Haven's story takes center stage for the majority of the adventure and controls feel a lot less polished. This isn't necessarily a bad thing, although you wouldn't be blamed for feeling that this a step down from how tightly designed Furi was.Haven does arguably look better than its predecessor though, and the world looks as beautiful as it is dangerous. Kay and Yu's character designs are just great, and each of the creatures that you'll find roaming around Source are visually interesting and help the planet feel alive. I spent a lot of my playthrough climbing to the highest points on these segmented playgrounds that make up Haven's overworld, and would often appreciate the views that the game rewarded me with. The day/night cycle also presents a lot of visual variety in each of the different areas, and also helped break up the games pace by forcing you to return to the next and sleep after exploring all day. The only complaint visually is that character animations could sometimes feel a little stiff, and rewatching the same animations during crafting and combat got old pretty fast. Luckily, the story here is pretty good, and the world building is some of the most natural I've seen in a video game. Maybe I'm just impressed after playing through MGS4 that a game managed to build so much lore about it's world without any 20 minute long exposition dumps, but for how much we learn about the Apiary and Kay + Yu's struggles through natural dialogue feels really impressive. It's incredibly naturalistic story telling, and none of the plot points ever felt forced. There's lot to infer about what we don't see about Haven's world, which is perhaps what The Game Bakers are best at. Somehow, they've made Tell, Don't Show work for their stories. Kay and Yu's relationship is also super well developed, and is only showcased more with incredible vocal performances from Janine Harouni and Chris Lew Kum Hoi. Both play the parts incredibly well, and it made the relationship between the two feel much more natural than what you would expect from an Indie game. Kay and Yu's journey keeps you much more emotionally invested as a result, and makes you really want to see the story through to the end. The only complaint is that the ending to their story feels a little abrupt, and perhaps inconclusive to many of the questions posed by the game's narrative, but at the very least it is absolutely worth the journey there.Haven's gameplay however, could've used some more work. The majority of the gameplay loop here is exploring Source looking parts to repair the Nest. Along the way you'll clean "Rust" off the planet, collect materials for crafting/cooking, and do some light RPG combat. It sounds fine in theory, but Haven's systems just aren't deep enough to keep the game engaging for the full length of the story. A lot of time is spent aimlessly gliding around the planet gathering rust and other materials, and it just simply isn't that engaging past the first few hours. Plants are just placed in seemingly random spots in the landscape so it's not like it is hard to find them, and unless you are going for the 100% islet cleaning achievement there's virtually no reason to continue collecting rust once you are two thirds of the way through the game. If there was a bit more of a survival aspect to Haven's exploration it could go a long way towards making the minute-to-minute gameplay more engaging. Fortunately, Haven does sport a pretty fun combat system, albeit very simple. You control both Kay and Yu at the same time while charging up different attacks against the enemies you face. It's a much more timing focused version of your usual JRPG turn based combat, and pulling off combos feels pretty great. It is perhaps a bit too easy at certain points, but it works well enough for the pace of the game. The crown jewel of Haven though, has to be it's incredible Soundtrack by DANGER, who also worked on some of the tracks from Furi. This soundtrack is absolutely incredible, one of the best I've heard in a videogame in quite some time and seems to get better with every listen. Danger perfectly captures the tone and feel of the story with his electronic beats, and the ending theme to the game is one of my favorite tracks from any game ever. The soundtrack is so good that is actually carries you through the monotony of gliding around Source, and lifts the overall experience that much more. Overall, Haven is a little rough around the edges. The unengaging exploration that takes up the majority of your game time and the unsatisfying ending sour the experience, but the characters and story are more than strong enough to carry your time through, and the combat system is surprisingly engaging for how shallow it is. If all else fails you'll at least hear some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome music during your time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is the latest game from The Game Bakers (the studio behind the critical acclaimed fast paced action game ‘Furi’). Haven is the game that detach itself from the intense fighting gameplay into more relax RPG-open world gameplay. A player will take a control of Kay and Yu, a couple who escaped together from 1984-esq dystopian planet to the seemingly deserted planet called ‘Source’, and it’s up to you to guide them to survive and get over any obstacle and reveal the mystery around Source.1.	Characters/Voice ActingWith game’s primarily focus on relationship between these 2 characters, if their chemistry was off, it could break the player’s immersion into the game. Thankfully it wasn’t. The Voice actors portrayed the nuance and style of those character so well with bits of unique personality, help creating an experience for player to spend time to progress the story further.2.	StoryFor short: While it’s not groundbreaking or bring anything new to explore behind the theme of love or freedom, it does its job pretty well and really emphasizes that ‘Every choice has a consequence’ and leave room of thought for players whether which choice is really ‘justified’ for each their own.For some of my insightful thought (SPOILER): 3.	GameplayAs I mention it is a RPG-open world genre game, plus the element of survival. The main gameplay aspect of this game is about exploring the planet to find a resource (food, medicine), fighting a monster that seemingly aggressive by something, and uncovering the mystery of this planet. The combat gameplay is quite unique as you have to rely your skill on timing action of both character (which means you have to control both characters if you playing solo). It might take a while to get used to this gameplay but I don’t have a problem with this gameplay. There is also an element of visual novel in this game where you have to choose a dialogue in certain parts. Some give you hilarious one, some give you a lightly cringey one, and some might make an impact to the story-wise. These make characters more lively and give you and an insight about characters’ backstory.Also, I love the gliding gameplay in this game. it gives you a sense of freedom and so fun to glide around the planet.1.	MusicDon’t get me wrong, I still love Danger’s musical style in both Furi and Haven (especially near the end of game, almost get me a tear). I just wish a more diverse music style in the game. if the artist added a more slow beat song in some dramatic scene, it would work a lot more better. It’s just my opinion.1.	ReplayabilityThe game has straight linear storytelling which means that there is not much you can do after finishing game on the first run. It’s a single time playing experience (unless you determine to discover all the secret in Source or complete all the achievement). Sure, the game doesn’t over stay its welcome, but with the chemistry of both characters that is so good, I wish there would be more story to play a little more. Some DLC might satisfy more, perhaps?2.	Some minor inconvenienceWhile there aren’t any bugs I found. There are some backtrackings you might have to go through and you don’t have a map at the starting point. You have to remember the path carefully or you might spend more time to search the way back to home until you get the map later in the game. A little inconvenience but acceptable.	Although Haven is not a groundbreaking or innovative game, but it still does a pretty good job at examine the theme of love and freedom through a relationship of 2 likable and charming characters. With variety of gameplay for unique combat, survive, and exploring the world aspects, the game will sure give you an unforgettably experience of playing this game that won’t be wash away by the waves of time too soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven has its ups and downs, sometimes I really enjoyed it and sometimes I was a little bored. The game itself doesn't feel like anything incredible or outlandishly impressive in any one regard, but the angle it takes on things is new, and refreshing. The negative bits I had to nitpick largely stopped when I stopped trying to be a completionist about clearing all the rust, getting all the collectibles, etc. I think 'just do what you want to do and screw all the rest' is a good mindset to have with this one.I think there's something to be said about the devs making the game to the best of their ability, because I can tell there was a lot of love put into the whole experience, and I think that makes it easy for me to look over the parts that I didn't like, and just think of all the fond parts instead. It didn't change my life or anything like that, but i'm happy I got to experience it, whereas most other games I play nowadays are more like, 'oh yeah, I did that, that was fun'.Haven is a game from the heart, and it'll stay in mine.

_childDocuments_.review: Some children inherit the best strands of their genetic source and manifest profound beauty, even if their parents are rather plain. This is exactly the opposite of what Haven is like. It's the horribly ugly child of JRPGs, visual novels, and open-world exploration; it takes the worst elements of these (over-dramatic story, clumsy turn-based combat system, lazy art-style, dysfunctional item management, vapid dialogue branches and an empty world) and provides nothing to counter-balance them. As for the supposed romance, the characters are barely human: you 'care' for them only in the way that you 'care' for your toilet when you clean out the ♥♥♥♥ stains -- as a means to an end, but the end isn't particularly gratifying in the first place. In fact, you would probably be better off spending the time cleaning your bathroom.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this for me and my gf to play together as we are long-distance,  and we were looking forward to playing the game together through remote play together.  The co-op isn't really co-op. One player can only control the characters in the open world at a time making the controls feel clunky and awkward because if my partner touched her controller at all it would  cause both the characters to become wonky. We couldn't get past the intro stage with how clunky it was, and moreover it just didn't feel like a co-op game. The story and concept seem neat, but I bought this for the co-op option and this just isn't a proper co-op option. It's co-op in the same way tales games are co-op and that is to say-- only in battle it seems. It's disappointing and really soured me on this game. Tales of Berseria allows for remote access play in the fights, but it doesn't advertise itself as co-op game.. I think the same should be said here. It's possible for co-op but it shouldn't be advertised or tagged as co-op. I can't recommend this game if you're looking a game to play with your partner. As a solo experience it's probably fine, but it's not why I bought the game. Don't buy this game if you're looking for a cute, little co-op experience with your partner. You won't get it.

_childDocuments_.review: You should buy this for the breathtaking, watercolored animation in this opening and ending credits alone.  Holy crap, I just openned the game to casually mess with the settings before diving into it and I was just casually greeted by the best animation I've seen in years.  I mean, yeah you could look it up on youtube but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, that level of art *needs* to be supported.That aside, the gameplay itself is a chill time.  It's essentially a VN (with some slight platforming and turnbased rpg elements) that's entirely voice acted, which is pretty impressive when you consider fact that each character has an interchangeable VA depending on their gender since you can pick between wlw, mlm, or a straight couple.  And for the most part, the dialogue is cute and sweet.  I genuinely wanted to see more of their interactions as the game went on and was surprised by just how much they had to talk about.My only nitpicky complaint is that the "platforming" part of the game feels like it took some inspiration from Jet Set Radio, but just didn't 100% understand what makes it or other platformers fun?  There's like, tracks that you're encouraged to follow perfectly, but you don't feel any faster taking them than just going straight, minus the couple odd ones that are sometimes the only paths to otherwise inaccessible spots.  They also often point you away from the spots of the map that have currencies you want to collect early on too, so in spite of the tracks being named flow....it breaks the flow?  That said, the ost is a blast and makes the okay traversal feel much more elating than it should be.And as for the rpg element, it was engaging; I liked trying to manage the semi-shared hp pool and prioritizing who attacks and who defends based on which of the two has more hp currently.  I just kinda wish that the max level wasn't as low as it was?  Every level up you usually get an associated cutscene to hammer in that not only are they stronger, but their relationship is stronger now too.  While it was nice, I get the impression the level cap was more reluctance to have additional cutscenes (since reminder, they're done 3x over for each couple) and less for balance or design reasons.  I'm not saying we need more cutscenes to go with them,  It just feels a bit disappointing when you reach max level and there's still so many side areas to explore and they're just suddenly less rewarding to explore because you hit cap already.  But this is also kind of a moot point in that for the most part you could just totally avoid the combat, so it's really more just a system that's there to engage with IF YOU WANT.  And I kinda did, I just wish there was a slight bit more.I say these nitpicks less to deter people from giving the game a chance and more just as hopeful feedback for the developers.  Again, the focus leans way more into the relationship's dialogue and it's still visually easy on the eyes and ears to explore and see the maps get cleaned up; I just hope that maybe the developers lean *a bit* more into what makes platformers and rpgs enjoyable for future titles, if they ever get to make another similiar game because if they just touched up those two elements ever so slightly I would say the game's perfect then.

_childDocuments_.review: This game tells a beautiful story about a runaway couple trying to escape the Matchmaker in an arranged marriage type of concept.Honestly, the dialogue, humor, and overall story of the couple has what kept me invested in playing the game. Even though there were some few questions lingering in my head that remained unanswered such as, "What was the Mark?" The soundtrack was also pretty good. The only problems I had was the lack of interesting gameplay. At some point, it just felt rather reptitive and plain. Just going around different Islets, collecting resources, pacifying creatures and trailing Flow over and over again.The combat, however, was what made the overall gameplay much more engaging, especially when you're playing with a friend. There are no timed or turn-based actions, you have to think of tactics/strategies for both Yu and Kay to knock down the enemies while keeping each other safe, and in the case of co-op, you'll have to coordinate and work together to make things work, which made it really fun.Aside from that, the interactions between Yu and Kay and the slow reveal behind the Apiary and Source is definitely the main attraction as well as the reason why I played the game (and kept on doing so) in the first place. I only hope for a sequel to go deeper into some terms that were left unexplained.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has such potential but is plagued by terrible design choice after terrible design choice that leaves a sour taste and ruins the enjoyment. I am writing this review after about 2 hours of play, just after unlocking duo attacks. I am hosting the game on my computer and playing with my partner via remote play together.There is no clear way to save and we've found ourselves repeating content thinking the game saved last time when it did not. It seems changing maps may save, but many times we needed to stop playing so we attempted to go back to the previous map but the characters will stop us and not allow us to return to the previous map, forcing us to progress forward in the story when we don't have any more time to play the game. If you are going to design a game around people playing together and allow remote play, why is there no save on demand option. This game was released at the end of 2020, well into the global pandemic. Remote play together should absolutely have been catered to or thought about, it is clear that it was not.Pressing escape takes you to the inventory/status/etc menu and you must keep switching menus to get to options. When I press escape I want the options menu, please. There is no excuse for this, even controller support. One can make pause bring up options and the select button the inventory like every other developer. In addition, I am using a controller while my partner does remote play on the keyboard. The game recognizes coop and has settings for "keyboard and controller" play. When playing it still only displays the button to press for the keyboard, as the controller player you must guess. I am glad I am the one on the controller because my partner would be astronomically confused if she were the one who had to guess. For designing the games UI for consoles it is astounding to me that this is such an issue.Oh, that reminds me about the dialogue fast forward feature that you can accidentally press LB on the controller and skip a whole scene and yet the B button does not cancel said fastforwarding. By the time you realize you have to press LB again to get it to stop the scene is almost over or you are at a dialogue choice with zero context. Riveting.Inside the ship you are able to walk around and see multiple options to have your characters do such as chatting, go outside, sleep, cook food, shower. Except there is often only one "correct" option and it does not tell you until you try to do it. I do not understand what prevents one from simply graying out the option or showing a little text message saying so. We do not need to see the characters talk about the option not being a good idea or it being too late every single time. It is asinine.There is not a clear way to heal. The game has you pack health kits with you on your first outing, yet there is not a clear way to use them on your adventures outside. You can see them in your inventory but cannot interact with them whatsoever. There is also a way to create healing pills but same thing. We found one campsite, but I don't remember if we could use the health packs at that point. Just before we found the campsite, we returned to our ship to heal from the complete lack of explanation on how to heal. The campsite was also not pointed out when we entered the area, this is something that the characters should immediately point out when you enter the area, as you are still learning the game. If so we would have simply used the campsite, we were even on the same map when we decided to return to the ship.I have read that there is some kind of way to hug each other to gain hp back. We were able to get our characters to hug once on the very first map, but never again. I don't know if this is something we need to unlock. Nothing is explained.The nail in the coffin for this negative review. Duo attacks are a neat concept but extremely difficult to pull off if you are doing remote play with a long distance friend due to the lag. It is quite infuriating and requires an astronomical amount of coordination and added stress to the supposedly "not difficult combat". It took us a long time to be able to get one to work, during a combat where we are being wailed on and the only way to win is something like 6 successful duo attacks. In addition, once you unlock a duo attack its forever unlocked and automatically start forever onward when both of you begin doing the same attack, so have fun dealing with that. Now that I am 2 hours in, the chill and easy combat has turned into an annoyance and effort in avoiding duo attacks as much as possible via micromanagement of myself and my partner. Again, this should be better handled given the release almost a year into pandemic and the rise of people staying at home playing via remote play.These are just my main complaints in the first 2 hours of trying to play this game. Sadly, I expect more of these terrible design decisions to annoy me.The characters are great, the dialogue and setting is great, and it seems to have a lot of potential. I really want to like this game, but I find many things frustrating and a chore to deal with. Ultimately I am confused as to why these terrible design decisions exist given the quality and potential of the rest of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute game that kinda overstays its welcome.The concept of the game is pretty cool: it's an adventure game, but one that focuses on the relationship between the two main characters. Rather than taking the easy way of exploring how they met and fell in love (as in pretty much every other piece of media ever), the game looks at a relationship that's already established, something that is much more difficult to compellingly depict.The usual gameplay loop consists of exploring the world to gather ship parts and food, before returning home to eat and sleep. Every time you do that, you get a little cutscene depicting some aspect of life together. Maybe they're cooking. Maybe they're cleaning the ship. Maybe they just had sex. Maybe they're discussing the future, or reflecting on the past. This is Haven at its best, especially since in 15 hours of gameplay and many nights spent on the ship, I never had any of the scenes repeat, so it stays fresh throughout.The same unfortunately cannot be said for the rest of the gameplay. You're going to have to travel through the same maps, manually (there is a kind of fast travel system but it's very restricted), fighting the same monsters (the combat system is original, but not particularly fun), suffering through the same unskippable cutscenes, and listening to the same barks. The crafting system is perhaps the most tedious part of this: making a new item requires adding elements one by one (which takes 3 seconds), then watching an (again, unskippable) cut scene (another 5 seconds) before a splash screen appears (2 seconds – yes, I've timed it all). So it takes 10 seconds to craft a single item. You can bring 4 types of battle items with you, and you can have 5 of each, meaning that to craft a full complement, you will need 200 seconds at the very least, or more than three minutes. None of this would be a very big issue if the game was shorter. But despite not being super long in the grand scheme of things (it took me 15h to complete), with these mechanisms, and given what it's trying to achieve, it's still a bit too long. Haven falls in the classic trap of having cool animations at the expense of a practical UX.Still, the game is very much worth trying. The graphics are clean and pretty, the music is excellent (I actually discovered the game through its main theme being suggested on my Spotify Discover Weekly, lol), the worldbuilding is creative, the dialog feels genuine (it's not nearly as naive and cutesy as one might fear), and the story and angle are novel. A nice game for fans of romance.

_childDocuments_.review: This game...how do i describe it.  if you watched a show where the main character falls in love and you want them to be happy...thats what this game made me feel like the whole time. I just wanted them to be happy. There were not many issues i had with this game. although traveling can be time consuming and making sure to get items before going out is a bit tedious, in the long run the game was fun and had hardly any bugs. smooth game play and a great story. already 4 stars for me. the only thing id say i disliked was the ending seemed lack luster. *** Spoiler***once i finished getting the bridge cut off so that my love birds could be happy together forever, all i could think was what will we do now? they of course wanted to just draw flowers, which is cute and of course they wanted to eat. I'm  not sure what i expected from the ending but...it just i guess left me wanting more. i wanted to know if they ever decide to settle the small issues that cropped up in the days before the big event. instead it was more of a lets just forget we had a small tiff and move on. I'm all for happy relationships but I also guess this is just how it works for them. everyone is different and they know they don't always agree, as such they move on with life. all in all this is a great game and i can tell a great deal of work went into it. really love the style and artwork.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the small things that really make this game special. Standing around, gliding straight and even staying in water for a while can cause unique dialogue or actions to happen. Whenever one happens it still surprises me with how funny or sweet it is.The story is fun and interesting with how the characters interact with each other and deal with problems, so I've yet to get bored playing this; if anything I need to remember to take breaks. There are so many aspects to this game that consistently show how much the characters care for each other. Which is very unique for me to play, as most games with romance I've played, have you build up to the relationship rather than one that is already established.So far, I give this game a 10/10. Maybe even more depending on the ending.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven, true to its name, is the perfect life most can wish for. A very calming, intimate and heartwarming experience from beginning to the very end. If you've ever dreamed of living on a lone planet alongside your loved one, and enjoy your life and love for each other to the fullest while exploring landscapes that feel like watercolor paintings, listening to chill synthwave, encountering all kinds of cute animals (that you can pet), finding weird but juicy looking fruits and making weirder but delicious looking food with them, or just stay at home and chat, and do goofy things together all day, this game is for you.It's not a challenging game. There's no deep mysterious lore or many characters. And I'll be honest, there aren't many enemy types, landscapes and combat will feel same-y but that's all fine because the random interactions and conversations are so cute and chill you will wish the game went on forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's been with the same person for more than a decade, I found the interaction between the main characters especially endearing.  My partner was often watching or listening to me play and remarked "Have these devs been spying on us?"  Seeing a romantic couple in a game having these very healthy and familiar interactions seems incredibly rare and it was something I really treasured.Another highlight for me was the gliding system.  Floating above the ground and zooming around without any fear of falling was oddly satisfying and enjoyable.  Steering took some getting used to though, and the grab-and-throw mechanic was extremely hard to do on a keyboard; however, it's not required to progress in the game except for a single part.I loved the soundtrack enough to buy the CD.  The artist is French musician "Danger" (Franck Rivoire) who I'd not heard of before but it really resonated with me.The main downside to the game for me was the combat.   While it was a cool idea and I liked the paired tactics, the timing of what move to choose made no sense, and was never really explained.  Most of the time I was just having one character block while the other attacked over and over, or doing double attacks and just accepting I was going to get hit.All in all, it was a very pretty and lovable game that is going to stick in my memory.

_childDocuments_.review: I was drawn to this game by its art style, but sadly art style alone can't carry it.  The movement system is extremely unwieldy, and the camera view can be chaotic.  The combat makes no sense at all on what it wants the player to do.  I was experimenting with various stuff in the game's first battle, and I wanted to end it with my characters getting wiped, thinking I could restart the battle at full health.  Surprisingly the game gave me the middle finger, and put my characters back to spawn, each with 1 health, and I was forced to use the expensive health kit, without the game telling me how to make more.Then there's the problem with storytelling: it seems to happen exclusive through dialogue of the couple, and there's a ton of skippable chitchats  with only occasional concrete information regarding to their situation.  Unfortunately, the amount of chitchat is a bit excessive, and making the main characters' personalities bland and generic.  This is the fatal flaw: it doesn't matter the actual voice acting isn't bad, there is no way I'd continue to play this game when I don't like the main cast for talking too much.Bottom line: there are plenty of fictions that are about a couple showing affections to each other in an isolated location; ones that are much better than Haven.

I played this game more times that I can remember and  I still play it. This game is not a competitive game, it's more relaxing with a splash of action, But I do see the possibilities of making speedruns of this game.This game can also be viewed as a couples game I do recommend playing with this with your significant on any Spectrum. Nowadays people don't know how to pull off romance stories and I'm very critical about that. You know they're not doing it right when your eyes perform a singularity bending space and time itself. but I can say for a fact that this does it right. Sometimes I find this game rivaling the Goodwill in me that has been taken for granted from others, This game Defiance what's in my mind that can't sit still. And I thank you for that. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a cross between light RPG, exploration and visual novel. Story is well written, resting almost completely on dialogue between protagonists. The relationship between the couple is well portrayed and progresses quite believably throughout the game. Voice acting is excellent and the music is perfect. Graphic is heavily stylized and beautiful. The world of Source is lush, dramatic, colorful and full of cute critters. And easter eggs (looking at you, Toriko). The exploration part of the game is well balanced, never falling into a grind. It is complemented by riding on flow threads, which is more action oriented, and by combat against corrupted creatures. Combat flows well, it is based on cooperation between characters and proper selection of actions and timing to exploit enemy weaknesses.  This is a gorgeous and heartwarming game, I wholeheartedly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is a cute little game that I would definitely recommend. It isn't perfect, and my biggest gripe with the game is such: for a game that centers around the romantic relationship of the two protagonists, I felt remarkably little chemistry between them. I was still rooting for them and their relationship, but I think it's just because I felt like I had to, because they were the protagonists? And I can't exactly put my finger on why. The voice acting is great, and the writing is good too, if a bit heavy-handed at times. The gameplay is quite fun and addictive. I wasn't sure if I liked it at first, but before I knew it hours had passed as I was so engaged in the game. Movement is extremely satisfying, except drifting which is awkward and difficult, and following flow threads is fun, especially aerial flow threads. There is a genuine drive to explore and discover, and always a clear objective that pushes you forward. The Nest is super cozy and fun, I love the cooking mechanic, I love pretty much all cooking mechanics in game. A big motivator for me to explore more was to find new ingredients so poor Kay and Yu didn't have to keep eating appledews lololol. Creature design is FANTASTIC, and while combat is a bit hard to pick up, once you get the hang of it it's pretty fun. The story and world is intriguing and unfolds in a very natural and compelling way. I'd love to know more about it, about the society they came from, and would definitely pick up any spinoff or companion works. Besides the first point about chemistry, my other gripes are all technical. The sound mixing is off sometimes and voice lines are super loud and blown out. There are also discrepancies between the spoken lines and the subtitles, which is annoying for me but a legitimate problem for deaf players. I found it quite annoying that Yu and Kay made comments every time you left an islet via the bridge you'd arrived on. At first it was helpful, but after playing for a while you learn to keep track yourself and sometimes you need to backtrack on purpose, to reach a campsite or Birble station or other landmark. All in all these are minor issues that only stand out because the rest of the game is quite good. For the price and the playtime I am really glad I played this game and I would definitely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: A Disappointing Co-op Experience: Why Haven Falls ShortAs an enthusiast of cooperative gaming experiences (A Way Out, It Takes Two, Overcooked, etc.), I approached Haven with high hopes, envisioning countless hours of enjoyment alongside my partner. Unfortunately, those hopes were quickly dashed as we discovered numerous flaws that rendered the game more of a chore than a source of entertainment. Here's why we cannot, in good conscience, recommend it:Lackluster Co-op Dynamics: Despite being marketed as a co-op game, Haven fails to deliver a truly collaborative experience. Instead of working together as equals, one player inevitably takes the lead while the other is relegated to a passive role, merely following along. This imbalance kills any sense of teamwork or camaraderie.Superfluous Conversations: Too much time is wasted on inconsequential dialogue that adds little to the overall experience. These conversations neither deepen the plot nor develop the characters, leaving us wondering why they were included at all.Bizarre Progression System: It's baffling that mundane activities like cooking, dating, and chatting yield more experience points than battling fearsome monsters. This skewed prioritization detracts from the core gameplay and undermines the sense of accomplishment derived from overcoming challenges through combat.Absurd Healing Mechanics: The inability to craft medicinal items outside the safety of our base proved to be a frustrating obstacle. With no means of replenishing our health during expeditions, we were constantly on edge, forced to retreat prematurely whenever our HP dipped dangerously low.Clumsy Combat Mechanics: Fighting monsters in Haven feels more like a clumsy dance than a thrilling battle. The mechanics lack fluidity and fail to provide a satisfying sense of impact, leaving us feeling disconnected from the action.Draining Experience: Despite our initial enthusiasm, Haven quickly became a source of frustration and fatigue. After enduring countless hours of lackluster gameplay, my boyfriend and I made the unanimous decision to abandon our playthrough, vowing never to subject ourselves to its shortcomings again.In conclusion, Haven fails to deliver on its promises of cooperative fun, burdened by its flawed mechanics and tedious gameplay loops. Save yourself the disappointment and seek out more fulfilling gaming experiences elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 GameI had no clue about this game until I saw Danger tweet about doing the OST for it. So I watched a trailer, liked what I saw, got a demo key at some point during the fall and loved it even more. Fast forward to release and it's incredible. The soundtrack is absolutely top tier. Danger is an amazing artist and imo is in the same league as Daft Punk, Carpenter Brut or Justice. This OST is even more refreshing compared to the other work by Danger so seeing this other side was amazingGameplay: It says co-op but it's only really co-op in combat I believe. I had no issues with combat really, the only things I could improve on explaining things a bit more. For instance you can charge up the same attack for each person to do a duo attack but if you hold that longer you can do a stronger one. Unless I missed something I don't think was explained. As well, there's one instance where you get interference from an enemy known as a Hornet that affects the timing of attacks but it also didn't explain how to do the timing. I didn't figure it out until much later accidentally. There's also a few bosses that have some boss only gimmicks as well. Gameplay loop outside of combat is fine, go around and collect things, explore, get collectibles. Only gripe with that is when you have free look enabled you can accidentally do a 180 a lot which is frustrating.Story: Heartfelt, cute, I loved it, I YEARNED. My heart. I loved it so much. It was also funny and wow. They had the voice actors in the same room to do recordings to make it more organic and it shows. Yu and Kay just work so much. I love them.Soundtrack: Once again, this sound track is perfect, go listen to it on Spotify, but it, everything. Danger is amazing.Other thoughts/comments to devs: Great game, seriously. I cannot put into words how warm this game made my heart. I want more. I didn't really experience too many bugs. One I encountered twice gave me a hard crash but I noticed what happened so I was able to avoid it. One bug let me go out of bounds on one island but it did nothing as it just respawned me on the island again. Couple of map bugs. Nothing that kept me from 100%ing the game though. Also a couple of typos but once again, nothing that kept me from immensely enjoying the game. So the 9/10 reflects the issues of those bugs. I will not hold the typos against you guys cause you are a French team and probably speak 1 more language than I do so lolSpoiler-ish stuffSecret boss (one of the guide says there's 3 but 2 are story related i'm 99% sure so it's impossible to miss them I think).It'll take you around 15-17 hours to 100% it. Maybe a bit more if you're speedrunning it. I've 100%'d it.There's 2 endings. It was a little confusing which dialogue I had to pick to get the other but luckily the game makes a separate autosave right before doing the last mission so getting both endings is easy and whew both endings..... bittersweet for one and just depressing for the other..... I know I said I wanted more but logically I don't think there's anything left to tell for Yu and Kay. Maybe another story in universe but not with them as the direct protagonists.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game! The art, world design, and soundtrack are all absolutely stellar. The dialogue and voice acting are both fantastic. They both make you easily become invested in Yu and Kay, and also make their relationship super believable. And also very horny, which I did not expect, but it totally fits. Side note: I know Yu and Kay are running away from the Matchmaker but I was really delighted to know Yu had two moms and it seemed so normalized. So in the Apiary, your mate will be chosen for you, but your sexuality is taken in to consideration at least? #DiversityWin or whatever that meme is. Overall the story is great, and interestingly both endings (even the "good" one) are bittersweet. My main gameplay critique is I would've loved a more detailed map, or at least a minimap. I can't tell you how many times I got utterly turned around and lost because I couldn't remember where a specific flow thread that goes up to a higher level was. Or circled a fragment over and over and over trying to find the last bit of rust.Also for some reason the game wouldn't recognize my controller properly so the button mapping was off, and changing the controller type in the settings didn't seem to help. I played solo so this really sucked in battles when I had to mentally remap all input commands for my P2 character instead of just relying on the spatial cues on screen. Hopefully that's just a me problem though, and in the end, the game is not super challenging so that issue was just mildly frustrating and not absolutely detrimental.EDIT: Eyyyyyoooooo gay update!!! We love to see it. Thank you devs.

_childDocuments_.review: I intentionally left some time after I ended my run (at around 45 hrs) before I write my review to let it all sink in. sorry if this is super wordy. ≧ヮ≦also note that this is probably biased as I mostly played the game with a friend.◤  • : flow-tracing is relaxing. if you're lost or finding unexplored parts, just trace the flow. wished they can run and jump, but I know it's gonna take a lot of redesigning and testing to sniff out bugs. glad they just focused on drifting because they did a great job. it feels nice to move after you've gotten the hang of it. - cleaning rust is a cool way to naturally explore terrain. a bit frustrating to find out where that last bit of rust is, but seeing your progress build up feels good. - it was fun taking turns exploring. one player "drives" while the other looks around for goodies. also helps when figuring out how to get to weird, flow-access-only spots. • : it was nice coordinating with my friend. ^ヮ^ feels like a rhythm game sometimes cuz you have to time your moves. - combat isn't too stressful but still engaging. have to pay attention to what the game is telling you + enemy patterns + the UI to figure out the mechanics. - when I was farming by myself to prep for our next session together, it felt weird fighting alone. I can quickly adjust to playing both characters tho.◤  • story is . there's bits of sci-fi worldbuilding and slice of life too. my friend and I had fun questioning things and putting the pieces together. • : some might find it annoying, but it actually helps sell the fact that they are actually a couple (I'm looking at you, FFXV) and not just lovers in name. cute chemistry; I actually prefer this to lots of unskippable cutscenes. - we had fun playing our parts and wondering what dialogue choice the other player would pick. I played as Kay! we both relate to our characters very much LOLOLOLOL why are the choices on point— • : you unlock them organically by doing things around the nest, which is really nice. doesn't feel like your typical quest line, and makes you think you've stumbled upon something really precious. - the struggles were also relatable and we had fun dunking on the villains. • : gives you a nice sense of progression. you can infer a lot from the objects you see and the nest feels lived in. • my friend cried at the ending :') it was that good.  • in a world where stories are cut into parts, closures hidden in DLCs, and sequel-baiting, the ending is honestly a breath of fresh air. there's enough room for a sequel without forcing/stretching it if they wish, but the .aight, my job here is done. I'm off to listen to the soundtrack for the 999th time because it's awesome. (been continuously listening for 3 months send help—)or play another run with both boys cuz . :') thank u game bakers, good game. ♡

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is an amazing game mostly if you're playing it with a soulmate, the devs said it themselves and I wouldn't have enjoyed it this much if I played it alone. Now that this important part is out of the way, I'll start with the pros of this game: -Pros:-An amazing story that can capture the "couple moments" rather well, I've played it with my boyfriend and we really loved the little quirky yet funny events Yu and Kay share, the discoveries and twists make it even better.-The soundtrack is amazing and captures a lot of the feelings that can be felt from the gameplay/story.-Most of the elements needed for such a game (map, fast travel, radar) are there and they're introduced with cool scenes.-The choice with each conversation makes you feel a bit more immersed and does have a little impact in the story and that is really appreciated.-Combat is heavily based around communication and the items you can craft are really useful and fun to use despite one flaw that can feel awkward.-In my experience, I didn't mind letting my partner take the reigns since it's all about being in sync with them. It can take some time to get used to it but I think the romantic aspect took over and I didn't mind being the second wheel (you're still able to collect ressources and win the seeds competition so keep that in mind :3) -Cons: -Lack of targetting in combats, either play alone (still don't recommend) or communicate as much as possible with your partner! (That's the solution I believe)-Lack of "manual save", I know there's a work-around but when I was playing, nothing of the sort existed and it can be annoying to have to change zones just to save (especially if you're in a hurry), nothing major but it could be a good thing. Making saves limited or time-limited to avoid save-scumming since it's a relaxing game to begin with.-The intro sequence can feel a bit awkward, I know me and my boyfriend felt a bit weird when we saw it since we weren't accustomed to the characters yet but it does a good job at setting the atmosphere in, it's only a little sequence to look at before enjoying the game so it's more of a heads-up than an actual bad thing.-The rust cleaning became a huge chore at the end of the game and isn't fun at all anymore.Overall, I would give the game a solid 8.5/10, it's an amazing experience and I would recommend it to most lovey-dovey couples.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic.  One of the best indie games I've played in a long time.  Has all the heart of Cloudpunk but much more actual game play.  It's not exceedingly "gamey," it's more like an extremely advanced visual novel, but there is just enough exploration/collection/combat to keep things interesting and moving at a brisk pace.  And the game is surprisingly huge for an indie game, with so many hundreds of randomly scripted "relationship" scenes that I'm absolutely shocked.Also one of the few games of this sort to treat relationships/sex/couple-life in an adult manner.  Through in a weird and interesting sci-fi world that leaves you always wanting more info, and I'm just amazed at how good it all was.  Truly emotional (sometimes shocking) endings to boot. Bravo guys.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler free review: If you're looking for a game about two characters so horny for each other they're willing to disrupt an entire working social system, this game is for you. If you're looking for a game where characters show affection and care for one another and their hobbies, don't go into this game.Warning spoilers for the end of the game are below. I will be using "she/her" for Yu and "they/them" for Kay because I played with w/w relationship and want to distinguish them.I was thinking for a long time how to properly write down my thoughts and I can't help myself but feel like the following describes the game the best. This feels like it's written by someone who's absolutely unironically adamant that Romeo and Juliet is about healthy romance, someone who believes that Hamlet's abuse of Ophelia was proof of his undying love, someone who is confident that The Little Mermaid should have ended with the Prince banging Ariel over the side of a ship, someone who thinks that Dorian Grey did nothing wrong, someone who finds a woman abusing a man as unironically hilarious and loving. Basically someone who thinks that abuse and sexual objectification are all that makes a healthy relationship.Look, now, I wasn't counting but I'm willing to bet that good 80%+ of the interactions between Yu and Kay are either about Yu being horny or Yu abusing Kay. There were cases of Yu comparing Kay's work that literally ensured they wouldn't starve to her taking a ♥♥♥♥. MULTIPLE TIMES. I honestly wish I was making that up. Whenever Kay tries to do or say something romantic or wholesome Yu just basically goes "Yeah, I don¨t care, let's bang." There were many cases from the gameplay dialogue when Yu berates Kay for doing example the same thing as she does. Like when Yu eats the food they want to save for cooking it's okay but when Kay does it, Yu shouts them down. There's a part close to the end of the game that Kay and Yu have an argument over their entire relationship being built on Yu's lies and deception. The conclusion? Kay apologises (albeit only hoping Yu hears that) and they never speak of that again. I don't know, for me it would be a bit of deal breaker if the person I loved literally sicced a psychopath at me and her only "defense" was "This is why your parents abandoned you!" Again, I really wish I was lying. Do they talk that out calmly and Yu apologises for the incredibly disgusting stuff she said? No, they go back to acting like nothing happened. And Kay is the only one feeling like they should apologise. Yu just goes on a rant how she needs Kay and can't function without them. And then a few minutes later she changes that into "Kay must be desperate without me"..... I mean, what?If I was doing a list of toxic behaviours in a relationship this relationship would meet at minimum 90% of that list.The entire relationship is about Kay doing their best for Yu and Yu over and over again abusing Kay and acting like sex was the only reason they're together. There's a scene where Kay talk about their motivation to leave and how Yu was the reason and Yu just replies "Oh, I wasn't talking about leaving, I was just saying I was cold, this was all your call." The same Yu then later guilty trips Kay over the psychopath she was supposed to marry and how Kay can't let her go back.Yu is a manipulator, hypocrite, liar, psychopath and even if half of the stuff she says about her arranged partner are true, they've honestly the perfect match! They're basically identical!I really wish there was a possibility at any point after the truth is revealed to simply go back to the Apiary as Kay. Because honestly, Kay is not perfect, they have their flaws, but they do NOT deserve this kind of abuse and this kind of toxic relationship.The worst part is that the supposedly bad ending features Kay actually looking happy. Kay is literally happier in an arranged marriage than ever with Yu. And honestly, no wonder. Yu is a manipulative and abusive psycho and this is about a toxic relationship that writer glorifies.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved playing Haven. This world that Game Bakers built using islands, glowing flow threads, unique animals and fantastic characters had me pulled in from the moment I started playing.The music is fantastic - Danger did a really great job at matching the feel of the music to the feel of the game and the story. There aren't any tracks that feel out of place to me, and every time a new one played I was pleasantly surprised. The art style used and the graphics of the game are great - Not hyper-realistic or super fancy, but honest-to-god beautiful. It's the small attention to detail that makes it for me here - the interaction between Kay and Yu, the funny-looking animals, the cinematics that show at various points in the game. The voice acting is stunning. Most of the time playing through the game, I completely forgot I was playing a game with voice acted characters. The actors matched their roles perfectly, and all of the dialogue feels so natural and realistic. With a majority focus on story, I finished this game in about twelve hours - but with a greater focus on some of the other events and goals around the map you may have a fifteen hour(or more) experience. Throughout this experience, everything was unique - I had one instance where an event happened twice, and two or three voice lines replayed because I was moving too slowly through the world. Other than those instances, every voice line and event was TOTALLY UNIQUE. I have no regrets about buying this game, and I HIGHLY recommend it. Also worth mentioning, the relationship between the two characters is downright adorable. Really, through every interaction I kept thinking 'couple goals'. This game was fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: if you like visual novels or a legitimately unique story, then buy Haven it is well worth the price. If you are not sold, then keep reading and let me explain.Haven graphics are simply astounding the watercolor look that “The Game Bakers” chose was an amazing choice. It is incredibly bright and vibrant. 20 years from now Haven will still look good because of the style they chose. The only real negative are the character models which are just okay.The voice acting overall is excellent. The music is the real selling point and best described as electronic. Those who have played “Furi” will recognize it. Haven is much more upbeat. It does not have the same bass that “Furi” had. It also lacks that sense of looming danger and high stress tension. The music in Haven is far more upbeat and lighthearted. Something you can listen to while riding your bike or going for walk or run.The gameplay is just average to be honest. It follows a rock, paper, scissors gameplay. You have four buttons: pacify, impact, blast, shield and that is it. This all happens in a turn-based real-time arena. The other part of the gameplay is to collect fruits or other materials to fix the ship as it is the main overarching plot point that follows you all the way to the end of the game. It is simple but it gets the job done and it does not overstay its welcome.  The game is about 8 to 12 hours long. So, no combat fatigue. One last note unlike “Furi” Haven is an amazingly easy game. the game straight up tells you right from the get-go that the combat is quite simple and there is really nothing that stressful for you to overcome.The story revolves around Kay and Yu as star crossed lovers who escape from their sci-fi society to live out on a paradise planet called Source far away from the “Apiary” that is the name the sci-fi Empire they came from. The story is made intentionally vague and only slowly unravels to reveal their backstory and the society they both ran away from. For the most part it is light-hearted, but the story ramps up when Kay and Yu must face the consequences of trying to escape the Apiary. That is about all I want to say about the story. I genuinely believe that you should experience the story for yourself.Haven over all is an excellent game 8/10 I will remember it and I will play again and not immediately delete from my computer. I hope that you all will give it a chance if nothing else buy it on sale. The games in only $25 dollars and is well worth your time. Such a genuinely feel-good game is something that I think everybody needs to purge the toxicity of 2020 and start something new.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a little marvel. Before anything else: I played this game after the same sex couple update released and I have only played the game with both characters female. I am only going to play with two female characters because that is the type of relationship i have a connection with. But having played the game as such I do not feel that it detracted from the story or the relationship. So if you are part of the "this game got woke and went broke" crowd you can politely get stuffed.If you have a problem with that then stop reading now.As I said this game is beautiful. Not from a graphical perspective because, in fact, this game seems to have been made on a budget. But the music is evocative and memorable with that sci-fi tone throughout that truly gives you a sense of the scale and wonder of it all.  The lore and the world they have built is engaging and makes me want to delve deeper and deeper and immerse myself in this universe. I have so many question I want answered (in a good way). But most of all the relationship between the two main characters is adorable and I love both of them deeply.It has been so long since I played a game with any kind of romantic plot line that didn't end in disaster for all those involved. Either because the writer went to the George R.R Martin School of "anyone could die so don't get invested in the characters" or because they think its a clever twist that makes their story "original" or "intelligent or "thought provoking". It's not its deeply unsatisfying and makes you wonder why you bothered investing 20+ hours into the game in the first place.And whilst I admit that both endings of have their sad, depressing and even concerning aspects (though one certainly more  so than the other in my opinion) the relationship between these two characters and the deep (believable) loving bond they share truly makes me believe they could overcome anything. Aside from getting lost more times than i am willing to admit the only gripe I had with this game is that my pinky finger now hates me for having to stretch to press the left shift for 15 hours.Overall this game is a beautiful and engaging little gem. I would dare to say romantic masterpiece. YES. WHETHER YOU PLAY AS A STRAIGHT OR HOMOSEXUAL COUPLE. GET OVER IT!! Anyway if you want a fun and interesting JRPG that will restore your faith in the power of love and that romance isn't dead, play Haven.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is about two lovers escaping the grasp of a tyrannical state and running off to make a new life for themselves on a distant, uninhabited planet. Throughout the game, you'll be exploring this planet, investigating the mystery of "rust", fighting local wildlife and evading the grasp of hunters coming after you. But most of all, you'll be enjoying the absolutely delightful and adorable relationship between Yu and Kay, the protagonists.Let's get the cons out of the way first:1. The combat is a relatively simple turn based system with a few basic moves and some consumables. Combos are added later on to spice up the fights, and it can be fun once you get better at it, but it's a pretty barebones system.2. Since you're on an uninhabited planet, there are no NPCs and no one to interact with beyond Kay and Yu. While their banter and relationship does a good job of carrying the game, I couldn't help but feel that the setting itself wasn't very engaging and found myself occasionally bored of exploring. It also doesn't help that Source isn't a very diverse place with most areas looking quite similar.3. The gameplay loop isn't very interesting. You go to a new area, you clean the rust, you collect food, you fight some enemies and you do it again. And again. And again. For about 40 times.4. I'm not sure what's going on with the voice acting but the audio quality isn't the best. This is a pretty egregious flaw IMO since the best parts of the game are LITERALLY the two characters just talking to each other.5. There are a lot of instances when the text doesn't match with what the characters are saying.6. No manual save. You have to leave an area for the autosave to work. Not a major complaint but a questionable decision nonetheless.7. No spoilers but there's an argument that the couple has towards the end of the game that seemed really out of character and forced. Definitely the weakest moment in the writing which is otherwise consistently great.8. The pacing has room for improvement as I felt that the game just kinda ended with the buildup not being particularly strong.1. While the audio quality of the voice acting isn't great, the actual voice acting is superb. Yu and Kay's voice actors did a fantastic job at bringing to life this young, brash couple deeply in love and the voice direction is on point.2. The music is amazing. Even though the tracks loop quite a lot, I never got tired of it as it's just THAT good. Even bought the OST.3. And finally, most importantly, Yu and Kay are wonderfully written and feel SO real. In fact, their relationship feels less like something somebody wrote and more like a documentary of an actual real, genuinely loving couple. They have fears, weaknesses, vulnerabilities but also a passionate love, a desire to grow and a sincere hope to make a real home and spend their lives together. Their banter is funny, the little meals and talks they have are touching and their story is just bursting with optimism and joy. I especially loved the little touches that the game has such as Yu and Kay coming closer to hold hands when gliding and hugging each other after a fight. The believability of their relationship is really helped by the fact that the game isn't about any of them in particular and doesn't take one's POV like most romance games. Haven is a story about a couple, not two individuals, and I felt that that's such a unique perspective that hasn't been explored much in the medium.Even with all its flaws, Haven is a masterpiece of storytelling and I'm delighted to have experienced it. I hope that the devs can build on it in the future with improved mechanics, more content, more customization options and, of course, more Yu and Kay. The Game Bakers is definitely now on my radar and I look forward to what they make next.

_childDocuments_.review: On an objective level in terms of game play, I'd have to give this game a 6/10. The combat is simple, easy, and very casual. It's mostly avoidable and unnecessary, and it can even get kind of stale except for a few moments where -because of story reasons- it gets extra intense. Exploration is fun and relaxing since your only mode of travel is gliding across the grass with hover boots, which can be janky sometimes, but for the most part is a good time. The world is divided into small self contained islets, which can look very samey, but at the same time it makes sense lore wise. The voice audio quality takes some noticeable dips every now and then, which is surprising. Graphically the game is average, but it's stylized in such a way that everything is just so colorful and appealing. The over all art design of the game, be it the intro or end credits animations, or the character portraits in game are excellent. The soundtrack is really good. It loops a lot, but I enjoyed the music more than enough to the point where it didn't bother me at all and was just good listening.After saying all that; I can still absolutely recommend this game with all my being. I enjoyed it from beginning to end, so much so that I can honestly say I was literally smiling the whole time I was playing. The story and writing as well as the voice acting, and the chemistry of the two characters, Kay and Yu, absolutely make this game worth playing. The story does an oddly good job at establishing this game's universe. So much so, that I'm genuinely curious if it will ever get expanded upon at some point in the future. TL;DR This is a very fun and satisfying casual game with a very heart warming, well written couple.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of a mix between a visual novel and a survival/crafting game; unfortunately, I didn't feel that Haven brought anything new or exciting to the table in either regard. Gameplay is quite standard, employing only the most basic genre mechanics to drive exploration: find ingredients for food and medicine, plant seeds to grow a garden, gradually add knick knacks and animal companions to your home base, etc etc.As well, you'll quickly realize there really is no environmental variety; no distinct biomes or anything, apart from a small optional swamp section, and the literal final hour of the game. The world is just green hills, blue skies, grey rocks; not much to look at.The framework for combat is actually very interesting, but they never do anything challenging or creative with it - you'll mostly be fighting the same 4 or 5 enemy types throughout the entire game. Of course, the devs clearly didn't intend this game to be an action RPG, but it's something you should be aware of going in.I did however love the soundtrack, and the two lead voice actors deserve high praise - there is a  of dialogue in Haven, and not a single line feels phoned in. While the actual events of the game aren't particularly interesting, the narrative backdrop behind it all is super compelling, and little bits of worldbuilding and lore details are rolled out at exactly the right pace to gradually paint a picture of what, exactly, is going on.It's clear that the writers at The Game Bakers are quite talented, and if Haven were just a straight-up visual novel, I'd definitely give it a thumbs-up and strongly recommend it to everybody. Unfortunately, the weak gameplay and uninspired world design make it a bit of a chore to get through.

_childDocuments_.review: What hooked me was the interesting premise of these two fugitives fleeing an authoritarian government, and it totally is cool, the game plays that parts very well. However to my disappointment (and maybe to your pleasure, dear reader), most of the dialogue and story in this game is about the two main characters. In fact, throughout the whole plot there are only a few points where it actually develops. The character's relationship does not evolve in any way and neither do they. Much of the dialogue is just "generic chatter" and some of it can be at times quite cringy, like in some cheap erotic novel they sell at the cashier in paperback covers... It is expertly voice-acted though, and the romance is rather wholesome, I just wished the game explored more about the lore and world they have created.Far as gameplay goes, it's really good. No real complaints there, the combat system is quite interesting mix of jRPG and time-based puzzles. One missed opportunity in game design was that they didn't add momentum to the movement system. It would have been 1000 times better if they added mechanics like Tribes skiing to this game and adjusted the terrain to match, then moving around would have been a lot more fun. As it is, the movement is mostly just visually pleasing but not really fun.And of course the OST - it's absolutely incredible. One of the best soundtracks I've heard in a long time.Overall I am happy with the purchase, but disappointed that the really cool world they have created for this game was not explored in due detail and the ending is... well... Let's just say that given what interested me in this game, this is not the ending I would have liked to see. I really wanted to see more of the lore, more other characters, some history of the world, other planets and locations. What is the "Mark"? What is the council? What other planets there are? Are there non-Apiary plants?  The game leaves many questions unanswered. Here is hoping they make more games in this universe. There's lots of potential there.In the end this is a "steamy romance" kind of game, not an adventure game. If you are into that sort of thing, it's pretty much the best one you'll get, since most others are cheap erotic trash and this is a proper high production value top-notch title. However, if you are looking for an adventure game set in a cool world with intriguing backstory and lore, prepare to leave with a lot of unanswered questions.

I recommend playing it with someone close and you decide each of the characters responses, makes it quite interesting imo. Also the combat is seemingly not fun if playing alone... The game is focused on the narrative and the two lovers Yu and Kay. If you expect epic RPG elements you will be disappointed. But in my book this game is a masterpiece for starting in the thick of their relationship, instead of all these stories about slowly building up love and interest. Truly a fresh air between all these games we get nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting such a great game! It really was a well written story and the characters are so likable. The gameplay wasn't anything groundbreaking, but it was a nice change of pace from the games I usually play. I felt so free while playing this game, that was probably the intended feeling the developers were going for, but just roaming around Source was really relaxing. The music and art design were amazing too! My ONLY complaint was the confusing combat system. Sometimes I wasn't fast enough to calm down the animal or shield myself and I kept forgetting how to access my battle items so I would just start pressing random buttons until I died or something happened. Other than that, this game was amazing! I would recommend this to anyone honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed it. I liked the overall story, thought they did a good job tackling two characters in a long term relationship which is not something I've seen many games do. _childDocuments_.review: yah it's a good game. extremely minimal and vague spoilers inbound but spoilers nonethelessthe battle mechanics really arent as atrocious as some people make them out to be, i wish the timing for some combos wasn't so strict but i really like how they illustrate the work kay and yu put in to make their relationship work; you have to mess around and find out to figure out what works and what doesn't with every new enemy/successive problem while working in tandem with your partner, where every battle becomes easier as you fall into a rhythm built on practiced trust (though the meta takes this one step further with the player controlling both characters simultaneously, like two halves of a whole.. T_T). i just thought it was Neat and seems to be something either people just didn't notice or haven't said anything about...i also thought the endings were well done but i've already run out of steam for thinking here so ill just say that i think more actions should have consequences, actuallyHowever. there's another thing....this is a game where the characters do the do and get high on-screen, but they can't cuss? any and all swears are censored with "bloot" which doesn't seem all too terrible until you have to watch one of the mcs tell the other one to go bloot themselves in the middle of an otherwise emotionally charged scene... it just never sounds natural and detracts much more from the dialogue than it adds to it, only really serving to make any dialogue appended to it feel incredibly silly/out of pocket and kills almost any tension in a given moment instantaneously and ultimately just completely befuddles me as to why the devs thought this was necessary but it wasn't cringe enough to make me want to put down the game or hate it so whatever

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this show indie developers achieve amazing things when they have a clear idea of what their game's central focus should be, and put all their efforts around serving that one main point.Haven is a game about a couple in love, for couples in love (though it can be single-player, it shines when played with your SO; there's both a hetero option and two gay options available); a couple eloping away from an authoritarian system which would deny their love and build a nest of their own away from everybody, finding in each other the strenght to deal with the adversities that come with it.The more the game's focal point is well done, the easier it is to forgive the minor flaws in "peripheral" systems. Who cares if the combat system is a bit clunky and unintuitive, when the characters are so charming and adorable? Who cares if the lore a bit simplistic, if the plot is made so intriguing by your emotional involvement with the characters? Who cares if the character models are a bit lacking, when the anime-style art is so delightful? Who cares if the controls can be a bit imprecise at times, when skating across such a beautiful alien world exploring for food, background story and various asides is so damn fun? Who cares if the game gets a bit samey towards the end, if there are so many fun little scenes and dialogues to be found by tasting new food, interacting with objects picked up around the planet, and so on?It's just so freaking nice. A simple and well-done feel-good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Been looking forward to this game for almost entire year. This wait, along with the game itself- was ABSOLUTELY worth it. This is NOT for those who want intense mechanics and reward/ failure penalties like Furi, their previous game. It is for relaxation purposes and "enjoying the story" as The Game Bakers promised.Having said that, the team has done a BLOOTING good job on it.The Game Bakers have hit it on the nail with what they were aiming for- seamless game play with everything in it complimenting their mature and spicy relationship. The music, wow. The design, wow. The details. Everything else about it- WOW, WOW, WOW, WOW, WOW.If you are looking for FANTASTIC humour, voice acting, and loads of crying too- then this game is for you!
