_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty solid.The characters have an established relationship already, so the focus isn't on them getting together. Moreover, the focus feels more on the cohabitation. It feels like the devs tried to make an actual couple, instead of the old trope of "will they or won't they?" The gameplay is rather unique, while also mostly fleshed out. The bugs have been rather minor, overall, and the co-op is exactly that. Much of the gameplay, dialog, puzzles, and even combat makes a true effort to incorporate both players input. Both players have to work together to achieve success. Agreeing on dialog, making joint strategy, and cooperating as a unit makes everything run more smoothly. If you're playing with someone who thinks very differently than you, and you disagree often, this game will either fix that or you won't make much progress. The design is amazing. Everything is explained in one way or another; the game goes into the right amount of detail. You're not left hanging, but the game doesn't hold your hand either. The characters are fleshed out, with jobs, hopes, dreams, and aspirations before the story starts. The personalities are likable, while not being without flaws and feel more human and relatable as a result. Getting around is fun and relatively easy, so long as you and your partner agree on where you're going. The world feels big enough to warrant this style of transportation. Gliding around, flying, hopping from island to island, and even just walking all feel like their own independent experience that is worth mentioning. I highly recommend giving this game your attention. It's definitely underappreciated.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely not a masterpiece. I barely recommend it as it is an edge case. I like it, but I don't love it. The word that I think summarizes it best is "cheap". I'll explain below.Two horny youngsters making out all the time, trying to repair their space ship (aka "Nest") and... I don't know... Build a lonely life on an alien planet? What can go wrong with that?It's an easy and effortless game (as in not challenging) which is a big relief to be honest. It's perfect relaxation when you are tired after a day's work, and don't want anything that requires lots of work and attention. The mechanics are simple and the story is simple.However, about being cheap... Let's start with the music. It's nothing memorable, no distinct melody that you remember afterwards. I get the impression that it's one single track on repeat, but that's not the case. You could call it "the style" of the music if you like. If being bland is a style.The gameplay loop is all about "exploring" floating islets, which all look the same (copy & paste cheap?), which isn't all that exciting, until you need to go back to your camp and resupply. You explore by "running" (floating, hovering?) all around those islets, pacifying enemies and collecting "rust" (pink crystals) and fruits. It gets repetitive, and kind of boring after a while. Occasionally you'll find a piece of something that triggers a cutscene. The cutscenes are of course also cheap. They consist of the two characters as 2D images on each side of the screen talking to each other.The story is the best part. It's not amazing, but it's good. And charming. I won't spoil anything here though.So... I can't tell you whether this is a good buy or not. It depends on your taste. But if you are someone used to AAA titles, or even better good AA indie titles, I think you will be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Wholeheartedly recommended. This game has the best portrayal of a romantic relationship I've ever seen. It is incredibly wholesome and cute, the characters feel genuine and they care for each other with authenticity.I have seen romantic movies and books, but this game makes you play that role and therefore achieves its intentions with much more impact. Granted, I played it with my girlfriend and we found Yu and Kay VERY relatable to our personal experiences. In fact, Kay may be the most relatable character to me I've ever seen.That's not only because of the relationship, but because Haven revels in the intimate, in the little dialogues and the quirky conversations, in building characters that engage in very human, very mundane activities that you can relate to. We ended up playing the whole game just to see what conversations we could unlock by the end, as every little detail was very enjoyable.As if that wasn't enough, the gamplay and aesthetics are polished to an excellent degree. Gameplay never feels stale despite being so simple. Flying around collecting Flow and collectibles was fun and engaging no matter who had the lead. And the combat was strategic, simple and fun. Although it could be that the fun is mostly in timing the attacks and blocks correctly with your coplayer. The only downside I can think of is that some flowthreads are kinda easy to miss and you may end up looking for them for a little too long.In terms of aesthetics, the opening animation is outstanding. Makes me wonder how much they spent on it. Nevertheless, it's absolutely worth it. The music is also very memorable and catchy. The character and enemy designs are on point and the design of the base (the Nest) is super cute and comfy. We loved looking through it in detail.Edit after one year: I didn't do the music enough justice. The OST composed by DANGER is an absolute banger. All the tracks are memorable and none feel like filler. I still listen to it almost everyday, I would put it up there with Persona 5. Other games have 1 to 3 songs that I keep for my work playlist, but I have over 10 of Haven's in there.Overall, unforgettable experience that I'll definitely relive with my gf in some years. 10/10, made me have so many overwhelmingly beautiful emotions. If any more content is released, I'll be very excited.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven may not be a challenging game, but it is a wholesome one. It's like finding that one slice of life anime you've enjoyed despite normally liking action type games.   While the combat system and graphics are simple, the entire experience more than makes up for it. The story, the world, the movement, and even the MUSIC are overwhelmingly great, and the banter between the main characters is impressive. Every step of the way is an amazing experience, and the game rewards you for being bold and confident with your decisions.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is not just a game, it's an experience. I found myself feeling a little hollow after finishing this game, and I waited until I had absolutely completed it before deciding to make a review. Why recommend it if it left me feeling this way? It took me back to when I was much younger, when I would spend hours reading stories and burying my face in a good book. That sensation you feel after you've read the last page, knowing that this is the conclusion to an absolutely wonderful story; THAT kind of hollow, is a good thing to feel. Haven feels organic, I feel like I'm outside looking in on two people genuinely in love with one another, watching their fate unfold before me. Every interaction, every moment they shared I had a goofy smile on my face just watching their love blossom and grow. Every argument, every battle, the connection between these two was tangible, and even if the very world was against them, you'd know they'd take the chance to remain as they are, damn the consequences. What this game does right, is tell a story. You may find yourself getting angry at them when they bicker over little things, or get on each other's nerves. You'll find yourself saying "Aww" perhaps internally or even externally. You'll let that music overtake you and simply enjoy the adventure, the novelty of spending time with these two as they overcome whatever life throws at them.Combat is simplistic and fun, throwing just a few curve balls here and there to keep it interesting. It functions with teamwork, and you'll have to work together to best enemies, though not perfectly. It can get frustrating to operate, but once you get the flow down, and learn the patterns, combat will run much more smoothly. Of course, combat isn't what you should be seeking out of this title. The music wasn't what I was expecting, I had anticipated more acoustic guitar and mellow tunes, not uplifting electronic. But you know what? It works, and it works damn good, found myself just vibing to the tune, and could feel the sense of adventure and calm all the same. I bought this on a whim, craving a good story driven game with a great art style, and I got exactly what I wanted, perhaps even more. The Game Bakers, thank you for this experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A cute slice-of-life x sci-fi cozy-style game that fills a few roles, depending on what you want. If you're looking for a light romance sim, you can head cannon to your heart's delight - with a bit of fun lore along the way. If you want a couch co-op with good music, beautiful imagery, and a cute (if campy) couple, then here you go. If you just want a game to drown out the ever-imposing drone of li- if you just want to zone out and chill this game is fun too.The style is unique and might not be for everyone, but it's a 10gb game that runs well on most any system, is made by a French company, and puts aesthetics at the forefront in a nice way. Also, any company willing to go back and add wlw/mlm/nblnb (even if just head cannon) couples in addition to the base hetero couple deserves to get a shoutout, since that's rare.Perhaps best played with as a couple, but my solo run so far is nice and there's only mild inconvenience in duplicating actions.8/10 game, finally glad to start playing it to complete it after starting it 3 years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: I've finished this Game today after 13.5 Hours of Gameplay. Some people need less, some need more Time to finish this Game. The Value you get for your price is justified in my opinion and worth it. Nontheless and besides that this is something only YOU can decide.Short Review (TL;DR):I'll rate this Game diferently than AAA-Games since this is a Indie Company and I want to respect this Game in exactly that regard. Its nothing of high triple-A Value, thats for sure, but its a beautiful little Gem that suprised me by being unique. Ratings:★★★★★ Story (It's cheesy but has a lot of beautiful moments as well]★★★★★ Voice-Acting (I want to have all my Games so life-like. They put alot of effort into Voicing these characters and I'm so grateful they did)★★★★★ Visuals/Graphics★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★ Soundtrack★★★★☆ World Design (Universe, Lore and Artwork)★★★☆☆ Level Design (Environment and Space)★★★☆☆ Exploration Factor★☆☆☆☆ Combat, Equipment and Enemies☆☆☆☆☆ Side Quests (There are None)★★★★☆ Certain Movement Mechanics (e.g Mount, climbing, gliding and swimming)★★★★☆ Certain Characters and Dialogue★★★★☆ Quest RewardsLong Review:seen the trailer, fell in love. The music and especially the intro are very well done. The characters are very well written and very well set to music. I like the style and it harmonizes with the music. Very nicely done, I'm thrilled. The Main aspects of Haven are definitely: Voice Acting, Environment and Story overall. It feels so life-like so full of emotion. Voice-Acting is superb and one of the best I've ever witnessed in my whole Gaming career from an Indie Studio. You Love these dialogues.The music is appropriate and atmospheric, the gameplay feels new yet familiar, this is especially true for the combat system, but the best of all the great things about the game is the synergy between the two main characters. I've played almost all of the games that the general public dubbed the best of the decade, and yet none of them have shown me such an honest and well-written relationship as Haven can. It's not just any Story - It's a beautiful Story.With that out of the Way - yes... There are huge flaws that shouldn't exist and definitely need to be accepted otherwise you won't have fun. Two of these aspects are camera and Combat. These two points are a huge Hit or Miss. Let me get this out of the way: If you're looking for a "walking-Simulator" with a little bit more than walking, enjoying a wonderful and relaxing story with superb Voice acting - here you are. If you expect an Action RPG Adventure with challenging combat then you might be disappointed. The Combat is the weakest point in the whole game. You basically have 2 attacks (Left or right Attack) and Enemys are only vulnerable to one of them. IF you found out what it is you basically spam the right direction and win after petrifying it. It gets really annoying later on and you're avoiding fights later on since they're draining your energy.Second is Camera. If you like to glide (As I did) and you want to move your camera you can't since its a standard that opt. off in the menu. You can activate rotating camera in the settings but it makes it so much worse. I often did a u-turn by accident simply because I was looking around and U-Turns are getting activated by Character position - NOT Camera position. So if you press the wrong direction - U-Turn will be your worst enemy. Camera is the hardest enemy in The Game and won't be your friend here.I also witnessed a few FPS Drops here and there, even though I use specs way above the recommended side. I use a 1440p Monitor @ 144hz with the following Specs:i9 9900kRTX 2080Ti32GB Ram @3000mhzInstalled on SSD.I witnessed drops from 144 to 116 FPS. Nothing major and not that often (Doesn't kill the mood) but you'll notice it sooner or later. I highly recommend the Game to anyone that just want a relaxing game with likeable Characters and let me get this out of the way:

_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others Haven is a title that addresses a love story on a seemingly deserted planet, which mixes elements of various genres. It presents RPG mechanics, with aspects of metroidvania, going through real-time turn based combat and a dash of visual novel.The “The Game Bakers” studio has already accustomed us to titles that stand out for their strangeness of appearance and that present good mechanics. Well, Haven is no exception to this rule, but addresses a topic that is very rare to see in video games, love. And it is this angle of the story that sets Haven apart from everyone else.The story is passed between two protagonists, Yu and Kay, fed up with a life full of routines, they decided to run away from a society that does not approve their relationship. So they try to build a life on a strange planet, with the name Source, full of small archipelagos and apparently uninhabited.Unfortunately an earthquake catches them off guard and their spaceship crashed down the canyon below. Without another option, the main objective of this couple is to recover the previous shape of their ship since they were unable to fly again. This earthquake also opened a kind of bridge between archipelagos that allows the exploration of 42 different points on the map.Between the exploration of the map and the whole romance, the previous life of both enters in the equation, since Yu's mother finds it through a signal emitted by a transmitter that they thought was disabled. However, Haven is mainly about survival in their new life, which consists mainly of harvesting alien plants for their meals, exploring all corners of these archipelagos, while gliding through the air with their special boots and trying to free areas contaminated with a kind of crystals that also plagues the fauna. It is interesting that this aspect brought me several memories of “Horizon Zero Dawn” and its corrupted areas.Unlike most titles of this genre, Haven offers a simplified RPG experience, free from any record of missions and skill trees. All your progress is made as the story is unwrapped and the relationship between characters is built. Although many of these progressions are made … in bed.It is an interesting pattern for titles with this profile, but it can raise some disinterest because it contains many lines of text with little interest. All lines of text have voice acting, but many times I ended up pressing the fast forward button because I really wanted to move on to the action. This fast forward button can also be pressed during combat, although without much strategy involved, it is an interesting aspect for the most impatient.Although very light, Haven also has some survival mechanics. As you explore all the Source archipelagos, some ingredients are presented that can somehow mix with each other, to produce meals that can help to recover some of the characters' statistics, such as making the couple more efficient in combat.Speaking of combat, all the combat mechanics in Haven are a little strange and implemented to be played with a partner. Still, playing alone won't be difficult either, since the controls are quite simple. As I mentioned earlier, combat is a mixture of turn-based combat and rhythm, as each character can deliver a blow alone, or make a stronger attack using the help of their partner. It is necessary to monitor the actions of the opponents and react according to their attacks.This whole adventure was played with a command and during the combat each joystick is assigned to one of the characters. The left joystick is assigned to the character shown on the left side of the screen, while the right is assigned to the character on the right. The player has at his disposal two attack skills, one of impact that delivers a melee attack, and a ranged ability. In this aspect the opponent will have a resistance to one of the attacks, so it is necessary to understand which attack is most suitable for each type of enemy. There is only one defensive ability which in this case is a shield. Finally, the ability to "Pacify", which allows to cure the animal that its in "rage" form.Fights don't present a great depth. Still, as the story progresses, some enemies require some strategy to overcome.Although Haven is somewhat monotonous and repetitive, its soundtrack full of catchy beats and melodies really manages to pull on the player. The portrait of an adult relationship is something to be admired. Now it remains for the player to see if he is interested in a somewhat moving love story.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick thing, ignore the LGBTQ+ tag in the game. This game is not in any way connected or related to that group just because there is now an option to have gay/lesbian characters.  Stop putting these tags on games where it doesn't fit. -------------------------------------------------Haven is another odd duck that I'm having difficulty placing exactly what genre it should belong to. Its a story-focused game that primarily centers around two lovers as the main characters, Kay an Yu.The enviornments in the game are quite pretty to look at, and very fun to traverse. There's also enough reason to explore casually. Not the most visually appealing spectacle in the world, but it gets the job done.The main characters I found to be, slight stereotypes, but aside from that the two grew on me pretty quick. Most of the game, honestly, is just messing around with various things and seeing what happens. Not to any gameplay benefit sometimes, but rather just to see the reaction. And it is fun. I cleared the game and I think I still missed some stuff, considering reloading my last save just to see all of it.As far as gameplay goes, well the game doesn't focus too heavily on it. Combat does exist, but its a pseudo-turn based system that has you choose the actions for both characters as is appropriate. Its takes a little getting used to, but isn't too brutal, and isn't supposed to be. This is more of a casual game than anything else in that regard, so be aware of that.I enjoyed the game most when playing for an hour/hour and a half near the end of my workdays, its a nice game to wind down and relax with. Well worth the asking price.Oh, and it does have full controller support, in fact probably works better with controller than without, but not to the same degree that Furi had (where you pretty much HAD to play with a controller, this is different).

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the game since I bought it, but....This update introduces same-sex couples, which is great, but why not include a Female Kay and Male Yu as well?From the developers: "Imagine a woman who likes cooking and is prudent, and a man who likes mechanics and is a hothead? Our original Yu and Kay broke those gender stereotypes and we didn't want to bring them back in the game. For our team, representation and inclusion are fundamental beliefs, for gender, ethnicity, sexual preferences, and all forms of inclusion, and have been included from the original design of the game."You ask us to imagine this scenario as if it were a negative thing. If you truly want to be inclusive, don’t dismiss this couple dynamic.My relationship mirrors this dynamic. What’s wrong with a man liking mechanics and being hotheaded? What’s wrong with a woman enjoying cooking and being prudent? This dynamic is valid and shouldn’t be erased if you claim to support inclusivity.It's hypocrisy and double standards to say you value representation and then exclude certain relationship dynamics.True inclusivity means recognizing and validating all types of relationships, including those that fit more traditional or stereotypical roles. By excluding these, you’re not fully embracing diversity. Inclusivity should encompass every form of relationship dynamic, not just those that break stereotypes.My relationship, where I enjoy mechanics and have a bit of a hot temper, and my partner who loves cooking and is more prudent, is just as valid as any other. Pretending it doesn’t exist is not inclusive; it’s exclusive.If you truly believe in representation and inclusion, then represent all dynamics.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a bit hard to categorize and I have no idea who the targeted audience is. On one hand, the game is cute and casual like it was made for kids but on the other hand, there's the romance part and although it is not explicit, I would not call it mild either. Yet in the dialogs they still have the need to replace "♥♥♥♥" with "bloot" while the characters lie on top of each other in bed, barely having any clothes on. I really don't know.The gameplay gets repetitive fast and the combat becomes mostly just an annoyance you need to get through to continue with the story. And even though the game gets more challenging toward the end, it's still not super hard. Perhaps it's designed to be played in co-op with casual gamers in mind? But the co-op feels more like a afterthought that an actual design decision so again, I don't really know what they were aiming for.Speaking of, the co-op is a bit strange. For the general world exploration, one player leads and the other can only follow and gather resources. For combat, both characters are controlled independently and for the conversation, both characters needs to select the same dialog option to continue, which is super weird and I don't really understand the reasoning behind this design.The camera controls are horrible and broken. There is an option to control the camera with the right stick when you're floating, but it works only once and after restart of the game, it never worked ever again. So basically you cannot control the camera when floating and when you actually can control it, both players control it at the same time which results in a total mess.The story is not super convoluted and pretty straight forward, but at the end, there are still open questions that are never answered.Overall the game falls into the "meh" category. It's not bad but I really don't know if I would recommend it. Or more precisely, who I would recommend this to. It can be played as a co-op so if you're looking for something casual to play with a friend, you can grab this on sale. I would not play this by myself though, it's a bit boring for my taste.

_childDocuments_.review: A touching, emotional story of two lovers who have escaped to a remote planet in order to escape their dystopian society. This is an adventure game with some light RPG elements that make the experience better. This is honestly one of my favorite games even though it has some flaws. Tl;dr - you should play this game if you like exploring strange new worlds, playing character-driven games, or reading a cute romance.THE GOOD:-The voice acting is top-notch. Seriously, kudos to the voice actors for their emotional, fun, often hilarious performances.-The story is engaging and will probably make you cry at least once.-The dialogue usually feels natural, and when it doesn't, I'm willing to forgive it because it's so snappy.-The leveling system is tied to relationship interactions and exploration goals, which are two of the best parts of this game. So leveling up feels natural and fun.-The combat is simple but makes you feel like you are really controlling two people fighting together. Bosses aren't too hard (except for the Hornets lol).-The game is really easy and intuitive to control on a gamepad. I have not attempted to play using a keyboard and mouse.THE BAD-The biomes often start blending together after a while. You'll sometimes struggle to tell one island from another.-The graphics aren't particularly distinguished.-The combat sometimes feels janky.-Building exploration is just Yu and Kay going into a building, making noise for a moment, then coming back out with an item. It doesn't ruin the experience, but does feel tacky and low-budget.THE CUTE-You will meet several adorable animal friends along the way! Give Oink some pets for me!!!-The Game Bakers pushed out a huge update in 2021 that added same-sex couples to play as. This is a VERY LGBTQ-friendly game and, as a card-carrying lesbian, I will NEVER get over how precious FemYu and FemKay are. *review devolves into incoherent squealing*-The romance in this game is just so so so so good. Seriously, you'll love it. Unless you hate cute romances, in which case, stay FAR away lol.-The main hub of the game, The Nest, is super cozy and will make you wish you had a house-spaceship to fly around in.FINAL VERDICTSolely on gameplay, Haven gets an 8/10 from me. It's a fun exploration/adventure game. The characters, dialogue, and sheer HEART, though, bump it to a 9/10. PLAY THIS GAME. You will not regret it!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I had such high hopes for this game so the disappointment hits especially hard. The game looks like a relaxing exploration game with some story, wholesome characters, fluid movement and some fights here and there - and all of this in coop. I was looking forward to the characters and story, as well as the exploration by gliding over the map with my friend. Sadly, there is too much that distracts from exactly this for "haven" to be a good game:- the coop mode (aka remote play) is a joke and absolutely useless. you have to agree on dialogue, can only move together (only one person can control the "flying"), there is no real advantage of playing this together- the flying controls are really bad and everything but satisfying. you constantly glitch, your character moves randomly, you perform uturns, characters move much further than they were supposed to and slide over a ledge, ...- the distances you regularly have to cross because you have to move back and forth between the base and exploring is also annoying. probably half of my playtime was spent flying the exact same way i've flown x times before.- the story is nice but spread so far between other "content" that it only pops up every now and again. "haven" could have been a cool visual novel or something but this format didn't do it much good- the exploration is a joke, sadly. many places look very much the same and if you stumble across a building or something, you have to watch from the outside, while the characters go explore.- then there are the fights. they are too big a part of this game imo. There is no real strategy behind them either, you have to choose between two different kinds of attack and hope that it will stick. Even on easy difficulty they will drain you HP so quickly that it feels more like a mechanic to prolong playtime by having to return to base to heal up (becase god fobid you just take some meds or eat something to heal up while on the go - that is only possible at certain locations).- the character moments are the only redeeming factor of this game but they are drowned by all the issues this game has. the relationship that is portrayed is real and authentic, not the romantic fairytale many other games/ stories tell. sadly, i was not able to enjoy this part enough between all the annoying mechanics.The story was meh as well, there are two options for the ending, both ideas are okay but very differently weighted (you get a fleshed out cutscene and everything for one, 4 pictures for the other), the story still left me feeling unsatisfied in the end. There is not much to the story to begin with, and then it is missing depth and information to the way the world works.My bf really liked "Haven" but without him i am not sure i would have finsihed it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:   This game is amazing.  Haven has amazing story-telling, amazing character relations, amazing music, and interesting combat.  I have read through a few of the reviews for this game and would like to add a few counter points instead of gushing about it like every other recommend review.Haven's gameplay shares the same central component that the story does; cooperation.  I personally have been playing this co-op with my long-distance boyfriend.  Now, for people coming in expecting Haven to be like other co-op games, you are likely to be sorely disappointed.  In order to get around needing to be in the same room, we decided to use remote play.  When I connected to him, the audio was screaming at me, but he had no issue with connecting to me, so that is how we played.  We did need to fanagle with the setting for who was which controller and whatnot, but eventually we got it all figured out.Dialogue requires you to agree with your gaming buddy on which options to choose.  The way my s/o and I chose to deal with this was by each picking one character to choose for, and the other following along when that character is the main focus.  Movement can be very confusing at first.  When outside of the Nest, each player is able to walk individually.  However, the faster form of movement is controlled my the player deemed "controller 1".  This does not mean that player two gets to just sit there and watch player one move around.  While player one is gliding, player two can sweep a blue... dot? (idk, they had a name for it.  I just cant remember) in order to collect item that may be just out of reach, or farther ahead.  SO while both players are not "in charge" both of them have an equally important task to do, just like in real relationships, with real tasks.Combat was also a bit tricky to figure out at first, but eventually it became almost second nature.  Combat is based about patterns and timing.  When playing in co-op this means communicating with the other player, talking about what you are doing next or if you need to support something the other person is doing.  It is almost like dancing.  Sometimes you are attacking while they defend, sometimes you are defending while they attack, and sometimes you throw all caution to the wind and go all out.  The better we got at recognising patterns, the easier combat got, which meant the gradual difficulty increase was not too steep, nor was it not challenging enough.The story is cute and relatable.  The concept of "confidence" has both me and my s/o intrigued as we still don't know the consequences of being confident or not.  Levelling looks like a twisted helix, and though we have been given no name for it, we have taken to calling it "synchronisation", gaining a stat boost when the characters are most "in sync."  In all honesty, because of how the game is put together and how the mechanics work, I almost feel like that is the very core of Haven.  To be "in sync" with your s/o.  For Yu to be in sync with Kay.We have barely touched the surface and we are both still very excited to see where this game will go next.  Just be warned that this game really is like nothing else I have played before, and that kind of ingenuity takes some time to grow accustomed to.

_childDocuments_.review: The game devs claimed that one of the main focuses of the movement system of this game was to make it as easy as possible to traverse these maps and that it had to be intuitive: well, they failed miserably in doing so.The game uses a glide system in which you "keep pressing" the Rt button (controller) to perform a sprint, which goes from 0 to a 100 at the press of the button.While in this sprint mode your turning radius is greatly limited and you achieve a better maneuverability with the drift, this is done by pressing the Lt button.Until now you would say that everything is fine, and I'd agree with you, but the game is based on gathering resources on the map and being a roomba cleaning the world out of a substance called "rust", removed by touching various hotspots highlighted by a bright red mark.The movement system and your objective do not cooperate at all: theoretically you would want to traverse these multiple maps by sprint, since the normal walk speed is really slow, so you have to keep pressing the Rt button and can get tiring since it's done 99% of the time.But this is only the tip of the iceberg.If you want to come to a full stop in this game you let go of the sprint button and the characters slide for a few meters at full speed then halt their movement by force.This middle ground option impairs fine tuning due to the forced halt and also forces you to account for the overshoot.This will cause more than enough situations in which if you miss some items or hotspots, your every option feels clunky and frustrating, either be it to stop and walk backwards 1 or 2 meter or drifting and circling back to it. The game tries to fix these situations (or some of these) with U-turns, which are performed by pressing the stick "downwards" (remember this, as it will be important) which holds your momentum and you flip 180° istantly returning on your previous tracks. The U-turn instead of fixing problems helped giving me motivation in writing my first not recommended review, hell even first review at all.The U-turn breaks the game: since it's direction-based, it's binded exclusively to the analogue stick. If you ever, by mistake, press downwards you have to stare at a 0.5-1 second cutscene where you cannot stop them from performing it once: then you go back to the previous problematics of the basic movement system if you want to nullify your mistake: either stopping awkwardly, turning with drift, or repeat the u-turn. It's reluctant to say that U-turning is unusable for fine tuning too.Another funny thing that this thechnique breaks is the ability to control your camera while gliding, which is cleverly toggled off by default because it is unusable and the devs knew it. Simply put the game should be played with fixed camera angle while gliding, as it will be very easy to trigger it, for example even if your camera isn't right behind the protagonists but watches them from the side, the game will still accept the down input, the opposit direction to the characters' movement and anything in between.Last but not least there are scattered around the map some "flow bridges" which are key in obtaining source required to clean the rust off of the maps or to reach spots otherwise unreachable since you can ride them and they can elevate to highgrounds.Even these are not exempt from flaws. For once they don't become visible until a close range,   and becomes annoying trying to find them. Secondly, trying to find the right flow bridge required to reach other maps or highgrounds between the many present in each map is also frustrating, since they are not always facing the direction they will take you to, but can swirl and twirl and bring you somwhere you would have not guessed. Also as a side note some spots on the map force you to stop in a buggy way and some slopes that looks climeable are not, but these are way less of a problem even if frequent than everything else.Combat on the other hand is really good although it never goes too deep to develop it, it's still a nice concept and the developers state at the start of the game that it is not meant to be hard. Do not help your teammate if the enemy is performing an attack, since it will soft-lock the game (fixed in a patch).For the story some may find it really good, some boring. It touches very hard on the sexual part of a relationship, still light stuff keep in mind. Nothing obscene and when there is nudity is always censored.I'm not here to talk about it in depth since it's spoilers, but one thing it's sure. It is best experienced if you have a partner to play with, some scenes lose potential when played alone. This will be hard if your SO not accustomed to playing games, since they will probably hate the unintuitive movement. (Turns out Co-op mode is not really a built in experience but more of a gimmick, so one of the two would just have to watch the other play for most of the time)The art style has it's good points and really emphasizes the scenery, the purple palette when used it's amazing. On the other hand the 2 main protagonists would have benefit a lot from cell shading and marked outlines to define their faces, since they look like a blob of the same color without depth. The devs' previous game, Furi, used the same art style, but there it was more effective since the characters had more complex  models which added more volume to their bodies and feature that made them stand out more, thanks partly to light having more surface to hit, and creating more shadows for added details.I don't recommend it unless you are fond of the genre and of wasting more time going backwards than going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! I'm debating on doing a second playthrough, partially to play with the male version of the couple (I played this one with the ladies) and partially to more completely play through it. I did still complete a lot of stuff even without aiming to 100% it, but there were definitely areas I hadn't explored and I had gotten close to but had not hit maximum romance level. I'm curious if there might be some more answers for certain threads and ideas that hadn't really been explored, but considering this game's focus on the couple's relationship maybe not. Game itself was gorgeous, the colors pop in the right ways, and it was quite fun to glide around once I got the hang of it. Combat's still a bit clunky though, especially with some enemies and combos that are needed, but it's got a bit of a quirky charm to it. Overall I'd say this game is worth a play.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game, easily 10/10 in the running for my favorite game of all time.  That being said it is not perfect.  But the thing that holds everything together is the love between the 2 main cast.  It is done wonderfully, I love these 2 to death and they have amazing chemistry and they are the perfect level of quirky that I just love them.  But because everything is tied to them and their relationship, if you don't absolutely love it then you might not have a fun time.  The story is nice, the worldbuilding is great, but it isn't active enough (at least to where I am) to carry the game without caring about these 2's relationship.  The game mechanics also are not enough to do it either, and I would even say some of the mechanics are a little lacking, but if you are as invested in the main 2 characters as I am then it doesn't matter.  The only "problems" I would say it has is the models are a bit basic at times, especially in comparison to the drawn images, but honestly its something you notice every once in a while and immediately forget it.  The music is also pretty nice, but it is all the same-ish genre so if you don't care for it then it will get old REALLY fast.  The game also lags a bit each time you clear an isle but it only lasts a second or 2.There is only 1 main issue with the story and that is SPOILERS: a game about a couple has a point where they get in a fight and "break up", and honestly the game did not convey why that particular thing was such a big deal.  It kinda seemed like they made it seem worse just to have the break up.  But all in all the break up doesn't last long so even though I don't think the actual breaking up was done well, they did have them go through a neat sequence and get back together after not too long.Being objective, this is probably an 8/10, maybe 9/10 considering it's an indie game.  But god I love this game so much that I cannot recommend it enough.  If you can get invested in the 2 main characters and you at least have a passing interest in the mechanics then this game can easily become one of your favorites.  As with many story-driven games, I would say Haven has little replay value (unless you play it with someone else the 2nd time, then it'll be a blast).
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game with my husband on 2 computers. I can't really recommend it, but it's not all bad. It depends on your expectations. 1. This game is cute because of the relationship and the story. 2. It is a bit boring in terms of exploring. Cleaning rust becomes repetative fast and you need to go around a lot just looking for that last piece of rust somewhere, to make that planet fully cleansed. 2. Unfortunatley I got the impression that this game is for two people playing together, but I realize that I misunderstood or that it is not made for playing on computer. The thing is that you should only buy one game and then both of you log in to the same account. (I waited too long to return mine.) That means you are not playing and controling one character each. You are each playing both of them but at the same time, always taking turns, since only one can be i in control of both characters who always go together everywhere, and the other player can mainly watch. Well you both are technically in control all the time. So you need to decide who is playing. 3. When flying you can cooperate, which sometimes makes it a little easier, but flying is in general very annoying because of the sharp turns. We might try it out a bit more, but maybe I just don't have the patience for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who can't get enough of story-driven games, this game hooked me right away, It's like playing through a very wholesome sci-fi shoujo manga. The couple's relationship feels so natural with minor daily interactions you normally don't see portrayed in any media. The plot also has a nice mystery to discover. The gameplay feels a little too relaxed and you can see that the devs intended for a satisfactory kind of gameplay, floating around and stuff, though the controls could be better and the exploration a little more rewarding. This game just begs to be played along a significant other, so the fact that I still played it even with my lack of a significant other being shoved in my face shows how pleasing the game is.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: A solid, small game that hits all the right beats. Gameplay is a bit shallow overall, but the main focus is the story and the relationship between Kay and Yu, and the gameplay serves more as a medium explore this. The characters are solidly written, their relationship is realistic, and leaves just enough questions to make you want more. 8/10 from me, will play again
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Haven did something that other, more expensive story-based games only wish they could accomplish. The romance between the two protagonists is intense, believable, adult without being graphic, and a pleasure to be party to. I fell into the love story of these two so deeply that I experienced real, honest regret at progressing the story, knowing there must be inevitable struggles in the future, but at the same time I found it impossible to put the game down. Its very short, and there isn't much challenge, but the many mechanics, from movement, crafting, and combat, are complex enough and unique enough to be interesting, adding exactly what the game needs to break up the charming and sincere interactions. The universe building is also fantastic; the immersion was complete, and I truly believed that these two characters lived in a universe where the society they discuss existed, even though the player hardly ever sees any evidence of that society. If you are in any way a lover of good love stories, imaginative Sci-Fi, or want a good cozy game to kill 20 - 30 hours with, you need Haven in your library. The game is criminally underrated, and I both find myself hoping that the creators will do more in this universe, and fearful that any addition would not, could not, compare.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent love story, broken up by pretty fun exploration and kind of mediocre combat.  It has a banger soundtrack and great voice acting.  Highly recommended, just keep in mind you're playing it for the story and atmosphere - this game is _nothing at all_ like the developer's previous game Furi, which is also great.

_childDocuments_.review: + Good game with a mix of RPG-lite elements and action-adventure+ Great character development between the two MC's, Yu and Kay+ Art design is really great+ Absolutely killer soundtrack composed by Danger- Confidence system isn't fully explained; you can't tell who has more confidence between the two main characters- The decisions you choose don't change the outcome of the story- Little to no replayabilityI went in with no expectations but enjoyed the time I had with the game.Solely bought it because Danger produced the OST, as well as having played The Game Baker's previous title, Furi, which is also a very good game with a great OST.Definitely will be looking forward to their next project.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review because i think this game and the devs deserve more recognition.If you're looking for cool gameplay, i don't think this game is for you; Haven is a story-based game; it's like a visual novel walking simulator with small bits of not challenging combat.While there's a lot of flaws in Haven (Most of the locations have little variety until about 4-6 hours in; Gliding around can be uncomfortable sometimes; Combat isn't that interesting; A few typos in dialogues, which aren't that important, but still this can bother a little) if you look past them you'll find the game pretty enjoyable and relaxing. The game is really atmospheric and all conversations between Kay and Yu feel so natural. Soundtrack is awesome. I loved the story and the feelings Haven gave me; the ending might make you think for a while.  I can't call Haven a masterpiece, but i like it a lot and i see how much love the devs put into it. I'm excited to see what new great games will the Game Bakers have to offer. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: FIrst off, I want to preface this by saying I enjoyed this game up to the amount of time I've played it so far.I see only one thing that needs to change: the loading transition on the flow bridges. For a game with such outstanding visual style, it is far too cheesy. Some of the dialogue is a bit cringy to be honest while other parts of it are very endearing. This game has a lot of heart and soul to it which is a nice change of pace from many story based games.The main characters are pretty interesting. Personally, I would have picked a different voice actor for the lead female protagonist because she sounds like every generic college girl on my campus. That said the voice acting is well done regardless of personal preference. English falls short in tone a lot, but these voice actors did a great job of not continuing that trend.The one major issue I take with this game is I can tell it was made by a Western mindset. (This has very little to do with modern day social political bs and much more to do with the dialogue/themes). It really is not an issue unless you have niche tastes or are tired of Western works (which I am at this point).This game bleeds the influence of Emeric Thoa. It has so much personality and quality game feel mixed into it that even if you only have an hour a day to play - it truly is worth spending that hour relaxing in Haven. I read a little about Thoa-san's design philosophy (would like to read more haha) and I think that he was absolutely correct. This game cannot please everyone - myself included - but the soul put into it can soothe almost everyone if they just relax. The soundtrack to the game aids this very effectively alongside the charming visuals.Cheers for the great title. This game is worth full price if you enjoy games that focus on a single mechanic surrounded by quality-of-life features.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 I absolutely recommend this game!My fiancee and I played this game together and we found it to be very enjoyable. It was a delightful co-op experience. For co-op mechanics, one person generally takes the lead, but there are plenty of ways for both players to participate throughout the game. It has a beautiful art style, engaging story, and wonderful relationship portrayal.  I found the combat to be simple and fun, but still challenging at times. I loved the creatures, voice acting, music, and the overall feeling of the game. This game was a beautiful escape for us in the challenging pandemic world. I highly recommend it for single players or a relaxed co-op experience.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I am really enjoying the game. It runs very smooth, even on older hardware on the highest setting; between 80 and 144 fps with a gtx 970 at 1440p. The graphics are a little on the simplistic side, but overall still very enjoyable with great color choice. In any case, buy this game for the story. It's a mature love story and the interactions between the two characters are great and honestly really authentic sounding. The RPG element and game portion is there really just there to tell these two lovers story. Is the game worth it at full price? Absolutely! If you like the feel of the story from the trailer videos, you'll like the game. It's a great game to chill and get lost in another world.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Sweet, fun, heart warming. Not the things you usually see in an action game. Couples update also makes it possible to experience love stories most games doesn't include. That inclusion means a lot, so thank you The Game Bakers! Love to see the wardrobe options available for all however!The graphics is not AA level, but the visuals are still stunning. Soundtrack is awesome, music by Danger was a nice surprise. The game play is maybe a bit repetitive, but still feels fluid and enjoyable, at least for me. The voice acting was good, since I played M/M I only heard those. The quality for the mic/studio wasn't really top notch, but that didn't matter much in the end. The things that mattered where all those small things that this game does great. Idle hugging animations that heals, the small loving jokes between the two and those small filler dialogues when they are going to bed, have a shower or just waiting for the bathroom.I would like to have seen some more polish on the ending however, it's a bit abrupt to me. But if it means we get to see a sequel I am all for it! All in all I love this game, it makes me feel warm, cozy, giggly and hopeful. Will replay it again soon!

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first play-through and all I can say is: This is quite simply the most organic depiction of a healthy relationship in a game I've ever seen. MAJOR kudos to the writer(s) and voice actors! I laughed, I cried, and I was moved by these two characters with every bit of dialogue.Pros: Lovable characters that take you through the highs and lows of any relationship.Fantastic score  by the very talented Danger!An atmosphere I find myself wanting to come back to. _childDocuments_.review: 12-18h 3/10 1 No Yes, multiple guides are available here on the steam guide section and on different console websites. I mostly used the guides on  4 on Astats No Yes, the one for don't have both characters dying at the same time. I think it kinda allows to have 3 ko's but I avoided ko's of both characters at all. If it happens you can quit the game and restart, it only saves when changing locations, so it shouldn't save after you die.  No No No No No, you can play on the easier difficulty, this makes the 3 optional bosses a lot easier NoWow.. this game blew me away, it was amazing! I was already very impressed by the voice acting and artwork in the trailer and on screenshots. When I first started the game I felt a bit awkward.. the characters are very corny from time to time and I sometimes felt I should leave the room/game. Also, the controls to "flow" around take some time to get used to. After I got used to the controls the game started the become very addictive. The timing for adding new mechanics was so right in this game. For example, at the moment I started to become annoyed with having to walk back to their "home" I got the option to use some sort of flightpath back and forth. Storywise you get dropped in the middle of the story and first don't know much about what is going on, but piece by piece you get to understand more and more and it gets very interesting. The game has a good and a bad ending, but they both are bittersweet in some way and I felt emotional with both endings, which is a good sign, the writers did such a good job with building up the story and getting you to care for the characters. A few of the achievements are story-related, but most of them you have to trigger in some way or another. Don't worry too much about them at the start, just enjoy the game, clean up as many areas in the game as you can (Why does cleaning up in games feel so much better than IRL!) but most of all, don't have both characters ko-ed at the same time. As stated above by missable, the game only saves when you change locations, so if it happens, just quit and restart and you should be fine. The developers added the feature to save the game before you get to the endings and have to make an important decision, which is amazing, this way you can see both endings without having to backup your save or have to start all over again.I have 3 last tips for this game:- While playing through it, switch from the main character from time to time because there is a system for them picking up seeds, not any of the 2 can pick up them all, so switch after a while and later do that again and you probably get most of them without having to worry about them. - The second tip, switch the combat menu in the settings to just pressing the buttons instead of holding them, that way combat feels so much easier. - The last tip is related to battle... please please please ignore most of the tips the characters give you during combat. They kinda lean toward switching between the character that is shielding and the one that does damage, but this doesn't seem like the optimal strategy. I would suggest almost always shield with one character and do the damage with the other. I give this tip because if you stand still in a non-combat for a while the characters will hug each other and the one with the lowest health will get health up to the level the other character's health level is. So it makes much more sense to keep the health of one character as high as possible so you can easily heal after a battle is over. This game is amazing, lovely, and sometimes very corny, but I had such an amazing time playing through this game and I hope you will as well!

_childDocuments_.review: Twenty hours of a somewhat-flawed game carrying two of my favorite characters --ever-- in a kind of Romeo & Juliet story.The main reason I looked into the game in the first place is the art by Koyorin.  That's mostly isolated to loading screens and the minimal number of JRPG-style talky-pictures. But I stayed because I immediately fell in love with Kay and Yu. They're a young couple who are totally enamored with each other, and it shows in how they speak, how they act, and how they touch. Yu really likes Kay's butt, and tells him about it every chance she gets.But the game! Back on the subject... It is important to note that the game is built primarily as a vehicle to deliver the story, and it makes no secret of it. At the beginning it tells you that, while you *can* turn down the difficulty, you really won't need to.  Indeed, your first and biggest problem is not combat, but just getting around.The game takes place on a series of small islands connected by force-bridges. Your primary method of travel are your jet-boots that sling you around the island, just a little bit too fast. You won't die from cartwheeling off a cliff, but you might miss a turn and cartwheel off a cliff and lose your progress in a climb. You will need to get somewhat skilled at this, because progress will depend on you being able to trace glowing lines in mid-air. Your only other alternative is walking... and these two walk SLOOOOOW.  Your choices are therefore either too damn fast flying or too damn slow walking.So where do you go? When the game starts, you have crash landed and you don't have a map. I don't even recall if you have a compass. If you're paying attention, the characters will try to help you out a little ("Weren't we just here?"  "Doesn't that go back to where we came from?") But you might find yourself drawing the first six islands into your own map, just to survive.  Just when I could not put up with it anymore, the game granted me a map.  It's a limited map, only showing the island links and not the islands themselves.  The characters keep helpful and amusing notes on the map as things progress.  The map limitation mean you may still end up combing islands for that one last item or enemy.A little further along, you will also receive a kind of fast-travel, and while you will definitely depend on it, it ends up being rather expensive in time, resources, and effort.  You see, the game wants you to go home often. More on that later.Finally, combat.  There *is* combat in the game, but it is super-simplified JRPG-ish style. When you see an aggressive creature, you can sneak up on it or it may attack you.  The game will then drop into a battle mode, one of the places where the game's odd two-playerness triggers. Primarily, you select one of two attacks or a shield and hold a key to charge it.  Attacks are in real-time, and the game incentivizes cooperation between your characters.  If they are both selecting the same attack, they can do a timed-powerup for extra effect.  Battles get slightly more complicated as you are given some additional tools, and you come across creatures who are immune to some effects at some times -- usually clearly telegraphed and often narrated by your characters. "That didn't work!"In the end, however, the game is not about the combat, so you'll be out into the world again pretty quickly.  Enemies don't respawn while you're on an island, and don't respawn at all once you've cleaned an island.After your battle, you're going to be bruised and beaten and here is where you hit what is possibly the most frustrating game design choice: camps.  You can only, practically, heal when you're either at home or at a camp... and there are only, like, four camps in the whole game, so you may end up roaming the islands for a bit before you either get home or find a camp.Oh, yeah... the save-game function is totally screwed up, too.  Don't expect to reenter a saved game at the location you left it.Camps are where you can heal up, cook or eat food that might heal you, and finally sleep. Once you sleep, your turn is over and you can't use the camp again for a while...?  Your ship is the same, but is also where your characters interact and bond more. You can also build some items here, as those things are unlocked.  Building, including cooking, is the other place where that incentivized cooperation shows up.  One character chooses the left ingredient, and the other chooses the right ingredient, making for a final product.It's silly and just becomes annoying at later junctures where you're required to go through this whole presentation just to refill your items. [Edit: This may have been fixed in the latest update. The changelog says, "Multiple capsules can now be crafted at once".  Thanks!]In any event, the master mechanic of the game is that you cook a meal, eat it, go to bed, wake up, have another meal, and then go out for the day.  This is the loop, and the games enforces it, with hunger, limited camps, and limits on where you can heal up.  It's frustrating and breaks flow, and is another reason why this isn't a great game.But did I mention how much I love the characters??  Did I mention they advance their relationship with homebrew hooch?? This is some of the best voice acting in the business. I paid $17 bucks for the game at a sale, but I also picked up the soundtrack, too.  I don't know that I would recommend it at that price, but if it ever gets below $15, and you're feeling kinda romantic... this might be a good buy. You might even actually try to play the game with two players...?  It could happen.

_childDocuments_.review: Yu and Kay have fled from the Apiary and their strict Matchmaking system in a bid for their own freedom to love each other; against the odds, they find an uninhabited but fragmented planet named Source, and settle there. All is not completely peaceful, settling down on a new planet is a struggle in itself with dangers and food sources to be documented, on top of that, a strange Rust seems to be engulfing the planet turning peaceful creatures hostile that originates from... somewhere? Hopefully everything works out fine. 10-18+ hours, explore 42 Islands and enjoy the excellent story and worldbuilding! LGBTQ+ friendly, you can change the genders of Yu and Kay at the start of the game if the traditional male and female relationship doesn’t interest you. While playing, there is a heavy emphasis on Yu and Kay’s relationship and there are many options that let them grow closer together as you explore the small but rewarding Islands. Combat is easy but can be frustrating due to controlling two characters at once, and I suggest re-binding controls if you use the keyboard and have difficulty with recalling which keys do what. One of my favorite things in Haven was all the varying dialogue, despite the games potentially substantial length, there was always fresh dialogue between the couple and multiple events; also the Soundtrack is amazing!

_childDocuments_.review: A quintessentially French game. That's really all I have to say - it's really, really French, and it shows, from the art direction to the writing, with constant Euro-English quirks in the dialogue. It is also very cute, and I honestly wish more games like this would exist where the protagonists are in a relationship for the entire game.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Look, this is not a bad game, but it absolutely is not for everyone. The story is great - I was charmed by the protagonists and intrigued by the strange world they found themselves in.The combat, not so much - The combat cycle, which does make up a sizeable chunk of the games' playtime just felt slow, samey and boring to me. Now I love a good strategy, turn-based game, but this isn't that either. The options you have are limited, and even if the creatures change, it's not like you have to change up your strategy all that much. I can certainly see the appeal if you are just looking for a chill game where you don't need to stress too much about the combat loop and just take it at a slow pace, but that isn't for me. I can also see how this game may work out well if you are playing co-op with a partner who is not too videogame inclined.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: You can really tell this game was a project the team loved, everything from the art to the music was just perfect. This game just made me feel good and it's exactly what I needed, the emotion you have while playing this game could probably be best described as zen.The credits, if you actually click to watch them in the menu were super touching as well. I don't think I've ever seen any project in my professional or personal life honor it's team members quite so externally and meaningfully. I definitely would like to see that more often.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great in a few ways, and really struggles in others. The story and characters are really great, and the loving and realistic relationship they have is something worth seeing. The music is also wonderful, and I really like the songs Danger made for the game. The art style is also fun, and I feel is a good balance between detail and artistic expression. However, the game-play is really lacking, and can easily become a struggle. I want to spend more time with Yu and Kay, but I don't want to do it in the context of the incredibly basic and monotonous game-play loop.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't mind awkward moments, despite how romantic and cute it is, this game's story is one I'd highly recommend playing through. The character development is one a person yearns for. The plot unfolds just as much as looking into a relationship.You can see a flower for what it is, but sometimes when you look closer, there may be damage within the petals. What matters is if it's still kept and cared for.That is what this story encompasses.

_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one for the story line. The story line is engaging, interesting and within a good duration. You can play with a significant other but it's a better experience when played solo as the co-op mechanism isn't too well worked out. The mechanism of the game itself is on the simple side, but this is not to say bad at all. Sometimes less is more. I love the gliding and the portals with the island-island style mapping but the fighting mechanism needs a tutorial as it can get confusing later on. The "confidence" mechanism where each character gets a confidence boost every time you make a certain decision seems wasted too, I think this can be integrated to the gameplay better. This is also a one off kind of game. It's not really replayable once the storyline is completed but the gameplay itself and the storyline makes up for the non-replayability. Overall, I would recommend this game. I will give it an 8.5/10 as there are some improvements that can be made.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: 100% recommend! This game has an insane amount of effort and detail worked into it. The characters feel like real people and the game also looks stunning! Combat is perfectly do-able, something I can appreciate. While running around the characters often comment on things as well as each other and there are a lot of things to explore, wait for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is an amazing game for what it is. The story and world are beautiful and impressively made, with not only charming attention to detail but a clear passion for the game itself. Haven above all else will leave you feeling good and motivated to follow your dreams. The message of this game is about fighting for freedom, and it shares that message brilliantly.

_childDocuments_.review: So as of writing this review I haven't finished the main story of this game but I just wanted to say my expectations were low based off other reviews about it being boring. Well I'm here to say that I find this game anything but boring and was blown away by the amount of content here. I love the exploration the dynamic between the two characters especially when they have a moment to themselves and there's actual backstory that makes you fill in the gaps and keeps you wondering about the time before the game takes place. _childDocuments_.review: 2024 Update: after finally playing through a game with the couple gender-selector DLC (I forget the name it's been a while) the addition of having a F/F and M/M adds additional flavor for those who may prefer them, but because the recordings were done during COVID lockdown the audio quality is not uniform.Before I bought this game I had never heard of The Game Bakers, but after playing it they have my attention and I hope they do more.Haven is a gameplay experience unlike anything I've ever had before.  It almost seamlessly blends in the chillness of environmental games like Abzu and Flower with the drive to explore and complete from Super Mario Sunshine, all the while keeping focus on the main protagonists, whose life on this world is the main attraction.  This is the sort of game you would pick up when you need to just lose yourself in someone else's story with calming music and lovely places.This game is not perfect, and the drawbacks remained constant through the game:1) The combat system draws heavily from 90's Final Fantasies where action bars fill up before taking actions and combat is never on pause, but the execution of acting and being acted upon breaks the flow of combat regularly, twice causing my game to lock up when trying to revive my partner.2) The movement is primarily driven by anti-grav boots, like a sci-fi Tony Hawk, which serves the purpose of a) sprinting, b) riding special rails around the area, and c) cleaning up the rust.  The system is less forgiving on Mouse & Keyboard than it should be, and more often than not my movement would be halted randomly until I re-positioned on foot and took off again, which was frustrating.In spite of the drawbacks this game kept me thoroughly engrossed and entertained, and most importantly it made me feel relaxed, which is Haven's strongest selling point.  The game can be cleared in 10-20 hours on the first run, probably less on subsequent playthroughs, which feels right for this type of game.  If you're looking for a unique experience in calm storytelling, this title is worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: It breaks my heart to give this a thumbs down, but there is no half-way thumb.The art, music, and design are beautiful.  The writing and the natural, organic feel of the way the characters interact was fantastic.  Anyone who has been in a committed relationship can appreciate the struggles Yu and Kay face.Where it fell down for me was the ending.  I won't post spoilers, but I personally found the end options to be very unsatisfying.  After the incredible writing of the rest of the story, the lackluster finish felt like the author had walked up behind me and flipped the book out of my hands while extending a middle finger.Now, other games have had bad/lackluster endings (Looking at you Mass Effect 3, and I see you hiding there Cyberpunk), but they have repeatability for their game aspects.  I will still play through Mass Effect from time to time because the core game loop is fun.  Same for many other RPGs, from eight bit classics like Final Fantasy to AAA monsters like Cyberpunk.  The game elements in Haven aren't bad, but I can not see myself repeating the game just to clear rust or fight the monsters.  The story is what held this game up, and it dropped the ball in the last ten yards.If you want a fantastic, story-driven game, there are many options, but unless you are into bittersweet endings, I'd give this one a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: In some unspecified future, humanity is ruled by a quasi-dictatorial, interplanetary regime. This regime is aided by an entity known as the Matchmaker which determines who will marry who. Ostensibly, this system of arranged weddings was created to resolve some defect known as the mark and was allowed to continue since. Clearly, in such a society, there is no room for romance. Two young people though, Yu and Kay, still manage to fall in love and decide that they can't let the Matchmaker decide their fates. In an act of defiance they escape to a long abandoned colony, in the cracked remnants of a destroyed planet. The game follows the two teens as they try to salvage material to repair their damaged ship, as well as get acclimated to a life together as exiles, fugitives and lovers.The premise is indeed fairly interesting and provides a solid foundation. It's a shame that it doesn't quite deliver. The characters and their relationship are supposed to be the highlight of the game. They are well voiced and well-designed, at least the default couple is. But they are not good enough to carry this game. There is a fair degree of cringe and disappointing developments in their relationship. Arguably, the game seems more interested in tearing down heteronormative standards than telling a good story. Kay, the boy, has to be the sensitive feminine one. Yu, the girl, has to be the decisive masculine one. This creates a fair number of awkward interactions, with Yu for instance being presented as lecherous at times, or refusing to help with housework. Don't worry, it's ok when the girl does it.This attempt to showcase the normalisation of such "alternative" couplings extends to the only other couple in the game. Yu's mothers. A lesbian couple. You would think that a society defined by arranged marriages for the sake of offspring would know better than to marry people of the same sex. Apparently not. Yes, the game is obviously playing identity politics. But you know what, even propaganda can be enjoyable, it can be fun. In fact, if it wants to be effective, it often should be. Herein lies the greater issue. Haven isn't particularly fun. It's one large fetch it mission where you drift from one semi-identical floating island to the next. Gathering stuff, fighting enemies, coming home to sleep and watch some cutscenes. Rinse and repeat. Initially, the exploration seemed to work, I was curious to see what's next, but the repetition soon numbed me. The promise of a heartwarming, romantic tale is what sold me on Haven. That promise it somewhat delivers, in a fashion. That delivery was not enough to make this a game I wanted to come back to. It could be that I'm not fond of playing the same sequence again and again. It could be that I'm just too old and jaded to be moved by the woke koolaid on offer. Whatever the case Haven disappointed, as such, I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is first a story before being a game.The game part is based on free exploration, very delightful because you are gliding at high speed on the grass and in the air. This exploration is well rewarded by dialogs or unique items.Then comes combats, which are not difficult and are based on cooperation, protecting each other and launching combined attacks. It's well done, but not everybody will like it.I loved the story, for all the details put in the game about the characters, for both characters trying to be strong and support each other, for all the discussions between them (and there are a lot of them). We are living their daily life, simply and shamelessly. We are seeing them fight, cry, laugh, flirt... I loved the humour in some cutscenes, the fact that in most of dialogs we have to choose if the characters feel confident or not. This is well written and well realised.We have here a lovely couple, with brilliant colours, beautiful soundtrack and a nice romantic and personal story. Cherry on the top, the voice acting is perfect!On the bad side, I think the game need an anti-aliasing, because the 3D view is not verry pretty and detailed. This is invisible while moving and exploring, but not at all when we are immobile for a dialog. Thankfully, while in dialog, beautiful 2D sprites of Yu and Kay are in the foreground, and after a couple hour, we forget the less detailed 3D model to focus on the 2D characters.I had an incredible good time playing Haven, and I think I will do it again, it's calm, reposing, relaxing, intimate and peaceful. You want to play it slowly and not miss any dialog, interaction, detail the game is made of.What else can I say? Except if you seek a nervous, active solo game like Furi, I think this game may pleased you.

This is  noticeable later on in the game when you might want to revisit islands that you've already cleared.Your character will flip and do a 180(flipping your camera as well) if given the command to move opposite their current direction. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful artistic space sci-fi adventure romance game. Exploring the beautiful vistas, discovering the story behind the two lovers. After 2 hours into the game, you'll notice that there are keys you're supposed to be press at the same time. It feels like you're supposed to be play this game with 2 persons. I love coop games, but i'm not interested in forced solo coop play mechanics. As an azerty keyboard person, all controls are just scrambled and unusable. It would have been nice if you could edit ALL the keys, but apparently the devs didn't think this was necessary to do so. The fact that this game is already out for so long and this hasn't been fixed, baffles me. Especially when you can't edit your AZERTY keys. It's a shame, because it feels like they have put a lot of effort and quality into this game, but I can't continue playing this game. _childDocuments_.review: A particularly well-written and overall decent game with gameplay that can get stale. The general plot is pretty basic but the character-focused writing and great world building not only saves it but also makes it shine. The characters and their interactions are the best part of this game. The game expresses the themes of love and freedom particularly well, both through its narrative and its mechanics. Unfortunately, the latter of these, mainly those regarding traversal, get somewhat repetitive since there really isn’t any meaningful upgrades or changes to the main gameplay loop to freshen things up. The combat should have also had some more fine-tuning. The soundtrack is really good. Haven is a game that I really liked since it knew how to tell a good story with endearing characters. It’s just a shame that the means in which it does so, happens to be a game that gets dull in the long run. But I must admit that the emotional impact the narrative left on me and the resonant serene beauty of the experience make me want to overlook a lot of its faults. If you are mainly looking for a pleasant story with endearing characters and can bear with some monotonous gameplay, go for it. I recommend it.

The only issues we've had are input lag when long distance, but trying to play in real time on the opposite sides of the world is not really something I can blame the devs for.I have my doubts as to the viability of this as a solo experience, but as something for you and your partner to play together, I can highly recommend it.
