_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this because I saw all the work behind it and I liked the concept, but as I write this review I am close to the end of the game, yet I couldn't bring myself to finish it. It may not be for everyone, and here's why:Pros:-Cute romance theme, well achieved, characters' interactions are interesting.-Very good art.-Characters express themselves in convincing ways, it really does make you feel the couple, both in good and bad situations; it's not overly dramatic, and includes every day scenes.-Pretty chill experience to have with someone else.Cons:-Art looks good. In-game graphics don't.-Gameplay is two-player based, all the time. There isn't a 'one player' option in which the gameplay of player 2 is automated, you always have to act for both characters, even if playing on your own. This is especially annoying and confusing in combat.-The game itself, outside of story, gets very repetitive very soon. The weird mechanics of it are interesting enough to keep you playing for some time, but not for the whole of it, I believe.-Note for potential buyers:Overall, the game is good if you have someone to play it with and you are both into the couple theme, as that is the complete centre of the game. If you play with someone who isn't into it they'll get bored and you'll feel awkward, and if you play it on your own it is way more often the kind of story to make you feel sad that you don't have that special someone, rather than to make you wish for that someone to arrive someday in your life.-Note for developers:This may sound silly to complain about, but when making, or at least at the polishing state of game development, you should definitely keep in mind the impact that the game has on your players, especially if the gameplay isn't all that fun in itself and the aim of the story is to make the player feel attached. As game developers you can argue that your target audience is couples, but that's just cutting yourselves too short. Most the problems this game has for single players (likely the majority of players, ironically) could be easily fixed, if the developers had into consideration a broader audience. That being said, I did like the concept of the game, and I really did like the characters and their interactions. Can't say I regret buying and playing it, but having all of my attention from the beginning, it wouldn't have taken too much to keep me invested, yet it didn't.

_childDocuments_.review: story of star-crossed lovers fighting for freedom rescues an otherwise average adventure game, with cobbled-together mechanics to support its quasi-RPG status. It's heavy on dialogue, chock full of scripted elements and has a tight yet admittedly basic loop where you eat, fight, flirt and fly within the fictional solace of Source. I have to say, I wasn't all that engaged for most of the time I spent with ; But a vague interest in the possibility of an optimistic end for our lovers, Yu and Kay, saw me through. Tied together by an empathetic performance from their respective VAs, their story is emotional, intimate and a source of constant joy - the chemistry between them emanates from the screen. So by the end, whichever conclusion you choose (or maybe even both like I did) you will likely be crushed that the journey is over as soon as it finally hits its stride. You'll miss the times spent with our pair, who have become painfully familiar in just a few hours. Inspiring, but basic. Ambitious but often falls short. It is not a game without flaws, but the story it tells is worth sticking around for.

_childDocuments_.review: The meat and potatoes of the game is the interactions between the two characters. If you don't like their dynamic, you will likely not enjoy the game. There's an overarching plot, some world building, and even some environmental storytelling, it's engaging enough, but the story is too rushed to actually go anywhere, and at a point it feels like an anime. Where you get introduced to a character/obstacle, and it is immediately made irrelevant.I would've liked this game to be a little bit longer so that the story around the characters could've gotten fleshed out more.I think making the game longer could've also fleshed out some of the more interesting/engaging aspects of the game-play as well, like base-building and gardening.  Overall though, because I dug the dynamic, I'd say it was a really nice 10 hour experience. Would recommend. Also; the soundtrack is worth 10$ all by itself, it slaps.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is NOT co-op.  The Co-op button on the main menu doesn't start a co-op version of the game, it just gives some instructions on how to get started once in the single player game.  (And those instructions are to just press any button on the second controller) Once you connect via remote play (Two players local should work the same, but take this with a grain of salt) you are given the very underwhelming options of ONE person controlling everything and the second the other player touches their controller (Or keyboard) you are in a desperate fight for control over one of the characters.That's right, while the game is ALL about a couple, you only control one of them at a time.  Player 1 and 2 do not pick a character to control, both zipping around and flying by themselves.  No, you control the same character at the same time so you get to watch as Kay or Yu spins and tries to listen to two sets of commands at once while the other character follows, possibly wondering why their lover is acting drunk.  There isn't even player 1 and player 2 dialog options, when Yu has a dialog choice, anybody can select it.  At the very least you would have thought they could make it so players were assigned characters in the dialog scenes, but no.While an absolutely charming and lovely game from what I played single player, the co-op is just a miserable, frustrating display of disappointing choices and misleading tags.  If you're going to play this solo, consider this a positive review and a recommendation to anybody looking for a beautiful setting, interesting story and likable characters.However, if like me you were looking for a "Shared/split screen co-op" game that you can "remote play together", this is a hard pass.  Co-op is not only optional, it's sub optimal.Playing any other single player game with your friends randomly interrupting you moving is just as co-op as this game.  Judging by this game's definition of Co-op, ANYTHING is co-op.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews for games very often, but I really enjoyed this one.Gameplay is so so, the gliding was a lot of fun once you got the hang of it, combat was pretty meh.The story and characters, however, really are what make this game special. _childDocuments_.review: Haven is a game that defies regular genres, so the best way to describe it is "A game where you follow the lives of Kay and Yu as they build their life and relationship on an alien planet".The game mechanics are not complicated or hard to understand and there is very little combat, but that's definitely not the main draw of the game, but rather the way the game works so synergistically (if that's even a real word) to convey the relationship between the main characters. From how the conversations play out, having you decide what both characters say and  how they interact with each other to what choices they make.Haven is perhaps the best game I've every played in my entire life that replicates a relationship, be it sweet parts and the rough parts of it. There are countless interactions between them and you learn more about them and you get to see them building their life and dealing with problems together.Haven is ultimately a game about relationships and you experience one of the best of them ever portrayed in fiction for that purpose.If I'm a stingy bastard and bought this game on release because the game deserves to be bought at full price, then this should tell how great this game is.PS: The soundtrack is super awesome. Do check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, Okay. I don't write reviews at all, but this game. This game, really made me want to write one.First off, You definitely 100%  need a controller to play this game. Don't ever use a keyboard it'll ruin the experience by A LOT.   The story in itself is pretty good not anything phenomenal, but good enough for it to be enjoyed till the end, What I love about most from the story is how dynamic and full of chemistry both the main characters were and are to each other. It felt real and full of life. They were very well written, full of conflicts and self passionsThe art style of the game is beautiful as well. Cute and filled with softness to it, absolute loved it.  The music albeit doesn't have a lot of tracks but I really enjoyed it, It gave sort of a electronic Lo-Fi vibe to it? (if that makes sense) I sometimes find myself just idling in game just to appreciate the music. Even now as I have completed the game I find myself going to Spotify just to listen to the album made by Danger.Now the combat of the game was what suprised me, I though it was going to be a traditional turn-based system like final fantasy and that kinda put me off. But, It's slighty different where there really isn't a per turn combat per se (y'all have to experience it to know what i'm saying lmao). It was refreshing and nice to see a different kind of combat system being used.Bought this game when it was on 50% sale, and I don't regret it at all (if i knew what i was getting into, I wouldn't mind paying full price tbh). It's a neat game that you can finish within a weekend.Kudos to the developers and those who were involved in making this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.First off, the story is great. I really enjoy the characters and thought they were interesting and had good dialogue throughout the experience. Their designs are engaging and I enjoyed playing as both characters equally in the game. The soundtrack in the game is also wonderful, and I think fits the artistic direction and aesthetic that the game was going for extremely well. Never had an experience where it felt jarring or the music stood out to me in a bad way. Combat fits well with this game and has you power up moves for each character that will then launch when they are ready. At the same time, enemies are powering up and launching their own moves as well. There are some fights that require good timing and strategy as to how you will deal damage and win against certain enemies, as you'll find that certain attacks don't have much effectiveness, or some attacks will even be countered dealing damage to you should you attack at the wrong time. This in and of its self can actually be pretty frustrating sometimes as you'll find yourself winding up for a move and then letting go of the button for the move just a split second too soon and it will cancel the attack entirely. That being said, combat is not the main focus of the game and clearly focuses more on the characters and their interpersonal story. The mechanics and game play loop centered around gathering different ingredients for different food recipes is also satisfying and enjoyable to do, resulting in different dialogue and cut scenes for the characters based on what you make. I never ran into a situation in which I ran out of ingredients or found myself at some kind of disadvantage or soft lock because I wasn't able to make a certain recipe that would prepare me to go out and adventure. You explore the world primarily through your flow boots which are like little boosters on your boots that allow you to glide around the world and do tricks if you jump off of high places which is a pretty neat little thing to see as you beep bop around the different islets that you can explore. There's not a whole lot of variety in the islets themselves, but there's enough of a difference to warrant conversation and speculation from the characters to where you don't really notice it. What this game really gets right is the writing. It was awesome getting to watch and listen to the conversations and discussions that the main characters had, and how different responses would impact and cause reactions. This being a love story there are many instances of romance, and the game does a great job of making it approachable and tasteful, although sometimes direct. It's never heavy handed with it though which is nice. The voice actors for the story also did a phenomenal job and were great in delivering emotion and feeling in their lines. *NOTE: I played my entire way through as the two female leads which may impact the audio and character discussion following considering the ability to play as them came out in a free update after the game released. There are some things about the game that aren't that great. The audio mixing can be a bit off here and there. You'll notice, although rarely, that sometimes Yu or Kay's voice will get louder or quieter at random during certain conversations. There's some peaking here and there and sometimes certain voice lines sound spacious like they were recorded from farther away or in a bigger space with no sound absorption. It's not a big deal because I can probably count on one hand the amount of times any of this happened during my 20 something hours of playtime. The 2D avatars of Yu and Kay that pop up when they are having a conversation are different from their actual in game world models, You'll notice that's Yu's shoulder cowl/cover is on her right shoulder on her 2D avatar and on her in-game model it's on her left. Kay's necklace is on her 2D avatar, but does not show on her in-game model at all (which is a story relevant item). This isn't really a problem, and didn't bother me at all, it's just something I noticed near the very end of my playtime. Given these minor inconveniences, it stands to mention that I encountered no bugs or glitches during my playtime that impacted my experience or game play, so objectively speaking from a technical standpoint it was a flawless experience. And then there's the endings and after story content. Light spoilers ahead, but just in case,  ahead so beware:First off, I think it's pretty clear that of the two endings one is canon and is the intended ending for the story. The other is an arbitrary, unsatisfying, and disheartening conclusion that I believe does not fit the character development overall for Yu and Kay and serves to be the obligatory bad ending. There is also some after story content you can unlock in the form of My biggest complaint with this is that the content you unlock is  available for your characters should you have decided to play as two same sex leads (at least it isn't for the female ones). I find this odd considering that the update that included this after story content came out well before (half a year) the update that allowed you to play as the two same sex leads so it's a little confusing why it wouldn't have been designed from the beginning that these different sex characters would also have that content, but they don't, which is really unfortunate. Final thoughts:I give this game a solid 9/10. I enjoyed my time thoroughly throughout and I think this is a game you should grab at any price. I was also able to grab all of the other achievements I wanted in the game within several hours of game time after finishing the story for the first time, so it's not a hassle to 100% this game if that is something you are interested in.Ultimately I wish they would remove the bad ending and add the ability to  for the new same sex leads, female Kay and Male Yu. The fact you can't do this is really weird and, as mentioned previously, super unfortunate for an overall amazing experience of a game. The bad ending felt so bad after finishing the game initially with the good ending that I had to go back and play through the finale one final time to finish on the good ending so I didn't have to finish with the bad one. Objectively it's a terrible ending, I understand why it exists, but I wish it didn't have to.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really shocked me.Haven is exactly what it says on the tin, an RPG of two. Yet it does so much with so little. The rich story is almost all dialog coming from these two lovable characters.  Nigh every other bit of dialog is about them and their choices. The game play is simple and smooth, I mean the combat can be played with the joysticks alone.  The mostly barren world they flee too creates a palpable sense of beautiful loneliness. Helped in no small part by the spectacular score, which even more so evokes solitude. All be it a solitude of two.  It’s also worth noting that the leads can be any gender the player likes without any changes to the story, a solid illustration of the maxim “Love is Love”.   Haven uses its limited palate to make the experience tight and highly focused and yet the worldbuilding is incredible.  Though the story begins with their ages of planning and harrowing escape complete, effectively starting in the second act, Kay and Yu paint a detailed tapestry of their former home.  One that was on the surface lovely.  Collectables, warm reembraces and other things show part of what the sacrificed to be together , but that slowly gives way to fundamental evils.  After all, why else would they leave?  For such a bright hopeful story, I found myself chilled with each reveal of the cruelty that just barely holds it together...and genuinely anxiety at what would happen to Kay and Yu if they were caught.  Yet you likely might have picked up on that from the trailer.  This is not a game that feels like it’s trying to surprise you, heck the Steam store page lays most of the game’s cards on the table.  Yet the execution is so stelar it makes Haven feel like something more.  Despite being adorable, warm and funny, it is deep and mature in its themes. Completing it may leave you contemplating on it for days afterwards.  I could, truthful, say this is one of the best games I’ve ever played, but that feels, to me, disingenuous. It is a game and said gameplay is fun, but outside of some of the optional achievements its difficulty is such that anyone can complete it. Complete it not beat it.  Beating it implies Haven is trying to keep you from something  Not so, the developers clearly wanted it to be experienced fully.  In that regard I think we lucked out. We, as humans crave illusions, in books, films, games, etc. But they can’t create an emotional depth at the level of real life interactions. They can’t, I thought. For me, this one did.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this by saying this isn't the type of game I usually play, so it was a new experience for me.That said, I loved this game! I found the characters and writing to easily be the best part, with an interesting universe that left enough unexplained to provide intrigue (I like the route they took where you learn via conversations between the characters, not an exposition dump or wall of text). The characters are believable and play off of each other really well, so by the end of the game I really wanted things to work out for them. I'll avoid spoilers here, but I found the morally grey area that much of the game bases itself in to be refreshing, with both endings being good and bad in their own ways. That said, I know which I prefer. Also the music slaps, thank you Danger for gracing my ears. Favourite track plays at the end of the game :)Overall 9/10 at least, would recommend at full price, if you see it on sale (Like now, 11/22/21) pick it up, you won't regret it. The combat and exploration may be a bit shallow, but it serves as an opportunity for the characters to interact with one another moreso than being deep. Kind of like an interactive visual novel.

_childDocuments_.review: No good. It just... It just sucks and I'm so disappointed.It has all the ingredients of a perfect game, but everything is a chore when nothing should be. You play as both and neither of two disagreeable characters. Want to cook food? It's too late to be cooking! Want to explore? I'm too hungry and can't eat the food I brought until I'm at a designated camp site! Want to attack an enemy? You used the wrong type of attack! Want to double back and look at something? "Ugh! I hate walking!" And on and on.I thought the characters would get more likable as their stories were fleshed out, but after several hours it's still really hard to empathize with them. Particularly Yu, an all around poor sport and serial complainer. Kay is a little better, but his obliviousness to his partner's blatant disinterest is frustrating from the player's perspective.So between the game repeatedly whining at you for playing it wrong ("That's where we came from!"), the unlikable characters, an inability to USE ITEMS, a lack of on-screen romance or even friendly intimacy besides holding hands once in awhile, and the lack of a SAVE feature, you should just pass on this. A patch isn't going to fix how fundamentally broken the gameplay is relative to what I suspect most people interested in this game would expect.Co-op is also awful with no simple way to switch between characters and single-player controls merely split in half instead of unique controls for each player (one player always uses XYAB, one uses D-pad) and dialogues requiring dual input are needlessly painful: both players need to manually select the same dialogue option for conversations to proceed, for example, or both players need to "cancel" a crafting screen to exit it.There are way better chill couch co-op games and way better romance games depending on what you're into, but this... This isn't worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven radiates with love at every seam of its contours. From the careful attention that The Game Bakers paid to its accessible UX to the little unbidden affections like the plethora of loading screen artwork, every effort was invested to make this game welcoming. Any of Haven's weaker aspects ultimately feel like fertile ground other games should stride forward with and follow up on. Whether they heed that call or not, Haven is an incredible origin point for games that discard elaborate mechanical trappings and focus on committed relationships.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: fine, assuming you meter your expectations. the combat is NOT good. Furi's combat was really good, so this is disappointing, but this is a primarily story-based game and you can set the combat to autoplay and turn the difficulty setting down, so I'm not that annoyed about it. the actual core mechanic of Haven is sliding around on tiny little floating islands, running over big red patches of "rust" to clean them up, which is very satisfying.Story: AKA the whole reason to buy the game at all. i think Haven might actually be unique in that it's a game centered around an ongoing romantic relationship where the relationship itself isn't the driving force of the plot. long story short, Yu and Kay escaped from some kind of dystopian science fiction society and landed on a remote planet, the people from their old planet want them back, and they want to avoid that at all costs. the writing is pretty charming and the voice acting is REALLY good, especially considering that Furi was lackluster in that area. there is a bit of sexual content (mostly verbal) but it's not anything that'll get you banned off of twitch for breaking tos.Visuals: very Game Bakers-y. simple geometry and bright saturated colors. i understand that motion capture is complicated so i forgive the character animation being awful. what saves it is the portraits of Yu and Kay that show up at the bottom during dialogue choices. they're cute and super expressive.Characters: dips a little too far into the "whiny man / ♥♥♥♥♥♥ woman" archetype early on, but both characters really grew on me. there is one section where they have a fight which isn't avoidable via dialogue choices, but they almost immediately make up and reaffirm their love for each other, which is something i really appreciate as a lonely and easily stressed person.Things that annoyed me:game studios, please stop making up fake swear words because they sound ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid. if your game has sideboob and erotic roleplay in it i have no idea why you draw the line at "♥♥♥♥" and make them say "bloot" instead. godthere is a dialogue choice that determines if you get the good or the bad ending, and you get exactly one chance to pick it. now that's fine on its own but the problem is that the dialogue choice itself literally sounds like the exact opposite of what it actually means. FORTUNATELY you can just continue your save in the menu and it drops you into right before that choice is made. otherwise i would be real mad and also pretty depressed for the next week or so.overall i really enjoyed the story and gliding around on little islands.

_childDocuments_.review: Never thought the studio behind Furi (a bullet-hell boss-rush game) would come out with one of the best depictions of a tested relationship between two young adults, but here we are. The exploration and combat are sufficient gameplay distractions, and there's plenty on Source to discover. _childDocuments_.review: My first "meeting" with "The Game Bakers" (aka developers) was around 4 years ago on Playstation 4 via game called "Furi". It was stylish and challenging action game, with unique & original visual style and amazing combat & bosses.To my surprise, "Haven" is quite a different experience, compared to that game. And definitely not in a bad way, so, let's start!The game starts with a couple - Yu and Kay - living on a distant uninhabited planet. The setting is rather interesting, because it's a mix between..... Adam & Eve and Romeo & Juliet. That was unexpected.Both Yu and Kay got a "designated" soulmate assigned to them by "A MATCHMAKER" in their homeworld, but they fell in love with each other and decided to escape together, using Yu's handmade spaceship (nickname "Nest") to escape. This is for Romeo & Juliet-like part.And due to some events and "luck" they ended up on this unknown planet, being only one man and woman on entire planet. And this planet is now their "Haven".(Adam & Eve reference)Now, you need to survive on this planet, scavenging resources, growing food, repairing your heavily damaged spaceship and resolving the mysteries surrounding this planet, which shows you the signs of someone living here around 1000 years ago, but all information regarding colonization of this planet was erased from archives.  Can't be a coincidence, right? Put your detective glasses on, while watching hilarious interactions between two main characters. Janino Harouni (Yu) and Chris Lew Kum Hoi (Kay) did a really great job voicing those characters, kudos to them. I'm more comfortable with XBox controller, though. Tested both configurations, so, it's fine to use whatever you want.The game itself is not an open world, but it's really big zones, separated by "Flow Bridges"."Flow" is something like an energy, which you will collect and use during your adventure. If you feel controls a bit clunky at the start, play a bit more until you unlock more features.The battles are rather simple, but interesting at the same time. During the battles you have some commands available: - a melee type physical damage attack - ranged type magic (flow?) attack - use it if the enemy look in that particular character direction. - now this is an original one. When your enemies reach 0 HP, they won't die, but will be knocked out instead. You will need to use Pacify in order to calm them and release them in the wild. "But why do i need to use Pacify in the first place?" - because if you won't then the enemy will rise up again, just with less HP.Try to remember the enemies you encounter and their weakness to either Impact or Blast for easier time.When you receive damage, either sleep, eat nutrition food or use healing items. At the start your food/healing options rather limited, but it will be much better later. There's Boss enemies in the game, which have a lot of HP and require a specific unique tactic (sometimes) to beat them.Launching the same attack with two characters simultaneously will result in a DUO attack (not available at the start) which is much stronger, compared to 2x solo attacks. Use it well.A really great experience, with nice focus on romance, psychology, good humour and interesting story/setting. Even if you are a super casual gamer, you can still enjoy the story by playing easy difficulty without any troubles.The devs are really generous with a regional pricing policy, which i respect a lot, especially during these pandemic times. Huge thanks to them for that.If you like this game  then try the game i mentioned earlier in this review -> Furi. Beware, that game is really hard.- This review was presented to you by "Casual Game Reviews" Steam Curator.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven was really fun, and pretty short. I put 22 hours into the game, mostly at a leisurely pace, because the game is about the relationship between Yu and Kay, the protagonists... not heavy action or an intricate plot. To support this, many of the game's systems support putting the characters in places to interact with each other, and excursions outside into the world of Source, the planet the two characters are on, are eventually meant to push you back to their base so they can talk and let their relationship unfold more. Systems like hunger, battling, and exploration are tuned so that even if you're really good at avoiding fights or winning fights... or exploring while avoiding enemies... you're eventually pushed to a position where you need to go back to base or find a place to camp. And that's when the meat of the game continues to present itself. In some ways, I actually thought this made this game one of the better RPG's I've played in a long time... the mechanics are very simple, as is the story, but they work well together to flesh out the most important part of the game: the protagonists. It's not about superior boss fights or grinding... it's about two characters escaping their destiny by abandoning their world and everything they know in favor of a life together. Combat is pretty simple once you get the hang of it, and something I really like about the combat is that once you've cleared a zone, it's stays cleared! (with one exception.) I really enjoyed that feeling of progression and it made the choice of whether to press on or explore more meaningful. The only thing I want to add is that you should manage your expectations. Again... this is about the relationship of these two characters. There is a lot of well-acted dialogue between them. I found there was a great balance between exploring their relationships and exploring Source, and it was a stress-free experience. You should buy this game if you like a fun, easy, relaxing game about a couple playing Castaway in space, and dealing with the consequences of defying their society's laws. It's a very sweet, very grounded game in that sense... Yu and Kay feel very much like a real couple, complete with quirks and flaws, (and a lot of love), and since they are a couple from the start, you get to dive right into the middle of their relationship. As for the gameplay, it's mostly exploration and gathering, which some light combat to clear zones. Even failing at a battle is only a minor setback that pushes the couple back to the nearest camp to recoup and heal up. I got hooked pretty quick. The game's art style, music, and dialogue really had me wanting to see what was around the next bend and hear what Yu and Kay had to say next. It was a pleasure all the way to the end, and it was a game I couldn't put down... which is probably the best compliment I can give it!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: With this game, The Game Bakers cement themselves as more than a one hit wonder; Haven is another masterpiece that elevates games a medium. I could write a thesis on the themes on this game. Freedom, rebellion, love, how humanity progresses - it's all tackled with maturity and subtlety rarely seen in games. The story is the main reason you're here, and it doesn't let you down at any point. The gameplay, the second reason you're here, is an interesting, unique blend on tactical, turn based combat, and somehow manages to mix in the real time tactics without too much of a hitch. It's not on the same level as Furi (The Game Baker's other game), but then again, nothing is. It's not difficult, as it stresses at the beginning. If you're expecting another twitch-shot bullet hell, you won't find it. As for exploration and the other mechanics surrounding combat, it's engaging enough right up til the end. I didn't get bored of it, and honestly I'd have loved to do more.The music, composed by Danger, is also God-tier. You may know him from the work he did on Furi, and with Haven he manages to flex his ability to create incredibly emotional but distinctly Danger tracks. You won't find music like this anywhere else. It's truly something to behold. I implore you to check out the rest of his discography, but this may well be his magnum opus.Haven is beautiful in every aspect it can be. It's an exploration of humanity in a world and universe so different from our own, and yet so similar. Your life will be enriched through playing it, and if nothing else - it's gonna make you smile.

_childDocuments_.review: The Game Bakers decided to follow up their success with Furi, that being Haven. Where Furi was a boss rush that had to fit in character background and exposition in little segments to sew the boss fights together, Haven has combat secondary and is far more focused on developing the two characters.And given the time to get to know these characters, I absolutely fell in love with both. The world you explore is rich with mystery and personality, as there was no point I ever felt the game was getting too same-y. While the game isn't particularly difficult either, the secret bosses all gave me a run for my money and I found combat pretty satisfying regardless with rpg-style combat without taking turns.Haven is absolutely a game that needs to be played through blindly. It's not too difficult, and rewards players for exploring with rewards or extra dialogue pieces. It's very hard to find any gripes with this game, and the icing on this cake is that it lets you choose between a straight, gay or lesbian couple for full representation. These devs continually show a lot of care and love into their games.I love Haven to bits.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I loved watching these characters' relationship unfold. It's a very sweet and charming story with a simple exploration-based gameplay loop to lead you to more interactions and cutscenes between the main characters. This is very, very focused on the main relationship, so if you're looking for world building or a wider message, you may come away from this with a lot of unanswered questions. But if you just want a love story, then this game does it very well. It didn't hit me very hard emotionally, but it was still pleasant with an acceptable resolution if you don't think too hard about the implications. Also, bonus points for letting you be gay. The only thing I didn't enjoy was the combat. If they had left it out entirely, I would have been much happier. It's... fine. Like it's not terrible. It's just annoying or tedious sometimes to the point that I dreaded seeing enemies out and about that I knew I'd have to deal with eventually. It felt more like a chore than something I wanted to do. Oh well. At least everything else was still fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a relaxing solo game, with adorable main characters, and great music that I now listen to outside of the game to wind down. The game is beautiful, and rightfuly so, as it is all about exploration, getting to understand the universe Kay and Yu live in, and getting to know them while you pursue your main objective (which I shall not spoil for you). I had a hard time using "Flow threads" (a fun way to move around in the world) with mouse and keyboard, but once I plugged my controller and used it instead, it became fluid and fun.This game is chill, though there is a small combat system that gives you a bit to think and react, but just enough to be engaging for the length of the game, nothing too crazy, and I actually enjoyed it very much.I thought it was smart, elegant, relaxing, and came back to finish off some of the achievements even if I had gone through the story already.And I am secretly hoping to know what happens next for Yu and Kay (well, since this comment is public, it isn't a secret anymore!). It's so refreshing to see story telling around a healthy relationship, kinky, and yet every-day-brushing-your-teeth-together relatable. Thank you for this experience! I am sad that it's over, like a good book... and no, imagining volume 2 with the cows rebelling against the outlaws won't cut it for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven

_childDocuments_.review: What a horrible experience! I couldn't sleep the following night after I had completed it. So... The game follows the development and relationship of two characters. They are really well written and with likable personalities. They have a great dynamic and they have a lot of dialog, so there is always something new going on. I won't say much about them, their journey has to be experienced, not told. It's most of all a personal story, you are just a mere passenger that can make a nudge here and there, but it's a story first of all. You need to love and a appreciate a good narrative to like this game. The story has intentional holes that leaves you guessing and questioning. The gameplay can be repetitive and in the end I found it a bit boring, but I guess that it would be natural if you were isolated on a planet with nothing else to do. The combat was good and simple, but still with a fair amount of depth, I felt it was okay for the length of the story. In conclusion, if you like me are a sucker for a good narrative, this is a must play. And if you like me is able to fall in love with a character like I did with Yu and Kay, then no matter what ending you will get, it will hurt, it will hurt a lot. One a lot more than the other though. So when I say it was a horrible experience and I didn't sleep the following night, it was because it was one of those experiences where you'd wish you could continue the story, to see more of their relationship and maybe, just maybe... Kick someone for ever dreaming of making THAT bad ending. Definitely one of the best emotional games I have played in years. TLDR:Story 10/10Gameplay 7/10Art style 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Haven exudes an amount of confidence that’s not often seen. Every piece falls into its place and there is never a moment to suggest that developer The Game Bakers had any doubts about the direction in which it wanted to take the game. Its satisfying exploration of interconnected levels, light survival, story-driven visual novel elements, and rhythmic combat all serve the greater experience. It boasts some of the most organic writing we’ve seen in a while and strong protagonists with excellent chemistry. Kay and Yu embody weakness and strength, childlike wonder and maturity, and kick ass together when the need arises. It’s hard to dislike them. Regardless if you’re in it just for its story or want to see everything it has to offer, Haven always finds a way to reward you and never wastes your time. .

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, let's get real. Spoiler free review ahead.I've just finished the game and, wow, what an ending. And as much as I may love the soundtrack, the characters and the animals living in this world...The game seriously feels unfinished. The entire time I felt like I was playing an alpha version of one of the futures greatest game ever. But its not. This is the finished game.The combat is completely simple: you have 2 different kind of attacks (which some enemies might be weaker against one and stronger against the other), a 'pacify' move which you use after draining all of the HP of an enemy, and a shield move. That's it. After a while the game adds a couple of more mechanics but the combat is extremely simple. And it's extremely hard to die in the game unless you're stubborn and refuse to go to a safe spot (which takes a while to reach one due to the many loading screens in the way) to heal or sleep. The game has a drastic difficulty spike in like, its last 30 minutes, but that's understandable. At the end the game basically hands you over for free an infinite amount of fruits and rust so you can freely explore everything before reaching the point of no return. One thing I disliked is the map. You get it a bit late into the game, like an hour or so into the game. This game has something called "flow threads" which are basically thin floaty paths you follow to reach some other place in the same area, like a floating island for example, along with "flow bridges" which allow you to move between areas. And the map might tell you, for example, you have an unexplored area to the north. But to reach THAT flow bridge to go towards the north, you FIRST have to FIND the flow thread which allows you to reach it. And sometimes you will spend HOURS trying to find the specific flow thread you have to follow to reach the area. Because they're not intuitive. That's an issue I have. The map is not intuitive and the flow threads are too confusing and scattered around. It's awful visiting an area you've already seen before, yet having to spend 30 minutes walking in circles until you happen to stumble upon a random flow thread that takes you to where you want to go.Another is the lack of 'visible' events besides the ones that happen at home. You will find a bunch of buildings outside in the world which the protagonists enter to explore, however you aren't able to see what is happening inside them. It's all dialogue which is a bit lame. And the dialogue brings me to another thing...I noticed more than a few mistakes on the subtitles. Double spaces, mixed letters like "tihs" instead of "this" or sometimes I feel like the subtitles were made for a line that was replaced after the subtitle was done, because the words or the verbs didn't match up completely. You can also tell when some voice lines were recorded on a different microphone or something, as they sound distinctly different, but that hardly happens at all.Cleaning up all of the rust and beating every enemy sometimes did feel like a chore. Walk around the island, blast enemies away until they all die, or just fly around until you find the flow thread you need to reach the top of the island and clear the final bit of rust.I also hated the wonkiness of the movement. Sometimes you jumped off a small cliff but the game would place an invisible wall in the air for no good reason at all. Or sometimes the characters do not want to fly over a little rock and you have to go aaaall the way around to the intended path.Overall, is the game good? Yes, it is. Should you buy it if you have the money for it? Sure, go ahead. But it really feels like I'm playing a pre-release version of it. This doesn't feel like a finished product. The areas get repetitive, they're all the same, the islands look too artificially chopped up, the combat is really simple, moving between islands isn't as fast as it should be... I can't say I'd recommend this game to someone that had to choose only one game to play for the rest of their lives.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute pleasure to play. _childDocuments_.review: Great little game. The gameplay itself is somewhat basic - flying around removing 'rust' from the various islands that make up the planet of Source, and battling monsters that get in the way. Combat is fairly basic but does get more complex later but is more a test of dexterity than strategy. There's some crafting to make food and buffs and you are travelling around trying to find pieces to repair your ship ('the nest').What absolutely makes this game however is the characters. I have never seen a game in which 2 characters are written so very obviously and authentically in love. This is not a game to play if nursing a recent breakup as it is joyous in the way the characters adore each other. The world building and story are strong but again, carried to impressive heights by the characterisation. There is a sexual tone to it, and some risque dialogue, but mostly its just genuine, warm affection.Its worth playing just for that alone. The rest of the game is decent (graphics, sound, achievements, crafting etc) but that's almost just a backdrop to what this game really is. An absolutely delightful love story.

_childDocuments_.review: Few games hit me in the feels like this.  One, was Life is Strange. I never thought I would find a story so real, and yet, fantasy at the same time.  I never thought I would find another Chloe and Max.  I was wrong.  It was another "Kiss or Town" moment.  I was always "Max and Chloe Forever" (If you know, you know)  And there seems to be the same level choice in this.  I chose "Yu and Kay" and didn't look back.Yu and Kay are just the cutest couple ever.   It isn't the large romance scenes or anything, but the every day life.  Watching them grow together and find their own way.  This game had me in tears so many times because the writing hit the perfect note, when it needed to.  The combat was a little annoying, but I learned and managed.  Still need to get some of the bigger enemies, but I will try that another time.  For now, like Yu and Kay.... I will rest and remember all that happened.If you are on the fence about this game.  Get it now.  If you love cute romance.  Get this now.  If you want a story that keeps you invented.  Get this now.  If you want a story that lets two people find their way into each other's arms... well, you get the picture.9/10 for me (Only cause combat is screwy)

The voice acting is spectacular. Flawless from what I saw. The art design, colour scheme, and level design had much to appreciate, I won't forget it any time soon. The story is great fun and I found the conclusion and epilogue to be both surprising, bittersweet and very satisfying.Before I played this game I thought my favourite Indie game of this year was Cloudpunk. Haven is better, it's difficult for me to measure exactly how but Cloudpunk is filled with Awe while Haven is filled with Love. _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Haven is cute visual novel with minimally engaging gameplay that gets very repetitive very quickly. Oh and also a second person is allowed to hold a controller.Partner and I were looking for a co-op game and were drawn to Haven for aesthetic, story, and survival aspect. To its credit, Haven is well voice-acted and the characters are adorable together, but that's pretty much all the game has going for it. The gameplay is shallow and repetetive with little room for decision making. We also felt like too many compromises were made to make the game playable by one person that the two-player experience is effectively non-existent.There are two modes in the game loop: Inside the ship and outside the ship. You flip between them, going outside to collect food then coming back inside to cook it and progress to the next day. When inside the ship, you are in a visual novel; you don't control the characters, but rather watch dialog and perform a few of the available actions. Even when making occasional dialog decisions, you don't make choices for each character independently...  players choose a dialog option for whichever character is speaking... and it has to be the same choice or you can't move on. Eventually you just fall into the pattern of both choosing the first option so you can get through it faster - there is really no decision making and literally no independence between players.Here again, there really is no co-op. One person controls both characters as you fly around the world, collecting food and exploring. Granted,  you can switch off who does the flying and the second player can try to grab stuff along the way, but that's about it. The only time you act independently is during combat, where you each select 1 of 4 actions to do over and over again. It got old after the first combat. Now to be clear, I understand why they made the outside mode this way - the fact that both character have to be on one screen at all times requires that you move as a unit. The problem here is that there just isn't enough for a second player to do, and even for the person flying that is pretty much  you do.

_childDocuments_.review: I need to say this right now: Haven is absolutely worth your time and money.I'm saying this now because Haven as a video game is nigh barebones and rather bland. The combat is stupid simple, the flying around each island with limited fast-travel options can be a slog and it often feels like the game is wrestling you for control, which is a major bummer for segments where you need pinpoint precision to continue. The gameplay of this game honestly feels like an afterthought, and considering it's, y'know... a GAME, that's not good.So why am I still recommending this game despite all of these misfires?It's the narrative, man. Holy wow.The two protagonists, the lovers Yu and Kay, are two of the most well-written characters I have ever seen in any media, straight up. They feel like an actual couple; they laugh together, they get annoyed with each other's antics, they tease each other, they get angry at each other and sometimes they don't say anything at all. They feel like real people with how they interact and play off one-another, and watching them just talk about their hopes and dreams is seriously entertaining.The story itself is great as well, revolving around the control and suppression of true feelings, enough to prompt Yu and Kay to deny the law of their world and escape to a planet where they hope no one can find them. It's an engaging story with solid world-building worked into it as well, which is delivered through well-written exposition. The game does expect you to pick up on a few cues throughout the dialogue to fully understand the narrative, but honestly anyone with half a brain cell can piece things together; that's the mark of good writing.The game is written like a visual novel with bland gameplay slapped on top of it. I honestly wish this was just a visual novel so I wouldn't have to critique half of the frankly boring game, and this is coming from someone who dislikes VNs most of the time. I do still recommend you experience this game for yourself, it's definitely a story you won't soon forget. Just be aware that the gameplay may not fully engage you like the narrative absolutely will.Also you can pet the cute lizard dog. Best game.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Conversations between the two main characters, Yu and Kay, and exploring the world of Source, cleaning up patches of Rust make up the bulk of the game. The dialogue between the two and their relationship is really the star of the game here; Yu and Kay are some of the most realistically-written, well-grounded characters I've seen in a video game and their relationship feels incredibly real.  The exploration paired with the excellent soundtrack is a very mellow and chill experience, and it's entertaining enough to not drag on over the course of the campaign (10-15hrs)Haven's combat (essentially sci-fi rock-paper-scissors) is easily the weakest part of the game -- but that doesn't really matter, because this game isn't a hardcore RPG, and you aren't playing it for the combat; it's a very well-told love story. Between this and Furi the Game Bakers are now on my map of developers to be paying attention to whenever they put a game out.My only real complaint is that the game probably could've used another month or two in the oven, some edges feel a bit rough. The movement can be finnicky if you need fine control. You'll hear combat call-outs repeated  plenty of times. You'll never hear conversations repeated but you'll occasionally hear throw-away lines repeated (such as when you exit your home).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm ngl, I was surprised by this game, both pleasant and unpleasantly. The story is really really captivating and really makes you want to learn more and more about the characters and their story. It doesn't start at the beginning and tell you everything, rather, it throws you in the middle and gives you bit by bits of information for you to make the bigger picture out of, which I love. The dynamic between the two main characters are also nice and they seem like actual people rather than characters in a story. However, I need to get into the game itself. Simply put, this game is not fun. It's an exploring game with rpg elements which are the worst. You get maybe like 10 moves max I think? Which is like, blast, guard, impact, cleanse, duo blast, duo impact, and bombs you can acquire later on. It's like the how final fantasy games, 7 which comes to mind, of the combat system, but worse. You have the "your opponents wait if you're attacking and vice versa" style, but you have to hold the button to attack, and let go at the same time for duo moves. It gets tedious and stale after the 5th encounter. Which is really sad considering I really love the story and I am hooked on it, but I just can't stand the game. You can be hovering around for 20-30 minutes, trying to find this last piece of rust to clear an island, only for it to be in a obscure place. I would recommend you just watch a game-play video of this game. 9/10 story1/10 game-play5/10 in total.

_childDocuments_.review: The Game Bakers have a talent for creating experiences that are aesthetically and narratively compelling. Most of the game consists of traversing small ‘floating island’ type areas covered in a sort of corruption and cleaning them before returning to your home (a crashed spaceship), or setting up camp for the evening. There's also very, VERY simple turn-based-RPG type battles, but the battles are extremely easy, so most your time is dedicated to exploration. That being said, both are just a means to progress the main attraction, the relationship between the two main characters. While most plots treat romance as an obligation tacked on with little to no tact, in haven it’s not an afterthought but the foundation that the entire story is built on, and it came across really well. I went into Haven hesitantly as Romance isn't a genre I typically like, but I ended up so hooked I binged Haven in just 2 days, and I can’t think of a better way to express my praise than that.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a beautiful game that has a little of everything. this is a world exploration game with a visual novel component to it, an RPG with a timing based combat system, and amazing dialogue that flows smoothly even if some of their made up words sound kind of cliche. One complaint that I have is that there is a bug where if you use your attacks in a weird way, everyone stops attacking and the battle goes to a stand still, the only fix is to restart from the last save, which isn't usually that far back. The art style is amazing, especially the watercolor animation for the start up screen and end credits. The music defines this game, sometimes i just wander around flying in the open fields listening to the music, something definitely worth vibing to. This game gives just enough exposition about the universe to get you wanting more information, the only thing I'd want to see in the dialogue, is have more interactions with the characters other than the two lovers, but then again, this is a game about Kay and Yu. Overall I'd say this game is worth the base price, but if you see it on sale, then definitely get it. If I had to give this game a rating, I'd give it a 9/10. The developers, artists, animators, and music designers really outdid themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: It's mesmerizing. I don't play romance games - hell, I'm barely a fan of exploration games: they generally fail to hold my attention. I believe that what allowed this game to keep my attention, besides its' beauty, is how although it is exploration-based, you're still given direction. You aren't left alone in a sprawling landscape, but explore on a smaller scale and then are led to other floating islands, each with its own quirks and secrets to discover.The two characters are fun - their relationship is cute, yet it's clear that they're still getting used to each other. For a complaint, I'd say that the downtime inside the ship is weird and that combat is only alright. Within the ship, you don't play as either of the characters - the two characters are frozen in place (doing an action) and you're just kind of floating around. I don't like how it feels. Combat is a bit clunky, I think I'd probably prefer open battles rather than getting roped in like a Pokemon battle - but it's understandable.Overall, very relaxing, beautiful and interesting game with tons of dialogue and discoveries. Not my type of game at all, yet it captivated me. Give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Heads over Heels: A Good Story More Than A Good Game. Like many of the others have review about this game, I would like to put my 2 cent on this one. Having finish this game in half of a day, it's clear to me that this game is more appeal for the casual. I would like to go through this review as to why I highly recommend this game to casual players:Pro: - The story: If I can describe the game story in one word, it's all about love. Love plays the main theme of this game, particularly young love. The story is about a couple trying to define the norms of conventional love, in a society where Matchmaking algorithm is consider to be the only option. Our young couple, Kay and Yu, who I presumed is in their mid 20s or early 30s are trying to break that boundary and decided to escape from their homeland to start a new life. The story itself is very simple yet compelling, a coming of age story that use a simple premise yet packs a lot of meaning. Throughout this game, you as a player get to experience what is like to felt in love and what to expect of love.  Further than that, you will able to experience what is mean to be in love with someone throughout their day to day life, from their own home to the great unknown of a planet far away from society. - The Characters: Both characters have a strong chemistry. Yu has an adventurous, outgoing person, often childish personality blend perfectly to the more nerdy, caring nurture, protective and supportive side Kay. The voice actors did an amazing job at capture the characters trait and personality. The uniqueness that both main protagonist in this game is the fact their characters are very much grounded, in a good way. Especially, in the way of that both characters expressing love for one of the other. Even in scenes when they both have their own dispute, it's come off very natural and not being forced.- The Environment: It's breathtaking. From the color choices to the animals in game, it's perfectly balanced. There is a good variety of animals in the game that makes it lively. The planet itself is interesting, how it tides to the story and in the game itself.- The Soundtrack: Some of the best soundtrack for a laid-back and casual experience. - The Art Style: Truly beautiful in both the character design and the world building.Cons:- Combat: Very lackluster, sometimes can be a little confusing.- Camera: Very stiff to say the least, the worst would be when you try to use Flow Thread which is the main form movement the game. Without a flexible camera, it can be frustrated in the early stage when you try to get a hang of the game core movement.In Conclusion: This is a solid game with a simple premise, the story is very captivating in itself with it's simplicity. The main protagonists of the game are very well-written, with the game colorful art style and a breathtaking world. Despite having a lackluster combat system and a questionable camera choice, the game make it up for it casual, laid back soundtrack. I highly recommend play this game as a solo, you can choose to play with a partner in the future. I do warn that, coop can be challenging especially during combat, so you have been warned. Other than that, I give this game a solid (8.5/10). Disclaimer: I wished to see more endings for the couple, so I could make an excuse for myself to replay this game while I am still single. Have a wonder day! :)

_childDocuments_.review: In a universe where habitable planets are tied together by "flow",  tells a story of youthful rebellion and morbid codependency. You, and another if you have someone to game with, play as Kay and Yu, star-crossed lovers who flee from civilized society to live together on a fractured planet in order to be together. As you progress though the game, flying from islet to islet gathering resources and fighting enraged alien creatures, you learn more about the two of them and the nature of their relationship. Most cut scenes are dialogue between the two and although there are some lines that might make you cringe, those moments breath life into their relationship as it makes you feel as if you are intruding on intimate moments. Often times it is the theme of needing each other that is hammered home throughout the development of their relationship, necessitated by their struggle to survive on a foreign world. The game play revolves around two players contributing equal parts when it comes to most things such as crafting, cooking, and combat (each player selects a part or action to contribute) except for moving the characters in the beautiful, anti-gravity archipelago map, and this is my biggest complaint with the game. It forces one player to sit back while the other drags them around. Although the game play is not the most engaging, the world looks great and the story is an exciting take on the individuals vs society trope. If you have two controllers, I would recommend playing it with your significant other, as that is how the game is best enjoyed.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven is a story, packaged as a game.  As a story it's fantastic, well-written, and enjoyable to experience.  It's the game part were Haven falls somewhat flat.  The game is very short, the world is very small, and it feels like it's entirely on rails the whole time.  The combat is innovative, but once you figure out 'the way to win' against a particular enemy, it rapidly becomes dull and repetitive.  Also, it's incredibly difficult to die.  But don't worry, if you do there's absolutely no penalty for that - you wake up back at your ship, heal up, and try again.  I'd say that overall Haven is the kind of game you play once, then never pick up again.  Worth it on a half-price sale?  Absolutely.  Worth it at the full asking price?  Only if you're in it for the visuals and the story, because the gameplay isn't the main draw here. 9/10 as a cinematic novel, but 4/10 as a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting and fairly unique game... somewhere between a cross of a romance VN, an RPG, a survival-crafting game, and a skateboarding game of sorts? With maybe hints of metroidvania-esque progression? I don't know how to describe better than that. But it's for the most part pretty fun! The gliding (read: skating) feels good, though it's the main thing you're gonna be doing all game so it doesn't stay compelling on its own. Gameplay pretty quickly falls into a loop of "visit a new islet, clean all the rust & clear all the mobs, explore to find the two or three things there, rinse, repeat" and probably wouldn't be sufficient to keep your interest alone, but that's where the story comes in - which is mostly romance scenes between the two leads, though there is a narrative besides that, and a pretty solid one with a few twists. It's... a bit awkward for me to talk about any of that as a very aromantic person myself but I found it enjoyable all the same, though the several-minute-long scenes occurring every time you sleep or every time you eat could be a pacebreaker at times - and wow there are so many scenes, all of them fully voice acted, which, that's pretty cool! If I did have nitpicks - the aerial flow bridges leading to places you -need- to go can get a bit tiring trying to find the right one - there's no indication and until you start riding one you have no clue where it's gonna go - and all the enemies being the same black and red colors does make it hard to tell which one you're fighting sometimes - which is annoying when different enemy types require different strategies to defeat. And looking at the same biome for most of the game can get a bit tiring, too - there are side biomes but they are all only a few islets big (and two of them, as far as I can tell, are completely optional to visit?) These are mostly minor gripes though for what was a very enjoyable game, and an experience you're not gonna get from any other game either, so... yeah, cool stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite a strong sense of art direction, this game is ripe with missed potential. The premise of a narrative driven experience which combines a visual novel presentation, a strong focus on exploration, and a turn-based battle setup within the framework of a co-op game is really promising. Unfortunately, the game doesn't really live up to any of these selling points in any meaningful capacity.Haven's narrative is largely contingent on two different story elements. The first of these narrative pillars is the relationship between its two protagonists. Despite such a heavy focus of the game's presentation being placed on its playable couple, it fails to really sell their romance in an endearing way. Most of their dialogue is presented through stilted writing and subpar voice acting that make the majority of the game's extended conversations feel incredibly unnatural. Perhaps the most praise-worthy aspect of this relationship is that the game allows you to gender-swap either character, allowing for homosexual relationships that are treated just as casually as their heterosexual counterpart. The second narrative pillar in the game is its overarching narrative about the main characters navigating the foreign world that they're stuck on. This aspect of the game, while not tremendously engaging, does employ some interesting aspects of soft world-building to develop its sci-fi setting. The game's story isn't necessarily bad, but it's simply not strong enough to carry the entire game's foundation on its back; its overall weakness causes the game's other bare bone areas to crumble.Exploration in Haven is largely contingent on a movement system that never really develops past its introduction. Hovering around and collecting materials is an initially engaging gameplay loop, yet it never really develops into anything beyond that. The game never really pushes the player to improve with any challenges in the overworld, and levels are so barren that you never have to really think about where you're going. Additionally, because the game limits your progress through a need to regularly feed the playable characters, you constantly end up backtracking through old areas that you've long since completed. The vast majority of the time spent in the overworld is ultimately boring, which is a shame since the game looks and sounds so great.The last nail in the coffin for Haven is its failure as an RPG. Despite its narrative and environmental shortcomings, a strong battle system could have been the glue that brought together the game's other underdeveloped traits. Unfortunately, the battle systems in this game have paper-thin depth. You're effectively restricted to only four options, with the pace of fights being stuck in an ambiguous space between turn-based and real time. For the vast majority of encounters, you just end up spamming one of two different attacks based on the target; combat almost never grows more complicated than that. Instead of doing something interesting with the choice to make you control two characters simultaneously, you instead end up with bare bones combat that feels like a late-stage addition to add the illusion of challenge. The only purpose I see in the enemy encounters is that they eat up your HP, forcing you to return back to your base and extend the game's runtime.While the vast majority of how I discuss Haven is negative, that comes from a sincere sense of disappointment. The game's premise is incredibly interesting, paired with a great art style and an amazing soundtrack from the electronic artist Danger. I really believe that a fleshed out sequel which properly develops the undercooked systems here could be a really special experience. Unfortunately, that level of potential doesn't translate into a quality experience here and now. I'll surely be anticipating the studio's next title, but I can't really recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to lie, when I started this game I rolled my eyes thinking it was out to set more of a political statement than a good story. But boy was I wrongI've never seen a more realistic and relatable relationship dynamic in a game before this game. There is no random unnecessary fights, no ridiculous feminist hierarchy of a woman to a man, no misogynist hierarchy of a man to the woman. What you have here is a perfect display of a relationship and how both couples have to apply equal effort to make it work under strenuous circumstances sometimes. You cook together, you organize together, you have rough nights and need to comfort one another, you have moments of shear uncertainty and need one partner to display confidence to overcome the situation, etc. There is an especially beautiful moment of the game when your nest ship falls off a cliff to a ridge below and you guys spend that night reorganizing your items with no talking, only 80s ambient music in the background which sounds like a partial instrumental rendition of "Right here waiting" by Richard Marx and it's beautiful. I nearly cried at that part. Gameplay:The gameplay is where some of its shortcomings come in. It's a cute addition that you need to find each other's hand when flying, but it slightly gets annoying because only one person can control the camera. This game would be better off in split screen.   You're essentially watching a brilliant relationship movie than playing a game. There are no puzzle additions or big boss bottles, it's essentially a couple simulator and that's it. This isn't a bad thing, but if you're looking for gameplay and story to mix, it's not here. Verdict: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: As stated in Steam's summary, it's as cliché as it sounds and goes. A tale of 2 lovers running away to escape from their home planet. Onto a journey as partners, lovers, and with multiple hardships faced. I'll try to keep this review as spoiler-free as I can but no promises!A tale as old as time, but with a twist as it goes! This time, Yu and Kay are trying to escape from the matchmaker. An all-knowing AI overlord that supposedly matches your potential partner with 100% accuracy, when faced with an  choosing my potential partner? Based on 0's and 1's?! Unacceptable! (Or is it 👀) It truly scares the crap out of me but at the same time humbles me that it can happen albeit in a sci-fi story but what's stopping from it coming to reality! It's truly a mystery how everyone accepts the matchmaker’s chosen partner without any sort of objection or opposition.So as how brave adventurers go, Yu and Kay refuse to accept their chosen partners. To run off into the unknown together, lumsecs away from their home planet. It truly is a miracle how they started initially meeting one another, to deep space. For their love which has no bounds, it's truly a heart-warming and oh-so-special feeling that really can't be described until you experience the story for yourself.Exploring Source together, the planet that Yu & Kay arrived by the skin of their teeth. Is something that it's hard to explain until you get to experience it yourself. The fear, excitement, happiness, worried & hunger all jumbling together as you have try to get your bearing after escaping your home planet. Truly alone as there is no one in sight as far as the eye can see.Conclusion: 8/10As mentioned previously, Kay and Yu are the protagonists of the story in Haven. Lovers with an act of unbelievable courage and willpower to oppose the matchmaker's fated partners they are assigned. In a last-ditch effort with nothing, but love, luck, mega-brainers, and a ship that’s not meant to withstand the distance they have supposedly travelled to. They pulled it off escaping their home planet.I can’t stress this enough, but the characters are what truly made me fell in  with the game. Yes, the story has it all, high pumping adrenaline paced action, heart-wrenching moments, slice-of-life & even  spicy & their realistic intimate moments🔥🔥 contents filled with their hilarious  that I can’t get enough of!What really sets apart the game from is really the characters themselves. Yu and Kay, from their perspectives on life, personality, and their immense bond for each other are truly a sight to enjoy. Last, but not least, it’s their beautiful chemistry with one another when they are bantering, it truly shines and paints the characters so realistically and romantically. Yu with sharp witty retorts while Kay expresses dumb poetic remarks.Though really(!), last of all, would be the  cast of voice actors for both Yu and Kay. Janine Harouni (Yu) and Christopher Lew Kum Hoi (Kay), you guys nailed the characters so much, it’s a sight to behold when the characters come to life with the support of your voices. During the heavy scenes, expressions of shock, the small important fleeting moments, and the loving banter between them. I will truly miss the banter after completing the game (twice!), it’s not something easy to replicate without it feeling forced and un-enjoyable, but Haven pulled it off! Just two people enjoying each other’s company. Conclusion: 9.5/10As the developers have emphasized it’s a game meant for SOLO first and foremost, however I think the experience is enhanced so much more when having someone to do some crazy couch co-op moments. It truly brought out a different experience when I was playing solo previously. While others have already stated the combat can be repetitive and wonky at times. There were some moments during combat, where our inputs just did not want to register it did leave a frustrating feeling as the aftertaste. It is mainly overshadowed by one of the cutest co-op style combat gameplay, where Yu and Kay have to prepare up the same attack style to dish out a combined combo, it is just so satisfying when it’s pulled off!I have to say, cooking in this game is one of the  parts of the game, the amount of thought, story, personality, and feelings were put into every scene the characters trying something new for the first time will always bring you in for a ride! Did I forget to mention the amount of animated cutscenes? The animation department truly went above and beyond on the intro with its unique art style which fits the theme of Haven. It is just filled with an insane amount of love when viewing every cutscene happening.Conclusion: 7.5/10I’m once again left speechless, even after an . The music just has to one-up the previous categories. If there is a word to describe it. It would be, Interstellar, not just because it fits the atmosphere in an unknown planet. Every soundtrack is memorable in its way from the action-packed, being on an isolated beach, and staring at the starry night skies. It’s hilarious how you can choose your music should you wish!Danger as the solo music artist responsible for all the soundtrack is truly stunning!Conclusion: 8/10I’m not much one to comment when it comes to UI if it’s done well, but man I truly had a moment when , the out-of-the-blue impact caught me off guard as it is done so beautifully well. In terms of day-to-day activities, the UI is not cluttering at all it’s very hands-off. To help us focus on the beautiful surroundings, which I can’t get enough of!Conclusion: 8/10As this is a biased conclusion since I’m recommending the game already, I will say that the story and the protagonists are what makes the game truly special, therefore this gets my stamp of approval✨✨✨.Overall rating: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is AWKWARD. The keyboard controls are horrible and clunky. The resource gathering/exploration mechanic doesn't really fit with the story we're being told. The visuals are over-saturated. I can tell the devs were going for an aesthetic, but all these bright saturated colors are really hard on the eyes, and it makes it hard to tell what you're looking at sometimes. The graphics are very low poly (and not in a good way). But the over abundance of grass suggest that the devs dont know how to implement LODs or optimize their game. The character's 3d models really need more detail in order to not look kind of scary when you zoom in on them. Finally, the voice acting is bad. I would have preferred no VA to this, which just makes you feel like a 3rd wheel to someones blind date. I had more fun actively making bad choices (and messing their relationship up) then going with good ones.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most heckin' adorable game ever.The voice acting is stellar. They got the two main character actors to do their lines together, and you can tell. It feels really natural.The script is well done, so far. The main characters are a bit hot-headed and don't use I-language as much as they should for solving interpersonal relationship conflicts, but it all flows well. Super kudos for consistency throughout the script (cylindrical planets!) and the few references to crazy complex board games.Combat is fairly simple though I'm still trying to master the timings of everything.Gameplay loop is good; there's always something exciting on the horizon to go and explore.Ultimately this seems like primarily a story game with gameplay being secondary. I don't see this as a bad thing, but I think it's important to point out.
