_childDocuments_.review: As all reviews, this will be 100% subjective. (Full spoilers ahead)First off, the aspects I found less than desirable.The game was built up to be played with a controller. I have none, so I played with my keyboard and mouse. This made it tough to get used to moving around. Especially because the game does not have an option to change mouse sensitivity. Battling and crafting was also difficult because the game is set on English keyboard settings, which makes the semi colon ( ; ) be someplace different.Another bad aspect was that the characters have, at some point, a cliche'd argument that ends up in... nothing. It resolves itself within 5 minutes of starting.And finally, there is no way to flee battles. This is a nitpick of mine, but there should be a way to flee. Maybe have a dual flow burst that knocks out enemies. That would be neat.NOW! Onto the good aspects! (which is practically all the rest of the game)Art:Simply fantastic. Both the opening and the ending have this unique style (watercolor, maybe?) that I like a lot. The 2D character models are beautiful, and I simply loved how the 3D models move their mouths at the same time the 2D ones do when talking.The animals and enemies are all unique, even in the corrupted (rusted?) forms, which makes it easy to remember what they're weak against. Oynk is super cute and deserves all the scratchies.Music:There are basically two tracks in the whole game. Open world theme, and battle theme. Sure, there are more, but these two are the ones you'll listen to for about 90% of your game play. I played for 12 hours, so I listened to them quite a lot. And I can say that they never felt repetitive. They were pretty well composed.Opening and ending themes are also pretty good. Would listen to them outside the game.Characters:Both Yu and Kay are very well written protagonists. You would think this to be obvious, but not many people can write believable characters in a romantic setting. Sure, Yu is kinda childish and Kay can be a bit of an idiot (the argument bit), but they ARE believable. They act and react in a way you would expect anyone to. Their comments on what they do and what they see are very well places.And the voice acting is superb. Even the characters that have less than 2 minutes of dialogue are well acted.World building:In this, I have to say, is where Haven sets itself apart.Sure, the game is about the characters and their romance, but the creators took their time to write a believable world building about their home world. This is especially impressive when you remember that we NEVER get to see it.The Apiary, the Matchmaker, the Council. Truth and Top. Even the way the characters swear (bloot!). Everything feels like it could exist. And we never get info dumps. Yu and Kay give only bits of information each time they talk about it, and they do not talk about it all the time.All in all, I think this is a very well done game. It certainly deserves the positive reviews. I'm excited to see what the developers do next.

_childDocuments_.review: I could probably write a dissertation on everything Haven does right, but the truth is, Haven is something you must feel. Your relationship with Haven will change over time, the nuances left on you only realized long after the controller has been put away. Haven is the game every game developer wishes they could make and every gamer wishes they could play for the first time every time. It cannot be overstated how beautiful Haven is in every sense of the word. Please don't just play Haven -- feel Haven.

_childDocuments_.review: This may not be Furi 2, but it is a very sweet and memorable game, regardless of whether you have a partner to play this with or not.This is the selling point of the game. It is relatable especially if you have experienced the ups and downs of a long term relationship.It follows the story of Kay and Yu, two lovers who fled to another planet to escape the grasp of a council that doesn't allow couples to coexist unless they've been matched by an entity called "the matchmaker". The game follows them on their adventure as they try to survive on a foreign planet, while fearing that each day might be their last one, before the council finds them.The game has done a great job of building suspense and getting me invested in their personal lives as I felt many moments from their relationship being very similar to the ones I've had with my girlfriend so far.Their dialogue is the main way the story is being built. That along with the voice acting truly captures the emotions of the two lovebirds. There are also many sexual references in the game, that don't feel out of place, but only make their moments even sweeter.When it comes to choices, the dialog choices only affect a small percentage of the game's narrative, except for the epilogue.Even though the main plot is perfectly wrapped up by the end of the game, I wished they had the time to fill in some of the gaps regarding their past. Overall the story has been a great adventure that I'd love to experience again.The game seems to use a slightly enhanced version of Furi's engine. It may not offer the best experience when it comes to drawing character faces, but it does create some cute environments. As a result, even though their dialogue interactions are very sweetly drawn, when it comes to their character models during gameplay, they could use a bit more detail.The gameplay is mostly focused on exploration in order to gather food, purify corrupted islets as well as the local creatures, while also progressing the main plot and enhancing their relationship.The combat relies on real time turn based combat. Kay and Yu are controlled simultaneously through either hotkey or the axes on your joystick. Successfully using the right actions on both of them is essential in winning every fight, as every creature is defeated in a different way. This type of combat can grow repetitive at times, but being so involved in the story I've enjoyed it regardless.I haven't experienced this game in co-op mode but I can confirm that you don't need a girlfriend to enjoy this game to its full extent.The game's soundtrack has been entirely remixed by Danger. If you've loved the soundtrack in Furi, you'll definitely love the one here as well, even if it has a less action oriented tone to fit this game.If you're not turned off by romance generally speaking, I would kindly recommend this game to anyone or at least to give the demo a try, since the developers have put a lot of love into this game, while still updating the game even today.  An even bigger reason to try it out if your partner is a gamer too.

_childDocuments_.review: This game oozes with tons of personality, small touches which make everything feel warm, inviting and enjoyable, the way an RPG should be. I really enjoyed the strong voice acting, which feels uncommonly authentic and charismatic. This really helps drive the central story about two people trying to make it, and who will only make if they stick with one another. Whether it be the excellent soundtrack, the anime inspired art-style, the cute loading screens, or the way the two characters hold hands when you fly close to one another, all of these elements fuse perfectly to create a nearly instantly enjoyable mood. I can't wait to play more of this game, and if you're a fan of JRPGs, I think you'll be excited too.

Its alien world is beautiful, the gameplay is far from bad, and the way this focuses in the protagonist duo and their romantic relationship is pulled off quite well (for the most part), but in the end, the severe lack of content, as well as challenge, soon turns this into a repetitive, and painfully boring chore.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't remember how I discovered this game, but I was entranced by its soft art style and character design. I just had to buy it. Whoever made the art behind this game, great job!I'm about 2 hours in by the time of this review and I absolutely adore this game. It's a wholesome alien love story between Kay, a biologist, and Yu, an engineer. They ran away from an oppressive interplanetary society and found their home on an abandoned planet called Source.When you start the game, you're immediately thrown into the romance with no questions asked - it threw me off at first, but the game makes up for it through the conversations Kay and Yu have throughout, with no dialogue being pointless to their character development.The combat mechanics are a bit weird - you control both Kay and Yu at the same time in a real-time battle with enemies. It takes a while to get used to, but the game is definitely not hard.The game is rated PEGI +18/ESRB M, but this doesn't feel like it. The worst you'll find in sexual content are the two main characters kissing, and nudity when taking a shower (you can only see a silhouette of their characters' bodies). Definitely needs to have those ratings checked again.9/10 from me!

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I played this while I didn't have internet, so I was offline and my hours didn't count.Had a lovely time playing this. The characters felt real, and some moments were just so domestic I couldn't help but smile, it was really heart-warming. And there are a bunch of small interactions throughout the game.Kay is a sweetheart and a big nerd. Yu did annoy me a little at the beginning, but she grew on me. Can't say the same thing about the fake swear words though, those are just weird. Just... Use actual swear words.Apart from that, the VAs did a really great job, and I love the portrait art of the characters. The music is nice and the game visuals itself are ok.Gameplay-wise, it's mostly exploration and you may occasionally have to fight something, but honestly... Can't say the combat really matters, it's just something extra and very simple. Most areas also look pretty similar, so it can feel kind of repetitive. That said, I still enjoyed my time exploring.tl;dr: Play this game if you want to experience a wholesome love story and don't care too much about the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games that made me feel refreshed, relaxed and rejuvenated after exhausting routine of FPS shooters (and some real life events). I might give an upper hand and say that this game is amazing masterpiece, but I've been in this place before and I can surely say that this gives me hard "Life is Strange" vibes, due to how I got attached to characters, but the recent example was executed well better. This was totally not an accident, as both "The Game Bakers" and "Dontnod" are developers from France, and, apparently, putting "X" on teenage girls' (and lonely coomers, like me) hearts is a trend. And what do you know, in both games the choices that you make DON'T MATTER because there are only two endings to the story. I mean, Haven never implied to have the "all choices matter" system, which is good! I'm not putting it as a flaw towards Havens' production, but rather how the latter game learned from it's predecessor of "nots" of game build. However, a lot of hard skeptics might tear this game to pieces due to how soy-ish and soft everything is, but honestly - there are as many opinions as there are people, so I don't care.Now about the actual flaws. The markers on the map were rather useless - I expected some sort of cursor to show up while I'm not looking at the map. Certain dialogues gave some HEAVY and CRINGEWORTHY Life is Strange vibes (bLoOt, BoRoN). After all, it's a romance game - it is something I had to see coming. Last: leaving out southern islets (the pollen-filled, yellow landscapes) was actually a disappointment because there wasn't much main story action going on in there and I visited them ONLY after completing the main story.The characters are basic, not going to lie, these "love swings" and drama is nothing new to me, but I can say that they're believable, as during the gameplay I reminisced about my previous relationship experience and realized how tough it is to keep such connection to each other for a long time and how sweet is to love and be loved. I mean, it's a game and it's not real so otherwise yes they would eat each other after being together on isolated planet for, like, F O R E V E R.Another hit in my heart was that the game concept and gameplay reminded me somewhat of Crash of the Titans and Ratchet and Clank series, which I hold dear to me because of childhood memories, as my love to free-roaming separate regions (levels), hitting stuff and enemies and just collecting items is endless and I'm glad it got revisited in this game as well.The gameplay, of course, gets boring with time, and it reminds of Pokemon series, like it was made for nintendo switch or something lol xDDDDD (It was, actually...), but I say it's perfect for it's price - I'm willing to pay a little over 10$ to enjoy  content for under 20 hours to complete the game to 100%. Short story, no difficulty-based achievements, good learning curve left me totally satisfied with the game, 8/10 for sure going to play this game with my future anime-furry-waifu-pervy-hentai-uwu-nerd wife.

_childDocuments_.review: Having only a few hours in to this experience the player is delivered a believable and compelling experience between two genuine lovers without being sucked into some disingenuous romance novel / game relationship style writing. The light RPG elements offer a solid feeling of progression that unfolds as the two characters grow with each other through storytelling, decision making, and good old-fashioned turn-based combat. The developers truly highlight the spirit of a relationship between two people working together weather they are holding hands while gliding through the various environments, talking to each other in the middle of the night, or covering each other in combat. Teamwork makes the dream work!On a personal note, I find the music track by DANGER offers a magnitude of depth to the game. It is truly tailored for this experience and I find myself just flowing through the environments and taking in the beautiful atmosphere vibeing to the music in ways that I haven’t experienced since Jet Set Radio or Doom (2016). 10/10This game is a romance novel, survival simulator, atmospheric experience, and RPG. And a damn good one written by developers who wanted to take the risk to provide what makes what indie developers are famous for, great artistic experiences in the video game medium.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Good, story-driven game. For only bad point I have (and how to deal with it), read last paragraph.Haven is a very good game, and one of the few that accurately shows a healthy relationship of two characters that are actually people and not tropes. It's light on the gameplay, and more of a chill experience than anything else, but still worth it in my opinion, as it does not outstay its welcome.The developers set out to write what happens to two lovers *after* they escape a tyrannical authoritarian regime that uses an AI to match people up with their perfect partners and does not accept dissidents. They (crash) land in a perfect world and that's where the game starts. Gameplay consists mostly of gliding around collecting ingredients for food and medicine or cleaning up the land of "rust", a weird red substance that covers the land and turns the otherwise peaceful animals evil.The combat is not directly turn-based, but not directly real-time either. It mostly consists of picking a shield-breaker move, a damage move or a shield move, like in a turn-based game, but the selection happens in real time, and so does the enemies. The combat is very simple and the game states outright that it's supposed to be that way as it is not the focus, and offers a speed-through option to those who aren't fans of it. Most of the combat can be avoided, as you can simply clear out an area of the rust and then leave and reenter and the creatures affected by it will be peaceful. But some of them spread it themselves, on those you will have to engage.Other than collecting food/medicine and pacifying creatures, the two characters are constantly engaging in conversation that fleshes them out better. Since you're always playing both characters at the same time, you can often pick between two choices, and while this has a slight effect on the game's ending, it is really non-choice that doesn't quite matter. There are no branching story-lines, and if you repeat diaologue options, you will often discover that if you select the other one, the response changes in such a way that you'll return to the main narrative thread.Example: Character 1 states that the mountain is... (you can pick: high or scary) and depending on what you pick, the response will be the respective other choice, ending in disagreement. The real choice comes immediately afterwards where you make up again, which is a neat little narrative trick that developers use to make you adore the characters more, and also to show that disagreements in relationships are inevitable, what matters is how you solve them. This vibe is in every conversation in the game, and showcases the utmost care with which the developers wanted to show a healthy, realistic relationship.Now, you might remember that 2 paragraphs above I mentioned the game's ending, which is untrue, as the game has two. This is where my only negative point comes in: One of the ending's is clearly supposed to be the canon one, with a proper epilogue, written conversations and a bit of fun gameplay. The other is dealt with in about 4 comic-style paintings which in a matter of 5 seconds, give you the gist of what happens. I truly wonder why the developers included this choice when they obviously focused on one ending more, and when throughout the game's entire run, every choice was a flavourful choice (i.e. what would the character rather say, something teasing or inquisitive), especially if the other ending leaves a sour taste in your mouth. In addition, which ending you get is decided at the end right before it happens. The choices you have up to that point only impact one aspect of one of the endings (the one with more work put into it), nothing else. I saw both endings and I can confidently tell you that you're better off not having seen the other one. So, my recommendation: At the end when the two characters need to do a thing to fix the big problem they're facing and that they've have been working up to fix the entire game, they will hesitate. You get the choice to either give into this hesitation (triggering the weak-sauce ending) or push through (triggering the good ending). I'd recommend pushing through. Trust me.

_childDocuments_.review: I am so torn on this game.The visuals are beautiful, the voice acting is incredible and most of the mechanics are very fun. That said, I feel like this game was about half-way done; it feels like there are so many parts that could have been extended with a little bit more effort to make a truly magnificent RPG experience.I hesitate to call this an RPG, in its current form, because it lacks some basic things that I've come to expect from any RPG like loot rewards and a legitimate progression system. Yes, you can "progress" but it all feels like it is on rails and you're just checking the same boxes regardless of how many times you play through it; there is little flexibility.My favorite parts of playing this were flying around exploring and the crafting system. The cooking is especially satisfying but, again, hindered by limited varieties of ingredients and no rewards for crafting different things. The novelty of flying around only lasted so long and I got to the point of forcing myself to play because I wanted to progress the story. The combat system feels innovative to me but, again, suffers from not being flushed out a bit more. It feels repetitive and there are no tangible incentives to even participate in it other than being forced to in order to progress the story.I want to recommend this and I want to love it but there isn't enough here for me. Yu's voice acting and expressions are probably the best thing about it but I ended up just looking up the endings on YouTube and kind of relieved I didn't finish playing through it because the endings are, in my opinion, pretty unsatisfying for the effort.Others might enjoy this but I would personally wait for it to go on sale. I'd try another Game Baker's game but I won't pay full price for one again without doing a lot more research first.

_childDocuments_.review: My play time on this game is not accurately reflected via what is listed on my profile. My partner and I played this game over at their house and spent 24 hours on it via co-op. We have never done remote play via steam so I cannot vouch for that. 	Honestly, there are a lot of positive things I can say about this game. It was a bonus for me and my partner to play together. However, I imagine if I played the game alone, I would have still enjoyed my experience regardless.	Just to keep my game spoiler-free, you play as a couple, Yu and Kay. They escaped from a world where they weren’t allowed to be together and are learning how to live on a new planet they landed on. The story is definitely sci-fi related and full of wholesome moments that couples can relate to. Aside from exploring the new world the couple landed on, there is a lot of dialogue, I would estimate that a good chunk but not too much of your game time will be taken up by that factor. I do not see this as a con as it dived deeper into the relationship they have as a couple. The voice acting felt organic and the characters felt relatable.	The bonus is, that you can play as a same-sex couple which was an inclusive move by the developers. I have yet to play the game as a same-sex couple but I don’t think it would change the gameplay. I will update in the future when I do a same-sex couple play thru.	There is gameplay such as exploring the islets, fighting the creatures that have been infected(you don’t kill them), and collecting materials and food items. Co-op is good but I only had one issue with it. If you play as a second player in the field you still follow player 1 and you get it collect things faster. However, when collecting seeds, player 2 will always have the upper advantage. Which was the only problem. I only played the combat via co-op but you do need to time certain mechanics right together to make sure that you can deliver the damage. The combat isn’t hard and is quite easy. I believe we only died two times in the game. Grinding isn’t required	I didn’t experience any glitches during my playtime. I did need to get used to the controls when I first started playing the game. 	Music and graphics? I’m not a big music person but I can say for sure I like the music in the game and it’s amazing. I was blown away at how well the music matches the environment and combat in the game. As someone sensitive to sound and such, I didn’t find the music overstimulating. I can see myself using the OST as background music when I study or just vibe. The graphics are good and easy on the eyes. The environment looks nice especially the transition from day to night. Yu and Kay look beautifully drawn during dialogue. I can’t imagine you need a super high-end computer to play this game as its minimum requirement is 4 GBs of ram. 	The audience for the game is young adults and older. The game contains sexual content but it’s more like what you would see in a normally average couple that likes to flirt with each other. There are some loading screens containing partial nudity but everything is covered up. There is the use of alcohol and drugs but not alot of it. 	For the price tag of 24.99 US dollars, The game is worth its value. I would have bought a copy for myself even if I solely played it at my partner’s place. In summary, this game is nice and wholesome. I for sure enjoyed my time playing through it with my partner. It is not difficult to play so you can just have a nice enjoyable moment putting a day aside to play it. Although I wish cream berries existed in real life cause it looks so good to eat.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know how I stumbled across this masterpiece of a game. I was browsing through Steam and saw it in the "More like this" category of a stupid dating sim. Liked the look, intrigued me and purchased. Best Steam purchase yet.The story is stunningly good written, the world is amazing and really makes you feel like exploring every single islet until you've cleared it. Endlessly looking for some flow paths to get to certain elevations was sometimes annoying but overall not much of a bummer. I took joy in clearing out every islet because it was satisfying seeing how it's slowly turning from a red mess to a pretty placeThe activities in this game are lovely, from cooking tens of different recipes to using food to bait the creature that enables fast travel to playing with toys to The voice acting was what made this game, though. There are so many voice lines it's crazy. I was really impressed by the "seed game" and how they were literally remembering the score with 80 different score combinations. Yu and Kay's emotions were palpable and so believable thanks to the actors, whenever they were sad, angry, yelling or in the mood.Yu and Kay, the protagonists, are excellent characters with so much depth to them, from how Yu  creamberries to Kay's random biology facts. I really enjoyed seeing them progress both as individuals and as a couple. They did not feel overly cheesy/cringy, they just felt natural, real.My only complaint with this game has to be the U-Turn mechanic. I played with mouse control enabled when gliding and an U-Turn would be done whenever I would  move my mouse like 45 degrees off the direction of Yu & Kay's glide.  It would be so unreliable, though, not actually being performed when i wanted it to. I can't stress enough how irritating this was for the game experience, it even made me fall out of a flow path in the ending and had to go through it again, ruining the pace. It would even fire in succesive, I would sometimes do 4 or 5 U-Turns. The game would have been so much better had this mechanic simply not existed or just fired by pressing the S key.In conclusion, it's a must if  you enjoy story-rich games with also some exploration and RP. Totally loved it

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, with a few caveats.The good: Kay and Yu were amazing. Their relationship was so well developed, you could really feel the love they had for each other. The dialogue was fun and sexy. I really liked that it didn't shy away from more sexual conversations without being fully explicit either. I was impressed with just how many different interactions they had, and how many different graphics there were for the two of them.The meh: Flying around should have been fun, and it probably would have if I'd been playing solo. But I played it co-op with a friend, and that meant the camera would attempt to keep both characters on screen, which resulted in difficulty controlling the characters at times. The flying could have used sharper turns in general without the drifting mechanics, too. I wish each island had a proper map, or at least some way to get an overview of things. Searching for that last bit of rust got a bit tedious. And then the battles... My friend and I set the battles to the easiest settings we could, and we're both glad we did. The battle system isn't bad, per se, but we were frustrated by the dropped inputs. But once we got the hang of it, it was really fun to coordinate our attacks. I would have hated doing the battles solo.In fact, a lot of things would have been more tedious solo, including cleaning up rust. The second player's bubble was really helpful for that.And then there are the endings. There are two endings, one of which is explicitly bad, the other of which is... a bit depressing. I know it's meant to be the good ending, but it has so many tragic elements layered onto it that it felt like too much of a downer. I wish it had ended on a slightly more optimistic note, since there was already the bad ending for the downer feels.Overall though I had a lot of fun with it and I do recommend it as a co-op game. I would not recommend it as a single-player game.

_childDocuments_.review: Does love truly conquer all? Two lovers gave up everything, left their entire lives behind, and escaped to a lost planet to be together. Play these lovers, Yu and Kay, at the same time as they settle into an unknown and eerie world. Explore the planet searching for parts and material to fix their ship and make it a cosy home. Enjoy life together as a relatable couple cooking meals, crafting, collecting resources and engaging in meaningful conversations. Fight against those trying to tear them apart by synchroniSing their actions in combat, finding the perfect timing and rhythm, while controlling both characters simultaneously. Glide through the mysterious landscape, explore a fragmented world and fight against what’s trying to tear them apart in this RPG adventure about love, rebellion, and freedom.

name: Streets of Rage 4
detailed_description: Reviews About the Game The all-time classic Streets of Rage, known as Bare Knuckle (ベア・ナックル Bea Nakkuru) in Japan, is a trilogy of beat ‘em up known for this timeless gameplay and electronic dance influenced music. Streets of Rage 4 builds upon the classic trilogy’s gameplay with new mechanics, beautiful hand drawn visuals and a God tier soundtrack. An iconic series like Streets of Rage got its iconic characters: Axel, Blaze, Adam and other veterans reunited to clean up the streets. With some brand-new moves and kickass tracks to take a listen, our heroes are ready to dish out beatdowns to a fledgling group of ill-advised criminals in full force. Streets of Rage 4 will be the first entry to the core series in 25 years, standing as Axel, Adam and Blaze’s glorious return to serving up side-scrolling beatdowns. With lush hand-drawn animations, new combat abilities, and fresh tracks from an amazing team of composers, Streets of Rage 4 will be a masterful tribute to and revitalization of the classic action fans adore The series is known for its electronic dance influenced music around the world. The soundtrack of Streets of Rage 4 is handled by an all-star line-up of musicians like Yuzō Koshiro, Motohiro Kawashima, Yoko Shimomura, Harumi Fujita, Keiji Yamagishi and many more whom will create new amazing tracks for this new episode of the Streets of Rage series. ● The comeback of the legendary Streets of Rage series. ● Beautiful graphics fully hand-drawn animated by the studio behind Wonder Boy: The Dragon’s Trap. ● Clean up Wood Oak City by yourself or with another friend online! ● For the very first time, team up to 4 people offline to take the city back! ● Classic gameplay enhanced with brand-new mechanics. ● Soundtrack by a wide all-star line up of world-class musicians. ● Braised chicken everywhere. ● A dozen former Streets of Rage characters unlockable and playable in their original pixel versions. ● Play with the music of the previous Streets of Rage games. ● 12 unique stages. ● Fight against your friends in the Battle Mode ● Or team up along to defeat the Boss Rush Mode!

With some brand-new moves and kickass tracks to take a listen, our heroes are ready to dish out beatdowns to a fledgling group of ill-advised criminals in full force. Streets of Rage 4 will be the first entry to the core series in 25 years, standing as Axel, Adam and Blaze’s glorious return to serving up side-scrolling beatdowns. With lush hand-drawn animations, new combat abilities, and fresh tracks from an amazing team of composers, Streets of Rage 4 will be a masterful tribute to and revitalization of the classic action fans adore The series is known for its electronic dance influenced music around the world. The soundtrack of Streets of Rage 4 is handled by an all-star line-up of musicians like Yuzō Koshiro, Motohiro Kawashima, Yoko Shimomura, Harumi Fujita, Keiji Yamagishi and many more whom will create new amazing tracks for this new episode of the Streets of Rage series. ● The comeback of the legendary Streets of Rage series. ● Beautiful graphics fully hand-drawn animated by the studio behind Wonder Boy: The Dragon’s Trap. ● Clean up Wood Oak City by yourself or with another friend online! ● For the very first time, team up to 4 people offline to take the city back! ● Classic gameplay enhanced with brand-new mechanics. ● Soundtrack by a wide all-star line up of world-class musicians. ● Braised chicken everywhere. ● A dozen former Streets of Rage characters unlockable and playable in their original pixel versions. ● Play with the music of the previous Streets of Rage games. ● 12 unique stages. ● Fight against your friends in the Battle Mode ● Or team up along to defeat the Boss Rush Mode!
short_description: Amongst the best beat’em up series ever created, jammin’ ‘90s beats and over the top street fighting, the iconic series Streets of Rage comes back with a masterful tribute to and revitalization of the classic action fans adore.

_childDocuments_.review: This would be a great game if it wasnt called streets of rage. This review is for Hard difficulty or higher. This review was from launch 1.0 there have been a few patches including one recently that addresses some of the issues mentioned here. as such this review needs a update and may get one if i build up the will to try it again as i still own it.Like the Turtles remake and the Double dragon remake. the games try to add something new but end up taking away from the player in odd ways.1 character can properly function under the system as intended. dont like cherry? good liuck its doable but much less enjoyable.It is fine to give enemies armored attacks. they always had these but not EVERYONE.Fast attacks certainly didnt have armor they might have been invincible but not armored. If you are pushing a system where you want the player to be aggressive you cannot give the enemies uninterruptable instant attacks they can do in the middle of your combo to stop it. this is not fun or fair it just feels awful to have a awesome combo going with a difficult to use character only for one of the basic enemies to unleash a lightning fast invincible uppercut that hits you before you are in visible attack range and you cant avoid because you are too slow. No. I dont use the superjoy to escape because honestly when you are good you dont even end up in a situation where you would need it. the real skill of the game is threat mitigation period. This game doesnt even let you do that because of the abilities they gave the enemies.If you are going to encourage juggles properly implement hit lift. enemies sink and there is no way to bounce or relaunch them with most chars other than cherry. adam has 1 way to bounce enemies and he doesnt go into a launcher fast enough to re-launch them. (as his fasted launcher is his back attack which doesnt hit at the range that his bounce allows.you are pushing aggression and punishing it at the same time. you also have enemies who can catch everything thrown at them...these enemies should not be among groups of normal enemies because the point of a thrown weapon is to give yourself some breathing room and/or prevent a distant approaching threat not give that threat extra range and damage.the game forces you to break off combat extremely often whereas in sor2 or 3 if a enemy had a strong attack there were 3 options try to brute force counter hit it and risk taking the hit. avoid it completely or learn how to properly counter it and answer offense with offense. not only do they take the first and last option away they punish you for it by either causing your combo to drop off due to cool down or your attack gets instantly countered by a armored move or a grab which the only thing you can do to respond is jump...which isnt supposed to be invincible this isnt devil may cry.I want to like this game...but I cant because its called Streets of Rage while playing nothing like a streets of rage game other than sharing the base beat em up and the IP

_childDocuments_.review: This thing doesn't hold a candle to another fan made game that can't be mentioned here. And it isn't free like that one is. Beat it in less than two and a half hours. The older characters (SOR1 are the only unlocked ones so far) weren't brought up speed and given strong movesets to be on par with the new characters. No unique attack animations for certain weapons on certain people.If you look at their art, the art that they themselves are proud enough of to put in the game as 'extras', you can tell there isn't a single creative soul on the team. They drew arrows on their path drawings like it was some sort of mystery as to how the characters are going to get around a table. Not a fan of fighting cops either, but given half the characters had side cuts its easy to tell why they put that in. Colorful hair, tattoos and leggings does not make one unique. The writing for the cutscenes was so cringy I had to skip it. Only one character can run. Blaze's voice acting is horrific. Didn't see any path choice like in 3 or the other fan game (look that tree up). Music isn't as good as the original but it is pretty awesome. No Zamza, no Jack, no Roo, no Jet. Either go full in on the nostalgia or make something new while being faithful. This half in on the nostalgia and one eighth in on new ideas. Not sure where the other pieces went but it wasn't into the game.Combo system is great. The art is amazing. Adam is seriously, unbelievably awesome. I'd rather have Skate but Cherry is a great substitute. Max and Skate should be FLC along with like three more hours of content to make it worth it, even with its small price tag. You made a game worthy of 1995 for sure. It would have been amazing then even if the art wouldn't work in that era. If nothing changes for this game buy it on sale.I will play this a few more times, unlock everything and see what I missed but so far this is pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Well, as a long standing fan of Streets of Rage the game is fantastic. My first contact with the franchise was SoR1 in the Mega Games 2 (The Revenge of Shinobi, Streets of Rage and Golden Axe) that was bundled with the Mega Drive. I played the hell out of that game and then played the other two when some friends lent them to me.The game as a whole gives the same aura as the other games and it is a worthy continuation of the franchise. I hope they get enough money and manage to make an even better fifth part.Controls are tight and you have to keep an eye of what is going on and what enemies are on screen to avoid being slapped into the next year. You can't smash the buttons because someone at the other end of the screen will rush at you or throw something at you.The design of about everything is really stylish and I have to acknowledge that I've become a fan of the character designer. Enemies are really good and I really chuckled at some of them. I wish the the "extras" had more designs.The music is barely making it as passable but this should be no surprise as ripping off techno hits is no longer an option and composers have to do their job.I'd say you have around 4 hours of content if you just want to finish it. If you want to keep it going, do some multiplayer and get better I'd say there are many more hours than that.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: This Review is based mostly on my Switch experience. Also, minimal spoilers ahead.Been waiting for the release of this game since it got publicly announced, everything looked good, I'll be quick with the pros and cons of this game since you're reading this to buy the game and not get bored to dead.Also bear in mind I've played SoR 1 to 3 several times and I still do on my Switch/PC from time to time.Pros:- Overall Fighting Engine is pretty good and smooth.- A decent rooster of characters plus the added SoR 1,2 and 3 pixelized characters.- A longer campaign going from the original 8 stages to 12 stages total.- The new controls, although weird for older player, are a friendship saver since you can't eat your friends’ chicken by mistake now since Attacking and Picking Up items have two separate keys. (You can still go back to legacy controls).- You can now play up to 4 characters in a single game, you can also turn off friendly fire.- With the now added Survival mode and new techniques for each character, the already good game just became more playable and less boring.Cons:- Everything is now a ping pong ball, in which you and your enemies can be launched across the map just by getting hit by a enemy headbutting you, in some stages with hazards you can lose a huge chuck of your life without having a chase to recover.- Axel and Blaze feel underpowered due to characters like Adam and Cherry having access to dashes and sprint, the game is not impossible to finish, even in Mania but it's just a really bad experience, since the solution to all in higher difficulties is to spam Jumps, which kind of kills the mood at least for me.- Specific Enemies like Goro, that can only be grabbed to dead or you risk yourself getting hard countered by his dreaded parries, make a run annoying, even more when you have more than one aiming at you.- Specific Stages, like Stage 7 Boss where you get to fight the main boss and 2 bosses from stage 2 that can mindlessly grab you do dead, once again not impossible but just annoying.- Stage 10, where there's a part with biker chicks that headbutt you and hipster girls that throw grenades at you all at the same time, in which if you get hit just once, since you have juggle mechanics and just fly across the map you can just lose a life from 100% to 0% in that moment that you let yourself get hit.- Clearly the developers are big SoR2 Fans, because the "Retro" Soundtrack has only music from SoR2 entries, with no music from SoR1 or SoR3, what got me sad is that each stage has the wrong music to it, even when you get to Stage 6 Boss Shiva you don't get to listen to Max Man, or any boss music to be exact, just some play normal stage music.- Stage 12 Big Ben Room has been revamped to no longer have the spike ball, making it a cheap way to die to rolling Big Bens.Overall the game is pretty good, hence my recommendation, but far from perfect, playing in Hardest and Mania can be quite the awful experience due to some of the cons I mentioned up there, otherwise it would've been a way better experience. Playing with your friends is a great plus, being possible to play online or local.So, do bear in mind if you want to get this game, the price is reasonable at 25€ base price not applying discounts.

_childDocuments_.review: For this review to be sorta legit I must first inform any readers I am biased for this game franchise, I have loved and played almost all SOR official releases and so everything this game offers is like a gigantic throwback into what I've grown accustomed to and already fell in love with over many times before, except this does it better.It's almost a relief to be saying that a sequel of a game I didn't think could be further refined has in-fact been improved. The formula is so simple it's brilliant, there's little to the combos and the chain is the only incentive (besides score that is) to keep you fighting enemies and pushing boundaries. Racking up the counter is great, seeing numbers go big is probably better but I just like that practically every mob is reactive to the smallest jab, I really dislike beat-em-ups where enemies just have no change to their body/face on being hit, even worse if trash mobs are tanking like pros.. none of that in this game fortunately.DOTEMU has been very good to us fans of the originals, the movesets and the music, I think almost all of what I think back on being good in prior entries is now packaged in here. There are things that could bother people, SOR4 characters don't sprint with the exception of Cherry, Adam is the only other for quick movement and it can be jarring to have enemies running circles around me when I'm slow as a tank, still for how often this occurs it balances out nicely with one exception.That exception being the Mania+ difficulty, where enemies are either on drugs or just have more frames than the player. Alright let me put my hands up in the air, I KNOW it's meant to be hard, like the hardest of all challenges here but it USED TO BE FAIR. Enemies used to have stock movement or close to it and the density was just boosted, yeah sometimes the amount on sections was questionable (stage 9 comes to mind here) but none of it felt plain wrong on learning and adapting to the spawns, it is very much clockwork to recall who comes in where and how they behave on entering.Putting aside that complaint I will mention there is a survival mode dlc which isn't as fleshed out as it could be, specifically in regards to scaling. Fine you know what? It isn't the most unbalanced thing and it'd be a bare-faced lie for me to claim otherwise, I still have bones to pick with scaling though, obviously I don't expect developers to have all the answers but this is what the community is for, I mean if adding suggestions is unbalanced make the most popular toggles. Or at the very least have a mod spotlight post like how Darkest Dungeon did, where the developers are not explicitly making anybody install or add onto the base game but are featuring it for those who would like it, just my two cents.Boss rush is good fun and I think out of all quickplay modes I would pick this in a heartbeat for a fast game, maybe they're a bit too easy to abuse when you've cleared it even once but the movesets are a joy to play against and they still get you every now and again. None of them really feel too easy either, I actually wonder who thought Barbon needed backup, I have to stand still and jump at precise moments just to evade his little combo, doing anything else during that other than the big ultra special moves just leaves you vulnerable to a chance of being hit, brilliant.While I am burned out I had already got my moneys worth long before it happened, I do also foresee myself returning to this in the future but as I'm not the biggest fan of the genre it is a safer bet to say I boot it up sporadically (like before I wrote this review for example) but yeah I do still boot into Arcade and play at minimum 2 or 3 stages straight through.Highly recommended, this is just a blast. Online is a godsend too, I don't mind if people are pros playing with me but man I have met some Gods who play this, just straight up never dying type of players.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. Firstly, there are a decent selection of characters (of which some you only unlock later in the game), all with unique play styles. I recommend trying each of them to find which one best suits your playstyle. The game is often times difficult, but never unfair. Its a decent challenge and there is a good pace to enemy difficulty scaling. Although the campaign is fairly short, its worth replaying to get the highest ranks. Its also worth mentioning that there are other modes unlocked upon completing the campaign. The combos that can be performed are very simple, but you can mix and match different moves and combos to maximise your combo counter, racking up points to earn extra lives. The controls are very simple, making for easily learnt combos. The soundtrack isn't anything too special, but it is however somewhat faithful to the original games. Lastly (and most important to me), the artstyle. This is one of the most beautiful, well designed beat-em-ups I've ever played. The colours are vibrant, the character designs are amazing and unique, the animations are smooth. The art direction in this game is WAY too great to ignore. Its also worth noting that there are interesting video filters in the settings.TLDR: Decent characters, challenging, great combat system, replayable, an ok soundtrack, AMAZING visuals and animations.I highly recommend this game, based on its fun, replayability (i probably butchered the spelling) and its price. I had SO MUCH fun playing it and I'm sure I'm still gonna be playing it for a while. Overall, I give this game a healthy 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems precision-engineered to annoy beat-up-up fans. Here are some gripes:- Armor, armor everywhere! Lots of enemies in this game have armor, hitting you out of strings so it's hard to get a beat-em-up rhythm going. Some bosses activate armor randomly so you don't know when you can get them into hit-stun.- Level design and enemy placements are designed to annoy. You have Dylans on a single-plane stage to take advantage of their long fly-kick reach, Ravens to quickly send you flying off stages with pits, to slippery stages because why not have awkward sluggish movement.- Enemies have over-generous hitboxes, from fat rolls that hit you at max jump height, to multi-dash attacks that cover a large amount of space in 3 planes, to enemy basic attacks being faster and having better Y-axis coverage than yours.- Bosses employ a lot of AOE. Drop whatever combo you have because you're suddenly playing MMO Raiding again, and stay out of the fire until you can safely DPS or your raid leader yells at you.- Finally enemy AI flank too aggressively, especially since their walk speed far outstrips everyone except Cherry and Skate. This causes a lot of awkwardness where everyone gets into a perpetual flanking dance until they get their best attack position.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, we get a sequel to one of the greatest beat’em up franchises ever (you could hardly argue it to be the best one, if only Guardian Heroes wasn’t a thing), and a worthy one. Although it’s from a franchise that is so great it makes hardcore fans go nitpicking around. And it’s easy to find flaws, especially since they essentially always exist. I’ll add my own personal flaws below but I don’t really mind them that much (they are a lot, but keep in mind it’s nothing but pointing out the room for improvement for a great game to be even better). I recommend this game regardless, it’s a step forward in the franchise, the game is harder, enemies are stronger and it feels different while still keeping its core identity. It’s a solid game worth the full price. Besides the amazing graphics, I love how in this game:-	Longest SoR game to date. Although the game is so enjoyable that you’d wish it had even more stages.-	Fall recovery isn’t input-abuseable (now spamming the command doesn’t work, you need to input at the right time)-	Classic unlockable pixelated characters from SoR1~3 are present and do blend in the game, unlike what it seemed to be through YouTube videos before the game launched.-	Said characters were optimized gameplay-wise and some of them are very strong (SoR1 ones in particular), made faster and since they have a less fluid animations they “skip frames” and they’re very fast in general. It’s balanced overall considering only the SoR4 characters are ranked on leaderboards.-	The gameplay is “smooth” and I’d say it’s not too fast nor too slow. Faster than SoR2 and slightly slower than 3.-	You can juggle around and make longer combos that weren’t possible before (enemies can too, btw)-	Said combos are satisfying and since the move set is simple, they’re also pretty easy to execute (and figure them out yourself).-      There is now a much needed Pick Up button. Now the only issue would be picking up life/money items while holding a weapon, but it's fine if you do it while not pressing any directional button.Now let’s go into what I don’t like, and some of my own personal “nitpicking” comes into play here:-	The soundtrack is not bad, but a game of this quality needs a 5* soundtrack, and not a 3~4*.-	The retro soundtrack option is there, but it’s a total mess. If it was something like  instead, it would be epic. But no, it’s a total mess AND there’s actually GameGear songs being used, songs that as no one cares about. Also, they're mostly SoR2/GameGear tracks, which are exactly my least favorite SoR games in gameplay, memorability and in soundtrack quality itself. (I actually had to check the SoR online community for once to realize that SoR2 is the fan favorite of most people, which is so unlike my opinion.) There's also no SoR3 tracks present and the argument for it is that the licensing costs are too expensive.-	The retro soundtrack as of this time is not customizable, which would mostly fix the previous stated flaw. Let’s hope either the devs or fans fix this (most likely the latter).-	At this time online co-op is not working perfectly yet. This was announced to be fixed probably soon.-	No co-op unique attacks (what gives? Multiplayer isn’t even ranked. Not even the original SoR1~3 characters have them in this game)- Take this as you will, I did a whole run with Adam Hunter SoR4 on Hardest (2nd hardest difficulty mode) and I actually couldn't do the Stage 6 - Chinatown, I was already pretty good with Adam. Finally after +20 tries, I gave up and gave Floyd a try. I beat the stage on my first try, with 3 lives remaining. I didn't even play with Floyd much before. He's OP (or maybe it's the rest of the cast that is UP).-	The Special mechanic… Specials don’t have a safe bar like in SoR3, which was an awesome mechanic imho. You lose recoverable life when using them.-	Also, Defensive Specials can’t cancel enemy combos (but many enemies can break yours) so the “defensive” part is only to predict and get invincible frames to prevent an enemy attack. Since you lose life when you perform a special, it would only make sense to use it to not get more damage. Instead, if you perform it at the wrong time, you will lose even more life.-	The Special mechanic works like you lose recoverable life and you can recover it by damaging enemies with normal attacks. But that can give you an intimidating feeling of (how I use to tell myself) a “failed promising Politian”, in which using a Special is a promise to not get hit the moments after, which many times it fails. This usually gives an unsatisfying feeling regarding performing Specials (totally the opposite of SoR3).-	My advice to this? Go nuts and master compact and specific combos along with normal attacks (which you can mix with at will), they do great damage in this game and they’re a must for those big juggling combos. Have fun with using them in moderation, and sometime later with mastery this flaw will be mitigated, somewhat. It's sad to see people doing S rank runs without barely (or at all) using Specials though, that says something.-	So many negative points regarding the Special mechanic, right? Here’s one more: the AI in this game is so aggressive that you can barely perform some Offensive Specials like Axel’s, if you perform that Special when there is more than one enemy on screen you  get hit and your attack/combo broken.-	This one is more subjective: fat enemies are all throwable, by everyone. This was something that made SoR distinguishable, glad that there are many more traits that make SoR SoR, thus not making this a really big deal.-	Also subjective and I don’t even really consider a flaw: this game based itself a bit off SoR2. Amongst the SoR4 cast, only one character can run and another can do a small dash. And there’s no rolling up/down like in SoR3 (unless you pick a SoR3 char). All other characters can only walk and jump.-	More than 1 ending? Alternate routes? Nothing here.All said and done, if you like beat’em ups or co-op fighting games go buy this game right now!

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let's get this out of the way... despite it being part of an iconic franchise, make no mistake, this is an indie game, and that means this is a low budget game, but crafted with love... and trust me, the lack of budget comes through rather quickly and harshly once you get past the amazing eye and ear candy... so temper your expectations.This is so hard to review, because on the one hand, as a "whole package" the game is good, particularly when considering the price point. It's probably a good "novelty game" for younger folks who've never really played these type of games. The aesthetics of this game are really really good, and you can feel the passion behind them.But then we come to the game's biggest issue: The game-play... and it's tied to the financial issues of it being a low budget indie game. To make this short, it's pretty simple: There's just a lack of variety in many regards, but most importantly in regards to enemy variety. That's a problem both because of repetitiveness and more importantly because less enemy types means having to design and balance the game around that deficiency, which leads to devs having to use "cheap" (in both senses of the word) tricks to make up for that lack of content... that's how we end up with obnoxiously frustrating mechanics, enemies with armor, unavoidable ultra fast grabs, and all kinds of "cheap" gimmicks.So here's the thing, personally, I just didn't enjoy playing this because the game seems hellbent on forcing me to play a certain way, when these types of games are more fun when you're allowed to play in a more free-form fashion. The game's perceived difficulty doesn't come organically, but rather it's forced on you by all the limitations imposed by the deficiencies I mentioned above. It's not that it's hard, it's just that it's frustrating (i.e. cheap), and in my opinion, that's just not as fun.That said, again, considering the whole package and the price point, I would actually recommend the game because I'm sure there's a lot of fun to be had for a lot of people. HOWEVER be warned, if you're looking for a specific Beat'em Up experience that's more similar to old-school titles (particularly people looking for something more similar to Streets of Rage 3 or the more recent Fight'N Rage), you need to be aware that this game isn't it AT ALL.So I suppose this is a nice game with a lot of passion behind it, but extremely flawed. I'd be REALLY interested in what this same team could do on a sequel, with a bit more money and a lot more content.Edit: Soooo good news, after many updates and additions to the game, I've changed my mind about it, because it has somewhat addressed some of the issues I had and it is now a pretty well rounded package of a game. It is now a lot more fun than it used to be, and has a lot of newer features (survival mode) that really extend the life of the game.My only wish is they had gone a step further and added the older games somewhere in there to truly be the most complete SOR experience possible... but hey, as it is, they did a good job with it and a really good job of working around the obvious limited budget they had for it.

_childDocuments_.review: An exquisitely hand animated sequel to the beloved Streets of Rage beat-em up franchise, DOtemu/Lizardcube have not only managed to recognize the high points of the series but also added their own mechanical additions to the series that elevates it to new heights and creates THE best entry in the series so far.It's very rare to see a nostalgia sequel that isn't just a cash grab, but manages to recognize exactly what made the originals great and pushes the envelope one further.The new DLC, Mr. X Nightmare, adds 3 playable characters, 2 recreations of fan favorites, and one new character which became a fan favorite quickly after the initial launch on TOP of an infinitely replayable roguelite horde mode that will test even the best players.If you like sidescrolling brawlers/beat-em-ups, you owe it to yourself to experience Streets of Rage 4, especially with the DLC. It has a ton of content for such a small price, the passion just oozes from every little frame of animation from the subtle jiggle of Floyd/Max's massive bulk in their idle animations to the powerful kinetic wind up of Estels drop kick. This is the new standard.

_childDocuments_.review: growing up playing the classic streets of rage games, alongside games like final fight, avp, etc. in the arcades, i absolutely love beat em ups. i've spent countless hours of my younger days playing the 3 streets of rage games, especially 2. i was disappointed sega never really made any new games based on their vast IP, and more so the streets of rage series.when streets of rage remake was released, it was a godsend. but sega shot it down. many had hoped it would mean sega planned to do something with the series. it was a long wait, but we finally got streets of rage 4.as for the game itself, it's not very long, typical of an arcade style beat em up. that being said, it's a good length. graphically, it's an upgrade to the old pixel art, and it looks great, standing up well to most modern 2D fighters. of course, many of us probably had hoped to see a bit more characters, or an extension to the story, there's still hope for future dlcs (as of writing).the one aspect of the game that some might argue was inferior, is perhaps the soundtrack. no longer do we have yuzo koshiro mixing it up, but personally, i think it's quite acceptable still.overall, it's a great, fun, bite-sized game, that you can pick up, play for a bit, then put it down. if you're a fan of beat em ups, and more so if you're a fan of streets of rage, this one is definitely well worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: Early impressions:Aside from not being a huge fan of the new artstyle, I'm really enjoying this game.The good thing is that it goes beyond just nostalgia (though there's a lot of it in there) - it's a really well made game that is fun on its own right too. I really enjoy the few changes made to the old beat 'em up formula.Enemies are pretty aggressive and the player doesn't have a "dodge" button like in SoR3 - instead, the Special Attack has few invulnerable frames, so you need to use it as a dodge mechanic plus counter-attack. This ties up on the change to special attack costs - they still cost health, but now this health can be recovered by attacking as enemies, as long as you don't get hit.The result is a dynamic combat in which the player needs to pay attention to what enemies are doing, as their attacks have wind-up animations and other giveaways. Timing your specials to dodge enemies while hitting as many of them as possible, jumping out of area-of-effect attacks, grabbing thrown weapons, etc.I'm enjoy the challenge level too. I'm playing on Hard and finding that the game puts up a good but fair fight. And there are still two difficulties above (and two bellow) that.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely isn't a bad game. It's a true homage to the classic beat'em up, but it tries so hard to be an homage that the game got stuck into the limitations of the classic SoR. For the true fans of Streets of Rage saga, this game will be a jewel, undoubtely. But when you compare it to other classics like Violent Storm (in my opinion the best beat'em up ever created), the game pales. I mean, the moveset for every character is somewhat limited, and soon the gameplay will become very repetitive, doing the same move again, and again, and again. This game would have really shine with a better moveset for the characters, just to add more variety and dynamism to the game. Indeed, it's a very good game. But unfortunately, it's not a step forward from the classic SoR in any way. In fact, I would have prefer a more pixel-y style, instead of that supersmooth look. Only get this if you are a true fan of the classic saga. If you are looking for a good beat'em up, get Fight'n Rage instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Streets of Rage 4 is a fantastic beat'em up that brings back the spirit of the 90s.It has everything that a game like this should have: tight controls, ridiculous combos, lively colour palette, awesome soundtrack and even lots of easter eggs from previous games. While the campaign doesn't last too long (though that's to be expected), the replayability is very high as there are lots of different characters and movesets to choose from.I enjoyed this game with a friend using Remote Play Together and we had lots of fun. Some levels (Chinatown, Y Tower, etc.) are exceptionally great: you know, when the screen is filled with enemies but it doesn't matter because the combat is super fluid and the soundtrack is really adrenaline pumping! Also, with the Mr. X Nightmare DLC, the content has been extended further and the survival mode proved to be a great and addicting inclusion along with some new, awesome music tracks.In short, if you are a fan of the genre, Streets of Rage 4 is worth every penny even at full price!

_childDocuments_.review: Streets of rage 4 manages to add a fresh coat of paint to this long dormant series. The comic book art style is amazing. Series veterans Axel Blaze and Adam make their spectacular return with all their moves in tact and some new tricks and are joined by new comers Floyd  and Adam's Daughter Cherry who both bring new Tricks to the table.  This time around Floyd pays the role of the bruiser and must have paid a visit to a certain metal armed special forces agent from another fighting game we all know and love and this is not a bad thing by any means and although slow he is capable of dishing out some serious damage. If you like a more fast paced damage dealer than Cherry is your girl she wields a guitar and if used properly she can bounce from enemy to enemy dealing damage to multiple combatants ant once also she has one of the best throw moves in the game in my opinion while Floyd can pick  up multiple enemies at once Cherry can literally tackle a single target and if you put her in the right throw position  deal loads of damage to that one enemy. If all of this isn't enough playing through the games 12 stages gives you a chance to unlock content such as the retro soundtracks to all 3 games as well as the ability to play the characters from all of those franchises with all of their original sprites. I also really enjoy the combo system they have taken a page again out of modern fighters with this one where you can Juggle enemies and deal massive amounts of damage special moves are also more viable now as doing a special move and fallowing up with a flawless combo regenerates the lost health. This game can also be played online with one other person or locally with up to 4 people. I am glad to see this excellent franchise get such a fantastic reboot. If you are a long time Streets of rage fan or a new comer to these types of games and are wanting to see the best the beat em up genre has to offer  and have $26 to $28 to spare than  you should not hesitate to pick Streets Of Rage 4 up as it is well worth  the price.The 1 Gripe I do have  with this game is that there are a few enemies that do feel a bit cheap especially the Riot Police these guys have shields and in order to fight them you have to break the shield but when you try to break the shield they knock you down with their night stick and recharg their shield.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is gonna sound real pretentious, it's impossible to talk about this game without feeling pretentious, it's one of THOSE games. This game feels less like a really good beat em up game and more like the pinnacle of the genre. It feels like every beat em up from Final Fight to Scott Pilgrim has been leading up to Streets of Rage 4's release.The controls are buttery smooth, the combat is intense, satisfying, and technical, the multiple characters all have vastly different playstyles. You are guaranteed to find a character that fits you, especially now with the unlockable and DLC characters added in. Combos are fun and interesting, while not being required to get good at the game. Depending on the character you pick, your optimal combos can be 4 or 5 inputs, or require tight jump loops and hard to execute cancels, it's ultimately up to you whether you optimize your damage, it's not a requirement at all.I came into this with high hopes, I had heard almost unanimous praise for this game, and even my expectations were blown sky high.Play this game, please PLEASE play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent return of a much loved series! There is also a varied roster of characters to choose from and even some hidden retro characters from previous games to unlock. It's not overly long but is pretty challenging even on Medium. There are a few easter eggs to discover on some levels that fans of the series will appreciate. As with previous games, this is best played with a friend. The Steam version allows you to share the game with someone on your friends list so you only have to buy one copy to get into co-op!The artwork and animation shown in the early trailers always looked a bit underwhelming and flash-game-like to me, but the final product looks amazing with lots of extra polish and detail and has some really cool lighting effects on the 2D characters. _childDocuments_.review: Please note: I initially played this via a review code provided to , which I am a long term writer for.  But have since purchased the full game with my own money.When my fellow Judge first game back to me, after having spent some time with Streets of Rage 4, his first words were “it’s like Streets of Rage 2, but better.” Rarely have words been spoken which is so wrong, and yet so right at the same time. This…where do I even begin? It’s amazing. Everything about it is just…just right. Featuring so many characters, including all of the legacy greats as well as some interesting new ones. Each with very distinct, unique fighting styles. It brings with it everything, literally everything, from every previous Rage game, as well as a few new tweaks that just make it even better.Remember those really cool, but really dangerous power attacks? The ones that would do massive damage, usually a combo of some kind, but also drain your health if your action bar wasn’t full? Those are back, just as strong, but now always drain your health. However, it’s not gone permanently. Rather, each application reduces your total health, but allows you to recover it all simply by hitting enemies. Assuming you land enough hits before you take one yourself, you become a raging, immortal force of nature, powered by sheer gumption and some of the best retro-future graphics I’ve ever seen in a side-scrolling brawler.It’s like the game came straight out of my memories, with the nostalgia filter applied to it full force. Making it not only as good as it was, but genuinely as good as you remember, if you follow my meaning. You know how nostalgic memories fill in a lot of the gaps in how rough something was at the time? Like the old Transformers cartoons, for example. Everything was so beautifully aminated and lively in your head, but is a bit dull and really cheap in reality (though still amazing).  Well, then this is The Transformers The Movie, if you follow the analogy. Just go buy this game. It’s amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: The honest reality is that this ended up being about as disappointing as I suspected it would be from the initial gameplay videos. The visuals are nicer and flashier, and they've finally added the story they couldn't fit into 90's technology. But that's about all the good that's come out of this.The fighting system is about as simplistic as where we left it back in the 90's, which works in the broad strokes, but comes across as clunky, dull, and, on occasion, a glint of cheapness comes through and I feel the icy touch of the arcade industry and its quarter-stealing tactics. It goes in with a goal of maintaining "authenticity" by glazing over decades of progress and comes out the other end as "serviceable but inelegant."Meanwhile, character movement is , clocking in at the pace of a geriatric dog. I cannot express how much this brings down the entire experience. Only one character has a run ability (her walk being just as slow as everyone else), and that's to make up for her being incredibly weak. Thus, closing the distance on your enemies requires slipshod alternative approaches, like weaving up and down the screen and hoping your enemy doesn't suddenly jump away at a speed I  we could move.But what really kills me is the one bit of modern gaming they  pick up on: DLC. Throughout the game, you'll see characters like Max, Roo and Shiva and think, "Oh boy, how do I unlock them?" Because that's what we did in the Genesis days. And if this had been really been true to its roots, that's exactly what would've happened here. There is not a question in my mind.Instead, here comes the Mr. X DLC to sell us what they cut out; whether it was cut out of the game itself, or out of their plans for the initial release, it makes no difference. Particularly at a $25 price point.It does nothing new, and what it's brought back isn't any more satisfying than what they did before. But I suppose there are worse sins than producing a lazy cash-in sequel. Maybe buy it on sale, or play it from a friend's library.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time fan of the series i was pretty nervous this game wouldn't live up to my expectations. Thankfully SoR4 is a worthy sequel & arguably the best in the series. The new combo system is my favourite addition- keep hitting enemies & the count rises & you accrue a score that builds with each successive hit. The score is cashed in when you fail to hit an opponent quick enough to keep the chain going (or are hit), but you risk losing it all if you're counter hit. Combo's are the key to high scores, & this game features a stage replay mode & boss rush where you can aim to get a perfect S rating.Each level brings with it some new environmental hazards to negotiate as well as new enemy types. There are 12 stages in all & all of them are good- with a few easter eggs & homages to the earlier games & some other Sega IP.Music was aways going to be hard to follow- but actually it's very good. It doesn't have the same impact that the Megadrive soundtrack did back in the 90's- largely because back then EDM in videogames was rare until the PS1 arrived with WipEout. Only really Sonic CD had a comparable soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: Streets of Rage 4 is a fantastic addition to the long dormant series. As far as the genre goes, SoR4 leans more towards the old school side of things, particularly when it comes to controls. There's no double tap to run except for one character. No blocks or parries. You gotta be on your toes and avoid being in direct line of sight of many enemies at the same time. Reminds me of some classics like the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles and Double Dragon games of old. Mind you, none of this is a bad thing in my opinion. It keeps the controls very simple and easy to just pick up and play, but also fun to learn and master as you go. In fact, the few different attacks you have combo very well for the most part and you are actively rewarded for keeping long combos going as they are worth more points (and with enough points you gain an extra life).Conversily, it also introduces a few interesting elements to keep the experience fresh. Characters have special move that cost health to use. Now the way that works is a portion of your health goes green (instead of the original yellow) to indicate spent health. Beat up enemies and you'll gradually regain that lost health, but get hit even once, and you'll lose ALL green health plus whatever the attack that hit you damaged you for. It makes strategic usage of special moves a good idea. The game features fantastic 2D hand painted art and incredible animation. It is a blast to play through it for this reason alone. As much as I like pixel art, there's no denying that the vibrant, comic book art style chosen for the game is gorgeous.The soundtrack features Dotemu's own composer, but also a fair bit of tracks by the original Streets of Rage composers, Yuzo Koshiro and Motohiro Kawashima and even a bunch of one-off guest composers. There's even the option to enable "retro soundtrack" in the menu, although this doesn't let you listen to the entire soundtrack of the old games. Just a few selected tracks from Streets of Rage 1 and 2 and a few "8-bit" style renditions of old tracks. The game also features unlimited continues by default, different difficulty settings and a small variety of assist mode options, so you can make the game as easy or hard as you like. You can ever turn on Arcade Mode for the genuine experience of beating the whole game in one go. The game is fairly replayable. The characters feel fairly unique (Blaze being very good with aerial attacks and Cherry being really fast, for instance). It also features a few unlockable characters as well as different modes (including the aforementioned arcade mode as well as a boss rush).Not only that, there's also an online mode avaible. While I haven't tried it yet I can say playing beat'em ups with friends always felt more fun to me personally.Whether you're new to the beat'em up genre and are looking to give it a try, a diehard fan of the Streets of Rage series or anything inbetween, Streets of Rage 4 is sure to provide some very fun hours of gameplay!

_childDocuments_.review: Such a blast from the past! Having beaten the story mode in just a couple of hours I can say that there is a lot of replay value to this game. The characters each have their own unique combos that make the game play fun and enticing while you try to figure out which character you like best. There is a larger myriad of weapons to be found in the game, some of which will help you unlock the secret boss fights. The art style is very refreshing and reminds me so much of reading comics back when I was a kid. They offer two button layouts, one being closer to the traditional SoR games and another control scheme that is honestly very nice. After Beating the story mode the first time I started up again but with a better understanding of the controls and combos, it made it a breeze. As you progress through the game you fill a little score bar. Get it to one of the three points along the bar and get something nice! My only gripe with the game is that it sometimes seems a little difficult to know exactly where to stand in order to pick up items. All in all I would highly recommend this game to anyone that enjoys that classic beat'em up style action. Bring some friends with you, you'll like it even more!
