_childDocuments_.review: Exceptional game, in graphics, game modes, and gameplay. Combat is extremely satisfying with each hit emphasized by sounds and visuals; The enemies are diverse, the scenarios detailed and unique.I also love how well balanced the game is in terms of its scenes and the length of its levels. It is a game that can be finished quickly, but there are so many characters, movements, and combos to perform, that the length of the game ends up being infinite if you like the dynamics of the game.I also bought the expansion “Mr. X Nightmare”, I was a little skeptical because I had heard that it was just a survival mode and nothing more, but it has a lot of content. It is a “Survival” mode but it has upgrades between each wave of enemies, as well as different scenarios, and on top of that, you can unlock moves for each character - which you can use in all game modes -, the expansion also adds some very good characters that serve as bosses in the story mode, but because of their moves and the way they play; They are extremely fun to try.In general, I was quite impressed, I think it is one of the best beat'em ups I have ever played; simply fantastic in every way.
_childDocuments_.name: Streets of Rage 4

_childDocuments_.review: The story leaves a lot to be desired and Skate(My favorite character) doesn't get an updated appearance, or any mention, nod or reference in the narrative, but aside from this, The game is really everything I could've hoped for across the 26 year gap between this and 1994's Bare Knuckle 3.It's absolutely gorgeous to see in motion and the new combo system gives the game levels of depth similar to Street Fighter, which is something Ancient was always striving for with Streets of Rage 2 and 3, The pacing is excellent as is the variety in enemy and level designs, and every fighter feels either authentic to a tee or extremely fleshed out, often both.With 12 extra Playable characters to unlock, 5 difficulty levels, an addictive scoring system, post Launch Support planned for the future, 2 player online (up to 4 with Steam Remote Play or Parsec) and surprisingly fun extra modes, You absolutely must check this game out if you're a fan of the genre, hell even if you aren't try it anyway, Video Games do not get more pure than this.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent follow-up to the SOR games. I was not sure about the cartoon graphics at first, but it grew on me after a while. Two small criticisms: 1) mobility is restricted compared to the previous installment in the franchise, SOR3; in SOR 3, every character could run by pressing back or forward twice or roll to dodge an attack by pressing up or down twice; in SOR4, only one character has the ability to run like this, however, without the ability to roll; I did get used to this, though; 2) the special ability from SOR3 was removed, and I am not talking about the Y button: in SOR3 on SEGA, you could press an action button (Z on the 6-button controller, if I am not mistaken) and a series of movement buttons to perform three variations of a special running attack; the same attacks could be performed simply by pressing the attack button while running by earning the required number of stars.For the most part, the game feels quite fair on normal, getting a bit punishing only at the last stage. Higher difficulties provide a good challenge. One walkthrough on normal doesn't take much time, but the replayability is there. Overall, a good beat-em-up, if you like SOR (especially 1 and 2) and are ready to overlook some differences from SOR3 (which I consider a step back. tbh), you will like it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran SOR play I can say with confidence GET THIS GAME! First few days were frustratingly difficult, but 2 things I had to realize. 1. It plays like and old school Street Fighter game.2. Learn the enemies tendencies, kinda like monster hunter. All of them, not just the bosses.Wake up moves and armor, counters, each characters weaknesses (except Floyd hehe) all have to be mastered. Long gone are the days of cheesy infinite stun locks with a jab or corner slams. However, if skilled enough, you can chain together combos that basically destroy a boss in seconds, so same effect, just much more fun this way. Easy to learn, fun to master.  I hope they add a few things TBH**Adjustments to the players hitbox. Far too many times you can get hit by the enemy but you cant hit them. Usually when they are standing slightly above you. This has to get fixed ASAP**-Pretty much everything done in the fan made Streets of Rage Remake game needs to make its way into SOR4 in some fashion. ESPECIALLY the concept of Blazes Shop for earning stuff. So much replay ability there. -New levels (with multiple routes to take. See Streets of Rage Remake for reference)-Raid-New characters-Optional A.I. teammate-New weapons (E.I. Nunchucks, Staff)-New skins to earn-A training room-A traditional pvp mode (like street fighter) yes I know itll need balancing but its doable-Mania+ difficulty doubling enemies health and small buff to speed-All characters without a dash get +15% movement speed buff*Not required, but would LOVE to see something like a slotted item to earn that gives you new and exciting ways to play. For example, a held item that allows you to gain a small over heal when regaining health lost from a special move. Or say, you get a damage boost if your health lost from special moves is more than 50% of your health bar (risk reward). Doesnt have to be exactly those, but something.Either way, the game is great, And I think they would be crazy not to support it with reasonably priced DLC.  Music IMO is the second best in the series close behind SOR2. I know some loyalist stuck in the 90's will disagree, but to me the tracks are solid and I can think of at lease 5-6 that would be a BANGER at any party in the world. Beautiful Graphics and crispy 60fps too and barely uses 2 cores to run it all in ultra detail (using 4 core i5-6402 processor). This game is well worth the price and in my opinion the BEST Streets of Rage game to date. Get this game trust me. To the Dev team... Outstanding job remaking one of my favorite games growing up!

_childDocuments_.review: I think we can skip the part where everybody writes in their reviews "This is a game serie from my childhood" because I am no exception. Lets get to the point, and everything I write down is my own viewpoint and opinion. After installing the game, I launched it, sat back and watched the entire intro play. After the "Press any button" showed, I felt void of any emotions. Nothing in the intro fueled me to get excited. Go watch the opening title of Bare Knuckle 1 or 2 (aka Streets of Rage). The melody alone makes you realize this city needs you. That darkness is looming over the city. That you, the player, are the one to take on the fight. Combine that with the text and images and you feel like pumped to get going. With Streets of Rage 4? Nothing. The music, dull. The images, nicely drawn but don't add anything. The "story", has potential but felt weak.Well, I should've went with my gut feeling. Playing the game was only confirming what I felt during the intro. I'll keep this part short because fanboys/girls are going to furiously deny and the haters of this game thing I am on their side.I don't know. I probably know why I loved SoR1, 2 and 3. The games felt gritty, raw, dark. Which is good. The art, the spriting everything fit this setting. The enemies were real street punks, giving you a hard time. (Final Fight does a good job on this part too). The bosses were real, strong. Everything about the classic SoR games is good because of these reasons.SoR4 brings us misery. Extremely polished dull looking enemies, fighting with boring movements and most of the time just staring at you. I played exactly for 37 minutes. Completed three stages and felt completely drained of any will to keep on fighting. Encountering so many "You cannot knock me down" enemies and cheap movement sets just made me really sad. Were there any good things about the game besides of all this? Probably there are, but I didn't find them. If there was anything good beyond Stage 3, I'll just take your word on it.The developers and designers try to balance and please both old fans and try to draw new fans. But looking at the protagonist line up, it feels like they attempted a remake/remaster, but slapped the story of a "new source of evil" to make it feel like a sequel.Not recommended. In my opinion not worth the current price. A dull game which aged poorly.

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a neutral review.Being a SoR fan since childhood, I really wanted to like this game, and in my opinion, it's one of the best beat 'em up revival attempts from the similar recently released titles (Ninja Warriors Once Again being the best one out of the bunch, imo), but this game has several problems or decisions I'm not a fan of.-Super armor. The main issue which ruins the experience for me. It always feels cheap and annoying, and even when you know when to strike, if you're half a second late, you will start hitting an enemy who doesn't give a f about your attacks, and will deal you cheap damage with no time to react, I hate it. The previous SoR entries didn't have any super armor, and always felt fair, with regular enemies and bosses teaching the player when you can or can't hit them.-The fighting system itself feels like a step back from SoR3/BK3 (and 2 steps back from SoR Remake). There's no run and roll, weapon specials, etc. The game in general feels much slower and less balanced, compared to the previous entries.-The aerial specials and juggling are good additions, but I don't like how you need to restore large chunks of health by attacking enemies after using specials in general; the risk is much higher than the reward, so I rarely used them, especially considering that you can't get out of the enemy's combos or grabs with a defensive special (so you either have to take damage or use limited star moves), and offensive specials don't seem to deal more damage than blitz attacks. More than that...-Most enemies' normal attack range is longer than the player's, some vertical hitboxes are wonky and won't trigger your hits (this is especially noticable on knife-carrying Galsias), many enemies' attacks have the aforementioned super armor, and some enemy attacks feel very cheap in general (especially the diagonal or projectile attacks, like Garnet's jumpkick, Heart's fire breath, belly flops and rolls, Silver's gun, etc. - if you're playing as a slow character who can't get close enough to these types of enemies, it will be very hard to get out of the corner and recover, as you can't run to get close to the enemies to hit them in time and you can't dodge their attacks in any way).-The idea of "upgraded" enemies of the same type isn't bad in itself, but I don't like how it is executed, as these enemies feel overpowered and cheap (like Donovans who can throw and catch weapons, bikers and thai fighters who use screen-wide diagonal attacks, and of course all of them have super armor).-The stages themselves look pretty good, but sometimes the use of colors makes them feel not as vibrant as in the previous entries. I'm also not a fan of the new enemy character designs and some of the old character redesigns; seeing old enemies such as Abadede, Jack and old bikers drawn in SoR4 style in the Gallery just makes me wish we got them instead of the stupid thicc bikers, generic cops, karate guys, and those annoying punk girls throwing junk at you.-Speaking of punk girls, I dislike how grenades work in this game - instead of dealing damage to both player and enemies, the grenades have a "friend or foe" identification system, which just feels weird.-The plot is silly even by SoR standards. Brainwashing by bad music, seriously? SoR1 and SoR2 were straight to the point, and SoR3 had some weird ideas in it (though robots were already present in SoR2, and Mr.X could've staged his own death, if we consider that the real Mr.X was shown in the bad ending, and the brain in the tube wasn't Mr.X's), but the tone was serious, and the stakes were high; it didn't feel silly or out of place. Also, the Y twins don't carry the same energy and charisma Mr.X had.-Not really an issue, but some elements are blatantly ripped off from the fan-made SoR Remake (train stage (right down to the warning sign and traffic lights you have to jump over), roof hopping stage, some of Adam's moveset), which makes me wish SoRR was the real SoR4.-It was noted in the dev interviews that some of the ideas which were cut from the original games would be restored in SoR4, such as the car crashing into a wall on stage 1. This is all cool, however, the bike stages from SoR3, which are some of the most known cut content of the series, are nowhere to be seen. To say that I felt disappointed when I saw heroes getting on bikes in the cutscene after stage 5, and there was no bike stage, is an understatement. SoR Remake had these stages restored and redone, and they were short and pretty fun. Shin Nekkestu Kouha Kunio-tachi no Banka also had some bike stages in pseudo-3D with a view from behind, and these stages made the game more memorable and varied.-The sound effects and voices are not as juicy, and lack the impact sfx and voices had in the previous entries.-The music is pretty good, but overall not as memorable as in the previous entries. Kawashima's and Koshiro's tracks are especially great, the guest tracks are pretty good, and Olivier's tracks are hit or miss for me (I like stage 3, 4 and 7 themes, but the rest ranges from "okay" to "meh"; I'm not saying Olivier is a bad composer, it's just some of his tracks don't carry the same energy SoR series' music is known for). The retro music feels very weird though - the placement of tracks itself feels random (SoR2 last boss theme at stage 1 boss? SoR2 boss theme at stage 2? Beatnik on the Ship, but not Max Man at Shiva fight? None of the elevator themes used in elevator sections? SoR1 ending theme at stage 9??? What were they thinking?!), for some reason the music from SoR1 is used from the SMS/GG versions, but not the original SMD version, and there's no music from SoR3 at all (Just why? SoR3 soundtrack was experimental, but it has some of the best tracks in the series!). Though I gotta say, the addition of unused tracks, such as Little Money Avenue or Walking Bottom was pretty nice.-Also, the Mr.X Nightmare DLC should've been a free DLC, imo. The new characters practically were already in the game as bosses, and while the Survival mode is pretty fun, it can get very random and unfair at times. The unlockable moves also feel lazily animated and executed, and most of the new weapons look silly. The new music is good though.-No playable Ash.Personally, this game feels like a step back after SoR3, and makes me feel spoiled by the amazing fan-made SoR Remake (which I highly recommend and consider to be the best SoR game and one of the best beat 'em up games in general).Despite the above, SoR4 a decent beat 'em up, and I can't say it's a bad game. You can definitely have some fun with it, but there are just flaws that ruin the game for me. It's definitely leagues better in terms of respecting the original series and in execution, compared to such atrocities as Double Dragon Neon, River CIty Girls or Battletoads 2020. I'd say get it on sale, it's not bad.

_childDocuments_.review: What a great beat 'em up game this is. I don't normally play games of the genre, but I used to have a Sega Genesis years ago and remember first playing this game on that. _childDocuments_.review: WOW. For an old timer this is like taking a stroll down memory lane and burning that ♥♥♥♥♥♥ to the ground! Beautiful animation and retro aesthetic abound with new moves, new characters and returning favorites make this new take on the series a worthwhile buy and a definite must have for anyone missing those awesome days of 16 bit. I like the soundtrack even though it in my opinion somewhat pales next to the classic (I'm listening to The Revenge of Mr. X from the Yuzo Koshiro Collection 2 as I write this.) and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is this a ton of fun. The animation is silky smooth and the combos can be started from every angle including throwing toons against the wall to have them bounce back and continue the juggling torture something the old series did not have but is a welcome addition to this new game.  The fluidity of combat can not be under stated, this is amazing. The design choice for Axel's pants leave a bit to be desired but his older looks jives with the 10 year time gap from 3 to 4. Mr. X can't be dead but if he is hell bring along his family X and Y chromosomes ;-) - I can't wait for the retro reveal soon too. I'll give this a 10 out of 10 because what the hell. I'm ♥♥♥♥♥♥' old and this is a bad ass game! Thanks developers from the bottom of my heart. This is AWESOME.After more time with the game I am hooked. I think people are being a bit tough on the game and seriously negative for no reason. Honestly the players do have a couple solid points though, about the game including the Run function from Streets of Rage 3 which was only INTRODUCED in that game. Same as Bare Knuckle. Second I did see the soundtrack option and it does sound good but the music from Part 1 is a mixed up fan boy like mess. I like that the music fits characters returning from part 1, 2 and 3 the original game music is not what the game sounded like on the Sega Genesis or in Bare Knuckle 1. I think it comes from one of Yuzo's compilations because several are 8 bit tuned and those are most definitely NOT from the original Sega Genesis sound chip. I do like the music being randomized somewhat for other themes. Honestly as a game this is different. Nothing can top the old Sega graphics for me because artistically they always did more with less and all the game graphics are amazing and there are a ton of options including CRT and Retro CRT. You can change it so complaints there to me are pretty weak. The run would be a welcome addition and I think they will do it. Community participation and buyers should receive that with the new update (Please developers. Thank you if you read this because we REALLY NEED the RUN function. Please.)The game play can be played and it is a bit rough on the D-pad setup but this seems to be a controller issue ONLY and not completely a game issue per se. You can also use the sticks on the controller too and this works beautifully but timing is a serious issue but it can be MANAGED. It seems the game is getting a crappy rep because of typical consumer entitlement (IMHO no offense intended) but it is worth a buy. The price is perfect as is. As a game it is 20 to 30 dollars cheaper than the original games when they were released and their MSRP was around $29.99 to 39.99 for SoR 1, $49.99 to 59.99 for SoR2 (which was truly F****** awesome when it was released) and SoR 3 was usually $49.99 to as high as $69.99 in some places during its original release in 1994. Bare Knuckle 1 through 3 was similarly prices in Japan too. The UK was generally 5 to 10 dollars more expensive because of the price of the British pound against our dollar, imports would always be more pricey.You now also have an auto save system so even if you get sent back you can work your way up. What people are really complaining about I think is the difficulty. That was the way it was in the originals until cheat codes so the save system also relegates certain cheat codes to the recycle bin. It can be a hassle but it is supposed to be part of the fun to need to replay it and replay it and getting your a** kicked was part of the bargain you signed when you bought games. Art style is beautiful, it is more fluid and animated and as an upgrade works. The art style has the original enemies actually looking cool now as opposed to pixilized.There are some updates, I like the mutual respect angle that shows up between one old enemy and the team and was pleasantly surprised when it happened I fan boy'd a bit :-)Recommended definitely, you play this for the difficulty, that was part of the package of side scrolling beat 'em ups. Final Fight no matter the iteration was always way more brutal in difficulty to me than any of the SoR games so it is nice from an older players perspective having played this when it came out the enhanced difficulty adjust works for me. I wish you would return some options like he amount of lives you start out with and the run feature from 3, plus the special feature from 1 maybe with Adam's department as back up as opposed to the police attacking you (which I thought was pretty sweet seeing that make a comeback in game). The Nostalgia level is through the roof so if you liked it before you really need to play it and be damned the difficulty. This game is definitely worth buying in my opinion.I have played even more since I reviewed this game and I was wrong about the sound track. Actually seeing the Credits at the end of the game I do take what I said earlier back. it isn't a mess and the option to switch it between the new sound tracks and the retro sound tracks is a HUGE plus for me. If not I can always listen to a play list of all the Yuzo Koshiro music I own so no harm no foul. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND this game. It deserves better than the negative reviews it is getting and these young pups have ZERO clue what makes a good game or even how to properly review a title. The negative reviews suck *ss and aside from the Run function missing they have zero clues what they're talking about. I MISS the old days of Diehard Game Fan/Club magazine, those guys would have known how to properly review this title. Aside from yours truly of course!;-)Edit: This game NEEDED to be nominated this year. If we want more really cool retro projects like this we NEED to support them fully, both on STEAM and in other media.

_childDocuments_.review: Prefacing this by saying this is the first game I've played in the series. The art and the music are incredible, each stage looks unique with a different setting with music for each stage. The characters are varied and have their own strengths and weaknesses and I can see myself doing another play-through with the other characters. The story is there but not too interesting but it's a vehicle for introducing other characters you can play and the environments you see.While I enjoyed the combat I felt it would have been great to have an ability to get out of throws and to be able to block. Throughout the game it's all offensive options and not enough defensive ones unless you consider strafing to dodge attacks which I found clunky, slow and not fun. When using your special moves, it uses a portion of your health which can be recoverable indicted by the green bar at the end of your health; in order to recover it you have to hit enemies. I feel like a special bar could have been better since food is already scarce and health is already so valuable because of how difficult it is to get lives. This goes back to all offensive but no basic defensive options like tech throws or blocking.Once you finish the story, you unlock a variety of additional modes. One of the standout ones is survival where you go through waves of enemies through more environments you didn't see in the story as well as new and reoccurring enemies. Each wave you get power-ups to make yourself stronger and it can be played in online co-op. It's fun and varied and you don't know what's coming next.I do love when you complete the story and do some survival, you're rewarded with being able to see the concept art of the environments and characters

_childDocuments_.review: When Streets of Rage Remake came out over 10 years ago I thought that was as close as we were going to get to a definitive version of the 90s sidescrolling beatemup. Now I'm finally happy to say that in 2020, Streets of Rage is BACK and better than ever! Dotemu & Guard Crush did such a great job translating classic SoR gameplay into a new era. The animation, which I was initially skeptical about, is beautiful in motion, the cast is unique and interesting, and the challenge is unforgivingly old-school in the best way. Subtle yet far-reaching adjustments like wall bounce combos and being able to rally back health add a surprising amount of depth to a game with two attack buttons. The best beatemup since SoR 2.

_childDocuments_.review: A polished, loving tribute to old school beat-em ups. This developer loves the genre, and it shows. Just the right amount of power and flexibility granted to the player while still allowing for real challenge the higher up the difficulty scale you go. No additional greedy monetization at launch, actual unlockable extras for play time and hidden bits here and there. This also serves as a welcoming entry to the genre for newer gamers who never experienced them in their heyday, with enough simplicity to ease players in, but enough variety to keep boredom from setting in too quickly. Multiplayer is a straight up joy, barring bad connections making things less enjoyable, and no drop-in or out(probably because of the way the game keeps score as well as coding complexity)makes for a fairly limited way of joining games randomly.The only drawback to the game for me at this time is the inability to select two playable characters who are in the game with modern artwork revision but only as the traditional sprites. I truly hope this changes down the road as they are wonderfully rendered in the new style. One last thing to add; the Story mode is long and packed with action, to the point where after one playthrough my hands need a break. Too long isn't exactly the term, but perhaps modifying the story to allow for branching paths could shorten the strain on my digits.

_childDocuments_.review: :It took nearly 30 years, but one of the most popular Beat ‘em Ups has finally returned. Developed by ,  and ,  is a follow up of Sega's Streets of Rage series, a trilogy of games released during the early 1990s for the Sega Genesis.I’ve been a long hardcore fan of the Streets of Rage series and when I heard that a fourth title would come out I was thrilled! However, after playing for a while this new title I rapidly realized that there were some odd gameplay mechanic choices that can hinder the overall experience.In this new title players can perform a  (stars are hidden throughout the stages). This powerful attack gives the player invincibility frames for a very short time but no longer covers the whole area, unlike its predecessors.. It’s the same mechanics as it was before: You can grab an enemy and toss him away. Also, ” from previous entries is present in this game too and each character has a unique signature move.Players can perform another special attack that leaves a portion of your HP in a blue color. Afterwards, it is required to hit enemies in order to regain your HP again, but if you get hit before regaining it, you will permanently lose it.  because using this ability means a , so you will, most of the time, avoid to use this unless you are swarmed by enemies. I understand that this was used to prevent players from spamming the special attack, but why not follow the Streets of Rage 3 footsteps? It was much better made. Basically, you have a bar that increases over time and when it’s full you can perform the special attack without health penalties. That’s not my only complaint though, since unlike its predecessors,  (aside from Cherry and some characters you can later unlock) so dodging some moves is impossible if you are in the wrong place at the wrong time!Many times I would see the attack coming but couldn’t do anything because of this game’s lack of any real way to dodge it and since the special attack doesn’t work once you get stunned, your only option is to have half of your health bar be taken away. This kind of gameplay turns out to be quite unfair and unbalanced in my opinion and it feels like older games are a bit more polished than this. Now to make everything even worse,  around them that negates any damage and also some of their attacks can even override your attacks entirely.: As you might already have guessed, movement can be on the sluggish side due to the lack of running and/or rolling ability making you a sitting duck in many situations. After playing with a Streets of Rage 3 character (you have the roll and run ability), I feel like that should be the way to play this game from the get go.: To grab food on the ground players have now another button designed just for it. It’s a welcoming change that contrasts previous games because sometimes I remember eating food by mistake since the attack button and the eating food button were the same. To avoid this, players would have to avoid attack near food in previous titles but now this is no longer a problem!: I know it’s a small new feature but I liked the fact that you can now grab a thrown item in midair. You can throw an object at your enemies and right away grab it in midair. Spamming this attack can really help you get away from, otherwise, dangerous situations. However, you need to be careful with some enemies that can also do the same to you! Aside from this, I wish characters could perform different special abilities with certain items like in older games. For example, only Blaze could perform a special ability with a knife or only Axel could perform a special ability with a pipe, etc.There’s another cool feature that was implemented in this game: . Basically, it counts the number of times you attack in a row without taking any damage. If you take damage or lose too much time to perform the next attack the combo breaks. Combos are important to gain extra points and thus extra lives!Overall, I think the gameplay of Streets of Rage 4 is fairly good, but it could be so much better and more polished so I guess it was a bit of a disappointment to me due to the, somewhat, unbalanced gameplay. Some previous games, while not perfect, feel a bit more polished and well designed.There’s a lot of content in this game regarding the playable Characters since you can have up to 17 choices! You start out only with a small range of playable characters, 4 to be more precise, but as you play the game various times you will earn enough points to unlock all the other characters. 12 out of the 17 characters are simply the retro versions from previous titles and they maintain the same abilities that they had on those games too. I think playing with retro characters was a really cool feature, but I would like to see all characters having the “modern approach” too. For example you can unlock the retro versions of Max, Skate, Shiva and Dr. Zan but you can’t play the modern versions of them.When comes to bosses, I can’t say I like them very much, really. There is one or two I find it pretty fun (like Nora or Shiva) but most of them are a bit plain and/or just frustrating. As I previously said, the white shield ability that Bosses have can get really annoying, especially in some bosses in particular like The Commissioner or Barbon because they can hit you very fast and are immune to your attacks.It’s pretty great that developers made a Story mode and an Arcade mode. Arcade mode was the only way to play the old titles (you had to go through the entire game without losing all your lives. Losing would mean starting from the very beginning!) but with Story Mode you can now have a more relaxing time playing the game and if you lose you only have to start again from the last stage. There’s also the Battle mode (it’s a PvP mode) and the Boss Rush mode. The Battle mode is super fun! You can have up to 4 players playing all against each other!In  you can have up to 4 players playing through the various modes! When I played through steam remote play there was no lag issues whatsoever and it was a very fluid and overall great experience! However, playing via “Online Game” things weren’t so smooth as it was somewhat laggy.The soundtrack of this game was a bit of a hit or miss for me. It doesn’t have those memorable tunes like the old games had but they aren’t bad. A very cool feature incorporated in this game was the fact that you can always toggle to the retro soundtrack from previous games anytime you want.All in all, I think Streets of Rage 4 is an above average game and a nice treat to all fans of the Saga. These are part of my childhood memories and that’s why I feel very fortune to see this game coming to life and I hope to see another Streets of Rage game in the near future! However, I would like to see some improvements, especially on the gameplay department, I know that this game could be much more polished and still has room for improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of salt from so many. But as far as tribute-style games go, SoR4 is pretty darn good. If you're the type of fanboy who creams in their pants over Call of Duty releases, this might not be for you.If you're one of those hipster dingleberries that play retro games for cool points, it also might not be for you.And that's fine. A game like this can't please everyone.This is a sequel/homage/love letter to the previous games, and the overall style of these kind of Final Fight-esque beat 'em ups. It has many of the same flaws and merits of them - which is what I think the developers were going for.If you enjoyed the originals. Or were fans of similar beat 'em up games like: X-men, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Final Fight, Alien vs. Predator, Double Dragon, Spider-man & Venom : Separation Anxiety, Battletoads, The Punisher, Captain Commando, Golden Axe, and Knights of the Round - you may very well enjoy this game. It's not perfect, but neither are the games I listed above. They have mechanics that can allow you to cheese it, and there are enemies that have moves that can cheese you. That was just the nature of the beast back in the quarter-munching machine days. I do think that the game does need some form of dash (not necessarily a run) just to be able to close distances to ranged attackers. And it might've been a nice touch to have options in the game to toggle on/off features that make the game play like the originals, but also allow for it to have added features like dashes, rolls, and/or blocks for those that wanted them from other games in the series. That's what I would've done. It would've allowed a broader audience to play the game a bit more like how they might want to play it.I also think that the game could've been longer. I do wonder if there'll be any DLC.I think my main complaints would be price point, and the unlockables. Why in the name of Buddha, Allah, or Zeus would I want to play a 16-bit pixelated version of a character from of a previous game's roster? With all the talent and effort put into what looks to be hand-drawn art, why didn't they just do a similar style "upgrade" to the various iterations to fit the tone of the new style? It's jarring to look at the highly-detailed graphics, and see a pixely figure wandering around in them.The price, at just shy of $30 (Canadian), seems a touch too steep for the experience. If this were around $20-25, given the lackluster unlocks and with what seems like no DLC coming,  I'd suggest waiting for a sale.So many reviewers are squealing about how disappointed they are because they were ultra-mega-over-hyped. And all I can say to that, is this:"Learn to manage your expectations".PROS:-Great presentation and updated graphical style.-Gameplay in-line with classic Beat-em-ups.CONS:-Price point.-Unlockables are mediocre.-No options to tailor gameplay to match prior versions in the Franchise.Score: 6/10Not amazing, but a very solid retro-styled beat-em up clearly made by people who enjoyed the originals. Just a few small bumps in terms of options and extra content.

_childDocuments_.review: An uneven but very worthy sequel.  With the new DLC and its moves customization, this game now boasts more playable characters than even the lovingly assembled Fan Remake.  Granted I wish it adopted more of its approaches like updating every character with every installments' mechanics including dashing.  Still the visuals ooze style, the music is generally catchy, the characters have satisfying moves, and most enemies are fun to take down.There's an unlockable level select, old fashioned arcade mode, and the DLC's survival mode so you can get whatever dose of bashed skulls you want that day.  On paper it should be the perfect installment.  Unfortunately some enemies are a little too cheap with their priority and armor, where the game expects you to more frequently use special moves with the new, risky life recovery mechanic.  Except every enemy's timing is different, the training mode skips to the next lesson as soon as you succeed, and none of it will help you against certain bosses who refuse to be staggered.  If there's a non-brute force solution I still haven't found it.  There are gimmicks here that could have used more thought or at least been explained.The game's biggest weakness is somehow the writing.  Yes, I'm complaining about the plot in a beat 'em up--maybe it's more accurate to call it the tone.  It leans further into sci-fi wackiness than 3 did, and that one had a mob boss turn into a Terminator and brain in a jar controlling a flying anime robot.  By itself that wouldn't be a dealbreaker, because bombastic Sega logic has its charm.  But the cutscenes between every level draw attention to how silly it all is while being too serious or quiet to be fun.**Spoilers from here on.**The new villains are two RWBY teens who'd be fine as regular bosses but aren't convincing as criminal masterminds since their only personality outside acrobatic fighting is throwing tantrums.  I'm not saying Mr. X was a deep or even sensible character, but all he had to be was an intimidating d*uchebag.  Not to mention his successors' names, Mr. & Ms. Y, are distractingly unmenacing.  Their plot to brainwash the city through a music concert is pure Saturday morning cartoon cheese, which is out of place next to the other grittier subplots about police corruption and implied mass deaths caused by a train full of civilians derailed in the middle of a city.The villains expose themselves to the brainwashing speakers while talking so they definitely aren't wearing earplugs, but aren't affected because the writers like to ignore pesky laws of physics.  This is after the heroes fight their way through Chinatown only for the stage boss to tell them he has nothing to do with anything and they should have checked the visible giant building shaped like a Y.  A lot of it's a parody plot with no jokes or self-awareness and would have been perfect handled more like Double Dragon Neon.If I had to guess, the creators came up with the stages first and had to string them together with a story later, which I sympathize with.  Those locales themselves are varied and artistically fantastic.  Still, it's the most obvious missed opportunity since fighting game and beat 'em up characters work a lot better with premises that add personality to them while hyping up the conflict with followable stakes, no matter how absurd.SoR2's ending worked because Adam being kidnapped is established in a dark and ominous intro building up to a last level that shares its memorable track.  The new game has fanservice moments with classic characters, but like the villains and their consequences, they fly in out of nowhere without tension or catharsis and drop out just as abruptly.  Stage 8 ends with a cutscene of a wall silently being punched that affects literally nothing.  Stage 9 drops two odd twists making you fight an evil Max Thunder and revealing the mind control music plot.  Neither of those were built up to, so you just kind of scratch your head wondering why you're fighting evil Max now and of all things the crisis really had to be resolved by fighting a faceless floating laser DJ.  If they just used the previous cutscene to show those were in the game and mattered, reaching them would feel hype instead of awkward.You'll still be happy by the end having smashed through all the escalating, epic set pieces.  But it all could have left a grander impression with a more memorable, hard-hitting story.  Especially now that being attacked by cops is extra relatable.I'm picking a lot at the negatives, but that's because the good parts of the game more than speak for themselves.  You can't create a game like this without genuine passion, and the flaws only stick out because they're so close to being a resounding masterpiece.  Ultimately it's a great game more than worth the price from creators brimming with future potential.

Thing is, if both don't go to the next level, progress is not saved and host needs to restart the entire level again.Next - only two filtering options - type of game & difficulty. Very barebones, to be honest. Have not tried co-op, due to social isolation stuff.2) Content - ok, there are characters from old games, nice to have them, but they really do not fit the game in terms of visuals, even if you set CRT+Retro(pixellation, basically) in game options. And that's it. There's hope for revamped characters from old SoR titles as DLC's, but I'm no fan of DLC's. Game is short, I think shorter than any SoR game. Good for replayability, especially in multiplayer, ESPECIALLY since there is no jump in-out functionality. Makes gameplay sessions clock at ~1h. But for solo player, once you get achievements for beating the game with every character, there's not much to do, besides polishing your skill and tackling higher difficulties. If that's your poison, you may not care about small amount of content.3) Difficulty - I don' mind it, it's old school and I'm old school, but mostly old nowadays :). My main concern is that once you loose, you start over from the begining of the level, which makes me quit the game, do somethin else and return to it at later point in time. I'd give an option for autosaves for every section in a level, but at a penalty - let's say, achievements are locked when those are set.I love the graphics, both backgrounds and characters.I like the difficulty curve (although at times it feels unfair, but, hey, maybe I just suck), I like that all characters have something unique to offer.Music, while not great from the get-go, grew on me. Beat 'em ups were my childhoold and my early teenage years, that is why I give thumbs up and because this is a diamond in the rough. However, I cannot reccommend this game to anyone at its current state at the price tag it has now. Get it at 30%+ discount, if you're a fan of beat 'em ups, get it at 50%+ if you're curious.

_childDocuments_.review: They've ruined the classic franchise for me. I have very fond memories of playing SoR 1-3 and they to this day are still very good games. This game however took the series into a bad direction.Where to start? First you can't run in this game. I remember SoR3's Skate being able to zip through the levels and doge all of the enemies. In this game I played as Axel and Floyd and it became extremely difficult to doge any enemy attack. Maybe the other characters can run but I didn't even bother to try because I was just so bummed about the gameplay mechanics they've changed.Second, the special move is no longer based on a cool down but rather a recoverable health meter. If you use a special move, you lose HP temporarily until you hit some enemies to gain it back. If you get hurt in this process, you lose that HP for good. This is a bad mechanic as SoR3's mechanic is much more addictive. It feels great to have a free move that recharges as opposed to a risky move that you may or may not lose HP. More often then not, you lose the HP because of some BS move the enemy does.Third, you have plenty of buttons on the controller but they decided that "yeah, let's reuse the same button for throwing a weapon as for picking up a food item". So sometimes you might be reaching for a turkey only to throw away a long reach weapon you had in your hand. WTF? Just assign a new button for pick up and a new button for throwing weapons. This makes absolutely no sense and adds to the already frustrating game.Fourth, I'm the type of person that can't stand to switch to easy mode or to add handicap to the game. But by the end of the game (to which I gotten so far without any "assist" items), the BS final dual boss (triple if you count the fight before) was extremely frustrating to fight against. At that point, I just selected max assist on the retry because I was ready to give up on this game.This is an unfortunate sequel that should have never been made. It's more frustrating than fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Streets of Rage 4

_childDocuments_.review: It's no surprise most veterans of the series don't like this game.  If you're a fan of the original games then you most likely know what made them so special.  SOR4 can be fun but it's critical failure is the enemy AI.SOR is no Final Fight, it was far better.  It wasn't an arcade game designed to suck your money.  It was brilliantly designed, your characters had all the tools to deal with whatever the game threw at you.  Example:SOR2 - The characters were slow, methodical and dealt great damage.  Likewise the enemies were slow, less likely to swarm you and at times just stood there.  Yes, they were dumb as rocks but a perfect marriage with your character's abilities.SOR3 - The gameplay was faster, rolling and running was introduced and as a result the enemy AI was cranked up in response.  Again a perfect marriage of AI and your abilities. SOR4 - SOR2 character abilities and SOR3 enemies in one game.  And this is the problem.What made the original games legendary is ultimate playability. Even on a sliver of life you always felt like you had a fighting chance.  Not so in SOR4, death is one 3/4 screen flying knee away.  Or a random charging headbutt from off screen.  Or a quick punch from a Galsia that just spawned a second into the game. Or consistent usage of wakeup abilities of a downed enemy.But here's the thing...if you had the TOOLS to deal with this then the fault is on you.  Rolling and running would have been a great help against SOR4's aggressive enemies but as it is the tools available to are insufficient when dealing with the constant spamming of enemy abilities, super armour and much faster movement.  Again the key to SOR was the perfect marriage of your abilities vs your enemy.SOR was NEVER cheap even on the harder difficulties.  This is called great game design and it's apparent the developers dont understand this.  There's a reason why other prolific beat em ups like Final Fight is forgotten yet 30 years later people still want more SOR.As it is SOR4 is a good knock off of a SOR game.  The critical element the developers got wrong is the enemy AI.  That said you might enjoy this game more if you've never grew up with the original games.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. This is a flaming uppercut of nostalgia! I remember back in the 90s playing Streets of Rage with my friends on Sega Genesis all the time. It was our go to game next to Mortal Kombat. Whoever led the team on this project obviously was a fan of the game as a kid as well because everything about this feels right. The hand drawn graphics and art are awesome. The old school characters retain their exact same move sets. The new music fits the Streets series (though I quickly checked the option to play the old soundtrack... what a throwback!). The game isn't long, but it can be challenging at times. Once you learn each enemies move set and counters you won't have that hard of a time throughout. Some of the bosses can be rather challenging. The two sisters fight and the final boss fight got me a number of times before I could get em. The new fighter additions are nice, and they feel like they belong. Cherry Blossom is basically a replacement for Skate from the older games. Big cyborg guy obviously is supposed to be a replacement for Max. For those of you who say "but, there is no block button" as I have read in a few reviews. There is, it's your defensive special move... you are invincible during it so use it when you are about to get hit and it acts as your block. Staying true to the old games, using your specials sacrifices a chunk of health, but you do have a chance to get it back by stringing together attacks without being hit afterwards. Once you get the hang of it you should be able to dodge most attacks.Technically the game is flawless. No crashes, perfect frames, no glitches whatsoever. Very polished. The game is NOT very long, and to obtain some of the unlockable items is a bit of a grind. It's neat that you can unlock the old pixelated original fighters with their original animations and sounds. My only issue is online play. I don't have anyone to play with locally so I thought I'd try out the online play. There are not very many games being played unfortunately (at least not many showing up in my playlist) and the few that I was able to get into were extremely laggy to the point of unplayable. This is unfortunate because it could breathe a bit more longevity to the play time. Once you have gotten to about 5 hours you have done everything and have a handle on every character. Now it's just about beating high-scores and unlocking everything. For old school fans of a series this is an absolute must have... you will feel 20 years younger when playing it and is worth the full asking price. For newcomers I might wait for a sale, it's still a great game though, albeit a tad short for $25.
_childDocuments_.name: Streets of Rage 4

_childDocuments_.review: Great graphics, cool new characters, decent combat, horribly cheap computer opponents. _childDocuments_.review: Streets of rage 2 was one of my all time favorite games for the Sega genesis and having a return of one of the best beatem up games ever made is like a return to my childhood. Streets of Rage 4 is not just a piece of nostalgia either but a good game in its own right with colorful graphics, decent music and challenging game play. Its been a while since I've had this much fun playing a game. My only gripe would be that the original streets of rage games had multiple endings depending upon the level of difficulty adding to the replayability of the games but this one is sadly lacking that. You get some replay factor in unlocking new characters, increasing the difficulty level, arcade mode and boss rush but its difficult to keep the same levels that you beat on a lower difficulty level fresh when you challenge them on the harder difficulties. Sill a great game that I recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a game made by people who genuinely understood and loved Streets of Rage, particularly the second game.It refines SoR's basic moveset to a shine and adds an absolutely ingenious risk/reward system for special moves (allowing you to regain health sacrificed for specials by hitting enemies with normal attacks) which perfectly compliments the aggressive new combo system and scoring mechanics. It doesn't let down on beat em up fundamentals either, this games spacing, footsies, and crowd control easily hangs with the best of the genre's 90's output.There's a lot of content too, so even casual fans of beat em ups who aren't planning on going for 1cc's or S-Ranks will find something to dig into here. There's really something for everyone and I can't recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This is just the side scrolling beat 'em up that I was looking for! The old school mechanics with modern anime-like graphics and just enough new fun commands. I also appreciate the different properties of the characters and the compelling single-player modes, but it's the online co-op gives you the ultimate SOR4 experience!Massive respect for allowing you to display the PlayStation buttons instead of the X-Box ones, and even to set what types of foods you'd like to appear during the game to recharge your health. Now that for a vegan like me is a truly thoughtful add ;) Enjoy this instant classic, guys!PROS:+ Retro core identity with a modern touch.+ Intuitive gameplay and tutorials.+ Nice and varied selection of characters.+ Unlockable features.+ Different game modes with insane difficulty levels for the bravest ones.+ Great overall design.+ It's an online co-op side scrolling beat 'em up, come on!+The best game available within this genre.NEUTRAL:~ Great soundtrack, but it used to be better.CONS:- The highest difficulty level may feel absurdly hard.- Given the genre, it'll feel short.- Some playable characters are way more effective than others. Little balance.FINAL SCORE: 8 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of side-scrolling beat 'em ups, and I'm also old enough to have played the first 2 Streets of Rage when they were first published. I sadly considered the genre basically dead nowadays: too repetitive, and its mechanics too basic to appeal to modern gamers. Boy, was I wrong. Combat system in SoR4 is deceptively simple: only 4 buttons and a few basic attacks. And yet, every time you play, you find out a new sly trick to prolong combos, juggling enemies against a wall or keeping them in the air longer than you did before. There's also the classic final fight-like special moves, but with a brilliant addition: energy lost this way can be recovered by hitting enemies (and without being hit). This adds a very interesting tactical layer.Characters looks very different and FEEL very different when played (personally i just love Cherry and her guitar).What can I say, this game surpassed every expectations I had, and demonstrated that beat 'em ups still have something to give.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Streets of Rage in the 90s, you'll love this, and if you weren't born in the 90s, you'll still probably love it. It has the classic gameplay of the original series (although with some tweaks and extra features such as having two 'levels' of super move) with an updated, sharp graphic style, as well as some fun unlockable features and characters. It's even entertaining when you join an online game and play with strangers, which is something I don't usually do. It's longer than the original games, although some levels are surprisingly brief. It's stable too; it hasn't crashed once while I've been playing and I didn't ever lose my online connection. I would highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Streets of Rage 4

_childDocuments_.review: Streets of Rage is one of my favorite beat 'em up series. Streets of Rage 4 is a great comeback for the franchise that captures the elements that made the classic games great. The animation is very fluid and has a sort of "comic book in motion" style to it that looks awesome. You can choose from 4 characters at the outset, including old favorites Axel and Blaze. As you progress through the game, you can unlock more characters from past entries in the series for a total roster of 12. The gameplay is on par with the rest of the series. You have your punches, jump kicks, specials, and throws. Just about everything you'd want gameplay-wise from a Streets of Rage title is present. A few of the bosses attacks feel a little cheap at times, but the difficulty is pretty fair for the most part. There's plenty of food throughout stages to keep you going. I played on normal, so it may be less on harder difficulties. One thing I would have liked to see is a dash feature, though.The music is good, but in my opinion not as memorable as the old games. It's by no means bad, it just felt more hit or miss than the past titles. I wasn't able to test out multiplayer at the time of writing this, so unfortunately I cannot comment. As always, these types of games are more fun to play with a friend.Overall, this is a solid return for Streets of Rage and it's definitely worth a playthrough for long-time fans and newcomers alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Streets of Rage 4

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played Streets of Rage before. But I do enjoy Beat'em up style games so when I saw this, I grabbed it immediately. And boy am I pleased. This game is very addictive. Love the graphics, score and the characters. Game is small and simple with 12 stages. It gets hard but not impossible. Has lots of replay value.That being said there are problems with the games mainly with the villains. Some villains are way too powerful and versatile in their attacks while giving the heroes very little ability to defend against some of those attacks. I am hoping these issues will be addressed in a future patch.I would rate it 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Streets of Rage 4

_childDocuments_.review: What a great beat-em-up game and callback to the days of Sega Genesis! I always loved Streets of Rage 2 the most out of the 3 original games but this one def takes the cake. It adds all that I loved about the old games to a whole slew of new things. Great artwork, really good music that def pays homage to the amazing tracks from Yuzo Koshiro in SOR2 with some new stuff by him as well. better still, you can switch between a retro and modern version of all the music on the fly. Good variety in the feel of the characters, to include the retro versions playing like they did in those games too. Just a great experience overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Streets of Rage 4

_childDocuments_.review: Wouldn't recommend to players unfamiliar with the Streets of Rage series. Beatable but very annoying enemy/boss design. Instant hyper armor, groups of tough enemies with weapons & projectiles, bosses that dance around you at lightning speed to evade your normals. You have no run or dash, and your only invincibility is from special attacks that consume health (which you can restore by attacking enemies), supers (which you only get from item pickups), and your throw animation.Any of these elements would be fine on their own, but with your limited movement speed and defensive options it turns levels into a chore of hit-and-run and praying that multiple enemies don't gang up on you with armored attacks. Especially in the final level, there are certain waves of enemies with tracking, armored attacks that can ONLY be interrupted with your super, leading to unavoidable damage if you want to save it for the boss.Also no mid-level checkpoints, no training room to practice combos, no difficulty selection for Boss Rush mode. Series veterans are probably used to things like this, but for newcomers learning the game it'll feel very tedious and punishing.
_childDocuments_.name: Streets of Rage 4

_childDocuments_.review: Streets of Rage 4 does not stray far from the staple of its brand. The gameplay is, in fact, repetitive to say the least. However, the game is also built to be a party game, with versus, online and local cooperative play up to 4 players. These additions make the game more enjoyable bar none. In reference to gameplay, controls are tight. The contrast in movement, combos and evasive maneuvers amoungst the characters was refreshing. They did not play like clone sprites. I did wish for more combos and moves. Maybe they will release extras with time. More skilled gamers will definitely have to play this game on Hard because it's really a childish game. On hard, i found myself sweating and starting over repetitively, which was satisfying. The game is completely illustrated by hand and the work is spectacular. Streets of Rage 4 is an excellent buy for artists and art lovers. Streets of Rage 4 has great potential replay value as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Streets of Rage 4

_childDocuments_.review: ☑ Content quality is a value at full price.☑ Content quantity is a value at full price.☑ Positive experienceHas it really been  already since the SoR3 / Bare Knuckle 3 ?Streets of Rage 4 snapped me right back to the 1990's, there is an immediate reaction to buying and playing this game for the first time; you have a great big smile plastered all over your face! Immediate nostalgia flashes across your brain and chest, this could be the early nineties all over again and the golden age of console gaming is neatly picked up from that time period and brought to modern day hardware.. Streets of Rage 4 has invoked a vividly fond memory of good times gaming in years long past.As soon as I've launched the game i played it till the very end with my GF (and that's something for a beat'em up game to keep the girl interested in), it was a very satisfying experience.Everything is back, and it's nostalgic as hell. Smashing cars, breaking mailboxes, picking up pipes, eating basted turkeys, and laying some sweet co-op smackdown on street thugs. (Now with online co-op!) The graphics are stylized and sharp, with smooth animations. Controls are responsive and tight.Whether you played way back when, or are new to the series, don't hesitate, dive in with a buddy and kick some @ss!....but the bonus? RETRO MODE with graphics straight out of the '90's! and SOUNDTRACK too!Great soundtrack and gameplay!Re-playability is quite high considering i've played the story three times before writing this review!A must-have purchase for long-time Street of Rage veterans and newcomers alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Streets of Rage 4

_childDocuments_.review: Played all three SORs, played the unofficial remake, and finished SOR4 at highest difficulty with all SOR4 characters.The Goods:- Its a new SOR since 1994, and it looks great. If youve ever played through SOR and wished for 1080p at 60fps with a shiny gloss of paint. This one checks out in spades.- Gameplay has not changed much, and that's a major plus. In a world where regenerating health, infinite lives, and rpg elements are almost standard ticks on a checklist, its nonexistence here is very gratifying- The game is very replayable. Its only 2 hours long to finish, but games like this extends its shelf life by making you come back for more. And with the multiple characters, you'll not be stuck playing the same 4 characters over and over.- Difficulty is balanced for the most part. Its not as difficult as it was in SOR2, and nowhere near as difficult as the remake at highest difficulty. In other words, its just right.- If you want to vent some steam and punch guys into other guys. This is the game for you. Not since SOR3 has a brawler been so cathartic.- Score multiples means you're rewarded by playing well. A major plus in a brawler.- Online multiplayer means you're not stuck with your kid brother whos sole motivation is to trigger you into playing SOR4 in real life with him.- Didn't think it was possible. But the game's soundtrack is awesome, even rivaling its great predecessor.The Bads:- Enemy having armor is one gameplay change that I think is just bad design in a brawler. Some situations traps you into areas where there's no chance of escape because of armor. Feels really cheap at times, and one of the bosses go so far as to have armor so often it almost feel like robbery.- Lack of variety in enemy design. Every enemy is a biped humanoid, and when your game has less enemy variety than a 1992 game, that's a baffling deficiency. Also, why no ninjas and samurais and yet have a Chinatown level that's just begging for it.- Retro soundtrack choices for the levels are...well...bad.The Ugly:- No run, no roll for all but 1 SOR4 character, who can't roll either. Why? SOR3 had it, and it was great. Why not SOR4?- No different attacks when using weapons. Its stab, swing or throw. Considering that SOR3 had different animations and types of attack depending on whos handling the weapon (Axel with katana, Blaze with daggers, etc.) why is the game having less stuff than its 20 year old predecessor?- No Victy/Roo. He makes a cameo, but not as a playable character? That's a missed opportunity. Hopefully it gets addressed in a later DLC.So is it worth it? I played through 20 hrs in a game where the average time of completion is 2 hrs. And I feel like I've just started. So yeah. Worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing first impression.Graphics are decent, and the lighting effects in particular are a nice touch. As a long-time SOR fan, the combat felt familiar and satisfying.But the game's best feature - co op - is crippled by terrible, stuttery performance despite the FPS counter reading 60 constantly. The removal of the run/roll feature also results in some challenging enemies or hazards simply being cheap - you should never be in a position where you punch an exploding barrel and have insufficient time to get away from it, but because Axel can't run, this happened almost every time I tried to use one.I'm seriously considering refunding unless the co op performance is addressed promptly. If this happens I'll adjust my recommendation.EDIT:I decided to not refund it and give the single player an honest try. Having played through the game solo, I can say that it is a largely fun throwback, and if you've got four friends living with you, local 4 player would be a blast. A lot of the new weapons are fun to use, and I found the mid-air grab a ton of fun to counter those flask throwers in particular and use them against them and other hapless foes.That said, it hasn't changed my mind about the cheapness of many of the enemies due to a lack of mobility. I feel that everyone should be able to run. The balance comes from different running speeds and I don't see why the decision was made to leave it out. I also miss the old teamwork maneuvers, I was sad to see they didn't return.On the whole I enjoyed the single player. If that or local co op is what you want, then it's not a bad buy. But the online co op needs to be improved. It's hard enough without having choppy motion making it harder to track enemy movement. I can't recommend it until the online co op is a smoother experience.2nd Edit: The online connectivity issues I experienced initially have been fixed. A lot of the cheapness from enemies and their armour frames is countered with practice. You have to readjust your mindset from the classic approach, and take advantage of wall bounces and combo opportunities, counter their cheapness with cheapness of your own.I still (and always will) think that every character should be able to run. But following the release of the DLC, the unlockable moves, extra characters and survival mode, I have to change my recommendation despite the no running.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Good game on its own merits; heavily inspired by the classic games, but at the same time quite different from them.Let's set expectations straight: If you are looking for an exact replica of SoR 1/2/3 gameplay; SoR 4 is not that. Go play those classic games, or go play the fan-made SoR Remake.SoR 4 is inspired by those classic games, but has completely new mechanics. There is more emphasis on combos and hitting opponents in the air or hitting them after they are knocked down. At first, it doesn't feel like SoR 1/2/3, and that's because it is not. Instead, it is SoR 4, its own unique game.What you get is a very good beat'em up game with new-but-familiar controls, hand-drawn sprites and backgrounds, dynamic light effects, and a brand-new soundtrack that dynamically transitions from one track to the other in sync with the gameplay. It's a strong game on its own merits.And it's also a game that builds on nostalgia. The new controls are good, but if you'd rather keep it like the classic games, you have this option. The new soundtrack is good, but you get the option to listen to the retro soundtrack. The new characters are also good and play very different from each other, but you also unlock the classic SoR 1/2/3 characters. The new story mode has each stage as a checkpoint (that even resets the number of lives), but you also have the option of playing an arcade mode with zero checkpoints.Are you a fan of beat'em up games? Then you will like SoR 4.Are you a fan of classic SoR, and you are willing to accept a new take on the franchise? Then you can enjoy the new formula of SoR 4.Is it frustrating? Sometimes it can be. With those opponents with a shield; or those that block your attacks and counter them; or when there are a few grenades exploding in sequence, combo-ing hits on your characters. Yeah, that can be difficult or frustrating. But that can also be seen as a challenge, as something that requires more tactics than just mindlessly going on full-attack. I don't completely like those moments, but I'm not sure if I would remove them (could make the game too boring); and for sure the classic games also had some annoying moments that are now shadowed by nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: This game really is a great big homage to the first 3 Streets of Rage games from the 90s, play them (or at least check out some gameplay of them) before giving this title a look, they’re great games and easily accessible these days on Steam and various other platforms.Pros- Just like old times. The gameplay in SOR 4 feels just like the originals from the 90s and that’s amazing, there’s no fancy blocking manoeuvrers or anything like that, you run forward and beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of all the thugs you see with wanton abandon using all the moves at your disposal, there’s a few innovations here and there but this is classic Streets of Rage through and through, OG fans will love it.- Combo meter. Get told exactly how many hits you’re dishing out and earn bonus points for pulling off long chains of attacks in succession, the addition of the combo meter is a simple but really nice way of incentivising fast paced aggressive play.- Unlockable characters. Unlike the old SOR games where your high score was just for bragging rights, in 4 the points you get contribute to a progress bar which unlocks retro versions of the protagonists at certain milestones, these retro characters look and play just how they did in the original 3 Streets of Rage games, allowing for some unique playstyles and a nice bit of nostalgia, a great incentive for repeat playthroughs.- Gorgeous art style. Seeing all the old 16 bit pixelated SOR protagonists and enemies lovingly recreated in a crisp new cartoon visual theme is amazing, there’s a lot of detail all round, especially in the environments.- Iconic soundtrack. As per usual for Streets of Rage. The game has a ton of really memorable tracks to pump you up for beating up thugs, spanning across a range of genres and keeping with the experimental dance music style of the old games. Cons- No sprinting. Unless you’re playing as the SOR3 retro characters or SOR4’s Cherry you’re not allowed to sprint, this creates a small loss of mobility compared to SOR3 where all characters could sprint and can make chasing after some of the faster moving bosses a bit tedious, it’s not a big deal but personally I didn’t see any benefit from its removal.- Arcade Mode not unlocked at the start. Before you unlock Arcade Mode where you have a set of lives that carries over throughout the whole game and a single continue, you’re forced to beat the campaign first, where your score and lives reset at the start of each stage and losing all your lives just means restarting the level, both modes are fine, but I’d prefer to decide which one I want to play from the beginning rather than having one gated behind another.- Only unlockable characters are retro variants. Besides , who you unlock mid way through the story, every other unlockable character is a retro protagonist from the older SOR games, it would’ve been interesting to unlock more SOR4 characters to play throughout the story, maybe more defeated bosses like .- Retro Soundtrack is disappointing. I was impressed when I first saw that the game gives you an option to toggle that replaces the SOR4 soundtrack with retro music from the old games, but the retro tracks the devs picked out mostly don’t even fit their stages and some of them sound outright awful, the only songs that were used for this retro selection were tunes from SOR2 and horribly compressed tracks from the Game Gear version of SOR1, very confusing decision there, could’ve done with some of the music from Mega Drive SOR1 and 3.Streets of Rage 4 is a really well made and enjoyable game and a heartfelt love letter to the classic beat em ups of the 90s, like its predecessors and the Final Fight franchise, as someone who played the original Streets of Rage Mega Drive games as a kid then got hooked back into the series by the amazing Streets of Rage Remake fan game for PC as a teen, this is the ultimate nostalgia trip for me as an adult, it manages to be faithful to the original trilogy while making its own advances too as a proper sequel, a must play any SOR or beat em up genre fan!
_childDocuments_.name: Streets of Rage 4

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing sequel and game to show that modern beat-em ups can not only be fun for older fans, but have so much potential for modern innovations and deep gameplay to keep you coming back to delve deep into each character. Artistically this game is fantastic as well. Animations are smooth and have enough weight to each of them that make faster characters feel frenetic, along with heftier characters to absolutely be able to pummel everyone with great visual additions to screenshake and ground effects. From backgrounds to lighting, to expressions and little bits of food on the ground you for some reason eat out of trash cans, it oozes style. Music wise it's a treat as well with each stage having a complete bop with varying styles to fit each stage or area. None of them overstay their welcome, and none repeat unless it's for Boss music as far as I can tell. The main draw is the combat however. Each character has their own style, specials, OTG's, dash or run (or lack-thereof), air abilities/combos as well. While at first I felt some were really basic and uninteresting compared to the rest (and especially DLC characters), taking each of them into training mode for a few hours really shows their potential for EVERY character. Learning their timings, abilities and combos combined with air/wall bounces and number of OTG's to get the most of your potential will take you hours for each character to master. Depending on the enemy as well they will have different properties and intertia to adapt to on top of that so you can't just do the same combo on everyone. It really feels like I'm trying to learn some Street Fighter or Marvel based stuff. My only issues are the lack of certain control options. Blitz attacks being tied -> -> □ instead of being able to map it to another button is just a little frustrating mid combo. A lack of a grab button or option to map it to one also makes certain scenario's annoying when dodging as I can go from dodging to just hugging an opponent with no escape. A lack of being able to map a button purely for charging up also is annoying when I have to time certain things, especially when Special is mapped to ▲ / Y. I could understand why all of these are the way they are, but I feel like for smoothness of combat and potential within players would be heightened a lot if I could just remap or tie certain actions to a button. Certain reliance on Super Armor for bosses or certain enemies is a *little* frustrating too, but I suppose that's just learning quirks and timings for everyone as well. DLC Cranks everything great up to 11 however. 3 New characters and new side mode with random upgrades/bonuses for each round completed. On top of that, each character gets a new move that is swappable to their arsenal. Specials, Blitz, Forward Specials, and Supers all get variations. Even MORE Possibilities in training, with mixing and matching. Each new character in my opinion is just even more cracked than the last and just gets more and more fun. From the huge OTG potential and police brutality with Estel, to the air-juggling and combos of Shiva, to what feels like I'm playing UMVC3 Haggar with Max, it's just too fun to describe how good this DLC is. There is one major issue with the DLC: Why in the hell can I only unlock the alternate moves in the Survival mode? You could have easily let us unlock them in campaign since you already have a scoring system built into that, or even make it Rank specific if you wanted players to go for great ranks. Survival is fun, sure, but it can just be repetitive climbing up to the more combo-worthy enemies. Besides the very small issues, this game screams fun and even more potential with future installments. That is an amazing feeling to know this could have more down the road when it's already THIS good.   The 100% for this game is overall not bad, it ranges from finishing the game with each main character (Only 1 per game required for Retro characters), clearing the game with 1 credit, to S-Ranking every stage with 1 character on Hard or Higher. None of this is really that difficult, and a few will take an attempt or two. But it's mostly manageable. A big problem however: Why are All Stages Clear achievements only SINGLE PLAYER? In a co-op focused beat'em up? This also doesn't make sense when co-op makes it harder and adds more enemies to balance it out. So even if you wanna grind with a friend for funsies, you still need to play through the campaign again with that character in SP to get the achievement. Bruh.The next real nightmare (no pun intended) starts with Mr. X's Nightmare DLC achievements. You must unlock EVERY alternate move with EVERY character. Main and retro. Co-op at this point is heavily recommended as you get XP for each character played while in survival, so if you play Shiva and your friend plays Cherry, you'll get XP/Moves for both, as will your partner. Even with a friend or two that will take hours of Survival grind. Each character is fun of course, but especially when you get to the more simplistic characters it starts to drag with the upgrades being very limited in what they can do. It's not hard per-se, but it is pretty time consuming for a beat-em up. Instead of making me want to learn characters, it made me just want to rush through the campaigns on Easy since I wouldn't get the achievements anyway if I wanted to play and learn with a friend for campaign runs.
