_childDocuments_.review: Streets of Rage 4 is a game that makes great first impressions, horrible second impressions, and has some incredible staying power if you stick to it long enough. I hated it during my first playthrough, and after that started loving it more and more. Let me explain with some examples.There's an enemy in the game, a fat bloke that runs at you while spewing fire. He tracks you really well if you're far enough, you can't jump over him and he has hyper armor, so you can’t stop his attack if he starts the animation. He was so frustrating the first time through. "How the hell am I supposed to dodge that?" I though. You can't dodge in this game, or run up or down the screen, this attack feels so cheap!The thing is, you're not supposed to dodge that attack. When he starts running, you are being punished for a mistake you made a few seconds ago. If you stick to him, or make sure you're always above/below him, he's harmless. It's the same story with most enemies. A bald guy keeps randomly uppercutting me in the air! Yes, he’s designed to punish jump attacks. But he's the only enemy to do that, you just must remember never to jump at him. A girl in a mohawk has this jump kick, that’s really had to dodge! But she’s also completely powerless up close, so just get to her as fast as possible. And so goes for every enemy. If you know all their skills and behaviors, the game becomes this tense puzzle of positioning, resource management and timing. But it takes a lot of learning to get to that place. And it makes for a bad couch co-op, where one person has very little experience in the game. But, if those caveats don't discourage you, there's a fantastic game underneath. Just so you know, the process of getting to the actual fun can be very frustrating. I almost gave up on the game -b ut I'm glad I didn't. I'm pretty sure it will be a mainstay on my pc, and I will be returning to it for many years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I loved all the other SOR games, and had a blast playing them with friends. This new one just has so many flaws that make it unenjoyable. I'll start off with a few positives:*The game looks great. I love the style of graphics, and effects.*Very impressed with the amount of characters in the game.*Speaking of characters, I do like that everyone has their own flavor and move set.*The move set, combos are a pretty cool addition. Juggling around an enemy is pretty fun.Now for the negatives:*I'm sure you've heard it before, but the super armor that EVERY enemy gets is a huge problem. Any enemy that is in this state is completely uninterruptible. The biggest problem with this is that they use it ALL THE TIME. Meaning you'll either have to avoid it, or take or hit. The bigger problem with this is the rating system. You stop hitting things. The combo goes away, and your rating plummets.*Your special moves CAN be interrupted. *Not every character gets to run. Only one character (that I know of) can run. Running would have been a HUGE help in dealing with some of the more annoying enemies (biker women).*No 4-player online. Can't ask for everything I guess.*Given the right time and place. You can be juggled until half your life is gone.*They've made some of the most useless enemies from the original 3 games, into the most annoying enemies in the game.*I wanted to play this for fun. I only find frustration.Like I said, I wanted to like this game. I wanted to give it a positive review, but the issues with the game just give me a headache. I expected fun nostalgia. I got frustration and annoyance.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game. Game play is simple to pick up but difficult to master. The characters all play their own distinctive way. The music is spectacular, my favorite tracks are police precinct, airplane, y tower, and art gallery. Includes unlockables and hidden things to discover. There's no artificial progress like pointless "leveling up" that so many games like to shoe horn in these days. The progression here is simply from you getting better at the game, taking on harder challenges like difficulty settings. There are multiple difficulties to build your skills with adjustments that go beyond simply adding HP/Offense to enemies turning them into damage sponges that murder in 2 hits; the AI gets better too. There are also other ways to increase difficultly too like the different game modes and pursuing higher scores. When you start to get it and you develop your skills it feels so bad ass to pull off crazy combos. You get online and local multiplayer. (although admittedly there are not many online games available this late in the game's life cycle.)There is nothing about this game that isn't perfect for what it is trying to be and is one of the most complete games you will find today. Even all of the gushing I have heaped upon this game still doesn't feel like it adequately expresses just how much I have loved this game. I don't care what kind of games you like, this is worth a look, and if you like beat em ups at all or have played them in the past this is an essential must play.  ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game.

LOVE the new characters, especially Cherry, she pogos all the punks and edgelords like a drunk at a Ramones gig.My very favourite thing though is that you get caught between a cop/punk war at the start, and both sides attack each other (as well as your character). _childDocuments_.review: Overall, this has to be an upvote. It's the classic mechanics from Streets of Rage I-III, with graphics lovingly bought into the modern age, while doing the franchise proud in terms by reworking old characters, enemies and even stages to some degree. In that respect this is in every way the modern-retro nostalgia fix you're looking for. What kinda sucks, is that after the first 6 stages or so seemingly having been carefully planned, prepared and polished - the game then suddenly starts to lack pace, with short easy-to-win stages, until you beat the game on a final boss that feels extraordinarily easy itself compared to many of the earlier ones. You'll also find the SOR1 retro characters are almost unbeatable once unlocked, allowing you to cake-walk the entire game without much effort.I truly was expecting a much longer game, but with awesome graphics, low system requirements, remote play, and a really addictive well-written soundtrack - it's a thorough recommendation nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: I think Streets of Rage 4 intially targeted a younger crowd with its clean, hip palette, but also exotic styles that appeal to certain woke, overrepresented demographics. The soundtrack is also pretty generic in tone and composition. They let Koshiro make a few tracks, but then It's like they held a Eurovision contest for the rest. Artistically, this is a seriously divergent sequel.There seemed to be a lot of complaints about Axel looking like a fat hobo (among other things). I was initially in that crowd. In retrospect, I think they didn't intend for him to look as ugly as he does. They simply messed up his anatomy a bit and made it worse by dressing him like a derelict-edition teen from the 90s. The design is borderline Rob Liefeld ugly. If you really look at Blaze, she actually came out worse in many of the art pieces  in-game sprites. In the distinct Rob Liefeld fashion (lol), her spine and pelvis are mangled into a near "S" contortion, and her neck and shoulders are just nebulously floating several inches back from where they should be. WHY!?Though I silently cringed at Streets of Rage 4's art, I learned to appreciate the fresh gameplay it has brought to the scene! The combat has a mix of high notes from many of Capcom's fighters as well as past beat em ups like Fight N' Rage.At its core, this is obviously Streets of Rage, but the gameplay is easily ahead of virtually all others in the genre. Even hack and slashers like Shadow Over Mystara could use some of what Rage 4 be flexin'. The action is so intense and complex at times, it's intoxicating! With cooperation from even just one more player, it reaches an even higher plateau! The combat's combination of features is simply impeccable! It's not all sugar-free Monster and pineapple pizza, though. There are a number of enemies with utterly no precedence for the abilties they have, nor the stubborn shoehorning that lets them use and abuse these abilities. On release, these problems were all over the place and were just !The biggest downside was and still is the content. The campaign is average, at best. Its main antagonists are two generic anime types with accompanying anime art, and it stands out in a very bad way. The boy is a stereotypical villain who's personality consists of even more stereotypical maniacal laughing. The girl is a stereotypical uppity, super serious villain. They simply do the campaign no favors. There's also very few good set pieces that are on par with the past games.If you don't like the campaign, you can at least challenge yourself and go for straight S ranks on Mania. I couldn't be bothered. Again, the action is great, but it's not good enough to overcome the campaign's overall dull composition. To a point, the same could be said of Survival mode because sometimes the traps are absurd; taking up to 80% of the fighting space! It can also take up to 30 minutes for the real fun to start. By that point, your power curve may already be way above anything the game can throw at you! Getting a fun seed is basically RNG.Fortunately, the answer to the above is a resounding YES!!! The latest (perhaps the last) patch added another Survival environment that is completely customizable. RNG elements?  if you so desire! Imbalanced player and enemy scaling?  upon your whim!Survival easily holds some the best moments I've ever experienced in gaming, especially co-op! Honestly, I think even that's underselling the sweet symphony that is Streets of Rage 4's bombastic, explosive brawling! What's more in v8 is all characters were given at least several major, positive revisions. Infinites were targeted down once again, but that's not strictly a bad thing. Characters like Estel can finally play as something other than spammy, strafing screen hogs!If you've been on the fence with this sequel, last call! It's not going to get any better! Seriously, go buy it and the DLC, git gud with a character, then experience the sheer badassitude of the best beat em up brawling of all bloody time!

_childDocuments_.review: It is fantastic.Beat em up for modern age.Graphics are crisp and clean, soundtrack is awesome, but what sets this game apart from other modern beat em ups I tried - is the feeling of input. Controls are tight, and every punch you deliver _feels_ like you're playing those 90ies beat em ups (Double Dragon, Final Fight, SoR 1).The moveset is richer than those old games, but it is incorporated into very standard moveset seamlessly.Don't even think, just buy it.Edited part:I am adding this just because its been quite few more hours I've been playing, and am in the skill tier where I'm trying to get S-ranking in top difficulty.If you reach this phase, you'll start noticing how the game is evil in some ways, and it'll probably cripple your enjoyment. For sure it crippled mine, since I can't enjoy longer playsessions now, due frustration.Few examples:- some enemies simply have longer range and if you approach them off the line - their attacks have priority AND longer off-the-line range. When you try to hit - you'll hit the air, but enemy will land a hit on you.- enemies will queue up to attack you literally when your invincibility frames stop, or during a longer animation recovery when you can't recover. This leads to attack tactics consisting of cheesing with 1-2 hits, and spamming AoE special to protect your back- enemies are faster than you, and will literally run away from you to wreck your combo - or run in position to hit you while you're locked in a hit animation. Without higher combo counts, it is impossible to nail that S ratingIn addition, not all characters are equally easy to play. Adam by _far_ outweighs almost everyone else, due to his long range specials and ability to dodge, and solid combos. Axel, my favorite, has snail-pace moving speed, and his attack animations are so long, you're as good as dead meat if you attempt anything above simple punches.It is _still_ a great, great game. I am just sad that at higher levels, as you start clearing stages on Hardest without losing a single life, or even without being hit - it becomes an exercise in frustration, rather than joy of feeling how your skill level increased. There won't be any "clever" combos to chain. You'll just play so safe, its boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Streets of Rage 4 is a good but not great Beat em Up that is worth the price if you enjoy replaying games like this, especially with friends/strangers in person/online. However, I need to address the "cheap moves" and "no run/dodge" comments I see from so many negative reviews. Cheap moves are absolutely meant to be countered and can be done so in a few different ways, depending on the situation. There's no such thing as an "unbeatable section" especially on Easy/Normal difficulty. The reason these enemies challenge you in specific ways is to teach you the core game mechanics, primarily using your Defensive Special as a reactionary block/counter.Also, there most certainly are sprinting and dodges, they're just not universal for every character. Diversity is largely achieved through mobility which is balanced with power on a sliding scale: More power, less mobility and vice-versa. Cherry can sprint and Adam can dash by double tapping left/right. Skate can sprint (also dodge up/down) and Shiva can dash by double tapping. Also, every character can jump (different height based on mobility) which can dodge most "ground based" attacks.Someone can always point to "what more" a game like this could've done given that it's relatively short in length, but not appreciate what it did do well. Graphics and level designs are all well done. Enemies are diverse with a decent handful of bosses. Soundtrack is fine and has a retro variant as well. Characters provide enough depth and replayability to make this purchase worth it. However, I wouldn't pay much more than the asking price (buy on sale) and it is not worth buying if you're going to play through it once and never touch it again.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games with a lot of wasted potential, and a very disappointing multiplayer. However I still fully recommend it if you're going to play single player or couch co-op.A few examples of what I mean:- Multiplayer isn't "drop in drop out" like it ought to be. You can't start playing and let people join in progress, you have to queue for a partner and then start the game together. If either person leaves the game ends. This basically kills MP.- It launched on GOG without MP at all (I assume because they used MP provided by Steam and the consoles and GOG doesn't provide that) so be careful if you get it there.- My games all felt pretty laggy. I had noticeable input lag if I wasn't the host, and there was frame stuttering most of the time too. Just feels like the MP was an afterthought kinda.No official modding. This game could have benefited from easier modding on PC. Easy palette swaps, model swaps, gameplay changes, etc would have helped with longevity. There are a few mods for the game, but nothing substantial.There is no post-launch content. Why is there no post-launch content??? (Keep in mind, I mean "expansion pack" type content, not "cash shop" microtransactions.)- Two of the bosses in particular would have made *excellent* additions to the playable roster and you'd think since they already have a bunch of animation work done for these characters it would be a reasonable amount of work to make them playable.The worst crime of all, however, is the ending credits music on Classic Soundtrack is not the SoR2 Ending Theme! >:(Finally, the time it takes to unlock all the characters is a bit long, particularly if you are plugging away at higher difficulties where you fail a lot. You aren't awarded XP until you complete the level (which is fine), so it kind of encourages you to just spam lower difficulty runs if you want to unlock the retro characters. I feel like there is probably a better way to do unlocks than this.But it's not all bad. If those things don't bother you, here are some pros- Solid port, great performance, decent options- Input options (though not made obvious) let you switch between Nintendo and Xbox controller layouts (A/B and X/Y position swaps) just by changing your button prompt style to Nintendo. Really nice if you're using something like an 8bitDo snes-style controller, or a Wiii U Pro Controller or something.- The option to use classic (three button) controls- The option to use the new or the old soundtrack(s) and you can swap it any time, even mid-stage- Stage Select, several difficulties- Great art style. It grew on me very quickly.- Fun characters. Both the returning and the new cast are good fun to play.- Good level design (for the most part). There are a couple places (Stage 7) that will leave you scratching your head, but by and large it's good.- Good boss fights (for the most part). Again some fights are better than others, but for the most part the bosses are memorable.- The retro roster! Being able to play the characters from the older games exactly as they were is great.- Retro boss fights. It's an easter egg, but there are a bunch of retro bosses you can fight throughout the game.- No monetary ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. No microtransactions at all. It's a very self contained "here's the price and you get everything the game has to offer" kind of deal. - Solid replayability. You can go through the game multiple times with a single character as you progress through the difficulties, or you can replay it with the different characters on the roster (and the game rewards you for doing that). You can also replay levels for higher scores, easter eggs you missed, and so on.As long as you're content to play it single player or couch co-op, the game is well worth it. If you were hoping for a great multiplayer experience this probably isn't for you.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; I've been playing Streets of Rage since the days of the Genesis / Megadrive and I will say this much... DotEmu, Lizard Cube and Guard Crush have come together to make a game truly worthy of the Streets of Rage title. This game is perfect and is not only a 10 / 10 but it's my personal Game of The Year.By blending classic arcade beat em up and fighting game mechanics, they've created an experience that (in my humble opinion) elevates the beat em up genre as a whole. Combat is easy to pick up, while also being a challenge and a joy to master. Combos are simple enough to pull off, but holding them to reap the extra points is where the deep challenge lies. Enemies are challenging but for the most part fair, and any time I lose a life or drop combos, its self induced.The art direction is flawless. The comic book style artwork feels right at home and is a welcome change to the series from the pixel art of previous entries. Playable characters and enemies alike are highly detailed and animated smoothly. You can tell a lot of love went into the art and animation.Olivier Deriviere took on a massive challenge in creating this games OST and he nailed it. The OST truly embodies the spirit of SOR by including the most popular EDM sub genres from the years surrounding release (2020). From start to finish it feels like a DJ set including original tracks of his own and boss tracks created by true legends of the industry including Yoko Shimomura, Motohiro Kawashima, and of course Yuzo Koshiro (hearing the title theme by Yuzo is pure nostalgia).On a technical level the Guard Crush engine serves up the entire experience without dropping a single frame (with the exception of online). The Guard Crush engine is truly impressive and I'm hoping to hear more about it in the future (seriously guys, licence this engine, it's perfect for beat em ups!).If you are a fan of Streets of Rage buy this game.If you are a fan of good beat em ups, buy this game.If you are a fan of arcade style games with great music and art direction, buy this game!If you are a SEGA fan thirsty for more SEGA IP, buy this game!!!Thank you DotEmu, Lizardcube and Guard Crush for making this game, and thank you SEGA for allowing them to make it. I'm looking forward to the DLC whenever it drops. Until this I'll be doing my best to maintain order on... *Edited 11/30 for minor punctuation.

_childDocuments_.review: Streets of Rage 4 is a great beat ‘em up and a quality example of the genre.I’ve thoroughly enjoyed it so far and find it easy to go back into it because it IS just simple, good fun. That is ultimately all you need to know about this game. Go ahead and buy it, if you’re after a tight old school style beat ‘em up.However, my further thoughts as a long time series fan are that it is not the game that I imagined the long awaited continuation of the SoR series to be. I feel a degree of disappointment as a result.The previous games were a product of their time: 90s games that looked and felt the way they did, as a result of the time they were made. The series still strived to impart a sense of intensity and did its best to seem bleak. Nothing reflected that more than the aggressive boss themes and the solemn intro themes respectively.SoR4 tends to look and feel more like an homage to the series as well as an overall pastiche to the 90s, sadly scrubbing some of the tone set in the earlier games.The game itself leans heavily into SoR2 for its foundations, only adding a few new touches (Cancels, juggling) to make the game a bit more fluid. This is one of the key reasons why it feels decidedly old school, yet refined and smooth to play. Very straightforward and satisfying.The new art direction certainly looks good and gives the game style and appeal to potential newcomers but overall, the vibrancy, and somewhat comic book/Street Fighter style seem to me to be far removed from what the original series went for and makes it feel a little disconnected to earlier games.Very importantly for me, the soundtrack whilst suitably stylish and well produced, lacks some of the hooks and edginess of the originals - especially SoR2. It seems to suffer from being both too layered, and yet muted. This despite series veterans Yuzo Koshiro and Motohiro Kawashima contributions. It all just feels like ‘just’ background music.Ultimately, I feel that SoR4 is a fitting and correct way to continue the series in the modern day. But for fans of the original, the disconnect that this newer game has between it and the older titles can make it hard to feel that this isn’t anymore than a homage both to its legacy, and as a rose tinted throwback to the 90s.As I opened on, this is a fun, refined example of a beat ‘em up with good replayability and accessibility. But for old timers, you might be left wondering a little cold.

_childDocuments_.review: Streets of Rage 4hmmmm....Okay so the game basically does not acknowledge that SoR3 exists apart from a few cameos. The music from 3 is not in the game and there is no vertical dashing (rolling) or running for most of the SoR4 cast (apart from cherry who is the new skate). My fave game in the series is the original because I like to score chase and this game has that. With the combos you do and how many star moves (invincible) clear moves you have at the end of a level increases your score. You health also plays a big part of it too and it is nice they have thought of this feature, it also has a scoreboard for each stage.Game ModesStory (get 2 lives every stage)Arcade (5 lives through out but you get more 1cc only)Boss Rush (boss rush)Versus (up to four players)The enemy is very sneaky and will hit you out of combos breaking them and not giving any reward. Its a risk reward mechanic in learning when to drop combos. Smashing the Rising Upper and the like will also get you caught out. What is different from SoR3 is instead of a free Heavy when you charge it up, you can regain your health which is in green after hitting the enemy. But if you get punched again you lose the green bar and it is sad times. Use these heavy moves wisely and you can get some sick combos there is also juggling in the game now but you have to work for them.I love mechanics in games, brawlers are also my fave genre. So the fact that Guard Crush made a good engine with decent A.I really makes me happy. It isn't like any other SoR game because its been a long time since the last one. Things have moved on a bit since the Megadrive.I have two complaints1: Dot Emu is famous for having terrible net code when playing with people, it still sucks.2: The music is a little too clean for the series. It does not have that thumping farty megadrive base that the other games do. I guess its why they added the soundtrack to SoR1 and 2 in the game. Not sure why they left out three? I know its not every ones cup of tea but its my cup damn it let me fill it with whatever I want!?!This game is a modern brawling classic and there are not many to go around. The Takeover and Streets of Fury EX?If your unsure wait for a sale but its worth a play if your a brawler fan.Thanks for reading <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game plays well and looks awesome, proving that despite of the simplicity, these games can look cool. It handles an action paced game very decently for the right amount of time, and it makes you feel you're back on the couch playing in front of your PC (if you're from my generation at least)The gameplay mechanics are rather simple. Maybe too simple. This emulates exactly the way these old platform games used to be, but nowadays there are many examples of these kind of games, where they went beyond it's origins, and added a lot of new mechanics. Despite that, the gameplay feels fluent, responsive and enjoyable, with simple controls that will have you enjoying the journey rather than too focused on complex controls. It feels nice though and the variety of foes and some times challenging waves of several enemies, will have you on your toes, at least if you play solo. Despite being simple, each NPC has a different approach to beat them easily, pushing you to adapt to each enemy type, so that you don't just smash the buttons. And the boss mechanics add some more spice to it.This looks very nice, on a cartoonish style of course. We should judge each thing for what it is though, and this game aims to this kind of graphics, and it nails it at it's best. The character designs are gorgeous and the streets of SoR 4 are so full of details that it makes them look awesome. They have even put hard work on each NPC design, making the game look excellent overall. Performance is pristine of course, I wouldn't expect any less from a game like this though. Any less would be a fiasco.Well, the story is fun. Period. It's enjoyable as much as you enjoy a low budget movie with a silly argument whose only intention is to be a parody and state of the art. Of course it's innocent, of course it's simple and dumb, but it's on purpose and that's the magic of it. Chuck Norris films are popcorn movies and they're still great! You have a villain, you have your over-stereotype heroes. And you need... nothing... else... You can simply sit and enjoy the action.This game is a short, fast paced and enjoyable action beat-em up in all it's spirit. The price is rather fair for the game you get and for a casual game this is a super fun one to play. You even have multiplayer and coop options that I haven't explored yet. And I believe the game even has an online multiplayer option (please check the facts on this). I think this is a well polished game and I totally recommend it. I'd say my rate for this one is a 9 (out of 10) considering it's a platform old school game. I love having a few of these games on my library, and this one was an excellent choice.CPU: Intel i7 6700 3.4 GHzRAM: 16 Gb - DDR 4 (2400 Mhz)Graphics Card: Msi NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 Super - 8 Gb GDDR6Hard Drive: SSD 500 Gb Wd Blue M2 2280

_childDocuments_.review: Streets of Rage 4 opens with a very simple question: how do you revive a franchise there's been no release for in over 25 years?DotEmu came with the answer, alright: "Let's take everything people loved about the series, let's take the same graphical style we had for Wonder Boy and keep the core mechanics largely the same as back then with a couple of additions."Streets of Rage 4 is an up to 4 player, 2d old-school style brawler, with a pumping soundtrack and enough special moves and other little nuances (Classic soundtracks, classic character iterations) to keep interest more than piqued. It was not just game of the year in my eyes, but also of my family who haven't really played anything since Streets of Rage 2 back in the day. They had a swell time with it as well and all it's sheer goofiness. Played more on the Xbox One and Switch.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the original SOR,  I was impressed when I saw the SOR4 demo videos. Many elements that made SOR great are missing and lots of tweaks would have to be made so the game could feel like and be enjoyable like the good old SOR. I would love to see a SOR 4.1 update, with a big list of improvements and extensions based on the input from fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still not crazy about the art style (same with WBIII and will probably never get used to it. But the game is a very solid best em up and worthy of the Streets of Rage name.All the characters, moves, and regular enemies feel excellent. I remember watching a making of video how the sor4 team made it so that once the enemies are on screen they can't be knocked out of it or try and "hide" off screen and do something cheap. Stuff like that, very cool. But, if only a few things were... different, this game would absolutely knock it out of the park. Unlocking stuff is great and keeps us playing. But here it's done in kind of a meh way. Get enough points to unlock a sor1, sor2, sor3 character. Ok, thanks? Seems like it should've been there from the start. It would've been so much better to unlock different things besides characters. The second and third things are more drastic to me. I found most of the music to be hugely disappointing. Yuzo is here, but I think he only did the main theme, character select screen and a single boss track. Most of the stage levels, (you know, the ones you'll be listening to all the time) are done by someone else and most of the tracks just don't do anything for me at all.Third thing is that after you knock a boss down, they will blink white and recover with invincibility. That, and many bosses have quick jumps all over the place, so many times it's just getting your slow character (which has zero of these moves btw), feel more like a cat and mouse game. Every boss will call in backup at their 50% mark. They also will pause the entire screen to show them "powering up" or something to do more cheap special moves, which hurt the flow. All this stuff really annoys me after a short while. I wish they would ease it up with a patch. Third thing is options- or lack thereof. You can enable retro soundtrack but it just recycles music from the other games. I was hoping there would be Genesis versions of the new music. Nope. Same thing with sound effects. No options to use the sor1, 2 or 3 sound effects which is a huge shame because sor2 sound effects are SO satisfying. The new ones don't even come close. There's also lots of difficulty selections which is great, but there's mania and mania+ but no very easy. Just easy, normal, hard, etc. Even on easy the CPU will do all the cheap stuff I mentioned before. But oddly enough there's options to change the food pickups to many different items...ugh, I mean really guys? That's what you included??? C'mon...I know it may look like I'm bashing the game but it's just a number of things that get irritating after a while. Don't get me wrong, if you played the crap out of sor2 like I did you'll most likely have a great time with this one. But sor2 still stands as the best beatemup to me.

_childDocuments_.review: To say the older streets of rage games are important to me is an understatement, these are games I played at a very young age and really helped me get into gaming as a whole alongside sonic and mortal kombat. To say I was worried about this 4th game was also an understatement, the art initially was very unappealing mostly because I was afraid of change.Thankfully my worries had been unfounded and all anxiety of this being a terrible followup quickly melted away when I played the game. If I wasn't so nostalgic for the older streets of rage games I'd say this was easily the best but I can safely say this is one of the deepest and most rewarding beat em ups ever made and is worthy of the streets of rage name. You have a massive selection of chracters thanks to the inclusion of mostly all playable fighters from every streets of rage, you have a fantastic variety of stages, plenty of extra modes, great dlc which adds a rogue-like survival mode with unlockable moves, colour pallets, online play and it's all topped off with a fantastic ost. But this would mean nothing if the game didn't play well but thankfully it does. Let's talk presentation first and whilst I didn't like the art style at first it's safe to say I love it now, stages are detailed and look seedy and grim but also are filled with easter eggs and call backs, characters look great with detailed facial expressions and special moves look fantastic. Combat is the star of the show of course and it's fantastic. You juggle enemies with an impressive assortment of attacks and special moves, utilising the walls to keep enemies in the air long after they've lost all their health for that fat highscore. All the playable chracters are incredible and feel vastly different to play as, even the old school SoR 1-3 chracters feel different enough despite lacking the newer tools their SoR 4 counterparts have. I do have some nitpicks, my SoR nostalgia is quite strong so whilst I adore this game I still have a couple of issues that I want to list out: - not all characters made the cut. Whilst DLC mostly fixed this I'm still upset we didn't get a SoR4 version of skate and we still missed out on SoR3 versions of Dr Zan and roo (we don't talk about ash.)- the villains look like they'd have tiktok accounts - the ost whilst absolutely incredible, especially the dlc offerings, didn't hit me in my feels as much as SoR2's ost did. It's definitely a 10/10 ost but the opening to SoR2 is still unbeatable.And really that's all the negatives I can think of.To be blunt this is simply the best beat em up ever made, a worthy successor to the orginal games and certainly a game that's quickly become one of my favourites. An absolute must play title.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Half baked' sums this game up entirely I'd say. Just buy River City Girls instead. There are nowhere near enough options in the gameplay. Only one character can sprint. There are no parries, there is no block button, there is mandatory friendly fire enabled, the music 'sounds' like Streets of Rage in a loose sense but lacks personality and memorable songs, the art is nice but cutscene presentation is abysmal due to minimal sound effects and no voice acting. Dialogue is displayed with plain white subtitles instead of even attempting to utilize its comic book aesthetic in a way similar to other classic Sega beat em up Comix Zone. There were a lot of good ideas and unquestionably good intentions put into Streets of Rage 4, but its stubborn refusal to actually commit to those good ideas and give us the look, sound and feel that a king of a forgotten genre deserves is extremely disappointing. The new additions to gameplay are largely great, have the confidence to embrace that and truly innovate instead of going off half ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Especially if you've got classic versions of the characters in the game anyway. It's okay to make those versions play like the classic characters, but make the present characters have much needed quality of life changes. Design choices aside, the experience is also hindered by extremely frequent frame rate dips.

Just missed the mark for me. Refunded.

_childDocuments_.review: You pick up the controller, select a character, and proceed to wallop bad guys. You look up at the clock and realise that two hours have passed by in the blink of an eye. Streets of Rage 4 is an incredibly addictive beat-em-up that understands what made the original games great, while introducing some modern flavours to keep things fresh.Every character's playstyle is slightly different and serves an archetype. Want a fast moving fighter with high mobility? Pick Cherry. Want to perform flashy OTG combo hits while screaming special attacks in Japanese? Blaze is for you. Or do you want someone who strikes like Shinya Hashimoto and delivers suplexes like Kurt Angle? Pick the pro wrestler Max (once you unlock him). Or if you just want a solid all-rounder who gets the job done, select Axel or Adam.Many familiar enemies return with the same old tricks, but there are plenty of newer and deadlier opponents that take time to get used to. By the late stages, you start to see dirty enemy combinations, such as grenadiers at the backline protected by riot-policemen wielding shields at the front. SOR4 is the most challenging game of the series, but the difficulty curve is fair. You will get better once you get used to your moveset and the enemy's attack patterns. And there are plenty of new tools to help you: Tasers are a prominent new weapon that stuns enemies temporarily. Enemy projectiles such as shurikens and grenades can be grabbed out of the air if you are fast enough, and tossed back at the sender. Every character now has an air special, making it easy to juggle airborne enemies for extra damage. When you lose all your lives, you can retry the level with additional extra lives (at the cost of a lower score).SOR4's netcode is solid for co-op play, and this is the ideal way to play the harder difficulties. Unfortunately, the old tag-team attacks from the previous games are gone.A small indie studio has accomplished what was previously thought impossible, and something that Sega themselves were reluctant to do: Create a worthy, official sequel to the Streets of Rage series. It took 25 long years, but it was well worth the wait.

_childDocuments_.review: As a die-hard SoR2 fan, I'm honestly on the fence about giving this an overall positive or negative review.I've played SoR 1 & 3 as well, and SoR4 feels like a remake. They introduced a couple new characters, and brought some old enemies back which really gives that nostalgic feel.Negatives:Gameplay-wise, it can get frustrating at times because your character (unless you're Cherry/Skate) feels like it's constantly chasing enemies around as they back-step or circle you before hitting you...not to mention enemy's invincibility flashes that are beyond annoying (I'm looking at YOU Commissioner) and also some enemies have a longer reach to hit you than you do them (Donovan). And don't get me started on Knife Galsia's hit box...Positives w/ suggestion for developers:Annoyances aside, I still enjoy playing SoR4. I just feel it could have been better, and it definitely could be with updates (please no paid-for DLC). ***Suggestion:***I LOVE that it gives you the option to include retro music from previous SoR games...but make them applicable to the level & situation!!! Example: Stage 2's Retro music is the boss music from SoR2...the entire level. Why not make that the boss music because that's what I remember it being tied to? Stage 3's music was perfect as that was the same music for the submarine level in SoR2. Keep it consistent so I don't feel I'm experiencing a constant mind-screw, ya know? =)The design looks great, I love the online multiplayer aspect, the newer characters are fun to play as and the new enemies can be challenging. There's a lot of replay-ability just like in previous SoR games, and I love the throwbacks/Easter Eggs. I just want to see this live up the hype.Would I recommend paying $25 for this? No.$10-$15? Yes.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I saw the announcement for SoR4, I was overly exited for it's release (which was still a while off), since I grew up with mainly SoR 1&2 on Mega Drive and Master Sytem. Now that I finished the Story and messed around a bit with the characters and modes, I'm left with very mixed feelings.Visually, the game looks very good and somewhat true to the original. The graphics remind me of comic book art, without being cell-shaded, all I can say is, that it works really well. Animations are fairly fluid, and little touches (like some leftover fire on the ground after a 'grand upper') show that a lot of work has been put into this part of the game.The soundtrack also sounds really good. Sure, it doesn't have the impact as the original games had back in the 90's, but it's solid none the less, with some songs reminding me of the original. Same goes for the effects, some appear to come straight from the original games... a nice touch!There's an option to play the original soundtrack over the game. Sadly someone just pasted the wrong songs on the levels/sections. Stage 2 started with the boss music from SoR2, with the boss itself having some other random track from the originals (and it's like this for the entire game) HOW DIDN'T ANYONE NOTICED THIS!!!Sadly this brings me to the gameplay, which was enjoyable at first, but frustrating halfway through the game. The movesets of the characters are very good, and well thought out. It's fun to string together combo's, and building up your hit counter for bonus points is a welcome addition to the series.Ennemies however are cheap. Jumping attacks (even a grand upper on a Big Ben's belly flop doesn't do anything) are nearly impossible to counter, grabs can't be countered with your defensive special (like in SoR2), ennemies can 'teleport' over to grab to deliver instant damage (black uniform policemen), some ennemy actions can't be cancelled (throwing something at a fire breather etc...),...Axel seems to suffer a lot from this, his combo's, moves and specials are fairly long, which keeps him open for a cheap jump attack or an attack from behind. I can't imagine how these things weren't noticed during playtesting the game...Bossfights also feel fairly underwhelming due to the large HP tanks of the bosses themselves.It's this last part that I'll remember in the future when thinking back about the game. Not the art, not the soundtrack, not the nostalgia... only the cheap frustrating mess which was the combat...As a fan of the original, I'd score this game a 7/10, however, if you never played these games before, it's probably more close to a 6... I still recommend this game, but I sincerely hope that the combat issues and the retro ost will get addressed in a future patch...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly as I remember playing Streets of Rage as a kid, but with upgraded graphics.Tips for players unfamiliar to this game or expecting something that this isn't:- You cannot run. Just walk, you'll be fine.- There is no dodge. Just move up and down to avoid attacks. Again, fine.- You do not have to spam attack. I wouldn't, either. Your normal attacks can stun lock enemies, allowing you to chain combos with the attack button or special button.- Art is really attractive- Soundtrack is catchy and funThe game is a solid beat-em-up with a variety of enemies. The bosses are interesting, there are weapons and special abilities to use, and the environment will hide health items (food) or point boosts (typically money). I haven't played Streets of Rage since I was a child on the Sega Genesis. I had no idea this game was coming out until last week, and it was a fantastic surprise. It's a great game. Most of the people complaining seem to be mad that this isn't the same game as one of the earlier entries...which it isn't. This is a new game, and it's a great game. Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked and grew up on Streets of Rage (Bare Knuckle) 1/2/3, you will like this. It's a sequel faithful to the original formula of tweak a bit, keep the good bits, add some new stuff. The artstyle is new yet familiar, and lots of art goodies inside the game itself. Fairly short but very replayable, just like the old games. The replayability is in trying out new characters, as they all play very differently, and finishing the higher difficulties. There are the usual game modes like Versus or Boss Rush if you're into that. Full retro options available if you want to play the old characters (with original sound effects and abilities), and retro soundtracks, though hopefully they put the genesis quality soundtracks in soon (apparently they couldn't get the licenses for those yet).The soundtrack is wicked sick as well. Awesome beats from the original composers as well as series newcomers (but all veterans of the industry, and amazingly talented). The soundtrack joins SoR2's on my favourite game soundtracks list easily.The combo system, which is new compared to past games, is a welcome addition, which alongside improved juggling mechanics allows for some great depth to the combat. The ability to animation cancel into moves gives it complexity approaching an actual fighting game, and allows for some very satisfying coop moments.Fully playable solo or with up to 3 friends, this game has tons of replayability, and is an awesome party/LAN game. Update edit: 74  hours later, I've just 100%ed the game achievements (including a few of my own). Played through the story countless times with all characters, because the gameplay loop is that fun. Worth every penny, and I will be playing this a lot more to come. Hopefully DLCs to come. Playable HD Shiva and Roo please!

_childDocuments_.review: Genesis kids: It's Streets of Rage. Buy it.For Those Who Never Witnessed Sega Doing what Nintendon'ted:Street Chicken!- Beautiful and fluid comic art/animation.- Pumping electric/retro dance sountrack.- Meaty yet straight-forward beat-em-up gameplay.- Character signature moves add replayability.- Various character unlocks and game modes.- Challenging difficulties available.Chicken you find on the street . . .- Short for the price.- Character combo paths the same.- Feels slow compared to modern games in same genre.- Online spotty. Some lag.- Retro characters have less options than default cast.- Some sound effects lack oomph.Recommend To:- All beat-em-up fans.- Anyone interested in gaming's history looking for a faithful recreation of an arcade cabinet designed to swallow quarters.- Musicphiles- Anyone with monied friends who enjoy fun pick-up-and-play games.Alternatively Suggest:- River City Girls (Not as pretty as this game, but more gameplay to sink your teeth into. Also gorgeous soundtrack, but more indie pop vs this game's electric/dance).- Fight N Rage (Also not as pretty, but more technical to control. Has AI partners to help better capture the experience if you drove all your friends away by constantly screaming 90s commercial catchphrases).

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the classic SOR1 a lot when I was younger in my MegaDrive and, years later, SORR.I love them both and now this game too!This sequel does a great job of updating the game to a modern audience:- Art is superb - fluid animation, memorable character design, super detailed backgrounds and all around great color use; it's so good that I don't miss the pixel style of the older titles (although I love it);- Music is good - there are a few good bangers but, as whole, I still prefer the vibe from the older games (more eletronic/techno I think, don't know that much about music);- Gameplay is super solid - great command response, all characters have very different styles of play, the combo system is engaging. I like that you can play arcade (the whole game in a go without saves) or save the game/choose the stage you want to play. The cherry on top is that you can play the classic characters too;- The short story of the game serves it's purpose of introducing the stages and allies/villains - it doesn't stand out, which means it also doesn't fall on its face trying to be something more (I don't think anyone was expecting much of a story anyway, it's just an excuse to beat'em up).There is not much to pick here except the lack of running and rolling options for most characters. Even though I would like to have those options, I don't think that the game is unbalanced without them and I don't think this is something that needs fixing/patching/DLC necessarily.I see myself playing this for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a classic  fan and considering this game, .On the slim chance you've ever played the fan-made game , then you've seen a lot of the "new features" already anyway, as they were ripped directly out of that title without any attribution. These include the survival mode, in-depth gameplay customizations (which this game tacks on but doesn't really use to the same positive effect), network play (which I have never tried as I don't play games online), and being able to "buy" new features or upgrades by grinding parts of the game repeatedly.I found the main story mode pretty difficult at first, but after some practice, the new mechanics clicked a little better (no thanks to the "training" mode which is  as designed). The game doesn't really hold your hand, for better or worse. If you can make it through training mode without wanting to break your game machine, you're doing better than me. I had several whole sections I couldn't complete in training because they were impossible for me to pull off. (I never had these difficulties in the older titles, oddly.)The graphics, sound, and music are all really decent. I didn't care for some of the new graphical UI effects, though, they were disorienting and a bit nauseating at times.What I absolutely  about this new title is that the "new" physics mechanic I noted earlier can largely be boiled down to juggling your enemies. That's the main salient new feature of SoR4. Really! It's just button mashing. High-tech, right?Juggling mechanics are a huge turn-off in fighting games for me, at least in part because I'm physically incapable of performing the necessary combos. When I realized that was basically all that's "new" about  I was left with an incredibly bad taste in my mouth. I haven't picked it up again since, as I've beat the (disappointingly short, incredibly boring) story mode within a day and didn't feel interested in spending any more time on these .

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent revival of one of my favorite series. Overall solid game that gets its SOR elements spot-on.It took elements from SOR2 and 3's gameplay to come up with a brand-new experience with fluid gameplay and smooth animations that make the beat-'em-up even more satisfying.The soundtrack is also spot-on for the series, and similarly to SOR2 and 3, songs change throughout the stage sections. This time, however, the songs bridge into each other during parts of the stage, and I loved that touch.Graphics are beautiful and, again, the fluidity of the gameplay heavily benefits from the smooth animation. It's quick, fun and reactive - as you'd expect from a SOR game.All characters play differently and you'll have to adapt to different ways of tackling the stages/bosses depending on who you pick, which really contributes to this game's replayability. I think their movesets and specializations were well thought and well implemented.And speaking of replayability, this game offers five different difficulty settings, at least three new game modes and online co-op - which really makes a difference when compared to playing through the stages alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, how the ghost of you clings. This is a peerless retro beat-down with enough nods to the early '90s classics to bring a smile to the face of those who punched and kicked their way through the originals and enough bare knuckle action to entertain an entirely new generation.The graphics are slick and the soundtrack is amazing. You can even unlock characters from the original trilogy (ye olde sprites and all) and a suite of the original tunes. The controls are tight and the addition of a risk/reward mechanism whereby you regain health following the execution of special move, by maintaining an unbroken combo, a la Dead Cells, ups the ante and encourages some spectacular showdowns. Online multiplayer seemed a little sparsely populated, but it worked seamlessly and in lieu of getting four of you round a big screen anytime soon it's great fun.I'm only a couple of hours and six levels in, so there's a slim chance things will go south later on, but from what I've seen so far I doubt it. This is clearly a game put together with care and attention and no small measure of love and respect for the franchise. There aren't many games that are an instant buy nowadays, fewer still that are a near instant review. This was one of them. My thumbs are still sore from dishing out a long overdue thrashing to the assorted criminal hordes that infest the streets, boats and sewers of rage that I've walked so far in this game, but I can't wait to get back to it. Great stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Streets of Rage 4

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite awesome for what it is, but I still think "Streets of Rage Remake" done by one guy (Bomberman Games) was superior. This game sports amazing 2D visuals... a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥' soundtrack done very well... but a lot of the design issues I just found more than annoying, and I've been playing the Bare Knuckle / Streets of Rage games since I was 13 back in 1991.  All of them presented a challenge, all were difficult to a point, but this game is often harder than it needs to be in 1-Player Mode for all the wrong reasons.  There's more of a focus on the *Combo Stuff* than just fighting it out.  The whole start every level with 2 lives even if you had 3+ by stage's end is just ridiculous.  Don't get me started about the final FINAL boss battle that's just stupid.  THAT SAID... I Do like the game and would recommend it, it's just not what I thought it would be.  On a scale of 1 - 10 I'd give it a 8.5

Only major issue is that any "video" type scenes can have slowdown, but otherwise runs great.  No sound issues, and my Hori arcade controller works perfectly via USB.Why this weird review?  I'm posting reviews for games that I love that will run on a Raspberry Pi 5.  I may go back and test on other single board computers, like my Orange Pi 5.How?  By using Box64.  It's as easy as installing stock Raspbian (latest is fine), and then installing Pi Apps, which makes it incredibly easy to install Steam and its requirements like Box64.Cheers.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've played in the last decade. It feels and looks crunchy too, you "feel" the impact of your hits when you're fighting imho, and that's what makes it so satisfying to do repeat runs with alternate characters, let alone your favourite.It also has one single DLC, of which is very good adding a sizeable sum of content relative to what this game is and, guess what? No FOMO, no battle passes, no over the top corporate-greed like monetisation.What you get here whether on sale or at full price is a PHENOMENAL game. Just buy it, trust me, if you're into the idea of a beat-em-up you're going to love this.

At the very least remix the end of stage chime.  Thankfully in retro mode the end of stage chime is still there.-Always hated it when games reused bosses, always feels like lazy programming or putting a band aid on getting the game out the door quicker. _childDocuments_.review: After a tiny hiatus of 26 years, SEGA allowed the continuation of their beat'em up series Streets of Rage with the fourth installment. Released this year, published by Dotemu and co-developed by Dotemu, Guard Crush Games and Lizardcube, SoR 4's events take place ten years after the third episode. One could've feared this bunch of developers couldn't live up to the fans' expectations... After hours of playing the game since its release, here's what's good and bad about :SoR fan or not this game is quite entertaining, especially in multiplayer where it further shines. It feels good, it looks good, it plays good, it sounds good... The drawbacks are rather minor compared to what SoR 4 can offer you. _childDocuments_.review: After playing through on Easy for the game, I think I have an idea of what to say.Pros:- The game felt like picking up one of the Streets of Rage games once more when I started to play.- I learned that the risk vs reward was a matter of using up health for special attacks, but then you can get this back with regular attacks. This led to learning too that I could negate some tricky situations by using the special attacks more often, and after a bit of playing and starting another run, it led to brawls that I was ending even faster and more efficiently, and taking less damage so long as I was doing things right.- The references and other things in the game I felt were done right. I had moments of "hey, that guy is here :D" just as I had moments of "hey, that guy is here... >:c"- There's a lot of variety to the characters, even just the four you can play as I found out.- Great soundtrack with 16 bit chiptune option.Cons:- Sometimes I didn't know what kind of inputs I was doing to get certain maneuvers to happen... Doing what I thought did something would regularly result with something else. (Example: I did a dash that positioned me behind the opponent, and I could beat them up from behind. However, trying to do this results in a dash-attack instead, and then when I stop trying I find myself somehow doing the "dash behind and beat up" maneuver rather reliably... but how?- Victy, where are you?- The game feels short... However that's just an observation. Really, it feels like perhaps the right length for a Streets of Rage game.- Story feels... hmm? Well, I mean, the original three from what I remember did have story, just not really cutscenes? It serves to explain the plot but I kinda feel like there's something missing...- Only certain characters can actually dash. I don't know if this was a balancing thing, but I was a bit confused when attempting to and nothing happened, and then would on certain characters.Also, I love the references and throwbacks to the earlier games and potential "jokes" that crop up throughout. Honestly if there was going to be more on the way I would look forward to more, but I'm also content with what is being presented at this current point in time as the game it is. :D

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a veteran of beat'em up's (started with Renegade, Double Dragon and Golden Axe way back), and I find SOR4 to be great looking but stiff and retardedly punishing gameplay wise. It has interesting mechanics, but giving some of them to the enemies as well is a bit stupid. The lack of a mechanic to close in to an enemy that is backpedalling faster than you can walk forward, the enemy's ability to perform their skills on the diagonal at great range (which causes the characters to look like they're floating on purpose to reach you 90% of the time), the enemy hit boxes being narrower than yours, is bad design. On top of that, adding intricate 1v1 fighting game like combos that rarely work because you only have 2 IFRAME skills (a throw and a standing special which are as usefull as tits on a hanar) and almost non-existent combo cancel options makes the game a bit too ambitious.I get it that some like it, but honestly, there are a lot of better old beat'em up games, mechanics and AI wise. The Punisher, Sengoku 3, Karate Blazers, Dungeons and Dragons, Rastan Saga, Hook, Final Fight, Double Dragon 3, Oriental Legend, Vendetta. Even some new ones, like Slaps and Beans.The purpose of a beat'em should be to make you feel powerful, but not that powerful, to be a fast paced fun game in which you kill a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of mooks and still be able to die because you make a mistake. But mooks here are something else... The game feels like it's meant to be played in co-op mode, because for single player it's quite frustrating of how powerful the AI is.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent revival of a SEGA Classic!Pros:- Plays and Feels like the originals (mostly)- Extra goodies to unlock, such as Characters, and Classic (Pixelated) Skins- Excellent Artwork, both Backgrounds and Sprites.- Great Soundtrack- Includes Classic (Genesis) Soundtrack if you prefer.Cons:- If you would have preferred a Pixel Graphic style, then perhaps you won't enjoy the look of this game quite as much as SOR 1 / 2 / 3. I will say that the Pixel Filter is pretty good, but it does not make the game look like the old Genesis titles. It is however, an otherwise excellently implemented Pixel Filter.Conclusions:If you want a 1:1 Copy of the original 3 games, you will probably find things to nitpick about. Otherwise, it follows the spirit of the classics and represents one of the best modern Beat 'em Ups.

_childDocuments_.review: Streets of Rage 4 is a very good beat 'em up, if you like beat 'em ups and that type of thing. No reinventing the wheel here, but what it does, it does well. It's not gonna change the minds of those who find the genre repetitive but fans will find a lot to enjoy. The new combo system works well, giving that risk/reward feel to the fighting, and it's fun catching weapons thrown at you by enemies, then trowing them back. Difficulty wise, once you get the hang of the combo/special system, and figured out a few enemy patterns, it serves up a fair challenge on normal and doesn't feel cheap for the most part. Even Mania didn't seem too bad, although I only tried the first level as Adam, so that could change. Graphics look great, and not at all like a flash game as I had initially feared, and the music is generally top notch too, as it should be, although you'll never get that "OH S%!T" feeling when the Boss music kicks in, sorry; but if you prefer your SoR soundtrack retro, you do have choices here, as the first two games' soundtracks are here if you wish to replace the modern one. Speaking of choices, with this Steam version at least, you can also opt for retro screen filters (scanlines etc) if you wanna go full on old skool, as well as the usual low/med/high/ultra options etc in the video settings (I mention these choices/options as they are all absent from the Xbox Pass version, which is "free" yet somehow not worth it). Online works well, mostly, with only a bit of lag/slowdown/judder, which I'm sure will be patched. It is a shame the 4 player support is only for local coop but who knows, it might get patched also. Controller support is good as you can play natively with either PS4 or Xbox pads, with in-game options for changing the button names to suit each pad, something else you can't do with the XB Pass version (I'm picking on XBP, but the GOG version has similar issues plus no online play, while XBP owners can at least play online with other XBPers, if they can get it to run... I'd avoid both of those platforms at the mo' with regards to this game) Overall this is a somewhat successful return to form for the series, with tight controls, fun, solid gameplay, and loads to unlock. BUT, it does seem like it was developed with pure disdain or at least disregard for SoR3, which I understand as it wasn't great, but Bare Knuckle 3 (the Japanese version of SoR3), is arguably the best in the series (bar the music) not 2. Fight me! This means that a lot of the improvements made there are missing here. So no Special gauge (although this has been replaced when it comes to health depleting specials). And no running! Or dodging! (Cherry can run, like Skate could in SoR2; and Adam can "shuffle" at speed, but everyone could run in SoR3. Have they all forgotten how? I mean some of them are old now but... Maybe some abilities are unlocked? Maybe) Also team attacks are out again too, so no throwing your buddies at bosses (there is a friendly fire option but it's redundant if you can't throw each other in to enemies, so leave it off, unless it's also an unlockable, then I'll be taking a lot of this back!). SoR1 had it, 2 forgot, 3 put it back in and now, here in 4, it's missing again! Also, throwing the "Big Bens" is back from 2 (whereas 1 and 3 you were crushed under their weight).So in summary, with lots to unlock, this is a great beat 'em up based on one of the most popular beat 'em ups of all time, just not on the (arguably) best entry in the Bare Knuckle franchise. That doesn't make it bad though. Obviously.7/10 (add a point or two if Sor2 was your favourite, I guess, or if my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ just need to be unlocked)

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Soundtrack, Hits are crispier than a bag of chips, Awesome Visuals. The evolution of the characters is great with Axel being ragged from all the time he has been fighting because that is what he does, Blaze always looking good with a new leather jacket and older look, Cherry having the best introduction with being the daughter of Adam, Floyd is a little underused but still has a believable backstory being the apprentice of Zan, and the Y twins are a believable and completely silly threat that fits with the story. Ms. Y being calm, collected and smooth with a sword, while Mr. Y being rough, disrespectful and violent with a machine gun to go with it. The gameplay is amazing and is very interesting in the fact that you can create your own combos with the distinct combat system they give you. A great addition to specials is that you can get the health back with you using them being encouraged to try not to get hit and actually use them and not just unbinding the button and using dash attacks. My only gripes are that there are not very good movement options for most of the cast and even the ones that can run feel a little clunky and can get in the way though there is usually a way to dodge certain attacks and battle mode is a little jank with some characters being way better than others at certain things basically making most of the retro characters unplayable because of Blaze. In all, a fantastic game with basically the best mechanics a Beat-em up could achieve.P.S: if you are wondering about the Online. It runs great but there are some bugs and is only 2 player.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Streets of Rage for the Modern Era. Four different characters available from the start, with others being unlocked as you play through the game; if you want to use old favorites (with the ability to run/dodge!) from older titles, you're able to do it.Each character has a different play style with different strengths and weaknesses, however, none of them feel like they're weaker when compared to others. For example, Cherry is the only character with the ability to run, but her damage output and stamina are significantly lower than everyone else. This leads to a hit and run play-style, versus more of a traditional brawler style with Axel or Floyd.Looks great, sounds great, the new combo system is an interesting way to keep any high score chasers invested.Instead of the old special move system from previous games, you now have three types (defensive, offensive, aerial) that temporarily drain your HP bar. Hitting enemies will refill it, making special usage more frequent, but it comes with the risk of getting hit and losing that HP. Instead of using your special move whenever it's "safe" to do so (timer from the old games), you're presented with a series of tactical decisions as you advance through a level. Will you deplete your HP at a particularly difficult section, at the risk of losing it all on the next hit? Or are you confident enough that you'll be able to replenish it without falling into a dangerous situation? How well can you manage your HP between special move usage to keep it at a health level? HP management becomes even more important, as it's a resource that fuels your most useful abilities as well as your primary life line.There's also a limited Super Move system (earned by collection stars) instead of the old Calling For Backup special, with every character getting a unique move with different properties.Story mode is linear without branching paths, but the locations and enemies are varied enough to make up for it. The story is decent for a beat-em up as well, referencing events that occurred within older titles.Online play is available for two players, although four player is restricted to local only. Using Steam Remote Play or a similar option works fine in these instances.If you're a beat em up, this is definitely worth you're time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a game for fans of the genre. If you grew up loving these kinds of games then you should enjoy this too.If I had some (mostly minor) gripes it would be that you can't run (well most can't) so some characters may feel slow and sluggish especially when enemy characters seem to have more mobility. I was hoping for a proper ending rather than just the credits roll. A practice mode should be available to lab combos. (Edit: a training mode has now been added in an update) The netcode needs work too. With that out of the way the game looks beautiful! I wasn't sure about the hand drawn style at first but the final product looks great and animates very fluidly. The initial trailer made everything look so bright and almost like a flash game but the way that the light and shadows interact with the characters through use of shaders makes them integrate seamlessly with the detailed backgrounds in the final release. They also nailed the music in this game IMHO. There are so many tracks that I couldn't help but bump my head to, and considering the legacy that the music had to live up to, it seemed like an impossible task. Now this is obviously subjective and not everyone will like the soundtrack but it felt like they obviously knew how important of a component the music was, and that effort shows. Gameplay feels tight and solid. It has a juggle/combo system that is quite intuitive the more that you play, and feels very satisfying once you can start landing certain combos and catching weapons that an enemy throws at you. It kind of feels like a cross between a beat 'em up and a fighting game. The special move mechanic in this game is interesting in that it will deplete some life when you use one, but if you can manage to attack an enemy after without being hit first you will replenish some life. The more you hit them without being hit, the more you'll replenish so if you're good enough, you can replenish all of your lost life. As expected, the game is even more fun in co-op and this allows up to 4 players simultaneously (2-player online though). There is also a battle mode where you can fight with other players in a fun little distraction. SOR4 is a labour of love that was made by fans. Some may be disappointed but I think most Streets of Rage fans will be pleased that this is the sequel that arrived after all of these years. Rarely will you see a comeback after so long that doesn't tarnish your memories. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: A very pretty game, but also a step back in game design when compared to developments we've since had in the twenty odd something years since the previous installment, while also not doing a good job at being a deliberately retro feeling game.XXXMy initial impression was quite positive. Visual presentation is gorgeous: minimalistic, yet easily readable UI, nicely detailed stage backdrops, a riot of color and motion in character design, some really good lighting effects here and there.Generally good use of enemy lineup and placement in conjunction to stage features to introduce the player to new concepts and add additional spins to enemy encounters. (I say 'generally' here because the start of the last stage is unnecessarily dickish; there are also inconsistencies in which cases enemies take damage from environment hazards same as the player character do and in which they do not, particularly where bosses are concerned.)No branching paths to spice up replay value though. And the stages themselves are short and simple, with some overpadding on boss and elite hp to stretch out the length of the game artificially. Any time there is any significant deviation from an empty rectangle in an encounter room layout, the enemies have no idea what to do with it and get stuck (probably the reason why you see stuff like indestructible tables and colomns only a couple of times during the whole game). I haven't been able to play this game with a buddy yet, but I've seen other people report that there is no difference in enemy encounters and resource distribution between coop and single player. Which is very weird, if true.Music I personally liked maybe a total two themes out of, but it's one of the more subjective kind of things. Less subjective, however, is the retro soundtrack option. Choice of songs is weirdly limited, ill-placed to where they play in stages and even appear to be using inferior versions of the songs.Sound effects do their job well enough, health refill in particular is nicely audible. Hit sounds lack the impact they probably should though. There are frequent vocal quips on often repeated actions for some of the player characters. It doesn't reach the levels of something like Megaman X4, but it is still never a good choice.Control scheme does not use the gamepad buttons effectively (not to mention the possibility of playing on a keyboard, since this is a PC release). With the barebones number of commands the player characters are capable of, you could feasibly place every single input onto a separate button, and still have some space left. The game even already does this, but only for a couple choice things.  There is also some button mashing involved when getting out of enemy grapples; not bad on its own, except for that one grab happy boss, in which case it is overtuned. Wasting the resources of your players' controllers and finger joints on a gameplay 'feature' that could easily be removed from any shade of relevance by simply using an autofire button or a macro is not good.Speaking of 'features', why does this game have a life system? You can restart any given stage you happen to be playing any number of times. Lives also matter only within that single stage, there is no carry over of excess lives if you've managed to save them up, or having to deal with lean times if you made too many mistakes previously. There is no carry over for score either, or any particular use for it, besides giving an extra life every x points. Which, given the tightly controlled pace of fixed score pickups, might as well have been replaced with a 1UP. Or better yet, just multiply the player character health by [insert number of lives here], grant a bonus health layer if certain conditions are met, and get rid of the whole thing. It is completely vestigal.No carry over for the 'bomb' powerup either. And no way to earn it besides getting a fixed drop, of which there are generally few. Not to mention that, compared to a screen clearer or equivalent super power you might expect in a beat em up (or shoot em up) game, it has been nerfed in range in addition to availability, while not getting an improvement of damage, or some other less direct benefit in return. I've read people claiming it works well for extending enemy juggle time, but in that case it should not be pretending to be the 'bomb' and just be a proper special move without requiring a scarecely drip fed ticket that is only given access to at a very specific time, with no influence of how well or poorly the player performs whatsoever.Speaking of special moves, it's not all sunshine and rainbows here as well. They are very pretty and flashy, but they cost health upfront on each use. The player can refund the cost by hitting enemies a few times, but if they take any damage, the remainder of forfeited health is lost, on top of whatever damage the attack has dealt. Yet, unlike some other games you might've seen something like this in, the defensive options the player has access to are more limited.There is no dodge, there is no block or parry of any sort. There is an old castlevania style jump, but it's slow, short and often hardcountered by enemies' anti-air, in addition to being unable to clear the rare landscape obstacle (probably another reason the stage layout tends to be so bare). You could very well end up using your jump button more often as a part of a grab toss move or to recover from being thrown yourself than to actually jump. There are some i-frames during throws, but there are periods of uncontrollable vulnerability before and after to screw you over with.The suggested, both in the help menu, and in gameplay during some early narrow stage sections, way to deal with incoming damage is the neutral special. Problem is, there seems to be this weirdly lengthy deadstick requirement before pressing it, which, if missed, tends to register me doing an offensive special instead, which very much has no i-frames.(Similar issue also happens when trying to pick up a health item while holding a weapon; if I don't stop for a fraction of a second to make sure it registers me standing still, I often end up throwing the weapon instead.) So in addition to taking the attack damage anyway, health is also wasted on the special activation. The cost can quickly add up on any difficulty above the easiest, especially since the player character is also subject to juggling rules and can easily eat more than half of the health bar worth of damage in a second. This is on top of such ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ as hard to judge positioning and hurtboxes along the Y axis, attacks with no telegraph or time to react to, unless you've accurately predicted them before they even started.The only other options left are positioning and spacing. One character can run, and another one can dash, but that's about it. There are no baseline mobility options besides the basic walk. And, of course, they have different walk speeds. And, of course, there is a stinker among them that is both slow and short range enough to have to chase a boss for twenty seconds straight to be able to hit them once, if the AI feels like it. And, what do you know, it is even the default player character choice in the menu.Games like Guilty Gear can afford to have characters with vastly different mobility, movesets, mechanics, etc, because they give everyone a minimal set of different defensive options that offer a baseline protection against undesirable gameplay situations, ideally even the ones the dev team weren't able to predict. This game fails at this task.This is not everything here either. If the game chose to deliberately disregard newer game design developments and go for a retro feel, it'd be one thing. But there is also stuff like enemy attacks with heavy tracking and hitstun resistance frequently used in encounters.
