_childDocuments_.review: The short version: Streets of Rage is back, baby! And it's got a combo/scoring system that's completely terrible, but the gameplay itself is so, so satisfying!Streets of Rage was a trilogy of side-scrolling beat-em-up games by Sega for the Genesis/Mega Drive. Here, a couple decades later, Axel and Blaze reunite, alongside newcomers Cherry and Floyd, to stop the children of the villain from the original games from taking over the world with mind control. It's a fairly barebones plot, and you don't even get an ending beyond the final boss exploding and screaming and falling to their death...but in a game like this, that's all you really need.But Axel and co. haven't been sitting on their laurels between games. SOR4 introduces a free-form combo system and some rudimentary fighting game aspects. (Don't worry, the most complex input is forward, forward + attack.) Now you can juggle, special cancel, and wall bounce the enemy into submission. Since the entirety of the game boils down to "go right, beat up bad guys, repeat", it's nice to have such an involved and satisfying system for said beatings-up. It feels a little more Guardian Heroes than Streets of Rage, but Guardian Heroes was an all-time great, so I'm alright with it.The music is also intensely satisfying. Yuzo Koshiro returns from the original games, alongside a couple more folks, to deliver the same banging house and techno beats you've come to expect. Personally, I don't think anything here dethrones "Go Straight" from SOR2 as my favorite song in the series, but then again, nothing could, and it's a hell of an attempt. The boss themes are a little flat, but the stage music is fantastic, and it even proceeds through multiple "parts" as you proceed through the levels.Speaking of the levels, there aren't a ton of them, though there's at least more than the old games. Locales are fairly varied as you traverse the city, giving some levels additional gimmicks.  Enemies can be bounced off of walls to extend your combos, or thrown into pits or off of buildings for an instant KO. One stage takes place atop a moving train, and forces you to jump occasionally to dodge signs. The real replay value comes from trying the levels again as different characters, seeing how their strengths and weaknesses lend themselves to the given encounters, or not.The city has more problems than just Mr. and Ms. Y, though. The game grades your performance in the various levels. That's always a terrible game design idea, but the real problem is the scoring. High grades require high scores, and high scores require high combos. But it's not the combo count that matters, it's the total damage dealt to enemies during the combo. After every hit you land (including on destructible objects) you have 5 seconds or so to land the next hit, or the combo ends, and your bonus is calculated and awarded. If you're hit while the combo indicator is onscreen, though, it counts as a "Break" and you lose all those extra points. Um, sometimes. The game never actually explains this part, and I can see why: it's utterly indefensible. The scoring system is the most poorly-designed aspect of Streets of Rage 4, easily. Sometimes you do keep your earned points if you're struck during a combo, but that should really be true all the time.Another problem lies in some of the enemies, especially the bosses. In order to keep them from getting overwhelmed too easily by such a combo-friendly system, the game has to let high-ranking enemies tank your attacks without flinching. They're nice enough to flash white in this state, but it happens so often that it slows things way down. There's nothing more obnoxious than using the right move in a situation, only for the boss to tank it and counter. This would happen sometimes in the original trilogy, with no visual indicator, and it sucked there too, but it was a rarer occurrence.The last thing I should at least warn you about is defense. There is no block button. The only ways to avoid damage are to either jump, throw an enemy, or use your neutral special move, and use their invincibility frames to spot-dodge. Well, that, or simply walking out of the way. I am already the sort of gamer to use iframes as my primary form of defense, so this doesn't bother me too much, except for the attacks that can't be spot-dodged or avoided. Floyd suffers greatly here, being big and slow and having a small jump, so there are lots of attacks that are too wide-ranged for him, or their hitboxes linger for too long, or maybe the boss just does another spin kick in a row and maintains their no-flinch status.Aside from those few issues, though, Streets of Rage 4 is a dazzling spectacle that'll hook you right away, especially if you are a returning fan of the originals. SOR veterans may not like every change to the formula, but SOR4 is extremely fun on its own merits. Scoring and grading are fundamentally broken, but they also don't unlock anything beyond a "lifetime score" that'll probably earn you everything after one or two trips through story mode anyway. If you're looking to feel the unbridled joy of punching the light out of a man's eyes a couple hundred times in an hour, you've come to the right game.

_childDocuments_.review: Being raised by the franchise, this long awaited sequel delivers perfectly. While there's plenty of new mechanics that makes it very different from previous entries, is overall a very solid and highly replayable game either solo or co-op. And even though the number of different enemies is kinda scarce, it won't affect the experience in the long run.If anything one very big part of the game to point out is that probably the hardest game in the series. The game introduces a combo system where the higher it gets the more scores and more 1-ups you can obtain in a single stage, by default starting with three lives. On the other hand the specials while still drains life like in SoR2, is recoverable as soon you start hitting enemies. However, if you get hit not only you'll lose the combo count but any potential health you could've healed from your specials, creating overall a game which rewards high risks.While this is overall a new system to learn, I have a few issues with enemy behavior. In stage 2 you get introduced to a boss with a lot of super armor and hard to avoid attacks, and as you progress through this trend begins to increase to some absurd levels where a big group of mobs will ignore your hits as they swipe the floor with your body. This is specially a big problem given a very scarce number of characters has some sort of evasive input, making some very easy to predict attacks require way more timing than it should. Combined with the fact the damage input of both players and enemies is quite high, at the last levels of the game you can easily lose a lot of health in a few minutes.The game is undoubtly a recomendation even if doesn't reach the length of SoR3 or the fanmade Remake. It might need a few tweaks to become a complete masterpiece like some balancing and add more evasive movements to most characters, but overall is a great game that becomes better the more you learn about its mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Well I finally beat the game and I guess it's time to review it!  Well what can I say, it's a very good beat em up with really simple controls and very easy to execute combos.  The hit stuns are long and very satisfying giving you a pretty good amount of time to execute your combos.  Doesn't take you very long to figure out some basic combos.  You have OTGs, wall bounces, ground bounces and a simple number of moves to abuse every single one of them.  It's very satisfying pulling simple elegant combos.  It's not nearly as technical as some other beat em ups like Sengoku 3 or Fight N Rage or even River City Girls, but it's not trying to be technical.  The music is considerably more hit or miss compared to the other Streets of Rage although I think the music is better than 3.  The animations are absolutely gorgeous as is the environments.  The art team did amazing jobs with the graphics.  I love the lighting effects on the sprites such as pipes where they get rim lighting from the environment, it's a very nice touch.  There aren't branching paths, but I really don't think a good beat em up needs them.  The unlockable retro characters and the desire to try out each character is reason enough to replay the game a couple of times.That's not to say there isn't a few issues I've had with the game too.  I'm not a big fan of the enemy types and behaviors as well as their placement.  For a game with such a beautiful and simple combo system, they sure make it hard to pull off fun combos without being stopped by a stray enemy or obstacle.  For example, in beat em ups that have air combos, such as Sengoku 3, Fight n Rage, Alien vs Predators, air combos were a way for you to avoid enemies on the ground while continuing your offense.  They are also a good way to get out of a cluster of enemies.  In Streets of Rage 4, I played as Blaze as my main and what made her stand out is her dragon kick that flies across the air.  While it does a great job carrying enemies a far distance, and offers great mobility, enemies with really quick anti-airs will hit her out of the air almost instantaneously.  Donovan's uppercuts are especially a big problem.  It's no fun having a very beautiful combo going only for it to get ruined by an anti-air that you can't avoid.  Hit and run enemies are also frustrating as you can gather all the enemies into a combo but they'd be the ones to run off and attack you from behind while you are occupied with the rest.  These problems are made worse by the fact that doing intricate combos requires you to use health to do your specials.  Although you can recover your health by doing normal hits on enemies afterwards, it's easy to lose all that health mid combo getting hit by a stray enemy.  This game needs a double tap up or down side step that cancels attack strings.  So you can stop combos when the situation is no longer safe and possibly invincibility during the active frames for Blaze's air super.If I were to put all my favorite beat em ups into a list, I'll put this somewhere just slightly behind Sengoku 3.  They're both quarter munchers except this one doesn't eat quarters just lives... So expect some unfair deaths.  I think the combo system is less intricate and technical than Sengoku 3, but I think this really lives up to what you'd want in a Streets of Rage game.  It's probably the best one in the series in terms of gameplay.  It's nowhere near as hard as the first 3, so I really recommend giving it a go.  Overall, I feel like it lives up to Streets of Rage's reputation and quality, but I also kind of feel like the team is capable of better.  They are definitely capable of pushing the boundaries by implementing more intricate gameplay.TLDR;Pros:-The graphics are pretty stunning to look at-Music for the most part is pretty good but not the best in the series-Moves are simple to perform and combos are easy to catch on to-A really good beat em up for both veterans and newbies to the seriesCons:-Enemy behavior ruins the fun of the combo system-Armored bosses especially a certain one can feel drawn out and boring-Some people might be turned off by the lack of rolls and running

_childDocuments_.review: A contender for the best beat 'em up of all time. It stands toe to toe with the original series in every regard.Gameplay is a logical evolution of the original series; you can can still combo groups of enemies, throw enemies into crowds and watch them all go flying, effortlessly back attack a goon ambushing from behind while beating down his friend. All great stuff. Added features include the ability to catch a weapon that you throw and ricochet off a goon's face with precise timing (it feels just as satisfying as it sounds), performing an aerial special attack, juggling enemies off of walls, the ability to change characters in between stages, and a very welcome stage select option!Just like the original trilogy, there is a high skill ceiling here. Every character has depth, and mastering the higher difficulties will require mastery of the characters. That's not to say that the game isn't accessible, because it certainly is. There are 5 difficulties, all of which are very fair (mania difficulty is an appropriate chaotic skill test). All of the characters also feel varied enough that you'll be sure to find a few that you like playing, if not every one. The music is SO good.There are a couple of little quality of life improvements that could further polish an already incredible experience:1) The ability to further refine the controls to your liking - it would be nice to have the ability to map attack and item pickup to the same button in the default controls, as it is in the legacy control settings.2) The option to display weapon durability.3) This one would likely affect the balancing, but it would be awesome to have a mode where all characters can sprint. It was extremely satisfying to sprint across the stage to knee an enemy in the face in SOR3.4) Enemy invincibility frames can make things distractingly meta, where you have to think about who you're allowed to attack because a certain enemy's attack can't be interrupted, or they will perform an attack immediately about getting to their feetIf you're a fan of the original trilogy you'll adore this game. It's made by people who very clearly are fans themselves, and was made with care and attention to the source material. If you haven't played many beat 'em ups this is a great one to start with; there is a ton of diversity in the stages and movesets, as well of customization options. Very highly recommended.

Double Dragon Neon is a bit sluggish, yes, but there are many different things you have to do to succeed in combat, such as using a specific power move of your own choice, dodging at the right time to get a massive power boost, and using the right moves to account for the specific enemy type. If that's an issue for you, you'll easily unlock all three SOR1 characters with original mechanics pretty early on, so just use them instead. _childDocuments_.review: Video games getting sequels is nothing new, but it's pretty special when one comes out over twenty years later and stays true to its roots like Streets of Rage 4. This game, launching 26 years after the last one, keeps the classic feel of fighting through city streets and enjoying Yuzo Koshiro's amazing music, but it looks and feels new for today's players.Set ten years after Streets of Rage 3, the game welcomes back old friends like Axel and Adam Hunter, and introduces us to new ones, including Cherry. The gameplay is just what fans love – a fun, 2D fight-your-way-through-the-city adventure. Players get to beat up enemies using different moves, with each character bringing their own style to the fight.Streets of Rage 4 keeps things interesting with new twists and turns, offering various fighting styles and creative levels that add fresh challenges. It's designed to be enjoyable for everyone, whether you're a long-time fan or new to the series. You can even adjust the difficulty to fit your preference, making it welcoming for all players.The game also brings the '90s vibe into the modern era with beautiful, hand-drawn graphics that keep the gritty, colorful feel of the original series. There are a few moments where it's hard to see your character in the chaos, but overall, the look and music of the game are highlights. Streets of Rage 4 shows that some things never go out of style, blending nostalgia with new experiences perfectly.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sad and disappointed that I must give this negative review. I love SoR series, I played SoR3 a lot back then on my Mega Drive and I love playing SoRR too (there's so much variety in that game). And I love beat 'em up games, I played them a lot back in the glory of arcade days. But SoR4 disappoint me, all the praises mostly just because of the nostalgia.The art direction is great, the soundtrack is good, the juggling is fun and satisfying, but why there's NO CONTINUE? Why the boss have super armor? Why only 1 character have running ability?When I read some of the discussion, here's the arguments for these questions:"Instead of continue, you can use assist or you can play it on easy or just git gud lol"If you use assist feature, you will lower the overall score you will get. So what? Who is still playing for the score!? Yeah, no one, except you need the score to unlock the additional characters.And git gud? Do I really need to be really that good playing beat 'em up game? What do you expect if you want to buy a beat 'em game?I played it on hardest, because there will be more enemies that I can punch, but I died when I meet the first boss (Diva). I lowered it on hard, I died again when I face Diva. Why? Because of..."If you want to beat the stage boss, just use poke and run"Really? If you look back on SoR series, did you found boss with super armor? I know that SoR4 doesn't need exactly to be like previous game, but if you think cheesing / hit and run a boss is a fun thing to do, I don't think it's fun for me. IMO super armor is just a cheap way to make the boss "harder"."It's like SoR2! Only 1 character that can run!"Come on, is giving some mobility to the character is really a bad thing? Good luck evading Diva's super armor attack using Floyd.In the end, SoR4 is a degrade from previous entry, it's kinda saved by the juggling mechanic, but it's not enough for me. If you want good beat 'em up game, you can play Yakuza series.If you want fun 2D beat 'em up, Castle Crasher is stupid and fun.If you want to play good SoR game, you can find SoR Remake and previous SoR is available on Sega Mega Drive Classic.If you really really want to play this game, hold your money and wait it for a big discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is Cheap.  Enemies have a host of abilities that the player doesn't such as invincible rushing attacks, counter attacks, diagonal hits, blocking and no-knockdown ability just to name a few.  If you don't give the player some of these abilities (all of the above the player doesn't have but has to face against), the game is going to feel one-dimensional and very cheap and is no fun.  Take the classic Nier Automata, the player has a host of options and different ways of attacking separate from his enemies and it creates a multi-dimensional experience.  This game's biggest failing is that it is an afternoon romp and is forgettable because its so one-dimensional and offers no attack strategies and the only real strategy is just hope you can outlast the number of invincible hits the enemy can do to you.  Horrible and worthless and tarnishes a nice IP.

_childDocuments_.review: For the positives, SoR4 is visually excellent, I really like the art style they went with and it does a great job of maintaining the important parts of the original games aesthetic.The addition of a Bloodborne style health recovery system after using a special attack (instead of just taking damage as in SoR2) also feels like a good alternative to SoR3's solution of having a cooldown to avoid damaging yourself. Also adding a visual effect for hyper armour, and having new ways for enemies to obtain it is a nice addition.Unfortunately it feels like a step back in almost every other way, despite having over two decades of game design to learn from. Other than the things mentioned above, mechanically all it really adds is a new super move and an aerial special attack, both of which are welcome, but at the same time it ditches the running and dodging mechanics of SoR3 (apart from one character who can sprint), which makes the gameplay feel extremely dated even by the standards of 26 years ago.The music is fine, but that's pretty much it. Nothing stands out as being amazing like SoR2, or even just 'different' as in the more controversial SoR3 soundtrack, which is pretty disappointing for a series famous for its incredible OST.I refunded the game before completing it, but I've heard it's only a couple of hours long, which isn't terrible by this genre's standards. But when you consider that the fan remake of SoR1, 2 and 3 can be obtained easily for free as one huge game, with additional fan made levels, all the characters from every prior game, with a vast amount of unlockables and updated visuals and mechanics, SoR4 kind of pales in comparison.I can only recommend this game at full price if you are a huge fan of SoR and are bored of playing the fan remake. Otherwise stick to/check out the fanmade SoR game for more content and better music/mechanics until you can pick this up in a decent sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics are awesome. Music is great. However, this is the most frustrating beat em up I've ever played. I've played difficult games and I recognize my own skill limitations as a gamer. To illustrate, I absolutely suck at hollow knight but I keep going back to it because the character movement is fluid and I know I just need to get good at it to make progress. In SOR4, It doesn't make sense that the characters walk around like they're wading through concrete while enemies can run circles around you. There's a boss who can twirl around like a ballerina and shoot diagonally and I'm trying my best to dash around to hit him but it is freaking impossible to catch him and do consistent damage and it draws out an already extremely frustrating fight. It doesn't make sense that you can only attack in a straight line with very limited range while enemies can dash attack you from across the screen or dash diagonally/vertically to hit you or grab you.  After playing for a few hours, my hands were hurting from trying to make my character move faster and I suspect I might break my controller if I keep at it. This game is stressful and not enjoyable and I will not be coming back to it.

_childDocuments_.review: About the game and a bit of my previous experience with this franchise.SoR1 - Played a bit with SMD&G collection. Very annoying enemies, with broken/outdated stuff, limited move set, and weird difficulty.SoR2 - Completed few levels on my phone. Huge improvement in comparison to first game.SoR3 - Haven't played it.Now about Streets of Rage 4.It's a decent game in the Beat em Up genre and developers polished/improved a few things in the classic SoR scheme, including combat. Worth playing, but has serious cons.+ 5 playable characters with different stats.+ Modes like Story, Arcade and Battle (1vs1 PvP mode).+ Overall feels like a modern version of old SoR game. For better or worse. Soundtracks included.+/- You can unlock playable character from SoR1-3. Unfortunately they have old stats, moves and sprites. Max and Shiva are in the game with SoR4 level graphics...+/- Art style is too vibrant. Weeb family makes it even worse.- Some enemies can be very annoying. Feels worse on later stages and higher difficulties (more aggression and number of enemies). Karate guys, fat truckers and maybe Muay Thai guys with white tank tops.- Universals armor system for bosses ain't cool.- Last stage is crazy. My first campaign was solo on Hard and after fighting too many fat guys etc., I had to fight weeb girl, then again with her and her weeb brother. After some damage, her brother used giant robot. I wasted more time on this than on the first half of the game combined =P. I mean you can learn a boss attack pattern but when he is armored and supported by his sister, it becomes annoying.- Online is crap. I played with few helpful people, but I also experienced this: People pause the game for no reason or to troll you (yes, any player can "make the game hostage" with pause button. Leave and restart...). People leave for dumb reasons, like when they weren't careful and died because of it. You can find player with ping from another galaxy. Also, some people love speedruns...Buy on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: first things first. if you are a fan of the Streets of Rage series or even if you are a fan of beat 'em ups in general, buy this game. seriously, stop reading this review, don't waste anymore time, and just buy the game. you won't regret it.that being said, i'll go into more detail. the game is incredibly faithful to the past games in the series and is incredibly old school. that of course is not a bad thing but it does carry some faults with it. one way that manifests itself is that this game can get damn brutal. enemies will happily take cheap shots as well as gang up on you. but with enough practice, you can get through it. imo, that's how a game like this should be. but if you get easily frustrated, it might not be for you. to add to that, the gameplay is mostly straight out of the 90's. to some that may be a bad thing, but in the context of the specific game, i think it works very well. there are no real ways to block or even dodge attacks; i do wish they had kept the sprint and roll features from SOR3, but even so the gameplay is tight and fluid. the art style is absolutely gorgeous. everything is super crisp, vivid and colorful. it has a comic book feel to it, and i know some people would have preferred the more 'gritty' style of the previous games, but i think the art style looks amazing but still holds much of the 'feel' of the previous games. playing this game absolutely feels like playing Streets of Rage. the music is also absolutely amazing and badass. again, it feels and sounds like Streets of Rage. they brought back the original composers and how ever much money they paid them, it was worth every penny and i'm very, very glad they came back.in conclusion, while this game has it's flaws (mostly due to keeping many gameplay elements from the 90's that some may say haven't aged well) it is still absolutely worth playing if you are a fan of the previous games or just a fan of beat 'em ups in general. seriously, at $25 this game is a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly the game is good. If you play solo it is everything you would want from a sor. I invite you to read other reviews to know the positive points in detail.But for now the online multiplayer part is unacceptable:Ping is high, very high (no matter the quality of your connection). Framerate is unconsistent and unpredictable.  With a good fiber connection (FTTH/500mb/s) you can't get lower than 60 ms of ping... The framerate constantly switch between 60 fps and 30 fps (locked by the game) so fluidity and latency constantly jump from bearable to absolutely atrocious (and no it is not because of my pc specs).Also, the online games lacks some quality of life features, like for example lobbies , chat between players (even only in between levels it would be ok) or maybe voip.So for now, even if the game is enjoyable in solo and local multiplayer, if you plan to play online its a solid NO, don't buy it.I would gladly correct this review if the devs release patch to improve the online part.TDLR: Good game, atrocious netcode.Edit: some people report the same problems as me, some don't, i don't know how many players are affected. So pretty much it's hit or miss.

_childDocuments_.review: I dig it - I love the SoR-Games since my childhood and was very excited to play this.It still feels and plays like the old games - don't expect anything groundbreaking new here, it is true to it's originials and does not offer many new things - which can be a bit dissapointing, but all in all its great, cause it is just more of the things we already loved in the first games.At first, i found the Artstyle a bit weird and didnt like it - after my second plathrough, I have to say, that it gets to you, and while you might not like it entirely, it fits the game very well.The soundtrack was the most memorable thing for me in the old games - will I remember this one for the next 23 years as well? No, sadly not - It has some great tunes, don't worry - Some REALLY good ones, but they aren't memorable at all. You will probably forget them in a few weeks.I had mixed feelings after the first playthrough with one of the new characters - after my second one with an original Retro-SoR Figher hand somehow I enoyed it waaaaaaay more than the first.If you want more Streets of Rage - you will get more - dont expect new mechanics and stuff!

_childDocuments_.review: Streets of Rage 4 is a revival of a of an old beat 'em up classic that was known for being easy to pick up, but hard to master.The Good:+The game is absolutely gorgeous, both the backgrounds and the sprites.+The soundtrack is rad as hell.+At least five different characters, not including the secret ones, with unique moves and strengths.+Tons of secrets and a few alternate game modes.The Bad:-The sound effects are kind of weak.-The game becomes extremely challenging, even on normal...-Because enemies can attack diagonally and move way faster than you...-Which is a problem because only one character can dash, one can sprint, and no one can block.Bottom Line:Let me be very clear, I recommend that you get this on sale, invite some friends via remote play, and enjoy it as a casual button masher. You'll have a ton of fun.If you try to master this in single player, prepare to chase every i-frame you can find and embrace every trial and error tactic available. It's a shame, but the combat design is in dire need of more features.

_childDocuments_.review: THE BEST STREETS OF RAGE GAME EVER!Which is a low bar to clear because the other one SUCK!! While this game isn't Cuphead levels of Challenging it still a strong enough to entertain most!! The best part to me at least is the completely overhauled Cell animated sprites mixed with 3d  Guilty Gear like animation which is a massive improvement of the crappy 3d of the past! _childDocuments_.review: Beat-em-ups were my bread and butter when I was a young kid in the ancient, ancient time known as the early 90s. I have a deep fondness for every main series of Beat-em-ups, from Final Fight to Double Dragon. And too many times I've seen people try to "reinvent" or "modernize" the very basic formula of the genre in a way that ruins the simple repetitive fun of punching a bunch of goons while walking right.Streets of Rage 4 is the greatest modernization of the genre since Double Dragon Neon, and surpasses that underrated classic in almost every way. It maintains the basic game feel that made the old Streets of Rage games classics of the genre (well... 2 and 3 anyway, that first one was rough) while adding levels of complexity and high end mastery that classic games could only dream of. This game's combo system and varied movesets have been likened to fighting games due to their depth, but all of it still serves the basic design and gamefeel of a true beat-em-up classic. Every aspect of this game's design works beautifully together.With a truly incredible soundtrack, gorgeous animated HD graphics, and a dizzying array of playable characters who all have their own unique playstyle, this is the most complete and replayable entry in the beat-em-up genre maybe ever. If you have even a mild fondness for this genre or a passing nostalgia for the old games, you owe it to yourself to buy this. And don't miss out on the DLC, which adds great new characters, swappable moves, and a near-infinitely varied survival mode featuring all sorts of classic enemies.I used to consider Streets of Rage the 4th best beat-em-up franchise, but between this frankly revolutionary entry and a certain amazing fangame from almost a decade ago, I think SOR now sits on the throne of Brawlers as the undisputed king.

_childDocuments_.review: Needs 4 player co-op Online. Also needs a way to see your connection to a potential host, 400 ping is awful. Story is fairly lacking, some bosses are disappointing(I don't like reused bosses outside of the trope to have you fight all the bosses before the final boss in the final level). Classic enemies are mostly intact except I have no idea why the bikers are now rotund dwarven women. New enemies are all over the place, some are great, others are annoying and the rest are very difficult to deal with. The SoR4 characters actually have high combo potential, more so than any normal beat 'em up giving the game a much higher skill ceiling than other beat 'em ups. There are quite a few unlockable characters which is a plus. The game can be quite difficult depending on what character you play. I don't recommend it in its current state, it lacks polish; reused bosses, fighting the first mid boss character repeatedly throughout the story, lacking dialogue and story elements as the game progresses(most notable in the final level). Beat 'em ups usually don't need elaborate stories to be classics but if you are going to do a story, make it a good one. Overall it seems to be rushed.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing Streets of Rage 2 on the genesis. I loved that game, warts and all, and put hours into it. When the trailer for this game came out I immediately knew I was going to buy it. The art-style is gorgeous, the music is catchy (with a built-in old school soundtrack), and it was a revival of the game that made me fall in love with beat-em-ups. My expectations were met and exceeded. Streets of Rage 4 only improves on the already magnificent formula of the other games in the series. Without going into excess detail there are lots of little tweaks that modernize and improve the game, mixing the classic beat-em-up style with fighting game technique. The story mode gives you about what you expect (evil rich person runs the city, you punch your way to them), but told with loving illustrations. The cast of characters is great whether you're a long time fan or coming into the series for the first time, and each iteration of the recurring classics is represented in the original pixel art, with the original moveset. And this is all before the DLC content. The DLC adds 3 more characters (all of them bosses in the base game), a survival mode with roguelike elements, new weapons, a new soundtrack and fighting game style palette swaps for each character (except the pixel sprites). At around 8 dollars I also recommend it, highly. The only warning I would give is that if you are buying it for the characters,  two of them are available in their retro forms without the DLC. The movesets are different of course, but I could see that being a disappointment. If you are a fan of this style of game, or even think you MIGHT be, you should buy Streets of Rage 4. As of writing I have played 74 hours and with the new survival mode I am fully confident that several more are on the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is one of the best sequels to a 90s game series in gaming history. In 1991, SEGA released its brand new game for the "SEGA Mega Drive" console. Streets of Rage. The game had a lot of potential in it, and since players could predict that the game would be a huge success and a banger, SEGA created the masterpiece itself; Streets of Rage 2 (1992). Streets of Rage 2 is still one of the best games in SEGA's history, the "Beat 'Em Up" category, and 90s gaming. The game had a gorgeous soundtrack, game mechanics, graphics (at the time), and difficulty. Two years later in 1994, SEGA released the final game in the original trilogy of "Streets of Rage"; Streets of Rage 3 (usually branded as Bare Knuckle III). The game didn't receive as much love compared to the second game due to the storyline being constantly changed based on the region where the game was sold. The game mechanics became worse, and the characters' appearance was strange. Because of all this, only a few people who truly fell in love with the franchise bought "Streets of Rage 3", and later stores gradually stopped selling the game in real life until it came out on "Steam" and "PlayStation 3". That was the end of the franchise...until now. At the very beginning of 2020, "Dotemu" decided to make the most epic heroic brave Batman deed OG gamers have ever seen. The return of the "Streets of Rage" franchise with its 4th game...and I love it. The graphics are amazing, the game is incredibly drawn, the soundtrack is also wild, and the game mechanics overcome its predecessors by a lot! It's also nice to have active haptic feedback on my controller when I fall, take, or do damage. One of my favorite additions to the game was when they added the "Retro Update". If "Dotemu" wouldn't add this, the hype that I had when I first saw this would drop. It's very nice to have a "Retro Soundtrack" option that allows you to change all the music in the game to music from "Streets of Rage 2", but they also added the new "Retro Characters" that you can unlock as you progress in the game. This addition is honestly one of the best, as it gives you a chance to try a modern version of a game series with its old 90s characters, but also a chance to play with characters from past games that weren't included in the original "Streets of Rage 4", such as Eddie "Skate" Hunter (SOR2-3) and Dr. Zan (SOR3). The easter eggs/references to the old games are also very cool.Yes! The game is very well made, the storyline is pretty good and you will like a difficult game with such great mechanics and graphics! The game is worth its $24.99, but I would recommend that you buy the "Streets of Rage 4 + Mr. X Nightmare DLC" bundle, as it gives you the game and the DLC at a small $3 discount. That's what I did. Instead of buying the game separately and then when you complete everything you don't have anything new to explore, you can get the DLC with the game so you can immediately go to the DLC exclusive content (e.g new playable characters and survival mode).

_childDocuments_.review: SOR4 is an amazing return to form for the franchise. If you enjoyed any of the Genesis trilogy, there's a good chance you'll find something to love here. This game takes a bit from every SOR game and blends it together to create an extremely fun, polished package, that over time since its launch has improved DRAMATICALLY, and only got even better with the recent DLC content (which also comes highly recommended).While you may not have running or rolling, every character's arsenal is as complete as it needs to be to deal with every situation the main story mode throws at you, and every character has a unique niche and strengths that add a ton of flavor and replay value to the package. Coupled with an astounding soundtrack, the experience is one of a kind.If you're on the fence, please give it a try! I would wholeheartedly recommend the DLC, Mr. X's nightmare as well, as it adds 4 new characters (one unlocked with a cheat code), new colors for every character, and an extra special move for each playable character's existing moveset (the amount varies when you compare SOR4 to Retro, but they have unlockable moves for ALL characters, including SOR1!) All of this for 8 dollars is a steal, and of course the soundtrack in the Survival mode is also incredible.Every beat em up fan owes it to at least give this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game that you have probably been waiting for most quite some time now. This. Is. It.There's hours of replayability packed inside, tons of unlockables (including characters and some other modes besides Story), and online coop which from my time playing works flawlessly and it's an absolute dream. Plus, the soundtrack is as good as it has ever been, and if the new OST isn't really to your liking, there's an added option to have the retro soundtrack that you remember and love. It feels exactly how it should, I don't know how they managed to do it, but they created the next step in the franchise without leaving the old fanbase behind.Go buy this game, go relieve the best beat-em up franchise and go have fun with this absolute gem!

_childDocuments_.review: I played mostly on PS4 before getting the steam release.  There are some problems with syncing a PS4 controller that makes the game crash from time to time, but other than that is is a near perfect game.Streets 4 is a dash of arcade style goodness with all the new bells and whistles we would expect for a series being revived from the game with a sexy new coat of paint.  The new combo mechanic and ranking systems give a clear indication what it means to be boys playing a game, and men taking on a serious challenge.  It is accessible for completion by veterans on the higher difficulties, or if you suck balls at video games then there is a mode even a degenerate such as yourself couldn't lose.  There is much to be loved and with the DLC on the horizon it can only get better.  I tip my hat to these developers.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let's give this game a 10/10. Scoop it up and you will definitely not regret it. But, here's some more info. *SoR = Streets of Rage*Pros: - Most if not all the past characters make a return.- Arcade brings back the classic feel of SoR. - New and Old soundtracks are amazing.- Enemy types vary immensely and even have you change how you approach certain foes. - New combat mechanics fit to the game nicely.- Environments are refreshing and transition cleanly from one stage to the next.- The story mixes well with the others in the series. Cons:- No truly NEW unlockable characters after Adam. (SoR4 Max, SoR4 Shiva, or Estel) who are already in the game. The experience bar fulls up to unlock SoR1 - SoR3 characters in that order. Afterwards it just disappears and you're left with obtaining points. - Online works great, but while playing co-op one player will have smooth frames with the other will not. This can also switch at random mid fight at times. - Online co-op caps at 2 players. It's understandable, but that's why local 4 player co-op is a thing. This game truly is worthy of being a Streets of Rage titled game and it has gotten my brothers all playing again (our last one was SoR2). If you don't scoop this game, you're really missing out.P.S.: To the Dev that designed how elevator glass works, you're amazing. Battle with a friend on the Elevator stage and you'll feel like you're a combo master while knocking them out into the abyss. Trust me.

_childDocuments_.review:
Publisher Dotemu (Wonder Boy, Windjammers 1/2) and developers Lizardcube (Wonder Boy) and Guard Crush Games today revealed Streets of Rage 4, an all-new continuation of SEGA's iconic arcade brawler series known for its radical fights, jammin' '90s beats and dashing sparring gloves and bandanas. 

Streets of Rage, known as Bare Knuckle (Bea Nakkuru) in Japan, is a trilogy of beat 'em up games developed and published by SEGA in the 1990s.

Famously known for its non stop action and electronic dance influenced music - scored by Yuzo Koshiro and Motohiro Kawashima - the series has gained the status of cult classic throughout the years. It is considered one of the best beat 'em up series of all time. After many years, Axel and Blaze are finally picking up the fight where they left.

Featuring hand-drawn visuals from the team behind 2017's gorgeous Wonder Boy: The Dragon's Trap remake, Streets of Rage 4 builds upon the classic trilogy's gameplay with new mechanics, a fresh story and a gauntlet of dangerous stages with a serious crime problem. Streets of Rage 4 recalls classic gameplay but it stands as an entirely original arcade-style romp thanks to the expertise of Guard Crush Games and Dotemu.

Whether players gang up with a friend or clean up the city solo, Streets of Rage 4 is a skull-bashing, chicken-chomping delight all set to a thumping soundtrack sure to get your blood pumping. 

Features:

* The comeback of the legendary Streets of Rage series.
* Beautiful graphics fully hand-drawn animated by the studio behind Wonder Boy: The Dragon's Trap.
* Classic gameplay enhanced with brand new mechanics.
* Soundtrack by a wide line-up of world-class musicians.
* Braised chicken served on a pristine plate.

name: Young Souls
detailed_description: Reviews About the Game As orphans, Jenn and Tristan's life path brought them to a mysterious scientist, who took them in and cared for them as his own children. But one day, he disappeared under very odd circumstances. While searching desperately for him, the duo found a hidden cellar and the Moon Gate portal, transporting them to a dangerous parallel world where goblins thrive. Your adventure begins as you fight to bridge these two very different worlds. ● Play a dynamic & deep side-scrolling RPG beat‘em up as Jenn and Tristan, solo or in co-op, as you explore the four unique biomes of the goblins' twisted world and the stylish world of the humans. ● Customise your combat gear by unlocking & upgrading hundreds of weapons, armour sets and accessories, to save the world as you know it. ● Unlock unexpected story paths as you fight your way through dozens of epic dungeons, hordes of enemies and over 20 fearsome bosses in the goblin realm. ● Young Souls combines the classic beat‘em up and story-rich role-playing genres through a beautifully crafted story, and in a world crafted with stunning art direction. Fighting goblins is not as easy as fighting the weight machine at Happy Fit. Combat is punishing and demanding, but you'll be rewarded with loot chests, which will help you forget the injuries you suffer on the battlefield. There are tons of possible combinations that vary the stats of your equipment, weapons and the gameplay of your character. Adopting an attacking, defensive or balanced strategy is easy for anyone who dares venture to the land of goblins. Brawling with enemies obviously means epic boss fights that will make you sweat. Young Souls is a journey between two worlds, each one full of experiences and encounters that will shape the character and fate of our heroes. After a well-deserved nap, you can hit the gym at Happy Fit and improve your statistics to gain more strength, resistance and stamina. If you're not too stiff, make sure to pay a visit to Solid Sneakers to get yourself the best kicks in town that will give you style and boost your characters' stats on the battleground. Teen Spirit shop is also open to those who need a makeover or just purchase a cool hat that fits with your brand-new sneakers. When you are done with having fun, it's time to kit yourself out from head to toe and enter the world of goblins – the place you want to be to bash some skulls and find the professor. Mobs of enemies will be waiting for you with spears and swords in the vain hope it will be enough to stop you...

_childDocuments_.review: The game has its fun side but overall it felt highly unsatisfying after beating it.  I wish what we had now is simply a beta version b/c that's honestly what it feels like. Story, battle, music are all underdeveloped.  The story is very generic and boring to say the least.  Why the developers  make the players feel we are the bad guys half-way thru the game is also unclear and unnecessary.   The ability to choose your responses to dialog only appears early in the game, but has no impact at the story at all.  It begs the question on why bother doing it at all if they are only going to be used in the early parts of the game.   There is only 1 town to visit and not much to do in town.  No sidequests watsoever.  The weapon and equipment system are pretty terrible with loads of items having bad status attached to them.  Elemental critical atk bonuses are a joke b/c most of the weapon doesn't even fire off any elemental attacks. This makes it only a very small handful of weapons/armor are useful.  The special skills part had potential but was not implemented very well.  If they can be used so a certain type of enemy or boss is very vulernable to a skill/attack, that would have been fun to discover and play around.  Or if you need to use a certain skill to discover hidden places or destroy obstacles that would have been cool as well.  But nope, the developers didn't take advantage of any of that.  Aside from bomb and landmine, everything else felt rather useless.  There is also limited resources for upgrading your weapons and special skills.  I didn't realize that until I was at the end of the game.  You cannot upgrade all your weapons and armor, some gems don't respawn and are only found in treasure chests.  The things to upgrade special skills is also limited. When you finally feel you got the hang of the game and a good build of weapons/armor the game pretty much just ends.  All the hard work you put in, nothing gets carried to the next game.  There is no New game +,  you start everything from scratch.   No post game dungeon, nothing!   The game had good potential, but almost every aspect is underdeveloped.  Overall, it just feels like a very shallow game.  A real pity.

_childDocuments_.review: first impressions:A very beautiful 2D beat-em-up ARPG. Only played solo so far. Playing on "challenging" and it has not been too hard for me yet (full disclosure: I like dark souls)Steam remote play co-op edit:After playing the game with my brother over steam remote play I can say this:+ even more excellent fun!-+ the difficulty ramps up with two players as its harder to recover hp via the twins tag-team feature+ forces you to try out different gear more-+ Steam remote play can be a bit laggy (depending on your internet ofc), making timed blocks harder. But the games accessibility functions can help (auto block etc).+ co-op adds loads more replay value!Solo play notes:+ Beautiful, the art style is simply awesome+ So far the itemization is interesting (upgrades, cool weapons, etc)+ Lots to be seen (town area) and everything can be done at a leisurely pace (lots of save points, fast travel to merchants)+ So far no bugs / glitches / issues-+ blocking based combat - time it right to stun the enemy and then open a can of whoop-ass. There's probably more to it, but haven't needed anything more fancy yet.-+ the writing is ok I guess, but if you compare that to the art style, the art wins 2-0.Strong recommendation!

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I enjoyed the first few hours, but around halfway through, the game started to get grating. The combat is good for the most part, but attacks eventually get to the point where there's almost no time between the wind up/"tell" and the attack. This is especially annoying as you deal with juggling attacking and blocking, and most shields do not allow you to block while an attack animation is playing. Also, as you get closer to the end, it becomes clear the team was running out of money and/or ideas, because the quality of both the gameplay and the story starts dropping and doesn't stop (♥♥♥♥ your spectral weapon 1 hp ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥).Then there's the story... It's... ok? I think? It comes off as someone tried to write a story where the protagonists and antagonists are morally ambiguous and that there's good and bad on both sides, but it doesn't stick the landing at all. Our protagonists are too reflective and empathetic to come off as bloodthirsty idiots charging into a foreign land, slaughtering any in their way. Our antagonists are too hateful and apathetic to come off as well-rounded people. When one side is, without reflection or guilt, sending soldiers to kill literal children who just want their parental guardian back who only fight said soldiers in self-defence while constantly offering peaceful alternatives... You don't have much room for moral ambiguity. The end gets closer, but still doesn't hit the mark. Again, I really wanted to like this game. I wish it was more thoroughly polished/written. But as it stands, I don't recommend it. If you're still interested, get it on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very pretty game with some satisfying combat, but it seriously could have used another QA pass. The camera follows player 1 at all times, making it a significantly more frustrating experience for player 2 as they often have to spend a great deal of time off of the screen while still under attack. The fact that the depth of field effect used to help with spacial awareness is tied solely to player 1 as well, making player 2 often out of focus, makes this even worse. I couldn't find any config file in the games core files to even remove the depth of field. Couldn't see any solution in a hex editor, eitherSprinting is also a double tap on the direction keys, which can not be unbound. Normally this wouldn't be much of an issue, but because the sprint interrupts your combos it can get real annoying over time.If you're playing singleplayer I'd recommend Young Souls, but otherwise you have to either have a high tolerance for frustration or a playstyle that involves rigidly staying in close proximity

_childDocuments_.review: Young Souls is a hack and slash action game. As the rebellious twin Jenn and Tristan, their normal life suddenly changes when they discover the gobbons living underground and their foster father is kidnapped by the gobbon empire which plans to take over the top for vengeance. Now the twin must gear up, seek out and help those who are willing to give them a hand, and rescue their father simultaneously preventing the gobbon invasion. Yes, this game features distinctive artstyle. Yes, it has an interesting customization visual-wise and function-wise. Yes, the combat is fun and rewarding. Young Souls has done a number of good thing, but the levels of those good deeds are basic. The depth of each feature is surprisingly lacking, which means the game can provide so much fun after one hour. Any time longer the fun will decrease drastically.→Satisfying combat and easy-to-use combo.→Lovely cartoony artstyle.→Nice soundtrack.→Simple but effective story.→Parrying is satisfying to pull off.Like: I like the variety of weapons(one-hand sword and hammer, twin dagger, great sword and great axe.) and armor in Young Souls. Each weapon and armor have distinctive visual and different bonus attributes when upgraded. Playing around their conditions can make the combat encounter extremely one-sided.Dislike: Even with all these interesting bonuses, the most dominant factor is still the damage. Late-game weapons easily outshine early ones just by being a sheer powerhouse. Armor ties directly to your max health. It's really a shame for me because I really like some of the early-game design. Using them late-game feels really underpowered and ineffective.The town the twin dwells in is a quiet little place. Pedestrian strolls by. Police patrols the street. Homeless guy sits on a bench with his dog. It`s such a peaceful town, and sadly that is all of it. Most of the pedestrians are just background props. The npcs you can interact with have the exact same dialogue each time you talk to them, no matter how many day passes. I wish the developer could put more things for players to interact with, more npcs with different lines as time goes by, and at least more places to go.I think its the natural flaw of this kind of game. Enemies can only attack what is in front of them and to some degree, behind them. Using X, Y, Z Axis, players will be completely save if they stand at Y axis of the enemies, which often creates hilariously easy-to-abuse opportunity to destroy the enemies. Bosses do have some attacks that hit around them but their starting frames take too long to land.I know the accessories function more as supporting skills to crowd-control or to deal with enemies far away. I still think there are still rooms for them to improve. I wish two accessories can be equipped at a time. This way players can create more synergies between weapons and accessories. Simple stuff like using Grappling Hook to pull enemy into Mines, or throw a bomb to knock down enemies so you can combo them safely.For the town, I wish the merchants could have more variety. The sneaker shop could have a feature of customizing your own sneaker, by combining two of the existing sneakers into one; the clothes shop could sell more kinds of apparels and accessories like scarves, gloves, or headphones. The town could even have a convenience store which can sell supplies that can temporally buff the players, and a barber that you can further customize the twin.For gobbon markets, I wish the blacksmith can sell upgrade materials after you finish the game since farming materials does not seem to be a thing in this game; the potion merchant needs to have new stocks besides simple stuff, like potions similar to the supplies in convenience store I mentioned before, but stronger and have a significant side effect; I wish the armor merchant could have the transmog system, changing the appearance of best late items to something the players prefer.→Difficulty does not affect much.→Wish all upgrade materials can be farmed.→Great axes and great swords need to have different movesets.→Levels don`t have much different beside visuals.中文小簡評→簡單卻不失特色的卡通畫風。→簡單的連招系統。→單純的劇情。→和平樸實的小鎮缺乏互動及生機。→關卡設計相對單調。→以XY軸來講，敵人沒辦法有效攻擊Y軸。→無論是哥布林或人類商人都缺少商品多樣性。

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game, I have changed the background of my phone lock-screen to one of the key art pieces on their homepage. When they announced the special edition, I pre-ordered it when it was available. While looking for further info on the game, I noticed the composer of the soundtrack was on Bandcamp so I followed them and got the OST as soon as it was out. This game has been out for quite a while on Google Stadia and while I totally respect the decision of the timed exclusivity, it wasn't quite worth it for me to get into cloud-gaming for this. But I don't think any game will ever get me to that point.Either way; sufficed to say, I was hyped about this game from the start and so far (after 4 hours playtime), it did not disappoint.Even though I like the concept of beat-em-ups, the classics like Golden Axe and Streets of Rage could never quite grab me. Young Souls, despite it's rather generic name instantly got my attention and motivated me to play more from the first second of gameplay.The fighting mechanics are very solid and make even a beat-em-up novice like me feel awesome. Parrying, dodging and chaining attacks on the multiple goons just feels right and the animations look quite cool. The various movesets of the different weapons and other mechanics like hotswapping characters (which also can generate an attack) and ranged options (like a bow and magic) keep it interesting in the long run.While this probably plays best with a controller, I always try to play my PC games with mouse and keyboard first and it feels quite good playing like that.Still, the game is pretty difficult at times. The first major boss before unlocking the second stage had me struggling for the better part of an hour but felt very fair throughout the multiple phases of his fight and the moment I managed to get his last healthbar to zero felt very rewarding.There's multiple difficulty options and accessibility settings to customize how hard the gameplay is, which is always a good thing to see in a video game. You could even go in the opposite direction and make it more difficult by just using weaker armor, weapons and not using the optional gym minigame to boost your stats.As far as I can tell, you could even go so far as to not level up at all since the game never seemed to require me to put the characters to sleep, which is required to actually use your exp to level up.The different stages had what seemed like level requirements on the front door of them but I remember going into a lvl 5 door, while only being level 2 or so.The soundtrack so far is nothing jaw-dropping but it's pretty nice nonetheless and I'm happy to have put it in my growing collection of game OSTs.Despite all the praise, there's still some aspects I don't really like about Young Souls.For one, the optional stat raising mini-game, which requires you to spam a button in just the right amount, was not fun at all.The amount of cutscenes, especially at the start, where a bit too much for me but with this kind of game I always put gameplay way above story so I often feel inclined to just skip the conversations and the litte, optional mini-cutscenes you get when looking at various things strewn about the overworld and in the dungeons.Speaking of the overworld; after unlocking all the points of interest, it's kind of annoying to have to run about the little town to get to where you want. The devs give you a moped and a fast-travel option in but not all the locations you visit frequently are included, so you still have to do some legwork (or take the vespa for a ride).At this point in the game, I'm not quite sure how to feel about the special locked chests that you can find all over the dungeons since they have different rarities and require different higher level keys that you get later in the game. That means I will probably have to backtrack and if the older levels still contain the same enemies as before, this won't be very fun.So far the only noticeable glitch I encountered, was when I kept jumping against the portal while it loaded up the level behind it, I just fell through the floor. Since this was the start of the level and I could still use fast-travel while falling, no progress was lost. Other than that, the game looks and feels pretty polished.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my God. I LOVE this game so much.It's a beat 'em up game with RPG elements (swords, armor sets, bows, magic), where you play as these two awesome twins full of style.The combat is tight and cool as heck. You got dodges, rolls, parries and blocks. Combos! If you are a beginner you are totally safe mashing buttons and trying to create your own combos, and if you're really into it you can make your own customized, deadly and cool-AF combos, juggling your enemies in the air for quite some time.And the gear? Jesus, the loot is so addictive. You'll always want to go to the next dungeons for stronger gear. And don't even get me started on the art style (really cool and unique) and the very polished gameplay experience overall. The soundtrack is awesome too, although (in my opinion) it gets too silent sometimes.I don't even like this genre, but I'm totally in love with this game. Do I need to say anything else?Young Souls for the win.Small update: Also voted on this game for the Steam awards. <3

_childDocuments_.review: After a Remote Play Together playthrough of this game I can recommend this, with this one piece of advice: Me and my friend cleared 1/4 of the worlds on Challenging and got about halfway through World 2 before lowering to Normal, at which point we had a significantly more fun, if easier, time.This game is a solid beat em up. However, the "Souls" in the name hints at the design direction, and unfortunately that twist on the beat em up formula is not well executed. This is not an issue of me or my mate not liking "souls" brand difficulty, we finished a Seamless co-op Elden Ring playthrough not that long ago. This is an issue of the game not living up to the genre's expectations. Instead of a challenging experience that's rewarding to overcome as you grow to learn how fair it actually is, I got the sinking feeling of realizing how badly the game was designed.Here's why, so you know what you're getting into:On Normal, you have enough health leeway to power through these sketchy elements... On Challenging, you don't. You will usually die in ~3 hits from a boss, so better stop taking risks, exercising agency, or enjoying your moveset. It is time to patiently parry everything, until it's your turn. (or use mana to skip to your turn, if you have it) Maybe that experience is easier in singleplayer, but I wouldn't expect that to be the case.It's like a bad imitation of Sekiro, with 10x less health to work with, an array of unreactable attacks, and you have a co-op partner, politely waiting for the boss to target them instead, because parrying focused combat essentially boils down to a rhythm game only one of you can play at a time.The RPG elements of this genre are also a mess, though not an active roadblock to fun like the above stuff can be. The art team put a lot of work into dozens of unique weapons/armorsets, but the majority just can't be viable because of how big the stat gap is compared to other equipment.Eg. Yarlanda weapons unlock the ability for the blacksmith to sell weapons of the same moveset. But Yarlanda weapons vastly outpace shop weapons, so why would I spend tons of money getting a mediocre two handed sword, when I just got one of the best two handed swords in the game?Heavy armor is also better than light armor, without much contest. Light armor speed is fun, but heavy armor will double or triple your HP while allowing you to keep comparable movement speed with lightweight weapons. As a bonus issue, the game has a currency for cosmetics when running around town, but equipping a cosmetic in your hat slot  and vice versa, which is one of the most baffling QoL issues I've ever seen in my life.While this review has focused on Young Souls' drawbacks, I want to emphasise that there is a fun co-op beat em up here, just as good as others in the genre when that's what it's focusing on. While the bossfight focus and RPG elements do not come together, bouncing enemies off walls like tennis balls is fun.Just please keep my warning in mind that the "developer intended difficulty" will not give you a fair or fun challenge, but instead a very unbalanced exercise in frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, here's the deal. This game is babies first RPG in terms of actual difficulty. Even on the Expert difficulty I was able to breeze through this game. But that's not the point. The point is I was able to breeze through this game with my wife. Anyone who is married to or dating a gamer can attest to how difficult it can be to find fun Co-Op games.Well, this is a fun Co-op game, Plain and simple.Its fun enough to keep your attention while being segmented enough that you can pick it up and put it down. Meaning you can play it together when you have the free time. So here is what I suggest.1. Buy the game.2. Find a partner to play with.3. Give them every good piece of equipment that drops. This will make them feel special and over powered. I could equip the starting sword and beat this game, so let them have the best gear. The parry mechanic is incredibly simple to execute so you don't need to worry and there is plenty of equipment.4. Save the blue tear drops until you get Teleport and then max it out and give it to them. It will instantly make them feel like a bad ass as they teleport around the map.5. The best sword in the game is called World's End. It is the chest reward from the third floor challenge dungeon. It's easy to overlook, as it doesn't have six upgrade levels. It only has three and will vaporize anything it touches in this game. Just encase your partner really sucks. If so just put them in heavy armor with teleport and this weapon and they will have a blast.

For the first point, i feel there is a heavy balance change between the first part of the game and the later part..... at first some challenges seem way too hard, while on the other side the second part of the game feels like a breezeStorywise.... it feels that in the end a lot of events are just mashed together at quick pace and happen one after the other, so it kinda loses impactStill, a good game to enjoy

_childDocuments_.review: This game had been on my watch list for a while, awaiting the date for it to drop. Getting news it dropped today i instantly purchased it. The game is a side scrolling beat'em up with RPG elements. It is beautifully drawn with very good scenes to tell a story. The opening alone is why action and camera placement matters when telling a story.The gameplay revolves around delving into short little dungeons filled with a multitude of monsters. Combat is very nice and rewards proper timing of your uses of attacks, special attacks, and either blocking, parrying or dodging. You can parry bosses and it's even encouraged due to their parry endurance. When you parry them enough to break their endurance you get a few seconds to lay on the damage.There's a few weapon types to play with and they have a flavor of different passive traits to suit a playstyle. Equipment sets can give you extra boons and reasons to keep with a set, be it a passive bonus, or the defensive bonus they can give to really help boost your HP.The game is singleplayer with the option to play couch co-op. It has remote play together which works rather well, my friend and i both played together for over 4 hours without any hiccups, though i am sure it works well with parsec if you run into any problems. When playing alone you control one of the two at a time and can "tag" the other in with the LB button if you are on controller. This mechanic plays like a tag in system like you see in fighting games, as one takes damage, they have a yellow section of the hp bar that fills whenever they are tagged out for the other sibling. This feature of course isn't present in co-op, however the potions you get, heals both players when used near each other and each player can use a potion once each before incurring cooldowns on it.The story of the game so far 4 hours in isn't something you should take seriously, however it is rather fun, the dialog between the siblings, those of the baddies you will encounter, all have a certain charm about them. "I live for the stone" has become a regular with my friend and I, and the siblings have rather natural sounding dialog between each other, being snarky teenagers whom have no parents to raise them.All in all, i very much recommend this game, it's a fun beat'em up, with charm.

_childDocuments_.review: The first few hours of this game were pretty fun, collecting keys to reach new areas from the hub world reminded me of games from the N64/PS1 era. Unfortunately after the second area the game throws that idea out of the window and becomes linear. The combat is enjoyable enough and different weapon types will let you perform a variety of combos and super moves. I have to say though that games like Castle Crashers handle this aspect much better. I also found the playable characters to be very grating. They act like modern day edgelords who hate everything for no reason. I can experience this type of behavior just by going out in public. Anyway Pick this up if it is $2.99 or less

_childDocuments_.review: Unfinished, buggy, amateur trash.GENERAL VIEW:Have played it for 12 hours already and it's barely getting tolerable thanks to the fact that the difficulty and complexity of the mechanics are barely getting interesting. The controls are very wonky, the difficulty is very cheap and frustrating, and the game as a whole is awfully repetitive. What drove me to witing this review is the fact that the game got bugged after beating the 4th? mayor boss, Fazmore, after an awfully cheap and infuriating fight, the guardian tears he dropped got bugged and I could not pick them up. After entering the room again, they were gone, after loading the save file again, Fazmore was dead and no guardian tears were available anymore, as if the game wasn't already frustrating, I wont be able to get all accessories to max lvl.SPECIFICSGood things first, the art is beautiful, Xavier Houssin's and the art team's backs must be shattering from doing all the heavy lifting for this game.1.- The mechanics - Fight, get useless weapons and armor, stick to those that dont suck that much, level up, go to the gym, upgrade stuff. Rinse and repeat. The art style is gorgeous but the world itself pretty small with little to nothing to see other than a few interesting characters and bland boring dungeon 3D backgrounds that could very well be asset flips. This is basically what the game is about. At some point you can get the Yarlanda great sword which feels broken and a white armor (forgot it's name) which is SUPER broken, literally everything else, a massive arsenal, is useless, magic is useless becuse the weapons that can use magic have awful stats, mana strikes are good but mana potions are useless, it's terribly balanced. Menus and user experience have a lot of flaws, the fast travel and the small overworld make me even wonder why there's an overworld at all. NPC dialogues are terrible, there's a currency for usefull items and another one for clothing, why? Lastly there's nothing to do in the overworld other than going to the equipment shop, gym and moon gate, again, you can revome the overworld and the experience is the same.2.- Performance -  The game is riddled with bugs. I cant browse clothing options I've bought for the girl because the buttons only work for the boy's clothes, stones and drops from pots and boxes can get stuck inside the walls, the characters will randomly run instead of walking even if you never double tapped the stick, pressing a certain button during a fight will bring up the equipment menu WHILE THE FIGHT CONTINUES (who in the WORLD needs to bring the equipment menu during a fight? That's terrible UX), some attacks land, some others dont, hitboxes aren't very consistent. Overall this heavily looks like the work of an amateur.3.- The story and the game itself -  The whole idea behind the story is nothing new, it's like "stranger things", some kids find out a hidden world and it's up to them to save their world now. Dialogues are nothing great, the characters aren't very likeable because, aside of the protagonists, every character feels very one dimensional. For some reason there's profanity in the dialogues, and the protagonists are a little bratty and not very likeable. The game, as a "beat em up" is very bland since there are a lot of reused enemy characters, the grunt with the sword, the stealthy ninja, the flying annoying piece of crap, the heavy hard hitter and their magical variations, ice one, fire one, electric one, etc. As an RPG, dont even get me started, like I said, weapons and armor, a huge arsenal, almost completely useless with the exception of a few good options, accessories too, the bow is good, bombs are awful, the magic staff is good, the teleporter is the only viable option. Potions, there are 3 so far in the game. 1 for regaining HP, 1 for mana, 1 for HP again but with a slow healing effect, why this one? everytime you use one there's a cooldown, why waste time with a potion that will heal slowly ovetime and waste a cooldown with it, when you can instanly heal with the first one? Mana potions are also useless, you gain mana by blocking and hitting enemies, you never find yourself in the complicated position of NEEDING MANA, just hit them a bit more and you'll get it, by the way, if you run out of mana from successfully hitting enemies with special attacks, they're probably all dead already anyway since each fight has a small number of them this makes the potions mechanic very one dimensional.The fights - Like I said, very frustrating. Enemies can hit you multiple times at the same time, if they all attack at once, even if they knock you down, they can hit you in the ground, the reason you cant fight a lot of enemies at once is because they could easily destroy you in an instant. Parrying is very inconsistent, some enemies can break your guard if even if you feel you parried them successfully. This is a very infuriating mechanic, some bosses or big enemies can constantly attack, your attacks cant interrupt theirs but theirs can interrupt yours, they can quickly guard but you cant break their guard and they can continue attacking regardless of mana, stamina etc. This makes it so that the best or even the only way of standing up to them is to successfully parry them, however, if you miss, they can punish you so hard, you're better off restarting the fight at that point.SUMMARY - The game is not a very good beat em up, a terrible RPG, riddled with bugs, terrible mechanics and overall an awful experience. Im not much of a quitter and I feel like I have to finish the game at this point but I really want to uninstall right now and refund.Absolute trash

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game on accident on the day that it got released. The art style really beckoned me in and I am a big fan of RPG style games with leveling and equipment, but I was hesitant to pay $22 on just that. Even so, I thought, screw it, I'll buy it and return it if I don't like it.Within 5 days, I sunk 24 hours into this game with a friend in order to beat it. I bought this game not only for myself but for two other friends because it is just such a fantastic game that I wanted to support the developers even more. This game is easily worth $25 and I would highly recommend buying it.There are definitely glitches, but since it's only been out for 5 days, I would hope that they are working on them, although none of the glitches that I've encountered are game-breaking, only once did I need to restart the game in order to fix a glitch.One thing that I really like is the accessibility options that are in the game, I think that accessibility options need to become more of a standard and this is a good start.
