_childDocuments_.review: Looking for a game to play with your buddies or want to play solo? Do you like upgrading your gear and stats? Do you enjoy challenging mode options? Want something that you can fully complete in around 12-15 hours? Look no further, this game has it all. Gear options, stat options, cute animation/cut scenes, and the option to play with friends or by yourself. Truly a well done game that was an absolute joy to play. Looking forward to their next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the game solo on the easiest difficulty, and it was fairly enjoyable.Playing on PC with my keyboard with the default keybindings led to some very small annoyances such as the left mouse click being used for TOO MANY things, like attacking, progressing in dialogues, opening doors... so I often had issues with breaking pots placed too close to doors.It might be linked to me playing in the easiest difficulty, but the first few chapters of the game were quite hard, but as soon as I got the justice armor and a weapon doing 90+ damage, I became Death itself, and all attempts from the game to challenge became laughable.But there *was* some good challenges for a long while, so I had my fun. But if the devs do another game, I would suggest to gradually make sure that enemies receive at least a % of bonus power depending on the players stats. Although, I don't know, maybe the harder difficulties are more balanced.Overall, the idea of mix between Beat'em all and RPG, where you also have to decide when you should leave the dungeon to sleep so you can convert your XP into levels, that's pretty neat. Might be like me where you go to bed almost as soon as you see that you can level-up, or you can push until you don't feel you can push anymore.Going to the gym allows you to somewhat specialize your character (I myself put everything into pure strength).Story-wise, I think more could've been done. The twins are cartoonishly edgy for no reason, between their look and the swearing, which seems to be mistaken for depth of character. But to be fair, if I was in their place, I think I would swear just as much.The whole prologue kinda killed any sort of surprise you could've had for the very last chapter of the game, though.It's also a bit of a shame that there was so much talk of the goblin people revolting, but the game never really show you their towns and such. That being said, the motivations of characters like the Mayor or the Goblin king are interesting enough, and you could almost feel bad for those you kill at times.Something that could've been better would've been to make characters like Baldwin sometimes play a role WITHIN the dungeons, instead of just being the equivalent of an encyclopedia in the portal room.

_childDocuments_.review: Short game, but very quality. If you like the art style. I enjoyed it, and would definitely recommend it.the controls are fairly tight and responsive, the combat feels good (albeit the part with the ghosts could have been left out, not much good crawling there), and the equipment makes a difference in a good way.Albeit ice magic MAY be a tad too stronk. Making the enemy unable to act is powerful, who knew!I just can't find much to say about the game that should keep you away from it. It is a pseudo-3D bsidescrolling brawler, the main characters are typical teenagers, the weapons play different and have different strengths and weaknesses. And the 2h block just effective as the 1h weapons, because your blocking is determined by your equipped shield, so 2h awayyyy~Armour is similar, but it seems like you generally want a lot of armour, since armour adds to your HP pool. And the difference between fast and slow is somewhat neglible, since this isn't dark souuls, where you fatroll before you know it. Also, dodging in this game isn't quite as "necessary" as in otehr games, because, aside from one attack each boss has, that is basically a huge, telegraphed charge, everything can be blocked (less effective) or parried (much, much more effective). Parrying is fairly eas to learn, and gives huge benefits. normal enemies become staggered (and grab-able) after one or two successful parries, bosses need a little more. You also take basically no dmg from a parried attack, while a blocked attack can still deal reduced dmg to you, as each shield has a certain strength.It's a really good game! If you enjoyed games like Double Dragon, Dust - Elysian Tail, etc. definitely worth a buy. And any sale with more than 35% off is a steal.It doesn't have much replayability, though. From what I have seen, you finish the game once, and that'S it, no NG+. But that isn't bad. I would DEFINITELY recommend playing this with a friend! It's gonna be a blast for an evening or two, and is easy to get (back) into!

_childDocuments_.review: It's not going to change the world, but it's a solidly-made brawleRPG: the basic gameplay is pretty standard brawling, but you do have to manage your gear to keep up with the increasing difficulty, as in an RPG. The wide variety of weapons and armor allows for some flexibility with character builds, which is a good thing, though you'll find there aren't really any bad builds. While the game is apparently designed with couch co-op in mind, it works perfectly well playing solo: you can switch between the two characters at will, which allows for adaptability by letting you use two different builds at once. Visually, the game is a little bit checkered. On the one hand, it features a charming French animation art style that's very easy on the eyes, if a little goofy at times. On the other, some of the characters are animated in a somewhat cheap-looking Flash style. This doesn't happen enough to really hurt the presentation, though.The sound aspect is... fine. It doesn't have voice acting outside of grunts and whatnot, which is honestly fine by me. Sound effects are appropriate to the action going on. What little music there is is completely forgettable, unfortunately.Other details: There are checkpoints every few rooms, which is helpful because there are a few fights that will probably take a few tries. You can customize your characters' clothing, but this is ultimately pointless since they always wear armor over it. This is just me, but I found it kind of jarring when the kids started dropping f-bombs, since imho it doesn't fit the overall tone of the game. I know that's how teenagers talk, but it's a bit tonally inconsistent when compared with most of the dialog.I know I've listed some gripes here, but overall it's a good game. Very crunchy, satisfying brawling action with some customization options, a great visual style, and a story that's worth a darn. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been very much into indie and small dev games in recent years and The Arcade Crew have shown to have a few good games and franchises under their belt with The Last Spell, Dark Devotion and some of the great games under Dotemu's belt.So, when I saw this previewed I added it to my wishlist straight away and was lucky enough to be gifted a review copy.First of all, I've not had much gameplay, but approx 3 hours into it so far and can already see a lot of content to come, with features still being unlocked. I will be continuing to play this on stream, but wanted to provide my early review here.Gameplay:So far, it combines beat 'em up and dungeon crawl level hack'n'slash really well, with a simplistic form. A few different buttons to perform different actions (charge attacks, spells/ skills, simple one-button combos). That works well for me, especially with the style of game, but the combat can be punishing with a block and stamina gauge, if you mistime or don't keep your eye out for other enemy attacks. With four different difficulty options, the recommended is the second hardest and boy is it rewarding. There's also a lovely in-depth RPG element that I won't go into here.Controls:The control defaults feel mostly fairly natural (on XB controller, not tried PC), but the option to fully remap is very nice and in general is easy to grasp otherwise (I only changed around the dodge button to a more common one). It also has some nice accessibility options, which is great to see. I might have a look more into these later.Sound:The sound design so far has been nice to listen to, with satisfying SFX for the UI, combat and overworld in general. I don't recall any music specifically, but that's generally for me a good thing, as it means it fits in well and feels natural without distracting from the gameplay.Visuals:The design of the game is gorgeous. The art feels simplistic, but the character and monster designs are well drawn, stylish and pretty emotive. The 3D backdrops also fit in nicely with the 2D models. I think the overall style of the game and the colour palettes for various themes work really nicely.Story/ Dialogue:I won't put too much here, but so far I'm liking the story of the game and they have written it well. It leans into some common tropes, which is fine, but really subverts expectations with some overused clichés which I loved to see. The dialogue between characters is also fun and feels real in the world they've built.Overall:I'm in love with this game. It feels very cool to play, the controls are nice and combat is satisfying when you win. I'm a little sad the coop is local only as this feels like it would be a great game to play (1P)2P. 5/5 would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a lot of fun playing this game, either with my brother or alone.Pros:- The game has a fantastic art style and spunk. Different weapons also allow for experimentation so there is replay value. - Good controls.- Difficulty was rewarding until about 2/3 of the game and a bit less on a replay.Cons:- Third and fourth floors/areas seemed short, also most bosses seemed to be just reskins of older bosses. _childDocuments_.review: Way to all your game design and chuck it out the window.Take all of the armor you earned and reduce it 1 HP.Take all the weapons you loved using and be forced to use two subpar crappy ones--no other ones will work, not even the accessories you grinded to their highest levels.  That's all useless now.Take all the leveling and strats you've been doing and make it useless.Hordes of the same enemies populating the screen in waves.You took everything we worked for to make us play a really crappy version of the same game.  You reset the power curve the player worked hard to earn.  You made the game not fun.  You ruined a good game.Psychonauts did it with Meat Circus.  Guacamele did it by turning the last level into Super Meat Boy.  Sifu did it by making the last boss immune to Focus attacks despite letting you invest crucial XP into Focus the whole game--It's just game design that becomes suddenly obtuse with no warning and resets all sense of progress and power the player achieved.  It's worse than bad game design--it's unfathomably bad game design at the very last breath of a spectacular game.  It just makes you walk away from an experience going like... WTF.

_childDocuments_.review: From someone who played co-op,Visually impressive, strong art direction, really good animations.Combat system is good and weighty, just enough depth. Particular highlight, cameras are always a problem in action games that have dynamic movements in multiplayer based on player positions, but the ability to teleport to each-other without consequence is really helpful to curb this. Touches like this gives confidence in the studio name of '1P2P' for developers legitimately looking to make good co-op experiences.Game economy and progression seemed well designed, for those who manage to make some initial progress.Steam achievements were only at 36% of players for a rather early on mandatory point of progress, I worry a lot got hung up on the difficulty of figuring out parrying. We honestly opted to enable blocking while attacking in Accessibility settings, makes it a lot more digestible, don't think it was compromising the games design either.Heavily appreciate built-in game manual to explain its rpg stats and combat systems. It's a thing games have sorely missed in the digital age, to have that essential information shipped with the product. There were still some aspects of the game it didn't explain that required additional playtime to figure out.Loading left a lot to be desired, on a NVME SSD it was still rather slow, particularly for navigating stages of a single floor up to a boss, let alone the entire zone. I can only imagine how slow the games loading screens are on hard disk drives. On top of the initially-cool animation transitions between locations in the game. No idea if the game loads while playing those either, the fast forward button always feels like a must.Mixed on the writing, sometimes nice, sometimes passable. The setting is pretty good. We had high hopes for more interesting and fun dialogue between the twins, but it wasn't really jiving with us.Worried about the sales on this, not a lot of reviews for the caliber of game on offer. The studio deserves to live on and keep exploring new titles, their premise is unfortunately scarce and unique in the industry right now. Getting attention is hard, on top of rather high demands for polish in the modern gaming space. In this case, Young Souls has rough edges, but the core game proved to be a worthwhile experience for us, and would definitely like to see more.

_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others (Video review soon)Young souls presents itself as a mix of elements between side scroller Hack and Slash and RPG, wrapped in very interesting environments and culminating in the adventure of two twin brothers, Tristan and Jenn, who live in the mansion of their adoptive father, simply known per professor. Little did they know that they would forever change the life of this peculiar town that has a secret that few know.The adventure begins when the professor disappears without a trace. The entire mansion is shrouded in mystery and a specific location is completely off-limits to the brothers, for security reasons. It turns out that after the disappearance of his adoptive father, curiosity, and concern get the better of them and the exploration of this area leads to the discovery of a community of goblins that have been living under the surface. The story unfolds along lines that are sometimes seldom addressed in titles of the genre. Although the whole environment is somehow appealing to the youngest, it addresses topics such as the difference between good and bad, moral choices, and the consequences of their actions. The depth of the story is in fact one of the points that somehow separates Young Souls from other  Hack and Slash titles, where the objective is essentially to fight and defeat the Boss of that level.It's not all bad to feel some affection for the bad side of the force, right? That's because even the story of the bad group is appealing. The interactions between the characters, the problems with each other, and even the pain of loss. All the lines of text do a good job of setting the player up and pointing out all the personality traits of each character. Jenn apparently has a need to swear to express her displeasure, but she has a giant heart and in a way, this is the way she found to hide her feelings. However, there is an option to apply a profanity filter. I was actually curious to test this option.But why do Goblins, or rather Gobbons, the correct name for the race, live underground? Both sides just want to live their lives on the surface and this is where the focus of decisions between taking down the enemy or helping the enemy intrudes on the story. Who will really is the bad guy in the midst of all this?The underground is divided into 4 different dungeons that have several paths until culminating in the boss area. In this sense, you also feel a hint of Metroidvania, as there are places where access is prohibited unless you have a specific key with you. It is possible to collect 4 different keys that allow the opening of specific zones and loot crates that contain equipment.Although with very generic scenarios and without much difference between them, enemies change their attack type. Thus, it is necessary to adapt the combat style and even the type of equipment that is brought to the different areas. There is a wide variety of defensive equipment that wedges between armor and headgear and that have different effects. For example resistance to ice attacks, fire, or effects like more speed.The gameplay is quite fun, with the possibility of choosing one of the brothers at your pleasure, with the simple touch of a key in a kind of tag-team mechanic. There is also some depth to this mechanic, as it allows each character to recover a portion of their lost health when not in the fight. This of course is in solo mode. In local co-op mode or through remote play (on Steam), it allows players to select, within the two brothers, the character they want and adventure together.The player has at his disposal, as indicated above, defensive and offensive equipment. In more practical ways, the use of a shield makes it possible to block enemy attacks and even parry them. Although something complicated, the feeling of parrying an enemy with a great club is super satisfying. Regarding weapons, they are distributed between two-handed and one-handed weapons. In this sense it is possible to equip a sword and a shield, both need one hand to use them, two daggers, one in each hand, or two-handed weapons such as grand swords or axes. Still in this sense, each weapon performs fast or slow attacks, so the player has to adapt to the attack style. Each piece of equipment also has a specific weight, in the style of a souls-like. This will have practical effects on the character's movement.There is no skill tree, but there are stats that can be improved according to the player's wishes and separated into 3 main branches. Strength, Stamina, and Stamina. Each new level automatically attributes points in these stats without any intervention from the player, however, there is the possibility of receiving a gym card that allows you to visit the city's gym and apply points in one of these branches. This is a physical activity that requires some finger dexterity from the player. So each branch is equivalent to a different physical activity, Strength is equivalent to lifting weights, Resistance is equivalent to sit-ups and Stamina is equivalent to cardio/cycling. Depending on the player's performance, it is possible to receive one star or even five stars in the activity, which is equivalent to more points.Young Souls is undoubtedly an interesting title and lovers of the genre will find many hours of fun in this one.

_childDocuments_.review: 8 hours in, about 50% completed.The game is amazingly fun played solo: the switch character mechanic is spot on, and you will exploit it both to recover and to deal extra damage when used in a combo (at the cost of longer cooldown).Arsenal is varied enough (I'd expect a bit more tho), and mana attacks really add an extra layer of tactics - every weapon (may) have its own, so you'll end up choosing weapons not only for their attack speed/damage, but also for the exclusive mana attack it enables.Bugs-wise, I only met a minor one (items not showing correctly). Performance is great.100% recommended--- First impressions after 3 hours: you can really feel the time and effort they put into creating this game.The combat is fluid, fast and skill based: they nailed the concept of an arcade beat em up mixed with a sort of "Dark Souls style" where parry and dodge play a crucial role if you want to stay alive... it's challenging without being frustrating, I'm really loving the gameplay.The art is awesome, music and sounds also are pretty good. Everything looks polished and well thought...Young Souls seems to be a real gem, a fantastic indie game.PS. I don't understand why many seems to criticize on the profanities... I mean, teenagers do swear a lot, especially when talking with other teenagers. Since the main characters are always together, and often speaking one to the other, it sounds pretty natural. Yeah sometimes it may feel a bit too edgy but...isn't "edgy" a pretty common adjective fitting for teenagers? ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I am not really a fan of beat-em up games. While I've played some every now and then, going back to the original Streets of Rage, they all typically boil down to 2 strategies:	• Instead of approaching enemies from the horizontal axis, approach the enemies from the vertical axis. Almost no enemy attacks the vertical axis, so this is likely a guaranteed safe way to deal with enemies. 	• Another strategy can involve equipping a weapon with long range so you can initiate your attacks sooner than your enemies do, making it relatively easy to not take damage. While the above strategies do work against REGULAR enemies in Young Souls, the developers have designed all the BOSSES around parrying such that you can't cheese the bosses and you really have to master them in order to beat them, which I really appreciated.First, let's describe what the core gameplay of Young Souls looks like. You play as two characters: Jenn and Tristan. They can both be equipped with different weapons and armor and you can switch between the two at any point. You have a normal attack, charged attack, a rising upper, jump attacks, and various weapon abilities (costs mana). You can also jump, dodge, block, and parry in order to avoid enemy attacks. All in all, this is a pretty solid foundation for any action game.In the beginning as I was playing Young Souls, I was hoping the combat would be similar to Devil May Cry. I.e. I would be doing various combos in order to defeat enemies. However, you can't really create combos in Young Souls. The combat is more like God of War in that you can only do pre-determined combos. Besides, the enemies don't have enough health for you to do any elaborate combos on them. Instead of Devil May Cry, the gameplay is more like Dark Souls in the sense that it's more methodical and focused more on the defense then on the offense.So as I mentioned, Young Souls in unique for a beat-em up game in that it has parrying (at least, it's the first one I've seen). The way parrying works is that if you block an enemy's attack right as they're about to attack, you'll parry them which will cause you to recover a bunch of mana and freeze time for everyone around you for a few seconds, allowing you to get a decent amount of damage in. More and more games have been incorporating parrying, but not all of them succeed. This is because even if a game has parrying, if the reward for parrying isn't high enough and/or it's more reliable to avoid attacks in other ways (e.g. dodge, block), then having a parry in your game doesn't matter because players likely won't use it. Thankfully, Young Souls is designed to really encourage players to use the parry. This is because bosses can basically auto-dodge/block your attacks to some degree. The only way to stun them and reliably damage them is to parry a certain number of their attacks (e.g. kind of like the poise system in Sekiro). Obviously, this forces players to master the parry system, which requires players to master the bosses they face. I really liked this.Now, the parry system isn't perfect because apart from bosses, you don't really need to parry. This is because against regular enemies, the most effective way to deal with them is to get a two handed weapon and use the charged attack, which will damage enemies around you in an AOE. I.e. why parry 15 enemies 15 different times when 2-3 good charged attacks will take care of all those enemies? Not only that, but while the developers encourage players to use the parry system, you can still beat bosses without parries (though it'll take longer) by using a hit and run strategy. While the parry system isn't nearly as refined as something like Sekiro, Young Souls has a pretty good one and it's enjoyable all the same. I am perfectly happy dealing with enemies a certain way (i.e. two handed charged attacks) and dealing with bosses a different way (i.e. bosses).There's a progression system in this game, and it's decent. As you beat enemies you'll get experience that will cause you to level up and increase your stats. There's unnecessary fluff with this system in that you can only level up by going into your room to sleep, and you need to play certain mini-games when you get "fitness tokens" from levelling up. Sleeping to level up and fitness tokens were completely unnecessary and only served to get in the way of the enjoyable gameplay in my opinion (i.e. I just wanted to stay in the dungeon and keep killing enemies instead of repeatedly exiting the dungeon to increase my stats). There's an equipment system where if you defeat enemies and open treasure chests, you can get various weapons and armor to equip. This was done better, but it's still pretty average. While it was exciting to find new weapons and armor near the beginning, after a while I simply stopped caring since I quickly learned that the key was to equip the weapon/armor with the best DPS/stats.There's a story……but I really didn't like it. Jenn and Tristen are on a quest to save their adoptive father from goblins. Relatively simple story…. But the game tries to take it a step further by making you feel bad for killing goblins and how they're living beings just like humans. The game's writing simply isn't competent enough to pull this off. The main problem is Jenn and Tristen. While I myself did start feeling bad for killing goblins as soon as the game pointed it out, Jenn and Tristen DIDN'T. So very soon into the story, I was thinking that Jenn and Tristen are total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It's not until like the VERY END that they changed their mind and were acting like complete brats/psychopaths leading up to the end with logic like "they started it" -_-. In my opinion, Jenn and Tristen should've more gradually started to change their minds instead of doing a complete 180 at the end.I would say Young Souls is the best 2D beat em up game I've played. Though of course, take that with a grain of salt since I typically don't like 2D beat em up games and so I haven't played a large variety of them. The developers were able to take a genre that's relatively simple in my opinion and add a lot of depth to it my creating a very well done parry system, along with an OK progression system. If you're a fan of 2D beat em ups or just action games in general, I'd definitely recommend Young Souls.

_childDocuments_.review: It honestly hurts to downvote this game - I remember playing the demo and thinking that this title had a lot of potential, but now that I see the final product, I think a fair amount of that potential is wasted. The big problem is just that the story isn't well written. While the premise is interesting, it is not developed in an interesting way. When the first major plot point occurs and the main characters find the magical world, they don't seem very surprised. Additionally, there really isn't any character development, either. Characters just show up, say what they need to say to continue the plot, then disappear. Beyond that, it's hard to say what the plot even is other than "There's a bad guy who's doing bad things". Of the couple of hours I played, most of it was spent dungeon-crawling, which is honestly the best part of the game. The gameplay is mostly solid, although it is frustratingly common for enemies to hit you when it felt like they shouldn't have, especially when you are fighting a group. But even then, the gameplay can essentially be boiled down to a simple blend of Castle Crashers and Dead Cells; in other words, it's good, but not exactly original. If all I wanted was fun gameplay, Dead Cells is much better suited, since it is a roguelike. The very thing that makes a title like Young Souls stand out is the story, which is unfortunately not very engaging in this case.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, Young Souls is a pretty decent game with a really nice art-style that reminds me a bit of Paper Mario. However, because combat is the primary part of this game and it has some serious hit-box problems (because it's a beat 'em up game and I've yet to find another in the genre that doesn't suffer from this problem), I can't really give it a solid recommendation. If you can forgive it's problem with combat or just look past them, you might have a really good time, but this one just isn't for me, and that's okay.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's super fun and challenging. Never felt like it was too unfair but never felt like it was easy. Especially in those special dungeons where you fight some stronger enemies for your level to unlock the better weapons and armour in the game. _childDocuments_.review: I liked the game as it reminded me of Castle Crashers and I had a friend to play it with (Pre-Expert Difficulty) . Review with pros and cons per line:- GEAR VARIETY: Chest piece for main armor and resistance, head gear minimal armor/weight, shoes for extra buffs, and various weapon types with bonus skills/specs.. BUT it's kind of annoying that you don't get access to heavier weapon types until like.. the last 4/5 of the game.- PLOT: There must have been a lot of thought put into the plot. Honestly, really like protagonist duo and relationship between ALL the characters. I think.. likewise to the prior, a pretty huge story bomb drops after Region 3.ALSO, there's a lot of dialogue...- COMBAT: There are a lot of weapon types, mobility, and the swap mechanic that contributes to the combat of the game. Very cool to swap between a fast character and a tanky one to keep in mind that you don't just live forever, you need to (or at least I needed to) coordinate myself to survive with the gear and lives I had avail. HOWEVER, this game doesn't have online multiplayer for some reason. Using the Remote function is really handy but if you don't have a good connection, combat will be less than ideal and you won't be able to really rely on blocking, dodging, parrying (all important mechanics) to get through zones.- Game Design: Very cool that they allow the speed up option for speed runners or.. depending on how you wanna focus on the gameplay. Also honestly love the style, character creation, and format of the game... My/our biggest quells were that there was a cut scene or slow-mo for every screen transition. It almost took us out of the game for all the times we had to wait or when the battle slowed down for critical hits. I think damage numbers could fill that role. - Convenience: Very cool that you can equip purchased clothes and gear from your player HUD. Slightly tedious that you can't equip/update gear if you're not in the retrospective area that you are active in. And kinda feel like its a really tedious process to have to go home to level up.. then GO TO THE GYM TO UPGRADE STATS. Should just make a gym in the kids' room.Finals comments: I wish I looked at the achievement list at the start, I would have risked my friendship for the highest difficulty to knock it out at once (Choose Expert Mode and adjust the settings if you must). The beginning message of the game cuts deep but the plot and parts of dialogue felt like they were for an angsty teen. Its dumb that you can speed up every non-combat scene but not the credits. The End

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like it, since the art is by one of my favourite artists, Xa Gueuzav. I went in and played it through, but there's something off about the game that didn't let me quite enjoy it. - The protagonists are edgy teenagers with an attitude (and a weird one at that). I get the edginess and all from when you're a teen, but it felt really weird and forced at some points. - There's no NPC that is actually memorable (like Baldwin), even when their designs say otherwise. Even the villains are extremely lackluster (except for one, who wants revenge after something we do). Not the goblins at the market, not even the gym lady nor the cool sneaker guys. They're just there and then they're forgettable -- like the junk store lady, which seems like she'll have more of a role and she just doesn't. So, in a sense, the writing was off and could've made some characters more memorable somehow, but didn't. The only really memorable one is the mayor's secretary and that's because of the attitude she has against our angsty teen heroes. - Combat feels clunky at best. Parry isn't even the issue, but the specials and some accessories: if you're ONE MICRA OFF THE LINE towards an enemy, you miss. Even when they're mega-chunky and your normal attacks would hit them, sometimes you toss a claw and miss... or do a big special move and miss harder. If that's how it felt on normal difficulty, harder ones are probably a nightmare...  - Music is... not there. Some ambience music is there, but it gets repetitive fast and you just want to get things done to get out of the map. Hell, I pretty much had a playlist on the background because it feels BLAH. All in all, a solid 4/10. Art is amazeballs, but the rest feels barely there.

_childDocuments_.review: From as much as I've played so far, the game can be enjoyed as a single player experience and could be a decent co-op dungeon brawler through remote play (there is no online co-op). The game devs want you to master parrying which is unforgiving because the timing is very tight on the attacks especially during boss fights since it's almost required to do real damage to them during their stun phases.Thankfully the devs were thoughtful to put accessibility options to make combat easier or harder as you please.All in all, despite a very steep learning curve, the game can be pretty fun especially with a second player who is willing to remote play with you. The story so far has not been very engaging though.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with the good stuff. Young Souls is consistently fun. The combat and progression are very satisfying, with many different move combinations that can be performed on enemies, equipment with different abilities and different ways to spec your two characters allowing for different playstyles and strategies. I turned my Jenn into a nearly unkillable heavily armored tank that pulled herself around the combat scene using the electric hookshot, and my Tristan into a super fast ninja glass cannon using a combination of speed sneakers, knives and all-strength to deal massive damage to most enemies. But I still missed out on all sorts of builds! Even though I never used, for example, two-handed swords (the most common equipment type), the game never felt neither grindy nor too easy to me. I liked the tag and assist mechanics too.The visuals are amazing. The animation goes hand in hand with the combat with how satisfying it feels. The goblin designs are funny and the protagonists are adorable, despite the game's attempts to pass them off as arrogant teenagers. You can dress them in all sorts of clothes you can buy in town - perhaps too many for the length of the game, even. I like the sets of the mansion and town, although they felt extremely underutilized. The dungeons themselves were less interesting, but I liked that there were side areas you could explore to go for additional loot.Unlike some players, I actually liked the plot. The goblin enemies are shown as actual people with ideals and fears. Every boss has its own personality, which shines through during the cutscenes and before combat. Neither side of the conflict is entirely in the right, and I appreciate that Jenn and Tristan start having doubts about what they're doing half way through.The music is a bit underwhelming, though. It had kind of a Kingdom Hearts vibe to it. It's not bad, but I'd have appreciated something more metal while genociding, er, most of the goblin species.The game is chock-full of all sorts of cool little mechanics and features. Unfortunately, many of them are underutilized. For example, there's a moped you can use to get around *fast*, which is really nice to use but almost immediately becomes obsolete since you can both fast travel and sprint and the game's "overworld" isn't that big. There's a whole currency whose only purpose is to buy clothes, which yield no status benefits. There are NPCs in town you can have conversations with, and at first your relationship with them seems to evolve but they never really go anywhere. There's a potion shop, but there are only three types of potions, and only two of them are even useful. There isn't even a stamina potion! Come on!Some of the game's utilized, fun mechanics are in need of a little rebalancing. The special weapon artifacts that give you special or ranged attacks are a super cool idea, but they are also quite overpowered! Though I suppose they allow the player to bypass having to become *too* good at parrying, which can be a little frustrating with some enemies. I would have liked to have a greater variety of knife weapons. Some status effects are basically useless in single player. And finally, let's get to the real bad: Bugs. Like all players, I've encountered various bugs. The game never crashed for me and all bugs would go away with at worst changing areas/fast travel, but there were annoyances like equipment selection paginators that would stop working, players falling off the level into void beyond, parts of the player models disappearing, conflicts between hats and helmets, etc. These bugs are getting in the way of what could otherwise be an excellent game.There are also some stupid design decisions that could easily have been patched away. For example, you can't select a different potion before the cooldown for the current one ends. When not in combat, dashing still uses up stamina and potions still have cooldowns. Why?? Characters also still have to tag out to recover yellow HP while not in combat. It's just wasting people's time.When you have a game as fun and solid as this one, it's criminal that more effort hasn't been put into sanding off those edges. You can't play the game without noticing them. But it *is* still a fun game, regardless, and I'm glad for the time I spent with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This is a charming and beautiful game with a lot of good ideas, that was regrettably spoiled for us because of its inconsistent and unsatisfying difficulty. We're no stranger to difficult games - we have soulslikes, Cuphead, and roguelikes under our belts - so just BEING difficult isn't a problem. The WAY that Young Souls does its difficulty is frustrating though.Broadly, enemies in Young Souls fall into two camps: enemies that flinch, and enemies that don't. You can deal with the former variety however you want; just keep attacking, and they won't be able to trike back. The latter is where the game falls apart. Enemies' attacks come out extremely fast, and it's rarely possible to sneak in an attack before your enemy is able to respond and punish you, whether you're attacking from neutral or trying to punish them on the wind-down from their combo. To make matters worse, lots of enemies block attacks from all sides, so even doing that is impossible.This means that you need to start on the defensive and land a parry in order to open an enemy up. Parries have very narrow and awkward timing and felt finicky throughout our playthrough. To make matters worse, many enemies, especially bosses, require multiple parries in short succession to break them open (a la Sekiro's posture system), so you need to lean entirely on this weak system for several of the most difficult fights in the game. This was brutally unfun, not just because it was difficult but because it was unpleasant to interact with.There's a lot to like here - the art direction is fantastic, the illustrations are great, and there are tons of fun characters to meet and goodies to find. Unfortunately, the way it's designed its difficulty makes that a slog, especially in the latter half, and I would take back the time I spent finishing it if I could.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 50/50 on this game. On one hand it is a pretty decent beam em' up challenge and at the same time it can be the total opposite. Pros: Combat system is addictive (You can switch weapons and armor to focus on going faster attacks with less damage or slower attacks but massive damage, there is a lot of customization you can do. I was able to wield A colossal sword with fast attack and it demolishes enemies.)Rarity (Each weapons give a unique build depending on what you do, you have knifes, swords, hammers and axes each one has a unique purpose. Plus certain weapons have higher rarities than others so depending on what weapons you get you could have a fun or worse time. It makes you think about investing instead of blindly investing.)Levels (Originally I thought this was a bad idea but it works brilliantly, instead of most fighting games where leveling up is mandatory. You sometimes have a choice to fight bosses at lower levels, meaning you beat the end boss at level 5 and still have a chance at winning. Not a huge chance but a chance none the less. It is a bit annoying needing to sleep to level up so I usually avoided sleeping to just play through the game normally.)Zones (Each area increases enemy health by 2x [Except the last] So be prepared for even tougher enemies as you go down into the abyss. Each one has their own elemental damage effects and each one is harder than the last, not to mention secret bosses with keys and even hidden shrine bosses of Yarlanda.)Yarlanda (Easily one of the hardest bosses I have went up against. Each time you defeat Yarlanda she gives a special weapon each weapon is what you face up against. From Longswords to a Meat Clever. She is the toughest boss I faced through my entire playthrough forcing you to play both defensive and offensively.)Bosses (There are quite a lot of unique bosses in this game and a majority provided quite a challenge, more than I was originally expecting, some are reskins while some of the hidden bosses are made completely unique. It is impressive how much effort was put in to make each boss unique.)However while I like what this game can do...I need to state why I dislike certain parts.Enemies...(For a unique variety of Bosses, enemies aren't too unique which is fine most beat em ups do a style like that anyway. However hit boxes are a pain, enemies can easily overwhelm you and if you aren't parry or blocking right back afterwards you can be stuck in a animation loop, since there is no invincibility frames. It can get really annoying especially on later levels)The First Part of Zone 4 (I won't spoil this part in detail so I will only tell you what it is like. On a Balanced run of the game this section is doable on harder sections it is way more stressful. You NEED to equip weapons that can deal damage to certain enemies and you don't get a say in this. You are shot right back down to 1 Point of Health and you have to go through 2 long hallways and an entire boss with these cursed weapons. While I beat it barely first try, I could imagine it could be the breaking point of the game for some other players. It is way more unfair than anything else in the game. The 2 Weapons you can equip is a sword, which you can at least equip a shield for but the other is a colossal weapon which you can block a single strike. WTF)Story (Now I understand story can be something really hard to perfect but it is so uninteresting. It has interesting moments [mostly near the end or at boss fights] but other than that it is about trying to reclaim you father from capture. So you will have huge chunks of nothing but combat then interrupted with story at one room before a boss fight, trying to make you care. I found the shops to be the most unique characters as they offered something, still sucks that 3 Shop characters are really only included in the story ONCE. There is a lot of problems I am not going to address, as I gave up halfway throughout the game but if you like it all power to you. I found Yarlanda to be a more interesting character than everyone else.)Side-Content (There is no sub stories or sidequests, which is good but that lead me to search every nook and cranny of the game to find keys. Which unlock chests which make the game feel way easier overtime. Which I like exploration but it never has a character talk about it or give hints to the player, so usually I find myself getting lost on where I am going. Maybe I am following the storyline or it is a side boss. Needless to say, I think they should have added something so a player didn't feel a bit lost.)Finally SummaryI will still give this game a 7 and recommend you try it. If you want a challenge or you want to play with a buddy go ahead, it is a pretty decent game I think a lot of people can find enjoyment in. I would just wait for discount personally.

_childDocuments_.review: My brother and I played through this game together, and it's great!The combat is challenging, timing based, and really rewarding to get good at. There were some really cool synergies that my brother and I tried too, in terms of gear loadouts and playstyles that would go together well.There's lots of cool looking gear to collect, and like I said above, you can mix and match to make some really powerful builds that synergize between the two characters.The story was pretty good too, nothing in terms of moral choices like some RPGs, but pretty good none-the-less. The dialogue was pretty mature without any super cringey moments, and a bit of well-timed lightheartedness sprinkled in.The only problems we had with it were that we both had to be using the same type of input device, otherwise the inputs would go super wonky. That being said, we played on controller and could each have our own button bindings, so that was nice. We also got a glitch where the screen would go almost pure white when we leveled up, the menus could just barely be made out, but the cursor would be plain as day. It didn't happen on every level up, but it was annoying when it happened because we would have to save, quit and re-launch the game.Picked this up on a Steam sale and don't regret it at all. Had a great time with it. Totally worth the full price too if it's not on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It will take about an hour before you stop getting constant tutorial popups and cutscenes, if you can hang around that long you'll be introduced to the main gameplay loop.The art is great, the characters are immediately lovable and the writing is outstanding but I still really, really felt the drag of the introduction and almost gave up waiting for me to be allowed to play the actual game so if you're looking for something that you can hop into and enjoy straight away this will frustrate the hell out of you.If you're looking for something with great atmosphere, story and gameplay that assumes you've got a bit of time to settle into a groove with it, definitely highly recommend Young Souls. The art is so good that I think most players with doubts will give it just a little bit of extra time anyway so if you're on the fence its almost certain something will win you over eventually.TL:DR; Its a good game that prioritises telling you a story over letting you get stuck into playing the game at the start. If you want to be spamming combos within 5 minutes this is not it, if you want what feels like a visual novel with some streets of rage and a little bit of grinding for gear then this might be your perfect (and weirdly niche) game.8/10 for me so far.

_childDocuments_.review: It's truly a shame this game didn't blow up-- or at least hasn't as of yet-- because it is solid. Visually, mechanically, and conceptually, it hits all the right notes. Tons of side-scrolling action, collectible and upgradable equipment, different abilities, effects and styles to play with, some very light crafting and economics, and the occasional story break. Everything built to enhance and keep the gameplay fresh.For one, I can already tell it isn't going to be a 100-hour game. Whether that's a bad thing will depend on you. (Personally, these days, I'll gladly take a game that can hold my attention for its entire 10 hour span over a "40-hour epic" that fades into a "20-hour to-do."For two, the price is may be a little steep. I would absolutely recommend it at around $15. Even $20 even doesn't sound too unreasonable. The issue lies in the co-op: if you and a friend want to get it, it's the difference between $30, $40, and the current $50. Oh, and there is the minor issue of in-game profanity. Nothing against profanity in games or in general. It's just in this specific case, it seems to be sprinkled in completely unnecessarily, as if it were written by a high school kid. The "mature language" is there, but the content, themes, story, dialog... it's all pretty "fun for all ages." Not a deal-breaker, just an odd inconsistency.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10A fun and enjoyable side scrolling beat-em-up with light RPG and slice of life elements!The story follows twin siblings as they try to save their father figure from a horde of goblins who have secretly been living under the earth for untold eons (hollow earth confirmed) and are now hellbent on taking over the surface world. That basically sums up the plot as the story serves more as a motivation for playing the game rather than trying to grip you with a narrative.A lot of the characters are visually memorable with the standouts being the twins and the goblin bosses themselves having the most spoken lines that gives a grain of depth to complement their unique looks. A good amount of the dialogue in this game is written well enough to not overstay its welcome and drag the game's momentum to a crawl (there would even be times where the twins could care less about the lore and just cuts the dialogue short just to get to the action).Speaking of looks, you (and a friend if you are playing coop) are given a good amount of customization options for the twins that range from purely visual changes with the street wear options to mechanical changes like armors sets and expensive sneakers that affect their stats to allow you to tune them to your preferred play style. You can also alter the stats of the twins by going to the gym in the game's town to train them through a series of mini games depending on the stat you want to improve.Combat is the main focus of the game where you (or with a friend) go through a series of interconnected levels fighting through gauntlets of enemies to collect gold, experience, items, and to progress the game's plot as well. It's a typical beat em-up with some modern mechanics thrown in like a stamina and parry system, as well as a weight system that affects your dodge roll depending on what kind of armor set you use. The weapons you choose to wield and the armor your choose to wear greatly affect the way you play providing a good amount of variety to how you wanna deal and receive damage throughout the game.The game overall is not that challenging on normal difficulty but I don't think that is detrimental to the experience at all since the combat and exploration feels really fun and encouraging enough to set your sights on getting overpowered by exploring all the dungeons and collecting all the upgrade materials to buff up your weapons and armor.Overall this is a fun action game that doesn't demand too much of you to get an enjoyable experience out of it. If you like beat-em-ups and Saturday morning cartoon action and antics then you should give this game a try!

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty fun. I feel like it would be better co-op, but it's not too bad in single player. You swap back and forth between the two as a sort of "extra dodge" and "extra health", and there's even an mechanic where you get some health back on one twin while they're on the bench. It has a great aesthetic, and there was clearly a lot of work placed into the art style and animations. The combat is fine, mostly, though it annoys me so much that enemies only strategy is to quickly roll behind you to try to flank you as quickly and as often as possible. Fair enough, there's not exactly a wealth of strategies available, but it makes combat really irritating since then you have to dodge roll to get behind them again, and you're basically compelled to fight on one side of the room at all times. Although, you can game the system a bit by purposefully facing the wrong way, which will make enemies dodge roll back where you want them.Overall, pretty fun if not exactly deep. Worth a look if you enjoy hack and slash style combat and charming visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Tried to use steam share to play with my wife for local co-op. The game doesn't have a function to lock the mouse in full-screen so the game would click outside of the screen leading to neither of us having control of our characters. Overall the game seems fun but it would have been nice to have an online co-op built in and locking the mouse to the game application. Steam share also lead to quiet a bit of input lag too for the second player. Loved the overall look of the game the dialog seemed a little off at times, just awkward phrasing, but it still was enjoyable. If the multiplayer issues get addressed I would 100% come back and play again, playing solo you shouldn't run into any of these issues, I can't recommend the game for online multiplayer but if you are fine with local co-op on the same PC or just playing solo it should be a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine. I didn't feel like I could get into the story at all and ended up skipping every scene. So I was basically just here for the gameplay and the style. It was great on those fronts.I didn't enjoy the parry mechanic as much as I wanted to because it became obnoxious when fighting multiple enemies that include larger ones as they cover the attack signals of enemies behind them. I also found myself comboed by too many enemies at some points which just felt cheap and like I should have had some more invincibility after being hit.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great beat 'em up with RPG elements and has fantastic style!The story is fun and filled with entertaining dialogue that fits right in.Co-Op mode has a great integration since even in Single Player you can customize both characters; only difference is in Co-Op each player controls one while in Single Player you control both.Loot is both co-op and competitive in the sense that both players get the same loot; but you can only equip armor and weapons once for both characters which makes sense.The areas are fun to run through and enemies are generally fun to fight.My only real issue is that for items it uses the "modern" cooldown system for items. But you don't get infinite amount of those items like in Diablo III. You still have to find or purchase potions but you're limited to how often you can use them. This is extremely frustrating because if I can rip through 10 potions the punishment is if I lose, I don't get them back; even if I win I lose 10 potions.I hate games that use this method to increase difficulty; when it's really just increasing frustration. I've had to hop off the game multiple times because of not being able to use items to clutch a boss fight because I had used an item at the beginning of the fight. And the cooldown feels extremely slow even with reducers.This wouldn't be terrible except lots of enemies, especially bosses; can just throttle your health into the ground in a couple moves. If you get stunned as well they basically clear your healthbar before you can move again.Beyond that it's a great game; I just despise item cooldowns.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: An artful genuinely quite enjoyable beat 'em up side-scroller that suffers more than a few mildly annoying bugs & glitches and some mild game balance issues. Most of which is readily and easily remedied.As well the game is somewhat short and relatively lacking in certain areas. Certainly room for improvement.The art direction in the game is absolutely magnificent. While the explicit style may not appeal to all, the character designs are distinct and varied and the cinematic work is unique, interesting, and dynamic.My first playthrough I 100% the game in just over 7.5 hours, and my 2nd playthrough I was able to beat in just under 4.5 hours on the hardest difficulty. Suffice to say the game is not terribly long.Personally I could care less about the story, but that's not to say it's necessarily bad. I think the general themes and idea's are endearing however the plot is pretty simple if not altogether predictable. That being said I feel the game is a 'game-first, story-second' sort of game, Which is fine and probably for the best. Speaking of gameplay, it's reasonably solid out of the box, but is best enjoyed with the use of accessibility settings which allow a player to enable/disable certain game functions, and as well tweak difficulty elements to ones liking, such as enemy/player attack speed, enemy health, attack-canceling, etc. In my opinion this is almost necessary as the game has some mild balance issues sort of across the board. Not a deal breaker per se, but as stated previously the accessibility options are a must to rectify those issues.On a vaguely related topic the game also suffers from various mildly annoying UI animation issues. Put simply certain UI animations/confirmations just take way too long to complete. One specific example being the level-up animation which sits on-screen for probably a  6 seconds for no reason. As well a similar issue with item pickup confirmations. As petty a complaint as that may sound, that's just one example of the sort of minor annoyances some might encounter. Again, not a deal breaker per se, but I can see something like this souring a persons experience, like stray hairs in an otherwise competent soup.As well the game has its slew of assorted bugs and glitches, such as falling through the world or getting stuck in objects/terrain when using the teleporter, UI elements getting stuck on-screen, items becoming unable to be picked up, etc. Most are easily remedied by either fast-traveling, loading into a new stage, or other simple fixes, so nothing really game-breaking.Lastly the game lacks any NG+ options, challenges, or collectibles. While not strictly necessary of course as the game is plenty enjoyable without it, but with how quickly I was able to experience everything the game has to offer, it's hard not to want for more. Of course I wouldn't necessarily count that against the game, but it would certainly be a welcome addition. Personally I really want the Pajama's worn by the twins when sleeping as unlockable clothing cuz Jenn's PJ's are adorable. But that's neither here nor there.At the end of it all, I do think the game is reasonably enjoyable for $25 despite any minor annoyances or issues present.But here's hoping the developers tweak/patch what needs, and possibly even add additional content.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Really addicting and quite enjoyable. I get the sense that each weapon is different and that I can "connect" with some really well given my play style, and others just don't jive with my attack and defense strategies. One downfall that needs to be addressed: Too much accumulation of human dollars and there is nothing functional to spend it on in the game once you purchase all the clothing items from the downtown area in the game.....I was able to purchase all the wearable items like during the first 2 hours of the game...so it's annoying and kinda a waste to farm for items in the levels by breaking boxes/crates etc., other than to obtain health, mana potions.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Quality 2D combat, natural and witty dialogue. The characters are memorable visually but not as much by name which is definitely the preferred way to cut it. The art direction is really nice to take in as you play, the settings above and underground are all fun to look at and interact with. The story is simple and sweet all the way through as well. The fast forwarding to get through cutscenes and fast travel is really creative and gives you something to look at in between play. I can't talk about the co-op gameplay but the tagging in and out mechanic allows for rapid swapping between two builds to help kick ass in fights.Definitely worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Solid co-op action game - not sure if I'd play this alone.  Note: To let the second player join, you need to go to the "Controls" menu while in game - kind of awkward.Straightforward campaign took us about 9 hours.  Some fun decisions about gear and play style (though balance seems off on a few items).  Not terribly difficult, but you have to pay attention and be careful. Frequent checkpoints reduced frustration of a few tough enemies.  More strategy/variety than most brawlers, and the two of us ended up playing quite differently.Story didn't really grab us, but game lets you fast-forward through talking/animation.  If you removed the random swearing this game would be rated E - not sure what they were going for in terms of tone.Anyway, this is a solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game, especially for 2p local co-op. Only some minor annoyances (e.g. camera focus and blurring in some scenes). Very nicely presented, with unique style. The writing is alright, but uneven.My main gripe is that it is shorter than I would've liked. The basic gameplay loop would have worked for a much larger game. Both the content and plot could have been padded. Of course, in a way it is a good sign when you wish a game was longer, but some of the non-dungeon combat systems seem like they could've been more meaningful (going to the city, gym training, conversations etc.). From "time played" it appears I and a friend played through the game in 24 hours, but we had to grind a bit and retry certain fights a lot due to (let's be honest here) us not being all that great, so the game can be completed a lot faster.There's plenty of difficulty/accessibility options so it's probably playable for most. In addition to that it's possible to take detours to find better gear and gain levels to make other routes easier.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Styling beat em up dungeon crawler rpg.  think Diablo 1, but side scrolling beat em up.  Great concept, neat story, dialogue iffy in places with no much time spent developing characters really.  The game is really front loaded so you think you're about to strap in for an epic journey with plenty to unlock, but I've completed the game in 16 hrs with 100%.  Lots of curse words in the dialogue too.  Not sure why they were so determined to push for a MA rating.  And even at $30 bucks...it's a decent deal (prolly worth $20 as far as content goes).  I recomend this game cause it's fun, though I was more impressed in the beginning.  lots of weapons to choose from, but mostly useless really.  I ended up being the game with a fully level pair of daggers that dropped n the first dungeon.  Also, only four dungeons in the game.  The game is worth playing.  hopefully they will release a sequel, or another game with similar gameplay but more content.  that would be ideal.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This game is tough and fun. Git gud at parrying and try not to die. It's also a decent length. Not too short, and not too long. Would definitely recommend playing with a friend for extra fun. :DYoung Souls starts off story heavy with some funny writing. If you're worried about it being too story focused - it luckily takes a back seat after the 1st hour, so you can enjoy your brawler gameplay!
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: An exceedingly well polished 2D Brawler with RPG elements and stunning art direction. The game mechanics are solid and the controls are nice and snappy. It doesn't reinvent the wheel or anything, but why should it? A full completion will run you between 7 and 10 hours depending on your difficulty. 100% Achievements will probably take you a bit longer for the gold farming ones. Some gripes:- Weapons upgrades in the early game feel meaningless -- upgrading early game weapons is almost not worth it as they easily get overshadowed by the next tier's unupgraded form. A few weapons are exceptions but for the most part, you'll be swapping to new weapon drops after a guardian fight almost unanimously.- One of the areas forces you into 1-hit-kill scenarios. Granted this is a very short section (approx 15-20 minutes). The enemy difficulty winds down a tad but it's not a very fun section.Some neutral points : - Low replayability value. Beat it once, maybe go another round if you want to go max-difficulty if you didnt the first go-around. I'd LOVE to see some DLC content for this with rogue-lite elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: So overall, Young Souls is a very good game for the beat ‘em up multiplayer genre. Even at full price I’d recommend it to those who enjoy games like Castle Crashers and Streets of Rage. The story might not be anything too special, and maybe the tone of the character’s dialogue might turn some off, but you’ll be engrossed by the entire charm of the game’s visuals, there’s quite a lot of depth here for different play styles whether you play solo or multiplayer. The constant progression of leveling up, getting new equipment, and discovering alternate paths and challenges really make the game for me. Young Souls is an easy recommendation from me.Check out my full gameplay review video for Young Souls. _childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game so far, fun mechanics and great visuals make for a very good time. There are a few things to throw out there that I have noticed as far as negatives go, but none enough to change my review to a cannot recommend one. As far as combat goes it is very very easy to get stuck in animation and become unable to dodge out of the way or shield. I have lost a lot of runs thanks to doing a perfect parry, but because my sword swinging animation technically wasn't done it did not happen. There are also a lot of bugs, none of which for me have been game braking, but there are certainly a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Young Souls

_childDocuments_.review:
As orphans, Jenn and Tristan's life path brought them to a mysterious scientist, who took them in and cared for them as his own children. But one day, he disappeared under very odd circumstances.

While searching desperately for him, the duo found a hidden cellar and the Moon Gate portal, transporting them to a dangerous parallel world where goblins thrive.

Your adventure begins as you fight to bridge these two very different worlds.

Young Souls is a gorgeous 2D brawler meets story-rich action RPG. Fight hordes of belligerent goblins, level up with hundreds of weapons and accessories, explore, and journey between worlds, as rebellious twins battle their way to save their foster father.

name: Operencia: The Stolen Sun
detailed_description: Play in VR for ultimate immersion. Though not required, virtual reality immerses you in a way offered by very few turn-based RPGs. So go ahead – look around and enjoy the scenery…but do keep an eye open for the ruthless enemies awaiting the perfect moment to ambush as you marvel at your surroundings. About the Game Zen Studios’ modern homage to classic first-person dungeon-crawlers takes you to the land of Operencia, an unconventional fantasy world inspired by a faraway land referenced in countless Central European folktales. An old-school turn-based battle system combines with inspiration from unexplored mythology to offer an RPG experience that feels unique yet also familiar. An unknown force has abducted the Sun King Napkiraly, leaving Operencia in a state of perpetual darkness – and eventual doom. From hidden royal tombs and cursed castles to an ascent up the World Tree to reach the Copper Forest of the Land of the Gods, explore diverse settings throughout the far reaches of the land…and beyond. Each location boasts its own unique atmosphere, visual style, level design and puzzles, and many take place entirely outdoors. Operencia is home to an intriguing mix of unexplored mythology and fantastical versions of actual historical locations (e.g., Deva Fortress, Balvanyos) and characters (e.g., Attila, Seven Chieftains of the Magyars), all coming together to form one cohesive new gaming universe. Several of your own seven party members take influence from heroes of forgotten tales told hundreds of years ago, such as the brave knight Mezey and Sebastian the Dragon Slayer. Along with a deeply strategic turn-based battle system full of spells and special skills to execute, tile-based movement encourages thorough exploration of each area. For added challenge, turn on Cartographer mode to plot out each of the 13 maps yourself. How many secrets will you find? Breathtaking hand-drawn cutscenes and fabulous 2D character portraits bring the story to life in a style not easily compared to any other game. More than 30 colorful characters are fully voiced through top-tier performances authentic to the game’s Central European roots. Explore 13 diverse, puzzle-filled levels Defeat more than 50 enemy types Switch between 7 fully upgradable – and memorable – characters Robust difficulty settings allow you to select options such as limiting saves, implementing permadeath, and disabling auto-mapping to create your own Stunning visuals powered by Unreal Engine 4 An epic orchestral score composed by Arthur Grosz Fully 3D environments, enemies and objects, plus high-fidelity advanced effects with dynamic shadows and lighting AAA Indie production quality and polish with top-tier voice acting, soundtrack, cutscenes and writing

_childDocuments_.review: Operencia is a 1st person dungeon crawler when it comes to gameplay, however there's one major difference between this game and the usual metric of the genre: the focus of the game. where's usualy these games are centered around exploring, combat and progression the main focus is here is clearly the characters and the story. the production quality is actualy quite impressive. pretty much every dialogue line is voiced, there's even a narrator and most of the voice-acting is quite good (there are some misses). what is even more impressive is the amount of voiced lines. not just the plot is fully voiced, but your party comments pretty much on everything, either with one-liners or full on conversations. find a locked door? comment. find a new enemy? comment. combat? comment. rest at a camp? comment. you get the picture. the writing is quite endearing and pretty upbeat most of the time. adin well crafted ingame cutscenes and hand-drawn (very pretty) stop-motion-movies and you get the most story heavy 1st person dungeon crawler...like ever. while the grafic won't win any prices, the art-design is top notch. enviroments, 2d portraits, 3d enemy models (especialy bosses) and npcs are very nice to look at. the presentation just flows very well. the soundtrack helps to carry the mood of the game and the ambient work is phenomenal (from nature sounds in forests, to cracks and rumbels in caves and dungeons).where the game is a bit lacking is the depth of other similiar games (like Wizardy or Might&Magic). character progression is based around attribute, 3 "skill-trees" per character, which consist of active abilities and passive buffs. there's also kinda like a perk-system. crafting evolves around "brewing" things in a couldron, which works through unique recipes you gotta find. it's kinda like a neat little minigame, design around a puzzle approach. everything neccessary is here, it just looks/feels a bit lacking compared to the big names in the genre.combat is turn based, which i personaly prefer to what some other games did. the game world itself is not just stunning, but also filled with secrets, metroidvaniaesque backtracking and puzzle (which are nice little diversion unlike what Bard's Tale 4 did, it's nowhere near as puzzle heavy...thankfully).i can fully recommend the game. you get alot for the price and most (nearly all) of it is defintily quite competend. however the negative i got to mention is the way your party evolves: you get to create 1 character after the tutorial/story-introduction, choosing between 3 classes. from there on out you find new npcs in a linear manner. these npcs kinda follow similiar "classes", and while offering more variety than your own innitial choices there's not a lot you can change build wise. so if you don't choose a mage at the beginng you will be stuck without a mage for quite a while and even when your party gets full: you get a druid and a healer, but no dedicated elemental mage. so if you want the "best" advice i can offer you: choose a mage. if Operencia had more depth when it comes to build variety and character progression it would definitly be an absolute highlight, but as it stand it's a very good 1st person dungeon crawler, which focuses on story/characters and will net a great a playtrought, but lacks in replayability. i usualy avoid all the "epic"-exclusive games (even the timed ones), but this one is my guilty pleasure....sue me ;)
