_childDocuments_.review: This game is MUCH better than I expected. I was ready for a mildly-serious turn-based dungeoncrawler with decent fairy-tale graphics.This game is actually one of the better classic dungeon-crawlers I have played. The story has much more emphasis than I expected and is decently well-told. Even better: The overall designs and ideas of this game seem to stem from folklore, the game is much bigger than is to be expected and the combat is actually decently challenging and fun. Just make sure to pick a mage on your very first playthrough to speed initial fights up as those can drag on a little. This is a VERY competent game with snappy humour. Now let's just hope for an "Operancia 2" down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: A must buy, but also a buy during sale.A game with a well-crafted core and with an awful lot of rough edges.Solid combat and exploration, good puzzles and downright gorgeous visuals.The main story is loosely cobbled together from over a dozen different myths and fairy tales, so don't expect too much of it, or of the companion characters who spend most of the time bickering instead of developing their personality or backstory. The world is colourful and has many cool things for the player to explore, and that's what matters.Combat can seem infuriatingly unfair at times, but the solution to all such problems is merely to backtrack a bit and level up more, because in Operencia big numbers make all your troubles go away. If not, try resetting you characters' skills and attributes.The puzzles are also problematic, since some of them have completely arbitrary solutions, while many others are made much harder and rather frustrating because of the grid-based movement and the games first-person view.If you want a game with nearly limitless character development options and hundreds of hours of non-linear content to explore, then go play Skyrim for the 20th time.But if you're looking for a game that ask you to help a lesbian stonemason chain the soul of her dead wife, makes references to a certain owl with and imposing copper bodypart, and lets you chill with the soul of Attila the Hun, then Operencia is definitely for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember when you were young, sitting on your grandparent's lap as they cracked open a worn storybook with the spine barely hanging together? As they turned the aged pages to reveal colorful, whimsical illustrations that despite the age were beautiful and mysterious? When they spoke in the accent of their home country and told the tale in a way that made the world feel alive with wonder and possibility?.............. Yea me neither, but if I did then Operencia would definitely remind me of that. It's a decent dungeon crawler with a magnificently crafted atmosphere... the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic 1st person dungeon crawler. It's not possible to grind, once you kill an enemy it stays dead, but you also don't need to as long as you explore and try to find all secrets.Speaking of secrets, for the most part you can't find all secrets in an area the first time around, so you need to make use of the fast travel system that opens up after a while to go back with new abilities to find new secrets and treasure. That's really nice.It's also really nice to see a dungeon crawler with heavy focus on story, it's been a while since we had one of those. The story is good, the characters are phenomenal, and the exploration and combat is great.There are however some weird quirks, such as digging up a secret treasure pops up the message "Alas! Treasure!"... it should probably be "Aha! Treasure!" or something that's not "Alas" since that's used to express pity.Anyway, it's a solid experience. Anyone who enjoys dungeon crawlers will probably enjoy this one. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: It has it's moments but falls short of being a good game by having some absurdly annoying enemies. The setting and story are both rich and interesting. Music and graphics are both good. Characters and puzzles are both well thought through. There is a huge amount of loot and enough variation in skills to keep progression entertaining. But so many fights just up being beyond dull. Fights are slow paced and nothing feels like it has an impact. Enemies drain energy and endlessly take hits so you end up hitting basic attack fight after fight. And there are a lot of fights...With some simple balancing this game could be great. But until that happens I would keep away.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is balanced well it feels like it has the right amount of battles, the puzzles are all unique, interesting and easy enough to figure out, thankfully you don't need do be a genius like some other games expect you to be to solve the puzzles.As long as you explore everything and discover all secrets you can get max level. And you can get upgrades to eventually be able to have 4 healing potions, so reviews saying you are limited to one are not correct.I like that you can respec easily as much as you want, so you can figure out what works best.I played on normal difficulty without any hard settings and did not find any of the enemies or most bosses too difficult as a mage and with Kela you can beat them quite quickly however I found 3 of the bosses quite challenging to beat.Gate to the underworld boss.Optional secret boss, Boband the final boss.The voice acting is mostly good, but some of it is terrible like they were having a bad day and couldn't be bothered. The bad is that there are only 3 playable classes and I usually go ranger, hunter, rogue type in games but hated the hunter in this game. It feels pointless to play as anything but mage. As you don't get a mage in your party until halfway through the game and you get plenty of warrior and hunter party members and the hero mage gets the best most damaging abilities in the game that only you can get as the main character. The party mage doesn't get those really good skills and is more of a healer. I don't like it when games make 1 class more essential, overpowered and enjoyable than the others. All classes should feel necessary and essential.What they say in combat is a bit too repetitive and cringeworthy.I liked the story, but at the campfire it was kind of boring at times with the group waffling on to the point  it was causing me to zone out and not hear anything they were saying.Overall this is a good enjoyable game which I loved exploring each area.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I feel conflicted writing a review to this. First of all, if there would be an middle thumb I totally would give it, but since recommendations on steam are binary I had to choose or I had to shut up, all in all the game wasn't that much bad to justify a thumbs down I suppose.The game has as many flaws as it has strenths. Graphically it may be the most impressive First-Person Dungeon Crawler I have played so far, great lighting imaganitive locations, it's like a dark fairytale.  The characters are lovely, even when you never explore them too well. It's pretty on the surface regarding interpersonal communication and characters like Joská and Mezey were written with a clear dynamic in mind which is explored in lots of tropes yet, but they're able to entertain the player even if you can't take them too serious. There are some plot twists towards that make the story more interesting, which is something the game pretty much lacks for most of the time and interesting narrative. I have to appreciate that somehow all you experience between the several locations is somehow interconnected, sometimes a bit too well, but in the end you play a pretty classical hero tale from start to finish, where your goal consists of salvage a sword for most of the time. There is one minor antagonist that keeps reappearing but overall there is not much surprise going on until the end, which can draw the motivation form the player if you aren't that much invested in the gameplay which focus shifts more and more towards the repetetive combat the further you progess.The turn based combat is simplistic but fast paced but I have to lie if I would say it never overstayed it's welcome. The problem is that it lacks depth on many ocassions starting with the illusion of character customization. After the intro you're asked to create your own character out of a few preset portraits, you can choose 3 classes and set attributes as well an permanent perk, but all of it is already layed out so that you're not really have much options unless you go for something totally stupid like an mage who has invested a lot of points in strength.Unlike in other First Person CRPG's like that, your avatar has an set personality and voice lines. I see no reason why they couldn't come up with an original design ditchting the customization part at all. I suppose you somehow have expectations in that genre that you need to fulfill even when it really not fits the narrative. In that case the game pretends to have more depth than there actually is and this translates to many ocassions.While you have a lot of equipment in the game and 3 skill trees you there is little you can do to prepare for the inevitable battles, so there are a lots of enemies that can inflict status effects to you, a lot of them make you lose control over your own characters, usually and typical JRPG's you're able to hold against it with items, like as long you're still in control of one of your characters you are slowly able to regain the control. This is hardly possible in this game. There is nothing that helps you to protect from said status effects. There are some skills that allow you to remove them but every skill in the game has cooldowns, so you can use them only once for x turns. That doesn't really help when later enemy groups conists of 5 enemies where 3 of them keep reapplying a "panic" effect where you're characters randomly attack eachother. The only thing that allowed me to survive these encounter is retrying until the RNG was in my favor and there is a loooot RNG, the outcome of the battle can drastically change and quickly become very onesided, this is something where I lost several times my faith on the game that tactics really matter.I have to admit that I played on the hardest settings possible except for permadeath (which is stupid in such an long and RNG-heavy game) so I suppose if you play it just normally you might not encounter the same issues, but then it suppose it generally becomes to easy since there is a lack of variety in enemy design.So there are overall 12 locations in the game, but for every location you may encounter only 1 or 2 enemy types, one of the worst offenders here is the "copper forest" where you encounter just the one and only enemy type over and over again. This enemy can draw out all your magic and there is little you can do to prevent it, so all you do is becoming more ressourceful in not refilling your energy as far as you could and spamming instant-kill at the beginning or normal attacks if this ain't workin because of bad RNG. Enemy groups are organzied and you encounter most of the time the same formation of tanks that redirect attacks, casters that summon and inflict a lot of damage and or "DMG" in the back or front row. The formation system, where you inflict different damage on different lanes on the field compensates for that at the beginning with seemlingly interesting choices, but it gets too old too fast, in the the end the approach stays the game from the beginning to the end.There are also minor annoyances that I would call "design oversights" so for example your party is predetermined and consists of all kind of class archtypes... except mages, so if you wanna go wild with spells, well you better have chosen a mage at the beginning or you have to deal with something half assed like Csilla (priest) or Kela (supporter)You also start the game with an character who is specialised in inflicting poison. Too bad that for the first three dungeons almost every enemy is immune or resistant to poison which renders this character pretty much useless for most of the time, you instead builing up his strengths you literally end up spending all his points in strength, because he becomes way more useful as an simple dmg dealer. Status effects overall seem to be only useful on the enemy side. There is one effect that is highly useful (silencing), everything else you can't apply to 90% of all enemy types, you better not spending points in useless skills like "sleep" or "charming". On the other hand, you can build up a high resistance to poison, but in the end after the second location, no enemy ever inflicts you with poison again, this is totally ridicilous, at the point you finally have a good resistance to poison, you no longer need it.Despite beeing a dungeon crawler there are a lot of convenicence option, like gaining exp even for deceased characters and getting fully healed when reaching a new level. These weren't necesarry in my opinion but I suppose they are were decided you can't run in a booby trap since enemies in the game are limited, they never respawn. In that fashion you also alllowed to reskill you characters, at every point with no penalty. This is were convenience has gone a little bit too far in my opinion. Allowing yourself to relocate point makes your decisions less impactful in best case you just redesign your party for every encounter in the best way possible (and even then you're not having that much options) in the end the skill tree's are so minmal you end up with having all skills and most of the passive stats bonuses anyway. Planning ahead does not longer feel rewarding if you can correct mistakes at any time. There is a lot of puzzle solving at the beginning but later in the game it becomes overshadowed by too much lengthy combat. Also the puzzle design is sometimes clever enough but sometimes questionable. It's these kind of puzzles were you do get not much hints and have to recognize a pattern for you own. So at one point you have to light light candles in a certain layout, but how do I know which candles to light up? Well  look at the ceiling there is a pattern above. So the solutions doesn't require much deduction, it's just you have to stumble on the solution by accident"Relics" are also just contextualized actions pretending to be a feature like items in Zelda, another example for pretending depth.Reached maximum text size ok i'm done! xd

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: I have very little time in this game. I was worried about loosing my chance to refund it if I lingered. I passed through the first dungeon and reviewed my 3rd party member (the fighter) before deciding to stop.Summary: While the characters, setting and world were interesting, the gameplay itself was underwhelming.The characters I met seemed interesting and I wanted to learn more about them. The artwork, design, and voice acting are good, even great. However, while a game can be beautiful, but if its not fun to play then I don't think of it as a good game.The talent trees were short and abilities were uninteresting. In combat you have your basic attacks,  a "defend" skill that recharges some of your resource bar, and various class skills that spend your resource. The Skills have some variety in what they can do, but there are too few to make what feels like a character with a sort of theme. Also the term "skill tree" implies branching paths of options. This game does not offer that. Each of the three "trees" a class has is a single linear path of 3-4 skills that have passives that are bland stat boosts.Another complaint is the character builder at the start has a "race" option that is really just an illusion of customization. You have 4 options, each which is good for a specific class, and one that gives a small boost to all stats. So for each class you can choose between the "ideal" race that most benefits your class choice (intellect for a wizard, dex for a ranged, strength for melee), the "jack of all trades" race which is a weird thing to include in a game where there is little felxibility in character builds, or one of the 2 other races that don't give you any stats of value for your class.I think this could be a great game with a rework of the talent system. However as it stands I don't find it fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Was It Good? 3/5Did I Like It? 3/5Basically Might&Magic / Legend of Grimrock, just not quite on par. Polished game, functions well, only 1 map bug (returned to a locked chest icon to find the chest unlocked). These games never have a real story and Operencia runs a Hungarian folklore mixed with generic fairy tales, and it is fully voiced, but you have no choices to make. If you've ever played Might&Magic it comes as a shock that you have to stop listen to a story. The characters are also fleshed out, and the voice acting is 90% good (not you Mezey). Also not you Kampo, which is why I never used you in the game. There are Grimrock-type puzzles sprinkled on almost every level, and they are generally good at breaking up the sameness of dungeon-crawling. The 2 real downsides are unbalanced gameplay, and an uncomfortable inventory/skill page setupOverall the game is relatively easy if you pay attention to your stats and skills. Quite a few skills are useless in certain situations (such as bringing fire spells to fire resistant enemies) but luckily you can reassign attributes and skills at no cost. I tweaked characters stats and skills on every level. Without doing this, enemy difficulty between levels can SEEM to be a massive step up. It helps that there are very few different enemy types per level, and there is no cohesion between different types either.Bob (he has 10,000 hit points in a game where end level mobs had 250) was easy, but the end boss took me 12 hours over 6 days to defeat. It was the only battle that you had to slow down and plan each turn and hope you won the RNG battle. I only won because the Succubi didn't charm or silence me until halfway through the fight. The main game is fun - the end battle is bloated and so one-sided it was just not fun. Every enemy group has the initiative on you. They attack first. That is, unless you get behind them to ambush you. Always ambush enemies if you can, it makes all battles 20% easier.The inventory/skill page setup is unlike most RPGs, as if things are not intuitively in the right place on the screen. You press “I” on the keyboard and you go into a full party inventory system, while you really want to use the “character” screen so you can compare weapons & armour stats. You never use “I”. Pressing “C” doesn't go into the character screen, its “P”. If you press “I” and then press “P” it doesn't switch to the character screen. You have to click the “left” arrow button. Changing party members also gives you the option to strip all their gear. You always accidentally press YES, then realise and have to remember what combination of gear you had with the character. I stopped changing my party halfway through and used the same 4 characters.In all, if you like these types of games this is must-buy. But expect Grimrock x 80%. Also, go with mage. Bob is weak to poison. Kampo is useless. Mezey is grim but your most important character. Every level is fun apart from the World Tree. F*** the World Tree.Was it good? 3/5Did I enjoy it? 3.5/5

_childDocuments_.review: The environments are stunning, the character progression satisfying, the adversaries often challenging, and the story is well fleshed out. There's a lot to explore and the lore is rich, interesting and engaging. And sometimes the writing and dialogue will coax a smirk or a giggle out of you. A great game to sink your time into. 8/10But...The game can feel very scripted. There are no randomized encounters, no randomized loot, and every shred of character XP is deliberate and limited. So you are pretty much forced to seek out every encounter in the game and traverse every inch of the terrain, or else your characters will start to suffer. The game will allow you to return to previous levels with new abilities (metroidvania style) and you should be vigilant about doing so, as some of the better gear and XP is gotten through this backtracking. Although the grid based movement feels out of place and "clunky" at first, the games puzzles and challenges utilize the feature well, and you'll soon understand why the developers went in that direction. Overall, the whole experience is gorgeous, very tight, but quite inflexible.

_childDocuments_.review: I am an old guy that was very excited about this game. I cut my teeth playing the old Strategic Simulations AD&D games like Pools of Radiance, and Operencia seemed like the realization of my hopes and dreams for those games realized. I started it up, and played through the prologue. There is clearly a lot of depth here, but I did not find it intuitive. While this is not explained, I now realize you start as max level characters, and use abilities freely, even if they aren't explained well. I actually ended up dying to the "boss", thinking that perhaps that was actually supposed to happen, and because I had not understood how to take care of my party, as you are just expected to figure that out. I had actually gone into the boss fight with everyone at very low health, and the idea of trying to struggle through it again wasn't appealing. I started again, and didn't play the prologue. Made a mage, lots of points in intellect, because that's how I've learned to play mages in these games for years. Entered the dungeon, cast some spells, quickly found myself out of mana. Spent the next 30mins swinging my sword, missing or being resisted 9/10 times. It immediately felt like a slog, and my reaction after a half hour of play is I should start over, as I have probably already messed this up. My experience is probably not the typical one. I'm probably just an old dude with overly nostalgic hopes and an expectation of having my hand held in the beginning of a game. I've no doubt many people have and will enjoy this game. I found it frustrating, unintuitive, and laborious.

I was worried the first few battles on how long it was taking to kill a monster, but your party can really hang in a combat.  The damage scalling is well done and skills both recharge and cost energy points to use.You create one character and gain others in your party as you go.  But each character progresses the story and adds to it as you go, so it really works well in this game.  You do not get a magic user until later in the game though, and not a dedicated mage at that either. _childDocuments_.review: It may have taken over a year, but Operencia has now arrived on Steam. I remember adding it to my wishlist a long while back, but the game then entered an Epic exclusivity deal, so it wasn't until this past week that I was finally able to check it out. Was it worth the wait? Well, that's debatable. So, for those that don't know, Operencia is a first-person dungeon crawler done in the same style as the classics. It's got the turn-based combat, the fantasy aesthetic that dominates the genre, and the movement that's restricted to a grid. However, the camera is done a bit differently here. Instead of being locked to the four directions, you can actually move the camera around freely.The game takes advantage of this in its numerous puzzles, which range from tedious to just okay. There are some solutions that are immediately obvious, but require a bunch of steps to complete, and then those that are a bit more random. In fact, the randomness of some of the puzzles was a bit annoying at times. From finding very small objects scattered about the map to stepping through a phantom wall that's hard to see, it can often be frustrating if you're going at it without a walkthrough. Of course, it's not all of the puzzles that are like this, but even the better ones are decent at best. Fortunately, as the game goes on, they become less important in favor of the combat.As mentioned previously, the combat is done in a turn-based manner, with party members moving along an action bar dependent on their stats. The game has an extensive skill and ability system that make up the bulk of each character's available moves. There are party buffs, single-target spells, moves that hit all enemies, and a number of other cool abilities. One of my favorites was a gambler ability, which, when activated, targets an enemy with a 50% chance to instantly kill them at the expense of having a 40% chance for my own guy to die in the process.Otherwise, the combat plays out just like you'd expect from a dungeon crawler. Although there are a lot of abilities and skills that can be learned, the base combat is simple enough that it doesn't ever feel too complex. If anything, the management of equipped items is more complex. If I had to complain, I would say that the lack of animation skipping can make the combat a bit slow at times, but that's more a quality of life issue. The overall combat is nothing special for the genre, but it's not bad either.However, if it wasn't obvious already, where Operencia really shines is with regards to its presentation. Everything from its graphics, to its animations, to even its 2D artwork is all excellently done and with some pretty high production values. I was very impressed when I loaded up the first dungeon and began wandering around. There was great use of lighting, an incredible amount of detail, and high-res textures all around. This extended into the combat as well, with a decent amount of enemies to fight all with their own unique animations.Then there's the audio side to the game. The soundtrack, while not the best I've heard in the genre, was nice and matched the game's atmosphere well. What really sold the audio though was the game's incredible sound design. While the soundtrack may have matched the atmosphere, the various sound effects and general ambience of the sound design pretty much made that atmosphere. It actually feels like you're wandering through a forest, an underwater castle, or even a dark cave. In fact, I hated exploring spider-infested caves because of how well it managed to capture that atmosphere. It was some excellent production values all around and made the genre feel much more "modern" in a way.Given all of that, I'll give Operencia: The Stolen Sun a light recommendation. While the puzzles can be tedious, the combat and exploration are fun enough that it's at least worth the look if you're a fan of the genre. Granted, they're not the greatest said genre has to offer, but combine that with the excellent presentation and cheesy, yet fun storyline and you have a decent overall package.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game, after playing for only a few minutes i couldn't stop until i got 100% completation, your party chat a lot and they give you very useful information, even tips on how to solve the puzzle sometimes, the characters have great personality and the voices are great, the male main character sound smug as hell, i loved it.The combat was just my kind of thing, turn based with all characters being mostly unique, enemies can give you quite a good challenge at parts, and the graphics are just beautiful, the world tree level is one of the most pretty stages i've seen in these dungeon crawler games, too bad my GPU couldn't handle everything at maximum.I had only one thing that i didn't liked as much, the puzzles were way too many and mandatory, some were easy but others took me more time than i would've liked (that dragon puzzle at the last dungeon, jesus). _childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence when I first played the game. One has to get used to some of the mechanics such as energy (needed for special attacks) doesn't really increase unless you use a "guard" or rest at a camp (which requires wood).Character creation: do a mage. - don't even consider not doing this. there is no real TRUE mage as companion found later in the game and they only come toward the end.Puzzles are ok , loot is good - always something to upgrade but semi confusing. They have a system where it tells you how it impacts your offense, defense or magic - and for some reason it will list an agility item boost my attack much better for my fighter -- which I would have thought strength would have done this.Battles are a lot of luck.  Example: a few you go against a pretty hard mob(lots of hp / resistances)   that will re-spawn other monsters to help - if one of those are a healer  -and you are up against a very hefty monster with a lot of hp  you are done - you cannot  - wipe - restart.   Want to target the healer first you say?  Most likely you cannot if a monster uses taunt and forces you to attack a specific monster that just taunted.  Golems come to mind here when you hit them (they have a few hundred hp - and your dmg is 2 - 5 per hit).Attacking: numbers are typically very low numbers - it's like you are throwing spitballs at them.Puzzles: most are ok - some are insane (thinking of a trial that has completely random tiles being zapped that you will fall through. You have to navigate a 10x3 or 4 grid and get to the other side - and the tiles which disappear has no pattern at all.  Fall in and you are back to square one.  Google this and see how many frustrated players are out there voicing how they have uninstalled the game because of this puzzle.  the developers apparently seeing this decided to make it easier and say if the game shows you keep falling they will add another second before the tiles disappear LMFAO.  My advice actually make it have a pattern that the typical person may be able to determine.Stats:  confusing in a way.   The typical stats toward certain classes you are used to - well not so much here. Initiative:  seems like the monsters you will fight will always have more than you.Monster Resists:  i have never yet had a silence spell work on any monster. It says it does - but they cast w/o any issues.There are areas in each dungeon you cannot access yet. I am on the fence with this mechanic. On one hand I am wondering did i miss something - only to find out (after using google)  it will require an ability I get much later in the game.  Game makers want us to think through these dungeons - but put in this type of mechanic which forces us to go online to discover after hours of searching and thinking something can't be done yet.The worst and this imo is the biggest sin of any game maker - is making the final battle way over the top difficult to the point of FRUSTRATION.    You invest hours into a game to just reach a point where it's so frustrating the game brings no enjoyment.  That is the end battle. _childDocuments_.review: First impressions: I've played my fill of grid based games from the old days of Eyes of the Beholder, Might and Magic, Wizardry and Stonekeep, etc.  There are a lot of modern titles like Grimlock 1 and 2, The Fall of the Dungeon Guardians, Dungeon Of Dragon Knight and Vaporum that have got a lot of love from the Steam Community.  Operenica fits right in.  Good music and graphics with a little different grid based design that works well with the gameplay.  I also liked at the beginning that besides turn based combat you would do a little more than just drop a stone on a lever or pull a switch.  It's a breath of fresh air to start out finding an item to put out a fire or move multiple mirrors to create a beam.  When you do get into fighting there's a lot of deadly options to choose from rather than your standard "slash" and the animations look good on screen.  I'm looking forward to spending more time with the game and delve deeper into what else it offers.  So far a lot of fun to be had. :)Update - 3 hours in and I can say this one is a keeper!  Top shelf audio throughout the game play, beautiful environnments, excellent music, very good level design with a little bit of retread if you want to go back later and get other goodies left behind.  My only small gripe is that I would like to have seen more creativity with the level designs.  At the beginning we had a nice puzzle adjusting the mirrors and it falls pretty flat in the variety of design back to level pulling and door unlocking.  I really liked the underwater areas but there could have been some missed opportunities here as you could have had random small whirlpools that would move around and possibly strike the group or undercurrents that randomly pushed the characters a few grids off depleting their air, etc.   All  in all though it is still very, very good.  The game is taking me back to the days of playing Lands of Lore.  That's really the feeling I'm getting while playing and that's a great thing. :)Newest update - 15 hours in and just finished Chapter 7.  Very surprised that only 17% have completed it with game almost out for a month but the game just keeps getting better the further you go.  I'm in the Copper Forest now and it is a beautiful steampunk like world.  Very impressed with many of the levels because they have their own fresh and unique look so gameplay is constantly new on every level.  Couldn't recommend this title enough.  :)Final update - Completed the game at 30 hours.  For the most part I had a lot of fun playing it as stated above.  The only problem I ran into was the Copper Forest.  While one of the most beautiful areas it was also the most deadly.  I found that against a party of 5 steam robots if you didn't strike them all well in the first round it would likely have deadly consequences for your party.  There were other comments about this area in discussions and I think the difficulty, even on Easy, could have been lowered a little to help.  For some reason this area is even harder than further levels and I wasn't the only one to notice this.  I even took on 10,000 HP "BOB" and beat him pretty easily too.  For those that do brave further and reach the end don't lose hope in the final battle.  It's a little deceptive thinking how much HP you will have to take the dragon down when in reality it plays out a little differently and he can be beat.  It took me about 3 times on Easy so it can be done. :)  As of right now there's only 6.1% on Steam who beat the boss.  If I can do it then you can too. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, It's a dungeon crawler blobber. Is it good? Yes. Is it revolutionary? Not really. In this rare genre, it's worth to play anything that comes out but no, its not the only reason to pick it up. After playing most of current games from this genre I was surprised that devs managed to sneak in some new things. First of all, there is a backtracking to previously visited locations through "teleport". And there is a merchant. And team composition with four active members and 3 in backup so you can switch them back and forth, depending on the situation. The turn based combat is just fine. Most blobbers are trying to solve the problem with hit and run tactics and this execution is really nice. On the other hand, besides tutorial a lot of things are unexplained. There are icons for the "elements" but I at some point I didnt really know what are Underground spells because the icon didnt tell me. Few skills simply didnt get to work. I was using correct weapon, on the correct line with correct attribute maxed and still didnt manage to deal more than 10 damage every single time - and I tried a lot. And the mentioned attributes are a mess. There is no description of what does what really. Strenght boost physical attack but it also boots health. Same as Vigor. But Vigor doesnt add much else over it so I basically threw everything into one main damage stat for every characer and managed to get away with it rather easily. While it might sound harsh, it didn't really kill my joy. I wouldnt bother about it but yeah - I would be happier without those issues. The plot is fine. Some really cool moments and decent worldbuilding. I love this genre because all of those games, even bad ones are extremelly immersive. Maybe because of the first person view, maybe because of how the world is constructed. There was always this kind of enclosing and claustrophobic feeling. In Grimrock where you had to travel through Tower or Fall of Dungeon Guardians where you are climbing up from deep prison. Previously mentioned fast travel kind of killed it for me. It was fresh but I wouldnt cry without it. But there is one thing that I absolutely loved. Little conversations that my characters had with each other. They were great, witty and funny. How the rogue guy was making fun of typical knight that didnt get how the sarcasm works. Or comments there were always dirrected to the fourth wall. Or comments about cliches in this genre - amazing! My final rating is 7.5/10. Good job guys and I'm waiting for the next one!

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a RPG fan, and do you like turn based combat, that is also a dungeon crawler, whilst exploring multiple levels, with a deep story? Then buckle up because Zen studios has released Operencia, the stolen sun, an amazing mix of story with all the rest of elements mentioned above. But do you want more of an in dept review  of what this gorgeous game has to offer, then I will be more then pleased to tell you our experience! What we liked: The general story: without going too in dept about this, there is an amazing story line behind the game. All throughout the different quests / levels, you experience your team telling you more about why they do certain things, and just generally interesting dialogues between them. This mixed together with other elements like narrators, makes it feel like a fairy tale you are experiencing first hand The music and sound effects: Zen studios has really gone out of their way to add the most complete sound design to a RPG game which I played in the last year. The music has a nice calm mood to it, that adds to the mythical experience all throughout, whilst certain basements / castle levels have a more mysterious vibe to them. Overall an experience to remember. The graphics and scaling: This game has amazing artwork packed into a complete overall package. Zen studio’s also nailed the fact that it supports 21:9 aspect ratio for a more immersive experience! The characters are custom drawn, every level has more and more different artwork, and the scenes are overall gorgeous to view and stair upon. The combat: In this game during your turn based fighting system, there is a surprising amount of dept that is linked to it. The game has a mana system that only allows you to cast certain spells for a certain amount of time, and if you want to regain mana during a fight, there is a tool, but that skips the combat for that character for that round, overall a good system! The difficulty options: this game allows you to choose how hard you want specific elements of the game to be, and all throughout the saving spots, it gives you the opportunity to modify those parameters in case you feel like it was too simple for you. A great touch that more developers should implement in my opinion!What we had mixed feelings about: Pc support: this game is a clear example of super great game but that has been made to support a controller. On mouse and keyboard, the gameplay felt a little odd. For example, having to define multiple keys to turn your head, whilst also only being allowed to move left right, and forward. But after about a level or so, I connected my controller, and it started to feel a lot more as it should, rather smooth and intuitive gameplay. The only remark I have about this is that I found myself making movements, and running against walls, because I am used to the fact that I can move freely and diagonally, but after getting used to the tile movement system, this was not really an issue anymore. What we didn’t like: to be honest nothing.. Overall impression: this game from Zen studios really shook up my perception about turn based combat and dungeon crawlers in generally. I was blown away by the gameplay, smoothness, and quest lines, all whilst being hooked to my pc screen to continue playing. For which I grant them a solid 95% score. As mentioned above, the only point I wish I had seen was that I could play it with mouse and keyboard, but then again, being able to lay on your bed whilst playing this gorgeous game is also just an experience to have! Want more reviews like this? Check us out on lifeisxbox.eu!

_childDocuments_.review: TL,DR OVERALL RATING:  7.5/10 if you like RPGs of this style, maybe 6/10 if you're just a fan of RPGs in general.  I'm writing this immediately after finishing my first playthrough and am already planning to start a second with some of the hard-mode options on.If you enjoy other grid-based first-person dungeon crawlers (such as Legend of Grimrock, Vaporum, Might and Magic Legacy, etc), definitely give this game a look.  Perhaps look for a sale if you're on the fence, but I'd wager that you'll enjoy Operencia well enough if you got a lot of playtime out of games like the ones listed above.The environments look very nice, and are quite varied in feel.  You won't be suffering from Grimrock 1's "oh look, more floor to ceiling stone walls" mindset.  The sound design wasn't spectacular, but didn't offend me any...I mostly didn't notice it much.The dialog can be a little unnatural feeling, and the voice acting would be decent for early 2000s but is not up to par for today's standards.  I ended up skipping a lot of the voice acting by mid game or so.The story (as far as I gather) is drawn extensively from Hungarian mythology.  It wasn't terribly compelling to me, but it was interesting at the least.  If you can at least enjoy hearing about foreign mythologies, you'll probably be entertained enough at this story to keep going.The combat and character build mechanics took a little while for me to get used to and figure out how to optimize.  This was probably my biggest draw to keep going with the game, which is typical for me as I'm very heavily a mechanics-driven gamer.  There's 5 main stats you can increase, an an entire page of sub-stats that these main stats have effects on.  It can take a bit of experimenting to pin down how important each of these things are, and how to approach each character's build based on their available skill trees.  With that all said though, a HUGE boon to this game is that you can respec any characters stats or skill trees at any time (outside of combat) with no cost.  Your fire mage hits an area with heavily fire resistant enemies?  Pop 'em over to the lightning tree for a while!  Realize that Joska's starting investment of agility doesn't really fit his skill trees of mostly strength and intelligence skills?  Pull those points out and make him more potent in the areas where he shines!  I did a decent amount of respeccing until I came up with builds that worked well for me (especially with one specific character later in the game who is just awkward to build).Unfortunately, the menus can be a little unwieldy (especially in VR) and the inventory management annoyed me quite a bit.  I think there were a few too many items that were too similar that end up cluttering up your inventory.  Plus you don't get access to a vendor to unload stuff you don't want for longer than I would have liked.  At the very least, you can always buy back items you've sold in case you find a use for one of these side-grade items later on.  And money never presented any major concern for me.Another minor draw is the VR support for the game.  I only played maybe a couple hours of my first playthrough in VR, but it was definitely a neat experience.  Being able to look around the gorgeous environments and actually see everything all around you is pretty fantastic.  However, I felt like the controls for the menus in particular were very detrimental to actually playing through the whole game in VR.  With the amount of time I spent fiddling with builds and stats and gear, I can't imagine having done all that through the VR controls and still enjoying myself.  I don't know if I would recommend this game to play entirely in VR, but if you happen to have the capability already, definitely give it a try for a little while.

_childDocuments_.review: To put it in gaming terms,  is a grid-based, old-school-style first-person dungeon crawler with an interesting, though not entirely unique, turn-based combat that emphasizes on tackling enemies based on the rows they are on, whether they are in front, middle or at the back. There are some pretty devious puzzles to solve; some epic dragon slaying to do, and an engaging story about defeating the creatures of the Underworld that are just spilling out onto the surface and sending them back to where the belong! Despite having a historical/mythical theme, I also really like that the game doesn't just use the typical, well-known stuff. Instead, you'll get to "meet" historical figures (with a dab of fantasy) like Attila the Hun as well as mythical heroes from lesser known legends. After all, a game doesn't always have to be about "King Arthur" or "Alexander the Great" to be great.For someone who isn't very familiar with dungeon crawlers of this format, however, I personally find some of the puzzles in this game to be rather tricky.  Maybe this is just me though! - I got stuck at a puzzle in this vid but I found the solution not long after...  :P Will make a part 2 then!- Also, note that although there's a bit of a stutter while streaming, the game worked great and smooth on my end.+ Devious puzzles - make sure to check everything, making sure you don't miss anything that you can interact with. + Strategic turn-based combat. You can get a nice "Ambush" advantage just by approaching an enemy from the sides or the back and the different rows where enemies are positioned (front, center or back) really changes how you build/develop your characters' skills. You'll want to have a team that has skill sets that provide a nice coverage of all three rows.+ Good voice acting that can sometimes be rather heavily accented. + Really nice graphics, especially the art during cutscenes and the underwater dungeon! + I enjoyed the story a lot so far, especially the good-humoured banter between Attila and his queen. + Lots of secret loot to find - make sure to explore every room/grid!+ The first-person dungeon crawlers that I've played has really rigid movements whereas this is not the case here. However, it does feel weird to be able to move along the grids so quickly - can be a bit dizzy sometimes. Works great when you're trying to ambush an enemy.+ Considering the hours you can get out of this game, the game is well-priced. Worth getting the game at full price but if money's a bit tight for you because of the virus, you can always add the game in your wishlist and check back in when there's a sale.- The game crashed at the end of my stream. Not sure what happened though! Operencia: The Stolen Sun may not be everyone's cup of tea but it's definitely an old-school-like dungeon crawler that's worth playing. The game's gorgeous as they go, and it does have really great writing. Being a fan of turn-based strategy games AND dungeon crawlers (though I usually prefer dungeon crawlers/action RPGs like Grim Dawn, Diablo, Torchlight, Path of Exile, etc), I love how the game uses row-positioning to ramp up the challenge a bit, making combat feels "fresh" and different. So, my verdict? Operencia may be an indie game; it's incredibly well-polished and it's fun! Buy it and play it if you love first-person dungeon crawlers or turn-based RPGs.

Turn based RPG so you won't be doing too much with your hands anyway.Doesn't hurt the immersion too much.Gameplay itself is very old school RPG.  If you've played Entrian Oddyssey it sort of reminds me of that game.  Heavy on mapping.  It's tile based so you can traverse the entire level while only looking at the map.There aren't too many RPGs in VR and this is one is pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: This game lets you pick whether the single character you can create is a Warrior, Ranger, or Sorcerer.I had to return the game for that reason.  It's just entirely too basic to be entertaining.  I expected to create a party with a variety of classes that could fill different roles.  I expected something that improved on Eye of the Beholder.Instead, most of your party will always consist of NPCs.  With only three classes in total, each of which fills a required role in combat, there are only a few viable party compositions.Maybe it was designed first as a VR game and mouse-and-keyboard play was secondary.  Maybe it's targeted at a young audience despite taking an archaic grid-based approach to dungeon crawling.  Whatever the cause, there's nothing to plan around or customize.  Each class has a talent tree, but each rung has an obvious best choice, which is no choice at all.If you're in it for the story rather than the gameplay, Operencia has a striking visual style and an interesting world, but it's a mile wide and an inch deep.

_childDocuments_.review: I love blobbers. That being said, I kind of hate this game. I don't mind premade characters, but I do mind when they babble endlessly about how SUPER DUPER POWUHFUL they are, like 7 year olds playing with action figures, all while treating you as if you are the idiot in the room. "MY GUY HAS A DEMON IN HIS SUPER HAMMER! OH YEAH? WELL MY GUY IS A KINGSLAYER!" And while that idiotic babble about how everyone you run into happens to be a superhero who know all the kings and queens and gods and whatever isn't screeching in your ear , they're screaming at you about how to solve every puzzle you come across. "GEE, LOOK AT THAT. IT'S A HOLE. IT LOOKS LIKE A HOLE FOR A GEAR. THERE MUST BE A GEAR AROUND HERE." Then, later, "I WONDER WHAT THIS GEAR IS FOR. I KNOW! THIS MUST GO TO THE THING YOU SAW EARLIER! WHAT IF YOU TURN IT CLOCKWISE! OH BOY, THAT DID IT!" Kinda defeats the purpose of having a puzzle, no? Also, whenever they'e happy about something, they say, "Alas! What a good day!" Like... what? That's not what "alas" means. Oh, and the art design. God, don't get me started. The short version is that their company is very clearly cynical as hell, has no interest in cultivating any kind of aesthetic that could be described as something other than "marketable pap for idiot children." It looks like WoW. Yeah. It's hideous.All I could think throughout my entire playtime was, "God. Shut up. Why won't they shut up? Who WROTE this trash? Oh look, another treasure chest full of so much money and ugly looking crap that I'll never want for anything. Why even have money in this game?" As for the combat: I play on the hardest setting and could pretty much just tie a blindfold around my face and click randomly and win. It's so dumb.Perhaps I am the idiot for buying this game and not refunding it after all.If it weren't for the writing I'd give this game a "meh" 4/10. Given how childish and idiotic it is, mixed with the awful aesthetic, I give this a 2/10. It's so stupid. SO stupid.Avoid. Do not buy. This is not the blobber you want. There is nothing interesting, innovative, or fun here.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this through multiple times on Xbox, and bought it on here to support it, though I can't see us ever getting another at this point.The music, artwork, characters and their banter, are all great. Level design is fun with different puzzles, hidden areas, and a small amount of fast traveling back to find hidden areas or items you couldn't get before having the right ability/tool. Turn based combat is good, but there are a couple of enemies later on that are just awful, namely one that drains your mana on a counter attack, and another that can confuse your whole party in one cast AND you can fight three of them at once, so no way to burn them all down in time. It is doable, though, as I've beaten the game on the hardest combat difficulty. Animations could be faster sometimes, when you're fighting 5 enemies at once and you have to wait for them all to go through the motions, I could see that frustrating people.My biggest complaint is that the thief/rogue class is entirely pointless. There are no full damage mages you can recruit, so going mage is great for AoE and a unique party setup. There's one warrior you recruit, but it's not a waste to go double warrior as they have the best single target damage with double strike, as well as high health/survivability. There are TWO rogues you get in the game, you can use them both at once, and your own rogue has no unique abilities, so why bother?Fun on first go, save a few fights, and it became a good comfort game I can go back to during a long week. Wish we'd get a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Operencia: The Stolen Sun is a somewhat simplified take on traditional RPGs, such as the Wizardry, Bard's Tale, and Might & Magic series.  Your party of adventurers will be exploring dungeons from a first-person perspective while fighting turn-based battles.The game begins with you creating your own character, but from then on you will be unlocking new party members as you make progress in the game.  You ultimately will unlock six party members, and once unlocked you can freely swap these characters in and out of your party of four active characters (including yourself).  Characters differ mainly in their skill trees; each character has three branches in their skill tree, with each branch typically representing a "role" akin to those in MMOs: tank, healer, support caster, damage caster, etc.  Skill trees contain a good mix of active and passive abilities, and your choice of abilities really does make quite a difference in how each character plays.The game is extremely linear, as you progress from one dungeon to the next, with a boss fight at the end of each dungeon.  You can go back and revisit dungeons you've already cleared to seek out enemies and secrets you missed the first time around, and the game provides a helpful counter on the map screen indicating how many chests, secrets, etc. you've missed.  The dungeons are not particularly large, but they are designed pretty well and are generally packed full of encounters, secrets, and puzzles.  Exploring these dungeons is definitely a highlight here.Like most modern takes on this type of game (The Bard's Tale IV, Might & Magic X, Lords of Xulima), there are no random encounters and enemies do not respawn; once you defeat a group of enemies, you can explore that area hassle-free to solve puzzles and find secrets.  Although I am not a fan of fixed, non-respawning encounters, this works fine in a linear game like Operencia.  You can reset and reassign attribute and ability points at any time, so you will never find yourself stuck with a subpar party.The difficulty level peaks early on and then quickly drops off from around the halfway point; this might disappoint players looking for a constant (or rising) challenge, but I enjoyed feeling increasingly powerful as the game went on.  It ends with a great multi-stage boss fight that isn't very difficult, but feels suitable epic.The game promises "a world inspired by Central European mythology," so I was disappointed to find that it's mostly your standard wizards and warriors slaying skeletons and dragons in caves.  There is a real focus on story and characters in this game, but I found neither to be interesting; the party constantly bickers back and forth like a bunch of elderly couples stuck together on a cruise around the world, and the script is a 50/50 mix of wordy exposition and zingers that are hardly ever funny.  Having said that, there are some nice environments in the second half of the game that look great and are pretty unique (the Copper Forest is definitely a highlight).Overall, though, I enjoyed my time with Operencia.  It's worth getting over the difficulty hurdle a few hours in and sticking with it.

_childDocuments_.review: The UI and experience are absolutely awful in VR. Opening cutscenes don't make it clear which way "forward" is, which is disorienting. Spawns a Windows Firewall prompt that can only be answered on desktop, which resulted in a glitchy pause screen over the opening (with sound effects) that I was _about_ to ctrl+alt+del out of as a softlock, before it sort of recovered itself. Opening dialog alternates between subtitled and not-subtitled. The game does not make it clear when you're frozen in place for a cutscene vs. when you aren't. Party members are invisible voices in your head. No debuff icons. No indication which party member an attack hit, unless you're specifically watching the turn order meter instead of the combat visual effects. Action prompts are not reliable. Enemy status text is Z-ordered in front of the enemy even when the enemy model geometrically occludes it, which is a bad and headache-inducing look in VR. A turn-based grid-based game in VR will always feel a little odd; that's okay, it's something of a novelty. But it would work _much_ better with a third-person camera, and a complete rethink of how to present information to a VR player. Most of the UI hovers in a flat plane in the "forward" direction, which sometimes becomes disaligned with the direction that combat is going in. It's got the exact 16:9 aspect ratio of a modern monitor, so this is clearly the screen edge UI of the flat view of the game. However, it's placed too close to feel comfortable and too far to the edges to be easily seen. A traditional RPG interface is difficult to design for VR; there are many different approaches and none of them are really satisfying, so it's a difficult problem to solve, but here it has also not been solved.Probably okay in 2D except for the lack of subtitle configuration and possibly opening-scene weirdness (I don't know what's VR-specific and what's a general part of the program's behavior). I feel like this was a sloppy VR conversion and there's a lot of _potential_ here but the UI needs to be completely redesigned.

_childDocuments_.review: Old school in spirit but a very nice looking game. I loved the beautiful artwork and level design reasonably strategic combat and creative puzzles, The game is pretty linear which I didn't mind. There are few jokes here and there that are mostly funny and the game is long enough to feel finished but short enough to not get to repetitive, definite must have for anyone who remembers grid based games of the old days. The only negative mention would be some puzzles (very few, not to spoil anything) that are quite annoying (if I wanted a puzzle game I'd get one) but the overall impression is still clearly positive.

_childDocuments_.review: As a dungeon crawler, this game is quite interesting, and the VR option (which I haven´t tried) makes it even more so, mostly due to the puzzles and the secrets scattered all over the different levels that are not as unique as they could, but all of them paint an interesting picture.Plot-wise, the game is clear, something has happened and the signs are telling you to go recover the Sun, the different characters form different stories that are connected. And in that regard, wanted to mention that this is one of the few games that explore Eastern Europe mythology making it extra interesting for those of us that know a bit but not enough.Exploration-wise this game is a shiny gem, due to the full control of the camera, making the secrets hard but not impossible to spot exploring everything is usually welcome, and since there are no random encounters, exploration does not become a boring task.Battle-wise the game is... unpolished. Initial levels are OK, but difficulty has many spikes that forced me to stop using the hunter MC since the damage output was not enough for the difficulty at the time, when the game keeps throwing you hp sponges in groups of 5 with not enough AoE in your team to counter or survive them. At the time I was a bit green regarding the game mechanics, so maybe it was my fault, but the Mage MC is just amazingly better.Speaking of game mechanics, I do believe the game could use better or deeper explanations to help new players understand their skills/stats better. Example of this lack of information is the way damage goes, every 10 points of the skill main stat (STR/AGI/INT) increase the damage of the skill, meaning that 27 STR is close to the same than 20. Another example would be that for archers, the melee weapons extra abilities (text in white underneath damage), are applied to long range attacks (and some of them even to spells (I am not 100% sure)).Music is memorable and some areas have very soothing OST, cannot speak about graphics since my laptop can only run on minimum, but even if nothing was crazy impressive, it wasn´t cheap either.If you like dungeon crawlers, this is a nice one, if you don´t, is still an interesting story, to enjoy as new players to the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Operencia: The Stolen Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a classic turn-based RPG in VR. I love it. I really love this. I've been waiting for something like this since I first tried VR. I have nothing bad to say about it. It even seems longer than most VR content. I got through the first dungeon and it looks like I'm nowhere close to finished the game. It's great, because we need stuff you can play seated, relaxed and with a controller if you want. I want a hundred more games like this.Anyone who gives this a bad review would give any classic turn-based game a bad review, because they're just one of those people who want action games or don't like the style of the classics. Finally a developer gets that we're not all the same so we can have some more variety in the types of game we can play. This is literally the first RPG I've played that's not an action RPG in VR after 5 years of owning a Rift and I'm not disappointed now. If you like classic turn-based RPGs, definitely get this. I hope we get a hundred more like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Operencia: The Stolen Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This for me is like coming from the cold self-destructing world outside, and getting into a nice warm candlelit bath with a glass of mulled wine: A reminder of when games were simple, but well structured and interesting - and when life was too! Only now with updated graphics and man....VR!!!I never thought I would ever see the day when I could actually enter the game, and actually be in one of those old dungeon crawlers. I played through most of the game (on Epic Game Store,), and then bought it again on Steam and started from the top in VR. It is a whole new deal in VR - so immersive and so - well... enchanting (there is a word I almost forgot existed). The VR purists (of which I am, at times, one) will moan and bit-ch about lack of controller support (works just fine with a Xbox controller - get over it!), of the way the menus are not congruent with VR, How they should be able to crawl around in their VR den interacting with objects etc etc. Younger games, who were not brought up on Dungeon Master, and all though old grid based games, will not be able to re-imagine the magic of those games and will complain about the grid based movement.[one criticism that will be levelled, that I will agree with, is he lack of graphical options. Don't get me wrong, the game looks just fine - but not as sharp or detailed as the flat version, and I am sure my rig could squeeze out a little more fidelity.]But in a ♥♥♥♥♥ world, I am so grateful to slump back in a chair, leave it all behind and breathe a sigh of escapism. So, cast your preconceptions aside, immerse yourself and go with the flow - and you will get hours and hours of harmless escapism and joy from this.  I am like a kid in a candy store with a big grin on his face - relieved of the burden of cynicism and criticism, I am free to just soak up and old school solid gaming experience, and old time story-telling in a whole new level of immersion.  I love the game and love the studio for bringing this to me - it is (at this time) *just* what I want.(sorry for the lack of formatting - something weird on Steam side)

_childDocuments_.review: Is this a game that could be the perfect purchase? Yes. Is it the perfect purchase? No. The game has amazing graphics. Perfect colours and characters that are ok. Music is a masterpiece. Great job too. But the game lacks of fair play. What do i mean. You are a great player and go smoothly into the game. You level up fairly good. You get extra moves and spells. If you have mana all is good. If you dont game nine over ten times wins. You wont stand a chance. Your basic attack gives 4 and 5 damage and the opponent gives four times more. In more advanced levels you will encounter enemies that stun you or frighten you. This means. You wont be able to move. Probably you wont be able to do anything from the first round. So, how do you recharge stamina? from camps. randomly placed in the maps. But is just only this? Nooooo, you must have find limited  sticks or woods to rest, otherwise you must buy them. How many are there? 3 at most if you get them they spawn again whenever the game wants. So in the end you do crazy maths and economy to heal your mana and energy and still it wont be enough. What about the weapons armor and magical equipment. I am feeling sorry for the guy who designed those perfect swords and shields etc. Also the one who gave great names but the weapons and other stuff , especially those in the market are pretty useless. You are almost ending the game m and you get to fine a nice fancy sword. Is better than the one you have?? NOOO. So what is the point. This keeps happening in the most objects to be fair. not all. Saving is also a pain in the head. you can only save in the camps. Why?? Why?? and then there is an option save and exit? where will you begin next time? in the camp? in the place you exit? in space? where? I m seriously thinking of quiting the game and play something else.Edit:  i ve reached final boss. Totally inhuman. Bye.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!  The movement and puzzles remind me a bit of Legend of Grimrock, but the combat is turn based.  The best part was the party members and voice acting.  Lots of comments here and there, and a decent amount of character development.  I finished the game, finding it a very enjoyable experience and well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: This one was a tough yes.  It is sort of a blobber, but it really works more like a puzzle game.  You can only create one character of your party and then you get to pick and choose from others as the game goes on (This is to help drive the story, but I do like to build my groups).  Monsters do not respawn.  You can't grind and get any better; you will just move along the same monsters killed as everyone else.  Items slightly differ, but they are hard to tell apart.  When you FINALLY get to see a merchant, the items available are capped per area.  So, we are left with some kinda cool mobs and some neat exploration, but eventually the puzzles get pretty obscure (or I missed clicking some pixel).  I have decided to hang it up.  It was fun for what it was worth; I just wish it had more encounters and skills.

_childDocuments_.review: POSITIVES:- A modern twist on some of some of my favorite 80's / 90's first-person, grid-based RPG's like Might and Magic.- Great writing. You really get to care for the characters and get a feel for them without it distracting from gameplay for too long. I feel like they have struck a great balance of dialogue versus actually playing the damn game. There are some pretty funny moments and characters tease each other like you'd expect of companions journeying together. There are no Mary Sue characters I've seen so far. One character in particular gets called out on a very immoral decision they had made, but it's handled the way I could believe human beings would react (not over-the-top or indifferent).- They employ some very subtle ways of avoiding breaking the fourth wall. Where most games just say "Press J to open your journal", in Operencia it is explained that one of your companions is writing those journal entries. It's even written from that character's perspective with their mannerisms and sense of humor. Little things like that just add to immersion of the game and make you feel like the developers put their love into the game.- Lots of puzzles and secrets to find which are mostly pretty clever and satisfying when you figure them out. I really like that the difficulty has multiple dimensions that affect gameplay rather than just a single slider. I'm currently playing my first playthrough with all difficulty settings set to normal except combat, which I set to hard. Beyond a few encounters where the difficulty spikes unexpectedly, it feels just right for my first run.NEGATIVES:- Despite there being an entire screen on your character sheet with quite a few stats which seem straightforward, there still seems to be some math going on behind the scenes that you can't really quantify. For example, you are told intelligence makes your spells more powerful but the game gives you no way to quantify this (it just shows you some of the related stats that are increased like critical damage / change, energy, etc). There are three numbers for physical power, defense, and magic power, but it isn't explained whether these numbers are actually being used for calculations or if they are just a way to summarize your stats. There are definitely items which read like they should make your spells more powerful, but the magic power number is lower than another item which would seem like it should be more defensive.- Some mechanics could use more explanation (or just be explained earlier). The ability types (Sun, Wind, Moon, Star?, Some temple looking thing?) are little icons in the ability descriptions, but it didn't really make that point very clear. These fill up these party abilities which you start getting before the game even tells you about them. I figured out they were there about an hour before the game bothered telling me "Oh, yeah, there's this thing down here that you've been using for a while already, but I waited until now to actually tell you about it."- Large enemies (pretty much every boss) don't fit on the screen if you are using an ultrawide (21:9) monitor. It doesn't interfere with your ability to target them, but there is some helpful information that appears above enemies that just gets chopped off when they are too tall. I just pretend it's an extra level of difficulty that I can't see bosses' remaining health and it hasn't bothered me too much. This is so far the only thing I've seen that doesn't work as intended on 21:9 aspect ratio, so it's definitely handled better than a lot of other games I've played at least.- Despite the dialogue being well written, some of the voice actors are very uninspiring at times. Some of the characters have consistently great voice work. Some of them have their ups and downs. One particular character is just annoying to listen to and sounds like someone trying to role play a goblin in their first ever game of D&D. It's still way better than anything Bethesda has ever put out, so I wouldn't let this affect your purchasing decision.OVERALL:Fantastic game! I'd give it an 84%.

_childDocuments_.review: As of the making of this review, I am still to fully finish the game.It's quite enjoyable, the art style is nice, the lore is a welcome change from the standard Norse or Greek affairs that are so common. As mentioned by others the game has lots of  dialogue and the VA's range from great to not bad but not good either.As also remarked by others the combat "skills" are few in number and lack depth, but for a game of this length and where battle is more of a means to an end rather than the main attraction I think its as deep as it needs to be. The last thing to be noted about this game is the reasonable business approach, a demo and not falling into the trap of standard pricing for games makes this game a steal and earns it considerable good will.TL;DR Fun game, shallow combat but not detrimentally so, voice acting ranging from great to so-so, interesting lore and setting that's not the standard template and Jóska best boy.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good indie dungeon crawler. Graphics are nice where it counts (in the game), comparable with Grimrock 2. Cutscenes are hand-drawn well enough. I only found the loading screens very bare-bones (Times New Roman-like font, no borders around the text elements. I think this is something the devs could easily fix and which would give the whole game a more cohesive and less amateurish look (which it deserves).Sounds and music are well done, as well as the voice acting. I also like the fresh setting based on Hungarian folklore, even though I found the story itself rather mediocre.Gameplay is excellent, striking a nice balance between combat, exploration, puzzles and party management. Some new ideas in here, which I really appreciated: I like the "logic puzzle  potion crafting" a lot, as well as the fact that you can re-skill and re-distribute attribute points for characters at any time. Game also has a metroidvania-feel to it, as you can return to earlier levels to access secrets with new abilities.I'd say price should be a tad (~5 $/€) lower but even at the current level, you get good value for your money. All in all, strongly recommended for fans of - and vastly superior to - Bard's Tale IV (DC) or Might & Magic X.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game on the day it came out on Steam, played it for 45 hours with two hard difficulty settings on. I had a great time!The game looks beautiful. Turn based combat feels solid, and paced well and responsive. Music is also not bad. Story is intriguing and interesting. Artifact system (puzzle solving mechanic) is brilliant and flavourful.A few things I didn't like about the game...Some puzzles and secrets are not so well made, not very clear or not enough clue, although I managed to find most of the secrets in the game.Sometimes voice overs are not easy to understand with gigantic hall reverb effect. And, some sound effects in combat are too loud, not well balanced.I got 3D motion sickness partly because the camera movement is always stuck with the mouse movement, unlike other games such as Legend of Grimrock in which you need to hold your mouse button down to look around. However, this free camera movement does make the grid based world much smoother and thus the game almost feels as if it isn't based on the grid.Very bad Japanese localization, sadly. I turned the Japanese subtitle on for the first level, couldn't bare with Google translate copy and paste.Looking forward to the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game! I have been playing this type of RPG for 30 years, Dungeon Master, Captive, Knightmare... the recent Legends of Grimrock 1/2, Vaporeum and many more.Operencia is a pure gem!The mouse-controlled camera is absolutely fantastic. Sometimes you forget is a "grid game".. feels right.The combat system turn-based is against the classic concept of this kind of games, but solve the problem of the "grid dance". It is nice, can be improved, but it is very nice.The classes leaves you many spec choices. There is not a single perfect party. You can mix the party in many ways:Party composition, class spec, equipmentAnd the characters you don't choose for your party still follow you and participate in the cutscenes...The cutscenes!! What a wonderful job they made!They are well made, hilarious, engaging! Outside and inside the combat. The cutscenes dispel the sense of loneliness that these games always have.I have finished the game with 100% achievements on the first run (No autosaves, No map, Hard mode)My main party was (characters names spoilers):Seriously, buy it :D

_childDocuments_.review: An entertaining, old school grid based dungeon crawler set in beautifully crafted, evocative environments. The graphics and music are impressively coherent and create a great atmosphere. The devs and artists did justice to the Central European mythological setting, there's just enough lore that it doesn't become a lecture. The characters are fully and well voiced and chatter quite a lot. Controls are straightforward, movement feels very fluid and free despite being grid based. Gameplay is linear, I haven't encountered any side quests yet, and the puzzles so far are very simple. However this gives you a constant sense of progress, every action advances the story. Combat is turn based and well balanced, most enemies feel challenging just enough to be interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Operencia: The Stolen Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly charming little game that seemed to come out of nowhere, and it's been making me really happy. I grew up playing the Wizardry and D&D dungeon games of old, and right away what caught my eye about Operencia is the ways that it tries to set itself apart, while still maintaining that oldschool vibe. Dungeon games tend to be about exploration first, character progression second, and story a distant, distant third. While this is a "dungeon crawler" in the most literal sense, right from the get-go the game distinguishes itself by introducing a rich mythology and narrative, which does a great job of setting the tone. This is a very story-driven game, with the campfire being a prime storytelling device, which really helps to add context. Another thing setting the game apart is the constant witty banter between you and your party members, which is really refreshing. Lastly, the art is absolutely gorgeous, and what they've done with the visuals is really impressive. Things up close are rendered in great detail and texture, but anything farther away becomes progressively "storybook" like, like an illustration in an old book of fairy tales, which is definitely intentional. As you're moving, objects and scenery gain more and more detail, and the transition is almost seamless. So far I've been very impressed with this game, and would recommend it to anyone who enjoys oldschool RPG's, but with a modern twist
_childDocuments_.name: Operencia: The Stolen Sun

_childDocuments_.review: In this video I take a look at Operencia: The Stolen Sun, a turn based RPG game.Initially it was a little disappointing to have such a great graphical environment with free look via your mouse but a classic RPG movement system that only allows you to move via a grid system forward, backwards, left or right. But this is the type of game it is supposed to be and the great graphics and the free look are just a bonus so I quickly decided to enjoy it for what it's meant to be, a modern take on these classic RPG titles. In that genre it appears to excel, with a great story, graphics, and strategic turn based combat. I played the opening sequence in the video and had a great time. The opening sequence has you playing the King and Queen for an epilogue so you are very powerful and take out enemies easily so you can learn the ropes but once it's over you create your own character and start the game as a weak beginner stuck in a cell. I had to end the video there because it was getting too long but it was really getting into a good story.I think this game is very well made with fantastic production quality so if you’re into RPG's you might want to check it out.Watch the video to see what the game is like...Check'n Games Video Curation, providing you with as many Let's Play's as we can.Thanks for watching. Please like comment and subscribe.
