_childDocuments_.review: Do not let the reviews deceive you, I almost did, and I do not regret doing that. This game is REALLY FUN, I am generally not interested in games that involve detective things but when I heard that this was procedurally generated, HECK YEAH!The game is VERY repeatable, with each case having its own fun, whichever step you take, is up to you, and you can solve it the way you want, the game does not force you in one path. The COOLEST part? What's so fun about this is how simulated this game is, you can literally witness the murders with your own eyes, you can see their clear intentions. Someone gets shot, they open a safe, steal what is in it, run around, run outside the apartment. That is just one of many reasons a murder can happen.Many reviews are just people who finally burst out their anger when 1.0 released, and instantly assumed that the game will be ignored, when in reality they said they are gonna release bug fixes and will still be adding more content AFTER those bug fixes. I love this game and will play SO much more of it, and I am excited for the steam workshop release as well.Please, do not let the reviews deceive you, if you REALLY want to buy this game and almost stopped because of the many bad reviews that are mad because "bugs and performance", do not fret, they are working on it and hopefully will get it fixed.I want to be honest, I have a RTX 2070 laptop GPU, and for some reason people with a 4070 or a much better GPU than me have horrible FPS, like under 30 or 15, and changing the graphics does nothing. And luckily I get much better performance than them, so I guess having a worse GPU was better than a GPU that's two generations better. But that's besides the point, this should 100% be fixed. Other than that, let this review be the reason you buy or maybe (not?) buy this game, you got 2 hours if not more (because steam allows you to refund games over 2 hours if their is a good reason for it) and within 14 days (again you can go more if their is a good reason) to play this game and see for YOURSELF.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game and love what it's trying to do. I find it incredibly immersive, atmospheric, dark, and often times comedic. There's something special about walking down a rainy street, ducking into a diner for a coffee and to warm up, before getting a hit on the police scanner and dashing to the crime scene before the cops get there. However, my biggest gripe -- and something I hope is addressed as more features are added -- is that this game is very easy, and pretty formulaic.In 24ish hours of playing, I've yet to encounter a case that I haven't solved in one or two in game days. I've never had a killer evade me long enough to kill a second time. The only exception was when I got a bug where the body/crime scene was inaccessible.I think a lot of the easy-ness will be alleviated by adding on more immersive sim systems. Hunger and thirst are a good starting point, but needing to sleep, or pay rent, or maintain a relationship with informants would add a lot of depth and difficulty. I guess, more plates to spin. I also think the apartments are kind of pointless outside of RP at this point. The decoration system is very cool but you can't cook, don't need to sleep, etc. I only ever go back to mine when I need to shower.There may be a road map out there that explains that stuff like this is coming, but I haven't been able to find a recent one. So overall, I really like this game, but I would LOVE it if there was more depth.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadows of Doubt

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is worth $25, and I really enjoyed the time I have spent so far. That being said, 1.0 establishing almost nothing new was honestly a bit disappointing. I don't necessarily think this game NEEDS a whole lot more, but once you figure out the way NPCs behave and what kinds of evidence solves cases the quickest, the game starts feeling pretty shallow despite its otherwise vast array of deep systems. The one thing I think I was hoping for the most with future updates when the game was still early access was a feeling of progression more significant than just the career milestones, which were non-zero, but barely. The gameplay loop is just too similar case to case, and I was hoping more kinds of play were going to be added, but they were not.TL;DR, game is good, worth the money or at least on slight discount, but once you get a grasp on the core evidence finding loop, that's the whole game.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Out of interest to confirm my review, I attempted to do a full playthrough. Initially I claimed the game was causing BSOD, but the truth is that it was Windows 11. All other performance issues I mention have remained though.With Shadows of Doubt hitting the big 1.0 full release update. I have to put my two cents in. This game at first seems shockingly in depth and promising. But if you put a few hours in, you'll quickly find how lifeless most of the game truly is. You have the finger prints, footprints with types of shoes and size, handwriting styles, etc. NPCs seemingly have A LOT of various traits you can work with. Need to find some information? Take a look in their house and find their job schedule to know when they leave and break into their home when they're out. Maybe break in while they sleep. Perhaps even toss a coin in the corner and slip past while they look away.A majority of these aspects of the game are pointless. Staking out a target for them to sleep is entirely unpredictable as NPCs will choose to wake up for random purposes whenever they really want, even when they should be at work, there's a chance they'll still be at their home or will come inside for no reason. There's plenty of tools and gadgets to use for luring and distracting NPCs, ways to block them off by wedging doors, using motion trackers to know when someone is coming... The stealth aspects seem promising but the best way to get information is just to beat the suspect unconscious. While they're completely unconscious, root through their pockets, grab their fingerprints, and have free reign of their home without needing to waste time sneaking around. There are zero repercussions for beating people unconscious multiple times so it's easy enough to just knock them out again when necessary.Similarly, the combat aspects seem initially interesting with how your fists let you time a parry and a counter attack when fighting. Except it only works against other unarmed targets so anybody with a weapon is just backpedaling to easily avoid their attacks. Your fists are also weak weapons, and it's far easier to just buy a sword to KNOCK OUT someone in two swings. They made a point that your character has sworn off guns to the point of using them as melee weapons but for some reason stabbing people is perfectly okay. This distinction is rather dumb, and pointing to the Yakuza series: characters in that game have no qualms with using guns and knives. However, a character with stricter morals like Yagami from Judgment can't use guns OR bladed weapons. Removing these more inherently lethal weapons as tools entirely makes more sense than deciding it's perfectly fine to stab everyone but a gun isn't. So from an immersion aspect, it's baffling that guns are off limits but a literal katana is acceptable.Let's also not forget the BIGGEST aspect here: the downright HORRID performance and bugs. I have a decently strong computer and will get stutters whenever the game wants, objects will load and pop in AFTER I run into their hitbox. This issue pulls into cases as well, with some side jobs giving you a picture of a briefcase somewhere. Except all the objects won't load in on the picture because I haven't been in that area yet. A murder happened in an apartment building? Let's go check that camera system! Except, oh wait, they didn't render any of the people walking around in this area so you don't even get a possible suspect. A rooftop that happened to generate so you can clamber down to an apartment's windows, smash them open, and get inside? There's a solid invisible wall preventing you from breaking the window or climbing inside to begin with.For a full release, this game's content and systems feels depressingly undercooked, the actual hardware performance of the game is horrid, and there's a real chance that you'll get shafted from something bugging out and ruining your experience. I would not recommend getting this game until the modders really flesh out the skeleton that was laid before them.

_childDocuments_.review: While the cases you investigate can start to feel a bit repetitious after a while, the act of finding and chasing down leads, piecing things together from the evidence you find, sneaking into buildings, and bypassing security systems can be very satisfying and addictive. Many of the side jobs are just as enjoyable as the main murder investigations and the atmosphere of the city itself is excellent. An absorbing and well crafted (occasionally a little buggy) game, with a lot of potential, that is well worth trying out.

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing game! There's a few bugs here and there, which is expected for for EA game, but it's truly a very solid and enjoyable experience already, very much a great detective sim drenched in atmosphere.It's raining. You're cold, shivering, and hungry as you turn off of a boulevard down an alley. You stop at a lit barrel for some warmth, pausing as you contemplate whether or not you could have brought to justice a killer before the loss of a second life. What if there was a missed fingerprint at the scene? What if you'd have placed higher urgency in tracking down the murder weapon? What if you hadn't been gunned down by a sentry turret and spent some time in hospital? So many what-ifs, you pack them away as you head for your favourite diner for a burger and a coffee, to pick yourself up before the next case jumps into your hands.There's plenty of potential. Certain things are a lot easier than they should be, other things feel far too random, and the AI could do with a tuneup, but even so, if you have a detective sim itch then you could easily lose hours and hours here.

Once you're out on your own with your own crimes it really doesn't pull any punches with difficulty.My only small gripe is sometimes the combination of identifying features can be quite frustrating, you have to arrest someone and all you have to go on is "long hair" and "works in X building" which has 16 floors! Hopefully once that's tidied up a little it'll be fine. But quite honestly thats the only gripe I've got at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was a bit comprehensive because I saw other people playing the game, and it might feel convoluted or repetitive, BUT OMG, I WAS WRONG. This game is phenomenal. The emotion you get unraveling murders in this dystopian world makes it one of the best games I have ever played unequivocally. It is exceptional and offers an experience I have never encountered in any other game. I suggest this game to anyone with a mild interest in the genre. It also supports a non-binary character option and other similar amazing features, like some couples in the city will be same-sex. Easily in my top 5 favorite games. My only real criticism is that the map/guidance system was somewhat hard to figure out, and even after I figured it out (It took me forever to realize you could move the map in the evidence section and search for addresses), its a little annoying to use but it's a very very minor annoyance. 9.6/10 would recommend, even if it was double the price.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very good game so far and has a lot of potential.- It is interesting to see how each NPC can live their life. They are not always home or at work. They can even be slacking off their job at working hours and you'd be trying to find them on street asking random people. They can have their favorite drink, AND they can be found drunk, shaking while walking somewhere. - Good variability in cases/gigs for an early access. It kept me playing for 2 days straight until I've noticed some repetance.- Game has a decent chunk of Roleplay to it. You can drink alcohol (and have a headache in the morning after drinking too much), you can be a good citizen and dispose your trash OR you can just throw it away like a pig. You can be a cola promoter and annoy people about it. You can get burrow money from some scum bank and if you dont return it back, person will come trying to take life from you.- Interesting to explore the world and explore mechanics of this game, it doesnt get boring to throw different things at the wall. Or to punch people and see them falling. It is quite fun. - I've got drawned in this game and I'd play -> sleep -> repeat Altho game has decent variability, but after some time gigs start repeating themselves, as well as murders. It is still good enough to keep you in game for hours, but you'd want to see more types/ways to get these gigs, murder cases. You want to understand people motives as well. It is hard to implement You can knock out npcs, you can arest them, you can steal from them, you can break into their house, and after a while they just forget about what you did and react like nothing happened, doesnt matter if you do it to a normal citizen or a policeman. You can even cuff the policeman and they'd be fine with you after some while. Different people can be more willing to share information with you, but they are pretty much the same. What you'd want to see is people being more people, you want to see them reacting to things, being disgusted by you, scared of you, grateful to you. Make them lie to you, dispose the evidence, make their loved ones protect them. You can think of as many things as you want, this can make this game like infinite times better.

_childDocuments_.review: After having played for roughly ~20 hours so far, I can say that the game is pretty great in concept. I'm enjoying the idea of procedural generated murder cases mixed with survival components and immersion. It's a fine mix and there aren't many games I've played that are like this, if any. The story scenario is a useful way of teaching the player the ropes of the game, although turning off the tutorial hints does not stop prompts coming up if you have selected this mode. Furthermore, the game suffers in terms of performance. After researching a little into voxel games, graphics cards just simply aren't built for voxel games which does explain for the drops in fps throughout play. Just note that after playing for about an hour, the game will begin to struggle to load evidence. I've found that when sifting through evidence, the game freezes for a few seconds, especially after around an hour or two of play time. This is usually fixed a little with a quick restart, although this does get tedious. This may be an issue only I have experienced, or perhaps others have too. There are various bugs in the game, mostly involving phasing through walls. In my most recent session, I had been given entry to an npc's home, and they collided with me into a wall, which caused be to phase through the wall, fall 7 stories to my death. Although I found this funny, this type of bug is persistent in every game session. As far as the procedural generation of new murder scenarios, as much as it will be a new victim and a new murderer, most of these seem to pick between a few base scenarios such as 'jealous employee leaves business card', or 'ritual murder leaves anagram' etc. Of course this game is in early access, therefore take what I have written with a grain of salt. For an early access game, it is incredible. The game needs work yes, but I wholeheartedly recommend giving it a try to see for yourself. And, despite its flaws, I know I'm going to spend many more hours trying to crack cases.

_childDocuments_.review: The foundation of a great game that was clearly built with attention and care. A must for fans of cyberpunk and neo-noir. Shadows of Doubt isn't just a fantastic sandbox detective simulator, it's a love letter to Blade Runner, hard boiled detective fiction, and classic film noir like Hitchcock's (1943) Shadow of a Doubt. Every corner of the generated cities is dripping with atmosphere and retro-futurism. Performance issues can hamper the overall experience, but Early Access does grant some considerable leeway in that regard. The game can certainly break, but it is *not* broken. NPCs will hopefully receive more depth and become far more conversational as time goes on. As of now the rather mundane dialogue can break an otherwise immersive experience.Still, the game offers something previously only dreamed of by fans of other noir settings. It's got the soul and artistic vision of a title from fifteen years ago, and modern tech to bring that vision to life. Worth it even in Early Access just to see where this goes.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and very interesting game. The way it generates cites and cases is amazing tech and works quite well! While Shadows of Doubt is not without problems its overall a great game.As for the problems I mentioned... Things like the more information you collect the more the game tends to slow down. Or the opening hours of many business feel inconsistent as if NPCs just aren't showing up for work. This is made worse by the fact you can only see the operation hours of a business by asking a worker while they are on duty. One other issue is with the finger print scanner the game will sometimes target an object (like a drawer or item) instead of the fingerprint on the object.One nice thing regardless of bugs is, on the in-game pause menu, theres a feedback option which lets you send bug reports and feedback directly to the dev team. Its always awesome when something like this is added into a game.PS The only reason I found this game was watching Mr Sark play it on his twitch stream. He made it look so fun that I just had to try it for myself. Lukily I had a $20 steam card laying around so I had no reason not to and Im glad I did!

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game almost every chance I could get and it is very worth it. I wont lie it is very difficult when you first start playing getting the general controls down and how to find any information for cases, but once you learn how to piece things together you'll go from needing 3-4 different victims to find the killer to 3-4 in game hours. I just retired my first character on the small map and i am extremely exited to make my next one. I suck at talking about all the good cause when it works it doesn't stick out like the stuff that doesn't so lets get on to that, keep in mind it is early access and I do highly highly recommend this game even though it I will spend more time talking about the bad. So while playing and going in and out of buildings I did notice that the world would not generate any of the objects around the map I would have to walk in and out multiple times for it to trigger the loading. Sometimes it would happen for the physical room where it would load in objects but not the room itself so i fell though the map and died. There also are secret shops that are in the city that you need codes to enter them I would enter codes i found all around the map they would say it was correct but then I couldn't use them. One thing I found a bit annoying looking over someones profile seeing that I know where they live and not being able to click on it to pin it to the board for investigating instead you have to find something else like an ID to pin it to the board. I think any information you have on a profile such as address or workplace should be able to be take off of the profile and not have to find there business card or ID. Also if you get the upgrade to make you taller while being very useful can become a bit in-convent getting stuck on doors and having to crouch to use phone booths. For my next game I will try to use vents more but as of the 29 hours I have played so far I have been in vents for a total of like 40 seconds the confusing lay out mixed with how slow you craw never seemed worth it when you can just lock pick doors or barge them. One thing I could not find out how to do is buy a better apartment that is on the higher floors I had only ever saw basement buildings witch (while work and fit for what they are) suck because it lives up to the real thing.Ending on some more goods and to stay with apartments I absolutely love the customization of the rooms. Being able to make a cozy place to hang up your hat in a crazy city full of chaos feel like home its just great. The amount of different options you can add while being early access is a lot I'm really looking forward to having a working stove so you are able to have a reason to go into the kitchen. I know for the most part I talked about the bad parts and I haven't even covered any of the good but I seriously recommend this game if ya want to have something to sit down and just think and try to connect the dots of who's done it. I'll probably be back to add more to the review after I play more but I am extremely exited for more updates to the game

_childDocuments_.review: In Summary: I wanted the game to be more simulation and less "gamey".Certain core parts of the game are super janky and take me out of the game.- stealth and trespassingbreaking in to peoples' apartments is a core part of the game. but it feels so broken and "gamey". No matter what, even if no one sees you and cameras are disabled, you still have a timer that basically counts down until enforcers arrive at the apartment and you need to escape in an air duct or hide or leave. Why? That experience isn't fun. And the gameplay loop is the same every single time.I don't even like that there are turrets and cameras mounted everywhere to begin with. It just seems unnecessary.- arrestsi arrive at the suspects apartment. she's sitting on a couch and doesn't hear me come in. I put her in handcuffs and search her apartment for evidence. found finger prints that place her at the scene (turns out that this wasn't enough evidence to prove it though). When she is in handcuffs, she doesn't say anything. No way to talk to her or ask her questions. I understand that this is a procedurally generated game, but I handcuff a random woman in her apartment and she just sits there. I can't ask her any questions or anything. Just feels odd in that respect. How do I now "arrest" her? I leave her handcuffed in her apartment and I go to the police station and deliver my paper. And magically she is "arrested" when they grade my report.It's hard to tell what direction this game will be moving in and for that reason, I'm not sure if it's worth buying and holding on to it or not.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty amazing and should be worth about $20 even if nothing else gets added - however - it needs a lot of bug fixes.It's got performance issues, and gameplay is a little janky. It's easy to get lost and combat is terrible.Still, this is a great use of procedural generation. Usually it's lots of shallow content but here I think we've got pretty intricate connections. Time will tell if there's enough variation to keep people playing a lot but like I said I think the price point is right.Also motion blur is disabled by default, so the devs clearly have some sense about them but there needs to be a lot more graphics options particularly for those with older systems. I get decent performance with a 3080 and i9-9900k in 1440p at 60hz.The in-game bug reporting system gives me a lot of confidence that this will be greatly improved. There's an interface for uploading your current save and screenshot within the game as well as describing what's going on.

_childDocuments_.review: About 30 seconds of an Insym  video convinced me I needed to play this game. If that is not enough to convince you, I have had a hard time putting it down for the past couple of days.Do not let the Early Access banner trick you into skipping this game, there is A LOT of content jam-packed into Shadows of Doubt already. Whether it is trying to solve a murder case because law officers do not, smashing up someone's apartment to get some crows [money], stealing secret company documents for a rare SyncDisk, or simply trying to purchase a nicer apartment, you are given a plethora of ways to engage with the environment and NPCs living within the city.There are a few bugs (as expected from an Early Access title), but I anticipate this game will only keep getting better.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadows Of Doubt is one of those game rare games that can only come about due to the passion of it's creator. It is the type of game that you wished existed, but didn't because large companies are not interested in making something that pushes the boundaries of what can be done. This kind of game is only created by a dreamer, and Cole, I tip my hat to you sir!If you have ever wanted to play a detective in a Sci-Fi Noir setting, where you have to find all the evidence, make the connections yourself, gathering evidence by any means necessary (true gumshoe style), while doing it any way you want to, then this is the game for you.Unlike other games, this one has a living, breathing, city; a city that keeps on ticking even when you are not there to see it. It is one of those games you have to experience to believe it.Every citizen in Shadows of Doubt go about their lives. Each with a job, relationship, friends, and a history that played out over two days (game time) before you even started. This time sets the scene for the first murder, allowing you to trace all evidence (no matter how insignificant it is) to it's logical origins. Find a receipt screwed up, check the time stamp, access the shop's CCTV cameras and follow the person that got the receipt by checking the footage around the time they bought it. Every citizen leave their own unique finger prints, and you can match them up to that person.This world is not without its dangers... and there are plenty, so don't expect this game to make things easy for you.Did I mention that all of this is fully procedural?Everything, the whole city and all its inhabitants are generated before you start, which means ever new play though will be different, with different murders. The full mode has you gaining jobs via many ways. Read the paper and decide to take up the case for yourself.Do yourself a favour and buy this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadows of Doubt

_childDocuments_.review: Warren Spector can finally have his one city block immersive sim, and so can we.  Time IRL flies by while I play this, because there are always three more things to do before I want to quit for the day. The main game is solving murders as a detective, but if you want to play a thieving rogue, there are nearly unlimited opportunities. There are restaurants, companies, black market dealers, factories, and residences just waiting for you to dig as deep as you can for information and items. If you don't want to steal, there are even abilities  that let you earn money by picking up trash, taking pictures of kitchens or bathrooms, or just reading books. They are slower to earn, but it's an option if you find them.As of mid-July 2023, there are still issues with placing items in your apartment accurately where you want them, but there's so much more to do, that I pretty much dumped the furniture that came with me to the new apartment and left rest of the unfurnished rooms empty just to get back out into the city and keep looking.  I've sort of settled into a comfortable loop as far as getting information needed for jobs to complete, but there are several alternate routes I have yet to try.  The side missions you take on are harder to find who you need, and I expect to be gently nudged into some of the methods I haven't devoted enough time to.This is way more than I expected from any game as far as depth of detail in a setting, and the fact it's still in early access makes me wonder what the release version will add.The main down side is that although it has gotten much, much better since the last patch, the game does start to lag a just bit when accessing things that are directly related to an investigation that already has a lot of pinned detail, but if you can wait a few seconds, it powers through.Highly recommend this game; it has pushed a bunch of AAA titles way back into my unfinished queue.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Really unique concept and, for the most part, really well executed. It's still a bit rough around the edges with some apparently missing features and fairly frequent bugs that make completing some missions (just side missions so far) impossible, but based on how good it is already, I'm pretty confident that will get ironed out.The main thing I'd like to see improved on is the dialogue options. It would be great to try and investigate via motive a bit more, by asking the friends and family of murder victims about them. At the moment the game is great at simulating the paper trail of a crime - you can check bank statements, sales records, emails, surveillance footage etc to try and figure out whodunit, but it is usually not viable to look into who a victim's enemies were, or if they were behaving unusually before the murder. Hopefully that gets fleshed out a bit in the future, but the game's a banger.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT:I unfortunately have to modify this review, and change my recommendation to "No." The game is not done yet. There are still bugs, optimization issues, and lack of gameplay. Yes, they've added new missions since my original review, but most of them play near identically to other missions, especially others of the same type. Despite this, the developers have stated that they are finished with this game, and that no updates are planned except for minor bug fixes. All the potential of this being the best detective game of all time just went down the drain. The gameplay loop is fun at first, but once you learn the game's shortcomings, everything becomes moot. Why sneak into someone's apartment when you can just knock on the door and kick it in, rendering them unconscious? Why avoid death when you can just run out of the hospital within 20 seconds? Why stake out an NPC, learn their work schedule, or anything like that when their schedule is usually broken anyway? In fact, something that is still an issue with this game is the passage of time. Most NPCs work 9-5, but because everyone has to walk to and from work, they end up having a 4-hour walk (or more) to their job, because the time moves too quickly. They end up waking up at 9am, walking to work and arriving by 12 (despite most places claiming to open at 9), getting off at 5pm, walking home and finally getting home around 9pm or later. If they decide to do anything else, like stop to eat, it takes them longer. Combat in this game is rendered useless when you learn you can just throw a heavy object at someone to instantly knock them out. Searching for suspects in this game is rendered useless when you learn you can just search the government database for almost anyone in town.Buying food is rendered useless when you realize it doesn't do much except add some saturation and color back to your vision. Although fun, like so many other abandoned early-access titles, this game in it's current state is still just a beta-build with plentiful bugs, below-average optimization, and repetitive gameplay.ORIGINAL REVIEW:Let me start by saying this game is still being developed. There are bugs and issues present while playing this game that the developers are still working to solve.Shadows of Doubt has been extremely fun. The whole game works differently than anything else I've ever played. The way that NPCs simply live their lives, and you can track them across the entire city, is simply amazing. You could follow an NPC from their home in bed, waking up in the morning, going to the local diner for a cup of coffee, then to their workplace for 8 hours of their office job. Then, they may return home or maybe go to the bar. Along the way, this NPC is leaving fingerprints that can be scanned, making phone calls that can be tracked, and getting caught on surveillance tape which can be checked. It's insane. This is every citizen in the game, whether there's a murder or not.PROS:- Insanely detailed NPCs with lives; friends, enemies, jobs, addictions, debts, and more.- Each city, NPCs, crimes, even the tutorial is procedurally generated. No two cities are exactly the same.- Many missions to follow, but also tons of ways to make your own fun.CONS:- The missions tend to get old as there aren't quite enough different types in the game yet. (EDIT: More mission types have been added which has made this problem a little better)- There isn't much of an actual story.- Your PC has to work hard if you want to be in a "large" size city. Simulating the lives of all those NPCs is hard work. You may drop frames.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review:So, the game has received a few patches and bugfixes. The game is a bit more playable now, but there's still some rough edges to be sorted out. Some things like not being able to use weapons (firearms) to defend yourself, cannot scan fingerprints when a culprit is sleeping or cuffed, asking for someone else in the same apartment room, and most noticeable, generation bugs/glitches are still present. I understand the devs didn't want this game to be an action detective shooter, but I honestly think it would be a nice addition to have at least some sort of weapon to defend yourself. Perhaps using weapons has a huge penalty, which means players will have to think before they decide to start blasting. Something to encourage players to blast responsibly. I still think this game is worth it, which is why I would definitely recommend to wishlist it to get it on sale. However, it's probably best to wait until it's fully released.

_childDocuments_.review: I love supporting indie devs that put passion into the craft they produced. I've always wanted a retro immersive sim game for a long time now. I've always appreciated the small actions you're able to do in video games such as opening a fridge, locking the door, or closing the blinds because it makes you feel like you're living in this world. Being able to fight crime and going home to a beer and takeout food solidifies that grungy, hard-working detective work and life I pictured in a film noir setting. I'm hoping the dev adds more features to game such as complex/advanced/dynamic dialogue with NPC's such as being able to warm up to the NPC and allow them to open up to you asking more specific questions about what they've witnessed. There should be more options to approaching a crime scene and gathering evidence (I've always found myself picklocking or crawling through vents or waiting for an NPC to leave their location to gather evidence for side jobs). There could be a wiretap approach where you can listen in on conversations, there could be a tailing feature where you could tail them with a risk they could notice you. So far the city and game feels so almost alive already and I'm hoping the dev adds more content and features to solidify that feeling. Maybe consider adding an end-game goal you can work towards; upgrading and furnishing your apartment is a good start and something more along those lines would be a great addition.

_childDocuments_.review: Almost immediately this game became one of my favourite games of all time. I love it. It's like the developers reached into my head, discovered what my ideal game would be, and built it. It's a world you can live in. In the first few dozen hours you're amazed at the scale and complexity of it. After a while the novelty wears off - as other reviews have mentioned, the game is procedurally generated, so there are repeating patterns in the cases, but still with enough variation and randomness that you can't memorise them. You still need to solve the case each time. The repetition doesn't bother me though, becauze I get to have the thrill of performing a task that I've honed and mastered. I watched dozens of videos teaching me different tips and tricks; it felt like studying a professional craft, and when I solve a case or completed a side-job I get such an endorphine boost and sense of professional pride, knowing that I really earned that win. The game doesn't hold your hand; you're not walking through a predetermined plot simply pressing buttons when prompted and interacting with highlighted clues; you have to decide what objects to look at, which locations to go to, which leads to follow up. Are you going to interview the neighbours? Break into the security office and check the CCTV at the time of death? Hack into their computer and search their emails for clues? Find out who last phoned the house and trace the phone call? Search for diary entries or mysterious notes? Go to their workplace and investigate their colleagues? This game gives me the same satisfaction as a game like Powerwash Simulator; sure, the format does get a bit repetitive after a while, but the core gameplay loop is so addictive that you don't care that you're performing variations of the same task over and over, because you're honing your skills.I also absolutely love the level of freedom in this game offers me. It's incredibly open-ended. I enjoy choosing which jobs to pick up, often juggling several at once, then methodically working my way through a case in whatever order I choose, constructing detailed case boards with red string connections and sticky note annotations. It makes me feel useful and productive in a way that even my real life job doesn't manage to!Plus it's so darn atmospheric. The voxel graphics and lighting are beautiful, and there are just enough life-sim aspect to make you feel part of the world without it becoming cumbersome. There are status effects like hunger, thirst, cold and illness; penalties for breaking the law; a black market trade where you can sell stolen goods; vending machines, shops and bars; plus you can buy and decorate apartments, which are useful places for storing unsold loot!The only con is, the bugs. It shouldn't have been released in this state. In fact, the number of bugs that have appeared in the last month seems to have increased. I assume that the devs are desperately trying to fix them, and Introducing new ones in their haste. It's still playable, but I find myself abandoning bugged quests a lot, and saving the game over and over as a fix to get the controls to bind correctly to my controller after they cease to work (I play on PC with a controller). I've submitted three or four bug reports this week, and only one of them has actually appeared in the bug queue, even though I uploaded all of the files they ask for. This needed another year in the oven, and it baffles me that they'd rather burn through the community's good will, potentially ruining the game's launch (which may be the time in the game's life cycle that it's seen by the most people), rather than delaying. You don't get a second chance at a launch. They must have been told by the publisher that their salaries won't be paid any more unless they release the game immediately, because I cannot comprehend why else they would sabotage their own game by releasing it like this. I didn't mind the game being buggy before, but having a fully released game that's as buggy as this is taking the pss.I've still recommended it because, like I said, it's one of my favourite games of all time, and it would break my heart if it didn't survive because of a bad release; but the devs need to get their act together, and fast.

_childDocuments_.review: Terrible optimization plagues this game in almost every aspect, shallow game design and broken systems within broken systems means you're fighting with the game on almost every aspect to pretend to be a detective. You are less of a detective in this game than you are a burglar, you'll have committed more crimes and ranked up a personal bounty attempting to solve the case.Want to investigate the murder scene? Sorry it's cordoned off by cops. Entrance is illegal. Want to investigate a possible leads house? You better hope they give you permission to enter, and hope any roommates of theirs also doesn't bug out and call cops on you for trespassing, all the while the murderer commits more crimes.Eventually the new game smell turns sour as you realize there aren't many types of murders generated, only four or five total. The steps and suspects to investigate are always the same within these types of murders. Did the victim leave a business card? The suspect is ALWAYS a coworker of the victim. This might not sound bad in context, but it feels bad in game when you understand this in a meta context, and are getting hamstrung in game via any alternative leads. This wouldn't be a fault of the game if there were more types of murders and crimes to investigate, as playing for 5-10 hours will show you every "type" of murder there is. This would all be forgivable if the developers took suggestions from the community seriously, and didn't release the game in it's current state as 1.0. They have done nothing but show disdain and bad faith by stringing us along for years with barely anything to show for it. You know why people want a gun and to smoke cigarettes in game so bad? It's because nearly every part of the game fails to capture that "detective" feeling in gameplay, and players are so desperate for it, that the simplicity of being an armed detective lighting up a cigarette and walking through the rainy streets which could partially fill that gap has been denied to us for years.Before this 1.0 release, we have been promised so much, and the developmental road map was carefully reworded and changed to make it seem as if there previous promises were fulfilled by lackluster content updates within unoptimized code. Now that 1.0 is out nothing has changed. I won't support these people again, and before you decide to buy it try it out yourself to see if it's worth it. This game was, without a shadow of a doubt, the biggest disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been a fan of Noir stories and the general detective genre. There is something enjoyable about piecing together a mystery from scant clues and seeing the bigger picture of what is going on. Approaching a crime scene to look for anything that might be helpful. A fingerprint, a bullet casing, maybe even a weapon, anything that can help build a profile. Sometimes, assumed clues lead you down utter dead ends. Other times, the clues are simply lacking a context to make it all fit together.And when it does? It scratches that part of the brain that enjoys sifting through the chaos, looking for reason.And this game does that quite well. I won't lie, there are some issues, mostly in the optimization. The game seems to run fine at max settings with a 2070 Super and I5-11600k, but there are times when everything just stutters really bad. It takes a while to load the large city but that's more a matter of the fact it's trying to load and calculate some odd few hundred people it seems. Interaction with items can be a bit finicky at times, especially when it's obscured by something ever so slightly larger. And there are bugs here and there, mostly of the amusing type, like people falling through stairs and teleporting back up, but nothing game breaking. These are minor things, I feel, in the grand scheme.I enjoy the procedurally generated murders. I've had some pop up that were really out there, requiring me to dig pretty hard to find out what was going on. One murder, I had a man murdered in his kitchen, his body placed in a heart. Killed by a shotgun, a size 10 heel mark in blood beside him, and a couple hulls of what was once buckshot around the room. Above him, written in what I assume is blood or lipstick, is the phrase "Frank + M Forever". Eyewitness only report someone suspicious at the early morning, wearing glasses. I have no finger print that doesn't match the victim nor his wife.His wife has no glasses and sports a size 13. Her name is Abigail. I rummaged around the apartment to find a written note telling him that he isn't being stalked and to take his pills. Hand written, I take note of it in my board of clues. I also find a notice from the building super about needing a form to check surveillance. I take this as my first clue and break into the surveillance room. It does me no good. The cameras are on every floor from ground to ninth. Frank lived on the 12th. The only figure with glasses moving about the building in the window of his death? A man with size 16 shoe.I go back to his room and check his address book. I find two names of note within, Miriam and Miranda. Their addresses and phone numbers are inside. They both live in the same building, so a quick stop might be all I need, but to no avail. Neither wears glasses and neither has a size 10 heel. I'm back at square one. I start rummaging through Frank's trash, looking for anything of use or note. I find receipts to some restaurant he visited the day before and head on to that diner. There, I get access to their security system and watch the cameras. I see Frank and take note of everyone wearing glasses. I check the images I print and narrow it down to two suspects. The only two women with glasses. One has a size 12 foot, the other a size 10. I show her picture to everyone in the street until one recognizes her. A woman he works with at some random corp. Her full name is given and I check the phone book.She lives in the same building as Frank. I pay her a visit. I ask her if she recognizes a picture of Frank, she rattles off the time she saw him last. It was the time of death. I beat her with my truncheon and handcuff her. This lets me search her. I find a shotgun on her person and buckshot. I got her name, address, evidence of being at the scene, weapon and arrested her. I turn in my form at City Hall and collect my reward for a job well done. It took me a couple real time hours to work through that, doing a lot of back tracking to search any clue that might help. But I got it done before she struck again. I am a good detective.My next case, I visit a flophouse apartment on the bottom floor. A woman is dead in an occultic circle. The only prints I find are hers and her partner. I look around the room for any evidence or notes left behind. I find all the details of the two people in the house: Karen Benjamin and Takola McCord. Both unemployed, but I have the full details of blood type, name and so on. I continue to search to find anything that might help, like an ID or weapon. I find a crumpled note."I want to play a game.R T O C D C M_. _ _ _ _ _"An anagram. I pin the note in my clue board and a name immediately catches my eye. Takola McCord.T. MCCORDI have her prints, her name and address. I simply wait in the lobby of her apartment building until she returns. Skipping time until she walks up. I see her and beat her with a truncheon, slap on the metal bracelets and search her. A box cutter, consistent with the slashing wounds on the victim. I turn in the case and get rewarded for about five minutes of work and a lot of in game waiting. I am a good cop.I found it mostly funny that the murderer was the person' partner, especially given another unnamed clue in a bathroom I never saw until I read the news scroll. Everything I needed was right there and it all meshed up perfectly. A nice break from the rough investigation I just finished. Even that hit that area of detective work. Even more so that the game lets you try and fail. There are some cases where you just lack a critical piece of info to cinch it and simply have to wait for the killer to strike again. And it's nice, enjoyable. Balancing the needs of food and water, making sure you don't stand out in the cold too long are all just nice little things that help round it out. The freedom to approach and attack a puzzle in any way you see fit, whittling away until it's all solved.I'm not sure I've seen a game like this one yet but the niche it seeks to fill? It does it very well and in very enjoyable ways. Even more so when showing off case notes with other friends as they work theirs. Seeing how they organize their clues and thoughts in a spider web of red yarn.Oh yeah, it's got the red yarn clue board to map out the latest theory on whodunnit. A real bargain at 20 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: I had it all figured out.  It had been a routine investigation and now I just needed to arrest the killer.  So I broke into their flat and waited for them to return from work....  A few hours passed.  I looked at my watch: they were running late -- where the hell were they?  That's when I heard the gunshots upstairs -- they were quite literally murdering their neighbour in the flat above me. :O  Ever since Watchdogs Legion, I'd hoped someone would take that technology and make a criminal profiling / manhunt game -- like in those films where the fbi have to catch the killer before they strike again. For all intents and purposes this is that game.  It's totally unique and at it's best the ultimate private detective simulator / sandbox.Is it perfect? No. The almost 100% proc-gen nature of the game results in a fair amount of jank (though it's gotten a lot more polished since early access), and if you're looking for a more hand-crafted experience you're not going to find that here.  There's lore and world building, but outside of the tutorial there's no real story to speak of.  What you see is pretty much what you get - the game builds a city, populates it, designates a murderer, and gives you the tools to investigate and track them down.  You can also take on smaller cases on the side while you wait for a break in your current case or a new one to start.  You can upgrade your character with cyberware of sorts and there is a progression system that eventually leads to your character's retirement, but it's relatively simple stuff.  There's also quite a lot of status effects like hunger and cold, which (thankfully) you can turn off if you prefer.  That's basically it -- and don't expect a pat on the back when you catch your killer.  Like real life, the motives for most murders in the game are random, senseless, and somewhat anti-climatic.  So I think the mixed reviews come from people expecting the final game to magically transform out of early access into something much bigger than the developers ever intended.  It's very easy to imagine a more 'complete' game with more sophisticated dialogue trees, deeper killer motives, a full story mode, and so on, while downplaying just what a technical accomplishment this game already is.  Bear in mind also that it was created by a small indie team, over 8 years -- the idea that they can work on it in perpetuity is unrealistic.  I guess what I'm driving at here is set your expectations accordingly: it's definitely more than "just a prototype", but even in it's finished form it is an experimental indie title.  I'd recommend watching someone play it on Twitch or YT to get a feel for how the game works.The real draw of course is the gameplay loop.  Every true detective knows it's about the chase, the hunt -- and that's where this game really excels.  This game is at it's best when you're sitting in a diner at 3 am, chowing down french fries and a coke while looking at office blueprints and bullet trajectories, trying to figure out which flat your sniper lives in.  Or rifling through office computers for their employee database and cctv footage.  Creating a spiderweb of evidence, suspects, and possible leads on your case board.  Returning to that one cold case you couldn't solve hoping that if you stare at it for long enough you'll find something, anything.  The moment where all the pieces fall together and you go "it's them".  Needless to say, the game is best enjoyed in the evening with a glass of whiskey and some jazz playing quietly in the background. I guess my main concern before buying this was "are the cases going to get repetitive?"  I would say 50+ hours in, for the most part no.  Some cases are more straightforward than others, and the killers do follow a limited number of archetypes / patterns, but I still get a dopamine kick every time the police scanner goes off to inform you that a murder has been committed (prompting you to drop what you're doing and leg it to the scene of the crime before the police arrive).  There is a grim excitement around exploring a new crime scene, and cases often play out differently due to the unpredictable nature of the game.  However, if things do start to get stale, you can always generate a brand new city.Ultimately, if you can appreciate it for what it is, and not what it isn't, I think there's a lot to enjoy here.  As far as I know, there isn't another game quite like this.  Just don't expect the cases to have the depth and complexity of an Agatha Christie novel.

_childDocuments_.review: As of August 2023, the phrase "Early Access" remains key. Shadows of Doubt is one of the greatest concepts I've seen in gaming, but it also has a lot of glitches to be ironed out before the final release. This offers a true sandbox experience with a cyberpunk flair with gameplay akin to a less violent version of the original Deus Ex. However a sandbox in this style isn't going to be for everyone - this game will make you THINK and sometimes present you with cases that have very little evidence to start with. You will find yourself flipping through the phone book searching for every single person in the city whose name begins with the letter "T" for example - and compiling a list of addresses for a LOT of legwork checking off each residence for further clues. For me - this is everything I could want in a sandbox - but for others it might be a frustrating exercise lacking guidance.

_childDocuments_.review: This game came out of nowhere but may very well be my favorite game of all time. Immersive Sim Detective game with infinite replayability. Even in it's current state it's worth the $20. Once the devs fix some of the most glaring bugs (of which there are few and they aren't even THAT huge) the game would be launch worthy. But the devs aren't even planning to stop at that, they have some pretty meaty updates to come over the next 6 months. I can see myself playing this game daily for weeks, and at least weekly for years to come. I absolutely adore everything about this game. Presented for your enjoyment, a tale with limited artistic embelishment:THE EDEN SKINNER Every single crime scene, I'd find a set of fingerprints. Fingerprint set "P". It was taunting me. Every single lead that i'd find would come up short. Every place of employment. Every Crumpled restaurant receipt. Everything, all dead ends. Then I noticed that both victims worked in Kang Gardens. a Clue! I was confident that the killer lived or worked there as well. I began breaking into every single office in Kang Gardens for multiple nights, checking through their employee files for fingerprint data. Along the way, my pockets SOMEHOW seemed to fill up with change from people's desks, and before long I had a pretty penny available. So I decided I wanted to stop being homeless and buy an apartment. A 3rd floor apartment in Boyle Tower, a perfect base of Operations for me. But just as I was feeling good about myself, the killer struck again. This time, the kill happened IN Kang Gardens. Further proof! I dash to the scene and investigate. The killer used a gun this time, a deviation from the MO, but still they'd painted "[Initials] PAID" In blood on the wall. And of course, one set of "P" Fingerprints could be found on a lightswitch and the doorknob. This time the apartment lead right out to a landing, and there were a number of people about. I began asking around, perhaps someone had seen something suspicious. My efforts were rewarded, as three separate individuals saw a suspicious man wearing glasses in the lobby right around my presumed time of death. This was not the first time I'd heard of a suspicious bespectacled man near the scene of one of these gruesome murders. But before it was a one-off report. now it was much more convincing. Plus, this lobby had a security system.  I was going to have to find Kang Garden's surveillance hub.After breaking into the security room when the guard went to the bathroom, I was thrilled to see that he had not logged out of his computer. Now I was able to access their camera feed. I accessed the 3rd floor lobby camera and looked for around the time of death. two citizens were detected. The victim's roommate, and an unknown citizen... wearing glasses. I printed out this image and immediately took to the streets, asking if anyone had seen this man! Reports were flooding in of seeing him around carter street. My blood ran cold. Carter street is where my new apartment is located. I Shook it off, and ran to narrow down my search.After canvassing a few more locals on Carter street, I was feeling anxious. Almost hopeless. Until it happened. "That's my friend Larry Shiver. He runs Shiver's management".The whole world stood still for a moment. I finally had my first solid lead. Off I ran to the bar on the corner to find a copy of the city Directory. I found Mr. Shiver's address: Carter Tower, 11th floor. He was a man of wealth. Again I was off like a bat out of hell, desperate for answers. Before I knew it the gate to the lift slid open and I was standing before a single door, 1101 Carter Towers. I Pulled out my scanner, hands trembling, and turned it on. Dozens of prints near the knob, as to be expected. I let the machine do it's thing, humming as it scanned the prints. Fingerprint set "P". Surely this was enough! But I needed to verify that Larry lived alone, and that those were indeed his prints. I knocked on the door, hoping for no answer. I heard footsteps and I ran back to the lift, not wanting to confront the murderer prematurely. I decided to instead go to Shivers management. Companies all keep fingerprint records for all their employees, it would have the evidence I needed. I had to move quickly, it had already been almost a full day since his last killing and I was afraid another innocent would die if I didn't get him behind bars.  I found another copy of the City Directory and looked up Shivers Management.Boyle. Tower. Larry Shivers is the Property Manager the building I was now living in. I could feel my blood boil as I raced to find his office. Security was thankfully lax, I was able to disable the poorly placed cameras and break into his office. Sure enough, his filing cabinet contained the information I needed. Larry Shivers, fingerprint set "P". I wanted to take him down myself, put the bastard in cuffs and call the enforcers on him. But I didn't even know where he was and every second could mean another victim. So I gave up the extra pay for arresting him myself, and instead I rushed my report to city hall, turning it in and ensuring an end to the Terrible reign of the Eden Skinner.

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much potential here - it could easily become the kind of detective simulator game that I've always dreamed of.Pros:- Goes for a very tech-noir Blade Runner vibe and does it well, so if you're a fan of that movie/that kind of atmosphere, you're gonna dig this. The game's current music tracks really help nail that overall feeling - kudos!- The case board and stringing together various clues is very responsive and easy to use. This feature is pretty much perfect in it's current state.- World interaction can be fun and dynamic at times (Ex: I broke a window at a closed SYNC clinic to get something I needed, I came back a day later and found that they had boarded up the window)- Tutorial case is excellent - I would definitely welcome more carefully crafted cases like this one in addition to the random sandbox ones.- Being able to upgrade through various sync discs gives the game a good sense of accomplishment + being able to get a new apartment is a nice incentive for all the money you'll earn from cases and side jobs.- Currently has a good variety of food, items and equipment + various status effects to deal with- The apartment customization system currently has a welcome amount of options to play around with. ay, sometimes you just wanna put a buncha roosters on your bedroom wall and call it a day.- Side jobs offer a nice distraction from the bigger murder cases and offer some pretty impressive rewardsCons:- Sandbox murder cases are a little too similar at the moment - too often it's an angry co-worker or neighbor that kills the person, nothing much more than that as far as I've seen. Looking forward to a lot more variation in future updates. Cases that involve unexpected variables like local gang involvement, dirty business cover-ups, cults (kinda seems like this might already be in the game?), missing people, drug problems, etc. would be great. More dynamic ways for a case to tell an interesting story would be ideal. - NPC interactions are too bland/basic at the moment - the writing needs a lot more character and refinement. More variation in what people say to you would be wonderful. All the NPC's feel like they're roughly the same atm.- Citizens will sometimes say very obvious things ("I work with them, I last saw them here *says address of workplace*") - Citizens are far too rude and uncooperative. I get that it's a dystopian society filled with miserable people, but just asking someone for their name shouldn't be a weird hurdle. I would get welcomed warmly into a store/diner/etc. and then get turned down from that same person on every social option. Pretty strange. - Bugs (as to be expected). One of the most unfortunate bugs I encountered involved my murder case file details becoming randomized again upon reload of a save file.-Technical performance/stuttering - There is a noticeable occasional stutter on my system, but it seems like this is currently being ironed out/fixed.Even with those cons, the foundation here is something special and I very much look forward to the upcoming content updates/bug fixes. Keep up the great work!

_childDocuments_.review: This city ain't what she used to be, see? The jazz-filled nights have turned to echoes of sorrow. Where dames once strutted with grace, they now cower in fear. The flickering neon signs have lost their luster, replaced by a grimy haze. Corruption crawls through every alley like a rat. The crooks in power, once men of honor, now wear their greed like a badge. Yeah, this city's gone sour, but I'm a gumshoe who don't quit. With my fedora tipped low and a smoking cigarette, I'll bring justice back to these mean streets.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Devs,Thank you! <3 This game is unbelievably good for an early access. I bought it only 2 days ago and have already been immersed for 10 hours... In the first 10 minutes of playing, I could just feel the passion and love put in to this, its rare to feel that in titles nowadays. Thank you for a breath of fresh air in the world of detective games, only you have raised the bar. I could see this being the 'Sea of Thieves' of detective games - what I mean by that is nothing else in its genre really would rival it, when you think pirate game you think Sea of Thieves, soon when you think detective game you will think Shadows of Doubt.I'm already looking forward to upcoming updates, as the possibilities with a game like this are endless; this would even make for the perfect VR game. As for now, ill continue to play it in its current state :) Wishing you nothing but success,Portfolio xoP.S.Some minor things I'd say would be great to have (as of v33.15):- Ability to open and close doors slowly (peek inside)- When moving furniture, for example to climb on when getting to a vent, if i drop it really slowly (low down), then the noise isn't detected throughout the whole house- Not as easy to enter a murder scene (front door) when police are standing outside the door- Sometimes civilian movements inside their houses repeat quite frequently (going in the bathroom every second), so maybe more natural movement(?)- ^^ Overall just making sneaking around houses more immersive

_childDocuments_.review: My previous review started with a sentence: "Shadows of Doubt is incredibly charming, has brilliant foundation and still can be fixed, it's in early access afterall [...]" which now seems like a bad omen or some kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up scenario of monkey's paw curling without me making a wish because the devs seem to want to rush the game to 1.0.The announcement it left me without a Shadow of a Doubt (pun intended) that instead of "Shadows of Doubt" we will be getting "Shadows of What Could've Been" due to the game definitely needing few more months of development at the very least if not years to fix all the fundamental issues and to polish out everything.Below are few snippets of my previous review that I was too lazy to incorporate into the new one, take it as you will. The game is definitely not worth the 25$ it will be sold for starting 23rd of August."For a game seemingly about solving crime, the player generally goes unpunished unless they somehow die, the moment you leave the building the crime has been commited in, the charges/crimes get immedietly cleared and forgiven, making brutal and aggressive approaches to solving crimes or doing things be completely without any risks while increasing the potential rewards. Even if the cameras see you, at worst the security system gets triggered, making it so you have to hide for few minutes depending on your offense and how it was triggered.The cases can sometimes be incredibly opaque due to RNG with how much information you get, especially in side-cases which leads to situations where you have to consider whether you got a very hard case or a bugged one, potentially wasting hours on something that cannot be completed without brute forcing it.You get decent weapon variety for an EA and can even upgrade your fists through sync cards but all of this goes into the trash once you realize that throwing objects really hard and knocking on somebody's door just to barge it open instantly knocks out basically anyone. The npcs also work in bizarre ways, my personal highlights are:- going for a leisurely walk, all bloodied up after murdering their neighbour- shooting somebody out of their window as soon as you leave their apartment- culprit giving away, completely willingly all the information I needed to arrest them while the distressed and confused loved one of the victim was incredibly crude and uncooperative"

_childDocuments_.review: My first case was a learning experience for me, as I chose to skip the tutorial and learn how to be a detective for myself. I was investigating a case of a corporate murder: the victim was left with a calling (business) card that complained about not getting a promotion and having to prove themselves. The business card had the same purple card as the victim's spouse's company. I had a lead.The victim's spouse worked for a company of SEVERAL disgruntled employees. I snuck in at night, took every ounce of information I could on all the workers, deduced that it was a "Samuel Trejo", and went about tracking them down. Everything seemed to line up, same apartment block, recently on probation at the job, incredibly abrasive when approached... all signs were pointing to this. It seemed perfect, kill the spouse as an intimidation tactic to get the promotion. But something wasn't adding up. That would be far too obvious. The spouse would immediately know who committed the murder. But the business card, it CAME from the spouse's business....But then I realized it was a red herring. The murderer had grabbed one of the business cards of the spouse's business to throw off my trail, and they had succeeded. It wasn't an intimidation tactic, it was a straight up act of retaliation. The employee and killer was from the victim's very own company. It was at this point that I discovered the fingerprint scanner (remember, no tutorial). I sprinted back and scanned the crime scene, found a fingerprint on the business/calling card. Ran to the victim's company and bought myself a guest pass to look around. There it was, a matching fingerprint, sitting right on the name placard of "Baran Naifeh". I snuck into city hall that night and ran the check in the government database - it was a match. I broke into the suspect's apartment while he was away and found a note describing the murder, seemingly written in a sick and twisted manner to reminisce on the fear of the victim. I had my evidence. I submitted my case, and after one fee for mispelling the name (whoops), I got the case solved and closed. Badabing, badaboom. I had solved a case due to a revelation and it felt GOOD. I went to the diner to celebrate and saw an advertisement for an apartment I could buy while munching on a hamburger.At this point I sat back from the game, and realized it expected me to stay in the world, to keep solving crimes. To watch as these people and businesses went about their lives, and to participate in this incredibly deep immersive simulation. It was wild, this was now a world that would have conflict and I would learn to resolve it.So I immediately started a new "Very Large" city, created a character I wanted to stick with, and got ready to dive in.Get this game, seriously. ImSims are getting better and better because of indie devs, and this one shines bright among such great titles already. It's fascinating to play, and that "eureka moment" is pure bliss. It's fun, it pulls you in, and you genuinely feel like you're a part of the world. Just the feeling of having a game where you can interact with everything and everyone is one thing, but having all those interactions mean something is even more impressive. Thank you to the dev Cole for such a wicked cool game.

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing before 1.0 and was very excited by the game. It had a lot of potential, the base of a really good game was there.Sure, the lighting was iffy, and there was some stuttering, and you didn't mess around with the city builder too much because it always seemed to be full of weird issues, but the foundation of something great was there.I've never once had a run at this game that went well start to finish. What I have had is:- notice board missions which stopped spawning details of the job they wanted you to do after 4-5 hours.- cities where no one every showed up to work. Meaning businesses just didn't open.- job contacts who tried to mug me on the way to talk to them and subsequently refused to give me all the information before trying to mug me again.- citizens who walk through the floor and down invisible flights of stairs, even in the pre-built city.- businesses that spawn with one side fully open inside an apartment building.- buildings that spawn with air ducts right behind doors so that you can't access apartments.I get that a sim is a huge undertaking, but this game is undercooked, and a waste of money since the dev has no plans to work on anything more than minor bug fixes.Hopefully someone can try this idea again in a few years, because there's the dream of something really special here.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels very immersive at the onset, with high interactivity and good attention to detail. The wow-effect wears down quite fast, compounded by the abominable performance, voxelised characters that look like walking rectangles, the lack of content and unique scenarios, and tons of bugs.The fully simulated city life sounds great, but in the current iteration feels rather dull, and imposes its own limits on the game. It also heavily relies on the player's willingness to roleplay, because without it nothing stops you from breaking into anyone's flat and stabbing them permanently unconcious while you do your thing. A citizen can spill an entire ocean of blood, but nothing ever kills them for good, as they get back up in mere minutes. They can get angry, but no one seems to remember you for any extended periods of time, so your actions feel inconsequential as a result. You can get incapacitated in a fight, end up in the city hall infirmary, storm through the front doors to avoid the treatment bill, and the police will shrug it off.The game does feel refreshing as one of the immersive sims, which have always been in short supply these years; however, it's far from finished, and the current experience is too rough.

_childDocuments_.review: I think my 25 hours is a thorough playthrough for the state the game is in as of writing this and I gotta say this is a very refreshing and unique game to play and I will definitely be revisiting it often. You might struggle to solve your first case but once you do you will be hit with the greatest sense of satisfaction you've likely felt in a video game in a long time. Sure, the game has some bugs now and it is clear that it's in early access but the world building and immersion all point to this becoming a very well executed and downright fun experience as time goes on. _childDocuments_.review: The concept of Shadows of Doubt is great. I really enjoyed playing SoD during Early Access, especially for the first few hours before I figured out how all the cases work. There were a lot of issues for me - no proper motives, bugs and crashes, not enough variety of case types, fingerprints being hugely overpowered - all of which I could look past due to the game's Early Access state. But considering all of these issues are still present in 1.0, I can't look past them anymore.The big 1.0 update introduced one new type of case, an umbrella, some bug fixes (along with more bugs to counteract them), a price rise (this was just before 1.0's release) and a statement from the devs saying "We've finished making the content we wanted to include in the final game. I'm very pleased with the amount of content we've been able to include". Make of that statement what you will. Luckily, the mod scene for this game is great, so it'll probably be left to the modders to expand and enhance this game.It's not a ♥♥♥♥ game, but it's not great. Definitely needed more time in Early Access to flesh it out. I'd say get it, but only if there's a decent sale. Otherwise, I'd probably leave it.

_childDocuments_.review: The story of detective Ace BandageIt was a rainy day in Charlotte Heights and I was sitting in a run down diner contemplating what I could do to make some money when I saw a posting by the payphone. It was from a troubled citizen looking for her prop gun. They requested a detective to find it. So as a good man and a poor schmuck I phoned the number on the note in hopes this person answered so I could finally make some money for a decent meal, and it seemed my luck finally turned around.The person was Niharika Vaish, a small time employee at a local joint. She provided me her address to come investigate someone taking her prop gun from her night stand. I quickly ran over to her apartment and knocked on her door. She looked very troubled and begged me to find it the prop gun giving me full access to her home. It was truly disheartening.I looked in her room for some fingerprints and found a safe. My curiosity took over but the safe was locked by a key-code, but as a true detective I have already found the pass-code on Niharikas desk. I made sure she was in the living room sitting around, opened her safe and stole all of her belongings, ran out the door, closed the case and went to buy a decent meal.10/10, I am the best Detective.
