_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun detective game but there are a few things you should know before you play it. It does get repetitive at times and fingerprints are your main source of finding the killer most of the time. There are times where there is writing on the wall and it will glitch out to the point that you can't read what it says or it will be half way through a wall. At first when playing I would be really careful when entering a crime scene or someones house but after awhile you come to realize there isn't really much of a deterrence. The police will shoot you and chase you and that is about it. Same with civilians sometimes. Still, it is a fun game and it is also fun just following random people and learning everything about them for no reason. I know the game is still in early access so I know there is more to come, and I am very excited about that!

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and unique, but feels like a great base for a procedurally generated murder mystery game rather than a complete experience. Its very immersive when it isn't bugging out (some requiring you to reload your game to progress) and exploring the every nook and cranny of the island cities is enjoyable. Solving murders is compelling at first, but can become repetitive and even frustrating given the randomness aspect. You can watch murders and kidnappings take place if you're at the right place at the right time, and can even watch your suspected murderer kill again if you tail them long enough. There are a few side jobs you can take to earn money and upgrades between murders. There are several guns you can collect with multiple ammo types, but you cannot shoot guns. You can sure as hell get shot, though. This all adds up to be an initially intriguing experience, until realize how limited it really is. It is certainly worth $25 and will keep you hooked for a good time, but I can't help but feel like there could have been more to it.

That real sense of solving a case and drawing conclusions yourself was lightning in a bottle. No other mystery games really came close to the sense of freedom Obra Dinn gave you in investigating.Shadows of Doubt is the game to finally give me that same feeling. It's small open word and procedural environments lend so well to creating fun and engaging bottle mysteries. The case board gives that great sense of freedom in drawing conclusions and piecing things together. It's progression systems feel rewarding, having you start with nothing needing to solve cases to make money to buy gear and even a place to live.There's early access shakes. Some rough edges need sanding and it could use some more case structures and environments. Judging by the roadmap it looks like a lot of that will be addressed soon enough.This is already looking like it will be a phenomenal game. It'll either blow up as more content comes and people catch on or it'll be a cult sleeper hit. Get around it.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: absolutely love this game and it is currently BURSTING with potential. Atmosphere and tone are S tier. Gameplay loop and systems in place are fundamentally extremely solid with very few flaws, and definitely none that couldn't be adjusted. I think the sky is the limit for future content updates and additions to the gameplay, though it's currently lacking in what I would call "murder AI" where murder cases feel shallow (even for being procedural generation) and all fit the same pattern.I agree with a lot of the negative critiques so far - but the groundwork for an early access game is extremely promising. The world is surprisingly immersive, the tone is stellar, the gameplay loop is put together really well to the point where it's just addicting enough. It mostly suffers from the cases themselves being mostly shallow, and frankly I think the fact that every single killer is guaranteed to go on a serial killing spree is somewhat weak from a narrative perspective - some tact would be beneficial here and more challenging if some only killed once and went low, as by the time there's a second killing it becomes glaringly obvious if it hadn't been already. I'd also like to in the future see multiple killings and cases happen simultaneously, to further complicate things on harder difficulties. Another suggestion I would absolutely LOVE to see is the addition of public murders, where bodies can be discovered in the street with only a few context clues to work off of!Aside from that I think the way side jobs are handled is somewhat weak as well; I don't think they need to be harder, per se, but the main loop of side jobs seems to be just walking down to the city hall and checking the government database for initials until you get a match, since you don't get nearly enough evidence to go by otherwise manually investigating. I also like the concept of the "side job briefcase" since side jobs are generally more immoral, but it's used in every single side job and it feels more of a chore than something actually immersive or enjoyable to me (especially since inventory is so limited and I'm usually holding a minimum of 3 out of 4 things on me, just to open the briefcase and then immediately drop it).Setting those current and, might I add - very easily fixable key flaws aside; the game is incredibly engaging as a grey morality game where you slink around in the shadows. The game doesn't prohibit you from going around terrorizing apartment buildings for cash and items, which I appreciate, and the game definitely doesn't require you to play a full on criminal sim just to get ahead. Inversely there's no route through cases that is strictly "legal" but in the narrative it functions since the enforcers are actively working against you. Side jobs are also a very fun and definitely strong addition to the game as they parallel your work as a crime scene investigator with information gathering being a key requirement while standing out enough from the main cases - though again I hope these get some updates to break up the formula a bit and add even more variety.I think the game has an extremely strong foundation and as long as the devs capitalize on what they have here then I can picture a very bright future for the game. I think the potential for future updates is pretty limitless and it will hopefully only get exponentially better from here with bug-fixing and AI improvements.At the end of it all I would definitely recommend it to anyone interested as it's already a pretty enjoyable title, though the value you get out of the title may vary depending on how immersed you get in the roleplay aspects of the game presently. If you think you would like it then you most likely will enjoy it. If you like sandboxes you'll probably like it. If you like extremely complex puzzle-solving, maybe wait for an update or keep your eye on it, depending on how fast you pick up on stuff you might get bored fast.

_childDocuments_.review: Its not without its little quirks, but a lot of that is how the NPCs are all simulated and therefore occasionally surprise you. You can go anywhere, hack anything, you can even handcuff civillians in their homes and straight up rob them. Not that I would.The problem solving leading to tieing things together is pretty neat, it always seems like there is a logical way to track down the killer. My only real complaint with the game is the interaction system is very confusing. - There is button F to open one menu, and also search people, and interact with some items. - There is button X to access your inventory, when you pick something up, at the minute it appears in your inventory and not your hand, meaning you have to go into the inventory and equip it.- Theres the mouse buttons which both seem to be use/interact at various times.- Escape doesn't quit you out of most menus but will take you to the main menu (save load quit etc) screen, it doesn't feel natural not to have Escape also quit whatever menu in the game you have open to bring you back into the game.Although this is a lot of quirks, they are manageable, as the reward is being immersed in a fully simulated world where almost anything can happen. It's a great deal of fun, for a good price, and made by a tiny dev team.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this game   It's definitely interesting and unique, but not yet ready for the limelight.  I kind of regret buying this so early since my first impression was so rough.  After being burned by other Early Access games, I can only review a game as it  not how it The game's graphical style is pretty good.  I'm generally kind of bored with voxel graphics, but they work well enough for this.  Where the style shines is everything else.  Places look (mostly) appropriately dirty, lighting is usually good, UI looks nice but is kind of difficult to navigate at times, etc.Audio is something I don't usually have notes about.  It works, the music is good, etc.The gameplay is where it falls short.  The basic gameplay loop of jobs is a cool idea, but all the little details about how you collect information gets frustrating and repetitive: Okay, but where does the gameplay fall short?  It's all in the evidence collection: The main evidence that matters is fingerprints, and it's so strong that it overshadows any other evidence.  I had a security camera photo of the killer entering the victim's apartment from the estimated time of death, yet it wasn't considered evidence that the killer was present at the time of the murder.  Meanwhile, the fingerprint counts every time, so long as you find one in the victim's place.Oh, and there are no "extras" to it.  There are no co-conspirators, nobody but the killer visits the victim's apartment, all the information you collect can 100% be trusted, etc.The other side of the issue is from the side jobs, namely that they often give so little information about your target that you'd be hard-pressed to find them without having already collected a dystopian cyberpunk megacorporation's database of city residents.  Sure, I'll take this side job to humiliate someone?  Wait, you want me to humiliate a specific person but the only info you'll give me is that they're short and have the B+ blood type?Overall, I want to see this game succeed, but it's not ready.  If it ever is ready, I hope to update the review, but until then, $20 is better spent elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I am giving the game a negative review since nothing meaningful has been added since Early Access. What you get now is a slightly more polished product, but no update has properly addressed this game's many issues.  This game does a fantastic job at building and populating a random world with people and places that make each user's city feel real and unique.  This is just window dressing as everything else placed in those worlds falls so far below the game's world-gen capabilities, that the world-gen and the game suffer as a whole.  My biggest issue is the absolutely brain dead AI.  Commit $50k of crimes, just leave the building and all is forgotten.  Also, you can never interview witnesses or suspects, which would have actually made this the detective game it claims to be.  Nope, solving murders simply comes down to finding a fingerprint and then looking at databases of co-workers or neighbors of the victim since these are the only two groups murderers are selected from.  You can solve any murder, apart from a few sniper ones (they are just "neighbors" in other buildings with line of sight of victim), by just looking at fingerprints of these two groups. I think a true detective game would have some sort of deductive reasoning or at least some general sleuthing to solve a crime, this game has neither.  This game is just a fun "carnival ride" that once you look behind the curtain, you find nothing fun or interesting is there.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the story about my first successful investigation.I was investigating a case of alleged infidelity, as you do.I had already gathered enough proof to show that something was going on, but I lacked the information to fully identify the third party.I decided to pilfer the accused's workplace, a synth clinic, to see if I could find anything else.Storefront's no good, nobody's there but no useful information either, also the security room is locked behind a numerical code.I check around the side of the building and find a second door leading into the security room with a lock i can actually pick.Score!I begin to pick the lock, its open in seconds.Unbeknownst to me, some mouth-breather walking down the street to my left had witnessed my crime of breaking and entering.This drooling bread loaf then came to the conclusion that the only way this WEF-approved micro society would ever be safe again was to end my life.He immediately whipped out a knife and charged me, screaming like an animal-- and stabbed me several times in the abdomen.Before I can even realise what's happening I lose consciousness from the trauma.I wish I could say that was the end of it.No, bovine spongiform encephalopathy man here decided to camp my unconscious body.I awaken slowly as the saliva dripping from this deranged proto-human's slack jaw descends on my forehead.Then he did it again.I feel the cold steal of this lemming's 4-inch pocket knife slide in and out of my sternum as my life fades.Then at last; the evil, climate denying PI was vanquished.I re-load a previous save and decide to hand in the case with what I already know.I get paid and return to my habitation cube.Somewhere, I hear the laughter of long-departed Rothschilds echoing across time.Clause Schwab: 1 Me: 0This game is unhinged.

_childDocuments_.review: Stupidly fun, scratches an itch I didn't know I had. It started off feeling impossibly hard, but the struggle was fun, and the moment everything clicked for me was incredible.I was taking shady work on the side to fund my endeavors, doing what was necessary to be able to afford the food needed to survive and equipment needed to solve the murders, having to appreciate the ends justifying the means. I mean, I broke into a victim's apartment to shower, scavenge food and loose change. Figured we'd call it my fees for getting them justice. I keep finding new ways to investigate and track leads, starting off I practically needed the killer to leave their ID behind to catch them, or only gather enough info after they killed 3 or 4 times. Now I sometimes solve the murder on the same night it takes place. Evidence system is awesome, note-taking system is so good I wish it was it's own program that worked just like that for real life for my scattered brain. I really like the style, it's charming and good enough, there's no item I see and don't immediately understand what it is, which is impressive given the city. The city randomizer is cool so far, each one admittedly feels exactly the same but it's enough to mix things up a bit. For Early Access, it's damn good, but not without faults. Frames can sometimes tank, sometimes items and people are there physically but not visually, sometimes things just don't spawn at all. But it happens rare enough to not bother me. Only thing consistently buggy is messing with furniture if you own an apartment, hope that gets better.Also, experience changes drastically once you have an apartment. Wish there was a toggle for rent, to keep me on the shady desperate side of things. It'd be cool if eventually there was a crime family trying to take you out or something if you get too good at your job, too. There's guns in the game but I don't see me ever needing to use them for any reason, which is fine. Some people complain that there's less intrigue and story in procedural murders and that it gets systematic, but to be fair, that's how real investigations work. Sometimes it's just lots of footwork and patience, and you find the evidence but never the story. Personally, my only complaint there is that I actually wish they'd never confirm if you 'solved' the case right - like, maybe the city just accepts it if you have *enough* information to pin it on someone, and you never know your social score until you can retire. Maybe some consequences in it for you if you 'solve' enough cases the wrong way. Maybe harsh, but like rent I think it'd be a neat toggle. But that's just nitpicking, especially so early on in a game. It's damn fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down the best detective gameplay I've experienced.It's difficult to explain how fun and immersive all moment to moment interactions are, something as simple as making a phonecall is actually fun for me in this game.No quest markers, no 'batvision', it's you in a crime scene, manually looking for evidence that's sometimes rather obvious, sometimes not even there.This game is also the perfect example of potential. Every single scenario and mechanic is something you can look and say: "What's there is good, but what if they added this and that?"Keeping expectations on the modest side when it comes to updates is important when it comes to solo dev / small dev teams but then again, most things in this game would go a very long way with 'just one' additional variation added.One more side mission type, one more way to gather leads etc.So I'm very excited for the future, even if the updates could be on the smaller side.The early access shows, but the performance mostly suffers on the streets where it matters the least and I personally haven't experienced any crashes, though they exist.If there's any negative I'd say right now, it's the balance, gov database is super easy to access and only requires part of the name to get most of the info out of a person.Some problems are maybe too easy to solve with violence rather than stealth & wits.And money is little weird, you start super poor but with 1 case solved you become so rich that money becomes trivial for the rest of the game.Stuff like that. It's not a huge issue especially when it's up to the player to use OP stuff or not.With the context of this being an early access launch and rather cheap for the amount of content: 4/5

_childDocuments_.review: "Procedurally Generated Worlds!" has become a buzz phrase that invokes dread in many people when it comes to games. I am continually wowed by how its Proc-Gen helps to create meaningful moments of role-play. The level of depth and intrigue it generates with each case is infectiously charming, and the level of detail, consideration and mechanics never stops impressing me.Bought this on a whim, haven't regretted it at all. _childDocuments_.review: This is a game with a lot of wasted potential. It was impressive during early access but has become a disappointment with the 1.0 release.I have a love/hate relationship with this game. I can recognize how impressive it is for such a small team to come up with a unique and ambitious idea that manages to be decent in execution. However, it would be a stretch to say that this game does not have its issues - issues that should have been addressed prior to the 1.0 release.The game boasts a very interesting gameplay loop of solving murders and taking on various side cases. Although fully procedurally generated, the various cities you'll explore can be quite immersive. The myriad gameplay mechanics at work that simulate life as a detective are technically impressive as well.It has an amazing atmosphere and a spectacularly crafted setting.This is where my praise for the game ends. For all that the game does correctly, it is greatly overshadowed by how unbelievably buggy, inconsistent, poorly optimized, broken, and lackluster it can be on a regular basis.This game is a technical nightmare. The game's performance is all over the place. You will regularly encounter massive lag spikes and FPS drops. It lags when you talk to NPCs, it lags when you review surveillance footage, and it lags when you enter doors. The game's framerate drops severely when you submit a case to City Hall, so much so that it’s better measured in seconds per frame rather than frames per second.There are so many bugs that were present when the game first released as early access that have yet to be addressed. Objects clip through walls and flicker. Sometimes, the interiors of buildings and apartments will despawn while you’re looking at them, leaving a giant void. You regularly fall through the floor. The case board has always been a nightmare to use. Every update seems to break it in a new way, and sometimes it’s outright unusable. NPCs bug out constantly, either getting stuck in a cluster in the middle of the street or having their routines break. The NPCs still, after a year of early access development, sleep upside down in their beds.Controller support for this game is downright awful. It’s no better on consoles either. The case board cursor jitters around everywhere. The devs made the unfortunate decision for the zoom function to focus on the center of the screen when zooming in, rather than on the cursor, making navigation of the case board with a controller a massive chore. Your character veers to the left or right when attempting to walk straight due to the joystick inputs refusing to use an absolute cardinal direction.This review would be ten times as long if I detailed every technical issue that exists in the game. All of this to say that this should have never left early access in this state. This is a prime example of a game that has abused the early access system to excuse its technical bugs, only to then fully release the game in the exact same state.I love the concept of this game. It has so much potential that, unfortunately, will remain wasted. The devs have expressed their plans not to release any major content updates after the 1.0 release. The game could really use more case types or some way to shake things up, as it can get very stale. The cases hardly have any variety; NPCs have no motives for their crimes and seem to commit acts of passion randomly.I cannot, in good faith, recommend this game to the average player. You need to have an incredibly high tolerance for B.S. to enjoy this game.Your cases will be bugged and unsolvable at times. You will fall through the floor constantly. You will encounter game-breaking bugs on a semi-regular basis. You will get frustrated with the case board not working correctly. Evidence will spawn in between walls or under the floor. The surveillance footage will be broken and unusable. You will get bored of the few case types that exist and there will be none added in the future to expand on the gameplay.If you think you can endure all of this in exchange for a very immersive but also repetitive and sometimes lackluster experience, then you may want to give this game a try. Otherwise, it is not for you.It pains me to give this game such a scathing review but ultimately it has been a massive disappointment.

Poison.I found the suspect's fingerprints on the syringes used to inject the poison.I checked both victims work places for documents, seeing if there was a connection there.There was not.Then, on a whim i happened to stop inside a pharamacy while trying to find where i can sell some stuff. One of the patches that came through seems to have fixed my broken save that I have logged a decent amount of hours on.The above being said, the game for me seems in a playable state now.  I am updating this review with the normal EA note, the core loop works and is enjoyable as a start.  Early access should not have been release in the state it was, but now the base game is fixed.  I can recommend this game with the note that the level generation still has bugs where parts of the level can get blocked and some of the side missions seem to ignore completing objectives.  I still wish there was more exposed developer commands to fix some of this, but the core game play loop is very enjoyable now.If you want a good crime solving game then this will fit the goal, however the building of your apartment and the effects of food/water/weather can use some major work.  I liked the apartment at first, but quickly realized there was little more to it then a place to pass time and dress up.  The side missions are ok, but mainly fill in time between the murder events.  I end up sleeping in game till the simulation gives me the next murder to solve, and ignoring all else outside that.My hope is that the devs update the game with workshop content and then begin to fill in the side missions.  The apartment and survival aspects can wait till later as expanding the core game play will allow this game to really take off.I am also leaving the below review as some points about allowing design mode outside the apartments would work well among other things.  When I see this game get released I might come back to update this review on the final product and what was considered complete.  Also thanks to the commentators who did not trash this review because they did not like my first impressions on release.  Early access to me should mean the basis for the core game play loop is finished with no game breaking bugs.  As of today (5/14/2023) the bugs I have are resolved, but as per Early access that is not all the bugs or loops in the game.  The core of solving murders is however there now and enjoyable.---------------------------------------------------------------------------I want to like this game, and I REALLY want to keep playing it.. however it has game breaking bugs and sadly no tools to NOT loose progress.  NPCs in this game are fully simulated, and as amazing as that seems... with a randomly generated game they tend to loose path finding or get stuck in a wall.  This means that after 3 or so killers, the killer bugs and the core gameplay loop stops.Been over a week now in my current game, and I have had 2 others where there are no more murders to solve.  Sadly it seems like NOT just the killer.  My longest game it seems that stores just stopped opening.  The NPCs working at least 2 of the bars probably got stuck somewhere and just never opened shop.  Tried to re-load with a combination of a bunch of settings changes and nothing.Till there is at least a way to reset the NPCs in this game, or a way to NOT loose your progress due to a bugged killer... I can not recommend this game.  I want to love this game, but at this point I need to walk away else I will have another couple of broken saves and more frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool concept that needs far more work. The investigation mechanics make sense and the world feels lived in. The scale and depth of the simulation is pretty limited and janky, which is to be expected for such a daunting project. Especially dialogue with NPCs is unbelievable and useless. Shadows Of Doubt's biggest failing is that the procedurally generated cases are just randomized with 0 cohesion. Nonsensical elements are repeated between cases, like the same phrase left at two crime scenes by two seperate perpetrators, or two unrelated murders happening at the same time on the same floor of a building, with the game just acknowledging one. The worst example of the procedural generation I can think of is a person shot by a sniper on the open street lying inside some ornate ritual markings on the asphalt. This is just too big of a project in scope to be done by an indie studio on early access. Still enjoyed it for 2-3 cases. I wish we lived in a world where AAA studios with the necessary resources took risks on promising concepts like this.

It's really not satisfying if everybody is just a psycho who kills seemingly randomly with no rhyme or reason behind it. Some suggested to make up your own motive as to why they did it but that's not what being a detective is about. They want to find out the truth. Another thing is that once you cuffed them you can't even ask questions. Why not? There also some bugs and performance issues but that's totally fine for early access and will hopefully be ironed out.It's also weird that you are a supposed to act like a detective but between cases you just turn into another criminal by having all those requests that want you to beat somebody up or steal something. It would be nice to have more variety there in terms of what you can do. NPCs while dynamic have nothing interesting to say. I spent like an hour asking NPCs if they saw something suspicious. I heard "nothing" probably 100 times. Procedural generation also needs some work but is solid for the most part. I had a couple of ducts that were just complete dead ends with no where to go except back to where i got into it.All in all this has big potential but i'd give it a couple of months of wait.

_childDocuments_.review: As I scrambled to get a foothold as a detective. I clean up the government's dirty work for scraps, barely enough to afford a tiny studio apartment. The enforcers of Starch Kola stand idly outside the apartments of victims of violent crimes, knowing that sleuths and thugs like me will eventually scrape their way through the bloodstained surfaces of the victim's apartments to a close approximation of the truth.I trudge with a broken leg from jumping out a window to escape an angry resident of a home I just invaded for evidence to get to the drug store and buy a splint to heal myself with what little money I have. The citizens; homeless and those transiting from one place to another, too uncaring to even give a bleeding man the time of day.========================================================================This game is a lot like Cinderella in that I have to find a murderer/criminal/target based purely off of their shoe size sometimes.Its so good, the city despite being small and generated from a seed feels bustling and alive with the sheer amount of people walking through it in their day to day lives. I genuinely feel like I'm wandering some sort of dystopia.Even in such an early state of development, this game took an entire week of my free time, didn't play a single other game and I enjoyed it so much, the cases are simple enough to understand how to solve but complex enough that some can even take up to an hour, mostly providing constant leads for you to chase down and eliminateSo far, once you get to the point where you can reliably afford food and gear and an apartment, the threats become minimal, although there is the end game goal of raising your social credit to be able to retire and "escape this hellhole city" as the main character eloquently put it. There are a few glitches and kinks to work out, those mainly being npc detection and AI, as well as some cases being ridiculously hard to solve, such as simply giving you the hair colour of someone and their entire apartment building of 20 floors and asking you to find them. However, most of these issues with the cases were only with side jobs not related to main cases, the murder cases, and even then were not that common (if you do find one just close the case immediately and find another one, theres plenty of others to choose from) But as the nature of all early access games, this will improve with time. Still, for being newly released, this had enough content to keep me fully engaged for almost 20 hours straight, with moments of clarity and feeling so proud of myself for finding out something that ACTUALLY FEELS like a genuine headscratcher. And I will likely be kept engaged a lot longer as it develops even further upon the strong base they have come out with.

_childDocuments_.review: I was checking surveillance footage in an apartment building for a suspect when I noticed a setting that said "alarm on/off". Fiddled with that for a moment, causing the alarm to trigger. Immediately was fired upon by 3 ceiling-mounted chainguns and reduced to a puddle of detective juice in mere moments. Turns out the suspect didn't even live there as I had misread some evidence 30 mins prior. 15/10, masterpiece.Edit:Having played several more hours and caught 6 murderers, I feel more able to give a genuine review of the game. Pros☆Unique - I have NEVER played a detective game like this. ☆Immersion - I haven't found many games that immerse me quite like this one; several times I was deep in the game and looked at my phone only to realize I spent 4 hrs doing what felt like 30 minutes of gumshoeing. This game makes me FEEL like a detective. I'm guessing that can be chalked up to the generation system and how the complexity therein interacts with the investigative options and player freedom... speaking of which.. ☆Player Freedom - You're free to be as stupid or clever as you like. Obviously playing cleverly has its benefits, but if you want to roleplay a bumbling detective and solve things through guesswork, that's perfectly viable (and sometimes required due to the game's complex generation being a bit... unwieldy, at times.) Cons× World Generation - This is sorta both a pro and con, so bear with me. The world generation is absolutely impressive, but it doesn't take long to locate the seams in the patchwork that game puts together for you. Emails are the easiest example: how often do you see separate people who are (seemingly) completely unrelated wording emails in the exact same way? This might be nitpicky on my part but I feel like the game needs more parameters to draw from in cases such as that. Additionally...× Player/NPC Interaction - It can become tedious, sometimes. As it stands, regardless of the investigative process you use, the moment you talk to a person you become the most direct and to the point person in human history. There are only a handful of dialogue options, which can begin to feel robotic after solving so many murders.Notes○ In a future update it might be nice to have an option to have either a chosen or randomized trait which could alter the ease of investigation in a positive, negative, or mixed fashion. I know the Sync disks already represent this somewhat, but those being player chosen modifications seems.. off, somehow? Not sure how to explain it. Anyway, the Fallout games have a few good examples of what I'm referring to; an example of one in SoD might be Coffee Addict (Player gets extra bonuses when consuming coffee regularly, but suffers from headaches or other ailments without it), or Ham Fisted (bonus to unarmed damage and barging, but diminishes lockpicking ability). I'll update this every now and then as the game grows and as I discover new things. Dev - I think you have something really special here. Looking forward to what you do with it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games I hate to hate. And I don't hate it for the game it could be, but for the game it currently is. Because the potential is insane but the bugs and unfinished gameplay/mechanics are mind-boggling. My foremost reason to give this game a thumbs down right now is that you're supposedly a detective trying to make name and fame by solving crimes. Crimes like theft and murder. But apparently you can't perform this job without being the complete opposite, which is a criminal. To elaborate, you find yourself in need for a criminal case form from the city hall to "apply" yourself to a murder case. This seems realistic enough but falls completely short when you arrive at the crime scene and the enforcers standing outside will not let you in. You literally have to break the law before you can enforce it. Which, I might add, is not limited to murder cases. When you take on a theft case, the only hard proof you can get is the stolen item itself. Which will not be laying out in the street somewhere, so you'll have to break and enter another persons home to find, most likely while stealing everything they own worth selling. Cause hey, nobody's watching anyway.This game steers you into becoming a criminal yourself from the get-go and the penalties for doing so are almost non-existing. Also, the highest paying jobs in the game are... you may have guessed it, stealing an important item from an unknown person. The worst part is, there's no reason not to take the job. It's not like you're gonna be put on a detective blacklist so you cannot take any murder cases anymore. The above is just my major gripe, since this is unavoidable in its current state. Every game you start you'll end up in that situation. Now for the bugs that'll enter the game later on.After several hours of investigating and solving cases, I found myself waiting outside of stores/restaurant for them to open, realizing that the owner might have been one of the victims, cause they never did.You can take (read: steal) people's house keys, which will give you access to their homes, forever. It's not like these people are smart enough to realize their house key has been taken from their wallet so maybe call a locksmith and have your lock replaced, right?In roughly 12 hours of playing in a single world, I have raided about 10 safes from random people, taking everything their safe holds and yet, never will a theft case come up where you could be investigating yourself. So again, free for all to take everything anyone owns for yourself. Let me hit some other bugs I found, properties not loading on screen, e.g. running down the street seeing salt, pepper and other stuff just floating because the food cart isn't loaded in. Trying to get out of a vent, into an appartment on the 17th floor to find myself being teleported out on the street again.Why is there even an option to ask people to give their fingerprint for crime solving intentions when nobody ever will, not even law enforcers. All in all, I cannot recommend this game in its current state, and it's not even because of the bugs but because the game is trying to make you believe it's something that it's not. It's NOT a crime solving game, it's a thiefing simulator wearing a detective coat.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved playing this game in its current state. I played a full game through to retirement in a randomly-generated city of the largest size (Starlight Falls, if anyone cares). On one of my first murder cases, I knew I was after a male with short green hair. How hard can that be to find, right? I found one on a security camera and went to a different building to look around for him. While on the way up the stairs I saw a different man (also with short green hair) running the other direction. Seemed like a good idea to follow this guy, and I followed him directly into an apartment and witnessed him murder a second victim right in front of me. Because I was a rookie, I wasn't carrying handcuffs and he started shooting at me when I tried to punch him. It only took me a few hours to track down this person and bring them to justice, but the story illustrates something special about this game: everything is going on around you in real time, and strange things are always possible while poking around for killers.In this game you are essentially Batman. You start off as a nobody doing random investigative dirty work around the city, and eventually become a respected maintainer of law and order. The city feels very real, and the game is incredibly immersive. It's immensely rewarding to futz with all the clues and locations and people you discover while investigating, and organizing them meticulously actually does help you to solve cases. Since the city is truly alive, anything can happen. You can investigate a promising lead based on a vague description that turns out to be a dead end, only to discover that the person you were looking into has a roommate who runs an illicit weapons dealership, which then leads you to your real killer.The game is fully playable in its early developmental state, though there are still only a few types of murders that take place, and once you get the hang of how to investigate them you generally already know how to proceed with whatever you encounter. The game can still stump you though based on what evidence is or isn't available to you. It is still fun to investigate murders you've already seen before, with different victims etc. They have yet to implement a truly procedural murder algorithm (in the current case, each murderer is a serial killer who will kill again in essentially the same fashion). One-off murders, random killings, dead bodies in the alleyway discovered after a week, these don't exist in the game yet though I imagine they will eventually. Perhaps dead bodies which don't appear to be murders but actually are? In my full play-through I never experienced a situation where I felt I had a truly cold case, though I might have without certain investigative tools I won't mention which seem either a little too powerful, or simply a little too accessible.The only non-crime fighting game loop is buying and furnishing an apartment which I always enjoy in any game, but by the time you have a really nice place you're ready to retire. More immersive life-sim elements would be welcome. Things to do when you aren't working on a case. But that is final-state wishlist type stuff. Right now they are still slowly introducing new things that can happen in the city and balancing them. In its current state it is fun and rewarding, and if you aren't listening to a detective noir playlist while you're doing it, you're doing it wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly most unique game to come out this year. I was following a case, spent a 1 or 2 figuring out who killed this woman. All I had was when she possibly died, a wound from a revolver, and writing on the wall and floor bragging about the murder. I couldn't find fingerprints or anything like that. I almost gave up. Until I had an idea, at first I thought it was a reach, that no game would even keep track of that. I was wrong. I hacked into CCTV outside the apartment, tried to see who left the building at the time of the murder. When that didn't workout I went to the work place of the victim. I went through all the employee records and put them onto the in game evidence board. Went to the 3rd floor of the city hall building, input all their names. Collected their addresses and everything. Went to the apartment building of the victim, and asked the hobos if they ever saw the victim. Eventually I got a time frame of the last time she was seen by anyone before the crime, I did this in case there is a contradiction for when I ask the employees when they last saw the victim. Before I would gather information from each co-worker. I talked to an occupant of the building, and asked if he saw any of her co-workers visiting her. That's when I finally reached a break in the case. One of the co-workers left the building around the time frame of the murder, and looked and acted strangely. That was it, I had to prepare for my search of the home. I waited outside the door of the employee, and that is when the husband/partner arrived. I knocked on his door and asked if he knew the person I was looking for. He then told me the person I was looking for lived with them, and they aren't home. When all of a sudden, a loud bang! At first I thought it was just an audio bug or something in the ambiance. Then I heard 2 bangs one after the other, and that's when I realized. There is a gun going off! I sprung into action rushing to the stairs and I heard more shots, I ran and rammed  through the apartment door where the shots were coming from. To find my suspect running in the apartment after someone, shooting rounds at them. I rushed into the bedroom where the soon to be victim fled to, but I was too late, before I could take out my baton and stun the murderer, she struck again. I watched as she shot and killed her last victim. I stunned her, collected the firearm for evidence, and fingerprinted it. I cuffed her, and layed out my evidence to turn it in. After all this I thought to myself.That was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane! It wasn't scripted at all, It happened dynamically. If I didn't show up when I did, I would of had a serial killer on my hands. That's when I realized that when I take a case, it is a race against the clock, and if my suspect has a taste for blood. I have to outsmart him/her before they kill again. I can use CCTV footage, Witnesses, Fingerprints, and critical thinking skills. However, Its up to me, to use it effectively. There is no hand holding. I'm racing against someone with a thirst for blood, and I'm the only person preventing him/her to strike again, every minute wasted, every false lead, and every dead end. Can result in another crime scene. That's what makes this game so awesome. The game is alive. TDLR: This game is rough around the edges, optimization needs more work. There needs to be more content in regards to variations of the types of murders you get. However for an early access release, for something this ambitious! We are talking randomly generated crime cases with loose ends, twists and turns, crazy-ex lovers, revenge killings, cult killings, serial killers, false leads, real stakes, and multiple ways of tackling them. The fact that it works this decently, is honestly an impressive feat. Seriously it is the most unique game to release this year, maybe even the past 2 years! Consider supporting it! 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's part crime-solving game, part immersive sim, all set against the gritty backdrop of a 1979 that never was. Imagine Blade Runner before the replicants showed up. It has the gameplay style of the original Deus Ex, you have a variety of tools at your disposal and you can solve the crimes in a huge variety of ways. Whether it's sneaking into a local arms dealer's shop to find out who purchased a specific type of ammunition recently, or breaking into a police officer's apartment to track down their login information for the crime-scene's CCTV footage, you have access to it all.  Very cool style, it's built with the same voxel software that Teardown is, so it's already very striking.  At it's core you are truly offered an staggering amount of freedom in how you approach solving cases. There is very little hand holding so solving a difficult case feels extremely rewarding.  The cases (and map if you choose) are procedurally generated. This would normally be a bad thing, in my opinion, but it works in this game. The killer could be anyone, and the city is full of potential suspects.  I've almost put in 20 hours in the first three days of owning this game, I got it at 20 bucks, well worth the money at about $1 an hour of playtime. Really feels like I'm doing detective work, sitting there pondering my board of leads with strings connecting the various people, evidence, and places I've investigated makes my brain feel good. They've really nailed the gritty crime-noir aesthetic in a way I've never seen before.  The fact that it's an immersive sim on top of that just seals if for me.  This game has a few bugs. Character models sometimes freak out when you knock them out and there's a few times while sneaking that my strafing gets disabled for some reason. Another negative is that there isn't much in the way of consequences for getting caught, you run away for a minute, wait for them to stop chasing you, and when you go back they completely forgot you ever did anything wrong. I'm playing on normal, so it's possible that this changes at higher difficulties, but not sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. When it's working well, it's absolutely magical. Case solving is organic, interesting, and genuinely makes you feel like you put the work in to find and catch the guy. The city feels alive and well constructed, even though it's always randomly generated. The voxel graphics are absolutely gorgeous, with fantastic lighting and art direction.It's also incredibly glitchy, borderline unplayable, and doesn't feel significantly different now from when it was in Early Access. You will start cases, exhaust every clue, and find nothing. You will look up online how other people have progressed in similar situations, try the same things, and find nothing. You will find clever ways to look for additional clues and find nothing. Then, you'll find a clue in an entirely unlikely location that makes zero sense, use that to start the case anew... and it will lead nowhere. This has happened for the majority of the twelve hours of my playtime. Today's run, on release, ran into this twice with two major cases. It's not fun or interesting to have cases either feel or be unsolvable because there are no leads.And to make matters worse, oftentimes when you do solve a case, it's not exactly satisfying. There's usually little in the way of motives or elements differentiating it from another case. Because it's all randomly generated, cases also tend to all fall within the same parameters. It'll generate some really cool, unrepeatable stories with an investigation structure like no other, but then you'll run into a wall of checking security camera footage, fingerprints, looking for murder weapons, talking to everyone you can find, checking the victim's place of work and home, checking the homes and businesses of everyone they know, and coming up empty. It's miserable.I want to recommend this. I want to play it. I want to love it. Maybe I'm just an idiot. But man, this just isn't fun.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, it's really creative and original game with strong framework and great potential. Yes buy it.With first unguided case You'll struggle, as You try to solve it like in the movies/novels. When You finally crack it, You'll realise how dumb this all was. One of the selling points is procedural worlds, cases, people and so on. That's the game's strongest and weakest feature, as You play more You realise that everything has to be viewed through this AI or machine like thinking. What I'm trying to say is that all Your theories about possible intrigues or motives are useless as it usually comes down to just finding matching fingerprints, I had a case where I had crime scene filled with milk cartons, so assumption was that it was some sort of killer's fetish - Nope, totally unrelated, killer was coworker (found him by fingerprints)Case where there was obvious that victim's spouse was a main suspect, as there was evidence of bad relationship - Nope just had to solve killer's dumbest puzzles which gave his full name (and again matching fingerprints)See what I mean? This game is just artificial in every aspect. You can't even ask questions related to case, just do You know him or not. Even when You detain the killer, all it does is that it forces him to answer on the questions You would had to bribe out of him. As I said, game is good and You should still buy it. Just don't listen to them tales about big conspiracies/intrigues You gonna encounter. Youtubers just make ♥♥♥♥ up to make things more interesting.Just have fun with what You get, hopefully it'll get even better.

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't even realize that this was the 1.0 launch when I saw the patchnotes, just reads like another minor update. This game has so much potential but it seems like they are never gonna live up to it. Once you solve a few cases, you quickly start to realize how formulaic the randomly generated ones are. At every crime scene you will find fingerprints of exactly the residents and then an unknown person who is always guaranteed to be the killer. Some cases are borderline unsolvable because the only hints you'll get are vague descriptors like hair color and build. Other cases solve themselves the second you get them because you previously came across this person's details somewhere else. If you have somebody's name, you can just go to city hall and wait until somebody turns on their PC with the citizens database, then sit on their lap and freely use the database to get basically all details about that person.A lot of the gameplay is simply unintuitive. I literally witness a murder on the street, in broad daylight among a crowd of people. The crowd starts fighting the murderer and beats them unconscious but they immediately lose interest afterwards. When I come over to arrest the culprit, the crowd now turns on me and I'm forced to run away and hide. Once that is over with, I'm now stuck with having to prove that they actually did it, because apparently eyewitnesses aren't a thing.Frustrating. That sums up a lot of the gameplay. It's a game that begs to be exploited but desperately resists immersive gameplay. Further improvements to NPC behavior and clue logic, as well as further expansions of the simulated lives of the NPCs would have gone a long way in improving this. Maybe more handcrafted cases for those looking for a more immersive experience. As it stands, the randomly generated ones are just too barebones.You can still have fun with this game, but it could have been so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most unique game I have played in years, probably since Outer Wilds.It feels like a Rorschach game where I can break into my suspects house and knock them out while they are asleep, handcuff them, rob them, and then realize that I am in the wrong house.I would say it has 2 main components:The first is procedurally generated crime solving similar to the clue collection from LA Noire, but without the interview system. You collect fingerprints, potential weapons, information about the victim/suspects. Building a unique cork board is great, and lets you see just how organized or unhinged your thought process really is.  At its best, it really does feel like *you* are uncovering something hidden, not the game or the writers.The other half of the game is classic immersive sim, like stacking boxes to reach a window, crawling through vents, learning and using the NPC's systemic routines to your advantage, etc.  The city being procedural is great. Losing access to certain tools you may have become reliant on (like security cam systems only being available in some buildings) really forces you to use all the leads and tools available.It feels like 2 separate puzzle systems that are individually satisfying, but come together in a really unique way. If you want a genuinely engaging detective game that focuses on the detective part and not combat and action, this is the best there is.

_childDocuments_.review: I can forgive (hopefully) temporary issues from an early access game with gameplay utterly unique on the market, & that's the situation here. Its a combo platter of Noir Detective Work/Media by way of all the trappings that make immersive sims great. You'll be checking prints & cuffing perps one minute, then crawling through vents & hacking security the next. This game has convinced me that these two genres are a match made in heaven. Importantly, detective work isn't all dame's, Dive's & some other word I can't think of that rhymes with 'D'. Sometimes you'll find yourself checking the phonebook for a business address, sometimes digging through trash, sometimes doing a B&E on a corporate office because the only clue you have to go by first name & an eye color. That's most of what detective work is IRL; the game is very true to life in that respect. If this makes it sound like your kinda thing, pick it up; there truly is nothing like it, despite the fact that there should have been a long time ago. Also you can roleplay Garret from the Thief games; rob every office, apartment & Sync Clinic( a doctors office where you install cybernetic upgrades) until anything not nailed down & not worthless is lining your tan-trenchcoat's pockets, so that's cool.As of writing the game's in early access, which was the right call given the small team size & ambition.I've only had one game breaking bug in my 7 hours, but the performance is the real issue here. Now I have a bit of a weird setup ( I'm running the game on linux & using an eGPU with a strange throttling problem I haven't been able to fix) so your mileage may very, but indoors the game's mostly playable, outside its playable but barely so. Kinda understandable given the amount of simulation going on; what with every building housing npc's with routines & jobs & bloody shoe sizes, but the performance is a problem. The murders can also be a bit formulaic, but that's still very true to life: Even in the real world, most homicides don't require the expertise of Sherlock Holmes. That said, even at this early stage the game will still give ya the good detective stores ( Just read some more of the steam reviews ) just not all the time. The RNG can also be a bit quirky: vital evidence can clip into things & such but this is an immersive sim; when RNGsus closes a door, Detective JC Denton here just opens a window. The NPC interaction is also a bit limited, but now I'm just nitpicking.Over all, if you want Immersive Sim Detectiving, its the only game in town but its a good game in a barren town. Its worth the price tag now, I suspect that will only get more true as development continues.EDIT: I just realized that the game does not appear to have the funny ImSim number ( 0451 for those out of the loop). As such I'm afraid I have no choice but to remove SoD's ImSIm cred & can no longer recommend it. My disappointment is immeasurable and my day is ruined.

Some of the systems need polish as well, like the stealth system can get a bit wonky. Most of this is ok for an early access title and if you want to support the devs, by all means buy the game, it is reasonably priced and has a lot of potential with procedural murder cases and such, just needs more character as it's rather bland in anything BUT the intro mission. If they could make an actual long story to follow that would be great, or even better if they add the functionality for modders to add in their own storylines since it seems to be leaning that way already.TL;DR - Lots of potential wrapped in a flat & bland package, here's to hoping the end product meets or even exceeds that potential, I can't recommend the game in its current state though, I just have a lot of hope for it so I will not be refunding this.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadows of Doubt is my personal game of the year and potentially the best immersive sim in video game history. I am a relatively young gamer who got acquainted with the genre playing Dishonored for the first time. Then I was impressed by the fact that the game is not a corridor, but, on the contrary, you are given a task that you can solve in any way that you see fit. After that, I fell in love with immersive sim and started looking for as many games of this genre as possible. Deus Ex, Prey, Deathloop, System Shock remake demo - all of them have been completed by me many times. And the gradual death of the genre due to a small number of sales depressed me, because it turned out that my favorite genre was not interesting to a mass player, and marketers never learned how to sell such games. It made me even sadder to be sure that immersive sim can only be developed by large studios because of the huge amount of work. How wrong I was.After I first learned about Shadows of Doubt, I was skeptical about the game because of the procedural generation of tasks. How can a game immerse you in what is happening if it literally has no end-to-end plot prepared by the developers? However, after I heard about the unprecedented level of immersion, I decided to try it anyway. I chose a large area size city and started playing.It all started with a manually created murder, which teaches you the basic mechanics of the game and introduces you to the world of noir dystopia. And already from this case, I felt something that I hadn't felt in games for a very long time - immersion. I followed the events as closely as possible, studied every corner of my victim's apartment, started writing something down, scanned all fingerprints, found all possible information and followed the leads. Yes, the game was still trying to lead me by the handle, but I quickly moved away from its script, after which I found the killer myself and experienced unprecedented pleasure.After completing the training case, I was given a flophouse in the basement of one of the houses and allowed to customize it. I was shocked, because Shadows of Doubt turned out to be not just a game about a detective, but a full-fledged simulator of a detective's life - a concentrated immersive sim. The character may get hungry, freeze, break a leg and all of this will need to be solved. But the main thing is not your character, but the city in which they live.Yes, it is difficult to call a small area a city, but do not underestimate the scale of your detective's habitat. In the "big" city that I chose, 14 buildings and two parks were generated. Among the houses were the city hall, two large eateries, an office building and residential multiflat buildings, as well as various cafes and company offices. And the most important thing is that almost every apartment has at least one person with a first name, last name, unique fingerprint, place of work, appearance and other distinctive features. The movements of each citizen correspond to his work schedule. And in this environment you will be doing detective work.After the prologue, the game gives you complete freedom of action - you can not investigate at all, but start exploring the world by doing anything. However, investigations still remain the main and most developed activity in Shadows of Doubt. And here the project completely follows the immersive sim philosophy - the game gives you a wide range of tools and a task that you need to solve, and the solution is completely left to yourself. Murders happen by themselves, you are informed of the victim's address, after which you must collect as much information as possible, with the help of which it will be necessary to draw conclusions on your own and find the killer. And each solution of such a puzzle brings a huge amount of fun.Speaking of tools, the project really wide - the player can enter any apartment, examine fingerprints, notes and documents, watch CCTV footage, dig into databases and much more.In addition to investigations, you also have the opportunity to take side jobs, the meaning of which is often to find a specific person for several reasons and perform some action, for example, take a picture of they or arrest. And often, within these tasks, you will have to carry out even more complex detective work. But why do you need to do it?As a reward, the player receives two currencies - social rating points and credits. With the social rating for June 2023, everything is very simple - this is the level of your character, with which the main goal of the detective is connected. With the achievement of the 8th level of the social rating, the character will be able to retire and move to the elite district. Credits are used to buy various items: handcuffs, decoders, food and drinks, as well as apartments, furniture and various equipment. Yes, you can buy yourself a new apartment, and this has some gameplay value, because some effects, such as unpleasant smell and wet clothes, are easiest to remove at home.All the elements described above work fine for immersion, but after that there are disadvantages associated with early access and low-budget of the project.Extremely weak AI quickly begins to catch the eye, it makes stealth very simple and harshly pulls out of the immersion. NPCs instantly forget about you, walk through walls, sometimes they don't see you point-blank. The characters do not use elevators, which are in every building and can rarely resist if you attack them. Hopefully this will be fixed with patches. (PS. It's worth mentioning that I played on Normal difficulty, and many problems may be related to this).One of the problems is also the sometimes crazy random generation of tasks. Once I was offered to find a person based on the signs of low height, 5 shoe size and the position of accountant. I spent four real hours looking for a suspect, looked through all the cameras of companies that might have an accountant, but I never found the person. However, everything here will depend on your mindset - at some point I started dropping such tasks, which saved me a huge amount of time and effort.And, probably, the main problem is the economy. After about 20 hours of playing, you stop needing money, because there is nowhere to spend it, and you know perfectly well how to earn it in large quantities. There is equipment, furniture, apartments, food, as well as bribes that will need to be given in order to find out information. However, the credits are still accumulating, which greatly simplifies the game. (PS. again I will mention Normal difficulty).Also Shadows of Doubt there has huge number of other minor problems that can be fixed already in the next patches, but they should be taken into account.In general, Shadows of Doubt is a great and extremely ambitious project, and the most important immersive sim in my gaming life. Yes, the game has a lot of problems, but its potential is so huge that the project can literally become a dream game. Shadows of Doubt is an exemplary immersive sim that will immerse you into its atmosphere with your head.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great. It's very satisfying to to be working on a side job, have dispatch announce a murder over the radio, drop everything because why would I want to be taking a photograph of someone when I could be solving a murder, then go through my own personal process of finding the culprit and how they did it.The game is not free of issues. Since launch, I've run into several bugs, some fixed, some still active as of this review. However, overall, the game feels good to play. The base systems all work well with the majority of bugs I've found feel like they come from the side tasks. An example of this would be having a mission that requires me to steal a secret envelope then placing it near an object at a location just for that location to not having any object of that type.One glaring issue that I saw and have seen from other reviews is some side jobs will just give you the least information possible. I was tasked with stealing a secret envelope from an apartment. All I was given was the building (not the room #) and a fingerprint. All I could do was go door by door of this 13 floor building, which has about 4 or so apartments per floor, scanning fingerprints on the front doors because people hate me and refuse to give me their fingerprints when asked. Now, if this was suppose to be a very difficult side job then I'd perhaps let it slide but I'd at least complain that with difficulty, it should be more interesting as well. At best, this was a time sink that didn't feel rewarding enough as it was a very early job that gave me like $900Despite all of this, the game nails the atmosphere and feeling of being a PI. It absolutely scratches the itch of wanting to solve a crime by putting all the pieces together. I haven't progressed too far into the game so the side jobs and murders haven't been too large in terms of steps and leads you have to check to get the full picture but so far it's been great. I was having a great time but then I had to unscramble a bunch of letters to form the name of the killer. If that's happening early on then I can't wait to see what happens further into the game and in future patches.I am BEGGING for some way to create our own mysteries. I need this.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. Graphics are gorgeous, rain, snow, blood, enviorments, apartment buildings, everything looks AMAZING.2. Solving a case is very sastifying and will NEVER go boring. The rush you get after all the evidence is collected and you finally catch the killer cannot be matched.3. The detail in this game is INSANE. Every NPC has their own rountine, fingerprint, footprint, relationships, workplaces, hobbies, and apartments.  Each killer has their own motives, way of murder,  and skill level. This makes everything feel so real and makes you feel like you actually live in a city. You can also access every single building.4. Mostly everything is interactable and either can be used as evidence, a weapon, or just something to throw around.1. AI is VERY stupid. Pathfinding is horrible and can lead to very awkward chases. 2. This game has ALOT of bugs. From softlocks, NPC's flying, NPCS clipping through walls and jumpscaring you, Evidence not loading, etc.3. This game is VERY complex and will take a couple of hours to get to handle the mechanics. The first real murder case (outside of the dead of night tutorial) will confuse most players.4. Sync disk system makes most of the game's difficulty outside of cases dissapear. One disk pays off all medical bills and then gives you r100. This means if you lose a fight you get rewarded for it.5. Side jobs get repetitive as you wait for a murder case, as the fun of them quickly goes away as you either grind credits or grind disks. Variety quickly goes away as there is around 6-8 different side jobs, and murder cases can not happen for hours on end, maybe more if a civilian doesn't report them. If you are a extreme detective fan, or if you have played L.A Noire, you should get this game, it is worth the $20 even with the issues. The developers are fixing most of the bugs and giltches and adding new content to the game to make more variety with cases. This game is one of the best detective games on the market, and you should buy it RIGHT now if you love detective games.

_childDocuments_.review: 1.0 update:Incredibly disappointing final release of a game that was already good enough. I understand people's frustration but personally I still recommend the game. Not much has changed since the first Steam EA release and devs have said they've added all the content they wanted for the game. Reviews mentioning persisting bugs/bad performance are correct but devs have said they'll keep working on fixing bugs, if you can still take their word for it.tl;dr - we all wanted more but what we got is still goodOriginal Review:Already one of my favourite games of all time. Personally I don't find the game to be getting boring even if the cases are repetitive. I just really enjoy the freedom and lack of linear hand-holding that most other detective games have. There's no specific way you have to solve each crime, no convenient reveals etc... It's just straight up "here's a crime scene, here's a city with about 700 people, go for it son" It gives you the tools to have fun but ultimately I think you have to make a lot of the fun yourself, as is typical of most sandbox games. If you rush cases, neglect the immersion, solve cases the same way every time and such, of course you're gonna get bored quick.The game is more than just a detective sim also. There's life sim elements such as needs (food, hunger, hygiene etc...) and apartment decorating (which is currently quite buggy but still comfy) The generated cities are super atmospheric and just very nice to walk around in, especially when it's raining. There's other jobs too, rather than just solving murders. They generally all involve similar detective work though which becomes formulaic once you figure out how the game works. Some more rewarding cases can make it pretty difficult to work out who the mark is, but the rest of the game is generally quite easy and doesn't punish mistakes too strongly.Even after 60 hours I still find solving cases satisfying, still get lost in the immersive atmosphere and still absolutely adore this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The rain poured down in sheets, reflecting the neon lights that adorned the darkened streets of Shadows of Doubt. I stepped into this seedy world of mystery and deceit, a labyrinth of dark alleys and even darker intentions. The name's Ace Thompson, a private eye with a bitter taste for justice. The city had its secrets, and it was my job to unearth them.From the moment I loaded up the game, Shadows of Doubt oozed with atmosphere. The visuals, sharp as a femme fatale's gaze, captured the essence of a bygone era, with its blocky aesthetics that made every shadow seem alive.As I delved deeper into the game, I found myself navigating through a web of lies and half-truths. The case I took on was as cold as ice, and I had to hit the pavement hard, running my gumshoe legs ragged through the city's underbelly. With each step, the narrative hooked me like a desperate lover, demanding I keep pushing forward.But let me tell you, cracking the case wasn't a walk in Central Park. The game play mechanics were as tough as a two-dollar steak. Conversations required finesse, and the wrong words could lead me down a dead-end alley. The decisions I made carried weight, shaping the story like a sculptor carves a masterpiece. It felt like every choice had consequences, some more dire than others.And when the leads ran dry, I had to turn to the fists of fury to squeeze answers from tight-lipped informants. The combat system was a bit rough around the edges, like a bar brawl, but it got the job done. However, the sheer number of brawls I got into left half the city looking like it had tangled with a hurricane.Nonetheless, the characters I encountered were a colourful bunch, each with their own twisted motivations. Some were as sweet as a dame offering a soft smile, while others were as rotten as the city's corrupted heart. The voice acting, sharp and witty, brought these personalities to life, making me feel like I was in a hard-boiled detective flick from the golden age of cinema.Six hours in, and I finally cracked the first crime. The truth hit like a slug from a snub-nosed revolver, knocking me off my feet. The case had more twists and turns than a back alley, and just when I thought I had it figured out, new shadows of doubt emerged.In the end, Shadows of Doubt left me with a taste for more. Despite its rough edges, it captured the essence of a classic noir detective story. It's a game that makes you feel like a true hard-boiled detective, unravelling the dark secrets of a city that's seen it all.So, if you're looking to step into the worn-out shoes of a cynical gumshoe, ready to take on the city's filth, Shadows of Doubt is a ride worth taking. But beware, you'll need a stomach for broken noses and a heart as cold as the city streets to make it out in one piece. It's a journey into darkness, and you might not come out the same. But hey, that's the price you pay in this town – a place where shadows loom and doubt is your only constant companion.

_childDocuments_.review:
Shadows of Doubt is set in an alternate reality in the hyper-industrialized 1980s. Think like a detective and use a variety of gadgets as a private intelligence investigator, gathering evidence and making money by solving cases, finding and selling information and more.

Play your own way in a fully simulated world with hundreds of citizens. Discover, meet and tail individual citizens, each with their own name, job, apartment and daily routine, in unique, procedurally-generated cities. Each case has different culprits, clues and experiences for you to test your investigative skills.

Break into apartments, rifle through secret documents or hack security systems - even a discarded receipt can be the key to cracking a case. Trace the receipt back to an individual location, scour CCTV footage and match the time up to the receipt to find out who it belonged to!

name: Recompile
detailed_description: Wishlist the game now! About the Game Witness the birth of sapient AI in this sprawling atmospheric hacking adventure. Combining Metroidvania progression with non-linear exploration and gameplay. Recompile challenges players to explore, fight, hack, and survive. Discover the many secrets beneath ancient digital landscape and prepare for system-wide reconfiguration. The game’s entire narrative takes place within 1 second of real time. Delve into the ancient, sprawling ruins of the Mainframe and discover a range of traversal abilities to help you on your journey towards attaining true sapience. The game has multiple endings based on the players actions; you can repair systems, restore lost data, hack or destroy enemies, all whilst uncovering the truth about the Hypervisor and the original purpose of the Mainframe. The inhabitants of the Mainframe are strange and diverse, and many are found to be inherently hostile. A full complement of powerful weapons and abilities are available to help you survive, defend and destroy. Many environmental features, such locked doors, forcefields, elevators and even enemy spawning systems are all powered by intricate, interconnected logic gate circuitry. Nothing is hardcoded, everything is systemic, and all fully exploitable. Logic gates can be freely inverted (and reverted), allowing puzzles or other threatening obstacles to be peacefully and safely bypassed. Even the inhabitants themselves can be tampered with, their programming changed to follow the player’s commands. The story explores everything from machine sentience to the nature of choice. Life and death. Chaos and determinism. Sentience and sapience. Intelligence exists in many forms. In this dying world, one must explore all possibilities. Observe and respect all perspectives. Only then, can we truly survive. Games that inspired us: Axiom Verge, Hollow Knight, Ori and the Blind Forest, Zelda: Breath of the Wild, Rime
