_childDocuments_.review: Man it's sad giving this game a negative review. If you love 3D platformers and you can put up with some crap then play it. It's got a lot of awesome things going for it. But this game has some serious problems, I highly doubt more than 1 or 2 people actually play tested it. I'm just gonna list all the issues in an arbitrary order. -: - I play with controller and this game has no deadzone setting for the analogue stick. This is a must imho. -: - Pushing Jump always gives you the same jump arch. Devs figured this out in the 80s... or maybe before even. That one is really baffling. -: - Pretty much all geometry in this game shamelessly uses mesh colliders, which is ridiculous. It wastes performance and makes it frustrating to platform. Little details on the floor forcing you to jump over with that ridiculous jump arch. Makes it feel like platforming was an afterthought entirely. The amount of gaps in the ground you can fall through... you wait for the elevators and fall down the shaft trying to walk onto the platform. Colliders are supposed to be slightly bigger than the mesh they're attached to to reduce these issues. Especially the thin pipes to platform on are a complete disaster. -: - This game has biomes which are connected with gates which do feel different enough which is nice. But you need points of interest to get people invested into the levels. Things you see in the distance that you naturally want to check out. But hardly anything in the distance looks worth to check out.Things look so samey I often times forget what direction I even came from. -: - There's nothing wrong making 2 games in 1. You can totally pull off a 3rd person shooter that turns into a 3D platformer at times (or vice versa). But the shooter part is strange, you can't really run while aiming, and there's often times no cover to abuse vs enemies. So if you want to aim you kinda have to tank shots. Why can't you just shoot without aiming? It's strange and I don't see how this is meant to be played. I pretty much just run from enemies and hope for the best. If they are far enough away I snipe them. -: -  They only sometimes allow you to skip forward. If you're a fast reader this will drive you crazy. Especially if you're in the middle of a fight and about to die and you get a text box you have to get through before that last shot kills you. Some text boxes even trigger multiple times if you revisit an area for some reason and you have to get through them again. -: -  You gotta keep in mind that this game is a metroidvaniaish game. But there are some rather unforgiving moments where you manage to reach an area only to find out you can't proceed further without an upgrade or something. Then you have to backtrack the whole thing carefully. This would be fine if the platforming was better. But it is what it is and it just feels bad, like getting punished for exploring.  But this game has many  too. It's creative, it's artsy, the glitch effects are awesome, the sfx are snappy and feel great, destruction physics is cool, the enemies are well designed (tho the combat is disastrous), the universe is interesting tho the way it's presented makes it hard to engage with. I really wish this game was better.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since Metroid: Prime 3 failed to set the world on fire despite releasing on one of the world's most popular consoles, we haven't exactly been spoiled when it comes to 3D Metroid-style games. Usually games that traditionally would've been considered a Metroidvania fall into soulslike trappings, forgoing the thrills of exploration and instead opting to make users partake in difficult and punishing combat.Not Recompile, though. There's not an ounce of soulslikeness found in this game. But it's also not as much of a Metroidvania as you might expect or wish for.After an underwhelming first 20 minutes you find yourself in a hub area that leads to 4 different biomes as well as a final area that you unlock once you finish the 4 respective bosses.Now, you can tackle these biomes in mostly any order you see fit, but to progress you will need certain abilities (i.e. you can't reach the yellow area without double jump, and you can't get very far at all in the blue area without a certain ability I don't want to spoil.)You can sometimes make headway in some areas even if you play them out of the correct order, but if you forgo certain abilities it will be punishingly hard.This game puts a heavy focus on exploration and platforming, which is about what makes up 80% of my time played. The combat, when it does happen, is generally enjoyable. You get a fairly standard assortment of guns (just with topical names, such as the rocket launcher, which this game cheekily calls the BSoD), that all feel really good and are satisfying to use, making enemies set off a barrage of particle effects upon their death. My main complaints about the game have to do with the level design: you travel between biomes with teleporters, making the world feel more like a series of levels rather than an intricate and interconnected web. Also once you're actually in one of these levels, it can be hard to tell where to go, as some of the areas the game asks you to traverse would barely register as a path in other games. There are quite sudden difficulty spikes once you get to the bosses, requiring multiple tries and adjusting your strategy to defeat them. They never feel quite unfair but some one hit kills can be frustrating.Audio-visually, the game is a total stunner. The art style has been masterfully realized and the soundtrack is the best one I've heard in ages. It moves between evoking Breath of the Wild, Kraftwerk and Akira Yamaoka's works in places. Let me be clear: the presentation alone makes this game worth the price of admission.The story, which is centered around a rogue Hypervisor-AI of a space station that made everyone mad is not uninteresting but I doubt it'll be the driving force of anyone playing this game.Performance leaves a lot to be desired, on my very modern rig sporting an RTX 3070 I can barely scratch 100 fps at 1440p. Obviously it's still very playable but I do feel like I should be hitting 144 easily as the graphics in this game are quite simple when you're out of combat.I think for fans of the genre, this game is a no-brainer. It won't quite as satisfyingly scratch that itch as you would hope, but at this point most of us will take just anything for another hit of the formula.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game.Starting out, it felt super promising. Awesome style, great music, and a wonderful environment. But slowly... the cracks in the concept start showing up. The game seems to be really confused about its identity. The first bit of exploring is super interesting, but slowly, jumping from oversized, unclear, gray pentagon to oversized, unclear, gray pentagon gets old. There's nothing really interesting going on. I can't even tell what type of game this is supposed to be. There are mini logic puzzles involving gates, except that there's an ability that lets you instantly skip any of these.There's over-the-shoulder fighting against bosses/enemies, but there are abilities that make these a cake walk.There's 3D platforming, but there's an ability that lets you skip it all.Every interesting part of the game seems to not be fleshed out, and instead you get an ability that lets you just skip all future parts of it.Additionally, the abilities you unlock, some of which are effectively mandatory for progression, are occasionally hidden and it's unclear you missed them. For example, I played through a majority of the game without unlocking the map/tab menu, which is both essential to multiple other parts of the game and is how you can access the in game collectibles later. I didn't have access to this menu for a large portion of my game, making it really awkward for me. This game had some good ideas and concepts, it just feels like none of them are fleshed out. And with me completing the game (with having to backtrack through multiple areas repeatedly to find the essential ability I missed) in only 6 hours, there's just not enough to justify this purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: In my 7.2 hours I was able to get 100% of the achievements, so this review is my complete perspective on the game as I don't see myself replaying it. TLDR: The game has a lot of good and a lot of bad, so it's hard to fully support. Even still, I enjoyed my time with it.The Good:- The game is absolutely stunning to look at, easily one of the prettiest games I've played- The music is very good in a Hyper Light Drifter kind of way. Very understated, but always perfect for the mood- The logs are actually interesting to read. 99% of video game logs I collect without ever actually looking at, but I was engaged with the majority of them here. I especially enjoyed any of the logs involving Saffhi.- The three above points mean that this game is one of my absolute favorites for world building and atmosphere, laying alongside Metro 2033- The game is short enough to fit in two dedicated sittings, but long enough that it doesn't feel like a waste of money- Once you have more upgrades, the exploration feels very good overall- This is the probably best map in any game I've ever playedThe Bad:- When you don't have all the upgrades, the platforming can feel extremely imprecise. This is common with 3D platformers, but it was especially annoying in the levels where you would fall for a good 30 seconds before being reset.- These resets frequently made absolutely no sense on where they placed you, often times feeling completely random- The combat is extremely poor. My biggest problem was that the mouse aiming almost felt like it was snapping on and off of the enemies, making minute movements impossible. It frequently felt like I couldn't aim at a target because it stuck on the left before jumping all the way across to the right without ever actually being over the enemy.- The boss fights were the worst part of the combat. The Cube boss and the Sphere boss are the main annoyances. 1 shot kills are rarely fun and that makes up the majority of both fights. However, the cube boss has a phase where it stops and shoots beam attacks out. The hit registry on these were completely random. There were times that I stood still and took zero damage and other times that I died in a split second. Having no idea how it worked, I simply spammed out as much damage as I could and was lucky that it died before that phase started. With the sphere boss, a similar story took place - laying out enough damage in a few seconds that I didn't have to learn the boss' mechanics.- There are certain parts that are just absolutely confusing. The big one was in the Yellow gated area, where an important pathway was locked off because I could not find the missing path. It legitimately took me an hour to figure out what to do, and I was very annoyed during that hour.Overall, I have so many problems with this game that make it highly unlikely that I will play it again in the future. Despite that, I really appreciate my time with it overall for this playthrough. It was gorgeous to look at and hear, the writing was stellar, and the gameplay had it's good moments. For the price, I'd say it is well worth experiencing this world.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel really bad about this. I REALLY wanted to like this game. I love the premise, and I love Metroidvania games, so when I saw this on Steam I was instantly sold. But after forcing myself through a couple of play sessions I realized that I just wasn't having fun. This game has so much potential to be truly great, but before that can happen, there are a lot of things that need to change:1. it's hard to tell where the "intended" path is. Everything in this game has collision. EVERYTHING. Not only does this lead to really janky platforming, but it's hard to tell what parts of the environment are things I'm intended to walk on and which parts are decoration. This lead me to a lot of dead ends which I'm not really sure if I was supposed to come back to later or not. And speaking of decoration...2. the glitchy polygons effect is just bad. The first time I played I actually thought my game was bugged. Only when you walk close to the object that the polygons make up do they return to normal. The problem is, sometimes these objects are platforms that you're required to walk on, meaning it's impossible to figure out where to go from a distance, or in some cases, even see where you're jumping to. Plus, it obstructs your view, and just generally looks ugly imo. I get what the creators were going for, making the inside of the computer look broken and decrepit, but there are much better ways of conveying that through art rather than slapping the effect on random objects. Personally I think this should be removed from the game altogether, although at the very least there should be an option in the settings to turn it off.3. the map is stylish, but useless. I love the ascii art aesthetic, but representing a 3D environment on a 2D map really doesn't work well. I can't tell what's ground and what isn't, what direction I'm facing, how high an upgrade or gateway is relative to me, etc. Metroidvanias with bad map systems generally suffer for it (for example, Metroid and Metroid II), and unless there's a map upgrade later into the game that I don't know about, this game just isn't very intuitive or fun to navigate.4. it isn't obvious which paths are opened by which upgrades. Sorry to keep going back to Metroid, but in that game, when you reach a dead end, the game makes it very obvious that you need something to go further, even if you don't know yet what that is. Then, when you get the upgrade, you immediately know that you can come back and keep going. I've gotten several upgrades for this game that, despite telling me what they're for, I don't know where in the game I'm supposed to be using them. That, combined with the fact that navigation is generally annoying, doesn't make it super fun to backtrack and figure out where you're now able to go, not to mention intended to go.5. save points aren't easy to identify. They're specific floor shaped objects that often times are made to blend into the environment, and I usually didn't know I was stepping on one until the game told me it had saved. It also shows save points on the map but... well, that's not helpful either. Maybe something that makes save points more obvious would help.6. the logic gate puzzles aren't a great idea. The early logic gate puzzles are cool and help people to learn how logic gates work. But as a computer engineer whose job is basically to work with logic gates all day, I can say that the later ones I've seen are ridiculously complicated. There's an upgrade that allows you to change a logic gate to another one, but doing that requires a currency/drop that you only get from enemies, which are few and far between. So your two options are: pull out a piece of paper and use your specialized college degree to decipher the logic gate puzzle, or grind enemies for points. Both of which seem to lead to about 30 minutes of anti-fun. Maybe for younger players, or players with different career paths, changing the logic gate puzzles to something easier for everyone to understand might be better.7. enemies can hit you from REALLY far away. Most enemies in video games have an agro range, but not these, these enemies will snipe you from across the entire map. And since the firing sound drops off with distance, there's often absolutely no indication that you're being shot at until you've been hit. And good luck getting that health back, because the only way to recover health (other than at specific spots or getting an upgrade) is to kill an enemy and collect its drops. Since enemies can hit you from areas you can't access yet, that usually means if you get sniped, that damage is going to be somewhat permanent. Making these enemies only engage at a much closer range would help a lot with this.I know a lot of things about this game can't just be "fixed", but this is my honest review of my experience with this game so far. I hope this game can become something better in the future, and I really hope it does well, but for now I unfortunately can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very, very boring game. In three hours of gameplay, I've "hacked" exactly one thing. It was a logic gate in needlessly complex "circuit" that was conveniently connected to all three outputs, and I "hacked" it by asking it nicely to invert its output! It took all of one minute, while the rest of three hours was spent:1. Falling through random gaps in platforms, I mean name one other game that leaves a gap between an elevator and the floor around it2. Missing my landings because the player character has no shadow to indicate where you're going to land3. Sustaining fall damage, and often dying, because there are absolutely no depth queues in the levels4. Watching boring unskippable ASCII animations5. Jumping and jumping and jumping and jumping some more6. Not hacking or recompiling anything and not engaging my brain in any way

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions of being about 75% done with the game in about 8 hours. Basically so far there have been 3 areas after the initial tutorial area. Each area has a focus on a specific game type but all of them still have elements of platforming, collection of lore data, finding upgrades for your character, and flipping switches to advance through the area. The HEX (Green Zone) focuses on hacking, where you can use Bits that you have collected from killing enemies to flip switches basically. The TET (Red Zone) focuses on fighting enemies with your gun, this is how you can collect bits and unlock a few abilities that makes combat easier. The OKT (Yellow Zone) is mainly about platforming, here you gain abilities that help with traversal. Trust me when I say this, start with Red, Green, then Yellow. In TET there is an ability that will slow down time to a crawl that has no limit of use. This was almost necessary for fights because the sensitivity is a bit off, you can't look as high as you need to sometimes, and you can't really run and gun as fast as you would want to.Platforming is solid and a lot of the time it made me super anxious, especially the OKT. Tons of tiny platform to land on which can keep you on the edge of your seat. The controls are a little weird, I think most people will want to play it on a controller as some of the abilities are bound to weird keyboard keys like X and I can't find a way to change it in the menus.Overall, this game is more of a platformer with some combat sections and a boss fight at the end of each section. I was kind of hoping there would be more combat than just platforming for long stretches of time but the game is beautiful and it's fun finding all the lore and figuring out how to get to where you need to go. Definitely worth a try! I will edit the review when I finish the game and will post a full review at RectifyGaming as well.

_childDocuments_.review: A first impression for sure, but one strong enough that I won't be spending any more time with this.Disclaimer: This could definitely be a me problem - I'd strongly recommend spending some time with a Let's Play or similar to get a feel for the gameplay before jumping in.I kinda wish I had a rogue program of my own that let me just read all the story pieces. They were intriguing, flavourful and well written. The problem is I have to play the game to keep finding them, which seems to consist of slowly jumping around stacks of featureless polygons looking for the next button to press or thingy to collect. This is occasionally interrupted by somewhat awkward combat, which I imagine was intended to add a sense of danger, but only served to gently irritate me. Add to that the precision platforming - which is always a risky choice at best in 3D - and the fact the background music seems to keep disappearing after a couple of minutes, and it all feels very half-baked.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the aesthetic and concept. But....I've often wondered why developers put so much effort into creating a game, only to screw it by messing up on what is arguably the EASIEST things to fix or adjust.So for example, you could have spent 2+ years building assets, graphical effects, Level environments, manually crafting behaviour, continuity, coding, whatever... then at the end you simply decide NOT to play through it and patch out stupid things that could be fixed in a fraction of the time it took to build them.Like terrible gunplay in a game that requires you to shoot things.Like level areas that make no sense in a game that requires exploration.Like infuriating camera handling delays in a 3rd person game.Like falling arbitrarily killing you in a game that requires you to fall a lot. (why let me in an area if the only way out is to fall and die because that area is "illegal" to land from?)Like the ability to miss an area with an essential upgrade.Can't recommend in current state. Its pretty, but needs a QoL update.Happy to change recommendation if levels are fixed and combat vs 4+hostiles is no longer suicidal due to bad controls.

_childDocuments_.review: Too many issues to make this an enjoyable experience.Supposedly this is a third-person metroidvania, but it hardly plays like one. The upgrades are just a few basic weapons and more jumps/dashing. Not exactly the typical approach that metroidvanias have with cool new features/abilities to unlock new areas of the map.Speaking about the map, prepare to get lost and then frustrated by the map. It's simply not properly thought out as implementation: The world is very 3D (by this I mean a lot of areas use height a lot), but the map is 2D and in ASCII. Good luck figuring out where you are and where you should go with a 2D ASCII representation of a 3D world. I actually gave up on the game in the Blue biome, because I was so lost with so little "sign posting" that I wandered around aimlessly until I decided to spend my time elsewhere.Oh, and the game is called "Recompile" and supposedly I have a "recompile" ability. However, after playing 5 hours I still haven't found the need or use for it. Not sure if this is supposed to be funny or just sad.Story is meh, bosses are meh (your weapons are quite poor, so you end up cheesing the bosses by ). I love the theme though, very Tron-like. But ultimately feels like a very cheap knock-off, so don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are amazing, the story is amazing, the writing is amazing, the gameplay is... very tedious.I was disappointed with the label Metroidvania, as most of the game is very linear with the exception of a gated boss fight and a few late-game levels. There is combat, but it's infrequent and annoying (can't aim above you, but many enemies fly).So what genre is it? To me it's somewhere between:- Zaktronics-like: the puzzles are about tracing logic gates -- think AND/OR/XOR/etc -- which I actually found fun, but I there's no in-game tutorial if you don't already understand digital logic.- Kaizo Mario-lite: At least 75% of the game is about precision platforming, often to blocks which often aren't fully revealed until you're close to landing.The platforming is particularly bad in OKC: many platforms are only 2x as wide as your hitbox and require double-jump-dashes from very specific spots to reach, which are only somewhat helped by an optional upgrade. If you miss a platform, you watch the character fall for 10 seconds and are sent back several platforms, and sent back even further after 10 deaths. I wondered if it was just me, but you can already find videos of people dying for 10min on a jump.And at the time of writing, the movement controls cut out every few seconds (I've tried two mice, two keyboards, and a controller and they all have this problem), which made the precise platforming of OKC unplayable and I had to edit the save file to progress.If you like precise 3D platformers this is your game! If you're really into games I think it's still worth playing to see how good the writing/music/graphics are. But otherwise the gameplay was disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: While i can understand why this game has mixed reviews, for me it ticked basically all the boxes i wanted it to. I want to provide a good idea of exactly what the game is, as i feel like that doesn't really get across very well what with it's metroidvania marketing and such.First thing's First, Recompile is a narrative driven action platformer way before it is a metroidvania. there are metroidvania elements, specifically with level design and pacing, but that takes a backseat to the amazing story it tells. This game does not have a lot of combat. what's there is serviceable, but it is not a focus. You will spend way more time platforming and reading than doing any sort of combat in this game. The weapons available allow for fun shootouts with drones and robots but it is not the forefront.what IS the focus are the amazing graphics and stellar story. The environments do a great job of complimenting the story being told in them through various data logs you pick up. I never encountered any area that felt outright boring, and never found a moment where the story wasn't gripping me.When reading about the Hypervisor AI you are "hacking", you will come to not only feel sorry for it, but the people it attempted to help before going offline. The narrative does a great job of making everything feel desolate, inside a computer of all things. I won't go too far into the story for spoiler reasons of course, but safe to say, the story will probably stick with me for awhile.There are 3 main areas, as well as a smaller sub area. Each with a different theme. Each area's theme not only correlates to a gameplay mechanic, but also a different part of the Hypervisor's Tasks and how it was helping the people it was assigned to. Some people didn't trust it, some trusted it too much. and the relationship between the Hypervisor and it's human companions was probably the most gripping part of the game for me, and what led me to getting every single data log for the true ending (which is the most satisfactory ending as well). The platforming was not as hard for me as it seemed to be for others. Matter of fact i personally ran into 0 camera or controls issues at all. I would however recommend playing this game with a keyboard and mouse if you can, as i could see how a controller could make the combat more tedious than fun in certain parts of the game.I will leave off with this; Recompile is a game made for a particular kind of person. it isn't a flashy combat driven action adventure game. nor will it scratch that 3D metroidvania itch you want scratched so much. Instead, it will take you on a beautiful and emotional adventure through the inside of a long comatose AI, an adventure that i recommend to anyone looking for a great narrative. I probably can't recommend buying this game at full price, what with it's short story. But if you catch it on a good sale, do yourself a favor and give it a try. it may surprise you. I wish the game got more love, as any chance of a sequel are probably dead in the water due to it's mixed reception. I hope my review maybe talked you into giving it a try. Thank you for reading :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential.  It could be really good, but it falls short on 3 major fronts, that most people will just put the game down and not finish it.1) Unskippable dialogue.If more of the dialogue was shown and it could be sped up, that would be ideal.  Instead, the player has to wait for it to be drawn on screen, which wouldn't be too annoying if it was clearer when dialogue would end.  There were so many times where I would think the dialogue was over, but it would just keep going on and on.  Then when it would end, if I had just gotten to a new area, I would regain control, move forward a little bit, and then an unskippable "cutscene" would play showing the whole area.People want to move around and not have to deal with unskippable things like this.  Every once in a while is fine, but it felt like it happened way too often.  I was interested in the story and the dialogue, but the way it was done in game is not to my liking.  It felt too intrusive.2) Which path to take in game.The pathing in the game is fine, but it could be better.  If you don't get the slow-mo upgrade early on, then having to face some of the bosses without it is going to be painful.  The developers should have had the pathing be such that the player would "choose" a path so that they can get key upgrades first.3) Unable to teleport to locations.Why can't I teleport to a gate that I've already visited?  If I need to do any backtracking, which I did near the end trying to figure out what else I needed to do, it makes it so annoying have to basically redo each level again.---There are other things that the developer could improve on quality of life wise, like showing on the map what items have already been gotten, but I don't want to be too hard on the game.  It had a lot of potential and could have been so much better, in fact it still can be so much better if at least #1 and 3 are patched into the game.  #2 would be a bit harder, but I digress.Would I recommend this game?....Maybe.  The story is interesting, the art style is great, the upgrades are cool, plays great on the steam deck.  It's not a bad game, but it's shortcomings are so glaring that it detracts from everything the game does well.

_childDocuments_.review: Terrible experience. The aesthetics and story are good, but the platforming and gunplay are intolerable.The platforming is really unpleasant and relies on you getting upgrades to compensate for the bad platforming, and then you enter OKT and have to do a bunch of precision platforming on random floating platforms to the point where I'm not kidding when I say it felt like playing Bubsy 3D. The gunplay is terrible because most of your weapons are weak. The only one that does respectable damage is the BSoD weapon you get for killing the TET boss, which does splash damage to you if you fire it point blank because it's a grenade launcher. All the other weapons are completely useless. Enemies also have a bad habit of flying directly over your head, which is bad because in FPSes and games where you are in 3D and are locked to two rotational axes, the mouse controls yaw (X) and pitch (Y), so what do you think happens when you look at the camera's "north pole" and try to look left? If you guessed that you just spin in place because you'd need to turn on the roll axis, then you're absolutely right. Aiming while looking up is impossible. So why the hell are enemies floating directly above you where you can't shoot them? Stupid design.I was able to tolerate all of this until I got softlocked. I have been playing the game like a normal person, exploring everything I see and beating the boss and getting to the end before returning to the hub, and I got everything I could find. However, this wasn't enough, as I am stuck in the bottom of ICO near where that portal door is. I do not have a jetpack. The game wouldn't give it to me at the end of OKT. I don't have any hacking abilities. I can't modify logic gates despite the game giving me a hacking mode at the BEGINNING OF THE GAME. A mode I haven't been able to use once. I have over 3700 bits that I can't use, and now I'm stuck in an area that to my understanding is almost impossible to get out of if you don't have the jetpack. WHO DESIGNED THIS?Technically it's not a true softlock as I could theoretically get out if I put a tremendous amount of effort doing extremely difficult and tricky platforming, according to one person in the thread who barely managed to escape the cave, but like hell I'm going to put that much effort into getting out when I don't even know how to progress. Let's imagine that I actually do it. What then? ICO was the last area and my last lead. I was supposed to finish this area and then finish the game. I still don't have any of the hacking abilities like this elusive ability to change logic gates that I've somehow gone the whole game without finding (recall that the game gave me recompile mode at the very beginning and I have had no ability to actually use said mode for the entire game). The ability that I need in order to get the jetpack and open the gate that I'm currently stuck at. If I can somehow get to the gate way out in the boonies that leads to the final boss, I might be able to finish the game, but I already saw someone doing it in a speedrun and just don't care enough to do it myself given that I've just gotten softlocked. To make matters worse, in the thread where other people were complaining about getting stuck in ICO, the devs said they would look into fixing it.♥♥♥♥ this game. I quit.

_childDocuments_.review: I was super excited for this game when I started seeing posts on Reddit about a year back. I added it to my wishlist and immediately bought the game the day it came out. Unfortunately, Recompile didn't really live up to my expectations.PROS:- Atmosphere is awesome.- Story has that "Dark Souls"-like way of being told. You don't have to look at text files at all and just get straight to gameplay.- Metroid-like upgrade system is good when it comes to movement upgrades.CONS:- Platforming was frustrating at parts. Especially in the Yellow Room.- Combat is odd. You can only shoot when aiming down the sights and that slows you to a crawl when a majority of enemies either rush you or have rapid fire weapons. You do get a matrix-like slow down upgrade, but without that, combat would have been even more frustrating than it was.- If you skip story and just focus on gameplay, there isn't a whole lot.- No post-game content (as far as I know). I finished the game in under 7 hours and I would have been happy with a Survival Mode or something to keep me in the game.- Gun upgrades seem useless. Once you get the grenade launcher, you might as well forget the other guns exist. 2 of the 5 are machine guns and one is a laser that's so slow to use, you'd be dead before you got a shot off.- Hacking is almost useless. You can get through most of the game without it and I think there are only 3 instances where it was needed. Overall, it was a good distraction and I enjoyed it despite the frustrations, but I could not recommend this game to anyone.With that being said, it does look like the devs are gonna keep working on it and I'm excited for what they come up with.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into Recompile without any knowledge of the underlying story. From trailers and short clips I assumed that it was your standalone fight-to-survive Metroidvania where it's you vs. the evil machine.Well, I was wrong.The more you venture into the Mainframe, the more you uncover and begin to realise that your fight isn't actually about you at all. You're both trying to complete your task for those who sent you as well as uncover the reason as to why you're here and what has been left for others to uncover. The story came to grip me as I wanted to find out all of the details as to why my character was here and what our purpose was. When I completed the game for the first time, I got a bad ending and couldn't accept leaving it like that so I went back and completed every ending there was to uncover the full picture. Music is fantastic and really has a way of setting the right mood for each moment. Aesthetics are great and coincide with the music very well. There is SOME occasions where the bloom is too high and makes it difficult to see, but this isn't often. I did come across one major bug where sometimes the final boss sequence wouldn't load correctly, forcing me to close the game and restart. Sometimes I had to do this multiple times before it would continue correctly. Overall, great game.*Despite receiving this game for free, it in no way sways my opinion of the title.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not only an enjoyable metroidvania, but much more flexible than most metroidvanias in how you play. There is gating, but it's more soft gating, meaning that multiple skills or abilities will allow you to get through different sections.The game is composed of 3D platforming, logic puzzles, and third-person shooting. These elements are present in fairly even amounts. However, as previously mentioned, the way you tackle these problems is very flexible. Hacking is an ability that effectively lets the player tailor the game to their preference. You can unlock hacking fairly early and it can do various things like modify the logic puzzles, take over enemies, and slow down time. This lets you trivialize or skip challenges that you don't like. However, hacking costs bits, meaning you can't use it to skip the whole game. This meant that I treated hacking like a costly skip button if I was ever just fed up with a challenge. This made the game feel like I was only ever doing the stuff I liked doing. Which in turn meant that I was having fun the entire time I played it.I also didn't even touch on the narrative, which is a fun exploration into the logs of long dead humans who were isolated in space. I really like reading through logs and getting a feel for people who had interesting, difficult, and at times conflicting goals.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially stumbled upon this game when the dev posted pre-alpha work in progress on Imgur. It is really fantastic to see the game finally dropped. TL;DR: Artistically everything one could want from a 3rd person adventure game. Story that draws you in with lore logs that tell a tale of survivors from a time long past. Gameplay (Puzzles/ Shooting) is clunky and rough around the edges like an indy game. Yet for all of its flaws it’s worth the price point.Recompile, for me completed in about 7 hours. Most of that was trying to navigate the levels and figure out how best to approach some of the ‘hacking’ puzzles.  Which… seemed excessively complex and ultimately easy to solve. Maybe that was Phigames’ intention? That said it feels intimidating but shallow, there was a lot of opportunity there missed.It’s clear a lot of thought went into the level design of the game… and the art direction I mean wow! Kind of reminds me of Darwinia in a distant but good way. The developers really captured the idea of being a program inside dystopian system post collapse that didn’t have to borrow directly from other, more well-established visual styles that lean on this team. They didn’t even break immersion buy adding a clunky out of place menu system. I felt like I was navigating an old pre-mouse GUI. Everything, artistically from front to back fit the game’s theme.I admit I blew through the first few lore logs, like who reads those? Well, the entire story are these logs. I really mean it. They are important to the game in such a way the developer ties them neatly into something of a necessity. Progress and the player’s success is measured with the narrative. Not something many game developers will take a chance on! The character’s all felt like they had personality, they had life. They were interesting people and dare I say… I want more! More out of this world, these people, the place we can’t see as players outside of the system we are placed in. So, I was sad to feel that ending hopefully the developer will take another chance on expanding this world.I need to say this; these logs carry weight. I mean I’m just as confused as some of these characters were when things beyond them were being explained. I apricate that the writing didn’t hand hold me, as the player through explaining everything. I’m given enough, told enough to have my own mind hooked and visualize the world being depicted. To me that’s fantastic writing. So much credit to the developers.Point and shoot right? That’s what we are here for. Well… not really. This is where the game falls short. There really isn’t much lost on death so there’s not much risk vs reward. Combat is a little rough. There is weapon options but they are about as shallow as the puzzles… again I get the feeling that this is kind of what the developer wanted.  Nothing too complicated but enough to keep the player engaged and give ‘enough’ of a challenge. As far as traversing the world? It has a little bit of a learning curve, thankfully one of the first abilities the player unlocks is jump! Platforming can be a pain but by the end of the game mobility is no issue.All in all, it’s a visually fantastic game. Some of the level design feels tedious, daunting, honestly hard to traverse at times. Combat is lacking and rough. However, the visual, sound, and story design are everything in this game and well worth a look into as it left me wanting more out of this world outside the system we as player's are dumped into.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Nice story (has a lot of reading and no voice acting) with decent but unpolished combat/platformingThe story is interesting. You have the current day one which is straight forward (you are a program trying to repair a broken computer system) and the backstory of what has happened in the past (which is revealed by collecting text logs in game and explains why/how the system broke). Also there is no voice acting.As for the gameplay it has a few issues:First and most important this game has reverse mouse acceleration (the faster you move the mouse the slower the cursor becomes - and this cant be turned off)Second is that some enemies are a bit too fast for controller aim (no aim assist of any sort)Third the logic gate puzzles can be hit or miss (i personally enjoyed them, but some reviewers didn't)Forth everything has collision, so dead enemies might trip you when running or  dashing (especially problematic on 2 of the bosses - the exit portal is your friend)Fifth and last there is no set order to explore the areas, so some abilities/weapons can be found early or late. But some are quite important in my opinion. One is in the red biome (can help a lot with combat - but i found it last)

_childDocuments_.review: Needs workthe first two areas were pretty fun, but when the game got to the third area, it decided to shift gears to turn into one of those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mascot platformers that forgot that it wasn't a quarter pinching arcade game and became hard as possible to maximize rental timeit required such incredibly precise jumps that I felt like I might have missed an upgrade, and was sequence breaking, but nope, I'm 99% sure that losing entire lives to just missing jumps and falling down bottomless pits was the intended progressionthe hacking system just lets you straight up skip gameplay which is never really good gameplay designupgrading jump height doesn't increase fall damage, which becomes incredibly apparent when you can triple jump off of a spawn platform, and turn what would have been a 6 inch step into a fatal fallthe level design also seems at odds with the art design, with the map being bathed in darkness, with only blindingly bright glows to guide your way, I've fallen off of an edge multiple times because some glowing nonsense was hiding where a ledge was.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit disappointed about this game. The controls just don't  feel good. _childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be frank, this game has a lot of good ideas. It's technically competent. But it's just... not good.Graphics: Well made, but the design is questionable. While the actual models are fine, the environments as a whole are /extremely/ same-y. You're basically jumping between random pieces of rubble. If you told me that the developers just had a few random unity asset packs sitting around and decided to use them to make the graphics, I wouldn't be surprised. Additionally, the environments come in either 'too bright to see', 'too dark to see', or 'covered in fog' way too often for a platforming-based game.Sounds/music: They don't really stand out too much either way. I'm basically neutral on them.Gameplay: I'll divide this into four sections, since there are four basic types of gameplay in this game-Puzzles: Terrible. The puzzles take the form of messes of wires linked by logic gates, which are triggered by pushing buttons. They're either absurdly easy, or complete trial and error. Further, one of the upgrades you can find in this game lets you bypass them completely. Some of them are actually unsolvable without that upgrade.-Combat: Mediocre. You can't move properly while you have your gun out, so you're basically stuck tanking enemy shots to fire back at them a lot of the time. Which you aren't really punished for due to the fact that most enemies drop a lot of healing, so I assume that's somehow by design. The bosses are decently fun, at least.-Platforming: Meh. It's just jumping across strings of floating platforms. There isn't much in the way of interesting challenges to it. In the platforming-dedicated area, there are a handful of moving platforms, but it's really just... not all that interesting.-Exploration: Tedious. The environments feel aimless and pointless. You're floating in a weird monochrome void most of the time, with no real purpose to anything. The character moves too slowly, the paths are extremely unclear, and usually the only reward for going off the beaten path is a lore fragment, which mostly feel like time sinks more than rewards for actually interesting challenges.Story: The closest thing this game has to a saving grace, the story is actually fairly interesting. The only real downside is that it's mostly told through optional lore fragments, which as mentioned, are tedious to acquire. If you're really curious, I'd probably just look up a compilation on Youtube or something; the story is not worth going through the other parts of the game to get at.Overall, the game has some interesting ideas, but it feels almost like the game itself was made by an AI that just copied bits out of other games without really understanding what made them fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a surprisingly fun adventure. I finished this in 12 hours. If you dislike or find 3D platformers challenging then this game is not for you. _childDocuments_.review: A little disappointed with this one. I play a lot of Metroidvania-style games and this one misses a few important marks. The platforming feels weightless, so it's difficult to gauge a lot of the jumps. The combat can also be a neon bleached mess most of the time. While the art style looks cool with stark contrast between glowing neon light and darkness, in practice this leads to a lot of missed jump and hidden gaps. The story is pretty interesting, but mostly presented in log text logs which I personally don't enjoy. I'd much rather the story be told through the environment or at least narrated.All of this is shown off in the video above if you want to see the game in action. Overall I have to recommend you check out a different game if you are looking for a Metroidvania-style action game.

_childDocuments_.review: Should be named "ReJump".This game had a lot of promise right from the beginning, then it turned in to a boring jump fest very quickly. The graphics are great, unless you're near a light emitter, then the entire screen is overpowered by an annoying bright fog. Level design needs work. Retracing your steps after completing some of the levels is very annoying, especially when you're able to make it all the way to the end, only to find out you need an upgrade to proceed. Since you've already dealt with the enemies, it then becomes a jump fest once again to backtrack.The gate/button puzzles are just annoying and convoluted. There's no reward or reason to waste time trying to figure them out when you can just hack one of the gates to get your desired output. It would have been much better if the puzzles actually required some thought and planning, like being able to change the type of gate in order to complete a circuit when powered with a button.Enemies are way too easy in general. _childDocuments_.review: To recompile is to re-assemble information from a variety of sources – and that’s just what you’re tasked with doing in Dear Villagers’ new game. The plot, is oblique, to say the least, with you taking control of semi-sapient program attempting to avoid deletion. As you battle the system from within, you uncover a cautionary tale of artificial intelligence and humanity’s extinction.  Inspired by movies such as Tron and The Matrix, and games such as Rime, Zelda and Axiom Verge, Recompile takes the form of a metroidvania with a sprawling interconnected digital world. Interestingly, and quite uncommon for the genre, everything takes place from a third person perspective. I’d describe the game as a 3D puzzle platformer, reminiscent of the Metroid Prime series in places.  Controlling the humanoid protagonist is similar to many 3D action games, with much focus placed on platforming. Navigating some of the vertical biomes can be quite tricky in places. Persevere though, as mid game upgrades make things much easier.  Talking of upgrades, you acquire new weapons, more manoeuvrability, and the ability to hack systems – the latter being, perhaps, the most original feature of the game. Combat plays out like a third person shooter with one button controlling character strafe movement, and another the cross-hair. Often, hitting switches necessary for solving puzzles, awakens dormant AI enemies, which attack in number. Initially, targeting enemies accurately can be difficult, but the superb Max Payne slow-mo upgrade mitigates this problem considerably. On PC, the game runs beautifully, and looks truly stunning, particularly when you enter a new area and are presented with a panning shot of the biome before you. The size and scale of the game world is breath-taking, sublime even. The plot becomes more intriguing as the game goes on; with the data files you collect revealing more about the origins of the rogue AI. Plus, there’s multiple endings to give you reason to play it all again. Don't write this game off after an hour, as it really takes some time to hit its stride!

_childDocuments_.review: Really went into this game wanting to like it and I'm mixed.-The Demo-I played the demo since I love neon and synthetic world kinds of aesthetics (Tron, Fract OSC, Heavy Bullets, Reboot, ect). It just has a cool world look/tone and feel. I'm for it.Real good conveyance for where to go and what to do, and the ability progression was so well paced and rewarding.Great demo, I was excited for this game ever since.-The Game-Playing this game still has a cool look/tone and feel. I really like the main character's flashes of light, the particle effects and jitter. The world is a particle effects display that is so enjoyable. The music is atmospheric, sometimes peaceful, sometimes foreboding, and a good mix of synthetic and orchestral. It lends to the game and ramps up for enemies and bosses in all the right ways. I wish I could make it quieter via in-game controls, but that could be fixed at later patches. Maybe I was never meant to ignore the music, maybe the game wants me to listen and be enveloped. I was. This game has a very slow start. Conveyance varies level to level and while there are two paths after the initial tutorial stage, the better option to progress is clearly one over the other (It's TET, go red, HEX is much more fun as a green stage after TET). During these stages you are at a low mobility point, once you get the blink ability and a double jump it's very serviceable, but still lacking. Had to watch a video two times when I got lost and even tried to restart my game completely before watching those videos in case I lost something, but there was no option to start a new game through option or main menu functions (maybe that will get fixed in later patches). Once you are at full FTL mobility it feels incredible to move around the stage. The bursts of energy and acceleration, coupled with the later slow motion controls is everything I wanted. It's the feeling I wanted since the demo. You feel invincible and unhindered.The story is all told through text files reflected in each of the biomes that get repaired. There are some buried elements in it, but the characters and their methods of type/speaking distinguish them enough to be a varied experience. Some elements are very cleverly buried and you can tell something is off from the get-go. The reveal is interesting but I wasn't overly impressed. This game was much more visuals and game-play for me, but I did read words they wrote. They happened.The ending to this game was just a powerful presence. I did the 100% ending and watched the other ones online and I was pleased with it. ---TLDR: Cool visuals, atmospheric music, fun abilities but a bit of a time sink to get there, ok story and decent ending.Get on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not very compelled to write bad reviews but Recompile really does everything to hinder the player's progress without delivering any motivation or explanation. The fact that the level design is non-linear with many hidden paths is not the problem although it becomes part of it. The main issue is that the difficulty curve is so steep in terms of world architecture that you are mostly confused before it all makes more sense. For example, I didn't find the weapon at first because everything was so dark that I didn't notice the path to the upgrade piece at all. I thought it was random environment.In the second level, the difficulty is ramped up in such a way that you'd think you have been tossed into the middle/later parts of the game. The platform sections are often way too obscure and divided into so many small sections that you fall down constantly. Precision platforming is required when it is very hard to make precise jumps. What surprised me most is the combat. Fighting - although it feels and looks good - is pretty frustrating because the enemy drones attack you when you have no way of properly manouvering - either you quickly fall down a platform or are forced to fight it out without any room to dodge.In terms of story, everything feels a bit forced and uninteresting. Furthermore, the story pieces are spread out throughout the levels where they become annoying pretty soon while you are so invested in overcoming the architecture and enemies of the level. Story pieces in between sections would have been much better, as well as fairer respawn points - at least in the beginning of the game.It's a shame because the game looks good and the unconventional level design makes it so that I really would like to see and play more of it. But as of now, I feel too pushed back with too many unfair design decisions that I have no motivation to continue playing - although I just started out.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: The game is great and mostly well made but sadly has been abandoned by the developer. They promised updated settings to change the sensitivity and to change key bindings but have been silent on it since their initial promise 2 months ago. Also be aware there are no save slots or even a new game button. Be aware that if you don't like the initial settings then you don't have a choice---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Initially I wrote a review based on first impressions. Now that I've completely finished the game I decided to come back and edit it. That being said,The game is very very solid, if I personally had to give it a numerical rating I'd probably say somewhere around 8.5 out of 10.The gameplay itself felt smooth and lean but at times felt a little awkward. There are some precision platforming sections that if you aren't used to it may give you a little bit of a headache but that you'd get past soon enough. The combat felt smooth as well and fun as well, one thing to note is that you can't aim in the air which is an understandable mechanic but still feels a little constraining.The story was great! Full disclosure I haven't quite read all the logs yet so I can't give an in depth review of that aspect but still it felt solid and well written.The graphics were gorgeous and matched the whole "hacker', "vaporwave", "Tron-like" aesthetic they were going for.The sound design was also extremely beautiful and satisfying. They managed to evoke senses of awe, confusion, disharmony, and just general mystery with many of the tracks. Even the sound of walking is satisfying to listen to.As fair as the difficulty curve, there are difficult sections within the game but even then it shouldn't discourage any players who don't have confidence in their abilities as there are certain abilities that you get early on that makes things much easier to handle while still being optional. Basically the game is as hard as you let it be.In conclusion I really enjoyed the game. It's not the best but it's pretty darn close. I definitely advise anyone who is interested in this game to get it. I enjoyed it so much I plan on playing it over again, just because of how fun it all was.

_childDocuments_.review: Straight to consBad optimization - stuttering, FPS drops, lags etc.Got soft-locked at third level w/o any way to start it over or get to earlier stages, explanation below.There's an electricity system in this game. You press a button, it transfers electricity through a wire to a green lantern, it turns on and reveals green platforms for you to come over. BUT! If for some reason game decides to transfer electricity in short bursts instead of one smooth line, those platforms begin to flicker and disappear from time to time, meaning you can't walk over those. There are no earlier saves due to control points system and no way back (I can get back to previous level, but it's designed in a way to prevent me from getting even further back). Only solution that I see is to start the game over from the very beginning and erase a couple of hours of progress.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was amazing. I absolutely loved the concept, I loved the graphics, I loved being drip fed story through the lore snippets. Each piece of lore was either part of an answer or a completely new mystery, and it was extremely satisfying when I'd find another lore snippet that confirmed my guesses.I started playing the game at launch, and finished it a couple weeks later, so most of the issues I had with the game have already been patched. Such as the game not having an audio editor, which I found weird that they didn't include one to begin with but patched it in after the fact, but I was perfectly fine just turning the game down through my computer audio.The gameplay felt entirely based around using a controller, which I did not do. The aiming with mouse and keyboard was tedious, and I'd often find that trying to snap to an enemy caused my character to turn well past them, usually leading to my character being shotgun blasted to the face or set on fire.It's akin to using a virtual joystick for a console emulator, if that makes it clearer for anyone.I found platforming to be rather tedious, and I'd often find myself feeling cheated, especially in the OKT biome, the yellow zone with the spinning platforms.Exploration was fun, although I'd often get lost, the map wasn't that helpful.I missed a few major upgrades and had to spend a while searching for them. My last upgrade was  which was something you acquired pretty early on, which would have helped me with most of my gripes, such as the platforming. I had just missed it and only found it while searching for lore when I was ready to finish the game. The bosses were amazing, the HEX biome boss was absolutely terrifying.  The boss I had the most issues with was the TET boss.  The other bosses were ultimately trivialized by the time I got to them due to the upgrades I had at the time.  I adored the logic gate puzzles, and honestly, I'd buy a sequel or spinoff that was entirely just logic gate puzzles, those were so fun and I was sad there wasn't more as I progressed.The upgrades made sense, up until they didn't. It felt like they shoved everything at the end, and it trivialized basically everything, including the final boss.The last weapon you get trivializes basically everything, why use the  when you can get the  My biggest pet peeve was with the movement upgrades. In one area I received  But in the exact same area, about 10 minutes after getting the other movement upgrades, I get  Although these overpowered upgrades were  but the  Overall, I loved the game. it was a relatively short game, but it was the perfect length for the quality product it provided.It seems that the game is receiving plenty of patches based on player feedback, so most issues I see in other reviews will probably be patched by the time you get around to playing.I'd definitely recommend a playthrough for the story alone. It's a great experience and I'm glad I picked it up.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.  One of the few games I worked to 100%.  I started off on the controller, but switched over to keyboard and mouse for better aiming and control.  The recent adjustments to the control settings helps a lot here (switching aim to linear for example).  At the core, the game is a platformer with some light combat built in.  I didn't find any of the combat particularly challenging, the upgrades available help with the difficulty level.  On the topic of upgrades, there are a few spots that are blocked by upgrades, and back tracking to get the missed upgrade can be tricky.  However I found that to be part of the challenge, don't dive in unless you know you can get back.The best part of the game for me was the story text.  As you progress through the maps, you will encounter data fragments from the system logs of the base.  The logs tell the story of what happened to the base in the past.  The story is great, I really enjoyed it.  I ended up missing a few logs by the time I was ready to finish the game and spent a few hours backtracking to find the missing ones just to get the complete story.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game since I got my hands on a super early version at Day of the Devs 2018.  The game has come a long way since then, and has turned into a beautifully crafted world with a story that you must piece together by finding memories throughout the game areas.If you played the demo of the game, you got a single short level where you were able to power up real quickly.  The final version spreads out the powering up over the course of the entire game, making it feel like a true metroidvania.  You'll pick up powers such as double jumps, dashes, and hacking abilities that let you manipulate certain things within the game.  There are also a total of 5 different weapons to find.  I finished the game in about 9 hours of play time.The powers themselves are mostly obtained linearly.  There were only two instances where I had to go to a different zone to pick up a power and come back later to pick up something I couldn't get before.  While a typical metroidvania would have you revisit areas a couple of times to get to that one area that you couldn't reach before, this game generally doesn't do that.The button puzzles in the game get quite complex, but can be brute forced pretty easily.  Learning how the logic gates works helps, but then you get to the second zone in HEX where there are literally tangled knots of logic gates.  Good luck!  I'm sure you could work out some of the puzzles by figuring out how the logic gates work, but I just decided to hit buttons randomly to see what they did.  Usually there was a reset button that let you reset the puzzle if you get yourself softlocked on the other buttons.  Generally I didn't have much trouble figuring them out eventually, and you can use hacking abilities if you get stuck.If you do die, you very often will not lose a lot of progress, provided you remembered to hit a save point!  This is good, because the enemies can seem a bit overwhelming at times.  The flying ones are especially bad because they often get above you and shoot at you at an angle you can't shoot back at them.  They also do a ton of damage if you stand still, so you have to be always moving against them.  Later in the game you can hack them to destroy them outright, or have them work for you, but of course that's a power you have to earn!One of the highlights of this game are the wonderfully constructed zones.  USER, HEX and TET are amazingly constructed, while OKT has a pretty epic atmosphere.  ICO is in its own category, as it's very vertical and disorienting to try to navigate.  I spent quite some time trying to find the last memory in ICO as a result, which is a good thing... you wouldn't want to be able to just accidentally stumble into all the memories.The other highlight is the story itself.  Without giving the actual story away, the story itself is quite serious but injects some amusing elements, and put together it makes you want to collect every memory to both further the story and see what kind of amusing things happen with the crew.  The writing is very well done.The game is not 100% perfect.  Elevators will move without you on them, I fell through a floor once, and I was able to glitch out one of the bosses to kill it easily.  Also, the game is missing the ability to rebind controls (I hear that may be coming in a future update), and there is only one save slot.  Finally, I found the OKT zone a bit monotonous personally, it's just a lot of jumping between platforms for literally the whole area.  Your mileage may vary on that last one.However, these issues do not detract from making this one of the best releases of the year for me.  I highly recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the first playthrough and I can tell you that this game isn't for everyone. If you are looking for something combat-oriented, look elsewhere. If you are looking for a short and sweet puzzle/platformer with gorgeous visuals and a killer soundtrack, then this is the game for you. My only complaint is that it could've been longer and there could've been more puzzles (the puzzles are all logic gate based, but they barely scratch the surface of how complex they could've been). Overall, it was a really fun experience and I would recommend it highly, especially if you can snag it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this. The art, level design, gameplay... Everything. I only wish it was longer, though it wasn't as short as I feared when I saw the file size.This game has huge potential for expansion, sequels... It could be a cornerstone IP. _childDocuments_.review: The game reminds me of metroid prime in a lot of ways. With over the shoulder shooting that feels natural and fluid and meaty boss fights.This game really has it all. Logic gates that reminded me of dabbling with restore in minecraft. Some good souls like lore.At it’s heart it’s a metroidvania and a damned good one. This game has style, mood, smarts and fun gameplay.You can tell this game is the product of a lot of love and commitment.Strong recommendation from me.The game isn’t perfect. The map is minimalistic to be nearly useless especially considering how the verticality of the 3d maps are ignored entirely. The pacing feels sporadic at times. I’ve beaten two bosses and have seen a number of references to using hacking but have not gained that ability yet. Levels tend to be hyper focused around a gameplay element, which would be engaging in shorter spans, but seems over done the way it’s presented.There’s minor enhancements that would make the game better.  That being said, the rush I felt when I figured out and beat the first real boss in the game was challenging and deeply satisfying. The logic gate puzzles are engaging and are pretty approachable, which is a near impossible balance to pull off. The game is challenging and very fun.If any of the above sounds engaging please give the game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: The artstyle is really cool and definitely the best part of this game. The volumetric lighting effects really make the artstyle pop out. Soundtrack does go a little overboard sometimes and the inspiration is pretty obvious. The platforming itself is actually really fun and has a good feel. Puzzles are somewhat simple and the recompile feature is neat at first but I barely used it unless necessary. That said, boss fights are not fun to play. They seem difficult at first but once you figure them out, you'll realize that they take some fun out of the game because they force you to play in a way that is not fun in my opinion. Combat in general is more function than fun. It is basic third person shooting that doesn't detract or add to the experience.In short, I thought the experience was worth my money and time (finished it in 6 hours and that is with me getting lost). If you are looking for a solid metroidvania experience, than you will enjoy recompile.

_childDocuments_.review: After experiencing all endings and receiving all but one achievement, here is my review:Pros:- the theme of the game obviously- the puzzles have nice difficulties. not too easy not too frustrating- the amazing feeling once your are fully upgraded (Iron Man intensifies)- the story is satisfyingCons:- a little confusion about where the next level / upgrade / gate is.- some elemental settings are missing, like keybind remapping, mouse sensitivity, borderless fullscreen window- backtracking might be necessary (no fast travel)- with 8h playtime to achieve 100% it is a little shortBottom line:I recommend the game! I think it is safe to say, that if the trailer looks appealing to you, you very probably will enjoy the game. It is immersive and somewhat addictive to progress. But each one has it's method and it's somewhat of a puzzle to piece together and figuring it out always felt good.the levels are all very pretty for the style of the game, and while early on navigating them is a little tricky at first. name: Expeditions: Rome
detailed_description: The future of Rome is in your hands: what will your legacy be? Take on the role of a young Legatus whose father was murdered by an unknown political opponent, forcing you to escape Rome and take refuge in the military campaign to subdue a Greek rebellion. Step by step, you increase your military prowess, strengthen yourself in the forge of combat, and become the Legatus everyone learns to both respect, and to fear. In Expeditions: Rome, you exert the will of Rome through your actions across the world stage, from the bright blue coasts of Greece to the deep forests of Gaul. Decide how people will view you, and Rome. Will you strike with an iron fist, or speak with a silver tongue? Will you embrace the political heritage of the Republic, or carve your own path as you navigate the complex politics of the Roman Senate? Every choice matters as you decide the fate of your legion, your close companions, and of Rome itself. Create your own Roman Legatus! Customize your character’s look, gender, class, and skills to match your playstyle and role-playing fantasy Engage in tactical turn-based combat powered by an extensive skill-based action system where every weapon changes your potency on the battlefield Adventure with 5 unique companions discovering their extensive backstories and unique personalities Explore a beautifully realized, colorful world across many different environments, including North Africa, Greece, Gaul, and Rome herself Experience a historically inspired story of political intrigue and personal drama through a fully voiced narrative where choices matter and consequences are far-reaching Level-up each character and select from a variety of skills and passive abilities to explore a wide range of tactical options Loot, Craft, and Equip a variety of weapons, armors, and tactical items to customize your game even further, providing a tremendous range of tactical options for each character Lead your legion on 3 extensive war campaigns across Greece, North Africa, and Gaul. Recruit legionaries, improve your warcamp, conquer regions, exploit resources, and defend your territories as you lead your legion to victory

_childDocuments_.review: Very recommended for people that want CRPG army management based on historical theme, overall gameplay is simple but not to shallow. the combat mechanic is turn based system like Wasteland 3 or othe similiar CRPG, the main push of this game is about Re-live certain historical point in Rome history and make your own decision. Overall time to finish on one ending more or less between 40+ hours or more it's depends on what difficulty you chose. For a CRPG the element of RPG is quite shallow as such you can only pick one dialogue path form 3 choises, they simplify Dialogue check which is common in another CRPG games and that a shame because you locked from other dialogue choises in game that can turn event or battles to your advantage

_childDocuments_.review: The game is LovelyIt works in niche little historical characters and aspects, there are nice historical facts (such as how the year is named) that are all historically accurate and it really makes it immersive, even something so overlooked as the status of a woman in Rome is worked in accurately and it makes the game feel rewarding when your character is looked at weirdly because she is female.Game mechanics work well, combat is challenging and also rewarding, but combat item drops aren't, the game forces you to use the crafting system which can be a bit annoying.However, it is very repetative, the legion control and armies warmap is the exact same, the legion camp is not historically accurate, and again repetative because it is an area where you spend a great deal of time, not to mention that the battle zones where you and your pretorians actually fight are the opposite, I don't know why they made things so.. lazilly with the legion war.In between story which is the main focus of the game, you're basically just grinding, equipment, weapons, legion gear and camp upgrades, it's a good way to kill time but is extremely repetative and becomes boring fast once you have learned how to use it.Overall, the game was clearly not made with a massive budget, I would have loved more customisation and, well better looking character customisation, earlier better looking armors than the basic lorica harmata, and perhaps better graphics (not kidding, the game could use it) But, with all that said, the game is a lot of fun, especially if you are into ancient rome, there are lots of little historical facts and niche things that nerds of Rome would appreciate.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a lowkey fan of the Expeditions series since its inception. I enjoyed Conquistador for the flawed gem it was and absolutely loved Viking, so when I heard that the series was going to look into a Roman setting I was overjoyed - with my joy only growing when the game came out and was utterly brilliant. I've really enjoyed the story, tactical combat and general feel of the game, but in spite of that I can't really recommend it at this stage due to it being such a buggy mess.As background I've started two separate campaigns, only to have to end each of them due to a bug wherein I get an automatic game over due to my having lost my last territory on the strategic map. This has not been the case in either campaign.Given that experience I can't really recommend the game. Might check it out a few months from now to see if the bug has been fixed, but if not well... beware.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is lots of fun and breaks the standard X-Com mission to mission grind.It has a really good story line that you want to listen to rather than skip.You get to play some of your other characters as the main, so it breaks things up a bit and I really like how there are quests that members of your group lead.  This means your personal character doesn't have to be in every single skirmish.Legion warfare as a concept is good, better than games like stellaris, etc, but it should have focused more on just being a card game using your tactics cards.  The visuals don't add much value and you just end up hitting auto-resolve to skip to the next tactic.  Other than loot the outcomes of your tactics are not explained much either so the value of playing one card over another isn't too clear.Crafting doesn't become that good till later in the game when you can upgrade as you find lots of loot as good as you can make early on.Overall I'm loving this game.  Especially the big end of act fights where you have everyone in your camp on the map... kind of like the UFO fights in X-Com where you ship crashes and all your people have to get in on the action  instead of the basic 6 player party, you get to run 16.

I enjoyed this so much when I first played through, I played it 6 more times as of the writing of this review.The setting is phenomenal. It's an alternate history, and whilst some creative liberties are taken, it's blended in really well with branching storylines, some minor, and some major.The characters really make this game though. The historical characters are done really well, but the original characters have depth, pros and cons, and every one of them is different to make your team so well rounded in terms of responses, dialogues and opinions on the actions you do and do not take throughout the story.Whenever I find myself bored, I often default to this game and begin another run. The music and atmosphere really immerse you in the setting and gameplay.You will not regret this purchase.
