_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Game and 10/10 for me!  Highly recommended if you love ancient Rome and turn-based tactic RPGs.This latest entry into the Expedition series is a major step up from their previous entries and was a joy to play through and through. The game takes you on 3 major campaigns across the Mediterranean from Asia Minor to Egypt to Gaul and Rome itself. From combat gameplay to graphics to artwork to the story, Expedition Rome was very enjoyable to play through. You can easily get your money's worth at full price, and if you’re hesitating, DON’T! Buy it! It’s worth it. Overall, Expeditions Rome is fantastic game. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Details:Combat -  is fun and diverse. You can use up to 6 characters in any order during your turn. There are at least three major combat trees (ranged, melee, distance melee) that forces you to maintain a diverse set of combat skills and companions to counter various enemies. and aside from that, you also have the ability to make and use ‘tactical’ items (such as pila, healing bandages, Greek fire, etc) which further add diversity to combat gameplay. Enemy AI is generally pretty good. Campaign minigame – Throughout your expeditions during the 3 main campaigns, you command a legion that allows you to conquer resource sites, cities, and regions like a typical strategy game. This is done in part through upgrading various buildings within your camp and maintaining enough troops to attack new cities or stave off attacks from the enemies. Missions throughout the military campaigns that require tactical combat also force you to use soldiers that you hire while on the campaign so you are not always stuck with the 6 or so main cast (which are generally well done). All of your characters have full item slots and skill trees. Major story plots and battles during the campaign let you tactically control your entire group of soldiers (12 I think) with AI help for epic battles!Skill Trees - Each of the 3 main classes has 3  unique skill trees that add a wide array of passive and active abilities. You won’t be able to use all of the skills throughout the campaign, however, your character will level up enough to use at least 2/3 of the skill trees.Weapon and Armor Customization - is on point, with a wide array of (mostly) historically accurate Roman, Greek, Macedonian, Egyptian, and Celtic armor, and weapon sets. Weapons have their own various skills (separate from character skills) which appear randomized, and you can upgrade your favorite looking armors and weapons so you can keep your characters looking and playing the way you want through the whole campaign.Graphics and Artwork - are pretty good, and the character art is excellent. While certainly not next-generation graphics, they are solid for this type of turn-based tactics RPG. Textures, particle effects, and animations are all well done. Character portrait artwork is realistic looking and very well done. Most of the female portraits are also very pleasant on the eyes (Cleopatra, yikes).Storyline –is excellent and a major part throughout the whole game. Expeditions take you through 3 main acts (Asia Minor, Egypt, Gaul) with intermediate stops back at Rome itself. While the game is not completely linear, it does progress along a general line while allowing you to make decisions both strategically on the campaign maps and during tactical combat story levels which will affect the endgame. I was quite impressed with how they maintained a solid fleshed out story until the end. Likewise, the voice acting for all the main characters is well done. The main characters throughout the game are diverse and come from a wide array of backgrounds (if that matters to you), but their incorporation is neither woke or preachy, and generally make historical sense for the time period (such as a female gladiatrix). Ambiance: The game does a great job of making you feel like you’re in ancient Rome during the end days of the republic. The incorporation of correctly pronounced Latin terms and names is great, and the music is generally pretty good, although I would have liked more unique sounding tracks for different regions of the world, such as when you’re in Egypt. The overall level design, buildings, weapons and armor, artwork, etc. do a pretty good job at representing the historical past in a video game. The storyline also contains a mixture of historical and fictional characters so you can certainly learn a thing or two about real historical events if you’re willing to do some outside research.  The game does contain a codex to help with these Latin terms as well.  Replayability – is excellent, as you can completely change your combat style with a different class, different armors and weapons, different strategies to use conquering regions, and different choices during main story events. At the end of the game, you will be shown a long set of videos which details the characters outcomes based on your choices (like the old fallout games or wasteland 3). Overall, I really enjoyed my time playing the game. I highly recommend Expeditions Rome if you love to turn based tactical combat, RPGS, Rome, or a good storyline. 10/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: “Most noble leader, illustrious tribunes, generals, most courageous fellow soldiers and all loyal honest citizens! You know well that the hour has come: the enemy of our faith wishes to oppress us even more closely by sea and land with all his engines and skill to attack us with the entire strength of this siege force, as a snake about to spew its venom; he is in a hurry to devour us, like a savage lion. For this reason I am imploring you to fight like men with brave souls, as you have done from the beginning up to this day, against the enemy of our faith. I hand over to you my glorious, famous, respected, noble city, the shining Queen of Cities, our homeland. You know well, my brothers, that we have four obligations in common, which force us to prefer death over survival: first our faith and piety; second our homeland; third, the emperor anointed by the Lord, and fourth; our relatives and friends.Well, my brothers, if we must fight for one of these obligations, we will be even more liable under the command strength of all four; as you can clearly understand. If God grants victory to the impious because of my own sins, we will endanger our lives for our holy faith, which Christ gave us with his own blood. This is most important of all. Even if one gains the entire world but loses his soul in the process, what will be the benefit! Second, we will be deprived of such famous homeland and of our liberty. Third, our empire, renowned in the past but presently humbled, low and exhausted, will be ruled by a tyrant and an impious man. Fourth, we will be separated from our dearest children, wives and relatives.This wretch of a Sultan has besieged our city up to now for fifty seven days with all his engines and strength; he has relaxed the blockade neither day nor night, but, by the grace of Christ, our Lord, who sees all things, the enemy has often been repelled, up to now, from our walls with shame and dishonour. Yet now too, my brothers, feel no cowardice, even if small parts of our fortifications have collapsed from the explosions and engine missiles, as you can see, we made all possible, necessary repairs. We are placing all hope in the irresistible glory of God. Some have faith in armament, others in cavalry, might and numbers but we believe in the name of our Lord, our God and Saviour, and second, in our arms and strength granted to us by divine power.I know the countless hordes of the impious will advance against us, according to their custom, violently, confidently and with great courage and force in order to overwhelm and wear out our few defenders with hardship. They attempt to frighten us with loud yells and innumerable battle cries. But you are all familiar with their chattering and I need say no more about it. For a long time they will continue so and will also release over us countless rocks, all sorts of arrows and missiles, like the sand of the sea. But I hope that such things will not harm us; I see, greatly rejoice, and nourish with hopes in my mind that even if we are few, you are all experienced and seasoned warriors – courageous, brave, and well prepared. Protect your heads with shields in combat and battle. Keep your right hand, armed with the sword, extended in front of you at all times. Your helmets, breastplates and suits of armour are fully sufficient together with your other weapons and will prove very effective in battle. Our enemies have none and use no such weapons. You are protected inside the walls, while they will advance without cover and with toil.For these reasons, my fellow soldiers, prepare yourselves, be firm, and remain valiant, for the pity of God. Take your example from the few elephants of the Carthaginians and how they dispersed the numerous cavalry of the Romans with their noise and appearance. If one dumb beast put another to flight, we, the masters of horses and animals, can surely even do better against our advancing enemies, since they are dumb animals, worse even than pigs. Present your shield, swords, arrows, and spears to them, imagining that you are a hunting party after wild boars, so that the impious may learn that they are dealing not with dumb animals but with their lords and masters, the descendants of the Greeks and the Romans.You are well aware that this irreligious Sultan, the enemy of our holy faith, violated for no good reason the peace treaty we had with him and disregarded his numerous oaths without a second thought. Suddenly, he appeared and built his castle in the straights of Asomatosso so he might be able to inflict daily harm on us. Then he put our farms, gardens, parks, and houses to the torch, while he killed and enslaved as many of our Christian brothers as he found; he broke the treaty of friendship. He befriended the inhabitants of Galata, the wretches rejoice over this, as they are unaware of the parable of the farmer’s son who was roasting snails and said, ‘Oh stupid creature,’ etc.Well my brothers, since he started the siege and the blockade, every day he opens his fathomless mouth and is seeking an opportunity to devour us and this city, which thrice-blessed Constantine the Great founded and dedicated to the all holy most chaste Mother of God, our lady, Mary the eternal virgin. She became the Queen of Cities, the shield and aid of our homeland, the shelter of Christians, the hope and joy of all wishes to destroy this city, which was once proud and blooming like a rose of the field.I can tell you that this city mastered the entire universe; She placed beneath her feet Pontus, Armenia, Paphlagonia, The Amazonian lands, Cappadocia, Galatia, Media, Georgian Colchis, Bosphoros, Albania, Syria, Cilicia, Mesopotamia, Phoenicia, Palestine, Arabia, Judea, Bactria, Scythia, Macedonia, Thessaly, Boeotia, Locris, Aetolia, Arcarnania, Achaea, the Peloponnese, Epirus, Illyria, Lykhnites, the Adriatic, Italy, Tuscany, the Celts, and Galatian Celts, Spain up to Cadiz, Libya, Mauritania, Ethiopia, Beledes, Scude, Numidia, Africa and Egypt.Now he wants to enslave her and throw the yoke upon the Mistress of Cities, our holy churches, where the Holy Trinity was worshiped, where the Holy Spirit was glorified in hymns, where angels were heard praising in chant the deity of and the incarnation of God’s word, he wants to turn into shrines of his blasphemy, shrines of the mad and false Prophet, Mohammed, as well as into stables for his horses and camels.Consider then, my brothers and comrades in arms, how the commemoration of our death, our memory, fame and freedom can be rendered eternal.”

_childDocuments_.review: In short:An absolute master class in game-play and story. 10/10The RPG element was turned up to 11. I just finished my first play through and was sobbing at the end of this game. You truly get involved with the main cast of characters, the epilogue at the end of the game is amazing. _childDocuments_.review: This game is epic in scope and brilliant in execution.  The story is riveting, frightening, rewarding and beautiful. There are so  many ways to influence the outcome of history that with several playthroughs I haven't yet found them all.There's a lot to learn in this game, and it does a great job of giving you the tools you need to do that.The combat mechanics are very good, and the balance of this with the story you're living makes it a game that's worth every penny of the purchase price.The art is fantastic.  The voice-acting especially so.This game puts you there, in the middle of what could have been history.  I've got over 1000 hours on the game, and after a bit of a break, I'm going back in to discover more.  And I'll enjoy it just as much.  The gladiator DLC is a bit of a distraction, and I don't fancy it very much, but it won't stop me from trying to find out 'what could happen if....' within the actual game.

_childDocuments_.review: You love XCOM-like strategy games and ancient Rome? Then this title is an absolute must have for you.The combat is easy to learn, but hard to master. There are a lot of options to customize your classes and let their subclass features play together. In normal mode the combat is doable for everyone but still challenging. The hard and especially insane mode are quite a different experience. So, the game is definitely for beginners and pros. The content might not be 100% historically accurate, but is full of real knowledge and fun easter eggs like "Occam’s razor". The story is fascinating and very detailed. Also, dialogs and story options are different playing as a male or a female.Sadly, developers removed the possibility for a special Bestia/Veles build, that allowed him to finish-off an entire encounter in a single round.Overall, it is absolutely worth its money and offers great replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game if you have no particular interest in Roman history. Not such a good game if you do. Expedition: Rome's gameplay is fundamentally solid. There is a heavy focus on tactical battles, which are, for the most part, engaging and well-designed, except for a few overly long siege battles. Likewise, character development allows for interesting and varied builds. The game's characters - mostly people in your camp and your companions - are interesting and fairly well developed. So there is a lot to like.If you approach the game with some knowledge of Roman history and the ancient Mediterranean, you may find the game's flaws too glaring to overlook though. There are minor ones you may be able to live with: out-of-period or plainly wrong military equipment, architecture, and dress, incorrect usage of Latin, etc. Then there are major ones that at least I found hard to accept: The game's chronology makes no sense, and major historical characters appear well outside the period in which they lived. Rome's political system is misrepresented in many ways that have a direct bearing on the game's story, as are certain non-Roman peoples. A few major plot points are totally implausible for anyone with even a moderate level of knowledge of Roman history and politics. All this adds up to a game world that becomes less and less believable and immersive the longer you play. Many of these errors are baffling, as they could have been so easily avoided: Why create colourful buildings but depict statues incorrectly as devoid of colour? Why give Egyptian characters a look that is centuries out of date? Why introduce major characters decades ahead of their time when the story's chronology could have been planned out far more convincingly? All this (and lots more) could have been so easily avoided.Another factor in this is that the shallowness of the game's story. This is supposed to be a story about political intrigue in the late Republican period. However, only a very few characters from that period actually feature in the story, and many intriguing historical figures have been omitted. As a result, the story feels far more shallow than it could have been. This is of course a game by a relatively small studio with a limited budget. Still, I cannot imagine that it would have been so very difficult and costly to give a larger number of historical figures at least a passing role in the story. This would have made the game quite a lot more believable and immersive. I rate this game as a missed opportunity to create a great historical RPG. All the bases are there, but there are just too many obvious and baffling errors. If you are here for the history, give this a miss. If you are looking for a solid RPG with a decent story, this game is still worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game, and one of those games where I wish there was a middle review option but unfortunately a clear step down from the previous installation in the series, Vikings.In the last one, it felt like the game world would change dramatically depending on your choices, whether you allied with a side of the war, or went your own way. The locations had various quests that involved more than just fighting, it felt like there was a reason to visit these places and interact with the characters.Unfortunately in this game, it seems to have just abandoned that with a far too streamlined overview map and few empty but strangely huge locations that seem to be just scattered with a few merchants and army vs army mini-game that doesn't really impact much at all. If you have more troops, you're probably going to win. I was excited to have these army clashes when I first heard about the game, and I knew we were never going to have Rome Total War style battles, but I expected more than a redundant card battler. Once you've inevitably won the battle, to capture the region fully you then fight a battle with your character with some contrived reason why it has to be the legion's top soldiers and officers going alone and pointlessly risking themselves. Not really a big deal as it is a fictional game, but it's bit immersion breaking to keep having your officer say for the 20th time "yeah err the only way the region will stop rebelling is if you go personally and sort it out yourself... again." As countless other reviews have said, it's like the game couldn't decide whether it wanted to focus on your armies or your party, and took a middling road that didn't do either too well.Fortunately the battles involving your character and their chums are fun, the combat has been improved greatly since Vikings. Instead of using the same usual skills that you would in the previous games, the weapons force you to use different skills and that often leaves you scrambling to think of new tactics on the fly in a battle, which is fun for me.I'm not a fan of the new loot and crafting system, again you have to run around the huge maps picking up scattered chests. No idea why the developers thought it would be fun for you to run about 5 minutes after the battle has finished in an empty map, waiting for all your characters to queue up and climb a ladder to get that last loot chest. You end up with far too many weapons and items of armour that you have to manually dismantle. A lot of the best armour and weapons that you get early on, you can't upgrade at the camp until you get to the final camp upgrade. This might be intentional to make you change equipment, but it feels like Cyberpunk with far too much loot, I don't want to be changing my gear after every single encounter, it's tedious.Overall, the game is decent and I have had fun with the game, but it is falls short compared to it's predecessor. However with a few quality of life changes, and perhaps addition of more quests and characters that actually contribute to the game play other than just "kill this person", I probably would recommend this game. However like a lot of modern games, it seems to have a lot of complexity streamlined out of it.Also the Twitch banners and a dedicated hot key to claim Twitch drops is annoying, it doesn't fit in with games aesthetic. I don't care if there's Twitch integration, but it's so garish when a tiny minority of players will actually use it.I would say if you're coming fresh to the game series without any previous expectations and like RPGs, you'll probably enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game with many different endings. The story was good and your choices felt like they had real consequences. The game has a lot of side quests and plenty of things to do. They threw in some mini games like the legion battles, but the main feature is the tactical fighting. Though it might have a few quirks, the game is well made and designed. Highly repayable to see different endings. If you are good at these types of games you might want to play on a harder difficulty as near the end you can make your characters quite strong. The character development and voices is well done. I would recommend it to anyone who likes turn based strategy games, Roman History, or choose your own adventure like games.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: Having a Rome themed RPG is a dream come true. The tactical battles are turn based but very challenging. I'm sure with practice it will get easier. The sole dislike is the legion combat system. Its abstract, which is OK, but its difficult to understand the nuances of your action choices (called Stratagems). Overall, its a fun immersive game.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy how the devs took time to study Roman art, life, society, warfare and all other aspects during the late Republic. One can see the care and hard work they invested to give players the feeling of Roman antiquity.With great pleasure, I noticed the detailed depicture of the Senate during the game. How intricate the floor tiles are depicted, the curtains etc.I've just nearing the end of ACT 1 but can say with great content, this game is a jewel.The game itself is a mixture of round - based tactical hex game and a pauseable real-world part in which you move with your legion or your praetorians (party) on a map in order to achieve specific goals.Meanwhile you will be hit with random encounters - some of them beneficial some not - in which you have to decide how to react. By doing this you gain/lose support with your praetorians.When you are on campaign with your legion you have to attack enemy encampments. This will lead to a new game experience because you have to decide who of your centuriones (kind of captains) will lead the attack. What follows is a series of rounds (3; engagement - confrontation - resolution) and the outcome of each is  modified by various tactical cards.. One can improve those cards by building the necessary building in your castrum (fort).Which brings me to the next item on the agenda, your legion's fort. When entering your fort, you are able to interact with different people who represent different building functions. There is a smithy, a bath, your legatus tent, a medical tent, a practice area, a merchant and a place to improve your tac-cards your workshop. Also you can talk to your VIP praetorians. Those have a character and story background, which the "normal" praetorians lack. The latter ones are recruitable from one of the tents. Forts can be built in different places on the campaign map requiring only a former hostile garrison spot.All that is left to say is...ROMA INVICTA ET ETERNA!!
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: In an alternate history you take over for Julius Caeser. Can you live up to his glory? Or will you change the course of Rome? This game really lets you live those choices, with fantastic characters and engaging stories. If you like anything to do with classical Republic of Rome then this is made for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game, and I really do wish I could play it again. The combat is hard and punishing, but not to an annoying extent. Visually, the game is absolutely beautiful with a breath-taking map. Plot wise, the game is quite good taking you through the third Mithridates war, an early version of Egypt, and finally Gaul. The only real downside is that legion combat, though fun, gets quite tedious in the second and third act. If you want a Roman RPG, this is the best game out there for it right now.9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: It's real good. Went in with the expectation of a strategy game with light RPG elements, but was pleasantly surprised that it's a full-fledged RPG with some light strategy elements. Story is pretty good, characters are nicely rounded and have some real growth, and the post-ending sequence is satisfying. First playthrough took almost 50 hours, but I might come back to this and do a second playthrough after some time has passed. Combat felt a bit wonky in the beginning, but once you get the hang of it, it's pretty solid turn-based tactical combat gameplay. Legion battles are basically card games and most of your cards suck.All around a really solid game. Roma Invicta
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest rpgs I have ever played, it has an amazing replay value, iconic characters, excellent plot and choices that actually matter, i wish I could thank individually every single person that worked on this game. Do not doubt to buy this game because it's absolutelly worth it. Not only if you're a history buff but also if you like sory rich rpgs.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some charming features. It's mildly fun throughout most of the experience. It's definitely not among the best games I've played, but it's fun enough to hold my interest. I nearly quit the game during a particularly frustrating timed mission where I had to set a couple bridges on fire, which made me have to reattempt the same missions 3-4 times. Luckily these annoying missions are relatively uncommon, so I'm able to overlook them. I've played a lot of games over the years so it's tough to give this a great score. I'll give it a generous 7 out of 10, but only barely. I'm having a bit of fun, but I honestly don't expect to remember this one for long after I've finished it.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: So far I like it, it's drawing me in. It is a be repetitive but no more then any other game of this nature, you either like them or you don't. My favorite aspect of the game is the saves, to me that is excellent, in most cases I can save wherever I am, that works great when nature summons me.  It works with triple monitors, but not real good, I just use single screen to play and that works fine for me with all graphics maxed. (and I have a 10 year old PC)
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: I already thought Expedtions:Vikings was a big improvment on the previous Expedition game. But somehow they improved on a already great game and made a even better one with Expedtion: Rome. Some of the reason might be the time period, but still they build up the world quite well. Furthermore the main story had a simple but enjoyabel enough red thread throughout all 3 campaigns. Also for how little content/time your companions get to have in the spotlight, they were still quite interesting and I  wanted to know how their story ended.The combat was the weakest part for me as it quickly got quite repetitive. Though legendary items you find mix it up a bit and made it passabel for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game! I cannot suggest it enough to fans of isometric turnbased strategies and Rome. While games like BG3 have opened up the genre to new people, Expeditions: Rome has been offering up a solidly Roman and very entertaining addition for the veteran community that should appeal to new comers as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first Expeditions game and it's pretty fun. The combat on Insane difficulty is challenging and fun especially as you start to skill up your characters and start crafting good gear or getting powerful unique items.  The text-based legion battles are ok I guess. The characters are good and well voice-acted. I'm also enjoying the story so far.Eager to look into their other titles after I finish this one.Edit: Very satisfying end to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: the game from the start is a 10/10, the story is amezing and well writen, the gameplay is really fun, but the game isn't perfect, there are many bugs, like: not be able to open some chest for some reason even when the chararter is next to it, not being refund the action point when you kill a untrained unit, you can't collect stuff from enemy dead body even when they are highlithed and one of my chararthes is next to it, and many more, but the team is fixing the bugs, so it will take some time before this game becomes perfect, one thing i would really like is a new game plus where you bring with you all the item you collected throught the game, and the skill point and the upgraded legion HQ, but the game gets harder with enemy increasing in level, hp and numbers. one thing that made me quite sad was the fact that there are not many fight where you can bring all your story chararther with, i would have love if there were more fights were you control your main units. the game is really great i give it a 10/10, i know i said that there are many bugs, but what games comes out perfect? keep up the great work i can't wait to buy all the possible dlc for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: What if you could step into history before it was written by great men? Before the rise of Gaius Julius. What if you befriended him and watched him die? Putting yourself in place to become what he did in actual history. To have Centurions that he himself spoke of in his biography. Would you stand before Cleopatra herself and be swayed by her charms as Caesar did... or will you see through her seduction and go forth of your own accord? This alternate history strategy game took me by surprise as I saw its' depth and challenge. I have become invested in it, in the choices, dilemmas, characters and spectacular attention to historical detail... even the stretches of fiction. Personally, I hold Expeditions: Rome up there with XCOM 2 and the fan favourites of the Total War franchise. A word of warning, though; Pay attention. This is not a lazy game, a careful commander will be victorious. Least one can do is try this game, I went in with a passion for Latin history and am still stuck in. I came, I saw and I could not believe my eyes.

_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: This was a surprise honestly. I did not expect to enjoy this game as much as I did, I think it is engaging, fun, and well made. _childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: "Pre-christian era Rome, the Empire had grown beyong its means, and the rule of senate elders had begun to fray at the eges. The people of Rome were exhausted, continually defending her from neighboring states. As the power struggle ensued the political arena, the quality of Roman life declined. The empire was racked by chaos. It was when a great man appeared, and changed the fate of Rome..." (My second favorite Rome-themed game)
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: Things that aren't so fun:- Limited character customization with few generic portraits to choose from.- Skill trees are kinda meh. You are forced to invest on some useless skills to get the ones you really want. Plus i haven't found any way to go back and redistribute them- You are forced to pick at least 3 generic NPCs which you are then again forced to use on important missions with one of the cannon NPCs. These come at random and you have to pray that they come with a good level, helpful attributes, mid to high loyalty, well-distributed skill points (cause you can't redistribute them, so its better to recuit a lvl 1 generic over a lvl 18 generic) and finally a portrait that isn't the same as your created character, or any other of the generics, cause that can be quite confusing.- Legions are so automatic you cant even give them a custom name.- Forging. Oh god Forging. I think i have spent my 27 in game hours with the sole purpose of unlocking the Foundry, and i only got the lvl 1 forge. You get tons of schematics through the game, which let you craft Epic/Legendary gear (Purple/Golden). You finally get your golden equipment, just to get to the next fight and drop a super common grey pitchfork that does more damage than your golden spear. Oh but don't worry, you can upgrade it to increase its damage. You only need to upgrade your lvl 1 forge to a lvl 3 foundry, which is literally the LAST of your camp upgrades. This feels like your characters are always badly equipped and everything you put on them is replaceable. You will spend 50% of your gametime comparing old and new gear between your cannon NPCs + generic NPCs, and you will still feel unsatisfied. It feels badly implemented, to the point where i get the feeling the game will end before you unlock all lvl 3 camp upgrades.- You get a ton of random gear as loot, which piles up fast making your inventory a mess. You can dismantle holding right click one by one. which takes an eternity, just to be piled up again 2 or 3 fights later.- Combat wise, i think just one action point feels a bit limited. Theres no point using most of the support skills to aid your second turn, since you end up doing less damage than just striking both turns.Things that ARE fun:-I'd say get this game when it's on discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend the game.There is a few things that do bother me, One is that the characters profiles pictures don't really match there character models that well. It's not a huge deal, but at the same time, it's more of a peeve to me personally.I feel like the game lacks on the more the political side of the game, the campaign and combat is fun, and enjoyable. But the political side I found is a bit lacking.I am being over critical, because there isn't much to critique, the game is solid and a very enjoyable experience, I recommend if your a fan of Roman games, this is a must have.RatingGraphics:6/10 the graphics are decent, character models need work.Gameplay 10/10, I'm still playing my first campaign.Story 8/10. The story is decent, choices you make seem to have an impact, I'm yet to finish, so we'll see if this score goes up towards the end of my first playthrough.Characters 7/10 characters are alright and have a bit of personality, Some of the narratives are bland.Difficulty 10/10 the game can be quite difficult and you have to use your brain to get passed certain parts and you must use the correct setups. Mistakes can make you have to reload an old autosave to re position for  certain events. I can't say more with out spoilers. Game can be difficult.Overall 8/10 If the character models get an update it's an easy 9/10 game. Whats is the game worth? _childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: Damn, I'd never played any of the Expeditions games before and after finishing Rome, I'm realizing its like a perfect mix of some of my favorite games. Take old school BioWare party based character interactions and role playing, mix in some XCOM turned based tactical combat, a little simplified Total War campaign map and legion battles plus a ton of fun Roman history and baby you've got a stew going!
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: When I picked this game up, I knew it hit like every checkbox for a game I would enjoy, but it is quite masterful in the story and immersion. The experience is also quite drastically different in tone if playing as a man or woman, which I for one entirely embrace. The game acknowledges the absurdity of everything my female Legatus accomplished, while also embracing that her unique set of skills are practically necessary. The game spans about 10 years within its own lore, in which you go on several campaigns, with some interesting potential ones along the way. Certain choices may also cut off great benefits, or offer long-term benefits (sometimes both, and you find out later).Long story short, the immersion and presentation are exceptional, the gameplay is difficult, but rewarding, and most of the endings I got are all unique and interesting. Will you become what you sought to fight against, or will you trust that Rome is as loyal to you as you are to her?
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely fantastic game. Great story and writing that has kept me hooked with choices that feel like they actually impact the game. The combat has a bit of a learning curve. Those who enjoy turn based strategies and table top war games will pick it up quickly. Once you get the hang of it, it's nothing short of amazing. Probably some of the most fun I've had in an RPG. As much as I love fantasy I find it refreshing to experience something grounded in historical realism. Though the story isn't historically accurate it's a fun alternate history.Also this game does something I love and hope to see more games do in the future. Modular difficulty settings. You can tweak almost everything. From how much of a damage handicap the enemy has in combat, their strategic thinking, how much of a disaster spiral do you want random map events to be, etc. I am always happy to see a game have more than just basic; easy, medium, hard for it's difficulty.All in all I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys tactical turn based strategy games. Some things can get a little repetitive but all in all, great game. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those cases where a game is really enjoyable but it still feels that it could have been much better.Don't get me wrong it is a very nice game and its historical, but in many ways it is worse than its predecessor (Expeditions: Vikings).On the good side, you have a very nice main story with various twists and turns along the way which makes for a very good hook to keep one's interest. The turn-based combat, which is the heart of the game, is both challenging and fun. Personally, I finished the game on "hard" and found it quite challenging but not frustrating as is sometimes the case. Sometimes the large battles might felt that they were taking too much time but that is not this game's fault rather than a side effect of turn based system. The RPG elements in dialogues were quite nice opening a variety of different ways to approach problems and advance the story depending on your RP.On the bad side, in many cases this feels like a missed opportunity to be a true gem especially if you compare it to vikings. In this game skills are greatly reduced to just 3 different classes. Each class has 3 different skill trees, and by the end of the game you can max out about 2 of them. The problem is that this system locks each character into a playstyle from the start. This is not necessarily bad, but compared to vikings this feels like a step back from a system that allowed you to mix skills from various classes with a wide array of general skills that could make each character feel unique. Also the ration/medicine system here serves no purpose as there is no way that you can run out of them. Again in previous entries of the series this was a constant challenge.Finally, the new feature, the legion battle mechanic is the biggest let down of the game. I have no problem with the slightly archaic graphics and feel of this mini-game but my biggest complaint is that it was truly inconsequential. There was no way that I could lose a battle were I went in with a higher legion strength and no way I could win one were my legion was weaker. This made all those strategems and cards that you unlock feel very useless by the end.All in all this was a very good experience and I strongly suggest it if you are a fun of turn-based RPGs. If you are a fun of the series, you will enjoy this for sure but be warned that vikings is still the best entry.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: A strategic RPG game like many others, no bugs as of my gameplay, everything nicely explained, big amount of Roman Empire knowledge (no idea if real). Well, on normal difficulty game is easy, not boring but if I would define strategic difficulty as set of rules that I need to follow to win, here I don't even think. Just need to remember to change gear for better. Same goes for army battles, they feel random and with money earned on normal difficulty max number of legion units can be reached almost instantly.Game generally feels like a nice Legatus adventure. Obviously it's possible to play on more difficult level (4 possible), but I feel that this game is much more valuable as a role-playing story - there's really many things that were surprising for me to exist in reality many centuries ago. I'm weak in history. It's a really interesting history lesson.If I would have to choose most surprising game element, I think it would be humor in options description (like graphics, audio etc.). Even before "new game" this was already positive experience for me. It's not really a game that will win every game award, but I think it has potential to become a classic, it simply feels good.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Worth every penny I spent. The endings were satisfying. _childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing experience. Expeditions games have a fantastic way of reeling me in with the story and keeping me entertained with the game mechanics. They do what I find to be a perfect balance between the two that I just find so satisfying it's hard to describe. There is a fantastic blend of historical accuracy with fictitious plot that allows you to follow down whatever path you may want to be lead down. It also allows for replay-ability in order to see what could have been during those tense moments. A nice solid game-play for the price that's challenging but doable. I'll always come back to these games as I eternally desire the feeling of satisfaction to finish one of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: Expeditions: Rome is a lot more enjoyable than Vikings ended up being. The party based combat is really enjoyable, there are a lot of elements to it from tactical items, terrain considerations, cover, abilities, party composition etc. These battles are also challenging for a reasonable portion of the game which adds to the enjoyment. There are larger scale battles as well, called sieges, where all of your companions and other praetorians are involved and these are tougher and require even more planning. The storyline is also quite good and there are quite a lot of different and impactful choices you can make throughout the game.The legion battles are pretty bad though - they are simplistic and your options aren't that important it seems. They also become extremely easy to win fairly early on in the game and  become a necessary and boring step in the conquest. The resource management is also not that interesting, there are 4 primary resources but you can easily manage these and often gather an overwhelming amount of them without too much difficulty. The crafting/modifying system is moderately interesting but you get the ability to craft every tier of every item in the game, which is cumbersome and unnecessary. Overall I enjoyed playing Expeditions: Rome quite a lot and would certainly recommend it. The difficulty doesn't scale that well into the later stages but the story carries it through this stage. I would rate it at 6.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: Well after 26 hours of gameplay, I'm not really sure, why this game is very positive.I have played expedition: viking and conquistador as well.The viking game I liked, that is the best entry in the series. This game has an identity issue.It feels like it wants to be a party based, tactical rpg, while being a grand strategy and it does not really succed in either of those.The tactical combat is very simplistic, facing of characters do not matter, attack from the side does not matter, you only flank the enemy if someone is behind them and in front of them at the same time.Skills are not really usefull, except for maybe archers and assisin type of characters, but most battles can be won without them.The map movement and conquering: not really inspired. The legion battle is just a 3 phased card game, with some icons moving. Wile playing I had endless space 1 vibes, but even that battle was more interesting, than army battla here.Also, pacifying, why can I not use my teammembers for that as well? I would understand if it was a quest where I send out a team to do it, while I'm exploring, but nope, the whole company goes to the place, but you need to use pratorians with one companion "leading" them and kiling everything that moves. Random events: 50% of them is someone getting injured without a say in the matter from you, the others are either battle, or having a choice if you do not care about the event, or someone gets hurt. I had maybe 2 encounters wich were interesting, but those are rare and far.All in all, I'm sad to say, this is a step back in my opinion from expedition viking.I hope the devs decide what their next entry wants to be, because I like expedition games, but this one is 60% just tedious time padding with barely flushed out gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews, but there was enough obvious thought and love put into this game that I felt compelled to offer a thumbs up.Overall: Quite good, and significantly better than I expected. + Only encountered one bug the entire game: One of the soldiers available for recruitment was Centurion STRING NOT FOUND. He died a hero.+ Combat is fast and bloody (if slightly repetitive), with decent AI. It's a nice change that allied soldiers are elevated above fodder level and can actually get some kills in before going down.+ Combat animations and sound are well done. Kills are satisfying, and you feel it when your favorite character slumps over after taking a sword to the gut.+ Weapon skills implemented thus far are varied - you'll find something you like for each class. That said, more would have been welcome.+ Solid story. It won't win any awards, but I legitimately didn't know how it was going to end or who most of the characters would side with. There might have been a few too many betrayals along the way in terms of plausibility, but it did successfully change my play-style from a hopeful peacemaker to a paranoid ass.+ Epilogue was rewarding and in no rush, covering what would happen to all the characters and places my choices had an effect on.+ Enjoyed spending time in areas/cultures that the market isn't saturated with. Gaul was cool, but the cluster-f*** of Rome trying to maintain control amidst warring African tribes and a merciless Pharaoh was the standout.+ Solid companions. Modeled on familiar stereotypes, but a lot of effort and care went into their personalities and dialogue.+ Overall campaign length was just about right. Been leaving the game on even while actually working during "work from home" (I know, the horror), so I don't have an exact timestamp, but I'm estimating around 35 hours.- Only real knock was the army battle system. Not particularly engaging, but considering the fights last about 60 seconds it's not more than a minor nuisance.Final word: Not sure I'll play through it again in the future, but I certainly liked it enough to pick up the next Expeditions game if it's made. A rare on-the-fence purchase that really worked out.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: the game is decent turn-based tactical, without the infuriating timers common nowadays in the "X-com-like" genre and with a very thick (for this genre at least) sprinkle of roleplay / storytelling and some superfluous mechanisms. It pays a decent homage to the epoch it portrays (including really good Latin pronunciation!), of course taking plenty of liberties  to meet modern expectations. Unfortunately, the quality visibly falls from the cliff in Act III, including a game-breaking bug that forced me to lose 2h of my play. A 7/10 and that's generous because of the Asterix & Obelix gag.Longer free-form: it has been some time since i seen a game so openly shouted "we rushed the final part of it because the deadline was approaching". After the first 2 Acts, i was quite happy to give the game 8/10, eager to overlook some shortcomings and dubious at best solutions (including a really murky "strategy" part of it, that follows a card-based battle system). However, Act III really underdelivers, both in terms of storytelling and gameplay; the latter of which somehow can get both repetitive ("do the same stuff you've been doing for the last 40h but more") and forcefully original ("here's a weird mission where we give you completely different tools to control, have fun"). Act III alone is 5/10 at best, moving the overall game from "good and fun" to "decent".In general, Expeditions: Rome offers quite a different approach, which, when compared to another Turn-based Tactical from 2022, Warhammer Chaos Gate, can be considered a polar opposite of the latter. And not only because you mostly fight in melee ^^'. While the combat section itself is tad bit simpler, the game adds a strong RPG component, with big focus on the story, decisions you take and the companions you have. Chaos Gate was mostly fighting-fighting-fighting, with some token of a story to justify going on subsequent missions. Expeditions: Rome is a story, which requires you to fight from time to time. Your characters are not expected to die everytime often, but grow attached to (or angry at) you. The base-building, world exploration part are means to progress the story, not the goal on their own.I mean, in how many "X-com-like" games you get to romance some of your companions? ^^This approach has its pros and cons, but overall I think it serves its purpose. For one, it is a nice change of pace not to have some impending doom keeping you on your heels ("monthly revies" or some inevitable invasion of aliens, mutant, demons that can pretty much derail the whole game if not tackled appropriately) and requiring you to play dozen of samey missions over and over again (yes Chaos Gate, looking at you). On the other, the roleplay part is still underdeveloped. Sometimes it forces you in certain ways (YES Ambiorix quest, im talking about you), that break the immersion a lot.Concurrently, battle mechanics-wise the game suffers a bit because of that. It has all the parts considered  for this genre, including some crafting, base building, party assignments etc. However, because they need to meet the historic criteria, none of them really stands out compared to other games. The whole legions battle / invasion system, while i understand from the story POV necessary, is really a wikipedia definition of a filler and probably could be improved a lot (either by reducing the RNG factor or adding some complexity). The team tactics part is fun and gives you some sense of accomplishment (yikes) as your characters get more and more powerful, but falls short compared to classics like X-com 1&2 - especially when it comes to creating powerful combos  your characters. But then, exactly because of the historic context, the game can't really a drop a "1million HP" boss on top of you, like some alien robot or Nurgle daemon... even the final bosses can be wasted in one turn on higher difficulties. And not because you cheese the game out...In summary: the game tries to marry two different approaches and excels at none. However - again, forgetting about the Act III debacle - it is still perfectly fine in its execution. It can be considered an interesting alternative, a break from some more "mini-maxing", doom-clocked, stressing games like Phoenix Point or Warhammer Mechanicus. It is also definitely a better introduction game for players not familiar with a genre; after somewhat steep learning curve early in Act I, the game can be considered quite easy (depending on settings) and allow you to enjoy the story more, instead of leading your virtual peons into a 438th battle similar to the previous ones. If you have time and cash to spare, definitely worth checking out - I got it during one of Steam Sales and don't consider my money wasted.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally, I'm not really into turn-based, hex-grid movement, combat games.... HOWEVER, I'll make an exception here. The story and the characters are intriguing, the world map and world building is interesting, has enough points of interest to explore to keep it interesting. The combat (as far as hex-grid, turned based combat goes) isn't TOO bad. I can not stress enough to NOT UNDERESTIMATE the power of archers! _childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly enjoyable experience so far, hard to describe as it is neither a CRPG nor a purely tactical experience such as XCOM but something in between, with very light CRPG elements, robust tactical combat which is certainly the back-bone of the game but doesn't dwarf every other aspect as it does in XCOM, leaving abundant space for the legion management element (somewhat reminiscent of Wrath of the Righteous' Crusader command), crafting and other significant systems that come together surprisingly well and make for a truly decent ride, if a bit linear. The game deserves praise also for another element that is not that common nowadays: its historical accuracy. The devs really went above and beyond in making Expeditions: Rome true to Roman history and culture, as is evident by details such as the Latin pronounciation of Roman terms that would normally be anglicanized in an English videogame.EDIT: I'm happy to add that the game gets even better as you progress, both story-wise (which is enjoyable, true to history and fully voice acted, too), in its CRPG component (which is certainly shallow but still somewhat deeper than I had described it), and in its tactical combat core as well, as it really comes together very well once you level up enough to unlock the bottom skill tiers and grasp how best to equip, train and use your men in battle. I would certainly urge anyone who's interested in Expeditions: Rome to download the free demo and try the game out for themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I am enjoying the game MAINLY because of the Roman theme, but I do feel that this game is more puzzle than it is tactical turn based combat. The reason I say this is because enemy reinforcements often come every 3 turns. Each battle has a specific objective such as "Escape or Kill XYZ leader or Destroy XYZ before X turns"This combined with the no unit kill experience makes it very hard to really even care about the combat, and instead makes you just rush to the objective as fast possible as you will earn the same exp amount no matter what. Legion battle are rather boring due to the same cards showing up every time and nothing really shown on your screen besides some boxes with icons swaying left and right. I am huge tactical turn based fan and there is currently just not enough meat here in that department. The classes are okay and often times "unique" weapons are weaker than ones you have already picked up even with the unique bonus they give. For Context I am playing on the hard difficulty setting. When I finish the game I will give a more detailed review.Edit 01/25/21---------------------So as to some of the comments that have eluded to not being more into the game. I did advance and find more cards for siege battles... however the battles are still boring and meaningless. The game spoon feeds you predictions and it does not change the fact the fights are merely boxes moving left and right with the same obscene catchphrases being yelled.I am not familiar with previous titles from this company so my viewing of this game comes from a purely turn based tactical fan. This game is not that. This game is a puzzle game. Plain and simple. Removing EXP from units destroys the purpose of combat. It feels more like a side thing to do. Which may just not be my play style. Spawning endless waves of low level reinforcements is not fun to me, its boring and repetitive. Having you move to X spot to leave combat or die to endless reinforcements is lazy.Hope this helps anyone make an informed purchase. There are a lot of games coming out in the next two months and I would personally wait for this go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the very best turn based RPGs I've ever played.  The story is great, starts fairly small, but by the end it's becomes pretty serious and epic, with a number of ways to resolve the end, some of which hinge on decisions made in earlier acts.  The companions are overall great, with a lot of commentary and interaction with them throughout the game.  If there is one thing I'd like to see them do in the future is spend a bit more time with companions and side missions for them.  What is already there is really good, but they are somewhat short.  The turn based combat is good, especially for a game without any kind of magic, and the army system is a fun side game to play, and feels like you spend just enough time with it without it getting tired.  Honestly, the best thing about it overall is the writing, I really enjoyed the story, and some of the decisions along the way are legitimately tough, and the ways they come back later on is handled well.Highly recommend if you like turn based RPGs, if like me you care more about story than game play/combat, and recommend it even more.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't normally review but I feel obliged to give this game props. I really enjoyed the story, history, mechanics, and slavery.- Narrative/story: It was nice how this game adopted real historical people and events to keep the story feeling believable. It isn't a perfect reproduction of history though, which is to be expected. The historical-fiction is this game's best aspect, especially if you're a fan of the period. The narrative lets you feel like a badass, even when you're struggling to win battles and keep getting screwed by the game's antagonists. The story does a great job of letting you accomplish great feats without the common videogame pitfall of making you the centre of the world. It is nothing like Skyrim, where you become the head of every group. One such example is defeating a famous Pontic king, but as part of a greater combined force. The PC is the victor on the battlefield but still subordinate to their commander. Moreover, the success earns the PC praise from some and scorn from others. The PC starts with the advantage of being from a powerful family and has the patronage of the current consul, but this has its own dangers.The slavery seems representative of the time. It is commonplace and considered a fate better than death. In fact, there are random encounters that consider slavery to be a morally neutral choice. There are options to apply your modern morality if you are overly sensitive, even though this is fiction. Luckily the game neither penalises or rewards your choice on the matter, so it is up to the player. But I recommend playing like a Roman.The sexism of the era is less clear, especially in respect to the aristocratic women. Because of this the authors decided to put some cliche tropes in the game with one particular companion. How you interact with this character has some very minor impacts to gameplay, but can have long-term impacts to story if not countered. There is a choice to play as a female character, but that seems out of place in the setting. I think it would have been a good opportunity to make the game significantly different and more difficult, but seems to be only flavour differences (I haven't finished a fem playthrough though). I would recommend playing as a male first time.The companion characters have their own quests independent of the player character. This is a fantastic idea and another example of the game not getting caught up in player character worship. Sadly these are few and far between. More companion missions and interactions with companions would have been great.Choices have big impacts. These aren't always apparent. For the most part they make sense and add some replay value. However, there are some choices that seem a little out of place. I won't spoil these, but an example is the Aquifer side-mission. Your choice to complete this mission does not recognise your lofty position in the republic, doesn't give you option to resolve outside of a binary, and has no impact on the overall story. Fact is, there needs to be some excuse or repercussions for your actions either way you choose to resolve this. There was also the throne-room choice which had impact, but seemed a little ham-fisted. These are the only two poorly written choices I can think of though.To summarise the story pros: The lore is historical and thus treats the PC like a real person. No over-the-top and unearned successes for the PC. Most of gameplay is story related. Whereas in something like X-com 2 there are only 5-6 story missions, at least 80% of the missions are story driven and UNIQUE. The rest are random encounters which are sometimes story related.- Combat Mechanics: Comparing to X-com 2 (A game I have sunk countless hours into), this game's combat is better in many ways. Can move one cell at a time without committing all of your movement points. The hex makes melee combat much better. There are flanking bonuses and deep interplay between character abilities (If one character blinds the next can knock down, etc.). The abilities are grounded in reality, which is a nice touch. This did make some skill trees a little boring though. Since the franchise is starting to pitch more RPG-like, future versions need more character class depth. You can also bump up the game-speed in options, and there are no tedious repeated cinematics during combat. However, there is no fog of war and pod-triggers. Would have been cool at have larger maps/battles but that might have ruined the narrative and dragged on. The game is pretty easy on normal, but there are some neat and really difficult challenges in there. You will be ambushed a lot.There is no RESPEC. It isn't necessary, but this would make for a much better first playthrough.- Non-combat Mechanics: The worldmap mechanics are fine. The army commands are a necessary part of the story, but the "battles" are uninteresting. I was taken out of the game by having to attack each territory. Especially since the enemy had chosen to break the military forces up into easily defeatable numbers. Would have been better to have more challenging scripted battles. Alternatively, they could have kept the card system and used that to determine the PC's positioning and enemy types with a tactical map battle against the opposing army.The crafting is okay but more RPG-like. The PC is the legatus of a legion, yet he must collect parts to create standard armor? I understand the need to place artificial limits on how much one can make, but the need for very specific parts that can be forged at the camp was dumb. There should not have been requirements like "Strong armor rings" or "Heavy armor plate." That being said, at least it was quite a versatile system. Unique items didn't have to be bound to the items they came with. I just think it could have been better thought out.- A score out of ten?I would give this an 8/10 because of the story and how it made you feel like you were accomplishing things. This isn't like an IGN 8/10. I would put Assassin's Creed: Greece at 5/10, and X-Com 2 at 7/10, Phoenix Point 5/10, and Total War Rome at 6/10. Those games are very different but share some relation by being historical or turn-based. And here's the thing, I like sci-fi more than history. Though I do love this era. However, true stories from history make for great storytelling. Even though the story here is very loosely based on historical events, those events give a believable and more personable dimension to the story. If the guys at Logic Artist ever read this, congratulations. This is probably one of my favourite stories in a game, ever. If I could make one criticism... I would make two:1. Don't be afraid to offend people by leaning into the brutality of history. Humans are ♥♥♥♥♥, and that's what makes stories interesting. I think the games would be more interesting if the morality system was focused on the era in which it was set.2. Expeditions: Crusades!!

_childDocuments_.review: Expeditions: Rome is a extremely well produced game that delivers on almost all aspects. A strong recommendation for anyone who has a interest in the turn-based tactical genre or anyone who has an affinity for Roman history.   Pros:• High production values across the board - great writing, excellent voice acting, amazing visuals and environments.  • Enjoyable turn-based combat system with in-depth tactics and unique classes. Positioning and skill usage is crucial.  • Gripping plot line with a satisfying and emotionally moving ending. • Unique loot, and the ability to upgrade said loot. • Captures the Roman period superbly. Cons:• The siege system isn't engrossing, and is more of a time sync. • Party limitations on the pacification missions were annoying. I would've preferred the option to roll with my main squad

_childDocuments_.review: To say i was surprised by this game is an understatement. I simply got the game on sale after buying another Roman-themed game on GoG (that being the infinitely inferior Age of Decadence in case you are wandering), and I was expecting a okay game with simple turn based combat. I was very much taken aback on how much I enjoyed this game. First and foremost, this game has one solid as hell story. It has good twists, it has good characters, it has phenomenal voice acting and great interactions between your MC and the companions you can gather during your travels. I never got the feeling that anyone you met was one dimensional, even small side characters had good reasons for doing what they where doing, and that is hard to pull off.  The combat in the turn-based battles between your squad and the enemy was also a treat, with a good level of complexity that grew organically with the 3 main chapters. Now, I played on Medium so I am unsure on how well-balanced the game is, and I am sure certain combination of skills breaks the combat, but I felt it had just the right amount of challenge even in the end game. Now, this game is not flawless. Outside of its story and its main combat, the rest of the elements are shallow and somewhat tedious. The moving of your legion around to capture bases, playing the same rather pointless mini game over and over again was a drag, even if the idea was sound. Army management was equally devoid of depth. Just the ability to build different troops, or a more proactive legion combat system instead of just playing ‘’the best card’’ would have improved this part. Both these parts felt like filler to get to the interesting parts, and that’s no good for anyone. Finally, the relationship system reflecting moral in combat rarely played into combat as I think it was intended to do, and you could always just stick dissatisfaction dudes in the bathhouse before a major battle anyway. Nevertheless, a game with this good of a story and mostly solid gameplay deserves a look. The price I feel might be just a tad bit high, but with these kind of production values, I understand it completely.  If you are a history nerd, a romabo or just a massive fan of this style of combat, buy it right now, and I know you will be pleased. If you are slightly on the fence, I say wait for a sale, and play it for its story. The developers are working on more games in this style, and I can’t wait to see what they do next. Expeditions Victorian age would kick ass is all I am sayin.

_childDocuments_.review: Good rpg, they improved upon the last two games for sure.Character creation lets you design your person and you can have it be a man or woman. This affects the dialogue quite a bit and playing as a woman, though rather silly also adds quite a lot of extra content. The only punishment really is your immersion. Another thing is the character models all look ugly, the portraits on the other hand look fantastic. They added a world map and an army for you to lead, a stripped down version of total war, but it is pretty good. You go around conquering settlements, hire generals to lead the army and dispatch the army to take over settlements. All rather good stuff. Then you can use the army to conquer strategic resources which can be used to upgrade your army outpost. Add troop composition, a more indepth battle simulation system etc. and it could turn into something even better definitely worth keeping going forward.The story is basically the life of julius caesar upto the civil war, with you taking his role as he dies very early into the game. Now, this presents some issues. Firstly, it makes the entire narrative rather predictable as you know exactly where it is heading. Secondly it shifts the focus very heavily onto the roman republic away from you personally as the entire game takes place during the events leading up to the Caesar's civil war. This leads to you going around doing the bidding for the senate conquering places and managing things with the RPG stuff on the side. But a large chunk of the game will be managing the military campaigns and issues that arise during them which gets rather repetitive, as there is practically no variation to the mechanics from acts 1 to 4Throughout the game you will end up getting 6 companions, who are all really good. Although it has to be said, the gladiator class, Deianeira (with DLC) is the weakest class. The retaliation mechanic doesn't make up for the lack of a shield or ability to wear heavy armor without speccing for it. The ability tree of the gladiator is also the weakest of them all, heavily focusing on morale and frightening which is another mechanic I didnt really care for. It is just annoying having to run after fleeing enemiesOn the topic of combat, it is rather tedious at times. Especially because whenever you are conquering settlements the game forces you to use praetorians instead of your companions to do the missions. The low level, undergeared RNG characters you hire. Why do I have to use these guys? Yeah, during the Act ending battles where you end up performing tasks in series with different groups it makes sense, you need more than 6 people, but why do I have to use them during missions that could just as well utilize the named companions and the MC? The end result of this is that these setttlement missions will be the most difficult in the entire game. People will die. To some farmers with bows throwing fire torches and oil jugs. Those are the toughest opponents in the game. Forget 6 armor gigachads with tower shields, some guy with a oil jug and a torch is going to suicide bomb you and kill your entire posse in 1 turn so you better watch your ass. Probably half of the missions require you to use RNG companions instead of your main companions. Stupid decisions. Not to mention timers. Timer missions are the worst, they pretty much always force you to send in the guy with most movement to throw a torch on an object or reach a certain area taking massive amounts of damage in the process. It sucks, especially as  the game also decides to give enemies constant reinforcements for some unknown reason. It gets annoying as ♥♥♥♥ and fast.Another issue is that you will have end game gear by the end of act II. That would be tier III, which is as high as it goes. You will also have fully upgraded your outpost in the early parts of act III which makes taking over strategic resources and settlements at that stage completely meaningless. It just feels like there should have been more to it, another tier for items items with better buffs that come later into the game etc etc. as every piece of armor I had on my companions by the end of the game I got in act I, I just upgraded them. Gear improvements are none-existent. Also, Bestia becomes overpowered very quickly being able to insta kill any boss on the first turn assuming he has the reach. And if he doesnt, Calida can snipe the boss from afar. This turns boss fights into a parody as they are over in the first or second turn almost every time. The final battle in rome lasted two turns, and that was only because you had to kill the boss twice. But a couple of peasants with torches??? Now that will mess you up.The romance stuff was good too, Deianeira is best girl ofcThe endings are good, there are basically four endings if im not mistaken, but you know which is the right one, and yes it is very good and satisfying. Overall, I would still recommend pathfinder games over this. The heavy focus on the military conquest side of things takes away from the roleplaying+the main storyline being  incredibly predictable doesnt help. Also the companion storylines are short and over very quickly without much effect on anything AND the combat being annoying with timed missions and enemies getting constant reinforcements... Annoying as hell. But, when you get past that it is a good little rpg stillAnd who knew cleopatra had such a massive pair of titties. I must say at times my loyalties to rome were questioned

_childDocuments_.review: Expeditions:Rome is a marvel I have accidentally stumbled upon but it was worth every hour I’ve played. It’s an amazing game with awesome story which takes all the good elements of a good tactical RPG’s, polishes them and offer them to you for one great experience. I recommend this game to every fan of the genre. You will not regret it. The game takes place in an alternative version of history during one of the most interesting times for the Roman Empire (still republic in the game). I will not go into many spoilers but you will meet many historical characters like Cleopatra and Cicero and shape their fate and future alongside that of Rome. The story is full with political intrigue and shows very accurately the political landscape in ancient Rome. Many of the quests could be solved in different ways and quite often something you say could have strong implications further down the story. Choose your words carefully, Legate!   The game follows the typical formula used for tactical RPG’s. You have a team of several characters, a number of classes to choose from, each with its own unique role and class trees (each class have 3). You also have your base of operation which you upgrade in order to get various benefits and so on. What made me love this game is the attention the developers have taken to polish all the things which usually annoy people in tactical RPG’s like the inability to bring all companions, having to force level backup characters you will need for 2 missions in the whole game and having nothing to do unless someone from the main get hurt, being forced by the game with some kind of timed mechanic preventing you from exploring the game and doing all side quests (Devs even joked about that in screen tips) and so on. Here you have exactly 6 companions and you can bring them all on a mission, the backup characters (called praetorians) are used for various tasks around your base and to solve world events and pacify regions, they level up with partial XP alongside your main party, being weaker but never more than a level or two behind. And so on. It just feels smooth. No other way to describe it. For about 120 hours of play I’ve never experienced a single crash, or bug or whatever. Everything went smoothly, the loading screens are fast, and everything is voiced over. Graphically the game isn’t the greatest but it is beautiful enough. I’ve bought this game via Humble Bundle, but I will fully recommend in on it’s full price. As for DLC’s - one which is non-mandatory. It adds 3 arenas, some unique items and a new Gladiator class (which is not very good). Nothing spectacular but the price is just 10 euros so it is relatively on par with what it offers. The arenas were quite fun

Too few unique companions and all are shallow. Generic companions are forgettable.2. Poor skill balancing. Half of the skills are pretty useless and quite boring. Soldier upgrades resembles XCOM but this game got some skills like 10% bonus health. Bruh.3. Basically level design issues. For instance, one of the first mission enemy will burn my units BUT, I got no way to put out fire because the game haven't provided me with necessary items to cure burning so if the unit gets burned he just dies. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for Deember 2023, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before December 5th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Exploring an ancient civilization through murder and dialogue trees. Expeditions: Rome takes the CRPG genre and drops the player into the time period of Ancient Rome.  Meeting Julius Caesar in the first scenes, players will take on the role of a man or woman who quickly ascends to a powerful military position and then joins the war efforts while trying to solve their father’s murder.  The writing here is good, though it does use a lot of Roman terms so players might need to look those up for full comprehension.  However, the story does seem interesting, and the battles are strategic and suitably large.The Strategy RPG genre though is a mixed bag.  While Expeditions: Rome does a great job of making it clear what each attack does, it also sometimes will feel unfair just due to how the genre uses random dice rolls.  Also, the story has historical inaccuracies which won’t upset most fans, but feels odd because the game shows a lot of love for the period as well though that’s ignoring the pronunciation choices.   And the tactical gameplay won’t appeal to everyone. Pick this up if you liked the original Fallout games but can do with less humor.  It’s a strategy RPG, where you get a large party, cruise around, talk to everyone, and wage war on an epic scale.  It might be a bit of a niche, with its heavy story and long gameplay, but it’s also perfect for those who like the genre.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:
