_childDocuments_.review: I have played it for about 150 hours (I recently switched to Steam after multiple problems on another platform).A great game if you like RPG with turn-based tactical combat, I enjoyed it a lot.The story, the companions with their personality and quests, and the historical backgrounds have been skillfully mixed, they improved this game even further when compared to Expeditions: Viking.The dialogues are fully voiced with a very good quality (I played the English version). There are many variations in the story and dialogues which depend on a number of actions or circumstances. Some are barely noticeable, some are really significant. The game will remember your choices and they may come back to you later, under one form or another.The combat is engaging, although it is turn-based and may sometimes seem long, but you can save anytime so that should not be a problem. The positioning and the terrain are important factors, which makes it even funnier. I found it more mature than Viking.The game offers a very good balance between story and combat, except at the middle of the first act when the side quests were temporarily lacking for me. The game really shines in the 3rd and 4th acts, with a plot that becomes more twisted and surprising, but never overdone. Each act feels really different, and not only by their beautiful environments.The character build is somewhat simplified in comparison to Viking and other RPGs. No class attributes, 4 classes with 3 skill trees each, and probably the worst is the limitation of 3 skill slot for the weapon and 6 slots for the class skills. The result was a fine selection of skills for me, but it may be frustrating for players who like to roleplay their characters a little further. Each class provides enough flexibility to cherry-pick skills in the 3 paths and vary the gameplay.(Note: the Death of Glory DLC adds a 5th class, among others)Expeditions: Rome is not meant to be a historically-accurate story, which would have been too limited for the gameplay. It gives a good sense of immersion in that period and enough freedom to the player but tries to remain as faithful as possible to "what could have been", given what we know of history and the historical figures who are represented in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let's get this out of the way.I do not give a ♥♥♥♥ about the historical revisionism or the identity politics they shoved into this game.  It's grating and clumsy.  Keep your modern ideals out of historical depictions, for the love of God.That aside, the game is very good.  The combat is challenging and intuitive.  The characters are excellent (for the most part) and the modern idealism is nowhere near enough to ruin the game.  The story line is compelling, the character development is nice and the choices felt appropriate.  I was invested from the moment I realized we were about to be boarded by "pirates" all the way up to deciding the fate of Rome itself.It's good stuff.  I liked it.Crazy cat lady can die.  A pox upon whoever thought her voice was anything other than audio cancer.I especially enjoyed the customization both in skills and equipment. There is power creep but it's only in three tiers.  You get plenty of material to keep up with things.  Upgrades are plentiful and there is no time limit in the campaign, which was refreshing.I should say that, despite how much fun combat was, the system is pretty easy to bust.  An army of Principes and Triarii is enough to dismantle anything the game will throw at you.  I went with four Principes and two Triarii and won every battle with little fuss.  There is plenty of fun to be had with a balanced team; the skills for the Velites and Sagittarii are versatile and potent.  However, nothing beats a solid shield and a long, pointy stick.I would be bothered by this if not for the fact that, historically, heavy infantry have been among the most potent and successful fighting elements to ever stomp across a battlefield.  Ultimately, the game leaves it up to you to figure out what is best and I could not be happier for it.The mass battles are a bit of a letdown but I can accept them.  It's a card game of sorts with wiggly little icons.  It's a side-show to the meat of the game.  To make up for it, the climactic final battles for each region are intricate and fun.  I was not ready for the first finale, although I managed to claw my way to victory.  I would like to see more, however, the game feels just long enough to leave you wanting more and not to over-stay its welcome.You decide the pacing.  You can push as fast and hard as you want or take your time.  The random encounters, skirmishes and other story elements are good.  It all meshes together nicely and nothing gets too complex.  Very X-Com but with ancient weapons, complete with base building and research (in a manner of speaking).It's good.  I had fun.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I played this blind on Insane/Iron Man. I found the game challenging but not overwhelming in most cases. That said, I highly DO NOT recommend playing Iron Man on your first playthough. It's entirely possible to get stuck and lose your playthrough. This did not actually happen to me, but it got very close, multiple times.There's a lot right with this game. Many of the tactical encounters are solid and the dialogue trees/choices great. The game feels fairly authentic with its cultural details.. mostly...The voice acting, while enthusiastic, is culturally tone deaf, meaning it is well acted but fails to represent most of the cultures accurately. Personally I'm pretty tired of ancient Romans in media having exclusively English accents. Every other culture in this game at least attempts to have an accent vaguely representative of their skin color. It really feels like they have White people accents, Brown people accents and Black people accents but definitely not authentic Italian, Egyptian and Germanic voice actors.Voice acting aside, there are many historical features and details that do add to the immersion of the game that other games don't really address: Roman law, interactions with the Senate, and political navigation within Roman society. I actually wish that the game focused more on those details than the military campaign.Normally I would prefer the grand strategy and tactical elements to the role play events, but there are some major design and quality of life features in this game that ultimately lead me to NOT RECOMMEND buying and playing this game. Grand Campaign Map: You are a Legatus. You command legions. On the campaign map you must conquer some 15+ fortresses per theater (Greece, Egypt, Gaul, possibly more? I haven't finished the game, 60 hours at the time of this review). This is BY FAR the most tedious aspect to the game. It's basically a few clicks and you lose a few soldiers. Nevertheless it still takes several, several minutes to pacify a region.I've never lost a legion battle in any of the theaters. It never came close. This whole thing is just a massive time and denarii sink for the player. The grand campaign is a mandatory feature that you cannot skip and your success in it has a major impact in how quickly you progress.A battle between armies drops the player on a battlemap that is symbolic only and has no meaningful impact on the resolution of the battle. Throughout the battle you are presented with 4 events and 3 cards per event. You select a card and both sides lose or gain some arbitrary amount of soldiers and then you get some loot at the end. As long as you keep army moral up (gained by certain cards as a flat stat) and enter the engagement with more soldiers than the enemy (you just buy more soldiers in camp, there are no types of soldiers) you cannot lose.Once you secure a region you must pacify it with a side quest. Sometimes it requires you to send your party to kill or destroy something where you'll fight a tactical battle. The problem is that you are not allowed to use your companion praetorians. You have to use the other praetorians that you hired and don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about, who likely don't have the best gear or specialization. Additionally they might have a low opinion of you which will cause them to route or act disobedient (you will lose control of the character for a turn).[[Anyone who has played a CRPG understands how time consuming it is to maintain gear for a 5 man party, especially a game like this with a crafting system (that requires in-game time to create by the way). If you understand how monotonous it can be for 5 characters, imagine having to do it for 15. 9 of which have no dialogue or character interactions]]Encounters: There are many things about tactical battles that this game does very well. The AI makes some surprising tactical decisions and I found MOST of the battles challenging but interesting. That said, it is entirely possible to find yourself in an impossible to win scenario. If you are playing on IronMan the autosave is at the beginning of the battle and if you cannot win the battle, you cannot proceed with the campaign. There are a couple situations where you might get stuck, Pacification quests (where you bring a sub-par party to a battle), companion quests, and the most likely one, Siege Battles.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: If one likes this kind of game - tactical rpgs - this game offers a wide variety of 'chess-like' battles in a great and vast scenario around the rise of a Roman Emperor.The campaign is well designed (do choices matter?), the crafting system simple but efficient, skills and perks both of characters and weapons are well thought, rounded-up by a variety of management tasks around your legion(s) and provinces, besides of developing and maintaining main and side characters.Some might say, it's too repetitive, but what can you do - a swordfight is a swordfight, no matter the repeating maps. It's an off-spring of chess after all :) The campain drives the game and connects the different story-lines, invasions and battles, which produces some kind of excitement about what's going to be next.On the other side, as a sophisticately developed off-spring of chess,  would not have been wrong. Especially game-play features with some automatisation for legion management, basic crafting or similar to-organize-tasks, mulit-selection menus (inventory) or similiar quality-of-life stuff would have been nice [or if they are there, easier to find]. Also ai is a bit strange in battles (as usual, who wants Skynet to learn basic battle tactics from a computer-game? ;), like the closer archer running further away to shoot and the 2nd running to the 1st's starting position to shoot, but in general the close range combat levers out these usual ai-weaknesses when featuring modern weapons ('Hey, hombre, why are you shooting me in the back?'). On contrary, sometimes there appears to be some ai tactics, which also seem to be easier to produce with antique weapons than co-ordinating an ai swat team...However, my bench-mark for this kind of games is (still) "Jagged Alliance 2" and on this scale a liking 6.9/10 for me, with actually a lot of potential imho. Hope, I have not missed anything, if so forgive me and enjoy this game.EDIT: After finishing the game I am happy to increase my liking to 7.5. It would deserve more but the above mentioned flaws remain. Choices matter and there is a chance I will replay it to see a different, less democratic outcome... ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the Expedition Series, classic old school inspired meaningful RPG's then you are going to love Expedition: ROME!Currently played a good amount of hours and I am sure I have not even completed 1/3 of the game yet. The amount of stuff to do overtime as you manage your Legion day by day keeps you pre-occupied before you even know what time it is! :DThe combat is incredibly satisfying and the tactics and range of strategy with each class archtype, skills and equipment provides you and your Praetorian Guard (Companion like party) with a diverse choice. There are multiple ways in which you can complete objectives at times and depending on how cunning or not so cunning you are, it can provide again that satisfaction.The game has some good humor build in to the characters, the voice acting is interesting along with the characters themselves and storyline. The developers have evidently put some degree of research into the Latin and how Romans would be perceived if speaking English to an extent! Of course in this modern world we now live in, there are slightly non historical sections of the inspired world but then that is not what the game sets out to do in its entirety.I have yet to encounter any issues, smooth performance and enjoyable experience, well worth the price and nice to see a finished product that provides that satisfaction for once!Manage your base, manage your legion, level up your commanders and conquer all who dare stand against ROME.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed the game but still have major mixed opinions on the game. I am a huge Roman history buff so I am inclined the like the game more than someone who isn't into Roman history. But for every good there is something I feel that is bad about the game.I enjoyed the combat as it is simple but takes some time to master it. However, I do not think that the difficulty balance is well adjusted and can use some work. Some missions are far too easy and some are far more difficult than I'd like. I think the biggest problem with the game is that I cannot prepare for each individual last mission as much as I'd like, especially for the sieges. Who is this guy on my team again? Oh it's that naked one. All you see before you start the battle is just the name of those characters but unless they have a really unique portrait instead of a generic photo, you probably aren't going to remember your individual praetorians. THQ should at least let you customize the looks of your praetorians and their names to make them more memorable. Your individual choices do feel like they have some sort of weight to them. In Act I, you are faced with helping either the choice of a religious zealot who initially opposes you but who has the people's best interest at heart or the wife of the previous leader who is a strong supporter for you but is implied to be a tyrant. Who do you choose?Commanding A legion in Act I and Act III was fun for me but the fact that you only control one legion for most of the game is absurd. Everyone makes you out to be this talented commander and yet you are commanding only one legion? In Act II you'll command two legions which was where most of the fun was as you had to balance out which legion was best suited for certain situations and which legion was better suited for something else.In addition, the time you spend in the city of Rome is honestly pretty disappointing. The trailer implies that you will have to carefully navigate and maneuver the political system. You are constantly overhearing how corrupt the system is but how can you feel it if you were never really a part of it in the first place?  The only time it is mentioned of you climbing the political offices is in the epilogue.All of that said. I really enjoyed the game and I found myself starting two more separate playthroughs because I found the story to be intriguing and that your actions and its consequences are repeatedly mentioned. I recommend this if you either like Roman history which games often don't often take advantage of, if you like simple but hard to master turn based combat or if you enjoy the feeling of adventure across many different settings. Hopefully, THQ will release a DLC where you can command legions on a much larger scale and where you navigate the political setting much more in-depth.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a point in the third chapter where things start to drag. I like that I feel like I got the best possible outcome but it still came at costs. I didn't get everything I wanted and not everyone lived through it. Just a very good historical RPG and it makes me excited for what might come next in this series.

It's insanely difficult on normal, it's too easy on easy. Your squad dies, it sucks, they die easily and quickly, they die repetitively.  Easy was fun, the balance was better,  it had some difficulty but it wasn't excessive.  I'm talking about the demo now.  I only put 21 minutes into the actual game when I ran into a brick wall that pissed me off. What made me request a refund is that I played the demo, I tried it out on normal and it was too damn difficult.  So I started again and played it on easy,  I finished the demo.  So I picked up the game,  but then after I was forced to replay the final part of the demo, which I easily won on easy, I'm told I have to go to Asia Minor.  So I set off moving my tiny 5 person squad across the sea to Asia Minor,  I make a left turn towards the east because there's a resource there I want to get closer to for a recon.  TWO of my squad gets injured, the game tells me in text format that it's a flood and I could have lost some of the crafting materials and supplies I had accumulated as well but that didn't happen, but it could have.  I have no 'doctor' to place them in 'Triage' to fix up their injuries and if I do nothing, they can die.....this was a game breaker for me.  It's dumb as hell and I won't tolerate it. Okay, this sucks I tell myself,  I guess I can put up with it because I'm on a pacified island that I own so I don't have to worry about an ambush with a 3 man squad, all I have to do is go to the far end of the island and return and they will be ready to go. _childDocuments_.review: Turn based tactical RPGs, there is no fantasy, based on Roman history (not accurate thought).- You play as a Roman noble (customizable), your are send as a legate into "missions" (like chapters). Each mission is in different locations (Egypt,Greece,Gaul, etc).- Inbetween you have story in Rome itself, you have allies/political enemies in Rome.- You "manage" an army and go on tactical turn based quests with your buddies. - Gameplay loop is motivating, finish challenging quests, gear up- level up, unlock skills, etc ...- You can make many decision, there are multiple ending, you can romance, etc ...I liked that one
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying this quite a bit. Good graphics, excellent voice acting, pacing seems good, I am a huge fan of Roman history and this greatly scratches an itch, taking place during the Third Mithridatic War which is within 20 years of events that people less versed in Roman history will recognize. There's an overland map that reminds me a bit of Mount and Blade. The tactical battles are fun (which is saying something as its a genre I don't usually play much). All in all, a pretty fun game at a good price that I've already got my money's worth out of and recommend it to people who enjoy tactical RPGs, Roman history, or games you can pick up and put down easily.

_childDocuments_.review: Great story, difficult but fair combat this continues the excellence of the Expedition Series of games. _childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do. It is a great turn-based RPG, with an excellent story and tons of great mechanics. But the combat is exhaustingly difficult. Sucks the life out of this game. You are expected to go into an area where you are overwhelmingly outmanned, the enemy has more tools and ranged archers than you, and rely on your mostly low-level buffs and swordsman-only characters to survive. The difficulty is *punishing*, and not in a good way like Dark Souls. Example: One level you have to ensure a roman governor survives. He is An AI so he stupidly goes out and fights anyone, putting himself in danger, and the enemy has an assassin class which can cloak and appear out of nowhere to kill you, and all of their archers have tacks, smoke and poison as a throwable which you cannot get yet because you haven't unlocked the crafting ability yet. It is literally your handicapped small platoon of units versus an army every single time. You have to be the most skilled and patient player to enjoy this, and if one set of things doesn't go right based on AI behavior, you just wasted 15-20 minutes to just replay it again. This is why I describe it as  "exhaustingly difficult". And keep in mind, I'm only at the first area where you need to liberate Asia. I can only imagine how much more punishing this gets down the road. It's too much!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was surprisingly good and even a great value the price.I came into Expeditions Rome with very little expectations. What I got was  Xcom-style combat, card based army battles with a layer of RPG with moral choice options that alter the ending of the game.You play as "the Legate" character on a quest for revenge. You lead a Roman legion. Your tactical combat troops consists of your followers and recruitable characters, making up your Praetorian Guard.some bullet points- Weapon/armor/item crafting and upgrading - gives you great options not only for damage/protection but design/style.- Followers are interesting to interact with and even romace'able, plenty of story and quests around them.- Card based field battles are not the core of the game but needed to progress.- Turn based combat on a 'hexagon grid' is the core of the game- Classes has 3 skill trees each and you get enough points to fill two of them I had great fun with it atleast.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay you're about to go out on a mission. You have your #squad of story NCPs that you've used for literally every mission so far. Oh, but for some reason, for these specific missions, you can't use your story NPCs. You have to send generic create-a-wrestler NPCS. EXCEPT YOU DON'T EVEN GET TO CREATE THEM YOURSELF, YOU CAN ONLY PICK THEM FROM A LIST.Why? The only time people play with generic NPCs in a game that has actual, real NPCs with their own dialogue, quests, etc. is if they hate the story NPCs personalities or they want to minmax. You can't even minmax in this game because the character system is so shallow, so forcing you to send generic NPCs on certain missions makes no sense. The game even says this is because these missions are basically beneath your MC. Then why do I still have to do combat with these generic guys? It's a massive layer of added tedium to have to manage an extra squad of interchangeable dolts I would never use otherwise. I would have refunded if this mechanic didn't start to appear after the refund window.
_childDocuments_.name: Expeditions: Rome

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 6/10 = close call / buy on sale onlyPros:-roman/historical theme works suprisingly well-great and layered companions that grow over time-amazing ambient storytelling (e.g. art, banter at camp/cities, etc.)-fully voiced, great quality-combat is solid, maps are varied (even the "random mission" ones)Cons:-too many features that contribute nothing (busy work)-very sharp decline in quality after Act II-Itemisation & crafting system is poorly designed-UI is not great or pretty either (with the exception of the portraits and their use, those are great)I got the game on sale and generally had my fun with it. At the same time, the last third of the game left a very bad taste in my mouth and I have no intention to hop into another campaign, play a different character or try a different path. For me, this is very unusual.On a sidenote: While the roman theme is charming, it is ultimately not very deep. A lot of stuff gets only a brief mention or is absent entirely. Caesar, which our character is a stand-in for, pulled off way more crazy stuff in the last 10 years of his life then we even get the option to.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was such an amazing and MASSIVE improvement from its predecessor (Expedition Vikings - to be fair, also a good game). I don't know where to begin <3Storyline and graphics are immensley beautiful. Really love how the developers really brought each era and culture to life in the details and storytelling. I love the banter as you explore the military camps and see the impact of the choices you make as you take over Rome really matter. They also did a great job showing how your gender really factored in how the world reacts to your actions (A woman as a legatus?! What madness!) Companions were a massive improvement as well. I was really invested in all of them and loved how all their stories are interwined. _childDocuments_.review: Exceeded my expectations.  Streamlined RPG elements, strong tactical gameplay.I'm enjoying this much more than Divinity Original Sin or either of the Pathfinder PC games.The character advancement and itemization elements are lighter (which is a relief after the second Pathfinder game!) and the tactical combat elements are strong.It feels more like Warhammer Mechanicus, which I also enjoyed a lot. _childDocuments_.review: I think Expeditions: Rome does alright.ProsMost of the companions interest me. The side characters as well.Battle system is very fun, and the use of tactical items are particularly enjoyable and add thrill to the missions.The dialogue options give the player a lot to do to roleplay a character that they have in their mind. Unlike other games, you are not punished in an unspoken way for being the bad guy (most of the time).The primary antagonist is a snake, and the story makes you relish to kill them every time you encounter them. Good to see, as many games' villains are not very well fleshed out and are just there to make the story resemble a plot.NeutralThe war system. I don't feel very involved in the process of the battles for cities and landmarks. Pick a card. This does this. This'll make you lose more than the others will. But, this game is mostly an isometric RPG so it doesn't really add or detract from the experience.ConsRomances are a bit underwhelming imo.Pacification missions. If I never see a bunch of weapon shipments that I have to burn again I will die a happy man.Random encounters, specifically the ones with battles, are obnoxious and don't add much to the game. Having simple text-based encounters were enjoyable enough and helped with immersion.8.5/10

name: Super Mega Baseball 3
detailed_description: Super Mega Baseball 3 refines the series’ formula with the deepest on-field simulation yet, comprehensive offline and online play including Franchise mode and the newly added Online Leagues mode, and vastly improved graphics. New content includes revamped UI plus tons of new audio, team/character content, and stadiums with variable lighting conditions. Features: Challenge your hand-eye coordination or relax and hit dingers with fluid gameplay that scales seamlessly from novice to beyond-expert levels of difficulty. Apply and refine your baseball instincts with a sophisticated baseball simulation featuring new pickoff and stealing mechanics, wild pitches/passed balls, designated hitters, and situational player traits. Take in the sights and sounds of 14 richly detailed ballparks, each featuring unique day, night and alternate lighting conditions. Guide an evolving team to greatness over multiple seasons in the all new Franchise mode featuring player development, aging, retirement and signing/releasing of free agents (1vCPU, 2vCPU, local or online). Organize a cross-platform league with your friends in the newly added, versatile Online Leagues mode (1v1, online only). Compete online to win pennants and climb to higher divisions in the cross-platform Pennant Race mode (1v1, online only, controller only). Create your ideal league with a comprehensive customization suite that includes season length/structure, team names/uniforms/logos, and player names/appearance/attributes. Play or simulate any combination of games/teams in customized Seasons and Elimination brackets, solo or with friends (1vCPU, 2vCPU, 1v1, 2v1, 2v2, CPUvCPU, local or online). Skip customization and compete for top leaderboard scores with standardized teams and settings (locked player attributes) in Standard Season and Standard Elimination modes (1vCPU, 2vCPU, local or online). Download the free demo to play an unlimited number of games in the competitive online Pennant Race mode, play Exhibition games against the AI, or experiment with the customization suite.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Basically SMB2, but slightly better. Franchise mode.So, right off the bat(Haha I'm funny) this is a great game. There are a lot of pros, and some cons. There are reviews out there that state this game isn't different enough from the previous iteration to justify another purchase, and that's a fair statement. It does hold weight. But for me, it's the smaller details that make this game shine, and make it worth the purchase. And there's a LOT of them. But first, the negatives.So I feel like this was a huge missed opportunity to add much needed gameplay options, such as adjustable camera angles for batting and pitching, options for reticles, like turning them off for added difficulty, or different interfaces. Think The Show. Also, there's some minor roster changes, not a big deal, but I kinda grew to like my players in the season I played in SMB2. Buuuuut, you can import all teams and leagues from your SMB2 saves. Perfect. Honstly, that's about it. Now, the positives. As I said, there are a LOT of new additions that make this game better than the previous, but they're not huge overhauls or anything. For instance, in game, there's a new presentation, and animations for batter walk ups, strikeouts(batter and pitcher), and all the batting stances(I think) have been upgraded. Also the announcer now says all the player names. Except custom players, which is cool as ♥♥♥♥. They've added pick offs, wild pitches, broken bats, several traits that any player may have (up to 2) which all add the the experience. At least for me, it does. I do find myself getting annoyed after 3 pick off attempts in a row when there's a speedy runner on first. They've also added most of, if not all, the DLC from SMB2. The stadiums, which now can be day, evening or night for any stadium, rather than every stadium having a set time of day. That's probably my favorite addition tbh. Actually, editing this in, my favorite thing is that there's now a casual throw to a cut off man when catching a fly ball out with no one on, whereas in SMB2 they'd rocket the ball in. That's actually my favorite addition. There may or may not be more, I was kind of in a hurry to get a review up. But it's all those little details that really enrich the experience for me, and if they do for you, it's worth it. If all that sounds negligible to you, I;d recommend not getting it. However, there is Franchise mode.I wont be getting into Franchise mode, because I've never been interested in franchise mode in any sports game, ever. I just like to play. Others will get into it, I'm sure. Not that anyone will ever actually see this. Pepesad

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. I come from years of The Show. This game really scratches that baseball itch I was looking for and on PC? Even better. I didn't buy into the first installments, partially because I was happy with my 2014 copy of The Show and partially because of the cartoony graphics. I have come to reconsider both of those and am glad I did. First, the gameplay is superb. This isn't a sim but everything from pitching to batting to fielding feels right and you can adjust the difficulty for each aspect of the game individually. Striking batters out with sliders feels rewarding and hitting that 500ft grand slam is pretty grand (ha) as well. Player ratings make big impacts you can see and feel, for instance, having a high fielding score means you can jump and dive further.The graphics and goofyness has absolutely stuck with me. From the player mannerisms to the silly company ads on the stadium back drop, it works. To be honest, I wish there were more poses and player celebrations/intimidation.I spend most of my time in franchise mode and to be honest, it took me a bit to warm up to. There is no "contract" length, players play for a set amount until they retire, you swap them for someone else, or some RNG makes them want to test free agency. Free agency is auction style, where player asking salaries decrease every game until a team scoops them up. There is no natural increase in skill game to game, season to season for players as you have to spend excess budget to train players for increases. The training is permanent but who is available week to week for training is RNG. There is no trading or waivers. I have come to enjoy this system, but in operation, I do have critiques. It works, it's very functional but I hope they build upon it.All in all this is a great game series that could eventually supplant The Show as my all time favorite baseball series if they flesh it out with QOL improvements. As it stands, it is one of the most fun baseball games I have ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: I needed something to help pass sleepless nights that wasn't depressing or violent.  SMB3 is a fun, surprisingly deep baseball game.  I believe it's probably great for kids and adults alike.  The art style is a bit comic book, but it has a charm that grows on you and a sense of humor that is welcome.  Even better, the style does not detract from the fact that the game is a decent baseball sim.  Personally I find the entirely fictional lineup a relief.  I was an avid fan of baseball years ago and it's refreshing to know some basics about the game without having to be up on who all the actual players are now.  The teams are all inventive and interesting.  The game even gives you the ability to make your own team (by modifying an existing one) and is pretty great at giving you options to make them your own.  There is a forgiving difficulty selection that allows you to really tailor the game to your own level.  Great for us old guys who maybe aren't as fast as we used to be.  But it's not all reflexes, you can employ strategy to a surprising degree and manufacture runs with the best of them.  I immediately found the pitching to be superior and intuitive.  The batting took me quite a few games and a youtube video or two to 'get'.  Controls on the PC are slightly quirky without a controller, but doable.  I have an Xbox wireless controller on order that should help immensely.  All in all, this is a great distraction from my usual hardcore strategy and action titles.  You can jump in for a quick three inning exhibition game or play a franchise through multiple seasons of 9 inning games.  For $45 I believe this is well worth it for the fun.   If you have kids that enjoy baseball there are a variety of co-op and pvp modes.  I haven't tried the multiplayer yet but have read it's decent.  This just seems like a really solid and fun title for your collection.  Especially while we are all stuck at home.  I don't think you will regret a purchase at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This is far and away my favorite baseball game since MVP 2005. Really the only thing missing is some sort of "farm system" in franchise mode, other than that, its essentially all here. The actual gameplay and ball physics are astonishing good. Better than a lot of newer AAA titles. The game is super customizeable allowing you to tweak the game to your liking and to your skill level. After 200+ hours I still play at a 65 ego (ego= difficulty) and have to have a good roster in order to win consistently at that level, the game goes up to 100 ego, so I still have plenty of room to grow and will be hundreds of hours more before the game becomes "too easy" for me at max difficulty... plus there is always multiplayer for an additional challenge against human opponents. Also there is a team, league and player creator which allows you to customize EVERY aspect of your franchise. All my 200 hours have been in multiplayer or in single player franchise leagues that I built from the ground up. One league I based around a choose your own adventure baseball book I read as a child that had fictional teams, and had fictional season stats for the players, I built the teams from the book and based each player on the stats from the book in order to create them, so Harold Carlson was my speedy, high contact, low power leadoff man, Ed Neighbor was my crafty veteran ace who used to be a fastballer but has had to rely on his breaking pitches as he has aged.... etc. etc. etc.There is just hours of fun to be had in this game in a multitude of ways. There is a flavor for EVERYONES tastes and its finally a baseball game that you can curtail EXACTLY to your liking. Worth the price 100%.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tricky one, so there are some caveats. The Super Mega Baseball franchise is fantastic. I'm not a baseball fan, but I love these games. But as for the third one...If you've never played a Super Mega Baseball game or you've only played the first game in the series, I definitely recommend this one. If you already have Super Mega Baseball 2, I'd wait for a sale because I just don't think there's quite enough here yet to justify the price. Franchise is cool, player traits are cool, and the huge number of stadiums are cool. This is definitely the best in the series, but I think it's a tougher recommendation if you already have Super Mega Baseball 2.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic arcade style baseball game. From someone who loves baseball and baseball games, this is the best baseball game I have played. I was skeptical because of the arcade style (I play MLB the Show for the authenticity and realistic gameplay compared to other baseball games), but this game won me over quickly because although the game has an arcade look the gameplay is surprisingly realistic. The animations are smooth and they do a good job with the pitching/hitting minigames and the baserunning. Catching flyballs are hard at first because there is no on-field reticle telling you where the ball will drop but after a while you get better at judging the flight of the ball and it makes flyballs much more interesting. The best part of the game is the ego system. Its a 1-100 system that changes your difficulty. At first I was killing team at 30 ego which is were the game starts you. I increased the ego by 5 each game I won. At 50 ego I was still beating teams really well so I kept going. At 60 I was beeating teams but it was close so I increased one more time to 65. At 65 I got destroyed two games in a row so I bumped it down to 62. The little increments really matter. At 62 I win most games but still lose at least a third, which is about right for how good my team is. The delicate balance of the difficulty is really good, especially with no sliders neccesary. My go to game mode is the Franchise mode. I like the customization for what type of league and how many games you want to play. I would really like to see a promotion/relegation system in a game like this as it seems like it would be perfect with this. The salary cap/player development system is fantastic, allowing you to go all out and buy the best talent you can or buy young cheap players and rely on developing talent over time. I do wish there was more roster flexibility but its still a good system as it is. I recommend this to anyone who loves baseball and baseball games. The quick paced games and fun atmosphere make for a time fly-by experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy The Show more than the SMB games - but you still can't play The Show on PC. So for baseball fans, this is your best option.And it's a really good option. Initially the cartoonish player designs turned me away from the series but there's surprisingly solid fundamentals here. The Ego system is really handy for slowly ramping up the difficulty so even someone with no experience playing a baseball game can jump right in to a full season and have fun. Franchise mode is maybe the highlight for me, as it is without the simulationist levels of management you get in OOTP. There is a time and place for that, SMB3 is more about on-the-field action. The tool for creating teams is very robust. The online is active at the time of writing. This scratches the baseball itch and is probably being overlooked by a lot of sports fans on Steam because the art style and lack of licensed teams/players. Which is a shame because those people are missing out.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best baseball experiences in the market at the moment. The Franchise mode really makes the game to the point where I am currently playing this mode exclusively. Although the mechanics around player development or trading do not resemble real world at all, they are very easy to grasp intuitively, and make sense in their own way. Seeing the team ebb and flow through the course of the season, as the pitchers stop line drives with their craniums, and batters hit hot and cold streaks, adds spice to an already fairly solid baseball game that manages to juggle arcade feel with pretty realistic game mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Another home run for this under the radar franchise. The core gameplay isn't tinkered with too much, but it's well refined and there's a new level of depth with franchise mode. The base running controls are a bit difficult to get used to and lead to some comically bad situations, but I'm sure I'll get used to it. Also, kudos to the developer... after three crashes in my first hour of play I was pretty frustrated, but the developer responded directly to me on Reddit AND released a hotfix within 12 hours of the game launching. Now completely stable. Highly recommended for all sports fans in these weird times.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great! I`ve owned the two previous games but neither of them struck me quite like this one has. In fact, no other sports game has ever struck me like this game. I`m the kind of person who buys sports games to create my own custom league and teams and watch the cpu play each other. I rarely ever play in the games myself. This game started the same way, but once I actually learned how to play it and the mechanics behind batting, pitching, fielding, etc. I actually love playing this game in franchise mode. My favorite feature is probably being able to customize the difficulty of every skill. I am a much better batter, pitcher, and runner than I am a fielder, so I can have the difficulty set higher on everything except fielding and it really allows me to have a great fun/challenge balance where I`m not winning everything but I`m not losing everything either.Franchise mode is a blast, and it really makes the game feel more realistic and dare I say story driven as of all of the players have their own lives separate from what you control.The main changes I would like to see in SMB4 is better/more face customization (it is very difficult to make asian-looking players which is a big deal if you have as many anime-based teams as I do, not to mention Shohei Ohtani), the addition of multi-year contracts, and the addition of user-controlled replays (so I can see where the bat hits the ball, replay exciting plays, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Whether you small-ball 4 runs over 8 batters or hit that grand salami; or you turn a sweet double-play or stack up 6 Ks in a row; every aspect of baseball is done supreme justice in this impeccable sports game. Even losing is fun.As I've played I've had to change my thoughts on a couple of things, so here's some tips once you've bought the game. Some might be obvious if you've played baseball before, and some if you've played video games before, but I think this game appeals to everyone and not baseball fans or video game players alone.1. Keep your Ego low until you can actually hit. And I don't mean home-runs, I mean Hits. If you can't even get on first then you're not gonna have fun, which is how baseball works. Keep your strike zone on screen (using your imagination), don't swing at everything, and hit the ball where the fielders ain't. And don't forget to bunt, which I do too often: if bunting worked for Ichiro, it'll do for anyone at all.2. On the other side, learn to field properly. There are some hard-coded Error probabilities in the game (not a lot; enough to break your heart when it wants to), but the vast majority of times the actual run-scoring errors have been on my end. Letting a run score cause you tried to turn a double-play when there's already 2 Outs is utterly low-IQ, but in the heat of the moment it happens. Same with base-running: sometimes you think it's a triple when it's a single and you feel like a moron. Familiarize yourself with the 'default intelligent play' for each situation, and develop the instinct (AKA 'game-sense') for it -- but that won't happen if you're not thinking at all about what that would be.3. Don't use the automatic swing/pitch button, but learn to use the power-gauge button (I forget what these are called -- you'll know what I mean), if only because you actually have more fun that way. You just don't feel the weight of the swing when you're tapping a button.4. The Ego rank names are actually very accurate. "50" isn't "average difficulty", it's legitimately Hard. Don't scale it up like mad and then get angry for losing -- start at 20, or 10 if you need to. (0 does seem a bit much.) Once you can comfortably win with a 3-6 run margin, scale it up. I'm currently at 60 and win/loss at roughly .500 but started at 25 and closer to .100, so you definitely get better at the game. Also note that you can change the Ego of various mechanics (Hitting/Fielding/Pitching) independently: the game is literally begging you to take control, and tailor your experience so you have the most fun.5. Part of this tailoring is to find a good team for yourself. I like the Freebooters, cause I like pitching. They're slow as ♥♥♥♥ and score runs only when you hit accidental doubles, but they get Ks. You're playing a game of attrition. Other teams require stealing bases, others homers: like I said, you tailor the game to your style, and almost no limitation is set in SMB3 on that count.6. Speaking of teams, play one of the other modes and don't stick to Exhibition games. One-off games are easy to launch and a short time-commitment, but sports are about investment. Once you know "your team", learn the strengths and weaknesses of your players; get them through injuries and bad mentalities. It's more fun that way. It's more baseball that way.7. That said, DON'T be intimidated by the many modes, or all the other "hard baseball simulation" facets of the game. If you download the Demo, just play Beewolves Versus Sirloins and learn to whack the ball. If you buy the game, don't worry about the player stats and the team stats and the game modes and the yada-yada until you've gotten involved enough that you become naturally curious about how they help you play better. Which, of course, will happen because this is a great baseball sim in addition to the sheer arcadey joy of swinging, missing, hitting, etc.I don't get to play as much of this game as I'd like, so these are only beginner tips. But if they can help you get a foothold in this spectacular game, then my job here is done. Call me back when the Angels trade Ohtani.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun. Arcady and enjoyable while playing solo, it's really good when playing with friends. Players looking for a simulation or a very challenging game may be a little frustrated, as several people noticed some flaws, but at intermediate levels it's a lot of fun. If you love baseball and you are looking for a fun game, this may be a great choice, especially if you have a couple friends to play with.A little negative: in the franchise mode, whenever you sign free agents they are not presented by their name during the game, instead they are presented with their number ("now pitching... number 34") which really lays waste to the great immersion this game manages to bring.Devs: if you make a DLC fixing this thing, I'd even spend a couple bucks for it (but I really think that it should be a base feature of the game, so please consider it for an eventual SMB4)

_childDocuments_.review: Owner of SMB1,2,3. I've given this game 60 hours. It's broken.The catchup mechanics are horrible. Doesn't matter WHAT you do or where you pitch, the CPU will SMASH anything even 99 perfectly placed pitches. This is 70 ego. If you are ahead the CPU WILL come back at some point. You can pitch curveballs completely in the dirt where the circle is LITERALLY in the dirt, and the cpu will smash it for a hit. ALL pitching at high ego is basically throw 2 strikes right away and PRAY that the cpu doesnt smash it, which it often does. If you don't, the cpu will not swing. Unless, as stated above, the cpu is behind or there's runners on base, in which case the cpu will smash it.The game is so utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at times. I've resorted to actually ALT F4ing whenever the cpu does unfair stuff like smash 99 aimed pitches or there's dumb fielder errors. But it doesn't matter, it keeps on happening.I uninstalled and I'm never buying another SMB game again. I played 2 full franchise seasons and wanted to love this game so much but it's so infuriating. And the devs won't change it. I'm out.------EDIT: It seems my review is resonating with lots of peopleHere's an in-depth thread where I explain much more: The comments here and in the thread prove my point. 90% are just insults about my "skill level", as if that is somehow supposed to offend me. The other 10% of comments do actually discuss the actual issue: The problems are objectively there; you can't deny that. But are the issues worth dealing with and is the game still good/fun despite them?That's a call you can only make for yourself. For some, they think it's fun DESPITE the issues, which is perfectly fine as long as you recognize them. But you can't deny the issues exist unless you're a total fanboy or being dishonest in order to validate your own purchase behaviors. Unfortunately, too many gamers connect their entire identities with their gamer choices...

This is a high quality, fairly realistic, non-MLB licensed baseball game with enough depth in mechanics and team management to keep me wanting to play more after playing for 14 hours over the past 3 days.Who needs MLB teams when you can make a team called "Hentai" complete with a mess of purple tentacles as a logo and go on to lead the league in home runs with your ridiculously OP right fielder, "Kiwi Frankencop"?

_childDocuments_.review: Superb. Almost perfection. The negatives a very VERY small so I'll list them first. There is no 1. instant replay which is a shame because you cant watch close up "climbing" the fence to get the out, (yeah they do that)pick-off of heavy leaders (yeah they do that too) Double plays, outfield to plate saves, etc;;you get the drift. amazing stuff happens and it would be cool to watch it up close. 2. The information of players could be presented a little better. for those that dont care about stats this is a good thing as the game moves along quickly. But this is baseball. It Is THE sport for Stat heads like myself. Dont get me wrong there is a lot of information, but it flashes too quickly. What I would do is show a large image of their BB card to the left with  some summaries of their daily performance to the right and maybe versus their season performance to the right of that. 3. Broadcasters are needed imo. It would give more "life" to the game. I would hope if they do add this in the next iteration of the game or a patch or DLC for this one, the announcers would be able to say player created names. This is 2020 i am sure the technology exist to say any word typed on a screen.Ok That was a lot of writing about some minor quibbles. Everything else I can think of about the game is polished and executed to the highest level. Just a brief list of tripple A features listed below:Animations of playersCalls of the Umpire Actual play of baseballPersonality of PlayersComplete editing of players, teams, logos, colors...The stadiumsAbility to add genders: wanna make an all lady team? not a problem. wanna change the gender of an existing player? not a problemAnother cool feature is some players have "traits". Like "Kman" giving a bonus to accuracy if the pitcher has 2 strikes on a batter or "contact vs LHP" giving a greater chance for a well hit ball verses a left handed pitcher.These traits are by no means a guaranty of success but they do add bonuses. And there are several of these traits that all players may have, some players even having two of these traits.If you like baseball AT ALL you owe it to yourself to go pick up this game. It is worth every penny. 10/10.EDIT:I know many, including myself dont even bother to read reviews without some real time invested in said game. So now I have nearly 30 hours in and nothing in that playtime has warranted anything except more praise for this game.....EDIT: 7/3/21With close to 100 hours in now I realized I left some things out of this review.1. Pitcher animation have LOTS of variety. From the wind up to the delivery. You will clearly see it in a game between opposing pitchers or when someone is rotated in.2. Batting stances as well. Some players lean way back on their back leg, some swivel their hips, some stand more upright and swivel the bat3. Facial animations are there too. Some players smile confidently at the pitcher, some look like a deer in headlights,...you get the drift...4. all of the above are editable for each player.5 The stadium lighting and atmosphere. Slight fog/haze effects, time of day, night time..it is all excellently representedthe player controls take some getting used to..but I think they did that on purpose so that as you get good on the controls it is represented by your team and gives you a great sense of satisfaction when you turn a double play, hit one yard, or throw the runner out at home plate from right fieldThis game is a polished as I have ever seen in any video gameEdit 3/24/21 SALE PRICE. If you like BB games at ALL buy it.Edit: One of the saddest days of my gaming life. Electronic Arts "Absorbed" Metalhead, to get rid of the competition in my opinion, and now this great developer must either follow the EA sports protocol of designing intetionally designing broken games. Or design their own EA baseball game, with the same intentional broken protocols. EA- "Can't have a perfect game or else why would they buy next years release." Doesn't matter though. EA is evil slime and the metalhead developers are destined for the chopping block, just like the 20 or so other developers absorbed by EA. Sad...Edit 6/22 1038 hours...I think that qualifies my review.

_childDocuments_.review: Super Mega Baseball 3 is a sports game with a strong arcade convention, just like the previous parts of the series. There are no real teams or players here. The graphic style is cartoonish, and the gameplay is not pragmatic. The individual mechanics are simple and accessible - both for throwing the ball and for bouncing.The production of Metalhead Software offers several variants of fun. The most important one is Franchise, something like a career. Not only do we play the entire seasons here, which consists of thirty-two matches, but we also get to manage the entire team: signing contracts with new players, getting rid of those who do not fit the bill, taking care of pecuniary matters, setting up tactics, and so on. There are also settings options, thanks to which we can modify the game to suit our needs. We can also determine how long the season should and can be, as well as an indicator called Ego Meter that allows players to determine the degree of difficulty on a scale from 0 to 99.In addition to the Franchise, we can also play a full season without the simulation elements, and we also have access to online competition modes, such as Elimination Mode and Pennant Race. The game also offers rich possibilities in terms of broadly understood editing. We can modify not only the game itself, as mentioned above, but also players, teams and so on. If you want to gradually approach the world of baseball, this title is the best choice to do so, so arm yourself with your glove and climb the pitcher's hill to start having fun.7.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best baseball game I've played in a long time, dating back to Nintendo days with RBI Baseball, Baseball (Super) Stars. Its online features are superb, the matchmaking feature pairs you up with opponent of similar skill using a stat called "Ego", which updates automatically based on your play. With both Online Leagues and something called "Pennant Race" playing online is a lot of fun, without making you dedicate hours into a season if you're short of time. In single player mode you're able to guide through multiple seasons with players retiring and new players coming on-board, allowing you to act as front office manager making decisions on who get signed. Again, the "ego" stat allows you to fine tune the difficulty level. Overall, this game is the one you want if you're looking  for either a casual arcade style action or an in depth baseball simulator. Thumbs way up!

_childDocuments_.review: I say this completely unironically: this is the best sports game on the market right now. The level of customization is unmatched. The gameplay is satisfying and polished. Don't be fooled by the art style, this game is a fantastic baseball simulation, with just enough arcade-y aspects to keep it fresh and fun. Nine innings will fly by, in a good way.The franchise mode is where the game shines, in my opinion. The roster moves and transactions are overly-simplified, with a free-agency market the only method of new player acquisitions. However, this does not detract from the thrill of building a team season-by-season. I prefer to play a custom league with 32 teams over 162 game seasons (you can simulate in custom leagues), but you can go as big  or small as you want. One major gripe I have: PC suffers from random performance issues. Despite my FPS counter saying I am getting 60, the game occasionally slows down to almost unplayable levels. It is rare enough to not keep me from playing, but when it happens it is really frustrating. It is an issue that only happens on PC, and the devs have said on reddit that they are aware of the issue, so hopefully it is fixed soon.

_childDocuments_.review: I started off recommending this game and I had to change my opinion.They ruined the pitching. That's really the beginning and end of it. They ruined the whole feel of crafting an AB as a pitcher. You know what these hitters literally never do? Swing at pitches out of the strike zone. They just do not do it. You might see them look at strikes but they will NOT swing at bad pitches. So, good luck, right? You're going to be pitching to contact no matter how amazing your pitch sequences or how perfect your spots are. And painting the corners / switching speeds in NO WAY induces weak contact. They will crush whatever pitch whenever if the AI RNG dictates.Want to throw a ball out of the zone? Well I hope you have a ball to play with because that hitter knows you are not throwing it in the zone. Want to pain the corner? Nail perfect accuracy? Better still be prepared for hard contact whenever the game feels like it. I loved this game at first but the other reviews that point out how the game breaks down at high ego are spot on. It just doesn't feel right. In the MLB, hitter swing at pitches out of the zone 30% of the time! They only make contact on 66% of those swings! 66% of 30% is nearly 20%! For every 5 pitches you throw just out of the zone, they oughta swing at least one of them! I've thrown at least 100 and they've never chased one. It just does not feel right. A shame, really. I can't recommend it. It's either win by 10 runs or face impossible hitting.

_childDocuments_.review: A superb game. Super Mega Baseball 3 is a relatively simple, yet difficult baseball game with intuitive mechanics and a lot of depth. Don’t let the arcade style graphics fool you – this game is right up there with other major titles for its accuracy as a baseball simulator.As a former fair-weather fan of baseball, this game has taught me much about real game; It’s rules, mechanics, the do’s and don’ts, as well as real life issues that batters, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and fielders have to deal with. Beware the hanging slider!The gameplay is both fun and challenging. The game’s difficulty system, or ‘ego’ as it is called, allows the player to adjust the difficulty on a scale of 1-100. At higher egos a single point increase or decrease can be immediately felt in gameplay. A change of 5 or more, such as my recent change from 65 to 70 ego, can mean the difference between storming to victory in the playoffs with a single loss, to likely finishing second last in the league. Perseverance, self-reflection, and a high tolerance before getting tilted by the CPU, will lead to an enjoyable and fulfilling experience.The ‘how-to’ popups and limited tutorial/tips system is useful, but as always, the best way to learn is to keep and open mind and just play the game. If you know how baseball works, nothing is very hard to learn. But if you’re like me, and you didn’t know much coming in, it may take awhile to get the basics down -- but eventually things will just ‘click’, as it were, and your journey to the next stage of enjoyment will begin. The game’s multiplayer is also quite fun but has minor and consistent connectivity issues in most games. At this time, I have yet to participate in the game’s major multiplayer mode ‘Pendant Race’, though I have heard good things about the format, including its ability to ego balance. Nothing is perfect.As for gameplay..Pitching is very clean and straightforward; but is certainly not easy at higher egos. While pitching is more simplified than other titles (looking at you MLB The Show with your minigames), the difference between a power pitch and a normal pitch can regularly make the difference between that walk off dinger and a harmless fly ball. The fact that the CPU can predict your pitches after a few batters can be quite frustrating, but it adds yet another layer to worry about when it comes to pitching. Paying close attention to every pitch certainly feels like it makes a difference.Personally, I find batting to be the most difficult aspect of the game. It was relatively easy on lower egos, as there is significant built-in aim-assist and forgiving contact mechanics for those playing at lower levels. But as my ego increased, I found it more and more difficult to make good contact. I started taking the stats of hitters much more seriously, controlling the box as it were, and choosing to only hit certain types of balls.. when I had such a luxury. It really started to feel like the real thing!Fielding is good, but takes a lot of practice... and there is certainly a lot of annoying things that you can’t control. It is very difficult to pick off batters (as it should be), but also stopping steals against the CPU is nigh impossible without some luck and perfect timing. There is nothing more frustrating when your CF fails to catch a flyball with only a 0.2% of failure, but I understand why such a system exists. ♥♥♥♥ happens. It helps keep things interesting.What is awesome about the ego system is that all these aspects can be increased in difficulty in either slight or large segments… or you can just adjust the difficulty of each section independently and leave the others where they are! Having a hard time batting but you like where your pitching difficulty is? No problem! Just turn down the batting difficulty! Problem solved. The ego system really is just so useful and easy to understand.The franchise mode is a fresh and interesting take on managing a team. I’ve played a lot of EA NHL in my time, and although it’s fun to run a team based on a half-ass and half-implemented ‘real life’ cap, contract, and trade system.. sometimes you just need a break. The no-trade, free-agency based world of Super Mega Baseball 3’s franchise mode is certainly different, but still fun and engaging. The balance between spending to the cap and choosing to keep some of that money available to develop players is an interesting gameplay mixture that leads to tough decisions needing to be madeOh woe is me!! do I let go of Jackie Slam and Jack Sports just because I’m not going to make the playoffs?? But they are on such good contracts!! So many tough decisions... I do wish that trades and contracts were a part of the equation though… but the system JUST WORKS™ without them regardless. The teams and players have a lot of charm, and you can easily grow attached to them after playing for awhile. The Jacks are the best team in the universe, the Beewolves are an OP evil empire, and I will always cry over losing Huffley Buffler to free agency year 3. Overall, there is a lot to like about Super Mega Baseball 3. It can be as arcadey or as serious of a baseball sim as you want it to be. Even if you don’t know a lot about baseball, playing the game (in real life or in a video game) is perhaps the best way to learn. I purchased this game knowing little about baseball and learned how to play it by myself, in tandem with watching a lot of MLB. Now, several of my friends, many of whom don’t care for sports at all, have purchased the game and are enjoying their time playing. I would 100% recommend Super Mega Baseball 3 to baseball and other sports game fans looking for a robust baseball game to sink hours into. And yes, you will sink hours into it. It’s baseball! Infinite replayability! For all others, I’d give the free demo a try for a bit and see if you enjoy the game at its core. Afterall... it is a baseball sports game.I give it a 9/10. The best sports game I’ve played in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: My initial impression upon release was that this felt more like SMB 2.5 than a full-fledged sequel. But that changed the more I played and with every subsequent patch. Lots of minor (DH, pick-offs, wild pitches, double switches) and major (Franchise mode, practice mode, more teams/stadiums, better customization) additions that make it a more complete package than its predecessor. Franchise mode in particular is the feature attraction; It's fairly deep and there's enough meat on it to keep it engrossing as you progress from season to season. And the Ego difficulty system is still one of the best I've ever used in a sports game, allowing you to adjust the challenge at a comfortable and steady pace as you improve.This is hands-down the best baseball video game I've ever played, and a continuation of the formula that Metalhead has been improving upon ever since the first game in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: After putting  hundreds of hours into its predecessor, SMB2, I was hesitant to try SMB3 which looked like a money-grab re-release, nearly the same game.  In a lot of ways, it absolutely is.However, eventually, we gave SMB3 a try and are glad we did.  Here is why: Franchise mode makes playing consecutive seasons with the same team more interesting.  You really have to angst over offseason choices and then see how they pan out for you during the following season.  You are never given enough money to do all the things you want to do, so each decision has weight and consequence.  For example, you hold off signing a free agent hoping for a lower price, (there are several dozen rounds in the postseason and everyone's asking price comes down each round,) and some other team snatches the player you were coveting at the higher asking price, and you have to pivot.  That makes the offseason somewhat exciting and engaging.There is a ton to love here.1. Game play is just fun.  That's #1 for any game.2. It's highly customizable just like its predecessor was.  You can approximate the logo of every MLB team or make up some awesome ones on your own.3. Stat tracking year over year is half of what baseball's all about, and this game has it.4. Franchise mode adds depth so you aren't just swinging away with the same overpowered team year after year.  Star players decline or quit, and you have to manage your roster and make smart replacements if you want to continue to compete every year.I do have some very real criticisms though.1. The AI never, ever makes a baserunning mistake.  If they run to 2nd on a ball which your outfielder fielded cleanly and gunned to 2nd base with a 99 power throw, there is basically still a zero chance you'll get an outfield assist, ever.  They NEVER run to 2B unless they're practically guaranteed to make it.  It takes some of the fun and realism out.2. Negative random events happen WAY too often.  In the course of a season you can expect a random player to lose up to 20 points of a stat every 10 games or so.  It's ridiculous.  Example:  "Handley Dexterrez doesn't see the ball as well as he used to.  -12 Contact."  (Permanently!)3. Players you've invested money in training can still randomly decide to retire or quit on you at the end of the season, wasting your investment outright.  In real life when your employer pays for training and you quit within X number of years, there's usually language in that contract where you have to pay them back for the training which made you more valuable to the job market.  I would have liked to have seen something like that implemented here.  Training dollars are too precious to waste like that (or to have them more-than-offset by stat losses from random negative events, as described in #2.)4. Pitching in this game has become disproportionately difficult compared to hitting.  Sometimes it feels predetermined that batters were going to get a hit on pitches that usually would get fouled off or swung on and missed.  Sometimes you execute perfectly and they still crush it.  I get that that happens in real life too, but, it feels like all that effort is wasted because it is detached from the quality of outcomes - at which point, what's the point of pitching well?  In SMB2 you always felt like you could pitch out of a jam.  In SMB3 I often feel like the only way out is to put in a new pitcher, because "the numbers dictate" that this pitcher will simply give up hit after hit no matter how well you execute.5. Lag is a real thing and has genuine impact on outcomes.  It is always frustrating to have a pitch blink through the zone that you had no chance at, because you didn't get to see its path coming in; it warped.  I wish they had come up with an asynchronous way to rectify this, by having pitch data communicated to all players prior to delivery of the pitch, then have that occur locally on the batter's machine, so that lag could not be a factor.  Then communicate the hit data back to the server afterward.  Split second timing is needed to hit pitches, and lag just ruins it sometimes.Lastly, I don't PvP in this game, only co-op, so I can only comment on the co-op aspect.  Final Note:I'm disappointed that this publisher was bought out and will not be making any sequels or enhancements to this product line any more (so, sadly, none of my issues above will ever be addressed.)  This game is just good fun to play, has a low bar for entry, and an equalizing difficulty factor called "ego" which that makes it possible for a seasoned player to play competitively with a beginner.  If you are into baseball games and don't mind the cartoonish graphics, pick this up on sale and see what the fun is all about.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the greatest game I've played this year.  One of the best sports games of all time. _childDocuments_.review: Videogames that changed my life:1. Portal (the game that made me a gamer)2. Celeste (the game that inspired my bachelor's thesis and opened my eyes to some of my mental health problems)3. Super Mega Baseball 3But why? I hear you ask. Let me explain:The game is masterfully designed. Every aspect of the gameplay is well crafted, easy to learn, hard to master, intuitive and incredibly juicy. I can't tell how, but the game amazingly conveys the creators' enthusiasm and love for the sport. Is it because of the goofy humour? The attention to detail? In any case: this love is contagious.Where I come from, Baseball is not really a thing. But when some American friends streamed it, they got me interested. Now one of my goals in the future is to take a vacation in the US and watch Baseball in the stadium.Another thing to mention is the team and character editor. While the graphics can be slightly goofy, just like the game's humour, they offer a wide variety of options to be creative. The ability to customise every player down to the shoelaces and then spend entire campaigns with them really made me bond with my first and still favourite team. In fact, this team even inspired me to write down their personal stories in what might be a  novel one day. Of course just as juicy, goofy and heartfelt as this game and as overly dramatic as this review!Up to today, only a few games in my life were as eye-opening and inspiring as Super Mega Baseball 3.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played most of the great baseball games through the years, both in the moment and retrospectively. From MVP 04 and 05, the mid 2000s MLB 2k games, and the late 2000s/early 2010s MLB the Show games as well as the current ones. I've also played a lot of the fun arcadey baseball classics like Super Sluggers and Backyard Baseball. I can say confidently that Super Mega Baseball 3 is the most fun I've had playing a baseball game ever, and it may even be my favorite sports game ever. No other sports game has such a good ai that makes singleplayer an actual challenge without being cheesy (well too cheesy anyways). Singleplayer game feel super tough and rewarding with the ai adjusting to your every move, this is paired with the EGO difficulty system which allows for precise modifications to the difficulty. This game also has a super fun franchise mode that isn't perfect but definitely works. This is also the most fun I've had in a sports game playing with friends. Going through the ups and downs of a season playing co-op with a friend on discord is some of the most fun I ever had gaming. This works great for both Co-op and VS your friends. And it works well with friends of different skill levels with each player being able to set an individual EGO level for themselves. The fiction players and teams are so fun and unique and give each team a personality. Me and my friends know these players and teams like the back of our hands and we all have our own opinions and run ins with some of this games best characters. The online competitive multiplayer is also amazing.Super Mega Baseball 4 has its early release tomorrow so I want to send this game off with a review, by far one of the greatest sports games ever. And SMB 4 looks to improve on it with a way more in depth francise, with better stat tracking, team chemistry system, player loyalty, and more. Heres to plenty more years playing Super Mega Baseball Shout out to Hammer Longballo
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is superb. Hitting and pitching is not too difficult to master, which is what I like. Sometimes I don't want to drop 100 hours in something like MLB The Show to get pretty good. Also the customization is out of this park (pun intended) because it has team customization, which is already better than what you would get from a large developer like EA. However, there's some things that I would personally want to change if there was to ever be a 4th iteration. - Signing players to actual contracts, instead of unknown lengths (since the players can choose to resign from their teams at the end of every season). I would like to keep track of how long I extended people and when they might need extensions, not be ♥♥♥♥♥♥ out of a player just because they decided "oh i'm just gonna opt out teehee". - Franchise trades. If we can sign and release people, we really need trades in franchise mode. Keep it the same player for player (or pitcher for pitcher) like how it is for sign and release. It allows for more of an interesting regular season, just like how sign and release does. - Rework of power hitting mechanics. Now, the power hitting mechanics on controller are absolutely abysmal. For those who don't already know, you have to flick the right trigger while (i'd assume) you hit A (or X i believe for you Playstation folks) to hit the ball. Please just make it LB or RB. I have small hands, so reaching my thumb to get to the right trigger while trying to hit A is just a mess. Also the negative power (at least for hitting) should be removed, in my personal opinion. I see why it's there for fielding, but hitting is a completely different ballgame. Thank god you don't need power hitting to hit dingers. In closing, this game is really fun and I'm not trying to say you shouldn't buy it by any means. I've had a blast playing this game for the 30-31 hours I've played so far, and I'd recommend anybody new to the SMB series to try it. I just think there's things that could elevate a potential SMB4.

_childDocuments_.review: Ridiculously in-depth team creation game with a fun little baseball minigame attached! All kidding aside, Super Mega Baseball is truly one of the greatest sports video game series ever and a worthy successor to the "Backyard Baseball" CD-rom games from the '90s and early 2000s. I might still consider Out of the Park Baseball the best baseball series on PC, but as far as actual gameplay goes, this one takes the cake. The third entry is a fine place to start if you're new, it's got the most refined gameplay and expanded features. Start a franchise, simulate a season or playoff bracket, design or download all your favorite teams, create your own fictional league with up to 32 teams, it's all up to you! The gameplay mechanics are tight, the customization is as open-ended as it gets and the fun is turned up to the max! SMB3 has the distinct advantage of having the best team creator tool in the series as well, I've really enjoyed creating all kinds of real life and fictional teams in the editor. A lot of the custom assets are not as useful for creating accurate real-life logos, but learning to use shapes and text characters to fit the puzzle can produce some surprising results in just 32 layers. Check out my Steam Guide for this game if you want to see some examples of what I've made.I highly recommend Super Mega Baseball 3 to anybody who loves sports or is curious about baseball in any capacity, it nails that balance between arcade and simulation feel with polish rarely found in non-AAA sports games.

You can make your own teams and players. The franchise mode is great, trading players is a lot of fun. The ego (difficulty) system is genius. This has to be one of the best games ever made. And of course, there is no loot crate microtransaction BS that has become so common in modern sports games. It's just pure innocent fun.
