_childDocuments_.review: Improvements upon an already-superior series without any steps backward. Though none of the changes are monumental, in my opinion that's okay; not every subsequent game in a series has to be some massive overhaul--it is enough to steadily improve and expand the experience while still retain the core functions that makes the series great. And it is a great series.Improvements I liked:-- Franchise Mode introduces an interesting strategic layer and is well-executed.-- Pick-off moves to bases, wild pitches lead to passed balls, dropped 3rd strike rule; all make the game more realistic-- Player traits add more nuance and strategic choices-- Generally better graphics and user interfaceNow, the price. I do believe you are getting $45 worth of a game here, however, I'm not sure it is $45 worth of content beyond what the previous game provided. So if this will be your first entry into the series, I think this is a great buy--best baseball series on Steam by far. If you already own SMB2 and are considering upgrading, waiting till this goes on sale or drops in price is not a bad idea.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think there's a baseball game I haven't played, so over the years I still have my all-time favorites. SMB3 may not seem like a big change from SMB2, but the quality of life improvements are almost worth it by themselves. It compiles all the good, all the stadiums, and all the DLC from SMB1&2 into one polished product. At the moment on PC, you have this or R.B.I. Baseball which is a terrible MLB licensed product. OOTP is cool if you like being the GM of your team, but that's all it is. You just don't see developers making baseball games like they used to in the early 2000's. The reason why I stand by this game is because it is SO CLOSE to replicating the feelings those old games gave you. In an age dominated by MLB the Show, a PS exclusive atm, Metalhead is providing a VERY GOOD baseball game. The default teams are amazing, and the ballparks are beautiful. But what I love is the customization options. You can create just about any team, and customize your players exactly how you want them. The recent update only enhanced this by doubling the layer count from 16 to 32. My only gripe with the game is that it limits itself in its possibilities. This game would easily surpass MLB the Show, MVP Baseball, Mario Super Sluggers, Slugfest and others on my All-Time list if it offered more arcade game modes in addition to a solid Franchise and Online mode. They say they have no plans on adding a Home Run Derby mode, or even a batting practice mode like Backyard Baseball had. Sometimes I just want to tee off and hit some dingers, not create an exhibition match on low ego to do it. I also would love if they allowed the PC community to create new ballparks via mods/workshop to enhance the experience. Or allow a logo vault to easily transfer logos from team to team without spending additional hours to simply copy and remake them. All that being said this is still one of the best baseball games being produced atm, which is why I highly recommend this game. Support these devs! More support = more features!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Thumb down... And I didn't see it coming...I was a huge fan of SMB1 and obviously SMB2... But this one is a big let down.But first the good things: no more lag when it comes to batting compared to SMB2 so that's good.No more over the top defensive moves - I find it good too.BUT, the revamped pitching system (or rather the batting AI) is a disaster... I was really happy with the realism of pitching in SMB2 (although you had to push the ego quite high to make it realistic). But now... basically it feels like you are playing a robot AI which knows exactly whether the your pitch is going to be a strike or a ball. No more the feeling that you crafted your AB to fool the AI and make it swing and miss. It won't happen. If it's a ball by a micron outside the black the batter won't move. If it's a micron inside the strike zone it will swing (and not miss much even at relatively lower ego like 75-80). In SMB2 I felt like I was punished if I didn't locate/control my pitch well - so it was satisfying that it was all on me. Here, I can locate perfectly and it won't make a difference. And the power pitch mechanic, forget it. At ego 75+ it is just impossible to control... I felt like SMB2 had a much better balance. I didn't even try the career mode...I just asked for a refund after 3 hours of exhibition play...So that's it, hundreds of hours of SMB2 and 3 hours of SMB3...Really disapointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: CPU catch-up mechanics are extremely noticeable. If playing in a franchise mode, expect to have multiple things due to "luck" not go your way. Fielding isn't as crisp, hitters tend to foul off every two-strike pitch or get a hit, pitches that are blatantly balls are called strikes, the list goes on. You can drop ego down 10-15 levels and all this stuff still happens if you are leading your division by more then 4 games in franchise mode.In multiplayer, the only issues you have to worry about are the constant connection and frame rate issues. Ever since SMB4 released, it seems the quality of online play against other players has gone down. Issues with pitchers being in their wind-ups and then the pitch already crossing the plate while hitting, pitch location and power being uncontrollable while pitching, balls put into play locked into the pitching screen until play is over, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Super Mega Baseball 3 is a great game that captures the spirit - and the irony that goes around - of the sport. Metalhead Software has done a good job from different points of view, managing to mix the arcade and a pinch of simulation. This offers so much depth of gameplay that both baseball connoisseurs and rookies alike can enjoy it. In addition, the difficulty is scalable in each department. Intuitive controls. Too bad for some "black outs" in the defensive phases but you have to get used to the controls. Same goes for the actions dedicated to stealing the bases.Excellent longevity with many modes present: friendly, seasons, Franchising, editor and much more. Not to mention the online and local multiplayer games.Technically speaking, the title looks pretty good. It's not perfect but the look is nice, self-deprecating and there is also a lot of variety. The models of the athletes are graceful, very caricatured, but at times fluctuating. This is the risk of the caricature style. The sound side that goes beyond the music and also focuses on environmental and first-level stadium effects is very good.Pros.Intuitive gameplay suitable for enthusiasts and newbies.Scalable difficulty.Graphically pleasing.Great sound.Long-lived and never repetitive.Many ways to play.Cons.Some small graphs of highs and lows.Sometimes the actions to steal the bases and for the eliminations of the runners are confusing.8 of 10Recommended to everyone, beginners and baseball lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I am originally from Pakistan I played loads of baseball games during my childhood especially on the PS2, even I had a chance to play it for real. Fast forwarding to the future as an adult I felt something was missing it was indeed baseball I miss it so much sadly it isn't that popular where I am from but this is the closest thing I have to appreciate the sport. Its a fun engaging arcade game has solid controls tons of customization and a funky looking game.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Apart from the Show, this is the best Baseball game out there. The ego system scales the difficulty pretty well, that is how they have kept me playing the game for so long. The customization detail is also amazing, very rich and allows you to build your own narratives very easily. I personally have never had issues with games feeling non-competitive or "scripted," but I will say most of the issues I have experienced were playing online. However the developers are very receptive and active on Reddit. This game was well worth my money.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually like baseball in general until I found this game, it made a sport I usually overlooked really fun. The combination of cartoon style while still being realistic makes for an amazing time. I feel its a more accurate baseball sim than any other game. This is the most fun I've had on a sports game in a long time. The teams, names, stadiums, and just overall style of the game is amazing. It takes skill while also being really fun. I love making custom teams and making cool players. The true beauty of the game is how I'm almost never frustrated with anything. The controls and everything is simple and to the point. All the things like base running, hitting, and pitching are easy to master after a while but deeper strategies develop making the game really challenging but once again fun. There is a constant theme of the balance of realistic and fun. And not to mention the constant way of making the game harder or easier with the ego you can make it harder for a challenge or a little easier while you start off. 10/10 Would buy a million times. And has made me like a sport I never even touched before. And nothing matches that feeling of hitting a home run.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've ever played. It just nails the feeling and strategy of baseball without getting too bogged down in complexity. The feel is arcadey but with just enough stat elements to make it feel like baseball. PvP pitching mindgames are awesome. You might have to wait a couple minutes for a pennant race match but it's a good time. My tip... if you're playing against the computer and hitting 10 home runs a game, up your ego setting, the extra challenge completely opens up the depth of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: A very simplified and cartoonish baseball game, definitely worth a try but it can be better. For example I wish in the Franchise mode you could earn money for your team easier, the game does not reward you with any cash even if you win all your games and it becomes difficult to build an all stars team, also the players on your team, even though you upgrade them from a nothing C grade rank to a superstar S rank they have the same salary and when they retire you don't benefit any money off of them which is very odd
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: One of the absolute best sports games I've played in a long time, the Super Mega Baseball series has been refined from the ultra-cartoony and kinda uneven Backyard Sports-style gameplay of the first game in this series to a look that, while still heavily stylized, looks much more human.What's more, under the hood of this game is one of the most utterly well-put-together baseball simulations since MVP Baseball 2005 way back on the PS2. Everything about this game, from pitching to batting to fielding to baserunning, just feels right. Responsive controls, great difficulty scaling using the 0-99 "Ego" system, with gameplay from the casual (contact swings and standard pitches going for home runs and unhittable strikes on the lower levels) to the ultra-hardcore (using the swing aim stick and the "power" swing type if you hope to hit the ball out of the infield at extreme difficulty levels.)Easily my 2020 Game of the Year, and one of the best if not THE best baseball game on all of Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game?  This is a real tough one.  The leap from SMB to SMB2 was huge and a significant improvement in every aspect of the game.  However, SMB3 looks and feels exactly like SMB2, and I mean exactly.    I suppose this isn't a bad thing at all right?  I mean, why change a near perfect formula for the sake of it?  I think it's a shame the small additions to the gameplay don't really make much difference at all.  The hitter strengths and wild pitches add nothing to the overall experience and can pretty much be ignored all together.  I think pitching was better in SMB2 as the wild pitches in that game felt like I didn't do something correct, rather than simply not releasing the button in time as in SMB3.   It's basically been made a lot simpler and easier in SMB3.   The stealing additions are just nice, not a major game changer.  Just Nice.  Yes the running has improved but other areas (pitching) have not. The franchise mode is again is a nice addition but it doesn't feel much different to the regular season mode.  I know the player has more management options with trades and upgrades etc, and some people may want to faff about with all that jazz but that isn't where the beauty of this game lies, and thus should not be it's focus.The beauty of this game is in the playing of baseball.  On the field.  Where the finely tuned pitching, hitting and catching mechanics are there to shine.  £34.99?  I'll certainly make sure I get my hours out of it and I'll enjoy every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: In my humble opinion, this is THE best sports games on steam. Fun designs to locations and characters. The Mojo mechanic is genius. The addition of traits is game changing. The player/team management system in franchise mode is deep enough. The game can be as arcade-y or hardcore simulation as you want it to be. Truly hall of fame worthy.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good baseball game. The mechanics are tight, the balancing is pretty good. I don't recommend it because it's not as good as the original.My biggest gripe with this game is how awful the player development feature is. The first game had stellar team management - you had a bunch of gear, coaches, and equipment that would change the attributes of your players. Everything had a plus, almost everything had a minus, and it was about balancing that out. The last game in the series did not have player development features in franchise mode, which was disappointing. When I first bought this, I did so because of the promised player development features.I quickly discovered how terrible they are. You will never be able to afford them. I am now twelve games into the season and I am now, for the first time this season, able to afford one training session for one player with significant downside. It's not made clear how you accrue extra money - other than that you make it over the course of the games you play - but, for the record, this is on Ego 50. What an awful system.Buy the original. Skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I've actually played this mostly on the Nintendo Switch during travels, but got it on PC as well cause it is that good.A lot has been said about the game already; it's quite simply a very well made baseball game, riding a line between simulation and arcade with a little more of the former than it lets on. In my opinion the best facet is its "Ego" system which is basically 100-levels of difficulty. If you're having too much trouble, knock it down a notch or two, and if it's too easy then just bump it up. It's a very clever, VERY well done system. At around the 90+ Ego ratings you're basically looking at real baseball speeds particularly on the batting.My only fault with the game is that the Franchise mode isn't all that spectacular. You can sign new guys and even do a little bit of training, but it's pretty passive. If this series ever implemented a really hardcore Franchise mode it'd really put it up over the edge.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: It works pretty smoothly whether playing by self or with another person as a team-mate... good in-season and off season stuff. You can set up your own league and also set one up, at same time, with a friend in a separate league. You can set your skill level (ego) and adjust it upwards as you get better. It's just a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Super Mega Baseball 3 is highly enjoyable and everyone who enjoys Baseball should give it a try. Pitching, Batting, Fielding and Baserunning are very intuitive and can be scaled in difficulty so that there is no barrier of entry for new players, but can also be scaled up to offer a challenge even for experienced players. If you're thinking about getting the game, do it, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best PC alternative to MLB The Show and it's not close. I was able to import a current 2021 MLB roster and have been loving Franchise mode as my favorite team. The gameplay is much more nuanced than the cartoony style would let you believe, and there is lots of depth to the game since it shines in both its online and offline modes. Couldn't recommend more for anyone looking to find a PC baseball game. Still hope MLB The Show comes to PC though lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING BASEBALL GAME! Imagine backyard baseball, but with better game play and amazing customization! Once you get the cartoony graphic and punny names it plays like a baseball game for baseball people and with a difficulty rating scale of 0-99 and you can even change individual of 4 difficulty of skills (baserunning, batting, pitching, and field) it has a setting for everyone! Highly highly highly recommend even for non baseball people, but people who just love sports game in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Ken Giffrey Jr and Nintendo Wii made a baseball game in 2020.  This is my first baseball game since 2014 and it's a good one.Pros:  Excellent game play.  Fun character names.  Takes sometime getting use too, but they have done a great job making every aspect of the game play a challenge but well balanced.  For example, you do most of the fielding yourself, pitching is fantastic,hitting is a challenge but possible.  All aspects of controlling the players is what makes this fun.Cons:  No instant replays.  Make a sick catch and you'll never see it again.  Unless you're recording the game yourself.No play by play anouncers.  Other than that the game is awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game fills the void in me of the MLB not happening so far this year. Its expensive but it just feels like a fully finished and polished game with no bugs that I've seen. You can also give a batter brain damage if you pitch a fastball at their head, but they can give your pitcher brain damage if they hit a perfectly placed line drive. I'm looking forward to dumping hours into this game. Go tribe.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: First, I hate the artistic style of this game. The exaggerated super-deformed swole dwarf aesthetic has got to go! For a long time I didn't think to play this because of the cartoon characters. Tried it out anyway during a free weekend and it won me over. Everything else about SMB3 shines. There's features in this that you'll be scratching your head as to why they aren't in The Show. My favorite aspect is how completely customizable everything is... from difficulty to players, teams, and logos.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this that the game is just like SMB2 and if you like that you will like this. If the main selling point for you is Franchise mode, like it was for me, maybe wait for a sale ($45 is a bit much with minor changes outside of Franchise mode).So now that i got that out of the way i wanted to say my favorite thing in sports games is franchise mode. it is by far my most played mode in sports game. I don't even touch online with 2k or Madden. The reason why is i love, more like am addicted to blowing up a team, drafting young blood and developing them into super stars. I knew going in SMB3, that wouldn't be exactly the same but they offered progression and signing/releasing players so i thought it would be good enough and i could make it work since i love SMB. The sad thing the franchise mode is a real weak mode right now, that i am desperately hoping is improved on in SMB4. My main grip with it is progression. It is almost impossible to take a young player and develop them easily. The reason for this is because the development/training in the game is completely random. It is hard to explain but essentially you have a salary cap for each team. Whatever not spent on salary is given to you each week to be spent on training. Usually you will have to save up this money over the course of multiple games to buy a training opportunity for one of players for them to improve. Some are more expensive than others and some are dirt cheap. The more money the more likely a bigger boost for one of your players. The frustrating part is how this is generated. You can only have 6 training opportunities at once. They will only be removed if they expire after multiple games or if you buy it. There is no way to remove one from the list. So if 3 or 4 of them are a waste of money or just not good you will have to wait around for it to expire ( on a normal season length that usually takes 4-6 games to expire). The next frustrating part is who is most likely to have an opportunity. I have played one season and simmed another and both times from what i have seen it is very unlikely for younger players to be given opportunities. On average player on the list is 28+, even when a majority of my roster is under 25. Since you can't train a player you want to get developed you have to hope they have an opportunity that season. And if you don't then you will only see them develop when moving onto the next season, which is not a huge change. All in all it is just sad that the franchise mode they have added is a handicapped version of what it could have been. I know wanting trading and a draft right out of the gate with the first franchise mode is asking for a lot, but at least make developing players enjoyable/possible. I do like the game. I will probably play another season or two, but it is just going to be a bit of a pain being so close to what i want in SMB, but just not there yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: While MLB The Show is a better Sim, and RBI Baseball is a better arcade game, SMB3 is this beautiful little in-between title that combines almost all the features you find in sim baseball games with the ease-of-play and quickness you normally see in arcade style sports games. It's an amazing game that won me over on the Xbox last year when I bought the 2nd game on sale. Thing is, on the PC, you can download a real MLB team mod and make the real MLB. The kicker? The in-game intergender squads are actually just as fun to play and rolling up a franchise with them has been some of the best sports game related fun I've ever had. Bottom line? You like baseball, then you're going to love this game. GO MOOSE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Most fun I've had in a sports game since MVP Baseball 2005 (Manny Ramirez on the cover).  If you look at this game quickly, you might glance right over it due to the cartoony looks and no real licensing, but DO NOT be fooled. The game play and mechanics in the game are no  joke. Small, tight knit community also contributes to the fun in loads of online leagues and the Pennant Race 'ranked pvp' mode.  If you're looking for a great sports title that plays great, but doesn't take itself too seriously, you're in for a treat!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Super Mega Baseball 3 is one of the best baseball games available on PC. The controls feel great and there's plenty of room to learn and be challenged while changing your ego level. Be it an exhibition game, season or franchise there's something available for everyone with an interest in a baseball game.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: 1000% the best video baseball I have every played.  This game is a perfect blend of arcade and simulation.  I play with a buddy online and I am always 100% happy with the outcome of the game, win or lose.  Unlike some AAA products where there's pre-determined gameplay sliders that tilt the advantage, the sliders here are simply the EGO and the stats of the team you use.  So, rest assured, you can always have a fair game with your pals, and not have to worry about in-game logic causing you to win or lose, as opposed to winning or losing on your own merits.Nice thing about this game is feedback is strictly for nice to have stuff1) Give me 1.5 extra seconds after an out to throw the ball around2) INSTANT REPLAY PLEASE!!!!3) Walk-off hit celebrations, HR bat flips (only bat flip we've seen is on a walk)4) Knuckle ball!5) More robust statistics (eg. cumulative stats for clubs in online leagues, full box scores for current and historical seasons, etc)6) More variation in crowd noise (eg. crowd getting loud in big moments, more booing situations rather than just on pick off attempts, etc)7) STADIUM EDITOR!!!  something that allows you to choose pieces of a stadium and connect in a modular fashion, apply colours, banners, etc8) Skewing options for logo editor so you can change the horizontal/vertical factor when stretching/shrinking logos9) HEX COLOUR INPUT for specifying team colours!!!10) Allow variable sliding so sliding player can hook slide at grounders that are too close for a dive, but not close enough to run through.Those are just some of the nice to have things that would enhance an otherwise FANTASTIC game further.Also, Devs, please do SM Football/Hockey...the demand is out there!! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really, really good. I'm not a baseball fan in any capacity and yet I'm having a blast playing this game.The customization is great, making your own team is fun (and having the announcer call out "Number 69!" every time a player steps up to the plate is always a big bonus).It's a very lighthearted, arcadey baseball game with great mechanics at its heart. There's something about it that makes ripping absolute dingers satisfying, yet grounding out into a double play not so painful.To me, this is basically a perfect sports simulation game.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: My advice is to wait for this game to be patched a few times, right now online is plagued by people who abuse the fact that you can steal with just about anybody. Offline at least at the difficulty I like to play with is nothing but errors on routine baseball plays that make the game difficult to enjoy.The potential is there, but if you're on the fence my recommendation would be to wait a few months until they iron out some of the nonsense.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I Love this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Game!!!  Only if Sony would make The Show this exciting to play!  I hate realistic baseball games bc the truth behold true baseball is boring to watch...This game brings it back to the roots of arcade style baseball gaming!!Franchise Mode with Full Customization of the League down to the Teams and its players!  You can improve your players with your budget and I think this is amazing to keep you coming back for more!There is a High Score mode which is awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect mixture of arcade style baseball gameplay like The Bigs, but realistic enough to provide a real challenge if you bump your difficulty up. The depth of the Franchise mode provides total control of the team, and gives room for hundreds of hours of gameplay taking a team through multiple seasons. Not to mention the co-op franchise mode which my friend and I have found to be an awesome alternative to playing head to head.Highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a quality baseball game that is both excellent for simulation and player controlled games!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: To me, as a european, baseball was that strange, boring game that US-americans watch while munching nachos and burgers. Thanks to Super Mega Baseball 3, I've come to understand and even appreciate the "american game". If you're williing to learn all the strange rules and accept that this is more a sport of the mind rather than the body, SMB3 will give you and awesome experience. The game is a charming indie title and you can tell that a lot of love has gone into it. The comic graphics and animations are light-hearted and adorable. But don't get fooled by the looks. The game is easy to learn yet hard to master. The mechanics for pitching and batting are quite deep. What I like the most is that the mechanics hit the sweetspot when it comes to the balance between skill/input and the the stats (strengths and weaknesses) of the player currently under control. For example, if a good hitter is at-bat, your "aiming reticle" is bigger. Players have few stats, but every single one of them matter. You can customize players and teams (logos/uniforms). This is particularly nice as baseball-lineups consist of only 9 players, so you will see the same players very often and bind very quickly with them. ("Oh no, Bobby Twinkles, don't you drop that ball again!!!! FFS!!!!*)(/&(=)/(§(=)()==)§!!!!!")
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good addition to the series. Very good control scheme, some pretty good visuals, nice sound and some cool variety of fictional teams/players. The franchise mode is most welcome if you're looking for some added depth. And there are some great multiplayer features for die hard Baseball fans.Baseball aint really my sport, but when it's done right in a video game, it can be a lot of fun. The Super Mega Baseball series does a great job and this entry just builds on what came before. Bit expensive at $64.95AUD, but there aren't too many other options out there for the PC. Casual players, get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I dunno. I've got a bunch of hours in SMB2 and SMB3 is so similar in most ways that it just feels like the same game again. I've gotten very disillusioned with the Ego system. "If the game's too hard, just tick down the difficulty by a few points until it gets too easy". This isn't a fun way to play a video game. When I succeed, it doesn't feel like a victory. It just feels like I put the difficulty maybe a few points too low. Having to set your difficulty out of 100 is just silly, there's far too many options. I wish there were more tools to get better at the game too.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Loved SMB1, skipped SMB2, have 80+ hours in to SMB3. I want to like it but I can't. Despite the devs and all saying there is no rubberbanding the fact that nearly EVERY time I start running up the score or have a team doing awesome in franchise, without fail, my players will start making errors left and right, can't hit anymore, and the opponent batters suddenly can hit everything exactly where my players can't get to it or out of the park. I've literally sat down with pen and paper to make sure my pitches aren't following patters, I've swapped pitchers when batters start anticipating, it doesn't matter. There is rubberbanding whether it's intentional or not.Dig around, I'm not the only one to notice this, ignore the fanboys who will rake anyone over the coals who suggests there is and will just blame your pitching or "♥♥♥♥ happens". I agree, stuff happens in baseball and sports, but when it always happens under the same circumstances regardless of team, pitcher, etc...it's not chance.It's a fun game, don't get me wrong, but it will frustrate you if you try to play a franchise or season mode game. One offs are ok but if you start destroying the competition in longer game modes you'll get the same effect.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I will recommend this game, but I will also say I am very frustrated with it. It is probably the best baseball video game since MVP 05, however, there are a couple reasons I am starting to hate it.1.Runner speed/throwing speed is off ratio.  If the CPU runner has a equal or higher run speed rating than the catchers arm rating, they will run on you all day, and there are a lot of players this applies to. Also, if the CPU hits a single with runner on 2nd there is a 95% chance they will score. 2.Difficulty is not right. The ego(difficulty) tops out at 99. I started at 50, then went to 60, then 70, won a championship each season I played, blowing teams out even on ego 70. I now went to 80 and it is impossible. I even tried 99 and If anyone can play on 99 I would be very surprised. It is physically impossible to hit the ball well because the speed of the pitches, and due to CPU being able to hit everything, almost never swing at anything close to the strike zone and mashing anything that is a strike It becomes very frustrating. When you are hitting your spots, throwing good pitches and they still rake off you its very frustrating. Then you get to bat with he best hitting team in the game and all your players seem to have warning track power at best. After leading the league in hitting with 6 players in my lineup on ego 70 and winning the championship with ease, I start the season 1-8 on ego 80. It makes no sense but I hate when I get so good at something and just hit a wall where I just can't go higher, but the game goes to 99. But hey maybe I just suck. I only put 80 hours into the game but maybe I'm trash. I don't think so though.But I hope these developers continue making games, for such a cartoony game the mechanics are very crisp and well done, the game modes are well thought out, although the franchise mode could use a little more depth. Despite some of the annoying qualities of this game, If you need your baseball fix on PC without an emulator, Play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best alternative to The Show. Since I can not play any EA Sports baseball game, this is the game I turn too. It offers pretty much everything they offer and it is loads of fun. I just get lost in franchise and try to build the best team possible and create mega dynasties. I highly recommend this game if you are looking for a great baseball game.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Fun arcade style baseball game.Easy to pick up and play.  The controls can be learned quickly, but lots of depth, and ways to customize the difficulty.  Graphics are cartoony and convey each character well.  No real teams, but you could make real players if you want and the team logo editor is great (better and easier to use than the one in The Show).Season mode is now in the game and lets you trade players (though you have to trade on a one for one basis).  The best baseball game out there, hopefully things will continue since EA bought this developer and they are making a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most refreshingly fun sports games I've played in a long time. I'm a huge fan of games with great customization and sim options, and this game delivers. It's also just a blast to play in general. Haven't touched online, but it seems like it would be a great game online. I just enjoy the franchise/sim aspect more.Completely recommend to those who are over licensed games. And even if you're not, it's worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: 7 hrs with the demo....I tried to resist the urge to pay full price with the steam summer sale coming...I ultimately took the plunge due to changes from SM baseball 2 and the developer. The developer appears to be pretty active on their subreddit and even have a shout out to the sub on a loading screen. The developer responds to criticism-which is welcoming. In some youtube developer series videos, they talk about planned future updates and changes they made in response to SMB 2...I like that and am glad to support a developer like that. Overall-I played the ♥♥♥♥ out of MVP 04 and 05...I had a craving for baseball and took the plunge. I am digging the situation bufs/nerfs as well as the pitching mechanic. I really enjoyed the online multiplayer and am excited to try out franchise and season. Batting is what you would expect from a baseball game. I love how quick and intuitive the controls are-it is so easy to quickly adjust IF and OF for situation. I like the more arcade style and look forward to playing this game as I wait out the MLB covid delay.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the lack of any licensing or the cartoon-ish looks fool you. This game is easily my favourite baseball game, hands down.The mechanics for hitting and pitching are easy to pick up, but reward you for mastering them. The difficulty setting("Ego"), which allows you to pick any level between 1 and 99, makes it easy to create an experience that challenges you as much as you like. You can also set different difficulties independently, such as 75 for hitting and 65 for pitching, versus simply picking 70 overall, for example.The game isn't loaded to the brim with complex systems like MLB The Show can be. While I think The Show is a great baseball game in its own right, SMB3 does more with less in my opinion. Players only have six or seven stats total, versus the 20-something stats The Show gives players. While I love baseball and I love obsessing over baseball stats, it's a welcome thing that I can judge a player's ability and how they can fit my team with one quick glance.I've also found it plays at a faster pace than The Show. Pitcher windups are faster, and there's less downtime between pitches. While it can only be a second or two, that adds up over 9 innings. A full game can run you anywhere from 20 to 40 minutes, while I've never had a game in the Show come in under 35.The game's franchise mode forgoes things that, to me, felt like jarring exclusions at first. There are no trades, and no contracts to manage. You sign players for a set salary, and this salary stays constant until they either retire or become a free agent. These happen randomly, though perhaps with some influencing factors. There's no minor league systems to manage, no coaching staffs to check up on, and salary cap is a hard limit for every team in the league. There's no salary negotiations, with players instead just lowering their asking price for every "round" of the offseason.However, after playing, I found that these things didn't bother me. In my experience, it gives me the experience and fun of building a good team, and I spend more time playing baseball and less time looking at spreadsheets and stat lines. There's still the risk of pressing your luck on the big free agent, hoping their price goes down before another team snaps them up, and the thrill of finding a bargain, or getting lucky in player development and growing a superstar yourself.On top of it all, this game makes creating custom teams and leagues a breeze, and the logo editor works like the rest of the game - keeps it simple, but without making you feel like you're missing out.While I haven't played much online, what I have played was decent. Not many connection issues(though my internet isn't great), and games being 5 innings means you're never locked in for a long time.All in all, SMB3 is a fantastic baseball game, and well worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: My first baseball game after only a few hours in Super Mega Baseball 2, and despite not traditionally enjoying sports games, I'm absolutely hooked.- It's incredibly accessible, with intuitive gameplay and simple controls- The game is action-packed, with very little forced downtime- It scratches the tactical itch without forcing complexity, allowing constant monitoring of defensive alignment, individual player skill sets and perks and in-game situations to contribute to the player's decision-making process (or not, just swing at strikes!)- The real gem of the game is franchise mode, with clever "arcade-y" compromises around salary caps, free agents, age-related career growth and decline, and player development that are easy to understand but add a feeling of investment and control over the long term success of your team
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: They ruined base-running in 3.  With runners on base and a fly ball, not only do I have to select the runners now and send them back (right-trigger doesn't work anymore), they aren't smart enough on their own to realize that it's a pop fly and they shouldn't be running...even when it's very obviously going to be caught. I've had so many guys thrown out because they weren't tagging on obvious fly outs.As far as feel/mechanics go: Stealing is way better. Pitching/hitting are worse. The amount of infield popups and dinky grounders is just way too high on the same EGO as in SMB2.The base-running thing though. It's those kind of decisions that just absolutely make me want to sit down to interview the devs and ask them how they hit their head on the day they made that call.  It makes zero sense to me and coming from SMB2 and 1 before that, I'll probably lose interest in the series before I unlearn the habit of holding RT on fly balls.UPDATE: Returned to the game only to find that it is way worse than it once was. Not only is the base-running still garbage, but the game ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed if you have multiple monitors. I have a 4K main monitor and a small touchscreen secondary. It insists on using the touchscreen res even if I have the game full screen on my 4K monitor. Seems like they were more interested in selling copies of SMBB4 instead of actually making sure the game we already paid money for is working properly. Scammy trash devs. Won't touch 4 if my life depends on it.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Seems like they fixed most of it.I love super mega baseball in general, but I need to give this a currently negative review because of the combination of fielding errors (Well-timed dives for line drives and the ball bounces away, at least every time I've tried), the loss of realism in batting AI (the AI's decision to swing or hold up seems to be excessively weighted towards "if it will be a ball, I won't swing" rather than "if it looks like a strike, regardless of whether it's a ball, I might swing." That is to say, the batters seem to have a preternatural ability to identify whether the pitch will be a strike or a ball out of hand, rather than seeming to respond to a pitch that slips just barely out of the zone on a 2 strike count the way a player might, feeling as if they need to swing. If they hold up, that's baseball, that's fine, but they seem to just watch them go by too much)The price point.If this game was 10 dollars or 20, these issues wouldn't be so bothersome. As it stands, I really look forward to changing this to a positive review when fielders are able to play baseball (I've made harder fielding plays than those my shortstop has knocked into the outfield 4 times in one game, and her dive was far better timed than mine ever was), and pitchers are able to pitch without the batter knowing in advance what the result will be. I know they'll fix these issues, but I'd like it sooner rather than later. It's quite frustrating.ALSO, there's an annoying bug that causes all stats in Franchise mode to only refer to the games you've played this session (or something). Just pitched to a player who I struck out last time I played in Franchise, but now, somehow, she's batting 1.000. And the guy I hit a homerun with last franchise session? was hitting .000 until 2 games in when I got him on the board.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game for players of all skill levels...+ The difficulty system is brilliant. There are 100 levels, and the ability to tweak batting / pitching / baserunning / fielding difficulty individually. As a complete baseball beginner it was perfect for me.+ Games are dynamic due to the pressure system, player traits, fitness, and mojo. There's a huge difference between facing a tense or confident pitcher.+ It autosaves between pitches (seamlessly) so you can drop in / out whenever. Perfect to pick up and play in short bursts.+ The stadiums look amazing!+ Franchise mode is a welcome addition. It's the only mode I play :-)- Franchise mode's player development system is questionable. Also the lack of multi-year contracts makes it seem not worthwhile to invest in.- HR celebration / strikeout animations could be improved.

_childDocuments_.review: A great arcade baseball game. _childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: The same magic of the last entry is back, only bigger, better, bolder.It improves upon its predecessor with more teams, more comprehensive options and play modes, with the star of the show probably being the much anticipated Franchise Mode that allows one's team to grow over time, as well as roster shaping via contracts and such.That said, the much beloved Pennant Race mode is also back and the developers have been working hard towards making the mode healthy and strong, and thanks to crossplay support, you are bound to find players easily for both casual and serious gamesMany of the issues with SMB2 (like the lack of a pickoff mechanic) have been addressed on this one, and the game is receiving polish continuously with each patch.The level of customization remains strong as well and should please those among the playerbase with more of creative touch, and this extends to custom leagues with flexible formats.If one single criticism can be levied against this gem is that the price may be a bit too steep for someone trying to dip their feet on some high quality Baseball action before buying, but the devs have been very generous with the demo's capabilities to allow a newcomer a good overview of where the game stands.As a lover of the sport, I can't recommend it enough; this one stands tall among the best of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to sound like a do not recommend the game, but I really do.  This is more of a wish list.They do need to make some improvements of the baseball mechanics, especially when you set the difficulty to 50 and up.  The number of double plays you can hit into is a little over the top and they badly need a circle or some other identifier on fly balls.  They are difficult to judge and if you miss it the ball will roll way away.The speed of many players is turtle slow.  On most teams, only your catchers should be that slow.  This seems random  more than anything and should be improved.It really gets hard to hit at 50 ego, as it should.  You  have to have some quick reflexes.  It's hard to dial in what ego to set for me.  It's either I kill the opponent or I can't buy a hit.  It could be a little more balanced.The way the opponent batters anticipate pitches is just not accurate to baseball.  You can throw a slider in the dirt and if they anticipated slider they can still jack out out of the park.  I haven't seen the uncanny ability to anticipate since the Houston Astros.  They really need to cut that part of the AI back.  There are tons of players available which is really nice, but the roster could be expanded the same as MLB teams.  When playing custom franchise mode, there is not nearly enough salary cap.  I won my first franchise season and half my players ended up leaving and it was impossible to field anywhere near as good a team with the low salary cap.  And after the first season, the player development funds make me think I will maybe get one improvement in a 50 game season.  A minor league callup system could be great too.And finally, I would love to see some updates with more funny player animations.  Maybe even a few baseball slap fights and suspensions would be really cool.  It's a huge part of the appeal of a fun game if you love baseball.  It could be made into an absolutely great one if they were to keep developing it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first Super Mega Baseball so just bare with me. I will put a tl;dr at the bottom of my review.This game is a throwback to all of the arcade-style baseball games during the N64 era (feels like Major League Baseball Featuring Ken Griffey Jr almost exactly). With that said, it suffers from the same issues as those games. A lot of stuff is easily exploitable (at least from Ego 65 and lower).As stated, this is my first SMB. I started out at ego 25 as recommended and pumped it up by 10 ego by the end of my second game. The mechanics were easy for me to catch onto and the game really helps new players and those who are not as skilled as others. By the end of my first season, I was up to ego 45. Every season after that, I would bump it up by 5 or 10. I'm currently able to play at ego 65, and I destroy the CPU after getting used to the speed. They, on the other hand, also destroy my pitching. I found myself struggling with fielding and accuracy of pitching. Fielding will always be rough until you play the game enough to understand how each hit is "supposed to go". There is no marker, so you yourself must be fast to react in fielding. I feel that the accuracy of pitching is that hardest thing to get down. Heck. Pitching in general is hard. Power pitching feels almost impossible for me to get down, so I just pitch for accuracy. I feel that your character that you play as (despite their fitness and whether they are locked in or not) will randomly be more or less accurate from game to game. Whether this is me losing control of the game, lag in my pc, or actual programming, it was nice and kept me on my toes. I tried going slightly above ego 65 with pitching. Suddenly, the computer started hitting everything. I know that there are game where the cpu is more aggressive than others, but they were hitting literally everything. I was pitching things that were way out of the strikezone, and they would get hits. Maybe there is something that I wasn't exploiting while pitching. Point is, pitching and fielding are rough for newer people. Hitting has been easy to pick up, along with bunting.Base running sucks. It flat out sucks as far as controls with a controller. I'm still struggling with making one after another go home without making everyone move on. I think it would have been easier to just touch the d-pad (like with stealing) to make individual players go to or back to the next base. Franchise is tons of fun, but I wish there was an option to just play 3-3-5 instead of 5-5-5 for playoffs. Playing 5 game against the same team is boring, but I understand it's the "standard" way. Online is great, and it's cool that you have different difficulties per player. The one thing that would be nice to add is a stat limit for custom teams. What I mean is allowing a custom team league but not allowing players with all 99 characters into the league by making sure that the stats points per team are 25 or less or something.Customization is almost perfect. I would like an addition of opacity for things so I could make things see through and blend. tl;dr It's a great arcade basbeball game. It's tons of fun but rough at times. Take your time with ego progression. I REALLY like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Mario Super Sluggers was probably my most played game growing up, and I played a lot of weird arcade baseball games on the Wii like THE BIGS 2 and MLB Power Pros 2008 (shoutout to those games if anyone remembers them). Now the options are MLB the Show or whatever you can find on the marketplace. The Show is too slow and realistic for me, so this game was it.This game is so good. If you like arcade baseball, it does that perfectly - it especially rewards patient hitting and good fielding. Higher difficulty pitching can be brutal but it doesn't ruin the game or anything. The 1 to 99 difficulty scale fixes a problem a lot of those old arcade baseball games had - either the highest difficulty is too easy or the second highest is too easy and the highest is impossible. The scale really helps you find the right difficulty.My friends don't even like baseball. We use this game to make custom teams full of stupid player names and watch them play in leagues against each other and see whose absurd goofball team goes all the way. I currently use the Project Randall MLB Team Pack to play as MLB teams for my current season. The price is a bit steep for a game like this but if you love arcade baseball it is worth it. If it's too much, the very similar Super Mega Baseball 2 is much cheaper and is still very good. Or you can wait for a sale. This is an easy game to recommend for arcade sports game fans.

_childDocuments_.review: A tongue in cheek baseball game similar in tone to the lego games but not as many jokes. I guess the same jokes over and over would get repetitive so the humor is in the players names and some of the animations. Game play wise this was initially engaging and the franchise mode had enough detail to keep me invested for about 1 1/2 seasons before things started to get repetitive. Its about a 20-30 hour game tops before you start to get fatigued. You will get more fun out of it if you have a friend to play of course. Gameplay was simple but i feel like the pitching and batting were kind of similar mini games. I thought there could  of been more depth with player traits and although there was an abiltiy to read a player's traits as a pitcher it would be nice if the batter would be able to pick up traits on the pitcher once in a while as well.  I feel like acquiring more traits good or bad,  for each player would add a little more personality over time and maybe mix up the gameplay a little more. All around an excellent arcade game with a decent franchise just wish the franchise had a bit more meat to its management simulation options and wish the gameplay had maybe 1 or 2 extra layers of depth to keep me going for a couple more innings. Would like to see some graphical improvements in the future, the grass detail in particular looks horrendous. I do feel $45 a bit high for the amount of content I would wait for a sale at $35 it would be a good deal. Overall 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: So far I am genuinely pleased with the improvements made from the already stellar Super Mega Baseball 2. For fans familiar with the series here are some aspects that I think were improved upon:1. Graphics; has been greatly enhanced with detailed textures in jersey material and the fields dirt and grass, the whole look of the game looks crisp and refined.2. Gameplay; in my opinion has been improved from what was near perfect in SMB2. As a baseball fan the game seems more technical in a sense where real baseball strategy seems to make a bigger difference than previous game, although it remains very familiar. Aspects like working the count, predicting pitch type, small ball, pitch selection, and defensive decisions feel more impactful and balanced to real baseball. Things like stealing are not quite as abbusive now with pickoffs and past balls make pitch selection more thoughtful. As far as hitting and pitching mechanics, they're mostly the same but I do think they are refined a bit to feel more sim like, Power pitching and Hitting aren't really there to use everytime now and I think its for the better. Lastly the trait system really refreshes things and brings variety and strategy.3. Game Modes; mostly the same as SMB2 with the addition of Franchise Mode which I personally love. With things like salary cap, free agents, player development and retiring/rookie players it really brings a lot of life to long term gameplay. I'm excited to see how my young players develop and how teams may change styles over the years, a non power hitting sirloins would be quite the site. Also it will be sad to have to let players go to save cap room and see team legends retire, but that's all part of the magic of franchise mode.4. Sounds; simply put the whole game sounds better. The intro music, the walkup songs, the crowd, umpire, bat sounds from hitting to breaking just sound fantastic.From a lifelong baseball and baseball video game fan this is truly a special series. Super Mega Baseball has encapsulated everything I love about baseball and video games into a magical experience, and Super Mega Baseball 3 is the pinnacle of the series for me and possibly all baseball games. I'm looking forward to playing another 100 hours+ and many seasons of franchise with the Sand Cats!

_childDocuments_.review: (Edit) - After playing for a fair amount of hours I can say the experience has improved enough to change my review from a negative from a positive. There were some terrible slowdown issues that the Dev's finally fixed in a recent patch and that was one of my final major criticism's. There's still some authenticity problems at high EGO (the AI still does not react quite realistically to pitch to) but It's not as bad as before, or maybe I have simply learned how to exploit the AI better. -New graphics, new game modes and new appeal; yet the same unpolished, broken, lazily designed AI and EGO system. I've dumped hundreds of hours into SMB2 playing the 90's in EGO finding myself constantly bitterly quitting the game from the same obnoxiously obvious unfair advantages the AI receives. As a sports game, SMB3 has a responsibility to see itself competitive to it's players. Unfortunately just like SMB2 that means the better you are at the game the less fun you will have.          I bought SMB3 the instant I knew it was released with the desperate hope that metalhead would've put any effort into balancing their game to justify a brand new release worth $40. But all the problems are still there. I jumped into SBM3 as soon as it was installed and played 3 EGO 80 games, 80 is 10-15 less EGO than I've played for months on SBM2. And all 3 matches shared the same trend that was so infuriating that was a problem back in SBM2, the AI simply doesn't play competitively fairly.         To make the AI compete with high skill players Metalhead has decided to simply allow it to cheat. The AI will spit on all of your breaking pitches, regardless how well you set them up with previous fastballs. The AI will spit on 100mph fastballs an inch off the plate, repeatedly. The AI will crush the very first fastball you throw in the strike zone after spitting on 2 99 rated offspeed pitches. Constantly over all 3 matches I threw perfect hard pitches with 99 ratings exactly where I was aiming them, and almost every time it was either crushed for a homerun or spat on. That is not fair or fun sports gameplay. The games should not be decided on whether or not the AI simply decides to crush a ball whenever it pleases.          Hitting is easy and fair enough, but as always, pitching is hell. The AI is simply designed poorly at higher EGO to react realistically and fairly to being pitched to. It's not fun. Pitching is arguably the most important aspect of baseball yet it's so poorly represented in SMB3. As someone who has played hundreds of hours of Super Mega Baseball, I absolutely cannot recommend any of the games in the series to anyone who thinks they will be good at it. It is simply unrewarding and unfulfilling to play at EGO ratings above 80. Until metalhead decides to get around to actually coding their AI at higher EGO my review will stay negative. However I doubt they will ever fix it as it had remained a known issue for years in SBM2 and is still prominent now in SBM3.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't believe I have ever reviewed a game on Steam before and I've had it for tens of years. I have hundreds of games in my library and have played all kinds of games. I love sports games and was so excited for Mega Baseball 3. What a freaking disappointment! This game has sooooo much potential. Graphics - 10, Animations - 10, voices - 10. Frankly, many 10's! But ONE incredibly HUGE 1 ! The AI is so screwed up at ego 55  and probably above, though frankly, haven't tried higher.Here's the MAJOR source of UNfun! The AI is terribly inconsistent in what works for the AI and what works for the Real life player. The AI will get hits and home runs off any pitch, almost anywhere, if it swings and makes contact. If you swing and make contact when the ball is on the black of the plate, it's almost a guaranteed out. However, if you pitch on the black, the AI will knock it for a hit or worse, a dinger, and hate to say...it happens A LOT! Pitch after pitch after pitch. Now, I don't mind one bit that you have to pick your pitches well, and swing at strikes, but if those strikes are in the high black area, guess what? it's either a popup or called strike...about 90% of the time. Why not make pitching consistent between AI and human? So in a nutshell, make the AI work the same way the human counterpart works. It's that simple developers. Get your head outta your bum and fix this. Can't recommend because this is a FATAL flaw. Consistency, that's all we ask. What's good for the goose, etc, etc. Now, how do I know this? Simple, take some masking tape, make very thin strips. Outline both yours and the AI's strike zone. Now, watch where the pitches are for both teams and watch the inconsistency. It's horrible. If you designed it to work differently for balance, then EXPLAIN that to the players. Don't frustrate us with your inconsistencies without an explanation as to why. You want to make it harder at higher levels? Fine, change the way you make it harder, don't penalize the player for playing proper baseball. Black on the plate, and out of the zone pitches should be hard to hit, even for the AI. Unfortunately, that is NOT the case. Sorry, Metalhead, with ALL the good, you've really f'd up the playability. Win us back. Do the right thing. Fix this and make it a 10 overall, instead of a 10 for presentation and a 3 for playability. Oh yeah, while you're at it, fix the outfielding, popups, and other fielding issues too. Find a way for a player to know where the heck the ball is going and the zone of fielding control instead of making it pure guesswork and luck to catch something you have no idea where it is going. How come professional BB players make so many errors (DEF a 4 btw). And lastly, fix the freaking line drive double plays because runners are too stupid to react to them. And it's not because players are too slow to react to the line drive, it's becasue the runners go WAY to far off the base. Nothing like real baseball players. If you want an arcade game and don't mind the fact that they make it seem like it's going to play very similar to the real thing, but doesn't, then by all means, buy it. If you're looking for an artsy game that plays fun as an arcade game, buy it. But if you want an accurate statistics based game, go elsewhere. This one is not for you. Your choice, but be warned of this problem. If you want something more realistic, don't buy Super Mega Baseball 3. Again, arcade or realism. The choice is yours! And this game will only provide one of those, unfortunately, it's the arcade one.

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance, it's a goofy cartoon... but as you play things can get deceptively difficultIf you are on the fence about buying this game, I'll give you one piece of advice. Give it at least 2 hours to dial in the difficulty (called EGO in the game). At default settings, the game is ridiculously easy... but the EGO meter is no joke. Crank it up to the 70 or 80 range and the CPU becomes ridiculously efficient. I don't have the world's greatest stick skills, but for me at least, the difference between being competitive against the CPU and getting consistently blown out is only a matter of 10 or so EGO points. Overall, the game's mechanics work very well... the classic sweet spot of "easy to pickup and play, hard to master". So I won't go over that too much, it's all stuff that's easy enough to see in a video review. Even in my positive reviews, I like to focus on the negative... as even in good games, I'd rather know about areas where the game is lacking... as small frustrations can ruin a title for some people. That said,  I do think there are some warts... even at midrange EGO settings, there needs to be more swings and misses for both CPU and HUM players. The amount of foul balls in the game border on ridiculous. When I initially started playing at EGO settings in the 40-50 range, it got to the point to where I could intentionally and repeatedly foul off pitches I didn't like... while at just about any EGO over 50, the CPU will basically never swing and miss at a pitch in the strike zone unless you have pixel perfect accuracy within the mechanic... and even then they rarely whiff. They are either putting in play or fouling it off. CPU baserunning is also a bit overpowered. Again, this is at midrange EGO settings between 50-60, if the CPU is advancing to the next base, either after contact or an attempted steal... they are essentially safe. They just won't make mistakes, if they are going it's almost impossible to get them. I've thrown out a few steal attempts but it requires absolute 100% perfection on the throw meter with an above average defensive catcher.  I'd like to see some slightly more "humanized" behavior... where occasionally they try to go 1st-to-3rd when they shouldn't... or more bad jumps from steal attempts.  The pitching mechanic works well enough and there are a ton of different pitching styles among the players. The problems only really creep in as the EGO level raises... it gets to the point where ridiculous things happen. I got the "anticipated 1st pitch FB" pop-up against a batter when during that game I might have thrown three 1st pitch fastballs across the first 25 batters I faced... and said earlier, when the CPU quickly becomes god-like with zone recognition and contact ability... adding on mind-reading anticipation mechanics just seems cruel. When it's all said and done, I will very likely have independently set EGO for all four categories (hitting, running, pitching and fielding). I think pitching difficulty ramps much more aggressively then hitting does, so it's nice that you can tweak them separately. The franchise leaves a lot to be desired in my opinion. I think the player development system is gimmicky and a bit too over the top... but it's a new approach for a sports game, so you might like it. Roster management is also a bit disappointing... You can't decide to carry an extra bullpen arm and drop a utility player... you have to swap a pitcher for a pitcher or a position player for a position player. (At least not anything I can find to do it differently). There are no trades between teams. Like I said, I like to concentrate on the warts... even with a game I am wholeheartedly recommending. Give it time to dial in the difficulty and this is a great game of baseball. In the grand scheme of things, I don't think it compares all that well to most of the recent releases of The Show, which manages a very realistic "human" feel to their CPU AI programming and just feels less predictable from game to game... but SMB3 is still a great game of baseball and the best option currently available on the PC.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. I really do. It seems quite a few people have fun with it, and the game itself looks great in its own ways.While all the SMB games are the top tier in baseball gaming, SMB 3 is the weakest of the lot. I aim to point out the flaws (and some improvements) in no particular order. It seems for every step forward, they took a couple back.First off, it is inherently obvious that they fired the design team. The design team is tasked with designing the game; such as gameplay mechanics and menu layout. Their primary purpose is to decide every facet of what the game should be. Game programmers are like brainless dogs, they're incapable of self-thought and proper decision making. The design team are the dog trainers. Well, it's clear the design team either quit or got replaced, because we're gonna look at a plethora of idiotic decisions only a game programmer could've made. I even wonder if they sent the game through QA.But let's start with a good decision! There is no DLC, and the previous game's DLC is included for free! This is unheard of in the present day. I'm tempted to recommend the game on this alone. Such a bold business decision should set the standard for others to follow. Hopefully SMB 4 follows such a standard (It won't).But now into the bad. The menu design... I'm incapable of making an assessment of it without cussing. It is generally terrible, maybe the worst menu I've ever seen in a sports game of this caliber. It's ripped straight out of baseball mogul (and I'm doing baseball mogul dirty by saying that). I have no idea how they could take the excellent and flavorful menu design of the previous game and somehow turn it into this ♥♥♥♥♥. It leaves a terrible taste in my mouth. I genuinely question quitting the game as soon as I open it. While SMB 1 & 2 menu's felt very down to earth and baseball-ey, this does not. This menu feels like corporate drovel, like something I'd see when checking into an airport. You may say "It's just the menu" but apart from gameplay, it is what the player interacts with most. It's as if Metalhead's ego was hyper-inflated from the last game's success, so they thought they could do whatever they want, as long as we buy it. This really sets the tone for the rest of the game. As a longtime fan, I feel extremely violated that Metalhead is now treating its customers like statistics and not people. We want the game to feel like baseball, damn it!!! Don't give me this McDonald's esque menu! It is NOT trendy, not even when the game came out!As a side note, in general all the aspects of the menu (especially players and their portraits) are much blurrier than the previous game. I am running the game at max settings. It is possibly a graphical error, but it seems unlikely.It only gets worse. The actual character and ballpark design is more gritty, a tad more realistic. This feels like eating peanut butter mixed with cat hair. The game is supposed to feel aracdey, like a game. If I wanted realism I'd just play MVP 05. While they shifted this game design in certain areas (mainly ballpark size!), they did not do so in others (player attributes). The worst offender is the lighting. It feels more cold and gritty; think of GTA IV compared to GTA V. An arcade game should have colors that pop off the screen, not dull. The shadows and lighting affects are too realistic. It all implies that the designer was a confused moron, unable to decide how the game wanted to go. I wouldn't mind a realistic SMB, but it would lose most of its charm. While the increased ballpark size makes robbing home runs and diving catches feel spectacular, it comes with its own set of flaws (more on that later). I'm about as torn on this subject as the game itself is. It's just too confusing! Pick a genre, Metalhead (oops I meant EA)!We descend even further into the worst aspects of the game; the gameplay and controls. The controls have been screwed over completely. I'd like to meet a Metalhead designer and ask them personally how they thought these changes were in any form good. I'm almost lead to believe that the design team (who is probably a single literal chimpanzee) has no logical ability. Baserunning, for some reason, has been extremely over complicated. From a simple button and trigger system, to a complex and easily broken stick control system. The problem with stick control is it's heavily prone to mistakes and not nearly as responsive as pressing a button. Removing the trigger control of "All go" or "All return" was a grievous injustice to the best baserunning control scheme in modern baseball gaming. I am clueless as to why they could take the simplest part of the game and absolutely mangle it. Baserunning as a whole is entirely broken. While the field size was increased, they did not increase the player's speed aspect in the physics engine. Which isn't a huge issue because they didn't increase throwing power either. But it is clearly noticeable at times, resulting in you feeling absolutely robbed by the game. You also have to manually jump to steal bases. It's not very difficult, but it's a step in the wrong direction for an arcade game. I don't want this game to feel like The Show or MVP 05!!! I would just play those games instead! The flaws don't stop there. The pitching in the game has become ridiculously easy. I'm not sure if they made the AI dumber, or if they're trying to cater to children. The control scheme was changed from RT to X as the power pitch button, which feels very uncomfortable when aiming a pitch. Again, a sign of no QA. Sure, they added pickoffs. But it's offset by the terrible controls. Sure, they added Franchise. But it's barely complete and the new "player traits" system taints it. But the worst of the entire game is the hitting. When playing an ego above 75, hitting power is  nerfed. In multiple instances, I was playing as a player who had above 70 power, charged up a 99+ power swing, timed for a slight pull, and hit a right-up-the-middle meatball, in the sweet spot just a hair below the dot...  That is absolutely inexcusable! In the previous two games, that would've been a home run at ANY ego. Then I proceeded to smack a pitch outside and high for a homer with a player who had 30~ power with barely a charge. It almost seems like the hit you are given is simply RNG (with an ego modifier) and not physics based anymore. It was very Madden-esque, which makes sense considering EA snatched this one up. Such jackass design gives companies like EA a boner, so it was only a matter of time. This leaves me deeply disappointed in Metalhead, a company I've followed from nearly the beginning. They created a great game in SMB: EI. They further improved and changed baseball gaming with SMB 2. But this one brings shame to the name. I wouldn't even call it Mega Baseball, let alone Baseball. I think this properly concludes my review. Thankfully, fielding was not touched much. But it doesn't matter when the hitting is just the same as rolling the dice. You should not support this hollow shell of a company. Go buy SMB 2, it is a proper game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent in terms of playing pickup, single games that don't go longer than a half hour and in which you invest no time. Just jump in and play a game and move on to something else when it's over. DO NOT PLAY FRANCHISE MODE! It will frustrate you, I promise. After taking one franchise for 3 seasons, I got tired of dominating, upped the ego settings by a few notches in the hopes the win/loss would be more realistic. Instead what I got from 3 separate attempts (that is, 3 different franchise starts and 3 different deletes) was an opponent AI that will "cheat" in order to appear as a more difficult opponent. In all 3 attempts, the best players on my team were ignored by the AI and did terribly. My ace pitcher lost 3 straight starts (while my lesser pitchers did fairly well) and my best hitter struck out or popped up. Every. Time. Essentially, the AI is not very deep and that's a serious disappointment. The game is programmed to shut you down once your difficulty (ego) settings rise and is boringly easy on lower settings. There is no balance. Don't get this game if you're looking for multi-season in-depth play. It is astonishingly unrewarding. I wish they'd release The Show on PC.•••Update: I have just finished a game against a division rival in which their record was about .500, against a pitcher with a high ERA that used to pitch for my team but I released because he did nothing but give up homers. I lost 5-1, and the entire game, my heavy hitters only ever managed to connect for weak grounders or bloop flies that were easily caught by the opposing players. Meanwhile, my fielders committed 2 unforced errors and one refused to dive for an easily stoppable grounder. No reason given, I just pushed the 'dive' control and the player just stood there. It didn't occur to me until now, but this game - at least in franchise mode - is using a similar algorithm EA Sports used for their baseball games 20 years ago. It's outdated code that handicaps you rather than uses a more intelligent AI. Like I said, this game is good enough for single matches where the pun-names for players can make you chuckle...just as long as you're not here to play an actual serious ballgame. Unfortunately the novelty doesn't take long to wear off. I wanted to love this game, which is why I wrote a novel-length review about it. But after the honeymoon period, the game becomes a slog and loses its appeal.

_childDocuments_.review: "Just get over the cartoony graphics and you'll see this is THE BEST Baseball simulator out there." Says people who have never played baseball. Let me tell you what you're going to get when you pick this up: Be prepared to NEVER strike out an opponent above EGO 50+. You'll get ahead 2-0 in the count and throw a perfect outside slider, it will get lined up the middle.You'll get up 5-0 in the top of the 9th only to lose by 1 run in the bottom of the inning. It's like playing with Mario Kart catch up. There is no excitement in going ahead, you know for a fact the CPU is going to go on a tear the next inning and rip up everything you just scratched away at. You will have to single your way around for every. single. hit. No, you can't leg out a double against the CPU unless they bobble something off their foot (which no, won't happen.) No, you definitely will never see a triple. You'll connect with SOOOO many beautiful balls only to have their ungodly outfield run down EVERYTHING.......or their infield turn into 4  nomar garciaparra's and eat up everything. Honestly, you never see a fly ball hit the ground in this game....the CPU catches it ALL! I don't find it "realistic". I find it "frustrating". You know what you're getting into before firing up the game. Sure, this routine will feel fun the first couple games. After your 7th consecutive 1 run loss after a furious 4 run rally, forget this.PLAYED AN ADDITIONAL 10hrs. I regret everyone of them. It's truly maddening. There is an invisible "Screw you" right around EGO 45. The online play is impossible. You're either playing with lvl 50+ pro's, or you'r playing with lvl 50+ pro's who sandbag to beat the crap out of rookies.

_childDocuments_.review: i would recommend if you like baseball, and maybe if you dont, too, but after a good chunk of hours played i have grown tired of itthe sim side is fun to mess with but not enough to pull in anyone thats not a baseball fan into simulating a full season, in my opinion.
