_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Below my first review is my updated review on the game. Please read both as they both give context. My first review left a negative impression(50 hours in), but after another 50 my second review is more positive. They both contain good points.I can't explain why this one just feels worse than Super Mega Baseball 2 but it just does. This one adds so many good features that going back to play SMB2 is very hard because of the quality of life changes brought to 3, but at the same time the gameplay feels so much worse than SMB2. Its left me torn, and frankly I don't want to play either game now. I'm sure if this is your first experience in the Super Mega Baseball franchise then you will probably enjoy this game. But if you're wondering if you should upgrade from 2 to 3, then don't. Save your money, and just play 2. You'll ruin the experience of both games and it will leave you feeling empty. This was my favorite casual game to play and now I just can't because of how this game feels. The graphics, framerate, features are all better. But actually playing the game feels sluggish and worse. Pitching is significantly worse, just feels like I can't find an ego that's balanced. Either its up too high and I can't possibly pitch to the other team without them wrecking me, or it's too low and I just stomp the other team. The base running is INFINITELY worse, I can't imagine how they could think this is a better system than in 2. I'm constantly getting picked off on line drives to players where I have no control over getting my player back to the base, it always results in a double play, and even after they apparently "fixed" it, it's still a problem. They didn't add a trade feature but they have free agents which makes no sense. Seems to me with a cap, a trade system is a no brainer. I imported all my teams from SMB2 on launch and it messed up all my numbers for players and such. They have since fixed it for newly imported teams but that doesn't help me, with my 30 teams to edit EVERY SINGLE NUMBER or re-import them and change EVERY SINGLE NAME of my team because it imports them as "team name - SMB2" instead of just the team name. I write the review out of frustration because after being so hyped for a 3rd installment of my favorite game series, its not ruined it to the point that I don't even play either games. Its sad really. If I could, I'd wipe this game from my memory bank and just blissfully play SMB2 not knowing better features exist, but with infinitely worse gameplay.EDIT(continued): After playing another 50 hours in the game, I can confirm a lot of the problems I had with the game have either been fixed or were placebo.The things fixed: Players getting doubled up too easily. The first baseman not catching balls he should. The teams being imported more correctly, with the numbers accounted for. The base running takes some getting used to if you're used to SMB2 base running. I still find myself messing it up occasionally, but overall now that I've gotten used to it and I think figured out a control method I didn't know existed before(Speculation, I can't remember the specific issue I had).Overall I'm getting used to it more and more. I still would really like a trade option for franchise, and outside of franchise I would like a "copy" or "move" player to another team. It's a big pain to move players from team to team as it is right now, takes about 5-10 minutes per player. It feels like hitting homeruns with balls low in the zone is impossible. Even if I get good contact on it, seems like it always ends up as a line drive or base hit, even if a powerful hitter. Makes the low ball perk pretty worthless IMO, unless it's on someone who only hits for average. Just seems impossible to get under the ball when its low in the zone. Overall I still probably can't recommend this to someone who enjoys SMB2 as it is right now. They only massive upgrade I can see from 2-3 is Framerate and the Franchise mode. The small upgrades include the addition of a DH spot, the perks are interesting, and the 4 new parks are a nice addition. If you are new to the series and are looking for a Baseball sim for the computer, this is EASILY your best bet. There isn't even another option until MLB2K makes its way to pc. And even then, the more arcade-y feel might be what you're looking for. It's a blast to play casually.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not terrible and can be fun, but certain aspects really, really aggravate.  Start with the pitchers, horrible.  I have caught little league, senior league, high school, college, and A-league fastpitch softball for a dozen years after that, and not even at the little league level are pitchers so totally lacking control.  Third-string high school pitchers can spot their pitches, but the pitchers in this game basically randomly toss it up there.Throwing bats is bush, and bats don't break as often as they break in this game, nor as wildly.Infield play is pretty good.Outfielders, particularly yours, look like they are running in jello, and their range and reaction time are just as terrible.  Fly balls in foul territory are thus rarely caught.Kind of a mixed bag this game.  Has its moments.

How it works is there is a circle that the baseball needs to follow, but the computer throws your mouse in random direction at a random speed and you have a limited time to get it back in the area. As such, at the higher difficulties, this feels like a game of pure chance rather than skill. If you want a casual game, then this is fine, though I think there are better baseball games out there. If you want to laugh at how bad you can guess what the computer will do, then give this game a try. But for me, it wasn't worth the hassle

_childDocuments_.review: In Terms of PvAi this game is worse than smb2. Just in ten hours it feels way more imbalanced. How can your sequel have a worse mojo system than it's predecessor. I can have a guy hitting 500 with home runs and rbi but he's tense the whole season because of two errors(total, not in one game) . Then my top hitter goes 0-4 and is still on fire? Like what? Pitching got harder which i like but the strike zone on the edges is complete bs. If you dont perfectly throw the ball 7/10 it will find its way "off" the edge which will be a ball that the cpu will ♥♥♥♥♥ eagle eye everytime even in an 0-2 count. 70 ego was way too easy but 80 becomes too annoying to play because of how consistently stupidly incosistent things keep happening. They added in a lot more errors. Picking the unit you want to control on defense got even worse. And you still cant keybind a controller. _childDocuments_.review: My main complaint is the fact that this has been specifically developed for Playstation controllers. It's extremely irritating.Additionally, I found the batting mechanics to be needlessly difficult to understand, and the AI felt artificially perfect. Never misses a catch or a throw, no matter how high or far, and throws the ball between fielders with the speed of a missile, while batters run at the speed of a pregnant cow.Maybe the problem is I'm not from the US and baseball isn't even a sport where I'm from, so I don't have a dog in this fight, but either way, I seriously disliked this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game from this top notch series.Just read the review I did for one of the previous games in the series, and then just look at this one, see what new extra mechanics they added this time, and if they sound like they are the kind of thing you would like, and you agree with my review on the other game, then you won't go far wrong with this one, I'm sure.It's been tweaked, a good load of new stuff has been added, including some stuff adding more depth to the stats side of baseball, which I mostly don't understand, being from the UK and having only a basic understanding of the rules of the game, let alone the core technical stuff that fans in the USA were brought up with and so understand it as easily as most Brits understand stuff like the off-side rule in football (sorry, I can't call american football "football", and real football soccer, especially considering you don't use your foot on the ball for like 99% of the game). Not that I'm a football fan, I can't stand the sport.Basically if you got along well with the earlier games, you will get along well with this one. If they just weren't your cup of tea, then likely this won't be either.If you liked the previous games, but wanted more "sim" mechanics to the team management and digging into the core stats and whatnot, then this will be your dream game, I reckon
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: So you want a game that's less realistic than MLB the Show, and a game with more depth/time put into it than RBI baseball, enter Super Mega Baseball series. If you loved the Mario Sluggers series, this will be what you're looking for, arcade like baseball game where home runs are plentiful, names are ridiculous, and has a surprising amount of depth, best part, you can just get the demo and play it online! So get a friend or two, make a temporary league (cross play is in it), and play some games! Really brought back Mario Sluggers vibes for me, which is something I have been searching for!

_childDocuments_.review: Best baseball game since MVP baseball. You see, online mode's only have one mode, Pennant Race. And unless you're wanting to sweat your rear end off in constant games, the adrenaline's going to kick in and you'll be playing for a long, LONG time.This wouldn't be a problem if this game's physics weren't, well, questionable. _childDocuments_.review: This is a bare bones arcade baseball game. It's advertised as more than that; those advertisements are wrong.The arcade baseball action is fun but I feel like it should be more over the top than it is. The game plays realistically but there's so much missing from its franchise mode that I feel like the devs really missed opportunities here. If I made a realistic baseball game I'd put as much from the pros in as possible. Since so much is missing why not make the experience more entertaining? And in this age of superfluous character customizations, why aren't there any options in the game?The controls aren't intuitive enough for me. Base running has been hard to get down. Outfielding has taken effort getting used to. Some of the animations are clunky to the extent they are jarring.Franchise mode doesn't have trades. There is no minor league. I have $10 million in salary cap but all the free agents are over-priced compared to similarly rated players on my roster. I can't meaningfully improve my team. The players don't seem to have contracts. Is it a persistent season-to-season experience? Sure. Is there a draft and player retirements? Supposedly. But that by itself does not a franchise mode make.There aren't story arcs over the season. There's no player drama. Basically, there's nothing to do other than play baseball. It's advertised as more than that but it's not true.I was hoping for more. I feel like I paid too much for this game. Knowing what I know now this should have been a $20 USD bargain bin purchase, maybe even $15. I feel a little conned.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. It has a tremendous amount of charm and polish.However, some of the play mechanics need a lot of work -- particularly on offense when you put the ball in play. The pitching and hitting mechanics themselves are fun, but when you put the ball in play, that's where the stupidity begins.No matter how on-the-button or well-timed your batter makes contact, the game will usually register it as a foul, or it sends your smash line-drive right at a fielder, or your towering, arcing shot is directly over an outfielder for a fly out. This happens time after time. Then, once in awhile, the RNG (or AI or whatever) lets you get a hit. Sometimes the AI (or RNG or whatever) lets you get a hit on the most pathetic, badly hit grounders. Also, in bat after bat, I don't think I hit for extra bases even once. Even if you send one shooting into the outfield just inside the foul line, there's a fielder right there, Johnny-on-the-spot. In actual baseball, a hard shot down the line past the corner-baseman would usually be giving the fielders some mileage on their cleats, unless they were set well outside the usual position. In this game, the field seems shrunken because the fielders vacuum everything up. It really does feel like RNG and probability tables vastly supersede any of the player's skill and timing when dealing with the hitting mechanics. I don't know, maybe it's a perception bias, but after trying dozens of at-bats and connecting with the pitch very solidly many times, frustrating results are what I experienced -- results that seemed out-of-whack with my inputs.It's a shame because there's a lot to like about this game.

All aspects of the game can be tweaked to find the perfect difficulty. Pitching and batting are simple to learn, hard to master. Fielding is a step down over 2 as they removed the very good AI that knew exactly what player you wanted. _childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. The overall flow of play just feels right. Pitching is particularly fluid; I love the physics motion of each pitch type. I do wish they offered a mechanic for knuckleballs and maybe a small selection of different change-up options, but it's minor quibbling. The endless tweakability is also fantastic. For fun and giggles, I created a custom league with the entire 1962 MLB teams with actual player names and basic stats. (My dad's favorite sports team ever was the '62 Giants). It's a total blast to send up Mays and McCovey against Koufax and Drysdale. *Edit -- The CPU AI does a good job of identifying situational baseball most of the time. The CPU pitchers will nearly always pitch around Mays if they can (no one on base, or with runner on base but with 2 outs, etc.). It will situationally have pitchers bunt (I play NL). Baserunning feels just right, with a good mix of solid steals when you time it right, but getting your backside handed to you if you get a bad jump or the pitcher catches you in a timed pitch out. One nuance the developers also got right --- playing baserunners from the outfield. It's rare to have a throwout at the plate or getting caught trying to stretch a double where it feels like the computer is cheating. Your good decisions on the basepaths are rewarded, and your bad decisions are punished appropriately. The Ego settings may take some time to dial in. After about 3 games I pushed it to between 32 and 35, but recognize that within another week or two will need to push up again. *Edit -- Pushed ego to between 45 and 50 and the game still feels just a *tad* too easy. My biggest worry about pushing to higher ego settings is the computer's proclivity for fouling off pitches. This creates a weird negative feedback loop with the very limited number of pitchers you can keep on your staff. You end up tiring out your limited number of relievers with these long, drawn-out plate appearances by the opponent CPU. I think the game logic needs to have a very slight adjustment to just have batters put the ball in play more (player and CPU). When you've only got 8 pitchers on staff and your starters' pitch counts can't really go above 90 before their performance falls off a cliff, wasting foul pitches is somewhat punitive. If pitch counts and fatigue/stamina were more controllable, it wouldn't be as a big deal. Or if they'd just open roster size up to the standard 25. I know they went with one more player per roster in SMB4 (22 total vs. 21 total). Not sure why you don't just go official MLB roster size, but what do I know? All that said --- take any minor complaints with a grain of salt. I'm loving this game and give it a wholehearted recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm in the top 150 globally on this game on the Nintendo Switch, about 900 hours played time. My ego sits around 82/75/75/67. Here's my review, which will tend to be critical of more niche things than what other reviewers talk about.To start off: This is the best modern baseball game I've played. Better than SMB4 in its current state. Better than The Show in any of its iterations. The only game I've played that could hold a candle to it is MVP Baseball 2005, and good luck finding that game. The hitting, the pitching, the mojo system -- all great.Some old reviews of this game claim it has "catch up mechanics" where the game assists the CPU when you're winning. This claim is just not true. I've won many games after trailing, and have not noticed any system that prevents this.Some players perform way better than the grade they're given, and this makes the game very fun for me. My league is dominated by Pedro Nixon, a backup catcher with a C grade who can't stop hitting home runs. Rip Dingers, who I think is graded A overall, can't seem to push his ERA above 0.225. Maybe different players will dominate your league. This is where the mojo system is so great.Ball paths tend to be a little formulaic. For example, it's much easier to hit a ball straight between the pitchers' legs than down the line. Ego curves in funny ways. Setting your hitting ego at 79 will make an opposing pitcher much more difficult than 78. You get used to it.Likewise, athletes range from legendary to trash tier. An A+ pitcher will be nearly unhittable. Meanwhile you can tee off on their C- reliever. Disappointingly, the CPU is not a very good manager. Many times, a struggling pitcher will be left out there far too long. I could keep going on, but I'll leave it here. It's a fun game that you should buy if you enjoy baseball.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I constantly find myself coming back to when I'm bored or looking for something to play. As a fan since SMB1, it took me a bit to get on board with the slight gameplay tweaks, but after a while I've come to appreciate the fact that the game largely perfects what has drawn me in to the series in the first place. Both the hitting and pitching mechanics are superb, and it's still incredibly satisfying to crush a pitch or paint the corners, even after hundreds of hours played across PC and console. Franchise mode is a really fun framework around the gameplay as well - I didn't think I would enjoy playing it without custom rosters, but the game does a great job getting you attached to key players and being a bit disappointed when they decide to walk in the offseason. Resource management is great as well, giving you the ability to use your budget to sign great players, or invest in improving your existing players. There is a bit of RNG at play, only allowing you to improve players based on random upgrades you're able to purchase after every franchise game. I'm not a HUGE fan of this and would appreciate a little more freedom with how I choose to develop my team, but I can appreciate the restriction of not being able to dump all my funds immediately into a single attribute such as power for my entire roster. My biggest gripe with the game is the lack of improvement in customization from SMB2 to SMB3. Customization is a fantastic part of this game, should you choose to devote your time to it. The emblem editor allows you to create some pretty great logos, and there are tons of uniforms to choose from. The issue though is that it can get a bit annoying to see the same 6 or 7 faces and expressions across an entire custom league with 32 or even 16 teams. There's enough here on an individual player basis to get you close enough to what you were hoping to build, but some more options would have gone a long way for me. Overall, as a long time fan of the series, it's fair to say I have some gripes and issues with a few minor aspects of the game, but it's easily my favorite baseball game of all time, and is definitely on my Mount Rushmore of greatest sports games ever.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: as I was expecting SMB4 now that EA has the developer isn't quite the upgrade a sequel should be. Stick to SMB3 it's the only baseball game you'll need. I bought this one on sale recently when it was $5. I have been looking for a solid, fun baseball game to play for awhile. As much as I previously have enjoyed The Show on Playstation, I have been losing interest in full simulation sports games as I have gotten older. SMB3 is a great balance of what I'm looking for.The game is approachable and has adjustable difficulty sliders for each aspect of the game, batting, running, pitching, and fielding. It may seem very arcade like from the appearance but under the hood, their are some serious baseball mechanics. Things that play on the psychology of the sport, the pitcher and batter duel especially. Give up a few hits or a big HR? Your pitcher may grown tense and their stats decrease from being rattled. Down by a run, bases loaded, 2 outs in the bottom of the ninth? Your batter gets tense. I love these aspects of the game. High pitch counts decrease stats as well, requiring bullpen subs and I use a specific relief pitcher as strike out closer too.It doesn't have the MLB license but I prefer it this way. I like having my own custom team, logo, and players. There are a lot of customization options for your logo and colors as well as players both male and female for your roster. Best of all, no outdated rosters making the game never feel aged. It may not have the depth in franchise mode as the Show but to me this works to it's strengths. It lets you get right to the point that I came here for, to play some baseball. SMB4 is coming out in June but honestly, I can't see myself migrating over anytime soon. SMB3 is just that good and checks all the boxes of a baseball game I have wanted for years.If you have any interest in baseball whether casually or a hardcore knowledge, I recommend giving the demo a try. For me, the greatest aspect of baseball which sets it apart from other sports is the mental and psychological aspects. This game captures just enough of that to keep my interest without requiring some excel spreadsheet moneyball style to keep track of everything.

_childDocuments_.review: Now with that out of the way, My hours on the Switch version alone should communicate that SMB3 is not only a great pick-up-and-play game, but it's a great time and baseball experience overall. SMB3 walks a perfect line between fun arcade sensibilities and realistic fundamentals, all within the realm of a charming, cartoon baseball league. The game comes with personality, decent single player components and some wickedly fun multiplayer modes.SMB3's aesthetic is not only fun and colourful, but witty too. Players come in all kinds of exaggerated shapes and sizes, complimented by some of the funniest stock names I've ever seen. I never get tired of see players like Sloop Whoopity and Stockton Brickhouse. What struck me the most in the visual department was actually the stadiums, which go beyond charming and look downright beautiful, especially during evening games. Throw in a fun little original soundtrack and some funny, albeit limited writing, and SMB3 will please the senses.As a baseball game, it feels sharp and responsive. I found the batting very intuitive to get to grips with, especially compared to MLB The Show, and the variable "Ego" difficulty system allows for you to optimise overall pitch speed to suit you as you develop at the game. The pitching mechanics are similarly intuitive and easy-to-grasp, providing numerous pitch types and even the ability to select the speed at which you want to pitch. Further depth appears when you weigh the risks between throwing harder and keeping control, alongside considering the sweet spots of certain batters. These are definitely the best arcade pitching mechanics of any baseball game I've played before. Throw in some reliable fielding and base-running mechanics, and what we have here is a full baseball package.There are decent single-player options on offer, from quick matches, to single seasons, to full-blown franchises. There's even a handy little practice mode included too, which I found especially useful for adjusting to game's complexities in a safe environment. Franchise is easily my favourite mode, giving you full control of a team, from their games, to player trades and even their training regimens. It lacks the depth of Out of the Park Baseball and MLB: The Show's franchise mode, but it's always fun to build your own little team. Definitely try your best at playing all the way to a world series title.If you know anything about this game, what you're really here for is the multiplayer scene. Pennant Race mode is a triumph and a really great scene to get stuck into. Chosing either a pre-existing team, or redesigning a team fit your aesthetic, you play games against other players in a weekly league, trying to rack up enough wins to take the highest spots on the leader-board. It's simple, but it's pretty damn addictive for anyone with a competitive streak who's interested in playing at the highest ranks. If you'd rather play multiplayer games in a more controlled environment or with friends, the 'Online Leagues' mode has you covered.I could easily rank SMB3 as one of the greatest baseball games ever made and a truly positive iteration in the SMB series. However, there are several aspects that do hold it back. The more you play any single player components of the game, the more you'll notice little algorithmic issues, such as where AI batters will hit seemingly impossible pitches. This is competitively similar to how racing games may have 'rubberbanding' present to artificially increase an AI opponent's ability to compete. Pennant Race also lacks reliable net-code or any fail-safes to mitigate damage done by dropped connections or players leaving, causing you to rack up losses and hurt your chances of winning if your internet is unstable. I'm hoping that this is less of an issue on PC, but it was certainly unbearable on the Switch.Overall, I can't recommend this game enough, both to baseball and multiplayer fans. It's got a rock solid foundation to please MLB: The Show players looking for good substitute on PC, and an excellent suite of single-player and multiplayer modes that accommodate anyone looking for a great, pick-up-and-play game with a great casually competitive scene. A new SMB game is coming soon apparently, so it was important to me to put down how much I do love this game, somewhere, in case we find ourselves moving on. Nonetheless, SMB3 should not be forgotten any time soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Best baseball game on any platform...period. Don't let the arcade visuals fool you, this game is deep and strategic. Pennant Race will have you throwing your controller across the room. Five minutes later, you're plugging it back in for some more punishment because winning is so rewarding. Think it looks too easy? Set the difficulty ego to 80 and watch the AI smash ropes deep onto the upper deck. Want to do the same? Set the ego down to 1 and crush 500 ft dingers to the cheap seats.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great.  If you're on the fence, just try it.  If you're a baseball fan, you won't regret it.  It's not licensed by the MLB, nor is the MLB the show quality but that's not a bad thing here.  The game play is buttery smooth and the arcade like graphics play just nice here.  i'm playing through franchise mode and the depth is surprising.  Even though the game is a few years old now, it holds up well.  Again, you won't regret the purchase if you're a fan of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game single-handedly made me care about baseball. I don't really have anything negative to say about it other than some apprehension about how EA will handle the 4th game. Good news is you can get this one now.Some pros worth mentioning:• The gameplay is super slick. Pitching and batting feels fair and the difficulty settings are very customizable, so that you can fine tune it to give you the exact level of challenge that you're looking for.• 14 stadiums each with 3 times of day/weather options. Never feels like you're playing in the same place over and over.• The players have some hilarious names and the stadium announcer will announce each of them.• The art style being more cartoonish actually looks more engaging than The Show and other sports games that get stuck in uncanny valley of motion capture.• Customizable teams and leagues offer a lot of options for replayablility.There's a free demo, no reason not to try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Lots of customization options. You can make your own players, teams, leagues etc.  You can have male or female players, and have co-ed teams if you want. You can also edit all of the players if you DON'T want female players. That's about it.Cons:Clunky user interface and menus.Horrific cartoony graphics.Not fun.Final thoughts:I liked the idea of having a complete fantasy baseball league, with male and female players. It wasn't a serious baseball game like MLB The Show, so why not?  Unfortunately I found using the menus and interface to be a terrible experience. I ended up switching back and forth from using an XBOX One controller to the mouse to get around. It's ridiculously clunky and annoying.  Graphics are a terrible cartoon style. I didn't expect AAA graphics, but come on, the players look hideous.The actual baseball part of the game just wasn't very fun.  I guess I'm spoiled by MLB The Show.Can't recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I paid full price for this game and have never regretted it. It's packed with tons of features, and for nine bucks it's a steal. That's not much of a sacrifice, and it's a real safe play. Run home and buy this game; you'll have a ball. I can't think of any strikes against it. After all, it's usually more than triple this price. Bunt.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Best baseball game on PC and consoles, hands down.  Easy to pick up fast game play and all teams have really well defined strengths and weaknesses.  Online play is top notch, large community of players and cross platform, so you are rarely waiting too long for a match.  Every week online mode resets, allowing you to change teams and every week each team has 4 players that either boost or loose stats, making it feel fresh every week.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Baseball, America's game. When I first hit a comebacker into the nutsack of the opposing team's pitcher and watched him keel over comically I knew this was the game for me. Deep down it's a solid baseball game but there's more than a smattering of personality that makes things entertaining and fun. Batter up!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game understands baseball better than any other game I've ever played. The mechanics are simple to learn but contain tons of nuance, and mastering them is extremely rewarding. The gameplay is arcade-inspired, but also somehow the most realistic baseball gameplay I've ever experienced. Not only is it super fun, but the game also has incredible customization options. You can create your own league, teams, uniforms, and players, and for me that's as much fun as actually playing the games. This game rules.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal balance between 'sim' and 'arcade'.  Have really enjoyed playing both single player and online co-op franchise modes.  Sound and graphics are good, but nothing crazy.  Honestly it's the best baseball game I've played in many years, and I'm impressed at how different it feels from SMB1.With that said, I do have some feedback for the developers.  Would love to see some more sounds overall - like the ball thumping off the fence or a 'cling!' after hitting a post.  Right now it's all kind of generic, and although it doesn't take away from the core gameplay experience, after 50+ hours it all kind of sounds the same.  Likewise, I would enjoy seeing the slider move just a tiny bit more towards sim in terms of animations and physics.  Again, just little tweaks to make the game feel more alive.  Like if I hit the ball into the dugout it should bounce around or there should be players in there that react.  Same with the crowd.  Maybe it bounces out of the stands like it does in real games sometimes.  I dunno, just spitballing.  Oh yeah, and while I'm thinking about it, an instant replay feature.  All those line drives back to the pitcher need to be reviewed in slow-mo to determine exactly where it hit them.Those sort of finishing touches would be great to see in SMB4!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: It is great fun.  You can customize your team and tweak it like crazy, or you can use the standard teams and test your skills.  I REALLY love the unisex aspect of the game including the umpires.  it makes the game truly diverse and cool.  The ability to customize your team is cool as they can look how you want down to the uniforms.  The only thing I don't like is that the announcer does not call the names of players not on standard teams.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not aware of a better modern baseball game on PC, although I hope one day MLB The Show comes to PC. I think the difficulty and catch-up mechanics are fine if you stay on top of the ego mechanic. Whenever I win a game I increase the ego setting. If I lose 3 in a row I lower the ego setting. It's a great way to keep the game challenging and helps account for some of the balance issues. I'm having a lot of fun with the game and I pop in to play a game about once a week in franchise mode where I have made my IRL friends make up the roster of my team.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good for a baseball game. I would love it more if there were actual league teams, but what they have are pretty varied. There is also customization. But, if you want a solid Baseball game that observes all the rules, then this is your best bet. The only real draw back is that the batting powerup isnt very clear from the getgo. But all in all, definitely buy this game, its better than its MLB counterpart.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly the best baseball game I've ever played.  Certainly the most realistic.  Having to carefully select a pitch, pitch location, while paying attention to pitch count is suspenseful.  Since the batters truly adapt to your pitching (looking for certain pitches and/or in certain locations on certain counts) keeps you thinking.As easy or as difficult as you want with a 1-100 difficulty scale. _childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is solid, although I hate having to try and aim with the controller when hitting. If you've played the game you will probably know what I am referring to. Pitching works very well, hitting, is a little to busy. Also, be warned that franchise mode is not at all a "franchise mode" in the traditional sense. You can sign players and release ones on your team. There are no contracts or years remaining, only a salary. At the end of the season random players just resign, nothing you can do about it...and forget about paying for that same player in the sign and release section. His requested salary has now tripled or quadrupled. There is no trading of players or picks. There is no draft.  The only thing you can do is sign and release players... but the budgets seem very low considering you can hardly afford any of the top players. Pick a low game count for the season as well. You CANNOT simulate your games in standard franchise mode.  So you will be playing 9 innings times 32 or however many games....and playoffs are best of 5. It takes forever to finish a season. Also, you don't have multiple save files...only one, as far as I can tell. I did like the way player development was tied to team salary. That is a neat idea, but it also takes away from you signing players and then the players you just developed can walk anytime they want. Twas a nice idea.The game is fun to play though. Aside from the aiming while batting (which I think doesn't work, maybe it is better with a mouse). The cursor moves automatically when the pitch is thrown. Then you are supposed to adjust the cursor, but also while you are powering your swing, watching the ball, making sure it is a strike. In baseball you watch the pitcher, not at the spot directly in front of my feet.  I just kept finding the game over compensating my swing actually making me worse than not moving the cursor anything at all...but if you don't move the cursor you just ground out of pop out weakly (on harder difficulties, because the pitchers hit the corners but you can't unless you aim). Like I said, if it was just a push in a direction, that would be fine, but the aiming isn't good on controller.  Zero settings in normal franchise mode. Almost no settings in any portion.  Overall, I was disappointed because I was expecting more, but I wasn't disappointed either. The game is fun. It is probably the best pitching system in any baseball game I've played. It is quick. I am not usually a big fan of defense in baseball games, and this has some automation added which makes it a little less cumbersome. I just want to pitch and bat, no fielding. Unless I am exclusively controlling one fielder.  So, ya, game modes are extremely weak. Game play is fun. Overall worth a good $15.Review is for solo players.feel free to correct if you think I got something wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best baseball game I have ever played, bar none.Despite its cartoony graphics, in terms of simulating the feel of actually playing baseball, this is the most realistic thing out there. Batted ball trajectory in relation to timing, pitch location, pitch type, and hitting over/under the ball is just like the real thing. Pitch speed is in that sweet spot where the hard stuff is fast, but hittable if you're sitting on it; but then that leaves you vulnerable to off-speed.Pitching feels exactly like the real thing too. If you know how to pitch in real life, those same pitches in those same locations will almost always result in the expected batted ball outcomes in the game (note: against human players online; dunno about AI). There are a couple of notable exceptions to this; namely down-and-away fastballs and low curveballs in general wind up being homers with unrealistic frequency, but I assume that's a conscious balance decision to prevent pitching low-and-away from being TOO effective. Another strong point is that messing up your pitch accuracy is just as likely to result in a hanger in the middle of the zone as it to resulting in a ball, whereas most games just have it result in a ball by default.Online play is smooth (mostly). Team customization options are great and make it really fun to take your team of James Bonds or whatever online instead of just the default teams.The only negatives I can think of: Fielding is a fairly useless stat, as Speed also governs fielding range and errors don't occur often enough with low Fielding to compensate for it. Faking out/♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up rundowns is WAY too easy; a "cancel throw" input should really exist. There are no knuckleball pitchers in the game. There's only a handful of stadiums, and none of them are "video game-y" at all, which would be kinda fun.Overall: 9/10. It feels like actual baseball.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun, changing the ego rating does change how the other teams play, and running a whole season is a bit of fun - create  your own team look and name and get in there and play. When you start at first, focus is on learning to hit and field. After that, you need to worry about hitting for optimal placement and strength to get runners moving around the bases. And stealing, base running, and fielding can make a big support for good batting & slugging. Different teams feel a bit different in how they play and even a team getting beaten up in the league can beat a great team if the stars align.  If you want to do some management but a lot of playing, Super Mega Baseball 3 is a good choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent baseball game with fun action for any level of player. A sliding scale of difficulty sends the game from banging homers almost every at-bat to nearly impossible to beat the AI- and everything in between. No matter your level of skill or enthusiasm for baseball, you will be able to dial in an appropriate difficulty. The graphics run towards the cartoonish side which is honestly refreshing in sports games which often go for photo realism instead. Character names are comical and you find yourself looking forward to hearing certain players' names called on by the announcer. Voice is limited to the announcer, which could use more dialog but is serviceable. If you don't touch the controls for a time, the announcer will begin to comment on your lack of engagement or start doing advertisements. It's a nice touch but there should have been more dialog to announce the action. The ump will say things like 'too high' rather than just 'strike' and 'ball' but overall dialog is pretty sparse. The baseball action is on par with any MLB title so far. Using either controller buttons or the twin sticks to swing and make pitches. I highly recommend a controller for this game. With a decent controller, all the various controls are smartly mapped and are intuitive without customizing. Just plug and play. The game has a franchise mode but it is stripped down in terms of contracts, negotiations, and real long term planning. This is my biggest complaint with SMB3- it's really let down by a bare bones franchise mode making single seasons or play off brackets the core of the game. SMB clearly puts the focus on playing rather than managing- although you are still given a good amount of control as manager for setting up your roster and developing players somewhat. The default teams offer a good variety of specialties but the same 'extreme hitter' teams tend to dominate the others. Even with teams having 'flavors', each game is different and I've had the 'defensive' team run up the score on me while other times the big hitter teams fail to score. SMB really gets sports gaming right. Without a real life license to be slave to, the game is refreshingly quirky while still delivering solid baseball gaming. It's ability to cater to the most casual to the most hardcore gives this game broad appeal. Finally a sports game that is every bit as good as the titles with the real world major league license. If there was a football and hockey version of this game, EA Sports would be in real trouble. SMB3 can be highly recommended for anyone that enjoys baseball games.

_childDocuments_.review: I will admit that a little bit of my love for this game might come from a small bit of bias due to the fact there is no good baseball games on PC and the sports world is dry as hell on PC as it is. I actually came across this game in an article called "25 Underrated Steam Games for Summer Sale" and it peaked my interest. From there, I ended up buying it and don't regret a thing. This game is just massively addicting and fun for any sports and especially for those who love baseball like myself. The game is pretty true and authentic to baseball while putting its own spin on it in the way of perks, different teams, and some pretty creative/funny player names. I love the pitching mechanics in this game and batting as well. Although batting is relatively easy and needs to be played on high ego in order to be challenging. The game runs smooth as butter and graphically it looks pretty great, even if some of the player models look ridiculous but it's part of the charm on the game. Stadiums look great as well as the crowds. I mean there isn't much to say other then it plays fantastically well for a baseball game with its own spin of a bit of arcade like style in the way of perks made for players and the fast paced nature of the game. I also love the idea of players getting hot or cold based on their mojo/fitness and the craziness of hitting a player as a pitcher or nailing the pitcher injuring him, it's always pretty funny. Lastly too, the animations are always a good laugh Much as I love this, it does have some issues. The perk system is a cool addition, same as the fitness and mojo but they can be annoying too. The idea that a pitcher who is locked in/on fire basically becomes un-hittable no matter how good a players contact or mojo are inducing soft contact almost every time, even if it's right down the middle of the plate. The lack of an announcer sucks for sure and fielding in this game ranges from super easy to what the hell am I doing. One major issue for me is the lack of being able to trade at all in franchise mode or just signing a player without having to release another. As with any sports game really, there are times where it just feels no matter what you do nothing works in a game which can lead to serious frustration. For a small little indie sports game, it's surprising the amount of depth and fun I've been having with this. I bought this game for 22 bucks on a sale and don't regret it at all. It's not perfect but given the complete lack of PC sports games, it's impressive how much fun this game is and what it has to offer. I've enjoyed this more than practically any game from EA when it comes to their major sports game over the past few years. Not sure I'd recommend this at FULL price unless you're desperate for a baseball game or a major sports fan but it definitely is worth it if you are. For the casual gamers or sports fans, it's worth it for sure, just at a price cut. I personally love this game flaws and all. What a hidden gem!

_childDocuments_.review: SMB3 is everything one could ever look for in an arcade-style baseball game. Interesting depth to each team, engaging game modes that keep you in pursuit of silverware, and some immersive spirit that makes you feel like you're at a ballpark that's just goofy enough to exist in a gaming sphere. The gameplay is intuitive and simple to understand, yet challenging once you crank up the difficulty, and if you're playing online, it keeps things fair between two players of differing skill levels. I've racked up almost 150 hours in just over three months, and there's some main points that stand out to me:- Franchise mode is addicting as hell. You can set a season length to 16, 32, or 48 games, with playoff series scaled best-of-3/5/7 respectively. The mode uses a payroll system that lets you allocate money into training to boost stats, or to sign free agents. Unfortunately there's no trade system.- Custom teams are a cool feature, with lots of potential for teams so goofy that you can't even get mad going up against them. Pennant Race (the weekly league system) as well as Online Franchise let you customize teams and bring them online. I went against the Seinfeld cast one time and Jerry hit a 3-run bomb on me.- The aforementioned Pennant Race is something I've been playing a lot more as of late. Moving up in the rankings (both matchmaking division and your own 15-team group which you're placed into every week), getting some online experience in single 5-inning games, and filling your awards cabinet is a nice pursuit.- Online Franchise, too, has potential for a lot of fun. Up to 32 people can go through a collective schedule where you hop on to face one another and play out a season (or several more, if you're crazy and dedicated enough).- All these modes make for a well-rounded game where you can hop around between modes whenever you get bored of one of them.On the (minor) downside of things:- The difficulty system, like almost every other sports game, suffers from a purgatory of sorts, where once you hone your skills to a certain point, the difficulty scale puts you in an awkward spot where the game is either way too easy or controller-breakingly hard. SMB manages to achieve this purgatory despite having a 0-100 difficulty scale; for me, it occurs around 65. A bit more patient of a playstyle would probably aid me to 70 or 75, but the arcadeyness turns my brain off a bit - I digress.- Crossplay is enabled in SMB3, and the stuttering connection against console players is supremely frustrating at times. Lag spikes range from a couple to a couple dozen times per game, and it might cost you some vital runs - I know it has for me.SMB3 is surely worth its sale price, however. Maaaaybe not the standard $45 if you're not sure, but I definitely got my money's worth out of it. I'm the kind of guy that loves having a laid back sports game when I'm not doing any other intense gaming, but rest assured, all of this game's modes will have you engaged and looking to taste victory.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Solid game, awesome style, lacking depth in actual gameplay and not much other content. 9/10 game with friends and drinks, 5/10 alone. 7/10 if you've never played Baseball - it's VERY accessible and would highly recommend as a game for 'getting into' Baseball and learning the basics.The game can unfortunately be reduced to very few minigames: Pitching, fielding and batting. That's about 80% of the entire game, with it being 95% of what you will be playing.With such a split, it’s a demand that these three minigames are amazing; and that’s where SMB3 doesn’t succeed. The game is a fantastic party game with baseball friends – but lacks the depth to make it enjoyable by yourself.In addition, there’s a vast disparity between what the CPU is able to do and what you can do. The CPU will instantly move fielders to the exact location of where you hit, they will foul all balls you send at them on a full-count and will make any hit at least a single – and that’s with ‘40/100’ difficulty.I adore the strategic elements of the game, but strategy jumps out of the window when the CPU can adjust within a split second and outperform even your perfect throws/pitches/bats.I think the best example is fielding: When you’re a human, you run for the ball and keep an eye out for where it’s landing. This logically means there is a chance you over- or undershoot it. Well, the difference is that you, as a player, aren’t looking at the ball – you’re looking at the fielders whose about to catch. This means that the last moments of the catch – the slide/jump/catch – is extremely difficult to gauge, which should be the easiest part of the catch. There’s been countless occasions where I’ve been standing directly under the ball, and the ball will just fly right over the fielder’ head, because they don’t have the brain to lift a hand unless you explicitly tell them to.Compare that to fielders that will instantly run to exactly where the ball is landing and will instantly throw the ball to the exact base a runner can’t reach in time at perfect speed and power, which is caught 99% of the time. Whereas my fielders have a ~25% chance to outright fail a catch if I’m not instructing them manually – oh, and my fielders can’t run unless I manually control them. The only possible scenario where my fielders will catch it every time, is a huge flyball straight to the fielder.Fun game with friends, waste of time alone unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a fun game with easy adjustable difficulty scale. pretty deep all things considered. Batting is fun, although i swear HR's are RNG. Pitching is fun and challenging. But i swear you can tell when the AI is gonna get runs and there's nothing you can do about it. just try to minimize it. I love the Mojo System. It goes from Rattled to Locked In and will affect your players stats accordingly. Nothing better than getting an opposing pitcher's Mojo to Rattled and taking advantage over balls over the plate. However, i wish the AI would replace pitchers sooner. I've had games where I've scored 15+ runs on a pitcher and he stays in. I dont know if thats due to the limited roster size, but at that point in the game, im trying to get it over with cause its boring. It'd be neat if there was a way to hire pitching coaches and you could have you pitching coach go out there to talk to the pitcher and there's a 50/50 chance to increase his mojo. Better coaches would increase the chance or would give you some info about the batter your about to face. Franchise mode is fun. I wish i could make some changes though. I wish i could adjust the season length after each season. 32 games is just too long for me, but i dont want to lose all the work ive gained in building this team and starting over. I developed  an internal rivalry with another team because of the fierce games we had every time we faced. It'd be cool if there was a rivalry system in place for something like that and games were a higher intensity, had more effect on Mojo, and things of the like. I learned over the course of a season how to throw at certain players. Feared facing certain pitchers, knowing i was in for a long game. There's a lot of strategy with roster customization and theres a lot of freedom to create the team that you want. But here's where i start to have some cons about the game. I'm not a big fan of free agency and acquiring players.  There's no trading which is kind of sucks. No contract management whatsoever. There's no draft to acquire a young player to groom into a starting role. Free agency is a massive gamble. You have a limited salary cap and after each game or in the off-season a player is available will have their salaries reduced a little. Trying to get the a player for as cheap as possible is a big gamble as the cpu has first dibs on players each week. i wish there was a way to offer contracts and see if they accept. Also, at the end of a season, players will just leave you team or retire, with no notice and either you overpay, or you have to find a replacement. I finished my first season the other day. I lost 2 of my top 3 players. 1 via free agency and 1 to retirement. I also had another starter leave via free agency and one of my top pitchers retired. A lot of holes and you gotta take some gambles. Their asking prices far exceeded what i could afford to field a team so i played the waiting game.  I was skipping weeks in free agency to try to lower some of the players i targeted to affordable contracts. In one week, the ai signed almost half of the available players leaving me with no one i was looking for and a lot of meh players remaining. My roster today is not what i had hoped it would be, but thats the gamble you take. I wish this system was overhauled. it's my only real big gripe with the game. I wanted a playstation for a longtime to buy mlb the show, and frankly if player acquisition was overhauled and theres was a little more depth and fine-tuning involved, I would say its a perfect game. It's worth the cost, and its a lot of fun. Don't let the cartoon-y graphics bother you, it really is an excellent game and hopefully future iterations will make this the only baseball game worth owning.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game in the free week, that they offered and I really enjoyed it!They managed to point out the essence of the game instead of capitalist egomaniac selflove of the MLB franchise itself.Without having to pay for the licenses, maybe they should have made the game half the price from the beginning. I appreciate the flawless work though. I didn't have a single issue on my mediocre machine.This game is really fast paced. Pitch after pitch, after pitch. No ego-trips, no waiting, no stupid animations (except for homers, there is about 5 seconds of celebration you cannot skip). Talking about Ego. That's what they call their difficulty level. It goes from 0-99. It defines the general speed of the game and the way the AI is selecting pitches. Hard for me to give a comment on that after a week, but you can dial it in to your preference at any time immediatly.Pitching, Batting and Fielding feels really intuitive and somewhat realistic. It's about reaction times, timing and preplaning your plays and a little bit of luck, just like in RL. I played defense with a joypad and offense with mouse and keyboard. You don't even have to assign controls when switching, just use both.Baserunning can be a little fiddly, when runners are close together (f.e. runners on 1st and 2nd, high fly ball to deep CF, runner on 1st taking a big lead, while runner on 2nd trying to tag up).Team management is really easy and fast.Of course there's another point about baseball, that is probably impossible to simulate. Hanging out at the ball park. Playing catch or just watching a game while having a hot dog, letting the sun shine on you, but for a computer game, it's pretty much all you need, if you like playing baseball and are not just a fan of some millionaire ball players.It looks good. It feels good. It's fun. It's addicting. It's baseball!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an old school gamer. I grew up playing games like RBI Baseball, Bases Loaded and Ken Griffey Jr Baseball. _childDocuments_.review: The only thing that this game takes seriously is baseball.  Silly names, cartoonish graphics (on purpose) and umpires that must've watched Leslie Nielsen in "The Naked Gun" don't detract from the fact that this is a serious baseball sim.Lack of an MLB license might seem like a downer, but for me it was fine.  That way, there are no expectations for your team, and you don't have to feel bad if your favorite player finished the season with a .179 BA.Player difficulty is very tunable, all the way from everything almost running itself to "you're on your own".In franchise mode, individual players get better with age, and then start the sad decline that eventually leads to retirement.  Although there is no draft, there is a free agency pool that get stoked with rookies waiting for the chance to show their stuff to a interested franchise, grizzled veterans testing free agency, as well as players forced into free agency by their former team.  Some of those testing free agency might be from YOUR team!  Each season starts with something like a draft from the free agency pool.  There are several rounds where you - and everyone else - gets to set up their teams.  The pool is available all season, and as the season wears on, players in the pool may start to reduce their asking salary to make themselves more attractive as a solution to a problem.  No trading, unfortunately.Random player events - mostly positive for young players, and negative for older players - change their abilities, as well as "training opportunities" that are available for a cost.Injuries happen, but there is no IL so the penalty is that an injured player plays with reduced stats until they heal.  Everyone injured is listed as "day-to-day", I suppose.There is a practice mode where you can practice your skills without affecting your team's season so you don't have to start out getting thrashed by every team you play.So, get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely make a point to play this game if you enjoy quality baseball video games.  I very much like the fact that this isn't another MLBPA sponsored game.  You can just enjoy it for the baseball.  Game play takes a little bit to master but it feels very fluid once you learn it.  Franchise mode is well-rounded with sign & release, player development, as well as off-season transactions.  Team names, player names and personalities are all fun.  The developer also supports the game well with periodic updates and fixes.Regular price may seem a little high but there is also no add-on DLC that can add to you cost, as there was with SMB2.  If you can catch it while it's on sale, even better.

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive. Some little play balance things: Starting a game against "locked in" CPU hitters can be frustrating (repeatedly giving up 0-2 power shots on perfect / near-perfect pitches); most 1B should have 1B range, not play like SS standing at 1B. Pitchers w/ mediocre control are frustrating because they tend to hit the corners, and I'm hitting about .100 when I swing at a pitch on the edge of the strike zone ... particularly frustrating trying to drive balls to the opposite field as it seems like the computer does not have an inside-out swing. Makes it hard to hit hanging curveballs on the outer half of the plate for power, which should be easy pickings. The "ego" feature is good, but smaller gradations would be nice. At Ego 49 I'm winning virtually every game, at Ego 50 I'm lucky to go .500 and can't beat good teams. One obvious flaw is that the announcer, who is hilarious, doesn't use names of computer-added players, just for the lineups of the first tier of teams, so the whole at-bat walk-up loses its luster when you get to a bunch of "Now batting, the shortstop, number 12," instead of using the goofy names.But for the most part, excellent. I find myself missing the cutoff man a lot and worrying that they'll lose mojo if I ignore them too often, it's that immersive.Wide variety of play modes for replay factor. 9.5 / 10, will buy SMB4.

Pitching and batting system are fairly good. Throwing system is good. Difficulty can be changed by each aspect of the game. Fielding pitching, batting ect. Though it isn't as clear as it could be. And It does suffer from the cheap difficulty feel, on higher levels. The A.I. is clearly the low point of the game. There are no percentage breakdowns for actions or rolls. It will do a thing on said level. And it will work or not work almost 100% of the time depending on the difficulty. Which means It feels more like the A.I. is cheating then you are playing someone skilled. I have it on 35. And am trying to see where I can bump it up to without the cheap feeling. And it has a higher percentage of being a ground out or pop fly regardless of the pitch type just because it is the first pitch. For some reason.Though there's a huge amount of customization. And I consider it a knock on any sports game to not have it. So the only reason someone who like baseball wouldn't like this game is if they really need higher difficulties to have fun. Try the demo mess around a bit. See if it's for you.In terms of sports games in general. Not just this game. I wish more was done with the reality of the extreme risk reward that exists in all forms of cheating. Not just ignoring it as though it doesn't exist. Or haha. Just freely giving you a stat boost. And likewise ignoring the extreme negatives associated with cheating. And punishments handed out for doing so. On a team and individual level. And the personal side effects as well.I wish there was the conscious effort  to acknowledge that players play 10 plus seasons with a team so really showcasing stats. And having League records and Halls or fame. And encouragements and rewards that are inherit in real sports. That would incentivise people or at least keep a real record of your time playing a game. For players who go  beyond playing one single season. And throwing the game back in the bin.I wish more was made of the risk of having star players. And the real cost and strains it can put on teams. Instead of just better players equals better team. That a lot of these people are tumultuous, childlike, selfish, overly pampered people. Who cause problems on the field. Off the field. And In the locker room. Is never touched by anyone. It's always just a 100% benefit to have them. Which is no where close to reality. The only acknowledgement ever made is the financial drain.I only make note of these things here. Because this is a successful non licensed game. And real leagues are too greedy and self interested to ever acknowledge the negative sides and problem that exist in their player bases and leagues. Which they themselves feed into.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a perfect mix between Ken Griffey Jr on the SNES/64 with a nice touch of modern day tactics/pitch selection needed to be successful at higher difficulties.  The names of the players are so top notch they make names like Catfish Hunter look as bland as white bread.  There's a huge amount of silly humor throughout the game and Metalhead doesn't take themselves too seriously with regards to it.  And I love them for it. All in all it's a relaxing game that you can make into it what you want.  You can just play exhibitions, play season to season, or online just like any other sports game on the market the past 20 years.  But this game truly has a loving touch to creating a deep fictional sports world and I love them for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: You ever play Hardball back in the '80s? This will bring back memories, only there's more everything. The game has an 'Ego' meter that you can control to set the difficulty how you like it, and you  can fine tune that number even more by making some aspects of the game easier (like maybe batting) while making others more challenging (that stupid left fielder can't even catch a cold). You can make your own customized teams, design your logos, uniforms, and just about everything. The Ball Busters don't win often, but they're a hilarious crew.I haven't played online at all yet, but the exhibition game mode is fantastic for when you want just a little bit of fun. 3 quick innings? Well, maybe, but it'll give you 3. The rest is up to you. Want to do a full 9 against the CPU or another player? No problem. I'm also 5 games into a 16-game regular season. The Platypi are 1-3, but you gotta hang in there. Plays best with a controller. Grab a second and park a buddy next to you. It's a lot of fun.OH, I almost forgot. You can smash a ball right into the pitcher's nuts. It's the most hilarious thing ever. Don't let the haters hate. I laugh my ass off every time, and I've had a urethra reconstruction.

I don't play online, so I can't comment on that. but if you are a fan of baseball, I think there's something here to enjoy. It's a great game for quick pop ins without a lot of time commitment.

It's incredibly entertaining and offers the ability to calibrate and fine tune the difficulty to your liking. There are a plethora of game modes to choose from with online play.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I endorse this game fully. It is fun and has a nice blend of action to capture baseball. I came late to the series having past the first two. I have been looking for a game like this that works on Win10 for some time.  That said there are a few blemishes to be aware of.The franchise and custom teams are limited. You can only pick from the teams included in the game, copy, and rename one. You can edit the players stats only at the start of the franchise except for one, their age. Since who you can have on your team is limited by the budget be sure to pick one with a large budget because your modified player's salary will change with their stats. Forget recruiting one and modifying them. You can't. Once that first season is over you can only recruit from the players available in the game and editing stats is no longer possible.Second is stats. Anyone who loves baseball lives for the stats. While the game tracks quite a few there are some glaring omissions. If you drop a player, their stats go with them. There are no totals so you can't see how many Homeruns your team has hit for example. Missing are also the batting stats for the pitchers so no Babe Ruth stats here (He started as a pitcher before becoming a fielder). Likewise some stats you expect are missing such as DPs made or hit into or POs. The EGO system only displays the lowest setting for a franchise rather than the highest or the average. Otherwise it is a good balancing system.There are some problems with the fielding and running that are not logical. I have had many opponents  get on base because my 2nd base fielder tossed to third instead of first even with no one on base. Likewise my catcher tosses to first instead of second on a stealer. Since I use only my keyboard and mouse rather than a controller, that might be part of the problem. Runners do not advance individuality but all together. For example I can't have 2nd run for third and then home without the batter trying for 2nd and usually a out (especially if he is a slow runner). Very frustrating in a close game.If these don't bother you, I very much recommend getting the game. It is worth the investment.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love MLB The Show, I have wanted something a bit simpler, but still feeling like a sim. This hits that sweet spot between sim and arcade style baseball game. Don't let the goofy character designs fool you, this is a solid baseball game. I haven't enjoyed a baseball game this much since MVP 2005.

_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down the best, most fun, most addicting baseball game on the market. Way more fun than Road to the Show. Obviously this game is more arcadey, and it's not licensed with the MLB so no real teams, but the game play itself is so damn fun. It's one of those games that's hard to put down, and you can sink multiple hours in the game without even realizing it. I've had so many close, sweaty games in my franchise mode.The game has a lot of customization, and you can make a complete custom franchise mode (which is what I've done) You can customize everything about the team, the logo (with a really in depth logo designer) the team jerseys, you can select the home stadium of your team from a pretty decent selection of stadiums, you can customize the stats of your players before you begin the franchise, and you can customize and create every other team in the league if you choose so. Definetely more customization options in this game than in pretty much any other Baseball game on the market. There's not much for me to complain about the game play. There are many different 'levels' you can choose from in this game which is known as 'Ego' Ego goes from 1-100 and the game can get really difficult playing on those higher Egos. I currently play on Ego 85 and I find it's the perfect combination of being challenging but not overwhelmingly difficult for me. This game is a 'hitters' friendly game so expect to give up a lot of hits and even home runs to your competition but you should expect the same for yourself once you start learning the timing of hitting in this game.There is also 2 really addicting online modes for the game. One being the traditional 'Pennant Race' which you play a handful of placement matches to see what rank you belong in. Once you've finished your placement matches and get put into your rank and league, you then start getting every stat and win/loss recorded for the Pennant Race. Pennant Races reset every week and you can rank up in divisions depending on your previous Pennant Race Win/Loss record. You can see the records for you and the rest of your competition and it can become really addicting trying to keep playing and winning so you can see your team move up in the divisional ranks. I also love that your teams stats get recorded during the pennant race as it would in a real MLB season. It's really cool to see which one of your players is struggling in the current pennant race and maybe make decisions to bench him/her. Honestly there are so many more great things I can say about the game but I think I've made my point by saying this game is freaking great.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: May seem pricey at first but offers a lot of value for playability.Pros: -Has everything fun about baseball-Don't need to upgrade every year for a new updated roster like NBA 2K -Variety of teams: From balanced to power hitting to bullpen beasts, each team has different strengths.-Franchise mode: Being able to trade and develop players is fun. Not as complicated as I expected. You can adjust your roster to fit your type of play style as you go.-Season mode: Great if you want to just play as a default team through the entire season without the GM role. -Ego: Able to customize difficulty, including fine-tuning for pitching, base running, batting, and fielding.-PvP: Online or offline. However, I don't play it. -Sense of Humor: Character names are creative (e.g. Manny Kays, Nacho Crisp, Junior Young Senior, Junior Young Jr.)-Stadiums: From ones inspired from famous MLB stadiums to Asian and Caribbean.-Customization: Can customize character looks/names, teams, team logos/names. Basically a lot of things you can do. Some people create teams after their favorite MLB teams or create a fictional league for their country like Canada.Cons:-You can only pickoff successfully if someone is stealing. If they aren't, they'll always be safe even if they are a slow runner.-Stats during a game. You can't really see how your players are performing from a paused screen. It only shows their current game at-bat stats when they walk up to the plate and on the big screen in the outfield. You can only see the game stat right after the game is over, but it isn't saved to be reviewed after. Overall, the Pros far outweigh the Cons. The devs are always making improvements to the game I appreciate it.

_childDocuments_.review: Best baseball game on the market.The hitting and pitching mechanics are waaaay better than the likes of MLB The Show or any other baseball game out there. Don't let the cartoonish graphics fool you into thinking that this isn't a true baseball sim. Customization is great, the new franchise mode gives season play an endless amount of replayability, and the online competitive mode is perfect if playing against AI doesn't do it for you. My only gripe with the game is that you cannot set separate sensitivites for pitching and hitting. That is a much needed addition, as pitching on mouse/kb becomes literally impossible at higher difficulties (70+ ego), so i actually have to use a controller to pitch/play defense and then switch back to my mouse when i go up to bat (but using controller on defense is generally a better option anyway, having 360 degrees of movement when fielding is important). I think $45 might be a little steep (especially considering that buying a $30-$45 controller is probably necessary to play the game properly), but i could easily see that price becoming well worth it as Metalhead continues to patch the game and add more content to it. At this moment in time i'd say the game is easily worth $35, so wait for a sale if money is an issue, but I gladly spent the $45 upon the game's release because i really wanted to support this amazing little indie developer. And custom franchise mode is so damn fun man. I had to say it again.
