_childDocuments_.review: This is the first SMB, I have played, out of the 3. That being said, I have no crazy blind loyalty to Metalhead or SMB, in general. So, I am going to give you the most truthful review I can give, after my first 60 hours.First, let's start out by talking about their newest addition to the game, Co-op Franchise. Now, on the whole, it's a great concept and it is the only reason I bought this game, in the first place. My buddy and I have played this and only this mode, so far, and we have been impressed by most of the aspects of this mode, with a few lacking in certain areas. Co-op FranchisePros:  1. Allows you to select a pre-made team or create your own team, from scratch, and team up with a buddy to take on the rest of the league. 2. There is a salary cap, which adds a little more realism to the mode (meaning you can't just stack your team with a bunch of "S" and "A+" players.3. There is a development system, for all players, throughout the season. You are able to purchase development packages, with development cash that is accrued throughout the year (Based on your team's "payroll surplus" which I will get to later). Players will also improve or get worse, throughout the year, in sometimes comical ways. (For example: "Peter Dragon was able to throw a paper ball into the trash, on the first try! +5 Accuracy" or "Amanda Hugginkiss won an arm wrestling match +10 Power")4. Players will be cut or leave the team, after the season, but you won't know who until they do it. Then you'll either need to replace them or you can resign them (usually for 20 mil more than what you were paying them).5. You get to play multiple seasons and the franchise keeps all of the stats, through every single one. Good stuff.Now, on the things I noticed that need to be added to the game, to improve Franchise.1. Multiplayer/Multi-team Franchise. Co-op is cool and yes it is fun, but let's be honest, we all love competition as well. They should add in the ability to control a team per person, just like "Season mode," but with the multi-season, free agency, development aspect that comes with Franchise. 2. Getting back to the "Payroll Surplus" nonsense. The way they have the development aspect of Franchise set up, is completely ridiculous. If your team has 0 surplus, you will get 0 for development, every single game. If you free up 10 mil of surplus (meaning releasing good players and replacing them with horrible players), then you will be able to make around 312,500 per game (based on a 32 game season, because the surplus is divided by the games per season). Sure, that sounds like a lot of development cash, but it's really just a fraction of what some of the packages will be. Yes there will be some that only cost you 200k or 500k, but most of them will be 1 Mil or higher. So, it will take you 3 games, just to make enough money to buy a package for just one player. That package will usually be something along the lines of...+1 Speed+3 Contact or +8 Contact (10% chance)+1 Power or +5 power (10% chance)Chance to earn "Low Pitch" trait (5% chance)Now, can you guess what that player, you just spent 1.3 Mil on, will get from that purchase? YEP! You got it! You will get +1 speed, +3 Contact, +1 Power and you will NOT get the "Low Pitch" trait. That is the story of development, throughout the entire Franchise. Getting the higher amounts or a trait is like winning the PowerBall and if you get any of them, you should lay your controller down and calmly, but also very quickly, go to your nearest gas station and put in your numbers, because you have now become the luckiest person on this planet for the next 15 minutes. 3. Keeping on with the development aspect of this mode. My recommendation would be to add coaches/managers into the game. Then, depending on the stats of said coach/manager, base the development odds off of them. For example...Coach Dill DoeHitting - POW: 30 / CON: 70 / TRAIT: (average them) 50%Pitching - VEL: 60 / JNK: 35 / ACC: 80 / TRAIT: 58%Fielding - FLD: 80 / ARM: 50 / TRAIT: 65%Baserunning - SPD: 20 / TRAIT: 20%  (or maybe divide it by 2, so that a guy with 99 doesn't have a 99% chance to get the trait)So, that would mean that this particular coach would be able to improve your team's contact, faster than power and so on, While having better chances to give his/her players a higher chance at getting, losing or keeping their trait. That pretty much sums up my thoughts on Franchise mode. Now I will go over a couple of random issues, I noticed, that hopefully will be patched (If Metalhead Games takes the time to care)1. The outside part of the strike zone seems to be pretty wide, for both AI and human players. I've had multiple pitches called strikes, that were clearly inside or outside of the strike zone. That goes both way as well. I've been using the exploit, where you can throw a change-up, curve or slider to just below the outside corner (where it is clearly a ball) and have it always be called a strike.2. Batter view. They need to allow us to change our view, because the low pitches all look the same. I've had some where I'm like "Yeah that's too low" and it will be called a strike, then the next pitch will look exactly the same and be called a ball. Perhaps a batters view that is angle more down or a zoomed in view, directly over the plate would be nice. 3. The AI needs to have the same restrictions as the human player, in terms of batting. I've seen some of the most ridiculous pitches crushed out of the park, by the AI, while that exact same pitch would always be popped up or dribbled to the pitcher for a human player. I feel like, as long as they make it somewhat believable, it would be cool, but an inside pitch being pushed to the opposite field for 475 feet is a tad ridiculous. Same goes for the curve ball that is literally about to hit the dirt. Trying to get the AI to chase a 3rd strike, in the dirt, turns into a golf swing that still hasn't landed yet. If the human player swings at that, it's going to travel a total of 6 inches. Come on Metalhead...I mean...Come on...4. I've NEVER known a power hitter, in my life, that doesn't love it when a pitcher is dumb enough to throw some high heat. It gets crushed almost every single time. That's something games like "MLB The Show" get right, but in this game, do not...I repeat...DO NOT swing at it. Metalhead doesn't understand that high fastballs are hit out of the park more than any other pitch on the planet. They seem to thing that those pitches will be popped up 10/10 times. EVEN IF YOU HAVE THE HIGH PITCH TRAIT!!! Just do yourself a favor and don't swing at them, until they get someone, who knows something about baseball, to come in and fix that nonsense.5. This is just a cosmetic issue, from what I can tell, but at times player photos will not be centered on the player card. Only half of their head and one shoulder will be showing. Again, not really a gameplay issue, so if you're able to ignore it, it really doesn't affect anything.6. Not sure if this is a Steam issue or if it's a game issue, but it'll randomly kick myself and my buddy out of the game and it'll completely close out, leaving me dumbfounded and just staring at the wallpaper of Scarlett Johansson, in a bikini, on my computer monitor, before having to turn on the game and go through the whole invite process all over again. In conclusion, as I said above, this is not a bad game by any means. It's actually a lot of fun, but could use a couple more additions and a tad bit of TLC. I do recommend this game. Hopefully some of these things are fixed or added, because then it would pretty much be a perfect game.

_childDocuments_.review: Have played smb for a couple years now and love the games. There are moments where the CPU feels like it's a little too good, but conversely, there are moments were the CPU makes a shockingly awful managerial decision and essentially throws a game.  Which I guess means that this is fairly true to real-life baseball.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game. The fielder selection isn't quite as good as SMB2, but I'm hoping that they incorporate a legacy option in a future update. I can see how somebody playing the game for the first time wouldn't be overly bothered by it. The devs seem to listen to the SMB community on Reddit as there have been some fair criticisms that they've responded to and addressed such as line out double plays and pick off attempts/base stealing.This is a way more in depth baseball game than the cartoony characters would have you believe. Mixing up pitches and pitch rhythm are very important when playing against the CPU. The EGO in this game to set your difficulty is also really fun and challenging. If you're coming from SMB2 don't expect to play at the same EGO you did on that game, this is a bit of a different beast.  If you're on the fence because of the price tag I would say that is fair as it is an expensive game. Definitely take advantage of Steams 2 hour refund policy if you are considering it.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

You can adjust the difficulty to suit your play style.  From wanting to smash home runs and strike out batters to eeking out a tight 2-1 win in the 9th inning.  The initial launch had some performance issues but they seem to ave fixed any complaints I had.  Wish there was Steam Workshop stuff but alas that hasn't happened.... yet.  Buy it and enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Keeps getting better each version, watch out MLB the Show. I'd hate for this game to loose steam when MLB The Show hits on the next Xbox system...
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great. but i think some minor adjustments would make the game amazing. Needs player collision for the fielders and base runners, base runners should be able to be hit by an incoming ball struck by the batter, fielding injuries from diving into walls or poorly timed diving catches. allow a chance for defensive players to fall, dive, or leap over walls to catch the ball. season ending injuries. with these little things added would give the game an extra kick of greatness in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Just like 1 and 2, SMB3 continues the awesome arcade-but-still-pretty-damn-realistic baseball gameplay on PC. If you loved games like Ken Griffey Jr.'s Major League Baseball on N64 or Backyard Baseball way back when then you are gonna absolutely feel right at home in this game.Many of the technical changes between SMB2 and SMB3 aren't on the same level as SMB1 to SMB2. But what SMB3 does do while taking on the backbone of SMB2, is a more in depth franchise system. Not to mention additional improvements to the game itself, like pick-offs and passed balls. Metalhead has done a great job with this series and is really in tune with the community. They are still actively taking feedback on the game and applying updates, so they're committed to getting it right.The Crocodons are the best team of all time and I will die on this hill.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: SMB 3 is great fun. It's not more realistic or more feature rich on the field as The Show. Don't expect The Show's endless control and camera options or anything  like that.   This game keeps its focus on the GAME of baseball and it does it well.   Everyone who left a positive review said most of the nice things I would say.I have criticisms though.  The franchise mode is a welcome addition and I'm enjoying it.  I could forgive it's simplicity as I'm not expecting a deep baseball world sim like you'd find in the Out of the Park Franchise.  That's not what this game is.  This game focuses on the GAME of baseball and in no way attempts to simulate the business end of it.  The franchise mode is there to give you a reason to play a lot of games and feel connected to your players and team.  And it works. And theres a few nice touches in there like a four pitcher rotation and things like that.   I'm simply disappointed in the small little options that could have easily been added.   You CAN have up to 32 teams and set up a league thats darn close to the MLB, but you should at least be able to customize the games the amount of playoff games played in each series.   And what would have been REALLY awesome is even bigger leagues.   I think they really dropped the ball here.  The possibilities could have been really cool and they really could have taken advantage of the fact that this game IS a little zany and DOESNT take itself too seriously to huge effect simply by adding a few menu choices.   128 team leagues possibly with relegation, maybe even cups and trophies like world sports. Scheduling options. Custom tournaments within the franchise. All possible but not there.  You're stuck with doing what you can already do in other sports games and in some cases less.  Sure you can make a league set up just like MLB (with a more simplified playoff format), but you should be able to make one even crazier and more fun than MLB if you wish.  And why is there no bullpen dynamic?  It's such a staple in video game baseball since I was a kid that it's odd that it's not there.  I guess one could argue that the game itself is more fun to play without having to warm up pitchers.  Just strange that its not there.Also the game simply could use a little MORE. More fun stadiums, more control options, more customization, etc.But thats nitpicking on what the game doesn't really even try.   The focus here is clearly on a fun, accessable game thats got that classic "easy to pick up hard to master" formula of gameplay.  And it captures that ongoing dynamic of pitchers facing batters over a whole game well.  The way your pitchers fatigue, throw over time.   The more I play the deeper and more fun it gets.  The way your opponent counters you...  all just very fun. It's not terrible realistic but it IS a great approach to video game baseball.  The price is high, I picked it up on sale but even at full price, I think they've earned their money.   There simply isn't a better on field game of baseball to be played on PC than there is in SMB3.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Good fun. AI is a bit suspect, but relatively active patching seems to have helped. There's still a bit of a mechanic wherein it seems like you're just destined to lose some games, no matter the ego or the ability of the players involved. But, that's baseball I guess. Still worth full price, and if you can get it on sale, well that's a no-brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Franchise mode & pickoff moves seem to be the new features in what is the best baseball game at this time made outside of Japan.  Non-MLB players and stadiums may be a turnoff to some, but the gameplay mechanics are outstanding and it's obvious the developers really understand baseball.  Very fun, tons of replayability, co-op - just a very very good baseball game.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge baseball aficionado and this is honestly a great baseball game. I come back to the SMB titles more often than I do with The Show. Beyond its cartoon-y aesthetic is fun, engaging gameplay that is true to the sport. I've played a few hundred hours of SMB2, and this game has already added a bunch of new features that I am happy with. The new ballparks are great, the morning/day/night time settings give each park some extra flair, and the franchise mode has some incredible depth that I am so happy they added.Ever since I wrote my original review, they have addressed just about every problem I had with the game, so major props to Metalhead for that.Things I would like for them to add in the next version of the game (hopefully that is in the works... and most of my points applying to custom teams/seasons/franchise):1. Better practice mode. I'd like a lot more customization over how to practice. Give me the ability to only bat or only pitch. As a batter I would like full control over the kinds of pitches the pitcher can throw. Not just in terms of pitch selection, but pitch location too. As a pitcher/fielder, I would like some control over the types of batted balls occur. Wouldn't it be nice to practice reacting to surprise bunts or ground balls?2. Revert the right fielder throwing ability to first base nerf. Throwing slow runners out from the outfield was fun and didn't even happen super often. Now, it pretty much never happens in normal or deep outfield shifts. Was this change made for realism purposes? This game isn't exactly going for that as a whole anyway!3. Pitchers need to not drop the ball when fielding first base quite as often. This is just a frustrating error to deal with.4. SLIDERS! No, not the pitch! The gameplay weight tweaks like from The Show. If I want to modify a global setting controlling some effect of the AI, that should be there. Injury frequency would be a great use of this setting. I'd like to tone down how often they happened. But what if we could also control how long injured players are injured for? Also how long AI pitchers stay in the game? I've seen starting pitchers get hit for 10+ earned runs in the first 3 inning and still pitch into the 5th. How often would that happen? They'd be pulled after the first 5 or 6 earned runs for sure.5. Flexible amounts of position players/pitchers per team (within reason...). Maybe increasing the number of players per team if I wanted to?6. Managers! Treat them like a player who can be signed for a certain amount of time, but instead of playing the game, they provide certain bonuses/detriments to the team as a whole or changes the playstyle of the team.7. Adding to that last point, player archetypes. The AI all pretty much act the same when pitching or batting, just with the stat variation. What if it were a characteristic of the player to be a patient hitter or an aggressive hitter? Also the batted ball tendency. Pull/push/balanced hitters.8. Here's a big one: Players should be able to evolve over time in their POSITION and the types of PITCHES they throw. God, I wish the game had this so badly.9. Closing pitchers as a position should be removed altogether. Just have it by default as the closer is the best reliever. I have simmed a significant amount of custom seasons, and by far closers are the worst pitchers in terms of ERA anyway, and no I do not think this was because any of them were less skilled than the other types of players. Proof of this is in the works, but this is my observation over dozens of seasons of 162 games.10. Wild Card games. Winner take all. Nuff said.11. Given all of the above points, deeper historical statistics to research players with. I would like to see the tendencies of the other team's batters. OOH! In addition to managers, how about scouting? What if the amount of knowledge you could gain on enemy players was dependent on how good of scouts you have? i.e. the better the scouts, the more accurate information you could have on enemy players. I need flesh this idea out some more, but there could be something there...Anyway, the fact that I am taking the time suggesting all of these improvements is a testament to how much I love and think about this game. So yes, buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This Game is the Best! Not a big fan of Sports games usually stick to strategy games. but I have to say this game is just down right fun. Stuck to the players and teams as is did no customizing. Now I feel like I know the players personally. Traded off a expensive pitcher for much needed short stop. Some of my better players were getting rundown. started tweaking my Line up... and rotating players to rest them... trying to figure out which player development gives you the best bang for your buck...the game is so much more fun than just winning a Game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I have not played any of this series before. I am really having a great time with it.  There is a short learning curve after which you can really pursue exploration of the nuances. I play franchise mode exclusively (after doing exhibitions to learn the mechanics) and have a lot of fun with player development and watching the ebb and flow of the players' performances over the season. In a Summer without any other baseball, this is a satisfying way to fill the void. I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best MP sports games (couch & online) out there.  Very playable, even if you don't know baseball.  But knowing baseball will give you an edge.  Hits the perfect spot between action, fun and simulation.  Plenty of SP options too:  season & franchise modes.  Dev's are responsive to the community and tweak the game regularly.  Well worth the money.  Really wish Metalhead would do "Super Mega Ice Hockey" next,
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually a big "interactive sports" game player because the actual game mechanics to hit, catch, run, etc. are often hard to master on keyboard, and the other aspects of the game (stats, overall standings) don't excite me as much as any single game play, but I found this game very intuitive to play with mouse and keyboard on both offence and defense so the games go so well the season and series are easy to get excited about.   For a casual fan like me there can be challenging crunch moments where all the action is happening at once like a triple play, and you've got a bunch of keypress options available, but the player AI covers for you well if you're slow on the draw and the plays seem to go well.  I am still using the default "aim and click to swing" batting, but hope to graduate to the trickier power hit mouse actions soon so I have another tool for high stakes games.  I highly recommend, it keeps my interest 9 innings at a time (and no, you can't quit mid-game after five innings and come back to it for another four later.  Just like real life, once you start, you're committed...  if you quit, you have to let the CPU compute how you would have done).
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Its pretty fun, the best baseball game I've personally played since MVP Baseball 05, the graphics are really nice compared to the other iterations of this game and the character models are refined and not as wacky as the first game but still maintain a hint of exaggeration.The best part is the absolute customization from top down to the games, to the number of teams, to the players, games, innings, its all up to you and I find this to be a really neat feature.When hitting, the pitches are pretty balanced and its not too difficult to know when to hit or layoff a ball going off the plate, I get a decent amount of walks whereas isn't something that happens too often in other games.The few knocks I have is the learning curve on some of the higher difficulties but I'm getting more adjusted and it isn't that bad once you get a feel for the mechanics but they are a bit challenging.The franchise is a little strict and from what I see you can't trade players which is slightly disappointing because I wanted to get 'Mash Taters' on my team but not play the team he is on. Still in my first season so we'll see how drafting, signing, etc goes. And one other knock that is probably the ONLY thing I really don't like about the game is the fact you don't have a knuckleball which is my favorite pitch and still a little sad they didn't add it, but who knows, DLC maybe? Overall I'm really enjoying this game and am investing a pretty good amount of time and crossing my fingers the devs might eventually add a knuckleball, and maybe a trajectory editor like in MVP 05 if its possible for the game.My score 9.7/10, really fun so far and I see myself adding quite a few more hours in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a fun and enjoyable game. This is my first experience with the SMB franchise. I am pretty impressed with franchise mode.Pros:Specially tailor game difficulty to what is most comfortable to youReplay-ability is highNo two games are the same/ No two franchises are the sameConsTakes a bit to find the "sweet spot" difficultyOverall, great game 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Never before has baseball been so exciting. It blows my mind that this was made by such a small indie team. If you're on the fence about purchasing this because of the price tag, I get it. I was too. However, I guarantee you that you wont regret it. My wife and i have already had hours of fun, and I am sure we will have many more in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game.  If you are the type of person that likes Xcom because you get to create your own squad, and you like baseball, you will like this game.  It's fun to hear the announcer call out their silly names, the stadiums have joke ads all over the place, and their baseball cards add life to the players.  It took me a bit to figure out what settings to play on to get the best simulation experience (about 30 - 35 ego).  The games are quick, and lots of customization.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed this game since it came out. The Franchise Mode is excellent and allows you to budget what players you want to keep long-term and what players you can do without. With the game-play ,the sound is much improved, much better bass and a lot of added features such as the pick-off and wild pitches. There is still a lot to be desired here but it's a firm improvement from #2.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: The greatest game ever and it's not close.  It can be frustrating at times and that is by design.  I have been a fairly hard core video game freak since BEFORE Pacman came out.  ... This game is not for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  Some call it an "Arcade" Baseball game.  This is correct in a way, but extremely deceptive.  This is a Simulation with arcade leanings with regard to presentation.  Forget licenses.  What makes this game great is that it is NOT real teams.  You are NOT comparing Joe Smith computer to Joe Smith last week.  Every player is what they are.  Also, the customization is just wonderful.  I have built around 25 custom teams complete with logo, uniforms and abilities.  ... I recommend this game extremely highly non ADD video gamers who respect old school games but also like the depth and graphics that come with new video games.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Baseball fans and arcade fans delight. I love baseball and american football but don't love the popular games. I don't want a baseball sim...I want updated arcade baseball. This is that. The franchise mode is deep enough but not too much. If you don't care for that you can just play individual games. I think this game is a beauty, inside and out.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game play and the presentation.  As someone who sets up his own leagues and likes to take on the commissioner role, the new Elimination and League options are great.   A few tiny things I would change;  I also love the new parks and the option to play the games under different conditions.1.  Allow the user to play Elimination and Season games in any order they wish instead of having to go in order that they are listed.  2.  Give us the option to set the series length per series instead of all series in elimination mode  having to be the same length.3.  Not 100% sure this is an issue, but give the player the option to set conditions and time of day for league and elimination games as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: After now owning all three Super Mega Baseball games, this one is by far the best baseball game on steam. This is my substitute for playing "The Show" off PS4. For the short time of playing Super Mega Baseball 3 the graphics and player  enhancements are great. The new franchise mode adds a sense of realism to the game like never before and the stadiums? Wow!. I look forward it another Super Mega Baseball game in the future and would totally recommend this game to fill that itch and love for baseball.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, there are some bugs that need to be worked on in CO-OP franchise mode. The game will randomly crash in the 9th inning, party members will be kicked out, and both players will need to restart their games if this happens. BUT this has been the most fun I have had in a CO-OP sports game. More sports games need to have the option of playing on the same team! I love competition, but it is a blast being able to crush Mash Tater together.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Great game and really builds on its SMB2.  My only gripe at this moment is that the developers stated they had worked on who the game chooses to field a ball if there is a ball that two fielders could potentially go for.  I think it is actually worse than SMB2.  There have been numerous instances of balls clearly easier for the outfielder to play than the infielder going out.  As a baseball player, it's always easier for an outfielder to come in than an infielder go out.  Too many times have I had issues with which player should be selected to fielding the ball.  Besides that issue, and I hope they really look at it again, the game is a great and fun baseball sim, with a ton of character.  Maybe let us use all the new teams in pennant races???
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: More of what the first two offered and better imo. Harder for me to hit against the cpu even on low ego settings which i like. Better textures and animations,and a new favorite player,Boomer Plattune! Still missing a couple features again imo, around the horn on groundouts and strikeouts,plus i'd like to be able to have and save replays when i make a cool play or someone takes a ball in the face or the unmentionables. Would like to see some old time style unis gloves etc for this game. And an Ebbets Field like stadium would be cool as well...
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't think this franchise could get any better, but Metalhead surprised me once again!  This game is a ton of fun, and realistic enough to keep me coming back for more.  All of the added feature improvements are excellent, and add to the realism.  The graphics enhancements are great as well.  I love this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Simply Amazing for those that love baseball games but can do without the total simulation of MLB the show series. SMB3 is an amazing arcade style baseball game with quick, fun, challenging games yet can satisfy your sim desires with franchise and season mode as well as online pennant race etc. Couch co op seasons also available here! Full create a team options, trade, sign, release players. Injuries occur, players age out etc. Get this today!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Last baseball game I remember playing was Super Action Baseball on the ColecoVision.  I bought this game for a change of pace from what I usually play.  I don't follow baseball either so not having the flavor of the year MLB players isn't an issue for me and some of the player names are rather amusing.It's fun, on lower ego levels it's friendly to new players, at higher ego levels I get properly owned.  It's frustrating when the computer scores a run off your infield errors and rewarding when you pitch your way out of trouble.  I can't compare to other baseball titles really but overall it's pretty much what I was looking for in a baseball game that's fun and challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: All aspects of a true baseball game are there with an animated atmosphere (think fort nite to PUBG with the show being PUBG). Great game overall would highly recommend until the show makes it to PC. If you're looking to fill that void, this definitely does it albeit in its own way. Quirky but stays true to baseball and a 9/10 in its own right. I wish there was a career mode (think road to the show). Would give a 10/10 if it had some sort of career mode focusing on a user created player. Great as is.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe not the best baseball video game in terms of sheer depth, but definitely the most fun... Franchise mode in SMB3 is better than any other franchise mode in any sports video game from AAA developers (EA,2K, etc.) that I've ever played. I feel so connected to my players,,, its weird, but makes for a fun experience. Price is a little steep but if you're thinking you might enjoy it, your probably will.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Few launch glitches that need to be addressed, for starters framerate dips (even after 3 updates) happen after a completed game (should not happen at 1080p on an RTX 2080ti with a R9 3900X), and the baserunning AI needs to improve.  Baserunners get doubled off FAR too often on line drives, they need to hold and make sure the ball goes through the infield before advancing to the next base; unless they're stealing then getting doubled off makes sense.  Few minor quirks and bugs in Franchise mode, but those aren't related to the core gameplay.Overall, a solid difficult game on higher ego settings and adds some nice changes to SMB2.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: It's clear the people making this knew a thing or two about baseball and worked very hard. The "ego" setting lets you scale the difficulty easily and makes it easy to find the difficulty you want to play the game on or adjust it based on the experience you want at that time. The signing and releasing method is pretty interesting as well. I do wish players in the field other than catchers showed more fatigue. I believe I've played most of them every single game so far and they've never fallen below "fit." All in all a great experience and a very fun game to play
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Super Mega Baseball 3 has so far been my favorite in the series so far. They introduced a Franchise mode which brings a lot more to the game. SMB 1 and 2 were both very bare when in came to modes. However, now there is so much to do. They made quite a few nice changes to the game like the DH and new base running mechanics. Franchise mode has been really enjoyable but there are a few things that should be added. First the off season can be quite boring as it consists of 32 rounds of just signing and releasing players. I would like for them to add a way to progress your players in the off season like a training program. I don't play online at all but I imagine it is as good as the rest of the game. They have made some nice changes from what I hear online. They even added a new mode and it looks fun but I have no friends that play this game. Overall, This game is great. Solid 9/10. There are some things that need to be addressed/added. For instance, Audio sounds are about the same as the ones in the first so I turn my sound allllll the way down to 0. Instant replay would provide some great moments to look back on.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I first played on the free demo. Found out I was totally inept. Decided to buy the game to see if I can be a bit less inept.Still totally inept.Great game and lots of fun.  Beaning a pitcher is a blast...as long as you don't kill him or her.  Pitchers adjust their jock strap or are they scratching their privates?...Oh, they also like to scratch their asses. Never played one or two...Love this one....They do need a home run derby and batting cage for players like me.You will not go wrong buying this  game.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a decent amount of Super Mega Baseball 2, and I have to say that this is pretty much an upgrade to it in almost every way. There are a few additions to this game that I find somewhat questionable, but I mostly enjoy it over 2. It's been a little difficult switching over to the new pitching mechanics for me, same with timing base steals, but it's all for the better in the long term i suppose.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: With each iteration SMB gets more refined as a baseball sim. It is easy to learn and play, yet difficult to master at higher difficulty levels. The ability to customize leagues, teams, and players persists and I can spend hours tinkering with my dream team. Id recommend SMB for hardcore baseball sim fans and casual baseball gamers. P.S. WE WANT HOCKEY!PROZE:Great designEasy to learn to playDeceptively deep baseball simGraphics have been upgradedNew features add even more realismDeep customizationKHANZ:While each iteration of the SMB series gets less "cartoony" graphically, some might assume that the baseball play mechanics are not sound and/or deep.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best non-official baseball game on the market. New Franchise modes and a solid online play experience, plus old favorites in season, elimination, and of course exhibition games means there is plenty to occupy your time. If you're like me and love creation and customization, the team editor is robust for logo and uniform design as well as character tweaking (Renaming, stat changes, etc) for offline play. I'd be lying if I said a significant amount of the time I've played wasn't dedicated to team creation.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Needs a better Franchise Mode.(Ultimately why I returned it)I'm not uniquely interested in baseball, but would love a good sports game where I am able to have a solid custom made franchise.If you're okay with running a team that has nearly no retained players (It has no long year contracts) and also forces you to recycle almost all your players each season. You can not run multiple teams at the same time. They do not maintain stats across seasons only during the season. There is no player draft, there is no hall of fame and they do not even keep track of how many times each team won the world series. (Which hardly really matters as its not like teams keep the same players for season to season anyway.)I would love this game if it were not for those things, particullary not being able to coach multiple teams or an entire league. You can only coach one team. (Which if that's all you care for then it's more geared toward that.)However there's a lot of good. You have a great deal of customization over nearly everything else that is not listed. From team names, icons, logos, player looks, player styles, ratings.If what I've listed here doesn't bug you and you like a arcade style Baseball game then this will be very good for you. However, for me, it needs more customization.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game, better than SMB2 with graphics, and game play. Pick off attempts, realistic base stealing, and more stadiums to play in. And of course, Franchise mode. Only thing I don't like about the game is the frequency of injuring the opposing teams pitcher by line drives. 3 in one game? That needs adjusting. Love everything else though. Would recommend it to everyone, especially those who have played SMB2
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything that's awesome about baseball! I've been enjoying SMB and SMB2 for years now and it feels like this third iteration hits that super sweet spot between arcade and simulation. Really can't express how much I enjoy this game and I cannot wait for custom pennant races this summer! I've already gotten a good group of friends together to start playing 2v2 games with.If you want an epic baseball game with ZERO pay to win (Looking at you EA) then you have come to the right place!I cannot say enough good things about this game!Its been available for about 105 hours now and I've got 45 hours played. Eat, sleep, work and baseball is how I'll be getting through the rest of this year! Hope to see you out there on the field!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Like all the other reviews, THIS IS the baseball game you want!  If you like customization and an arcade feel, this is the game for you!  I love everything about it:  The challenge, team customization, SMB2 team import, leagues, tournaments, I could go on and on, but I'd like to get back to playing!  If you are a baseball fan who fondly remembers Bases Loaded or even Backyard Baseball, this game is like the 2020 new and improved version of those.  Love this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I love this series. Though, I do wish MHS did give prior owners (SMB1/SMB2) a discount. Either way, I think the game has enough content for the full price. Graphics have changed, and I did notice different time of the day games that I don't recall from SMB2 (correct me if I'm wrong). Gameplay is still the same, with a few tweaks that are good/bad. The only thing I don't like is the baserunning controls but it might just be me. Everything else feels like it should, and I think it's a little better than the previous game. I'm glad they brought Franchise mode back, it does make single player a little more enjoyable than just season mode. For what it's worth, this game will get many hours out of me. I love baseball games, and there is honestly no good ones for PC besides this series right here. I love what MHS has brought us, and I hope they explore other sports in their future. Whether you agree or not, SMB3 is a solid game and a must buy if you like baseball and/or played the previous games. 9/10 easily.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game allows you to play online, have a franchise mode, and play exhibition games. This game is great with only one flaw. The franchise system only allows 1 year contracts. There may be an issue with the programming to allow multi year contracts, but that would be also a good challenge for the studio to embark on. If this studio manages to put in multi-year contracts in franchise mode, then I would be much more ecstatic in recommending this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome baseball game. Not too silly, not too realistic. (Some of the player names are amazing lol)Easy to pick up controlsOnly thing I'd like to see added in the future is some sort of 'Superstar Mode' (Think Road to the Show) so I can see a single player's career thruBut now that the devs have mastered the baseball sport, PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE go to hockey, basketball, soccer, anything really.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: i loved super mega baseball 2 on the switch and with super mega baseball 3, getting to play it on pc with the updated graphics and all, i love it even more! The increase in price will be worth it in the end imo as they are supporting the game post release for awhile and taking feedback (and doing it very well i might add!) and honestly the game is already worth it as in its current price.  My favorite feature currently is the ability to watch cpu vs cpu because i love sim games so im currently in the work of making my own teams and league so i can sim it a bunch lol. Super exicted and ready to dump a bunch of hours into this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really like baseball or enjoy watching it in any way. I played baseball for one day when I was maybe 9, got hit in the face with the ball and decided it wasn't for me. However I've really enjoyed every aspect this game so far! I've played a few games and customized a few characters and I'm loving every second!! The controls aren't too difficult to get the hang of but I definitely suggest using a controller instead of a keyboard and mouse. In all this game has redeemed baseball in my eyes and got me more interested in it than ever before! It's worth playing even if your like me with very little interest in the sport itself as this game is just too much fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to say, and love about this game. SMB2 was plagued with issues on PC with stuttering, slow motion, etc after the last few updates. However, the things SMB2 did well, this game does even better. The graphics upgrade is awesome, great looking textures. Love that the hitting and fielding is classic controls with a bit more on the fielding side. Hitting, just as you'd come to expect. There's a challenge to be had with higher egos, but don't kill yourself trying to master it at 100. A great upgrade from the last game, and look forward to seeing if we get any DLC, etc. One piece of feedback would be that there's a new audible "do do do" every now and again (high pitch noise after every contact, etc). It's not awesome, happens a bit too often, and is in the audible range of "sticking out". Would be better if it wasn't there at all, or an option to turn it off? Otherwise, I love this game. As an avid baseball fan, this is a great thing to have on PC!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: I have put well over 200 hundred hours into the previous version between both the xbox and PC.  I have had more good nights with friends playing against PC's celebrating our wins and venting our frustrations.  I love this developer.  They have listened well and every one of our issues were fixed.  The ability to change defenders HUGE improvement.  Steals can happen before the pitch, you can run up the wall.  There is a franchise mode.  If you are looking for the best baseball game out of the MLB sponsored games (and arguably, I think this is better then the show) buy this.  From playing solo, to having some couch coop with a friend, hands down one of my favorite games and this is just an improvement.  Look forward to the next couple hundred hours on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Big upgrade of SMB2.  The lighting effects are much improved, including both day and night games.  The mildly cartoonish players are perfect - better than reality-  and you can customize their looks and abilities to capture the essence of any player.  This game has the potential to be the ultimate baseball time machine, and I am much encouraged by the ballparks included in this edition, which include two traditional designs from the early 20th century.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I'm absolutely loving SMB3. It's got some depth. Franchise mode is a hit. Lots of stuff you can do in regular modes as well. Starting to feel reallllly polished now.I highly recommend this game as there are other baseball games out there that are filled with bugs. This is well polished. So polished they didn't even have a beta this time around.They've made adjustments to pitching, making it a lot more difficult to pitch and hit the marker for power. Really enjoying the pitching. Feels rewarding now.Buy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Pro's- Stayed with the SMB2 look (personally a fan of the look, silly pro, I know but if you compare it to SMB 1 you'd agree)- QoL changes for fielding, editing, overall customization (simplified which has its +/-'s, but still a plus in my book)- Franchise mode! (Signing Free Agents, and forcing you to find creative solutions to make your team more effective!)- Fielding control and switching players improved (Not perfect mind you!)Con's- Would like to see an stadium builder for our franchise teams but hey maybe i'm greedy (Future Update? wink* ;)- No customization to hitting reticle. (Not that I dislike the default but might be nice to see a few other choices or colors)- Very Small con but the baggy option for pants looks awkward and It makes me sad (Okay i'm just being mean now, but someone out there understands) All in all, Metalhead Studios has made SOOO many Positive changes since SMB1, while each game had its con's this series stands out in a market with few choices. Final opinion? If you a baseball fan like myself and missing our beloved pastime, please give this game a chance! Its not MLB the Show and that's a good thing! This game brings back retro gaming in a modern and fun experience for everyone!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Franchise mode looks so much more polished so far in this outing of the game, played the first game and while the gameplay is very much the same I can say it does feel more fluent and enjoyable. First bat at the game and I smash one back at the pitcher making him ragdoll. Customization of teams is also A+, for not having many options of baseball games on PC I am actually surprised this game hasn't popped off but I feel as it is only a matter of time! Keep up the good work Metalhead!
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Everything from the last game (including its DLC), alongside more stadiums, a new mode, improved graphics and a more dynamic camera. I played the last game for literally hundreds of hours, and getting this edition was an absolute no-brainer. They also revised base stealing and a few other rules, making this the most accurate baseball simulation the series has ever had.I'm looking forward to playing for many hundreds of more hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Edit, flipped the review following update 7Still a decent game but changing the terms required to access it over two years after the game was released is a huge issue for me and I'm not going to recommend it anymore on that basis unless they offer refunds to anyone who doesn't agree.  Probably spitting in the wind.Oh boy.Super Mega Baseball 1 was an unpolished gem, in the same sense that MLB The Show is a polished Turd.  SMB 1 was extremely rough around the edges but it was also fun and it captured the essence of baseball as well as any game on the market in its time.  SMB 2 worked to polish that gem and in some ways it succeeded too well.  It was in every sense superior to the first game, a joy to play or just sit with and work on the next team or league structure.  It was so good that it made it more apparent that it hadn't quite reached its potential, it lacked meaningful player progression, any sort of franchise mode, and a lot of fan requested items never made it in.  Well here we are.  Super Mega Baseball 3 takes the thought that the first two games started and carries it to a wonderful place.  There's a franchise mode, there's more customization options (as well as the ability to import your old teams and leagues), there's an optional DH and you can set it per conference.  It's outstanding and it does all this while holding onto the heart and soul of the first 2 games.The strength of this franchise has always been creating tremendous depth in a simple interface and the new franchise mode delivers beautifully.  It doesn't take itself so seriously but it takes itself seriously enough to not ruin immersion.  There's a complex bidding process for free agents behind the scenes that works as well if not better than a formal draft.  Players will experience skill progression or regression between games and seasons, they'll age, decide to test free agency, or retire independent of what you might want for the team.  You have to not only identify good overall stats, but find quality B- and C players to grab on the cheap, and figure out what you're willing to pay for star talent.I adore this game, if it never sees another update I'll be happy with my purchase.That said I do have a wishlist.  It could stand some optimization, some of the stadiums are significantly more choppy than others and I do see some stutter/dropped frames.  Nothing at inopportune times and nothing that harms the game's playability (I am also on an older GPU).  Franchise could use an injured reserve list and I'd like to see a franchise tag feature.  I would also dearly love to be able to customize team budgets to create an unbalanced league or have some sort of fluidity to the budget season to season, based on performance.All that said, I've played the Show for years and this is hands down the superior game, it's easily the best baseball simulation on the market.  An outstanding job from Metalhead on this game.Edit:  I made a guide for new players over on reddit
_childDocuments_.name: Super Mega Baseball 3

_childDocuments_.review: Run up the score in a relaxed slugfest or push the limits of your reflexes in this refined baseball simulator. The third entry in the series features an all-new Franchise mode, major graphical enhancements, and on-field additions including pickoffs and situational player traits.

name: Phantom Abyss
detailed_description: Phantom Abyss is a massive asynchronous multiplayer game that casts players into procedurally-generated temples and tasks them with retrieving the sacred relics hidden within deadly chambers. Intrepid adventurers will dodge scores of hidden traps, leap treacherous chasms, and flee relentless guardians through branching paths until one of the relics are claimed or the devices of death overwhelm them. Be warned, you only get one attempt at each temple and failure or settling for a lesser relic means you will never see that temple again... The cleverest players will use the phantom runs of failed attempts from other players to their advantage and avoid the missteps and mistakes that led to their doom. Once the legendary relic at the bottom of each temple is found, the temple goes away forever and becomes the priceless trophy of the skilled adventurer. Asynchronous Multiplayer Explore the perilous halls and colossal rooms of each temple alongside the phantoms of fallen players that came before you and use their successes and failures to your advantage to progress deeper than they ever could have hoped. Watch and learn from the mistakes of up to 20 phantoms including your Steam friends that have attempted the same temple and steal their whips as they fall. Unlock More Treacherous Floors Recover keys from chests to unlock deeper, deadlier sections of the temple that house more coveted relics. The more difficult a relic is to obtain, the greater the reward - the final Legendary Relic of a temple allows you to claim the whole temple so that it's gone forever. Blessings from the Gods As adventurers venture further into a temple, offerings of collected treasures can be made at altars to gain a new blessing for the rest of the run. Collect as much treasure as you can to please the gods and gain a double jump, glide jump, extended slide, damage protection, and more! Unlockable Whips Unlock new whips with success and choose from your collection before venturing into your next run. Each whips carries a minor blessing but also a curse that may complicate your attempt at riches and glory. Social Connections Players can share Temple Codes for their failed runs allowing friends to attempt the same temple or share their Adventure Code which yields a playlist of temples that a player has attempted in the past.

name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown
detailed_description: The Vale is an audio-based action adventure game that places you in the worn leather boots of a blind adventurer. Features: 5 hours+ gameplay. Specialized 3D audio provide an incredibly immersive game experience Action-adventure with RPG elements: Choose equipment, play-style, magic abilities, companions and quests. Emotionally engaging story, quality sound design and voice performance. Fully blind accessible Headphones recommended for best experience Story: As your elder brother takes his place on the throne, you are made warden of a small castle on the outskirts of the kingdom. Blind from birth and sheltered for much of your childhood, you welcome your exile as a chance for a little adventure. ​ En route to the castle, your convoy is attacked by a huge invading army. You find yourself alone in hostile lands where you must scrape together supplies and seek out allies in hopes of surviving the long, dangerous journey home. The path home follows a dark and winding valley known simply as “The Vale”. It shrouds the land’s darkest secrets including startling truths about your family’s past.
