_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game for my blind daughter to try.  It's very difficult to find audio based games for her, and she is tremendously jealous of her sighted brother as he loves to play video games (as I do!).  I loaded up the game for her, and let her play.  It is 100% accessible from the first menu through the end of the game.  She was completely engaged in both the story and gameplay, and didn't want to stop playing.  Between play sessions, she told us about the characters and what was going on, and she was excited about it.  It took her 8 hours of game time to complete the game, and I'm sure she will go through it again, as she didn't want it to end.  Thanks to the developers for the quality experience, and I hope you think about a sequel or more games like this one!
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I lost my sight a few years ago I have been on the lookout for good games that I am still able to play. Most audio games are light on depth, but this one has a bit of depth to the gameplay. I enjoyed the story and the voice acting and sound design were good. Hopefully there will be a sequel or just more blind accessible games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing this game I felt compelled to write a review.Have you ever wondered what it would be like being blind? What it truly entails? This game gives you a glimpse in what life would be like being blind. The concept is unique; You play as a blind woman traversing a medieval world. As you are playing a blind woman, you literally stare at a black screen (with coloured lights to reflect the type of environment that you are in) for a few hours.The feat accomplished here is not small; the players engagement entirely depends on the voice acting, and the story being told. The vale does this masterfully. The vale has an incredible sound design, which makes you feel immersed in the world that it is presenting itself to you. The game made it a point to make sure the player understands that while being blind is limiting, you are in no way helpless. Everyone relies on somebody, and this is no different in the game.Movement relies on the sound stage (hence the recommendation of headphones). You navigate the world purely based on sound. This can be a fun, but also perhaps a terrifying experience. Since you have no visual on anything, you literally only have sound to go by. This is also reflected by the main characters state when things unbeknownst to her are happening; she can only infer based on sound. This also applies to the combat in the game. Based on directional sound, the player needs to either block or attack at the right time based on sound cues. This makes for a very fun (albeit sometimes hard) experience to survive combat encounters (based on the difficulty setting).I really recommend you try out this game, its an experiance in and of itself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Played and streamed it for nearly two hours, it's really addictive. I'm severally blind and i can't wait to get back on and play more. A great step in the right direction for accessibility for all.just the descriptions and surround sound alone make the scenes come alive. Visually impaired or not, you'd enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely play with headphones.I use corrective lenses, contacts and glasses.  When I take them off, I cannot see any words on my computer screen, have limited depth perception, and cannot tell objects apart unless their colours are dynamically distinct from their surroundings, I played and streamed a bit of this without any corrective lenses and it felt absolutely wonderful.  Worn glasses since 8 years old with gradually deteriorating eyesight ever since.  So corrective lenses have always been my normal, but when I played this game, even streamed it, I was comfortable and entirely engaged.  Even the little "stars" (just dots but to me they looked like stars) of colours that I could see without my lenses were a pleasant touch because they gave me to option to see something if I wanted to.  To rely on hearing more was so satisfying for the combat and is an aspect that is easy to take for granted in just about every other game.  I remember telling my friend when he was playing a jump rope challenge FFIX to closes his eyes and listen for the sound cue because that would be more accurate than his vision.  We enjoy sound in stereo for movies and audio books and tv shows, why not for games too?  The story is very engaging and the voice actors they found for it we very well done.  I forgot I was streaming while I played this game. Even the voice for the menu screens was pleasant and didn't sound out of place with the dynamic of the story so I could remain in the story world even when I had to bring up stats menu or main menu screens.I was not expecting the quests I got.  It made the world in which the story takes place come alive as not all of them are part of the main story.  It would have been just fine if the developers just made a story and had you just play that as a nice adventure tale.  But they took time to make a world with people who have wants, needs, greed, desires, all walks of life and the actors add many details that helped all of that build and come together in my mind's eye.What's the most satisfying feeling for me, though? I get sick usually playing first person games.  The camera motions make me queasy.  This is the first game I have been able to say I can play first person. And honestly, that's enough to make me cry for joy.So, yes, get this game, Try this game...but most of all, tell people that this game and this developer exists.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Play with a good headset and close your eyes. The immersion and game experience will be far better than with open eyes and normal loudspeakers.This is a very unique game, since you experience the whole game from the eyes of a blind woman, meaning you won't see anything. So you will rely on your hearing and orientate and fight through audio cues. The cast delivers an awesome job in bringing the characters to life and I always wanted to know how the story continues. While this game won't be for everyone, I had 6 hours of fun (time didnt count in steam somehow) and can attest, that not only blind gamers will like this one.For the negative points: I played the game in 30 minutes bursts, because after that time I had to pause. I'm not used to keeping my eyes closed all the time and the additional mental load on my brain for navigating all the time just by ears was tiring me. As a seeing person, I also had bigger problems of navigating by ear and making a mental map of the areas. I nearly always just walked directly towards the audio source, but couldn`t  learn the layout of the areas. But those points didn`t diminish the fun I had, so I would advice you to try this game out. If it's not for you, you can always return it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: It’s like Kingdom Come Deliverance if Henry was blind.I like to think that behind the black screen and floating dots, there's actually an in-game engine with amazing graphicsThis is one of the best video games I've ever played, and I finished it with my eyes closed. The Vale is an audio-based game that is best played with headphones. The only graphics are floating colored spheres that don't help you so you might as well just close your eyes. But this is not just a glorified audio book. It's an actual game. The game uses audio cues and directional sound to direct you to attack and block in one of three directions. It sounds simple but the combat actually gets more complex as it unfolds with hunting with bows and arrow, a little magic, parrying, heavy attacks, interrupting attacks, etc. It was just so cool to close your eyes and listen to the direction of the enemies and block and attack. It was so incredibly unique. The audio aspect gave me some Hellblade vibes.  I chose to play on the hardest difficulty. It was challenging at times but totally fair and it made the combat and the game even more immersive.You play as a blind female protagonist who is led by a guide in a fantasy realm where enemies are after her. The devs created an incredible female protagonist and it was really cool to have no video as it put you in the shoes of the protagonist as she is blind and can only respond to the sounds of her environment as well. It was a massive step up in terms of immersion. The main story and voice acting were really high quality and I really enjoyed how it all unfolded at the end. The entirely verbal story felt surprisingly intimate. It was an all-around beautiful experience. There are even side quests in the game that had a unique way of being unlocked and played. You follow sounds in a town square, are prompted later to press a button to start the quest, and then you travel to a self contained area to complete the quest. You might be traveling and come across an inn with shops nearby. You’ll hear the sound of sword smiths working on swords, the banging of steel. Walk towards that if you wanna buy and sell gear there. You might hear chickens in the distance which will tell you it’s a spot you can buy food and stuff. You can go inside inns and take on side quests. I had one quest where you had to find treasure behind a waterfall. Well you and your companion search for said waterfall and you’ll hear it in the distance. The game is also fully accessible to visually impaired as all the menus are voiced like the inventory menu. It's a pretty great thing that someone who is visually impaired cannot only relate to the protagonist but can also fully play a video game.I feel like a lot of people write it off pretty quick because you’re blind in game and see nothing, but it’s so much more than that. The story is good. It’s an RPG at heart. The combat is actually engaging and makes you focus and listen carefully. I never had a game tell you and show you so much without having anything on screen. It was such a unique experience to, well, experience something simply by only sounds. I had to pay attention to the things I would normally not even notice consciously.  It was definitely weird at first, I was totally looking for visualy but got used to it after a bit. I loved the ending too, I somehow did not expect that. I have to say, that even despite the negatives and the drawbacks outlined by some, I think this game deserves a standing ovation for really trying something new and being very innovative, and I sincerely hope more of this type of thing becomes a thing. While I'm not blind, nor do I know anyone who is (that would be likely to play video games), I just love that this was made.Don't let this gem pass you by. It's an incredibly unique twist on video games the likes you’ve probably never experienced before. Probably the easiest 10 I have ever given because it was so unique and immersive.Seeing the average reviews on by people who never gave it a chance though, no wonder the triple A gaming industry is in such a sh*t place right now. For these people if it isn't the new yearly Call of Duty or FIFA shovelware, it's trash.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This graphics-less “audio game” works pretty intuitively, and it's deeper than I initially expected. It plays like Punch-Out with stealth and RPG elements. Some combat functions are finicky--blocking, even when inputted early, often lets the first attack of a combo go through, and hunting with a bow demands more precision than I can personally manage with audio alone. But blind combat is otherwise a satisfying (and steep) challenge.The real star of the show is the dialogue, which feels surprisingly organic and intimate. Tightly written, beautifully voice acted, and weaved into the mechanics, it fits the game like a glove. I don't want to spoil anything other than the fact that the dialogue caught me off-guard.I love medieval fantasy settings and character-driven stories. The Vale offers both in a way I’ve never seen before. It’s weird, it’s different, and it’s unforgettable. My experience playing The Vale was novel not just because it lacked visuals but also because its characters were intensely human. I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: The Vale caught my interest as it is a completely audio-based game, something I have never encountered thus far.It's comparable to an audio drama, expect for the added agency you have via the gameplay, which is surprisingly fun with various elements that switch it up every now and then. It, together with the excellent sound design and voice acting, made for an immersive, unique experience I would very much like to see more developers test around with. The in-game menus can be navigated by audio only, but are of course also visible. Headphones are a must as you need to differentiate between the directions sounds are coming from in combat.The only thing I would have liked is just... more. I loved Alex's story, the people she met along the way, as well as the RPG mechanics. But it really is quite short, so be aware of that. To conclude, I'm glad I stumbled upon this game and I hope other developers pick up on its ideas and the potential it has, for accessibility's sake and for pushing the medium itself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to explain in words just how special this game is, but I can try.The Vale is, quite simply, marvelous. In this game, you play as a blind princess in a medieval fantasy world filled with monsters, bandits, and soldiers trying to kill you. Yes, this game is designed to be played without vision, but make no mistake, that's not a gimmick here. This is a full, complete game, with a rich world, RPG elements, side quests, branching paths, moral choices, the works. If anything, removing the visuals opens up an entirely new style of play that I've never had the chance to experience before. You are listening for every footstep and sword swing, using your ears to guide you through the experience. It's intensely gratifying and rewarding, and it's backed up by the best sound design in the business. The Vale places you into a vivid and lush world, and because you need to really focus on hearing everything around you, it feels like you're really there. It says something that the most immersive game I've played in years has no visuals.The Vale includes a surprisingly complex combat system, with enough depth and choice to satisfy a wide variety of playstyles. Stealth and ranged combat are both options, as well as magic, and different methods of hand-to-hand combat. Throw in a few incredible boss fights and a bunch of different enemy types, each with their own attack pattern, and you got a recipe that will please any fan of action.Of course, the real highlight in my mind is the story. All the characters here are wonderfully fleshed out, carried by some spectacular voice acting and great chemistry. The plot is filled with enough intrigue and twists to keep me not only interested but invested. I admit, there were a handful of moments where I did tear up a bit. And, not to get into spoilers, but The Vale sticks the landing with a satisfying ending.If you're put off by the concept of playing an action RPG with no visuals, trust me, you do not want to miss this. Rather than detracting, it adds an entirely new dimension to a formula that had been getting stale for some time. The Vale is the kind of game that sticks with you long after you're done with it. If anything, it's worth it just to support a developer doing great work on making games accessible. Go on this journey. You won't come out the same way.Oh, and it should go without saying, but you're gonna want a good pair of headphones for this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this game promoted on Axios, really liked the idea of playing as a blind hero. Have been playing for an hour and a half and combat is a lot more interesting than I thought. Play this blindfolded (I used a sleeping mask) and with over the ear headphones or a surround system, I don't believe it can be enjoyed with cheap computer speakers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: A classic well-written story about a blind princess' journey through a country under invasion.This is a game that is played by following the sound queues, it is fully sound-based and everything is voiced, all the menus and options included. Fully accessible for people with visual impairments and is a worthy experience for anybody else.The sound engine is quite simplistic, especially compared to other games with strong superiour sound work (example - Hunt: Showdown), but it is serviceable.So is combat - serviceable. Enemies attack from three sides with audio cues (some of them are harder to decode than others), each enemy type has different patterns of attacks (there are 5 types of enemies, some vary their patterns, some have a gimmick). You have 2 types of attacks, directional block, stamina management (no stam bar) and a couple of extra abilities. The voice work is well-produced and well-written, despite the fantasy tropes, The music is ok, so are the visuals - you get some if you wanna look at your screen.The whole game can be completed in about 5 hours.While being nothing special as a fighting marvel, it is a game that tries and, in my opinion, prevails at a goal of making a uniquely accessible game. Considering it's made by a small team, The Vale is a gem of a journey.Worth buying, playing and supporting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I am not visually impaired in any way. Before playing this game I'd never really considered how the visually impaired may be locked out of my favorite hobby. So if you're looking to expand your perception of the world, look no further.Aside from the above, The Vale manages to retain many of the trappings of a good RPG, all while maintaining a unique game experience that can be played entirely with your eyes closed.I highly recommend checking out The Vale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sighted person and I greatly enjoy the game! The navigation is easy with every major point in a town making some kind of distinctive noise. The battle system is creative with different strategies you can use, reacting to the acustic clues the enemies make. The quest system is nicely solved by entering a tavern, navigating through available quests and instantly teleporting to the place where you need to be.This is well made and I hope the developers come up with more creative ideas to make other genres available for blind people.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: What a cool concept! This game obviously lends itself to a strong narrative focus, but still has action-y bits to keep things interesting. I feel like I was really well eased into the whole "Learning to play without seeing" thing, with the tutorial being spaced out as new concepts got introduced. It even seems like background noise is pretty minimal early on, but as you get used to the game, picks up a bit. So even just hearing the right thing is a challenge that levels up as you go.Loved the story, and the voice acting (And menu narration) was phenomenal. Wasn't really necessary, but I played blindfolded just so I could get the full experience of going through menus while being guided by a voice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This can only be described as a masterpiece. everything sounds, and even feels, real.To new players, a magical medieval world of adventure, wonders, and even some horrors, is within this game.You only need to close your eyes.Sidenote- this is, like, the only game of it's kind. I am surprised that I did not notice that fact sooner. (edit: I have found more. a lot more "Audiogames". The Vale opened up my world in that regard)Sidenote(2)- We need more of these games.Also, some extra details on gameplay (this'll be a long one, so just play the game! why are you still here?!): the game is (at least) 3-4 hours long for a run-thru, and it's fairly replay-able. There are things you won't find in one run alone, but by the end of the first run you are going to want to set the game to "hard mode" for a challenge (or if you want to gloat to everyone and anyone like me). As I said before, in different words, the story is BEAUTIFUL and you will NEVER get tired of it (don't you dare disagree, I've ran this 5 times and I know what I'm doing XD) no matter how many times you repeat it. In so many words: just buy the game and hear it's tale, and know you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute experience this was. One of the most unique and amazing games I've ever played.For that sweet immersion, I suggest putting on your best pair of headphones, a blindfold (and try not to peek), and definitely no eating/chewing while playing bc being able to hear the audio is super important!!Give me part 2. Now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I loved The Vale!! I actually put on a blindfold to play so I could focus on the sounds. Great story line! I don't want to give too much away here but I wish there was more. What happens next? The game ended and it felt like a big power up. Game one we face the enemy horde and game two we face the Fae...just a suggestion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game.A truly unique experience.The sound design, music, and voice acting really shine and allow one to be immersed in this game.The game mechanics are simple, but even so the game manages to set interesting challenges.The story is very good and full of emotion.Whether you are a visually impaired person or not, this game is a unique experience and 100% recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get this out of the way immediately, this game is fantastic.It is an audiogame similar in some respect to the game A Blind Legend with added layers of RPG.You play the female protagonist who is blind. As she goes along you are taught how to use the sword and board along with bow and arrow and magic. All this with no need to use your eyes, just your ears.Earn money by completing quests, earn or buy better gear.Full text to speech on all menus and fantastic audio all round.Multiple skill levels.Acheivements.All in all this is the best audiogame I have played and I wholeheartedly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very enjoyable game. [10/10] I would recomend this to anyone and even try to convince people to try it. The story is interesting and well written.Please translate the game to other languages! I'd love to get my family/friends to expierience this in german so they can understand.I can't confirm what the few negative reviews I saw here said. I try to give my thoughts on the points those brought up. It is part of the Story to lose sometimes, don't be deterred by that. Someone criticized that you can't set different sound levels for SFX/Dialog/etc. - imho that is not a flaw, that is done on purpose because the mixture of different sounds is an important gameplay element. Someone said in combat gameplay is a mess and I disagree strongly - yes it gets confusing at times and that is what it should be or better has to be. You need to learn to listen properly first, then you can get good at combat in this game. You are supposed to be disoriented in some situations - you are playing as a blind person afterall and that is part of the experience.Play this game! :D Have a nice day!
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: The Vale allows you to explore a fantasy adventure through your sense of hearing alone, as you make your way back to the kingdom of your birth meeting interesting characters along the way. While on your journey you complete various side quests, hunting, fighting, delving into dungeons - all guided by an accessible interaction system that builds in complexity over time. The voice acting and sound design is well considered throughout and with good headphones you can really concentrate on what is happening and feel immersed in the world that comes alive in your mind.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game with an amazing story. You play as a princess who gets lost in the land far away from the city. A shepherd helps you find your way back to the castle and on your way there you chose to help people, ignore them, or fight them. It's worth the money for how great it is. You can play it even if you're blind so make sure you have headphones since it relies heavily on sound.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to leave a negative review here, because this game is a very cool attempt at something both artistically new and morally correct. I mean, hey, removing the video part from video games? Making a game completely without a visual aspect, which also doubles as making it accessible to blind people? What's not to be intrigued by in this proposition?The problem with The Vale is simple. It's just not very good of a game. It's ingenuity ends at the concept. To back this opinion let me bring up some statistics: ~80% of people have killed the first enemy, ~50% have completed the first side quest, ~25% have completely finished the tutorial, and only ~15% have beaten the game. Considering the game's rather short - 6-10 hours - that's a pretty rapid dropoff rate, don't you think? Oh, but you could say that this is because playing as a blind person is probably not very fun for most people. That might be true, and indeed, it could be the reason for those low stats. To me, however, playing while blind was actually by far the best part of the game. I even played blindfolded, so that my brain would completely shut off the "seeing" functionality. Having my mind construct the world purely on the soundscape and how it changes was  quite something.So how does it play? During fighting, you press arrow keys to attack an enemy that is standing in a given direction. Which direction? Use your ears. The enemy might block, so it's possible you'll have to attack when they're getting ready to strike themselves. Or block and counter. Sometimes you'll even have to face multiple enemies at once; headphones absolutely necessary.Now that sounds pretty sweet, doesn't it? That's the thing. It gets boring pretty fast.And this is arguably the biggest issue with the game. You fight quite a bit, and yet fighting simply doesn't feel good. I mean; I can confidently say the devs juiced it up as much as possible. The slash sounds, the footsteps, the grunts and screams, all top notch. But I feel like the format itself is just... not that fun. You also get to walk around a bit. That's much more interesting, having to navigate purely based on sound. It's a lot more fun than it sounds, and noticing the sounds spicing up your idea of the world is also quite amazing. Sadly, again: once the novelty runs out it just becomes... flat.There's also some system of managing weapons and inventory. Navigating the menus is not fun as well, probably because you have to hear the explanation of what options are there and how to choose between them. I feel like this part could've been done better, but how? Using shortcuts maybe? I'm not going to lie, I wouldn't know how to make a good game in which you can't see a thing. This is definitely a noble attempt, and we need more of those - if nothing else, so that one eventually gets it right and creates a completely new way to include lots of previously excluded people in the world of video games.All my complaints... for blind people this is probably normal, in which case I'm really sorry. I'll never take my sight for granted, and I hope that one day technology allows you to perceive the world the way we, seeing folk, do. Or at least to give us a game that both groups of people can enjoy just the same. This one is probably not it, even if it's arguably worth playing just to understand how the world looks like to those who can't see.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: A unique game that definitely deserves more recognition.Playing as the blind Princess Alex, you are desperate to get to safety. The only handicap is that you can not see anything and must rely on your hearing to see you to safety. The audio for the game is absolutely incredible and crisp, the orbs/fireflies you see throughout the game are rather hypnotic too.The game is best played with headphones!
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: As a non-native english listener with problems to understand voices (even, in a lesser extent, in my native language), that game is really hard to enjoy because of the absence of subtitles.Listening to dialogs without having any text support always led me to fatigue and miscomprehension. This is the same here.It seems like a very interesting experience, but as I played the few first minutes of the game, i'm not sure i can say how many different people talked, nor who they are despite some titles and links were dropped.What i understood was that there was someone (who smell very bad) that i needed to punish for leaving some king near a cliff while playing a game of some sort. Based on description and reviews, i'm far enough from the real plot to not wanting to go back to that game.Subtitles would greatly help, but doesn't exists.Note that, if you are fluent, it shouldn't be hard, so you should definitively try that game. I'm just bad at understanding voices.I'm quite frustrated by my inhability.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: A great time! Made me realize how hard most other games lean on eye candy to gloss over mediocrity on so many other fronts.Only caveat I can think of is, make sure you have a good set of headphones. The archery does require some good hand-ear coordination, which would be difficult without stereo sound.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique experience. A true test of game design and narrative design mastery. And I think that devs passed the test well!Plus, I want to note the performance of the voice actors. If you're reading this and thinking whether you should play it or not, hear me out.It's mostly a linear, but still great fantasy story. The gameplay is not that sophisticated, but it's entertaining enough.But the main thing is that there are no games like that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: My only complaint about this beautiful game is its length...I want more!!! I was impressed by The Vale's narrative, pacing, and worldbuilding. As a sighted person, I also loved the empathy generated by the blind perspective of the main character, and how much agency she has. Hey dev team: I beg of you, please make a sequel or ten.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible experience, with no visuals throughout aside from the necessary menus, which are all beautifully narrated, and the wonderfully done visual ambience that works both as a way to orient ones self for those who can see, but also add to the environment, by falling like rain or snow, or rising like embers. Yet despite the lack of more complex visuals, I don't think the game loses a single thing compared to even large titles. The story and world are deeply immersive in a way that's incredibly unique, that may be even more immersive than the most polished visuals, as it makes you see the world in your mind. That alone to me feels worthwhile, even if just for the new focus on a sense considered secondary for most people. The game-play itself is intuitive and enjoyable, simple at its core, yet provides a challenge, and take both focus and practice to master. It is truely unlike any other game I've played in the most amazing way. The story itself isn't long, even with all the side quests along the way, but it is packed with emotional moments, wonder, and good twists that only serve to deepen the story. It's, some of the most incredible representation, both for the disabled community, as well as women in both a form of media, and in a genre that sorely lacks stories focused on women as people.I look forward to future works in this style, especially if its more in this world that they created, and just like the hero of its story, this game can take on giants, despite of, or because of its differences.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: At the very least I have to recommend this as I'm not sure I've played anything like it, nor do I expect to again in the future. It's not some exceptional experience that is above all games or something. It's an intimate leap into bounds of the lives of other real people, and done tastefully so.When I got The Vale I thought it would be just a novelty accessibility game for the blind. It certainly fits that category, but I got a little more than that. I am sighted, so I used a blindfold/darkness and played with a keyboard and mouse. Surround sound headphones are pretty much obligatory, since essentially every gimmick relies on your ability to detect the directions of sounds in the environment and combat.You play a blind princess in a medieval setting. Most of this is pretty cliche, but some characters add some personality to pull you along the narrative enough to stay interested. Being purely audio, the voice acting and music is pretty good, as you could expect. I also felt like the directional aspects of the surround sound were very accurate and played well to the main designs around this concept.I do think that the plot thickens and twists near its abrupt end, which is a shame. It took me around 10 hours to complete, but it felt like it could have been summed up better in another hour or two of more deliberately unraveling some of the story's complexities instead of oversimplifying its resolution.  The game follows a pattern where you go from destination to destination as a "base" in which you find a few quests/town interactions where you must rely on sound to avoid hazards and attack/defend in combat. You get a bow, heavy or light weapon, armor, and shield to upgrade over time in a linear fashion. I don't see why someone would play and not do all of the few quests in each town, so you're never out of money and there is not much choice there. This system could have been expanded slightly, I think. You also gain an ability later on that can affect different aspects of combat that has different ways of being upgraded, as well as forks in the story that you do choose to change, albeit with the same ultimate destination.The uniqueness of gameplay of The Vale is enough to try, and its quality for being developed by such a small group is admirable and impressive. I definitely recommend it for any PC gamer who wants something different, and, of course, for those without sight, I cannot speak to how this experience would be for them, but I think it would still be fun and challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long time gamer and someone who has seen pretty much everything when it comes to RPGs so imagine my surprise when I found something that offers a unique gaming experience! While this is an RPG, it's also in a category of its own in terms of mechanics and that's hard to do in this day and age.Whether you're blind or sighted the game has a lot to offer, it tests your ability to perceive the world through sound alone (use a headset!) Your success of failure depends on your ability to recognise the direction and distance of different sounds and respond accordingly.The story line is compelling and while it may not be up there with the giants of the RPG industry, it's strong and enhanced by quality voice acting. I care about the main character and feel connected to the companions. The story also has a way of teaching you the mechanics of the game without the need for a tutorial which is really nice.The management / customisation / inventory side of things is basic but this isn't necessarily a bad thing.I'd be happy to see more games in this genre, it certainly feels like there's a lot of potential in this style of RPG.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This game's unique take on accessibility and ability to put you in the shoes of a fully visually impaired protagonist is probably the most immersive video game experience I've had to date. I played most of the game in bed with a pair of headphones, a controller, and a pillow draped over my eyes to act as a blindfold. Full text to speech in all the menus was a welcome feature and one that I greatly appreciate the devs thinking of. The audioscapes are great, with excellent sound design and just the right amount of challenge to keep me forging ahead through the captivating storyline. Combat is easy to pick up with several tutorials at different points in the story. There was never a point where I felt overwhelmed with the different audio cues, although the difficulty does climb gradually as you learn to navigate your way through increasingly complex environments and battles. Alex is a fantastic protagonist and at no point in the story does she ever feel anything less than a capable, independent badass.I wholeheartedly recommend this game for anyone who likes good stories, unique mechanics, immersive games and a challenge that's unlike any other game I can think of. I hope this inspires a whole genre of audio-games and I'm looking forward to seeing how this genre of gaming evolves.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game. What it does, it does extremely well, especially the audio and story. Original too. It is not cutting any corners for its setup. Gameplay length is about 5-7 hours and that is perfect for what it is. It is great for visually impaired and regular gamers who like RPGs.Tip: Difficulty can be adjusted at any time, so you can play on hard and then adjust it where necessary if you would want to keep it challenging, but not overly difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique games for me to play. it is very easy to grasp the mechanics as the game guides you through them one after the other. I generally struggle with seeing in some games which hinders my ability to enjoy the experience. However, this one was very engaging to the point where I felt entranced without having to worry about not seeing something or straining my eyes. I love the story, the effort put into the audio, and the advocacy aspect behind the game. Highly recommended for a nice, engaging, and exciting experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: E: I've now finished the game. I liked it a lot. I'm not too good with words, so I'll leave it at that.PS: This game was also very relaxing and felt smooth to play.PPS: Headset/headphones & two functional ears required!My first 100 minutes were great. Very immersive- I just turned of all the lights, my screen, and removed my glasses.A few bumps with the borders of the scenes. Stumbling about. I wish  sounds were a bit louder - there's a bit of a difference when you hear people yelling in front of you in villages/towns and then entering dialogue with them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game I wasn't sure if I was going to like it. After playing the game for 5 hours straight and completing it, it left me wanting more (in a good way). This made me realize how interesting video games can be with only sound and no visuals. I would love there to be more games like this one.Games like this provide blind people an immersive way to enjoy video games and gives others a new way of playing video games. Amazing job well done.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Besides the obvious novelty of an audio only experience, the game mechanics do stand on their own as a worthy challenge. I recommend playing on hard mode, because you will certainly be put through your paces. You can choose different combat styles right away, slow and methodical, or high risk, high reward. There are branching paths, which also function as optional difficulty spikes. There's a large ambush that you aren't meant to survive, but you can defeat it if you really want to. You are just about able to do it, as long as you don't make more than 2 mistakes. My main concern was that the novelty of this game would wear of, and that the combat wouldn't be interesting. So I'm writing this review to let others know that the combat mechanics are good. The hard mode is actually hard.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I get frequent migraines from focusing my eyes especially on screens & being able to rest my eyes while i play this game has been amazing. I can't read books anymore due to the strain reading has on my eyes & audio books don't capture my attention well enough to be enjoyable, but this game has enabled me to enjoy & immerse myself in a great story again without any pain. The voice acting is fantastic, the soundscapes are very immersive, i absolutely loved the story, & the combat was very fun! My only complaint about this game is that it isn't longer. I just finished the game on normal difficulty after almost 8 hours & I'm now looking forward to my next play through on the hardest difficulty!
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very unique title and I will start this review by applauding the concept!If more games like this gets developed and expanded upon, I'll be slightly less panicked by the thought of loosing my sight one day..But I think there are things to improve on:I feel like the difficulty is too low at first; those super slow charge-up roars, like every enemy is doing a Frostie's commercial, it felt almost condescending. Of course, later on, when a thousand things are happening at once, they're a welcome variety, but I feel like they should learn pretty quickly to not use such an over-telegraphed attack? But maybe that's just a necessary narrative compromise for the game to exist, like the fact that we're never attacked from behind...But I'm not blind, so I've been playing all these other games with a variety of telegraphing-difficulty - so I don't know that it's a fair comparison against a blind person, whom I assume this game is meant for??I just feel like the sound design could be made sharper, I guess. More distinct sounds and less clutter.I'm really glad I'm not blind though, when purchasing items in this game! Going through the stats on gear, with my eyes closed, is a merciless process at first, trying to remember all the details..I also find it tedious to listen to the narrator's help comments every time I need to choose quests or being told how to accept whatever, using my spacebar - being blind is not equal to being imbecile, I CAN remember simple functions. So maybe wait a little longer before reminding me of the same mechanics, over and over again? Or establish a help button to press when needed. I mean, when speech and sound are the only things the player relies on, maybe avoid wearing me down with them..On the other hand, if I zoned out during a side-quest briefing, I'm screwed, since there's no way to have them repeat the issue at hand..The baker fight was super difficult, mainly because the kid does this fireball combo from each side in very quick succession (how that works, I've no clue! I can clearly hear him growl to my far right, how does he hit my left side, without moving??), which, in order to block, you have to know that the shield actually lingers in a position even though you've started blocking the other direction. This took me many attempts to figure out, since there's no lesson to be taught about it. I really feel like it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanic, compared to the rest of the game!Some narrative stuff; Shepherd being pessimistic about every side-quest I wanna do, felt kinda bad. The achievements completely disagrees with him, at least, and even though the story might have a reason for him to have been like this in the end, I feel like I have to decide against the narrative to explore and see everything the game offers. It rubbed me the wrong way..I think it's awkward if games like this can only be about the player character being blind. It's an obvious story, and they handled it well, but I'm sure this doesn't have to be the case in a game like this. - just a thought..Last little thing; I didn't care for the pop-piano filler in the beginning - it felt really out of place compared to the rest of the soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such an incredible experience, the story is spectacular and intriguing, the gameplay is really fun and can be challenging at times. The only sad part is that I really wanted to play more, the game is a little short. That being said the game is really creative and unlike anything i've seen before (pun intended) and  I highly recommend it if you like great stories and trying out new things.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know where to begin with this; incredible doesn't even begin to describe it. Buy the game right now, twenty dollars is nothing for this exquisite masterpiece as not only is it a downright amazing game but it also supports an incredibly niche group of developers creating games for the sensory impaired.The gameplay is varied and in depth, there is more than combat and combat itself is nuanced and tactical. The world in the 5-8 hours you may be in it feel alive and the characters are more emotive and real then any other game I've ever played; never before have I shed tears for the tutorial narrator. I have never felt true helplessness or doubt while playing a game; I've always known that it was something that I could just quit out of, but with my eyes closed and Shepard and my ears my only guides and what felt like a hopeless situation ahead, I felt true dread.I don't know how many other ways I can say this: buy this game, now!
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played a game like this before and I can almost guarantee you haven't either. A full-fledged RPG conveyed entirely through sound alone, The Vale makes excellent use of audio to engage you in a mix of exploration, battles, stealth, and conversation like any other game of its genre but in ways you've never experienced before. The story is a tightly executed adventure with the supernatural and political intrigue meshed together as you are thrust into the midst of a brewing war that will decide the fate of multiple kingdoms.Not just a novelty, it's a genuinely solid game that is fun to play. I'd recommend only getting it if you have a decent pair of headphones though, positional audio cues are key to the gameplay and being able to make them out isn't really optional.

_childDocuments_.review: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown is probably one of the best audio adventures I've played in a while.The voice acting, atmosphere, and gameplay are well done. You play as a young blind princess trying to make her way across a kingdom being invaded as her journey to her new home on the outskirts of this kingdom is cut short. Make choices, complete side quests, buy equipment, and enjoy an interesting story that can last 5+ hours. All menus are read out loud, and it is easy to navigate the world and while similar to other audio games, combat feels good. Would LOVE to see more like this game in future, maybe another story in the same universe even! Would be interested in learning more about things you find out about later in the story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: The Vale could quite conceivably be played with your monitor turned off as every element of the menus and interface is spoken along with clear instructions of what buttons you should be pressing.  But an accessible UI is just the beginning.  How do you make a 5+ hour adventure/RPG engaging and entertaining with absolutely no conventional graphics?  It’s well known that when one of your senses stops functioning the others will compensate, and in this case it’s all about the audio.So the game starts off with you, a young girl, traveling by wagon to your new castle on the outskirts of a kingdom now under rule by your brother, the new king.  Blinded at birth, you can only hear the creaking of the wagon and the plodding of hooves until your wagon is stopped by a guard who says they are under attack from an invading army and you should flee at once.  Again, everything is voice and sound effects only with nothing more than dust motes swirling around the screen; purely artistic with no relevance to the actual game, nothing to give sighted gamers an unfair advantage.From this moment you are on your own as you must complete the long and perilous journey home through the winding valley known as The Vale.  In true RPG fashion you’ll need to equip yourself with a weapon; a variety of weapons in fact along with magical abilities and the occasional companion to aid you on several quests while always relying on your most powerful ability…your hearing.  Your ability to identify and locate danger through audio alone is something quite unique.  Hearing a growling wolf is one thing but listening to the subtle changes in that growl to nail the perfect timing of your attack is another.  At first you’ll likely being swinging your stick around wildly, much like any newly blind person would, but once you settle down and learn to listen you can actually start to enjoy the engaging combat system that will slowly rise in difficulty as you learn to mix light and heavy attacks with perfectly timed counters and even learn to fire a bow.  You’ll eventually face off against multiple enemies at once, learn to listen for archery fire, and even traverse some surprisingly terrifying stealth sections.  The sinister audio in these moments really sparks the darkest parts of your imagination.Read the full review at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: If you want an action packed fighter, this is not one for you. No visuals except from the glowing dots floating around.If that did not scare you away I could not recommend this game more. It is entirely new and fresh, and I found the story and game design to be very good. There are some forced moments here and there where it felt a bit unnatural, but I could enjoy the game even with the overly simple structure and the restriction that all enemies and challenges are navigable by sound.More than anything, however, I appreciated the experience to play a game without relying on my eyes for once. Losing one of my most relied on senses made the experience all the better and all the more inclusive. It is so nice to see games made available for those with a handicap or missing function.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I was sceptical at first but the game pulls you in from the very first moment. Play it with headphones and controller. _childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: PS I personally know the developers and play tested for bugs. I have played more hours outside of SteamAccessible  Audio Game for the visually impaired and/or blind or sightedMy favourite aspect of The Vale is the character, story and voice acting. Character personality is portrayed perfectly through voice acting and it is very easy to imagine what they may look like. Dialogue is organic and engaging. I really enjoyed the characters' journeyPlayed with xbox one controller for PC. Avoids X/Y/A/B buttons, Right and left triggers are used as accept and decline in menus, left and right stick are used for movement and look direction during locomotion and shield and sword during combat respectively. 3 difficulties (casual, normal, hard). Bosses can be deceptively difficult and combat is very aurally engaging. Highly recommended to play with headphones. I have played with speakers on either side of my desk before due to aux port issues; it's not impossible but much harder to face in the proper directions.Absolutely recommended for anyone to play. Sighted or not, first gaming experience or not

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:I loved the game.It's an experience of you being in a story with some lovable characters.There was a decent amount of lore that was hinted at. You don't know exactly why everything happened at the end of the game, but in a way that makes you want a sequel. The combat mechanic was fun and a good challenge at times.When you fail in combat, it fits the story and doesn't feel like your trying the same level over and over again.It hit me in the feels a couple of times. Here are the cons I can think of:I wasn't a huge fan of using the bow. It seemed a bit unpolished, but it's not too important to the game.No chapter select feature. This makes it really time consuming if you want to go back for achievements because you have to do another play-through.Most choices in the game were "do this or don't do this." You don't get a lot of freedom to define your character. I would have loved to see the ability for your character to choose how she ends the story, but you just get a brief "This is how it happened" at the end. But again, this is part of the idea that you're a character living in a story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: You're blind. And honestly aside from shopping for stats, you don't need your eyes. Recommend you to have a pair of headphones for this game. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time in The Vale.  The story was great-  far far better than it had to be. _childDocuments_.review: Amazing game from beginning to the end. Highly recommend playing the whole game with your eyes closed. I first saw this game during the demos and loved the concept, and having finished the game I can the mechanics of having a sound only game is amazing. Though the mechanics are simpler than other sword fighting games, the fact that you have to listen to subtle sounds of armor shifting to track enemies and react in a melee where the chaos of battle in the background is a real problem. The entire experience makes the fights more intimate, you are listening to clues to see how the fight is going (damaged enemies make more pained sounds when attacking, and fresh enemies taunt you when you flail wildly). I would love to see this expanded even further since there could be so much more that can be done with an audio only combat system.In terms of story, the overall journey is pretty similar to other hero's quests, the underlying story of some otherworldly influence does add a layer of complexity. I think the story is carried by the supreme voice acting of the main characters, especially the lead. _childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game out of curiosity. It'd be real easy for this game to coast on it's novelty, but it goes above and beyond what I expected. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a sighted person and got bored of the usual visual games. I've tried every imaginable genre, VR games as well as non-VR, text based games as well as more immersive graphical ones. I thought nothing in the gaming world could surprise. Until I heard about the Vale and decided to give it a try. I was blown away. I find it such a rewarding challenge to rely on hearing instead of vision to navigate a gaming. I was afraid that as a sighted person who relies on vision too much it would be overwhelming, but I found it surprisingly simple and intuitive. The devs did a really good job with the sound design that closely mimics real life experience. And the ambient sounds and immersive feel of it all just blew me away.Definitely play this with headphones. Also if you are sighted consider using a blindfold. There are minimalist graphics- little dots that shift left or right to show you which way you are turning or turn blue during the nighttime, also a convenient map of the world you are exploring- but they aren't important. You'll want to concentrate on what you are hearing as much as you can and to do that it is best if you are blindfolded. The story is compelling. The voice acting is phenomenal. And the sound design is pretty out of this world. The combat is a lot of fun and progressively gets more challenging. And there's tons of stuff to do with all kinds of quests to do to earn coin and upgrade your gear.Playing this games is like reading a book: your minds fills in all the blanks and creates and colors the world you are experiencing through your hearing. Since most games- with all their visuals- rarely leave anything to your imagination, this game is a refreshing change of pace and reminds me of my childhood when I skipped school just to read the latest Harry Potter book, mind full with students in cloaks cursing each other and zooming around on broomsticks.This game is a truly unique experience and has gotten me excited for a new gaming experience for the first time in a while. I would recommend it to anyone who wants a unique, compelling challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great experience for anybody who likes games that are unique. It's completely blind accessible, and plays very smoothly. I will say, I do wish a few of the audio cues for attacks were a little more distinguished to better paint a picture of what was going on, but it was a great experience nonetheless. There's partical effects to help orient yourself for those too attached to visuals to function. But, you don't need those by any means to play through the whole game. In fact, I deliberately blindfolded myself to give it that extra realism. Once you get the combat figured out, you'll start to feel like a badass. Strongly recommend to blind folks and anybody looking for something different.

_childDocuments_.review: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown is a groundbreaking audio game that sets a new standard for interactive storytelling, especially for the blind community. As a visually impaired gamer, I was immediately drawn into the immersive world of The Vale, where the story of Alexandra Denholm unfolds with a richness and depth that is rarely seen, or rather, heard in gaming.The game's narrative is compelling and deeply personal, resonating with me on many levels. Alexandra Denholm's journey is one of courage, resilience, and discovery, and it was a joy to experience her story. The interaction feels so natural and intuitive that I was completely engrossed, making choices and navigating through the game world with ease.One of the standout aspects of The Vale is the character of Abdul Rashid, also known as Shepherd. Shepherd is not just a guide; he is a mentor, a protector, and a friend to Alexandra. His wisdom and experience provide Alexandra with the strength and knowledge she needs to navigate her perilous journey. Shepherd’s calm and reassuring presence is a constant source of support, and his deep, resonant voice adds a layer of authenticity to his character. Through his eyes, Alexandra—and by extension, the player—learns to "see" the world in a new way, relying on sounds, smells, and tactile sensations.Shepherd's backstory and his own journey parallel Alexandra's in many ways. He, too, has faced loss and adversity, and his journey of redemption and service adds depth to his character. The dynamic between Shepherd and Alexandra is beautifully crafted, with moments of tension, humor, and heartfelt connection. Their relationship evolves naturally over the course of the game, from one of necessity to genuine friendship and mutual respect.Alexandra Denholm, the game's protagonist, is a character of remarkable depth and complexity. Despite her noble birth, she is thrust into a world that requires her to rely on her wits and inner strength. Alexandra's determination and bravery are inspiring, and her development throughout the game is both believable and compelling. She is not a passive character; her choices and actions drive the story forward, making her an active participant in her own fate.The developers deserve high praise for their innovative approach and dedication to accessibility. The voice acting in The Vale is exceptional, bringing each character to life with authenticity and emotion. Every voice actor delivered a stellar performance, enhancing the overall immersion and making the story even more engaging.In conclusion, The Vale: Shadow of the Crown is a must-play for anyone who appreciates a well-crafted story and values accessibility in gaming. It is a remarkable achievement that showcases the power of audio storytelling, and I cannot wait to see what future chapters hold for Alexandra Denholm and Shepherd. Great work to the entire development team and voice actors for creating such an unforgettable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game on a saving sound sale. I have to say it is amazing. I haven't experienced such a great 3D stereo experience. Many AAA games have been doing trash for sound effects lately. The game play is based somewhat similar to "For Honor" with the 3 directions attack/defense. It your not familiar left, center, right. Really engaging. Other missions include navigating mazes of different sorts with deadly hazards. Hearing gravel fall as you near a precipice is amazing when you can't see and actually fear for your character.The voice acting and story is very well done. It is for the most part scripted. The only thing I would say this game could do better was light attacks while blocking and just more game. There is a combat ring event side quest. I would have liked it more developed as well as the hunting one. My favorite battle was a melee ranged exchange with a rival seer. I wish I could have fought that in the combat side quest as well. Easy a great purchase.
