_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful work of art! Voice acting is marvellous and the plot is captivating. The gameplay is pretty decent too, albeit somewhat repetitive - most of the time you either block or swing a sword in one of three directions, but there are also hunting missions with a bow, and stealth/exploration sections where you need to carefully navigate the environment. Would love to see a continuation, either in some neighbouring genre or with more depth/variety to the gameplay.This game could use just a bit more polish however, for example:1. No support for multiple saves. You can't really "die" in this game, but trying out different plot paths is difficult.2. Unskippable plot scenes. While technically there is some replayability, I would imagine sitting through every dialogue (as great as they are) just to try a different choice two thirds into the game will get old pretty fast.3. The player and shop inventory is both narrated and displayed as text, which is great, but player's coin amount is only narrated but not displayed - what's up with that?...
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Tis game was innovating! The controls, the sounds, the decorating visuals, the in-game screen reader...This game had to win  the innovation in accessibility award instead of Forza. Sign language was never more effective than subtitles imo.You better play this blindfolded, as you'll stick with your character a lot more and it'll also help you to focus on the sounds better.Definitely worth the try, play it, now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: The Vale is a bit of a rough gem, but fortunately it's worth is greater than the sum of its parts.First off, this game is a pretty novel experience, relying entirely on the soundscape to drive its narrative, game play and action elements. For me, it's like playing a good "Choice of... " game (a series of choose your own adventure e-gamebooks) in that the minimalist graphics allow the player to invest in their imagination, which can bring the world more to life than some other standard games do. It also reminds me a bit of "Unheard", in that the player needs to focus intently on the soundscape for clues, again drawing the player further into the experience. For that alone, it's worth experiencing at least once.The game isn't perfect, of course. The combat, while polished and enjoyable, can start to feel a bit repetitive towards the end of the game. Combat does have it's fun points, especially where you are presented new types of foes, having to listen to totally new audio cues, as well as adapt to new behaviour patterns. It's a pity that these weren't done more in the game. The bulk of combat eventually simplifies into a pattern of waiting to block, strike back, abandon combo strikes if needed to block multiple opponents, repeat. Despite the juicy options of throwing heavy strikes and casting magic, ultimately this is the dull but most effective way to proceed. There were also missed opportunities for the combat system to shine. For example, if the player could execute timed rhythm combo attacks, or precisely timed perfect blocks at the moment of an opponent's strike (in the style of Death's Gambit), that would entice and challenge players to play more skillfully and take more risks. Magic is, likewise, a bit lackluster. Despite how much the game emphasizes your character's skill in magic, magic basically boils down to one AoE and one critical chance modifier, both of which end up not changing the routine combat pattern at all. Again there is a missed opportunity here to do creative stuff like raise a rock wall to protect one side (a character was shown to be able to bring down a mountain avalanche), cast darkness or blinding light (so that, as a seasoned blind fighter, you gain a huge upper hand as your opponents flail blindly), an adrenaline rush type skill to remove endurance drain, or some kind of super sensory focus to filter out distracting background noises (the chaos of the soundscape in a full on melee fight between armies at the end part of the game was terrifying and exhilarating at the same time). These are merely ideas that feed directly into the game's combat system, and already they are much more varied than what the game has.Story-wise, the game is ok. This is more of an audio book and less of an RPG, in that there are very few times you get to make a decision in the game, and these decisions basically boil down to taking path A over B, with the only consequence being fighting different groups of enemies. The story doesn't change. There's also no time limit or consequences to side quests, so the logical thing to do is to take on all side quests. It would have been nice to have certain side quests conflict with each other, or have lasting tangible consequences. Over time you stop paying attention to your companion's pleas to think about your own safety too, which doesn't help with story immersion.Despite these imperfections, the game is great to experience at least once, and still highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: As a sighted person, this game was a complete delight! I played it fully blind folded and feel completely into the world and thoroughly enjoyed my 6+hrs of game time to complete the whole story. The mechanics are something I could see expanded upon further which is really exciting, but they were just beginning to wear on me by the end. They were simple and effective, so I'd be excited to see how they could be expanded upon in a sequel, if it is ever on the cards.The voice acting and sound design were, as expected, top notch and worked really well in tandem with the gameplay. The design challenge of making a game for the visually impaired is something very intriguing to ponder and also makes me very aware of how fortunate I am to be in the position I'm in. It's awesome to see a game advertised to this group of people (even if it might be small and not the money making market that many games attempt to tap into).
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing work! I am not visually impaired but I am highly nearsighted, so I can totally appreciate the idea of creating a game that relies only on hearing. Playing this game with my eyes closed makes has brought me an unprecedented immersive experience. I paid attention to NPC's accent and ambient sound, and fill the void with my imagination. The latter half of the plot is very interesting, especially the vision. However, I think the ending was a bit hasty. Actually I really hope to see Alex claim the throne lol.What I particularly like is that the story is set in a medieval society of gender equality. Looking forward to more female player character game!PS. If subtitles or repeat playback is available, it will be easier for non-native English speakers like me to understand the plot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game with an incredible story and simple mechanics that build on each other in brilliant ways and are taught in a wonderful one. Frankly. this game was entirely worth the money I spent on it and I cannot recommend it enough.Even with the game being built on audio and sound cues, there is still a wonderful atmosphere built with the simplest effects. You won't just be staring at a blank screen the entire time.If you do play it, don't feel limited to the one path. You're not on any strict time limit and what you find and face is up to you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. As a sighted person, I simply close my eyes to play, and they do such a good job worldbuilding with sounds and characters that my brain has no problem painting the world automatically. The combat is fun and engaging, quests are pretty fun and full of well-voiced dialog. Would happily recommend to anyone who wants a fun RPG experience! Oh and my name's Alex so it really feels like they're talking to me throughout the game! haha
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game! I played it while recovering from laser surgery for my eyes, so I couldn't do much, but I wanted to play video games. So I got this game beforehand and man, what a good buy.The game is really fun to play, interesting mechanics and usage of sound cues. Very well done sound design, and the story is interesting although cliche.Loved it. Felt like a real adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful little game with a very unique mechanic. The story is simple but effective, and the gameplay is very innovative, relying mostly on you hearing in which direction the ennemies are coming. The blindness mechanic works extremely well and really makes you use your imagination to picture the world.The game is really good and short but it doesn't overstay its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I originally bought this thinking "we should support projects like this" but not sure if I'd play it. When I got around to it, it was a really wonderful experience. I found this a perfect fit for the Steam Deck with good bluetooth ear buds, and I played it at night either in a dark room or in bed, like an interactive audio book. I always kept my eyes shut, imagining the scenes around me, which are quite varied and immerse you in 3D sound.... well, 2D I guess since I don't think there's much above and below you, but plenty in front, left, right etc., and with a lot of fun side quests.Combat is interesting and a bit overwhelming; I was fine against one enemy but had to mostly dial it down to  ("") after losing the multi-enemy fights about twenty times each on  difficulty. I think I never really got to grips with that and would have liked some sort of save system where I could now replay at least some of the game and retry the fights after finishing the game once. I think the repeated combat is how I turned "5.5 hrs play time" into my 11 hrs.Aside from the lack of save points (which might be too hard to do with audio-only) I'd personally have liked a bit more narration to move it  more toward an interactive audio book. I never got tired of hearing the wonderful lady say "Falling Squirrel and Creative Bytes present..." (by the way that's not a spoiler, there are  in the game although there is ).Like other reviewers, I wish there were more games like this, It's a genre I'd keep going back to. Thank you, developers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. It's a short narrative experience with deeper mechanics then you would first think. Take about 7-9h to play and is best played with headphones, gamepad and closed eyes. It is a game the is unlike any other as such it execute on it's intension perfectly. Absolutely recommend to try it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely underrated. I don't know if actual blind people can play it, probably due to lack of experience with gaming in general, but while playing this game I was wearing a blindfold myself, and I knew exactly everything that was going on due to the sound design, which is so well made. It actually feels like I am there, all the sounds and noises around me and the very detailed stepping and people speaking in my ears. The combat is specially made in order to convey everything that is going on, and it does so very clearly. I so am glad I've played this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellently rendered audiogame. It has a diverse cast of characters and a fairly diverse cast of actors. Furthermore, it would not be too difficult for someone to pick up and play, even if that person has never played audiogames before. The combats are stationery, but there are also realtime walkabout sections as well. The choices while playing are a little limited, but in general, they are meaningful to the story. Other than some simple "where should we go" style choices, you are also in charge of what weapon, shield, and armor you wear. There are honest tradeoffs here: will you be a slow, heavily armored fighter who bashes through everything? Will you be a lightly armed flash who sneaks about and attacks with speed? The story won't change very much from playthrough to playthrough, but your choices do effect the style of combat you take, the risks you take, and some of the interactions you have. Overall, it's a well done game that, while a little shorter than I'd like, offers hours of entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: The game was a fun experience, my advice is to play with an eye-mask/a blind-fold if you are sighted, it helps to get more immersed and to listen to the audio queues.The story, while pretty simple was enjoyable, and the gameplay was fun.The game is entirely in first person, and works by sections: you travel to a village and have stealth/combat/story moments during this travel.Then you arrive to a village, and have a number of sidequests to do and equipment to buy.There are two different gameplay sequences:- The ones where you are moving your character while locating yourself with sound cues, these can be stealth sections, more action oriented, or when you are moving around in a village- The ones where you are fighting, you will have to fight using your ears in front/on the left/on the right. Your character doesn't move during these sections and everything is done with the two sticks (on xbox controller).A few critics:- It didn't happen often, but there was two times where the auto-save system made me miss side-quests because I didn't understand it would make the game go to the next "chapter". Most of the time you can cancel a side-quest and go back to it later.- Some game mechanics where not very clear even after the tutorial, and it took me some time to understand them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Audio based RPG. i love it and I don't even like RPG.The fighting kept evolving which opened up for some new strategies for battling, Being able to freely walk around in the villages and find your way by walking towards specifick sounds was a cool touch. The story was creative and kept my interest and the characters were easy to connect with. It took me about 6 hours to play through and I tried to play through all quests but I must have missed some since I didn't get the award.If this is your first audio game and you are on the fence I recommend to try out the demo. That's what I did. Would've been nice if the save from the demo was carried over to the full game, but I can't really complain since most games out there on Steam don't even have demos.I also recommend to checkout Blind Drive, It's the only other audio game I have finished so far but both were good. I will continue to explore more games in my newly found genre of audio only.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I am not one to write a review, and this game is very short (12 hours played, including "deaths").  However, this is one game I can absolutely 100% recommend people give a try (especially us old gamers that are looking for something to scratch that itch that modern games just can't scratch).  It's unique to say the same, but the mechanics are very similar to old school games where the boss flashes before attacking.  You'll have the added bonus that you can claim that you can beat a game with your eyes literally closed (like I did, lol).
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game and find the fact i can play it with my eyes closed both unique and enjoyable.  The mechanics are easy to pick up and the story engaging.  You cant see much of anything so its a bit disordinating at first.  If your curious about the game just try the demo, and developers please make more in this vein.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely fantastic. It's designed to be played without visuals so all of the effort went into execution and the devs created something amazing. The story is very well written, I was immediately invested in the characters; This was greatly helped by the STELLAR voice acting and atmospheric music. I suppose it goes without saying that a game designed to be played with your ears is going to have good audio, but you never really recognize good voice acting until you've played a game like this where it shines so brightly that other games just can't compare anymore.I picked this up because I thought it was an interesting gimmick but now I'm just well-satisfied having played such a cool, unique, and well made game. Devs like this who put their heart into making truly quality content for people who can't engage with mainstream media deserve all the love.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: The Vale is an awesome game. I’m not blind, but it was a great experience, and actually exactly what i was searching for. I don’t like very stressful games, so it was incredible here to play laying on my bed like I was sleeping. The story is quite short but interesting and very good told (I mean i was crying when she was crying). I really want more games like this, it’s absolutely my type of game and I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Looking at the store page, this might seem like a gimmick game with no substance. A one-trick pony where it just plays around with a few things related to blindness and then ends.This is not the case. The Vale is a fully featured RPG with a better story than some AAA games can conjure. Intense moments, mechanics with actual depth, likable characters with good voice acting, and a system that you can actually be good at.The Vale is absolutely worth the pricetag, and worth considering if you're just looking for a good RPG to play through even if you don't consider its unique accessibility. Like the people it was made for, The Vale is not defined by its disability, but it's strengths.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a must buy for someone that wants a great relaxing game, There are visuals but mostly for menus and weapon stats but you get so much more out of the game by playing it blindfolded or with your eyes closed, you really get a sense of what the developer was going for.Great game would recommendEdit: Just completed the game, absolutely brilliant game some of the dialogue was very emotional and thought provoking the Dev's did a brilliant job
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: - This is the happiest I've ever been with the voice acting in a game.- The story is great, and got me invested in the world.- The audio is well designed and extremely immersive.- The mechanics are fun, and the combat was enjoyable.If you are a fan of RPGs and are down to try out an audio-only game, this is a must play. _childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a welcome, little, audio-only adventure RPG. Even if a little underdeveloped and not blooming to full potential, I still recommend playing it just for the very rare experience of a well made audio-only game. 8/10. Add a point if you're visually impaired...The combat is simplistic sort of waiting-out & reflex type of minigame relying on audio cues to figure out what button to press, but it's working and a quite refreshing change. Given the short game length of < 10 hrs it doesn't have much chance to get tiring, but doesn't have enough depth to sustain a longer title. You have a little bit of freedom roaming through village centers following audio cues to points of interest. Although it all seems to be awfully similar and predictable nearing the end of the game. The game features a very simple equipment&gear system, where you can buy better weapons and armor, but frankly it's superficial and doesn't add much to the experience.While the game has a couple of twists, there's nothing groundbreaking. Expect a little bit of medieval fantasy with an underdeveloped lore of a "Fey realm" squabbles. Some side quests feel tacked on living up to their name, not having much consequence on the world or having a lot of exposition. That's the price you pay for playing an RPG game with such a short playtime.You don't have any dialogue trees in this game, however you may still be grasping at straws if your English is not very good, as the characters speak in very strong accents making it sometimes hard to decipher what are they saying. Sadly this game doesn't have subtitles to help you with that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very different experience. You can't see anything and you have to rely on sound to do anything. The game hinges on sound design, and it knocks it out of the park. The sound of water rushing, the way chainmetal rubs against itself as its owner moves, music of the tavern growing warmer with every step you take. Put on a sleeping mask or a blindfold, and you can feel yourself inside this sightless world.But this would've worn its welcome if not for the game's engaging story, and it kept excited to discover what lies ahead, completely integrating the protagonists's blindness into the narrative, and doesn't overstay it's welcome.It's a very good game, and I'm certain it's very enjoyable for people regardless of their vision.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Superbly unique in concept,  stood out to me as a very interesting title. I was so intrigued and curious, in fact, that I ended up buying the game, installing it, and started playing it all in the very same evening. As someone who's normally got an exceedingly long process from discovery of a title to sitting down and playing it, this is unheard of. Happily, I was not let down. It was interesting to explore how this type of game differs from more typical games, as well as how playing video games might be experienced by sight-impaired individuals. I almost exclusively played through the game wearing a blindfold, although that is not necessary.Gameplay-wise, the controls can take some time to get used to, but feel satisfying once one pulls them off. The difficulty is too uneven, especially comparing early and late game (I played on normal), spiking somewhere along the way. The different types of weapons seem at first to suggest that experimenting with different combat strategies is encouraged, but the actual fights one ends up in often require one strategy over any other, and so there is little room for experimentation in practice. In several towns the smith has also only got one weapon for sale, further locking one out from experimentation. The magic mechanic seems largely pointless: you unlock the ability not long before the end, and so there are few opportunities to use it, explore it, and level it up. (I don't know the extent to which any of these things apply to any of the other difficulties than normal.)At times it was difficult to keep up with what was going on, making me confused as to what was happening, or had just happened. For example, at one point I had to infer after the fact that someone had probably succumbed in the confrontation I had just lived through. It could very well be argued that this is just how it is for people who rely in most part on their hearing for outside information, however.The story seems simple at first, but is nevertheless enjoyable. However, it abruptly gets rather involving towards the end, and I couldn't help but feel more invested. It would've been nice to have that happen earlier, and not shortly before it is all over.The sound design is magnificent, though it needs to be for this kind of game to work well. Paired with the nice voice work and 3D audio, it certainly makes for an immersive world, which has a massive impact on the enjoyment of a game like this.What I enjoyed perhaps most of all was learning to take in information to make my decisions based on sound, instead of sight, by relying on audio cues to determine where the enemy is, and how they will attack. That certainly makes for a positively unique experience, and I am sure to come back for more. 7-/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This game, were do I even start.This Game had me crying, the mechanics are amazing, the fighting works well (even with bad headphones) and the story had me feel all emotions, happyness, anger, sadness etc..I tried to guess what the story is about from what you hear in the first part, i tried to guess plotpoints, I could only guess 1 of many parts in the story. The story is easy to follow and just a masterpice with trust and decision making.This game will have a place in my heart for sure, I only wish you would hear a bit more of what happens at the end, to your friends, the citys and the people you helped.If you can speak english, buy it, you will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: The Vale was one of the best RPGs I have played in recent memory. Its unique style of replacing visuals with a purely sound-based experience is extremely refreshing in an ocean of other titles which follow the same formula time and again. In terms of mechanics, the use of directional sound has you sneaking past enemies, aiming a bow towards the source of a noise, and blocking and trading blows with enemies from different directions. You learn to listen out for the creak of armour as an enemy changes position, the rush of footsteps as they charge towards you, arrows whistling through the air towards you. It truly is an experience like no other. For these systems to work the best it is highly recommended to use a quality pair of headphones so you can get a full sense of the directional sound, and a controller makes combat thoroughly enjoyable and gripping.These systems are carried through by a strong narrative and decent world building, with characters showing satisfying depth and quality through stellar voice acting. In short, just get the dang game :P
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: A must experience type of game. I am not blind but I did blindfold myself after pressing start game on steam and it only enhanced the game for me. Sooooo worth the 20 dollars.  It is like a playable audiobook and for someone who cant look at screens for long it is perfect. Honestly, just wish there was more to this game, sequel, dlc, anything. I would play the hell out of it. A truly amazing experience. 9.9/10 (only because there wasnt more to play)
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Let's put it this way... It was so good that I'm sad I rushed my first playthrough, and will be going through more times to experience everything the game has to offer. _childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: I was dubious at first, because you can't see anything in game and it seemed silly to play something with your eyes closed, but the reviews were so positive, I found myself curious enough to try it.This game is actually quite incredible. The story and voice acting is amazing, and I found myself drawn in from the very beginning. The biggest surprise came from the fact that the gameplay was actually very fun! I enjoyed myself from start to finish. There's a very reasonable learning curve, and it was never too difficult (or too easy) thanks to just the right amount of tutorial sprinkled throughout what was going on.The plot was intriguing, and it kept developing the further I went along. The characters are all unique and grow on you over time and make you care. Even the side quests never feel dull or like a waste of time.I used a sleep mask over my eyes and played with headphones and a controller, and the immersion was completely worth it. This was a truly unique experience, and I would absolutely purchase a sequel if one ever came out. Don't even wait for a sale -- this game is worth full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really unique experience and thoughtfully designed around its concept. The voice acting and sound design are top notch as you might hope for in an audio-centered game. The script is very well written and, as someone not super into the fantasy genre, engaging and memorable without becoming overwhelmingly trope-y and the length feels just right. The quests, tutorials, and dialogue scenes are thoughtfully cut into short segments and the gameplay is kept simple in all regards, almost too simple at times although it would likely become confusing with much more going on (and in a few scenes it can overload you a bit with audio information). Combat is basically a slightly more complex whack-a-mole but it is quite impressive that it works as well as it does.I find this to be a nice compliment to a game like Return of the Obra Dinn that is also about listening carefully but in a more puzzle focused way, in contrast to the action adventure focus in this, and while Obra Dinn has a distinct visual style as well, this offers a complete immersive audio experience that by the end had really engaged my imagination in a way I've not experienced in a game before (but have in narrative podcasts).
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Really interesting game that manages to pull off exactly what it wanted to be. Since the whole game is portrayed in audio they leaned in so much on its quality, it is bafflingly good! The cues, the backgrounds, the story, and best of all the characters are done at the highest level of quality. Love it all! If you want to try something new and be more immersed in a video game than you ever have, get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: OK so at the time of writing my review I've only played for about 2 hours and dam this is really funthe voice acting, music, and sound design is spot on. its easy to get immersed into the game and just fully embrase that your character is blindand the gameplay is simple but rewarding you really do have to pay attention or youll be overwhelmed when dealing with more than 1 enemy

_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Not a very long but memorable game, first time I played an audio only game and i must say its is really great and relaxing, it's like listening to an audiobook I played while in bed in the dark and it was really immersive. _childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: A wholly unique video game experience that is playable entirely without the need of vision. Great voice acting and sound effects all around. I am very interested in Radio Theater and this game is fascinating as a concept.The Vale is also surprisingly strong narratively, and the choice to make the main character blind makes perfect sense. A lot of the audio devices/narrative tricks used to describe flashbacks, and death/respawns are really smart. Example: If she dies in battle, it sounds like she passes out, only to wake up suddenly, saying she had a premonition of the threat ahead (it was only a dream when she died), and the game then offers you a choice to try that again or go a different way, because of your foreknowledge.Cons: The gameplay is fairly limited, due to the constraints of the medium. At its best, it feels like a proof of concept of what could be an entire genre of games. If something like Oculus Rift were leveraged, it would greatly improve the game by allowing you to turn your head towards sounds and swing your arms. The greatest weakness of The Vale is that stereo sound can only offer so much, and the developers chose to only present sounds in front of and to either side of the player, never behind (because behind sound exactly like in front). Even so, what the game manages to offer is surprisingly engaging considering it is entirely audio based. This is an rpg complete with movement, combat, and equipment management all done without any visuals at all. All menus can also be navigated without sight.If you want a very unique and interesting concept for a video game, and especially if you have any interest in games accessible for vision impaired people, definitely check this game out.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely wonderful and unique experience! At first I thought it would be weird playing the game with my eyes closed, but I came to enjoy it quite a bit. I highly recommend playing with headphones and a controller and you definitely should be playing with your eyes closed.The voice acting and sound quality is some of the best I have heard. Which is a must for a game where that is all you have to go by. The combat is easy to learn but thrilling to do. Standing in darkness, knowing you are surrounded by people who want to kill you, listening to the creaking of armor or the splash of water. The game manages to draw you into the moment and feel the panic.The cast is very well written and the protagonist is a prime example of a strong female character. Definitely one of the most enjoyable games I have played in a long time and I can't recommend it enough!Only complaint is the lack of save slots so I can show it off to my friends.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: It is a weird sensation to play a game with your eyes closed. The concept doesn't work perfectly, overlapping sounds are a problem when trying to discern the direction of attacks and the scope obviously had to be limited and adjusted to not just have thousands of RPG menues that need to be read out one by one. As a whole it works surprisingly well, though. The immersion achieved by just relying on your hearing in detailed soundscapes is pretty impressive. And while the story and world are standard medieval fantasy, the characters really shine through good writing and emotional performances. I really liked the concise side quest structure, offering self contained vignettes that get straight to the point and can offer variety in setting more easily due to the lack of visuals needed to build unique spaces. Another surprise was the combat system, which has an unexpected depth to it, adding new mechanics constantly throughout the 6 hour experience, while still remaining accessible and simple. This is an interesting counterpart to Before Your Eyes this year and I recommend checking this out just for the novelty of the interaction, it is definitely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun as hell! As the desc says, it's from the POV of a blind knight as she fights off bandits, cruel warriors, supernatural horrors, the usual fantasy stuff. Only get it if you have good headphones or earbuds, it relies almost entirely on directional hearing!EDIT: I have now finished the game, and if I could give multiple positive reviews, I would. This story ripped absolute ass, and even though it only lasted me about 8 hours, I have a feeling it'll stick with me for a long time!

_childDocuments_.review: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown, or The Vale, is an action adventure game from Falling Squirrel and Creative Bytes studios.You play as Alex, a blind princess sent to a distant castle in her brother’s kingdom. After surviving an invading army’s surprise attack, you need to find your way back to safety while learning about the world, the war and your place in both.The Vale is uniquely experienced only via audio. Its only visuals are particle effects indicating motion, weather, and time of day. The game even reads the menus aloud, presumably allowing people with visual disabilities to enjoy the game without aid.Much of The Vale relies on the player deducing directions and distances using only sound. For example, enemy combatants telegraph upcoming attacks with yells, allowing you to raise a shield or time counterattacks in that direction. Evading enemy camps may require listening for their crackling fires or banter. Good headphones help, as does enabling any 3D or directional audio enhancement. The Vale executes well. Most challenges are intuitive or quickly learned. You return to the challenge’s start if you fail, sometimes with a short hint. However, discerning multiple incoming attacks while using your abilities can be tricky in the more complex fights. Communicating setting and dialog solely via voice can be slow. However, The Vale‘s script is tight. Descriptions are vivid and concise, and I never got bored or frustrated waiting for dialog. The choices of accents and voice acting are brilliant, immediately identifying the speaker. The story is similarly tight and has many twists and reveals. Flashbacks teach skills and build relationships. “Flash forwards” unexpectedly show incorrect paths.Removing visuals also awakens the player’s imagination. Like reading a novel, you wonder what characters and scenes look like based on accents and the occasional brief but lucid description.The Vale makes you realize how visuals dominate games. Even for games that use stylized or simplified graphics, simple things like art and animation dominate the language used to describe them.The Vale also reinforces that game accessibility is not about reducing the difficulty. Accessibility is about reimagining and redesigning game interaction and content. That said, The Vale is still niche. Visuals are more effective at quickly communicating information and adding emotional context than sound. Using sound for feedback means the game cannot have a soundtrack. The Vale will not dethrone any AAA games from the top sellers’ charts.The Vale is also short, requiring about eight hours to complete, including all side quests. The game introduces ideas, uses them a few times then moves on to the next ones.The Vale succeeds as a game, experiment and tech demo, and it will appeal to those looking for something unusual, those with visual impairments or students of game design.Hopefully, these ideas spread and are enhanced or included in other games. Imagine the same techniques applied to imaginative, story-rich, graphics-lite games like Disco Elysium or Planescape: Torment.Originally appeared at .

_childDocuments_.review: The Vale is clearly the love child of a very small, but dedicated team of developers. _childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: Very highly recommend to try it out. The sound design is fantastic (as you would expect from a game which is entirely audio) and the combat is a good challenge. i found the difficulty curve very interesting, it less based on enemy health and damage and more based on quantity and amount of background noise, you start of mostly fighting 1 enemy at a time in a quiet forest but as you go you eventually end up fighting multiple enemies at once whilst listening out for arrows being fired at you all being drowned out by the sound of other nearby combat or the splashing of water. The stealth sections take on an almost horror game feel as you try and sneak between multiple patches of terrible sounds which at some points can feel like there are only centimetres away.
_childDocuments_.name: The Vale: Shadow of the Crown

_childDocuments_.review: The story, optional quests and combat system are interesting enough to keep you engaged during the more or less 6 hours of gameplay.In the walking part of he gameplay you orientate yourself by listening to sounds in the surrounding like merchants, water, fire or enemies talking, which in some cases you can avoid with stealth. But those parts are quite short and you will not get lost at all.Combat consists of blocking, light/heavy attacks and counters. When fighting multiple enemies it requires some concentration and timing but it is not too hard and you can adjust the difficulty. With bow and arrow you always have enough time to aim carefully, especially in the optional hunting quests.The equipment upgrades are quite basic but at least allow you to choose between a slow/heavy or fast/light fighting style, but don’t expect anything RPG-like here.Overall it was quite relaxing to enjoy the story and combat with closed eyes

I do wish there were more choices as the choices they do give you were really good and engaging.Gameplay is the real highlight. Many cool and fun spell and magic tool combos make for some really solid and fun combat. Spiders could be a little slow and boring to fight, and trolls can take a bit too long, but that is fixed the further into the game you go, and how well you built your build.Exploration is mixed. _childDocuments_.review: - By  was a pleasant surprise that had a lot more to it then I had originally thought I was going to get out of it. While the "learning in class" aspect that was sold as a concept by the game is there, it is lacking in the depth I would have liked to see from the game. While I understand having an entire class of learning about the lore of the world you inhabit would be  time consuming and boring, it would have been nice to have a short excerpt of something to sell the idea rather than just a cut-scene of happy go lucky kids learning. The story was engaging and you never stray too far from it at any point and the progression to go along with it fit the narrative well. While I wish there was more creative solutions to taking care of enemies rather than the simple loop of combat and avoiding them, the combat was actually a league far above what I thought was capable with a single-player action game based around magic. The movements and animations are well made and snappy as well as all the spells you learn having some use to initiate a combo on any foe you come across. This game is also perfect for those that love to be rewarded for taking their time to explore and be rewarded  with countless puzzles, prizes, and unique interactions all across the castle and landscape, not letting more than a few yards feel like unused space and taking full advantage of the resources and world that has been built by the giants before them. All in all a whopping 8.5/10 and good buy on or off sale for a relaxing third-person experience you can come home from work to.

_childDocuments_.review: I think a good pros cons message will be best for this one.Cons:1. First off lets address the elephant in the room: The transsexual voice actor was subpar, unneeded, and made that entire quest chain obnoxious and pointless. I avoid the three broomsticks like the plague so that I can avoid that awful voice acting. Lets also agree that the character they animated does not match the voice at all. 2. Sociopolitical agendas: The inclusivity in this game is so forced I really struggled to invest. The movies did well because, for the most part, they didnt force racial/sexual agendas and when non-Caucasian cast members appeared they didnt feel forced because the casting reflected the population. Just like it would be obvious to expect that if you went to Ougadou academy that it would be predominately black.  3. Quests: This game could really have benefitted from a different quest system. I hate to sya this, but maybe even a little “go kill this many monsters and return” quest from time to time. It felt like they were trying so hard to come up with a new and original quest for each chain that the content was left wanting.4. Duality: I felt conflicted morally in the game more than a few times; In particular with unforgivable spells. The main character could use them willy nilly in front of everyone and no issues, but anyone else and it was banning from the academy and azkahaban. 5. Environmentalism: This one was super weird because your killing poachers by the hundreds all for the sake of saving the magical beast then you start your own animal breeding farms where you sell their offspring to the beast store, oh and to “save them” you catch them against their will from their natural habitats.  6. Entering buildings: The slow walk thing was unneeded and very annoying.7. Completing challenge: Unfortunately the amount of work you had to put in to complete a challenge was a ton of time and energy, and when you completed the challenge you often got nothing more than a horrendously ugly piece of clothing. 8. Campaign: The campaign really bummer me out because it felt like there were really only two times in the game that your choices had consequences. Every other time, you could say and do whatever you wanted. I also found it super weird that all these different NPCs would send students on super dangerous missions and then get made if the student asked for compensation……..Pros:Now if you read the cons you might think I hated this game, but in fact I think this game was a really good game and if those things up top could have been mitigated in the game this might have been one of the best RPG games I have ever played.1.	The fighting system: The Fighting system was amazing, well thought out, and well designed. It was amazing how the spells played off each other, and every time I thought I was close to becoming bored, a new part of the fighting system would come into play (i.e. new spells, talents table, ancient magic). Transfiguring an enemy into a exploding barrel and then tossing that barrel at another enemy may be one of the most satisfying fighting dynamics of any game I have played.2.	Room of Requirement: Well, this room is freaking amazing! The customizability and just overall graphics of the room are fantastic. I admit that I probably spent 1/4th of my game time changing, customizing, or going to purchase things for the room. 3.	Beast rooms: Although the beast rooms are technically part of the room of requirement, they are so much fun that they get their own section. The designs of the beast areas are magnificent, my only regret is that I couldn’t interact with the furniture (i.e. sit in or on them), I would have built a bunch of beach chairs and sat there and watched animals play with the toys. 4.	Transportation:a.	The first part is that floos were fantastic and covered essentially what was a well laid out fast travel system.b.	 The broomsticks were really enjoyable to use and I appreciated the realism involved with you not having to dismount to collect certain items and to fly around inside broken down buildings and such. That made it enjoyable. I also found the racing competitions to be challenging and fun.c.	The other mounts unfortunately were a huge bust. I wont lie, I was really disappointed in my flying mount (and that I couldn’t get a dragon), and my riding mount. The riding mount was cool and fun to ride for about 20 minutes or so of game time, but was too big and cumbersome to ride near towns and you couldn’t even ride your mounts within Hogsmeade. Your flying mount was slower in the sky than your broom…..so other than for fun it didn’t really serve a purpose. 5.	Graphics: I have a decent gaming system, so there might be some bias to the quality of the game, but the game really put out some amazing graphics and were amazingly detailed.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you want to be a dingdang wizard? Then be a dingdang wizard! Shag-all to the shenanigans going on about this game, it's fun. That's the point and the only hope we can give to vidya as a collective whole. Anyway here's a three hour review of mostly wandering aimlessly and just enjoying the immediate world.The parallels to the 'Shadow Of' series are really nice, lending to fluid gameplay. I must say it is indeed a YMMV moment as far as if KB/M is more or less comfort than a Controller so play whichever you prefer.Do you like collectibles and puzzles? We gotchu boo~. Mirror puzzles that encourage exploration too, so there's no need to feel bad about sidetracking for all the shinies before the main quests! Just... remember to come on back eventually because some of those will be locked behind progression.Plenty of loot for the looter, of which you can apparently find high-tier items from quite literally the first chance you get to play, and plenty of glamour for the true end game of all; Fashion.The minor irk that I did find is the Protag voice. Voice pitches are a bit odd? I don't quite enjoy them in other games and I *half* tolerate this one? Cutscenes have a habit of making our Protag sound terribly warped if the ambient sounds or voice effecting properties of the room are just right. But hey there's even some good news! Voice pitch is something you can alter whenever, so y'know~

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't call myself a Harry Potter fan at all, and only recently watched the movies. I purchased the game after watching content creators on YouTube and found it fascinating. At the moment, I am half way through my first playthrough as a Gryffindor student. I have thoroughly enjoyed every minute of playing. I would say the quests are pretty interesting, particularly the side quest with Sebastian and Ominis. Enemies are very tough to take down, but satisfying once you've defeated them - especially Trolls and Pensieve Guardians. I feel I have improved a lot with combat and it isn't too much to learn with only a few spells of each - damage, control and force. The ancient magic is fun to use as well. The exploration element of the game is fun, whether you're on foot, broom or beast. There is lots of room for you to explore, and the scenery is amazing. I love the fact that the game producers added seasons, which makes exploring feel different throughout the year. Don't miss the snowmen in the Winter.I would say there are some negatives, main one being the lack of time spent in Hogwarts itself. It would have been a much better game if we could see what it would be like as student attending classes - as many classes are just a cut scene, which is very disappointing. I also disliked the dialogue of my character and NPCs - it seemed very repetitive at times. Overall I would give this game a 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Alright, while the below is still valid, I'm going to have to turn this around into a recommendation from a not recommendation. The reason being is that this game simply looks quite beautiful regardless, and Hogwarts, I feel, is somewhat exquisitely crafted. Many animations are quite smooth, and the care and detail put into multiple locations is impressive.I was forced to upgrade my CPU to a 7800X3D in order to enjoy the graphics.While this does still follow the usual formulas for contemporary open world games in a multitude of ways, overall I have to say that I'm just impressed after seeing more and more of the world that was crafted. A decent amount has a dearth of meaningful content, of course, but overall it still just finds ways to impress me every time I start it up. The moving paintings are a treat, and often include sound to go along with them. It's clear some amount of love was put into this.I am not sure if this is worth a $60 price tag, however if you can catch it on sale, I do believe it is worth it.Original review:I have a 4090 RTX and a 5950X. For some reason this game is coded so poorly that it lags and stutters yet when I open up any system monitor, it often isn't even using 50% of my GPU.I'm sorry, what? I enjoy the atmosphere but it's not nice when it's a stuttering mess and it isn't even because of your hardware, or your settings being cranked too high for your hardware.. It's because whoever coded it was so garbage at coding that they couldn't utilize said hardware.Also, apparently it's CPU bound because it chooses to be: it uses 50% of 2 cores, which indicates that it's basically single core, double threaded. That's freaking pathetic. There are few other games this generation which are executed as badly as this garbage.

Breaks the immersion a bit.-Quidditch was left out, feels like a time-issue in development (though i personally dont really miss it)-Few Potions (and i would have wished for a bit more work doing it the first time, like actually getting the ingredients right)-Which leads to a big problem: It doesnt really feel like you are going to school there at all. You can do what you want and when you want it - which in principal of course is great for open world - but if its about the experience of being a pupil in a wizarding school, then Schedules and Rules should play a part.-Classes are pretty much cutscenes - again, feeling is lost here.-Diversity in Hogwarts is a little overdone for 1800, one comes to ask himself, what the hell Dumbledore did, for the school to look like it does in the movies.-Tacked on Trans-Bartender wont win prices in my book. I hated the entire discussion and the social media outrage and i also dont need some virtue-signalling from the developer - i simply dont care.Even though the Contra List is substantial, the Pros more than enough make it a good Game. The Contras are more a grain of salt, since it shows wasted potential, that is visible on many places. Still good, but not as great as it could have been. 80/100

_childDocuments_.review: Make no mistake: This is a fantastic game. It oozes quality. The story, characters, every design is made with imagination, care, and skill. It's a work of love. The production values are stupendous. Hogwarts is recreated in glorious detail - it looks fantastic, with each square inch lovingly crafted. This makes it sound like it should be small, but no, it's also huuge. Garments and characters are equally lusciously crafted with character and care. Seriously - I played the first five hours of this with my jaw on the floor.The actual game and gameplay is great, with a storyline that feels suitable for a harry potter book, with lots of great characters and moments. The open world aspects are good and meaningful, with a reasonable amount of various minigames. It lacks a bit of depth - it definitely is there to tell one story well, and your choices, while reacted upon then and there, are not, ultimately, of much weight. (With a few exceptions.).This is probably the best franchise based game I've played, and is not at all a cheap cash-in on a good name.Edit: Running it on a 6 yo computer with an updated GPU (3060). It runs perfectly fine on 3440*1440 at 'high', no stuttering or artifacts of any kind.M+K controls work fine, but I hear controllers can be a bit moody. It has all the accessibility settings you'd expect and more.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Amazing immersive game, if you like a fantasy world setting then you should play it, even if you're not a fan of HP stuff.Great game, lots of good things done right and that's why I'm leaving a positive review. However, I'm gonna focus and start with the cons:- The game has a huge FPS drops and stuttering (I'm using a high end GPU) in some parts of the world, this started to be noticeable during the winter season so it might have been the reason, also the game crashed twice on me, but it has an auto save so not a big deal.- Second issue is, a lot of the mechanics and animations in this game get repetitive over time, like picking locks and doing Merlin puzzles was nice for a while but having to wait for the animation every single time is tiring and boring, and yes a large part of this was felt when I was 100%ing the game but I felt this way earlier too.- Another mechanic that felt useless literally the second you get it is potion making, you never run out of potions and never need to use them at all, same with the plants. - Speaking of useless mechanics, even money/coins gets obsolete at like mid to late game which makes you not really being rewarded for exploring and picking up armor to sell.- SELLING GEAR SEPARATELY every single time is tedious af, and you can only carry 20 at a time while wearing 6 pieces of those, so you gotta take a turn to the shop every time and sell one by one... Please add the option to sell them all, it will make it much better, especially when you're doing a good job by not displaying the currently used gear. And yes I know you can increase it to 40 by endgame but that's still nothing, in fact 40 should be the starting capacity if not more.- Game is waaaay too easy, but I guess this is to be expected.- Enemy variety leaves much to be desired.- For some reason, you can't pause the cutscenes which is annoying since sometimes I have to. Anyway, it might seem that I'm just whining since I'm only focusing on negatives, but that's not the case, I really enjoyed the game a lot, exploring Hogwarts and Hogsmeade for the first time was such a joy and a fun experience, flying is well done, the characters are fun to listen to and the dialogue is good, most of the quests and lore are cool and it made me read a lot even tho I'm not a lore guy.Overall, definitely play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Abstract: Great game, also for a younger audience with some potential.Positive:+ The game ran well on Linux out of the box+ Graphics+ Sound/Soundtrack+ Key NPCs are displayed very immersively in cutscenes+ Great model of the Hogwarts castle and Hogsmeade+ The game is a bit like Skyrim but in Hogwarts universe+ Technically, the game can be modded well being based on Unreal Engine+ Magical environment allows e.g. shimmering traces on the ground to look immersive+ The game contains logic riddles+ The game does create autosaves frequently so you don't lose much progress if it crashesNeutral:* Single player only gameNegative:- Most of the NPCs are very anonymous. They just mumble superficial stuff which makes just a bit sense referring to the atmosphere described in the Harry Potter books. I would clearly place the atmosphere of Hogwarts Legacy below the one created in games like The Witcher.- The NPCs which e.g. like to hinder you getting somewhere move very generically appearing very unhuman/dumb. There is no entropy in the AI. As a result, you do repetitive stuff to proceed. It's not like you had to react much on unexpected situations in this game, like people suddenly walking other routes etc.- If you hit a student in Hogwarts, what reduced the hit points of enemies by 1/4 does no harm to them at all, they just keep walking like zombies. If you walk in them, at least they complain a little about it sometimes.- Nobody chases after you if you attack the cats or destroy sculptures in Hogwarts, the cats run away at least. Nobody chases you for attacking their cattle and you can't kill cows/chicken etc to loot them. Whatever evil thing you do in this game, there are no negative consequences to the world or yourself.- If Peeves creates a mess, students complain that they would be in trouble but no one like teachers etc. chases them either. The vitality of Hogwarts is somewhat missing despite the well designed objects.- Part of the game is stealing from people's homes while they are present. They just don't show any reaction if you loot their chests. Other games do a lot better in that case!- Since the game displays many characters that appear like young aged people, the modding of the game is extremely limited. Clothing mods are overexaggeratedly removed from the internet as well as mods that allow attacking other students with an effect on their displayed health status etc.- Some things you just can't do at the beginning and there is no explanation why and when it will get unlocked.- The default HUD settings reduce immersion significantly, since everything is enabled. I recommend very much to disable e.g. HUD tracking icons, the mInimap etc.- If Skyrim felt like whiskey to you, in some scenes this game might appear like tea to you. Might be helpful to target some younger audience but might feel a little weak to the older one.- You find legendary items too easily and you can even buy them. I can't see any difference in the distribution of green, blue, violet or amber items aside from the upgradability - the items look like quite generic loot, no matter which color they havePerformance:+ I'm playing on Linux with an RX 6800 XT, 32 GiB memory and a Ryzen 7 5800X with disabled SMT. The render resolution is 100% at WQHD. The setting is Ultra. I haven't experienced any noticeable performance issues yet, everything ran butter smoothly with one exception: In Hogwarts, when using Lumos on the main floor, due to many reflections the frame rate appeared to have dropped below 20 FPS. (Just my gut feeling.)- Unfortunately I have experienced game crashes many times. I just landed on my Desktop. This appears to happen regularly and might be a memory leak or something, because it seems to be connected with switching the environment very often. I guess this might be a Linux specific issue - not sure though since I don't have any reference from other operating systems.

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell this game was made with so much love and care. The studio did an amazing job bringing the world to life.The castle is a character in and of itself and you can spend hours upon hours getting lost and still feel like you've only scratched the surface. And then when you think the game is just that map, there's actually a whole world outside of it to explore, filled with stunning details and challenges that dot the map.The magic system is fun to use. With a variety of spells implemented fairly well for the use of a controller. All spells feel unique and have their own applications.And beyond that they actually managed to incorporate herbology and magical animals into the game as actual mechanics, not just throwaway minigames. Actually nothing feels like it's a throwaway in this game.Everything from the animations, to the music, to the environment is just chef's kiss.If you're a fan of the franchise and have read all the books, there's so many details for you to enjoy. If you've never even seen the movies or anything, I dare say you would still enjoy this game for what it is.Couple of cons are the inventory system. You can thankfully make all items you wear, look like other items you've collected. So you can always look how you want. but you have to re-apply it every time you equip a new item. And it's kind of a hassle going to the stores to sell your surplus items to open up your relatively small inventory. It can be expanded but the method is a bit time consuming.And there's not actually enough build variety to differ from character to character. Every playthrough would end up roughly the same, and if you specialise in something you'd be marginally better at it than if you were to opt for a different specialisation. Think Fable 2, mixed with the Witcher 3, and then meticulously worked out to perfectionEDIT:  After a bunch of playthroughs and several speedruns, I will have to amend my review to include that the game's world design, though beautiful, doesn't offer a whole lot of depth. Especially after a certain number of hours and all you do is finish the world map's objectives which start to feel like a chore. Still do recommend, but don't expect top tier gameplay design.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're just looking for a quick review on this game, here: It's great. If you can get past the.. certain author of the series, the combat is very enjoyable and the world feels amazing. If not, then you probably shouldn't be considering buying the game anyway..Lets start with the pros:Combat. It feels SO fluid, and honestly has such a good feel to it. It has a high enough skill level that I'm able to sink my teeth into it and really get good at it, but it isn't annoyingly difficult.Character customization. I know this is fairly common for AAA games nowadays, but I don't play many of them, so the amount of character customization was completely new to me, and it really felt like I was able to make my character look however I wanted, freely.The world. It's amazing. I just love games with amazing worlds and landscapes that I can freely explore, and this one is no exception, I could spend hours just exploring. (If I had the time, that is..) My only complaint is I wish there were more settlements to explore. Other than that, I have no complaints.And now for the cons:The story. It's... acceptable. Sure, its enjoyable if you don't pay attention to the specifics, but when you really pay attention to it, there are a LOT of major plot holes. For example, I would love an explanation as to why you show up as a 5th year...? The excuse of you being "special" doesn't really cut it for me. Side quests. They aren't the best. A lot of them feel more like a chore than something I'd like to spend my time doing.Enemy variety. It's really bland. A few spiders here and there, some dark wizards, trolls, statues, and maybe a few other things thrown in. That's really it, and I would love to see some more variety in what enemies you face while exploring / doing quests.Overall,Story: 6/10Combat: 9.5/10World: 8/10Performance: 10/10(Note: I play this on a very high end gaming computer, so the performance will most likely vary.)Personally, I find it quite enjoyable. Is it my favorite game? No. That doesn't stop it from being fun, and something I like spending time playing and exploring the world.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the game and getting 100% worth of the achievements, I thought to write a review. While playing the game the graphics were truly incredible. It was nice to see Hogwarts castle and be able to run around in it. There were a couple changes done to the castle for the game such as the Greenhouse's got reworked and there wasn't a long stone bridge that led to the castle. The areas they were able to include puzzles at within the castle felt well placed. The side quests had you coming back to multiple areas in the castle and introduced new features through them which was a nice touch. It was cool that you were able to fly around on the broom around the outside regions of the castle. For the Greater Hogwarts region, Hogsmeade felt like it deserved to be able to fly through with the broom. You would just experience this giant barrier every time you flew towards that direction. If you wanted to go to a place on the other side of it, you would have to get off the broom, fast travel to a point, or go around the Hogsmeade area with the broom. Other than that, I didn't have too much of an opinion about the region. I felt like they did a good job at incorporating the infamous enemies (mini bosses) across the map. As for the regular enemies that spawn everywhere. The trolls were definitely built to be tanks. I had a big problem in trying to kill them quickly everywhere I went until I upgraded my Offensive strength score in equipment. One problem I did have with the infamous enemies was that after a while, I was able to just one shot them with the Ancient Power. There was definitely a lot of content through the side quests reaching around (60+) quests you can do across the region. Each House at Hogwarts has their own unique side quest before you reach one of the critical story missions. My personal favorite was the Hufflepuff quest line since it took you to Azkaban. After you finish the unique quest, it is the only one that will appear to be unique throughout the entire game. I wish they had more quests that were unique to each House. The relationship quest lines don't provide much besides more side quests and items. Depending on which House you chose at Hogwarts, you would get a different common room and these would be at different places in the castle. I think the future of the game is strong if they add DLC's to it. There is a lot of hope that the DLC's will be well polished since the base game was extremely well polished compared to other game releases we have received in the past few years. If they decide to create a second game, it definitely will be hard to make it unique compared to this one since they will have to rebuild up the known spells and traverse Hogwarts Castle yet again. I definitely hope to see some type of Quidditch component from them in the future. Overall my experience with the game was quite enjoyable and definitely would come back to it if they added more content to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible game, and already a strong competitor for GOTY. The amount of detail that went into building Hogwarts is insane to me. I can't imagine how much time and effort the developers put into it, looks like something that would have taken a a year if not more to make. Hogwarts FEELS huge, and there is so many secret areas and puzzles around the castle to find. I was really just blown away by all the smaller and intricate details you'll see at and around Hogwarts. The picture frames, display cases, fossils, classrooms, tapestry, windows, lounge areas, etc. I could go on and on but that's what I'm talking about, everything is just so frickin detailed to me, blows my mind. I just can't stop playing it, been playing it since day one of early access, several hours a day, and when I get off work I just look forward to getting back into the game. I can easily see myself putting 100+ hours into this game, but I don't want to come off as making it sound "tedious" to me the game is designed in a way that motivates and excites the player to explore Hogwarts and the surrounding area. I personally am just having fun exploring in general and just taking it all in, even sometimes just casually walking around Hogwarts slowly and admiring the scenery. I love the visuals so much that I've been taking screenshots left and right. I'm trying to avoid spoiling too much, but there is A LOT to do in this game, and at no point in time so far have I felt bored once while playing this game. You eventually get access to a room that you can decorate to your hearts content, and let me tell you, the developers give you full access for the most part to decorating it. You can pick from 100's of decorations, pictures, you can change the colors of decorations, and even the size! You can change the ceiling, floor pattern, and even the ambiance of the room to fit the style/theme. When I unlocked this room I spent AN HOUR AND A HALF just decorating and playing around with the design system. I keep going back to detail and aesthetics, but you really have to appreciate just how much work the developers put into this game, when I look at the game it looks like something that was worked on meticulously and with care. I know we're only into the start of 2023, but as far as I'm concerned, other games are going to be hard pressed to beat this, we'll see, but I really do think the developers deserve all the awards and praise for their work on this. I really haven't had any qualms at all with the game, it really is a fantastic Harry Potter RPG and the one I imagined experiencing someday when I was younger, but now it's here. A DREAM HAS COME TO LIFE!

_childDocuments_.review: Visually this game is incredible. The castle is huge and densely packed, the countryside is rustic and charming, the hamlets and towns are bustling with people going about their days. The draw distance in this game is astounding. From almost anywhere on the map, if your high enough you can see the castle. One thing I absolutely adore is being able to change how my characters clothes look compared to what they are actually wearing, I wish more games did little things like this, as now I don't have to choose between having good stats and looking good for the cut scenes.Game play wise it's pretty solid, with only 1 or 2 minor gripes on my part. The spells are all fun to use and their mix and match combos spice up game play considerably. Flying is great for long distance journeys or for sight seeing, but i found it a bit challenging on some of the time trials for the tight turns and rapid up / down. Several time I would find myself just doing circles trying to hit a missed ring or balloon due to the camera and controls not cooperating with me. The single most frustrating part of the game so far is that there are certain optional mini platform sections, and my wizard becomes extremely hard to coordinate these jumps without messing up and having to start over. I must have wasted 10 minutes just face planting into these stone pillars before managing to pull it off.Story is your basic ' I have great power, but can't use it right away' that i'm sure everyone has heard of before. Not to say it is bad, in fact I feel they put a nice spin on the tried and true formula, but just know that is the basic premise for your character. So far being about 1/2 way done I feel more invested in my side story characters compared to the main plot, but that is probably because the interactable characters are just so relatable. If the main story is about great power and the struggle around it the side stories are about students being students and trying to help in what ever way they can.TLDR; Its a good game, i recommend even if your not a Harry Potter fan.
