_childDocuments_.review: : I’ve even read some debates about whether it’s even a RPG. I think that it is, it has most of the characteristics of a RPG, they’re just all very weak. There’s “caves” or “dungeons” but that are usually repetitive and are only a bit more interesting when tied to the main story. Inventory system isn't incredible and you're flooded with too many pointless items that are just good to go sell almost right away considering your inventory space (But then again I feel like it’s pretty common among other games). You’re never really hyped by what you find. At times you see the item has a little green arrow implying it’ll raise your stats a bit but that’s it. Items are upgradable which is cool. There’s no class system. The skills tree isn’t very interesting. There’s no morality system or ways to shape your character’s identity and personality beside having the choice to give an answer or another during dialogues and that have no impact on the story.But I don’t think they could really have done a great intricate RPG, something to rival Skyrim or the Witcher. It’s a game that’s targeted to a lot of people who are going to play for the lore, the story and the nostalgia, including kids. So while I was a bit disappointed in some of these aspects, I’m not sure if they could have done better to make it accessible to everyone who wanted to have a cool Harry Potter universe experience. Now as an overall action game, it does the job well. Especially when you consider the combat system, which is pretty much one of my favorite combat systems ever. It's super fun, non-stop action, you can get rid of enemies in a lot of different ways, through the use of a wide range of spells with which you can find a lot of cool synergies. The “shield” systems work great whether it’s for your character or as an added challenge with the enemies. I loved every single time I came into combat. It was often too easy but I believe I could have upped the difficulty.I played most of the game with a mod, “Mouse gesture to spell” that made it much more fun and makes you feel like you’re actually moving a wand. I really really recommend it. Before it it was a bit annoying to circle through the different spell.Exploration is a mixed bag. Trying to find everything on the map can be a chore. There's too much, and too much of the same thing. When you come across one of these "puzzles" or "caves" you often can't be bothered to do the same thing for the 67th time. I wanted to complete he game so I went through with it but it wasn't fun on that aspect. There could have been easily 3 times less caves and Merlin Trials. Some of these puzzles, secrets or challenges scattered around the map are more fun and less numerous than others though which is cool.The difference is night and day when you compare Hogwarts itself to the rest of the map. Exploring Hogwarts is one of the best part of the game, it gave me strong Harry Potter 3 nostalgia where you could also try to find a lot of secrets and puzzles hidden in the castle. It’s HP3 times a hundred. It can be challenging to find everything but it's fun to take the time to find how to open every single door, reach all the chests and field guide pages. The puzzles are often not too complicated, but as explained above, they had to go for a very accessible experience and despite the easiness it was very fun to find most of the secrets. Actually one or two were very challenging now that I think about it. What they did with the room of requirement is perfect : customization, herbology, magic creatures… etc. It was the best possible use of this important part of the castle as a personal room to centralize almost all the crafting and personalisation. Most of the more challenging steam achievements were cool to get, although it would have been nice to be able to track your progress through it. Just a bit ridiculous to have 3 of them only reachable by playing the whole game again as another wizard house, considering how little this “class” aspect impacts the game. It basically requires you to play through a few hours of the game 3 times without any novelty each time. Can’t be bothered. : The story is OK. Some themes and elements are great and engaging, others cliche and more boring. I read a lot of negativity about it, but it’s really not that bad. They also tried to be inclusive in the characters identities without forcing it and assuming you can fix racism or transphobia by simply adding the right pixels to a video game without getting rid of class society as a whole which is the root cause of oppressions and how our institutions function which is cool. Maybe I’m getting a bit off the subject. There’s just that African student, that transgender character (who is a good addition considering the whole JK Rowling thing. I don’t get why she’s portrayed as a literal nazi by everybody when her positions aren’t that extreme really, even though I disagree with them), and it’s perfectly normal and mundane, it didn’t make me feel like they were trying to make a game just to put that in. I just really hoped I could have participated in something like the  a hundred years before it’s time but there was no clear way to liberate them from the slave work they’re subjected to. The references to Harry Potter whether it’s in the dialogues, story, exploration, are cool. I’ve had a lot of moments where a mission reminded me of another in the first Harry Potter game, some story in a parchment of something in books, or a puzzle from the movies. The overall vibe and music really get you back to the best aspects of the movies, which is clearly the biggest selling point of the game, nostalgia. That with the beauty and richness of the castle of Hogwarts make the game a real success. Some aspects are just a bit too simple or wholesome compared to the universe we’re used to. Walking through Hogwarts at night for example isn’t a problem, whereas if you’re used to the books or the movies you know it’s supposed to be scary and forbidden. There’s no real “mean” teacher or Slytherin kids which is disappointing too. The worst I’ve seen from a teacher is the Headmaster cancelling Quidditch because the developers didn’t have the time or means to add it to the game.  : pretty bad in the beginning. I tried playing around with the settings to find a sweet spot of quality / performance but it was never really satisfying. My system is getting a bit old (i5 4690 / 980ti) so can't complain too much. Over time it improved. I tried various mods or patches when it came out that helped a bit, not sure if they're still useful. The game looks good overall while not trying to be hyper realistic.There was some buggy parts, I fell under the map once (managed miraculously to get back up by using my broom and flying back up) and some broken "skeleton physics" forced me to restart the game once or twice.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game ONLY if you're a big Harry Potter fan. With that said, I'm sure most of the people looking at this game are Harry Potter fans.The world is beautiful, detailed and lots of places to visit and lore to discover. It can be great just walking through Hogwarts which is absolutely huge. You will find yourself quickly wandering off and forgetting about the main quest.However, game play is very slow. A lot of puzzles and secrets in the game are locked behind abilities which you will need to play the game for a considerable amount of time before you can do them. This was frustrating to me as I don't like passing up locked rooms and chests over and over because I don't have the spell to unlock them. I think the biggest issue is that I feel the ability to unlock doors should have been one of the earlier quests in the game. I also feel that unlocking a broom to ride was much later in the game than I would have liked and there are places outdoors that you can't just hop on your broom and fly off. I would also like to see more interaction with the world. Most of the NPCs will talk about you or what you're doing, but you can't interact with them other than bumping into them. I would of also liked more class mini-games and to get an actual grade from your classes.I don't want to run around Avada kedavra'n the world, but more dialogue options with more classmates would have been great. Side quests are fun but they run out quickly. I would of also liked to see more choices for classmates to make friends with and have adventures.I haven't experienced a lot of performance issues, I play on a laptop with an i9 11900h, 32GB ram, SSD, and a 3070 laptop GPU. However, I left everything on recommended and didn't try to crank it up to ultra settings.Overall, this is easily the best "Wizarding World" game ever made and is a lot of fun. But if you're not a fan of Harry Potter, I'd recommend waiting till it goes on sale and Avalanche Software gets a chance to optimize the game a little more.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Wizarding World, I approached Hogwarts Legacy with high expectations, and I’m thrilled to say it exceeds them in almost every way. From the moment I stepped into the game, I was spellbound by its attention to detail and immersive world-building.The game’s visual fidelity is nothing short of breathtaking. Hogwarts Castle itself is a marvel, with every corridor, classroom, and hidden nook lovingly crafted to evoke the wonder and charm of J.K. Rowling’s universe. The attention to detail is remarkable, and it’s evident that the developers poured their hearts into recreating the magic of Hogwarts.Character customization and the ability to shape your own magical journey are standout features. The depth of the role-playing elements allows for a truly personal experience. Whether you’re a Gryffindor, Slytherin, Hufflepuff, or Ravenclaw, the game makes you feel like you’re truly living out your Hogwarts fantasy.The spellcasting mechanics are engaging and intuitive, offering a satisfying blend of strategy and action. The variety of spells at your disposal, combined with a robust combat system, makes every magical encounter thrilling. Plus, the inclusion of a rich narrative with well-developed characters adds layers to the gameplay that keep it fresh and exciting.One of the most enjoyable aspects of Hogwarts Legacy is the freedom it offers. You can explore the castle, venture into the Forbidden Forest, and delve into side quests at your own pace. The game’s world feels alive, filled with secrets and surprises around every corner.The soundtrack and sound design further enhance the experience, with a score that perfectly complements the magical atmosphere. The voice acting is top-notch, bringing the characters and story to life with genuine emotion and charm.While there are a few minor bugs and performance hiccups here and there, they do little to detract from the overall enjoyment. These are easily overshadowed by the game’s many strengths.In summary, Hogwarts Legacy is a triumph for fans of the Wizarding World and newcomers alike. It captures the magic, mystery, and excitement of Hogwarts in a way that feels both nostalgic and refreshingly new. If you’ve ever dreamed of attending Hogwarts or wielding magic, this game is a must-play. Grab your wand, don your robes, and prepare for an unforgettable adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-enjoyable exploration-large and detailed world-great main story and wonderful side characters/stories -good fighting mechanics-fun mount/flying mechanics-good variety in puzzles-decorating the Room of Requirements is a lot of fun-enjoyable talent systemCons:-troll attacks lock on to PC and allow them to follow through on attacks over long distances-flying can be challenging as keyboard controls are clunky-too many side objectives and locations are useless (cave with no enemies, puzzles, or challenges to just get 1 piece of gear)-upgrading the Room of Requirements makes the game way too easy-waiting on events or side quests to continue can be unnecessarily long-lack of replayability-leveling at the high end becomes grueling and unimportantOverallIt's a fun game that I would recommend to anyone that even tangentially likes or is interested in the Harry Potter world. Can be completed in 15-20 hours if you run through it, or 70-90 hours if you are trying to complete everything. I enjoyed the combat and the flying. Completing Merlin challenges is a must to increase inventory space and doing the ancient magic challenges makes the game even easier than it already is. Troll fights can be extremely irritating due to their attacks tracking and following the PC, but once you know this it's easy to adjust and then they are as easy as anything. The parkour challenges are annoying due to the movement system showing it's weaknesses there, but you can just jump on a broom and glide through it easily.It still good.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an extremely enjoyable game with great combat, GFX are great, environments is well designed, customisation is great, you can design your own wand etc. You can change pretty much any aspect of yourself in the local town too if you fancy a change of hair/eye colour and you can also transform the appearance of any item of clothing you have on with previously collected which is fantastic. Combat is just so satisfying, the spells and combos you can do are very flashy but combat can still be a challenge if you become complacent. Enemies level up with you as you progress so you'll always have something to fight. You get a modest list of special spells such as Levioso, Accio, Expelliarmus  etc etc to assist with combat, puzzles and traversing dungeons which can be upgraded via a talent tree as you advance with a bonus effect.You can design your own little personal space inside the school if you're into that with decorations, tables, crafting stations, etc. You can also look after animals and breed them like a Wizardy version of animal crossing in your little personal space which in turn give you material. This seems to be a massive feature of the game as you get multiple side missions to go rescue 'rare' animals but sadly I don't think it's utilised fully, maybe in later DLC it'll become worth more investing time to it. Mainly used for upgrading clothing, making potions and plants for battles but the game does give you option to buy your material with in game gold if you can't be bothered doing animal crossing: Hogwarts.Only some minor issues I can think of such as the EN voice acting is a little poor in places and facial animations of your character can sometimes be a little out of place like: "My father died for me" Me: SMILES, however, the friends/relations you make are all very wholesome and great experiences. The main story starts off nice and strong with twists and so on but I feel like the shocks and surprises fall off towards the end. Some really good missions though kept me coming back for more. Feel like there could of been more of a house based story line personally along side the main story to make you feel more associated with your house you get sorted into. There is also the odd glitch here and there but usually funny such as ragdolls/item physics doing zoomies into the distance, only game breaking bug I had was I stunned a major enemy during a transition to the final phase which required a reload of the last auto save but the game regularly auto saves so no real biggie. Otherwise the best Wizarding game I've played in a long time. Not sure if I'll ever replay it fully but mods will definitely make me want to revisit the game in future I reckon,I might go visit Professor Garlic again.  All in all, I got 67 hours out of this game so I'd say I've easy got my money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: In my personal opinion,I have thoroughly enjoyed playing this game and believe that it fulfills everything I have ever wanted in a Harry Potter game.The story is well-written, and the voice acting by non-player characters is exceptional. However, the player characters' voices do sound slightly robotic, likely due to the pitch, but this did not significantly detract from my gameplay experience. The combat system is engaging, but I would have appreciated more variety in the enemies we encounter. The game's depiction of Hogwarts and the surrounding world is incredibly detailed, and I have found myself getting lost in exploring the castle multiple times.Unfortunately, I do have a few criticisms of the game that I hope will be addressed in the future. For example, the lack of a photo mode and certain animation issues with foes such as the trolls who sometimes lag in completing their animations. Additionally, there is a noticeable lack of enemy variety, and I would have liked more school-focused missions and student life activities, such as Quidditch and Wizards Chess, to make the game feel more immersive.Despite these minor criticisms, I believe that Avalanche has done an outstanding job of bringing the Harry Potter universe to life through this game. I look forward to future developments, including potential downloadable content (DLC) or similar games exploring other parts of the wizarding world, such as Ilvermorny, Beauxbâtons, Durmstrang, or stories focused around the adults of the universe, such as Aurors or Unspeakables. I believe that many others would also enjoy playing these types of games.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game surprised me. I was scared it was going to be just a fan service filled experience -and to some extent it was- but I actually had a lot of fun playing it, as you can probably tell by the number of hours.This game does have the classic problems every open world game has nowadays: a bigass map filled with useless and a little bit repetitive side activities and nothing else, pushing you to use fast travel whenever you can. And yet, as I decided to *not* use fast travel too much, I found exploring is actually a nice experience! Hogwarts has TONS of secrets, with most of them requiring you to know a specific spell to uncover them, and the world surrounding the school is filled with side quests which are... actually very well made! I mean, they tend to just require you to go to an enemy camp or a dungeon full of spiders and battle your way through, but the characters and their requests are never the kind you would expect from a fetch quest. There aren't actually real fetch quests in the game, nobody asks you to just collect x things and come back to give you a useless reward: every side quest has a little story of their own, and just a few of them can be considered fetch quests, but they only require you to explore at your pace, and they're usually not even required to finish all the quests in the game.The recurring side characters are also very interesting and fun to interact with, both during lessons and during their "relationship quests", as the game calls them. Their stories are very intriguing, and by the end of the game you can't help but grow fond of them! Mind you, though, that I am a Slytherin, and I only played this game once, so of course I cannot speak for every Hogwarts house.But is this game actually perfect? Unfortunately, far from it. Being a game that lets you live the life of a Hogwarts student you would expect the classic school life: going to lectures, learning a lot of spells and other things, curfew and other enforced school rules. I mean, way older games managed to perfectly do that, like Bully from Rockstar. And yet, this game suffers from the same problem a lot of modern games suffer: it's just a beautifully crafted diorama. Outside from quests you cannot interact with anyone, nobody really reacts to whatever you do, you can even use Dark Magic right in front of Hogwarts professors and nobody will say anything. There are no rules, no laws, no detention, you can do whatever you please, go everywhere in the entire world (even private houses), everything is right there for you to take, and nobody will even bat an eye.You can go to lectures and learn spells, but they come in a limited number, and more often than not they're just a cutscene with a useless minigame at the end to make you learn the new spell. They could have done soooo much more with the immersion in this game.And yet, I still recommend this game, at least if you're a fan of Harry Potter and the Wizarding World in general. And if you can at least close an eye to that whole Rowling mess. The plot is basic, but main quests are filled with mysteries, beatiful scenes and fun boss fights, and exploring the game world is still quite fun.

_childDocuments_.review: "Hogwarts Legacy" is a spellbinding experience that transports players to the wizarding world of J.K. Rowling's beloved universe. The game boasts an immersive storyline that keeps players engaged from start to finish, with a richly detailed world filled with magic, mystery, and adventure. The graphics are simply stunning, bringing the Hogwarts castle and its surrounding areas to life in breathtaking fashion.One of the standout features of "Hogwarts Legacy" is its combat system, which offers a satisfying blend of fast-paced action and strategic spellcasting. Players can choose from a wide range of spells and abilities, each with its own unique properties, to defeat their enemies and complete missions. The spellcasting system is intuitive and engaging, and the game's pacing is spot-on, providing just the right amount of challenge to keep players on their toes.The musical score of "Hogwarts Legacy" is nothing short of stunning, perfectly capturing the mood and atmosphere of the movies and books. The sound effects are also top-notch, adding an extra layer of immersion to the overall experience.One small negative aspect of the game is that the protagonist's name is never mentioned by any of the non-player characters (NPCs) during the story, which detracts slightly from the overall immersion. However, this is a minor quibble in an otherwise exceptional game that is sure to delight fans of the wizarding world.In conclusion, "Hogwarts Legacy" is a tour de force that delivers a rich and engaging experience for players. Its stunning graphics, tight combat system, and breathtaking musical score make it a must-play for fans of the franchise. The game's immersive world, full of magic and adventure, is sure to keep players captivated for hours on end.

_childDocuments_.review: After 60 hours I finished the main story and all the relationship missions. I did some collectibles but they aren't fun to me so I just left them at some point and only collected them while I was around them.First I want to start that it isn't a bad game. I'd rate if as very average with some bigger and smaller complaints, but they don't drag it down to a bad game level. I based the purchase off on the first tutorial area of the game and thought it looked amazing. I was super excited to get it too.GAMEPLAYThe way your character moves around flows really well as well as any transition to combat. Combat itself is quite fun and sometimes even on normal difficulty, if you don't react fast enough or just aren't paying enough attention then you might just get roughed up pretty good. By the end of the story I was quite tired of the combat system as it was doing the exact same thing over and over again. You might have a lot of spells available but you only use few of them. Curses go through shields and to break shield normally you have to match up with the correct type of spell. It makes you use three different type of spells all the time until you get your first curse.There aren't very many different enemy types, you're mostly killing either poachers (humans), goblins or spiders. Few trolls here and there. They all have their weaknesses and that makes you also use certain spells against them just so it would go quicker. It gets boring fast on that part and you learn the attack patterns quickly.The game emphasises a lot on collectibles in the game, something that I absolutely hate. I hate going around in places collecting stuff that doesn't matter in the long run. Maybe if it was all marked out like in some games you can buy treasure maps to locate all collectibles or what ever.The world itself felt like it was dead outside of Hogwarts of Hogsmeade. The creativity, which was based off the movies, dies as soon as you stopped outside of them. All the areas look the same, acted the same, exploration wasn't really a thing here that was interesting. Caves were all small and didn't offer much.In general, the world doesn't react to what you do.I'll add here aswell the point that I didn't like the character customization a lot. Sure it helped to make a human looking person, but there weren't many choices and if you wanted to change your voice pitch, then they artifically lowered of heightened it instead of casting an actual actor with such a voice type.STORYThe story is in my opinion pretty bad. I never liked games where you are the demigod main character. In the beginning of the game you find out that you can use ancient magic. It seems that this is also the reason you are able to so quickly pick up on regular magic.The story itself is full of cliches and annoying characters. I was constantly holding my head not wanting to speak like my character does nor trust most of the people I talked to. There is also a lot of power play like your character being the level 100 speech master or just overpowering any enemies while being first year in Hogwarts.Sidemissions weren't very much better either. Sebastian's story was the most interesting out of the bunch with the secrets of Salazar but it fell apart by the end. There weren't many memorable moments.The general theme of the story had a lot of inconsistencies. For example the general theme is that there are poachers around but then you as a character have a choice to save some animals. At some point when you're told that you can sell animals in Hogsmeade then you can basically be a poacher yourself: capture all the animals in their nest and sell them for profit while calling it "saving" them. You can also breed them and then sell them, making you think that why didn't poachers do the same. Would have been cheaper and easier.LOREThe game has problems with the lore of Wizarding World really well. Sure it all happens in the context of it and characters act like it in cutscenes such as tellling that dark magic is bad. The reality is that you can cast avada kedavra at people in front of your teachers or friends and nobody will think of you otherwise. This is inconsistent compared to that you can send someone to Azkaban for using killing curse on another person.I think I mentioned stuff I wanted to bring out here too. I recommend you read longer negative reviews as they some have described very well how this game is lacking.In general it is very mediocre and doesn't deserve the price it costs.PS! Professor Garlick is hot

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing AA game. The world is built with so much attention to the book series, sprinkled with the visuals from the movies, made coherent and gorgeous and lovable. There aren't that many sidequests, and collecting the collectibles is for once not a chore -- at least for me, I loved diving back in and Revelio-ing everything to death. It's a cozy world, inhabited by bright individuals. The gameplay loop, the way the quests build upon each other, I enjoyed these things tremendously. But the story is nowhere near where it could have been. The books are written like mystery novels where you never expect the revelations that come at the end. Here, though, the ending is as plain as they get. The villains don't have additional depth. The consequences of the only meaningful choice you make are resolved offscreen. To receive the final three achievments you're forced to spend up to nine hours replaying the game from the beginning, tutorials included.So, yes, I loved it and a fourteen year old me would have thought it was flawless, but it's not perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: BLUF: If you’re a Potter fan, this is probably the best game there is right now.  If you’re not, go for Elden Ring, The Witcher 3, or Skyrim instead.  Hogwarts Legacy is a beautifully crafted landscape of the eponymous castle and its surrounding land.  The wonder and strange chaotic magical mess of the source material is there.  The sheer detail in the environment makes you feel like this really is the Hogwarts you want to explore.  It may even be enough to carry you through the game.  The gameplay sure won’t though.  The RPG elements of the game are all half-done and generations behind the times.  The combat is OK.  The systems work as intended and well enough.  The inescapable realization comes quickly though that there are actually only 10 enemy types.  Even then, it doesn’t matter which one you are fighting, you fight almost all of them the same way.  There’s stealth, but the game isn’t really built for stealth.  There’s one mission where you must use stealth.  After that, you never need it.  When your character says they should remain unseen, it’s really just flavor text.  Nothing bad happens if you’re seen because you just kill everyone. Stealth kills can replace combat, except the game isn’t really built for it.  There are no interesting patrol patterns because this isn’t a stealth game.  Story missions constantly try to force you out of stealth with scripted scenes, though oddly you can just stealth again before the arriving foes see you.  Stealth isn’t even used for crimes like lock picking and theft.  You just do it in broad daylight in front of the property owner’s face and nobody cares.  Your combat stats are based on your equipped gear, which is limited by your character level. Chest drops and enemies are all leveled to you though, so it’s a treadmill from level 1 until max level.  You don’t actually get stronger, you just keep up.  There is no unique gear, and Legendary pieces are quite common.  You won't ever have a piece of gear that you are fond of or feel was hard earned.  The reward system is not well thought out.  Gear has tiers like most RPGs, but the drops are all randomized, so your Legendary gear probably all just came from random chests you found, not from completing an epic adventure.  Completing mini-challenges that you find in the world will get you experience and such, but it’s largely of no consequence.  Except one type of challenge that for some reason increases your gear inventory space.  You want to do that one.  But why does it let you carry more stuff?  And why is that even tied to a challenge?  Leveling up also lets you buy upgrades from a skill tree.  Some are cool spell upgrades.  Well done.  Most are miscellaneous upgrades that don’t really belong in a skill tree, but they couldn’t figure out where to put.  Like potion upgrades.  They don’t come from some Herbology or Potion-making challenge where you develop wizarding skills.  No, you earned that by flying through balloons or murder or something.  Speaking of murder, you do a lot of that.  Which is normal for a video game.  But the world also has the idea of “Unforgivable Curses” such as the “killing curse”.  So that’s unforgivable, yet every other quest has you killing humans and goblins in scores.  And you’re no “I only knocked them out” Batman either.  Your character says things like, “there’s one less poacher”.  They’re dead.  But not in an unforgivable way at least.  Exploding your enemies into a fine mist is apparently not Dark Wizard territory.  You don’t get a say in any of this either.  Every mission is linear when started.  There is no extra information that ever changes an outcome.  There are no choices that matter.  Keep someone else's heirloom and they get mad and then nothing of importance comes of it.  All the dialog is for flavor alone.  You don’t want to be a thief for petty revenge?  You can’t do that quest because that's the only path you get.  Here are some other things that I found odd.  There are so many “mini-dungeon” caves dotting the overworld, yet they’re all mostly copy-pasted one-room no-puzzle caves with nothing but one random treasure.  The actual puzzles are all extremely simple, even the ones considered to be great mysteries of Hogwarts.  Simple is good in this case though, since some of them attempt to be unique yet suffer poor design and would never pass as an escape room puzzle. You can’t actually talk to anyone when they’re not part of a quest, or a vendor.  You can’t say, “hi,” to your classmates.  You can’t do anything in your dorm room except check your owl mail.  Literally nothing.  You can’t even sleep. There’s no skill point respec.  But that’s ok because some of the skills are useless anyway.  You can have flying beast mounts, but they’re functionally identical to a broom.  In fact, beasts are, for some reason, clunkier to take off and land with.  They have no landing attack or magical defenses or whatever.  Wizarding games are mentioned but you don’t really get to DO any of them.  Gobstones where?  Quidditch where?  You CAN play Summoner’s Court, but only as a limited number of official matches.  Same with dueling other students.  I think they really did not have the time to finish all of these systems that they planned.  So many things seemed penciled in and then the “temp just for now finish later” elements became the final piece as time grew short.  The game really is quite expansive, and the environment shows that it was built with good intentions.  Hogwarts Legacy is not a bad game per se.  There are just so many half done systems that the RPG experience is simply not a modern one.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game. Only gripes I have with it is that I wish there was more immersion in the school life aspect. Kinda in the direction of Bully, but more in depth.Could use a more diverse roster of enemies, but who knows what the future holds for this game so I'm not pressed.Having an active disciplinary system would've been nice. Losing/gaining points for your house, detention, actual consequences to using dark magic in front of the general public, wandering the school grounds at night being monitored by teachers.Going into the Forbidden Forest should've been more of a challenge with a significant power creep in varying enemies and a bit of survival elements thrown in the longer/deeper you go.This game seriously needed a morality system. Nothing mattered whether I acted like a Hero or a Villain.Last thing for me was the lack of impact making friends/companions was outside of questing. Would've been nice to have classmates to do activities with. A good chunk of those students pretty much got thrown away as soon as you finished their respective questlines.Again, I'm optimistic of the future of this game, and hope some very interesting content is in store for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The gear system is boring. Getting new loot is never interesting and nothing is impactful, it's basically just dress up. Dialogue isn't the type of cringe you see in modern games like the latest Borderlands or Saints Row, but it's extremely boring. I've yet to be interested in anything the NPCs say. All characters are flat and they look just as soulless as they feel. The exploration could be interesting but they opted to make it formulaic instead of handcrafting anything. So you don't find cool new secrets, just another one of a few different categories of brainless puzzles and at the end you get new piece of meaningless level scaled gear.In between story quests you often have to do several social/school quests that are essentially pointless fluff made for fan service and at the end you get a new spell.I just keep hoping something interesting would happen but I'm starting to lose hope. Several aspects of the game have potential but never reach it.Why couldn't this game just have been Rockstar's Bully but set in Hogwarts. Instead they copied the Ubisoft open world model but without its redeeming qualities.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, it's really nice that a game has finally been released that wasn't completely buggy at launch, which is no longer a given these days. Hogwarts is also structured in a way that everyone can find their way around the game and the story, even if they don't know the Harry Potter movies and books. The world is quite large and there is so much to discover that I mostly skipped using the broomstick and just walked around. Overall, it's really one of the best RPGs of recent years. However, there are also 1-2 things that I would have wished for. More influence on the course of the game: you can't really play good or evil. Yes, you can be nice to everyone or sometimes blackmail for completed tasks, but the answer options are very limited and actually have no influence on the course of the game. For the second part, I would like to see more options to behave significantly more good or evil, as these are often not possible in decisive situations. I would also have liked more reference to the house you are assigned to, such as the dormitory as a kind of base with a wardrobe where you can store all your found clothes. These are actually my only two criticisms. Otherwise, the game is simply nice and it was fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Hogwarts Legacy is a good game, although it may not be considered exceptional or groundbreaking. However, it delivers an intense beginning to the story, with enjoyable levels of fan-service that reference the Harry Potter and Fantastic Beasts movies. The game's overall atmosphere is positive, and it benefits from almost flawless technical implementation, a rare feat in today's gaming industry.One of the game's strengths is its strong combat mechanics, which start simple but become more complex and engaging as the game progresses. The graphical design and art style are also impressive, especially at extreme settings at 4K, although a decent PC is required to run the game this way.On the downside, the game suffers from repetitiveness and an overabundance of points of interest on the map, which can feel like mere placeholders after a while. The Merlin trials also feel lackluster, and the caves and camps become monotonous after the middle game. These factors contribute to the game feeling like a grind, which may not be appealing to non-diehard fans of the series. The sound and music also become repetitive, which can be a turn-off.The most significant technical problem is the difficulty in focusing on enemies or objects when there are many on the screen. The user interface could also be more user-friendly, with features like a "Sell All" button or the ability to buy multiple potions at once.Despite these flaws, there is potential for interesting story-based DLCs in other locations, which could make for an enjoyable gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it doesn't matter if you're a fan of the universe the game takes place in or not. The lore, the characters, and the rather nicely sized open world map feel nice to explore in, the combat is fun, and for once we have the rare and exquisite quality of having NPCs that match your movement speed. Plus, being able to deck yourself out in whatever cool clothes you want as collected cosmetics and still keep the stats of the better gear is a wonderful addition that more games need to replicate. For fans of the franchise, it's a lovely delve into a world you're already familiar with and getting to see different sides of wizarding life like you haven't gotten to before. For those people who are just buying it to try it because of the hype, you will not be disappointed. Go out, explore the Forbidden Forest, jump into the Black Lake, and soar through the skies to your hearts content while blasting people apart with your favorite spells. The devs and everyone behind the scenes creating the game and storyboard for it have put together a fantastic experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I admit I was weary when first considering purchasing this game.The negative reviews lead me to believe this game was nothing but a cheap but pretty modern game cash grab; but I am so glad that they were wrong.This game has by far the most engaging story and feel I have ever experienced in a game.It is as they say, a must have for any Harry Potter world connoisseur.The music is outstandingly composed and brings that John Williams feel into the game that you experience in the first two movies. Never before have I experienced a game that changes its music depending on the season.The amount of detail placed into the world, in all seasons, is simply out of this world. Having the ability to play this game on maximum settings with ray tracing made me take more pictures than I ever did in my lifetime. The views, the school, the creatures and everything the game has to throw at you are simply amazing.The battle mechanics are great, although quite challenging as you only have 4 spell slots and have to change them using the F1 - F4 keys. But the great thing is, they are fully customizable. And if you play your cards right you'll gain access to all three unforgivable curses which completely transform your fighting style.It takes about 50 hours to complete the main quest and the best thing is, the game tells me I've only completed 51% of it. So if you're looking for a long game to sink your claws into, this is definitely the game.You can customise your wand, your appearance, your broom and your room of requirement.You can tend to all sorts of magical plants that you can turn into handy potions.You can tend to magical beasts which in return provide you the resources to upgrade your clothing attire.My final words are...If you put up with some of the more 'modern stuff' that people have been going on about in the negative reviews, it really is a great game to play for those who enjoy magical worlds.

_childDocuments_.review: Hogwarts Legacy is a role-playing video game developed by Jam City, released for mobile devices in 2018. The game is set in the Wizarding World and allows players to create their own character, attend Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, and experience life as a student wizard.The graphics in Hogwarts Legacy are impressive and accurately capture the look and feel of the Harry Potter world. The character customization options are also extensive, allowing players to create a unique avatar. The story is engaging, with new mysteries and challenges to uncover as the player progresses through the years at Hogwarts. The voice acting is top-notch, with many familiar voices from the Harry Potter movies reprising their roles.One of the standout features of Hogwarts Legacy is the magic system. Players must learn and master spells in order to progress through the game and complete challenges. The spellcasting mechanics are well designed, making the process of casting spells feel intuitive and enjoyable.The game also offers a rich social experience, allowing players to interact with other students and build relationships. Players can join clubs, make friends, and even have romantic relationships with other characters. This adds a new level of depth to the game, making it feel like a truly immersive experience.Overall, Hogwarts Legacy is a must-play for fans of the Harry Potter franchise. The game is well-designed, with impressive graphics, engaging storytelling, and a wealth of content to enjoy. Whether you're a die-hard fan or just a casual player, you'll find something to love in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: After spending little over 100 hours on this game I must say that I love it. It really feels new and different from many games that are already out there and really threw me for a loop even if I had quite high expectations for this game.The combat is great. The environment is beautiful. The characters you meet and befriend are likable, relatable and most of the time interesting. The mechanic with taking care of beasts almost had me in tears the first time I walked into the vivarium,BUT! And there is a big but. There is a reason I do not give this game 10/10. First  the beginning and middle of the game your character feels REALLY... Mary Sue ish... Your character goes to learn a spell, learns it on the first try and everyone is in awe. I mean really compliments you like you are Jesus born anew. You go to retrieve something at the bottom of a lake. Have you ever dove before? No? Everyone is in awe of your ability to be able to dive so well on the first try. At beast class you pretty much befriend all beasts by looking at them etc etc. Your character is SO perceptive and intelligent and can do no wrong. It kind of ticked me off to be honest. Also the fact that it felt like the developers already had a character in mind for this story, how they would act what they would be like etc. The only thing you really control are some choices, what your character look like and whether this character is an ahole or not. I mean what if my character love spiders? Pretty much every time when you defeat spiders the main character comments how much they hate spiders. What if I want my character to be more like Hagrid? And I wanted my character to be an all loving beast freak and it felt like my character was not allowed to because the developers already had put up a frame of what my character should be like. The Mary Sue thing gets better by the end portion of the game but God I almost wanted to punch all characters that treated me like a messiah. I mean I know the chosen one trope is kind of a given but the chosen one can have layers, make mistakes etc. Just take Mass Effects commander Shepherd. *SPOILER ALERT*I mean commander Shepherd fails a couple of missions, and he sucks at dancing, not everyone agrees with his decisions and sometimes for good reasons, he even has to work with the bad guy for a while and he is still "the chosen one" with a lot of skills etc. And you still feel like you can mold commander Shepherd into what character you wish for him or her to be like. So Id have like more choices for your character.Then we have the mini games... Or specifically the alohomora mini game...Guys seriously... Alohomora is supposed to be a convenient spell that opens doors quickly... Who thought it was a brilliant idea to make a mini game for a spell that is supposed to be the most practical and convenient spell?! I mean it is not a hard mini game and it does not take up much time but when you have to go through that mini game to open 50 different doors it gets old pretty fast... And again the spell is supposed to be the most practical and convenient spell and you just managed to make it tedious as f to use.... I sighed every time I had to unlock a bloody door.Then we have the Merlin trials...I actually really liked them. I really really liked the concept and thought it was fun before I found out I would have to do them almost 100 times if I wanted to complete them all. Seeing as I like to complete as much as possible in any game I play, something I liked and enjoyed quickly turned into another thing I sighed about every time I saw that leaf icon pop up everywhere I went. I get it you don't have to do all of them. But it still bugged me that they could not have implemented some of these challenges into the game without needing to do them almost hundred times to complete them all.The story is also really nothing special. It is not bad by any means and they could have done way worse on that front. It is fine and somewhat creative but not a story I will remember for years to come type of deal.Having said all that I still love love LOVE this game. It is a magical experience to say the least. The magic that is implemented in the exploration aspect is so much fun and everything in this game is simply wonderful and feels magical (except the things I mentioned above.) The quests never got boring and the side quests themselves where a joy to play through, exploring the world and Hogwarts for hours was a wonder and delight and just yeah. This game is great!

_childDocuments_.review: A game that does not aim to be the best looking or most innovative game ever created. Here you just get what you see: an interesting story in the harry potter universe, no gamebreaking bugs and no mtx or tons of uneccesary dlc content. and thats what you should appreciate at a time like this. For a fan of the universe this potentially is goty material just cause of the presentation and the details of the world, for everyone else its a decent open world rpg with repetetive open world objectives, but still a good amount of interesting main and sidequests.the rpg mechanics (equipment, skill, attributes) could be more interesting for sure, but the combat gameplay and spellcasting + animations are fun enough to keep you engaged.overall i can recommend the game to everyone who does not completly hate open world games.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd describe it as 3rd person Skyrim with almost Dark Souls style (ranged) combat assuming you play this on HARD, which you def should.  Even on HARD, it feels just a smidge too easy; I chose to do the Dueling quest without a companion which pits you against 4x other caster enemies and as long as you time your "block" spell correctly - you can do that without taking any damage at all.  Still fun gameplay imo, absolute LOADS of collectibles to explore and find and it's all kept track of so you know what you might be missingAs for the "politically devisive" aspects; the first time you meet the trans character it is very jarring - like why is this a thing?  And everyone always referring to you as "They/them" instead of he/she is def annoying, but if you ignore those aspects, I'd still recommend this game to anyone who likes the Harry Potter books or just likes this style of gameplay.PS there is a mod available if you want to actually play as a white person; the default "whitest" setting is still quite tan, and there is a reason everyone praises how attractive Professor Garlick is (all the other female npcs... aren't)Keep in mind; there are still loads of performance issues at the time of this writing.  Some people cannot see more than the epilepsy warning before crashing, others have constant stuttering issues, your mileage may vary, but I'd hope they'll all be fixed with some more patches

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:The architecture is unrealThe outfits are really incredibleThe combat is very satisfyingThe story is interesting and compellingThe world is huge, with a ton of stuff to doFlying on the broom is very satisfyingConsI only have one major con with this game, but it is a big one:The rewards for completing quests, side quests, defeating difficult enemies is...lackluster at best. You don't really feel compelled to go find a secret tunnel to an underground dungeon or solve a difficult puzzle room only to get another pair of quidditch gloves. The biggest oversight to this game in my opinion is that the rewards are very unsatisfying. There should be spells that you can learn or special magical items (that actually do something interesting when used) whenever you complete certain side quests or kill certain infamous foes. You want to feel like your character is getting more powerful in unique ways when you do something that isn't necessary to the main plot but difficult none the less. I hope they fix this in the sequel, but I'm doubtful seeing as how it would be a complete overhaul.

_childDocuments_.review: Hogwarts Legacy, a visually stunning game that captures the magic of the wizarding world, is an impressive display of artistry. The art team deserves big kudos for the stunning visuals that make the game look beyond beautiful. From the intricately designed Hogwarts Castle to the spellbinding environments, the attention to detail is phenomenal.However, the same cannot be said about the game's storyline, which falls short of expectations. It lacks depth and fails to engage the player. The missions are repetitive, offering little variety, and the side missions are lackluster, seemingly thrown in for the sake of being there without providing any real challenge.Despite the game's shortcomings, it is undeniable that the art and music teams have done a fantastic job in creating a captivating world. The music, composed by a team of skilled musicians, perfectly complements the visuals and adds to the immersive experience.In conclusion, Hogwarts Legacy is a game that looks beautiful but lacks substance. While the art team has done an excellent job in creating a visually stunning world, the repetitive missions and uninspiring storyline are a letdown. Nonetheless, fans of the wizarding world will still enjoy the experience of exploring Hogwarts and interacting with the magical creatures that inhabit it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hogwarts Legacy has a lot of polish, but as soon as you get away from the starting regions, the world starts to feel empty and incomplete. Take for example the dungeons that contain randomized loot. Upon entering the dungeon, your character mentions something along the lines of "staying vigilant" or "being wary", when for the most part you 1) run in, 2) get the loot, and 3) run back out. These dungeons feel dull compared to the very first dungeon that you get access to that you may miss altogether (in Hogsmeade during the night in the graveyard).In addition, the actions that you take don't really matter in the game. Regardless of what class you take, the story options are essentially the same, outside of the one quest that differs in the main quest line. There are multiple answers you can choose within quests, but outside of one side quest near the end of the game, your choice does not matter. All options lead to the same conclusion outside of minor changes that has no overarching effects on your character.Based on what most players will first encounter within the Hogwarts school, the world feels so alive and you end up wanting more (listening to student's banter, Peeves and its antics, and the life style of the elves and ghosts). Yet when you take that same expectation and travel outside of the school and Hogsmeade, you can clearly see that the developers did not have enough time to put the same amount of liveliness outside the regions.And it's because of that expectation that I can't recommend this game. It feels incomplete, like the world isn't complete. It feels like the developers spent so much time making Hogwarts and Hogsmeade just right, that they had to quickly finish up the main/side quests, and didn't have time to implement anything else. Maybe if the developers go back and flesh out the world (making the dungeons actually "dangerous", enabling Quidditch, allowing random events on the road), the game will finally feel complete and I will be able to recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really tried to love this game, given that Harry Potter is my favourite series.Good, but uninspired for what it COULD be. The shield-breaking thing is cool, if not canon, so it gets points for that from me. Other than that, it's a lot of the same. Here they did really well. They’re loveable, unique and generally quite well-animated. Side quests and collectable lore tidbits don’t really do anyone justice though, or make me think anything different of them, which sucks. They don’t have a role other than to add flavour - and even then, they don’t add any  to the game.But that's about where the good ends for me.This game took some of the best elements of Elden Ring and The Witcher 3 - and put the Harry Potter IP on it - then COMPLETELY neglected to flesh any of those elements out and make it a masterpiece. After 8 hours, there is no reason to want to explore, since you know every single thing you COULD encounter, each of which involves the same set of empty mechanics recycled over and over for each point on the map.A lot of the mechanics, spells, and potions are recycled in the most dull ways across the map, and are soulless and meaningless. They're also locked behind story quests - not classes - even though your character is a student.The main story elements that they force you through - they’re all the same, and don’t entice you to use your spells in any meaningful or intelligent way beyond some puzzles.No Quidditch. No Patronuses. No familiars. No classes. - not even a brewing minigame.Outside of its beautiful facade, and some really nice background chatter and dialogue, the school is devoid of life or magic. There’s no real reason to return to the castle at all. Learning spells is a quicktime event and the “classes” are scripted cutscenes. You’re allowed to just walk or fly off the school grounds whenever you want with no ramifications - there are prefect and teacher patrols in two quests - to teach you disillusionment, and how to sneak, and then never again. The staff don’t patrol here, nor do they chill in their rooms after hours, considering you can just break into them for lore tidbits that, given how uninspired the rest of the game is, I'm not even tempted to read. The Restricted Section isn’t full of forbidden books, it’s just a set of rooms locked behind some bars that you can then access forevermore after the first time. The librarian is nowhere to be seen beyond that first sneak quest, and the caretaker waits in the same spot every day and night so you can collect stuff for his silly side quest. The only reason to return - the “collect-a-thon” aspect for the caretaker - is locked behind meaningless side quests, using spells that are useless aside from collecting.After about an hour of flying around the open world, I guarantee that you've seen everything there is to see, other than the new scenery in other areas. The same sort of camps, landmarks etc. are recycled constantly, with the same enemies, same spells and potions required, etc. The flying is clunky and unintuitive, even with the best broom in the game. There's no reason to explore unless you want new screensavers - because even when you land, the world has no magic other than the visuals. Also, there's the ability to jump, but there's barely anything you can jump OVER. Would have been better combining it into a vault/dodge mechanic. There are only about 20 spells out of the hundreds in-universe, and none of them interact with each other in a meaningful or creative way. The coolest thing you can do is solve puzzles, or juggle enemies in the air with dumb, uninspired combos. You can learn the Unforgivables - but there are no ramifications for being a dark wizard, which directly opposes the universe. Casting them in front of civilians has no ramifications, either. Six or so of them. Same as spells, just a simple “collect these ingredients” and it’s an uninvolved animation that you have to wait to complete. Not a brewing process, no minigame, nothing. The potions themselves are useless unless it’s for combat and you want to face the same enemies over and over and over again across the map at the Witcher-esque bandit camps. Or on the story, which is boring as ♥♥♥♥. I initially wanted to explore so I could tame magical beasts, and again, it’s locked behind half of the really ♥♥♥♥ story. This could have been amazing. Can you bond with them? Choose your own mount? No. You can sell them, breed them (and then sell them), or harvest their body parts for potions ingredients. For the useless potions. Also, you “tame” them by casting spells on them, chasing them down and kidnapping them. And you can’t even tame the one dragon there is. Also with all the collecting you can do - you don’t get a familiar or pet, OR have reason to or means of casting a Patronus.  A cosmetically-customisable room that you spend more time in than your own dormitory. Cool... for a room that you go back to… to power up your cosmetically-customisable clothing (this would have had more of an impact for me if the game itself was magical enough for me to want to walk slowly through it and explore and be a PART of it, without coming across more of the same thing, everywhere). You can also brew your useless potions here, or grow plants, also just time-locked queueable interactions. Useless. No prefect patrols, no meaningful ways to use it. Especially in the story. There are some areas where scripted enemies jump out of thin air who are supposedly powerful enough to see through your disillusionment, just so they can say a line that’s barely pertinent to the story and force you into the same uninspired, easy combat anyway. If you wanna avoid anything outside of the story, use your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ broom. The models and attention to detail graphically are gorgeous. The shaders are pretty terrible, though, and lose a lot of the immersion and magic for me. I run a 3080Ti, and even with Raytracing and max graphics, this is far from the prettiest game I’ve played this generation.This has to be one of the most disappointing games that I've ever played - and I was hyped for NMS on release.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal world design, directly drawn from the Harry Potter universe, but everything else falls completely flat. The characters are one-dimensional, without any additional complexity beyond "good" and "evil," and the dialogue is ridiculously childish to the point of lunacy. The main character is your generic self-insert chosen one protagonist, which can be executed fairly well, but isn't in this case. Your status as a "student" is completely inconsistent with the gameplay and power fantasy plot, while there is almost no interaction with fellow students in a realistic way besides them simply praising you as this yet unbeknownst prodigy. Roleplaying elements are "present," but they feel more haphazardly tacked on rather than actually adding anything of meaning (side quests are as generic as they can be, and dialogue choices offer no real choices or complexity). The gameplay is actually fairly well-executed, duels are fun and engaging, but certain fights certainly rely on sponginess, and the UI design is abhorrent (animations are impressively slow, while important gameplay elements are locked behind talents). Performance issues are present, but not unusably so, although it is comical for this to be an issue in a game with character models ripped straight out of 2015. Despite all this, it's definitely not a terrible game, with a very polished open world, beautiful art direction, and complete faithfulness to the Harry Potter lore, but it's by no means an especially great one, offering nothing new or special despite the illustrious Harry Potter skin. As far as licensed games go, this is a fantastic one, and Harry Potter fans will likely love it, but as far as games go in general, I'd find it difficult to recommend, even though I loved this series when I was younger.6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game still has lag problems but for me this considerably improves the problem I know every one is fed up hearing about supposed fixes to the stuttering and low FPS issues, but these 3 actually worked for me on a 5600x and 3070. Before I did this, I was getting dips to 20fps and even below, some cutscenes went to single digits. I'm not sure exactly which one fixed it for me since I applied these all at once, but I hope this works for others too!    Enable hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling (I had turned this off because it caused issues in another game, I can't remember which one). Windows search for "GPU" to find this setting, a restart is required.    Navigate to "AppData\Local\Hogwarts Legacy\Saved\Config\WindowsNoEditor" and backup "Engine.ini". Add the following to the bottom of the file and save it:[SystemSettings]r.bForceCPUAccessToGPUSkinVerts=Truer.GTSyncType=1r.OneFrameThreadLag=1r.FinishCurrentFrame=0r.TextureStreaming=1r.Streaming.PoolSize=3072r.Streaming.LimitPoolSizeToVRAM=1[ConsoleVariables]AllowAsyncRenderThreadUpdates=1AllowAsyncRenderThreadUpdatesDuringGamethreadUpdates=1AllowAsyncRenderThreadUpdatesEditor=13. This only applies to Nvidia users, set the shader cache size to 10GB in Nvidia control panel global 3D settings.Edit: Wow! I posted this just before bed and super glad to hear it's working for other people as well - I knew it wasn't placebo! The game definitely still needs some optimization patches, but at least it's actually playable now.I forgot to mention, if you have a GPU with more than 8GB VRAM, you can change the pool size from 3072 to 4096, this should help even further. Below are the recommended values for r.Streaming.PoolSize depending on your GPU memory:6GB - 20488GB - 307212GB+ - 4096-5120 (Some people have reported setting it even higher can help on high-end cards like the 4090). I would recommend trying 4096 first, if you notice no improvement then you can try setting it to half of your GPU's VRAM size. This only applies to high end cards with more than 12GB memory.It seems like the Engine.ini fix seems to do the trick for most people. You might also want to try with TextureStreaming turned off (set to 0), some people have said this gives them even better performance. I've not noticed a difference myself, but it might vary depending on your PoolSize setting. Do not set your PoolSize above 3072 if you have an 8GB GPU as it makes the low frame drops return.

Hufflepuff. Ravenclaw. Slytherin. Long ago, the four houses studied together in (mostly) harmony. Then everything changed when the dark wizards attacked. Only a powerful wizard, master of ancient magic, could stop them. But when the world needed one most, they vanished. Hundreds of years have passed, and the Keepers discovered the player, a new 5th year at Hogwarts. And although their magical skills are great, they have a lot to learn before they're ready to save anyone. But I believe the player can save the wizarding world.*Hedwig's Theme plays in the distance*I was one of the people who played the movie adaptation games in the early 2000s. Chamber of Secrets on PS2 was the first open world game I ever played and I absolutely adored it; with my enjoyment of it being the candle I held all other open world games to, until RDR2 came along. I've waited over 20 years for a new Wizarding World game to overtake CoS, and honestly didn't think it would ever happen. I was wrong.This game can be called a Harry Potter spin-off, however I admit that the story and world of Hogwarts Legacy are so convincing and intriguing that you will legitimately forget Harry Potter ever existed while playing. The entire experience felt not only genuine in every way to the Wizarding World, but it stood entirely on it's own as a masterpiece. Being a Wizarding World fan, like me, without a doubt adds to your enjoyment of the game. However, even someone completely turned off to the books/movies can fully appreciate this remarkable, densely packed, made-with-love experience.You can call me the Professor Binns of Hogwarts Legacy reviews.I could write a 20 page essay on my entire thoughts on this game, the good and the bad, and would still have more to say. I could make an Angry Joe review look like a YouTube Short in comparison. However, unfortunately, there's a character limit on Steam reviews, making it impossible to bore you to tears like many students experience in history class at Hogwarts (WHICH YOU CAN ATTEND BTW). My final remarks are that this game is without a doubt worth every penny of the full price, and I hope dearly that this is not the last we will see of Avalanche delving into the Wizarding World. Avalanche have proven themselves as a more than competent, driven, hard-working collection of highly talented industry professionals who are not afraid to put all of their love into creating the best experience possible; even when that experience is far more than most studios would consider adequate.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve never played a Harry Potter game before this, because they  all seemed to just play through the book and movie plot lines over and  over again. Sometimes as Lego people. I read the books, watched the  movies, and therefore held no interest in the franchises foray into my  favored hobby. Legacy has quite literally the game I’ve been waiting for and that’s a shared sentiment I’ve seen.Story wise, we play a newcomer to Hogwarts but we’re inducted as a fifth year. Extremely rare but not unheard of. Your custom character’s backstory is completely obscured and the story nor dialog reveals a single iota of information about who they are and where they come from. It’s up to us to fill in those blanks.Immediately in the tutorial/prologue (the tutorials continue well into the game itself) it’s revealed that our MC (main character) possesses the rare ability to witness and utilize a form of “ancient magic”. We then discover a strange, previously unknown symbol to the wizarding community and alongside your mentor Professor Fig, that kicks off the main plot. In my first impressions I considered this a bit derivative, as if it’s banking off the movie’s success. The game doesn’t waste a single chance to reference something from the books or movies, like the mooncalves first seen in Strange Beasts or the mandrake replanting class from Chamber of Secrets. Some moments are cute, but during the mandrake replanting I found myself thinking we’d explore literally anything else because per my previous point; I’ve seen that already. Other times are more subtle, like how you can literally stand at the entrance to the Chamber of Secrets with a little lore page detailing a little snake etching but no other in-game indication of what it could mean. I prefer the subtle approach to fanservice like that. As stated, some moments are better than others but this game takes the shotgun approach.One of the things that awed me about the game is how absolutely gorgeous it is, down to the atmosphere. Despite what other reviews state, I find the facial animations to be some of the best I’ve seen. There is the occasional oddity where after every spoken line, an NPC will briefly revert back to their neutral expression which can be jarring depending on how stable your game is. It’s often seamless, but sometimes my computer lags a bit (I’m a bit under the minimum requirements) and I just see their faces cancel itself out.As I always say to anyone who will listen, the first once or twice I did the flying class I could not stop smiling. The teacher spoke to me as if I was on an amusement park ride but I didn’t care, as I got a fairly scenic route through the Hogwarts grounds that we didn’t really get in the movies. Tutorial mission thought it might have been, the music cues were perfect for the mood it was going for.Fans of Harry Potter may very well be in two camps. One wants to capture their childhood nostalgia, the idea that they could be whisked away to a whimsical school to be taught reality breaking spells. The other camp perhaps just want a nice action RPG that just happens to be set in the universe and lore that they love. The first camp will absolutely adore the first 10-15 hours, after which the classes will very much dry up. They’re cute, giving the usual “move the mouse in a certain way” minigames. I do wish they were more complex, or there was more to do but I also completely understand that this game is very much marketed towards teens so they need to keep the pace going and the objectives accessible. Meanwhile, the second camp of fans will very much enjoy themselves. The whole prologue of the game can take a few to several hours before the final mechanic of beast-rearing is introduced, so after that the combat takes center stage....And the combat is actually quite great. There can be a good flow between using the right category of spell to cancel out color coded enemy shields, while making sure to counter or dodge as the right prompt presents itself. Players of Arkham, Mad Max, or Middle-Earth will be familiar with the flow. After a while however, the region level locking became a problem as the late game became far too easy. At one point I was a level 35 (cap is 40) but I kept facing level locked enemies like 20 or 30, almost all of which only took four basic attacks to kill. I had to resort to mods to remedy this issue and increase the difficulty. Hard mode in-game does well in raising the reaction times needed, and it also makes enemy shields come up much quicker, often quicker than your cooldowns which forces more spell switching which I enjoy a lot. However for those who catch onto the flow of it, even Hard difficulty can come across as fairly easy. Another thing I went to mods to help with.I feel like this game brings to the table that HP fans have  wanted. If you wanted the school experience, it’s here in in bite sized  chunks, a class or two at a time for you to navigate the wonderfully  designed school with all kinds of bits and bobs to discover. If you’re  one of those HP fans who thought the combative implications of the world  went under explored, then there’s plenty of it to be had here as well  between shooting at wolves, spiders, bandits, rebels, and other  creatures with fake made-up names.    It is perhaps not as much of an open world as players may have wanted.  There’s plenty to explore to find chests and loot, sometimes blocked by  ways you don’t have access to quite yet. The game doesn’t throw every  tool at you immediately to let you loose upon the world and for good  reason; because there’s not a whole hell of a lot to do town by town.  This is not a “pick a direction and go” kind of world, as early on you  get a tutorial notation saying that some activities are straight up  locked until you get certain spells.  The real meat of the game is in its quests. I will say most of the side quests are rather uninspired and after a couple dozen hours I was only really doing them to unlock appearances and crafts for our Room of Requirement, a place you can decorate and utilize as you see fit. But most of the writing in them were fairly basic. You help one goblin get his cart with art supplies, and that’s really the end of that story. Another you help track down a woman’s missing brother, which just introduces the Inferi (undead) of the lore. Game tells you to hit them with fire, and that’s all there is to that story.In fact, a lot of the game is tutorialized in the first half which can be grating for those of us who catch onto how the game works quickly. This was particularly obvious when you are introduced to the Room of Requirement, where a Weasley ancestor spells out every little thing you can do in the room down to making you place five rugs and five wall hangings before the quest continues, as if doing it once isn’t enough to understand the basics. Again I understand that they do this to keep the game accessible for the lower end of age brackets. While we’re talking about that kind of thing, some of  the activities can feel a bit like busywork. I am particularly irritated  at Merlin trials, which are never complex but always tedious. There are times where I couldn’t even find the solution, despite flying around spamming the Revelio (revealing the area, Eagle Vision Style) and then discovering that if you go to far away from the  trial it resets itself.  They’re also the only way to increase your inventory space  (which fills up quickly because loot is absolutely everywhere). I’m okay  with the various bandit camps and animal lairs but it does reek of that  Ubisoft-ness that has tired gaming in the last few years. 100 hours in and I probably have another 20-30 more to go as I continue exploring the nexus mods page. I do not at all regret buying the game and I’m enjoying it greatly. It really was the game I was waiting for, and I really hope the developers take notice and work on expanding the great foundation they laid out for us.

_childDocuments_.review: Before diving into the review, let me make one thing perfectly clear: Hogwarts Legacy is an open-world action RPG, not a Hogwarts Student simulator, and should be approached and measured as such. This means that the devs have had to make certain... contrivances that die-hard fans of the Harry Potter universe might take issues with, including but not limited to:-Modern day Hogwarts is know for it's rather draconian rules regarding student freedom of movement and usage of spells outside of school. However since these rules were not in effect in the mid-1800s none of this applies to the PC - a 15-year-old underage student - who are free to roam everywhere, at any time and use magic everywhere without penalty. The PC will also get into fights to the deaths with wild beasts and adult wizards on an almost daily basis and rack up a kill tally to make even you-know-who jealous, in addition to engaging in the usual RPG petty thievery and trespassing without much attention or oversight from the authorities.-While the game has a day/night cycle this is mostly inconsequential. Even tho students roaming about at night is a big no-no in the Harry Potter canon, no-one bats an eye at the PC going for a night-time stroll. While certain quest NPCs are only available at either day or night, most of the world goes about it's business: shops remain open for instance. You can wait and pass time anywhere, and your House dormitory is mostly for show - there's little reason to go there.-Lessons in magic serve as mostly plot advancers and are not required to be attended at a fixed schedule. You can go to them at your leisure. While lessons sometimes include small mini-games, it's mostly just a short cut-scene, before you are back to the open-world. While references are made to the Hogwarts house points, there isn't actually a tally to worry about and your actions or inactions have no impact.If you can suspend your disbelief in these points - possibly by surmising that in the 1800s things were probably much less organised than in modern times - you're gonna have a great time with Hogwarts Legacy. -The game is absolutely gorgeous and Hogwarts and the surrounding lands are beautifully created with a reasonable faithfulness to the source material.-The story is well-written and engaging and fairly well paced; you're never left wondering what you're doing or why for very long.-Combat is fast-paced and similar to other games in the 3rd person action RPG genre such as Elden Ring or The Witcher and requires both blocking and dodging in addition to selecting appropriate counter-attacks to exploit weaknesses. There is little lasting consequence to failing, and this makes the whole experience a lot less frustrating and more welcoming to new players of the genre, tho veterans may find it a tad too easy even on the hardest setting.-Talents allows for limited PC customization that emphasize different play-styles: raw spell damage or additional spell utility, consumable empowerment or stealth.-Many sections of the game require stealth and puzzle solving but the difficulty is well-balanced.-Tons of small and neat references to the books and movies.
