_childDocuments_.review: I think the game as such is pretty amazing, but for me, it was perhaps a bit disappointing because I had a lot of expectations from the game given the marketing and my lifelong obsession with the Harry Potter series. I've finished it once and haven't felt the need to play it again since then, but I can't quite put my finger on why exactly that is. I feel like there's something missing, even though the graphics are amazing, the combat is likewise interesting, even the characters are well written and you truly feel like you're at Hogwarts. I especially appreciated the addition of magical beasts, though, to be honest, taking care of them soon became boring and repetitive. For me, it's lacking "depth" or additional details that would make the game more immersive. First of all, there is no morality system in the game. While you can choose how you act in certain situations and what your response will be, there's basically no punishment if you choose the worse options - such as not returning someone's things back, being rude to a random stranger or, on the other hand, helping the bad guys. Everywhere you walk, people are always super happy to see you and view you as the hero and saviour, no matter if you just stole someone's books or robbed an innocent person just a few seconds ago. As a result, I felt like my choices didn't really matter that much in the end. Even though you can improve and gain experience throughout the game, I sometimes didn't even feel the need to do that because since the first time you set foot in Hogwarts, you just seem to be everyone's favourite. You're allowed to do anything you want inside the castle and out, even though the other students can't leave the castle after a certain time. You can't sleep in your dorms and the way night/day are handled seems a bit awkward to me. You can't just sit in the Great Hall and have a lunch with friends while talking about something school-related. As such, I sometimes felt like a Hogwarts visitor rather than a student, since you have a lot of privileges as the main character that just aren't relatable for some reasons.Having said that, I really enjoyed the 73 hours I spent playing this game and I'll most likely return to it again one day. It truly is a great game with lots of things to do and a lot of places to freely explore, which is probably the main benefit of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This thumbs up comes with a bit of a caveat. The game is notorious for running poorly (for seemingly unknown reasons) even on top-notch hardware. If you're a Harry Potter fan, it's probably everything you ever hoped for. Tons of references and a living, breathing Hogwarts that was created in amazing detail. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start with the obvious, this game is worth the buy. If you are a fan of the Wizarding World, this is not news to you. Gameplay is fun, graphics are pretty (Atlhough performance issues are real), you get to play around with your spells, and the exploration is (in most parts) great! Now, here are the things I found negative about the game.- Friendship, it is at the center of the Harry Potter books, and I could not give a ♥♥♥♥ about these people... not only do they never interact between each-other (They are only YOUR friends and that's that) but they are emply shells only here to give you a questline... with the only exception being Poppy, who is 100% best character in the game.- Story was generic, with an overpowered protagonist, and the ending is loosely strung together with a single boss fight and very little consequences to the size of the actual threat.- The exploration at times feels like a chore, there are too many different types of collectibles, and Merlin Trials are really just annoying since there are like 5 minigames and 95 trials. The map is not that helpful either, I could of used those famous 'Ubisoft Towers' to know where all of the collectibles where ahead of time in certain zones.- Immersion... you can cast Avada Kedavra without any consequences, you have no choices in quest lines, even if you pick the 'no' dialogue options, your character end up saying yes... it's kind of sad because in the end, you are only playing that one character the devs wanted you to play.Overall, I think the game could have been improved by simply focusing on Hogwarts Scholarship, slice of life-type story with an over-arching story to give you a big bad by the end... I feel like the lack of real friendship (And romance) made this game feel a little... impersonnal.

_childDocuments_.review: Good story and exploration!! You are able to customize your character extensively and customize your clothing freely without needing to worry about what gear options help gameplay but look gross. Rowling's previous controversy towards the LGBTQIA+ community, it seems the developers actually tried to incorporate trans and queer people into this game, without having any of the characters respond negatively in game.The story is very interesting and involving. You can choose what quests to go on when, or just explore if that's more up your alley. However, the facial expressions on the characters as well as the voice acting is merely decent. Though, its tolerable due to the level of detail in nearly everything else.There are numerous glitches, but I've not come across any that interrupt gameplay. In fact, the glitches I have come across have done nothing but make me laugh. (Not saying they shouldn't be fixed as they do somewhat interfere with immersion, just that they aren't something to completely put you off about the game.)TLDR; If you like the style of RDR2, puzzles, magic, and mythical beasts, this will be the game for you. Also, if you're queer or an ally and you've been thinking of buying this, yet don't want to support J.K. Rowling, keep this in mind; Rowling is a rich white lady who, no matter what, is gaining money day-by-day. Your $60 purchase will be going to the other developers before it even touches Rowling. If you want to buy this, just bite the bullet. It will bring you joy, and that's whats important.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game for Harry Potter fans who've always dreamt of stepping foot into the world of Hogwarts, attention to detail and atmosphere is up there in terms of one of the best I've ever seen in a game, truly a must play for HP fans who want to immerse themselves in the story.However, I will say the game has a few notable flaws. Firstly, throughout my game play I encountered numerous bugs, most were just annoying visual glitches but occasionally I'd have to load back in certain areas where puzzle pieces would go missing or my character would be unable to move.Secondly, while combat is initially fun and unlocking new spells is exciting, combat soon becomes rather repetitive and ends up feeling more like a chore toward the end of the game. When I reached the final boss area, every time I had more enemies chucked at me I was simply thinking 'Ugh....This again?' which made it significantly less immersive. Puzzles also become rather repetitive, dungeons too, making it rather frustrating to even bother dealing with them unless you're a completionist like me. Lastly, there are some minor annoyances like not being able to multi-sell items, only 40 inventory slots in a game based on a series where you can quite literally own bags that lead to other dimensions???, being unable to scrap potions (which is frustrating if you've reached max capacity of a certain potion, therefore unless you discard one, the slot will be taken up on the potion maker) and lastly, in my opinion the game lacks replayability, once you've seen it all there's truly no point in starting again unless you want to replay everything you've already seen. I will say however, if you're looking for an extremely immersive world with beautiful scenery, seamless travel between checkpoints, beautiful oddities and wonderful customisation, this is truly the game for you. While things may get repetitive, simply the world itself is enough to keep you immersed, I really did feel like I was re-living my childhood playing this game. All in all an 8.5/10 game for me, well worth playing for those of you who love Harry Potter, and even those of you who do not.

_childDocuments_.review: My time in Hogwarts Legacy has been memorable, marvellous, and magical... and yet also mediocre, misguided and monotonous.The world building in this game is of course fantastical, with the setting that Harry Potter books describe, it is hard not to be successful, yet inspired games are the majority of most Harry Potter games I have played. Hogwarts Legacy actually succeeds in bring the imagination alive with Hogwarts itself and a few choice locations in the world whose ambience was successfully illustrated to the players great satisfaction. I believe the world is the greatest selling point of this game, and considering how much time you spend in it, a good thing indeed.This for me is where the positives end, in my opinion... however I imagine for most, some of the points I bring up will still be attractive to the average gamer.The gameplay I would describe as easily accessible to anyone picking up this game for the first time. With multiple difficulties available to choose from affecting neither story or achievements, anyone can jump in. I personally like a bit of a challenge though, and found that starting the game was as difficult as it got. The more you progress the greater the tools and spells you have access to, some of which in my opinion are so overpowered that playing with them takes the fun out of it. For others this will be good news but I personally found it to be unbalanced. That said it is still fun blasting enemies with your multitude of spells in various combinations to achieve increasingly damaging affects.Aside from spell casting combat which has colour coded parse checking for the spells you use... which fine, its so anyone could get it, there is some level of quick time events, with perfect block mechanics, but it is so easy to do I felt the reward for succeeding in anything becoming rather mundane. There is some flight sequences side quests, but mostly it serves as an increased movement function. There is like one mini-game which I found lack lustre, and a large amount of frankly simple puzzle solving, with maybe one or two optional exceptions you may never come across if you aren't going out of your way.There is unfortunately a lot of progression related blocking in the game right from the get go, where you have to progress in the story to have the necessary abilities to do certain things... The reasons for this decision make no reasonable sense as you are a student studying magic... you have next to no choice on when you study things or what, as looking into your curriculum is entirely out of your hands, which really breaks immersion and frustrates the player as it means a lot of back tracking for things that could otherwise have been done when the player comes across it.There are some good characters and great voice acting, but ultimately the story is pretty linear with no player choice to speak of, and where there is choice it has no overarching affect on the game except in like two situations I can think of. Both towards the end of the game.It's a pretty brute force plot, with mcguffins a plenty. You can't expect too much when they are inserting characters into an already established world, with a story that has no affect on the universe.You might like some characters but you probably won't care about whats going on with the story.Character customisation is pretty good I think. A wide variety of clothing options... but you have to unlock or find them. The character creator is okay, I think it could be worse, and it could be better.Sound design is actually very in tune with the movies, and I enjoyed the ambient music and sound effects. It isn't overly complicated, and has little bearing on assisting you in terms of gameplay but it is okay.Level Design... oh dear, some of the choices made in terms of level design were crap, some were brilliant. Hogwarts for example, bloody fantastic! A veritable treasure trove of nooks and cranny's to explore, everywhere you go there is a call back to the books in some fashion, and it is a delight to just wander around... the over arching world leaves something to be desired, though the general appearance is well done in terms of English and Scottish countryside. When it comes to "dungeons" or smaller single instance locations, then it kind of breaks down. No really memorable places, with 90% of them being uninspired caves. Some of the puzzles are nice, but none overly difficult, so none are really rewarding... well for me anyway, very accessible to all ages though.I wouldn't play this game for the gameplay. Play it for the world, it's individual characters, and then get out. You do not stand to benefit trying to treat this as an expansive game with a level of challenge befitting something with an in depth combat system, branching story lines which reward you for time invested or for anything else you might expect this game to be. Harry Potter fans, you can have a field day I am sure!6/10

_childDocuments_.review: ___It is still good and i still recommend it even to non HP fans. But it's not perfect.  The spell UI. Having only 4 sets of 4 spells is endlessly annoying! I know it's a dpad  thing but there must be a better way. Let alone on a Keyboard. Switching the sets when there are 6 (six) more number keys is tupid already. But there are too many spells you regularly need for even the 4x4 limit. You HAVE to constantly shuffle them around manually. It is plain . And there is not yet a mod that really fixes that. There are some Auto Hotkey script work arounds to avoid the switching but they don't raise the number.  While it is a good Harry Potter esk story with not too much open world filler, the writing is weird. People talk in what the writers probably thought like a 19th century way. It just isn't. It's some weird cumbersome variant of modern english (read some Dickens or Twain to compare)  Also voice acting  is agressively friendly making it highly unimmersive and weird for Slytherin players.Play Hugfflepuff or Gryffindor for the writing CLEARLY is aimed at that.   Biggest one is timers. Like long potion brewing and plant growing timers with very little yield.  It is way too tedious and pace killing. It's busywork that is also slowed down. Then too long spell cooldowns (worse  for the 4x4 switching problem). . Self tips all 2 secs  while doing puzzles are absolutely You feel treated like an absolute  idiot.  Puzzles are not so hard you need them. Deek constantly talking to you. The fast travel lady constantly talking to you....   (mods: NoPuzzleHints, BeQuiet, Deek Silencio)The UI looks suspiciously like AC Oddyssey. And the open world gameplay does of course the ususal things.  But everything about  the game is just much better. You can tell they don't try to sell you XP/Ressource microtransactions because even the level system and the looting/crafting are ok. Much less of it, much less grindy, the world is not spammed with nonsensical xp/loot grind spots, and the level system even make sense in the context, given you are literally learning in a school.  The level system is also much less brickwally.  Fights become more challenging but managable. not: easy. While AC Odyssey: Enemy up to 3 levels above you=Easy. 4 levels above Immortal one hitting god.Tbf AC Valhalla fixed at least that problem too. In HPL you have a hard fight but a chance against high level enemies.  The story takes a much more important role over the open world stuff and isn't an afterthought.Not every side quest is a masterpiece but also no lazy xp grinders.  Or mega lazy "liberate 10 areas-the end" crap.   Also the details were more important than plain world size. And finally, no Ubisoft launcher, mod support (No-spider mod available), no forced online crap (+ EAC spyware)....

_childDocuments_.review: I was in primary school when the first Harry Potter novel came out and I remember at the time that we were basically going through a literary crisis. There were concerns that people, especially children, would no longer read novels for enjoyment and reading would become a thing of the past. Anyone who was interested in reading was made fun of or bullied. Harry Potter was truly a phenomenon. J.K. Rowling was a rockstar and droves of kids and adults turned into bookworms because of Harry Potter alone. It was an exciting experience to have... Truly magical.As an adult, I still read often, but the magic of Harry Potter is hard to find in other works of art. I've found novels, games, and shows that I enjoy, but nothing compares to the magic I felt in my youth during the HP craze. Enter Hogwarts Legacy. I'm a bit of a casual gamer lately. Adulting isn't easy and takes up most of my time, but I like to unwind and relax with a good game. I tend to gravitate towards multiplayer or games that involve survival or building. I was concerned that I wouldn't enjoy Hogwarts Legacy as much, due to the fact it's single-player. It's a given that I wanted to experience the wizarding world Avalanche created, but I never expected to enjoy the gameplay as much as I do. My jaw has been on the floor the whole time playing it and I'm constantly pausing and running to my partner to show him parts of the game... Speaking of, I couldn't let my partner and some friends miss the experience. I HAD to purchase copies of the game for them as well. Hogwarts Legacy is very much a work of art and any Potterhead or non-HP fan alike will have a blast.Quidditch DLC and Modding community hype!

_childDocuments_.review: Hogwarts Legacy is a 3rd person action/exploration game that takes place in the wizarding world. You join hogwarts, get sorted into a house, and attend your classes, all while trying to discover the secret to an ancient magic. You have the entire school, the quaint little village down the path, and the rest of a massive valley to explore. Fight dark wizards, poachers, and fantastical beasts as you explore the magical world.Overall the story is pretty ok. Nothing special and pretty predictable. They give you RPG choices, however they barely matter as they rarely influence the story or end result. The game excels in the world, as just existing in it is enough to make you want to play for hours. The combat is a little jank, however once you get used it to it flows really well and its very satisfying to pull of flashy combos. Stick with it and try out different spells on each enemy to see what works well for them.The game falters with its performance. On PC its pretty all over the place, sometimes achieving 60FPS no problem but rarely inside the school anywhere. Lots of bugs all over the place like NPCs getting stuck, character spazzing out, falling through the world, puzzle elements straight up not spawning, and strange artifacts occasionally appearing. The UI is also horrendous and cumbersome, the default controls on PC are aggravating (why is it Tab+3 to use a broom but only B to dismount when B does nothing else ??????). Transmog armor is appreciated, but you have to reapply it every time you switch armor which is pretty often.The game is a collectathon which means you have to find lots of invisible things with a spell to level up and keep pace with the content. It took me roughly 53 hours to collect EVERYTHING including all collections, caves, beasts, and max out everything. Most of these are tracked, but sometimes the map doesnt show everything, including some easily missable things like pages or butterflies that are needed to 100% or reach max level. Generally fighting enemies doesnt give XP so in order to max level yourself you must 100% all collectables. Interesting choice and it'll turn some people off of the game for it.Overall the game is good, although it needs some serious patches to improve the performance and fix the bugs.Soundtrack 8/10Story 6/10Voice Acting 4/10Performance 5/10Combat 9/10Environment 10/10Character Customization 5/10 (Sliders for color choices ???? and voice pitch changes makes you sound like a robot)Replayability 6/10Overall 7/10. Very fun and if you enjoy the wizarding world, you'll probably enjoy the game. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game! The story and all the side quests so far seem really engaging. The NPC's you can talk with are limited, but I've found I'm getting invested in them. There are a lot of fun puzzles to figure out too. The glam system is pretty nice, where you can make any piece look like something else from the same category (and the glams are permanently unlocked). There are definite performance issues where the FPS plummets randomly, but it's not a constant or consistent thing. One complaint I have is the inventory system... it fills up rapidly, and your only options are to leave where you are to go sell stuff (breaks immersion), or destroy the items to make room for an unknown item. Would be nice to preview the items before you try to clean up the inventory to fit it. Also as another reviewer mentioned, make sure you have inventory space before opening the large legendary chests... if you don't have room, the chest is bugged and won't give you anything (won't even let you try again after clearing up space).

_childDocuments_.review: + :Always been an Open-world adventure girl, and I've been obsessed with the Harry Potter franchise since I was a kid. This is honestly the BEST of both worlds.The Map is HUGE and there is so much to do beside the Main Story quests, with the Merlin trials, ancient magic hotspots, the numerous animal dens, Goblin/Poacher/Ashwinder camps, astronomy tables, etc. And, of course, the side-quests!- :There ARE some very annoying bugs, like disappearing locks on cages (if you unlocked them too early in the game) and I had to restart the last part of the 'Snidget' quest because the last cutscene wouldn't trigger (ran around for about 10 minutes trying to figure out how to continue lol).The character customization is good, but not amazing.All in all, amazing graphics, so much gameplay, since you have some different missions per house and you have the choice to be 'good' or 'evil', some annoying, but fixable, bugs and honestly a very engaging story.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gave me a weird sense of fulfilment. The game play is super enjoyable and I loved that it was open world with exploration encouraged but not required. The NPCs had good backstories and I actually found the side quests actively engaging, which is unusual for me!The music is amazing and very nostalgic and it feels like a love letter to the films. I liked that there were morality questions in the game but found the lack of consequences for your character to be a little odd - using unforgivable curses in front of teachers for example without repercussions - and the voice lines can get a little repetitive.Overall though I really loved this game, it felt magical to play and would definitely recommend it, especially for those who grew up alongside the books and films.

_childDocuments_.review: An average game held up by a fantastic settingObviously, the selling point of this game is that it is a beautiful recreation of Hogwarts. If you are a Harry Potter fan, this is worth the $60 right there. It's a lot of fun to meander around the halls and explore the grounds on a broom, but the actual game here is just OK. The best action/adventure games challenge players with puzzles and interesting combat systems, but every problem in Hogwarts Legacy can be solved with a simple wave of your wand.Honestly, the most difficult part of this game is just keeping track of which spell is bound to which key. Dying in combat (at least on normal difficulty) usually just means you accidentally pressed 4 instead of 3 and turned your wand into a flashlight or some such nonsense. Pro tip: a gaming mouse makes this game so much easier.

The game spends up to a minute or more at launch compiling shaders.  The menu interface feels heavy and slow on a Ryzen 7500 with Radeon 6600M - poorly optimized.  This same system made it through CP2077 no problem.  You need to dismiss about a dozen popups about cosmetic freebies before you can start playing.  Once you start you are locked into a tutorial quest that robs of you of the ability to save when you want to until its complete.  This quest is reported to take 1-3 hours to complete.  I don't play games that don't value my time.

I love the designs of everything as well as outfits and spells and the entire open world. It's been a long time since I've played a game that made me feel like actually going out and exploring as well as looking for new quests that stray from the main story. If I had to write something negative, it would primarily be that I've had mixed results with the game's frame rate (even with DLSS set to performance). The game will start chugging. Sometimes it calms down, once in a blue moon it crashes (I am using a 2080 super gpu with a 3900x cpu and have the game installed on an m2 drive for reference). However, I'd guess this one is very dependent on your rig. Overall, I really love this game. It's really been a crazy long time since I really found a game that I don't want to put down.

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game! The exploring and combat was super fun, making it a very God of War/Elden Ring type experience. Pros: -Great Gameplay-True sense of Adventure and Exploring-Amazing options for spell combos-Customizable Appearance Settings are super-Has a building element to it, where you can build structures etc-Huge list of Customizable Decorations-Can Care for Magical Creatures-Map is fairly large-Stunning Environments-Crafting is kind of funCons: -Fairly short main story-No Demontors-No Quidditch-Combat can be repetitive-Enemies don't scale, so it's not that challenging as you get stronger-Your choices don't seem to impact the story to a very large degree-Limited types of EnemiesDon't get put off by the list of Cons. They're just there as a note of what I would have liked to see in the game. While the game could definitely be better, it's one hell of an experience and enables any Harry Potter fan to truly live their Hogwarts dream of exploring, breaking rules, attending class and so much more! As far as I'm concerned, it's an absolute must-play, totally worth the time and money! Looking forward to New Game + and DLC expansions!

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game. I had a lot of fun exploring and doing quests even though I'm not a Harry Potter fan. Gotta give it a 7/10. Fun gameplay and a nice world to explore. Casting spells here and there to kill your enemies done right. The actions are fun. Voice acting is exceptional too. Kinda a bit grindy if you want to upgrade gear, but the hassle is only on the beginning.However, the loot, especially armour, is kinda meh. Stories on the latter part is kinda rushed so it feels off but still enjoyable nonetheless. If you use mouse and keyboards, you should mind or customize the key bindings yourself. Because I think this game is meant to play with controllers.All in all, it's a nice game to play if you want to chill and fulfill your dream to become a wizard or witch.

_childDocuments_.name: Hogwarts Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: You get exactly what you ask for in a hogwarts wizarding game. All aspects of the game are amazing. The spells, the story, the side quests, the classes, the beasts, potion cooking, flying all of these aspects are well made and balanced. The best of all is the Hogwarts Castle. There simply isn't anything like it. You can spend hours just exploring the castle and its pretty accurate to the books. There are so many sections in there that are not associated with the story and you can only discover those locations in the castle if you know where things are as described in the harry potter books, for example, the house hourglasses that store house points. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Hogwarts Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it. Most of the player choice is pretty shallow. Absolutely beautiful visuals, design of the castle and world, characters, general graphics, the whole lot. Broom controls could be refined. Combat is satisfying but not particularly hard regardless of settings or if you use a controller or mouse/keyboard. Voice acting is mostly good, and the characters are interesting. Its a game that kind of lets you do everything whenever you want, so there is a necessary shallowness to some of the characters and story telling. Over all a very good game, and i'm excited to see if Portkey games continued to innovate with the material they've made.

_childDocuments_.review: About 12 hours in and I can safely say this will be a game of the year contender for 2023. If you are a fan of Harry Potter and have always wanted to go to Hogwarts, this is your chance. Make your own Witch or Wizard, attend classes, learn spells, fly brooms, duel, explore, solve puzzles. Pretty much everything you would ever want in a Harry Potter game is in here. Graphics are beautiful, game play is fun and challenging, characters are amazing, story is interesting as well. It also sticks to the lore so if you are a fan of the Wizarding World you wont be disappointed. This is going to be a hard 9/10 for me.  Only issue I have been having are FPS drops. Make sure you have a pretty decent gaming rig to play. There are some know issues with stuttering and FPS drops. Hoping patches will fix this. But its far from unplayable. You may or may not notice it. Pretty much my only complaint about the game. Please ignore the losers on Twitter who are crying about this game. Regardless of your feelings on JKR the game itself is fun and the developer deserves all the praise in the world for putting a much need Harry Potter game into the world.Oh and also..... SLYTHERIN FOREVER!!!9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a HUGE Harry Potter fan. I never read the books, but I've seen the movies, and I enjoy them. Well, this game has blown me away. I get goosebumps every time I play this game, the story, visuals, combat, everything works fantastically. I have been bored with gaming over the past few years and have been installing a game in my library, play it for and hour then quit and uninstall. I thought I was done with gaming until now. I've played 23 hours as of writing and have yet to find anything I don't like about this game. Portkey Games knocked it out of the park on this title. This game truly feels like a final and complete game at launch, unlike most games these days that ship in an unfinished state, this game has minimal issues and in my experience thus far have yet to run into any game breaking bug, the game did hard crash once but that was near the end of a 12 hour play session. I feel like if a day one release title plays solidly for 12 hours straight and the biggest issue I had was the game hard crashed at 6:30 am, that is acceptable. I am in love with this title and recommend it everyone I know. If you are on the fence about committing to a game, or feel like you have fallen out of love with games, give this one a try. I can't speak highly enough about how engrossed I become with the story, the visuals, character interactions. Hogwarts Legacy, IMO, is the GOLD STANDARD for games in 2023 and beyond. I chose to purchase on steam vs console because my PC is a last gen enthusiast machine. I'm using a Ryzen 5900x on a Corsair 360mm AIO w/six Noctua NF-F12 industrialPPC fans in push pull config, EVGA RTX 3090 FTW Ultra Hybrid 240mm AIO w/four Phanteks T30 Fans running in a push pull config, CL17 4000 DDR4, EVGA DARK X570 MOBO, and x2 WD SN850x m.2 nvme ssd in Raid 0. All that being said, running this title on ULTRA settings with RT OFF at 2560x1440, I see 1% lows around ~75 fps with average frames ~100. When I change settings to HIGH, ~120 1% lows and average around ~185 fps. The dips only occur when transitioning from indoors to outside and vice versa. If I didn't have such a powerful PC I would have bought this title on console, but the visual differences are night and day on pc compared to console. If you have a mid to high end PC, buy this title on Steam, if you are rocking older hardware, and have an Xbox Series X or PS5 then buy it on console. If you are on the fence about this game, don't be, it is a masterpiece. I have yet to find someone playing this game who doesn't like it, everyone raves about this game and for good reason. If you have any questions or comments about this review, drop a comment, I am willing and happy to discuss anything with you folks. Hogwarts Legacy 10/10 Would Recommend!!!! Don't think about it, just buy it already!

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone who read this as a teenager, or as a kid, and imagined being in this world - you will not be disappointed. To start: it is a beautiful game, I have often just stopped and looked around in game. The decision into making it a period piece, that dates far before Harry Potter's existence, was the way to go. There are familiar names, spells, and of course Hogwart's itself (exploring and coming into the Great Hall for the first time, was nostalgic to say the least), which makes it a familiar game; But, this also allows the player to identify with their character and how they develop in this story, versus playing a character through a story, we already know. If you liked/loved the books and movies - this game will be enjoyable! Also, to all puzzle lovers reading this - there are so many cute little puzzles to do! Finding them becomes like a puzzle itself, in that it's almost like and endless game of hide and seek! Don't even get me started on their own "Pokemon" type side quests! Staying on track with story quests won't even be necessary to stay entertained. It's been GREAT fun - and I'm not even halfway through! I, personally, give, all the stars, tomatoes, and thumbs up - this is an amazing game!

_childDocuments_.review: hogwarts legacy is a satisfying and nostalgic diving in Rowling's world. at the first time i could explore not only the entire castle, but the region around it. every potterhead one day dreamed about this experience and it is finally given, with stunning graphics and a complete world creation. YES! Everything is here: spells, magic beasts, creatures, buildings, detailed stuff in castle... a magical game for a magical word.not that awesome, but yet nice, the game's history is short, ordinary and unfortanely with copied events from the original plot: troll invasions, gringotts visit, rescued orphan, among other situations. i think it's bad because Rowling's universe is giant and detailed, making easy to create great and different stories adding value to this universe. copying early plots is just... lazy.the problem about playtime gets worse when the main and secondary missions are over. collectibles are painful, repetitive and boring to do, while the enemies are the same not challenger obstacles.actually, the disregard with the plot is kinda incomprehensible. until now, i just talked about the graphics. but the gameplay is terrific. battle mode is exciting and there are a lot of combinations to do with the spells. you can float the enemy and pull it down, blow it away, freeze, burn, aresto momentum, filipendo, turn them in barrels, Unforgivable Curses combo... really, a lot of possibilities.an other feature that own my heart is the Room of Requirement. i love architecture and design. the chance to build the rooms with so many objects is simply amazing. I spent hours and hours building the most beautiful and workful Room of Requirement. and not happy with it, the game gives you FOUR FREAKING DENS to spread out your beasts and decorade as you wish. this mechanical puts the game in another rating level.hogwarts legacy is HUGE, GREAT  and MAGICAL enough to honour the World of Harry Potter, but the silly  short plot and the lack of an online mode, gives it no legacy.
_childDocuments_.name: Hogwarts Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Want to give a neutral rating. Nostalgia does a lot of the work carrying the game. An enjoyable game but suffers from the same lazy design/world building that is so typical of AAA games these days. Everything is autogenerated. Oh cool I got another identical scarf but the name is purple and this one is +1 defence higher than the last one. It's almost not worth opening chests. All quests are fetch quests and the few puzzles are less puzzles and more cast the spell that matches the symbol on the block. Game is fun enough, it's neat to explore the castle, story is interesting enough to suffer through the "puzzles" and fetch quests. The world has no immersion, shops are open 24/7 waiting for you, night and day cycle are nothing more than a button away. Nobody reacts to anything you do.... but the true disappointment is getting excited from finding secret passageway, or fighting through a whole castle, or stumbling on a troll cave and when you find that big chest at the end of the area.... its gonna be a random nameless scarf with -2 defence. tldr; Is the game fun? Yes. Is it a meaningful gameplay experience? lol no. Should you play it? Yes, if you read the books/watched the movies as a kid. Should you pay full price or buy the mega ultra deluxe edition? lol not a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a wonderful experience, very fun to play and has a fantastic progression model, you get things slow, so you have time to play/learn how to use them. The cosmetic stuff is ridiculous and very cool at the same time. You can at almost any time make yourself look how you want to, which is a very nice touch, imo. Combat is engaging and the story develops in a very fun way (the parts I got to, at least). Combat can get a little repetitive, but in a way that still makes you have to pay attention and flip through your spells to keep on top of the bad dudes.I'm giving this a thumbs down because there was some update that happened somewhere between February 16-18, I took a break for a few days to play some other games during that time. This update corrupted my 57 hour playthrough, along with many other people and I am not wanting to go back through the grind of everything I did. I spent a decent amount of time trying to follow some steps to recover my game file, but none of the guides were helpful. I absolutely would have played through a 2nd time, maybe more, I don't know, but this left a really sour taste in my mouth and I tried again today 2/28/23, to see if the Devs addressed this, and nope. So, the lack of care there makes me quite disinterested. I may come back at a later date, but, that was a lot of time lost for no reason.Hopefully this doesn't happen to anyone else, but this was my experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat 8/10Graphics 9/10Immersion in the world 10/10Side quests 8/10Story quests 9/10The traveling around on a broom 9.5/10I mean for a AAA game studio to actually release a quality product that looks amazing and feels amazing in the day and age is just wild. The characters you meet are all very different. Walking around and exploring hogwarts is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ magical. The puzzles dont seem out of place like many games (looking at you god of war). I mean you do alot of puzzles that require different spells to complete and they just make sense for the world. Also a big thing is that in most open world games they tend to feel a bit empty because you go to a town and you can go into like 1/8 houses. In this game not only can you pretty much go in 95% of the buildings but they are also decorated differently and it seems like alot of work went into really feeling like specific people live there. To be honest i did not expect it to be this amazing, AAA studios have let me down in the past 5-7 years but this one did it right. Also i have encountered very little bugs. Seen like 2 npcs glitched into a wall but they were just random not important ones. Had one bug that happened when my game crashed due to me not updating my drivers and i had to reload a save from like 5 minutes previous and then it was fine. Only graphical issues i have seen were some ray tracing issues but thats to be expected given how new and advanced it still is. Overall though man 9.5/10 Its fantastic in almost every aspect[Also very little of my review has to do with nostalgia of liking harry potter as a child, i was mainly trying to speak on how this AAA studio handled an open world game VS others in the past decade. The only nostalgic part is walking around and seeing things inside hogwarts i remembered reading as a child.  It is still absolutely amazing the amount and depth of detail has been put into the game

_childDocuments_.review: I expected this game to be well mediocre at best coming from devs who hadn't really made much. _childDocuments_.review: I have seen no genuinely valid criticisms of this game, only of the author behind its universe. My review is not about Rowling's political takes or any controversy, but about the state of the gameplay experience.10/10So, let me talk about the game. It is incredible. I am not, and never have been, a fan of the Harry Potter series. This is not for any reason in particular, I was always just too busy obsessing over Tolkien's universe as a kid. Every time I tried to get into the books I failed to do so and went to another series. This does not mean I can deny the sheer brilliance of the world-building and comfort it provided many other children, however. This is now a comfort I know myself.This game has made me love Hogwarts. it has gotten me into something I always thought I hated. I have given it the true chance I never gave the books (but now will). It makes me feel so free and so cozy. I have never experienced a more immersive game in which I play as a witch and utilise magic so wonderfully. The school is warm and welcoming, the characters are well-designed and voiced, and the creatures are all so unique. I am immediately immersed as I open the game and load into the school.From class "assignments" to serious story quests, there is always something to do in terms of tasks. Outside from this, I find myself spending time flying around on my broom for no reason other than I love the way it feels, or exploring the Forbidden Forest just to see how lively and beautiful the world is. Jumping mushrooms, singing flowers, and rolling birds. I have never before experienced such a magical game. Sometimes, it makes me feel like a witch as intended. Other times, I escape the school grounds for a while and feel like a fairy.The school itself is also so whimsical, from speaking portraits to poltergeists and ghosts that feel as though they are just like any other people (or at worst, annoying) rather than frightening. As someone dipping into Rowling's universe for the first time really, I am blown away by just how comforting everything is even when taking elements that are otherwise portrayed as "scary" or negative. The game takes elements from some of my favourite genres, too, allowing you to do so many things. These include botany, potion-brewing, and DECORATING A HUGE SPACE! I spent ages playing with furniture, colours, and wallpapers last night after unlocking my unique room. Seriously, I keep discovering more and MORE to do in the game. I see myself spending hundreds of hours in it.As for soundtrack, it is as beautiful as the scenery. The writing is, too. Everything is. In terms of inclusion, it marks every box. I am a woman who is attracted to the same sex and running into Nora Treadwell was absolutely heart-warming. An older lesbian couple who is passionate about archaeology and history?! Precious...Please play this game. Please do not let the opinions of chronic Internet dwellers take this magical experience away from you by convincing you that somehow your purchase funds any sort of bigotry. And if you are those people, touch grass. I have already had multiple people block me on this platform just for playing the game. It is utterly ridiculous how such a wholesome experience is being twisted into something so sinister when it should not be.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an impressive world. The Hogwarts grounds feel familiar from the movies while also expanding upon the parts we have seen with new areas and details. It feels alive and like the developers had a passion for the world. The combat is fluid and has a similar pacing to the movies and feels pretty intuitive. Overall the appearance and atmosphere of the open world is the strength of this game! The Castle is great, the music is excellent, and the sound effects are immersive. Loading screens are few and far between and I am very glad that Hogwarts is fully traverseable by foot and not just by flu. The Story is fine, and some of the characters are nice. I like seeing the occasional recognizable last name! Feels tied to the Harry-potter world without it just feeling like a continuation of the story we already know. Good job avoiding being Star Wars, where everyone is either secretly a Skywalker and a saint or is secretly a Palpatine and a villain! New Characters are a good thing instead of wearing old ones out. Also, the clothing and cosmetic options are good, and I am very glad that I can choose what my items look like instead of having to choose between "High stats but I look like an edgelord or a thriftshopper" and "I love how my character looks but my stats are ♥♥♥♥". I Hope all RPG/Open-World games incorporate something similar going forward! And thank you for not requiring me to be online/connected to some proprietary launcher and web service, that crap grinds my gears! (Looking at you Ghost Recon/ubisoft) Also the house dorms/common rooms are great and beautiful.With that said, there are a couple areas that are a bit lacking. Namely the lack of player choice and the voice of Sirona Ryan in game. While the World is beautiful, you get very little chance to make your experience unique from other players or prior play-throughs and little to do once the story is complete. This is not Red Dead Redemption 2 or Kingdom Come Deliverance. The Story is very linear and the pacing feels too rushed early on. While you are free to explore early, it ruins the pacing of the story. You cannot make your character your own, and your dialogue options are just cosmetic and don't have any meaningful impact. I would like to see the "open" world freed up a bit and offer a bit more replay-ability in the future. DLC perhaps? I often return to RDR2 or KCD to just "live" in the world, hunting or fishing and just soaking in the atmosphere. You really get the feeling of the setting and time period in those games even though they are fictional. Hogwarts Legacy unfortunately doesn't yet lend itself to that sort of laid-back enjoyment of the world. The addition of activities other than spamming "r" to find Crates would be much appreciated. Maybe capturing rare creatures for sale? Surely witches and wizards hunt also, as evidenced by the trophies adorning the walls. Maybe more activities around the castle, more friendly dueling or potion making. Quidditch! Decorating my dorm even if it is a set of options. Anything to give me something to do and just feel immersed. The strength of Video Games as a medium is that you (the player) have agency, otherwise it is just a movie that I have to press buttons in. Long story short, I love non-grindy, non-linear games. Locking abilities or skills behind "levels" or similar is fine early in the game, but then I want to be free and I want to be able to skip the learning grind on my next play through! I hate grinding for Items, let me do the activities I like and then buy them for reasonably amounts! I already paid for the game with my money, please don't make me pay with all my time as well. (This last bit was more in terms of what I want to see in future developments of this game, as of now there is little grinding and I want it to stay that way if there are expansions.)Also, more "sidekicks" and choices between them. Not just assigning the same two "friends" every game.Lastly, and I won't dwell on it too long: Sirona Ryan. The voice is jarring, comical, and takes me right out of the game whenever I have to hear it. Hopefully voice mods are coming soon. Supposedly the voice is only male in the English dubbing, go figure. Why try to pander to a group that refuses to buy the game at the expense of the normal people that already did? It seems like a fools errand to bend over backwards to try to avoid being labeled "tRanSPHObiC!1!11!!" for being normal in today's world. Not everything needs to have "trans" characters, and I find it telling that the "trans" voice and dialogue is probably only present in the english-speaking or "western" language options, and that other parts of the world don't have to hear this pandering.Good title, strong setting, I'm optimistic for it to grow even deeper in the future!

I know a lot of people would have liked more spells to have been added, but people do need to remember that this is the main character's first year at Hogwarts. The fact that the main character is able to learn so many spells despite it being their first year in Hogwarts is already impressive from a story point of view. Of course mechanically, they had to ensure the player had access to a good amount as well in order for the game to be fun and entertaining. The story was pretty good overall, though I will admit I often got sidetracked exploring the castle. Just wandering through the castle provided a few hours of entertainment. Outside of the castle was cool too of course. Seeing Hogsmead was a treat as was the Forest. But nothing beats the castle.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give this a thumbs up because the nifflers are so damn cute. 😍Just kidding, read my in-depth analysis...At first, I thought HL was soft and aimed at children. However, while it's neither particularly difficult, scary, nor bloody, it does address the death of close relatives and the double-edged unforgivable curses quite a lot. I'd like to highlight the  quests positively, as they evoked deep feelings in me.The main quests are quite decent. My favorites were the one taking place inside  and the one where you drink .On the other hand, most side quests are uninspired fetch quests. I found it especially annoying how most NPCs would utter something like "I always wondered about item X in location Y" and were content with you exploring it instead of doing so themselves. Decisions have few consequences, except for getting paid afterward, which you always must ask for, sometimes gravely upsetting the quest giver.Sadly, the relationship quests are chopped up into small pieces like modern TV shows. You often have to travel someplace just for a cut scene. What I'm sure is supposed to foreshadow and keep you hooked, seems to me like the devs are spreading the butter really thin to maximize your playtime.Hogwarts and Hogsmeade are great and truly feel like Harry Potter, but the open world looks like every other modern triple-A RPG. It contains few memorable places and too many too elaborate dungeons with too lousy loot.There are comparatively few enemy classes (mostly spiders, poachers, goblins, trolls, spiders, and more spiders), and they all fight kind of the same, regardless of their class or subclass.It might have been a great coincidence, but HL seems very well balanced in terms of experience points as I reached the maximum level () by finishing the last side quest and thereby finishing the last challenge. 💯Combat is fun because it's fast-paced, packs a lot of punch, and you always have countless methods at hand. Chaining enemies together with curses and ultimately casting Avada Kedavra, killing them all at once in a mighty strike of green lightning, is simply satisfying. Setting up your spell decks and skills reminded me of the trading card games of my youth. The dueling feats are also a nice touch, forcing you to try more unintuitive ways of fighting. Unfortunately, the concrete numbers behind upgrades that "greatly" or "significantly" increase damage are not shown but would interest me, considering that offense and defense stats for outfits are actually shown.Flying is also fun and well-implemented, especially after the broom upgrades. Contrary to public opinion, one does not need a gamepad/controller to play HL on PC, but extra mouse buttons do help when flying and casting spells.The beasts are pretty, well-rigged, and have cool animations. Feeding and brushing them for resources also adds a nice touch. Although I find it a bit ironic how beasts are "rescued" by removing them from their natural habitats and locking them up or selling them, and how nobody seems to mind because obviously the player's cages are more comfortable than the poachers' cages.The manifold riddles are interesting at first but become increasingly annoying, given the fact that you need to solve hundreds of  to get the achievement. I haven't been able to bring myself to do it yet.In HL, you don't collect weapons, only wand appearances, which you don't see while casting spells, making it an entirely unnecessary feature. I also didn't care about expanding my base () beyond the essentials because base building is something that becomes less fun with every game that features it.Lastly, being able to change the appearance of every clothing item to any other once collected, thus separating stats and aesthetics, is a genius idea, and more games should do it! Some of the outfits also look very cool.Well, everything looks great on an RTX 4090 with i9-12900k. However, I frown upon the frequent (visible!) frame rate drops caused by HL generally being too bloated for the version of the Unreal Engine that is being used. Also weird is "shaders preparing" every time I launch the game, which takes about a minute. Admittedly, I have ray tracing and all settings on Ultra and DLSS off, but if not even the highest-end hardware can handle it, what can? 🤔While the devs' understanding of inclusivity felt more like ticking off ethnic/diversity boxes to me, I guess they had to make the game "woke" in order to disassociate themselves from JKR's inappropriate remarks. I could even get used to all ethnicities of the world being represented in 1890's Scotland because: magic. But telling the blind kid of all things to "stay in place until we're out of sight" is either a cruel joke or a plain oversight. 😅HL is a good game that reignited my Harry Potter fever, but it's by no means revolutionary to the genre.

The game is good and while not all dialogue affects the main story line, it does affect what people say to you. If you make a student pay to get her diary back she will basically say that you are a extortionist to others and when you walk by. If you use unforgivable spells around professors or classmates they say you shouldn't be using those spells. I have not done another save yet so I can't say that doing different choices on main story quests do or do not change things ending wise. The world of NPC is fairly interactive as they talk about current events of side quests or story quest that are on going. As you walk around pretty much anywhere there are tons of NPCs talking about all sorts of different topics which is cool. Side quests range from boring to very story rich so best to mix up the character specific story missions with other random side quests.I feel like for the first 4-6 hours of playing the game i just wanted to wander around Hogwarts and explore everything I could. After 30 hours I can say that I have still not explored everything as I found new statues and rooms literally before writing this. There is so much to do in this game from animals to gear crafting to potions and plants to finding all sorts of collectibles.Combat is good but if its all you do it can get boring casting the same spells over and over. I can so comboing the unforgivables then instant killing a group seems to never get old. Yes the game is hard to run. _childDocuments_.review: I REALLY wanted to love this game. I watched lots of the early content, and I really love the wizarding world. Its been a while since I felt this let down by a game. I did beat it, and I did all the major side quests, and a good chunk of the lesser side quests. So I have a very good grasp on the game. I am also a very experienced RPG player.Pros:* The world of quite large, and some areas (Hogwarts and Hogsmead) have a huge attention to detail* Hogwarts itself is fantastic. You can go and explore almost anywhere you can think of* The voice acting is done pretty well (except for Prof Black)* The character creator is adequate, and you can change how gear looks. You aren't stuck with how something you got looks.* Lots of familiar places that you can visit* There are lots of familiar families. Which is good if you like that. But they kind of feel a bit forced, and some are poorly done, such as Professor Black.Cons:* The world is very large, but there isn't much to do* There are ZERO consequences. You can use "unforgivable" curses RIGHT IN FRONT of professors, and they DON'T CARE. Not to mention the killing curse makes most boss fights a 5 second fight. You can even kill bosses that somebody come back to life to talk to you after the fight.* You cannot make choices that matter. Most of the time if you are given two options, they are just slightly different wording with the same result. The scripting is very much set in stone.* Wish they had gotten the rights to the music from the movies.* There is a severe lack of enemies. You basically have humans, goblins, trolls, zombies, spiders, and some giant toads. There is no variation between them. They all act and do the same things.* The enemy AI is straight up dumb, some of the worst I have seen. You can cast a spell and cause an explosion, then cloak and sit behind something, and they will completely forget you ever existed within seconds. They will also often get stuck behind things, and you can then just shoot them and they can't do anything back.* There are lots of treasure caves you can go into. But the vast majority of them appear to have been copy and pasted from each other. The very end room varies a bit on some.* There is almost no reason to ever go down any of these treasure caves, or go out of your way to find chests to open. You might find a few gold, you may find a new piece of clothing, that's it. I started out trying to do every single one, until I learned they are all the same with similar gear.* If you like hunting for gear to upgrade your character, you will hate this. There are obviously zero weapons to find (You do learn new spells). You can only find clothing which offers slightly different levels of defense, and some may have a bonus state.* You can upgrade your gear. And in theory, its a cool system. Except that it makes very little difference.* The "Merlin Trials" appear to be tailored towards kinder gardeners. I was hoping they would have some adequately fun puzzles. But this is certainly not the case.* Not sure I understand the purpose of money in this game. I ended the game with well over 40K gold, and I wasn't trying to save it up. If money is so easy to get, why even make it a thing?* This game is extremely easy to get over leveled in. Which then makes the game even easier than it should be.If you read all the above, I am surprised, but thankful. Hope it helps you out with your decision.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up on Harry Potter, watching the Philosopher's Stone when I was 5 years old. The dream over the next few years of getting a letter from Hogwarts when I turned 11 propelled me through primary school. I'm pretty sure my letter got lost in the post somewhere (maybe Errol was delivering it) but this has been the closest thing I've had to going. I've seen thousands of videos online saying things like "things you have to know before you play Hogwarts Legacy" and the truth is that you don't need to know anything. Almost everything is Cosmetic in terms of Brooms and Wands or you could even import your wand from the Wizarding World website if you're interested in that. I don't believe there are things you can "miss" due to progressing the game too quickly (not 100% certain on that) but I would still recommend taking the time between main missions to explore, do classes/assignments and most importantly the relationship missions (arguably better than the main story sometimes). Its a beautiful game that you can play through fast and action packed, or slow and enjoy the world that's been created. I've played through the game twice, first play through was for the pure story and consisted of choices I believe I would have personally made, the second was a bit more thorough and utilised a bit more of a barbaric approach. I am biased due to nostalgia, but I thought the game was brilliant, the story was good (not perfect, other characters had better development than the main). Gameplay was extremely fun and I loved the different combinations you could pull off with the various spells. I unfortunately had to play on Low Graphics (possibly due to the age of my machine) even though the medium graphics settings were recommended and even so I dealt with huge stutter problems through both play throughs due to the way the game loaded the surroundings, but if you have a good rig and can max out the graphics I imagine the experience would be stunning. I may venture into 100% completion in the near future but personally I thought the game is absolutely amazing, it isn't perfect, and there are things that everyone will find that bug them (especially if you're an arachnaphobe) but for a taste of what they can do with the world of Harry Potter and video games, I truly hope this is the beginning of bigger and better projects.

_childDocuments_.review: Critically speaking, I feel like I should give it something like a 7.5: I dislike the slow, linear main story missions, but the combat looks and feels great, and the setting is so strong it carries a lot of weight, moreso if it meant something to you as a child. Make sure to sync your old Pottermore account right away if you have one, you get stuff. The detailed and well-storied world keeps a mediocre main plot from dragging the whole atmosphere and sense of adventure down much, barely at all. It is very immersive and pretty.Most overworld puzzles are more basic even than the disliked Breath of the Wild dungeons, and therefore feel a bit like errands, but the promise of new spells and features keeps pulling things along. Character building options and roleplaying in dialogue are both on the shallow side, especially the latter, but the spells are cool and so is the gear. Friend side-stories are more fun than the main plot, but as long as you can deal with the handholdy slow start, it's a good time. I wouldn't rush to get it unless you have the patience not to be able to spread your wings for a few hours. I can't wait to have all the spells to experiment with in combat.

_childDocuments_.review:
LIVE THE UNWRITTEN - Hogwarts Legacy is an immersive, open-world action RPG set in the world first introduced in the Harry Potter books. Now you can take control of the action and be at the center of your own adventure in the wizarding world. Embark on a journey through familiar and new locations as you explore and discover fantastic beasts, customize your character and craft potions, master spell casting, upgrade talents, and become the wizard you want to be.

Experience Hogwarts in the 1800s. Your character is a student who holds the key to an ancient secret that threatens to tear the wizarding world apart. You have received a late acceptance to the Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry and soon discover that you are no ordinary student: you possess an unusual ability to perceive and master Ancient Magic. Only you can decide if you will protect this secret for the good of all, or yield to the temptation of more sinister magic.

Discover the feeling of living at Hogwarts as you make allies, battle Dark wizards, and ultimately decide the fate of the wizarding world. Your legacy is what you make of it.

_childDocuments_.review: An OK little puzzle game. The presentation is simple but charming. The controls straightforward and adequate.Alas, the puzzles are far too easy. Some are so trivial that they feel like busywork rather than challenges. And the story, though fleshed out with nice narration, is skin deep. _childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is an unexpected gem that has a sweet, metaphorical story and lots of charm. I didn't expect to enjoy it as much as I did, but I ended up finishing the first of 3 worlds in one sitting, and would like to return at another time to finish the remaining two. 97% positive Steam reviews may suggest a masterpiece, but there are some areas which could be improved. Some things it lacks are camera controls, voice acting, and an overview screen/world map. A rotating camera is like power windows/seats in a car - not necessary but makes the ride feel better. One actor provides all the dialogue and does a fine job too, but having separate actors for the main characters would be ideal. The lack of an overview screen is something common in indie games, and I think it makes the game less cohesive. Despite these minor flaws, I recommend checking this one out and feel it's worth it at the sale price.

_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a delightful little game that combines puzzles with an intimate and emotional story. The visuals and music are sublime and add to the whole experience. I think the game had a great message and I liked how it didn’t hold your hand, you had to figure out what to do next yourself. The puzzles aren’t too hard but at the same time aren’t too easy. The controls are simple and the journey is linear (you move from one campfire to another) but also exploratory (you're free to move around in each of the areas to explore and find lost embers). This is a wonderful experience and a rewarding game to play, I absolutely loved everything about it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Played it through a couple times now, and every time even way after the fact--weeks, months--I'll still be thinking about it sometimes. Not only is the narrative and pacing really well done, but the puzzles are really fun but also not too hard either. And they're scaled throughout the game to steadily get harder at a reasonable pace as well, so it's fun the whole time. The art style is wonderful; looking at straight art the whole time you're playing. The little ember you play is adorable; just a wholesome bean. But what got me the most was just the phrases and statements and messages along the way. As odd as it sounds, I feel like anyone experiencing mental health stuff (depression, anxiety, etc.) would really enjoy this game. Not only does it feel like this game puts what those feelings and experiences are like into words PERFECTLY, but it also gives a really soothing, hopeful message about how to live and work through those bad brain moments. And in a really sincere, pleasant way. Not pedantic or condescending or anything at all. That's the part that keeps me coming back the most. Tackles it really well. Either way, super recommend this game for everyone to play!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite a little gem - no wonder the devs are not afraid to share a demo :D Beautiful visuals, incredible atmosphere, and a story that's more emotional than rational, yet very captivating.The gameplay itself is a mix of exploration and environment puzzles. The exploration is very enjoyable, thanks to the excellent visual design, and the game is careful to ensure it doesn't get overly lengthy (and thus, boring). The puzzles are interesting and generally satisfying, although not very difficult - they serve as a slightly cerebral counterpoint to the otherwise very emotional nature of the game. This mix works quite well together - and at 6-7 hours, it's the right length, there's always enough fresh stuff to keep the player interested.When people debate that video games are an art form, The Last Campfire is an excellent example. Very much recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Tried out the demo and just fell in love with Ember the main character so had to get the full game. The animation especially was SO ADORABLE (climb animations were just so well done, I could just watch Ember's ears go flip flap like all day). Puzzles sometimes got challenging but the cute art helped to not let it get stressful. The story was good too, and I liked the ending. Emotional journey overall with a message. Thanks Lost Campfire team![Edit] I saw some comments about the narration. Personally I loved it. The lisp made the overall experience, and I thought it fit the overall cute art style.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campire is a very beautiful and cute puzzle adventure game with a story emphasizing mental health in a light and wholesome way.The puzzles aren't too hard, some you will figure out eventually, some very straightforward. There's always a sense of progression, something to discover or someone to talk to. The voice-over does a good job at narrating and speaking dialogues.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful aesthetics, interesting story, cute little puzzles and characters. The puzzles aren't tremendously difficult, but the stories are so engaging--each little puzzle walks through the story of someone's pain, how things in life can get twisted around and lost. Excellent commentary on pain and trauma while still maintaining a lighthearted and visually pleasing aesthetic. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A gem of a game.  Moving around and reacting with the environment is refreshingly simple.  The environment and characters are captivating.  The auto save system works well.  Puzzles are good and well laid out within the framework of the game.  I found some difficult, but they were all very satisfying.  The graphics and voice acting are charming.  The game has a strong emotional element which builds throughout.   I gave in at the end and wept.  No bugs were encountered.The forlorn beings and the main character are referred to using the pronoun "they".  There is nothing to suggest gender, which can be a little confusing at first, but it grows on you, and anything different would have detracted from the meaning, as the beings are little souls, embers,  so gender references would just get in the way of the beautiful story.I just stumbled on this game and I am glad that I did.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Camfire is a wonderful, heartfelt, short, and sweet experience. The game tackles some life topics while giving you fun and interesting puzzles to solve. The narration of the game with a sweet woman throughout really conveys a unique and warm atmosphere.A great game from Hello Games would gladly recommend it to folks that want to relax and enjoy this atmospheric game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible journey and a symphony of elements of game design, narrative, music and art style. Every step makes you wonder more about yourself and others.The puzzles are creative, and although not challenging, you find yourself amazed on how each one of them brings something different. The puzzle name's and composition tells a story on their own, which every correct step rewarding you with more.The secrets are clever and funny to find; the game is not shy to guide you in a general path, but its your choice to look further and find everything. How you'll proceed your journey is up to you. At the end, Rachel August' stellar narrative of all characters and wonders, brings you to an incredible story about a little Ember, while sitting at a campfire.It's not every day you have an experience such as this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game with a discount and paid less than 5$. I think the regular price might be a little bit high, considering how short the game is, but it was more than enough for the money I spent. I like puzzles and cute graphics, so I did not think much when buying this game and I am really glad it found its way to my Steam library. The story is simple, yet very touching and although I did not spend too much time with the main character, I felt somehow connected with it. The Last Campfire is about journey, about dealing with a loss and the importance of hope. It was really easy for me to immerse in the story. The puzzles were fun and not too frustrating, so I've had a lot of fun with them as well. Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone who would like to embark on a melancholic, atmospheric journey in a pretty world full of interesting creatures and fun puzzles. For me, it was a great experience and I'd love to be able to forget this game, just to play it for the first time again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Off the bat, I would recommend this game to any player looking for a relaxed, emotion based puzzle experience.The laid back feeling this game gives off, with its gentle mix of puzzles and story driven gameplay is a perfect blend for anyone who just wants a relaxing experience.The art style is wonderful and the controls are super easy to use, especially on the SteamDeck.If puzzles aren’t your thing, whilst they’re not hard, there is a mode which focuses more on the story than puzzles.There is no combat in this game, just logic and an emotionally driven story.Unfortunately, this game also doesn’t lend itself to re-playability, perhaps becoming a pick up once every few years type of game.I would also recommend waiting until the game is on sale to purchase it, as I had completed the game in puzzle mode collecting all of the hidden objects in just under 6 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet. The game took me a little over 5 hours to complete. I finished the core game a bit faster than that but there is a journal entry collection that I wanted to complete.Overall the game is nice and relaxing. Some of the controls weren't perfect but it was not a huge detriment to the gameplay. I swapped between mouse and keyboard but you could play with either exclusively. It was playable on SteamDeck too.The puzzles kind of remind me of Sausage Party, but not as complicated. There were 21 puzzles in-game (I think some were optional to complete the game since it seems like I could have progressed to next area before finishing all the puzzles in the current area) with 4 more that gets unlocked after you beat the game. The narrator's voice is pretty soothing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't listen/care about soundtracks. But this one is beautiful. I especially love the soundtrack for the pig in the Marsh!! I love the environmental details, like being able to run through things and they react. I also love just playing games where I can be a little critter. The art style is cute.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This wonderful friend was recomended to me by a friend. I bought it because it seemed like my kind of game, and it did not dissapoint. _childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet puzzle game. The world is very pretty, the soundtrack is beautiful and responds nicely to player input (something I always love), and there isn't much pressure to backtrack to turn every stone for a secret. The story's themes focus on grief and despair, and how to move on from that; both for yourself, and for helping others move past their own sadness.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The puzzles are a perfect balance of accessibility and difficulty so just about anybody can play and enjoy. The story is cute and aims to be deeper than it really accomplishes but is still well done. There is a single narrator for everything which is a bit of a double edged sword in that it gives it a real night time storybook vibe but can also come off as lazy in regards to voice acting in parts.All in all - it's not going to win game of the year but it absolutely deserves the "Overwhelmingly positive" review status. Not every game needs to be the best of the year and Last Campfire doesn't try to earn this title. Instead it just aims to be a charming story backdropped by some very enjoyable puzzles and it hits its mark perfectly in that regard.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Cute characters and world, mostly pleasant soundtrack. Fun overworld puzzles that are interspersed with self-contained and unique block-pushing puzzles that do not overstay their welcome. A very tight experience. I do not much care for block-pushing puzzles, but since they were self-contained, and each puzzle was super unique, it was very fun. The overworld puzzles were a nice change of pace as well. There is no padding in the game, and it did not overstay its welcome. The block-pushing mechanic also felt pretty uniquely implemented. Even if you've played similar games, I don't think you'd be bored.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a nice game with an interesting setting with missions and puzzles that are not too hard but also not too easy to complete. Even though this game is a shorter one for one or two nights to play, in my opinion is worth your time and money. The plot may not be as memorable for many as for others, many may not even understand it, but at the end of the day it provides an interesting insight to how many different individuals experience variety of negative emotions and how many different individuals have different kind if ways to find themselves and resolve those issues. Overall, the game is not a waste of anyones attention. I personally recommend it with a big thumbs up.
