_childDocuments_.review: Just finished playing The Last Campfire! Such a good game, I give it an 8/10! Here's why:Art: 10/10The art was so cute in this game! Ember, the adventurers and the forlorn but ESPECIALLY the pigs. They were so adorable and chunky! Graphics: 10/10The graphics were so aesthetically pleasing, it felt cozy and I was very immersed in the game.Music: 8/10It definitely has a great soundtrack, it was pleasing to listen to while playing.Sound Effects: 10/10Whoever worked on the sound effects, let me tell you... you are amazing! My ears were super pleased with every sound effect. I especially loved the crispness of the campfire and the sound of chains.Game Mechanics: 6/10It was a bit wonky and I didn't really care much with the controls on the keyboard it didn't feel natural. It took a bit of time to get used to but still playable.Bugs: 3/10This game was really buggy. I constantly got stuck in walls or stairs. Two time I even got stuck under stairs and had to re-start the game because there was no way to get un-stuck. The biggest one though was that during my second to last play-through of it between each transition the game would break the screen. The screen would be split in half and mirrored upside down! I've never seen that happen in a game before! It definitely added an element of surprise but unfortunately it was unplayable and had to re-start the game a few times until it "calmed down".Story: 8/10Cute story about life and the struggles that come with it. Puzzles: 8/10Pretty good puzzles, a lot of them were too easy. I got stumped in a few of them. I had to take a break and come back to 3 of them and I only had to look up the answer to 1 of them. I wish there was more balance in the complexity of the puzzles but otherwise enjoyable!Price: (My range: Awful-Bad-FAIR-Good-Great)The price is 14.99 which I find it to be fair for this game. Overall: It's a rounded up 8! It was definitely enjoyable to play although frustrating at times, I recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a number of strategy, puzzle and cozy games but never left a review. This game is the first game that made me really want to tell other people just how amazing it is. Yes it's on the shorter side (about 8 hours), but the story is a beautifully poignant metaphor for facing life struggles, mental health challenges, and contemplating the time we have in our lives. It's a meditative story about connection, hope, curiosity and acceptance. The music is soothing, the puzzles are interesting but not too frustrating, and the pace is calm. I felt interested in the game but took my time and could easily pick it up for a half hour at a time to relax. I got this game on sale and wish I had paid full price for the thoughtfulness that went into this game. This is so well done.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% recommend the game for anyone that likes this genre or style of game. I LOVE seeing small indie games like this get such positive feedback and this one has definitely earned it's +98% overwhelmingly positive reviews as of this post.Not a game I would have ever found on my own and super glad I stumbled across it. _childDocuments_.review: is an adventure game created by three people at Hello Games, primarily developed for mobile devices and later ported to PC and consoles. Compared to their first ambitious game (), The Last Campfire has a smaller scope, being more like a bedtime fairy tale filled with short puzzles. The story is told through a brilliant narrator who describes, in a fable-like manner, actions, thoughts and emotions of all characters, reminding me of 's marvelous storytelling. We play as a cute little Ember who is suddenly separated from his companions during a boat ride. Lost and confused, we must find our way back, while also trying to help those we encounter.The Last Campfire is not just a puzzle game, it's a magical journey of self discovery that deals with fears and mental issues. Those who not only lost their direction but also their hope, have turned into statues and become "Forlorn". Touching them transports Ember inside their puzzled minds, which need to be cleared in order to revitalize their bodies and bring them back to the campfire. These sequences usually consist of finding a way to reach a blue spark locked in a cage; they are quite easy to solve and mostly rely on simple logic. As we progress and obtain new abilities, puzzles become slightly more challenging, but never frustrating. They are very relaxing and somehow resemble 's diorama structure and melancholic tone.After helping a decent amount of Forlorn, we can decide to light the campfire and continue our journey, or we can try to find all of them before leaving the area because, as the game suggests, no one should be left alone.Unfortunately, there is no reset option for puzzles; if you want to restart them, you need to touch the Forlorn statue and then touch it again, which can be annoying. A few times I got stuck in the middle of a puzzle, and I even glitched inside a rock once, but my only option was to quit and reload the checkpoint from the main menu. These small hiccups didn't have much impact on my experience, which was still very pleasant.The world of The Last Campfire is a beautiful colored limbo populated by Forlorn, Embers and other fantastic creatures, always followed by charming melodies that perfectly set the tone for each area. Forests, swamps and caves include multiple platform sections that require us to find key items to unlock new paths. Exploration feels rewarding, as we may find hidden Forlorn and chests containing missing pages from a wanderer's diary, though getting to them is often a puzzle in itself.The mobile nature of its design is pretty noticeable especially when taking a look at controls, which are better suited for touch screens. As a result, on PC you can simply use your mouse to play the entire game like a point and click adventure or, if you prefer, use keyboard or controller for a more casual experience. The interface is almost non-existent, with just a small inventory to store a few key items. The game is probably best experienced during brief sessions, as it’s quite short and taking in consideration how well-suited for mobile the controls are, it would be a perfect fit for Steam Deck. It took me 7 hours to reach the ending, solving all the puzzles and finding all the missing diary pages. Part of me wanted it to last longer as I was getting more and more attached to Ember, but I understand the risk of it becoming too repetitive. The Last Campfire is a gorgeous work of art that both children and adults can enjoy. It's a lovely experience, and it delivers a strong message that overcomes the low difficulty of puzzles. If you are looking for a pleasant, meaningful and stress-free puzzle adventure game, this is the one for you.

_childDocuments_.review: So my FIRST (and most surprising, for me) praise is that I did not have to look up the solution to *any* of the puzzles! I looked up “starting hints” on one, but took it myself from there! The puzzles just made sense to me visually, and also their names were such great hints at their solutions.But I think my BIGGEST praise is that everything was so…perfect. The characters matched the environment matched the music matched the narration matched the animals matched the puzzles matched the story…They must have had a *strong* vision board, because I suspect that getting the overall vibe to be so consistent is NOT easy!Every single puzzle/Forlorn had an individual story that you *believed*. Nothing seemed forced or trite or heavy-handed. And you liked everyone! Every animal was adorable and fun. You wanted to help every single Forlorn. Even the "bad guys" were adorable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect to get gut-punched in the feels by an adorable puzzle game, but here we are. The music and cute character design were my favorite parts. The one thing I would change would be to make the final puzzle more substantial. It felt a little anticlimactic compared to some of the other puzzles, but maybe that's intentional so you aren't frustrated when watching the last cutscene.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A superb little adventure game with an interesting story line, excellent level design and beautiful graphics. Travel around rescuing comrades who have become stuck in a world that is very Zelda-like. The puzzle mechanics are fairly simple and the use of the inventory is limited. You "learn" one major skill that enables you to move parts of the levels to complete the later puzzles. And while the puzzles themselves are not too challenging I never felt bored always feeling satisfied when I managed to solve them. I seldom finish games but this one I have completed and thoroughly enjoyed it from start to finish. It left me begging for more but somethings are better because they come in a small package. Completed on the Steam Deck without a single issue.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little game in terms of presentation and story, the puzzles are passible at worst but some are pretty good about making you think. I'd also say know what you're getting into this isn't a game I would recommend if you want a lot of excitement but rather enjoy exploring a world and the story it tells at a slower pace. There are collectibles which can occasionally provide some extra exploration but they are more just expanding on the existing narrative and don't benefit you to seek them nor detract from the game if you miss themOverall an enjoyable experience and a nice way to spend a couple evenings.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute beautiful game! I feel as though words cannot to it justice, but I will try.- What amazingly captivating and beautifully atmospheric graphics. So smooth, calming and gentle.- The narrator is absolutely adorable; I could listen to her speaking for hours. I couldn't wait to hear the story unfold. The language and words used were so endearing and gentle - I felt nurtured and connected to the character and their journey.- The story is beautiful, easy to follow and extraordinarily touching. _childDocuments_.review: I am not sure whether I, as a grown-up, am in the main target group of the game. I bought it because what I saw reminded me of Little Nightmares (rather, a brighter version of), which I enoyed a lot. With that expectation, I was a bit disappointed by The Last Campfire. Which is sad, because in many aspects the game is well made and has great potential, it was just slightly boring for me.The puzzles were too easy for my taste, I just ran around and solved them, there's actually not much you can do wrong. All interactive elements are highlighted which always gives a good clue what to do next. Keyboard control is a bit weird (because of the moving perspective), luckily you cannot fall or die at all. Starting to row the boat didn't work at all with the keyboard (they always climbed back up the ladder instead of rowing away - until I noticed I can use the mouse for the boats).What really annoyed me is that I couldn't skip dialogs and video sequences, even when seen for the 2nd time. At the end of the game I thought about going for the last 3 achievements, made the mistake to interact with a specific character again, which resulted in a long dialog I already read and a long sequence I already watched. At that point, I force-killed the game to get out.

_childDocuments_.review: i really enjoyed this game! it was quite short, it took me around 6.5 hours to complete, and the puzzles were not to challenging. i love how new mechanics are introduced throughout the game, and they are merged very well with the mechanics from the earlier stages of the game - it makes the puzzles feel quite intricate, often made me feel ''nostalgic'' in a way, thinking like ''oooh i remember this''....i'm seeing a couple reviews that say they dont like the voice acting, but i personally loved it! the actress sounds so charming, with a soft accent that i can't quite decipher - sounds either french or scandinavian-rooted to me, and i believe it enhanced the game experience for me because it did feel like i was experiencing another world that was translated to me in a way. throughout the game, there are hidden stone ''boxes'' that have pieces of lore descriptions inside, and when you open one, the actress will say ''[character name] found a scrap of journal'' and idk theres just something so charming and sweeet about the way she says ''scrap of journal'', im obsessed with it hahanothing bad to say about the game! i think the story is a bit convoluted and mysterious, its not really explained in the end, but i guess its all up to interpretation, especially considering that there are some obvious motifs relating to mental health topics, so i think its good that the story is up to interpretation because everyone experiences mental health in a different way.all in all, a wonderful game! i would recommend c:

_childDocuments_.review: I strongly enjoyed this game, and it touched my heart. The story is captivating and heartwarming. I enjoyed the puzzles in this game, even when they were very simple, and found that the game play was very smooth.I love all the exploration that the game allows, and how there are collectibles in the game for those who want to explore further. _childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is brimming with exceptional craftsmanship and attention to detail. The environments, the sound design, the tactility of interactions, the voice acting, the animation, the level and puzzle design--it feels like every single person working on every part of this brought an incredible amount of skill to the table to make a wonderful little gem.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a game about hope. It may look bright and colorful on the outside, but on the inside - and going by just the title - lies a more melancholic game. A puzzle game, to be more specific, but in adventure form.In The Last Campfire it’s your task to guide lost (forlorn) creatures to the campfires. There are three campfires to guide creatures to and this means that there are also three areas to explore: a small one (a forest), a large one (a marsh) and a medium sized one (caves). Exploration happens on foot, but in the last area you also get to use a boat.Along the way you can find secret journals located in chests. You’ll sometimes have to manipulate the environment in order to find or grab these. Hence why they are called secret (although they’re usually very easy to spot).Each area has eight forlorn creatures you have to guide towards the campfire. These are guided by solving puzzles. Touching a forlorn creature transforms the surroundings into a temporary puzzle area that changes back whenever you touch the creature again or, ideally, when you manage to solve the puzzle. Finding these creatures usually also requires solving an environmental puzzle and interacting with other characters. Most of the times you’ll need to find a specific item in order to progress, like finding a fishing net or seeds. These are fun puzzles to solve that make use of the entire area you’re currently playing in. The forlorn puzzles on the other hand are usually the block pushing kind, but there are also puzzles involving snakes (in which they move like the phone hame of yesteryear) and wind blowing blocks. And more obviously. They range in difficulty from simple to medium hard, with one puzzle in particular (in the first area) that stood out as difficult, to me anyway, or at least more complex in nature. But otherwise they can usually be easily solved with just a little time, patience and logical thinking,After finding each of the forlorn you can ask the campfire spirit to help you move on. This actually means moving to the next area. However, if you’re still missing one or more forlorn then you can ask the spirit for more direct hints that will lead you to their location. I personally never continued before moving on so I’m not entirely sure if you are required to find them all of just a minimum amount. But I think all have to be found before you can progress.Playing through the entire game, doing literally everything, will take about five hours. Afterwards there’s no reason to play it again, but given the price that shouldn’t be a big deal.I never encountered any bugs or glitches, but the camera - especially in the first area - didn’t always show me the entire layout properly which resulted in sometimes stumbling on a forlorn by coincidence.Graphically the game is pretty with simple, yet detailed areas and nicely modeled and animated characters, although the animations are quite limited to be honest. It’s a game with a colorful exterior, but a more moody interior when you look closely.There’s no voice acting, but there is a narrator who does a decent job. She sounds a bit dull, even uninterested at times. Maybe to match the sadder vibe of the game, but in any case I didn’t care for it.There’s very limited use of sounds, although there are ambient sounds like birds chirping that make the world feel alive. The music also sounds great with melancholic melodies that feel hopeful at the same time. Very nice.The Last Campfire is a good puzzle game that shouldn’t be overlooked. It isn’t a long game and the puzzles aren’t terribly hard which means it can be enjoyed by anyone. While the game is colorful and it looks playful there’s a sadder, but simple, story behind it all. It never gets to the point that it becomes depressing, though. Considering the price they ask for this this is an easy recommendation for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The cute design captured my attention, but when i played it, my gosh, the story is so sweet and deep. The narrator guide you all around a beautiful environment with such a sweet voice. Loved every moment. The puzzles weren't easy but neither extra difficult. Enjoyed it so far. Lovely details and music.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire has an enjoyable mix of exploration and puzzles. The difficulty is on the lower side with simpler but rewarding puzzles, and hits the sweet spot with few headscratchers but avoids anything you'll get stuck on for 10+ minutes. Cute story, if not a bit overbearing- do yourself a favor and turn off the unbearable narrator voice in the main menu. Easily recommended at the current sale price of $4.49, I wouldn't feel bad paying up to ~$7.49.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a not-too-hard puzzle game with a lovely story that I definitely recommend picking up - especially if it's on sale for $3 again. It very well could make you tear up by the end if story elements align with your experiences with depression or anxiety, and it's a good reminder that you shouldn't lose hope and should try to surround yourself with people who truly care about you (and that you truly care about in return).Overall, just a nice time that can help you unwind and reflect.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Short, enjoyable puzzle game. Puzzles were pretty simple. The story is a downer, I guess an attempt at being an inspirational downer. It's worth it on sale if you like puzzle games and a little story. I'd give it a 6/10While it has overwhelmingly positive reviews it's worth noting if you look at the achievements only 35% of people that have played it have completed it. For a game that takes 5hrs to 100% it seems incredibly low.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: While I absolutely loved this game, I did catch it on sale when it was half off.  The game itself is not very long, so I do recommend that you get it on sale if you're able to.However, it has a nice story and beautiful graphics.  The puzzles are challenging, but not too challenging.  Definitely worth a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very calm game with a melancholic, compelling story. The puzzles are not too hard. As a result, the flow of the game is not interrupted but rather enhanced by them. The vivid colours and simple shapes along with the soothing narrator's voice and pensive music make for several relaxing evenings.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty well-balanced puzzle game. It has two levels: main story where you move through the different parts of the game world, collect some items and use them to unlock more of that world, and some pure puzzle rooms where you solve a problem with a set of different mechanics in a sandbox setting. The items-related part might be a bit too easy because it's always obvious which item should be used where and which you need to find to unlock something. I quite liked the world exploration: it's not completely linear, and you can run around between a few connected areas to unlock all puzzles and pieces of the storyline. Sandbox puzzles vary in difficulty, some are too easy and get solved in seconds, others are more interesting and made me think and try a few times. I wish the game had a bit more of the challenging puzzles, at least as optional challenge.The story is a bit melancholic, but leaves you with hope and touches some deep topics. All this with some very nice, even cute narration.P.S. the game should have been named "Forlorn". It's a cool word and is used a lot in the game
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable all the way through.Not only the Characters and their Story or little conversations, the narrator fits perfectly and adds a lot to the feeling you have during the playthrough.You play as a little lost soul, that doesnt know where it is and whats going on. During your exploration of the world, you find other lost souls and with different puzzles you can help them.The whole game I felt really emotional and the more I was exploring, the more I got surprised by the beauty of it.All the detail - seriously I have nothing to complain about this game.It is adorable throughout!Here is a little playthrough, but in German:
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a great game for those who like to help others.. it is absolutely adorable and the story sucks you in. Filled with puzzles that will tickle different parts of your brain, it will provide a challenge for everyone. If there was a sequel or another game in this style, I would absolutely play. So worth my time, I would definitely buy again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A short game, but a meaningful game. Stylized and stylish, smooth and touching. I was motivated to seek out every hidden location, in a way I am not usually. Reminds me a lot of Journey in that way, and that is a compliment.Puzzles follow a nice curve in difficulty, but remain accessible. They are nuanced and reflect the story being crafted. Play it with a controller.Don't ever lose hope.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: What a nice, little gem of a game! Mechanic-wise, most of the gameplay is consisted of puzzles, relatively simple, well executed, and with very small difficulty factor. Graphics and overall aesthetic is superb, and ties well with the atmosphere of the story, the game's best element.Story follows Ember, an elemental(?) entity travelling through what can be described as the "middle world", the place between the living and the afterlife. Ember's purpose is to help others like them to process their past regrets and fears, serving as a beautiful allegory for the human concept of death, and the feeling of loss that comes with it.In the end, the game might be described as a well-crafted metaphorical journey about death, grief, and the fear of moving on. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a relaxing journey where you have to complete puzzles, some harder than the others but I found them essentially easy and more or less the same with some variants.It's solid and well made, graphics are nice and I really like the soundtrack. The voice of the narrator, Rachel August, was great too. It made me feel like I was a kid hearing a story told by another kid. :)The story has a beautiful message and just that makes it worthwhile to play and complete it.Good for a casual gamer who wants to experience a journey.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with interesting puzzles. Played for about 6 hours. Received no achievements even though I finished all puzzles. No support to assist with solving achievement problem.Started a new game/save and got the first two achievements; however, I shouldn't have to play the game all over again for the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A cute puzzle-adventure game with extremely likeable cast of characters in the veins of an old fantastical tale. The environment, the voice acting, and the pacing is extremely well designed. Puzzles are fine, I didn't find them to be too difficult or too simple. Highly recommended for puzzle-adventure fans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I was completely immersing myself in the mysterious atmosphere they had created and really enjoying its art.I think it tells a story about finding others' hopes and  lost souls to help them be alive again, by solving puzzles. But I'm very unhappy about the part that I can't quit long conversation when I accidently start it!It has open ending. They may or may not find the way home but at least they were still trying and be together. And there was always a choice left-live in the forest. Because the key point of hoping and moving up is to find a satisfied and realistic way to live.It is a story about community, trying and hope. It has guided me to see the good point of community and friendships-one of the forlorns said: now I've seen that I need better friends. And just like puzzles to forlons' hope, paths in the reality are not straight.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a simple and interesting puzzle game with an intriguing child-like story line. The controls are easy to master and the graphics are pretty good despite it's simplicity. It is somewhat poetic in parts and immersive enough to continue playing for a few hours. It is not an overly long game (I completed it in about 7 hours) but is great if you are looking for something less stressful that promotes self-awareness.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Shape the world to move on in the story, find your way to restore the flames of the embers <3*Relaxing game with beautiful and meaningful story/messages. *Puzzles range from very easy to medium.*Voice-over takes some getting used to, but the way she speaks adds to the feel of the story imho.Would definitely recommend it if you're in for a relaxing atmospheric story puzzle game.(Game took me about 6 or so hours, I left the game open by accident >.<)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The game is gorgeous if you're into that kind of art style.That is all the positive things I can say for this game.Gameplay-wise, the game feels like a chore to play after a while. The puzzle felt repetitive and uninventive, it only revolves around permutating the movements of the objects using specific order or directions to solve it. That is it for most of the time.On top of that, too many invisible walls and flawed game logics. Just because the floors are 1 inches higher or lower, your characters cannot walk through it. I mean, come on!!!Also the outdated distracting journal scavenging, it is a 2021 game, ppl should come up with better implementation for side-story notes instead of treating it like a meaningless note collecting mission that tortures the minds with OCD and ADHD. It doesn't even feel rewarding to collect them all, it even breaks the immersion at times.Story-wise, I'm quite neutral. I dont hate nor do I love it. But I wont call it story that much since it is more like poetry.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Oh well... it's one of those games again.It's reasonably well made -- technically. Looks excellent, sounds nice, plays nice. It could use a map, though.What ultimately made me go "I can't recommend this" is the story -- it's boring, repetitive, and boring. And if that wasn't enough, it's also boring and repetitive. I still don't really know what it is about though, but I'm glad I finished it. And the game looking good can't make up for that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A very good Puzzle Game with positive Messages.The Puzzles themselfs aren't crazy difficult, so it's also solveable by a younger Audience.If you're looking for a Game for your kids, you could 100% let them play that, the topics are safe and supportive.The one thing that personally annoyed me about the Game is the long breath it has, i wish there was an option to increase text speed/shorter narration and an faster way to reset puzzles.The biggest selling point of this Game is clearly the adorable Artstyle and the nice Music.Overall i would give this Game a 6.5/10 (or 3,5 Stars out of 5)If you liked the Artstyle and the Music i can recommend 2 other Games for you that you should definetily check out aswell:- TUNIC (9/10)- Death's Door (9/10)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game with amazing music, storytelling and art style. The story is deeper than you'd think with this lighthearted art style. Has a satisfying ending and with it being only about five hours long to beat the story, I just couldn't help but explore every nook and cranny of the map. _childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Charming little puzzle game that you can take at your own pace, and it's not too difficult.  I completed all but 2 puzzles without help.  Nice touch that you can choose your boat style from the builder, although paddling was a bit hit and miss regarding the directions. Very enjoyable, just wish it was a bit longer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Such an adorable game. What an experience. Entire game is beautifully narrated by one person. The atmosphere is somewhat relaxing and heartwarming. Helping 'the forlorn' by solving the puzzles. The puzzles weren't that hard, although I did get stuck on a few, particularly The Cave's campfire. With 100% achievements that can be completed in one playthrough, this game is sure to offer an enjoyable gameplay and kindness.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the last campfire, and let me tell you.......that was beautifulHelping others who have become too discouraged to push onward, helping them through their despair, and to finally reach the end of your journey as a wanderer yourself. An amazing game. and completed in about 4 hours.but if you have a small brain for puzzles in could take longer
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing little gem.It takes ideas from many other works that I already loved:1) from Hob it takes the fantasy world and the type of camera (I have to say that when I played Hob years ago, Iwas not a big fan of the static camera; however, it fits well in both games)2) from Tom Raider it takes the puzzles3) from Ghibli & Henson it takes the characters (spirits and creatures taken from Mononoke & Dark Cristal)4) from Moss it takes the concept of small-independent areas in a big scenario, plus a cutetiny character (let's make this clear though: Moss is - and will always be - the CUTEST character EVER)Overall, TLC is a very good game; technically is not very demanding yet very beatiful, with simple but nice visualeffects; the sound and music are not from other worlds but they are still good enough, the lady that gives her (English)voice to the narrator does a superb job (This also happens in Moss).I bought it during a weekly sales (75% off) but I would have paid the whole 12.5€ price for the 9 hours that tookme to complete it (with all achievements/collectibles).I will keep an eye on next "hello games" games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Chill and cute puzzle game with really nice worlds and simple mechanics. It's perfect for lazy evenings and should last you 6-7 hours, or 8 if you're a completionist. By the way, a note for completionists: there is no achievement for finding all diaries here, so you can skip them if you need an external incentive. The puzzles are on the easy side, sometimes making you wonder it that long pathway with wind statues was supposed to be a puzzle or not. The characters are voiced in a lovely but kinda melancholic way, which fits the theme of the game focused about the final journey. I liked the atmosphere of all locations a lot.After beating the game, don't forget to check out the puzzles screen - there are some additional puzzles that have previously unused mechanics! I liked those the most, but I understand that they might have been a bit too difficult or tedious for the main game.Overall, I can recommend it on a sale, where it's an appropriate price for its length and difficulty. Puzzle enthusiasts might crave something more headscratching, but the characters, story, and narration make up for the lack of challenge in my opinion.Runs flawlessly on a Deck, out of the box.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game has no right to be as heavy as it is. It's beautiful, it's ugly, it's bright, but oh so dark. Get a cup of tea going, toss your favorite blanket in the dryer for 10 minutes, schedule an appointment with your therapist & take this game as slow as you need to. The goal is to experience the game, not to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Cute laid back puzzle game with nice sounds and visuals, at times felt a little sad, but I enjoyed it. It was quicker to play than my play time indicates, but I left it open. I would definitely recommend this game, which made me think, and I enjoyed the puzzles, some of them were a bit challenging to figure out, which is nice. I'd like to see something else similar from the devs in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game for 1.5 euros. So very cheap and saw the overwhelmingly positive reviews, and because i like puzzle adventure games i thought this would be a very good time. Well not quite. While it is a little charming and soft it really doesn't convince me on selling the whole compassion thing it tries to tell you. This is more of a children's game that you let your 6 year old play rather than an adult. And I do think adults can enjoy many games which are meant for children, this is not one of those IMO. While i haven't played that much of it until i decided to refund it, i still wanted to give it a chance and try out some puzzles. But ultimately it just wasn't for meImportant note: This game has a child narrator to invoke the feeling of a cutesy, cozy children's fairytale. If you dont want everything narrated and just want to hop into puzzles after puzzles with some original, fresh adventure take to boot, then you gonna feel left dissapointed.  It just falls a little flat on the deepness side and feels kinda shallow in my honest opinion.Games like these are better off without any narration and minimal dialogue. This game hasn't any crazy amount of dialogue but more than i found necessary. Sometimes it is better to show or let players experiment rather than tell them.This game wants you to feel mystery and to solve that mystery in order to give you a reason to complete the puzzles. But i found the mystery kinda shallow and lacked originality. I seen these things before and even though it tries to touch some weird aspects on mystery, it lacks the creative ''weirdness'' that i would want from a game like this. I just expected more of an old school vibe when i purchased this game rather than the soft, cutesy, little preachy game that i played.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I never ever write reviews... BUT this game deserves one!I can highly recommend this game; it has such a nice atmosphere, music, gameplay (I play with a PS4 controller) and is just very enjoyable to play. The puzzles aren't too hard and I just fell in love with this game. The only thing I didn't like was the narrator's voice, but you get used to it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with beautiful music and nice story. The puzzles were mostly easy but fun, couple ones got me thinking and trying longer and made me little frustrated. I hoped there would have been more these harder puzzles.One thing I didn't like was that the narrator and all the characters you talk to, are the same voice actor. Everything else was nice and I really liked this game. Good work Hello Games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: "It's not like I'm a preachy cry baby that gives over emotional speeches about hope all the time ... what?" - Katara, Avatar: The Last AirbenderSeriously, SO CUTE. I loved it. And honestly, I kinda needed the message right now in my own journey irl. Never give up hope because you fear the unknown. It's always worth pushing forward!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful game, with great audio. The world is interesting, there are lots of great little touches and a touch of mystery and wonder. Its story is reminiscent of children's books that have little lessons, and I thought it was a neat touch. The puzzles aren't frustrating, even a bit easy (so far!), but it was a really good evening spent lying on the couch with the partner while having vaccine brain fog.Congrats Hello Games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Simply a beautiful experience.Overflowing with symbolism, packaged within the most wholesome of children's book style writing, and a sprinkle of eeriness to boot - with perfectly crafted audio-visual aesthetic that fits all three of those descriptions.It took some obvious inspirations from Journey, but that's not a bad thing in any way. I enjoyed every second of this game, and I'm glad I decided to play this gem after it had been catching dust in my Steam library for years.9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A game about death, fires, and people becoming hollow (or "forlorn")? Yep, it's a souls-like.On a more serious note, it's a fun short kids' game with an obvious amount of care put into the storytelling and puzzles without requiring you to invest too much time or energy (my initial playthrough took around 6 hours). I found myself playing it to unwind after Platinum-ing Furi and was surprised at the emotional depth on display, it was everything I'd hoped GRIS would be (vibrant and reflective instead of monotone and empty, somewhat populated instead of isolated, etc.). Minor details, like some Embers not wanting to be helped or the journal scraps of the previous person to complete a full pilgrimage, really helped to flesh the world out and ground it to a degree. I can't say how many children's games over the years have been this cathartic because I certainly never played (m)any of those, so I wouldn't go so far as to call this a masterpiece, but it's definitely one of the best games I've played in the past couple of years in terms of overall experience, and I'm glad that 7 months later I can finally support it on Steam as well.The OST deserves to be sold on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it was a nice indie game (don't regret playing it).For 15 USD I got an artistic puzzle game with a moral theme (life/ death/ hope).Never got stuck, all puzzles were moderate difficulty at best.Enjoyable for kids/ adults alike in their respective way I believe.Wouldn't play it again, but that's all good, just like a book, sometimes reading it once is enough.I always enjoy trying new games like these from time to time.GG.7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a very beautiful game. It has cute graphics and a lot of metaphors to think about and relate to. Overall I would say it is a cozy puzzle game, that gave me 6 h of joy. You can feel the love the creators put in it. Also the achivements are placed in a fair way and you dont necessarily need a second playthrough. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Very lovely and heartfelt game. I really liked the storytelling and the narrators voice.The puzzle and riddle aspects weren't too much or too annoying (I'm usually not a fan of those).The whole thing was just super sweet, a little story about hope and helping others, bringing their happiness back into their lives. Definitely recommended.My favorite part was my green custom duck boat :') Adorable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a 7-10 hr adventure puzzle game whose main focus is on the story and puzzles. It is quite linear and the puzzles are quite easy to solve. Yet, the story and the overall cuteness of the game can hook to finish it. I thoroughly enjoyed it from a story perspective. If you enjoy puzzle games, don't give this a miss. This is made by the team behind No Man's Sky.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game. First let's start with WHY I DON'T recommend this game.I fell asleep a few times playing this game on different occasions to be honest. I was streaming too. LOL! Zzzzzzzzzz.............The pacing is slow and objectives are repetitive. The game is a tad too long for what you are doing and that is due to the puzzle difficulty. Most puzzles offered a great challenge but due to the length of the game I just wanted to get through 'em towards the end. Overall the game just didn't hit me emotionally the way I was expecting considering I've played similar games like this. I appreciate the emotion, and bringing attention to mental health. Now here's WHY I DO recommend this game.I LOVED the narration! Maybe that's why I fell asleep a few times. I felt like I was being told a bedtime story. I took me back to "Room on a Broom" or something. The art style was beautiful, the characters were very cute and the metaphors surrounding metal health, life, struggle, triumphs, fear, doubt, uncertainty, hope, determination were genius. I also can't complain about unlocking 100% achievements in one run. I feel the game rewards you for going off of the beaten path to quench your curiosity. So I had a love/dislike (not hate) relationship with the game. If you have the patience of a monk and seek enlightenment then this game is for you.I give The Last Campfire a 7.0 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Compelling story and interesting gameplay. None of the puzzles was too hard that it made me want to give up but it didn't feel like they got progressively harder; there were some very simple puzzles in the last section of the game. I was able to complete the gameplay and all puzzles/achievements in 6ish hours. Definitely worth the time spent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A smart and artful game about the passage of the soul into the afterlife and the acceptance of life's natural end. For a game seemingly about something as morbid as death, it's quite beautiful. It keeps to its strengths with environmental AND instance based puzzling that walk the fine line between easy and hard. Creating a continually rewarding experience full of momentary realisations. It also does a good job of making its little map  larger than it is, with the use of multiple interconnecting pathways and puzzle solutions that lie in the next plain. Its an intelligent little few hours. And has a distinct polish to it (despite the occasional clipping through environments). I would recommend to it to pretty much anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful little game. The story is poetic and emotionally touching. Music and voiceover are delicate but very atmospheric. Game mechanics are simple. Most puzzles are easy - albeit not obvious - but there some tricky ones.Advice #1: playing it with your kids can provide the right level of challenge for them and a chance to talk about our inner feelings.Advice #2: try it on the Steam Deck. Controls are perfect, the game is not taxing on battery, and the experience is highly absorbing, almost meditative.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game primarily because I wanted to support Hello Games. Was totally pleasantly surprised and wanted to leave a positive review. I highly recommend buying it on sale if you want a quick, endearing little adventure with visuals, audio, and a story that all punch far above their weight. Took me under four hours to complete.Biggest Pros- World design, audio engineering and animation are absolutely top-notch and so much fun. - Charming story and characters; probably the main draw, cool little story with some nice revelations and thought-provoking outcomes.- Controls/puzzles are all nice and tight and I didn't run into any issues.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely cannot recommend this game enough. I had bought this game due to its promise of fun puzzles and cute style, which it delivered on completely throughout the entire experience. I hadn't expected such a heartfelt and relatable message at its core, with thoughts and feelings I think just about anyone can relate to.This is a game that's worth every penny and one that you can just feel the love that was poured into its creation. The Last Campfire is definitely a game I intend to revisit again.

_childDocuments_.review: You can totally skip this game! nothing special at all!The puzzles are too easy and kinda are reminiscent of Breath of the wild shrine puzzles (without being physics dependent) which is fine for an action adventure game but not enough for a Puzzle game. there are also some weird level design elements like unpolished extra rooms and spaces which looks like hidden paths with no rewards, or no/weak environment colliders that leads to bugs.the story is also another cliche about hope which is overused in video games, although I enjoyed the narrative choice.Verdict: 6/10 - a cute but simple puzzle game that could be enjoyable on steam deck or if you want a relaxing experience. but don't expect much from it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely charming, and relaxing. Don't expect any head-scratchers from the puzzles. A hard mode would be welcomed, but tbh it's not necessary. _childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely, relaxing, heartfelt story about keeping hope and sharing hope with those who are in despair. It's also about empathy and understanding that some may not be ready to receive your help or may want to figure things out their own way. Great reminders for teens/adults, great lessons for young ones.It took me 6 hours to complete, and I played it for 6 hours straight. It's not a difficult game for teens/adults, though some puzzles may be challenging for younger kiddos. I don't believe the point of this game was to be difficult; it's an interactive story. I highly recommend it. I think it's worth full price, but for full transparency, I definitely bought it on sale. Either way, I don't regret my purchase. If you like these kinds of games, then this belongs in your library.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game so badly. I'm thankful that I waited for a sale to pick it up. The Last Campfire is clearly made with a lot of intentionality and care. Unfortunately, the whole game feels very hollow. The puzzles are easy to figure out and not incredibly rewarding or satisfying to solve. It became frustrating to have to run all over the place just to get to the next one. I think that what killed this for me was the BEYOND annoying narrator. I felt that the game was trying to almost baby me through obvious events and cut scenes by pointing out things that the player can clearly see happening. I don't need to be verbally told every time I find a journal entry or item that I have found a journal entry or item. I can read two lines of text when an NPC is talking to me, I don't need it read to me out loud in the same boring droning voice. It became annoying very quickly and I had to just make a decision to move on.

_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a beautiful puzzle adventure game with cuddly looks, but a very deep theme about loss, death and despair. If you like  games that make your brain hurt with their puzzles like Forgotten Anne, Sonority or Ori and the Blind Forest, you might like The Last Campfire, too.+Well done score that is subtle, but still gives you goosebumps at the right moments+Well thought out puzzles with different levels of difficulty+Intriguing writing, that will make you wonder what all of that even means+Cuddly, sweet art style with creepy or weird splotches from time to time+Great pacing, that let's you have breaks and keeps you hooked at the same time-it's very short-the meaningfullness of all the messages, settings, and dialogue might seem a little over the top, if you are not willing to engage-an overview map of the world is missing. And that is a big deal! And also the run button has to be pushed again once you switch screens (why?!!!)Rating for gamers: Rating for people who love to solve a variety of puzzles: The Last Campfire has a lot going for it: well thought out puzzles, a mysterious story, sweet art work, great pacing, ... The list goes on. But it has one treat to offer, that should be the main reason you play this gem: a captivating charm, that will make you think about it even when you are not playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a lovely little game with a beautiful art style and touching story. The puzzles are thought provoking but nothing too strenuous to prevent you from continuing play, the music is wonderful and the play style is super easy to pick up. _childDocuments_.review: I just had surgery on my left shoulder and was looking for a game to play (to not "think" about the pain). But I saw this on my desktop as I've previously purchased it and haven't played it yet.And boy was I surprised! I was torn whether I should be sad that I haven't played sooner, or glad that I am now immersed in it after surgery. It was such a lovely game that I have to type a review with one hand. The controls were easy too (was able to play with just my mouse). The puzzles were of mixed difficulty but were all manageable (if not, walkthroughs are available). As someone who loves exploring every nook and cranny I find the visuals breathtakingly amazing. The story is captivating with its fairy tale vibe and it's cute with its storybook way of narration, not to mention the narrator's voice is adorable and dreamy! Even the music and sound effects add to the appeal of being in a different world. The story is astounding especially if you are experiencing (or have experienced) grief of losing someone you love, or if you've lost something precious — this game will hit you in the right places as I've bawled my eyes out on some parts or dialogues. Truly a lovely game! I feel sad the journey ended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a cute little puzzle adventure game. Running in at just 6 hours, it’s a short little experience that isn’t very difficult. Wrapped in a cute aesthetic, the deep non-religious philosophical themes about life and death can be experienced fully without feeling frustrated by difficult gameplay. Whether this amount of content is worth the $15 asking price is up to you. But pricing aside, it is a fun quick and simple experience I recommend. The gameplay is very basic and straightforward. You are a little character known as an Ember, and you need to help free other Embers so they can continue their journey. This will have you running around some hand-crafted environments with different areas as you look for these Embers. When you find one, you will have to solve a puzzle to free them. These are positional/maze-type puzzles. Most of them are easy to figure out, but there might be a few that take a little longer.The controls are very simple. On keyboard:As you can see, the controls are very simple (there is no rebinding, unfortunately). Camera angles are fixed, so there’s no camera movement required. There is no platforming, no combat, no abilities, and no loot to equip. Everything in the game is there for a specific purpose. Outside of some optional collectables, it’s all a straightforward journey. There are some environmental puzzles outside of the primary puzzle levels, but nothing too crazy.As small as the puzzles are, they typically reflect the internal obstacle the imprisoned Ember is facing. So the puzzles, and the gameplay, tie into the themes and story of the game. I don’t think this is something you play for the gameplay; it’s a game you play for the experience. And the gameplay complements the that experience in a simple and non-distracting way. The themes, story, and accompanying presentation are the main reasons for playing. This is a cute short little game with a focused scope that doesn’t overstay it’s welcome. The game is very philosophical, and wrestles with the questions of life and death in a non-religious way. Feelings of fear, regret, catharsis, and more are explored on this little journey. Whether you agree with the conclusions or not, the game portrays real feelings and concerns of people who are faced with life’s greatest questions. And it leaves you thinking for a little bit after you’re done, reflecting on your own views and feelings around these topics. To clarify, the story itself is not some accomplishment of innovative storytelling. It’s a very simple tale, almost like a children’s story, or a folk tale. But it’s simplicity helps to convey those deep questions in an accessible way.The presentation is very cute and charming. The artstyle and environments are colorful but simple. I wouldn’t say they look low budget. More like they fit the scope of the game very well. Areas read clearly, and it’s easy to figure out where you need to go. The Embers all look cute, and the small cast of supporting characters all look whimsical.The sound complements the game well. The narration throughout the game is very integral to the tone. Her light voice almost sounds child-like, and adds that tonal layer of a bedtime story. The music adds a somber tone, and doesn’t feel too repetitive, even though it often is. It’s probably not a soundtrack you’d buy, but it fits the game well enough.Overall, the story conveys themes that are deep but in a way that’s not too heavy, and the presentation complements this small but focused direction the game aims for. I do want to point out that a lot of the praise I give to this game is based on the context that it is a small short game. It’s trying to do a small focused thing, and I think it does that well. But I also don’t think this game is a technical masterpiece, or an innovator of story. It’s a small contained game, and I think the atmosphere is reflected well within those limitations. The Last Campfire is a short indie title that’s largely about the experience of playing through easy puzzles that reflect on deeper themes. The gameplay and atmosphere are both simple presentations, which is why the depth of the themes is so surprising when you actually play through it. However, it is a short game, and there’s no replay value here. I got this game on sale for $1.49 and it acted as a nice palette cleanser that I enjoyed my time with. But at $15 it’s up to you if that’s worth a 6 hour light puzzle game with a somber yet charming experience. Do I recommend it? Yes. But it’s up to you how much this experience feels like it’s worth.

_childDocuments_.review: However, I would like to start off with a . Because I see this game generally described as cute, relaxing, calm, suitable for children… So please be aware that there is a jumpscare plus two tense scenes in the last chapter.Also, if you have a phobia of , those few scenes may make you extremely uncomfortable.OK, so many games have way scarier things than this. And we get some forewarning through textbites that the creature ( ) is not out to harm you and that it really is only . But still – this is *not* relaxing and *not* nice, in a game that is otherwise gentle and kind. I found it terribly jarring – and am also very annoyed when devs throw stuff like this into otherwise casual and relaxing games. Please don’t! Otherwise, I found this well-made and enjoyable. The overall themes are loss, loneliness, sadness, hope, companionship, perseverance and kindness. With more of a wistful than a sad tone. Thankfully not too heavy-handed on the “lessons learned” bit, nor cloyingly cute. Puzzle-adventure with no platforming, timed elements, or stress – other than the scare mentioned above. No combat, killing or dying. A few skeletons lying about, but friendly-to-neutral and non-gory. Some mild childish-type gross humour (gluttony/pigs).I found the puzzles well integrated in the gameplay. And neither too easy, nor too frustratingly difficult, grindy or obtuse. With a decent variation in puzzle type mechanics. And fairly consistent difficulty levels. Game can be played without solving all the puzzles, and you can choose to go back to the puzzles later via the main menu. When game is completed, 4 bonus puzzles unlock.It looks nice (colours, graphics, scenery, …). The dialogues are good, give some depth without being too many or too long. And – thankfully ! – none of that tedious line-by-line, (or even worse, letter-by-letter) that some games insist on. I tend to play most games with sounds off or low, so didn’t pay that much attention to the music and voice – but they’re perfectly fine I reckon.Ran well, encountered no bugs. Manual saving – always appreciated, thanks dev. I played on KB+M with no issues. On a standard laptop (WIN10) with no special gaming anything – my CPU tended towards “lightly fried” on long playing sessions but fine overall.I’m an old lady newbie and don't feel competent to comment on tech stuff. Other reviewers have done that so well, and already.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this beautiful game.  It was a joy to play and experience and I found the ending incredibly emotional.  The artistry is beautiful, colorful and clean lines.  The little embers reminded me of the wayfarers in my most favourite game,  Journey.  I loved the narrator too.  I felt after a long number of years that I was being read to again like a child.  The puzzles were just hard enough for me that I couldn't solve them right away, but only had to look for an online solution once.   I definitely recommend this game.  I was sad because I knew I reached the end, but was pleased to see there are a couple of extra puzzles to complete.  I really want another game like this one!  This was a gift from my friend and I can see why they enjoyed it so much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

A few really made me think, several were way too easy, the rest sat somewhere inbetween. Overall I'd say it's moderately challenging, and there's enough "solvers satisfaction" to make you feel like you've got the brain working.I played on Steam Deck, worked ootb, set to 40hz/40fps for battery longevity, and it was a perfect relaxing on the sofa game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an adorable and pretty game! I loved the variety of environments, and there was a nice cast of characters to meet.Sometimes I did feel like the narration and animations slowed down the game a bit. It's supposed to be kinda like a storybook, but the writing could be a bit "tell, don't show", even when the player could see what was going on. Still, the narration was pretty charming, and I do think it added a lot to the characters (I especially liked the Builder).The visuals were really nice, and the environments were super pretty! The bloom could be a bit much, and it felt like I couldn't really see some details with how bright it was. I think the caves, both at the beginning and the end, were my favorite locations. I guess I just love dark areas with bright colors lol.Overall, a nice little cute game with good puzzles (the extra puzzles really stumped me at first). _childDocuments_.review: Its a great game. About 8 hours playtime, lots of puzzles. A few of them really got me desperate but I didnt need to look up any of them. The game design is very well done, guiding you where you need to go without directly telling you. Looks beautiful and still runs on my rather mediocre laptop. The puzzles themself are very diverse, nothing feels like its repeated too much. The music is incredible, I actively enjoyed it - very well done! I think what really sets this game apart is the narrator. I have never played a game with such beautiful narration that guides you through the whole story. The voice is so calm and beautiful, agh I am in love! The story itself and the little dialogues feel very meaningful, some stories and comments really hit me in the feels. The whole game is like a carefully crafted tale, every little piece fits well and forms a very enjoyable journey. I would definitely recommend this to everyone who loves stories, puzzles and games that leave a little mark after you played it. <3

_childDocuments_.review: It is cute little indie puzzle game. It is aesthetically gorgeous, the puzzles are not overly difficult yet also never tedious -- a good balance of being able to solve the puzzle but making you think a bit essentially, and the story is interesting, mostly revolving around a not so subtle theme of death. Another plus is you get 100% on achievements for beating the game on first playthrough if you care about that sort of thing. As for cons, the game's controls feel a little wonky, almost as if this is a somewhat failed console port. And the soundtrack was pretty forgettable if I am being honest. Regardless, good game as a whole. Worth it on sale in the five dollar range. Provides give or take 5-6 hours worth of content.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short and cute puzzle game which plays like an old Zelda game. You solve puzzles, you pass by blocked segments, you solve puzzles, you get an item that unblocks new parts of the game or provide you new gameplay and keep solving puzzles. The puzzles are not too hard even though some can be a bit tricky. There is no hint system but you can always try another puzzle. There are also puzzles in the world itself which gives you small bits of lore.The story is pretty simple but the characters and the environment are very well done and lovable.It's very easy to suggest this game if you enjoy Zelda-like games with simple puzzles and exploring. It's very straightforward and doesn't require much backtracking which is a nice plus.. It doesn't try to inflate the game time with useless walking trips.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Don't expect difficult puzzles. This game's beauty definitely lies in its simplicity. Took me about 8 hours to finish all the content and I appreciate every single second spent in this game.I strongly recommend playing with headphones and a controller while laying relaxed on your chair, bed, sofa, bean bag... just make sure you're in a comfy spot and no one disturbs you so you can properly devour everything this game has to offer. The music is brilliant and the atmosphere created by the SFX is just amazing.Overally, it has a certain innocence to it. The story telling is beautifully progressing throughout the levels, following the main character's movement across the levels. Reminded me of Bastion and Transistor in a way. One other thing that's in the same zone with those two: all dialogue and replies have a certain maturity and wisdom to them.To conclude: I wouldn't have regretted spending 12 euros on this product and am strongly recommending it at its current price offer (8.74 euros).

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying the game so far. It's one of those games that gives you minimal information and hints as you go and you pretty much have to figure things out for yourself which I appreciate as I feel like a lot of games spend too much time babying people in a tutorial setting, This game has a variation of puzzles but the one's I've encountered so far have not been mechanically hard to complete they've been something that you need to sit and work out logically (opposed to a platforming-ability-test.) Enjoying it so far, some of the messages/dialogue that are included in the game I really appreciate "not every problem is something that is ready to be resolved right now" is very appropriate with the themes of moving on, grief, feeling trapped in a situation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Okay what can be said about The Last Campfire?In short: It's pretty, cute, colorful, relaxed, full of puzzles and collectables, the controls are simple and so is getting the achievements.Now for the somewhat longer version....(I know most of you all don't like to read about a book lenght of review so I will keep it short.)The Last Campfire is a game made so simple in control use that even a child can do it, you simple move around by using WASD, the arrow keys or just by clicking with your mouse on the screen.What I love about the game is that you don't feel any rush to get something done, you are free to roam around and explore and there are no time limits for anything, but however some collectables to seek out.The whole experience feels relaxed, the surrounding and music are pretty and puzzles range from very simple to quite complicated but however never impossible.If you feel like you messed up a puzzle you can simply walk back to the individual you are helping, return to the world and then when you go back in the whole thing is reset.The puzzles do not have hints however and sometimes it's really just a matter of trying with mistakes and error until you find the right way.Personally I am one of those people who gets lost in games easily, but I have to say that it was not as much a problem here.Now the story of this game is as much sad as filled with hope and the willingness to help, the narrators voice is soft and gentle and the story is easy to understand.Occasionally there is put in a little joke or a deeper understanding of some stuff, but even if you wouldn't catch it, it wouldn't take away from the game it self. For as far as I have noticed there aren't any bugs or issues with this game which to me is a big plus!Overall if you are just looking for some brain training and relaxation this will be the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire was very relaxed, there was no rush on figuring out the puzzles, allowing time to explore as well.I did glitch out of bounds on the east cave bridge a few times though, exiting out the game and logging back in fixed it.I really enjoyed The Last Campfire, and the  ending was heartwarming.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS IS A NEUTRAL REVIEW. The Last Campfire is a solid puzzle/adventure game. The strong points are - the colorful, vibrant graphics. - the complex, engaging story, about a being that loses itself in a journey, but then ends up helping numerous souls who were stuck in a sort of limbo- the main character is likable- the narrator did a nice job - most of the puzzles are okHowever, what I value most in games is the gameplay. My rule of the thumb is: if the game for some reason doesn't draw you every day to play it, there is something wrong. So the negative sides are: - the gameplay wasn't engaging for me, - there is a vast, empty world, where exploration is not very rewarding, the optional collectibles you collect are some vaults with parchments, on each parchment there is a one sentence message that is supposed to mean something but in my opinion is disjointed with the rest of the game- there are 3 maps/campfires, with 7 souls to help each, each soul is 1 puzzle to solve. But also you have to solve many puzzles in order to navigate the vast world and to find each soul and to find each campfire. There is no minimap, and that is a grave error by the developer. I found it boring to find the souls in that vast map withouth a minimap. - the pacing of the game is slow- some puzzles were annoying- when the ending comes with the final cutscene, you get to understand that the story is not nearly as deep and interesting as you thought. If I understood correctly, it actually revolves around the fear of death. In my opinion that is dissappointing, because only atheists/materialists have such an intrinsic worry about death being the ultimate end. - there is only 1 voice actress, so she has to do voice over not only for the main character, but also for all the other beings he/she encounters, that is kind of cheapI'm sure hardcore fans of puzzle/adventure games would like this game. I don't feel like giving it a negative review because it was clearly done with hearth and a lot of effort. But it's not nearly as good as the majority of reviews say it is.

_childDocuments_.review: This review should be prefaced with the disclaimer that as a rule, I do not play puzzle games. This game however has won me over. Fully-voiced, beautifully presented and with a soundtrack that has been undersold, this is a puzzle game that I can get on board with. You start as a lost 'ember' in an unfamiliar world and are tasked with the job of bringing hope to those forlorn who have lost their inner lights. The game gives you many choices, whether you want to help others or just take yourself to the end. Truly a heart-warming experience. Those who like Gris will love this game, and vice versa. I will note that some puzzles and aspects of the adventuring had me stuck for over fifteen minutes, but in the end I loved it. While there is limited potential for replays, as the story does not change, it's certainly one you can come back to each year and happily relive the adventure. I'm very grateful this game exists

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has recently lost a lot of hope, I hadn't realized I needed this game. Every one of the forlorn felt like a piece of me, every puzzle solved a promise to that piece to keep going. But in the end, I'm still left with questions - who helps Ember? Who shares their flame with Ember when they feel as if they can't keep going and have no hope to give to anyone else? Why did their friends at the beginning not check on them? Why didn't they ever turn around or even seem to notice Ember was gone?And to the overwhelming group of people who seriously think this is a children's game... I'm sorry you missed the part where the story is much more than most children would be able to get.It's worth every penny, even when not on sale. Short, bittersweet, puzzles that are just good enough they won't make you tear out your hair in frustration. Stop caring about achievements and find everything and help everyone. They need it.

_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled across this game on a sale and it was quite the surprise. The colors and graphics were soft and inviting, the controls were simple, and the puzzles were just challenging enough to hold my interest.The Last Campfire sees you playing as a being known as Ember. They awaken in a cave and see that they must make a journey home. Along the way they meet other embers and characters who have lost hope in the journey or in life itself. It's up to Ember to save them and lead them home, wherever that may be.The Last Campfire is a simple puzzle platformer. You won't be jumping or fighting enemies, rather you will moving blocks and manipulating objects to solve puzzles. In the main world, you can explore, find items, and beings called Forlorn. They are embers who have lost and have turned to stone. Once you interact with them, you will transported to a puzzle stage in which you have to move or manipulate objects to reach the goal and save them. Each world you go to has a set amount of Forlorn you must free to continue on and reach the end.The game has great graphics, nice use of colors, and great narration to keep you interested in the story. The whole thing has a storybook kinda vibe and I totally dig it. The best part is that it's not a terribly long game. You can extend it a bit by looking for collectibles from a being known as The Wanderer. They are not necessary to get %100, but still fun to find.I think my only gripe with this game is simple. With puzzle games like this, it's almost necessary to have some kind of hint system in place for your puzzles. This game does not have that. Most of the puzzles were simple to solve and may need a few more brain cells than normal to solve, but some of the later puzzles really had me stumped and I had to look up videos just to help guide me in the right direction.Final verdict? This was a fantastic little game. I loved the vibe, the story, and the puzzles had a great "Ah Ha!" feel to them at times which always feels good. If you're looking for calm and chillaxful puzzle game to play, The Last Campfire might be what you're looking for. Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those inoffensive games that ends up looking better in Steam's binary ratings than it actually is. It doesn't do anything great -- but it also doesn't do anything bad and it comes with a lot of charm and a short playtime, so it doesn't overstay it's welcome.It is quite easy -- not necessarily a bad thing! -- just know that if you're a hard-core puzzle player you're likely to be disappointed by this. I am not a hard-core puzzle and even I thought many of the late-game puzzles were ridiculously simple.I don't think it is marketed this way but this is really a "cosy puzzle game", where there's only a smidgen of challenge so you've always got warm fuzzies about making progress.It doesn't have much of a story. It mostly coasts on melancholy vibes. What story there is is the same kind of thing as Spiritfarer -- lost souls in a kind of afterlife need help moving on. None of them have more than a vibe -- this one is anxious, this one is lonely -- and none of them even have names, so there isn't exactly some deep, emotional resonance to the game.If this tried to be a longer, fuller game all these creaking faults would eventually cause it to tumble apart. But you can finish it in 5 hours -- even the slowest player is unlikely to take more than a few days -- so the charm manages to carry it during its brief duration.This is a very recommended with reservations kind of thing. If you're looking for a brief palate cleanser and don't think whatever price you're paying for 5-hours, you probably won't be disappointed. But this is also pretty slight and forgettable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a wonderful family friendly puzzle adventure game. I think the best part of the game is the voice acting of the narrator who makes the story feel like a book on tape and brings emotion to the characters. The story overall is pretty good and the ending has a deeper meaning than I anticipated. The puzzles are well designed and most are not too difficult, which makes this a good entry level puzzle game. Exploring the world feels good too because sometimes its a puzzle to unlock a new part of the map. The gameplay is very simple, there is no combat, just lots of puzzle solving which I love.

And I love the fact that you may find an item and at first it seems to be unimportant, but later it turns out that you really need it, I RECOMMEND ^^

_childDocuments_.review: - The graphics are cartoonish and 3D. Not a visual powerhouse by any means, but still looks nice- The music was fine, but I didn't find myself humming along- The voice acting was serviceable- Without spoiling anything important, you play as a little being named Ember who wants to help other little beings make their way to the end of a mysterious set of caves to find rest- It's a sparse story with few plot points, but a definitive narrative isn't really the focus- The game focuses much more on the philosophical tapestry you weave together yourself from your brief encounters with strangers and the journal scraps you find along the way- The mood is pensive and mysterious, and rarely strays from that throughout its length- The game takes place around 3 main environments, each with a central hub with a campfire in it. Your goal is to help guide some requisite number of lost souls move on before you're able to progress- Each so-called "forlorn" you encounter transports you to a puzzle you must solve to save them. Some are surprisingly easy, while others take a bit of trial and error. Some of the tough ones are pretty cool- It's not horribly difficult to 100% this game (just rescue all the forlorn), so many players may find a lack of motivation to replay it- The game ran flawlessly on the Steam Deck- I ran into a bug where I actually squished and trapped myself with a column. Quitting out and loading back in fixed it- . If you like the idea of going from puzzle to puzzle while a bittersweet little story plays out in the interludes, this is a pretty worthwhile experience

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art, excellent puzzles, adorable characters, and a just-deep enough story.
