_childDocuments_.review: In short: This game has amazing atmosphere and a fantastic art style, but the game is pretty short and the replay value is a bit lacking. If you're looking for a whimsical and emotive experience, definitely worth buying. I would recommend it regardless, but if you're looking for something more substantive, I'd recommend waiting for a sale. If you're looking to scratch an indie-game itch, this is definitely worth it.The game is beautiful--the environments are vibrant, the soundtrack is gorgeous, and the character designs are cute and memorable. I couldn't praise the team more, they really hit it out of the park. I'm not that emotional of a person, but even I found myself moved by the end of the story and I really do think a large part of that comes from how phenomenal the presentation is.On the other hand, the content of the game is a bit lacking. It is a puzzle game, and most of the puzzles are isolated logic/brainteaser puzzles, like block-pushing or rotation puzzles, that spring up as you try to help various strangers. There are more dynamic puzzles in the overworld, but those also tend to be fairly isolated to a single area. However, the puzzles are really hit-or-miss. I more or less breezed through most of the puzzles and the few that I couldn't figure out right away only took a few minutes of trial-and-error to get the solution right. Some of the puzzles I could hardly call puzzles, and the 1st area (which you play in the demo) does a really bad job of showing the player what puzzles they could expect. For example, there's a puzzle where you need to place a prop on a pedestal to move to the next section, send the prop down to the next level via elevator, and do that two more times. There's no thinking involved, as there's only one move you can make every time. Even if you want to say that it's for the sake of getting the player familiar with the mechanics, it's disappointing that they would have to hold your hand that tightly. That said, the puzzles do have their own narratives that progress as you complete the puzzle, so they may be thought more like cinematic setpieces, but even so, I'm sure there could have been more engaging puzzles.If I'm not mistaken, I completed every puzzle available in the game. There are also some extra collectible notes you can find along the way and I think I got most, if not all of them on my first playthrough. At the end, my playtime was a bit shy of 5 hours after starting with the demo. And while the game was a pleasant experience, the underwhelming puzzle design holds me back from wanting to jump back in. If you're looking for that breath of fresh indie-game air, this is THE game for you, but otherwise, there's nothing wrong with waiting a little while to get it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game and I think it's one of the cutest puzzles games out there with an interesting lore. The puzzles aren't extremely hard, but do require you to think on some levels. Finding the Wanderer's Journal was like finding hidden Easter eggs in the game. Sadly, whether you manage to find them all or not, it doesn't count towards your achievements (though, I really wish it would've been some sort of hidden achievement for the players that went through the trouble of collecting them all.) I loved the graphics, music, and ambiance of the game.Overall, this game was an absolute blast to play and I would definitely recommend it if you're looking for a casual indie game with a bit of adventure to pass time.Overall Rating: 10/10 highly recommended!

I found the controls a bit unwieldy sometimes (moving blocks), but I enjoyed myself very much. Very much worth it to pick up in a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The last campfire is a puzzle game with a story about finding hope in bad situations. There are two main sets of puzzles, the ones contained within the individual characters, and the ones that open up the environment so you can progress through the game. The self contained puzzles are all very straightforward, as in you always know what you are meant to be doing, but the action of completing them can be complicated, especially towards the end of the game. The environmental puzzles are often a result of getting sections done to do more sections. If you can't figure out how to get somewhere or do something, then you probably should come back to it later, because there might be something you haven't done/gotten yet. The game took me 6 hours to complete fully including all collectable pages, with minimal backtracking, and it feels like a good length for it. As much as I enjoyed it, it's one of those games that would actually suffer if it had too much filler.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely puzzle game with fun and challenging levels. It rewards exploration and has a beautiful and soothing art style. The story is compelling as well. If I had to say one bad thing about it, it would be that it's rather short. I would have happily continued for twice the time. Highly recommended if you enjoy puzzles in a relaxing setting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The game's visual style is colourful, which fits well with its touching narrative about life and loss.The puzzles in the game are engaging but not particularly difficult. They often involve moving objects or guiding flames to specific points. This isn't a hardcore puzzle game; it's more about the journey and the feelings it evokes.A standout feature is the narration, which adds a lot of charm and helps to convey the story's emotional weight. The voice acting is soothing and complements the game's gentle atmosphere perfectly.On the downside, there are some technical hiccups. I have experienced occasional graphical glitches and control issues. These don't ruin the experience but can be a bit annoying.If you enjoy thoughtful narrative-driven games with light puzzles, having played it through twice I'd say it's definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This was just an absolute joy from start to finish. Charming, cute, and cozy this is the perfect game so relax with and an excellent game to play with kids. None of the puzzles were particularly hard, but they do require innovative thinking and this makes them fun (not irritating as I've found in some other puzzle games). I 100% the entire game in just under 7 hours (You should be able to get all achievements within normal gameplay) and I cannot recommend it enough!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: It's worth it for its price. There are various of puzzles in the game and although the puzzle mechanics were sometimes a bit repetitive, each puzzle has its own unique flavor so it doesn't get boring. I got stuck a lot of times trying to figure out what I need to do because there were no instructions or goals. Some of them were obvious, some were not. The story and the world itself was beautiful! I have like 50+ screenshots from this game!  Overall, 10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game. The puzzle difficulty well it's not Cosmic Express or games like that and it shouldn't be because the focus here is on the story. The puzzles are good throwing a variety of mechanics at you, but most will not take more than 5-15 minutes to complete. The puzzles are generally good and varied with few annoying puzzles. I personally struggled with some due to having aphantasia as I had to rely on much more trial and error as I couldn't properly visualize the proper sequence, but all in all very good puzzles. The story is very good indeed. It's told partly via a narrator describing what's going on much like Bastion, partly via dialogue with characters scattered about and partly via diary logs (also scattered throughout) that fill in the gaps of what has gone before. There are 40 diary logs, I found most of them but not all. The story is best experiences and not told here as it's basically a metaphor for something. Something doesn't mean it's vague it means you are allowed to fill in your own interpretation of what this metaphor is and at the end you have a conversation and you are allowed to pick responses fitting with your interpretation, at the very least it fit my interpretation very much. I liked this very very much indeed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice casual puzzler with a saccharine voiceover that marvels breathlessly at every cutesy thing that happens, following the trend of "deep" puzzlers that hint at themes of loss, sadness and loneliness and have children as main characters, except they are fantasy creatures, so they aren't actually children, just look and act like them. It's about as deep as a typical instagram feed or a reality show whose participants cry in every episode. But if you just ignore everything it says, it's a fine game with mostly great graphics. The puzzles are not difficult and you still get to think a little bit before you get it on the larger ones.There is a lot of running around from place to place, sometimes I wish there was a fast travel option.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I have finished the game in under 6 hours going out of my way to look for every collectable. The first thing I would like to mention that this game is amazing I went into it thinking it would be an amazing puzzle game but as the game went on the story was amazing. the puzzles were amazing not spoiling any of them but the complexity is pretty simple so if your not a good puzzle solver this game would be pretty OK for you. the longest it took me to beat one puzzle is 2 minutes but to be fair I play a lot of games. I would recommend if you can afford and like puzzle games or want to try a good puzzle game
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful, atmospheric puzzle game with amazing visuals, beautiful audio, and a meaningful story about always holding on to hope, not falling into despair, and the importance of helping others ignite their flame. Not only is it a gorgeous game, but the characters are also super cute. The puzzles fall on a spectrum of difficulty with some being quite easy, some taking a bit of trial and error, and most fall in between. There is also a variety of different, creative puzzles so you will not feel as though the game is getting too repetitive. I believe that all of the achievements are story based so there is no stress about getting full completion and you can just enjoy the ride. It is a fairly short game but I think that it is most certainly worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game... a bit heart-wrenching emotionally and a little difficult to navigate the character, but gorgeous graphics and music. It's a little frustrating that the player is unable to manipulate the perspective/point of view in order to look around corners, etc., but once I got used to that, I realized that if you cannot look around a corner it means that nothing is there to see. Challenging puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a beautiful, soothing, comforting game that is friendly to casual players. There is no time pressure, the story can be as fast or as leisurely as you like, and the storytelling is well done. The antagonist is a genuine force to be reckoned with, but has its own story that gradually becomes clear, and has a resolution of its own.I have played this game much more than my hours on record suggests, having previously played it a number of times on Switch. In fact, it is the game that introduced me to modern gaming after a very long spell where I played only retro games on my 2000s consoles. It showed me some of the ways that gaming had grown and changed and made me interested in learning more.By now, the puzzles are straightforward for me, but I do remember there being some reasonable brain-teasers on first or second play. I don't remember them being frustrating enough to take me out of the immersion, though. I enjoy the puzzles but the interest factor for me now is mostly in simply enjoying the environment and music and story progression. This is a game you can play in an evening, if you're so inclined, but you can also drag it out over a few sessions, especially if you track down all the Wanderer's Diary fragments. Either way, it's rather like being wrapped in a comforting blanket. It's a game I sometimes turn to when I'm having trouble switching off from a stressful day or event.Although it's a third-person game, characters (including the protagonist) are mostly not of any particular gender or life stage, and "they" pronouns are used. For people who prefer first-person play, this may be helpful in being able to view the protagonist as a self-insert.Others have spoken at length about the depth of meaning and touching nature of the story and messaging. I won't labour that point except to say that I share those sentiments. There is a lot of making-sense-of-life meaning to be found here, and it's unpacked in a way that is touching and yet also light-touch.The Last Campfire is a beautiful experience. I can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: "The Last Campfire," developed by Hello Games, is a heartfelt adventure puzzle game where you guide a lost ember through a beautiful and mysterious world to find meaning and a way home. The game features a series of clever puzzles and a touching narrative that explores themes of hope and perseverance.The art style is visually stunning, with enchanting environments and a soothing soundtrack that enhance the game's emotional depth. The narration adds a storybook quality, making the journey feel like a comforting fable.Pros:-Beautiful and enchanting visuals.-Thoughtful and engaging puzzles.-Heartfelt and emotional narrative.-Soothing soundtrack and narration.Cons:-Relatively short game length.-Some puzzles might be too easy for hardcore puzzle enthusiasts.Overall, "The Last Campfire" is a poignant and visually captivating adventure that resonates on an emotional level. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely incredible fun adventure puzzle indie game. Took about 6 hours to complete the whole game, all puzzles and achievements done. Fantastic flow to the game, great story narration throughout. Nice graphics, really relaxing game to play and I enjoyed working out the puzzles. Had to use YouTube for a couple but the rest I worked out myself. 😀 Highly Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game! The atmosphere that the story unravels in (forest setting) is beautiful and relaxing. The riddles are very carefully crafted and the level of challenge increases as the game progresses. The whole setting reminded me of ancient civilizations and the primitive technology that operated motion and transport. It was a refreshing experience. The game also communicates positive thoughts and emotions, such as hope, respect, mutual aid.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot different than the type I usually play but I quite enjoyed it. The puzzles are fun and vary from extremely simple to slightly difficult. The artwork is great, it looks a little cartoony at a glance but the textures upclose are fantastic. it has some sad and dark elements throughout the story that helps balance the "cute" look. What I really enjoyed is how chill it is. I found it relaxing to wander through this world saving souls and moving various objects in various ways to proceed
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: *INSERT SCREAMING JONAH*Ahhhhhh! This was SO CUTE. From the Scottish narrator, to the general message of the story, it really moves you along. I beat the game in ten hours and the first night I had played three and a little over a half hours. Which means, I played like six and a half today. It wrapped me in. I also enjoyed how it wasn't a huge grind for everything, the game was challenging but also super relaxing. This definitely filled the hole it was meant too. Meaningful and different. A palette cleanse after seventy hours of Zelda: Skyward Sword. Loved the puzzle solving and exploration and story in this game. The artwork - MAGNIFICENT.Also, I got this on sale for $4.75?! A STEAL.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a presentation-forward puzzle/exploration game. The game is certainly gorgeous, but I had some stuttering, collision and visual glitches throughout. Rewards for exploration are often lore notes, which is a bit frustrating if you're not interested in those. Puzzles themselves tend to be higher-order Zelda puzzles: block pushing, mirror turning, item arranging, etc. Again, the presentation is beautiful but the substance is pretty straightforward. Overall this is a perfectly adequate game for people who really like Zelda puzzles but aren't looking for a grand sweeping adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. The characters that you help throughout the game feel like they honestly need the help and their issues are something understandable to the player. This make it incredibly rewarding to help each character and makes you feel warm, especially with the couple of characters that converse with you afterwards. The message is something hard to deal with but delivered in such a way as to allow the mind to properly comprehend it. While the puzzles are not the most challenging, the story is better for it as you don't get so lost in the puzzle that you forget what the game it telling you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Basic but pretty graphics design, which is the only redeeming point. Narration is way overdone. If you were annoyed at all in Ocarina of Time (you know what I'm referring to), then best to turn off narrator voice right away (doesn't take away the overabundant forced written narration prompts, but at least it's an improvement).  Simplistic puzzles could be alright but are put down by a clumsy interface, making it a frustrating experience. Absolutely zero controller customisation, so if you're using an adaptive solution (i.e. for disabled gamers), look elsewhere. Story is very bland and does a poor job of getting you to care about anything. All in all, I bought into this game looking for a relaxing experience, but found myself bored and irritated most of the time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful short experience based around the concept of passing on and accepting death, fairly simple puzzles although one did bug out on me leading to me thinking the way i tried wasn't correct (it was), so I spent a ridiculous amount of time trying to figure out how to do it before looking up a walkthrough and seeing i had done it correctly and it was just a bug lol
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Tried the demo last year, and I knew straight away I am going to get this game.The last campfire is a very cozy puzzle game of you playing as Ember, the cute tiny creature who tried to help rescue other 'forlorn' to get back their flame. Surprisingly a wholesome game with a serious undertone about losing hope and depression. However, little ember will try to help and give some advice that is applicable for us players. In fact, the game hits me hard at times and got me a little emotional. Fully narrated with a bit of accent, and she also had lisp - it is not a bad thing; I find it matches the vibe of the game.The only downside, as a puzzle players I found a lot of the puzzles (especially the last leg of the game)  very simple and easy. It felt a little bit underwhelming. This game has a bit of challenging puzzles as well, so It has a good range but mostly pretty simple puzzles. Definitely would play again this game sometime, recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best puzzle game I have ever played! the puzzles are fun and interesting, the graphics are amazing, and this is probably the best I've ever seen the topic of mental health explored in a video game,the story may be a bit simple and the puzzles aren't particularly difficult, but the target audience is children so who cares
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. It's not a complicated or overly long game and that's fine! This game knew what it wanted to say and it said it, no content stuffing. Art is beautiful, narrator is fantastic. For me the puzzles were challenging but not overwhelming which was perfect cause I"m bad at puzzles. Could have used more variety for dialogue lines for certain situations but that's a super tiny nitpick. Can't wait to see more games from this developer!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, let's get the negative out of the way. The puzzles are awful. They are not difficulty or witty. There are no "ah ha!" moments. Nothing. The same couple moves that you use to solve the first few puzzles are the same moves you'll be solving the last. The more "difficult" puzzles just require you to use the same moves just more times. If you are buying this game for the puzzle aspect I do not recommend it. That being said, what a wonderful game. I genuinely loved my time spent in this world. The are direction is fantastic and the world feels rich and grounded. The narrator is charming and gives the whole thing a "story book" vibe to it. It's such a cozy game. Pour yourself a cup of tea and grab a few biscuits and play this for a couple of hours. It's worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics, animation and sounds are all very well done.The narrators soft and gentle voice is perfectly suited to the story.The story is about the choices in life, so well presented.Interesting puzzles which can be challenging at times but all are doable with some patience and attention to surrounding areas for clues.It can be played in 2 modes, Explorer (simpler/fewer puzzles) or Puzzles. All the achievements can be obtained in a single play through in either mode. In the main menu is an option to do 25 puzzles separately. I played as Explorer so the harder puzzles didn't break the story immersion and then did the puzzles afterwards.Not a game to be rushed, savour the journey. I didn't want it to end.Amazing !!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: i don't usually make reviews but for this one i will.the graphics are wonderful and imo, pretty immersive as it is. the sound and music are very chill and comfortable. as for game play, i'd say it's simple that it doesn't break the flow of things. for people who aren't used to puzzles, it can get pretty tricky but i would say they won't frustrate anyone too much. as someone who likes puzzles, solving the puzzle was pretty instinctive though so i was able to focus on the story.the story is great and the narration just fits so perfectly well, rounding up the entire game as an experience. the game touches on meaning, hope, and hopelessness in a way that can get a little personal but not too on the nose that you'd scoff at it.the game is "short" apparently can be played for 3 hours but i played it for 6 hours, so that sounds worth it. so anyway i might have cried a hell lot after i finished the game. thanks for the tears, i had a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A game that captures your heart and does not let go. The Last Campfire is not particularly difficult, only one of the puzzles really stopped my progress, and even then the answer required that I pay slightly better attention. The story, the soundtrack, the visuals are all phenomenal, and this is an experience that is well worth the price. I wholeheartedly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Very short puzzle game, if you're good at solving puzzles quickly. A bit of exploration is needed to discover all puzzles, but it can be done really easily if you search thoroughly. I recommend getting this game at a discount, since I finished the game is under 5 hours without needing a guide and solving puzzles in less than 5 minutes each.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: What a great little game. The art style, the voice acting and the set up for the game was an absolute joy. I had no expectations for this and when it popped up in steam it grabbed my attention straight away having recently play Hoa I wanted another short but puzzle friendly game to play and this scratched that itch nicely. If you are looking for super difficult puzzles this isn't the game for you but if you want to chill and have to think just a bit then this is perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game. Overall a very relaxing experience. There isn't much challenge, the puzzles are fairly easy, most of the game is exploring and finding all the hidden pathways and collectibles. The laid back difficulty suits this game perfectly. This game deals with some heavy and dark subject matter, but the twee narration and super cute characters offset the melancholy a bit. It's hard to discuss the story beyond that without spoiling anything, so I'll just say it's bittersweet throughout and ends just the way it should.Highly recommended. I look forward to playing through this one again after some time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game. A story about people losing hope and replacing it with sadness and despair.ProsCute characters and a really good art style. They look like they have pillows garments over their bodies but still very cute. The puzzles were interesting. Not too difficult but they kept me entertainedConsThis game should have had a few features. A quick travel system would have helped. I was looking for the last few chests and I had to walk over the entire game and it was a hassle. The sprint animation was weird that I have to press the spring button over and over. These are all just nitpicks. The game is short and sweet that these cons listed doesnt affect the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire has some really good elements to it. The artwork is beautiful, the music is peaceful and relaxing, but the story, the puzzles, and frankly the voice narration leave something to be desired. I guess I am in the minority but I strongly disliked the choice of narrator, didn't really get involved in the story, and I thought the puzzles were generally boring and repetitive. As such, I just can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little game, enjoyed every moment of it.Beautiful music, well made level designs and quirky art style. The story indeed has more meaning underneath its surface and it is beautifully narrated.Finished it in about 6 hours, casually playing and taking in every little detail. I haven't tried using a controller yet, but you can use either a keyboard, a mouse, or both.Thank you Hello Games, for this wonderful little gem.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game from start to finish! The puzzles are creative and challenging, but not so challenging that I ever felt so frustrated I wanted to give up. The story is beautiful, and the graphics and music are gorgeous. My only issue with the game is the constantly moving world. There's no need for it and you can't disable it, which messed with my motion sickness a bit. Otherwise I had a lot of fun and would definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys a nice, chill puzzler with a lovely story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a cute little adventure/puzzle game. It's got an adorable art style, the puzzles aren't that challenging however there are some good brain teasers mixed in, and the music and sound is all absorbing. I'd argue the games biggest strength is its narrative, not for its strength of writing (though it is good), or for its complexity, or even its uniqueness. It's a rather straightforward tale, with only a few moving parts. However, it's delivered with a rare sincerity and earnestness that was not only compelling but emotionally impactful. I could tell where about it was all going fairly early on (playing enough games or reading enough stories will do that), but in spite of that fact it still managed to illicit tears from me (the 2nd game to do so for me personally) by the end. It's a brief, enjoyable, satisfying experience that I'd highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Bought for just 2 bucks, started with no expectations, and yet they were exceeded. Incredibly relaxing and beautiful game, with a very emotional atmosphere. The puzzles aren’t particularly difficult, except maybe 1 or 2, and the story is a mix of cuteness and sadness. Highly recommended, but for 16 bucks it’s a bit too much. Wait for a sale, and the game is a 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy adventure, hidden object and other puzzle games definitely give it a try. I was a bit hesitant to buy the game as the graphical style seemed geared, IMO, towards pre-teens but I did enjoy the puzzles which range from easy to slightly difficult.  The only troublesome one that had me going back and forth was the steam pipes. The game is certainly colorful and there is enough variation in the puzzle mechanics to keep puzzle lovers interested. Bought this in conjunction with "Shapik: The Moon Quest" and both are very good games but between them I'd give the nod to The Last Campfire.  8 or 8.5 / 10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely and wholesome game! The graphics are simple yet gorgeous, the narration really fits and brings a cozy vibe, the puzzle mechanics are always well presented before needed and, although the puzzles themselves are not hard, they get quite clever. The game is not very long, but it gets you through an amazing journey, from beginning to end. In general, I really feel this game was built with a great deal of care and love from everyone involved. Would absolutely recommend, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually leave reviews but this game was amazing. Puzzles were just the right difficulty that I was able to solve most of them myself but had to look up a walkthrough for a few puzzles. A nice, comforting, and beautiful game (with fantastic voice acting) that I definitely recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

The story is touching and enticing and I loved every minute of the game.. Makes you think about how you view life a little too.. I would definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a wonderful game all around, very sweet story and interesting puzzles. If you like breaking things too you get an item a bit into the game that you can use to peer out of bounds in a good chunk of the rooms, so if you need a break from the puzzles you can zoop around with the camera for a little bit.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Over a year after release and this game still has bugs. These devs would not have jobs if this was the 90s when you were actually required to finish your games. Things as bad as going down a ladder and your character just sinks through the floor instead. Puzzle breaking bugs too that got me stuck for a good hour until I left the area and came back only to find out I wasn't stuck at all, the puzzle was just bugged and wouldn't let me progress. There's a lot to like about this game but I'm not going to recommend a game the devs refuse to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic puzzler with tons of charm. The vibe and tone of all the game elements meshed well - Kudos to the voice actresses performance. The puzzles were all enjoyable, ranging from easy to moderate, depending on your skill level - some of the difficulty was in discovering what options you had available in the puzzle solving and once realized, everything falls into place (smart puzzle design in my opinion). Overall the pleasing visuals, adorable characters and soothing narration makes you care about the journey, giving the player all the more reason to happily and satisfyingly, push through the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This was a snore fest. Everything felt boring. All the puzzles were extremely simple, solvable in a minute, two at best. The premise is cute (main character goes around, saving people from depression), but the story wasn't as captivating as people say. In fact, I didn't care about it after the first hour, it was just as boring as the gameplay. After almost 4 hours I just deleted it cause I had no interest in continuing.To summarize you in this game you can enjoy the story, gameplay and maybe visuals. The story wasn't interesting for me but it's subjective. The puzzles (which are the only real gameplay aside from running around) were extremely simple and not engaging. The graphics were ok for an indie  game but some models were straight from PS1. It's an ok game for kids but I regret buying it,
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is much more enjoyable than I thought it would be. I suck at puzzles, but with some help from the website and youtube videos, I can completely beat this game! (Super proud)The thing I love the most from this game is the narrator's voice acting. It really makes the game feels real. Oh yeah, amazing soundtrack and lovely graphic too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I usually like cute visuals and puzzle games but The Last Campfire did nothing for me. Visuals are nice but the puzzles are too easy, the pace is slow and I just didn't care about anything in it. I would've probably enjoyed this game if I was a child.Got bored and couldn't finish. I kept playing hoping it would get better but it didn't and now I can't refund it. Ah well, at least I got it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game. It's cute with a beautiful unique artstyle, a lot of exploration and puzzles. The gameplay is relaxing and slowpaced and the story feels quite heavy (in a good way), there is a lot to contemplate for me. The narrator has a wonderful voice and voice acting and reminds me a bit of one of my favourite music artists. Can absolutely recommend, but it hits different when you're dealing with mental health issues (again, in a good way).
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game but not for me.Pros: Absolutely gorgeous graphics, unique character designs, etc.Fully-voiced narrator if you're into that.Variety of puzzlesSome clever puzzle mechanicsInteresting world to exploreCons:Puzzle complexity varies wildly, has no lead-up to more complex levelsOverworld doesn't have strong visual language leading you places; I like secrets as much as the next person, but going around in circles isn't very funExtremely clunky controls - feels like a portYou have to hold 2 keys AND direct your character in order to run??????Options are only accessible from the main menu. Why do games do this.Story feels like I'm being spoonfed, which ig is okay for a kid's gameA lot of people go on about how good this game is, and I'm glad they had a good time, it's just not for me. I was forcing myself to start the game and try and make more progress (which the map confusion made ever more fun, bc every detail of this thing slides out of my mind the second I close it out) and just couldn't have any fun aside from some odd "oh, that was a neat puzzle detail" moments.Anyways, I hope other people enjoy this more than I did.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A very well designed puzzle game with a rich 3D world. The narration and story is heart-warming and has a lot of meaning. It's slow paced and the music is cute.My only issue is that between major puzzles it forces you to do dumb micro-puzzles and tasks like collecting items and turning a key. The difficulty goes from 10 to 1 which feels jarring.$10 or less is a bargain for so many hours of fun and contemplation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: From the game's website: "The Last Campfire is an adventure, a story of a lost ember trapped in a puzzling place, searching for meaning and a way home”. I agree, because I've finished the game and I'm still searching for meaning. This game is clearly trying to convey a melancholic tone and tries to make you feel sad because "the ember people around you are sad" with no real explanation. The only deeper meaning to be found in this game is that which the player projects onto the game itself. Otherwise, it feels sad for the sake of being sad, which is no replacement for a more concrete storyline. For the most part, the puzzles are very easy. There are a few well-designed ones, but most of the puzzles feel more like speedbumps than anything challenging. And apparently a HOT-TAKE: I'm not enamored with the voice acting like a lot of people seem to be. I can only take hearing "Ember found a scwap of jouwnal" so many times.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire makes for a great weekend game. You know the kind; it doesn't take too long, can finish it in maybe two or three sessions, is fairly relaxed and doesn't test you too much. That's not to say there's nothing to the game, but it clearly doesn't aspire to be more than a pleasant and charming experience with a thoughtful message underneath it all. As a puzzle game, there were only a couple of instances where I was left thinking for the solution for longer than it took for me to actually do all the inputs to make it happen. Part of that is that the game makes it incredibly clear what it wants you to do and that when you are solving something it's pretty bitesize.The trade-off is that the puzzles end up not being overly challenging, but I'd rather that than anything feeling unfair or completely esoteric. There are a few dozen collectables to find which break up the pacing as they're typically found through exploration, although some do come with their own puzzles that can be quite fun to solve. The narrative driving you on is again pretty simple and is delivered, along with all of the text, in voice over. I went between finding the tone of this spot-on and annoying, though with specific regards to the latter, I do think children would actually engage with this part of the game quite well. In fact between that and the relative simplicity of the puzzles, this would probably be a great puzzle game for younger kids. At the end of the day it's a charming and satisfying game that doesn't outstay its welcome. I'd have liked it to push you a bit more, but over the course of the weekend I enjoyed it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt I can recommend this game if you want 6 hours relaxing atmosphere with an interesting story. If thats what you are after MUST BUY.Even after being through the story you get some additional challenges (and from my first look they deserve this name). There are also collectibles if you look for something like that and some are quite well hidden.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. The nature and the scenery are enthralling and beautiful and the story is touching and emotional. The puzzles in this game are just challenging enough to never get boring, and easy enough to not want to give up. This game is like a warm blanket for the soul and is easily one of my favorite video games. The Last Campfire is a must-play for anyone who hasn't yet. If you dislike this game, shame on you!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game with mild to moderately challenging puzzles.  Great narration, wonderful accent!  Recommended with some caveats:- The game does the camera work for you, but sometimes does not position itself well - especially as you search every nook and cranny for hidden journal entries- It's unclear which objects you can interact with; the game is inconsistent about marking these, which could lead to missing some journal entries- It doesn't have a quit-to-desktop option from the in-game menu- Many creatures in the game suffer from a condition where anxiety will petrify them - literally!  It's a miracle that they aren't extinct.  Maybe that's why their ancestors are all statues with ghosts...
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Its a decent puzzle game. - this is going to sound heartless, but I couldnt care at all for the artsy fartsy story. The poetic mumbojumbo held me back from playing and wasnt needed for my playthrough- this is one of those games, where you have to look for the right path in an semi open map, but there is realistically only one way to go. This leads to the player wasting time to look for the right path and I would have prefered a more linear experience. But it honestly isnt that bad, just unnecessary.+ the puzzles have good variety+ good lengthIf you like puzzles, this is a good game to playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The last campfire is a beautifully narrated puzzle game. The story explores the meaning of life, finding purpose and going on a journey. The whimsical artstyle, the mellow music and the uncertain moody atmosphere make this game very immersive.The puzzles in this game are easy and because of that the game can use a show and don’t tell approach to their design. _childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a visually gorgeous game about the quest for the meaning of life and what defines home.  It explores the need for hope in our lives and has a touch of melancholy when it dives into our human frailties.  It is very cute and colorful, but there is a dark side to it that may frighten children under the age of 8.The whole game has a relaxing feel to it.  There is no pressure other than what you put on yourself.  There is no violence, no fighting.  Just a lot of brain teasers and some delightful characters along the way.  Be prepared to be touched now and then by the dialogue as you can relate to how the forlorn feel.The story is about Ember who gets lost and has to travel through forest, marsh and caves to find his way back home.  On his quest, he meets fantastical creatures and spirit guides who are at each campfire.  It is from the spirit guides that he discovers about the forlorn…embers who had given up or who had lost their spark.  Ember carried the light of hope within him and his compassion and love for the forlorn really strikes the heart.Many of the forlorn are us when we are drowning in sorrow; when we lose hope and our confidence; when we feel abandoned or lonely; when we feel confused or discouraged; when we are full of doubt or regret; when we feel a failure and want to give up.  All of us need an Ember in our lives and some of us are an Ember to others.  We stir others up to try one more time and that is the story of friendship and community.  These are the topics that come out in the narrative of this game.  Very deep and sometimes sad because not all forlorn want help or to move on.The narration is by a woman with an English accent and she voices the emotion that each forlorn is feeling at the time.  When Ember touches a forlorn, a puzzle is started.  These puzzles are easy to medium level, with a few hard ones thrown in.  These include mirrors and blocks and require some strategy.  Graphics are crisp and colourful.  Each environment is crafted beautifully and the music compliments this.  It is never intrusive, but is enough to enhance what is going on.  Game play is simple.  You can use the arrow buttons (I used keyboard) or just click the ground in front of Ember and he runs to the spot.  His motion made me laugh because he always looked like he was drunk as he rolled side to side!  You also control lights deeper in the game and use WASD to rotate them.I struck no bugs in this game.  The small developer team did an excellent job here and delivered a very meaningful game.  Achievements are easily obtained by just completing each environment.  There are hidden boxes which hide messages and notes from The Wanderer who preceded Ember.  Not finding all of these won’t affect your achievements.Highly recommend.  9/10.   This Ember is now heading off to put a bonfire under someone’s backside!!  Keep shining your light of hope to others.Postscript:  At the end of the game, go back to the main menu and click on puzzles.  There were 5 puzzles that weren't in the game, so a little hidden bonus for us!

_childDocuments_.review: Really liked the whole game. I started playing it knowing a little of what I was getting into, but I was not expecting to feel immersed or even invested in it. Very quickly the game had me walk in a pre-determined path, then when there were multiple routes, I was compelled to explore. This game really satisfies the completion oriented player, I found myself going down every path and looking for every crate. The narrator really drove my curiosity and it passively hooked me into the story while I searched for what I could find. The puzzles are satisfying, challenging, and the mechanics vary enough that it does not feel repetitive. The symbolism in the narrative, the feelings surrounding the concept of accepting death, really made an impact and the end was a satisfying closure. Overall, I am really happy with this game and I would recommend it if you like puzzles, exploring, and near 100% completion. The game took me about 6 hours but I would not have asked for more, I felt it was pretty perfect. Thank you developers, this was a really great experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Apart from the vague story similarities, The Last Campfire couldn't be further from the developer's previous game No Man's Sky. Whereas that game is a megalomaniac scifi feature buffet, the Last Campfire is a simple, small puzzle game that only does a couple things and focuses on doing those things well enough.The joyful, vibrantly colored art style is beautiful and also helpful in leading the player to notice the important elements of each puzzle. The art goes well together with the softly-spoken narrator. Together they make the game feel like a bedtime story, which is a choice I quite enjoy.The game only gives the player a few tools to use. As such you never feel overwhelmed by your options. Instead the game is about using those few tools effectively in increasingly convoluted puzzles. More tools and gizmos would not have necessarily made the game better.What would have made the game better, however, would have been the option to remap controls - the defaults are rather clunky - and maybe a bit more length: 5 hours for 100% completion is not a whole lot. Though in fairness, the price of the game isn't that high either.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid example of a game that uses puzzle solving as a parable for dealing with difficult emotions. If you're looking for a hard puzzler, or just not fond of games that shine specifically because of their narrative--rather than their gameplay--then I'd be cautious about this one and look for sales.  However, If you love games that shine by combining all of their elements into a greater whole--and especially if you're onboard to get all blubbery over a couple of sock monsters having a very difficult time--this one will satisfy. It has the added bonus of doing a good job of being family friendly without feeling too young for adult players. This can serve as a great tool for both introducing any audience to gaming while also providing langue and examples regarding emotional processing. Just go in knowing that there are some clunky PC controls, consider breaking out a controller, and plan to have a straightforward, casual experience. The game does exactly what it says on the tin, and is never trying to trick you. Which is deeply appropriate for the story it's telling, but can result in experienced gamers being deeply confused about what to do with a second bowl of soup.  I just want the frozen golem to have soup. Please. It's so cold.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a puzzle game, where you play as a creature known as Ember who tries to complete their journey, and help fellow embers along the way. I tried this game because people say its similar to Lost Words: Beyond the Page, and its true. The overall vibe and atmosphere of both games are alike, the difference is that LW: BtP's levels are more linear, 2D-ish, and with some platforming parts. TLC is 3D, has levels you can roam freely (usually around a hub area) and focuses more on puzzles, with no platforming as you cannot jump.The gameplay focuses on exploration and puzzles. There are hub areas, named Campfires, where to progress you must save several forlorn souls. They're usually in side areas near the hub. You don't have to save them all to progress, but you better do. To reach a forlorn you sometimes need to explore or solve a puzzle, but the real puzzle begins when you enter their head. Each forlorn has a unique "puzzle room" for you to solve. The puzzles range from very easy to a bit confusing, but nothing too difficult. If you missed a forlorn, don't worry as you can backtrack to previous areas.The puzzle is basically to create a path to their soul, either by activating levers, moving heavy objects with your Lanthorn, reflect lights, etc. A good feature the devs made is that the solved puzzles can be played straight from the menu, with some bonus ones. It's nice to be able to replay puzzles without going through the whole game again, but the only ones available are the forlorn puzzles, not the ones you encounter in the "real" world.Lastly, the game has a pretty meaningful message, like how sometimes, if not most times, the journey and helping others along the way are more important than the goal itself. It's kinda deep and touching, but not really sad, rather heartwarming I think. If you love puzzle games, or ones with cute aesthetics, give The Last Campfire a try. We need more of those "cute-but-kinda-bittersweet-puzzle-games", like this and Lost Words.

_childDocuments_.review: In this surprisingly heartwarming puzzle adventure, you’re not a warrior, a chosen hero, or some grand savior. Nope! You’re a little creature who lost its way, just trying to figure out why everyone else around here seems so profoundly sad. It’s a rare example of a game that asks you to be a listener, a helper, and a thinker, rather than a conqueror. There’s no rush, no competitive drive—just a journey that might leave you thinking about what it means to be lost and found.You play as Ember, a small, hooded creature who wanders into a world filled with other lost beings called Forlorns—souls who have given up hope and turned to stone. They’re trapped by self-doubt, sadness, and fear, and each is a small story waiting for someone to help them rediscover their purpose. Through a series of gently melancholic puzzles and encounters, you learn that the way forward involves rekindling campfires to bring life back to these lost souls. In doing so, Ember not only helps others but moves toward finding meaning and direction for themself.The game is a blend of puzzle-solving and exploration, leaning on the simple mechanics of moving, pushing, and sometimes manipulating elements like light and fire to solve puzzles. Each puzzle is a gentle brain teaser with a purpose, designed to mirror the inner struggles of the Forlorn it represents. If you solve a puzzle, you don’t just advance in the game—you help a character find their spark again, literally and figuratively.From the art to the music, The Last Campfire creates a cozy little world that’s one part fairy tale and one part tiny therapy session. Soft, ethereal visuals make every nook and cranny feel like the dream of someone who reads a lot of poetry and drinks tea out of tiny cups. The environments range from  forests and windy caves to otherworldly landscapes with mysterious ruins, all wrapped in soft, moody lighting.The Last Campfire is like a hug in game form, with a sprinkling of melancholy and enough cute, squishy characters to keep you smiling—even while questioning the purpose of existence.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game.  Fantastic art, fun puzzles, and a much deeper story than one might expect.  It reminds me of a bit of The Legend of Zelda mixed with Brothers and Journey.  It means what you want it to mean and the ambiance keeps you playing.  It is as mournful as it is hopeful and as beautiful as it is cute.  So long as you like a good puzzle, you won't be disappointed.  Art direction and lighting are very well done.  I particularly enjoyed the voice acting of the narrator.  This is what an indie game should be: a phenomenal achievement by a small and exceptionally talented team.

The main gameplay is a not-that-tough (for me) puzzle game, but the story and graphics makes the experience amazing.  In between puzzles you talk with other super-deformed art-style characters and enjoy the environment.  The story itself is a great tale of experiencing anxiety about the future and how to deal with it.  I recommend the game.  I think only people that don't like cutesy graphics or want hardcore puzzles wouldn't like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so pretty, and the landscapes are so pleasant to explore with super vivid color and fun details. The story is well above average, too. It's mostly a logic puzzle game, with about 4 inventory item puzzles thrown in for variety. The puzzles are pretty easy, making this very accessible to all ages and extra fun to play with a child at your side who could "help" with some of them. While the puzzles are very easy, none are so obvious as to be boring to "solve". Most take at least a few seconds of thought, and perhaps a little experimentation. But you'll never rage quit - the hardest took a couple retries and maybe 3 minutes to solve. I would have enjoyed slightly harder puzzles, but I never regretted the time I put into this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a a puzzler with some very minor exploration elements added to the mix. The puzzles are all on the easier side, but the game doesn't outstay its welcome and has a decent atmosphere thanks to the competent narration and nice presentation that is somewhat reminiscent of Ghibli films. The short playtime makes the game a good palate cleanser, and if you're looking for some relaxed puzzle-solving, you can definitely pick up The Last Campfire during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The decision to recommend this game (or not) is a tough one. First of all, I was surprised about how attached I could get to a little creature barely showing a face. Dear me, it's so heart-melting, I wanna give a hug to some of these sad, pondering, scared characters and tell them they're gonna be alright!What I really liked was the very relaxing atmosphere and soothing music - I fell asleep twice. So this game did something that some more expensive sleeping aid apps couldn't do for me. That's why I give it a thumbs up. The puzzles are quite easy to solve, a bit repetetive maybe, but always surrounded by beautiful scenery. What really spoiled it for me was the story's end. While the narration allowed for personal interpretation at first, the ending shoves a truckload of pseudo-religious "wisdom" right into your face. And wow, is it depressing! So if you are the type of person who radiates so much positive energy that other people feel blinded, if you wake up beaming with joy every morning and are getting tired of your own constant happiness, this game might be your cure. If you want a game to explain to you , go for it, but please, don't follow that stupid, stupid advice. If you ever experienced hard times in your life or even tend to have some mental health issues, please stay away from this, or at least, call it out on its prophet of doom glorification, and don't take it serious. After all, it's only a puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The store page blurb is a great summary. In my words, "A saccharine yet charming story commenting on the human response to hope and despair, taking the form of an easy puzzle game." This will appeal more to people interested in sentimental storytelling and 2010's-indie-developer aesthetics, moreso than to avid puzzle game fanatics. A laid-back experience perfect for cozy, upcoming fall and winter days. The phrase "baby's first Outer Wilds" captures my perception of this game.Three things I liked:1) Puzzle mechanics were unique and easy to learn (good sign-posting/discoverability).2) Challenges and mechanics build progressively.3) Pleasant story and art style.Three possible improvements:1) Puzzles were not difficult - I finished the main game in <6 hours and only had to restart two of the puzzles (this might be subjective based on one's experience with puzzles).2) Short game - 6 hours of main content and a handful of bonus puzzles upon completion felt short, especially since I did not find the puzzles particularly challenging.3) More story development - It was difficult to gauge progress from the story beats. I had to be told "Oh you're going to the final area next, then your journey will be over." The story felt more like a string of isolated concepts than a tale progressed by my actions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game from the art, to the voice acting to the music, the sound design, the story, and the themes.The puzzles start out easy but then get harder and incorporate more elements and the map or navigating around becomes it's own mini-puzzle sometimes.Explore and talk to everybody.There are some very emotional themes about going through life and challenges and keeping hope with no end in sight. At first glance it may seem like a surface-level story-telling device but if you pay attention to the dialogue, there is some inspiring and compassionate commentary.Played great on Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little puzzle game. So far I finished the 1st "world" and it wasn't that hard, but enjoyable. Looking forward to see where the story goes. I really like the soothing voice of the narrator, reminds me of Bjork.Edit: finished the game after nearly 8 hours. Really a pleasant experience. At the end we are confronted with the  (in a very lighthearted simplistic way). Puzzle were neat, while not really complicated.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game that is so emotional and melancholy without being depressing. I love how tactile everything is, you don't just flick a switch to pull a lever but pull the lever itself. I also love that there are individual puzzles however they are interspersed by overarching world puzzles which keeps the game interesting and non-repetitive
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of platform puzzlers, this is pretty tame and easy. The puzzles are pretty much spoon fed to the player and don't require much thought.The story is super depressing, filled with dispair and hopelessness. You have to go into this with a positive attitude to make it through. The dialog is super woke and uses genderless pronouns.I finished in 5 hours, and this just wasn't worth the price. This is a $0.99 app store sale kind of game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Cute art-style with great animation, but the game is lacking as a puzzle game - I wish the puzzles were much harder (they are really easy, on the verge of not requiring thinking at all), especially as not all of them are required to progress - if the game is catered to more casual audiences it would be nice to have at least some challenging levels for more puzzle-focused players. There is also a lot of walking and backtracking between the puzzles, so I really would describe this game as a "casual adventure game" rather than a "puzzle game" since puzzles are so easy and are only a minor part of the time you spend in a game. Even entirely optional (not even needed for achievements) journal entries are easy to find and are locked behind trivial "gates" to get them.So, do I recommend this game? I'd give it a mixed rating if I could - if you are looking for a puzzle game - it's a really simple, casual and unsatisfying one. But as an adventure to sink few hours into and relax, it gets the job done. That's why I decided to give it a "thumbs up", but you must be aware what you are looking for. I was a little disappointed, but I still enjoyed my time with it.Runs great on Steam Deck too (my playtime is higher than 1.8h, but I played it entirely on SD and some of it did not register).
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: eh... it's kind of ok.... sorta.. but not really. The narrator is annoying as hell. (Thank f### you can disable it). The environments look decent but also pretty plain and uninteresting at the same time. Even tho it's a pretty short game. My time with it felt more forced then intrigued and enjoyable enough to finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: this is my first time playing this type of puzzle game. i never playing this on ps5 so i played it on my laptop. it was really worth to buy and play, i really liked that we can exploring and interacting every stuffs in there. the plot twist in this game was really mind blowingbut sadly, there's some ember statues that i couldn't solve it yet
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: 5:02:34 (100% achievement, finished the game) No. No. No. is a puzzle game about a creature called Ember, which is trying to save their kind that has turned to stone. The journey isn't that simple, though. You need to solve puzzles on your way to reach them.- 25 puzzles with varied mechanics- Collectibles have markers for easier tracking- Unable to skip animations- It's hard to distinguish between climbing stairs and paddling a boat since they use the same buttonIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650Most areas look simple, but the presentation makes it seem that they don't. Decorations, crumbled walls, and fogs help to obscure the areas, hiding hidden paths to collectibles and making the area look more gorgeous and vast. It's still easy to traverse the area and find your way through, and the marking that shows when you are near interactable objects does a good job to distinguish it from the decorations.The story was told like in a children's book, albeit with more difficult words. It tries to tell the story in poems and short words, and sometimes it can be hard to understand what was being told because of it. The voice actor does a good job with it, though. The voice sounds soothing and mysterious at the same time, while still trying to be distinct whenever another person is talking. has two kinds of puzzles. One is where you need to explore your surroundings to unlock new areas and another where you have to go to a closed space and solve puzzles to save another Ember. The first one is easier since it serves as a warm-up before you get to the juicy part, and although some of the second kind of puzzles will require you to exercise your brain, they are still easy to solve.The exploration puzzles require you to remember your surroundings. The most that they can do is to trick your eyes, as they have hidden areas and secrets that conceal collectibles. You need to remember where you need to use objects, the puzzle mechanics, as well as all abilities that you have to uncover everything. Although it might look simple, there were times when I didn't realize that I can do things and stumped for a while. Puzzles are unique. All puzzles might look similar at first glance, but they usually have a different focus. One might require you to push a box to a certain spot, another might want you to fiddle with switches. The variance help to make the puzzles not boring, and although some are reused, they are usually positioned far from each other. Some of them also can be brute-forced, and others might require you to think outside the box.The in-game clock says that I finished the game at 5:02:34. I did get everything, from saving all Embers and obtaining all of the collectibles. As I said before, the game is easy to beat. There might be puzzles that can leave you stumped, but it's mostly because you need to rethink your approach and try other things. Brute forcing might be helpful in some puzzles, but not without having an idea of what to do beforehand. As for collectibles, they are still easy to track as long as you know what to do. The game also has a counter for the collectible in each area for easier tracking. Although the game looks beautiful, it can be boring to see the same animations over and over again, especially when you are doing a puzzle that is required to save the Embers. The game will usually show the same animation after you finished the puzzle with a minor change based on the one that you saved. Despite that, it doesn't allow you to skip the animations.There is also no restart button, so you need to revisit the area and have to see the opening animation again every time you reenter the puzzle room. Lastly, the game tends to fail to distinguish between paddling a boat and climbing a ladder. Both actions use the same button and you will encounter them in a lot of areas. is a puzzle game for casual players. The short playtime and easy difficulty are perfect for its target audience, and the cute-looking creature help to increase its charm. The atmosphere that the game has also helped you to relax, and with how small each area is, it's easy to finish everything without missing out. It's a cute, charming little game that will leave your heart melting with its presentations.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended. I'm not much of a puzzle game fan, but I loved the entire aesthetic of this when I saw the trailer. Very happy I tried it. This is a relaxing game and just what I needed. The story is mysterious and has a wonderful message. The puzzles are on the easy side overall but the sense of accomplishment is still rewarding. I only got stuck on the "frog and turtle" and "Iron Claw" sections but those were quite different than the rest of the mainline puzzles. No biggie. Glad I stuck with it and finished it. Well worth my time and money!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This has been my favorite game since I bought it. I played through all of it twice on switch and once on PC when it released on Steam. This is an absolute gem and you won´t find another experience like it. You explore bigger, relatively open areas to find forlorn embers that you can help by solving puzzles. These puzzles have a wide range in difficulty but if you have trouble getting past one you can progress anyway. The Art direction, music and story are beautiful. I really can´t name a bad thing about this game except for some janky collision in some corners that might softlock you, but you generally don´t lose any time or progress to it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely puzzle game about helping others to find hope and move on.Pros:- The puzzles are more varied than I first expected; I was worried they were going to get very samey but there are different mechanisms, even if the overall goal is roughly the same in each puzzle. Outside of the main puzzles, sometimes you have to move things around or deal with obstacles to navigate the environment. I liked this as it kept things interesting, I didn't feel like I was just running around between puzzles.- I liked the overall level of difficulty. Most of the puzzles were easy but still satisfying, and a few were just enough to feel a bit challenging without getting frustrating.- The narration is soft and not intrusive. I know it's only a small detail but it kept me playing the game when I was unsure about it at first. Sometimes voice acting can throw off the atmosphere if it doesn't fit but this was perfect.- The overall game design and atmosphere. It's wistful and sad in places, but that's balanced out with some fun characters that you can meet and help (and vice versa) along the way.Cons:- At some points it wasn't clear where I needed to go, or routes weren't very obvious. But this is quite a minor point since you can't really get stuck or lost, and it feels like one of those games that just wants you to explore rather than following a map, anyway,- Had a few instances where the sound glitched for a second, but again this is very minor, didn't affect the gameplay at all (and I'm being picky in search of cons because I really don't have many).
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best game I've ever played. I wish I could Eternal Sunshine myself so I could experience it again. The visuals are fantastic, but what really got me is the story - the forlorn, and their journeys, and Ember's part in it all. The puzzles were also fantastic, and really engaging and just enough of a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a great game! The atmosphere, soundtrack, puzzles, the minimal but absolutely joyous dialogue. I really had a lot of fun playing it. Congrats to all of the team for making this gem of a game!As a side note for Hello Games, please don't make your next games store-exclusives. I almost hadn't played The Last Campfire because I had no idea that this game had been released for a while, but only on Epic Store. Don't alienate players from experiencing your games, because you guys are really talented!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Was a fairly casual game where no real harm can come to your character and no decisions are permanent and all puzzles can be solved with persistence (though a couple are pretty tricky) and even then not all are required and there are even a couple of hints to find the last missing ones.The tone was pretty mopy throughout, but overall I guess its positive message of reigniting the spark of motivation in all the ember's friends.  Still by the end the story even managed to gain a little emotional impact though the pacing with the puzzles and the lack of clear plot got in the way of this a little bit.Worthwhile, as I clocked about 8 hours with finding pretty much everything and completing all puzzles and I got it for about $5
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a cozy puzzle game with a cute art style, this game is for you! The music and environment are so peaceful and the puzzles are challenging but not too hard. There are some funny bits in there that made me laugh. The narrator's voice is very soothing to listen to.I got this game on sale so it was definitely worth it but I did finish it within 6 hours so it's not the longest game out there and while I would have liked there to be more gameplay the timing of everything did feel right.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice and relaxing adventure puzzle that is about 10 hours long. The puzzles are not too challenging; sometimes their solution feels like a conjuring tricks. If you are looking for difficult puzzles, look somewhere else. The story is good and touching, but not sad. My interpretation (of such stories) goes as follows, if you perish you would be happy to undergo a last journey. If you play this game, then you can experience such a journey. The english audio is very good. I enjoyed this journy and had my light bulb moment, but you might not have it!The game works fine with the Xbox-controller.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Especially with the current sale (80%) if you dont get this game, I am concerned. Even if I had paid full price for this masterpiece, it would have been worth it. Such a cute story of helping spirits. It isnt overly difficult, but definitely isnt super easy either. A great game for a cozy night with some tea. Beautiful artstyle, and well voice acted!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: It is very hard to satisfy me, as active programmer with unique gaming desires (stealth, puzzle, hidden objects - less or zero action, freedom and self projection), so for me this was one of few games I cannot find anything negative. Liberty in environment interaction and controller support was one of biggest surprises I enhanced after very long time. Well designed levels with tile grid for easy collisions and zero problems from efective and fast driving. Only a few minor bugs gained from lower computer performance, I believe. I've got absolutely fascinated how clever and minimalistcally aids, hints, directions, acive points and hotspots was derived and indicated. So as software developer myself I am hardly finding anything I could deliver or design any better. And for music, sounds and graphics - that is just breathtaking. Yeap, that is very negative to me.
