_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty, charming, and cozy despite its heavier themes. Focuses more on mood and metaphor than story which means you kinda need to be in the right mental space to fully appreciate the message. The frequent narration can be excessive and the diary entries rather vague, but the gentle hopefulness is part of its charm. I found the puzzles to be well-designed and enjoyable; not too challenging, but some are tricky.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I love a game with a "vague message" that can be interpreted a number of different ways. The sadness and hope this game combined was beautiful. The art is so so charming and the puzzles were the perfect level of complicated. The only downside for my was the narrator but i just turned their voice off and read the words instead. I really enjoyed this game and will likely play it again in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: i played adventure not explore. mechanics are simple enough that i don't get frustrated. puzzles are simple but challenging enough that i don't get bored or frustrated. it's fairly guided, but i never minded and it helped me not worry about accidentally getting stuck or missed something. plot-wise it was all kinda predictable of an arc, but there were little surprises in the design of it all that was amazing and it was a very satisfying arc and ending. everything was intuitive, the options were cute, adn the art/creatures were delightful. i also appreciated the they/them/it/its. it's cozy and safe and so hopeful. it's rare that video game is so good that i've played through so much so quickly (15 hours in 2 days). i just really love it a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game had such a wonderful and touching story, as well as adorable character design. My favorite thing was watching Ember pick up things that were comically large relative to their size. Big frog statues yes yes.  The puzzles were challenging, but rewarding once you figured them out. (Hint: there are walkthrough videos and articles if you need them... like I did).
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty nice puzzle game. None that will remove hair from your head, but still worth the challenge.It has too much of sentimentalism, which I sincerely dislike, not my cup of tea. The Ember is too fearful, fragile, everything is depressing (even being a colorful game). The girl who narrates the history has sweet voice, but again, making it more sensitive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This story is bittersweet and very important. I went to read on the symbolism of the game and learned that it was all refering to Life and Death. During my playthrough I was absolutely convinced it was about mental health. And while the original meaning makes a bit more sense when I think about it, my meaning is also relevant. The characters are cute, the puzzles are just the right amount of challenging, never too easy, never too hard. The voice acting is absolutely amazing.I am so happy to have picked it up, I didn't even intend to play it and almost played it in one sitting. I literally didn't sleep. Anyway, it's worth the full price in my opinion so don't hesitate. (I also might have shed a tear or two when the credits rolled)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Narration is topnotch and the puzzles are somewhat in the middle of difficulty. The moment I spent minutes in the solving one of the puzzles then I realized that it will take a long time playing this which bumps up the value of this game even higher.One improvement I can see with the game is the consistency of the FPS. There are times which my game lags more so that I expected.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a bittersweet, short, but oh so powerful and moving game. The narrative is beautiful and compassionate and moving, dealing with a range of topics in mental health in such a beautiful and metaphorical way that is immaculately handled. Part of my soul was healed playing this game, a part I didn't know was broken. To top it all off, the soundtrack is amazing, the characters are adorable and well designed, and the scenery too is incredible. The puzzles were challenging enough but not too hard or unforgiving, and the game guides you gently and rewards exploring. Overall it's an immaculate game and I'm glad to have finally played it 🔥✨
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best narrative game I have played. Feels like a child's story book coming to life. The messages really touches you if you get it.Heartwarming and lived up to it's name, aroused campfire within me. The "last campfire" catered to the individual players!Gameplay was slightly straightforward and tedious, but the core I believe is the narrative and it did a wonderful job getting that across!Conclusion: 9.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, one of the most beautiful, charming and emotionally charged games I have ever played. The narration throughout sets the perfect scene for the game, and it is rewarding to keep seeing all of your little saved Forlorn's around the campfire as you progressively save each one. Well worth purchasing, I picked it up in the sale to try out on my Steam Deck without having a proper look at the gameplay, but I would've been happy to pay full price for it now I've played it through.Well done devs, great game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous little game about courage, hope and never giving up. Beautiful music, art style and graphics. Absolutely loved playing this through. Puzzles were fun, only found a few of them difficult but I appreciate that they weren't all hard - made the gameplay a lot nicer for me personally. I loved the narrator as well, it was so calming and I definitely felt a lot of emotion through their voice.Such a wholesome little journey and a magnificent game overall!! well done devs ♡︎
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is an adventure puzzle game.This is an astonishingly good game in all aspects and I loved playing through it. The story is immaculate and interesting, the characters and absolutely lovely (the main ones of course) and the music is mostly atmospheric, but it fits the game to perfection. The puzzles varies from easy to average in difficulty, it is definitely not a challenging game and it would be a good introduction to people who want to get into adventure puzzle video games. The goal of the game is to save everyone who are ready to be helped, making them happy again by reigniting their flames using your puzzle prowesses.The graphics are wholesome and cute as well and the game passes a strong message if you do read and listen to everything. I have a few minor gripes with the game but they're honestly not important at all, namely: the controls could be better, very few dialogues are repeated (like the snake's) and it's a little short. The last element it perhaps for the best however, as I did not ever get bored of the game at any point!Overall, fantastic game and deserving of it's rating. I would still get it on sale considering the price for 5 hours of content, but I will admit that the price is justified for such a polished and well-rounded game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to dislike this, but I just don't think it's very good. I would say it's best described as a children's game, but not in the good way that makes it a fun experience for people of all ages, but rather something both too dull and simplistic as well as overly try-hard artsy too offer much of value. The puzzles are rudimentary without providing any sense of progression, the narration is the annoying kind of poetic that's verbose without saying anything at all and the story is likewise pure fluff. Ultimately I didn't enjoy it and don't think it was time well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: "There is a place where the lost embers go. As their light begins to fade..."This game is super cute and very relaxing to play. There are a lot of puzzles that can stump you for a moment, but nothing too complicated. I have backtracked a couple of times, 'cause I just didn't want to miss anything and the game encourages you to do that, too. At a certain point I was afraid I had missed a lot of stuff, but the game brought me back to the same place a couple of times, so the chance of you missing something is very, very small. I definitely recommend this game if you like puzzle-, relaxed and story driven games. The message behind it is truly beautiful <3 I really enjoyed playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a very sweet little puzzler. the controls are very satisfying even on mouse and keyboard (although the game is definitely designed with controllers in mind), and everything feels very intuitive. the story is simple but meaningful, and the message it communicates is an important one. the narration gets a bit heavy-handed at some points, but it's not too bad; it's about as subtle with its message as a Pixar movie, which makes sense given that it feels designed for a younger audience as it is.the biggest thing i like about this game is the level design. i personally have a very poor sense of direction and tend to play games with one eye on the minimap, otherwise i'll get hopelessly turned around. The Last Campfire has no minimap and a lot of branching paths, but the game uses little environmental puzzles as breadcrumbs to guide you through one step at a time. you never find yourself wandering in circles trying to find the next piece of the story, but because the environments are so complex, you still get a sense that you're "finding your way" - unlike a game like Skyrim, where levels are basically a long corridor from point A to point B. the puzzles themselves were, to my brain, lightly challenging but ultimately straightforward, perfect if you want a "hmmm... OH, okay, got it" experience. hardcore puzzle fans will not find anything to really sink their teeth into, but for me personally, it was exactly the relaxing but stimulating experience i was looking for.there ARE a few graphical glitches near the end of the game, and i ran into a few bugs that stopped me from making progress due to being either stuck in a wall or mysteriously walking on the ceiling, but honestly, i think they were largely my own fault for controlling the game like a maniac. quitting to the main menu and loading back in fixes it, too, so it's really not a big deal at all.overall, i really enjoyed this game and i can definitely see myself coming back to it again. highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A heartwarming and really adorable game with a heartmelting storyline. I have loved and adored every single second of this game, from the puzzles to the exploration to the dialogues between the Forlorns and our dear Ember. It is my humble request for all who read this to try it for once. The pacing is just right, and it will soften your soul to the depths.Highly Recommended. :thumbsup:
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Lost Campfire has charm and character. The Puzzles are a good mix, some are trivial but some are very satisfying to complete. Sadly there is no really challenging puzzle.The game has a polished feel to it. while there where some minor glitches nothing really bothering.It is short and does not drag on needlessly.The story starting to be depressing near the end.In short:It is a nice experience with chill puzzles and a bit heavier story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are challenging without getting frustrating and the character designs are super cute! Love the way Ember scampers about with floppy ears. The story line is touching and heart warming as you are retrieving souls and returning them.  Highly entertaining for anyone that enjoys a creepy cute game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a puzzle game characterized by a melancholic and somber atmosphere. The puzzles to solve are quite varied and challenging, making the game and its resolutions engaging at every stage. There are also some fun and lighthearted moments. The dialogues are rather cold and rigid, but they help immerse the player in a unique atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A cute and mellow point and click puzzle game. The game is not very big, it took me under 9 hours to complete fully. The story is simple but effective, little Ember makes their way through a "limbo" of sorts helping lost souls along the way. The art and background scenery are beautiful, and hidden collectibles encourage the player to explore every nook and cranny. There are subtitles for the narration in multiples languages, and all characters are gender-neutral. There is an "explore" option which says it removes most puzzles, I haven't tried it yet, so I don't know if it's as engaging. Some turning mechanics for wheels were a little janky, the Lanthorn (similar to the magnet in BotW) was also a bit unreliable, sometimes it was difficult to move objects, other times they quickly move too far. But nothing "game breaking".Overall enjoyable little game, good for sitting back and relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are very easy and never really pick up difficulty even in the challenge levels. this is a shame since they introduce a bunch of interesting mechanics but never let them interact in challenging ways. The biggest problem here is that Time and Time again I would see the solution to the puzzle and then have to sit trough 5 min of animation and walking to actually execute this solution.Most dialogue reads like a children's book. However, it has a suprisingly dark theme. It seems like they asked a LLM (large language model) to generate some inspirational quotes to motivate depressed people. Maybe there was some deeper meaning to it, that would certainly make finding it the most challenging puzzle this game offered.the graphics are file, although I did not find them breathtaking by any stretch. I feel like they fit a puzzle game really well, everything is nice and visible yet there was effort put in to make every bit look different (wear on materials, clutter, etc.).However if you would like to play a puzzle game to gasp at it graphics play  "The Witness", "The Vanishing of Ethan Carter" ,"Ether One", "Fez" or "Obduction" (I could go on) Instead.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a very charming and stylized puzzle game, that I enjoyed from start to finish. Most of the puzzles were interesting and fun, but I wouldn't call the game difficult. On the surface - a relaxing and whimsical experience, but as you go further, the game introduces the topics of grief, hopelessness, finding the strength to move on and find it in you to help others do the same. The narration was very good, too, and really added to the charm of the game! If you want a game to enjoy with a friend or family member, who aren't too into games, or if you just want to play it for yourself, I definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Nice puzzle game that looks great and cute. Not to difficult but you could get stuck at a puzzle. To bad i finished the game in 7 hours. Wish it took me longer but totaly worth the money. If they would make a new one i would def buy it. Play every campfire 100% before moving on to the next one to get the most out of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: is a lovely puzzle adventure that brings an inspiring story about hope. This story is lived by Ember, who in a very kind and compassionate way tries to help other characters in the game, called forlorns, to have again hope and a purpose to keep moving on.In addition to the heartwarming story, the game also features very cleverly designed and creative puzzles that will always bring a pleasant satisfaction for solving them. The art is wonderfully inviting, and the soundtrack is a treat to the ears. It has no missable achievements, and the collectibles, while not necessary for completion, add a lot to the game's narrative.I finished the game in about 8 hours and I'm glad I explored every bit of it, because it was definitely worth it. It holds a special place in my heart now, and I invite you to also experience it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Finally game,where you dont kill anybody and dont hurt anybody.Just use your brain and enjoy great journey in this sad world.Game seems for kids (similar as Cuphead),but even old players can fight with difficulty.As you move in story solving the puzzles.And not all of the puzzles are easy.Some take few minutes,some can push your brain for hour to find solution.But mostly its just about how to move something somewhere :) Great game,when i will have more time i am going to finish it :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo for 2 hours and decided to just go ahead and buy the game. Quite nice when games port over your demo save. I like that the puzzles scale but are lightly challenging. The storytelling makes this a light but emotionally deep game. Easy controls, a few minor visual bugs but nothing game breaking.Edit: finished it, still stand by my same review.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome cozy puzzle game. Even if you look for achievements you can just play this game and didn't worry to much. Lovely music, game design and concept.Enjoyed every second on the Steam Deck, No technical issues or something else...If you look for games with Action don't buy, If you are ok with cozy games this is a must Play!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Some small facts first:This game has very positive reviews.It usually takes less than six hours to complete.Less than a third of the players have finished it.So how is that? How is it that a game, that bores two thirds of the players out of their skull an hour into a game, gets so good reviews? Here are my two cents:What do you do if you have story that isn't good enough for a book?Make it a game!What if the game isn't good enough?Make it artsy!How do you hide that this really is drivel?Have it narrated by an adult speaking like a child with oddly consistent flaws in her grammar to give it a childish appearance. This way nobody dare offer any critique because they are afraid of revealing that they are "not getting it". And besides it is art, isn't it? You are not supposed to get art, you are supposed to feel or something.There was this scientist once that commented on the supposed autopsy video of an alien, and he said "I can't say that that isn't an alien. I do not know how they look like. However, I do know what rubber looks like." So to paraphrase: "I can't say this isn't art, as one cannot really describe what good art is. However, I do know what childish drivel is."For more info see the emperor's new clothes
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little characters with a dozen puzzle mechanics built in. The story is great with quite some room for self-reflection and open interpretation. Although i felt most of the puzzles may be a tad too easy with just one or two exceptions of difficult ones sprinkled in. The game time is rather short so maybe consider getting it on a sale?
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a puzzle game with a  story of the human condition; about feeling lost and being kind. The puzzles are mostly straightforward though there were a few that tripped me up.  It's a sweet game to play when feeling down. It helped me focus on a task and reminded me I'm just feeling the feels like most everyone else.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I intended to only play this game for a few hours today and then ended up finishing the entire thing in one go because I didn't want to stop playing. The voice acting sets the mood extremely well and the atmosphere of the game is incredibly cosy in a very specific way. All of the scenery is so pretty too, as is the sound design. The puzzles were tricky at times but not too difficult which really lends itself to the style of this game, not obstructing the story with frustration and allowing everything to flow nicely. The story is touching and I adore the open world adventure feel of the gameplay. Everything is so beautifully crafted; I'm in love!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok, but middling reviews aren't a thing, of course. Further, I'd hate to give it a negative review with how cute it is, so note the following:1. I don't see it being worth full price, though it's on sale a lot.2. The game constantly slaps you in the face with its overt theme.3. It will likely be more touching if you've experience with social anxiety, depression, etc.4. It'll likely be  touching if you're a person of faith who derives motivation/hope, personal value, perseverance, peace, etc. from other sources.+Colorful and cute, family-friendly+Nice music+UI shows how many collectibles remain on each screen+Two difficulties: Explore mode is apparently all storytelling+Autosaves every screen transition, collected item, or completed puzzle+Frequently on heavy discount~Overall, it's not very difficult~No combat, death or forced stealth - just story and puzzles~Roughly 4-7 hours of play~Camera is frequently uncooperative~I'm not sure if my yawning at times was from relaxation or boredom~The UK narrator will annoy some people-There is no subtlety or relief from the game's theme-The collectibles are a waste of time, providing little insight or interest-No fast travel to previous areas?-Game doesn't explain how to save-Game doesn't explain difference between Normal and Explore modePlayed on:Win11, i7-14700K, RTX4060 Ti 8GB, 32GB DDR5-6000 @ 1920x1080Using PowerA Enhanced Wired Controller for Xbox Series X|SNormal difficulty
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Visually and musically beautiful game. Fairly easy puzzles for someone who plays hardcore puzzle games, but not a total snooze-fest either. Some thought-provoking messages in it. Game autosaves. Does not require fast reflexes anywhere.I played with controller - I would think keyboard and mouse would be a bit annoying due to needing to moving at angles that don't fall on exactly on or between the 4 cardinal directions. I got 100% achievements just by completing every puzzle to get to the end - it seemed there were some options to skip some puzzles - not sure..The only negative is there are a lot of "dialogs" - I use quotation because they are all spoken by same narrator who has a pleasant,  perhaps-Icelandic (they sound like Bjork), accent. You can can skip each snippet of dialog by clicking, but you have to keep clicking until all snippets are exhausted. Truth is, you can probably get by by simply not starting a conversation with anyone, although there are a few that are unavoidable to advance to the next section.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This was a super relaxing but nice game. The game has even a deeper meaning in the story and i like that kind of stuff. The puzzles are not really hard to clear but give you a nice challeges now and then. The animation of the game is cute and very beautiful. For a few euro's a winner that i recommend you to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful little game, got it one sale (though I agree that it's original price is a tad high, I'd say it's worth around $5)Emotional well designed, never felt unfair and I only had to look up 2 puzzle solution and instantly felt a little silly in not getting it right away.Haven't looked at the exploration mode so that might offer more content as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: First review I ever give because this game needs more praise Spend 7 euro's on this game being bored while having covid. _childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Art style is so pretty! _childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so relaxing and delightful. I got it as a gift from my boyfriend. Puzzles are well designed and can be challenging but doable. The art was so unique and the little characters were adorable. The ending made me cry, and most of the journey I began to think philosophically about life. Absolutely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game was recommended to me and I'm very glad I listened. It's a narrative puzzle game about values such as hope and friendship (will hit you in the feels). The puzzles are just the right difficulty and aren't repetitive. If you get stuck on a puzzle (happened once to me), there are great guides to help you out.To finish the game you can expect 4-5 hours.Worth the money, can only recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a beautiful game+Graphics(I really like how it looks and especially the chosen style)+Gameplay(easy to learn)+Atmosphere+Puzzle+Good sound and music+Story(simple but good)The Last Campfire is a simple and relaxing game that offers a pleasant experience and puzzles to solve and a decent story.10/10 Must Play! I highly recommend buying it at full price or at a discount, it's worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game to those who like to explore the surroundings, solving puzzles from time to time and have some philosophical thoughts about life."We cannot see what lies ahead of us on the path, yet, we keep on sailing, but at one point, the fire of hope within ourselves extinguishes, because we just cannot seem to continue on our journey, it feels like there is no end. But even if we stop at one point, hope will still slip away gradually, reliving the same loop, who wouldn't go insane? We hope, we try, we fail, what comes next? Why bother having hope?""The journey was never easy, no one will be able to sail the path effortlessly, that is why so many has turned forlorn. But that is not the end, by spreading hope and light, helping each other to reignite that fire within them, we all can continue sailing together. We fail time to time, and that is okay, what is important is that we have hope, and we keep on trying, and I believe, we will succeed one day. But if we were to lose hope, and never bother trying, we will not have any chances of succeeding."You play as Ember, who got lose on their way to the main campfire (I suppose). Instead, Ember will have to find another way, to head back to the main campfire. Along Ember's journey, Ember found many who turned forlorn, those that had lost hope of themselves, this may be due to high expectation on themselves but fail to achieve it, or got betrayed by their friend, or left behind by their friends and many more. Ember helped to find back their inner fire (hope) by solving puzzles. To me, the puzzles, range from easy to feeling-a-sense-of-achievement-if-you-manage-to-solve-it-yourself. After a series of puzzles and exploration and helping new friends, Ember will be able to advance to the next place, and in the end, reaching the main campfire, along with those that Ember had helped on the way.Took me 7.5 hours to help all the 21 forlorns + 3 friends. Tried to explore as many places as I can at the same time, but still I only manage to collect 35/42 forgotten journal entries. I am able to get all the achievements in my first play through, so I will not go for a second time. Seems like the journal entries are a bonus, it will not contribute to the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. It's super cute, the music is peaceful, and the narrator's voice is *chef's kiss*.The story is nice and the puzzles are enjoyable too. Environment is really beautiful and I really love all of the characters. Played with both M&K and Controller. Definitely preferred it with the controller. My only issue with this game is that when I Alt-Tab/ Switch tabs, the game crashes instantly. A bit inconvenient. But that's my only issue.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting graphics and sound effects. The narration is excellent. Could not imagine a better voice actor to do this work.  The story makes you want to keep playing to help the NPCs. The puzzles are probably easy for some but I find them a bit challenging. Even the ones that frustrate me do not feel invincible, just complicated to solve.I would recommend playing with a controller.  I am usually a M/KB person, but the controls feel a little less reliable.  Some of the puzzles require specific placement and it can be frustrating if the controls are getting in your way.Definitely can recommend this as a novice puzzle person.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it on sale, 100% in 4 hours, i was hoping for a bit more but that's alright.However i have no complaints about the game itself, puzzles have a nice learning curve {though a bit too easy}, i did brute force one snake puzzle because i'm stupid.overall 9/10, had a good time, was sad, helped everyone i could and got cozy by the fire.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Baby's first Dark Souls. Not really, this game is ridiculously easy, there is no challenge to be found here. I only had to look up one puzzle, and even that was just because I was severely sleep deprived at the time. All of this is very funny in contrast to the fact that the lore and premise of this game is just Dark Souls but kid-friendly. It's nice though. It's a cozy, chill, turn your brain off kind of game. The art direction is pretty, character models are great and the controls feel good. The music is great and reminiscent of No Man's Sky at times. Which makes sense since it's from the same developer. Yeah, I was surprised too. Also, for the achievement hunters, this is an easy 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: I loved the game. It offered a lot of puzzles and puzzles to get to puzzles. Most where very easy. The entire game is narrated even some of your actions are narrated. Achievements are very easy to get.Story: It is short and sweet. Won't spoil it. It isn't memorable for me but it isn't a bad story by any means. It does deal with death so don't come looking for cheer. Graphics:The graphics can be at times (very seldom) obviously glitching out. Meaning flickering (mostly on floor pieces). Otherwise it was well done and very beautiful.Atmosphere: Very calm. Quite charming. No rush to complete things. Music: Very calm music even on full volume I didn't notice it more than half the time. So it wasn't grating on my nerves at all. A undertone of sadness to entire game. Repeated music wasn't a problem. The only time I noticed it was one section. It was music that played above the normal calm sadness music of the game. Sound: Sound is very good. Nothing that didn't fit the atmosphere of calm they where going for. Combat: No combat in the game whatsoever. Just plain puzzle solving.Controls:Typical controls for moving and picking things up. Though I will note you cannot change them (controller and mouse and keyboard).Achievement Hunters: This is a easy game to complete. Literally all the time taken is just to complete puzzles. No hidden achievements that you could miss. It takes less than 9 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a short exploration and puzzle game. Beautiful art, great music. Puzzles are not hard, though some require more thinking and may be tricky.And that would be an excellent game if not for the setup. As a character you are helping others, each puzzle sets the others onto a better path. But with so many problems [of other characters] mentioned and due to how atmospheric this game gets combined with good quality narration, it made me sad during the playthrough and completing the game left an overall depressing feeling even though the whole message of the game is completely opposite - to not lose hope when you fail, to keep on trying and striving.As a result, I cannot recommend this otherwise splendid game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Witnessing the games 96% positive rating, I've bought the game at an 80% discount. After playing the game and fully completing it, I wouldn't recommend it.Considering that the "Puzzle" tag is the first tag for this game, I expected the game to have more puzzles and the puzzles to be more complex. The puzzles are very easy and didn't really offer the challenge I'd hoped for.Playing the game using keyboard and mouse adds an extra challenge, which makes it very hard to turn objects, such as valves and keys, so make sure to use a controller for these parts. Moreover, the game tells you that you have the ability to dash, explains that a key has to be pressed, which is the wrong key (it’s ‘x’, apparently). After having learned which key to press and how to use this ability, I’ve never felt the need to use it. Why is this part of the game?Looking at my Steam library, I noticed that I’ve never really been a player of storyline or dialog games, so take that into account for the next part. The game looks very good, but the dialog is honestly depressing. Everyone is depressed and is your job to give them hope again. After some time, I just zoned out of the dialog and focused on the puzzles and environment.I didn’t mind the game being short, but for some people this might be a turn off. I completely finished the game in about 4 hours (I just clicked through the dialog after some point), then spend some extra time doing the puzzles so steam would give me the last trading card. So, the puzzles are (too) easy and the story is depressing. Wouldn't recommend it...
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game does many things well, but it absolutely perfectly nails the pacing. From the minute I started playing, I couldn't stop. I played through the entire thing in 2 days. It never gets tedious, because there's something new to discover around every corner, and for the most part, the puzzles aren't too difficult, so they don't get frustrating. I admit I did get stuck and looked up the solution to a puzzle 3 times, but that's just because I sometimes miss really obvious things. Most people won't have any trouble with them, especially if they're fans of puzzle games in general.The world and character design are both beautiful and charming. You can tell the developers actually cared about what they were making and poured a lot of love into it. This game is about as far as you can get from a soulless big studio money-grab.I will say however, that this game may not be for everyone. The mood overall is very somber. There is no combat. Instead the conflict is all provided by the emotions of the characters and the player's drive to help them. If you are someone that struggles with negative thoughts and feelings, this game may help you feel seen. If your loved ones play this game, maybe it will help them understand a little better. But, I'm not a mental health professional, so take that for what it's worth.All I know is that I very much enjoyed this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I was playing this while going through a number of puzzle games and it ended up being the easiest of them. I think the game is intended more so for kids due to the gentle challenge and colourful aesthetic. Reminds me of games from the early 2010's on the xbox 360.If you're looking for a light challenge or just a gentle story puzzler then you could have fun with it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it on sale and don't regret it. Really atmospheric and deep game, which is perfectly reflectable on your own life. Anxiety, failure, finding the will to move forward, all of these points carry on throughout the story.  While helping those in need never forget to care about yourself and accept not everyone wants to be saved.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: this was so delightful!! got it on sale because i thought the style was cute and it ended up being so enjoyable and lovely to play through. the puzzle design was neat, nothing super difficult but it managed to change things up enough that it still felt fresh and enjoyable as the final hours of the game approached. character and world design were adorable, not really much to complain about here (would like a borderless fullscreen mode though)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Cute graphics, a bit of exploring, bittersweet short story, puzzles that need some thinking but not extremely hard. A great game to pass time with and enjoy. _childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Seeing the overwhelming positive reviews for this game, I had high expectations. Unfortunately I can't recommend this game. The visual were very nice and the music was calming. But the puzzles and game play were just too boring. The puzzles were either extremely easy or, at times, very annoying. Maybe pick it up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle gamethat makes you think of the emotionally deeper aspects of life.The objective is to free the souls of the lost and aching, but from time to time, you'll encounter some souls that are content only to suffer and wither away.Very reminiscent of real life,but in a colorful, innocent waythat reminds me ofwhen I was a kid. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely marvelous little game. Yes it's one of the shorter ones but I'll take a well made immersive experience over longer repetitive grind any time. Beautiful dynamic environments, immersive BGM and sound effects, simple but fun puzzles, everything is narrated with a soothing voice. It just pulls you in.. Just the type of game you want pick up after work.Technical notes:Runs flawlessly on the SteamDeck. Getting 100% is practically guaranteed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a great mix of calm puzzles and beautiful story. The sound design was immersive and captivating. It's a great game to slow down and take in. One downside is that everything is narrated so it can feel a bit fatiguing on the ears. Also, though new gimmicks are introduced as the game progresses to keep the puzzles interesting, the difficulty level remained fairly constant throughout. There was also a small plot hole at the end of the story but it's not huge if you gracefully overlook it. Overall, I'd give this a 9/10 and recommend all atmospheric puzzle fans to give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere, nice story that hit some good emotional notes at times. Puzzles were nice if slightly simple if you're used to puzzle games. There was really only one I had trouble with and looking back, it was due to a small bug where a cube with wind extinguished a fire through a solid block that I thought blocked the effect.The game was a bit short, but didn't overstay its welcome.  Took maybe 4 hours to 100% (I think my total time was just over 5 hours but I tend to dillydally).I don't have a lot of time to play games anymore, but I'm glad I had a night to play through this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The game has suuuch a cute design and animation. I also really love the voice acting that was going on, although I would have enjoyed different voices. The story line seems very simple yet very interesting. I still haven't finished the game yet, but I'm very excited to see how it will all unfold. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: " is a beautiful game inside and out.  Its world is a joy to explore, its simple mechanisms feed into elegant puzzles effortlessly, and its narrative touched my heart in ways I never expected it to.  While the puzzles won’t burn your brain like some titles in the genre, I think that helps to keep focus on the story, ensuring that the emotional core of the game is never lost under the weight of frustration.  There’s truly something special here, and it’s certainly managed to light a fire in my soul like few games before it."Full review
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Very very cute little puzzle game that was simple and easy to perfect, the puzzles aren't too hard but they're still interesting enough to not get tedious. Definitely recommend!Also it probably took more like 8 hours rather than 18, I just left the game open a couple times by accident lol
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful tale about sorrow and hope. With soothing music and simple but nice graphic design. You meet lovely characters along your journey. I really enjoy playing this puzzle-platformer. I played through it in a long day. I can recommend this to everyone who needs a soothing and relaxing game to wind down after some stressful times. The controls are really easy and the puzzles are not that hard, lightly challenging you. Just enough to give you that little high of accomplishment every time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good little puzzle game with simple yet touching story. Not much to say about it so i'll probably keep this extremely short.Gameplay is very simple – you run around solving puzzles. You get few huge areas to explore and a bunch of collectibles to find. Each area has sub-areas with its own puzzles, characters or quests. The story is told without words.The main focus here is obviously puzzles which are mostly different and require different approach. But none of them are too hard so don't worry, you won't get frustrated, you'll have fun.On top of that you're presented with a very nice heartwarming story and melancholic atmosphere so you want to progress further to unveil the whole story and see how it ends.It's also a very chill and relaxing game, there's no pressure, you can just sit back, relax and enjoy.Graphics are very cute and the game in general looks wonderful. Performance obviously is great and it has ultrawide support.Sound design also is good and adds to the overall atmosphere.Get this on sale, it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I've finished this game and it is a peaceful and wonderful game, the puzzles creative and are mostly simple to solve and it isn't boring too. The story line is quite nice and stays on theme and the scenery is wonderful. The sounds and narration soft, many things to explore and see. 10/10 for me one of my favorite gameplays ever.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This was beautiful and fun. The puzzles are interesting without ever getting too frustrating. The story is in the background but is sweet and thought-provoking.A very nice thing: you can't, as far as I can tell, get yourself into an impossible position.Sometimes the areas to wander through got complicated enough that it took effort to keep track of where I'd been, but it never got impossible.I played through the story in around 7 hours (over a few days).
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a cute adventure game that explores themes of self-discovery in a big, scary world. The art style is lovely, and the puzzles are engaging. As you play, you reflect on your own life while guiding a little character through challenges. It’s a heartwarming experience that blends charm and meaningful storytelling. Overall, it’s a delightful game that encourages you to think about your own journey.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, short puzzler game that plays with themes of hope, friendship and purpose. Took about 5 hours to complete the game completely. Although its concise storyline, it is tremendously wholesome and adorable. I was fully immersed within the first few minutes, and I would have been for another 5 hours if it had permitted it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game was visually beautiful, lovely soundtrack, adorable and heart aching story, with fun puzzles to boot. If you want a relaxing game with all the whimsy from your favorite calm games this might be your cup of tea. While my time does say roughly 17 hours, you can beat this game in about 8. I actually walked away for a bit and forgot my computer was still on. I believe this game is worth the price, its a very well loved project that shows the effort that went into it. With my initial thoughts out of the way, here are the pro's and con's.PROS: - Amazingly soothing soundtrack- Beautiful and captivating aesthetics - Wonderful voice acting - Cohesive to follow - You feel connected to the main character- You can receive hints that don't just give it all away- The tasks don't seem redundant or medial CONS:- While this project was very well loved some of the graphics have issues with collision - You can't change control keys, and the run button is in an awkward place- If you "fail" certain puzzles you get restarted to the beginning of the puzzle including the title sequence. - The puzzles are almost too easy, taking a minute tops for most of them- While the voice acting is amazing from the one narrator, I do wish we had a variety of voices for all charactersAll in all, if you enjoy calm simple games to pass the time this is for you. However if you want more of a challenge, this might not be the best game to buy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game with some pretty existential themes like battling your inner demons and learning to let go and accepting things and remaining hopeful; allowing yourself to move on. I really liked how it showed that you cant save everyone, not everyone wants to be saved and some just need more time.The puzzles weren't super challenging overall except for a few but that's not necessarily a drawback, and allows for more to enjoy the story and journey.One thing that would be nice is more clarity on when and where the game saves.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I got this one on a sale for less than 5$.Worth the money for sure.I played it on the Steam Deck in just 3 sessions. I did not have any technical issues and I think it is brilliant game for this device.While the puzzles were challenging enough, I never got frustrated or stuck for long.The soundtrack and the voice over of the dialogues are nicely done. Animations and graphics are just adorable! You can feel the developers passion and love for this game.I highly recommend to add this one to your library, It is still on a sale for another week and a half, while I am writing this review.I will follow the developers, curious for their upcoming releases!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the easy pace of this game and it was a really relaxing experience. The voice narration was perfect and really added to the overall feel of the game. Ember was so cute! The puzzled were fun to complete and some were more challenging than others. I would log on for half an hour and found that 3 hours had gone past. Was a lovely way to spend a rainy afternoon...although it took me a few afternoons to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful journey ! It may be short but it was pleasant from start to end. Pretty glad I gave it a try especially since it speaks about subjects that deserve imo more attention nowadays such as depression and loneliness. But even if it's quite heavy subjects for some, the game still taking care to approach them with lightness and kindness. The game itself would probably feel too easy for some, but the puzzles are nice and smart enough to make the product memorable.Love these indie gems.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A lovingly made little puzzle game with enchanting music and graphics. The story sent me on a journey that I needed in this difficult time of the pandemic. The last time I felt this way was when I was playing Journy. I hope I can relive the experience in the future again. Thank you dear development team.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire ReviewA mesmerising and wholesome experience from start to finish. The Last Campfire is such a joy to play to the point that i tired to slow down, stop and smell the roses, so that the game would last as long as possible before coming to the end. The puzzles are fun and creative. Some challenging, some easy but can make even seasoned gamers scratch their heads. They make you try and experiment with simple, beginner friendly controls. The environment is just so captivating. You can just stand there and look at the colourful plants and creatures, listen to the beautifully composed music with gentle nature sounds and just get lost in it all.The story is surprisingly moving. I am sure many can relate to it and even learn from some interactions. I really love that the characters all look like plushies. I completed the entire game on Steam Deck. Especially if you see it on sale, i suggest you don’t think twice and go for it. A lovely and memorable journey awaits!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing and engaging story. My girlfriend and I played through this together and it was a lot of fun. If anyone else has a partner who has never picked up a game before, this is a great absolute beginner friendly experience, with the ability to switch between mouse and wasd it is really approachable. We both loved the art style and the puzzles were challenging but fun to solve and tied well into the story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I hate doing this, because there is so much I like about this game, but ultimately, The Last Campfire is a better storybook than it is video game. I can't say I was disappointed to have checked it out, as it is only 4-6 hours long (6 hrs if you complete everything, which I did), but I also can't say I can wholeheartedly recommend it.By far and away the biggest issue is the game's difficulty, or lack thereof. I usually don't knock a game for being easy; not every game has to be hard and I've certainly enjoyed games with nice, relaxing playthroughs. But this one might be the easiest full game I've ever beaten, and uh, I've played a -lot- of games. Technically this is a "puzzle game" but it's hard to call what's in here puzzles; my jar was agape at how simple some of the solutions were. The first hour of this game is one of the worst first impressions I've had with a  game, as the tutorial section drags on way too long for being such a simple game, but truth is the bigger issue is you feel like you're always in a tutorial. It gets slightly, and I mean slightly, more complicated as you go, so you get a bit more engaged, but in the end I don't think a single puzzle took more than 2 minutes to solve, with most solved in 30 seconds or less. I found myself audibly whispering "no way.." under my breath in disbelief every time I ran into yet another puzzle that I couldn't believe actually made it into an otherwise very polished game. I'd say maybe this game is meant for kids, but I know the games I was beating as a kid, and this would have been way too easy for me even then. Don't come in expecting any feeling of accomplishment here; the puzzles are simpler than I am even making sound.The game is gorgeous, reminding me a lot of Runic Games' 2017 release "Hob," which it borrows much of its style and premise from. That isn't a bad thing, as by far the most enjoyable thing about the game is exploring its overworld and seeing all there is to see. The entire game is narrated storybook-style by a woman with a soft, bespoke accent, which I initially disliked but I grew to appreciate. It isn't "Bastion" levels of quality in narration, but she fits the game quite well. She isn't helped by the writing though, which keeps true to its wondrous, storybook theming throughout, but ends up being quite repetitive. This compounds with the already simple and chore-like nature of the puzzles to make this short playthrough a bit of a drag. I enjoyed exploring the varied environments, and there are actually a lot of unique elements in each area and across the puzzles, but in the end everything is so straightforward it doesn't feel inspired, but more of the same. You go through the game finding and saving lost souls, each of which the narrator gives you very similar sounding lines for. And then you do that 20+ times until the games over. Very often the puzzles are so easy I'm finishing the task before the narrator even finishes her lines.The story is a central focus but there isn't exactly a plot here. It's more a vibe, and that's fine. A lot of time is spent on trying to fill out a story that can be summarized in a sentence of two, but in the end it does a fair job of giving us the setting, visuals, and environments, which again are all top notch. There are also these optional collectables which are journal entries that are once again rather repetitive; I found my brain turning off as the narrator read off yet another of the 40+ entries hidden throughout the game. I'm not sure they added a lot, as there's just not a whole lot to say, but man it sure tries. Lots of writing to say not very much.The OST is unintrusive; nothing special but filled with ambiance. Rather forgettable honestly, as you can tell by how few listens it has on Youtube / other platforms outside the game itself. It's not a weakness but certainly not a strength of the game either.I should mention that there are a handful of bugs here and there (I had one that broke a puzzle on me). The initial cutscene actually broke for me and I had to restart (which certainly didn't help my first impression). Not the best look after Hello Games' notoriously bug-riddled previous game, No Man's Sky, but truthfully the couple bugs I encountered didn't sully the experience too much. There was a handful of frame drops (which shouldn't happen with my monster of a PC), which are apparently far worse on other platforms (Switch, notably). Again, not a big deal, but figured it was worth mentioning.Overall, The Last Campfire has a ton of charm, with a relaxing, laid-back vibe that is maybe is a bit -too- laid back, verging on boring. It's got an awesome world to explore, and fulfills its mission of being like a children's book in design and feel, but uh forgets to have a game somewhere in the middle. Like I said, there is a -lot- I like about this game, but ultimately it fails the core, most fundamental question that needs to be asked when evaluating a game: "Is it fun?" And uh, not really? It's about as fun as flipping through a children's book and looking at the pretty illustrations and art. But then there's 6 hours of it and for some reason it wants you to complete the simplest puzzles of all time to flip the page. Ultimately, the repetitive nature made it hard for me to connect with the game. I don't need it to be a brutally hard puzzle game, but it doesn't even do enough to keep me engaged. If that aspect was different, I'm sure I'd rate this game far higher, but in the end, it's simply not fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say that I was very captivated by this game. The atmosphere, the music and the story were very well chosen. I had a lot of fun with the puzzles, there were many with a high challenge and many puzzles where you had to think around the corner a lot. My only negative point is that if you play it on a PC and then move things with the mouse, it is usually difficult (there was a slight frustration, especially in 1-2 puzzles).I recommend you to buy this great game.Special praise goes to the lady who set the game to music.I actually had to cry a little at the end.No game has managed that for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game, puzzles were enjoyable but not too difficult which was nice. The music was also very good. Got the game on sale so the price for me at least was absolutely worth it. Would recommend, a short but enjoyable puzzle game with nice atmosphere, game play and music. I would rate it a 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun little game! I loved the narration and the general feeling of melancholy with a spark of hope. Sometimes the simplest lessons are the ones we need to learn over and over. The puzzles were fun, but never very challenging. It's a relaxing game to spend a couple of hours on and works great on the Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: There was a place the embers went when the lights went out. Here we are. We, too, are grove whose light has gone out. We are trying to find our way in this land like other embers. But some embers freeze in despair during their journey. We also help these embers. The game has very sweet animations and a very sweet story. You can find yourself in the sentences of some embers who have lost hope. Don't be sad that there is no hope at the end of the road, the important thing is the journey. Good luck on your journey.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this, but with the caveat that you should turn off the narrators voice and just use the subtitles.  The shallowness of the plot was emphasized by having one narrator read every line from every character.  The graphics are cozy and the puzzles are simple but relaxing.  There isn't much content and the game can be finished very quickly, so it would have been nice if the plot and character development had been a bit more fleshed out.  They make a note that not everything is as simple as solving a puzzle, and yet all the problems are either left unsolved or solved with a simple puzzle.  Any morals or explanations come at the level a mom would communicate to a young child.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a sweet and heartwarming game with such a sweet little message of never loosing hope, even at our lowest. And when we are not able to, the sharing of the ember of hope is what drives this game and its story. A small gathering, little campfire, being together with each other and sharing our stories, and  listening and helping each other is a lesson this game teaches us.Also, the voice actor Rachel August is so sweet and does these cute little impressions when voicing the characters, it makes my heart melt <3Overall, had a very heartfelt moment while playing this small but very beautiful game.Never loose hope, my fellow embers!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little puzzle game with excellent narration (voice over) and story. Cozy game type that had my gf glued to the screen until she finished. Some of the puzzles are not obvious, and there's a little bit of backtracking involved but it all makes you explore the maps more. Takes around 8-10 hours to finish. Solid recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead). The Last Campfire is a short indie adventure and puzzle game where you control a small creature called ember, similar to a Jawa Jawa from SW but cuter and with bright colors, that has to save other creatures from their species by solving puzzles.The story is interesting and well narrated and the environments, NPCs and objects are highly detailed and with vibrant colors and are very distinct from each other. The puzzles you have to solve have a lot of variety and several different mechanics, that you have to use both in the open world as in each puzzle's individual location, but all of them are easy to solve for an adult, so I’d guess the game is mostly targeted at children.  22 Achievements. Around 5 hours. Easy, the puzzles are simple to solve.    Easy. Saving all the creatures will grant you all the achievements. The Last Campfire is a beautiful but short adventure puzzle game, with puzzles that a child can solve but that might feel too easy for an adult. Still, definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a complicated game to review. Overall I would give it 6/10.It is a charming game and incredibly well-crafted.But from a "fun" standpoint it's really very simple, has an uninspiring (and a bit tedious) storyline related to loneliness and hope and whatever. These factors detract from the overall fun it provides.So even though this game has an "overwhelmingly positive" score (there is strong agreement that the score should be 5+/10) it's DEFINITELY not a 10/10. And since you can't possibly give it a "not recommended" rating... everyone agrees it's a good game (but just barely, and nothing special).I paid a few bucks for it, but I would be perfectly happy if I hadn't.Having said all of that: the craftsmanship in this game is exceptional. There are complicated mechanics and very few bugs (I got stuck by the stairs frequently at the first frog pool where the fisherman sits). If the mechanics had been more inspired then this game would have been incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, but this is such a lovely game, I nearly teared up at the end. I think this one will fit for all ages, the little ones sure would love the colorful world and great puzzles, but the story is bound to hit older folks much harder. Little embers have a way of presenting heavy topics so gently that it feels both healing and validating. I think it is a very healing game, in general. The first time an ember happened to be unapproachable was very surprising, but added a great nuance to the overall message; but at the same time, the game doesn't judge, just... kindly informs you that this might be not the right time, or you might be not the right person - I guess this part would make more sense for those who have played. Special thanks to the narrator and their absolutely lovely voice, it's a perfect fit for the game and adds so much more than simple text/sound effects could have done. 10/10, have and will recomment for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: THE cutest puzzle game accompanied by an emotional story. The animations are very advanced for such a simple game. If not for the story, the puzzles would've not held such elevated meaning. I fully recommend for people who are looking for a catchy game that is perfect for relaxation. I haven't felt frustrated a single time while solving the puzzles and that's a big plus for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Journey before Destination little Ember.Cute little game with some really good puzzles. First and foremost this is a puzzle game with light exploration aspects. _childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle game. Puzzles are relatively easy but enjoyable. Worth playing this game for a relaxing time. Music  is pleasant and voice actor has a nice voice. Compared to other puzzle games I have played (Seasons After Fall, Silence- the whispered world) this game has a lot more puzzles to solve and items to find. It is a short game about 9 hrs.
