_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply wonderful.  So sweet and poignant with some brilliant puzzles.  I need a moment for my little heart to recover before starting something new. ❤The story is simply lovely.  You play as Ember, a little lost ember trying to help others who have become 'forlorn' in order to find their way.  When Ember encounters a forlorn, they have to solve a puzzle, in order to reach the light at the end and restore their hope.  But there are also those that can't be saved, and Ember must accept that.Neither Ember nor the others actually speak, rather the whole thing is narrated by a woman with a soft voice and lovely accent, almost like being read a storybook.  It's enchanting.The graphics too, while crisp and gorgeous, retain a little of that childlike nature, furthering the illusion.The puzzles aren't too difficult, though there are a number of them that will have you scratching your head - such as rolling cubes that are only solid on one side to make a path.  But in a good way!  Nothing complicated enough to ever become frustrating or unsolvable without a walkthrough.  There are some hidden journal entries in each location which you may need a guide to help find, but they are not necessary, they merely add some more context to the backstory. It took me 12 hours to play this game, and I admit I may have allowed myself to become lost in the magic of it at times, just listening to the music and admiring the scenery, pretending to sit around the campfire with the forlorn that Ember has saved.  ^-^PS: The narrator is Rachel August, you may recognize her as Trylla from the Hilda movie.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: It is a 5h "puzzle" "game" and I use both terms very loosely:• "Game" because it is essentially a walking sim.• "Puzzles" because they are beyond trivial and very repetitive.You'd think in a walking sim, they'd have at the very least put extra effort into the narrative, music and narration but:• The narrative is underwhelming, an overly simplistic message of "maintaining hope in the face of the unknown, not allowing fear to take over" - and even then, it does a poor job of conveying said message. Journey did it way before TLC and it did it without a single spoken or written word, furthermore the way it was designed, it allowed space for other interpretations as well.• The music is not even close to being as good as a game of this type needs it to be:-- for a direct comparison ie. a walking sim with puzzles, it doesn't even hold a candle to that of Journey.-- for a comparison to games that don't play similarly but are extremely similar in aesthetics/ art design (generally soundtracks and art design are very interwoven), it doesn't even come close to the soundtracks of Death's Door or Tunic.• I didn't enjoy the narration, mainly because the VA sounded whiny.Beyond the cutesy art direction, The Last Campfire has nothing else to offer.2/5
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: There is not a lot to spoil on this game I think, but still I felt good going in mostly blind. The gameplay itself is really nice. Interesting puzzles, lots of variations on ideas and mechanics. These vary from pretty obvious to more challenging, and at least for me none were particularly frustrating. One thing I was really impressed by is how the game has a story to tell, but it mostly doesn't slow you down to tell it. The narration will play even as you close a message. This lets you move towards your next task while taking in the story. It is easy for this sort of choice to go unseen because it is elegant and well executed.Another impressive choice for me, was seeing additional story hidden around the world. You can get the core story without these. But for those who explore and want to find everything, this is what turns up. The richness of this story made seeking out all these little notes rewarding. Instead of grinding out secret little trinkets like most games, here you truly are rewarded for nosing around a little longer.Because of how well executed the gameplay is, it seems simple and intuitive throughout. That is important because it stands aside and lets the story shine, and this story does. It is thoughtful and melancholy, bittersweet and engaging. Some stories rely very much on the plot, some hang thinly on . The Last Campfire deftly navigates tone and content, coming out stronger for it and very affecting as well. Most of the NPCs get only a sentence or two, and a great many of them stopped me a moment to reflect on their story and my own. That is a triumph for any medium.Absolutely worth your time and money to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little puzzle game better than anything ubisoft or EA has put out. It is really well designed and polished. There is more variation in the puzzles than in breath of the wild. It also looks great and runs like a charm on linux and steam deck. It has no ruddy microtransactions or always online nonsense. It is great for unwinding after a long day, so support the devs an pick this one up, you wont regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Loved it. I only paid a few dollars for it, but would have paid more. It took me about 8 hours to finish and I was sad it was over. The game did get stuck for the final scene, but I was able to shut down the game and redo the last 10 minutes or so to watch the last cut scene. The overarching story was kind of depressing, which isn't my vibe, but the in-game play was cute enough that I didn't mind. Overall, fun puzzle game without any combat, which I love.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I've already played this game on my switch, but then saw there was achievements and I just HAD to buy it on steam. If you are into puzzle games, this game is for you! Its beautiful and not hard at all. You can go at your own pace and and the narrating is actually helpful. This game has beautiful graphic design into it and so much detail! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really nice 3D puzzle / adventure game! With a good (but little sad) story.Puzzles are generally quite easy, and maps aren't too big when you have to look around and find solutions. It's a relaxing game, not a challenging one, and I certainly like that.Very nice visuals/graphics and sounds. I like the style.Easy 100% achievement completion (and counts on you profile).
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Not a long game, but a poignant and heartfelt one. The puzzles were enjoyable but not terribly difficult. I did get stuck a couple of times, but I feel like that was due to momentary obtuseness on my part as much as anything else.Overall I really enjoyed this game. It's a pretty chill atmospheric experience with some fun little puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Wow... Genuinely one of the most beautiful and gripping stories of any game I've played in a while, let alone on that is only $10 (I got it for $3 on sale). The gameplay isn't terribly difficult, but some of the puzzles still pose a bit of a challenge. This game will make you think.. a lot. The ending will really move you. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: if you want a calm puzzle game, this is it.  The puzzles are challenging but doable with a little effort and the spirit guardian gives hints that tell you where to look if needed. The only  pressure to go faster is if you pressure yourself. It isn't the longest (I took about 6 hours), but you can replay the puzzles at any time after completing them in game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. The way I interpreted the storyline is you are an "ember", a lost soul stuck in purgatory, and your job is to approach sad souls stuck in thought patterns or a state of despair, and you enter into their world, solve a puzzle, and that helps them through and allows them to join others at a group campfire. Sadly, but realistically, you come across souls who do not want to be saved or aren't ready. It's just really beautiful. The puzzles are fun to solve, not overly complex and each level can be figured out (even if you're stuck) by retracing your steps and connecting the clues. The game was short and sweet, and stress-free but challenging enough that you never get bored. Truly the kind of game to stick with you for a while, in the best way.For those on the fence, I started playing this game with the demo available from the store page before committing to purchasing the whole game. The demo encompasses 1/3 of the game and is very indicative of the gameplay for the remainder.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Hra mě zaujala svým zpracováním, a tak jsem si ji musela koupit. Není moc dlouhá ani moc složitá. Ovládání je jednoduché a hádanky přijatelně náročné. Sice jsem musela párkrát zapojit více mozkových buněk, ale zdárně jsem proplula celou hrou. Hra má zajímavý příběh, krásnou hudbu a grafiku. Hra není úplně vhodná pro osoby, kteří mají problém s orientací v prostoru, tak jako já. :-D Občas se mi stalo, že jsem absolutně netušila, kde se toulám, ale vždy jsem se nějak vymotala. Cenově je tato hra dražší, když si porovnáte délku hrací doby a plnou cenu necelých 15 euro. Ale pokud se zas objeví někde v akci, tak vám doporučuji si koupit, stojí to za to. :-) The game impressed me with its design, so I had to buy it. It's not too long or too complicated. The controls are simple and the puzzles are acceptably challenging. Although I had to engage more brain cells a few times, I successfully sailed through the entire game. The game has an interesting story, beautiful music and graphics. The game is not entirely suitable for people who have a problem with orientation in space, like me. :-D Sometimes it happened that I had absolutely no idea where I was wandering, but I always somehow found my way out. In terms of price, this game is more expensive when you compare the length of playing time and the full price of less than 15 euros. But if it appears again somewhere on sale, I recommend you to buy it, it's worth it. :-)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campire is a fairly short cozy puzzle game where you search for meaning and help others along the road.- The puzzles are mostly easy to solve (there were some that took me a while longer to solve). If you're looking for a more challenging game, this is not it as it's focusing more on story telling. If you're looking for a more casual experience, this is for you!- The graphics and music create a very soothing and calm experience.- I had a bit of a hard time with the voice of the narrator. Her accent sometimes makes her sound like she's speaking in "UwU" and I had a hard time dealing with that. If you don't mind this, then you're perfectly fine. My personal preference would've been an entirely different person for the narrating or at least having different voices for different characters (she does all of the voice acting and narrates over basically everything you do during the entire game).- Keep in mind that this game is short. I clocked just under six hours and that was after doing everything there was to do and also struggling a little with some of the puzzles.If you enjoy casual cozy puzzle games, I recommend this. Definitely pick this up when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The story of the game is beautiful. The narrator's voice is very relaxing, with a perfect immersive tone, and the graphics are adorable. The puzzles are not so hard, so you don't drive crazy trying to solve them, which would tear you away from the atmosphere that the game proposes. I'm delighted. Very recommendable if you like the style.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A really cute puzzle-exploration adventure with a deep melancholic undertone. That said, most of the puzzles are really casual (only in the end they get a bit more complex, but never truly hard), so don’t expect this to be a brain scrambler. No, this game definitely again is more about the journey, the tale and the experience. And in this regard, it delivers really well. Music and graphics are nice, love the girl’s story-teller voice, and even though the explanations/journals all in all keep being kind of cryptic and the length isn’t too long (only 3 main areas), I actually don’t mind this at all here. It’s just perfect as it is (even easy to perfect it 100% achievement-wise, just remember to reconstruct the boat at least once). So thumbs up from me, no question. Little earworm fun thing by the way, the more you listen to the intro music in the menu, after a while it somehow remembers you a lot of Sounds of Silence (especially in the Disturbed version, just continue with ‘hello darkness, my old friend’), check it out for yourself, I guarantee the connection will get stuck pretty fast in your head as well ;) Oh, and before I forget, there are a few dialog choices at some point (which I normally dislike, especially in games with autosaves that don’t really have much replay value), but don’t worry here, the answers are completely the same, so if you’re like me, just don’t think about it, you don’t miss anything.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is an extremely cute, well-made game. The graphics are fantastic, level design is amazing, music is awesome, and the narration voiceover is perfect. Writing and pacing are great, I love all of the side characters (and even the cute environmental animations! It really gave life to the world and the story. The main story itself was incredibly touching and solidly written very satisfying to complete. As someone with depression, I really enjoyed this game and would definitely play again. Got tripped up on a few of the puzzles, but overall the puzzles were well-done and they all felt fresh with their designs and solutions. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful game. The puzzle difficulty is enough to make you sit and think, but not too strenuous to encourage frustration. The locations and graphics overall, with the music and the soothing voice of Rachel August, is just a perfect recipe. The story was short but meaningful, with humble and wholesome lessons within each puzzle, if the story was any longer it would have spoilt it. When completed though, it was nice to be able to replay the puzzles with some added extras in there.It was a seamless game and I didn't come across any bugs or glitches. I struggled to get my head around steering the boat with the keyboard, and some of the objects, but once I started using just the mouse it just worked. It was easy to navigate Ember with just the keyboard though. Overall it was a perfect wholesome game, and definitely recommend it at retail price let alone on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A decent puzzle game with a cute story and likeable characters. I enjoyed the atmosphere a lot, but found the controls a bit annoying at times. Some puzzles are way more challenging, while others are very simple, but I don't mind that mix, as it didn't frustrate me to the point of needing to quit the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire was actually intended as a Pile Of Shame purchase, after Hello Games has been bringing updates and expeditions into No Man's Sky at no cost for years, which other publishers would have packaged into DLCs. Then Steam Deck arrived and I installed it as an easy to use title to get used to the device. After a little over 5 hours of play (Steam presumably doesn't count time without an internet connection) I had it finished including all the Achievements. It's a fantastic mix of clever but quite easy puzzles, cute graphics and a beautifully told story, making Ember's journey a real pleasure. Together with the sense for the style of a children's fairy tale, these parts add up to a recommendable result, filled with themes that are close to all of us and not really just set in a faraway world. Inspired by the Brothers Grimm, among others, real-life problems are addressed in a fantastic way. Adult themes, for example concerning fears and loss, are cleverly packaged in an easily digestible way without resorting to violence at any time.It's a tiny world compared to NMS, but one that can be enjoyed by all. A puzzle adventure without any grind elements, with an emotionally touching story and consistently entertaining tasks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Game was gifted to me.Very nice and enjoyable game. I had a nice time with the puzzles. Only one gave me a bit of trouble, but all of them are resolvable the moment you try them. Found a couple of bugs: 1- On the pig's Marsh, where you have the elevator and the slide, I thought I had to lower the pig through the elevator, and it got stuck there.2- Whenever I rotated one of the light orbes, the character animation would get stuck.3 - At the caves, on the main room, after doing the event that triggers the snake, the dialog would keep repeating.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it mostly to see what hello games is up to beyond no man's sky, got surprised with a fantastic little game, with pleasing visuals, fair puzzles and a neat story, my only gripe would be the clunky keyboard controls, it definitely feels like an afterthought in certain interactions and so a controller is advised for the best experience.Recommended if you are looking for a calm and interesting game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game which connects to your inner world in a way so familiar yet also so different with its story and design. The dialogues are enhancing the meaning of the game, creating more depth to it. The puzzles were interesting and some quite challenging, not making the game too easy and making it different from a more visual novel-like thing in the absence of combat or other types of interaction. The most accurate word to describe this game is probably nothing other than beautiful as it touches your soul in the cutest way possible. Bought it for my boyfriend as well, and he liked it too. (: I'd certainly recommend it if you're usually hard on yourself; helps you remember that life isn't always that easy lol...Took me 6.5-7 hours to finish as an amateur (and wanderer), and my boyfriend 5 so hope that gives an insight!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a beautiful story. It is a game about hope, death, loneliness, fear, the need for community, and especially perseverance, amongst the other parts of what makes up the human experience. It is definitely a story worth paying attention to while playing, but the game could be skipped through pretty easily if you weren't interested. There were some really beautiful moments throughout. I also just enjoyed the art style, beautiful but simple.The puzzles were all really enjoyable and I wouldn't call any of them overly difficult. For a full playthrough of about 6 hours I enjoyed them. The game also has a really enjoyable soundtrack that doesn't distract or annoy at all, which I think is really important for a puzzle game.Overall, I give it a solid 8-8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I had wanted to buy this game for a long time. I bought it when it was 60% of and that was a good price for it. I wouldn't however pay the full price, since I played the game with full achievements in approximately 7 h. I just mean that I have paid the same amount for many games and played them from 30h to 300h. But approcimately 5 euros for 7h of fun yeah that is a good bargain. Anyway, the game is lovely. The art is great, the story is a bit sad but cute. The voice actor is stunning and I love all the short poems. Some of the puzzles where actually a bit tough and took me 5-10min but most of them where pretty simple.I mean you can take this however you want, I like to play casual games so it was nice, but i would have wanted a bit of a challenge sometimes too.Great game, recommend totally playing it ! But wouldn't buy it full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Super wholesome puzzle solving. Puzzles are not too hard, very casual. Beautiful artwork and design. I also cannot emphasize how good the audio is in this game. The movements you make and how you interact with the world makes such wonderful noises. And I love having a narrator while playing. Super chill game for anyone who likes casual puzzle solving
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A very cozy little puzzle game, with a truly great story told very well. The puzzles are simple but just interesting enough not to bore me.I can heartily recommend it to anyone, at any price. It is an experience as lasting as the best of novels. I will think of the little Embers of The Last Campfire as often and as fondly as I think of McCaffrey's dragons, Asimov's robots, or Tolkien's Hobbits.It isn't a long game, it is the perfect length for the story it wants to tell. An Asimov novel would not improve if you add a thousand pages, likewise this game should not be any longer than it is.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant if I would enjoy this as much as I'd hoped in the first hour or so of gameplay. The puzzles were very easy at the beginning. But as the game progressed the puzzles became more engaging and enjoyable and required at least a little bit of brain power. The artwork is great and the game itself is beautifully done and probably worth the $15 price tag but pro tip - it goes on sale for $1.50 every single month.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A great indie game but it has some flaws. There were a lot of glitches in which I had to restart to the last checkpoint because the game was broken ( ex. My character went under the map when I tried to open a wanderer's box ). A few puzzles took me some time to think but most of them weren't difficult. I wish there was more than a voice actor, doing all the lines in the game. Hearing the same voice over and over again. If there wasn't another VA, adding a simple noise to each type of characters or items would suffice. Still a good game don't get me wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: its a cute, very pretty looking game. art style and music are very good!but the puzzles... mostly pretty boring, repetitive and probably not a challenge for most people. also the story is not really worth mentioning. it has a cute end, but thats about it.still enjoyed playing it tho, can recommend it to people who just want to relax and enjoy a sweet, pretty looking game.(6.5/10)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game on my wishlist for a long time and never thought of getting it because I thought it'd be another random puzzle game. I am pleasantly surprised and I cannot remember a game that I have played recently that made such an impact on me. This is not just a puzzle game and is an emotionally charged piece that you should go into blind. Buy this game, especially if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I still gave it thumbs up but I don't think it's as perfect game as other people say. My biggest problem was that you are put in a location which is then branching into more and more sublocations and I felt a bit lost, losing a track of where I am, which sublocations I finished and which ones are left.I recommend to get this game on a sale. You then get a game with pretty decent puzzles which are fun to figure out and lovely art style which doesn't outstay your welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little puzzle game, with some heavy topics. I can recommend this game to everyone that like a chill puzzle experience with some good music and mostly easy (except with a few) puzzles. The graphics and atmosphere are well done and the game offers a few likable characters and an intruiguing mystery
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The last campfire is a real gem. At first I thought it would be boring because I'm not a huge fan of puzzles and everything related to them. While playing the game I was able to enjoy the good soundtracks, the gameplay was fun and the story was magical. I recommend the game to everyone.Thanks to the game developers and everyone who made this masterpiece possible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable little treat of a game that features some exceedingly clever yet not unreasonably complicated puzzles alongside a very soft and comforting narrator. Whether it's during a mini-dungeon or while you're out exploring the world, getting new lines of narration is a nice way to let you know that you're on the right path. If you're looking for something wholesome and perfectly perplexing to fill a quiet evening, you'd be hard-pressed to find a game more fitting than The Last Campfire.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, not my type of game at all, or so I thought! I generally play FPShooters but like to have a break from time to time but struggle as my attention span seems to be terrible - anyway - thinking this game looked light a reverse situation to little nightmares (a game i did enjoy) I thought I would give it ago! Well I absolutely loved it. I thoroughly enjoyed the narration too when that's usually a pet peeve of mine and tend to mute it if I can but it felt perfect for this game, beautiful soothing voice which can be said about the game also! I  would recommend it to anyone and for 11.39 its absolute steal.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the dialogue is simply crushing. The smallest acts of generosity are met with shock and deep-welling gratitude from these sweet creatures who want nothing more than a kind word, or a kind face in the dark. There are some you can't save. There are some who don't want to be saved. It feels awful to leave them behind, but God knows you can't force healing on people who aren't ready.The narrator is very sweet-sounding and it's nice to listen to her accented English. Some of the puzzles are easy and some are randomly really hard, but they are mostly enjoyable. Most of all, I REALLY wish there was a map.Overall, this game settles into a category I would call "bittersweet but hopeful" and I really am enjoying it. I think it's something really special to say that kindness is both powerful and contagious. The world is cruel, but people don't have to be.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game on a youtubers backlog list and thought I'd give it a try. It's a cute little puzzle game, which is all I thought it would be. Instead as you go through puzzle by puzzle the developers tell a story that brings emotions I didn't think I'd have by the end. I won't spoil for anyone but it's definitely worth checking out. It's not very long but it takes you on a journey that hits you right in the feels by the end. I loved dabbling in the puzzles after a long day and would highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game and I would even go as far to say that it is my favourite game I've played ever! Aspects I love is the story element, the colourful and beautiful world you get to explore. I also love how the quests are set out and how you learn to recognise things to look out for - or the little hints that helps you figure out what to do next. Lastly the puzzles are truly so well thought out. Some are easier than other...and some really had me scratching my head, but when you manage to solve it you feel so satisfied! I will definitely play this again! Thank you so much for creating this game and giving me the chance to play something truly magical!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: While the puzzles weren't overly difficult, I found The Last Campfire fun to play. The environments are cute, and while I was originally apprehensive about the narration, it grew on me over the course of the game, building an interesting narrative throughout the game. Took me a little under 6 hours to complete with all achievements, which was a decent length without overstaying its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly delightful game the puzzles were reasonable (tho i did search up three of them but that's honestly on me lol) the story itself is very calming and peaceful the music is pretty nice too and i really liked that all of the journals were just fun little things and that there is no achievement for collecting all of them because that'd take way too much time (i got more than half idk how many exactly and still it took me 5h to complete the game) the only thing i disliked was narrator maybe that's just me but i really disliked both their voice and how they read but again that could be just me thing so back to review it's great game and I absolutely recommend
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the art style, music, and story progression of this game! The game has a narrator for the story, which I found interesting, and it feels like the narrator is telling a story of the past while you are playing as Ember (search carefully and you will be rewarded with extra fun bits of information). I love a good puzzle, but sometimes I just want to play the kind of game I can grab my coffee and/or snack and play for a couple of hours without breaking my brain and focus on the story. This game fits that description, and if that sounds like your kind of game, give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely lovely game. Fully completed it, and then did every extra thng I could to squeez every last minute out of it. Puzzles aren't too hard, and sometimes I may have preferred a little bit more of a challenge... but other times they were definitely more difificult than I expected from this game!Story is good, and I love the fact that you don't need to 100% it to progress to the next area, and that you always have the option to go back and explore an earlier area further. This was very pleasing for the complitionist side of me. All in all, I loved the experience this game gave me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: took about 10 hours to complete the game. it was a really fun puzzle game that was really enjoyable to play. the puzzles were tricky enough that some took several tries but I was able to complete them all without having to look up any clues, which is always nice. definetly rec for anyone who enjoys relaxing games
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I think everyone who enjoys puzzle games should play this. While 5 hours of gameplay isn't that long, it's already so compacted so there's no time wasted wandering. The level is designed is very well designed so that when you passed it the first time, you can already imagine what kind of stuffs you'll need to do to complete the level. The puzzles can be summed into a different kinds of repeating category, which sounds bad I know but it's very well designed that it varies so well.The narrative of this game reminded me so much of Celeste. Where as in , you experienced Madeline's journey first-hand and how'd she try to overcome her depression and anxiety. While in , you travel around helping others that had lost their hope. On your journey, you will see all kinds of reaction of people dealing with hopelessness. Some people wants others to help them directly, some didn't want any help, and some just needed time to heal. It's very beautifully wrapped and it made me quite emotional at the end. Buy this game now (or on sale because it's very cheap)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A short game with a melancholic theme, but still hopefulSpeaking to other forlorns who have lost hope for various reasons and solving a puzzle to help these lost souls. Albeit not every forlorn you approach can be helped by solving a puzzle as some either don't want to be helped or simply cannot be. The narrator acknowledges that not everything can be solved with a puzzle.Each character had their own different reason for losing their hope. Themes of: loss, despair, mental illness, depression - were all portrayed through these characters.When it comes to the puzzles themselves, they were either too easy or somewhat challenging. Each puzzle stage had a different theme, accompanied by the appropriate narration.Visuals were great, no qualms about that either. The achievements are also fairly easy to get, but I didn't bother to 100% it.Overall, a cute game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is truly a worthwhile experience.  The story line is fantastic and the narrator's voice perfectly brings you into the tone and world of the story.  The game play is relatively short, but this is also dependent on how quickly you get through the puzzles.  Some are harder than others.  I would highly recommend playing this game, especially if the demo is still available, you can try it out and see if it's for you, but I think that after playing, you will find yourself needing to purchase in order to continue playing.  I think even at full price, the game is worth the money, but if you find it on sale, definitely pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Very beautiful, relaxed, narrative and child-friendly puzzle game. The emotional story is about fear, hope and regret. The puzzles are clever but never too difficult or frustrating. There is no time pressure at any time. I really enjoyed the time I spent playing the game.NOTE: I had to play through the game twice to get the achievements as none were shown the first time through. It is probably because I had installed the demo and then bought the game and played it through immediately without restarting Steam. So I would recommend restarting Steam after purchasing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful little puzzle game. Music is good and narrator is pleasant. Puzzles are not very hard and there is even a "explore" mode that skips most of the puzzles. (Not recommended as puzzle mechanics are cool) The story/theme is very clear and easy to understand but not heavy handed in any way.The characters are adorable and there are all kinds of cute animations - the environment and levels remind me of Hob, but much simpler. Fairly short game, but doesn't feel rushed, perfect length. There are some harder puzzles in the menu if you want to play some more.There are three different control schemes: Mouse only, Mouse and keyboard, ControllerThey all work well, except mouse and keyboard can be a bit finicky when you want to rotate things with the arrow keys and row the boat. Nothing game breaking.One slight annoyance is the boat undocking procedure, the button to row is the same button to climb back up the ladder, which sometimes makes it difficult to sail away.All in all, great little game, plus there is a demo you can try before you buy!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very calming game to play when you need a temporary escape from the world's chores. I love all the messages the fellow forlorn and embers I meet along the way remind me, it's a little warm hug and a space to breathe when everything seems rushed and urgent.Puzzles are just the right amount of tricky and pleasure! 10/10 would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful, family friendly, story puzzle adventure.  A gentle heroes journey.  Reminds me of a children's book.  You are Ember gathering up the Forlorn, lost characters scattered throughout the lovely 3D landscapes.  Forlorn are "troubled" embers; some have lost hope, some fearful of what is to come.  They are stuck in a kind of limbo.  Ember solves puzzles to gather up the light and return a spark of "life" to each forlorn.  Puzzles can be pleasantly challenging and one or two a little frustrating as they send you back to the beginning.  The music is very nice, graphics are well done.  I particularly enjoy the narrative.  I rarely listen to the voice overs (reading faster than the narrative) yet the voice is so very lovely and calming I can't help but listen.  It has replay value.  I have not encountered any bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Short simple game that sticks to its core ideas.The game has a high degree of polish and well considered design and flow.Accessible puzzles for all ages.Sweet story with a philosophical nod to atheism.Don't seek this game out if you want your brain to melt in frustration, cause it's not that difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game a lot. I enjoyed the puzzles. There was a good variety. I would say about 50% were easy, 30% were straightforward but you still had to think about them, 10% were challenging, and 10% were pretty difficult.I also enjoyed the story. It had a mystical, ethereal feel to it. There are elements of being in harmony with nature, friendship, and lost souls finding their way. It's thoughtful and reflective. It had a very tranquil atmosphere with many moments of melancholy, but with a spirit of hope.There is a journal with pages dispersed throughout the game that you have to find. They're a combination of storytelling and poetry. I thought it was a nice element added to the game. Spoiler: It's not a long game. It took me a little over nine hours to beat. I'm the kind of person that likes to stop and explore everything and talk to all the people, so if you're the type that only cares about gameplay and the story doesn't matter to you then you could get it done even quicker.I recommend playing it with a controller. I found it more enjoyable that way, but it's perfectly functional with a keyboard or mouse. I say "or" because you could play the whole game with just the keyboard or just the mouse. The controls are extremely simple. There's nothing mechanically intense about the gameplay.All in all, I enjoyed the game and recommend it to anyone who likes puzzles and stories.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more than just puzzles, it's about the journey of searching for meaning and helping others, literally finding light in the darkness. The main theme is woven beautifully throughout, making it a delightful experience. For me, it was a cozy, touching adventure that left me seeing hope from a different perspective.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a puzzle-driven adventure game. The puzzles range from extremely simple to requiring some thought (though ultimately not being all that complicated except for one puzzle that got me pretty good...). The atmosphere and visual aspects of the game are quite nice and the characters are charming. The only thing I disliked about the game was the voice acting, but it ultimately doesn't substantially detract from the overall gameplay. The game took about 6 hours to complete in its entirety. I recommend this game if you are generally a fan of the genres associated with this game (puzzle, indie, adventure, some minor exploration, relaxing, etc).
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with a touching and meaningful story, The riddles are creative but never frustrating. Some people might find them too easy, but I liked the difficulty level.Steam shows I only have 4.5-5 hours of playtime but it's slightly above 7. Steam stopped tracking it thanks to internet connectivity issues. Price might still be too high for some, but if it ever gets discounted again it's worth it for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This cute and lovely little puzzle game comes along with a beautiful and heartfelt story that makes you think about life and how you may view it. The puzzles are not too hard, few were headscratchers. Most of the time taking a break from the puzzles helped to reset the brain and solve them a bit later.Definitely recommended if you like a more relaxing gameplay and enjoy a good storyline.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly underrated. Honestly, it deserves way more attention. The story, dialogues, puzzles, adventures.. best 7,5 hours i've spent on a game so far. Recommend to everyone. Graphics are amazing, every aspect from the game is just perfectly balanced. Don't hesitate to spend 12 euros on it, its so worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The mood of this game is kind of melancolicIt is short, I have finished the main story of th game in 5h30The puzzles are challenging, without needing me to break my head for hours on it, also I liked the peaceful soundtrack, and it was enjoyable to discover the different maps, truly it is a great game to chill
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely, sweet and melancholy game about hope when the final journey is near and light fades. This is a puzzle game, but nearly all of the puzzles are so simple as to hardly be considered puzzles at all.  It is more akin to a walking simulator, which is to say, everyone will get to the end and the story was the main draw.On the subject of the story itself, it is thoughtful, touching, and though sad at times, overall, it was positive message of bravery and grit in the face of adversity, when others had lost their way.  You are the Ember that rekindles the hope of many.  Yet, I also appreciated that you cannot save all those who are lost to despair, as not everyone is ready to be saved. It is a game worthy of your time, and with a short 6-8 hours of playtime, doesn't overstay its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game. It's visually beautiful and its world is mysterious and haunting. The puzzles range from very straightforward to challenging (for me anyway), and I never stayed stuck for long. Helpfully, there's a way to get broad hints on where to find the next main story goal, and if you get really stuck in a puzzle, there's a way to reset and try again. For me, this meant the game stayed fun and interesting even when it was challenging. The childlike narration, subtle music, and cute character design gave the game the feeling of an interactive bedtime story. I found some points in the story quite sad and tragic, in moments where the player is made to reflect on despair and loss, and the inexorable encroachment of death and darkness in the game's world. There's a kind of beauty in it though, especially when the story reaches its bittersweet, but hopeful, conclusion. Working gently against the dying of the light feels like quite a prescient theme.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: ᴘʟᴀʏ ɪᴛ ꜰᴏʀ ᴛʜᴇ ᴊᴏᴜʀɴᴇʏSimple puzzle game with a really nice story. I don't think having more difficult puzzles would benefit the game. It's really impactful as it is.   • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • •I have found some glitches with the piggies (vanishing into walls and such).The Italian translation has some errors. I can get around with little translation mistakes during the game, as they don't prevent you from understanding what you have to do and finishing the game, but I cannot excuse things wrong the main menu. Please fix "SELEZIONA SALVA". It really hurts.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: I expect for a lot of people that the narrator is hit or miss. For those that don't know, there is a female narrator that narrates the entire game, what NPCs say, how you feel, what things are, etc. These bleeds into the philosophy of "show, don't tell" in games, and the narrator can step over this boundary sometimes, including telling you how the protagonist feels, which should largely be up to the player in my opinion. In the beginning, I was very disappointed about the narrator being there to begin with, and talking as much as she did, largely because I'm not used to have someone narrate the entire playthrough of any puzzle adventure game I've played. With that said, this narrator grew on me a lot as I played the game, and she speaks in a very "story time-esc" way. After finishing the game, the narrator is maybe one of the most memorable parts of the game, and I'm really glad I played it. However, I still wouldn't be surprised if others wouldn't like this element of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: From the creators of No Mans Sky, Hello Games presents their most recent game in an indie puzzle adventure called The Last Campfire.The story is about an Ember who has become separated and lost from their group and is trapped in a world of puzzles and mazes. As the story progresses you encounter various locations and characters and solve puzzles as you try to find your way back home together. The puzzles themselves are all enjoyable as there are both small-scale and large-scale ones to solve which do vary in difficulty. At times they do get you thinking as to how to solve them and thinking outside the box is key. Throughout the game is also narration and dialogue which is narrated by a soothing female voice, which I enjoyed and found relaxing to listen to along the way. All in all, it is a wholesome and fun time with positive messages about affection and friendship.The graphics and visuals are magnificent with the charming indie vibe. Environments are beautiful and detailed throughout with an interesting use of colour palette. Characters themselves such as the Ember you play are cutely designed and watching them run is rather cute. Lots of uniquely designed anthropomorphic characters like the chunky pig and sleepy fisherman are compelling to run into. The various locations and worlds you go through have different tones as well which makes it feel more like an adventure as it keeps the game more exciting and vibrant. A shot taken pretty much anywhere would make for an appealing screenshot. Music too is a solid point with some lightened tempo in terms of audio and music, adding to the calming tone of the game.Controls are quite simple to play with as there aren’t too many keys to take note off. Though an option to rebind keys would be a beneficial addition as I was playing with keyboard and mouse, and it feels a bit awkward to move around with w, a, s, d and using x which is right underneath to run. Playing with keyboard and mouse is fine but I feel it would feel more comfortable to play with a controller while sitting back somewhere and having an enjoyable time.The game isn’t expensive and for the entertainment that it offers with the puzzles and world exploration, as well as messages that it presents, I would say that it is worth grabbing at. Overall, it is a charming adventure and puzzle game that provides fun puzzles to solve and beautiful sights to discover.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a short and sweet puzzle game with very nice visuals, good music and an intriguing world to explore. I tried the game both with a controller and keyboard and it felt like the intended way to play the game was with the controller.The story is about an Ember who is trying to find its way home while helping other lost embers on the way. There is an overarching theme about mental health struggle which is probably relatable to anyone.There is a good variety of puzzles, both in difficulty and content. I was stuck on some puzzles for up to 15-20 minutes while some I just breezed through.The visuals are stunning. Some cool character and environment design with lots of variety.I was unsure what think about the narration at first but it grows on you and becomes quite charming.Overall an 8/10 experience, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Campfire

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is an absolutely delightful animated adventure about a Lost Ember trying to find his/her way home and helping other Lost Embers along the way. The sound track is a combination of music and narration (I loved the music but am a bit neutral on the narration). The environments are very detailed, reflect different moods, and are interesting to explore. There is some dialog with characters but it is not extensive and can be read and clicked through. I found that playing with a controller was easiest for me, although the mouse/keyboard work just as well.You travel through three major areas (Forest, Marsh, and Cave), each with a central campfire that tracks the number of ' forlorn' embers who are lost in the area.  Your first task is to locate them (often solving puzzles to create paths to new areas) and then assisting them by completing a mechanical puzzle. There are about 24 major puzzles to complete and all are easily solved with a bit of logical thinking. There are also  handful of fetch quests that  play a part in the story.The game auto-saves on a regular basis and returns you back to your position at the time of exit. If you quit in the middle of a puzzle, you will lose your progress only on that specific puzzle (which is not a bad thing if you want to reset a puzzle and start it over).Completionists should reach 100% if they find and assist all 'forlorn' embers at each campfire. There are collectible notes scattered around the environment that are fun to search for but do not count towards achievements (there is no recap at the end to tell you how many you missed).  I believe that you can choose to locate only a handful of 'forlorn' embers in each area and choose to move forward without completing all puzzles.This was a relaxing and sweet game with a metaphysical overtone. It was a great break from games that require focused coordination or stealth and evasion. It is peaceful and allows you to play at your own pace, doing tasks in whatever order you choose.  All in all, The Last Campfire is fun to play.  When you finish the game, you can circle back through the environments at your leisure. There are also a few additional puzzles that can be played from the main menu.I recommend this to those who enjoy a sweet story and an interesting but not-too-hard adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: That's all I can really say on it. I'm really conflicted between leaving a positive or a negative review on the game and this is one of those moments where I wish there was a middling score on Steam. I ended up settling on a positive score because the base price is a measly $15 and I can say it's worth that at least. I do have a few questions on the 9/10 praise I'm seeing, especially with the "perfect experience" phrasing.As for the good, I can easily say that the artwork is amazing. Environments are pretty, the visuals are well done, and I adore the character design. The characters all remind me of some sort of mixture between the Pi'illo people from the Mario & Luigi RPGs and the robed figures from Journey. They're so fluffy and cute, I love them. I see a lot of potential from the fluffballs and fan-made original characters from them, I'm just sad they didn't do more with them. The designs aren't all that varied with most of them just swapping out the tips of their heads and colors around, but there are a few that are given some feather accessories or a little hat. I'd love to see a sequel just for more of the little buggers. As for another positive, the gameplay is okay. It's really just puzzles and they're all pretty straightforward. Nothing groundbreaking with the design, but you should be able to solve them all without having to resort to a guide. That's all I can really say positive-wise about this game, as it's incredibly short. It's a short 4 to 5 hour adventure, but I've had others report it as much longer.My biggest complaints with The Last Campfire stem from 2 major reasons. The first has to do with its narration and the second has to do with its lack of staying power. The story itself is fine, but that narration really brings it down. Bringing a narrator to a video game is not only unnecessary for the medium, but also extremely difficult to do right. And unfortunately, The Last Campfire's narration doesn't hit the mark. What's the point of a narrator? Well it's to tell you how a character feels or what a character is doing, something that's completely pointless in a visual medium like a video game where you can see everything going on. The narration especially holds the game back from having any personality considering every character is voiced by the same person. Why have voice acted dialogue if it all sounds the same? It doesn't help that I wasn't a fan of the voice actor's work anyway, as I quickly started wishing that there wasn't any voiced dialogue at all. Oh and as for my latter issue, it's just that I don't see people talking about this game in the future. I've heard so little about this game and the only reason I found it was because of my frequent stalking of new Steam releases. Never heard a peep out of it and that's surprising considering it appeared to be an Epic exclusive, so you'd think a year of being released would've generated more press. Also, kind of a bad thing that you can't rebind any of the keys. Had to use the arrow keys because the sprint button isn't meant for WASD at all.And that's all there really is to talk about with The Last Campfire. A short review for a short game. It's worth the small fee, but I don't think it would be worth any more. I think the game is fine, but it's nothing special.  I don't know, this game just didn't speak to me at all.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy simple leisurely games that lean more towards storytelling rather than battles, then this game is perfect!  Similar to games like Journey, Sky: Children of Light or even the new Jusant, it blends together simple puzzles with themes of overcoming grief, trauma and what may happen at 'end of life' in a calm and composed manner.  While these types of themes may not be for everyone, The Last Campfire does such a good job of presenting these heavier tones in ways that aren't too depressing or in your face; more so, I feel that the game makes players think about many different types of mental illnesses, grief, varying traumas and such and how people face them, whether it be the person themselves or their loved ones.Main Points:1) The game can be completed in as little as a few hours to a couple days, depending on how fast one wants to play.  If quick & easy games are your thing, than say no more!2) The other aspect of this game are its puzzles, which can be turned off in Explorer Mode.  However, in my own opinion after having played and completed the game, the puzzles make the game more entertaining.3) There are no battles, which makes this a very cozy and leisurely game that can be played at your own pace.  It only has an autosave feature, so be aware of that!4) For younger audiences, it would be a great way to present these otherwise heavier life themes, as they are inevitable and they will face them sooner or later.  Having a simple and calm game like this is a good way to open the path for discussion.5) I personally would not consider this game as having religious tones or themes, rather presenting its ideas on handling grief and traumas in a neutral manner, but it is open for interpretation as anything is. The characters are called 'embers' and their world is a 'place between places' where they all go to prepare before moving on to the next world.  What is that next world?  You may decide for yourself~Please pick up The Last Campfire and play it for yourself!

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Campfire is a really lovely game that has a poignant and touching story.Its greatest strength is that it's very atmospheric. The environments coupled with the music and narration create an engaging experience. A lot of the time I just played silently because I was captivated. The music is beautiful and is quite melancholic. There is one narrator who does all of the dialogue which makes it feel almost like a fable.The puzzles were well-integrated and fun. Some were challenging but never frustrating. You can also see if you're on the right path because snippets of narration will start playing! The characters are super charming and I'm in love with little Ember. The animation where Ember approaches a forlorn melts my heart. The character interactions show the importance of compassion.I think the story could be a  tighter. I'm not asking for it to be straightforward, as the slight ambiguity is good. But something that is open to interpretation can still be well-constructed.I think there could be additional parts to bring it more together - in particular, the characters and their personal stories, such as The Wanderer. Maybe some more cutscenes? There are scattered notes in hidden chests but these are optional for the player.Having said all that, I don't have a problem with the story overall. I guess I just wanted more, because I liked it a lot! I was absorbed the whole time.Definitely play this beautiful game!

_childDocuments_.review: A quirky little puzzle game albeit a bit short. The artwork has that cell shaded vibe to it that is popular in so many little indie games lately, and it was a treat to explore and work on puzzles in it. The puzzles range from the incredibly easy to the occasional head scratcher and to be honest I don't feel that they were balanced at all. Instead of saving the more difficult ones towards the end it mostly felt like I would trip over a difficult one at a random interval and be stuck for a few minutes while I figured it out.My only real big gripe is the camera is largely locked in. For a puzzle game that has hidden collectibles scattered around (although they're solely for lore and don't count towards achievements), it was frustrating to fight with the camera to see if there was anything actually hidden or if it was just an artistic way to hide a dead end.I played this puzzle game when I wanted a break from the more difficult games I picked up and ended up enjoying it. The ending had a lot more weight to it than I expected for a 4 hour game and it surprisingly tugged at my heartstrings. I think this would be a good beginning puzzle game to play with along kids or someone just getting into gaming. Its not going to take the gaming world by storm but it did leave me with a sense of fulfillment when I beat it.8.0/10.0

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lovely, wholesome delight. The graphics are adorable, the story is engaging and heartfelt, and the sound design was peaceful and enjoyable. None of the puzzles seemed too hard, though some were definitely harder than others. A few had my stumped for quite a long time, until I suddenly saw the answer and solved them right away. Others I solved instantly. So I think the difficulty sort of ranges depending on what kinds of puzzles are intuitive to the player and which aren't. Overall I loved playing through this. It tugged on my heart strings, challenged my brain, and made me smile. Can't ask for much more in a basic puzzling game. 4.5/5

name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III
detailed_description: Welcome to the New Class VII – Explore the newly annexed lands of the Empire with a brand new squad, and catch up with familiar faces from the past. An Immersive Story – Experience an epic story developed across three titles, and crafted for new and old fans alike. Also includes an interactive introduction to catch up new players to the ongoing story so anyone can dive right in to the world of Trails of Cold Steel. Combat Honed to a Fine Edge – Challenge oncoming threats with a combat system that has been refined over the course of decades. The addition of features like Brave Order and the Break System open up new possibilities in battle. Story Rean Schwarzer uncovers a dark plot that threatens his homeland. To face their enemies, he must prepare a new generation of heroes as an instructor at a new branch campus and guide them towards victory. Nearly a year and a half has passed since the Erebonian civil war, and much has changed since then. From the shifting stances of countries to the internal politics of the Empire, and even the life of Rean Schwarzer, the shadows of the past have given way to the embers of a new chapter. Now graduated from Thors Military Academy, Rean has become an instructor at the Thors Branch Campus, a newly-opened academy that quickly finds itself thrust onto the national stage. It is here that he takes the lead of a brand new Class VII, and must guide a new generation of heroes into an unknown future. Though all is calm now, the nefarious Ouroboros organization continues to weave a dark plot that could engulf the entire continent in war...or perhaps something even more sinister. Trails of Cold Steel III invites players into a world full of intrigue and excitement that is years in the making. They will embark on a whirlwind tour through the never-before-seen lands of the recently expanded Erebonian countryside, and encounter fresh faces as well as old friends familiar to fans of the series. In true Trails fashion, the deep, engaging story pairs with an incredible cast of characters and a combat system refined over decades of innovative RPG worldbuilding.

_childDocuments_.review: An unexpected gem with outstanding turn based combat. You have to LOVE Anime though. There are many plots, politics as well as spectacular fighting and various kinds of character interaction that impact team performance. Visual backgrounds are a little wooden but it's like being in a Japanese comic...or cartoon.  The story is quite good and refers back to the previous games. The characters are all interesting in their own way, especially NPCs. Looking forward to continuing.

_childDocuments_.review: Only 26 hours in and on Chapter 2 right now, but so far the game is already exceeding expectations. If you've been following the ongoing Legend of Heroes saga, this game builds on the previous storyline and brings in new characters, twists and turns. You get to visit a whole bunch of new places in Western Erebonia, and re-visit a certain BELOVED place Speaking of that, I HIGHLY recommend playing all the Trails games up til now, to ensure you get the proper experience. This is an extremely story-heavy game (I mean heck, if you play on Easy or Normal, it almost feels like a visual novel at times, with some occasional fights).These previous games are: the 3 Trails in the Sky games (although if you have to skip 3, it's not the end of the world), Trails of Cold Steel 1 and 2, Trails from Zero and Trails to Azure (Crossbell Duology).In my personal opinion, the Crossbell Duology is the BEST, story, pacing and gameplay-wise, out all the previous games. I'm really hoping Cold Steel 3 and 4 match my enjoyment from the Crossbell games... So far, 3 is definitely looking to do so, or even exceed them...I look forward to finishing this game and eventually enjoying Cold Steel 4. Worth every penny.It's a shame XSeed isn't localising the games anymore, but honestly, NISA has done an INCREDIBLE job. Apart from some minor text formatting issues (falling off the side of the textbox), I haven't noticed any issues yet. Great job, NISA. Honestly, the terminology, names, lore etc all seems pretty on point, and I haven't noticed any egregious changes to the meaning of dialogue. DON'T WORRY - the quality is fine.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III

_childDocuments_.review: Still on my way to catch up with Cold Steel and finally done with Cold Steel III!Since what makes me getting glued to Cold Steel until this point is its story, I'll focus my review on it.It's a bit of a bummer that I saw only a little of the (old) class VII given how the first two revolved around Rean and co, but the story introduced the new class VII well and I love the youngsters all the same. Also, I could understand this 3rd one put a considerable effort to blend the entire Kiseki Franchise together, with characters from other arcs come and go. Though at some point it feels rather forced and jam-packed.Still prefer the first and the second, but it's a great game all the same. So yes, 1+ from me.Now at last, onto Cold Steel IV. Here I go!
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III

_childDocuments_.review: *Pre-warning: Advise playing LoH: Trails of Cold Steel 1 & 2 prior to playing for better knowledge of backstory*One of the best RPG's I've played that so few people know about. As I mentioned before, if you are new to the series I would definitely play at least ToCS 1 & 2 first at least, maybe even Trails in the Sky.  Yes you can definitely play this as a stand alone RPG, but the biggest up side of this series is the amazing story line and arc.  Some of the character lines can be "cheesy" and over the top, but the story will definitely make you feel something.  The graphics are nice with only one spot that you felt a little graphics lag.  Characters are mostly interesting, and you'll find yourself wanting to find out more about who they are.  Crafts/Arts have a wide variety of choices.  Overall I'd say if you want a great story with some very solid gameplay, pick up the Legend of Heroes/Trails of Cold Steel games.  I would say right now the only downside is waiting for ToCS 4 to release for PC ^^;

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I would like to talk about the sadness I have felt towards this series for a long time. It hurts even as I write this review, but it's time for some facts to be understood. This review will be a harsh review. Actually, there is more I want to write, but the Steam character limit does not allow it.As someone who played Kuro no Kiseki 2 and played Ys X, I can say that Falcom's situation is not getting any better. Unfortunately, Falcom is in the process of collapse day by day. It is currently blacklisted in Japan because of Koto (Falcom's CEO) who mistreated his employees and dismantled JDK in a disastrous manner.The announced sales figures dropped so much that even the company's president, Kondo, said there was a possibility that they would stop making the Trails series. In fact, they are guilty of this and they are aware of it, but since it is a classic Japanese company, they see the fans as the culprit. Even fans in Japan can't get over Cold Steel betraying them. People are tired of Falcom's policy of a lot of money for little effort.The Cold Steel arc killed this series. Apart from the small number of anime enthusiasts who follow this series on Reddit, 4Chan, Falcom Discord and Twitter, there are not many real fans left.Let me make an explanation right away. The series is not improving. Unfortunately, there is no magic of the Sky and Crossbell eras. Reverie and Kuro 1 are good games, but they still feel like Cold Steel. Kuro 2 in particular is a complete freak. The other two games do not even come close to the quality of Crossbell and Sky.Falcom's decreasing quality day by day and its policy of making a lot of money with little effort ruined the entire Trails series. It even ruined the Ys series. Falcom is constantly lying to and milking their fan base. They never improved themselves. Now they just make and sell their games with the same formula under the same formula: cheap product = a lot of money. According to Kondo's statement, they are planning to release 4-5 games a year. Yes, you heard right. They are going to release 4-5 games a year! I laughed. That means 4-5 crappy games every year. We have a company that does not understand that the costs of game production have increased and that a game cannot be released once a year like in the 1990s and 2000s. Kondo says, if we want, we can release a game every 5-6 years, but we don't want to. He said he talked to his employees and they all complained about time and money. However, they make no effort to fix this situation. They will most likely play Kai no Kiseki, which is their last trump card. Even the name is strategic. If the series dies, it's a great place to leave it.As someone who is a fan of this series, this makes me very sad. So what actually went wrong? Let me tell you the whole truth. Let me also share the information I learned from Japanese forums.Crossbell was the pinnacle of this series and was a great game in many ways. Sky was just as great in the arc. The Cold Steel arc was originally planned to be even better than those two arcs, but the whole thing was ruined by Falcom's momentary greed for money. For the CS arc, Olivert was originally planned to be the main character. The outline of the entire scenario was written for Osborne and Olivert as a mature imperial adventure with political conflicts. Later, this idea was changed and it was decided to create a squad reminiscent of the Sky days. The popularity of the Sky arc was not as widespread as Crossbell, so they would have both introduced Sky and made a game as great as Sky. That was the plan. Alisa's prototype version was designed. She herself is a divine blade. In a way, she was a mix of Estelle and Anelace. Rean would be a side character. He himself was a combination of Joshua and Crow. He also held the rank of military officer. An adventure similar to Sky journey was planned. Later, this project was scrapped and the entire script was destroyed. In fact, this situation was revealed long ago. There are even some designs. So this event has been proven to be real. You can still officially access the images on the internet.Let's come to today. Falcom saw that the series with light novel isekai and harem genre concepts were selling well at that time. Because of this, Falcom destroyed the entire original script. At the same time, they wanted to take advantage of Marvel's popularity while making CS3 and CS4. Because of this, Rean was made the main character and given all the cliché traits you can see. Actually, Trails always had its tropes and problems, but it got out of hand in the CS arc. The reason for this was because of this situation. The aim was to attract horny Japanese teenagers to the series by marketing Rean. This was somewhat successful, but Falcom killed the series for the sake of marketing Rean in every game. Every arc they tried to praise Rean enough and remind him of how special he is. Rean didn't start out as a Mary Sue, but he became one by the end of his journey. At the same time, because Falcom lowered the age audience, they made everyone look as sweet as possible.Even Bleublanc is an incredibly sweet person in this game. They turned this maniac, who even wanted to sexually assault Kloe in Sky games, into a sweet man. Every CS game got worse. 3 and 4 are retcom games that ultimately serve nothing. At the same time, New Class 7 is officially a disaster. There is something wrong with the brains of those who love them. Old Class 7 were the best cast with great backgrounds but Falcom ruined them. New Class 7 also damaged the entire story and lore but people took the bait.Actually, I want to explain the reasons one by one, but as I said, the character limit is not enough. In the end, it all came down to a cosmic evil, an evil Gundam war. The CS arc constantly damaged the story of all previous arcs with fake information. Characters like neither Towa nor Juna existed in previous games, but they added them just because they ruined the lore. Kuro 1 is still not a mature and well-established game, it's just mature CS. There are many things it does right, but it is still far from the quality of Sky and Crossbell. At the same time, Kuro 2 was a mistake. Actually, I could write a tens-page review for all of these, but the character limit is not enough.In summary, after the CS betrayal, Kuro games did not catch on in Japan. Falcom urgently needs to modernize. The games developed by Falcom fell far behind the standards of our age. Modern gaming standards are not like that. I would write down the mistakes in Falcom's games one by one and point out what they need to fix, but it's still the character limit problem. To be specific, Falcom is in the process of collapse and will most likely close down. Kai no Kiseki is their final trump card. None of Falcom's games started selling more than 40,000 units. This is a huge decline. They will either change course and focus on cheap gacha games or close down completely. This seems to be the case. At best, they will turn to new series and start to come to their senses, but after the betrayal of the Trails series, there is a serious loss of trust. This is now a difficult possibility. Anyway, constantly meeting with Gacha companies is not a good sign. Now Falcom wants to make fake waifu games. To summarize, there is wrong things with this company. It's a shame, but let's accept this fact. Trails to Azure was the last great Trails game we got.Kondo even refrained from making a statement to shareholders at the shareholder meeting. They are now seriously in their final stages.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily my favorite entry in the series so far. It's everything you can expect from Trails and Falcom. Amazing music, great cast, fun gameplay and a solid story with twists that will leave your jaw on the floor. This game made Rean my favorite MC in the series with how well he's fleshed out. New Class VII are an amazing cast with how they bounce off each other, I've never enjoyed a group this much since Azure.The gameplay is a bit wacky with how Nightmare is a decent challenge for the first half of the game and being too easy in the second half.I was expecting the switch of publishers to NISA to be jarring, but surprisingly this is a pretty solid localization with a lot of QoL improvements.And despite the game being the longest in the series so far, it doesn't drag on for more than necessary. Each event is well spent in serving the characters and the narrative, plus the first three chapters feel like a love letter to each of the arcs that came before, rewarding players that invested their time in this series in release order.And that ending.... THE ENDINGDefinitely one of my favorites in any game I've played and hyped up me so much for the conclusion.
