_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III is a direct continuation from Cold Steel II, so it's important that ->  before going into III.I saw this common question a lot of times on steamboards.This game is also a continuation for Zero no Kiseki (Trails of Zero) duology, which was never officially translated. Let's hope that NISA will bring them over, they are amazing games, both Zero and Ao. Thus, if you never played Zero, you will miss a backstory for all Crossbell characters, like Randy Orlando and if you never played Sky trilogy, you will miss backstory for Tita, Agate and many others. It's not critical, but pretty interesting to known. Playstation 4 release was in October-2019 and we got a PC port here in March-2020, quite fast, i'd say. , which many of you remember, because he was also involved in CSI & CSII PC ports and some other games. He also created a DSFix for original Dark Souls and let's be honest, was the only one option to play DSI normally on PC, since the basic port quality was atrocious at best. (Awful/pixelated graphics, no keyboard+mouse support and many other things, it was probably the worst PC port ever done by Namco Bandai)The PC port quality is pretty good, there's a lot of additional graphic options, great KB+M/gamepad support and the usual important features like x3-x6 speed. Also, each graphic options contains a detailed commentary.: you can perfectly play with Keyboard + Mouse or any type of controller/gamepad. Even a chinese Logitech copy from 2004 works perfectly (aside from "Vibration", but i don't care about that, personally), but actually it's done by the same people, who worked on Cold Steel I & II, both translators and voice actors. So, kudos to them for doing this amazing hard work (CS III contains a gigantic script, it's not an easy task).Now, let's move to While it's my speculation, but it's kinda obvious either way. Falcom wanted to reach a bigger audience and NISA offered them a few things:- More language localizations, at this point Cold Steel III also translated for French users.- A Nintendo Switch ports.- Better promotion/advertisement/etc.  and if they will start to do that, it will heavily impact development of other titles. They learned that from making Playstation 4 ports for Cold Steel I & II and they said it will be the last ports from them.While i do love and respect XSeed, we can't deny that those "terms" from NISA are better. Well, anyway, a change with publisher didn't affect this game and we still got an amazing entry in the series with a proper translation.Since it's a direct sequel, the game skip about one year after the ending of Cold Steel II. Specifically, it skips the annexation of North Ambria (after Crossbell) and some other Crossbell stuff. After graduating from Thors Military Academy and doing various war missions as his father's pawn, Rean Schwarzer arrived at a new established Thors Academy Military Branch campus, which turns out is something like a "prison" for all the dangerous/rebellious individuals, some of them was your enemies in previous games. Of course, this goes with a bonus of the most dangerous missions, since the safety of those campus people is a non-concern for higher ups. Rean is given a position of instructor for a "New Class VII", which  at the start will only contain 3 members, it will grow bigger overtime, but i'l stop here since more is a spoiler. i'm gonna assume that you played CSI & II so gonna cover only the new/reworked stuff.- Since tha game was developed for Playstation 4 this time around, the graphics are much better, especially character models. - the Overdrive mechanics got completely removed and there's no save data transfer bonuses, as it was with CSI & II.- New much more powerfull field attack is introduced, you can launch it in the monster face and initiate a TRIPLE ADVANTAGE bonus at the start of the fight. The downside is that you can't spam it and you can only hold 2 uses at a time. In order to refill the gauge, you need to break objects or initiate battles with simple field attacks. - Brave Order system is introduced, which use your BP for teamwide strong buffs, like +20% damage for 8 turns or -50% damage received for 6 turns. However, if you're gonna use BP for Brave Orders, you will be unable to use big Rush attacks, since those are also consume BP, so choose depending on the situation.- Break Guard system is introduced, which is, basically, a free stun + bonus damage + 100% unbalance proc combined. Activates after you deplete (by pretty much anything) the enemy's Break Gauge.- Bosses will extremely power-up themselves at low HP or if certain conditions are met, so it's wise to use your Limit Break S-Crafts to finish the bosses, instead of using them right away at the start of the battle.- Fishing was reworked and now DOESN'T HAVE A LIMIT and provide a pretty amazing rewards, like U-Materials or bunch of various Quartz. Heck, you can fish up 99 U-Materials right at the start of the game in Chapter I in the town river. Get this Snow Crab ^ for some EZ U-Materials, x3 per one Crab.- Use a cooking trick, to make some easy Mira at the start of the game for fishing and equipment.- You can use two Master Quarts now, which is straight up gay (aka overpowered). - You can skip every cutscene/dialogue, no exceptions. (HOOOORAY!)- More stuff that i'm lazy to mention.Cold Steel III is an amazing continuation for a famous RPG series, which is much more prettier now due to native PS4 development this time around (previously CSI & CS II was originally for PS3/PSVita). With a thrilling story, better graphics and superb soundtrack & characters, it's one of the best RPG experiences out there.- This review was presented to you by "Casual Game Reviews" Steam Curator.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Free Weekend review and I only have experience with Tokyo Xanadu eX+ before this game. I have tried the game and played through its prologue chapters and finishing the first labyrinth, so what are my first impressions of the game and its series?First and foremost, since I am new to the series, playing the 3rd game I expected myself to not knowing a ton of stuff that went before the 3rd game starts. I was right to assume that we are playing as students of a military school ala FF Type 0, with the mentor / senior / teachers mostly being formerly playable characters. A friend of mine told me that the 3rd is a new arc in a new perspective after playing as Rean in the 1st and 2nd game. I was shown a picture of probably their own school uniforms hinting at their past adventures prior to becoming seniors. Furthermore, since coming from Tokyo Xanadu,  the artstyle is exactly the same with buttery smooth framerates as well so there's that sense of familiarity. Oh, and be prepared to hear lots of dialogue too. Nihon Falcom might just be famous / infamous for it. You can skip them though.Comparing to Tokyo Xanadu, I noticed that the ARCUS's Quartz system is exactly the same as Gear system in UI alone. However, unlike that game, alongside passives, some are equippable as "magic spells" aka Materia of FF7. Attacking builds up CP which then allows us to perform Arts and then if built up further allows players to perform their ultimate flashy attacks. Fair enough. The battle is turn-based and uses spatial positioning to strategize various AoE attacks to hit as many targets as possible, and avoid clumping together unless broken. Imo, the battle system is very solid and allows for some great aha and shock moments in every battle. I'm very sure there's a ton more depth to find but I can't do that in my short time. There's also moments like the Link system and character hotswapping moments too that battles can make you feel like a genius when your tactics pay off. I'd say Falcom achieved their magnum opus of player engagement here.If there's one thing I gathered from playing a slice of this game on the free weekend, it's that it's worthy of one of the best JRPGs in terms of gameplay alone. Story is 2nd as it can get too long at times. I don't know if the game has actual romance but coming from Tokyo Xanadu? I doubt it. So it's not exactly a dating sim in my eyes (I can be wrong), but I'm sure there'll be cute moments here and there. 9/10. Would recommend on discount if you're looking for a new JRPG to sink into. Make sure you start from the 1st though.

_childDocuments_.review: "Ah, okay then. The only suitable punishment for that is D E A T H "-Rean, the siscon===============================Cold steel 3 for PC is finally here. Needless to say, it's highly recommended to play at the very least previous two CS games before starting this one, though IMO you might want to start from Sky trilogy then Crossbell duology before starting CS. It's a direct sequel of CS 2. taking place about 2 years after the ending of CS 2. I already waited for the release of CS 3 for PC from the moment I finished CS 2 and directly put a pre order the moment of their steam page was up, so my expectation for CS 3 is big. Although there are some flaw here and there as I playing, I can say that overall I'm very satisfied with playing through the whole CS 3.(+)- Let's start with the translation quality because some of the recent NISA game have a bad quality at launch (one of them is YS8). Actually, I was kinda doubting about their works with CS 3 because of this, and XSEED did a very good job dealing with CS 1 and CS 2 TL quality. Turned out I was worried over nothing. The translation and localization quality is actually as good as I remember.- The game is HUGE. Your playing time can easily get past the 100 hours mark in one playthrough, though about half of that is from talking no NPC and other character while you are touring the town everytime the plot progressing. - Beautiful town detailed setting. Each of the town you'll visit have their own unique style and people, making touring through each town is a new experience and never a bore- The main cast, NPCs and character dialogue is as good as ever, if not better. If you are into this in previous trails series, you'll enjoy it even more in CS 3. - Improved animation. While it is still kinda stiff here and there, it is still a huge upgrade from CS 2- Good soundtrack, but IMO it is not as memorable as CS 1 and CS 2. Also I'm glad I can finally hear the super arranged The Decisive Collision in that epic moment, really hyping up the battle. Sadly, the in game battle of that scene is literally a joke even on high difficulty. - Low specs friendly. I only have a mid-end laptop and can easily run the game with medium preset at 60 FPS consistently without a single crash. The only FPS drop I ever get is in walking in the mid of the certain city because it is a biggest area of part of the city in the game with so many detailed building, furniture, and NPC.- All of the PC exclusive feature from the previous CS 1 and 2 is still in CS 3: turbo mode, last save load, graphic setting, dual language, etc(-)- The problem in CS 2 is somewhat still lingers in CS 3. You can probably guess it by the first two of that kind of scene after beating a certain major enemies. By the next similar scene you'll already go with 'Ah, here we go again' and start cringing. Seriously, can't they put the event like that in, like, literally any other way? Well, at least now you really beat the crap out of the enemies in the end instead they are going with 'haha not bad, but it's not even my 10% of power' and you suddenly getting help from a bigshot out of nowhere. - Some of the scene can be a cringe fest but hey, it's a JRPG- Bland dungeon and open field. The same problem like previous game.- Though they somewhat rebalance the previous battle system, like nerfing evasion and delay even further, or nerf certain craft, they introduce an easily abuseable new mechanic called Break and Order. Sure, it seems balanced at the early stage of the game, but later on, not even the so called 'strongest' enemy have a speck of chance under the right setup. It is more broken in another sense than delay or evasion abuse, (~)- The bonding event is still the same as usual. That's mean you can still romance one of your former classmate and ignore the 'canon' one. Well, I heard it is still that way even on CS 4- Some of scene can be too long and a drag, so if you are looking for more fight and action, you are probably choosing a wrong game. Though it is questionable that you can handle the problem in previous game but not in CS 3- The storyline and plot is a bit slow, but still good. They kinda rushed it at the end with most of the answer is dumped into a single scene full of narration though. Also, they give us another massive cliffhanger, arguably worse than Sky 1 or CS 1. ======================I highly recommend this game ( or more like the entire series ) if you have a thing for JRPG. If you love CS 1 and 2, then there is no reason to not play CS 3 at all. If you are interested in this game but you haven't playing any other one before, you might want to start with previous title first. Now gotta start the second playthrough soon~

_childDocuments_.review: The key point of this game and highlight, is the story. It is rich in the story aspect of it, to be expected from a Trails game. The desire to know more of what's happening and all the hidden plots and agenda kept me playing.10/10 if you are a Trails fan. I'd like to compare this to the Marvel Cinematic Universe, with CS3 being Avengers: Infinity War.I do find certain parts a bit cringe, but this is nitpicking at best and is overshadowed by its large brilliant plot.Introduction of a new system known as Brave Order brings about tons of new combination... to break the game. Overdrive was removed. Nonetheless, it is rather refreshing and frankly, I see essence of bringing it to more contemporary styles. Still turn-based, with the Quartz system though.Has Quality of Life features, Japanese voices, turbo, and an auto-save function. Excellent on this front again, just like the previous Trails. Step Ahead, Sword of Biting Gale and Spiral of Erebos among the ones that stood out to me.If you are a Trails fan, this is an auto-get. Bewarned though, the ending will leave you wanting more. Way more. To the point you might want to wait closer to Trails of Cold Steel IV release if you have not started. Such an agonising cliffhanger.If you are not a Trails fan, wants to try it and is not an old-school gamer, start with Trails of Cold Steel I. The older games might be off-putting in terms of gameplay/graphics that it overshadows the story for you.If you are not a Trails fan, wants to try it and is an old-school gamer, go back all the way to Trails in the Sky.If you are not a Trails fan, and only want to try this game, you are likely going to have tons of questions. To get the maximum immersion, you will need to have played some if not all of the previous games to have an appreciation of to the plot being slowly revealed to you, as the player. _childDocuments_.review: Trails of Cold Steel 3 is a great game and there is a lot to enjoy, but it isn't super friendly to newcomers of the Trails series.The Good:-Story: I enjoyed the story a lot. The plot is very much intertwined with previous games of the series, which I think gives it more depth. I will say that since it is part of a 4 part saga, it doesn't hold up well as a standalone story, but that isn't really the purpose of it.-Characters: The characters are one of the best part of the game and series as a whole. The new class VII has a great variety of likable characters with lots of personality and there are also a lot of returning characters from previous games.-Music: Another strongpoint of the game. The ost for this game is very pleasent to listen to and strikes a good balance between peaceful orchestral music and impacful action music.-Turbo mode: This game has a great additional feature called turbo mode, which allows you to speed up cutsenes, dialogue, and movement in combat and the overworld, which can be useful if you're in a hurry. -Combat: The combat in Cold Steel 3 plays similarly to its predecessors, but with additional features such as the brave orders and the break gauge, which can make the game a lot more interesting and complex.-Difficulty: The game is as hard as you want it to be, with multiple difficulty settings that can be changed in-game (unless you are playing nightmare mode). The Bad:-Not for new people: This game is the third in it's series arc, not including the previous 5 games that came before the Cold Steel series (Sky and Crossbell). The game assumes you have a general understanding of most of the events in the previous games, so if you're new YOU WILL BE CONFUSED as to what is going on. -Anime Tropes: There are a lot of rather cliche anime tropes in this game. While that isn't inherently "bad" (and it is a JRPG, what do you expect?), it may be a deal-breaker for some.-The story isn't self-contained: Self-explanatory.Overall, I absolutely loved playing Cold Steel 3, but be aware that this is the 3rd game out of a 4 game series, which is also a part of a larger ongoing story. Because of this, I can't recommend it to players that haven't at least played Cold Steel 1 and 2. If this game looks interesting to you for story reasons, I would first recommend trying out Cold Steel 1.

_childDocuments_.review: A tentative recommendation. It's definitely better than the previous Cold Steels, but is nowhere close to the heights of Sky or Zero/Azure. The school setting is a lot more tolerable in this entry since you're a teacher rather than a student, and combat isn't as horrendously cheesable as CS2, at least until chapter 3 or so when you get Scorpio. Then the game devolves into Sledgehammer -> Chrono Burst/AT Accelerate spam to kill basically every boss before they get a chance to act a 2nd time. Still manages to be more engaging than CS2's click 1 or 2 juiced up s-break to win tho. Not a fan of Rean as a protagonist but Juna is my goat for basically straight up saying Zero/Azure were goated and Cold Steel sucks LMAO. The majority of the old Class VII redesigns are pretty good, even if there are a few stinkers like Alisa and Fie (granted I've never been a fan of either to begin with). Overall I did like story, but at the same time am feeling character/plot thread bloat. There are a lot of QoL additions to this entry as well, being able to trade for high rarity equipment is nice even if a bit too costly. Most quests and events are marked on the map this time around, which lessens the need for a guide substantially even if you'll still want one for character notebook entries. The addition of Break and Orders to the combat system do make the loop more engaging and satisfying compared to CS1-2's barebones BP system, although they are a large factor in being able to break the game rather easily (the other being the aforementioned Chrono Burst now being able to chain into itself for some reason to give infinite turns with enough EP recovery). Divine Knight battles still suck, but are better with the addition of more playable mechs. And finally, a big negative on Chapter 4 requiring so much inventory management with so many playable characters being used simultaneously. Overall a mid experience, but an improvement over the past 2 entries.

_childDocuments_.review: I guess the movement control order during this past few weeks are a good excuse for me to catch up on the Kiseki series. Even though Cold Steel 3 has been out for a few months now on the PS4, it is only been recently that it came out for the PC. Woot!The game continues after a one year time skip from the end of Trails of Cold Steel 2, where Rean has decided to become an instructor at the branch campus of Thors Military Academy at Leeves. Initially I was like, 'A school setting again? Come on..." but it's actually quite refreshing as you return this time not as a student, but as an instructor. It's kinda fun watching the students grow up and become kinda dependable especially the new Class VII. I eventually grew quite fond of them, even much more than the old Class VII as they kinda act like guest party members in this game, so it's a bit hard to get all chummy with them again. Especially when you have only one bonding event with them throughout the whole game! And no, the festival events do not count. <Sighs>. I guess there's no helping it as they are just too many characters now that can join your party.‌The battle system is largely similar to the past games with some differences. The minor ones are like S-Craft feels a bit underwhelming now, so you cannot do 4 S-Crafts in a row at the start of the battle and win like in the previous games. (Well you still can, but you have to work a bit for it.) And if you have not managed to kill the boss after that, you are somewhat doomed as all bosses (well, the noteworthy ones) will go to a berserk state where they will remove all their debuffs, hit a lot harder, do their own S-Craft, or even worse, heal themselves. God. But you cannot whittle their HP bit by bit as they will still enter this state after they lost a certain percentage of their HP. Haha. Attrition battles are NOT recommended for this game.However, the berserk state is not to be feared completely; they are now more susceptible to 'break'. What is this 'break', you ask? Well, there is a new meter below the enemies' health meter that when emptied, the enemies are considered 'broken' which will lead to their buffs being dispelled and them unable to act during their turns. Hence, try to break them if it is possible but be cautious whenever the enemies' turns are nearing as they are in a berserk state after all. (The Lance Maiden instakilled using her own S-Craft after my party tried breaking her using S-Breaks; T_T Thank god for the Sophia master quartz).Besides break, there is another feature that is implemented in the game to help you fight healing bosses: Brave Orders. Remember those points you get when you managed to unbalance enemies by using the correct weapon type in the earlier Cold Steel games? Now you can use them to execute Brave Orders, which is used to give certain beneficial effects to the party INSTANTLY. Yes, you read that right. Need a strength buff before hitting the boss? There is an order for that. Want to heal? Also covered. Increased critical hit chance and damage? Yup, it's there. Accelerate your allies turns and repeat so you can have endless turns against the boss? My personal favorite. As long as you keep farming those Brave Points, hey, who's stopping you from killing the boss without it getting a turn?To conclude this review, this is a great game to play but feels kinda like a tease especially with THAT cliffhanger at the end of the game. For those who are on the fence about buying this game or just want to preserve your sanity, I will suggest for you to wait until next year as NISA already announced that Trails of Cold Steel 4 will be coming out then. _childDocuments_.review: Succeeds at what Cold Steel 1 originally promised.As a teacher this time, you take your kids on field trips around the western parts of the country, establishing setting and character very effectively at the same time. All the new characters are very likable, and even the side characters are a major step-up from the first game.Sadly of course, there's a catch. Absolutely nothing happens this entire game until the last 10 hours, but the game isn't confident enough in it's character writing to carry you there (understandably so due to the sheer length of this game). This means every chapter you get major villains just doing nothing causing ruckus, only to act coy and elude to setting up some larger plan. If the characters don't grab you and you only got this far into Trails because of the overarching story, you're absolutely boned as this will be the slowest 100 or so hours you'll ever experience. However, I still feel like this is the best of the Cold Steel games simply because of how it feels to play. There's no pressure, no grand threats and you just get some time to let Rean and both old and new Class VII explore Erebonia, learning more about both the world and themselves while they do it.tldr:Great characters and worldbuilding, extremely slow story.

_childDocuments_.review: Forget the combat (which will be boring after doing it 1k times), the graphics (which is a huge leap down in performance), the art (where the lazywork means they actually reused art from game 2 for secondary characters like Elise and Alfin and went with their 15 y.o. "versions"), the most important part of the game is the story! It's JRPG after all. Now, about that..Writing and the plot became utterly hopeless because they went down the trope leading nowhere. Even the amateur writer will know that:- . When you squeeze all of your story into a single act, it becomes very hard to digest and almost impossible to grasp. And no, appearance of some characters in prior chapters speaking riddles noone will understand doesn't count as a "story". You're kept in dark 4 chapters and the story is barely dragging its feets. Then in the last moment it becomes painfully obvious there's too little time for too much stuff to explain.- . Having too much going on does not equal good story. All of these different groups and an attempt to maintain 3 or 4 different plots in parallel leads to confusion, distraction and in the end lack of time to actually include anything properly for any of them. If they wanted to depict proper political ploys and games, they would need to have all 4 acts to be filled with real meaningful story dedicated to each and every group, their goals, how they interact, their motives and so on. But that's too much work I guess. So all that political muscle flexing looks very shallow in the end.- . When you have to pull out stunts , you know the plot is beyond salvation and your writing has failed. In this game they made it so that everything happened in game 2 is of no - or at most, very little - concern. Kind of the same what they did in game 2 with respect to game 1, but on a much larger scale. Having stunts like these completely nullifies the value of decisions, tradeoffs, sacrifices and even characters - past or future.- . Game 4 plot is doomed. If they pull out more stunts with stuff like  or time travel (I wouldn't be surprised at this point), then it's just won't be believable and they will need to unmake the game 3, i.e. everything prior to game 4 won't matter. If they don't pull out any stunts - then the plot is what it is and to avoid too many spoilers.. it's not great and goes against the very agenda they try to push (which is "yay, teamwork and friendship trump everything!")And there are other issues I would call "minor", but it's only because of the huge issues above they pale to compare to. To name the few:- . A lot of issues with it. For once, it's impossible to believe it. Rean being almost bullied by his students with no response. And actually, why does he run with his class, is he a student? Sara didn't bother, so? Next, what's the point of all the Ashen Chevallier fuss  And that's just a fraction of issues with only Rean. If I include his students and former class 7 and the others.. it will be a 5 pages review.- . I told it in game 1 and 2 and I'm telling it in game 3: if the fight is intended to be a lost one - make it a cutscene. To game 3 defense - they have almost no mechanically unwinnable battles (i.e. when in the game combat the boss will OHK you no matter what you do). But they actually managed to make the whole thing even worse! Now you can beat the boss, obliterating it in 1 - 2 turns and it doesn't matter because the very next cutscene the boss is wiping the floor with you and another rescue saves the day- .  It seems the writers are confused in their own plot and can't figure out any direction nor motivation for own characters.- . Its when there's the "woops" moment. I.e. when what happened or told is impossible, even with stunts they presented so far. - . There are times for it and there are not. The writers are really pushing their luck here.  - . They try to keep it complex but in the end, there's only one trope for the story. It's a JRPG so it's fine, but then there's no need to hide it behind all of that complexity. You might as well sit back and relax, the outcome will be exactly the same. Heck, even very minor things like  . To be fair, railroading is the issue in both game 1 and 2, but in this game it's blatantly obvious after the last boss fight. The game denies you from any kind of achievement. No matter how much you invest into characters, no matter how good you perform, the story will go where it goes and there's nothing you can do.In the end, game 3 is very, very different from game 2 and even more so from game 1. Sure, game 1 has an edge of novelty, but the story there was leagues ahead. Engaging, but not overcomplicated, no stunts, feeling of achievement, characters with at least a glimpse of goals and motivation etc etc etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Trails of Cold Steel III is an excellent continuation to the previous two games of the series. If you enjoyed any of the other The Legend of Heroes games, then you will also likely enjoy Cold Steel 3. That being said, this game does not seem to be meant to be understandable as a stand-alone game since many story references require knowledge from games earlier in the Trails series. Thus, .Similar to previous games, the major characters are endearing and grow throughout the game while the minor characters also have their own amusing little stories. Additionally, the previous Class VII characters have also developed to become more mature and responsible. Unfortunately, the previous class VII characters are usually only available for a limited amount of chapters and you are only consistently able to use half of the new Class VII characters. As for the story itself, it is fairly slow paced and only starts to ramp up towards the end of the game. We finally are given some answers to many of the important questions that were left unanswered in the previous two games and it all wraps up into a very climactic finish.Players are no longer able to simply end most boss fights with full S-craft rotations. Instead, a new "break" bar has been added to enemies that allows for repeated link attacks once an enemy's "break" bar is depleted. When used in conjunction with the "break" system, the new "brave orders" allow for extremely powerful combinations that are reminiscent of the delay spam that was possible in Cold Steel I. Overall, I would rate combat to be a significant improvement over the previous two iterations, though it definitely has a slightly steeper learning curve.To my untrained ears, the music is fitting for the location but not particularly outstanding. I definitely have no complaints about the music quality, as it is just as good as it has always been, but you will probably not remember it years down the road. As for the graphics, as far as I can tell it is a decent upgrade over the previous two games. Similar to the music, the graphics are hardly mind-blowing but they are definitely good.Everything is now visible on the map, so it is far harder to miss any optional quests or other optional tasks. Additionally, the buffer for max rank AP is even larger than it was previously. Best of all, you no longer need to break your keyboard (or controller) and fingers to catch the end-game fish. If you enjoyed the previous Trails games, then Cold Steel 3 is worth every penny. The only regret that you will be left with is your progressively emptier wallet as you get ready to shell out for Cold Steel 4 in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game (8.5/10). For me, probably the best JRPG not named Persona or made by SquareEnix in recent years. Trails is a great series to pick up if you are looking for more JRPG goodness but have already finished the more mainstream games. Trails of Cold Steel combines exciting turn based combat with an epic story spanning 9 games! Trails of Cold Steel 3 improves on the honestly lackluster visual aesthetic from Trails of Cold Steel 1 or 2, streamlines the gameplay with additional quality of life improvements, and begins to tell the story on a much larger scale than previous games. I really enjoyed the story, even when I was rolling my eyes or cringing at some of the dialogue (it basically is just your typical shonen anime).But be warned: don't start with this game. Don't start with Trails of Cold Steel I even. A good analogy would be that this game is sort of like Infinity War in the MCU. Even if you started with Trails of Cold Steel I, that would be like watching only the Captain America movies before Infinity War, not having seen Thor, Black Panther, and so on. You would be missing out on countless details, inside jokes, etc if you haven't started with Trails in the Sky. I made this mistake when I first played this game: even though I started with Trails of Cold Steel, I was pretty lost for this particular game, since this game really begins to bring the whole story together. Also, the gameplay actually doesn't change all that much between entries, but it changes enough to keep you from getting bored of it (or at least it did for me). That is like 500 hours of gameplay though so...I hope you have a lot of time on your hands.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so.Regarding this 3rd game. If you're a fan of the series like I am, you will unquestionably like it. I do however recommend that newcomers play the Crossbell and the Trails in the Sky arcs, or there will be characters and concepts you might not understand. There is however a summary on the title screen that tells you about the previous 2 games in the Cold Steel series if you need the info, along with a library in-game regarding concepts found in-game.Now, graphic-wise, this is a step up from the past 2 games, as you may have guessed. There's always some clipping with the hair and arms depending on the character's positions, but that's a minor offense.Gameplay-wise, there are new "battle orders" which are basically character-based buffs that last for a determined amount of turns, which help you turn the tide or destroy things much faster. A new mechanic has also been added, based around "Breaking" foes, which makes them take more damage, among other things.Sound-wise, the music has some catchy songs as usual, some are returnees from past games too, which may or may not pull at your heartstrings, depending on the scene. Now, I've played the game in English text with both Japanese and English voice acting, and perhaps it's just an impression of mine, but the English voice not only sometimes seems louder at the same volume, but also has... Some kind of reverb? Could be just me. It's the one minor reproach that I could give this game.Story-wise, this is set 2 years (1 and a half) after the events of Cold Steel 2. Rean has graduated and has signed up as an instructor in a newly-built branch of his beloved Thors Military Academy. There he encounters new faces, some old ones, and works towards the betterment of the Empire in his own way. Whereas the first 2 games took you across the Eastern half of the Empire, most of this one will take you in the Western part of it, where you'll meet old foes and new ones. Going further would spoil the game, so I'll let you discover it.Regarding controllers, I've played this game entirely with my keyboard. I would have liked to use my Saitek Cyborg Rumblepad, but not only is it not supported by Steam anymore, even x360 (a third-party app) had trouble with the camera and some buttons would compound 2 functions. =/ Such issues were also present within the 2nd game, but not within the first. Regardless, you are warned.All in all, it was a good time. Good reveals, more questions. Even on nightmare difficulty (NG+), it wasn't too hard as long as you know what you're doing. Enjoy this and await with bathed breath the 4th game which will come next year (on PC anyway)!

_childDocuments_.review: Trails of Cold Steel III and IV are probably the least-accessible Trails game to newcomers, despite how it's been advertised. Cold Steel 3 is the eight game in the "Legend of Heroes: Trails" series, and despite being called Cold Steel 3, I'd argue it is more accurate to call it a sequel to the Crossbell arc (Which itself was a sequel to Sky.) Despite that, I think the game does make efforts to make it more accessible. While it still follows Rean from the Cold Steel games, it introduces a new Class VII as his students. One of these new students being a resident of Crossbell, allowing them to explain things fairly naturally. No matter what though, here is a lot of stuff in this game that not only spoils earlier titles, but you would get the most emotional impact if you played the others first. They more or less completely recreated a decent chunk of Crossbell in this game (including most of it's NPC's.)I am someone that did play all of them in release order, so going to give my perspective on this game. That said, if you are absolutely committed to playing just the Cold Steel games, I'll go ahead and try to pitch this.To begin, if you liked Cold Steel 1, basically this game returns to the school format from the first game, only with Rean as a teacher this time. This game largely is structured like the first Cold Steel, but with a major difference. There are less chapters, but they managed to greatly expand the writing and length of both the school and Field study sections.Despite being a soft-reboot in some areas with this game, you will be gradually introduced to characters both from the previous Cold Steel games, as well as the aforementioned Sky and Crossbell arcs. This game's plot continues to escalate to a level of intensity that even the previous game didn't go to. Ouroboros, the villains of the entire series, take center stage for most of this game, throwing a dream team of lots of villains that you've fought in games prior. Because of this, there are some crazy boss fights that really mean a lot to someone who is a massive fan of the series.Now, to talk about my personal opinions. I didn't like the school sections in Cold Steel 1, and I don't really like the school sections in this game either. These school sections, like I said are very very long. Not to mention, it is largely faithful to Cold Steel 1's structure, featuring a combat fort that is basically this game's abandoned schoolhouse.But the field studies were all pretty amazing in my opinion, with the plot escalating in scale fairly early, and only continues to do exciting things chapter to chapter. Chapter 2 being a huge highlight for any fan of Crossbell. But, they also do go on for a little too long too. With each chapter altogether taking around 20-30 in-game hours for completionists. The combat also got a lot of changes since the last game. Newly added are shield meters on enemies, putting them in a break state if you manage to deplete them. This delays their turns, and makes it so enemies cannot act when their turn comes. Alongside this are Orders which use brave points to give temporary boosts to your party members. I actually like both of these additions a lot, and add options that increase the amount of strategies you can employ. That said.....These new features seriously have balancing problems. Most notably, you can kill entire bosses and never give them a turn if you have the right orders. It is incredibly unbalanced, but I think most players won't figure out how to do this. Cold Steel 4 uses this same system, but rebalanced it to not be so much in the player's favor. Still, I do like the additions.All in all, I feel the simplest way to sum up this game is Cold Steel 1 but bigger, more intense, while setting up a high-stakes finale in the sequel. Wish it wasn't so easy to break, but hey that's what challenge runs are for. I think every Cold Steel game gets better with each game, and I hope you enjoy it :)

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I want to give you my experience of playing Trails Of Cold Steel 3 PC (TOCS 3 PC). The last time I played Trails Of Cold Steel 2 was back in 2018. It has been two years and I forgot many things from the series. The names that I remembered when I first playing TOCS 3 is the main character, Rean, the Instructor Sarah, and definitely FIE!. But I’m glad that there’s a backstory feature inside the game to refresh my mind and try to remember the story and the characters from the previous games in order to catch up to TOCS 3. The gameplay and the combat mechanic of Trails Of Cold Steel 3 are still great, just like the previous games. I liked the combat mechanic and enjoyed it. It's engaging and challenging for me. The music is also really great for me. Music in Falcom games are great and it's another reason why I play Falcom games.So far, I enjoyed playing Trails Of Cold Steel 3 PC on my Gaming Laptop. I’m on 22 hours playing TOCS 3 PC (just finished Chapter 1). I play the game on Asus TUF FX 505DD with Ryzen 5 3550H, GTX 1050 3GB VRAM, and 16GB of RAM. I mostly play the game on High Preset and 720p resolution. I capped the FPS to 30 FPS because for me 30 FPS is enough (maybe it’s different for you) when playing a JRPG. But in that setting, I could get around 30-60 FPS when I change the FPS limit to 60 FPS. The game doesn’t have major performance problems, unlike other PC port games that NISA published (you know I’m talking about Ys VIII port problems). I want to give props to Durante and his PH3 Games team for porting Trails Of Cold Steel 3 PC and for me, it’s a good PC port and the game is running well on my Gaming Laptop.I also appreciate that the game still gives a Portable preset so that there’s still a chance for low-end PC gamers to play TOCS3. Props again to Durante and his PH3 teams for making the game still be able to be played on a Low-End Laptop. I tested the game on my Low-End Laptop, Asus X455LJ with Intel Core i3 5005U, GeForce GT 920M (and Intel HD 5500), and 8GB of RAM on Portable preset and 720p (1280x720) resolution. I got more than 30 FPS (around 30-60 FPS) when playing the game on my Low-End Laptop. After I tested the game on the GeForce 920M, I continued to test the game on Intel HD 5500. Surprisingly, the game still managed to run Intel HD GPU on Portable Preset and 576p (1024x576) resolution and got around 20-60 FPS. That’s really a good result for me. It’s a surprise because I thought Trails Of Cold Steel 3 PC would be more demanding than the previous games. The minimum specs of TOCS 3 PC are also higher than TOCS 1 and 2. So I was expecting that the game couldn’t able to run comfortably on Intel HD GPU but I’m wrong now. After I tested the game on Intel HD GPU, I tested again the game on GeForce 920M GPU but with limiting the RAM of my Laptop to 4GB RAM and I got another surprise. Even though the min. RAM requirement for TOCS3 is 8GB RAM, I could still manage to play the game on 4GB RAM on Portable Preset and 576p resolution and get more than 30 FPS.For me, the main reasons why I play Trails Of Cold Steel 3 (or other Trails series/Falcom Games) aren’t because of the graphics and visuals but mainly because of the story, the characters, the combat mechanic, the music and definitely because of FIE! haha.  I want to know how the story ends for Rean and Trails Of Cold Steel saga. That’s my impression/quick review of the game. I definitely will finish the game because in the end one of the main reasons why I got hooked by the game is the story itself. The PC port quality of Trails Of Cold Steel 3 PC is definitely good. Thanks for Durante and his PH3 games team for making a good port of Trails of Cold Steel 3. I hope that Durante and PH3 Games could port another Falcom games like Trails Of Cold Steel 4 and Ys IX: Monstrum Nox to PC too! So yeah. I definitely recommend you to buy and play Trails Of Cold Steel 3! If you enjoyed playing the previous Trails Of Cold Steel games, I believe you will also enjoy playing Trails Of Cold Steel 3. It’s worth the money. Come on guys, buy Trails Of Cold Steel 3 PC so that NIS America could bring Trails Of Cold Steel 4, Ys IX and other Falcom games to the west and to the PC!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best JRPG i've played these last years.The combat is fast and addictive. The story follow the previous game, a lot of mysteries and revelations with a lot of interesting characters. The OST in this game is the best of the trilogy (i dont know about CS4 for now), its rich and there is some good epic music.Im a bit disappointed about the overall difficulty of the game, on hard the first two chapters have some encounters in which if you're doing bad moves its very punishing but after that the game becomes very more and more easy, you obtain very powerfull quartz,Master quartz and orders and some build are completly overpowered.Note : 9/10Pros :-Beautiful and rich OST, the last 2 dungeons musics are my favorite.-Good story, a bit slow but with a ton of different and some returning characters and a lot of revelations.-A lot of differents places to explore, the bestiary is quite good too (lots of differents ennemies).-Combat is better than the previous game with some new possibilities.-The game is long, on hard it took me 102 hours with all quests and side activities done. 70hours for a second playthrough 2 years after but i didnt skip the dialogues, only the side content.-Very good port, lot of graphics options and it runs flawlessly 99% of the time.Cons :-Game becomes too easy past the first 2 chapters, you gain more powerfull quartz/MQ and some orders are completly broken. Arts are very weak early/mid game but become very strong late game with the right MQ/quartz/gear, Crafts are always powerful through the game and arts need to be balance for next entries.-Sometimes there are too much dialogues during the story.-You cant save your quartz builds and its a chore to switch them between differents characters (happen a lot near the last third of the game).-Lip syncs are a bit off most of the time : characters keep speaking but their lips dont move. The game need more voices acting in japanese during the important part of the story.-Combat with mechs are not that great.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing JRPGs, and somehow this is the first one (that I've ever run across) that made the core design choices I wanted most:1) While individual game plots are mostly self contained, they also _really_ impact the world of other games in the franchise (contrast with Final Fantasy, where even the related X games have major world upheavals so it's just a flimsy excuse to reuse a cast)2) New Game+3) While characters lean one way or another (magic, melee, etc) there is a Quartz system that you can load out anyone with Attack or Cast Time Reduction or Healing and they'll at least "do"4) Difficulty slider that meaningfully nerfs enemies if you want to play on easyThe biggest negative this game has (within the genre conventions) is that if you are a completionist/collector, there are dozens of "can't go back" gates in the game/series - which the game is usually PHENOMENAL about warning you about ("Are you sure you want to [do thing]?  The plot will advance and limited time quests may become unavailable!"), but if you're not in the mood for the minigame (which is fun, but hey, sometimes I've got a mood to run a dungeon gosh darn it)... you may have to bench the game or push through. All in all, not a super big complaint, but it has been a bit of an emotional drag when I sat down to play for a bit and wanted my last! half! hour! of playtime to finish something ELSE up.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this series of games to DEATH. Gameplay is very satisfying and the storyline had me very eager to buy the latest installment. I love the improvements to the combat system using the new "orders" function, although I do miss the overdrive feature from ToCS 2. Some of the master quartzes could also be tweaked so they're more beneficial to the numerous party members you have, but that's a minor grievance I can let that slide I suppose. However, my next two points are the most crucial. 1. The ending of the game was just TRAUMATIC. In ToCS1 I accepted the ending simply because it made the most sense and it led nicely into ToCS2. In ToCS2, it pained me to see the death of Crow, but I accepted it mainly because he was the only real casualty. That, and the fact that his death was used as a kind of encouragement for his classmates. I guess. BUT THIS GAME. I did not expect to see so many of my favorite characters get killed off like that. Maybe the devs were trying to avoid a whole sunshine and rainbows happy ending, but I think the way some of the characters went out was just... wrong. And heart wrenching besides. 2, and this is the most important part: the giant friggin spiders. Holy crap you guys took these things to a whole new level. This game could give me nightmares with those friggin things. Tone it down a little will ya? Aside from those two points, great game, I'm going to be playing it RELENTLESSLY for the next few weeks probably.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, this is the first time I post reviews. Honestly, after playing through trails of cold steel I to III, I would say III is the best game out of the three. I am only going to talk about the story since this is the reason why I play the series. I am also going to talk a little bit about trails of cold steel I and II as a comparison.For trails of cold steel one, I felt  90% of the hours I put into the game doesn't even matter because only the last chapter is important in terms of the story line. As for the second game, the hype died after Rean found all his classmates. I understand that the plots in the first and second game are necessary. However, the only feeling I get after beating those two games is that I am glad I survived 140 hours of torture. I mean, it's not that the story is bad, it's just the story moves in a snail pace and I don't like it.Now onto trails of cold steel III, although the game pace is similar to the first game, the story is a LOT more interesting and engaging. The villians are a LOT more active. The new class VII members have a lot more depth compared to the previous two games characters. Like, I actually felt Juna's passion for crossbell, Ash's heartfelt hatred due to his past.... etc. The ending is pretty amazing too which make me want to play the fourth game right away. _childDocuments_.review: This game RUINS me. It's such a hard one for me because the characters are great, and everything in the story is necessary for the ending of the game to make sense, but it was so. darn. long. I'm told that Trails games are this long going on from here, so I'm braced for that now. The characters in this game are GREAT. Honestly, New Class VII is my favorite main cast of a Trails arc since the first two Sky games. Juna is a great character who is used to explore the complicated politics of Erebonian/Crossbellan relations, Altina is a master class in trauma, emotions, and learning empathy, Ash adds SO much it's insane, Musse is super plot relevant (much to my chagrin, I hate her innuendos so much), and Kurt is there too! The Orbment system in this game is on par with Azure for me. Having two master quartz slots is amazing, and the combination quartz feel rewarding to synthesize/modify.The ending of this game is INSANE, and makes the long, drawn-out story of the past two games feel completely worth every second in my opinion. It carries its momentum into the rest of the arc and had me actually screaming out loud on call with my girlfriend. This is a GREAT game, but you officially need to play the Sky trilogy, Crossbell Duology, AND the previous two Cold Steel games for the full effect of the plot payoffs.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot stand this game. Rest of the Sen/Cold Steel games range from good to mediocre but this game is one of the few that I hate. Altina is returning and she is clearly where all the good in this game went. Juna in Sen III is just Alisa II but from Crossbell. Kurt is really dull and boring. Musse just constantly flirts with Rean. It is chuckle worthy at first but it gets old quick.I almost forgot about the relationship reset too, so anything you did in Sen I and II is irrelevant to this game. Why they did not just have a little questionnaire at the start of the game asking who you chose for X event(s) in Sen I & II baffles me. They ended up doing it with Hajimari and that is not even a Sen game.They replaced Blade with Vantage Masters and whilst VM grew on me I still have more fun with Blade. Graphics are alright but I am not a graphics ♥♥♥♥♥ so I could not care less unless it looks like a PS1/X or an early PS2 game. Altina is more than an entertaining villain/adversary. Ash is pretty decent for Sen III standards. Besides these things I have listed, everything else sucks.Somehow the Falcom Sound Team managed to make an abysmal soundtrack. There are only a few decent tracks in this game and most of them only play in the last bloody chapter. _childDocuments_.review: I'm only 5 hours in yet I noticed less emotion in the voice acting, and even quotes at the end of battles lack personality unlike Trails 1 and 2, it really feels like the emotion is gone from a lot of the returning characters (listen to Claire's voice acting for example) while a whole bunch of the new ones look and sound generic. I'll still recommend the game though because if you have 3, you likely loved 1 and 2, and I feel I will come to love this with time. Right now, it's just kind of boring.16 hours later and the game has its own charm that feels different from Trails 1 and 2, while it may be lacking in OST and voice acting it makes up in a larger amount of characters that you will have interest in, and the way I feel for the new Class 7 is like how I felt for Millium in 1 and 2, like she's my kid. The sense of responsibility you feel being an instructor this time around is a completely different vibe, and I do like it. The combat is better, the graphics are better, and the reunions feel awesome. TLDR; It feels like a completely different game from 1 and 2 with improvements in Combat and graphics, and dowgrades such as voice acting and soundtracks. If you played 1 and 2 give 3 a shot. Edit: I'm now 60 hours in and I can confidently say this is my favorite of Trails 1-3, I still believe the OST is a step down from 1 and 2 however it makes up for in immensely by having some of the best characters yet, the new class 7 crew on me after a while and I see them as my own kids. This game is incredible and was a great direction for cold steel. Final Edit: I'm 85 hours in and I just finished the game. Every element of 1 and 2 (besides OST) was surpassed by a considerable margin. Starting off, it felt completely foreign and I didn't like the idea of the change, however this was truly for the better. I love my students, and I cried for the one who made me laugh the most through 1 and 2. I can't wait to play Trails 4.

_childDocuments_.review: The Legends of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel 3 is a fantastic game, both as a standalone entry and as the 8th title in the Legend of Heroes: Trails franchise. Unlike most JRPG franchises, The Legend of Heroes: Trails games all take in the same universe/timeline as each other, meaning that this is the 8th entry in an epic story that spans, currently, 10 games. As a longtime fan of the series, for me, this is what differentiates the Trails games the most from other JRPG franchises.Should you buy and play this game? Yes. But if you want to get the most out of this series, you should also experience the other games, in the order of their release: Trails in the Sky FC > Trails in the Sky SC > Trails in the Sky the 3rd > Trails from Zero > Trails of Azure > Trails of Cold Steel 1-3. Trails of Cold Steel 3 brings plenty of improvements from the other titles. The game engine has been improved from Cold Steel 1 & 2, with better models and animations, and the game itself introduces new mechanics that further your strategy and tactical options while playing, such as the Orders system. If you're a JRPG fan and still haven't given the Legends of Heroes franchise a shot, you are doing yourself a disservice. Check it out!As a final thought, regarding the DLC, yes there is a literal ton of it, that in its entirety costs more than 2x the price of the game itself, which is kind of not a great look. However, none of these DLCs are mandatory, you can beat the game and experience all that it has to offer without purchasing any of it, as it is cosmetics and consumable items.

_childDocuments_.review: Total play time is actually 94 hours!Yes, I cannot recommend this game highly enough, it's the most enjoyable Trails game I've played thus far and it's incredible how Falcom improved on everything as each game progressed.This third title boasts a complete graphical upgrade, there's textures on EVERYTHING now so it looks fantastic, they added Vantage Masters which is variation of an old card game they created over 2 decades ago and I highly recommend you learn and play it, for me it was as good as Gwent, far, FAR better than Blade from the first 2 games which was more luck based.But yeah, tons of quality of life upgrades and a story that was just amazing from start to finish, these games are just stupidly good really, now gonna dive into the 4th Cold Steel!Non spoiler tips:1) If you want to do Vantage Masters, buy the cards at stores early to help.2) If you plan to do fishing, buy the best reels early on, you can make and sell food to help with that. They're expensive but it's almost impossible to catch tough fish with a normal rod. Also helpful tip: The idea is to reel the fish in, but stop reeling when it turns red over the fish, then reel again you're welcome lol.3) When you do dungeons every now and then, do yourself a favour and grab all the loot AFTER the end bosses, (this really isn't a spoiler) because annoyingly, (my only gripe really) you have to double back and go through the dungeon again to leave which if I had to do it again, I'd whip my way through super quick and then take my time when leaving so it's not so boring.4) If you do the minor swimming quest, don't be angry if you can't beat the Principal, it's almost impossible so it's honestly better to quit than wanna throw your controller lol. You have to get, 'Great' on every go pretty much to beat it and it's near impossible.Hope this helps : )

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer!!!! Try not to play this game unless you can understand Japanese or its much closer to Cold Steel 4s western release! I sunk 150+ hours between Cold Steel 1, 2, and 3 and now I need to wait 3 months to finish the story! (And that is on Switch/PS4, I have no idea when 4 is getting localized on PC) :COk serious review time: Cold Steel 3 is a fantastic JRPG experience. I highly recommend playing 1 and 2 before this but this game does have a backstory menu at the title screen if you want to jump straight in. This review is for people who have already played 1 and 2.Graphically Cold Steel 3 is a rather massive upgrade over Cold Steel 2, higher quality, more detailed, better enviroments, but the biggest improvement is scene animations, Scenes are still a tiny bit choppy in terms of animation and sometimes animations seem slower then they should nut it still miles ahead of the animations in Cold Steel 2. Sound is of course a massive plus, music and sound effects are staple pluses of the Cold Steel series. The english voice acting is amazing mostly. Some characters have low effort battle lines but most characters, especially the newly introduced ones, are fantastically voiced. The new characters start off a bit generic but each newbie's personality and story fleshes itself out over the course of the game very well. You can however tell that they did not have the budget to voice act nearly as much as they wanted, my guess is the graphics upgrades ate into the budget, A few scenes are only half voiced, with some characters only having text while others have voice. It can be a but jarring to experience the first few times but by the end of the game I had gotten used to it.The minigames are improved, Vantage Masters is a big upgrade over Blade, fishing is no longer a button mash, the cooking system is easily accessible as you get the ability for party members to cook when they are not in the party rather early. Sadly snowboarding is gone, as are Cold Steel 2's lost arts and overdrive system. The monster chests are also gone.Overall pick this game up if you like JRPGs with fleshed out lore, hilarious well developed characters, a deep story with plenty of politics, great soundtracks, good voice acting, and fun combat. I would however highly recommend picking the game up on PS4 or Switch as the PC release of Cold Steel 4 is likely over a year away. You do get cleared game benefits in Cold Steel 4 if you met certain conditions in your Cold Steel 3 save file so it makes sense to play on console for now.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm serious, you'll thank me later. They're both fun games, they're a little older, but it's not old enough to be concerned about. There is SO SO SO MUCH reference to the first 2 games in this one. You will enjoy this game 100x more if you play the first few prior to playing this.Ok, how many good things can I say about this game. Too much to write, I'm not that dedicated to write a 4 paragraph review so I'll just say this. The entire world of the legend of heroes saga, is phenomenal and are probably some of my favorite games of all time, top 5 for sure.Gameplay 10/10: It's not open world or anything, but there's enough freedom that you don't really mind, and for a story driven JRPG, that's gold. Story 11/10: It's really really good, but play the first two gamesCharacters 9/10: The important characters are really good, only complaint I really have is that the 'side characters' aren't super impactful. Tbh I don't know how they could fix this in a way that would make sense so I really didn't mind. Biggest complaint I have is that the main character (whom you play as) makes really sappy lines or speeches sometimes but honestly the other characters kind of make fun of him for it so I don't mind too much.Voice Acting 10/10: Specifically Sean Chiplock (English voice of Main character), he's really good. Fun fact, he also plays the voice of Revali from legend of zelda breath of the wild, among others. The rest are really good too but I just wanted to say something about Sean.Enjoyable Difficulty 8/10: Early on it's a little rough , but after you learn the best ways to fight and what mechanics to use it gets really easy. Not to say it isn't enjoyable, but I had the difficulty on hard from the beginning and rarely died after the first couple bosses. It's fun, but going higher than the Hard difficulty probably wouldn't make it any better.RPG Elements 8/10: Side quests, decisions, etc. they're there but they don't really affect the big picture, the decisions you make just  affect the overall "score" you get for that chapter. Romance options are nice but just like the first two games, they're not super focused on until the sequel. (Trails 4)Again I love this game, I never really review stuff and this probably isn't the best review, but I love this game so much that I had to say something about it. Do yourself a favor and play all the legend of heroes games. (Although some aren't available in the US yet, namely Zero No Kiseki which takes place about the same time as trails 1 and 2)P.S. There are 3 legend of heroes games that take place before this game, Trails in the sky, I would advice playing those before trails of cold steel 3, but they don't really matter too much for Trails 1 and 2.  DEFINITELY PLAY TRAILS IN THE SKY (or look up summaries etc) BEFORE PLAYING TRAILS 4
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with loads of content. Trails as a series is one I particularly enjoy even as someone who's not a major JRPG fan. The series avoids a lot of common complaints of the genre, no grinding needed, no random encounters, no nonsensical plot. Of course, playing the first 2 Cold Steel games is a necessity if you're serious about the story, and playing all the others Trails games certainly wouldn't hurt with that as well. The plot is definitely a wild ride to be on and you never know what's coming next. The battles are very tactical, the characters all have multiple different abilities and different ways to spec them, and you have a turbo button if you want to get through things quickly so things never get dull.  The characters all interact nicely and you can choose which of your party members you'd like to bond and spend time with for further development later on. The game has a gorgeous artstyle which goes for an anime look instead of pushing the limits of the latest technology. It's quite the step up from the previous 2 Cold Steel games. Trails of Cold Steel 3 is a further refinement of the Trails series and is worth every moment you spend with it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III

_childDocuments_.review: What a ride... and where to start. If you've been following the Trails saga since its beginnings in Trails in the Sky, this truly is the epic culmination of everything thus far. What else is there to say? Play it, and strap in for the ride with the best Trails game to date, which even surpasses the Crossbell arc. Below FREE of spoilers, I'll elaborate a bit on Trails of Cold Steel 3 traits:Gameplay: 10/10 - Best combat mechanics by far. Engaging and fun to pick up and look at for the casual players (I played in NORMAL difficulty.) But I feel it's also strategic enough for the veteran JRPG players looking to put themselves against the wall and overcome the overwhelming odds.Music: 9/10 - Falcom Sound Team JDK delivers yet again. Great tracks all around, although this is subjective from me. I feel like it missed a truly epic song that would transcend to the player. It's difficult to put into words. "Get Over the Barrier!" "To be continued!" from the Crossbell arc, and "Silver Will" from Trails in the Sky, those tracks fall into that category.Story: 10/10 - The amount of world-building and storytelling shines at its brightest in this entry. Every plot point from past games is connected, developed even more, or given closure. Although I HIGHLY recommend having played the past games first. Trust me, it will increase your experience exponentially. Characters: 10/10 - I didn't think the cast from the previous two Cold Steels could be rivaled, but Falcom REALLY hit it out of the park on this one. You will come to love these new characters early on, and you'll witness the new and old ones reaching even greater heights.And remember! Be wary of spoilers and most importantly, have fun and enjoy the game!

_childDocuments_.review: Cold Steel 3 is significantly better than 2 in just about every way. Soundtrack is great, and the updated visuals (especially for character models) are a plus. The writing is much better. It might be my personal favorite in the Erebonia arc up to this point.

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel 3 continues to uphold the high standards set by the previous entries in the franchise, offering an even more polished and immersive experience that is sure to captivate players for countless hours. The game's compelling storyline picks up where the previous installment left off and offers a deep and engaging narrative that is woven into a vast and rich world. Players will find themselves fully immersed in the intricacies of the Erebonian Empire and the struggles of the characters they have come to know and love.One of the standout aspects of the game is its well-realized characters, who are not only distinct and memorable, but also evolve and grow as the story unfolds. The relationship-building mechanics, which have become a staple of the franchise, return and allow players to further deepen their bonds with the characters and impact the story and gameplay. The writing is top-notch, with well-crafted dialogue and character interactions that are sure to keep players engaged.The game's turn-based combat system is challenging and rewarding, requiring players to make strategic decisions and use a variety of tactics to succeed. The game's mechanics are both deep and accessible, offering a traditional RPG experience that will appeal to players of all levels. The game's design is intuitive, making it easy for players to navigate the world and engage in battles. The many side quests and optional content provide hours of additional gameplay and further flesh out the world and its characters.The graphics and art style of Trails of Cold Steel 3 are nothing short of stunning, with a beautiful aesthetic that perfectly captures the game's sweeping landscapes and intricate character designs. The world is rich and detailed, and players will find themselves fully immersed in its sprawling vistas and intricate dungeons. The soundtrack is equally impressive, with a sweeping orchestral score that perfectly complements the game's epic scope and grand themes.The level of refinement and polish that has been applied to the game is evident from the moment players start playing. The game feels smoother and more polished than previous entries in the series, with improved mechanics and a more seamless experience overall. This level of refinement is a testament to the development team's commitment to delivering an exceptional gaming experience.In conclusion, The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel 3 is an outstanding RPG that offers a rich and immersive experience for players. Its compelling storyline, well-realized characters, deep gameplay mechanics, and stunning graphics make it a must-play for fans of the franchise and anyone looking for a new RPG to play. Whether you're a fan of the previous games or just starting your journey in the world of Trails of Cold Steel, this game is a title that you won't want to miss.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently discovered the Trails series, more specificly i just started playing the steel series after finishing the sky series.I've been playing nothing but these games for the past 3 months and forgive me but at this point my braincells might slowely be starting to rot bit by bit but even that can't take away how much i liked this game.Having just come fresh off the ending of Cold Steel 1 and 2 this game had alot to live up to and boy did it deliver, better pacing, better combat and a new class with arguably better characters then the old class 7.`Now before you lynch me and set me ablaze let me explain whyThe new class is alot smaller then the old one and as such they each get alot more time to develop over the course of the game, i'll admit i wasn't too happy with them at the start but they honestly grew on me ( noone can replace laura in my heart of hearts though )The beat of the story is very much like the first game except modernized and it just feels good, sure the side quests are still more or less the same boring crap as before but i never minded due to how fun the combat is.I can see alot of people who loves the OG class 7 disliking this simply due to them taking a back seat this game more or less but honestly the new class can handle itself just fine.The game is gorgeous, no more Vita, no more psuedo ps1 visuals lol.The story continues the plot at a nice pace while also at the same time feeling like it barely gets anything done at all ( alot like the first game )

_childDocuments_.review: song:This is the story that never ends.It goes on and on my friendsMore of your game time is spent doing errands than actually following one of the main story plot threads. If you avoid side quests where possible, the main threads are poorly tied together, so you are often asking why you're bothering or why it's relevant. The game only really stays on track and heats up in the last quarter, so you'll need to be tough to get there since the game will takes many people over a 100 hours.The story editors need to be better, or they need to hire one. Proper editors know that, when writing a story, you can't hang onto every little scene/skit idea you had. Plus, if a long boring event is needed then you skip when it's so obvious/droll that audience is smart enough to assume it. A "Tales" game, for example, if you only stick to the critical path then it always feels relevant. While I enjoyed the game 50% of the time, half of the content in the shortest-path-possible can be discarded as pointless fluff.Some parts of the game seem like the ending but they're not and you're like "dammit there's more"; this is because there's so much filler in the critical path that some of the important plot points can be forgotten because they're so far apart in your memory. Most of the filler is just non-core-plot errands, and by the end you'll be begging your parents to mow the lawn instead. The writers dig deeper to cover up their poor story editing capability, where the excuse for the main character being unable to focus on the main plots during the shortest path is that he is always told he's such a helpful guy (he must be using the Procrastination power-up).If you're not a total obsessive completionist, then part of the gameplay is to avoid as much of this drawn-out side-story drivel as much as possible because of the pain you're already experiencing on the main path. Avoid doing every side quest. If you have decent Level for the monsters, run past the rest. Some fans might say, "but it's character development!" Light-hearted moments are just nice filler, not character development.It's also slow because scenes try to ask every cast member for their opinion on the smallest stuff, akin to asking your entire office who should go buy the milk, which makes the errands even longer. At least they don't make you go through making their beds and brushing their teeth.All that aside, I- gave it a thumbs up cuz I like anime games and liked the characters- persevered to the end for some strange reason, despite it being as long as two games with only the content of one

_childDocuments_.review: This game, like the first two is an excellent continuation of the series.  Only consider this game honestly if you want to play through the first two, which I also highly recommend.  I don't see a lot of other reviewers showing this, but on average each game can range from 80-100 hours depending on how much of a completionist you are.  Therefore, if you want to experience the entire Cold Steel series, you're looking at a possible 400 hour investment.  If this sounds good to you, then jump in.  (I'm not including the time spend playing the Trails in the Sky series since I haven't played them personally.  I feel like I should've played those first, but you live and learn.)It's been so long since I played CS2 that I had to re-check what was added and removed.So, things that were removed that I'm a bit bummed about:- Being able to call Valimar into any battle and wreck stuff with him.  I'm sad it's not in this game, but maybe it'll be in 4.- Overdrive.  This ability was broke as hell and I remember I tweaked out my party so hard that I killed the final boss before he even got a turn in.  Granted, this is still possible in CS3, but I had to mess with my items a bit to get it to work.The new Break system is nice and it allows you to pummel enemies and bosses for a bit, which helps since a lot of bosses get way nastier in their second phases in this game.  Difficulty can sort of be all over the place given you'll destroy 90% of the field encounters only to have a boss kill you several times before you devise a good strategy.  The longer the game goes, and the more time you invest in combat, the easier it gets though.  By the end I was so powerful even the final boss wasn't "that" bad compared to some crazy difficult earlier ones.The story is still good, but I will admit I felt a point of severe frustration when the story was hitting me with a ton of build up and no payoff whatsoever until the very last points in the game and well, it delivered.  It delivered pretty darn well.  I'm really looking forward to part 4 to finish off this excellent series.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is this complicated. While, like me, you can get away with an introduction to the series through Cold Steel 1 & 2 without to much confusion this is where not playing the other games (one of which isn't in English I don't think) becomes a hurdle. After this I'm going to have to go back and play the first three... five? before I play 4, and hopefully wait for the price to come down.As for the game itself its very good. I do love Rean's natural flow into becoming a teacher for the same school that meant so much to him, and as all the others go off to become part of the world he stays where he is determined to not let the best part of his life slip away. I just wish I could say that all the other characters got as much thematic and narrative weight as him. You get 3 students starting out (later expanded to 5) and only really Juna has enough character and personality to really get invested in; her whole back story about being from Crossbell and its recent annexation into the empire and how it wants to strip them of their culture well taking the best parts for its self. Something very complicated and with a lot of nuance that the game gets right. Then you have Kurt. And... You remember Jacob Taylor from Mass Effect? Of course you don't. Kurt is pretty much that. I have zero complaints about him, but that's only because he has such little presence in every moment that he just fades into the background. Lastly you have Altina and... I just hate her. A combination of two tropes I do not like, the robotic like person and the very adult acting child. Which especially the former I've grown to despise in my older age because they're so easy to write and lack any agency in a story. All they do is just "Stoic response" to everything, and that's all Altina does. And of course old class 7 returns but considering it has to balance 5 new primary characters, plus an entire schools worth of secondary characters they don't have much to work with, with most of their important plot stuff getting pushed to the end of the game.Speaking of the end of the game: this game gets HEAVY on the exposition in the last chapter. And I mean HEAVY. And well it is all needed I feel like maybe it could have been better sprinkled through the game so its not like reading a text book at the end. It could also use a lot of trimming. I like a good long game as much as the next person, and this is probably more my fault for trying to get through it all in 2 months, but this game is a little to long. I was by no means rushing through the game but my play through still ended up being nearly 90 hours. That's a very sizeable game. Which fair enough, bang for your buck. But the narrative feels like it would have worked just that much better if we could rope it down to an even 60 hour experience. Because by hour 70 it really started to drag its heels at one or two points. But that ending. Wow. I had trouble going to sleep after because of the bomb shells it dropped on me at nearly 3 am. Trails of Cold Steel 4 is going to have a lot to answer, and as much as I'd love to jump right into that I need a breather from long RPG's for a bit.Really great game, so long as you have the time and patience for these long form RPG's and have played or have a familiarity with the rest of the series.
