_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly good. The plot twists are wild. The gameplay is relaxing and NPCs enjoyable. The new characters are really good, they have a bit more depth to them than Class 7 from the previous two games, as well as having character arcs and backstories very closely linked to the main plot. And the main plot is extremely exciting; it gets you playing all day without even realising. It's also got tons of callbacks to not just CS1 and 2, but the Crossbell and Sky games as well; and seeing that payoff, and plot lines from those games continued, is so cool to see. Don't start with this game though. It's advertised as a good start point but it's not, you won't get half as much enjoyment from it as you could do if you start with it. Start with Cold Steel 1 or preferably Sky FC. The story is very detailed and a direct continuation of the first 2 cold steel games, and indirect continuation from the other 5 games before those ones. If you have played the first two CS games, you probably don't need a review to tell you how fantastic the game is anyway, but it's here regardless. Because the game is fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally done with my first playthrough, 100+ hours really well spent. Better give a positive review for this game, it deserves it.First of all, I can't say I've been really fond of the Cold Steel arc so far, I liked CS1, but CS2... not so much, it left me dissapointed in a lot of ways, and overall felt like a downgrade compared to the Sky and Crossbell arcs, in terms of both story and characters. CS3 improves in both aspects. I like the new Class VII a lot more than the old one, the smaller roster works better for developing the characters, and a few of them, like Juna, Ash and Musse, really brings a lot more dynamics to the group. Even the other classes students are more interesting this time around. But I guess the biggest joy I had was seeing the returning characters and visiting certain locations introduced in the previous arcs. Falcom was also spot on with the OST that plays when you visit those places.Gameplay didn't change drastically from the previous games, but the Brave Orders and break system are interesting new additions. Though after finishing the game on Nightmare, the brave orders are definitely OP. Actually, this seems to be a trend with the Cold Steel games, every game introduces new mechanics that can be easily abused to make the game easier. A bit about the PC port to finish. Thankfully, NISA did a much better job compared to the initial release of Ys VIII, hiring Durante to work on the game was the right decision, the PC port is solid, lots of graphical enhancements and very stable.Now, to wait for Cold Steel 4... damn, Falcom really loves their cliffhangers.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal game. The first two chapters felt all-too-familiar to anyone who played the first two games. The third chapter felt like it dragged way too long, and nearly pushed me to skip the side content, but after chapter 3, the game and story picked back up, giving it the strongest ending of all three games. I can't wait for Trails of Cold Steel IV to be localized now. When playing the first two titles in the series, it didn't feel necessary to play any of the other games set in the same universe. But this game made me feel like I was missing out on so much for not playing any of them (not just Trails in the Sky, but Trails from Zero and Trails to Azure as well -- perhaps even Dragon Slayer: Legend of Heroes). When playing the game, you *MAY* be able to get away with not having played the other trails games (even Cold Steel), but you will be at a loss in most aspects of character development and plot points, as the game tries to avoid explaining subtleties and nuances that have been described in earlier titles. This game held many cameo character and plot points that were relevant in the other trails games, that I felt I was missing information on because I started with Cold Steel 1 rather than any of the other legends of heroes games. I would certainly recommend the game, but it is a very large commitment (as seen from my playtime). Between the tree cold steel titles alone, I have invested approximately 300-350 hours. And I play with turbo mode enabled, and while completing any side content within reason (I don't seek out hidden quests or complete the recipe book, but I will visit any event with a map marker). And for this title specifically, while trying to rush the story on easy mode (with the side content completed too, but no grinding), I still spent about 120 hours to complete. I can only imagine how much longer the game would have taken for a completionist. Again, the game isn't for everyone, especially since the quality of your experience depends on having played the previous titles, but if you have the time to play, it will be a very enriching experience, to say the least.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game. Story is bad. It copy paste Cold Steel 1. With infamous ‘fall scene’, that I fist thought as omage, but in the end I think it is still this same terrible writing. Unfortunately if you try retell this same story, all it flaws are clearer visible, and whole dish starts to smell like old fish.First 3 chapters is getting to know ‘new class seven’, and reintroducing villains. There is something, something plot about some tests, but it don’t play ANY role overall (these whole tests are better summarised by one mech battle scene around 15-20 minutes long). Chapter 4 is quite nice climax to whole story It was mostly good, we forgot about silly moustache twirling villains, and go silly spies hunting, but still it was interesting and trilling piece of story… But I said “mostly”, because ending of chapter 4 happened “The Big Reveal”… This “Big Reveal” is such dumpster fire of terrible writing I CANNOT FORGIVE, and have to spoil it… After that we have “final chapter” and gauntlet where you fight with Big Bad Evil Doers, but at this point I stopped caring.Nothing matter, there is no consequences anyway.Combat system it is ‘same old’ with few tweaks. By the endgame I HATED juggling orbments (there is moment in these games where you have to much orbs so finding specific one is pain), and didn’t care for optimization, too bad that story was even worse.Characters are mixed bag. Kurt was a bit bland but in the end he grew on me. Juna represents “tsun” character… while in general I Like “tsuns”, the one that are made by Falcom I find obnoxious. She also get some more obnoxious points for overdramatising stuff. Altina was nice character earlier, and here is still one of my favourites (the best in new class 7). Ash is bad boy, also got really short stick with his place in story, he is OK. Muse while I was intrigued by her, in the end she became another point of terrible writing, but it mostly comes in play in CSIV, and after her big reveal in CSIV I drooped series, and probably won’t finish it. For her story to work all reality had to be bent around her. Also we supposed to know her not by her actions, but by badly written story (they don’t show, but tell). _childDocuments_.review: An astonishingly well-crafted game, Cold Steel 3 comes back onto the landscape as a worthy addition to the Erebonian Saga, boasting greatly improved graphics and general gameplay, while continuing its tradition of strong worldbuilding and intricate story. Taking place in the wake of the Erebonian Civil War of Cold Steel 2, Cold Steel 3 showcases the lives of both well-known comrades and fresh new faces in its aftermath. The saga continues in interesting and intricate ways, culminating in a complex tale that will grip both veterans and newcomers to the franchise, and leave you hungry for its conclusion in Cold Steel 4.Coming from Cold Steel 1 and 2, many characters will be familiar faces, with some new additions. Many of the old characters have now moved on, having their own lives and being individual, independent characters who are not reliant on our main character, Rean, to have signifiance. Most of the new characters have reasonably acceptable backstory and motivation to be part of the game's overall plot, and their development, while slow, does show progress.Despite a colorful and well-developed cast of characters, Cold Steel 3 fails to utilize its full potential in character writing. Many characters fail to remain relevant throughout the entirety of the game’s runtime, and development of characters is unevenly spread. Many characters take the limelight for certain portions, only to disappear for the rest of the game; other characters’ development are either delayed until the end or essentially glossed over. The result is a rather enjoyable ensemble that still leaves the player somewhat wanting, especially if the player’s favorite characters drew the short straw. Two words can sum up the one greatest improvement to Cold Steel 2's gameplay:  . Easily the most hilarious and best part of gameplay, this one attack is over the top in terms of humor, and you'll continue to use it for the entire game just to hear the dulcet tones of Machias saying "You've failed your inspection" over and over.Veterans will feel right at home with CS3 and its familiar quartz system, which allows a player to add more artes (magic) or raw stats. The system, while a bit daunting at first glance, is well explained and easy for newcomers to pick up and build with. The Overdrive Mechanic from CS2 is gone, likely because Falcom realized that going first and being able to nuke your enemies down with multiple spells immediately was unbalanced to the point of steamrolling the game. In its place is a new mechanic named "Orders", which are party-wide, arena-wide buffs to your battle members that use Battle Points/Bravery Points for cost. These are much more balanced compared to the Overdrive mechanic; however, they retain the same problems as their predecessor. Some Orders can easily be abused to leave monsters with no turns to attack, even on the hardest difficulty.The other new mechanic in Cold Steel 3 is Break, which helps prevent monotonous battles from extending too long for comfort. It as a secondary health bar, smaller in magnitude than the first. Upon reaching zero, the enemy is stunned and vulnerable to attacks. Again, combined with Orders, this mechanic can be easily abused to give enemies no chance of retaliation in battle.Finally, Rean's  is horrendously overpowered beyond comparison. It is a basic craft that attacks twice and will end up doing more total damage compared to an S-Craft.Cold Steel 3 also offers a couple of minor side activities to break up the main gameplay flow: fishing and Vantage Masters. Fishing is not very complex, and provides an easy method to gather materials, making it a welcome addition whenever a player needs to get more materials. As for Vantage Masters, it is a card game based on summoning monsters who have various stats, abilities, range, and elemental advantages. While entertaining, neither of these mini games are particularly engaging (fishing quickly becomes monotonous, and Vantage Masters is easily broken), and as such neither of them will take the majority of your time.While in general gameplay has been balanced and designed better compared to the previous games, ways to completely break the game and to remove all sense of difficulty still exist. Overall, this game is not exactly well-known for its gameplay, nor should you expect fantastic gameplay mechanics.Cold Steel 3's story has many high points with some scattered low points. The main drive of the story has the party take a whirlwind tour of Erebonia, giving the player both essential plot information as well as showing off the beautifully crafted environments of Erebonia's various locales. Both new and old friends alike await you at every twist and turn, simultaneously advancing old plot lines while beginning (and weaving in) new ones. This seamless intertwining and extension of the story is masterfully emphasized by the feeling of increased stakes in the story. With every new locale, the player can feel history being made, and the weight of every event and happening is apparent. Personally, I must congratulate Jusis's voice actor for doing a spectacular job in the final dungeon. That one voiceline still gives me chills whenever I think of it. However, what would have been a masterpiece of a story is unfortunately hindered by confounding or tangential elements. There are several introductions of new variables, powers, and characters which can create confusion, as they continue to muddy previous historical power levels established in the past from previous entries in the Trails series. In addition, the game has not showcased how characters from the previous games (Trails in the Sky trilogy) compare to characters presented in Cold Steel. This is a vital missing piece in an otherwise exemplary feat of world building; indeed, it's somewhat baffling that they haven't, given their obvious skill in weaving together old and new within the Erebonian saga. Finally, the story, while great overall, is ended with In conclusion, if you are looking for a RPG that has been historically well-known for its effort in creating a giant world and establishing important historical events and figures, along with an enjoyable individual story, fantastic graphics, and likable characters, look no further than Cold Steel 3. While it is important to have played  and  , the Backstory section should suffice for giving a new player the context needed to understand events that occur.

_childDocuments_.review: No one's gonna read this but I figure out I would write my thoughts about this game especially after playing it for 150+ hours. Finished this game on hard + difficulty rebalance mod (you can get this from reddit). Sigh, quarantine is really something else to make me write an unimportant essay about video games that no one ask for. Anyway here goes my review.-COMBAT- 9.5/10Easily my favorite part of the game. The new brave order system allows for more strategic gameplay. Take the previous titles' support craft but you can use it on any team member's turn provided you have enough brave points. You can reduce delay per turn, heal EP, HP and CP, etc. The newly introduced sub-master quartz also allows for more creative and innovative builds. You can combine Thors and Gloom for extra damage output or Regulus and Brigid for literally infinite amount of CP, fun stuffs. Despite all of these awesome additions, I feel like Falcom did not take enough time to rebalance some of the game breaking builds like spamming chrono burst, stacking evasion, etc (you name it). Fortunately, there is a difficulty rebalance mod to fix that. (I strongly recommend this mod)-GAMEPLAY- 4/10Cold Steel 3 retains the same game structure from CS1 but instead, you are in Instructor Sara's shoes and you are forced to participate with every activity with your students. In every chapter, there is this sort of pattern and formula that the game follows (those who finished the game will know what I'm talking about). This was fine the first few chapters but later on became somewhat repetitive and mundane. The lack of freedom in between these  makes the game feels claustrophobic since you are trapped in this mundane cycle of life and I can't help but grown somewhat tired of it (even as a player lol). A good example of how Falcom handles a good game structure would be CS2. While there is also some sort of formula and pattern that they follow, the ability to just ride a bike and chill out/explore anywhere you want allows the player to break free from this routinely cycle and unwind themselves. -CHARACTERS- 8/10They did a really good job on these new casts. I'm talking about the new Class VII and even the other students from branch campus. Each character feels unique and distinct from each other (different faces and physiques) instead of just generic faces and different hair colors. The new class VII while smaller in size, feels much more dynamic and lively. Their relationship as friends also feels more genuine and believable than the old Class VII. Juna is very protective and caring towards Altina and Kurt (love seeing her hugging Altina) . Ash's exchange with Kurt and Juna is also hilarious to watch. Musse, on the other hand, contributes to Rean's daily boners. The contrast and clash between the members' personalities and motivations are what made it good.CS2 (yes, 2) missed out on the chance to further put in these little details and exchange between each member of the old class VII. Their relationship feels... shallow like they are only friends because of what they are going through together and not because they really like each other's presence (think of a coworker relationship). Little effort is put to deepen their personal relationship with each other (dont include Rean also rip Laura x Fie). There is no bond between girls-only and boys-only relationships within the class. The girls feel like they are all competing for who can suck Reans dong the most. The boys on the other hand have no contrast between each other. All of them are just too nerdy, serious and one dimensional (which is why I miss Crow's presence in the class). The result? that awkward reunion scene. And don't get me started with CS3 (my god those cheesy ass "as a class VII member" lines). I could go a long day on this but theres just not enough space ;-;.-STORY- 7.5/10 (SPOILERS)CS3 deals with much darker themes compared to older titles.  They touch on several sensitive subjects like suicide, hopelessness, genocide, death, even  and a lot more. Personally, I really appreciate Falcom’s effort on this and I think they did a pretty decent job conveying that. We can especially see this in . That Juna scene at the rooftop was probably the most emotional scene in the game in my opinion.My biggest problem with the story is the pacing. The pacing was a bit slow compared to their older flagship titles like Ao and SC. CS3 develops the plot mostly during field exercises. You repeat the same kind of thing for 3 chapters. The ending is also somewhat predictable (for the first 3 chapters) as they follow the same kind of formula. At some point, I felt like the game kind of dragged for too long until then. Looking back, the first 3 chapters’ major happenings don’t really connect with the final part of the game aside from some foreshadowing and character developments here and there. Chapter 4 is where ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan. That final chapter though was really something else. They blew up my expectations throwing characters with plot armors like that . However, the graphical limitations do not do justice for the scene at all (stiff animations, limited set of facial expressions,etc). They really tone down the characters' emotion here. Here’s hoping Falcom will have a bigger budget.-SOUNDTRACK- 9/10That final dungeon theme was bop.TL;DR – People dubbed CS3 as the SC to the Liberl arc or Ao no Kiseki to the Crossbell arc for the Cold Steel series. Like a normal human being, of course I would set my expectations for this game sky high. I mean we know how effin awesome SC and Ao was. Sadly, I cannot wholly agree to that. If SC and Ao were a rollercoaster, CS3 was more like a train.. with too many stops (?). CS3 didn’t really quite live up to my expectations. That said, I still enjoyed the game and in the end that’s what matters. In hindsight, I might have put a little too much time to finish the game (2x the normal average playtime). My advice is to finish the older title first especially Zero and Ao no Kiseki (still the king). Trust me you will appreciate the little details and references that Falcom had put into the game. Still looking forward to CS4 though.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm only adding a review to this game to add another positive review to the gigantic pile of positive reviews this game already has, because, well, I love Trails.Trails of Cold Steel III is a direct story continuation of Trails of Cold Steel 1 and 2. Therefore, you absolutely have to play both Trails of Cold Steel 1 and 2 for this game to make any sort of sense. Considering that those two games combined are roughly 150 hours of game time, you shouldn't need any help to answer any "do I buy this game?" questions. If you liked 1 and 2, obviously you will want to know what happens next and will purchase and play this. If you didn't, well, why did you put in 150 hours into games that you don't like? What's wrong with you?On another note, some people will say that you should also play the three Trails in the Sky games and the two Crossbell games (Zero/Ao) before playing this. They're not 100% wrong, playing those games will definitely add to your understanding of various plot points, but it's not completely necessary. The game has been written in such a way to accomodate both Trails veterans and people who started with Trails of Cold Steel. That said, if you have a spare 300 hours or so, there's no reason not to play the older Trails games before playing Trails of Cold Steel... They are quite fantastic.So yes, obviously, buy this. It's a lot like ToCS 1 and 2, but better. The story is slightly better, the pacing is substantially better, the game mechanics have seen some interesting new additions, the visuals have been improved quite a bit, the music is awesome as usual, the localization and PC port are both perfectly fine and up to the standards of ToCS1/2. Just buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Set a couple years after Trails of Cold Steel (ToCS) 2 comes a sequel that moves Rean and class 7 into new roles in the world. I played through on normal difficulty and even utilizing the turbo mode extensively it still took ~81 hours to clear the first time through making it probably the longest game in the entire Legends of Heroes series.The good:If you’ve played ToCS 1&2, it’s basically the same format. Go to school, have free time, complete quests, go on field exercises, fish, cook food, feel good, save the world, yadda yadda. Surprisingly, it still works well, although does get a little long in the tooth.The combat system is basically the same as you’ve ever known and seemly like every Legend of Heroes game they just add a little twist every game to keep things fresh. Things still feel and work good and nothing really to complain about here. All your favorite abilities are here, and they added a few cool new things I had not seen in previous games. Combat is easy to exploit even on normal and I think most people shouldn’t have much problem clearing the game.The overall story is good, probably the best of the entire Legend of Heroes series. It’s a little cheesy here and there, but generally a lot of interesting twists and turns. If you thought things were wild in the last two games you haven’t seen nothing yet!There’s a ton of characters in the game, but I think that’s part of what makes the series good. Many characters from the past, and some surprises from earlier games. Characters are well wrote, if not a big cheesy at times. The voice acting is well done for the most part. You also get the chance to play as most major character.Overall a good solid port. Game never crashed and generally works pretty well.The bad:Unlike ToCS 1&2, if you haven’t played the Crossbell arc or the Trails in the Sky series you are really missing out on a lot of background to some of the characters and events. There are characters from these past games that appear in this game. I guess you can argue they aren’t the main characters and so not a big deal. You’ll still make it through just fine but it’s so much better if you play the previous games first.Graphical performance on this game is subpar. For how the game looks I’d expect a GTX 1080 to be able to play on ultra 60 FPS at least. Not so! Some outdoor scenes will crush even high end GPUs. Milliums voice actor didn’t return for this game, and the replacement is not as good. Not the end of the world but just enjoyed the other voice actor more. Everyone else seemed the same.The game is too long. I say this about most of the Legend of Heroes games, they are just padded with too much useless stuff. You could easily cut 30-50% of the game, still tell a great story and feel satisfied having played it. I felt after maybe the 40-50 hour mark things where starting to get a big sluggish. The game doesn’t hold you back from playing quickly due to turbo mode and quick travel and still feels too long.TLDR;Decent port, same structure as 1&2, way too long. Good game. If you are fan of series you need to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is in my opinion one of the weaker games of the series. At this point in the story there are way too many characters coming into play, literally. There are points in this game where you have to manage and equip around 15 different characters at a time while controlling two separate parties at a time. Its frustrating because You spend time finding equipment and items for your main squad only for them to suddenly be split up and not available to use. At the same time they thrust many returning characters on you all at once, giving you no time to properly build them up and get a feel for how to use them in battle. In previous games in this series when returning characters joined your roster, it was usually one or two of them at a time and you were given the option to use them or swap them out for someone you already spent time gearing up and such. I feel like the immense roster is starting to hinder other newer characters development as they arent given proper time to shine in the spotlight. Other than that the game is actually pretty fun, and still retains the general feel of the franchise. Good graphics and a slightly updated battle system to go with it. Although this is the first game in the series I feel like I cant recommend just because I don't really agree with the direction the newest games in the series are going.

However, quickly I realized the changes to the combat system and menu systems were universally an improvement. Furthermore, as the story progressed and looking back on it now I can say this may be one of the greatest sequels I've ever experience. Where as many good sequels  (such as CS2) are really the second half of the same story, CS3 is a true sequel and manages to add new characters and grow the plot in interesting ways while respecting the old characters and letting them continue to develop from the characters you know and love.  Its a balance much media struggles to achieve and I'm truly impressed.

_childDocuments_.review: NISA: You can start with Cold Steel 3!Reality: You should NOT start with Cold Steel 3! It will bring in characters from both the Liberl and Crossbell games, as well as reference events that happened in them, not to mention you have two other Erebonia games that are pretty vital to setting the stage for this entry.Okay rant over. Review time. This is definitely a strong entry, and probably my favorite of the Cold Steel games thus far. Combat has been made a bit more snappy with mapping actions to buttons, not to mention the graphics overhaul giving it a true HD look (albeit some areas are prone to frame drops). Admittedly, the pacing of the game is a bit repetitive and each chapter other than the final plays out the exact same way with different plot beats. This is also the longest Trails game I've played to date, clocking in just over 90 hours. I did do whatever side content I found to be fair...but I was surprised it added up that much.The new Class VII is also a much smaller group than the past 2 games, so the game is allowed to explore these characters more than the past 2 could...Rean is still a bit of a blank slate though. The plot itself is also just more interesting, and those who've been playing up to this point are going to start seeing some payoffs when returning characters or locations show up.The only downside of beating CS3 is I've realized I only have a couple more games to go before I'm caught up. How did THAT happen!?

_childDocuments_.review: Trails of Cold steel tends to get compared to the Avengers a lot and there is a reason why. CS3 is a build up of 20 years of stories all coming together. There really isnt anything else like this and while its by no means perfect its amazing to finally be able to see it through the Sky trilogy, the Crossbell duology and now the Cold Steel quadrilogy.Outside of the story this is a masterclass in a how to do how to execute turned based combat effectively. Yes you can spec yourself to get so utterly broken that spec around all or nothing one hit kill attacks or extreme speed with almost guaranteed counters upon getting hit or just loading the enemy up with so many negative effects that they can barely get a turn in. Depending on the difficulty setting this is can be a very glass cannon game, you can devastate but so can the enemy so setting up chains of maneuvers to get a single devastating turn is very addicting. The cons are of course the time investment, persona 5s loading screens tell you to take your time, thats a single 100 hour game, this is a series of 100 hour games. The benefit of that time is that this gets to properly set up its world like no other series so payoffs hit out the park. The other issue is of course this isnt a big budget title, these games are using indie game levels of low budget so you can see that in general animations, graphics and lack of voice acting in a lot of areas.Falcom did something special with this series, there is nothing like this in any form of media(for good reason). Any jrpg fan owes it to themselves to play this series, by the time its finished its probably going to be a 700-1000hour mountain but man is it worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Sen no Kiseki 3. What a game, what a lovely game. Sen no Kiseki 3 brings us the improved graphic thanks to the new engine, and new game mechanic to the table. "Enhanced" state basically enemies get powered up but can be cancelled by breaking the BREAK gauge. They also nerfed a lot of things like overall damage, AT delay, evasion stat (you can still build evasion albeit harder). Other things like quartz, master quartz (With Arcus II, you can equip sub MQ which gives you fraction of the stat), etc. still the same. Some mechanic like Lost Arts and Overdrive are gone (to compensate break and other new thingy i think). As for difficulty nothing too difficult even on Nightmare difficulty, except for some late game boss.As for the story it follows Rean after several years graduating from Thors Main Campus after the event of Sen no Kiseki 2, new threat looms the Erebonia and Zemuria and its up to Rean to stop them. Rean no longer with old Class VII, instead you get to meet a new Class VII which is as good and as interesting as the old one. Overall story is...a roller coaster of emotion, that's it, go play it by yourself you won't regret it. I recommend playing all of the previous Trails series to experience this to the fullest.Verdict

_childDocuments_.review: As an RPG, Trails of Cold Steel III is fine. The updates to the Trails formula from a mechanical perspective are smartly incremental, not quite changing anything too drastically but introducing a number of great elements that make combat more engaging. But as a narrative experience, this is an aggravating case of drowning the player in nostalgia, cameos, and callbacks to other games in the wider Trails universe while doing astonishingly little to progress the questions Trails of Cold Steel I and II presented. There are some high points. Juna and the portion of the story that takes place in Crossbell show immense promise, though again, it's hindered by a lack of forward motion. The new UI takes some getting used to, but I think aside from font size problems it's mostly an upgrade for the better. Certain locations, especially Crossbell, are as realized as the series has seen, and there's lots to do and see.But every chapter is a regurgitated mess of characters from previous games in nonsensical ways that only add more questions to a series already bloated with them. When you're constantly bombarded by twist after twist and old character after old character, all of it ceases to matter. New characters have real potential but are often shoved to the side to make way for temporary party members. It's a narrative mess that also somehow continues to be predictable in its way of resolving nothing and letting none of its biggest moments mean anything. If you're looking for forward motion or a continuation of the great plot from the first two games (well, first game and a half, anyways), this isn't it. It's a graduation yearbook of a game, but I guess if you are obsessed with the question of "where are they now?" this is perfect for you.

_childDocuments_.review: CS3 is a fantastic game, much like its predecessors. QOL, a deepening battle system, and more of the characters you've come to love through the first two Cold Steel games. It's a good time and wonderful to see how our characters grow.That said, it doesn't come without faults: - The story is a bit weaker than the previous two games, even if we see many satisfying moments for fans of the series and get more many questions answered while having delightful twists peppered throughout. It's still very enjoyable, but certain themes and ideas were done better in previous titles or simply don't match the content surrounding them.- The gameplay, while deeper, is arguably too easy to cheese for a larger chunk of the game. More customization is always fun, and new systems to interact with the battles for tactical decisions are great, but it comes at the expense of big fights being laughably easy. That's not to say the earlier games weren't guilty of this same issue, this one is just even more readily broken.- The change from CS2's more open world to CS3's linear go to this hub then the next while leaving the previous hubs inaccessible does make the game world feel slightly smaller. I confess this is an issue of perception, but it is one that bothered me somewhat.- The cast is GIGANTIC. Ignoring how big just the playable cast is, including guest characters, there are a lot of threads running tangent with each other. While it's appreciable, at times having so many characters on screen can grind things to a halt, and causes many cutscenes to balloon wildly in length. To my understanding, this will only get worse with CS4.Those complaints aside, the game is still very enjoyable as a core JRPG experience. If you need to scratch that itch for a very anime feeling game, CS3 lives up to your need!

This is the first game NISA published and they're trying to sell it to you right now with their marketing narrative which was that you could start with this game (which just isn't true) and since they can't put the older games under a free weekend since they're not the publishers we've got a flood of negative reviews from people who probably shouldn't have even ever played the game in the first place.This review is more here to inform the people who don't know what's going on here to head out and if they're really interested to not waste their time with this game in particular. Go play Cold Steel 1 or Trails in The Sky outright before you even think of buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the first Trails of Cold Steel; I loved the second one.  This one I did not enjoy.  In films, the rule is "show, don't tell".  In video games the rule is "do, don't show".  Trails 3 fails here.  You don't do, you frequently don't even get shown.  You get told.  Sometimes you don't even get told, you have to read a book about what happened after the fact.  I could forgive the exposition dumps were it not for the cutscenes.  If you play through this game in 120 hours, I wager 80 of those hours will be spent watching cutscenes.  It gets really tedious after a while.  Second complaint I have is that while the first game felt extremely grounded, and the second one introduced the mechas but was otherwise pretty grounded, the story in this one just abandons any pretense of realism.  I won't do spoilers, but the plot becomes weird.Third: One of the things I liked about ToCS1&2 is that you had a team and you built relationships with the other characters and those relationship choices had consequences.  All that character development is gone here.  There's no save file import.  If you and Laura ended ToCS2 getting basically engaged, doesn't matter, you're just good friends again.  Oh, and the old team is gone.  Rean is still the protagonist and Class VII all get cameo appearances, but the game centers around a new Class VII of just the most boring and one dimensional characters.  The most interesting character is the girl whose whole deal is that she has no personality, that's how little you will care about these new characters.Fourth: ToCS1 was my first Trails game.  I never played the previous titles from Nihon Falcom, and those legacy characters start bleeding into the new title pretty heavily here.  So if you're a long-time veteran you might enjoy that, but if you're like me you just have these random people showing up with no backstory and I'm supposed to care about them and I don't.  So the crossover thing might be a positive for some people, but I didn't appreciate it.I played through once for the story, but I didn't go achievement hunting in NG+ because most of the game is skipping cutscenes, then skipping two more back-to-back cutscenes, then running next door and skipping two more cutscenes.

_childDocuments_.review: if you haven't played The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel, you should probably that one first. The Trails series is one of the finest JRPG experiences you'll find on the PC. Its deep and interconnected narrative--spanning nine entries between the Trails in the Sky series, the two Crossbell games and the four Trails of Cold Steel games--is truly something you don't see much of from video games. They're not literary masterpieces, sure, but if you're looking for a fun JRPG about friendship, adventure, and how horrible it is to live in a buffer state between two warring imperialist powers, your ultra-specific wish has been granted. If you combine that with a deep combat system, a smorgasbord of well-written and likable characters, and enough anime tropes to choke a horse, you've got the Trails series. If that intrigues you, start with either Trails in the Sky or Trails of Cold Steel, then play the rest before you hit Trails of Cold Steel III. It is technically possible to play just the Cold Steel games, but Trails of Cold Steel III introduces a number of returning characters and locales from previous games that might make things confusing.If you have played Trails of Cold Steel and Trails of Cold Steel II, well, uh, play this one. It's a true successor to Cold Steel and Cold Steel II in every way. Set a year and a bit after Trails of Cold Steel II, everyone's favorite traumatized war hero Rean  Schwarzer is now an instructor at the Thors Military Academy Branch Campus, teaching a new Class VII. The way the new Class VII interacts with the old Class VII, as well as Rean's other Thors classmates and returning characters from Trails in the Sky and Zero no Kiseki/Ao no Kiseki is a lot of fun, and gives some fresh perspectives into what it's like to live in the Erebonian Empire. Cold Steel III's battle system takes some getting used to; the addition of Brave Orders complicates the combat system in a daunting way, but once you understand how everything works and get more adept at managing your BP, Brave Orders feel like such a natural addition that you completely forget that they took Overdrives out of the game. The addition of a new Break system adds another layer of strategy as well, leading to a lot of interesting new combat strategies. Panzer Soldat fights are still infrequent, but the fact that most of the ones I've seen so far feature more than one-on-one combat spices it up a bit.So yeah, Trails of Cold Steel III is the best the series has ever looked, it plays the best and leads up to the absolute cluster (in a good way) that is Trails of Cold Steel IV, so you really don't have an excuse to not pick this one up.(hi falcom and/or NISA pls localize zero no kiseki and ao no kiseki thanks ily)

_childDocuments_.review: Trails of Cold Steel III takes place a couple of years after the events of its predecessor and marks the beginning of a sort of convergence, bringing everything from the preceding games together. The new Class VII fixes a massive the problem the old class had, chemistry. It's aided by being a significantly smaller cast, but much more cohesive nonetheless. While I do feel that the character writing has consistently been on a decline since the first Cold Steel entry, I'm happy to say CSIII makes a great attempt at getting back on its feet. At times the formulaic approach was tedious, especially since it was very similar to CSI. The lore and world-building however are still gripping and expansive.My BIGGEST gripe with this game was the awful sound design and in my opinion having the weakest soundtrack within the entire series so far. Perhaps it was a result of the music always being way too quiet even at max volume, but nearly none of the tracks that weren't just reuses/remixes of older tracks were at all memorable. Trails has always excelled very much in the battle themes, and with them being mixed so poorly I found nearly all the battles just... not exciting. I have a very strong preference towards music in games, it can be a make or break for me, and this complaint alone probably puts CSIII to the least of my favorite Trails game. I have the same complaint with Ys VIII regarding the mixing of the score, but at least it was fantastic, yet I still worry this will be a consistent problem going forward with Falcom releases.Despite that, I still recommend the game. _childDocuments_.review: Where do I begin. I've been following the Trails series ever since the first game came out on the PSP in NA. Cold Steel 3 sort of feels like the culmination of everything it's been building up towards for it's story and characters. And for the MOST part, it works. For a cast as huge as this, they do a pretty damn good job at covering all their bases. The characters are pretty likable and I really like where they end up as a result. Yet despite that, I'm starting to notice a certain problem this series carries as a burden to it's writing. The writing is afraid of displaying consequences for the overarching plot. It's afraid of committing to morally gray actions certain characters go through. There's a certain plot twist that happens here that kills all the actions leading up the entire Erebonia arc. Maybe Cold Steel 4 provides better context to why this certain plot twist needed to exist, but suffice to say I was let down by it immensely.That aside it's still a damn enjoyable game. The Arcus and Quartz system makes for some incredibly fun setups, leading to some super fun combinations that can break the game. And I really liked playing with all the different types of characters that were introduced in the entirety of the Trails series. Despite my issues with what the last act offered for Cold Steel 3, the franchise is well worth experiencing for what it is. Here's hoping Cold Steel 4 wraps things nicely.

_childDocuments_.review: Trails of Cold Steel 3 appeared on my recommended a week ago and with 100% reviews combined with a love for JRPGs this was a slam dunk, right? Wrong, the game is an over-convoluted mess that makes you wish the dialogue would just end so the game can actually carry on. The characters are generic and one dimensional, most being from the previous game so you get plenty of flashbacks. The combat, at first, seems fine but as the game progresses it's a joke. The story- ToCS3, as implied from the name, is the 3rd of the Cold Steel series. Now, grabbing a series midway can be a naive approach. However, they state "Experience an epic story developed across three titles, and crafted for new and old fans alike" so I figured, okay newcomer friendly, excellent. Earlier, I mentioned flashbacks, that's the storytelling. Constant flashbacks to reintroduce characters from previous intervals in the story to the point you will just naturally hold down the Turbo trigger. A character shows up and the character looks surprised? Flashback. Character that "died" in previous games? Flashback. Rean trying to remember if he left the oven on? Flashback. I don't mind large story archs but the problem is I've spent most of the game meeting new characters who never want to stop talking to the point when they show up again I physically groan. I don't care that Rean and you ransacked a local orphanage, can I focus on my own ensemble? I think it was 4(?) hours before I managed to get to my first actual free roam area (with enemies).The characters- If the characters were anymore generic the color white would sue them. In no particular order; Generic Tsundere Female, Generic Instructor, Generic Little Brother, Generic Lolicon, Generic Tsundere Male, Generic Prince, Generic GENERIC GENERIC. The characters have no flaws except their age. Their lack of maturity and inexperience being their biggest factors. The instructor has no flaws, he's generic vidya gam protag, he's white bread with a glass of water, he's a boring Gary Stu that apparently has this amazing power from the previous games(that he of course won't use until the story let's him :)) who drives a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ legendary gundam but is the same level as a bunch of kids for balance reasons... Seriously, how am I supposed to like the generic anime cast when they're just that. That's not including the characters from the previous games who will join you randomly throughout the journey, usually accompanied by a flashback explaining who they are, then a flashback showing who they know, then a flashback showing how they were involved in the rise of fascism. I haven't beaten the game, probably won't, but I can only assume the growth becomes, for example "i may b small and my style different bu i am jus as capable" and he grows stronger? I actually saw someone praise Ash, like he was a good character. Yes, every Japanese school setting would like to show you their "tough guy". Some green haired ♥♥♥♥♥ is aloof too, who cares?The combat- At first it feels fun cause it has all these bells and whistles. OOH BREAK? MORE DAMAGE!? CRITS?!?! AREA OF EFFECT!!! PRETTY! Then when the initial dopamine wears off you realize it's just a broken jumbled mess. Bosses heal? (Before I get some people complaining that my characters heal too, well the boss can ONE SHOT MY TEAM, under no circumstances can my team one shot the boss) I don't know why a robot is able to self heal constantly, but all the fights boil down to chip (until they start to heal and increase their stats too, can't forget that) and burst or just abuse -delay%. Why not just have a fight that's challenging the whole way through instead of encouraging burst strategies? You've already made me completely uninterested in the cast and now I can't even use strategy with the bosses. God ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ forbid you start a fight with no brave points (Or CP) on higher difficulties, not because it's hard, but because when enemies get the first turn they can wipe out your whole party with 1-2 moves, get better.If you liked the previous entries, you'll like this game considering it's the exact same story. If you have no knowledge and like the overly used trope of school settings along with rpgs, this might be up your alley. If you have no knowledge and none of that seems appealing then stay away. I do NOT recommend this game. If you can get it for $15 on sale go for it, it is not worth 60 for what feels like Trails of Cold Steel DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: First, ignore the publisher's ridiculous and stupid description that you can start the series here. This is a direct continuation of the story started in Cold Steel 2 and 1. You need to start there to properly enjoy the story. If you played the Trails in the Sky series and Ao No Kiseki, then some events and characters will have extra meaning but it's not obligatory or a big deal.Cold Steel 3 is a fantastic continuation of the saga. Bigger and better than ToCS2, the ending was truly shocking (but with foreshadowing enough that it worked) and leaves on a massive cliff hanger for the concluding ToCS4. As usual, the main story unfolds very slowly in a structured way and most of the real excitement is in the last 2 chapters. This slow pacing is a recurring issue in the series, but the early game events are fun enough that I didn't mind it too much.For gameplay, the combat is fluid and feels fun. Nightmare is far easier than even hard from the Trails in the Sky saga, but there a couple of difficulty spikes early on, before you can customise your team much. Once you have freedom to set yourself up and optimise and depending on who is in your party at the time, it's often possible to win battles without even giving a boss a single turn through skilful use of the break system and orders, allowing insane turn manipulation combos. In short, it's pretty imbalanced, but it's fun, flashy and fluid, which I think is all you need for a game that relies mainly on its story and characters.I enjoyed having an adult mentor figure as the protagonist this time  after a time skip from the previous game and the world building as always is the game's main strength as you get to explore various cities and really feel a sense of attachment to all the characters you've slowly gotten to know before the inevitable major crisis puts them all in danger- and to a greater extent than anything we've seen in previous chapters.The new Vantage Masters minigame is actually a surprisingly fun strategy card game- I could see myself playing this on a tabletop. It's a shame the AI is very dumb, so any kind of coherent gameplan and smart plays will easily win except versus a couple of "boss" opponents. I definitely enjoyed this a lot, though playing without a guide I missed collecting 1 card somewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Since this is part III of the Trails of Cold Steel series, you should know how it goes by now. Great story, great music, great worldbuilding and of course great characters. In regards to the improvements:- Graphics are quite a bit better all around;- Hidden events are indicated on the minimap;- UI and combat got improved (Break status);- Fishing bait isn't limited anymore;- More character customization options (3 parts instead of 2, and some different hair colours you can collect).There are still free days, campus days, cities you travel to, and lots of backstories to take in. But this time you have an interesting new roster of Class VII, who are all great characters in their own right. In this part of the series the history of Erebonia will become a lot clearer, but plenty of questions remain. So enjoy the continuation of the story, with old and new characters and allies alike (Altina yey!). So yeah, this gem of a series is easily the best game I have ever played. So do yourself a favour, and take a dive into the world of Erebonia/Zemuria. If you've come this far, you won't regret it one bit.

_childDocuments_.review: In general, I found this entry to be an improvement on Cold Steel 2; which was the low point in the entire Trails series for me. I quite enjoyed the instructor angle with Rean although he still is a bit of a blank slate. The new class 7/branch campus is a wonderful cast and I liked all of them. Free of the nobility/commoner issues of 1/2, they can focus on developing the personalities of the characters in more detail/in a natural manner. Plot wise, I'd say it's generally an improvement and it seems to be building up towards a significant end (finally). However everything to do with the writing still has the Cold Steel drawbacks. Hard to care as deeply as the Sky/Crossbell games. Further on, the execution of some story events or how some characters are being built up will still make you roll your eyes a bit.Though, going back to Crossbell in one of the chapters particularly hit very hard and I found myself getting quite emotional during those events. Gameplay wise, everything is solid (I played on hard difficulty). Though the new order systems and access to some good items early on really make this the easiest Trails game by far. You really can break the game Chapter 1 onwards.Visually, the character models are a big upgrade from 1/2 and finally can be enjoyed properly. The soundtrack in Cold Steel 3 for me has been the best of the Cold Steel games. Some really enjoyable tracks in there, notable mention to the Einhel Keep and the mech fight tracks. Overall, the game still has the same Cold Steel complaints of old. I'd just say make your peace with it and enjoy the good parts of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I played it offline on my Steam Deck, so I actually logged a few dozen hours and finished it despite the fact that it says I played it for 5 hours or so.Whereas Cold Steel I and II felt like Sky FC and SC, that is to say, a single really long game split in half, this one does feel like an actual sequel due to the fact that it picks over a year after the previous game's ending and that means a lot of things have changed. The Erebonian Civil War is over, Crossbell has been annexed, Class VII has graduated and gone on their separate ways, and Rean has become the instructor of a new Class VII in the newly established Thors Military Academy Branch Campus, while all the political scheming by the different governments and other groups like Ouroboros and the like continue.I loved this one because it felt like the story had moved forward quite a bit and we are starting to make sense of a lot of things that have been building up throughout eight whole games, and I also really enjoyed seeing some familiar faces come back and see everybody grow as characters. I especially loved being able to visit Crossbell and see how familiar and different it seemed under Erebonian rule, and see so many of the familiar NPC's I got to know in Zero and Azure, as well as catch up with Agate and a grown-up Tita. Gameplay-wise it was mostly what I expected, that is to say, the same systems from the previous games with a few minor tweaks. I'd say the biggest change in mechanics is the fishing mini-game.This is probably my favorite Cold Steel so far, though I realize many of the reasons why I loved it have to do with having played all the previous games in the franchise in release order. Now on to part IV.

_childDocuments_.review: A continuation of Trails of Cold Steel I and II. You don't need to have played the other two trails series to enjoy - they will definitely enhance the experience, but its not needed as Cold Steel follows Rean and his perspective of the events. You do need to play I and II first though. Trails in the Sky is available on steam if you would like to play that series. The Crossbell games are also now available for the full experience.That being said Cold Steel III is another long game. It has a lot of similarities to CS I. Be warned that this game doesn't have an ending and CS IV will pick up where it leaves off. Just like CS I and II. So you may want to wait for IV to get closer to release before purchasing/finishing the game. Think of CS I/II as the first chapter and CS III/IV as the second. Total gametime for the CS series when IV is here will likely run you over 320 hours.The combat system is mostly the same, but with new features that can be way too powerful when used correctly. Even on the hardest difficulty the game is fairly easy with the right combinations, but its still satisfying to find those combinations bringing out the maximum potential of each character. The Mech battles (previous you really only used your Valimar) were further refined and there are a good amount of them throughout the game with the player controlling up to 3 units at a time. The difficulty of the mech battles are way too easy and mostly feel like a side game to add flair.The relationship system is somewhat different as link levels no longer equal trust levels. You'll have to pick and choose who to boost your relationships with. This includes your new Class VII members as well as the old ones and several other characters. On the plus side you won't be limited to seeing just one special scene at the end of the game in a single playthrough. A good amount of these are potentially romantic, but most are just bonding with your companions.The graphics definitely got a big boost in this game and its nice to see everyone with the updated style. It does actually take getting some used to though as it feels like a simplistic/trendy style compared to the previous games.It was a rare thing, but I did sometimes notice the VAs sounded off or that it sounded like they were talking into a cheaper mic. The game has as much dialogue voiced as previous titles if you look at the numbers, but sometimes voices are used for one line and then not again or only used in one a couple lines at the end of a conversation. It actually gets pretty annoying at certain points for the voices to be going in and out. You'll have a lot of conversations where Rean isn't voiced, but whoever he is talking to is. Unfortunately there are various bonding event/relationship scenes like this which really takes away from them. Sometimes I even wished they wouldn't voice anyone in a scene because it was so distracting to go from reading to listening to reading to listening.Overall I liked most of the new characters and thought the story was decent enough.One of the biggest issues of the series is that its pretty much a shounen anime where the writers are too afraid to kill off anyone despite the fact they are fighting with guns/mechs/tanks/etc. It can often feel like no matter what you do you can't actually beat the bad guys. This makes it feel more like a VN where you are just watching the story unfold with battles only being arcade games with no real meaning. This feeling wasn't as bad in CS I/II as you are a bunch of kids (and you do actually make a difference in II), but sadly its a constant factor in CS III. Hoping CS IV gives us back the feeling of accomplishment, but even if it doesn't its still a fantastic series if you are willing to put in a lot of hours to play through it all.

_childDocuments_.review: A really great game and I enjoyed it a lot (Story, Characters & Gameplay). It's a step up from the previous games and continues the story from where it left off in II with characters from the other games (Sky, Zero & Azure) start to come together. What blew me away most first when launching the game was that I was greeted with a really great music (Start Line) playing in the main menu. I will always let the main menu music loop itself once before starting to play the game every time i launched it. Overall, the whole soundtracks for the game is amazing starting from "Pancakes on the Way Home" all the way to "Spiral of Erebos". I even bought the digital album from Apple Music.You will be controlling the same main character from the previous two games but now have a different party to work with (which will be your main party). Old characters from the previous games will appear as party members from time to time but it is best to focus on the current main one. Characters are great, some are kind of a repeat personality from the previous games but overall still unique (Especially Ash & Musse).The story continues from the previous games with more of the lore and mystery explained. Due to that, different factions (Class VII, Bracers, SSS, etc.) start to come together to deal with the threat which felt really epic, knowing you've got all these talented people working with you at different parts of the world in their own way. This will also lead to one amazing adventure and climax which will be the next game, Trails of Cold Steel IV.Really looking forward to Trails of Cold Steel IV next year for Steam, and really hoping that the Crossbell Arc gets localised so I can buy to play it, understand the story and also support the developers.All in all, a great game that will explain more of the lore and mystery that has been around.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing through the entire Trails series in order, this one is one of my favorites. IMO it's prob not quite as good as a game as sky sc, but it might be more fun to play. I really enjoyed the revamped combat system, and it looks great too. The only issue with combat is some of the new features (orders) can be broken at times. I beat big name bosses without getting touched multiple times abusing the system. I would say combat balance is a bit off, most enemies (even mini bosses) on the map are laughable easy. And some of the bosses you either don't let them even touch you, or they one shot your entire team using their S crafts. Minor annoyance there, but overall combat is super fun.People who have played Sky and crossbell series will love a lot of the fan service. This game does A LOT more to bring up previous games than CS 1 or 2. You even get to play as quite a few former characters. The story is pretty good, but it can get a bit much at times. There is so much going on with so many people it can get confusing. I think that is what they are going for setting up future games though.One of my biggest gripes with CS2 was I hated Rean so much. He was such a weiner kid. He is not near as lame in this game. He is still however apparently the only man in the world any girl wants to hook up with. It can be kind of laughable watching every girl in the game fight over him, but laughable in a fun way. This game packs a lot of adult jokes in a light hearted anime looking game, I did find that fun.Very good game, I'm mad that as a pc user I have to wait an unknown amount of months to play CS 4 now though =[

_childDocuments_.review: This is the demo that got me into one of my new most favorite series! Such a treat whenever a new title releases. It feels like one of those series that constantly rewards you for being a fan. Each game is a fun JRPG with plenty of content and characters to explore and learn about. An incredibly detailed and well fleshed out world, and a fun story with nice connectivity between different titles and arch's. Yes, it's not the most incredibly well-written, with nearly 50+ playable characters and over 10 titles, with returning villains and different plot threads, all connecting up with one another, it's not really feasible to do so, nor is it really the draw of the series imo either. I think what makes Trails so fun and engaging, is seeing how the universe and world gets more fleshed out with each entry. To me it's lighthearted,  and fun, whilst also still having enough of those more serious moments and plot points to keep you engaged and wanting more. It's cool to see how protagonists you play in one title, then return as say, a side character or additional party member to you in another title of the series. With each title, you see more and more different sides to your characters . I can't think of another series that quite does this, and that to me is why I love the series so much. It's very much investing in a kind of universe/world, and the more you get in the more you feel rewarded for it.If you've ever wondered if the Trails series is right for you, try the demo. If it isn't for you, then it isn't for you and I wouldn't bother, but if it is! I highly recommend jumping in! I personally started at Trails of Cold Steel (TOCS) 1 after trying this demo and immediately was excited to jump into TOCS 2 right after as a result.Don't worry too much on the exact title you start with, it's not the end of world to start here with TOCS 3, or 1. Only try the even older titles (e.g., Trails in the Sky, and Trails in the Sky Second Chapter) if you know for sure really want to: they're definitely a bit aged by today's standards. I think they're at their most fun and enticing for big fans of the series that want all the lore they can get

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really hard game to recommend outright because there are so many caveats to a recommendation for a game that's the third game in a series which is, itself, the third of three arcs. If you've never played any Cold Steel games before: Not recommended. Play at least 1 and 2. If you've played just Cold Steel 1 and 2: Possible recommend; this is the part where a lot of characters and plotlines start crossing over from the other arcs in the series. The dialogue does a pretty okay job of filling in most of the gaps if you really want to skip the other two arcs, but you'll get the full experience if you start with Trails in the Sky First Chapter (also on Steam). If you've played Trails in the Sky, the Crossbell games, and Cold Steel 1/2: You probably already own this and why are you bothering to read my review?It's more Cold Steel: sweet characters with tender moments of connection and characterization, a colorful world, a great soundtrack, some janky combat (strongly recommend a balance mod) and the occasional writing or plot detour that makes you question the blood alcohol level of the writer. The new Class VII are more interesting and seem better written than most of the old Class VII. There's a lot of quality of life stuff added, like fast travel through more than just cities and you almost always have access to a horse or the orbal cycle for faster travel. There's still an Old Schoolhouse-like mechanic, but the runs are a lot shorter and you don't spend as much time in there. The Divine Knight battles are more or less the same, but added mechanics allow for a bit more dynamism than in previous outings. On the downside, there seems to be less voice acting and entire conversations between the main character and others where only one person's lines are spoken (at least in the English; I don't know if the Japanese voices are like that). Angelica is still a pile of miserable LGBTQ+ tropes, most female characters look like they were designed by a hentai artist, and there's an outright molestation scene that's played off for laughs (it was between villains, but still) and the game does crawl at parts. So it's fine: it's still Cold Steel and if you've gotten this far into the series, you're going to play it no matter what. If you haven't, I'd still say it's a good game (if you can handle the aforementioned downsides)....provided you step back and play the previous games in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are afraid of long games and even longer series, I do not recommend this for you.If you made it this far into the games you probably are in for the long haul lol.This was kino once again, though I do wanna say that some of the new additions make this even more ridiculous than Cold Steel 2's combat. Orders and the Break gauge are very welcome mechanics to add more wrinkles to combat, but there are some specific ones (Delay -70% and certain other orders that have ACCELERATE) that let you infinitely loop an enemy into the grave for every fight once you have those unlocked. Sledgehammer Gaming. Of course, you can actively choose not to wipe the floor with the game if you want, and there are TONS of customization options if you choose not to, it's super fun. But with just that strategy you can basically kill anything and everything. Mech fights are much improved and way more fun, they feel a lot better than CS2's, which are obviously way better than CS1s but not a lot of variety. Now you have more allies, break, cheaper Finisher (and rush in regular fights, whoops) and partner arts are more useful. Just lots of fun in general, but this is still a bit of a slow burn. For me it was about 16 hours longer than Cold Steel 2. If you're like me you might get antsy as the hours go on and want the game to just end or speed things up. 6x fast forward is your friend.Looking forward to playing CS4 now.

I played this with a fan-made Chinese language patch so steam no longer recognizes my in-game status.The game is amazing, it lives up to the expectation of a trails fan. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:If you've never played a Trails game before, this is a terrible entry point. The latest starting point for you is Cold Steel 1.For those invested in the series: You will get this anyway, and you are right to do so now more than ever.Review:The text-heavy RPG franchise is back with a decent enough translation. Almost all of the NPCs still get their own story told over time, and reading what everyone has to say is still rewarding, though less so compared to the previous entries.The English VA is still hit or miss, though at least they were able to keep most of the actors for continuity's sake.Rean is less annoying, the new class 7 is comparably interesting to the old, graphics got a slight upgrade,  the music is great, and the PC port is fantastic.What makes CS:3 great for LoH fans, especially those who've played since Trails in the Sky, is that much of what we've learned, people we've met, places we've visited, politics we've witnessed get tied into the fold and continue to be fleshed out and built upon. "Oh so THAT's why xxxx tried to xxxx in Trails the 2nd"! It's a shame the Crossbell arc wasn't translated, but CS:3 does a good job of getting you up to speed. I don't know how a series like this still manages to sell in an ADHD social media world, but I will continue to throw money at Nihon Falom for as long as they keep the spirit of the franchise alive.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to preface that this game just absolutely ripped me to shred. I ain't felt like this since playing the Crossbell Saga. This is the eighteenth installment of the Legend of Heroes series. This game is essentially the beginning of the time skip within the Trail of Cold Steel / Erebonia World. This means that this game and review will contain many spoilers and knowledge required from previous games.This is the eighteenth installment of the Legend of Heroes franchise, and I recommend for those who want to enter this game to follow the story in order. This is essentially the marvel cinematic universe. And this is pretty much: Marvel Avenger: Infinity War of this entire game series. You do not want to lose out on various key information has it's a big part of the connecting lore of the 3 sagas. The following games are played in order:Trail in the Sky FC,Trail in the Sky SC,Trail in the Sky the 3rd,Trails from Zero,Trails to Azure,Trails of Cold Steel 1,Trails of Cold Steel 2.( There is an anime called Legend of Heroes: Northern War which further explains the North Ambria War and what centered around the time Rean became the Ashen Chevalier. ) It isn't required, however, it gives an insight into some crucial parts.This story takes place 2 years after TOCS 2. Rean is older now and has taken a job as an instructor in Thor's Branch Campus. He is tasked with instructing a new class 7 who will be the center of the last two Trail of Cold Steel games. You will be familiar with the unique setting from TOCS 1 as you are back within the school arc. However, there are key notes including that Rean has become a hero, original class 7 have made it big in the world and returning characters from Crossbell and Liberal saga will be returning to this game.  Rean during the events between TOCS 2 and 3 has essentially been bossed around by the Blood and Iron Chancellor, Osborne. As he fought to annex Crossbell and North Ambria while minimizing casualties. This story takes place after as you will be going along with New Class 7 to see the post aftermath of the Noble War and Annexation of two major cities. As this is the calm before a big ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ storm, you will slowly begin to unravel the mysteries behind the Phantasmal Blaze Plan, the secrets behind the Black Workshop, Ouroboros and The Imperial Government. The key characters in this game have been probably one of my favorites so far, especially with the return of my favorites including . This story is heartwarming, heart wrenching and filled with lore that you won't find in any other Legend of Heroes game so far. I have cried a few times playing this game which I haven't done since Ao no Kiseki / Trails to Azure.The characters  being memorable and amazing has now been further enhanced by the crazy upgrade to the Art style and Graphics. I have to take this part to talk about it because it's a HUGE STEP UP from the last game. The UI is clean, the crafts are nicer and the environment in this game is absolutely stunning. I do have problems in 1 - 2 areas that have FPS drops but it was worth it taking in everything. This accompanying the new music has been such a delight lately. This is probably my most spent hours on any Legend of Heroes game so far primarily because of everything that it gives. I have yet to start TOCS 4 yet and I will keep you posted in the next review for that. So far, everything has been such a delight to my eyes that it left a genuine tear.Now the gameplay is amazing. What I really mentioned before was how diverse the game can be when you are testing out new builds on various characters. Tanker, debuffer, cp battery, damage dealer, arts spammer, etc. This game has really outdone themselves with the new introduction of Battle Orders and Double Master Quartz Equip. I think this is one of the greatest directions they have done so far in the series as it allows us to pick and choose different strategies when playing this game. And I think that's extremely important, the versatility it can give and the sense of thinking has left me with nothing but praise. Thank you Nihon Falcom. I do also want to briefly mention that tactics have been so much nicer now that you can adjust your party anywhere in the grid, which further enhances the diversity and flexibility of this game.The difficulty is actually challenging. It does still have some things that can be easily abusable if you really look for it. However this game actually has a really nice nightmare difficulty. It can get pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous if you not farming constantly or building your character. I followed a guide on what to build which you can find here if you are lost like me when starting out: I also followed a guide from Zoelius which I think the community should give a round of applause for the handwork that Zoelius has done for our community with these guides. But not just Zoelius:. Zennvirus, TheDarkn1ght and Berserker Blade deserve props too. The difficulty helped promote building around certain scenarios at times and also gave you a diverse amount of setups and a range of teams that can really give you a run for your money.Music choice in this game this time was actually really nice. It really fits the game atmosphere and as you go onward towards the final chapter, you really feel the setting that they were trying to portray. The battle theme isn't that bad either and I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love it when they pull out the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ opening theme during battles. ♥♥♥♥ got me hyped the ♥♥♥♥ out. Cities have wonderful music, the environment has calming themes, everything that this game has done continues to improve with each game. And I know that people complain about the lack of good music recently, but I think they are trying their best to keep on improving and I really appreciate their efforts.We are back again with collectables. And a lot of books then before, you will be collecting recipes, black records, chronicles, etc. While getting bonding gifts for old and new class 7 characters along with additional characters. The gifting system and bonding events in this game has made a lot of them deeply memorable and (Some of them are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing). The side quests in this game are actually quite nice too because you will be able to see returning characters from previous games and previous antagonists come back during the story and side quests. This game pretty much rewards you well for keeping up with the series through these side quests while also giving you pieces of lore of side characters from  previous characters. In case people were always wondering what happened to this or that person. Again turbo mode is of course back and it's really nice to have with us again. I have 100% the game now and man doing playthrough after playthroughs because I missed one and two things sucks. This is why I decided to look at a guide for TOCS 4 now. I recommend this game to those who are continuing to support and follow the game closely. We are reaching the end game of the Trail of Cold Steel saga. The unique and insane story is slowly taking a major turn and you definitely wanna play this game out to finally get the answers you've been slowly looking for. This game will bring in the 3 sagas into the settings of Erebonia and begin to unravel the mysteries of the biggest antagonist yet. Be sure to go back and play the previous games to keep yourself updated because the next game is Marvel's Avenger: Endgame. Everyone is coming back including your favourite protagonist from the previous game. To finally conclude the Trail of Cold Steel Series. I have been following and being a fan of this game for a long time and I am proud of it. I'll finally get to see you all over in the next game:THE LEGEND OF HEROES: TRAILS OF COLD STEEL 4: THE END OF SAGA!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
