_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has completed The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III thoroughly twice now (first on the PS4, then on the PC), I have now decided to review this game. My overall rating of this game is that it is a masterpiece. The Trails (Kiseki) series is my favourite video game series of all time, because of four main things: 1. The rich story and writing, 2. The characters and character development, 3. The world building and interconnection between each game, and 4. The music, all of which are, in my experience, unparalleled to any other video game / video game series out there. Trails of Cold Steel III is certainly no exception to this, and is, so far, my favourite game in this series.For those who are new to this series, I highly recommend starting off with Trails in the Sky FC, and then playing each Trails game in chronological order, like I did. This is because unless you do so, you will not understand a lot of the references that are made in this game (Unfortunately, Zero and Ao no Kiseki have not been officially translated into English yet, and although there are fan translations of them, I prefer to wait until the official translations are released). I also highly recommend not watching any playthroughs of this game and avoiding all spoilers prior to playing it. Trails of Cold Steel III, like every other Trails game, is best played when you do not know what to expect.One significant difference between Trails of Cold Steel III from the previous two Trails of Cold Steel games are that the graphics have significantly improved in this game. Certain locations, such as , , and even  at sunset, look visually stunning. In addition, the character models look much nicer and smoother than before, and their movements and animations are much less clunky.The soundtrack of this game is amazing. Every day I find myself listening to Trails music on YouTube because of how good it is. If I were to pick out my top five songs for this game, they would be the following: 1. "Brave Steel", 2. "Now, Thing to Do", 3. "Beyond a Little Hope", 4. "Little Rain", and 5. "Burning Appearance".In this game your homebase is , where . It is similar to Trails of Cold Steel I in that you spend a day doing various quests in the village, and at the end of that day Rean and  go through a trial. Then you spend three days at several locations where you do , and where you encounter the main antagonists. Then you return and spend an evening in , where you can talk to people and do various quests, and the cycle repeats itself.The combat of Trails of Cold Steel III is turn-based like every other Trails game. This time, though, whenever you enter a battle, instead of warping to a pre-made battle map, the battle takes place in whichever location you are at on the map. In addition, each time you unbalance an enemy, you receive Brave Points (BP), which you can use to issue Orders. Orders give you special bonuses in battle and can be used once per turn. I found the combat system of Trails of Cold Steel III to be highly enjoyable, and the default battle BGM, Brave Steel, is in my opinion, the best BGM in the whole soundtrack. .I will not comment much on the story, since I want this review to be as spoiler-free as possible. All I will say is that the story and writing is the best thing about Trails of Cold Steel III (and every other Trails game). I enjoyed seeing Rean develop in character and maturity in his new role as an . I also enjoyed learning about the different members of the , each of whom are very interesting and likeable, like Rean and the . It was also good to see . Moreover, I was greatly interested in seeing the central antagonists' mysterious plans unfold gradually. Although the game is quite slow-paced, especially early on, there were many exciting moments in the story later on which made me eager to see how things would play out. The new locations were fun to explore while things were building up, anyway. Regarding the conclusion,  Also, just a quick caution: there are a few scenes in which the characters bathe and talk to one another. Fortunately, they are not naked, and most of the conversations are just about the characters' lives.Another great thing about this game is the NPC dialogue. Like in every other Trails game, in this game each NPC is full of life and has their own unique story to tell, so if you are eager to learn more about the game's world, I highly recommend you talk to every NPC you encounter. Furthermore, I recommend talking to every NPC more than once, since almost all of them have between 2–4 different sets of dialogue each time you speak to them. I have found that the NPCs give the game a very pleasant and immersive atmosphere, much more than in any other game I have played. Sometimes they even give you extra quests to fulfil, so that is another incentive to talk with them all.Although I have not listened to the Japanese voice acting for Trails of Cold Steel III yet, I was greatly impressed with the English voice acting. I can tell that each of the voice actors were carefully selected for the role, and that they all gave it their best shot, which I appreciate.Regarding mini games, there are two main ones: the first is fishing, similar to the previous Trails games, and the second is a new card game called Vantage Masters. In contrast to the previous card game, Blades, this one requires a lot more strategy. There is actually a moment in the story in which you have to play Vantage Masters, so it is best to at least learn the basics of it, for those who do not like card games.I will now end this review on one last positive note. I greatly appreciate the little moments in this game that made me laugh or that I found to be heartwarming. It is moments like these in the Trails series that keep me coming back to it.  In addition, I found it very satisfying to do all of Altina's bonding events,  In conclusion, as I said before, my final rating for this game is that it is a masterpiece. (Just like all the other Trails games) I highly recommend The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III to all people who love story-rich JRPGs with highly interconnected narratives and strong world building, and I look forward to playing more entries in this great series.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even begin with this?Trails of Cold Steel 3 is, as the name suggests, the third game in this Trails series. While I found the first two games to be quite enjoyable and generally competent, this third installment blew all my expectations clean out of the water. The game handles itself with uncommon grace and poise. Combat is similar to the previous games with some minor feature improvements, but that is hardly criticism considering its elegance and relative ease-of-learning. The master quartz and gem system has also maintained its core features, with a secondary master quartz system adding more customization options and flexibility to what has always been a rather engaging system of personalization.However, where this episode really hits its stride and surpasses its previous entries is in the story. Without spoiling too much, the journey through this installment will not only see you leading a new Class VII, but also bring back the entire cast of the first two games for an encore performance. For anyone who has played the first two games, you would have grown to love most, if not all, of the original cast (if not, you’re probably a monster). To see them all return now, in their respective positions as leaders in various spheres of society and legends from their various contributions in the first two games is truly awe-inspiring, and a generous payoff for any series veteran who has stuck it out the first two games. The returning cast makes more than just a token appearance, however, and continues to play active roles throughout the entirety of the game, as not only party members, but also mentors to the new successors in Class VII. This is a story of kinship and bonding that was only possible to cultivate through several games worth of preparation and emotional investment.The new cast is mostly likeable (Musse is a true gem of a character, and probably one of my favorites in any game), and the old extended cast from the previous games all get some time to shine in this game as well.  While the writing is very occasionally clumsy, and the many lore elements more than often confusing due to its sheer aggregated volume, the vast majority of the game generally conducts itself with confidence, and the twists and turns are more spectacular than ever in the series. This is also a game not bothered by its dated graphics and animation, but concerned only with delivering an epic across several titles. At the time of writing this review, this game has an ‘Overwhelmingly Positive’ review across the board, and it is easy to see why. For anyone who has played through the first two games, you already know whether or not you want to play the third – this is an absolute no-brainer for you (why are you even reading this?). For anyone who is considering picking this up, but who did not play the first two games, I highly recommend you go back and play the first two instead of reading through the summary that is available in the main menu of this game – the pay-off is well worth it.This has proven to be a saga well worth following, and I absolutely cannot wait for the final game in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Warning:  Long review incoming.  The TL;DR is that this game is absolutely amazing.-Objective review I wrote after I gathered myself from the emotional tidal wave-This game is absolutely incredible - but that is no surprise seeing that every game in the Trails series is a masterpiece.  There simply is no other series in video games that does world-building like this.  This is the eighth game of said series, and basically is like the "Avengers" of this universe as it finally starts blending all of the different arcs and characters together.With that being said, you might not want to start this as your first Trails title seeing that all the games in the series build on one another.  Ideally, there are two ways to go through the series if you don't speak Japanese.  The first is the order of release:Trails in the SkyTrails in the Sky SCTrails in the Sky 3CTrails from Zero (no English release yet)Trails to Azure (no English release yet)Trails of Cold Steel Trails of Cold Steel IITrails of Cold Steel III However, if you don't want to bother at first with buying the Japanese version of Zero and Azure then downloading fan translations (the Geofront one for Zero is excellent quality, and they are working on Azure), you can go in this order (which is what I did):Trails in the SkyTrails in the Sky SCTrails in the Sky 3CTrails of Cold Steel Trails of Cold Steel IITrails from Zero (no English release yet)Trails to Azure (no English release yet)Trails of Cold Steel III This is okay because Zero/Azure spoil CS/CSII and vice versa.  Once you get to the point that you need Zero and Azure though, you'll be so hooked you won't be bothered about having to jump through a few hoops to play them.You COULD also treat this as your first entry just to test the waters to see if you mechanically like the game, but don't expect to understand a huge amount of references being made throughout the game.  There's a history section available in the main menu of the game that summarizes the stories of CS1 & CS2, but it serves as a refresher for those picking the series back up after having played those titles rather than being a comprehensive replacement for having played those titles.  If your hell-bent on starting w/ the Cold Steel series, I'd suggest just playing CS1 and CS2 to make sure you like the series, then going back and catching the previous titles before diving into this one.Regardless of order though, you have to play the Trails series as a whole if you are a JRPG fan.  You will literally find nothing like this in gaming.-Subjective review I wrote right after the credits rolled-I've been a die-hard JRPG fan since I first was introduced to Final Fantasy I on the NES as an idiot grade school kid. I have grown up with this genre, and it has been one of my greatest passions and escapes throughout my childhood into my adult life.As an adult, I tripped over Trails in the Sky in 2013 by accident and thought I'd give it a try. I was immediately hooked and played through the trilogy. I could not get enough of this world Falcom had built. At that time, the Cold Steel arc was all that was readily available to me so I played through 1 & 2 even though all of my research was pointing out that Zero and Azure were must-plays.I put the series down for a bit after that until I heard they were localizing Cold Steel 3. I knew I needed to be caught up for it. As such, I read threads on reddit to figure out how to buy and translate the Crossbell arc which I have literally never done for any other game. They were absolutely amazing and more than worth the effort I put into figuring out how to play them as a monolingual dude from the Southeast US.Tonight, I finally finished Cold Steel 3, and I am beside myself. It is so bittersweet for me. At last, I've caught up, but I couldn't be more melancholy. If you guys need me, I'll be in a corner in the fetal position in a puddle of my own tears. These games are the best.(Thanks for coming to my Ted Talk.)

_childDocuments_.review: This review is intended for people who haven't bought the game and are unsure whether they want to purchase it yet. The best advice I can give is, if you think you will like this game don't worry about the reviews just play and enjoy. My negative review is just a guess on how the majority of people reading reviews for advice might end up feeling if they bought and played it.1) If you're new to the genre or video games in general, don't start here. This game is a big time sink and also not among the best of it's genre. Play the persona series, pokemon, or maybe some dragon quest.2) If you're new to the series but are familiar with the genre, don't start with this one. The story is the main draw here and you will be missing all the context the series has built up over many games. Play the crosbell duology or the trails in the sky trilogy. Ideally both before tackling any of the cold steel games.3) If you have played all the other games (or at least cold steel 1 and 2) I honestly think this game isn't worth your time. Your time is precious and honestly the game does not earn your money. Here is where I'm going to start breaking down the game for people (SPOILER FREE)Audio:The game has fine sound effects, fine music, the voice acting is usually ok although some of the lines and the hammy acting can kind of be distracting. I don't blame the voice actors tho I think anime is cringe and reading translated works in english is just insanely hard to get right. There isn't a ton of new music original to this game (that I noticed) and nothing stood out to me. I won't be looking up any tracks to listen to on my own time at least.Visuals:The visuals on display are fine. Definitely a step up from previous titles in the cold steel games, but it lacks a lot of personality. The game has a basic cookie cutter art style and I doubt me or most other people would be able to distinguish art in this game from other anime/anime style games. Characters occasionally have drip. The game throughout it's runtime will often repeat camera movement in a pretty irritating way. To me it feels like a lazy "We'll just copy and paste this camera movement 100 times" type of design that I really don't like. Occasionally the settings can be nice but they are all really similar. There are a few levels and towns that are a nice change of pace and I really appreciate them.Gameplay:This game has 3 "modes". Visual Novel mode where you are reading through a combination of dialogue and inner thoughts. Free Roam mode where you are walking around the world and going to either battle or talk. Finally Combat mode where you are fighting things in your turn based format. This all funnels into gameplay but I think they represent different aspects of the design of the game so I'm gonna discuss each.Visual Novel/Narrative:This story is (in my subjective opinion) overall not very good. I like anime and while I struggle to really love jrpg stories, this one stands out to me as a particularly poor experience. I have had worse, but not many. This game is designed as an "infinity war" vibe bringing in characters from previous games in order to have a really bombastic feel, so to pick up on all the intricacies you need to have 7 whole other games in your memory. I'm not gonna pick on it for that because the audience that is continuing to play it are likely going to meet that requirement. That said, I do think the story plays so hard into tropes and contrivances that it is legitimately hard to take seriously. I don't mind some tropes, but I really hate the harem aspect of anime and this plays into it a lot.That said there are some moments or reveals I really enjoy. There is a particular plotline regarding the main characters family that actually is gripping whenever two characters share a room and it's exciting to watch that get teased. Those moments however are way too few and far between to earn it's 100 hours of SPED UP gameplay.Free Roam/Exploration:The game has some fun hidden side quests that necessitate exploring the world and the world has a lot of lore. We actually get to read about it's lore and even see how it's rich history is reflected in the fiction of the world. Awesome. I also like the strategic elements of equipping your characters with different loadouts. This game is actually at it's best when you are challenged by the future combat encounters to the point of deliberately equipping your characters with specific move sets to allow you to overcome the challenges ahead. It can be meticulous but it's very rewarding to hit on a few fun builds or strategies. The game has also increased it's strategic arsenal by allowing for Brave Orders (Party wide buffs that require certain characters to be in your party) and secondary master quartz, allowing you to mix and match master quartz abilities in a way that inspires creative build diversity. Characters tend to be suited for specific playstyles but this is still engaging and you have a lot of flexibility. The game inherits most of these good elements from the previous titles, but they make the game more fun and it does expand on it so cool it is nice in this way.Combat:I have the least to say about this. They have really not innovated that much on this element of play since way back in the first trails of the sky title. They have made next to no changes since the first cold steel title. This is honestly a little one not. Combat will slowly become a chore as you progress through the game. The strategies are fun to execute, but you really only need to do that a few times, and third of this game if not more is spent in combat. This is what you sign up for when playing a turn based game, but yes there is not a whole lot of variation or excitement in this aspect of play.Overall I think if you care about the story, watch a video breaking it down. Read about what happens. Don't get sucked into a 100 hour game where the moment to moment story telling and are a drag to get through for way too little payoff.Also if you think you would like this game, or you have already played it and enjoyed it, Awesome! I would much rather people like this game than not. It's just that I don't have that expectation for most players. That said if you've made it this far in the trails series maybe you love the story telling and the gameplay. My personal experience was that I got bored of the gameplay and the story telling feels worse than the other games and it's not like they masterpieces before.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I am updating my review. So far this is what I think:TLDR: If you don't own a PS4 or PS5, get this version. Now, the good:The graphics are better than the PS4, crisp and beautiful. The game can renders more than the PS4 could and all that, so in general you're having the exact same version of the PS4 Version 1.0 here on PC with better graphics, constant 60FPS and if your PC is good enough, no slow downs at all.The bad:The game has two big points I hate on PC.The UI carries the PS3 button layout from Cold Steel I and II replacing the PS4 button layout from the original game this was ported from. I don't know why, I can see why the TURBO icon is the same, to keep the "consistency" there, but the PS3 buttons looks ugly and unfinished in the PC version.But the worst of all, is the fact that this game STILL didn't get the updates the PS4 version has. One example: You have to apply a patch made by fans to fix quartz descriptions and functons so they actually work in-game. That IS fixable by patches, what is not are script errors: The first time you met Neighthart when you go see Eliot`s father, Laura congratulates him for his promotion, a very in-character for a formal noble lady like her who respect others and aknowledges their growth. In english on the 1.0 scrip, she just says: HeeHee. Like she's Alissa seing someone being funny in front of her. In japanese you can hear her congratulating him while the Hee-Hee line is on your face.That made me so angry on PS4 at the time, but they fixed there, and when I decide to get the game here I see that this issue is still present here. IT's not like they have to do a lot of work, they fixed for PS4, why can't they fix here on PC too? NISA should keep consistent with every single platform they have. While I'm having to deal with these small nit-picks (but for a stoy-based-game an error in translation is not that small), Trails from Zero is getting updates for freaking Water particles that no one will go look at them. What I'm trying to say is this: If you have the PS4 version of this game, you don't need to buy the PC version, but if you do, you will have a beautiful version with better FPS and rendering BUT you will still have the 1.0 erros in translation (that exists in a lot of places), and you will have to accept the Old 360 or PS3 button schemes because someone thought it would be nice to replace the good looking buttons instead of updating their XBOX versions to the one, just downgrade the PS4 to 3 versions. IT looks awful. But that's a nit-pick. again, I can't say enough: This series are awesome. But it's clear that it's not Nisa`s will to update this game anymore, even if they have done in other platforms. And that's just sad, a trend I didn't want from them.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game has all the makings of a fantastic JRPG classic. It's long, has a great cast of characters, good voice acting, deep lore and all the rest. OK, the music is a bit repetitive and the combat has gotten pretty boring after 3 games. But still, it could've been a classic. But right after finishing it, I just wish I'd bought it on a DVD so I could throw the thing in the trash. I'm SO TIRED of:1. Fights where you win, but the opponent you beat gets to their feet with a "well fought, but clearly you're nowhere near as strong as me yet!" AGAIN AND AGAIN.2. Smart storytelling and politics ruined by GLORIOUS NONSENSE metaplots with supernatural mcguffins that make ZERO sense whatsoever3. No bad guys ever die, they just keep coming back. But the game is fine with sacrificing your friends when it feels like it. USELESS.4. Bad guys with zero rationale for all the stupid stuff they do.5. Everyone being related to one another.6. No one being able to actually, coherently explain the background despite literally dozens of hours of text. Is this just poor translation? Or is the original japanese game this confused itself?7. Final thing: I like Rean, but the first game at least had other characters with conflicts and desires and goals. In this game, NO ONE BUT REAN MATTERS. Every girl loves him, every guy wants to be his friend. There are no other friendships, no other romances. It's all about Rean, and only about Rean. It's like he's a black hole, sucking in all the light from anything that passes close by.8. Really final thing: The game never ends. It's like the death scene in Deadpool 2 where he spends like 5 minutes dying for comedic effect. The game just goes on and on and on. If it had ended at Chapter 4's end, it might've been decent. But wow, the last chapter/ending section is just endless cutscenes and brain pain.I've loved this series, and I really enjoyed parts of this game. But I need a few years break from this series before I can stomach another shrilly voice screaming out "REAN!" or the chanchellor's ridiculous voice talking glorious nonsense.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a third game, out of a 4 game arc, which sits as the third arc in the greater scheme of an ongoing JRPG series. Most reviewers will inform you to not start with this game first and to at least backtrack to Cold Steel 1 (preferably Trails in the Sky even) better appreciate the enjoyment in this game. Trails of Cold Steel III I can best describe as a colorfully beautiful but messy game. It has at many moments made me smile and have me in excited suspense, while other times left me lulled to sleep or constantly being in and out of the game trudging through slow parts. Being the third entry it has succeeded two games which means there are similarities and improvements made leading to this entry. But also unfortunately there are either new issues or the same issues that also exist. I would prefer to list my most important generalized pro/con first:Cons:•	Bonding events are still in the game, these events have always felt shallow to me since games like Persona are better suited for these. I would rather they do the fire emblem route where they would trigger from utilizing characters rather than just checking in to raise points I guess. •	Semi-voiced cutscenes – many times characters will have cutscenes that aren’t voiced, but then you will have another character who is being fully voice acted on their lines but then people will reply with unvoiced lines. It just comes off as goofy because in the Crossbell arc they at least used the semi-voicing to emphasize important messages and not disjoint. •	Now more than ever, the main character is a dislike for me. He is a character who is loved by everyone for doing the bare minimum, everybody idolizes him, and I don’t believe the game does a good job of convincing me why I should enjoy him the way the game loves him. •	Repetitive formula – if you’re like me, the repetition in Cold Steel 1 bored you to the point where it hurt, this game thankfully does it much better but its still repetitive. The chapters move the same after you’ve experienced chapter 1 unfortunately. •	Losing cutscenes – a general trope among JRPGs, but they’re egregious in this game. So often you fight a boss that is supposed to be out of your league, only to absolute smoke them in game and then the cutscene will show you hunched over wondering why they’re so strong. It’s annoying because if I’m going to lose to these people at least do me the courtesy of being smacked by the boss and then at last minute cutting away or something more interesting for the game. All too often they will just bring in a new character that wasn’t in the fight to do the “not so fast” thing and intervene and save you. Happens in every chapter. Pros: •	Music – the music in this series has always been enjoyable, and they continue to blow me away with great themes in and out of battle. A good chunk of this soundtrack is in my playlist•	Better animations – I am not sure if the game is running on a different engine, but if you’ve played CSI&II you’d know that those games moved very rigid for 3D games and overall looked pretty ugly by the standard that they were released in. Now in this game characters are much better animated with few stiff animations, hair physics (Laura’s strand of hair doesn’t clip through her chest anymore) that clip less, and improved facial animations as well. •	Expanded Battle system – there are two new features in battle, one is the break gauge for enemies, and the other is the Orders command. These new features add another layer to a great battle system that now rewards aggression and if timed correctly you can dog-pile bosses and turn the battle in your favor.•	Access to the Japanese & English Dub – CSI&II were only in English for our localized releases, many of the Vas in English just unfortunately are bad and it made playing those two games a headache for me. Having Japanese dubs back in 3 has allowed me to enjoy my time much more because you can tell the Japanese voices were originally directed with them in mind and the English ones tried to fit in as best they could. Some English VAs are still good, but many remain lackluster. •	CSI&II took out a lot of features that older trails games had that are integral to JRPG’s with a lot of reading, such as reading the chat log in case you missed or skipped a message and replaying the line. 3 brings back this feature, along with an insanely fast fast-forward feature which can make repeat playthroughs much quicker.Even with a list of negatives, I loved this game, and definitely had many standout moments in the mid-game and the final chapter was some of the most fun I had since Trails to Azure's end game between its suspense and final battles being personal bouts. I am excitedly moving to Cold Steel IV with optimism.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast. I think I got time-travelled to another dimension for about 250 hours or so.Being honest, I have been pre-ordered those expensive games for years now, however, only few of them is worth the price they originally offered, most of them just don’t prove themselves worthy. Neither being fun to play nor being educational for gaining some knowledge I don’t know. Yet, this game is entirely on another level, it’s like digging out a grand treasure in a royal vault. Though it happened to be a random per-order I’ve made in the past.I am more than respectful to see Falcom(the company behind development of this franchise )to grow, little by little, eventually become one of the finest video game makers in the world of JRPG genre. I played Sky FC around 2000s and loved it ever since. Alright, I won’t let myself get too carried away, so, here’s the real thing: I’d like to focus why Trails of Cold Steel III should be a no miss JRPG title and whats so special about it. In addition, I will divide this review in certain parts and sum in the end, hope to cover as many characteristics as possible, regarding the fantastic continent of Zemuria, the ultimate charm of the CS III.StoryThe all time favourite hero Rean Schwarzer, known as Ashen Chevalier is back! Now he’s one of the instructors of the brand new Thor Military Academy branch campus, breeding the children of the War of the Lions, the future of Erebonia. Lying down and enjoying the long waited peace within the nation while the crisis and destruction are lurking in the shadows. Forces are gathering, the war is imminent, super natural phenomenon is outbursting. The Erebonia empire is sitting on a brink of the peace before the hurricane of the despair strikes! This is your journey where it starts, as an instructor of the branch campus, to guide your next talented generations to prepare facing the unforeseen challenge ahead before all is too late. The story is unmistakably well-written, with vast rich lores serve its side, heavily real-life inspired political incidents planting across the story, it surely makes your nerve on edge at all times and never let you lose the interests to continue, while kept you busy guessing what’s the plot’s next move.CharacterCS III is not only an extraordinary lengthy game but also gathered a large scale of character section from the past 2 games(CS I & II) and made quite amount of heroes from the past return to push the story to its utter climax. While shipped the entire new group of protagonists(new Class VII) to you as the fresh blood in exchange. There are more than 20 characters you will get chance to play, moreover, the dev still managed to give every one of them an unique personal background: each one of them is recognised and  appreciated by its total difference. You probably will never mix them up since not a single character’s personal story is even similar, nor do them being easily forgotten, because everyone plays its irreplaceable part in this legend, and their paths are not just shining on their own but interwinds, comes across, constantly make you wows your journey while diving deeper into its story. Which will bring the next section on live. The...Dual AudiosBefore this game, I never really appreciate dual audios despite where I am from. I hardly set my game using English Audio since  large number of JRPGs using English audios were done poorly which I unfortunately didn’t enjoy very much. Not to mention, dual audios are costly, no point to get a game’s price up for something does not seems necessary. That’s what I always thought about it. However, it is at a loss when terms come to CS III. I tried English audios throughout the game and all the voice acting behind the scene have my sincere gratitude. The actors & actress did an unforgettable amazing job on voice acting, in order to represent the diversity protagonists in game. Ex. like the top protagonist Rean gets so matured with his voice also ‘grows’ quite much while being the same actor behind it compare to the past 2 games; Juna, a particular difficult role to portrait, since she’s pretty emotional, all her sentiments show up quite straight forward, making her too moody to voice if not skillful enough. On top of that, there’s a huge incident about her in Ch.2 putting the skill of actress behind her directly into a challenge, yet, she never let us down, did an excellent job to it. Kurt, the youngest son of Vander family who served the Imperial royal heir since the nation was built, is a humble and clam swordsman, intelligent and diligent at the same time, his voice is perfect there to serve these traits that I found none other could do any better; Altina, also known as black rabbit, a shy but cute character set to be emotionless, but from time to time, she changes with bond she made with her classmates. Whoever give her voice behind the scene made sure I can feel her growth little by little through those changes via voices. Not to mention, the old Class VII is a rich selection of nobilities: Alisa, Laura, Emma, Elliot, Fie, Jusis, Gaius, Machias....the list can go on and on. Even in the faction of the formidable foes lies some identical magnificent voices such as the Steel Maiden; the Boss; Azure Chevalier; Campanella the Fool and Vita, the 2nd Anguis of Ouroboros'. Darn Vita, I shouldn’t mention her, her voice is surely something else....I will put a stop here. Anyway, in the end, there isn’t a character I don’t care about because of the brilliant voice acting, none of them feel like an empty shell. The game slowly introduces you its rich content. Moreover, full of surprises,  there’s no doubt, without these unforgettable vivid voices behind them, giving lives and characteristics to each and all, the world of CS III would be undone.Battle system & BossesLegends of Heroes is a franchise with a long history, battles are turn-based on with its own tweaks. You equip quartz to use arts( magic) while carrying normal equipment dealing damage by using skills. Different difficulties proves easy gaming to someone masters the game to challenge. The levels of them are noticeably different. It also made sure providing variety range of interesting bosses to fight while touring the world of Erebonia. There are bosses who get excited when their HP hit to critical, and starting  healing themselves up when caught you off guard. There are bosses who get panic in the middle of the fight and starting summoning allies everywhere, trying to outnumber you and regaining their advantages. There are bosses who can’t accept their defeat, revive themselves with enhanced status, then the battle ended up really intense and fierce, you got fired up when dealing with them as well. There also are bosses who inflict hell amount of status ailments, making you literally can’t hit them unless your party wearing the right accessories that immune their status ailments attacks. There is a boss will trick your S-crafts hit your own allies if you’re not carefully enough reading its actions etc. Anyways, bosses fights in this game really puts your understanding of the battles and strategies into a test via story and difficulties(nightmare is really hard for newcomers, just saying).Mini gamesCold Steel III offers couples of interesting mini games in exchange of mood, if when you’re bit tired of the main plot and want some fresh air. Mainly are Panza Soldat fight; Vantage Masters card game; fishing as usual; horse riding; short side missions etc. I’d like to specially put the Panza Soldat fight and Vantage Master card game to spotlight. Despite Gundam things were originally started by Bandai( manga, anime, games etc), but their own gundam games on steam aren’t that interesting to play if you ask me. Panza Soldat (Divine Knight) fight is like CS 3’s own turn-based on Gundam game, but more likely wielding its own charms. Despite its more like a mini game you do it now and then, not selectively doable

_childDocuments_.review: Trails of Cold Steel III (CS III) is the 8th installment in the Trails franchise, taking place roughly 1.5 years after Trails of Cold Steel II. If you haven't played the previous 7 games, you've wandered around in the wrong place. Everything you knew about all previous game's stories pays off big in CS III. With a huge cast of NPCs and playable characters, Trails of CS III feels amazingly satisfying to play through. Seeing some familiar faces (and location!) coming back into the series gives you the nostalgic feeling and it makes it so much better. The story just keeps getting better with each Trails game. CS III is a huge game; it took me a whooping 115 hours to complete. I took my time to play through it, and I'll say it was well worth the time, the story is just really good.The graphics has gone through a major overhaul than the previous games, and it's one of the best thing CS III offers. The art style looks more fluid and natural, the character designs closely reflect their age and personality. The graphics improvements are really my favorite part after the story. The combat has also been improved a lot alongside UI, basically everything has gone through an upgrade than the previous CS games. I'm just so glad to see such a phenomenal improvement!The fast travel has been made so much better that it's very easy to instantly move across from one point to another, this also has been another huge QOL improvement even though it may be overlooked. A lot of games should really look into this excellent feature.That twisted ending near the end was simply mind-blowing! Can't wait to jump into CS IV!

_childDocuments_.review: Okay. So first off. Yes I recommend this game. Yes I love this game. And yes it is awesome. And it's worth the price. You see my playtime? subtract 15 hours from that due to real life circumstances and you'll have an accurate representation of how long I've played this game from start to finish. Doing all the side quests, listening to everyone speak and barely skipping anything. This is how long I played the game. Oh but I did skip the same fighting animations. I mean, after the 20th time you're done looking at that. But even so, look at my playtime. It's impressive.HOWEVERI feel I MUST go into the things that drive me crazy about this game. I MUST tell people about the things that really pissed me off with this game. (but these are personal qualms, and have nothing to do with the quality of the game)1. There is another game or two in-between Trails of Cold Steel 2 and 3. And therefore you are expected to already know a bunch of stuff coming into the third game. Since I couldn't play those games (no official english translation) I missed out on quite a bit of backstory coming into this one. Which is a damn shame.2. The beginning is a bit off. If you played the first two and then come into this one, the first 6 hours of this game, 6-10 hours is just gonna really bug you and get on your nerves. Almost making me not want to play anymore. It's story and characters were causing this feeling. But if you push past that you'll start to really enjoy the game and become addicted to it like I did. (If you enjoyed the first two that is because this game is very similar to those)3. The voice acting is all over the place. Sometimes its good. Sometimes its bad. Sometimes this character talks while no one else does. Sometimes everyone talks then mid conversation the voice acting stops. Its like the actors were paid by the word and thus they had to keep it limited on how much they were actually allowed to voice act. It's pretty bad and gets kind of distracting.4. The story is garbage. Sorry but it is. I love trails of cold steel. And in the first two games its happy go lucky, no one dies in war or in terrorist attacks, death is rare, friendship solves everything blah blah blah, corny cliche speeches blah blah blah. In the first two games well...it was acceptable. Kind of lame but kind of inspiring. They just a bunch of kids in school so it makes sense and this game is meant for everyone I suppose even though it has foul language in it. But in this game? It's out of place. It just doesn't make any sense. You're legit in some serious situations but still everyone is like "yay! Friendship!" then they get their butts kicked, they're saved by someone bigger and stronger and then their like "yeah! Frienship saved the day!" it's just...pathetic at this point. And there are some major gaps, and confusing little points that just come out of nowhere. It feels like some of the plots and twists were literally just added in there to be random plots and twists..for the sake of being twists. Some of the decisions juts make no sense at all. Imagine watching DBZ and suddenly in the third season goku turned out to be evil for the rest of the show. Makes no sense, came completely out of nowhere and possibly ruins the show. But it was a good twist so we added it in. No hints. No clues. No nothing, just right out of left field with no logic just to push the plot forward.5. The games ending is disappointing. I know they had to leave it off for the next game coming out next year but still, what a horrible way to go. Think of the worst ending possible, and thats what you're gonna get. It makes you feel like garbage. Not to mention I was barely able to follow along with what was happening and why and that's after almost 100 hours of gameplay. I was still confused. I have to go online and read the details just so I know what the hell is happening AFTER i've beaten it.6. Oh and the things that'll REALLY make you mad happen around the end too. It's like, "We gotta fight these super strong guys who we've never stood a chance against before. We haven't gotten any stronger but lets place the fate of the world on us beating them THIS time." do they win? no...of course not. So it was pointless and lacking in common sense from all parties except the bad guys. They knew these dumb kids who weren't strong enough were gonna challenge them. They knew they'd win. So they went ahead with their plans. In fact, the bad guys are the smartest strongest guys in this universe and hell..as much as I hate to admit it. They deserve to win.But I hated that ending. Not gonna tell you what happens but I hated it. I know its set up for the next game next year but it still irritates me. And the mentality of the characters really irritates me too. You'll know what I mean. It's like...hey look, an evil bad guy who caused all this. I'm gonna go kill him since that's justice for all the horrible things they've done. And everyone is like "nuuu don't do it" and i'm sitting here thinking why the f**k not!!?? He's evil! Look at all he's done!But...if that happy go lucky, friendship is magic, good guys can die but if bad guys die it makes you the bad guy, kind of mentality is your thing. Then you'll absolutely love this game. but quite frankly, that kind of mentality, whether its in video games or anime just pisses me off.I recommend this game because besides the last few hours of the ending, the game was great. But be prepared when you get to that ending because it's just gonna irritate the crap out of you. Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: CS3 is the start of the second half of the Erebonia arc of Cold Steel following the duology of Cold Steel 1 and 2. The graphics and gameplay have been improved across the board, the new cast of students has a fun dynamic about them, the game has a great soundtrack, and there is even a fun card-game minigame to partake in. The story is largely a "set-up" for CS4 and can feel like it is proceeding pretty sluggishly (in Trails fashion), but all these events build and climax into something that feels profound and grand on an amazing scale. Turn-based, story-driven JRPGCS3 largely retains the combat system of other Trails games but makes the battle controls more streamlined and button-input focused, replacing the wheel of input navigation in more recent games. For example, now instead of scrolling the wheel until you get to Crafts, you can just press (PS4 face button) Triangle, or if you want to use items, you can just press (D-pad) Left. Other new additions include the brave order system, which allows you to deploy orders to your team during combat that buff certain stats (e.g. lower turn speed delay or STR+ & ATS+ for three turns) using BP which is accumulated whenever you unbalance an enemy. The break system is also introduced which gives all enemies a secondary bar that can be broken by hitting their weaknesses, and when the bar is broken the enemy's turn will be delayed and they will take increased damage until they recover.All characters can now equip a sub-quartz alongside their master quartz, but the only caveat is that they will only gain some a few from the quartz as opposed to all of them.The rest of combat is pretty standard, unchanged Trails combat: turn order manipulation, enemy turn delaying, S-crafts, Crafts, arts, ailments, follow-up attacks, divine knight battles, etc. largely remain the same. In terms of general gameplay, you will find yourself doing more of the same as previous Trails games: complete given quests before proceeding with main story, do a main story encounter, get some kind of free day of downtime/small story bits, and repeat. Besides that, you can be prompted to play the optional card game "Vantage Masters" with named/random NPC's to earn new cards/card masters, and eventually obtain a new master quartz if you win all encounters.CS3 runs on a new and improved engine from CS1&2 and thus is probably more demanding than those games. I first played it on my old PC before upgrading (AMD FX 6300 & RX 480 8GB) on Highest Settings with no issue. Of course, YMMV based on your own specs. The game looks much better than CS1&2 with higher quality character models, better animations, detailed environments, and improved menu/combat UI.CS3 takes place about two years after the events of CS2. You retain the role of the protagonist, Rean Schwarzer, who has now graduated from Thors Military Academy and is about to start his new job as an instructor at Thors Military Academy's new Branch Campus. While learning to guide his new students, you will encounter familiar faces, both allies and foes alike. Ouroboros, the mysterious society that constantly rears its head for no discernible reason, is active again performing strange experiments while people that appear to have died also suddenly emerge from out of the blue. It is up to Rean to fulfill his promise to his old Class VII friends, and new Class VII allies, to fight back against these mysterious forces and save Erebonia.•CS3 looks great across the board compared to CS1&2. 1&2 character models/chat heads often looked a little blocky and low polygon, while characters in 3 look more lifelike and detailed.•New Class VII is a smaller, but more focused and developed version of old Class VII. They all have unique personalities that mesh well with each other and you see them grow alongside one another throughout the entire game compared to in CS1&2 when the large number of classmates was always shuffled around for every chapter. Shoutout to Ash's VA, Austin Lee Matthews, who absolutely kills it in his English voiceover.•The continued Trails worldbuilding helps develop Erebonia's large-scale even further by allowing you to visit cities and towns that weren't seen in CS1&2 like Leeves, Saint-Ark, and Ordis, while also allowing you to return to previously visited places like Crossbell (hell yeah!) and Heimdallr. •CS3 has a great soundtrack. Some of my favorites are: Start Line, Brave Steel, Proud Grudge, and of course, the best Final Dungeon theme of all time: Spiral of Erebos. If I had to rank the OST, it would be: Zero/Azure > CS1 > CS3.•Rean's growth as a protagonist is nice to see as he is now older, more mature, and more experienced. He still retains his characteristics of self-doubt and feeling lesser than others, but he has a stronger sense of responsibility when it comes to his new job and his new students.•Character builds are varied and experimental. You can kit anyone out to be strong as a physical or magical DPS, tank, or evader, but obviously some characters are more built for those roles than others based on natural stats. That being said, just stacking Fie or Ash with 100% evade and critical chance is always a fun time.•Vantage Masters is a fun distraction from main story activities.•The combat is pretty abusable if you take advantage of break bars and turn delay reductions using Kurt and Juna's orders. Choosing to use this strategy basically trivializes the game if that is your goal.•If you despise slow-burn games like CS1, CS3 is basically more of the same. Like CS1 is the setup for CS2's payoff, CS3 establishes the foundation for CS4's payoff. The plot proceeds slowly as you travel to other cities for your field exercises, fight enemy forces, and they just disappear while leaving crumbs of hints for you to pick up on every time. •The game expects you to know the backstories/plots surrounding the returning cast characters of previous Trails games. Playing CS3 without having played (or at least watched story summaries of) the Liberl/Crossbell arcs is all-around a bad idea if you are invested in the Trails lore. •The story always loops around to a particularly similar event whenever Rean is in trouble and is about to call Valimar for help. Sure, it reintroduces characters, but 3 or 4 times in a row of the same thing is kind of meh.•The worst Japanese-game tropes remain the worst tropes, as in Angelica is still just a thirsty demon lusting after all women regardless of age, and Shirley still sexually harasses other women by groping them because well, Japan.8.5/10Solid JRPG, solid Trails game

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, if you have played Cold Steel 1 and 2, if not pass on to another Trails game. This game is easily the weakest of the Cold Steel series. Anyone who says that the new Class VII in this game is better than the old Class VII is either full of crap or just horny. The new students personalities and/or story arcs revolve around Rean (the main character) almost everything they do is because of him, they do not have time  to be their own person.Examples:Altina: Her entire story arc is about doing stuff for herself and not because Rean told her too. . . except she learns that by Rean telling her not to do stuff because he said so.Kurt: Goes from insecure sword boy because of his brother, to insecure sword boy because of ReanJuna: Her dealing with Crossbell's annexation was actually a good part, however after she comes to terms with that her whole personality revolves around being happy and stuff that Rean tells herMusse: I know it's technically not her real personality, but in this game her entire personality is trying to get into Rean's pants.Ashe: Best new Class VII member, just kind of a jackass who joined Class VII because it would be challenging and fun. His story arc is not based around Rean. <------ More characters like this FalcomThe game also fails to immerse the player in the school aspect of the game. In Cold Steel 1 there were enough members, even at the beginning of the game, to make Class VII feel like a class at a fancy private school. That made it much easier to make the school part of the game believable. In Cold Steel 3, Class VII at it's largest barely has members to play a game of street basketball. It is obviously just a contrived way to have a school setting and get the party together. I understand that they wanted a smaller class so they wouldn't overload the game with characters, but if you wanted a smaller cast set it somewhere other than a school. Another note on characters. Why does every girl in this game have to be in love with Rean. I understand that many people who play this game will never talk to another woman other than their mom and sister, but this makes the characters worse in every way. It makes all of the female cast way too similar. It be fine if it were just 1 or 2 people but every woman does not need to be wishing that Rean would show her the Eight Leaves Sword  style.Final note on gameplay. The game adds a new mechanic called Brave Orders. It is a interesting mechanic that allows you to spend your BP on something other than Rush attacks. However, it becomes a necessary to abuse Brave Orders to essentially break the combat system to beat many of the bosses in the game. I enjoyed my time in Cold Steel III bust most of my enjoyment came from the overall story, the returning cast, and the villains. If I had never played a game in the Trails series, Cold Steel 3 would have most likely killed my interest in the series all together.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been almost 3? years since I went down the gutter in search of a good JRPG after persona 5 rekindled that flame. The trails series (*not* tales of, also not trials, trails) is a long running JRPG franchise from one of the oldest game developers in the world, Nihon Falcom.They do have a bunch of JRPGs lined up, the Ys series, Zwei series, Xanadu and Tokyo Xanadu. They all each have their quirks but Trails goes out of its way to bring back the old style turn based JRPG that Square Enix neglects since at least final fantasy XIII, but even then, it'd gone out of its way to 'modernize'.Trails, at its core, is a massive book, one that you get to choose which extra parts you want to read. You can enjoy the main story and be done with it in the *short* timespan of 60/70 hours. Or you can go out of your way and read almost everything the game has to throw at you and roughly do 100 hours, but these aren't hidden things you look hunt for, not for the most part. The game rewards you for exploring its world, not only with extra gear but with important details to the story.Being a massive book in a massive book series, most of those extra details delight you with references to the older games, even if they are not shy to reference the previous ones (which happen from 4 to 2 years before this game, unlike skyrim to oblivion for example)This franchise IS the jrpg genre. The old one, the one that people yearned for since FFX, and the one that led to modern jrpgs enjoyed by the mainstream audience. This *book* is just another entrance in a massive tale of, well, a legend of heroes.The interesting thing is that this isn't only just a book, it's a fun game with great game mechanics, incredible music, and a fantastic PC port to boot. I've played the japanese version for the PS4, and the english localization of it, and my god, this game on the PC is the way to play the game. Loading times are gone, FPS drops are DELETED and even the achievement images are artworks that were drawn specifically for the game by artists.If anything about the idea of losing yourself into a massive lore that spans almost 10 games and almost twice as many years, then please, go ahead and test the demo out. This is the best JRPG on steam, and will be for the forseeable future, although the only true competitor is the other franchise Nihon Falcom has, and that's Ys 8.Do yourself a solid and hop on board.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: yet another half-azzed "port", made with no regard for PC players. Now, hearing that they having a free weekend on Part III, I decided to give it a try. Maybe they have fixed it? But seems not. It is as bad as it was... maybe even worse. So below is my experience with this game:The Bad:1) Still very silly & childish story, even most anime nowadays have better2) Combat...I never liked combat in this game. Somehow it is even worse than in your average JRPG. Yes characters has flashy moves but they all do pretty much the same....3) Controls are still not optimized for PC. Hello Japan, PC players use keyboards! Yet you still map controls for console buttons, not add "quit" or menu button in game and so on. This is pure disrespect to PC players and makes game very clunky to use.4) Linearity. In the first game , I did spend awful lot of time courting Laura, yet as I saw later it will have no effect on anything whatsoever. _childDocuments_.review: This review is for players who have completed Cold Steel I and II. If you haven't, then I recommend playing those first.I consider CS3 to be the weakest entry in the Cold Steel series and possibly all of the Trails games. It's still a  game, but you'll be able to enjoy it much more if you adjust your expectations going into it.It's Cold Steel I but with more woo, less character development, a few annoying retcons and a  weaker ending. Lowlights include:Trails games are anime-style so don't expect photorealism. Some key points about the game's graphics:Overall, the graphics are "good for this genre" and that's really the only fair way to rate it - it's not an Elder Scrolls or Dark Souls game.Generally excellent in terms of both the soundtrack and the voice acting, except for one immensely immersion-breaking fault that comes up again and again: scenes in which  characters are voiced and others aren't (usually Rean).It's fine to have a combination of voiced and unvoiced scenes, but an entirely different matter when players have to switch between listening and reading on a line-by-line basis. It's not a localization problem, either; I played with English voices, but I checked Japanese and it has the same problem. Every time this happened (and it happened ) it completely took me out of the game.I don't know if Falcom was trying to save money, or up against a deadline, or what, but they could have trivially fixed this by simply  the voices from scenes in which they didn't/couldn't get the Rean lines voiced.A modest improvement over CS1-2, though not without some faults. Lots of quality-of-life improvements such as ubiquitous map markers and fast travel, save/load anywhere, skip any cutscene or animation, etc. Much more forgiving than previous Trails games in terms of "permanently missable" items/quests. Few but very prominent misspellings ("Calvary", "Bandanna", I cringed every time), cooking seems nerfed (in the rare cases you actually need to use an item in battle, cooked items don't heal enough), Arts are semi-useless due to emphasis on Break, and NG+ doesn't unlock any new content/play-styles and is therefore pointless. Orders and Break mechanic are cool additions that make battles more tactical and further de-emphasize grinding, but also tend to make every battle follow the same template and effectively make "cheesing" an intended mechanic. Game allows you to min-max very early through crafting and fishing, but doing too much of this mid-game can throw off the endgame balance.If you're a fan of the series, go ahead and grab this game, preferably when it's on sale, but don't expect it to have the same wow-factor as CS2, which was in my opinion the best of the series, or even CS1. It's a decent game, with lots of content, but overall a downgrade from its predecessors.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're familiar with the Trails of Cold steel series this is more and continued refinement, well worth getting.  If you're not... I do not recommend starting here but it isn't an impossible place to begin.  The Trails series is multiple interconnected branches so there's every chance you haven't played EVERYTHING before you play this game and that's alright.  The plot is approachable without background knowledge (only a hint confusing at times) but you'll get a whole lot more out of it and appreciate a bunch of things if you do have the background.Gameplay wise the game is a mix of non combat sections and combat sections.  During non-combat sections you'll fish, bond with people, play card games, and try to decide when you're supposed to be on a railroad and when you're supposed to buck the trend a little.  This can be annoying at times if you're a completionist (guilty) but if you're not too OCD they're usually pretty fair.  In combat you'll use a turn based system but there's a number of clever twist and revisions that make it more then just 'throw a punch or spell, wait for an enemy to throw a punch or spell, try to figure out an enemy's weak element'.  To put it simply you have some ability to control and interupt turn order, figuring out when, where, and how to use this is an important part of combat.  All in all I don't know if I'd call it the best JRPG of all time but this series is easily up there in the top 10% for me.

_childDocuments_.review: *It's spoiler free for those wondering.This is actually my second playthrough. I had already played this game on PS4 when it launched last year. Decided to buy and replay again on PC now because PC is the only place where you can play all the Trails games.Definitely worth it having it in my collection, in a single unified cross-gen platform that is PC. I'm just copy-pasting my old PS4 review here and added a few notes about the PC port. It's long, so take your time lolIn my opinion, Trails of Cold Steel III is the best game I've ever played and by a far margin. I felt like Falcom has put their heart and soul into making this game, it was a full high quality JRPG experience and the longest game I've ever played clocking at 103 hours. It's impressive how much value is included in a $60 package if you compare to many AAA that can be finished in just 7 hours for the same price.Everyone here already knows that Falcom excels in world building and character development. Every one of the characters is properly developed with their own backgrounds, complexity and reasons, including the villains and this is specially true in Cold Steel III because this game is where everything converges from all 7 previous games and a bunch of loose threads are explained. For everyone who played all the previous titles, CS3 is a story packed with emotion; we are all more intelligent, we have a better understanding of the story, all the knowledge gained from the previous games, and the same goes for the characters, they are stronger, they have more experience and are fighting together as Class VII, both old and new. It was amazing to see all the old characters reappear in CS3, not only from the Cold Steel arc but also from the Sky arc and the Crossbell games and I loved the new characters too, they are all unique with their own personalities and problems that they overcome together. The Trails series has characters that we actually care about, we remember their names and their personalities, even the NPCs, and we develop emotion for them.The music is also excellent and definitely above average. They never disappoint when it's about music, it all fits so well into the game that sometimes I wanted to spend more time in the city just to keep listening to the relaxing music that is playing, and the fights are also epic and hype with the background music playing with all that violin goodness. They even put it all for free on Spotify and let us use the tracks for any purpose without worrying about copyright issues, a very generous company for sure.Gameplay is also refined to it's best when it's about JRPGs. Equipment, orbments, status bonuses... everything counts to create a proper character build, and strategy during combat also plays a big part into this game so knowing how to use Brave Orders, breaking the enemy, steal the enemy's turn with S-Craft and explore their weakness can change the battles dramatically specially during Boss battles. Menu navigation is also very smooth and easy to understand not only when choosing equipment/orbment, but also during battle where each action is mapped to one button. Well, and that's not just that, being able to change to any character with a single button, fast-travel to the areas around, 60fps glory and Turbo Mode all add up to the overall game quality that are not present in other games. I had a great time with CS3 mechanics, every single move felt rewarding and the Boss battles were great and challenging. It's also worth to note that Falcom values our time, giving us the option to lower the difficulty and try again in every game over screen, so no need to worry about grinding levels if the focus is story only.Now all I have to do is wait for the English CS4 release on PC and keep studying Japanese to be able to play Hajimari no Kiseki. I have already played CS4 in Japanese using the available spreadsheet, but I'm looking forward to playing it again in full official English localization here on PC in order to better understand the story before going all out into Hajimari.The real problem of playing a game series so good and story rich like the Trails series is that everything else feels short and boring. It's become even harder to satisfy me, in a good way I'd say these series really ruined my gaming experience, but I'm very happy about it. After all the money and time I've spent for the past years into gaming, I never expected I would experience something like the Trails series. I feel a little bit ashamed of myself that it took so long for me to discover this series two years ago, but better late than never lolTo tell the truth, I think there's absolutely nothing out there that can match what Falcom is doing with the Trails series, a story so big and complex with incredible world building including many political aspects, military, conspiracy groups, religion and ancient history. All of this in a series that has started 15 years ago, 9 games until now, over 700 hours of JRPG, all in one central plot and we're still in the middle of the full story of the continent. Things that we see in the previous games continue in the next ones, not only as just a nostalgia cameo, but important parts of the main story. A lot of things from previous games are explained several games later and Falcom is not afraid of continuing the series like this, they keep doing it.The current state of the gaming industry is quite unfortunate with so many AAA titles that the developers make just for the money, so many compromises made to their vision, cut-off content being sold as DLC and so on... I'm glad Falcom is still a small company, so they can make their games without any compromises, I feel like they reach their fans by touching our hearts, not through millionaire marketing campaigns.About the PC Port, it's great and made by the same people who brought us the previous Cold Steel games. The game runs well and never crashed. I was able to play it at 1080p60 High on a GTX 1050 Ti. A few frame rate drops on more demanding scenes, but nothing really severe.My only complaints are that shadows and anti-aliasing are kinda broken. Some shadows are blocky and pixelated even at High setting and create a lot of shimmer and the anti-aliasing solution isn't very effective to clean up the jagged edges. I think the PS4 version has better implementation of AA and shadows but these are minor issues and not game breaking. Well, this was a very long post. If you've read it all thank you very much.I just had to write something about it. It is painful not being able to talk about these series with any of my friends at college, so if even a single person reads this I'm already happy. Thanks

_childDocuments_.review: Just when you though the trails series couldn't get any better! my only gripe the slow paced divine knight battles have been redeveloped into Gundam brawls! We finally get to curbstomp crytpids with panzer soldats! We finally get an even better character brawl than Trails of the Sky 3rd, the max character team you get for this one is 16! but you can switch between them on the fly. Holy crap that ffffing cliff hanger! I even got the ps4 cold steel 4 since I couldn't wait any longer. okay time for a normal review, CS3 is the continuation of CS2 and if you believe anyone that says you can jump into it without playing the other games you got scammed. CS3 is like the infinity war of the Trails series. if brings together the cast of Trails in the Sky (liberian Heroes), Trails to Zero (special support section) and Trails of cold steel ( Class 7). even in the back ground you get Llyod, Elie and Kea for SSS, Estelle, Joshua, Rene , Schezard and Cassius for the liberian heros and there are just referenced but they are part of the story. The game is action packed to a degree you even wonder how the hell these guys continue trying to leave normal lives, the tales of each character is blended excellently through all 8 games for example, Rene Schewarzer (CS 1-3), Cassius Bright (FC,SC and 3rd), and Arios Mclane ( Zero, Azure) are all taught by the same master of the 8 leaves one blade school. thats no even including Tio and Randy (Zero, Azure) , Tita, Oliviert and Agate (FC,SC,3rd) are part of this one. Game play is solid as they improved everything from the old game. the most notable is the Divine knight battles, 2nd is the max party size, in one of the battles here you get to compose a massive raid like battle where you use 2 teams of 5 and 1 team of 6 to beat up the living hell out of a boss. The quality of life updates such as Markers for hidden quests and events are a boon, so you dont have to talk to every single fing person to get them all. the fishing mechanic is much harder while cooking is now easier since even absentees can cook anytime.Graphics didnt change much, sound is still superb, the story line is engaging and I teared up more the once seeing the characters I see slowly grow over CS 1 and 2, and the return of some from the Sky and Zero casts. I absolutely cannot wait for the 4th one which is said to be the END GAME of the trails series were the massive roster of Sky, Zero and Steel come together. Falcom is such a master of story telling, the VA's (japanese) outdid them selves as I immersed myself int he story. I repeatedly thought the last trails game I played was the best starting from the Trails in the Sky SC, but each and every game outdid it self and I thank XSEED Games and NIS America for localizing 7 of the 9 games, hopefully someone does Zero and Azure but if you cant wait The geo front patches are excellent, and you can pick up the original japanese copies and apply the patches. _childDocuments_.review: Cold Steel 3, after finally playing through the Ao/Zero Duology and Trails in the Sky 1-3, I've finally been able to return to the Cold Steel series which had started me off in this glorious journey through Falcoms brilliant games. This game was fantastic. Ill be mentioning some minor spoilers but nothing relating to the overall point of the plot.I don't think Cold Steel 3 will be topped even by Cold Steel 4, purely because of the impact of every new mechanic, graphical fidelity and plot development at once. I was extremely excited to play this game as it was the first Falcom game I would play that resembled a modern JRPG, visually. Starting on Nightmare, the combat wasn't as hard as anticipated though I took time to farm every party member and search for as much side content as possible to outfit my characters properly, so this may be why. However, the game was sometimes made trivial by the "Battle Orders" System, which is a very interesting mechanic, effectively allowing every character to have an ability or three that can be activated during anyone elses turn (much like an S-Break), using Brave Points which would give team buffs, acceleration, or healing. This added yet another layer to the synergy of parties that you could construct, and the versatility I gained from experimenting with different than usual substitute characters and main party members was huge, and characters I previously were not interested in were now to be considered for their glorious Battle Order. With the correct buffs and character builds, it was possible to almost destroy a boss in one hit. Whilst I enjoy the synergising the player has to go through to achieve this, its probably too OP (and was addressed in CS4), however it really added a new layer to the already interesting combat and customisation. One small thing to address was Rean, I highly appreciate the shift of Rean to a more strength orientated character, it gave each character a more defined role, and meant I didn't have a person who could shift into everything, which I enjoyed as it allowed me to use different party members in different ways to how I usually would.Linked to the combat, the upgrade to the battle orbment system is also gracefully welcomed, the addition of "sub master quartz" which allowed you to take the abilities, some stats and the first major ability (out of the 3 or 4 abilities you get from master quartz) from a usual master quartz. Meaning I could have Rean main quartzing a double damage but double delay quartz for the Strength buff, the double damage and the 1/2 Fire arts cast (or whatever it was), but also have him sub quartz where the first ability would give him more craft points from being damaged, allowing him to become a self-sustaining resource machine with a huge amount of damage. You could also have 1 quartz in use as a main and a sub at one time, meaning you dont need to worry about getting 2 of 1 quartz if someone is already using it as their main, and you want it as the sub.The divine knight combat is another lesser thing I thought that was majorly improved, as every CS manages to do. The combat feels alot more fluid and thought out in this game, with team fights being present. However, I still think they are boring due to their degree of simplicity, and nightmare making the fights drag out alot longer than they should. They are a welcome addition as a campus activity, however, I would love to see the fights made even more interesting for future releases. Campus activities in this game were one of my favourite past times, taking every return back to school as a reason to look around and check peoples dialogue, progress as a student, side quests, and to play card games, was very fulfilling and seeing the new cast being well fleshed out behind the scenes, was a fun experience. The use of a branch campus in this game gives a sense of rivalry and camaraderie, as the character list is alot smaller compared to CS1/2, meaning you interact and relate to the side characters much more. The replacement for Blade in this game was awesome. It effectively played like Hearthstone, having a master, various monsters and spells and effects, with a mana crystal gauge like Hearthstone. I completed it fully and had an amazing time with it, whether it be the interactions with the people you played against, or simply just collecting the cards and 100%ing that. I love the addition of these card games ,it really gives me a reason to return and double check over cities and towns and the campus, when time passes.I won't mention anything to the story, but man this game really hit hard with the story, masterfully intertwining the Ao/Zero duology with the cold steel universe, and this game really lent itself to setting up what is to come in the End of Saga. I put in 130h into this game for my first playthrough, finishing all the card games and collecting all the cards, all the fish, doing pretty much all the side quests and almost maxing out the social links within the game. I will most definitely be returning to this game in particular to 100% it, as it was a particularly enjoyable experience out of all the games so far. It gave me SC levels of enjoyment, though this is probably because of the bombardment of new features and enhanced graphics offered by the PS4 era. Whilst I won't be immediately moving onto CS4 (the change of Laura's English VA is partially to blame, whilst the new one isn't bad, I really miss old Laura), I fully intend to after I finally finish Ys Origin on Nightmare, as i've been well enjoying the Ys series from Falcom over Christmas.I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love Nihon Falcom man, they're just so good
