_childDocuments_.review: The third game in an overrated, disappointing series filled with the same lazy writing that makes anime unpalatable to most looking from the outside in.The positives of this game are the OST and...yeah, the OST. I mean it's a shonen JRPG where you play as a celebrity playboy with demon powers and a weapon with the power of a small country's military. The villains in the game might as well be pokemon wandering around waiting for the MC so they can popup for a random encounter, because they sure as hell aren't convincing antagonists. Almost every single big plot point in this game is an excuse to make the characters fight each other. The antagonists/villains don't even try to sound like they have a coherent plan, they just have a hard-on for fighting.WHICH IS ACTUALLY OKAY. Fighting is awesome. Shonen anime are also awesome. The problem is Cold Steel masquerades as a political thriller when its really just a shallow, lazily written shonen power fantasy. The dialogue in this game reads like a Gintama parody skit, and can be boiled down to a few generalizations, depending on what's happening.Antagonists"Don't disappoint me!""Haha you've improved!""Haha you can't control your power yet?""Oh not bad, guess I'll have to get serious!"Antagonists talking about plans"Heh...guess the stage is set, and all the actors are about to begin...heh..." (I'm not kidding. Play the game and look to see how many "The stage/actor" metaphors you can find. It feels like an inside joke)"Hmph. *Vague rambling about some vague plan related to something ANCIENT and POWERFUL WHOA.Protagonists about to fight"OKAY CLASS SEVEN, OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO DEFEAT OUR OPPONENTS. USE ALL OF YOUR MIGHT AND FIGHT YOUR OPPONENTS THAT ARE IN FRONT OF YOU!""Yeah!"Okay!""You got it rean!""Let's defeat our opponents!""We can defeat our opponents because we're class VII!""You're right! We are class VII!"The writing is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad that there's a scene where a character dies towards the end of the game, and I just started laughing my ass off. It was so obvious they wanted it to be impactful but there was no buildup to the scene, just melodramatic, over the top voice acting and a slowpan over the falling "corpse". I also laughed because the concept of death in this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game is about as important as the "political worldbuilding" which means that it basically doesn't exist. Characters don't die, they experience death and are brought back as convenient plot armor for our celebrity MC whenever he's in a pinch, or some deus ex machina ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at the end of the game so the mouthbreathing weebs who love this dumpster fire can say, "Whoa I remember that guy!". Because yeah, saying "I remember you!" is peak storytelling. The writers are witless Christmas hams and completely lack the imagination to write the plot they tried to setup with previous games like Kiseki and Trails FC/SC.Overwhelmingly positive? I'm overwhelmed that a living, breathing, thinking human being managed to shovel this garbage down their throats for 100+ hours and then ask for seconds. I slogged through Cold Steel 1, which was somehow worse than this abortion of a product, nearly threw in the towel at 2 when we had to run around finding all of our classmates so we could...restore the academy that we don't use in the third game? The ♥♥♥♥?This game man. I just hated it so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much, I came to the end and was in disbelief. "That's it?" All these hard-working devs and THIS is the game people call a masterpiece? According to the anime community, games like Nier Automata and ToSC are the same quality-wise. Let that sink in.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t think i’ll be able to make this review long since I’m in a broken state right now i’ve lost many in this game alone. To start with the positives this series just continues to go on being masterfully written and just going into a role of an instructor is just amazing. The way you grow from student to instructor is amazing and you genuinely see how hard it was for Instructor Sara to have raised you in the first 2 games. Being introduced to a cast of students that give no respect to you from the start was worrying on top of just wanting to be back with your old family from the first 2 games but they grow so beautifully and perfectly its like seeing how you, yourself grew in the first 2 games as Rean you see how amazing it is watching your kids grow up, Juna, Kurt, Ash, Altina, and Musse will forever be precious to me in how they developed to be such amazing characters to becoming my kids….. But with that of course there’s tragedy seeing your kids get hurt and certain circumstances there’s point where something happens and you can’t do anything about it. Seeing your family from the first 2 games grow to such adults is beautiful to see and seeing how happy and strong they’ve become made me truly realize how amazing my family truly is. Emma is like the best thing to have ever happened to me from these games she keeps going through struggles but when it comes to you she still smiles and supports you and just wants to be there for you it makes you realize how there’s no girl like that in real life sadly LMFAO but on top of that it just amazes me how she continues to be the same bundle of sunshine she’s always been. As to how this game ended though…. It truly has broke me… this tops both the first 2 games in the sadness it gives you and just seeing people you cared about deeply with how you bonded with them and…. Seeing someone from your family being taken as well it just hurts to the point of numbingness I honestly praise whoever tries to play this game and those who have already played it. I’m not gonna say more I could say play this game and such but I already have but at this point if you play this series proceed with caution cause it will hurt and it will hurt a lot. The symbolism at the end with how Rean loses himself perfectly represents how you, yourself in a sense lose yourself from such tragedy… Thank you to whoever read this it means a lot I continue onwards to Trails of cold steel 4 even if I got this pain I carry it to finally finishing all this tragedy and hopefully finally being able to enjoy happiness.

_childDocuments_.review: + Great story-gameplay balance+ Fun turn-based combat+ Interesting and well-written story+ Nice quality of life features+ Excellent port- Slow pacing and structured storytelling- Uninspired dungeon designThis series has consumed my time for the past couple months. In anticipation of Cold Steel III's release, I went and played through I and II, two games that have been on my backlog for years. It was my first time playing a game from this monster of a series and I was pretty impressed, so of course I was excited to get into CSIII.Cold Steel III is a solid followup to its predecessors, further expanding upon what made the previous two games great. Fun combat, great writing, well-developed characters, excellent quality of life features, it has all the makings of a great JRPG. It did take a step backwards with regards to its pacing and story structure (more in-line with Cold Steel I than II), but it's still a solid JRPG all things considered and definitely one I would recommend. Just be sure to at least play the first two games before giving this one a shot, less you want to be very confused as to what's going on.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Part 3 of the Cold Steel quadrilogy adds a lot of new features to the combat, and introduces a large amount of new characters, most of which are welcomed additions. Graphics and presentation are improved as well. And as usual, the soundtrack is legendary. This game took me quite a bit longer than the previous two, my playthrough clocks in around 105 hours, though I'm not sure if the game is any longer than part 2 was, or if I just played a bit slower.Cold Steel 3 continues the story of it's predecessors, revealing many secrets and really ramping up the stakes. As is the case with all Trails games, the story and world building is what makes this series worth playing. The cliffhanger ending was to be expected though.Sadly, I cannot say that any improvements were made to the combat. The game is just as easy, if not even easier than the previous two games. With the addition of Battle Orders and support member swapping upon death, the battles lean even more heavily in your favor than ever before. Bosses go down very easily in this game to the point of being laughably bad at best, and utterly disappointing and immersion breaking at worst. And this is on Hard mode as my usual first playthroughs are. I highly recommend playing on Nightmare if you want to have to think during battles at all. (Fortunately you can change difficulty in the options menu at any time)With all that being said, I do recommend this game for fans of the series, and for RPG fans that can appreciate the large scale world building of the Trails series. For non-RPG fans, I wouldn't recommend this game at all.

_childDocuments_.review: The Legends of Heroes series of games always do at least one very important thing that some other JRPGs or even regular RPGs don’t get right: a story that spans and connects among different sagas, yet being able to tell us the origin stories of so many characters in every single of those sagas, while doing it correctly, and more importantly, consistently.With the Cold Steel saga, being composed of 4 games, things started a bit slow in the first game, it was the introduction of these so many important characters, with little references to the previous material we knew, which was the Trails in the Sky saga. A very good game still, with one of the most famous cliffhangers in the series, and overall it felt quite epic really.Cold Steel II was a big improvement in many fronts especially when it comes to character development and connection with other games in the franchise, you could feel things were starting to truly connect everywhere, also a really amazing game.And then here we are in Cold Steel III: this is yet another great evolution of the saga, and the series overall. The characters of older games are more mature now, and the new characters introduced have some of the most well written and complete developments in the series, in my opinion, for being just done in a single game.This is Nihon Falcom’s strength, story, character development and world building, and we get to care about every single one of these characters, even some of the casual NPCs we can find around, or interact and learn about their lives in secondary quests. It is Falcom’s seal of quality for these games, and we have tons of that in Cold Steel III.This game is probably the longest so far in the saga, maybe IV will be longer, it seems everything points towards that, which I’m happy about, there’s a lot to cover.I don’t do spoiler reviews but…yeah, I really enjoyed CS III’s story overall and that ending...I was expecting something like that, since this is Falcom we’re talking about, they had to set the stakes even higher for the last game in this saga, and they did.This is also a game that provides great legit good fan service moments, not just the cheap kind of fan service, but the one directed to fans of the series as a whole, not just Cold Steel fans. And those moments, some subtle, some more prominent, are all great and very well done.On the technical side of things, being used to the top notch quality level standards that the PC ports for CS I and II set, Durante and his team at PH3 Games set the bar even higher once more for CS III’s port: it is simply amazing and it really spoils the hell out of me having such high quality PC versions of these games, because then I go and play other PC ports from other games and the experience isn’t that great on the PC settings front in other games, haha :PI first played this game when it came out for PC on a R5 3600 and GTX 1070, and it ran pretty nice with everything maxed. Controls are nice, and the option to use either keyboard prompts or PS4/Xbox buttons is always welcome. There are a plethora of graphical settings to choose from, as usual, in the launcher, so you can expect to run being able to run this game in a wide range of PCs too.Now that the PC version of CS IV has a release date for April 9th, 2021, it is a good time to revisit these games once more, and as usual, keep on dreaming for what’s to come.Cold Steel III is a great game in the series, overall, which improves a lot on the new full 3D style this saga introduced, and that Falcom seems to have completely embraced in future games.I also want to give a big shout-out to the incredible job and performance of the English voice actors in this game, and the whole CS saga so far: without their great skills some of the characters wouldn't feel the way they do, I know they sound great in Japanese as well, but this English localization team did a very good job, there's a lot of incredible talent here and hopefully they continue using most of them in future games, they deserve it. The translation to English is also really good, kudos to the team them as well.Finally, reviewing a Falcom game not mentioning that the soundtrack is absolutely epic and badass seems like sacrilege to me, and yeah in this game we get some very nice tracks worthy of the best Falcom games, I love listening to them even after playing their games, quite often in fact. Some tracks, especially for the break / slice of life segments in the game remind me a lot of another great Falcom game: Tokyo Xanadu, obviously since it's the same team making music for all these games, but it's so cool, really, I love their soundtracks.Playing these games just...makes me smile a lot, I feel so happy despite so many heart-wrenching moments too in these games, and I can only hope this continues to be the case in future games and sagas, and I can't wait.

_childDocuments_.review: Great sequel and great portI finished CSI and CSII just last week and couldn't wait for the release. Now that it's released, I'm very happy with it so far.It's the same old familiar gameplay from previous game, but the remap of controls does need to get used toIt's great that they finally added some quality of life features as well. Such as cutscene skips, auto-link when you revive someone and logs on ALL dialogues (as opposed to just voiced ones from before).The new battle features are really nice as well and make it a very different strategy experience. It used to be just spam all your craft and then S-craft the bosses, now the new break system and brave order really added a lot more strategic play into it.graphics are prettier, but the art style stayed very similar and everyone is still as recognizable (except for Fie, but I feel that's intentional). There's also a lot more customization you can do with the characters (even if you didn't buy any of the DLCs). Although I definitely recommend getting Juna's swimsuit if you are looking for DLCs.English voice is still one of the best I've seen. Normally I would play only Japanese audio but this is one of the game where the character personality is still there on the English voice overs, and you can swap the voice-over language without having to restart the game unlike previous ones.The new mini-game is also much more fun than Blade from previous games. This one is a tuned down version of Hearthstone and there's a lot more strategy to it than previous games. And I love how you actually need to WIN them as opposed to lose on your first turn. The fishing mini-game also got more challenging but fun as well.Overall, a great job!

_childDocuments_.review: Having played all trails games before (except for the crossbell arc since it hasn't been localized yet) I enjoyed this game a lot and can't wait for the next (and maybe last) installment of this arc given this game ended with a huge cliffhanger and where everything will (probably) come together.The story starts of with the main protagonist of CS I/II and some time after the events of CS II. Well, actually, the game starts with a future event in the second half of the game, spoiling some stuff like available characters etc. Not sure why the developers think this a good idea and they did the same thing back in CS I.The game introduces to you some other main (and new) characters and after playing it for a bit I felt right back home. Each character (main/antagonist/some NPCs) is brimming with personality and has been crafted carefully. As the story progresses more and more (mostly from the old cast) characters will (temporarly) join you. It is quite difficult to give them all the time/love they deserve and the next installment will even have more. The story is as usual interesting and convoluted. Some revelation are made, but a big chunk is still shrouded in mystery at the end. There are also TONS of optional elements (fishing, collecting books, talking with NPCs) and optional quests luckily they are marked (thanks developers). You will probably spend half of the time watching the story/cutscenes.The turned based battle system has been improved and revamped giving it a fresh feel and making it fun even after having played with the same battle system at its core in the previous titles. You take turns attacking each other while having the possibility to interupt turns, casting magic (called arts), positioning yourself and (which is new) buffing your allies temporarily via so-called orders. I abused the latter heavily to get through the battles and the game relies on it a bit too much for my taste (I played in the difficulty mode "Normal" by the way). One thing I miss here is the ability to restart/quit the game while battling. The dungeons are often too long. Although you can skip the battles by running away from the enemy you will need experience to tackle the boss.There is a lot to customize and I liked to spend my time optimizing the equipments to give me the edge in battles. The menu UI looks quite nice now compared to previous titles.As usual again, the music is awesome. The composer are really able to maintain this quality since the beginning of this journey. Should you play this game? Absolutely, but play the previous titles first to fully appreciate the story up to this point. You will miss lots of references if you don't.

_childDocuments_.review: This will be long. skip to the sections you are interested in. *TLDR*Great game where you can see the evolution of rpgs as well as this series. Yes you *can* start with this game. *Background about reviewer*I'm going to review this as someone who has not played part 1 and 2. I have played some titles in the series but didn't finish them because I got bored. I thought trails of cold steel looked cool but I haven't invested the massive amount of time (playing 5 games, 7 if you count cold steel 1 and 2) recommended to be "allowed" to play. I have been playing rpgs since the nes and I have played most of them. If this sounds like you, great, read on. ---------------------------------------*background about the game/series*This is the first NISA published translation for all the legend of heroes games.This is legend of heroes (LOH) 13. First mini series is 2 titles. The ones on psp everyone says are badly localized has 3 titles. Then there is trails in the sky 1 through 3 which are available on steam. Then there are 2 games which are not available on pc in English. Then comes Trails of cold steel 1 through 4. A New one is about to come out in Japan. LOH 1 through 5 serve as a background for the world that starts with trails in the sky. FC is a soft reboot. From trails in the sky FC to this game, a span of several years have passed but not enough years to have a major effect on the characters' age. The games evolve slightly with each title. It's not like dragon quest where you are playing the same game with a new story. It's not like final fantasy where some gameplay can change dramatically between titles. It sits in between. It's not a AAA game, it's an AA game. The artists put a lot of effort in the game but they don't have the budget to anime actions like persona 5. You will see a lot of snes or playstation style emotes, you will see things similar to tales games. You will see things similar to Persona. It has its own style but doesn't ignore what other games are doing. Fight start when you run into a monster and your advantage of disadvantage is based on how you enter combat. The combat uses initiative turn based orders, spells that take time to cast, a resource called CP that goes up when you get hit or hit something. CP goes to 100 where you can then use your "ultimate" or you can let it go up all the way to 200 to increase the power of your ultimate. The initiative gauge also includes bonuses like 100% critical chance and free heals which both you or the enemy can trigger. You can manipulate the turn order by casting spells or interrupting turns using your ultimate attack (with 100 CP or more). You and the enemies also occupy a position on the field which affects AOE spells or who you can smack with your weapon. Think of Grandia. You get exp scaling based on your character's level vs the encounter level. Lower level characters get more exp.You can do basic levels of cooking and crafting and since trails in the sky, you get abilities by slotting them in your orb slot. Trails in the sky also starts including steampunk, then straight out sci-fi elements. The games are divided in chapters and are fairly linear in that you can not go wherever you want at any time in the story. I think all the games have missables but later games get more generous by allowing you to buy some stuff you missed or didn't think was important.Falcom games have awesome music.---------------------------*Combat in Cold steel 3*I didn't find the combat very engaging in the first LOH games. In this game, I was engaged. You can wipe out on normal encounters if you play very poorly. If you don't manage bosses well, you can wipe. On the other hand, like previous titles, if you spam 200 CP ultimates on bosses, you can wipe them out in 1 or 2 turns. Your characters have unique animations and cut ins for special attacks and they look cool. The music changes when you are struggling. If you get sick of fighting, you are rarely forced to fight anything and combat is easily avoided. Healing outside a battle isn't a hassle. ------------------------*gameplay loop in CS3*You get (skippable) in game cutscenes and interactions for the story. You can also find collectables that affect your "score". At the end of sections, you receive rewards based on how much side content you accomplished. As mentionned before, the game is divided into days and chapters and the game rarely surprises you with "oops you just progressed past a barrier and now have to watch a ton of cutscenes and you can't go back anymore." Most are telegraphed to you very clearly. This NISA version also auto saves the game every 5 minutes over 12 slots. All npcs have development plots, including the shopkeeper which is a favorite of fans of the series. In this game, greyed out talk icons means the dialogue hasn't been updated and all npcs update their dialogue at fairly obvious times. There are mini games like a card battle. It's fairly easy and a fun pass time. The one in this title is an evolution of the one found in CS1 and 2. This means it is -not- the same mini game. -------------------------*Story*As someone who has played a ton of rpgs, I was entertained. There is some element of "pick your love interest". Story has some anime elements but isn't overloaded with fan service.----------------------------*Music and sound*Falcom (the developers) have done great music since nes chiptunes and they have a band playing their tracks. The music is good. A lot of dialogue is voiced but not all of it. I would say over 75% is voiced. ----------------------------*Settings*This game has a lot of quality of life additions you will rarely find in Japanese games, nevermind rpgs. The first time you run the game, it will ask you to customize graphics, language and "cheats" like how fast your turbo mode is in combat and on the field (you can set those independently). When you start the game directly, from steam, you can start the game through the custom screen, normally or AUTOMATICALLY SKIP ALL SPLASH SCREENS AND GO TO YOUR LAST MANUAL SAVE. Wow. Didn't know how awesome that was until this game did it. I was really impressed with the extra quality of life features and I think it's one of the defining good parts of the game.-------------------------------------*Negative*Game ends suddenly. You are expected to play cold steel 4 for closure.-------------------------------------*Can I start with this game?"Most people will tell you no because "every game builds on the previous titles and characters come back from LOH 5 to 12 so you will miss a lot of nuance". Logically, I agree with this. However, I will say, YES, YOU CAN START WITH 3 (LOH13). The game gives you background information about what happened in cold steel 1 and 2. I read those for about 1 or 2 hours and I thought, "ok, I don't know if I will remember all that and all these characters but let's start." That's not enough to catch you up. However, the game also introduces flashbacks, the characters reminisce about that one time that happened" so you always feel in the loop. It doesn't make the previous games worthless. I actually feel like going back to the game I was doing (LOH6 in my case) and keep going. Movies make prequels and sequels and they work and I would argue that playing older titles later would be like playing a sequel. Pacing issues from Trails in the sky FC and Cold steel 1 are "fixed" and the game doesn't drag like them. Recommend to people who already like rpgs, reading and anime fans in particular. _childDocuments_.review: As a Trails game, it fufills  all the things we enjoy about the Cold Steel arc of games. It's a 100 + hour story with tons of politically-driven + slice-of -life elements, extremely detailed world building, and a quick to grasp combat system with many game breaking mechanics to play around with.Gameplay: If you don't mind many of the game's mechanics being overpowered to the point of being too easy, you will have a fun time playing around with all the neat ways you can defeat enemies in just a few turns, or even one hit. However, it's also the biggest criticism because alot of the game's depth feels less rewarding when you don't have any challenges to complement that depth. Story: This is a continuation of Cold Steel 1 and 2, so please play those games before this one, or else you won't understand the plot at all. As expected of a Trails game: super detailed lore, lots of dialogue, etc. However, these games are what would be described as "Story RPG's", meaning most of the game is almost like a visual novel, with 80% of the game being long stretches of dialogue, with some combat in between. It isn't for everyone, but if story is your priority, you'll enjoy Trails games. Cold Steel  3 is no exception. Contains a  mixture of sci-fi, fantasy, politics, and slice-of-life; all with a relatively "anime" flavor to it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an improvement over the previous two Cold Steel games, but its still pretty rough overall.The smaller core cast works well and gives the new characters a much better chance to shine than those in CS1 and 2, but keeping so many other legacy characters involved in the story made it feel much more bloated than necessary. The plot suffers a fair bit from the need to simultaneously flesh out its new characters and remind you that all the other characters still exist and are doing important things, bloating the story with way more than was really needed.At least the team building side of the gameplay was handled well since the old and new characters were kept separate most of the time, letting you both put a lot of effort into building an effective team for the new cast (since you'll have them for the whole game) while still offering variety thanks to the occasional involvement of characters from previous games.As for the actual combat, I like the theory behind the new mechanics but they're horribly unbalanced in their current state. Bosses take a huge amount of damage before their defenses break and, unless you're using Juna's order to boost break damage then they'll heal whatever damage they took before long anyway. The only strategy I could put together that consistently worked was to stack orbs and orders to increase break damage, unleash a bunch of S-Crafts right off the bat, and hope to god that you can finish them off before they recover from the break. Anything else just failed to work, leaving the boring and exploitative strategy as the only real option.Cold Steel 3 isn't bad. I like it better than the previous Cold Steel games. But its still far from the peak of the earlier titles in Sky and Zero/Azure.

_childDocuments_.review: TLOH: TOCS III story is a continuation of the previous two entries in the series (so you better play the prior two games before this one) while also making references to prior games that took place in a different part of the continent (i.e. Trails in the Sky and the two "Crossbell arc" games, which have yet to be officially released in English as of this writing).In this entry, Rean (the main character) goes back to the military campus lifestyle, but as an instructor this time around, so this game goes back to the old TOCS I style of "campus life + battle facility + field trip missions and battles" which, while it was a unique trait that the first game had, it isn't necessarily something I wanted to see 'revisited" in a later entry in the series (I much would've preferred if they continued the style of storytelling that was introduced in )The story itself isn't bad and there were many MANY "jaw dropping/shocking" moments in this entry up till the very end, although I will say that, personally speaking, I'm , so even though I understand why the story in this game went in that direction, I personally much prefer a "happy closure" to the story, even if it was a "temporary" happy ending (as it was done in TOCS II) leading-up to the events in the next installment in the series.This entry introduces some brand new characters who will form the "new class 7" (while having Rean as an instructor), while also meeting some familiar faces from prior games in the franchise, who will become playable for a limited time as the story progresses. In that sense, it is not that different from the prior two games in the series, and while I did end-up liking some of the new characters, I will say I didn't like the "new smaller class 7" as much as I did the original class 7 characters.On the other hand, the villains in this games are mostly characters seen in prior games (while sprinkling in some new villains here and there) and as usual, this franchise is known to have a great variety of interesting villains, so I have no complains here. Although, as the 3rd entry in the TOCS series, I wish they had at least revealed the full cast of the villains that constitute the entire villainy organization (Ouroboros) rather than just show-off some of them and not giving any details of what the remaining members of the organization are doing IMO.As someone who LOVES intense boss fights and intense battle music, THIS is the main reason I got into the series in the first place. When The Legend of Heroes series is mentioned, the first thing that comes to mind in the AWESOME boss battles and battle music (both regular and boss music) that this franchise it has, so obviously I will have high expectations for those aspects whenever a new Legend of Heroes game is released.Now, having said that and in comparison to the prior 2 games in the TOCS series, while this 3rd entry still did very well in terms of boss fights and battle music, I will say it did  perform as good as I hoped for compared to the previous games. The best way to explain it in comparison to TOCS II would be:-  Is very  while attempting to sound "threatening" vs. bosses.-  Is a mixture  while attempting to sound "threatening" vs. bosses.And don't get me wrong, the boss music in this entry wasn't bad at all, it is just that I personally prefer the INTENSE/FAST-PACED THREATENING boss music that Trails of Cold Steel II had rather than the "calm-er beautiful sounding" boss music that Trails of Cold Steel III had.The bosses themselves were cool/epic to fight, although on the whole, I personally prefer the human bosses we had back in Trails of Cold Steel II (both friendly and evil boss battles) than the ones here in Trails of Cold Steel III.Despite my critic on some aspects of this entry when compared to past entries in the series, The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III is  that builds on the events of the past 2 games, while setting the stage for what I could only hope to be the greatest finale of them all when The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel IV (The End of Saga) is released later down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm Torn when it comes to reviewing this title. On the one hand i enjoyed playing it, on the other hand i hated it. People's complaints about the cutscenes in this game are more than justified, they could easily cull 2/3 of the cutscenes and still get their point across. The majority of the cutscenes go like this, "Thankyou for (insert task here)", with a reply like "Oh no there is no need to thank me for (insert task here)".I truly loved 'The last remnant' (TLR) and was pleased to see that the combat in this title was similar, the way you can chain opponents together for better rewards and xp, it may have tickled my itch for another TLR, but it certainly didn't scratch it.TLR was a more serious title, this title was base around children being the most powerful, and anyone over 19 years old is considered OLD. Alot of the reviews for this title will say "You really need to have played the previous titles to understand whats going on in this one. I disagree, i watched every cutscene, and there are alot of flashback moments that explain things, albeit not in the detail of playing previous titles, but enough for me to understand what was going on.I guess if you enjoyed 'Bleach' or 'Naruto', you'd enjoy this game, a bunch of teenagers saving the worlds. If you're a voyeur and like looking up the skirts of young girl's, YOU'LL LOVE THIS TITLE! As a fully grown man i felt so wrong with the amount of up skirt action.So i'm recommending this game to teenagers, it has a lot motivational, "Find your resolve", "Setup networks of friends" and "Excel at what you choose to do", Same thing as you would see or read in just about every anime/manga.For an adult, the story is just tedious, and the ending is TERRIBLE.Will i play an NG+? HELL NO. The problem with an NG+ is the cutscenes. Even if you skip them all, they transition in and out meaning your watching nothing for 30 seconds, and then the VERY poor decision to divide cutscenes into smaller cutscenes, so instead of skipping the entire section, they are divided into smaller sections, so you are actually skipping anywhere from 2-10 scenes individually, as i mentioned before, that can add up to 5 minutes per cutscene.If your a fan of the 'Trails of' series, well you'd love how many characters reappear, for me, this is all i need to see from the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I played every single game of the Trails of Cold Steel series and i have to say that is one of the best JRPG indie series out there.You don't need to play the old Trails in the Sky, this is a new series which take place in the same world and after some years so they are connected but there is no need to play the older games because it's a new story with new characters in fact i didn't play the old ones.However i HIGHLY recommend to start from the 1st game and not this one otherwise you won't understand what's going on and who the characters are.It's true that here we have a new Class VII but trust me this is not the entry point of the series. _childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend you play Cold Steel 1 and 2 before playing this one.  If for whatever (stupid) reason you can't, then this actually is a better starting point than 2 since 1 and 2 are almost right after one another and this one starts a new "arc" within the Erebonian section of the Trails series.  The game does its best to help those in that unfortunate situation by having a very comprehensive recap menu section of 1 & 2's characters/events.  If you can't be bothered to read and go through those parts, then you won't like this game anyway as it is very lore heavy with lots of reading/dialogue as all Trails games are known for.That out of the way, it is another great Trails entry with what you have come to expect from these games.  Like I mentioned before, there is a bit of a timeskip since Cold Steel 2 ended, so this makes room for new characters to be developed.  The old class VII does take a backseat to these new characters, but fear not, as the ones you've grown to love from the first two games still find ways to be relevant to the game.  This is also where Trails starts to reward fans of the other Liberl/Crossbell arcs as some of the characters from those games will start to show up and make themselves known.  If you are a Trails fan you will not be disappointed.  I do want to note that while the music is still the great quality you expect from Falcom's sound team, I did feel that Cold Steel 2's soundtrack has a definite leg up on this one, but that's a small fault to pay for more Trails entries.

_childDocuments_.review: 👎 As much as I've been enjoying the Trails franchise, this entry has been a time consuming disappointment. It appears that CS3 is a setup for the events of CS4, a repeat of what they did with CS1 and CS2. In other words, it's a padded time filler, where you are once again placed in a school, following school related events. Most of it is meaningless and it's only in the last few hours of the game where anything of import is revealed. There are now too many characters, and it's affecting the game. There's so much switching in and out that it's affecting the consistency and continuity. There are so many characters, that at some points you have to manage three different groups in dungeons; it might sound like a treat but it gets tiring after a while as the presence of too many people dilutes focus and character development and story. It gets a bit silly at times because some of the friends will disappear for a bit, come back, and have to explain that they're caught up with the current story because another friend told them about it. Repeatedly.  There are now so many characters, that several of them even  the same, and I was having trouble telling them apart. I think they really need to reign it in. It feels a bit stupid at times too, because everything is focused around Rean, the main character. It seems it's impossible to have a simply platonic friendship, no, every woman in the game must be attracted to Rean, every guy finds him interesting and wants to be his friend... it's a pointless pseudo-harem-for-gary-stu for no reason. Not just friends, but there are also many, many gray characters standing around in cutscenes with eyes closed, explaining that everything is going according to plan. Repeat ad nauseum. When you do eventually get to fight the much hyped enemies, it ends with no conclusion, except for them brushing it off and quipping that they might have to get serious now. There is no satisfaction from the story-fights against the 'bad guys', and no real conclusions. Towards the end it gets even sillier as you have to face a series of 'enemies' for no reason other than to trim down the size of your main group. New fight mechanics have been introduced, but I think they took it a bit too far... it's now at a point that arts have become useless, you can just dump all points in speed and overpower everyone.  The story is trying to keep its cards way too close to its chest, and there are numerous threads going on. It's very difficult to follow the story for most of the game, until they spend some time explaining some of the backstory right towards the end. Speaking of cards, there's a new minigame involving card deck battles, and it is boring as hell. For some reason the music this time feels generic, and unmemorable. None of them were awful, but they weren't great either. They were just there as background... a departure from the rest of the Trails series. The only track I like was 'Alley of Silence'. 👍 There are still some things the game does do well. There's a turbo mode so you can speed through scenes; the game is so long that they had to introduce it. The graphics are well improved, and the environments are still nice to run around in. Fishing doesn't suck, it's well designed!The combat  still satisfying, it's now mainly centred around criticals and speed, and it can be satisfying to overpower a powerful enemy with 'bursts'. That said, it's a shame that arts users are not really needed, but they still exist and only take up space. The clothes don't suck, thankfully, and for many characters you can now get costume drops while playing, which is quite nice! There are also alternative hair colors you can get for some of the characters but they just make them look out of place. ➡️ Overall, an unsatisfying entry in the trails series, it's an excessively padded filler with the real story towards the end. The 4th entry will probably be enjoyable, but this current filler has left me fatigued.

_childDocuments_.review: I do love Trails series, and as a whole, I think it offers an epic fantasy experience that no other series does, and it has been my favourite JRPG series for a long time now... but that doesn't mean its without flaws. The story is very linear and very plot driven. Although the characters are great and you rarely feel like the plot is driving the characters into a direction they would not naturally go themselves, there's still a ton of sudden "revelations" that don't really make sense, or inexplicable plot armours on certain characters to keep them alive no matter what. Also the game (and the series in general) feels like its constantly at war with itself because its based on a quite dark story, but most elements of the game (mainly the characters) are blindingly bright, optimistic, cheery and cheesy at times. It makes the main characters feel way out of their depth at times, like when they're casually having honest conversations with their enemies who have slaughtered hundreds of people and plan to ruin the world. The enemies are basically treated like naughty children upto no good, when actually they should be treated like psychopaths they are. Well anyway, the negative things aside, I am extremely looking forward to the next instalment although this arc has gone longer than it should have. Gameplay is really fun and one of the best turn & party based games out there in my mind. Other games should take note of how this one tries as much as possible to force the player to use all its cast of characters. I'm already thinking of doing a second playthrough despite just finishing the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: I was originally worried when I first heard NIS America was doing the work for this. They had a few botched titles in the past. But this game was on another level from their past work. There were a few bugs but many of them got fixed very quickly. The game runs very smooth without any hiccups. I'll keep updating this review if I do find any issues but their PS4 translation and work was amazing so I'm counting on this one being of similar quality. Story: 9/10 - One of the most unique stories I've ever come across. There are a few cliche characters but each of them still feels unique. The characters from CS1 and CS2 in my opinion are much better written and fleshed out, but that's a given seeing as they had two full games to develop them. Seeing some characters from other games in the series was a huge treat! I won't spoil who here but they were spot on and perfect. There are plenty of twists and turns and some predictable outcomes and some very not-so-predictable outcomes keeping you on your toes the whole time.GFX: 7/10 (Art 9/10) - Falcom isn't known for their super high quality graphics but they are very passable. The art style is still very beautiful and the art team did an amazing job with the GFX engine they were confined to. All the characters are very well stylized and the environmental artwork is beautiful. Animations are a bit wonky sometimes with awkwardly long handshakes or body language. This might be more on the animation team though. Its a minor nitpick but it is noticeable.Sound: 10/10 - Not much to say here other than AMAZING. The music in this series has always been some of the best. The SFX and voice overs are spot on with included options for English or Japanese voice acting with English subtitles.Gameplay 8/10 - Gameplay is smooth and intuitive. All buttons are mappable and I highly suggest mapping your own button layouts if you're using a keyboard and mouse. I have not used a controller on the PC version but on the PS4 the button layout was, in my opinion, perfect. The out-of-combat camera and movement is clean and responsive and the in-combat mechanics, which are turn-based, are deep enough to keep battles and strategies interesting. I'm not a fan of the auto-battle function as the AI is rather daft and never uses the ideal arts or crafts. Side activities such as cooking and fishing have been improved from CS1 and CS2 and I do like the changes. I wish their was mouse support on the camp menu and maybe the quick travel menu but I believe that is due to more of an game engine limitation being a port of a PS4 game.Overall: Great job NISA and I'm looking forward to seeing your work with CS4. I'm hoping the voice cast is the same as they did an amazing job. Thank you for putting your best into this one.

_childDocuments_.review: So Trails of Cold Steel 3 as a fan is concerned is pretty much something you should pick up to complete your journey toward the stories finale. The game adds some new mechanics to the game such as Brave orders which help confer a tactical advantage during some of the tough boss battles. Though most of the game mechanics set up in the previous game are left intact and have only been added to, so no gripes there. The story of Trails of Cold Steel 3 is still pretty much the same collection of political intrigue, international conflicts, and personal hang ups. However something felt off about this game in comparison to the previous release. I don't know if it's the final boss battle and ending being sequel bait rather than a satisfying conclusion for ToCS3. Perhaps it was the new class VII appearing to be MacGuffins rather than characters unto themselves half the time. The McGuffins even extended into the story revelations that were supposed to be shocking but happened so often it started to feel flat and dull opposed to shocking and exciting. Despite all my gripes I still enjoyed the story overall for the most of the game and found a good deal of the character development outside the scope of the main story was fun and enjoyable. The final verdict on this game really comes down to whether you have played any of the previous entries in the series. If you are a fan of the previous games then picking up Trails of Cold Steel 3 seems an obvious choice. Pick it up at full price and all the little DLC items are up to personal preference rather than necessity. It doesn't do anything outside the mold of the previous games and that could be something you really dislike or something you are happy about. However if you have never played any of the previous games in the series then this will seem to be a a average and old RPG experience with a bloated cast of characters that you may or may not care for. I would probably suggest it at a sale price of maybe 25% to 50% off.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, excellent saga. (I'm writing this after playing 1 to 4 straight)(EDIT: for short, I want to let you know that all the TRAILS OF: games are connected not matter which one. They occur around the same time in the same continent on different "countries"; events covered in one game are metioned in another; all of this because the director of the franchise wanted to create a big world with entaglement in a Game of Thrones size/fashion; so these are story-heavy and if something feels odd, probably it was covered/going to be covered in another Trails of.) I have to make a big review for this one: Gameplay-wise, it's an updated version of 1 and 2. Mechanics are tuned up, in battle a new "break bar" is added which works as an "armor" for enemies (break it and you get some free turns for your team);  also now we have "orders" which are party buffs you can use instead of always going for the classic "all-out attack" from previous game; so it deepens the strategy you have to use.This is a "reboot" of the 1 and 2; where you have to use mostly the new cast; you will have to start again from level 1. (Old cast have their skills already but they are weaker; so you will learn the "TRUE" version of each skill making them strong again). Good thing is you already know who is the "mage", who the "cleric", who the "evasion tank"; etc.The new cast, while shorter-staffed, they are all more customizable; they will be easily adaptable to several roles; while having their "senpais" specializing more on fixed builds. On the bad side, I did not like the "meet this condition" fights because one wrong move and it was impossible to complete.I absolutely loved the mini card game, a simplier version of Magic! the gathering. I didn't enjoyed mini games like this since Triple Triad in FFVIII.Story-wise; it has it's ups and downs: Your protag now instead of student; it's a teacher; and you will have to lead your new Class. Actually you don't do it, because you just bond with them like in previous games, but it feels nice all the call backs to Rean's own school days. The new school is fine; but I would have like it to be set on the old one. It took a lot of time; maybe too much to get to know the new cast, mainly because you are constantly being helped by guest members from the previous games; so you will be more inclined to use the power-house witch you already intuitively know rather than using the new rifle ""mage"" which I first build with physical damage until I realized all her skills were magic-typed.Anyways, I really liked the story so far, so much, it hooked me enough to want to try all the TRAILS OF games. I want to see these grand story by myself.(Also some the cluncky mechanics from the PSP era are back; like summoning a way-to-big motorcycle hard to handle on "turbo mode" that crashes into every mob you try to avoid)

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, after getting further, I'd say 'neutral' on the review if I could, but honestly don't think it deserves the "overwhelmingly positive" rating. Rean's turned into a nosy tool, the new characters that make up your team are dull and uninteresting (Their back stories are plenty interesting, but the people themselves have no real differing personalities or drives). The chemistry that made up I and II is all gone. They also kind of spit in the face of the emotional impact of events in the other game, which is kinda lame.Best comparison I can do is that it's like watching through Scrubs again and hitting Season 9. Sure, some of the characters you know and love are still there, but the soul's gone out of them, and all the people who are gone are replaced by boring nobody's who couldn't fill the shoes of a toddler, let alone shoes the size that their predecessors left.Edit: Also, not much I can say that wouldn't spoil the story...but holy hell do the decisions a lot of otherwise reasonable characters made in the last few hours of the game make absolutely no sense. Sincerely hope there's more to it, because that was just dumb.Edit 2: Alright, finished everything on the final game too. A part of me loves it, because it reminds me of a really good, well thought-out DnD plot by a loving DM, who is forced to come up with spur of the moment explanations for things due to the idiocy of his party. But ultimately, as the culmination of four AAA-priced games, this entire series falls pretty flat.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid entry in the Cold Steel series. There are a few notable improvements from the previous entries. The most noticeable is the overall presentation. Although the game uses the same engine as the previous games, the character models are a lot cleaner. They also improved the battle interface, it is now sleek and intuitive. The game, overall, feels a lot more "modern". A big departure from the previous games is that we are now introduced to a new main cast. Without any spoilers, the new students are engaging enough that the chemistry feels comfortable enough to carry the whole game. It does make you miss the old cast, though. There's not much to say. If you're already invested in the previous games, this is a very engaging sequel. You probably already know everything you need to know from the previous games. If not, then I wouldn't recommend you play this entry without playing the previous games.

_childDocuments_.review: I kind of like this game since I love turn-based JRPG and anime in general and I give it a 7/10 and a the same time a thumbs down. For the first game, there was a similar pacing and it was bad as well, but I tried to be patient since it's a 4 games series and the first one was meant to be an introduction. But game #3? The main story should have picken up by now and while some stuff did happen in game #2, the transition between that game and the third is really bad. 40 hours of gameplay and I'm like "feels like nothing happened yet, except for the heavy filler dialogues". I give this game a 7/10 because gameplaywise I have fun and I like anime. However, I still feel like giving it a thumbs down because of the poor pacing the series suffers as a whole, which makes story advancement terrible and for a JRPG, this sucks bad.

_childDocuments_.review: There's not much to tell about the gameplay, since its not really different from the previous games. I mean it's not a bad thing, because the core gameplay of Trails is already very good from the beginning. They did add some minor features, and all of them made the gameplay even better than before. About the story, Falcom gave us a more serious story and focus more about the politics and the corruption inside the Erebonian Empire. This time, the story told us more about the "dark side" of a vast nation and full of conflicts between the social classes. They did a fine job, as usual, but they did not forget the "slice of life" aspect, and I appreciated it. The story can be confused with those who didn't play the previous games, especially Cold Steel 1 and 2. But hey, the name of this game is Cold Steel 3, so anyone who intend to play it should realize that, right?Apart from the old characters from the previous Trails games, Cold Steel 3 introduced us to some more, and I'm quite surprised that Falcom managed to give all of them decent time and moment to develop their characteristic and chemistry to each other. A very good game, to be honest. Put aside the story and characters, I think that the gameplay is better than Cold Steel 1 and 2, and almost perfect. Highly recommended, and if you're gonna play it, it's worth your time, just... remember to play Cold Steel 1 and 2 first.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the third entry in the "Cold Steel" series, and as such is not a good launching point. The Legend of Heroes series is one that benefits greatly from playing through a majority of the previous titles. I recommend at the very least starting with Cold Steel 1; though playing through "Trails in the Sky" would be your best starting point to the series as a whole. As for the game itself, it's an excellent continuation of the franchise. If you enjoyed the previous Cold Steel titles, you'll enjoy this. It contains the same strong emphasis on characters as the others, and talking to the various inconsequential NPC's that populate the towns and cities is just as interesting as ever. Graphically it's more beautiful than any other in the series, with significantly improved animations both in and out of combat. If you did not enjoy the previous games, there will be little here to convert you.

We get a development of what went on in Crossbell, and characters from Liberl finally appear again. Also, we get backstories that we were waiting for a loong time! _childDocuments_.review: Yeah...so just so we're clear, again, I'm not saying this is a bad game.  It's not.  But...I mean fresh off a replay of 1 and 2 and the flaws are just so glaring that I simply can't.  There are times it feels like a completely different game/experience and times it feels like an evolution of what came before.  It's just so inconsistent it's frustrating.This of course is the start of the NISA era, where less care and attention was given to the game and it clearly shows.  It's better than 4, but a huge step back from 1 and 2.✅Graphically it's superior to 1 and 2 in nearly every way.✅3 has the best music tracks of the series (some are reused but there are some new ones here).✅3 obviously focuses on New Class VII, and as a result their character development is stellar here, especially Ash and Musse.✅The new control scheme didn't go over well with everyone, but I thought it was awesome personally.  Made battles go a very good deal faster.✅From a story perspective, 3 did the best job at expanding almost everything and helping you better understand the situation that was going on in Erebonia at a macro level.✅This is the first Cold Steel to actually have auto-advance text (and believe me, it's welcomed).⛔Old Class VII is relegated to cameo appearances where they just come and go.⛔Most of Old Class VII doesn't act like they actually care about Rean with the exception of Alisa and maybe Elliot.⛔There's a weird bug with 120fps where when you do the strong field attack, your character does a breakdance.  It's weird.⛔There are parts of the game that feel rushed.  George's actions, the end game, the build to Ash's actions, Musse's reveal, etc.  They're very lightly hinted at, then all of a sudden out of nowhere, "TA DA!".  It got old real fast.⛔3 is the first (and I believe only) one in the series that lets you use characters that are otherwise NPCs in battle, such as Jessica, who's actually a decent fighter.  But you only get to use her for one quest fight.  It makes me think they had broader plans to make more of Thors playable and changed their mind at some point.⛔While 3 has "better" music tracks, they don't fit the scenes nearly as well as 2 did.  ⛔Arguably half of the quests feel like padding, where you're just going around acting like a bracer but not really developing or learning anything.⛔The amount of voice acting.  I tracked it.  It's about 30% of the amount that you had in Cold Steel 1.  That's just unacceptable.  This wouldn't bother me much, except...⛔There are some cutscenes that are longer than 15 minutes.  Since these are unvoiced, this gets real boring, real fast.  I don't think Xenosaga 1 was this bad.  If they were fully voiced it'd be fine, since I can listen from another room.  ⛔They still never explained (as in, SHOWED ME IN CUTSCENES) the lead up to Rean and Altina pairing up, or her assignment to Thors.Again - NOT a bad game.  But a huge step back from what came before.

_childDocuments_.review: BEFORE STARTING THE REVIEW:Please for the love of god play Trails in the Sky FC, Trails in the Sky SC, Trails in the Sky the 3rd, Trails from Zero, and Trails to Azure before even playing ANY of the Cold Steel games. It will make you much more invested and immersed in the overall world and playing Cold Steel games before them would be doing yourself a HUGE disservice. Trust me, every game is worth every second spent in them and the overall story in the past eight games (including this one as the eighth) has been truly amazing and a well worth experience.Wow, there is so many things I have to say about Trails of Cold Steel 3. There is so many amazing things about this games that make me love the trails series even more. The first thing that comes to mind is the story for Cold Steel 3. The story was ABSOLUTELY SPECTACULAR. It continues on roughly a year after the events of Trails of Cold Steel 2 in a whole new environment. You get to explore areas of Erebonia that you couldn't explore before. These areas primarily consisted of the field exercises of the opposite group you were put into from Trails of Cold Steel. The story keeps a nice pace throughout it, letting you explore areas as it starts to ramp up. Speaking of ramping up, THIS STORY RAMPS UP REAL HARD. I am FLOORED at how many twists and genuinely unexpected things that happened in this game. I was left speechless multiple times throughout the game, which primarily related to characters. The story also made me tear up and cry almost as much as the Sky games did.Speaking of characters, most of the newer characters are genuinely great. I didn't particularly like Ash or Major Micheals that much at all, but outside of those two I enjoyed every new character that was introduced in this game. They also expand upon the character stories from Class VII in more detail, letting you understand their histories even better. They also expand upon characters which have been either mysterious for multiple games (Lechter) or for characters that have not been expanded upon in the previous Cold Steel games. Also in regards to the character bonding, it was pretty satisfying in this game overall. I enjoyed spending time with Towa and gushing over how cute she is. The only complaint I would have about the bonding system would be that there are only three characters which you can romance in this game. Those characters are Laura, Emma, and Alisa. However, this is amended in the next game Trails of Cold Steel IV, allowing you to romance other characters like Towa. In regards to the music, it is like previous Trails games where it's constant banger after banger after banger, and Cold Steel 3 is definitely no exception. The whole OST is extremely well made and uses some of the tracks you're familiar with from previous Cold Steel games along with introducing new songs as well. I could jam out for hours on end just listening to every song in this game, especially the final dungeon theme and the boss themes. The music ends up being perfectly timed to the current scene going on and generally enhances the mood, either making you cry/tear up to feeling excited for whatever battle you are getting into.For the general gameplay, I definitely have to say it's the most satisfying out of Trails of Cold Steel 1-3. The order system that gets introduced into the game adds a new layer of strategy that you can use to either deal significantly more damage than you could before, or reduce incoming damage in prep for massive attacks that you may be unable to avoid (I recommend using Impede 3 plus another Impede orbment, it's funny hitting bosses and general enemies while they're trying to cast arts and then just saying haha no.). You're also introduced an interesting sub-mater quartz system where you can use some of the skills/stats from another character's Master Quartz and use it on another character (albeit limited to one sub-Master Quartz use per Master Quartz). The Link system also feels a lot more fluid than before and the designs they did between the characters you're linking, making it a lot more clean and less confusing. In terms of art, this game's art SLAPS. The new character portrait art they've done for every single character's S-Craft is so good. The new art style is really satisfying and adds even more character to each S-Craft. This usage also doesn't apply to only the characters you control, even enemy characters will have their own S-Craft art too, and man some characters look AMAZING in their S-Craft art. The same art from the S-Crafts are also used when doing combos with your links or when doing an all out attack on the enemies. In regards to the 3D models, they're just as amazing as well. The new models compared to the older 3D models are just night and day. Everything about them and the other UI/Art in the game scales up wonderfully to higher resolutions like 4K. Even the environments are more captivating than ever before, especially when looking out onto places like an ocean or in other pretty areas. They made sure to go all out with the new 3D models and environment with this gameOverall, I love this game and everything it brings to the table. It doesn't matter what the game does, it just does it EXTREMELY well and truly adds more wonderful things to the Trails series. It definitely gave me a lot more game time as well, which is more than welcome with any Trails game in my book. Another small note, the voice acting for this game has expanded a lot, leading to more voiced scenes (I use the Japanese dubbing) compared to previous entries in the Cold Steel series. I would 100% recommend this if you are continuing off of Trails of Cold Steel 2 and have completed the previous games in the whole Trails series. Definitely recommend it at both full price and discounted.Another Side Note:I love Towa, she's so cute and amazing. This is now my 3rd game going down the Towa bond route and I plan on continuing to romance/bond with her in the 4th game of the Cold Steel/Erebonia arc. Towa best.

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III. This is the 3rd series following I and II. The story begins about a year and a half after the ending of the previous ones. So if you're focused on the story, it's recommended to play the previous ones first, but if you're interested in an improved JRPG system with the newly game engine, it's okay to play this game in advance. As you may know, this third work has been released as the PS4 console version first. Since the previous ones are based on PSVITA / PS3, such a lead platform replacement has played a major role in improving game quality. Especially, the battle system has fairly enhanced. It still follows the active time battle like the last series, but the UI was changed more intuitively, and the battle implemented the seamless battle. In addition, the visual graphics are pretty neat and of good quality. This is definitely a good model for the next generation JRPG.The story is interesting overall. You can meet your grown game characters you have played before, and you can also start ties with new characters. Despite the many characters, the stories with them are natural and immersive. However, some events are somewhat repetitive and have the same progress pattern. Other mini games and side quests are another great place to relax and play. The game play time for reaching the ending is at least 60 hours. As the game enters the last part, the story tends to be rather abrupt. Except for those parts, the overall game experience is great.The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III. This is a somewhat innovative JRPG. The game has been greatly improved due to the replacement of the lead platform. The battle parts and visual graphics are particularly impressive. The gameplay convenience is better than any other series. As well as existing characters, new characters are constantly being added, but the scenario plot is still interesting except for the latter part of the story. If you are interested in experiencing the new generation of JRPGs, this game will be for you. Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: [NO SPOILERS]ToCS3 is finally here, and it's excellent. There were fears that the localisation was going to be a botched job, but thankfully it has turned out to be stunning. How good is it?STORY: 8/10The story is constructed like ToCS1, you start in a prologue that sets the stakes for the first half of the game, and then finally you reach that point and fight the boss. Then you spend the next half of the game with significantly raised stakes and a big event occurring in Erebonia. Very exciting.CONS: Sometimes the motivations for these characters are a bit bizarre. You have the typical "I must do it for my friends! For class 7!" But you also have "I must stop the evil guys, who are doing something evil, even though it hasn't been revealed to me how or why it's evil!"  PROS: There are some really emotionally shaking events that occur. You'll see for yourself what I mean when you play the final chapter. When the stuff happened, I was gutted, shocked etc. Just like 1 and 2, the story ends with a very big event going down, and the end of 3 tops them all.GAMEPLAY: 9/10PROS: There are a ton more master quartz, arts and fancy mechanics to play with. yay! Also, the game has been balanced. No more infinite AT delay stacking nonsense from 2, and no more 500k damage arts. We now have the break mechanic to focus on. Each opponent has a break gauge. Damage depletes the gauge and when it is broken the enemy enters a completely vulnerable state where all attacks deal crits and they cannot take any actions for a turn. Dealing crits fills your brave point meter. You can spend brave points in combat to grant powerful buffs to your party, like 0.3x delay, -50% damage, instant arts, perfect reflect etc. Each playable character in your party offers their own buff you can select from, with more powerful buffs requiring more brave points. CONS: If you like to min-max your party, do every side-quest and collect every gear, you'll find hard mode too easy towards the end. I recommend you pick nightmare, but beware, there are boss fights around the beginning and middle that will absolutely crush an unprepared party even on hard.  The final dungeon is also not as good as 2 was. The final boss is easier too, and this is why you should play nightmare if you are a min-maxer. TIPS:Recommended party roles:> Breaker: A role stacked with +break damage quartz who has crafts with break damage. Sole role is to rapidly deplete gauge meters. Juna has a Brave Point buff that increases party break damage by 300%, highly recommend using this at the start of battle and making Juna a breaker.> Evasion tank: Ideal for Kurt/Fie, better for Fie. Works the same as in ToCS2, but this time you have the sirius master quartz that makes your evasion counter attacks deal +600% damage. Add rage quartz for 100% counter attack crits and you can wipe out enemy parties whenever simply by standing in the middle of them. Annoyingly, Kurt is quite bad at this because his swords knockback enemies out of his own range whenever he attacks, so for many enemies you have to walk him right up to them and not attack, which is a complete waste of potential. Fie is however, as usual, the perfect girl.> CP battery: Obviously this is Rean's function. By the end of the game, you will be able to recharge over 100CP every turn. Don't use this to spam S-craft however. instead, keep his spirit unification permanently on, and only S-craft if you use a delay negating Brave point buff. With a good build and buffs, you can actually make Rean a CP battery with 100% evasion and 100% crits with 100% increased STR/ATS/SPD. An absolute monster. > Instant Arts caster:Arts have been nerfed compared to 2, but still become insanely powerful by the end, and there are more of them. More statuses too, but these are irrelevant to bosses so don't worry too much. The build you want to work towards is a +SPD -cast time -EP cost. By the end you'll be able to throw map wiping arts with a lower delay than walking.And now, my favourite build using the interactions of the game mechanics. I call it the lmao-tank, for reasons you will see. I haven't mentioned it yet, but in ToCS3 you get to slot 2 master quartz, a primary and secondary. You get the 3 main effects of the primary and the 1st main effect of the secondary, and you can slot a secondary MQ at the same time another character is using it as their primary.Master quartz: KeeperThis MQ reduces damage recieved as HP drops (30-99%) So if you have low health, you take very little damage. Sub Master quartz: SophiaAutomatically recover from K.O. (Recover 100% HP, CP +200, *twice* per battle)Accessories:1st slot: Platinum pecky badge: +9999 HP.2nd slot: Blue Star Lion Heart Medal: STR/DEF/ATS/ADF +100, Abnormal Stats NullifyThe second slot is optional. You can make this even more overkill by switching Blue star withLi'l Devil doll: HP +1000 / Prevents K.O. Revives with full HP (doesn't break)or if you have a boss with problematic status use a grail locket to prevent all statuses.I put all of these on Jusis to make use of his perfect reflect craft, and then made him cast seraphic ring whenever he got low on health. Seraphic ring btw revives all party members to max health. At the end of the game he has over 20k health and takes a fraction of the amount of damage based on his remaining health in %. One shot boss S crafts do several hundred damage when they get him low. And regeneration which heals % of health completely negates boss damage at lower healths. If you feel the need to panic, just cast seraphic ring and go back to full health. I never once had Jusis KO. But in theory if I did, I would have to bear through the arduous process of losing all his health again 4x before he finally kicks the bucket.  This build does not die. It can face tank as many boss S crafts as you can throw at it and I haven't even mentioned quartz. I recommend you make it and then have it in your reserves in case something gets tricky. It is the ultimate get-outta-jail-free card.

_childDocuments_.review: A grand step up from Cold Steel 1 and 2. Visuals are much better, the character models in particular are fantastic, the size of the main party is much smaller which allows each character to have more development and relevance, and the story is on a much greater scale than it's predecessors. I HIGHLY recommend playing ALL of the previous games before this one, not just Cold Steel 1 and 2. The first two chapters of this game is blatant fan-service for the Sky and Crossbell arcs and they could feel very underwhelming if you haven't experienced those games. This might be one of series's best yet.

_childDocuments_.review: For the last six months I've been playing through the Trails series from the beginning with Sky FC. It's pretty amazing to see just how far the series has come across several different console generations and up to current gen. Cold Steel III is a gorgeous game that really pushes the envelope for the Trails series, the music, visuals, gameplay, everything has been leveled up here.For someone who has played through all the other games in this series it also feels like a true love letter to fans. The number of references to previous games even going all the way back to the original Sky trilogy, and finally seeing where the story picks up after the Crossbell games has been amazing. Without spoiling anything of the story, I'll just say that Cold Steel IV can't come soon enough and I'm dying to see what happens next in this series.
