_childDocuments_.review: I 100% completed this game in 2020 minutes in one sitting just to write this review and I can say this without a doubt.One Punch Man a hero Nobody wanted is a game that nobody should own as it currently is. The game is plagued with terrible design decisions and can be extremely infuriating at the later stages.Before I really get into the problems with it, I just want to state I honestly do not hate this game as much as most people do and so, if you do like this game please take this review with a punch of salt.STORYThe games story is basically a rehash of the original OPM season one but with some added fluff plus your very own OC which you can customise (even though it’s very little at first) and send them out to help the Hero association and climb the ranks to become the S rank hero of your dreams. The story isn’t as bad as I expected since its basically the same thing but in a different POV. However, my problem is how lifeless most of the cutscenes are and the fact most characters don’t ever change their facial features and just look like they’re staring at what game they’re in and just freeze up.Your OC doesn’t escape this fate either and is normally the person doing it in the first place almost every time mine got into danger he’d have a big bright smile like he wants the end now it broke the immersion of the cutscenes for me.Another poor decision (however a very minor one) was the contribution points system they added and how they force you to get more and more to even progress the game, it essentially incentivises you to play the branch and hero missions but eventually, especially at the last few chapters. Instead of doing maybe 3-4 missions you have to do around 15-20 just to progress to the next cutscene and right after it will ask you to just do the process all over again. Overall, even with the minor repetitiveness that getting contribution points are, the main story isn’t all that bad. Since they already had the building blocks of a good story already, but I just wish they fix up the expression of the characters eventually to make it not look funny.GAMEPLAYThe gameplay is the games biggest flaw while the main game itself is an arena fighter and is honestly kinda fun sometimes when it comes to just playing free mode. Not only that but the styles your OC gets are all unique and fun to play even if it’s just regular OPM character move sets you can still have a ton of fun with. But the moment they added RNG elements to it the game became an absolute dumpster fire.For you to fully understand how bad it is I have a video from a unfair 2v3 I played I was forced this match since its story related it was the last 10 seconds and I was going to win but meteors got RNG into the match and they stunned me enough to make the clock run out before I could win.Now for how RNG works in this game. From what I know when you start a match the game searches for heroes to assist you. It can range from other characters OC that range from newbies to seniors (lv1 to lv99) or actual characters from the show (including Saitama but his chance is most likely below 1% but can be increased with a skill) or the game can decide that it can’t find no one and you have to do a 1v3 and have to cheese your way to victory, this happens more commonly on the harder mission and it gets to a point where you’ll have to reset the match until you get help or equip a skill that increases the chance for a hero to join which wastes a slot you could use to increase a stat.However, that is just a minor thing to the fights actual RNG and where the game really gets hit hard. In every match there’s a chance for the following to happen:-	A random hero will come onto the field and use their special attack on the opponent. This of course ranges from C class to Saitama game ending your opponent.-	A natural disaster which can be something as basic as ground dragon putting you into the dirt, a lightning storm, Geryuganshoop slowing down the fight, Marugori stomping his foot onto the ground, Boros spaceships bombs and the Dreaded Meteor shower.-	A drone which can drop Stamina boost, Defence boost, Attack boost, Max out your Special meter, regain half your health and a chance for the drone to after dropping the item to fly into you and inflict 20% damage at worst.All three of these RNG effect the game significantly and turn a fun match into an unfair stomp from the losing side. I cannot explain how many times I’ve almost defeated an enemy only for the drone to regen half their health and in return getting almost killed by its explosion and being timed out. And since most of the game is this, you’re going to have to get use to it if you want to unlock all the characters since they’re all locked behind story progression.Final ReviewThis game is poorly made and had potential only for it to be wasted on having OC hero and an annoying RNG system to go with it. I don’t recommend this game unless you’re a uber OPM fan and its below $20 or if you friend gifts it to you. If you do get the game or just decided to buy it at full price, it can be fun. For example here is just a few fun things I found while progression throughout the game.My OC turning into Tube man and beating up a monsterA TypoThe fact that every time you level up your master level it spams you with achievement progressGetting chased on the streetThe fact when you walk away from someone they turn black or despawn

_childDocuments_.review: I can definitely see why people would not recommend this game, because it is not without its flaws.  Some of those flaws, like how over the top ridiculous some of the parts are ("Lecture Maaaaaann!") ... I chalk that up to being part of the charm.  OPM is a parody, and it's only fitting that a game based on OPM is also something of a parody.  That said, some of the fighting mechanisms are rather broken, and if you go into it thinking you're getting a "real" fighting game, you're gonna get frustrated.  Like if you get in the first hit, you can pretty much dominate an entire fight by never letting your opponent get a shot in.  Similarly if you DON'T get the first hit, it's entirely possible that you're boned no matter how powerful your character is/skilled you are.Ultimately I chose to play this game in offline mode, because I really am not all that interested in multiplayer/PvP.  And it's perfectly enjoyable as a single-player experience.  I haven't quite finished the story mode yet but what I've seen so far, it basically follows the first season of the OPM anime, retelling the same stories but with you inserted into the world.  Genos is still Saitama's disciple...but when you ask to join, Saitama makes you a disciple of Genos instead.  When Sonic attacks Saitama downtown, you have the option of fighting Sonic as your own character...or you can switch to Saitama to one-punch him if you don't want to bother.  That kind of thing.Is it worth $60?  Ehhhh...I guess to me yeah because I have a disposable income, but if I only had $60 to spend on a video game, I might have gone with something else.  If you're an OPM fan, you'll enjoy it a LOT more than you otherwise would.  You're basically paying for the ability to insert yourself into the OPM universe and experience the story from a slightly different angle than just watching it on TV.Ultimately I'd give this game a 60% rating.   I'm enjoying the experience, I don't regret my purchase, but at the same time I completely sympathize with all those who gave it a thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real example of a mixed bag. If you like One Punch Man, I still would not really recommend it unless heavily discounted and you know what to expect. The One Punch Man content is basically season 1 of the anime, but with making a character and playing your character in the role of Saitama when Saitama isn't seen on screen. Saitama is a wild card character that appears depending on several factors, but notably he is also invincible, he can't take damage from NPC enemies, and he does 9999 damage with a single punch.You start the game off as a level 1 character. Your stats are all 1. The main stats are hp, attack and killer move. They're pretty obvious in what they do, hp gives more health, attack makes your regular attacks stronger, killer move makes your special moves stronger. The technique stat does , yet costs more than any other stat (save for appeal). Appeal is a stat which causes  to show up and help you during a fight.Fights are nVn, where n is an indeterminate number. Heroes will show up to come to your aid without any need for you to do anything (other than wait out their arrival), and while the limit is 3v3, technically defeated heroes get removed from your team, freeing up those spaces for other heroes to show up. And some heroes will show up and attack your enemy even if they can't join your team. It's just a chaotic comedic nonsequitur at times. If Saitama shows up and the enemy doesn't have iframes, he will end their existence. You can influence Saitama showing up by using the Baldy Bandana and having a higher Appeal stat.The item system is a bit of an oddity. For completing missions you get what are called "town chips." These come in three colors. These can be used for buying a variety of things, including items which increase exp/contribution. You can buy an item called the cell phone, and the more of them you have, the more likely that heroes will show up to aid you, you start off with 0 but can get up to 99 of them (so I would assume that the likelihood of an event is +n%). You can get accessories that you can equip which have varying changes, like one that will raise your effective hp/attack/killer move stat.Now for my real issue with this game, the combat system. Enemies can attack you in combos, and you can attack enemies in combos. Some enemies have the ability to cancel out of and dodge your combos, but you do not have the ability to cancel out of and dodge an enemy's combo. Even if you do dodge backward to the end of the arena, enemies can close the gap in one or two swings, so even avoiding the enemy's attack can be punished by an enemy who will hit you in the face right after you dodge. The game tells you to press the throw button combination to guard against an enemy's throw, but I don't think throws are telegraphed well enough for you to actually do this. Some fighting styles are absolutely ridiculously overpowered, for example, psychic combat. Psychic attacks are all reach attacks, the jab button shoots waves of psychic power at the enemy, and the power button shoots tornadoes (which you can charge up to launch multiple tornadoes) which have seemingly no limit to their range. If you figure out the timing you can create  combos. I've hit enemies for 34 hit combos, just absolutely destroying them without a chance for them to retaliate.Online play is bad. Like the wait times are bad (in a game that is already notorious for its load times), but there is no restriction on the usage of Saitama as a character. Because of how Saitama is the titular one punch man, it's pretty obvious that using him should be restricted but it isn't. For this reason, it's an unwritten rule that players should avoid using Saitama in online play. There are people in the forums who question why people wouldn't use Saitama, which is silly. Everyone knows that Saitama will win. And in a fight of Saitama vs Saitama, the first Saitama to land a hit will be the victor. Saitama can't be  so instead he excuses himself to go catch the latest sale at the grocery store. Another issue with the online play is that using avatars relies on the stats of the avatars, so unless you already trained your stats, you're going to get destroyed.You can unlock various attack styles like Power (Tank Toppers), Psychic (Tatsumaki/Fubuki), Machine (Genos), and Weapon. You can unlock a variety of killer moves, and even super killer moves if you complete the affection bar for the appropriate hero of the fighting style you want. More than likely once I complete this game, I won't want to replay it again. There's not really any replay value. You can level up every fighting style to its max, you can change your stats by respecializing, there's no permanence to any of the decisions you make.I really love One Punch Man, but it feels like a lot of other anime adaptation fighting games where the source material might be there to some extent, but the game play surrounding is the issue. There's not really much in the way of exploration to be done, you get half a city block, and even that is heavily gated off at the beginning until you do story missions to open them up. And when things get opened up, that doesn't give you a whole city to run around in, it's just a couple of alleys to find shop keepers. That's all.

_childDocuments_.review: At a 60% or more discount worth it.75% for sure.It is much akin to Xenoverse and the likes.It has some good points:1) Character Creation2) Easy to learn and use system.3) A large plethora of missions.4) A leveling system allowing stat customisation and unlocking more skill/ability slots etc.5) Season 1's story mode.6) A few funny though probably meaningless optional things like designing your room, running around the city etc.The downsides:1) Lack in variety of enemies and abilities/fighting styles due to the fact it focusses purely on season 1 and thus has too little to draw from.2) Lack of character design options due to the fact that 1) Certain fighting styles override your look/design too much. _childDocuments_.review: Let me get this out of the way: One Punch Man: A Hero Nobody Knows is not a great game. It has more than its share of issues, including:- Clunky and awkward controls, with most moves having a delay.- Unbalanced gameplay.- Tons of loading screens that are even worse on modern systems than older systems.- Pace-killing elements like tons of e-mails, tutorial screens, and redundant pop-up messages.- Random battle elements (like meteor showers) that are more annoying than fun.- Getting up from being knocked down VERY slowly.- Getting stun-locked by enemy attacks where you end up spending several seconds just watching your character get knocked around and not being able to do anything about it.- Controls that don't seem to respond to your inputs properly. For instance, if I punch my opponent twice while he's blocking, I will pause then hold my attack button to do a guard break, but often my character will continue the combo despite my pause, leaving me vulnerable to counter-attacks. There were also many times where I wanted to throw my opponent (done by simultaneously pressing 2 buttons) but ended up accidentally punching them instead, again leaving me vulnerable. I also can't count how many times I was holding block and tried to dash out of range of my opponent's charge attack, only to not have the dash register at all and end up getting hit.- Extremely repetitive gameplay.So if you take fighting games seriously and want a balanced, polished experience that tests your skill while offering you deep fighting mechanics, this isn't the game for you. Having said that, I still ultimately got a decent amount of entertainment from the game and recommend it despite its many flaws.You play the game's main story mode with a character you create yourself. The character creator is fun to use and, more importantly, you can change any part of your appearance at any time (except your gender, which you can only change after you beat the game's main campaign). As you progress you unlock more and more clothing and accessory options, and you are given a lot of flexibility with the accessorries in particular, allowing you to change where they are positioned as well as their size, color and rotation. Because of this flexibility you are able to create some very unique and imaginative characters. In fact, all the opponent characters that aren't pulled directly from the show are made with the same tools and parts you have access to, and many of them serve as great examples of how to use these pârts creatively (for instance, a Kappa-like character you fight early on uses the "soccer ball" accessory clipped into his head to recreate the plate on his head that kappas are known for). Some parts are a little over-used (it's funny the first time you fight a horse-headed opponent, not so funny the twentieth time), but overall I was impressed with the variety of wacky characters the devs created. You also eventually unlock the ability to transform into a "powered up" form during battle, which you can customize just as you can your regular form. I gotta admit I love when my dark-grey, wide-eyed, modest-framed bunny girl transforms into a larger, more muscular red-skinned bunny beast with wilder hair and a sterner expression, especially when I'm able to pull off a cinematic super-killer finishing move.The character you create is going through the process of becoming a hero and ascending through the ranks (from C to S), just as characters from the show do. In fact, the game takes place during the first season of OPM, so you get to witness and take part in several key battles from the show, as well as build relationships with the show's many memorable characters. Building these relationships (by doing missions linked to specific characters) is how you learn killer moves which you can assign to yourr character's move loadout. You also learn a variety of fighting styles, each of which has many unlockable moves. In theory this gives you a lot of flexibility in terms of how you want to fight (you can pick a speedy, weapon-based style or a slow-but-more-powerful machine-based style, among many others), but I generally only experimented with each style in order to bring them each to level 5, after which I returned to the one or two styles I felt more comfortable with.As much as I criticized the fighting mechanics, it's worth noting that there is fun to be had on a visceral, flashy level. It is satisfying to effectively combine combos and killer moves to do a lot of damage in style, and this remains satisfying even through hundreds of repetitive fights. While there isn't much depth to the mechanics, you do learn some strategy such as charge-attacking enemies as they get up from the ground or dashing around psychic-type opponents who are difficult to approach head-on. Many battles include optional objectives that net you extra rewards if you accomplish them during battle. Mostly these are simple tasks such as getting a minimimum of a 3-hit combo or using at least 2 killer moves, but sometimes they are more challenging such as having to beat the battle within 30% of the time limit having passed. I found these objectives added reason for me to pay at least a little bit of attention to what I was doing instead of button-mashing my way through fight after fight.There's also a mechanic involving support characters who are often depicted as racing to your location to help you out in your battle. Once they arrive, you can switch to that character. This will give you the opportunity to play as a possibly stronger character (especially near the beginning), try out killer moves and fighting styles you wouldn't necessarily use with your character, and play as many recognizable characters from the show. Yes, you occasionally get to play as Saitama himself, and he's as overpowered as you'd expect.There are multiplayer modes, of course, but I only dabbled a little with the online features and haven't played against any other players (I focus mostly on single-player experiences). I can't speak for how fun it is to play with others, but the online functionality will be closing down in February 2022 so don't bother getting this if online functionality is important to you.In conclusion, despite its issues I enjoyed OPM:AHNK enough to not only play through the main campaign but to unlock every achievement (most of which were reasonable, but getting to level 99 was pretty grindy). I had a good time but I don't see myself going back to play it again. While I do recommend it for some simple fun (especially for fans of the show), I would strongly suggest waiting for a big sale. The regular price seems quite high in my opinion, but I got it for 85% off (the DLC, too) and for that price I got more than my money's worth out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Unless you are a super fan of the anime and or manga, avoid this game.Combat system is shallow, I bet you could play this on a smartphone touch screen. The AI has two modes during combat, block and relentless attacking with no interruptions. The combos are barely worth the name, the killer and super moves are flashy but have the most random hitboxes.Story follows season one of the anime, but its done in the most bland method possible (think Naruto games, but far worse). There's too much busy work and random crap you need to progress, and the sudden difficult spikes are just the boss/enemies becoming damage sponges whilst holding nukes.But my biggest gripe with this game is the loading screens and cut scenes. I have a pretty decent gaming PC with an NVMe SSD and this still caused the loading screens to take forever to finish. Nevermind the fact that there's one every 30 seconds, and the cutscenes as well take forever to complete (but at least you can skip then by holding a button)There's a couple different fighting types that you can unlock, each one having different killer moves that you have to unlock from gameplay. However, the coolest mode that you only get after beating the game's story mode, has its skills locked behind the toughest mission fights in the game, and they are tedious.the only reason I finished this game and did a 100% run was because I like the franchise, but any "sane" gamer will probably be bored after 1- 3 hours.Only pick up this game if you are both a super fan of the anime, and the game is on a MASSIVE discount

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this hoping it would be an enjoyable fighter with characters I enjoy. Nothing of the sort. Sometimes I like to play boring generic fighting games, at least then there is some content to play. This game just isn't it...The fighting is all over the place. - There is no point in mastering a style when you can pick the most broken and unbalanced. - The recovery window is atrocious, you can easily get infinite combo'ed by certain styles if you can't time a perfect block. Then while an enemy is down they take too long to get back up, like they're taking a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nap.- Mode changes are completely useless, it doesn't last long enough to do anything. And for half that time you or your opponent is most likely going to be on the ground, waiting for that recovery period.- Stage hazards are just atrocious. It's bad enough I'm getting infinite spammed by NPCs and I have tor revert to cheesing my own said combos just to survive. I have to pray to god I don't get struck by a stray meteor or lightning, completely ruining any moment I had. LOADING SCREENS, WHY ARE THEY SO LONG? SSD or not, this game is incredibly slow and kills any willingness to grind out missions. You'll spend half your time waiting, pressing A, reading tips on a stagnant background.Graphics are terrible. - This art style did not make a graceful leap to 3D, I can't flog it too much for that.- At max setting I could visibly see pixels on textures in the over-world, even when things are fairly far away. - This game looks like it was made for hardware from the 2007 console era.- Animations are reused constantly, are stiff, and lack any impact and emotion.The game felt like I was playing a beta. It's an unpolished mess, made to cash out on new season hype. This is one of the only games I have ever played and genuinely had ZERO fun while playing it. I'm mad I couldn't get a refund. So save your money and don't get it, even if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - This is an average across the board anime arena fighter. Best Played with a gamepad on somewhat up-to-date hardware. Better on sale and more fun for fans of the series than not.Artstyle 70% - Faithful recreation of the designsGameplay: 70% - Standard for an anime arena fighterStory: 65% - It's the plot of One Punch Man but as a gameMultiplayer: 85% - Roster is fairly large. Local with online option both ranked and casualReplay Value: 65% - Story mode, no. Multiplayer, yes.Length: 60% - Unlocking characters for MP is too long; story mode is fine on it's ownOverall grade: 75% -- C - Average but enjoyableGraphically; this game is about what can be expected. Cartoonish 3D take on the anime art style from One Punch Man. The voice acting is fairly decent and the soundtrack is also quite good. Gameplay is also not groundbreaking; tag team battles in a 1v1 setup with special moves, dodging/blocking, and a wide area to fight in. Character customization is a bit lacking considering only a year ago Jump Force released with an at least mildly more in depth customization function. Outfits are for the most part uninspired; all decently passable but bland at best. The hub feels a bit cramped and pop-in can get a bit annoying as this seems to happen even on very beefy machines.The game runs smooth enough; minimal if any chugging. Highly recommend a gamepad; as is most preferable for any 3d fighter. If OPM is a favorite for you; 60$ may be worth it; the Deluxe Edition if you really want everything there is. However for anybody looking for a solid all around multiplayer fighter; seek out just about anything else. The story takes the main focus for this game; multiplayer being a big chunk of the appeal though.All in all; this is a fairly average game. It's nothing super fleshed out like Xenoverse or super unsatisfying like Jump Force, just an unimpressive; meh. However, for any fan of the series, this is a good enough game. Earning a mediocre C grade from me.EDITS :: (Scores Edited to reflect number of people who don't like a simplified 1-100 scale.)(TL;DR shortened to remove redundancy and simplify information)(Forgot to change decimal notation to %: Fixed in post)(Cleared up confusion around score for the Multiplayer)-- Addendum --This game is fun; but not for everyone. It's not designed for Keyboard users as its an arena fighter. Decent Roster size; locked behind the single player. i do recommend this game as it is enjoyable as a fan of arena fighters; and better if you like One Punch Man.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like waiting, this game is for you. This game is garbage and not worth full price.Enemies spend most of their time blocking, take very little damage, and force you to sit there and reconsider your life choices every time at the end of each combo where it takes twenty minutes before your character gets up. The battle system isn't quite deep or engaging enough to make the gameplay fun, especially between the copious loading screens.The character creator is fun, and I only continued playing because my character was perfect. Even if I'm beating the crap out of Boros, the battle still ends with my character failing.Ultimately, the game is somewhat cute, but absolutely overpriced for how low budget and unpolished it is.

_childDocuments_.review: One Punch Man A Hero Nobody Knows is a game based on the hit series One Punch Man, I love One Punch Man and I was looking forward to the game because of the trailers that we were giving.  I was looking forward to what the combat system had to offer as it showed potential and the fact that we all could play as our favorite characters felt amazing.  However, even as a huge One Punch Man fan, I can not recommend this game as it’s a mess of a game on many fronts and I have a lot to say about it.  So the story starts out with the character you make being hired by the Hero Association and it’s your job to save lives from all over the city and you start by being a Class C hero.  After that, you are sent on a mission to go help the city folk and you meet some of the pro heroes.  After that, the Hero Association calls you in to help some people that are being hunted down by Vaccine Man and your job is to protect the citizens of that area.  You fight Vaccine Man only to find out that you are not doing a lot of damage to him, then all of a sudden Saitama appears and takes out Vaccine Man with One Punch.  Then the character you make asks to be Saitama’s apprentice and he says no because you are not like Genos and you can’t pay his rent or have a toothbrush of your own.  Now the story is PAINFULLY SLOW and should have not been taken this way, it takes way too long for something to get done as the game is giving you side missions and other things to do when you just want to get on with the actual story.  What they should have done was to make us play as Saitama in the first mission, then we play as Genos in the next mission and make the timer go down for Saitama to come and so forth.  I know this story might have been a lot shorter as it only goes up to the Alien Conquerors Ark but they could have made up missions where we play as other heroes or something or give us a story where we play as the villains on their perspective. The character creation is a nice touch, however, I feel something empty when making my character.  Most of the cosmetics you want to use are locked and that is fine but they don’t really give us a lot of room to really do anything.  The whole character creation thing is cool but I just feel some sort of emptiness when making the character I wanted, it looks more like a Saitama doll than anything like a character.  Really the character I made feels like they are dead inside.  Then you have your bedroom where you can design it and put all sorts of things inside, it’s a nice thing to have I guess but like the character creation, it feels empty yet again and it’s just sad to see this.  You have to get most of the declarations which make sense and it gives you a reason to spend the money you get that the game gives you.  Now the gameplay is also underwhelming, the trailers mostly showed the fights and how the characters played.  This is fine but the devs did not really show us the whole hub world part, in the trailers that the game showed us, there was nothing of a hub world shown at all and it felt like it was put in as an afterthought.  To make matters worse the hub world feels dead, there are NPC’s and if you are online there are players but to me, it just feels dead and nothing is really happing.  Now for the fights themselves, well the characters feel floaty and the controls are clunky, to say the least.  There is a basic combo and you have heavy attacks, however, it feels too basic and none of the characters require any skill what so ever and you are not rewarded on how good you are.  To top it off, some characters are outclassed, you are going to want to use the higher ranking characters simply because they do more damage can take out the weaker ones in a few hits.  To get these characters you have to play through the slow story mode so your favorites are not even available at the start of the game which is sad because I bet everyone expected all the characters to be available.  Now the characters feel floaty because when you do a combo, they can get comboed into oblivion, as when you get back up sometimes you can just get hit again and you have to dodge as soon as you get back up.  The characters take a little too long to get back up and pressing buttons does not help matters either and you can’t roll dodge to get out of the way and that should be something you should be able to do.  The character that you make starts off weak but you can upgrade them to get stronger like doing more damage, more health, speed, and more special attack damage.  The main issue with this is that the work does not feel satisfying and the special moves that the character you make is a cool idea, however, I, for the most part, don’t feel anything special performing them.  As a matter of fact, none of the special moves that the game has feel great to pull off and that is something that I think a fighting game should do and that is to make us feel like we are doing something when performing a special move.  To get these special moves you have to wait for this charge meter to go up, certain special moves require a certain amount of charges, the main issue with this is that sometimes you take out your opponent before even doing a special move.  The game feels dead and when I say that, it means the game has no life in it.  The character creation is cool but it feels dead, the story feels dead, the hub world feels dead in a way, the gameplay just feels dead.  The game just simply feels like no life or thought was put into it and that is sad as I wanted this game to be good and what we have here is a train wreck of a game.  The intro to the game actually was really well done and it makes it look like that the game and the game’s intro are two different games altogether.    One Punch Man A Hero Nobody Knows is an insult to the One Punch Man series and it’s sad to see this, a great IP and we just got a shoehorned fighting game that is not fun to play.  To make matters worse, it’s 80 dollars CDN and I was dumb enough to buy the season pass, this game is not 80 dollars, it feels more like a 20 dollar game than anything.  Azur Lane Crosswave, which was released two weeks before, has more charm then what this game has given us and it’s a VN with some gameplay.  Do yourself a favor and stay far away from this game and save your money and if you want a good arena fighter wait for My Hero One’s Justice 2 to come out, as that game can appeal for all kinds of fans in my eyes and it’s coming out in two weeks as well almost.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This is not a good game. Do not buy it. No online mode anymore, EAC is still installed despite this.• Is this a bad game overall? — This answer is going to be more complicated than a yes or no.As a fan of the series, I enjoy the thought of making a character in the world I love, getting to interact with characters I have enjoyed greatly, and participating in the story as I grow stronger and slowly learn new fighting styles that I might enjoy. As a fan, it has a lot of that feel of Xenoverse 2 where you are kind of like most of the characters you love: You are a side character, taking the initiative to survive and be the main character of your own story...That is where my praise stops on this.Combat is basic, almost too basic, to where it feels almost unresponsive in some cases where you perfect dodge, but you feel as though the dodge wasn't something you caused and instead felt like you were given the dodge. Enemies blocking your onslaught of attacks cannot be easily transitioned into a grab as when you are done with your combo (or stop mid-way to attempt a grab) there is a long lag for that, allowing them to counter and tear through you. Random events happen in every battle, which can be fun at times, but many of them don't make sense. I had the mole appear before the Vaccine Man fight in the story and grab and pull a random guy into the ground that I fought while Garo ran in to help me during a thug fight. In a game where the combat helps push the story, you have to consider if this makes it a poor game. Loading times (even on an SSD) are an issue where you will run to a shop two streets over and may have to wait a minute or two to have a character pop into existence, or be returning to a fetch quest and have to wait a few seconds as you run back and forth in the spot the character should be only to have them pop into reality when they feel like it. Character creation is very basic, you have to earn and unlock many parts that will make you unique...But unlike something like Xenoverse 2, I will give it props that the costume is an aesthetic choice only, leaving you to go for your own sense of fashion.

I will probably give up before ever actually getting to play the game mode I came to play.To illustrate my point, I am playing this two years after release. _childDocuments_.review: ONE PUNCH MAN: A HERO NOBODY KNOWS manages to do something amazing - it makes One Punch Man boring Why you should avoid this game:- there is a mechanism where you have to raise 'hero contribution' to do main missions. Hero contribution is awarded for doing the same stupid missions over and over again - optimization is terrible - it is a loading screen simulator- seriously, 70s loading screen for 10s dialogue into another 70s loading screen into 20s fight into 70s loading screen into 15s dialogue into 70s loading screen into the hub is a common occurrence in every mission and side mission  - characters pop up after 5s if you move behind a corner. That also counts for hub enemies which is just lovely as they can pop up on you and force you to fight them- The same arenas over and over again. 90% of this game is grass arena - Battles are all the same and they are beyond boring - 100% scripted - if the objective is 'put the opponent to 50% hp' you get a losing animation even if you are still at 100% hp- forced grind of the same missions over and over again - no loadouts so you have to set everything manually every time if you change gear (and some missions require a specific class or gear so get used to that) - No voice acting for the majority of the game- a zero difficulty - once you get a correct loadout the enemy won't be able to hit you ever- invisible walls in arenas so you can corner yourself- Combat is basically 'do you combo, wait for opponent to get up, dodge behind them, do your combo and repeat until they die'After 12 hours I just unlocked the remaining 11 achievements with unlocker. Why?- 'S rank required 89 000 exp' - I was getting max 2k per mission - The game told me to get to  26,000 hero contribution from my 23,000. I did 7 side missions. It gave me a story mission where I fought 3 generic monsters, and then it told me that I needed to be at 31,000 hero contribution for the next story mission.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love One Punch Man and this comes with a heavy heart for me to not recommend this game. This game is just an absolute disaster with seemingly zero actual budget behind it. Not just that. The multiplayer servers are shutdown. They STILL have anti-cheat on this game. Even when you choose to play offline, it still runs in the background.You have to manually force the game to run on performance mode or whatever to stop the slowdown. There's a guide on it I found in the discussions and it was a random comment on a post someone made regarding the slowdown. This game has a myriad of issues that are beyond infuriating. The biggest offender is the absolutely absurd and abhorrent input reading the AI has. They have an answer for everything. They counter everything easily. They always infinitely combo you or hit you into combo starters or just heavy hits you until you die and they do this while you are getting up and the frame your iframes end. The hitboxes and iframes are insane. You'll eventually be able to pull off taking advantage of the AI, mechanics and rely on abusing them like your life depends on it because  of how impossible this game can be and you'll find yourself S ranking and 3 starring every level 4+ difficulty mission within seconds. Unless you get 3 star requirements that involve guard breaking, grabbing, doing some kind of weird grab counter cancel or whatever that might as well be impossible to do. (I've spent over 20 minutes on some of the harder missions because of how abysmal the AI programming is and how impossible it can be to get just 1 of the star requirements because of how the AI works.)There's barely any kind of unique fashion. You're just mixmatching things from every other hero or villain or monster in the game and even then, the character creation for it is BAD for the player model. Female faces don't actually look like females either. They all look male and the way the player model customization is, the body forming will make them look ugly and deformed in some way. Customizing your room is annoying because it's the most barebones customization and the way collision works, you can never get around your house unless you just put everything against a wall so you can walk around and even then, you can't actually interact with anything beyond a description of what an item in it is. It's more of an inconvenience on yourself to make your room look nice. There's no satisfaction. You can't sprint around town. You have to do a light jog everywhere and it can take forever to get anywhere you need to.You can't use your ultimate attack either without charging or getting destroyed by the AI long enough to get 6 charges on your gauge so you can transform and then activate it, only for the AI to guard your ultimate casually and make it fail. The ai will immediately follow up with some kind of combo that will either outright kill you or make you want to just surrender and retry immediately.A lot of this game just feels like it exists to waste your time and effort. My list of issues the game has is just scratching the surface it feels like.

_childDocuments_.review: I always loved One Punch Man, it's kind of a guilty pleasure anime for me. I've watched the anime probably a dozen or so times. It's still funny, the fight scenes are cool, the characters are interesting. The premise despite being a parody is actually appealing.And this game is legitimately so awful it can only be described as a soulless cash grab. From the outside looking in, it looks like basically what you would want out of a OPM game: make your own hero, grow through the ranks, interact with favorite characters, and develop your own fighting style by imitating the heroes.Well, you make your own hero. The customization is hilariously lacking. Grow through the ranks, sure. It follows beat for beat the plot of Season 1 with a handful of side missions so your character can be stuffed in, even in moments where this doesn't make any sense (see: when you are in the ship fighting Boros). Your "reward" for story battles is often just... screenshots pulled directly from the anime highlighting the story beats you just went through.I feel like calling this game "budget" implies there was effort expended within limitations, when really it feels like the exact opposite. Nearly every element of this game feels like the absolute bare minimum to put out a OPM product in order to cash in on the popularity of the anime. I don't play anime/arena fighters so I can't comment on what is or isn't standard to gameplay, but the gameplay of this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ . Enemy AI blatantly reads your inputs and pulls off impossible blocks and perfect dodges, and will wombo combo the absolute ♥♥♥♥ out of you. Fights essentially rotate between you dumpstering whatever you're fighting or being absolutely dumpstered. The RPG elements make fights horridly balanced, not even getting into how some fighting styles are just absolute monsters compared to others. And even if you aren't bothered by the gameplay, the game may as well be described as "One Punch Man: The Game That Never Loads". Nearly every single move into a fight scene, or a cutscene, or another area, you will be greeted with a 30+ second load screen. There are story moments where you will fight for 10 seconds, 30+ second load screen, 20 second cutscene of dialogue, 30 second load screen, and then another 10 second fight scene. It is legitimately boggling how much of this game is literally just loading screens. I would estimate half or  of my playtime is actually just staring at loading screens.I picked this up in a bundle, so I paid less than 10$ for it, and I  feel ripped off. I cannot imagine paying 60$ (or more with the DLC!) for this. Even if you are a One Punch Man fan, please do not be suckered into buying this game. It is not worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, do you like popular anime series One Punch Man? Do you like loading screens? THEN HAVE I GO A GAME FOR YOU!Seriously though, this game is a hot mess. There's a lot of baffling design decisions you could spend a lot of time discussing and not even get close to the actual fighting mechanics of this fighting game. But for me the breakpoint was the loading times. And to be clear I'm not exactly running a potato here. But the amount of time you spend in this game just waiting to do things. Start the game, wait for it load, change areas, wait for that to load, run over to the pc who's giving out missions and the wait for them to load in as well. Then wait for the mission select screen and then, finally, you can wait for the actual fight to load. And you better hope you're not doing a story mission because get what happens if there's any cutscenes or additional stages? The problem with all this hanging around is that the actual fights can be over in less time than it takes to get them. And honestly they're... not that great. I'm no connoisseur of fighting games, but it mostly seems to come down to whoever stun locks or juggle combos the other person first. Can be OK as a bit of button mashing fun, except it's simply not worth the wait.The character creator deserves a mention as it's actually pretty good. Not quite City Of Heroes (RIP) levels of great, but pretty much everything you fight in game is made with it so it does provide some variety. But honestly it could do with more options for making actual super heroes. Even most of the unlockable options are just normal clothes.There's several pieces of DLC and I did get the season pass, but honestly they don't seem to add much to the game. There's only one that I even got as far as accessing the missions for and they're just like what you get in the main game: A couple of short fights against random monsters and maybe after you'll get some extra costume pieces or whatever assuming you have the patience to wait for them to LOAD.The weird tacked on online features are honestly not even worth talking about since they don't really seem to impact the game in any meaningful way. Outside of the strange hub structure of the town. It's like they wanted this to be an MMO or something, but had no clue how that would even work with a fighting game. The answer there being it doesn't, concentrate on something the game actually needs. Like optimisation.

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna keep this short because I'm not gonna write a long review for a game that definitely doesn't deserve it. If you're a fan of One Punch Man, you'll most likely enjoy playing with friends or just playing as your favorite characters. The gameplay is eh to fun for the most part. This feels like they quite literally copied the main engine assets from Jump Force and slapped OPM on top of it (but that isn't all that bad because Jump Force is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and couldn't keep my attention. This game does keep my attention though). The story mode is very slow and boring. To progress through the story you have to do a ♥♥♥♥ ton of side missions to gain reputation to unlock the next main story mission (which they don't last long they're 1-2 battles with short cutscenes). Then its back to playing 10-20 generic missions where you fight CaCs with rubber horse costume heads on calling themselves monsters.I have yet to beat the game but 8 hours in of me just messing around a bit while doing the missions and I'm about 75% done with the game. This game is short, and I'll be it not that good. The overall quality of the game is similar to Jump Force, both games look like a fan made game created by 3 individuals. Spike needs to stop making these anime games because it just gives anime games a bad name. Oh, and there's way less customization than Jump Force too.In short, I'll recommend the game just because it does a better job than Jump Force at keeping me entertained (and it's One Punch Man). Does this game deserve $60? No, its a quick money grab just like Jump Force. Don't buy this if you're expecting an awesome game, or want more than 15 hours out of it. Once I beat the story mode I'll most likely only open this game again to play with Garou when he is released in the summer time then it will be uninstalled afterwards.- 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Hold on tight guys. This is going to be a long one.This game is a disaster and one of the worst things I ever played, based on of the best animes I've ever seen. As the angry video game nerd once said, a game is becoming worse and worse once all of the cr*p starts piling up. Let's start with the Singleplayer mode, or the campaign. You have to make a custom fighter, just like in Sonice Forces, which is rather a welcomed idea. Only issue is that you are very limited, because all the nice stuff is locked. Okay, maybe it's not that bad, but it definetely feels unpolished and tested once you experiment with the accessoires. You can wear a clown nose on the top of your head, or as some googles. Same goes with the party hat, which you can wear as a nose.Now, that was probably the least concerning issue about this game. Let's continue. After creating your own OC, you are playing through the main events of the first One Punch Man season, and as some may recall, it's only 12 episodes long, so it must be stretched out in the game (And it is). Before you actually drop into the story though, you get to see the overworld, which is relatively small, but not too shady. The best part of the game is here: the chill overworld music.So, you'll get through a tutorial, then get to see one of the original characters in the game, Lecture Man. At this point you'll notice how poorly every character is designed, some wearing fairly odd sets of clothes. And this applies to everyone, especially the enemies. You'll often find yourself fighting against a man or woman with a cardboard on top of their head, sometimes it's just people with horseheads that are also samurais or some schoolgirls or maybe you'll fight against some of the freakiest npcs I've ever seen. None of them fit in the One Punch Man universe, and fighting them wasn't fun at all. You see, not only do the characters look bad in this game, but the fighting, the main core function of this game, is horrible. You get 2 different normal moves that you can also charge, three special moves, air moves, and a berserker mode. But you cannot use them properly, because once you use a combo, you'll knock your enemy down. Then, you have to wait until the enemy gets up. In what game is it fun to way 3 whole seconds every time you knock your enemy to the ground. And let me tell you, no combo is strong enough to defeat your enemy, so you'll find yourself knocking your enemy multiple times down.So now you know how the combat is. But how often do you actually fight in this fighting game?The answer is: a lot. A lot, as if you are grinding, because that's probably what comes the closest to it. Each time you want to continue the story mode, you'll have to earn points for your hero rank. These points are earned by completing tons of missions, in which you'll be fighting against these random-looking enemies. One Punch Man related heroes will occasionally show up and help you, but you'll never be able to select them. Luckily enough though, you can switch your fighting style, like cyborg mode, bat mode, esper mode and so on. I guess this is a poor excuse why you never play the main heroes from the beginning.Saitama sucks here. You'll be grinding 20 minutes each time just to play him for less than half a minute. All of his attacks are one shots, no matter what you pick. So it's always just grinding, until you fight someone from the anime, then Saitama shows up and now you can repeat all of it. It's just the same, so you'll end up grinding for the most cheapest cutscenes instead. Your character has no mouth animations and no voice, and it always looks weird when they interact with others.In the overworld, you can also do sidequests that will not give you more or enough points to rank up. They will give you more friend points with the hero you interacted, which is how you unlock them in most cases. You unlock them for the MULTIPLAYER mode only though. All other sidequest involving random looking npcs are build on the same pattern: You get from point a to b, and maybe fight a monster. By the way, you can always encounter an enemy on these missions, because they spawn everywhere in the city. It's always a big waste of time.None of this is fun. I played this game for almost 8 hours just so I can unlock enough characters for the multiplayer mode. But it turns out, nobody plays this game anymore. Either that or the match making is as good as the overwatch damage role matchmaking, but at least 3 times worse. So yeah, nobody showed up. I couldn't test any of the characters because playing against Cpus was hell in the story mode, so who wants to play against them in the multiplayer mode?Now, to some of the smaller issues which pilled up to be a big issue of a game. First things first: I couldn't run this game properly at all in the beginning, because only this game has decided to not run at top performance. I had to specifically look that up, in that case you had to configure it in the pc settings that this game has to run at top performance. At this point I uninstalled and reinstalled the game, hoping it would work and I would get some nice action out of it.Then I also noticed how clunky all of the animations are. You run way too fast, but you can't walk at all. All of the npcs look horrible. The town just looks horrible. The enemies look like they were made by some 12 year olds on blender. The character animations look like the game has never been tested at all. And the most annoying out of all of this were the loading screens, which are comparable to Sonic '06. Everytime you enter something, every time you fight someone, every time you see a cutscene, you'll have to go through a loading screen that is about 30 to 60 seconds long. How can a poor looking game like this load so long?! And the worst part of it is that each time you'll finish one of these grind fights, you'll be redirected back to the quarters to select a new mission. So: you'll select a fight, one loading screen. You finished the fight, another loading screen. You'll select a second fight, another loading screen. Let me remind you: You have to do about 4 to 8, sometimes even more than 10 grinding missions just to continue the main story. You'll be seeing these loading screens way too much. Did you also know that these screens are also very cheap looking? Like, what is it even suppoused to resemble? There are a few punch stickers, a kiss sticker, some hands, but nothing really fits to the One Punch Man theme. There isn't even a soundtrack playing when loading, so it's just a blank screen with some random stickers.Honestly, if you skipped all of this text I just wrote, let me wrap it all up. Cheap looking textures, extremely long loading screens (and lot of them), cheap animations, cr*ppy fight mechanics, cheap looking npcs and enemies, almost no way to play your beloved heroes or foes from the anime, nobody is playing multiplayer, the story isn't worth the grinding, there is an absolutely unnecessary grinding mechanic in this game, this game is way too pricey for a barely finished product and in the end, you grinded for absolutely nothing. Think about it: You finish the story. And then what? You have all the characters you can use for Cpu fighting. So you'll be doing the same thing just like when you were grinding, but this time with the actual heroes, as it should have been in the story mode. Playing this game was a pain in the butt, even spending 7 hours on it is more than regrettable. The disappointment is immeasurable. Also you can wear Saitamas suit which is worth almost all of your ingame currency

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really write reviews but after playing this game for longer than I ever expected I would and buying this game at release (sacrificing my baby for it, Desert Eagle | Pilot Minimal Wear) I want to vent my frustrations out and hopefully maybe change the opinion of at least ONE person. This review is very long and goes into detail for each component I felt like talking about, I made headers for your convenienceONE PUNCH MAN: A HERO NOBODY KNOWS, is definitely is one of the most overhyped and worst games of 2020. It is a great concept, an anime like OPM with such diverse characters can create a great roster and it can be very easy to have new/custom characters, conceptually it sounds very unique to have a overpowered gimmick character in a fighting game. On release, we got a very barebone fighting game, with a One Punch Man sticker slapped on it. This game disappointed not only fans of the show, but it disappointed as a fighting game also.In OPMAHNK, you are required to make a character when beginning the game, this will be the hero for the story mode. The character customisation is a design abomination, the easiest way to describe this is: think legos, but instead of using bricks, you are using pieces of the OPM characters in the show, so using Saitama's face with Puri Puri Prisoner's hair, etc. It also provides the option of using miscellaneous accessories placed anywhere, e.g a cardboard box on the waist of your character. This leaves customisation being mentally unfulfilling and  exploitable, as you are given very limited resources to create anything cool or unique to other players. This also translates into the game, many of the NPC heroes just wear a recoloured version of Saitama's costume and since there are no different body types, NPC Monsters are just recoloured humans with fish masks on or metal knight’s head. For your character's combat, game gives you a handful of fighting styles with different moves to equip on your character which is nice, but in my playthrough I never really used the other styles besides the default because it’s the best.The roster for this game is unfinished and confusing. It boggles the mind to try and find a reason why BANDAI cut some people from the game, and why they allowed others to be playable characters. Let's examine the most critical flop first,  Fan favourites do not exist, Zombieman? Nope. Flashy Flash? Na. Drive Knight? Drive Who? and Watchdog Man is a DLC character! It is just so disrespectful to the characters that they weren’t added in, especially as how others made it in. For example, why can we play as Tanktop Tiger and Tanktop Black Hole when we already have his frickin' master in the game!?! You're telling me they didn't add in a large portion of the S Ranks and instead we got...  They also unbalanced the roster heavily, since Mumen Rider is meant to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the show, playing with him just puts yourself at a disadvantage. Saitama of course, is the most cheesy and boring character to use, the only way they could balance it out is by using a timer, but that just means play defensively until he arrives. You can't even see most of his moveset unless you are using the weaker "dream" version. Now, I would dare to say I wouldn't have been as upset with this game as I am if the gameplay was decent,  As I said before, this game is insanely easy to cheese, this game has essentially no difficulty gameplay wise, if you figure out the timings and which special moves are good and bad. NPCs are very brainless (even on the hardest missions) and other players have no control over their character if you can  Stun Prison them. The only difficulty comes from artificial stats and XP you have to collect in order to level up your health, damage, etc. This game has RPG elements but just does so to create a difficulty barrier and unnaturally lengthen the game. In order to stir this bubbling pot of plain white rice and try to add  element of flavour into it. This game has random events, powerups will come down from RC drones! The goliath from the first episode will stomp down on you! That's right! There is RNG in this fighting game, you think skill always determines the winner? No! Now someone can just get lucky!Don't let anyone fool you about the game having open world elements by the way! You are TRAPPED in a miniscule town with lifeless npcs. There is nothing added to the game by making an open world lobby, it’s just more work because you have to walk to the shops to buy stuff. Speaking of which, eventually you will have too much money to know what to do with, this game has almost nothing to buy, except for different coloured variations of the same furniture, which you can put in your apartment, which as I know of does nothing because no other players can visit your apartment.The best way I can describe how this game plays is this: Imagine the fighting mechanics used in the Naruto Ultimate Ninja Storm Series or Jump Force, now imagine that someone cringe tried to port the game over to roblox. Imagine they had to cut a lot out to make it work, like substitutions (which births prevalent stunlocking), removed tag team moves and power (ruins roster comp) and a lot more!The worst part about this game is the story. The story is just essentially a rehash of the first season, however with  in it! Your character tends to just be there, lingering around Saitama and you replace Genos for a lot of the scenes, such as when Saitama fights Genos for training, it is now you fighting Saitama. Fights in the story are programmed so the odds are zero that you will lose, this is to show how [] weak and pathetic [/i] you are and how the chad Saitama can just kill everything in a single hit. It feels asinine to play these missions; you don't have a slither of a chance of winning just to instantly win after you lose.This game is also , OPMAHNK is a game with reason to exist canon-wise. This game adds absolutely nothing to the game whatsoever! No new concepts, no new areas, no new plots. You can get the same experience of the story just by watching the show! It’s meant to be based on the events of the first season, so somebody please tell me why Fubuki is here, besides the game pandering to the opposite sex.The side missions have no depth to them, it’s just “stop the monsters attacking the city!” and that’s all it describes, no b-plots, nothing… with a setting like OPM with all the monsters, espers, kung fu warriors, cyborgs, I’m sure something really cool could have been introduced as a game-only plot.When you do get to S-Rank, there is no ending to your character’s story, Saitama doesn’t come out and suck your ♥♥♥♥, you just unlock more of the same missions to do.Or lack thereof. This game doesn’t care, you expected that much? This game has dialogueless npcs, undescriptive side missions, no customisation. I just wanted to talk about some stuff that didn’t really fit in the headings. The game’s voice acting is okay at best and diabolically cringe at worst, a few of the monster voices do this really virgin line to introduce themselves “don- do- don’t- AHHHH IM SORRY!” and I use a killer move called the one inch punch and my character always says “This is it!” before punching no matter which voice I use. If your character has six bars of power they can go into a super sayian mode and unleash a ultimate killer move, however, ⅔’s of the roster are missing a killer move and ¾’s of the roster are missing special costumes for when they do activate that mode (silver fang rips off his shirt, Saitama goes serious faced, etc)0/10 :)

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this is not a $60 game. Lucky for me, I got it on a sale for $8 and that is way closer to the true value of the game.Second, if you're a fan of the anime then I think you'd overall enjoy the gameplay and learning how to string together combos with your favorite characters. It's pretty funny playing as Saitama but the gimmick does get old. There's really nothing else I can say that is positive about the game. The gameplay is here is pretty standard for an anime-based 3D fighter (think Naruto: Ultimate Ninja, Jump Force, DBZ: Kakarot). Here you have a pretty limited open-world where you can find side-quests, item shops and character customizations. The fighting gameplay is found in the story and side missions and it's also similar to games of the genre. Nothing really unique or special going on here.The story is pretty much 1 to 1 the first season of the anime. The only real difference is the inclusion of your created hero. It's not necessarily a bad thing but considering that the cut-scenes are just the 3D avatars going through the dialogue, it gets really boring really fast. I think the game would've benefited from taking a 2D visual approach for both the cut-scenes and the gameplay to better match the style of the series (which is the show's biggest appeal in my opinion). It would also feel like less of a repeat if your character actually impacted the story at all. There are some instances where you can choose between 2 different dialogue options in a story cut-scene, but they don't influence the narrative in any way.My biggest criticism of the game is the inexhaustible well of loading screens. I expected loading screens between fights and story animations. What I did not expect was to have loading screens between cut-scenes and other loading screens. I have this game installed on an expensive 2TB SSD and each loading screen still feels like a minimum of 20 seconds. I am known to be impatient but this is just ridiculous.I kind of enjoy the game but I really only play it for the progression and I want to see if I can reach Class-S and obtain Sataima-level power.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played up to level 48, I am having trouble wanting to play this game anymore.Of all the fighting games I've played, this is the first one I've ever played that requires the blocking animation to fully complete before the game will actually block attacks. Making blocking impossible to achieve while in combat. You need to block pre-emptively, not in response to an incoming attack. Or it just will not work.You may think that perfect guards are the loop hole, or perhaps to stagger an opponent. I hate to say it, but the computer can block in combat, and you can only perfect block once in a while because it drains your stamina. Staggering kind of works, there was one enemy that couldn't be staggered when I played and that was frustrating. It all really boils down to not being to block. You can't break combos because of this, you can't counter attack because of this. And it circles back to perfect guard, it works, sometimes. But it can only be used when you have full stamina. All in all, this game is worth less than $20, I regret having paid full price.This game is repetitive because you can't actually fight, you need to find cheese and exploit the hell out of it to make progress.The game does strive for fan-service, which is kinda fun. But the remainder of this game for all of the potential is just broken by the block function not working properly.If it ever gets fixed this would immediately be worth full price. Until then, save your money, watch someone stream it if you want to see it.

_childDocuments_.review: My expectations for this were incredibly low... but since I like One Punch Man a lot I grabbed this on mega-sale (84% off).Again, I was expecting so very little - and was still blown away by how bad the "first hour" experience is here.  Everything feels like a placeholder.  The OPM universe (which is incredibly rich and creative) feels absolutely bland here.  I swear I spent more time in loading screens than doing anything like "playing".  That and being flooded with a ton of nonsense about the career mode and progression.  People like "Open World" games when there's interesting stuff to do in those worlds.  If your open world is just a way to pick your next "quest" (fight), then just have it be a menu.  Sorry, you can also get a couple dialog phrases out of "Determined Hero" or "Experienced Hero" standing around the Hero's Association... but so far that whole part of the game is just absolutely depressingly empty and lifeless and pointless.  It just adds 3 more loading screens between every tiny bit of entertainment.  I'd absolutely be OK with an Injustice/New Mortal Kombat experience here where the single player campaign was just fights separated by cut scenes (or even just dialog bubbles) featuring OPM characters.  That would be fine.  Instead it feels like whoever was involved in making this wanted to be making some other kind of game, or had an ambitious plan but no time/budget.  I feel like I've already spent more time on this review than they spent on game design, so I'm just going to stop.  The game is an inexplicable train wreck.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start I wish to make clear I wont be whining how repetitive this game is like a lot of the other reviews I saw before I bought it because I couldn't care less as I love the series it comes from so interacting with it gave me great joy up until a point. I will also make this numbered for ease of access anyway lets begin.1. This game is drastically overpriced for its design quality and considering that it should halve its price and yes I mean that.2. Loading times are trash when compared to the gameplay experienced its just unreasonable and no I don't run a potato and even though I use HDD I can load far more complex games much faster.3. Events mid battle are great and allow for thinking on your feet unless its a meteor shower in which case any skill is tossed out the window and you may as well kiss your S rank goodbye and hit rematch because it is basically a stun lock that pretty much destroys  1/2 to 2/3 of your health bar and the game uses it regularly over most other events past phase 1 quests and it pretty much hits 80-90% of the area with 2-3 second intervals and for context getting up from a stun/knockback takes 4 seconds.4. Difficulty was what killed this game for me, the game makes you feel great like your skills mean something then they introduce phase 3 quests. The problem with phase 3 quests is enemy hit boxes are drastically smaller however the player characters hitboxes get significantly larger to the point the enemy can swing from 2 metres away and still connect but to top it off they get unavoidable stun attacks that cant be dodged or blocked as well but wait I am not done because events that I mentioned in point 3 occur almost from match start and if you read point 3 you can understand the difficulty you face. 5. I tried online features very briefly but the moment I did I got a weird audio bug that persisted through everything so figuring the lobbies would be a ghost town anyway I closed the game entirely then reopened it in offline mode. There is other bugs however they were unrelated to online features.In summation its a fun game but the points above were what killed the experience for me but sadly thanks to the failure of this game theres likely not gonna be another OPM game.

_childDocuments_.review: One Punch Man: A Hero Nobody Knows is not a very good game, but it is a beautifully charming mess that perfectly embodies OPM. So chock full of “bad design” that somehow feels right in the context of the universe. To understand what I mean, One Punch Man is a superhero story that has a power scale that ranges from “Can kill God with one punch” to “I like to ride a bicycle!”. I’m not exaggerating… Those two fight beside one another. This game embraces that aspect and doesn't even try to "balance". You’ll know Saitama’s pain as you fail the “Use 2 special moves” objective because you killed your opponent in one. You’ll feel the C-class fear as you unleash your epic hundred hit combo to deal 2% of an enemy’s life bar. Oh, and when Saitama takes to the field… that’s a feeling.The balance is offset a bit by a mechanic they call “Arrivals”. Building on the traditional 3v3 fighting game format, many missions have the allies “Running to the scene”. When the timer runs out, they’ll join in the fight. (Items, Combos and other skillful play can speed up their arrivals)This minor mechanic leads to interesting challenges such as - Two C-class heroes need to hold out against a powerful monster until the A class backup arrives and you can actually fight back.- The enemy has backup on the way that you can avoid by playing aggressively and winning before they arrive. - Hold out against a ridiculously insane OP boss until Saitama arrives to save youBut, at the end of the day, interesting challenges don’t hide the fact that this IS a crappy fighting game.  You’ll get stun locked, can’t cancel animations, and normal attacks are so weak that you’ll be repeating the one special move you can equip at your current skill level. It feels more like an RPG with it's focus on grinding for stat points, new moves, and different fighting styles. (Even as an RPG it’s not that good)This grind continues into the story as you need to grind for “contribution” points to unlock missions that award “rank” points and eventually unlock the next chapter. Don’t get me wrong, I actually enjoy it and the pacing hasn’t been too bad so far… but it IS pure grind.Despite the negatives so far, my opinion of the game was highly positive and I would have recommended it. But some of the technical aspects absolutely magnify and sabotage every bit of goodwill that it built up.Loading takes FOREVER (30+ seconds for me) and happens all the time.  Walk to the HQ [Loading] Select a mission [Loading] Watch a cutscene [Loading] Accidentally one punch a dude [Loading] Watch a cutscene [Loading] Rewards [Loading]. It’s funny to win a fight in less than one second, but it’s not funny to have loaded 30 seconds into that fight and 30 seconds after  I can literally say “I’ve spent more time on loading screens than I did playing this game”This tech continues into the game itself. I’m constantly running towards a quest marker and having to wait 20 seconds for the character to load in so that I can talk. A single quest involves talking to multiple people, cutscenes, and battles… and that means ENDLESS waiting instead of a fun non-interrupted experience.I do genuinely like this game and can recommend it for OPM fans that want a unique experience. For a cheap price, it’s a one-of-a-kind game unlike anything I’ve played before. But as an actual a game? Look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I have this about 2.7 hours, two solid play sessions, but I just can't do it any more man. I wanted to like this, I really did, but it just blows. I just submitted a refund request which I assume will show up on this review soon.I'll go over some of the cons:-Ugly. This game looks awful. I know SC isn't known for 3D models that look good, but man... the only thing I think that looks okay is OPM's face since its like three lines or something. Everything else looks straight of a 2008 Free to Play MMO. -Clunky. Not only does it look bad, but it *feels* bad too. Walking around the town feels unnatural, and the jump button is bound to a different jump button than the fight jump button so I keep pulling up the STUPID menu that takes FOREVER to load. And the fights are even worse, I don't know if they intentionally designed the early fights to feel awful but they feel AWFUL. It's so slow, it takes forever to recover and you have nothing to do to speed that up, and it pretty much boils down to "Does the enemy stun lock you to death, or did you grind enough to have so much hp that it doesn't matter?"-Load times. Why on EARTH does EVERY SINGLE load screen take upwards of 5 minutes PER SCREEN no matter that. It's insane! I honest to god have spent more time in load screens than actual gameplay, its that bad. Is it the shoddy internet connection (On the game's end not mine)? Is it poorly optimized (probably this one)? I had this on my SSD, there is no excuse for how long it takes. -The English dub. _childDocuments_.review: “One Punch Man: A Hero Nobody Knows – A Flimsy Punchline”🔥 Entry Log 666: Doom Slayer’s ReviewBackground Noise: Heavy metal riff, chainsaw revving, demon growlsListen up, fellow heroes and pixelated punchers! The Doom Slayer here, fresh from ripping apart Hell’s finest and saving countless dimensions. But today, I’m not wielding my trusty Super Shotgun—I’m wielding my keyboard. It’s time to dissect One Punch Man: A Hero Nobody Knows, a game that swings and misses harder than a blindfolded cyclops.The Premise: A Punchline in Itself 🌐🔍One Punch Man shouldn’t work as a video game. Why? Because the main protagonist, Saitama, can defeat any enemy in one punch. Infinite power, zero stakes. Where’s the drama? Where’s the tension? And how can that possibly translate to engaging gameplay? The answer in the source material is brilliant: turn the whole story into a comedy that subverts action anime clichés. Unfortunately, A Hero Nobody Knows doesn’t quite capture that magic.A Hero Nobody Cares About 📻🕊️In this game, you control Saitama only sparingly. Instead, you play as a custom character trying to become a professional hero. Early customization options are disappointingly limited, but stores frequently update with new items as you progress. The available clothing and add-ons get stranger and stranger, allowing you to wear the costumes of your favorite heroes from the anime or create your own absurd hero outfit with things like horse masks. I appreciate how willing A Hero Nobody Knows is to let you make yourself look like an absolute fool. Completing missions nets you points that can be applied to things like health and power.Combat: A Flimsy Punchline 🎭🌟The combat feels nearly identical to Spike Chunsoft’s previous effort, Jump Force. Camera-over-the-shoulder combat with simple combos and easy-to-execute special moves. It’s like déjà vu, but less exciting. The repetitive, mission-based gameplay? Well, it’s repeated. And the story presentation? Lackluster. In screenshots, A Hero Nobody Knows looks remarkably close to the show, but in cutscenes, characters move with stilted, uncomfortable animation. It’s like watching a puppet show where the strings are tangled.Doom Slayer’s Verdict: A Missed Opportunity 👗🌌Now, here’s the real tragedy: A Hero Nobody Knows doesn’t quite capture the essence of One Punch Man. It’s like a hero throwing a punch and missing the mark. While the visuals pay homage to the anime, the gameplay lacks the comedic brilliance that defines Saitama’s world. So, if you’re a die-hard fan, you might find some enjoyment here. But for everyone else, it’s a flimsy punchline in a hero’s journey.Doom Slayer’s Verdict: ⭐ (One BFG blast out of five)Disclaimer: No demons were harmed during the writing of this review. But my inner critic? Yeah, it’s sharpening its pen. 🖋️🎮🤔
