_childDocuments_.review: Yet another game where one’s forced to use a controller. I attempted to play it with KB+M, but their control scheme is so busted. This game uses L to interact. That button is thousands of miles away from WASD, driving inconvenience. There’s also the fact that the game’s KB controls aren’t consistent, so I couldn’t change the interact button. I should have known not to bother, being that I absolutely hated the dev’s KB+M support on Jump Force.Even the controller has issues. The jump button changes between combat and free roam. I jumped using X in arenas and O in the city/hub. Sure, jumping is basically cosmetic in the hub, but one should still expect consistency from a “AAA” game.This game perpetuates the low standard for PC support most anime games set. One might rate the console editions higher, but there are different standards for PC games. I do not recommend this if you prefer KB+M.Edited: I should have mentioned that this game has a wonderful awakening system. You can set what your character looks like when awakened and when in normal mode manually, which allows you to add the spikey hair that Xenoverse 2 should have. Were they to release Xenvoerse 3, I sincerely hope they copy this feature. It would be grand. Imagine a blue golden form for Freiza's tribe, rather than being locked to the golden form that Freiza "chose." Players should also have a choice. This game gets bonus points for that!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best fighting games for single player if not the best. Plenty of content, character interactions, customization, a great selection of fighting styles and moves, and Puri-Puri Prisoner hits on you so you know.....10/10. The only issue I have actually had with the game is loading screens, I'm well above the recommended specs and FPS is not a issue but even with SSD it feels like I get PS4 level loading screens.    Long load times are not inherently bad and WE ALL enjoyed games with long load times for years, the real issue comes in with how many loading screens you are required to go through for just a single fight. You are looking at around three loading screens a fight unless it is a fight including story and other characters then you can end up with 5-7 loading screens plus another two or three after the mission is done with each being almost or right at a minute. So a  10 minute fight could end up being 15 minutes or more because of loading screens and this is the one big issue with the game to me because you have to climb your way up the hero association like how Saitama and other heroes have to do so you have to do a lot of missions to earn recognition and rank. To put this into perspective my first wall was requiring around 4000 recognition with each mission available at the time giving anywhere from 250-400 recognition meaning at least 10 missions to continue the story, adding up three minutes from three loading screens for each mission ends up being almost 30 minutes......half a hour lost in the process and for what?   If you can stand losing a bunch of time to loading screens then this is a great single player fighting game (I don't play it online at all so I can't really speak on that aspect of the game) with plenty of customization and content. Solid 7/10 being a 9/0 if they would fix the damn load times.

_childDocuments_.review: Very characteristic of the risk-averse JP game devs and their greedy backers to think that the same circlejerked thing would work a 1000th time. Why would you put another CaC fighting game on the market? Are you that afraid of creating an actually good game? Anything else could have worked better, an ARPG or JRPG, simulation, MMO, anything but a watered down CaC fighting game in order to represent the blinding speed and terraforming destructive force of superheroes. How can you sufficiently represent a superhero theme through a fighting game, are they dense? They take the fans of this series for a fool apparently? "Just shove the same watered down copy pasted fighting game that we've done for every other anime, and they'll take it."Not only that, but the Monster Fighting style doesn't even work properly, because it's Killer Moves don't scale with your Killer Move statistics, actually I don't think they scale with anything at all, making it the weakest and most useless fighting style. Have they not tested at all?Also Technique stat actually doesn't make a difference in move gauge regeneration rate in any way shape or form despite the ingame instructions. I've measured it using a chronometer for how many seconds it would take to boost one bar of energy, and I've also observed the amount of gauge generated by basic attacks too, and they were all the same for different values of Technique stat. It's as if the devs thought players would buy into their uncoded bullcrap game mechanics and nobody would notice.On another point, the game has no real reaction or acknowledgement towards your character's personal feats and achievements. There's no real character or NPC acknowledgement of your character becoming an S class hero, they wrote only one dialogue script for everything, and everyone acts like you are some bottom of the barrel trash hero whether you are S class or C class. It doesn't matter. Did you Perfected a story boss with no damage? The cutscene will show you panting on the ground, and the "more prominent hero" will come "saving you" or backing you up, then you fight the story boss a second time together. Low tier C class heroes calling out to you to be careful taking out some trash monsters while you are in S class. Hellish Blizzard calling you to join in Blizzard Bunch missions and treating you like an underling. There's no end to this list. This is crappy, and lazy. Japanese developers treat their fans like children, and this needs to get better.There is a Stadium map, but it's never actually used in the story, it's obvious from all the references made in the side quests that there was supposed to be a martial arts tournament story saga as well, but they've obviously scrapped it and cut everything pertaining to Garou saga lacklusterly short. He has a total of 2 missions himself.And they've completely closed down the servers, there's no way to play with others or use the other multiplayer functionalities (like a certain skill that makes your friends come help).---------------I've really wanted a good game for a One Punch Man custom create-your-own-character immersive experience that simulates the world, action and feeling of the story and the power of being a hero adequately. But what I've got was feeling like this is an embarrassment to be in my library. Like you know how some people are embarrassed of having hentai sex games in their library? At least those have an explanation, and some of them are good. All in all, those are still better than this, at least you get what you pay for, and you get what was promised most of the time. But having to keep this in your library is a net loss and a legit embarrassment from a game quality point of view, and a cheated customer point of view, with no apparent upsides. Bandai Namco doesn't care jack crap about quality control nowadays apparently.

If you're a fan of the series, get it on a big discount as I did, as it's certainly not worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I typically like arena fighters as something to do with friends who don't really play fighting games. One of my friends absolutely loves OPM so I thought I'd pick this up for us and play over Steam's Share-Play. Well, to get to the point of being able to play this with a friend you have to finish the first 2 chapters of the game, which are an extremely boring tutorial. This wouldn't be too bad but this game has some of the LONGEST loading times I've seen in a long time. I have an SSD and a rig that can manage most games at 120fps+ on high/ultra settings. No amount of hardware is going to make this game load in a reasonable amount of time, and load screens are everywhere.Loading aside this game just really isn't that fun. Arena fighters are ideally easy to get into and play and fun to watch. Well, this is certainly easy to play so check mark there I guess, but it is anything but fun to watch. The combat is slow, the supers are uneventful and take a long time to play out for little pay off and even something like being knocked onto the ground is just like 2-3 times longer than it should be.I picked this up on a massive discount and I'm glad I did. I'm not getting my money's worth since absolutely no aspect of this game is enjoyable. I wish I'd picked it up from Steam directly so I could get a full refund but only being out $10 isn't too bad. Save yourself the time and give this a pass. Even if you're a fan of the series there just isn't enough on offer here.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game. Had fun playing it.My PC is bad so I could barely play it when I had everything turned to the lowest, and even then it was like the game was in slow motion. _childDocuments_.review: To be honest, this game is very low quality, they clearly cut corners that they never went back to finish, but all on all the left enough in to have a perfectly functioning game that is uncontested in the one punch man gaming market, they really just needed to include more characters, storylines, and stuff. a prime example of this was i took like 15 hours to grind up to class S on one of the very first missions (on my second playthrough) and there was no alternative dialogue or anything, it was still me being whatever class they expected me to be at that point and still my guy looking beat up after battles I easily won.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love One Punch Man you'll love this game. While not as expansive as Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, there are a lot of fun customization options to fill the need to feel like you're in the One Punch Man universe. _childDocuments_.name: ONE PUNCH MAN: A HERO NOBODY KNOWS

_childDocuments_.review: The fighting in "OPM: A Hero Nobody Knows" is pretty good, and this universe is riddled with good characters, who's abilities look amazing in a fighting game. It's specially fun to play versus a friend, where you can pick the characters you want and just go at it. The story is the same has in the 1st season of the show, except you've the POV of a random hero trying to go up in association rankings. Saitama does one punch everything but I would say the mechanic is pretty balanced. there's no main menu, instead you have a small "open-world" that acts has a menu (tip: versus mode is located in the Association HQ, took me ages to find it). Characters to play in versus mode are locked behind the story/missions (except starter and DLC), meaning you have to complete the game to be able to play every single character in VS mode. And there are too many loading screens, an annoying amount of loading screens.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE PUNCH MAN: A HERO NOBODY KNOWS

_childDocuments_.review: It's a OPM game where you make an OC, pick a fighting style and some moves, train hard to get to the top, fight against powerful monsters with impossible odds, then have Saitama show up and end the fight with one punch. All in all a pretty faithful recreation of what it's like to be Genos. But seriously, the game is a pretty alright fighting game and a fun enough time to play through. Will you like it if you aren't a OPM fan? Eh, can't say. Will you like it if you are a OPM fan? Probably, I do at least.

_childDocuments_.review: The game-play is rather repetitive, and I found myself switching over to japanese for nostalgia purposes, but the overall play of the game is rather fun. You at least 5 different types of battle modes to choose from, with the standard being the all around jack. Standard is the format for those wising to play the Saitama power base, but the fun is switching between the different ones altogether. There are still glitches with the relations portion of the game, or social standing, between your character and the in-game npc's, like Mumen Rider who, no matter how many missions I do with him, the social standing keeps starting back at the bottom for each increase. The blocking system is a bit sketchy as your character can get knocked down to the ground and will take forever to get back up. During this the opponent can start to attack you, and you won't be able to block it. It feels one sided for the most part. You are either powerful enough to take on each opponent without difficulty or you get beaten down quite a bit. I still enjoy the game for the comedy, beat-em up fighting, and the leveling system, but if you don't put most of your points in the beginning towards skill and hp, you are looking at a struggle.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE PUNCH MAN: A HERO NOBODY KNOWS

_childDocuments_.review: Had some fun with the story mode. It turns into a grind toward the end. Some of the basic fighting mechanics are flawed. Especially when you are knocked down. You can't delay or get up faster. The timing is always the same. So the opponent can set up an unavoidable attack every time. This is fun to do vs the AI but online it is really cheesy. No neutral or real defensive options. They have made several games in this style. None of them are good. But they can be fun for a little while.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE PUNCH MAN: A HERO NOBODY KNOWS

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it's has the most flimsy and unreliable combat mechanics in any fighting game I've ever played. What saves this game is that it takes place in the One Punch Man universe, where you can customize and play with a character of your own.It's quite obvious that the game is a cashgrab by Bandai Namco, taking advantage of fans love of the franchise. I like this game as I'm a huge OPM fan, but I'd never recommend it to someone who's just looking for a quality game.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE PUNCH MAN: A HERO NOBODY KNOWS

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the game and unlocking all the characters through the story mode, I can say I actually do like this game. You have to realize that this isn't a game for fighting game fans. The gameplay is very barebones and I'm positive that my 12 year old brother who hardly even plays as many fighting games as I do can perform very well in this game. You should only play this if you like really casual games and are also a fan of One Punch Man. The latter of which seems to be really important. If I were you, buy this game when it's HEAVILY on sale, and try not to take it seriously when you do the actual fighting. Much like the storm games, one piece burning blood, dragon ball xenoverse, and jump force, the fighting is super easy and all you gotta do is just remember when to press RT + Y after pressing X. TL;DR - Buy it for fun times, but get it cheap, it ain't worth $60+

name: Lightmatter
detailed_description: A Letter from Virgil, CEO, Lightmatter Technologies Dear Visitor, If you are reading this, you are quite fortunate. You have been personally invited to the world debut of Lightmatter—the greatest breakthrough in renewable energy since the sun was born. I know. You must barely be able to contain your excitement. This invitation includes a one hour tour through my facility, a ten second glance at the launch of Lightmatter, as well as five seconds of eye contact—with me. If that is not enough, bring your wallet. An investment will give you the full tour and prolong our time together. If you behave, I will even let you shake my hand. During the tour, you will witness mind bending technological wonders. They might force you to think in ways that are difficult for you. But don’t worry, you will come out a smarter human being. The only thing I ask of you before you enter my facility, is to embrace the future, open your mind, and your backpack. Yes, cameras, journals, and other useless items will be confiscated by James, my head of security. Don’t try to shake his hand, he might break yours. - Virgil CEO, Lightmatter Technologies PS: During your visit, you might stumble into our cat, Lux. So if you experience skin rashes, headaches, or hair-loss keep in mind that you might be allergic to cats. About the Game An Homage to First Person Puzzlers Play Tunnel Vision Games’ love-letter to the genre. Use lateral thinking to solve mind-bending puzzles with lights, shadows, beams, platforms, and lightmatter. Starring David Bateson as Virgil “Now that I'm thinking about photon power cells, let me test an idea on you. Have you ever wanted to stay awake forever?” Fan favorite, David Bateson leads as Virgil, CEO of Lightmatter Technologies Virgil’s Vision For The Future “Imagine at the center of a city, a CORE - providing sustainable and renewable energy to millions. That is the future we are striving for. '' What will you sacrifice today for a brighter tomorrow? The “Aha” Moment “If you are contemplating suicide, by all means - jump that gap with the lamp.” Lightmatter is a game of the floor is lava with deadly shadows and consequences. Examine your surroundings closely. Think smarter, not harder!

_childDocuments_.review: A quick game, but the puzzles were decently challenging and the characters were fun to listen to. The game mechanics were given with a "show, don't tell" mentality, and the effort put in in their design really shows in the puzzle design. This game also has a wonderful aesthetic, a mix between low poly with simple textures and stunning post processing effects. Failure was common (at least for me) but the progress saving mechanics are almost *too* forgiving, which kept frustration to a minimum.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing!!! , you can see that the studio really loved making this game. Lightmatter is a puzzle game with lights, its is very influenced by portal ( which is always a good start in my book). The puzzle are clever the controls are fun and the dialog is funny and engaging. sadly this game is pretty short ( which is understandable for the amount of effort put into it)so i highly suggest you buy this game and try it out for yourself.tl:dr buy this game if you loved portal  9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: Lightmatter is a good, not great game.  It tries so hard to be Portal, but it isn't.  The free-to-try aspect is neat, and lets players know if it's their jam or not.  I went and bought it before trying it, because I love first person puzzle games.  The puzzles are decent, but not that difficult...  a walk in the park compared to games like The Talos Principle, and easier than Portal or QUBE.  The plot isn't anything amazing, either.  Graphics are nice, though.  And there are enough achievements and secrets to add a few hours to the 4-5 hours the main game will take...  although beware, many of the secrets require staring at things for a minute, or even 20+ minutes.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy Portal, or any puzzle games like Quern, The Witness or Talos Principle, then this game is for you.The puzzles and environment were very fun but not overly taxing, although a few good 'levels' had me scratched my head for a while. The game was about 5 hours for me, it would have been nicer if it lasted a bit longer but it was more than worth the £15 to buy the full version and complete it.Very impressive considering a small indie team made this, I believe it may be their first game too. It feels far more polished.I would recommend. It would be great to see a Lightmatter 2! There's scope for a bigger and better game and I would certainly pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet love letter to the true 3D puzzlers of yesteryear. Lots of throwbacks to portal and oddly similar to the Talos Principle. Great contained story with a bit of an unfulfilled feeling. Recommend playing, however, I see a lot of potential in the shadows kill mechanic that could easily span a longer game. Worth a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is fun and reminds me of the good ol days like Portal. I want to recommend this game but I cant given I cant go past level 23 as it just crashes over and over then puts me way back to a really far back point. I load the level manually and it just closes the entire game so I cant finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of reviews say the puzzles are easy, a few say "easy with a guide" which... yes? Isn't that true of all puzzles?My experience was the puzzles were "just right" - not super easy but didn't need a guide. I appreciated the short length, I'd rather a game end while the puzzles are still fun than keep going until it reaches the point where you have to look up how to solve a puzzle. (Though I wouldn't say no to longer with more novel mechanics - I just wouldn't have wanted it to go to harder puzzles with the same mechanics.)Crashed once for me during a level transition, and no progress was lost. I liked that the game was quite "jump failure tolerant" - since the focus was puzzles, if you fall off a ledge you lose like 3 seconds of progress, not starting the level again, which is the right thing to do unless you're primarily a jump precision game (and sometimes even then - making people repeat stuff they already succeeded at is the worst!) I did have to start one level again due to getting it into a state that couldn't be recovered from (a lamp on a moving platform angled to trigger the switch that changed the direction of the platform, so it never stopped moving or reached a position where you could remove the lamp.)Weird that the 'demo' is the game, and the rest of the game is DLC, instead of the more normal model of just having a demo and the game separate. Normal model for a phone game I suppose, but unusual and unnecessarily confusing to install on Steam. (I got the paid game and Steam was like "before you can install the game you have to install the game". The most puzzling puzzle!)
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: a very fun puzzle game with a relatively unique mechanic of restraining you to areas that are covered by light, paired with a relatively basic if not enjoyable story told by a charming narrator. my one problem with the game was that i disagreed with its final conclusion, declaring that the sacrifices made today are not worth the lives saved tomorrow. but other than that, i have few qualms with the game, and i thoroughly recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: Nice Puzzle Game with a clever idea.The Puzzles are challenging at the end but never really hard, maybe also because there are only ever 2 ways of interacting with the shadows, a Lamp and a Proton Stick (Okay 3 ways if you count jumping over moving shadows).Narration is well made and funny sometimes, the game is also looking good.Its abvious the Devs like Portal, because there are at least 5 references to Portal in the course of the 4h duration of the game ;PBy the way, in this 4 hours the game crashed twice, so once per 30 minutes and also the UI is broken on Ultrawide, otherwise I had no bugs.The Achievements are also a bit... special, they mostly consist of staring on to objects for a prolonged perios of time, not really interesting, but completely optional if you don't care about themOh yeah and there's also a free demo which is great
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: Office Decorator: Floor Lamp Edition.Bottom shelf Portal. I enjoyed it for what it is and I think anyone who just wants something like Portal and is willing to settle quite a bit will also have fun with this. The game would have been a lot better without the Portal tie-ins and constantly openly calling for comparisons between the two games. While quite a few of Portal's puzzles were also easy the big difference is that teleporting and flinging yourself and other objects is intrinsically fun, but in this game the primary mechanic is pointing a flood light in a direction and pressing w.Most of the puzzles are super easy but there are enough tricky ones to keep me engaged to the end. The game tried to keep the puzzle elements simple, but I think they went overboard. There needs to be more stuff to do or interact with.If you keep your expectations low then this game with entertain you by adequately meeting them.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: When there is light, shadows roam and fear reigns.  When I initially looked into this game, the visual feeling was pulling me to it like a moth.  Upon spending time with this game, I noticed that this game had many nuances that made this game go from puzzle to intriguing time travel.  Hours went by and the game was finished.  Unlock the original feeling after completing a puzzle game. I was drawn to completely beat this and get all the achievements. Now I speedrun this game.  The game is engaging with just enough story to keep you engaged, but giving you enough freedom to play without worry.Pro:- Visually interesting- Engaging story that keeps you wondering for the next lore entry.- Puzzles difficulty increase as you progress with building blocks from the previous. - Engaged dev team that works to improve the in game experienceCons- Early access woes with minimal bugs.- The difficult could ramp up quickly for some.Overall:Game is worth the investment and time.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

It's enjoyable and doesn't overstay its welcome. For $20, I recommend it.Hopefully, they make a sequel with some expanded/additional mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing for an hour and it's a solid game. I'm a fan of both Talos Principle and Portal, and while this game has less diverse interactions, it makes you think. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR a clever third person puzzler in the vein of Portal. The mechanics are original, the puzzles interesting and satisfying to complete, and the narrative is amusing and engaging. Definite recommend for puzzle fans. Only bugbear is the game doesn't feel smooth to play. Camera panning and general motion feels "30fps"ish even though it was running above 60fps. Also it crashed a few times. Not a big deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game that reminded me of portal, another super amazing game, even when it wasn't doing so itself. I loved the voice acting, the play-style, the puzzles were all at least a little challenging especially that one near the end, and just the idea of using light to create safe spaces as opposed to the shadows is a really intelligent way to create the game. I just loved everything about it and beat it in 2 days, I could've done it quicker it's not the longest game but definitely worth 20$ for the rest of the game. 10/10Would recommend if you enjoyed portal. Try the game before you buy, it the first hour or so is free until you hit a point to where you have to buy the game in the form of a dlc, which is also a super cool idea.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: Portal light version. Literally. The screenshots do not do the game justice. Try it out yourself. There are so many cleverly designed puzzles involving light placement and thinking a few steps ahead while doing so. it's really fun and it's accompanied by a really good story with a great antagonist akin to GLaDOS (but human). Anyone waiting for and wanting Portal 3 - play this, it really delivers.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: (Ignore my playtime, its a bit skew to be lenghtly, check how long to beat for more accurate info)Intentional shortish reviewA short puzzle game, manageable difficulty with very pretty graphic/art-style.- Gameplay is alright, nothing feels bad about moving around it but don't expect anything super crazy. The movement is tuned nicely tho to feel fluid and responsive and nimble.- As mention before the difficulty is fair, tends to lean on the easy side starting out but throws a few quirks at ya that might challenge you in ways you might not expect.- Game isn't too long, can finish this in 1 long session or a single day if you try. The game doesn't overstay its welcome nor feels too short either.- There are some nice QOL features where resets from dieing are fast and doesn't interrupt the dialogue. Keeps the pacing going nicely as you make mistakes. Notice latter in the game that they tuned the dieing speed to be faster when they expect you to fail allot.- Performance is okay, FPS caps are 30-60 FPS. My FPS was 90~ average but isn't comparable to average user due to my rig being higher tier than most users PCs. Imo with the pace of the game, playing it at around 60 would be absolutely fine and playable.- Game length from memory might be 4-5 hours depending on personal pacing and solution solving speed.- Dev commentary is pretty wholesome. If you wanna hear some somewhat awkwardly spoken people explaining their heartfelt product, might be worth a listen to ya. Although maybe listen to it online via video vs in-game to save you some time between commentary tracks.Bad stuff:- Not sure why but crashes happened sometimes in the mid-game, not sure what caused it and it went away during the late game.- Save points are not communicated effectively I feel, lost progress allot between closing the game breaks due to not realizing I did not solve the level entirely to save.Overall I would recommend this game to others. Got it for free via a short-term friend who deleted themselves from the internet to save their appearance. Hoping that doesn't effect the review but I don't think it did. With that being said though I cannot properly judge a price I would be chill with buying this game at.Just beware that if you are buying this game for difficulty or longevity you are better off looking somewhere else for something to play. This game is more for the parents to try out a game for once and or a younger kid who likes light puzzle stuff. Regardless of those parts tho, I had a good time and din't regret playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: Lightmatter - I played this game some time ago and it really left a lasting impression. The game has this unique premise where you navigate a mysterious facility filled with puzzles, all while avoiding deadly shadows. The way light plays a central role in both the gameplay and the story is incredibly clever.If I remember correctly, you’re trying to uncover the secrets of this facility and the company behind it, which adds a nice layer of intrigue. The puzzles are challenging but satisfying, and the atmosphere keeps you on your toes. I loved how the light mechanics forced you to think creatively.Even though it’s been some time, I still find myself thinking about those clever designs and the eerie vibe of the game. If you're into puzzle games that mix storytelling with a unique concept, I definitely recommend giving Lightmatter a try! They even give a nod to Apature in this game, like they were some rivals in the lore or something like this and I loved every moment of this.

_childDocuments_.review: I received a key for this game from the Devs.This isn't normally a type of game I'd play, but I gave it a full hour and was pretty impressed. The graphics are pretty amazing and everything feels fantastic. The puzzles really make you think and the first person perspective is awesome!I suggest you get this game, it's totally worth the $20 for the full game!

_childDocuments_.review: Quite good albeit short game. Reminds me Talos Principle and have lots of jokes towards Portal games. If you like interesting puzzles - go for it. It's only 4-5 hours, but story is fully narrated and fun, puzzles are interesting and sometimes even challenging and the visual design is fresh and stylish.A gain of salt: there is few quite hardcore platformer moments with very little margin for timing error, that could a problem for someone. Be warned.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting little game that felt more like a 2 Trick Pony Talos Principle, and from Portal the story and Narrator like figure talking to you.This game has 39 levels, but fewer puzzles than that, and most are solved fairly quick with some deduction, although the last was by far the one I spent the most time on.  Notice I didn't say it was hard.  I figured it out quite quickly, but spent over an hour trying to make it happen.A little buggy.  I had two crashes to desktop. Also had the jump button stop working once.I feel like $20 is bit steep when you compare it to Portal 2, which is miles better and has hours more playtime, not to mention coop.  I got Lightmatter cheap though, and I did enjoy it most of my playtime.  Glad I played it, but there is little to no reason to ever revisit/replay the game.

_childDocuments_.review: There's alot of things about this game thats good.So before I get into why im giving a negative review of it, let me list off why its good.For one, the art direction is nice. Very simplistic, but very pleasing to the eyes.Then the actual puzzling of the game is great. If the obvious portal references wern't enough to tell you, this game seems very inspired by portal. I found myself 'thinking with light' the entire time. The puzzles are very intuitive, and uses the mechanics in a great way. The difficulty curve is also nice and smooth, with every puzzle requiring some amount of thinking.The 'tutorial' is also nice, in that there is none. Because of the simplicity of the art, and the yellow outline of the things you can pick up, its obvious what you do. Pick things up, put them down, press buttons. Easy.Now for the bad.The biggest gripe I have with the game is the lack of content. Or, at least the lack of expansion of content. There's about 30 levels in the game, but i never really felt too challenged until the last 5 or so. The difficulty curve is there, but by the time it ramps up the game is already done. On top of this though, there's only 3 main mechanics to the game. The lamp, the light switches, and the catylist things. Its not until the last few levels that you use all of them, which was very hard. Took me half an hour to figure one level out. But to see all these come together into really nice puzzles that made me stare at the screen thinking just to have the game suddenly end leaves me disappointed. Especially during the last segment of the game that isnt anything puzzle related, but a massive parkour section.I know its hard to make games, and it takes a long time to go through and make puzzles like these. I totally understand it, and I wouldnt mind the lack of content... If it wernt for the price. For 20 USD, I was hoping for more. More levels, more mechanics, more toys to play with. I was honestly thinking that they would have their own version of the portal gun somewhere in the game, but thats when the game ended. There is a demo that claims to be an hour long, but from a couple of reviews ive seen, its a projected hour. Its more like the first couple of levels are free, then you have to pay. So you can try the game, but again, I cant recommend buying it with the lack of content as I stated previously. If the game was priced at 10 USD, or even 15 it feels a bit more appropriate. But unless they add more levels, a level designer, or incorperate some sort of workshop support for people to run with the idea the creators have made, I cant recommend this.A great game, but not for the price point. Beat it in almost 4 hours and left wanting more. Hopefully they add more to it soon, but since its stapled as a full release, its unlikely.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: Storywise, Lightmatter is a sibling of Portal. Here we have another Science Facility where an experiment has gone and continuously is still going wrong.The gameplay is simple in its elements, but makes you think enoug to keep things interesting.You have lamps and light beam connectors, switches that activate when lit, movin platforms, doors and elevators.The objective is, to create a light path to the exit, because one step into the dark aka shadow and *slurp* you're gone.Nicely enough, you respawn after the last safe action you've done. If that's not available, the game takes the next action prior to that. And so it goes room after room after room - which looks more interesting than it may seem from my description.The story is basically told by the man who invented the project lightmatter ingame - but to him, the player is nuisance and he's barely hiding it.There are some mentions to Portal so this is supposed to play in that same universe and at one time a radio is even playing an instrumental cover of "Still alive".The last bit is different, because here we have a partly time based 3D Jump & Run. But dont fear: it's fair most of the time. I had only one place where I couldn't get the jump right in the first dozen tries, the rest was a piece of cake.All that's left in the end is a moral question.And then there is the conclusion:It's short (plain playthrough: ~5 hours), but it's (about) pushing all the right buttons.

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game, the inspiration from Portal really shines through in a good way. The mechanics and puzzles are well established and very satisfying to master. Well worth your time - try it out and buy the full game if you like what you see!(Don't mind the playtime - played it on a different game client)

_childDocuments_.review: I played through the entire game, I did not play a second time for the hidden achievements. The game was fun but a bit short sighted and entirely a rip-off of Portal. 95% of the puzzles were simple enough to be solved within 5 minutes, with the only decently hard puzzle being the very last one (and in my opinion was less of an actual puzzle and more of an abuse of game mechanics). The plot is fairly underdeveloped with an almost non-existent cast of characters and the main antagonist being a 100% copy of Cave Johnson (which the game readily acknowledges). In fact there are so many Portal references in the game its hard to see any real originality. That all being said, I would recommend a playthrough of this game if you have it from a bundle or if it is on sale, otherwise this game severely lacks many of the good components of Portal which it is desperately trying to copy - just go play Portal for the 20th time instead, it's the better of the two.

_childDocuments_.review: Lightmatter is a fun first person puzzler with a very neat and interesting concept revolving around shadows and light and would definitely recommend trying it outi do wish there were some more puzzles, possibly some longer ones as well, since i do feel the concept doesn't get a chance to really take off, by the time some of the late puzzles begin to get going they are already over due to how short they are, especially since there looks to be a lot of potential that can be done that is just sitting therei still recommend giving this game a look at, especially since there is a free portion to try and then possibly looking into the full experience

_childDocuments_.review: I've got a full review up here , but in short: Lightmatter has a really good central mechanic. Manipulating light, especially in this crisp cell-shaded environment, is fun and creates some organic-seeming solutions. (If you think too long about any one puzzle, they're very clearly contrived.) It also manages to get quite a lot of depth out of the limited number of tools: there's essentially a spotlight and a beam-reflecting "photon connector" that helps to arc light around corners, and then some standard contraptions like elevators and conveyors and switches (nothing too complicated). The narrative is comedic enough to keep you entertained while solving puzzles, and the science-fiction seems plausible enough: a mad scientist, trying to solve the world's energy crises, accidentally gives birth to shadows that devour organic matter? But herein lie the complaints. The caustic dialogue mirrors that of Portal, but with less purpose, and the puzzles don't really deepen your understanding of the technology they're based upon. It's a good, fun game, but it's also a /light/ matter, and I'm hoping this development team gets enough interest from this first release to really expand on things in a sequel.If you like first-person puzzlers, you'll likely find about three hours of pure enjoyment here, but it's neither groundbreaking nor breathtaking in the way those games it emulates.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun, a great take on the First-Person Puzzle game. The Monochromatic-esque style is absolutely stunning and the sometimes witty commentary of Virgil (though perhaps not as lovable as GlaDOS from Portal is) is a lot of fun to listen to as you make your way through the puzzles. The puzzles themselves are fun and the mechanics are interesting. However some puzzles share a bit of similarities with others, and they can be a little finicky on occasion. All in all I have to say that the story and the storytelling are great, and probably the greatest part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: Lightmatter is essentially a Portal clone and it's not shy with referencing it. I think Black Mesa was also mentioned once or twice. So it's an homage to Portal and the shared Half-Life universe, but I would've preferred the game to have an identity of its own, like The Talos Principle for example. I enjoyed the puzzles, most of which are fairly straightforward and challenging enough. You can't mess up too much, since you can't jump with anything you pick up. The checkpoint system is actually surprisingly good, although I had to restart a couple of puzzles. I also enjoyed the art style, the music and the pacing, but the game's relatively short length of 4-5 hours works against it. The antagonist will chime in more often than perhaps you'd like and he's hopelessly trying to insult you, without the charm and wit of GLaDOS. David Bateson sounds a little too pleasant for this role, reminding me more of The Stanley Parable than Portal tbh.JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST! JOURNALIST!That's most of what I remember about the story. For a short while I was also referred to as an "assistant" and eventually a "spy." Why they deemed it necessary to really drive these home, I've no clue, but I will not be hypnotised to work in any of these professions if that's what they intended. Maybe I was a spy, I'm not sure, after a while I stopped listening to the antagonist and the voice recordings I found along the way.It's a solid experience to consider during a sale, personally I don't regret the 12.59 I spent on it (thanks for the coupon, devs), cos it's still a pretty fun puzzle game. The demo did its trick and I've still got achievements left to go. I'm not sure if this review will go under the free version (first hour) or the DLC (the actual full game), but hopefully you'll see this, potential purchaser.

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly short, unique puzzle game inspired by Portal, which nods to Aperture Labs in-game multiple times, although there are no portals here. It is what it appears to be in the video and every other review: An escape game self-described as being like the-floor-is-lava, but here a sort of quantum experiment has gone wrong and the very darkness has been attuned such that it dissolves organic material; aka, your body.The unique concept and superb execution make this well worth a sale price, and maybe full price if you're the sort to pay full price for PC games. The one detraction is that it is fairly short; I beat it in under 6 hours over 3 evenings with my teenage son, and if I weren't noodling around looking for hidden things which rarely existed, it could have been 4 hours. My son especially liked the parkour levels at the end, and we both enjoyed the puzzling. Most of the puzzles are solvable without resorting to guides, although a couple got tedious and I did pull up the guide. They make you retrace your steps a bit in some puzzles, and it's not always obvious that what you need to do is possible. The simplistic environment leaves me wanting for things to collect, but it's refreshing to not need to sift through a vast inventory. The game does a good job of unfolding the story with no audible feedback from your character so you're never really sure what you were doing in this place before wake up from its evacuation, although Virgil does his best to come up with your story as he watches you work. Once you're done with your first playthrough they give you easy access to every stage of the linear game, and all of the achievements are super easy to get to once you know where they are; this is officially the third game in which I've completed all achievements.Lightmatter runs well on my nVidia GeForce RTX 2070 SUPER, but while it's running at 120 FPS it has a certain laggy feel to the rendering that can be off-putting if flicker bothers you. There is a feeling of a lack of polish, but it never crashed. The plainness feels as intentional as it feels like it could've been smoothed a bit more before release. As a gameplay experience goes this is one you shouldn't want to miss, unless by chance you hated Portal.

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique and challenging puzzle experience. It's a short game, but the mechanics were so unique and challenging and it has so many mind-bending puzzles, for only $20 it really is worth your time and money. Some of the Portal references were a tad bit heavy-handed, IMO, but the voice acting is superb and the graphics and animation are top-notch.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: i think the thing that these Portal inspired first-person puzzlers fundamentally forget, is that executing the puzzles in Portal is actually fun. it's not that you figure out the solution and then you have to slowly, trudgingly carry around big lamps one place, turn around get the other lamp, set it on the other side and then go back and carry the first lamp further. because the mechanic of Portal is portals, you get to get where you're going instantly and shoot across large distances. and i'm not saying "hey! just copy portal!", but when you're designing puzzles they shouldn't just be fun to solve, they have to also be fun to execute also, because otherwise why are you in first-person instead of doing some sort of top-down puzzle grid like Filament? think about how your players actually engage with the puzzles, and if it's not fun to execute, go back to the drawing board. this game might have satisfying puzzles as you get deeper in, but an hour in it's so mindnumbingly boring to actually *play*, that it just isn't worth the investment.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: What a cute little game! Short and sweet. Definite Portal vibes, and I would imagine that it was a source of inspiration with this. I enjoyed how the core mechanic shifted throughout the game, and the platforming aspects were nice and simple. If anything, I would wish for more variety in core mechanics, but with the length of the game I think this is perfectly fine. The puzzle were good and not so complex that I would be driven almost to insanity, which is nice. The narrative is intriguing, if a bit simple, and as I like shorter games I loved this, it did not linger a second more than it needed to, and left me wanting more. I wish the team the best, and hope that they get funding for bigger and better projects in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! Proudly wears its Portal inspiration on its sleeve, and does so really well. I love the visual style, it works really well in tandem with the gameplay elements. The puzzles are fun and challenging, and the light (no pun intended) parkour - especially at the end - is good. Plot is fairly predictable, but the characters that drive it forwards are great. Conflicted on how I feel about Virgil, honestly, so great job on that. Short game overall, but well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: "The floor is lava, but with shadows."If you played portal, talos principle, you like first person puzzles in general and want more, this will not disappoint because the game is set very similarly.Lightmatter is a short 5-ish (maximum) hour puzzle game with a well fitted story (though if you do not care, you can play on silent or with any kind of music over it) and easter eggs everywhere.I enjoyed it a lot and very thoroughly.Controls are simple, learning curve is set very nicely, graphics fit the mechanic well, story is extremely linear, puzzles are short (it can be played in "pills")Also what I liked most is that you are free to experiment and run around and jump down without restraint because it will save EVERY step done and it will NOT stop dialogs.The only thing I do not recommend is the price (non sale-price I see at the moment is 16.79€), because of how short it is and non-replayability. The reason I have it is because of HumbleBundle, but if you like whatever I said and feel it's worth the price, I see no reason you should skip this 3-4 hour game.

_childDocuments_.review: Lightmatter is a first person puzzle runner developed by Tunnel Vision Games that borrows the Laboratory theme & narrator from games like Portal while adding & focusing on the mechanic of Light vs Shadow meets Floor is Lava. Think the Shadows in the Library episode of Doctor Who but gamified. Lightmatter can be purchased for $28.95aud or $14.47aud on sale.With that said, light is your friend providing you with 2 tools (limited to the level zone) that need to be used to open paths and complete each level.The torchlight is a single direction light source that can be placed onto a solid surface and shines a few steps away from its placement location.The Photon Connector allows you to connect photon light sources & channel the generated light into multiple rooms. The Photon Connector also creates a light source around its placement/carry location.The game does have a story, with it focussing on the lab, it's experiment with Lightmatter and a Cat. This story played out over the course of 38 levels eventually leading to the games conclusion. Similar to Portal, the 38 levels increase in difficulty as you progress.The Soundtrack for Lightmatter was unexpectedly good and suited the theme and environment. Voice over work by Actors was impressive and suited the characters to which they played. Without spoiling more, this game offers a FREE demo of the first couple of levels. I HIGHLY suggest downloading the demo & testing the waters to see if this is the game for you. You'll even have a chuckle when you reach the final demo room. IF you enjoy the game it's definitely worth the on sale price but I wouldn't say it’s worth nearly $30 if you aren't going to replay it at a later date, as a single play through for myself was around 5 hours.

Still, generally a very cool game for anyone who loved TALOS, PORTAL, and similar physics-based first person puzzlers.

_childDocuments_.review: As a cheapskate I always wait for games to go on sale before I buy them. I mean why pay full price when  you can wait a little bit and buy a game at a fraction of the price? That's the thought process of a thrifty person. They will wait for their game to be discounted before buying it. But I go one step further. I wont throw my money at just any discount. Oh no my friend. The moths that live in my wallet are huge and ferocious. I will not open their cage for anything other than a massive price reduction.Now that you understand that about me what I am about to tell you might shock you to your very core. It might be better to sit down before reading this...I will wait...Take a seat...Ready?I paid FULL PRICE for this game!! :OI know right! Told you it was shocking news. "But why would this self proclaimed tight wad do this?" you might ask. Or another question you might have, "Why is this unfunny moron over dramatising like this?" Both are very good questions. I will only answer the first question, not the second. It's not nice calling me a moron.Quite simply the reason why I paid full price is the game is a rare first person puzzler. I am tired of violent games. They are just clones of each other in varying packaging but at the core they are all the same. It's refreshing to have a unique game like this. I'm a huge fan of Portal and this game reminds me of it without being it. I loved all the portal references. The puzzles were not hard at all but they were enjoyable. It's not overly long. I have already completed it in 6 hours and even though I paid $30 I'm not bothered. I happily support any developer in making a unique non violent game that I can play or let the kids play.The voice acting was great. The puzzles were great.The story line ... not so great. ( I was hoping to find out who "I" was and why I was there.)The ending was weird. Maybe I didn't understand it due to my lack of intelligence but I have no idea why the guy helped me in the end. So yeah the game isn't perfect but still it I had a good time playing it.I also liked the way it was free to play for the first few levels. It really gives you a taste of the quality and game play before making a decision to buy it or not. I wish more games would adopt this concept.If you love puzzlers like portal then I know you will love this game too.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: Intriguing first-person puzzle. Many options to set the graphics quality and performance, so this will run on older hardware. So far I finished the free part in 2.4 hours, so it was already a great experience so far, much to do. So the rest of the full (paid) game must have a lot more to offer then. Really worth playing through this free version - even if you don't plan on buying the rest of the game, if you want a unique and non-violent first-person puzzler with a great storyline.Controls, graphics and audio are great.Note that the game freezes up in later parts and the game must be closed and reopened. But you won't loose any progress, the game saves at regular intervals your progress - the game consists of nicely done sections that you pass through seamlessly, but are designed in such a clever fashion that if you have to restart a section, there is very little to be redone overall and the game feels comfortable and relaxing (even if I had to restart the game two or three times in a row, seriously). And force closing this game is always very easy and smooth - either Windows will ask to close the unresponsive app (if you click and hit keys repeatedly/Alt+Tab), or you just hit Alt+F4. The game runs in windowed fullscreen.So far I can't say anything bad about this game, even despite the sporadic freezing.Definitely give this one a try if you like the promotional teasers. And the story is very good as well, don't be put off at first, give it time to unfold. It's a lesson about life and social relations which many of us know too well but unfortunately ignore more or less.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good first-person puzzle game.  Scratched that itch, etc.  Mechanics are well-done.  I'm seeing some complaints of, "Action?? In MY video games??"  There is some light platforming strung together at the end, wherein you jump over shadows or gaps in a bridge, which you will have been doing to some degree the rest of the game anyway.  It's easy, and, if you fall, it restarts you in a convenient location.As for the story, Bill Gates decides being rich and smart and saying "science" a lot gives him the right to make you drink poop water and eat bugs.  The only real creative part is that this is presented as villainous.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I remember how I discovered Lightmatter, I think I was exploring the Steamdb looking at the last uploaded pages of that day when I saw it and I was "Damn, this really looks interesting, has a lot of Portal vibes and the main mechanic sounds great" and then just started following it until the release day came and here we are now, reviewing a really cool puzzle game with tons of great moments, so let's get this review started, shall we? Story is really simple, you are.... you who get's stuck in Lightmatter Technologies, a massive installation where the CEO and founder, Virgil, alongside his scientists are experimenting with a new type of power source called Lightmatter, clean and self-sustainable but something goes wrong and shadows become dangerous as they absorbe all matter, so to escape our only chance is to use light sources to open our way, explore the installations and discover the secrets inside. Must say that this game is full of Easter Eggs and references to another game, please, do not miss them and explore as much as you can, I'm sure you will love them, also, listen to what Virgil says, you might remember someone similar who started his carries with shower curtains and lemons. Technical aspects of the game are easy to describe, a really cool visual style in which Light and Shadows are the main resource with a few touches of color here and there, all with a cell-shading effect that looks really good also, the scale of the installation is stunning, you will feel like a little person exploring an enormous place. Sound is subtle but works really well, voice acting is really well done and music creates a cool atmosphere. Performance is not bad at all although can't say it's the best of the best, game ran really smoothly tho so I wouldn't say my experience was bad, if anything just a few fps drops before each level but once charged, smooth as butter. And game's length will depend on how fast you solve the puzzles but it will probably take around 3-4 hours in the first run, less if you are doing a second waltkthrough or more if you are taking pictures of this great installation non-stop.  So, as my final thoughts, I enjoyed Lightmatter a lot, and I really really recommend it, it's a very well done game, puzzles are great, characters are good, story is simple but works and all this sense of humor is as nonsensical as Portal 2 which is FANTASTIC.Please check this game, I think you will enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. The light puzzles gradually get tougher as one progresses. then another light device is introduced to keep things interesting. Then during the final stages, agility dodging moving shadows add another quite exciting finale to this enjoyable puzzle game. The difficulty was just right for me so I could progress in a manner that neither created endless frustration nor boredom. Well done team. I recommend this game, definitely.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed the game. Solved all puzzles without having to look up a solution. Actually, that's a small lie: a couple of times I got stuck at the jump platforms ("carpets" with overhanging stripes) which seem to be buggy: unless you're jumping from a very specific position, you won't be able to climb up. I almost gave up on the whole game at the very beginning because of the buggy jump platform. Overcoming some of the jump platforms was the only thing I had to look up on youtube walk-throughs. _childDocuments_.review: This game makes an almost uncomfortable number of portal references, but I feel like it earns them.  This game is clearly a love letter to portal, giving me pretty much everything I would hope for in a portal-like game, and I can think of of few games in the genre that would fit into the aperture universe as well as Lightmatter does.Its puzzles are interesting and challenging without ever being unnecessarily complex or cryptic.  Its visuals, while striking and stylish, are really just an effective visual funnel keeping your attention focused where it belongs.  The story is simple and unsurprising, but solid performances and relevant themes keep it from feeling boring, and its solid pacing builds to a pulse pounding crescendo of shadow-skipping parkour through the facility you have finally mastered,At ~4 hours, it doesn't overstay its welcome, and leaves you wanting more.  Like Portal did.  If there is ever a Lightmatter 2 (or a wholly different puzzle game from this talented studio), I will be there, day one, without hesitation.

As a huge fan of those I do enjoy the occasional Aperture Science reference, although I’m not quite sure whether I personally find it to be slightly overdone in Lightmatter. Not so much in quantity but it could have been a bit more subtle sometimes. Apart from that I am happy about every decent puzzle game and for me, Lightmatter is among the better ones. _childDocuments_.review: Lightmatter unfortunately doesn't hold a candle to either Portal or Talos Principle and do be warned that the concept of dynamic light and shadow felt largely unexplored. However, I still enjoyed the game with the impressive voice acting and stylish high-contrast environments. The soundtrack, while subdued, helped the mood, too. The player has two types of objects to freely position, with the rest being button pushing and timed platforming (no physics objects). The unique piece is the standing directional lamp, since there is a blind spot before the cone of light and you get more lighting coverage the further away you can set the lamp from a path. The other is a routine "connect the dots" pole, which has a buffered trigger area due to the ray of light, which gets used to some effect. The pole does not reflect the ray from beyond it's position unless there is another node in sight, so rotating the pole isn't a factor for puzzles.For the $20 price, I take some issue with the shallowness of the mechanics and the level design to a degree, since the dynamic shadows felt underutilized in the puzzle segments. There's no object manipulation, so you can't alter a path by moving boxes. The standing lamps are never modified, so no flickering or protective grating that casts its own shadow. Refraction or reflection is surprisingly not explored in a game about light, which could have added some geometric complexity and introduced tangential "faked" simulations, like changing the refraction index by altering the density of a gas or solid transparent medium through applying "heat" generated by the lightmatter's energy. Wavelengths are ignored, so there's no color mixing and matching. The red rays in the photos is just the same signal as the white rays, but approaching a barrier (served to caution a player that they are about to break connection and likely instakill themselves). The dynamic and volumetric lighting looks really nice, but I had a lot of performance issues on an RX 6600 with ~30% gpu/cpu utilization and while the game never stops to load, there's noticeable chugging during certain transitions which aren't well hidden. That's not ideal with the friendly nod to speedrunning via an optional timer UI.My favorite part was probably the platforming course towards the end, which kind of reflects negatively on the puzzling as none of the tools or setups really get called back to during this sequence. It's still a charming experience with some nice visuals, so I'd recommend it on a sale, but if you want to test your reasoning and senses on novel puzzles, you'll serve yourself better playing its more thoroughly-designed contemporaries first (whether its directly referenced by this game or not).

_childDocuments_.review: Lightmatter is the first Portal-like I've played that's even in the same weight class as Portal.That said -- it certainly isn't as good.I know! It seems unfair to judge a game by comparing it to Portal, but it's hard not to --Lightmatter seems to have an almost fetishistic adoration for it. This game's GLaDOS euivalent stand-in even mentions Aperture Science twice by name! There are other little nods I won't spoil!In terms of writing and charm, Lightmatter falls short of matching its one true Orange-Boxed love. But in terms of puzzle quality? Call me heretical, but I might even say Lightmatter's puzzles are a little bit better.While Lightmatter is a little short (~3-5 hrs depending on your puzzle prowess), and makes the mistake of comparing itself to a perennial classic which it can never match, I nonetheless recommend giving it a go. The "Ah-Ha!" moments I was having by the end of the game were incredible.The demo doesn't get to the really juicy stuff - (imagine playing a Portal demo that ended before you got to shoot both Portal colors) - but you should play it, and if you're still even vaguely interested, you should lay down the dollars and play the rest.Outer Wilds aside, it's the best puzzle game I've played in a while by a large margin.

_childDocuments_.review: Lightmatter is a puzzle game which is played from a first person perspective. It takes place inside a research laboratory where a science experiment intended to use light energy as a power source has gone wrong, causing shadows to be deadly. The player must find a way to escape the lab while staying in the light, because standing on dark ground even for a moment will cause the shadows to consume you.Some shadows are small enough to jump over, but to progress through large rooms and long corridors that are completely dark, you’ll need to use lamps, which shine a light in one direction, and photon connectors, which shine beams of light to other connectors that are in direct line of sight. Most of the puzzles involve repositioning lamps and photon connectors to create a safe path, while occasionally pressing buttons to open doors or move platforms – which can also change the position of the shadows.The puzzles are mostly enjoyable to solve, although you do kind of have to ignore the fact that most of the early puzzles would be solved immediately if you were allowed to simply hold a lamp horizontally instead of vertically, therefore shining the light down at your feet.The story is okay. As you wander around, the head scientist, Virgil, talks to you over a radio about what has been happening recently inside the lab, and he makes several references to Valve’s Portal games and Aperture Science. The main thing I didn’t like about the story is that You can’t rebind keys, which is a function that I consider to be essential for any PC game, but at least there are two layouts to choose from. I crashed twice but thankfully didn’t lose any progress because of frequent autosaves. I finished in just under 4 hours, which feels short.If you like puzzle games, Lightmatter is worth playing, but I would recommend waiting for a sale.I received this game as a gift from my work colleagues.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun puzzle game where you navigate levels by avoiding shadows and darkness (the-floor-is-lava) style. Seriously though, this isn't a nod to Portal, it's full-fledged prostration. I don't know how they're allowed to pull so much from Portal but it's awesome.The asking price is a bit high considering the length - in my eyes it's worth it, I fully enjoyed every minute in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Lightmatter is an okay first-person puzzler, but it suffers from low production values and dubious writing.Environments are sparse, assets are insufficiently varied, and the underground complex feels empty. All signs e.g. are devoid of writing. The player character inexplicably doesn't cast shadows; otherwise the puzzle mechanic wouldn't have worked.The writing is okay but unexceptional. E.g. there are some references to Portal, and they're incredibly on-the-nose (like namedropping Cave Johnson). The the plot doesn't make much sense. This is ostensibly a story about the futility of striving beyond human means, almost encroaching on the territory of god (unlimited free energy!), and falling from grace. The CEO is certainly portrayed in such a light. But the actual story instead gave the impression that the technology could've worked, until someone committed an act of terrorism. And then the reveal of the Bad Thing makes as little sense as it did in Matrix, for the same reason (entropy, energy conversion ratios, etc.). There are also a bunch of plot holes.The game ends with a lengthy final non-puzzley section, which feels like a weird choice.This was an okay experience. At 4h, though, I can't quite recommend it. I'll give the game the slightest of downvotes, like a 6.5/10 or something.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected a simple, basic puzzle game from Lightmatter but this really felt like a game from someone with a love of puzzle games, and it shows through the nods and references it makes. Starting from simple ideas and adds to the puzzle complexity over time, with puzzles designed to give you exactly the space you need to solve them. The story gets unravelled during the time spent travelling between levels in a way that doesn't feel intrusive or like you have to slow down to get it all. There were only two puzzles that bordered on frustrating, but given they turned out to be the last puzzles of those 'sections' of the game it's nice to have that challenge.The only downside is the game's definitely short at less than 5 hours, likely less than 4, so keep that in mind when weighing up how much you're happy to pay for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, this is the first time I write a review for a game, but I think I really need to put my thoughts out there.I had an absolute blast playing this game! I played it from start to finish, at first I was playing the trial version but when I got to the end of the free content I just had to buy it and keep playing! By the way, I found the fact that you can actually buy the full version while still playing ther demo and that there is clever dialogue around it very creative.What is there to say, the core mecanic is very simple and immediately understood, yet the developpers crafted ever more interesting puzzles. Sometimes I got stuck but finding the solution was always satisfying and never did I feel like the game was unfairly unclear or hard, it always felt like I got stuck because I wasen't thinking about the puzzle the right way and when I found the solution it felt like my accomplishment.Visually, he game is also beautiful! It has a unique visual style that I think mends itself quite well to the atmosphere and more importantly to the fact that light is at the heart of the game. Talking about light, I love the way that the game uses light, it really builds the oppresive atmosphere of the game, but also contributes a lot to making it amazing looking.And the soundtrack and sound deseignare also incredible. I sometimes found myself stopping for a few seconds to just look and listen for a while.Finaly, the game wears its inspiration from the Portal games on its sleeve, especially Portal 2 with Virgil and Ellen being somewhat parallels to Cave Johnson and Dough Ratman, yet despite this clear inspiration the game never felt like a "discount Portal 2" but instead trully has it's own Identity. I really appreciated how the devellopers inserted the game in the same uiverse as those games: far from feeling like a funny reference that was being pushed to far, I think it had its place in the narrative and that is added something to it. (And I'm a huge fan of the Portal games so that helps :p ).So TL;DR: Loved it! It had me from start to finish, and I would totally recommend it to anyone.That said, I did notice that in complex scenes, mainly some with complex lighting or big spaces like the core room at the very end, the game did have a tendency to slow down. Another thing: in the credits, "Co-director" is misspelled as "Vo-directot" ;)That's litterally all the complaints I have about this game, at least those that I can think of now.

Had great fun. Would even consider it my second favorite game after portal, for games of this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Lightmatter is a short first-person game (<5 hours) where you're trapped in a research facility and have to solve puzzle-room after puzzle-room while a disembodied voice taunts and insults you. And if that doesn't sound familiar to you, don't worry, the game will help you remember with regular references to the Portal-franchise.Despite the obvious inspiration, the game manages to differentiate itself through its main premise: Shadows are evil and will kill you when you touch them, so you'll have to direct lamps and light beams to help you navigate through the rooms and activate switches which makes for a variety of fun-to-solve puzzles that scale nicely in difficulty and don't overstay their welcome.My one gripe with the gameplay is that the last section ditches the puzzle aspect completely in favour of a platforming section which is fine, but I enjoyed the puzzles a lot more.Visuals and soundtrack are very appealing, and even though the story is nothing special, the voice actors did a pretty great job delivering their lines.Although the game could have been longer, I would still recommend it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: A short puzzler I thoroughly enjoyed. It's not as complex as Portal or The Talos Principle, but it features an interesting core mechanic that if explored more, I believe can leave to much higher complexity. The only negative I have to say is that the game is capped at ~60 fps and can be offputting at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: Lightmatter joins a handful of titles like Portal, The Stanley Parable, and The Talos Principle in distinguishing itself from the average first-person puzzle game by doing more than placing you within a sterile museum of puzzles to halfheartedly push through without any motivator; its expertly narrated story and oppressive environments provide enough tension to make sure you never become too comfortable, and should drive you forward to the end without wondering to yourself why you're still going. While its story does ape some tropes from the big titles, Lightmatter's primary mechanic of using light to survive and open paths forward within overwhelming darkness is enough to keep it from being a clone.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: It's a short but decently paced puzzle game.Is it worth 20 dollars? Depends on how much the pros and cons affect your experience. For me, it's more worth at most 15 dollars. Luckily, it's on sale at a really nice price!Here's the pros and cons, and you can decide if you want to get this.Pros:- Art direction is spectacular, with fantastic work put into the environment of the levels, and an okay variety in locations.- Puzzles are very tricky, but not stupidly difficult. Once you figure out the solution, it'll seem obvious, and you'll probably blaze through it on replay. Very satisfying- Voice acting is fantastic, with a lot of dialogue that can commentate on what you do, what you look at, and how long it takes you to solve a puzzle. Helps make the lack of humans you see feel less empty.Cons:- Rather short for 20 dollars, with not much extra outside of dev commentary and speedrun timers.- Plot is predictable, and even used audio logs to tell you what's already mostly told to you by the guy on the speakers.- Ending is kinda abrupt. Delivers its moral message, but it's unclear what happened to you.- Dialogue, while plentiful, is kinda simple in writing. There's lots of world building dialogue, but nothing too interesting. And the comedic bits are usually pretty weak. Plus, a few too many on-the-nose references to another puzzle game, when one would be enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Lightmatter

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this quasi Portal clone. The puzzles are engaging and often require out of the box thinking without holding your hand, it's a unique take on lava floors, the narrative is pretty cool, it looks good and the cel shaded environments work well, although unlike Portal and, say, The Turing Effect, I'm finding it's lacking a bit in narrative engagement. You find things to expand the story but they're few and far between, which might explain why I'm tending to play a few levels and then drop out and back in again, whereas with those other games I played them for hours continually. I like the voice acting, but something about the story doesn't drag me into the mystery that other similar games have.It does lack graphical optimisations at this stage - 2nd Feb. Means that when you're turning, on controller or mouse, the frame rate looks a bit laggy, but it's nothing that majorly affects the game, and the FPS counter still registers at 60fps for me. It still clearly holds up to 60fps at 4k with everything on high. Some of the shadows are jagged, even with shadows on high. I've had a couple of crashes, but it saves a lot. So these are minor issues, because from a small studio at this price point this is an excellent game and I'm glad I bought it.Gameplay is great, and the interaction with the world is consistent throughout. If you like puzzlers of any kind, liked Portal, The Turing Test, The Talos Principle, The Witness, then you'll definitely find this very appealing and very satisfying. It more than makes up for its faults by being, at its core, an excellent addition to the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. A unique concept, good level of challenge, entertaining humor and plenty of playtime. It has some obvious resemblance to the Portal games (which it routinely references), but the experience is very much different, so it doesn't feel like a copycat overall. Absolutely worth the price if you ask me. P.S. I was rooting for Virgil (at least until I saw the secret ending on YouTube).

_childDocuments_.review: I have completed the game 5-6 times so far, and I still find value in the Trophy Hunt, some achievements are really hard to figure out. Some of the puzzles were a challenge on first play through, the game's weakest point is probably the narration that can be a bit too much of the same, though it still keeps the story fresh! With respect to a 5 man indie team, and a first title, this is a really impressive feat! The game can take from 6 - 12 hours to complete depending on who you are, and how well you understand the language. The tutorial is skipped, and its satisfying that the tutorial like narration still leaves most up to the player to figure out what can and cant be done. Personally i think the monochrome look is a bit cheap, however that is just taste, technically its great and in all my 12.3 hours of play so far i've only had the game crash once. I get stable 100FPS with my old AMD toaster rig, though there are reports of nvidia rigs who crash often. This might be a memory thing. Who knows! It brings vibes of Portal while it keeps being its own thing, its clear that some influences come from both LIMBO and Portal. Its a really good First Person Escape Room, and i would reccomend it, of the few things i miss, i would accept it because its a first release and a brand new studio, with about 5 developers. Community is great and helpful, and contact with devs is as close as you can get! The free to try concept is something i fully support, its honest to give the first taste free and don't expect blind faith from costumers who might expect it to be more than it is! Though I think its remarkable who high quality it is! 9/10. Would Deffinitely recommend and its a must play for Portal fans.
