_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why I'm addicted to this game.  It's basic as all hell, but the simplicity makes it good for someone with a short attention span.  My main complaint is that what little complexity the game does have, it doesn't bother explaining.  I don't know what is happening most of the time, various status effects aren't explained or communicated all that clearly, so you have to learn by trial and error, or by ignoring it entirely.  There's like a heat system, or something, and a few other random variables that you can exploit to do better, I think? There's no real structure here, just choose a character and it throws you into random battles, no story or fanfare.  It's a card game, so you can choose a theme for your deck, which determines what cards you get.  And since it's a rogue like (which I normally despise, so thumbs up there), you don't keep anything after each run, aside from leveling up cards and getting gear for perks.  Each stage rewards you with more stuff for that run, so you need to choose wisely.It does get a bit frustrating (dare I say, hideously unfair) at times, when later enemies start throwing c*ckblock cards at you.  Some wipe your armor every turn you draw, some just take up space in your hand, and then there's the f*cking infinite venereal disease card that quickly takes over your whole deck, so unless your RNG god blessed you with a card to counter it, the run is basically over.  Nothing more frustrating than pulling 5 hands of literally unusable cards as you get attacked relentlessly with no way to fight back or defend yourself.Graphics are okay, though the music and overall sound are pretty generic, but it's put together well and feels solid.  Oh yeah, it's got cute anime baps too.  It's just a fun, short burst kind of game that you can easily play with one hand while you eat pizza or something with the other.

_childDocuments_.review: After the first hour: So it’s a card-based tactical game. I’ll be honest, this game screams Slay the Spire, there’s no way to get away from that comparison, and yet I like this game. There’s a ton of personality here.This is like Slay the Spire if you chose missions instead of paths, and I think the mission choices are a better option. I’ve seen two bosses, several elites, and they all look good, though not unique, I’ve seen a drill enemy, something like a malboro from Final Fantasy, and more, but the art looks good.There’s a LOT of style to this game, perhaps too much, the camera will shake at certain moments which isn’t the best, and can be turned off, but at the same time, it is a very impressive game, and the action is great. I can’t talk much about the late game or if the mechanics of each character is different, I hope they are. But the one character I did play and the two bosses I downed in the first hour were interesting.So let’s get to two issues I’ve seen so far out of the way. The playable characters are all very busty women, and yeah, I like busty women, but the outfits shown in the tutorial are a bit much. Also, the tutorial is horrible. It’s just a video and even the tracking on the bar was pretty bad. Yet neither is a real dealbreaker, and I don’t think it should affect many people’s opinions. There is an in-game tutorial as well that’s very useful.Five minutes into the game I groaned about how similar this is to Slay the Spire, and it is. But this game just came out in February of this year, and it feels well done with a lot of unique ideas. If you are a fan of card games or a fan of Slay the Spire, I think you’ll have a good time here. If you hate that game, this one probably won’t change your mind, but I wouldn’t expect it to. _childDocuments_.review: Why would I not recommend a game I've played so much?Simple.  While this game could be enjoyable, it's a deck building game where ultimately your deck, choices, skills and even ability to play mean nothing.  When you get to the final boss you'll notice that rather then try to be creative or even give the appearance of being compatent game designers, they just decided to make that boss immune to everything.  And not just powers and cards, like ... everything.  Build a deck that blocks damage?  It has unblockable damage.  Build a deck based on reduced mana costs?  Haha, idiot, this boss punishes and hurts you for casting low cost spells and if that doesn't work it just randomises your card costs.  Build a deck built on buffing yourself?  Idiot, this boss fully strips all your buffs every round.  Build cards that have carry over effects?  Cancals them too.  It literally dosn't matter.  A monkey could build a deck by tossing crap at the wall and it's deck would be as good as yours in the finial fight.That's not to say the boss is difficult.   After all, if they had the competence to make a challenging boss they wouldn't need to just make it immune to everything. It's pretty easy all said and done.  It just is so pointless getting to what should be the final test for your deck building skills and facing a boss that not only is stupidly easy and almost exclusively luck based, but one you might as well be using a random deck against.I simply can not support game designers with that level of incompatence.  They do not deserve our funding and should not be encouraged to make new games.  Give your money to developers who understand game design on even teh fundamental level of "not being able to use  your skills and powers is not fun".

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Slay the Spire and similar games, you will enjoy this.  If you actively dislike them, then you probably won't.This game is one of the latest in the growing set of Roguelite Deckbuilders -- you make a run through several battles, events, and other nodes, until you fight a boss.  Beat three bosses to win the run.  Whether you fail or win, you receive points to unlock additional ability options for future runs, as well as a small bonus for your next run that improves the further you go.  All this is pretty standard -- it very much is reimplementing the Slay the Spire model here.So, what's different?  First, this game is gorgeous.  I'm not a player who usually cares too much about graphics, as long as the gameplay is good, but this game easily beats all the others in this genre that I've played.Second, it replaces the fantasy theme used by most other games in this genre with a sci-fi/fantasy hybrid that works well.Thirdly, it makes a lot of interesting choices with character abilities -- it's not just cribbing from similar games, but from the start blazes its own trail with abilities like 'Overheat' -- a mechanism where you receive a penalty to your Max HP if you don't manage it carefully, meaning that you can actively choose whether to try and take a battle slowly to avoid that penalty, or rush a battle to avoid taking too much damage, at the possible cost of resources for future battles in that run.The last thing is that it simplifies and improves upon many mechanisms in this game space.  One example is the choice of nodes.  In Slay the Spire, you go through a long tree of nodes, choosing forks in the path, and mapping out your intended path basically from the start of the level, with limited deviation possible once you've 'locked it in'.  In this game, this is simplified into a series of binary choices that still give you plenty of chances to take the kind of path you want.  Likewise, instead of shops being a rare option, they're *always* open to you outside of battle, and visiting a shop node is necessary only to refresh the items the shop offers.  And finally, instead of relics, the game goes with a 'skill point' system each run, where you can buy and upgrade known skills to improve your abilities for the run, or can gamble and take an ability you haven't yet discovered.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent but not good enough to recommend given how many other games are doing similar things but better. If you played Slay the Spire and wished The Silent looked like an anime figurine, this could be the one for you.Variations on common mechanics:- skills instead of relics/artifacts. It is not quite a talent "tree," as you can buy anywhere in the square, but the "legendary" skills on the edges require that you buy a whole line- the shop is always available and resets only when you choose- there is not a map to navigate, just a pick of three fights at each of 15 points. Each fight has a degree of difficulty and an attached quest like "use 5 Instant cards." You need not complete the quest during that fight, just sometime (or don't, but there are rewards).- "precision" and "parry" mechanics for doing exactly enough damage to kill the enemy or having exactly enough block to stop an attack- "combo" mechanic for using cards in a particular order (randomized each time)As you will see in other discussion, the difficulty level is low. You can dial it up, but I did not find the mechanics interesting enough to pursue that path. There is a lot more going on than in most similar games, but little of it feels relevant or worth paying attention to. Your character's head can get very noisy with icons.The visuals are fancier than in most competing games. You can pay to unlock more boobs. I received an in-game reward of a costume that turned out to be a bikini. I did not check how stripper-ific the other costumes were, but the game is selling "schoolgirl" DLC, so they have certain expectations about you as a player.Entertaining spectacle, but I could use more crunch.

_childDocuments_.review: I completed Slay the Spire and tired of it, but I wanted for another card game like StS which feels fresh with new mechanics. And you know I did not found another game like StS, no good clones I mean. Steam recommended me NEOVERSE and after it was started for sales I bought it very quickly. And NEOVERSE is very nice made card rogue-lite game I say! It is not one by one copy of StS, but inspired it (like StS inspired by Dream Quest). What is different for the first time I taste:- Drawing cards mechanics (StS more linear in this - 95% of time you just think about combination of cards you have in a hand; in NEOVERSE you play more randomly because you can redraw a card instead of played card (if this option does not blocked) until your 'mana' points are over)- You can upgrade your chatacter'OK, I put up with'-feels:- Graphics style like a Sci-Fi Korean MMO (many glows, bright lights, sharp effects)- Animation fast but some clumsy (not critical for me)Overall I totally recommend this game to all who searches another CCG rogue-lite. Or waifus.Just what I need now - more translations to another languages like in StS. I wish success to the developers!

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to Slay the Spire in a lot of ways but also introduces a lot of unique (or somewhat different) mechanics to the game. I'll get to those in a second, but I do just want to warn people that it's a lot easier on the default difficulty. However, you can immediately raise the difficulty up to ascension 10 and there is also an end-game mode where you use a custom deck you built during a run.Some other things unique from most Slay the Spire clones is that you have a class that uses either healing and/or lifesteal. There's a combo system which gives you a critical strike if you play cards in a certain order. There's a randomized skill tree in the form of a grid. Roguebook and Tainted Grail do have similar passives you can choose from, but this is different in that you get to see all of your choices at the beginning of your runs.One thing similar but handled in a unique way is relics. You don't find randomized drops during your run, but you do have equippable relics you can buy after your runs with trophies (in-game currency) you earn during the run. The trophies are also used for revives and required for those end-game runs I mentioned earlier (which use a deck you save from a completed run). You can also get trophies from buying cosmetic DLCs ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: A game with cool UI, nice visuals, good diversity of cards, and some ugly monsters.I really enjoy building strange decks in hunter mode and try them out to see if they actually work. I believe it would be good if hunter mode had infinite levels, sometimes I would like to see how far my deck could go.That being said, a randomly-generated skill tree is making it pretty hard to try out certain deck ideas that are dependent on skills, although starting a new run might give me the skill I want, I will lose all bonuses from last run. Why not letting players take a few skills when starting the run, or give players the ability to modify the skill tree during the run?One big problem of the game is, just after a few playthroughs you will find the enemies and their skills are quite repetitive, I would say the diveristy on the player side is pretty good, but there's still great potential of improvement on the enemy side. Enemies could have more passives, and more actively working with each other. If the only real difference between playthroughs is the player's deck, players will get bored once they have tried out all decks they could think of, aren't they?There's also a minor bug with items, there were a few times when I'm unable to delete unwanted items, could be quite annoying when you miss a powerful item because of this.Overall the quality of the game is pretty decent for an early-access game, but it can still be improved, and I would love to see it improved.

_childDocuments_.review: You can't really talk about this game without talking about the game it mimicks, Slay the Spire.  So I won't try to avoid that. If you like Slay the Spire, this will scratch the itch.The graphics are solid, and some of the creatures are quite clever.  The game is played in multiple acts, with some of them themed with high fantasy or greek mythology settings.  It's an interesting skin on top of the game.  The sound is... well, there's definitely sound.  It's not jarringly bad or anything, it's just there.Right now there are 3 characters; I've not played enough wtih all of them but I'm not sure they are all fully developed (hey, it is early access).I picked this up because I clocked over 150 hours in Slay the Spire and wanted something similar but different enough to be fresh. _childDocuments_.review: A deckbuilding dungeon crawl along the lines of Meteorfall, Monster Slayer, and most famously, Slay the Spire... It doesn't innovate on the formula too much, but that's not to say I'm in any way disappointed... it's new characters with new mechanics, a new card list, and a new list of artifacts (or "Skills", as they appear in this game... which is not all that different but slightly superior as a system, I'd say). It's also quite nice graphically... I'll confess it seems to feature some bugs (I had one run ruined when I spontaneously lost the ability to remove cards from my deck for some reason), the dialogue features occasional Engrish, and the music is bland... but I have no other complaints, really... Mechanically, I'd argue it's every bit as strong as most games in this vein including Slay the Spire... stronger than many, even. Goodness knows if and when you'll see a meaningful update to the content to whatever game in this vein you might already play, which means a new game's worth of content with 3 whole new characters and decks is worth the price of admission if you're like me and basically would always enjoy more games of this sort, and the biggest reason you stop playing at any point is you've run out of "new" to experience in what you have. If you're new to the genre, this is more or less as good a place as any to start (Slay the Spire is more popular and thus a more active community, and I'd actually say Monster Slayer is the criminally under-rated best of the genre, but it's a sold choice if not my first or second). If you're into the genre and would like more new takes on the same concept, this is a definite buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Neoverse is a rogue-lite turn-based card game. In the point of core mechanic, it is simliar to Slay the Spire (but definitely not a rip-off), but a more forgiving one. If you are fan of STS, try this for a diverse experience. If you think STS is difficult, you might find this game a cheer-up.Neoverse has a more diverse graphic design. Being a Korean game (I noticed there are lots of names look like Korean in the credit list, so I persume it is), it has done a good job on designing characters (not being biased, but Korean game companies has fame of designing erotic female characters and they do a very good job on it). Some of my friends even regard it as adult version of Slay the Spire (and then they recommend to me haha). Three characters are all beautiful and hot, and what is even more attractive is they all have vivid boob and bust physic.Like Slay the Spire, debuffs on the characters or enemies disappear as turns go on. Yet, block is not removed at the end of every turn unless you meet enemies with the ability to remove block at the end of turn. To be balanced, some buffs decrease every turn but there are several that stay the same. Artifacts in the STS is replaced with skill in Neoverse, which need skill points to purchase. You can do it anytime even in battle. So does purchasing in the store. There is no random event in Neoverse as STS. If you want to get some certain rewards you just choose a battle provides you this, by finishing a certain required mission. However, unlike the store, you cannot claim you rewards anytime. It requires to be not in the battle. Every characters has three different types of playstyles, and a daily deck to choose from, which offer you different cards as your start deck (although they are not all very distinctive, which I will discuss later). Unlike STS you only have certain amount of cards in one turn, in Neoverse if your Mana (energy) is not run out, you can draw cards automatically and infinitely, until there is no empty space in your hand, or all of your cards are used and need shuffle.Being an early access work, it inevitably has a few flaws. I hope the devs can read it, but if you are someone looking for purchase opinions, I recommend you not to cause it is long and time wasting.To me it is not a small problem. There are some questionable cards. I catagorse those card as redundant, rarely used and disadvantages outweigh advantages. Examples of being redundant probably are most among all these three types. Being redundant doesn't mean cards is useless, but the effects of some cards are highly alike. Some might say it is no big deal. But you could see it is pointless if the outcome has no critical differences. The card Order of Helena. It activates the guardian ability once, but you has Order Attack, which will also order guardian to attack (in most case it is the same except the guardian is griffin, but griffin is rarely used) and some other effects. Naya's Radioactive Shoot and Radioactive Cut, the effects are highly the same. Why bother to make two cards? There are more example if you pay attention to the card effects. There are no big differences, just tiny differences which can be completely ignored considering the huge amount of HP of the enemies and yours. So why bother? Rarely used means in most circumstances the cards are unless. For example, Destory, select three cards and consume them. It only works when you meet enemies who prefer add unplayable or forbidden cards to your deck, who is not common to meet. This circumstance is not fatal. I am fine living with it and win, rather than adding an almost useless card to my deck. And there are more like the card Reservoir, the item used will not be consumed, yet the fact is using item is not very common in this game, at least you don't need a 2 cost card to prepare for it.I refer disadvantages outweigh advantages types to most of the "self-injury" types card in this game. Such as Mission Impossible, deal 30 (50 in evolved version) to everyone including you. If I use twice or three times I almost die, and there is no quick measure to recover my health during battle. Stealth mode, extremely costly for 5 Mana and gain only one stealth. If the enemy perform a 4*6 attack, it is flushed at the first attack and you still take 3*6 damage. A special types of example is evolved version cards. They are a few evolved cards are surprsingly weakened in a non-direct way. Like Mission Impossible I mention, and there are cards that evolved version cost more Mana and bigger negative effects but outcome are unworthy. I am really confused about the way these evolved cards designed.There are too much information appears at the same time. It doesn't look nice and some of them are really redundant, such as, the bar on the top left corner, why I need a health bar when I already have one with the character? What those cubes mean I still don't quite figure out (I think it is battle tech but I don't know how to read). Why shows so many skills on the left and all the missions including the ones I finish on the right by default? I sometimes miss information because above the health bar there are so many BIG and ugly icons that I forgot a certain one I should take measure to avoid it. I highly recommend to redo the UI to make it looks neat and simple.At the start of every universe or battle, the defence is okay, but with the battle goes on when enemies inflict buff to themselves or when you meet stronger enemies as journey goes on, defend is largely weakened, unless you can inflict 15 or more defence at once, because at that phrase enemies (noted that it is plural) deal 40, 50 or more damage at one turn in total (specially in Hunter mode), while your default defence card can only do 4 to 6 blocks. No one will do defence as it is clearly wasted, which is also the reason I say Griffin is rarely used. Some might say just do another strategy when you can't block like dealing large amount of damage to destroy them at once, which is fine, but I specially point the defense situation out cause it happens extremely common that I don't think it is balanced at all. The devs really should weigh the balance of HP, attack and block very carefully.I like Clarie's priest and vampire playstyles, which I think it is most disctinct one among all different playstyles of all characters. Even so, I find it very confusing by gaining cards after battle or buying cards from the store, different playstyles can be the same. I mean, even I choose priest deck, I can still get lots of vampire cards to play in a vampire or a hybrid way. So why makes it different at the beginning?  Let alone that most of playstyles is not so disctinct. For example, offensive and defensice type of Helena. I don’t know if I misunderstand how these two play or something, I find those two are played in almost same way. It might because of the defence issue I mention as Griffin is almost useless, but anyway in my opinion there are not very different and should be improved. Hunter mode is my least favorite part of this game. It is ridiculous. I mean, why make one? The devs just want to put all their proud strong monsters at the battle at the same time, with all the ridiculous buffs and damage you should awe, ignoring the basic principle of a card game is balance, not slaying stupid monsters that ramdomly pile up. I think it should be removed if just put super strong enemies togetherand think it is how to make it hardcore.Anime is fine, but the devs should really work hard on optimazation.Naya's head seems a bit off. It is oddly big for her body.Sometime the health bar blocks the head.Card art design is not in the same style. I feel odd about it, especially Helena's card only put animal on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Neoverse is virtually non-existent in terms of presentation - no style, no atmosphere, dull colors, mediocre music, general blandness and unoriginality rule the ball. It looks like Raid: Shadow Legends and plays like Slay The Spire, but with all the fun and soul sucked out of it. I wouldn't buy it, but if you'd get it for free or at a huge discount - give it a whirl maybe, it's a mechanically competent time waster.Put on your own music, scoop up some of that insipid, lukewarm porridge from this bowl and proceed to chew on it mindlessly. These moments in life are also important, I guess. See? I can't even hate the game properly, I don't feel anything, I'm but a husk of a man after playing it. _childDocuments_.review: This game has a solid base (a revised version of Slay the Spire, which is fine), but there are some points that could certainly be improved.1. The game is just TOO EASY. Maybe it's my experience with the aforementioned StS, but I don't think a player that is new to a game of this genre should have two wins in two runs. The amount of buffs is overwhelming, it doesn't take much to just use as much cards as possible without giving much thought as to which ones would benefit the most. There should be less energy available per turn, and the rewards given for completing mission should be nerfed.2. The game has no choices and little variety. This is basically a battle gauntlet, a set of multiple battles that end up in a big boss fight. IMO there should be some sort of events that would make things less mundane. 3. Enemies could use more variety.4. Locations could use more variety.5. Music could use more variety. I may be wrong, but I think there isn't even a special soundtrack for boss battles? Kinda diminishes the importance and intensity of the battle.Even with these points I've mentioned, I still think this is a promising game. The graphics are nice and the battle system is not an StS clone, adapting noticable changes. I just hope the developer doesn't abandon the game, as there is a lot of work to do to make it a truly GOOD game.I'd give it a 6.5/10 for what it is at the moment.Edit: You know what? Forget about this being "easy". Hunter mode is... ooof.

_childDocuments_.review: Neoverse is basically Slay the Spire's weeby cousin. Alongside three different characters with different playstyles among them, the games come with a few bells and whistles to add upon the experience - skill boards, a combo system, accessories that impact gameplay, etc. While the game tries to impress you with the above features and its 3D models, it's all style over substance. I have two main gripes with Neoverse. The first is how homogeneous the game feels. Alternatives like Slay the Spire or Monster Train do a good job of making its cards and, more importantly, its enemies look different and act differently from one another. You can easily recognize what an enemy does based on their design or simply from past experiences. That isn't really the case in Neoverse. While it makes sense on paper to give each card a color hue to denote what a card's type is, it makes most of the cards blend together; the art as well doesn't seem diverse or dynamic enough to remember what a card does by its art alone, a big issue for a game where you spend most of your time looking at cards. The enemies also don't pop out or have noticeable features that reasonably define what they do. However, it may be because of the second problem of this game that this first problem doesn't really matter.The second issue with Neoverse is that it feels trivially easy - especially while using the character with the built-in health gain mechanics. I don't suppose there's even a need to remember what the enemies or cards do anyways if I can just speed spam all my cards and beat the run. I've made it to what seems like the penultimate difficulty repeating the same thing, over and over again, and I can't stand playing this anymore. I just don't feel engaged without the traditional amount of difficulty a rouge-like should bring.TLDR: Neoverse is a lot like its female protagonists - pretty, but with no personality. Its oversimplicity and how boring everything looks and feels makes it a lot less memorable than its alternatives like Slay the Spire, Monster Train, or Griftlands. Play those instead.

_childDocuments_.review: It reminds of Slay the Spire.  It has some solid mechanics that allow for multiple playstyles through deck building.   Don't play attention to the weeb blondes on the splash.  They could have picked puppies and it would play the same.  The avatars aren't the focus of the game. _childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying that I beat my first two games with ease. If you're looking for a Slay The Spire look-a-like that's easy, this is it.But, for me, the game sadly falls short on pretty much everything. I played the game after hearing many remarks on its many deckbuilding options, but after playing it I'm not really sure where that's coming from. Maybe everyone is talking about the third character I didn't try yet?In terms of assets (which I think is what the game is trying to market the most?), graphics are meh. Sounds are meh. Animations are meh. All of the assets seem as though they've been purchased online. Particle effects are pretty at least.In terms of mechanics:- Most deckbuilders have maps that let you choose routes which will give you access to shops. Neoverse gives you the shop option 24/7, even mid-battle.- Block from cards is not reset every turn. This would be fine if over half the bosses didn't wipe block from you, ruining your strategies.- Many of the cards and status effects are very typical and uninteresting. Others are flatly dumb. As a basic example, I once ran into a fight with two enemies that gave eachother a buff that made my attacks do 1 damage each for the whole fight. Fun.- New cards you get are hardly better than your starting cards. (example: basic attack is 1 cost and deals 3 damage. cool fancy attack is 0 cost and does 2 damage) It often feels like you can win the game by just having cards, rather than by intelligently building a deck. Not a very rewarding experience.- Enemies are very underwhelming and not threatening. One of the first enemies you fight comes in a group of one (1) and has an attack that deals three (3) damage. Your basic block cards block all of that. You have five energy and infinite draw, so it would be a challenge to get damaged at all. It's as if the game wants me to win 100% of the time without a challenge.I know these are all negative notes and no positives, but... the only interesting part of the game that I can think of is the combo system. And even still, that's just the game rewarding you for doing what the game wants you to do. Everything else is just borrowed from other games, but made less intelligent.Oh well. I'll probably revisit the game in the hopes that I'm wrong and this game actually turns out to be challenging and unique. The game has good ratings. Maybe you'll like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone likes to compare these card games to slay the spire, however regarding the game mechanics they would be right in this case.  That being said, honestly I’d say this game does it better because you can actually keep your shields onto the next turn, just to give one example of its impressive card balance.  You’ll quickly find that NEOVERSE offers a lot of diversity for the player to dive into with the three classes of gameplay.Visually, what’s to complain about?  Sure it looks like a jumbled set of assets from a repurposed shooter, but the core game is there and works really well.  This game guarantees tons of ENJOYABLE battles that leave you with a sense of accomplishment after they’re done.  The progression of the game moves along nicely as well, giving you plenty of nice things to unlock and synergize with.All in all, don’t be fooled by the game’s art style.  NEOVERSE’s a sophisticated card game is very well thought out and very fun to play, it just so happens that you get the benefit of eye candy as you kick ass through the levels.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're familiar with Slay the Spire, Neoverse is incredibly similar, except with a few tweaks to give it its own flavor. Disclaimer: while I'm familiar with Slay the Spire gameplay through watching a decent amount of streamers play it, I do not play it myself, so take that as you will.For one, block, or rather, armor, does not reset between turns (though certain bosses cause a reset between turns). The game is balanced around this, but it's technically possible to build up hundreds of armor in a battle.Furthermore, whenever you play a card, you draw a new card in its place, until you reach the end of your draw pile. Once you reach the end of your deck you'll stop drawing, but if you have a specific skill you may draw a new hand after exhausting all cards in your deck.There's also no map, and the only events are battles. At each stage you select a battle, which may be normal, elite, or a boss at the end of 5 stages. Each selection also has a mission associated with it such as "complete 3 combos", "block 50 damage in a single battle", or "take no damage in a battle". Missions are permanent, and they give a range of rewards such as 30% healing, skill points, a selection of a card, upgrades to cards, permanent energy upgrades, and so on once you complete them. Once completed, you can choose when to select the reward, so for example, if you're at full HP but completed a healing mission, you can choose to wait until hurt before claiming the reward.Another difference is that there's no relics. Your passive gains are selected from a randomized skill grid that's generated at the start of each run. You gain skill points by buying from the shop, completing certain objectives, and randomly at the end of combat. Skills can be anything from "one card from the shop will have its price reduced to 0" to "every time you play an attack card all enemies take 1 damage" to "gain  7 max HP". You can see all available skills as soon as you start a run, and when you complete a line of skills (either vertical, once unlocked, or horizontal on the grid) a generally stronger skill is available at the end. You may want to focus down a line for a specific skill or pick skills from around the board to work with whatever build you're trying.There's also three equipment slots for meta progression. For example, one equipment piece is one that removes random item drops from the game, and at the start of each battle gives you a random selection of items. Great for if you have "too good to use" syndrome, but it also means you can't curate what items you have available for any given battle. You buy these pieces of equipment with trophies, a meta currency you get for defeating bosses.There's also a few new mechanics, like combos, parries, and precision strikes. Combos are done by playing cards in order of type that the game tells you to do, doing this will raise the damage of your next attack. Precision strikes are triggered by doing the exact amount of damage required to kill an enemy (so, if a enemy has 5 HP left, do a 5 damage attack), and net you some extra money. Parries are done by having the exact amount of armor necessary to stop damage from an enemy (if an enemy is going to do 5 damage, put up 5 armor to trigger a parry). Parries will stun an enemy for the next turn, and can be triggered while still taking damage, because you can perfect block one enemy in a group (enemies go in order from left to right) while taking damage from the rest of the enemies that move after it.It's pretty clearly a "clone" of Slay the Spire, but it certainly has a decent amount of its own stuff going on to set it apart (other than graphics, obviously).It's a good time, and it's pretty easy to recommend at 20 USD. Honestly, just by looking at it you probably know if you would like it or not.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a surprisingly good deckbuilder roguelite. It's not going to dethrone the kings of the genre, but if you want more of the same, put this one high on your list.There are a few unique characters which you can slightly tweak before the run. There's a standard progression through stages with okay enemy variety. Combat mechanics are fun, with different buffs, debuffs, cobmos, etc to consider beyond standard defend/attack.It really shines with the different decisions you get to make each run. Beyond standard card choices, there's quests to choose with varying rewards, a randomized skill grid to upgrade as you progress, items to grab, a shop to uh shop at, etc. All these choices make it really fun to replay.Solid recommendation to anyone interested.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very similar to Slay The Spire in many ways. However, this game stand out with its visuals and unique mechanics, such as precision kills (not over killing enemies) and parries (blocking the exact damage). In addition, you can collect trophies from bosses (every 5th fight) to buy gadgets that change some of the mechanics of the game to add replay value, which they've constantly added since I've played the game. In terms of difficulty, this game is easier than Slay (I've cleared Transcended Universe 15), because you have more control over your deck and you have access to the shop to buy cards and items even during fights! If that's not enough, you can reroll the shop listings anytime at an increasing cost per roll (starting from 0).If you're a fan of Slay the Spire, you will not be disappointed with this game.Update, I nominated the game under the intuitive category, because we need more new ideas in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: A nice slay the spire type game. The graphics are nice as well as the game play. The girls' different abilities and styles are a nice addition. Its not a hard game but doesn't require some thinking to progress in the game. I think it would be interesting to see a multiplayer pvp added but its really not needed. I also would also like a few more characters to play with but that is merely personal opinion. Do pick this game up!!!update: Its nice to see the developers are still adding to this even though most it cosmetic.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprise to be sure, but a welcome one.Just when you look at it and think this is utterly uninspired clone of Slay the Spire, it just goes and gutpunches you with a couple of surprises hidden in the mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: Very fun Slay-the-Spire-like with plenty of replayability and decent graphics. The three classes currently present in the game have their own very unique mechanics and I like all three of them.The environments, monsters and bosses are varied and the game can be played on a more easier setting as well as in some more challenging modes.Only thing I don't like is the card art as it is ugly and has a tendency to not cover what the card is doing at all. Other than that a fun addictive game for a small price. Easily recommended if you want something to scratch the rogue-like card-drawing dungeoneering experience that Hearthstone and STS pioneered.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 3: They finally changed the gear buying system from timed to static, although I'm unsure if the holiday gear (outside of the costume change one) are all available (I think so? I wasn't paying super attention after they added that timer stupidity). I'm tentatively changing this back to yes because that was a significant flaw and poor decision and it appears to have mostly been an inexplicable 1-of that they've corrected. I have only done a few runs since the latest patch, I think the balance is a little off (many defense cards feel way, way too weak) which limits the viable cards a bit more than in the past but you can still build a strong deck in a few ways.Previous Review -----------------I think it's a good game overall, I think I preferred the previous way many of the buffs / debuffs like Radiation and such worked, but it was messy so I understand trying to clean it up. The reason I'm leaving a negative review is that it's a single player game, in early access, and they are adding "Games as a service" concepts like equipment you can unlock (for trophies you earn in-game, NOT real money, worth noting) but that equipment becomes unavailable over time. It's a single player game. Don't have GaaS bull in it. End of story. I actually preferred this over Slay the Spire but going to uninstall and walk away before they make it any worse.Edit: While I appreciate the developer response below, I just refuse to endorse any single player game that has time limited content,  it cycles back around. It the antithesis to my goals playing a single player game. I would much rather have a "big mess" of a shop until you can implement a more organized one than deal with stuff not being available when I have time and desire to play. So barring that, maybe I will check back in a few months (if I have any desire to play again) and see if a full implementation with no time limits is in then.Edit 2: The developer has confirmed that the special Halloween event equipment will only be available during Halloween. That means that gameplay-altering options will not be available to anyone who buys this after first week of November, until (maybe) next Halloween. That's like having relics in StS or mods you can only unlock one time a year completely blocked off from you. That's inexcusable.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Deckbuilding game with awesome graphics. The 3 chars have a relatively distinct playstile and each char has at least 2 primary themes that they can focus on: The paladin can either try to accumulate Faith points for passive healing or give in to her dark side and turn into a vampire which offers more offensive cards and your attacks drain life.The balancing and wording is still a bit off, but it's fully enjoyable, stable and without any too obvious bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: You clicked for the art, but there's a legitimately good game here. And this is coming from someone who's played STS and Monster Train into the ground.The thing I like the most about it is that the power level is relatively flat. I got this on special for $10 and it's an absolute steal at that price.

_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was all "What the hell is this waifu simulator that sells solely on putting tits in your face" but looking at some gameplay made me think about giving it a shot. If you can get over the characters being what they are, it is actually enjoyable. Some differences in mechanics compared to Slay the Spire, but also very similar. _childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Neoverse is clearly using a lot of ideas made popular from Slay the Spire but also adds enough to set itself apart.  While I haven't played a lot yet, what time I have played has been enjoyable and prompted me for just one more game.   I have tried the Agent, Paladin and Summoner (think those are the correct names) and each has it's own unique feel.   As mentioned however the classes are very similar to those in Slay the Spire.   One big difference is that you don't really pick a path to follow like in StS, instead you are presented with a challenge before each fight that controls some of the rewards you will get.  All in all the game is solid and I do recommend it to my friends that like card games.  However if you don't like card games, or card games in the vein of Slay the Spire then most likely you will want to pass Neoverse for something else.  That all said there is enough here to cover the asking price, even more so if on sale.   There are a few translation gaffs here and there and the UI has some clutter that quite honestly can be overlooked, all in all a stable and fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, 9/10.The animations and character designs are great, the sound is great, the enemy variety is great... this game is just great. I'm particularly fond of the card and deck building variety and the fact that each character has like three different mechanics exclusive to them - it makes for several different builds for each character. There's also three different modes to play through, so there's a lot of replay value. Especially considering I'm still finding new enemies and mini-bosses in each era that I haven't seen before, or running into new enemy abilities I have to adapt to. There's a lot to see here (and that's with the game still being in Early Access at the time of writing).I honestly like this game better than anything else I've touched in the rouge-light deckbuilder genre by far. It never feels like it's cheating you, not letting you build how you want, rigging the odds because that's the only way to make you lose, or scrubbing away any sense of progression.My only desires would be an even harder mode, preferably one where I can build the base bones of my own starter deck. I'd buy it again just for that (I kinda regret buying it on sale anyway, because I honestly feel it's worth more than I paid).All in all, I can't wait to see where this game goes when it's finished. Grab it, even at full price it's cheaper than most similar games. I don't think you'll regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: I usually avoid Rougelike/rouglite games, but this one looked interesting, cuz it ls flashy and shiny!I got to try it on gamepass, I liked it and the difficulty seemed fair, so I later bought it on Steam.And first try, I got my butt kicked and I suspected PC version is a different build, cuz I beat the main mode in one try on Xbox.But no, it was just luck and learning what cards serve you better in the long run.Still, sometimes I play and I don't get very good card drops, so there is that luck element.But each time you beat it, you have the chance to get better stuff and unlock new cards.Sometimes you'll get very OP, and I love it lolBut don't worry, if you're up for it, there are 15 levels each with its modifiers to make things more difficult, called transcend levels.There is also Hunter mode, and Challenge mode. I've played Hunter mode but haven't tried challenge yet. WHich is just a more limited mode.The 3 characters feels different to play and have different cards. But I wish they had more of their personality reflected, they're very stoic lolIn terms of unlockables, there are two outfits for each character, and a lot of custumization items that have gameplay effect.Another thing I like about this game is that you can stop at anytime, and your progress will be saved. Each runs takes me about 50 minutes on average, but if you have to go do something or just tired, don't worry, your progress is saved :)If you lose, you get 1 free retry, after that it will cost 5 trophies.You unlock 1 trophy by completing a run, or more depending on your performance. But when I first bought the game, I got the collector edition with all DLC, and I got a few hundred trophies. Idk if it was with the DLC or just like that.So after 30 hours, and 50% of achievements unlocked, I give this a YES!
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun and has a great basis, but it lacks content and is way too easy. I'd give it a positive review if it wasn't so ultra grindy. If you want to tackle the "true endgame" you have to grind, grind, grind a MADDENING amount. You get like 1-4 trophies per run and you need to buy an accessory that costs 20. To reliably farm that by beating all the stages and to make your characters more unique, you need to buy other equipment on top, which ranges from 5 to 15. I've played over 7 hours and have ONE additional item after feeling forced to get the "50% chance to get 2 trophies"-farm item first.

The game play is tense, the iconography enhances immersion, graphics are pleasing, and sound effects are satisfying.  The latest update really separates the game now, from its predecessors. Nice job!

But also, the 3D graphics here aren't great, the scenarios are poorly made and the effects are not particularly nice. _childDocuments_.review: I am only recommending the game based upon gameplay and IF there is a sale.  The base price of $20 is way too high, I'd say $10 is about fair for what you get.If you like slay the spire but think it's too difficult than you'll most likely enjoy this game.  The 3d models are a nice touch on the whole slay the spire card battle model and the game is not too punishing and takes about 1 hour to beat a run.  The nice thing about this one is you can use the shop any time and the biggest compliment I can provide is during one of my runs I lost track of time which means I was enjoying myself.  Worth it if you're into the card battler type games which I'm honestly not that into but I'm glad I played it.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Essentially Slay the Spire but with none of the nuance. The biggest issue I have is frankly how everything is so accessible. You can access a store mid fight, where the only limiting factor is how much money you have. This lets you buy new cards, buy upgrade points, and even items during your fight, as well as reroll as much as you want for a cost. Instead of some kind of items you find that grant passive bonuses, you can pay to buy upgrades with a secondary currency, which is again available at the shop every time you reroll. The only limitation is that the final tier of upgrade needs all previous ones in a line before it. The only other ugprades you can get are stuff you can equip on your character which require trophies to unlock and are extremely strong. Like the first one I got literally lets me heal, upgrade or remove a card literally whenever I feel like. Because of all this, theres less to see each run, and everything feels a lot easier. Hell, even the final boss was a joke. Overall, the game isn't bad by any stretch of the imagination, but it doesn't contain enough content or skill to really make someone keep coming back outside of just some variety from other similar games. Maybe buy it on deep discount, but otherwise its nothing special.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, very playable, very pretty and of course very "Slay the Spire"...whilst almost totally lacking originality in game mechanics, having lifted nearly all of them shamelessly from the aforementioned roguelite card battler "NEOVERSE" is an absolute joy to play and very beautiful and atmospheric visually (and no, I'm not just meaning the waifus)... I love STS and this is  very much a 3-d version where you skip across different dimensions as one of 3 very different, but all female charachters, whilst fighting a variety of well-realized fully animated enemies. There are normal battles, elites and bosses just like in the game's obvious inspiration and just about every other gameplay element from your favourite ccg too, all wrapped up in shiny new graphics with very different and interesting to play protagonists and opponents. So far I am really enjoying it and finding the balancing pretty good and the gameplay smooth and addictive. If you have to choose between STS and this, I'd still say choose the former, but if you already have and love STS then you are almost certainly going to enjoy this little gem.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: NEOVERSE caught my eye in the May 2020 Humble Monthly bundle, and wow am I glad I checked it out! This is a deckbuilding roguelike very much in the vein of Slay the Spire with a sci-fantasy aesthetic from a South Korean indie studio. This game is very much a StS-clone (I say this as a compliment) but does add some changes to the formula, a couple of examples being a persistent item/card shop that you can use even in the middle of a battle, or skillpoints you can use to build your character a specific way during a run (as opposed to the random relics you get in StS). My very first run took about 2.5 hours (idle and AFK time included) and ended in a clear, so it did seem a little bit easy at first, but if anything, I'm even more eager to dive back into the harder difficulties that are now available.Give this one a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this game for a while now and have been here for at least four or so updates. As i recall, the first made the UI more crisp, the second added hunter mode and daily decks, etc, but this last update where you lowered the atk and def effectiveness was not cute. The first UI was beautiful as it was I don't know why the timer was moved and skills and combos, etc moved. It wasn't broken so why fix it :( Lowering the attacks/defense unnecessarily draws out the battles they were already hard and unforgiving enough and I end up stuck in a loop where I can only do, if im lucky, 10 damage a turn just for the enemy to recover 10 hp every other turn. At least if you're going to do that lower the enemy atk too because they're still pushing out x5 x8 and x10 damage. Honestly I can't even imagine going into hunter mode with cards like this.  And WHY does precision not give skill points anymore? I don't want gold I want skill points. Not to have a completely negative review, I truly adore this game, i'm just upset that the game I loved so much did a complete 180 with this last update and not in a good direction.

_childDocuments_.review: It might look like it's trying to cash in on cheap eye candy, but the true colors of the game show through in the mechanics -- it's an authentic roguelike deckbuilder styled after Slay the Spire. I suspect some might say it cuts a bit  close to its inspiration, but while there are abundant very obvious similarities, each of the playable characters has decks and mechanics with more than enough difference from similar games to make them distinct. Personally, I enjoy both the graphics and the mechanics of Neoverse more than Slay the Spire itself (which really should be the case; the innovation was done by Slay the Spire and Neoverse is iterating on the concept). The addition of allowing you to see the entire "deck" each enemy is playing from allows for more strategy even when you're dealing with unfamiliar opponents, and the quest system allows you to pick an ongoing challenge with every encounter in the run, rewarding you for essentially meeting goals you partially get to customize yourself. I far prefer this to the ongoing progress systems in Slay the Spire.All that said, the one major issue I have with Neoverse is that the effects and icons can be so busy/flashy at times, it's actually hard to take in the important information. Slay the Spire has a simple but clean interface that communicates clearly. That is  the case here.If you're familiar with Slay the Spire and want a  similar game that's fun and well-made, this is an easy recommendation.If you're not familiar with Slay the Spire but like roguelike deckbuilders, this is still very easy to suggest checking out.Even if you're just into turn-based roguelikes in general, I still don't think this is a bad game to check out, but there are a lot of other options I'd sooner recommend once you get that into a genre that broad. Also, some of the mechanics may be harder to understand without playing Slay the Spire first, since it feels like there's more than a bit of assumed knowledge on the part of the developers. If you can get past that, there's very much still an enjoyable experience to be had here.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty alright; so far it feels like an easier slay the spire that sometimes has a decent difficulty spike just due to RNG (which is to be expected in a card game).Overall the different character decks, mechanics, and system seem to be rewarding.My main gripe is the game is having a bit of a "rocky" development it seems. As from patch to patch certain bugs get fixed/reintroduced. A supposedly common bug with the engine (haven't determined if its just unity or the game itself) but apparently it will have issues relating to your USB ports. This is odd as the system shouldn't interact with my USB ports in any way; but certain devices while plugged in will stop the game from launching (and when re-plugged in will crash it).At the current patch this is fixed which is why i'm able to give it a positive review now; but i'm concerned as this bug has been fixed before apparently.Hopefully this is fixed going forward as i've enjoyed the game so far and have been looking to play something after i've finished slay the spire.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Neoverse isn't a bad game but it also isn't a good one either so that makes it just mediocre. it's like slay the spire but a bit easier once you get the mechanics down so if you find that game hard this one maybe perfect for you.neoverse is a rogue-lite with no real story and only 3 girls to pick from and not at the same time so fights are 1vs1-4 but they do show what attack most enemies will use that turn. playing cards use action points where you start with 5 and use cards that cost 0-4 then once you run out you toss your hand in the discard pile and end your turn. you'll start a game with about 8 cards from 4 starting decks and you gain or lose more as you play (some mode may vary). the rogue-like elements come in as you die or beat the 10,15, 20 required fights (bosses on every 5th). if you die your run it over though if you beat a stage you will get some new abilities and cards tossed into your RNG pools. you'll get a random shop and ability tree that change every run plus you keep any trophies you get from bosses. there are also missions like use so many of X cards, block X damage, ect that give none permanent stuff when completed. as with any rogue-lite it comes in on the fights where they can be very unfair depending on your build killing your run.trying to unlock the extra items with trophies feels like a grind or you can just buy the dlc as each give you 100 trophies.there is a solid game here outside the girls but the grind for the unlockables without buying the dlc is a pain.5/10update: they no longer do rotating items in the trophy shop.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely recommended for fans of card battlers in the vein of Slay the Spire, this one does enough different to stand well on its own and looks great while doing it.+Good visuals for player, enemies, and backgrounds+3 heroes to choose from, each with 3-4 starting decks/classes+Hero items unlockable to change appearance and improve stats+Easy to play, controls work well and are rebindable+Runs can be completed in about 50 minutes+Good variety of enemies, bosses are fun+Tons of cards, different for each hero+Items and always-available shop add more variety+Skill points further customize heroes during a run+Good variety of difficulty options-Could benefit from even more heroes-Like many roguelikes, can get repetitive

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot to offer, and it is deep enough to keep my Magic the Gathering and Dominion riddled brain entertained. Basic thought of a deckbuilder is, that your strategic, round based battles are determined partially by drawing luck and strategic thinking about your hand cards and mana resource, partially by deciding, which cards to get in between battles. There are more systems in place, like consumables, skills, equipment and the combo meter. Some are unlocked, some are bought by ingame resources. No story whatsoever!One enemy in particular (roman soldier type) is unfair to ragequit levels, but everything else is well manageable, and even he isn't an ensured runkiller. Overall, I like most of what is here. If its price is ok, I don't know. But on Sale it is a competent deckbuilder single player experience.Follow my curator at

_childDocuments_.review: In the current state, the game is a rough diamond-There is plenty of potential, but also, plenty of room for improvements...Still, the presentation is a LOT better than in other games of the genre, and some mechanics, that i found lacking in STS, have been improved:If you play a card, you will instantly draw a new one (as long as there are cards in the draw pile),relics are not random anymore, but a permanent, random selection can be bought directly (as skills),you have five mana per turn,and before each stage, the player can choose between two modes: Weaker enemies, but lesser special rooms, or stronger enemies, but more special rooms. And finally, traders stay, and can be accessed between battles at will, dont refresh their stock, though, unless you spend a big amount of cash, or visit a new trader...Which reduces the randomness a lot, and grants the player a much better feeling of control and depth.Also, other than in STS, i have the feeling, that unlocking new cards and skills adds to the games depth, instead of reducing it...It really is amazing, how the devs took an existing concept, and keep refining it...If the game continues to grow and improve, Neoverse will become my personal standard for the genre...And even now, its a great game, that fans of the genre shouldnt miss!

_childDocuments_.review: To keep it short and sweet..If you have played and love Slay The Spire.. GRAB THIS GAME RIGHT AWAY!!If you haven't let me explain how the game works. It's a card building rogue-like game. You'll be drawing cards from your deck to battle enemies. You'll be doing runs ranging from 10-40 minutes depending on your skill and luck. You'll choose from 3 characters who start with their own 10 different cards that you can upgrade and add to. Every encounter whether it be a battle, elite battle, event, and shops are random every time.  I think the only thing that can hinder this game's rep is that it's extremely similar to Slay The Spire, but is that really a bad thing? One of my most favorite mechanics in this game is Skill Points. An awesome mix of skill and randomness that will definitely keep you hooked on until you unlock everything and master the mechanics. I'M ADDICTED.If you have any more questions about the game that I haven't answered here feel free to leave a comment on my Youtube Let's Look At of NEOVERSE and I'll reply as soon as I can! _childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying, I never ever in my life have played deckbuilding/rouge-like games like Slay the Spire. This is my first title. I'll list the pros and cons after my around 9 hours of experience (still yet to explore more).Pros:- Beautiful graphics with great animations and enemy design (not the most creative of naming for the monsters, you can obviously see its inspired by other titles).- Games does a great job explaining the mechanics, but it doesn't go into too details about combo whombo.- Different characters with each having their own 3 unique decks, making repetition a lot of fun.- Game runs smoothly on the highest settings with 60 FPS even on an old rig like mine.- The combos are super fun and you can immediately learn after few battles.- Since its rouge-like, each run is a new experience with random cards, so build your deck as you defeat battles or by completing missions during battles or from the shop.- There is a nice  skill system with unique combo to make your deck even more unique.Cons:- Some builds are more OP than others, and if you don't get lucky with the deck building, then GG just restart.- Some enemy bosses have annoying passives, the machine that keeps spawning pets after you reach 10 drawn cards.- Also, at higher difficulties a lot of enemies will be immune to your debuffing skills; radioactivity, making Agent Naya with radioactivity build useless unless you get rid of the immunity.- Game is very short, I finished it in 44 minutes after 3 runs. I would love if they expand on the story, probably add more levels to the normal "Adventure Mode", or worlds where you can choose which path to take.- Paths yes, it's random. The game does have different level branches, some take you to Gods realm, some to an Alien ship etc.. Unfortunately, you cannot choose that pathway, it's completely randomized.Yeah, I think I'll leave it here. I really like the game, I love the art-style and the combat mechanics. The game is a really good one for someone interested in trying Slay the Spire like games with nice anime graphics!I like it and definitely recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Presentation is very good, and mechanics are enjoyable. Compared to StS, it would be a less stressful and an easier experience. I would still recommend it because it's a good game when you just want to relax instead of praying RNJesus.As one negative review mentioned, you have a lot of (maybe too much) control over your deck, and you can often achieve almost any build you want to. The only thing that is not available very often is to remove cards to have a lean deck, but the difficulty overall doesn't make having a couple extra cards too punishing.This abundance of player agency can be seen as a negative, as the game is not as challenging nor punishing as its competitors. I also enjoyed their randomized skill tree system which is quite unique and an interesting idea, though you will be able to get any skill you want, since you can buy skill points at the shop and the shop itself can be reseted many times before it gets too expensive. Overall you are indeed showered with rewards, and finishing a run won't be much of a hassle in normal difficulty, even if you're new to the game.If you're feeling in a more casual mood and wanna play a relaxing game of cards, This game is quite an enjoyable experience and might be up your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: I CANNOT recommend this game enough. I played Slay the Spire quite a bit, but eventually you get tired of being screwed by RNG you couldn't have prepared or countered for. Neoverse takes every aspect of Spire and figures out how to make it more interesting and give you more control. And of course, more control comes with more challenge. Enemies are more aggressive and have more abilities to screw you than in Spire.It's in early access at the time of this review, and there are definitely some balancing issues. Shooting builds are wildly OP to the point where I managed to take on the final boss in the accelerated game mode, which consisted of 2 tough units and 2 boss units. I killed three of them on my first turn and brought one of the bosses down to 1/8 health, then had damage immunity for my next turn. Hopefully the balancing gets worked out because Neoverse just has so much to offer.Like Spire, it offers three characters with three class card pools and a common card pool, however the builds are more distinct here to the point where you get to choose your starting deck type, and the basic attacks and defends are not identical the way spire does it.I look forward to more gameplay additions and maybe an elongated mode, but even now there's so much enjoyment to be had.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for about an hour and watching some gameplay on YouTube, I feel as though I have a fairly good grasp on what this game currently has to offer. Because I feel that Slay the Spire is the most familiar of the deck-builder rogue-likes I am going to list comparisons with that title. There are probably more new mechanics that I failed to mention, but these were readily apparent to me. While these mechanics do mix up gameplay, they do have drawback. While the auto-draw system allows you to burn through your deck and kill weak enemies very quickly, it quickly trivializes many encounters (in the base game) and over-incentivizes adding cards to your deck. The limitation on shuffling means that you could set yourself up for a turn where you are unable to use all of your mana. The smaller your deck size, the more frequently you will encounter your issue. Unless you have cards that allow you to shuffle, this effectively punishes you for trimming your deck, which I find unappealing.In StS, all of the random events have personality. I have seen all of them, but because they appear randomly, they add variation to the gameplay. In Neoverse, I saw the same scene where a robot offers me the ability to perform one of two bonfire actions. Further, all of the loot in the game is a card plus two types of currency and possibly a consumable. Although you can use one form of currency to buy skills that offer benefits similar to relics, I felt like the rewards you get just had very little impact on gameplay. Because you pick your skills, I never felt like I was encouraged to develop different strategies. Because rewards are the same, I saw no need to play through epic fights or go to a treasure event or a random event.To me it seems like the logical progression could be (1) adding relics or another permanent buff as a reward for epic fights, treasure events, and random events, (2) shuffling mid-turn and removing shuffle cards, and (3) adding cosmetic equips (not outfits). Any one of these changes would lead to a substantial improvement of the game. Without these changes, I do not see myself playing the game again.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Between all of the pros listed below, this game has so much potential to be so, so good, but it honestly falls short in one minor way, and one critical way. I was originally going to get this for my friend's birthday in a few days, but I think I'll spare him.Pros-The love for Slay the Spire is there. I can see it in how the game piggybacks off of mechanics in STS.-Unlike in STS, you can continue a battle right where you left off, even down to how many action points you have left. Perfect if you want to jump in and play for ten minutes.-The graphics are high quality. Personally, I preferred the art style of STS, but to each their own, so I'll list it as a pro.-The mechanic to disincentivize going for a thin deck is interesting. The mechanic: although you draw a card after every card you play, you don't draw if there's no deck to draw from. Therefore, you're incentivized to go for a fatter deck so you have less "flat" turns.-The battle tech system is really quite unique. If you kill or block with just the right amount, you activate a tech. If you kill an enemy with 3HP left with an attack that does 3HP of damage, you get extra gold. If you block an attack that does 3HP of damage with 3 block, you parry the attack and stun the enemy. Furthermore, if you combo certain types of cards in a designated order, the next attack will do double damage.-The quests mechanic is also very cool. You get really good rewards if you accomplish some of the harder ones, such as "upgrade all cards of a certain type in your deck," which, going back to the fat deck, can be super good if you have a lot of cards to upgrade at once.-I was a little put off by the fact that you can buy stuff basically whenever you want, but since going for a fatter deck is better, along with how much gold you can potentially get, the store is actually quite balanced.-The skills system is really interesting too, and basically subs in for STS relics.-As is common with roguelites, succeeding in the game helps in future runs by unlocking new cards.-Character mechanics are interesting. I won't go too in depth, since this is already getting long-winded.*However,* personally, in spite of all of this praise I have for the game's systems, there are two things that really killed the game for me: the nerf of the lean deck, and consistent, uniform difficulty. First, I know I listed the disincentive against lean decks as a pro above, but this can be a con too. The reason lean decks are so strong is that they're much more consistent than fat decks. Nothing feels better than conquering a difficult game and becoming extremely powerful, and that is more difficult with tat decks, as there's a chance you'll get all attack cards when you need a defend card. Not a problem with a lean deck.Second, a lot of the enemies are honestly too easy. On my second playthrough ever, I got the achievement "Kept your starting HP during ten battles and won them." Some bosses are even too easy. Then you find ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Tulu, which is constantly spawning new enemies, that not only attack you, forcing you to use resources to defend, but also give Tulu buffs that increase its survivability and attack, all while it's passive breaks your defenses every turn, and it gets to amass its defenses every turn. Plus, it's not like attacking them will do anything, because the zombies die after five turns anyway, which will then heal Tulu for 10% of its HP, or give it passive armor without needing to defend.I seriously wanted to like this game. If the difficulty were more uniformly distributed, I could probably look past the disincentive against the lean deck. Right now, the easy enemies gas you up, then when you find something "real" (or even OP, I can't tell), it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ infuriating as ♥♥♥♥, leading to angry reviews like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: NEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: I played Slay the Spire and thought "I love this, but I can't wait for more games like this to come out that are better." Neoverse is a step in that direction. The graphics and style are cool. There's an interesting grab bag of styles in the game, which I suspect was done to take as much advantage of diverse art talent as possible. It could be weird, but since story isn't really a think, it works, and provides refreshing variety. Also, all three playable characters are hot chicks, which is a plus.The gameplay is solid. There are at least two main playstyles per class, and it's easy to form preferences. There is a decent variety of enemies that present different challenges. I do feel that some cards, mechanics, and enemies are not well balanced, but I also might just suck. After a dozen hours of play, even if it turns out they are just broken, I still got my money's worth trying to figure it out. The Early-Access-ness is no issue at all. It's already worth your money. There's some nitpicky text and UI things they should fix, and probably some balance to do. And of course more content would be cool. But the game is easily ready to go for this price point. Biggest complaint: Randomness is to be expected in the cards you're presented with, but I don't like how there's so much randomness in the system to purchase passive skills. The passives can make or break your deck, but to get them, you only have a limited set of choices and a big wall of complete randomness. All in all, it's very easy to recommend this game. If you're at all interested in any sort of roguelike deckbuilder, then it's a no brainer.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game from humble bundle... I say that because of what happens next. I like to open the games I get from humble bundle and play for a few moments so I can see what the game is all about. I fully expected to not like it because it just doesn't fit the mold of any kind of game I like. I hate turned based RPG's, I hate card games, and am really not a fan of deck builders. The odds were not good. I opened the game and next thing you know I had been playing for an hour and was really enjoying myself. The game is really good about introducing new concepts slowly so that you understand what's going on - almost to an annoying degree. At first I did get a bit annoyed by all of the tips, but I was able to quickly forgive that as they go away as soon as you acknowledge them.I can't put a finger on why I like it, but I think it's the simplicity and elegance. This game doesn't try to do everything, it just tries to do one thing well which is great turn based battles with interesting mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: It hass less rng when compared to Slay the Spire. Some people say it makes the game too easy but I actually prefer having a bit more control since there is still rng involved anyway and the higher Transcended levels are still hard.It is kind of easy (still not on the highest Transcended levels though) after you finish it enough times to buy equippable items that help you on the future runs. Some of them are so good that they disable scoring though but you can use them and still get achievements. Best example is the extra skill points that would normally cost you hundreds/thousands of gold to buy which would be like 5-20 extra encounters cleared (total cost of those skill points otherwise depends on multiple things like shop reset count, skills, Transcended level etc.).There's also a lot of cards that you'll quickly realize to be just useless and some that are really good. Also just like in StS, it's often better to just skip the card reward.There are some balance issues between cards, the characters and their skills. Also some builds are just painfully slow even if they are really good. Every character also has a daily deck that is often a lot better than any of the default starting decks so that's usually when I go for the highest level of Transcended (15).One big difference is that you always keep drawing until draw pile is empty. Usually it makes things easier but sometimes it can mess you up if your draw pile is exactly the amount of cards you draw so you won't be drawing more cards and it also won't be reshuffled until your next turn.There's also three important extra mechanics: precision, combo and perfect block.Precision gives you extra gold if your damage is exactly enough to kill off the enemy. I mostly like it but it does sometimes waste a bit of time setting up when really trying to maximize the gold gain from it.Combo means playing cards in a certain order (by card type) and being rewarded with double damage on next attack if you do it. Combo is a randomly selected order of card types, 3-5 cards, and it resets and its randomized again if you don't play it in the order shown. I like combo system since I can just do it if the random order works for me and I can ignore it if it doesn't and then see if the new order is better.Perfect block happens when your remaining block is exactly the same as what the enemy is trying to damage you for and it stuns the enemy for 1 turn. With some cards/decks you can often get it and sometimes you might get it accidentally when not even calculating for it but mostly I didn't pay too much attention to it as I didn't feel the need to.I see people complaining about the English translation but I've never had any trouble understanding the descriptions and mechanics. Also didn't see any typos or bad grammar. Most I saw was just a word or two that could have been replaced with something better but they were still understandable.Most of my hours were before they added a lot things in though so everything I wrote might not be completely correct anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and challenging card battling game. This is one of the card games where I didn't had to worry about bad RNG draw, because the game is designed on 99% strategic thinking. It's simple and graphically very charming. There's no story but the gameplay alone makes up for it. There are 3 classes to play from, each having their unique battle style. The sword girl relies on shooting, shield girl relies on healing, and the priest girl relies on guardians. The classes are all well-balanced. Personally, I found priest girl to be easiest to play with, her white beast guardian is really strong. With shooting girl you've to manage overheat a lot. The shield girl's battle style is a little weird, she is based on 'vampire style' (healing + damaging) decks which doesn't really suit a shield user, but it does work nonetheless. Overall a solid and flexible card game.
