_childDocuments_.review: An exceptional SRPG which has a couple of frustrating battles. It's a really strong recommendation for fans of the genre, and one of the more unique offerings as well. While certain stylistic influences are apparent at times, this game is a true original. This can be very refreshing if you're sick of games like Dark Deity or Fell Seal which are content to completely copy existing franchises (FE and Tactics Ogre respectively).Aside from the very-occasional difficulty spike, there are only two minor criticisms I have with Fae Tactics: the lack of a dialogue skip (which can get annoying for repeating battles or doing a NG+), and the sometimes sketchy translation. Apostrophes tend to find themselves in places where they shouldn't be... meanwhile, commas tend to find themselves noticeably absent from some places where they should be. But when that's all the negative stuff I can say about the game, it's pretty clear that I've found a real gem.Perhaps the most refreshing aspect of Fae Tactics was its level of challenge. Way too many SRPGs err on the side of being too easy. Fae Tactics isn't afraid to throw you some battles which force you actually think. And this is a very good thing, even if a small handful of these battles end up being a little bit frustrating. Fae Tactics isn't grind-based, either; monsters will scale with your level, so you can't simply grind your way to victory unlike in badly-designed SRPGs such as Mercenaries Saga or God Wars. Fae Tactics certainly understands that STRATEGY RPGs should have STRATEGY in them. Again, a very good thing!Characters are fairly well-designed too, with creative gimmicks to distinguish each other. Some can tank, others are long-ranged snipers, and others are hybrid support/ranged attackers. There's a certain degree of customization, too: you can equip different scrolls and weapons, and you can also level up characters' stats in 3 categories, sort of like in XCOM. Yet, customization is not COMPLETELY open-ended to the point that every unit can do everything. This is also a good thing as far as SRPGs are concerned; what's the fun in playing a strategy game where every unit is the same?Fae Tactics has got quite a few hidden secrets, too. Boss fights that can only be found on certain days, extra dialogue options, extra items, etc. Maybe I'll have to replay this one at some point.All in all, a modern-day classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Fae Tactics was an abusive relationship for me in the early hours of the game. I fell in love with it almost immediately and I was having a blast until I hit a difficulty spike that just beat my cheeks into the dirt. It was extremely frustrating but I kept going back for more and I didn’t know why. I really wanted to blame the game for my failures but I knew deep down that was not the case. Fae Tactics is challenging and refuses to pull its punches but it gives you everything you need to succeed. Nearly every fight seems one-sided, with the odds weighed heavily against you, but between the multitude of different units and spells at your disposal, there was always a way to readjust your strategy, even if that meant stepping out of your comfort zone. There are major differences between this title and the obvious comparison it will have to the Final Fantasy Tactics sub-series. The customization isn’t as deep as FF Tactics but it makes up for that with the nuance in its battle system. Fae Tactics’ strength lies in the simplicity of its presentation and although it gives short tutorial messages in the beginning, it absolutely will not hold your hand and I feel as if this encourages constant experimentation. The story was surprisingly good and that was something I didn’t realize until about half way through. At first, it seems to be your standard fantasy story but there are quite a few dark moments and good twists that really shocked me and it was well worth it to pay attention to all the dialogue.All in all, I had a great time with this title and was tempted to play through it again with my new game+ file but I have a long backlog of other titles to catch up on.Video review: The Good:+Story+Battles+Character Roster+StrategyThe Bad-One frustrating boss fight in particular

_childDocuments_.review: I would be careful with getting this game. Valdis story was an amazing game, so I was pretty excited to see this game. My buddy picked it up for me and I'll get back to giving this a fair shot soon but it doesn't scratch any itch. It pretty much feels like one of those free phone games, everything is done with the same button, and I'm waiting for them to sell me crystals to buy more characters.At the time of this brief blurb, I'm 6 hours in and there is no story pertaining to your character. No direction at all. I've met 2 unique NPCs and one of them ended up in my party. No talking about joining, just opened my party window and bam he is there. Your starting companions are mute, your main character might as well be. We are on the grand adventure to fix our bike, which is what gates the game on where you can travel. The story might get better but it starts off horribly.The combat is strange. You have 1 move for support, attack and waiting. Each element of monster seems to share some abilities, so that cuts down a bit of the abilities. You can eventually unlock super mode and I really dislike how it works. You store up charges from almost every action. This includes getting attacked. That means the bosses who tend to be a bit of walking meat bags now have large aoe moves that can sometimes ohko you but mostly does a large portion of your health. When you "kill" a boss they go into a countdown phase in which any ally can revive them by touch OR any magic, which when you get a map with 4 bosses on there, they can run some sandbagging + revive with a special and take their turn right away. It has not caused me to lose any battle yet since the AI itself only reacts when you get in range. Later there might be better ways of dealing with this but it needlessly drags out battles. Small annoyance for me is that the movement range of characters is very low. Maps aren't HUGE but a movement of 2 is just silly. You can have a character that buffs people with more movement and that is a lot of fun spending 5 turns and one slot for a unit to make characters move normally.  Some good ideas but really lacking polish.The biggest thing is there is no view info button. They have many terms that are highlighted but no ability to actually check it out. I really am not a big fan of having to look up every interaction due to language. I'll give this game some more care later on but right now, I'm hoping this game is in it's beta stage and will get fleshed out to be a decent game.

_childDocuments_.review: If this game got rid of level scaling it would be almost certainly an immediate recommended. Doubly so if they also got rid of the randomness.There's a lot to like about the game. I played it a fair bit and enjoyed it until the cracks started to appear and the randomness and scaling began to really hit hard. The sheer tankiness (along with endless regeneration of health and mb) of basically all enemies I was encountering after level 18/20 or so really made this game super difficult in not fun ways.The worst thing was I realised had the exact same monster summoned with no mb shield and they'd take 2 hits from normal enemies and die while the opponent's one would get 3 hits from my team. And if there's some of the tankier monsters prepare for an utter slog, especially when the maps restrict movement to the point backstabs etc become near impossible without flying units.Not giving arcane enemies an elemental weakness was a massive flaw.I missed a thing and was doing a bunch of story missions that are 3 swords some with skulls. Then went to 1 sword story missions (no idea what this actually means I assume 3  with skulls is harder  than one with no skulls) and these missed early story mission are absurdly hard. As far as I can tell exp isn't shared so lesser characters can be left to languish.There's story missions that are a linked set of mission that you can't quit, so another story mission and come back to later.Also levelling up is poor. You get a few more tools but compared to the level scaling it doesn't match up. You can't grind to do better, you can only really grind for random drops. Random drops make improving your character/set up etc much harder than it should be.

_childDocuments_.review: There are plenty of reviews going over the nitty gritty of the game, I just want to chime in and say as someone who's been looking for something that scratches that FFT itch, this game has been the closest to doing just that. While similar in only the most  basic sense, Fae Tactics has an identity all it's own. It's very story light, and everything is built for speed. While not as deep as some tactics game out there, it still has plenty to consider between battles and during. The sprite work is stellar, and the music fits beautifully. There are some oversights in design, such as unclear skills/abilities and attributes, and the inability to save between multi-stage story encounters, but the overall package is worth more than $20 in my opinion. An absolute buy for any tactics fan, especially if you've always wanted to just smash your party against the enemy with just a dusting of story.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could have given a positive review on this, but given that the final boss is impossible to beat (max level characters, summons, fire weapons, characters, etc.) I can't recommend this.The final boss summons mana pylons every other turn, and they transport unless you can 1 hit them. Oh, and they're out of reach for the first few rounds so boss gets 175+ def before you even get close enough. Then he builds his ultra so fast you can't keep up on hunting down enemies.His grip can 1 hit all my characters and if I don't have protector on every....single....turn I'm screwed.If I don't try to keep all the enemies from throwing their 4-6 spot attacks and wiping out my team, the boss just summons more pylons.I was playing this on Easy, and im no slouch to Tactics games (I've beaten FFT more times than I can count, including hidden dungeon). Devs, I suggest looking into the mechanics of the final boss and attempt to beat it without having any of the hidden characters.

_childDocuments_.review: + quite good mechanics mostly dependent on buffs, crits dependent on elements (everyone has one), verticality, reflects and generally a lot going on+ characters with different stats and passives feel very different+ each character can be buffed or cursed with only one effect at a time, so you have to manage that + sometimes genuinely difficult+/- your characters have to stay close all the time to resurrect each other+/- various bonus exp for "flawless" fights - great in theory, but in practice it gives less experience for harder fights, eventually giving you effectively nothing+/- enemies at the back have a tendency to be passive and buff each other waiting for you - if it takes you too long they become much harder to deal with+/- vertical levels - always important to look at it and gives a great bonus, but on the other hand enemies generally start from high ground and often one-shot your characters- this one became a complete game-breaker as time went on - does not respect my time. This includes slow combat (speed can be set up to 2x, which is not nearly enough), no cutscene skips, AI that is defensive for half of the fight slowly buffing each other on their end of the map (seems like it is specifically design to do that - if they were aggressive the fights would become impossible in many cases) and the resurrection mechanic (leaders have to be kicked when down multiple times, otherwise they will resurrect - e.g.  five attacks in three turns and most characters can only attack once per turn)- some enemies (mostly bosses) have multi-attacks, which can insta-kill you and then you basically cannot win afterwards (you only have three leaders and up to three summons, which are much weaker, so you cannot afford to lose people)- no friendly fire, so enemies can spam powerful AoE with no repercussions - it also could've made the game quicker, but it seems to be against the design?- uneven difficulty - some fights are a breeze and some are very hard especially on bosses (if any of your leaders fall during a boss fight then you instantly lose the fight - why add this mechanic? I guess you are effectively doomed in this case, but not always so why make it even more infuriating?)- and when you realize that the boss is too hard and want to go back to world map then guess what - you will have to go though the same 2~ maps again to get to the boss! and look at the same enemies doing their dance in their corner of the mapI wanted to like it, but I've had enough.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I just walked through my apartment pacing and trying to figure out if there was anything expendable enough laying around that I would be okay with smashing it into little pieces after attempting the same stage in this game 4 times in a row.  I determined the hasty answer to be 'no' and sat back down and decided to right up this review instead.Here's a bit of background info about myself and tactical RPGs.  I've dumped HUNDREDS of hours into Final Fantasy Tactics and Tactics Ogre: Let us Cling Together.  Successfully accomplishing virtually every challenging thing those games had to offer.  Along with many Fire emblems and other similar tactical RPGs, it's one of my favorite genres.  I feel I'm pretty good at them.Now, there are certainly aspects of this game that I enjoy and can appreciate when it comes to differences from other TRPGs.  However, I am petty right now and just want to list the things about the game that piss me off.1.  The enemy levels keep pace with your own group regardless of whether it's a story mission or a grind map.  While this may not bother everyone and even excite some, this completely kills the option of grinding to get ahead.  I would rather see players be allowed to create their own challenge by choosing not to grind.  I don't think the option to get ahead should be removed.2.  You are limited to 3 'heroes' (one of which is locked in the party, at least where I'm at in the game) and get a certain amount of summon slots to summon pokemon type fae creatures that all have different summon values.  These summons mostly all suck and die quickly.  You tend to only get 2 or 3 and if they die, they die for the rest of the fight.  The enemies on the other hand, tend to have about 8-10 of these things in addition to being able to summon new ones almost constantly.  You also get to choose 3 'spells' to equip that all have various cooldowns based on their power levels which is an interesting feature but then again, so do the enemy leaders.  Oh also, if your main chick gets knocked out, it prevents your usage of spells.3.  Hero characters can be revived when downed by healing spells or just any character that can click on them.  The problem is that the enemy leaders work the same way.  Both your heroes and the enemy leaders need to be hit several extra times while downed to actually be removed from the map.  Guess which side has the massive advantage here?  Not only do they often have over a dozen units compared to your 5 or 6, but they also have healing spells that can res an enemy anywhere on the map.  You can technically win by just knocking out all the leaders, but they are often pretty spread out and prioritize spells and unit actions to get their leaders up off the floor.  Oh, at least where I'm at in the game, the leader enemies have 2-300 health and 2-300 mana barrier.  My tankiest characters is my dog with like 160ish HP.  Have fun trying to smack an unconscious baddie 4-6 times to remove him from the map before he gets woken up and punches your guys in the crotch.4.  This game uses elemental strengths and weaknesses as the main crux of the combat, but my elementally stronger units still get 2 shot by theirs.  Not to mention you are at a numbers disadvantage anyways and you don't know what elements are going to be summoned in until you've tried out a map.  5.  The RNG in this game is a joke.  Does missing an enemy that has an 8% evade rate twice in a row sound fun to you?  Get used to it.  You figure on using lots of negative status effects (curses) on the enemy to proceed to victory?  Will rarely ever stick on them.  They will stick on you, though.   even if it does, there are so many enemies at any given time that they constantly cleanse negative effects.6.  This game loves locking you into 2-3 fight scenarios where you cannot exit to the main map until you've completed them all.  This happened occasionally in TO/FFT but this game LOVES THEM.  Failing on the third fight because its manned by some boss even stronger than the other enemy leaders you've been facing?  Figure it out because if you back out you lose all progress on the previous stages you got through.7.  This game's plot is about as rudimentary as it gets.  It's amazing to me that in a genre that has always excelled on storytelling for the most part, a lot of these new age TRPGs have no real depth to them in that department.I'm sure there are more things to rant about, but I'll stop there.  If you want an overly difficult tactical role playing game where the deck is virtually always massively stacked against you, then have at it, you masochist.  I like being able to brute force grind past the wall of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in these types of games and this game won't let you do that. This game ain't FFT/TO or even Fire Emblem.  It has some cool ideas going for it while gleefully watching you having to redo maps over and over, causing you to call virtually every enemy leader a '♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥' about 15 maps in.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I found combats to be quite interesting. I started playing on the Hard mode and bosses have REALLY required interesting strategies.There are things I like and things I dislike though, I wouldn't call it "my favorite tactical RPG" but it is a fun little game and haven't completed it yet with 25 hours of gameplay. Short thoughts...Graphics (6/10): They are just okay but honestly imo this barely matters for my enjoyment.Classes/Characters (7.5/10): Overall I feel the characters are unique and fun. Basically every character has an attack/wait skill/support/ex/ultimate skill. By far one of the most unique systems I have seen in a long time. Sadly even though it is super unique I much prefer TRPGs like FFT/Fell Seal.Strategy Required (9/10): I think the best part of the game is how interesting some boss fights have been. This is probably partly because of the unique limited abilities characters have.In Game Help (5/10): A lot of mechanics aren't really explained and enemies take some playing to figure out what is going on sometimes.Story: (7/10): Again this isn't really important to me but the story is just "ok". I think I have played too many video games since most storylines feel bland to me. Overall (8/10): I feel it is a good game overall mainly because I found the combats to require interesting strategies. Nothing is worse than playing a game where combats require 0 strategy.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10 ~Strongly recommend You play as Peony, a mysterious young girl that wields magic and attempts to help and/or befriend anyone she can due to unresolved past trauma. As a person somewhat unfamiliar with the wide world, you slowly uncover why everything/everyone has gone afoul. Really fun tactics game. Very cute and endearing, but there are definitely lots of dark themes throughout. This is a HARSH world (trigger warnings for cartoonish murder, torture, abandonment).So far over 40 hours and still not at an obvious ending, but I'm assuming another ~10 hours depending on if I attempt all side quests/unlockables.Age recommendation 14+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Pros and cons, some minor spoilersPositives:-All but 1 or 2 of the main characters I really enjoyed. Thematically, they are all really fun to play.-Similar to Final Fantasy Tactics with some rock/paper/scissors/shotgun/lightning elemental properties, kinda pokemon like in that way, but only ~9 party members and ~35 summons/pets. -Story moments are really interesting/intriguing. Heart wrenching and heart warming moments abound.-Animations and Art style overall is greatNegatives (least to greatest):-Music gets a little stale-Some of the combat interactions are unintuitive and unexplained until they happen-With a few bad combos, things go south suddenly-Many of the battles are really long and drawn out, but not in a strategic way-The majority of the story is not particularly linear and very wide/spread out instead of long, some describe it as episodic. This leaves the story to unravel overtime as plots start and stop without much warning. Ultimately, the worst part about this is you have to play without stopping or you will probably forget characters, locations, etc-I wish the main character had more than one facial expression, or at least was drawn with her mouth closed, rather than agape (this is the thing I dislike the most about the game, which is not a huge deal, mostly a missed opportunity)

_childDocuments_.review: So I picked this game up because of the ludicrously high user review score and because the art looked cute and I love tactical RPGs. I was intrigued at how something that looked so mechanically simple could have such a high user score. Well, 38 hours later, now I know.What a ride! I don't know who these developers are or how much of the gameplay is original or cribbed from other sources, but despite the simplicity of a lot of the game mechanics they work together beautifully and the experience never once felt shallow to me. It gives you a lot of options and tools and makes you think about how you use them... to an extent. I didn't really grind and though there were a couple challenging encounters most of the game felt pretty easy. I don't remember whether or not I selected a difficulty, but if I did it was the middle option.I want to keep this review short, so here are my bullet points:* Extremely addictive and satisfying gameplay* Likeable characters and a fun story with a few really good moments* Mechanics are simple to pick up but allow diverse options, never feel shallow* Normal difficulty probably too easy for tactics game veterans* First (blind) playthrough was 38 hours. I would estimate I saw about 70-80% of the content in that time.Tl;dr - Very, VERY easy game to recommend to anyone who likes tactical RPGs. Well done to the developers!

_childDocuments_.review: This game rules. The art style's great. The mechanics are tight. I think the reason some people don't like it is they expect they can pick a core team, build them how they want, and use them in every fight. This... isn't the case.The type chart determines what crits, so you have to change your team based on the enemy makeup. The game is clearly designed around this, as it lets you completely respec everything and change who's in your party after you get to see the map. I got my butt kicked a lot early game as I was figuring all that out.The one thing I wish was less of a factor was the day of the week. An element gets buffed based on what day it is, and that means fights can be way easier or way harder without a ton you can do about it other than coming back later. That is pretty easy to do for most of the game. You have like 5 story quests active at any given time so if you realize you walked into a fire boss on a fire day, you can just return to map and go fight some earth enemies. The one exception is the final boss, who locks you into the day after getting the last macguffin. So watch out for that.There are some missable characters and weapons, so if you're the type of person who wants all of those I'd suggest looking up a guide (the one by Senzai3 is excellent).I love this game. I hope it gets a sequel. The epilogue designs for everyone go too hard for them to be trapped with one single image.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first bought Fae Tactics I was expecting and almost cutesy game, maybe a little awkward too with some strange mechanics, instead what I ended up with was a game that did indeed have some cute elements to it but also ended up living up to the term Fae, fairy tales are often actually rather dark in the past, oft with creatures that we all too often consider cute or funny looking in modern day tales but are in fact rather deadly creatures, although it has it's happy moments this game is filled with adversity but an adversity with purpose to it rather than just lot's of bad for the sake of it, that's as much as I'll say but it makes for an almost haunting story dood.But enough about the story aspects, as much as they shockingly ended up one of my favourite aspects of it out of nowhere but let's talk gameplay, this game has been the first game in many years that has had me fully invested in how it plays, it handles elements mostly nicely although I admit there were two elements so to speak that needed more love and made two particular characters difficult to play as but for the most part they make up for that with two other unique weapons for the leaders, talking about leaders you have three units, the protag Peony (who is precious) and two other characters to take into battle but is that all? nope! you have one of two main mechanics in the game too dood!The first main mechanic is Fae summoning, you use cards to summon Fae, depending on what you chose as your birth date you get certain unique one's to start off with along with an elemental boost to that element too (I was Salmon lol) you use them as units in battle and choose their elements accordingly to take on the opponents, you unlock more by defeating units on the map and hoping they drop their card, (quick tip use weaknesses to get the cards easier) the second thing is magic cards! now these are rather interesting as they have a variety of uses from healing, buffing, dealing damage and even a few rather interesting utility spells, a lot of which are unlocked from treasure chests in a map only so keep an eye out for those or lose out!? well until new game plus anyway doodThe battles are grid based with a myriad of mechanics to them such as water, units that swim and get buffed in water. units that fly, units that dig underground, units that teleport, all useful traits that allow units to travel in a myriad of ways and avoid some rather nasty issues such as drowning, (because there's a push mechanic) falling into pits, fall damage from heights and even how much damage you do from a birdseye view which I've seen go up to a 275% damage boost myself during play but I can see it going higher with a certain character, there are even environmental hazards that effect both you and the enemies which I highly appreciate in any game myself dood.Let's talk more about units a sec, I like this system, leader units have their normal health but also if they fall down a pit or are taken down they have a secondary health bar, if that's depleted they retreat, you only get a game over if all three units die unless they are killed in an important fight it's a game over for even losing one leader, there are no penalties for losing Fae units but they don't get the extra health bar so with a small exception if they fall down a pit due to an enemy or hazard say bye bye dood!Level designs are nice and varied with some great visuals at times with suitable soundtrack to go with each level/area and such, it really made the moments in certain scene's stand out for sure, there are a decent amount of maps at that too, to add enemies level based on how many chapters you do or so I've been told, I prefer this to the typical enemies level with you as it give you the chance to grind if you need to which I never found you did as long as you got how to play dood.Right next up is slots, you have three, first is your weapons which I mentioned, second is scrolls, now these are fun as they have a lot of uses and effects that can make some fight easy as anything suffice to say one character I had felt pretty much immortal for the final boss fight which was hilarious to me they range from buffing your leader unit specifically with a unique effect or even buffing the whole team based on element and finally even some debuff effects for enemies, the third slot are gems, they do similar things but let's just say they are much more difficult to acquire and will become available later in the game, you can't miss it dood. Okay so some gripes I had with the game to finish up, I almost hate myself for bringing them up because it's such a good game but hey what games perfect really? so lets see, the first is one I mentioned earlier and that's two elements in particular, one just has no Fae units with that element, even if they had like three piddly small fae it would have made up for it but sadly nope! it's reserved for like four leader units you have of which you can only take three at a time, this makes the lightning scrolls not only not needed but also hard to get as usually you get scrolls of elements based on enemies with that element, the second is non elementals, I bet you're thinking "No weaknesses? that's awesome!...isn't it?" well the answer is a resounding no sadly, with how defence seems to work and such normal damage is too much if you get hit by more than one unit which sadly with the movement range and attack range of some units will happen a whole lot, this is bad for one unit as it's main skill is to protect others and there is sadly no cancel function which let's you just wait and the other unit despite having range is a glass canon that lacks enough canon to be all that useful outside of specific shaped maps, it really made it strained to use them outside of story levels where you are forced to, which is a shame because they are both great characters in their own right dood.Then there are the magic damage spells later in the game lose any real use as the damage it says on the card is lowered based on enemy resistance and even worse enemies can dodge spells too, granted the player is afforded this boon too but it certainly makes them rather useless compared to the games start where they are almost too powerful funny enough, that said buff and utility cards never go out of use and some attack cards can at least have different uses such as lowering defence or tangling enemies and such so it's not all bad dood.Okay back to good stuff to finish off! so each unit has unique effects to them, whether it's starting with a special buff such as never missing or getting stat boosts for ally units of the same element, heck even unique Fae traits such as going stealth which is usually something unique to a single element and usually has to be cast on a unit itself, even the way some attack are fantastically unique and allow for some interesting combat scenarios that can make a fight much easier if you're smart about it, the variety and how the game almost makes you use that variety or get severely punished for it is honestly great in my eyes and how a strategy RPG should be dood. To finish I just want to say there are many types of players out there, some will find this hard as heck, other will find it a breeze, both I have seen mock the game for it, now granted they made some fixes to it I hear since the beginning for balance but even so whether it's too easy or too hard, one should ask is the game good? the answer is yes, very much so if you are into good SRPG's don't let pro's or salty amateur's sway your judgement as to whether you buy this game or not, instead get past the (rather difficult) tutorial of a beginning and get a feel for yourself, give this treasure of a game a chance because it really does deserve it and has become one of my personal favourite games of all time for doing so much right and truly keeping me my eyeballs gorilla glued to the screen all the way through dood (please send help)

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. A lot. I played the demo, I was happy and quite excited for it to be released. And I still thing this game is 100% worth playing. The game overall is fantastic and entertaining. I don't think there's a need to say "If you liked FF Tactics you will like this game", the trailer, the pictures, other reviews will be more than enough to hammer that point in. There is, however, a major balancing problem with this game, which is why, for now, I am reviewing this game negatively.The enemies scale up as your characters and summons level up, but, the stats your party and summons gain are far, FAR too underwhelming and at a certain point, meaningless once you get past lvl 20. I am stuck fighting a super boss (Pazuzu) in the mines. Not only his BASE HP is 4202, he gains stats almost every single turn. My summons get ravaged with one of his 30% chain ranged magic attacks (30% that feels like 100%, as not only it NEVER misses, it ALWAYS hits at the very least, 3 of my units). He uses "Sandstorm" as his Ultra Attack (which hits every single one of my units TWICE), there are two mana totems at opposite sides of the map. The fact you are limited to 3 spellcards - and no "extra summons" - while the boss NOT ONLY can summon enemies very quickly but can also just cause massive damage as it pleases, alongside the fact the mobs surrounding him will instantly rush (and get to him on Turn 2) to buff him endlessly makes this battle impossible to win. It doesn't matter if you have 3 healing magic cards, 3 damage magic cards, 3 protecting party members, 5 ranged party members, anything!It doesn't matter whether you had a "perfect food mini game" for extra stats or whether you've crafted all the items in the Crafting menu, you just can't do anything against him as more and more mobs are summoned, and you can't keep your health above "sure death" line.Whether you grind or not, the AI enemies will always level up with you, and even harmless mobs become overpowered overtime. It doesn't matter what equipment you have, you will be thrashed. In some cases, yeah you can admit that *maybe* you've made a tactical blunder and that you need to redo the battle with a different approach - I like this component of the game, it's a tactics game after all. But the game outright punishes you as you are always handicapped to "Only 3 Spells" "only 3 Units" "only 3 summons" per battle, all the while the enemy bosses have 8+ mobs around them, the ability to summon as many mobs as they please and some bosses even having self-buffs that make their ATK and DEF go way, way above 200+ within 2 or 3 turns, before you even have the chance of reaching them.And this Pazuzu battle is just *one* of many battles where the glaring balancing issues are visible. I do hope the developer addresses this very soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Partial review based on a few days of play: after 15 hours the game is still putting out new mechanics, new ways of tackling battles and setting up your team, while constantly expanding on the map, sidequests and general content. What might initially seem a very limited gameplay system gradually opens up in meaningful and engaging ways: customization starts with basic stats allocation and ends up with altering passive traits, attacks modes, reaction skills and many more; the combat itself evolves by introducing new resources and providing multiple ways to expend them, such as costly all-out attacks or less expensive single-use augmentations. Elemental affinities, barriers and the way they affect buffs and debuffs seems interesting at first and soon proves itself to be a system very well put together, adding layers of depth to an already engaging core gameplay. Lastly, while "fast" is not a term that usually pairs well with tactics, in my opinion it doesn't feel like a slow game at all: battles do last a while, mainly due to low movement distance (which is required for balance), but the action itself feels quick thanks in particular to snappy animations,While the gameplay is clearly the focus here, I'm also finding some enjoyment in the story, with likable characters (a bit gimmicky in personality, but it's fun to see their interactions) and an adventure unfolding gradually in many directions while the player explores a menu-based map and discovers new subplots, leading to events, battles and rewards.For full disclosure I want to point out that in its launch state the game suffers from some bugs, including crashes, but the devs are on the ready fixing them as soon as they are reported, and have already released a few patches in the span of days.Fae Tactics is a highly recommended game for any fan of the tactics genre and I want to applaud Endlessfluff Games for both innovating many mechanics and delivering a staggering amount of content with an engaging pace that constantly hypes up the excitement and the desire to master the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fae Tactics is probably the best SRPG I've played outside of Fire Emblem (I like 3-10), Final Fantasy Tactics (Advanced and A2), and various FE fangames. SMT Devil Survivor gets an honorable mention. I am a fan of the genre, but there are a lot of games I just couldn't stomach. Things like Phantom Brave, Disgaea, newer Fire Emblem, Agarest, and Stella Glow to name a few, just never felt right for various reasons. Generally, if I am playing a SRPG I want exactly that, not a strategy game or a RPG. This is a bit of a lengthy intro, but I hope it gives you an idea of what I like and what I don't.Fae Tactics checks all of the boxes of what I like in a SRPG. I like how positioning units feels like it really matters. There are many mechanics that present real choices because sometimes tight formations are better while other times it is better to spread out. The game mechanically is more similar to Final Fantasy Tactics, but manages to add some complexity, while not making things confusing. I like the writing overall. The plot isn't perfect, but I would say I feel the main points feel really satisfying. I think the key is the character interactions really bring out their personality. The script doesn't seem that long, but it manages to do justice to each character's story and makes the bonds between this group of misfits shine. One thing I liked during my second playthrough was using different characters to see different dialogue. The art is also stylized fantastically.Some minor complaints include that a completionist run really requires 2 playthroughs and some help. Some of the missable things are a bit odd, but I think it is a minor bug that really doesn't affect the playability, just 100% ability. The standard game speed is a bit slow, but the 2x speed in the options makes it much better. I wish some of the information on game mechanics was better organized and more available. There are tool tips, but they are only available during loading screens and are random in those screens. Overall, I love Fae Tactics and I'm super glad I played it. If you are a fan of SRPGs this is a definite must play.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never beat a TRPG before as I didn't used to be interested in them but I wanted a new challenge, and that's what I got. The battle system is a lot of fun but I wish there was a better option to speed the animations up more or have effects activate at all targets at the same time instead of having to watch an animation for each character effected.  I'd also like an option to save between battles as they can get quite lengthy and when you do them back to back, it can seem a bit much.  Maybe that's part of the challenge though because I could be making better battle choices.So far I'm around day 80 in game and fortunately it looks like I still have quite a bit left while clocking in around 38 hours real time.  The game gives you a lot to think about and I find it enjoyable.  Also it plays great on my GPD Win Max even when I turn the TDP down to 15 Watts to save battery power.*edit*I have beat the game clocking in slightly over 55 hours.  Its been a lot of fun and I think I'll start a second playthrough perhaps on hard mode this time.  I look forward to seeing more from this developer.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit2: Very fun, just play it on normal. It's a little easy on normal, but hard mode is not worth it.Edit: Game mellows out significantly once you have more strategic diversity, but it's still very punishing at times. The early game is *rough* because you can't adjust your strategy, and the game expects you to anyway. Also, kudos to the devs for getting so many patches out so fast! The AI changes were very helpful, and they're no longer impossible to keep alive (health got quadrupled for most of them, and they're less suicidal). Game is very fun but also frustrating. If that's for you, I recommend it. Otherwise, I do not.Note that all of this is for the early game, and if you do end up playing, I strongly recommend normal mode because hard mode swings wildly between "very easy" and "very unfair," and if you get caught by the unfair side, you will lose several hours of story progress, including all xp and items gained since your most recent return to "town."1) On hard mode, all attacks deal at least half your units' health, and about half one-shot kill your non-tank unit. No, that is not an exaggeration. I cleared through the first "no retreat boss," and at this very early point in the game, NPC enemies have nearly twice as much attack power as your units of the exact same type. When units die, it's usually because they are weak to the enemy, but there's not a lot you can do about it because you have to take the same three units into every level. One of these units is a water unit, who is weak to about 1/3 of the enemies and strong against literally 0 of them.This usually isn't a problem because you can heal downed units and take the turn they would have had in that combat round. The dog can take hits for units within three tiles (the protection should really be tied to an area and not the units in the area when the ability was activated), so to survive the incredible dps the AI throws out, the dog ends up dying over and over again, and the other units revive him every time he goes down since excess damage doesn't carry over to the downed state.2) Haste is straight-up broken. Most units have a speed of 2-3 tiles. Haste increases that by 2 (and initiative by 1, which isn't irrelevant) and, like other enchantments, lasts indefinitely. You get a flying unit early on that has a mv of 4 tiles who can apply haste as an assist. Some of the other assists can be good, but doubling the mv of your artillery units  is key to keeping them alive.3) Ultra mode needs to have its activation requirements drastically increased. You unlock it at level 10, but so do bosses (of which there are 1+, usually two, in every fight). I dinged 10 right before I finished off an otherwise trivial map (I think I was overleveled after clearing the harder of two branching plot lines), and it unlocked the ultra abilities for the boss. The ultra needs 6 charges to activate (each time the boss takes damage, they gain a charge, which means they get multiple charges if you combo them), and used it on the same turn to deal 100+ damage to all of my units with a 3 square radius (regardless of tile height), which was all of them because the max attack range is 3. Only my tank unit survived. I was able to revive my other two leaders, but then the boss started spawning 2-3 units a turn, and the other boss revived with 3/4 hp (when you revive, you come back with about 1/4), and I wasn't able to win before the turn limit expired.Regardless, the boss has more than 100 hp and a static 40% chance to take half damage on top of an implicit half-damage shield (and you can't flank cause the dude won't leave the corner). The DPS isn't high enough to kill them before they hit the uber, and since the uber one shots everyone in attack range, I guess the intended play pattern is to just face tank it with somebody and revive them afterward?It's worth noting that you can't control when the ability is used, and it is expended on assists.If they doubled the number of charges required or if they made it such that back-attacks don't grant charges (which is how all of the other mechanics work), it could maybe work, but the main problem is obviously the abilities themselves. As is, there's no counter play. You have to hit the boss to win, you have to be in range to hit the boss, and if you're in range of the boss, then the boss is just going to kill you with the charge you gave them. There's no way around it without stalling, and some maps have a very small turn limit.4) You can pass your turn, but the AI cannot. This is an insane advantage for the player which is compensated by the swingy mechanics above. As long as you're willing to let the AI move, you can essentially take your turn in any order, which means that if you have high initiative units, you can take two turns in a row without the AI being able to do much of anything to contest you. (A hotkey for passing initiative would be very helpful because something resets the cursor to the center of the screen when you pass it with the mouse).5) One of the defeat conditions for the first boss is that this NPC not die, but the NPC is *weak to the bosses element* and dies in about 1.5 shots. If she takes damage from a random enemy, you have to baby sit her with your tank as she runs around randomly, attacking from range and triggering the boss's ice-nova defensive counter attack because, while I don't think the boss will intentionally target her, the boss fires a beam that hits everyone in a line. The tank can only absorb one of those hits, so even if you do babysit her, it might kill her anyway if you're really unlucky. Regardless, it's a lose condition that the player has minimal control over, and the boss routinely crits for 70-100 damage. 6) Often times, battles occur in an inescapable series 3+ long. If you get to the end, and the fight is super overturned (I have yet to see one that isn't), you may not be able to beat it. Usually, this is because they threw in a  turn-limit that is impossible to meet without blitzing the boss (which will get you killed by the uber abilities). If you can't win, you have to return to town, and you LOSE ALL PROGRESS, INCLUDING ALL ITEMS AND XP GAINED. If you want to go back to the boss fight, you have to repeat all of the battles leading up to it, which could take hours.There are some other things, but I lost track of them somewhere in the ranting above. I really wish I could recommend this game. If they can address some of the problems, I *would* highly recommend it. The music is great, of course; Hyperduck does fantastic work.  Visually, it's gorgeous. I like the minimal leveling system and the creature collection parts. I might start the game over on normal and see how that goes. If I try not to abuse the initiative system and haste mechanics, it might even out the difficulty. Perhaps the hard difficulty was a late-inclusion and not properly tested? It certainly isn't balanced.I'm not one of those gamers who is obsessed with difficulty (although It's certainly more important to me in strategy and tactics games). My concern isn't that it's too easy or too hard. It's that it's both. It's often very easy up until the point where you just lose out of nowhere (see 6. I didn't have any issues with the other fights in the chain, but the boss fight was literally impossible, especially while babysitting not one but two NPCs). Often times, some new mechanic pops up (like an aoe counter that freezes your units) that just wipes everyone out.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a good tactics game. I haven't played much in the genre, but I'd rank this on par with my favourites; Into The Breach and the first two Fire Emblem games. It's a 9/10 for the genre. The story follows Peony, a 15 year old girl who leaves her mountain village in search of her mother (who left without saying goodbye). Peony is a witch, which is just a human that can use magic (a very rare thing in the world). This world has both men and beasts familiar to earth and magic "fae" creatures, which have inhabited the world since the time of the "elemental gates" being destroyed (they used to inhabit their own realm beyond the gates). She finds two companions along the way, a dog and a cute fae baby bird-like creature. This is where your journey begins. The story progresses a lot, you recruit more companions to your team, and your goals change as the world changes around you. This game is purely a tactics game. Each level, you choose which companions to use. The limit is 3 (except rare boss battles), and you almost always have to use Peony (and sometimes other character are locked in for certain missions). You can also summon up to 3 fae creatures each missions, and bring 3 spells (there are rare missions where you can't access magic and can't do either). You recruit more fae to your roster and find more spells in the missions. Killing a fae you don't have will drop its essence (unless its a leader unit), and spells will randomly be found in levels. Both your main characters and your fae can level up. The max level for companions is 60, each level granting 1 trait point which can be allocated to three different bars which max out at 20: Offense, Defense, and Special. These will grant 2 stat bonuses each, one is the same for all character and the other unique. Example: Offense always grants Attack damage for each character, and for Peony it also grants Crit Dmg, while Chico instead gets Back Attack Dmg. These stat points can freely be changed at the start of every single fight, which is cool because its another way the game allows you to strategically prepare.There are also scrolls which you randomly find in battles. Each companion can equip one, and they grant passive stat bonuses. There are 42 in all, and each one can be leveled up to lv5 (collecting multiple of the same scroll lvs it). I didn't collect all in one playthrough. Then there are multiple (up to 3) weapons for each character, which you find as you progress through the story. Lastly, there are gems that characters can equip. You are first given gems in the mid-late game. They usually trigger the cast of a spell on your third attack, and also have a secondary bonus. I didn't collect even half the gems. So there is lots to plan before a battle even begins. You can see the map and inspect all the units beforehand. There is also elemental type to consider, which is a big part of the combat in this game. There are 6 elements, + normal and arcane (which both are neutral, but arcane crits every 3 attacks). Certain elements are strong vs others meaning they always crit. Those that are weak vs other will do half damage. While this game does ease you into a lot of the complexities (for example, you start with no faes, no spells, no scrolls, alternate weapons, or gems), there is still quite a lot right off the bat. Because each creature is loaded with abilities. Chico, your dog friend has 8. A basic early gremlin witch has 4. And it's not uncommon for units to exceed 10. These abilities are denoted with icons, so you start to memorize what they mean over time, but it's quite a lot of information overload nevertheless. There is also quite a lot of complexities with what you do with your units in battle. Each unit has 3 available actions (you can only do one each turn): wait, assist, and attack. Assisting is helping an adjacent ally. It's effect is determined by the element of the unit (ex. water types heal with their assist). Waiting can be done anytime, anywhere. It's effect is different for each unit, usually a self buff, and usually the weakest of the 3 actions. Attacking: There are melee and ranged units. Higher elevation, and back attacks are buffed. After reaching a certain level, your companions get an "ultra" bar that fills up every time they deal or take damge, or assist. Once full, it unleashes a much stronger and different attack or assist. Companions, and some fae, also have reaction abilities that have a % chance of triggering when that unit is attacked.Overall, I like the complexity and depth this game has. It is ovewhelming at first. And the game didn't draw me in that much in the beginning tbh. But as I played more, I started to enjoy it more. It has a good difficulty level for normal. I could beast most regular fights on the first try. But I had to prepare well, and play well. Oversights in either area can swiftly result in a loss. The hardest levels are the boss battles. There are some that took me more than 3 attempts. You also want to try to keep your fae alive and beat the battle quickly, because these give experience multipliers. It's a long game. I'm not sure how many hours it took, because I played on a steam deck and the SD is bugged for hours played. I would guess more than 50 hours. I beat it on day 76, which means 76 missions. And each mission will have 1-4 battles. There's also a good amount of story dialogue between battles. And there's a couple things to do outside missions, like play the quick camping minigame (a memory match game that rewards stat buffs for next mission), and upgrading your equipment for various bonuses like extra xp, damage for certain elements, etc. The biggest negatives for this game:-Some stats, like speed which determines initiative, are not displayed anywhere on the character.-You can delay a unit's turn, which moves them down 2 spots on the initiative track. That's great. But it's also a huge pain because it should let you decide to delay multiple times at once. Instead you have to wait for that char's turn to delay again. And usually it's optimal to make all your units delay at the start of combat until enemy units are in range. So there's a lot of time wasted doing this.-You can't access the menu during story moments (which happen between battles). The biggest problem with this is, I like to mute the game during battle so I can listen to something else. But I want to hear the music during stoy moments as it really helps set the mood, and I'm unable to unmute then.-The game suffers from information overload, as I mentioned earlier.-There's a mechanic called "lucky day" which gives each elemental type (save normal) a bonus for each day of the week (each mission passes time by a day). You can see what day it is and the bonus on the mission select screen. The problem is, you have no idea what enemies you'll be facing when you select a mission. So you can just get unlucky and run into a bunch of fire enemies on the day they get buffed. You can exit out of missions freely, but it's also kinda a pain as you'll have to go through the story section again next time you enter. Lucky day adds nothing to strategy and shouldn't exist.The Positives-Amazing art, great music-The companions are all quite unique, likeable, and each have a good amount of their own story. I believe they all have their own mission arc that expands that companion's story and usually ends with unlocking a new weapon for that char.-I like everything about the combat. There are so many possiblities with how to play each battle. -The story is great, I found it quite interesting and unique. -Lots of optional side missions. -I found the difficulty level was pretty spot-on.-Lots of tactical depth, including pre-battle planning. Lots of things to consider. Lots of different ways you can choose to approach a battle.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for Final Fantasy Tactics for PC since 1999. Alas, it never came. But you know what? I don't need it anymore because Fae Tactics easily, and I mean EASILY, satisfies my tactics RPG itch. This game is absolutely gorgeous. The hand drawn sprites look fantastic and they animate like butter. Everything is so cute and colorful; I just want to jump into my screen and bathe in the lovely 32-bitness of it all. Battles play out like FFT, where....HEIGHT actually matters. Why can't other developers factor in height in their tactical RPGs? It's here and it's good to be on top, literally!Oh, as a fairy, or Faery, you recruit the cutest little companions to fight on your team. It's got a Pokemon vibe. Watching your little fuzzy friends beat the crap out of goblins and monsters never gets old. Did I mention the music? No? Shame on me! Music is buttery nice and totally fits the mood of the game. Honestly, I can't believe this is $20. I was totally expecting a $40 price tag. Do yourself a favor, and buy this game. The developer is a small team but the love and attention they put into this game really shows.

_childDocuments_.review: good game but with a lot of busy work. this game is more for people who love min/maxing things. before fights you need to look at enemies so you can change your party, cards, ability, states (you can +/- hp, st, and a counter with points you unlock with levels), and you even have to take into account the day of the week as they each boost an element. you also have to change all these thing in the ui as you can't just add characters to a grid to take in like Final fantasy tactics did. you need to carefully take into account all these things or your people will get 1shoted. you also need to min/max for xp as you get bonus xp for having all enemy leaders downed instead of killed and you'll get bonus xp and parts if none of your people get taken out. you also have to make sure you grab all items/summons dropped because any left on the field after a fight are not collected. even if you do all these things fights can still be hard so if you don't do these things your gonna lose a lot. as for characters go you'll have 3 main characters that you can swap and 3 slots for summons. you will not always have 6 characters though because summons use up points. you start with 3 points and can max it to 6 and normal summons can use up to 4 and special ones will use 6. attacks in fights is a bit different because characters don't use abilities like most tactical games instead here your characters will either just range or melee. melee characters do have added use as they will attack after other characters if they are in melee range of said enemy and this is in addition to their normal attack. main characters will also have a power move but once it's powered up it will be used the next time you attack if you want it to or not. along with attacks most character have 2 buffs a self buff and one for allies. you also get to take 3 cards that will charge up and these cards can be elemental attacks or buffs for your characters. just know enemy leaders can also have cards and will be able to keep summoning things as long as they are not downed or dead. one last annoying thing is you can not attack then move you must move then attack so if you play a _childDocuments_.review: This is an original take on a genre I am a particular fan of. The gameplay is reminiscent of Final Fantasy Tactics, which is a good thing in my opinion, with enough fresh elements to make it stand out as its own game. The writing is enjoyable (and humorous at times), the music is great, the art/animation is pleasant, and the game is just downright fun to play. Unlike Final Fantasy Tactics, I find myself encouraged to use a new squad in nearly every match to counter the particular setup of that field, and the variety helps keep things fresh. Not so much in a "let me bar off your A squad so you're forced to use your B squad," more of a "there are a lot of fire units in this battle so I need to field some water units to deal with them." Even more so, I find myself adjusting the traits of my leader units frequently to accommodate the new lineup. Each battle feels like its own victory, as many of the enemy leader units are fairly difficult to deal with, and (as of yet) I haven't found any "do this every time and win" strategies. About 25 hours into the game, I have three suggestions, two of which are simple quality-of-life improvements. The first has to do with the time it takes for enemy turns to pass. When they're doing something that impacts my team I think the time is appropriate, but when there is a lull in the fighting and a lot of units on the field, I'm not really that interested in seeing cannons shot at nothing, for example. I think an option to speed up the enemy animations when desired would be ideal. The second QoL suggestion I have is in the user interface. When I'm confronted with a new attribute (for example, when first equipping a "Teamwork" scroll or mousing over some effects in combat), currently I have to go into a whole different menu to figure out what that does. I really love the space bar menu, so perhaps that could be expanded with various enchants and curses, or ctrl + clicking an option would bring up additional tooltips.The other suggestion i have would be simply to keep adding variety to the units. I think being confronted with new enemies about 30% faster would be perfect.Overall, this game is a fun, true-to-its-roots game, while expanding the genre in its own fresh and meaningful way. Other than the few suggestions listed above, 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good, it deserves more attention.Clearly heavily inspired by games like Final Fantasy Tactics or Tactics Ogre, it rips out the class-based leveling system, and instead focuses on giving you a host of character and summon options that can be swapped out at the start of combat based on the forces you are up against.  This change shifts the focus from "how do I want to level my characters" onto "what are the best tools to bring to this fight" in a way that I found very engaging.  Although the character progression is more simplified, it still has the slightly sloppy, occasional bursts of "wow, what just happened was ridiculous," that underpin the games it is inspired by.I played on hard, and found the difficulty to be pretty much exactly where I wanted it to be.  I had to retry quite a few fights - particularly in the first half of the game - to adjust my composition, but only 2 or 3 of them took more than 1 retry (and 1 of those multiple retries was to meet a more difficult hidden condition I had been spoiled on.)  The game gives you some pretty powerful come-back mechanics to counter-balance the sometimes ridiculous power bosses (and occasinally enemy leaders) can bring to bear.  I can understand why I have seen people complain both about the game being too easy also also too hard, but I overall found the game to push back on me in a way that kept the game just challenging enough to be engaging without being overly punishing.The game generally does a good job explaining what abilities and effects units have, but some things occasionally slip through the cracks.  In particular, I had to ask the internet what +teamwork was (it increases the AOE of assist skills), the internet couldn't give me a satisfactory answer of what combo crit was (I believe it is bonus damage when doing a combo attack), and I still wish I could look up what an EX attack did once I was in combat.The story is well written and well paced.  It starts off very low stakes as a way to focus on the character and world building without having to dump exposition on you.  It is mostly upbeat, with a few (good) emotional moments.  The plot itself is fine.  It grew on me as the game went on, but the story is more engaging in the moment-to-moment then as a whole.  Things did get a little exposition dumpy right before the final boss, but otherwise I enjoyed it all the way through the game.In the vein of a Tactics Ogre, there are a lot of hidden conditionals tied to how much you use characters and a few hidden conditionals inside of fights themselves to unlock characters/equipment, and that have an impact on the ending slides.  I can respect a game making this decision in 2020.I have seen complaints of repetivity - the game is long, taking me more than 70 hours to get all the way through.  However, mostly playing in bursts over the course of most of a month I didn't feel the length, and enjoyed my entire playthrough.I really enjoyed this game, and highly recommend it.PS. The music is excellent.  Composer/devs, please release a soundtrack with every song, I would pay around $10 for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fae Tactics is a fun game in the style of Final Fantasy Tactics or Fell Seal, but without all the endless character optimisation grind those multi-class-systems have.The only thing that really annoys me about Fae Tactics is that it often feels like a bad console port. Yes, sure, these kind of games originally comes from consoles, but seriously, dear devs, if you release a game like that for the PC at least put some work into it.For example: To play efficiently you pretty much use the "delay turn" option dozens of times in each and every combat - you always want to move all your units without being interrupted by enemy turns, thus you always let the enemies act first and then position your units for optimal combo synergy. Would it really be asked to much to have a QUICK KEY for "delay turn"? Or at least not deliberately move the mouse cursor to the centre of the screen every time you delay one units turn, so you have to constantly move it to the bottom left, wait for the animation and rinse repeat?!? If i had a cursor plot for playing this game, i'm pretty sure the most prominent element would be a huge line from the centre of the screen to the bottom left.And why does the cursor have to be invisible at the end mission screen? And why isn't there a soft-stop to prevent the cursor from constantly getting out of the game on a multi-monitor setup? And why does the game auto-save on the currently active save slot instead of having a dedicated auto-save slot? Seriously, overwriting the last save automatically is just a bad habit from old console games, where you only had four save slots because there wasn't more space on the cartridges... So pretty much all my criticism comes down to "console issues", which all could have been averted easily if the devs wouldn't try really hard to make the game feel like a console game, purposefully implementing console issues just for the sake of it.Minor non-console-related criticism is that the game could really need a 3x Speed option, the skipping of the intro animations should have an option in the menu (seriously, it's 2023, why do we have to edit config files for stuff like that?!?) and the AI is often terrible. The game rewards you for keeping multiple enemy leaders downed without killing them, so could somebody please tell the AI not to go full murder-hobo on every downed enemy leader?!?Okay, that sounds all very negative now - it's still a game i would recommend despite all of these smaller flaws. I finished it twice for all the achievements and took 88 hours for that.

_childDocuments_.review: A menu-less turn based tactics game in the style of many others before it. With some interesting game play changes from the standard tactics game, it's focuses on quicker battles, is ridiculously addictive, and has a strange "open world" element to it that makes it feel like a proper adventure.Though often not talked about, I highly suggest playing this for the story, especially if you've played many other tactics-style games. It works amazingly as a companion piece to games like Final Fantasy Tactics or Fire Emblem. It's also refreshing to see what could have been a grimdark apocalyptic setting with all the edge end up feeling very... sweet and wholesome.From smaller stories of helping a baker figure out what's going on with her cookies to international politics, it really has a very good "feel" to it. <3If I have one complaint, it's that the games open world style and flag-based advancement makes it feel very easy to miss out on things. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this, but I don't know who this game is for.It's supposed to, I think, be a simpler tactics game aimed at a younger audience - and I knew that going in. I love tactics games so I can look past the youthful stuff. It does succeed in making a simpler tactics game but I think they never stopped to ask the question - what is a tactics game without, you know, tactics? The game has almost no plot, the characters are generic, the combat is mediocre, the music is average and the graphics are ok at best. A lot of battles also come in series, where you can't save, which is just unacceptable. Sometimes something comes up, sometimes I'm just bored. Don't make me redo what i've already done or sit through 20 more minutes because you think I should. Thats a good way to make me hate your game.Some of your special moves look nice, and the game does have the bare bones of strategy, but it feels like it's missing anything to make it special...and without special, it's a far below average tactics game.I wanted to like it, but after 6 hours its just boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Fae Tactics definitely gives me nostalgia for playing Final Fantasy Tactics Advance and I've been having a great time with it. The animations carry a lot of personality for all the characters, the OST's nice, and the combat's fun. I enjoy recruiting lots of different monsters and then mixing up my teams to get through tricky situations. I think my biggest gripe would be that enemies scale directly with you in level and in unlocking new abilities. There's multiple quest routes you can take and I'm never sure quite which one I should be on. The direct level scaling plus no difficulty indicator for the battles you're about to take on can make it frustrating when you take on something that you might not have the tools on hand to complete. Sometimes things feel like a walk in the park and then I reach a boss at the end that feels like I can't pass them no matter what I try. Not sure if the answer is to just recruit more allies, get more equipment, advance down a different route or grind more parts and scrolls.I see people have mentioned there's little customization, all I have to say is keep playing and doing quests. You'll unlock new ways to utilize your 3 leaders. It makes them feel like completely new units imo.I would definitely recommend this to anyone with an affinity for strategy RPGs, though I'd be hard pressed to recommend it to complete newcomers to the genre due to the odd difficulty curves you can run in to sometimes with the direct level scaling.

_childDocuments_.review: Those who are fans of the tactic genre should give this game a go. The graphic, music, characters and gameplay are all high quality, very high by indie standard.The one thing you must know though is that Fae Tactic is a rather difficult game. Most Tactic games let you brute force or turtle your way to victory with a broken build you no longer need to change. Fae Tactic though keep the min-maxing to the minimum but instead rely on pure strategy and composition to counter what the enemy will throw at you. Go in with the right comp and you will win easily but keep going at it wrong and you will likely find yourself complaining on the steam forum.And because of the above design point, Fae Tactics have some of the best boss fights you can get in a tactic genre. The big boss really feel like you're tackling raid bosses where you have to maintain a good balance between damage, healing and add clearing while also playing along with the boss mechanics and making sure you don't go over the 20-turn counters which will turn on the rage mode. An absolute blast to play and you will absolutely love and hate yourself after you finally kill that one boss after retrying for 2 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, this has been somewhat of a pleasant surprise.  Don't take that it's all roses.  It does have problems, but it's definitely a good building block.Here's what I like:Combos... more games need this.  Though, this is a double edge sword as well, as it can make the game somewhat easier.  When one of your party members is next to an enemy and you attack, they will also get in a turn.  If they're surrounded, they'll attack all enemies.Summons... you can add creatures you've come across as party members, but only a limited amount.  At the beginning you'll get three 'bubbles' and each creature uses that as a cost.  So, you can take three creatures with one bubble, etc.Spells... you can pick any three spells, you pick up along the way, at the beginning of each fight.  Heals, More HP, More MP, etc.  There are cool downs though and you can only use one spell per round.Assists... every character has an assist skill.  i.e. Heal, haste, buff defense, etc.  Some are more party useful, some are individual.Positioning... many games of this sort forget about this.  Attacking from behind is an auto backstab... even ranged.  You get bonus for attacking on height advantages as well.  So, it's possible to have a height advantage from the back with a combo for insta deaths.Here's what I don't like:Graphics... these are honestly not very good.  They appear to have been made at 640x480.  While the animations aren't bad, everything else is just a pixelated mess.  I would not doubt if this came out for the Switch.  Also, the static conversation backgrounds of the characters need more variety.  I honestly get tired of seeing Peony and her surprised face over and over and over.... You can see it in one of the previews above.  It's awful and I wish I could turn it off.  If they ported this to Unity or Unreal and provided proper fullscreen res, it would make the immerssion experience a whole lot better.AI... it's also pretty bad, almost gamebreaking bad.  In some maps the enemies will just constantly buff themselves and not move until you get, not within range, but in some weird radius were they can't attack.  It's tactically not sound.Here's some things that I'm MEH about:Traits... you get these when you level up.  They are pretty basic.  Power, Defense, Evade/move.Equipment... very basic again.  You find something on the battlefield and you equip it, but there's only one slot (not sure if there's more later).Story... It's hard to enjoy/like the story with Peony's same expression.  I honestly don't even know what's going on.So, that sums it up for me.  I'd give it a good 7.5 in it's current incarnation.  I do think it can be much more though.  There's a lot of good ideas, but definitely some headscratchers.  Give it a go.  $20 seems like a lot, but I'd support their efforts for some balancing and enhancements.  I think you should too if you like 2D tactical games.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. Tactical turn-based party RPGs are probably my favorite genre. Final Fantasy Tactics is one of my favorite games of all time, and more recently Fell Seal: Arbiter's Mark and XCOM 2 have been games that I really enjoyed playing and fully finished. I should be the prime target audience for this game, and the core gameplay system underneath everything seems fine, but I gave up on it around 5 hours in. There are positive things about the game but I'll just list the reasons why I couldn't keep playing it:Lack of character customization. Every other similar game I have played has at least some sort of "build" options that allow you to figure out a unique playstyle and composition for your party. The entire time I played this game, I was stuck with the same three main characters and their same set of abilities, along with a few monster summon characters. With the rock-paper-scissors elemental system, you have even less choice because you always need to pick summons that are strong against the enemy elements. I would use the tank character's guard ability over and over, heal him over and over with the healer character, and use the rest of the characters as DPS. The upgrades had some choices, but overall it just felt like I was leveling everyone up rather than getting to actually pick unique builds. Even the unique monster summon characters didn't get their own unique abilities, because the elemental abilities were always the same for that element, and the main character abilities were just pulled from a small list of possible ones.Slow/tedious gameplay elements. In a normal tactical RPG, there are almost always ways for the combat to become unbalanced. In Final Fantasy Tactics for instance, it's pretty easy to grind a bunch of characters in a bunch of different jobs, until you have a set of OP characters with all of the OP class abilities. This game seems pretty obviously designed to prevent the player from ever being too powerful, but it ends up just making the game tedious. If you go back into existing areas to grind, you will have to sit through a ton of enemy animations where they sit around and do nothing for half of the battle. There is no way to field a team of a bunch of monster summons instead of main characters to help level them all up at once, and there is even a limitation where each monster has a power rating and the total power rating across all summons has to be a low number. The story missions are a series of battles rather than one battle and it just feels unnecessary to group them like that other than to pad out the gameplay content between cutscenes. You have to waste time sending your characters to physically pick up all of the item drops during the battle instead of just receiving them afterwards like every normal RPG does it. The terrain and lack of long ranged attacks makes it optimal to just stay grouped the whole time and take on enemies one by one rather than send your characters to different parts of the battle map. The first few battles seemed fun as I learned the abilities, but after a while it became very stale and slow.Terrible story. I did not get through a ton of the plot of the game, but the story events were actively off-putting. The structure is similar to Final Fantasy Tactics where it's just cutscenes before and after battles, and normally that kind of thing works pretty well even if it's mostly just passively watching the plot move forward rather than making any decisions. Unfortunately, all of the cutscenes are bland or boring. Two of the three main characters are animals that don't talk, so it's mostly the main human character interacting with everyone. Sometimes she talks to random NPCs about boring topics like trying to get parts for her motorcycle, sometimes she runs into fights between different fantasy creatures. Everyone seems to hate her including those that she goes out of her way to help. Characters will spout exposition about exciting events that happened off screen, and then there will be a random battle against generic creatures for vaguely related reasons. There were very little reasons given for me to care about anyone or have any kind of long term goal for why I would be fighting all of these battles, and nothing was introduced that made to want to finish the game to find out where the plot might go.
