_childDocuments_.review: I thought I would like this game and I did at first. It is beautifully done and the story is also good. However, the leveling system is pretty garbage. It feels like enemies level up with you for each battle. So if you wanted to grind for a few levels to get better because it just isn't there. Every enemy will level up with you. Now normally this is fine because you expect a certain level of challenge in a game like this. However, your whole party does not level up equal. So when you have that important character you've been neglecting even for a few battles they get super behind and just get one-shotted in a future battle where you MUST use them. It then becomes super difficult to kill enemies which are effectively just damage sponges. Also, many of the tougher enemies in the game will use those spell cards every single turn, but you are limited on yours based on a number of turns cooldown. It feels super unfair and just makes it not fun. Especially when they can keep on summoning more and more familiars and you're stuck with just the ones you started with.  This is a real shame too because they almost had something really great here if they'd just tweak that difficulty a little bit or make it so none of your familiars are left behind when leveling. Or at least give me some opportunity to level them up without having to also level up my other characters too. Or just explain how it works in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games ever!Gameplay: Just because it's mostly just clicking your mouse doesn't mean it's easy. In fact, a lot of the negative reviews here are from people playing the game at the easiest level and still finding it difficult. You'll find that clicking at certain places from certain angles will give you different results. I usually just have this open on the side during a busy workday or while having a meal. I've had a few boss fights run for almost an hour or more (probably because I try very hard to keep everyone alive for the bonus). Hitting hard and building a solid defense can be very very satisfying once successful. This game will NOT hold your hand. Graphics: Beautifully made art with great animations. I would explore a(n open) world built around this. Maybe a sequel about the world after this game. Maybe we could even get the original cast to appear as guests. Seeing certain stages for the first time can be jaw dropping (I mean it's still pixels but it sure is pretty).  Of course, I came in with no expectations so that's still up to you.Sounds: Music is often appropriate but there are certain parts that really hit the spot. Voice acting in the future might help get the audience even more engaged by giving the characters more life. Characters: Even the ones that are similar feel distinct. Party leaders often have distinct play styles that feel right for the personalities they have. You'll have the ability to unlock certain optional characters later on and they're an absolute delight to use. The Fae are also interesting in terms of variation. Story: You'll wish there was more. Deals with surprisingly slightly more mature topics. Audience: Likely all ages.System Requirements: I could probably run this on my toaster.Bugs: Hasn't crashed or lagged even once on me. Probably since I've bought it at this stage of its life. Difficulty: Slightly challenging. Victories are satisfying. Easy after understanding how it works.Value for Money: Properly priced. Definitely great value when on sale. Conclusion: I love this game so much and I hope you do too! Side note: This game is made by Endless Fluff Games, and for that name alone this game deserves a purchase. (More fluffy Fae in the future please).
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: People keep comparing it to FFT, but apart from the graphics and being a tactics game it hardly has any other connection to FFT.I truly wanted to like this game, it has a nice story, decent character development, graphics are gorgeous and has a kicking soundtrack.But damn, the frustration balances out the good, lets mention some of the bad points.-Way too RNG based, there are chances to freeze, petrify, etc. all kinds of debufs, which you AND the enemy can do, meaning if you get really lucky you can keep enemies in a stuntlock, and the enemies can do the same to you. This can make or break your plans, especially when it comes to leaders (aka bosses or mini-bosses) since they tend to be more resilient against status effects. OFC there are also chances to evade, hit, crit... all this RNG just makes this feel more like gambling rather than tactics.-Unbalanced enemies, this especially applies to maps which have multiple stages, sometimes you gotta fight 2-3 times in a row to finish a zone. So here is the thing, you pass with ease through the first two battles which are made of normal mobs, with the final stage being a boss battle. Some bosses often one or two shot you or even worse it has a chain attack (a type of attack which branches out through nearby characters) and can clean off the entire party. Ohh and guess what, if you fail a stage you can restart it, but if you quit it, well, you gotta pass through out the other two stages again next time you retry.-Speaking of battles, the game offers an option of 2x times speed up of battles, it is worthless since they still take ages to finish, enemies almost never wait a turn, they just keep buffing each other even when some of those buffs last one turn and the next they again buff each other, why? My party is nowhere near those enemies and cannot touch them in 1 turn, this just prolongs the battle unnecessarily.-Levels, most objectives are: defeat the leader/s, here is the problem, all levels have those bosses placed all the way at the back, forcing you pretty much clear every other mob until you reach them, and they often get some height advantage.-It has an RPG tag… but it has barely any RPG elements, you can unlock 3 things for your main characters, and nothing for the summons, just level them up, that is it… And regarding leveling, if you think you can just do some grinding and pass those bosses I mentioned earlier, well guess what, enemies scale with you!It has a few more points to mention but I will stop here, this is enough. This game looked like it had elements which I could enjoy, but it turned up to be a pile of frustration and disappointment, sad really.

_childDocuments_.review: I has alot of good qualities. But it lacks what makes a tactical game actually tactical. Variety in abilities.Each character has an attack, support, defense, and passive.....  One ability per thing. The kicker is that many units have the same abilities. And they never change. EVER.  Main characters get like a super move after beating up others a certain amount, and you get 3 spells to choose from that you can cast during the battle. You can also get other monsters as team members, which is supposedly the main hook of the game. Go around getting creatures to make a party.Problem is, all these monsters share the same abilities. Congrats! You got a cute bunny! It works almost as similar as that bird you got. The difference between creatures is so small that you could replace them with colored pawns.So without character customization, I can't call this a tactics game. It's more like a chess game. You have set pieces with set moves.Their is in fact a certain degree of strategy that is required. It's just less complex then most other tactic games.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid strategy rpg game, clearly taking influence from final fantasy tactics. A solid 30 hr story with grind free gameplay makes this one of my favorite games of the year.Pros:-Solid character driven story. The game starts out a little aimless but once the main plot picked up I became fairly invested.-Fairly grind free. Your enemies do not have preset levels and scale to your party so you almost never run into enemies that are too strong or too weak. Your out of party teammates also gain passive exp so none of your characters end up too underleveled compared to one another. There is some grinding to get all the weapons and 100% the game but that's optional.-Ability to customize your characters between every stage. You can always change your weapons and skill allocations so you never have to worry about something being irreversible. You're also always able to strategize an optimal set up for each stage.-Replayability with newgame+ and collecting all the scrolls/summons/weapons.Cons:-Some of the bonus/missable characters don't get as good story chapters as the main cast. Was a little dissapointed there. Also outside of one of the lead characters most of the cast are fairly linear in terms of character.-Some of the sidequests/content is very missable. Had to look up guides to see how to do everything correctly.Overall I thought that this was a very solid game. Feels very much like a throwback to the gba and ds type rpg games. A solid game length with plenty of content that also doesn't overstay its welcome. None of the "sidequests" feel like filler; you want to do all the content as it fleshes out the characters and the world. Would recommend to anyone who likes these kind of tactics games.Rating: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: At first I thought this game was great. A lot of the challenge posed early on is the lack of explained mechanics. Cursor locking doesn't help but when you realize it was heavily inspired as an accessible SRPG by Pit People, you can see why it starts to fall short.After you start learning mechanics the difficulty is entirely gone. Even if you choose not to exploit broken enchants like Dance, even the worst characters are broken in the right situations. It's always 3 Leaders, 3 Summons, 3 Spells and unfortunately the majority of all three categories is just filler for enemy leaders. Every enemy leader in the game is unplayable. Not every fae that isn't a leader is acquirable and great pixel art be damned, it all comes down to palette swaps.There's no hidden depth, only brute force. If your first boss encounter is Pazuzu it seems a lot more difficult than it will be since every other boss is a joke in comparison. The flow of boss battles is that it's dangerous for the first 4 rounds and then it's just slowly whittling down their 11x HP values. The only challenge you can really give yourself is playing it on hard mode and challenging levels on their beneficial days of the week and then it's depth is just everything oneshotting everything else. There's no subtlety, there's no tactics, it's just you vs. swarm with hyper inflated stats.The story is pretty sub-standard, the main character is unlikable and flat, the surrounding characters are all the same personality barring a mangy mutt. It's just A/B endings based on your choices so it requires two play-throughs to get everything. Lots of missable stuff but the missables aren't really significant, they either lead to the different endings or block off your chance to get an item. Then the worst of it all is that there's no post-game, it's just a no-warning New Game+ where you have to sit through twenty minutes of tutorial stages again. There's no dialogue skipping, pace changing. There's no Fae only playthroughs that give you access to the unplayable leaders, no evil paths, it's just what you got the first time around with the benefit of having the convenience spells and unusable fae since your gadgets were all reset.There's not a lot of stages. At the point of confronting the final boss there's about 8 open options which are just re-hashed story events. They change daily but quite a bit are just a couple enemies. Normally in games where they scale to your level it punishes you for dawdling too long, except most mechanics are hidden in 20 level breakpoints that then make the game a joke.Pixel art is great. Sounds effects are awful and over-used. Same old Sam English recycled rip-off music from classic RPGs. This really should have been a mobile or portable release instead since in very small doses, it's fun. Would not openly recommend, I'm glad all the buzz about it died off before it launched, the game is a disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Absurd difficulty spike mid game.No Saving during back to back battles.Enemies can camp and become OP buffing themselves over and over while other troops prevent you from stopping them.Elemental Totems ruin stages. Especially boss battles.Enemies leaders take 6+ hits to completely get rid of while the player has 2 to 4 hits on each character.Overpowered Bosses.Your units are so fragile compare to the enemies and they always outnumber you.Was loving the game till these issues showed up.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I got lured in by the bright graphic, but the game's system is terrible!I honestly don't have a clue how you could call this a tactic game.1. Tutorial was weird. Introduce to you a ton of mechanics in 5 straight map with no freedom. You got shown a ridiculous amount of system and possibilities - which you don't really have any chance to test out, because at the time you have exactly 3 fixed party members. Just force-feed the info, try to swallow it.2. Monsters regularly drop loot which you have to run up to their corpse to loot. Otherwise they will disappear at the end of battle or when another monster move there. If you happen to ranged kill a monster on the other side of a cliff and they drop a card, well, tough luck.3. The system was normal, only slightly bad until they introduce to you LIMIT BREAK or ultra something whatever they call it. Basically randomly between 1 to 6 turns, a leader character (you MC or the boss) could store up enough gem and *overwrite* all of their abilities into another version. Overwrite mean you are forced to use the limit break ability and cannot choose the normal one. It sucks. It turns the whole tactic thing into a RNG fest.For example the main girl, who has the ability to wait 1 turn to change her ranged attack into a chain lightning thing. It allows her to both AoE and reach far away targets. But just when you wasted one turn to charge the chain lightning. Some mofo just decided it's fun to touch her a bit, and suddenly she's mad: now her attack is an AoE around *herself* the same range as her normal attack. You just wasted a turn for nothing.Or the little chicken who I equipped +teamwork item, which allow her heal to become an AoE heal+debuff, which is OP as heck... at least when she's not in limit break mode. Because then it completely disable the equipment's effect and become a single target heal.Imagine when your party got hit by a huge AoE, everyone's near dead. Now is the best time for AoE heel to shine!Or not, because the little bird's mad. She's so mad she can only heal 1 people.Did I just mention huge AoE? Those are bosses' limit break. They could also randomly decide it's totally fair that they have a 3-space radius AoE that can 1 shot half of your units.Although, in the end, I must say the game does one thing really well: it introduces quite a bit of fresh air into the tactic genre. It has a ridiculous amount of systems, a lot of them are fairly creative ones. And although I complained a lot, and have stopped playing because I (very) don't like some of them. I am still impressed with the freshness they brought. They're not well done, or deep enough, but they feel new.Play this game if you are tired of all those final fantasy tactic <s>clones</s> "inspired" games, and just want to see something new.Well don't play this game if you want to play a  tactic game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of pretty much every tactics game ever made, I personally found this game to be annoying. Whoever decided every possible thing needs a loading screen followed by a confirmation, has clearly never played a game. The battle in general also has way too many confirmations for everything. Controller joystick support is wonky, making it pretty hard to get it on the perfect spot. Nothing tells you the range of skills, so you have to position around to find the range of things. The graphics and music are okay, but everything else is bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping this game would be like Final Fantasy Tactics Advance, a favorite game of my childhood.  And, indeed, it is very similar!  Very cute, good story so far, and combat is satisfying.  I think the combat is probably more intricate, actually.  Gotta think about element advantages, spells to bring, and how to customize each character before each battle.Anyway, I think it's safe to say that if you like turn-based strategy on a grid, you'll like this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Weak imitation of actual sRPGs / tRPGs. Shallow, dull and incredibly poorly balanced.On the plus side: It looks great and the soundtrack is good. It has some neat ideas, but the execution is not good.Unless you have extra time and money and are desperate for something that resembles an sRPG, just play something better.Also, I'd like to add: I've seen multiple people compare this to FFT for some reason. This game has three things in common with FFT: 1- "Tactics" is in the title, 2 - Isometric viewpoint, 3- Looks vaguely similar? That's it. The game plays absolutely nothing like FFT.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only a few hours in at this point but so far I'm impressed! The elemental system is straightforward, but with Summons and Spells you can really strategize how best to tackle a battle. All the character items are unique, the upgrade system is solid, and combat itself is clean and fast.The story also seems good, though I'm not deep into it. I look forward to playing more!
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game worth the buck if you want a good tactical turn-based game.  You will not have a class system or anything like that, but you will be able to add/remove trait points at will and eventually be able to max all of them.  Game uses a combat system without menus so that means all the actions you can do is applied through passives, on wait, assists, and such.  You can delay a unit's turn which reduces their speed by 2 for that turn only.  You can see how much speed each character or enemy has at bottom left of screen.  The number displayed in the cards is the current speed of character.  The game will slowly introduce lot of the battle mechanics at the beginning so pay mind to the tips when they appear for them.  Shortly into game, you gain ability to summon creatures at start of the battle and will be able to use up to 3 different spells that will have their cooldowns.  You can find more creatures and spells by playing the game and looting chests and such.  Monsters may drop scrolls or the magic cards or summons for you to use later.  These are not consumables so you don't need to worry about needing to collect 100 spell cards of same spell or anything nor can you get duplicates of a summoned monster card (more than 1 may drop of same monster if 2 or more exist and you kill them before looting the card drop, but it will still always count as 1).The game is really fun and I really enjoy the music, sound, graphics, and gameplay a lot.  Don't just take my word on it as other people will provide much better reviews than I would.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I love the genre, but this game goes beyond being a very mechanically competent Tactics game. It is also incredible story wise. At 45 h played, I have beaten the game once. I missed quite a few things, so I might dive back into it for a New Game+.There's quite a few in-depth reviews, so I'll keep mine short.- The credits in the game are ridiculously short. Two developers. One music composer. Everyone else are third parties (publishers, localization staff, etc). And it is a BIG game. Took me 45 hours to beat and I can see a few hours more of extra content.- Incredibly balanced and challenging game. There are many many things to consider going into battle: Which elements are in the battlefield? Which abilities will I need and what elements should I use for my summons/spells/characters? And the choices multiply once you are in battle.- The story is VERY interesting. You don't expect much at first, but it develops continuously until the end. I sincerely hope more games set in this world appear.-
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is fun but tough. The art style is kitsch, and extremely video-game-esque. I have no idea why the main character is wearing headphones.The music is beyond annoying. The quest design is bland/bad, and you'll end up choosing random quests out of an under-explained menu with no real idea of what you're in for. This tends to make fights either a cakewalk or a brick wall, so get ready to reload.The game's fatal flaw is the the art style and the difficulty is at odds with each other- kids will struggle to advance but the story is childish. Strategy vets will demolish gameplay, but the story  and design of the game is clearly targeting children. I don't really understand who this game is FOR, and I can't bring myself to finish it.Fun, but flawed.C+
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a good game.   I wouldn't compare it to FFT; there's enough difference that I think this is it's own standalone category.PROS:  The storyline was pretty immersive and cool.  Depending on what you did in your run, you can trigger some interesting side stories or end credits.  Battle system is somewhat easy to understand and it allows for certain creative strategies to happen.  The biggest advice I can give is to play around with elemental weaknesses.CONS: Certain boss fights really pigeonhole you into a certain strategy to win; especially near the late game phases.   While it's true you do get SOME creativity in building your team before fights - there's certain scenarios where you just can't have your favorite unit on the field because someone is either just better suited or it's an elemental disadvantage. Most of the negative comments I'm reading about the battle system are just either not A: people who weren't smart enough to understand the system and how to beat the bosses or B: Understand the system but just want to whine about how it's hard/cant have their favorite person.  If I could change one thing - it would be to have versions or possibilities to have more elemental coverages on everyone - so we could run with our favorite characters through the entire storyline.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: A tactical RPG with a simplified system. You move your characters around on a grid, and have three choices of action - attack, assist another character (heals and buffs), or wait. There is the ability to set up combos as well. Outside of combat, characters level up by allocating points between Attack or Defense, which offers small stat bonuses. One other feature is that when you kill monsters, you can sometimes pick up artifacts that will let you summon them to assist you later. I can see the simplicity being a strength for some, but I think they game is overly long and ends up feeling simplistic the more you play it. As a result I couldn't stick it out until the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great! Beautiful pixel art, detailed animations for every enemy, and very tight tactical gameplay that doesn't feel overwhelming. The game does a good job of slowly introducing concepts to you so it doesn't become overwhelming, but after about an hour or two in you can start to see the real depth of the mechanics. Highly recommend to anyone who enjoys tactical RPGs. Strong FF: Tactics vibes, which is always a plus.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: What a pleasant surprise. I was not expecting how good it would be. Very fun tactical game with not too much grinding. _childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: So at first glance i really liked some of the ideas of this game, but man was this game obviously not play tested well before release .... i got into about the 5th fight in the story line and despite saving OUTSIDE combat im forced on reload to enter combat every time against a turtle that spams Def+ and even if you run straight at him and die trying to get there hes already at the point where you do like 3 damage a critical in the back or front or side .... witht he allies around him spamming magic barrier and defense up he has like 1000 total HP ... i cleared the entire stage and just wambod hime for like 25 turns before the "we made this fight mathematically impossible in 200000000000 rounds but have a 20 turn kill you mechanic kicked in and overwhelmed me." I am a veteran of probably 20-30 turn based tactics games .... i theoretically could have won it if i wanted to go through an incredibly long slogfest of specifically teching my spell cards to be able to overwhelm the boss once alone ... but there's no certainty i could have gotten him alone safely without the support spells i went into the fight with.I can understand a fight of this difficulty for some out of the way optional boss for the games ultimate weapon or something ... but its like the 4th story quest ..... absolutely no care to balance or playability was tested for this game and it shows. Its sad too because the level up mechanics are incredibly simple so its not like you would have to try a lot of iterations ... there's only three level up categories you can spend points in.I knew at this point i needed to just cut my losses .... a turn based tactical rpg isnt a turn based tactical rpg when you have to completely respec, change every character in your line up (only two adjustable slots at this point), for every singloe encounter .... tactics games are about using what you have and making good choices ..... this is more of a computer program simulator ... you have to have the exact setup so it compiles and runs properly for every fight. So if you want a tactics game that is an excel spreadsheet with only one working path for each fight ... go right ahead, but im going to look for one that has more choice and good gameplay personally.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun enough but still super buggy. _childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I've never written a steam review despite having over 250 games and many years under my belt, but this game warranted one. I was following it only about a week before its release and as a fan of final fantasy tactics, was interested.In the first 2 days i had the game i played 24 hours. This does not usually happen with me, but this game has blown me away. More than any SRPG I've played each level is truly a well crafted puzzle. Environment matters (cannons, ring outs, water, cliffs), element matters, placement matters, and all of these elements come together in such a way that most battles (at least when starting out) you barely scrape by and very much feel you've earned your victory. The story is also phenomenal and impressively complex. Don't be fooled by the "childish" look of some of the (really well done) portraits, the story is gritty well told and morally grey. People are struggling on the outskirts of society, your character faces constant discrimination, and villains are smart and manipulative. The characters that travel with you are a delight to play and learn about. Each character has multiple arcs in which they gain new equipment and the game does a great job showing who they are. They're vibrant and real, and I'm going to very much miss them at the end of the journey.If you like unique, well-developed worlds, engaging tactical gameplay, an amazing soundtrack and monster collecting, you will love this game. Take the plunge, it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Game started strong but I couldn't bring myself to completing it. There are some interesting mechanics like the crits, but I found that most of the battles turned out to be very annoying. Also, enemies scale with your level so it's not possible to grind when you're stuck in a battle. Once you've beat a few battles the game likes to make things difficult by making you lose the first time you face a battle while giving clues on how to beat it, which as a player sounds like a waste of my time.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Fae Tactics is a tactical RPG that I only recommend to huge fans of the genre. It's simplistic, the UI is bad, I don't like the art (YMMV), and in battles you're usually outnumbered 3-to-1 so you spend most of your time watching the AI move around. So far (ten hours in) the story is the same stuff as any other game like this and the writing is stilted. It's not an awful game, and if you love tactical RPGs and have played everything else then you'll have fun with this, but for most people there are better alternatives.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly a pretty fun game.  The mechanics are simple, clear, and interact well with the battles.  The characters are cute, if pretty archetypal, the story is good.It's all ruined by the most insufferably awful boss fights.  There are few worse mechanical sins that a game can commit than to have simple, understandable, and even elegant mechanics, and then to make the bosses ignore them.  A major early boss fight with almost 50% evade that doesn't move, is stationed over water so that most melee characters can't attack it, and ignores the principal reason to use melee characters, assist attacks, is especially egregious.The whole thing was very much a slap in the face.  After spending the prologue and first area learning the basic mechanics of the game, for a major story boss to come along and just say "No, all of that is worthless, go away." just leaves me not wanting to bother picking the game back up, because it doesn't respect my time or its own mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I tried playing this game on two occasions. The first time I took a break because I lost significant progress in a story mission. An AI teammate decided they had a death wish and wanted to fight the horde of enemies that spawned behind us mid-battle.My second time around, I didn't find the party customisation interesting enough to continue playing. Characters are tied to 1 attack, 1 melee-range team assist, and 1 buff for taking no action. Party leaders can build meter for a special move, but they can also accidentally waste the ability if they're forced into a combo or retaliation.Levels give you points to improve ATK/DEF for the most part. The only meaningful perks are after investing the maximum 20 points into one stat. I unlock new characters and often find I can't fit them in the active party because of poor element match-ups. Their element is tied to their only weapon and many weapons are gated behind future battles somewhere. I also find a lot of tedium in preparing my team for every mission. I have to set leaders on one screen, set the MC's element on another screen, then set my summons on a third screen. There's an optional mini-game for playing concentration (matching card pairs) before every match for temporary but huge stat buffs.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Great Game; bought it for the cute graphics and FFT murmurs, and it exceeded all my expectations. The Good: Bright, shiny graphics Imaginative elements and world buildingCute and engaging charactersAn acceptable length, and sufficient missables that replays are worth the timeThe less-than-good: Meh. Nothing deal-breaking. Some elements take some figuring out, some fights are frustrating. Personally, I never got used to a horizontal map, but it doesn't detract from the enjoyment of the game. Some weird inter-species mating that I had to try to ignore. The Great: The story; there's an actual story, not just flimsy excuses to go kill things.You actually get to caring about the charactersThe current-era (not in the bad way) affectations lend humour and depth to the charactersThe Really Great: I've never come across anyone else that knew who Tom Tildrum and Tim Toldrum were. It gives me a warm feeling of acknowlegement to have them included. Finally...the worst part of my experience with this game is that my seasonal allergies acted up a little bit at the ending and kind of made my eyes a little watery. JUST ALLERGIES, OKAY? I really want to see what comes next from EndlessFluff.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving this. I don't usually seek out JRPG style games but, this is wacking my nostalgia bone for Final Fantasy Tactics, without being overly serious. Which is also nice! But, I'm just looking to bop baddies with critters. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the most disappointing thing about the game is that it ends, and I don't know if there's higher praise I can give a game. Some stuff can be a bit weird or awkward, but even then, by the end of playing this it's probably one of my favorite games I've played, and puts a lot of other turn based games like it to shame.The game shines in perfecting the things it does right, and while it does certainly have flaws, many of those flaws are simply due to the definition of how the game type works, rather than any fault of the game itself. Sometimes battles can be a bit slow, but that's just how these work, and it's much better pacing than many others. The story and characters are very good, and learning more about them over time feels natural, rather than being stuffed in some corner of menus and just having to read it all at once, though it is still heavy on reading.I didn't play it on the high difficulty, and that meant that while there was still challenge, I never found myself too frustrated, though some bosses could feel a bit unfair, sometimes it's just about figuring out the right way to do it.I'm not going to true-ending it, because... well yes that's certainly a flaw that it's annoying to true ending, can't skip dialog (to my knowledge) and such, but if the main problem with a game is that it's not great for true ending after having already loved it the first time, then I feel like that's proof of a game that's certainly worth playing at least once through. Look, the game is lovely, and I'd be more than willing to shower it with praise, but the simple truth is that you probably already know if it's something you'd like from the simple phrase "dialog-heavy turn-based tactic game." The art is good, the story is good, the gameplay is good, the only reason not to love it is if it's simply the type of game you'd never like.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: It resembles Final Fantasy Tactics Advance in the container, but not in the content. Anyone who has been drawn to this game thinking that it is just like the Square game has to be prepared for a disappointment.⭐ Great sprite work, ideal for pixel Junkies.⭐ Nice user interface and simplified controls. I think it's pretty intuitive and plenty of explanations for smooth combat.⚠️ Little itemization and summoning progression. In FFTA and sequel you have at your disposal a mileage theorycrafting of races, jobs, skills and equipment. Objects are not simple stat buffs, they allow you to learn new skills and change jobs to get, for example, a paladin with thief or ninja skills and have a more balanced team. That offers a huge range of customization and is what I like the most about this game. In Fae Tactics you can have just three characters on the battlefield, each one with the same three actions (basic attack, assist and wait), scrolls that give stat buffs and you can only put one per character and summons that can't carry items and they're just to buff the three main chars. That's all.⚠️ Combat takes too long. Not just story driven combats, simple trash mobs fights for grinding purpose take a fair amount of time because the boss is either summoning new minions or shielding itself non-stop, so most of combats end up being to knock down a wall.⚠️ The plot is dull and you won't even remember it while you play. Combat is all that matters and is easy to burn out.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: If you like tactics-type games (ala Disgaea or Final Fantasy Tactics) try this out. It's not those, but it's damn good. The art, the gameplay, and the story are all fantastic. In addition, the pace feels much better than some of the older tactics games: it's a little slow into the tutorial, but after that the game opens up and it's just go-go-go. Two things to note are that enemies level with you (so grinding doesn't SUPER matter) and to take note of elemental weaknesses. Once you do that, the game's combat goes from "what the heck, why did I get one-shot" to fair.All-in-all, fantastic game. 9/10 and currently my GOTY 2020.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game that scratches that tactical RPG itch. You won't spend much time setting up your party as there is very little in terms of equipment and no Job/skill leveling. That does not take away from the game as it is a blast to play through. Battles are still engaging, enemy monsters can be caught when defeated, adding to your roster and variety of parties you can form. The story is fun and engaging, the characters are developed well. There is a huge emphasis on elemental resistances and weaknesses in the game, so alot of times you will be setting up your party to counter the elements of enemies.Highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: A few things to note about this game:1) It is a female lead character, with 6 of the 10 possible squad members being female. (There have been players query if there is a gender choice option - there isn't). None of the males are human either. For those who make an issue over gender, you're ruling out playing a good game.2) it has cute pixel graphics reminiscent of SNES/ Mega-drive era, but does provide a worthy challenge as you have to factor in the elemental alignment of both the enemy and your team. Each element has strengths & weaknesses E.g. Ice is weak to fire but strong against water & earth enemies. You also have to consider your facing and height difference to the enemy when attacking. This is very important to consider when facing the bosses in game.3) All the upgrades: health boosts, scrolls (leader buffs), crafting materials & summoning cards are collected by a friendly unit finishing their turn on that tile. If you do not collect them during the battle, you WON'T receive them after the battle. This is important to consider as the odds of certain items dropping (scrolls & summons) is relatively low; you can spend ages grinding to get certain summons. Regarding summons 24 monsters have 2 forms, but you must collect their default summons card first before you can acquire their alternative form. e.g. Gremlin thief is Wind first then Ice second. It won't spawn a summons card if you don't have the wind form in your summons list.4) The date of birth you enter will assign you a star sign; these correspond to the 12 date ranges in the western zodiac. This will influence the 3 spells & 2 summons you start with along with your inherent summons bonus. e.g. Your water & earth summons have stronger defences or your fire & arcane units have stronger attack values.5) Play the pairs memory game often; it will give you an assortment of stat buffs depending on the cards you draw.  There are 'junk' cards and camp skill cards. Each camp skill card allows you to select one boost from the list on the left; each party member adds a skill option. Note you must select which skill(s) you want to apply before selecting [DONE]. The junk cards are singles that by default provide no benefit but can be converted to bonuses by certain camp skills. E.g. rotten fruit can become wine if Eri is in your party.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: A great game for SRPG veteran and casuals a like.  Just a disclaimer, I played SRPG at a casual level and I played this game on normal difficulty. So my word cannot stand for those "hardcore" people. Also, instead of "reviewing" the game, I just want to talk about those common criticism (negative aspect) people might see in... for example, some Steam reviews.1. Non-existed player progression  By far this might be the biggest criticism I've seen. Enemy level scale with your story progression (or your level maybe?), making grinding levels for easier story progression basically pointless. And limited Character-specific build turn off a lot of people. Let me give you my take on this.  The SRPG series I grew up with is Summon Night series, the game allow character builds that could be pretty OP. And the game has system make attack deal bonus/penalty damage depend on the "Gap" between the levels of attacker and defender Regardless of their parameters. Which means that, once players' "Build" is completed, and you are few levels ahead of your enemies (BTW the game do very little to stop you from doing that), you can throw "Tactics" out of the window and trivialize the combat. The few times that player actually need to consider tactics are ironically first few levels of the game.  Compared to Fae Tactics here, it’s quiet obvious that Fae Tactics tried to avoid those issues and provide a decent challenge to the player. Within-character progression is minimized, instead the game gives you decent amount of customizations and a lot of team members and Fae (summoned allied creature) with different abilities to tackle different situation.  The goal is NOT to build ONE OP team and use it on every combat, instead player needs to rearrange team’s equipment, teammate and summon choice for EVERY SNGLE BATTLE. Kind of like the game allow (to some degree “forced”) player to “Respec” their character every battle. Which means the true “progression” of the game is actually the variety of customizations you gather along the way (teammates, weapons, scrolls, summons etc.), the more “options” you have, the more likely you have the specific “tools” to win the battle.  Which I understand why some people might dislike, but to me it’s fun and challenging2. Suicidal NPC  Funny enough that I didn’t encounter this issue at all, there are some NPCs might die if player neglect them. But it could be easily solved by having a character support them or just use spells (magic) to remote heal them. Most NPCs are tanky as heck, most of the time it’s even more difficult to intentionally let them die. It’s actually very funny that some NPCs join your team later on, and as soon as they join you, they suddenly become very wimpy and die in like two hits.  Yeah, the AI itself is not reliable, but what do you expect? My guess is that the developers patched and make NPCs very tanky because too many people complained about it, or maybe it is an issue specific to hard mode. Which I kind of agree on, I don’t think people will struggle with it now.3. Difficulty Spike  …Which is kind of true, kind of not true.   First of all, there are just missions designed to be hard. Second, missions are triggered by multiple storyline in the game, if the players keep doing a specific storyline, they might trigger missions early which have late game boss in them. Boss themselves will be around your level, but player might lack the correct tool to bring them down. Moreover, a lot of Fae Tactic’s missions contain several battles, and finding oneselves stuck on third or even forth battle and forced to retreat can be very frustrating.  That said, retrying and retreating actions themselves are pretty forgiving. Entering the wrong mission? Just retreat and pick a new one. Realizing you picked a bad loadout after the battle started? Just retry and adjust your team. There are no direct penalty regarding these two actions, outside of… you have to do those reseted part again.  And that sums up my opinion about the game, and yes there are still a lot of issues about the game. But I still think it’s a great game, and I hope I can help you to have a good enough expectation about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep down there's a good game here for TRPG fans, but it's rough around the edges making it hard to recommend to anyone other than hardcore fans of the genre.The user experience definitely needs a lot more polish. For instance there is no option to change the difficulty during the campaign. Whatever difficulty you pick at the start, you're stuck with it unless you restart. The default language is Chinese (although that's easily fixed in options), and it's missing things like glossaries, tutorials and a bestiary (there are some loading screen tips, but they don't cover a lot of important concepts). You're limited to 4 save files and you can't name them (although strangely they are automatically named after your in-game zodiac sign). The game also doesn't really explain that you can save during missions (which typically run 3-4 battles in a row), but it does autosave if you exit to the title menu. Unfortunately it never explains this and there's no option to save during battle, so I did initially think I had to play an entire mission in one sitting. I've encountered some glitches with the audio as well. It might all seem like nitpicking but it adds up to become pretty frustrating.What the game gets right is the battles themselves. Actual strategy during battle is far more important than character optimization and each battle is going to require some strategic instead of just serving as a level check. Props where it's due, this game gets that part right and a lot of TRPGs don't. When you're in the heat of battle, the game feels tense, especially on the higher difficulty levels. The choices each turn are simple but consequential.There are a few frustrations with the gameplay though. There's not a ton of ways to experiment with different builds for the characters, as there are no character skill trees or anything, just 1 equipment slot (it eventually becomes 2) and different stats to improve when you level up. If you're the type who really loves minmaxing characters in creative ways you'll be disappointed. The AI is not great. This is quite frustrating when you have guests in your party, especially when you have to keep them alive. But it can also makes battles feel weird, like the enemy is holding back.The story is certainly not going to blow your socks off, but it doesn't get in the way of the gameplay too much, at least. It's just a basic fantasy setting full of all the classic tropes.So do I recommend this game? Yes, for a very specific type of gamer. There are better examples of the genre out there, but it has its own charm if you're willing to deal with a wonky user experience. If you're on the fence, get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love FFT, you will DISLIKE this game.Story for the first 10 hours: Lame, a good Lv1 girl whiling to help everybody for free. She doesn't mind if it's about the mob wanting someone dead, bandits taking a city, a cookie thief for a bakery, a war between clans, or getting into Chernobyl.Dialog is all about this, a girl helping everybody because she wants to, talking with her dog who always reply "woof" and her bird that always reply with "pio".Oh, and she is a witch, nobody must know because it's dangerous for her... so SHE F*CKING TELL EVERYBODY ABOUT IT, and when she doesn't, she start casting magic so everybody will say out loud "oh, you are a witch lel but I won't say anybody lel". There is a line, a 3 seconds pop-up emote, a line, a 3 seconds pop-up emote, a line, a 3 seconds pop-up emote, a line, a 3 seconds pop-up emote, a line, a 3 seconds pop-up emote, a line...Gameplay: They should replace TACTICS with "grid movement" in the name. There is no tactics here. Every single unit has (basically) 3 movements. A basic attack, a self-buff triggered when waiting, and a 1-range friendly assist. All 3 for free, unlimited. In the end, it's all about basic attacks and a super basic attack which occurs automatically every 3 turns.The AI is CANCER, faraway enemies just spam the assist or buff until death (mana-shield, heal, buff) even when already applied. All of them will just wait until you get closer to attack one-by-one and be killed.This game promotes sand-bagging all day, you almost can't die, if killed, you can resurrect for free with an assist. If you revive an unit, this unit can act, so you can do a revive-chain every single turn and be immortal.Grindy as hell. Slow as hell. This game includes a 2x Battle-Animation option, you will wish there where a 100x EVERYWHERE option.No equipment, no spell tree, no jobs, no menu, aff...Being a little fair, the Artwork is beautiful, looks like a pixel-art Legend of Mana.Music is cool, scenarios are cool. _childDocuments_.review: There are many positive aspects of this game, but this particular review is not about them. Instead, I want to point out the mind-boggling racist implications of having a main villain group composed entirely of Black people, while almost every light-skinned character is not evil. (Yes, one person defects from the villain group to join you. No, that doesn't solve the problem of the game's racism either in-universe or in a real-world context.) It's horrifying that this decision was made and approved of for a game released in the 2020s. I would say I'm baffled as to how it could have been allowed to happen, but sadly I can imagine all too well the misguided thinking that went into this design and story choice.There's also a male character who, when in your party at the same time as a certain female character, spends his dialogue verbally sexually harassing her even after she makes it very clear she's not interested in him. This is played for 'comedy' and not called out as problematic - at least, not in the first several instances. After those, I just stopped using that character so I wouldn't have to listen to his infuriating dialogue.If it weren't for massive issues such as these, I would have happily given this game somewhere between a 7 and 9 out of 10 (depending on how well the later sections play) for its various merits in other areas. As it stands, however, these aspects badly spoiled my experience and I imagine would spoil the experience of many other people. I really hope that the devs might someday patch the game to fix these issues - it wouldn't be too huge a task. A lot could be achieved by swapping out the harassment dialogue for something else (or simply challenging it early and solving it that way) and updating the art for the villain group (to be of various skin tones at minimum).Until that day comes, I hope this review can help people to be aware of these issues before purchasing/playing.You can follow my Steam Curator page at !

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. It's fairly simple as far as tactical RPGs go (you play the whole game with your mouse), but there's a ton of content, the characters are fun, and the story is really interesting. Im also a big fan of the lack of window nesting in combat. Since every character has at most like 5 abilities, all of which depend on how that character acted on their turn (attacking, waiting, assisting, EX, or Ultra), you dont find yourself looking through ability menus in the fight, you just figure out how that unit is using their turn and position appropriately. As much as I love number crunching 'collect all of the attacking abilities' type TRPGS like Disgaea, Tactics Ogre, and FF Tactics, Im a fan of Fae Tactics take on unit effectiveness. You bring the right unit for the job, no duplicates, and you learn to play into that unit's strengths and around their weaknesses. I also really love the Critical system. Whether or not a unit crits against another unit is decided by element, not luck, so playing well and positioning the right units to engage enemies you have an advantage against is just about always rewarded with a faster battle.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't review many games. Matter of fact, I usually don't. Matter of fact, I'm usually actually paid for my writing, so I tend to not do it for free, game reviews or short stories or anything else of substance. But this game deserves everything I can write and more! Ya start out, and it's "oh, cool, kinda looks like FFT ♥, sweet!", then there's "huh, neat systems!", then there's the "lol, cool pop culture references 😹", but there's so much more to it. It takes a masterful degree of artistry to blend a fun and cute tactics game, with meaningful strategic choices at literally every turn; that also had me fighting Harry, Marv, and Kevin at one point...AND can make me cry so much over the trials and sacrifices of the characters! I've not been so deeply challenged and profoundly touched by a game in a very long time, if ever. The contrast is what made it for me. We've all played tons of grimdark games with a gritty edgy feel to them that have those moments of shock and awe. The edgelords of gaming so to speak, their goal seemingly to make folks uncomfortable, using edge instead of compelling story and character development. Or the horror games that rely on jump scares and gore. And so on. Which all get the same "meh" from me. To see a game with such bright cute graphics and cheery music tackling some very real and very profound facets of human nature is such a rare treat! I was not expecting a story that cut me to the bone like this did! I was not expecting to be so utterly heartbroken by, and proud of, the main characters actions at the end of the game. Nor was I expecting the gameplay to have such depth to it!This is a gem. One of the few real true gems of gaming. After feeling like I was searching for gold in my cat's litter box for so long, I finally found a real gem! If this game was a meal, it'd be a free 8 course dinner at one of those snooty restaurants, without the snoot. If it were a person, it would be the person you fall in love and grow old happily with. If it were a day, it would be the last day of school, when you also find out that you won the lotto, and have your first kiss with the person you've been interested in since 5th grade...and you find out they were also secretly interested in you the whole time. "Is it really that good?!?" you might be asking. No, it's better. I'm a legit professional writer, somehow and for some reason, and the magnificence of this game eclipses my ability to describe. I can only hope that a sequel happens...the least of the reasons I was sad at the ending, but still definitely A reason, was that the game was over, there wasn't any more! If you're on the fence about buying this game, do yourself a solid and get it. It's worth it! Without naming names, I've paid way more for games that were less fulfilling and less satisfying and less thought provoking.

IF you finish a battle exceptionally well and get bonus exp... well so do the enemies, if you take 200 days to progress to the next area while doing nothing, well the enemies they don't get stronger... Literally tied to your level, which again, is beyond poor game design.- Boss enemies can quite literally one shot full health and full shield units, up to 5 of your teammates per attack, they can attack three times in a row.  Do the math.- Boss enemies can be revived by any other unit (as can yours), by any spell (well yours can be brought back with heals) and they will simply get back up themselves over time. At time of writing teams's around level 25.Unlike most of the other reviewers i would argue the game has a very low amount of rng, yes enemies can block, parry, evade and so on but on the grand scheme of things in battles it doesn't tend to matter.As an example there's this one electric boss in an area where earth attacks do extra damage, the boss can parry and does so with chain attacks which can annihilate your party. I tried multiple times to beat him with the usual strategy of stacking melee fighters next to him and then spamming ranged and got destroyed, i was really close sometimes but never did it, the rng always balanced out, if i got no parries for too long, i'd then get a few in close succession.So i switched the strategy, i placed the centaur girl up high, buffed her damage a ton and the boss died in 2 hits without me losing a single party member.What i want people to take from this example is that the rng provides only marginal advantages or disadvantages most of the time and it tends to balance out during the course of hard battles.Btw most of the people complaining about it only have 3 to 6 hours so, not a super informed opinion.The game does have issues but i mostly wanna fight back the misinformation in the top reviews.Also comments are enabled if you disagree.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Simple controls, yet the gameplay is rather in-depth. As for the difficulty, although the learning curve can be a bit steep in the beginning, personally I found rather easy once I got used to it. Half the battle is knowing which units/equipment/spells to bring, which keeps the gameplay fresh as you'll be using different parties for different stages. Enemies are scaled to your level, so you can play the various arcs in any order you want, and don't have to grind for levels.I really liked the story too. It was well written, with a good mix of lighthearted and comedic moments, as well as dark and serious moments. I especially liked Eri's arc, and the subtle foreshadowing in it. There are a few grammar errors, though.The music isn't bad either. I like the use of leitmotifs in some of the soundtracks.There are a couple of downsides, though. There isn't any option to skip dialogue which you have already seen, and the combat animations can sometimes be rather lengthy even with 2x speed. Spells which affect multiple allies or enemies are especially guilty of this; the animation plays for each target one at a time. Worse still, some enemy bosses can multicast their spells, so the animation plays 2-3 times.Also, the AI can be rather stupid. Once, an allied NPC I was supposed to protect attacked and unfroze an enemy that I had frozen. Another time, an NPC stood directly in the range of a powerful telegraphed attack, which was rather ironic given that her dialogue before the battle advised against just that. I also sometimes notice enemies wasting their turns operating turrets/cannons that would not hit, or targeting my unit which resisted their element when they could have targeted another one which was weak against them.I'd recommend this if you like strategy games, especially those old school ones.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how many of these turn based RPGs I've played so far. Maybe a dozen. So Fae Tactics was a must-buy. But after playing it for a while, it turned out to be something completly else: Simply not fun to play. Success in battle relies heavily on using combos and therefore positioning your characters on the right spots. But this is tedious, since you can't decide which one moves first. The fastest moves first, the slowest last. Many enemies are so fast that they move after the first half of your party. Making it hard to use/position your party effectively. Especially the slow characters.In addition to that the enemy can spawn a lot of reinforcements. Suddenly you're surrounded by three times as many enemies as there were at the start of the battle. And some can one shot you. Especially cheap when one character stands on a bridge and gets pushed off it.The difficulty itself is pretty random. Maps that have three swords and a skull next to their name can be far easier than a map with only one sword. Do they even symbolize the difficulty? I don't know. Generally there is so much going on that it's hard to pay attantion to everything. After two hours of playtime my main characters alone had 7-8 modifiers each. Every enemy also a bunch. Do you want to read all of them before you do a single move? I don't. And that's just the modifiers.If you see such games more like a puzzle or a game of chess than you can give Fae Tactics a try. But for me, it is just not interesting and fast enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore my scant 2hrs of recording play time, as I'm a convert from piracy :P Excellent indie TBS that's so far managed to keep me hooked on it until 5am and broken my draw to Destiny 2. Helped by a seemingly simple, yet decently deep gameplay system complete with a bit to grindy got-to-catch-them-all minion system that'll have you hooked hunting for the little blitters. Also while the AI enemies can seem very unfair, there are plenty of systems for you to exploit to bring doom down upon them. Even with weaker summons :3 Or by changing Peony's magic attack to another element via scrolls. It also has excellent pixel art and music. Which make the 10's of hours you will sink into this all the more enjoyable :P About the only criticisms I have are:- It's a little opaque sometimes about it's systems, but that's fixable with a manual or guide - Animations can take awhile, which can make bigger battles take a long time to run through each turn for large (15+ enemies and allies) battles. - Absolutely will chuck you in the deep end on normal difficulty :3 - Leader Fae will not drop talisman's, so no trolls or harpies for you. Probably most criticisms of the above will be fixed via patches and game guides, so at this point I consider this game a solid buy-now. Now if you'll excuse me, I need to hunt for some more minions and laugh at the stupider negative recommendations. And get some fluffing dinner already.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is terrible. Full stop.1) Loads of interface issues. It attempts to streamline SRPG play (no superfluous attack types with faux-choice, commands are divvied based on target - none, friendly, hostile, etc), but the execution is so bad it ends up making the flow / experience worse.2) Interface con't - Despite exposing lots of enemy information, it's a dense, poorly organized mess that requires more reading / prep than existing games, and not because the rules themselves are more complicated (does this unit AOE? On which attacks? enjoy spending 5 minutes per unit doing that)3) Poorly designed engine - Game struggles to run a map with 12 sprites on a PC that handles 3d gaming just fine. The sprites are not ultra detailed,4) Poorly designed systems. There's a card system! There's a gear system! there's a scroll system! there's a potato pie system! They're neither useless nor overpowered, but they also don't fit into concert, so it feels like you're just chaining together nonsense words "purple monkey dishwasher" in terms of integrating them into an action plan.5) The dialog display system is so bad, it would bring down my evaluation of this game allllllllll by itself. There's loads of it, and it doesn't have a tap-to-full-display, nor does it roll at a sensible pace, it just. displays two. words when. it feels. like it. which is. very slow. I get this is an indie developer, but it literally would have been less effort to have a better system by just doing less.6) Loading. Inbetween everything the loading is slower than just starting up another game. Imagine how much fun this is combined with #5 when there was a "cut scene" loading a small house, two sprites, and they had a 12 chat bubble conversational exchange, with loading for the battle before, loading for it. loading for after it. and more loading. 7) The system requirements compared to the game you play really should hammer home how bad this is.8) I'm pretty sure I had more, but my first write up disappeared when I went to confirm this wasn't the developer's high school art project because then these comments would be totally unfair and this is a fine semester project by some kids (it's not).9) This game is so bad, that all of the content creators that recommended this game are now very suspect as far as I'm concerned.POSTSCRIPT - I forgot that the post-move "set facing" is so fiddly that I eventually gave up and decided being crit on was simply putting me out of my misery all the faster.

_childDocuments_.review: Fae Tactics is a 2D Iso retro pixel console ported JRPG style turn based tactical game.  Build a party of samey retro pixel whatevers and play a turn based combat game worse than, well, just about every other one that was ever made.Fae Tactics is a bull run attempt at hitting every single bingo card number for "Things You Must Never Do In Game Development".   We got: Lazy retro pixel "Art", no working full screen, 2D graphics, console port on Steam, ripoff of other games, only worse... the list goes on.   Let's break it down. They chose to use obsolete retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result. The game maps PC gaming peripherals (HOTAS, Pedals, Racing Wheels etc) as if they are console peasant childrens toy gamepads.  This makes the player move constantly in one direction and makes the game completely unplayable.  There's no way to turn this off.  The developer would have picked this up with basic testing on PC.There's no working fullscreen mode, and resolution seems locked.  As far as I can tell, see, by mapping PC gaming controllers like they're peasantpads, it's impossible to access the menu and configure the game.  Maybe there is a full screen... but if the controls are so broken that you can't use the menu, that counts as not having a fullscreen mode for all intents and purposes.So we have this massive, epic failure of a crapfest with everything wrong with it.  Definitely a candidate for one of the worst games on Steam.  And they want $20 for it!!!! I'm not even kidding.  This is more expensive than Divinity: Original Sin 2 or Persona 4.   You can't fake this level of delusion.

_childDocuments_.review: Game: Fae Tactics: a strategy turn-based JRP with minor creature collection elements. Traverse a new world where man and magic have been forced together. Play as Peony, a young witch searching the land for her missing mother.  Score: 8/10Pros:•	Unique world containing elements of magic and machine, with a few shakes of Wild West for flavor.•	A wildly varied cast of party members, including a centaur and boxing bird-man.•	Collect fae to fight alongside you, some of which are tricky to find.•	Weapon upgrades that don’t affect damage (per se) but change how the character works on the battlefield. •	The inclusion of some surprisingly dark subject matters despite the cute aesthetic of the game.•	YOU CAN PET THE DOG!!!•	New game plus•	Hidden characters•	Multiple epilogs depending on actions taken in the game.Cons:•	Difficulty—While it can be adjusted between hard and normal, enemies level up based on all story missions you do. This can overwhelm you if you jump right into the game and do story missions. Some grinding helps this (even making it too easy for a time); however, the game will catch up to you by the end.•	Balancing—The game can feel unbalanced with some obviously better characters, weapons, fae, etc. This stifles experimentation with party composition, leading to me forgetting about some.•	Some minor bugs – nothing a quick reset couldn’t fix.•	Everyone moves slow•	Can’t skip the Limit break animations.•	You have to waste turns to pick up items.VVVVVVVVVVVVVVV 	       spoilers past this point		VVVVVVVVVVVVVVVVVVVI enjoyed this game. I love the combination of technology and magic; this game gives it such a refreshing spin. Many worlds and set designs have an almost post-apocalyptic feel, and I enjoyed the maps and ideas explored there. As such, I wish there were more missions that involved us helping out the world's citizens: the bakery plot, helping the fairies living in the abandoned dwarven mines, and the pirate quest. I would have loved more nonstory or party-related side quests.On that, I have some gripes with the story beats, particularly the side stories. Most of these boil down to wanting them to be expanded upon; once you complete a character's side story, they have absolutely nothing to add or say to a situation in the main story. When Claudia joins, she almost seems to cause this to happen to Peony, as Claudia becomes the driving force for the story and game. In addition to that gameplay, she is a little bit broken, and I almost wish she hadn’t become a party member. I also feel this game would benefit from a more linear story progression. This is partly because I think things flow a bit better narratively, giving us more time with certain characters before getting a bunch. On my first playthrough, I did the Kinkin fight late in the game, in which Payachin’s Awakening is locked behind. It felt off for that to happen when it did. Also, I had Claudia with me in Grunhold (as only humans can be used there, even after we're not trying to sneak around), and her lack of comment on the events transpiring also felt off. I know writing for any number of situations can be tricky, and I don’t begrudge the game makers, but having a set path would have avoided all that.Overall, though, there is nothing that makes it unbearable or ruins the story. I played through the game twice and loved my time with it. If anything, my complaints above come from that place of love, wanting to see and experience more of what this game offers. I would have loved to see more of Pichon wooing Orowantus, his determination and heart of gold melting through her wounded heart. I would have loved to see Matilda come to terms with her new body and maybe, with the help of her friends, know peace. I would have loved to see more of Tom’s mischief in his pursuit of food. These untold stories are left to my head, cannon, and imagination, but I hope Endlessly Fluff games will return to this world someday. They captured the makings of something great, hitting a sweet spot of fantasy and dark that doesn’t go too far in either direction. It feels mature without being depressing and whimsical without being too saccharine. If this developer has disbanded, I hope the people behind it at least keep making games and stories because this one was a winner in my book.The Pettiest of complaints and other funny thoughts ( don’t take too seriously) :•	For the love of god, could Peony please close her mouth! Any other character portrait would be nuanced, but that one was just a thorn in my side. •	10/10 sprite work, especially on the Ice Nymph’s ass. Gives 2B a run for her money•	The gem bosses MB is too damn High! •	I really wish there was more to do with the stuff I pick up, especially after finishing the upgrades and Matilda. I finished both of those quickly, and then it was just bugging me to keep getting junk, but it had nothing to do with it.•	Fredrick got “Yamcha-ed”. Hilarious,  but I felt terrible for him, unlike Yamcha.•	♥♥♥♥ the cooking mini-game; I’m so bad at it! The food does look good, so I give you points for that.•	Is Chico’s Stormwulf form a super Sayan reference or a monster Hunter Rajang reference? I’m leaning toward Monster Hunter, but only because I recently watched some videos that attempt to put Rajang’s thunder power into biological terms.

_childDocuments_.review: For the longest time, I have been searching for a game that scratched a very specific itch; that itch being Final Fantasy Tactics Advanced. Advanced specifically, mind you. There are many games that provide the feel of the original FFT, but this is the first game that sent me back to those very fond memories of playing the first game on my Game Boy Advance.It's a charming, colourful game with a lovely and wide variety of characters as you go along your journey. The story moves along nicely, with some nice story plot points that had me theorising and even caught me off guard a couple times. You learn about the world, and the main character as you explore it, her troubles and her inability to not want to help people. The combat is a square tile, turn based RPG. Your characters speed decides the turn order, and their various stats allow them to do various different things on the battle field. Every non-summon character has their very distinctive role, and none of the were ever really benched. The game does a good job and making sure you use all of them, and help you realise where their strengths can be. Most characters on the battlefield, have an element. Fire beat grass, grass beats wind, etc. I like how at any time during battle set up, you can see the type charts, as it could get a little overwhelming sometime. The game is very good at making sure you pay attention to the arena and the enemies in it. Some stages might have pits with enemies that can push you. Some might be very vertical with enemies at the top, teaching you about height advantages. Some stages even have canon placements, where you can either go around or try and power through it. The bosses in particular make sure you always think about your set up before starting the battle, and how you approach them. I played the game on normal, and found it a nice challenge at times. My younger brother played it on hard, and he said it could be quite a slog and the bosses turn into damage sponges. I ran into that issue a couple times, particular with side content bosses. I'd say that's my only real gripe with the game, Magic Barriers can take quite long to reduce. One particular fight near the end of the game, I had the enemy pinned by four units, all comboing crit damage with each other and it still took like, 5 turns as they could barely damage me.Over all, a very strong recommend if you like this sort of combat system. My gaming tip for you all, the Teamwork scroll is very useful. And Apex lets you avoid critical damage a number of times, which can be vital in some fights. Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: TL DR;Pros - Solid and simple gameplay, great soundtrack, lots of stuff to do, lots of stuff to collect, great character design, good story, lots of hours of gameplay, quite some room for customization and optimization;Cons - A few aesthetical choices are bit effy, a couple of battles could be a bit shorter, at times the autosave can be more of an anti-feature, rare freezes and crases;People tend to exaggerate how hard the game is, calling it Dark Souls with rainbows. It is not that hard as long as you properly read and understand the mechanics. The gameplay is simple, yet ellegant. everything is rather squishy as long as you do it right, which includes your characters. Yeah, there are a couple of battles here and there that could be shorter, but for most of the time if the battle is taking too long it is because your strategy is all over the place. Bring the right people, setup the team accordingly and things will go decently fast, otherwise you will be playing a even more colourful version of Hoshigami. Oh yeah, the pixel art is great, but there are a few aesthethical choices - namely pixel aspect ratio - that are a bit weird. It eventually grows into you as mimicking GBA games, but still.
