_childDocuments_.review: Although there is lesser room for strategic thinking compared to similar games, Moving Out offers a chaotic and hilarious experience for anyone who wants a change from the usual co-op games. Yes, there is no story per se and there is no big goal to achieve in-game. What you get with Moving Out is short intense sessions, full of fun, clumsy movements, and high-fives over the gold medals.+ Fun and engaging mechanics with some fresh twists+ Simple, yet addictive gameplay+ Easily accessible for all ages+ Short intense gaming sessions+ You get better with relocations as you play- No solid story to follow- The gameplay might feel repetitive- No online multiplayer- Frogs are annoying as hellWhat if you are tasked to move someone else’s stuff and do it the way YOU want to, without any responsibilities or restrictions? What if you – together with friends – are allowed to stomp, throw, and break things? Could this be fun? The answer is – absolutely! A new title from Team 17 – Moving Out – proves that dragging things to the truck could be both hilarious and joyful. You are a Relocation Technician who has just been certified as an employee of a company called Smooth Moves. Your job – and your team’s – is to help people move from one house to another in Packmore Town. The more popular your clumsy team gets, the more contracts are available for you to get dragged into.Each relocation project in Moving Out is a separate level and it always starts about the same way. You and your team of movers have to drive to the building the occupants want to move out from and load every item in the house into the van you drove to the building. Items in a house can vary from chairs, lamps, and other inanimate objects to living things like pets. Sounds simple? You are in for a big surprise.Every level has a certain number of items that you should drag (or throw) to your van. The tricky part is to move all the items before the time runs out. Depending on how fast you can move the stuff to the truck, you will receive a gold, silver, or bronze medal. While it is easy to blitz through some levels and get quick gold medals, you would have to sweat over and over to achieve bronze medals on others.There is also an Arcade mode that lets you play on a designated map by completing tasks while earning coins and navigating obstacle courses. The Arcade mode is basically a condensed and refined version of what the main levels are.When you complete your first level in Moving Out, the first thought that could pop up in your mind is “Hm, this feels like Overcooked 2! Same chaos, same energy, same tension”. Well, yes, and no. For me, the formula of this game is “Overcooked without stress”. I enjoy cooking series quite a lot, but sometimes it could be very, VERY challenging, putting junior gamers to a halt.  Moving Out is very kid-friendly in a casual way as there is always some task you could assign to kids while adults are dragging sofas and tables.Levels are usually taken 6-12 minutes to complete, which is perfect to keep kids’ attention focused. You complete the level, you refresh, you go for the next, or simply stop.  Simple and fast. Even my wife – who’s idea for a perfect gaming evening is 1-2 hours of Heroes of Might and Magic 3 – happily joins our gaming session. We having fun running around houses, destroying stuff, and throwing things over the pools. It’s just fun.Not everything is perfect of course. The main issue with the game is how dragged out some levels can be. These levels tend to have lots of boxes and items to move which can be boring especially when you have to replay the whole level with your co-op partner. Asides from that, carrying big items such as TVs, sofas can also feel sluggish and not optimized, but I guess this is done on purpose, so you could feel the size and the weight of the furniture.By far, I believe you have already figured out, that the game should only be played in couch co-op mode. There is no online multiplayer and there is just no fun in playing solo. So grab whoever can properly hold a controller and start moving things around.

_childDocuments_.review: I started Moving Out mere hours after helping my roommate move in real life. Tired from lifting couches and tables, the gamified version was leagues more fun - namely because it didn't matter if I broke anything. Despite moving being the last thing I wanted to focus on that day, Moving Out's streamlined gameplay loop and ingenious level design quickly shoved away those feelings. Instead, I enjoyed a fully-realized gameplay experience that sells the idea of becoming a master mover. Best described as Overcooked, but moving, Moving Out stars your animal character as an aspiring mover-outer in the lovely little town of Packmore (also known as a Furniture Arrangement & Relocation Technician or F.A.R.T.) Your boss finds gigs and exploits you and up to three friends to carry belongings out of people's houses. Only, a mysterious client starts asking for suspicious boxes to be moved, hinting at a more sinister plot at play. It's up to you to find out what's going on.The story is delivered in short, three to four phrase conversations at the beginning and end of each stage. These generally consist of your character's hilarious ignorance (the boss is useless and totally taking advantage of you) and pop culture quips, but hints of the greater plot at hand are sprinkled in between conversation and the stages themselves.For the rest of my review on TechRaptor, check out this link:

_childDocuments_.review: This is my absolute favorite game of all time. I really, REALLY love this game and I would love to play it whenever I have enough time to spend. Here are some pros and cons of the game!<Pros>1. The concept of the game is very good; You have to pick up items from each house (with each house acting as one level respectively), and take them to the moving truck parked next to the house. This gets pretty fun to do because you have to plan out all the routes and have to think which objects to move before the other. The process is even more fun when you play with friends.2. The game is well-balanced; One player, two players, three players, four players- all are very much enjoyable without any trouble on terms of balance. The game controls its difficulty accordingly to the number of people in the game, and you can pretty much beat the levels if you just yearn over it. If you have a troublesome member who just can't get a level done (especially in the Arcade, which is a place where players do challenging stuff that's a bit different from the main levels), you can just play the level next time without that player to beat the level, and move on further to another level. If you and your mates aren't that good at cooperative play, maybe you can play alone to stack some gold medals and achieve bonus objectives. Everything stacks up if you just use the same slot (to save the games), so you don't need to worry that much. (i.e. After you saved the game after four players played together, you can still go load the saved game and still have the progress intact. Maybe you can earn some golden medals alone and join your friends later to boast about them :>)3. Everything is pretty self-explanatory; You'll notice when you play the game, but everything is pretty much self-explanatory. When the object you're holding is too burdening, your character would start sweating/farting/or something else, which means you would need another player to help you.4. The design is very well-done; The graphics, characters, colors- they're all absolutely amazing.5. The soundtrack is awesome; I feel like the upbeat music helps me work harder and enlighten the mood up! <Cons>1. You must play locally; I tried gifting this game without knowing that this game does not support online co-operation... you *could* use Steam Remote Control, but it won't work well if your computer is laggy.2. The controls for the keyboard are quite inconvenient in my opinionl; The controls for a controller (I use XBox) are pretty okay, but for the keyboard, you would have to span through a lot of keys. Once I invited a friend over to play this game, but it turned out that two players playing with one keyboard is very elusive, especially because my keyboard did NOT have a Right Ctrl key. If you don't have a Right Ctrl key or a controller, you should consider that disadvantage.I did indeed have some troubles with this game at first, but it didn't take long for me to get adapted to everything and absolutely love this game. I would like to rate this game a 9.9/10! Thank you developers for crafting such an amazing game- I just love the concept and everything because I really like organizing my house myself IRL, lol. Anyway, have fun playing, y'all!

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy games like Overcooked and Out of Space, then this will scratch a similar itch while providing a more open level design.By abandoning Overcooked's recipes, Moving Out encourages players to experiment with their approach to each level. Does one tackle the couch in the back room first? Or maybe start by clearing out the garage? The levels are not procedurally generated, as in Out of Space, which means that players can test to see if one strategy is faster than another. Considerable communication skill is also required, arguably even more so than Overcooked. Many objects require players to work in tandem, which means that both must be able verbally indicate how they want their partner to manipulate that heavy fridge or hop across that croc infested river.While the skill ceiling is rather high for the game, the developers are clearly trying to cater to a casual audience. There are various accessibility settings that effectively remove the time crunch of the game (and with it, all need for strategy). Also on the fun side are bonus challenges, specific to each level, that players can optionally include in their runs. To get the most out of the game, then, you'll need at least one dedicated partner with whom to develop a communication strategy. If you already enjoy this genre, then you probably already have that partner ready to go. If your new to these types of games, Moving Out is an excellent example of the genre. Try the demo (which also allows for remote play) to see if it suits you!

_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Moving Out is a phenomenal game! I'm surprised more people don't already know about it.It's a game in which you are hired on as part of a moving company. Your job? Move people's stuff!It's silly and goofy, the wobbly physics of hauling stuff to the truck are great, and there's a fair amount of skill involved in getting all of the objects through any obstacles and to get them all to fit! In addition, there's a lot of options to adjust the difficulty of the game, if you're struggling with certain elements, and they do not affect the achievements or the quality of the play. I really enjoyed every minute of both the main game and the DLC. It's sort of designed with the idea of co-op in mind, but you can play singleplayer too, in fact that's how I completed every bit of this game.Overall this is just a really fantastic game, I think it'd be a really fun time with friends, but there's also plenty of fun to be had on your own. I'd highly recommend playing with controller for a smoother experience, I can't remember exactly now but I had issues and found I had to have a controller. It's just a really fun, really funny, game. 10/10, would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Get this game if you enjoy hectic gameplay, puzzles, platforming, and/or want something to play with people who will no longer play Overcooked with you (lol). I got this game some time in January after watching DrLupo play it with his brothers. I already had the game on my WL but watching someone play was what got me to buy it, esp since it was on sale at the time. I didn't play the game, however, until last week. I wanted to try it with friends and got them to join me through Parsec because there's still a pandemic. Four days and ~23 gameplay hours later, I have a 100% achievement completion rate in the game. I think the only things I haven't done now are getting a few Platinum medals and completing Moving In levels. Here is what I have to say:PROS:+ Very funny (to me) and humor is clean from what I remember+ Simple but effective tutorials+ Music and graphics are great+ Tons of fun+ Even more fun with friends+ Many maps even without the DLC+ There's a lot to do even without the DLCCONS: - Can get frustrating very quickly- Some objectives feel repetitive- Movement, esp with some objects, can feel a bit wonkyOverall, I think this is a great game. It was addictive. The completionist in me was pushed to just do and collect every little thing that I could. I got Movers in Paradise almost immediately after completing the base game because I was having fun and wanted more to do.

_childDocuments_.review: The concept is great, but the physics are janky to the point of being frustrating.This is mostly the case when loading items into the truck, which is like Tetris in some ways: trying to arrange a lot of items to fit into one space, while fighting against the physics engine as things continuously tumble back out of the truck.  Throwing items onto the truck, rather than walking them up, can help prevent this, but it's still very hit-or-miss in my experience.There's an "Assist Mode" where you can disable that (by having items disappear as soon as they hit the truck), but with that on, the game feels *too* simple and repetitive: all you're doing at that point is moving items from point A to point B repeatedly.It's a clever take on a concept Overcooked popularized, but you're supposed to be frustrated with whatever your friends are doing, not frustrated with the physics engine.  Overall, I'd say stick with Overcooked 1 & 2 + their DLC, which are all much better games, and buy this only if you've exhausted all of that content and are hungry for more of the formula.

_childDocuments_.review: Moving Out is a pretty much a perfect game for hot seat. I understand that people complain why there isn't online multiplayer available, but being an old school gamer who likes to enjoy his multiplayer games with friends that are physically present, I don't really have issues with the matter.The basic idea of the game is simple and fun, and everyone can easily get the hang of it. From all the "party games" that I have presented to various people, I think this one has likely being the best received. For example Moving Out could be easily compared to Overcooked -games and although I do like those also, an average player seem to lost their interest / mind way easier with them. Moving Out feels a bit less hectic and gameplay is a bit more enjoyable, even if you are not that experienced gamer.Then again being a really good in the game and getting all the gold medals etc. requires some practice. After playing the game tens and tens of hours I was able to receive all the gold medals in the single player mode. Then again platinum times seem to be really hard to reach even with the know how + skill I have gathered with these playing hours. Could be that with couple of experienced friends the platiums would be way easier to achieve. And of course it could also be, that I just suck.I like to collect achievements and those are done just about right; challenging, but not too challenging. For example if there would be a achievement related to the platinum times, it would be way too hard for a normal gamer, but the gold medals are perfectly doable with just a bit practice.Although I really love the game, one negative thing needs to be mentioned: "That's Not Landfill!" -achievement (=Deliver the hidden console from each story level) was broken for eleven months before it was fixed. The issue was reported basically right away when the game was released in 2020 and since then multiple users (myself included) continued to inform that the achievement isn't working, until on 11 months later the fix finally arrived. Not something that an average player worries about, but pretty annoying for a person like me, who likes to collect all the achievements from the best games.Well, like said that one issue is fixed now, so nothing to complain anymore. Highly recommended especially for hot seat, but works fine as a single player game also.

_childDocuments_.review: DON'T LISTEN TO THE NEGATIVE REVIEWS. Any negative review slandering it for being couch co-op only is poisoning the reviews. Yes, the game is couch co-op only, yes it is meant to be played with multiple people, and yes, it came out during a time where that isn't possible. HOWEVER, Steam Remote Play makes that extremely easy for everyone to play together, and it means only one person has to buy it (making it better IMO). Yeah maybe not everyone gets stellar graphics because you are playing with someone else remotely but I think that is a fair trade off.To the review: I have a group of friends that I play with and we absolutely love this game. We have perfected 4 levels so far and did a few side missions at about 3 hours of game time. Honestly, it is better than Overcooked in my opinion because it is way less focused on actually coordinating with your teammates and more about doing your own thing, sometimes with the assistance of others. There are unique challenges for each level that add a bit of replayability to them, and also the usual rush to get the best time. They also have an arcade and other special levels that are different from the usual levels, leaving room for many hours of fun. If you have a group of friends to play remotely with, I HIGHLY recommend it especially if you enjoyed Overcooked and Overcooked 2.

_childDocuments_.review: For some reason, people seem to not like this game. I can't figure out those people.So, Moving Out. Got it on sale (like every single other game I have ever got) for a good price. Next thing you know, I can't get enough of this wonderful game!Ok, so, it seems to me that people think this game is no good because it doesn't have multiplayer, and playing it yourself is lonely. The first one is sorta true. Though multiplayer would be nice, it would take  to much time to add, and I'm not sure how many people would actually use it due to it probably going to be overloaded with idiots. The second thing I totally don't find it lonely at all. Even though you're doing all the moving yourself, the story makes it quite interesting. There is also boss (He's indestructible) who often makes plenty of interesting remarks, and there is always one more character who is sitting in the truck (Teamwork!) that often talks with your character, also making interesting and funny remarks. (They did fix the "That's Not Landfill" achievement btw) I have also heard that some people don't like the later levels. _childDocuments_.review: So many games try to transplant Overcooked's fantastic gameplay to different themes... And so far they all failef. That's because the nature of cooking is essential to its success. The fact that you constantly have to wait for stuff to get cooked/fried, do other things in the meantime to optimise BUT come back at just the right moment so food doesn't get burned creates constant tension and little loses/victories. No other theme has the same dynamic (at least none attempted by Overcooked wannabeed) so the games fall back to grading you on total time needed to perform all task. Which is way, WAY less engaging that frantically dashing towards a steak that about to get burned to you can serve it mere seconds before a guest leaves out of frustration.Moving out is in the same boat. It's... OK. But not even in the same ballpark when it comes to engagement. It also doesn't force task splitting tasks between players which, once again, makes the game  less fun. Honestly, it's kinda boring, and I was trying really hard to like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I had a fun with the game, I don't recommend this game in general.The idea is great, the execution is not good. A lot of players are rating this game positive, but how much playtime do they really have? Did they even finish the game?If you just want to finish all the levels once, the game feels funny with weird controls. The physics feel janky at times when pieces get stuck and the characters have a very heavy feeling to them like you would control a crane. However, it's fun.Each level however has a gold time (now even a platinum time) to beat for a medal and 3 extra goals.While the first levels seem fun and pack a small challenge, this goals really turn the game upside down. There are levels that go for 6mins and if one of the players missteps once, the level has to be restarted. If you combine this with the heave and indirect player controls and put time pressure, it ends up in frustration for everyone and really takes the fun away.Comparing this game to the competition just shows that the game is not well thought through. I recommend sticking with Overcooked, Unrailed, Out of Space etc. If you already finished all those games and you're looking for more content you can try this game. But you've been warned about the frustrated and unfair challenges in the later game.The DLC levels are a little better than the original ones.UPDATE:Currently doing a second playthrough and it reconfirms my review.I'm stuck solo on Contraband Cluster getting gold time because the printer is not entering the trick in more than 50% of the cases. There is so much jank in this level, I wonder if it has been tested properly. Casually this game is fun, trying to 100% it, is pure pain.

_childDocuments_.review: My girlfriend fell in love with the Overcooked series and we straight out brought everything from Overcooked 1 and 2 including DLCs. When we found that the same developers made this, well it was basically a holiday for us. But 20 minutes into the game, and my girlfriend and I were already frustrated with the game. It's clunky, and what made Overcooked so lovable was that the objectives were clear, and the controls were also amazing. This game's keyboard controls are just not intuitive at all, and what sucks is we're kind of held back not by our skills but rather by the design of the game that just stops us from doing our best, by that I meant we spent 20-30 seconds just trying to hold a bed, and another 30 wondering if it's even going to fit through the door.Another thing that made Overcooked so good was it really created a strong sense of urgency, something that we're not getting here. I'm really disappointed to be returning this game, but I'm hoping that Team17 can work on this and improve it further. Cheers to you guys and great job regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: Moving Out is a co-op focused console ported 3D rendered top down action/physics game where you must hustle boxes and furniture into a moving van, while avoiding various obstacles on the sometimes mazelike maps. While the game does support 4K, the graphics are excessively lazy ripoffs of the Nintendo Wii low poly art style.   This art style was presumably used to cover up a lack of budget/talent from the developers in arranging more contemporary graphics, but then some degree of polish went into the game despite using poor quality low poly "art".  Talk about lipstick on a low poly pig. Inexplicably there's no online co-op, but local co-op for PC is a lot like an ashtray on an iron lung.   It's probably very appealing to console peasants who like that kind of thing, but this is Steam.   Finally, the controls on this game are a dogs breakfast.  They're just sloppy, loose, and unresponsive.  That's less fun than the premise for the game.  Don't take my word for it, however.  The game is so bad that only 60% of the people who own it on Steam bothered to complete the 2 minute tutorial.  Ouch.So, we have a badly done console port on Steam, with sloppy controls, lazy low poly Nintendo Wii ripoff "art", and the developers never heard about the internet so they didn't consider online gaming.  How much would you expect to pay?  $2? You got it!  Oh no wait.  Now the genuine fun begins.  The developers seriously seemed to think this is worth $25 USD.  More money than Doom Eternal costs on sale.  Finally, this game gave me some genuine amusement.

This was crucial during the final level, because the movement really had to be precise, but the objects themselves forced repeating each phase of the stage too many times.The game nailed the humour - it's dumb and naïve, but in a good way and it made me chuckle a few times. And of course you want to throw furniture through the window to save time, who wouldn't?Recommended for short gaming sessions in 2-4 people - may get stale pretty quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute and often challenging yet rewarding game. I often get bored of games and move on quick, but even now having 100% completed the game I anticipate going back to play levels from time to time. If anyone is looking to play to completion I recommend keeping track of what achievements you've gotten and what you've done for each level. This is especially important for getting the consoles, animals, standing on the toilets, and slapping the mailboxes. While Steam technically keeps track of these achievements you may accidentally think you've gotten them all and then get to the end and then realize you're missing one somewhere and you don't know what level you're missing (definitely not speaking from personal experience or anything). However, I absolutely adore this game. The DLC is amazing as well, it plays as fun as the game with a few extra fun elements which keep it interesting. I am also someone who enjoys a good story-line and I love the silly little story-line this game has, which has the antics continue even into the DLC which is awesome! Truly just a great game, especially to play with friends! <3

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this exclusively for the purpose of playing with my kids. We were able to split keyboard and use a controller so all three of us could play. From what I understand there can be any combination of up to 3 controllers and up to 2  people on keyboard. I'm not too concerned that online play isn't an option, we have DSL speeds because of our location. There are parts that definitely make you work as a team to win. But if it gets too hard there is an option to change difficulty or change certain features to make it easier on the player. I disabled some of the things that were frustrating us and it improved our experience. The best part is the features can always be turned back on as we improve with practice at our own pace. Also has text size and dyslexia friendly accessibility options. The graphics aren't demanding on the RTX 3070, and I imagine many systems would be able to handle it at at least mid quality video settings. Game play is simple but made into a challenge with a timer, obstacles, hazards, goofy physics that make you feel bouncy, and the occasional wild pet. Players can customize their character but there aren't so many options that you spend hours in the selection menu. Replay value varies depending on your skill level and what settings you have enabled and whether or not you want to try for the bonus points. There is a humorous approach to the story and some darker humor along the way. The employees make jokes and references to the lifestyle attached to manual labor in a joyful nonchalant and eerily accepting manner. I'm waiting for the boss to admit the employees legally signed off their personhoods to the company. So far this game has made us laugh and rage but mostly it's made us laugh. The only thing I don't like is the orientation of the controls being at an angle, to the map. Intuitively I want to only use up to go up, left to to go left etc. However that sends you at an angle along the map instead of perpendicular to the map. So in order to go up the map in a straight line, the up and left or up and right keys must be held down. To go left or right it's the same concept. That makes it extremely hard to play for anyone who struggles with hand and finger control that might be on the keyboard or using only the keypad.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: only one person needs to own this game as you are forced to play with steam remote, parsec, or couch co-op. for people with not the greatest internet, this might pose a struggle when playing multiplayer. this game combines the frantic pressure of moving out with silly physics that leave players dying of laughter. it makes players come up with solutions to many problems such as runaway chickens, heavy couches that require multiple people, and fitting everything into a singular van. the levels are unique, and there are many of them on top of the hidden achievements. a big selling point for me was that it has accessibility modes,  which can make it easier for you if you are struggling with a particular level. i only used it in the factory with the goo to give myself extra time to complete it. there are multiple settings you can toggle to make a unique and fair experience. i found the dialogue to be witty and the game to be an overall solid pick for any co-op enthusiasts. i got my copy on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: for those who say that theres no online playeven though that is true, that doesnt mean that parsec doesnt existyou can play this game with your friends there ONLINE, or you can use the arcade ption there to stream it to different people and play it aswell with themit doesnt take much memory and its really handy for other stuff like literally streaming to friends what youre building in minecraft or anything thats on your computer reallyit (mostly) doesnt lag and its the same quality as your monitor. i really recommend this game to play w/friends and also get parsec
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Good enough game, probably more fun in multiplayerControls are FINE, they have their frustrating quirks, like the character frequently getting stuck because furniture sticks to any wall it touches, but otherwise they aren't bad, but could be better and less physics reliantThe artstyle is cute and charming and the dialogue kinda witty, pretty good presentation over allLevels are fine, but they feel all a bit too sameyAlso not cool locking the platinum goal until after clearing around 5 levels, why not since the beginning? What's the point in blocking that?
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I haven't played for very long yet, but I do wanna give a shoutout to the devs for both the accessibility features AND the option to have your character in a wheelchair.My little sister uses a wheelchair and has limited mobility, her eyes absolutely lit up once she saw that her character could use a wheelchair. She was so happy to have a character like her, and I was happy that the accessibility features would allow us to play together and have fun <3
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Played this using Parsec due to no official online play. This game is a lot of fun. The biggest and I mean BIGGEST flaw. It has NO online play. Maybe not matchmaking as that would be horrendous and possibly very hard to play (maybe code?), but peer-to-peer CO-OP online would be very nice. Small games like this and other "Indie" titles get looked over by myself, friends and many others due to no online function. Couch CO-OP restriction knocks this game down a lot for me. But, if you use Parsec or Steam Remote play (when it decides to work), it is barrels of fun and can't imagine the fun on couch CO-OP but no gamer friends IRL over here.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah alright, it's not Overcooked. But there's still a lot of fun to be had here. In some ways it's a better on-ramp for people who have zero gaming experience, but it's also more frustrating to deal with the controls that actively "spin" your character when you're holding something, causing you to walk off ramps unintentionally and such. Buy on sale, enjoy probably the first half of the game. Especailly the farm level. Oh man, the farm level.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Hard Yes.It's like Overcooked... only better somehow. Yes, I said it. It's better than the product that inspired it. In fact, I'd call Moving Out the current king of the 'multitasking co-op' genre.I've tried a fair few competing products and they just aren't anywhere near as fun (or funky) as Moving Out.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC! We are on level TWO, and I say that with full confidence. You can use a controller, play with up to 4 other people, and the game actually runs well on my computer. There are hidden jokes (like the graphics settings), and tons of achievements. The art style is adorable, and the game isnt too hard. And if it is? There is an assist mode, which is the first I've seen of its kind. I have right arm pain from under my ear to my fingertips and down the side of my ribs. I don't have much hand control left. I'm in my mid twenties. If I were older, or much younger, or had worse disabilities, I'm sure I'd appreciate it even more. But with my condition the way it is, I cried upon seeing that. There are settings for everything, and once you turn on a setting for one player, you can change it for the other. Example being tap to pick up and tap to throw if you can't hold the button down. There's customizable characters with wheelchairs, and 2 difficulty settings I've seen. It had us asking ourselves why games aren't like this all the time. Thank you for setting hopefully a new standard to future game makers, Moving Out, and thank you for all the time and effort you put into this game. It shows, even this early on. Thank you thank you thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing imagine human fall flat meets overcooked. It's chaotic, funny, challenging and really well designed. Whilst many chave complained about the lack of online co-op, I have had absolutely no issues with using the Steam remote play with friends and I have had no issues whatsoever. We both have solid computers and good internet speeds. The game is really well designed, funny throughout with many Easter eggs and jokes which make it enjoyable. I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Moving Out is an amazing little couch co-op physics based game where you and your buddies have to work together to move all of the required objects into the moving van, trying to do it as fast as possible. After completing a mission for the first time you also unlock bonus objectives that add more challenge, like not being able to break any windows. I loved playing this game, it is a bit harder solo cause you can’t move heavy objects as easily and you have less hands to do the work, but its still fun. I was able to play it with some members of my family (one person on the keyboard, and one using a controller), and we had a lot of fun. Relatively easy to pick up for non-gamers. The game also just oozes charm, silliness, and the graphical style is just so pleasing to look at.I do agree, however, that online coop is very much needed. While the game is fun with friends, in this day and age it isn't as easy to get people to come over just to play a game on your PC.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: This game was hilarious to play with a group of friends. The more friends (max players of course) you have to play the funnier it gets. Definitely recommend for a game night or party game as it definitely makes the time go by. This game makes you use teamwork and strategy to win and can be very complicated on certain rounds. Definitely recommend to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Just like Overcooked, Moving Out is a chaotic co-op game that mixes silly fun with unique gimmicks and real challenges. It's easy to learn, and it's a game for all, from the advanced gamers to total beginners. The humor is quirky and cute, and I loved interacting with all the hidden parts of each level, getting all of the challenges, and playing through the memory levels. My favorite part about this game is Assist Mode, which makes the game easier in various ways you can toggle. It made a second playthrough a lot more enjoyable because we could ignore the most frustrating parts of the game and focus on the achievements. My friends and I had a blast with this game, and I cannot recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very fast paste game with lots of fun homes to move out off, I would want more of my friends playing it cuz team work is key! The designs are very cute and it's always something adorable or totally random to play as, I was just an green egg with a (not) vilking helmet and braids. I do recommend this and the dlc looks amazing as well so looking forward to that!
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun coop game. If by fun you mean mental abuse your friend, surely you will love this game. The levels are so easy and fun if you dont know what fun is. Please, I recommend everyone to play this game since I've played it, and feel how stressed the ♥♥♥♥ I am, I want you all to feel the same. Btw Rats are dumb af, they should just extinct tf off. Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Look, the game is "OK". It has some interesting mechanics, and is sorta fun for a party game. It's not as fun as Overcooked or Out of Space, but there's a lot of content here - 30 base levels, 3 objectives each, lots of hidden achievements, secrets and Easter eggs, then alternate mode with "moving in". The devs put a lot of effort in, just premise-wise note really that exciting. Played this couch co-op with my wife, this game would be practically unplayable as single player.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Only get this if you played through both overcookeds and you are still hungry for more, even if 'more' is effectively the bargain bin version of gameplay and the humor falls flat. Even the gf lost interest (Kevin kept her riveted through 2 Overcooked games+all DLC).Also, this is a co-op focused arcade-ish game released in the 2nd half of 2020 with no online mp. WHY?!
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, i played it alot on PS4 + Switch, so thats why i only have 4 hours on it here. I played it with some friends on PC and also other platforms! And it is one of my favorite games of all time, love what they have done with this! And i was so happy when it received the first DLC "Movers in Paradise" because i could not wait to get back into the game, and this time on vacation! Nothing else to say 10/10 Perfect co-op game!
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever questioned if someone is just that stupid?No more. Invite these people to move the sofas around and you will have all your questions cleared.Thinking on how expensive is college or university?Ask your kiddos to move the refrigerator in collaboration and decide if that invesment will really worth.Amazingly fun is not enough to describe this game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game but it would be great if multiplayer functionality was added.  Remote play has not worked both times I tried to play the game with friends in two different parts of the world.  I am sure if you were locally sharing a computer it would work fine that is not an option for me and my friends.  It is difficult to share how great the game is and knowing that they also created Overcooked with multiplayer functions well seems like they could get that part as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really great. Lots of laughs and little details and really fun gameplay. What I love about it is "assist mode" where if you're struggling with a level you have a whole menu to tweak the difficulty. You can tick boxes to personalise it to how you want, you can add time to the time limit, reduce the difficulty overall, have items disappear once on the truck to save space, make the items lighter to carry, etc. You can even skip the level entirely if you fail it. This means the game is always fun to play because you can reduce frustration if you get really stuck, and make the game just slightly easier. You can then just turn it off after you get past the part you're stuck on. I wish more games would have this feature because I game mostly with my Mum and she can struggle when the difficulty is too high. Highly recommended, and I also recommend buying the DLC
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: It's not quite at the dizzying heights of OverCooked, but it's still fun. Some definite teething problems in the early months of release that they ironed out with patches. The gameplay, like OverCooked, has a style that it sticks to throughout, and overall I and my partner had a lot of fun. AGAIN like OverCooked, there was also a strange learning curve which meant that every fifth level or so was mad difficult while the rest were easy.Loved the sarcastic workers as well. Their miserable dedication to their work was admirable :P
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Great game but it more a console game, if you want to play with your friend via steam remote play either you or they have to use the controller. 2 Players coop via remote play is controller-free.3 and 4 players will need at least 2 more controllers ^_^Having a great time playing this, recommend to get the DLC too so the game will have more replay values. Steam remote play may suck if your internet or your friend's internet is bad, So keep that in mind. 7/10 compare to other coop games like Overcooked, Battleblock but still great
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: It is both a very cool game and very funny. Even though you're essentially doing the same thing over and over again, it doesn't feel too monotonous and it's easy to pass the time if you get bored. Although it's true that it's best if you have a friend to play with, it's also fun to play alone. The only thing I don't like is that it's a lot harder to get gold medals in Solo than the creators think, but otherwise it's a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like games where you just run around frantically shouting at your friends and family telling them what to do?Is Overcooked 2 a bit too stressful? If you answered yes to these, then this game may be the one you've been looking for, it's absolutely crazy and brilliant fun. You can even play alone and the game changes the levels slightly so you can move items without help.play with 2 to 4 players though for the best fun, it is guaranteed to make you swear and get frustrated but all in good fun :) I have changed the controls to toggle the pickup/drop buttons to make it easier to play on XBOX ONE controllers, otherwise holding the bumper and running and throwing can all get a bit messy :) The graphics are awesome as you'd expect from Team 17, cute and perfectly drawn I turned the music off and put Spotify on in the background with some 80's tunes, it seemed to work well ;) Buy it now while it's on offer, it's well worth the money. One thing I will add is that when I bought it thought the Sale, I was not offered the Deluxe addition :( If I had seen that I would have bought that instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute classic. Hilarious, chaotic, strategic, and just flat out fun. A great time with any number of players and satisfying to go back to get all the things you missed, or just improve your time by a second or two. Chock full of laughs and good times. This is one of those games I get on pretty much every system I have, just because it's always worth playing alone or with friends wherever you are.As others have said, though, it's a real shame there is no online multiplayer built into a game that so heavily relies on playing with others for most of its entertainment value.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy playing this game and the dlc is very fun too, however, half the levels in the base game are quite frustrating, the dlc did a better job. I much prefer the levels where you clear out different houses by throwing stuff out windows rather than trying to move a sofa while you're being shot at and you're surrounded by lava.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Our family's absolute favourite game and the very best local multi-player *actually* co-op game I have ever played.6YO and 8YO playing with their Mum who doesn't really game and struggled with Overcooked 1&2 all find this an absolute delight.  The "Assist mode" is perfectly pitched down to the loading screen suggesting "Not having fun?  Why move if you aren't enjoying it?".  It has loads of tweaks to let you tailor game-play to let all the players have the perfect blend of challenges and can even be tweaked mid-game.The humour is hilarious from the quirky characters to the game-intro comments and cheesy voice-over comments.The level select screen is so good, the kids spend time playing that while waiting for their parents to get drinks!There are even bonus levels you can earn through speedy completion and others through crazy achievements.I'm a game developer and I don't think I can fault a single thing this game does.  It's... astonishing!If you like actual co-op, just buy it!HTH :)
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Its a fun Couch coop. It is not as great as overcooked, but it scratches the same itch. I would not pay 20 euro for this, but it is one of the most played games, from the bundle i got it in. The base mechanics are simple but fun. New mechanics are presented in just a high enough amount and interval to not get boring. because the game is so simple, every map doesnt have a long longevity. especially not with the same people. the game is NOT easy to 100%, so if you like chasing such a thing, this game is way harder to do  it in than overcooked(1+2). overall: this game is now part of my "regular" couch coop games.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, especially for the co-op play.We enjoyed this quite a bit. The graphics are cute, audio fitting and the gameplay is pretty interesting. There are various levels with bonus objectives and a neat set of challenge levels that you can unlock too. The controls can sometimes feel a bit wonky, but its part of the charm. It is definitely a bit on the short side of content for the price as it expects you to play the same levels over again for the unlocks, but if you get it on sale, its definitely a fun co-op game.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable, not only is it just like the Overcooked series, but it's actually a lot more relaxed. The mechanics of the game are fairly simple, you take furniture from the house and throw it in a van. How you get it there is the fun part, throw it out the window, run it through doors that spank you back. The game is silly, and so enjoyable if you play with friends.At the moment the game is only playable on LAN so that means you must Steam Remote Play or other game sharing services.That being said, this game is so enjoyable alone, or with friends. The maps are made realistic and the times for them are actually beatable if you go for them with some kind of plan.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Great party game. It's a lot of fun and truly chaotic playing with this friends! I've been playing through with my girlfriend and she loves it because it's such a simple concept.For a while it's a lot of fun since each level slowly adds more and more complex mechanics, like holding down buttons, or conveyor belts.. but eventually you come across a few levels where you'll have to balance on a tiny ramp and if you fall or drop your items, they respawn in the default position. That's when we stopped progressing and just went back to the early levels because it was too frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Turn on Assist Mode!  It doesn't affect achievements and you'll have more fun.Objects disappear once you load them in the truck, carrying big furniture feels right (playing solo), and gold medal times are much more forgiving.  It's very satisfying to run around, throwing light objects across the map, bonking heavy objects into all the walls and windows.Without Assist Mode, the game has some unfun features that maybe sounded good on paper like: loading physics objects in the truck, or having big furniture feel clunky to move by yourself (I played solo).  God tier gold medal times that maybe require two players to earn.The game even suggests to turn on Assist Mode if you're not having fun, but I think they should have just turned it on by default, and labeled the default: Hard / Unfun Mode.Turn on Assist Mode and get movin!
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: -Art direction and sounds support the wacky aesthetics you’d expect from a party game-Core gameplay loop is solid and entertaining-Only multiplayer option is local co-op-Physics (tables and arcade machines particularly) and geometry (moving through doors) can become heavily annoying from time to time-Complete lack of a story and the jokes/puns are horrible, that being said, that’s not exactly a priority in games of this genre, but still, I’d advise you give this title a chance and take it out for a spin,For more detail on the above points and a look at gameplay, please feel welcomed to check my thoughts in this video:.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to overcooked, your team needs to cooperate and find creative ways to move all of the necessary furniture and load them onto the truck as fast as possible. Hidden missions that reveal themselves upon level completion can offer some challenge for replayability. In addition to the hidden missions, your primary goal is to move out as fast as possible. Just yeet some furniture out the window and hope they dont break
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Moving stuff has never been so much fun. Getting through the game is rather easy and doesn't take very long, but you  can spend countless hours improving your times and getting the special achievements that unlock more content for the arcade mode and historical missions. And if it's too hard for you or your kids, you can always enable various assist modes.I just don't get all the complaints about no online multiplayer. I played solo and enjoyed every minute of it, especially after enabling easier 2-person item handling in the assist mode. All I missed was not being able to throw couches around. Besides, you can always play it with steam remote play together, without having to buy the game for each person involved.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great fun to play with friends, very similar to Overcooked (a good thing!). Apart from the SPACE LEVELS... RIDICULOUS! And there are quite a few of them. Would really prefer ordinary houses (but larger and more difficult), offices or industrial levels instead. Everyone I have played with found the space thing not fitting very well.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Played with the SO, slapped him silly for a job well done, blocked his path so he fell into the pool while carrying a table, and we're still together! This is a great game if you're looking for something light to spend some time together. It's like overcooked, with a splash of absurdity and ghosts/chicken/livestock chasing after you while you try to move furnitures.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: + the gameplay itself provides tons of family fun and laughter!- however, controls get can absolutely clunky (horrible) and tends to get remapped halfway through the gameplay (e.g. player 1's Hold button suddenly swapped with player 2's), ruining our tempo and spoiling most of the fun. Happens 10 out of 10 matches in the 2 hours I've played. Literally unplayable.- also, no multiplayer mode outside of "local co-op".Why is the developer doing this? Sigh.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: I did not expect to enjoy this game as much as I did. The game surprised me with its variations, and the first half of the game doesn't do coop justice. But stick through the first 10 or so levels and the second half does bear rewards. I only wish they expanded more on the second half of the game.Some nitpicks I have with the game:1. Its time targets are fairly brutal for two players (we never got a single gold and only a sprinkling of silvers), which in itself didn't feel very achievable either.2. The game only tracks gold medals, so we never knew how many levels we completed up until the end. (And loading the save after the end tells me I've only done 25% of the game, which isn't very accurate either.)3. Levels are sprawled over the city and not numbered. While it gives a nice environmental ambience, it doesn't help with doing a second run-through since you can't go in order any longer.4. The world map camera is zoomed too far in. you can't see many levels and your progress with those levels at a glance. Coupled with the number of obstructions around town, surveying the lay of the land and levels is tough.5. The direction you grab onto something was slightly finicky, so we had to realign ourselves a lot of times (especially when you need to be on opposite ends to throw items).
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just like the Overcooked 2 chaotic and funny and really good to play with friends, but after ~5 hours it gets terribly hard and annoying. The difficulty curve is just terrible. In the first few hours it's easy to complete the levels to bronze medal, but hard to complete to silver or gold, as it should be in a couch game, but after that it gets just annoyingly hard.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: This is a little more forgiving on your relationships than Team 17's other couch co op game, Overcooked 2.With remote play together, the awesome 80's soundtrack and hilarious dialogue and animations, this game is absolutely glorious.Just make sure you don't play with any less than 2 more people. Truely, the more the merrier. This game almost passed under my radar and I have no idea why. Co-op game of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: This game is polished and truly a blast in co-op mode, but sadly it's over all too soon.Stylistically I would also compare Moving Out to the Overcooked games, as they do look and feel very similar. But when playing with a friend, there's more fun to be had with Moving Out. Lugging around awkwardly shaped furniture just presents abundant opportunities for silliness and fumbling about. There's also plenty of humor written into the character dialogue. The game mechanics are simple to learn, work very well and we didn't encounter any bugs or glitches.Me and my spouse had tons of fun with Moving Out, but were bummed out when we realized the game was over after only about 7 hours of playtime. Granted, we went through each stage without chasing high scores or extras. But there isn't really an incentive to go back and perfect your technique. We never needed more than two attempts to clear a stage, and once you've done that you can move ahead. It would have been smarter to set overall score requirements that you needed to clear to progress to the next set of stages, so that you would have to come back to the earlier levels and really nail them. Maybe there will be some free DLC later that will make this game better value. For the money I would have expected about twice the playtime.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game with friends and family. Please note: IT IS BEST PLAYED WITH A CONTROLLER. PLAYING WITH A KEYBOARD IS NOT IDEAL. The levels become more and more creative as you advance, the secret objectives are fun to accomplish, arcade levels are also quite fun. I have run it with 2 and 3 players and it's a box of laughs. Download the demo so you can have a taste before deciding but keep in mind cooperative play is what the game is all about so grab a partner.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Good game - ideal for wasting a bit of time and my 5 and 7 year old really like it. Difficulty is scaled fairly well for them (using the assist mode) and it's at its most entertaining when you're doing things wrong, which is a frequent event for them! Works nicely using my Steam link in front of the TV
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Great game to play with friends! It's simple, silly, and has cute writing between missions. We are having a blast!Relying on Remote Play however, was definitely not the way to go. The quality of the stream degrades more and more as people join and has frequent disconnects even with 1 gigabit up/down. Wish they just implemented proper multiplayer. They are also losing out on up to 3/4 of potential PC sales since only 1 person needs to buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a hilarious, fun, and inviting couch co-op game, this is it. Reminiscent of the Overcooked series but vastly different. Steam Remote Play is where this game really shines, although solo play can be quite enjoyable. The devs seriously took a lot of time making this game fun and enjoyable and you can see that through the play through. The game did leave me wanting more and seeing the amount of updates and work the devs put into the game prior to launch, I feel that I will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun with friends, more balanced than Overcooked. Having more players actually means better performance, not more stress :DI see people leaving negative feedback because their Remote Play Together experience is subpar, that has nothing to do with the game - quality depends on your hardware and internet connection speed of host and other players.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great physics based alternative to the Overcooked style multiplayer game!  My friend pre-ordered this game for me for my birthday (thanks josh!) and I couldn't be happier with this fun moving strategy title on day 1.  It's just like when he helped me move back in college, comically funny and challenging.  I love the extra little bits of details they put in the game and the 90's music is a great touch of personality.  Finding the perfect position can be a little frustrating at times and timing the two-person throw can be difficult but it's all about understanding the mechanics and communication.  My friends and I are pretty average gamers, but not new to games at all, and were only able to get bronze stars on most the levels.  I think the difficulty level of this game can be a little harder to achieve full rank than most, but that is not a bad thing.  It creates a more challenging strategy to correctly communicate what you do together as a team.  We really enjoyed it and appreciate the work the studio's artists did to create this masterpiece.  I'd recommend this to casual party gamers, as it's easy to pick up and hilarious in a group, but difficult to perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

_childDocuments_.review:
Moving Out is a ridiculous physics-based moving simulator that brings new meaning to "couch co-op"!

Are you ready for an exciting career in furniture? As a newly certified Furniture Arrangement & Relocation Technician, you'll take on moving jobs all across the busy town of Packmore. Smooth Moves may not be the biggest moving company, but there's no task too dangerous or strange for this busy team of go-getters. Grow your business to brave new heights, recruit colourful customizable characters, and save your town from furniture peril!
_childDocuments_.name: Moving Out

name: Ring of Pain
detailed_description: Twitch extension for streaming Our official Twitch extension lets your viewers: Draw creatures and items to replace game art. Vote on item choices. Drawings are moderated by you or your Twitch mods. About the Game Delve into randomly generated ring dungeons where encounters come to you! Observe and plan your route. Will you go for the loot or backstab a creeping horror? As you scavenge, fight and sneak to new encounters, the ring reacts to your actions. Play as fast or slow as you like in this challenging, turn-based roguelike. Just be careful where you tread - You may find yourself ambushed, or worse... See the outcome of your choices so you can focus on decisions. Creatures broadcast their actions in a hostile environment, ready to erupt. Will you flee or find a way to use the dungeon against itself? Positioning is key to survival. You can be quickly overwhelmed... Observe the Ring and strategise. Learn, adapt, or face demise. Mimics offer you a choice for a price. Take what you can hold and build a combination of gear with passive powers. Maybe you’ll be quick and evasive, with an acid soaked blade. Or maybe you’ll be a brute force juggernaut, or a fireborn damage sink with an affinity for explosions. Buy your way to power or adapt with what you scavenge in these unforgiving depths. Deep in the Ring of Pain you will discover new paths into the unknown. Places with new friends, powerful loot, and cryptic rhyming lore. Find pleasant reprieve and howling terrors best left undisturbed. The brave may be rewarded for their risk... or crushed by their ambition. In darkness, careful where you tread. What was unknown now fills with dread. Ring of Pain launches Oct 15th with these features and more: 16 Core path dungeons plus 2 branching endings to test your final build. Medium and Hard modes to unlock for those who thrive on pain. _childDocuments_.review: Really excellent game.  Somewhat similar to slay the spire except instead of building a deck you build around a set of stats and abilities that are formed by picking up equipment and stat buffs.  Starts out seeming a bit shallow, but the more you play the deeper it gets.  First rogue-like card game I have thoroughly enjoyed since slay the spire, it definitely adds something new to the genre.One of its best features is its lightening fast gameplay. Once you learn what most of the cards and enemies do, you can blitz through levels in about a minute.  This made gameplay very satisfying as it lets you blow through the early game quickly and then slow down later when you need to think more carefully.  It also tends to make dying or trying out a new build a lot less frustrating. Even when you mess up, it only takes about 15-20 min to get back to the same point and try again.Some people have complained that there is too much RNG, but I disagree.  A lot of high level play comes from meta-knowledge about what enemies appear when, and either what stats are needed to defeat them or tricks to get around them.  What starts out seeming like a senseless death soon becomes "ah I need either high defense or speed by mid-game in order to beat X".  After learning how fast you need to ramp your stats to stay viable, the surface level of RNG fades away and it becomes all about skill and planning.  The more I play, the farther I consistently get.  If it was truly RNG based I would expect to die a lot early/mid game instead of making it to late game almost every run.One of the first games in a while that is truly a rogue-like, both in the sense of starting completely from scratch every run, and in the sense that the deeper your knowledge of the game, the more the game becomes about planning and decision making and less about RNG.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty decent strategy roguelike. It's far from perfect in a lot of areas, but still entertaining, and it has the merit of doing its own thing, instead of just being another poor man's Slay the Spire.First of all, the game has a stunning artistic direction. Its gloomy aesthetics and soundtrack hit the spot for me, and surely will for anyone who's into horror movies and/or macabre in general.On the gameplay side, it's simple and innovative. Decision-making can be a little unintuitive at first, but it gets better very quickly. Other than that, the game succeeds in giving strategic interest to a very limited amount of actions, which I find refreshing.Now on the negative side, I'd say Ring of Pain is failing as a rogue-like, as it's pretty much only your build that makes runs different from one another. Random events to choose from sound interesting on paper, but it's mostly just extra enemies and loot, and there's very few enemies in the game that actually require you to specifically gear up or change your approach even a little. Some people might probably argue that's a standard for strategy roguelikes, but here, it's actually true.Another downside is how uninformative the game can be. There's a fair amount of stuff you'll probably never find on your own if you don't look it up, and some mechanics (notably boss behaviours) lack clarity.Despite the fact that some items do significantly alter gameplay, at the end of the day, winning is usually just about racking up enough stat points.On top of that, decision-making becomes rather obvious as you get more experienced, which includes hard mode. Actually tough choices are scarce, and the direction you take is mostly dictated by the first few items you find. It does require some reflexion to make the most of it, but there's not much room for creativity, balancing late scaling versus early upfront, taking risks and making concessions... Basically what keeps this sort of games interesting in the long run.Finally, while the game may look like it's deeper than what it looks like, spend enough time on it and you'll realize the vast majority of runs are merely about racking up enough stat points. There aren't many items that significantly alter gameplay, and a lot of those clearly are traps, and probably weren't tested thoroughly enough.For all these reasons, the game pretty much feels like "the same run, over and over".So basically, you get in, die a few times, git gud, try out most things, and move on.There's a lot of content though, and once again, the AD and core mechanics are at least worth one's curiosity, so I'd still recommend it, despite its questionable replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant for a while whether I wanted to recommend this game, but after about 11 hours of play I can say: It's addictive and despite the massive RNG almost fair once you learn what each creature, each room, each event does ... and once you've unlocked some additional items through achievements.The concept is very simple. You move along a ring (hence the name) made out of cards. These can be either enemies, treasures, events or exits.Enemies come in all different sorts, some follow you, some run away, some explode, some take something away, etc.Treasures have a completely randomized loot table depending on their rarety. Treasure chests have to be unlocked via souls, which you gain by killing enemies.Events are things like teleporting pylons, healing or curse potions, etc.And exits move you along to the next ring (of pain). The game has plain exits, which just transport you to the next regular level, and special exits, which can be shops, events, or dangerous extra levels. More risk, more potential rewards ... and you'll likely need those rewards.The game furthermore gives you 5 stats to play with:Health is self-explanatoryAttack determines for how much damage you can hit an enemy. If this is lower than the enemy's defense, you will only hit for 1. It's imho the 2nd most important stat, and I'll explain below why.Defense determines how high your chance of completely negating an attack is. For this to work your defense has to be higher than the enemy's offense though, which makes it a potentially wasted stat if you can't get above a certain threshold by the end. If you can get it high enough though you have a decent chance of negating many otherwise devastating attacks.Speed is by far THE most important stat, as it determines who will go first in combat. This combined with a high attack rating means you can oneshot enemies without taking damage.The last stat is sth called clarity I think and it's mostly pointless imho. It gives you more souls, makes healing potions stronger and gives you a higher crit chance I think, which doubles your attack damage. Of course there are a metric ton of items in the game, which can make or break your run. They can synergize perfectly or ♥♥♥♥ you up completely, especially if you're not quite sure how they work at first. For example, there is an item that pushes enemies away from you if you "pass" them (i.e. not attack, try to dodge), which, as it turns out, is a horrible idea if there's a ranged enemy in front of you. Another item automatically attacks every passed enemy, which sounded great in my head with a 100% dodge rate, until I realized that this meant massive explosion damage and instant death.Yet another item let's you freeze all enemies permanently, but only allows you to carry 4 items in total, gimping you in the stats department. I still think I got a winning run with that, not sure.The game does seem to offer different strategies. For example, I took an item that increased my speed by a lot right from the start, but also made it so that the one with the lower speed always goes first, so the strategy was to exchange speed for other stats and carry -speed items to get close to or below zero. This way I was able to focus entirely on attack and defense (and health), instead of having to juggle 4 stats, which is basically impossible. You WILL always have to leave two or even three stats in the dust, depending on your RNG.I do think the game needs more variety though. Most "builds" can get to the later levels, even the bosses, but those levels are a HUGE difficulty spike. If you were just one-shotting enemies in the previous levels, all of a sudden these new ones are not only twice as tough, but twice as fast, going from something like 15 to 20 speed to 30+, making your entire strategy pointless, if you don't know that. Maybe having more items in general for more diverse builds and having more item options each time might alleviate that.I've beaten the game on normal now, both light and dark, so now it's either on to higher difficulties, doing daily dungeons or just wasting time and unlocking stuff in normal mode, but I feel like I've experienced everything the game has to offer. So, I hope there are more plans for updates? We've gotten three already.

_childDocuments_.review: "Ring of Pain" is a console ported "card battler" game, which shouldn't be confused with a CCG/Deckbuilder, it's more of an RNG/stat platespinner like Dead in Bermuda where you click through cards that come up at you (you have a choice where to click) and wait and see if the RNG will erode your stats or not.  There's the impression that knowing how to play, or skill, will somehow influence this game, but it doesn't, it's just about whether you are lucky or not.  You might as well sit down and roll dice and see how many times the number 6 comes up... and if that sounds boring, it's not that much better than this game. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The game features mostly static, barely animated 2D images, the kind of thing you expect to see in browser/flash games.  While the artwork itself, while mediocre, might be considered passable, the visual presentation here is negligible, it might as well be a slideshow or a Youtube video.  Pac-Man, Space Invaders and Asteroids had more advanced animation and visuals going on than this game does.The controls can't be customised because the game has such a dumbed down, simplified interface that it's just iPhone screen tapping stuff.  The fact that the interface is this dumbed down might be seen as a problem in itself, however... this is a fairly shallow experience if you're the kind of gamer that likes to play games with deep, rich control schemes and interaction.  You'll get none of that here.The game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game, to avoid doing the important job of level/map design.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness.  Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content.Because this is designed for consoles, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.This looks and feels like a mobile app, but I wasn't able to find it on the app stores.  Maybe it was removed, maybe it was rejected by Apple and Google (they do have more rigorous quality standards than Valve does for Steam, after all).Regardless, for all intents and purposes "Ring of Pain" might as well be a mobile app, it has the same limitations and dumbed down qualities.  It's impossible to recommend such a game to PC gamers.  We don't spend all this money building gaming rigs so we can pretend they're iPhones and play games that might as well be mobile apps.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Warning: This game behaves as spyware and collects "telemetry" and personally identifying information.  While there is an option to disable this, there's no guarantee that will work.  The developers will make the unverifiable claim that this data isn't personally identifying, of course that's BS as they're collecting IPs and all kinds of other information about gamers, when combined with other profiling data this can 100% identify an individual.  They say it's for "QA" purposes but there's an admission that they sell user data to third parties as they spy on you.  Should you trust them?  Of course not... if they had any concerns about user safety and privacy, .  There's simply no reason to trust them and gamers should avoid this game because of this unacceptable privacy invasion."Ring of Pain" has the completely unrealistic cash grab price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Yeah, despite being shallower, this costs more than games like Slay The Spire.  This is also competing with over 9,000 free games available on Steam, many of them far better than this paid product.  Hearthstone and Magic The Gathering games are free to play!  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  Because this is the kind of game you can just play for free on mobile phones, it's impossible to recommend anyone should pay money for the same experience on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelike deck builders have exploded since Slay the Spire, and I couldn't be happier about it. This relatively newer genre just really does it for me, the tight mechanics, the combos and interactions, a solitaire experience when you want it with way more flavour and interesting decisions.But since then, there's been a lot of copycats or just games that do too little with the formula, and don't feel innovative or tight. It's been a while since I've played one as much as I've enjoyed Circle of Pain.Initially thought it was gimmicky--so monsters come at me in a ring, big deal, it's not so different from one-on-one. Boy was I wrong, and positioning adds such a depth to the battles! Having the ability to try and run/stealth away from danger isn't about weakness, it's about smart, calculated plays. Facing some nasty critter you can't possibly survive? Well, you can soften him up immensely by beating on some weak goon in front of him and applying splash damage, or lure exploders to him. The "resources" at your disposal, your stats and the currency exchange of souls for my health pool was complex enough without it being bogged down or too breezy. For whatever reason, all the systems really click with me, in a natural way. The enigmatic world you're in is both charming and disturbing, and the rhyming couplets just kinda work. It's not an easy game, and there will always be some luck involved: I've bombed out of a run in less than 30 seconds (and was surprised with an achievement!), but also completed the "dark" ending within my first 2 hours. These games always have an element of chance, but I also feel firmly in control.Another run is never the question, it's about how many more!
