_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game, its style is on point and I can't help but mention the admiration I have for the developers since they continue to work on something that, in my humble opinion, was already finished a year or two ago. It goes to show their dedication and love for their product, and since they've yet to release any DLC (not that I'd be opposed to it if it were substantial enough) it shows that they are far from greedy since they're willing to put out new content for FREE.DLC is something that is introduced to many, if not most games outright in an attempt to draw forth new funds for the work that was done post release of a game. So it's nice to see a developer ditch that mindset, and I presume it's to cultivate a fanbase which is honestly harmless and awesome to see. I feel that we have a lot of game studios that don't care about feedback, or fanbases, they just want a successful product and are willing to capitalize on its' success if achieved. Hell, even if the product is acceptable to people who purchase the base game, with ratings of 80-89% for instance, they'll still try and pull out the DLC. Anyways, the core gameplay is hard at first but once you understand what you're doing and what items to pick for certain builds you'll have fun trying those specific builds. Some of these may seem to break the game until you reach the end and are promptly destroyed, going to show that nothing is imbalanced or done without reason. It is fun to try out new items, or builds, and see what works best or what doesn't. In addition to the items, you'll need to coordinate which stats you prioritize in leveling up as you have attack, defense, health, speed, and clarity. Then there is critical strike chance, dodge, and stealth chance of course. Personally I've yet to try any builds involving clarity, but I have enjoyed utilizing a high stealth chance in order to avoid damage from mobs as I pass them. Typically most builds I like to try involve either attack and speed, or attack and defense. Health is thrown in depending on the situation, as after a certain level you'll be draining your stat points in order to build others. There are a lot of gameplay mechanics in general that are interesting, which could involve the differing mechanics imposed by wearing certain items. One of my particular favorites is Hermit's Tiara which could be interpreted as a game-changing item, up until you reach the final boss and realize it doesn't apply to him! It freezes enemies as you attack them, so when paired with high speed you can get away with permanently freezing any enemy you are fighting. Another caveat of using this item is you can only have 4 total items equipped, including the candle item that you start with every run. All in all, a very fun game and each run is relatively quick, lasting at most an hour. This means you can play it in short bursts or try a multitude of builds in the span of a few hours of playing if you're truly focused, or chilling at night. I would recommend it to anyone who likes roguelikes, but as others have said do not expect it to be like any other roguelike you have played such as Slay the Spire. There is no deckbuilding here, yet every run utilizes all of the items you have unlocked in previous runs which gradually increases the chaos that is experienced through different combinations of items.

_childDocuments_.review: After giving it a several months' worth of pause and watching some playthroughs of people who know what they are doing, I had decided to come back. I found the game to be more balanced through multiple updates.It still has cryptic interactions that are unexplained in advance while still being punishing enough to not really leave much room for blind exploration. I do know that for some people it's much less of a turnoff; either way, that's a thing to consider if you're reading reviews to help you make up your mind.For me personally, now the initial mechanical idea was raised enough to flip the boolean representation of my enjoyment. Doubt the further improvements of comparable magnitude are to be had.___________________________________________________________________So, this game has some pretty visuals(not *pretty* pretty, but they are well done and atmospheric). The idea is fresh, the item concepts are interesting and different. However, no matter how I play and what I try to do, the enemies seem to outscale me so quickly that by the 8-9th biome I hardly ever seem to have enough damage+armor+sustain to actually make it through without an inevitable net loss of health that results in a death a couple dungeons later.The only time I won I had a goldfish set of items that allowed me several options to fairly consistently avoid enemies and to pick them off at a distance without actually fighting them. And, while winning felt nice(duh), it felt like a gifted victory that after a couple of pickups catapulted a similarly doomed slog into an autopilot where the only responsibility left was avoiding exploders. A cascade of achievements, an unfortunate death a bit later and a subsequent roguelike-esque reset to the start, where I was never able to replicate whatever it was that I may have done "right" to beat the game.The lore seems to be there, but it is artificially elusive through stylistically consistent if unimpressive rhymes, feeling either locked away for some fan fictions enthusiasts to unlock or too bland and flat to just put out as is. I never care for the lore much anyway, but it will hardly be the catch here.TL;DR: mechanically, the game feels new and inspired, I love the grotesque palette and shaping, but playing it for a bit left me unsatisfied and with no understanding what is one supposed to do. Maybe I am just bad lol

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting novelty, abundant with intrigue but direly lacking in satisfaction. Makes for a decent new experience but definitely not one worth prioritizing very highly.The game is absolutely dripping with cosmetic polish. It looks really interesting, the sound design is fantastic, the lore and world design are fairly intriguing; but overly vague as well. The premise of playing within the confines of a ring is a new take on choice-driven strategy in rogue-lites. But there's just not much gameplay.Combat is a damage race advanced by clicking on targets, there's no more depth to it than that. Meanwhile item selection often comes down to choosing the most obviously non-self-destructive piece of equipment available. Most of the strategy in playing comes from players choosing when to fight and when to move to the left or right; often to avoid taking too much damage.Players can use this to avoid explosions, find healing potions or escape to the exit but there's not much variety to it beyond that. Often the choice to fight, move left, or move right comes down to players looking at how much damage they will receive by taking each action; and choosing the action that won't result in death or severe harm. Occasionally the game will actually fail to properly calculate what will happen so sometimes players will lose because of programming oversight. The only other diversifying element is when players decide to use their items, which does add some more depth but only some.Ultimately the game is entirely governed by random chance as the strength of the player is determined by what items and statistic upgrades they find, while the difficulty of the game is determined by what enemies spawn and if the player gets bad dice rolls on certain percentage based mechanics. Otherwise all of the actions the player can govern could be easily handled by the computer, avoiding lethal damage and choosing the most statistically favourable upgrades. Overall resulting in a very effortless and minimally thoughtful gameplay experience in which players basically roll an invisible dice over and over; then take credit for the random outcome. There are moments where strategy prevails, but it's only possible randomly.There isn't much variety in player builds either. There are a handful of tangibly viable builds such as petrify, poison and freeze due to how common their major items are, while builds that revolve around other things like dodge, critical hits, high attack and speed, or stealth are often useless due to how niche getting a viable combination of those items is. In general it feels extremely obvious that building defense every time is the best option for the player; because damage is inevitable so mitigating it is largely crucial to survival here. Speed and attack do not mitigate much damage unless players get so much they can immediately one-shot an enemy, which is extremely unlikely. It seems that the safest and most reliable way to play the game is just to always build on defense to outlast every threat while gradually increasing your damage through petrify, poison, freeze and slight attack ups. Trying to build anything else can quickly result in a loss because the player doesn't have enough defense, since whatever they're trying to build isn't effective enough to compensate for the lack of such.The game isn't awful, it's just shallow after the initial novelty of the artistic atmosphere and moderately unique gameplay wears off. There's clearly a lot of care in how the game presents itself, but the gameplay just fundamentally lacks depth and variety. It makes for a solid new experience and is low-effort enough to play that it's easy to drop in and out of; but it's not compelling enough to merit the longer term player dedication rogue-lites can foster.If you're interested in finding more games like this I've probably reviewed quite a few on my curator page .

_childDocuments_.review: is a very good roguelike card-based dungeon crawler with — oddly enough — horror elements. Its only downside is that everyone speaks in truly atrocious poems; everything else is done so well I'll need to uninstall the game now if I want to break its spell.. You walk a magic circle of rooms, with special areas between them. In every room, you'll find enemies, loot, and potions, all placed in a circle you can strafe left and right along. Your goal is to get to the room's exit (sometimes there are several), killing or avoiding enemies in the process. The outcomes of all actions are visible in advance, so you can plan your moves. This tactical approach is where the fun comes from.Rewards come in the form of loot, numerous and generous. There is a number of stats and all kinds of special effects to combine and experiment with (and then find a legendary jar that converts all excessive healing to damage to all enemies and win with it). The levels aren't big, and the general pacing is very good. Deaths also feel  unfair enough to warrant a "come on, one more run."And since many items have downsides as well as benefits and you can plan ahead, the depth of the game is quite significant.. Top-notch! Apart from the poems (which really are horrible enough to warrant a second mention), everything else is brilliantly creepy. The art, the slick UI, the music, the theme, the itemization — everything works together to make this rather static genre unnerving. Is it just me, though, or was the between-the-levels whispering sound effect taken directly from Bloodborne?. Might be minor to some, but I appreciate how everything is structured around rings. The Owl's eyes look like rings. Every level is a ring looping back on itself. The bigger level structure is a ring too. The constant replayability of a roguelike evokes this imagery too. And the plot is esoteric enough to possibly be about rings as well., this is definitely among my top-10 games of the year. It's well-designed, well-balanced, original in presentation and draws you in, and this particular take on the dungeon crawler formula (placing enemies in circles so the player can move in either direction) is fresh enough. If you like the genre, this one is an easy pick; and it might be worth trying even if you don't.Also, sheesh  is creepy.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried the demo awhile back and for whatever reason it did not captivate me. but after giving the full release a go for a few hours now I can safely recommend this for anyone that likes strategy roguelikes or card games! Deceptively simple, this game sees you basically choosing whether to attack/activate one of two cards in front of you or trying to sneak/pass by while looking around the ring of other cards that await you. Along the way you'll pick up new gear that will alter your stats and offer bonuses (or detriments) and will influence how you play if you hope to survive.This is an extremely quick game to pick up and play, easy to play mouse only and windowed if you want to have it going on while watching sports or whatever (some runs I've had lasted less than a minute) but it also rewards you for taking your time and thinking. All results are shown to you before you make an attack, though enemies outside your front two cards can also attack you and/or mess up your plans so you have to be aware of that. If I had to sum this up, I'd say it is a very rapidly paced (if you want it to be) roguelike card game that is easy to pick up and hard to put down. Despite my initial misgivings with the demo (for which I cannot recall why), this has quickly become a favourite game to play in the background while watching sports or giving it the proper full screen treatment so I can enjoy the atmosphere and music. Lots of fun but be prepared to die...a lot!

_childDocuments_.review: i started playing the demo  ago, and.. i just couldn't get it out of my head since then. the style, the story, the mechanics all flow together in this addictive loop of  the gameplay is so much fun.i feel like the rng involved has never been a massive flaw. every spiral around the ring of pain is very fast, probably an hour at most if you hit the endgame sequence, and there's always  you could have improved on to survive.not to mention: ring of pain doesn't make death feel like a complete loss. it feels like, 'well, let's try something different!'. that feeling might vary for you, but it's why ring of pain has a demo to try out, too!i haven't seen all there is to see in ring of pain, but i think something needs to be said here.  the idea that a story must be fully explained, all events accounted for, or grounded by a semblance of reasoning, is a very, very subjective one. i appreciated ring of pain's narrative far more than many of the games i've played with gigantic, expansive worlds.there is a story in ring of pain, and it is not going to hold your hand to its conclusions. every rotation gives you more and more little strands to put together, and it's not hard to start to see the scope of the ring in the first dozen tries. ps: so proud to find out the devs are australian, this game is an absolute gem. i owe you lot a few cartons of beer.

_childDocuments_.review: It's time I write a review for this game. I may have played it a little bit much.First off, this game is hard. It looks simple and you ultimately only have 2 decisions on every turn. Skipping or attacking. Since you know the WORST outcome of every fight, you can make decisions based on that. The more you progress, the more items you unlock, because this game is intense without unlocking a bunch of items first. To be absolutely clear: You're probably not gonna win your first few runs or even get far at all.It looks simple but there's a lot of item combinations, positioning, planning and long term strategies involved, which you only develop through knowledge and PAIN. You can't plan for situations you had no clue will even appear, so you're gonna die - a lot. This is to expected and totally fine. Runs are short and while it can feel unfair, if you really think about it, it was your own bad decisions earlier in the run that got you there. That said there will definetely be situations that are impossible (such as being placed between two blockers without any way to skip or kill them), but those are RARE. There's almost always a way.Unlocking different lights transforms this game completely. They have unique properties and effects that will totally change what item combinations you can go, which ones are good and HOW you actually play the game. My favorites are the inverted candle and pain. Inverted candle inverses all item stats and pain progressively gets -1 on all stats per win you got with it. There's so much replayability value that I didn't even see / register until the 100 hour mark.I love the artwork and the seemingly simple binary choice of the gameplay. Every decision matters. Every skip or attack you do changes the dungeon. You can go through runs without killing anything. You can go through runs without attacking at all. There's so many options I just love it.Recently there have been new updates with new enemies, items and achievements and I've been having a blast finally unlocking all the items I didn't have before because I didn't "grind" for the achievements (most of which are really doable and only a few are tough, which, again, is fine). I can only recommend at least reading the achievements because there are plenty of achievements you won't get randomly unless you know their conditions. Like doing a run with a specific item set. And there are many, many items you should have unlocked for your harder runs. 10/10 value for my money

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow manages to cram RNG into every possible aspect of its gameplay. It's normal for roguelikes to have RNG force your hand in the builds you go for and the strategies you're allowed on a run, but this game goes completely overboard by having almost every interaction heavily hinge on RNG in some way. The chance you take or avoid damage, hits to kill, rerolls, whether potions heal or damage you, bad enemy placements, etc. etc. run rampant and the extremely limited item selection per reroll means it's never really guaranteed you roll consistent solutions to these problems on a run. It ends up creating a game that feels less like I won or lost by my ability to strategize and adapt to RNG and more like the outcome was up to luck from the start. It gets even worse with the challenge achievements (which you're encouraged to chase for unlocks), many which impose restrictions that gimp your available strategies even further.

_childDocuments_.review: Ring of Pain is well, a ring of pain. 17 hours and I am no master at this game but I have some understanding on how things work. This game is very gambling heavy, and there are no builds you can hope for in this roguelike. It truly is a ring of pain by gambling away souls, which is the currency in this game where you buy chest and items from the visitor shops in the game, to progress further as it gets harder and harder the more you delve deeper into the ring.  Items are the key feature of the game as there are currently 289 cards in the game, which doesn't seem like much but really waters the loot pool in weird ways, because as it turns out most cards are combined into sets. These sets give a brief overview on how the card sort of functions in a run, I believe there are four sets in total but some cards are not placed in a set which I guess makes five sets if include cards that are a part of a set. However, the four main sets detailed as being attack, defense, stealth, and clarity. Those aren't really the names but those are the stats those sets cover. How it works and why this waters the loot pool down to an annoying degree is that, mimic chest will drop only two items when unlocked and you have to choose which one you want, and these two items are grouped by the sets mentioned before, so you will usually end up getting two items from the same set. However, you can reroll a white chest for free once, and then you start paying souls to reroll more, and this is where is boils down to being gambling on getting the set you want.  This is getting lengthy already, but another thing to add is the stats themselves. Besides the items which boost your stats, there are cards that give you the decision to pick from three stats and boost it by either 1 point, 2 points, or 4 points at the cost of reducing other stats by 1. This is from the specialist update, which just sprinkles some more confusing choices in an already inflated system. To makes matters more annoying, you really can't specialize seeing as having one low stat can just ultimately end your ruin.TLDR: If you like really heavy gambling mechanics in your roguelike games, and or have a thing for chance based games this one is for you. However, I will say its difficult  and have reached the near end game once in my hours of play times.

_childDocuments_.review: Ring of Pain is a stylistic roguelite card-based dungeon crawler with exceptional execution in every area.The (optionally) fast pace does wonders to make it more approachable for a quick game than vaguely similar games, like Slay the Spire, while not skimping on any of the equivalent strategy and planning.Every run has its own build and challenges, and those moment you hit upon a strategy that works... and then accidentally explode yourself... it's fantastic fun.I don't feel like this is a game for everyone, with its dark themes and minimal guidance post-tutorial, but for those who enjoy rouge-likes and rogue-lites and card battlers you'll likely have a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: Not quite a dungeoncrawler, not quite a deck-builder, and not quite Rogue (or 'Rogue-lite' by some definitions of what meta-progression is and isn't), but what is here is a superbly-executed combination of light RPG and Rogue-lite mechanics that is mechanically and aesthetically so dissonant from the aforementioned genres that they are more familiar suggestions than accurately-descriptive terms. There is also the owl.This is a 'card' game insofar as the deck is the level of the dungeon you are trawling through, with enemies, NPC's, loot, and obstacles visible in front of you at all times, with progression further into a run tied to flipping through the cards in front of you to either 'run' from a threat or to click on it to interact - meaning to usually attack - it. There's very little you can or will do to interact with this 'hand' in regards to what will come up and the game does not emphasize construction in that sense, it is very much *not* a card game in the mode of Slay the Spire so much as in its presentation. There is also the owl.Very addictive, very quick, and with a very wide variety of items to engage with the spread in front of you or manipulate your stats to accomplish the same end, with several extreme options you can stumble onto to wildly swerve an existing build or course correct into something feasible - with the *real* game starting after you complete a run for the first time, and get to choose different conditions and items with which to start as a result. There is also the owl.Ultimately I think it's still one of the best things Humble Games has published even four years later, as someone who has come back to the game sporadically since first trying its initial release, and in a solidly polished and complete state as of now, even if it's unlikely to get further updates in the near future. There is also the owl.

_childDocuments_.review: Core design: 7/10 As the tittle of the game suggest, ring of pain whereby monsters , treasures , curse/reward are in a ring. You need to move around or kill those monsters for souls, use souls for better treasures, better treasures means dealing monsters much more simpler and the cycle continues.RNG: 3/10What we like slay the spire the monster and this game doesn't is plan based and not pure RNG. You don't have much information to work on for planning to deal with monsters. Hence this is a ♥♥♥♥ up mechanism.Difficulty scaling: 2/10When in hard mode, not only you start items like candle that trade stats, but also the monster scales up pretty badly. The main flaws for hard mode is piercing attack/high speed and so on.I doubt that the hard mode has tried multiple times with the QA testers.The suggestion I could make would be slowly scale the monsters with Ascensions like monster train / slay the spire.Balance: 4/10As mentioned above stated, the current balance of the game is 50 - 50, you have a good run with it or not. There isn't in between nor well plan ahead to get better items. By luck - either you can defeat or not. There is also meta progression such that you have to keep playing to via unlocking better items in specific quest... I don't think I can win without powerful meta progress items.Some items like spoon / tiara shouldn't exist in the game...In conclusion: 16 / 40 I will put this game down once other early access game is available. Meta progression + 12) Ambush dungeon gives free rewards upon killing monsters. 3) Looter the guy where he leaves the dungeon gives free pots and stats4) When you are in dungeon 10 or so hope you have some blue or even golden items... if not please restart the game.Updates:Old meta: Light Concoction + Channeling Kilt = Heal to deathNew meta: Get lots of clarity + Skirt Of Visions + Soul Hourglass + Crown Of Clarity

_childDocuments_.review: In short this game is GREAT.The art, sound, and game play are super polished... the mechanics and combos are really fun, and if you are a fan of rougelite card games, this one should be right up your alley. What makes it different than a Slay the Spire?? Well.. there is NO deck of cards to cycle through. You live and die by your gear slots and movement.. The game is actually a lot closer to Fate Hunters (without the deck... and a VERY different combat system). You progress through a series of rooms working your way deeper into the game.The combat loop is BRUTAL, seriously you can die in less than 30 seconds. The ring will force you to pay attention to the ENTIRE ring not just what is immediately to your left and right or..  laser focusing on shiny baubles in the distance. You can stealth, you can stick and move, run from exploding creatures, cause chain reactions... good stuff! Try to avoid poisons, bosses, lightning fast creatures, and curses, with the assistance of a cracked out looking big bird in the ... RING OF PAIN!

_childDocuments_.review: I got Ring of Pain in a bundle. I didn’t read over the store page much, but from the little I did read, I was excepting a Slay the Spire knock off. That is not what it is. It is a roguelite, but it is completely different from Slay the Spire. It may be tagged as a card game, but I wouldn’t really call it that. It’s certainly not a deck builder. Basically, how it works is that enemies are represented by cards, which you attack in a turn-based fashion. 2 of these cards are active at a time, meaning you can interact with them. You can rotate all the cards over by 1 either left or right. In addition to enemies, cards can contain doors to the next area and gear to upgrade your character with. Like with most roguelites, you lose all you’re gear when you die, but you can unlock new gear for future runs. It’s not the best game I’ve ever played, but it is fun, and I’d recommend it. If you are interested, there is a demo you can try, which will probably give you a better idea of if you will like this or not than reading a bunch of these reviews

I felt the need to come back and address what I feel like are a lot of reviews that are dismissive. The most common complaint in negative reviews is the RNG factor, the claims that the game is unfair and the implication that RNG undermines skill. _childDocuments_.review: A very fun roguelike, Ring of Pain feels amazing once you get a hold of the basic mechanics. While at times it can feel a bit luck based, overall it feels a lot more skill based than the vast majority of other roguelikes. Learning how and when to move is the largest skill I felt myself getting better at while playing, and is one of the largest keys to winning a run. Along with that, knowing what stats to increase, how certain items can synergize, and reducing the ramifications of luck are other big contributing factors to winning a run. All of this makes it feel like skill is required to win, instead of blind luck getting certain items that might or might not synergize with your build. The only form of meta-progression is unlocking new items  meaning you don't feel as if it's a grind just to get a single win. Some of the unlockable items are extremely powerful, but I didn't feel as if I couldn't do a challenge without a specific one.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: My scores/reviews are almost always based on having bought the game at close to the "lowest historical price" on steam at time of purchase.Quick score: 5/5Notes: Awesome aesthetic and addictive gameplay, however it is extremely RNG heavy. To the point that it basically feels like an elaborate slot machine dressed up as a roguelite.  It's not pure luck, and there is for sure strategy involved in how you can perfectly play any given situation or choice. But even with theoretically perfect play I would guess your chance of finishing a run would still be under 20%. I haven't played the game a ton yet to say 100% for sure, but im fairly confident. It took me about 25 runs before I "finished" my first run. Which unlocks the 2nd difficulty (Out of 3).HOWEVER, despite the relatively simple slot machine gameplay, the game is still very fun and I would recommend it for sure, just understand that it is very random and failure is almost certain. As an overall experience though, the game is great.Also worth noting, while your success rate is very low, successful runs generally only last about 20-25 minutes. So it's not a RNG fest like darkest dungeon that also wastes hours of your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Very addicting turn-based roguelike card game. Not exactly a deckbuilder, though, because you have no deck. You rather draft items cards to go into specific slots and directly attack enemies on the ring. The RNG is pretty heavy on this one, though that doesn't mean that strategic builds and game sense aren't paramount. It will likely take you several hours of failure before finishing a run, but it's oh so satisfying when you do. Has a decent sized collection of items to make for a handful of viable builds. Most of the very good gear has significant drawbacks, so choose carefully.Beyond gameplay, the game has a delightfully creepy atmosphere. From the uncanny macabre art style to the characters speaking in cryptic rhymes, this game nails its nightmarish tone. The soundtrack also slaps. It earned a soundtrack purchase from me, and could easily deserve some playtime to set the tone at a haunted house or Halloween party.

But this isn't the case. I'd almost call it a bait-and-switch. In the end, even after completing a run, I'm left very unsatisfied with the overall experience despite the admittedly very solid gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews, so the fact I felt deeply compelled to come and write this really says something about the game. You can really tell the people behind this game put a lot of care into it, and that feels really good.The game is overall great. If you, like me, are the type of person who enjoys games, usually deck builders, where you start off small and end up with a crazy strong build just to find out there are crazy strong enemies that make it so you still need to think at least a bit about how you're playing not to lose everything on a silly mistake, I think this game is for you.Other than that, the game seems to have a very interesting lore, which I'm sure some people are going to spend days upon days trying to figure out, but I personally just enjoy how it makes you wonder, in a sort of whimsical way. _childDocuments_.review: is a roguelite card game that's unique and unlike anything I have played in the past. Accompanied by stunning graphics, the fun and challenging game is easy to learn but still requires a lot of strategic thinking.There is a very short tutorial, which is hardly necessary, because the game is very self-explanatory as you play.On the screen you will see two cards each time. The card can be a monster, spell, skill, potion, exit, etc. You need to choose one of these and go left or right to get to other cards.If you are facing a monster card, you need either to fight or to sneak past. If you fail in your sneak attempt, they will attack. Some monsters will explode when you defeat them, hurting you. Other monsters have poison or first strike. You have to be careful in your decisions.During your playthroughs of the game, you will learn why you are there and just what is going on.If you die, it's game over, but you can get new cards that will then be unlocked. There are a total of 177 cards to unlock.The graphics are top notch and very colourful.The music is a bit eerie, which is good for this game.The game is fully playable with a mouseI think the price is a bit steep for a fairly simple card game. The base price is €19.99, same in USD. It's worthwhile overall for this game, but I would rather it be closer to €14.99. You will end up playing this game in short bursts, not long sittings. is a very unique card-based game that's fun and very easy to learn. While you will partly advance with luck, you will also need to employ some strategical skills to make it far. The graphics is one of the best card games I have played. But the price is a bit high, so it's reasonable to wait for a sale, especially when the game sessions are going to be fairly short.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: After almost 30 hours I have beaten the game on normal difficulty through both paths available.  This game is VERY much about luck until you start unlocking more items.  Once you have more items to work with then you can start using new strategies to beef yourself up.  No items feel overpowered (except Light Concoction.....) and each item feels unique in it's abilities.  I've seen some people say this game is too hard, but I would disagree.  At first the game is super difficult.  But the more you play, the more you unlock new items that make the game progressively easier on each run. Yes, sometimes RNGeezus will strike you down but each run is fairly quick from start to finish (20ish minutes maybe a little more or less depending on your build) so you don't feel like you've wasted too much of your life on a failed run.  Overall this is a great little roguelike with a unique approach to combat, progression through levels and great replayability so far.  I can't recommend this enough.

The gameplay itself is interesting and diverse, I have played many runs and despite some others opinion, I find my choices matter every single time. _childDocuments_.review: It's not a deckbuilder, so not similar to StS or Monster Train if that's what you're looking for. Instead, what we have here is an excellent card battler with really nice mechanics. Dying is usually the fault of the player although item RNG can be an issue some runs. It's difficult to get consistent win streaks going because of this, but regardless, it's a ton of fun playing. The RNG should be able to be tweaked with future content/patches though and what's here now is worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, and I think overall it was a positive experience. However, I will describe my negative experiences - I rage quit way too many times. For having permadeath, this game does a terrible job at making you feel like your deaths are your own fault. I think this is a fairly common fault among roguelites.More often than not (up to the point of writing this review at ~10 hours), I have died because of a failure on the developer's part to convey mechanics to me which I feel should be explained with simple text. I will be 30-60 minutes into a run and see something new, and it doesn't say what it does. So I try it out and then it either kills me, or stupidly cripples me in some way that makes me feel so awful that I rage-quit. Maybe other people don't mind this, but the impression I get is that I need to spend an entire run to learn each new mechanic, at which point I will die, and start over again.I am just tired of game mechanics that aren't explained. Almost every run I've played, the thing that killed me was a mechanic that was never clearly explained.Add to that the other deaths I've had were due to misclicks, which is a minor failure of UI design.I actually changed my review to positive, because I feel the game is still worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the things I like about Ring of Pain is that the strategy is mostly deterministic. For most actions you intend to take, you can see the direct result of that action beforehand. There are some aspects with randomization (item drops, dodge, crit, stealth, deflect and some item secondary effects) but for the most part you aren't relying on randomization to succeed. For me, this makes the strategy in the game play feel meaty, and less prone to fate then many other rogue-likes.
_childDocuments_.name: Ring of Pain

_childDocuments_.review: Ring of Pain is a great example on how developers could mix different genres and make something unique.It's a combination of dungeon crawlers and a roguelites where each run could go either way. It also has a lot of variety on the items it offers and various ways it offers for you to play the game with most items being locked up under achievements which motivate you to push further.Another thing that is different about this game is that it is essentially a card game where each choice you make is either to go to left or right with scrolls and books being an exception to that. A lot of the gameplay is based on this movement mechanic so if you would not enjoy that I don't think you could get very much out of this game. There is also different candles which act as your starting modifiers each making significant changes to the way you play the game, some making it harder some easier and so on. You also unlock these as you progress and beat the game with different candles.The game is also intentionally hard even on normal difficulty so it will take some practice until you get used to it but it's really rewarding after you get through that phase. Overall I think this is a hidden gem, get it!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Quick to get inMost things are explained wellCreepy-cute designCons:Often left with no option except to dieExplosive enemiesGame thinks "5" is "4" for a specific item. This game is, essentially, an extremely boiled down aRPG. You build up your stats, find new gear, and tackle rooms while trying to reach the next one alive. If you're a streamer who plays competitive games, and need a good queue game, you can't really go wrong here.If you like roguelikes with simple mechanics, also a solid game. Overall I would rate this 6/10. It's a cute little game, but it doesn't have the staying power of other Roguelikes. Good for a few hours of play. This is a great buy if you can get it for $10 or less, otherwise you might want to wait.EDIT: I am upgrading my rating on this from 6 to 8 based entirely on the devs willingness to address the flaws that have been reported in the game. Everything else stands as is.

_childDocuments_.review: Ring of Pain is a nice little roguelike dungeon crawler with cards that almost feels like a puzzle game. If you like the genre and happen to find the game on sale, you will probably enjoy it. I wouldn't buy it on full price though, because it is rather short - I've played 10 hours and have seen all available endings. The amount of items is rather small compared to other roguelikes. All that is left for me now is beating the game in hardmode, which I wouldn't recommend due to the fact that the game very much relies on luck (as other reviewers stated as well). For people who are here for the "roguelite"-tag: This is more a rogue than a rogue. You start every session under the same conditions, neither stronger nor weaker. You have a chance of encountering the items you discovered in your last run, but this is not necessary the case. Also, those items are not necessary better - just different.

_childDocuments_.review: As others have pointed out, Ring of Pain is extremely RNG based. Actual runs don't take very long but they can be literally impossible to complete even from the first room just due to how the numbers stack up. The art is unique among the card roguelikes and its use of RPG mechanics allows it to stand out but that's about as far as it goes. It's different, but it's not better. I wouldn't even go so far as to call it good. There's kind of elements of a story here but unless there's something hiding behind completing the highest difficulty with multiple starting items it doesn't actually go anywhere.If you haven't already, go play Slay the Spire. Go experience Griftlands. Heck, give Monster Train a shot. They're simply better.

_childDocuments_.review: Ring of Pain is a roguelike game with puzzle like combat with a focus on finding the right synergy of equipment to help you escape the ring shaped "dungeon".It has one of the most unique gameplay I've seen in game. While the concept is simple (rotate through the ring of cards and find the exit), it's puzzle like nature and fast gameplay keep the game both deep and engaging.The core of the game revolves around carefully positioning around the ring of cards that can consist of anything from enemies, potions or some sweet loot. Knowing where and when to rotate as well as which enemies to fight and which enemies to TRY and sneak by is a challenge the game constantly throws at you. However, the biggest determinant of whether you will win the run is how good you are at making smart combination of equipment to boost the right stats and create powerful synergies between equipment effects.The runs are relatively short (usually less than 1h) which is great if you don't have a lot of time for gaming. There is nothing I didn't like about the game outside of the fact that it has some, but not too much RNG and that sometimes you will find yourself in some rather strange situations (explained below)That being said, while it's tagged as a card game, don't expect any deckbuilding or any kind of typical card play. It's tagged as a card game since you are technically drafting item cards, a lot of aspects of the game are depicted in card format, but it could have been easily something else.  + Unique gameplay that's both fun and engaging.+ Quick runs that can be finished in less than 1h.+ Grim aesthetics. + A LOT of variations in items and strong replay value in terms of item combinations. * RNG can screw you over...a bit. Sneaking past enemies, critical chance, getting cursed and item drops are all chance based, which while they keep the suspense and variation up, may cause a bit of frustration when things don't go your way. Personally, it never reached high frustration levels for me, but you've been warned that it's not RNG free. -  There are some rare but weird situations that happen from time to time that are unfun. One time, during the final boss fight I spent a lot of time running around in circles while being chased by a huge enemy that can one shot me. I needed to attack the boss but If I stopped to do that the huge enemy would just smack me. Occasionally the enemy would delay his move and I could get an attack in to the boss, but then he would catch up again and we were stuck in a loop where neither of us could win until the enemy for some reason delayed his move again. Interesting idea in theory, followed up by a great execution. Ring of Pain is not a game to be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: Most of my hours are actually on the Nintendo Switch (Approx 300 hrs).This game is a very unique and minimalist take on roguelike dungeon crawler. The game is extremely fun and the variations are amazing. Something of note is that this game has a fairly harsh difficulty curve, which is expected, and you will find yourself dying A LOT very early on if you didnt get lucky with some draws (Or you play it ultra safe, which is no fun for me!).However in times you actually pass that early game difficulty curve, you'll find that the game has some of the most interesting mix and matches you can make with your equipments (And in extension, skill and play style) to the point of breaking the game (At least until you get hard countered).As an example, my favorite item is the Hermit's Tiara which let's you guarantee a freeze attack on enemies if you have 4 or fewer items equipped. At that point you are basically guaranteed a kill on every enemy whom you manage to hit first. I actually managed to beat the final boss with only 4 items equipped because of this mechanic though there were some close shaves with death.This is one of those games i have in my "Arcade"/"Pick up and go" type of game that is simple enough to just play, does not need saves and has enough depth to at least keep things interesting for a long time!

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Steam Deck.10/10 roguelike, perfect for Deck too! The way you build using gear instead of a deck feels like StS but just artifacts so you don’t have to worry about a bad draw and swings the focus to the titular Ring mechanic. _childDocuments_.review: Ring of Pain is a roguelite, turn-based cardgame and dungeon crawler with many surprises and a beautiful artstyle.  The game immidiatley starts. You have different stats like Attack, defend, speed and many more. Speed decides who attacks first. If you attack an enemy they get damaged based on your attack and his defend. It's pretty self-explantory really.  Whats special? The story is really mysterious and told through multiple runs. You don't get what the game is about first. The more you play and the more runs you do, the more you explore the world. It's really exciting to explore more of the world. Thats all im saying without telling to much as you should do it by yourself.  Unlocking achievements unlocks new cards/items for future runs. There are around 180 items to unlock. You can get armor, special abilities, one-use items, a mask, hand gloves, shoes and many many more. Every item gives you bonuses on stats or even special abilities. Many items have pro and cons depending on what playstyle you like. You also can find +1 Attack, Defend, Speed or health cards in a dungeon.  There are several bosses. You never know if you really should attack someone or try to get to the exit. Maybe this boss is to strong? Maybe you'll get something special later if you don't attack him? Maybe you get something special if you attack him? Maybe you never see him again in that run? Every run is different. Sometimes you get new routes in your 10th or 20th run. In my playtime of around 15 hours i never had the same run twice. This is a beautiful made game. It's really great and addictive. It's a game you don't want to put away. You lost? Try again. Your next run could be your lucky one.  If you're still reading this: GET THE GAME IMMIDIATLY AND START PLAYING. It's really worth it if you're into turn-based strategy games.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an interesting concept and I'll come back to it from time to time - but the game is not good enough to recommend.At the end of the day you just build up numbers and click things. And hope that the game gives you things with smaller numbers. There are very few synergies between items. The RNG is strong, but not like Darkest Dungeon, where you can build around reducing its impact. In fact, you can't really HAVE a build in Ring of Pain because all the actually impactful items are single or triple use only and then disappear. Imagine Slay the Spire but it's only potions and the standard attack card.Again, I love the art style and the idea of a min max game like this, it's just badly executed.

_childDocuments_.review: The main mechanic of the game is completly chanced based. You can pass by monsters in the ring but that is based on your stealth stat which is only 20% if you don't have some very specific items. Relying only on rng like that is a bad choice. They could have easily made the mechanic tied to stacks of an item or conditionally on something else to make it possible to actually plan your turns instead of: let's see if can slip past or die. Additonally every enemy has at least 1 piercing damage which renders defense pretty useless when you can never 100% block an attack but always have to take damage. Imagine Slay the spire if you could only block 80% of all incoming damage each turn. Speaking of Sts: Ring of pain has no classes and no starting layouts. Which is really a huge minus. Every run feels the same. There are mutators in the daily challenge but you can't even make a custom game yourself. I am suprised this game isn't early access as it feels like it needs a lot of rebalancing and added content to be worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR this game is another gem in Roguelike games and still has a lot of potentials to explore.I've played this game more than 10 hours after buying it last weekend. It is very addictive and I appreciate its simplicity on choices. I don't hate RNG elements as some other comments mentioned. I can see the game has been well polished before releasing. In short words, if you ever played slay the spire and you like it, don't miss this one: it is another totally different style and having almost same level of quality.My major criticism on the game (don't get me wrong, even with these "drawbacks", this is still already a great game and kudos to dev's innovations and efforts!) is the depth of game elements at this stage. After several trial runs, soon I found 180 (so far) items are not enough for such a item-based RL game. Even slay the spire (a card-based game) has more items to maximum the playing experience, and it has three characters with their own skillsets. I'm not trying to take adbvantages of dev's hardwork here -- I'm totally happy to pay another 10, 20 bucks for extension packs. Another problem is item still needs some balancing. Clearly some legendary items are OP. I played the game with different language versions so I miss the official names, but the one doing AOE when adding HP and the spire attacks monster when approaching them is totally game changer. I'm not advocating nerfing them (they make the game experience wonderful!), instead, I hope other legendary items have similar strengths. So the game would not be just about "oh I lose the game because I didn't run into item XXX".

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. This is one of the best rogue-like/card based games in this genre I have ever played. If there are comparisons in terms of feeling, I would compare this to Darkest Dungeon's gloomy setting with dashes of hope hidden here and there. You are pushed into the absolute limits of your survival. Enemies at each flank are working to take you down and prevent you from learning about the Ring of Pain. The time to recover and catch your breath will be brief, and it never feels like enough. No problem. It is our turn to take the fight to them.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has it all to shine, the theme, art, music, creatures, even the story and the ruthlessness of the game; all of this manages to be cohesive in a way that feels seamless.To speak of the gameplay itself, it's a very minimalistic take on dungeon crawling, keeping only the essential parts to cut on the time wasting and transforming it into a turn based puzzle game where a single mistake can spell your doom. And trust me, there are pitfalls waiting for you at every step... heheheheh!It has a random aspect to room compositions, loot and some special effects, but most of the interactions stay fully controlled, giving the game a high skill ceiling. The fairly wide array of equipment allow interesting combinations, although some items feel clearly stronger than others, it doesn't prevent from using most of them depending on the configuration.Now you might say I'm only singing praise of this game... and you'd be right, because I instantly fell in love with it when I tried the demo! Now, I know it has some flaws, sometimes unfair with no chances of escape, sometimes huge strokes of bad luck can kill you in a flash, or a bad starting room that makes you snowball into a vicious circle of getting weaker.And all of this can happen, that's true, but I played enough to tell you that it can be hugely mitigated through choices. Skill is also a big part of learning how to lower the impact of randomness by making the best choices to lower the risks. And if you still get unfairly killed? That's not an issue, you can just restart and jump right in again due to the fast paced gameplay! So die, and die again, until you become strong enough to overcome your fears and shadows!Don't hesitate, this game is worth it.Walk the Ring of Pain, you won't regret it.Trust me friend, I would tell no lie.This is the truth, look in my eye.

_childDocuments_.review: Unique horror-themed dungeon crawler card game.  The circling mechanic is ingenious and adds something new that other dungeon card crawlers do not have. Enemy variety could be higher, but it's a solid start for a beta, and most of the enemies have different gruesome sounds that illustrate their personalities. _childDocuments_.review: A really clever rogue-lite game that relies on extremely simple base mechanics with a high amount of emergent strategy.   There are only a few controls -  attack left/right,  move left/right, or use your spell/scroll item.   I've played many many roguelites and deckbuilders and TBS games.  I can't believe how DIFFICULT this game is.  I have 42 hours on the game as of writing, which is probably 300+ runs, and only like 3 victories.   I would like to say each loss feels "fair", but really the RNG is very strong in this game.  I think some runs are just unwinnable.  In fact, some runs it feels like impossible to even  pass the 1st or 2nd level!!   I dont' mind this difficulty, but you should understand that the RNG is heavy and very punishing.  TBH there's not THAT much control you have over each run, because the enemies are random and the items you find are random.  You can spend your souls to re-roll items (at an increasing cost) but this is pretty limited.   Anyway the game design is slick, very clever and unique idea.  It's downright fun to play.  The runs are much shorter than most rogue-lite games, unless you are on a winning run (then maybe 30-45 minutes?), but these are rare.   Because many runs end after only a few minutes, it has a really strong "one-more-run" element to it.  I hadn't launched the game in many months, and was pleasantly surprised to see new updates, new game modes when I launched!  Seems like devs are continuing to improve and support this game. On sale, definitely worth it.  Full price, worth it if you like this kind of game (punishing RNG roguelite).  I mean... if you can get 4+ hours out of it then it's probably already worth full price on a purely financial level. One thing I imagine could improve this game greatly would be more variety of items,  possibly more synergies between items (there are "sets" but i'm not sure if they do anything?  It's almost impossible to collect a full set anyway).   Also if there were some kind of skills or spells you could use beyond just the basic controls and solitary spellbook, that could add a lot of depth here.     But I understand the game is streamlined in a certain way, and it does that well. Graphics are simple (everything is a card) but quite well done, and the aesthetic is pleasing.  There is a surprising amount of tension that arises on tight runs, considering it's a turn-based "card" game!   7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ring of Pain

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little roguelike card game. I am not that into these type of games but the simplicity of Ring of Pain appeals to me. The spooky aesthetic is neat and everything is quick and snappy so the endless runs are always enjoyable. I ultimately suck at the game though and will probably never get further than halfway through, but it was worth the couple bucks I spent on it. If there were a more impactful form of meta progression aside from unlocking items that may or may not show up on future runs, I would stick with it, but unfortunately that’s all there is. Eventually things get pretty repetitive and remain tough, so there’s not much reason to keep banging your head against the wall.

_childDocuments_.review: Singular aesthetics and simple mechanics combine with a wide breadth of implementations to make a game with excellent replayability, especially in the kind of bite-sized chunks it seems designed for. While the RNG can feel especially obtuse, the constrained sets and values of numbers make any upgrades and progression within a given run feel meaty and satisfying: switching from one weapon to another, even within the same tier, frequently feels like a meaningful change in your capabilities. Consistent unlocks of starting modes and new items keep the gameplay varied and engaging. A solid 8/10 for gameplay, and unique and unimpeachably stylistic art earns it a 9/10 in visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible dungeon crawler with an awesome spooky art style. I just completed my first run, maybe the 5th or so run? If you're good at other roguelite deckbuilders (though it's arguable whether this counts as a deckbuilder) then you can apply a lot of the same logic and strategies to this game.I see a number of people saying the game is too based on rng, but from my experience that's part of the game's experience. At any moment you're only able to take one of a few actions, and you need to figure out which of those actions is going to provide you with the most valuable outcome. Sometimes that means taking risks and getting curbstomped by the dice, but that's how it is in these run-based games. I think I've played enough of these types of games now that I can "see the matrix" and pick apart game mechanics, which is further helped by myself being a games programmer. The first run I completed I had utterly broken stats, which was indeed aided by good rng with the items I found along the way, but it was built off the back of several failed runs before, and knowing which items I wanted to take a chance with equipping.For anyone struggling to progress further in the game, consider if items that provide knockback or other board-manipulating items could give you an extra option or two when you're coming up against a sticky situation. And I'd honestly just forget about the clarity stat, as it doesn't get you many benefits and there's some very powerful items that require you to have as low a clarity as possible! You can then focus on speed and defence, which are arguably more important than attack, as many items provide you with damage buffs based on other stats or item synergies.Overall, an awesome game that's exactly what I was hoping for from this genre. And for those who are still to beat it - I believe in you!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice addition to my roguelite deckbuilders that I didn't even know I needed.  This game is great at giving both some decent strategy but also in a really fast / rapid way.  While I love Slay and Monster Train, this game is something entirely different and a really good one at that.  True to the game's name, the cards are all arranged in a ring and you can skip over enemies with sufficient stealth or they'll take a free shot at you if you fail the check.  Enemies are mixed with buffs and treasures etc so you can finish the whole 'level' and get all the bonuses while fighting everything or you can just bolt for the exit as soon as you see it.  This dynamic is a really cool one that makes me consider deckbuilders in a way that I've just never really needed to before.  Oh and stay on the Owl's good side.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple addictive card game roguelike. The game is by design quite random (as card games are!). To put simply: In the game you play somewhere around 20 floors (hands) where you'll try to simultaneously survive and improve both your gear and stats for subsequent levels that include end-game boss levels.The first clears player manages to get are probably ones where he/she gets by luck awesome gear combination and avoids worst idiocies. In some runs the game blesses you and in some it throws hilariously hideous stuff. In between those lies however huge area where player can try to manage according to his/her skills and learn planning further ahead than the next move. The game contains potentially much decision weighing: "Is it smart to waste X health and Y souls for random epic equipment?", "Is it smart to reroll stuff for cost or can I manage with this stuff?", "Do I skip this floor, even if I can't then afford equipment from next shop?", "Is my character strong enough to risk going into 'reckless' room?", "Should I aim for specific build?", "Is my dodge, parry and stealth chance high enough to risk passing heavy-hitting enemy", "Do I run away from chasing enemy, even if I don't know cards that are further ahead" etc. etc.After clearing the game on harder difficulties or different scenarios (achievements are quite nice) and then going back to normal difficulty (where the journey started) makes you feel surprisingly achieved.

_childDocuments_.review: My partner played this through family sharing and loved it so much they wanted to leave a recommendation:This game looks and sounds amazing. The art style is really unique and psychedelic as well as being a little unsettling. It feels magical because of the cosmic horror elements and the claustrophobia of the dungeons but the items and sounds are so bright and colourful. The tension is well maintained as you progress and there are sweet and funny surprises throughout the journey. The theming is really consistent and creates an interesting world with a larger backstory. The game mechanics are simple and easy to grasp quite quickly, although it's sometimes hard to trace through a chain reaction to understand what happened. I'd recommend this game to people who have had a nice intro to turn based card games like Slay the Spire, but I don't think you need to be a card expert to play. There is enough there to hold the attention of more experienced players yet it's versatile and beginner-friendly. All in all, great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not my favorite rogue-like, but visually interesting and mechanically unique enough to stand out. The whole aesthetic is very eery and psychological. RoP never tells you exactly who you are or why you're here; as best I can tell from context clues, the whole game takes place "inside the player's mind" and is a metaphor for fighting depression.The left/right action structure of each level is something I haven't seen in a game before and I like it. Gives way to a lot of strategically interesting options as you discover new items. Feels easy to learn, but long term success in this game depends on learning the delicate dance of when to attack and when to move. One wrong pass is the end of a run.Early runs felt kind of monotonous, but--as with most roguelikes--unlocking items and learning the game have made it much more enjoyable. Definitely worth a try for fans of the genre looking for something a little different.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game from a bundle, otherwise i would never have seen it. And i'm glad i did.I really liked the style of this game, not only in the cards'art, but also in the fever dream-like atmosphere it creates (it kinda gave me that feeling i got playing the first stages of Inscryption). And the music is GREAT.Gameplay is quite fun and can get challenging at higher difficulties, but the core mechanics are very simple to understand.The price might be just a little bit too high for what it offers at its current state, but if you find it on sale it's a must buy.Overall it's a 7/10 with a LOT of room to improve and potentially be one of the best dungeon crawler roguelikes ever.Note: Game is currently tagged as Deck-builder and Roguelite, both of these are not really correct. Despite everything looking like cards, there's no deck building at all. The most similar element is having to choose and replace equipment that fits your build better.As for rogueliTe, there's not really that much meta progression, you just unlock new "cards"(equipment) during your runs whenever you complete achievement. It's not like in Hades or other games where you get permanent upgrades between runs.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most original games in recent times, and it works.Despite what it might look like at first glance; this is NOT a deckbuilder. I would qualify it more as a minimalistic roguelike RPG.Absurdly simple in its basics: Each turn you are faced with 2 options, and you choose to either interact with it (attack/pick up/activate), or try to skip it. That's it. That's the game. And it's amazing.I do feel like there's maybe a tad too much RNG for a game with such heavy focus on making correct decisions, but most of it feels fair enough for a game that aims to be tricky.

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelike "card game" with very unique mechanics:* Ring-shaped dungeons. The ring consists of enemies / healpots / pickups / doors. Killing an enemy or consuming a pickup decreases the size of the ring* You can move left/right past enemies.  There is a Stealth stat which governs if you are detected and attacked while doing so* Equipment is random (it's a roguelike), but you can reroll for cash (souls). Very synergy based!* Starting and restarting is very quick, no forced fluff.* Achievements unlock new equipment and starting gear. This starting gear has *major* influence on a run e.g. massive stealth boost, convert all stats, sacrifice health instead of moneyAlso worth noting:* Exceptional hand drawn art! The devs are proud of their creepy monsters with good reason!* Difficult achievements, e.g. minimal health run, minimal equipment run, don't use higher level equipment, etc. Took me 106 hours until I got all achievements* KBM/Controller. Works perfectly well with both, you don't need many buttons.* They're adding more content!

_childDocuments_.review: Ring of Pain is interesting and enjoyable in ways that can keep you enthralled despite doing almost the exact same thing for hours. It nails the creepy aesthetic from the art and sound design right down to the way it plays. It can make you feel a bit unsettled no matter what stage of the game you're at and how confident you're feeling. Ring of Pain swings between frustration and satisfaction but thankfully leans heavily to the latter most of the time. _childDocuments_.review: It's an addictive game that I continue to come back to time and time again. It's quick to pick up and restart yet enjoyable to play for hours testing new builds. It might not be everyone's cup of tea since it can be very unforgiving and fail to rng at times. Some people who I know are fans of card games weren't too patient playing this game and found it not enjoyable with how frequently you die in runs when you're figuring things out. You just have to be patient and test out new strategies to stick with. The art style is appealing and different, yet clearly illustrates the aspects pf each card. The safest build I found most luck with even on the highest difficulty mode is going with a compounding petrify/ freeze/ or poison side effect and bulking up defense so high nothing can touch you except poison. You'd have to find an item that randomly attacks other creatures on a turn to deal with creatures with intimidation and poison. Splash weapons can be your downfall if you can't see all the cards and accidentally get cornered with explosives. The other build for getting you far enough in the game is if you can find the freezing tiara and go with a high speed/ stealth. Which can take a long time just slowly picking away at big bosses. This ultimately fails though when you reach a boss that is resistant to freeze. The story is too mysterious to gleam much out of without heavy theorizing and coming up with a backstory yourself but it doesn't make the game un-enjoyable because the mechanics by itself makes the game fun to play that a decipherable story isn't needed to be entertaining.There are some points left to be desired. I really wish there was an endless mode to see how crazy your numbers can get given some of the manic and chaos items really play with stats. The game doesn't last long enough to create a glass canon. Some runs I feel like I never reach the full potential of a build to try out some wild tactics. And, though understandable, I feel this game would fit really well on a mobile port with how basic the controls are. It would be cool if the game was easily mod-able by the community, like Inscryption, with an endless mode and creating new cards. The game has a fantastic game mechanic with a ton of potential. I'd definitely recommend the game to those who love strategy games without much commitment. Given how frequently I've played the game and returned to it, I'd put it in my all time top favorite games to play list.
_childDocuments_.name: Ring of Pain

_childDocuments_.review: I have to agree with the reviews that are complaining about RNG. I played this game for roughly 30 - 45 minutes and immediately started telling my friends how interesting this battle system was. I was having fun just going through the rooms in the early game... until I started getting a bit further. It sucks having to go back and tell everyone to wait on this. I would've refunded if I could because I'm so disappointed with how the scaling works. Up until around room 6, everything's fine. Then you come across enemies that can one-shot you no matter how you've been building up until that point. For instance, I have 22 Health at this moment and 5 Defense. I've tried to take Defense items every chance I've gotten, and this is all the game's given me. Fine, hopefully being at full 22 Health is enough....Oh, the next room starts me with two enemies that each deal over 20 damage. Wtf is a Crooked Loombird and how did it make it into the game? This combined with other dumb stuff like Skulker (that I guess always bring you down to 1 health?) have ended every single one of my runs (and right now I've spawned on a floor with two of them in front of me). I know the impulse is to say 'Oh, you have to LEARN and GET GUD' but there's nothing I could've done differently. Every single time I get to room 7 or 8, assuming I don't just use a spell to instantly leave the floor, I run into one of these guys and die. If I'm supposed to keep beating my head against the wall until I unlock higher tier items, I just won't do it. In the early rounds, you're actually making micro-decisions based on your current stats to maximize efficiency and clear floors/get loot. That feels great. It's as soon as you step outside of those first few rooms that you're no longer making decisions and just doing whatever the floor gave you. If I can go left to live a little longer, or attack an explosive barrel and die instantly.... that's not a choice. If I can attack a Crooked Loombird and die, flee from a Crooked Loombird and have a 70% chance of dying, or come on here and leave a negative review.... well, that's not a choice either.EDIT: Well, the Dev responded, but I can't say it's comforting. I've used both colored doors and regular doors in my runs, but those later paths always act as a complete block. I don't expect to kill every enemy, but if the previous room had enemies deal 6 damage on average, and the very next room has them dealing 20?????? that's a pretty big jump guys. I really hope you're actually considering balance changes beyond just labeling doors 'hard' or 'easy'.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to see this in my Humble Choice options for the month, since this had been on my list of games to check out. I really wanted to like Ring of Pain. At this point, I've played enough of it now to feel like I understand what makes it tick, what are good choices and bad choices, and I've experienced the endgame on more than one run. Ultimately though, it relies too heavily on RNG for difficulty, lacks sufficient player agency, and suffers from an excessive amount of death-explosion creatures. These elements combined make it unfun to wade through.Compared to Ring of Pain's obvious competitors, it comes up short where it counts, and it's a real shame because the artistic design of the game and atmosphere are superbly executed.There's a lot to like here, honestly!Sadly the negatives outweigh the positives.I want to reiterate that I really, really wanted to like this game. Ring of Pain looks great, is interesting conceptually, and felt like it had something unique to offer when I dove into it. Ultimately though, the game doesn't reward you for the time put into it, and it doesn't feel good putting that time in. The more I played it, the more I found myself thinking I'd rather be playing Slay The Spire, or Monster Train, or any of the several other similar games in my library that do feel good to play and reward time put in, learning, and good decision making.I'll keep an eye on Ring of Pain, since it looks like the developer is still putting in work into it and I hope they find a way to improve the experience, but as it stands I just can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Has a lot of promise, but there are just too many glaring flaws that make it tough to enjoy this game for more than a couple hours.  It has the standard Isaac problem where a ton of items are locked behind arbitrary achievements, and it is totally up to debate whether you are better off unlocking them.  There are too many trash items, or items that are completely useless without specific combos.  The more items you unlock, the less likely you are to get said combos. All of the items that give you a benefit for having a negative stat value are a complete joke and a waste of programming space.  You need to stack them to get even marginal benefits, and the odds of getting multiples of the set in a given game are astronomical.  Even if multiples did appear, since you have to pick items one at a time, there is literally no scenario where I would ever take one of these, and it's loaded with them.  There is no ability to block certain items in a given run - a feature that it would benefit from massively.  Seriously, if I could just turn off 10 or 15 trash-tier items, that alone would probably push my review to positive.Item 'value' seems to have little to do with how strong an item actually is.  The 160-cost chests are just as likely (if not moreso) to contain worthless garbage as any free chests.  The item balance just isn't there; it's like they threw darts at a board to determine what stuff gives you and shuffled them into rarity tiers completely at random.  They actually rate 1 HP to be just as valuable as 1 defense.  Let's see... I could take one more damage to kill in total, or I could reduce ALL damage I take by one for the rest of the run.  Yeah, tough call there.The idea of choice is largely illusory.  Sure, you can swipe left or right, but you usually just smash whatever in front of you and only move to get away from the explodey dudes, or chase down ranged attackers.  The stealth mechanic is too random and unlikely to work to justify moving past enemies 90% of the time.  On that note, there is just too much RNG in general, and I absolutely do not trust their lying percentages.  20% stealth seems to be more like 30-40%, while a 75% curse resist chance is more like 10%.  I seriously drank 100 or so curse potions over the course of my many runs, with an average curse resist of maybe 55-60%, and I could count the number of times they didn't curse me on my hands, and still have enough fingers left to go bowling.It was pretty fun for a couple hours, but without some major balance changes I don't think it's worth even a heavily discounted sale price.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Have to flip my review on this one.  I did enjoy the game at first, but later rounds of balancing have forced the game into a place where randomness affects the game much more.  If you are hungry for a card game, there are better options out there.  Ultimately, I only load up Ring of Pain when I'm bored of everything else in my library, and always close it after a few runs.  It's boring now.This game is a reverse deck builder, if that makes any sense.  You pit yourself against various arrays of enemy cards.  The path you choose through them, the decisions to fight or flee from them and in which order is the strategic premise.  In practice, I spent my health far more generously than my currency.  Potions are plentiful.  Killing monsters is the only sure way to get currency, so being shy isn't rewarded.  Chugging potions while you trade stabs with the monster next door pays though.  The random loot drops are very run-defining at first, but because you can only have one of each kind, later loot drops must frequently be discarded or change you strategy mid-game.It's challenging.  The theme, art, and sound are all great.  The lore gets old fast though, especially the mandatory lore rooms that you can't click through.  These have only 3 different lines you can chose from to read and after 100 runs you've seen it all and it's just a hassle.At least, that's how it looks to me.  Play this game.  It's good.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot like some other roguelikes that I've played, namely Slay the Spire and sort of like Dead Cells. Granted, I've only got a couple of hours played, but I've already gotten the general concept of Ring of Pain very quickly. Don't be discouraged that the tutorial seems a bit barebones and doesn't tell you about any stats, they're super familiar and easy to latch onto once you look at them and see how they change with items and such. You'll be min/maxing your builds in no time at all.NOW. That being said, I enjoyed playing my three hours and getting a couple 20 minute runs here and there, thought I knew the ropes, and got to a boss room. As a roguelike, I expected this to be hard. The boss wasn't really a tough fight though - usually a first timer can at least put up a fight, but considering that I had around 25 max hp at the time and it did 63 damage in one turn, and not to mention it had about 30x the amount of health I could deal in a single hit, I didn't last more than three turns. I was a little bit surprised, which is strange coming from a guy who's used to having bosses that are difficult. Did I expect to win? No, not even close, I wasn't clearing rooms full of regular baddies regardless of their late game stats. Did I expect to take a hit worth twice my hp bar? Not even close. I've still got a lot to learn, but I'm ready to bang my head against this brick wall for a long time - rewarding gameplay loop and fun build variety make this an instant classic, and like Slay the Spire there is no mechanical skill, it's all about the strategy, so you never have to worry about BS hitboxes or anything of the sort. 10/10 would get daddied by the Owl again

_childDocuments_.review: Check out Isla Blake's review (the most up voted/most help negative review overall) to see a review that sums up the game. Just gives you the same ending as you get on normal or medium (for some reason the dev of this game thinks medium has a different meaning then normal when it comes to difficulty, when in truth, both words mean the same thing in that regard, dude shoulda just went with normal/hard/very hard, but whatever).So ya, my advice to anyone who buys this game, is just enjoy it until you get bored of it.
